questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 6408 × 8 + 27 – 15 ÷ 10 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 6408 ÷ 8 − 27 + 15 × 10 = 801 − 27 + 150 = 924.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 81, 65, 50, ?, 23, 11

In a certain code language, X + Y means ‘X is the sister of Y’, X − Y means ‘X is the son of Y’, X × Y means ‘X is the husband of Y’, X ÷ Y means ‘X is the mother of Y’. Based on the above, how is T related to X if ‘T + U − V × W ÷ X’?
questions.explanation: T is U's sister and U is V's son, so T is V's daughter. V is W's husband and W is X's mother, so X is also V and W's child: T is X's sister.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All crows are parrots. All eagles are parrots. All parrots are birds. Conclusions: I. No crow is a bird. II. Some birds are eagles. III. All birds are crows.
options: Both conclusions I and III follow.
Either conclusion II or III follows.
questions.explanation: Every crow and every eagle is a parrot, and every parrot a bird. So all crows are birds (I fails), and as all eagles are birds, some birds are eagles (II follows). Nothing says all birds are crows (III).

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different. The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster
questions.explanation: RTTUWW, ACCDFF and IKKLNN follow the steps +2, 0, +1, +2, 0 (R T T U W W). NOPPSS goes +1, +1, 0, +3, 0, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FLAKE’ is written as ‘&2348’ and ‘LAKES’ is written as ‘23@84’. How will ‘S’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: L, A, K and E are in both words, as are 2, 3, 4 and 8 in both codes. The letter left in LAKES is S and the symbol left in its code is @, so S = @ (and F = &).

questions.text: The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if each of the letter in the word ‘IMPROVE’ is arranged in English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: IMPROVE in alphabetical order is E I M O P R V. Position by position (I/E, M/I, P/M, R/O, O/P, V/R, E/V) no letter stays where it was.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All peas are vegetables. All carrots are vegetables. All vegetables are greens. Conclusions: I. All peas are greens. II. All greens are carrots. III. Some greens are peas.
options: Both conclusions II and III follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: All peas are vegetables and all vegetables are greens, so all peas are greens (I), and therefore some greens are peas (III). Nothing makes all greens carrots (II).

questions.text: The same operation(s) are followed in all the given number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 12 : 8, 72 : 48 and 36 : 24 the second number is two-thirds of the first. Two-thirds of 24 is 16, not 4, so 24 : 4 is the odd one.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 15 − 7 ÷ 4 + 36 × 9 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 15 + 7 × 4 − 36 ÷ 9 = 15 + 28 − 4 = 39.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BAKE’ is coded as ‘FDMF’ and ‘TURN’ is coded as ‘XXTO’. How will ‘MOCK’ be coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +4, +3, +2, +1: BAKE → FDMF and TURN → XXTO. So MOCK → QREL.

questions.text: Select the term from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. MY 84, KW 80, IU 76, GS 72, ?
questions.explanation: Both letters move back 2 each time (M, K, I, G, E and Y, W, U, S, Q) and the number falls by 4: EQ 68.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the given sets. (3, 9, 27) (4, 16, 64) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each set is a number, its square and its cube: 3, 9, 27 and 4, 16, 64. Likewise 7, 49 and 343.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? XJUM, VLSO, TNQQ, RPOS, ?
questions.explanation: The first and third letters move back 2 (X, V, T, R, P and U, S, Q, O, M) and the second and fourth forward 2 (J, L, N, P, R and M, O, Q, S, U): PRMU.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 4 : 32 7 : 98
questions.explanation: The second number is twice the square of the first: 2 × 4² = 32 and 2 × 7² = 98. Likewise 2 × 3² = 18.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (84, 63, 42) (79, 47, 64) (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The third number is twice the difference of the first two: 2 × (84 − 63) = 42 and 2 × (79 − 47) = 64. Likewise 2 × (71 − 53) = 36.

questions.text: Select the word-pair that best represents a similar relationship to the one expressed in the pair of words given below. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Frequency : Hertz
questions.explanation: The hertz is the SI unit of frequency, as the lux is of illuminance. Power is measured in watts, resistance in ohms and force in newtons.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. X _ _ Y_X X _ _ X _ _
options: Y X X Y Y X X
X X Y Y A A X
X X X Y X X Y
Y Y X Y A X X
questions.explanation: With X, X, X, Y, X, X, Y in the blanks the block XXXY repeats: XXXY XXXY XXXY.

questions.text: Who among the following Indian classical dancers is associated with Kuchipudi?
questions.explanation: Vempati Chinna Satyam was one of the great gurus of Kuchipudi, the classical dance of Andhra Pradesh. Sanjukta Panigrahi was an Odissi dancer.

questions.text: How many ICC World Cups has India won in ODI?
questions.explanation: India won the ODI World Cup in 1983 and 2011.

questions.text: With reference of Ajivikas, consider the following statements. a) Makkhali Gosala was the prominent teacher of this sect. b) Ajivikas believed in fatalism. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Makkhali Gosala was the leading teacher of the Ajivikas, who held that everything is fixed by fate (niyati). Both statements are correct.

questions.text: Who first stated the principle of refraction that postulates that every substance has a specific bending ratio – ‘refractive index’?
questions.explanation: Willebrord Snellius (Snell) found in 1621 that the sines of the angles of incidence and refraction are in a constant ratio for two given media: Snell's law, the basis of the refractive index.

questions.text: Who among the following was appointed as the Chief Economic Advisor (CEA) to the Indian government in 2022?
questions.explanation: V. Anantha Nageswaran was appointed Chief Economic Adviser in January 2022, succeeding K. V. Subramanian.

questions.text: Which Article in the fundamental duty is invoked when you see in a private party that the Indian flag has been used as a covering for the speaker’s desk?
questions.explanation: Article 51A(a) asks every citizen to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem. The Flag Code forbids using the flag to cover a speaker's desk.

questions.text: Kati Bihu is celebrated in which of the following months in Assam?
questions.explanation: Kati (Kongali) Bihu falls in mid-October, in the Assamese month of Kati, when lamps are lit in the paddy fields.

questions.text: Coir conductor Coomi Nariman Wadia was awarded with which of the following awards by the Government of India in 2023?
questions.explanation: Coomi Nariman Wadia, the Mumbai choir conductor of the Paranjoti Academy Chorus, received the Padma Shri in 2023.

questions.text: What is the gas evolved when zinc reacts with sulphuric acid?
questions.explanation: Zinc displaces hydrogen from dilute sulphuric acid: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂.

questions.text: Name the pension scheme that seeks to ensure old age protection for unorganised workers.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (2019), set up for the old-age protection and social security of unorganised workers; it pays ₹3,000 a month from the age of 60. (The Atal Pension Yojana is also aimed mainly at the unorganised sector, but is open to citizens in general.)

questions.text: Who published Systema Naturae in 1735 classifying the three kingdoms of nature and outlining the sexual system for the classification of plants?
questions.explanation: Carl Linnaeus published 'Systema Naturae' in 1735, setting out his classification of nature and his sexual system for plants.

questions.text: In 2022, who has been appointed as new Attorney General of India?
questions.explanation: R. Venkataramani became Attorney General of India on 1 October 2022, succeeding K. K. Venugopal.

questions.text: The most common rainfall measurement is the total rainfall depth during a given period, which is expressed in ________.
questions.explanation: Rainfall is measured as the depth of water collected, in millimetres; hectopascals, millibars and kilopascals are units of pressure.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a kharif crop?
questions.explanation: Wheat is a rabi crop, sown in winter and harvested in spring. Cotton, paddy and soyabean are kharif crops, sown with the monsoon.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the second five-year plan is INCORRECT?
options: The plan was based on the Keynesian Model.
Electricity, Railway, Steel etc. industries were established during the plan.
The plan stressed the rapid industrialisation of heavy and basic industries.
The socialist pattern of the society was reflected in the plan.
questions.explanation: The Second Plan (1956-61) was based on P. C. Mahalanobis's model, not the Keynesian one. It did stress heavy industry, with the steel plants at Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela, in pursuit of a socialist pattern of society.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Being the President of the Indian National Congress, who among the following had called for complete independence from the British Raj in 1929?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the Lahore session of the Congress in December 1929, which adopted the Purna Swaraj resolution.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a tributary of Ganga?
questions.explanation: The Lohit is a tributary of the Brahmaputra. The Yamuna, Kosi and Gandak all join the Ganga.

questions.text: Which of the following ministries launched the PM Daksh scheme?
options: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
questions.explanation: PM-DAKSH, a skill-development scheme for Scheduled Castes, backward classes and sanitation workers, is run by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

questions.text: When a person is NOT paying anything for public goods, it is known as _________.
questions.explanation: Public goods are non-excludable, so people can enjoy them without paying; such a person is a free rider.

questions.text: Which of the following team events is included in the Target Olympic Podium Scheme?
questions.explanation: TOPS, the Sports Ministry's scheme for athletes with Olympic medal prospects, includes India's men's and women's hockey teams.

questions.text: __________ is often touted as Tansen of the 20th century, this musical genius blended the best of classical music and created a unique style of his own.
questions.explanation: Bade Ghulam Ali Khan, the Patiala gharana vocalist, is often called the Tansen of the 20th century.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In 1936, The Independent Labour Party was founded by _______.
questions.explanation: B. R. Ambedkar founded the Independent Labour Party in 1936.

questions.text: Which of the following is another name of vitamin C?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid. Pyridoxal, pyridoxine and pyridoxamine are forms of vitamin B6.

questions.text: Articles 214 to 231 in Part VI of the Indian Constitution deal with the __________.
questions.explanation: Chapter V of Part VI (Articles 214 to 231) deals with the High Courts in the States; the subordinate courts follow in Chapter VI (Articles 233 to 237).

questions.text: Which of the following Sultans of Delhi primarily adopted a policy of consolidation rather than expansion?
questions.explanation: Balban concentrated on consolidating the Sultanate, strengthening the army and the Crown's authority, rather than conquering new lands. Alauddin Khalji, by contrast, expanded far into the Deccan.

questions.text: XAB and XCD are two secants to a circle. If XA = 18 cm, AB = 22 cm and XC = 24 cm, then find the value of XD (in cm).
questions.explanation: By the secant theorem XA × XB = XC × XD. XB = 18 + 22 = 40, so 18 × 40 = 24 × XD and XD = 30 cm.

questions.text: Find the fourth proportional to 4, 9 and 16.
If the medians of a triangle are equal, then the triangle will be:
questions.explanation: If all three medians are equal, all three sides are equal: the triangle is equilateral.

questions.text: The length, breadth and height of a room is 15 m, 9 m, and 5 m, respectively. From each can of paint 40 square metre of area is painted. How many cans of paint will be needed to paint only the walls of the room?
questions.explanation: The four walls cover 2(15 + 9) × 5 = 240 m², and 240/40 = 6 cans.

questions.text: A motorboat, whose speed in 15 km/h in still water goes 50 km downstream and comes back in a total of 7 hours 30 minutes. The speed of the stream (in km/h) is:
The marked price of a bed sheet is ₹500. At the time of its sale, two successive discounts of 10% and 5% are available. Find the selling price (in ₹) of the bed sheet.
Hema is 20 years old and her sister Neha is 30 years old. How many years ago were their ages in the ratio of 3 : 5?

Three pipes, P, Q and R, together take four hours to fill a tank. All the three pipes were opened at the same time. After three hours, P was closed, and Q and R filled the remaining tank in two hours. How many hours will P alone take to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: Together they fill 1/4 of the tank an hour, so 3/4 in three hours. Q and R fill the remaining 1/4 in 2 hours, so 1/8 an hour; P alone fills 1/4 − 1/8 = 1/8 an hour and takes 8 hours.

questions.text: The distance between the longest chord and the centre of a circle is:
options: equal to the half of the radius
questions.explanation: The longest chord is a diameter, which passes through the centre, so its distance from the centre is zero.

questions.text: A mango juice is made by mixing water and mango concentrate in the ratio 9 : 7. If x litres of water and 3x litres of mango concentrate is mixed in 160 litres of mango juice, then the new ratio becomes 13 : 14. What is the quantity of the new mango juice (in litres)?
questions.explanation: The 160 litres hold 90 litres of water and 70 of concentrate. (90 + x)/(70 + 3x) = 13/14 gives 1260 + 14x = 910 + 39x, so x = 14. The new juice is 160 + 4 × 14 = 216 litres.

questions.text: The marked price of 55 items was equal to the cost price of 99 items. The selling price of 56 items was equal to the marked price of 35 items. Calculate the profit or loss percentage from the sale of each item.
questions.explanation: MP/CP = 99/55 = 9/5 and SP/MP = 35/56 = 5/8, so SP/CP = 9/8: a profit of 12.5%.

questions.text: The least number which must be subtracted from 7278745 so as to obtain a sum that is divisible by 11 is:
questions.explanation: The alternating sum of the digits from the right is 5 − 4 + 7 − 8 + 7 − 2 + 7 = 12, which leaves remainder 1 on division by 11. Subtracting 1 gives 7278744 = 11 × 661704.

questions.text: Ten chairs and six tables together cost ₹5,140; three chairs and two tables together cost ₹1,635. The cost of 1 chair and 1 table is:
questions.explanation: Three times the second equation is 9 chairs + 6 tables = ₹4,905; subtracting it from the first gives 1 chair = ₹235. Then 2 tables = ₹1,635 − ₹705 = ₹930, so a table is ₹465 and a chair and a table ₹700.

questions.text: In an election between two candidates, P received 42% of the valid votes and Q won by 45,360 votes. 20% people did not cast their vote. If 10% of the votes cast were found invalid, what is the total number of votes registered in the poll booth?
questions.explanation: Q got 58% and P 42% of the valid votes, so the margin of 45,360 is 16% of them: 2,83,500 valid votes. They are 90% of the votes cast (3,15,000), which are 80% of the votes registered: 3,93,750.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Obstinate
questions.explanation: 'Obstinate' means refusing to change one's mind: 'stubborn'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank. My grandmother ________________ the preparation of every festival celebration in my house.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'initiates'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Aesthetic value is specifically a way in which we “can get positive conclude value” from the world at large.
questions.explanation: An adjective is needed before 'value', not the verb 'conclude': 'conclusive' is the adjective formed from it.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. P. and has also created a wide gap between them Q. laid too much stress on R. teachers and students S. online mode of education has
questions.explanation: 'Online mode of education has (S) laid too much stress on (Q) teachers and students (R) and has also created a wide gap between them (P).'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A thing that can be easily carried by hands
questions.explanation: Something easily carried is 'portable'; 'potable' means fit to drink.

questions.text: In the question, four alternatives are given for the underlined word in the sentence. Choose the alternative which best expresses the opposite meaning of the word. It was as if the newer hybrids had an “insatiable” appetite for chemicals.
questions.explanation: 'Insatiable' means impossible to satisfy; its opposite is 'satisfiable'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Left out in the cold
questions.explanation: To be 'left out in the cold' is to be ignored or excluded.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. He always wants to be in the company of those who are intellectually superior than him.
questions.explanation: 'Superior' takes 'to', not 'than': 'superior to him'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Break the ice
options: To say or do something that makes people feel more relaxed, especially at the beginning of a meeting, party
Ill-feeling carried by a person over a period of time
questions.explanation: To 'break the ice' is to ease the tension when people first meet.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I have sing ‘Let It Go’ before a crowd of thousands of people.
questions.explanation: The present perfect needs the past participle: 'I have sung'.

questions.text: Identify the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. Lady Stranleigh continued to smile at him “brilliantly.”
questions.explanation: To smile 'brilliantly' is to smile brightly; the opposite is 'dimly'.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. O. want P. movie tonight Q. do you R. to watch S. the
questions.explanation: 'Do you (Q) want (O) to watch (R) the (S) movie tonight (P)?'

questions.text: Select the option that correctly expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Mr. Amar refused him admittance.
options: Admittance would be refused to him by Mr. Amar.
Admittance shall be refused to him by Mr. Amar.
Admittance was refused to him by Mr. Amar.
Admittance will be refused to him by Mr. Amar.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'refused' becomes 'was refused' in the passive: 'Admittance was refused to him by Mr. Amar.'

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. P) always favours Q) only the R) fortune S) bold
questions.explanation: 'Fortune (R) always favours (P) only the (Q) bold (S).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank. The summer was ______ hot this year.
questions.explanation: 'Too' means excessively: 'too hot'. 'To', 'two' and 'tow' sound the same but mean something else.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. A. Only for themselves B. Is full of C. People who live D. The world
questions.explanation: 'The world (D) is full of (B) people who live (C) only for themselves (A).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank. The mothers, who suffer from postpartum depression, feel ______ by their children. (vexed)
questions.explanation: 'Vexed' means irritated: 'annoyed'.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the sentence. Can you please come back to reality from the “fectitious” world you live in?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'fictitious', meaning imaginary. 'Factitious' (artificial) is a different word.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Purify
questions.explanation: To 'purify' is to make clean; the opposite is to 'pollute'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Trigonometry has been taught by him for donkey’s years.
options: He has been teaching trigonometry for donkey’s years.
He had been teaching trigonometry for donkey’s years.
He is teaching trigonometry for donkey’s years.
He has been trigonometry teaching for donkey’s years.
questions.explanation: No option gives the plain present perfect 'He has taught trigonometry'; 'He has been teaching' keeps the present perfect, in its continuous form, which suits an action lasting 'for donkey's years'. The others move to the past perfect or the present continuous, or scramble the word order.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Music is perhaps the most popular and widely practised (1)______ of fine arts, transcending all kinds of cultural and linguistic barriers. Any form of fine art is (2)________ to master and almost impossible to perfect, and music is no exception. Nature, it is learnt, has blessed almost two-thirds of the human race with musical ability of some sort. Music has the power to (3)______ out the deepest emotions. In fact, it is a magic medicine, and many seek refuge in it when they are depressed or stressed. It is this intimacy that makes us listen to music (4)______ even hum or sing sometimes. This singing, or realistically speaking, expressing one’s emotion musically sometimes takes a serious turn. The desire to sing before an audience is innocent and beautiful, and indeed, it is perfectly alright to have such a genuine desire. But it is also important to understand that singing is an (5)________ art—a highly refined one at that, which requires systematic, prolonged and strict training to be acceptable.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: Music is a 'form' of fine art, as the next sentence says: 'Any form of fine art'.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.

Choose the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
