questions.explanation: A cartoon 'rendition' of Mike Tyson: a depiction of him.

questions.text: The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if all the letters in the word MENTOR are arranged in English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: MENTOR in alphabetical order is E M N O R T. Only N, third in both, keeps its place.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. JAP: BSH :: NDZ: FVR ::LCX:?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 8 places back, wrapping round after A: J → B, A → S, P → H and N → F, D → V, Z → R. So L → D, C → U and X → P: DUP.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. 3 — 20 — 7 5 — 26 — 8 NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The middle number is twice the sum of the other two: (3 + 7) × 2 = 20 and (5 + 8) × 2 = 26. Likewise (8 + 6) × 2 = 28.

questions.text: 51 is related to 256 by certain logic. Following the same logic, 53 is related to 266. To which of the following is 55 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is five times the first plus 1: 51 × 5 + 1 = 256 and 53 × 5 + 1 = 266. So 55 × 5 + 1 = 276.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? WIX, VHW, UGV, TFU, ?
questions.explanation: Every letter moves one place back each time: W, V, U, T, S; I, H, G, F, E; X, W, V, U, T. The next cluster is SET.

questions.text: The question contains pairs of words that are related to each other in a certain way. Three of the following four word pairs are alike as these have the same relationship and thus form a group. Which word pair is the one that DOES NOT belong to that group? (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.)
questions.explanation: Loud/noisy, honest/truthful and tired/exhausted are pairs of words with similar meanings. Close/open are opposites.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Sugar : Sweet :: Habanero : ?
questions.explanation: Sugar tastes sweet; the habanero, a chilli pepper, tastes spicy.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘DRIVE’ is coded as ‘62749’ and ‘RIDES’ is coded as ‘76284’. What is the code for ‘V’ in that language?
questions.explanation: D, R, I and E are in both words, as are 6, 2, 7 and 4 in both codes. The letter left in DRIVE is V and the digit left in its code is 9, so V = 9.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 1064 × 2 – 653 ÷ 2 + 89 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 1064 ÷ 2 + 653 × 2 − 89 = 532 + 1306 − 89 = 1749.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘she is girl’ is coded as ‘7 3 9’; ‘he is boy’ is coded as ‘9 6 5’ and ‘girl is tall’ is coded as ‘9 3 8’. How is ‘she’ coded in that language?
questions.explanation: 'is' is in all three sentences and 9 in all three codes, so is = 9; 'girl' and 3 are common to the first and third, so girl = 3. That leaves she = 7.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is S related to P if ‘P × Q ÷ R − S × A’?
questions.explanation: P is the wife of Q, Q is the father of R, R is the brother of S, and S is the wife of A. S is female and, like R, a child of Q and P, so S is P's daughter.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘÷’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘+’ are interchanged? 37 ÷ 56 – 7 × 2 + 6 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 37 − 56 ÷ 7 + 2 × 6 = 37 − 8 + 12 = 41.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that when placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the letter series. _ Y Z K X K X _ Z K X _ X Y _ K X K X Y Z _ X K X Y
questions.explanation: With X, Y, K, Z, K in the blanks the block XYZKXK repeats: XYZKXK XYZKXK XYZKXK XYZKXK XY.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some pineapples are oranges. All oranges are bananas. All bananas are plums. Conclusions: I. Some pineapples are plums. II. All oranges are plums. III. No pineapple is a banana.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: The pineapples that are oranges are bananas, and so plums: some pineapples are plums (I). Every orange is a banana and every banana a plum, so all oranges are plums (II). III is false, as some pineapples are bananas.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'TABU' is written as 'SBAV' and 'TANK’ is written as 'SBML'. How will 'TAIL’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move −1, +1, −1, +1: TABU → SBAV and TANK → SBML. So TAIL → SBHM.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (5, 80, 16) (18, 108, 6)
questions.explanation: The middle number is the product of the other two: 5 × 16 = 80 and 18 × 6 = 108. Likewise 13 × 7 = 91.

questions.text: Three of the following numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the odd one out. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 16 – 9 – 139, 12 – 7 – 79 and 17 – 5 – 80 the third number is the product of the first two minus 5 (144 − 5, 84 − 5, 85 − 5). 25 × 7 is exactly 175, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 300, 152, 80, 48, 40, 52, ?
According to the Varna system that was prevalent in the Vedic period, which of the following was NOT a Varna?
questions.explanation: The four varnas were the Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras. The Samiti was a popular assembly of the Vedic period, not a varna.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Sido and Kanhu were leaders of which of the following tribal rebellions?
questions.explanation: The brothers Sido and Kanhu Murmu led the Santhal rebellion (the Hul) of 1855-56.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who founded the Brahmo Samaj in Calcutta in 1828?
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha, later the Brahmo Samaj, in Calcutta in 1828.

questions.text: According to the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways’ annual report (2020-2021), which position does India have in terms of road networks in the world?
questions.explanation: MoRTH's annual reports describe India's road network as the second largest in the world, after that of the United States.

questions.text: The outermost part of the Earth is known as __________.
questions.explanation: The crust is the Earth's thin outermost layer, above the mantle and the core.

questions.text: Who among the following is one of the Deputy Chief Ministers of Uttar Pradesh as of July 2023?
questions.explanation: Keshav Prasad Maurya, with Brajesh Pathak, was a Deputy Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh in July 2023; Yogi Adityanath is the Chief Minister.

questions.text: Find out why white silver chloride turns grey in sunlight.
options: Due to rusting of silver in presence of oxygen
Due to the decomposition of silver chloride into silver and chlorine by light
Due to the displacement of silver chloride to silver oxide
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives decomposition: sunlight splits silver chloride into grey silver and chlorine (2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl₂), as NCERT describes it. Strictly, this decomposition is also a redox change (silver ions are reduced, chloride ions oxidised), but 'decomposition by light' is the fuller answer.

questions.text: Why does the milkman add a very small amount of baking soda to fresh milk?
options: To maintain the pH of the fresh milk at 6 for a longer time
To reduce the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly alkaline
To increase the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly alkaline
To reduce the pH of the fresh milk from 6 to slightly more acidic
questions.explanation: Baking soda makes the milk slightly alkaline, raising its pH from 6, so the milk does not turn sour as quickly.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Under which of the following Acts, the Board of Control was established in England to control and supervise the administration of British India?
questions.explanation: Pitt's India Act of 1784 set up the Board of Control in England to supervise the East India Company's civil, military and revenue affairs in India.

questions.text: The ________ of every state unfurls the flag in its capital on the Republic Day.
questions.explanation: On Republic Day the Governor unfurls the national flag in the state capital; on Independence Day the Chief Minister hoists it.

questions.text: Which marine carotenoid is abundant in brown seaweed, macroalgae and diatoms?
questions.explanation: Fucoxanthin is the carotenoid that gives brown seaweeds and diatoms their colour.

questions.text: Harrod Domar model was the main idea behind the __________ Five Year Plan.
questions.explanation: The First Five Year Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar growth model; the Second followed the Mahalanobis model.

questions.text: Which of the following are west flowing rivers?
questions.explanation: The Mahi and the Sabarmati flow west into the Arabian Sea. The Godavari, Mahanadi, Krishna and Kaveri flow east into the Bay of Bengal, as does the Ganga, which the Yamuna joins.

questions.text: The Upper House of a State Legislature is known as the ____________.
questions.explanation: The Vidhan Parishad (Legislative Council) is the upper house of a state legislature; the Vidhan Sabha (Legislative Assembly) is the lower house.

questions.text: When was the Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana introduced to provide health insurance to people below the poverty line?
questions.explanation: The Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana, health insurance for families below the poverty line, began in 2008.

questions.text: Part IV A of the Indian Constitution was inserted in the Indian Constitution through _____________ Constitutional Amendment Act.
questions.explanation: Part IVA, the Fundamental Duties (Article 51A), was added by the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976.

questions.text: Which of the following states was the overall champion in both men and women categories in the first Janjatiya Khel Mahotsav?
questions.explanation: Odisha, the host state, was overall champion in both the men's and women's categories at the first Janjatiya Khel Mahotsav, held at KIIT, Bhubaneswar, in June 2023.

questions.text: Money supply is a _____ concept.
questions.explanation: Money supply is the stock of money held by the public at a point in time, so it is a stock concept; income, by contrast, is a flow over a period.

questions.text: The Parliament passed the Essential Defence Services Bill, 2021 in August 2021. Which of the following is an objective behind passing it?
options: To prohibit strikes, lockouts and layoffs in units engaged in essential defence services
To appoint more women in defence services
To encourage more FDI in defence services
To implement one rank one pension
questions.explanation: The Essential Defence Services Act, 2021 lets the government prohibit strikes, lockouts and lay-offs in units engaged in essential defence services.

questions.text: In the context of periodicity, a unit called picometre is used to measure the __________.
questions.explanation: Atomic radii are tiny and are measured in picometres (1 pm = 10⁻¹² m).

questions.text: Who among the following was the Former Secretary (HRD), Information and Broadcasting (I&B) and has been appointed as the advisor to the Prime Minister of India in October 2021?
questions.explanation: Amit Khare, formerly Secretary of Higher Education (HRD) and of Information and Broadcasting, was appointed Advisor to the Prime Minister in October 2021.

questions.text: Who among the following is/was a famous sitarist?
questions.explanation: Pandit Ravi Shankar was a famous sitarist. Bhimsen Joshi was a vocalist, Zakir Hussain a tabla player and Bismillah Khan a shehnai player.

questions.text: Three Poets Pampa, Ponna and Ranna are called as the ‘Three Jewels’ of:
questions.explanation: Pampa, Ponna and Ranna, poets of the 10th century, are called the 'Ratnatraya' (three jewels) of Kannada literature.

questions.text: Who was the first Indian woman wrestler to represent the country at the 2012 London Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: Geeta Phogat became the first Indian woman wrestler to compete at the Olympics, at London 2012.

questions.text: Indian classical violinist Annavarapu Rama Swamy was awarded with the _____________ in 2021.
questions.explanation: Annavarapu Rama Swamy, a Carnatic violinist from Andhra Pradesh, received the Padma Shri in 2021.

questions.text: A circular arc whose radius is 24 cm makes an angle of 60° at the centre. The perimeter of the sector formed is: (Use π = 3.14)
If three cubes of volume 512 cm³ each are joined end to end, find the surface area of the resulting cuboid.
questions.explanation: Each cube has side ∛512 = 8 cm, so the cuboid is 24 × 8 × 8 cm. Surface area = 2(24 × 8 + 8 × 8 + 24 × 8) = 2 × 448 = 896 cm².

questions.text: A shopkeeper offers the following discount schemes for buyers. I. Two successive discounts of 15% and 20% II. Successive discount of 25 % and 10% III. A discount of 33% The selling price will be minimum under the scheme:
questions.explanation: Scheme I leaves 0.85 × 0.8 = 0.68 of the price (32% off) and II 0.75 × 0.9 = 0.675 (32.5% off). III's 33% is the largest discount, so it gives the lowest selling price.

questions.text: At what angle θ, the value of sin (θ) and cos (θ) will have the same value?
questions.explanation: sin θ = cos θ when tan θ = 1, that is at θ = 45°, where both equal 1/√2.

questions.text: A number r when divided by 8 leaves remainder 3. What will be the remainder when (r²+6r+7) is divided by 8?
questions.explanation: Any r = 8k + 3 gives the same remainder, so take r = 3: 9 + 18 + 7 = 34, which leaves remainder 2 on division by 8.

questions.text: If ∆ABC and ∆QPR are congruent triangles such that AB = 7 cm, AC = 8 cm, ∠B = 65° and ∠C = 75°, then which of the following is true?
questions.explanation: ΔABC ≅ ΔQPR matches A with Q, B with P and C with R. So PQ = AB = 7 cm and ∠R = ∠C = 75°.

questions.text: The sum of five consecutive numbers is 80. Find the largest number.
questions.explanation: The middle number is 80 ÷ 5 = 16, so the numbers are 14 to 18 and the largest is 18.

questions.text: A certain sum of money is given at a certain rate of simple interest for 6 years. Had it been given at 7% higher rate, it would have fetched ₹1,512 more. Find the sum (in ₹).
If the system of the following equations has the value of the variables as three consecutive integers, then the value of a is ____. x - y + z = 2a x + 4y - 2z = 3(4 - a) 2x - 3y + 4z = 6 - 2a
questions.explanation: Solving in terms of a gives x = 3a, y = 6 − 4a and z = 6 − 5a. Only a = 1 makes them consecutive integers: 3, 2 and 1 (check: 3 − 2 + 1 = 2 = 2a).

questions.text: In a constituency, 45% of the total number of voters are males and the rest are females. If 60% of the males are illiterate and 60% of the females are literate, then by what per cent is the number of illiterate females more than that of literate males? (Rounded off to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanation: Of 100 voters, 45 are male and 55 female. Literate males = 40% of 45 = 18; illiterate females = 40% of 55 = 22. 22 is more than 18 by 4/18 = 22.22%.

questions.text: A motorboat travelling at some speed can cover 24 km upstream and 40 km downstream in 17 hours. At the same speed it can travel 32 km downstream and 12 km upstream in 10 hours. The speed of the stream is:
questions.explanation: With upstream speed u and downstream d: 24/u + 40/d = 17 and 12/u + 32/d = 10. Doubling the second and subtracting the first: 24/d = 3, so d = 8 and then u = 2. Stream = (8 − 2)/2 = 3 km/h.

questions.text: The perimeter of a rectangular garden is 48 m. If the length is 6 m more than the breadth, the area (in m²) of the garden is:
questions.explanation: l + b = 24 and l − b = 6, so l = 15 m and b = 9 m. Area = 15 × 9 = 135 m².

questions.text: Find the mean proportional of 36 and 100.
questions.explanation: Mean proportional = √(36 × 100) = 6 × 10 = 60.

questions.text: A chord of length 32 cm is drawn at a distance of 12 cm from the centre of a circle. Find the radius of the circle.
questions.explanation: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord: r = √(16² + 12²) = √400 = 20 cm.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. The appearance of most of the animals in jungle is “deceptive” in nature.
questions.explanation: 'Deceptive' means misleading; its opposite is 'honest'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank. He ________ his bike as fast as he could to reach home.
questions.explanation: 'Rode' is the past tense of 'ride'; 'road' and 'rowed' sound the same but mean something else.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who eats the flesh of his own species
questions.explanation: A cannibal eats the flesh of its own kind.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Forsake
questions.explanation: To 'forsake' is to 'abandon'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the idiom in the given brackets. His PhD degree seems to be (Penelope’s web).
questions.explanation: Penelope unpicked by night what she wove by day, so 'Penelope's web' is a task that never ends.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. The long-standing “feud” between the two villages was settled due to the intervention of the two chiefs.
questions.explanation: A 'feud' is a long, bitter quarrel; its opposite is 'harmony'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill the blank in the given situation. I thought Sadhna would always stick by me, but when I got into trouble, she turned out to be a/an ___________.
questions.explanation: A fair-weather friend stands by you only in good times and leaves when trouble comes.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. An “intense” wish to learn something keeps the nerves active.
questions.explanation: An 'intense' wish is a strong, 'powerful' one.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Autonomy
questions.explanation: 'Autonomy' is self-government or independence; its opposite is 'dependence'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'mischievous'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. “Humour that describes the weaknesses of the other person” is itself a crime among peer groups.
questions.explanation: Satire is humour that exposes people's weaknesses or follies.

questions.text: Select the sentence in which the ‘-ing’ form of verb expresses the continuity of an action/event.
options: I am fond of reading science fiction.
The optician advised me to use reading glasses.
Reading novels is my favourite pastime.
Please do not disturb me. I am preparing for exams.
questions.explanation: In 'I am preparing' the -ing form makes the present continuous, an action in progress. In the others it is a gerund ('reading' as a noun) or part of a compound noun ('reading glasses').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Exceptional
questions.explanation: 'Exceptional' means unusually good: 'outstanding'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank. Helium is used with oxygen for asthma treatment because it ____________ very easily.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'diffuses'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Sivamani “is working” as an electrician for the past 22 years.
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and is still going on takes the present perfect continuous: 'has been working for the past 22 years', with 'has' for the singular subject.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Dipesh will send Rakesh away to college for certain reasons.
options: Rakesh would have been sent away to college for certain reasons by Dipesh.
Rakesh will be sent away to college for certain reasons by Dipesh.
Rakesh will have to be sent away to college for certain reasons by Dipesh.
Rakesh would be sent away to college for certain reasons by Dipesh.
questions.explanation: The future active 'will send' becomes 'will be sent', with the agent kept: 'Rakesh will be sent away to college for certain reasons by Dipesh.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined segment. My father always tells “amusing and true stories” from his childhood at bedtime.
questions.explanation: Anecdotes are short, amusing stories about real incidents or people.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined word segment in the given sentence. Her thinning grey hair was “hanging on” her bony forehead.
questions.explanation: Hair that 'straggles' hangs in thin, untidy strands: 'straggling over her bony forehead'.

questions.text: Select the option that spots the error in the use of preposition in the given sentence. Deepa and Seema are both good with running, but Deepa is also good at catching the ball and throwing it to the right corner in time.
questions.explanation: One is good 'at' an activity: 'good at running', as the sentence itself says 'good at catching the ball'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Why are you repeatedly called by her?
options: Why had she called you repeatedly?
Why was she calling you repeatedly?
Why does she call you repeatedly?
questions.explanation: The present simple passive 'are you called' comes from the present simple active, and the question takes 'does': 'Why does she call you repeatedly?'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The limbs of the flying squirrel are interlinked with a membrane. When the creature (1)________ into the air, the membrane opens and the squirrel seems to (2)_______ swiftly downwards. This movement gives the (3)_______ of flight. However, it is not flying really. It is a (4)_______ in the air from a higher level. It is also noteworthy that a squirrel cannot (5)_____ its direction while it is in flying mode.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: When the creature 'leaps' into the air: jumps, with the singular verb the subject needs ('spring' would have to be 'springs').

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The limbs of the flying squirrel are interlinked with a membrane. When the creature (1)________ into the air, the membrane opens and the squirrel seems to (2)_______ swiftly downwards. This movement gives the (3)_______ of flight. However, it is not flying really. It is a (4)_______ in the air from a higher level. It is also noteworthy that a squirrel cannot (5)_____ its direction while it is in flying mode.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The squirrel seems to 'glide' downwards: to move smoothly through the air.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The limbs of the flying squirrel are interlinked with a membrane. When the creature (1)________ into the air, the membrane opens and the squirrel seems to (2)_______ swiftly downwards. This movement gives the (3)_______ of flight. However, it is not flying really. It is a (4)_______ in the air from a higher level. It is also noteworthy that a squirrel cannot (5)_____ its direction while it is in flying mode.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The movement gives the 'impression', or appearance, of flight.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The limbs of the flying squirrel are interlinked with a membrane. When the creature (1)________ into the air, the membrane opens and the squirrel seems to (2)_______ swiftly downwards. This movement gives the (3)_______ of flight. However, it is not flying really. It is a (4)_______ in the air from a higher level. It is also noteworthy that a squirrel cannot (5)_____ its direction while it is in flying mode.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: It is not flight but 'a motion', a movement, through the air from a higher level. 'Progress' takes no 'a', and 'wave' and 'sign' do not fit.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The limbs of the flying squirrel are interlinked with a membrane. When the creature (1)________ into the air, the membrane opens and the squirrel seems to (2)_______ swiftly downwards. This movement gives the (3)_______ of flight. However, it is not flying really. It is a (4)_______ in the air from a higher level. It is also noteworthy that a squirrel cannot (5)_____ its direction while it is in flying mode.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: To 'swap' something is to change it for another: the squirrel cannot change its direction in mid-glide. 'Adept' is an adjective, and 'adopt' and 'replace' do not fit with 'its direction'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is A related to D if ‘A × B ÷ C + D’?
questions.explanation: A is the wife of B, B is the father of C and C is the mother of D. So A is C's mother, and C is D's mother: A is D's mother's mother.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 272 × 16 + 97 − 23 ÷ 4 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 272 ÷ 16 − 97 + 23 × 4 = 17 − 97 + 92 = 12.

questions.text: Select the number that will come in the place of the question mark (?), if ‘+’ and ‘ – ‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged 121 × 11 – 28 ÷ 3 + 17 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 121 ÷ 11 + 28 × 3 − 17 = 11 + 84 − 17 = 78.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. (7, 333) (5, 115) (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is the cube of the first minus 10: 7³ − 10 = 333 and 5³ − 10 = 115. Likewise 4³ − 10 = 54.

questions.text: Each of the letters in the word ‘SLANTED’ is arranged in the English alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English alphabetical series between the letter which is fourth from the left end and the one which is second from the right end in the new letter-cluster thus formed?
questions.explanation: SLANTED in alphabetical order is A D E L N S T. The fourth from the left is L and the second from the right is S; between them come M, N, O, P, Q and R: six letters.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘HIT’ is coded as ‘132’ and ‘SBYZ’ is coded as ‘144’. How will ‘YRF’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter takes its position counted from Z (A = 26 … Z = 1), and the sum is multiplied by the number of letters: HIT = (19 + 18 + 7) × 3 = 132 and SBYZ = (8 + 25 + 2 + 1) × 4 = 144. So YRF = (2 + 9 + 21) × 3 = 96.

questions.text: Two sets of numbers are given below. In each set of numbers, certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number result(s) in the second number. Similarly, certain mathematical operation(s) on the second number result(s) in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in the given sets? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 7 – 14 – 28 – 38; 4 – 8 – 16 – 26

Select the set in which the numbers are related to each other in the same way as are the numbers of the given sets. (28, 224); (47, 376) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The second number is 8 times the first: 28 × 8 = 224 and 47 × 8 = 376. Likewise 31 × 8 = 248.

questions.text: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that DOES NOT belong to that group? (Note: The odd man out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
questions.explanation: HGF, VUT and KJI are three consecutive letters in reverse order (−1, −1). AAY moves 0, then −2, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different. Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.
questions.explanation: In YWT, XVS and ZXU the letters move −2, then −3. WUQ moves −2, then −4, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 20, 25, 25, 35, 30, 45, ?, 55, 40
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 20, 25, 30, 35, 40 (+5) and 25, 35, 45, 55 (+10). The missing term is 35.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘play in the sunshine’ is coded as ‘sh ko zm fq’ and ‘the sunshine is bright’ is coded as ‘ko sh gp rs’. What is code for ‘sunshine’ in that language?
questions.explanation: 'The' and 'sunshine' are the words in both sentences, and 'sh' and 'ko' the codes in both, so 'sunshine' is either 'sh' or 'ko'.

questions.text: Three of the following numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the odd one out. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 11 – 363, 13 – 507 and 9 – 243 the second number is 3 times the square of the first (3 × 121, 3 × 169, 3 × 81). 15 – 450 is 2 × 225, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. CARBON : ACIYNO :: DAMAGE : ADNZEG :: MARGIN : ?
questions.explanation: The first two letters swap, the middle two are replaced by their opposites (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y, …) and the last two swap: CARBON → AC IY NO. So MARGIN → AM IT NI: AMITNI.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? MJPT, PGMW, SDJZ, ? , YXDF
questions.explanation: First letters move +3 (M, P, S, V, Y), second letters −3 (J, G, D, A, X), third letters −3 (P, M, J, G, D) and fourth letters +3 (T, W, Z, C, F): VAGC.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that when placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the given letter series. L M N _ O L L M _ Q O L L _ N Q O _ L M N Q _ L L M
questions.explanation: With Q, N, M, L, O in the blanks the block LMNQOL repeats: LMNQOL LMNQOL LMNQOL LMNQOL LM.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘TRIED’ is coded as ‘54123' and ‘TREAD’ is coded as ‘12365’. What is the code for ‘I’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: T, R, E and D are in both words, as are 1, 2, 3 and 5 in both codes. The letter left in TRIED is I and the digit left in its code is 4, so I = 4.

questions.text: How was the growth in all food grains after the Green Revolution?
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution's gains were uneven: wheat output, and later rice, rose sharply while pulses and coarse cereals lagged, so food grains did not all grow alike.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: India has single citizenship: there is no separate citizenship of the states. An independent judiciary, universal adult franchise and a blend of rigidity and flexibility are all features of the Constitution.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of major industrial region of India?
questions.explanation: NCERT lists the Chotanagpur region among India's eight major industrial regions; Bhojpur-Munger, Bilaspur-Korba and Jaipur-Ajmer are minor industrial regions.

questions.text: What correctly defines change of inventories of a firm during a year?
options: Sale of the firm during the year – Production of the firm during the year
Production of the firm during the previous year – Sale of the firm during the year
Production of the firm during the year – Sale of the firm during the year
Production of the firm during the year – Sale of the firm during the previous year
questions.explanation: Goods produced but not sold in the year add to the firm's stock, so the change of inventories is the year's production minus the year's sales.

questions.text: Chariot festival is dedicated to Lord Jagannath along with Subhadra and _________ .
questions.explanation: In the Rath Yatra at Puri, Lord Jagannath is drawn in his chariot along with his brother Balabhadra and sister Subhadra.

questions.text: ‘Padayani’, a local dance form primarily performed in ________ to please Goddess Bhadrakali.
questions.explanation: Padayani is a ritual dance of central Kerala, performed in Bhadrakali temples.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers is an east flowing river?
questions.explanation: The Godavari flows east into the Bay of Bengal. The Narmada, Mahi and Tapi flow west into the Arabian Sea.

questions.text: Filtration of waste products in humans happens in the kidneys. There is a large number of filtration units present inside the kidneys to help them in doing this job. These filtration units are called:
questions.explanation: Each kidney has a large number of filtration units called nephrons. Bowman's capsule is only one part of a nephron.

questions.text: Which number is called Avogadro's constant, named after the 19th century scientist Amedeo Avogadro?
questions.explanation: Avogadro's constant, the number of particles in one mole, is 6.022 × 10²³.

questions.text: The Epidemic Diseases (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020 amended which of the following Acts?
questions.explanation: The Epidemic Diseases (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020 amended the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897, notably to protect health workers from violence during epidemics.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which Indian political leader was called as Lok Nayak?
questions.explanation: Jayaprakash Narayan, the socialist leader of the 1974 'Total Revolution' movement, was called Lok Nayak.

questions.text: Under the ‘Mero Rukh Mero Santati’ initiative launched by the Sikkim Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang in 2023, how many trees will be planted for every child born in Sikkim ?
questions.explanation: Launching 'Mero Rukh Mero Santati' in February 2023, the Sikkim government announced that 100 trees would be planted for every child born in the state.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the political parties in India?
options: All parties are registered with the Supreme Court of India.
A political party symbol is assigned by the President of India.
India has a multi-party system classified as national, state or regional level.
Status of party is accorded by the Parliament.
questions.explanation: India has a multi-party system, with parties recognised as national or state parties. Parties are registered with, and symbols allotted by, the Election Commission, not the Supreme Court, the President or Parliament.

questions.text: Which of the following kingdoms was divided into subdivisions called Aharas or Rashtras that meant districts?
questions.explanation: The Satavahana kingdom was divided into districts called aharas, each under an official called an amatya.

questions.text: Raja Bhalindra Singh trophy is associated with which of the following national sports events?
questions.explanation: The Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy is awarded to the best-performing team at the National Games.

questions.text: The renowned ghazal singer Girija Devi was born in ________.
questions.explanation: Girija Devi, the Banaras gharana singer best known for thumri, was born in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, in 1929.

questions.text: Which Indian musician from Maharashtra received the Padma Vibhushan 2023?
questions.explanation: Tabla maestro Zakir Hussain, listed from Maharashtra, received the Padma Vibhushan in 2023.

questions.text: Which of the following is a landlocked Salt Lake in South-West Asia between Israel and Jordan?
questions.explanation: The Dead Sea, a landlocked salt lake, lies between Israel and Jordan.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Daroga system in 1792 was introduced by whom among the following Governor- Generals in India?
questions.explanation: Lord Cornwallis divided districts into thanas, each under a police officer called a daroga.

questions.text: Three Indians were featured in Time Magazine’s list of ‘100 most influential people of 2021’. Whose name was NOT included in the list?
questions.explanation: The three Indians in Time's 2021 list were Narendra Modi, Mamata Banerjee and Adar Poonawalla; Amitabh Bachchan was not on it.

questions.text: ______, authored by Tolkappiyar is the earliest Tamil literature.
questions.explanation: Tolkappiyam, a work on grammar and poetics by Tolkappiyar, is the earliest surviving Tamil text. Narrinai and Kalittogai are among the Ettutogai (eight anthologies) of Sangam poetry.

questions.text: Sports Authority of India comes under which ministry?
options: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
questions.explanation: The Sports Authority of India is under the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are true based on the 4NH₃(g)+5O₂(g)→4NO(g)+6H₂O(g)? (a) N gets oxidized. (b) O gets oxidized. (c) N gets reduced. (d) O gets reduced.
questions.explanation: Nitrogen goes from −3 in NH₃ to +2 in NO, so it is oxidised; oxygen goes from 0 in O₂ to −2 in NO and H₂O, so it is reduced.

questions.text: The Drought Prone Area Programme (DPAP) for providing employment to people in drought prone areas was started by the Government of India during the _______.
questions.explanation: NCERT records that the Drought Prone Area Programme was started during the Fourth Five-Year Plan, to provide employment in drought-prone areas and create productive assets.

questions.text: Which branch of ecology deals with the characteristics of ancient environment and their relationship with ancient plants and animals?
questions.explanation: Paleoecology studies ancient environments and their relationship with ancient plants and animals. Mycology is the study of fungi and ichthyology that of fish.

questions.text: After offering two successive discounts a toy with a marked price of ₹150 is sold at ₹105. If the value of the first discount is 12.5%, what is the value of the second discount?
questions.explanation: After 12.5% off, ₹150 becomes ₹131.25. ₹105/₹131.25 = 0.8, so the second discount is 20%.

questions.text: In a ∆PQR, PQ = PR and PT is perpendicular to QR. If PQ = 17 cm, PT = 15 cm, then what is the measure (in cm) of QR?
questions.explanation: In an isosceles triangle the perpendicular from the apex bisects the base. QT = √(17² − 15²) = √64 = 8 cm, so QR = 16 cm.

questions.text: If arcs PAQ and RBS of a circle are congruent, then find the ratio of PQ and RS.
questions.explanation: In the same circle congruent arcs have equal chords, so PQ : RS = 1 : 1.

questions.text: In a circular race of 4800m, A and B start from the same point and at the same time with speeds of 36 km/h and 54 km/h. When will they meet again for the first time on the track if they are running in the opposite direction?
questions.explanation: Running in opposite directions they close the gap at 36 + 54 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s, so they first meet after 4,800/25 = 192 seconds.

questions.text: Pipes A and B can fill a tank in 6 hours and 8 hours, respectively. Both pipes are opened together for 3 hours. After that pipe A is closed, and B continues to fill the tank. In how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.explanation: In 3 hours A and B fill 3 × (1/6 + 1/8) = 7/8 of the tank. B fills the remaining 1/8 in 1 hour, so the tank is full 4 hours after the start.

questions.text: Find the remainder, if 19²⁰⁰ is divided by 20.
questions.explanation: 19 = 20 − 1, so 19²⁰⁰ leaves remainder (−1)²⁰⁰ = 1 on division by 20.

questions.text: In an election between two candidates, the one who gets 88% of the votes is elected by a majority of 684 votes. What is the total number of votes polled? (all polled votes are valid)
questions.explanation: The winner has 88% and the loser 12%, so the majority is 76% of the votes: 684/0.76 = 900.

questions.text: The average weight of 10 students is increased by half a kg when one of the students weighing 51 kg is replaced by a new student. Find the weight of the new student.
questions.explanation: The total rises by 10 × ½ = 5 kg, so the new student weighs 51 + 5 = 56 kg.

questions.text: A total of ₹2,00,000 is divided into two parts for investing in different banks on simple interest. One yields 4% p.a. while the other yields 6% p.a. If the total interest at the end of one year is equivalent to 4.7% p.a. on the whole amount, the amount (in ₹) invested in each bank is ________, respectively.
The present ages (in years) of A and B are in the ratio of 3 : 4. Five years back, the ratio of their ages was 2 : 3. What is the present age (in years) of A?
questions.explanation: Let the ages be 3x and 4x. (3x − 5)/(4x − 5) = 2/3 gives 9x − 15 = 8x − 10, so x = 5 and A is 15.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given group of words. On cloud nine
questions.explanation: To be 'on cloud nine' is to be extremely happy.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. A. So I am not very sure B. I have a driving license C. Of myself reaching home safely D. But no real driving experience
questions.explanation: 'I have a driving license (B) but no real driving experience (D), so I am not very sure (A) of myself reaching home safely (C).'

questions.text: Select the option that can substitute/replace the bracketed word correctly and complete the sentence. He (seek) for the wallet in his pocket.
questions.explanation: The sentence narrates a past action, so the simple past 'sought': 'He sought for the wallet in his pocket.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given group of words. A bitter pill
questions.explanation: 'A bitter pill' (to swallow) is an unpleasant situation or fact that one has to accept.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence. (P) dreams provide an escape (Q) where reality is suspended (R) into a world (O) of endless possibilities
questions.explanation: 'Dreams provide an escape (P) into a world (R) of endless possibilities (O) where reality is suspended (Q).'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Can you compose an inspiring poem?
options: Can an inspiring poem by you composed?
Can an inspiring poem be composed?
An inspiring poem can be composed by you.
Can an inspiring poem be composed by you?
questions.explanation: 'Can you compose' becomes 'can … be composed by you', and the question stays a question: 'Can an inspiring poem be composed by you?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Rohan exercised and ate a lot, “lest he should not be weak” .
options: lest he would not be weak.
questions.explanation: 'Lest' already means 'for fear that', so it is not followed by 'not': 'lest he should be weak'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank. Calder Hall is a nuclear power station in England which is known as the first nuclear power station to generate electricity for ___________ purposes.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'commercial'.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling to fill in the blank. When numerous ideas are presented in a historical context, more than mere ______ can be seen.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'parallelism'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. People admired him, for / he lived by the same principals / that he preached.
options: he lived by the same principals
questions.explanation: A rule of conduct is a 'principle'; a 'principal' is the head of a school. He lived by the same 'principles'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The tutor was not teaching the student.
options: The student was not taught by the tutor.
The student was teaching the tutor.
The student was not being teaching by the tutor.
The student was not being taught by the tutor.
questions.explanation: The past continuous 'was not teaching' becomes 'was not being taught': 'The student was not being taught by the tutor.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word in the given sentence. Despite his “annoyance”, Rahul knew that rushing the delicate process would only lead to mistakes.
questions.explanation: 'Annoyance' is irritation; its opposite is 'serenity', calm.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Tendency
questions.explanation: A 'tendency' to something is a 'proneness' to it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. Bankrupts are those who are “incapable” to pay their debts.
questions.explanation: 'Incapable' takes 'of' ('incapable of paying'), but 'incompetent' can take 'to': bankrupts are 'incompetent to pay their debts', unable to pay them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Condone
questions.explanation: To 'condone' an offence is to overlook or 'pardon' it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given word. Pugnacious
questions.explanation: 'Pugnacious' means quarrelsome, eager to fight. Of the options, 'waspish' (irritable and sharp-tongued) is closest; 'good-tempered' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Kilter
questions.explanation: 'Kilter' means good working condition or 'order', as in 'out of kilter'. The other three mean disorder.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that means the same as the underlined group of words to fill in the blank. Most of the rivers dry up during the summer season, but the Ganga is full of water “round the year” because it is __________.
questions.explanation: A 'perennial' river flows all year round. 'Biennial' is every two years, 'annual' once a year and 'biannual' twice a year.

questions.text: The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. We were on the way/ to the party;/ suddenly, there/ will a heavy downpour.
questions.explanation: The sentence is in the past and the clause needs a verb: 'there was a heavy downpour', not 'there will a heavy downpour'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Dogmatic
questions.explanation: 'Dogmatic' means insisting that one's own beliefs are right; its opposite is 'liberal', open to other views.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. This Diwali is more significant because we are going to celebrate it after three years, without the evil shadow of Covid-19 that (1)________ looming over all festivities. The lockdowns and endless bad news of death and (2)________ had turned our country into a zone of gloom. But, this season of Diwali (3)________ all the sorrows of people by lighting the candle of hope in their lives. We can see the lights, the candles, the lanterns, and the busy people coming out of their houses and purchasing toys for their children. Let’s (4)________ those people who have made such a huge contribution to (5)________ good thoughts and saving people's lives.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The singular, past 'evil shadow of Covid-19 that was looming over all festivities'.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The 'bad news of death and disease' of the pandemic years.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.
