Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Their contribution to 'spreading good thoughts' and saving lives.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A – B’ means ‘ A is the father of B’; ‘A $ B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’ and ‘A % B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’. Based on the above, how is P related to S if P + Q − R $ S % T?
questions.explanation: Q is R's father and R is S's daughter, so S (T's sister, hence female) is R's mother and Q's wife. P is Q's mother, so P is S's husband's mother.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘MORE’ is coded as ‘14 - 12 - 9 - 22’ and ‘KNOW’ is coded as ‘16 - 13 - 12 - 4’. How will ‘SAID’ be coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is coded by its place counted from Z (27 minus its place from A): M = 14, O = 12, R = 9, E = 22. So S = 8, A = 26, I = 18 and D = 23.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (21, 504, 8) (15, 270, 6)
questions.explanation: The middle number is three times the product of the other two: 21 × 8 × 3 = 504 and 15 × 6 × 3 = 270. Likewise 16 × 7 × 3 = 336.

questions.text: Select the word pair that best represents a similar relationship to the one expressed in the pair of words given below. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Control : Domination
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Manipulation : Deceive: domination is control exercised over others, and manipulation is a way of deceiving them, so both pairs are about power over people. 'Descend : Fall' is also a pair of near-synonyms, so the key's choice is arguable; the other two pairs are opposites.

questions.text: Three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the letter-cluster that does NOT belong to that group? (Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their positions in the letter-cluster.)
questions.explanation: MPR, CFH and EHJ move +3, then +2. IKN moves +2, then +3, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if each of the letter in the word ‘HUSBAND’ is arranged in English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: HUSBAND in alphabetical order is A B D H N S U. Place by place (H/A, U/B, S/D, B/H, A/N, N/S, D/U) no letter keeps its position.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 10 : 110 :: 7 : 56 :: 9 : ? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is the first times the next number: 10 × 11 = 110 and 7 × 8 = 56. Likewise 9 × 10 = 90.

questions.text: Which two numbers (not digits) should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 19 + 125 ÷ 25 – 100 ÷ 5 + 4 × 3 = 52
Select the option that represents the letters that when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the letter series. _ _ C _ D C _ _ C C _ _
questions.explanation: With C, D, C, C, D, D, C in the blanks the block CDC repeats: CDC CDC CDC CDC.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BIRD’ is written as ‘DKTF’ and ‘KITE’ is written as ‘MKVG’. How will ‘EAGLE’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: BIRD → DKTF and KITE → MKVG. So EAGLE → GCING.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusion(s) logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: No medicine is a capsule. Some capsules are tablets. Some tablets are laptops. Conclusions: I. Some capsules are laptops. II. All tablets can never be medicines.
options: Neither Conclusion I nor II follow.
Both Conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: Some capsules are tablets and no capsule is a medicine, so those tablets are not medicines: all tablets can never be medicines (II). The capsules that are tablets need not be among the tablets that are laptops, so I does not follow.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which conclusion/s logically follow/s from the given statements. Statements: All beaches are sand. Some deserts are sand. All mountains are rocky. Conclusions: (I) At least some beaches are desert. (II) At least some sands are rocky.
questions.explanation: All beaches are sand but only some deserts are, so beaches and deserts need not meet (I fails). Nothing links sand to the mountains or to anything rocky (II fails).

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 3, 6, 9, 18, 21, ?
questions.explanation: The terms alternately double and add 3: 3 × 2 = 6, 6 + 3 = 9, 9 × 2 = 18, 18 + 3 = 21, 21 × 2 = 42.

questions.text: 40 is related to 53 following certain logic. Following the same logic, 8 is related to 13. To which of the following numbers is 68 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each pair is n² + 4 and (n + 1)² + 4: 40 = 6² + 4 and 53 = 7² + 4; 8 = 2² + 4 and 13 = 3² + 4. So 68 = 8² + 4 goes with 9² + 4 = 85.

questions.text: Three of the following numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the odd one out. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 3 – 72, 4 – 128 and 7 – 392 the second number is eight times the square of the first (8 × 9, 8 × 16, 8 × 49). 8 × 11² = 968, not 882, so 11 – 882 is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the option that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. NW17, PY19, RA21, TC23, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move +2 (N, P, R, T, V), the second letters +2, wrapping round after Z (W, Y, A, C, E), and the numbers +2 (17 to 25): VE25.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will logically complete the series. QUA_TO_ANT_UAN_KU_NT
questions.explanation: With N, U, M, T, A in the blanks the series reads QUANT OUANT MUANT KUANT: the first letter moves back 2 each time and UANT repeats.

questions.text: Select the number that will come in the place of the question mark(?), if ‘+’ and ‘ – ‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged 93 – 7 ÷ 65 × 13 + 34 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 93 + 7 × 65 ÷ 13 − 34 = 93 + 35 − 34 = 94.

questions.text: Identify a monoatomic molecule.
questions.explanation: Noble gases such as helium exist as single atoms. Carbon monoxide (CO), chlorine (Cl₂) and oxygen (O₂) molecules each have two atoms.

questions.text: Who among the following is the first vocalist to receive the Bharat Ratna in 2008 and is also credited to have popularised 'Khyal Gayaki'?
questions.explanation: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, the Kirana gharana khyal singer, was named for the Bharat Ratna in 2008. None of the other three received it.

questions.text: Which of the following institutions has contributed mainly in improving the economic status of the poor women in rural areas?
questions.explanation: Self-help groups of rural women pool their savings and borrow from banks, funding small enterprises that raise their income.

questions.text: The Pandya Kingdom was first mentioned by Megasthenes, who said that their kingdom was famous for pearls. Their capital was:
questions.explanation: Madurai was the capital of the Pandyas. Uraiyur and Kaveripattinam were Chola centres, and Thanjavur the later Chola capital.

questions.text: With which of the following dances is Yamini Krishnamurthy associated?
questions.explanation: Yamini Krishnamurthy is best known as a Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancer.

questions.text: Easter festival is celebrated by which community?
questions.explanation: Easter, which marks the resurrection of Jesus, is a Christian festival.

questions.text: Who among the following is NOT a member of the National Human Rights Commission?
options: Former Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
Former Judge of the Supreme Court
Former Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.explanation: The NHRC is chaired by a former Chief Justice of India or Supreme Court judge, and its members include a former Supreme Court judge and a former High Court Chief Justice or judge. A District Magistrate has no place in it.

questions.text: Which state of India has the maximum number of large dams?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra has by far the most large dams of any state, according to the Central Water Commission's National Register of Large Dams.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT related to reticulate venation?
questions.explanation: Maize is a monocot, with parallel venation. Tulsi, coriander and China rose are dicots, whose leaves have net-like (reticulate) venation.

questions.text: In which of the following Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka is the Kalinga war mentioned?
questions.explanation: Major Rock Edict XIII records the Kalinga war and Ashoka's remorse over its slaughter.

questions.text: Consider the following statements and identify the INCORRECT statement(s). 1. The ‘Saksham Anganwadi and Poshan 2.0’ scheme has been implemented under the National Food Security Act, 2003. 2. It is an ongoing, Central Government-sponsored scheme under the Ministry of Women and Child Development. 3. It is extended to children aged below 6 years only. 4. Six services are provided under this scheme through the National Health Mission and Public Health Infrastructure.
questions.explanation: The National Food Security Act is of 2013, not 2003 (1); the scheme also covers pregnant women and lactating mothers, not only children under 6 (3); and only three of its six services (immunisation, health check-ups and referrals) are delivered through the National Health Mission and public health infrastructure (4). Statement 2 is correct: it is a centrally sponsored scheme of the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

questions.text: ‘Bhagirathi’ and ‘Alaknanda’ rivers confluence at:
questions.explanation: The Bhagirathi and the Alaknanda meet at Devaprayag to form the Ganga.

questions.text: Which of the following chemical reactions takes place when quick lime reacts with water?
questions.explanation: Quicklime (calcium oxide) reacts with water to form slaked lime, calcium hydroxide, giving out much heat: CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂.

questions.text: As of 14 October 2021, which Indian footballer was in the news for breaking Pele's 77 international goals?
questions.explanation: Sunil Chhetri passed Pele's 77 international goals at the SAFF Championship in October 2021.

questions.text: In which five-year plan was the 'food, work, and productivity' slogan used?
questions.explanation: 'Food, work and productivity' was the watchword of the Seventh Plan (1985-90).

questions.text: Identify a spiral-shaped bacteria.
questions.explanation: Spirillum bacteria are spiral; bacilli are rods, cocci spheres and vibrios comma-shaped.

questions.text: Ranjana Prakash Desai who became the first woman chairperson of the Press Council of India originally worked in which of the following organs of the government?
questions.explanation: Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai is a retired judge of the Supreme Court; she became the Press Council's first woman chairperson in 2022.

questions.text: In which year did the Central Government launch the National Air Sports Policy?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Civil Aviation released the National Air Sports Policy in 2022.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following Acts introduced ‘provincial autonomy’ by discontinuing the application of dyarchy?
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act, 1935 ended dyarchy in the provinces and gave them autonomy (and proposed dyarchy at the Centre instead).

questions.text: According to Census 2011, which district displays the highest population?
questions.explanation: Thane, in Maharashtra, was India's most populous district in Census 2011, with about 1.1 crore people.

questions.text: Which committee recommended Constitutional recognition for the local government bodies in 1989?
questions.explanation: The P.K. Thungon Committee recommended in 1989 that local government bodies be recognised in the Constitution.

questions.text: The third edition of the Khelo India University Games was hosted by which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh hosted the third Khelo India University Games in 2023.

questions.text: Harivarasanam award is given in the field of music by which of the following state governments?
questions.explanation: The Harivarasanam award, named after the hymn sung at Sabarimala before the temple closes each night, is given to musicians by the Kerala government.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following Sikh reform movements was started in 1873 in Amritsar?
questions.explanation: The Singh Sabha movement began at Amritsar in 1873 to revive Sikh teachings and spread education.

questions.text: Which of the following is an inosilicate amphibole mineral used in highway construction and as railroad ballast?
questions.explanation: Hornblende is the commonest amphibole, a double-chain silicate (inosilicate); rock rich in it is crushed for road building and railway ballast. Olivine is a single-tetrahedron silicate, shale a sedimentary rock and geyserite a silica deposit from hot springs.

questions.text: Pipe Q can fill the tank in 60 hours while pipe R may fill in 45 hours. Q and R pipes are opened together for 6 hours after which pipe W is also opened to empty the tank. All three pipes are opened simultaneously for 24 hours to reach the half level mark. How much time (in hours) will pipe W alone take to empty the entire tank?
questions.explanation: Q and R fill 1/60 + 1/45 = 7/180 of the tank an hour: 7/30 in 6 hours, and 24 × 7/180 = 14/15 in the next 24. W must empty 7/30 + 14/15 − 1/2 = 2/3 of the tank in those 24 hours, so it empties the whole in 36 hours.

questions.text: Find the average of first 125 natural numbers.
questions.explanation: The average of 1 to n is (n + 1)/2 = 126/2 = 63.

questions.text: If the selling price of an article is ₹1,792 after a 20% discount, then the marked price of the article is:
questions.explanation: The selling price is 80% of the marked price: 1,792 ÷ 0.8 = ₹2,240.

questions.text: An investor, invested ₹2,00,000 in shares. The shares rose by 18% on the first day, fell by 15% on the second day, and then fell by 3% on the third day. What is the net percentage increase or decrease in the value of the investor's shares? (Rounded up to one decimal place)
questions.explanation: 1.18 × 0.85 × 0.97 = 0.9729, so the value falls by about 2.7%.

questions.text: The side MN of a parallelogram MNOP is produced to Q such that MN = NQ. PQ intersects ON at R. The point R divides ON in the ratio:
questions.explanation: NQ = MN = PO and NQ ∥ PO, so triangles RNQ and ROP are congruent (equal alternate angles and an equal side) and NR = RO: 1 : 1.

questions.text: A man can row a distance of 6 km in 1 hour in still water. He can row the same distance in 45 minutes with the current. Find the total time taken by him to row a distance of 16 km with the current and to return to the starting point.
questions.explanation: With the current he rows 6 km in 45 minutes, 8 km/h, so the current is 2 km/h and against it he rows 4 km/h. Time = 16/8 + 16/4 = 2 + 4 = 6 hours.

questions.text: A seller sold 19 cookies for ₹95 instead of 20 cookies in one kg, cheating a customer. What is the gain (in ₹) if the seller bought the cookies for ₹76?
questions.explanation: ₹76 buys 20 cookies (one kg), so the 19 he sells cost him 76 × 19/20 = ₹72.20. He sells them for ₹95, gaining ₹22.80.

questions.text: Find the area (in cm²) of the sector, where the radius of the circle is 24 cm and length of the arc is 7 cm.
questions.explanation: Area of a sector = ½ × arc × radius = ½ × 7 × 24 = 84 cm².

questions.text: If A:B = 6 : 8 and B:C = 7 : 12, then A:B:C is:
questions.explanation: A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 7 : 12. Making B the same (28): A : B = 21 : 28 and B : C = 28 : 48, so A : B : C = 21 : 28 : 48.

questions.text: If we extend a chord infinitely on both sides, then the chord becomes a _____________.
questions.explanation: A line through two points of a circle, extended both ways, is a secant.

questions.text: Anna and Ben each have a collection of marbles. If Anna gives one marble to Ben, they will both have an equal number of marbles. Conversely, if Ben gives one marble to Anna, she will end up with three times the number of marbles that Ben has. What is the total number of marbles they both have?
questions.explanation: Anna has 2 more than Ben (a − 1 = b + 1). If Ben gives her one: b + 3 = 3(b − 1), so b = 3 and a = 5. Together they have 8.

questions.text: Aman borrows a sum of ₹192208 at the rate of 15% per annum simple interest. At the end of the first year, he repays ₹20196 towards return of principal amount borrowed. If Aman clears all pending dues at the end of the second year, including interest payment that accrued during the first year, how much does he pay (in ₹) at the end of the second year?
questions.explanation: First-year interest: 15% of ₹1,92,208 = ₹28,831.20. After the repayment the principal is ₹1,72,012, which earns ₹25,801.80 in the second year. Due at the end: 1,72,012 + 28,831.20 + 25,801.80 = ₹2,26,645.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. Economics began with growth and removel of poverty as its grand theme.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'removal'.

questions.text: Identify the correct antonym for the given word. Envious
questions.explanation: 'Envious' means resentful of what others have; of the options, its opposite is 'generous', glad to give and share.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A short stay that you make while on a longer journey
questions.explanation: A stopover is a short stay at a place in the course of a longer journey.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Do you know “where does she reside” ?
questions.explanation: In an indirect question the subject comes before the verb, with no 'does': 'Do you know where she resides?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. Coffee was too “hot”; it burnt my tongue.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'hot' is 'frigid', very cold. 'Scorching' is a synonym and 'balmy' means pleasantly warm.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate verb / verb phrase to fill in the blank. They ________________ their house for the past two months, and it’s finally starting to look fantastic.
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and is still going on ('for the past two months') takes the present perfect continuous: 'have been renovating'.

questions.text: Select the word with the correct spelling to fill in the blank. Hiren loves to use ________ words while writing anything.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'colloquial', meaning informal or conversational.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. People know Stellenbosch for its greenery and delicious street foods.
options: Stellenbosch was known to people for its greenery and delicious street foods.
Stellenbosch have been known to people for its greenery and delicious street foods.
Stellenbosch had been known to people for its greenery and delicious street foods.
Stellenbosch is known to people for its greenery and delicious street foods.
questions.explanation: The simple present 'People know' becomes 'is known to people'; the other options change the tense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in the brackets to fill in the blank. Dhara _______ the way to Mumbai. [lost]
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'lost' is 'found': 'Dhara found the way to Mumbai.'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. People will respect his bravado.
options: His bravado will have to be respected by people.
His bravado will be respect by people.
His bravado will be respected by people.
His bravado will being respected by people.
questions.explanation: The simple future 'will respect' becomes 'will be respected'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Having unlimited power
questions.explanation: 'Omnipotent' means all-powerful; 'omniscient' is all-knowing and 'omnivorous' eating everything.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hit the roof
questions.explanation: To 'hit the roof' is to become very angry suddenly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. A computer can’t function without “it’s” mother board.
questions.explanation: The possessive is 'its'; 'it's' is short for 'it is'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He never talks / for anybody. / He is alone / all day.
questions.explanation: One talks 'to' somebody: 'He never talks to anybody.'

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. A: new facts and advanced B: but my opinion is C: he has discovered D: unchanged E: new arguments
questions.explanation: 'He has discovered (C) new facts and advanced (A) new arguments (E) but my opinion is (B) unchanged (D).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Creature of habit
options: One who does same thing in the same way
questions.explanation: A 'creature of habit' is someone who always does the same things in the same way.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Much more than usual or expected
questions.explanation: 'Exceeding' means very great, far beyond what is usual.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. A period of free outdoor play can provide a very necessary “respite” from the hustle and bustle of the day.
questions.explanation: A 'respite' is a short rest or relief: a 'break'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Mellifluous
questions.explanation: 'Mellifluous' means sweet or musical to hear; 'cacophonous' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Triumphant
questions.explanation: 'Triumphant' means victorious; its opposite is 'unsuccessful'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. According to a poll conducted in 2018–19 by an online internship and training platform, (1)__________ number of businesses actively (2)__________ intern profiles has increased over the previous five years. This study demonstrates that India received 80% more internship applications in 2018, with 2.2 million applications (3)________ 1.27 million in 2017. The rise was influenced (4)__________ part by an increase in the number of industries seeking fresh perspectives and innovative ideas to improve (5)__________ on existing projects. Obtaining an internship prior to entering the job market, which was once viewed as a Western concept, is quickly gaining steam in Indian workplaces.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'The number of businesses' refers to a particular count, so it takes the definite article.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. According to a poll conducted in 2018–19 by an online internship and training platform, (1)__________ number of businesses actively (2)__________ intern profiles has increased over the previous five years. This study demonstrates that India received 80% more internship applications in 2018, with 2.2 million applications (3)________ 1.27 million in 2017. The rise was influenced (4)__________ part by an increase in the number of industries seeking fresh perspectives and innovative ideas to improve (5)__________ on existing projects. Obtaining an internship prior to entering the job market, which was once viewed as a Western concept, is quickly gaining steam in Indian workplaces.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Businesses 'actively seeking' intern profiles, that is, looking for interns.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. According to a poll conducted in 2018–19 by an online internship and training platform, (1)__________ number of businesses actively (2)__________ intern profiles has increased over the previous five years. This study demonstrates that India received 80% more internship applications in 2018, with 2.2 million applications (3)________ 1.27 million in 2017. The rise was influenced (4)__________ part by an increase in the number of industries seeking fresh perspectives and innovative ideas to improve (5)__________ on existing projects. Obtaining an internship prior to entering the job market, which was once viewed as a Western concept, is quickly gaining steam in Indian workplaces.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 2.2 million applications in 2018 'compared to' 1.27 million in 2017.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. According to a poll conducted in 2018–19 by an online internship and training platform, (1)__________ number of businesses actively (2)__________ intern profiles has increased over the previous five years. This study demonstrates that India received 80% more internship applications in 2018, with 2.2 million applications (3)________ 1.27 million in 2017. Obtaining an internship prior to entering the job market, which was once viewed as a Western concept, is quickly gaining steam in Indian workplaces.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'In part' means partly: the rise was partly due to more industries seeking fresh ideas.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. According to a poll conducted in 2018–19 by an online internship and training platform, (1)__________ number of businesses actively (2)__________ intern profiles has increased over the previous five years. This study demonstrates that India received 80% more internship applications in 2018, with 2.2 million applications (3)________ 1.27 million in 2017. The rise was influenced (4)__________ part by an increase in the number of industries seeking fresh perspectives and innovative ideas to improve (5)__________ on existing projects. Obtaining an internship prior to entering the job market, which was once viewed as a Western concept, is quickly gaining steam in Indian workplaces.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Improve' needs a noun object here: industries want to improve 'efficiencies' on existing projects.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. _ D R G _ Z D R _ B Z D _ G B Z _ R G B
questions.explanation: With Z, B, G, R, D in the blanks the block ZDRGB repeats: ZDRGB ZDRGB ZDRGB ZDRGB.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All cars are birds. Some birds are plants. All plants are leaves. Conclusions: I.Some birds are cars. II.Some plants are birds. III.Some leaves are plants.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow.
Only conclusions I and III follow.
questions.explanation: All cars are birds, so some birds are cars (I). Some birds are plants, so some plants are birds (II). All plants are leaves, so some leaves are plants (III). All three follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FLBS’ is coded as ‘156’ and ‘MXT’ is coded as ‘228’. How will ‘VDZN’ be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: The code is 4 times the sum of the letters' positions: FLBS = 6 + 12 + 2 + 19 = 39 and 39 × 4 = 156; MXT = 13 + 24 + 20 = 57 and 57 × 4 = 228. VDZN = 22 + 4 + 26 + 14 = 66, so 66 × 4 = 264.

questions.text: Three of the following four options are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that does NOT belong to that group? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 26 – 95 – 21, 20 – 15 – 51 and 16 – 45 – 21 the first number is even and the other two odd. In 22 – 67 – 22 the third number is even as well, so it does not belong.

questions.text: Select the term from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. PJ 16, SM 25, VP 36, YS 49, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move 3 forward (P, S, V, Y, so B after wrapping round); second letters also move 3 (J, M, P, S, so V); the numbers are 4², 5², 6², 7², so next is 8² = 64: BV 64.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BIRTHDAY’ is written as ‘ADHTRIBY’ and ‘CONGRESS’ is written as ‘SERGNOCS’. How will ‘DIVISION’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first seven letters are reversed and the eighth stays at the end: BIRTHDA + Y → ADHTRIB + Y and CONGRES + S → SERGNOC + S. So DIVISIO + N → OISIVIDN.

questions.text: The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if each of the letter in the word ‘CERTAIN’ is arranged in English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: CERTAIN in alphabetical order is A C E I N R T. Compared with C E R T A I N, no letter is in the same place.

questions.text: G is the brother of F. E is the father of K.. C is the daughter of A. F is the mother of E. C is the sister of E. How is G related to A?
questions.explanation: C is A's daughter and E's sister, so E is A's child; F is E's mother, so F is A's wife. G is F's brother, so G is A's wife's brother.

questions.text: 30 is related to 41 following certain logic. Following the same logic, 14 is related to 21. To which of the following numbers is 54 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is a square plus 5, related to the next square plus 5: 30 = 5² + 5 → 6² + 5 = 41 and 14 = 3² + 5 → 4² + 5 = 21. So 54 = 7² + 5 → 8² + 5 = 69.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? BKUZ, ENWB, ?, KTAF, NWCH
questions.explanation: First and second letters move 3 forward (B, E, H, K, N and K, N, Q, T, W); third and fourth letters move 2 forward (U, W, Y, A, C and Z, B, D, F, H). The missing cluster is HQYD.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some balls are toys. All circles are balls. All balls are pits. Conclusions: (I) Some circles are toys. (II) All pits are toys.
questions.explanation: All circles are balls, but nothing says any of them is among the balls that are toys, so I does not follow. Only some balls are toys, so not every pit need be a toy: II does not follow either.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different. Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.
questions.explanation: In KNQ, SVY and BEH each letter is 3 places after the one before it. ILN moves +3 then +2, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 101 ÷ 48 − 13013 × 13 + 12 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 101 × 48 + 13013 ÷ 13 − 12 = 4848 + 1001 − 12 = 5837.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 96,77,60,47,36, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are −19, −17, −13, −11: the prime numbers in falling order. The next is −7: 36 − 7 = 29.

questions.text: 189 is related to 21 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 234 is related to 26. To which of the following is 468 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each number is related to its ninth: 189 ÷ 9 = 21 and 234 ÷ 9 = 26. So 468 ÷ 9 = 52.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘÷’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘+’ are interchanged? 4 + 9 × 48 – 6 ÷ 7 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 4 × 9 + 48 ÷ 6 − 7 = 36 + 8 − 7 = 37.

questions.text: ‘Magnify’ is related to ‘Expand’ in the same way as ‘Curtail’ is related to ‘________’.
questions.explanation: 'Magnify' and 'expand' both mean to make larger; likewise 'curtail' means to 'restrict' or cut short.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the given sets. (429, 514), (688, 773) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g., 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: In each set the second number is the first plus 85: 429 + 85 = 514 and 688 + 85 = 773. Likewise 546 + 85 = 631.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Wood’s Dispatch of 1854 primarily dealt with which of the following subject matters?
questions.explanation: Charles Wood's Despatch of 1854, often called the Magna Carta of English education in India, set out a plan for education from primary schools to universities.

questions.text: If GNP is 16% higher than the last year and the rate of inflation is 9%, production in the economy has grown by:
questions.explanation: SSC's key takes the usual shortcut: real growth ≈ nominal growth − inflation = 16% − 9% = 7%. (Worked exactly, 1.16 ÷ 1.09 ≈ 1.064, a real growth of about 6.4%.)

questions.text: Which of the following gases get released when dilute sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄) reacts with magnesium (Mg)?
questions.explanation: A reactive metal displaces hydrogen from a dilute acid: Mg + H₂SO₄ → MgSO₄ + H₂.

questions.text: Prabha Atre, who received the Padma Vibhushan Award 2022, belongs to which Gharana?
questions.explanation: Prabha Atre, the Hindustani classical vocalist, belongs to the Kirana gharana.

questions.text: An inscription, Takht-i-Bahi recovered from Mardan near Peshawar, indicates the rule of which of the following dynasties in north-western area of present Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The Takht-i-Bahi inscription is dated in the reign of Gondophernes (Gondophares), the best-known king of the Indo-Parthian dynasty.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of private sector industry in India?
questions.explanation: Tata Iron and Steel Company (now Tata Steel) is privately owned; BHEL, Oil India and SAIL are public sector undertakings.

questions.text: When was pro kabaddi league inaugurated for the first time in India?
questions.explanation: The Pro Kabaddi League's first season was played in 2014.

questions.text: Who among the following Indian women boxers was elected as the Chairperson and a voting member of the International Boxing Association in 2022?
questions.explanation: Lovlina Borgohain, the Tokyo Olympic bronze medallist, was elected chair of the IBA's Athletes' Committee in 2022, which made her a voting member of its Board of Directors.

questions.text: Identify the Indian classical dancer associated with Kathak.
questions.explanation: Rohini Bhate of Pune was a noted Kathak dancer. Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma is linked with Kuchipudi, Sharodi Saikia with Sattriya and Kelucharan Mohapatra with Odissi.

questions.text: Who among the following was the successor of Mughal Emperor, Babur?
questions.explanation: Babur died in 1530 and was succeeded by his son Humayun.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: British Parliament introduced Indian High Courts Act in which year?
questions.explanation: The Indian High Courts Act of 1861 provided for High Courts at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras.

questions.text: In which of the following years was the Election Commission of India founded?
questions.explanation: The Election Commission of India was set up on 25 January 1950, a day now marked as National Voters' Day.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers best describes the number of white pieces used in chess?
questions.explanation: Each side in chess has 16 pieces: a king, a queen, two rooks, two bishops, two knights and eight pawns.

questions.text: Which set of diseases are caused by bacteria?
questions.explanation: Typhoid, cholera and tuberculosis are bacterial. Dengue, influenza and the common cold are caused by viruses, and malaria by a protozoan (Plasmodium).

questions.text: Which of the following hills is located in the Eastern Ghats?
questions.explanation: The Shevaroy hills, near Salem in Tamil Nadu, are part of the Eastern Ghats. Anai Mudi is in the Western Ghats; the Khasi and Mizo hills are in the north-east.

questions.text: Paryushana festival is celebrated by the people of which of the following communities?
questions.explanation: Paryushana is the Jain festival of fasting and reflection.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?.
questions.explanation: Egg yolk is rich in fats and proteins, not starch. Maltose comes from cereal grains such as barley, fructose is found in grapes and lactose is the sugar of milk.

questions.text: In which year was the MPLADS scheme implemented?
questions.explanation: The Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS) was launched in December 1993.

questions.text: Which of the following duties has been NOT prescribed by the Indian Constitution as Fundamental Duties? 1. To defend the country 2. To pay income tax 3. To cast the vote in election 4. To safeguard the public property
questions.explanation: Article 51A includes defending the country and safeguarding public property, but neither paying income tax nor voting is listed among the Fundamental Duties.

questions.text: According to Census of India 2011, which Union Territory has the highest slum population?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Delhi had the largest slum population of the Union Territories.

questions.text: Bhupen Hazarika was one of the most well-known personalities from the state of ________.
questions.explanation: Bhupen Hazarika, the singer, composer and filmmaker, was from Assam; he was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2019.

questions.text: The tropical cyclones in Australia are known as ________.
questions.explanation: NCERT gives the regional names of tropical cyclones: cyclones in the Indian Ocean, hurricanes in the Atlantic, typhoons in the western Pacific and South China Sea, and willy-willies in western Australia. (Australia's own weather bureau calls them tropical cyclones.)

questions.text: Calorimeter is a small container made of a thin sheet of _________ with good thermal conductivity.
questions.explanation: A calorimeter is usually a thin copper vessel: copper conducts heat well, so the vessel quickly takes the temperature of its contents.

questions.text: In Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana, beneficiaries are provided with how much amount every year?
questions.explanation: PM-KISAN pays eligible farmer families ₹6,000 a year, in three instalments of ₹2,000.

questions.text: If A:B = 6 : 8 and B:C = 7 : 10, then A:B:C is:
A shopkeeper marked the price 20% more than its cost price. If he allows a discount of 30%, then find his loss percent.
questions.explanation: Take CP = 100. The marked price is 120, and after 30% off the selling price is 84: a loss of 16%.

questions.text: The average of the squares of the first 47 natural numbers is
questions.explanation: The sum of the squares of 1 to n is n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6, so their average is (n + 1)(2n + 1)/6 = 48 × 95/6 = 760.

questions.text: If the simple interest on ₹7,200 in 3 years at the rate of 16% per annum equals the simple interest on ₹9,600 at the rate of x% per annum in 4 years. The value of x is equal to:

In a collection of rare coins, there is one gold coin for every four non-gold coins. If 20 more gold coins are added to the collection, the ratio of the number of gold coins to that of non-gold coins will be 2:3. The total number of coins in the collection will now become ________.
questions.explanation: Let there be g gold and 4g other coins. (g + 20)/4g = 2/3 gives 3g + 60 = 8g, so g = 12: now 32 gold and 48 other coins, 80 in all.

questions.text: Find the measure of the central angle of a sector if its area is 16π and the radius is 8.

Akshara and Siddharth travel from point P to Q, a distance of 72 km at a rate of 8 km/h and 10 km/h, respectively. Siddharth reaches Q first and returns immediately and meets Akshara at R. Find the distance from P to R.
questions.explanation: When they meet they have covered twice PQ, 144 km, between them at 8 + 10 = 18 km/h: 8 hours. Akshara has gone 8 × 8 = 64 km, so PR = 64 km.

questions.text: For what value of k, the system of equations kx - 15y + 7 = 0 and 7x - 21y - 19 = 0 has NO solution?
questions.explanation: No solution needs k/7 = −15/−21 ≠ 7/−19. k/7 = 5/7 gives k = 5, and 7/−19 is different, so the lines are parallel.

questions.text: AP and AQ are two tangents drawn to a circle with center O from an external point A. If ∠PAQ = 40°, then ∠POQ is:
questions.explanation: The radii OP and OQ meet the tangents at right angles, so in quadrilateral APOQ ∠POQ = 360° − 90° − 90° − 40° = 140°.

questions.text: Find the least value of k for which a 7-digit number 249k876 is divisible by 6.
questions.explanation: The number is even, so it needs only a digit sum divisible by 3: 2 + 4 + 9 + k + 8 + 7 + 6 = 36 + k, so k = 0, 3, 6 or 9. The least is 0.

questions.text: At what angle is the arc length half the perimeter of the circle?
questions.explanation: Arc length = (θ/360°) × 2πr. For half of 2πr, θ/360° = 1/2, so θ = 180°.

questions.text: In a company, all employees are getting equal wages. If the number of employees is increased by 20% and their wages per head are decreased by 18%, what is the percentage decrease in total wages?
questions.explanation: Total wages = employees × wage per head, so they become 1.2 × 0.82 = 0.984 times as much: a fall of 1.6%.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. My cousin works “day and night” to achieve success in life.
questions.explanation: 'Around the clock' means all day and all night, without stopping.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The study of coins
questions.explanation: Numismatics is the study of coins; cartography is map-making and choreography the composing of dances.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Labour
questions.explanation: 'Labour' is hard work: 'toil'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Ram went to _____ an ice cream.
questions.explanation: To 'buy' is to purchase; 'by', 'bye' and 'byre' (a cowshed) only sound alike.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment in which the article has been used INCORRECTLY. UNESCO works to / strengthen an intellectual / and moral solidarity / of humankind.
questions.explanation: The solidarity is a particular one, that of humankind, so it takes 'the': 'strengthen the intellectual and moral solidarity of humankind'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. In those days, we did not expect luxuries; we were thankful if we could “keep the wolf from the door”.
questions.explanation: To 'keep the wolf from the door' is to have just enough to live on and avoid hunger.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. It is very hard for her to provide “the necessities of her family” .
questions.explanation: One provides something 'to' (or 'for') someone: 'provide the necessities to her family'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. To the general public, William was best known as a crusader “for peace and as an admired critic about” social, political and ethical subjects.
options: for peace and as an admired critic by
about peace and as an admired critic about
in peace and as an admired critic about
for peace and as an admired critic on
questions.explanation: A critic writes 'on' (or 'of') a subject: 'an admired critic on social, political and ethical subjects'. 'A crusader for peace' is already right.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. He will give a lecture on personality development.
options: A lecture on personality development will be given by him.
A lecture on personality development will be giving by him.
A lecture on personality development can be given by him.
A lecture will be given on personality development.
questions.explanation: 'Will give' becomes 'will be given', with 'a lecture on personality development' as the subject and 'by him' as the agent.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. Note: This is an advertisement of an ice-cream brand. (A) That’s why Silky is deliciously different and exceptionally versatile, natural, thick and durable ice cream. (B) Beautifully firm, nice, silky rather than thin and watery, it stays in shape and stands on top of fruits or pastries without soaking in. (C) Silky thick double ice cream has a unique, fresh taste and texture.
questions.explanation: C introduces Silky ice cream, B describes its firm, silky texture, and A concludes with 'That's why': CBA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Bully
questions.explanation: A 'bully' uses strength to intimidate weaker people: an 'oppressor'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Entire
questions.explanation: 'Entire' means whole or complete; its opposite is 'incomplete'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. His behaviour vexes me sometimes.
options: Sometimes he vexes me with his behaviour.
I am sometimes vexed by his behaviour.
He is being vexing me with his behaviour
questions.explanation: The object 'me' becomes the subject 'I', and 'vexes' becomes 'am vexed': 'I am sometimes vexed by his behaviour.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Thankful
questions.explanation: To be 'obliged' to someone is to be grateful for a favour: 'thankful'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who is inclined to see the worst aspect of things
questions.explanation: A pessimist expects the worst; an optimist expects the best.

questions.text: Select the sentence that contains a spelling error.
options: The host institution must provide the delegates with accomodation at a subsidised rate.
The occurrence of the lunar eclipse is often a mystery for children.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'accommodation', with a double 'c' and a double 'm'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. Dr. Sinha has / brought about a new / book on social / impact of child labour.
questions.explanation: To publish a book is to 'bring it out'; 'bring about' means to cause: 'Dr. Sinha has brought out a new book'. ('On the social impact' would also read better, but SSC's key marks 'brought about', the clear error.)

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'efficient'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. No matter how “hard work you”, your boss will not recognise your efforts.
questions.explanation: After 'no matter how' the adverb comes first and the clause keeps its normal order: 'No matter how hard you work'.

questions.text: Select the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word in the given sentence. Feeling “discouraged”, she finally finds the motivation for pursing her goal.
questions.explanation: 'Discouraged' means having lost confidence or enthusiasm; its opposite is 'inspired'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. I have a recurring dream. Actually, I have a few: one is about dismembering a body , I’d rather not get into it, but the (1) ________ pertinent one is about college. It’s the end of the semester, and I suddenly (2) ________ that there is a class I forgot to attend, ever, and now I have to sit for the final exam. I wake up panicked, my GPA in peril. How could I have done this? Why do I so (3) ________ dissatisfy myself? Then I remember I haven’t been in college in more than a decade. Someone with (4) ________ knowledge of my academic career might point out that this nightmare scenario is not that far removed from my actual collegiate experience, and that at certain times in my life, it did not take the magic of slumber to find me completely unprepared for a final. And, well, (5) ________ of what may or may not be true of my personal scholastic rigour, I suspect the school-stress dream is quite a common one.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Of the writer's few recurring dreams, 'the more pertinent one' is about college: 'more' forms the comparative.
