questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. READER : ERZWRE :: SERIAL : ESIRLA :: JINGLE : ?
questions.explanation: The first two letters swap, the middle two are replaced by their opposite letters (A↔Z, D↔W, R↔I) and the last two swap: READER → ER ZW RE and SERIAL → ES IR LA. So JINGLE → IJ MT EL: IJMTEL.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’, ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the father of B’, ‘A $ B’ means ‘A is the son of B’, ‘A % B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’, ‘A / B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A * B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’. Which of the following means P is the Son's wife of T? i. T / B – K * P + O ii. T + K * P + B % O iii. K * P + B % T + P iv. P + T * K + B % O
questions.explanation: In i, T is B's wife and B is K's father, so T is K's mother, and K is P's husband: P is T's son's wife. In ii, T is K's mother and K is P's husband directly. iii makes P and T each the other's mother, and in iv P is T's mother.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘RETAINED’ is written as ‘ENIATERD’ and ‘MATURITY’ is written as ‘TIRUTAMY’. How will ‘FIREWALL’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first seven letters are reversed and the eighth stays put: RETAINE + D → ENIATER + D and MATURIT + Y → TIRUTAM + Y. So FIREWAL + L → LAWERIF + L: LAWERIFL.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 9 17 33 65 129 ?
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before minus 1: 9 × 2 − 1 = 17, 17 × 2 − 1 = 33 and so on, so 129 × 2 − 1 = 257.

questions.text: 16 is related to 30 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 81 is related to 110. To which of the following is 49 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some Toys are Plastic. Some Plastic are Metal. No Metal is Chemical. Conclusions: (I) Some Chemicals are Plastic. (II) No Toy is a Chemical.
questions.explanation: Metal is kept apart from chemicals, but nothing fixes how chemicals relate to plastic or to toys. Neither 'some chemicals are plastic' (I) nor 'no toy is a chemical' (II) is certain.

questions.text: The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if each of the letters in the word ‘SIGHTED’ is arranged in the English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: In alphabetical order SIGHTED becomes D E G H I S T. Comparing position by position, G (3rd) and H (4th) stay where they were: two letters.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? RLYV, PJWT, NHUR, ? , JDQN
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places back each time: R, P, N, L, J; L, J, H, F, D; Y, W, U, S, Q; V, T, R, P, N. The missing cluster is LFSP.

questions.text: Three of the following four number-pairs are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which number-pair does NOT belong to that group? (NOTE: The relation should be found without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits)
questions.explanation: All eight numbers are primes. 31 and 41 have one prime between them (37), as do 83 and 97 (89) and 61 and 71 (67). 73 and 79 are consecutive primes, with none between, so they do not belong.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the given statements. Statements: All fruit are sour. Some sour are vegetables. Some vegetables are green. Conclusions: (I) All vegetables are sour. (II) Some sour are green.
questions.explanation: 'Some sour are vegetables' does not make all vegetables sour (I), and the green vegetables need not be among the sour ones (II). Neither follows.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘×’ is replaced by ‘÷’, ‘÷’ is replaced by ‘+’, ‘+’ is replaced by ‘×’ and ‘−’ remains unchanged? 42 × 3 ÷ 4 + 9 − 17 = ?
questions.explanation: After replacing the signs: 42 ÷ 3 + 4 × 9 − 17 = 14 + 36 − 17 = 33.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 107 + 2028 × 6 – 427 ÷ 7 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 107 − 2028 ÷ 6 + 427 × 7 = 107 − 338 + 2989 = 2758.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters which, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. f h _ h _ g f _ h g _ h _ f f _ g _ h _ f
options: g h f f g h f g
g h f h g f f g
g h f h g h f g
g h f h g h h g
questions.explanation: With g, h, f, h, g, h, h, g in the blanks the block fhghhgf repeats: fhghhgf fhghhgf fhghhgf.

questions.text: Based on the position in the English alphabetical order, three of the following letter-clusters are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the odd letter-cluster. Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.
questions.explanation: TWYZ, EHJK and YBDE move +3, +2, +1 (Y to B wraps round). SVXZ moves +3, +2, +2, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the triad in which the numbers are related to each other in the same way as are the numbers of the given triads. (148, 126, 104), (98, 76, 54) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: In each triad the numbers fall by 22: 148, 126, 104 and 98, 76, 54. Likewise 157, 135, 113.

questions.text: Presently, which of the following countries is NOT a beneficiary of India's Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Angola. India's DFTP scheme is for the least developed countries (LDCs), and Angola left the UN's list of LDCs in February 2021; Rwanda, Burundi and Myanmar are still on it.

questions.text: A small object is placed on the focus on the left side of a convex lens. Where will be the image formed?
options: At infinity on the right side of the lens.
At infinity on the left side of the lens.
At the focus on the right side of the lens.
At the centre on the right side of the lens.
questions.explanation: Rays from an object at the principal focus of a convex lens leave it parallel, so the image forms at infinity on the other side.

questions.text: After the fall of the Guptas, different kingdoms emerged in various parts of India. Among them, the Maukharis emerged in which of the following areas?
questions.explanation: The Maukharis ruled from Kannauj after the Guptas declined; Thanesar was the seat of the Pushyabhutis and Valabhi of the Maitrakas.

questions.text: Which of the following is a public sector industry?
questions.explanation: Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL) is owned by the Government of India; Adani, Reliance and Tata are private groups.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Indian National Army was formed in which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: The Indian National Army was organised in Singapore in 1942 from Indian prisoners of war, and Subhas Chandra Bose took command of it there in 1943.

questions.text: Which of the following nations won the ICC World Test Championship, defeating India, in 2023?
questions.explanation: Australia beat India by 209 runs in the 2023 World Test Championship final at the Oval.

questions.text: One of the greatest of Chola ruler Rajaraja I ruled from 985 AD to ______.
questions.explanation: Rajaraja I ruled from 985 to 1014 AD; his son Rajendra I succeeded him.

questions.text: Indian Olympic Association was established in which of the following years?
questions.explanation: The Indian Olympic Association was set up in 1927.

questions.text: Which of following is NOT a device of parliamentary proceedings?
questions.explanation: Half-an-hour discussions, short-duration (two-hour) discussions and Zero Hour are all devices of parliamentary proceedings; there is no 'full-day discussion'.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers marks the eastern-most boundary of the Himalayas?
questions.explanation: In NCERT's division of the Himalayas by river valleys, the Brahmaputra marks their eastern-most boundary; the Satluj, Kali and Teesta divide sections within the range.

questions.text: Padma Bhushan awardee, Ustad Sabri Khan played which of the following musical instruments?
questions.explanation: Ustad Sabri Khan was one of India's best-known sarangi players.

questions.text: Exfoliation is a form of _________.
questions.explanation: Exfoliation, the peeling away of rock in curved sheets, is caused by physical forces such as expansion and contraction with temperature changes, so it is physical weathering.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: Article 80 sets out the composition of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha); Article 81 does the same for the Lok Sabha.

questions.text: Which of the following is India’s national academy of dance?
options: Centre for Cultural Resources and Training
questions.explanation: The Sangeet Natak Akademi is India's national academy for music, dance and drama; the Lalit Kala Akademi is for the visual arts.

questions.text: What is the empirically fitted relationship between the rate of change of money, wage, and rate of unemployment known as?
questions.explanation: A. W. Phillips fitted an inverse relationship between the rate of change of money wages and the rate of unemployment, from British data: the Phillips curve.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who asked James Rennel to prepare the map of Hindustan?
questions.explanation: Robert Clive asked James Rennell, the East India Company's surveyor in Bengal, to produce maps of Hindustan.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi is celebrated as the national festival of India. In which of the following years was Gandhi ji born?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi was born on 2 October 1869 at Porbandar; Gandhi Jayanti marks the day.

questions.text: Who among the following is appointed as the new Chairman of Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) in March 2023?
questions.explanation: Deepak Mohanty, a former Executive Director of the Reserve Bank of India, was appointed Chairman of the PFRDA in March 2023.

questions.text: Transition elements are the elements that are found in Groups 3-12 of the modern periodic table, that constitute the _____.
questions.explanation: Groups 3 to 12, in which the d orbitals are being filled, make up the d-block: the transition elements.

questions.text: Which Article in the fundamental duty applies, when a construction worker takes his 8-year son to the site rather than sending him to school?
questions.explanation: Article 51A(k), added by the 86th Amendment in 2002, makes it the duty of a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to a child between six and fourteen.

questions.text: The Nandi Award for Best Male Playback Singer was instituted by which state in the year 1977?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Andhra Pradesh, whose government presents the Nandi Awards for Telugu cinema.

questions.text: Which Bill was passed by the Parliament, in July 2021, to help in the availability of working capital for the micro, small and medium enterprises sector?
options: The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Bill, 2021
questions.explanation: The Factoring Regulation (Amendment) Bill, 2021 let many more NBFCs take up factoring (buying firms' receivables), easing working capital for MSMEs.

questions.text: Identify the structural formula for magnesium hydroxide.
questions.explanation: Magnesium forms Mg²⁺ ions, each balanced by two hydroxide ions (OH⁻): Mg(OH)₂.

questions.text: What kind of phyllotaxy was examined in the Guava plant?
questions.explanation: NCERT gives guava, with Calotropis, as an example of opposite phyllotaxy: a pair of leaves at each node, facing each other.

questions.text: P and Q are two fixed points 10 cm apart, and R is a point on PQ such that PR = 6 cm. By what percentage is the length of QR decreased when the length of PR is increased by 5%?
questions.explanation: QR is 10 − 6 = 4 cm. PR rises 5% to 6.3 cm, so QR falls to 3.7 cm: a decrease of 0.3/4 = 7.5%.

questions.text: A trader owes a merchant ₹9,810 due in 1 year, but the trader wants to settle the account after 6 months. If the rate of simple interest is 9% per annum, how much cash (in ₹) should he pay?
questions.explanation: SSC's key values the debt from today: ₹9,810/1.09 = ₹9,000 now, which grows to 9,000 × 1.045 = ₹9,405 in six months at 9% a year. (Discounting ₹9,810 straight back six months, 9,810/1.045 ≈ ₹9,387.56, is not among the options.)

questions.text: A discount series of 10% and 16% on an invoice is the same as a single discount of:
questions.explanation: After 10% and then 16% off, 0.9 × 0.84 = 0.756 of the price is left: a single discount of 24.4%.

questions.text: P and Q start running in opposite directions on a circular track from the same point. If their speeds are 10 m/s and 8 m/s, respectively, then after what time will they meet if the length of the track is 1620 m?
questions.explanation: Running in opposite directions they close the gap at 10 + 8 = 18 m/s, so they meet after 1620/18 = 90 seconds.

questions.text: Two different quantities of the same solution having ingredients A and B are stored in two different containers. In the first container, there are 252 litre of A and 441 litre of B. In the second container, the total quantity of the solution was 1188 litre. How much of the solution in the second container was made up of ingredient B?
questions.explanation: It is the same solution, so A : B is the same in both containers: 252 : 441 = 4 : 7. B in the second = 1188 × 7/11 = 756 litres.

questions.text: The radius of the circle is 8 cm. The distance of a point lying outside the circle from the centre is 17 cm. The length of the tangent drawn from the outside point to the circle is:
questions.explanation: The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact: √(17² − 8²) = √(289 − 64) = √225 = 15 cm.

questions.text: Which digits should come in the place of x and y, respectively, if the number 62684xy is divisible by both 8 and 5?
questions.explanation: Divisible by both 5 and 8, the number must end in 0, so y = 0. The last three digits, 4x0, must then be divisible by 8: of the options only 440 is (8 × 55), so x = 4.

questions.text: For which of the following values of a and b do the given equations, have NO solution? x - ay = 2 - a; (1 - a)x + 6y = a + b
questions.explanation: No solution needs 1/(1 − a) = −a/6 ≠ (2 − a)/(a + b). The equality gives a² − a − 6 = 0, so a = 3 or a = −2. With a = 3 the first two ratios are −1/2, and −1/(3 + b) ≠ −1/2 needs b ≠ −1.

questions.text: 2 varieties of tea powders worth ₹250/kg and ₹300/kg are mixed with a third variety of tea powder in the ratio 1 : 1 : 2. If the mixture is worth ₹350/kg, find the price of the third variety tea powder.
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The children have made the box.
options: The box is being made by the children.
The box has been made by the children.
The box had been made by the children.
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'have made' becomes 'has been made': 'The box has been made by the children.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who eats a lot
questions.explanation: A glutton eats far too much; a chef cooks, a steward serves and a chauffeur drives.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank. The ____________ was decorated with candles and chocolates everywhere.
questions.explanation: Only 'floor', the surface of a room, fits the sentence; 'flour' and 'flower' sound alike but mean something else.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A period of ten years
questions.explanation: A decade is ten years; a biennium is two, a lustrum five and a century a hundred.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. a large, flat area surrounded by seats used for sports or entertainment
questions.explanation: An arena is a large, level area surrounded by seats for sports or shows.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I have the hundred reasons to not attend the meeting tomorrow.
questions.explanation: An unspecified number takes the indefinite article: 'I have a hundred reasons', not 'the hundred reasons'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence. A. When we connect this design with a wire, electricity flows. B. These metal strips were put in a sulphuric acid solution. C. He made two strips of different metals. D. Alessandro Volta discovered electric battery.
questions.explanation: D introduces Volta's discovery, C says how he began (two strips of different metals), B what he did with them and A the result: DCBA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. All his friends admired him because he was a “straight shooter”.
questions.explanation: A 'straight shooter' is an honest, straightforward person.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. A. The upper part of the river B. Continuous rain on C. Week, there had been D. During the previous
questions.explanation: 'During the previous (D) week, there had been (C) continuous rain on (B) the upper part of the river (A).'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. They are organising a concert for charity.
options: A concert is being organised by them for charity.
They are organising a charity concert.
A concert for charity is organising by them.
They are being organised a concert for charity.
questions.explanation: The present continuous 'are organising' becomes 'is being organised': 'A concert is being organised by them for charity.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. I was “happy” to know that Sheila passed her final exams.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'happy' is 'sad'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined word segment in the given sentence. The wedding was “put on” until January.
questions.explanation: To 'put off' is to postpone: the wedding was postponed until January. To 'put on' is to wear or stage something.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. Sheila ________ (failed) all her classes.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'failed' is 'passed'; 'fizzled', 'flopped' and 'flunked' all mean failed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in the brackets to fill in the blank. She ________ the target by an inch and lost the gold medal. [hit]
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'hit' is 'missed', which is why she lost the gold medal.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. After I retire, I started a second career / as a writer and published several books / which allowed me to share my stories / and insights with a wider audience.
options: which allowed me to share my stories
After I retire, I started a second career
and insights with a wider audience
as a writer and published several books
questions.explanation: The sentence is in the past ('started', 'published'), so 'After I retired', not 'After I retire'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'occurrence'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. My uncle lives in New York, so I only see him “once in a blue moon”.
questions.explanation: 'Once in a blue moon' means very rarely.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'tangible'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence. One of Ram’s “leisure” activities is tennis.
questions.explanation: 'Leisure' activities are those done in one's free time, for 'recreation'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Earthquake is the (1)_________ breaking and displacement of substantial portions of the earth's outer rocky crust. During an earthquake, rock disturbances can cause rivers to change their flow. Landslides (2)__________ by earthquakes can cause significant destruction and loss of life. Tsunamis are a (3)_________ of damaging waves caused by large earthquakes that occur under the ocean. Earthquakes rarely directly kill anyone. Many (4)__________ and injuries are caused by falling debris and the fall of structures. The (5)_________ of an earthquake relies on how much and how far rock cracks and shifts.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: An earthquake is the 'abrupt' (sudden) breaking and displacement of the crust.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Earthquake is the (1)_________ breaking and displacement of substantial portions of the earth's outer rocky crust. During an earthquake, rock disturbances can cause rivers to change their flow. Landslides (2)__________ by earthquakes can cause significant destruction and loss of life. Tsunamis are a (3)_________ of damaging waves caused by large earthquakes that occur under the ocean. Earthquakes rarely directly kill anyone. Many (4)__________ and injuries are caused by falling debris and the fall of structures. The (5)_________ of an earthquake relies on how much and how far rock cracks and shifts.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Landslides 'triggered' (set off) by earthquakes.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Earthquake is the (1)_________ breaking and displacement of substantial portions of the earth's outer rocky crust. During an earthquake, rock disturbances can cause rivers to change their flow. Landslides (2)__________ by earthquakes can cause significant destruction and loss of life. Tsunamis are a (3)_________ of damaging waves caused by large earthquakes that occur under the ocean. Earthquakes rarely directly kill anyone. Many (4)__________ and injuries are caused by falling debris and the fall of structures. The (5)_________ of an earthquake relies on how much and how far rock cracks and shifts.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: A tsunami is a 'succession' (series) of damaging waves.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Earthquake is the (1)_________ breaking and displacement of substantial portions of the earth's outer rocky crust. During an earthquake, rock disturbances can cause rivers to change their flow. Landslides (2)__________ by earthquakes can cause significant destruction and loss of life. Tsunamis are a (3)_________ of damaging waves caused by large earthquakes that occur under the ocean. Earthquakes rarely directly kill anyone. Many (4)__________ and injuries are caused by falling debris and the fall of structures. The (5)_________ of an earthquake relies on how much and how far rock cracks and shifts.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Earthquakes rarely kill directly, but falling debris and structures cause many 'fatalities' (deaths) and injuries.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Earthquake is the (1)_________ breaking and displacement of substantial portions of the earth's outer rocky crust. During an earthquake, rock disturbances can cause rivers to change their flow. Landslides (2)__________ by earthquakes can cause significant destruction and loss of life. Tsunamis are a (3)_________ of damaging waves caused by large earthquakes that occur under the ocean. Earthquakes rarely directly kill anyone. Many (4)__________ and injuries are caused by falling debris and the fall of structures. The (5)_________ of an earthquake relies on how much and how far rock cracks and shifts.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The 'magnitude' (size) of an earthquake depends on how much and how far the rock cracks and shifts.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'A ? B' means ‘A is the mother of B’, 'A ! B' means ‘A is the wife of B’, 'A & B' means ‘A is the brother of B’ and 'A x B' means ‘A is the father of B’. Which of the following means that Z is the wife's father's mother of L?
options: Z ? B x T & J ! L
Z ? B ! T & J x L
Z ! B x T ? J & L
Z & B ! T x J ? L
questions.explanation: In Z ? B x T & J ! L, J is the wife of L, T is J's brother, B is the father of T (and so of J) and Z is B's mother: Z is L's wife's father's mother.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Magician : Magic :: Dancer : ?
questions.explanation: A magician performs magic, as a dancer performs a dance.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘VAT’ is coded as ‘43’ and ‘AWW’ is coded as ‘47’. How will ‘ZHU’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet: V + A + T = 22 + 1 + 20 = 43 and A + W + W = 1 + 23 + 23 = 47. So ZHU = 26 + 8 + 21 = 55.

questions.text: The following contains two pairs of words which are related to each other in a certain way. Three of the following four word-pairs are alike as these have the same relationship and thus form a group. Which word-pair does NOT belong to that group? (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be grouped based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word)
questions.explanation: In the other three pairs the words are close in meaning (joy/peace, problem/concern, worry/fear); misery and happiness are opposites.

questions.text: 13 is related to 117 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 23 is related to 207. To which of the following is 51 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each number is related to 9 times itself: 13 × 9 = 117 and 23 × 9 = 207. So 51 × 9 = 459.

questions.text: Select the word-pair that best represents a similar relationship to the one expressed in the pair of words given below. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Kaziranga : Rhinoceros
questions.explanation: Kaziranga National Park is known for its one-horned rhinoceros, as Periyar is for its elephants. Gir is known for lions, Gahirmatha for olive ridley turtles and Ranthambore for tigers.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? BHVC, ZLTG, XPRK, ? , TXNS
questions.explanation: First letters move back 2 (B, Z, X, V, T), second letters forward 4 (H, L, P, T, X), third letters back 2 (V, T, R, P, N) and fourth letters forward 4 (C, G, K, O, S): VTPO.

questions.text: Each of the letters in the word ‘REDUCTION’ are arranged in the English alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English alphabetical order between the letter which is the third from the left end and the fourth from the left end in the group of letters thus formed?
questions.explanation: REDUCTION in alphabetical order is C D E I N O R T U. The third and fourth letters from the left are E and I; between them in the alphabet come F, G and H: three letters.

questions.text: Three of the following four options are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that does NOT belong to that group? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In the other three the first number is the square of the second plus the cube of the third: 10² + 4³ = 164, 6² + 3³ = 63 and 12² + 6³ = 360. But 8² + 2³ = 72, not 82.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 2864 × 4 – 168 ÷ 2 + 69 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 2864 ÷ 4 + 168 × 2 − 69 = 716 + 336 − 69 = 983.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 22, 23, 27, 54, 70, 195, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 1³, 2², 3³, 4², 5³ (1, 4, 27, 16, 125), so the next is 6² = 36: 195 + 36 = 231.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 63 : 441 51 : 357
questions.explanation: Each second number is 7 times the first: 63 × 7 = 441 and 51 × 7 = 357. Likewise 39 × 7 = 273.

questions.text: Two sets of numbers are given below. In each set of numbers, certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number result(s) in the second number. Similarly, certain mathematical operation(s) on the second number result(s) in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in the given sets? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 9 – 27 – 31 – 36; 10 – 30 – 34 – 39
questions.explanation: In each set the steps are × 3, + 4, + 5: 9 → 27 → 31 → 36 and 10 → 30 → 34 → 39. Likewise 5 → 15 → 19 → 24.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘×‘ are interchanged and ‘−’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 27 − 6 + 4 × 8 ÷ 6 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 27 ÷ 6 × 4 + 8 − 6 = 4.5 × 4 + 8 − 6 = 18 + 2 = 20.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the letter series. _ O _ O _ _ O _ P _ O _
questions.explanation: With O, P, O, P, O, O, P in the blanks the block OOP repeats: OOP OOP OOP OOP.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'ESTATE' is written as '80', 'FAMOUS' is written as '85', how will 'FOREST' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet plus 10: ESTATE = 5 + 19 + 20 + 1 + 20 + 5 = 70, coded 80, and FAMOUS = 75, coded 85. FOREST = 6 + 15 + 18 + 5 + 19 + 20 = 83, so 93.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Where was the Hindu College established in the year 1791?
questions.explanation: In 1791 a Hindu college (Jonathan Duncan's Sanskrit College) was set up at Benaras to encourage the study of ancient Sanskrit texts. The better-known Hindu College of Calcutta came later, in 1817.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year was the Gandhi-Irwin Pact signed?
questions.explanation: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931; Gandhi then attended the Second Round Table Conference.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT the socio-economic objective of Industrial Policy Statement 1980?
options: Consumer protection against high prices and bad quality
Allowing the maximum foreign direct investment
questions.explanation: The 1980 statement aimed at higher employment, export-oriented industries and consumer protection against high prices and bad quality, among other goals. Opening up to foreign direct investment came with the 1991 policy.

questions.text: The name ‘Piyadassi’ is associated with whom among the following Mauryan kings?
questions.explanation: Ashoka's inscriptions call him Devanampiya Piyadassi: 'beloved of the gods', 'pleasant to behold'.

questions.text: In which of the following years will India host the World Badminton Championship?
questions.explanation: The BWF awarded the 2026 World Championships to India, with New Delhi as host; India had held them once before, at Hyderabad in 2009.

questions.text: Which of the following plants is used to cure cold and cough?
questions.explanation: Tulsi (holy basil) is a common home remedy for cold and cough.

questions.text: Where is the Gulf of Mannar located?
options: Between the south-eastern tip of India and the southern coast of Sri Lanka
Between the south-eastern tip of India and the eastern coast of Sri Lanka
Between the south-eastern tip of India and the north-western coast of Sri Lanka
Between the south-eastern tip of India and the western coast of Sri Lanka
questions.explanation: The Gulf of Mannar lies between the south-eastern tip of India and the western coast of Sri Lanka, south of Adam's Bridge.

questions.text: Name a common electrolyte disorder that occurs when the amount of sodium in your blood becomes abnormally low.
questions.explanation: Hyponatremia is too little sodium (Latin 'natrium') in the blood; hypokalemia is too little potassium.

questions.text: Who was the player of the match in the semi-final of the T20 Women's World Cup 2023 played between India and Australia?
questions.explanation: Ashleigh Gardner (31 off 18 balls and 2 for 37) was player of the match in the semi-final at Cape Town, which Australia won by 5 runs.

questions.text: Who among the following won a Gold Medal at the 2021 World Cadet Wrestling Championship held in Budapest, Hungary?
questions.explanation: Priya Malik won gold in the 73 kg category at the 2021 World Cadet Wrestling Championships in Budapest.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of current?
questions.explanation: The ampere is the SI unit of electric current; the volt measures potential difference and the ohm resistance.

questions.text: How many members are nominated by the President to the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: Under Article 80 the President nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha for their knowledge of literature, science, art or social service.

questions.text: Sangeet Natak Akademy Awardee Sulochana Chavan was a famous ________ singer.
questions.explanation: Sulochana Chavan, known as the queen of Lavani, sang Maharashtra's Lavani folk songs.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a component of a flower?
questions.explanation: Calyx, corolla, androecium and gynoecium are the four whorls of a flower. Spines are modified leaves or stems, not flower parts.

questions.text: Which is the colloquial term to describe the occurrence of pre-monsoon rains in India especially in parts of Kerala, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu?
questions.explanation: Pre-monsoon showers in Kerala and coastal Karnataka are called mango showers because they help mangoes ripen early.

questions.text: Tera Tali folk dance is primarily associated with which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Terah Taali is performed by women of the Kamad community of Rajasthan, with cymbals tied to their bodies.

questions.text: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar described Directive Principles of State Policy as __________of the Indian constitution.
options: The most precious part of the constitution
a novel feature of the constitution
questions.explanation: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called the Directive Principles 'novel features' of the Indian Constitution.

questions.text: Which of the following crops is NOT grown during the Zaid season in India?
questions.explanation: Rice is a kharif crop. Zaid crops, grown in the short summer season between rabi and kharif, include watermelon, muskmelon and cucumber.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a non-tax revenue source for the government?
questions.explanation: Fees and fines are non-tax revenue; value-added tax, corporate tax and personal income tax are taxes.

questions.text: The festival of ‘Rath Yatra’ of Puri in Odisha is dedicated to which deity?
questions.explanation: The Puri Rath Yatra carries Lord Jagannath, with Balabhadra and Subhadra, from the Jagannath Temple to the Gundicha Temple.

questions.text: Sangeet Kala Acharya Award is given by which organisation every year since 1993?
questions.explanation: The Music Academy, Madras presents the Sangita Kala Acharya award each year, alongside its better-known Sangita Kalanidhi.

questions.text: As per article 123, the ordinance making power is the most important legislative power of ____________.
questions.explanation: Article 123 lets the President promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session: the most important of the President's legislative powers.

questions.text: Grignard reagent is represented as:
questions.explanation: A Grignard reagent is an alkyl or aryl magnesium halide, R-Mg-X; methylmagnesium chloride, CH₃-Mg-Cl, is one.

questions.text: Which of the following schemes was launched for the welfare of the unorganised sector workers and labourers on 26 August 2021?
questions.explanation: The e-Shram portal, a national database of unorganised workers, was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment on 26 August 2021.

questions.text: Who among the following was the Vakil under the reign of Mughal Emperor, Akbar, who received the title of Khan-i-Khanan?
questions.explanation: Bairam Khan, Akbar's regent in his early years, served as vakil and held the title Khan-i-Khanan.

questions.text: In the following sets, which set represents the angles of a triangle?
questions.explanation: The angles of a triangle add up to 180°: 30° + 60° + 90° = 180°. The other sets add up to 170°, 220° and 190°.

questions.text: If the curved surface area of a cylinder is 880 cm² , then the product of its height and radius is:
questions.explanation: Curved surface area = 2πrh = 880, so rh = 880 × 7/44 = 140 cm².

questions.text: The perimeters of two similar triangles ΔRST and ΔABC are 26 cm and 39 cm, respectively. If AB = 24 cm, then RS is ___.
questions.explanation: The sides of similar triangles are in the ratio of their perimeters, 26 : 39 = 2 : 3. So RS = 24 × 2/3 = 16 cm.

questions.text: A class of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 62, and that of the rest is 72. What is the average score of the class?

A sum of ₹10,000 is taken as a loan by Rajesh at a rate of 15% p.a. simple interest for 2 years. But Rajesh could not repay it at the agreed time and asked for an extension of two more years. So, the lender included the interest amount for the period as principal for the next two years at the same rate of interest. The total amount paid by Rajesh at the end of 4 years is:
questions.explanation: Interest for the first 2 years: 10,000 × 15 × 2/100 = ₹3,000, making the principal ₹13,000. Interest for the next 2 years: 13,000 × 15 × 2/100 = ₹3,900. Total paid: 13,000 + 3,900 = ₹16,900.

questions.text: The area of a sector of a circle of radius 12 cm, formed by an arc of length 7 cm is:
questions.explanation: Area of a sector = ½ × arc length × radius = ½ × 7 × 12 = 42 cm².

questions.text: Kalyan spends 80% of his income. His income increases by 15% and his expenditure also increases by 5%. The percentage of increase in his savings is:
questions.explanation: Take income 100: spending 80, saving 20. After the rises income is 115 and spending 84, so saving is 31. The saving rises by 11/20 = 55%.

questions.text: 2 biscuits and 1 chocolate cost ₹69. 2 chocolates and 3 cups of coffee cost ₹127. 3 biscuits, 4 chocolates and 2 cups of coffee cost ₹229. Find the total cost (in ₹) of 5 biscuits, 5 chocolates and 5 cups of coffee.
questions.explanation: Solving the three equations, a biscuit costs ₹17, a chocolate ₹35 and a coffee ₹19 (2 × 17 + 35 = 69, 2 × 35 + 3 × 19 = 127, 3 × 17 + 4 × 35 + 2 × 19 = 229). So 5 × (17 + 35 + 19) = ₹355.

questions.text: Two pipes P and Q can fill a tank in 36 minutes and 45 minutes, respectively. If both pipes are opened together, the time taken to fill the tank is:
questions.explanation: Together they fill 1/36 + 1/45 = (5 + 4)/180 = 1/20 of the tank a minute: 20 minutes.

questions.text: Find the mean proportional of 12.96 and 0.16.
Simplify the following. 16 ÷ 2− 7 × 15 ÷ 3 + 5 × 5 + 4 × 3 − 10
questions.explanation: Division and multiplication first: 8 − 35 + 25 + 12 − 10 = 0.

questions.text: Find the remainder: (17¹³ − 21) ÷ 18
questions.explanation: 17 = 18 − 1, so 17¹³ leaves remainder (−1)¹³ = −1 on division by 18. Then 17¹³ − 21 leaves −1 − 21 = −22, that is −22 + 36 = 14.

questions.text: A manufacturer announces a trade discount of 30% on his products for his dealers. One of the dealers purchased 6 smart phones manufactured by the company at the rate of Rs.25,000 each. What is the amount of trade discount?
questions.explanation: The price of 6 phones is 6 × 25,000 = ₹1,50,000, and 30% of it is ₹45,000.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the incorrectly spelt word in the following sentence. The government has ordered for the maintainance of the roads.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'maintenance'.

questions.text: Give one word substitution for : A person who is unsure about God’s existence
questions.explanation: An agnostic holds that God's existence cannot be known; an atheist denies it and a theist believes in God.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. If someone “babbles”, it means that they talk in a confused or excited way.
questions.explanation: To 'babble' is to talk rapidly and confusedly; its opposite is to be 'quiet'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined part in the following sentence. Everyone called the reporter “a daredevil” after he came back safely from the war zone.
questions.explanation: A daredevil is a person who takes bold risks: 'a fearless person'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given word. Illiterate
options: A person who cannot read and write
questions.explanation: 'Illiterate' describes a person who cannot read and write.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Radhika stood by Monica’s side “through thick and thin”.
options: Under easy situations wherein she could ensure Monica’s safety and security
In all the happy moments, personally spending most of her time
In the moments when Monica couldn’t complete some simple tasks
Under all conditions, no matter how challenging or difficult
questions.explanation: 'Through thick and thin' means under all conditions, however difficult.

questions.text: In the following sentence, four words are underlined out of which one word is misspelt. Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word. I felt absolutely (A) fit at the summit. My mind was absolutely clear.(B) I didn’t feel tired, I felt exhelarated. (C)It was a very clear sensation.(D)
questions.explanation: The underlined words are 'absolutely' (A), 'clear' (B), 'exhelarated' (C) and 'sensation' (D). (C) is misspelt: the word is 'exhilarated'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Martha made pancakes yesterday.
options: Pancakes had been made by Martha yesterday.
Pancakes were made by Martha yesterday.
Pancakes were being made by Martha yesterday.
Pancakes was made by Martha yesterday.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'made' becomes 'were made', plural to agree with 'pancakes'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in the brackets to fill in the blank. Akash went to ______ his school uniform. [sell]
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'sell' is 'buy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined word segment in the given sentence. Carnatic music is usually performed by a “small troupe of actors”, consisting of a principal performer, a melodic accompaniment, and a rhythm accompaniment.
questions.explanation: Carnatic music is performed by musicians, a principal performer with melodic and rhythmic accompanists, not by actors: an 'ensemble of musicians'.

questions.text: Choose the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word in the given sentence. The war was followed by a long period of “prosperity”.
questions.explanation: 'Prosperity' is success and wealth; of the options its opposite is 'failure'. 'Affluence' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. His approach was filled with such “perseverance” that it was difficult to overlook his merit.
questions.explanation: 'Perseverance' is persistence in spite of difficulty: 'doggedness'.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence and forms a meaningful sentence. In November, Lakshman fell (P) / with fever (Q) / seriously ill (R) and pneumonia (S).
questions.explanation: 'In November, Lakshman fell (P) seriously ill (R) with fever (Q) and pneumonia (S).'

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into five segments. The first segment has no error. Select the option that has the segment with the grammatical error. Due to the pandemic, / the prices of / medicines increased / every day since / last December.
questions.explanation: 'Since last December' needs the present perfect: 'medicines have increased' (or 'have been increasing') every day since last December.

questions.text: In the given question, a statement divided into different segments is given. Rearrange all the segments to form a coherent statement. O: also benefit from knowing P: there are several reasons Q: why even parents would R: more about how and why S: children do the things that they do
questions.explanation: 'There are several reasons (P) why even parents would (Q) also benefit from knowing (O) more about how and why (R) children do the things that they do (S).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Affirmative
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'affirmative' (saying yes) is 'negative'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who speaks less in a forum.
questions.explanation: A reticent person says little; 'loquacious' and 'gabby' mean the opposite.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase. An important person who represents his/her country in a foreign country
questions.explanation: An ambassador is a diplomat who represents his or her country in a foreign country.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. I will be gifted a fancy doll by them the next day.
options: They will gift me a fancy doll tomorrow.
They gift me a fancy doll the previous day.
They gifted me a fancy doll yesterday.
They are gifting me a fancy doll the next day.
questions.explanation: 'I will be gifted … by them' becomes 'They will gift me …', keeping the future tense; the other options change it. (This option also renders 'the next day' as 'tomorrow'.)

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. Identify the part that has an error. Select 'No error' if there is no error. Although the team had “trained diligently” “for months”, they “had still overwhelmed” by the opponent's unexpected tactics.
questions.explanation: The team was acted upon, so the verb must be passive: 'they had still been overwhelmed' (or 'they were still overwhelmed').

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. (1) _________ a letter came to inform them that Raka’s mother Tara had another breakdown and was in a nursing home in Geneva and that Raka’s grandmother Asha, (2) _________ seen another grandchild safely into the world, was flying to Switzerland to be with her, Nanda Kaul (3) _________ her lips, (4) _________ the blue sheets of paper with that distasteful sprawl (5) _________ them, and hid them in her desk.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'When a letter came …, Nanda Kaul pursed her lips': a time clause. 'Sooner' would need 'no sooner had'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. (1) _________ a letter came to inform them that Raka’s mother Tara had another breakdown and was in a nursing home in Geneva and that Raka’s grandmother Asha, (2) _________ seen another grandchild safely into the world, was flying to Switzerland to be with her, Nanda Kaul (3) _________ her lips, (4) _________ the blue sheets of paper with that distasteful sprawl (5) _________ them, and hid them in her desk.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Asha, having seen another grandchild safely into the world': the perfect participle for an action completed first.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. (1) _________ a letter came to inform them that Raka’s mother Tara had another breakdown and was in a nursing home in Geneva and that Raka’s grandmother Asha, (2) _________ seen another grandchild safely into the world, was flying to Switzerland to be with her, Nanda Kaul (3) _________ her lips, (4) _________ the blue sheets of paper with that distasteful sprawl (5) _________ them, and hid them in her desk.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: To 'purse' one's lips is to press them together in disapproval.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. (1) _________ a letter came to inform them that Raka’s mother Tara had another breakdown and was in a nursing home in Geneva and that Raka’s grandmother Asha, (2) _________ seen another grandchild safely into the world, was flying to Switzerland to be with her, Nanda Kaul (3) _________ her lips, (4) _________ the blue sheets of paper with that distasteful sprawl (5) _________ them, and hid them in her desk.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: She 'folded up' the sheets and then hid them; 'tucked away' and 'hid away' would repeat the hiding.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. (1) _________ a letter came to inform them that Raka’s mother Tara had another breakdown and was in a nursing home in Geneva and that Raka’s grandmother Asha, (2) _________ seen another grandchild safely into the world, was flying to Switzerland to be with her, Nanda Kaul (3) _________ her lips, (4) _________ the blue sheets of paper with that distasteful sprawl (5) _________ them, and hid them in her desk.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The handwriting's 'distasteful sprawl across them': it spread over the sheets.

questions.text: The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if all the letters in the word BINDER are arranged in English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: BINDER in alphabetical order is B D E I N R. B (1st) and R (6th) keep their places: two letters.

questions.text: In the following series, only one letter-cluster is incorrect. Select the incorrect letter-cluster. YCG IMQ SVZ CGK MQU
questions.explanation: In each correct cluster the letters move +4, +4 (YCG, IMQ, CGK, MQU), and each cluster starts 10 letters after the one before. The third should be SWA; SVZ moves +3, then +4.

questions.text: Three of the following four options are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that does NOT belong to that group? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 540 – 188 – 128, 81 – 101 – 92 and 90 – 22 – 12 the first number is 9 times the difference of the other two (9 × 60, 9 × 9, 9 × 10). In 72 – 284 – 266, 9 × 18 = 162, not 72.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 342 × 18 + 79 − 45 ÷ 3 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 342 ÷ 18 − 79 + 45 × 3 = 19 − 79 + 135 = 75.

questions.text: Two sets of numbers are given below. In each set of numbers, certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number result(s) in the second number. Similarly, certain mathematical operation(s) on the second number result(s) in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in the given sets? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 18 – 36 – 72 – 107; 15 – 30 – 60– 95
questions.explanation: Each set doubles twice and then adds 35: 18 → 36 → 72 → 107 and 15 → 30 → 60 → 95. Likewise 22 → 44 → 88 → 123.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? IMHP, MPJQ, QSLR, UVNS, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +4 (I, M, Q, U, Y), second letters +3 (M, P, S, V, Y), third letters +2 (H, J, L, N, P) and fourth letters +1 (P, Q, R, S, T): YYPT.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FACED’ is written as ‘GZDDE’ and ‘VACAY’ is written as ‘WZDZZ’. How will ‘LABOR’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, −1, +1, −1, +1: FACED → GZDDE and VACAY → WZDZZ. So LABOR → MZCNS.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'FIVE' is written as '12184410' and FOUR is written as '12304236'. How will 'THREE' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as twice its position in the alphabet: F, I, V, E → 12, 18, 44, 10. So T, H, R, E, E → 40, 16, 36, 10, 10: 4016361010.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All pages are diaries. Some diaries are books. All books are notebooks. Conclusions: I. No page is a notebook. II. All pages are notebooks. III. All diaries being notebooks is a possibility.
options: Both conclusion I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: Only the diaries that are books are certainly notebooks, and pages may or may not be among them, so neither I nor II follows. Nothing rules out every diary being a book, and so a notebook: III follows.

questions.text: Select the word-pair that best represents a similar relationship to the one expressed in the pair of words given below. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Virus : Parasite
questions.explanation: A virus is a kind of parasite, as the amaltas is a kind of tree.

questions.text: Select the number from the given options to complete the series. 25, 30, 40, 55, 75, ___
questions.explanation: The differences grow by 5 (+5, +10, +15, +20), so the next is +25: 75 + 25 = 100.

questions.text: ‘WISK’ is related to ‘DRHP’ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, ‘LENT’ is related to ‘OVMG’. To which of the following is ‘BANG’ related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite letter in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on): W→D, I→R, S→H, K→P and L→O, E→V, N→M, T→G. So B→Y, A→Z, N→M, G→T: YZMT.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 247 ÷ 13 + 16 × 3 − 148 = 119
The position(s) of how many letters will remain unchanged if all the letters in the word ‘ENTOMB’ are arranged in English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: ENTOMB in alphabetical order is B E M N O T. Position by position (E/B, N/E, T/M, O/N, M/O, B/T) no letter stays where it was.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the given sets. (213, 157), (185, 129) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g., 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: In each set the second number is 56 less than the first: 213 − 56 = 157 and 185 − 56 = 129. Likewise 164 − 56 = 108.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is 4 related to 2 if ‘4 + 3 ÷ 2 ÷ 1 − 5’?
questions.explanation: 4 is the mother of 3, and 3 is the father of 2. So 4 is 2's father's mother.

questions.text: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that DOES NOT belong to that group? (Note: The odd man out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
questions.explanation: In FDZ, JHD and AYU the letters move back 2, then back 4 (counting round from A to Z). In KJE they move back 1, then back 5.

questions.text: The organisms that do not have a defined nucleus or organelles are classified in to _______ Kingdom.
questions.explanation: Monera (bacteria and blue-green algae) are prokaryotes, with no defined nucleus or membrane-bound organelles. Fungi, Protista and Plantae are all eukaryotes.

questions.text: Kathakali, one of the classical dances of India, is predominantly performed in which of the following states of India?
questions.explanation: Kathakali, the dance-drama with elaborate make-up and costumes, is the classical dance of Kerala.

questions.text: In 2002, Zakir Hussain became the youngest percussionist to be honoured with which award?
questions.explanation: Zakir Hussain was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2002, after the Padma Shri in 1988.

questions.text: Microbes like Rhizobium, Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter are used for:
questions.explanation: Rhizobium fixes atmospheric nitrogen in the root nodules of legumes, Nitrosomonas turns ammonia into nitrite and Nitrobacter turns nitrite into nitrate: all steps of the nitrogen cycle.

questions.text: Which is the National Mission for Financial Inclusion to ensure access to financial services, namely, a basic savings and deposits accounts, remittance, credit, insurance, pension in an affordable manner?
options: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana, launched in August 2014, is the National Mission for Financial Inclusion.

questions.text: What is net investment?
options: Sum of all the investments in a country
questions.explanation: Net investment is gross investment less depreciation, the part of the capital stock used up during the year.

questions.text: In which state/UT is the Hemis festival celebrated?
questions.explanation: The Hemis festival is held at Hemis Monastery in Ladakh to mark the birth anniversary of Guru Padmasambhava.

questions.text: A javelin thrown by an athlete is in ________ motion.
questions.explanation: A thrown javelin follows a curved path, so its motion is curvilinear; rectilinear motion is along a straight line.

questions.text: Who among the following is the world renowned exponent of the bamboo flute?
questions.explanation: Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is the best-known exponent of the bansuri, the bamboo flute. M.S. Subbulakshmi was a Carnatic vocalist, Ravi Shankar a sitar player and Bismillah Khan a shehnai player.

questions.text: The magnificent Kailasa temple at Ellora was built during the reign of which Rashtrakuta king?
questions.explanation: The Kailasa temple at Ellora, cut from a single rock, was built under the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I in the 8th century.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides that ‘there shall be a Vice President of India’?
questions.explanation: Article 63 reads 'There shall be a Vice-President of India'.

questions.text: Purvanchal Himalayas does NOT comprise of:
questions.explanation: The Purvanchal hills comprise the Patkai Bum, Naga hills, Manipur hills and Mizo hills. The Pir Panjal range is in the western Himalayas, in Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh.

questions.text: Which of the following plays was NOT written by Harshavardhana?
questions.explanation: Harshavardhana wrote the Sanskrit plays Nagananda, Ratnavali and Priyadarshika; 'Vikramorvasiyam' is Kalidasa's.

questions.text: In August 2022, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment launched the ________ scheme, with an aim to provide comprehensive rehabilitation services to people engaged in begging in 75 municipalities.
questions.explanation: Under SMILE-75, launched in August 2022 as part of the SMILE scheme (Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise), 75 municipal corporations rehabilitate people engaged in begging.

questions.text: A student, on his school assignment, is taking a session on how to make compost at home for using it at a park. Which fundamental duty is he performing?
options: To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity
To protect and improve the natural environment
To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
questions.explanation: Making compost and using it in a park helps protect and improve the natural environment, the duty in Article 51A(g).

questions.text: India won the ICC Men Cricket World Cup for the first time in which of the following years?
questions.explanation: India first won the Men's Cricket World Cup in 1983, under Kapil Dev, beating the West Indies in the final at Lord's.

questions.text: Calculate the oxidation number of ‘S’ in H₂S₂O₇ .
questions.explanation: With H at +1 and O at −2: 2(+1) + 2x + 7(−2) = 0, so 2x = 12 and x = +6.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an amendment made to the Airport Economic Regulatory Authority (AERA) Amendment Act, 2021?
options: The government can call any airport a major airport just by notification.
A major airport is one which has an annual traffic of minimum 35 lakh passengers.
The government will club together profit-making and loss-making airports.
The government can offer airports as a package in PPP mode to the prospective bidders.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the 35-lakh threshold, which came in with the 2019 amendment (raising it from 15 lakh). The 2021 amendment let the government group airports, profit-making with loss-making, notify the group as a major airport and offer it as a package for PPP bids. (The power to notify any airport as a major airport was also in the Act before 2021.)

questions.text: In which year did India make its Olympic debut in hockey?
questions.explanation: India first played Olympic hockey at Amsterdam in 1928, and won the gold medal.

questions.text: Who among the following was selected as the Sherpa for India’s G20 hosted in 2022-23?
questions.explanation: Amitabh Kant, former CEO of NITI Aayog, was appointed India's G20 Sherpa in July 2022, succeeding Piyush Goyal.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: With reference to Sepoy Mutiny of 1857, on which of the following dates did the soldiers at Meerut start their journey to Delhi?
questions.explanation: The sepoys at Meerut rose on 10 May 1857 and set out for Delhi, which they reached the next day.

questions.text: The green revolution technology resulted in an increase in production of cereal production from 72.4 million tons in 1965-66 to ________ million tons in 1978-79.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 131.9 million tonnes, India's total foodgrain output (cereals and pulses together) in 1978-79, up from about 72 million tonnes in 1965-66.

questions.text: Identify the oldest iron and steel company of India from the following options.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives TISCO, registered in 1907 at Jamshedpur. IISCO was formed in 1918, and the Mysore Iron Works at Bhadravati, later named after Visvesvaraya, in 1923. (In 1936 IISCO took over the Kulti works of the Bengal Iron Company, whose history goes back to the 1870s.)

questions.text: Which of the following is the largest artificial lake of Asia?
questions.explanation: Of these, only Bhopal's Upper Lake (Bhojtal), traditionally credited to the Paramara king Bhoja in the 11th century, is man-made, and SSC's key gives it; it is often called Asia's largest artificial lake, though reservoirs such as Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar (Rihand) are larger. Chilika is a natural lagoon, and Dal and Naini are natural lakes.

questions.text: Which digits should come in place * and $, respectively, if the number 72864*$ is divisible by both 8 and 5?
questions.explanation: Divisible by both 5 and 8, the number must end in 0, so $ = 0. The last three digits, 4*0, must then be divisible by 8: of the options, 440 is (8 × 55), so * = 4.

questions.text: A shopkeeper marked an article at ₹5,000. The shopkeeper allows successive discounts of 20%, 15% and 10%. The selling price of the article is:
questions.explanation: Successive discounts leave 0.8 × 0.85 × 0.9 = 0.612 of the price: ₹5,000 × 0.612 = ₹3,060.

questions.text: The measures of the three angles of a triangle are in the ratio 17 : 13 : 15. Find the positive difference between the greatest and the smallest of these three angles.
questions.explanation: 17 + 13 + 15 = 45 parts make 180°, so one part is 4°. The difference between the greatest and the smallest is (17 − 13) × 4° = 16°.

questions.text: A certain sum of money becomes seven times itself when invested at a certain rate of simple interest, in 14 years. How much time (in years, rounded off to 2 decimal places) will it take to become 18 times itself at the same rate?
questions.explanation: Becoming 7 times itself means interest of 6 times the sum in 14 years. Becoming 18 times needs interest of 17 times the sum: 14 × 17/6 = 39.67 years.

questions.text: In a triangle PQR, S is a point on the side QR such that PS⊥QR, then which of the following options is true?
questions.explanation: By Pythagoras in the right triangles PSQ and PSR: PQ² = PS² + QS² and PR² = PS² + SR². Subtracting, PQ² − QS² = PR² − SR², so PR² + QS² = PQ² + SR².

questions.text: M and N walk along a circular track. They start at 5:00 a.m. from the same point in the opposite directions. M and N walk at a speed of 5 rounds per hour and 2 rounds per hour, respectively. How many times will they cross each other before 6.30 a.m. on the same day?
questions.explanation: Walking in opposite directions they close 5 + 2 = 7 rounds an hour on each other and cross each time they close one round. In 1.5 hours that is 10.5 rounds: 10 crossings.

questions.text: Two pipes, A and B, can fill a tank in 10 minutes and 20 minutes, respectively. The pipe C can empty the tank in 30 minutes. All the three pipes are opened at a time in the beginning. However, pipe C is closed 2 minutes before the tank is filled. In what time, will the tank be full (in minutes)?
questions.explanation: If the tank fills in t minutes, C is open for t − 2: t/10 + t/20 − (t − 2)/30 = 1. Multiplying by 60: 6t + 3t − 2t + 4 = 60, so t = 8.

questions.text: The incomes of P, Q and R are in the ratio 10 : 12 : 9 and their expenditures are in the ratio 12 : 15 : 8. If Q saves 25% of his income, then what is the ratio of the savings of P, Q and R?
questions.explanation: Let the incomes be 10k, 12k, 9k and the expenditures 12m, 15m, 8m. Q saves 3k, so 15m = 9k and m = 0.6k. Savings: 10k − 7.2k = 2.8k, 3k and 9k − 4.8k = 4.2k, i.e. 14 : 15 : 21.

questions.text: The average of 12 numbers is 48. The average of the first 5 numbers is 45 and the average of next 4 numbers is 52. If the 10th number is 10 less than the 11th number and is 5 more than the 12th number, then the average of the 11th and 12th numbers is:
questions.explanation: The last three numbers total 576 − 225 − 208 = 143. With the 10th = a, the 11th is a + 10 and the 12th a − 5, so 3a + 5 = 143 and a = 46. The 11th and 12th are 56 and 41: average 48.5.

questions.text: Raj divides ₹1,200 in the ratio 2 : 1 : 3 among three of his friends. The amount equal to the sum of three times the largest share and two times the smallest share is:
In triangles ABC and DEF, AB = FD and ∠A = ∠D. The two triangles are congruent by SAS criterion if:
questions.explanation: For SAS the equal angles must lie between the equal sides. ∠A lies between AB and AC, and ∠D between DF and DE; with AB = FD already, AC = DE is needed.

questions.text: If 28.9 : x :: x : 36.1, and x > 0, then find the value of x.
questions.explanation: x is the mean proportional: x² = 28.9 × 36.1 = (17² × 19²)/100, so x = 17 × 19/10 = 32.3.

questions.text: A payment of ₹120 is made with ₹10, ₹5 and ₹2 coins. A total of 25 coins are used. Which of the following is the number of ₹10 coins used in the payment?
questions.explanation: With a, b and c coins of ₹10, ₹5 and ₹2: 10a + 5b + 2c = 120 and a + b + c = 25, so 8a + 3b = 70. Of the options only a = 8 gives a whole number of ₹5 coins: b = 2 and c = 15 (80 + 10 + 30 = 120).

questions.text: Identity the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Secure
questions.explanation: To 'secure' something is to make it safe from harm; to 'attack' it is the opposite. 'Save' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Acquiesce
questions.explanation: To 'acquiesce' is to accept or agree without protest: to 'concur'. 'Thwart', 'cease' and 'desist' do not mean agreeing.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. In Indian mythology, most of the Asuras wish to be “never able to die”.
questions.explanation: 'Immortal' means never able to die. 'Invincible' means impossible to defeat, and 'impervious' unaffected.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. The genuine beliefs, though not unconsciously acquired by most children; and even if they depart from these beliefs in later life B. Something of them remains deeply implanted, ready to emerge in a time of stress of crisis C. The importance of education in forming character and opinion is very great and well recognised by all D. Education is, as a rule, the strongest force on the side of what exists and again fundamental change
questions.explanation: C states the importance of education in forming character and opinion; A, on the beliefs children acquire, and B, 'something of them remains', develop it; D concludes that education is the strongest force on the side of what exists: CABD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. In my new office, all employees were different, so I felt like a “fish out of water”.
questions.explanation: To feel like 'a fish out of water' is to feel uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank. During Covid times, many organisations made ________(sentimental) appeals to raise funds for migrant workers.
questions.explanation: 'Mawkish' means sentimental, often excessively so. 'Practical' and 'cynical' point the other way, and 'sincere' means genuine.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. If I “was the queen”, I would give a handsome sum towards education.
questions.explanation: An imagined, unreal condition takes the subjunctive 'were': 'If I were the queen, I would give ...'

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'exhilarate'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice. Sonam does not like bananas.
options: Bananas had not been liked by Sonam.
Bananas have not been liked by Sonam.
Bananas are not liked by Sonam.
Banana is not liked by Sonam.
questions.explanation: The simple present 'does not like' becomes 'are not liked', agreeing with the plural 'bananas': 'Bananas are not liked by Sonam.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence. His “ambition” in life is to become a happy and satisfied man.
questions.explanation: 'Ambition' is a strong desire to achieve something; of the options 'eagerness' comes closest. 'Apathy' is its opposite.

questions.text: Read the sentence carefully and select the most suitable idiom to fill in the blank. The renowned publisher decided to withdraw a book from the market. No one was interested in the book as the arguments presented were ____________.
questions.explanation: 'Beside the mark' means irrelevant, missing the point, which is why no one was interested in the book.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. Mrs. Sreelakshmi’s / musical intelligence / is superior than / Mrs. Suma’s.
questions.explanation: 'Superior' takes 'to', not 'than': 'is superior to Mrs. Suma's'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence. He is an “atheist”, although he respects everyone’s belief.
options: One who does not believe in God
questions.explanation: An 'atheist' is one who does not believe in God; one who does is a 'theist'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Receive
questions.explanation: To 'receive' someone is to welcome or admit them; to 'exile' them is to send them away. 'Admit' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Gourav was “no good” than a foolish person.
questions.explanation: 'Than' needs a comparative: 'no better than a foolish person'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice Someone has taken my secret diary.
options: My secret diary has to be taken by someone.
My secret diary had been taken by someone.
My secret diary will have been taken by someone.
My secret diary has been taken by someone.
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'has taken' becomes 'has been taken': 'My secret diary has been taken by someone.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. That which cannot be conquered
questions.explanation: 'Invincible' means too strong to be conquered or defeated. 'Ineffable' means too great to be described, and 'indelible' impossible to remove.

questions.text: Select the option that corrects the error in the given sentence. He ran quick to catch the bus.
questions.explanation: The verb 'ran' needs the adverb 'quickly', not the adjective 'quick'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word-substitute for the given group of words. “A false idea or belief”
questions.explanation: A fallacy is a mistaken idea or belief. 'Atrophy' is wasting away, 'reticence' is reserve, and 'entropy' is disorder.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The beginning of the story is (1)______ in its presentation but (2)______ the style eases out and becomes haunting in its simplicity. The author brings out the human elements in his story.
