This common element of sympathy and sacrifice is given a new (3)_____ by the old artist who shows by his last desperate act that one can be a hero for one day if only one cares (4)______. O Henry’s treatment of his material is balanced and controlled, a fine (5)______ of humour and pathos.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The opening is 'quaint', attractively unusual or old-fashioned, in its presentation, in contrast with the simplicity that follows.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The beginning of the story is (1)______ in its presentation but (2)______ the style eases out and becomes haunting in its simplicity. The author brings out the human elements in his story. This common element of sympathy and sacrifice is given a new (3)_____ by the old artist who shows by his last desperate act that one can be a hero for one day if only one cares (4)______. O Henry’s treatment of his material is balanced and controlled, a fine (5)______ of humour and pathos.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'But gradually the style eases out': the change comes little by little as the story goes on.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The beginning of the story is (1)______ in its presentation but (2)______ the style eases out and becomes haunting in its simplicity. The author brings out the human elements in his story. This common element of sympathy and sacrifice is given a new (3)_____ by the old artist who shows by his last desperate act that one can be a hero for one day if only one cares (4)______. O Henry’s treatment of his material is balanced and controlled, a fine (5)______ of humour and pathos.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The old artist gives the common theme of sympathy and sacrifice a new 'dimension', a new aspect.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The beginning of the story is (1)______ in its presentation but (2)______ the style eases out and becomes haunting in its simplicity. The author brings out the human elements in his story. This common element of sympathy and sacrifice is given a new (3)_____ by the old artist who shows by his last desperate act that one can be a hero for one day if only one cares (4)______. O Henry’s treatment of his material is balanced and controlled, a fine (5)______ of humour and pathos.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'If only one cares enough': 'enough' fits after the verb; 'tough', 'through' and 'though' do not.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The beginning of the story is (1)______ in its presentation but (2)______ the style eases out and becomes haunting in its simplicity. The author brings out the human elements in his story. This common element of sympathy and sacrifice is given a new (3)_____ by the old artist who shows by his last desperate act that one can be a hero for one day if only one cares (4)______. O Henry’s treatment of his material is balanced and controlled, a fine (5)______ of humour and pathos.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'A fine blend of humour and pathos': a mixture of the two.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question marks (?) in the given series? 16, 36, 64, ?, ?, 196, 256, 324
questions.explanation: The terms are the squares of the even numbers: 4², 6², 8², 10², 12², 14², 16², 18². The missing terms are 100 and 144.

questions.text: Two sets of numbers are given below. In each set of numbers, certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number result(s) in the second number. Similarly, certain mathematical operation(s) on the second number result(s) in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in the given sets? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 10 – 12 – 8 – 15; 12 – 14 – 10 – 19
questions.explanation: In each set: add 2, subtract 4, then double and subtract 1: 10 → 12 → 8 → 15 and 12 → 14 → 10 → 19. Likewise 11 → 13 → 9 → 17.

questions.text: Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the letter-cluster that DOES NOT belong to that group? (Note: The odd man out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter-cluster.)
questions.explanation: In DGK, HKO and MPT the letters move +3, then +4. ACG moves +2, then +4, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (11, 16.5, 22) (14.5, 20, 25.5) (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is 5.5 more than the one before it: 11, 16.5, 22 and 14.5, 20, 25.5. Likewise 18, 23.5, 29.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? HPL, KLQ, NHV, QDA, TZF, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +3 (H, K, N, Q, T, so next W); second letters −4 (P, L, H, D, Z, so V); third letters +5 (L, Q, V, A, F, so K): WVK.

questions.text: In a certain code language, A + B means ‘A is the son of B’, A − B means ‘A is the wife of B’, A × B means ‘A is the brother of B’ and A ÷ B means ‘A is the daughter of B’. Based on the above, how is P related to R if ‘P × S ÷ M − T + R’?
questions.explanation: T + R: T is R's son. M − T: M is T's wife. S ÷ M: S is M's daughter, and so T's. P × S: P is S's brother, so T's son. P is R's son's son.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All cards are postcards. Some postcards are books. All books are novels. Conclusions: I. Some postcards are novels. II. No card is a book. III. All cards are novels.
options: Only II and III conclusion follow
Only I and II conclusion follow
questions.explanation: The postcards that are books are novels, so some postcards are novels (I). Nothing says whether any card is a book or a novel, so neither II nor III follows.

questions.text: ‘NGRP’ is related to ‘JCNL’ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, ‘FKLT’ is related to ‘BGHP’. To which of the following is ‘SQUO’ related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places back: N → J, G → C, R → N, P → L and F → B, K → G, L → H, T → P. So SQUO → OMQK.

questions.text: Three of the following numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the odd one out. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 12 – 7 – 209, 19 – 11 – 330 and 15 – 9 – 264 the third number is 11 times the sum of the first two (19 × 11, 30 × 11, 24 × 11). For 23 – 8 that would be 31 × 11 = 341, not 343.

questions.text: Which of the following operations should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 12 + 12 − 4 × 4 ÷ 2 = 22
Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. E_GHEI_GELK_ _OME
questions.explanation: With F, I, F, E in the blanks the series reads EFGH EIIG ELKF EOME: each block starts with E, the second letters move +3 (F, I, L, O), the third +2 (G, I, K, M) and the fourth −1 (H, G, F, E).

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘talk to me’ is coded as ‘aq yt bl’ and ‘do not talk’ is coded as ‘yt me wc’. What is the code for ‘talk’ in that language?
questions.explanation: 'talk' is the only word in both sentences and 'yt' the only code in both, so talk = yt.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 16 ÷ 4 + 8 × 8 − 4 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 16 × 4 − 8 ÷ 8 + 4 = 64 − 1 + 4 = 67.

questions.text: 346 is related to 245 by certain logic. Following the same logic, 580 is related to 479. To which of the following is 613 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is 101 less than the first: 346 − 101 = 245 and 580 − 101 = 479. Likewise 613 − 101 = 512.

questions.text: Select the word-pair that best represents a similar relationship to the one expressed in the pair of words given below. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Duleep Trophy : Cricket
questions.explanation: The Duleep Trophy is a cricket tournament, as the Agha Khan Cup is a hockey tournament. The Durand Cup is a football tournament, not a cricket one.

questions.text: Each vowel in the word ‘STAMINA’ is changed to the preceding letter in the English alphabetical order and each consonant is changed to the following letter in the English alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English alphabetical order between the letter which is the third from the right and the fourth from the left in the group of letters thus formed?
questions.explanation: STAMINA becomes T U Z N H O Z. The third letter from the right is H and the fourth from the left is N; between them come I, J, K, L and M: five letters.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘can we play’ is coded as ‘ae tc nx’ and ‘play in school’ is coded as ‘tc rm ef’. How is ‘play’ coded in that language?
questions.explanation: 'play' is the only word in both sentences and 'tc' the only code in both, so play = tc.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BOOK’ is written as ‘ZNNI’ and ‘SHOP’ is written as ‘QFNN’. How will ‘NOTES’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Consonants move 2 places back and vowels 1: BOOK → ZNNI and SHOP → QFNN. So NOTES → LNRDQ.

questions.text: Chand Bardai’s famous literary work ________, mentions Prithviraj Chauhan‘s love story and heroic deeds.
questions.explanation: Chand Bardai, the court poet of Prithviraj Chauhan, wrote the 'Prithviraj Raso', an epic of the king's life, love and battles.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who established Shantiniketan and when?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore started his school at Santiniketan in 1901; it grew into Visva-Bharati University in 1921. The ashram there had been set up by his father, Debendranath Tagore, in 1863, not 1915.

questions.text: In which year was the Digital India mission launched?
questions.explanation: The Digital India programme was launched on 1 July 2015.

questions.text: In July 2020, which state initiated the 'Ashirwad Scheme' to extend financial support for a daughter's marriage who belongs to a family earning a lower income?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Punjab, which runs the Ashirwad Scheme for the marriage of daughters of low-income families.

questions.text: Hindustani singer Pandit Venkatesh Kumar was honoured with 'Kalidas Samman-2022' by which state government?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Madhya Pradesh, whose government confers the Kalidas Samman, a national award for the arts that includes music.

questions.text: Which of the following institutes was founded by Mrinalini Sarabhai who was a Bharatanatyam and Kathakali dancer?
options: Sri Thyagaraja College of Music and Dance
questions.explanation: Mrinalini Sarabhai founded the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts in Ahmedabad in 1949.

questions.text: Which of the following hills is located in the Eastern Ghats?
questions.explanation: The Shevaroy hills, around Yercaud in Tamil Nadu, are part of the Eastern Ghats. Anamudi is in the Western Ghats, and the Khasi and Naga hills are in the north-east.

questions.text: Who among the following players is related to table tennis?
questions.explanation: Manika Batra is a table tennis player. Pankaj Advani plays billiards and snooker, K Srikanth badminton, and Manish Narwal is a para shooter.

questions.text: What are the five Fs of indirect transmission?
options: Fruit, fingers, flu, food and fluid
Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fluid
Flies, fingers, friends, food and fruit
Flies, fingers, fomites, food and fruit
questions.explanation: Faeco-oral infections spread indirectly through flies, fingers, fomites (contaminated objects), food and fluid (water).

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of public sector industry in India?
questions.explanation: Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited is owned by the Government of India; Tata Steel, Bajaj Auto and Dabur are private companies.

questions.text: The Election Laws Amendment Bill passed in the Parliament recently seeks to implement certain electoral reforms. One of them is the eligibility date. Till now, only one date – 1 January was considered for deciding eligibility with respect to age. What reform does the Bill seek in this regard?
options: Eliminating the idea of eligibility date – enrolment throughout the year
Introducing three dates – 1 January, 1 May, 1 September
Introducing four dates – 1 January, 1 April, 1 July, 1 October
Introducing two dates – 1 January and 1 June
questions.explanation: The Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021 gives four qualifying dates a year for enrolment: 1 January, 1 April, 1 July and 1 October.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty of the Indian citizens?
options: To cherish and follow the noble ideas that inspired our national struggle for freedom.
To develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
questions.explanation: Article 51A has no compulsory national service; it asks citizens to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so. The other three are Fundamental Duties.

questions.text: ______ leaves are used to make bidis.
questions.explanation: Bidis are rolled in the leaves of the tendu tree (Diospyros melanoxylon), a minor forest produce of central India.

questions.text: Buddhadev Dasgupta is famous for playing which of the following musical instruments?
questions.explanation: Pandit Buddhadev Das Gupta was a leading sarod player.

questions.text: In which of the following years was Pro Kabaddi League established in India?
questions.explanation: The Pro Kabaddi League began in 2014.

questions.text: According to Census of India 2011, what is the gap between male and female literacy rate in India?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 put male literacy at 82.14% and female literacy at 65.46%: a gap of 16.68 percentage points.

questions.text: In which form of exchange are goods used as medium of exchange?
questions.explanation: In barter, goods are exchanged directly for other goods, without money.

questions.text: What is the product formed when zinc and sulphuric acid react?
questions.explanation: Zinc displaces hydrogen from dilute sulphuric acid: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂.

questions.text: In the state legislative assembly, the Money bill can be introduced with the prior permission of __________.
questions.explanation: Under Article 207 a Money Bill can be introduced in a state legislature only on the recommendation of the Governor, and only in the Legislative Assembly.

questions.text: Which of the following gases emits red light when electricity is passed through it?
questions.explanation: Neon glows red-orange when a current passes through it, as in neon signs.

questions.text: The Vedangas are Hindu auxiliary disciplines that originated in ancient times and are linked to the study of the Vedas. These are _________ in number.
questions.explanation: The six Vedangas are Shiksha (phonetics), Kalpa (ritual), Vyakarana (grammar), Nirukta (etymology), Chhandas (metre) and Jyotisha (astronomy).

questions.text: Gangaur Festival, Pushkar Fair, Nagaur Fair and Urs Fair are the popular fairs and festivals of which state?
questions.explanation: Gangaur, the Pushkar and Nagaur fairs and the Urs at Ajmer are all held in Rajasthan.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following freedom fighters is known as ‘Deshbandhu’?
questions.explanation: Chittaranjan Das was called 'Deshbandhu', friend of the nation.

questions.text: What was the actual growth rate of the first five-year plan?
questions.explanation: The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) aimed at 2.1% annual growth and achieved about 3.6%.

questions.text: The average of the squares of the first 46 natural numbers is
questions.explanation: The sum of the squares of 1 to n is n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6, so their average is (n + 1)(2n + 1)/6 = 47 × 93/6 = 4371/6 = 728.5.

questions.text: The MP of an article was Rs.180 and it was sold at a discount of 15%, the discount in Rs. is:
In ΔDEF, the bisector of ∠D intersects side EF at point N. If DE = 36 cm, DF = 40 cm and EF = 38 cm, then the length (in cm) of NF is ________.
questions.explanation: The bisector of ∠D divides EF in the ratio DE : DF = 36 : 40 = 9 : 10, so NF = 38 × 10/19 = 20 cm.

questions.text: Find the area of a sector with an arc length of 44 cm, which subtends a central angle of 30°.
questions.explanation: Arc length = (30/360) × 2πr = πr/6 = 44, so r = 84 cm (π = 22/7). Area = ½ × arc length × radius = ½ × 44 × 84 = 1848 cm².

questions.text: A thief pursued by a policeman was 150 m ahead at the start. If the ratio of the speed of the policeman to that of the thief was 5 : 4, then how far (distance in metres) could the thief go before he is caught by the policeman?
questions.explanation: In the time the policeman runs 5 m the thief runs 4 m, so the policeman gains 1 m. To make up 150 m, the thief runs 150 × 4 = 600 m.

questions.text: The ratio between male and female members in a club is 2 : 3. If the number of male members is increased by 200, the ratio becomes 5 : 6. How many female members are there in the club?
questions.explanation: Let there be 2x men and 3x women. (2x + 200) : 3x = 5 : 6 gives 12x + 1200 = 15x, so x = 400 and there are 1200 female members.

questions.text: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 48 minutes and 66 minutes, respectively. If both the pipes are opened simultaneously, then after how many minutes should pipe B be closed so that the tank gets filled in 32 minutes?
questions.explanation: In 32 minutes A fills 32/48 = 2/3 of the tank, so B must fill the other 1/3: 66/3 = 22 minutes.

questions.text: Every month, a man consumes 20 kg of rice and 8 kg of wheat. The price of rice is 20% of the price of wheat, resulting in a total expenditure of ₹300 per month for rice and wheat combined. If the price of wheat is increased by 20%, what percentage reduction in rice consumption is needed to maintain the same expenditure of ₹300? (Given that price of rice and consumption of wheat is constant.)
questions.explanation: With wheat at ₹w a kg and rice at 0.2w: 20 × 0.2w + 8w = 12w = 300, so wheat costs ₹25 and rice ₹5. At ₹30, 8 kg of wheat costs ₹240, leaving ₹60 for 12 kg of rice instead of 20: a cut of 8/20 = 40%.

questions.text: In triangle ABC, the length of side BC is 2 cm less than twice the length of side AB. The length of side AC exceeds the length of side AB by 10 cm. The perimeter of the triangle is 40 cm. Determine the length (in cm) of the smallest side of the triangle.
questions.explanation: With AB = x: BC = 2x − 2 and AC = x + 10, so 4x + 8 = 40 and x = 8. The sides are 8, 14 and 18 cm.

questions.text: From a point T, the length of the tangent to a circle is 32 cm and the distance of T from the centre is 40 cm. The diameter (in cm) of the circle is:
questions.explanation: The radius is perpendicular to the tangent: r = √(40² − 32²) = √576 = 24 cm, so the diameter is 48 cm.

questions.text: Two cylinders have the radii of their bases in the ratio 4 : 5 and their heights are in the ratio 5 : 7. Find the ratio of their curved surface areas.
questions.explanation: Curved surface area = 2πrh, so the ratio is (4 × 5) : (5 × 7) = 20 : 35 = 4 : 7.

questions.text: In a garden, there are 6 daisy plants the first year. Each year, a gardener adds 3 new daisy plants. He has 26 jasmine plants the first year and loses 2 each year. When will the number of daisy plants equal to the number of jasmine plants after the first year?
questions.explanation: After k more years there are 6 + 3k daisy plants and 26 − 2k jasmine plants. 6 + 3k = 26 − 2k gives k = 4: 18 of each.

questions.text: Which of following numbers is NOT divisible by 11?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 11 when its alternate digit sums differ by a multiple of 11. For 128041: (1 + 0 + 2) − (4 + 8 + 1) = −10. The others give −11 (109153), 0 (5445) and 11 (80124).

questions.text: For the following equations, what are the values of a and b to have infinitely many solutions? ax + by = 2; 3x - (5 - 2a)y = 6
questions.explanation: Infinitely many solutions need a/3 = b/(−(5 − 2a)) = 2/6. So a = 1, and b = −(5 − 2)/3 = −1.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. He had ________ the ________ into smaller clips.
questions.explanation: 'Had' takes the past participle 'clipped'; the object is a noun, 'clipping' (a piece cut from a film or recording).

questions.text: Select the sentence that does NOT have a spelling error.
options: The focus of the exibition is to reinforce versatility and creative thinking.
The insouciance of the rock star considering the importance of the occasion, came as a shock to the audience who expected stressful moments.
The artist received recognition for her impressive etchings, buclic landscapes, and recreation of natural scenes around her.
The paintings are structured chronologically, starting from cubism to surealism.
questions.explanation: The other sentences misspell 'exhibition', 'bucolic' and 'surrealism'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. My sisters “wished me good luck” before I went on the stage to sing.
options: Told me to break an arm
Told me to break the ice
Told me to sit on the fence
Told me to break a leg
questions.explanation: 'Break a leg' is said to a performer before going on stage, to wish them good luck.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The drug pedlar was arrested by the narcotics team.
options: The narcotics team arrest the drug pedlar.
The narcotics team has arrested the drug pedlar.
The narcotics team was arrested the drug pedlar.
The narcotics team arrested the drug pedlar.
questions.explanation: 'Was arrested by' is simple past passive, so the active is simple past: 'The narcotics team arrested the drug pedlar.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. Many people love to visit “enchanting” hills.
questions.explanation: 'Enchanting' means delightfully charming: 'alluring'.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. A. needs to be B. the shelf in C. a piece of wood D. the kitchen E. need to buy F. replaced, so I will
questions.explanation: 'The shelf in (B) the kitchen (D) needs to be (A) replaced, so I will (F) need to buy (E) a piece of wood (C).'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The list of subjects to be discussed at a meeting
questions.explanation: An agenda is the list of items to be discussed at a meeting; the minutes record what was said.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. She has _______ (witty) remarks about everything.
questions.explanation: 'Witty' means cleverly amusing; its opposite is 'unamusing'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Paralysed
questions.explanation: 'Paralysed' means unable to move through illness or injury. Of the options only 'healthy' points the other way; 'stifled' is close in meaning.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an adverbial usage error. Mr. Arun / will pay dear / for his / financial mistake.
questions.explanation: With 'pay' the adverb should be 'dearly': 'Mr. Arun will pay dearly for his financial mistake.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. Listening to the same lecture everyday appeared very ___________ to him. (boring)
questions.explanation: 'Monotonous' means dull through sameness: boring.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We have postponed this movie outing too many times, so we are going tomorrow, come _____ or shine.
questions.explanation: 'Come rain or shine' means whatever happens.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. O. went P. yesterday Q. we R. to the S. park
questions.explanation: 'We went to the park yesterday': QORSP.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Repulse
questions.explanation: To 'repulse' is to drive back: to 'repel'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. One must be confident of winning and gaining one’s goals and must face situations, disasters, trials and setbecks of life with confidence.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'setbacks'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Five years later, I “was eating” this same dish at the same restaurant.
questions.explanation: SSC's key picks 'am eating': five years on, the speaker is eating the same dish now. 'Was eating' also reads correctly as a past narrative, but there is no 'no substitution' option; 'has been eating' does not agree with 'I', and 'will have be eating' is ungrammatical.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Scientists were conducting experiments on the newly discovered species.
options: The newly discovered species has been conducting experiments by scientists.
Experiments were being conducted on the newly discovered species by scientists.
The newly discovered species has been experimented on by scientists.
Experiments on the newly discovered species had been conducted by the scientists.
questions.explanation: The past continuous 'were conducting' becomes 'were being conducted' in the passive.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence. (P) the sun (Q) to our planet, Earth (O) provides essential energy (R) sustaining life and warmth
questions.explanation: 'The sun (P) provides essential energy (O) to our planet, Earth (Q) sustaining life and warmth (R).'

questions.text: The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. The employees were comfortable / with me and they talked about / their problems since / I has worked there as a manager.
options: with me and they talked about
I has worked there as a manager.
questions.explanation: 'I' does not take 'has'; in this past-tense sentence it should be 'since I had worked there as a manager'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. People often say that the stars govern their fate but they forget the fact that success or failure is the result of one’s own (1)________. If we sow chaff, we can’t reap grain; and the result or consequence of an action depends on what one does and to the extent he (2)________ it. If we work hard, we succeed only to the extent that we work. People who think that the law of karma is (3)________ may feel that if one is destined to get something he will always get it whether he strives for it or not. But experience tells us that reward and punishments are the direct result of our action. Honesty and hard work never go unrewarded and (4)________ and evil deeds never go (5)________. In fact even the law of karma, in its proper sense, means that the fruit we get is decided by whatever actions we did in the past.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Success or failure is the result of one's own 'actions'; the passage later calls rewards and punishments 'the direct result of our action'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘RIVAL’ is coded as ‘PKTCJ’ and ‘TEXTS’ is coded as ‘RGVVQ’. How will ‘POINT’ be coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: The letters move −2, +2, −2, +2, −2: RIVAL → PKTCJ and TEXTS → RGVVQ. So POINT → NQGPR.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No lotus is a daisy. All lotuses are tulips. All tulips are sunflowers. Conclusions: I. All daisies are tulips. II. Some sunflowers are daisies. III. No sunflower is a daisy.
options: Either conclusion II or III follows
questions.explanation: Nothing links daisies to tulips, so I does not follow. II and III cannot be settled on their own, but they are a complementary pair (some sunflowers are daisies / no sunflower is a daisy), so one of them must be true.

questions.text: Which letter cluster can replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? AZFX, EWHW, ?, MQLU, QNNT
questions.explanation: First letters move +4 (A, E, I, M, Q), second −3 (Z, W, T, Q, N), third +2 (F, H, J, L, N) and fourth −1 (X, W, V, U, T): ITJV.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'MUTUAL' is written as '12121202113', 'MARKET' is written as '2051118113', how will 'MODULE' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is reversed and each letter written as its place in the alphabet: MUTUAL → L A U T U M → 12 1 21 20 21 13 and MARKET → T E K R A M → 20 5 11 18 1 13. So MODULE → E L U D O M → 5 12 21 4 15 13: 5122141513.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. ALW: NYJ :: CNY :PAL :: DEP:?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 13 places forward, wrapping round after Z: ALW → NYJ and CNY → PAL. So DEP → QRC.

questions.text: Which number will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 49 × 7 − 6 ÷ 2 + 15 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 49 ÷ 7 + 6 × 2 − 15 = 7 + 12 − 15 = 4.

questions.text: Three of the following four are alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the one that does NOT belong to that group? The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster
questions.explanation: In JOR, AFI and MRU the letters move +5, then +3. LQS moves +5, then +2, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: All of the letters in the word ‘FROWNED’ are arranged in alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English alphabetical series between the letter which is fourth from the left end and the one which is second from the right end in the new letter-cluster thus formed?
questions.explanation: FROWNED in alphabetical order is D E F N O R W. The fourth from the left is N and the second from the right is R; between them come O, P and Q: three letters.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. FISH : DKQJ :: POND : NQLF :: SIZE : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move −2, +2, −2, +2: FISH → DKQJ and POND → NQLF. So SIZE → QKXG.

questions.text: Three of the following number-pairs are alike in some manner and hence form a group. Which number-pair does not belong to that group? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 21 – 361, 18 – 256 and 11 – 81 the second number is the square of two less than the first (19², 16², 9²). 121 is 11² = (14 − 3)², so 14 – 121 is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters which, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. f d _ e _ e f _ d d _ d _ f f _ d _ d _ f
options: d d f e e d e d
d d f e f d e e
d d f d e d e f
d d f e e d e e
questions.explanation: With d, d, f, e, e, d, e, e in the blanks the block fddedef repeats: fddedef fddedef fddedef.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. 3 — 5 — 30 2 — 4 — 16 NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The third number is twice the product of the first two: 3 × 5 × 2 = 30 and 2 × 4 × 2 = 16. Likewise 6 × 6 × 2 = 72.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the father of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’. Based on the above, how is K related to O if ‘K ÷ L − M + N × O’?
questions.explanation: K is the daughter of L, L is the husband of M, M is the mother of N and N is the father of O. So K is N's sister, and N is O's father: K is O's father's sister.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (34, 17, 27) (42, 21, 31) (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is half the first and the third is the second plus 10: 34 → 17 → 27 and 42 → 21 → 31. Likewise 54 → 27 → 37.

questions.text: 44 is related to 1936 by certain logic. Following the same logic, 59 is related to 3481. To which of the following is 77 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is related to its square: 44² = 1936 and 59² = 3481. So 77² = 5929.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 7, 13, ?, 145, 721, 4321
What was Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier's most important contribution to chemistry in 1789?
questions.explanation: In his 'Traité élémentaire de chimie' (1789) Lavoisier set out the law of conservation of mass: matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

questions.text: An electric iron requires a ________ fuse to prevent short circuiting.
questions.explanation: An iron of about 1 kW at 220 V draws 1000/220 ≈ 4.5 A, so it needs a 5 A fuse, the example NCERT uses.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following is primarily connected to the World’s Parliament of Religions convened in Chicago, 1893?
questions.explanation: Swami Vivekananda addressed the World's Parliament of Religions at Chicago in September 1893.

questions.text: Khuallam is a famous dance of:
questions.explanation: Khuallam is a traditional Mizo dance of Mizoram.

questions.text: The concept of Public Interest Litigation originated in _______________.
questions.explanation: Public Interest Litigation began in the USA in the 1960s; in India the Supreme Court developed it from the late 1970s.

questions.text: Thrissur Pooram is one of the famous temple festivals celebrated in _______.
questions.explanation: Thrissur Pooram, held at the Vadakkunnathan temple in Thrissur, is one of Kerala's best-known temple festivals.

questions.text: Identify the group of districts that are NOT an example of industrial districts of India.
questions.explanation: NCERT's list of India's industrial districts includes Cuttack, Kota, Kanpur, Agra, Jabalpur and Bhopal, but not Alwar or Bhiwani.

questions.text: Ustad Zia Mohiuddin Dagar was a ___________ player of profound depth, favouring sparse and slow realisations of ragas.
questions.explanation: Ustad Zia Mohiuddin Dagar, of the Dagar family of dhrupad musicians, was a master of the rudra veena.

questions.text: The headquarters of the second Green Revolution cell was in ________.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Patna, in Bihar; the push for a second Green Revolution was aimed largely at the eastern states.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was the Viceroy of India when Mahatma Gandhi started Dandi March on 12 March 1930?
questions.explanation: Lord Irwin was Viceroy from 1926 to 1931, so he was in office when the Dandi March began; the Gandhi-Irwin Pact followed in 1931.

questions.text: Who is the world’s most popular leader as per Global Leader Approval Ratings released by US-based Morning Consult in February 2023?
questions.explanation: Morning Consult's Global Leader Approval ratings released in February 2023 placed Narendra Modi first among the leaders it tracked.

questions.text: In which year was Smart Cities Mission launched?
questions.explanation: The Smart Cities Mission was launched in June 2015.

questions.text: Which of the following nations won the seven times women’s Asia Cup cricket Championship?
questions.explanation: India has won the Women's Asia Cup seven times, the seventh in 2022.

questions.text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution provides that the State must secure a social order to promote the welfare of people?
questions.explanation: Article 38, a Directive Principle, asks the State to secure a social order for the promotion of the welfare of the people.

questions.text: Identify a water-harvesting system found in Jaisalmer.
questions.explanation: Khadins are the water-harvesting structures of Jaisalmer; johads are found elsewhere in Rajasthan, and guls and kuls in the western Himalayas.

questions.text: The _________ were tributary chiefs of the Gupta dynasty. They established an independent kingdom in western India. Dhruvasena II was the most important ruler of this kingdom.
questions.explanation: The Maitrakas, once Gupta feudatories, ruled from Valabhi in Saurashtra; Dhruvasena II was a contemporary of Harsha.

questions.text: As of 31 May 2021, only 47% of total routes and 39% of airports (unserved and underserved) have been operationalised under UDAN, according to ICRA. What is the full form of UDAN?
questions.explanation: UDAN, the regional air connectivity scheme, stands for 'Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik'.

questions.text: Which of the following options is the most appropriate cause for unemployment in India?
questions.explanation: With the population, and so the labour force, growing faster than jobs, overpopulation is the cause among these; India has no lack of labour, and the other two do not cause unemployment.

questions.text: As of the June 2021, how many biosphere reserves are established in India?
questions.explanation: India had 18 biosphere reserves in June 2021, 12 of them in UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves.

questions.text: In which of the following battles did Muhammad of Ghor defeat Jayachandra of Gahadavala dynasty in 1194 AD?
questions.explanation: In the Battle of Chandawar (1194) Muhammad of Ghor defeated and killed Jayachandra, the Gahadavala king of Kanauj.

questions.text: The growth form of a plant, comprising its size, shape and orientation is known as:
questions.explanation: A plant's habit is its general form (herb, shrub, tree or climber), its size, shape and orientation; its habitat is where it lives.

questions.text: When and where did India win its first World Championships medal in Athletics?
questions.explanation: Anju Bobby George won bronze in the long jump at the 2003 World Championships in Paris, India's first World Championships medal in athletics.

questions.text: Tabla maestro, Bickram Ghosh, was awarded with which of the following awards in 2023 in the Contemporary Category?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, given by India's national academy of music, dance and drama.

questions.text: According to the Census of India 2011, the percentage of adolescent population (10-19 years) from the total population is how much?
questions.explanation: The 2011 Census counted about 253 million adolescents (10-19 years) in a population of about 1,211 million: 20.9%.

questions.text: A pair of straight lines from an external point F intersects a circle at A and B (FA < FB), and touches the circle at C. O is the centre of the circle. Given that ∠ACF = 50° and ∠AFC = 30°, find ∠AOB.
questions.explanation: By the alternate segment theorem ∠ABC = ∠ACF = 50°. In ΔFCB, ∠FCB = 180° − 30° − 50° = 100°, so ∠ACB = 100° − 50° = 50° and the central angle ∠AOB = 2 × 50° = 100°.

questions.text: The difference between a discount of 25% and two successive discounts of 15% and 20% on a certain bill was ₹28. Find the amount of the bill.
questions.explanation: Successive discounts of 15% and 20% leave 0.85 × 0.8 = 0.68 of the bill, a 32% discount. The difference, 32% − 25% = 7% of the bill, is ₹28, so the bill is ₹400.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 2, 5, 10 and 11?
questions.explanation: Divisible by 10 (and so by 2 and 5), the number must end in 0. For 11, in 589270 the alternate digit sums 5 + 9 + 7 = 21 and 8 + 2 + 0 = 10 differ by 11; in 1234560 they differ by 3.

questions.text: Which of the following is the sum of the values of a and b if the equations 2x + y = a, 8x + by = 12 have infinite solutions?
questions.explanation: For infinitely many solutions the coefficients must be in proportion: 2/8 = 1/b = a/12, so b = 4 and a = 3. a + b = 7.

questions.text: How much simple interest will ₹6,700 earn in 13 months at a 12% interest rate per annum?
Find the smallest value that must be assigned to number ‘a’ in order for 91876a2 to be divisible by 8.
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 8 when its last three digits are. 6a2 must be a multiple of 8, and the smallest is 632 = 8 × 79, so a = 3.

questions.text: A boatman goes 2 km against the current of the stream in 1 hour and goes 1 km along with the current in 10 minutes. How long will it take to go 6 km in stationary water?
questions.explanation: Upstream the speed is 2 km/h and downstream 1 km in 10 minutes = 6 km/h, so in still water it is (6 + 2)/2 = 4 km/h. 6 km takes 6/4 = 1.5 hours.

questions.text: Find the values of x, y and z, so as to satisfy the equations given below: 5x – 3y + 7z = 22; 3x – 5y – 2z = – 46; 2x – 2y + 5z = 24
The mean proportional of 2 and 32 is _____.
questions.explanation: The mean proportional of a and b is √(ab) = √(2 × 32) = √64 = 8.

questions.text: The profit gained on selling a certain product is 320% of the cost. If the cost increases by 10% but the selling price remains constant, then what percentage of the selling price is the profit (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.explanation: Take the cost as 100: the profit is 320 and the selling price 420. With the cost at 110 the profit is 310, which is 310/420 = 73.8% of the selling price.

questions.text: A circular arc whose radius is 12 cm makes an angle of 30° at the centre. Find the perimeter (in cm) of the sector formed. (Use π = 3.14)
A merchant mixes two varieties of sugar of 5 kg and 3 kg, which costs him ₹4 and ₹6 per kg, respectively. What is the cost price (in ₹) of the mixture per kg?
The proportion of Suresh's spending to saving is 3 : 1. His salary rises by 25%. What percentage of his expenditure will increase if his saving grows by 10%?
questions.explanation: Take the salary as 400: spending 300, saving 100. The salary rises to 500 and the saving to 110, so spending becomes 390: up 90/300 = 30%.

questions.text: If the sectorial angle with radius 9.6 units is 75°, what is the length of the arc?
Select the option that correctly expresses the given sentence in passive voice. I will never overlook this creativity.
options: This creativity will never be overlooked by me.
This creativity will be overlooked by me.
This creativity will being overlooked by me.
This creativity will not never be overlooked by me.
questions.explanation: 'Will overlook' becomes 'will be overlooked', with 'never' kept in place: 'This creativity will never be overlooked by me.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A place where birds are kept
questions.explanation: An aviary is a large enclosure where birds are kept; a hive houses bees, and a sanctuary protects wildlife in the wild.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Catastrophe
questions.explanation: A 'catastrophe' is a disaster; its opposite here is 'success'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Beyond skills, experience, and training, companies search for applicants who display excitement — those they believe “shall carry out allocated responsibilities” cheerfully and cooperatively.
options: shall take up any designated obligations
should pick up all skills and works
questions.explanation: What the companies believe applicants will do takes 'will', not 'shall': 'those they believe will execute assigned duties'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. After years of fights with his neighbour Ram, Shekhar decided to hold out the _______ and invited Ram for tea.
questions.explanation: To 'hold out an olive branch' is to make an offer of peace.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'contemptible'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. One must be very “strong” to lift this box of glass jars.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'strong' is 'weak'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. Anand personally believes in the motto, “When life gives you lemons, make lemonade.”
options: Earn the maximum out of business
Enjoy the most when the season is favourable
Make the best out of difficult situations
questions.explanation: 'When life gives you lemons, make lemonade' means to make the best of a difficult situation.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Monotonous
questions.explanation: 'Monotonous' means dull and unvarying; its opposite is 'engrossing', absorbing. 'Tiresome' and 'tedious' are synonyms.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence. You need to be concious enough to listen to the question.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'conscious'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym to replace the underlined word in the given sentence. How did we end up in this “rapturous” situation?
questions.explanation: 'Rapturous' means full of great joy: 'ecstatic'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The mother asked the child, “Will you tell me “who did accompany you” to the airport?”
questions.explanation: The plain past tense is wanted: 'who accompanied you to the airport'. 'Did accompany' is the emphatic form, which nothing here calls for.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the sentences in the correct sequence to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A)This past summer, my dream finally came true. B)Strange lands, exciting places, and new cultures have always fascinated me. C)Ever since I was a little girl, I dreamed about travelling overseas. D)I got to travel to England, France, Switzerland, and Germany.
questions.explanation: C states the childhood dream, B says what drew her to it, A says it came true this summer and D says where she went: CBAD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Rectify
questions.explanation: To 'rectify' is to put right: to 'amend'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. To __________ the ticket, Amith had to visit the travel agency many times.
questions.explanation: One 'confirms' a ticket; 'conform' means to comply with a rule.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. My brother received / his MBA degree into / the university last year.
questions.explanation: A degree is received 'from' a university: 'his MBA degree from the university'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Mobile phones or smartphones are becoming popular all over the world. B. But at the same time, it also harms us in many ways. C. It is the most widely used means of communication today. D. Today, it is very affordable and available to everyone.
questions.explanation: A introduces mobile phones, C and D say why they are so widely used, and B, beginning 'But at the same time', turns to the harm they do: ACDB.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase. Incapable of being defeated
questions.explanation: 'Invincible' means too strong to be defeated; 'ineluctable' means unavoidable.

questions.text: Select the option that correctly expresses the following sentence in passive voice. Who invited you to this party?
options: By whom you are invited to this party?
By whom are you invited to this party?
By whom you were invited to this party?
By whom were you invited to this party?
questions.explanation: 'Who' becomes 'by whom', and the past simple question takes 'were you invited': 'By whom were you invited to this party?'

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error in the usage of the interjection. He replied / in a dry tone, / “Ouch! I will not work / for you anymore.”
questions.explanation: 'Ouch' expresses sudden pain, which does not fit a dry refusal; an interjection such as 'No!' would.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Gandhi, (1)_________ father of the Indian nation, practiced ‘ahimsa’ in his personal and political life. He firmly believed that non-violence is not meant merely for monks, saints and priests; it is for commoners too. If violence is the law of the (2)_______-beasts, non-violence is the law of the civilised human species. ‘The spirit of the brute is inactive and so he knows no law; he knows only physical might. The dignity of man requires obedience to a higher law, to strength of the spirit,’ Gandhi said. Ahimsa, to Gandhiji, meant that one should love all; even (3)________ enemies. And the expression of love, ahimsa, should be in such a manner that it impresses itself indelibly upon the so-called enemy, and then the enemy must return that love. It is a practically (4)________ philosophy. Gandhi was realistic; he believed that non-violence provides the fullest protection to one’s self-respect and sense of humour. It won’t work in the defence of (5)_______ gains and immoral acts. He called his marches off when people indulged in violence during protests for India’s freedom. His faith in ‘ahimsa’ played an influential role in enabling the creation of an independent India in 1947, with minimum bloodshed, breaking the shackles framed by the British.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Gandhi is 'the father of the Indian nation': the definite article, as there is only one.
