questions.text: Which two numbers (not digits) should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 48 ÷ 3 + 12 × 4 – 6 × 7 + 21 = 27

In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (280, 140) (186, 93)
questions.explanation: The second number is half the first: 280 ÷ 2 = 140 and 186 ÷ 2 = 93. Likewise 118 ÷ 2 = 59.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All bottles are jugs. Some bottles are flasks. All flasks are bins. Conclusions: I. Some bottles are bins. II. Some jugs are bins. III. Some flasks are jugs.
options: All conclusions I, II and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
Only conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: Some bottles are flasks and all flasks are bins, so some bottles are bins (I). Those bottles are jugs, so some jugs are bins (II); and the flasks that are bottles are jugs, so some flasks are jugs (III). All three follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, A + B means ‘A is the son of B’, A − B means ‘A is the wife of B’, A × B means ‘A is the brother of B’ and A ÷ B means ‘A is the mother of B’. Based on the above, if ‘P + Q ÷ R − T × M’, which of the following is true?
options: T is the brother of P.
M is the sister of T.
P is the brother of R.
Q is the mother of M.
questions.explanation: P + Q makes P the son of Q, and Q ÷ R makes Q the mother of R. So P and R are both Q's children, and P, a son, is R's brother.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. RATE : SCWI : : HIGH : IKJL : : OPEN : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, +2, +3, +4: RATE → SCWI and HIGH → IKJL. So OPEN → PRHR.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘CONFUSED’ is coded as ‘7’ and ‘CHAIN’ is coded as ‘4’. How will ‘ADULTHOOD’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded as its number of letters minus one: CONFUSED (8) → 7 and CHAIN (5) → 4. ADULTHOOD has 9 letters, so 8.

questions.text: The question contains pairs of words that are related to each other in a certain way. Three of the following four word pairs are alike as these have the same relationship and thus form a group. Which word pair is the one that DOES NOT belong to that group? (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters / number of consonants/vowels in the word.)
questions.explanation: In the other pairs the specialist treats that part of the body. A urologist treats the urinary tract; the uterus is a gynaecologist's field.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. q p _ r _ r q _ p _ r p _ q _ p r _ p _ q
options: r p q r r p r q
r p q r r q r p
r p q r r q r r
r p q q r q r p
questions.explanation: With r, p, q, r, r, q, r, r in the blanks the block qprrprq repeats: qprrprq qprrprq qprrprq.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 17, 38, 84, ?, 376, 772
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before plus 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 in turn: 38 × 2 + 8 = 84, 84 × 2 + 12 = 180 and 180 × 2 + 16 = 376.

questions.text: The same operation(s) are followed in all the given number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In each pair the first number is 8 times the second minus 1: 17 × 8 − 1 = 135, 19 × 8 − 1 = 151 and 13 × 8 − 1 = 103. 128 is exactly 16 × 8, so 128 : 16 is the odd one.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? GASM, CCOO, YEKQ, ? , QICU
questions.explanation: First letters move back 4 (G, C, Y, U, Q), second letters forward 2 (A, C, E, G, I), third letters back 4 (S, O, K, G, C) and fourth letters forward 2 (M, O, Q, S, U): UGGS.

questions.text: The position(s) of how many letters will remain unchanged if all the letters in the word ‘MEADOW’ are arranged in English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: MEADOW in alphabetical order is ADEMOW. O and W stay fifth and sixth; the other four letters all move. So two are unchanged.

questions.text: ‘Summer’ is related to ‘Season’ in the same way as ‘Cotton’ is related to ‘________’.
questions.explanation: Summer is a kind of season, as cotton is a kind of cloth.

questions.text: 16 is related to 112 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 26 is related to 182. To which of the following is 44 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The second number is 7 times the first: 16 × 7 = 112 and 26 × 7 = 182. Likewise 44 × 7 = 308.

questions.text: 8 is related to 512 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 12 is related to 1728. To which of the following is 15 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The second number is the cube of the first: 8³ = 512 and 12³ = 1728. Likewise 15³ = 3375.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 14014 × 14 – 10 ÷ 8 + 14 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 14014 ÷ 14 + 10 × 8 − 14 = 1001 + 80 − 14 = 1067.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'DEMAND' is written as ‘410132144' and 'SUPPLY' is written as '194216161225'. How will 'PRODUCT' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as its place in the alphabet, with vowels doubled: DEMAND → 4, 10, 13, 2, 14, 4 and SUPPLY → 19, 42, 16, 16, 12, 25. So PRODUCT → 16, 18, 30, 4, 42, 3, 20.

questions.text: Consider the following statements associated with the India Infrastructure Project Development Fund (IIPDF). 1. IIPDF was set up in 2017. 2. The funds for IIPDF are provided by the Central Government’? 3. This scheme is notified under the Department of Economic Affairs. Which of the above statements is/are INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: The IIPDF was set up in 2007, not 2017, as a fund in the Department of Economic Affairs with money from the Central Government; the DEA notified it as a central sector scheme in 2022. Only statement 1 is incorrect.

questions.text: Which party formed the government in Britain in the year 1945?
questions.explanation: Clement Attlee's Labour Party won the general election of July 1945 and formed the government.

questions.text: Which type of radiation has very short (<10⁻³ nm) wavelengths, produced by nuclear explosions, lightning and less dramatic activity of radioactive decay?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays have the shortest wavelengths of the electromagnetic spectrum, below about 10⁻³ nm, and come from nuclear processes such as radioactive decay.

questions.text: Bharatanatyam dance style is associated with which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: Which Indian marathon event is considered the largest marathon in Asia?
questions.explanation: The Mumbai Marathon (now the Tata Mumbai Marathon), run every January, is billed as the largest marathon in Asia.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following organisations, divided into two branches, was established by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant?
questions.explanation: In 1916 Tilak set up his Home Rule League at Belgaum and Annie Besant hers at Madras; the two leagues worked side by side for self-government.

questions.text: Consider the following statements and choose the correct statement(s) from the following: 1. The UDAN scheme has completed five years since its implementation in 2017. 2. It is the flagship scheme of the Ministry of Science and Technology. 3. The Airports Authority of India is the implementing agency of this scheme.
questions.explanation: UDAN, the Ministry of Civil Aviation's regional connectivity scheme, flew its first flight in April 2017 and completed five years in 2022; the Airports Authority of India implements it. Statement 2 is wrong.

questions.text: In which of the following years did India NOT host the ICC Cricket World Cup Tournament?
questions.explanation: India co-hosted the World Cup in 1987, 1996 and 2011; the 1983 tournament, which India won, was held in England.

questions.text: Ebony and Mahogany trees are found in which type of forests?
questions.explanation: Ebony, mahogany and rosewood are hardwoods of the tropical evergreen forests.

questions.text: Who among the following was one of the Navratnas of Akbar?
questions.explanation: Tansen, the musician, was one of the nine jewels (navratnas) of Akbar's court.

questions.text: In which year was the PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission launched?
questions.explanation: The PM Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission was launched in October 2021, at Varanasi.

questions.text: When was the Duty-Free Tariff Preference (DFTP) Scheme for Least Developed Countries (LDCs) announced by India?
questions.explanation: India announced the DFTP scheme for LDCs in April 2008, at the India-Africa Forum Summit in New Delhi; it came into effect that August.

questions.text: Which of the following options is mostly caused by overpopulation?
options: Reduction in the scarcity of water
Land and other renewable resources are under pressure
Increase in the area covered by forests
questions.explanation: A growing population puts more pressure on land, water and other resources; the other options are the opposite of what overpopulation causes.

questions.text: On which of the following dates does India celebrate its Constitution Day?
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949, and the day has been marked as Constitution Day since 2015. (26 January is Republic Day.)

questions.text: Which of the following pairs do NOT share any borders?
questions.explanation: Bhutan borders Sikkim, West Bengal, Assam and Arunachal Pradesh. Meghalaya lies south of Assam and does not touch Bhutan.

questions.text: Palladium on barium sulphate (Pd/BaSO₄) is also known as:
questions.explanation: Palladium on barium sulphate, partly poisoned, is the Rosenmund catalyst, used to reduce acid chlorides to aldehydes.

questions.text: Which of the following types of direct tax collection increased as of 10 February 2023 budget?
questions.explanation: Octroi and commercial tax are not direct taxes. Personal income tax and corporate tax collections both rose; in the CBDT's figures to 10 February 2023 personal income tax grew faster (29.63% gross, against 19.33%), which is presumably why SSC's key gives it.

questions.text: Which Ghazal singer was conferred with the prestigious Deenanath Mangeshkar Award in April 2023?
questions.explanation: In April 2023 the Mangeshkar family named the ghazal singer Pankaj Udhas for the Master Deenanath Mangeshkar Award, for his contribution to Indian music.

questions.text: What kind of radiation is absorbed by the ozone layer?
questions.explanation: The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs most of the Sun's ultraviolet radiation.

questions.text: The organisation that Comptroller and Auditor General heads is known as ___________.
options: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
questions.explanation: The Comptroller and Auditor General heads the Indian Audit and Accounts Department.

questions.text: Which of the following categories does Gonyaulax belong to?
questions.explanation: Gonyaulax is a dinoflagellate; its blooms cause red tides.

questions.text: Valabhi, a city of ancient India was the capital of the _________ dynasty from the 5th to 8th Century CE.
questions.explanation: The Maitrakas ruled from Valabhi in Saurashtra (Gujarat) from the late 5th to the 8th century.

questions.text: Who has written the book ‘Fearless Governance’, published in January 2021, describing her stint as Governor?
questions.explanation: 'Fearless Governance' is by Kiran Bedi, then Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry.

questions.text: Shab-e-Barat is celebrated by which religious group?
questions.explanation: Shab-e-Barat, the night of the 15th of Sha'ban, is observed by Muslims.

questions.text: In a rhombus ABCD, O is any interior point such that OA = OC. What is five-ninths of the degree measure of ∠DOB?
questions.explanation: OA = OC puts O on the perpendicular bisector of AC, which in a rhombus is the diagonal BD. So D, O and B lie in a straight line and ∠DOB = 180°; five-ninths of it is 100°.

questions.text: A group of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 62, and that of the rest is 62. What is the average score of the group?
questions.explanation: Both groups average 62, so the whole group does too: (12 × 62 + 18 × 62)/30 = 62.

questions.text: If asin³ X + bcos³ X = sinXcosX and asinX = bcosX, then find the value of a² + b², provided that x is neither 0° nor 90°.
questions.explanation: From asinX = bcosX, write a = k cosX and b = k sinX. Then k sinX cosX(sin²X + cos²X) = sinX cosX, so k = 1: a = cosX, b = sinX and a² + b² = 1.

questions.text: Find the smallest number to be added to 999, so that 99 divides the sum exactly.
The interest accrued on a sum of ₹16,000 lent at a simple interest rate of 14% p.a. for the time in those many years, which gives a simple interest of three-fifths of a certain sum at 10% p.a., is:
questions.explanation: Interest of 3/5 of a sum at 10% needs 10 × T/100 = 3/5, so T = 6 years. Then 16,000 × 14 × 6/100 = ₹13,440.

questions.text: In a circle, two chords MN and PQ intersect at O. If MO = 9 cm, ON = 5 cm and OQ = 6 cm, then the value of OP (in cm) is:
questions.explanation: For intersecting chords MO × ON = PO × OQ: 9 × 5 = OP × 6, so OP = 7.5 cm.

questions.text: A rectangular courtyard is 4m 95cm long and 16m 65cm broad. It is to be paved with the square tiles of the same size. Find the least number of such square tiles required to pave the rectangular courtyard.
questions.explanation: The largest tile has the HCF of 495 cm and 1665 cm as its side: 45 cm. Tiles = (495/45) × (1665/45) = 11 × 37 = 407.

questions.text: In an election between two candidates P and Q, P got 78% of the total valid votes. If the total votes of the electorate were 75,60,000, then what was the number of valid votes that Q got if 10% of the voters did not cast their vote and 15% of the votes polled were declared invalid?
questions.explanation: Votes polled = 90% of 75,60,000 = 68,04,000; valid votes = 85% of that = 57,83,400. Q got the other 22%: 12,72,348.

questions.text: Solve the given set of three equations to get the value of the unknowns: x + 2z = 3; x + 2y + 3z = 5; 3x - 5z = -13
questions.explanation: From the first equation x = 3 − 2z; in the third, 9 − 11z = −13, so z = 2 and x = −1. The second then gives −1 + 2y + 6 = 5, so y = 0.

questions.text: A shopkeeper, on the eve of Diwali, allowed a series of discounts on television sets. Find the selling price of a television set, if the marked price of television is ₹1,200 and successive discounts are 15% and 10%.

Mrudula starts her job with a certain monthly salary and earns a fixed increment every year. If her salary was ₹28,400 after six years of service and ₹52,997 after fifteen years, find her annual increment.
questions.explanation: Nine increments take the salary from ₹28,400 to ₹52,997: 24,597 ÷ 9 = ₹2,733.

questions.text: In a division problem, the divisor is 4 times the quotient and 2 times the remainder. If the remainder is 32, then find the dividend.
questions.explanation: The remainder is 32, so the divisor is 64 and the quotient 16. Dividend = 64 × 16 + 32 = 1056.

questions.text: Atul gives Vishu a head-start of 20 seconds in a 900 m race and beats him by 135 m. While running the same race again Atul gives a start of 189 m and beats him by 8 seconds. In how much time can Vishu complete the full race of 900 m?
questions.explanation: Let Vishu run v m/s and Atul take t seconds for 900 m. First race: v(t + 20) = 765. Second race: Vishu runs 711 m in t + 8 seconds, so v(t + 8) = 711. Subtracting, 12v = 54 and v = 4.5 m/s: 900/4.5 = 200 seconds, or 3 minutes 20 seconds.

questions.text: A sum of money is divided among P, Q, R and S in the proportion of 4 : 9 : 2 : 3. If Q gets ₹560 more than R, then the share of S is:
questions.explanation: Q − R = 9 − 2 = 7 parts = ₹560, so one part is ₹80 and S gets 3 × ₹80 = ₹240.

questions.text: Select the option that correctly expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The teachers of our school have already taken this training.
options: This training has already been taken by the teachers of our school.
This training has already been taken by the our school teachers.
This training was already taken by the teachers of our school.
This training has been taken by the teachers of our school.
questions.explanation: The present perfect passive is 'has been taken', with 'already' after 'has': 'This training has already been taken by the teachers of our school.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Awkward in movement or manner
questions.explanation: Someone 'clumsy' is awkward in movement or manner.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. He was very “cruel” in dealing with the students.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'cruel' is 'kind'.

questions.text: The following sentence contains a word with a spelling error. Rectify the sentence by selecting the correct spelling of the identified word from the given options. I was upstaires when somebody rang the doorbell.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'upstairs'.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (A) while the employees (B) meeting on time (C) the boss arrived at the (D) despite the heavy traffic (E) were late
questions.explanation: 'Despite the heavy traffic (D) the boss arrived at the (C) meeting on time (B) while the employees (A) were late (E).'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. An instrument for viewing distant objects in space.
questions.explanation: A telescope is an instrument for viewing distant objects in space.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. (A) he had to take the bus (B) his friend, who used to give (C) to his office because he had (D) him a lift, was on vacation (E) never learned to drive and
questions.explanation: 'He had to take the bus (A) to his office because he had (C) never learned to drive and (E) his friend, who used to give (B) him a lift, was on vacation (D).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. She was “overstrung” before her dance performance.
questions.explanation: 'Overstrung' means very nervous or tense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the following word. Forbid
questions.explanation: To 'forbid' is to refuse to allow; its opposite is 'allow'. 'Prohibit' is a synonym.

questions.text: Substitute the underlined word-segment with most appropriate idiom. The doctors “tried very hard” to save his mother but they were unsuccessful.
questions.explanation: To 'move heaven and earth' is to make every possible effort.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice. Ravi will play the match.
options: The match is played by Ravi.
The match will have been played by Ravi.
The match will be playing by Ravi.
The match will be played by Ravi.
questions.explanation: The future active 'will play' becomes 'will be played': 'The match will be played by Ravi.'

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. It is he who work for the company for more than a decade.
questions.explanation: 'Who' refers to 'he', so the verb must be singular, and an action going on for more than a decade takes the present perfect: 'It is he who has worked for the company for more than a decade.'

questions.text: Identify the correct synonym of the word given below. FATIGUE
questions.explanation: 'Fatigue' means tiredness; 'vigour' is its opposite.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The windows / violent banged / during the / storm yesterday.
questions.explanation: A verb is modified by an adverb: 'The windows banged violently during the storm yesterday.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Adversity
questions.explanation: 'Adversity' means misfortune or hardship.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. Our legal system must frame proper legal rules for “juvenile” criminals.
questions.explanation: 'Juvenile' means young: juvenile criminals are young offenders.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words in the following sentence. Despite recent superficial moves toward political reconciliation, Libya remains in the grip of a bloodstained corrupt military “exclusive circle of people with a common purpose”.
questions.explanation: A clique is a small, exclusive group of people who share interests or a purpose.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence and select its correct spelling from the given options. His acquiantance with the author led to many fruitful collaborations.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'acquaintance'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Charles Darwin is renowned for his book on evolution, ‘On the Origin of Species’, which “laid down a treasure of substantiation” that evolution occurs, and projected a mechanism, that is, natural selection, for how it does so.
options: laid away a treasure of substantiation
laid about a treasure of substantiation
laid out a treasure of substantiation
laid into a treasure of substantiation
questions.explanation: To 'lay out' evidence is to set it out in full; 'lay down' means to establish a rule or principle.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hit the nail on the head
options: They hit a nail with a hammer.
They have accurately identified or explained something.
questions.explanation: To 'hit the nail on the head' is to describe or identify something exactly.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav is an (1) _________ by the Government of India to celebrate and remember 75 years of independence and the beautiful history of its people, culture and achievements. This Mahotsav is (2) _________ to the people of India, who have not only been instrumental in bringing India this far in its evolutionary journey but also (3) _________ the power and potential to realise Prime Minister, Narendra Modi's (4) _________ of activating India 2.0, fuelled by the spirit of Aatmanirbhar Bharat. questions.text: The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if each of the letters in the word ‘JEALOUS’ is arranged in the English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: JEALOUS in alphabetical order is A E J L O S U. E (2nd), L (4th) and O (5th) keep their places: three letters.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which conclusion/s logically follow/s from the given statements. Statements: All apples are mangoes. All mangoes are lemons. All lemons are kiwis. Conclusions: (I) All apples are lemons. (II) All mangoes are kiwis.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: All apples are mangoes and all mangoes are lemons, so all apples are lemons (I). All mangoes are lemons and all lemons are kiwis, so all mangoes are kiwis (II). Both follow.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (34, 15, 64) (29, 17, 63) (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The third number is the first plus twice the second: 34 + 2 × 15 = 64 and 29 + 2 × 17 = 63. Likewise 25 + 2 × 14 = 53.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 3, 20, 121, 604, 2417, ?
In a certain code language, 'VAIN' is written as 'OKBY’ and 'VAST' is written as 'UUBY'. How will 'VERB’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is reversed and its letters move +1, +2, +1, +3: VAIN → NIAV → OKBY and VAST → TSAV → UUBY. So VERB → BREV → CTFY.

questions.text: Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. You have to consider these statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts. Decide which of the given conclusions logically follow/s from the given statements. Statements: All pens are pages. Some pages are pins. Some pins are boards. Conclusions: (I) Some pins are pens. (II) Some boards are pages. (III) Some pens are boards.
options: Either conclusion I or conclusion III follows.
questions.explanation: The pins that are pages need not include any pen (I), the boards that are pins need not be pages (II), and nothing links pens to boards (III). I and III are not a complementary pair, so none of the conclusions follows.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? DBOI, FEQL, ?, JKUR, LNWU
questions.explanation: First letters move +2 (D, F, H, J, L), second +3 (B, E, H, K, N), third +2 (O, Q, S, U, W) and fourth +3 (I, L, O, R, U): HHSO.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 186 : 103 156 : 73
questions.explanation: The second number is the first minus 83: 186 − 83 = 103 and 156 − 83 = 73. Likewise 95 − 83 = 12.

questions.text: ‘Lavish’ is related to ‘Austere’ in the same way as ‘Prejudiced’ is related to ‘________’. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.)
questions.explanation: 'Lavish' and 'austere' are opposites; the opposite of 'prejudiced' is 'impartial'.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below will complete the letter series. _ C _ W _ _ _ C _ W _ _
questions.explanation: With W, W, C, W, W, W, C, W in the blanks the block WCW repeats: WCW WCW WCW WCW.

questions.text: In a certain code language, A + B means ‘A is the wife of B’. A − B means ‘A is the son of B’. A × B means ‘A is the husband of B’. A ÷ B means ‘A is the father of B’. Based on the above, how is P related to T if ‘P − Q + R ÷ S × T’?
questions.explanation: P is Q's son, Q is R's wife, R is S's father and S is T's husband. P and S are both sons of R, so P is T's husband's brother.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term is related to third term. TRAINER : VTCIQHU :: RADIANT : TCFIDQW :: CUSHION : ?
questions.explanation: The first three letters move +2, the fourth stays and the last three move +3: TRAINER → VTC I QHU and RADIANT → TCF I DQW. So CUSHION → EWU H LRQ: EWUHLRQ.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different. Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster
questions.explanation: In GDI, XUZ and SPU the letters move −3, then +5. LKP moves −1, then +5, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the triad in which the numbers are related to each other in the same way as the numbers in the following triads. 8-17-35 23-47-95 (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is twice the one before it plus 1: 8 → 17 → 35 and 23 → 47 → 95. Likewise 12 → 25 → 51.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BUZZY’ is coded as ‘10’ and ‘KING’ is coded as ‘8’. How will ‘ABROAD’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word's code is twice its number of letters: BUZZY (5) → 10 and KING (4) → 8. So ABROAD (6) → 12.

questions.text: Select the number that will come in the place of the question mark(?), if ‘+’ and ‘ – ‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged 41 – 54 × 6 ÷ 9 + 7 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 41 + 54 ÷ 6 × 9 − 7 = 41 + 81 − 7 = 115.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘÷’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘+’ are interchanged? 8 + 6 ÷ 51 – 17 × 13 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 8 × 6 − 51 ÷ 17 + 13 = 48 − 3 + 13 = 58.

questions.text: Three of the following numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the odd one out. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 65 – 104, 75 – 120 and 90 – 144 the numbers are in the ratio 5 : 8 (13 × 5 and 13 × 8, 15 × 5 and 15 × 8, 18 × 5 and 18 × 8). 45 – 70 is 9 : 14, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Tabla player, Ustad Zakir Hussain was awarded which of the following awards by the Government of India in 2023?
questions.explanation: Ustad Zakir Hussain received the Padma Vibhushan, India's second-highest civilian award, in 2023; he had received the Padma Shri in 1988 and the Padma Bhushan in 2002.

questions.text: Which of the following famous Indian athletes won the Zurich Diamond League final 2022 in September 2022?
questions.explanation: Neeraj Chopra won the Diamond League final in Zurich on 8 September 2022 with a javelin throw of 88.44 m, the first Indian to win a Diamond League title.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following battles is considered the formal beginning of the British Raj in India?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey (1757), in which Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah, Nawab of Bengal, is taken as the start of British political power in India; Buxar (1764) consolidated it.

questions.text: How many chambers are there in the heart of fishes?
questions.explanation: A fish's heart has two chambers, one atrium and one ventricle, and pumps blood only to the gills.

questions.text: Which of the following Table Tennis World Championship events was held in India?
questions.explanation: The 19th World Table Tennis Championships were held in Bombay in 1952, the first time the championships came to Asia.

questions.text: Taxus wallichiana Zucc (Himalayan yew) is a medicinal plant found in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: The Himalayan yew grows in the temperate Himalaya, including the Kullu, Mandi and Shimla districts of Himachal Pradesh; it yields precursors of the anti-cancer drug paclitaxel (taxol).

questions.text: When haloalkanes and aryl and vinyl halides react with magnesium metal they yield which reagent?
questions.explanation: Haloalkanes, and aryl and vinyl halides, react with magnesium in dry ether to give organomagnesium halides (RMgX): Grignard reagents.

questions.text: Who among the following, while praising the amending feature of the Indian Constitution said that ‘This variety in the amending process is wise but is rarely found’?
questions.explanation: K. C. Wheare praised the Indian Constitution's range of amending procedures (by simple majority, by special majority, and by special majority with ratification by the states) in these words.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following cities did Mahatma Gandhi lead the peasant movement against the imposed indigo cultivation by the British planters?
questions.explanation: Gandhi's first satyagraha in India was in Champaran, Bihar, in 1917, against the forced cultivation of indigo by European planters.

questions.text: Chittani Ramachandra Hegde was associated with which of the following dances?
questions.explanation: Chittani Ramachandra Hegde was a celebrated Yakshagana artiste from Karnataka.

questions.text: Anna Chandy, the first Indian woman to serve as a judge at a high court was oppointed in which High Court?
questions.explanation: Anna Chandy became a judge of the Kerala High Court in 1959, the first woman to sit as a High Court judge in India.

questions.text: What is the unit of measurement for optical power of the lens?
questions.explanation: The power of a lens is measured in dioptres (D): a lens of focal length 1 m has a power of 1 D. The katal measures catalytic activity, the radian measures angles, and yotta is the prefix for 10²⁴.

questions.text: As in July 2021, The NIPUN Bharat Scheme was launched by which of the following Ministries?
options: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
questions.explanation: NIPUN Bharat, launched by the Ministry of Education on 5 July 2021, aims for every child to gain foundational literacy and numeracy by the end of Grade 3.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India expressly provides that the President is eligible for re-election?
questions.explanation: Article 57 makes a person who holds or has held the office of President eligible for re-election. Article 56 deals with the term of office, 58 with qualifications and 59 with conditions of office.

questions.text: As per the report of the NITI Aayog in 2023, which among the following states in India has the lowest percentage of the total population that is multidimensionally poor?
questions.explanation: In NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index: A Progress Review 2023, Kerala had the lowest share of multidimensionally poor people (0.55%), ahead of Goa (0.84%) and Sikkim (2.60%).

questions.text: Gangu bai Hangal and Prabha Atre were exponents of the ___________ Gharana.
questions.explanation: Gangubai Hangal and Prabha Atre were vocalists of the Kirana gharana of Hindustani classical music.

questions.text: Which of the following cups/trophies is NOT related to the Indian domestic cricket?
questions.explanation: The Durand Cup is a football tournament, first held in 1888. The Duleep, Deodhar and Ranji Trophies are Indian domestic cricket competitions.

questions.text: Who among the following was the last sultan of Delhi sultanate?
questions.explanation: Ibrahim Lodi, the last Sultan of Delhi, was defeated and killed by Babur at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.

questions.text: The idols of which three Gods are installed in Jagannath Temple, Puri?
questions.explanation: The Jagannath Temple at Puri enshrines Jagannath with his elder brother Balabhadra and his sister Subhadra.

questions.text: In the context of water bodies, Neap Tides occur:
options: when the sun and moon are at right angles to each other
when the sun and moon are on the opposite sides
when there is so much interference by continents
when the earth, moon and sun line up in a straight line
questions.explanation: Neap tides occur when the sun and moon are at right angles as seen from the earth, so their pulls partly cancel; spring tides occur when the earth, moon and sun are in a line.

questions.text: According to the Ashrama system of Vedic life, which of the following was the third stage of life?
questions.explanation: The four ashramas are Brahmacharya (student), Grihastha (householder), Vanaprastha (forest-dweller) and Sanyasa (renunciation), so the third is Vanaprastha.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
options: Mitochondria: Power house of the cell
questions.explanation: The nucleus holds the cell's DNA and controls its activities; lipids are made in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.text: The Government of India allowed automatic approval of _____% of FDI by Reserve Bank of India in nine categories of industries.
questions.explanation: In the reforms of the 1990s the RBI could give automatic approval to foreign equity of up to 74% in nine high-priority industries of the metallurgical and infrastructure sectors.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian states has the least number of operational airports as of 2022?
questions.explanation: Mizoram has a single operational airport, Lengpui near Aizawl; Karnataka, Maharashtra and Bihar each have several.

questions.text: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 200 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at the rate of 10 km/h and 11 km/h, respectively. What is the distance (in metres) between them after 9 minutes?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 11 − 10 = 1 km/h, that is 1,000 m an hour, so in 9 minutes he closes 1,000 × 9/60 = 150 m. 200 − 150 = 50 m.

questions.text: S borrowed some amount from R and promised to pay him 8% interest. Then S invested the borrowed amount in a scheme, upon which he earned a profit of 5% after paying R, the principal amount with interest. How much percentage R would have gained, if he would have invested in the scheme directly?
questions.explanation: On a borrowed sum P, the scheme returned 8% of P for R's interest and a further 5% of P as S's profit: 13% in all, which R would have earned by investing directly.

questions.text: If the ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is 25 : 144, the ratio of their corresponding sides is:
questions.explanation: The areas of similar triangles are in the ratio of the squares of their sides, so the sides are in the ratio √25 : √144 = 5 : 12.

questions.text: In ∆ PQR, M, N, and S are the mid-points of sides PQ, PR and QR, respectively. If the area of the ∆ PQR is 46 cm², what is the area (in cm²) of the quadrilateral MNRQ?
questions.explanation: MN joins the mid-points of PQ and PR, so ΔPMN has half the sides of ΔPQR and a quarter of its area: 46/4 = 11.5 cm². MNRQ = 46 − 11.5 = 34.5 cm².

questions.text: △ABC and △RPQ are congruent, then the side of △ABC that corresponds to PQ is:
questions.explanation: In △ABC ≅ △RPQ the vertices correspond in order: A ↔ R, B ↔ P and C ↔ Q. So PQ corresponds to BC.

questions.text: If 0.4x + 0.16y = 1.7 and 0.3x + 0.12y = 3.4, then which of the following is correct?
options: The system has finitely many solutions but not unique.
The system has infinitely many solutions.
questions.explanation: The coefficients are in the same ratio, 0.4/0.3 = 0.16/0.12 = 4/3, but the constants are not (1.7/3.4 = 1/2): the lines are parallel and never meet.

questions.text: Find the average of the prime numbers lying between 50 and 76.
questions.explanation: The primes between 50 and 76 are 53, 59, 61, 67, 71 and 73. Their sum is 384, and 384 ÷ 6 = 64.

questions.text: The salary of a worker is first increased by 25%, then it is decreased by 12%. The percentage change in his salary is:
questions.explanation: 1.25 × 0.88 = 1.10, so the salary rises by 10%.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers is divisible by both 2 and 5?
questions.explanation: A number divisible by both 2 and 5 is divisible by 10, so it must end in 0: 63840.

questions.text: Pipe A usually fills a tank in 6 hours. But due to a leak at the bottom of the tank, it takes extra 2 hours to fill the tank. If the tank is full, then how much time will it take to get emptied due to the leak?
questions.explanation: A fills 1/6 of the tank an hour; with the leak it takes 8 hours, so 1/8 an hour. The leak empties 1/6 − 1/8 = 1/24 of the tank an hour: 24 hours.

questions.text: How many years will it take for ₹8,400 to amount to ₹11,928 at a simple interest rate of 7% per annum?
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Merit
questions.explanation: 'Merit' is the quality of being good or worthy: 'virtue'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence. A. It contains high levels of Vitamin A and D. B. Cod liver oil is thus used to treat arthritis. C. This supplement is made from the liver of cod fish. D. Cod liver oil is a nutritional supplement.
questions.explanation: D introduces cod liver oil, C says what it is made from, A what it contains, and B, with 'thus', what it is used for: DCAB.

questions.text: Select the option that can replace the underlined phrase and make the sentence grammatically correct. The programme on TV “was now shown the blurring faces of the inmates of the rehabilitation centre” .
options: was now showing the blurred faces of the inmates upon the rehabilitation centre
were now showing the blurred faces of the inmates of the rehabilitation centre.
were now showing the blurring faces of the inmates from the rehabilitation centre
was now showing the blurred faces of the inmates of the rehabilitation centre
questions.explanation: The programme (singular) 'was showing' the faces, which had been 'blurred'; 'was shown' makes the programme the thing shown, and the inmates are 'of' the centre.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Layla is the Sultan’s “consort”.
questions.explanation: A 'consort' is the wife or husband of a ruler: a 'partner'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Jump the gun
options: To do something too soon and too quickly
questions.explanation: To 'jump the gun' is to act too soon, like a runner who starts before the starting pistol.

questions.text: In the given question, a statement divided into different segments is given. Rearrange all the segments to form a coherent statement. O: population is expected to triple in P: the next 50 years Q: among the world’s poorest countries R: population shrinkage in that period S: whereas many rich countries will see
questions.explanation: 'Among the world's poorest countries (Q) population is expected to triple in (O) the next 50 years (P) whereas many rich countries will see (S) population shrinkage in that period (R).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. In Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice, Shylock's connivance aimed to “jeopardise” Antonio's life.
questions.explanation: To 'jeopardise' is to put in danger; its opposite is to 'safeguard'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Rahul thinks he is as smarter as his friends in the class.
questions.explanation: A comparison of equality takes the positive degree: 'as smart as', not 'as smarter as'.

questions.text: Select the word OPPOSITE in meaning to the given word. Deficient
questions.explanation: 'Deficient' means lacking; its opposite is 'ample', more than enough.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To read between the lines
options: To understand more than what the words suggest
questions.explanation: To 'read between the lines' is to find a meaning that is implied but not stated.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Neither my brother nor my brothers-in-law / attended the meeting / as his health is not more good.
options: as his health is not more good
Neither my brother nor my brothers-in-law
questions.explanation: 'Not more good' is wrong: the sentence needs 'as his health is no longer good'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Two of the fugitives managed to remain free by adeptly avoiding the____________ of the police.
questions.explanation: The fugitives stayed free by escaping the police's 'pursuit', their chase.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence . She recieved an award for her outstanding performance.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'received' ('i' before 'e' except after 'c').

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice. The car was repaired by the mechanic.
options: The mechanic is repairing the car.
The mechanic has repaired the car.
questions.explanation: The simple past passive 'was repaired by the mechanic' becomes the simple past active: 'The mechanic repaired the car.'

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence. (P) kindness and empathy (Q) in a world that can be (O) bring light and positivity (R) harsh and challenging
questions.explanation: 'In a world that can be (Q) harsh and challenging (R) kindness and empathy (P) bring light and positivity (O).'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who is trained to travel in a spacecraft.
questions.explanation: An astronaut is a person trained to travel in a spacecraft.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Each candidate was making tall promises.
options: Tall promises will be made by each candidate.
Tall promises are being made by each candidate.
Tall promises are made by each candidate.
Tall promises were being made by each candidate.
questions.explanation: The past continuous 'was making' becomes 'were being made' in the passive, agreeing with the plural 'tall promises'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'conscientious'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Jovial
questions.explanation: 'Jovial' means cheerful and friendly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Meander
questions.explanation: To 'meander' is to follow a winding course; its opposite is to go 'direct'. 'Ramble' is close to a synonym.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Appearances may not reveal the man. So, you shouldn't make (1) _________ about a man's character based on how he (2) _________ . People smile and smile, yet prove to be (3) _________ . On the other hand, people with rough exteriors prove to be the (4) _________ and most considerate people on earth. They are the people who are beautiful from (5) _________ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: One should not make 'assumptions' about a man's character from his appearance.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Appearances may not reveal the man. So, you shouldn't make (1) _________ about a man's character based on how he (2) _________ . People smile and smile, yet prove to be (3) _________ . On the other hand, people with rough exteriors prove to be the (4) _________ and most considerate people on earth. They are the people who are beautiful from (5) _________ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Judging a man by 'how he looks' is what the passage warns against: appearances may not reveal the man.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Appearances may not reveal the man. So, you shouldn't make (1) _________ about a man's character based on how he (2) _________ . People smile and smile, yet prove to be (3) _________ . On the other hand, people with rough exteriors prove to be the (4) _________ and most considerate people on earth. They are the people who are beautiful from (5) _________ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: People who smile may yet prove 'grumpy': the word must contrast with smiling.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Appearances may not reveal the man. So, you shouldn't make (1) _________ about a man's character based on how he (2) _________ . People smile and smile, yet prove to be (3) _________ . On the other hand, people with rough exteriors prove to be the (4) _________ and most considerate people on earth. They are the people who are beautiful from (5) _________ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: People with rough exteriors may prove the 'kindest' and most considerate: a superlative to pair with 'most considerate'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Appearances may not reveal the man. So, you shouldn't make (1) _________ about a man's character based on how he (2) _________ . People smile and smile, yet prove to be (3) _________ . On the other hand, people with rough exteriors prove to be the (4) _________ and most considerate people on earth. They are the people who are beautiful from (5) _________ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: They are beautiful 'from within', in character rather than in appearance.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. R F _ G T R _V G _ R F V _ T _ F V G T
questions.explanation: With V, F, T, G, R in the blanks the block RFVGT repeats: RFVGT RFVGT RFVGT RFVGT.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘MAN’ is coded as ‘15316’ and ‘SHE’ is coded as ‘21107’. How will ‘OUT’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is coded as its place in the alphabet plus 2: M, A, N → 15, 3, 16 and S, H, E → 21, 10, 7. So O, U, T → 17, 23, 22: 172322.

questions.text: Select the word pair that best represents a similar relationship to the one expressed in the pair of words given below. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Calcium : Osteomalacia
questions.explanation: A lack of calcium causes osteomalacia (softening of the bones), as a lack of iron causes anaemia.

questions.text: All of the letters in the word ‘JUNGLE’ are arranged in alphabetical order. How many letters are there in the English alphabetical series between the letter which is second from the left end and the one which is third from the right end in the new letter-cluster thus formed?
questions.explanation: JUNGLE in alphabetical order is E G J L N U. The second from the left is G and the third from the right is L; between them come H, I, J and K: four letters.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (66, 57, 48) (94, 85, 76) (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is 9 less than the one before: 66, 57, 48 and 94, 85, 76. Likewise 81, 72, 63.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 17 : 253 19 : 271
questions.explanation: The second number is 9 times the first plus 100: 17 × 9 + 100 = 253 and 19 × 9 + 100 = 271. Likewise 21 × 9 + 100 = 289.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some rats are mouse. No mouse is a rodent. Some rats are kittens. Conclusions: I. No rodent is a kitten. II. Some rats are rodent. III. No kitten is a mouse.
questions.explanation: None is certain: kittens and rodents may or may not overlap (I), the rats that are not mice may or may not be rodents (II), and the rats that are kittens could also be mice (III).

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. OUR : NPTVQS : : BIG : ACHJFH : : FOR : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by the letters just before and just after it: O → NP, U → TV, R → QS. So F → EG, O → NP, R → QS: EGNPQS.

questions.text: In a certain code language, BRING is coded as ‘7149182’ and SMILE is coded as ‘51291319’. What will be the code for FORGIVE?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and each letter written as its place in the alphabet: BRING → G N I R B → 7 14 9 18 2. FORGIVE reversed is E V I G R O F → 5 22 9 7 18 15 6: 5229718156.

questions.text: In a certain code language, R + T means ‘R is the sister of T’. R – T means ‘R is the father of T’. R * T means ‘R is the wife of T’. R ÷ T means ‘R is the mother of T’. Based on the above, how is M related to Q if ‘M * N – P + Q ÷ R +T’?
questions.explanation: M is the wife of N, N is the father of P, and P is the sister of Q. So Q is N's child, and M is Q's mother.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 304 × 19 − 101 + 23 ÷ 5 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 304 ÷ 19 + 101 − 23 × 5 = 16 + 101 − 115 = 2.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 164 – 173 ÷ 110 + 140 × 5 = ?

Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different. Note : The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster
questions.explanation: BCD, JKL and RST are three consecutive letters in forward order; ONM runs backwards, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 12, 25, 49, ?, 197, 395
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before, plus and minus 1 in turn: 12 × 2 + 1 = 25, 25 × 2 − 1 = 49, 49 × 2 + 1 = 99, 99 × 2 − 1 = 197 and 197 × 2 + 1 = 395.

questions.text: The same operation(s) are followed in all the given number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 56 : 9, 44 : 7 and 68 : 11 the second number is (first − 2) ÷ 6: 54 ÷ 6 = 9, 42 ÷ 6 = 7 and 66 ÷ 6 = 11. For 72 this gives 70 ÷ 6, not 12, so 72 : 12 is the odd pair.

questions.text: Two sets of numbers are given below. In each set of numbers, certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number result(s) in the second number. Similarly, certain mathematical operation(s) on the second number result(s) in the third number and so on. Which of the given options follows the same set of operations as in the given sets? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 14 – 196 – 186 – 172; 15 – 225 – 215 – 200
questions.explanation: The number is squared, 10 is subtracted, then the original number is subtracted: 14² = 196, 186, 186 − 14 = 172; 15² = 225, 215, 215 − 15 = 200. Likewise 9² = 81, 71, 71 − 9 = 62.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will logically complete the series. BYN_J_YNF_X_NFJVY_FJ
questions.explanation: With F, Z, J, Y, N in the blanks the series reads BYNFJ ZYNFJ XYNFJ VYNFJ: YNFJ repeats while the first letter moves back two places (B, Z, X, V).

questions.text: Lata Mangeshkar was honoured with the Bharat Ratna in the year ________.
questions.explanation: Lata Mangeshkar received the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

questions.text: What is the reason for the similar size of the vascular bundle in monocot leaves?
questions.explanation: Monocot leaves have parallel venation, so their vascular bundles are of nearly similar size (except in the main veins).

questions.text: In which state of India was the Neeru-Meeru programme introduced for construction of water harvesting structures?
questions.explanation: Neeru-Meeru ('Water and You') was Andhra Pradesh's programme for building water-harvesting structures such as percolation tanks and check dams.

questions.text: Hariprasad Chaurasia, an Indian flutist in the Hindustani classical tradition, was awarded with which of the following awards in 2000?
questions.explanation: Hariprasad Chaurasia received the Padma Vibhushan in 2000, after the Padma Bhushan in 1992.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following events took place in the United Provinces in February, 1922?
questions.explanation: At Chauri Chaura, in Gorakhpur district of the United Provinces, a crowd set fire to a police station in February 1922; Gandhi then called off the Non-Cooperation Movement.

questions.text: What do we mean by Allen’s rule?
options: The body compensates low oxygen availability by increasing red blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing the breathing rate.
Some plants have no leaves – they are reduced to spines – and the photosynthetic function is taken over by the flattened stems.
Desert lizards lack the physiological ability that mammals have to deal with the high temperatures of their habitat.
Mammals from colder climates generally have shorter ears and limbs to minimise heat loss.
questions.explanation: Allen's rule: mammals of colder climates have shorter ears and limbs, which reduces heat loss.

questions.text: Ernest Rutherford used about ________ thick gold foil for alpha scattering experiments.
questions.explanation: Rutherford wanted as thin a layer as possible; his gold foil was about 1,000 atoms thick.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the conduct of business of the Government of a state?
questions.explanation: Article 166 covers the conduct of business of the Government of a State. Article 164 deals with other provisions as to Ministers, and Article 167 with the Chief Minister's duties towards the Governor.

questions.text: In which of the following districts of Rajasthan are the ‘Barchans’ found?
questions.explanation: Barchans are crescent-shaped sand dunes of the Thar Desert. Jaisalmer, in the far west of Rajasthan, is the only desert district among the options.

questions.text: In May 2022, Then President Ram Nath Kovind appointed _________ as the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi.
questions.explanation: Vinai Kumar Saxena was appointed Lieutenant Governor of Delhi in May 2022, succeeding Anil Baijal.

questions.text: Which of the following Constitutions inspired the law-making process in India?
questions.explanation: India's law-making procedure, like its parliamentary system and the rule of law, is borrowed from the British Constitution.

questions.text: According to which of the following foreign travellers, people of Delhi used to write letters containing abuses to the Sultan, therefore, in order to punish them Sultan decided to shift the capital?
questions.explanation: Ibn Batuta records that the people of Delhi wrote letters full of abuse to Muhammad bin Tughluq, and that he moved the capital to Daulatabad to punish them.

questions.text: How many players are there on each side of the Kabaddi Team in the field?
questions.explanation: A kabaddi team has seven players on the court at a time.

questions.text: In 2022, which of the following railway stations has been selected for the ‘One Station One Product’ scheme launched by Indian Railways, which identifies Kanchipuram sarees as the chosen product?
questions.explanation: Under the pilot of the 'One Station One Product' scheme, Southern Railway opened a Kanchipuram silk saree stall at Chennai Central in March 2022.

questions.text: Which of the following definitions best describes the concept of microfinance?
options: A microfinance institution is a digital-only and mobile-first bank.
Microfinance is a banking service provided to unemployed or low-income individuals or groups, who otherwise would have no other access to financial services.
Microfinance refers to providing banking services to individuals living in rural areas.

A microfinance institution is a company registered under the Companies Act, 1956, and engaged in the business of loans and advances and acquisition of shares/stocks/bonds/debentures/securities issued by the government.
questions.explanation: Microfinance provides small loans and other financial services to low-income or unemployed people who have no access to ordinary banking.

questions.text: How long will a sound wave take to travel 1.5km, which has a frequency of 5 kHz and wavelength of 6 cm?
questions.explanation: Speed = frequency × wavelength = 5,000 × 0.06 m = 300 m/s, so 1,500 m takes 1,500 ÷ 300 = 5 seconds.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: With reference to Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909, consider the following statements. a) They are also called the Indian Councils Act, 1909. b) They increased the strength of Legislative Councils. c) The right to separate electorate was given to the Muslims. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct: the Morley-Minto Reforms were enacted as the Indian Councils Act, 1909; they enlarged the Legislative Councils and gave Muslims separate electorates.

questions.text: Which of the following types of unemployment is found in India when people are employed for a certain period of a year in tourist resorts and various tourism-related activities in the mountain regions, but are unemployed in off-seasons?
questions.explanation: Work that is available only in some seasons, such as tourism in the hills, leaves people unemployed for the rest of the year: seasonal unemployment.

questions.text: Which of the following terms is NOT related to cricket?
questions.explanation: Deuce, a tie at 40-40, is a tennis term; no ball, wide ball and wicket belong to cricket.

questions.text: Which of the following schemes enables students mobility across Higher Education Institutions?
options: Structured Assessment for Analysing Learning Levels (SAFAL)
questions.explanation: The Academic Bank of Credits, set up under the National Education Policy 2020, stores students' credits so that they can move between Higher Education Institutions.

questions.text: When was the Jawaharlal Nehru Manipur Dance Academy established?
questions.explanation: The Jawaharlal Nehru Manipur Dance Academy in Imphal, now a unit of the Sangeet Natak Akademi, began in 1954 as the Manipur Dance College.

questions.text: Who developed the theory of combustion as a chemical reaction with oxygen in the 18th century, that excluded phlogiston theory?
questions.explanation: Antoine Lavoisier showed that burning is a reaction with oxygen, overturning the phlogiston theory.

questions.text: The Mahalanobis model was the basis for which Five-Year Plan?
questions.explanation: The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61), with its stress on heavy industry, was built on P. C. Mahalanobis's model.

questions.text: ’Poush Mela’ is a unique festival celebrated in which of the following Indian states?
questions.explanation: Poush Mela is held every winter at Santiniketan in West Bengal.

questions.text: Vasudeva I who issued coins in gold (dinars and quarter dinars) and copper (single denomination) was a _________king.
questions.explanation: Vasudeva I, the successor of Huvishka, was a Kushana king.

questions.text: Naman bought few apples for ₹720 from a shop. He negotiated the price and the shopkeeper reduced it by ₹2 per apple. Due to this Naman could buy four more apples than what he had bought earlier. How many apples did he originally buy?
questions.explanation: If he first bought n apples, 720/n − 720/(n + 4) = 2, so n(n + 4) = 1,440 and n = 36 (at ₹20 each; then 40 apples at ₹18).

questions.text: What is the ratio of the mean proportional of 1.21 and 0.09 with the mean proportional of 0.16 and 0.36?

If Ram purchases a fan, he gets 8% discount, however, if he purchases three fans he gets 6% on the first, 10% on the second and 12% on the third. If the price paid by the Ram for three fans is ₹6,800, then what will be the marked price of each fan?
questions.explanation: For three fans he pays 0.94 + 0.90 + 0.88 = 2.72 times the marked price, so the marked price is 6,800 ÷ 2.72 = ₹2,500.

questions.text: The tank is filled by three pipes with different uniform flow rates. While the first two pipes are operating simultaneously, they fill the tank in the same duration that the third pipe takes to fill it alone. The second pipe can fill the tank 5 hours quicker than the first pipe, yet 4 hours slower than the third pipe. What is the time (in hours) needed for the first pipe to fill the tank?
questions.explanation: If the first pipe takes x hours, the second takes x − 5 and the third x − 9, and 1/x + 1/(x − 5) = 1/(x − 9). This gives x² − 18x + 45 = 0, so x = 15 (x = 3 would make the other times negative). Check: 1/15 + 1/10 = 1/6.

questions.text: In ∆ABC, two medians AD and BE intersect at G at right angles. If AD = 12 cm and BE = 9 cm, then the length of AB is equal to:
questions.explanation: The centroid divides each median 2 : 1, so AG = 8 cm and BG = 6 cm. As ∠AGB = 90°, AB = √(8² + 6²) = 10 cm.

questions.text: A class of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 62, and that of the rest is 74. What is the average score of the class?
A boat can go 54 km upstream in 6 hours. If the speed of the stream is 4.8 km/h, then how much time (in hours) will the boat take to cover a distance of 279 km downstream?
questions.explanation: Upstream speed = 54/6 = 9 km/h, so the boat's own speed is 9 + 4.8 = 13.8 km/h and its downstream speed 13.8 + 4.8 = 18.6 km/h. 279 ÷ 18.6 = 15 hours.

questions.text: Replace * by the smallest digit so that 723*56* is divisible by 6.
questions.explanation: Both stars take the same digit d. For divisibility by 6 the number must be even and its digit sum, 23 + 2d, a multiple of 3: the smallest such d is 2 (7232562, digit sum 27).

questions.text: A cuboid of dimensions 50 cm, 150 cm, 175 cm can be divided into how many identical largest cubes?
P and Q are centres of two circles whose radii are 7 cm and 3 cm, respectively. If the direct common tangents to the circles meet PQ extended at A, then A divides PQ _________.
questions.explanation: The direct common tangents meet on PQ produced, at the point that divides PQ externally in the ratio of the radii: AP : AQ = 7 : 3.

questions.text: Sohan borrows a sum of ₹1,41,545 at the rate of 11% per annum simple interest. At the end of the first year, he repays ₹25,490 towards return of principal amount borrowed. If Sohan clears all pending dues at the end of the second year, including interest payment that accrued during the first year, how much does he pay (in ₹) at the end of the second year?
questions.explanation: First-year interest = 11% of 1,41,545 = ₹15,569.95. After the ₹25,490 repayment, ₹1,16,055 remains and earns ₹12,766.05 in the second year. Total = 1,16,055 + 15,569.95 + 12,766.05 = ₹1,44,391.

questions.text: In a ΔLMN, ∠L = 118° and LM = LN. Find ∠N.
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Failing to give proper care and attention
questions.explanation: 'Lax' means not careful or strict enough: negligent.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. A big fancy dress ball was arranged to celebrate their homecoming. B. It must have been a terrible shock for a young girl. C. They had been married a month, just home from their honeymoon. D. Just as the guests were starting to arrive, Charnley locked himself into his bedroom and shot himself.
questions.explanation: C (married a month, home from their honeymoon) must come before A (the ball for their homecoming), and A before D (the guests arriving). Only BCAD keeps this order, with B's remark leading in.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Expertise
questions.explanation: 'Expertise' is great skill or knowledge: 'proficiency'.

questions.text: In the following sentence, four words are underlined out of which one word is misspelt. Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word. I took out a water “tumbler”(A) for a drink, but found the water in the metal “container” (B) had frozen so I couldn't “quanch” (C) my thirst. I ate some biscuits and “offered” (D) some to Hillary.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'quench'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. He must deliver pizza.
options: Pizza can be delivered by him.
Pizza must be delivered by him.
Pizza has to be delivered by him.
Pizza have to be delivered by him.
questions.explanation: 'Must deliver' becomes 'must be delivered', keeping the modal: 'Pizza must be delivered by him.'

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence. (P) an open mind (Q) seek it with (O) for personal growth and development (R) knowledge is a powerful tool
questions.explanation: 'Knowledge is a powerful tool (R) for personal growth and development (O); seek it with (Q) an open mind (P).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. The________(crux) of his argument was that education should continue throughout life.
questions.explanation: The 'crux' of an argument is its central point: its 'essence'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. “Success” is not a destination, it’s a journey.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'success' is 'failure'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. She believed she had been “blamed for the mistakes of others” for what happened.
questions.explanation: A 'scapegoat' is someone blamed for the mistakes or wrongdoing of others: 'She believed she had been made a scapegoat for what happened.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. Out of those group members, Rohan is the “one who opposes others”, no matter what they tell him.
questions.explanation: An 'antagonist' is one who opposes or contends with another; a 'protagonist' is the leading character, or a supporter of a cause.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank. All the chefs in the world are famous because of their _____________ skills.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'culinary', to do with cooking.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Solutions to the country’s interior problems are still a long way away.
questions.explanation: Problems within a country are its 'internal' problems; 'interior' means the inside or inland part of something.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Brittle
questions.explanation: 'Brittle' means hard but easily broken; its opposite is 'resilient', able to withstand strain and recover.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The letter was being typed by the secretary when the phone rang.
options: The secretary will type the letter when the phone rings.
The secretary is typing the letter when the phone rings.
The secretary was typing the letter when the phone rang.
The secretary types the letter when the phone rings.
questions.explanation: 'Was being typed' is the past continuous passive, so the active is 'was typing', and the 'when' clause stays in the past: 'The secretary was typing the letter when the phone rang.'

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. When I “saw him”, I will ask him to return the book he borrowed.
questions.explanation: A time clause about the future takes the simple present: 'When I see him, I will ask him to return the book.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Nobody’s fool
questions.explanation: Someone who is 'nobody's fool' is shrewd and not easily deceived.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A dime a dozen
questions.explanation: Something 'a dime a dozen' is very common and of little value.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Paramount
questions.explanation: 'Paramount' means more important than anything else: 'supreme'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. They secret / decided / to leave / the town.
questions.explanation: The verb 'decided' needs an adverb, not the noun 'secret': 'They secretly decided to leave the town.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Now, we have Mr. X as the President of India. It has come as a surprise (1)______ Scheduled Tribes who are (2)______ the most marginalised groups of the country. The Adivasis of India have been (3)______ socially, economically and culturally. Despite various efforts taken by the Government of India, they are still under (4)______ and suffering. Therefore, the (5)______ a leader from a marginalised community or group does not indicate that now the entire community will be uplifted. However, this kind of move may bring certain changes in the status of the Adivasis.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.1
questions.explanation: Something 'comes as a surprise to' someone.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Now, we have Mr. X as the President of India. It has come as a surprise (1)______ Scheduled Tribes who are (2)______ the most marginalised groups of the country. The Adivasis of India have been (3)______ socially, economically and culturally. Despite various efforts taken by the Government of India, they are still under (4)______ and suffering. Therefore, the (5)______ a leader from a marginalised community or group does not indicate that now the entire community will be uplifted. However, this kind of move may bring certain changes in the status of the Adivasis.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.2
