This particular fashion was largely brought (3) __________ by the urgent need to disguise the ravages of smallpox, (4)_________ left their faces pitted and scarred. During this same period, the ‘beauty spot’ was introduced to cover (5) __________ a facial defect.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The ladies covered their own faces: the possessive 'their'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. From the beginning (1)_________ the eighteenth century, the ladies of European cities covered (2)_______ faces in layers of paint and powder. This particular fashion was largely brought (3) __________ by the urgent need to disguise the ravages of smallpox, (4)_________ left their faces pitted and scarred. During this same period, the ‘beauty spot’ was introduced to cover (5) __________ a facial defect.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Brought about' means caused: the fashion was caused by the need to hide the scars of smallpox.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. From the beginning (1)_________ the eighteenth century, the ladies of European cities covered (2)_______ faces in layers of paint and powder. This particular fashion was largely brought (3) __________ by the urgent need to disguise the ravages of smallpox, (4)_________ left their faces pitted and scarred. During this same period, the ‘beauty spot’ was introduced to cover (5) __________ a facial defect.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: After a comma, the relative pronoun for a thing (smallpox) is 'which'; 'that' is not used after a comma.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. From the beginning (1)_________ the eighteenth century, the ladies of European cities covered (2)_______ faces in layers of paint and powder. This particular fashion was largely brought (3) __________ by the urgent need to disguise the ravages of smallpox, (4)_________ left their faces pitted and scarred. During this same period, the ‘beauty spot’ was introduced to cover (5) __________ a facial defect.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: To 'cover up' a defect is to hide it.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. CWE:ZFX ::PYT:MDI :: KIL:?
questions.explanation: In each pair the positions of matching letters add up to 29: C(3)→Z(26), W(23)→F(6), E(5)→X(24), and P→M, Y→D, T→I likewise. So K(11)→R(18), I(9)→T(20) and L(12)→Q(17): RTQ.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? MFT, NIS, PLQ, SON, WRJ, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +1, +2, +3, +4, +5 (M, N, P, S, W, so next B); second letters +3 (F, I, L, O, R, so U); third letters −1, −2, −3, −4, −5 (T, S, Q, N, J, so E): BUE.

questions.text: Three of the following numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Pick the odd one out. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In 36 – 84, 66 – 154 and 72 – 168 the two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 7. 33 × 7/3 = 77, not 72, so 33 – 72 is the odd one.

questions.text: Which two numbers (not digits) should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 24 ÷ 3 – 4 × 2 + 6 × 5 +12 = 50
The position of how many letters will remain unchanged if each of the letter in the word ‘JANITOR’ is arranged in English alphabetical order?
questions.explanation: JANITOR in alphabetical order is A I J N O R T. Position by position (J/A, A/I, N/J, I/N, T/O, O/R, R/T) no letter stays where it was.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different. Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their position in the letter cluster.
questions.explanation: In PSUV, FIKL and TWYZ the letters move +3, +2, +1. BEHI moves +3, +3, +1, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. P _ A A _ _ Z A _V _ _ A _ _
questions.explanation: With Z, V, P, A, P, Z, A, V in the blanks the series reads PZAAV PZAAV PZAAV: the block PZAAV repeats.

questions.text: Which of the four options will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? XF 11 , YI 15, ZL 19 , AO 23, ?
questions.explanation: First letters run X, Y, Z, A, so next is B; second letters move +3 (F, I, L, O), so next is R; the number rises by 4 (11, 15, 19, 23), so next is 27: BR 27.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘SILK’ is written as ‘TIML’ and ‘INSECT’ is written as ‘IOTEDU’. How will ‘CHANGE’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each consonant moves one letter forward and each vowel stays: SILK → TIML and INSECT → IOTEDU. So CHANGE → DIAOHE.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 321 – 371 ÷ 22 + 216 × 6 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 321 + 371 × 22 − 216 ÷ 6 = 321 + 8162 − 36 = 8447.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (12, 145) (9, 82)
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first plus 1: 12² + 1 = 145 and 9² + 1 = 82. Likewise 14² + 1 = 197.

questions.text: In a certain code language, A + B means ‘A is the son of B’, A − B means ‘A is the sister of B’, A × B means ‘A is the brother of B’ and A ÷ B means ‘A is the mother of B’. Based on the above, how is T related to P if ‘P ÷ Q × R − M + T’?
questions.explanation: P is the mother of Q; Q, R and M are siblings; and M is the son of T. So T is the other parent of P's children: P's husband.

questions.text: Select the number from the given options to complete the series. 35, 38, 43, 50, 59, ___
questions.explanation: The differences are the odd numbers 3, 5, 7, 9, so the next is +11: 59 + 11 = 70.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (19, 456, 6) (16, 320, 5)
questions.explanation: In each set, first × third × 4 = second: 19 × 6 × 4 = 456 and 16 × 5 × 4 = 320. Likewise 18 × 9 × 4 = 648.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (34, 47, 62) (119, 142, 167) (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each set is three consecutive perfect squares minus 2: (34, 47, 62) = 6², 7², 8² − 2 and (119, 142, 167) = 11², 12², 13² − 2. Likewise (79, 98, 119) = 9², 10², 11² − 2.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘SET’ is coded as ‘37’ and ‘MIX’ is coded as ‘35’. How will ‘WAR’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter takes its position counted from Z (A = 26, B = 25, …, Z = 1) and the code is their sum: SET = 8 + 22 + 7 = 37 and MIX = 14 + 18 + 3 = 35. So WAR = 4 + 26 + 9 = 39.

questions.text: What is the length of Indian Railways network, according to Railway Yearbook 2019- 20?
questions.explanation: According to the Indian Railways Year Book 2019-20, the network's route length was 67,956 km.

questions.text: Which of the following is the largest crustal plate on Earth with an area of over 103,000,000 km²?
questions.explanation: The Pacific plate, at over 103 million km², is the largest of the Earth's lithospheric plates.

questions.text: ‘Nuakhai’ is the state festival of:
questions.explanation: Nuakhai, the harvest festival at which the new rice is first offered, is the state festival of Odisha, celebrated mainly in western Odisha.

questions.text: Which of the following is a straight-chain alkyl carboxylic acid with the chemical formula CH₃CH₂CH₂CO₂H?
questions.explanation: CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH has four carbon atoms: butanoic (butyric) acid. Methanoic, ethanoic and propionic acids have one, two and three.

questions.text: Who among the following was the youngest instrumentalist to be awarded the Padma Bhushan, the third highest civilian award of India in 2002?
questions.explanation: Tabla maestro Ustad Zakir Hussain received the Padma Bhushan in 2002. Of the others, Bhimsen Joshi was a vocalist, and Ravi Shankar and Bismillah Khan received theirs in the 1960s.

questions.text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution prohibits providing of any religious instruction in the educational institutions maintained by the State?
questions.explanation: Article 28(1) bars religious instruction in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds.

questions.text: Article 77 of the Indian Constitution deals with the __________.
options: oath of office by the Vice-President
conduct of business of the Government of India
term of office of the Vice-President
questions.explanation: Article 77 covers the conduct of business of the Government of India: all its executive action is taken in the President's name.

questions.text: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 deals with subsistence allowance in which of the following Sections?
questions.explanation: Section 5 of the 2019 Act entitles a Muslim woman against whom triple talaq is pronounced to subsistence allowance for herself and her dependent children.

questions.text: In which year was the 'Naye Bharat Ke Sapne' campaign launched by Meta and the Ministry of Women?
questions.explanation: Meta launched the 'Naye Bharat Ke Sapne' campaign with the Ministry of Women and Child Development in 2023.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: Fats and oils get reduced over time and smell bad.
Antioxidants are added to foods containing fats and oil to prevent oxidation.
Chips manufacturers usually flush bags of chips with Nitrogen to prevent the chips from getting ranicid.
Fats and oils are oxidised, they become rancid.
questions.explanation: Fats and oils go rancid because they are oxidised, not reduced, which is why antioxidants are added and chip bags are flushed with nitrogen. So the first statement is incorrect.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Under which of the following Acts was the power to rule India, transferred from the English East India Company to the British Crown?
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act 1858, passed after the revolt of 1857, transferred the power to govern India from the East India Company to the British Crown.

questions.text: Which of the following countries won the first men’s Asian Hockey Championship trophy?
questions.explanation: India won the first men's Asian Champions Trophy, held in Ordos, China, in 2011.

questions.text: Silappathikaram (the Jewelled Anklet), the earliest epic poem in Tamil was written in the 5th - 6th Century CE by _________.
questions.explanation: Silappathikaram was written by Ilango Adigal; Sittalai Sattanar wrote its sequel, Manimekalai.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct?.
options: The five-year plan focuses mostly on private intervention in the economy.
The five-year plan permits long-term intervention by the government in the economy.
The five-year plan always focused on the growth of the tertiary sector.
A five-year plan always stresses market-oriented activities.
questions.explanation: A five-year plan sets out long-term government intervention in the economy; it is not about private intervention or market-oriented activity alone.

questions.text: In Pradhan Mantri Gramin Awaas yojana, the cost of unit assistance is shared between Central and State Governments in the ratio ___________ in plain areas.
questions.explanation: Under PMAY-G the Centre and the States share the cost of unit assistance 60 : 40 in plain areas, and 90 : 10 in the north-eastern and Himalayan states.

questions.text: Who was the revenue minister during the reign of Akbar?
questions.explanation: Raja Todar Mal was Akbar's revenue minister and devised the zabti system of land revenue.

questions.text: Hot local wind that flows over north India in summer is known as:
questions.explanation: The Loo is the hot, dry wind of the north Indian plains in May and June. The Chinook blows in North America, and mango showers are pre-monsoon rains in the south.

questions.text: As per the definition of Census of India, a ‘marginal worker’ is a person who works for:
options: more than 183 days (or six months) in a year
less than 183 days (or six months) in a year
questions.explanation: The Census of India counts as a marginal worker anyone who worked for less than 183 days (six months) of the year; 183 days or more makes a main worker.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Nrityagram, an Odissi dance institution, located?
questions.explanation: Nrityagram, the Odissi dance village founded by Protima Gauri in 1990, is near Bengaluru, Karnataka.

questions.text: At which Olympics was Kho-Kho featured in an exhibition in the main stadium?
questions.explanation: Kho-kho was shown as a demonstration sport at the 1936 Berlin Olympics.

questions.text: Which of the following goods needs further transformation in the economic process?
questions.explanation: Intermediate goods, such as raw materials and parts, are used up in making other goods, so they still need further transformation; final goods do not.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following devised the system of ‘Subsidiary Alliance’?
questions.explanation: Lord Wellesley, Governor-General from 1798 to 1805, devised the Subsidiary Alliance.

questions.text: Which of the following is an inactivated (killed) polio vaccine developed in 1952?
questions.explanation: Jonas Salk developed the inactivated (killed) polio vaccine in 1952; Sabin's oral vaccine uses live, weakened virus.

questions.text: Which of the following personalities is a Padma Shri awardee folk singer from the state of Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Ajita Srivastava, a folk singer from Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh, received the Padma Shri in 2022. Teejan Bai is a Pandavani singer from Chhattisgarh.

questions.text: A number is first increased by 12% and then increased by 23%. The number, so obtained, is now decreased by 34%. What is the net increase or decrease percent in the original number (nearest to an integer)?
questions.explanation: 1.12 × 1.23 × 0.66 = 0.909, so the number ends about 9.1% below where it started: a 9% decrease to the nearest integer.

questions.text: A stock portfolio consists of four stocks. Stock A represents 20% of the portfolio and has a return of 6%. Stock B represents 30% of the portfolio and has a return of 8%. Stock C represents 20% of the portfolio and has a return of 4%. Stock D represents the remaining 30% of the portfolio and has a negative-return of 5%. What is the average return of the portfolio?

A thief noticed a policeman at a distance of 600 metres. The thief started running and the policeman chased him. The thief and policeman are running at speeds of 12 km/h and 15 km/h, respectively. Find the time (in minutes) required for the policeman to catch the thief.
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 15 − 12 = 3 km/h = 50 m a minute on the thief, so he closes 600 m in 12 minutes.

questions.text: What is the perimeter (in cm, rounded off to one decimal place) of the sector of a circle with a radius of 10 cm and of angle 30°? (Use π = 3.14)
If 7845K854 is divisible by 11, then what is the value of K?
questions.explanation: For divisibility by 11 the sums of alternate digits must differ by 0 or a multiple of 11. Odd places: 7 + 4 + K + 5 = 16 + K; even places: 8 + 5 + 8 + 4 = 25. 25 − (16 + K) = 0 gives K = 9.

questions.text: In a ΔPQR, the bisectors of ∠Q and ∠R meet at point O, inside the triangle. If ∠QOR = 107°, then the measure of ∠P is:
questions.explanation: Where the bisectors of ∠Q and ∠R meet, ∠QOR = 90° + ∠P/2. So 107° = 90° + ∠P/2 and ∠P = 34°.

questions.text: If the equations 4x + (k − 2)y + 3 = 0 and (k − 2)x + 9y − 5 = 0 (k > 0) are parallel, then find the value of k² + 6.
questions.explanation: Parallel lines have proportional x and y coefficients: 4/(k − 2) = (k − 2)/9, so (k − 2)² = 36 and k = 8 (as k > 0). Then k² + 6 = 70.

questions.text: Ramesh has ₹18,000. He deposited ₹7,000 in a bank at the rate of 5% per annum and ₹6,000 in other bank at the rate of 6% per annum simple interest. If he received ₹1,160 as simple interest at the end of one year, then the rate of interest per annum on rest of the capital is equal to:
questions.explanation: The first two deposits earn 5% of ₹7,000 + 6% of ₹6,000 = ₹350 + ₹360 = ₹710. The remaining ₹5,000 earned ₹1,160 − ₹710 = ₹450, which is 9%.

questions.text: In a clearance sale, a sari whose marked price was ₹10,490 is now sold for ₹9,441. What is the discount percentage on the sari?
questions.explanation: Discount = ₹10,490 − ₹9,441 = ₹1,049, which is 10% of the marked price.

questions.text: Two triangles EFG and HIJ are congruent. If the area of ΔEFG is 124 cm², then the area of ΔHIJ will be:
questions.explanation: Congruent triangles are identical in shape and size, so their areas are equal: 124 cm².

questions.text: A pipe can fill an overhead tank in 12 hours. But due to a leak at the bottom, it is filled in 18 hours. If the tank is full, how much time will the leak take to empty it?
questions.explanation: The pipe fills 1/12 of the tank an hour, but with the leak only 1/18, so the leak empties 1/12 − 1/18 = 1/36 an hour: 36 hours for a full tank.

questions.text: If the length, breadth, and height of a cuboid is 8 cm, 4 cm, and 6 cm, respectively, then the volume (in cm³) of the cuboid is:
questions.explanation: Volume of a cuboid = l × b × h = 8 × 4 × 6 = 192 cm³.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence and select its correct spelling from the given options. I receieved a parcel in the mail today.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'received' ('i' before 'e' except after 'c').

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. An order of law requiring people to remain indoors
questions.explanation: A curfew is an order requiring people to stay indoors, usually between set hours.

questions.text: Which of the following idioms means ‘to steal from a shop’?
questions.explanation: A 'five-finger discount' is slang for shoplifting.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The tea at this café is best than at the Costa Café in our office.
questions.explanation: Two things are compared, so the comparative is needed: 'is better than', not 'is best than'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given word. Edible
questions.explanation: 'Edible' means fit to be eaten. Of the options only 'nutritive' (nourishing) is close; 'noxious' and 'noisome' mean harmful or offensive.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Morbid compulsion to consume alcohol continuously
questions.explanation: Dipsomania is a morbid craving for alcohol; kleptomania is a compulsion to steal.

questions.text: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. P. having the opportunity of observing people’s Q. we respect and appreciate their point of views R. the advantage of travelling different places and S. culture, custom and lifestyle, is that
questions.explanation: 'The advantage of travelling different places and (R) having the opportunity of observing people's (P) culture, custom and lifestyle, is that (S) we respect and appreciate their point of views (Q).'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank. The elaborate syllabi had to be ________(summarised) to make a presentation in the UGC assessment meeting.
questions.explanation: To 'recapitulate' is to summarise; 'expanded', 'prolonged' and 'lengthened' mean the opposite.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. The question papers are placed in the lockers of the school in a way that they “can’t be reached”.
questions.explanation: Something that cannot be reached is 'inaccessible'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'mischievous', with no 'i' before '-ous'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The painting was admired by art enthusiasts from around the world.
options: Art enthusiasts from around the world have admired the painting.
Art enthusiasts from around the world admired the painting.
The painting was being admired by art enthusiasts from around the world.
The painting has been admired by art enthusiasts from around the world.
questions.explanation: 'Was admired by' is simple past passive, so the active is simple past: 'Art enthusiasts from around the world admired the painting.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Miserable
questions.explanation: 'Miserable' means very unhappy; its opposite is 'cheerful'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. Fatima was “at her wits’ end” trying to decide on a serene place for spending the holidays in.
options: So worried, confused or annoyed that she became unconscious
So calm and composed that she knows what to do next
So worried, confused or annoyed that she does not know what to do next
So worried, confused or annoyed that she insulted others for no reason
questions.explanation: To be 'at one's wits' end' is to be so worried or confused that one does not know what to do next.

questions.text: Select the word segment that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the sentence meaningfully. (Each participant have) performed well.
questions.explanation: 'Each' takes a singular verb: 'Each participant has performed well.'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. He will be made President by the people.
options: He will be made President by the people.
By the people, he shall be made the President.
The people will make him President.
People will be making him the President.
questions.explanation: 'Will be made' is the future passive of 'will make': 'The people will make him President.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Taut
questions.explanation: 'Taut' means stretched tight: 'tight'. 'Slack' and 'flaccid' are its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Confiscate
questions.explanation: To 'confiscate' is to take away by authority: to 'seize'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank. He has the ________ to express his thoughts.
questions.explanation: He has the 'right' (the entitlement) to express his thoughts; 'write' and 'rite' sound the same but mean something else.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. There are many factories in the “operative” area of the city.
questions.explanation: An area full of factories is an 'industrial' area; 'industrious' means hard-working.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I are dancing with my husband at my sister’s wedding.
questions.explanation: 'I' takes 'am': 'I am dancing'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Tea prices in the domestic (1)__________ continue to rule high in the current year despite the expectation of a higher production as compared to the previous year. During the past three months, tea prices have been (2)__________ with the prices of other companies. Unlike last year, tea prices have generally shown (3) __________, when tea prices rose dramatically, this year, prices seem to have (4) __________ at a rather high level. In the subsequent four months, the (5)__________ average price showed a downtrend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Tea prices in the domestic market': prices are set in a market.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Tea prices in the domestic (1)__________ continue to rule high in the current year despite the expectation of a higher production as compared to the previous year. During the past three months, tea prices have been (2)__________ with the prices of other companies. Unlike last year, tea prices have generally shown (3) __________, when tea prices rose dramatically, this year, prices seem to have (4) __________ at a rather high level. In the subsequent four months, the (5)__________ average price showed a downtrend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Prices have been 'aligning with', that is moving in line with, the prices of other companies.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Tea prices in the domestic (1)__________ continue to rule high in the current year despite the expectation of a higher production as compared to the previous year. During the past three months, tea prices have been (2)__________ with the prices of other companies. Unlike last year, tea prices have generally shown (3) __________, when tea prices rose dramatically, this year, prices seem to have (4) __________ at a rather high level. In the subsequent four months, the (5)__________ average price showed a downtrend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Shown an uptrend' fits the passage's point that tea prices continue to rule high.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Tea prices in the domestic (1)__________ continue to rule high in the current year despite the expectation of a higher production as compared to the previous year. During the past three months, tea prices have been (2)__________ with the prices of other companies. Unlike last year, tea prices have generally shown (3) __________, when tea prices rose dramatically, this year, prices seem to have (4) __________ at a rather high level. In the subsequent four months, the (5)__________ average price showed a downtrend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: After last year's dramatic rise, prices this year 'seem to have stabilised', settled, 'at a rather high level'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Tea prices in the domestic (1)__________ continue to rule high in the current year despite the expectation of a higher production as compared to the previous year. During the past three months, tea prices have been (2)__________ with the prices of other companies. Unlike last year, tea prices have generally shown (3) __________, when tea prices rose dramatically, this year, prices seem to have (4) __________ at a rather high level. In the subsequent four months, the (5)__________ average price showed a downtrend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The passage follows prices month by month, so 'the monthly average price'.

questions.text: How many medals did India win in the 2012 Summer Olympics?
questions.explanation: India won 6 medals at the London 2012 Olympics: 2 silver and 4 bronze.

questions.text: What is the rank of India in the Human Development Index 2019?
questions.explanation: In UNDP's Human Development Report 2019, released in December 2019, India ranked 129th of 189 countries, up from 130th.

questions.text: Constantan is an alloy of copper and _______.
questions.explanation: Constantan is an alloy of about 55% copper and 45% nickel; its resistance hardly changes with temperature, so it is used in precision resistors, and it is also used in thermocouples.

questions.text: Who among the following was the mascot of the Men's Hockey World Cup held at Bhubaneswar in 2018?
questions.explanation: The mascot of the 2018 Men's Hockey World Cup in Bhubaneswar was Olly, an olive ridley turtle. Borobi was the mascot of the 2018 Commonwealth Games and Shera of the 2010 Commonwealth Games.

questions.text: The rating for a fuse used in a household electric circuit is provided on the basis of:
questions.explanation: A fuse is rated by the largest current it can carry, in amperes (for example 5 A or 15 A); a larger current melts its wire and breaks the circuit.

questions.text: What is the rank of India in the Global Peace Index 2019?
questions.explanation: In the Global Peace Index 2019, published in June 2019 by the Institute for Economics and Peace, India ranked 141st of 163 countries.

questions.text: Which of the following is the lowermost layer of the Atmosphere?
questions.explanation: The troposphere, where weather occurs, is the lowest layer of the atmosphere; above it come the stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere and exosphere.

questions.text: Who among the following is the Chief Minister of Mizoram as on November 2019?
questions.explanation: Zoramthanga ('Pu' is a Mizo title of respect) of the Mizo National Front became Chief Minister of Mizoram in December 2018, so he held the office in November 2019. Conrad Sangma was Chief Minister of Meghalaya and Neiphiu Rio of Nagaland; Laldenga, who led Mizoram when it became a state in 1987, died in 1990.

questions.text: Which of the following ministries is NOT associated with the initiative of Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao Scheme?
options: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Women and Child Development
questions.explanation: Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao was launched in 2015 as a joint initiative of the Ministries of Women and Child Development, Health and Family Welfare, and Human Resource Development; the Ministry of Rural Development had no part in it.

questions.text: In July 2019, which of the following schemes was launched to accelerate water harvesting and conservation measures?
questions.explanation: The Jal Shakti Abhiyan, launched in July 2019, was a campaign for water conservation and rainwater harvesting in the country's water-stressed districts.

questions.text: Who of the following authored the book 'Revolution 2020'?
questions.explanation: 'Revolution 2020' (2011) is a novel by Chetan Bhagat.

questions.text: Under which Amendment to the Constitution of India was Goods and Services Tax imposed?
questions.explanation: GST was brought in by the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016, which inserted Article 246A.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers was known as Purushni in the Vedic period?
questions.explanation: In the Rigveda the Ravi is called the Parushni (Purushni); the Chenab was the Asikni, the Beas the Vipas and the Sutlej the Shutudri.

questions.text: In 2019, IIT-Madras launched the country's first indigenously designed standing wheelchair named as:
questions.explanation: Arise, launched by IIT-Madras in November 2019, lets a wheelchair user move between sitting and standing without help.

questions.text: In which state is the festival of Uttarayan uniquely celebrated?
questions.explanation: Uttarayan, Gujarat's name for Makar Sankranti, is celebrated there with kite flying, including the International Kite Festival at Ahmedabad.

questions.text: Who among the following is NOT a recipient of the 2019 Mother Teresa Memorial Awards for Social Justice?
questions.explanation: The 2019 Mother Teresa Memorial Awards, on the theme of combating modern forms of slavery, went to campaigners against child labour and trafficking, among them Kailash Satyarthi, Ajeet Singh and Priti Patkar of Prerana. Medha Patkar, of the Narmada Bachao Andolan, was not among them.

questions.text: What does 'C' stand for in ITCZ?
questions.explanation: ITCZ stands for the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone, the low-pressure belt near the equator where the trade winds of the two hemispheres converge.

questions.text: Which tales are related with the painting and sculptures of the Ajanta caves?
questions.explanation: The paintings and sculptures of Ajanta illustrate the Jataka tales, stories of the Buddha's previous births.

questions.text: Which of the following states does NOT share its boundary with Nepal?
questions.explanation: Nepal borders five Indian states: Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Sikkim. Assam does not touch it.

questions.text: Which among the following is a non-biodegradable waste?
questions.explanation: Plastic is not broken down by microorganisms, so it is non-biodegradable; flowers, vegetables and dead animals decompose.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who signed the treaty of Alinagar with the British?
questions.explanation: Siraj-ud-Daula, Nawab of Bengal, signed the Treaty of Alinagar with the East India Company in February 1757, after Clive retook Calcutta, which the Nawab had renamed Alinagar.

questions.text: Who among the following initiated 'Din-i-Ilahi'?
questions.explanation: Akbar started the Din-i-Ilahi in 1582, a path that drew on several religions.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following events did NOT occur in 1919?
questions.explanation: The Partition of Bengal took place in 1905 (and was annulled in 1911). The Rowlatt Act was passed and the Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in 1919, and the Montagu-Chelmsford reforms were enacted by the Government of India Act, 1919.

questions.text: 'Pedology' is the science of:
questions.explanation: Pedology (from the Greek 'pedon', soil) is the study of soils: how they form, their properties and their classification.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Having something more than required
questions.explanation: A 'surplus' is an amount more than is needed. A surcharge is an extra charge, and a surrogate a substitute.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. We must get this post send as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: After 'get' and its object, a passive sense needs the past participle: 'get this post sent as soon as possible'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. I was sitting at home doing nothing when I “had heard” that song again.
questions.explanation: An action that interrupts one in progress takes the simple past: 'I was sitting … when I heard that song again.' The past perfect would put the hearing before the sitting.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. They also visit ailing friends and relatives, or attend to personal matters even during office hours. B. Once in office, they receive friends and relatives who call them any time without prior appointment. C. We can frequently find a large number of people sitting here and there and doing nothing. D. Even those who are employed often come late to office and leave early unless they are forced to be punctual.
questions.explanation: C introduces the people doing nothing, D turns to those who are employed, B says what they do once in office and A, with 'also', adds more: CDBA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Abort
questions.explanation: To 'abort' something is to end it before it is finished.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. “What are you going to call the puppy, Jane?” the boy asked.
options: The boy told Jane what she was going to call her puppy.
Jane asked the boy what is he going to call the puppy.
The boy asked Jane what she was going to call the puppy.
The boy wondered what Jane were going to call the puppy.
questions.explanation: The question is reported with 'asked Jane', 'you are' becomes 'she was', and the word order becomes that of a statement.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. In a way, adult education is an educational movement through the medium (1)______ village schools. In the beginning, the (2)______ were suspicious. It was hard to persuade (3)______ to realise that they were really getting something (4)______ the schools. They were not at all sure that they wanted their (5)______ to leave their homes.

Select the most appropriate option for the blank numbered 1.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is 'through the medium of', meaning by means of: 'through the medium of village schools'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. In a way, adult education is an educational movement through the medium (1)______ village schools. In the beginning, the (2)______ were suspicious. It was hard to persuade (3)______ to realise that they were really getting something (4)______ the schools. They were not at all sure that they wanted their (5)______ to leave their homes.

Select the most appropriate option for the blank numbered 2.
questions.explanation: The schools were for the village adults, so it was the 'villagers' who were suspicious at first; the passage goes on to speak of their children.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. In a way, adult education is an educational movement through the medium (1)______ village schools. In the beginning, the (2)______ were suspicious. It was hard to persuade (3)______ to realise that they were really getting something (4)______ the schools. They were not at all sure that they wanted their (5)______ to leave their homes.

Select the most appropriate option for the blank numbered 3.
questions.explanation: 'Persuade' takes an object, and the pronoun for the villagers is 'them'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. In a way, adult education is an educational movement through the medium (1)______ village schools. In the beginning, the (2)______ were suspicious. It was hard to persuade (3)______ to realise that they were really getting something (4)______ the schools. They were not at all sure that they wanted their (5)______ to leave their homes.

Select the most appropriate option for the blank numbered 4.
questions.explanation: One gets something 'from' a source: 'getting something from the schools'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. In a way, adult education is an educational movement through the medium (1)______ village schools. In the beginning, the (2)______ were suspicious. It was hard to persuade (3)______ to realise that they were really getting something (4)______ the schools. They were not at all sure that they wanted their (5)______ to leave their homes.

Select the most appropriate option for the blank numbered 5.
questions.explanation: The villagers were not sure they wanted their 'children' to leave home.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'guidance'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. One evening, when father was coming home from work, I “played” in the front garden.
questions.explanation: Two actions in progress at the same time in the past both take the past continuous: 'when father was coming home from work, I was playing in the front garden'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. Accommodation and food were given free. B. This was held in a hostel for poor students built by a philanthropist. C. A few years ago, I was the chief guest at a small function. D. But the inmates of the hostel had to bear other expenses like clothing and toiletries.
questions.explanation: C sets the scene, B says where the function was held, A says what the hostel gave free and D, with 'But', what the inmates still had to pay for: CBAD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Emerge
questions.explanation: To 'emerge' is to come into view; its opposite is to 'disappear'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Mellow
questions.explanation: 'Mellow' means soft and gentle; its opposite is 'hard'. 'Soft' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Suzerainty is having political control over a ______ state.
questions.explanation: Suzerainty is a dominant state's control over a 'dependent' state, which usually keeps its own internal government.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. My cousin’s study on the reading habits of school children across three states has been recognised as a ______ piece of research.
questions.explanation: A study recognised for breaking new ground is 'pioneering'.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Sita has no taste in classical dance.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'in': for a liking for something, 'taste' takes 'for', as in 'Sita has no taste for classical dance'. 'Taste in' is also used, of judgement in matters of style ('good taste in clothes'), so the sentence can be defended, but there is no 'No error' option and none of the other parts could be at fault.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom. Blind alley
options: A person who comes to meet occasionally
A situation in which no further progress can be made
Taking first step after somebody’s approach
questions.explanation: A 'blind alley' is literally a dead end: a course of action that leads nowhere.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom. The acid test
options: A fact, event or situation that proves something
questions.explanation: The 'acid test' is a decisive test that proves the worth or truth of something, from the use of acid to test gold.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Exceed
questions.explanation: To 'exceed' is to go beyond: to 'surpass'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Anger about an unfair situation or about someone’s unfair behaviour
questions.explanation: 'Indignation' is anger at unfair treatment. 'Indulgence' is giving way to one's desires, and 'induction' a formal introduction or a kind of reasoning.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. The commander ordered his soldiers to move forward and attack the enemy camps.
options: The commander was ordered by his soldiers to move forward and attack the enemy camps.
The commander ordered his soldiers to be moved forward and attacked the enemy camps.
The soldiers were ordered by their commander to move forward and attack the enemy camps.
His soldiers were ordered by the commander to be moved forward and attacked the enemy camps.
questions.explanation: The object 'his soldiers' becomes the subject and 'ordered' becomes 'were ordered'; the infinitives 'to move forward and attack' stay active.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers forms the Dhuandhar waterfall near Jabalpur?
questions.explanation: The Narmada forms the Dhuandhar Falls at Bhedaghat, near Jabalpur in Madhya Pradesh, as it enters its gorge of marble rocks.

questions.text: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana offers a protection term insurance cover of ______ to the insurer.
questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, launched in 2015, is a one-year renewable term life cover of ₹2 lakh for death from any cause.

questions.text: What does 'T' stand for in ATM?
questions.explanation: ATM stands for Automated Teller Machine: it does a bank teller's work, such as paying out cash.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs is CORRECT with reference to mountain passes?
questions.explanation: Lipulekh Pass, in Pithoragarh district of Uttarakhand, is on the route to Kailash Mansarovar. Bomdila is in Arunachal Pradesh, Nathu La in Sikkim and Rohtang in Himachal Pradesh.

questions.text: The scientific study of a cell is called:
questions.explanation: Cytology is the study of cells; histology studies tissues, physiology the working of living things and taxonomy their classification.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas is celebrated on:
questions.explanation: Pravasi Bharatiya Divas is marked on 9 January, the day in 1915 when Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa.

questions.text: Which of the following states does NOT share its boundary with Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: Bangladesh borders West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. Manipur borders Myanmar, not Bangladesh.

questions.text: For which game has the Father of Leander Paes been a member of the Indian National Team?
questions.explanation: Vece Paes, Leander Paes's father, played hockey for India and won a bronze medal at the 1972 Munich Olympics.

questions.text: Where is the Dharmraja Ratha monument located?
questions.explanation: The Dharmaraja Ratha is one of the Pancha Rathas, monolithic rock-cut temples carved under the Pallavas in the 7th century at Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram), Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: Which among the following is a cation?
questions.explanation: A cation is a positively charged ion. Ammonium (NH₄⁺) is positive; fluoride, chloride and iodide are negative ions, anions.

questions.text: In December 2019, the Rohtang passageway in Himachal Pradesh was renamed as:
questions.explanation: On 25 December 2019, Atal Bihari Vajpayee's birth anniversary, the government named the tunnel under the Rohtang Pass the Atal Tunnel.

questions.text: Select the correct pair of dance form and its state.
questions.explanation: Padayani is a ritual masked dance of the Bhagavati temples of central Kerala. Thang Ta is a martial art of Manipur, Dalkhai a folk dance of Odisha and Kalbelia a dance of Rajasthan.

questions.text: The Council of Ministers during the time of Shivaji Maharaj was known as:
questions.explanation: Shivaji's council of eight ministers was the Ashta Pradhan. The Navaratnas were the nine gems of Akbar's court, and the Ashta Diggajas the eight poets of Krishnadevaraya's court.

questions.text: With reference to the Vedangas, which of the following terms denotes 'Ritual'?
questions.explanation: Of the six Vedangas, Kalpa deals with ritual; Shiksha is phonetics, Vyakarana grammar and Chhanda metre (the other two are Nirukta, etymology, and Jyotisha, astronomy).

questions.text: The power of a lens is –2.0 D. Here 'D' stands for:
questions.explanation: The power of a lens, P = 1/f with f in metres, is measured in dioptres. A lens of −2.0 D is a concave (diverging) lens of focal length 0.5 m.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Indian National Congress session of September 1920 was held at ______.
questions.explanation: The special session at Calcutta in September 1920, presided over by Lala Lajpat Rai, adopted Gandhi's programme of Non-Cooperation; the regular session at Nagpur in December 1920 confirmed it.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book 'Wise and Otherwise: A Salute to Life'?
questions.explanation: 'Wise and Otherwise: A Salute to Life' is a collection of real-life stories by Sudha Murty.

questions.text: Which of the following monasteries is located in Sikkim?
questions.explanation: Rumtek Monastery, near Gangtok, is in Sikkim. Tabo and Kye (Key) are in Spiti, Himachal Pradesh, and Hemis is in Ladakh.

questions.text: Which among the following has its refractive index closest to that of crown glass?
questions.explanation: Canada balsam has a refractive index of about 1.53, very close to crown glass's 1.52, which is why it is used to cement lenses. Ruby and sapphire are about 1.77 and diamond 2.42.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India guarantees the Right to Freedom of Religion?
questions.explanation: Articles 25 to 28 guarantee the Right to Freedom of Religion. Articles 14-18 cover the Right to Equality, 19-22 the Right to Freedom and 23-24 the Right against Exploitation.

questions.text: In which year was the first amendment to the Constitution of India made?
questions.explanation: The Constitution (First Amendment) Act was passed in 1951; among other changes it added the Ninth Schedule.

questions.text: The Pritzker prize is an international award given to recognise contribution in the field of ______.
questions.explanation: The Pritzker Architecture Prize, founded in 1979, is given each year to a living architect and is often called the Nobel Prize of architecture.

questions.text: Which Indian male cricketer won the BCCI CK Nayudu Lifetime Achievement Award for the year 2019?
questions.explanation: Former India captain K Srikkanth received the Col. C.K. Nayudu Lifetime Achievement Award at the BCCI awards in Mumbai on 12 January 2020, which honoured the 2018-19 season.

questions.text: Who was appointed as brand ambassador of Visa - the payment technology company in 2019?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives P.V. Sindhu: in September 2019 Visa signed her, then the world badminton champion, to Team Visa for the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, and press reports named her its brand ambassador.

questions.text: Which among the following is NOT an insulator?
questions.explanation: Mercury is a metal, liquid at room temperature, and conducts electricity. Ebonite, glass and dry paper are insulators.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'across'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Look down upon
options: To look down from a height
questions.explanation: To 'look down upon' someone is to regard them as inferior.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Sacred
questions.explanation: 'Sacred' means connected with God or religion and worthy of reverence: 'holy'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one word substitute for the given group of words. A game in which neither party wins
questions.explanation: A game that ends with neither side winning is a 'draw'.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. The children sang the National Anthem with great enthusiasm.
options: The National Anthem was being sung with great enthusiasm by the children.
The National Anthem was sung with great enthusiasm by the children.
The National Anthem is sung with great enthusiasm by the children.
The National Anthem has been sung with great enthusiasm by the children.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'sang' becomes 'was sung' in the passive: 'The National Anthem was sung with great enthusiasm by the children.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Native
questions.explanation: 'Native' means belonging to a place by birth; its opposite is 'foreign'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Advertising is the promotion of goods and services. It provides an (1)______ to the manufacturing companies to sell their (2)______ better than their competitors. Every time we switch (3)______ the television we find some product or the other (4)______ pushed towards us. It cannot be denied that the (5)______ behind commercial advertising is to increase sales and earn more profit.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (1).
questions.explanation: Advertising gives companies an 'opportunity', a chance, to sell their goods better than their competitors.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Advertising is the promotion of goods and services. It provides an (1)______ to the manufacturing companies to sell their (2)______ better than their competitors. Every time we switch (3)______ the television we find some product or the other (4)______ pushed towards us. It cannot be denied that the (5)______ behind commercial advertising is to increase sales and earn more profit.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (2).
questions.explanation: Companies sell their 'products': the goods and services the passage begins with.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Advertising is the promotion of goods and services. It provides an (1)______ to the manufacturing companies to sell their (2)______ better than their competitors. Every time we switch (3)______ the television we find some product or the other (4)______ pushed towards us. It cannot be denied that the (5)______ behind commercial advertising is to increase sales and earn more profit.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (3).
questions.explanation: A television is turned on with 'switch on'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Advertising is the promotion of goods and services. It provides an (1)______ to the manufacturing companies to sell their (2)______ better than their competitors. Every time we switch (3)______ the television we find some product or the other (4)______ pushed towards us. It cannot be denied that the (5)______ behind commercial advertising is to increase sales and earn more profit.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (4).
questions.explanation: The product is being acted upon as we watch, so the passive '-ing' form is needed: 'some product or the other being pushed towards us'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Advertising is the promotion of goods and services. It provides an (1)______ to the manufacturing companies to sell their (2)______ better than their competitors. Every time we switch (3)______ the television we find some product or the other (4)______ pushed towards us. It cannot be denied that the (5)______ behind commercial advertising is to increase sales and earn more profit.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (5).
questions.explanation: The 'motive' behind advertising is its purpose: to increase sales and earn more profit.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. The traveller said to a passerby, "Can you help me find my way, please?''
options: The traveller asked the passerby could you kindly help me find my way?
The traveller asked the passerby that he can kindly help him find his way.
The traveller asked the passerby if he could kindly help him find his way.
The traveller requested to the passerby if he can help him find his way.
questions.explanation: A yes-no question is reported with 'if', 'can' becomes 'could', 'me' and 'my' become 'him' and 'his', and 'please' becomes 'kindly'.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error' He married with a rich heiress last year.
questions.explanation: 'Marry' takes a direct object: 'He married a rich heiress last year', without 'with'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Weary
questions.explanation: 'Weary' means very tired: 'exhausted'.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error' The famous author and actor are being honoured at a function today
questions.explanation: With the article only once, 'the famous author and actor' is one person, so the verb is singular: 'is being honoured'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Repulsive
questions.explanation: 'Repulsive' means causing disgust; its opposite is 'attractive'. 'Hideous' and 'revolting' are close to synonyms.

questions.text: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word. She was loved by her employees for her ______.
questions.explanation: 'Benevolence' is kindness and goodwill, which would make her loved; 'malevolence' and 'insolence' would not, and 'condolence' is sympathy at a death.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Keep abreast of
questions.explanation: To 'keep abreast of' something is to keep oneself informed of the latest developments in it.

questions.text: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word. The minister gave an ______ that strict action would be taken against the culprits.
questions.explanation: An 'assurance' is a firm promise that something will be done; 'insurance' is cover against loss.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. When a calf is born under water, the mother must get it to the surface before it drowns. B. The young ones remain with their parents for up to fifteen years or more. C. Often another whale assists the mother nudging the baby gently and encouraging it to swim. D. Whales have highly developed maternal instincts.
questions.explanation: D introduces whales' maternal instincts, A describes the mother lifting the newborn calf to the surface, C adds that another whale often helps her, and B says how long the young stay with their parents: DACB.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one word substitute for the given group of words That which cannot be satisfied
questions.explanation: 'Insatiable' means impossible to satisfy.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. Scarcely had the passengers boarded the plane “when the captain welcomed them.”
options: when the captain had welcomed them
questions.explanation: 'Scarcely had ...' is followed by 'when', with the simple past for the second action: the sentence is correct as it stands.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. While he was doing this, he missed seeing a velvet purse full of gold coins lying on the road. B. Ramesh always worried about how he would become sick and weak in old age. C. To try how he would cope with blindness, Ramesh started walking with his eyes closed. D. He feared that he might even lose his sight and go blind.
questions.explanation: B gives Ramesh's worry about old age, D his fear of blindness, C how he tried walking with his eyes closed, and A what he missed while doing this: BDCA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. Mother was watching a movie when the lights “were going off.”
questions.explanation: A longer action in the past continuous is interrupted by a sudden one in the simple past: 'when the lights went off'.

questions.text: The SASTRA - Ramanujan Prize is awarded in the field of:
questions.explanation: The SASTRA Ramanujan Prize, given by SASTRA University since 2005, honours mathematicians aged 32 or under (Ramanujan's age when he died) for work in fields influenced by him.

questions.text: The first electron shell which is the nearest to the nucleus never holds more than 'n' electrons, where 'n' is equal to:
questions.explanation: A shell can hold at most 2 × (shell number)² electrons, so the first (K) shell, nearest the nucleus, holds at most 2 × 1² = 2.

questions.text: Which among the following is the food tube?
questions.explanation: The oesophagus, or food pipe, carries swallowed food from the pharynx to the stomach. The aorta is the main artery, the thymus a gland and the larynx the voice box.

questions.text: The Battle of Chausa was fought between Humayun and ______.
questions.explanation: At Chausa, near Buxar in Bihar, Sher Khan (later Sher Shah Suri) defeated Humayun in 1539.

questions.text: Which of the following is an east flowing river?
questions.explanation: The Brahmani flows east through Odisha into the Bay of Bengal. The Sabarmati and the Mahi flow west into the Gulf of Khambhat, and the Sharavati west into the Arabian Sea in Karnataka.

questions.text: In the context of rivers and their tributaries, which of the following pairs is correct?
questions.explanation: The Pindar joins the Alaknanda at Karnaprayag. The Subansiri is a tributary of the Brahmaputra, the Kabini of the Kaveri and the Manjra of the Godavari.

questions.text: Which country hosted the 13th South Asian Games?
questions.explanation: Nepal hosted the 13th South Asian Games in December 2019, in Kathmandu, Pokhara and Janakpur.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct with reference to the Karachi Session of the Congress (1931)?
options: Mahatma Gandhi presided over the session
The Khilafat movement was launched at this event
questions.explanation: The Karachi session of March 1931, presided over by Vallabhbhai Patel, endorsed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact and adopted the resolution on Fundamental Rights and Economic Policy. The Quit India Resolution came in 1942.

questions.text: How many degrees does the Earth rotate about its own axis in one hour?
questions.explanation: The Earth turns through 360° in about 24 hours: 360° ÷ 24 = 15° an hour.

questions.text: With which sport is Archana Kamath associated?
questions.explanation: Archana Kamath is an Indian table tennis player.

questions.text: Which female Indian cricketer won the BCCI C.K. Nayudu Lifetime Achievement Award for 2019?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Anjum Chopra. At the BCCI awards on 12 January 2020 (for the 2018-19 season) she received the Board's Lifetime Achievement Award for women; the C. K. Nayudu Lifetime Achievement Award itself went to Krishnamachari Srikkanth.

questions.text: Which ISO certification pertains to Environmental Management Systems?
questions.explanation: ISO 14001 sets out the requirements for an environmental management system. ISO 9001 covers quality management, ISO 27001 information security and ISO 22000 food safety.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book 'Hazaar Chaurasi Ki Maa'?
questions.explanation: 'Hazaar Chaurasi Ki Maa' is the Hindi title of Mahasweta Devi's Bengali novel 'Hajar Churashir Maa', about a mother whose Naxalite son is killed.

questions.text: Which of the following monuments is NOT a part of the Qutub Complex?
questions.explanation: The Buland Darwaza, built by Akbar, is at Fatehpur Sikri. The Alai Darwaza, the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque and the Qutub Minar stand in the Qutub complex in Delhi.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs is associated with the taxation system of the Marathas?
questions.explanation: The Marathas levied chauth (a quarter of the land revenue) and sardeshmukhi (a further tenth). Polaj and parauti were Mughal classes of land, iqta and jagir assignments of revenue, and zat and sawar mansabdari ranks.

questions.text: In which year was NABARD established?
questions.explanation: NABARD, the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development, was established on 12 July 1982.

questions.text: Under which Article can the Parliament amend the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 368, in Part XX, gives Parliament the power to amend the Constitution and lays down the procedure.

questions.text: Which of the following states does NOT share its boundary with Bhutan?
questions.explanation: Sikkim, West Bengal, Assam and Arunachal Pradesh border Bhutan; Meghalaya does not.

questions.text: Under which of the following Amendments to the Constitution of India is defection to another party after election made illegal?
questions.explanation: The 52nd Amendment (1985) added the Tenth Schedule, the anti-defection law, under which a legislator who defects is disqualified.

questions.text: Ozone at the higher level of the atmosphere is a product of ______ acting on oxygen molecules.
questions.explanation: In the stratosphere ultraviolet radiation splits oxygen molecules (O₂) into atoms, which join other O₂ molecules to form ozone (O₃).

questions.text: In July 2019, which among the following operations was launched by the BSF to fortify the Pakistan border in Punjab and Jammu?
questions.explanation: The BSF launched Operation Sudarshan on 1 July 2019 to strengthen its anti-infiltration grid along the Pakistan border in Punjab and Jammu.

questions.text: Which of the following is a heritage site of Madhya Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The Bhimbetka rock shelters, with their prehistoric paintings, are in Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Sasaram is in Bihar, Hampi in Karnataka and Lepakshi in Andhra Pradesh.

questions.text: In January 2020, with which country did India sign a MoU for content exchange programme between All India Radio and Betar?
questions.explanation: Betar (Bangladesh Betar) is Bangladesh's state radio, the counterpart of All India Radio. The two signed their content-sharing agreement on 14 January 2020, at a meeting of the Indian and Bangladeshi information and broadcasting ministers.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Act that transferred the power from the British East India Company to the British Crown in India was:
questions.explanation: After the revolt of 1857 the Government of India Act, 1858 ended the East India Company's rule and placed India under the Crown, with a Secretary of State for India.

questions.text: The Arid Forest Research Institute is located in ______.
questions.explanation: The Arid Forest Research Institute, under the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education, is at Jodhpur in Rajasthan.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. A child could understand his theory.
options: His theory was understood by a child.
His theory is being understood by a child.
His theory could be understood by a child.
His theory can be understood by a child.
questions.explanation: 'Could understand' becomes 'could be understood', keeping the modal: 'His theory could be understood by a child.'

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. We had a long discussion at a cup of coffee.
questions.explanation: A talk held while drinking something is 'over a cup of coffee', not 'at a cup'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Pull a fast one
questions.explanation: To 'pull a fast one' is to trick or deceive someone.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. These lotteries organised by State Governments sell dreams. B. Lured by this, millions of poor people waste their hard-earned money. C. Crores of rupees and gold are offered as prizes. D. People buy lotteries hoping to become rich overnight.
questions.explanation: D introduces lotteries, A ('These lotteries') says they sell dreams, C names the prizes and B ('Lured by this') gives the result: DACB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. FICKLE
questions.explanation: 'Fickle' means changing often and unpredictably; its opposite is 'stable'. 'Flighty' is a synonym.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Agra's marble-marvel has such an overwhelming presence (1)______ other monuments in the town have been relegated (2) ______ oblivion. Amongst such 60 odd monuments in (3) ______ town, the Red Taj is the most (4) ______ and relatively well-preserved. The tomb in red sandstone was (5) ______ by Ann Hessing, widow of a Dutch officer, after his death in 1803.

Select the correct option to fill in blank 2.
questions.explanation: The phrase is 'relegated to oblivion': pushed aside and forgotten.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Agra's marble-marvel has such an overwhelming presence (1)______ other monuments in the town have been relegated (2) ______ oblivion. Amongst such 60 odd monuments in (3) ______ town, the Red Taj is the most (4) ______ and relatively well-preserved. The tomb in red sandstone was (5) ______ by Ann Hessing, widow of a Dutch officer, after his death in 1803.

Select the correct option to fill in blank 3.
questions.explanation: 'The town' is the one already named, Agra, so it takes the definite article.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Agra's marble-marvel has such an overwhelming presence (1)______ other monuments in the town have been relegated (2) ______ oblivion. Amongst such 60 odd monuments in (3) ______ town, the Red Taj is the most (4) ______ and relatively well-preserved. The tomb in red sandstone was (5) ______ by Ann Hessing, widow of a Dutch officer, after his death in 1803.

Select the correct option to fill in blank 4.
questions.explanation: The Red Taj is 'the most elegant' of the monuments; 'active', 'efficient' and 'adequate' do not describe a tomb.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Agra's marble-marvel has such an overwhelming presence (1)______ other monuments in the town have been relegated (2) ______ oblivion. Amongst such 60 odd monuments in (3) ______ town, the Red Taj is the most (4) ______ and relatively well-preserved. The tomb in red sandstone was (5) ______ by Ann Hessing, widow of a Dutch officer, after his death in 1803.

Select the correct option to fill in blank 5.
questions.explanation: The passive 'was built by Ann Hessing' needs the past participle 'built'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. HASTE
questions.explanation: 'Haste' is hurry; its opposite is 'delay'. 'Rush' and 'dash' are near synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. “If they will get married” , they will probably settle in Mumbai.
options: If they will be getting married
questions.explanation: In a first conditional the 'if' clause takes the present simple, not 'will': 'If they get married, they will probably settle in Mumbai.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Have you ______ for a job in this company?
questions.explanation: One 'applies' for a job.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'delegate'.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The both children go to the same school.
questions.explanation: 'Both' comes before the article: 'Both the children' (or 'Both children'), not 'The both children'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. DISHEARTENED
questions.explanation: 'Disheartened' means having lost hope or confidence: low in spirits, 'depressed'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. These are generated by a violent undersea disturbance or ocean activity. B. Once generated, they travel outward on the ocean surface in all directions. C. A tsunami is made up of a series of very long waves. D. Spreading thus, they look like ripples caused by throwing a rock in a pond.
questions.explanation: C introduces the tsunami, A says how 'these' waves are generated, B how, 'once generated', they travel, and D ('Spreading thus') what they look like: CABD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. CORDIAL
questions.explanation: 'Cordial' means friendly and sincere: 'warm'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. They “stopped to laugh” as soon as the teacher entered the classroom.
questions.explanation: 'Stop' with the '-ing' form means to cease doing something; 'stopped to laugh' would mean they paused in order to laugh. They 'stopped laughing' when the teacher came in.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. See eye to eye
questions.explanation: To 'see eye to eye' with someone is to agree with them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate one word substitution for the given group of words. Pertaining to an individual from birth
questions.explanation: 'Congenital' describes a condition or trait present from birth.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate one word substitution for the given group of words. To increase the speed
questions.explanation: To 'accelerate' is to increase speed; to 'exhilarate' is to make very happy.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Mahesh said to Rita, "Don't play in the sun."
options: Mahesh told to Rita to not play in the sun.
Mahesh ordered Rita that not play in the sun.
Mahesh requested Rita that don't play in the sun.
Mahesh advised Rita not to play in the sun.
questions.explanation: A negative command is reported with a suitable reporting verb and 'not to' + verb: 'Mahesh advised Rita not to play in the sun.'

questions.text: The Indian Army is set to commission the first batch of women soldiers by year ______.
questions.explanation: When the exam was held (March 2020), the Army's first women soldiers, recruited for its Corps of Military Police, were due to join by 2021; the first batch of 83 was inducted in May 2021.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Definition' is spelt correctly; the others should be 'competitor', 'proliferate' and 'beneficiary'.

questions.text: Select the appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To take the bull by the horns
questions.explanation: To 'take the bull by the horns' is to face a difficult situation directly and with courage.

questions.text: Select the passive form of the given sentence. They are constructing a residential youth hostel.
options: A residential youth hostel has been constructed by them.
A residential youth hostel is being constructed by them.
A residential youth hostel is constructed by them.
A residential youth hostel was constructed by them.
questions.explanation: The present continuous 'are constructing' becomes 'is being constructed' in the passive, with the agent 'by them'.

questions.text: Select the correct synonym of the given word. Erudite
questions.explanation: 'Erudite' means having or showing great learning: 'learned'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. Although I had a fear of water, I thought it was an important skill I should learn. B. However, what I didn't realize was that it would also make me a more confident person. C. I also thought it would be a good exercise that would make me physically stronger. D. One of the hardest things I've had to do was to learn how to swim.
questions.explanation: D names the hard task, learning to swim; A gives the fear of water and the first reason, C adds a second ('also'), and B, with 'However', the result the writer had not expected: DACB.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Drug addiction is the continued use of a particular drug (1)______ harmful consequences.
