Drug addiction not only affects an individual’s health and relationship, but also (2)______ the society and the environment. Prevention of a particular list of drugs can be possible by (3)______ their sale without a prescription. Drug addicts should be given proper medical treatment and (4)______ facilities. Motivational and awareness camps should be organized to scale down the consumption (5)______ drugs.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1
questions.explanation: 'Despite' takes a noun directly: 'despite harmful consequences'. 'Despite of' is wrong, 'in spite' needs 'of', and 'though' needs a clause.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Drug addiction is the continued use of a particular drug (1)______ harmful consequences. Drug addiction not only affects an individual’s health and relationship, but also (2)______ the society and the environment. Prevention of a particular list of drugs can be possible by (3)______ their sale without a prescription. Drug addicts should be given proper medical treatment and (4)______ facilities. Motivational and awareness camps should be organized to scale down the consumption (5)______ drugs.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2
questions.explanation: 'Not only affects ... but also impacts': addiction affects society and the environment as well as the addict.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Drug addiction is the continued use of a particular drug (1)______ harmful consequences. Drug addiction not only affects an individual’s health and relationship, but also (2)______ the society and the environment. Prevention of a particular list of drugs can be possible by (3)______ their sale without a prescription. Drug addicts should be given proper medical treatment and (4)______ facilities. Motivational and awareness camps should be organized to scale down the consumption (5)______ drugs.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3
questions.explanation: Misuse of these drugs can be prevented by 'restricting' their sale without a prescription.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Drug addiction is the continued use of a particular drug (1)______ harmful consequences. Drug addiction not only affects an individual’s health and relationship, but also (2)______ the society and the environment. Prevention of a particular list of drugs can be possible by (3)______ their sale without a prescription. Drug addicts should be given proper medical treatment and (4)______ facilities. Motivational and awareness camps should be organized to scale down the consumption (5)______ drugs.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4
questions.explanation: Addicts need medical treatment and 'rehabilitation', help to return to a normal life.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Drug addiction is the continued use of a particular drug (1)______ harmful consequences. Drug addiction not only affects an individual’s health and relationship, but also (2)______ the society and the environment. Prevention of a particular list of drugs can be possible by (3)______ their sale without a prescription. Drug addicts should be given proper medical treatment and (4)______ facilities. Motivational and awareness camps should be organized to scale down the consumption (5)______ drugs.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5
questions.explanation: The phrase is 'the consumption of' something: 'the consumption of drugs'.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. No least than fifty participants were present for the singing competition.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is 'no less than': 'No less than fifty participants were present'.

questions.text: Select the correct synonym of the given word. Violent
questions.explanation: 'Violent' and 'aggressive' both describe forceful, hostile behaviour; 'mild', 'calm' and 'kind' are opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select No improvement. When I was working in a software company, it was mandatory to “register my legally” as an authorized software developer.
questions.explanation: The speaker registers himself or herself, so the reflexive 'myself' is needed, and the verb takes the adverb 'legally': 'to register myself legally'.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. “Hello”, he said to his friend. “What can I do for you?”
options: He said hello and asked his friend what can do for him.
He asked and greeted his friend that what he can do for him.
He told hello and asked his friend what he could do for him.
He greeted his friend and asked what he could do for him.
questions.explanation: 'Hello' becomes the verb 'greeted', the question becomes a statement after 'asked what', and 'can I ... for you' shifts to 'he could ... for him'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select No improvement. “Many of a students” were not shortlisted for the personal interview.
questions.explanation: 'Many of' needs a determiner such as 'the' before the plural noun: 'Many of the students'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the groups of words given. A long and aggressive speech
questions.explanation: A 'harangue' is a long, forceful speech that attacks or lectures its listeners.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The old man did not wanted to eat any food.
questions.explanation: After the auxiliary 'did' the main verb takes its base form: 'did not want'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. All his endeavors to win his teacher's favour proved ______ and did not bring the desired results.
questions.explanation: Efforts that did not bring the desired results proved 'futile', that is useless.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. During the celebration, many people display a set of ornamental dolls known as 'Hina' dolls. B. Hinamatsuri is a celebration of the girls in Japan wishing them a bright future. C. These royal-looking dolls are dressed in the clothing of the Heian period. D. These dolls represent the Emperor, Empress and other royal representatives.
questions.explanation: B introduces Hinamatsuri, A the dolls displayed during it, D whom the dolls represent, and C, 'these royal-looking dolls', how they are dressed: BADC.

questions.text: Select the correct antonym of the given word. Allure
questions.explanation: To 'allure' is to attract or tempt; its opposite is to 'repulse', to drive away or disgust. 'Attract' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the groups of words given. The school or college in which one has been educated
questions.explanation: One's 'alma mater' is the school, college or university one attended; 'alumni' are its former students.

questions.text: Select the correct antonym of the given word. Bizarre
questions.explanation: 'Bizarre' means very strange; its opposite is 'usual'. 'Strange' and 'weird' are synonyms.

questions.text: Select the appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To flog a dead horse
options: To make the best use of resources
questions.explanation: To 'flog a dead horse' is to waste effort on something that has already failed or been settled.

questions.text: Name the author of the 2019 released book - 'The Scent of God'.
questions.explanation: 'The Scent of God' (2019), a novel set in a boys' boarding school run by a Hindu monastic order, is by Saikat Majumdar.

questions.text: Which of the following is an INCORRECT sequence of Mughal rulers?
questions.explanation: The Mughal emperors ruled in the order Babur, Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan, Aurangzeb. Jahangir came before his son Shah Jahan, so 'Akbar, Shah Jahan, Jahangir' is out of order.

questions.text: How many members did the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have as of January 2020?
questions.explanation: The IMF had 189 member countries in January 2020, Nauru having joined as the 189th in 2016. (Andorra became the 190th in October 2020.)

questions.text: What is the name of the phenomena in physics and astronomy which involves the splitting of a spectral line into two or more components of slightly different frequency when the light source is placed in a magnetic field?
questions.explanation: The Zeeman effect, found by Pieter Zeeman in 1896, is the splitting of a spectral line when the source is in a magnetic field. The Raman effect is a change in the wavelength of scattered light.

questions.text: The 3rd Khelo India Youth Games 2020 is hosted by which Indian state?
questions.explanation: The third Khelo India Youth Games were held in Guwahati, Assam, in January 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following is an Indian Research Station in the Antarctica Region?
questions.explanation: Maitri, opened in 1989, and Bharati are India's working research stations in Antarctica. Orcadas is an Argentine station and Mawson an Australian one.

questions.text: The American scientist Edwin Hubble's name is associated with which of these theories?
questions.explanation: In 1929 Hubble showed that galaxies are moving away from us at speeds proportional to their distance (Hubble's law). This expansion of the universe is one of the main pieces of evidence for the Big Bang theory.

questions.text: Name the company that has acquired an online travel portal Yatra Online Inc., for an enterprise value of $337.8 million, in an all-stock transaction.
questions.explanation: In July 2019 the US company Ebix Inc. agreed to buy Yatra Online in this all-stock deal; when the exam was held (March 2020) the merger had been agreed but not completed. (It never closed: Yatra called it off in June 2020.)

questions.text: Former union minister and former Karnataka CM, D.V. Sadananda Gowda is a cabinet minister in the current central cabinet (February-2020). What is his portfolio?
questions.explanation: In February 2020 D. V. Sadananda Gowda was Union Minister of Chemicals and Fertilizers, a post he held from May 2019 to July 2021.

questions.text: Which of these is the energy conversion that happens in the process called photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: In photosynthesis green plants use the energy of sunlight to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water, storing light energy as chemical energy.

questions.text: When does the entire earth experience equal days and nights?
questions.explanation: At the equinoxes, about 21 March and 23 September, the Sun is overhead at the equator and day and night are of equal length all over the earth. At the solstices the days are longest in one hemisphere and shortest in the other.

questions.text: Who is the only scientist in the world to have won the Nobel prize in Chemistry twice?
questions.explanation: When the exam was held (March 2020), Frederick Sanger was the only person to have won the Chemistry prize twice: in 1958, for the structure of insulin, and in 1980, for sequencing DNA. Marie Curie won Physics and Chemistry, and Linus Pauling Chemistry and Peace. (Barry Sharpless became the second double Chemistry laureate in 2022.)

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was the then Governor-General of British India, when ‘Sati Pratha’ became illegal and punishable?
questions.explanation: Lord William Bentinck's Bengal Sati Regulation of 1829 declared sati illegal and punishable by the criminal courts.

questions.text: From which of the following states does 2019 Padma Vibhushan winner, Teejan Bai hail?
questions.explanation: Teejan Bai, the Pandavani singer who performs the Mahabharata, is from Chhattisgarh; she received the Padma Vibhushan in 2019.

questions.text: Iranian Major General Qasem Soleimani was recently (2020) assassinated by the US military in ______.
questions.explanation: Qasem Soleimani was killed in a US drone strike at Baghdad airport, Iraq, on 3 January 2020.

questions.text: Who among the following is the current (January 2020) Governor of Kerala?
questions.explanation: In January 2020 the Governor of Kerala was Arif Mohammed Khan, appointed in September 2019.

questions.text: Four multi-storied illegal constructions - Jain Coral Cove, H20 Holy Faith, Alfa Serene and Golden Kayaloram - were razed to the ground in January 2020 following Supreme Court instructions. In which state did this happen?
questions.explanation: The four apartment complexes at Maradu, near Kochi in Kerala, had been built in breach of Coastal Regulation Zone rules; on the Supreme Court's orders they were brought down by controlled implosion in January 2020.

questions.text: What is the name of the phenomena (driven by the scattering of light) in which mountain tops acquire a rosy or orange hue around sunrise and sunset?
questions.explanation: Alpenglow is the rosy or orange glow on high peaks just before sunrise or after sunset, when they catch light scattered in the atmosphere. Barrel distortion and the circle of confusion are terms from optics and photography.

questions.text: Name the two Indian actors who shared the National Best Actor Award (Male) in the 66th National Film Awards 2019.
questions.explanation: At the 66th National Film Awards (for 2018), Ayushmann Khurrana ('Andhadhun') and Vicky Kaushal ('Uri: The Surgical Strike') shared the Best Actor award.

questions.text: Bhavai and Kalbelia as traditional dance forms, owe their genesis to which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Bhavai, in which dancers balance a stack of pots on their heads, and Kalbelia, the dance of the Kalbelia snake-charmer community, are folk dances of Rajasthan.

questions.text: Who is the author of the delightful and anecdotal history of Indian cricket titled - 'A Corner of a Foreign Field: The Indian History of a British Sport'?
questions.explanation: Ramachandra Guha's 'A Corner of a Foreign Field' (2002) traces the history of cricket in India from colonial times.

questions.text: The city of Vijayawada lies on the banks of which of these rivers?
questions.explanation: Vijayawada, in Andhra Pradesh, stands on the Krishna, where the Prakasam Barrage crosses the river.

questions.text: Only one Indian batsman has scored a triple century in test cricket other than Virender Sehwag. Name this batsman.
questions.explanation: Karun Nair scored 303 not out against England at Chennai in December 2016; when the exam was held (March 2020) he and Virender Sehwag were India's only Test triple-centurions.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following is known as the 'father of Muslim renaissance' in Bengal?
questions.explanation: Nawab Abdul Latif, who founded the Mohammedan Literary Society in Calcutta in 1863 to spread modern education among Muslims, is called the father of the Muslim renaissance in Bengal.

questions.text: The recently revoked 'Article 370' is associated with which of these states of India?
questions.explanation: Article 370 gave Jammu and Kashmir its special status. It was made inoperative in August 2019, and the state was reorganised into two Union Territories.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. Upon returning from his travels, he was forced to live in a house where his large family lived. B. Vaikom Muhammad Basheer was a Malayalam fiction writer from Vaikom in Kerala. C. The household was always noisy and full of chaos, no place for a writer surely! D. Apart from family members, myriads of domestic animals also treated the house as their own.
questions.explanation: B introduces Basheer, A tells how he came home to live with his large family, D adds the many animals that shared the house, and C concludes that it was no place for a writer: BADC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Sparse
questions.explanation: 'Sparse' means thinly scattered or scanty; its opposite is 'abundant'. 'Scanty' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. Did the problems you had to face discourage you?
options: Have you been discouraged by the problems you have to face?
Were you discouraged by the problems you had to face?
Are you being discouraged by the problems you had to face?
Are you discouraged by the problems you had to face?
questions.explanation: The simple past question 'Did … discourage you?' becomes 'Were you discouraged by …?'; the clause 'you had to face' stays in the past.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Being a millionaire, he is leading a ______ life.
questions.explanation: A millionaire leads a 'luxurious' life, one of comfort and costly pleasures; 'destitute' means very poor.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'itinerant'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. One who is preoccupied with his own interests
questions.explanation: An egoist is self-centred, concerned chiefly with his own interests.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Milton Hershey returned to the village where he had been born, in the heart of dairy country. He opened his chocolate manufacturing plant (1)______ 1905. With access to all the fresh milk he (2)______, he began producing the finest milk chocolate. The plant (3)______ opened in a small Pennsylvania village is today the (4)______ chocolate factory in the world. The confections created here are (5)______ around the world.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 1.
questions.explanation: A year takes 'in': 'in 1905'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Milton Hershey returned to the village where he had been born, in the heart of dairy country. He opened his chocolate manufacturing plant (1)______ 1905. With access to all the fresh milk he (2)______, he began producing the finest milk chocolate. The plant (3)______ opened in a small Pennsylvania village is today the (4)______ chocolate factory in the world. The confections created here are (5)______ around the world.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 2.
questions.explanation: 'All the fresh milk he needed'; 'kneaded', which sounds the same, means worked like dough.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Milton Hershey returned to the village where he had been born, in the heart of dairy country. He opened his chocolate manufacturing plant (1)______ 1905. With access to all the fresh milk he (2)______, he began producing the finest milk chocolate. The plant (3)______ opened in a small Pennsylvania village is today the (4)______ chocolate factory in the world. The confections created here are (5)______ around the world.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 3.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun for a thing is 'that': 'The plant that opened in a small Pennsylvania village'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Milton Hershey returned to the village where he had been born, in the heart of dairy country. He opened his chocolate manufacturing plant (1)______ 1905. With access to all the fresh milk he (2)______, he began producing the finest milk chocolate. The plant (3)______ opened in a small Pennsylvania village is today the (4)______ chocolate factory in the world. The confections created here are (5)______ around the world.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 4.
questions.explanation: Compared with every other factory 'in the world', the superlative: 'the largest'. 'Most largest' is a double superlative.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Milton Hershey returned to the village where he had been born, in the heart of dairy country. He opened his chocolate manufacturing plant (1)______ 1905. With access to all the fresh milk he (2)______, he began producing the finest milk chocolate. The plant (3)______ opened in a small Pennsylvania village is today the (4)______ chocolate factory in the world. The confections created here are (5)______ around the world.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 5.
questions.explanation: The confections are popular everywhere: 'favourites around the world'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A geometrical figure with eight sides
questions.explanation: An octagon has eight sides; a pentagon has five, a hexagon six and a heptagon seven.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Solitary
questions.explanation: 'Solitary' means single, the only one ('a solitary example'): 'singular'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hold water
questions.explanation: An argument that 'holds water' stands up to examination: it is valid.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Fury
questions.explanation: 'Fury' is violent anger.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. I am believing you have submitted all the necessary documents.
questions.explanation: 'Believe' is a stative verb and is not used in the continuous tense: 'I believe you have submitted all the necessary documents.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Bring to light
questions.explanation: To 'bring to light' is to reveal or make known.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. The lawyer said to me, "There is no proof of your involvement in this case."
options: The lawyer told that there is no proof of my involvement in that case.
The lawyer told me that there is no proof of your involvement in this case.
The lawyer said me that there was no proof of my involvement in this case.
The lawyer told me that there was no proof of my involvement in that case.
questions.explanation: 'Said to me' becomes 'told me', 'is' becomes 'was', 'your' becomes 'my' and 'this' becomes 'that'.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. No sooner did we receive your message when we heaved a sigh of relief.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner' is followed by 'than', not 'when': 'No sooner did we receive your message than we heaved a sigh of relief.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'. Your advice will “benefit to me.”
questions.explanation: 'Benefit' takes a direct object, without 'to': 'Your advice will benefit me.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Friendship
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'friendship' is 'enmity'; 'amity' is a synonym.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. Even the most ill-equipped laboratory would have been better than their shed. B. Thus, they did not allow any difficulties to come in their way. C. But their mind was set upon the discovery of radium. D. The Curies had to work in extreme poverty.
questions.explanation: D states the Curies' poverty, A describes their shed, C ('But') turns to their resolve to discover radium, and B ('Thus') concludes that no difficulty stopped them: DACB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Children under five years are ______ from passport biometrics.
questions.explanation: To be 'exempted' from a requirement is to be freed from it; 'acquitted' is said of a person cleared of a charge.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No substitution. “Where you left” your bag yesterday?
questions.explanation: A question in the simple past needs 'did' with the base form of the verb: 'Where did you leave your bag yesterday?'

questions.text: What was India's position in the Brand Finance Nation ranking of 2019?
questions.explanation: In Brand Finance's Nation Brands 2019 ranking India rose two places, from ninth to seventh, with a brand value of about US$2.6 trillion.

questions.text: Who among the following was the last ruler of the Nanda dynasty?
questions.explanation: Dhanananda was the last Nanda king of Magadha; Chandragupta Maurya, with Chanakya's help, overthrew him and founded the Maurya empire.

questions.text: Which of the following was previously known as 'the Lady Willingdon Park'?
questions.explanation: Lodhi Gardens in New Delhi, around the tombs of the Sayyid and Lodi rulers, was laid out in 1936 as Lady Willingdon Park, after the Viceroy's wife, and renamed after independence.

questions.text: 'Industry 4.0' is a complex cyber-physical system which synergies production with digital technologies. The Ministry of Railways and the Department of Science and Technology have joined hands in partnership with which institution for taking up a unique project on 'Industry 4.0'?
questions.explanation: In September 2019 the Ministry of Railways and the Department of Science and Technology launched an 'Industry 4.0' pilot project with IIT Kanpur at the Modern Coach Factory, Raebareli.

questions.text: In January 2020, Home Minister Amit Shah released a book ‘Karmayoddha Granth’. This book is based on the life of ________.
questions.explanation: 'Karmayoddha Granth', released by Amit Shah in New Delhi on 7 January 2020, is a book on the life of Narendra Modi, Prime Minister when the exam was held (March 2020).

questions.text: Ajatashatru, a ruler of the Haryanka Dynasty, was the son of _____.
questions.explanation: Ajatashatru succeeded his father Bimbisara on the throne of Magadha; Udayin was Ajatashatru's own son and successor.

questions.text: In which state has the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) opened the first silk processing plant?
questions.explanation: In January 2020 KVIC opened Gujarat's first silk processing plant, at Surendranagar, to bring down the cost of silk yarn for Patola weavers.

questions.text: Borra caves are situated on the East Coast of India in which of the following hills?
questions.explanation: The Borra Caves lie in the Ananthagiri Hills of the Araku Valley in Andhra Pradesh, in the Eastern Ghats; the area was in Visakhapatnam district when the exam was held (March 2020) and has been in Alluri Sitharama Raju district since 2022.

questions.text: Objects that shine in the night sky are known as:
questions.explanation: The sun, the moon and all the objects that shine in the night sky are called celestial bodies.

questions.text: Which law of physics states that the force between the two electric charges reduces to a quarter of its former value when the distance between them is doubled?
questions.explanation: By Coulomb's law the force between two charges varies inversely as the square of the distance between them, so doubling the distance cuts it to 1/2² = 1/4.

questions.text: Archaeologist R Nagaswamy was honoured at the Silver Jubilee International Conference of Art by which country?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Bangladesh: the Tamil Nadu archaeologist R Nagaswamy is reported to have been honoured in Dhaka at the Silver Jubilee International Conference of Art. (We could not confirm the honour from an independent source.)

questions.text: Who became the first Indian equestrian to qualify for the Tokyo Olympics 2020?
questions.explanation: Fouaad Mirza won India an individual eventing place at the Tokyo Olympics, the first Indian equestrian to qualify for the Games since 2000.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Madhavpur Mela celebrated?
questions.explanation: The Madhavpur Ghed fair, at Madhavpur near Porbandar in Gujarat, celebrates the marriage of Krishna and Rukmini.

questions.text: Which state’s Legislative Assembly adopted a new logo consisting of the national emblem and foxtail orchid (Rhynchostylis Retusa), the state flower, in January 2020?
questions.explanation: In January 2020 the Arunachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly adopted a new logo pairing the national emblem with the foxtail orchid, Arunachal's state flower.

questions.text: Which of the following festivals means 'Merry making of the Gods'?
questions.explanation: Lai Haraoba, Manipur's festival of the traditional Meitei deities (the Umang Lai), means 'merrymaking of the gods'.

questions.text: Which of the following glands is present between the lungs?
questions.explanation: The thymus lies in the chest, behind the breastbone and between the lungs; the pineal gland, the hypothalamus and the pituitary are in the brain.

questions.text: In which of the following countries was the 95th edition of the prestigious Hastings International Chess Congress held?
questions.explanation: The Hastings International Chess Congress is held in its home town, Hastings, on the south coast of England.

questions.text: In which state was the Global Investors Meet, ASCEND 2020 organised?
questions.explanation: Ascend Kerala 2020, the Kerala government's global investors' meet, was held in Kochi in January 2020.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year was the foundation stone for the Gateway of India laid in Bombay (now Mumbai)?
questions.explanation: The foundation stone of the Gateway of India, built to mark the 1911 visit of King George V and Queen Mary, was laid in March 1913; the arch was completed in 1924.

questions.text: Wings India 2020 is scheduled to be held in which of the following airports?
questions.explanation: Wings India, the civil aviation show organised by the Ministry of Civil Aviation, the Airports Authority of India and FICCI, is held at Begumpet Airport in Hyderabad; the 2020 edition was set for 12 to 15 March 2020.

questions.text: When we cut an onion, the synthase enzyme converts the amino acid sulfoxides of the onion into which acid?
questions.explanation: Cutting an onion lets the enzyme alliinase turn its amino acid sulfoxides into sulfenic acids; lachrymatory-factor synthase, the enzyme the question names, then turns the sulfenic acid into the volatile compound that makes the eyes water.

questions.text: Who among the following was honoured with the 50th Dadasaheb Phalke Award?
questions.explanation: Amitabh Bachchan received the 50th Dadasaheb Phalke Award, for 2018, announced in September 2019.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a vertebrate?
questions.explanation: A snail is a mollusc and has no backbone; birds, fish and mammals are vertebrates.

questions.text: In which district of Karnataka is the Brahmagiri Wildlife Sanctuary located?
questions.explanation: Brahmagiri Wildlife Sanctuary lies in Kodagu (Coorg) district, on Karnataka's border with Kerala.

questions.text: Which of the following is the major component of vinegar?
questions.explanation: Vinegar is a dilute solution of acetic (ethanoic) acid in water.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to substitute the underlined word of the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No improvement’. There is a great “degrade in values” in modern age.
questions.explanation: After 'a great' the sentence needs a noun, and 'degrade' is a verb: 'There is a great degradation of values in modern age.'

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. He said to me, "What are you doing?"
options: He asked me what I was doing.
He said that what I was doing.
He said what I had been doing.
He asked me that what was I doing.
questions.explanation: A reported question takes 'asked', drops the question order and shifts the tense back: 'He asked me what I was doing.'

questions.text: Select the synonym of the given word. PATHETIC
questions.explanation: 'Pathetic' means arousing pity: 'pitiful'.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The modern man is busy acquiring more and more wealth and designing ways to invest it in more sense pleasures.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'in more sense pleasures', taking the noun 'sense' to need an adjective: 'sensual' (or 'sensuous') pleasures. The other three segments are correct as they stand, though 'sense pleasures' (pleasures of the senses) is itself in use.

questions.text: Select the antonym of the given word. HILARIOUS
questions.explanation: 'Hilarious' means extremely funny; its opposite is 'sad'. 'Blithe', 'happy' and 'merry' are close in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. It is an ______ day to start your new business.
questions.explanation: 'Auspicious' means promising good fortune, the right word for a day to start a business; 'ominous' means the opposite.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Machines were made to be man's servants. Yet, man has grown so (1)______ on them that they are in a fair way to become his (2)______. Already men spend most of their lives looking after and waiting (3)______ machines. Machines are very stern bosses. They must be fed with coal and (4)______ petrol to drink and oil to wash with and must be kept at an (5)______ temperature.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 1
questions.explanation: Man has grown so 'dependent' on machines that they may become his masters; 'dependent' is the word that takes 'on'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Machines were made to be man's servants. Yet, man has grown so (1)______ on them that they are in a fair way to become his (2)______. Already men spend most of their lives looking after and waiting (3)______ machines. Machines are very stern bosses. They must be fed with coal and (4)______ petrol to drink and oil to wash with and must be kept at an (5)______ temperature.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 2
questions.explanation: Made to be man's servants, machines are on the way to becoming his 'masters'; the next sentences call them stern bosses.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Machines were made to be man's servants. Yet, man has grown so (1)______ on them that they are in a fair way to become his (2)______. Already men spend most of their lives looking after and waiting (3)______ machines. Machines are very stern bosses. They must be fed with coal and (4)______ petrol to drink and oil to wash with and must be kept at an (5)______ temperature.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 3
questions.explanation: To 'wait upon' is to serve: men spend their lives looking after and serving machines.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Machines were made to be man's servants. Yet, man has grown so (1)______ on them that they are in a fair way to become his (2)______. Already men spend most of their lives looking after and waiting (3)______ machines. Machines are very stern bosses. They must be fed with coal and (4)______ petrol to drink and oil to wash with and must be kept at an (5)______ temperature.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 4
questions.explanation: The passive continues from 'must be fed': machines must be fed coal and 'given' petrol to drink.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Machines were made to be man's servants. Yet, man has grown so (1)______ on them that they are in a fair way to become his (2)______. Already men spend most of their lives looking after and waiting (3)______ machines. Machines are very stern bosses. They must be fed with coal and (4)______ petrol to drink and oil to wash with and must be kept at an (5)______ temperature.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 5
questions.explanation: 'Optimum' means best or most favourable: machines must be kept at the right temperature.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. Can I borrow your camera? B. I will give it back to you next week. C. I am going to jungle safari tomorrow. D. My friend told me that jungle is beautiful in these days.
questions.explanation: C says where the speaker is going, D why a camera is wanted (the jungle is beautiful), A asks for the camera and B promises to return it: CDAB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate segment to substitute the underlined segment of the given sentence. If no substitution is required select ‘No improvement’ A man in need “pleaded for help.”
questions.explanation: To 'plead for' something is to ask for it earnestly, so the sentence is correct as it stands.

questions.text: Select the correct active form of the given sentence. The thief was being arrested by the police.
options: The police has arrested the thief.
The police had arrested the thief.
The police was arresting the thief.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the only option that keeps the tense: the past continuous passive 'was being arrested' becomes the past continuous active. Strictly, 'the police' takes a plural verb ('The police were arresting the thief.'), but no option has that, and the other three change the tense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom A snake in the grass
questions.explanation: A 'snake in the grass' is a treacherous person who pretends to be a friend: a secret enemy.

questions.text: Select the synonym of the given word. PENITENCE
questions.explanation: 'Penitence' is sorrow for having done wrong: 'repentance'.

questions.text: Select the antonym of the given word. VICIOUS
questions.explanation: 'Vicious' means cruel or wicked; its opposite is 'virtuous'. 'Baneful' and 'sinful' are close in meaning.

questions.text: Select one word for the following group of words. A period of ten years
questions.explanation: A decade is ten years; a century is a hundred, a millennium a thousand, and a fortnight two weeks.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. Nevertheless, sound health, economic security and mental satisfaction are desired by all B. A change that is conducive to happiness may be termed as progress. C. But different people find happiness in different things. D. So, If a change contributes to the growth of these factors, it is progress.
questions.explanation: B defines progress through happiness, C notes that people find happiness in different things, A ('Nevertheless') names what all desire and D ('So') concludes: BCAD.

questions.text: Select the wrongly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'practical'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom On shank's mare
questions.explanation: To go 'on shank's mare' is to walk, the shank being the leg: on foot.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. He ______ a heinous crime.
questions.explanation: One 'commits' a crime; 'happen' and 'occur' take no object, and one does not 'make' a crime.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The Prime Minister, along with the other ministers have left for America.
questions.explanation: With 'along with', the verb agrees with the first subject, 'The Prime Minister': 'has left', not 'have left'.

questions.text: Select one word for the following group of words. One who leaves his own country to settle in another
questions.explanation: An emigrant leaves his own country to settle in another; seen from the new country, the same person is an immigrant.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Affront
questions.explanation: An 'affront' is an action or remark that causes offence: an 'insult'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'queue'.

questions.text: Spot the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the options given. As soon as we went for an afternoon siesta, my pet rabbit Tia digged a huge hole right in the middle of the lawn.
options: As soon as we were going for an afternoon siesta, my pet rabbit Tia digged a huge hole right in the middle of the lawn.
As soon as we went for an afternoon siesta, my pet rabbit Tia dug a huge hole right in the middle of the lawn.
As soon as we gone for an afternoon siesta, my pet rabbit Tia digged a huge hole right in the middle of the lawn.
As soon as we gone for an afternoon siesta, my pet rabbit Tia dug a huge hole right in the middle of the lawn.
questions.explanation: The past tense of 'dig' is 'dug', not 'digged'; 'went' is right for the completed action.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. My pocket has been picked.
options: Someone’s pocket has been picked by me.
questions.explanation: The present perfect passive 'has been picked' becomes the active 'has picked', with the unnamed agent supplied as 'someone': 'Someone has picked my pocket.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. She should run “the fast” to win the race.
questions.explanation: To win the race she must be faster than all the others: the superlative, 'the fastest'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Ravenous
questions.explanation: 'Ravenous' means extremely hungry; 'esurient' means hungry or greedy.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Strain every nerve
options: To try extremely hard to do something
questions.explanation: To 'strain every nerve' is to make every possible effort.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I never could quite get the idea ________ my mind that I should do some teaching, yet I felt a great deal of satisfaction with the pastorate.
questions.explanation: To 'get an idea out of one's mind' is to stop thinking of it: 'get the idea out of my mind'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. After wearing the complete sports gear, he looked “lean, tough, and sinewy”.
questions.explanation: 'Wiry' describes someone lean, tough and sinewy; 'wirey' is a misspelling.

questions.text: Identify the option that arranges the given parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. a) PB Shelly was an English poet. b) He was expelled from Oxford for publishing a tract entitled ‘The Necessity of Atheism’. c) He detested tyranny and institutionalised servitude. d) Born into a wealthy upper-class family.
questions.explanation: a introduces the poet and d, a fragment, continues it with his birth; c gives his convictions and b the tract that got him expelled: a, d, c, b.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. The movie I watched last Saturday was “much better interesting” than the one I watched today.
questions.explanation: 'Interesting' forms its comparative with 'more', which 'much' can strengthen: 'much more interesting'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank. I really admire his ___________ to fulfil his dream to join navy.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'persistence'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Looking or sounding foreign, bizarre, strange, unfamiliar
questions.explanation: 'Outlandish' means looking or sounding bizarre or unfamiliar.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. She “has returned” from Delhi a month ago.
questions.explanation: 'A month ago' marks a finished past time, which takes the simple past, not the present perfect: 'She returned from Delhi a month ago.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Tedious
questions.explanation: 'Tedious' means long and dull; its opposite is 'exciting'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Jump the gun
questions.explanation: To 'jump the gun' is to act too soon, like a runner who starts before the starting gun.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Siege
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'clearance'. A siege surrounds a place and cuts it off; 'clearance', the removal of an obstruction, is the nearest to an opposite among the options, and 'deference', 'trance' and 'inference' are unrelated.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in the brackets to fill in the blank. When the lady answered the knock at her door she found a _____________ (destitute) man.
questions.explanation: 'Destitute' means without money or the necessities of life: 'indigent'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. First of all, planting trees should be given (1) ___________ attention. Above all, tree is the (2) ____________ of oxygen. Unfortunately, due to (3) __________ of buildings many trees have been cut down. This (4) __________ reduces the amount of oxygen in the environment. Growing (5) ___________ trees means (5) _________ oxygen. Hence, growing more trees would mean better life quality.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Planting trees deserves 'massive' attention; 'lesser', 'trivial' and 'minor' contradict the passage's point.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. First of all, planting trees should be given (1) ___________ attention. Above all, tree is the (2) ____________ of oxygen. Unfortunately, due to (3) __________ of buildings many trees have been cut down. This (4) __________ reduces the amount of oxygen in the environment. Growing (5) ___________ trees means (5) _________ oxygen. Hence, growing more trees would mean better life quality.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Trees release oxygen: they are its 'source'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Growing (5) ___________ trees means (5) _________ oxygen. Hence, growing more trees would mean better life quality.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? AYC, EUG, IQK, MMO, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +4 (A, E, I, M, Q), second letters −4 (Y, U, Q, M, I) and third letters +4 (C, G, K, O, S): QIS.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1.Perilous 2.Pessimist 3.Pedestrian 4.Perceive 5.Perfect 6.Peasant
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Peasant (6), Pedestrian (3), Perceive (4), Perfect (5), Perilous (1), Pessimist (2).

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when placed from left to right in the blanks, will complete the letter series. M _ W Q U N S _ Q U O S W _ U P S _ Q _
questions.explanation: With S, W, Q, W, U in the blanks the series reads MSWQU NSWQU OSWQU PSWQU: the first letter moves on one each time and SWQU repeats.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: In 678 : 7, 366 : 5 and 546 : 5 the second number is the average of the first number's digits (21 ÷ 3, 15 ÷ 3, 15 ÷ 3). For 282 it would be 12 ÷ 3 = 4, not 6.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 42*19*4*69*81*9*58
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 40*2*15*30*5

The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs, EXCEPT one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: In the other pairs the second number is 6 times the first (40 × 6 = 240, 25 × 6 = 150, 30 × 6 = 180); 35 × 6 = 210, not 280.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term. 27 : 99 :: 21 : ? :: 13 : 43
questions.explanation: The second number is 4 times the first minus 9: 27 × 4 − 9 = 99 and 13 × 4 − 9 = 43. Likewise 21 × 4 − 9 = 75.

questions.text: The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) is/are followed in all the number-pairs, except one. Find that odd number-pair.
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of one less than the first: 11² = 121, 5² = 25 and 7² = 49. But 9 gives 8² = 64, not 100.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row:5, 9, 56; Second row: 4, 7, 33; Third row:10, 11, ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the number into its constituent digits. For example, 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is the difference of the squares of the first two: 9² − 5² = 81 − 25 = 56 and 7² − 4² = 49 − 16 = 33. So 11² − 10² = 121 − 100 = 21.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'MAP' is written as 'QBN' and 'LEAP' is written as 'QBFM'. How will 'CROWN' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and each letter moved one place forward: MAP → PAM → QBN and LEAP → PAEL → QBFM. So CROWN → NWORC → OXPSD.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some boxes are houses. Some houses are tents. Some tents are castles. Conclusions: I. Some castles are houses. II. Some tents are houses. III. Some castles are boxes.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: Some houses are tents, so some tents are houses (II). The 'some' links give no definite overlap between castles and houses or between castles and boxes, so I and III do not follow.

questions.text: Seven friends P, Q, R, S, T, U and V, each has a different height. P is taller than only U and R. R is taller than U. Q is taller than S but shorter than T. T is not the tallest among all. The height of how many people is between the heights of Q and R?
questions.explanation: P is taller than only U and R, and R is taller than U: from the shortest, U, R, P. Of the rest S < Q < T, and T is not the tallest, so V is: U, R, P, S, Q, T, V. P and S stand between R and Q: two people.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row- 5, 16, 77; Second row- 13, 12, ?; Third row- 8, 19, 149 (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is the product of the first two minus 3: 5 × 16 − 3 = 77 and 8 × 19 − 3 = 149. So 13 × 12 − 3 = 153.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term. 6 : 40 :: ? : 148 :: 3 : 13.
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first plus 4: 6² + 4 = 40 and 3² + 4 = 13. 148 − 4 = 144 = 12².

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. GAINS : SNIAG :: ANVIL : LIVNA :: INBOX : ?
questions.explanation: Each word is written in reverse: GAINS → SNIAG and ANVIL → LIVNA. So INBOX → XOBNI.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 283, 359, 428, 490, 545, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 76, 69, 62, 55, falling by 7 each time, so the next is 48: 545 + 48 = 593.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1.Dictation 2.Dictator 3.Distribute 4.Decadent 5.Distilled
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Decadent (4), Dictation (1), Dictator (2), Distilled (5), Distribute (3); 'Dictati-' comes before 'Dictato-' and 'Distil-' before 'Distri-'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, “EASY” is written as “YAES”, and “KIND” is written as “DIKN”. How will “SOME” be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters are rearranged 4th, 2nd, 1st, 3rd: E A S Y → Y A E S and K I N D → D I K N. So S O M E → E O S M.

questions.text: For the first part of her journey, Sunita travelled at a speed of 450 m/min and, for the rest of the journey, at a speed 1.4 times of her initial speed. If Sunita travelled a total distance of 33.3 km in 1hour, what was the distance that Sunita travelled at a lower speed?
questions.explanation: At 450 m/min for t minutes and 1.4 × 450 = 630 m/min for the rest: 450t + 630(60 − t) = 33,300, so 180t = 4,500 and t = 25. The slower part was 450 × 25 = 11,250 m = 11.25 km.

questions.text: 40 men can complete a piece of work in 18 days. 9 days after they start working together, 5 more men join them. How many days will they now take to complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation: The work is 40 × 18 = 720 man-days; 40 × 9 = 360 are done, and the 45 men finish the other 360 in 360 ÷ 45 = 8 days.

questions.text: A sum of money is invested at a rate of compounded interest that is paid out yearly. In the first two years, the interest was ₹400 and ₹420 respectively. The sum is:
questions.explanation: The second year's interest exceeds the first's by ₹20, the interest on ₹400 for a year, so the rate is 20/400 = 5%. Sum = 400 ÷ 0.05 = ₹8,000.

questions.text: A man spends 20% of his monthly salary on food and one-fourth of the remaining salary on charity. If he saves ₹9,600 per month, which is equal to half of the balance after spending on food and charity, then his monthly salary is:
questions.explanation: After food 80% is left; charity takes a quarter of it (20% of the salary), leaving 60%. Half of that, 30% of the salary, is ₹9,600, so the salary is ₹32,000.

questions.text: What is the length of the arc of a circle whose radius is 35 cm and arc subtends an angle of 36° at the centre of the circle? (Take π=22/7)
Find the value of ‘a’ using the concept of BODMAS. 42 ÷ 2 + a × 3 − 22 = 8
questions.explanation: Division and multiplication first: 21 + 3a − 22 = 8, so 3a = 9 and a = 3.

questions.text: In an examination, the Average marks of 7 children was 20, that of 3 children was 45, that of another 4 children was 15 and that of 2 children was 0. What is the average marks of all the 16 children? (Correct to one decimal place)
questions.explanation: Total marks = 7 × 20 + 3 × 45 + 4 × 15 + 2 × 0 = 140 + 135 + 60 = 335, and 335 ÷ 16 = 20.9375, which is 20.9 to one decimal place.

questions.text: A washing machine is sold at a discount of 10% on its marked price. A further discount of 5% on the initial selling price is offered if a person makes the payment in cash. If the marked price of the machine is ₹54,000, how much will a customer paying in cash have to pay for purchasing it?
The length, breadth and height of a room are 7 m, 4 m and 9 m, respectively. Find the cost of whitewashing the walls of the room and the ceiling at the rate of ₹7.50 per m².
questions.explanation: Four walls = 2(7 + 4) × 9 = 198 m² and the ceiling 7 × 4 = 28 m²: 226 m² × ₹7.50 = ₹1,695.

questions.text: Find the selling price of an article if a shopkeeper allows two successive discounts of 5% each on the marked price of ₹80.
Which of the following numbers is NOT divisible by 15?
questions.explanation: A number divisible by 15 must be divisible by 3 and by 5. All four end in 5, but the digits of 2995 add up to 25, which is not divisible by 3.

questions.text: If the length, breadth and height of a cuboid are 7.5 m, 22 m and 13 m, respectively, then find the volume of the cuboid.
What is the average of first 10 multiples of 6?
questions.explanation: The first 10 multiples of 6 are 6, 12, …, 60; their average is (6 + 60)/2 = 33.

questions.text: The price of a bike is ₹75,500. What will be the price of the bike after a reduction of 17%?
If the compound interest on a principal for one year is ₹350 and the compound interest for the second year is ₹420, find the rate of interest.
questions.explanation: The second year's interest exceeds the first's by ₹70, the interest on ₹350 for a year: 70/350 = 20%.

questions.text: The area of quadrilateral is 336 m² and the perpendiculars drawn to one diagonal from the opposite vertices are 16 m and 12 m long. Find the length of this diagonal.
questions.explanation: Area = ½ × diagonal × (16 + 12) = 14 × diagonal = 336 m², so the diagonal is 24 m. SSC's key gives '24 cm': all four options print the unit as cm, a misprint, since the question's lengths are in metres.

questions.text: In which of the following years was Lata Mangeshkar, a legendry playback Indian singer, awarded with the Padma Vibhushan, the second-highest Indian civilian award?
questions.explanation: Lata Mangeshkar received the Padma Vibhushan in 1999; she had received the Padma Bhushan in 1969 and went on to receive the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

questions.text: In February 2021, ___________ broke into the Top-100 WTA doubles rankings, becoming the second woman, after Sania Mirza, to do so.
questions.explanation: Ankita Raina entered the top 100 of the WTA doubles rankings in February 2021, after winning her first WTA title, the Phillip Island Trophy doubles, with Kamilla Rakhimova.

questions.text: Who among the following won the prestigious Abhinandan Saroja National Award 2021?
questions.explanation: The National Institute of Indian Classical Dance gave its Abhinandan Saroja National Award for 2021 to Aparna Satheesan, a US-based Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancer, at a ceremony held online in November 2021.

questions.text: Identify a way that does NOT prevent a non-communicable disease from occurring in someone.
questions.explanation: Adequate sleep and a balanced, healthy diet lower the risk of non-communicable diseases such as diabetes and heart disease; a blood transfusion is a medical treatment, not a way of preventing them.

questions.text: Identify the group of the periodic table to which iron belongs.
questions.explanation: Iron (Fe) is a transition metal in Group 8 of the modern periodic table, with ruthenium and osmium.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘Five Point Someone’?
questions.explanation: 'Five Point Someone' (2004), set at IIT Delhi, was Chetan Bhagat's first novel.

questions.text: For what discovery was Jan Evangelista Purkinje known in 1839?
questions.explanation: In 1839 Purkinje coined the term 'protoplasm' for the living substance of the cell.

questions.text: In which year was the Indian Football Association established?
questions.explanation: The Indian Football Association was founded in Calcutta in 1893.

questions.text: The Konark Dance Festival is held at an open air auditorium in the backdrop of the _________ which is also known as the Black Pagoda.
questions.explanation: The festival's open-air auditorium at Konark, Odisha, has the 13th-century Sun Temple as its backdrop; sailors called the temple the Black Pagoda.

questions.text: Among the following, whose autobiography is ‘My Confession’?
questions.explanation: Leo Tolstoy's 'A Confession', also translated as 'My Confession', recounts the spiritual crisis of his middle years.

questions.text: ‘Drawing From the City’ is a visual autobiography of which of the following Indian folk artists?
questions.explanation: 'Drawing from the City' (Tara Books, 2012) is the visual autobiography of the self-taught folk artist Teju Behan (Tejubehan), who began drawing after moving to Ahmedabad.

questions.text: ‘All minorities, whether based on religion or language, shall have the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice’. Which article of the Constitution of India guarantees this right?
questions.explanation: Article 30(1) gives all minorities, religious or linguistic, the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.

questions.text: What is the common name of C₆H₆?
questions.explanation: C₆H₆ is benzene, an aromatic hydrocarbon. Methanol is CH₃OH, acetic acid CH₃COOH and acetone CH₃COCH₃.

questions.text: Phytoplankton, small sea-dwelling organisms, belong to which trophic level of the food web?
questions.explanation: Phytoplankton make their own food by photosynthesis, so they are the primary producers, the first trophic level, of aquatic food webs.

questions.text: Which of the following serves as the cell's digestive system, serving both to degrade material taken from outside the cell and to digest the undigested components of the cell?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes hold digestive enzymes that break down material taken into the cell as well as the cell's own worn-out parts.

questions.text: What is India’s rank in the 2021 Global Hunger Index?
questions.explanation: India ranked 101st of 116 countries in the Global Hunger Index 2021.

questions.text: Pandit Swapan Chaudhuri is associated with ___________ instrument.
questions.explanation: Pandit Swapan Chaudhuri is a leading tabla player.

questions.text: Who among the following became the first Indian male shuttler to win silver in the men's singles event at the BWF World Championships on December 19, 2021?
questions.explanation: Kidambi Srikanth lost the final of the 2021 BWF World Championships at Huelva, Spain, to Loh Kean Yew of Singapore, and became the first Indian man to win silver at the event.

questions.text: Who among the following founded the ‘Kalakshetra’ in 1936, an Indian arts academy that was especially dedicated to the cultivation of the Bharatanatyam tradition?
questions.explanation: Rukmini Devi Arundale founded Kalakshetra in Madras (Chennai) in 1936.

questions.text: Pankaj Advani is related to which of the following sports?
questions.explanation: Pankaj Advani is a many-time world champion in English billiards and snooker.

questions.text: Which of the following is true?
options: Gross Domestic Product + Depreciation = Gross National Product
Gross Domestic Product + Depreciation = Net Domestic Product
Gross Domestic Product – Depreciation = Gross National Product
Gross Domestic Product – Depreciation = Net Domestic Product
questions.explanation: Net Domestic Product is GDP minus depreciation (consumption of fixed capital); GNP is GDP plus net factor income from abroad.

questions.text: Who among the following is the founder of the Indore Gharana of music?
questions.explanation: Ustad Amir Khan founded the Indore gharana of Hindustani vocal music.

questions.text: Anup Jalota is famous for which of the following categories of Indian music?
questions.explanation: Anup Jalota, known as the 'Bhajan Samrat', is famous for his devotional bhajans.

questions.text: Mallika Sarabhai is the most famous Indian dancer renowned for ____.
questions.explanation: Mallika Sarabhai, daughter of the dancer Mrinalini Sarabhai, is known for Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam.

questions.text: As per Census of India 2011, which state has the highest percentage of Scheduled Tribe population to total Scheduled Tribe population in India?
questions.explanation: By Census 2011, Madhya Pradesh has 14.7% of India's Scheduled Tribe population, the largest share, followed by Maharashtra (10.1%) and Odisha (9.2%).

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'harass', with one 'r'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an INCORRECTLY spelt word. The management is not perturbed about appointing / someone who is knowledgeable but is more inclined / towards filling the position with a person / who will be obsequous and will dance to their tunes.
options: someone who is knowledgeable but is more inclined
The management is not perturbed about appointing
towards filling the position with a person
who will be obsequous and will dance to their tunes
questions.explanation: 'Obsequous' is misspelt: the word is 'obsequious', meaning too eager to please or obey.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The vendor sold the vegetables in the market.
options: The vegetables are sold by the vendor in the market.
The vegetables were being sold by the vendor in the market.
The vegetables were sold by the vendor in the market.
The vendor had sold the vegetables in the market.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'sold' becomes 'were sold' with the plural subject 'the vegetables': 'The vegetables were sold by the vendor in the market.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A short text written on tombstone
questions.explanation: An epitaph is a short text in memory of a person, written on a tombstone. Calligraphy is decorative handwriting, and extempore means spoken without preparation.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Food blogs are often authored by food aficionados, sometimes known as ‘foodies’. B. The blogger can benefit from it if he or she uses it professionally. C. Food blogging is food journalism that combines an interest in food, blog writing, and food photography. D. The greater the popularity of a food blogger, the more options for him/her to monetise his/her work.
questions.explanation: C defines food blogging, A says who writes food blogs, B says the blogger can benefit by using it professionally, and D adds that popularity brings more ways to monetise the work: CABD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence. Though Mr. Swami “ran in” debt, he did not stop wasting money.
questions.explanation: To 'run into' debt is to get into debt: 'Though Mr. Swami ran into debt, he did not stop wasting money.'

questions.text: Complete the sentence with an appropriate ANTONYM of the word mentioned in the bracket. The old house was so ________(sturdy) that it could be shattered into pieces with a single blow.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'sturdy' is 'feeble': a house shattered by a single blow is weak.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He ran _________ the field to catch the ball
questions.explanation: To go from one side of an area to the other is to run 'across' it: 'He ran across the field to catch the ball.'

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Though many of my family members can cook well, “I can cook more well than others.”
options: I can cook best than others
I can cook more good than others
I can cook good than others
I can cook better than others
questions.explanation: The comparative of the adverb 'well' is 'better', not 'more well': 'I can cook better than others.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hobson's choice
questions.explanation: A 'Hobson's choice' is no real choice at all: take what is offered or nothing.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. A “strong dislike or fear of people from other countries” can never serve the goal of the country’s friendly neighbourhood policy.
questions.explanation: Xenophobia is a strong dislike or fear of people from other countries. Arachnophobia is the fear of spiders and cynophobia the fear of dogs.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Pugnacious
questions.explanation: 'Pugnacious' means eager to fight: 'truculent', aggressive and defiant. 'Sagacious' means wise and 'germane' relevant.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Shanti heard the children “who were shouting outside”
options: who were thrashing in the open air
who were flaying in the open air
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'who were screaming outdoors', the only option that keeps the sense: 'screaming' is close to 'shouting', and the adverb 'outdoors' means outside ('outdoor' is an adjective). The sentence as printed is already correct, and there is no 'no improvement' option.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The problem will be solved by my friend.
options: My friend was solved the problem.
My friend will be solving the problem.
My friend will solve the problem.
questions.explanation: The future passive 'will be solved by my friend' becomes the future active: 'My friend will solve the problem.'

questions.text: Select the sentence which has no spelling error.
options: Patience is a nesecessary quality for a teacher.
The soil is necessary for plantation.
Water is a necesary element for life.
Sharp observation is naicessary for a detective.
questions.explanation: 'Necessary' has one 'c' and a double 's'; the other three sentences misspell it.

questions.text: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Wise managers _________ opinions, get information, ask advice, act ________ and know the art of __________ responsibilities to the subordinates.
questions.explanation: Wise managers 'solicit' (ask for) opinions, act 'transparently' (openly) and know the art of 'delegating' (handing over) responsibilities to subordinates.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the options given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. There are (1)______ ways to empower women. Individual people and the administration must work (2)______ to make this a (3)______. Girl's education must be made mandatory so that they do not become (4)______, uneducated, and unable to support themselves. Women must be (5)______ equal rights and opportunities in all fields, regardless of their gender.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.1.
questions.explanation: 'There are several ways to empower women': the passage goes on to name some of them.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the options given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. There are (1)______ ways to empower women. Individual people and the administration must work (2)______ to make this a (3)______. Girl's education must be made mandatory so that they do not become (4)______, uneducated, and unable to support themselves. Women must be (5)______ equal rights and opportunities in all fields, regardless of their gender.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.2.
questions.explanation: Individual people and the administration must work 'cooperatively', that is together.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the options given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. There are (1)______ ways to empower women. Individual people and the administration must work (2)______ to make this a (3)______. Girl's education must be made mandatory so that they do not become (4)______, uneducated, and unable to support themselves. Women must be (5)______ equal rights and opportunities in all fields, regardless of their gender.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.3.
questions.explanation: To 'make this a reality' is to bring it about.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the options given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. There are (1)______ ways to empower women. Individual people and the administration must work (2)______ to make this a (3)______. Girl's education must be made mandatory so that they do not become (4)______, uneducated, and unable to support themselves. Women must be (5)______ equal rights and opportunities in all fields, regardless of their gender.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.4.
questions.explanation: Education keeps girls from becoming 'ignorant', a word that sits with 'uneducated' in the list.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the options given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. There are (1)______ ways to empower women. Individual people and the administration must work (2)______ to make this a (3)______. Girl's education must be made mandatory so that they do not become (4)______, uneducated, and unable to support themselves. Women must be (5)______ equal rights and opportunities in all fields, regardless of their gender.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.5.
questions.explanation: Rights are 'accorded', that is granted, to people: 'Women must be accorded equal rights and opportunities'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, “CAUTIOUS” is written as “CUAITUOS”, and “DEADLINE” is written as “DAELDNIE”. How will “ECONOMIC” be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters stay and the letters between are swapped in pairs: C AU TI OU S → C UA IT UO S. So E CO NO MI C → E OC ON IM C: EOCONIMC.

questions.text: If 30 July 2015 was Thursday, then what was the day of the week on 03 September 2016?
questions.explanation: From 30 July 2015 to 30 July 2016 is 366 days (29 February 2016 falls between), 2 odd days: Saturday. From 30 July to 3 September 2016 is 35 days, exactly 5 weeks, so it is also a Saturday.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row: 8, 13, 25; Second row: 12, 7, 25; Third row: 9, 15, ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the number into its constituent digits. For example, 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is the square of the difference of the first two: (13 − 8)² = 25 and (12 − 7)² = 25. So (15 − 9)² = 36.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (11, 8, 33); (33, 5, 924) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: The third number is the first times the difference of the first two: 11 × (11 − 8) = 33 and 33 × (33 − 5) = 924. Likewise 24 × (24 − 15) = 216.

questions.text: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark(?) to complete the given series? PUCH, QTDG, RSEF, SRFE, ?.
questions.explanation: The first letters run P, Q, R, S, T; the second U, T, S, R, Q; the third C, D, E, F, G; the fourth H, G, F, E, D. The next cluster is TQGD.

questions.text: If M denotes ‘−’, N denotes ‘÷’, O denotes ‘×’ and P denotes ‘+’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? (72 N 9) O 4 M 26 P 97 M (36 N 2) = ?
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given number series? 7350, 7345, 7345, ?, 7360, 7375
questions.explanation: The differences are −5, 0, +5, +10, +15, rising by 5 each time: 7345 + 5 = 7350, then 7350 + 10 = 7360.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 3 * 4 * 2 * 10 * 17 * 2
questions.explanation: 3 × 4 × 2 + 10 = 17 × 2, as both sides equal 34.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row: 162, 91, 71; Second row:218, 126, 92; Third row:194, 79, ?
