(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the number into its constituent digits. For example, 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is the first minus the second: 162 − 91 = 71 and 218 − 126 = 92. So 194 − 79 = 115.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 46*16*4*21*72*4*57
If 15 August 1947 was Friday, then what was the day of the week on 26 January 1950?
questions.explanation: From 15 August 1947 to 15 August 1949 is 366 + 365 = 731 days (1948 was a leap year), 3 odd days: Monday. From 15 August 1949 to 26 January 1950 is 16 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 26 = 164 days, 3 more odd days: Thursday.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? TCID, YJRO, ?, IXJK, NESV
questions.explanation: The letters move +5, +7, +9 and +11 in the four places, wrapping round after Z: T → Y → D, C → J → Q, I → R → A and D → O → Z. The missing cluster is DQAZ.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All stones are bricks. No cement is a brick. Some marbles are stones. Conclusions: I. Some bricks are marbles. II. Some cements are stones. III. No marble is a brick.
options: Both conclusions I and III follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: The marbles that are stones are bricks, so some bricks are marbles (I), and III is false. As every stone is a brick and no cement is a brick, no cement is a stone, so II does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'FAMOUS' is coded as '19 21 15 13 1 6', and 'GARDEN' is coded as '14 5 4 18 1 7'. How will 'LEADER' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and each letter written as its place in the alphabet: FAMOUS → S U O M A F → 19 21 15 13 1 6. So LEADER → R E D A E L → 18 5 4 1 5 12.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 558, 570, 555, ?, 552, 576
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 558, 555, 552 fall by 3, and 570, ?, 576 rise by 3, so ? = 573.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term related to third term. 27 : 196 :: 19 : 100 :: 17 : ?
questions.explanation: The second term is the square of half of one more than the first: (27 + 1)/2 = 14 and 14² = 196; (19 + 1)/2 = 10 and 10² = 100. Likewise (17 + 1)/2 = 9 and 9² = 81.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 14, 18, 54, 58, 174, 178, ?

Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. REASON : ROSAEN :: SOCIAL : SAICOL :: TRAVEL : ?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters stay and the four between are reversed: R EASO N → R OSAE N and S OCIA L → S AICO L. So T RAVE L → T EVAR L: TEVARL.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'SCREEN' is written as ‘14e5r3s’ and ‘SHOT’ is written as ‘20o8s’. How will 'CODE' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and its letters written alternately as their places in the alphabet and in lower case: SHOT → T O H S → 20 o 8 s. So CODE → E D O C → 5 d 15 c: 5d15c.

questions.text: What is the mean proportional between 64 and 4096?
questions.explanation: The mean proportional of a and b is √(ab) = √(64 × 4096) = 8 × 64 = 512.

questions.text: A and B together can finish a job in 40 days. A can do the same job on her own in 60 days. How long will B take to do the three-fourth of the same work all alone?
questions.explanation: B alone does 1/40 − 1/60 = 1/120 of the job a day, so the whole job takes 120 days and three-fourths of it 90 days.

questions.text: A sum of ₹5,000 was deposited for 3 years at 10% per annum, compounded annually. The difference between the interest for 2 years and that for 3 years is:
questions.explanation: The difference is the third year's interest: 10% of the amount after 2 years, 5,000 × 1.1² = ₹6,050, which is ₹605.

questions.text: If cotθ = cot 30° cot 60° and θ is an acute angle, then 2θ is equal to:
A shopkeeper mixes three types of rice costing ₹50 per kg, ₹60 per kg and ₹75 per kg in the ratio of 3 : 1 : 2. The average cost of the mixture per kg is:
If x +2 y = 10 and 2xy = 9, then one of the value of x − 2y is:
questions.explanation: (x − 2y)² = (x + 2y)² − 8xy = 100 − 4 × 9 = 64, so x − 2y = ±8; one value is 8.

questions.text: One single discount which is equivalent to 20%, 10% and 5% is given by:
questions.explanation: 0.8 × 0.9 × 0.95 = 0.684 of the price is paid, so the single discount is 31.6%.

questions.text: P sold an item to Q at a 20% gain, and Q sold it to R at a loss of 10%. If R bought the item for ₹1,080, then at what price did P purchase it?
questions.explanation: R's price is P's cost × 1.2 × 0.9 = 1.08 × cost = ₹1,080, so P paid ₹1,000.

questions.text: A householder spent his monthly salary of ₹7,200 on different items. If he spent ₹4,000 on food and ₹400 on education, then the central angles respectively are:
questions.explanation: In a pie chart each item gets (amount/total) × 360°: 4,000/7,200 × 360° = 200° for food and 400/7,200 × 360° = 20° for education.

questions.text: Rice worth ₹96 per kg and ₹104 per kg are mixed with a third variety in the ratio 1 : 1 : 2. If the mixture is worth ₹113 per kg, the price of the third variety of rice per kg will be:
Successive discounts of 10% and 20% are given on the purchase of a purse . If the price of the purse is ₹2,250, find the selling price.
What is the surface area of a sphere whose diameter is 30 cm? [Use π = 3.14.]
questions.explanation: The radius is 15 cm, so the surface area is 4πr² = 4 × 3.14 × 225 = 2826 cm².

questions.text: Find the compound interest on ₹5,50,000 at 7% per annum for 2 years, compounded annually.
What is the smallest natural number that should be added to 54321 so that the sum is divisible by 6?
questions.explanation: 54321 = 6 × 9053 + 3 (its digit sum, 15, makes it divisible by 3, but it is odd), so adding 3 gives 54324, which is divisible by 6.

questions.text: How many spherical balls of radius 5 cm can be made by melting a spherical clay ball having a radius of 15 cm?
questions.explanation: Volumes go as the cube of the radius: (15/5)³ = 27 balls.

questions.text: The average monthly expenditure of a family for the first four months is ₹13,750, for the next three months is ₹11,750 and for the last five months is ₹31,750. If the family saves ₹15,550 during the whole year, find the average monthly income of the family during the year. (Consider integral part only)
What is the value of 12-8÷2-{16 of -2+3×5-4}?
questions.explanation: 'Of' first: 16 of −2 = −32, so the bracket is −32 + 15 − 4 = −21. Then 12 − 4 − (−21) = 29.

questions.text: ‘A’ and ‘B’ are two stations 494 km apart. A train starts from station ‘A’ at 3 p.m. and travels towards station ‘B’ at 83 km/h. Another train starts from station ‘B’ at 4 p.m. and travels towards station ‘A’ at 54 km/h. At what time do they meet?
questions.explanation: By 4 p.m. the first train has covered 83 km, leaving 411 km. Closing at 83 + 54 = 137 km/h, they meet 411/137 = 3 hours later, at 7 p.m.

questions.text: One of the angles of a triangle is 108°, and the other two angles are equal. What is the measure of each of these equal angles?
questions.explanation: The other two angles add up to 180° − 108° = 72°, so each is 36°.

questions.text: In a panchayat election Candidate A secured 30% of the total votes and did NOT qualify by 6 votes. Candidate B secured 40% of the total votes and got 6 votes more than the bare minimum to qualify. The total number of votes were _________.
questions.explanation: The qualifying mark is 6 votes above A's 30% and 6 below B's 40%, so 10% of the votes is 12 and the total is 120.

questions.text: Which of the following Tiger Reserves/ National Parks and states situated in is INCORRECTLY matched?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans National Park is in West Bengal, in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta. Manas is in Assam, Bandhavgarh in Madhya Pradesh and Corbett in Uttarakhand.

questions.text: Yamini Krishnamurthy was honoured with the ___________ in 1977.
questions.explanation: The Bharatanatyam dancer Yamini Krishnamurthy received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 1977; her Padma Shri came earlier, in 1968.

questions.text: Which of the following countries never organised Olympic games?
questions.explanation: South Africa has never hosted the Olympic Games. Australia (Melbourne 1956, Sydney 2000), Japan (Tokyo 1964) and China (Beijing 2008) have.

questions.text: Who among the following does NOT belong to Rampur Sahaswan Gharana?
questions.explanation: The Rampur-Sahaswan gharana was founded by Ustad Inayat (Hussain) Khan, and Ghulam Mustafa Khan and Rashid Khan are among its best-known singers. Ustad Fateh Ali Khan belongs to the Patiala gharana.

questions.text: Which of the following minerals is NOT found in rivers (alluvial placers) and on the coast, especially beaches (beach placers)?
questions.explanation: Placer deposits hold minerals that water does not corrode, such as gold, platinum and tin. Bauxite forms instead from the weathering of rocks rich in aluminium silicates.

questions.text: Who among the followings was an Indian singer of the Khayal genre of Hindustani classical music from Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Gangubai Hangal of Dharwad, Karnataka, was a leading khayal singer of the Kirana gharana.

questions.text: L Bino Devi, Sangeet Natak Akademi Award winner had received the award for his contribution to which of the following dances forms?
questions.explanation: L Bino Devi (Laipubam Bino Devi) of Imphal, a Manipuri dancer and Sutradhari singer, received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Manipuri dance.

questions.text: Which of the following is a correct pair?
options: Vijay Kumar Singh – Courage and Conviction
K Natwar Singh – Straight from the Heart
questions.explanation: 'Courage and Conviction' (2013) is the autobiography of General V K Singh. 'Straight from the Heart' is Kapil Dev's autobiography and 'Matters of Discretion' I K Gujral's.

questions.text: In May 2021, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MTA) signed an MOU with which organisation to support the digital transformation of tribal schools?
questions.explanation: In May 2021 the Ministry of Tribal Affairs signed an MoU with Microsoft for the digital transformation of tribal schools such as the Eklavya Model Residential Schools and Ashram schools.

questions.text: In 1879, who observed cell division in salamander embryos, where cells divide at fixed intervals?
questions.explanation: Walther Flemming described cell division in salamander embryos in 1879 and later named the process mitosis.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the novel “Mrignayani”?
questions.explanation: 'Mrignayani', a historical novel about Raja Man Singh Tomar of Gwalior and his queen, is by Vrindavan Lal Verma.

questions.text: In 1976, Natya Tarangini, was founded in the National Capital Region, by world renowned Kuchipudi Dance duo ___________.
questions.explanation: Raja and Radha Reddy, the Kuchipudi couple, founded Natya Tarangini in Delhi in 1976.

questions.text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the election of the Vice-President?
questions.explanation: Article 66 lays down how the Vice-President is elected: by an electoral college of the members of both Houses of Parliament.

questions.text: The body of animals of the phylum Protozoa, such as Paramecium, Amoeba, Euglena, shows ________ grade organisation.
questions.explanation: In the older grading of animal bodies, protozoa, single cells that carry out every function within their protoplasm, show the protoplasmic grade; sponges show the cellular grade.

questions.text: According to Mendeleev's periodic table, which unknown element of group III had an atomic mass of 68 that was later replaced by gallium?
questions.explanation: Mendeleev left a gap below aluminium for 'eka-aluminium', with a predicted atomic mass of about 68; gallium, discovered in 1875, filled it.

questions.text: Which of the following equipment is used in throwing events?
questions.explanation: The shot, a solid metal ball, is thrown in the shot put; the other throwing events use the discus, javelin and hammer.

questions.text: Which of the following is an objective of the Government Budget? (A) GDP growth (B) Reallocation of resources (C) Balanced regional growth
questions.explanation: A government budget aims at economic growth, reallocation of resources, reducing inequality, economic stability and balanced regional development, so all three are objectives.

questions.text: Which of the following vocalists of Calcutta was the first artist of the sub-continent to record on the gramophone commercially in November 1902?
questions.explanation: Gauhar Jaan of Calcutta made the first commercial gramophone recordings in India, for the Gramophone Company in November 1902.

questions.text: Which of the following personalities have NOT been nominated for a Grammy Award?
questions.explanation: Lata Mangeshkar was never nominated for a Grammy. Vishwa Mohan Bhatt ('A Meeting by the River'), T H Vinayakram ('Planet Drum') and A R Rahman ('Slumdog Millionaire') all won one.

questions.text: In 1674, who used a single-lens microscope to examine pond water and observed dozens of protists, which he called 'animalcules', as well as spirogyra, or green algae?
questions.explanation: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, with his own single-lens microscopes, described the 'animalcules' of pond water in 1674.

questions.text: Ramali Bin Ibrahim, a Malaysian choreographer of Bharatanatyam and Odissi dance forms of India, received the Padma Shri in which of the following years?
questions.explanation: Ramli Ibrahim, a Malaysian Odissi and Bharatanatyam dancer and choreographer, received the Padma Shri in 2018.

questions.text: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Package (PMGKP) Insurance Scheme was extended by the Central government in June 2021. This provides that the families of health workers would get _______ lakh compensation in case of personal accidents.
questions.explanation: The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Package insurance scheme gives health workers fighting Covid-19 a cover of ₹50 lakh.

questions.text: Why does the effective nuclear charge experienced by valence electrons decrease down the group?
options: The outermost electrons are closest to the nucleus
The innermost electrons are farther away from the nucleus
The outermost electrons are farther away from the nucleus
questions.explanation: Down a group each element adds a shell, so the valence electrons lie farther from the nucleus, with more inner electrons shielding them, and feel its pull less.

questions.text: In October 2021, ‘Operation Sajag’, a measure to reduce crime in society, was launched in which state/Union Territory?
questions.explanation: Delhi Police's North-West district launched Operation Sajag in October 2021, with combing and checking drives against street crime.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of ‘A Movable Feast’?
questions.explanation: Ernest Hemingway's 'A Moveable Feast', a memoir of his years in Paris in the 1920s, was published in 1964, after his death.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'pronunciation': the verb is 'pronounce', but the noun drops the 'o'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. To think that a computer would one day replace a book is indeed unthinkable and far fetched. B.The thoughts and ideas contained in a book are immortal like Tulsidas’s Ram Charitra Manas, Ved Vyas’ Mahabharata, The Bible and many other religious and literary works like Shakespeare’s plays etc. C.On the other hand a computer is but a machine, that at best can visually display the contents of a specific book. D.A good book in the words of John Milton “is the precious lifeblood of a master spirit, embalmed and treasured up to a purpose to a life beyond life.”
questions.explanation: D opens with Milton's praise of a good book, B adds that a book's ideas are immortal, C sets against it the computer as a mere machine, and A concludes that its replacing the book is unthinkable: DBCA.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an INCORRECTLY spelt word. Shanu’s inquisitive mind could not / accept the seemingly ingenous reply / of the man and he resolved to solve the mystery / to mitigate the pain of the old couple.
options: of the man and he resolved to solve the mystery
to mitigate the pain of the old couple
questions.explanation: 'Ingenous' is misspelt: the word is 'ingenuous' (innocent, artless), or 'ingenious' (clever).

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. The newspaper dedicated “a report giving the news of the death and details about the life of the deceased.”
questions.explanation: An obituary is a newspaper notice of a death with an account of the person's life.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A pause between the acts of a play
questions.explanation: An interlude is an interval between the acts of a play, or something performed in it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Face up to
questions.explanation: To 'face up to' something is to accept and deal with a difficult situation.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error The perception / of success / vary / from person to person.
questions.explanation: The subject 'The perception' is singular, so the verb must be 'varies'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Eccentric
questions.explanation: 'Eccentric' means unconventional or odd: 'queer' in its older sense of strange.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. An instrument for detecting an earthquake
questions.explanation: A seismograph detects and records earthquakes.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hale and hearty
questions.explanation: 'Hale and hearty' means strong and healthy, said especially of older people.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Fall back or sink again (into a worse state after an improvement)
questions.explanation: To 'relapse' is to fall back into a worse state, such as an illness, after an improvement.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Ludicrous
questions.explanation: 'Ludicrous' means absurd or ridiculous: 'crazy' in that sense.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. Fiona enquired whether I had gone to school on Tuesday.
options: “Had you been going to school on Tuesday?” Fiona asked me.
“Where are you going on Tuesday?’’ Fiona asked me.
“Did you go to school on Tuesday?’’ Fiona asked me.
“Are you gone to school on Tuesday? Fiona enquired.
questions.explanation: 'Whether' marks a yes/no question, 'I' becomes 'you' and the past perfect 'had gone' goes back to the simple past: 'Did you go to school on Tuesday?'

questions.text: Which word in the given sentence is the ANTONYM of – jeopardy? We were reluctant to leave the relative safety of our hotel.
questions.explanation: 'Jeopardy' means danger; its opposite in the sentence is 'safety'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He didn’t / called me / in the / last week.
questions.explanation: After 'did' (or 'didn't') the verb takes its base form: 'He didn't call me'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. He invited me to his place yesterday.
options: I invited to his place yesterday.
I was invited by him to his place yesterday.
To his place I was invited yesterday.
questions.explanation: The object 'me' becomes the subject 'I', the simple past 'invited' becomes 'was invited', and the doer follows as 'by him'.

questions.text: Select the correct homonym from the given options to fill in the blank. The wind________ so powerfully that the door closed.
questions.explanation: 'Blew', the past tense of 'blow', matches 'closed'; 'blue', the colour, only sounds the same.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Everything (1) _________ us makes our environment. Living and non-living things form the (2) _________ of our surroundings. Plants, animals and microbes are parts of our environment. Humans have affected the environment in multiple (3) ______ like clearing of forests, building houses and farms, making roads, etc. This is the root (4) _______ of air, water and land pollution on the planet. Ecologists across the globe are making efforts to educate mankind about the (5) _________ of nature, the crisis we face and the methods of managing these crises.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Everything around us', all that surrounds us, makes up our environment.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Everything (1) _________ us makes our environment. Living and non-living things form the (2) _________ of our surroundings. Plants, animals and microbes are parts of our environment. Humans have affected the environment in multiple (3) ______ like clearing of forests, building houses and farms, making roads, etc. This is the root (4) _______ of air, water and land pollution on the planet. Ecologists across the globe are making efforts to educate mankind about the (5) _________ of nature, the crisis we face and the methods of managing these crises.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Living and non-living things are the 'components', the parts, that make up our surroundings.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Everything (1) _________ us makes our environment. Living and non-living things form the (2) _________ of our surroundings. Plants, animals and microbes are parts of our environment. Humans have affected the environment in multiple (3) ______ like clearing of forests, building houses and farms, making roads, etc. This is the root (4) _______ of air, water and land pollution on the planet. Ecologists across the globe are making efforts to educate mankind about the (5) _________ of nature, the crisis we face and the methods of managing these crises.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Humans have affected the environment 'in multiple ways', which the sentence then lists.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Everything (1) _________ us makes our environment. Living and non-living things form the (2) _________ of our surroundings. Plants, animals and microbes are parts of our environment. Humans have affected the environment in multiple (3) ______ like clearing of forests, building houses and farms, making roads, etc. This is the root (4) _______ of air, water and land pollution on the planet. Ecologists across the globe are making efforts to educate mankind about the (5) _________ of nature, the crisis we face and the methods of managing these crises.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'The root cause' is the set phrase for the basic reason something happens.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Everything (1) _________ us makes our environment. Living and non-living things form the (2) _________ of our surroundings. Plants, animals and microbes are parts of our environment. Humans have affected the environment in multiple (3) ______ like clearing of forests, building houses and farms, making roads, etc. This is the root (4) _______ of air, water and land pollution on the planet. Ecologists across the globe are making efforts to educate mankind about the (5) _________ of nature, the crisis we face and the methods of managing these crises.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Ecologists teach mankind about 'the wonders of nature' before turning to the crisis we face.

questions.text: If 14 January 2022 was Friday, then what will be the day of the week on 28 February 2025?
questions.explanation: From 14 January 2022 to 14 January 2025 is 365 + 365 + 366 = 1,096 days (2024 is a leap year), 4 odd days, so 14 January 2025 is a Tuesday. 28 February 2025 is 17 + 28 = 45 days later, 3 odd days: Friday.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term related to third term. 5372: 7532 :: 4928: 9842 :: 9284:?
questions.explanation: The second number has the first's digits in descending order: 5372 → 7532 and 4928 → 9842. So 9284 → 9842.

questions.text: Seven friends A, B, C, D, E, F and G, each has a different height. C is taller than D. A is the shortest among all. Only four people are taller than C. E is taller than G but shorter than F. F is not the tallest. The height of how many people is between the heights of B and G?
questions.explanation: Four people are taller than C, so C is fifth tallest; A is seventh, so D, shorter than C, is sixth. F, E and G come in that order among the top four and F is not first, so B is the tallest, then F, E and G. F and E stand between B and G.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) ATM : Bank :: Ambulance : ?
questions.explanation: An ATM is a service of a bank, as an ambulance is a service of a hospital.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘ADDITION’ is written as ‘EBJEJUOP’ and ‘SUBTRACT’ is written as ‘VTUCBSUD’. How will 'MULTIPLY’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward and the letters of each pair then swap: ADDITION → BE EJ UJ PO → EB JE JU OP. So MULTIPLY → NV MU JQ MZ → VN UM QJ ZM: VNUMQJZM.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1.Assertive 2.Astringent 3.Astronomy 4.Aspirations 5.Ascertain
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Ascertain (5), Aspirations (4), Assertive (1), Astringent (2), Astronomy (3). 'Asc', 'Asp', 'Ass' and 'Ast' come in that order, and 'Astri' before 'Astro'.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 9, 18, 15, ?, 55, 330
If I denotes ‘÷’, J denotes ‘×’, K denotes ‘−’ and L denotes ‘+’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? (18 I 9) J 12 L 22 K 41 L (36J2) K 2 J 8 = ?
Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? RSDA, WDUX, ?, GZCR, LKTO
questions.explanation: Wrapping round the alphabet, the first letters move 5 places forward (R, W, B, G, L), the second 11 (S, D, O, Z, K), the third 17 (D, U, L, C, T), and the fourth 3 places back (A, X, U, R, O): BOLU.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 5, 30, 35, ?, 143, 286
Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? WXYZ, XWZY, YVAX, ?, ATCV
questions.explanation: The first and third letters move one place forward (W, X, Y, Z, A and Y, Z, A, B, C); the second and fourth move one place back (X, W, V, U, T and Z, Y, X, W, V): ZUBW.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (45, 37, 360) (17, 14, 51) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: The third number is the first times the difference of the first two: 45 × (45 − 37) = 360 and 17 × (17 − 14) = 51. Likewise 34 × (34 − 26) = 272.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 36, 45, 63, 90, 126, 171, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, multiples of 9, so the next is 54: 171 + 54 = 225.

questions.text: Which two numbers, from amongst the given options, should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? (17×4) – (7)²+ (63÷9)×6 + 83 – 41 = 83
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 25*5*10*2*4*21
Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term 6 : 43 :: ? : 203 :: 20 : 407
questions.explanation: Each second number is the square of the first plus 7: 6² + 7 = 43 and 20² + 7 = 407. As 203 − 7 = 196 = 14², the missing term is 14.

questions.text: Which letter will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? V, S, O, L, ? , E
questions.explanation: The letters move back 3 and 4 places in turn: V, S (−3), O (−4), L (−3), H (−4), E (−3).

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (41, 24, 39) (10, 5, 13) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: The first and third numbers add up to three times the second plus 8: 41 + 39 = 80 = 3 × 24 + 8 and 10 + 13 = 23 = 3 × 5 + 8. Likewise 22 + 37 = 59 = 3 × 17 + 8; no other set fits.

questions.text: In a certain code language, “ISLAND” is written as “SIALDN”, and “LAWYER” is written as “ALYWRE”. How will “LAUNCH” be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters of each pair swap: IS LA ND → SI AL DN and LA WY ER → AL YW RE. So LA UN CH → AL NU HC: ALNUHC.

questions.text: The mean of five numbers is 18. If one number is excluded, their mean is 16. The excluded number is:
questions.explanation: The five numbers total 5 × 18 = 90 and the other four 4 × 16 = 64, so the excluded number is 90 − 64 = 26.

questions.text: After seeing a policeman from a distance of 500 m, a thief starts running at a speed of 10 km/h. After noticing, the policeman chases immediately with a speed of 12 km/h, and the thief is caught. The distance run by the policeman is:
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 12 − 10 = 2 km/h, so he closes the 0.5 km gap in 0.25 hours, running 12 × 0.25 = 3 km.

questions.text: A varies jointly with B and C. A = 6 when B = 3 and C = 2. Find A when B = 5 and C = 7.
questions.explanation: A = kBC, and 6 = k × 3 × 2 gives k = 1. So A = 5 × 7 = 35.

questions.text: Which of the following options has the greatest value?
questions.explanation: 20 + 4 − 8 − 2 + 3 + 6 = 23, the only positive value; the others are −33, −68 and −155.

questions.text: In ΔABC, if G is the centroid and AD is a median with length 9 cm, then the length of AG is:
questions.explanation: The centroid divides each median in the ratio 2 : 1 from the vertex, so AG = (2/3) × 9 = 6 cm.

questions.text: A sum of ₹14,375, when invested at r% interest per year compounded annually, amounts to ₹16,767 after two years. What is the value of r?
The average of 10 observations is 21. A new observation is included and the average of these 11 numbers is 1 less than the prevoius average. The 11th observation is ______.
questions.explanation: The 10 observations total 10 × 21 = 210 and the 11 total 11 × 20 = 220, so the new one is 220 − 210 = 10.

questions.text: Which of the following is the least 6-digit number that is divisible by 93?
questions.explanation: 93 × 1075 = 99975, which leaves 100000 − 99975 = 25 over; the next multiple, 100000 + (93 − 25) = 100068, is the least 6-digit one.

questions.text: A number x is three times another number y. If the sum of both the numbers is 20, then x and y, respectively, are:
questions.explanation: x = 3y and x + y = 4y = 20, so y = 5 and x = 15.

questions.text: A person could save 20% of his income. A year later, his income increased by 25% but he could save the same amount only as before. By what percentage has his expenditure increased?
questions.explanation: On an income of 100 he spends 80 and saves 20. On 125 he still saves 20, so he spends 105: a rise of 25/80 = 31.25%.

questions.text: The marked price of a table fan is ₹3,750 and is available to the retailer at a discount of 20%. At what price should the retailer sell it to earn a profit of 15%?
questions.explanation: The retailer pays 80% of ₹3,750 = ₹3,000; a 15% profit means selling at ₹3,000 × 1.15 = ₹3,450.

questions.text: Ravi drove for 4 hours at a speed of 70 miles per hour and for 2 hours at 40 miles per hour. What was his average speed (in miles per hour) for the whole journey?
questions.explanation: He covers 4 × 70 + 2 × 40 = 360 miles in 6 hours: 360/6 = 60 miles per hour.

questions.text: What is the height of a solid right circular cylinder whose radius is 3 cm and total surface area is 60 π cm²?
questions.explanation: Total surface area = 2πr(r + h) = 6π(3 + h) = 60π, so 3 + h = 10 and h = 7 cm.

questions.text: 45 people can repair a road in 10 days, working 6 hours a day. In how many days can 30 people, working 6 hours a day, complete the same work?
questions.explanation: The work is 45 × 10 × 6 = 2,700 person-hours; 30 people working 6 hours a day need 2,700/180 = 15 days.

questions.text: Under a discount scheme, a dozen pair of gloves quoted at ₹200 is available at a discount of 20%. How many pairs of gloves can be bought for ₹320?
questions.explanation: A dozen pairs costs ₹200 × 0.8 = ₹160, so ₹320 buys two dozen: 24 pairs.

questions.text: A pen passing through two hands is finally sold at a profit of 44% of the original cost price. If the first dealer makes a profit of 20%, then the profit made by the second dealer is:
questions.explanation: 1.2 × (1 + p) = 1.44, so 1 + p = 1.2 and the second dealer's profit is 20%.

questions.text: A shopkeeper purchases 20000 units of a product at ₹1 each, 15000 units at ₹1.15 each and 5000 units at ₹2 each. What is the weighted average price of one unit? (Correct to two decimal places)
In 1928,who discovered that when a ray of coloured light enters a liquid, a fraction of the light scattered by that liquid is of a different colour?
questions.explanation: In 1928 C. V. Raman found that a small part of the light scattered by a liquid changes in wavelength, and so in colour: the Raman effect, which won him the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics.

questions.text: Which of the following autobiographies is written by former English footballer, David Beckham published in 2003 ?
questions.explanation: 'My Side' (2003) is David Beckham's autobiography.

questions.text: Which sport scheme was extended from 2021-22 to 2025-26 in March 2021?
questions.explanation: Khelo India, the Sports Ministry's main scheme for grassroots sport, was extended from 2021-22 to 2025-26, as the Sports Minister told Parliament in March 2021. Rajiv Gandhi Khel Abhiyan, the Urban Sports Infrastructure Scheme and the National Sports Talent Search Scheme had been merged into it in 2016-17.

questions.text: In which state is cactus vegetation found in dry areas of Thorny Bushes in the form of spines?
questions.explanation: NCERT places India's thorn forests and scrub (acacias, palms, euphorbias and cacti) in the semi-arid north-west, Rajasthan among them; in cacti the leaves are reduced to spines to cut water loss. West Bengal, Assam and Odisha are far wetter.

questions.text: Kalamandalam Rajan received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2009 for which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: Kalamandalam Rajan, a Kathakali actor from Kerala trained at Kerala Kalamandalam, received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 2009 for his contribution to Kathakali, the classical dance-drama of Kerala.

questions.text: What is the duration of the interval in a football match?
questions.explanation: Under the Laws of the Game the half-time interval in football may last up to 15 minutes.

questions.text: Diving comes under which category of sport?
questions.explanation: Diving, like swimming and water polo, is an aquatic sport.

questions.text: Which of the following Bollywood choreographers has won the 63rd National Film Awards in the category of Best Choreography for his/her excellent work in the Hindi movie ‘Diwani Mastani’?
questions.explanation: Remo D'Souza won the National Film Award for Best Choreography at the 63rd awards for the song 'Deewani Mastani' in 'Bajirao Mastani' (2015).

questions.text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution empowers a High Court to issue writs for the enforcement of the Fundamental Rights of the citizens?
questions.explanation: Article 226 lets a High Court issue writs for the enforcement of the Fundamental Rights and for any other purpose; Article 32 gives the Supreme Court that power for the Fundamental Rights.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct pair?
questions.explanation: Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma revived Mohiniyattam and is known as its mother. Sonal Mansingh is an Odissi and Bharatanatyam dancer, Shovana Narayan a Kathak dancer and Balasaraswati was a Bharatanatyam dancer.

questions.text: ‘Faster than Lightning - My Story’ is the autobiography of _____.
questions.explanation: 'Faster than Lightning' (2013) is the autobiography of the Jamaican sprinter Usain Bolt.

questions.text: Which is a major essential lipophilic (fat-soluble) vitamin required for the protection of cell membranes and the formation of red blood cells (RBCs)?
questions.explanation: Vitamin E, a fat-soluble antioxidant, protects cell membranes from oxidative damage and is needed for healthy red blood cells.

questions.text: Gangubai Hangal was an Indian vocalist of Hindustani classical tradition who was awarded the Sangeet Natak Academy Award in 1973. From which of the following musical Gharanas did she belong?
questions.explanation: Gangubai Hangal was one of the leading vocalists of the Kirana gharana.

questions.text: The long jumper ______________ won Silver in the U-20 World Athletics Championships in August 2021.
questions.explanation: Shaili Singh won silver in the women's long jump at the World Athletics U20 Championships in Nairobi in August 2021, missing gold by one centimetre.

questions.text: In which year did Rudolf Virchow published an essay titled ‘Cellular Pathology’ in which he famously declared that "every cell arises from another cell”?
questions.explanation: Rudolf Virchow put forward 'omnis cellula e cellula' (every cell from a cell) in 1855, the date NCERT gives.

questions.text: Who among the following Hindustani classical musicians blended the best of classical music and created a unique style of music of his own who was often touted as the Tansen of 20th century?
questions.explanation: Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan of the Patiala gharana was called the Tansen of the twentieth century.

questions.text: By what metabolic process in the kitchen can you make food like curd, paneer and sauerkraut?
questions.explanation: Curd and sauerkraut are made by fermentation, in which bacteria turn sugars into lactic acid. Paneer is strictly curdled with an acid such as lemon juice rather than fermented, but condensation, pasteurisation and steaming make none of the three.

questions.text: Which of the following is an organic compound with the formula C₆H₄Cl₂ that is used as a fumigant insecticide to control cloth moths?
questions.explanation: Paradichlorobenzene (1,4-dichlorobenzene) is the moth-repellent fumigant used in mothballs against clothes moths.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Kumar Gandharva was a Hindustani classical vocalist, not a guitarist. Zia Mohiuddin Dagar played the rudra veena, Kadri Gopalnath the saxophone, and Bombay Jayashri is a Carnatic vocalist.

questions.text: In which sport did TP Ouseph receive the Dronacharya Award in the Lifetime Achievement category for outstanding coaches in Sports and Games 2021?
questions.explanation: T. P. Ouseph, an athletics coach, received the Dronacharya Award in the lifetime category in 2021.

questions.text: In which year was International Booker Prize established?
questions.explanation: The International Booker Prize began in 2005 as the Man Booker International Prize; the Booker Prize itself dates from 1969.

questions.text: In the format of the IUPAC name of the organic compound, the term ‘Root’ is used to represent:
options: functional groups that may be present in the compound
the cyclic or acyclic nature of the given compound
the number of carbon atoms in the parent chain
the presence of side chains or substituent groups
questions.explanation: In an IUPAC name the word root gives the number of carbon atoms in the parent chain (meth-, eth-, prop-); the prefixes and suffixes show substituents, saturation and functional groups.

questions.text: Ms. Kamalini Asthana and Ms. Nalini Asthana are conferred with one of the top highest civilian awards of India, Padma Shri 2022. Which of the following dance forms of Banaras Gharana are they known for?
questions.explanation: Nalini and Kamalini Asthana, sisters of the Banaras gharana, are Kathak dancers; they received the Padma Shri in 2022.

questions.text: Ustad Hassu Khan, Ustad Haddu Khan and Ustad Nathu Khan were exponents of the ___________ Gharana.
questions.explanation: Hassu Khan, Haddu Khan and Nathu Khan were the leading early masters of the Gwalior gharana, the oldest school of khayal singing.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate spelling that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. “Compparision” with others is not always good.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'comparison'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. I don’t get on with the new boss, so I “have asked to transferring” to another branch of the company.
options: will have ask to be transfer
have been ask to be transferring
questions.explanation: 'Ask' takes a passive infinitive here: 'I have asked to be transferred to another branch of the company.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A word that has the same or nearly the same meaning as another word in the same language
questions.explanation: A synonym has the same or nearly the same meaning as another word; an antonym has the opposite meaning.

questions.text: Recognise the erroneous part in the given sentence and choose the most appropriate answer from the options given to ensure a meaningful sentence. As she kept walking to me, my heart skipped a beat .
options: As she kept walking within me, my heart skipped a beat.
As she kept walking from me, my heart skipped a beat
As she kept into me, my heart skipped a beat.
As she kept walking towards me, my heart skipped a beat.
questions.explanation: Movement in someone's direction takes 'towards': 'As she kept walking towards me, my heart skipped a beat.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Snake in the grass
questions.explanation: A 'snake in the grass' is a treacherous person who pretends to be a friend.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'exhibitionistic'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Get one’s dander up
questions.explanation: To 'get one's dander up' is to become angry: to lose one's temper.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Usnis has not used the computer for weeks.
options: The computer did not used by Usnis for weeks.
The computer has not been used by Usnis for weeks.
The computer was not been used by Usnis for weeks.
The computer has not being used by Usnis for weeks.
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'has not used' becomes 'has not been used' in the passive: 'The computer has not been used by Usnis for weeks.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. All the young boys and girls / in the family / will try his luck / in the card games tonight.
options: All the young boys and girls
questions.explanation: The subject 'all the young boys and girls' is plural, so the pronoun must be 'their': 'will try their luck'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. The fishermen of our village are constantly complaining of the poor “number of fishes getting caught” these days.
questions.explanation: A 'haul' is the quantity of fish caught: 'complaining of the poor haul these days'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The world is constantly living in risk, uncertainty and fear of _________.
questions.explanation: Living with risk and uncertainty goes with the 'fear of death'; fear of life, the body or nature does not fit the sense.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Thus, children in India have the unique opportunity to receive a world-class education. B. Since ancient times, India has been known for its great educational system. C. Today, there are thousands of schools in India, many of which are among the best in the world. D. The country's first university, Nalanda, was founded over 1,000 years ago.
questions.explanation: B introduces India's long tradition of education, D gives its earliest example, Nalanda, C moves to today's schools, and A concludes with 'Thus': BDCA.

questions.text: Select the sentence which has no spelling error.
options: Pneuonomia can be treated at home.
The chief cause of pneumonia is a microbe.
Aspiration pneunomia is found in French bulldogs.
Arctic explorers cannot catch pneunomeea in frozen north.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'pneumonia'; the other sentences misspell it as 'pneuonomia', 'pneunomia' and 'pneunomeea'.

questions.text: Which word in the given sentence is the ANTONYM of – susceptible? The president claimed he was immune from prosecution.
questions.explanation: 'Susceptible' means open to being affected by something; 'immune' means protected from it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Renounce
questions.explanation: To 'renounce' something is to give it up formally: to 'abjure' it. 'Embrace' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence. A dishonest employee “plays fast” with his boss.
questions.explanation: To 'play fast and loose' with someone is to treat them dishonestly or irresponsibly.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. A new policy for peace and tolerance was formulated by the member nations in the Universal Council meeting yesterday.
options: The member nations formulated a new policy for peace and tolerance in the Universal Council meeting yesterday.
The member nations in the Universal Council meeting yesterday were formulated a new policy for peace and tolerance.
The member nations in the Universal Council meeting yesterday were formulating a new policy for peace and tolerance.
A new policy formulated the member nations in the Universal Council meeting yesterday for peace and tolerance
questions.explanation: The agent, 'the member nations', becomes the subject and 'was formulated' the simple past 'formulated': 'The member nations formulated a new policy for peace and tolerance in the Universal Council meeting yesterday.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The term ‘health’ refers to human beings’ state of physical, psychological and (1)________ well-being. Health and fitness are (2)______ linked and we must concentrate on maintaining our health and (3)_______. If we need to be healthy, we must (4)_______ our wellness. We (5)______ start taking care of ourselves because health is wealth.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Health is physical, mental and 'social' well-being, as the World Health Organization defines it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The term ‘health’ refers to human beings’ state of physical, psychological and (1)________ well-being. Health and fitness are (2)______ linked and we must concentrate on maintaining our health and (3)_______. If we need to be healthy, we must (4)_______ our wellness. We (5)______ start taking care of ourselves because health is wealth.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Health and fitness are 'inextricably' linked: so closely that they cannot be separated.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The term ‘health’ refers to human beings’ state of physical, psychological and (1)________ well-being. Health and fitness are (2)______ linked and we must concentrate on maintaining our health and (3)_______. If we need to be healthy, we must (4)_______ our wellness. We (5)______ start taking care of ourselves because health is wealth.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: We must maintain our health and 'fitness', the pair the sentence has just linked.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The term ‘health’ refers to human beings’ state of physical, psychological and (1)________ well-being. Health and fitness are (2)______ linked and we must concentrate on maintaining our health and (3)_______. If we need to be healthy, we must (4)_______ our wellness. We (5)______ start taking care of ourselves because health is wealth.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4
questions.explanation: To be healthy we must 'prioritise', that is put first, our wellness.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The term ‘health’ refers to human beings’ state of physical, psychological and (1)________ well-being. Health and fitness are (2)______ linked and we must concentrate on maintaining our health and (3)_______. If we need to be healthy, we must (4)_______ our wellness. We (5)______ start taking care of ourselves because health is wealth.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses necessity: we must start taking care of ourselves, because health is wealth.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'BREAK’ is written as 'BSEBK' and 'FAST' is written as 'FBSU'. How will 'BREAKFAST' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Letters in odd positions stay and those in even positions move one place forward: BREAK → BSEBK and FAST → FBSU. So BREAKFAST → BSEBKGATT.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 132, 133, 129, 156, 140, 265, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are +1, −4, +27, −16, +125: odd cubes added and even squares subtracted (1³, 2², 3³, 4², 5³). Next comes −6² = −36: 265 − 36 = 229.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 26*56*4*17*49*7*30

Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some chairs are racks. All beds are trays. All racks are beds. Conclusion: I. Some chairs are beds. II. All beds are racks. III. All trays are chairs.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: The chairs that are racks are beds, since all racks are beds, so some chairs are beds (I). All racks being beds does not make all beds racks (II), and nothing makes all trays chairs (III).

questions.text: In a certain code language, “ABILITY” is written as “BDLLITY”, and “CONDUCT” is written as “DQQDUCT”. How will “DISPLAY” be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first three letters move 1, 2 and 3 places forward and the rest stay: ABILITY → BDLLITY and CONDUCT → DQQDUCT. So DISPLAY → EKVPLAY.

questions.text: If M denotes ‘−’, N denotes ‘÷’, O denotes ‘×’ and P denotes ‘+’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? (14 O 7 ) P 41 M (26 O 3 ) P (176 N 2) = ?
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 192,408,283,347,320,?
questions.explanation: The differences are +216, −125, +64, −27: the cubes from 6³ down, added and subtracted in turn. Next is +2³ = 8: 320 + 8 = 328.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. LARGEST : ESTGLAR :: QUALITY : ITYLQUA :: QUICKLY : ?
questions.explanation: The last three letters come first, then the middle letter, then the first three: LAR G EST → EST G LAR and QUA L ITY → ITY L QUA. So QUI C KLY → KLYCQUI.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? AAVR, XEQX, ?, RMGJ, OQBP
questions.explanation: First letters move back 3 (A, X, U, R, O), second letters forward 4 (A, E, I, M, Q), third letters back 5 (V, Q, L, G, B) and fourth letters forward 6 (R, X, D, J, P): UILD.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs, except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first plus 5: 6² + 5 = 41, 4² + 5 = 21 and 7² + 5 = 54. 8² + 5 = 69, not 70, so 8 : 70 is the odd pair.

questions.text: Which two numbers, from amongst the given options, should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? (132÷12) + (6×11) + 18 – (64÷16)×8 = 70

Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 12 : 67 :: 21 : 112 :: 17 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is five times the first plus 7: 12 × 5 + 7 = 67 and 21 × 5 + 7 = 112. Likewise 17 × 5 + 7 = 92.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 17 : 78 :: 15 : 68 :: 28 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is five times the first minus 7: 17 × 5 − 7 = 78 and 15 × 5 − 7 = 68. Likewise 28 × 5 − 7 = 133.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row - 14, 64, 10; Second row - 7, 18, 12; Third row - 23, 88, ? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: In each row the middle number is twice the difference of three times the first and the third: 2 × (42 − 10) = 64 and 2 × (21 − 12) = 18. So 2 × (69 − ?) = 88 gives ? = 25.

questions.text: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? XQNH, YOQD, ZMTZ, ?, BIZR
questions.explanation: First letters move forward 1 (X, Y, Z, A, B), second letters back 2 (Q, O, M, K, I), third letters forward 3 (N, Q, T, W, Z) and fourth letters back 4 (H, D, Z, V, R): AKWV.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the sixth number is related to the fifth number. 3 : 26 :: 7 : ? :: 5 : 74
questions.explanation: The second number is three times the square of the first minus 1: 3 × 3² − 1 = 26 and 3 × 5² − 1 = 74. Likewise 3 × 7² − 1 = 146.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'COUNTY' is written as 'YTNUOC', and 'DEFEAT' is written as 'TAEFED'. How will 'FAMILY' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is written backwards: COUNTY → YTNUOC and DEFEAT → TAEFED. So FAMILY → YLIMAF.

questions.text: If 13 January 2006 is a Friday, then what will be the day of the week on 28 March 2008?
questions.explanation: 2006 and 2007 have 365 days each, so 13 January moves on one day a year: Saturday in 2007, Sunday in 2008. From 13 January to 28 March 2008, a leap year, is 18 + 29 + 28 = 75 days, 10 weeks and 5 days: Sunday + 5 = Friday.

questions.text: A shopkeeper marks his articles at 30% above the cost price and allows the purchaser a discount of 20% for cash buying. What profit per cent does he make?
questions.explanation: On a cost price of 100 the marked price is 130, and 20% off leaves 130 × 0.8 = 104: a profit of 4%.

questions.text: If P varies directly as Q, and P = 227 when Q = 232, find P when Q = 116.
questions.explanation: P/Q stays constant, and Q is halved from 232 to 116, so P is halved too: 227 ÷ 2 = 113.5.

questions.text: In a 1200 m race, the ratio of the speeds of two contestants Meenal and Nitu is 5:7. If Meenal has a start of 500 m, then Meenal wins by:
questions.explanation: With a 500 m start Meenal runs 700 m. In that time Nitu, at 7/5 of Meenal's speed, runs 700 × 7/5 = 980 m, so Meenal wins by 1200 − 980 = 220 m.

questions.text: The tax on a commodity diminishes by 14% and its consumption increases by 10%. Find the effect on revenue.
questions.explanation: Revenue = tax × consumption: 0.86 × 1.10 = 0.946, a decrease of 5.4%.

questions.text: 40% of Ranita’s income is equal to 56% of Bhaskar’s income. If Ranita’s income was ₹800 more than what it is and Bhaskar’s income was ₹ 2,000 more than what it is, then the ratio of the incomes of Ranita and Bhaskar would have been 4 : 3. What is the actual combined income of Ranita and Bhaskar?
The average weight of 18 persons increases by 2.5 kg when a new person comes in place of one of them weighing 72 kg. The weight of the new person is:
questions.explanation: The total rises by 18 × 2.5 = 45 kg, so the newcomer weighs 72 + 45 = 117 kg.

questions.text: If 15 people take 5 days to complete a job, in how many days can 25 people finish that work?
questions.explanation: The job takes 15 × 5 = 75 person-days, so 25 people need 75 ÷ 25 = 3 days.

questions.text: A sells a car to B at a gain of 10% and B again sells it to C at a profit of 5%. If C pays ₹4,06,000 to B, what is the cost price of the car for A? (Consider integral part only)
questions.explanation: C pays 1.10 × 1.05 = 1.155 times A's cost, so A's cost = ₹4,06,000 ÷ 1.155 = ₹3,51,515.15; the integral part is ₹3,51,515.

questions.text: One dozen books quoted at ₹120 are available at 15% discount. How many books can be bought for ₹51?
questions.explanation: Each book is quoted at 120 ÷ 12 = ₹10 and costs ₹8.50 after 15% off, so ₹51 buys 51 ÷ 8.5 = 6 books.

questions.text: Find the compound interest on ₹35,000 in 2 years at 6% per annum, the interest being compounded half-yearly (nearest to a ₹):
questions.explanation: Half-yearly, the rate is 3% for 4 periods: 35,000 × 1.03⁴ = 35,000 × 1.1255088 = ₹39,392.81, so the interest is ₹4,392.81, or ₹4,393.

questions.text: Which of the following options is NOT divisible by 18?
questions.explanation: A number divisible by 18 must be even and have a digit sum divisible by 9. 245798 is even, but its digits add up to 35, not a multiple of 9; the others' sums are 18, 27 and 27.

questions.text: In November 2021, who became the chairman of ICC Men’s Cricket Committee?
questions.explanation: Sourav Ganguly was named chairman of the ICC Men's Cricket Committee in November 2021, succeeding Anil Kumble.

questions.text: How many organisations are part of ‘One Health’ Consortium, launched in October 2021?
questions.explanation: The Department of Biotechnology's 'One Health' consortium, launched on 14 October 2021 to track zoonotic and transboundary infections, has 27 organisations, led by DBT-NIAB, Hyderabad.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a correct pair?
options: How I Became a Hindu - Sita Ram Goel
questions.explanation: 'Unbreakable' is the autobiography of the boxer Mary Kom; Abhinav Bindra's is 'A Shot at History'.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT included in the value added method of calculating national income?
options: Value of final goods and services produced in economy
All value of producing enterprises in primary sector
questions.explanation: Second-hand goods were counted in the year they were produced; reselling them adds no new value, so they are left out of national income.

questions.text: Which period in India is referred to as a steady population growth period?
questions.explanation: NCERT divides India's population growth into phases: stagnant 1901-1921, steady 1921-1951, rapid (the population explosion) 1951-1981, and high but slowing after 1981.

questions.text: Who among the following Padma Bhushan Awardee dance legends has created a new dance form by the name of Bharat Nrityam?
questions.explanation: Padma Subrahmanyam, the Bharatanatyam dancer and scholar, created Bharata Nrityam from the movements described in the Natya Shastra.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘The Room on the Roof’?
questions.explanation: 'The Room on the Roof' was Ruskin Bond's first novel, written when he was seventeen.

questions.text: What is the width of the tennis court for Doubles?
questions.explanation: A tennis court is 10.97 m (36 ft) wide for doubles and 8.23 m (27 ft) for singles.

questions.text: Which Part of the Indian Constitution deals with the State Legislature?
questions.explanation: Part VI, on the States, covers the State Legislature in Articles 168 to 212.

questions.text: Which of the following are non-vascular flowerless plants in the taxonomic division of Bryophyta?
questions.explanation: Mosses are bryophytes: flowerless plants with no vascular tissue. Ferns are vascular, pines are gymnosperms and the pea is a flowering plant.

questions.text: Who was awarded the Society's Royal Medal for his atomic theory in 1826?
questions.explanation: John Dalton received one of the Royal Society's first Royal Medals, in 1826, for his atomic theory.

questions.text: Lata Mangeshkar was awarded with the Bharat Ratna in __________.
questions.explanation: Lata Mangeshkar received the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

questions.text: Which protein acts like a binder, holding food together and adding a ‘stretch’ property, and is found naturally in some grains, including wheat, barley, and rye?
questions.explanation: Gluten, the protein of wheat, barley and rye, holds food together and gives dough its stretch.

questions.text: Asad Ali Khan is a maestro of playing ____________.
questions.explanation: Ustad Asad Ali Khan was a master of the rudra veena, the instrument of the dhrupad tradition.

questions.text: Who among the following has authored the famous novel ‘To kill a mockingbird’?
questions.explanation: Harper Lee wrote 'To Kill a Mockingbird' (1960).

questions.text: Which of the following is a white, crystalline organic acid often used as an acidulant in grape and lime-flavoured drinks, gelatine desserts, jams, jellies, and hard sour confectionery?
questions.explanation: Tartaric acid, found naturally in grapes, is a white crystalline acid used to give foods and drinks a sharp, sour taste.

questions.text: The 2023 Asia Cup Cricket tournament (ODI Edition) will be organised by which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: Pakistan was the host of the 2023 Asia Cup. Under the hybrid model agreed in 2023, four matches were played in Pakistan and the other nine, including the final, in Sri Lanka.

questions.text: Karnataka transgender dancer Manjamma Jogathi was conferred with the Padma Shri award for her contribution to _________ in 2021.
questions.explanation: Manjamma Jogathi, a transgender artist from Karnataka, received the Padma Shri for her work in folk dance, notably the Jogathi nritya.

questions.text: The bacterium flagellum is composed of three major structural elements. Which of the following is NOT one of these elements?
questions.explanation: A bacterial flagellum has three parts: the filament, the hook and the basal body. There is no 'torso'.

questions.text: Who is the first classical dancer of foreign origin who was conferred the Padma Shri in 2006 for her contributions to Odissi?
questions.explanation: Ileana Citaristi, born in Italy, trained in Odissi under Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra and received the Padma Shri in 2006.

questions.text: Who is the Chief Economic Advisor of India appointed in January 2022?
questions.explanation: V Anantha Nageswaran was appointed Chief Economic Adviser on 28 January 2022, succeeding K V Subramanian.

questions.text: ‘Born in India Made in England’ is an autobiography of Balraj Khanna. For which of the following art forms is he known?
questions.explanation: Balraj Khanna was a Punjab-born painter who made his career in Britain; 'Born in India Made in England' is subtitled 'Autobiography of a Painter'.

questions.text: Who among the following Musicians was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2019?
questions.explanation: Bhupen Hazarika, the Assamese singer and composer, was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2019, with Pranab Mukherjee and Nanaji Deshmukh.

questions.text: In which of the following cities was Lata Mangeshkar born?
questions.explanation: Lata Mangeshkar was born in Indore on 28 September 1929.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. You have made only “perfunctory” attempts to understand me!
questions.explanation: 'Perfunctory' means done carelessly, as a mere formality; its opposite is 'careful'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Imprisonment
questions.explanation: 'Incarceration' is confinement in prison: imprisonment.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hit the sack
questions.explanation: To 'hit the sack' is to go to bed: to go to sleep.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'sacrilege'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. In queer street
questions.explanation: To be 'in queer street' is to be in debt or in financial difficulty.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. When we got / to the train station, / the Rajdhani Express / had already been leaving.
questions.explanation: An action completed before another past action takes the past perfect: 'the Rajdhani Express had already left'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The students / and the teachers / worked hardly / to make the event a success.
options: to make the event a success
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' means scarcely; the adverb meaning 'with great effort' is 'hard': 'worked hard'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. I “guessed her feelings” when she started crying.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'estimated her emotions', the only option that keeps the sense of 'feelings': 'rejoinders' and 'ripostes' are replies, and 'reactions' changes the meaning. The sentence as printed is already correct ('guessed' fits better than 'estimated'), but there is no 'no improvement' option.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. His friends arranged for the ambulance and took him immediately to the hospital.
options: His friends would have arranged for the ambulance and taken him immediately to the hospital.
His friends were arranged for the ambulance and taken him immediately to the hospital.
The ambulance arranged for his friends and took him immediately to the hospital.
The ambulance was arranged for by his friends and he was immediately taken to the hospital.
questions.explanation: 'Arranged for' becomes 'was arranged for by' and 'took him' becomes 'he was taken': 'The ambulance was arranged for by his friends and he was immediately taken to the hospital.'

questions.text: Complete the collocation. When we met first it was very difficult to ______ the ice.
questions.explanation: 'Break the ice' is the set phrase: to ease the first awkwardness between people who have just met.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank Tagore and Gandhi were undoubtedly the two outstanding and _________ figures of India in the first half of twentieth century.
questions.explanation: Tagore and Gandhi were 'dominating' figures, the most influential of their time; the other words do not describe a person's standing.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. Raman is finding it difficult to adjust as he “has come to a different country from his own country for settling”
questions.explanation: An immigrant comes to live permanently in a foreign country; a pilgrim travels to a holy place and a globetrotter travels widely.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A.They also resolved to impose restrictions on the Russian central bank's ability to access and deploy the country's 'war chest' of an estimated $630 billion in foreign exchange reserves. B.Saturday's announcement by the US, the UK and European allies, including France and Germany, of a raft of 'further restrictive economic measures' to increase the costs on Russia for its invasion of Ukraine has just raised the risks of a more widespread economic fallout from this war. C.The immediate impact of these moves on Russia's economy and financial markets have manifested in a sharp depreciation in the value of the Rouble. D.With a view to further isolating Russia from the international financial system, the Western allies decided to block 'selected' Russian banks from the SWIFT messaging system that banks and financial institutions use to validate and complete international payment transactions.
questions.explanation: B announces the new measures, D gives the first (cutting banks off from SWIFT), A adds another with 'also', and C describes their immediate impact: BDAC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Defile
questions.explanation: To 'defile' is to make dirty or impure; its opposite is to 'purify'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Exorcise
questions.explanation: To 'exorcise' an evil spirit is to drive it out: to 'expel' it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Who is talking “in” the phone?
questions.explanation: One talks 'on' the phone: 'Who is talking on the phone?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. You can sleep here but this bed is “squalid” and wet.
questions.explanation: 'Squalid' means dirty and unpleasant; its opposite is 'clean'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Union Budget, 2018-19, has proposed to treat school education holistically without (1)__________ from pre-nursery to Class 12. Samagra Shiksha - an overarching programme for the school education sector extending from pre-school to class 12 has been, therefore, (2) ______ with the broader goal of improving school effectiveness measured in terms of equal opportunities (3) _______ schooling and equitable learning outcomes. The Goal SDG-4.1 states that, “By 2030, ensure that all boys and girls complete free, equitable and quality primary and secondary education (4) _______ to relevant and effective learning outcomes”. Further the SDG 4.5 states that, “By 2030, eliminate gender (5)___________ in education and ensure equal access to all levels of education and vocational training for the vulnerable, including persons with disabilities, indigenous peoples and children in vulnerable situations”.

Select the most appropriate option to fill blank 1.
questions.explanation: The plan treats school education as one whole, 'without segmentation' into separate stages from pre-nursery to Class 12.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Union Budget, 2018-19, has proposed to treat school education holistically without (1)__________ from pre-nursery to Class 12. Samagra Shiksha - an overarching programme for the school education sector extending from pre-school to class 12 has been, therefore, (2) ______ with the broader goal of improving school effectiveness measured in terms of equal opportunities (3) _______ schooling and equitable learning outcomes. The Goal SDG-4.1 states that, “By 2030, ensure that all boys and girls complete free, equitable and quality primary and secondary education (4) _______ to relevant and effective learning outcomes”. Further the SDG 4.5 states that, “By 2030, eliminate gender (5)___________ in education and ensure equal access to all levels of education and vocational training for the vulnerable, including persons with disabilities, indigenous peoples and children in vulnerable situations”.

Select the most appropriate option to fill blank 2.
questions.explanation: The present perfect passive 'has been prepared' needs the past participle.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Union Budget, 2018-19, has proposed to treat school education holistically without (1)__________ from pre-nursery to Class 12. Samagra Shiksha - an overarching programme for the school education sector extending from pre-school to class 12 has been, therefore, (2) ______ with the broader goal of improving school effectiveness measured in terms of equal opportunities (3) _______ schooling and equitable learning outcomes. Further the SDG 4.5 states that, “By 2030, eliminate gender (5)___________ in education and ensure equal access to all levels of education and vocational training for the vulnerable, including persons with disabilities, indigenous peoples and children in vulnerable situations”.

Select the most appropriate option to fill blank 3.
questions.explanation: 'Equal opportunities for schooling': 'opportunity' takes 'for'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Union Budget, 2018-19, has proposed to treat school education holistically without (1)__________ from pre-nursery to Class 12. Samagra Shiksha - an overarching programme for the school education sector extending from pre-school to class 12 has been, therefore, (2) ______ with the broader goal of improving school effectiveness measured in terms of equal opportunities (3) _______ schooling and equitable learning outcomes. Select the most appropriate option to fill blank 4.
questions.explanation: Education 'leading to' relevant learning outcomes: the participle describes the education.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Union Budget, 2018-19, has proposed to treat school education holistically without (1)__________ from pre-nursery to Class 12. Samagra Shiksha - an overarching programme for the school education sector extending from pre-school to class 12 has been, therefore, (2) ______ with the broader goal of improving school effectiveness measured in terms of equal opportunities (3) _______ schooling and equitable learning outcomes. The Goal SDG-4.1 states that, “By 2030, ensure that all boys and girls complete free, equitable and quality primary and secondary education (4) _______ to relevant and effective learning outcomes”. Further the SDG 4.5 states that, “By 2030, eliminate gender (5)___________ in education and ensure equal access to all levels of education and vocational training for the vulnerable, including persons with disabilities, indigenous peoples and children in vulnerable situations”.

Select the most appropriate option to fill blank 5.
