questions.explanation: The goal is to 'eliminate gender disparities in education', that is remove inequalities, as 'ensure equal access' confirms.

questions.text: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All sparrows are peacocks. Some peacocks are birds. Conclusions: I. All birds are sparrow. II. Some sparrows are not birds.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Some peacocks are birds, but nothing ties birds to sparrows, so neither 'all birds are sparrows' (I) nor 'some sparrows are not birds' (II) must be true. Neither follows.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term is related to third term. PLANK : RMDOM :: TABLE : VBEMG :: ZEBRA : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +2, +1, +3, +1, +2: PLANK → RMDOM and TABLE → VBEMG. So ZEBRA → BFESC (Z wraps round to B).

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 34 : 169 :: 42 : 209 :: 28 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is five times the first minus 1: 34 × 5 − 1 = 169 and 42 × 5 − 1 = 209. Likewise 28 × 5 − 1 = 139.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term. 8 : 48 :: 19 : ? :: 16 : 112
questions.explanation: The second number is 8 times (the first minus 2): 8 × 6 = 48 and 8 × 14 = 112. Likewise 8 × 17 = 136.

questions.text: If 31 August 2000 was Friday, then what was the day of the week on 31 August 2009?
questions.explanation: From 31 August 2000 to 31 August 2009 is 9 years, two of them (taking in 29 February 2004 and 2008) leap years: 9 + 2 = 11 odd days, that is 4. Friday + 4 = Tuesday.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 14*11*97*67*10

Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row: 58,−28,−90; Second row: −17, 21,−12; Third row: −8,−7, ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the number into its constituent digits. For example, 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is −3 times the sum of the first two: (58 − 28) × (−3) = −90 and (−17 + 21) × (−3) = −12. So (−8 − 7) × (−3) = 45.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: In 2437 : 7342, 3569 : 9653 and 1786 : 6871 the digits are reversed. Reversed, 4328 would give 8234, not 8324, so it is the odd pair.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'you can do' is written as 'mat hat pat', 'They can work' is written as 'rat pat ant' and 'they do think' is written as 'ant hat cat'. How will 'Think' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: 'can' and 'pat' are common to the first two sentences, 'do' and 'hat' to the first and third, and 'they' and 'ant' to the second and third. That leaves think = cat.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'PIZZA' is written as 'PZZIA' and 'CHEESE' is written as 'CSEEHE'. How will 'PASTA' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The second letter and the second-last letter swap places: PIZZA → PZZIA and CHEESE → CSEEHE. In PASTA, A and T swap: PTSAA.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 9, 12, 21, 36, 57, 84, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 3, 9, 15, 21, 27, rising by 6 each time, so the next is 33: 84 + 33 = 117.

questions.text: In a certain code language, “SUIT” is written as “SITU”, and “CUTE” is written as “CTEU”. How will “WASH” be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first letter stays and the second moves to the end: SUIT → SITU and CUTE → CTEU. So WASH → WSHA.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 79 * 2 * 58 * 2 * 14 * 143
Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? AXUV, ?, YZWT, XAXS, WBYR
questions.explanation: First letters move back one (A, Z, Y, X, W), second letters forward one (X, Y, Z, A, B), third letters forward one (U, V, W, X, Y) and fourth letters back one (V, U, T, S, R). The missing cluster is ZYVU.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term related to third term. 7689 : 120 :: 6178 : 88 :: 3284 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is four times the sum of the first number's digits: (7 + 6 + 8 + 9) × 4 = 120 and (6 + 1 + 7 + 8) × 4 = 88. Likewise (3 + 2 + 8 + 4) × 4 = 68.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. p _ r _ p o _ p o r b _ o _ p o r b _ o r
options: o b p p o p
o b o p r p
o b r p r o
o b r p r p
questions.explanation: With o, b, r, p, r, p in the blanks the series reads porb por porb por porb por: 'porb' and 'por' alternate.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row: 32, 51, 33; Second row: 28, 33, 25; Third row: 16, 27, ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the number into its constituent digits. For example, 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is half the first plus a third of the second: 16 + 17 = 33 and 14 + 11 = 25. So 8 + 9 = 17.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1. Hypocrisy 2. Hilarious 3. Humidity 4. Highlight 5. Hallucinate
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Hallucinate (5), Highlight (4), Hilarious (2), Humidity (3), Hypocrisy (1). 'Ha' comes before 'Hi', 'Hig' before 'Hil', and 'Hu' before 'Hy'.

questions.text: The difference between a discount of 35% and two successive discounts of 20% and 20% on a certain bill, was ₹22. Find the amount of the bill.
questions.explanation: Two successive 20% discounts leave 0.8 × 0.8 = 0.64 of the bill, a 36% discount. The 1% difference from 35% is ₹22, so the bill is ₹2,200.

questions.text: Riya runs 3/2 times as fast as Prerna. In a race, if Riya gives a lead of 100 m to Prerna, find the distance Riya has to run before both of them meet.
questions.explanation: In the time Riya runs d, Prerna runs d − 100, so d : (d − 100) = 3 : 2. Then 2d = 3d − 300 and d = 300 m.

questions.text: A shopkeeper sold an article for ₹1,326 after allowing a discount of 15% on its marked price. Find the marked price of the article.
questions.explanation: The selling price is 85% of the marked price: 1,326 ÷ 0.85 = ₹1,560.

questions.text: If (x + 2) and (x − 3) are the factors of x² + k₁x + k₂ , then:
questions.explanation: (x + 2)(x − 3) = x² − x − 6, so k₁ = −1 and k₂ = −6.

questions.text: In a right circular cone, the radius of the base is 14 cm and the height is 48 cm. A cross-section is made through the midpoint of the height parallel to the base. The volume of the upper portion is: (Take π=22/7)
questions.explanation: The upper portion is a cone of half the height and half the radius, 24 cm and 7 cm: V = (1/3) × (22/7) × 7² × 24 = 1,232 cm³.

questions.text: On a sum of money, when invested for 2 years, compound interest and simple interest are ₹300 and ₹250, respectively. For both simple and compound interests the rate of interest per annum is the same, and for compound interest, interest is compounded annually. Find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.explanation: Simple interest is ₹125 a year. Compound interest exceeds it by ₹50, the second year's interest on the first year's ₹125: 50/125 = 40%.

questions.text: Find the greatest possible value of (a + b) for which the 8-digit number 143b203a is divisible by 15.
questions.explanation: Divisible by 5, a is 0 or 5; divisible by 3, the digit sum 13 + a + b must be a multiple of 3. With a = 5, 18 + b allows b = 9, so a + b = 14 (with a = 0, b is at most 8).

questions.text: P, Q and R are batsmen. The ratio of the runs scored by them in a certain match was P ∶ Q = 16 : 17 and Q : R = 15 ∶ 16. At the end of the match, they scored a total of 956 runs. The number of runs scored by R is (nearest to an integer):
The average weight of 8 men is increased by 1.5 kg when one of the men who weighs 65kg is replaced by a new man. The weight of the new man is:
questions.explanation: The total rises by 8 × 1.5 = 12 kg, so the new man weighs 65 + 12 = 77 kg.

questions.text: There is a continuous growth in the population of a village at the rate of 5% per annum. If its present population is 18522, what was the population of the village 3 years ago?
questions.explanation: Three years of 5% growth multiply the population by (21/20)³ = 9261/8000, so 3 years ago it was 18522 × 8000/9261 = 16000.

questions.text: If 15 boys earn ₹900 in 5 days, then how much will 20 boys earn in 7 days?
questions.explanation: Each boy earns 900 ÷ (15 × 5) = ₹12 a day, so 20 boys earn 20 × 7 × 12 = ₹1,680 in 7 days.

questions.text: The expenditure of a company increases by 25%, then increases by 30%, then further decreases by 20%.The overall percentage change in expenditure is:
By using faulty weight, a shopkeeper cheats to the extent of 6% while buying and selling rice. Find his gain percentage (rounded to two decimal places).
questions.explanation: Buying, he takes 106 g for the price of 100 g; selling, he gives 94 g for the price of 100 g. Gain = (106 − 94)/94 × 100 = 12.77%.

questions.text: Find the total surface area of a cylinder with diameter of base 28 cm and height 70 cm. (Take π=22/7)
M S Subbulakshmi, a legend in India is known for which of the following?
questions.explanation: M. S. Subbulakshmi was a Carnatic vocalist and the first musician to receive the Bharat Ratna (1998).

questions.text: Which term is used to describe all living communities on earth, including animals, plants, bacteria, fungi and photosynthetic microbes?
questions.explanation: The biosphere is the part of the earth where life exists, taking in all its living communities; a biome is one major type of community, such as a desert or a grassland.

questions.text: ‘Waiting for A Visa’ is a famous autobiography of ____________.
questions.explanation: 'Waiting for a Visa' is Dr B. R. Ambedkar's short autobiographical account of his experiences of untouchability.

questions.text: Who among the following personalities along with his sons played ‘Raga for Peace’ in the year 2014 at the ‘Nobel Peace Prize Concert’?
questions.explanation: Ustad Amjad Ali Khan, the sarod maestro, played 'Raga for Peace' with his sons Amaan and Ayaan at the 2014 Nobel Peace Prize Concert in Oslo.

questions.text: Who is the author of the historical novel ‘Twilight in Delhi’?
questions.explanation: Ahmed Ali's 'Twilight in Delhi' (1940) portrays a Muslim family of Delhi under British rule.

questions.text: Lalgudi Gopala Iyer Jayaraman used to play which of the following instruments?
questions.explanation: Lalgudi G. Jayaraman was one of the great violinists of Carnatic music.

questions.text: ‘Sea of Poppies’ is a novel written by which of the following writers?
questions.explanation: Amitav Ghosh's 'Sea of Poppies' (2008) is the first novel of his Ibis trilogy.

questions.text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution deals with the definition of the Money Bill?
questions.explanation: Article 110 defines a Money Bill; Article 109 sets out the special procedure for passing one.

questions.text: _______________ was established between informal groups (SHGs) and formal financial institutions (banks) for catering to the financial needs of the poor.
questions.explanation: Under the SHG–Bank Linkage Programme, begun by NABARD in 1992, banks lend directly to self-help groups of the poor.

questions.text: Hydroelectric power stations generate electricity by using the force of water that falls into the turbines and spins the shaft. By rotating the shaft of the turbine, the potential energy of water is converted into ________ energy.
questions.explanation: The falling water's potential energy becomes kinetic energy, which turns the turbine; the generator then turns this into electrical energy.

questions.text: Which is the highest peak in peninsular India?
questions.explanation: Anai Mudi (2,695 m), in the Western Ghats of Kerala, is the highest peak in peninsular India. K2, Kangchenjunga and Kamet are in the Karakoram and the Himalaya.

questions.text: Padma Shri awardee Ileana Citaristi, an Italy born Indian dance exponent was conferred the award for her major contribution to which of the following dances?
questions.explanation: Ileana Citaristi, Italian-born and based in Bhubaneswar, received the Padma Shri in 2006 for her contribution to Odissi.

questions.text: In 1838, who published an article discussing the structure and origin of plant cells?
questions.explanation: In 1838 Matthias Schleiden concluded that all plant tissues are made of cells; Theodor Schwann extended the idea to animals in 1839.

questions.text: The famous singer Jagjit Singh is known for which of the following genres?
questions.explanation: Jagjit Singh, known as the 'Ghazal King', brought the ghazal to a wide popular audience.

questions.text: The Men's World Boxing Championship 2023 will be hosted by which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: The 2023 Men's World Boxing Championships were held in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.

questions.text: ___________ was awarded the title of Hanjaba by the Maharaja of Manipur and the Sangit Natak Akademi Award in 1966.
questions.explanation: Guru Bipin Singh was one of the great gurus of Manipuri dance; he founded the Manipuri Nartanalaya in Kolkata.

questions.text: In July 2021, Mangubhai Chhaganbhai Patel was appointed as the Governor of _________________.
questions.explanation: Mangubhai Chhaganbhai Patel, earlier a minister in Gujarat, became Governor of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text: What is the name of the zone where trade winds converge?
questions.explanation: The north-east and south-east trade winds meet near the equator in the Inter-tropical convergence zone (ITCZ), a belt of rising air and heavy rain.

questions.text: __________ was the first woman dancer to receive the Padma Vibhushan, the nation’s second-highest civilian award.
questions.explanation: Tanjore Balasaraswati, the Bharatanatyam dancer, received the Padma Vibhushan in 1977.

questions.text: Who among the following was awarded the Dhyan Chand Award for Lifetime achievement in Sports and Games 2021 in Boxing discipline?
questions.explanation: The boxer Lekha K. C. was among the 2021 recipients of the Dhyan Chand Award for lifetime achievement.

questions.text: Who found out the relationship between the current I flowing in a metallic wire and the potential difference across its terminals?
questions.explanation: Georg Simon Ohm found that the current through a metallic conductor is proportional to the potential difference across it (Ohm's law, V = IR).

questions.text: As of August 2021, which Indian state organises Qila Raipur Sports Festival, also known as India’s Rural Olympics, annually?
questions.explanation: The Qila Raipur Sports Festival is held every year at Qila Raipur, near Ludhiana in Punjab.

questions.text: In the early 1980s, an aspartic acid-containing dipeptide sweetener was discovered, that was about 2000 times sweeter than sucrose. What is the name of that sweetener?
questions.explanation: Alitame, developed by Pfizer in the early 1980s, is a dipeptide made from aspartic acid and alanine, about 2,000 times as sweet as sucrose; aspartame is about 200 times as sweet.

questions.text: US-based Bharatanatyam/Kuchipudi exponent _________ has won the prestigious Abhinandan Saroja National Award 2021 by the National Institute of Indian Classical Dance at Samarpan on November 15th 2021.
questions.explanation: Aparna Satheesan, a US-based Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancer, received the National Institute of Indian Classical Dance's Abhinandan Saroja National Award for 2021, at a ceremony held online in November 2021.

questions.text: In which sport is the equipment called antenna used?
questions.explanation: The antennae on a volleyball net are flexible rods at its sides that mark the space through which the ball must cross.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She raced ______ towards the train.
questions.explanation: 'Frantically' means in a hurried, desperate way, which suits someone racing for a train. 'Berserk' is an adjective, and 'crazily' and 'hectically' do not fit the sense.

questions.text: Complete the sentence with an appropriate synonym of the word mentioned in the bracket. Diseases like Verminosis and Mastitis only ___________ (damage) domestic cattle.
questions.explanation: To 'afflict' is to cause suffering or harm: diseases afflict cattle. 'Delight', 'relieve' and 'assist' are nearly opposite to 'damage'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We have _______ long weekend ahead.
questions.explanation: 'Long weekend' is a singular countable noun mentioned for the first time, so it takes 'a'; 'an' goes only before a vowel sound.

questions.text: Spot the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the options given. There were more than thirty delegates who attend the training programme last summer.
options: There are more than thirty delegates who attend the training programme last summer
There were more than thirty delegates who attends the training programme last summer.
There was more than thirty delegates who attend the training programme last summer
There were more than thirty delegates who attended the training programme last summer.
questions.explanation: 'Last summer' places the action in the past, so the verb must be past tense too: 'who attended'.

questions.text: Select the sentence which has no spelling error.
options: There are more than 3500 types of moskuitoes in the world.
The common reaction to mosquiteo’s biting is itching.
Female mosqueteos have a longer life than their male mates.
Like all flies, mosquitoes also have four stages in their life.
questions.explanation: Only the last sentence spells 'mosquitoes' correctly; the others have 'moskuitoes', 'mosquiteo' and 'mosqueteos'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Simba and snowy are “cute” than the other puppies.
questions.explanation: Two are compared with the others ('than the other puppies'), so the comparative is needed; 'cute' is a short adjective, so it takes '-er': 'cuter'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. Upon hearing the great achievements of the historic character, he was in “a state of awed admiration and respect.”
questions.explanation: 'Wonderment' is a state of awed admiration or respect: 'he was in wonderment'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Snail’s pace
questions.explanation: To move at a 'snail's pace' is to move very slowly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Hopefully, things will return to normal in the __________.
questions.explanation: Things are hoped to return to normal in the time to come: 'in the future'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The teacher gave the question paper.
options: The question paper was given by the teacher.
The question paper was being given by the teacher.
The question paper was gave by the teacher.
The question paper has been given by the teacher.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'gave' becomes 'was given' in the passive: 'The question paper was given by the teacher.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The young king tried to speak, but his tongue seemed to ________ the roof of his mouth, and his lips refused to move.
questions.explanation: To 'cleave to' something is to stick fast to it: his tongue seemed stuck to the roof of his mouth.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. Ipshita “knows many languages” like French, Dutch and English, and she speaks them fluently.
questions.explanation: A polyglot is a person who knows and uses several languages.

questions.text: Identify the option that arranges the given parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. a) Jumped off the bus in front of the old woman’s home b) It was mid-morning and a very cold, bright day c) Holding a potted planted before her, a girl of fourteen d) On the outskirts of town
questions.explanation: b sets the scene (a cold, bright mid-morning); c introduces the girl, who is the subject of a ('jumped off the bus in front of the old woman's home'); d says where that home was: b, c, a, d.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'knowledge'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Any resemblance of a character in this book to a living person is ______ incidental.
questions.explanation: 'Purely' means only or entirely: any resemblance is there by chance alone. It is the usual word in such disclaimers.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. The movers and shakers
options: People who have a lot of power and influence
questions.explanation: 'Movers and shakers' are the people with power and influence in a field.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. (1) _________ areas are also known as the ’countryside’ or a ‘village’ in India. It has a very low population (2) _________. In rural areas, agriculture is the chief source of livelihood along with fishing, cottage (3) ___________, pottery etc. The (4) ___________ to discover the real rural India still continues in great earnest. Almost (5) ___________ economic agency today has a definition of rural India.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Rural areas', the subject of the whole passage, are those known as the countryside or villages.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. (1) _________ areas are also known as the ’countryside’ or a ‘village’ in India. It has a very low population (2) _________. In rural areas, agriculture is the chief source of livelihood along with fishing, cottage (3) ___________, pottery etc. The (4) ___________ to discover the real rural India still continues in great earnest. Almost (5) ___________ economic agency today has a definition of rural India.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Rural areas have a low 'population density': few people for their area.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. (1) _________ areas are also known as the ’countryside’ or a ‘village’ in India. It has a very low population (2) _________. In rural areas, agriculture is the chief source of livelihood along with fishing, cottage (3) ___________, pottery etc. The (4) ___________ to discover the real rural India still continues in great earnest. Almost (5) ___________ economic agency today has a definition of rural India.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3
questions.explanation: 'Cottage industries', small-scale production at home, are a livelihood alongside fishing and pottery.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. (1) _________ areas are also known as the ’countryside’ or a ‘village’ in India. It has a very low population (2) _________. In rural areas, agriculture is the chief source of livelihood along with fishing, cottage (3) ___________, pottery etc. The (4) ___________ to discover the real rural India still continues in great earnest. Almost (5) ___________ economic agency today has a definition of rural India.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The 'quest', or search, to discover the real rural India 'still continues'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. (1) _________ areas are also known as the ’countryside’ or a ‘village’ in India. It has a very low population (2) _________. In rural areas, agriculture is the chief source of livelihood along with fishing, cottage (3) ___________, pottery etc. The (4) ___________ to discover the real rural India still continues in great earnest. Almost (5) ___________ economic agency today has a definition of rural India.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Every' goes with a singular noun and verb: 'almost every economic agency today has a definition'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. ABROAD : BAILDA :: BEFORE : EBULER :: COUPLE : ?
questions.explanation: The first two letters swap, the middle two become their opposite letters (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on) and the last two swap: AB RO AD → BA IL DA and BE FO RE → EB UL ER. So CO UP LE → OC FK EL: OCFKEL.

questions.text: If 28 February 2015 was Saturday, then what was the day of the week on 28 February 2021?
questions.explanation: From 28 February 2015 to 28 February 2021 is 6 years with two leap days (29 February 2016 and 2020): 6 + 2 = 8 odd days, or 1 beyond whole weeks. Saturday + 1 = Sunday.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 9 : 32 :: 17 : 56 :: 15 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is 3 times the first plus 5: 9 × 3 + 5 = 32 and 17 × 3 + 5 = 56. Likewise 15 × 3 + 5 = 50.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 78*3*12*5*59*17*44
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 12, 17, 29, 55, 102, 177, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 5, 12, 26, 47, 75, which grow by 7, 14, 21, 28. The next difference is 75 + 35 = 110: 177 + 110 = 287.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 17, 34, 31, ?, 119, 714

Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row: 2, 3, 17; Second row: 4, 6, 100; Third row: 5, 2, ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the number into its constituent digits. For example, 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is the cube of the first plus the square of the second: 2³ + 3² = 17 and 4³ + 6² = 100. So 5³ + 2² = 125 + 4 = 129.

questions.text: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? OHVY, NFSU, MDPQ, ? , KZJI
questions.explanation: The first letters move back 1 (O, N, M, L, K), the second back 2 (H, F, D, B, Z), the third back 3 (V, S, P, M, J) and the fourth back 4 (Y, U, Q, M, I): LBMM.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 14 : 112 :: 24 : 312 :: 18 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the first times one more than its half: 14 × 8 = 112 and 24 × 13 = 312. Likewise 18 × 10 = 180.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 215, 226, 210, ?, 205, 236
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 215, 210, 205 fall by 5 and 226, ?, 236 rise by 5, so the missing term is 231.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 21, 126, 131, ? , 527, 1054
In a certain code language, 'MYRA' is written as '1426192' and 'VIAAN' is written as '23102215'. How will 'VIDHI' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as its place in the alphabet plus 1: MYRA → 14, 26, 19, 2 and VIAAN → 23, 10, 2, 2, 15. So VIDHI → 23, 10, 5, 9, 10: 23105910.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘SCALE’ is written as ‘UACJG’ and ‘LIGHT’ is written as ‘NGIFV’. How will ‘LIMIT’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +2, −2, +2, −2, +2: SCALE → UACJG and LIGHT → NGIFV. So LIMIT → NGOGV.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? VYU, TWS, RUQ, PSO, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places back every time: V, T, R, P, N; Y, W, U, S, Q; U, S, Q, O, M. The next cluster is NQM.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All jacks are aces. No ace is a king. Some queens are kings. Conclusions: I. Some queens are jacks. II. Some kings are jacks. III. No jack is a king.
options: Only conclusion I and III follow.
Only conclusion I and II follow.
questions.explanation: All jacks are aces and no ace is a king, so no jack is a king: III follows and II cannot. Nothing links queens to jacks, so I does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FRIEND’ is written as ‘GQJDOC’, and ‘READER’ is written as ‘SDBCFQ’. How will ‘NUMBER’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1 and −1 in turn: FRIEND → GQJDOC and READER → SDBCFQ. So NUMBER → OTNAFQ.

questions.text: If 29th September 2015 was a Tuesday, then what was the day of the week on 28th September 2019?
questions.explanation: From 29 September 2015 to 29 September 2019 is 4 years with one leap day (29 February 2016): 5 odd days, so 29 September 2019 was a Sunday (Tuesday + 5). The day before was a Saturday.

questions.text: If I denotes ‘÷’, J denotes ‘×’, K denotes ‘−’ and L denotes ‘+’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? 19 L (22 J 4) K (66 I 11) L (16 J 2) = ?
Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term 24 : 171 :: ? :115 :: 4 : 31
questions.explanation: Each first number times 7, plus 3, gives its pair: 24 × 7 + 3 = 171 and 4 × 7 + 3 = 31. So ? × 7 + 3 = 115 gives 16.

questions.text: If x² – 9x + 1 = 0, what is the value of x⁸ – 6239x⁴ + 1?
The weekly earnings of a shopkeeper in February 2021 are ₹21,980, ₹20,580, ₹22,380, ₹22,616, respectively. What is his average daily income in February 2021?
3 men and 7 women can complete a task in 10 days. On the other hand, 4 men and 6 women, take 8 days to complete the same task. How long will it take 10 women to complete the same task?
questions.explanation: 10(3m + 7w) = 8(4m + 6w) gives 30m + 70w = 32m + 48w, so 1 man = 11 women. The task is 10 × (33 + 7) = 400 woman-days, which 10 women finish in 40 days.

questions.text: What is the volume of a cylinder with radius 15 cm and height 119 cm? (Take π=22/7)
A table fan, passing through two hands, is sold finally at a profit of 30% of the original cost price. If the first dealer makes a profit of 25%, then the profit made by the second dealer is:
questions.explanation: 1.25 × (1 + r) = 1.30, so 1 + r = 1.04: the second dealer makes 4%.

questions.text: A few boys and a few girls appeared for a test. The average score of the boys was 52, the average score of the girls was 72, while the combined average was 60. What was the ratio of the number of boys to the number of girls who took the test?
questions.explanation: By alligation, boys : girls = (72 − 60) : (60 − 52) = 12 : 8 = 3 : 2.

questions.text: The number 123456 is divisible by:
questions.explanation: Its last two digits, 56, are divisible by 4, so 123456 is too. 123456 = 7 × 17,636 + 4, so it is not divisible by 7, 14 or 56.

questions.text: Anjali and Babita are running on a circular track in opposite directions from same time at same point with speeds of 8 m/sec and 6 m/sec, respectively. If the length of the circular track is 960 m, how many times distinct points they will meet?
questions.explanation: Their speeds are in the ratio 8 : 6 = 4 : 3. Running in opposite directions, they meet at 4 + 3 = 7 distinct points on the track.

questions.text: Khushi went to purchase a mixer. The marked price of the mixer was ₹6,000 and 20% flat discount was offered on it by the shopkeeper. How much does Khushi have to pay for the mixer?
The ratio in which a transverse common tangent drawn to two circles with radii 4 cm and 6 cm, respectively, divides the line joining their centres is:
questions.explanation: A transverse (internal) common tangent divides the line joining the centres internally in the ratio of the radii: 4 : 6 = 2 : 3.

questions.text: The annual salary of Suhas has increased from ₹18,00,000 to ₹22,00,000. What is the percentage increase? (Correct to two decimal places)
A man borrows a sum of ₹1,025 and pays back in two equal yearly instalments. If the rate of interest is 5% p.a, compounded yearly, then how much is each instalments?
Find the mean proportional between 0.04 and 0.0036.
Evaluate 107 × 93.
The length of the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle is 37 cm and the length of one of its other two sides is 12 cm. What is the area of the triangle?

A washing machine marked at ₹28,000 is sold at two successive discounts of 15% and 10%. An additional discount of 5% is offered for cash payment. The selling price of the washing machine at cash payment is:
Which of the following is NOT correct regarding the election of Vice-President?
options: He/she is qualified for election as a member of the House of People.
He/she is qualified for election as a member of the Council of States.
He/she has completed the age of 35 years of age.
He/she must be a citizen of India.
questions.explanation: Under Article 66(3) a Vice-President must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old and qualified for election to the Council of States (Rajya Sabha), not the House of the People.

questions.text: Which of the following autobiographies is written by the great Indian santoor player Shiv Kumar Sharma in 2002?
options: Journey with a Hundred Strings: My Life in Music
Abba - God’s greatest Gift to Us
questions.explanation: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma's autobiography, 'Journey with a Hundred Strings: My Life in Music', came out in 2002. 'That Long Silence' is a novel by Shashi Deshpande.

questions.text: Which of the following does NOT create any corresponding liability for the government? Revenue receipts; Capital receipts
questions.explanation: Taking the two items in the order printed as (a) and (b): revenue receipts (a), such as taxes, fees and interest, create no liability for the government, while capital receipts (b) either create one, as borrowings do, or reduce its assets.

questions.text: India finished its best-ever performance at World Athletics U20 Championship at Nairobi in August 2021 with:
questions.explanation: At Nairobi India won silver in the 10,000 m race walk (Amit Khatri) and the long jump (Shaili Singh), and bronze in the mixed 4 × 400 m relay.

questions.text: Tanvi Shah, Indian musician to bring home a Grammy has been conferred the award for which of the following contributions?
options: Best song written for Visual Media
questions.explanation: Tanvi Shah wrote the Spanish lyrics of 'Jai Ho' from 'Slumdog Millionaire', which won the 2010 Grammy for Best Song Written for Motion Picture, Television or Other Visual Media.

questions.text: Rashtriya Kalidas Samman was conferred to which of the following personalities in 2019-20?
questions.explanation: The Kathak dancer Sunaina (Sunayana) Hazarilal received Madhya Pradesh's Rashtriya Kalidas Samman for classical dance for 2019-20; Shanta and V.P. Dhananjayan received it for 2020-21.

questions.text: Which of the following novels is NOT written by the famous Hindi writer Premchand?
questions.explanation: 'Kashi Ka Assi' is by Kashinath Singh. 'Idgah' is a Premchand story, 'Mansarovar' his collected stories and 'Godaan' his last completed novel.

questions.text: Which Act was enacted in India with the aim of curbing illegal trade in wildlife and derivative parts?
questions.explanation: The Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 protects listed species and controls trade in wild animals and plants and in their parts and products.

questions.text: The Winter Olympics games 2022 was organised by which of the following city from 4 February to 25 February 2022?
questions.explanation: Beijing hosted the 2022 Winter Olympics (they ran from 4 to 20 February 2022), becoming the first city to host both the Summer and the Winter Games.

questions.text: Guru Debaprasad Das Awardee Durga Charan Ranbir is a teacher and performer of which of the following classical dance forms?
questions.explanation: Durga Charan Ranbir is an Odissi dancer and guru, known for the style of his teacher Guru Debaprasad Das.

questions.text: Who among the following Hindustani classical instrumentalists won the Grammy Award in 1993 for his album ‘A Meeting by The River’ with Ry Cooder?
questions.explanation: Vishwa Mohan Bhatt, who plays the Mohan veena he designed, won the Grammy for Best World Music Album with Ry Cooder for 'A Meeting by the River'.

questions.text: Manjusree Chatterjee was awarded with the honour of Padma Shri in 2019 for which of the following styles of dance?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Kathak: Manjusree (Manjushree) Chatterjee is a Kathak dancer and teacher of the Lucknow gharana. (We could not confirm the 2019 Padma Shri the question mentions.)

questions.text: Hafiz Ali Khan was an Indian __________ player of the Bangash gharana.
questions.explanation: Ustad Hafiz Ali Khan, father of Amjad Ali Khan, was a sarod player of the Bangash gharana.

questions.text: Which of the following is an autobiography of the Indian boxer, Mary Kom?
questions.explanation: Mary Kom's autobiography is 'Unbreakable' (2013). 'Undisputed Truth' is Mike Tyson's, 'Playing It My Way' Sachin Tendulkar's and 'The Test of My Life' Yuvraj Singh's.

questions.text: What is a good way to measure the population density of fishes found in lakes?
options: The number of fish caught per trap
questions.explanation: NCERT gives the number of fish caught per trap as a good enough measure of their population density in a lake.

questions.text: Who among the following personalities was awarded the Padma Shri in 2021 for contributions to Folk dance ?
questions.explanation: Manjamma Jogathi, a performer of Karnataka's Jogati folk dance, received the Padma Shri in 2021.

questions.text: According to Köppen's climate classification scheme, dry climates are subdivided using the capital letter S for semi-arid regions or steppe and W for ________ region.
questions.explanation: In Köppen's scheme the dry (B) climates are divided into BS, steppe, and BW, desert (from the German 'Wüste').

questions.text: As of March 2021, which state of India formulated a new education scheme that will facilitate the upgradation and modernisation of the education sector in the state comprehensively, at a total cost of ₹4,000 crore?
questions.explanation: Telangana's 2021-22 budget, presented in March 2021, announced a new scheme to upgrade and modernise the infrastructure of government schools at a cost of ₹4,000 crore.

questions.text: Which river in India flows through a rift valley?
questions.explanation: The Narmada flows west through a rift valley between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges.

questions.text: In 1972, ________ coined the term ‘pyramid of numbers’ that represented the total numbers of individuals (population) present in each trophic level.
questions.explanation: Charles Elton described the pyramid of numbers (the Eltonian pyramid) in 'Animal Ecology', published in 1927; the question's 1972 appears to swap the digits.

questions.text: With reference to the major regions of the northern plains, Bhabar is:
options: the older alluvium along the river beds forming terraces higher than the flood plain
a narrow belt of about 8 to 16 km that runs in the west-east direction along the foot of the Himalayas from the river Indus to Teesta
composed of newer alluvium and forms flood plains along the river banks
a broad long zone of northern India and southern Nepal running parallel to the lower ranges of the Himalayas
questions.explanation: Bhabar is the narrow belt of pebbles the rivers deposit along the foot of the Shiwaliks. The other options describe the bhangar, the khadar and the terai.

questions.text: Which of the following launched People's Plan Campaign 2021- Sabki Yojana Sabka Vikas in September 2021 ?
questions.explanation: The People's Plan Campaign, 'Sabki Yojana Sabka Vikas', is the Ministry of Panchayati Raj's drive in which gram panchayats draw up their development plans.

questions.text: Who among the following was the founder of the Banaras Gharana of style of khayal singing?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Pandit Gopal Mishra (1921-1977), the Varanasi sarangi master whose family, including his nephews Rajan and Sajan Mishra, carried the Banaras khayal style; common lists of gharanas name him as its founder.

questions.text: Areas like the southern part of Gujarat, eastern Tamil Nadu, northeast peninsula covering Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, and East Madhya Pradesh receive rainfall between _________.
questions.explanation: NCERT puts southern Gujarat, eastern Tamil Nadu and the north-eastern Peninsula (Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, eastern Madhya Pradesh) in the zone of moderate rainfall, 100-200 cm.

questions.text: In which of the following years was India the host of Asian Games?
questions.explanation: India hosted the Asian Games in 1951, the first Games, and in 1982, both times in New Delhi.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The clock that we have in our town square is “a big” in the whole town
questions.explanation: 'In the whole town' calls for the superlative with 'the': 'is the biggest in the whole town'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Comic
questions.explanation: 'Comic' means funny; its opposite is 'tragic'.

questions.text: Complete the sentence with an appropriate ANTONYM of the word mentioned in the bracket. My fascination with Tyler's items ____________(approached) into distant memories.
questions.explanation: To 'approach' is to come nearer; its opposite, to 'recede', is to move back or grow fainter: the fascination 'receded into distant memories'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. These carriers of bacteria and viruses cause many diseases like Yellow Fever, Malaria etc. so panchayats and municipalities are taking a lot of care to protect people from them. B. There are thousands of species of mosquitoes that are known to the people of the world. They mainly live in still water and other places where water is stored. C. Mosquitos are everywhere now. Villagers, as well as city dwellers are afraid of these small creatures. D. Usually, female and male mosquitoes take feed on plant’s or fruit honey, however female mosquitoes mostly suck the blood of humans.
questions.explanation: C introduces mosquitoes, B says how many species there are and where they live, A names the diseases these carriers spread, and D ends with what they feed on: CBAD.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Easily provoked
questions.explanation: An 'irascible' person is easily angered. 'Invincible' means unbeatable and 'iridescent' showing shifting rainbow colours.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Mr. Pramod couldn’t “wait to trying out” his new recipe.
questions.explanation: 'Couldn't' takes the base form 'wait', and 'wait' takes the to-infinitive 'to try', not 'to trying': 'couldn't wait to try out his new recipe'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Funny stories made me and my brother_________.
questions.explanation: Funny stories set them giggling: they made them 'giggly'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. I know her.
questions.explanation: In the passive 'know' takes 'to', not 'by': 'She is known to me.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Uniform
questions.explanation: 'Uniform' means the same throughout; its opposite is 'variable'.

questions.text: The given sentence contains an error in tense form. Identify the error and choose the option that correctly rectifies the error. Bakshi will going to call you later in the evening.
options: Bakshi was gone to call you later in the evening.
Bakshi will go to call you later in the evening.
Bakshi is going to call you later in the evening.
Bakshi goes to call you later in the evening.
questions.explanation: 'Will' cannot be followed by 'going'; a planned future action takes 'is going to': 'Bakshi is going to call you later in the evening.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Upset the “apple-cart”
questions.explanation: To 'upset the apple-cart' is to spoil someone's careful plans.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. They attend / a meeting / in Chicago / this weekend.
questions.explanation: A personal arrangement for 'this weekend' takes the present continuous (or 'will'), not the simple present 'They attend': 'They are attending (or will attend) a meeting in Chicago this weekend.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence. His “perverse” thoughts were very disturbing so he decided to try seeing a therapist.
questions.explanation: 'Perverse' here means abnormal and unacceptable: 'deviant'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'champion'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. The rich man was known all throughout the country for his noble deeds, kindness and as “one who makes an active effort to promote human welfare.”
questions.explanation: A philanthropist works to promote the welfare of others, especially by giving money. A spendthrift or squanderer wastes money, and a pacifist opposes war.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Pocket an insult
questions.explanation: To 'pocket an insult' is to put up with it without protest.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Settlers ______ a new colony in the early 18th century.
questions.explanation: Settlers found, or 'established', a colony; 'entrenched' means firmly fixed, and 'fixed' and 'extended' do not fit a new colony.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There was once a young man who wished to (1)_________ his heart’s desire. And while that is, as beginnings go, there was much about this young man and what happened to him that was unusual, (2)_________ even he never knew the whole of it. The tale started. The town of Wall stands today as it has (3)_________ for six hundred years, on a high (4)_________ of granite slab amidst small forest woodland. There is a road from Wall, a winding track rising sharply up from the forest, where it is (5)_________with rocks and small stones.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: To 'achieve' one's heart's desire is to attain it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There was once a young man who wished to (1)_________ his heart’s desire. And while that is, as beginnings go, there was much about this young man and what happened to him that was unusual, (2)_________ even he never knew the whole of it. The tale started. The town of Wall stands today as it has (3)_________ for six hundred years, on a high (4)_________ of granite slab amidst small forest woodland. There is a road from Wall, a winding track rising sharply up from the forest, where it is (5)_________with rocks and small stones.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Although' joins two contrasting clauses: 'unusual, although even he never knew the whole of it'. 'Despite' and 'in spite' need a noun, and 'even though even' repeats 'even'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There was once a young man who wished to (1)_________ his heart’s desire. And while that is, as beginnings go, there was much about this young man and what happened to him that was unusual, (2)_________ even he never knew the whole of it. The tale started. The town of Wall stands today as it has (3)_________ for six hundred years, on a high (4)_________ of granite slab amidst small forest woodland. There is a road from Wall, a winding track rising sharply up from the forest, where it is (5)_________with rocks and small stones.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The town 'stands today as it has stood for six hundred years': the present perfect of 'stand'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There was once a young man who wished to (1)_________ his heart’s desire. And while that is, as beginnings go, there was much about this young man and what happened to him that was unusual, (2)_________ even he never knew the whole of it. The tale started. The town of Wall stands today as it has (3)_________ for six hundred years, on a high (4)_________ of granite slab amidst small forest woodland. There is a road from Wall, a winding track rising sharply up from the forest, where it is (5)_________with rocks and small stones.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: A 'jut' is a part that sticks out: the town is on a high jut of granite.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There was once a young man who wished to (1)_________ his heart’s desire. And while that is, as beginnings go, there was much about this young man and what happened to him that was unusual, (2)_________ even he never knew the whole of it. The tale started. The town of Wall stands today as it has (3)_________ for six hundred years, on a high (4)_________ of granite slab amidst small forest woodland. There is a road from Wall, a winding track rising sharply up from the forest, where it is (5)_________with rocks and small stones.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: A track 'lined with rocks' has them along its sides.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. MASTER : AMHGRE :: LUXURY : ULCFYR :: FORMAL : ?
questions.explanation: Take the letters in pairs: the first and last pairs swap (MA → AM, ER → RE) and each letter of the middle pair becomes its opposite in the alphabet (S → H, T → G). So FO → OF, RM → IN and AL → LA: OFINLA.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 31*13*7*54*12*4*20
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 96 * 3 * 5 * 56 * 16 * 120
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 45*9*3*7*5*21
Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1. Elegant 2. Electrician 3. Elephant 4. Elated 5. Elongated
questions.explanation: Elated (4), Electrician (2), Elegant (1), Elephant (3), Elongated (5): 'Ela' comes before 'Ele', the 'Ele' words follow their fourth letters c, g, p, and 'Elo' comes last.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row: 124, 38, 100; Second row: 78, 25, 64; Third row: 94, 31, ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the number into its constituent digits. For example, 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is half the first plus the second: 124 ÷ 2 + 38 = 100 and 78 ÷ 2 + 25 = 64. So 94 ÷ 2 + 31 = 78.

questions.text: In a certain code language, “TAUGHT” is written as “VYWEJR”, and “SIMPLE” is written as “UGONNC”. How will “RETURN” be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move 2 forward and 2 back in turn: TAUGHT → VYWEJR and SIMPLE → UGONNC. So RETURN → TCVSTL.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'HONEST' is written as 'NTRHUU', and 'LABOUR' is written as 'RFFRWS'. How will 'ENOUGH' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move forward 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1 places: HONEST → NTRHUU and LABOUR → RFFRWS. So ENOUGH → KSSXII.

questions.text: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? ETRE, HSPJ, KRNO, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +3 (E, H, K, N), second letters −1 (T, S, R, Q), third letters −2 (R, P, N, L) and fourth letters +5 (E, J, O, T): NQLT.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 14, 26, 11, ?, 8, 32
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 14, 11, 8 falls by 3 and 26, 29, 32 rises by 3.

questions.text: If ‘A’ denotes ‘+’, ‘B’ denotes ‘×’, ‘C’ denotes ‘–’ and ‘D’ denotes ‘÷’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? 18 A 23 C 6 B (96 D 16) A 3 B 12 = ?
questions.explanation: After substituting the signs: 18 + 23 − 6 × (96 ÷ 16) + 3 × 12 = 18 + 23 − 36 + 36 = 41.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 154, 165, 148, ?, 142, 177
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 154, 148, 142 falls by 6 and 165, 171, 177 rises by 6.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (31, 26, 155); (18, 12, 108) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed.)
questions.explanation: The third number is the first times the difference of the first two: (31 − 26) × 31 = 155 and (18 − 12) × 18 = 108. Likewise (17 − 9) × 17 = 136; the other sets would need 112, 76 and 144.

questions.text: If 1 January 2020 was Wednesday, then what was the day of the week on 28 February 2021?
questions.explanation: 2020 was a leap year, so 1 January 2021 came 366 days later, two weekdays on: Friday. 28 February 2021 is 58 days after that, 8 weeks and 2 days: Sunday.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? DWE, GTH, JQK, MNN, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +3 (D, G, J, M, P), second letters −3 (W, T, Q, N, K) and third letters +3 (E, H, K, N, Q): PKQ.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 84 * 6 * 25 * 13 * 3
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 78, 97, 54, ?, 30, 145
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 78, 54, 30 falls by 24 and 97, 121, 145 rises by 24.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘ACNE’ is written as ‘XZVM’ and ‘BODY’ is written as ‘LYBW’. How will ‘EVIL’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter becomes its opposite in the alphabet and the letters of each pair then swap: ACNE → ZXMV → XZVM and BODY → YLWB → LYBW. So EVIL → VERO → EVOR.

questions.text: If two supplementary angles differ by 74°, then one of the angles is:
questions.explanation: x + y = 180° and x − y = 74°, so the angles are 127° and 53°.

questions.text: By selling an article for ₹255, there is a loss of 15%. When the article is sold for ₹357, the net result in the transaction is:
questions.explanation: Cost price = 255 ÷ 0.85 = ₹300. At ₹357 the profit is ₹57, and 57/300 = 19%.

questions.text: The difference between a single discount of 20% and two successive discounts of 16% and 4% on a bill of ₹50,000 is:
questions.explanation: The two discounts leave 0.84 × 0.96 = 0.8064 of the bill, a total discount of 19.36%. The difference, 0.64% of ₹50,000, is ₹320.

questions.text: Kuldeep offers his customers a discount of 10% on the marked price of a suitcase and he still makes a profit of 20%. What is the actual cost of the suitcase marked for ₹2,500?
questions.explanation: Selling price = 0.9 × 2,500 = ₹2,250, which is 120% of the cost: 2,250 ÷ 1.2 = ₹1,875.

questions.text: X does a work in 6 days, while Y does it in 12 days. If they work alternatively and X begins, in how many days will the work be finished?
questions.explanation: In each two-day pair X and Y do 1/6 + 1/12 = 1/4 of the work, so four pairs, 8 days, finish it.

questions.text: What should be subtracted from 246837 to make it divisible by 13 ?
questions.explanation: 13 × 18987 = 246831, so 246837 leaves remainder 6 on division by 13; subtracting 6 makes it divisible.

questions.text: The fourth proportional to 14,21,28 is:
After spending 20% of his salary on grocery and 30% of the remainder on monthly house rent, a man is left with ₹8,400. What is his monthly salary?
questions.explanation: After 20% on grocery and 30% of the rest on rent, 0.8 × 0.7 = 0.56 of the salary is left: 8,400 ÷ 0.56 = ₹15,000.

questions.text: A car travelled distances of 10 km, 20 km and 30 km at speeds of 30 km/h, 40 km/h and 60 km/h, respectively. The average speed of the car is:

The distance between stations A and B is 778 kilometres. A train travels from station A to station B at a uniform speed of 84 km/h and then returns to station A at a uniform speed of 56 km/h. What is the train's average speed (in km/h) throughout the journey?
questions.explanation: Over equal distances the average speed is 2 × 84 × 56/(84 + 56) = 9,408/140 = 67.2 km/h; the distance itself does not matter.

questions.text: Two numbers are less than a third number by 30% and 37% respectively. By how much is the second number lesser than the first?
questions.explanation: If the third number is 100, the other two are 70 and 63. The second is 7 less than the first: 7/70 = 10%.

questions.text: Ramesh bought a house for ₹2,00,000. At the end of the first year, he sold it at a loss of 10% on his investment. He invested the money thus obtained at a rate of 20% p.a. interest compounded aunually for 2 years. The value of this investment would amount to ___________.
tan (π + θ) = ?
questions.explanation: π + θ lies in the third quadrant, where the tangent is positive, and tan has period π: tan (π + θ) = tanθ.

questions.text: Number B is 17.5% less than number A, while number C is 22.5% more than number B. If the value of C is given as 8085, what is the value of A?
If 9 × 4 of 3 ÷ 2 - 5 × Q + 2 × 3 = 10, then find the value of Q.

The average of the four numbers, given in a particular order, is 48. The average of the first three numbers is 42, while the average of the last three numbers is 50. What is the average of the first and last numbers?
questions.explanation: The four numbers add to 192. The first three add to 126, so the fourth is 66; the last three add to 150, so the first is 42. (42 + 66)/2 = 54.

questions.text: In a school, the final grades of a subject for an academic year are calculated, based on the grades that a student gets in his assignments, tests and a final exam. Assignments have the weightage of 28%, tests of 22%, and the final exam of 50%. If a student has an assignment grade of 80, a test grade of 75, an exam grade of 86, then his overall grade for the year is _________.
The total surface area of a hemisphere is 64.57 cm². Find its curved surface area.
questions.explanation: The total surface area is 3πr² and the curved surface 2πr², two-thirds of it: 2/3 × 64.57 = 43.046… cm², the 43.04 cm² of the options.

questions.text: The expression x⁴ – 8x² + m will be a perfect square when the value of m is:
questions.explanation: x⁴ − 8x² + 16 = (x² − 4)², so m = 16.

questions.text: A wall 10 m long, 5 m high and 20 cm thick is to be constructed using bricks of dimensions 25 cm × 20 cm × 10 cm. How many bricks are required?
questions.explanation: The wall is 1,000 cm × 500 cm × 20 cm and a brick 25 cm × 20 cm × 10 cm = 5,000 cm³: (1,000 × 500 × 20) ÷ 5,000 = 2,000 bricks.

questions.text: In which year will India host the 15th Men’s Hockey World Cup?
questions.explanation: India hosted the 15th Men's Hockey World Cup in January 2023, at Bhubaneswar and Rourkela in Odisha.

questions.text: Income of the state which arises out of the property left by the people without a legal heir is called ______________.
questions.explanation: Escheat is property that passes to the State when its owner dies without a legal heir; Article 296 of the Constitution vests such property in the State or the Union.

questions.text: In the case of Aparna Bhat vs State of Madhya Pradesh in 2021, the Supreme Court set aside the judgment of Madhya Pradesh High Court which prescribed ______________ as condition for bail.
questions.explanation: In March 2021 the Supreme Court set aside the Madhya Pradesh High Court's bail condition that a man accused of sexual assault visit the complainant with a rakhi and ask her to tie it on him.

questions.text: Who among the following is a 19th century exponent of the Kathak dance?
questions.explanation: Kalka Prasad and his brother Bindadin Maharaj were the great 19th-century masters of the Lucknow gharana of Kathak; Birju Maharaj was Kalka Prasad's grandson.

questions.text: Who among the following was one of the founders of Kerala Kalalayam in 1952?
questions.explanation: Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma, the Mohiniyattam dancer, set up Kerala Kalalayam at Tripunithura in 1952 with her husband, the Kathakali artist Kalamandalam Krishnan Nair.

questions.text: Who proposed the ‘plum pudding’ theory of the divisible atom in which negatively charged electrons were scattered in a lump of positive charge like a raisin in plum pudding?
questions.explanation: J. J. Thomson, who discovered the electron, proposed the plum pudding model of the atom in 1904.

questions.text: In India, from where do the tropical cyclones, which enter the Indian subcontinent from the west and the northwest during the winter months, originate?
questions.explanation: The western disturbances, the cyclonic depressions that enter north-west India in winter, originate over the Mediterranean Sea and are brought into India by the westerly jet stream.

questions.text: In April 2021, which Indian cricketer was named as ‘Wisden Almanack’s ODI Cricketer of 2010s in the 2021 edition of the Wisden Cricketers’ Almanack?
questions.explanation: In its 2021 edition Wisden named Virat Kohli its ODI Cricketer of the Decade for the 2010s.

questions.text: Who was the winner of the 7th ICC T20 World Cup cricket?
questions.explanation: The seventh T20 World Cup, held in the UAE and Oman in 2021, was won by Australia, who beat New Zealand in the final.

questions.text: Who published the book 'Method de nomenclature (System of Chemical Nomenclature)' along with Claude Berthollet and others that determined the modern method of naming substances?
questions.explanation: Lavoisier wrote 'Méthode de nomenclature chimique' (1787) with Guyton de Morveau, Berthollet and Fourcroy; it laid the basis of modern chemical names.

questions.text: Which of the following State Governments started the Lata Mangeshkar Award in 1984?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh instituted the National Lata Mangeshkar Award for light music in 1984.

questions.text: R Muthukannammal is a __________ dancer who got the Padma Shri in 2022.
questions.explanation: R. Muthukannammal of Viralimalai, Tamil Nadu, one of the last exponents of Sadhir, the temple dance from which Bharatanatyam developed, received the Padma Shri in 2022.

questions.text: A pyramid of biomass is a diagram that shows the population at each level of the food chain. Accordingly, ________ occupy the base with the highest biomass.
questions.explanation: In an upright pyramid of biomass the producers, the green plants, form the base, with the greatest biomass of any level.

questions.text: Which of the following names belong to Bharatanatyam ?
questions.explanation: Narthaki Nataraj, a Bharatanatyam dancer, was the first transgender person to receive the Padma Shri, in 2019. Birju Maharaj danced Kathak, Kelucharan Mohapatra Odissi and Guru Bipin Singh Manipuri.

questions.text: Which chemical compound, with the chemical formula CH₃CH₂Cl, is used as a blowing agent in foamed plastics?
questions.explanation: CH₃CH₂Cl, an ethane with one hydrogen replaced by chlorine, is chloroethane (ethyl chloride). Chloromethane is CH₃Cl and 1-chloropropane CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl.

questions.text: Who among the following Indian music directors introduced Western tunes in the Hindi film industry, who was popularly known as ‘Pancham Da’?
questions.explanation: Rahul Dev Burman, son of S. D. Burman, was known as 'Pancham Da'; he brought Western tunes and rhythms into Hindi film music.

questions.text: Who was famous for the invention of the vacuum pump in the 17th century and also pioneered the concept of the absolute vacuum of space, measured the weight of air and used air pressure to predict the weather?
questions.explanation: Otto von Guericke built the first air pump around 1650, showed the force of air pressure with the Magdeburg hemispheres and used a barometer to forecast the weather.

questions.text: What is the common name of the members of family Phaeophyceae?
questions.explanation: Phaeophyceae are the brown algae, such as kelps, coloured by the pigment fucoxanthin.

questions.text: ‘Jakhan Choto Chilam’ is an autobiography written in the Bengali language by which of the following Indian Bangla film directors?
questions.explanation: 'Jakhan Choto Chilam' is Satyajit Ray's memoir of his childhood, published in English as 'Childhood Days'.

questions.text: Who among the following personalities was awarded the Padma Shri for his contribution to Bundeli Folk Dance in 2022?
questions.explanation: Ram Sahay Pandey of Sagar, Madhya Pradesh, received the Padma Shri in 2022 for his life's work on Rai, the folk dance of Bundelkhand.

questions.text: Pandit Ravi Shankar was one of the best known players of the ________.
questions.explanation: Pandit Ravi Shankar was the best-known sitar player of the twentieth century.

questions.text: The Fifteenth Finance Commission was constituted in:
questions.explanation: The Fifteenth Finance Commission, chaired by N. K. Singh, was constituted under Article 280 in November 2017.

questions.text: In which of the following categories did the weightlifter Mirabai Chanu bag a silver medal at the Tokyo Olympics 2020?
questions.explanation: Mirabai Chanu won silver in the women's 49 kg weightlifting at Tokyo 2020, India's first medal of those Games.

questions.text: Which of the following novels by Krishna Sobti was originally published as ‘Dilo-Danish’?
options: A Gujarat Here, A Gujarat There
questions.explanation: Krishna Sobti's 'Dil-o-Danish' appeared in English in 2005 as 'The Heart Has Its Reasons', translated by Reema Anand and Meenakshi Swami.

questions.text: Which of the following awards was conferred on Krishna Sobti in the year 1980 for her Hindi novel ‘Zindaginama’?
questions.explanation: Krishna Sobti won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1980 for 'Zindaginama'; she later received the Jnanpith Award (2017).

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Deception
questions.explanation: 'Deception' is the tricking of others; 'cunning', skill at deceit, is the nearest in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Frivolous
questions.explanation: 'Frivolous' means not serious, light-minded; its opposite is 'serious'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. “Don’t provoke Harsha”, otherwise, she will give you a slap.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'Do not exasperate Harsha': only 'exasperate' (to irritate greatly) keeps the sense of 'provoke', while to vacillate, hesitate or equivocate is to waver or be evasive, which does not fit. The sentence as printed is already correct, and there is no 'no improvement' option.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We're asking them to ______ the deadline.
questions.explanation: A deadline is 'extended', moved later; 'increase', 'enlarge' and 'broaden' are used of size or amount.

questions.text: Select the sentence which has no spelling error.
options: When Reema saw her mother, she was in ecstasy.
Students got in acstasy during inter college baseball match.
Sandeep was in ektasy when his son won a scholarship.
My cousin closed his eyes in extasy at the thought of coffee.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'ecstasy'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who makes an active effort to promote human welfare
questions.explanation: A philanthropist works to promote the welfare of others; a philanderer is a man who has casual love affairs.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. I am training a new batch of officers now.
options: A new batch of officers are trained now.
A new batch of officers were being trained by me now.
A new batch of officers are training me now.
A new batch of officers is being trained by me.
questions.explanation: The present continuous 'am training' becomes 'is being trained', the singular 'batch' taking 'is': 'A new batch of officers is being trained by me.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. “We are waiting” for the minister for the last two hours.
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and is still going on, with 'for' and a period, takes the present perfect continuous: 'We have been waiting for the minister for the last two hours.'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Teachers love their students.
options: Students are being loved by their teachers.
Students are loved by their teachers.
Students have been loved by their teachers
Students will be loved by their teachers.
questions.explanation: The simple present 'love' becomes 'are loved': 'Students are loved by their teachers.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Benign
questions.explanation: 'Benign' means kindly and well-meaning: 'benevolent'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. I find playing chess “to be difficult” than playing poker.
questions.explanation: 'Than' needs the comparative: 'I find playing chess to be more difficult than playing poker.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. In your birthday suit
options: A suit which covers one’s entire body
A suit which is designed for only birthday functions
questions.explanation: 'In your birthday suit' means naked, as on the day you were born.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who loves and collects books
questions.explanation: A bibliophile loves and collects books; a bookworm simply reads a great deal.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. I need to evaluate all the options available by the end of this month.
options: All the options available will be needed to evaluate by the end of this month.
I needed to evaluate all the options by the end of this month.
All the options will be needing evaluation with the end of this month.
All the options available need to be evaluated by me by the end of this month.
questions.explanation: With 'need to' and a verb, the passive is 'need to be evaluated': 'All the options available need to be evaluated by me by the end of this month.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Fanatic
questions.explanation: A 'fanatic' holds extreme, intolerant views; the opposite is 'tolerant'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'occasion'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Cast aside
questions.explanation: To 'cast aside' something is to reject or discard it.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. People post images of their cuisine, daily cosmetic routines, shopping videos, and dance videos. B. Uploading photos to social networking sites has grown popular in today's society. C. Because of the rising influence of social media on people, they want to constantly appear their best. D. Therefore people have become more image sensors and begun to prioritise personal care.
questions.explanation: B introduces the popularity of uploading photos, A says what people post, C gives the reason (wanting to look their best) and D the result ('Therefore'): BACD.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Conservation of water is not the (1)______ of only the government. Common citizens can also make a significant (2)______ in this field. To begin with, we must be conscious that water is life, that it is a precious natural resource and needs to be used (3)_____. Being conscious will help us to avoid (4)______. There are a few simple things that all of us can do. We must not use (5)______ water to clean our car or house.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Conservation is not the 'responsibility' of the government alone: citizens can help too.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Conservation of water is not the (1)______ of only the government. Common citizens can also make a significant (2)______ in this field. To begin with, we must be conscious that water is life, that it is a precious natural resource and needs to be used (3)_____. Being conscious will help us to avoid (4)______. There are a few simple things that all of us can do. We must not use (5)______ water to clean our car or house.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Citizens can make a significant 'contribution' in this field.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Conservation of water is not the (1)______ of only the government. Common citizens can also make a significant (2)______ in this field. To begin with, we must be conscious that water is life, that it is a precious natural resource and needs to be used (3)_____. Being conscious will help us to avoid (4)______. There are a few simple things that all of us can do. We must not use (5)______ water to clean our car or house.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: A precious resource must be used 'judiciously': with care and good sense, without waste.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Conservation of water is not the (1)______ of only the government. Common citizens can also make a significant (2)______ in this field.
