There are a few simple things that all of us can do. We must not use (5)______ water to clean our car or house.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Being conscious of water's value helps us avoid 'wastage'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Conservation of water is not the (1)______ of only the government. Common citizens can also make a significant (2)______ in this field. To begin with, we must be conscious that water is life, that it is a precious natural resource and needs to be used (3)_____. Being conscious will help us to avoid (4)______. There are a few simple things that all of us can do. We must not use (5)______ water to clean our car or house.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: We must not use 'drinking' water to clean a car or house.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation. 57*35*7*14*2*71

The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number-pairs EXCEPT one. Find that odd number-pair.
questions.explanation: In the others the second number is the square root of the first minus 3: √169 − 3 = 10, √196 − 3 = 11 and √64 − 3 = 5. For 36 this gives 6 − 3 = 3, not 2.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. REMOVAL : MEROLAV :: TYPICAL : PYTILAC :: NUCLEAR : ?
questions.explanation: The first three letters are reversed, the fourth stays and the last three are reversed: REM O VAL → MER O LAV and TYP I CAL → PYT I LAC. So NUC L EAR → CUN L RAE: CUNLRAE.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when placed from left to right in the given blanks, will complete the letter series. J _ M K L J J _ K L J J _ K L _ J P _ L
questions.explanation: With J, N, O, J, K in the blanks the series is JJMKL JJNKL JJOKL JJPKL: the third letter of each block runs M, N, O, P.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (25,19,14); (50, 28, 30) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: In each set the first number minus the second, plus 8, gives the third: 25 − 19 + 8 = 14 and 50 − 28 + 8 = 30. Likewise 35 − 22 + 8 = 21.

questions.text: If 1st August 2009 was a Saturday, then what was the day of the week on 1st August 2013?
questions.explanation: From 1 August 2009 to 1 August 2013 is four years, one of which contains 29 February 2012: 4 + 1 = 5 odd days. Five days after Saturday is Thursday.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 7, 19, 4, ?, 1, 25
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 7, 4, 1 falls by 3 and 19, 22, 25 rises by 3.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'GREEN' is written as 'HTHIS' and ‘SAFFRON’ is written as ‘TCIJWUU’. How will 'WHITE' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move forward 1, 2, 3, 4, ... places in turn: G + 1 = H, R + 2 = T, E + 3 = H, E + 4 = I, N + 5 = S. So W + 1 = X, H + 2 = J, I + 3 = L, T + 4 = X, E + 5 = J: XJLXJ.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'I know you' is written as 'Ha Hi He', 'I Like French' is written as 'Ho Hu Ha' and 'You like me' is written as 'He Ho Haa'. How will 'me' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: 'I' is in the first two sentences and 'Ha' in both their codes; 'you' is in the first and third, with 'He'; 'like' is in the last two, with 'Ho'. The code left for 'me' is 'Haa'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 13 : 195 :: 7 : 63 :: 18 : ?
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by itself plus 2: 13 × 15 = 195 and 7 × 9 = 63. So 18 × 20 = 360.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: In the others the second number is the cube of half of one more than the first: 9 → 5³ = 125, 13 → 7³ = 343 and 7 → 4³ = 64. For 11 this gives 6³ = 216, not 49.

questions.text: If 15 August 2001 was Wednesday, then what was the day of the week on 2 October 2001?
questions.explanation: From 15 August to 2 October is 16 + 30 + 2 = 48 days: 6 weeks and 6 days. Six days after Wednesday is Tuesday.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 16*2*4*8*10*30

Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All ices are blues. No ice is yellow. Some pinks are ices. Conclusions: I. Some yellows are blues. II. No pink is blue. III. No yellow is blue.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.
questions.explanation: All ices are blue and some pinks are ices, so some pinks are blue and II is false. Only the ices are known not to be yellow; the other blues may or may not be, so neither I nor III is certain on its own, and the two cannot both be true.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 14*18*7*79*33
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation 60*6*3*18*49*5
In a certain code language, 'PENCIL' is written as '1771771418' and 'ERASER' is written as '6204231024'. How will 'SHARPNER' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter's position in the alphabet is increased by 1, 2, 3, ... in turn: P (16) + 1 = 17, E (5) + 2 = 7, N (14) + 3 = 17 and so on. SHARPNER gives 19 + 1, 8 + 2, 1 + 3, 18 + 4, 16 + 5, 14 + 6, 5 + 7, 18 + 8 = 20, 10, 4, 22, 21, 20, 12, 26.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? HSDA, IZQT, ?, KNQF, LUDY
questions.explanation: First letters run H, I, J, K, L; second letters move 7 forward (S, Z, G, N, U); third letters 13 (D, Q, D, Q, D); fourth letters 19 (A, T, M, F, Y). The missing cluster is JGDM.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row - 67, 25, 101; Second row - 55, 17, 97; Third row - 45, 19, ? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is 3 times the first minus 4 times the second: 3 × 67 − 4 × 25 = 101 and 3 × 55 − 4 × 17 = 97. So 3 × 45 − 4 × 19 = 135 − 76 = 59.

questions.text: What value must be given to ‘*’ to make 6347*25 exactly divisible by 11?
questions.explanation: For divisibility by 11 the sums of alternate digits must differ by 0 or a multiple of 11. From the right, (5 + * + 4 + 6) − (2 + 7 + 3) = 3 + *, which is 11 when * = 8.

questions.text: The average runs of a cricket player in 20 matches is 30. If the average of the first 12 matches is 40, find the average of the last 8 matches.
questions.explanation: Total runs 20 × 30 = 600; the first 12 matches gave 12 × 40 = 480, leaving 120 in 8 matches: 120 ÷ 8 = 15.

questions.text: The ratio of the cost price to the marked price of an article is 4 ∶ 7. A discount of 25% is given on the marked price and the shopkeeper made a profit of ₹50. Find the cost price of the article.
questions.explanation: Let CP = 4k and MP = 7k. SP = 0.75 × 7k = 5.25k, so the profit is 1.25k = ₹50 and k = 40. CP = 4 × 40 = ₹160.

questions.text: A shopkeeper claims that he is selling sugar at Rs.27/kg which cost him Rs.30/kg, but he gives 750 grams instead of 1000 grams. What is his profit or loss percentage?
questions.explanation: 750 g costs him 0.75 × 30 = ₹22.50 and he sells it for ₹27. Profit = 4.50/22.50 × 100 = 20%.

questions.text: Two trains having lengths of 230 m and 240 m are 130 m apart. They start moving towards each other on parallel tracks, at speeds of 160 km/h and 200 km/h, respectively. In how much time will the trains cross each other?
questions.explanation: The trains close at 160 + 200 = 360 km/h = 100 m/s and must cover 230 + 240 + 130 = 600 m: 600 ÷ 100 = 6 seconds.

questions.text: 40% of the cost price of an article is equal to 30% of its selling price. The approximate percentage of profit or loss on the cost price is:
questions.explanation: 0.4 × CP = 0.3 × SP, so SP/CP = 4/3: a profit of 1/3 of the cost, or 33.33%.

questions.text: Find the compound interest on ₹1,60,000 at 10% per annum for 2 years if the interest is compounded half-yearly.
questions.explanation: Compounded half-yearly: 5% for 4 periods. Amount = 1,60,000 × 1.05⁴ = 1,60,000 × 1.21550625 = ₹1,94,481, so the CI is ₹34,481.

questions.text: If y varies directly with x, and y = 61 when x = 42, find y when x = 54 (consider integral value).
questions.explanation: y/x is constant: y = 61 × 54/42 = 61 × 9/7 = 78.4, or 78 as a whole number.

questions.text: The salaries of X, Y and Z are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. By what percentage is the salary of Z more than that of X?
questions.explanation: Z earns 5 parts to X's 2, that is 3 parts more: 3/2 × 100 = 150% more.

questions.text: The average of two numbers is 96. If 2 is added to the smaller number, the ratio between the numbers becomes 2 : 3. The smaller number is _________.
questions.explanation: The numbers add up to 2 × 96 = 192. (x + 2)/(192 − x) = 2/3 gives 3x + 6 = 384 − 2x, so 5x = 378 and x = 75.6.

questions.text: Which of the following is the debut novel of Indian novelist Chetan Bhagat, who received the Society Young Achievers Award and the Publisher’s Recognition award for his works?
options: The Three Mistakes of My Life
questions.explanation: 'Five Point Someone' (2004) was Chetan Bhagat's first novel; 'What Young India Wants' is a book of essays.

questions.text: Identify the disease caused by a monkey bite.
questions.explanation: Rabies spreads through the bite of an infected mammal, monkeys among them. Malaria is spread by mosquitoes, typhoid by contaminated food and water, and influenza through the air.

questions.text: Which dancer was awarded in 1968 with a gold medal by the Mexican Government for her choreography for the Ballet Folklorico of Mexico?
questions.explanation: Mrinalini Sarabhai, the dancer who founded the Darpana Academy in Ahmedabad, received the Mexican government's gold medal in 1968 for this choreography.

questions.text: Padma Bhushan awardee Vikku Vinayakaram is a __________ player.
questions.explanation: Vikku Vinayakram is a master of the ghatam, the clay-pot percussion instrument of Carnatic music.

questions.text: Who among the following won Arjuna Award 2021 in athletics discipline?
questions.explanation: Triple jumper Arpinder Singh, the 2018 Asian Games champion, received the Arjuna Award in 2021 for athletics.

questions.text: Which water body is the world's third largest ocean spread over an area of 70,560,000 km² on the earth's surface?
questions.explanation: The Indian Ocean is the third largest ocean, after the Pacific and the Atlantic.

questions.text: Microfinance Institutions Network (MFIN) and Sa-Dhan along with FIDC (Finance Industry Development Council) have jointly launched the _______________ for the micro credit industry in the year 2019.
questions.explanation: In September 2019 MFIN and Sa-Dhan, the microfinance industry's self-regulatory bodies, launched the Code for Responsible Lending with FIDC, setting common rules for all lenders in micro-credit.

questions.text: Ustad Zakir Hussain is the son of ____________, an Indian tabla player.
questions.explanation: Zakir Hussain was the son of the tabla maestro Ustad Alla Rakha.

questions.text: Malaria is a deadly disease caused by parasites that are transmitted to people through the bite of ________.
questions.explanation: Malaria's Plasmodium parasites are spread by the bite of the female Anopheles mosquito; Aedes carries dengue and Culex filariasis.

questions.text: Who won Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award 2021 in football discipline?
questions.explanation: Sunil Chhetri, then India's football captain, received the Khel Ratna in 2021, the first footballer to do so.

questions.text: Which ministry launched the ‘Start-up India Seed Fund Scheme’?
options: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
questions.explanation: The Startup India Seed Fund Scheme is run by DPIIT, the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

questions.text: Death Valley is a desert valley in the ________ that is the hottest and driest place with a world record highest air temperature of 134°F.
questions.explanation: Death Valley lies in the Mojave Desert of California; its 134°F (56.7°C) was recorded at Furnace Creek in 1913.

questions.text: Lakshmi Shankar was a Hindustani classical vocalist of the _________ Gharana.
questions.explanation: Lakshmi Shankar, Pandit Ravi Shankar's sister-in-law, was a vocalist of the Patiala gharana.

questions.text: Whose autobiography is titled ‘An Unsuitable Boy’?
questions.explanation: 'An Unsuitable Boy' (2017), written with Poonam Saxena, is the film-maker Karan Johar's memoir.

questions.text: Who among the following Indian classical musicians was known as ‘The Queen of Thumri’, who was bestowed the Padma Vibhushan in 2016 for her contribution to music?
questions.explanation: Girija Devi of the Banaras gharana, known as the 'Queen of Thumri', received the Padma Vibhushan in 2016.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘Narcopolis’?
questions.explanation: 'Narcopolis' (2012), a novel set in Bombay's opium dens, is by Jeet Thayil; it was shortlisted for the Booker Prize.

questions.text: Name a common ingredient made from the starchy part of corn kernels used as a thickening agent for gravies, marinades, sauces, soups and casseroles.
questions.explanation: Corn starch, from the starchy endosperm of maize kernels, thickens sauces and gravies; gelatine comes from animal collagen, potato starch from potatoes and pectin from fruit.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The first linguistic state in India got established in:
questions.explanation: Andhra State, the first state formed on linguistic lines, for Telugu speakers, came into being on 1 October 1953 after Potti Sriramulu's fast unto death.

questions.text: What disease in adults means ‘soft bones’ that usually develops due to a deficiency of vitamin D (often from not getting enough sunlight), or less often, digestive or kidney disease?
questions.explanation: Osteomalacia, literally 'soft bones', is the softening of adult bones, mostly from a lack of vitamin D; osteoporosis is a loss of bone density.

questions.text: Bala Saraswati was a prominent exponent of which classical dance form?
questions.explanation: T. Balasaraswati was one of the great exponents of Bharatanatyam.

questions.text: The 7th ICC T20 World Cup Cricket was jointly organised by ________.
questions.explanation: The 2021 men's T20 World Cup, the 7th, was hosted by the BCCI but played in the UAE and Oman because of the pandemic.

questions.text: In which of the following sports is 'Bishop' used?
questions.explanation: The bishop is a chess piece that moves diagonally.

questions.text: Padma Bhushan Kumudini Lakhia is a _________ dancer.
questions.explanation: Kumudini Lakhia, founder of the Kadamb school in Ahmedabad, was a Kathak dancer and choreographer.

questions.text: Which mountain range is the source of Krishna River?
questions.explanation: The Krishna rises in the Sahyadri (the Western Ghats) near Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. She has written many books.
options: Many books were being written by her.
Many books have been written by her.
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'has written' becomes 'have been written' in the passive, with 'many books' as the subject: 'Many books have been written by her.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Satiate
questions.explanation: To 'satiate' is to satisfy fully.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. For the next two years the Franks and another family lived cloistered in the ‘Secret Annex’ of an old office building. B. In 1942, with the Nazis occupying Holland, a thirteen-year-old Jewish girl, Anne, and her family fled their home in Amsterdam and went into hiding. C. In her diary Anne Frank recorded vivid impressions of these experiences during this period. D. Cut off from the outside world, they faced hunger, boredom, the constant cruelties of living in confined quarters, and the ever-present threat of discovery and death.
questions.explanation: B introduces Anne's family going into hiding in 1942, A says where they lived for the next two years, D describes what they faced there and C says Anne recorded these experiences in her diary: BADC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Tick all the boxes
options: To make a bad situation worse
questions.explanation: To 'tick all the boxes' is to meet every requirement.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Once in a blue moon
questions.explanation: 'Once in a blue moon' means very rarely.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The General have ordered that the troops should move immediately.
questions.explanation: 'The General' is singular, so it takes 'has': 'The General has ordered that the troops should move immediately.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Child’s play
questions.explanation: 'Child's play' is a task that is very easy.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. She “does not helping to getting angry” when she sees someone being treated unfairly
options: is not help to being getting angry
may not help to got angry
will not help to gets angry
questions.explanation: 'Cannot help' is followed by a gerund: 'She cannot help getting angry when she sees someone being treated unfairly.'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The sweet mangoes were eaten by the children.
options: The children were eating the sweet mangoes.
The children was eating the sweet mangoes.
The children are eating the sweet mangoes.
The children ate the sweet mangoes.
questions.explanation: The simple past passive 'were eaten by the children' becomes the simple past active: 'The children ate the sweet mangoes.'

questions.text: Complete the sentence with an appropriate synonym of the word mentioned in the bracket. If you're feeling brave, try this ___________ (savoury) dish made by me.
questions.explanation: A 'savoury' dish is salty or spicy rather than sweet: 'salty'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The old woman was helped by the boy while crossing the road
options: The boy has helped the old woman while crossing the road.
The boy is helping the old woman while crossing the road.
The boy was helped the old woman while crossing the road.
The boy helped the old woman while crossing the road.
questions.explanation: 'Was helped by the boy' is the simple past passive; in the active the boy is the subject: 'The boy helped the old woman while crossing the road.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The activity of writing dictionaries
questions.explanation: Lexicography is the writing and compiling of dictionaries.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who is well versed in many languages
questions.explanation: A polyglot knows and uses several languages.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The careful crafted personality / of Anahita / did not help her much / in the electoral campaign.
questions.explanation: The participle 'crafted' is modified by an adverb: 'The carefully crafted personality'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an INCORRECTLY spelt word. It was really surprising / that the two bosom friends fought / over such a triviale matter / and stopped all communications with each other.
options: and stopped all communications with each other
that the two bosom friends fought
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'trivial'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Stupendous
questions.explanation: 'Stupendous' means astonishingly great or impressive: 'stunning'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'alimony'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Living organisms (1)_________ their own kind through a process called reproduction. Plants also increase in number through the process of reproduction. Different plants reproduce in different ways. Most of the flowering plants produce seeds. Plants produce many seeds. Few of these seeds (2)_________ and germinate into new plants. When a seed gets the (3)_________ amount of air, water, soil and sunlight, it grows into a plant. Fruits have seeds (4)_________ them. When a fruit (5)_________ up, the seeds inside it can be used to grow new plants of the same kind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Living organisms 'create', that is produce, their own kind through reproduction.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Most of the flowering plants produce seeds. Plants produce many seeds. Few of these seeds (2)_________ and germinate into new plants. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Only a few of the seeds 'survive' and germinate into new plants.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: A seed grows into a plant when it gets the 'right' amount of air, water, soil and sunlight.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: When a fruit 'dries' up, its seeds can be used to grow new plants.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘PALACE’ is written as ‘ZKZOVX’ and ‘DEVINE’ is written as ‘VWREVM’. How will ‘SLOWLY’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y, ...) and then each pair of letters is swapped: PALACE → KZOZXV → ZKZOVX. So SLOWLY → HOLDOB → OHDLBO.

questions.text: Manoj is the son of Eyup’s father’s sister. Ronaldo is the son of Rihana, who is the mother of Jorge and grandmother of Eyup. Dario is the father of Sheila and the grandfather of Manoj. Rihana is the wife of Dario. How is the wife of Jorge related to Sheila?
questions.explanation: Rihana is Jorge's mother and the wife of Dario, Sheila's father, so Jorge is Sheila's brother. Jorge's wife is therefore Sheila's sister-in-law.

questions.text: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? GODT, JMAV, MKXX, PIUZ, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +3 (G, J, M, P, S), second −2 (O, M, K, I, G), third −3 (D, A, X, U, R) and fourth +2 (T, V, X, Z, B): SGRB.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term related to third term. 6789 : 34 :: 1786 : 26 :: 4327:?
questions.explanation: The second number is the sum of the digits plus 4: 6 + 7 + 8 + 9 + 4 = 34 and 1 + 7 + 8 + 6 + 4 = 26. Likewise 4 + 3 + 2 + 7 + 4 = 20.

questions.text: Two statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some books are pens. All pens are pencils. Conclusions: I. Some pencils are books. II. Some books are not pencils.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: The books that are pens are pencils, so some pencils are books (I). Nothing places any book outside the pencils, so II does not follow.

questions.text: The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) is/are followed in all the number-pairs, except one. Find that odd number-pair.
questions.explanation: In 4:15, 12:143 and 3:8 the second number is the square of the first minus 1 (16 − 1, 144 − 1, 9 − 1). 8² − 1 = 63, not 66, so 8:66 is the odd pair.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 23, 138, 143, ?, 575, 1150
Pointing to a woman on the stage, Noor said, “She is the wife of the son-in-law of the wife of my father”. How is the woman related to Noor?
questions.explanation: The wife of Noor's father is Noor's mother; her son-in-law is her daughter's husband, and his wife is that daughter: Noor's sister.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. BRIGHT : THGIRB :: DANGER : REGNAD :: FOREST : ?
questions.explanation: Each word is written backwards: BRIGHT → THGIRB and DANGER → REGNAD. So FOREST → TSEROF.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 4, 21, 41, 66, 98, 141, 197, 270, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 17, 20, 25, 32, 43, 56, 73, which grow by the primes 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17. The next difference is 73 + 19 = 92, so 270 + 92 = 362.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term related to third term. 9876 : 26 :: 8671 : 18 :: 3427 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the sum of the digits minus 4: 9 + 8 + 7 + 6 − 4 = 26 and 8 + 6 + 7 + 1 − 4 = 18. Likewise 3 + 4 + 2 + 7 − 4 = 12.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'TABLE' is written as '2012125' and 'CHAIR' is written as '381918'. How will 'STAND' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as its place in the alphabet: T = 20, A = 1, B = 2, L = 12, E = 5 gives 2012125. So S = 19, T = 20, A = 1, N = 14, D = 4 gives 19201144.

questions.text: In a certain code language, “SPOT” is written as “POST”, and “PLOT” is written as “LOPT”. How will “SINK” be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves to third place: S P O T → P O S T and P L O T → L O P T. So S I N K → I N S K.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? QTGC, RBVY, ?, TRZQ, UZOM
questions.explanation: First letters move +1 (Q, R, S, T, U), second +8 (T, B, J, R, Z), third +15 (G, V, K, Z, O) and fourth −4 (C, Y, U, Q, M): SJKU.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 600,1500, 3750, 9375, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 2.5 times the one before: 9375 × 2.5 = 23437.50.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs EXCEPT one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: In 32 - 40, 64 - 80 and 56 - 70 the second number is 5/4 of the first. 5/4 of 48 is 60, not 62, so 48 - 62 is the odd pair.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 75*85*17*12*6*8

Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row - 12, 25, 19 Second row - 35, 50, 60 Third row - 24, 70, ? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is twice the first minus a fifth of the second: 2 × 12 − 25/5 = 19 and 2 × 35 − 50/5 = 60. So 2 × 24 − 70/5 = 48 − 14 = 34.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 14, 17,23,35,59,?
questions.explanation: The differences double: 3, 6, 12, 24, so the next is 48: 59 + 48 = 107.

questions.text: If Priya and Renu can do a job in 12 hours (working together at their respective constant speeds) and Priya can do the job alone in 18 hours, in how many hours can Renu do the job alone?
questions.explanation: Renu does 1/12 − 1/18 = 1/36 of the job an hour, so alone she takes 36 hours.

questions.text: The surface area of a cube is 726 cm². Find the volume of the cube
questions.explanation: 6a² = 726, so a² = 121 and a = 11 cm. Volume = 11³ = 1331 cm³.

questions.text: If a number 7P323Q is completely divisible by 88, then the values of P and Q, respectively, are:
questions.explanation: 88 = 8 × 11. For 8, the last three digits 23Q must be divisible by 8: 232 is, so Q = 2. For 11, (7 + 3 + 3) − (P + 2 + 2) = 9 − P must be 0 or a multiple of 11, so P = 9.

questions.text: If a : b = 2 : 5 and b : c = 3 : 4, find the value of a : b : c.
If two circles of radii 28 cm and 18 cm touch each other externally, then the length of a common tangent is _________. [Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.]
questions.explanation: Touching externally, the centres are 28 + 18 = 46 cm apart. The direct common tangent = √(46² − 10²) = √2016 = 2√(28 × 18) ≈ 44.90 cm.

questions.text: How much water (in ml) should be added to 300 ml of a 75% milk and water mixture so that it becomes a 45% milk and water mixture?
questions.explanation: The mixture holds 225 ml of milk. For that to be 45% of the whole, the whole must be 225/0.45 = 500 ml, so 200 ml of water is added.

questions.text: The marked price of a shirt is ₹1,200. The shopkeeper gives successive discounts of 25% and 20%. Find the selling price of the shirt.

A batch of 30 students took an intelligence test in an institution. 20 of them scored an average of 75 marks and the remaining students scored an average of 87 marks. What is the average score of the entire batch of students?
Sundar lends a sum of ₹6,000 to Mahesh at an interest rate of 10% p.a., compounded annually. What will be the amount at the end of 2 years?
At 19% discount, the selling price of a book is ₹453.60. What is its marked price (in ₹)?
questions.explanation: The selling price is 81% of the marked price: 453.60/0.81 = ₹560.

questions.text: Kumar’s salary is ₹ 30,000 per month. He spends 25% of this on food and rent and 20% of the remaining on education. But he pays 5% of his total salary on paying the income tax and saves ₹ 8,000 after all these three deductions. What is the amount (in ₹.) available with him after his savings?
questions.explanation: Food and rent take ₹7,500, education 20% of the remaining ₹22,500 = ₹4,500, and tax 5% of ₹30,000 = ₹1,500. That leaves ₹16,500; after saving ₹8,000 he has ₹8,500.

questions.text: A ship sails out to a mark at the speed of 15 km/h and sails back to the starting point at the speed of 10 km/h. The average speed of sailing of the ship is:
questions.explanation: For equal distances, average speed = 2 × 15 × 10/(15 + 10) = 300/25 = 12 km/h.

questions.text: A woman spends 25% of her income. If her expenditure is ₹1,250, then find her income.
questions.explanation: ₹1,250 is 25% of her income, so the income is 1,250 × 4 = ₹5,000.

questions.text: Which of the following terms is NOT related with cricket?
questions.explanation: The striking circle is the 'D' in front of each goal in hockey, from inside which a goal must be scored. Googly, full toss and short pitch are cricket terms.

questions.text: Saw dust is used to adulterate:
questions.explanation: Sawdust is a common adulterant of powdered spices such as coriander powder.

questions.text: Rajkumar Singhajit Singh was awarded the Padma Shri in 1986 for his contribution to which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: Rajkumar Singhajit Singh, a guru of Manipuri dance, received the Padma Shri in 1986.

questions.text: In 1978, the _______ to the Constitution removed the right to property from the list of Fundamental Rights.
questions.explanation: The 44th Amendment (1978) removed the right to property from the Fundamental Rights; it is now a legal right under Article 300A.

questions.text: Who among the following Tennis players won the Laureus World Sportsman of the Year Award 2021?
questions.explanation: Rafael Nadal was named Laureus World Sportsman of the Year at the 2021 awards, after winning his 13th French Open title in 2020.

questions.text: How many players can remain outside the circle in the first six overs of a T20 cricket match?
questions.explanation: In the first six overs (the powerplay) of a T20 innings, no more than two fielders may be outside the 30-yard circle.

questions.text: Which of the following are the most primitive non-vascular plants?
questions.explanation: Bryophytes (mosses and liverworts) have no vascular tissue and are the simplest land plants; pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms are all vascular.

questions.text: Which functional group compound is obtained by the reaction of an oxoacid with a hydroxyl compound, such as alcohol or phenol?
questions.explanation: An oxoacid, such as a carboxylic acid, reacting with an alcohol or phenol gives an ester and water.

questions.text: Mallikarjun Mansur, an Indian classical singer from Karnataka and an excellent vocalist in Khayal style, belonged to which of the following Gharanas of music?
questions.explanation: Mansur belonged to the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana. After early lessons from Nilkanth Bua Alurmath of the Gwalior gharana, he was trained by Manji Khan and then Bhurji Khan, sons of Alladiya Khan, the gharana's patriarch.

questions.text: The Government of India, in February 2022, approved ₹26,275 crores for an umbrella scheme for the modernisation of the police force in India for the next how many years?
questions.explanation: In February 2022 the Union Government approved the umbrella scheme of Modernisation of Police Forces, with a central outlay of ₹26,275 crore for the five years 2021-22 to 2025-26.

questions.text: Who among the following personalities has been conferred the prestigious Padma Shri Award for his contribution to Folk Dance form Panthi?
questions.explanation: Dr Radhe Shyam Barle of Chhattisgarh, an exponent of the Panthi folk dance, received the Padma Shri in 2021.

questions.text: V Satyanarayana Sarma is recognised as a __________ classical dancer.
questions.explanation: Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma was a Kuchipudi dancer, celebrated for his female roles such as Satyabhama.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Guru Bipin Singh was a master of Manipuri dance, not Kuchipudi. The other pairs are correct.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a part of the process of the manufacture of steel in India?
questions.explanation: Ginning separates cotton fibre from its seeds. Steel making runs from the blast furnace to pig iron, then steel, then the shaping of the metal.

questions.text: Which sportsperson’s autobiography is titled ‘Mind Master: Winning Lessons From A Champion's Life’?
questions.explanation: 'Mind Master: Winning Lessons from a Champion's Life' (2019) is chess champion Viswanathan Anand's book, written with Susan Ninan.

questions.text: What layer of Earth's mantle lies beneath the lithosphere that has enough pressure and heat to allow rocks to flow like a liquid with a viscous, caramel-like consistency?
questions.explanation: The asthenosphere, the weak upper mantle below the lithosphere, is hot enough and under enough pressure to flow slowly.

questions.text: Pandit Birju Maharaj was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan in ____________.
questions.explanation: Pandit Birju Maharaj, the Kathak maestro, received the Padma Vibhushan in 1986.

questions.text: What do you call a base that dissolves in water?
questions.explanation: An alkali is a base that dissolves in water, such as sodium hydroxide.

questions.text: Which of the following novels is set in the background of life in New Delhi after the declaration of Emergency in the 1970’s?
questions.explanation: Nayantara Sahgal's 'Rich Like Us' (1985) is set in New Delhi during the Emergency.

questions.text: Which part of the ocean layer is the flattest and smoothest in the world?
questions.explanation: The deep sea (abyssal) plains are the flattest and smoothest regions of the world.

questions.text: Which of the following classical music instruments is performed by Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma?
questions.explanation: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma made the santoor, a hammered dulcimer from Kashmir, an instrument of Hindustani classical music.

questions.text: Which of the following is a function of money? (A)Used as a store of value (B)Used as a measure of value (C)Used as a medium of exchange
questions.explanation: Money serves as a medium of exchange, a measure of value and a store of value: all three.

questions.text: Who among the following has written the novel ‘The Blue Umbrella’?
questions.explanation: 'The Blue Umbrella' is a novella by Ruskin Bond.

questions.text: Pandit Pannalal Ghosh also known as Amal Jyoti Ghosh, was a ____________ player and composer.
questions.explanation: Pannalal Ghosh made the bansuri, the bamboo flute, a concert instrument of Hindustani classical music.

questions.text: Which team won the men’s bronze medal in Asian Table Tennis Championship 2021 in Doha?
questions.explanation: India's men's team won bronze at the 2021 Asian Table Tennis Championships in Doha, losing the semi-final to South Korea; China did not take part.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Meagre
questions.explanation: 'Meagre' means scanty, too little; its opposite is 'plentiful'. 'Sparse' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Slender
questions.explanation: 'Slender' means thin and slight of build; of the options only 'frail', slight and delicate, comes close.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To draw a blank
options: To be unsuccessful at eliciting a response
questions.explanation: To 'draw a blank' is to get no response or result, as when a question or a search yields nothing.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words Take and use the thoughts, inventions, etc. of another person as one’s own.
questions.explanation: To 'plagiarise' is to pass off another person's work or ideas as one's own.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. Kavi asked Gina if French was her mother tongue.
options: “Whether French is your mother tongue?” Kavi asked Gina.
“Your mother tongue is French,” Kavi enquired Gina.
“French is your mother tongue,” Kavi told Gina.
“Is French your mother tongue?” Kavi asked Gina.
questions.explanation: A reported yes/no question ('asked … if') becomes a direct question with the verb before the subject, and the past 'was' returns to the present 'is': 'Is French your mother tongue?'

questions.text: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A major ________ of modern times is that we have come to assume that all creation is ________ to the material interests of us, the homo-sapiens inhabiting earth, which has cut the _________ relationship we otherwise enjoyed with other constituents of creation
questions.explanation: A 'fallacy' is a mistaken belief: we wrongly assume that creation is 'subservient' (subordinate) to human interests, and this has cut our 'symbiotic' (mutually beneficial) relationship with the rest of creation.

questions.text: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. We have already said that inconsistency is not a matter of __________ education or lack of logical ______________.
questions.explanation: Inconsistency is not a matter of 'inadequate' education or a lack of logical 'rigour', strictness of reasoning. No other pair makes sense in both blanks.

questions.text: Select the correct homonym from the given options to fill in the blank. Nadia had an apple and a________for breakfast.
questions.explanation: A 'pear' is a fruit, eaten here with the apple; 'pair' (a set of two) and 'pare' (to peel or trim) sound the same but mean something else.

questions.text: Identify the option that arranges the given parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. a) Though she was a woman of slim build b) Mrs. Hima Raman used to teach us geography at school c) she was remarkably strong and energetic d) She had beautiful eyes and a sharp nose
questions.explanation: Part b introduces Mrs. Hima Raman, d describes her looks, and a ('Though she was a woman of slim build') leads into c ('she was remarkably strong and energetic'): b, d, a, c.

questions.text: Which word in the given sentence is the ANTONYM of – doubtful? The poverty of his childhood played a decisive role in his adult life.
questions.explanation: 'Decisive' means settling a matter firmly, leaving no doubt: the opposite of 'doubtful'.

questions.text: Select the correct homonym from the given options to fill in the blank. I wonder if the committee members changed________plans.
questions.explanation: The possessive 'their' (belonging to them) goes with 'plans'; 'they're' is 'they are' and 'there' refers to a place.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Chastise
questions.explanation: To 'chastise' is to rebuke or punish someone for doing wrong: to 'discipline' them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. We are waiting “to” the arrival of our cousins from the West.
questions.explanation: One waits 'for' something: 'We are waiting for the arrival of our cousins'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The news of the robbery spread faster than ________.
questions.explanation: News that travels very fast is said to spread like wildfire; 'faster than fire' uses the same image.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Man of letters
questions.explanation: A 'man of letters' is a learned person: a scholar or writer.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Ignominy
questions.explanation: 'Ignominy' is public shame or disgrace; its opposite is 'glory'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Jump the gun
options: Start something too soon or act hastily
There is always a cost to do something
questions.explanation: To 'jump the gun' is to act too soon, like a runner who starts before the starting pistol.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. They propose to build a dam for irrigation purposes
options: Build a dam for irrigation purposes.
For the irrigation purposes a dam has been built.
It is proposed to build a dam for irrigation purposes.
questions.explanation: With 'propose' followed by an infinitive, the passive takes the impersonal form 'It is proposed to …', and the agent 'they' is dropped.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Bestial
questions.explanation: 'Bestial' means like a beast, savagely cruel: 'brutish'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The students stopped / their chatter / as soon as them noticed / the teacher enter the classroom.
questions.explanation: The verb 'noticed' needs a subject pronoun: 'as soon as they noticed', not 'them'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The (1)_________ of roads in the 1700s and 1800s made the (2)_________ of goods and people much easier. Many nobles and businessmen (3)___________ their wealth in building bridges and tunnels. John Metcalfe was one of the most (4)__________ road builders of this period. He was blind and felt the surface of the road. This was done to make sure that it met his (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: It was the 'improvement' of roads that made moving goods and people much easier; 'stagnation' and 'setback' would have made it harder.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The (1)_________ of roads in the 1700s and 1800s made the (2)_________ of goods and people much easier. Many nobles and businessmen (3)___________ their wealth in building bridges and tunnels. John Metcalfe was one of the most (4)__________ road builders of this period. He was blind and felt the surface of the road. This was done to make sure that it met his (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The 'transportation' of goods and people is their carriage from place to place; 'shipment' and 'delivery' suit goods, not people.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The (1)_________ of roads in the 1700s and 1800s made the (2)_________ of goods and people much easier. Many nobles and businessmen (3)___________ their wealth in building bridges and tunnels. John Metcalfe was one of the most (4)__________ road builders of this period. He was blind and felt the surface of the road. This was done to make sure that it met his (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Wealth is 'invested' in a venture: the nobles and businessmen put their money into bridges and tunnels.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The (1)_________ of roads in the 1700s and 1800s made the (2)_________ of goods and people much easier. Many nobles and businessmen (3)___________ their wealth in building bridges and tunnels. John Metcalfe was one of the most (4)__________ road builders of this period. He was blind and felt the surface of the road. This was done to make sure that it met his (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: A blind man who built roads was among the most 'remarkable', outstanding, builders of his time; 'credulous', 'fascinated' and 'attentive' do not describe a builder's standing.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The (1)_________ of roads in the 1700s and 1800s made the (2)_________ of goods and people much easier. Many nobles and businessmen (3)___________ their wealth in building bridges and tunnels. John Metcalfe was one of the most (4)__________ road builders of this period. He was blind and felt the surface of the road. This was done to make sure that it met his (5)_________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: A road 'meets someone's requirements' when it satisfies the standards they set; Metcalfe checked the surface by touch to make sure it did.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. A _ D K P A B _ K P A B F _ P A B _ K P
questions.explanation: With B, E, K, G in the blanks the series reads ABDKP ABEKP ABFKP ABGKP: the third letter moves on one each time (D, E, F, G) while A, B, K and P repeat.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and the fifth number is related to the sixth number. 15 : 105 :: ? : 196 :: 4 : 28
questions.explanation: The second number of each pair is 7 times the first: 15 × 7 = 105 and 4 × 7 = 28. So the missing number is 196 ÷ 7 = 28.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1.Assignment 2.Assortment 3.Asymmetric 4.Astrology 5.Astronaut
questions.explanation: All begin 'As'; by the third letter, 'Ass' (Assignment, Assortment) comes before 'Ast' (Astrology, Astronaut) and 'Asy' (Asymmetric). Then i comes before o and l before n: 1, 2, 4, 5, 3.

questions.text: In a certain code language, “DISEASE” is written as “EKVEASE”, and “FACULTY” is written as “GCFULTY”. How will “HELPFUL” be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first three letters move +1, +2 and +3 and the rest stay: DIS → EKV and FAC → GCF. So HEL → IGO: IGOPFUL.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: The second number is twice the sum of the first's digits: 6 + 7 + 8 = 21 → 42, 5 + 4 + 6 = 15 → 30 and 1 + 2 + 5 = 8 → 16. For 283 it would be 2 × 13 = 26, not 28.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (43, 34, 387) (13, 10, 39) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: The third number is the first times the difference of the first two: 43 × (43 − 34) = 387 and 13 × (13 − 10) = 39. Likewise 18 × (18 − 13) = 90.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 627, 636, 619, ?, 611, 652
questions.explanation: The differences are +9, −17, +25, −33, +41, growing by 8 and alternating in sign: 619 + 25 = 644, and 644 − 33 = 611.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (78, 13, 30)
questions.explanation: The third number is the first divided by the second, times 5: 78 ÷ 13 × 5 = 30. Likewise 280 ÷ 70 × 5 = 20.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. CHAISE : EHIASC :: MODULE : EOUDLM :: SLIDER : ?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters swap, as do the third and fourth: CHAISE → EHIASC and MODULE → EOUDLM. So SLIDER → RLDIES.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? WAVR, ZHGG, ?, FVCK, ICNZ
questions.explanation: First letters move +3 (W, Z, C, F, I), second letters +7 (A, H, O, V, C), third letters +11 (V, G, R, C, N) and fourth letters −11 (R, G, V, K, Z), wrapping round the alphabet: CORV.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term. 10 : 40 :: 17 : ? :: 14 : 112
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by the number 6 less than it: 10 × 4 = 40 and 14 × 8 = 112. Likewise 17 × 11 = 187.

questions.text: If 12 January 2019 was on Monday, what was the day on 14 December 1917?
questions.explanation: 14 December 1917 to 14 December 2018 is 101 years with 25 leap days: 101 + 25 = 126 odd days, a whole number of weeks. The 29 days on to 12 January 2019 add 1 odd day, so 14 December 1917 fell one day before Monday: Sunday.

questions.text: The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number-pairs EXCEPT one. Find that odd number-pair.
questions.explanation: The second number is the square root of the first minus 3: √100 − 3 = 7, √169 − 3 = 10 and √64 − 3 = 5. But √25 − 3 = 2, not 4.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All birds are parrots. No parrot is a crow. Some owls are crows. Conclusions: I. Some parrots are owls. II. No crow is a bird. III. No owl is a bird.
options: Both conclusions I and III follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: Every bird is a parrot and no parrot is a crow, so no crow is a bird (II). The owls that are crows are not parrots, but nothing ties the other owls to parrots or birds, so I and III are only possibilities.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 75 * 25 * 40 * 63 * 92 * 91

Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. MADE : JXAB :: RULE: ORIB :: GOAL:?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back: MADE → JXAB and RULE → ORIB. So GOAL → DLXI.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 17*3*48*42*14
In a certain code language, ‘UNDER’ is written as ‘WLFCT’ and ‘WORDS’ is written as ‘YMTBU’. How will ‘LOFTY’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +2, −2, +2, −2, +2: UNDER → WLFCT and WORDS → YMTBU. So LOFTY → NMHRA.

questions.text: If A denotes ‘+’, B denotes ‘×’, C denotes ‘−’ and D denotes ‘÷’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? (17 B 4 ) A (29 B 3) C (85 D 17 ) A 26 C 13 A 52 = ?
The marked price of an article is 30% more than the cost price. A discount of 15% is offered on the marked price. By what percentage is the final price more than the cost price?
questions.explanation: The final price is 1.30 × 0.85 = 1.105 times the cost price: 10.5% more.

questions.text: The average run of 8 players is 6.5.The average run increases by 1 when 2 new players are included. What is the average run of new players?
questions.explanation: The 8 players made 8 × 6.5 = 52 runs; the 10 average 7.5, so 75 runs. The two new players made 75 − 52 = 23 runs: 11.5 each.

questions.text: The population of a city increased by 5%, 2% and 6% in the first, second and third year, respectively. At the end of the third year, the population became 56,763. Find the initial population of the city.
Find the area of a triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm, and 5 cm.
questions.explanation: 3² + 4² = 5², so the triangle is right-angled and its area is ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 cm².

questions.text: Rani covers a distance of 475 m in a minute. How much distance would Rani have covered in an hour if she travelled at 1.2 times of her current speed?
questions.explanation: At 1.2 times her speed Rani covers 475 × 1.2 = 570 m a minute: 570 × 60 = 34,200 m = 34.2 km in an hour.

questions.text: The population of a city is 225000. If the annual birth rate and death rates are 4.5% and 2.5%, respectively, calculate the increase in the population of the city after 2 years.
What will be the average of the odd numbers from 21 to 81?
questions.explanation: The odd numbers from 21 to 81 are evenly spaced, so their average is that of the first and last: (21 + 81)/2 = 51.

questions.text: If two successive discounts of 10% and 5%, are given, then what will be the net discount percentage?
Find the ratio in which pulses at ₹80 per kg can be mixed with pulses at ₹95 per kg to get a mixture worth ₹85 per kg.
questions.explanation: By alligation, cheaper : dearer = (95 − 85) : (85 − 80) = 10 : 5 = 2 : 1.

questions.text: When payment is made online, the discount offered is 20%. Additional discount of 8% is given to ABC credit card holders. Sandeep buys a laptop of ₹35,000 by paying online and pays through his ABC credit card. How much does he need to pay?
Two triangles ΔABC and ΔDEF are similar. If AB = 6 cm, BC = 8 cm and DE = 9 cm, find EF.
questions.explanation: Corresponding sides of similar triangles are proportional: EF/BC = DE/AB = 9/6, so EF = 8 × 1.5 = 12 cm.

questions.text: If a man were to sell his home theatre system for ₹ 14,400, he would lose 25%. But if he wants to gain 20%, the item should be sold for:
questions.explanation: At a 25% loss, ₹14,400 is 75% of the cost, so the cost is ₹19,200. A 20% gain needs 1.2 × 19,200 = ₹23,040.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers is NOT divisible by 150?
questions.explanation: 150 = 2 × 3 × 5². All four numbers are even and end in 50 or 00, so divisibility by 3 decides: the digit sum of 463750 is 25, not a multiple of 3, while the others' are 15, 12 and 6.

questions.text: If x+y=13, then (x-8)³+(y-5)³ is:
questions.explanation: (x − 8) + (y − 5) = x + y − 13 = 0. When a + b = 0, a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) = 0.

questions.text: The product of three consecutive odd numbers is 693. What is the smallest of the three numbers?
questions.explanation: 693 = 7 × 9 × 11, three consecutive odd numbers; the smallest is 7.

questions.text: Who among the following is NOT a tabla player?
questions.explanation: G. N. Balasubramaniam (GNB) was a Carnatic vocalist; Swapan Chaudhuri, Tanmoy Bose and Bickram Ghosh are tabla players.

questions.text: What type of precipitation is common at the equatorial depression in the Congo Basin, the Amazon Basin, and the islands of Southeast Asia?
questions.explanation: Near the equator strong heating makes warm, moist air rise almost every afternoon, giving convectional rain (the option's 'Conventional' is a misprint for it).

questions.text: Who among the following founded the ‘Shillong Chamber Choir’?
questions.explanation: The Shillong Chamber Choir was founded by the composer and pianist Neil Nongkynrih.

questions.text: To which of the following states does Ramchandraiah, a Koya tribal singer, who received Padma Shri 2022, belong?
questions.explanation: Sakini Ramachandraiah, a singer of the Koya tribe's oral traditions, is from Telangana; he received the Padma Shri in 2022.

questions.text: In March 2021, _________ became the first female Indian cricketer and the second, internationally, after England's Charlotte Edwards, to breach the 10000-run mark in international cricket.
questions.explanation: Mithali Raj passed 10,000 international runs in March 2021, the first Indian woman to do so.

questions.text: Whose memoir is titled ‘My Life in Full: Work, Family and Our Future’?
questions.explanation: 'My Life in Full: Work, Family and Our Future' (2021) is the memoir of Indra Nooyi, former chairperson and CEO of PepsiCo.

questions.text: Arvind Adiga wrote his famous award winning novel ____________ in 2008.
questions.explanation: 'The White Tiger', Aravind Adiga's first novel, won the Booker Prize in 2008.

questions.text: With whom did Camillo Golgi receive the Nobel Prize in 1906 for his work on the structure of the nervous system?
questions.explanation: Camillo Golgi shared the 1906 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Santiago Ramón y Cajal for their work on the structure of the nervous system.

questions.text: Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam, awarded with the honour of Padma Bhushan by the Government of India, is known for his brilliant performance and choreography in which for the following styles of Indian classical dances?
questions.explanation: Vempati Chinna Satyam was the great reformer and choreographer of Kuchipudi, and founded the Kuchipudi Art Academy in Chennai.

questions.text: Who among the following has written the book ‘A century is not enough: my roller coaster ride to success’?
questions.explanation: 'A Century Is Not Enough' (2018) is Sourav Ganguly's memoir of his cricket career.

questions.text: In which year was the Pro Kabaddi League founded in India?
questions.explanation: The Pro Kabaddi League began in 2014; its first season was played in July and August that year.

questions.text: With which musical instrument can you associate the name of Ali Akbar Khan?
questions.explanation: Ustad Ali Akbar Khan, son of Allauddin Khan, was one of the greatest sarod players.

questions.text: Atal Ranking of Institutions on Innovation Achievements is an initiative by:
questions.explanation: The Atal Ranking of Institutions on Innovation Achievements (ARIIA), which ranks higher-education institutions on innovation and start-up support, is an initiative of the Ministry of Education (formerly the Ministry of Human Resource Development).

questions.text: Yamini Krishnamurthy, who received the Padma Vibhushan Award in 2016, is an Indian dancer in which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: Yamini Krishnamurthy is a leading exponent of Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi; of the options, only Bharatanatyam is hers.

questions.text: Identify the chemical structure for potassium hydroxide.
questions.explanation: Potassium hydroxide is KOH: a potassium ion (K⁺) with a hydroxide ion (OH⁻). K₂O is potassium oxide.

questions.text: Vidyagauri Adkar is associated with _________ classical dance form.
questions.explanation: Vidyagauri Adkar is a Kathak dancer of the Jaipur gharana.

questions.text: Which element’s symbol is derived from the Greek name hydrargyrum, meaning ‘liquid silver’ – indicating its shiny surface?
questions.explanation: Mercury's symbol Hg comes from 'hydrargyrum', the Latinised form of the Greek for 'water-silver', after the liquid metal's silvery shine.

questions.text: The idea of a single citizenship in the Constitution of India was borrowed from:
questions.explanation: Single citizenship, like parliamentary government and the rule of law, was borrowed from the British (UK) Constitution.

questions.text: Padma Bhushan awardee Pandit Nikhil Jyoti Ghosh was a _________ player.
questions.explanation: Pandit Nikhil Ghosh was a tabla player, teacher and musicologist who founded the Sangit Mahabharati in Mumbai; his brother Pannalal Ghosh was the flautist.

questions.text: Which element of Group 13 of the periodic table liquefies just above room temperature?
questions.explanation: Gallium melts at about 29.8 °C, just above room temperature; it can melt in the hand.

questions.text: What was the rank of India in AIBA World Youth Boxing Championship 2021 held in Poland?
questions.explanation: India topped the medal table at the 2021 AIBA Youth World Boxing Championships in Kielce, Poland, with eight gold medals.

questions.text: Since 2017, the Finance Minister in India has been presenting the Union Budget for the country on which date?
questions.explanation: Since 2017 the Union Budget has been presented on 1 February, brought forward from the last working day of February.

questions.text: Which of the following is a soft metal that ignites in air and reacts violently with water and has atomic number 37 in the periodic table?
questions.explanation: Rubidium (Rb, atomic number 37) is a soft alkali metal that ignites in air and reacts violently with water. Caesium is 55, francium 87 and gallium 31.

questions.text: What type of forests, consisting of bushes and scrubs, exist in India where the regions receive less than 70 cm rainfall?
questions.explanation: In regions with less than 70 cm of rain the natural vegetation is thorny trees, bushes and scrub: tropical thorn forests.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Chip off the old block
options: Someone who makes the right decision
Someone who tries to escape from their parents
questions.explanation: A 'chip off the old block' is someone who resembles a parent in character or behaviour.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. He ran “most happily” to receive his father.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the plain adverb: 'He ran happily to receive his father.' 'Happy' and 'happier' are adjectives and 'more happily' needs a comparison; 'most happily', meaning 'very happily', is also acceptable English, but there is no 'no substitution' option.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The rumours usually _________ like wild fire.
questions.explanation: A habitual action with the plural subject 'rumours' takes the simple present plural: 'The rumours usually spread like wild fire.'

questions.text: Fill in the blank with the correctly spelt word. There was a feeling of __________ in his eyes.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'vengeance'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He always ____ a tantrum about something or the other.
questions.explanation: To 'throw a tantrum' is to have a fit of temper; its past tense is 'threw'. 'Through' only sounds the same.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Intelligent and strikingly attractive, Tess is indisputably the central character of the novel that bears her name. B. But she is also more than a distinctive individual: Hardy makes her into somewhat of a mythic heroine. C. Her name, formally Theresa, recalls St. Teresa of Avila, another martyr whose vision of a higher reality cost her, her life. D. Tess’s story, thus, is a story representing a deeper and larger experience than that of a single individual.
questions.explanation: A introduces Tess, B ('But she is also more ...') says Hardy makes her a mythic heroine, C supports this through her name, and D ('thus') draws the conclusion: ABCD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in the brackets to fill in the blank. In 1024, a king named Mahmood ____________ (robbed) a city called Anhilwad.
questions.explanation: To 'plunder' a place is to rob it by force, as an invading army does.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The mob / is believing / every word / the leader says.
questions.explanation: 'Believe' is a stative verb and is not used in the continuous: 'The mob believes every word the leader says.'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Parker has been bitten by a rare species of spiders.
options: A rare species of spiders had bitten Parker.
A rare species of spiders is biting Parker.
A rare species of spiders has bitten Parker.
A rare species of spiders bit Parker.
questions.explanation: The present perfect passive 'has been bitten' becomes the present perfect active 'has bitten': 'A rare species of spiders has bitten Parker.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error Investing on real estate / can earn you quick profit / but it comes with / a certain amount of risk attached to it.
options: a certain amount of risk attached to it
questions.explanation: One invests 'in' something, not 'on': 'Investing in real estate'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The minor project put forward by the government “is now moving around into” its third year.
questions.explanation: A project enters its third year: 'is now moving into its third year'. 'Moving around' means going from place to place, and 'are' does not agree with 'project'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'bibliography'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Rahul “shall write” the exam at this time next week.
questions.explanation: An action that will be in progress at a set time in the future takes the future continuous: 'Rahul shall be writing the exam at this time next week.'

questions.text: Select the sentence which has no spelling error.
options: Mala asked students to aggreggate examples of many chemicals.
Final results will be declared on the basis of agregate marks.
Chromosomes are aggregatte and closely linked in a cell.
My son’s aggregate marks were very poor in the previous year.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'aggregate': 'gg' only after the first 'a', and a single 't'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Resolute
questions.explanation: 'Resolute' means firm and determined: 'strong' in purpose.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. An omission of duty
questions.explanation: Delinquency is a failure to do one's duty. Deliberation is careful thought and delineation is description or outlining.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The next Faerie Market was held (1)_________ schedule (2)_________ the other side of the wall. The two boys were not allowed to go to the market, but they wanted to. This was a source of great (3)__________ to the boys. The younger of the two had a kitten. She grew slowly but was the sweetest cat in the world, until, one evening, she began to (4)_________ around the house impatiently. The cat was off in the dark and the boy never saw the cat again. He was (5)_________ for a while.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Something held at the planned time is held 'on schedule'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The next Faerie Market was held (1)_________ schedule (2)_________ the other side of the wall. The two boys were not allowed to go to the market, but they wanted to. This was a source of great (3)__________ to the boys. The younger of the two had a kitten. She grew slowly but was the sweetest cat in the world, until, one evening, she began to (4)_________ around the house impatiently. The cat was off in the dark and the boy never saw the cat again. He was (5)_________ for a while.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The next Faerie Market was held (1)_________ schedule (2)_________ the other side of the wall. The two boys were not allowed to go to the market, but they wanted to. This was a source of great (3)__________ to the boys. The younger of the two had a kitten. She grew slowly but was the sweetest cat in the world, until, one evening, she began to (4)_________ around the house impatiently. The cat was off in the dark and the boy never saw the cat again. He was (5)_________ for a while.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Being kept from a market they wanted to visit was a source of 'irritation'; 'abhorrence' and 'hatred' are far too strong, and 'ebullience' means cheerfulness.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The next Faerie Market was held (1)_________ schedule (2)_________ the other side of the wall. The two boys were not allowed to go to the market, but they wanted to. He was (5)_________ for a while.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: A restless cat 'prowls', moving about stealthily, around the house.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The next Faerie Market was held (1)_________ schedule (2)_________ the other side of the wall. The two boys were not allowed to go to the market, but they wanted to. This was a source of great (3)__________ to the boys. The younger of the two had a kitten.
