questions.explanation: The emphatic 'themselves' refers back to the plural 'vaccines': the vaccines themselves, as against the diseases.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term is related to third term. POINT : TPKQP :: BONES : SPPHB :: SEVEN : ?
questions.explanation: The last letter goes first and the first letter last, and the middle three move +1, +2, +3: POINT → T P K Q P and BONES → S P P H B. So SEVEN → N F X H S: NFXHS.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 11,33,38,266,275,?
questions.explanation: The terms are multiplied by 3, 7, 11 and increased by 5, 9 in turn: 11 × 3 = 33, + 5 = 38, × 7 = 266, + 9 = 275, × 11 = 3025.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'FLUTE' is written as 'VGFOU' and 'EXILE' is written as 'VORCV'. How will 'BLOOD' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and each letter replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y and so on): FLUTE → ETULF → VGFOU. So BLOOD → DOOLB → WLLOY.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 115 * 25 * 15 * 2 * 3
questions.explanation: 115 − 25 = 15 × 2 × 3: both sides are 90.

questions.text: Each of the seven friends, Kirti, Siya, Amita, Preeti, Deepika, Jeet and Pari, has scored different marks in an exam. Pari has scored more than Kirti but less than Siya. Deepika has scored less than Preeti but more than Amita. Kirti has scored more than Preeti. Siya is not the highest scorer. Who among the following has scored more than Pari?
questions.explanation: Siya > Pari > Kirti > Preeti > Deepika > Amita. Siya is not the highest, so Jeet is, and Jeet scored more than Pari.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row:16, 12, 48; Second row: 9, 8, 24; Third row:4,24 ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the number into its constituent digits. For example, 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is the second times the square root of the first: 12 × √16 = 48 and 8 × √9 = 24. So 24 × √4 = 48.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row- 14, 4, 31; Second row- 38, 10, 79; Third row- 30, 8, ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is the first plus four times the second plus 1: 14 + 16 + 1 = 31 and 38 + 40 + 1 = 79. So 30 + 32 + 1 = 63.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 54*14*5*72*18*31*11

Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (15, 5, 150); (7, 5, 14) (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: The third number is the first times the difference of the first two: 15 × (15 − 5) = 150 and 7 × (7 − 5) = 14. Likewise 16 × (16 − 8) = 128.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All shoes are boots. All boots are heels. Some slippers are shoes. Conclusions: I. All shoes are heels. II. No slipper is a boot. III. All shoes are slippers.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: All shoes are boots and all boots are heels, so all shoes are heels (I). The slippers that are shoes are boots, so II is false; and nothing says every shoe is a slipper (III).

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 11, 22, 19, ?, 71, 426
questions.explanation: The terms are multiplied by 2, 4, 6 and reduced by 3, 5 in turn: 11 × 2 = 22, − 3 = 19, × 4 = 76, − 5 = 71, × 6 = 426.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs, EXCEPT one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: In the other pairs the second number is 10/3 of the first: 93 → 310, 54 → 180, 33 → 110. 48 × 10/3 = 160, not 165.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? WVU, RQP, MLK, HGF, ?
questions.explanation: Each cluster is three consecutive letters in reverse, and the first letters W, R, M, H move back 5 each time. Next comes C: CBA.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'RISE' is written as ‘QSHJRTDF’ and ‘FALL’ is written as ‘EGZBKMKM’. How will 'KING' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by the letters just before and after it: R → QS, I → HJ, S → RT, E → DF. So KING → JL HJ MO FH: JLHJMOFH.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? XHFM, TEDL, PBBK, ?, HVXI
questions.explanation: The first letters move back 4 (X, T, P, L, H), the second back 3 (H, E, B, Y, V), the third back 2 (F, D, B, Z, X) and the fourth back 1 (M, L, K, J, I): LYZJ.

questions.text: If 19 September 1999 was Sunday, then what was the day of the week on 19 January 2001?
questions.explanation: 19 September 2000 is 366 days later (2000 was a leap year), 2 odd days on, so a Tuesday. From there to 19 January 2001 is 11 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 19 = 122 days, 17 weeks and 3 days: Friday.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 16*8*10*2*4*28
Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1.Ancestors 2.Analyze 3.Antibiotic 4.Analogies 5.Android
questions.explanation: Analogies before Analyze (o before y), then Ancestors, Android and Antibiotic (c, d, t after 'An'): 4, 2, 1, 5, 3.

questions.text: Which two numbers, from amongst the given options, should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? (2)³ ÷ 4 + (72 ÷6)×9 – (21×3) + (15×7) = 92
A bought a toy at a discount of 35%. If he paid ₹975, then find the marked price of the toy.
questions.explanation: ₹975 is 65% of the marked price: 975 ÷ 0.65 = ₹1,500.

questions.text: Calculate the 3rd proportional to 14 and 28.
questions.explanation: The third proportional to a and b is b²/a: 28² ÷ 14 = 784 ÷ 14 = 56.

questions.text: The marked price of 42 items was equal to the cost price of 70 items. The selling price of 25 items was equal to the marked price of 21 items. Calculate the percentage profit or loss from the sale of each item.
questions.explanation: MP = 70/42 = 5/3 of the CP, and SP = 21/25 of the MP = 21/25 × 5/3 = 7/5 of the CP. Profit = 2/5 = 40%.

questions.text: The average weight of 8 men is increased by 2 kg when one of them, whose weight is 90 kg, is replaced by another man. What is the weight of the new man?
questions.explanation: The total rises by 8 × 2 = 16 kg, so the new man weighs 90 + 16 = 106 kg.

questions.text: The population of a city increases by 10% annually. If its present population is 21,000, what will be the population in 3 years?
A motorcycle covers 50 km at a speed of 25 km/h. Find the speed of the motorcycle for the next 50 km of the journey so that the average speed of the whole journey will be 30 km/h.
questions.explanation: 100 km at 30 km/h takes 10/3 hours, and the first 50 km at 25 km/h took 2 hours. The other 50 km must take 4/3 hours: 50 ÷ 4/3 = 37.5 km/h.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 15?
questions.explanation: A number divisible by 15 must end in 0 or 5 and have a digit sum divisible by 3. 3 + 0 + 6 + 0 + 4 + 5 = 18; the others' digit sums are 29, 25 and 26.

questions.text: Among the following options, which are NOT sides of a triangle?
questions.explanation: Any two sides of a triangle must add up to more than the third, but 3 + 1 = 4 is less than 5.

questions.text: Find the volume of the cuboid, if its length is twice more than its breadth and its breadth is 8 cm, which is twice its height.
questions.explanation: SSC's key reads 'twice more than its breadth' as the breadth plus twice it: 8 + 16 = 24 cm (a length of twice the breadth, 16 cm, gives 512 cm³, which is not an option). The height is 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm, so the volume is 24 × 8 × 4 = 768 cm³.

questions.text: Under a sale offer for an item, Mahesh was offered 24% discount on the part of the marked price that was paid in cash, but was charged 1.5% on the part of the marked price paid through a credit card. If Mahesh paid 40% of the marked price in cash and the rest through a credit card and his total final payment was ₹6,391, what was the marked price of the item?

Ali and Badal start from the same position and at the same time in a 1200 m circular race, with speeds of 27 km/h and 45 km/h, respectively. Find after how much time they will meet again on the track for the first time when they are both running in the same direction.
questions.explanation: 27 km/h = 7.5 m/s and 45 km/h = 12.5 m/s. Running the same way, Badal gains 5 m/s and meets Ali again when he has gained a full lap: 1200 ÷ 5 = 240 seconds.

questions.text: A man spends 15% of his income on house rent, 60% of the rest on household expenses and saves the rest. If he saves ₹52,500, what is his total income (in ₹, rounded off to the nearest tens)?
questions.explanation: After rent 85% is left, and 40% of that is saved: 0.85 × 0.4 = 0.34 of the income. 52,500 ÷ 0.34 = 1,54,411.76, or ₹1,54,410 to the nearest ten.

questions.text: Find the volume of a cuboid 16 m long, 12 m broad and 6 m high.
The area of a triangle whose perimeter is 36 cm and length of two sides is 17 cm and 9 cm will be:
questions.explanation: The third side is 36 − 17 − 9 = 10 cm and s = 18. By Heron's formula, area = √(18 × 1 × 9 × 8) = √1,296 = 36 cm².

questions.text: Madhuri spends 80% of her salary and Sushma spends 95% of her salary. But the savings of both are equal. Find the income of Sushma, if the sum of their incomes is ₹10,000.
questions.explanation: Madhuri saves 20% and Sushma 5% of her salary. 0.2M = 0.05S, so S = 4M; with M + S = ₹10,000, M = ₹2,000 and S = ₹8,000.

questions.text: Thetakudi Harihara Vinayakram, an Indian percussionist, is known for popularising which of the following musical instruments?
questions.explanation: T. H. 'Vikku' Vinayakram is the best-known exponent of the ghatam, the clay-pot percussion instrument of Carnatic music.

questions.text: What is the name of Pt. Ravi Shankar's autobiography?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'My Life, My Music', the option nearest to Ravi Shankar's 1968 book 'My Music, My Life'; the option prints the two halves of the title the other way round. His later autobiography is 'Raga Mala'.

questions.text: The Chairman of the Legislative Council is:
options: elected by the Chief Minister and their Cabinet
appointed by the Chief Minister of that state
elected by the members of the Legislative Council
appointed by the Governor of that state
questions.explanation: Under Article 182 the Legislative Council chooses two of its own members as its Chairman and Deputy Chairman.

questions.text: Sheik Chinna Moulana used to play which of the following instruments?
questions.explanation: Sheik Chinna Moulana (1924-1999) was a celebrated nadaswaram player of Carnatic music.

questions.text: ‘Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar’ is given by which of the following bodies?
questions.explanation: The Sangeet Natak Akademi gives the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar to young artists in the performing arts.

questions.text: What is a way in which adaptation does NOT take place?
questions.explanation: Organisms adapt through their structure (morphological), body functions (physiological) and behaviour; 'emotional' is not a type of adaptation.

questions.text: Ricky Kej a globally acclaimed musician from India won the 57th Grammy Award for which of the following contributions?
questions.explanation: Ricky Kej won the Grammy for Best New Age Album at the 57th awards (2015) for 'Winds of Samsara', made with Wouter Kellerman. 'Divine Tides' won him a later Grammy.

questions.text: In 1817, which law of periodicity showed that the atomic weight of phosphorus is the mean of those of nitrogen and arsenic?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Döbereiner's law of triads: in 1817 Johann Döbereiner noticed that strontium's atomic weight is about the mean of calcium's and barium's, the first of his triads of similar elements. (The question's example does not hold: phosphorus, 31, is not the mean of nitrogen, 14, and arsenic, 75.)

questions.text: Which of the following countries won the highest gold medals in Tokyo Olympics 2020?
questions.explanation: The United States won the most gold medals at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, 39, one more than China.

questions.text: In 1820, who found that electric current causes a nearby magnetic needle to move and thus discovered electromagnetism?
questions.explanation: In 1820 Hans Christian Oersted saw a compass needle deflected by a current in a nearby wire, the first evidence that electricity and magnetism are linked.

questions.text: Which of the following instruments is played by Anokhelal Mishra?
questions.explanation: Pandit Anokhelal Mishra was a tabla player of the Banaras gharana.

questions.text: Which of the following is a tributary of Damodar river?
questions.explanation: The Barakar, on which the Maithon dam stands, is the Damodar's main tributary.

questions.text: Which 19-year-old wrestler became the first Indian wrestler to win a silver medal at World Wrestling Championship in October 2021 in the 57 kg weight category?
questions.explanation: Anshu Malik took silver in the women's 57 kg at the World Championships in Oslo in October 2021, the first Indian woman wrestler to reach a world final.

questions.text: Shanta and VP Dhananjayan were awarded the Rashtriya Kalidas Samman for 2020-21 for significant contribution to which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: Shanta and V. P. Dhananjayan are a Bharatanatyam dancing couple from Chennai, founders of the Bharatakalaanjali school.

questions.text: Which of the following has been designated as the self-regulatory origination for Micro finance institutions in India?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank recognises Sa-Dhan, an association of microfinance institutions, as a self-regulatory organisation for the sector.

questions.text: Manjamma Jogati became India’s first transgender folk dancer to receive a Padma Shri honour for her contribution to art in the year ____.
questions.explanation: Matha B. Manjamma Jogati, a transgender Jogati Nritya dancer from Karnataka, was awarded the Padma Shri for art in 2021.

questions.text: Who gives the Bharat Muni Samman?
questions.explanation: The Nalanda Bharata Muni Samman is given by Mumbai's Nalanda Dance Research Centre at its annual Nalanda Nrityotsava.

questions.text: In which sport is free throw used?
questions.explanation: A free throw is an unopposed shot from the free-throw line in basketball, awarded after a foul.

questions.text: The lifting of an object up and down, the parade of an army and the free fall of a heavy object are all examples of which motion?
questions.explanation: Motion along a straight line is rectilinear: an object lifted straight up and down, soldiers marching in a parade and a freely falling body all move in straight lines.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book ‘All From Memory: An Autobiography’?
questions.explanation: 'All From Memory' is the autobiography of B. V. Acharya, the senior Karnataka lawyer and former Advocate General of the state.

questions.text: In February 2022, which state launched the ‘Paray Shikshalaya’ scheme under which elementary education and mid-day meals for students from class 1 to 7 will be provided in open air classrooms?
questions.explanation: West Bengal's 'Paray Shikshalaya' (neighbourhood school) began in February 2022, with open-air classes near their homes for pupils of classes 1 to 7 after the Covid-19 closures.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘The Coward And The Sword’?
questions.explanation: Actor Jugal Hansraj wrote 'The Coward and the Sword', a children's fantasy novel published in 2021.

questions.text: According to the Henry Cavendish experiment conducted in 1797-1798, what was the value of the universal constant of gravity?
questions.explanation: Cavendish's torsion balance gave the Earth's density, from which G works out at about 6.74 × 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg², within about 1% of today's 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹. SSC's key gives 6.75 × 10⁻¹¹, the only option of the right order of magnitude.

questions.text: As per the Essential Defence Services Act, 2021 new plan, how many ordnance factories that make ammunition and other equipment for the armed forces will become part of the seven government-owned corporate entities?
questions.explanation: In October 2021 the Ordnance Factory Board was dissolved and its 41 factories were divided among seven new government-owned companies.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The lawyer had presented the facts of the case well.
options: The facts of the case had presented the lawyer well.
The facts of the case had been presented well by the lawyer.
The facts of the case were being presented by the lawyer well.
The lawyer was presented well by the facts of the case.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had presented' becomes 'had been presented', with the lawyer as the agent: 'The facts of the case had been presented well by the lawyer.'

questions.text: Complete the collocation. Since I like him a lot, I _____ him out.
questions.explanation: To 'ask someone out' is to invite them on a date, which suits liking him a lot.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. It was in this spirit that my little ones crept about me the other evening to hear about their great-grandmother Field, who lived in a great house in Norfolk (a hundred times bigger than that in which they and papa lived), which had been the scene—so at least it was generally believed in that part of the country—of the tragic incidents which they had lately become familiar with from the ballad of the Children in the Wood. B. Here, Alice put out one of her dear mother’s looks, too tender to be called upbraiding. C. Children love to listen to stories about their elders when they were children ; to stretch their imagination to the conception of a traditionary great-uncle, or grandame, whom they never saw. D. Certain it is, that the whole story of the children and their cruel uncle was to be seen fairly carved out in the wood upon the chimney-piece of the great hall— the whole story down to the Robin Redbreasts—till a foolish rich person pulled it down to set up a marble one of modern invention in its stead, with no story upon it.
questions.explanation: C states the general idea (children love stories about their elders), A follows 'in this spirit' with the great-grandmother's house, D describes the carving in that house's great hall, and B gives Alice's response: CADB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Maverick
questions.explanation: A maverick is an independent-minded person who goes his own way; the opposite is a 'conformist'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. Shylock was a cut-throat and was known as “someone who was only interested in the amount of money that he could get from a situation.”
questions.explanation: A 'mercenary' person is interested only in the money to be made.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Crocodile tears
questions.explanation: 'Crocodile tears' are a false or insincere show of sorrow.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. Raman had always been attracted to “the scientific study of sound” and decided to take up a course in sound engineering to pursue his dream career.
questions.explanation: Acoustics is the branch of physics that deals with sound.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To hold good
questions.explanation: To 'hold good' is to remain valid or true.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Allay
questions.explanation: To 'allay' fear or pain is to lessen it: to 'relieve' it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. It's all Greek to me
options: I am aware of the historical facts
I can understand the cause of something
questions.explanation: 'It's all Greek to me' means that something is impossible to understand.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'pitch'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. My brother is a “connoisseur of food” and does not miss any chance to experiment with new dishes.
questions.explanation: A 'gourmet' is a connoisseur of good food; a glutton merely eats too much.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Ambiguous
questions.explanation: 'Ambiguous' means open to more than one meaning, uncertain; its opposite is 'certain'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Quaint
questions.explanation: 'Quaint' means attractively unusual or old-fashioned; of the options the nearest is 'queer' in its sense of odd or strange.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. As I review the events of my past life, I realise how________ are the influences that shape our destinies.
questions.explanation: 'Subtle' influences are delicate and hard to notice, which is why the writer sees them only on looking back.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech. He asked us, “When are you reaching?”
options: He asked us whether we are reaching.
He asked us when we will reach.
He asked us when we were reaching.
He asked us when will you reach?
questions.explanation: The question becomes a statement after 'when', the present continuous moves back to the past continuous and 'you' becomes 'we': 'He asked us when we were reaching.'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. We will not remind you again.
options: You will not be reminded by us again.
You will not remind us again.
You will not have reminded us again.
You will not be reminding us again.
questions.explanation: 'Will not remind' becomes 'will not be reminded', with 'you' as the subject and 'us' as the agent.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. When Sanathan asked Mr. Jignesh / for a fresh evaluation of his performance / in the last financial year, / little did him know that the results will come out worse than expected.
options: for a fresh evaluation of his performance
little did him know that the results will come out worse than expected
questions.explanation: After 'little did' the verb needs a subject pronoun: 'little did he know', not 'him'. (In the same segment 'will' should also be 'would'.)

questions.text:

She is not the only one (2)__________ that flight, since there was also a flight attendant who kept checking on people. And telling them they were going to be fine (3)__________ they had giant pieces of aeroplane carpet stuck to their heads. I can’t (4)_________ land a plane or tell the wounded people that they would be fine soon, due to the fact that I would be (5)_________ too hard and throwing out what ever food I had throughout the day.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Vomiting', along with 'throwing out' the day's food, describes being sick.

questions.text: In a certain code language, “ABROAD” is written as “DROBAA”, and “ACTIVE” is written as “ETICAV”. How will “BISHOP” be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters are taken in the order 6th, 3rd, 4th, 2nd, 1st, 5th: ABROAD → D R O B A A and ACTIVE → E T I C A V. So BISHOP → P S H I B O: PSHIBO.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term related to third term. 11:1309 :: 15: 3345 :: 7:?
questions.explanation: The second number is the cube of the first minus twice the first: 11³ − 22 = 1309 and 15³ − 30 = 3345. Likewise 7³ − 14 = 329.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? FDH, IGK, LJN, OMQ, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward from one cluster to the next: F, I, L, O, R; D, G, J, M, P; H, K, N, Q, T. The next cluster is RPT.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 648,448,294,180,100,?
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 60*19*4* 94*42
Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the following words in a logical and meaningful order. 1- Haripad 2- India 3- South-East Asia 4- Kerala 5- Asia
questions.explanation: SSC's key orders the places by size, from the largest to the smallest: Asia, South-East Asia (about 4.5 million km²), India (about 3.3 million km²), Kerala, Haripad (a town in Kerala). India lies in South Asia, not South-East Asia, so this is not a chain of each place lying inside the one before; no other option gives a sensible order either way.

questions.text: In a certain code language, “CODE” is written as “DCEO”, and “MAKE” is written as “KMEA”. How will “HEAD” be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters are taken in the order 3rd, 1st, 4th, 2nd: CODE → D C E O and MAKE → K M E A. So HEAD → A H D E: AHDE.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term 5 : 7 :: ? : 271 :: 22 : 466
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first minus 18: 5² − 18 = 7 and 22² − 18 = 466. As 17² − 18 = 271, the missing number is 17.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 7, 42, 47, ? , 191, 382
questions.explanation: The operations alternate: × 6, + 5, × 4, + 3, × 2. So 47 × 4 = 188, and 188 + 3 = 191.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term. 12 : 139 :: 7 : ? :: 18 : 319
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first minus 5: 12² − 5 = 139 and 18² − 5 = 319. Likewise 7² − 5 = 44.

questions.text: If A denotes ‘+’, B denotes ‘×’, C denotes ‘−’ and D denotes ‘÷’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? 92 A (121 D 11) C (6 B 3) D 2 A 7 B 8 = ?
Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? HMSE, BIPC, VEMA, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move back 6 (H, B, V, P), the second back 4 (M, I, E, A), the third back 3 (S, P, M, J) and the fourth back 2 (E, C, A, Y), wrapping round after A: PAJY.

questions.text: Seven friends P, Q, R, S, T, U and V, each has got different marks in the board examination. P scored higher than only U and R. R scored higher than U. Q scored higher than S but lesser than T. T has not scored the highest among all. How many persons scored between Q and R?
questions.explanation: P beat only U and R, and R beat U, so P, R and U are 5th, 6th and 7th. T is above Q, Q above S, and T is not first, so V is 1st, T 2nd, Q 3rd and S 4th. S and P come between Q and R: two persons.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 5 : 117 :: 6 : 208 :: 8 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the cube of the first minus 8: 5³ − 8 = 117 and 6³ − 8 = 208. Likewise 8³ − 8 = 504.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term. INSTEAD : NISTEDA :: JUSTICE : ? :: LIBERAL : ILBERLA
questions.explanation: The first two letters swap and so do the last two, the middle three staying put: IN STE AD → NI STE DA and LI BER AL → IL BER LA. So JU STI CE → UJ STI EC: UJSTIEC.

questions.text: The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number-pairs EXCEPT one. Find that odd number-pair.
questions.explanation: In 81 : 12, 64 : 11 and 100 : 13 the second number is the square root of the first plus 3 (9 + 3, 8 + 3, 10 + 3). √121 + 3 = 14, not 16, so 121 : 16 is the odd pair.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some pots are boxes. All stands are boxes. Some cartons are stands. Conclusions: I. Some cartons are boxes. II. Some cartons are pots. III. Some pots are stands.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: Some cartons are stands and all stands are boxes, so some cartons are boxes (I). Nothing links cartons or stands to the pots that are boxes, so neither II nor III need follow.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 60, 67, 81, 109, 165, ?
questions.explanation: The differences double each time: 7, 14, 28, 56, so the next is 112: 165 + 112 = 277.

questions.text: A single discount equivement to two successive discount of 20% and 10% on the marked price of an article is
questions.explanation: After 20% and then 10% off, 0.8 × 0.9 = 0.72 of the price is left: a single discount of 28%.

questions.text: The average of 25 numbers is 13. If the average of the first 13 numbers is 11.5 and the average of the last 13 numbers is 14.5, then the middle number is:
If the volume of a cube is 64 cm³, then find its total surface area.
questions.explanation: Side = ∛64 = 4 cm, so the total surface area is 6 × 4² = 96 cm².

questions.text: A student's marks were incorrectly entered as 94 instead of 69. Due to this error, the average marks of the class got increased by 1.25. What is the number of students in the class?
questions.explanation: The 25 extra marks (94 − 69) raised the average by 1.25, so the class has 25 ÷ 1.25 = 20 students.

questions.text: Shyamal covers 1 km in 10 min, whereas Radha covers the same distance in 8 min. By what distance does Radha beat Shyamal?
questions.explanation: When Radha finishes, after 8 minutes, Shyamal has covered 8/10 of 1 km = 800 m, so Radha wins by 200 m.

questions.text: The sum of the first 78 natural numbers from 1 to 78 is divisible by
questions.explanation: 1 + 2 + … + 78 = 78 × 79/2 = 39 × 79 = 3081, so the sum is divisible by 79. It is not divisible by 61, 29 or 30.

questions.text: The monthly income of two persons is in the ratio 4:5 and their expenditures are in the ratio 7:9. If each saves ₹50 per month, then their monthly incomes are:
questions.explanation: With incomes 4x and 5x and expenditures 7y and 9y: 4x − 7y = 50 and 5x − 9y = 50. Solving, y = 50 and x = 100, so the incomes are ₹400 and ₹500.

questions.text: The population of a country has been declining at 1% every decade. If the projected population of the country in 2030 is given as 1940598, what was the population of the country in 2000?
questions.explanation: Over three decades the population is multiplied by 0.99³ = 0.970299, so the 2000 population was 1940598 ÷ 0.970299 = 2000000.

questions.text: Giri bought an old machine for ₹2,000 and spent ₹500 on its repair. He sold it for ₹4,000. His profit percentage is:
If the length of a cuboid is 20 m, breadth is 5 m and height is 4 m, then find the length of diagonal of the cuboid.
If x = 32, y = 33 and z = 35, then evaluate the expression x³+ y³ + z³ – 3xyz.
In what ratio must a shopkeeper mix two types of rice worth ₹60 per kg and ₹80 per kg, so that the average cost of the mixture is ₹75 per kg?

The monthly income of a person was Rs12,000 and his monthly expenditure was Rs10,000. In the next year, his income increased by 12% and his expenditure by 5%. Find the percentage increase in his savings.
questions.explanation: Savings rise from ₹2,000 to ₹13,440 − ₹10,500 = ₹2,940, an increase of 940/2,000 = 47%.

questions.text: A shopkeeper gives a discount of 25% on a purse. If he gives a discount of 37%, he earns ₹120 less in profit. Find the marked price.
questions.explanation: The extra 12% discount (37% − 25%) costs ₹120 of profit, so 12% of the marked price is ₹120 and the marked price is ₹1,000.

questions.text: The volume of a sphere is 8 times that of another sphere. What is the ratio of the surface area of the bigger sphere to that of the other?
questions.explanation: Volumes in the ratio 8 : 1 mean radii in the ratio 2 : 1 (the cube root), so the surface areas are 2² : 1² = 4 : 1.

questions.text: Three numbers A, B and C are in the ratio of 15 : 21 : 27. The ratio of the difference between B and A to the difference between C and B is:
questions.explanation: B − A = 21 − 15 = 6 parts and C − B = 27 − 21 = 6 parts, so the ratio is 1 : 1.

questions.text: Which of the following countries will host the 35th Summer Olympics games in the year 2032?
questions.explanation: Brisbane, Australia, will host the 2032 Summer Olympics, the Games of the XXXV Olympiad.

questions.text: As of February 2022, __________ is the youngest Flex Award winner in the field of Indian classical music instrument Pakhawaj and has joined the Ali Akbar College of Music for his research in Pakhawaj under the guidance of Padma Shri Pandit Swapan Chaudhuri.
questions.explanation: Nishant (Nishaant) Singh, a pakhawaj player from Kalimpong, was reported in February 2022 as the youngest Flex Award winner on the pakhawaj; he joined the Ali Akbar College of Music in California to research under Pandit Swapan Chaudhuri.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the famous English classic novel ‘Pride and Prejudice’?
questions.explanation: 'Pride and Prejudice' (1813) is Jane Austen's novel. 'Jane Eyre' is a novel by Charlotte Brontë, not an author.

questions.text: Who among the following Indian Musicians and tabla players was the very first to be invited in 2016 by the then American President Barack Obama to attend the All-Star Global Concert held in the White House?
questions.explanation: The tabla maestro Zakir Hussain was invited by President Obama to the International Jazz Day All-Star Global Concert at the White House in April 2016.

questions.text: Padma shri Ananda Shankar Jayant, is renowned for her significant contributions to which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: Ananda Shankar Jayant is a Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancer and choreographer from Hyderabad.

questions.text: Which of the following techniques can be used to separate the impurities in Milk?
questions.explanation: Chromatography separates the components of a mixture by the different rates at which they move through a stationary phase. Microscopy and microtomy (cutting thin sections) examine samples, and an autoclave sterilises; none of them separates anything.

questions.text: Which of the following is 'George David Roberts’ thriller novel that is based on his own experience in Mumbai?
questions.explanation: 'Shantaram' (2003) is Gregory David Roberts's novel drawn from his years in Bombay (Mumbai) as a fugitive. (The paper prints his first name as 'George'.)

questions.text: Kishori Amonkar is famous for which of the following forms of music?
questions.explanation: Kishori Amonkar was a leading Hindustani classical vocalist of the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana.

questions.text: The Academic Bank of Credit (ABC) scheme, which was launched in ________________ 2021, aims at facilitating the academic mobility of students, giving them the freedom to study across the higher educational institutions in India with the help of a ‘credit scheme’ mechanism.
questions.explanation: The Academic Bank of Credit was launched on 29 July 2021, the first anniversary of the National Education Policy 2020.

questions.text: How many Primary Health Centres are there in rural areas of India as per 31st Macrh 2020 data?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 30,813. By the Rural Health Statistics 2019-20, India had 24,918 Primary Health Centres in rural areas and 5,895 in urban areas on 31 March 2020: 30,813 is the two together, so the key counts all PHCs, not only the rural ones.

questions.text: _______________ is one of the taxes, where the impact lies on the person for whom it is legally imposed.
questions.explanation: A direct tax, such as income tax, is paid by the person on whom it is imposed: its impact and incidence fall on the same person. An indirect tax, such as GST or VAT, can be passed on to others.

questions.text: Mrinalini Vikram Sarabhai, the Bharatanatyam and Kathakali legend has NOT received which of the following awards?
questions.explanation: Mrinalini Sarabhai received the Padma Shri in 1965, the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1970 and the Padma Bhushan in 1992, but never the Padma Vibhushan.

questions.text: In a resistor, what happens to the current when the resistance is doubled?
questions.explanation: By Ohm's law I = V/R, so at the same voltage doubling the resistance halves the current.

questions.text: Which is the tallest self-supporting moss species found in New Zealand that usually grows to a height of 60 cm?
questions.explanation: Dawsonia superba, found in New Zealand and Australia, is the world's tallest self-supporting moss, with stems up to about 50-60 cm tall.

questions.text: Arjuna’s Penance, a mammoth architecture with finely carved rock sculptures, serves as a venue for the Mamallapuram Dance Festival, in the backdrop of the ___________.
questions.explanation: Mamallapuram (Mahabalipuram), where Arjuna's Penance is carved, stands on the Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal, south of Chennai.

questions.text: _______ of the Constitution deals with the amendment procedure of the Constitution.
questions.explanation: Article 368, in Part XX, sets out Parliament's power to amend the Constitution and the procedure for doing so.

questions.text: ________ zone is generally defined as an environment with moderate rainfall throughout the year or parts of the year, with sporadic dry, mild to hot summers and cool to cold winters.
questions.explanation: Temperate zones, between the tropics and the polar circles, have moderate rainfall and distinct seasons, with warm summers and cool to cold winters.

questions.text: The Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puruskar 2021, for the identification and nurturing of budding and young talent, was given to ____________.
questions.explanation: Manav Rachna Educational Institution received the 2021 Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puruskar for the identification and nurturing of budding and young talent.

questions.text: Which Indian shuttler defeated World Champion Loh Kean Yew of Singapore in the Men's Singles final at the 2022 India Open?
questions.explanation: Lakshya Sen beat the reigning world champion Loh Kean Yew in straight games in the India Open final in January 2022.

questions.text: Identify the method that is NOT used to purify organic compounds.
questions.explanation: Sublimation, crystallisation and distillation are standard ways of purifying organic compounds. Sedimentation, letting solids settle out of a liquid, is not one of them.

questions.text: Where is the Green Park Stadium located?
questions.explanation: Green Park Stadium is a cricket ground in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh.

questions.text: ‘Revenue Stamp: An Autobiography’ is written by which of the following Indian poets, who was a prominent figure of Punjabi literature?
questions.explanation: 'Revenue Stamp' ('Rasidi Ticket') is the autobiography of the Punjabi poet and novelist Amrita Pritam.

questions.text: Falguni Pathak is a renowned singer known for which of the following genres?
questions.explanation: Falguni Pathak is known for Gujarati folk music, above all the garba and dandiya songs of Navratri.

questions.text: Guru Bipin Singh was a _________ dancer awarded with Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1966.
questions.explanation: Guru Bipin Singh was a leading teacher, choreographer and scholar of Manipuri dance.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them contains a grammatical error. Select the option that has the error. He continued staring at the elephant, as if he had not see one before.
options: as if he had not see
questions.explanation: After 'had not' the verb takes its past participle: 'as if he had not seen one before'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. A visit “in” Ladhak is a must these days.
questions.explanation: One pays a visit 'to' a place: 'A visit to Ladhak is a must these days.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The NCERT “was set up ahead” by the government to assist and advise the Central and State Governments on policies and programmes for qualitative improvement in school education.
questions.explanation: To 'set up' an organisation is to establish it, and 'ahead' adds nothing: 'The NCERT was set up by the government'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option fill in the blank. I have been studying this course ______ two years now.
questions.explanation: A period of time takes 'for': 'for two years now'. 'Since' goes with a point in time.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Incite
questions.explanation: To 'incite' is to stir up or provoke: to 'inflame'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice This match is being watched today by more than thirty-three million people worldwide.
options: This match is watching more than thirty-three million people worldwide today.
More than thirty-three million people worldwide have been watching this match today.
More than thirty-three million people worldwide are watching this match today.
Today more than thirty-three million people worldwide have watched this match.
questions.explanation: The present continuous passive 'is being watched by' becomes the active 'are watching', with the agent as the subject: 'More than thirty-three million people worldwide are watching this match today.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Sum and substance
questions.explanation: The 'sum and substance' of something is its essence or gist.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A.The current concern is that it is rising day by day due to various resources of pollutants. B.It has been there in different forms since a long time, even before human evolution, such as volcanic eruptions, wildfire which led to various photochemical reactions in the atmosphere. C.Pollution has become a very common yet serious issue in today’s world. D.And, one of the main pollutants are humans and man-made machines.
questions.explanation: C introduces pollution as a serious issue, B says it has existed in natural forms since before humans, A turns to the current concern that it is rising, and D names humans and machines as main pollutants: CBAD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Under duress
questions.explanation: 'Under duress' means under pressure or threat.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Apple of one’s eye
questions.explanation: The 'apple of one's eye' is someone very dear to one.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Direct and outspoken
questions.explanation: A forthright person is direct and outspoken. Fortitude is courage in adversity, and to fortify is to strengthen.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Pretence
questions.explanation: 'Pretence' is a false show; its opposite is 'reality'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'repetition'.

questions.text: Spot the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the options given. Is Savita is joining us for lunch today?
options: Is Savita joining us for lunch today?
Savita is joined us for lunch today?
Savita joining us for lunch today?
Are Savita joining us for lunch today?
questions.explanation: A present continuous question needs 'is' only once, before the subject: 'Is Savita joining us for lunch today?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Precocious
questions.explanation: 'Precocious' means developed earlier than usual; its opposite is 'backward', slow to develop.

questions.text: Complete the collocation. I met my professor yesterday and we _____ a long conversation about books and work.
questions.explanation: 'Have a conversation' is the set collocation; 'did' does not go with 'conversation', and 'spoke' and 'talked' do not take it as an object.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Fleck
questions.explanation: A 'fleck' is a small mark or patch: a 'spot'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The finance minister will announce the budget.
options: The budget will have announced by the finance minister.
The budget were announced by the finance minister.
The budget are announced by the finance minister.
The budget will be announced by the finance minister.
questions.explanation: The future active 'will announce' becomes 'will be announced': 'The budget will be announced by the finance minister.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Allowing or assisting to discover
questions.explanation: 'Heuristic' describes a method that helps or allows a learner to discover things for themselves.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The most urgent areas of attention and immediate action are nutrition, health and education of children, whose well-being (1)__________ the health of the society and caring outlook of the polity. Since the causes of malnutrition of children are many, like exploding population, (2)__________ against the female child, weak and suffering mothers, the remedy calls for ‘care of the mother and care by mother’,(3)__________, an effective control over population explosion. Ignorance on what food should be taken is another (4)__________ factor that results in malnutrition among women and children. The implementation of various schemes to fight the (5)__________ of malnutrition and undernourishment of children requires planning, co-ordination and monitoring by high-powered bodies right down to the village level.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Children's well-being 'reflects', that is shows, the health of the society.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The most urgent areas of attention and immediate action are nutrition, health and education of children, whose well-being (1)__________ the health of the society and caring outlook of the polity. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Bias against the female child' is one of the causes of child malnutrition listed.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Ignorance about food is another 'contributory' factor, one that helps cause malnutrition.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The most urgent areas of attention and immediate action are nutrition, health and education of children, whose well-being (1)__________ the health of the society and caring outlook of the polity. Since the causes of malnutrition of children are many, like exploding population, (2)__________ against the female child, weak and suffering mothers, the remedy calls for ‘care of the mother and care by mother’,(3)__________, an effective control over population explosion. Ignorance on what food should be taken is another (4)__________ factor that results in malnutrition among women and children. The implementation of various schemes to fight the (5)__________ of malnutrition and undernourishment of children requires planning, co-ordination and monitoring by high-powered bodies right down to the village level.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: To fight the 'menace', the threat or danger, of malnutrition.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 176, 218, 228, 291, 280, 364, 332, ?
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 176, 228, 280, 332 (+52 each) and 218, 291, 364 (+73 each). The next term is 364 + 73 = 437.

questions.text: The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) is/are followed in all the number-pairs, except one. Find that odd number-pair.
questions.explanation: In 48 : 7, 15 : 4 and 8 : 3 the second number is the square root of one more than the first: √49 = 7, √16 = 4, √9 = 3. For 25 that gives √26, not 8, so 25 : 8 is the odd one.

questions.text: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark(?) to complete the given series? EMXB, ?, YGRV, VDOS, SALP
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back: EMXB → BJUY → YGRV → VDOS → SALP.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 24*6*51*31*3
Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term. 5 : 35 :: 9 : ? :: 14 : 224
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by two more than itself: 5 × 7 = 35 and 14 × 16 = 224. Likewise 9 × 11 = 99.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1. Knight 2. Kitchen 3. Kinship 4. Kinetic 5. Kind
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Kind (5), Kinetic (4), Kinship (3), Kitchen (2), Knight (1). 'Kind' comes before 'Kine', 'Kine' before 'Kins', 'Kin' before 'Kit', and 'Ki' before 'Kn'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 7 : 71::13 : 209::16 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the first times three more than itself, plus 1: 7 × 10 + 1 = 71 and 13 × 16 + 1 = 209. Likewise 16 × 19 + 1 = 305.

questions.text: In a certain code language, “NOPE” is coded as “100”, and “EGG” is coded as “38”. How will “LAP” be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each code is twice the sum of the letters' positions in the alphabet: NOPE = 2 × (14 + 15 + 16 + 5) = 100 and EGG = 2 × (5 + 7 + 7) = 38. So LAP = 2 × (12 + 1 + 16) = 58.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'STATE' is written as '38401405' and 'EXILE' is written as 5489245'. How will ‘ARENA’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each consonant is written as twice its position in the alphabet and each vowel as its position: S T A T E → 38 40 1 40 5 and E X I L E → 5 48 9 24 5. So A R E N A → 1 36 5 28 1: 1365281.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. BIRTHDAY : HDAYBIRT :: CHILDREN : DRENCHIL :: PROGRESS : ?
questions.explanation: The two halves of the word swap places: BIRT HDAY → HDAYBIRT and CHIL DREN → DRENCHIL. So PROG RESS → RESSPROG.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All huts are houses. No villa is a house. Some buildings are villas. Conclusions: I. Some buildings are huts. II. Some houses are buildings. III. No hut is a villa.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: Every hut is a house and no villa is a house, so no hut is a villa (III). The buildings that are villas cannot be houses, and nothing says any other building is a hut or a house, so I and II need not follow.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 5, 16, 28, 36, 71, 90, 234, 342, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 11, 12, 8, 35, 19, 144, 108, and each differs from the one before by +1³, −2², +3³, −4², +5³, −6² in turn. The next difference is 108 + 7³ = 451, so the term is 342 + 451 = 793.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 16*2*4*8*10*34
Select the option that represents the letters that, when sequentially placed from left to right in the blanks below, will complete the letter series. t u _ _ x _ _ _ u u_ _ x y _ _ _ v x x _
options: u v x y u v x t u u y
u v x x t v x t u u y
u v x y t v x t u u y
u v x y t v x t u u u
questions.explanation: With u, v, x, y, t, v, x, t, u, u, y in the blanks the block tuuvxxy repeats three times: tuuvxxy tuuvxxy tuuvxxy.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation 104*26*13*7*18*77
In a certain code language, ‘THREE’ is written as ‘UISFF’, and ‘SEVEN’ is written as ‘TFWFO’. How will ‘EIGHT’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: THREE → UISFF and SEVEN → TFWFO. So EIGHT → FJHIU.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 58,117,237,479,965,?
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before plus the next odd number: 58 × 2 + 1 = 117, 117 × 2 + 3 = 237, 237 × 2 + 5 = 479, 479 × 2 + 7 = 965, so 965 × 2 + 9 = 1939.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 12, 32,123,609,?
A train crosses a 400 m-long platform in 50 seconds. It crosses another 600 m-long platform in 60 seconds. What are the length and the speed of the train?
questions.explanation: The extra 200 m of platform takes 10 more seconds, so the speed is 20 m/s = 72 km/h. In 50 seconds the train covers 1,000 m, its length plus 400 m, so it is 600 m long.

questions.text: The curved surface area of a hemisphere is 1232 cm². Its radius will be: (Take π=22/7)
questions.explanation: The curved surface area of a hemisphere is 2πr²: 2 × 22/7 × r² = 1232, so r² = 196 and r = 14 cm.

questions.text: The population of a city increases 5% annually in compounded manner (yearly compounding). The present population of this city is 93051. The population of this city 2 years ago was:
questions.explanation: Two years ago the population was 93051 ÷ (1.05)² = 93051 ÷ 1.1025 = 84400.

questions.text: Asha and Bhuvan can do a piece of work in 6 days and 9 days, respectively. They work on alternate days, starting with Asha on the first day. In how many days will the work be completed?
questions.explanation: Asha does 1/6 and Bhuvan 1/9 of the work a day, so each two-day pair does 5/18. After 6 days 15/18 is done, and on day 7 Asha does the remaining 3/18 = 1/6.

questions.text: The ratio of measures of the angles of a triangle is given as 3 : 4 : 8. What is the measure of the smallest of the three angles?
questions.explanation: The angles add up to 180°, so the smallest is 3/15 × 180° = 36°.

questions.text: The marked price of a refrigerator is ₹60,000. A shopkeeper offers a flat discount of ₹12,000 on full cash payment. Further he offers an extra discount of 5% on the marked price to his regular customers. How much does a regular customer have to pay for the refrigerator?
Soham’s initial expenditure and savings were in the ratio 5: 1. His income increases by 25%, while his savings increase by 20%. If Soham’s current expenditure is ₹4,347, what was his initial income?
questions.explanation: With expenditure 5x and savings x, income was 6x. Now income is 7.5x and savings 1.2x, so expenditure is 6.3x = ₹4,347 and x = 690. Initial income = 6 × 690 = ₹4,140.

questions.text: A 25% profit is made when a discount of 25% is given on the marked price of an item. When the discount is 35%, what will be the profit? (Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.)
questions.explanation: Take the marked price as 100. At 25% off it sells for 75, a 25% profit, so the cost is 60. At 35% off it sells for 65: a profit of 5/60 = 8.33%, about 8%.

questions.text: What is the remainder when 8127 is divided by 8?
questions.explanation: 8127 = 8 × 1015 + 7, so the remainder is 7. (Only the last three digits matter: 127 = 8 × 15 + 7.)

questions.text: If a ∶ b = 2 ∶ 3 and b ∶ c = 6 ∶ 8, then find a ∶ b ∶ c.
questions.explanation: b : c = 6 : 8 = 3 : 4, and b is 3 in both ratios, so a : b : c = 2 : 3 : 4.

questions.text: In what ratio must a grocer mix two varieties of pulses costing ₹15 and ₹20 per kg, respectively, so as to get a mixture worth ₹18 per kg?
The average of the first 43 natural numbers is:
questions.explanation: The average of 1 to n is (n + 1)/2 = 44/2 = 22.

questions.text: If x + y = 14, then the value of x³ + y³ + 42xy is:
questions.explanation: x³ + y³ = (x + y)³ − 3xy(x + y) = 2744 − 42xy, so x³ + y³ + 42xy = 14³ = 2744.

questions.text: If the length and the breadth of a rectangle are increased by 15% and 20%, respectively, then by how much percent the area of the rectangle will increase?
questions.explanation: 1.15 × 1.20 = 1.38, so the area increases by 38%.

questions.text: A pen was sold for ₹28.75 at a profit of 15%. If it was sold for ₹25.75, then what would have been the percentage of profit?
questions.explanation: Cost price = 28.75 ÷ 1.15 = ₹25. Selling for ₹25.75 gives a profit of ₹0.75, which is 3% of ₹25.

questions.text: In animal cells, which membrane-bound cell organelles are generally smaller and help to separate waste products?
questions.explanation: Vacuoles are membrane-bound storage sacs, small in animal cells and large in plant cells; some store or expel wastes and excess water.

questions.text: The Men's Hockey World Cup 2023 will be organised by which of the following states?
questions.explanation: The 2023 Men's Hockey World Cup was held in Odisha, at Bhubaneswar and Rourkela.

questions.text: Agumbe, a biodiversity-rich region that receives 7640 mm of average annual rainfall in South India, is located in which state?
questions.explanation: Agumbe, in the Western Ghats in Karnataka's Shivamogga district, is one of the wettest places in South India.

questions.text: What resource is found in sedimentary rocks on the western and eastern flanks of the peninsula in Gujarat?
questions.explanation: Petroleum occurs in sedimentary rocks; Gujarat's oil fields, such as Ankleshwar, lie in such basins.

questions.text: ‘Sense and Sensibility’, ‘Mansfield Park’ and ‘Emma’ are written by whom among the following authors?
questions.explanation: 'Sense and Sensibility', 'Mansfield Park' and 'Emma' are novels by Jane Austen.

questions.text: The 8th T20 Women’s Cricket World Cup will be organised by _________.
questions.explanation: The eighth ICC Women's T20 World Cup was held in South Africa in February 2023.

questions.text: Famous musician Shakoor Khan was associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.explanation: Ustad Shakoor Khan, of the Kirana gharana, was one of the leading sarangi players of the twentieth century.

questions.text: A candidate seeking election as Vice-President is required to make a security deposit of _____.
questions.explanation: Under the Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952, a candidate for Vice-President must deposit ₹15,000, as must a candidate for President.

questions.text: Which ecologist’s research provided revolutionary new insights into how energy and nutrients move through the ecosystems?
questions.explanation: Raymond Lindeman's 1942 paper 'The Trophic-Dynamic Aspect of Ecology' showed how energy flows through an ecosystem's trophic levels.

questions.text: Metabolic reactions in our body are carried out by:
questions.explanation: Metabolic reactions are catalysed by enzymes, and almost all enzymes are proteins.

questions.text: Famous classical dancer Vidyagauri Adkar is recognised with ____________ Gharana of Indian classical dance form.
questions.explanation: Vidyagauri Adkar is a Kathak dancer of the Jaipur gharana.

questions.text: Identify the component that is unique only to prokaryotes.
questions.explanation: A mesosome, an infolding of the cell membrane, is found only in prokaryotic cells such as bacteria. A nucleus and nuclear membrane belong to eukaryotes, and both kinds of cell have chromosomes.

questions.text: Tansen, one of the well-known musicians of medieval India, was in the court of which of the following Mughal emperors?
questions.explanation: Tansen was the leading musician at the court of Akbar.

questions.text: Which journalist’s autobiography is titled the ‘Devil’s Advocate: The untold story’?
questions.explanation: 'Devil's Advocate: The Untold Story' (2018) is the memoir of the journalist Karan Thapar.

questions.text: In January 2022, which Indian state received a loan of ₹1,000 crores for the protection of social services from the World Bank?
questions.explanation: In January 2022 the World Bank approved a $125 million loan (about ₹1,000 crore) to help West Bengal's poor and vulnerable people reach social protection services.

questions.text: Ustad Alla Rakha is famous for his contribution to playing which of the following instruments in Indian Music?
questions.explanation: Ustad Alla Rakha was a tabla maestro, and the father of the tabla player Zakir Hussain.

questions.text: Guru Shyama Charan Pati, was conferred the Padma Shri for his contributions to mainly which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: Guru Shyama Charan Pati of Jharkhand was a leading exponent of the Seraikela style of Chhau.

questions.text: The famous novel ‘Pinjar’ based on riots during the Indian independence, was written by ________.
questions.explanation: Amrita Pritam's Punjabi novel 'Pinjar' (1950) is set against the riots of Partition.

questions.text: Identify the plant that shows adaptation through leaves that are reduced to spines.
questions.explanation: In Opuntia, a cactus, the leaves are reduced to spines to cut water loss, and the flattened green stem carries out photosynthesis.

questions.text: Which of the following Hindustani musical Gharanas is the oldest among all the Khayal Gayaki styles?
questions.explanation: The Gwalior gharana is the oldest of the khayal gharanas.

questions.text: Which of the following organisations won the Etienne Glichitch Award in May 2021?
options: Board of Control for Cricket in India
questions.explanation: In May 2021 the FIH gave Hockey India its Etienne Glichitch Award for its contribution to the growth and development of hockey.

questions.text: The title of Asthana Narthaki (‘Resident Dancer’) was bestowed upon by the Tirumala Tirupathi Devasthanam temple to whom among the following prominent dancer?
questions.explanation: Yamini Krishnamurthy, the Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancer, was made the Asthana Narthaki of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams.

questions.text: Banks issue KCC to support credit in agriculture. KCC stands for ____________.
questions.explanation: KCC is the Kisan Credit Card, which gives farmers short-term credit for growing crops.

questions.text: Who among the following Indian Cricketers (Female) won Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award 2021?
questions.explanation: Mithali Raj was among the sportspersons given the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna in 2021.

questions.text: Who among the following is the recipient of Sangeet Natak Akademi for Bharatanatyam?
questions.explanation: Geeta Chandran received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Bharatanatyam for 2016; Anita Ratnam's award that year was for contemporary dance.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. She will be / write her / examination by this / time tomorrow.
questions.explanation: After 'will be' the verb takes the -ing form: 'She will be writing her examination by this time tomorrow.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Something that is pertaining to controversy
questions.explanation: 'Polemical' means relating to controversy or heated argument. 'Laudatory' means praising, and 'putative' means supposed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The children sat _________ the tables instead of the chairs.
questions.explanation: Resting on top of a surface takes 'on': the children sat on the tables instead of on the chairs.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person as a source of intellectual light or moral inspiration
questions.explanation: A luminary is a person who inspires or enlightens others. A luminaire is a light fitting, and a lunette a crescent-shaped window or space.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Impudent
questions.explanation: 'Impudent' means rudely disrespectful; its opposite is 'polite'. 'Insolent' is a synonym.

questions.text: Complete the sentence with an appropriate synonym of the word mentioned in the bracket. Watching the setting sun and the _________________ (tranquil) surface of the water relaxes my mind.
questions.explanation: 'Tranquil' means peaceful and still: 'calm'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word
questions.explanation: 'Whipe' is misspelt: the word is 'wipe'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'wisdom': 'wise' drops its 'e' before '-dom'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We love to go to the ____.
questions.explanation: We go to the 'sea'; 'see' sounds the same but is a verb.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To pay lip service
options: To express loyalty, respect, or support for something insincerely
To pretend to be very old
To ignore what someone is saying
questions.explanation: To 'pay lip service' to something is to express support for it in words without really meaning it.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Rhea and Heena are both great dancers, “but Rhea is the best.”
options: but Rhea is one of the best
and yet both of are equally good at it
questions.explanation: Comparing two people takes the comparative degree: 'Rhea is better'. 'The best' is for three or more.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. In the theatre, the audience threw flowers on the screen.
options: In the theatre, flowers were thrown by the audience.
In the theatre, flowers had been thrown by the audience.
In the theatre, flowers was thrown by the audience.
In the theatre, flowers are thrown by the audience.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'threw' becomes 'were thrown', plural to agree with 'flowers'. (Every option leaves out 'on the screen'.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined part in the given sentence. This rule is “necesary” to maintain discipline.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'necessary': one 'c' and a double 's'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. William Shakespeare and Christopher Marlowe, the two great playwrights of the Elizabethan era, were “living in the same time period.”
questions.explanation: Contemporaries are people who live or work in the same period.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Judicious
questions.explanation: 'Judicious' means showing good judgement; its opposite is 'foolish'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Every dog has his day
options: Celebration of dogs as man’s best friend
Everyone has good luck or success at a point of time
questions.explanation: 'Every dog has his day' means that everyone gets a spell of good luck or success at some time.

questions.text: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Very carefully I ______ the tree I have referred to, and avoiding contact with the creepers, the upper _______ and leaves of which might have been visible from where the tiger was lying, I climbed to the fork, where I had a comfortable seat and perfect _________.
questions.explanation: He 'stalked' (approached stealthily) the tree, kept clear of the creepers whose upper 'tendrils' might have been seen, and sat in perfect 'concealment' from the tiger.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Come about
questions.explanation: 'Come about' means to happen: 'How did this come about?'

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. The Taj Mahal's history is also one of the world's greatest love stories known to everyone. B. She was the neice of Meherunissa who was married to Prince Salim (later the Empress Nur Jahan.) C. It all started in 1607, when Mughal Prince Khurram, first laid eyes on the lovely Arjumand Banu Begum. D. Khurram, the son of Emperor Jahangir, voiced his wish to marry Arjumand, and their marriage was celebrated with great pomp.
questions.explanation: A introduces the love story, C begins it with Khurram first seeing Arjumand in 1607, B says who she was, and D tells of their marriage: ACBD.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The (1) ___________ that comes out of the story The Grasshopper and the Ant has to be subtly put to the children in such a way (2) ___________ they realise the worth of hard work, the pleasures of hard work and the comfort it offers. Laziness, which is a (3) __________ trait here, should be discouraged, (4) ___________ emphasizing on the (5) ___________ note which is hard work.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The 'value' that comes out of the story is its lesson, the worth of hard work. ('Morals' is plural and does not agree with 'comes'.)

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The (1) ___________ that comes out of the story The Grasshopper and the Ant has to be subtly put to the children in such a way (2) ___________ they realise the worth of hard work, the pleasures of hard work and the comfort it offers. Laziness, which is a (3) __________ trait here, should be discouraged, (4) ___________ emphasizing on the (5) ___________ note which is hard work.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'In such a way that' introduces the result: they realise the worth of hard work.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The (1) ___________ that comes out of the story The Grasshopper and the Ant has to be subtly put to the children in such a way (2) ___________ they realise the worth of hard work, the pleasures of hard work and the comfort it offers. Laziness, which is a (3) __________ trait here, should be discouraged, (4) ___________ emphasizing on the (5) ___________ note which is hard work.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3
questions.explanation: Laziness is a 'negative' trait, set against the 'positive note' of hard work later in the sentence.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The (1) ___________ that comes out of the story The Grasshopper and the Ant has to be subtly put to the children in such a way (2) ___________ they realise the worth of hard work, the pleasures of hard work and the comfort it offers. Laziness, which is a (3) __________ trait here, should be discouraged, (4) ___________ emphasizing on the (5) ___________ note which is hard work.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'While' joins two things done together: discouraging laziness while emphasising hard work.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The (1) ___________ that comes out of the story The Grasshopper and the Ant has to be subtly put to the children in such a way (2) ___________ they realise the worth of hard work, the pleasures of hard work and the comfort it offers. Laziness, which is a (3) __________ trait here, should be discouraged, (4) ___________ emphasizing on the (5) ___________ note which is hard work.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Hard work is the 'positive' note, in contrast with the negative trait of laziness.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 25*5*10*2*4*3

The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs except one. Find that odd number pair.

Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All apples are bananas. All grapes are bananas. All bananas are nuts. Conclusions: I. All apples are nuts. II. All grapes are nuts. III. No nuts are bananas.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: All apples and all grapes are bananas, and all bananas are nuts, so all apples and all grapes are nuts (I and II). Some nuts are bananas, so III does not follow.

questions.text: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? XYZA, YACE,?, AEIM, BGLQ
questions.explanation: First letters run X, Y, Z, A, B; second letters move +2 (Y, A, C, E, G); third letters +3 (Z, C, F, I, L); fourth letters +4 (A, E, I, M, Q). The missing cluster is ZCFI.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘SCHOOL’ is written as ‘TDIPPM’ and ‘COLLEGE’ is written as ‘DPMMFHF’. How will ‘UNIVERSITY’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: SCHOOL → TDIPPM and COLLEGE → DPMMFHF. So UNIVERSITY → VOJWFSTJUZ.

questions.text: If 26 January 2019 was Saturday, then what was the day of the week on 30 January 2022?
questions.explanation: From 26 January 2019 to 26 January 2022 is 3 years with one leap day (29 February 2020): 4 odd days, so 26 January 2022 was a Wednesday. Four days later, 30 January, was a Sunday.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. ACCURATE : RATEACCU :: ANALYSIS : YSISANAL :: CAPACITY : ?
questions.explanation: The last four letters move to the front: ACCU RATE → RATEACCU and ANAL YSIS → YSISANAL. So CAPA CITY → CITYCAPA.

questions.text: In a certain code language, “ABROAD” is written as “BDUNYA”, and “BECAME” is written as “CGFZKB”. How will “CANCER” be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, +2, +3, −1, −2, −3: ABROAD → BDUNYA and BECAME → CGFZKB. So CANCER → DCQBCO.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 13, 26, 23, ?, 87, 522

options: s r t r a r t s a
s r a r s r t s a
s r t r s r t s t
s r t r s r t s a

questions.text: If P denotes ‘×’, Q denotes ‘÷’, R denotes ‘+’ and S denotes ‘−’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? 130 S 61 R (23 P 4) S 83 R (62 Q 2) = ?
