It did not sing, and sat (5)_________ silent.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The past participle is needed: a hut 'built of thatch and grey clay'. 'Build' is the base form.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A question like "How big is Faerie?” does not admit (1)_________ a simple answer. Faerie, after all, is not one land, one principality or (2)_________ Maps of Faerie are unreliable, and may not be (3)_________ upon. Faerie is bigger than England, as it is bigger than the world. In the middle of a wood so thick it was very nearly a forest was a small hut, (4)_________ of thatch and grey clay. A yellow bird in a cage sat on its perch outside the house. It did not sing, and sat (5)_________ silent.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The bird 'did not sing', so it sat 'mournfully' (sadly) silent; 'blissfully', 'gaily' and 'chirpily' all suggest cheerfulness.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 25*5*10*2*8*56

Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. FLOWERS : OLFWSRE :: HOSTILE : SOHTELI :: IMPORTS : ?
questions.explanation: The first three letters are reversed, the middle letter stays and the last three are reversed: FLO W ERS → OLF W SRE and HOS T ILE → SOH T ELI. So IMP O RTS → PMI O STR: PMIOSTR.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 375 : 592 ::423 :640 :: 198 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the first plus 217: 375 + 217 = 592 and 423 + 217 = 640. Likewise 198 + 217 = 415.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 13, 78, 83, ?, 335, 670
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 5, 8, 24, 57, 109, 184, 288, 423, ?
questions.explanation: The differences 3, 16, 33, 52, 75, 104, 135 grow by 13, 17, 19, 23, 29, 31, the prime numbers. The next prime is 37, so the next difference is 135 + 37 = 172: 423 + 172 = 595.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term. 56 : 217 :: 38 : ? :: 73 : 285
questions.explanation: The second number is 4 times the first minus 7: 4 × 56 − 7 = 217 and 4 × 73 − 7 = 285. Likewise 4 × 38 − 7 = 145.

questions.text: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? OSRE, QOXH, SKDK, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +2 (O, Q, S, U), second letters −4 (S, O, K, G), third letters +6 (R, X, D, J, wrapping round after Z) and fourth letters +3 (E, H, K, N): UGJN.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 7 : 105 :: 9 : 153 :: 13 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the first times (the first + 8): 7 × 15 = 105 and 9 × 17 = 153. Likewise 13 × 21 = 273.

questions.text: If 11 July 2020 was Monday, what will be 14 October 2028?
questions.explanation: 11 July 2020 to 11 July 2028 is 8 years with two leap days (29 February 2024 and 2028): 10 odd days, or 3. 11 July to 14 October 2028 is 20 + 31 + 30 + 14 = 95 days, 4 odd days. 3 + 4 = 7, whole weeks, so it is again a Monday.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'PUNCH' is written as 'IDOVQ' and ‘CRACK’ is written as ‘LDBSD’. How will ‘BREAK’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and each letter moved one place forward: PUNCH → HCNUP → IDOVQ and CRACK → KCARC → LDBSD. So BREAK → KAERB → LBFSC.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 24, 48, 45, ?, 175, 1050

Seven friends A,B,C,D,E,F and G, each has a different height. A is shorter than B but taller than C. B is taller than only four others. E is taller than G but shorter than C. D is taller than B but shorter than F. Who is the tallest among all?
questions.explanation: B is taller than only four others, so two are taller than B. D is taller than B and F is taller than D, so F is the tallest.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All pillows are beds. No table is a bed. Some tables are chairs. Conclusions: I. No pillow is a table. II. Some chairs are pillows. III. No bed is a chair.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.
questions.explanation: All pillows are beds and no table is a bed, so no pillow is a table (I). Nothing ties the chairs to the pillows, or rules out chairs that are beds, so neither II nor III follows.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row- 5, 6, 19 Second row- 7, 7, 35 Third row- 8, 9, ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: In each row, first × second − (first + second) = third: 5 × 6 − 11 = 19 and 7 × 7 − 14 = 35. So 8 × 9 − 17 = 55.

questions.text: If M denotes ‘−’, N denotes ‘÷’, O denotes ‘×’ and P denotes ‘+’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? (16 O 7) P 124 M 92 P (86 N 43) O 18 M 29 = ?
In a certain code language, “AN” is coded as “16”, and “NO” is coded as “212”. How will “US” be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is the product of the letters' alphabet positions plus 2: AN = 1 × 14 + 2 = 16 and NO = 14 × 15 + 2 = 212. So US = 21 × 19 + 2 = 401.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? YXV, TSQ, ONL, JIG, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 5 places back from one cluster to the next: Y, T, O, J, E; X, S, N, I, D; V, Q, L, G, B. The next cluster is EDB.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 67,83,71,91,80,118,?
questions.explanation: Two series alternate. 67, 71, 80 grow by 2² and 3², so the next term is 80 + 4² = 96; 83, 91, 118 grow by 2³ and 3³.

questions.text: In an election, there were three candidates: A, B and C. 10% of the eligible voters did not vote. Out of those who voted, 45% voted for A, 35% voted for B and the remaining 20% voted for C. 30% of the votes polled for A and 20% of the votes polled for B were later deemed invalid, while all the votes polled for C were deemed valid. If A got 882 more valid votes than B did, how many valid votes did C receive?
questions.explanation: If V people voted, A's valid votes are 0.7 × 0.45V = 0.315V and B's 0.8 × 0.35V = 0.28V. 0.035V = 882, so V = 25,200, and C's votes, all valid, are 0.2 × 25,200 = 5,040.

questions.text: The frustum of a right circular cone has the radius of the base as 5 cm, radius of the top as 3 cm, and height as 6 cm. What is its volume?
Find the total surface area of a closed hemisphere whose radius is 3.5 cm. (Use π=22/7)
questions.explanation: A closed hemisphere has a curved surface of 2πr² and a flat face of πr²: 3πr² = 3 × 22/7 × 3.5 × 3.5 = 115.5 cm².

questions.text: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 650 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at the rate of 8 km and 10.5 km per hour, respectively. The distance (in metres) between them after 12 minutes is:
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 10.5 − 8 = 2.5 km/h, so in 12 minutes (1/5 hour) he closes 0.5 km = 500 m. 650 − 500 = 150 m.

questions.text: The price of a cell phone is ₹20,000. On Sundays, the shopkeeper offers a cash discount of ₹1,000 on the purchase of the cell phone. Further, if someone purchases it through a credit card, he gives 5% additional discount. If someone is purchasing the cell phone on a Sunday through a credit card, then how much does he/she have to pay?
The price of a tablet is first increased by 10%, and then decreased by 2.5% due to reduction in sales. What is the net percentage change in the final price of the tablet?
What is the fourth proportional to 16, 24, 8?
The volume of a cone of radius 13 cm is 507 π cm³. Find its height.

Subir claimed to sell his items at only 5% above the cost of production, but used a weight that had 1 kg written on it, though it actually weighed 960 grams. What was the actual profit percentage earned by Subir?
When f(x) = 15x³ – 14x² – 4x + 10 is divided by (3x + 2), then the remainder is:
The average present age of four members of a family is 27 years and average increases by 3 years when one of their relatives joins them. The age of the relative is:
questions.explanation: Five members averaging 30 total 150; the four totalled 4 × 27 = 108. The relative is 150 − 108 = 42 years.

questions.text: In an engineering institution, a student’s grade is assessed based on Internal tests (30%), assignments (30%) and external exams (40%). If a student scored 90% in internal tests, 95% in assignments and 75% in the external exams, then the overall grade of the student is:
30 men can complete a piece of work in 24 days. 12 days after they started working together, 10 more men joined them. How many days will they now take to complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation: The work is 30 × 24 = 720 man-days, of which 30 × 12 = 360 are done in 12 days. The other 360 take 40 men 360/40 = 9 days.

questions.text: The difference between a discount of 35% on ₹8,000 and two successive discounts of 20% and 15% on the same amount is:
questions.explanation: 35% of ₹8,000 is ₹2,800. Successive discounts of 20% and 15% leave 0.8 × 0.85 = 0.68, a discount of 32% or ₹2,560. The difference is ₹240.

questions.text: What is the largest 6-digit number divisible by 52?
questions.explanation: 999999 = 52 × 19230 + 39, so the largest 6-digit multiple of 52 is 999999 − 39 = 999960.

questions.text: The average speed of a train running at a speed of 30 km/h during the first 100 km, at the speed of 40 km/h during the second 100 km and at the speed of 50 km/h during the last 100 km is nearly ________.
questions.explanation: Time = 100/30 + 100/40 + 100/50 = 47/6 hours for 300 km, so the average speed is 300 × 6/47 = 1800/47 ≈ 38.3 km/h.

questions.text: The population of a country has been growing at a rate of 4% every decade. If the projected population of the country in 2030 is given as 1,58,18,400, what was the population of the country in 2000?
Sheikh Chinna Moula was an exponent of the ________, a musical instrument.
questions.explanation: Sheikh Chinna Moula was a celebrated player of the nadaswaram, the double-reed wind instrument of South Indian temple music; born in Andhra Pradesh, he settled at Srirangam in Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: In which year was India the host of Commonwealth Games?
questions.explanation: India has hosted the Commonwealth Games once, in Delhi in 2010.

questions.text: Which vitamins are present in Milk?
questions.explanation: Milk supplies vitamin A, B vitamins such as riboflavin (B2) and B12, and vitamin D (often added by fortification); it has very little vitamin C.

questions.text: Which ministry launched an All-India dance competition 'Vande Bharatam Nritya Utsav' as part of Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav?
questions.explanation: Vande Bharatam Nritya Utsav, a nationwide dance competition held in 2021 under Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav, was run by the Ministry of Culture with the Ministry of Defence; its winners danced at the Republic Day parade of 2022.

questions.text: SLR is an important tool used by RBI to control money supply in the economy. The full form of SLR is ____________________.
questions.explanation: SLR, the Statutory Liquidity Ratio, is the share of their net demand and time liabilities that banks must keep in liquid assets such as cash, gold and government securities.

questions.text: In November 2021, under the Atma Nirbhar Bharat Abhiyan, the Central Government has approved the SPV that would privatise the electricity distribution business in which of the following Union Territories?
options: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
questions.explanation: In November 2021 the Union Cabinet approved a special purpose vehicle to take over electricity distribution in Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu and transfer a majority stake in it to a private bidder.

questions.text: As per statistics published by National Crime Records Bureau for 2020, which state registered the second highest number of crimes against women [Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Special and Local Laws (SLL)]?
questions.explanation: In NCRB's 'Crime in India 2020', Uttar Pradesh recorded the most crimes against women and West Bengal the second most, followed by Rajasthan.

questions.text: 'The Man Who Made the Elephant Dance by Kurien’ is the audio autobiography of ____.
questions.explanation: 'The Man Who Made the Elephant Dance' is the audio autobiography of Verghese Kurien, who led India's White Revolution in milk through Amul and the National Dairy Development Board.

questions.text: In which sport does the score depend on putting the ball in a hole?
questions.explanation: In golf the player tries to hole the ball in as few strokes as possible.

questions.text: Nirmala Mehta is an exponent of which Indian classical dance form?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Manipuri, the classical dance of Manipur, as Nirmala Mehta's form.

questions.text: The Himachal is a range in the Himalayas. It is also known as:
questions.explanation: The Himachal, the middle of the three parallel ranges, between the Himadri to the north and the Shiwaliks to the south, is also called the Lesser Himalayas.

questions.text: Javelin thrower Annu Rani, who registered a throw of 63.24 m at the Federation Cup Senior National Athletics Championships to set a new national record, represented the state of ___________________________.
questions.explanation: Annu Rani is from Meerut district in Uttar Pradesh, the state she represents in national competitions.

questions.text: Among the following Indian actresses, whose autobiography is ‘Unfinished’?
questions.explanation: 'Unfinished' (2021) is Priyanka Chopra's memoir.

questions.text: Which Part of the Indian Constitution provides for the Union Public Service Commission?
questions.explanation: Part XIV (Services under the Union and the States, Articles 308-323) provides for the Union and State Public Service Commissions in Articles 315-323.

questions.text: Which statement is NOT correct regarding the food chain?
options: Every component of food chain forms trophic level.
Inter-relation between different food chains is known as a food web.
All the chains formed by nutritional relations are used to understand energy flow.
In food chain, energy level increases from lower trophic level to higher trophic level.
questions.explanation: Only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level passes to the next, so energy decreases, not increases, up a food chain.

questions.text: In the electronic configuration of an atom, What does ‘n’ signify in the formula 2n²?
options: The number of the given shell from the nucleus
The number of valence electrons present
questions.explanation: 2n² is the most electrons a shell can hold, where n is the shell's number counted from the nucleus: K (n = 1) holds 2 and L (n = 2) holds 8.

questions.text: Who among the following started the Kuchipudi Art Academy at Madras in 1963?
questions.explanation: Vempati Chinna Satyam, who did much to shape modern Kuchipudi, founded the Kuchipudi Art Academy in Madras in 1963.

questions.text: Which of the following sportspersons has written his/her autobiography ‘Ace against Odds’?
questions.explanation: 'Ace Against Odds' (2016) is Sania Mirza's autobiography.

questions.text: What is the starting voltage of an AA battery used for home gadgets such as remote controls, small toys, and wireless kitchen appliances?
questions.explanation: A fresh AA cell, alkaline or zinc-carbon, has a nominal voltage of 1.5 V.

questions.text: Which day marks the founding of the World Health Organization (WHO) and aims to draw the attention to the important health issues facing the world every year?
questions.explanation: World Health Day, 7 April, marks the founding of the WHO in 1948; each year it takes up a health theme.

questions.text: Which is a visible sign of severe iodine deficiency?
questions.explanation: Severe iodine deficiency enlarges the thyroid gland, a swelling in the neck called goitre. Night blindness comes from a lack of vitamin A and bleeding gums from a lack of vitamin C.

questions.text: The first recipient of the National Award for Best Music Direction was _______ who was honoured for his composition in the Tamil film Kandan Karunai.
questions.explanation: K. V. Mahadevan, a leading composer of Tamil and Telugu film music, received the first National Film Award for Best Music Direction, instituted in 1967, for 'Kandan Karunai'.

questions.text: In which of the following years did Pandit Bhimsen Gururaj Joshi give his first ever live performance?
questions.explanation: Bhimsen Joshi gave his first live performance in 1941, at the age of 19.

questions.text: Padma Shri awardee Chittani Ramachandra Hegde is known for his contribution to which of the following dance forms in India?
questions.explanation: Chittani Ramachandra Hegde was a leading artist of Yakshagana, the dance-drama of coastal Karnataka; he received the Padma Shri in 2012.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. A student __________ in ragging can be expelled from the institution
questions.explanation: To 'indulge in' something is to take part in it, usually something undesirable: a student 'indulging' in ragging.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Four grams of sodium chloride was added to the mixture by the research team.
options: The research team added the mixture to four grams of sodium chloride.
Four grams of sodium chloride added the mixture to the research team.
The research team added four grams of sodium chloride to the mixture.
The mixture added four grams of sodium chloride to the research team.
questions.explanation: The agent, 'the research team', becomes the subject and 'was added' becomes the simple past 'added': 'The research team added four grams of sodium chloride to the mixture.'

questions.text: Identify the option that arranges the given parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. a) However, through sheer grit and determination b) Nick was able to get admission to a high school c) Nick Vujicic was prevented from d) attending mainstream middle schools.
questions.explanation: 'Nick Vujicic was prevented from (c) attending mainstream middle schools (d). However, through sheer grit and determination (a) Nick was able to get admission to a high school (b).'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Ronaldo is / a famous / player of / the football.
questions.explanation: Names of games take no article: 'a famous player of football'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Sceptic
questions.explanation: A sceptic doubts what others accept; the opposite is a 'believer'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. The uneducated man was “flummoxed” by the legal document.
questions.explanation: 'Flummoxed' means bewildered, thrown into confusion; of the options, its opposite is 'comfortable', at ease.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who gives money or help to another person or cause
questions.explanation: A benefactor gives money or help to a person or a cause.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He was a ______ stranger to me.
questions.explanation: 'A complete stranger' is the set phrase for someone entirely unknown to one.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Red letter day
questions.explanation: A 'red-letter day' is a memorable or especially happy day.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Elina is / travelling / since / yesterday.
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and is still going on takes the present perfect continuous with 'since': 'Elina has been travelling since yesterday.'

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'privilege'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The love of man or mankind
questions.explanation: Philanthropy is the love of humankind, shown in helping others; philology is the study of language.

questions.text: Select the sentence which has no spelling error.
options: Beethoven is known to be a prodigious musician of all times.
His business gives him cash in prodigeous amounts.
Ashley caught the spectators by his prodigiuos tricks.
Dusty is a prodegious novelist of the present era.
questions.explanation: 'Prodigious' (remarkably great) is spelt correctly only in the first sentence.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Read between the lines
options: Be afraid of doing something again
Speak the truth even if it is unpleasant
Understand something that is not said outright
questions.explanation: To 'read between the lines' is to understand what is meant but not said outright.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Reema and Aasha “were frolicking in the park”
questions.explanation: To 'frolic' is to play cheerfully, so 'were playing' keeps the meaning; 'enjoy' needs an object ('enjoying themselves'), and 'participating' and 'performing' do not fit. Every option also changes 'park' to 'garden'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A kick in the teeth
questions.explanation: 'A kick in the teeth' is a great disappointment or setback, especially when one hoped for support.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Pace
questions.explanation: 'Pace' means speed.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. My father teaches students.
options: Students are being taught by my father
Students are taught by my father.
A student is taught by my father.
questions.explanation: The simple present 'teaches' becomes 'are taught' in the passive: 'Students are taught by my father.' 'Are being taught' is the present continuous.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In April 1945, during the Conference to set up the United Nations (UN) held in San Francisco, representatives of Brazil and China proposed that an international health organization be (1) ______ and a conference to frame its constitution convened. On 15 February 1946, the Economic and Social Council of the UN instructed the Secretary-General to (2)___________ such a conference. A Technical Preparatory Committee met in Paris from 18 March to 5 April 1946 and (3)___________ proposals for the Constitution which were presented to the International Health Conference in New York City (4) _______ 19 June and 22 July 1946. On the basis of these proposals, the Conference drafted and (5)___________ the Constitution of the World Health Organization, signed 22 July 1946 by representatives of 51 Members of the UN and of 10 other nations.

Select the most appropriate option to fill blank 1.
questions.explanation: After 'proposed that', the passive takes 'be' with the past participle: 'be established'.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In April 1945, during the Conference to set up the United Nations (UN) held in San Francisco, representatives of Brazil and China proposed that an international health organization be (1) ______ and a conference to frame its constitution convened. questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row : 24, 9, 108 Second row : 38, 5, 95 Third row : 12, 17, ? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the number into its constituent digits. For example, 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/deleting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: In each row the third number is half the product of the first two: 24 × 9 ÷ 2 = 108 and 38 × 5 ÷ 2 = 95. So 12 × 17 ÷ 2 = 102.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 14*11*22*56*8
Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term. 24 : 137 :: 14 : ? :: 18 : 101
questions.explanation: The second term is six times the first minus 7: 24 × 6 − 7 = 137 and 18 × 6 − 7 = 101. So 14 × 6 − 7 = 77.

questions.text: Which two numbers, from amongst the given options, should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 82 – 5 + (24÷6) + 17 + (5×8) = 127

Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. NEUTRAL : NAUTREL :: PACIFIC : PICIFAC :: LOYALTY : ?
questions.explanation: The second and sixth letters swap places: NEUTRAL → NAUTREL and PACIFIC → PICIFAC. So LOYALTY → LTYALOY.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs, except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: The second number is the sum of the first number's digits: 5 + 3 + 7 = 15, 9 + 1 + 7 = 17 and 6 + 7 + 3 = 16. But 4 + 5 + 9 = 18, not 19, so 459 : 19 is the odd pair.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'MUSIC' is written as ‘LNTVRTHJBD’ and 'VIOLIN' is written as 'UWHJNPKMHJMO’. How will 'CHORD' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by the letters just before and after it: M → LN, U → TV, S → RT, I → HJ, C → BD. So CHORD → BD GI NP QS CE: BDGINPQSCE.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? RRQZ, MADQ, ?, CSDY, XBQP
questions.explanation: First letters move back 5 (R, M, H, C, X), second letters forward 9 (R, A, J, S, B), third letters forward 13 (Q, D, Q, D, Q) and fourth letters back 9 (Z, Q, H, Y, P), wrapping round the alphabet. The missing cluster is HJQH.

questions.text: If 30 January 2010 was Saturday, then what was the day of the week on 01 March 2011?
questions.explanation: 30 January 2010 to 30 January 2011 is 365 days, one odd day, so 30 January 2011 was a Sunday. 1 March 2011 is 30 days later (1 + 28 + 1), two odd days on: Tuesday.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 41*3*53*48*3*18*5*36
If 22nd January 2011 was a Saturday, then what was the day of the week on 23rd January 2015?
questions.explanation: The four years from 22 January 2011 to 22 January 2015 take in 29 February 2012, so they add 1 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 5 odd days: 22 January 2015 was a Thursday, and 23 January a Friday.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given number series? 1244, 624, 314, ?, 81.5, 42.75
questions.explanation: Each term is half the one before plus 2: 1244 ÷ 2 + 2 = 624, 624 ÷ 2 + 2 = 314 and 314 ÷ 2 + 2 = 159; then 159 ÷ 2 + 2 = 81.5.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word and the fourth word is related to the third word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Centre : Central :: Character : Characteristic : : Ambition : ?
questions.explanation: Each noun is paired with an adjective formed from it: centre → central, character → characteristic. So ambition → ambitious.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? DPSQ, GTXW, ?, MBHI, PFMO
questions.explanation: First letters move forward 3 (D, G, J, M, P), second letters 4 (P, T, X, B, F), third letters 5 (S, X, C, H, M) and fourth letters 6 (Q, W, C, I, O), wrapping round after Z. The missing cluster is JXCC.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 7, 8, 12, 39, 55, 180, 216, ?
questions.explanation: The differences alternate between cubes and squares: +1³, +2², +3³, +4², +5³, +6². The next is +7³ = 343: 216 + 343 = 559.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'THEORY' is written as ‘YROEHT’ and ‘OPTION’ is written as ‘NOITPO’. How will 'EXPERT' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is written in reverse: THEORY → YROEHT and OPTION → NOITPO. So EXPERT → TREPXE.

questions.text: If ‘A’ denotes ‘+’, ‘B’ denotes ‘×’, ‘C’ denotes ‘–’ and ‘D’ denotes ‘÷’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? (48 D 12) C 71 A 14 B (96 D 6) A 3 B 12 = ?

Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All plants are herbs. Some herbs are trees. All trees are shrubs. Conclusions: I. Some shrubs are plants. II. Some shrubs are herbs. III. Some trees are plants.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: Some herbs are trees and all trees are shrubs, so some herbs are shrubs: some shrubs are herbs (II). The plants need not be among the herbs that are trees, so I and III do not follow.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term related to third term. 8 : 516 :: 6 : 219 :: 4 : ?
questions.explanation: The second term is the cube of the first plus half the first: 8³ + 4 = 516 and 6³ + 3 = 219. So 4³ + 2 = 66.

questions.text: If a positive integer N is divided by 7, the remainder is 3. Which of the following numbers yields a remainder of 0 when it is divided by 7?
questions.explanation: N = 7k + 3, so N + 4 = 7k + 7 = 7(k + 1), which 7 divides exactly.

questions.text: The population of a town is increasing at the rate of 5% per annum. What will be the population of the town on this basis after two years, if the present population is 16000?
The price of a TV has been reduced by 20%. In order to restore the original price, the new price must be increased by:
questions.explanation: A price of 100 falls to 80; getting back to 100 needs a rise of 20 on 80: 20/80 × 100 = 25%.

questions.text: A discount of 20% on the marked price of an article is allowed and then the article is sold for ₹1,380. The marked price of the article is _________.
questions.explanation: 80% of the marked price is ₹1,380, so the marked price is 1,380 ÷ 0.8 = ₹1,725.

questions.text: The difference between the compound and the simple interests for 3 years at the rate of 20% per annum is ₹432. What is the principal lent?

One candidate received 60% of the total valid votes in an election between two candidates. A total of 20% of the votes were invalid. What is the number of valid votes the other candidate received if the total votes were 16250?
questions.explanation: Valid votes = 80% of 16250 = 13000. The other candidate got the remaining 40% of these: 5200.

questions.text: A car covers a certain distance travelling at a speed of 60 km/h and returns to the starting point at a speed of 40 km/h. The average speed of the car for the entire journey is:
questions.explanation: Over equal distances the average speed is 2 × 60 × 40/(60 + 40) = 4800/100 = 48 km/h.

questions.text: A can complete a task in 12 days and B can complete the same task in 18 days. They start working together but A works for only 2 days. The remaining work is completed by B. If the total wage is ₹2,400, then what is B's share (in ₹)?
questions.explanation: A did 2/12 = 1/6 of the work and B the remaining 5/6. Wages follow the work done, so B gets 5/6 × 2,400 = ₹2,000.

questions.text: A solid right-circular cylinder, whose radius of the base is 15 cm and height is 12 cm, is melted and moulded into the solid right-circular cone, whose radius of the base is 24 cm. What will be the height of this cone?
questions.explanation: The volumes are equal: π × 15² × 12 = (1/3) × π × 24² × h, so 2700 = 192h and h = 14.0625 cm.

questions.text: A shopkeeper makes a profit of 12.5% after allowing a discount of 10% on the marked price of an article. Find his profit percentage if the article is sold at the marked price, allowing no discount.
questions.explanation: SP = 1.125 × CP = 0.9 × MP, so MP = 1.25 × CP: selling at the marked price gives a 25% profit.

questions.text: With an average speed of 42 km/h, a train reaches its destination in time. If it moves with an average speed of 14 km/h, it is late by 35 minutes. The length of the journey is:

The first number is one-third of the second number. The second number is 1.5 times of the third number. The third number is three times the fourth number. If the average of the four numbers is 10, find the largest of the number.
questions.explanation: Taking the fourth number as x, the third is 3x, the second 4.5x and the first 1.5x. Their sum is 10x = 4 × 10 = 40, so x = 4 and the largest, the second, is 18.

questions.text: A solid cylinder has a radius of 9 cm and a height of 25 cm. What is the ratio of its total surface area to its curved surface area?
Find the fourth proportional to 18, 36 and 52.
The radius of a solid metallic sphere is equal to 15 cm. It is melted and drawn into a long wire of radius 15 mm having uniform cross-section. Find the length of the wire.
questions.explanation: The volumes are equal, with 15 mm = 1.5 cm: (4/3)π × 15³ = π × 1.5² × L, so 4500 = 2.25L and L = 2000 cm.

questions.text: If a tradesman marks his goods 25% above the cost price and allows his customers a 12% reduction on their bill, then the percentage profit he makes is ______.
questions.explanation: The selling price is 1.25 × 0.88 = 1.10 times the cost price: a 10% profit.

questions.text: In 2017, Deepika Reddy got the Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards 2017 for her contribution in the field of ____________ dance.
questions.explanation: Deepika Reddy is a Kuchipudi dancer; her Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 2017 was for Kuchipudi.

questions.text: Which of the following is the autobiography of Dr. Manmohan Singh, the ex-Prime Minister of India?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'Changing India' (2018), a five-volume collection of Dr Manmohan Singh's own writings and speeches, which the question calls his autobiography; it is the only one of these books by him. 'A Shot at History' is Abhinav Bindra's, 'Ace Against Odds' Sania Mirza's and 'My Country My Life' L. K. Advani's.

questions.text: Which of the following is the autobiography of the first female judge of India, Anna Chandy?
questions.explanation: Anna Chandy, India's first woman judge, published her autobiography 'Atmakatha' in 1973. 'Ente Katha' is Kamala Das's.

questions.text: In 2020,VP Dhananjayan and Shanta Dhananjayan were honoured with Sri Shanmukh ananda National Eminence Award in the field of ______.
questions.explanation: V. P. Dhananjayan and Shanta Dhananjayan are a celebrated Bharatanatyam dancing couple, so their honour was in the field of dance.

questions.text: Which of the following countries was ranked first in Paralympic 2020 medal tally?
questions.explanation: China topped the medal table at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, with 207 medals, 96 of them gold.

questions.text: Who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1926,‘for his work on the discontinuous structure of matter’?
questions.explanation: Jean Baptiste Perrin won the 1926 Nobel Prize in Physics; his experiments on Brownian motion confirmed that matter is made of atoms and molecules.

questions.text: Which base unit, discovered in 1820, represents one coulomb of electric current per second?
questions.explanation: The ampere, the SI base unit of electric current, is a flow of one coulomb of charge per second. It is named after André-Marie Ampère, whose work on electric currents began in 1820.

questions.text: ‘The Wings of Fire’ is an autobiography of which of the following Presidents of India?
questions.explanation: 'Wings of Fire' (1999), written with Arun Tiwari, is the autobiography of Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam.

questions.text: Who among the following Khayal singers of 19th century was given the title of ‘Tanras” by Bahadur Shah Jaffar, the last Mughal Emperor of India?
questions.explanation: Meer Qutub Baksh, a khayal singer at the court of Bahadur Shah Zafar, was given the title 'Tanras Khan' by the emperor.

questions.text: Who among the following was appointed as the Chairman of ICC Men's Cricket Committee in November 2021?
questions.explanation: In November 2021 the ICC named Sourav Ganguly chairman of its Men's Cricket Committee, succeeding Anil Kumble.

questions.text: Which structural layer surrounds the algal, fungal and plant cells and provides tensile strength and protection against mechanical and osmotic stress?
questions.explanation: The cell wall, outside the cell membrane, gives plant, fungal and algal cells strength and shape and protects them against mechanical and osmotic stress.

questions.text: Who won the Dronacharya Award for outstanding coaches in Sports and Games 2021 (Regular Category) in Table Tennis discipline?
questions.explanation: Table tennis coach Subramanian Raman received the Dronacharya Award (Regular Category) in 2021; Manika Batra and Sathiyan Gnanasekaran are players.

questions.text: In which state of matter is the kinetic energy of molecules greater than the forces of attraction between them, such that they are so far apart and move independently of each other?
questions.explanation: In a gas the particles' kinetic energy far exceeds the attraction between them, so they are far apart and move freely and independently.

questions.text: In February 2021, in the Devilal vs ____________ case, the Supreme Court observed that juvenile offenders under 18 years and above 16 years are to be remitted to the jurisdictional Juvenile Justice Board.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the State of Madhya Pradesh: the case is Devilal v. State of Madhya Pradesh, decided by the Supreme Court in February 2021.

questions.text: Which Articles of the Indian Constitution deal with the Union Executive?
questions.explanation: Articles 52 to 78, Chapter I of Part V, deal with the Union Executive: the President, the Vice-President, the Council of Ministers and the Attorney-General.

questions.text: What was India's rank in the world in 2019 for crude steel production?
questions.explanation: India overtook Japan in 2018 to become the world's second-largest producer of crude steel, after China, and was second again in 2019.

questions.text: The Kathak dance exponent Birju Maharaj is associated with which of the following Gharana?
questions.explanation: Pandit Birju Maharaj was the leading exponent of the Lucknow (Kalka-Bindadin) gharana of Kathak.

questions.text: GDP that takes into account the costs in terms of environmental pollution and exploitation of natural resources is called __________.
questions.explanation: Green GDP adjusts the conventional GDP for the depletion of natural resources and the cost of environmental damage.

questions.text: Which of the following civilian awards was conferred to Ustad Bismillah Khan in 2001?
questions.explanation: The shehnai maestro Ustad Bismillah Khan received the Bharat Ratna in 2001.

questions.text: In which track and field event is the baton used?
questions.explanation: In a relay race each runner carries the baton and hands it on to the next runner of the team.

questions.text: Alarmel Velli was awarded with the ‘Chevalier of Arts and Letters award’ from the Government of _________ in 2004.
questions.explanation: The Bharatanatyam dancer Alarmel Valli was made a Chevalier of the Order of Arts and Letters by the French Government in 2004.

questions.text: Identify the structural formula for ethene.
questions.explanation: Ethene (C₂H₄) has a double bond between two CH₂ groups: H₂C = CH₂, with four bonds on each carbon.

questions.text: Bickram Ghosh, a recipient of Global Indian Music Award, is a music composer and an Indian classical _________ player.
questions.explanation: Bickram Ghosh is a tabla player and composer.

questions.text: Which is a perennial carnivorous plant of the sundew family that attracts preys and usually traps insects and then breaks them down with digestive enzymes?
questions.explanation: The Venus flytrap (Dionaea muscipula), a perennial of the sundew family Droseraceae, snaps its leaves shut on insects and digests them with enzymes.

questions.text: India’s last living Sadir dancer from Tamil Nadu, Muthukannammal, was honoured with which of the following highest Indian civilian awards in 2022?
questions.explanation: Muthukannammal of Viralimalai, the last living Sadir dancer, received the Padma Shri in 2022.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. The incident was narrated by somebody to Naresh.
options: Somebody was narrating the incident to Naresh.
Somebody narrated the incident to Naresh.
Somebody was about to narrate the incident to Naresh.
Somebody will narrate the incident to Naresh.
questions.explanation: The past passive 'was narrated by somebody' becomes the simple past active: 'Somebody narrated the incident to Naresh.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I was waiting “from” two hours.
questions.explanation: A period of time takes 'for': 'I was waiting for two hours.' 'Since' goes with a point in time.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. My success was complete and the delighted directors ________ me the privilege of developing automatic regulators which were much desired.
questions.explanation: To 'accord' someone a privilege is to grant it to them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She was laughing from the ______ exuberance of the performance.
questions.explanation: 'Sheer' means pure, nothing but: laughing from 'sheer exuberance' is the natural pairing.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hard and fast
questions.explanation: Rules that are 'hard and fast' are fixed and cannot be bent: strict.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.. Human beings are usually ones who are “naturally able to eat both, plants and flesh.”
questions.explanation: An omnivorous creature naturally eats both plants and flesh; herbivores eat only plants, carnivores flesh, and cannibals their own kind.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. As soon as she opened the cages, the birds __________.
questions.explanation: 'As soon as' links two past actions, so the simple past: 'the birds flew away'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'apology', with one 'p'. 'Extravert' is an accepted spelling of 'extrovert'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Siddharth is floating a grand plan by next week.
options: Siddharth is being floated by a grand plan next week.
A grand plan is being floated by Siddharth next week.
Next week is keeping afloat by Siddharth’s grand plan.
A grand plan is being floating by Siddharth next week.
questions.explanation: The present continuous 'is floating' becomes 'is being floated' in the passive, with Siddharth as the agent: 'A grand plan is being floated by Siddharth next week.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Former
questions.explanation: 'Former' is the first of two things mentioned; its opposite is 'latter', the second.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Savage
questions.explanation: 'Savage' means wild and uncivilised; its opposite is 'civilised'.

questions.text: Select the sentence which has no spelling error.
options: Geet runs a pharmasutical chemist shop at New Delhi.
My elder brother works in a pharmaceutical company.
The pharmaetuical company develops and market drugs.
Many phramaeutical companies supplied vaccines in pandemic.
questions.explanation: Only the second sentence spells 'pharmaceutical' correctly; the others give 'pharmasutical', 'pharmaetuical' and 'phramaeutical'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank. The ________________ of the worksheets is not an easy job.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'reconciliation', from 'reconcile'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. You have lost your note book.
options: Your note book have been lost.
Your note book has been lost.
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'have lost' becomes 'has been lost', singular to agree with 'note book': 'Your note book has been lost.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence. The affection of her husband “carried her up” in the midst of all her problems.
questions.explanation: To 'bear someone up' is to support or sustain them: her husband's affection 'bore her up' through her problems.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The beauty of our festivals lies in ‘unity in___________’.
questions.explanation: 'Unity in diversity' is the set phrase for oneness among varied peoples and cultures.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. But while it may seem normal to you, your child may be negatively affected by your and your partner's actions. B. There is no telling when a squabble between a couple may aggravate and escalate into something ugly, which when witnessed by a child, might devastate them gravely. C. There's no relationship that does not falter. D. Arguments, disagreements and conflicts are extremely common even in a healthy relationship.
questions.explanation: C says every relationship falters, D that arguments are common even in healthy ones, A turns to the effect on a child, and B warns how a squabble can escalate: CDAB.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Poetry and novels became very (1)_________ in the 18th century. Robinson Crusoe by Daniel Defoe was published in 1719. This is regarded as the first successful English novel. It is partly based on the true life adventures of a traveller called Alexander Selkirk. Jonathan Swift’s Gulliver’s travels was written in 1726 and (2)_________ four imaginary journeys of a ship’s doctor named Gulliver. Poetry (3)_________ around British people and places. Poets also considered nature as a source of (4)_________. The poets wrote in a simple style and language so that the (5)_________ masses could understand it.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Poetry and novels became very 'popular' in the 18th century, as the success of the novels that follow shows.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Poets also considered nature as a source of (4)_________. The poets wrote in a simple style and language so that the (5)_________ masses could understand it.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The novel 'describes' four imaginary journeys: it gives an account of them.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Poetry and novels became very (1)_________ in the 18th century. Robinson Crusoe by Daniel Defoe was published in 1719. This is regarded as the first successful English novel. It is partly based on the true life adventures of a traveller called Alexander Selkirk. Jonathan Swift’s Gulliver’s travels was written in 1726 and (2)_________ four imaginary journeys of a ship’s doctor named Gulliver. Poetry (3)_________ around British people and places. Poets also considered nature as a source of (4)_________. The poets wrote in a simple style and language so that the (5)_________ masses could understand it.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: To 'revolve around' is to centre on: poetry revolved around British people and places.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Poetry and novels became very (1)_________ in the 18th century. Robinson Crusoe by Daniel Defoe was published in 1719. This is regarded as the first successful English novel. Poets also considered nature as a source of (4)_________. The poets wrote in a simple style and language so that the (5)_________ masses could understand it.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'A source of inspiration' is the set phrase: the poets drew inspiration from nature.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Poetry and novels became very (1)_________ in the 18th century. Robinson Crusoe by Daniel Defoe was published in 1719. This is regarded as the first successful English novel. It is partly based on the true life adventures of a traveller called Alexander Selkirk. Jonathan Swift’s Gulliver’s travels was written in 1726 and (2)_________ four imaginary journeys of a ship’s doctor named Gulliver. Poetry (3)_________ around British people and places. Poets also considered nature as a source of (4)_________. The poets wrote in a simple style and language so that the (5)_________ masses could understand it.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The simple style let the 'ordinary masses', the common people, understand it.

questions.text: If M denotes ‘−’, N denotes ‘÷’, O denotes ‘×’ and P denotes ‘+’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? (38 O 13) N 19 M 27 P (38 O 3) P 43 M 68 = ?
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 8, 16,13,?,47, 282
In a certain code language, ‘APRON’ is written as ‘CNTMP’ and ‘EARTH’is written as ‘GYTRJ’. How will ‘HEAVY’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +2, −2, +2, −2, +2: APRON → CNTMP and EARTH → GYTRJ. So HEAVY → JCCTA.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when placed from left to right in the given blanks, will complete the letter series. D E _ W G _ E F _ G D E F U _ D _ F T G
questions.explanation: With F, D, V, G, E in the blanks the series reads DEFWG DEFVG DEFUG DEFTG: the fourth letter goes back one each time (W, V, U, T).

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 34*4*15*51*27*9*40
If 28 February 2017 was Tuesday, then what was the day of the week on 28 February 2019?
questions.explanation: From 28 February 2017 to 28 February 2019 is 365 + 365 days with no 29 February in between, and each 365 days moves the day on by one: Tuesday + 2 = Thursday.

questions.text: Seven friends M, N, O, P, Q, R and S, each has a different age. Only two people are older than Q. P is older than Q but younger than O. M is older than R but younger than S. Only three people are younger than S. N is the youngest among all. The age of how many persons is between the ages of Q and R?
questions.explanation: Q is third oldest, with O and P above it (O > P > Q). Three are younger than S, so S is fourth, then M and R (S > M > R), and N is last. Between Q (3rd) and R (6th) come S and M: 2.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it. First row – 13, 50, 104; Second row – 11, 42, ?; Third row – 18, 70, 144 (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed)
questions.explanation: In each row the second number is 4 × the first − 2 and the third is 2 × the second + 4: 13 → 50 → 104 and 18 → 70 → 144. So 11 → 42 → 2 × 42 + 4 = 88.

questions.text: 09 April 2023 is Friday. What will be 30 April 2023?
questions.explanation: Going by the question's premise, 30 April is 21 days, exactly 3 weeks, after 9 April, so it falls on the same day: Friday. (On the real calendar 9 April 2023 was a Sunday, and so was 30 April.)

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? XAPE, BIBU, ?, JYZA, NGLQ
questions.explanation: First letters move +4 (X, B, F, J, N), second +8 (A, I, Q, Y, G), third +12 (P, B, N, Z, L) and fourth +16 (E, U, K, A, Q), wrapping round after Z. The missing cluster is FQNK.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs, EXCEPT one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: In 8 : 512, 6 : 216 and 4 : 64 the second number is the cube of the first. In 8 : 64 it is the square, so that pair is the odd one.

questions.text: If I denotes ‘÷’, J denotes ‘×’, K denotes ‘−’ and L denotes ‘+’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation? 37 L 25 K (14 J 2) L (2 J 13) K (62 I 31) = ?
In a certain code language, 'DANCE' is written as 'ADNEC' and ‘DISCO’ is written as ‘IDSOC’. How will 'DREAM' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first two letters swap, the middle one stays and the last two swap: DANCE → AD N EC and DISCO → ID S OC. So DREAM → RD E MA: RDEMA.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. GENIUS : IUNGES :: HOLDER : DELHOR :: LIGHTS : ?
questions.explanation: The fourth, fifth and third letters come first, then the first, second and sixth: GENIUS → IUN GES and HOLDER → DEL HOR. So LIGHTS → HTG LIS: HTGLIS.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 45*9*3*7*5*133
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 199, 211, 196, ?, 193, 217
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 199, 196, 193 (−3 each time) and 211, ?, 217 (+3 each time). The missing term is 214.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 19 : 80 ::23 : 96::16 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is 4 × the first + 4: 19 × 4 + 4 = 80 and 23 × 4 + 4 = 96. Likewise 16 × 4 + 4 = 68.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 67*88*8*14*3*19*17
After allowing 15% discount, a dealer wishes to sell a machine for ₹1,22,700. At what price must the machine be marked? (Consider up to two decimals)
questions.explanation: The selling price is 85% of the marked price, so the marked price = 1,22,700 ÷ 0.85 = ₹1,44,352.94.

questions.text: The average weight of 15 athletes and three trainers is 60 kg. When four more athletes of average weight 63 kg are included in the group, what is the average weight (in kg, rounded off to the nearest integer) of the group?
How many 25 cm × 11.25 cm × 6 cm bricks will be required to construct an 8 m × 6 m × 22.5 cm wall?(ignoring other material used)
If triangles ABC and PQR are both isosceles with AB=AC and PQ=PR, respectively. If also AB=PQ and BC=QR and angle B=50°, then what is the measure of angle R?
questions.explanation: AB = PQ, AC = PR (since AB = AC and PQ = PR) and BC = QR, so the triangles are congruent and ∠R = ∠C. In isosceles ΔABC, ∠C = ∠B = 50°.

questions.text: The average marks scored by a student in 4 subjects is 75. But when the marks of English are added to it, the overall average became 70. How much did he score in English?
questions.explanation: The four subjects total 4 × 75 = 300 and all five 5 × 70 = 350, so English = 350 − 300 = 50.

questions.text: If P : Q = 10 ∶11 and Q ∶ R = 11 ∶ 12, then P + Q ∶ Q + R ∶ R + P is:
The total surface area of a solid hemisphere is 16632 cm². Its volume is: (Take π=22/7)
How many two-digit numbers are divisible by 3 or 5?
questions.explanation: Two-digit multiples of 3 run from 12 to 99 (30 of them) and of 5 from 10 to 95 (18); multiples of both, i.e. of 15, run from 15 to 90 (6). 30 + 18 − 6 = 42.

questions.text: The price of an article is raised by 45% and then two successive discounts of 15% each are allowed. Ultimately the price of the article is _________.

The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest on a given principal is ₹1,725 in 2 years and the rate of interest in both cases is 25% per annum, and in the case when interest is compunded, it is compounded annually. Find the principal.
X’s salary is increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. What is the change in salary?
questions.explanation: 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96 of the original salary: a 4% decrease.

questions.text: If Mona and Sona together can finish a typing work in 18 days and Sona alone can finish it in 24 days, find the number of days in which Mona alone can finish the work.
questions.explanation: Mona does 1/18 − 1/24 = (4 − 3)/72 = 1/72 of the work a day, so she alone takes 72 days.

questions.text: The population of a town is 80,000. It decreases by 8% in the first year and increases by 5% in the second year. What will be the population of the town at the end of 2 years?
questions.explanation: 80,000 × 0.92 = 73,600 after the first year, and 73,600 × 1.05 = 77,280 after the second.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘Fasting, Feasting’?
questions.explanation: 'Fasting, Feasting' (1999), shortlisted for the Booker Prize, is a novel by Anita Desai.

questions.text: On the basis of the track width of Indian Railways, what type of gauge is Matheran Hill Railways?
questions.explanation: The Matheran Hill Railway, from Neral to Matheran in Maharashtra, runs on 2 ft (610 mm) narrow gauge.

questions.text: A R Rahman, the famous musician won the 52nd Grammy Award for which of the following songs?
questions.explanation: At the 52nd Grammy Awards (2010) 'Jai Ho' from 'Slumdog Millionaire' won the award for best song written for visual media; Rahman also won for the film's soundtrack album.

questions.text: Which plateau, with an average elevation of about 600 meters (2000 feet), is bounded by three mountain ranges: the Satpura range to the north and the Eastern and Western Ghats on either side?
questions.explanation: This is the Deccan Plateau, the triangular tableland of peninsular India. The Chota Nagpur Plateau lies mainly in Jharkhand, the Meghalaya Plateau in the north-east and Marwar in Rajasthan.

questions.text: Lack of financial discipline by the government can lead to ______________. (A) excess expenditure (B) inflation
questions.explanation: Without financial discipline a government spends beyond its means, and a deficit financed by borrowing or printing money adds to demand and pushes up prices. Both follow.

questions.text: Which is a slow cooking process that begins around 320°F, removes water from a sugar and breaks down the sugar into complex polymers with a sweet, nutty, or bitter taste and thus produces a golden-brown to dark brown colour?
questions.explanation: Caramelisation is the browning of sugar alone by heat. The Maillard reaction needs amino acids as well as sugars, and gelatinisation and dextrinisation are changes in starch.

questions.text: When was the National Hydrogen Mission (NHM) launched?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the National Hydrogen Mission in his Independence Day speech on 15 August 2021, to make India a hub for green hydrogen; it had first been proposed in the Union Budget 2021-22.

questions.text: Pandit Bhawani Shankar is a ________ player.
questions.explanation: Pandit Bhawani Shankar is a leading exponent of the pakhawaj, the barrel-shaped drum that accompanies Dhrupad.

questions.text: Which cricket player’s autobiography is titled ‘281 and Beyond’?
questions.explanation: '281 and Beyond' (2018) is VVS Laxman's autobiography, named after his 281 against Australia at Kolkata in 2001.

questions.text: Which of the following is the oldest High Court?
questions.explanation: The Calcutta High Court, opened in July 1862 under the Indian High Courts Act of 1861, is the oldest High Court in India. Allahabad's dates from 1866 and Delhi's from 1966.

questions.text: Who arranged the elements with chemically similar properties, such as lithium, sodium, and potassium, and showed that the properties of the middle element could be predicted from the properties of the other two?
questions.explanation: Johann Döbereiner grouped similar elements into triads, such as lithium, sodium and potassium, in which the middle element's properties lie between those of the other two.

questions.text: Maitya Ram Reang (Satyaram) was conferred with the Padma Shri for his contributions to which of the folk dances?
questions.explanation: Satyaram Reang of Tripura received the Padma Shri in 2021 for Hojagiri, the Reang community's folk dance.

questions.text: Which is the first of India's traditional dance to be refashioned as a theatre art and to be exhibited widely both at home and abroad?
questions.explanation: Bharatanatyam, Tamil Nadu's classical dance, grew out of the temple dance once called Sadir; the Ministry of Culture describes it as the first of India's traditional dances to be refashioned as a theatre art.

questions.text: Which of the following is a meteorological instrument consisting of a funnel-shaped collector attached to a measuring tube used to measure rainfall per unit area at a given time?
questions.explanation: A standard rain gauge collects rain through a funnel into a measuring tube. An anemometer measures wind speed; hygrometers and sling psychrometers measure humidity.

questions.text: Identify the word that means horizontal rows in periodic table.
questions.explanation: The horizontal rows of the periodic table are periods; the vertical columns are groups.

questions.text: Who won the Bronze medal in badminton women's singles at Tokyo Olympics 2020?
questions.explanation: PV Sindhu won the bronze at Tokyo 2020, beating He Bingjiao; Chen Yufei won gold and Tai Tzu-ying silver.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a symptom of Beriberi caused due to the deficiency of Vitamin B1?
questions.explanation: Beriberi damages the nerves and heart: limb pain, difficulty speaking and involuntary eye movements are among its signs. Slow-healing wounds point to scurvy, from lack of vitamin C.

questions.text: ‘Straight from the Heart: An Autobiography’ is an autobiography of which of following sportspersons?
questions.explanation: 'Straight from the Heart' (2004) is Kapil Dev's autobiography.

questions.text: Who among the following personalities was awarded the Officer of the Legion of Honour award?
questions.explanation: France made Lata Mangeshkar an Officer of the Legion of Honour, its highest civilian order, in 2007.

questions.text: As per statistics published by National Crime Records Bureau for 2020, which state registered the highest number of crimes against children [Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Special and Local Laws (SLL)]?
questions.explanation: In NCRB's 'Crime in India 2020', Madhya Pradesh registered the most crimes against children, about 13% of the national total, ahead of Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra.

questions.text: Padma Bhushan awardee Uma Sharma is a ________ dancer.
questions.explanation: Uma Sharma is a Delhi-based Kathak dancer and guru; she received the Padma Bhushan in 2001.

questions.text: Teejan Bai, Jhaduram Devangan, Ritu Verma, Usha Barle and Shantibai Chelak are famous for which of the following forms of folk music?
questions.explanation: They are exponents of Pandavani, Chhattisgarh's sung narration of the Pandavas' story from the Mahabharata. Lavani is from Maharashtra, Bihugeet from Assam and Bhatiali from Bengal.

questions.text: Which of the following is an adventure sport?
questions.explanation: Paragliding, flying a light foot-launched glider, is an adventure sport. Cycling and snow hockey are ordinary sports, and the Paralympics are a multi-sport event.

questions.text: Veteran classical dance guru from _________, Jatin Goswami was given the National Kalidas Samman for 2017.
questions.explanation: Jatin Goswami is a guru of Sattriya, the classical dance of Assam.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Variance
questions.explanation: 'Variance' here means disagreement or discord (as in 'at variance'); its opposite is 'harmony'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. One should work “hard than” others to succeed.
questions.explanation: A comparison with 'than' needs the comparative: 'One should work harder than others to succeed.'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Pygmalion was written by GB Shaw.
options: GB Shaw was written by Pygmalion.
questions.explanation: The simple past passive 'was written by GB Shaw' becomes the active 'GB Shaw wrote Pygmalion.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. There is many ways / to make / a stranger feel / welcome in the community.
questions.explanation: The plural 'many ways' needs a plural verb: 'There are many ways'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Memorial'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Robin has “less marbles” than George.
questions.explanation: 'Fewer' goes with countable nouns such as marbles, 'less' with uncountable ones: 'Robin has fewer marbles than George.'

questions.text: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The minute you start _______ and tolerating __________, it becomes the new norm and the slide begins and therefore, we must constantly __________ to give our best and be recognised, not simply aim to do just enough to ___________ that we don’t get found out.
questions.explanation: Once we start 'compromising' and tolerating 'mediocrity' it becomes the norm, so we must 'strive' to give our best, not do just enough to 'ensure' that we are not found out.

questions.text: Select the correct homonym from the given options to fill in the blank. Which________does the minister take to reach the Assembly?
questions.explanation: A 'route' is the way taken to reach a place; 'root' sounds alike but means something else.

questions.text: Select the sentence which has no spelling error.
options: Gupta empire posed a competetoin to the invaders in ancient India.
Neeta represented Global School in the state level debate competition.
There is a high market compettion due to the advent of online shopping.
The cooking compitition was judged by the head chef of Garland Hotels.
questions.explanation: Only the sentence about Neeta's debate spells 'competition' correctly; the others misspell it as 'competetoin', 'compettion' and 'compitition'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who is well-versed in the knowledge of plants
questions.explanation: A botanist is an expert in the study of plants; a florist sells flowers.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Win laurels
questions.explanation: To 'win laurels' is to gain honour or praise, the laurel wreath being the victor's prize in ancient times.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. The teacher said, ‘“the sun raises in the east” every day’.
options: the sun will rise in the east
the sun rises in the east
the sun rises at the east
questions.explanation: A habitual fact or universal truth takes the simple present, and the verb that takes no object is 'rise' ('raise' needs one); the sun rises 'in', not 'at', the east.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Ramu went with his friends on a trip to ___________ new paths.
questions.explanation: On a trip one sets out to 'explore' new paths, to travel through them and discover them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence. I was “carried” by her rapturous song.
questions.explanation: To be 'carried away' is to be so moved or excited that one forgets everything else.

questions.text: Identify the option that arranges the given parts in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. a) Non-verbal communication is a means b) This is possible by using visual clues c) By which you are able to communicate without speaking d) Such as facial expressions, eye-contact, postures, gestures etc.
questions.explanation: 'Non-verbal communication is a means (a) by which you are able to communicate without speaking (c). This is possible by using visual clues (b) such as facial expressions, eye-contact, postures, gestures etc. (d)'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the options given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Tree plantation is the (1)______ of transplanting saplings or seeds to maximise the amount of greenery and focus on promoting (2)______. Planting trees can be a very rewarding and fruitful (3)______! Not only is it (4)______ beneficial for this planet, but it also contributes to helping create an environmentally friendly place to live, as trees help reduce pollutant (5)______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.1.
questions.explanation: Tree plantation is the 'process' of transplanting saplings or seeds.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the options given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Tree plantation is the (1)______ of transplanting saplings or seeds to maximise the amount of greenery and focus on promoting (2)______. Planting trees can be a very rewarding and fruitful (3)______! Not only is it (4)______ beneficial for this planet, but it also contributes to helping create an environmentally friendly place to live, as trees help reduce pollutant (5)______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.2.
questions.explanation: Planting trees promotes 'afforestation', the growing of forests; 'deforestation' is the opposite.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the options given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Tree plantation is the (1)______ of transplanting saplings or seeds to maximise the amount of greenery and focus on promoting (2)______. Planting trees can be a very rewarding and fruitful (3)______! Not only is it (4)______ beneficial for this planet, but it also contributes to helping create an environmentally friendly place to live, as trees help reduce pollutant (5)______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.3.
questions.explanation: Planting trees is a rewarding and fruitful 'endeavour', an effort or undertaking.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the options given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Tree plantation is the (1)______ of transplanting saplings or seeds to maximise the amount of greenery and focus on promoting (2)______. Planting trees can be a very rewarding and fruitful (3)______! Not only is it (4)______ beneficial for this planet, but it also contributes to helping create an environmentally friendly place to live, as trees help reduce pollutant (5)______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.4.
questions.explanation: Trees are 'ecologically' beneficial for the planet, which fits the environmental benefits the sentence goes on to name.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the options given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Tree plantation is the (1)______ of transplanting saplings or seeds to maximise the amount of greenery and focus on promoting (2)______. Planting trees can be a very rewarding and fruitful (3)______! Not only is it (4)______ beneficial for this planet, but it also contributes to helping create an environmentally friendly place to live, as trees help reduce pollutant (5)______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.5.
questions.explanation: Trees help reduce the 'concentration' of pollutants in the air.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 17, 20, 60, 64, 256, 261, 1305,?
questions.explanation: The steps alternate +3, ×3, +4, ×4, +5, ×5, so the next is +6: 1305 + 6 = 1311.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1.Beginner 2.Beheld 3.Beggar 4.Belief 5.Behind
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Beggar (3), Beginner (1), Beheld (2), Behind (5), Belief (4). 'Begg' comes before 'Begi', and 'Behe' before 'Behi'.

questions.text: Seven friends P, Q, R, S, T, U and V, each has a different age. P is older than only U and R. R is older than U. Q is older than S but younger than T. T is not the oldest among all. The age of how many persons is between the ages of Q and R?
questions.explanation: P is older than only U and R, and R is older than U, so from the youngest the order begins U, R, P. T is not the oldest, so V is; with S younger than Q and Q younger than T, the rest is S, Q, T. Between R and Q come P and S: two persons.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'Read the code' is coded as '18 20 3', 'Decode the code' is coded as '4 20 3' and 'code is easy' is coded as '3 9 5'. How will 'make one code' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded by the alphabet position of its first letter: Read = 18 (R), the = 20 (T), code = 3 (C), Decode = 4 (D), is = 9 (I), easy = 5 (E). So make = 13 (M), one = 15 (O) and code = 3: 13 15 3.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 78*43*2*56*27*4
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 230 * 1 * 5 * 16 * 41 * 21
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 41*4*39*73*25*4*30

The second number in the given number-pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number-pairs EXCEPT one. Find that odd number-pair.
questions.explanation: The second number is the first squared times one less than the first: 4 × 4 × 3 = 48, 6 × 6 × 5 = 180, 8 × 8 × 7 = 448. But 9 × 9 × 8 = 648, not 639.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the letters that, when placed from left to right in the blanks, will complete the letter series. _ P N I E X _ N I E Y P N _ E Z P _ I _
questions.explanation: With W, P, I, N, E in the blanks each block is PNIE after the next letter from W to Z: WPNIE XPNIE YPNIE ZPNIE.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. BROWSER : SERWBRO :: CAPTURE : URETCAP :: DESKTOP : ?
questions.explanation: The last three letters come first, then the middle letter, then the first three: BRO W SER → SER W BRO and CAP T URE → URE T CAP. So DES K TOP → TOPKDES.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 93*65*3*56*14*40

The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs, except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.explanation: In 2 : 15, 3 : 20 and 5 : 30 the second number is 5 times one more than the first (5 × 3, 5 × 4, 5 × 6). For 6 that gives 35, so 6 : 36 is the odd one.
