questions.explanation: Sunil Gavaskar wrote 'Runs 'n Ruins' (1984) as well as 'Sunny Days'. 'Playing It My Way' is Sachin Tendulkar's autobiography and 'Democracy's XI' is by Rajdeep Sardesai.

questions.text: As per Union Budget 2020, the Government of India intends to double the country's milk processing capacity by the year ______.
questions.explanation: The Union Budget 2020-21 set out to double milk processing capacity, from 53.5 million tonnes to 108 million tonnes, by 2025.

questions.text: Which of the following ports is used to connect a computer to a wired network?
questions.explanation: An Ethernet (RJ-45) port takes the cable that connects a computer to a wired network.

questions.text: Which of the following is a vector-borne disease?
questions.explanation: Malaria is spread by a vector, the female Anopheles mosquito. Pneumonia and mumps spread through droplets and cholera through contaminated water or food.

questions.text: Which of the following states launched India's and South-Asia's first blockchain-enabled rooftop solar trading platform in December 2020?
questions.explanation: In December 2020 Uttar Pradesh began a pilot in Lucknow, with UPNEDA and the state's power utilities, for households to trade surplus rooftop solar power on a blockchain platform, the first in India and South Asia.

questions.text: Who is the Governor of the state of Chhattisgarh as of May 2020?
questions.explanation: Anusuiya Uikey became Governor of Chhattisgarh in July 2019. Bhupesh Baghel was the state's Chief Minister.

questions.text: Which of the following cells is NOT used in watches?
questions.explanation: Lead-acid cells are large rechargeable batteries used in vehicles and inverters. Silver oxide, mercury and zinc-air cells are small button cells used in watches and hearing aids.

questions.text: Where is the Rumi Darwaza located?
questions.explanation: The Rumi Darwaza in Lucknow was built under Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula in 1784.

questions.text: In December 2020, the Chief Minister of ______ announced that India's biggest hockey stadium is being set up in the state.
questions.explanation: In December 2020 Odisha's Chief Minister, Naveen Patnaik, announced a new hockey stadium at Rourkela, planned as India's biggest, for the 2023 Men's Hockey World Cup.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Aditya passed the driving test quite easily.
options: The driving test had passed quite easily by Aditya.
The driving test have been passed quite easily by Aditya.
The driving test could passed quite easily by Aditya.
The driving test was passed quite easily by Aditya.
questions.explanation: The past simple 'passed' becomes 'was passed', with 'the driving test' as the subject: 'The driving test was passed quite easily by Aditya.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To cut corners
options: cut something easily without spoiling it
be able to do a job effortlessly
not do a thing well in order to save money or effort
questions.explanation: To 'cut corners' is to do something in the easiest or cheapest way, at the cost of quality.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Cook the books
questions.explanation: To 'cook the books' is to falsify a company's accounts.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Doctors say that home isolation is far more effective than hospitalise in cases of mild infection.
questions.explanation: 'Than' compares 'home isolation' with another noun, so it needs 'hospitalisation', not the verb 'hospitalise'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. “Sometimes the family liking” to play a game together after dinner.
questions.explanation: A singular subject in the present simple takes a finite verb ending in -s: 'Sometimes the family likes to play a game together'. 'Sometime' means at some unstated time.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Have you thought about the ______ of the recent decision you took?
questions.explanation: The 'consequences' of a decision are its results, which one should think about before taking it.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, select the one that gives their correct order. A. On either side of the trunk there are a few scattered tufts of short grass. B. It is towards one of these fallen trees that I am now looking. C. A very violent cyclonic storm has struck the forest, uprooting a number of trees. D. The trunk of the tree is ripped apart and the branches are lying all around it.
questions.explanation: C tells of the storm uprooting trees, B singles out one of the fallen trees, D describes its ripped trunk and A the grass on either side of the trunk: CBDA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Paranoid
questions.explanation: 'Paranoid' means unreasonably distrustful of others: 'suspicious'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'persistence'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. One who has the power to do anything
questions.explanation: 'Omnipotent' means all-powerful; 'omnipresent' means present everywhere.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The headmaster ______ on the stage and gave a short speech.
questions.explanation: The headmaster 'appeared', that is came into view, on the stage before he spoke.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. BRAVERY
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'bravery' is 'cowardice'; heroism, strength and courage are close to synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. ABSOLUTE
questions.explanation: 'Absolute' means total, without any limit: 'complete'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Clandestine
questions.explanation: 'Clandestine' means done in secret, usually because it is improper; of these, 'honest', open and above-board, is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who presents a radio/television programme
questions.explanation: An anchor presents a radio or television programme and links its parts.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. “Had you not interfering” in my affairs, I would have been in the US now.
questions.explanation: A third conditional with the 'if' left out puts 'had' first and takes the past participle: 'Had you not interfered in my affairs, I would have been ...'

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. His father shifted his own ambitions to those of his son, providing him with models and support for his first exhibition at the age of 13. B. Pablo Picasso was the son of José Ruiz Blasco, a professor of drawing, and Maria Picasso López. C. From that point his ability to experiment with what he learned and to develop new expressive means quickly allowed him to surpass his father’s abilities. D. His unusual adeptness for drawing began to manifest itself early, around the age of 10, when he became his father’s pupil.
questions.explanation: B introduces Picasso and his father, a professor of drawing; D says he became his father's pupil at about 10; C, 'from that point', says he soon surpassed his father; and A tells how his father then shifted his ambitions to his son: BDCA.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The need today is for both sides / to introspect and re-examine the issue carefully / and resolve it amicably.
options: to introspect and re-examine the issue carefully
The need today is for both sides
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: 'for both sides to introspect and re-examine ... and resolve it', with the verbs in parallel after 'to'.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. My niece said, “I have decided to take coaching in badminton.”
options: My niece told me that she had decided to take coaching in badminton.
My niece told that I have decided to take coaching in badminton.
My niece said she is deciding to take coaching in badminton.
My niece said she will decide to take coaching in badminton.
questions.explanation: In reported speech the present perfect 'have decided' moves back to the past perfect 'had decided', and 'I' becomes 'she'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Kanjirapally has the highest number of rainy days in Kerala. It receives the highest (1)_____ of summer rains, winter rains and northeast monsoons in Kerala, (2)_____ it one of the very few (3)_____ in India enjoying equatorial rainforest type climate, with no (4) _____ dry season. The well-distributed rainfall pattern of Kanjirapally is the (5)_____ reason for the phenomenon of high yield of latex from rubber plantations in and around the town.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.1.
questions.explanation: Rain is measured as a quantity, so 'the highest amount of summer rains'; 'number' counts separate things.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Kanjirapally has the highest number of rainy days in Kerala. It receives the highest (1)_____ of summer rains, winter rains and northeast monsoons in Kerala, (2)_____ it one of the very few (3)_____ in India enjoying equatorial rainforest type climate, with no (4) _____ dry season. The well-distributed rainfall pattern of Kanjirapally is the (5)_____ reason for the phenomenon of high yield of latex from rubber plantations in and around the town.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.2.
questions.explanation: A participle phrase gives the result of the clause before it: '..., making it one of the very few places'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Kanjirapally has the highest number of rainy days in Kerala. It receives the highest (1)_____ of summer rains, winter rains and northeast monsoons in Kerala, (2)_____ it one of the very few (3)_____ in India enjoying equatorial rainforest type climate, with no (4) _____ dry season. The well-distributed rainfall pattern of Kanjirapally is the (5)_____ reason for the phenomenon of high yield of latex from rubber plantations in and around the town.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.3.
questions.explanation: 'One of' takes a plural noun: 'one of the very few places in India'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Kanjirapally has the highest number of rainy days in Kerala. It receives the highest (1)_____ of summer rains, winter rains and northeast monsoons in Kerala, (2)_____ it one of the very few (3)_____ in India enjoying equatorial rainforest type climate, with no (4) _____ dry season. The well-distributed rainfall pattern of Kanjirapally is the (5)_____ reason for the phenomenon of high yield of latex from rubber plantations in and around the town.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.4.
questions.explanation: The rain is well distributed through the year, so there is 'no distinct', clearly marked, dry season.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Kanjirapally has the highest number of rainy days in Kerala. It receives the highest (1)_____ of summer rains, winter rains and northeast monsoons in Kerala, (2)_____ it one of the very few (3)_____ in India enjoying equatorial rainforest type climate, with no (4) _____ dry season. The well-distributed rainfall pattern of Kanjirapally is the (5)_____ reason for the phenomenon of high yield of latex from rubber plantations in and around the town.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.5.
questions.explanation: The rainfall is 'the primary reason', the main one, for the high yield of latex.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. 28 : 50 : 94
questions.explanation: Each number is twice the one before it minus 6: 28 × 2 − 6 = 50 and 50 × 2 − 6 = 94. Likewise 36 × 2 − 6 = 66 and 66 × 2 − 6 = 126.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 8, 8, 11, 11, 14, 14, ?
questions.explanation: Each number appears twice and then rises by 3: 8, 8, 11, 11, 14, 14, 17.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All rats are cats. Some cats are not dogs. Conclusions: I. Some dogs are not rats. II. Some dogs are rats.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: All rats are inside the cats, and some cats are outside the dogs, but nothing fixes how dogs and rats overlap. All dogs may be rats, or none may be, so neither conclusion must follow.

questions.text: Select the word-pair in which the two words are related in the same way as are the two words in the given word-pair. Mathematics : Teacher
questions.explanation: A teacher teaches mathematics, as a coach trains players in hockey: the subject and the one who teaches it.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. s _ t m s r _ m _ r t _ s _ t m
questions.explanation: With r, t, s, m, r in the blanks the block srtm repeats: srtm srtm srtm srtm.

questions.text: Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the word that is different.
questions.explanation: Steel, brass and bronze are alloys; nickel is a metallic element.

questions.text: The cost of 5 pens and 12 pencils is ₹45. What would be the cost for 20 pens and 48 pencils?
questions.explanation: 20 pens and 48 pencils are 4 times 5 pens and 12 pencils, so they cost 4 × ₹45 = ₹180.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (313, 2732, 98211)
questions.explanation: The digits of the three numbers add up to 7, 14 and 21: 3 + 1 + 3, 2 + 7 + 3 + 2 and 9 + 8 + 2 + 1 + 1. Likewise 6 + 0 + 1 = 7, 9 + 4 + 0 + 1 = 14 and 7 + 1 + 4 + 2 + 7 = 21.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers does NOT belong to the group? 423, 171, 801, 900, 701
questions.explanation: The digits of 423, 171, 801 and 900 add up to 9, so each is divisible by 9. The digits of 701 add up to 8.

questions.text: Three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: In AEKM, IMPV and JMSU each letter comes later in the alphabet than the one before it. YTSR runs backwards.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number. 166 : 415 : : 256 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is 2.5 times the first: 166 × 2.5 = 415. Likewise 256 × 2.5 = 640.

questions.text: M's wife is N's daughter-in-law. P is the husband of O, who is the sister of M. How is P related to N?
questions.explanation: M's wife is N's daughter-in-law, so M is N's son. O, M's sister, is N's daughter, and P, her husband, is N's son-in-law.

questions.text: If in a code language, ORGAN is coded as 17141518 and FINGER is coded as 56791418, then how will you code NECK?
questions.explanation: The code lists the alphabet positions of the letters in ascending order: ORGAN = 15, 18, 7, 1, 14 → 1 7 14 15 18. NECK = 14, 5, 3, 11 → 3 5 11 14: 351114.

questions.text: In a certain code language, HUSBAND is written as ABDHNSU. How will HOUSEWIFE be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters are rearranged in alphabetical order: HUSBAND → ABDHNSU, so HOUSEWIFE → EEFHIOSUW.

questions.text: Which two digits and signs need to be interchanged so as to balance the given equation? 75 − 13 + 19 × 8 ÷ 5 = 93
questions.explanation: Interchanging 5 and 8, and − and ÷: 78 ÷ 13 + 19 × 5 − 8 = 6 + 95 − 8 = 93.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. SHORTLY : OHSYLTR : : WALKING : ?
questions.explanation: The first three letters are reversed, then the last four: SHO RTLY → OHS YLTR. So WAL KING → LAW GNIK: LAWGNIK.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. Wakeful : Sleepless : : Sitting : ?
questions.explanation: 'Sleepless' means wakeful; 'sedentary' means spent sitting down.

questions.text: Arrange the following words in a meaningful sequence. 1. Manager 2. Worker 3. General manager 4. Supervisor 5. Owner
questions.explanation: From the top of the hierarchy down: Owner (5), General manager (3), Manager (1), Supervisor (4), Worker (2).

questions.text: In which year did Gongsa Ugyen Wangchuck become the first monarch of Bhutan?
questions.explanation: Ugyen Wangchuck was crowned the first hereditary king (Druk Gyalpo) of Bhutan on 17 December 1907.

questions.text: Who among the following is the youngest test debutant in the history of cricket as on May 2020?
questions.explanation: Pakistan's Hasan Raza made his Test debut against Zimbabwe at Faisalabad in October 1996, aged 14 years and 227 days by his recorded date of birth, though that date was later doubted.

questions.text: Which of the following state governments approved the Freedom of Religion Bill 2020 in December 2020?
questions.explanation: The Madhya Pradesh cabinet approved the Madhya Pradesh Freedom of Religion Bill 2020, against unlawful religious conversion, in December 2020.

questions.text: Bangladesh was a part of Pakistan from ______.
questions.explanation: Bangladesh was East Pakistan from Partition in 1947 until it won independence in 1971.

questions.text: Which of the following is a pass on the Pir Panjal Range?
questions.explanation: The Banihal pass, on the road from Jammu to Srinagar, crosses the Pir Panjal range. Zoji La lies on the Great Himalaya, Fotu La on the Zaskar and Khardung La on the Ladakh range.

questions.text: Which of the following is a primary storage device in a personal computer?
questions.explanation: RAM is the computer's primary (main) memory, which the processor works from directly; hard disks, compact disks and pen drives are secondary storage.

questions.text: In which Olympic Games did Shabana Akhtar, the first female athlete to represent Pakistan, participate?
questions.explanation: Shabana Akhtar, a long jumper, competed at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics, the first woman to represent Pakistan at the Games.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following years did the Santhal Revolt take place?
questions.explanation: The Santhal Hul, led by Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu, broke out in 1855 and was suppressed in 1856.

questions.text: Which Indian Cabinet Minister was appointed as Executive Board Chairman of World Health Organization (WHO) in May 2020?
questions.explanation: Dr Harsh Vardhan, then Union Health Minister, became Chairman of the WHO Executive Board in May 2020.

questions.text: Who among the following boxers won a gold medal in the 57 kg category at the Cologne Boxing World Cup held at Germany in December 2020?
questions.explanation: Manisha Moun won the 57 kg gold at the Cologne Boxing World Cup in December 2020, beating Sakshi Choudhary in an all-Indian final.

questions.text: 'Puanchei' is the traditional dress of ______.
questions.explanation: The Puanchei, a colourful hand-woven wrap-around skirt, is the traditional dress of Mizo women.

questions.text: The concept of fiscal policy is based fundamentally on the ideas of ______.
questions.explanation: Using government spending and taxation to manage demand rests on John Maynard Keynes's 'General Theory' (1936).

questions.text: What is the currency of Myanmar?
questions.explanation: Myanmar's currency is the kyat. The riel is Cambodia's, the dong Vietnam's and the ringgit Malaysia's.

questions.text: Due to which of the following reactions are household bleaching agents using phosphorous, sulphur and chlorine formed?
questions.explanation: In alkali, chlorine is both oxidised, to hypochlorite (the bleaching agent), and reduced, to chloride: Cl₂ + 2OH⁻ → ClO⁻ + Cl⁻ + H₂O. An element oxidised and reduced in the same reaction is disproportionating; phosphorus and sulphur react in alkali in the same way.

questions.text: A major portion of 'Sufed Koh' mountain range lies in ______.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Pakistan, the only one of these countries the Safed Koh (Spin Ghar) reaches: the range runs about 160 km from the Peshawar valley in Pakistan west to the Logar valley in Afghanistan, forming a natural border between the two.

questions.text: Which natural port is located along the west coast of India?
questions.explanation: Marmagao in Goa is a natural harbour on the west coast. Visakhapatnam is also a natural harbour, but on the east coast, where Haldia (a riverine port) and Chennai (an artificial harbour) lie too.

questions.text: Which day in May 2020 was observed as 'International Tea Day'?
questions.explanation: The UN General Assembly declared 21 May International Tea Day; it was first observed in 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following is a polar molecule?
questions.explanation: Water's bent molecule leaves its bond dipoles uncancelled, so it is polar. The symmetrical shapes of carbon tetrachloride, carbon dioxide and benzene cancel any bond dipoles.

questions.text: Which one of the following features is NOT shown by metals?
options: Can be made into a wire
questions.explanation: Metals are lustrous (shiny), not dull; they are also malleable, ductile and good conductors of heat.

questions.text: Who authored the book 'Jinnah: His Successes, Failures and Role in History'?
questions.explanation: 'Jinnah: His Successes, Failures and Role in History' (2020) is by the political scientist Ishtiaq Ahmed.

questions.text: To which of the following Gharanas did the Hindustani classical vocalist Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan belong?
questions.explanation: Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan was the leading singer of the Patiala gharana.

questions.text: Which one of the following is a computer virus?
questions.explanation: Creeper (1971), which spread over ARPANET, is regarded as the first computer virus. Penguin and Panda are Google search updates, and a spider is a web crawler.

questions.text: Which was the first part of India to hold an election based on universal adult franchise?
questions.explanation: Manipur held elections under universal adult franchise in 1948, under its Constitution Act of 1947, before independent India's first general election of 1951-52.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. That is why they are considered the best indoor plants to keep at homes and offices. B. The indoor bonsai plants enhance the aesthetic appeal of the space and offer multiple health and psychological benefits. C. Bonsai is an important part of Japanese culture dating back to the 14th century. D. It is the art of cultivating small trees within a container that take the shape and scale of full-size trees.
questions.explanation: C introduces bonsai, D says what the art is, B gives the benefits of indoor bonsai and A ('That is why') draws the conclusion: CDBA.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. The plumber told Ranjit that he had fixed the leaking tap.
options: The plumber told to Ranjit, “He had fixed the leaking tap.”
The plumber told Ranjit, “Had he fixed the leaking tap?”
The plumber said to Ranjit, “You had fix the leaking tap.”
The plumber said to Ranjit, “I have fixed the leaking tap.”
questions.explanation: In direct speech 'told' becomes 'said to', and 'he had fixed' goes back to the plumber's own words, 'I have fixed'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. A heavy fine “will be inflicted with them” if they do not pay the taxes in time.
questions.explanation: A penalty is inflicted 'on' someone: 'A heavy fine will be inflicted on them'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. She managed the company / so well that it is made / a huge profit that year.
options: so well that it is made
questions.explanation: 'It' is the company that made the profit, so the verb is active and past: 'so well that it made a huge profit'.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. How much will they pay you?
options: How much will they be paying?
How much will you be paid by them?
Payment will be done by them?
They will have paid you how much?
questions.explanation: The object 'you' becomes the subject and 'will pay' becomes 'will be paid': 'How much will you be paid by them?'

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement' According to J Krishnamurti, education is not about having a career but about being able to look, “observation” and listen.
questions.explanation: The three verbs after 'able to' must be parallel: 'to look, observe and listen'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Poke one’s nose
options: Not be careful about one’s health
questions.explanation: To 'poke one's nose' into something is to interfere or meddle in what does not concern one.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'conglomerate'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The kite was stuck so high on the tree that it was ______ the reach of the boys.
questions.explanation: Out of the boys' reach is 'beyond' their reach.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Allege
questions.explanation: To 'allege' is to claim, without proof, that someone has done wrong: to 'charge' them. 'Soothe', 'placate' and 'appease' all mean to calm.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Drab
questions.explanation: 'Drab' means dull and colourless; its opposite is 'bright'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. CLEAN
questions.explanation: 'Clean' can mean free of wrongdoing, as in 'a clean record': 'honest'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. He will be leaving / home at 8 a.m. / to beating / the office rush hour.
questions.explanation: Purpose is shown by the infinitive: 'to beat the office rush hour'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The nest of a squirrel, typically in the form of a mass of twigs in a tree
questions.explanation: A drey is a squirrel's nest. A burrow and a lair are the dens of other animals.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A fire in someone’s belly
options: one who is energetic and enthusiastic about something
one who is rich and powerful and exploits the poor
one who comes from a middle class background
one who continues to work without wanting a reward
questions.explanation: To have 'a fire in one's belly' is to have strong drive and enthusiasm.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. DISJOINTED
questions.explanation: 'Disjointed' means lacking connection; its opposite is 'connected'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. A good teacher is the one who can explain the most complex subjects in a ______ way.
questions.explanation: A good teacher makes complex subjects simple, explaining them in a 'straightforward' way; 'lengthy' and 'roundabout' are the opposite.

questions.text: Examine the four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order. A. They can travel to the airport by personal vehicle or registered cabs only. B. Finally, all passengers are advised to strictly follow social distancing markers. C. According to the Government guidelines, air travel is declared open from May 2020 for passengers. D. Once there, they can walk in through the Entry Gates, which shall be kept open.
questions.explanation: C says air travel has reopened, A how passengers reach the airport, D what they do 'once there', and B ('Finally') closes: CADB.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A sentimental longing for a time in the past
questions.explanation: Nostalgia is a sentimental longing for the past. Sepia is a brownish tint, myopia short-sightedness and dystopia an imagined bad society.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. According to Harari, a leading thinker, we are all busy (1) ______ a fantasy self online. It is the age of Facebook and Instagram, wherein (2) ______ are busy creating perfect stories about ourselves. For example, pictures (3) ______ perfect holidays never show the stress of traffic snarls and a host of (4) ______ problems faced. We soon begin to believe in this perfect online self to be (5) ______ real one.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: 'Busy' is followed by the -ing form: 'busy creating a fantasy self online'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. According to Harari, a leading thinker, we are all busy (1) ______ a fantasy self online. It is the age of Facebook and Instagram, wherein (2) ______ are busy creating perfect stories about ourselves. For example, pictures (3) ______ perfect holidays never show the stress of traffic snarls and a host of (4) ______ problems faced. We soon begin to believe in this perfect online self to be (5) ______ real one.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
questions.explanation: The clause needs a subject that matches 'ourselves': 'wherein we are busy'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. According to Harari, a leading thinker, we are all busy (1) ______ a fantasy self online. It is the age of Facebook and Instagram, wherein (2) ______ are busy creating perfect stories about ourselves. For example, pictures (3) ______ perfect holidays never show the stress of traffic snarls and a host of (4) ______ problems faced. We soon begin to believe in this perfect online self to be (5) ______ real one.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3.
questions.explanation: 'Pictures of perfect holidays': pictures showing them.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. According to Harari, a leading thinker, we are all busy (1) ______ a fantasy self online. It is the age of Facebook and Instagram, wherein (2) ______ are busy creating perfect stories about ourselves. For example, pictures (3) ______ perfect holidays never show the stress of traffic snarls and a host of (4) ______ problems faced. We soon begin to believe in this perfect online self to be (5) ______ real one.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.
questions.explanation: 'A host of other problems': problems besides the traffic snarls.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. According to Harari, a leading thinker, we are all busy (1) ______ a fantasy self online. It is the age of Facebook and Instagram, wherein (2) ______ are busy creating perfect stories about ourselves. For example, pictures (3) ______ perfect holidays never show the stress of traffic snarls and a host of (4) ______ problems faced. We soon begin to believe in this perfect online self to be (5) ______ real one.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5.
questions.explanation: The one particular self that is real takes the definite article: 'to be the real one'.

questions.text: ‘Craniology’ is related to ‘Skull’ and ‘Oology’ is related to ‘Eggs’ in the same way as ‘Pedology’ is related to _____.
questions.explanation: Craniology is the study of skulls and oology the study of eggs; pedology is the study of soil.

questions.text: If 31 August 2008 was Sunday, then what was the day of the week on 30 August 2012?
questions.explanation: From 31 August 2008 to 31 August 2012 is 4 years with one leap day (29 February 2012): 1,461 days = 208 weeks + 5 days. So 31 August 2012 was a Friday (Sunday + 5) and 30 August 2012 a Thursday.

questions.text: M is the only son of R. P is the sister of Q. X is the father of C, who is the wife of R. Q is the daughter of X's only daughter. How is M related to X?
questions.explanation: C is R's wife and M is R's only son, so M is C's son. C is X's daughter, so M is X's grandson.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. {6, 15, 27}
questions.explanation: 6, 15 and 27 are 3 × 2, 3 × 5 and 3 × 9: they are in the ratio 2 : 5 : 9. So are 4, 10 and 18 (2 × 2, 2 × 5, 2 × 9).

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: In CGLR, QUZF and NRWC the letters move +4, +5, +6 (wrapping round after Z). LPTA moves +4, +4, +7, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 7, 9, 14, 24, ?, 67
In a certain code language, CHECK is written as 6165622 and SURGE is written as 392136145. How will PRIEST be written as in that language?
questions.explanation: SSC's key follows the rule CHECK shows: each consonant is written as twice its place in the alphabet and each vowel as its place (C = 6, H = 16, E = 5, K = 22). PRIEST → 32, 36, 9, 5, 38, 40 = 3236953840. SURGE's code as printed fits the rule except that S, which should be 38, appears as 39; with S = 39 no option would fit.

questions.text: Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given words in the order in which they appear in an English dictionary. 1. Pleasant 2. Placard 3. Plentiful 4. Pleased 5. Plight
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Placard (2), Pleasant (1), Pleased (4), Plentiful (3), Plight (5). 'Pla' comes before 'Ple', 'Pleasa' before 'Pleased', 'Plea' before 'Plen', and 'Ple' before 'Pli'.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 10 –15 × 9 ÷ 6 + 8 = 8
questions.explanation: Interchanging − and ÷: 10 ÷ 15 × 9 − 6 + 8 = 6 − 6 + 8 = 8.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some teachers are graduates. Some graduates are females. All females are women. Conclusions: I. Some females are teachers. II. Some women are teachers. III. All women are females.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow.
questions.explanation: The teachers who are graduates need not be the graduates who are females, so neither I nor II follows; all females are women, but not all women need be females, so III does not follow either.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given letter series will complete the series. a c _ d a _ d d a _ _ d a c _ d
questions.explanation: With d, c, c, d, d in the blanks the block acdd repeats: acdd acdd acdd acdd.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. DGKP : BJGU :: HKOT : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move −2, +3, −4, +5: D → B, G → J, K → G, P → U. Likewise H → F, K → N, O → K, T → Y: FNKY.

questions.text: Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the word that is different.
questions.explanation: The potato is a tuber, an underground stem; the cucumber, pumpkin and bean are fruits that grow above ground.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (11, 5, 246)
questions.explanation: The third number is the square of the first plus the cube of the second: 11² + 5³ = 121 + 125 = 246. Likewise 14² + 6³ = 196 + 216 = 412.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and the fifth number is related to the sixth number. 12 : 146 :: ? : 443 :: 16 : 258
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first plus 2: 12² + 2 = 146 and 16² + 2 = 258. So ?² + 2 = 443, ?² = 441 and ? = 21.

questions.text: In a certain code language, HIGHER is written as JIIHSF. How will CODING be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each pair of letters is swapped and every letter then moves one place forward: HI GH ER → IH HG RE → JI IH SF. So CO DI NG → OC ID GN → PD JE HO: PDJEHO.

questions.text: Which of the following teams has won the Indian Premier League (IPL) trophy five times as of November 2020?
questions.explanation: Mumbai Indians beat Delhi Capitals in the IPL 2020 final for their fifth title, after 2013, 2015, 2017 and 2019.

questions.text: Second generation computers (1955-1964) were made of:
questions.explanation: Second-generation computers used transistors in place of the vacuum tubes of the first generation; integrated circuits came with the third.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India details 'Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth'?
questions.explanation: Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

questions.text: Where were the terracotta models of the plough excavated in Harappan civilisation?
questions.explanation: Terracotta models of the plough have been found at Banawali in Haryana and at sites in Cholistan.

questions.text: Who among the following started the construction of the Qutub Minar?
questions.explanation: Qutb-ud-din Aibak began the Qutub Minar in Delhi; his son-in-law Iltutmish added further storeys.

questions.text: Which of the following institutions conducts the survey on employment and unemployment?
options: National Institution of Economic and Social Research
National Council of Applied Economic Research
questions.explanation: The National Sample Survey Organisation (since 2019 part of the National Statistical Office) carries out India's surveys of employment and unemployment, now the Periodic Labour Force Survey.

questions.text: In which year did Akbar analyse the state revenue statistics for the last 10 years, which contained information on price fluctuations and land productivity?
questions.explanation: Akbar's revenue system of 1580 (the dahsala) rested on a survey, under Todar Mal, of crop yields, prices and areas cultivated over the ten years 1570 to 1580.

questions.text: Which of the following provisions and the constitutions of different countries from which they have been adopted in the Constitution of India has been INCORRECTLY paired?
options: The idea of the rule of law - British Constitution
Charter of Fundamental rights - United States Constitution
Directive Principles of State Policy - Irish Constitution
Principals of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity - Canadian Constitution
questions.explanation: Liberty, equality and fraternity were borrowed from the French Constitution, not the Canadian. The rule of law is British, the fundamental rights American and the Directive Principles Irish.

questions.text: Purna, Manjira and Pranhita are tributaries of:
questions.explanation: The Purna, the Manjira and the Pranhita are tributaries of the Godavari.

questions.text: With which bank did Indian Army sign an MoU for serving retired personnel in December 2020?
questions.explanation: In December 2020 Bank of Baroda renewed its MoU with the Indian Army, and signed MoUs with the Navy and the Coast Guard, for its 'Baroda Military Salary Package' for serving and retired personnel.

questions.text: When an economy is facing inflation, what will the central bank of the country do?
options: Reduce the cost of money by reducing rates
Raise the cost of money by raising rates
Set up more ATMs to help the public
questions.explanation: To curb inflation a central bank tightens money: it raises its policy rates, which makes borrowing dearer and slows spending. Printing more notes would add to inflation.

questions.text: Which everyday morning ritual is part of quantum mechanics?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the alarm clock: the time it keeps is ultimately set from atomic clocks, which define the second by the frequency of a quantum transition in caesium atoms. The question is loosely put, since chemistry such as making tea also rests on quantum mechanics.

questions.text: Which of the following is a dance form of West Bengal where there is a confluence of dancing, singing, drama and recital?
questions.explanation: Alkap, from Murshidabad and Malda in West Bengal, combines dance, song, drama and recitation. Tippani and Hudo are folk dances of Gujarat, and Bhavai a folk form of Gujarat and Rajasthan.

questions.text: Which of the following is a capacity-building scheme that was launched in 2020 for civil servants aimed at upgrading the post-recruitment training mechanism of the officers and employees at all levels?
questions.explanation: Mission Karmayogi, the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building, was approved by the Union Cabinet in September 2020.

questions.text: Who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature 2020?
questions.explanation: The American poet Louise Glück won the 2020 Nobel Prize in Literature. Genzel, Penrose and Ghez shared the 2020 physics prize.

questions.text: In which of the following options is the substance INCORRECTLY paired with the acid present in that substance?
questions.explanation: Lemons contain citric acid; lactic acid is the acid of curd and sour milk.

questions.text: Which Indian film was the first film to win the ‘Palme d'Or’ at Cannes Film Festival?
questions.explanation: Chetan Anand's Neecha Nagar shared the Grand Prix, the top award at the first Cannes Film Festival in 1946; the Palme d'Or replaced that award in 1955.

questions.text: How many bits does an IP address consist of?
questions.explanation: An IPv4 address is 32 bits long, written as four 8-bit numbers; the newer IPv6 addresses are 128 bits.

questions.text: Who among the following is the head coach of India’s men’s (Senior) football team as of December 2020?
questions.explanation: Igor Stimac of Croatia took charge of India's senior men's football team in 2019, succeeding Stephen Constantine, and held the post until 2024.

questions.text: Which of the following ships was launched on 14 December 2020 in Kolkata?
questions.explanation: INS Himgiri, the first Project 17A frigate built by Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers, was launched in Kolkata on 14 December 2020.

questions.text: Who among the following is the first table tennis player to win the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award?
questions.explanation: Manika Batra received the Khel Ratna in 2020, the first table tennis player to do so.

questions.text: India's longest LPG pipeline is from Jamnagar to ______.
questions.explanation: GAIL's Jamnagar–Loni pipeline, from Gujarat to Loni in Uttar Pradesh near Delhi, was India's longest LPG pipeline at the time.

questions.text: According to ‘Population estimation of tigers in reserves for 2018-19’ which of the following is India's largest tiger reserve?
questions.explanation: SSC's key reads 'largest' as holding the most tigers, which is what the cited estimate counts: 231 in Corbett, more than in any other reserve (Nagarhole 127, Bandipur 126, Dudhwa 82). By area Dudhwa (about 2,200 km²) is larger than Corbett (about 1,290 km²), and the largest reserve of all is Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam.

questions.text: Onions produce the chemical irritant known as syn-propanethial-S-oxide; this stimulates the eyes' ______ glands which release tears.
questions.explanation: Tears come from the lachrymal (lacrimal) glands; the parotid, sublingual and submandibular glands make saliva.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. COMPLETE
questions.explanation: 'Complete' means whole or entire; its opposite is 'partial'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The prisoner was very upset and angry and there was ______ in her voice.
questions.explanation: The prisoner was upset and angry, so her voice carried 'bitterness', resentful anger.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. We've decided to spend our time play online games as we will not go out on a vacation this year.
questions.explanation: 'Spend time' is followed by a gerund: 'spend our time playing online games'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'convene'.

questions.text: Select the option which means the same as the group of words given. One who cannot be reformed or changed
questions.explanation: An incorrigible person cannot be corrected or reformed. 'Indelible' means that cannot be erased, 'infallible' never wrong and 'invincible' that cannot be defeated.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, select the one that gives their correct order. A. It becomes evident from their stories that their desire to succeed became their driving force, their purpose in life. B. We read many stories of people who overcame serious disabilities. C. This is what made a paralytic, Wilma Rudolf, win three gold medals on the track in the 1960 Olympics. D. They wanted to prove to themselves that they could do it in spite of all odds - and they did it.
questions.explanation: B introduces stories of people who overcame disabilities, A says their desire to succeed drove them, D says what they wanted to prove, and C ('This is what made...') gives an example of it: BADC.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A person who pretends to have morals and beliefs that he or she doesn’t believe in
questions.explanation: A hypocrite claims morals or beliefs that he or she does not really hold.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. We mow the lawn once every month.
options: The lawn was mowed once every month.
The lawn has been mowed once every month.
The lawn is mowed once every month.
The lawn will be mowed once every month.
questions.explanation: The simple present 'mow' becomes 'is mowed' in the passive: 'The lawn is mowed once every month.'

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order. A. They were covered with mud from head to foot. B. Two men were fighting, crying out and cursing, at the bottom of the ditch. C. “Stop that!” shouted the sergeant. D. Three or four soldiers, holding torches, were standing around a ditch.
questions.explanation: D sets the scene (soldiers with torches round a ditch), B shows the two men fighting in it, A describes them covered in mud, and C, the sergeant's shout, ends it: DBAC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. Ashoka was one of “the greater king” of India.
questions.explanation: 'One of the' takes a superlative and a plural noun: 'one of the greatest kings of India'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. NONDESCRIPT
questions.explanation: 'Nondescript' means dull, with nothing distinctive; its opposite is 'distinguished'. 'Ordinary' and 'common' are near synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A blessing in disguise
options: something good that isn’t recognised at first
a person who blesses others quietly
questions.explanation: 'A blessing in disguise' is something good that at first seemed bad or went unrecognised.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. The supervisor said to the staff, "Make sure that every room is disinfected properly."
options: The supervisor instructed the staff to make sure that every room had been disinfected properly.
The supervisor instructed the staff to make sure that every room was being disinfected properly.
The supervisor instructs the staff to make sure that every room is disinfected properly.
The supervisor instructed the staff to make sure that every room was disinfected properly.
questions.explanation: An order is reported with 'instructed ... to', and after the past reporting verb 'is disinfected' becomes 'was disinfected'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Needle in a haystack
questions.explanation: 'A needle in a haystack' is something almost impossible to find.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. COMPLICATED
questions.explanation: 'Complicated' means 'complex'; 'simplified' and 'plain' are its opposites.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Amphan, the more severe cyclone in the Bay of Bengal since the super cyclone of 1999, made landfall in the afternoon on Wednesday.
questions.explanation: 'Since the super cyclone of 1999' compares it with every cyclone in that period, so it needs the superlative: 'the most severe cyclone'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. Just like a spider that spins its own web and later destroys it, human beings can also destroy the web of desires that “engulfs it”.
questions.explanation: The pronoun refers to 'human beings', which is plural: 'the web of desires that engulfs them'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. DELECTABLE
questions.explanation: 'Delectable' means delicious or delightful: 'luscious'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. With a lot of difficulty, he could ______ only two tickets for the train from Mumbai to Ranchi.
questions.explanation: To 'procure' is to obtain something, especially with effort, as tickets here. One 'incurs' costs or losses and 'attains' goals.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Students in the sixth grade of a certain school in Navi Mumbai love (1)______ History lessons, thanks to a novel teaching aid. It (2) ______ not surprising given the fact that their study material (3) ______ comic books and they use their textbooks for (4) ______ to put things into perspective. Besides, students are (5) ______ to tap other sources of information as well.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: The students love 'their' History lessons: the possessive for 'students'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Students in the sixth grade of a certain school in Navi Mumbai love (1)______ History lessons, thanks to a novel teaching aid. It (2) ______ not surprising given the fact that their study material (3) ______ comic books and they use their textbooks for (4) ______ to put things into perspective. Besides, students are (5) ______ to tap other sources of information as well.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: 'It' is singular and the passage is in the present: 'It is not surprising'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Students in the sixth grade of a certain school in Navi Mumbai love (1)______ History lessons, thanks to a novel teaching aid. It (2) ______ not surprising given the fact that their study material (3) ______ comic books and they use their textbooks for (4) ______ to put things into perspective. Besides, students are (5) ______ to tap other sources of information as well.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'their study material' takes 'includes', in the present like the rest of the sentence.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Students in the sixth grade of a certain school in Navi Mumbai love (1)______ History lessons, thanks to a novel teaching aid. It (2) ______ not surprising given the fact that their study material (3) ______ comic books and they use their textbooks for (4) ______ to put things into perspective. Besides, students are (5) ______ to tap other sources of information as well.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: The textbooks are used for 'reference': they look things up in them to put things into perspective.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Students in the sixth grade of a certain school in Navi Mumbai love (1)______ History lessons, thanks to a novel teaching aid. It (2) ______ not surprising given the fact that their study material (3) ______ comic books and they use their textbooks for (4) ______ to put things into perspective. Besides, students are (5) ______ to tap other sources of information as well.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: Students are 'encouraged' to tap other sources: urged and supported to do so. 'Boosted', 'heartened' and 'cheered' do not take 'to' and a verb in this sense.

questions.text: Select the word-pair in which the two words are related in the same way as are the two words in the following word-pair. Bread : Wheat
questions.explanation: Bread is made from wheat, as sauce is made from tomatoes.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some magicians are psychologists. All psychologists are tourists. Conclusions: I. All tourists are psychologists. II. All magicians are tourists.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: All psychologists are tourists, but not all tourists need be psychologists (I fails); only the magicians who are psychologists must be tourists, and nothing is known of the rest (II fails).

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. RIGHT : UGKKR : : CHAOS : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +3, −2, +4, +3, −2: R → U, I → G, G → K, H → K, T → R. Likewise C → F, H → F, A → E, O → R, S → Q: FFERQ.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation. 7 * 96 * 8 * 39 * 25 = 70
Five of the following six numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the number that is different from the rest. 8, 24, 125, 343, 1331, 2197
questions.explanation: 8, 125, 343, 1331 and 2197 are the cubes of the primes 2, 5, 7, 11 and 13. 24 is not a cube.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (3, 3, 11)
questions.explanation: Twice the sum of the first two numbers, minus 1, gives the third: 2 × (3 + 3) − 1 = 11. Likewise 2 × (7 + 11) − 1 = 35; the other options give 17, 25 and 41, not 18, 26 and 47.

questions.text: Three of the following four number triads are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.explanation: In (3, 6, 9), (1, 2, 1) and (4, 8, 16) the third number is the square of the first. In (2, 4, 8) it is 8, not 2² = 4.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. Dolphins : Click : : Jackals : ?
questions.explanation: The sound a dolphin makes is a click, and a jackal's is a howl.

questions.text: In a certain code language, VIRTUE is written as XCBYAN. How will MODEST be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each half of the word is reversed (VIR TUE → RIV EUT) and the letters then move +6 and −6 in turn, giving XCBYAN. MODEST → DOM TSE → D + 6, O − 6, M + 6, T − 6, S + 6, E − 6 = JISNYY.

questions.text: If in a code language, DISK is coded as 65 and WIRE is coded as 53, then how will you code CELL?
questions.explanation: The code is the sum of the letters' positions counted from Z (Z = 1, A = 26): DISK = 23 + 18 + 8 + 16 = 65 and WIRE = 4 + 18 + 9 + 22 = 53. CELL = 24 + 22 + 15 + 15 = 76.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number. 27 : 702 : : 12 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the first times one less than itself: 27 × 26 = 702. Likewise 12 × 11 = 132.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 5, 9, 16, 31, 60, 119, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is double the one before, minus 1 and minus 2 in turn: 5 × 2 − 1 = 9, 9 × 2 − 2 = 16, ... 60 × 2 − 1 = 119, so 119 × 2 − 2 = 236.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. k l _ p n _ k l m p _ b _ l m _ n b k _ m p n b
options: m, n, b, p, k, l
k, l, m, n, b, p
m, b, n, k, p, l
n, m, b, l, p, k
questions.explanation: With m, b, n, k, p, l in the blanks the block klmpnb repeats: klmpnb klmpnb klmpnb klmpnb.

questions.text: Rohit is three times the age of his son Rishabh. Five years ago, he was four times older than Rishabh. What is Rohit’s age at present?
questions.explanation: SSC's key reads 'four times older' in its usual sense in these questions, four times as old. With Rishabh x and Rohit 3x: 3x − 5 = 4(x − 5), so x = 15 and Rohit is 45. (Read strictly as five times as old, it would give 30, also an option.)

questions.text: Three of the following four letter-clusters are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: ULO, ILO and ENO are vowel, consonant, vowel, each ending in O. UOD is vowel, vowel, consonant.

questions.text: Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the word that is different.
questions.explanation: Horde, ambush and herd are collective nouns (an ambush of tigers, a herd of cattle). A piglet is a young pig.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of ‘The Brahma Sutra – The Philosophy of Spiritual life’?
questions.explanation: Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan wrote 'The Brahma Sutra: The Philosophy of Spiritual Life', a translation of the Brahma Sutra with his commentary.

questions.text: Which company invested ₹11,400 crores during the financial year 2019-2020 across its market payments and wholesale business units in India to strengthen its foothold in India?
questions.explanation: According to regulatory filings reported in December 2020, Amazon put about ₹11,400 crore into its Indian marketplace (Amazon Seller Services), payments (Amazon Pay) and wholesale units in 2019-20.

questions.text: Who became the Chief Justice of Jammu and Kashmir High Court in December 2020?
questions.explanation: Pankaj Mithal, a judge of the Allahabad High Court, was appointed Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh on 31 December 2020, after Gita Mittal retired; he took oath on 4 January 2021.

questions.text: A mass of snow and ice that moves slowly under the influence of gravity along a confined course away from its place of accumulation is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A glacier is a mass of ice and snow that moves slowly downhill under its own weight, away from where it accumulated.

questions.text: Who among the following is one of the seven winners of the Young Champions of the Earth 2020 prize given by UNEP?
questions.explanation: Vidyut Mohan, co-founder of Takachar, which turns crop residue into fuel and fertiliser, was one of UNEP's seven Young Champions of the Earth in 2020.

questions.text: As of January 2021, how many Olympic medals did India win in the sport of field hockey?
questions.explanation: India had won 11 Olympic medals in hockey: 8 gold, 1 silver (1960) and 2 bronze (1968, 1972).

questions.text: In 711 CE, Arab general ______ conquered Sind, which became a part of the Caliph’s domain.
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Qasim, a general of the Umayyad Caliphate, conquered Sind in 711-712 CE.

questions.text: On which of the following days is World Computer Literacy Day observed?
questions.explanation: World Computer Literacy Day, started by NIIT in 2001, is observed on 2 December.

questions.text: Which of the following recommends Minimum Support Prices for crops in India?
questions.explanation: The Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) recommends the MSPs; the government then announces them.

questions.text: Who among the following was adjudged as the 'Player of the Series' in the Australia versus India T20I series played in December 2020?
questions.explanation: Hardik Pandya was Player of the Series as India won the December 2020 T20I series in Australia 2-1.

questions.text: A message that tries to trick a person into providing information such as his social security number, bank account information or login username and password for a website is a type of malware called:
questions.explanation: Phishing messages pose as a trusted source to trick people into giving away personal details such as bank or login information.

questions.text: What is the molecular formula for hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid is HCl. H₂SO₄ is sulphuric acid, HNO₃ nitric acid and KOH potassium hydroxide, a base.

questions.text: Mount Jopuno is situated in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Mount Jopuno is a peak in western Sikkim, in the Kangchenjunga region.

questions.text: From which of the following sources does the brain get energy?
questions.explanation: The brain runs almost entirely on glucose carried by the blood.

questions.text: Which of the following is the largest river island in India?
questions.explanation: Majuli, in the Brahmaputra in Assam, is the largest river island in India.

questions.text: What is the minimum age requirement for appointment as a Governor?
questions.explanation: Under Article 157 a Governor must be a citizen of India who has completed 35 years of age.

questions.text: Which of the following was included as an official Olympic sport in December 2020?
questions.explanation: In December 2020 the IOC added breaking (breakdancing) to the programme of the Paris 2024 Olympics.

questions.text: Who among the following was appointed as the Chairman of the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in December 2019?
questions.explanation: Girish Chandra Chaturvedi, a former Petroleum Secretary, became Chairman of the NSE's governing board in December 2019 with SEBI's approval.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was the President of the Indian National Congress when India won its freedom in the year 1947?
questions.explanation: J. B. Kripalani was President of the Congress at independence: he presided over the Meerut session of November 1946 and resigned in November 1947, when Rajendra Prasad succeeded him.

questions.text: ISRO launched ______, it’s 42nd communication satellite, in December 2020.
questions.explanation: CMS-01, launched by PSLV-C50 on 17 December 2020, was ISRO's 42nd communication satellite.

questions.text: As of December 2020, under the Startup India Initiative, the monthly allowance for startups with women as founder/co-founder was ______ per month for a period of one year.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives ₹20,000: in December 2020 the Startup India portal's page for women entrepreneurs listed a monthly allowance of ₹20,000 for one year for startups with a woman founder or co-founder, under the Andaman & Nicobar Islands policy. It is a Union Territory's incentive shown on the portal, not a national Startup India grant.

questions.text: Who among the following won the Golden Globe 2020 award for ‘Best Performance by an Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama’?
questions.explanation: Joaquin Phoenix won the 2020 Golden Globe for Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama for 'Joker'.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of the three parallel ranges of the Himalayas in its longitudinal extent?
questions.explanation: The Himalayas run in three parallel ranges: the Himadri (Greater), the Himachal (Lesser) and the Shiwaliks (Outer). 'Himshikha' is not one of them.

questions.text: With which of the following musical instruments is the musician Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma associated?
questions.explanation: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma was a santoor maestro, credited with making it a classical concert instrument.

questions.text: Which of the following festivals is called the month of merits and is celebrated between May and June?
questions.explanation: Saga Dawa, the 'month of merits', falls in the fourth Tibetan lunar month (May-June) and marks the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and parinirvana; it is celebrated in Sikkim.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To add insult to injury
options: to work hard on making up
questions.explanation: To 'add insult to injury' is to make a bad situation worse.

questions.text: Given below are four sentences in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. Then he started on his eighteen kilometer expedition back to his village. B. Mohan first equipped himself with a long, sturdy stick. C. At several points, he lost the road and had to swim his way ahead. D. It was a journey he would never forget where he had to use his stick constantly to locate the road.
questions.explanation: B says what Mohan did first, A ('Then') sets him off on the journey, D describes the journey and C gives its hardships: BADC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. He is very impulsive and does things “without rhyme or reason”.
questions.explanation: Doing things 'without rhyme or reason' is doing them for no sensible reason that could explain them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. LAVISH
questions.explanation: 'Lavish' means extravagant or generous; its opposite is 'frugal', sparing with money. 'Excessive' and 'luxurious' are close to synonyms.

questions.text: Examine the four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order. A. Next, keep tapping the pot on all sides and at the bottom until the plant loosens. B. Finally, slide the plant gently and remove the old potting mix on a newspaper. C. The first thing to do when repotting is to remove the plant from the current pot. D. Begin by holding the plant gently, and turning the pot sideways.
questions.explanation: C names the first step, D begins it ('Begin by'), A follows with 'Next' and B ends with 'Finally': CDAB.

questions.text: Fill in the blank with most appropriate word. This part of the sea ______ with sharks.
questions.explanation: To 'teem with' is to be full of: that part of the sea is full of sharks.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. AFFINITY
questions.explanation: 'Affinity' is a natural liking or attraction; its opposite is 'aversion', a strong dislike. 'Inclination' and 'attraction' are close to synonyms.

questions.text: Select the misspelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'arrival'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. LIVID
questions.explanation: 'Livid' means very angry: 'furious'.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. He drove the car very carefully on the hilly terrain.
options: The car was driven very carefully on the hilly terrain.
The car is being driven very carefully on the hilly terrain.
The car has been driven very carefully on the hilly terrain.
The car is driven very carefully on the hilly terrain.
questions.explanation: The simple past active 'drove' becomes the simple past passive 'was driven', with the car as subject.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. If you rent a house near your office, it will save you time as well as also money.
questions.explanation: 'As well as' already means 'and also', so 'also' is redundant: 'it will save you time as well as money'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. Small desert animals burrow underground “across the days” and come out only at night.
questions.explanation: Something done in the daytime is done 'during the day', in contrast with 'at night'.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. “I love Bollywood music,” Deepu said to Reena.
options: Deepu told Reena that he loved Bollywood music.
Deepu will say to Reena that he loved Bollywood music.
Deepu says to Reena that he loves Bollywood music.
Deepu had told Reena that he loved Bollywood music.
questions.explanation: 'Said to' becomes 'told', 'I' becomes 'he' and the present 'love' moves back to the past 'loved'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Killing of one’s mother
questions.explanation: Matricide is the killing of one's mother; patricide is the killing of one's father, infanticide of an infant and regicide of a king.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Notwithstanding we were / all busy that weekend / we had to / cancel the outing.
questions.explanation: Being busy is the reason the outing was cancelled, so the clause needs 'As' or 'Since': 'As we were all busy that weekend, we had to cancel the outing.' 'Notwithstanding' means 'in spite of'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'titillate'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. CALLOUS
questions.explanation: 'Callous' means showing no concern for others' feelings: 'insensitive'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given words. a period of two weeks
questions.explanation: A fortnight is a period of two weeks.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement' I must have dropped “one” of my gloves in the car.
questions.explanation: 'One of' is followed by a plural noun, and 'one of my gloves' says that a single glove was dropped, so no change is needed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. It is ______ to see so many of our fellow Indians help the migrants in their struggle to go home.
questions.explanation: 'Heartening' means encouraging or cheering: the sight of people helping lifts the spirits. 'Savouring' and 'relishing' mean enjoying something, which does not fit 'It is ___ to see'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. In the ‘Kingdom of Fools’, both the king and the ministers were complete fools. They didn’t want to do things (1)______ other kingdoms, so they decided to (2)______ night into day and day into night. They (3)______ that everyone should be awake at night, (4)_______ their lands and run their (5)______ only after dark and should go to bed as soon as the sun came up.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: They did not want to do things 'like' other kingdoms, that is, in the same way as them.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. In the ‘Kingdom of Fools’, both the king and the ministers were complete fools. They didn’t want to do things (1)______ other kingdoms, so they decided to (2)______ night into day and day into night. They (3)______ that everyone should be awake at night, (4)_______ their lands and run their (5)______ only after dark and should go to bed as soon as the sun came up.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: They decided to 'change' night into day: the phrase is 'change into'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. In the ‘Kingdom of Fools’, both the king and the ministers were complete fools. They didn’t want to do things (1)______ other kingdoms, so they decided to (2)______ night into day and day into night. They (3)______ that everyone should be awake at night, (4)_______ their lands and run their (5)______ only after dark and should go to bed as soon as the sun came up.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: The king and his ministers 'ordered' that everyone should be awake at night.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. In the ‘Kingdom of Fools’, both the king and the ministers were complete fools. They didn’t want to do things (1)______ other kingdoms, so they decided to (2)______ night into day and day into night. They (3)______ that everyone should be awake at night, (4)_______ their lands and run their (5)______ only after dark and should go to bed as soon as the sun came up.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: To 'till' the land is to plough and prepare it for crops.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. In the ‘Kingdom of Fools’, both the king and the ministers were complete fools. They didn’t want to do things (1)______ other kingdoms, so they decided to (2)______ night into day and day into night. They (3)______ that everyone should be awake at night, (4)_______ their lands and run their (5)______ only after dark and should go to bed as soon as the sun came up.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: People were to 'run their business', their trade and work, only after dark.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: In BDMS, HKPT and KMPV each letter comes later in the alphabet than the one before it. MIGF runs backwards, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: ₹481 is distributed among A, B and C in such a way that B gets two-thirds of what A gets and C gets three-fourths of what B gets. How much does B get?

Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All statements are answers. Some statements are questions. Conclusions: I. No question is a statement. II. Some answers are statements. III. Some questions are statements.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
Either conclusion I or III follows
Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: All statements are answers, so some answers are statements (II). Some statements are questions, so some questions are statements (III), which rules out I.

questions.text: If 'A + B' means 'A is the mother of B', 'A × B' means 'A is the sister of B', and 'A * B' means 'A is the daughter of B', then how is R related to P in the following expression? 'R + V × Q × M * P'
