questions.explanation: A cofferdam is a temporary enclosure built to keep water out of an area, so that work such as laying a dam's or a bridge's foundations can be done in the dry.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. He often spread rumors that his neighbours were thieves. B. After being released, one of them sued him for wrongly accusing them. C. One evening, some of them were arrested by the police. D. After the investigation, they were proven innocent.
questions.explanation: A says he called his neighbours thieves, C has some of them arrested, D has them proven innocent and B has one of them sue him after release: ACDB.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in the active or passive voice. Teachers should cover all the topics in the syllabus.
options: All the topics in the syllabus should be covered by teachers.
Teachers should be covered the syllabus in all the topics.
Teachers should be covered all the topics in the syllabus.
All the topics in the syllabus should cover teachers.
questions.explanation: The passive of 'should cover' is 'should be covered', with the topics as subject: 'All the topics in the syllabus should be covered by teachers.'

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. The yoga instructor said to us, “Doing yoga daily will help you to develop a healthy mind and body."
options: The yoga instructor said to us that daily yoga will help us to develop a healthy mind and body.
The yoga instructor was told them that daily yoga would help them to develop a healthy mind and body.
The yoga instructor said to us that doing daily yoga will be helping us to develop a healthy mind and body.
The yoga instructor told us that doing yoga daily would help us to develop a healthy mind and body.
questions.explanation: 'Said to us' becomes 'told us', 'you' becomes 'us' and 'will' moves back to 'would': 'told us that doing yoga daily would help us to develop a healthy mind and body'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution ’. My daughter could not find the words to say why she “has been crying” on a day when she should have been happy.
questions.explanation: The sentence is set in the past ('could not find'), so the reason is in the past too: 'why she was crying'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'failure'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. For each question, four ______ are given as options.
questions.explanation: 'Alternatives' are choices to pick from; 'alterations' are changes and 'altercations' quarrels.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, select the one that gives their correct order. A. I saw a middle-aged man sitting beneath the tree with his knees drawn up to his chest. B. When I was a street away from my house, I saw a huge banyan tree to my right. C. My heart went out to him as he was crying bitterly. D. His head was bowed and his body was shivering continuously.
questions.explanation: B brings in the banyan tree, A the man sitting beneath it, D describes him and C gives the narrator's response to his crying: BADC.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. the scientific study of the universe and planets
questions.explanation: Astronomy is the scientific study of the universe and the bodies in it; astrology claims the stars and planets influence human affairs.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Severity
questions.explanation: 'Severity' means seriousness or harshness.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Eat or drink food quickly and in large amounts
questions.explanation: To 'gulp' is to swallow food or drink quickly and in large mouthfuls; to 'sip' is to drink in small amounts.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. The green shirt is too “lose for me” to wear.
questions.explanation: 'Loose' (not tight) is the adjective needed; 'lose' is a verb, to misplace or fail to win.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A grey area
options: A special part of the brain
questions.explanation: A 'grey area' is a situation that is unclear, not clearly one thing or the other.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To be in the dark
options: to always be in a bad mood about darkness
to learn to face dark places without fear
to be afraid of darkness and refuse to go out at night
to not know something others are aware of
questions.explanation: To 'be in the dark' about something is not to know about it while others do.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. GRACEFUL
questions.explanation: 'Graceful' means smooth and elegant in movement; its opposite is 'awkward'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Select the segment that contains a grammatical error from the given options. I'm sorry, sir. / How many is / the fine for / returning the books late?
questions.explanation: A fine is an amount of money, asked about with 'how much': 'How much is the fine for returning the books late?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Constant
questions.explanation: 'Constant' means unchanging; its opposite is 'fluctuating', rising and falling. 'Unchanging' and 'static' are synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. EMERGE
questions.explanation: To 'emerge' is to come out into view: to 'appear'.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The children were warning not to try to climb the cliffs as they were very steep.
questions.explanation: The children received the warning, so the verb must be passive: 'The children were warned not to try to climb the cliffs'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. During her vacation, Shanta ______ her mother when she went to work in the mall.
questions.explanation: To 'accompany' someone is to go somewhere with them: Shanta went along with her mother.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. These are the various symbols used on garbage bins. The wheeled-bin (1) ______ which is crossed out indicates that the item (2) ______ be disposed of separately from household waste. The item should be handed in for recycling (3) ______ to local environmental regulations for waste disposal. By (4) ______ a marked item from household waste, you will help reduce the volume of waste sent to landfills. It will also (5) ______ any potential negative impact on human health and the environment. For more information, please contact your nearest civic official.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The passage is about the 'symbols' used on garbage bins; the crossed-out wheeled bin is one of them.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. These are the various symbols used on garbage bins. The wheeled-bin (1) ______ which is crossed out indicates that the item (2) ______ be disposed of separately from household waste. The item should be handed in for recycling (3) ______ to local environmental regulations for waste disposal. By (4) ______ a marked item from household waste, you will help reduce the volume of waste sent to landfills. It will also (5) ______ any potential negative impact on human health and the environment. For more information, please contact your nearest civic official.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Recycling 'according to' local regulations; 'accordance' would need 'in accordance with'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. These are the various symbols used on garbage bins. The wheeled-bin (1) ______ which is crossed out indicates that the item (2) ______ be disposed of separately from household waste. The item should be handed in for recycling (3) ______ to local environmental regulations for waste disposal. By (4) ______ a marked item from household waste, you will help reduce the volume of waste sent to landfills. It will also (5) ______ any potential negative impact on human health and the environment. For more information, please contact your nearest civic official.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'By separating' a marked item from household waste: keeping it apart, as the passage asks.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. These are the various symbols used on garbage bins. The wheeled-bin (1) ______ which is crossed out indicates that the item (2) ______ be disposed of separately from household waste. The item should be handed in for recycling (3) ______ to local environmental regulations for waste disposal. By (4) ______ a marked item from household waste, you will help reduce the volume of waste sent to landfills. It will also (5) ______ any potential negative impact on human health and the environment. For more information, please contact your nearest civic official.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Separating such items will 'minimise', that is reduce, any harmful impact on health and the environment.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. JOKERS : NKOAVO : : ROMING : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +4 and −4 in turn: J → N, O → K, K → O, E → A, R → V, S → O. So ROMING → V K Q E R C: VKQERC.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. Spoon : Feeding : : Microscope : ?
questions.explanation: A spoon is used for feeding, as a microscope is used for magnifying.

questions.text: Four options have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the option that is different.
questions.explanation: Eczema, psoriasis and vitiligo are skin disorders; scurvy is a disease caused by a lack of vitamin C.

questions.text: Three of the following four numbers are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the number that is different from the rest.
questions.explanation: In 2105, 4328 and 3124 the middle two digits are the product of the first and last: 2 × 5 = 10, 4 × 8 = 32 and 3 × 4 = 12. In 6457, 6 × 7 = 42, not 45.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 34, 39, 50, 67, 90, ?, 162
questions.explanation: The differences are every other prime number: +5, +11, +17, +23, +31, +41 (skipping 7, 13, 19, 29 and 37). So 90 + 31 = 121, and 121 + 41 = 162.

questions.text: In a certain code language, PAINT is written as QZHOU and BASK is written as CZTL. How will MOVIE be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Consonants move one place forward and vowels one place back: P → Q, A → Z, I → H, N → O, T → U. So MOVIE → NNWHD.

questions.text: If in a code language, ROHAN is coded as 3136 and SHYAM is coded as 4356, then how will you code RAM?
questions.explanation: Each code is the square of the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet: ROHAN = 18 + 15 + 8 + 1 + 14 = 56 and 56² = 3136; SHYAM = 66 and 66² = 4356. RAM = 18 + 1 + 13 = 32 and 32² = 1024.

questions.text: What will be the value of the given expression if ‘A’ means ‘+’, ‘B’ means ‘–’, ‘C’ means ‘×’ and ‘D’ means ‘÷’? 15 C 7 B (24 D 8) A 16 C 4 B 21 D 3
Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (11, 20, 81)
questions.explanation: The third number is the square of the difference of the first two: (20 − 11)² = 81. Likewise (36 − 25)² = 11² = 121.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (1, 2, 6)
questions.explanation: Each number is the one before it times one more than itself: 1 × 2 = 2 and 2 × 3 = 6. Likewise 5 × 6 = 30 and 30 × 31 = 930.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some lights are wires. All appliances are lights. All bulbs are appliances. Conclusions: I. Some lights are appliances. II. Some wires are bulbs. III. All bulbs are lights.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions II and III follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.
questions.explanation: All appliances are lights, so some lights are appliances (I); all bulbs are appliances and all appliances are lights, so all bulbs are lights (III). Nothing links wires to bulbs, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. p r _ b n _ r q _ n p _ q b _ p _ q _ n
options: q, p, b, r, r, n, n
q, b, p, n, r, n, r
q, r, n, p, b, r, n
q, p, b, r, n, r, b
questions.explanation: With q, p, b, r, n, r, b in the blanks the block prqbn repeats: prqbn prqbn prqbn prqbn.

questions.text: Arrange the following words in a logical and meaningful order. 1. Eat 2. Rinse 3. Buy 4. Cut 5. Cook
questions.explanation: Food is bought, rinsed, cut, cooked and then eaten: 3, 2, 4, 5, 1.

questions.text: Which of the following four letter-clusters is different from the other letter-clusters?
questions.explanation: The letters of ILORUZ, EGIKOT and ABEGIJ are in alphabetical order; those of ASOJIB are not (after A they run backwards: S, O, J, I, B).

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number. 54 : 81 : : 6 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is one and a half times the first: 54 × 3/2 = 81. Likewise 6 × 3/2 = 9.

questions.text: U is the father of M. V is the wife of K. D is the mother of K's only brother M. How is U related to D?
questions.explanation: D is the mother of M and U is M's father, so U is D's husband.

questions.text: There are three books coded as A, B and C. The price of book A is twice the price of book B and one-third the price of book C. If book C costs ₹84, then what are the costs of book A and book B, respectively?
questions.explanation: A costs one-third of ₹84, which is ₹28, and A is twice B, so B costs ₹14.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. Circle : Arc :: Flower : ?
questions.explanation: An arc is a part of a circle, as a petal is a part of a flower.

questions.text: Which of the following is an input device?
questions.explanation: A scanner feeds images and documents into a computer, so it is an input device; speakers, projectors and monitors are output devices.

questions.text: Rafael Nadal won the Men's 2020 French Open title after beating:
questions.explanation: Nadal beat Novak Djokovic in the 2020 French Open final, played in October, for his 13th title at Roland Garros.

questions.text: As of the financial year 2018-19, which of the following is the largest raw jute producing state in India?
questions.explanation: West Bengal is by far India's largest producer of raw jute, growing most of the country's crop.

questions.text: Which filmmaker won the Best Screenplay award at the Venice film festival for ‘The Disciple’, a Marathi drama, in 2020?
questions.explanation: Chaitanya Tamhane's 'The Disciple' won the Best Screenplay award at the 77th Venice International Film Festival in 2020.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: What was the meaning of ‘Ryot’ in British records in the 18th century?
questions.explanation: In British records 'ryot' meant a peasant cultivator; the Ryotwari settlement was made directly with these peasants.

questions.text: Amarkantak plateau in Chhattisgarh contains an abundant deposit of which of the following minerals?
questions.explanation: NCERT names the Amarkantak plateau, the Maikal hills and the plateau region of Bilaspur-Katni as the main bauxite areas.

questions.text: Which of the following musical instruments is an example of the stringed instruments played by the Manganiars of west Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: The kamaicha, a bowed string instrument, is played by the Manganiar musicians of western Rajasthan; the jhanj and the manjira are cymbals.

questions.text: Who is the founder of the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Yunus founded the Grameen Bank, a pioneer of microcredit; he and the bank shared the 2006 Nobel Peace Prize.

questions.text: Which Indian president used the pocket veto for the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill, 1986?
questions.explanation: In 1986 President Giani Zail Singh neither signed nor returned the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill, the best-known use of the pocket veto.

questions.text: Who among the following kings founded the Maurya empire in ancient India?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya founded the empire in about 321 BC; Bindusara, Ashoka and Dasaratha were later Mauryan kings.

questions.text: Who among the following is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: Under Article 64 the Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

questions.text: A topology for a Local Area Network in which all nodes are individually connected to a central connection point like a hub or switch is called:
questions.explanation: In a star topology every node has its own link to a central hub or switch.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the famous Chitradurga Fort located?
questions.explanation: Chitradurga Fort stands in Chitradurga district of Karnataka.

questions.text: Which of the following movies won the ‘Best Tamil Film’ award at the 66th National Film Awards?
questions.explanation: 'Baaram', directed by Priya Krishnaswamy, won the award for Best Tamil Feature Film at the 66th National Film Awards (for 2018).

questions.text: The 2018 edition of Commonwealth Games was hosted by:
questions.explanation: The 2018 Commonwealth Games were held at Gold Coast, Queensland, in Australia.

questions.text: Which of the following combinations of measures of quantity and unit is NOT a correct match?
questions.explanation: Weight is a force, measured in newtons; the cubic metre is a unit of volume. Kelvin, pascal and kilogram are the SI units of temperature, pressure and mass.

questions.text: As of January 2021, how many Olympic medals did India win in the sport of badminton?
questions.explanation: Saina Nehwal won bronze at London 2012 and PV Sindhu silver at Rio 2016; Sindhu's Tokyo bronze came later, in August 2021.

questions.text: What is the importance of the ozone layer for life on Earth?
options: It protects us from ultraviolet radiation.
It protects us from acidic rainfall.
questions.explanation: The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

questions.text: Which country hosted the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Ministers meeting in October 2020?
questions.explanation: India, then chair of the SCO Council of Heads of Government, hosted the 7th meeting of the SCO Justice Ministers by video conference on 16 October 2020.

questions.text: Primarily, an ant’s sting has which of the following?
questions.explanation: An ant's sting injects formic (methanoic) acid, which is what makes it burn.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a plateau situated in India?
questions.explanation: The Maikal is a range of hills, the eastern part of the Satpuras in Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh; Chota Nagpur, Bundelkhand and Malwa are plateaus.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an effect of an earthquake?
questions.explanation: Earthquakes can set off avalanches, tsunamis and soil liquefaction; they do not bring rainfall.

questions.text: Which of the following government schemes was launched with the objective of delivering government services to citizens electronically by improving online infrastructure and by increasing internet connectivity?
questions.explanation: Digital India, launched in July 2015, aims to deliver government services electronically through better online infrastructure and internet connectivity.

questions.text: The International Conference on Nano Science and Nano Technology (ICONSAT) was held in March 2020 at:
questions.explanation: ICONSAT 2020 was held at Kolkata on 5-7 March 2020, hosted by the S N Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences under the Department of Science and Technology's Nano Mission.

questions.text: Which of the following organisations launched the 'United for Biodiversity' coalition made up of zoos, aquariums, botanical gardens, national parks, natural history and science museums from around the world, on World Wildlife Day 2020?
questions.explanation: The European Commission launched the 'United for Biodiversity' coalition on World Wildlife Day, 3 March 2020.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Until I was / still a little weak, / I decided to walk home / from the metro station.
questions.explanation: 'Until' (up to the time when) makes no sense with 'still'; the clause needs a contrast: 'Though I was still a little weak, I decided to walk home'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. People have overcome poverty, drug addiction, abuse, divorce, mental illness, and virtually every ______ known to man.
questions.explanation: Poverty, addiction, abuse and the rest are difficulties to be overcome: 'virtually every challenge known to man'.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. You can see vast valleys sloping into the distance.
options: Vast valleys had been seen sloping into the distance.
Vast valleys can be seen sloping into the distance.
Vast valleys are seen sloping into the distance.
Vast valleys will be seen sloping into the distance.
questions.explanation: 'Can see' becomes 'can be seen', with the object 'vast valleys' as the subject and the general 'you' dropped: 'Vast valleys can be seen sloping into the distance.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. No other place in India gets “much rainfall” as Mawsynram.
questions.explanation: A comparison of equality takes 'as … as': 'No other place in India gets as much rainfall as Mawsynram.'

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement' It is wise to insure one’s home “on” fire.
questions.explanation: One insures something 'against' a risk: 'It is wise to insure one's home against fire.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. PUNGENT
questions.explanation: 'Pungent' means sharply strong in taste or smell; its opposite is 'mild'. 'Biting' and 'sharp' are close to synonyms.

questions.text: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option. The craze for taking selfies has only increased our ______ with our own image.
questions.explanation: An 'obsession' is a preoccupation one cannot shake off: 'our obsession with our own image'.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The government has announced a gradual reboot of air travel who was halted two months ago due to lockdown.
questions.explanation: 'Who' refers to people; for 'air travel' the relative pronoun is 'which' (or 'that'): 'air travel which was halted two months ago'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. An imaginary, perfect state or place
questions.explanation: A utopia is an imagined place or state of perfection; a dystopia is its opposite, and an arcadia an idealised scene of simple country life.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A bolt from the blue
options: a strange dream that wakes one up suddenly
questions.explanation: A 'bolt from the blue' is a sudden, unexpected event, like lightning from a clear sky.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'rifle'.

questions.text: Examine the four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order. A. That abandoned house is the childhood home of the director Achal Misra, who recreates it in this semi-autobiographical film. B. It is spread over three decades. C. ‘Gamak Ghar’ is a unique movie telling the story of a home. D. These are from 1998 to 2019, wherein the film observes the house age as it is gradually abandoned.
questions.explanation: C introduces the film 'Gamak Ghar', B says it spans three decades, D names them (1998 to 2019) and says the house is gradually abandoned, and A identifies 'that abandoned house': CBDA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. RESPLENDENT
questions.explanation: 'Resplendent' means splendid and shining brightly: 'dazzling'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Cost an arm and a leg
questions.explanation: Something that 'costs an arm and a leg' is extremely expensive.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. INORDINATE
questions.explanation: 'Inordinate' means unreasonably large or excessive; its opposite is 'reasonable'. 'Exorbitant' and 'disproportionate' are close to synonyms.

questions.text: Select the option which means the same as the group of words given. So small or unimportant as to be not worth considering
questions.explanation: 'Negligible' means too small or unimportant to be worth considering; 'feasible' means possible and 'plausible' believable.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. BULL-HEADED
questions.explanation: 'Bull-headed' means obstinate: 'headstrong'.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. “I am going to walk to the market to check which shops are open,” said Anant.
options: Anant said that he was going to walk to the market to check which shops were open.
Anant said that he is going to walk to the market to check which shops were open.
Anant said that he went for a walk to the market to check which shops were open.
Anant said that he will be going to walk to the market to check which shops were open.
questions.explanation: With the reporting verb in the past, 'I am going' becomes 'he was going' and 'are open' becomes 'were open'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order. A. To kill a whale, hunters used spears called harpoons. B. Whale hunting is not easy. C. These harpoons had very long and strong lines tied to them. D. It was extremely difficult and risky before modern methods and machines began to be used.
questions.explanation: B says whale hunting is not easy, D how difficult and risky it was before modern methods, A describes the harpoons hunters used and C the lines tied to 'these harpoons': BDAC.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Many hundreds of years ago, a Brahmin lived in a town in Northern India. He spent many years (1)______ the ancient books and talking to the learned priests (2)______ came to visit the city. After much effort, he (3) ______ the knowledge of a certain spell. He was (4)______ proud of this and guarded his secret (5)______ .

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: 'Spend' time takes the -ing form: 'He spent many years studying the ancient books'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Many hundreds of years ago, a Brahmin lived in a town in Northern India. He spent many years (1)______ the ancient books and talking to the learned priests (2)______ came to visit the city. After much effort, he (3) ______ the knowledge of a certain spell. He was (4)______ proud of this and guarded his secret (5)______ .

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'who', the relative pronoun for people, here the subject of 'came': 'the learned priests who came to visit the city'. 'That' is also used of people, especially in speech, but 'who' is the usual choice; 'which' is for things and 'whom' is an object form.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Many hundreds of years ago, a Brahmin lived in a town in Northern India. He spent many years (1)______ the ancient books and talking to the learned priests (2)______ came to visit the city. After much effort, he (3) ______ the knowledge of a certain spell. He was (4)______ proud of this and guarded his secret (5)______ .

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: Knowledge gained through effort is 'obtained': 'After much effort, he obtained the knowledge of a certain spell.'

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Many hundreds of years ago, a Brahmin lived in a town in Northern India. He spent many years (1)______ the ancient books and talking to the learned priests (2)______ came to visit the city. After much effort, he (3) ______ the knowledge of a certain spell. He was (4)______ proud of this and guarded his secret (5)______ .

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: An adjective such as 'proud' is intensified by 'very': 'He was very proud of this'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Many hundreds of years ago, a Brahmin lived in a town in Northern India. He spent many years (1)______ the ancient books and talking to the learned priests (2)______ came to visit the city. After much effort, he (3) ______ the knowledge of a certain spell. He was (4)______ proud of this and guarded his secret (5)______ .

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: A secret one is proud of is guarded 'carefully'.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation. 110 * 728 * 28 * 15 * 413 = 87
In a certain code language, REASON is coded as 51 and BAKE is coded as 47. How will MARRY be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Vowels take their places in the alphabet and consonants their places counted from Z: REASON = 9 + 5 + 1 + 8 + 15 + 13 = 51 and BAKE = 25 + 1 + 16 + 5 = 47. So MARRY = 14 + 1 + 9 + 9 + 2 = 35.

questions.text: Four words have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the word that is different.
questions.explanation: Growth, progress and stride (a step forward) all mean advance; a hindrance holds one back.

questions.text: Four numbers have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number that is different.
questions.explanation: 2197 = 13³, 1331 = 11³ and 2744 = 14³ are perfect cubes; 1726 is not (12³ = 1728).

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: In ACZX, KMPN and DFWU the third and fourth letters are the opposites (counted from Z) of the first and second: A/Z and C/X, K/P and M/N, D/W and F/U. In HJRQ the opposite of H is S, not R.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. DOCILE : CDEILO : : LABOUR : ?
questions.explanation: The letters are rearranged in alphabetical order: DOCILE → CDEILO. So LABOUR → ABLORU.

questions.text: From the given options choose the one in which the set of numbers do not follow the same Logic/Rule/Relation as the numbers given in below set. (165, 16, 91)
questions.explanation: The first and third numbers add up to the square of the second: 165 + 91 = 256 = 16². So do 76 + 45 = 11², 57 + 24 = 9² and 99 + 97 = 14²; but 85 + 59 = 144 = 12², not 13².

questions.text: Rama is the daughter of Radhika, who is the only daughter-in-law of Rekha. Mohan is Rishi’s father and Rekha’s husband. How is Rishi related to Rama?
questions.explanation: Mohan and Rekha are Rishi's parents, and Radhika, Rekha's only daughter-in-law, is the wife of their son. Taking Rishi as that son (the options offer no 'uncle'), Radhika's daughter Rama is Rishi's daughter, and Rishi is her father.

questions.text: The sum of the two digits of a two-digit number is 13 and the number obtained by interchanging the two digits is 27 less than the original number. What is the original number?
questions.explanation: With digits a and b: a + b = 13 and (10a + b) − (10b + a) = 9(a − b) = 27, so a − b = 3. Then a = 8 and b = 5: 85.

questions.text: In a certain code language, EXHALE is written as IFEBBY. How will HINDER be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and its letters moved alternately 4 forward and 6 back: EXHALE → ELAHXE → IFEBBY. So HINDER → REDNIH → VYHHMB.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given words in a logical and meaningful order. 1. Colour wash 2. Wall 3. Decoration 4. Foundation 5. Roof 6. Floor cementing
questions.explanation: Foundation, walls and then the roof; the floor is cemented once the roof is in place, so that the roofing work does not damage it, and colour wash and decoration come last: 4, 2, 5, 6, 1, 3.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given letter series will complete the series. l _ chtlgc _ tlg _ ht _ gc _ tlgch _
questions.explanation: With g, h, c, l, h, t in the blanks the block 'lgcht' repeats five times: lgcht lgcht lgcht lgcht lgcht.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 9, 10, 13, 24, 37, 66, 97, ?
Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. {6, 9, 18}
questions.explanation: The third number is the product of the first two divided by 3: 6 × 9 ÷ 3 = 18 and 10 × 15 ÷ 3 = 50. The others fail: 8 × 12 ÷ 3 = 32, 12 × 18 ÷ 3 = 72 and 9 × 13 ÷ 3 = 39.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All bulbs are tubes. Some bulbs are tumblers. Conclusions: I. No bulb is a tube. II. Some tumblers are bulbs.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: 'All bulbs are tubes' contradicts I. 'Some bulbs are tumblers' means some tumblers are bulbs, so II follows.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. 9 : 50
questions.explanation: The second number is half the square of one more than the first: (9 + 1)² ÷ 2 = 50 and (13 + 1)² ÷ 2 = 98. The others give 40.5, 72 and 18, not 42, 63 and 16.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. Prism : Glass : : Rope : ?
questions.explanation: A prism is made of glass, as a rope is made of hemp, a plant fibre. Pulp is used for paper, ore for metals and latex for rubber.

questions.text: Select the option in which the words share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of words. Famine : Drought
questions.explanation: A famine is caused by a drought, as devastation is caused by a hurricane.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Fort Saint Louis was a ______ fort that stood in Pondicherry on the eastern coast of India.
questions.explanation: Fort Saint Louis was the French East India Company's fort at Pondicherry, the chief settlement of French India.

questions.text: ______ is the process of allowing particles in suspension in water to settle out of the suspension under the effect of gravity.
questions.explanation: In sedimentation suspended particles settle to the bottom under gravity; decantation then pours off the clear liquid above them.

questions.text: Who among the following wrote the book 'Indomitable Spirit'?
questions.explanation: 'Indomitable Spirit' is a book by A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.

questions.text: Who among the following received the ’ASSOCHAM Enterprise of the Century Award’ in December 2020?
questions.explanation: At ASSOCHAM's Foundation Week in December 2020 Prime Minister Narendra Modi presented the 'Enterprise of the Century' award to Ratan Tata, who received it for the Tata group.

questions.text: Which of the following cities of Madhya Pradesh were included in the list of UNESCO’s world heritage cities under its urban landscape city programme in December 2020?
questions.explanation: In December 2020 Gwalior and Orchha were taken into UNESCO's Historic Urban Landscape project, under its World Heritage Cities Programme.

questions.text: Which of the following banks appointed Infosys Finacle to power its digital transformation in November 2020?
questions.explanation: XacBank of Mongolia selected Infosys Finacle's core banking, treasury and corporate banking suites for its digital transformation in November 2020.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Lucknow Pact of December 1916 was an understanding between the Indian National Congress and the ______.
questions.explanation: In the Lucknow Pact of 1916 the Congress and the All-India Muslim League agreed on joint demands for constitutional reform, the Congress accepting separate electorates.

questions.text: What is the boiling point of water at sea level?
questions.explanation: At standard sea-level pressure (1 atmosphere) pure water boils at 100°C.

questions.text: Which Indian holds the Olympic record as on March 2021 for most goals scored by an individual in an Olympic men’s hockey final?
questions.explanation: Balbir Singh Sr (Dosanjh) scored five goals in India's 6–1 win over the Netherlands in the 1952 Helsinki final, the Olympic record for a men's final.

questions.text: West Bengal's first oil and gas reserve - the Bengal Basin, dedicated to the nation on 20 December 2020, is the ______ oil and gas producing basin of India.
questions.explanation: On 20 December 2020 the Bengal Basin, where ONGC's Asokenagar-1 well in North 24 Parganas had begun producing oil, was dedicated to the nation as India's eighth producing basin.

questions.text: ‘Ong’ and ‘Tel’ are tributaries of the river ______.
questions.explanation: The Ong and the Tel are right-bank tributaries of the Mahanadi.

questions.text: Who was the Solicitor General of India as of January 2021?
questions.explanation: Tushar Mehta was appointed Solicitor General of India in 2018 and held the post in January 2021; K.K. Venugopal was then the Attorney General.

questions.text: ‘Nuakhai’ is the greatest harvesting festival of Odisha, celebrated one day after of which of the following festivals?
questions.explanation: Nuakhai, western Odisha's festival of the new rice, falls on the fifth day of the bright half of Bhadrapada, the day after Ganesh Chaturthi.

questions.text: Which form of farming is called ‘slash and burn’ agriculture?
questions.explanation: In slash-and-burn (shifting) cultivation a patch of forest is cleared, burnt and farmed until the soil is spent: a form of primitive subsistence farming.

questions.text: In which of the following states is Kali Tiger Reserve located?
questions.explanation: The Kali Tiger Reserve, formerly Dandeli-Anshi, is in Uttara Kannada district, Karnataka.

questions.text: Jog Falls is the most thrilling spectacle in the entire western region of ______.
questions.explanation: Jog Falls, on the Sharavathi river in Shivamogga district, is in Karnataka.

questions.text: ‘Wings of Fire’ is an autobiography of ______.
questions.explanation: 'Wings of Fire' is A.P.J. Abdul Kalam's autobiography, written with Arun Tiwari.

questions.text: In which year was the first ever version of Microsoft Word - Word 1.0 launched?
questions.explanation: Word 1.0, first called Multi-Tool Word, came out in 1983 for Xenix and MS-DOS.

questions.text: JPEG is a commonly used method of lossy compression for digital images. What is the full form of JPEG?
questions.explanation: JPEG stands for Joint Photographic Experts Group, the committee that created the standard.

questions.text: As of January 2021, how many states have the upper house called State Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad)?
questions.explanation: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh have Legislative Councils; Jammu and Kashmir's was abolished in 2019.

questions.text: ‘Sakewa’ is a religious festival celebrated in the state of ______.
questions.explanation: Sakewa, the Kirat Khambu Rai community's worship of Mother Earth (Bhumi Puja), is celebrated in Sikkim.

questions.text: As per ’Basel III: A global regulatory framework for more resilient banks and banking systems’ released in December 2010, banks will be required to hold a capital conservation buffer of ______ of risk weighted assets (RWAs) in the form of common equity to withstand future periods of stress.
questions.explanation: Basel III requires a capital conservation buffer of 2.5% of risk-weighted assets, held in common equity, above the minimum capital requirement.

questions.text: Which two Indians became the first pair to reach the finals of all Grand Slams in a year in the Open era, winning French Open and Wimbledon as top seeds?
questions.explanation: In 1999 Leander Paes and Mahesh Bhupathi reached the men's doubles final at all four Grand Slams, winning the French Open and Wimbledon.

questions.text: In December 2020, Kyle Coetzer was honoured with the ICC Associate Player of the Decade award. Which of the following countries does he represent?
questions.explanation: Kyle Coetzer, Scotland's captain, was named the ICC Associate Cricketer of the Decade in December 2020.

questions.text: The Energy and Resources Institute and NDMA has launched a Flood Early Warning System (FEWS) for Guwahati to alert local authorities about flash floods or any heavy rainfall in August, 2020. What is the full form of NDMA?
questions.explanation: NDMA is the National Disaster Management Authority, India's apex body for disaster management, chaired by the Prime Minister.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. We have been waiting here for you “since two hours”.
questions.explanation: A length of time takes 'for'; 'since' marks the point when something began: 'waiting here for you for two hours'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Get One’s Ducks in a Row
options: have nothing properly organized, though ready
questions.explanation: To 'get one's ducks in a row' is to have everything properly organised and ready.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Bland
questions.explanation: 'Bland' means dull, lacking flavour or interest; its opposite is 'exciting'. 'Boring' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. There is an ______ in the advertising company for a copy writer.
questions.explanation: An 'opening' is a vacant job: the company has a vacancy for a copywriter.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. In an enthusiastic way
questions.explanation: 'Heartily' means with warmth and enthusiasm. 'Earnestly' means seriously and sincerely, and 'encouragingly' in a way that gives support.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Lint
questions.explanation: 'Lint' is the soft fluff of short fibres that comes off cloth; of the options only 'fur', a soft fine coat, comes close to it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Pernicious
questions.explanation: 'Pernicious' means harmful or destructive; its opposite is 'beneficial'. 'Malicious' and 'nefarious' are close to synonyms.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in the active or passive voice. A kite’s nylon ‘manja’ (string) has cut the throat of a scooterist.
options: A kite’s nylon ‘manja’ (string) has been cut by the throat of a scooterist.
The throat of a scooterist has been cut by a kite’s nylon ‘manja’ (string).
A scooterist’s kite’s nylon ‘manja’ (string) has cut the throat of someone.
The throat of someone had been cut by a scooterist’s kite’s nylon ‘manja’ (string).
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'has cut' becomes 'has been cut by', with the object 'the throat of a scooterist' as the new subject.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'pursuit'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. Netra says that the flowers look beautiful.
options: Netra said, “The flowers are looking beautiful.”
Netra says, “The flower have looked beautiful.”
questions.explanation: The reporting verb 'says' is in the present tense, so the reported verb keeps its tense: Netra says, 'The flowers look beautiful.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The branch of science concerned with the study of Earth and its composition
questions.explanation: Geology is the study of the Earth, its rocks and its composition; metrology is the science of measurement.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Keep looking, and / you are sure to find the meaning / of the word on that page.
options: of the word on that page
you are sure to find the meaning
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: a command ('Keep looking') joined by 'and' to what will follow from it ('you are sure to find the meaning').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Wistful
questions.explanation: 'Wistful' means sadly longing for something lost or out of reach; of the options, 'sorrowful' is closest.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Wasim agreed to share his notes with Arif “on conditions that he are return” them in a day.
options: on condition that he will be return
on his condition that he is returning
on the condition that he would return
questions.explanation: The phrase is 'on the condition that', and after the past tense 'agreed' the future is expressed with 'would': 'on the condition that he would return them in a day'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. That magic is believing in yourself a hundred percent. B. There is only one magic in life that can help you turn your dreams into reality. C. You will be able to face life’s challenges with courage only if you believe in yourself and in your capacity to meet those challenges. D. Therefore, the most important lesson that a family can teach its members is to have this faith in oneself.
questions.explanation: B mentions the 'one magic', A says what 'that magic' is, C explains why believing in yourself matters, and D draws the lesson with 'Therefore': BACD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Child’s play
options: Something that is very easy to do
Something for a child to play with
Something children have made by themselves
questions.explanation: 'Child's play' is something very easy to do.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. In arid regions it may form an almost erect shrub. B. The grape is usually a woody vine, climbing by means of tendrils and often reaching a length of 17 metres or more. C. Small greenish flowers, in clusters, precede the fruit, which varies in colour from almost black to green, red and amber. D. The edible leaves are alternate, palmately lobed and always tooth-edged.
questions.explanation: B introduces the grape as a woody vine, A adds the shrub it may form in dry regions, D describes the leaves and C the flowers and fruit: BADC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. If our product does not meet your ______, we will refund your payment in full.
questions.explanation: A refund is offered if the product does not meet the buyer's 'requirements', that is needs. 'Procurements' are things bought, which does not fit.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Most hotels / offer for their guests / complimentary breakfast / during their stay there.
questions.explanation: 'Offer' takes the person directly, without 'for': 'Most hotels offer their guests complimentary breakfast'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In 1938, the famous actor, Orson Welles, terrified New York. (1) ______ radio play about an invasion of the city by Martians sounded totally real. It sounded so real that many people (2) ______ that it was an actual news report. Thousands of people (3) ______ and there was chaos and disorder in the streets of the city for several hours. Today, however, we know that there aren’t any “little green men” on the (4) ______ nearest Earth. There was going to be a Martian invasion – only this time it was going to be in the (5) ______ direction.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The radio play was Orson Welles's own, so the possessive is 'His'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In 1938, the famous actor, Orson Welles, terrified New York. (1) ______ radio play about an invasion of the city by Martians sounded totally real. It sounded so real that many people (2) ______ that it was an actual news report. There was going to be a Martian invasion – only this time it was going to be in the (5) ______ direction.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The play sounded so real that many people 'believed' it was an actual news report.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In 1938, the famous actor, Orson Welles, terrified New York. There was going to be a Martian invasion – only this time it was going to be in the (5) ______ direction.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Chaos and disorder followed in the streets because thousands of people 'panicked'.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: This time the invasion would go the 'opposite' way: from Earth to Mars rather than from Mars to Earth.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. 61 : 97
questions.explanation: 61 = 8² − 3 and 97 = 10² − 3, the squares of consecutive even numbers less 3. Likewise 141 = 12² − 3 and 193 = 14² − 3.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the numbers in the given set. (14, 11, 27)
questions.explanation: The third number is the cube of the difference of the first two: (14 − 11)³ = 27. Likewise (35 − 31)³ = 4³ = 64.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 24 ÷ 4 + 50 – 20 × 6 = 35
Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 45, 49, 57, ?, 105, 169
questions.explanation: The differences double each time: +4, +8, +16, +32, +64. So 57 + 16 = 73, and 73 + 32 = 105.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given in the options, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: In MQTXA, SWZDG and JNQUX the letters move +4, +3, +4, +3. In PTXBF every step is +4, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: A drum contains 40 litres of milk. One-fourth of the milk is taken out and replaced with water. Then, half of the mixture is taken out and replaced with water. What is the respective quantity of milk and water left in the drum?
questions.explanation: Taking out a quarter leaves 30 litres of milk, topped up with 10 litres of water. Taking out half leaves 15 litres of milk and 5 of water; refilling with 20 litres of water gives 15 litres of milk and 25 of water.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. Z _ C Y E _ X _ Y _ Z X C _ E
questions.explanation: With X, Z, C, E, Y in the blanks the block ZXCYE repeats: ZXCYE ZXCYE ZXCYE.

questions.text: ‘Farsightedness’ is related to ‘Eyes’ in the same way as ‘Gout’ is related to ‘______’.
questions.explanation: Farsightedness is a disorder of the eyes, as gout, caused by uric acid crystals, is a disorder of the joints.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (169, 289, 361)
questions.explanation: 169, 289 and 361 are the squares of the primes 13, 17 and 19. Likewise 529, 841 and 961 are the squares of the primes 23, 29 and 31; every other option includes the square of a number that is not prime.

questions.text: Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some teeth are colours. Some colours are objects. Conclusions: I. All objects are teeth. II. Some colours are teeth. III. Some objects are colours.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
Either conclusion I or III follows
Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: 'Some teeth are colours' gives 'some colours are teeth' (II), and 'some colours are objects' gives 'some objects are colours' (III). Nothing ties all objects to teeth, so I does not follow.

questions.text: In a code language, ROBIN is written as TRFNT. How will PETER be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move forward 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 places: ROBIN → TRFNT. So PETER → R H X J X: RHXJX.

questions.text: Asmit's wife is Reena and Rani's husband is Aditya. Rani's father-in-law is the paternal grandfather of Reena's only daughter Sia. How is Asmit related to Aditya?
questions.explanation: Rani's father-in-law is her husband Aditya's father, and Sia's paternal grandfather is her father Asmit's father. They are the same man, so Asmit and Aditya are brothers.

questions.text: In a certain code language, LIABILITY is coded as 950759513 and PROCTOR is coded as 8642146. How will PICTORIAL be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter keeps its own digit: L = 9, I = 5, A = 0, B = 7, T = 1, Y = 3, P = 8, R = 6, O = 4, C = 2. So PICTORIAL = 8 5 2 1 4 6 5 0 9: 852146509.

questions.text: Three of the following four words are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: A carpenter, a journalist and an architect are people who follow an occupation; a job is the occupation itself.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. USY : RPV : : MXQ : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back: USY → RPV. So MXQ → JUN.

questions.text: Who among the following is an Indian diplomat elected to the United Nations Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Questions in November 2020?
questions.explanation: In November 2020 the Indian diplomat Vidisha Maitra was elected to the UN's Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Questions (ACABQ).

questions.text: With which of the following sports is Samiya Imad Farooqui associated?
questions.explanation: Samiya Imad Farooqui, from Hyderabad, is a badminton player.

questions.text: Who among the following has assumed the DGP charge of Andaman and Nicobar in December 2020?
questions.explanation: Satyendra Garg, a 1987-batch IPS officer, took over as Director General of Police of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in December 2020.

questions.text: The members of the Constituent Assembly signed the Constitution of India on ______.
questions.explanation: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949; the members signed it on 24 January 1950, two days before it came into force.

questions.text: The book 'Indian Parliamentary Diplomacy - Speaker's Perspective' is authored by ______.
questions.explanation: 'Indian Parliamentary Diplomacy: Speaker's Perspective', by the former Lok Sabha Speaker Meira Kumar, was published by the Lok Sabha Secretariat in 2015.

questions.text: Sarbpreet Singh is the author of which of the following books?
options: Night of the Restless Spirits: Stories from 1984
40 years with Abdul Kalam - Untold Stories
questions.explanation: Sarbpreet Singh wrote 'Night of the Restless Spirits: Stories from 1984', short stories set in the anti-Sikh violence of 1984.

questions.text: ______ is a deep red soil found in tropical regions and often developed on mafic igneous bedrock.
questions.explanation: Laterite is the red, iron- and aluminium-rich soil of hot, wet tropical regions. Arid, saline and pedocal (lime-rich) soils belong mostly to dry regions.

questions.text: Which of the following empires was founded by Harihara and Bukka in 1336?
questions.explanation: Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty founded the Vijayanagara empire in 1336.

questions.text: Which of the following is a small piece of software that uses computer networks and security holes to replicate itself?
questions.explanation: A worm copies itself across networks through security holes, with no host program; a Trojan horse poses as useful software and does not replicate itself.

questions.text: When did Bangladesh get independence from Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Bangladesh, then East Pakistan, became independent of Pakistan in 1971, after the Liberation War.

questions.text: Which of the following is a weak electrolyte?
questions.explanation: Ethanoic (acetic) acid ionises only partly in water, so it is a weak electrolyte; sodium chloride, calcium chloride and magnesium sulphate are salts that ionise fully.

questions.text: In which of the following states was the ‘One District-One Product scheme’ launched in January 2018?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh launched its One District One Product scheme on 24 January 2018, UP Diwas, to promote a traditional product of each district.

questions.text: Which of the following operating systems guarantees a response within specified time constraints?
questions.explanation: A real-time operating system guarantees a response within fixed time limits, as control systems in aircraft or industrial machines need.

questions.text: With which of the following classical dances is ‘Kottakkal Sivaraman’ associated?
questions.explanation: Kottakkal Sivaraman was a Kathakali artist celebrated for his female roles.

questions.text: Who among the following won the Male Sportsperson of the Year Award at the FICCI India Sports Awards in December 2020?
questions.explanation: At the FICCI India Sports Awards in December 2020 the wrestler Bajrang Punia was named Sportsperson of the Year (male); the shooter Elavenil Valarivan won the women's award.

questions.text: Who among the following cricketers won the ‘ICC Spirit of Cricket Award of the Decade’ in December 2020?
questions.explanation: In December 2020 MS Dhoni won the ICC Spirit of Cricket Award of the Decade, voted by fans, for recalling Ian Bell after a controversial run-out at Trent Bridge in 2011.

questions.text: Peppara Wildlife Sanctuary is situated in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Peppara Wildlife Sanctuary is in Thiruvananthapuram district, Kerala, in the Western Ghats.

questions.text: Kumbh Mela 2021 organised at ______.
questions.explanation: The 2021 Kumbh Mela was held at Haridwar, on the Ganga.

questions.text: Which of the following metals reacts with the moist carbon dioxide in the air and slowly loses its shiny brown surface and gains a green coat?
questions.explanation: Copper reacts with moist carbon dioxide in the air and slowly gains a green coat of basic copper carbonate.

questions.text: The drainage pattern formed when rivers discharge their waters from all directions in a lake or depression is known as ______.
questions.explanation: In a centripetal pattern rivers flow inwards from all sides into a lake or depression; a radial pattern is the reverse, with rivers flowing out from a central height.

questions.text: Which of the following banks has launched an online platform ’Infinite India’ in December 2020, to cater the needs of foreign companies looking to establish or expand business in India?
questions.explanation: ICICI Bank launched 'Infinite India' in December 2020, an online platform offering banking and business set-up services to foreign companies entering or expanding in India.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a water or hygiene related disease?
questions.explanation: Diabetes is a metabolic disorder. Trachoma spreads where hygiene is poor, schistosomiasis is caught from water carrying the parasite, and Buruli ulcer is linked with wet, swampy places.

questions.text: In which of the following states are the snake boat races held in the months of August and September?
questions.explanation: Kerala's snake boat races, such as the Nehru Trophy Boat Race on the Punnamada Lake, are held in August and September, around Onam.

questions.text: Which of the following states was a major producer of jute in 2017-18 as per the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India?
questions.explanation: West Bengal grows most of India's jute, with Bihar and Assam next; Telangana, Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh grow little of it.

questions.text: What is the state-wise representation of members from Gujarat in Lok Sabha as of December 2020?
questions.explanation: Gujarat elects 26 members to the Lok Sabha.

questions.text: Fill in the blank with most appropriate word. I am sorry to ______ on you at this late hour.
questions.explanation: To 'intrude on' someone is to disturb them without being invited: 'I am sorry to intrude on you at this late hour'. 'Interfere' takes 'in' or 'with', and 'interrupt' takes no preposition.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. There was a bell over the door “that jingled whenever” a customer entered.
questions.explanation: The underlined part is correct: 'that' refers to the bell, 'jingled' keeps the past tense of 'was' and 'entered', and 'whenever' means each time.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. SPURIOUS
questions.explanation: 'Spurious' means false or fake; its opposite is 'genuine'. 'Artificial', 'counterfeit' and 'phony' are close to synonyms.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Where did you kept the sack of wheat that I bought from the market?
questions.explanation: 'Did' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'Where did you keep the sack of wheat'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'fascinate'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. No version of the origin of California’s name has been fully accepted, but there is wide support for the contention that it derived from an early 16th-century Spanish novel. B. California is a constituent state of the United States of America. C. It was admitted as the 31st state of the union on 9 September 1850 and by the early 1960s it was the most populous U.S. state. D. The influence of the Spanish settlers of the 18th and 19th centuries is evident in California’s architecture and place-names.
questions.explanation: B introduces California as a US state, C ('It was admitted') continues its history, A turns to the origin of its name in a Spanish novel and D to the Spanish settlers' influence: BCAD.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A close-fitting cover for the blade of a knife or sword
questions.explanation: A sheath is a close-fitting cover for the blade of a knife or sword.

questions.text: Given below are four sentences in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. In such places, strong winds blow raising heaps of sand. B. Some deserts are almost totally without water. C. These dunes shift and move endlessly across the desert. D. This sand is deposited in huge mounds called ‘sand dunes’.
questions.explanation: B introduces deserts without water, A says strong winds there raise heaps of sand, D says 'this sand' forms sand dunes and C says 'these dunes' shift: BADC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Kunal did not anticipate the need, “so he did not carries his own” water bottle.
options: so he did not carry his own
so he does not carry his own
so he did not carried his own
questions.explanation: 'Did not' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'so he did not carry his own water bottle'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. They said that they would issue the certificate the following week.
options: They said, “They issued the certificate the following week.”
They said, “They are issuing the certificate the next week.”
They said, “Could we issue the certificate the following week?”
They said, “We will issue the certificate next week.”
questions.explanation: In direct speech the reported 'they would issue' becomes 'We will issue', and 'the following week' becomes 'next week'.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. The poor washerwoman washes dirty clothes from morning to evening.
options: Dirty clothes are washed by the poor washerwoman from morning to evening.
Dirty clothes are being washed by the poor washerwoman from morning to evening.
Dirty clothes were washed by the poor washerwoman from morning to evening.
Dirty clothes have been washed by the poor washerwoman from morning to evening.
questions.explanation: The simple present 'washes' becomes 'are washed' in the passive, the plural subject 'dirty clothes' taking 'are'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The team leader asked for a ______ report to be given, in not more than one page.
questions.explanation: A report of not more than one page is 'concise': brief but complete. 'Curt' means rudely brief.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Pavan returned back home / when he completed / his assignment abroad.
questions.explanation: 'Return' already means to come back, so 'returned back' is redundant: 'Pavan returned home'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. Terrorists kill thousands of innocent people in “cold blood”.
questions.explanation: To do something 'in cold blood' is to do it deliberately and cruelly, without emotion.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Hazy
questions.explanation: 'Hazy' means misty or unclear; its opposite is 'clear'. 'Dim' and 'faint' are close to synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Novice
questions.explanation: A 'novice' is a beginner; 'expert' and 'adept' are its opposites.

questions.text: Select the misspelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'brutal'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. DIVULGE
questions.explanation: To 'divulge' is to make known something private: to 'reveal'. 'Suppress' and 'conceal' are its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A sea change
questions.explanation: A 'sea change' is a complete or profound transformation.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate one-word substitution for the given words. a seven-sided figure
questions.explanation: A seven-sided figure is a heptagon; a hexagon has six sides, a pentagon five and an octagon eight.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. I had the train compartment to myself up to Rohana and then a girl got in. The couple who saw her off were (1)______ her parents. They seemed very anxious (2)______ her comfort and gave the girl (3)______ instructions as to where to keep (4)______ things, when not to lean out and how to (5)______ speaking to strangers.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: The narrator only guesses who the couple were: 'probably' her parents. Used alone, 'likely' is normally an adjective ('likely to be her parents'), and 'absolutely' and 'exactly' express certainty.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. I had the train compartment to myself up to Rohana and then a girl got in. The couple who saw her off were (1)______ her parents. They seemed very anxious (2)______ her comfort and gave the girl (3)______ instructions as to where to keep (4)______ things, when not to lean out and how to (5)______ speaking to strangers.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: To be 'anxious about' something is to be worried about it: 'anxious about her comfort'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. I had the train compartment to myself up to Rohana and then a girl got in. The couple who saw her off were (1)______ her parents. They seemed very anxious (2)______ her comfort and gave the girl (3)______ instructions as to where to keep (4)______ things, when not to lean out and how to (5)______ speaking to strangers.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: The parents gave 'detailed' instructions, covering where to keep things, leaning out and strangers.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. I had the train compartment to myself up to Rohana and then a girl got in. The couple who saw her off were (1)______ her parents. They seemed very anxious (2)______ her comfort and gave the girl (3)______ instructions as to where to keep (4)______ things, when not to lean out and how to (5)______ speaking to strangers.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: The girl is told where to keep 'her' things; the possessive refers back to the girl.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. I had the train compartment to myself up to Rohana and then a girl got in. The couple who saw her off were (1)______ her parents. They seemed very anxious (2)______ her comfort and gave the girl (3)______ instructions as to where to keep (4)______ things, when not to lean out and how to (5)______ speaking to strangers.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: The parents told her how to 'avoid' speaking to strangers.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs to balance the following equation. 40 * 5 * 7 * 24 * 6 * 38
Select the option in which the words share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of words. Rat : Rodent
questions.explanation: A rat is a rodent, and an ostrich is a bird. A frog is an amphibian, not a reptile; a whale is not a shark; and 'Cattle : Cow' reverses the order.

questions.text: Select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 14, 28, 31, 124, 129, ?
questions.explanation: The steps alternate ×2, +3, ×4, +5, ×6: 129 × 6 = 774.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. 122 : 340 : 726
questions.explanation: Each number is an odd number cubed minus 3: 122 = 5³ − 3, 340 = 7³ − 3 and 726 = 9³ − 3. Likewise 2194 = 13³ − 3, 3372 = 15³ − 3 and 4910 = 17³ − 3.

questions.text: Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some pins are roses. No rose is a machine. Conclusions: I. Some roses are pins. II. Some pins are not machines. III. All machines are pins.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: 'Some pins are roses' converts to 'some roses are pins' (I). The pins that are roses cannot be machines, as no rose is a machine, so some pins are not machines (II). Nothing says all machines are pins (III).

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the numbers in the given set. (850, 645, 410)
questions.explanation: Twice the difference of the first two numbers gives the third: (850 − 645) × 2 = 410. Likewise (440 − 229) × 2 = 422.

questions.text: In a code language, CANDLE is written as FMEOBD. How will FIXING be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and each letter moved one place forward: CANDLE → ELDNAC → FMEOBD. So FIXING → GNIXIF → HOJYJG.

questions.text: In a certain code language, LIABILITY is coded as 141 and OFFICIATE is coded as 166. How will STATUTORY be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter takes its position counted from Z (Z = 1, A = 26) and 3 is taken off the total: LIABILITY = 144 − 3 = 141 and OFFICIATE = 169 − 3 = 166. STATUTORY = 8 + 7 + 26 + 7 + 6 + 7 + 12 + 9 + 2 = 84, and 84 − 3 = 81.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: In YWTP, MKHD and USPL the letters move back 2, 3 and 4 places. In PMJG they move back 3 each time, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given words in the order in which they appear in an English dictionary. 1. Deceive 2. Deceptive 3. Decapitate 4. Decency 5. Decamp
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Decamp (5), Decapitate (3), Deceive (1), Decency (4), Deceptive (2). 'Decam' comes before 'Decap', and 'Decei' before 'Decen' before 'Decep'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. UDM : YZQ : : QCT : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +4, −4, +4: U → Y, D → Z, M → Q. Likewise Q → U, C → Y, T → X: UYX.

questions.text: A father’s age at the time of the birth of his son is the same as the present age of the son. If the age of the son was 15 years five years ago, then what is the current age of the father?
questions.explanation: The son is 15 + 5 = 20 now, so the father was 20 when the son was born and is 20 + 20 = 40 now.

questions.text: Three of the following four words are alike in a certain way and one is different. Select the odd one.
questions.explanation: Applaud, honour and admire all express approval or praise; criticise expresses disapproval.

questions.text: Four numbers have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number that is different.
questions.explanation: 198, 165 and 132 are multiples of 33 (33 × 6, 33 × 5 and 33 × 4); 177 = 3 × 59 is not.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. 263 : 271
