questions.text: Who is the author of the book 'Pathway to God'?
questions.explanation: 'Pathway to God' gathers extracts from Mahatma Gandhi's writings and speeches on God, truth and prayer.

questions.text: Which helpline was launched by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment in September 2020?
questions.explanation: KIRAN, a toll-free mental health rehabilitation helpline, was launched by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment in September 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following banks has launched contactless ‘RuPay Select’ debit card in association with NPCI (National Payment Corporation of India) in December 2020?
questions.explanation: Central Bank of India launched the contactless 'RuPay Select' debit card with NPCI on its 110th Foundation Day, 21 December 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following lakes of Maharashtra has been included in the list of Ramsar Sites in November 2020?
questions.explanation: Lonar Lake in Buldhana district, a crater lake formed by a meteorite impact, was declared a Ramsar site in November 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following is the most literate district in India as per Census 2011?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 put Serchhip in Mizoram at the top, with a literacy rate of about 97.9%.

questions.text: Who has authored the book titled ‘India’s 71-Year Test: The Journey to Triumph in Australia’?
questions.explanation: The cricket writer R Kaushik wrote the book, published in 2020 with a foreword by Ravi Shastri; it follows India's tours of Australia up to the first series win there, in 2018-19.

questions.text: As per The Indian Tourism Statistics (ITS) 2020, which Indian state attracted the highest number of domestic tourists in the country in 2019?
questions.explanation: India Tourism Statistics 2020 put Uttar Pradesh first for domestic tourist visits in 2019, with about 536 million, ahead of Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: As of January 2021, who among the following is the Union Minister of Rural Development?
questions.explanation: Narendra Singh Tomar held Rural Development, with Agriculture and Panchayati Raj, from 2019 until the reshuffle of July 2021.

questions.text: ______ is generally called as milk sugar as it is found in milk.
questions.explanation: Lactose, a sugar made of glucose and galactose, is the sugar found in milk.

questions.text: Which of the following cities is situated on the banks of river Saryu?
questions.explanation: Ayodhya, in Uttar Pradesh, stands on the bank of the Saryu (Sarayu).

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Bias
questions.explanation: 'Bias' is an unfair leaning for or against someone; its opposite is 'fairness'. 'Prejudice' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Someone who studies elections and voting statistics
questions.explanation: A psephologist studies elections and voting patterns.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To be all ears
options: To be ready and eager to listen
questions.explanation: 'To be all ears' is to listen eagerly and attentively.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The project is / tough and I / can't be able to / complete it by Monday.
questions.explanation: 'Can't' already expresses inability, so 'can't be able to' says it twice: 'I can't complete it' or 'I won't be able to complete it'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'distraction'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. We will definitely win the match / this time because our team / has prepare well.
options: We will definitely win the match
questions.explanation: The present perfect takes the past participle: 'has prepared well'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. The main activity of Palampur is farming and 80 families of the upper caste own the majority of land in Palampur. B. Palampur village has around 450 families which belong to different castes and creeds. C. The neighboring towns of the village are well connected and all-weather roads are also well connected. D. There are other activities in Palampur like dairy, transport, small-scale manufacturing, etc. which also help run the economy in the village.
questions.explanation: B introduces the village and its families, A gives its main activity, farming, and who owns the land, D adds its other activities, and C closes with its links to neighbouring towns: BADC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. “Seldom do we find” so many birds nesting during this season.
questions.explanation: After a negative adverb such as 'seldom' at the start of a sentence, the auxiliary comes before the subject: 'Seldom do we find' is correct as it stands.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Fritter
questions.explanation: To 'fritter' money or time is to waste it bit by bit; the opposite is to 'hoard' it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. This training programme for students will help the ______ understand the different methods of communication.
questions.explanation: A training programme helps those taking part in it, the 'participants'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Bolster
questions.explanation: To 'bolster' is to support or 'strengthen'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in the active or passive voice. The central team visited eight villages in the state to assess the damage to the crops.
options: The damage to the crops was assessed in eight villages in the state by the central team.
Eight villages in the state were visited by the central team to assess the damage to the crops.
Eight villages had visited the central team to assess the damage to the crops.
The central team assessed the damage to the crops in eight villages in the state.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'visited' becomes 'were visited', with the object 'eight villages' as the new subject and 'by the central team' as the agent.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. I cannot understand “that you” are trying to say.
questions.explanation: The object of 'understand' is the thing being said, so 'what you are trying to say'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Doing something awkwardly or in a clumsy manner
questions.explanation: To 'fumble' is to handle something or do it clumsily.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiomatic expression given. Caught red-handed
options: Caught in the act of doing something illegal
Caught with a hand covered in blood
Caught by someone wearing a red wristband
Caught stealing red objects like apples and tomatoes
questions.explanation: To be 'caught red-handed' is to be caught in the act of doing wrong.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Random
questions.explanation: 'Random' means without plan or pattern: 'arbitrary'.

questions.text: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the right order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. Understanding a printed text comes from the interaction between printed words and one’s prior knowledge of the world. B. Comprehension is the ability or process of understanding something that is spoken or written. C. Listening comprehension, however, involves multiple processes in understanding and making sense of spoken language. D. In active reading, readers think about their reading, and make connections and inferences.
questions.explanation: B defines comprehension, A explains how a printed text is understood, D adds active reading, and C turns, with 'however', to listening comprehension: BADC.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech. “Where did the children leave their record books?” the sports coach asked the class prefect.
options: The sports coach asked the class prefect where the children had left their record books.
The sports coach asked the class prefect where the children leave their record books.
The sports coach asked the class prefect where have the children left their record books.
The sports coach asked the class prefect where the children are leaving their record books.
questions.explanation: The question becomes a statement in reported speech ('where the children had left', no inversion), and the past 'did ... leave' moves back to the past perfect 'had left'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Have you checked if we have ______ information about the location?
questions.explanation: The check is whether there is enough information: 'sufficient'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In the 19th century, there was an industrial revolution in Europe. As a result, millions of people left the (1) ______ and went to work in big factories in cities. Today, it is the reverse. In several major cities, people have started moving out. Why? They want a cleaner, (2) ______ environment. There are fewer jobs in ‘heavy’ industries like steel and power generation. (3) ______, there are more jobs in service industries like banking, tourism and food delivery. Besides, modern transport and communications have made it easier for people to (4) ______ to work or even work from home. The result of this revolution in the 21st century will be ‘spread cities’ – cities are growing fast, but (5) ______, away from city centres and people are choosing to live 40, 50 or 60 kilometres away.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: People 'left the countryside' to work in factories in the cities.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In the 19th century, there was an industrial revolution in Europe. As a result, millions of people left the (1) ______ and went to work in big factories in cities. Today, it is the reverse. In several major cities, people have started moving out. Why? They want a cleaner, (2) ______ environment. There are fewer jobs in ‘heavy’ industries like steel and power generation. (3) ______, there are more jobs in service industries like banking, tourism and food delivery. Besides, modern transport and communications have made it easier for people to (4) ______ to work or even work from home. The result of this revolution in the 21st century will be ‘spread cities’ – cities are growing fast, but (5) ______, away from city centres and people are choosing to live 40, 50 or 60 kilometres away.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: A 'cleaner, greener' environment: the opposite of the industrial city they are leaving.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In the 19th century, there was an industrial revolution in Europe. As a result, millions of people left the (1) ______ and went to work in big factories in cities. Today, it is the reverse. In several major cities, people have started moving out. Why? They want a cleaner, (2) ______ environment. There are fewer jobs in ‘heavy’ industries like steel and power generation. (3) ______, there are more jobs in service industries like banking, tourism and food delivery. Besides, modern transport and communications have made it easier for people to (4) ______ to work or even work from home. The result of this revolution in the 21st century will be ‘spread cities’ – cities are growing fast, but (5) ______, away from city centres and people are choosing to live 40, 50 or 60 kilometres away.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Instead' introduces what has replaced the lost jobs in heavy industry: more jobs in services.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In the 19th century, there was an industrial revolution in Europe. As a result, millions of people left the (1) ______ and went to work in big factories in cities. Today, it is the reverse. In several major cities, people have started moving out. Why? They want a cleaner, (2) ______ environment. There are fewer jobs in ‘heavy’ industries like steel and power generation. (3) ______, there are more jobs in service industries like banking, tourism and food delivery. Besides, modern transport and communications have made it easier for people to (4) ______ to work or even work from home. The result of this revolution in the 21st century will be ‘spread cities’ – cities are growing fast, but (5) ______, away from city centres and people are choosing to live 40, 50 or 60 kilometres away.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: To 'commute' is to travel regularly between home and work.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In the 19th century, there was an industrial revolution in Europe. As a result, millions of people left the (1) ______ and went to work in big factories in cities. Today, it is the reverse. In several major cities, people have started moving out. Why? They want a cleaner, (2) ______ environment. There are fewer jobs in ‘heavy’ industries like steel and power generation. (3) ______, there are more jobs in service industries like banking, tourism and food delivery. Besides, modern transport and communications have made it easier for people to (4) ______ to work or even work from home. The result of this revolution in the 21st century will be ‘spread cities’ – cities are growing fast, but (5) ______, away from city centres and people are choosing to live 40, 50 or 60 kilometres away.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Spread cities' grow 'outwards', away from the city centres.

questions.text: Four numbers have been given in the options, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the number that is different.
questions.explanation: 2704 = 52², 2116 = 46² and 1936 = 44² are perfect squares; 1948 is not.

questions.text: Select the correct option that indicates the arrangement of the given words in a logical and meaningful order. 1. Armlet 2. Belt 3. Ascot 4. Socks 5. Turban
questions.explanation: From head to foot: turban (head), ascot (a broad scarf worn at the neck), armlet (upper arm), belt (waist) and socks (feet): 5-3-1-2-4.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. 173 : 125 : 85
questions.explanation: Each number is 4 more than the square of an odd number, the odd numbers falling by 2: 173 = 13² + 4, 125 = 11² + 4, 85 = 9² + 4. Likewise 365 = 19² + 4, 293 = 17² + 4, 229 = 15² + 4.

questions.text: Select the combination of letters that when sequentially placed in the blanks of the given series will complete the series. _ S _ E _ S Z _ F S _ E
questions.explanation: With F, Z, F, E, Z in the blanks the block FSZE repeats: FSZE FSZE FSZE.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 56, 56, 54, 162, 158, ?
questions.explanation: The terms are multiplied by 1, reduced by 2, multiplied by 3, reduced by 4 and multiplied by 5 in turn: 56 × 1 = 56, 56 − 2 = 54, 54 × 3 = 162, 162 − 4 = 158 and 158 × 5 = 790.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. Googley : Cricket :: Gambit : ?
questions.explanation: A googly is a kind of delivery bowled in cricket; a gambit is a kind of opening in chess.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. TAMPO : SCJTJ :: FIFTY : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move −1, +2, −3, +4, −5: TAMPO → SCJTJ. So FIFTY → E K C X T: EKCXT.

questions.text: In a certain code language, NAMELY is coded as 74 and MANAGE is coded as 45. How will MUSHER be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each code is the sum of the letters' positions in the alphabet plus 4: NAMELY = 70 + 4 = 74 and MANAGE = 41 + 4 = 45. MUSHER = 13 + 21 + 19 + 8 + 5 + 18 = 84, and 84 + 4 = 88.

questions.text: Manyak is the son of Aravind. Manyak and Kashyap are brothers. Durga is the mother of Kashyap. Sanhit is the brother of Aravind. Hruday is the son of Sanhit. How is Hruday related to Kashyap?
questions.explanation: Manyak and Kashyap are brothers and Manyak is Aravind's son, so Kashyap is Aravind's son too. Hruday is the son of Sanhit, Aravind's brother, so he is Kashyap's cousin.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 25 × 7 + 20 – 40 ÷ 4 = 210
Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. 93 : 87
questions.explanation: The second number is the first minus the difference of its digits: 93 − (9 − 3) = 87. Likewise 58 − (8 − 5) = 55; the others fail (96 − 3 = 93, 64 − 2 = 62, 49 − 5 = 44).

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some insects are animals. Some animals are frogs. All frogs are cats. Conclusions: I. Some cats are frogs. II. Some frogs are animals. III. Some animals are insects.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: All frogs are cats, so some cats are frogs (I). 'Some animals are frogs' and 'some insects are animals' convert to 'some frogs are animals' (II) and 'some animals are insects' (III). All three follow.

questions.text: Four letter-clusters have been given in the options, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the letter-cluster that is different.
questions.explanation: In FKOR, RWAD and LQUX the letters move +5, +4, +3 (W + 4 wraps round to A). JNRV moves +4, +4, +4, so it is the odd one.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'PENCIL' is written as 'CEILNP' and 'FROST' is written as 'FORST'. How will 'DUSTBIN' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters of each word are rearranged in alphabetical order: PENCIL → CEILNP and FROST → FORST. So DUSTBIN → BDINSTU.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (4, 25, 105)
questions.explanation: The third number is five times the difference of the first two: (25 − 4) × 5 = 105. Likewise (50 − 14) × 5 = 180.

questions.text: Select the option in which the words share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of words. Papaya : Vitamin C
questions.explanation: Papaya is a rich source of vitamin C, and so is gooseberry (amla). Carrots are known for vitamin A rather than B, guavas for vitamin C rather than A, and apples contain no vitamin D.

questions.text: When was the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) established in India?
questions.explanation: The Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry was founded in 1927, with G. D. Birla and Purshottamdas Thakurdas among its founders.

questions.text: How many monasteries and temples are there in Ellora caves?
questions.explanation: The Ellora caves in Maharashtra are 34 monasteries and temples: 12 Buddhist, 17 Hindu and 5 Jain.

questions.text: Which was the first Indian institution to receive the United Nations Population Award for 2020?
questions.explanation: HelpAge India, which works for older people, received the UN Population Award for 2020 in the institutional category, the first Indian organisation to win it in that category.

questions.text: Phodong Monastery is located in ______.
questions.explanation: Phodong Monastery, a Buddhist monastery, is in North Sikkim.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: ______ was the Mughal emperor during the revolt of 1857.
questions.explanation: Bahadur Shah II (Bahadur Shah Zafar), the last Mughal emperor, was proclaimed their leader by the rebels of 1857 and was exiled to Rangoon afterwards.

questions.text: Which of the following state governments launched the 'Digital Seva Setu Programme' for rural areas in October 2020?
questions.explanation: Gujarat launched Digital Seva Setu in October 2020 to bring government services online to its villages.

questions.text: Which of the following is the output device of a computer?
questions.explanation: A plotter prints drawings and graphs, so it is an output device. Joysticks and scanners are input devices and a pen drive is storage.

questions.text: Which of the following states leads in sunflower cultivation?
questions.explanation: Karnataka is India's leading producer of sunflower.

questions.text: In 1959, the Central Government of India undertook the governance in Kerala under ______ of the Constitution of India.
questions.explanation: In 1959 President's Rule was imposed in Kerala under Article 356 and E. M. S. Namboodiripad's government was dismissed.

questions.text: A file with the ______ file extension is a Word Open XML Macro-Enabled Document file.
questions.explanation: '.docm' is Word's macro-enabled Open XML format; an ordinary '.docx' file cannot hold macros.

questions.text: In August 2020, who was promoted to ICC’s international panel of umpires?
questions.explanation: K. N. Ananthapadmanabhan, a former Kerala cricketer, was added to the ICC's International Panel of Umpires in August 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following organisations awards the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences?
options: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences
questions.explanation: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences awards the economics prize, as it does the physics and chemistry prizes; the Swedish Academy awards literature and the Norwegian Nobel Committee peace.

questions.text: ______ was the first person who discovered cells.
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke saw and named cells in a thin slice of cork in 1665.

questions.text: Which of the following formulas related to monetary and liquidity aggregates is NOT correct?
options: M4 = M3 + Total deposits with post office savings organisations (excluding national savings certificates)
M2 = M1 + Savings deposits with post office savings banks
M3 = M1 + Net time deposits of post office savings
questions.explanation: M3 is M1 plus the net time deposits of commercial banks, not of post office savings. The other three are the textbook definitions: M1 is currency plus demand deposits, post office savings bank deposits are added in M2, and total post office deposits in M4.

questions.text: What is the tenure of the chairman of the State Public Service Commission?
options: 6 years or the age of 60 years, whichever is earlier
5 years or the age of 60 years, whichever is earlier
5 years or the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier
6 years or the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier
questions.explanation: Under Article 316(2) a member of a State Public Service Commission, the chairman included, holds office for six years or until the age of 62, whichever is earlier.

questions.text: Which of the following waterfalls is located in Jharkhand?
questions.explanation: Hundru Falls, on the Subarnarekha near Ranchi, is in Jharkhand. Jog Falls is in Karnataka and Dudhsagar in Goa.

questions.text: Manitombi Singh was a ______ player from Manipur.
questions.explanation: Laishram Manitombi Singh, from Manipur, was a footballer who played for India and captained Mohun Bagan.

questions.text: Sardar Sarovar Dam is situated in the state of ______ and on the river ______.
questions.explanation: The Sardar Sarovar Dam is on the Narmada at Kevadia in Gujarat.

questions.text: Leprosy is caused by a bacterium called:
questions.explanation: Leprosy is caused by Mycobacterium leprae; Mycobacterium tuberculosis causes tuberculosis.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: A large area of land demarcated as Damin-i-Koh in 1832 was declared as the land of the ______.
questions.explanation: In 1832 the British demarcated the Damin-i-Koh in the Rajmahal hills as the land of the Santhals.

questions.text: Which of the following institutes got the first rank in the Atal Ranking of Institutions on Innovation Achievements (ARIIA) 2020 in the category of ‘Institute of National Importance’?
questions.explanation: IIT Madras ranked first among Institutes of National Importance in ARIIA 2020.

questions.text: Enzyme linked immuno-sorbent assay is a technique used in detection of which of the following diseases?
questions.explanation: ELISA detects antibodies to HIV in the blood, so it is used to diagnose HIV infection and AIDS.

questions.text: Which is the largest of the following Duns with an approximate length of 35-45 km and a width of 22-25 km?
questions.explanation: Dehra Dun, about 35-45 km long and 22-25 km wide, is the largest of the duns, the longitudinal valleys between the Shiwaliks and the Lesser Himalaya.

questions.text: India's first 'Fire Park' was set up at ______ in January 2021.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Bhubaneswar, where Odisha's Chief Minister opened a Fire Park in January 2021 to teach people, students above all, basic fire safety.

questions.text: Who among the following persons secured the fourth position in the Dhaka Marathon 2021?
questions.explanation: Jigmet Dolma, a runner from Ladakh, finished fourth in the Bangabandhu Dhaka Marathon in January 2021.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the groups of words given. A remedy for all diseases
questions.explanation: A panacea is a remedy for all diseases, or a solution to every problem. Nectar is the drink of the gods, or the sugary fluid of flowers.

questions.text: Select the wrongly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'professional', with a double 's'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Enunciate
questions.explanation: To 'enunciate' is to pronounce words clearly, or to state an idea clearly: to 'articulate'.

questions.text: Select the antonym of the given word. Ascend
questions.explanation: To 'ascend' is to go up; its exact opposite is to 'descend', go down. 'Rise' and 'climb' are close to 'ascend' in meaning.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in blanks with the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Trees help man in three ways, by supplying wood etc., by providing shade and by helping to resist drought and flood, of (1)______ the last is the most important. Man, (2)______, has brought on his own ruin, by mass deforestation. History shows that great empires built on depletion of forest reserves, have toppled being unable to cope (3)______ floods and food-shortage. Though the Government can make laws (4)______ denudation of forests, it is difficult to prevent it unless people are educated enough to realize its (5)______ consequences.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: 'Which' is the relative pronoun for things, here the three ways just listed: 'of which the last is the most important'. 'Whom' refers to people, and 'what' cannot introduce such a clause.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in blanks with the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Trees help man in three ways, by supplying wood etc., by providing shade and by helping to resist drought and flood, of (1)______ the last is the most important. Man, (2)______, has brought on his own ruin, by mass deforestation. History shows that great empires built on depletion of forest reserves, have toppled being unable to cope (3)______ floods and food-shortage. Though the Government can make laws (4)______ denudation of forests, it is difficult to prevent it unless people are educated enough to realize its (5)______ consequences.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 2
questions.explanation: 'However' marks the contrast: trees help man, yet man has brought on his own ruin. 'Whoever', 'whenever' and 'wherever' make no sense set off by commas here.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in blanks with the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Trees help man in three ways, by supplying wood etc., by providing shade and by helping to resist drought and flood, of (1)______ the last is the most important. Man, (2)______, has brought on his own ruin, by mass deforestation. History shows that great empires built on depletion of forest reserves, have toppled being unable to cope (3)______ floods and food-shortage. Though the Government can make laws (4)______ denudation of forests, it is difficult to prevent it unless people are educated enough to realize its (5)______ consequences.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 3
questions.explanation: One 'copes with' a difficulty: the empires were unable to cope with floods and food-shortage.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in blanks with the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Trees help man in three ways, by supplying wood etc., by providing shade and by helping to resist drought and flood, of (1)______ the last is the most important. Man, (2)______, has brought on his own ruin, by mass deforestation. History shows that great empires built on depletion of forest reserves, have toppled being unable to cope (3)______ floods and food-shortage. Though the Government can make laws (4)______ denudation of forests, it is difficult to prevent it unless people are educated enough to realize its (5)______ consequences.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 4
questions.explanation: The blank begins a phrase describing the laws: 'laws prohibiting denudation of forests', that is laws that forbid it. A finite verb such as 'prohibits' or 'have prohibited' cannot follow 'make laws' here.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in blanks with the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Trees help man in three ways, by supplying wood etc., by providing shade and by helping to resist drought and flood, of (1)______ the last is the most important. Man, (2)______, has brought on his own ruin, by mass deforestation. History shows that great empires built on depletion of forest reserves, have toppled being unable to cope (3)______ floods and food-shortage. Though the Government can make laws (4)______ denudation of forests, it is difficult to prevent it unless people are educated enough to realize its (5)______ consequences.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 5
questions.explanation: Serious, dangerous consequences are 'grave' ones, the set word with 'consequences'. 'Small' contradicts the passage's warning, and 'large' and 'big' speak of size rather than seriousness.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. All the employees of the nationalized banks are “in” strike.
questions.explanation: People who stop work in protest are 'on strike': 'All the employees of the nationalized banks are on strike.'

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Gary said, "I have finally cleared my exams with distinction!"
options: Gary told that he have cleared his exams with distinction.
Gary said that he has finally cleared his exams with distinction.
Gary exclaimed that he cleared his exams with distinction.
Gary exclaimed that he had finally cleared his exams with distinction.
questions.explanation: The exclamation mark calls for 'exclaimed', and with the reporting verb in the past, 'I have finally cleared my exams' becomes 'he had finally cleared his exams'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the groups of words given. The life history of a person written by himself.
questions.explanation: An autobiography is the story of a person's life written by that person; a biography is written by someone else.

questions.text: Select the correct antonym for the given word. Harsh
questions.explanation: 'Harsh' means severe or unkind; its opposite is 'gentle'. 'Tough' and 'bitter' are close to 'harsh' in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The sales team ______ the engineers for the organization’s failure to bag the mega deal.
questions.explanation: One holds someone responsible for a failure by blaming them: the sales team 'blamed' the engineers for it. 'Liked', 'appreciated' and 'praised' do not go with 'for the organization's failure'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. She declared that “it was the last straw” and fled.
options: it was the last time she would use a straw
it was last time she would hold a straw
questions.explanation: 'The last straw' is the last of a series of troubles, the one that makes a situation unbearable.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Janki burnt her boats with her previous supervisor by ______ him in public.
questions.explanation: To 'burn one's boats' is to do something that makes going back impossible, as criticizing a supervisor in public would. 'Applauding' and 'appreciating' would not, and 'flaunting' a person makes no sense here.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. One of the twins was driving better than the other. B. Mahesh kept comparing them every day. C. After two months of driving daily, finally both the twins were at par. D. Mahesh was teaching the twins how to drive.
questions.explanation: D sets the scene (Mahesh teaching the twins to drive), A says one twin drove better than the other, B says Mahesh kept comparing them, and C ('After two months ... finally') ends with both at par: DABC.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence? Who killed Ravana?
questions.explanation: In the passive, 'who' becomes 'by whom', and the question keeps the auxiliary before the subject: 'By whom was Ravana killed?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Assemble
questions.explanation: To 'assemble' is to gather together, as is to 'amass'. 'Disband' and 'detach' mean nearly the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Upset someone’s applecart
options: Upsetting someone by dropping the apples
Making someone angry by ruining business
Doing something that fails someone’s plan
Spoiling the apples in someone's cart
questions.explanation: To 'upset someone's applecart' is to spoil their plans.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Samurai Jack drawn his sword to exact revenge on his superiors.
questions.explanation: 'Drawn' is a past participle and cannot be the verb on its own: 'Samurai Jack drew (or has drawn) his sword'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. He commanded that Birbal should leave his kingdom. B. Birbal left, and started working on a farm in an unknown village. C. Once upon a time, Akbar the great, became very angry with his minister, Birbal. D. As months passed, Akbar started to miss his favourite minister.
questions.explanation: C introduces Akbar's anger with Birbal, A says he ordered Birbal to leave the kingdom, B says Birbal left and worked on a farm, and D ('As months passed') says Akbar began to miss him: CABD.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Queen Elizabeth got marrying to Philip, former Prince of Greece and Denmark.
questions.explanation: One 'gets married to' someone; 'got' needs the past participle: 'Queen Elizabeth got married to Philip'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. The director wanted Aziz to play the role of the doctor “as well also” that of the apprentice.
questions.explanation: 'As well as' joins the two roles: 'the role of the doctor as well as that of the apprentice'. 'As well' and 'also' together say the same thing twice.

questions.text: At one stage in the Vedic Age, the king was called 'gopati' which meant '______'.
questions.explanation: 'Gopati' joins 'go', cow, and 'pati', lord or master: in the cattle-keeping society of the early Vedic age the chief was the lord and protector of the cattle.

questions.text: ______ is the oldest hockey tournament in India.
questions.explanation: The Beighton Cup, played in Kolkata (Calcutta) since 1895, is the oldest hockey tournament in India.

questions.text: DefExpo-2020, a flagship biennial event of the Ministry of Defence, Government of India, was held in ______ from 5th to 9th February, 2020.
questions.explanation: The eleventh DefExpo, the Defence Ministry's land, naval and homeland security systems exhibition, was held in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, from 5 to 9 February 2020.

questions.text: ______ is famous for Muga silk.
questions.explanation: Muga, a golden silk spun by the silkworm Antheraea assamensis, is produced almost only in Assam and carries a geographical indication tag.

questions.text: Vyommitra is______.
options: a humanoid built by Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO)
the first banking robot in India
a humanoid robot introduced to assist teachers at schools in India
a chatbot developed by Indian Railways Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC)
questions.explanation: Vyommitra is the half-humanoid robot ISRO unveiled in January 2020, built to fly on the uncrewed test flights of the Gaganyaan mission.

questions.text: Which of the following tiger reserves is NOT located in Karnataka?
questions.explanation: The Pench tiger reserves are in Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra. Bhadra, Dandeli-Anshi and Nagarhole are tiger reserves in Karnataka.

questions.text: ______ is also known as the ‘All India War Memorial’.
questions.explanation: India Gate in New Delhi, designed by Edwin Lutyens, was built as the All India War Memorial to the soldiers of the British Indian Army who died in the First World War and the Third Anglo-Afghan War.

questions.text: Which of the following is a vertebrate?
questions.explanation: A snake, a reptile, has a backbone. The roundworm (a nematode), the millipede (an arthropod) and the earthworm (an annelid) are invertebrates.

questions.text: Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori in a battle in the year ______ but lost to him the following year.
questions.explanation: Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain in 1191, and lost to him in the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192.

questions.text: Who was appointed as the Chief of the Indian Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) in June 2019?
questions.explanation: Samant Kumar Goel, an IPS officer of the Punjab cadre, was appointed Secretary of the Research and Analysis Wing in June 2019, succeeding Anil Dhasmana; Arvind Kumar was named Director of the Intelligence Bureau at the same time.

questions.text: The traditional rod puppet of Bihar is known as ______.
questions.explanation: Yampuri is the traditional rod puppetry of Bihar. Sakhi Kundhei is a puppet form of Odisha, and Bommalattam the puppetry of Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: In April 2020, Facebook—an American social media and technology company —announced its plan to buy ______% equity stake in Reliance Jio.
questions.explanation: On 22 April 2020 Facebook announced it would invest ₹43,574 crore for a 9.99% stake in Jio Platforms, the Reliance group's digital business that owns Reliance Jio.

questions.text: Who was the Director-General of the World Health Organisation in April 2020?
questions.explanation: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus of Ethiopia had headed the WHO since July 2017, so he was its Director-General in April 2020. Roberto Azevêdo was then head of the World Trade Organization.

questions.text: The world wide web was invented in the year ______.
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the World Wide Web at CERN, near Geneva, in March 1989.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Indian Federal System?
options: Division of powers between the Centre and the States
questions.explanation: Federalism divides power between at least two levels of government, in India the Union and the States; a single tier is the mark of a unitary state. A written constitution, an independent judiciary and a division of powers are federal features.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian-origin UK politicians was previously Chief Secretary to the Treasury before being appointed Chancellor of the Exchequer (United Kingdom) on 13 February 2020?
questions.explanation: Rishi Sunak was Chief Secretary to the Treasury from July 2019 until 13 February 2020, when he succeeded Sajid Javid as Chancellor of the Exchequer.

questions.text: The Jharia and Chandrapura coal fields are located in the state of ______.
questions.explanation: Both are in Jharkhand: the Jharia coalfield, in Dhanbad district in the Damodar valley, is the country's main store of coking coal, and Chandrapura lies in neighbouring Bokaro district.

questions.text: NPK is a:
options: Fertilizer used for increasing fertility of soil
Sanitizer used to clean dusty leaves
questions.explanation: NPK fertilisers supply nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P) and potassium (K), the three main nutrients plants take from the soil.

questions.text: The Great Leap Forward (GLF) was a campaign initiated in ______ in 1958 aimed at industrialising the country on a massive scale.
questions.explanation: Mao Zedong launched the Great Leap Forward in China in 1958 to industrialise the country quickly through communes and mass campaigns; it ended in a severe famine.

questions.text: ‘Tenpins’ refers to the game of ______.
questions.explanation: Tenpins, or ten-pin bowling, is bowling in which a ball is rolled down a lane to knock down ten pins.

questions.text: Name the holy city recognized as the birthplace of the first and fourth Jain Tirthankaras.
questions.explanation: Jain tradition places the births of five Tirthankaras at Ayodhya, among them Rishabhanatha, the first, and Abhinandananatha, the fourth.

questions.text: ______ was a web browser developed by the National Centre for Supercomputing Application (NCSA).
questions.explanation: Mosaic, released in 1993 by the National Center for Supercomputing Applications at the University of Illinois, made the graphical web browser popular. Navigator was Netscape's browser and Safari is Apple's.

questions.text: Union Legislature alone can make laws on matters related to ______.
questions.explanation: Railways are on the Union List (entry 22), so only Parliament can make laws on them. Police, public health and local government are on the State List.

questions.text: ______ is the inflammatory compound in pepper spray.
questions.explanation: Pepper spray is made from oleoresin capsicum, whose active compound, capsaicin, is what makes chilli peppers hot. Curcumin comes from turmeric and gingerol from ginger.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Come hell or high water
options: Not ready to go on adventures
Tired of all kinds of dangers
questions.explanation: 'Come hell or high water' means whatever happens: no difficulty or obstacle will stop the person.

questions.text: Select the wrongly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'permanent', ending in '-ent'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Something that is expressed in a confusing way
questions.explanation: 'Incoherent' describes speech or writing that is unclear and confusing. 'Eccentric' means odd, 'inaudible' too quiet to be heard and 'gullible' easily fooled.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Rama said to me, "I need your help for my new assignment."
options: Rama says to me that she needs my help for her new assignment.
Rama said to me that she is needing my help for her new assignment.
Rama said to me she needs your help for the new assignment.
Rama told me that she needed my help for her new assignment.
questions.explanation: 'Said to' becomes 'told', the present 'need' moves back to 'needed', and the pronouns change: 'your help' becomes 'my help' and 'my new assignment' 'her new assignment'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. I remember watching a TV series on bringing up children that showed parents being obsessed (1)______ their children’s performance in school exams. The series highlighted how parents often give (2)______ higher importance to their children’s academic performance than their aptitudes. So many parents push and goad their children to study hard and score (3)______ possible in their exams. They believe that academic (4)______ guarantees a successful career and they want their children to be the next ‘Albert Einstein’ not knowing that Einstein (5)______ was a rebel and didn’t follow any of his parents’ plans for him.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'about'. 'Obsessed' usually takes 'with', which is not among the options, but 'obsessed about' is also used (like the verb 'obsess about'); 'of', 'in' and 'to' do not go with it.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. I remember watching a TV series on bringing up children that showed parents being obsessed (1)______ their children’s performance in school exams. The series highlighted how parents often give (2)______ higher importance to their children’s academic performance than their aptitudes. So many parents push and goad their children to study hard and score (3)______ possible in their exams. They believe that academic (4)______ guarantees a successful career and they want their children to be the next ‘Albert Einstein’ not knowing that Einstein (5)______ was a rebel and didn’t follow any of his parents’ plans for him.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
questions.explanation: 'Significantly' (by a large amount) can qualify the comparative 'higher'; 'completely', 'fully' and 'largely' do not go with a comparative.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. I remember watching a TV series on bringing up children that showed parents being obsessed (1)______ their children’s performance in school exams. The series highlighted how parents often give (2)______ higher importance to their children’s academic performance than their aptitudes. So many parents push and goad their children to study hard and score (3)______ possible in their exams. They believe that academic (4)______ guarantees a successful career and they want their children to be the next ‘Albert Einstein’ not knowing that Einstein (5)______ was a rebel and didn’t follow any of his parents’ plans for him.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3.
questions.explanation: The 'as ... as' comparison takes the plain form, so 'as higher as' and 'as better as' are wrong, and one scores 'high' (or 'well'), not 'good': 'score as high as possible'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. I remember watching a TV series on bringing up children that showed parents being obsessed (1)______ their children’s performance in school exams. The series highlighted how parents often give (2)______ higher importance to their children’s academic performance than their aptitudes. So many parents push and goad their children to study hard and score (3)______ possible in their exams. They believe that academic (4)______ guarantees a successful career and they want their children to be the next ‘Albert Einstein’ not knowing that Einstein (5)______ was a rebel and didn’t follow any of his parents’ plans for him.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.
questions.explanation: 'Academic performance', the phrase used earlier in the passage, is what such parents believe guarantees a successful career.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. I remember watching a TV series on bringing up children that showed parents being obsessed (1)______ their children’s performance in school exams. The series highlighted how parents often give (2)______ higher importance to their children’s academic performance than their aptitudes. So many parents push and goad their children to study hard and score (3)______ possible in their exams. They believe that academic (4)______ guarantees a successful career and they want their children to be the next ‘Albert Einstein’ not knowing that Einstein (5)______ was a rebel and didn’t follow any of his parents’ plans for him.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5.
questions.explanation: The reflexive 'himself' stresses 'Einstein', one man: 'Einstein himself was a rebel'. 'Oneself', 'themselves' and 'itself' do not agree with him.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. When I first met my neighbours I took an ______ liking to them.
questions.explanation: The blank sits between 'an' and the noun 'liking', so it needs an adjective: 'an instant liking', one formed at once. 'Instantly' is an adverb and 'instance' a noun.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Invincible
questions.explanation: 'Invincible' means too strong to be defeated; its opposite is 'vulnerable', open to attack or harm. 'Unstoppable' and 'supreme' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Deport
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'permit': to 'deport' is to send someone out of a country, and to permit someone to enter or stay comes nearest to the opposite. 'Expel' means much the same as 'deport', and 'transport' and 'conduct' mean to carry and to lead.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. When the actress “comes to know” that she was declared winner of the best actress award, her joy knew no bounds.
questions.explanation: The rest of the sentence is in the past ('was declared', 'knew'), so the simple past 'came to know' is needed.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Covered with a material or substance in order to stop heat, sound etc. From entering or escaping
questions.explanation: 'Insulated' means covered with a material that stops heat, sound or electricity from passing. 'Hydrated' means supplied with water and 'calibrated' adjusted or marked for measuring.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Even though we found ourselves in a ______ situation during our climb, we decided not to give up the expedition.
questions.explanation: 'Precarious' means dangerous and uncertain; 'even though' sets that danger against the decision not to give up. 'Pleasant', 'permissive' and 'plausible' do not fit the contrast.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The country has the lowest per capita income and needs to create jobs to the youth.
questions.explanation: Jobs are created 'for' people, not 'to' them: 'needs to create jobs for the youth'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options select the one that gives their correct order. A. He went into a part of the city I had never seen before and walked around a few alleys. B. At one point I distinctly saw him turn around, as if to make sure no one was following him; then he darted away. C. From my conversation with the cook I had learned that Ram Parshad had started to head out of the house at the same time every evening. D. One day I followed at a distance to know where he went every day.
questions.explanation: C gives the background (Ram Parshad went out at the same time every evening), D says the narrator followed him one day, A says where he went, and B ends with him looking round and darting away: CDAB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. There is “a lot of” confusion among students due to recent changes in the examination pattern.
questions.explanation: 'A lot of' is the correct phrase for a large amount, so no change is needed. 'Allot' is a verb meaning to assign, and the phrase takes 'a' and no '-s'.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. Savita will deliver a speech on the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti.
options: On the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti a speech is being delivered by Savita.
On the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti a speech was delivered by Savita.
On the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti a speech will be delivered by Savita.
On the occasion of Ambedkar Jayanti a speech is to be delivered by Savita.
questions.explanation: The future 'will deliver' becomes 'will be delivered' in the passive, with the object 'a speech' as the subject: 'a speech will be delivered by Savita'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Reproach
questions.explanation: To 'reproach' is to express disapproval of someone: 'berate', to scold angrily, is closest. 'Indulge', 'supervise' and 'train' are unrelated.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options select the one that gives their correct order. A. You can also wear a hat to cover your hair and scalp to protect them from toxic particles that could be harmful. B. Therefore,when you are exposed to bad quality air, try and wear full sleeved clothes to cover as much of your skin as possible. C. All the above precautions could save you from serious skin diseases. D. Air pollution plays a major role in skin and hair related problems for which you need to take precautions.
questions.explanation: D introduces the problem (air pollution harms skin and hair), B gives the first precaution ('Therefore ... wear full sleeved clothes'), A adds another ('also wear a hat'), and C sums up 'all the above precautions': DBAC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Idleness
questions.explanation: 'Idleness' is a lack of activity or effort: 'lethargy'. 'Energy' and 'industry' (hard work) are its opposites.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. I declined the lunch offer by Suresh, not because I do not want to go, but because I had no time.
options: but because I had no time
I do not want to go
questions.explanation: 'Declined' and 'had' put the sentence in the past, so the middle clause must be too: 'not because I did not want to go'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Out of bounds
questions.explanation: 'Out of bounds' describes a place people are not allowed to enter: 'forbidden'.

questions.text: Who was the chairman of the Economic Programme Committee (EPC) that was formed by All India Congress Committee in 1947?
questions.explanation: The Economic Programme Committee that the All India Congress Committee set up in 1947 was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru; its report, in 1948, recommended a permanent Planning Commission.

questions.text: Which festival is also known as ‘Mahakumbh of the East’?
questions.explanation: The Ambubachi Mela, held each June at the Kamakhya temple in Guwahati, Assam, draws so many pilgrims that it is called the 'Mahakumbh of the East'. The Hornbill Festival and Moatsu Mong are festivals of Nagaland.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian actresses was honored with UNICEF's Danny Kaye Humanitarian Award in December 2019?
questions.explanation: Priyanka Chopra Jonas, a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador, received the Danny Kaye Humanitarian Award at UNICEF's Snowflake Ball in New York in December 2019.

questions.text: On 10th December 2019, which of the following states received the 'World Habitat Award?'
questions.explanation: Odisha's Jaga Mission, which gives slum dwellers land rights over the homes they live in and upgrades their settlements, won a bronze World Habitat Award, announced in December 2019.

questions.text: Who won the Women’s 'Leading Cricketer of Year' award for 2018?
questions.explanation: Wisden named Smriti Mandhana its Leading Woman Cricketer in the World for 2018, the year the ICC also gave her its award for the best woman cricketer.

questions.text: In which year was the new Indian Rupee symbol officially adopted by the Government of India?
questions.explanation: The Union Cabinet approved the rupee symbol ₹, designed by D. Udaya Kumar, on 15 July 2010.

questions.text: Which Indian Forest Service (IFS) officer was selected for the Asia Environmental Enforcement award by the United Nations Environment Programme in October 2019?
questions.explanation: Ramesh Pandey, an Indian Forest Service officer, received the UN Environment Programme's Asia Environmental Enforcement Award in 2019 for his work against wildlife crime.

questions.text: In which year was the Rigveda manuscript included in the UNESCO's Memory of the World Register?
questions.explanation: Thirty Rigveda manuscripts held by the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, Pune, were added to UNESCO's Memory of the World Register in 2007.

questions.text: Who defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the first Battle of Panipat?
questions.explanation: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat in 1526 and founded the Mughal Empire.

questions.text: Which of the following planets is known as a gas giant?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is a gas giant, made mostly of hydrogen and helium; Mercury, Venus and Earth are rocky, terrestrial planets.

questions.text: How many function keys are present on a standard PC keyboard?
questions.explanation: A standard PC keyboard has 12 function keys, F1 to F12, along its top row.

questions.text: Who was appointed as the first-ever Chief of Defense Staff (CDS) by the Union Cabinet in December 2019?
questions.explanation: On 30 December 2019 the Government named General Bipin Rawat, then Chief of the Army Staff, India's first Chief of Defence Staff; he took charge on 1 January 2020.

questions.text: Which scientist won the Nobel Prize in 1915 for describing the nature of the structure of chlorophyll in plants and also noted magnesium as the central element in its structure?
questions.explanation: Richard Willstätter won the 1915 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for his research on plant pigments, above all chlorophyll, in which he showed magnesium to be an essential part.

questions.text: Which Nobel laureate wrote the book ‘India: A Million Mutinies Now’?
questions.explanation: 'India: A Million Mutinies Now' (1990) is by V. S. Naipaul, who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2001. Olga Tokarczuk, Peter Handke and Patrick Modiano are also literature laureates.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which governor general introduced the policy of Subsidiary Alliance, under which the Indian ruler agreed to keep British forces in his territory?
questions.explanation: Lord Wellesley, Governor-General from 1798 to 1805, used the Subsidiary Alliance: an Indian ruler kept British troops in his state, paid for them and accepted a British Resident. Hyderabad was the first to accept it, in 1798.

questions.text: Superconductivity was discovered by ______, who was also awarded the Noble Prize for Physics in 1913.
questions.explanation: Heike Kamerlingh Onnes found in 1911 that mercury loses all electrical resistance when cooled close to absolute zero; his low-temperature work, including liquefying helium, won him the 1913 Nobel Prize in Physics.

questions.text: Who was elected as the protem Speaker of the 17th Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Virendra Kumar, the BJP member from Tikamgarh, was the pro tem Speaker who swore in the members of the 17th Lok Sabha in June 2019, before Om Birla was elected Speaker.

questions.text: Which of the following instruments is used for the measurement of direct beam solar irradiance?
questions.explanation: A pyrheliometer, pointed at the Sun, measures its direct beam of radiation. A chronometer measures time, a refractometer the refractive index and an optometer the refraction of the eye.

questions.text: Which of the following disciplines studies human populations mostly with respect to their size, their structure and their development?
questions.explanation: Demography is the statistical study of human populations: their size, their structure by age and sex, and how they change through births, deaths and migration.

questions.text: What is the pH of rain water during acid rain?
questions.explanation: Normal rain is slightly acidic, about pH 5.6, from the carbon dioxide dissolved in it; rain with a pH below 5.6 is called acid rain.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs is NOT matched correctly?
options: Alt + E – Edit options in current program
Alt + Shift + D – Insert the current date
questions.explanation: Ctrl + K inserts a hyperlink; the shortcut to cut selected text is Ctrl + X. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.text: How many times has Viswanathan Anand won the World Chess Champion title as of January 2020?
questions.explanation: Viswanathan Anand won the World Chess Championship five times: in 2000 (FIDE), 2007, 2008, 2010 and 2012.

questions.text: The ideals of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity (contained in the Preamble of the Constitution of India) are borrowed from the constitution of which country?
questions.explanation: The ideals of liberty, equality and fraternity in the Preamble were taken from the French Constitution, after the motto of the French Revolution.

questions.text: Which of the following is a breed of sheep?
questions.explanation: Mecheri is a sheep breed of Tamil Nadu. Barbari, Jamunapari and Beetal are goat breeds.

questions.text: Who became the first gymnast to receive the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award?
questions.explanation: The gymnast Dipa Karmakar received the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna in 2016, together with P. V. Sindhu, Sakshi Malik and Jitu Rai.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order. A. He decides to leave home and sets out to find him with the help of his best friend called Sungreen. B. It narrates the story of a young and sensitive boy in a tough world. C. ‘A Boy and Sungreen’ is a film by the Chinese filmmaker, Ahn-Ju-Young. D. When he finds that his supposedly dead father is alive he decides to act.
questions.explanation: C introduces the film, B says what it is about (a sensitive boy in a tough world), D says he learns that his supposedly dead father is alive, and A says he leaves home to find him: CBDA.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The word is spelt 'liaison', with an 'i' on both sides of the 'a'.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. Did you inform him about the ticket cancellation?
options: Was he informed about the ticket cancellation by you?
Will he be informed about the ticket cancellation by you?
Is he being informed about the ticket cancellation by you?
Was he being informed about the ticket cancellation by you?
questions.explanation: The object 'him' becomes the subject 'he', and the simple past question 'Did you inform' becomes 'Was he informed ... by you?'

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Studies have shown that there is no standard advice one can (1)______ to parents. Some guidelines however, may (2)______. The first one is that children are all different and there is no one way (3)______ bringing them up. Each child should be treated as (4)______ individual. The second is that heredity is important, both for intelligence and (5)______.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: After the modal 'can' the verb takes its base form: 'no standard advice one can give to parents'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Studies have shown that there is no standard advice one can (1)______ to parents. Some guidelines however, may (2)______. The first one is that children are all different and there is no one way (3)______ bringing them up. Each child should be treated as (4)______ individual. The second is that heredity is important, both for intelligence and (5)______.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
questions.explanation: Guidelines are provided by someone, so the verb is passive, and after the modal 'may' it takes the base form: 'Some guidelines however, may be provided.'

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Studies have shown that there is no standard advice one can (1)______ to parents. Some guidelines however, may (2)______. The first one is that children are all different and there is no one way (3)______ bringing them up. Each child should be treated as (4)______ individual. The second is that heredity is important, both for intelligence and (5)______.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3.
questions.explanation: The phrase is 'a way of doing something': 'there is no one way of bringing them up'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Studies have shown that there is no standard advice one can (1)______ to parents. Some guidelines however, may (2)______. The first one is that children are all different and there is no one way (3)______ bringing them up. Each child should be treated as (4)______ individual. The second is that heredity is important, both for intelligence and (5)______.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.
questions.explanation: 'Individual' begins with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an': 'treated as an individual'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Studies have shown that there is no standard advice one can (1)______ to parents. Some guidelines however, may (2)______. The first one is that children are all different and there is no one way (3)______ bringing them up. Each child should be treated as (4)______ individual. The second is that heredity is important, both for intelligence and (5)______.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No.5.
questions.explanation: A noun is needed to pair with 'intelligence': heredity matters 'both for intelligence and personality'. 'Personal' is an adjective, 'personnel' means staff and 'personalise' is a verb.

questions.text: Select the correct Indirect form of the given sentence. The minister said, “It is tragic that the Australian bush fires have claimed the lives of so many helpless animals.”
options: The minister said that it was tragic that the Australian bush fires had claimed the lives of so many helpless animals.
The minister said that it was tragic that the Australian bush fires claimed the lives of so many helpless animals.
The minister said that it was tragic that the Australian bush fires were claiming the lives of so many helpless animals.
The minister said that it was tragic that the Australian bush fires have been claiming the lives of so many helpless animals.
questions.explanation: After the past-tense 'said', 'is' becomes 'was' and the present perfect 'have claimed' becomes the past perfect 'had claimed'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. In our metro cities the contrast between the high rise buildings with the slums behind is ______.
questions.explanation: High-rise buildings with slums just behind them make a shocking contrast: 'appalling'. 'Interesting' is too neutral for such inequality, and 'comforting' and 'laudable' (praiseworthy) contradict the sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Keep up appearances
options: To pretend to be happier or richer so as to conceal the real situation
To spend a lot of time on appearances so as to lead the fashion world
To deliberately appear shabby and not care to impress people
To waste a lot of money on mindless shopping and not bother about the consequences
questions.explanation: To 'keep up appearances' is to go on pretending that all is well, or that one is better off than one is, to hide the real state of affairs.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. The week-long Theatre Festival has begun with a wonderful “lines of” plays.
questions.explanation: 'Line up' replaces 'lines': a singular noun must follow 'a', and a line-up is a set of events or performers arranged for an occasion ('a wonderful line-up of plays'). The sheet's underline also takes in 'of', which the options leave out.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Mani Kaul begun his career as an actor and a director of short films before doing his debut feature film, ‘Uski Roti.’
options: begun his career as an actor
questions.explanation: The simple past of 'begin' is 'began'; 'begun' is the past participle and needs 'has' or 'had': 'Mani Kaul began his career'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. In the blink of an eye
options: Within a very short period of time
Within a very long period of time
questions.explanation: 'In the blink of an eye' means in a moment, very quickly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. Some people believe that 2020 “is going” to be a very significant year in our history.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: '2020', a single year, takes the singular 'is', and 'is going to' states what is expected to happen. 'Will going' is not English, and 'were' and 'are' are plural.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The politician was responsible for ______ violence in the university.
questions.explanation: To 'incite' violence is to stir people up to it, which a politician can be held responsible for.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. COMPATRIOT
questions.explanation: A 'compatriot' is a fellow citizen of one's own country; its opposite is 'outsider'. 'Brethren' and 'countryman' are near synonyms.

questions.text: Select the word that means the same as the given group of words. Unable to think clearly because of a mental illness
questions.explanation: 'Deranged' means mentally disturbed, unable to think or behave normally. 'Eccentric' and 'whimsical' mean odd or fanciful, and 'balanced' is the opposite.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order. A. He would be accompanied by fifty or sixty torchbearers. B. When dawn broke the Emperor would alight, say his prayers and return by 8 a.m. C. They would all head towards the river Jamuna. D. During the winter months the Badshah Bahadur Shah Jafar would set off on his horse at 3 a.m.
questions.explanation: D sets out the emperor's routine (leaving on horseback at 3 a.m.), A says who went with him, C where they all went, and B what he did at dawn: DACB.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Often hailed as one of the greatest industry leaders of India, Ratan Tata take across the reins of the company, leading from the front.
options: the greatest industry leaders from India,
Ratan Tata take across the reins of the company
questions.explanation: 'Take' does not agree with the singular 'Ratan Tata', and the phrase is 'take over the reins', not 'take across': 'Ratan Tata took over the reins of the company'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. DETERIORATE
questions.explanation: To 'deteriorate' is to become worse: 'worsen'. 'Improve' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. DESPONDENT
questions.explanation: 'Despondent' means low in spirits and without hope: 'depressed'. 'Cheerful' and 'energetic' are near opposites.

questions.text: Select the word that means the same as the given group of words. A person working on a trial period
questions.explanation: A probationer is someone serving a trial period in a new job. A petitioner makes a formal request, and a practitioner practises a profession such as medicine or law.

questions.text: Who has created LISP, the Programming Language for Artificial Intelligence?
questions.explanation: John McCarthy designed LISP at MIT in 1958; he also coined the term 'artificial intelligence'. Grace Hopper is known for her work on COBOL and Leslie Lamport for LaTeX.

questions.text: Who is the first Indian male cricketer to play 100 matches of T-20 format?
questions.explanation: Rohit Sharma played his 100th T20 international against Bangladesh at Rajkot in November 2019, the first Indian man to reach the mark.

questions.text: In which year were the first modern Summer Olympic games held?
questions.explanation: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896.

questions.text: Who is the Minister of Youth Affairs and Sports as of February 2020?
questions.explanation: In February 2020 Kiren Rijiju was the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Youth Affairs and Sports, a post he held from May 2019 to July 2021.

questions.text: Who is the current (23rd) Chief Election Commissioner of India?
questions.explanation: When the exam was held (October 2020), Sunil Arora, in office since December 2018, was the 23rd Chief Election Commissioner; Sushil Chandra succeeded him in April 2021.

questions.text: Which article of the Indian Constitution prohibits trafficking in human beings and forced labour?
questions.explanation: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings, begar and other forms of forced labour. Article 25 deals with freedom of religion, Article 13 with laws inconsistent with fundamental rights, and Article 5 with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution.

questions.text: All parallel circles from the Equator to the poles are known as______
questions.explanation: Parallels of latitude are the circles drawn parallel to the Equator, growing smaller towards the poles. The Tropic of Cancer and the Arctic and Antarctic Circles are particular parallels.

questions.text: Which among the following is a western coast island?
questions.explanation: Elephanta Island lies in Mumbai Harbour, off the west coast. Pamban Island lies off Tamil Nadu between Palk Bay and the Gulf of Mannar, the Parikud islands are in Chilika Lake in Odisha, and Sriharikota is on the Andhra Pradesh coast: all on the east.

questions.text: Who was the winner of the Dadasaheb Phalke Award which was presented in 2019?
questions.explanation: Amitabh Bachchan received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2018 from President Ram Nath Kovind in December 2019. Shashi Kapoor, Manoj Kumar and Vinod Khanna (posthumously) received it for 2014, 2015 and 2017.

questions.text: Which of the following is a dance form of Meghalaya?
questions.explanation: Laho is a dance of the Pnar (Jaintia) people of Meghalaya. Cheraw is from Mizoram, Dalkhai from Odisha and Rangma from Nagaland.

questions.text: Where is the Baglihar Dam located?
questions.explanation: The Baglihar Dam is a hydroelectric project on the Chenab in the Ramban district of Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.text: Which of the following is the allotropic form of carbon?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives graphite, a pure crystalline allotrope of carbon, as are diamond and the fullerenes. Coal is an impure fuel rather than a form of the element, and charcoal and lamp black are impure, amorphous carbon: some books list them as amorphous allotropes, but graphite is the only option that is a distinct allotrope.

questions.text: What is the Rigvedic name of the river Ravi?
questions.explanation: In the Rigveda the Ravi is called the Parushni; the Vitasta is the Jhelum, the Asikni the Chenab and the Shutudri the Sutlej.

questions.text: Who is the Miss Universe crown winner for the year 2019?
questions.explanation: Zozibini Tunzi of South Africa won Miss Universe 2019, held in Atlanta in December 2019. Catriona Gray of the Philippines had won in 2018.

questions.text: Who won the Women US Open title of 2019?
questions.explanation: Bianca Andreescu of Canada won the 2019 US Open women's singles, beating Serena Williams in the final.

questions.text: What was the name of the oldest female black rhino which died in 2019?
questions.explanation: Fausta, a black rhino believed to be the oldest rhino in the world, died in Tanzania's Ngorongoro Conservation Area in December 2019, aged 57. Suidae and Canidae are the scientific names of the pig and dog families.

questions.text: Hydrochloric acid is secreted in which part of our digestive system?
