questions.explanation: The gastric glands in the wall of the stomach release hydrochloric acid, along with pepsin and mucus; the acid makes the medium acidic, which pepsin needs to work.

questions.text: At which place was the Saffron Mission initiated in 2010?
questions.explanation: The National Saffron Mission, launched in 2010, supports saffron growers in Jammu and Kashmir, which grows nearly all of India's saffron, chiefly around Pampore.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was the Mughal Emperor at the time of Battle of Plassey?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757, when Alamgir II (1754-1759) was the Mughal emperor. Siraj-ud-Daulah was the Nawab of Bengal who lost the battle, Mir Qasim became Nawab later, and Shah Alam II succeeded Alamgir II in 1759.

questions.text: ‘Kalamezhuthu' is a ritual art form found in:
questions.explanation: Kalamezhuthu is a ritual art of Kerala in which images of deities such as Bhadrakali are drawn on the floor with coloured powders.

questions.text: When was the National Stock Exchange of India established?
questions.explanation: The National Stock Exchange of India was established (incorporated) in November 1992. SEBI recognised it as a stock exchange in April 1993, and trading on it began in 1994.

questions.text: A computer on the Internet that uses HTTP protocol is known as:
questions.explanation: A web server stores web pages and delivers them to browsers over HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol). A LAN and a WLAN are local networks, and WAP (Wireless Application Protocol) is a protocol for mobile access to the internet.

questions.text: Who has created a record for longest single spaceflight in 2019?
questions.explanation: In December 2019 Christina Koch passed Peggy Whitson's 288 days, setting the record for the longest single spaceflight by a woman (still hers when the exam was held, October 2020); she returned in February 2020 after 328 days aboard the International Space Station.

questions.text: Which is the rarest element?
questions.explanation: Astatine is the rarest naturally occurring element in the earth's crust: it forms only in the radioactive decay of uranium and thorium, and all its isotopes are short-lived.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given: Satisfied, with no desire to change or improve
questions.explanation: 'Complacent' means so pleased with oneself or one's situation that one sees no need to change or improve. 'Beneficent' means doing good, and an 'adolescent' is a teenager.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom: Sleep on it
options: To prefer to sleep than take action
To wait before making a decision
questions.explanation: To 'sleep on it' is to put off a decision until the next day, so as to think it over.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word: Fraudulent
questions.explanation: 'Fraudulent' means dishonest, meant to cheat: 'deceitful'. 'Genuine' is its opposite, and 'repellent' means causing disgust.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word(s) to fill in the blank: My family is my priority but there were times when I had to ______ because of work pressures.
questions.explanation: To 'pull away' is to withdraw or keep one's distance: work pressures sometimes took the speaker away from the family. 'Look into' and 'put off' need an object, and 'sit in' means attend as an observer.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One day Willy stumbled upon a novel in a (1)______ bookshop-a Perry Mason book written by Erle Stanley Gardner. He (2)______ the book simply because the title of the book cover looked (3)______. Although it was an unabridged book Willy was able (4)______ it with sufficient comprehension. This was partly because the novel contained (5)______ written in simple, conversational language.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: The adjective 'local' describes the bookshop: 'a local bookshop', one in the neighbourhood. 'Location' is a noun and 'localize' a verb.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One day Willy stumbled upon a novel in a (1)______ bookshop-a Perry Mason book written by Erle Stanley Gardner. He (2)______ the book simply because the title of the book cover looked (3)______. Although it was an unabridged book Willy was able (4)______ it with sufficient comprehension. This was partly because the novel contained (5)______ written in simple, conversational language.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
questions.explanation: To 'pick up' a book is to take it casually, here because its cover caught his eye. To 'pick on' someone is to bully them, and to 'pick at' food is to eat it without interest.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One day Willy stumbled upon a novel in a (1)______ bookshop-a Perry Mason book written by Erle Stanley Gardner. He (2)______ the book simply because the title of the book cover looked (3)______. Although it was an unabridged book Willy was able (4)______ it with sufficient comprehension. This was partly because the novel contained (5)______ written in simple, conversational language.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3.
questions.explanation: After the linking verb 'looked' an adjective is needed: the title 'looked attractive'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One day Willy stumbled upon a novel in a (1)______ bookshop-a Perry Mason book written by Erle Stanley Gardner. He (2)______ the book simply because the title of the book cover looked (3)______. Although it was an unabridged book Willy was able (4)______ it with sufficient comprehension. This was partly because the novel contained (5)______ written in simple, conversational language.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.
questions.explanation: 'Able' is followed by the to-infinitive: 'able to read it'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One day Willy stumbled upon a novel in a (1)______ bookshop-a Perry Mason book written by Erle Stanley Gardner. He (2)______ the book simply because the title of the book cover looked (3)______. Although it was an unabridged book Willy was able (4)______ it with sufficient comprehension. This was partly because the novel contained (5)______ written in simple, conversational language.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No.5.
questions.explanation: 'Conversational language' points to 'dialogues', the characters' conversations, which made the novel easy to follow. A monologue is a speech by one person, and a prologue and an epilogue open and close a work.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. The film by itself was good but “the bit long” than I had expected.
questions.explanation: 'Than' needs a comparative, and 'a bit' (not 'the bit') means slightly: 'but a bit longer than I had expected'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order. A. It is played by turning around while reciting a rhyme. B. The circling motion is like that of a Sufi dervish. C. Fahim Irshad has made a film called ‘Aani Maani’. D. The movie title is based on a game popular among little children in Uttar Pradesh.
questions.explanation: C names the film, D says its title comes from a children's game, A says how the game is played, and B compares its circling motion to a Sufi dervish's: CDAB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word: BUOYANT
questions.explanation: 'Buoyant' means cheerful and optimistic; its opposite is 'gloomy'. 'Cheerful' and 'bouncy' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the correct Indirect form of the given sentence. “It is a fact that kids model parental behaviour,” said the researcher.
options: The researcher said that it is a fact that kids model parental behaviour.
The researcher has said that it is a fact that kids have modeled parental behaviour.
The researcher has been saying that kids model parental behaviour.
The researcher says that it is a fact that kids model parental behaviour.
questions.explanation: The reporting verb 'said' stays in the past, but a fact or general truth keeps its present tense in indirect speech: 'that it is a fact that kids model parental behaviour'.

questions.text: Select the wrongly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Deterent' is misspelt: the word is 'deterrent', with a double 'r'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given: To make perfect or complete
questions.explanation: To 'complement' something is to complete it or make it perfect. 'Attainment' is achievement, an 'impediment' a hindrance and 'deportment' a person's bearing or behaviour.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. People with full time sedentary jobs who commuting long distances, may have sleep problems due to lack of exercise.
options: People with full time sedentary jobs
questions.explanation: The relative clause needs a finite verb after 'who': 'who commute long distances'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word: Indomitable
questions.explanation: 'Indomitable' means impossible to defeat or subdue: 'invincible'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom: Keep your shirt on
questions.explanation: 'Keep your shirt on' tells someone to stay calm and not lose their temper.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word: CAUSTIC
questions.explanation: 'Caustic' means bitterly sarcastic or cutting, so its opposite is 'kind'. 'Sarcastic' and 'bitter' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order. A. Since then, Pathak has performed in several plays and films. B. While studying there, he saw ‘Equus,’ a play that changed his life forever. C. Vinay Pathak was pursuing MBA in New York. D. He decided to change tracks and study drama.
questions.explanation: C introduces Vinay Pathak studying in New York, B says he saw 'Equus' while studying there, D says he then changed tracks to drama, and A ('Since then') sums up his career: CBDA.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. According to a recent study, drinking green tea thrice a week is associated with a longest and healthy life.
options: drinking green tea thrice a week
questions.explanation: The superlative 'longest' does not fit after 'a' or beside 'healthy'; the life is compared with that of people who do not drink green tea, so both adjectives take the comparative: 'a longer and healthier life'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Shivangini, the 12 year old archer who ______ an injury has been successfully operated by a team of doctors at A.I.I.M.S.
questions.explanation: To 'sustain' an injury is to suffer one. 'Ordain' means order or appoint as a priest, 'maintain' keep up and 'pertain' relate to.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. Dr. Verma advised patients to try out a new medicine for migraine.
options: The patients were being advised to try out a new medicine for migraine by Dr. Verma.
The old patients had been advised to try out a new medicine for migraine by Dr. Verma.
Patients were advised to try out a new medicine for migraine by Dr. Verma.
Patients have been advised to try out a new medicine for migraine by Dr. Verma.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'advised' becomes 'were advised' in the passive, with 'patients' as the subject: 'Patients were advised to try out a new medicine for migraine by Dr. Verma.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. I like the place “which” I live but it would be wonderful to live in the mountains.
questions.explanation: The place one lives in calls for the relative adverb 'where' (that is, 'in which'): 'I like the place where I live'.

questions.text: Which Indian Institute of Technology launched the country’s first indigenously designed standing wheelchair in collaboration with Phoenix Medical Systems?
questions.explanation: IIT Madras designed 'Arise', India's first indigenous standing wheelchair, which lets its user rise from sitting to standing; it was launched in November 2019 with Phoenix Medical Systems, which makes it.

questions.text: The 'Loor dance' is a traditional folk dance, performed only by women, in the state of:
questions.explanation: Loor, danced by women and girls in spring around Holi, is a folk dance of Haryana.

questions.text: What does HLL stand for in computing?
questions.explanation: HLL stands for High Level Language: a programming language, such as Python or Java, that is closer to human language than to machine code.

questions.text: In which of the following cities was the 4th edition of the India International Cherry Blossom Festival 2019 organised in November 2019?
questions.explanation: Shillong, the capital of Meghalaya, held the 4th India International Cherry Blossom Festival from 13 to 16 November 2019, when its Himalayan cherry trees bloom in autumn.

questions.text: Who among the following was honoured with the prestigious 27th Ekalabya Puraskar for the year 2019?
questions.explanation: The Odisha weightlifter Jhilli Dalabehera was chosen in November 2019 for the Ekalabya Puraskar 2019, the award that IMPaCT, the trust of the Indian Metals and Ferro Alloys group, has given young sportspersons of Odisha every year since 1993.

questions.text: Lines joining places located at equal travel time from a common centre are called:
questions.explanation: Isochrones join places that can be reached in the same travel time from a centre. Isohalines join places of equal salinity, and isobronts places where a thunderstorm occurs at the same time.

questions.text: Maps showing natural feature of the earth such as mountains, plateaus, rivers, plains, oceans, etc. are known as ______.
questions.explanation: Maps of natural features such as mountains, plateaus, plains, rivers and oceans are physical or relief maps, as the NCERT Class 6 geography book defines them. Political maps show states and boundaries, thematic maps one subject such as rainfall, and topographic maps man-made features as well as natural ones.

questions.text: Which state secured the top rank in the Swachh Survekshan Grameen Awards, 2019?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu was ranked the best state in Swachh Survekshan Grameen 2019, the central government's survey of rural sanitation, with Haryana and Gujarat next; Uttar Pradesh won the award for the most citizen participation.

questions.text: Who among the following cricketers has become the youngest Indian cricketer to score a half-century in international cricket?
questions.explanation: Shafali Verma, aged 15, made a half-century against West Indies in a T20 international in November 2019, breaking Sachin Tendulkar's record from 1989 as the youngest Indian to do so in international cricket.

questions.text: Who was conferred with the Italian Golden Sand Art Award, 2019?
questions.explanation: The Odisha sand artist Sudarsan Pattnaik received the Italian Golden Sand Art Award 2019 in November 2019, the first Indian to win it, while taking part in the International Scorrano Sand Nativity event in Lecce, Italy.

questions.text: Which India-born businessperson occupied the top spot in Fortune’s Businessperson of the Year 2019 list?
questions.explanation: Microsoft's chief executive Satya Nadella, born in Hyderabad, topped Fortune's Businessperson of the Year list for 2019.

questions.text: National Highway 18 does NOT pass through which of the following states?
questions.explanation: NH 18 runs from Gobindpur near Dhanbad in Jharkhand through Bokaro, Purulia in West Bengal, Jamshedpur and Baripada to Balasore in Odisha; it does not enter Bihar.

questions.text: On 14 January 2020, with which Indian bank did the South-Central Railways sign an MoU to implement door-step banking at 585 railway stations?
questions.explanation: South Central Railway signed the MoU with the State Bank of India on 14 January 2020: SBI collects the cash earnings of all 585 stations of the zone, which used to be sent in cash safes on trains.

questions.text: Who among the following was conferred with the 28th Bihari Puraskar for 2018 for the novel ‘Swapnapash’, in November 2019?
questions.explanation: The K K Birla Foundation's Bihari Puraskar honours a Hindi or Rajasthani work by a writer from Rajasthan; the 28th, for 2018, went to Manisha Kulshreshtha for her novel 'Swapnapash'.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was one of the founders of the Congress Socialist Party?
questions.explanation: The Congress Socialist Party was formed within the Congress in 1934 by Jayaprakash Narayan, Acharya Narendra Dev, Ram Manohar Lohia and others. S K Patil and Atulya Ghosh were Congress party bosses, and C N Annadurai founded the DMK.

questions.text: Who among the following did Babur defeat in the year 1528 at Chanderi?
questions.explanation: In 1528 Babur took the fort of Chanderi from the Rajput chief Medini Rai, an ally of Rana Sanga. Ibrahim Lodi had fallen at Panipat in 1526, and Bappa Rawal was an eighth-century ruler of Mewar.

questions.text: Which wrestler claimed the second silver medal for India after going down to Japan’s Haruna Okuno in the finals of UWW Under-23 World Championships at Budapest in 2019?
questions.explanation: Pooja Gehlot won silver in the women's 53 kg at the 2019 Under-23 World Championships in Budapest, losing the final to Haruna Okuno.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was the founder of the Ramakrishna Mission?
questions.explanation: Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897, in the name of his guru Sri Ramakrishna. Swami Dayanand founded the Arya Samaj, Atmaram Pandurang the Prarthana Samaj, and Debendranath Tagore led the Brahmo Samaj.

questions.text: The 5th International Film Festival with the theme ‘Comedy’ was organised by the Culture and Tourism Departments in collaboration with Prayas Production (Mumbai) in which city?
questions.explanation: The 5th Khajuraho International Film Festival, held in 2019 in the temple town of Khajuraho in Madhya Pradesh, had comedy as its theme.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a scalar quantity?
questions.explanation: Torque, the turning effect of a force (r × F), has a direction as well as a size, so it is a vector. Volume, temperature and time have size only.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT unicellular?
questions.explanation: Spirogyra is a green alga made of many cells joined in long filaments. Amoeba, Plasmodium (the malaria parasite) and Paramecium are single-celled.

questions.text: Which of the following viruses is responsible for causing influenza?
questions.explanation: Influenza viruses were classed as myxoviruses (now the family Orthomyxoviridae). The varicella virus causes chickenpox, the rubeola virus measles, and the poliovirus polio.

questions.text: In which of the following countries was the first Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer, the first programmable general purpose electronic digital computer, developed?
questions.explanation: ENIAC was built at the University of Pennsylvania in the United States by John Mauchly and J Presper Eckert, and completed in 1945.

questions.text: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution are Indian citizens guaranteed the right to six fundamental freedoms?
questions.explanation: Article 19(1) guarantees citizens six freedoms: of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession or trade. A seventh, to property, was removed by the 44th Amendment (1978).

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The police used tear gas to ______ the crowd.
questions.explanation: To 'disperse' a crowd is to scatter it, which is what tear gas is used for. 'Disburse' means to pay out money.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Take something with a pinch of salt
options: To take long to understand what is being said
To think of oneself as always right
To believe only part of something
questions.explanation: To take something 'with a pinch of salt' is to believe only part of it, doubting that it is wholly true.

questions.text: Select the word that means the same as the given group of words. A person weak and disabled by illness
questions.explanation: An 'invalid' is a person made weak or disabled by illness or injury. An activist campaigns for a cause and a petitioner makes a formal request.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'pneumonia', with a silent 'p' followed by 'eu'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. All her life Ms. Foster had a great fear of missing a train, a plane, a boat or (1)______ a theatre curtain. In other respects, she was not a (2)______ nervous woman. But the mere thought of (3)______ on occasions like these would throw her (4)______ such a nervous state that a tiny muscle in the corner of her left eye would (5)______ twitch .This would disappear once she had boarded the plane etc.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: 'Even' introduces the most surprising item in the list: besides a train, a plane or a boat, she feared missing a theatre curtain.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. All her life Ms. Foster had a great fear of missing a train, a plane, a boat or (1)______ a theatre curtain. In other respects, she was not a (2)______ nervous woman. But the mere thought of (3)______ on occasions like these would throw her (4)______ such a nervous state that a tiny muscle in the corner of her left eye would (5)______ twitch .This would disappear once she had boarded the plane etc.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed before the adjective 'nervous': 'not a particularly nervous woman'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. All her life Ms. Foster had a great fear of missing a train, a plane, a boat or (1)______ a theatre curtain. In other respects, she was not a (2)______ nervous woman. But the mere thought of (3)______ on occasions like these would throw her (4)______ such a nervous state that a tiny muscle in the corner of her left eye would (5)______ twitch .This would disappear once she had boarded the plane etc.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3.
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'of' a gerund is needed, and her fear is of arriving late: 'the mere thought of being late'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. All her life Ms. Foster had a great fear of missing a train, a plane, a boat or (1)______ a theatre curtain. In other respects, she was not a (2)______ nervous woman. But the mere thought of (3)______ on occasions like these would throw her (4)______ such a nervous state that a tiny muscle in the corner of her left eye would (5)______ twitch .This would disappear once she had boarded the plane etc.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.
questions.explanation: To 'throw someone into' a state is to put them suddenly into it: 'throw her into such a nervous state'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. All her life Ms. Foster had a great fear of missing a train, a plane, a boat or (1)______ a theatre curtain. In other respects, she was not a (2)______ nervous woman. But the mere thought of (3)______ on occasions like these would throw her (4)______ such a nervous state that a tiny muscle in the corner of her left eye would (5)______ twitch .This would disappear once she had boarded the plane etc.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5.
questions.explanation: After the modal 'would' the plain verb follows, and 'begin' takes a to-infinitive: 'would begin to twitch'.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Subhash Gidwani is selling dolls, which are type of Madhya Pradesh’s village culture, at the Annual Dastakar Bazaar, held in January every year in Delhi.
options: held in January every year in Delhi
which are type of Madhya Pradesh’s village culture
questions.explanation: 'Type' is a singular countable noun and cannot stand without an article; the sense needed is 'which are typical of Madhya Pradesh's village culture'. The bazaar segment is correct whether read as the sentence prints it ('at the Annual Dastakar Bazaar') or as its option does ('in the annual ...').

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order. A. Finally, she takes the decision to go searching for livelihood in the nearby town. B. They are: Lakua and his wife, Nathuni. C. The latter, burdened with a paralytic husband and two children, battles to survive. D. The film ‘Wayfarers’ narrates the journey of a poor couple in Jharkhand.
questions.explanation: D introduces the film and the poor couple, B names them, C turns to 'the latter', Nathuni, and her struggle, and A, beginning 'Finally', gives her decision: DBCA.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order. A. The Emperor would view the comic acts from the jharokha, a special window of his palace. B. On the festival of Holi, the Emperor was entertained with mimicry, impersonation and play-acting. C. Bahadur Shah Jafar’s life and times are described in a book called ‘City of my heart.’ D. Finally, the most talented of the performers would be generously awarded by the king.
questions.explanation: C introduces the book on the Emperor's life and times, B describes the Holi entertainment, A how the Emperor watched 'the comic acts', and D, beginning 'Finally', the rewards: CBAD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. The Delhi Birla International School “alumnus occupy” leading positions in different areas of profession and service.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'alumni occupy': leading positions in different areas of profession and service point to many former pupils, so the plural 'alumni' (singular 'alumnus') takes the plural verb 'occupy'. 'Alumnus occupies' is also grammatical, but it would have one person holding positions across many fields.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of given sentence. The foreigner said to the farmer, “Can you tell me the way to the nearest hotel?”
options: The foreigner told the farmer if he could tell him the way to the nearest hotel.
The foreigner suggested the farmer if he could tell him the way to the nearest hotel.
The foreigner exclaimed with the farmer if he could tell him the way to the nearest hotel.
The foreigner enquired of the farmer if he could tell him the way to the nearest hotel.
questions.explanation: A question is reported with a verb of asking, such as 'enquired of', followed by 'if'; 'told', 'suggested' and 'exclaimed with' do not report a question.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. CONGENIAL
questions.explanation: 'Congenial' means pleasant to be with because of shared interests or character: 'compatible'. 'Servile' means too eager to please, 'aloof' distant and 'bombastic' pompous in speech.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. PACIFIST
questions.explanation: A 'pacifist' opposes war and violence; a 'warmonger' seeks to stir up war. A 'nihilist' rejects all moral principles.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Full of sound and fury
options: Someone who gets angry very quickly
Merely loud and angry words but ineffective
questions.explanation: 'Full of sound and fury', from Shakespeare's 'Macbeth', describes loud, angry talk that means or achieves nothing.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. You must make a choice immediately because there is few time left.
questions.explanation: 'Few' goes with plural countable nouns; 'time' is uncountable, so it takes 'little': 'there is little time left'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Ritu is an ______ reader. I always find her with a book.
questions.explanation: An 'avid' reader is a keen and eager one, which fits someone always found with a book. 'Erratic' and 'inattentive' suggest the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. PEDIGREE
questions.explanation: 'Pedigree' means a line of descent or ancestry: 'lineage'. A 'mongrel' is a dog of mixed breed, the opposite of a pedigree animal.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. For the last two years Shweta “has being” diligently working with Rohingya refugees to create colourful table mats using their local weaving techniques.
questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous is 'has been' with the '-ing' form: 'Shweta has been diligently working'. 'Have' does not go with the singular subject.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. PROLIFIC
questions.explanation: 'Prolific' means producing much, so its opposite is 'unproductive'. 'Rich' and 'abundant' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. Chhattisgarh organised the first ever ‘All India Folk Dance Festival’ in January 2020.
options: The first ever ‘All India Folk Dance Festival’ was organised by the Chhattisgarh State in January 2020.
The first ever ‘All India Folk Dance Festival’ was being organised by the Chhattisgarh State in January 2020.
The first ever ‘All India Folk Dance Festival’ will be organised by the Chhattisgarh State in January 2020.
The first ever ‘All India Folk Dance Festival’ had been organised by the Chhattisgarh State in January 2020.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'organised' becomes 'was organised' in the passive; the other options change the tense.

questions.text: Select the word that means the same as the given group of words. Happening every two years
questions.explanation: 'Biennial' means happening every two years; 'biannual' means twice a year, 'triennial' every three years and 'centennial' every hundred years.

questions.text: Which instrument is used to measure the level of humidity?
questions.explanation: A hygrometer measures the humidity of the air. A hydrometer measures the density of liquids, a fathometer the depth of water and a galvanometer small electric currents.

questions.text: The first barcode system was developed by:
questions.explanation: Norman Joseph Woodland and Bernard Silver invented the barcode; their patent, which described codes of straight lines and of concentric circles, was granted in 1952. John McCarthy coined the term 'artificial intelligence'.

questions.text: Which of the following forms of martial arts is from Kerala?
questions.explanation: Kalarippayattu is the martial art of Kerala. Paika Akhada is from Odisha, Gatka from Punjab and Silambam from Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: How many Vedangas are there in total?
questions.explanation: There are six Vedangas, the auxiliary studies of the Vedas: Shiksha (phonetics), Kalpa (ritual), Vyakarana (grammar), Nirukta (etymology), Chhanda (metre) and Jyotisha (astronomy).

questions.text: Which of the following characteristics of sound is measured in hertz (Hz)?
questions.explanation: The hertz, one vibration a second, is the unit of frequency. Loudness is expressed in decibels and wavelength in metres.

questions.text: In which year did NITI Aayog come into existence?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015.

questions.text: The term ‘monsoon’ is derived from a/an:
questions.explanation: 'Monsoon' comes from the Arabic 'mausim', meaning season, after the seasonal reversal of the winds.

questions.text: In which year did the first Elected Parliament with two houses come into being in India?
questions.explanation: After the first general elections of 1951-52, the first elected Parliament, with the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, came into being in 1952.

questions.text: Who is author of the book ‘The Judgement: Inside Story of the Emergency in India’?
questions.explanation: 'The Judgement: Inside Story of the Emergency in India' (1977) is by the journalist Kuldip Nayar, who was detained during the Emergency.

questions.text: Who among the following is nicknamed the ‘Baltimore Bullet’?
questions.explanation: The swimmer Michael Phelps, born in Baltimore, is nicknamed the 'Baltimore Bullet'.

questions.text: In January 2020, who among the following launched the first girder of the Mumbai Trans-Harbour Link (MTHL)?
questions.explanation: Uddhav Thackeray, then Chief Minister of Maharashtra, launched the first girder of the Mumbai Trans-Harbour Link at the Sewri end on 15 January 2020.

questions.text: Who Inaugurated the National Tribal Festival "Aadi Mahotsav" in New Delhi in November 2019?
questions.explanation: Home Minister Amit Shah inaugurated Aadi Mahotsav, the national tribal festival of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs and TRIFED, at Dilli Haat, INA, on 16 November 2019.

questions.text: Which country ranked first in the 2019 Human Development India Index?
questions.explanation: Norway topped the Human Development Index in UNDP's Human Development Report 2019, released in December 2019, ahead of Switzerland and Ireland.

questions.text: Who won the International Hockey Federation’s (FIH) Player of the Year award in 2019?
questions.explanation: India's hockey captain Manpreet Singh was named FIH Player of the Year for 2019, the first Indian to win the award.

questions.text: The Hornbill Festival is celebrated in which state?
questions.explanation: The Hornbill Festival, a showcase of the cultures of the Naga tribes, is held every December in Nagaland, at Kisama near Kohima.

questions.text: Telangana became the 29th state of India in which year?
questions.explanation: Telangana was formed from Andhra Pradesh on 2 June 2014, becoming India's 29th state.

questions.text: Which of the following was invented by Walter Hunt?
questions.explanation: The American inventor Walter Hunt patented the safety pin in 1849. The miners' safety lamp is Humphry Davy's.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was a leader from Allahabad (now Prayagraj) in the revolt against the British in 1857?
questions.explanation: Maulvi Liaquat Ali led the revolt of 1857 at Allahabad. Tatya Tope fought at Kanpur, Khan Bahadur Khan led at Bareilly and Rani Laxmi Bai at Jhansi.

questions.text: The Bomdila Pass is located in which state?
questions.explanation: The Bomdila Pass is in the West Kameng district of Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.text: Trackball is which of the following devices?
questions.explanation: A trackball is a pointing device, a ball rolled by the fingers to move the cursor, so it is an input device.

questions.text: Which country is the 2019 ICC Cricket World Cup champion?
questions.explanation: England won the 2019 ICC Cricket World Cup, beating New Zealand at Lord's on the boundary count after the final and its super over were tied.

questions.text: The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of the following Indian states?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer crosses Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram; Andhra Pradesh lies wholly south of it.

questions.text: Who among the following is one of the Deputy Operations Director of the Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM)?
questions.explanation: Nandini Harinath of ISRO was one of the Deputy Operations Directors of the Mars Orbiter Mission, launched in November 2013.

questions.text: Which of the following is the second largest artificial lake in Asia?
questions.explanation: Dhebar (Jaisamand) Lake near Udaipur, Rajasthan, formed by the dam Maharana Jai Singh built across the Gomati river in the late 17th century, is the lake usually cited as Asia's second-largest artificial lake. Chilika, Chandubi and Kolleru are natural lakes.

questions.text: In October 2019, which of the following pairs of Indian cities was included by UNESCO in its network of ‘Creative Cities’ on the occasion of World Cities Day 2019?
questions.explanation: On World Cities Day, 31 October 2019, UNESCO added Mumbai (film) and Hyderabad (gastronomy) to its Creative Cities Network.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank: As part of the ______ Classical Indian Music Festival leading vocalists and instrumentalist are taking the stage this evening.
questions.explanation: 'Ongoing' means still in progress, which suits a festival whose performers are taking the stage this evening. A 'postponed' festival would not be under way, and 'foregone' and 'onset' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom: Under the weather
questions.explanation: To be 'under the weather' is to feel slightly unwell or in low spirits.

questions.text: Select the correct Indirect form of the given sentence. “Let’s sit out in the sun,” Anya said.
options: Anya is suggesting that we sit out in the sun.
Anya had suggested that we sit out in the sun.
Anya suggested that we sit out in the sun.
Anya was suggesting that we sit out in the sun.
questions.explanation: A suggestion with 'Let's' is reported with 'suggested that', and the past reporting verb 'said' keeps it in the simple past: 'Anya suggested that we sit out in the sun.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word: ALTRUIST
questions.explanation: An altruist is a person who selflessly works for the good of others: a 'philanthropist'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Jonas Karlsson and Ruth Osborne are two chefs who (1)______ about promoting zero waste in cooking, whether it is (2)______ restaurants or at home. It means using every part of a food (3)______. So for example, you needn’t peel carrots. You can (4)______ scrub off the surface lightly and cook them You can also find ways (5)______ and recycle by- products like using coffee grounds to make biscuits.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: 'Who' stands for the plural 'two chefs' and the passage is in the present tense, so the verb is 'are'; the adjective 'passionate' (not the adverb 'passionately') goes before 'about': 'who are passionate about promoting zero waste'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Jonas Karlsson and Ruth Osborne are two chefs who (1)______ about promoting zero waste in cooking, whether it is (2)______ restaurants or at home. It means using every part of a food (3)______. So for example, you needn’t peel carrots. You can (4)______ scrub off the surface lightly and cook them You can also find ways (5)______ and recycle by- products like using coffee grounds to make biscuits.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
questions.explanation: Cooking takes place 'in' restaurants or at home: 'in' is used for being inside a place.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Jonas Karlsson and Ruth Osborne are two chefs who (1)______ about promoting zero waste in cooking, whether it is (2)______ restaurants or at home. It means using every part of a food (3)______. So for example, you needn’t peel carrots. You can (4)______ scrub off the surface lightly and cook them You can also find ways (5)______ and recycle by- products like using coffee grounds to make biscuits.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3.
questions.explanation: The blank needs a noun naming the item of food whose every part is used: 'a food product'. A 'food producer' is a person or firm, 'food production' is the process, and 'productive' is an adjective.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Jonas Karlsson and Ruth Osborne are two chefs who (1)______ about promoting zero waste in cooking, whether it is (2)______ restaurants or at home. It means using every part of a food (3)______. So for example, you needn’t peel carrots. You can (4)______ scrub off the surface lightly and cook them You can also find ways (5)______ and recycle by- products like using coffee grounds to make biscuits.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.
questions.explanation: 'Just' means simply: instead of peeling carrots you can simply scrub the surface lightly. 'Rarely', 'seldom' and 'never' would contradict the advice.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Jonas Karlsson and Ruth Osborne are two chefs who (1)______ about promoting zero waste in cooking, whether it is (2)______ restaurants or at home. It means using every part of a food (3)______. So for example, you needn’t peel carrots. You can (4)______ scrub off the surface lightly and cook them You can also find ways (5)______ and recycle by- products like using coffee grounds to make biscuits.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5.
questions.explanation: 'Ways' takes a to-infinitive with the base form of the verb, here paired with 'recycle': 'ways to reuse and recycle by-products'. 'Redone' and 'reused' are participles, and 'redo' does not fit the sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. I think “you’d better paid” online immediately as you may not get time to visit the bank later on during the day.
questions.explanation: 'Had better' ('d better) is followed by the base form of the verb: 'you'd better pay online immediately'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word: COARSE
questions.explanation: 'Coarse' means rough or crude; its opposite is 'refined'. 'Vulgar' is close in meaning.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given: A part of the city especially the slum area
questions.explanation: A ghetto is a part of a city, especially a slum area, lived in by a minority group. A suburb is an outlying residential district and a metropolis a large city.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. The vet told me to put eye drops and ointment in my pet’s eyes.
options: I had been told by the vet to put eye drops and ointment in my pet’s eyes.
I am being told by the vet to put eye drops and ointment in my pet’s eyes.
I was told by the vet to put eye drops and ointment in my pet’s eyes.
I was being told by the vet to put eye drops and ointment in my pet’s eyes.
questions.explanation: The object 'me' becomes the subject 'I', and the simple past 'told' becomes 'was told': 'I was told by the vet to put eye drops and ointment in my pet's eyes.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom: The straw that broke the camel’s back
options: To show strength and continue without a fuss
To be the last in a series of events leading one to feel that it is intolerable
To undertake a difficult journey across a desert
To make a wish for an escape from existing conditions
questions.explanation: 'The straw that broke the camel's back' is the last of a series of small burdens or problems, after which a situation becomes unbearable.

questions.text: Select the wrongly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'privilege'. 'Mileage', 'gait' and 'truism' are spelt correctly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word: CONTEMPLATE
questions.explanation: To 'contemplate' is to think about something deeply; its opposite is to 'ignore' it. 'Meditate' is close in meaning.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given: Making one feel very sad
questions.explanation: 'Heart-wrenching' means causing great sadness. 'Heart-stopping' means thrilling or frightening, 'heart-searching' is close examination of one's own feelings, and a 'heart-to-heart' is a frank talk.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order. A. At the onset of his journey, his mother guides him how to survive and navigate the world. B. ‘Silo’s Journey’ is a film made by a wildlife film director. C. It follows the journey of a young reindeer’s first year at close range. D. Sharing this journey is his friend-a curious red-haired squirrel.
questions.explanation: B introduces the film, C says it follows a young reindeer's first year, A tells how his mother guides him at the start of his journey, and D adds the friend who shares it: BCAD.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Firecrackers have seized by the government went off while being defused on the banks of the river Ganga, in a town in West Bengal.
options: on the banks of the river Ganga
Firecrackers have seized by the government
in a town in West Bengal
questions.explanation: A past participle alone should describe the firecrackers: 'Firecrackers seized by the government went off ...'. 'Have seized' adds a second main verb and the wrong, active sense.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. A 12 year old archer was airlifted to Delhi when he met with an accident while practice for the Khelo India Games in Guwahati.
options: when he met with an accident
while practice for the Khelo India Games
questions.explanation: After 'while' a participle is needed: 'while practising for the Khelo India Games'. ('12 year old' would usually be hyphenated, '12-year-old', but that is a matter of punctuation, not grammar.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Prince Harry and his wife, Megan Markle announced their decision to ______ from their role as senior royals by leaving United Kingdom and limiting their royal commitments.
questions.explanation: To 'step back' from a role is to withdraw from it, which fits leaving the United Kingdom and limiting their royal commitments. To 'step up' is to increase or take on more, and to 'step in' is to intervene.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order. A. Soon a special friendship develops between the two girls in war torn Syria. B. While at her grandmother’s place, Suzan meets Rana, a Syrian girl, who lives in a nearby refugee camp. C. ‘Summer with Rana’ is a film by Sanne Vogel, who began her film career as early as 17. D. Her film revolves around Suzan, the young girl who is spending her summer holiday with her grandmother, while her mother has gone to Syria, as a war reporter.
questions.explanation: C introduces the film and its maker, D says it revolves around Suzan staying with her grandmother, B has Suzan meet Rana there, and A tells how their friendship develops: CDBA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word: HAUGHTY
questions.explanation: 'Haughty' means proud and looking down on others: 'arrogant'. 'Humble' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement . It is evident from current research that young adults “is more like” to develop an interest in spoken English if there is a change in methodology.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'young adults' takes 'are', and the adjective needed before 'to develop' is 'likely' (probable): 'young adults are more likely to develop an interest'.

questions.text: Which of the following cell organelles is responsible for the storage, modification and packaging of products in vesicles?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus stores, modifies and packages products made in the cell and sends them off in vesicles. Mitochondria release energy, plastids hold pigments or stored food, and the endoplasmic reticulum makes and carries proteins and lipids.

questions.text: In which state is the ‘Chapchar Kut’ festival celebrated in the month of March every year?
questions.explanation: Chapchar Kut is Mizoram's spring festival, held in March once the forest has been cleared for jhum (shifting) cultivation.

questions.text: In Microsoft Office 2016, which shortcut key is used to open the Design tab?
questions.explanation: In Word and PowerPoint 2016, Alt + G opens the Design tab. Ctrl + A selects everything, Shift + F3 changes the case of selected text and Ctrl + K inserts a hyperlink.

questions.text: The Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare launched a campaign to reduce child mortality due to pneumonia in November 2019. What is the name of that campaign?
questions.explanation: SAANS (Social Awareness and Action to Neutralise Pneumonia Successfully) was launched by the Health Minister, Harsh Vardhan, in November 2019 to reduce child deaths from pneumonia.

questions.text: Which article of the Constitution of India states that no citizen can be discriminated against on the basis of his/her religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth?
questions.explanation: Article 15 forbids the State to discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

questions.text: On whose birth anniversary did Kanshi Ram found the Bahujan Samaj Party?
questions.explanation: Kanshi Ram founded the Bahujan Samaj Party on 14 April 1984, the birth anniversary of B. R. Ambedkar.

questions.text: Which type of computers is used to control air traffic and radar of national defence?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives hybrid computers, which join analogue parts that take in continuously changing signals, such as radar returns, to digital parts that process them; computer-awareness textbooks list defence and radar systems among their uses. (Such systems today are built from digital computers fed through analogue-to-digital converters.)

questions.text: In which year was the ‘Ramnath Goenka Excellence in Journalism’ award instituted in India?
questions.explanation: The Indian Express Group instituted the Ramnath Goenka Excellence in Journalism Awards, named after its founder, in 2006; Prime Minister Manmohan Singh presented the first of them in New Delhi in April 2006.

questions.text: Aqua regia is a freshly prepared mixture of concentrated hydrochloric acid and concentrated nitric acid. What is the ratio of this mixture?
questions.explanation: Aqua regia is three parts concentrated hydrochloric acid to one part concentrated nitric acid; it dissolves gold and platinum.

questions.text: Who won India's first gold medal at the Asian Wrestling Championship 2019?
questions.explanation: Bajrang Punia won the men's freestyle 65 kg title at Xi'an, China, in April 2019, India's only gold at those championships.

questions.text: In which year did Babur defeat the Sultan of Delhi, Ibrahim Lodi, at Panipat and capture Delhi and Agra?
questions.explanation: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat in April 1526 and took Delhi and Agra, founding the Mughal Empire.

questions.text: At which position was India ranked at the 14th Asian Shooting Championship?
questions.explanation: At the 14th Asian Shooting Championships, in Doha in November 2019, India finished fourth in the medal table with 5 gold, 10 silver and 11 bronze, behind China, South Korea and North Korea.

questions.text: Which of the following is the most dominant species of trees found in the Tropical Deciduous Forests of India?
questions.explanation: Teak is the dominant tree of India's tropical deciduous (monsoon) forests. Deodar is a Himalayan conifer, and coconut and rubber belong to the wetter tropics.

questions.text: What is the height of Mt. Godwin Austen, also known as Mt. K2?
questions.explanation: K2 (Godwin Austen), in the Karakoram, is 8,611 m high, the second-highest peak in the world.

questions.text: In which year did the government of India approve the release of a commemorative stamp to mark the 50th anniversary of the Bhakra-Nangal Dam?
questions.explanation: The Bhakra Dam was dedicated to the nation by Jawaharlal Nehru in October 1963, and the commemorative stamp for its 50th anniversary was approved and released on 22 October 2013.

questions.text: In which year was the Kaziranga National Park declared as a Reserved Forest?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga, first notified as a proposed reserve forest in 1905, was declared a Reserve Forest in 1908; it became a national park in 1974.

questions.text: In which city was the ‘11th Nuclear Energy Conclave (NEC)-2019’ held?
questions.explanation: The India Energy Forum held the 11th Nuclear Energy Conclave in New Delhi on 18 October 2019; its theme was the economics of nuclear power.

questions.text: As of January 2020, how many cultural properties from India were inscribed in the UNESCO World Heritage List?
questions.explanation: In January 2020 India had 38 World Heritage Sites: 30 cultural, 7 natural and 1 mixed (Khangchendzonga National Park). The Walled City of Jaipur, inscribed in July 2019, was the latest.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was appointed as the Curator of Ancient Monuments in 1880?
questions.explanation: Henry Hardy Cole was appointed Curator of Ancient Monuments in India in 1880. Alexander Cunningham was then Director General of the Archaeological Survey, and John Marshall took that post in 1902.

questions.text: Which Mumbai cricketer became the youngest batsman in the world to score a double hundred in list A cricket?
questions.explanation: Yashasvi Jaiswal, aged 17, scored 203 for Mumbai against Jharkhand in the Vijay Hazare Trophy in October 2019; when the exam was held (October 2020) he was the youngest batsman to have scored a List A double century.

questions.text: According to a Social Mobility Index released by World Economic Forum on 20 January 2020, India was ranked at which position?
questions.explanation: The World Economic Forum's first Global Social Mobility Index, released in January 2020, placed India 76th of 82 countries; Denmark was first.

questions.text: What is the chemical formula of dichlorodifluoromethane?
questions.explanation: Dichlorodifluoromethane (Freon-12), a CFC once widely used in refrigerators, is methane (CH₄) with its four hydrogens replaced by two chlorines and two fluorines: CCl₂F₂.

questions.text: How many countries were members of International Finance Corporation (IFC) till April 2019?
questions.explanation: Tuvalu joined the International Finance Corporation, the World Bank Group's arm for investment in the private sector, on 16 April 2019 as its 185th member country.

questions.text: On 19 January 2020, India successfully test fired a nuclear-capable K-4 ballistic missile off the coast of Andhra Pradesh. What is the strike range of this missile?
questions.explanation: The K-4, a submarine-launched ballistic missile built by the DRDO for the Arihant-class submarines, has a range of about 3,500 km.

questions.text: Who among the following writers was conferred with the ‘29th Saraswati Samman’ for his short stories collection 'Chequebook'?
questions.explanation: The Sindhi writer Vasdev Mohi received the 29th Saraswati Samman, for 2019, for his short story collection 'Chequebook'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'gallery', with an 'e'.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. Gulliver easily pulled all the warships of the enemy after him.
options: All the warships of Gulliver were easily pulled by the enemy after him.
All the warships of the enemy were being easily pulled by Gulliver after him.
All the warships of the enemy had been easily pulled by Gulliver after him.
All the warships of the enemy were easily pulled by Gulliver after him.
questions.explanation: The object 'all the warships of the enemy' becomes the subject, and the simple past 'pulled' becomes 'were pulled', plural to agree with it: 'All the warships of the enemy were easily pulled by Gulliver after him.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. Order was quickly ______ in the area after the scuffle between the two groups.
questions.explanation: Order is 'restored', brought back, after a disturbance. Things that are broken are repaired or rebuilt, and 'recovered' does not go with order.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. CANDID
questions.explanation: 'Candid' means frank and open; its opposite is 'devious', sly and dishonest. 'Frank', 'genuine' and 'truthful' are close to synonyms.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. During organised tours, tourists can visit a former Nazi compound 40 kilometres (1)______ Berlin called the ‘Forbidden City’. Twenty thousand people (2)______ here every year to learn about Nazi military history. The Nazis (3)______ militarily active at the compound, (4)______ was kept secret in a forest and behind a fence. The Nazis (5)______ much of World War II from here.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 1.
questions.explanation: A distance is measured from a place: '40 kilometres from Berlin'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. During organised tours, tourists can visit a former Nazi compound 40 kilometres (1)______ Berlin called the ‘Forbidden City’. Twenty thousand people (2)______ here every year to learn about Nazi military history. The Nazis (3)______ militarily active at the compound, (4)______ was kept secret in a forest and behind a fence. The Nazis (5)______ much of World War II from here.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Tourists 'visit' the compound to learn its history: 'Twenty thousand people visit here every year'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. During organised tours, tourists can visit a former Nazi compound 40 kilometres (1)______ Berlin called the ‘Forbidden City’. Twenty thousand people (2)______ here every year to learn about Nazi military history. The Nazis (3)______ militarily active at the compound, (4)______ was kept secret in a forest and behind a fence. The Nazis (5)______ much of World War II from here.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'The Nazis' and the past time need 'were': 'The Nazis were militarily active at the compound'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. During organised tours, tourists can visit a former Nazi compound 40 kilometres (1)______ Berlin called the ‘Forbidden City’. Twenty thousand people (2)______ here every year to learn about Nazi military history. The Nazis (3)______ militarily active at the compound, (4)______ was kept secret in a forest and behind a fence. The Nazis (5)______ much of World War II from here.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 4.
questions.explanation: After a comma, a relative clause about a thing, the compound, begins with 'which'; 'who' and 'whom' refer to people.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. During organised tours, tourists can visit a former Nazi compound 40 kilometres (1)______ Berlin called the ‘Forbidden City’. Twenty thousand people (2)______ here every year to learn about Nazi military history. The Nazis (3)______ militarily active at the compound, (4)______ was kept secret in a forest and behind a fence. The Nazis (5)______ much of World War II from here.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The secret compound served as a headquarters, from which the Nazis 'planned' much of the war.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Make a beeline
questions.explanation: To 'make a beeline' for a place is to go straight to it, quickly.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Flesh eating animal
questions.explanation: A carnivore eats flesh. An insectivore eats insects, an omnivore both plants and animals, and a herbivore only plants.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Look after
questions.explanation: To 'look after' someone or something is to take care of them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. RECONCILE
questions.explanation: To 'reconcile' differences is to settle them: 'resolve'. 'Agitate' and 'scatter' are nearly opposite.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A ruler with total power over a country, typically one who has obtained control by force
questions.explanation: A dictator rules with total power, usually having seized it by force. A democrat supports rule by the people, and a traitor betrays his country.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. I said to Kirti, "These plants will take about two months to flower."
options: I told Kirti that those plants will be taking about two months to flower.
I told Kirti that these plants will take about two months to flower.
I told Kirti that those plants would take about two months to flower.
I told Kirti that those plants take about two months to flower.
questions.explanation: 'Said to' becomes 'told', and after the past reporting verb 'will' moves back to 'would' and 'these' becomes 'those'.

questions.text: In the given sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. When the boys were playing the match, it suddenly starts raining.
questions.explanation: The story is in the past ('were playing'), so the main clause needs the past tense too: 'it suddenly started raining'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. While my “parents talked” to the visitor, I made tea in the kitchen.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'parents were talking': after 'while', the past continuous presents the talk as an action in progress, against which the tea was made. The simple past 'talked' is not ungrammatical for two actions at the same time, but the continuous is the usual form for such a background action.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. In December 2019, Typhoon Kammuri came to the Philippines. B. They closed schools and evacuated hundreds of thousands of people from their homes. C. Officials closed the international airport in the capital city of Manila for 12 hours. D. It flooded streets and damaged many houses and power lines.
questions.explanation: A introduces the typhoon, D says what damage it did, C says officials closed Manila's airport, and B adds what 'they' (the officials) also did: ADCB.

questions.text: In the given sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. The publics are not satisfied with the new act.
questions.explanation: 'Public', meaning people in general, is a collective noun used without a plural '-s': 'The public is not satisfied with the new act.'

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. The cable was thick as pack-thread, and the bars were the size of knitting needles. B. Then I made fifty hooks by twisting three bars together at a time. C. I ordered a great quantity of strong cable and bars of iron. D. I twisted the cables together and made fifty strong cords.
questions.explanation: C says what was ordered (cable and iron bars), A describes them, D says the cables were twisted into cords, and B ('Then') says the bars were twisted into hooks: CADB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. He ______ his studies even after leaving college and finally got a Ph.D. degree.
questions.explanation: To 'pursue' one's studies is to continue with them. 'Persisted' would need 'in' and 'carried' would need 'on', and 'sought' does not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. After “switching off the light,” he went off to sleep.
options: he has switched off the light
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: 'he' is the subject of both the opening phrase 'After switching off the light' and the main clause, and 'the light' is a particular one.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. SALVAGE
questions.explanation: To 'salvage' something is to rescue it from loss or damage: 'save'. 'Lose' and 'waste' are nearly opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. CONVENIENCE
questions.explanation: Convenience is ease and freedom from difficulty; a 'hindrance' is something that gets in the way, the nearest opposite here. 'Assistance' is close in meaning.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India states the directive principles of state policy on ‘promotion of international peace and security’?
questions.explanation: Article 51 directs the State to promote international peace and security, keep just and honourable relations between nations, foster respect for international law and encourage settling disputes by arbitration. Article 49 protects monuments, Article 62 concerns the election to fill a vacancy in the office of President and Article 69 the Vice-President's oath.

questions.text: Who is the first IPS officer to be honoured with Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award?
questions.explanation: Aparna Kumar, a 2002-batch Uttar Pradesh cadre IPS officer who has climbed the highest peak of every continent, received the Tenzing Norgay National Adventure Award 2018 for land adventure in August 2019, the first IPS officer to receive it.

questions.text: Who is the first Indian American to become Governor of State of USA?
questions.explanation: Bobby Jindal became Governor of Louisiana in January 2008, the first Indian American to govern a US state; Nikki Haley of South Carolina followed in 2011. Bill Clinton and John Tyler were US Presidents.

questions.text: Transistors belong to which of the following generation of the computers?
questions.explanation: Second-generation computers replaced vacuum tubes with transistors. The first generation used vacuum tubes, the third integrated circuits and the fourth microprocessors.

questions.text: Which of the following is the basic SI unit of thermo dynamic temperature?
questions.explanation: The kelvin is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature. The mole is the unit of amount of substance, the candela of luminous intensity and the metre of length.

questions.text: Related area of Golden Revolution is:
questions.explanation: The Golden Revolution is the growth of horticulture, fruits above all (and honey). Eggs are linked with the Silver Revolution, oilseeds with the Yellow and fish with the Blue.

questions.text: Which of the following sites of Indus valley civilization is not on the bank of river Indus?
questions.explanation: Ropar (Rupnagar) in Punjab stands on the Sutlej. Mohenjodaro, Chanhudaro and Kot Diji are all in Sindh, in the Indus plain; Kot Diji lies on the east bank of the Indus, opposite Mohenjodaro.

questions.text: Who among the following won the World Badminton championship title in 2019?
questions.explanation: P V Sindhu won the women's singles title at the BWF World Championships in Basel in August 2019, beating Nozomi Okuhara in the final, and became India's first badminton world champion.

questions.text: Which state does not share its boundary with Myanmar?
questions.explanation: Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram border Myanmar. Sikkim borders Nepal, Bhutan and China.

questions.text: Which of the following is a group of bacteria found in human intestines, whose presence in water indicates contamination by disease-causing microorganisms?
questions.explanation: Coliform bacteria such as E. coli live in the human intestine, so finding them in water shows it has been contaminated with faeces and may carry disease-causing organisms.

questions.text: Which of the following is the base year of a new WPI series effective from April 2017?
questions.explanation: The Wholesale Price Index series with base year 2011-12 replaced the 2004-05 series, effective from April 2017.

questions.text: Who had proposed the motto of Olympics?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Pierre de Coubertin, who proposed 'Citius, Altius, Fortius' as the Olympic motto when the IOC was created in 1894. He had borrowed the phrase from his friend Henri Didon, a Dominican priest, so Didon is credited with the words themselves.

questions.text: Which state in India was the first to introduce the 'Mid-day Meal Scheme' for school children?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu pioneered school midday meals: Madras city's schools served them from the 1920s, and the state extended them widely under Chief Minister K Kamaraj (1954-63), decades before the national programme of 1995.

questions.text: Which of the following observations DOES NOT help in determining whether a chemical reaction has taken place?
questions.explanation: A chemical reaction shows itself by a change in state, a change in colour, the evolution of a gas or a change in temperature. A change in height is not one of these signs.

questions.text: 'Khuang' is a traditional musical instrument of which state?
questions.explanation: The khuang is the traditional drum of the Mizos of Mizoram, played at their dances and festivals.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution deals with formation of New States?
questions.explanation: Article 3, headed 'Formation of new States and alteration of areas, boundaries or names of existing States', lets Parliament form new States and change existing ones. Article 2 covers admitting into the Union, or establishing, States that were not part of India, Article 4 says laws made under Articles 2 and 3 are not amendments under Article 368, and Article 5 deals with citizenship.

questions.text: When was the Human Development Report first published?
questions.explanation: The UNDP published the first Human Development Report, prepared under Mahbub ul Haq, in 1990.

questions.text: Pasi Kongki is folk dance of which state?
questions.explanation: Pasi Kongki is a folk dance of the Adi people of Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.text: Who among the following drafted Article 370 of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: N Gopalaswami Ayyangar, a member of the Constituent Assembly and a minister without portfolio in Nehru's Cabinet, drafted Article 370 on Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who proposed Wardha Scheme or Basic Education?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi set out his plan of basic education (Nai Talim), learning through a productive craft, in 1937; a conference at Wardha endorsed it that October, and a committee under Zakir Husain drew up the Wardha Scheme.

questions.text: Which is the source of Krishna river?
questions.explanation: The Krishna rises in the Western Ghats near Mahabaleshwar, in Maharashtra's Satara district. Multai is the source of the Tapi, Tala (Talakaveri) of the Kaveri and Amarkantak of the Narmada.

questions.text: Who is the author of the Ben-Hur : A Tale of the Christ?
questions.explanation: 'Ben-Hur: A Tale of the Christ' (1880) is a novel by the American general and writer Lew Wallace.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a softcopy devices?
questions.explanation: A plotter prints large drawings on paper, a hard copy. Monitors, projectors and speakers give soft copy output, which is shown or played but not kept on paper.

questions.text: Former finance minister Arun Jaitley passed away in which month of 2019?
questions.explanation: Arun Jaitley died on 24 August 2019 in New Delhi.

questions.text: On which date International Day of Biological Diversity is celebrated?
questions.explanation: The International Day for Biological Diversity is observed on 22 May, the date in 1992 when the text of the Convention on Biological Diversity was adopted.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the given sentence which contains the grammatical error. Soni take her daughter to the park in the evening in a stroller.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'Soni' takes a singular verb in the simple present: 'Soni takes her daughter to the park ...'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Unpretensious' is misspelt: the word is 'unpretentious', modest and not trying to impress.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A type of magic in which spirits, especially evil ones, are used to make things happen
questions.explanation: Sorcery is magic that uses the power of spirits, especially evil ones. Alchemy was the medieval search for a way to turn base metals into gold, and mimicry is imitation.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank in the given sentence. We must not take the future for granted; rather, we should enjoy the ______ joys of our humdrum lives.
questions.explanation: 'Everyday' (one word, an adjective) means ordinary and daily, which goes with 'humdrum lives'. 'Habitual' means done out of habit, and 'future' contradicts the sentence.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One of the reasons we fail to talk convincingly about climate change is that we present it as something “out there”. We (1)______ to make it clear (2)______ it’s linked to (3)______ daily decisions, such as walking (4)______ driving, and not talk about it in (5)______ of abstractions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Need to' says what must be done: 'We need to make it clear ...'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One of the reasons we fail to talk convincingly about climate change is that we present it as something “out there”. We (1)______ to make it clear (2)______ it’s linked to (3)______ daily decisions, such as walking (4)______ driving, and not talk about it in (5)______ of abstractions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Make it clear that' introduces the clause saying what is to be made clear: 'that it's linked to our daily decisions'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One of the reasons we fail to talk convincingly about climate change is that we present it as something “out there”. We (1)______ to make it clear (2)______ it’s linked to (3)______ daily decisions, such as walking (4)______ driving, and not talk about it in (5)______ of abstractions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The writer includes the reader, as 'we' in the same sentence shows: climate change is linked to 'our' daily decisions.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One of the reasons we fail to talk convincingly about climate change is that we present it as something “out there”. We (1)______ to make it clear (2)______ it’s linked to (3)______ daily decisions, such as walking (4)______ driving, and not talk about it in (5)______ of abstractions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Or' joins the two alternatives of the daily choice: 'walking or driving'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank.
