One of the reasons we fail to talk convincingly about climate change is that we present it as something “out there”. We (1)______ to make it clear (2)______ it’s linked to (3)______ daily decisions, such as walking (4)______ driving, and not talk about it in (5)______ of abstractions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'In terms of' means with regard to: not talk about it 'in terms of abstractions'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A deep fissure in the earth's surface
questions.explanation: A chasm is a deep crack or opening in the ground. A tremor is a slight shaking of the ground and an earthquake a violent one.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. “Have you got confirmation” of the receipt of the donation?
questions.explanation: 'Have you got' is correct: 'has' needs a third-person subject, 'did' takes the base form ('did you get'), and 'have' takes the participle 'got', not 'get'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank in the given sentence. A literature festival on the beach: With waves crashing on the beach, the Kerala Literature Festival got ______ in Kozhikode with a range of panel discussions in English and Malayalam.
questions.explanation: To 'get underway' is to begin: the festival began in Kozhikode. 'Wayward' means wilful and hard to control.

questions.text: Select the option that is the passive form of the given sentence. This book explores the secret of leading a long and meaningful life.
options: The secret of leading a long and meaningful life is explored in this book.
The secret of leading a long and meaningful life was being explored by this book.
The secret of leading a long and meaningful life have been explored by this book.
The secret of leading a long and meaningful life had been explored by this book.
questions.explanation: The simple present 'explores' becomes 'is explored' with the singular subject 'the secret': 'The secret of leading a long and meaningful life is explored in this book.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. MOTIF
questions.explanation: A motif is a decorative design or pattern, or an idea that recurs in a work: 'design'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. Have you heard the news that Hema is “looking for greener pastures?”
questions.explanation: To look for 'greener pastures' is to seek better opportunities elsewhere, often a new job.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. EXPUNGE
questions.explanation: To 'expunge' is to erase or remove completely; its opposite is 'insert'. 'Deplete' and 'exhaust' mean to use up.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. The father then wanted his son to pick him up at four in the afternoon so that they could go home together. B. A teenager had just passed his driving test and was eager to drive his father’s car. C. He asked his son to drop him at a place that was some 18 miles from home before he took the car for servicing. D. His father agreed.
questions.explanation: B introduces the teenager eager to drive his father's car, D says the father agreed, C has the son drop him 18 miles from home before taking the car for servicing, and A, with 'then', adds the pick-up at four in the afternoon: BDCA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. Ashutosh “kept a stiff upper lip” even when he was reprimanded in the presence of clients.
questions.explanation: To keep a 'stiff upper lip' is to hide one's feelings and stay calm in difficulty: Ashutosh showed no reaction to the scolding.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Acquaintance' is spelt correctly; the others should be 'requirement', 'exquisite' and 'squirrel'.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the given sentence which contains the grammatical error. The wedding reception will be hosted in Mumbai at a late date.
questions.explanation: 'At a later date', meaning at some time in the future, is the fixed phrase: 'The wedding reception will be hosted in Mumbai at a later date.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. “The book’s page seem” to have been torn by someone.
options: The page of the book was seems
The page of the book has seem
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'page' takes the singular verb 'seems': 'The book's page seems to have been torn by someone.'

questions.text: Select the option that is the direct form of the given sentence. Explaining her work she said that she made films for posterity to remember.
options: Explaining her work, she said, “She makes films for posterity to remember.”
Explaining her work, she said, “I will make the films that will remember posterity.”
Explaining her work, she said, “She made films for posterity to remember.”
Explaining her work, she said, “I make films for posterity to remember.”
questions.explanation: In direct speech the reported 'she' becomes 'I' and the past 'made' returns to the present 'make': 'I make films for posterity to remember.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. APEX
questions.explanation: The apex is the top or highest point; its opposite is the 'base'. 'Pinnacle' means the same as 'apex'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. ACCRUE
questions.explanation: To 'accrue' is to collect or build up over time, as interest does on a deposit.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. In reality, however, we exist in compartments, separated by walls of caste, religion, and geography. B. But we find that ignorance levels are growing as well because the rate at which we are accumulating information is not commensurate with the rate at which our awareness is growing. C. Technologically we live in a borderless world. D. Another paradox is that we take pride in describing ourselves as a knowledge-based society.
questions.explanation: C says technology has made the world borderless; A ('however') says that in reality we live in compartments; D adds 'another paradox', that we call ourselves a knowledge-based society; and B ('but') says ignorance is growing too: CADB.

questions.text: 'Wings India’, Asia’s largest civil aviation event, will be held at Begumpet airport, Hyderabad in March 2020. What will be the theme of this event?
questions.explanation: The theme of Wings India 2020, the civil aviation show organised by the Ministry of Civil Aviation, the Airports Authority of India and FICCI at Begumpet Airport, Hyderabad, for 12 to 15 March 2020, was 'Flying for All'.

questions.text: Which scientist won the Nobel prize in Physics in 1918 for the discovery of ‘Energy Quanta’?
questions.explanation: The 1918 Nobel Prize in Physics went to Max Planck for his discovery of energy quanta, the start of quantum theory. De Broglie won in 1929, Heisenberg in 1932 and Chadwick, for the neutron, in 1935.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers is the fifth largest river and the largest west flowing river?
questions.explanation: The Narmada, which rises at Amarkantak, is the largest of the west-flowing rivers of peninsular India and runs through a rift valley to the Arabian Sea. The Godavari and the Subarnarekha flow east to the Bay of Bengal.

questions.text: 'A Shot At History: My Obsessive Journey to Olympic Gold' is the autobiography of which Indian shooter?
questions.explanation: 'A Shot at History', written with Rohit Brijnath, is the autobiography of Abhinav Bindra, who won India's first individual Olympic gold, in the 10 m air rifle at Beijing 2008.

questions.text: The famous cultural site Rani-ki-Vav (the Queen's Stepwell) is situated on the banks of which river?
questions.explanation: Rani-ki-Vav, an 11th-century stepwell at Patan in Gujarat, stands on the banks of the Saraswati; it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014.

questions.text: Who is India's youngest IAS officer to be appointed to the Chief Minister's Office of Telangana? She/he is also known as 'The People's Officer'.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Smita Sabharwal, a 2001-batch IAS officer who in 2014 became the first woman officer appointed to the Telangana Chief Minister's Office, and who is known as 'the people's officer' for drawing citizens into solving local problems.

questions.text: The definition of ‘money bills’ is given in which article of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: Article 110 defines a money bill. Article 33 lets Parliament restrict fundamental rights for the armed forces, Article 44 deals with a uniform civil code and Article 93 with the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

questions.text: Which wildlife sanctuary is a tri-state protected area in northern India? It is also famous for the Critically Endangered gharial, the red-crowned roofed turtle and the Endangered Ganges river dolphin?
questions.explanation: The National Chambal Sanctuary runs along the Chambal through Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh and protects the gharial, the red-crowned roofed turtle and the Ganges river dolphin. The other three sanctuaries are in Kerala and Karnataka.

questions.text: In November 2019, which Indian athlete was listed in ‘Time 100 Next’ that spotlights 100 rising stars who are shaping the future of business, entertainment, sports, politics, etc.?
questions.explanation: The sprinter Dutee Chand was among the advocates on TIME's first '100 Next' list, published in November 2019.

questions.text: Who created history by securing Gold in the women's Singles SL3 event at the ‘BWF Para-Badminton World Championships’ in 2019?
questions.explanation: Manasi Joshi won the women's singles SL3 gold at the 2019 BWF Para-Badminton World Championships in Basel, Switzerland, beating Parul Parmar in the final.

questions.text: Which of the following dance forms is also known as the 'Royal Dance of Ladakh'?
questions.explanation: Shondol, once performed for the kings of Ladakh on special occasions, is known as its royal dance. Jabro is a dance of the nomads of Changthang.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following movements was started in the year 1930 by Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.explanation: Gandhi began the Civil Disobedience Movement in 1930 with the Dandi March, breaking the salt law. The Khilafat Movement began in 1919, the Non-Cooperation Movement in 1920 and the Quit India Movement in 1942.

questions.text: Where did the Chief Minister of Odisha, Naveen Patnaik, inaugurate the National Tribal Craft Mela-2019?
questions.explanation: The eighth National Tribal Craft Mela was held at the State Tribal Museum complex in Bhubaneswar, Odisha's capital, from 23 to 29 November 2019; Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik opened it.

questions.text: As of January 2020, what was the upper limit of fund transfer using Unified Payments Interface (UPI)?
questions.explanation: In January 2020 NPCI's general limit for a UPI transfer was ₹1 lakh per transaction.

questions.text: Which of the following is the chemical formula for Nitre (saltpeter)?
questions.explanation: Nitre, or saltpetre, is potassium nitrate, KNO₃, used in gunpowder and fertilisers. KCl is potassium chloride.

questions.text: Which of the following mountains is situated near the Siachen region of Ladakh in India?
questions.explanation: K12, a peak of the Saltoro range, rises near the Siachen Glacier. Kangchenjunga, Kabru and Kirat Chuli stand on the Sikkim-Nepal border.

questions.text: In the context of computers, WORM is an acronym of:
questions.explanation: WORM, Write Once, Read Many, is storage that can be written only once and then read any number of times, such as a CD-R.

questions.text: Which country honoured Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi with its highest civilian honour 'Zayed Medal’ in 2019?
questions.explanation: The UAE announced its highest civilian honour, the Zayed Medal, for Narendra Modi in April 2019 and presented it to him in Abu Dhabi in August 2019.

questions.text: As per a World Gold Council (WGC) report that was released in January 2020, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was ranked ______ in terms of buying gold abroad among central banks of the world.
questions.explanation: The World Gold Council's report of January 2020 ranked the RBI sixth among the world's central banks buying gold, with 25.2 tonnes in the first ten months of 2019; only the central banks of Russia, Turkey, Poland, China and Kazakhstan bought more.

questions.text: Which of the following passes is located between Nilgiri Hills to the north and Anaimalai Hills to the south?
questions.explanation: The Palghat (Palakkad) Gap, between the Nilgiris to the north and the Anaimalai Hills to the south, links Kerala and Tamil Nadu. The other three passes are in the Himalaya and the Karakoram.

questions.text: Which of the following books was translated as ‘The Razmnama’ (Book of Wars) during the reign of Akbar?
questions.explanation: The Razmnama is the Persian translation of the Mahabharata made at Akbar's court. The Baburnama is Babur's memoir and the Akbarnama Abul Fazl's history of Akbar's reign.

questions.text: According to the Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP) annual report that was released in January 2020, what was India’s rank in corporate commitments to science-based targets?
questions.explanation: The Carbon Disclosure Project's India report of January 2020 ranked India fifth among the countries surveyed for companies committed to science-based targets, emission cuts in line with what climate science says is needed.

questions.text: The 5th edition of ‘Indian International Science Festival (IISF) 2019’ was held in which city?
questions.explanation: The fifth India International Science Festival was held in Kolkata in November 2019.

questions.text: Which former cricketer and captain of the Indian team was formally elected as the President of BCCI in October 2019?
questions.explanation: Sourav Ganguly, a former India captain, was elected unopposed as president of the BCCI and took charge on 23 October 2019.

questions.text: In the context of the contribution of scientists for which they were awarded Nobel Prize, which of the following pairs is INCORRECT?
options: Diffraction of X-rays – Max Von Laue
questions.explanation: Galileo (1564-1642) lived centuries before the first Nobel Prizes of 1901, and quantum mechanics came only in the 20th century. Raman (1930), von Laue (1914) and Lorentz (1902, shared with Zeeman) won for the other three.

questions.text: Given below are four sentences in a jumbled order. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. Add the product to your shopping cart. B. Select the brand you like. C. Enter the card details and buy the product online. D. Look for the product you want to purchase.
questions.explanation: The steps of buying online in order: D looks for the product, B picks the brand, A adds it to the cart and C pays by card to buy it: DBAC.

questions.text: Select the correct antonym for the given word. Formidable
questions.explanation: 'Formidable' means inspiring fear or respect by being large, powerful or difficult; its opposite is 'trivial', of little importance. 'Dangerous' and 'scary' are close to it in sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Delinquent
questions.explanation: A delinquent is someone, especially a young person, who commits minor crimes, so the adjective means 'offending'.

questions.text: Identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. The old woman in our locality is knowing for her hot temper.
questions.explanation: To be famous for something is to be 'known for' it; 'know' is not used in the continuous form here: 'The old woman in our locality is known for her hot temper.'

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The two men bowed to one (1)______ and parted. Tom found himself in a difficult (2)______. He was going to (3)______ three duels in a (4)______ of three hours. "Even if I am killed, it will be a (5)______ death," he thought.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no.1
questions.explanation: 'One another' means each other: the two men bowed to one another.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The two men bowed to one (1)______ and parted. Tom found himself in a difficult (2)______. He was going to (3)______ three duels in a (4)______ of three hours. "Even if I am killed, it will be a (5)______ death," he thought.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no.2
questions.explanation: Facing three duels, Tom is in a 'difficult situation', a hard position to be in.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The two men bowed to one (1)______ and parted. Tom found himself in a difficult (2)______. He was going to (3)______ three duels in a (4)______ of three hours. "Even if I am killed, it will be a (5)______ death," he thought.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no.3
questions.explanation: A duel is 'fought': he was going to fight three duels.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The two men bowed to one (1)______ and parted. Tom found himself in a difficult (2)______. He was going to (3)______ three duels in a (4)______ of three hours. "Even if I am killed, it will be a (5)______ death," he thought.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no.4
questions.explanation: 'In a matter of' three hours means within no more than three hours.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The two men bowed to one (1)______ and parted. Tom found himself in a difficult (2)______. He was going to (3)______ three duels in a (4)______ of three hours. "Even if I am killed, it will be a (5)______ death," he thought.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no.5
questions.explanation: A 'glorious' death is one that brings honour, which is how Tom consoles himself. 'Spurious' means false and 'laborious' needing much effort.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Prodigious
questions.explanation: 'Prodigious' means remarkably great in size or degree: 'immense'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The yoga instructor was ______ at the student's flexibility.
questions.explanation: To be 'amazed' at something is to be greatly surprised by it, which suits the student's flexibility; one is not 'ridiculed at' it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The government enterprises were privatized as they were ______ heavy losses on a daily basis.
questions.explanation: Losses are 'incurred', that is suffered; profits, not losses, are earned.

questions.text: Select the wrongly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Voracous' is misspelt: the word is 'voracious', meaning very hungry or very eager.

questions.text: Select the correct antonym for the given word. Identical
questions.explanation: 'Identical' means exactly alike; its opposite is 'different'. The other three are close to it in sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. “Tons of sheep” were grazing in the field.
questions.explanation: The collective noun for sheep is 'a flock', and 'tons of' is informal. 'Sheep' has the same form in the plural, so 'sheeps' is wrong.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. When Harry come back home, he saw blood everywhere.
questions.explanation: The main clause is in the past ('he saw'), so the 'when' clause needs the past tense too: 'When Harry came back home'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Something like an opening, particularly one in the body such as a nostril
questions.explanation: An orifice is an opening, especially one in the body such as a nostril or the mouth. 'Obtuse' means slow to understand, 'obscure' little known and 'oblique' slanting.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Flying off the handle
options: Flying away, being launched from a handle
questions.explanation: To 'fly off the handle' is to lose one's temper suddenly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. The Dean said, "You can have “neither jam nor butter,” but not both."
questions.explanation: 'Neither ... nor' rules out both, which makes 'but not both' meaningless; 'either ... or' offers one of the two: 'You can have either jam or butter, but not both.'

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Something that is extremely unpleasant
questions.explanation: 'Horrendous' means extremely unpleasant or horrifying. 'Humane' means kind and 'heightened' increased.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Peter said, "He broke his glasses."
options: Peter said that he had broken his glasses.
Peter said that he is going to break his glasses.
Peter said that he is breaking his glasses.
Peter said that he break his glasses.
questions.explanation: After the past reporting verb 'said', the simple past 'broke' moves back to the past perfect: 'had broken'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To cost an arm and a leg
options: To give away an arm and a leg
questions.explanation: Something that 'costs an arm and a leg' is very expensive.

questions.text: Given below are four sentences in a jumbled order. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. The police suspected the man to be a thief. B. Then the trial began in the court. C. He was soon arrested by the police. D. The thief was sentenced to two years’ imprisonment.
questions.explanation: A begins the story (the man is suspected of theft), C follows with his arrest, B with the trial and D with the sentence: ACBD.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. The police arrested the thieves yesterday.
options: The thieves were arrested yesterday by the police.
The thieves have been arrested yesterday by the police.
The thieves were being arrested yesterday by the police.
The thieves had been arrested yesterday by the police.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'arrested' becomes 'were arrested' in the passive, plural to agree with 'the thieves': 'The thieves were arrested yesterday by the police.'

questions.text: Name the first Chief Scientist of the public health division at the World Health Organisation.
questions.explanation: Dr Soumya Swaminathan, an Indian paediatrician and former Director-General of the Indian Council of Medical Research, became the WHO's first Chief Scientist when the post was created in March 2019.

questions.text: What was the theme of International Nurses Day in 2020?
questions.explanation: The International Council of Nurses' theme for 2020, the bicentenary of Florence Nightingale's birth, was 'Nurses: A Voice to Lead - Nursing the World to Health'. The earlier 'A Voice to Lead' themes ended in 'Health for All' (2019), 'Health is a Human Right' (2018) and 'Achieving the Sustainable Development Goals' (2017).

questions.text: Locomotion in ______ takes place with the help of a muscular foot.
questions.explanation: Snails, like other molluscs, creep on a muscular foot. Earthworms move by their body muscles and bristles (setae), jellyfish by contracting their bell and sea urchins by tube feet.

questions.text: The Maharaja of ______ was the first Indian cricketer to serve as President of the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI).
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Vizianagaram: 'Vizzy', the Maharajkumar (a younger prince, not the ruling Maharaja) of Vizianagaram, who captained India in three Tests in England in 1936, was BCCI president from 1954 to 1956, the first president to have played Test cricket.

questions.text: ‘FIR Aapke Dwar', an initiative whereby police officials would visit homes of victims to register a First Information Report (FIR), was launched in the state of ______ in May 2020.
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh Police launched 'FIR Aapke Dwar' on 11 May 2020 as a pilot in 23 police station areas: a complainant dials 100 and police come to the home to register the FIR, so there is no need to go to the police station.

questions.text: Which of the following states was declared as the cleanest state in Swachh Survekshan 2019?
questions.explanation: Chhattisgarh was adjudged the cleanest (best-performing) state in Swachh Survekshan 2019, the urban cleanliness survey of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, ahead of Jharkhand and Maharashtra.

questions.text: Which of the following sites does NOT feature in the United Nations’ World Heritage List as of June 2020?
questions.explanation: The Ajanta and Ellora caves (both inscribed in 1983) and the Elephanta caves (1987) are World Heritage Sites; the Buddhist rock-cut caves at Karla in Maharashtra are not.

questions.text: Who has developed the Automatically Programmable Tool (APT)?
questions.explanation: APT (Automatically Programmed Tool), a language for programming numerically controlled machine tools, was developed at MIT in the late 1950s under Douglas T. Ross. Gary Kildall wrote the CP/M operating system and Ralph Baer built the first home video game console.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a terrestrial natural disaster?
questions.explanation: A landslide, the movement of rock and earth down a slope, is a disaster of the land surface. Blizzards, tornadoes and thunderstorms are atmospheric (weather) disasters.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Indian Government annexed ______ in 1948 under the code name 'Operation Polo'.
questions.explanation: Operation Polo, the Indian Army's 'police action' of September 1948, ended the Nizam's rule and brought Hyderabad into the Indian Union.

questions.text: Who was India's first Chief of Defence Staff?
questions.explanation: General Bipin Rawat took office as India's first Chief of Defence Staff on 1 January 2020.

questions.text: Depression is a ______ disorder.
questions.explanation: Depression is a mood (affective) disorder: its main features are a lasting low mood and loss of interest in things.

questions.text: The sino-artrialnode is located in the ______.
questions.explanation: The sino-atrial node, a small mass of tissue in the wall of the right atrium, is the heart's natural pacemaker: it starts each heartbeat.

questions.text: Inscriptions composed in praise of kings of ancient India are known as ______.
questions.explanation: Prashastis were inscriptions composed in praise of kings, such as Harisena's prashasti of Samudragupta on the Allahabad pillar. The Tripitakas are the Buddhist canon and the Jatakas stories of the Buddha's earlier births.

questions.text: Which of the following states has one of the richest monazite deposits in India?
questions.explanation: Kerala's coastal sands, as at Chavara, are among India's richest sources of monazite, the mineral from which thorium is obtained.

questions.text: 1 Petabyte (PB) = 1024 ______.
questions.explanation: Each unit is 1024 times the one below it: 1 PB = 1024 TB, just as 1 TB = 1024 GB.

questions.text: The Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve is located in the state of ______.
questions.explanation: Bandhavgarh Tiger Reserve is in Umaria district of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text: As of April 2020, ______ holds the record for delivering the most number of balls by any woman cricketer in Women's test history.
questions.explanation: Diana Edulji, the left-arm spinner who captained India, bowled 5,098 balls in women's Tests, the most by any woman as of April 2020.

questions.text: In May 2020, the Government of India raised the net borrowing limit for state governments to ______% of the gross state domestic product (GSDP).
questions.explanation: In May 2020, as part of its Covid-19 relief package, the Centre raised the states' borrowing limit for 2020-21 from 3% to 5% of GSDP, part of the extra borrowing being tied to reforms.

questions.text: ______ is a traditional Indian sport, whereby athletes perform various types of gymnastics moves and hold various poses on a vertical wooden pole.
questions.explanation: In Mallakhamb, athletes perform gymnastic and yoga postures on an upright wooden pole (or a hanging rope). Kalaripayattu is a martial art of Kerala and Yubi Lakpi a Manipuri game played with a coconut.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: ______ was a mentor to both, Mahatma Gandhi and Mohammed Ali Jinnah.
questions.explanation: Gandhi called Gopal Krishna Gokhale his political guru, and the young Jinnah, then a moderate in the Congress, looked up to him and wanted to become 'the Muslim Gokhale'.

questions.text: Yadgir, Bidar and Gadag are districts are in the state of ______.
questions.explanation: Yadgir, Bidar and Gadag are districts of northern Karnataka.

questions.text: The first Backward Classes Commission of India was headed by ______.
questions.explanation: The first Backward Classes Commission, appointed under Article 340 in January 1953, was headed by Kaka Kalelkar and reported in 1955. The second was the Mandal Commission (1979).

questions.text: With which bank has Ashok Leyland, the commercial vehicle brand, tied up in November 2019 for vehicle loans for a period of 2 years?
questions.explanation: On 25 November 2019 Ashok Leyland signed a two-year agreement making ICICI Bank a preferred financier for customers buying its trucks and buses, with a focus on semi-urban and rural areas.

questions.text: The ______ festival is celebrated by the Ahom people of Assam on 31st January every year in memory of the departed.
questions.explanation: Me-Dam-Me-Phi is the Ahom festival of ancestor worship, held on 31 January each year to remember the dead.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. Over the past 20 years, there “has been” a constant decline in the variety of vegetables that we eat because the native varieties are no longer available.
questions.explanation: 'Over the past 20 years' covers a period lasting up to now, which takes the present perfect: 'there has been a constant decline' is correct as it stands.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Call a spade a spade
options: Plan to attack someone with rude words
Say the truth about something, even if it is not pleasant
Lash out unkindly at someone for no reason
Say things that are untrue and painful
questions.explanation: To 'call a spade a spade' is to speak plainly and truthfully about something, even when the truth is unpleasant.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. BENEVOLENT
questions.explanation: 'Benevolent' means kind and generous; of the options only 'stingy', unwilling to give or spend, is its opposite. 'Generous', 'liberal' and 'friendly' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. You’ve probably noticed, with great disappointment, that the battery doesn’t seem to last as long as it did when it was brand new. B. Partial charging is just fine for lithium-ion batteries and can actually have some positive benefits for cell longevity. C. Smartphone users are forever in search of longer battery life, but unfortunately, battery capacity inevitably declines with age. D. However, one thing you can do to prolong the life of your battery and handset is partial charging.
questions.explanation: C states the problem (battery capacity declines with age), A turns to the reader who has noticed it, D offers a remedy with 'However' (partial charging), and B explains why partial charging is fine: CADB.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. At the age of 94, Harbhajan makes barfi only on order and people come to collect the freshly made barfi at her (1)______. The most remarkable thing is, she manages everything (2)______ her own, from roasting the gram flour to cutting the (3)______ shaped barfis. She believes that it is better to wear out than to rust out. Due to her hard work, she received the best (4)______ when she was named ‘entrepreneur of the year’. This 94 year old woman (5)______ that it’s never too late to do a start-up.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 1.
questions.explanation: After the possessive 'her' a noun is needed for the place where she lives: 'at her residence'. A 'resident' is a person, and 'residential' is an adjective.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. At the age of 94, Harbhajan makes barfi only on order and people come to collect the freshly made barfi at her (1)______. The most remarkable thing is, she manages everything (2)______ her own, from roasting the gram flour to cutting the (3)______ shaped barfis. She believes that it is better to wear out than to rust out. Due to her hard work, she received the best (4)______ when she was named ‘entrepreneur of the year’. This 94 year old woman (5)______ that it’s never too late to do a start-up.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 2.
questions.explanation: To do something 'on one's own' is to do it alone, without help: 'she manages everything on her own'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. At the age of 94, Harbhajan makes barfi only on order and people come to collect the freshly made barfi at her (1)______. The most remarkable thing is, she manages everything (2)______ her own, from roasting the gram flour to cutting the (3)______ shaped barfis. She believes that it is better to wear out than to rust out. Due to her hard work, she received the best (4)______ when she was named ‘entrepreneur of the year’. This 94 year old woman (5)______ that it’s never too late to do a start-up.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 3.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed before the participle 'shaped', and 'perfectly shaped barfis' praises her skill; 'hardly shaped' would mean barely shaped.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. At the age of 94, Harbhajan makes barfi only on order and people come to collect the freshly made barfi at her (1)______. The most remarkable thing is, she manages everything (2)______ her own, from roasting the gram flour to cutting the (3)______ shaped barfis. She believes that it is better to wear out than to rust out. Due to her hard work, she received the best (4)______ when she was named ‘entrepreneur of the year’. This 94 year old woman (5)______ that it’s never too late to do a start-up.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Being named 'entrepreneur of the year' is recognition of her work: she received 'the best appreciation'. 'Gratefulness' is the feeling of the one who receives a kindness, and 'charm' and 'content' do not fit.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. At the age of 94, Harbhajan makes barfi only on order and people come to collect the freshly made barfi at her (1)______. The most remarkable thing is, she manages everything (2)______ her own, from roasting the gram flour to cutting the (3)______ shaped barfis. She believes that it is better to wear out than to rust out. Due to her hard work, she received the best (4)______ when she was named ‘entrepreneur of the year’. This 94 year old woman (5)______ that it’s never too late to do a start-up.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The woman herself shows something by her example, so the active present perfect is needed: 'has proved that it's never too late'. 'Was proved' and 'is proved' are passive.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Ravina asked her little brother, “Where are you going to play?”
options: Ravina asked her little brother where he was going to play.
Ravina said to her little brother where he was going to play.
Ravina asked her little brother where he would like to go to play.
Ravina asked her little brother where will he be going to play.
questions.explanation: A reported question keeps 'asked', takes statement order with no question mark, changes 'you' to 'he' and moves 'are going' back to 'was going': 'where he was going to play'.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. The country has to struggled with the problems of child labour.
questions.explanation: 'Has to' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'The country has to struggle with the problems of child labour.'

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'disposable': the final 'e' of 'dispose' is dropped before '-able', as in 'advisable'.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. The Indian cricket team was done very well this year and is ranked number one now.
options: and is ranked number one now
questions.explanation: The team itself performed, so the verb must be active, not the passive 'was done': 'The Indian cricket team has done (or did) very well this year'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. One who examines accounts officially
questions.explanation: An auditor officially examines the accounts of a business or organisation. An aviator flies aircraft, and a radiator gives out heat.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. Swami Vivekanand’s vast knowledge of Eastern and Western culture appealed to all those “who come in contacts” with him.
questions.explanation: The main verb 'appealed' is in the past, so the clause needs 'came', and the phrase is 'come in contact with', with a singular 'contact': 'all those who came in contact with him'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. REMORSE
questions.explanation: 'Remorse' is deep regret or guilt for a wrong one has done: 'regret'. 'Reproach' is blame or disapproval of someone else.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. In ______ of the great work he is doing for economically weaker children, he has been given a special award.
questions.explanation: 'In recognition of' means as an acknowledgement of someone's work or merit, the usual phrase with an award.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. They are laying new telephone cables in our colony.
options: New telephone cables are being laid in our colony.
New telephone cables were laid in our colony.
New telephone cables were being laid in our colony.
New telephone cables will be laid in our colony.
questions.explanation: The present continuous 'are laying' becomes 'are being laid' in the passive: 'New telephone cables are being laid in our colony.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. We found it ______ to climb further due to bad weather and decided to give up the expedition.
questions.explanation: The bad weather made climbing further 'impossible', which is why they gave up the expedition; 'boring', 'exciting' and 'pleasant' do not explain giving up.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order. A. So, what exactly are we eating? B. They found that the vegetables contained very high, toxic levels of banned pesticides, and the pesticide levels were more than 1000 times the permissible levels. C. And is our food giving rise to the many health problems today? D. A survey conducted by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India under the Union Agriculture Ministry tested random samples of vegetables in markets all over India.
questions.explanation: D describes the survey, B gives its finding ('They found ...'), and A and C ask the questions that follow from it: DBAC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Be behind the times
questions.explanation: To 'be behind the times' is to be old-fashioned, not keeping up with modern ideas or ways.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Repetition of an initial sound in two or more words of a line
questions.explanation: Alliteration is the repetition of the same initial sound in nearby words, as in 'big brown bear'. Assonance repeats vowel sounds, and rhyme matches the endings of words.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. CONSPICUOUS
questions.explanation: 'Conspicuous' means clearly visible or attracting notice; its opposite is 'obscure', hidden or little known. 'Apparent', 'distinct' and 'noticeable' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. TIMID
questions.explanation: 'Timid' means lacking courage or confidence: 'shy'. 'Strong' is nearer its opposite.

questions.text: The script ‘Gurumukhi’ for Punjabi language was invented by the Sikh guru ______.
questions.explanation: Guru Angad Dev, the second Sikh Guru, is credited with developing and standardising the Gurmukhi script in the 16th century; the Sikh scriptures are written in it.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a North East Indian sister state?
questions.explanation: The 'Seven Sisters' of the north-east are Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura. Odisha is on the eastern coast.

questions.text: Who among the following is NOT a lawn tennis champion?
questions.explanation: Manika Batra is a table tennis player, who won the women's singles gold at the 2018 Commonwealth Games. Leander Paes, Rohan Bopanna and Sania Mirza have all won Grand Slam titles in tennis doubles or mixed doubles.

questions.text: Who has been appointed as the 47th Chief Justice of India?
questions.explanation: Sharad Arvind Bobde was sworn in as the 47th Chief Justice of India on 18 November 2019, succeeding Ranjan Gogoi, and held the office when the exam was held, in October 2020.

questions.text: ‘Santosh Trophy’ is an award for the winning team of ______.
questions.explanation: The Santosh Trophy is India's national football championship for state and institutional teams, first held in 1941.

questions.text: Abhijit Banerji, an India born researcher, was one of the winners of Nobel Prize 2019 for ______.
questions.explanation: Abhijit Banerjee shared the 2019 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences with Esther Duflo and Michael Kremer for their experimental approach to alleviating global poverty.

questions.text: The Buddhist sites Vaishali and Nalanda are situated in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Vaishali, where the Second Buddhist Council was held, and Nalanda, seat of the ancient Buddhist university, are both in Bihar.

questions.text: Which of the following cricketers is NOT a part of the Sri Lankan team?
questions.explanation: Kedar Jadhav is an Indian batsman who has played for India. Lasith Malinga, Angelo Perera and Thisara Perera (printed 'Tusara Perara') have played for Sri Lanka.

questions.text: On which day of the year is the earth farthest from the sun, at a position called aphelion?
questions.explanation: The Earth reaches aphelion, its farthest point from the Sun, in early July, around 4 July; it is nearest the Sun (perihelion) around 3 January.

questions.text: Which is the correct sequence of rulers of the Mughal Empire?
options: Babur, Humayun, Aurangzeb, Jahangir, Shahjahan, Bahadur Shah, Akbar
Babur, Aurangzeb, Humayun, Jahangir, Shahjahan, Bahadur Shah, Akbar
Babur, Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, Shahjahan, Aurangzeb, Bahadur Shah
Babur, Jahangir, Humayun, Akbar, Bahadur Shah, Shahjahan, Aurangzeb
questions.explanation: The Mughal emperors ruled in the order Babur, Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb, who was followed in 1707 by Bahadur Shah I.

questions.text: ______ is defined as the study of behavior of individual decision-making units, such as consumers, resource owners and firms.
questions.explanation: Microeconomics studies the choices of individual units such as consumers, resource owners and firms; macroeconomics studies the economy as a whole, through aggregates such as national income and inflation.

questions.text: Which of the following devices is NOT used to enter data into a computer?
questions.explanation: A monitor is an output device: it displays what the computer produces. The mouse, keyboard and scanner are input devices.

questions.text: What kind of depositional landforms are formed when streams flowing from higher levels break into foot slope plains of low gradient?
questions.explanation: Where a stream from higher ground reaches a gentle foot slope it slows and spreads out, dropping its coarse load in a fan-shaped deposit, an alluvial fan. Flood plains, natural levees and point bars form along a river's course on the plains.

questions.text: The ‘Bharat Ratna Award 2019’ was NOT conferred upon:
questions.explanation: The Bharat Ratna for 2019 went to Pranab Mukherjee and, posthumously, to Nanaji Deshmukh and Bhupen Hazarika. Medha Patkar, the social activist of the Narmada Bachao Andolan, was not among them.

questions.text: Which of the following Public Sector Undertakings does NOT have 'Maharatna' status?
questions.explanation: When the exam was held, in October 2020, Engineers India Limited was a Navratna company, while SAIL, GAIL and Coal India were among the Maharatna central public sector enterprises.

questions.text: 'Behdienkhlam' is a traditional dance festival of which state?
questions.explanation: Behdienkhlam is the festival of the Pnar (Jaintia) people of Meghalaya, held at Jowai in July, after the sowing, to drive away disease and evil.

questions.text: Which Mauryan ruler became a follower of Buddhism?
questions.explanation: Ashoka turned to Buddhism after the Kalinga war (about 261 BCE) and spread its teaching of dhamma. Samudragupta was a Gupta king, and Chandragupta Maurya is said to have become a Jain.

questions.text: The President of India can hold office for a term of ______ year/s.
questions.explanation: Under Article 56 the President holds office for a term of five years from the date of entering upon it.

questions.text: When blue litmus was added to an unknown liquid in a test tube, it turned red. What was the liquid?
questions.explanation: Acids turn blue litmus red; alkalis turn red litmus blue, and neutral liquids such as water and saline leave both unchanged.

questions.text: Cirrus and cumulus are types of ______.
questions.explanation: Cirrus clouds are thin, wispy high clouds; cumulus clouds are puffy, cotton-like heaps with flat bases.

questions.text: Kartarpur Sahib corridor connects Dera Baba Nanak Shrine in Gurdaspur, India to Kartarpur Gurudwara in Pakistan, which is located near the banks of the river ______.
questions.explanation: Gurdwara Darbar Sahib Kartarpur, in Pakistan's Narowal district, stands across the Ravi from Dera Baba Nanak; the corridor between them opened in November 2019.

questions.text: India is called a secular country because citizens have the fundamental right to:
options: freedom to profess religion of one's choice
questions.explanation: Articles 25 to 28 give every person freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion, and the State has no religion of its own; this is what makes India secular.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Look before you leap
options: Caution others before taking a step
Pull someone out from a disaster
questions.explanation: 'Look before you leap' means think carefully about what may follow before you act.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. SACRED
questions.explanation: 'Sacred' means holy; 'profane' means not holy, or showing disrespect for holy things. 'Divine', 'solemn' and 'pious' are close to 'sacred'.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Mother said to Kavya, "Switch off the light before you go to sleep."
options: Mother told Kavya to switch off the light before you go to sleep.
Mother told Kavya to switch off the light before she is going to sleep.
Mother told Kavya to switch off the light before she goes to sleep.
Mother told Kavya to switch off the light before she went to sleep.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'before she went to sleep': with a past reporting verb the command becomes 'told Kavya to switch off', 'you' becomes 'she' and the present 'go' shifts back to 'went'. 'Before she goes to sleep' is also heard when the bedtime is still to come, but the textbook rule is the backshift.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A period of one thousand years
questions.explanation: A millennium is a thousand years. A century is a hundred years, a decade ten, and a centenary the hundredth anniversary of something.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Roman civilization emerged around the sixth century BC. At the height of (1)______ power, the Roman Empire ruled over a huge chunk of (2)______, and all the present-day Mediterranean countries (3)______ part of ancient Rome. Early Rome was (4)______ by kings, but later, the people took control over their own city and ruled (5)______. They introduced a council known as the Senate which ruled over them. From this point, Rome was referred to as the Roman Republic.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The pronoun refers to 'the Roman Empire', a singular thing: 'at the height of its power'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Roman civilization emerged around the sixth century BC. At the height of (1)______ power, the Roman Empire ruled over a huge chunk of (2)______, and all the present-day Mediterranean countries (3)______ part of ancient Rome. Early Rome was (4)______ by kings, but later, the people took control over their own city and ruled (5)______. They introduced a council known as the Senate which ruled over them. From this point, Rome was referred to as the Roman Republic.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 2.
questions.explanation: An empire rules over territory: 'a huge chunk of land'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Roman civilization emerged around the sixth century BC. At the height of (1)______ power, the Roman Empire ruled over a huge chunk of (2)______, and all the present-day Mediterranean countries (3)______ part of ancient Rome. Early Rome was (4)______ by kings, but later, the people took control over their own city and ruled (5)______. They introduced a council known as the Senate which ruled over them. From this point, Rome was referred to as the Roman Republic.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The passage is about ancient Rome, so the verb is past, and plural to agree with 'countries': 'were part of ancient Rome'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Roman civilization emerged around the sixth century BC. At the height of (1)______ power, the Roman Empire ruled over a huge chunk of (2)______, and all the present-day Mediterranean countries (3)______ part of ancient Rome. Early Rome was (4)______ by kings, but later, the people took control over their own city and ruled (5)______. They introduced a council known as the Senate which ruled over them. From this point, Rome was referred to as the Roman Republic.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 4.
questions.explanation: A state is 'governed' by its rulers: 'Early Rome was governed by kings', which the next clause contrasts with the people ruling their own city.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Roman civilization emerged around the sixth century BC. At the height of (1)______ power, the Roman Empire ruled over a huge chunk of (2)______, and all the present-day Mediterranean countries (3)______ part of ancient Rome. Early Rome was (4)______ by kings, but later, the people took control over their own city and ruled (5)______. They introduced a council known as the Senate which ruled over them. From this point, Rome was referred to as the Roman Republic.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The reflexive pronoun must match 'the people', which is plural: they 'ruled themselves'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. PERISH
questions.explanation: To 'perish' is to die or come to an end; to 'grow' is to live and develop. 'Vanish', 'wither' and 'crumble' are close to 'perish'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. When he returned, there was more than just his dog waiting for him. B. A koala had joined the dog in the car’s more comfortable climate. C. A winemaker in South Australia left his air-conditioned car open to help keep his dog cool in the heat. D. Although the human struggled a while to make the koala leave, it did leave his car eventually.
questions.explanation: C says the winemaker left his car open for his dog; A says he came back to find more than his dog; B says a koala had got in; D says it left only after a struggle: CABD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The important ______ is where to arrange the funds from.
questions.explanation: An 'issue' is a matter to be decided, which is what the question of where to find the funds is.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. All these boys have come to college without few knowledge of English.
questions.explanation: 'Few' goes with countable nouns; 'knowledge' is uncountable, so it should be 'without much knowledge' (or 'with little knowledge').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. MOROSE
questions.explanation: 'Morose' means gloomy and bad-tempered: 'sullen'. 'Optimistic', 'friendly' and 'cheerful' are nearly opposite.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Rebelleous' is misspelt: the word is 'rebellious'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. People in a small Chinese town were shocked to see a wild elephant wandering in their town. B. The elephant eventually left the town. C. Authorities followed the large mammal’s every movement. D. But the locals will probably never forget this special visit.
questions.explanation: A introduces the elephant in the town; C says the authorities followed its every move; B says it finally left; D, opening with 'But', closes on the locals' memory of the visit: ACBD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Several villages in Kashmir have been ______ due to heavy snowfall.
questions.explanation: Villages cut off from everywhere else by heavy snow are 'isolated'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. The house has a garden in front, “is it?”
questions.explanation: A positive statement takes a negative tag built on its own verb, and 'is' does not match 'has': 'The house has a garden in front, hasn't it?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. Many attempts “has been made” to climb the Everest before Tenzing and Hillary succeeded.
questions.explanation: The attempts came before another past event, Tenzing and Hillary's success, so the past perfect is needed, which also suits the plural 'attempts': 'had been made'.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Everyone are asking for passes to the music festival at Nehru Park.
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' takes a singular verb: 'Everyone is asking for passes ...'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. AFFLUENT
questions.explanation: 'Affluent' means rich: 'wealthy'. 'Destitute' and 'impoverished' are its opposites, and 'proficient' means skilled.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A plantation of grapes
questions.explanation: A vineyard is a plantation of grapevines. An orchard grows fruit trees, a grove is a small group of trees, and a nursery raises young plants.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Chill out
questions.explanation: To 'chill out' is to calm down and relax.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. He spent a lot of money on movies.
options: A lot of money had been spent by him on movies.
A lot of money was being spent by him on movies.
A lot of money was spent by him on movies.
A lot of money is spent by him on movies.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'spent' becomes 'was spent' with the singular subject 'a lot of money': 'A lot of money was spent by him on movies.'

questions.text: On August 13, at what cost did the Dikom Tea Estate of Assam sell its 'Golden Butterfly' tea at the GTAC, auction centre?
questions.explanation: On 13 August 2019 a kilogram of the Dikom Tea Estate's 'Golden Butterfly' tea, made from buds, sold for ₹75,000 at the Guwahati Tea Auction Centre, a record price at the time.

questions.text: Which of these eminent personalities is the one to not receive the Bharat Ratna from the Honorable President in the year 2019?
questions.explanation: Pranab Mukherjee, Nanaji Deshmukh and Bhupen Hazarika (the last two posthumously) received the Bharat Ratna from President Ram Nath Kovind in August 2019. Sachin Tendulkar received it in 2014.

questions.text: Where were the Khelo India Youth Games held between January 10-22, 2020?
questions.explanation: The third Khelo India Youth Games were held in Guwahati, Assam, from 10 to 22 January 2020.

questions.text: According to the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Bill 2019, what is the proposed minimum compensation for hit and run case wherein, the victim die?
questions.explanation: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Bill, 2019 raised the compensation for a death in a hit-and-run case from ₹25,000 to ₹2,00,000.

questions.text: What was the name of the mega-ocean that surrounded the single continental mass before the continental drift as described by Alfred Wegener?
questions.explanation: Wegener called the single supercontinent Pangaea and the vast ocean around it Panthalassa.

questions.text: Which of the following ministries launched the two campaigns, named Angikaar and E-course?
options: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Ministry of Human Resource and Development
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs launched, in August 2019, the Angikaar campaign for beneficiaries of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) and an e-course on the Vulnerability Atlas of India.

questions.text: Which environmental phenomenon has been linked to synthetic chemicals like chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)?
questions.explanation: Chlorofluorocarbons release chlorine in the stratosphere, which breaks down ozone; the Montreal Protocol was agreed to phase them out.

questions.text: Above which layer of the atmosphere does the Exosphere lies?
questions.explanation: The exosphere, the outermost layer, lies above the thermosphere. Going up, the layers are the troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, thermosphere and exosphere.

questions.text: Which of the following trees will you find in the Littoral forests?
questions.explanation: Littoral (swamp) forests are the mangroves of coasts and deltas; the sundari tree, after which the Sundarbans are named, is typical of them.

questions.text: Who among the following is the 15th Chairman of the Finance Commission of India?
questions.explanation: N. K. Singh chaired the Fifteenth Finance Commission, set up in November 2017. Y. V. Reddy chaired the Fourteenth, Vijay Kelkar the Thirteenth and C. Rangarajan the Twelfth.

questions.text: In which year was the Harappan civilization first discovered?
questions.explanation: Daya Ram Sahni's excavations at Harappa in 1921 first brought the civilisation to light; Mohenjo-daro followed in 1922.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles ensures to provide free and compulsory education to all children in the age group of six to fourteen years as a Fundamental Right to Education?
questions.explanation: Article 21A, added by the 86th Amendment (2002), makes free and compulsory education for children aged six to fourteen a Fundamental Right.

questions.text: On January 6, 2020, how many Oman ships arrived at Goa to participate in “Naseem-Al-Bahr”, the Indo-Oman bilateral naval exercise?
questions.explanation: Two Royal Navy of Oman ships, Al Rasikh and Khassab, came to Mormugao, Goa, in January 2020 for the 12th edition of Naseem-Al-Bahr.

questions.text: Which of the following teams did the India Under-15 team defeat with a 7-0 score in the final of the SAFF (South Asian Football Federation) U-15 Championship 2019 held at Kalyani Stadium, West Bengal?
questions.explanation: India beat Nepal 7-0 in the final at Kalyani to win the 2019 SAFF U-15 Championship. Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan are not SAFF members.

questions.text: What is the shortcut key for the central alignment of a line or text in MS Office software?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+E centres the selected text in Word and PowerPoint. Ctrl+C copies, Ctrl+A selects all and Ctrl+G opens Go To.

questions.text: Which of these is an excretory organ of the human body?
questions.explanation: The skin removes water, salts and a little urea in sweat, so it counts among the excretory organs, with the kidneys, lungs and liver.

questions.text: Which among the following states won the final of the 25th Senior Women's NFC 2019-20 at Arunachal Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Manipur beat Railways 1-0 in the final at Pasighat, Arunachal Pradesh, in September 2019 to keep the title, its 20th Senior Women's National Football Championship.

questions.text: On 7th January 2020, who among the following was the Chairman of the second National GST Conference and Central and State Commissioners that was held to streamline the Goods and Services Tax?
questions.explanation: Revenue Secretary Ajay Bhushan Pandey chaired the second National GST Conference of Central and State Tax Commissioners in New Delhi on 7 January 2020.

questions.text: Which of these is not an Operating System?
questions.explanation: SQL (Structured Query Language) is a language for working with databases. Unix, Linux and Mac OS are operating systems.

questions.text: In which state did the 'Saila' dance originate? The dance is performed by boys after the harvest season.
questions.explanation: Saila, a stick dance performed by young boys after the harvest, is a folk dance of Chhattisgarh.

questions.text: Which of the following states will you go to enjoy the famous Gaura-Gauri Puja that is celebrated every year?
questions.explanation: Gaura-Gauri Puja, the worship of Shiva (Gaura) and Parvati (Gauri) at Diwali time, is a festival of Chhattisgarh.

questions.text: Which of the following are the 5 groups that plants are divided into?
options: Mollusca, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms and Angiosperms
Thallophytes, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms and Angiosperms
Arthropoda, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms and Angiosperms
Annelida, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms and Angiosperms
questions.explanation: Plants are grouped as thallophytes, bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms. Mollusca, Arthropoda and Annelida are animal phyla.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year was the Second Anglo-Mysore war fought between the Kingdom of Mysore and the British East India Company?
questions.explanation: The Second Anglo-Mysore War (1780-1784), fought by Hyder Ali and then Tipu Sultan, ended with the Treaty of Mangalore.

questions.text: In which of the following states of India is the Bomdi-La Pass located?
questions.explanation: Bomdi La is a pass in the West Kameng district of Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.text: In which year was the Dronacharya Award instituted?
questions.explanation: The Dronacharya Award, for outstanding sports coaches, was instituted in 1985.

questions.text: In the given sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. There are some members who haven't paid his subscription yet.
questions.explanation: 'Members' is plural, so the pronoun that refers to it must be 'their': 'who haven't paid their subscription yet'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. REVERED
questions.explanation: 'Revered' means deeply respected; its opposite is 'despised', looked down on. 'Cherished', 'esteemed' and 'valued' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Four jumbled sentences are given. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. The middle sun was the one we usually see every day, but the ones on either side were the sun’s smaller reflections. B. It looked like there were three suns in the sky. C. A local meteorological centre explained that reflection is caused by sunshine high in the sky and light passing through snow crystals in the air. D. A rare celestial phenomenon appeared in Mongolia.
questions.explanation: D announces a rare sight in Mongolia, B describes it (three suns), A says the two outer suns were only reflections, and C gives the meteorological centre's account of how such a reflection forms: DBAC.

questions.text: Four jumbled sentences are given. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. Put equal quantities of water and milk in a sauce pan and keep it on the flame. B. Now put some ginger, tea powder and sugar as per taste and boil it for a couple of minutes. C. Tea is one of the most common Asian drinks and is very simple to make. D. Turn off the flame, strain it into a cup and serve it hot.
questions.explanation: C introduces tea, and the steps follow in order: A (heat water and milk), B ('Now' add ginger, tea and sugar and boil), D (turn off the flame, strain and serve): CABD.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The Ken Gharial Sanctuary is a wildlife sanctuary near Panna in Madhya Pradesh. It is part (1)______ the Gharial Conservation association where captive bred gharials (2)______ released to help regenerate the gharial ecosystem. (3)______ is located at the Ken River, north of Panna National Park. Here you can also (4)______ the majestic Raneh Falls on the Ken River. The Sanctuary is (5)______ for visitors during monsoon season.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 1.
questions.explanation: A thing belongs to a larger whole as 'part of' it: 'It is part of the Gharial Conservation association'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The Ken Gharial Sanctuary is a wildlife sanctuary near Panna in Madhya Pradesh. It is part (1)______ the Gharial Conservation association where captive bred gharials (2)______ released to help regenerate the gharial ecosystem. (3)______ is located at the Ken River, north of Panna National Park. Here you can also (4)______ the majestic Raneh Falls on the Ken River. The Sanctuary is (5)______ for visitors during monsoon season.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'captive bred gharials' takes 'are' in the present passive: 'gharials are released'. 'Was' and 'is' are singular, and 'had' would give 'had released', making the gharials the ones doing the releasing.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The Ken Gharial Sanctuary is a wildlife sanctuary near Panna in Madhya Pradesh. It is part (1)______ the Gharial Conservation association where captive bred gharials (2)______ released to help regenerate the gharial ecosystem. (3)______ is located at the Ken River, north of Panna National Park. Here you can also (4)______ the majestic Raneh Falls on the Ken River. The Sanctuary is (5)______ for visitors during monsoon season.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The pronoun 'It' stands for the sanctuary, the subject of the passage: 'It is located at the Ken River'. 'These' is plural, and 'This' or 'That' would seem to point back to the conservation work just described.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The Ken Gharial Sanctuary is a wildlife sanctuary near Panna in Madhya Pradesh. It is part (1)______ the Gharial Conservation association where captive bred gharials (2)______ released to help regenerate the gharial ecosystem. (3)______ is located at the Ken River, north of Panna National Park. Here you can also (4)______ the majestic Raneh Falls on the Ken River. The Sanctuary is (5)______ for visitors during monsoon season.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Visitors go to 'see' a sight such as the Raneh Falls. 'Look' would need 'at', 'regard' means consider, and 'climb' does not suit a waterfall.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The Ken Gharial Sanctuary is a wildlife sanctuary near Panna in Madhya Pradesh. It is part (1)______ the Gharial Conservation association where captive bred gharials (2)______ released to help regenerate the gharial ecosystem. (3)______ is located at the Ken River, north of Panna National Park. Here you can also (4)______ the majestic Raneh Falls on the Ken River. The Sanctuary is (5)______ for visitors during monsoon season.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 5.
questions.explanation: A place shut to the public is 'closed' to visitors: the sanctuary is closed during the monsoon. 'Locked' and 'finished' do not suit a sanctuary, and it is visitors, not a place, that are 'banned'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A small compartment in an aircraft for the pilot
questions.explanation: The cockpit is the compartment from which the pilot flies an aircraft. The fuselage is the aircraft's main body, the canopy the transparent cover over a cockpit, and a chassis the base frame of a vehicle.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Mother said to Avika, "Finish these sums before you go to the park."
options: Mother told Avika to finish those sums before she goes to the park.
Mother told Avika to finish those sums before she went to the park.
Mother told Avika to finish these sums before you go to the park.
Mother told Avika to finish those sums before she was going to the park.
questions.explanation: An order is reported with 'told ... to': 'these' becomes 'those', 'you' becomes 'she' and, after the past reporting verb, 'go' becomes 'went'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'delicious'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. All the shops and restaurants “have been closed” during the bandh last Saturday.
questions.explanation: 'Last Saturday' fixes the action in the past, so the simple past is needed, not the present perfect: 'All the shops and restaurants were closed during the bandh last Saturday.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. Avika understands French, “does she?”
questions.explanation: A positive statement takes a negative question tag, with 'does' for a verb in the simple present: 'Avika understands French, doesn't she?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Cool it
questions.explanation: 'Cool it' is an informal way of telling someone to calm down and relax.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. GLUM
questions.explanation: 'Glum' means gloomy and dejected, so 'dismal' is closest. 'Bright' is nearly its opposite, and 'afraid' and 'nervous' describe fear, not gloom.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. When he came back home safe that night, everybody ______ a sigh of relief.
questions.explanation: One 'heaves a sigh of relief': the set phrase for letting out a long, deep sigh.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Go off at a tangent
questions.explanation: To 'go off at a tangent' is to turn suddenly from the subject to something quite different.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. For reaching the station, they hired an auto.
options: For reaching the station, an auto was being hired by them.
For reaching the station, an auto had been hired by them.
For reaching the station, an auto was hired by them.
For reaching the station, an auto is hired by them.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'hired' becomes 'was hired', and the object 'an auto' becomes the subject: 'an auto was hired by them'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. DECAY
questions.explanation: 'Decay' means rotting or gradual decline; its opposite is 'growth'. 'Decline', 'rotting' and 'corrosion' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. Our professor speaks English with a ______ Oriya accent.
questions.explanation: 'Pronounced' means very noticeable: 'a pronounced accent' is the usual phrase for an accent that is easy to hear. 'Widespread' describes how far something has spread, not how strong an accent is.

questions.text: In the given sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Someone have walked away with my umbrella.
questions.explanation: 'Someone' is singular and takes a singular verb: 'Someone has walked away with my umbrella.'

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A garden with fruit trees
questions.explanation: An orchard is a piece of land planted with fruit trees. A vineyard grows grapevines, a grove is a small group of trees and a nursery raises young plants.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. OPULENT
questions.explanation: 'Opulent' means rich and luxurious, as 'sumptuous' does. 'Poor' is nearly its opposite, and 'economical' and 'depressed' do not fit.

questions.text: Which of the following is an input device of a computer?
questions.explanation: A scanner turns printed pages and pictures into digital data for the computer, so it is an input device; speakers, printers and monitors are output devices.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who gave the slogans ‘Dilli Chalo’ and ‘Give me blood and I will give you Freedom’?
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose raised both calls, 'Dilli Chalo' and 'Give me blood and I will give you freedom', while leading the Indian National Army in South-East Asia during the Second World War.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian classical dancers has been INCORRECTLY matched with her dance form?
questions.explanation: Saswati Sen is a Kathak dancer, a senior disciple of Pandit Birju Maharaj, not a Bharatanatyam dancer. Madhavi Mudgal is an Odissi dancer and Radha Reddy a Kuchipudi dancer.

questions.text: Select the correctly matched pair of name of the company and its founder.
questions.explanation: Wipro began in 1945 as Western India Vegetable Products, founded by Mohamed Hasham Premji, Azim Premji's father. ITC began as the Imperial Tobacco Company of India, Infosys was founded by N. R. Narayana Murthy and six others, and Reliance by Dhirubhai Ambani.
