questions.text: When are neap tides produced?
options: When the sun and moon are at right angle to the earth.
When the sun partially contracts pull of the earth.
When the earth and moon are in a straight line.
When the sun lowers the gravitational pull of the moon.
questions.explanation: Neap tides occur when the sun and moon are at right angles as seen from the earth, so their pulls partly cancel and the tidal range is smallest; spring tides come when they are in a line.

questions.text: Which award is given to the best coach in sports and games?
questions.explanation: The Dronacharya Award is India's award for sports coaches. The Arjuna Award and the Khel Ratna honour sportspersons, and the Dhyan Chand Award lifetime achievement in sport.

questions.text: Which Indian English author was given the ‘Jnanpith Award 2019’?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Amitav Ghosh, the first writer in English to receive the Jnanpith Award, which was presented to him in June 2019. Strictly, his is the 54th award, for 2018, announced in December 2018; the award for 2019 went to the Malayalam poet Akkitham Achuthan Namboothiri. None of the other three writers had received it when the exam was held (October 2020).

questions.text: Who was the first president of Independent India?
questions.explanation: Dr Rajendra Prasad became the first President of India when the Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, and served until 1962.

questions.text: Which scientist/s proposed the theory of relativity?
questions.explanation: Albert Einstein published the special theory of relativity in 1905 and the general theory in 1915. Watson and Crick described the structure of DNA, John Dalton proposed the atomic theory and Charles Darwin the theory of evolution by natural selection.

questions.text: Which of the following places in India would you visit to see Mughal emperor Humayun's library?
questions.explanation: Humayun used the Sher Mandal, an octagonal tower in the Purana Qila (Old Fort) in Delhi, as his library; he died after falling on its stairs in 1556.

questions.text: Who among the following was given the ‘Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna’ award and which game did she/he excel in?
questions.explanation: The shooter Gagan Narang received the Khel Ratna for 2010-11. Sania Mirza (2015) plays lawn tennis, Yogeshwar Dutt (2012) is a wrestler and Ronjan Sodhi (2013) a double-trap shooter, so the other pairs name the wrong sport.

questions.text: The concepts of wages, rent, interest and profit are studied under which branch of economics?
questions.explanation: Wages, rent, interest and profit are the rewards of the factors of production (labour, land, capital and enterprise); how they are set is the theory of distribution, part of microeconomics, which studies individual units and markets.

questions.text: Novak Djokovic defeated Rafael Nadal to help his country pick up the ‘ATP Cup’. Which game do these players excel in?
questions.explanation: Djokovic and Nadal are tennis players: Djokovic beat Nadal in the final of the first ATP Cup, in January 2020, as Serbia beat Spain.

questions.text: What is the name of the first research station in Antarctica built by the Government of India?
questions.explanation: Dakshin Gangotri, set up in 1983-84 during India's third expedition to Antarctica, was its first research station there. Maitri (1989) and Bharati (2012) came later.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a portable device?
questions.explanation: A desktop computer is built to stay on one desk, with a separate monitor and keyboard; iPods, laptops and thumb drives are made to be carried.

questions.text: Which of the following abbreviations related to categories of Indian Civil Services is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives ICS: the Indian Civil Service was the civil service of British India, replaced after independence by the Indian Administrative Service, so it is no longer one of India's civil services. The question's wording is loose, as ICS is a real abbreviation, but of a service that no longer exists; IAS, IPS and IFS (the Indian Foreign Service, or the Indian Forest Service) are current services.

questions.text: Which of the following organs are NOT parts of the Alimentary canal?
questions.explanation: The liver and pancreas are digestive glands that lie outside the alimentary canal and pour their juices into the duodenum; the buccal cavity, oesophagus, stomach, intestines, colon and rectum make up the canal itself.

questions.text: At which of the following hill stations can tourists visiting in winter experience living in igloos?
questions.explanation: Since 2017, igloos have been built each winter near Sethan village in the Hamta valley above Manali, Himachal Pradesh, and tourists can stay the night in them.

questions.text: Vinesh Phogat is an ace Indian ______.
questions.explanation: Vinesh Phogat is a freestyle wrestler, gold medallist at the 2014 and 2018 Commonwealth Games and the 2018 Asian Games.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: During the rule of Tipu Sultan, which was the capital city of his state Mysore?
questions.explanation: Srirangapatna (Seringapatam), on an island in the Kaveri, was the capital of Mysore under Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan; Tipu died defending it in 1799.

questions.text: To which continent of the world do India, China and Japan belong?
questions.explanation: India, China and Japan are all in Asia, the largest continent.

questions.text: Jeff Bezos is the CEO of:
questions.explanation: Jeff Bezos founded Amazon and was its CEO when the exam was held (October 2020); Andy Jassy succeeded him in July 2021. Myntra, Snapdeal and Flipkart are Indian e-commerce companies.

questions.text: Organic compounds are compounds of the element ______.
questions.explanation: Organic compounds are compounds of carbon, usually bonded to hydrogen; carbon's ability to form chains and rings gives them their great variety.

questions.text: The Char-Dham Highway Project will connect four holy places: Yamnotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath and Badrinath. To which Indian state do these places belong?
questions.explanation: Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath and Badrinath, the Char Dham, are all in the Garhwal Himalaya of Uttarakhand; the Char Dham highway project is to link them by all-weather roads.

questions.text: Which country is called the ‘Coffee Bowl of the World’?
questions.explanation: Brazil, the world's largest producer of coffee, is called the 'Coffee Bowl of the World'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order. A. While the most common belief is that these traits remain fixed, research studies show otherwise! B. One such research study suggests that we can change our traits provided we want to change them. C. We all possess certain personality traits that set us apart from the rest. D. These traits, a mix of good and bad, define how we respond to situations and people.
questions.explanation: C introduces personality traits, D says what these traits do, A brings in the common belief that they are fixed and the research that disagrees, and B gives one such study: CDAB.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. One whom it is impossible to defeat
questions.explanation: 'Invincible' means too strong to be defeated. 'Inimitable' means impossible to imitate, and 'dissatisfied' and 'cowardly' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. The manager said, “I want you to attend the conference.”
options: The manager said that she wanted me to attend the conference.
The manager said that she want me to attend the conference.
The manager told to me I am to go to attend the conference.
The manager said I am wanting you to attend the conference.
questions.explanation: In reported speech 'I' becomes 'she' and 'you' becomes 'me', and after 'said' the present 'want' moves back to the past 'wanted'. The other options keep the present tense or are ungrammatical.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'messenger'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Red okra from Karnataka. Black rice from Gujarat. Red corn from Tamil Nadu. What you would (1)______ as exotic varieties of food today are (2)______ indigenous crops that belong to a specific region. Many such (3)______ crops have gone extinct. Many more are on the brink. But with Indian households (4)______ more conscious about healthy eating and the natural benefits of consuming local food, (5)______ among both consumers and farmers is increasing.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Would' is followed by the bare infinitive: 'What you would describe as exotic varieties of food'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Red okra from Karnataka. Black rice from Gujarat. Red corn from Tamil Nadu. What you would (1)______ as exotic varieties of food today are (2)______ indigenous crops that belong to a specific region. Many such (3)______ crops have gone extinct. Many more are on the brink. But with Indian households (4)______ more conscious about healthy eating and the natural benefits of consuming local food, (5)______ among both consumers and farmers is increasing.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Mostly' makes the generalisation: most of these so-called exotic foods are in fact indigenous crops of particular regions. 'Indigenous' is not a matter of degree, so 'incredibly' and 'surprisingly' cannot qualify it, and 'openly' makes no sense here.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Red okra from Karnataka. Black rice from Gujarat. Red corn from Tamil Nadu. What you would (1)______ as exotic varieties of food today are (2)______ indigenous crops that belong to a specific region. Many such (3)______ crops have gone extinct. Many more are on the brink. But with Indian households (4)______ more conscious about healthy eating and the natural benefits of consuming local food, (5)______ among both consumers and farmers is increasing.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Native' crops are those that belong to a region, the indigenous crops of the previous sentence; 'global', 'foreign' and 'new' contradict that.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Red okra from Karnataka. Black rice from Gujarat. Red corn from Tamil Nadu. What you would (1)______ as exotic varieties of food today are (2)______ indigenous crops that belong to a specific region. Many such (3)______ crops have gone extinct. Many more are on the brink. But with Indian households (4)______ more conscious about healthy eating and the natural benefits of consuming local food, (5)______ among both consumers and farmers is increasing.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 4.
questions.explanation: After 'with' and a noun, the -ing form describes what is happening: 'with Indian households becoming more conscious'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Red okra from Karnataka. Black rice from Gujarat. Red corn from Tamil Nadu. What you would (1)______ as exotic varieties of food today are (2)______ indigenous crops that belong to a specific region. Many such (3)______ crops have gone extinct. Many more are on the brink. But with Indian households (4)______ more conscious about healthy eating and the natural benefits of consuming local food, (5)______ among both consumers and farmers is increasing.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 5.
questions.explanation: As households grow more conscious of healthy eating and local food, 'awareness' among consumers and farmers increases.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. You've cleared the ______ examination, haven't you?
questions.explanation: An 'entrance examination' is the test taken for admission to a course or institution, the kind one 'clears'.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. A Delhi bound aircraft has to make an emergency landing at Mumbai airport as a woman passenger suddenly developed a serious breathing problem.
questions.explanation: The landing happened in the past, as 'developed' shows, so the verb must be 'had to make', not 'has to make'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. My doctor knew that I would eventually recover and do the kind of work I “would be doing” before.
questions.explanation: The work went on up to a time in the past, so the past perfect continuous is needed: 'the kind of work I had been doing before'.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. My friend narrated a very interesting story at the International Storytelling Festival.
options: A very interesting story was being narrated by my friend at the International Storytelling Festival.
A very interesting story has been narrated by my friend at the International Storytelling Festival.
A very interesting story was narrated by my friend at the International Storytelling Festival.
A very interesting story is being narrated by my friend at the International Storytelling Festival.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'narrated' becomes 'was narrated' in the passive: 'A very interesting story was narrated by my friend'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The student has made a ______ to the police about a false video of her that is being circulated by some miscreants.
questions.explanation: After the article 'a' a noun is needed: one makes 'a complaint'. 'Complain' is the verb, and a 'complainant' is the person who complains.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. The teacher said that all “that” students who did not complete the task in the given time should attempt it again.
questions.explanation: 'Students' is plural, so the demonstrative must be plural too: 'all those students who did not complete the task'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Let off the hook
options: Not made to wait for a long time
Not allowed to take part in an activity
Made to pay for one's actions
questions.explanation: To 'let someone off the hook' is to free them from blame, punishment or a duty.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. According to environment activitists, demolition of unauthorised apartment complexes are became a lesson for land encroachers.
questions.explanation: 'Are became' is not a verb form, and the subject 'demolition' is singular: 'demolition of unauthorised apartment complexes has become a lesson'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Parthian shot
questions.explanation: A 'Parthian shot' is a sharp remark or blow delivered while leaving, after the Parthian horsemen who shot arrows back as they rode away: a parting hit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. DEROGATORY
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'sarcastic', the only option close in sense: 'derogatory' means disparaging or belittling, and 'sarcastic' means mocking or scornful. 'Favourable' and 'appreciative' are opposites of 'derogatory', and 'lethargic' means sluggish.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order. A. Vijay the bus conductor was always there in one of these trucks. B. He had now quit his old job and joined politics. C. In the week before the elections, trucks bumped up and down the dirty streets of Laxmangarh, full of young men holding microphones and shouting: “Stand up to the rich!” D. That was the thing about Vijay; each time you saw him, he had done better for himself.
questions.explanation: C sets the scene of trucks full of young men before the elections, A places Vijay in one of these trucks, B says he had quit his job for politics, and D remarks that he always did better for himself: CABD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. INCOHERENT
questions.explanation: 'Incoherent' means unclear and hard to follow; 'intelligible' means able to be understood.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Soon passing out or of a short duration
questions.explanation: 'Evanescent' means soon passing out of sight or existence. 'Extempore' means unprepared, a 'fluke' is a lucky chance and 'frostbite' is injury from cold.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. OPTIONAL
questions.explanation: 'Optional' means left to choice; 'compulsory' means required. 'Elective' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. DEPLETE
questions.explanation: To 'deplete' is to use up or reduce. 'Raise' and 'increase' are its opposites.

questions.text: The last Mauryan ruler to be killed by Pushyamitra Shunga was:
questions.explanation: Pushyamitra Shunga, the army commander, killed Brihadratha, the last Mauryan king, in about 185 BCE and founded the Shunga dynasty.

questions.text: Who is the 47th Chief Justice of India?
questions.explanation: Sharad Arvind Bobde became the 47th Chief Justice of India on 18 November 2019, succeeding Ranjan Gogoi, and held the office when the exam was held (October 2020); N V Ramana succeeded him in April 2021.

questions.text: How many gold medals did India win at the ‘1986 Asian Games’ held in Seoul, South Korea?
questions.explanation: India won 5 gold medals at the 1986 Asian Games in Seoul, with 9 silver and 23 bronze; P T Usha won four of the golds in athletics.

questions.text: In which year was the Bharat Ratna award instituted?
questions.explanation: The Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, was instituted on 2 January 1954.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When was the Indian national song ‘Vande Mataram’ sung for the first time on a political occasion?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore sang 'Vande Mataram' at the 1896 Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress, its first singing at a political gathering.

questions.text: Which is the second most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Dry air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen by volume; argon and carbon dioxide make up most of the rest.

questions.text: In which medium does sound travel faster?
questions.explanation: Sound is carried by vibrating particles, which are most closely packed and most stiffly bound in solids, so it travels fastest there; it cannot travel through a vacuum at all.

questions.text: Batholith is a type of:
questions.explanation: A batholith is a large mass of intrusive igneous rock, such as granite, formed when magma cools and solidifies deep within the crust.

questions.text: With which of the following sports is Manika Batra associated?
questions.explanation: Manika Batra is an Indian table tennis player; she won the women's singles gold at the 2018 Commonwealth Games.

questions.text: The GST council is headed by the:
questions.explanation: Under Article 279A the Union Finance Minister chairs the GST Council; the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance and a minister nominated by each state (usually its finance minister) are its members.

questions.text: The ______ is responsible for Earth's magnetic field.
questions.explanation: Currents in the molten iron of the liquid outer core, driven by convection and Earth's rotation, generate the magnetic field. The inner core is solid.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book 'The Blue Umbrella'?
questions.explanation: 'The Blue Umbrella', the story of Binya, a village girl in the Garhwal hills, and her prized umbrella, is by Ruskin Bond.

questions.text: A higher ______ index represents inequality in income distribution.
questions.explanation: The Gini index runs from 0, perfect equality, to 1 (or 100), where one person has all the income, so a higher value means a more unequal distribution. CPI measures prices, and GDP and NDP output.

questions.text: 'Disha Act' was passed by which of the following state in December 2019?
questions.explanation: In December 2019 the Andhra Pradesh Assembly passed the Disha Bill, which sets short deadlines for investigating and trying sexual offences against women and children. It is named after the Hyderabad veterinarian raped and murdered in November 2019.

questions.text: Rambir Singh Khokar received the ‘Dronacharya award’ for:
questions.explanation: Rambir Singh Khokhar, a kabaddi coach, received the Dronacharya Award in the lifetime category in 2019.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an e-commerce website?
questions.explanation: Google Maps is a mapping and navigation service; nothing is bought or sold on it. Flipkart sells goods online, and Uber and Swiggy take orders and payments online for rides and food delivery.

questions.text: International Astronomical Union (IAU) named minor planet 2006 VP32 (number -300128) in September 2019 after a famous Indian. Who is this Indian?
questions.explanation: Minor planet 300128 (2006 VP32), found in 2006 by the Mount Lemmon Survey, was named 'Panditjasraj' in 2019 after the Hindustani classical vocalist Pandit Jasraj.

questions.text: In which part of a plant are mesophyll cells found?
questions.explanation: Mesophyll is the tissue between the upper and lower epidermis of a leaf; its palisade and spongy cells, rich in chloroplasts, carry out most of the plant's photosynthesis.

questions.text: ______ is a diagrammatic representation of a program logic.
questions.explanation: A flowchart shows the steps and decisions of a program or process as boxes of standard shapes joined by arrows.

questions.text: The Constitution under Article ______ mandates the Election Commission, to conduct elections to the Parliament and the State Legislatures.
questions.explanation: Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections to Parliament, the State Legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President in the Election Commission.

questions.text: Which river is also called 'Dihang' in India?
questions.explanation: In Arunachal Pradesh the Brahmaputra is called the Siang or Dihang; in Tibet it is the Tsangpo.

questions.text: Birthplace of Guru Nanak known as Nankana Sahib today, was earlier called.
questions.explanation: Guru Nanak was born in 1469 at Rai Bhoi di Talwandi, a village later renamed Nankana Sahib after him; it is now in Pakistan's Punjab.

questions.text: A force due to which moving objects (wind and water current) tend to deflect to the right in Northern hemisphere and left in Southern hemisphere is known as:
questions.explanation: The Coriolis force, which arises from Earth's rotation, deflects moving air and water to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern.

questions.text: 'Dhimsa' is a tribal dance form of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Dhimsa is a group dance of the tribal communities of the Araku Valley and nearby hills of Andhra Pradesh (in Visakhapatnam district when the exam was held, October 2020, and in Alluri Sitharama Raju district since 2022); it is also danced in southern Odisha.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. I learnt to adapt quickly to new schools because we moved to new places quite frequent.
questions.explanation: The verb 'moved' needs an adverb, not the adjective 'frequent': 'we moved to new places quite frequently'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. ROWDY
questions.explanation: 'Rowdy' means noisy and disorderly: 'boisterous'. 'Calm' and 'amenable' (easily persuaded) are nearly opposite, and 'charming' does not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. BARREN
questions.explanation: 'Barren' means bare and unable to support life or crops: 'desolate'. 'Fertile', 'bountiful' and 'fruitful' are its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Once in a blue moon
options: Happening only once in a lifetime
questions.explanation: 'Once in a blue moon' means very rarely, not only once in a lifetime.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. To close the day on a high note, we decided to spend the rest of (1)______ evening at a 100-year-old historic watering hole in downtown Juneau. We wanted to (2)______ our bear sightings and how it feels to be in the wild. While raising a toast and reminiscing (3)______ our time in the woods, I felt a deeper connection with nature. It was a (4)______ experience to walk for miles with no particular reason or intention other than absorbing (5)______ solitude of the jungle, open to the sky.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: The writer speaks as 'we', so it is 'our' evening; the pronoun 'ours' cannot stand before a noun.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. To close the day on a high note, we decided to spend the rest of (1)______ evening at a 100-year-old historic watering hole in downtown Juneau. We wanted to (2)______ our bear sightings and how it feels to be in the wild. While raising a toast and reminiscing (3)______ our time in the woods, I felt a deeper connection with nature. It was a (4)______ experience to walk for miles with no particular reason or intention other than absorbing (5)______ solitude of the jungle, open to the sky.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
questions.explanation: 'Wanted to' takes the base form of the verb: 'to celebrate our bear sightings'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. To close the day on a high note, we decided to spend the rest of (1)______ evening at a 100-year-old historic watering hole in downtown Juneau. We wanted to (2)______ our bear sightings and how it feels to be in the wild. While raising a toast and reminiscing (3)______ our time in the woods, I felt a deeper connection with nature. It was a (4)______ experience to walk for miles with no particular reason or intention other than absorbing (5)______ solitude of the jungle, open to the sky.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3.
questions.explanation: 'Reminisce' takes 'about': to reminisce about something is to recall it with pleasure.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. To close the day on a high note, we decided to spend the rest of (1)______ evening at a 100-year-old historic watering hole in downtown Juneau. We wanted to (2)______ our bear sightings and how it feels to be in the wild. While raising a toast and reminiscing (3)______ our time in the woods, I felt a deeper connection with nature. It was a (4)______ experience to walk for miles with no particular reason or intention other than absorbing (5)______ solitude of the jungle, open to the sky.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.
questions.explanation: Walking for miles, absorbing the solitude of the jungle and feeling a deeper connection with nature is a 'profound', deeply felt, experience. 'Sincere' describes people and feelings, and 'comical' and 'dismal' do not suit the passage.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. To close the day on a high note, we decided to spend the rest of (1)______ evening at a 100-year-old historic watering hole in downtown Juneau. We wanted to (2)______ our bear sightings and how it feels to be in the wild. While raising a toast and reminiscing (3)______ our time in the woods, I felt a deeper connection with nature. It was a (4)______ experience to walk for miles with no particular reason or intention other than absorbing (5)______ solitude of the jungle, open to the sky.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5.
questions.explanation: The solitude is a particular one, defined by 'of the jungle', so it takes 'the'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. Some such common events that bring us happiness for a short time include passing an exam, getting a job, going on a vacation or buying a dream house. B. Happiness is more difficult to achieve than peace as we keep striving for it daily. C. Peace, on the other hand, is sustainable for many years, costs less energy, and doesn't depend on external events such as these. D. Events that we struggle for in our daily lives to bring us happiness only come randomly, stay for a short time and subside.
questions.explanation: B sets happiness against peace, D says the events that bring happiness come randomly and do not last, A gives examples of 'such' events, and C, opening 'Peace, on the other hand', closes the contrast: BDAC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. We've had a long day. We should rest now, “shouldn't we?”
questions.explanation: A positive statement with 'should' takes a negative tag with the same auxiliary and subject: 'We should rest now, shouldn't we?' The sentence is correct as it stands.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'bungalow'.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Roopa said to me, "Please accompany me to the market."
options: Roopa said please accompany me to the market.
Roopa said to me that you must accompany me to the market.
Roopa requested me to accompany her to the market.
Roopa is requesting me to accompany her to the market.
questions.explanation: A request with 'Please' is reported with 'requested', the imperative becomes 'to' + verb, and Roopa's 'me' becomes 'her': 'Roopa requested me to accompany her to the market.'

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the given group of words. Arrangement of events or dates in the order in which they happen
questions.explanation: Chronology is the arrangement of events or dates in the order in which they happened. Geology studies the earth's rocks, archaeology the human past through its remains, and ecology the relations of living things to their surroundings.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. There was a range of ______ that kept tourists engaged during the International Film Festival in Goa.
questions.explanation: Tourists are kept engaged by a range of 'activities', things to do; 'moments', 'conversions' and 'employments' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. CONCEALED
questions.explanation: 'Concealed' means hidden; its opposite is 'revealed'. 'Masked' and 'hidden' are synonyms.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. We are arranging an exhibition of sarees from different states of India at Dilli Haat.
options: An exhibition of sarees from different states of India is being arranged by us at Dilli Haat.
An exhibition of sarees from different states of India was arranged by us at Dilli Haat.
An exhibition of sarees from different states of India has been arranged by us at Dilli Haat.
An exhibition of sarees from different states of India will be arranged by us at Dilli Haat.
questions.explanation: The present continuous 'are arranging' becomes 'is being arranged' in the passive, with the singular subject 'an exhibition of sarees'.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. The environment protection policy need to become stricter if we wish to combat climate change.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'the environment protection policy' takes a singular verb: 'needs to become stricter'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. He flew down, searched for her until he found her and then asked her to become his wife. B. A hawk flying about in the sky one day decided that he would like to marry a hen whom he often saw on earth. C. The hawk was delighted and flew away after giving her a ring as an engagement present, and telling her to take good care of it. D. She at once gave her consent on the condition that he would wait until she could grow wings like his, so that she might also fly high.
questions.explanation: B introduces the hawk who wants to marry a hen, A tells how he flew down and proposed, D gives her condition that he wait until she grows wings, and C, the delighted hawk flying off after giving her a ring, follows: BADC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. I had a stroke at an early age, but what I thought was a great ______ at that time changed my life for the better.
questions.explanation: A stroke at an early age, which the speaker took for a misfortune at the time, is a 'setback'; 'but' sets it against the better life that followed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. ADMONISH
questions.explanation: To 'admonish' is to scold or warn firmly; its opposite is to 'applaud', to praise. 'Belittle' and 'attack' are close to it in sense.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the given group of words. Someone who freely gives money and help to people who need it
questions.explanation: A philanthropist freely gives money and help to those in need. A philologist studies the history of languages, and a receptionist greets visitors.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. Rohit Sharma “have declared” the best batsman of 2019.
questions.explanation: Rohit Sharma was declared the best batsman by others, so the verb must be passive, and the singular subject takes 'has': 'Rohit Sharma has been declared the best batsman of 2019.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To leave someone in the lurch.
options: To come to compromise with someone
Constant source of annoyance to someone
To desert someone in his difficulties
questions.explanation: To 'leave someone in the lurch' is to abandon them when they are in difficulty.

questions.text: Which Indian cricketer has scored the most number of runs in a single World Cup?
questions.explanation: When the exam was held, in October 2020, the Indian record for one World Cup was Sachin Tendulkar's 673 runs in 2003; Rohit Sharma made 648 in 2019. (Virat Kohli passed it with 765 runs in 2023.)

questions.text: Who wrote ‘Humayun Nama’?
questions.explanation: The 'Humayun Nama' was written by Gulbadan Begum, Babur's daughter and Humayun's half-sister, at Akbar's request.

questions.text: Which of the following symbols must be used before a formula in a Microsoft Excel sheet?
questions.explanation: Excel treats an entry that begins with '=' as a formula, for example =A1+B1; '$' marks an absolute reference inside a formula.

questions.text: How many Indian bowlers have taken a hat-trick in International test cricket?
questions.explanation: When the exam was held, in October 2020, three Indians had taken a Test hat-trick: Harbhajan Singh (against Australia, 2001), Irfan Pathan (against Pakistan, 2006) and Jasprit Bumrah (against the West Indies, 2019).

questions.text: The moon is an example of a ______ object.
questions.explanation: The moon gives out no light of its own; it is seen by the sunlight it reflects, so it is non-luminous.

questions.text: When was the PIN Code (Postal Index Code) introduced in India?
questions.explanation: The six-digit Postal Index Number (PIN) code was introduced on 15 August 1972.

questions.text: Which of the following oil companies started an LPG bottling plant in Balangir district of Odisha in December 2019?
questions.explanation: Bharat Petroleum's LPG bottling plant at Balangir, Odisha, was dedicated to the nation on 27 December 2019.

questions.text: Which article in the Constitution of India empowers the President of India to promulgate ordinances when the Parliament is in recess?
questions.explanation: Article 123 lets the President promulgate ordinances at any time except when both Houses of Parliament are in session; Article 213 gives a Governor the same power for a state.

questions.text: As of February 2020, who is the Governor of Goa?
questions.explanation: In February 2020 the Governor of Goa was Satya Pal Malik, who took office on 3 November 2019. Pramod Sawant was the state's Chief Minister and Bhagat Singh Koshyari the Governor of Maharashtra.

questions.text: In which of the following cities was the ‘India International Science Festival (IISF)’ held in November 2019?
questions.explanation: The fifth India International Science Festival was held in Kolkata from 5 to 8 November 2019.

questions.text: 'Income and employment theory' is the other name for which branch of Economics?
questions.explanation: Macroeconomics studies the economy as a whole, its total income, output and employment, and so is also called the theory of income and employment.

questions.text: According to a report released by Greenpeace in Aug, 2019, India is the highest emitter of which of the following pollutants (gases)?
questions.explanation: Greenpeace's August 2019 analysis of NASA satellite data found India the world's largest emitter of man-made sulphur dioxide, mostly from coal-burning power plants.

questions.text: The solar tracking (moving in the sun's direction) of the sunflower is called ______.
questions.explanation: Heliotropism is the movement of a plant part that follows the sun across the sky, as young sunflower heads do. Phototropism is growth towards light in general, thigmotropism a response to touch and hydrotropism to water.

questions.text: What is the full form of BASIC in context of the BASIC computer language?
questions.explanation: BASIC stands for Beginner's All-purpose Symbolic Instruction Code; John Kemeny and Thomas Kurtz designed it at Dartmouth College in 1964.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book 'Bridgital Nation – Solving Technology's People Problem'?
questions.explanation: 'Bridgital Nation' (2019) was written by N Chandrasekaran with Roopa Purushothaman.

questions.text: Slate is a type of ______ rock.
questions.explanation: Slate is a metamorphic rock, formed from shale under heat and pressure.

questions.text: Who among the following is/was a famous Tabla player?
questions.explanation: Ustad Alla Rakha was a tabla maestro, the father of Zakir Hussain. T N Krishnan is known for the violin, Bhimsen Joshi for Hindustani vocal music and Hariprasad Chaurasia for the bansuri.

questions.text: How many fundamental duties are set out in Part IV A (Article 51A) of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: Article 51A lists 11 fundamental duties: the 42nd Amendment (1976) added ten, and the 86th Amendment (2002) the eleventh, on parents providing education for their children aged 6 to 14.

questions.text: The process that moves, elevates or builds up portions of the earth’s crust is called:
questions.explanation: Diastrophism covers all the processes that move, elevate or build up portions of the earth's crust, such as folding and faulting. Denudation and weathering wear the surface down.

questions.text: Who is the author of 'Malavikagnimitram'?
questions.explanation: 'Malavikagnimitram', a Sanskrit play about the Shunga king Agnimitra and Malavika, is by Kalidasa.

questions.text: Who is the only Indian to be nominated for the ‘IWGA Athlete of the Year 2019'?
questions.explanation: Rani Rampal, India's women's hockey captain, was put forward by the International Hockey Federation and was the only Indian among the 25 athletes nominated for the World Games Athlete of the Year 2019; she won the public vote in January 2020.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Translated into English, the motto of the Indian National Army (INA) was ______.
questions.explanation: The INA's motto was 'Ittehad, Itmad aur Qurbani': Unity, Faith, Sacrifice. 'Do or Die' was Gandhi's call in the Quit India Movement, and 'Unity and Discipline' is the motto of the NCC.

questions.text: Deficiency of thiamine results in ______.
questions.explanation: Thiamine is vitamin B1, and its lack causes beriberi. Rickets comes from a lack of vitamin D, pellagra of niacin (B3) and scurvy of vitamin C.

questions.text: River Sutlej enters India through which pass?
questions.explanation: The Sutlej, which rises near Lake Rakshastal in Tibet, enters India at Shipki La in the Kinnaur district of Himachal Pradesh.

questions.text: 'Matki' is a popular folk dance of which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Matki is a folk dance of the Malwa region of Madhya Pradesh, performed by women balancing earthen pots (matkis) on their heads.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. My mother is watching a new serial about the life of Dr. Ambedkar.
options: A new serial about the life of Dr. Ambedkar is being watched by my mother.
A new serial about the life of Dr. Ambedkar was being watched by my mother.
A new serial about the life of Dr. Ambedkar is watched by my mother.
A new serial about the life of Dr. Ambedkar will be watched by my mother.
questions.explanation: The present continuous 'is watching' becomes 'is being watched' in the passive: 'A new serial about the life of Dr. Ambedkar is being watched by my mother.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. The new product “will be arrive on” supermarket shelves only next year.
questions.explanation: The modal 'will' takes the base form of the verb: 'The new product will arrive on supermarket shelves only next year.'

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Rama said to me, "I need your help for my new assignment."
options: Rama says that she needs my help for the new assignment.
Rama said to me I need your help for my new assignment.
Rama said that she was needing my help for her new assignment.
Rama told me that she needed my help for her new assignment.
questions.explanation: 'Said to me' becomes 'told me', the present 'need' moves back to 'needed', and 'I', 'your' and 'my' become 'she', 'my' and 'her': 'Rama told me that she needed my help for her new assignment.'

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. An imagined society where everything is perfect and everyone is happy
questions.explanation: A utopia is an imagined place or society where everything is perfect. A hypocrite pretends to have virtues or beliefs he does not have.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Recently, I visited an orphanage for differently abled (1)______ in Delhi. The courteous staff (2)______ me feel at home and allowed me to interact (3)______ with the children. I was told beforehand that I could carry food packets and items of daily use like stationery, blankets, and clothes (4)______ the children, who were in the age group of five to 13. The children were a cheerful lot, the smiles on (5)______ faces reflecting the joy within on receiving gifts.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 1.
questions.explanation: An orphanage looks after many children, so the plural noun fits: 'an orphanage for differently abled children'. The singular 'child' would need an article, and the possessives 'child's' and 'children's' would need a noun after them.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Recently, I visited an orphanage for differently abled (1)______ in Delhi. The courteous staff (2)______ me feel at home and allowed me to interact (3)______ with the children. I was told beforehand that I could carry food packets and items of daily use like stationery, blankets, and clothes (4)______ the children, who were in the age group of five to 13. The children were a cheerful lot, the smiles on (5)______ faces reflecting the joy within on receiving gifts.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The visit is in the past ('Recently, I visited'), and 'make someone feel' is active here: the staff 'made' me feel at home.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Recently, I visited an orphanage for differently abled (1)______ in Delhi. The courteous staff (2)______ me feel at home and allowed me to interact (3)______ with the children. I was told beforehand that I could carry food packets and items of daily use like stationery, blankets, and clothes (4)______ the children, who were in the age group of five to 13. The children were a cheerful lot, the smiles on (5)______ faces reflecting the joy within on receiving gifts.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The staff let the writer mix with the children without restriction: 'allowed me to interact freely with the children'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Recently, I visited an orphanage for differently abled (1)______ in Delhi. The courteous staff (2)______ me feel at home and allowed me to interact (3)______ with the children. I was told beforehand that I could carry food packets and items of daily use like stationery, blankets, and clothes (4)______ the children, who were in the age group of five to 13. The children were a cheerful lot, the smiles on (5)______ faces reflecting the joy within on receiving gifts.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The packets and clothes were brought for the children's use: 'clothes for the children'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Recently, I visited an orphanage for differently abled (1)______ in Delhi. The courteous staff (2)______ me feel at home and allowed me to interact (3)______ with the children. I was told beforehand that I could carry food packets and items of daily use like stationery, blankets, and clothes (4)______ the children, who were in the age group of five to 13. The children were a cheerful lot, the smiles on (5)______ faces reflecting the joy within on receiving gifts.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The possessive 'their' goes before the noun 'faces': 'the smiles on their faces'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Get something off your chest
options: Remove something from you as it is troubling you a lot
Have difficulty in doing something that is quite easy
Express something that has been worrying you, and you want to say
Tell people some good news that you know and you want to share
questions.explanation: To 'get something off your chest' is to talk about something that has been worrying you, and feel relieved for having said it.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'privilege'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Incapable of making mistakes
questions.explanation: 'Infallible' means incapable of making mistakes. 'Ineligible' means not qualified, 'negligible' too small to matter and 'inevitable' certain to happen.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. IDLENESS
questions.explanation: Idleness is a lack of activity or effort, and 'lethargy', a lack of energy, is closest to it. 'Energy' and 'industry' are nearly its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. REPROACH
questions.explanation: To reproach someone is to express disapproval of what they have done; to 'berate' is to scold angrily.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. Einstein had a deep distaste for enforced learning, and was known to skip many of his college lectures. B. Einstein was also severely critical of the exam-based education system. C. The great physicist Galileo too said, “You cannot teach anybody anything. You can only help them discover it within themselves.” D. He often felt that formal education interfered with his natural desire to learn and explore.
questions.explanation: A introduces Einstein's distaste for enforced learning, D ('He often felt') explains it, B adds his criticism of exams ('also'), and C brings in Galileo, who 'too' held the view: ADBC.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. I think Virat Kohli will remain the captain of the Indian team in a year 2020.
questions.explanation: A year named by its number takes 'the', not 'a': 'in the year 2020', or simply 'in 2020'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. Soon, the idea took its final shape and she started selling barfis under the brand name Harbhajan's and the tagline "You’ll remember your childhood”. B. That's when Raveena suggested that she should start selling her signature 'Besan ki Barfi'. C. Today Harbhajan Kaur is truly living by these words as she now sells tasty barfi and makes good money. D. It all started in 2016, when 94 year old Harbhajan's daughter asked her if she had any regrets in life, to which she expressed that she never earned a penny for herself.
questions.explanation: D begins the story in 2016 with the daughter's question, B says that is when Raveena suggested selling the barfi, A says the idea soon took shape under a brand and tagline, and C ('Today') shows her living by those words: DBAC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Parents who are very ______ later repent giving their children too much freedom.
questions.explanation: 'Permissive' parents allow their children a lot of freedom, which fits parents who later regret giving too much of it. 'Strict' and 'overbearing' parents do the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. SPIRITUAL
questions.explanation: 'Spiritual' concerns the soul or spirit; its opposite is 'physical', of the body and the material world. 'Righteous' and 'pious' are close to it in sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. It is said that children who learn to use their body, mind and emotions for their own wellbeing, work ______ the wellbeing of others.
questions.explanation: To work 'towards' something is to work for it, in its direction: 'work towards the wellbeing of others'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. TESTIMONY
questions.explanation: Testimony is evidence or proof given in support of something; its opposite is 'disproof'. A 'witness' gives testimony.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. After walking a few steps in the forest, our guide “sensing” some sort of movement in the foliage behind us.
questions.explanation: The sentence needs a main verb, in the past to match the narrative: 'our guide sensed some sort of movement in the foliage behind us'. 'Was sensed' would wrongly make it passive.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Plain as day
options: Very simple and easy to do
Very obvious and easy to understand
questions.explanation: Something 'plain as day' is very obvious and easy to see or understand.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. We can see much changes in Government schools these days.
questions.explanation: 'Much' goes with uncountable nouns; the countable plural 'changes' needs 'many': 'We can see many changes in Government schools these days.'

questions.text: The capital of which empire was NOT in south India?
questions.explanation: The Palas ruled Bengal and Bihar, in eastern India, from the 8th to the 12th century. The Chola (Thanjavur), Chera (Vanchi) and Pallava (Kanchipuram) capitals were all in the south.

questions.text: Which application was launched by Reserve Bank of India in January 2020 to help visually challenged people identify new currency notes?
questions.explanation: The RBI launched the Mobile Aided Note Identifier (MANI) app on 1 January 2020; it reads a note's denomination through the phone's camera and tells the user by sound or vibration.

questions.text: Who was India’s first Chief of Defence Staff?
questions.explanation: General Bipin Rawat took office as India's first Chief of Defence Staff on 1 January 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following is a popular dance form of Lakshadweep island?
questions.explanation: Kolkali, a stick dance, is a folk dance of Lakshadweep, as are Parichakali and Lava. Koli is a fishermen's dance of Maharashtra, and Kuchipudi and Kathak are classical dances.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book ‘Reset: Regaining India's Economic Legacy’?
questions.explanation: 'Reset: Regaining India's Economic Legacy' (2019) is by the economist and politician Subramanian Swamy.

questions.text: 'Leukopenia' is an abnormal ______.
questions.explanation: Leukopenia is a low count of white blood cells. A fall in red cells is anaemia, a rise in red cells polycythaemia and a rise in white cells leukocytosis.

questions.text: Which stadium was renamed as Arun Jaitley Stadium in 2019?
questions.explanation: Delhi's Feroz Shah Kotla stadium was renamed on 12 September 2019 after Arun Jaitley, the former Finance Minister and long-time president of the Delhi and District Cricket Association, who had died that August.

questions.text: India got its first 3D Smart Traffic Signal System in August 2019. This system was designed by students of______.
questions.explanation: The 'Intelights' system, launched by the Punjab traffic police at a crossing in Mohali in August 2019, was developed by students of Chitkara University.

questions.text: 1° latitude is equal to approximately ______ km.
questions.explanation: A circle round the Earth through the poles is about 40,000 km long, so each of its 360 degrees of latitude spans about 111 km.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a central economic problem, solved by the Production Possibility Curve (PPC)?
questions.explanation: The production possibility curve illustrates the central problems of what to produce, full use of resources (a point on the curve rather than inside it), efficiency and growth (an outward shift of the curve). Sustainable consumption is not one of them.

questions.text: As per the eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India, how many languages are referred to as scheduled languages?
questions.explanation: The Eighth Schedule listed 22 languages when the exam was held (October 2020). It began with 14, and the last four, Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali, were added by the 92nd Amendment in 2003.

questions.text: Third generation computers used:
questions.explanation: Third-generation computers used integrated circuits. The first generation used vacuum tubes, the second transistors, and the fourth VLSI microprocessors.

questions.text: Which of the following plates has the slowest rate of movement at less than 2.5 cm/year?
questions.explanation: NCERT notes that of the spreading ridges the Arctic Ridge moves the slowest, at less than 2.5 cm a year, and the East Pacific Rise the fastest, at more than 15 cm a year.

questions.text: Through which of the following states does the Tropic of Cancer run?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer runs through eight states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

questions.text: India’s ‘National Sports Day’ coincides with the birthday of which sportsperson?
questions.explanation: National Sports Day, 29 August, marks the birthday of the hockey player Major Dhyan Chand, born in 1905.

questions.text: The fifth incarnation of Vishnu is known as:
questions.explanation: Vishnu's ten avatars begin Matsya, Kurma, Varaha, Narasimha and Vamana, so Vamana, the dwarf, is the fifth.

questions.text: 'Piklihal' and 'Utnur' are important ______ sites.
questions.explanation: Piklihal and Utnur are Neolithic sites of the southern Deccan; Utnur is known for its ash mounds, left by burning heaps of cattle dung at old cattle pens.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about Rajya Sabha?
options: It has powers that protect the rights of states against the union.
It can amend a money bill.
Twelve of its members are nominated by the President.
It is the upper house of the Parliament of India.
questions.explanation: Under Article 109 the Rajya Sabha cannot amend a money bill: it can only recommend changes within 14 days, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject. The other three statements are true.

questions.text: Who among the following won the ‘JCB Prize for Literature 2019’?
questions.explanation: Madhuri Vijay won the JCB Prize for Literature in November 2019 for her debut novel 'The Far Field'.

questions.text: Pineapple is a ______ plant.
questions.explanation: Although it is grown in the humid tropics, the pineapple is built like a xerophyte: its stiff, waxy leaves store water, and it uses CAM photosynthesis, opening its stomata at night to lose less water.

questions.text: Who was the youngest Member of Parliament to be elected in 2019?
questions.explanation: Chandrani Murmu of the Biju Janata Dal, elected from Keonjhar in Odisha at the age of 25, was the youngest member of the Lok Sabha chosen in 2019.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank in the given sentence. Over 7,50,000 people from 192 countries have pledged to go vegan for a month which, they say, would reduce carbon ______ by 45000 tons.
questions.explanation: Going vegan would cut the gases given off into the air: carbon 'emission'. 'Omission' means leaving something out, and 'inclusion' and 'exclusion' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. HOLISTIC
questions.explanation: 'Holistic' means dealing with the whole of something rather than its parts: 'comprehensive'. 'Sketchy' and 'superficial' are nearly its opposites.

questions.text: Select the option that is the passive form of the given sentence. The Principal gave her a warning about coming late to school every day.
options: She was given a warning about coming late to school every day by the Principal.
She has given a warning by the Principal about coming late to school every day.
She gives a warning to the Principal about coming late to school every day.
She was giving a warning by the Principal about coming late to school every day.
questions.explanation: The object 'her' becomes the subject 'she', and the simple past 'gave' becomes 'was given': 'She was given a warning about coming late to school every day by the Principal.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. AGITATE
questions.explanation: To 'agitate' is to stir up or make anxious; its opposite is to 'calm'. 'Excite' is close to it in meaning.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Simply put, happiness is satisfaction of mind. However, different individuals (1)______ different perceptions of how to achieve (2)______. For some, happiness lies (3)______ wealth; for others, it is in (4)______ and position; yet happiness is (5)______ to most.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'different individuals', in a present-tense statement of a general truth, takes 'have'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Simply put, happiness is satisfaction of mind. However, different individuals (1)______ different perceptions of how to achieve (2)______. For some, happiness lies (3)______ wealth; for others, it is in (4)______ and position; yet happiness is (5)______ to most.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The passage is about how people try to achieve 'happiness', and the next sentence says where different people find it.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Simply put, happiness is satisfaction of mind. However, different individuals (1)______ different perceptions of how to achieve (2)______. For some, happiness lies (3)______ wealth; for others, it is in (4)______ and position; yet happiness is (5)______ to most.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Something 'lies in' what it consists of: for some, happiness lies in wealth.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Simply put, happiness is satisfaction of mind. However, different individuals (1)______ different perceptions of how to achieve (2)______. For some, happiness lies (3)______ wealth; for others, it is in (4)______ and position; yet happiness is (5)______ to most.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Rank and position' go together as marks of status, which others see as the source of happiness.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Simply put, happiness is satisfaction of mind. However, different individuals (1)______ different perceptions of how to achieve (2)______. For some, happiness lies (3)______ wealth; for others, it is in (4)______ and position; yet happiness is (5)______ to most.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Yet' sets up a contrast: whatever people seek, happiness stays 'elusive', hard to find or achieve, for most.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'discrimination', without the extra 'i'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. LURK
questions.explanation: To 'lurk' is to wait or move about out of sight, usually with bad intent; to 'prowl' is to move about stealthily, as if hunting.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. Anu “jumped the gun” and announced their plans at the dinner table.
questions.explanation: To 'jump the gun' is to act too soon, before the right time, like a runner who starts before the starting pistol.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. So, clearly, where you get your news from matters, since you can’t possibly be expected to verify and authenticate every bit of ‘news’ you receive. B. Are you really sure those apparently sound bits of medical advice you received as forwards would pass muster with your doctor? C. Yet, we do often forward these in the belief that we are doing a good deed to our friends and relatives. D. Being educated is no guarantee against falling prey to fake news.
questions.explanation: D makes the general point (education is no guard against fake news), B gives an example (forwarded medical advice), C admits that we forward such messages anyway, and A draws the conclusion ('So, clearly'): DBCA.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Bouquet', a bunch of flowers, is spelt correctly. 'Frequensy' should be 'frequency' and 'Secquence' 'sequence', and 'Acquirum' is not a word.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Relating to the healing of diseases
questions.explanation: 'Therapeutic' means relating to the healing of disease. 'Inoculation', 'immunity' and 'preventive' are about keeping disease away rather than curing it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom Looking for a needle in a haystack.
options: Be interested in sewing and embroidery
Searching for small things to do
questions.explanation: 'Looking for a needle in a haystack' is searching for something almost impossible to find: a task with next to no chance of success.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. There is a double-digit growth in salaries of vocational jobs now and the trend “are likely to continue” in the coming years.
questions.explanation: The subject 'the trend' is singular, so it takes 'is', and 'likely' is followed by a to-infinitive: 'the trend is likely to continue'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A group of people who have come together in a religious building for worship and prayer
questions.explanation: A congregation is a group of people gathered in a place of worship for prayer. A crowd, a throng and a multitude are large gatherings of any kind.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. HEINOUS
questions.explanation: 'Heinous' means utterly wicked or hateful; of the options, 'agreeable', pleasant, is its opposite.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. While an average person lives up to 72 years of age, the life expectancy of doctors is only about 59 years, the shocking IMA study concluded. B. The sudden death of Dr. Meena Kumar at an International Conference in London after suffering a cardiac arrest has alarmed the medical community. C. She was a well-known medico recognised for her services as a consultant neurologist with a career of over 25 years. D. Her death brings to the fore the fact that even doctors have risky life-styles and a hard life, a study by the Indian Medical Association conducted on doctors, said.
questions.explanation: B reports Dr. Meena Kumar's sudden death, C says who she was, D says her death highlights the risky lives of doctors, citing an IMA study, and A gives that study's finding: BCDA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. His uncle advised Naveen “to keep away from” involving himself in the controversy.
questions.explanation: 'Advise' takes an object and a to-infinitive ('advised Naveen to keep'), and one keeps away 'from' something, so the sentence is correct as it stands.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the given sentence which contains the grammatical error. Aryan told Sriram, “Don’t worry I can be able to climb that tree to reach the fruit.”
questions.explanation: 'Can' already means 'be able to', so the two cannot be combined: 'I can climb' or 'I will be able to climb'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. He is your brother, ______?
questions.explanation: A positive statement takes a negative question tag with the same auxiliary and pronoun: 'He is your brother, isn't he?'

questions.text: Identify the segment in the given sentence which contains the grammatical error. Have I ever told you what lovely pickles my grandmother used to made when she was in Visakhapatnam?
questions.explanation: 'Used to' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'used to make'.

questions.text: Select the option that is the direct form of the given sentence. The child asked his mother if he could swim in the pool there.
options: The child said to his mother, “Will I swim in the pool here?”
The child asked to his mother, “Can he swim in the pool there?”
The child asked his mother, “Could he swim in the pool there?”
The child asked his mother, “May I swim in the pool here?”
questions.explanation: In direct speech the child speaks of himself as 'I' and says 'here' for 'there', and a request for permission, 'May I', is reported as 'if he could'. 'Will I' would have been reported with 'would'.

questions.text: As per the Constitution ninety-first amendment act, 2003, the total number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, in the Council of Ministers in a State cannot exceed ______ of the total number of members of the Legislative Assembly of that State.
questions.explanation: Article 164(1A), added by the 91st Amendment, caps a State's Council of Ministers, Chief Minister included, at 15% of the members of its Legislative Assembly (and sets a minimum of 12).

questions.text: The State Government of Goa launched the ‘Swasthya Sakhi Project’ in January 2020 to ensure the:
options: overall health of new-born female children
wellness and welfare of rural men or women
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the wellness and welfare of women: Goa's health department launched the project on 11 January 2020 together with a breast cancer screening drive and the Yashaswini scheme for women entrepreneurs, and the state government announced all three as schemes for women.

questions.text: Which of the following movies won the Golden Globe 2020 award for ‘Best Motion Picture – Drama’?
questions.explanation: Sam Mendes's First World War film '1917' won Best Motion Picture - Drama at the Golden Globes in January 2020. 'The Irishman', 'Joker' and 'The Two Popes' were also nominated.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: The President submits his resignation to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
The President submits his resignation to the Vice-President.
The President submits his resignation to the Chief Justice of India.
The President submits his resignation to the Prime Minister.
questions.explanation: Under Article 56(1)(a) the President may resign by writing under his hand addressed to the Vice-President.

questions.text: Who among the following was elected as the Jharkhand Assembly Speaker in January 2020?
questions.explanation: Rabindra Nath Mahato, the JMM MLA from Nala, was elected Speaker of the Jharkhand Legislative Assembly unanimously on 7 January 2020. Stephen Marandi had been the pro-tem Speaker, and Draupadi Murmu was then the state's Governor.

questions.text: Which of the following teams won the Diamond Jubilee edition of the ‘Subroto Cup International Football Tournament’ for sub-junior boys (under-14) category in August 2019?
questions.explanation: Saidan Secondary School of Mizoram beat the defending champions, Manipur's Unique Model Academy, 2-0 in the final in New Delhi on 29 August 2019. The Subroto Cup, the inter-school football tournament held under the Indian Air Force, was in its 60th (Diamond Jubilee) edition.

questions.text: Which of the following animals is used for transport in Tibet?
questions.explanation: The yak, a long-haired ox suited to cold and thin air, carries people and loads in Tibet. The llama is the pack animal of the Andes.

questions.text: Tagore Centre for the Study of Culture and Civilization is located in ______.
questions.explanation: The Tagore Centre for the Study of Culture and Civilization was set up at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study in Shimla, Himachal Pradesh.

questions.text: Robert has sandy soil in his fields. The ideal crop for his field is:
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives corn (maize), a crop commonly grown on light, well-drained sandy soils. NCERT names clayey and loamy soils, which hold water, for wheat and gram; cabbage is also grown on sandy loams, so the key is the best of the four but arguable.

questions.text: Which of the following environmental movements/conflicts of India was directly related to the prevention of felling of trees?
questions.explanation: In the Chipko movement of the 1970s, villagers in the Garhwal Himalaya hugged trees to stop them being felled. The other three were campaigns against dams: at Tehri, on the Narmada and in Kerala's Silent Valley.

questions.text: Who among the following formulates the monetary policy in India?
options: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India frames and carries out monetary policy; since 2016 its Monetary Policy Committee sets the policy repo rate.

questions.text: Which of the following carries blood from the heart to the kidneys?
questions.explanation: The renal arteries, branches of the aorta, carry blood from the heart to the kidneys; the renal veins take it back, to the vena cava.

questions.text: Which among the following is a vaccine developed by CSIR, Ministry of Science and Technology for Johne’s disease affecting sheep, Goat, Cow and Buffalo so as to immunize them and increase milk and meat production ?
questions.explanation: Johne's disease (paratuberculosis) is a long-lasting gut infection of cattle, buffaloes, sheep and goats, and the JD vaccine is the one named for it. Porcine parvovirus affects pigs and infectious bovine rhinotracheitis is a viral disease of cattle, while DIVA names a kind of vaccine whose use tests can tell apart from infection.

questions.text: Who among the following won the ‘Golden Globe 2020’ award for ‘Best Performance by an Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama’?
questions.explanation: Joaquin Phoenix won the Golden Globe for Best Actor in a Motion Picture - Drama in January 2020 for playing the title role in 'Joker'.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following years did Sarojini Naidu preside over the Indian National Congress session?
questions.explanation: Sarojini Naidu presided over the Kanpur session of the Indian National Congress in 1925, the first Indian woman to do so.

questions.text: Goods and Services Tax (GST) was enacted by Parliament vide ______Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 on 8th September 2016.
questions.explanation: The Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016, which brought in GST, received the President's assent on 8 September 2016; the tax itself came into force on 1 July 2017.

questions.text: In the context of computing, a byte is equal to ______ bits.
questions.explanation: A byte is a group of 8 bits.

questions.text: Hardwood trees like sal, teak, neem and shisham (useful for making furniture, transport and constructional material) are found in which type of forests?
questions.explanation: Sal, teak, neem and shisham grow in the tropical deciduous (monsoon) forests, which shed their leaves in the dry season.

questions.text: As of 15 January 2020, who among the following was the Number one ranked women tennis player in the WTA rankings?
questions.explanation: Ashleigh Barty of Australia was ranked number one in the WTA singles rankings in January 2020; she had held the top place since September 2019.

questions.text: Which of the following is a type of memory and is similar to RAM? It is used by computers to move data between the RAM and the CPU.
questions.explanation: Cache is a small, fast memory between the CPU and the main memory (RAM) that holds the data and instructions in current use. ROM is read-only memory.

questions.text: The ______ layer starts at Earth's surface and extends 8 to 14.5 km high (5 to 9 miles). This part of the atmosphere is the densest and almost all weather is in this region.
questions.explanation: The troposphere, the lowest layer of the atmosphere, holds most of the air's mass and nearly all its water vapour, so almost all weather happens in it.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: To whom did Mahatma Gandhi give the title ‘Deen Bandhu’?
questions.explanation: Gandhi called C F Andrews, the English missionary who worked for Indian labourers and the freedom movement, 'Deenbandhu', friend of the poor.

questions.text: As of 15 January 2020, which of the following nations was the Number one ranked ODI team in the ICC Men's ODI Team Rankings?
questions.explanation: England, the 2019 World Cup winners, were ranked first in the ICC Men's ODI Team Rankings in January 2020, ahead of India.

questions.text: ‘Daskathia’ is a form of ballad singing prevalent in ______.
questions.explanation: Daskathia is a ballad-singing tradition of Odisha, named after the 'kathia', a pair of wooden clappers the singer plays.

questions.text: Who among the following won ‘ICC Women's ODI Cricketer of the Year 2019’?
questions.explanation: Australia's Ellyse Perry was named the ICC Women's ODI Cricketer of the Year for 2019, and also won the Rachael Heyhoe Flint Award as the best woman cricketer; Alyssa Healy was the T20I Cricketer of the Year.

questions.text: In the given sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The Commonwealth Games had a grand opening ceremony with spectacular cultural performings.
