questions.explanation: 'Performings' is not standard English: the plural noun for shows is 'performances', so 'spectacular cultural performances'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A situation in which many people leave a place at the same time
questions.explanation: An exodus is a mass departure of people from a place. Immigration is coming to live in a foreign country, and mitigation is making something less severe.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate segment to substitute the underlined segment of the given sentence. In the jungle, I saw “a group of lions.”
questions.explanation: A group of lions is called a 'pride'. 'Flock' is used for birds or sheep, 'herd' for cattle or elephants and 'school' for fish.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. INTEGRATE
questions.explanation: To 'integrate' is to bring parts together into a whole: to 'unite' them. 'Divide' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Increasing levels of air pollution are (1)______ for higher incidence of respiratory diseases and other illnesses. Various studies carried out in Delhi reflect the correlation between air pollution and its (2)______ impacts. To tackle the problem of air pollution, a number of measures have been taken in the past, such as switching to (3)______ fuels, tightening vehicular emission limits, phasing out of old vehicles and maintenance of in-use vehicles, closing or relocating (4)______ industries, plantation activities etc. However, a lot more still needs to be done if the capital desires to (5)______ clean air.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Air pollution is the cause of the diseases, so it is 'responsible for' them. 'Responsive' means reacting readily, 'responsibility' is a noun, and 'are responding for' makes no sense.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Increasing levels of air pollution are (1)______ for higher incidence of respiratory diseases and other illnesses. Various studies carried out in Delhi reflect the correlation between air pollution and its (2)______ impacts. To tackle the problem of air pollution, a number of measures have been taken in the past, such as switching to (3)______ fuels, tightening vehicular emission limits, phasing out of old vehicles and maintenance of in-use vehicles, closing or relocating (4)______ industries, plantation activities etc. However, a lot more still needs to be done if the capital desires to (5)______ clean air.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Respiratory diseases and other illnesses are effects on people's health: 'its health impacts'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Increasing levels of air pollution are (1)______ for higher incidence of respiratory diseases and other illnesses. Various studies carried out in Delhi reflect the correlation between air pollution and its (2)______ impacts. To tackle the problem of air pollution, a number of measures have been taken in the past, such as switching to (3)______ fuels, tightening vehicular emission limits, phasing out of old vehicles and maintenance of in-use vehicles, closing or relocating (4)______ industries, plantation activities etc. However, a lot more still needs to be done if the capital desires to (5)______ clean air.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Switching to 'cleaner' fuels, which pollute less, is a measure against air pollution. 'Guiltless' and 'righteous' describe people, and 'immaculate' (spotless) does not describe a fuel.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Increasing levels of air pollution are (1)______ for higher incidence of respiratory diseases and other illnesses. Various studies carried out in Delhi reflect the correlation between air pollution and its (2)______ impacts. To tackle the problem of air pollution, a number of measures have been taken in the past, such as switching to (3)______ fuels, tightening vehicular emission limits, phasing out of old vehicles and maintenance of in-use vehicles, closing or relocating (4)______ industries, plantation activities etc. However, a lot more still needs to be done if the capital desires to (5)______ clean air.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Polluting industries' are industries that cause pollution; the '-ing' form works as an adjective before the noun. 'Polluted industries' would be industries that have been polluted.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Increasing levels of air pollution are (1)______ for higher incidence of respiratory diseases and other illnesses. Various studies carried out in Delhi reflect the correlation between air pollution and its (2)______ impacts. To tackle the problem of air pollution, a number of measures have been taken in the past, such as switching to (3)______ fuels, tightening vehicular emission limits, phasing out of old vehicles and maintenance of in-use vehicles, closing or relocating (4)______ industries, plantation activities etc. However, a lot more still needs to be done if the capital desires to (5)______ clean air.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 5.
questions.explanation: After 'desires to' the verb takes its base form: 'to breathe clean air'. 'Breathes' and 'breathed' are inflected forms and 'breather' is a noun.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate words to fill in the blank in the given sentence. I dislike people with ______ who say something and do something else.
questions.explanation: People with 'double standards' hold one principle in words and follow another in practice: they say something and do something else.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. However, in today's ever changing world, power looms are replacing the traditional handloom textiles. B. Handloom refers to the use of wooden frames of various kinds by skilled artisans to weave fabric from natural fibres. C. One of the most prominent among Indian handlooms are Banarasi textiles. D. Banarasi textiles are made with gleaming gold threads and weaving techniques as old as time.
questions.explanation: B defines handloom, C names Banarasi textiles as one of the most prominent Indian handlooms, D describes them, and A ('However ...') turns to power looms replacing them today: BCDA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Not mince (your) words
questions.explanation: Not to 'mince your words' is to say plainly what you think, even if it may offend.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Roshan said to me, "Sandeep made a new year greeting card for his teacher".
options: Roshan told me that Sandeep had made a new year greeting card for his teacher.
Roshan was saying that Sandeep made a new year greeting card for his teacher.
Roshan said Sandeep had made a new year greeting card for his teacher.
Sandeep made a new year greeting card for his teacher said Roshan.
questions.explanation: 'Said to me' becomes 'told me', the reported clause is joined with 'that', and the simple past 'made' goes back to the past perfect 'had made'. 'Roshan said Sandeep had made ...' leaves out the listener, 'me'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. Why did the teacher “ask all four of you” to stay back in class in the break?
questions.explanation: After 'did' the verb takes its base form, 'ask', and 'all four of you' is the idiomatic order, so the segment needs no change.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. DISABLE
questions.explanation: To 'disable' is to make unable or stop from working; its opposite, 'enable', means to make possible or allow, as 'permit' does. 'Disapprove', 'disallow' and 'refuse' point the same way as 'disable'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. The ______ entered the house in disguise saying his uncle lived there and robbed the place.
questions.explanation: The blank is the subject of 'entered' and 'robbed', so it must name a person, and of these words only 'technician' does. 'Technical' is an adjective, and 'technicality' and 'technique' name things, not people.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. INCITE
questions.explanation: To 'incite' is to stir up or urge on; to 'restrain' is to hold back. 'Instigate' and 'provoke' are its synonyms.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. In India, forests are huge catchment areas for rivers and streams as they help in storing water. B. If these forests continue to be felled indiscriminately, rivers and streams will dry up leading to drought. C. Due to this many states are facing shortage of water in the summer months. D. Unfortunately, these dense forest areas are disappearing.
questions.explanation: A says forests store water for rivers and streams; D ('Unfortunately') says these forests are disappearing; C gives the result, water shortage in summer; B warns that further felling will dry up the rivers and cause drought: ADCB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Rub the wrong way
questions.explanation: To 'rub someone the wrong way' is to annoy or irritate them.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. To laugh at something in a cruel way
questions.explanation: To 'deride' is to mock or laugh at scornfully. To 'deprive' is to take something away, and to 'defy' is to resist openly.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. I use jaggery to sweeten my tea in winters.
options: Jaggery is used by me to sweeten my tea in winters.
Jaggery is being used by me to sweeten my tea in winters.
I have been using jaggery to sweeten my tea in winters.
In winters jaggery was used by me to sweeten my tea.
questions.explanation: The simple present 'use' becomes 'is used' with the singular subject 'jaggery': 'Jaggery is used by me to sweeten my tea in winters.'

questions.text: Select the wrongly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Clearify' is misspelt: the word is 'clarify', although it is related to 'clear'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. TOLERANCE
questions.explanation: 'Tolerance' includes the capacity to bear pain or hardship, which is 'endurance'. 'Impatience' is nearly its opposite, and 'oppression' and 'aggression' are unrelated.

questions.text: In the given sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. My domestic help was taking ill the day I had a party in my house.
options: the day I had a party
questions.explanation: The idiom is 'fall ill' or 'be taken ill', and it happened on one day, so the simple past is needed, not 'was taking ill': 'My domestic help fell ill (or was taken ill) the day I had a party in my house.'

questions.text: As of October 2019, what is the total number of wildlife sanctuaries in India?
questions.explanation: India had 551 wildlife sanctuaries in autumn 2019: the Wildlife Institute of India counted 551 on 30 September 2019, and the Environment Ministry gave Parliament the same figure in November 2019. The count changes as states notify new sanctuaries or upgrade existing ones to national parks.

questions.text: The famous Chinese traveller Hieun Tsang visited India during which Emperor's reign?
questions.explanation: The Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang) travelled in India in the 630s and early 640s CE, during the reign of Harshavardhana, and studied at Nalanda.

questions.text: The first Five-Year Plan’s main emphasis was to improve the condition of agriculture in India. The plan began in the year:
questions.explanation: The First Five-Year Plan ran from 1951 to 1956 and gave priority to agriculture, including irrigation and power projects.

questions.text: Which of the following cities is home to one of the famous Swaminarayan Akshardham temples in India?
questions.explanation: India's Swaminarayan Akshardham temples are in New Delhi, opened in 2005, and in Gandhinagar, Gujarat.

questions.text: Who among the following was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature 2019 "for an influential work that with linguistic ingenuity has explored the periphery and the specificity of human experience"?
questions.explanation: The Austrian writer Peter Handke received the 2019 Nobel Prize in Literature with this citation. Olga Tokarczuk received the 2018 prize, announced the same day; Abiy Ahmed Ali won the 2019 Peace Prize and Michel Mayor shared the 2019 Physics Prize.

questions.text: What is the Palk Strait?
options: It is the border line between China and India in the western side.
It is the boundary line between India and Pakistan.
It is a water body that separates India and Sri Lanka.
It is the boundary line between northeastern India and China.
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait is the stretch of sea between Tamil Nadu and northern Sri Lanka, linking the Bay of Bengal with Palk Bay.

questions.text: Who among the following was the first recipient of the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award?
questions.explanation: The chess player Viswanathan Anand received the first Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, for 1991-92.

questions.text: Which of the following group of scientists was awarded the 2019 Nobel Prize in Chemistry "for the development of lithium-ion batteries"?
options: Joachim Frank, Richard Henderson and Jacques Dubochet
Kip Thorne, Rainer Weiss and Barry Barish
John B Goodenough, M Stanley Whittingham and Akira Yoshino
Fraser Stoddart, Jean-Pierre Sauvage and Ben Feringa
questions.explanation: John B. Goodenough, M. Stanley Whittingham and Akira Yoshino shared the 2019 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. Frank, Henderson and Dubochet won the 2017 Chemistry prize (cryo-electron microscopy), Thorne, Weiss and Barish the 2017 Physics prize (gravitational waves), and Stoddart, Sauvage and Feringa the 2016 Chemistry prize (molecular machines).

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: The Vice-President can dissolve the Legislative Council of a State.
The Governor can dissolve the Legislative Assembly of a State.
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha can dissolve the Lok Sabha.
The President can dissolve the Rajya Sabha.
questions.explanation: Under Article 174(2)(b) the Governor may dissolve a State's Legislative Assembly. The Lok Sabha is dissolved by the President, not the Speaker, and the Rajya Sabha and a State's Legislative Council are permanent bodies that are not dissolved.

questions.text: Which of the following is a very high-speed semiconductor memory which can speed up the CPU?
questions.explanation: Cache memory is a small, very fast memory between the CPU and main memory that keeps frequently used data and instructions close at hand, so the CPU waits less.

questions.text: Who among the following invented the aeroplane?
questions.explanation: Orville and Wilbur Wright made the first controlled, sustained powered aeroplane flight near Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, on 17 December 1903. The Lumière brothers are known for early motion-picture cameras and projectors.

questions.text: Reserve Bank of India, which acts as a banker to the Central Government, was established on:
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India was set up under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 and began operations on 1 April 1935; it was nationalised in 1949.

questions.text: Which female Indian boxer won silver in the AIBA Women's World Boxing Championships in October 2019 in the light flyweight category (48 kg)?
questions.explanation: Manju Rani won silver in the 48 kg class at the 2019 Women's World Championships in Ulan-Ude, Russia. Mary Kom (51 kg), Jamuna Boro (54 kg) and Lovlina Borgohain (69 kg) won bronze there.

questions.text: Which of the following consists of an electronic writing area and a special ‘pen’ that works with it?
questions.explanation: A graphics tablet (digitiser) is a flat input surface on which the user draws or writes with a stylus, and the strokes are passed to the computer.

questions.text: What is the traditional bamboo dance of Mizoram called?
questions.explanation: Cheraw is Mizoram's bamboo dance: dancers step in and out between pairs of bamboo poles that others clap together in rhythm. Thang-ta is a Manipuri martial art.

questions.text: As of January 2020, who among the following has the distinction of having the highest career batting average in Twenty20 Internationals?
questions.explanation: In January 2020 Virat Kohli's career average in T20 Internationals was above 50 (52.66 at the end of 2019), the highest among established T20I batsmen at the time; Rohit Sharma, Brendon McCullum and Chris Gayle averaged in the 30s.

questions.text: How many women candidates were elected to the 17th Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: 78 women were elected to the 17th Lok Sabha in 2019, the most until then, about 14% of its members.

questions.text: The centre of a cyclone is a calm area. It is called the ______ of the storm.
questions.explanation: The calm centre of a tropical cyclone, where air sinks and skies are nearly clear, is its eye; the strongest winds blow in the eyewall around it.

questions.text: Which of the following nations won the FIFA World Cup most number of times?
questions.explanation: Brazil has won the World Cup five times (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994 and 2002). When the exam was held, in October 2020, Germany had won it four times and Argentina and France twice each.

questions.text: In terms of area, which is the smallest Union Territory of India?
questions.explanation: Lakshadweep, with about 32 km² of land, is the smallest Union Territory by area.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: ______ was an important member of the Hindustan Republican Association, who along with his associates executed the train dacoity at Kakori.
questions.explanation: Ashfaqulla Khan, with Ram Prasad Bismil and other members of the Hindustan Republican Association, held up a train at Kakori near Lucknow on 9 August 1925 and seized the government money it carried; he was hanged in 1927.

questions.text: JP Nadda was elected as the President of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on 20 January 2020. He is the ______ president of the BJP.
questions.explanation: J. P. Nadda, elected unopposed on 20 January 2020, is counted as the BJP's eleventh president, after Atal Bihari Vajpayee, L. K. Advani, Murli Manohar Joshi, Kushabhau Thakre, Bangaru Laxman, K. Jana Krishnamurthi, M. Venkaiah Naidu, Rajnath Singh, Nitin Gadkari and Amit Shah.

questions.text: Who among the following headed the nine-judge constitutional bench that declared the right to privacy as a fundamental right?
questions.explanation: Chief Justice J. S. Khehar headed the nine-judge bench in Justice K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India, which held on 24 August 2017 that privacy is a fundamental right.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year did the Dalai Lama cross over into India and take asylum?
questions.explanation: The 14th Dalai Lama fled Lhasa during the Tibetan uprising of March 1959, crossed into India at the end of that month and was given asylum; he later settled at Dharamshala.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. She “was looking troubled” when the teacher asked her to submit the homework.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: the past continuous of the linking verb 'look' with the adjective 'troubled' (worried) says how she seemed at that moment. 'Was troubling' would mean she was causing trouble.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Come in the way of
questions.explanation: To hamper is to hinder, to get in the way of something. 'Facilitate' is nearly its opposite, 'indulge' means to allow oneself a pleasure and 'deprive' to deny someone something.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Neeta said, "Let me see how Pragya performs in her preboard examinations."
options: Neeta said that she wanted to see how Pragya performed in her preboard examinations.
Neeta said I would see how Pragya performed in her preboard examinations.
Neeta wants to see Pragya's performance in her preboard examinations.
Neeta wanted to see how Pragya would perform in her preboard examinations.
questions.explanation: 'Let me' expressing a wish is reported with 'wanted to'; 'me' becomes 'she', and after the past 'said' the present 'performs' moves back to 'performed'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. An unforseen happening which creates some damage
questions.explanation: A mishap is an unlucky accident, usually a minor one. A menace is a threat, and 'mystery' and 'magical' do not fit.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. A recent census of waterbirds conducted as a part of Asian Waterbird Census (1)______ an increase in their population in Najafgarh Jheel this year. The census also showed a (2)______ in the number of threatened species. Last year, the number of waterbird species were thirty-one which climbed to fifty- four this year, while the threatened variety (3)______ from four to six in the same duration. The region also saw a healthy monsoon in 2019, which would have (4)______ impacted the quality of habitat, making it (5)______ to more birds.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 1.
questions.explanation: A census 'records' what it finds: the census recorded an increase in the waterbird population.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. A recent census of waterbirds conducted as a part of Asian Waterbird Census (1)______ an increase in their population in Najafgarh Jheel this year. The census also showed a (2)______ in the number of threatened species. Last year, the number of waterbird species were thirty-one which climbed to fifty- four this year, while the threatened variety (3)______ from four to six in the same duration. The region also saw a healthy monsoon in 2019, which would have (4)______ impacted the quality of habitat, making it (5)______ to more birds.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The threatened species went up from four to six, so the census showed a 'growth' in their number.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. A recent census of waterbirds conducted as a part of Asian Waterbird Census (1)______ an increase in their population in Najafgarh Jheel this year. The census also showed a (2)______ in the number of threatened species. Last year, the number of waterbird species were thirty-one which climbed to fifty- four this year, while the threatened variety (3)______ from four to six in the same duration. The region also saw a healthy monsoon in 2019, which would have (4)______ impacted the quality of habitat, making it (5)______ to more birds.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The change happened over a finished period, from last year to this, so the simple past 'rose' is needed, like 'climbed' earlier in the sentence.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. A recent census of waterbirds conducted as a part of Asian Waterbird Census (1)______ an increase in their population in Najafgarh Jheel this year. The census also showed a (2)______ in the number of threatened species. Last year, the number of waterbird species were thirty-one which climbed to fifty- four this year, while the threatened variety (3)______ from four to six in the same duration. The region also saw a healthy monsoon in 2019, which would have (4)______ impacted the quality of habitat, making it (5)______ to more birds.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 4.
questions.explanation: A healthy monsoon would have 'directly' affected the quality of the habitat. 'Dutily' is not a word, and 'decently' and 'deftly' (skilfully) do not fit.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. A recent census of waterbirds conducted as a part of Asian Waterbird Census (1)______ an increase in their population in Najafgarh Jheel this year. The census also showed a (2)______ in the number of threatened species. Last year, the number of waterbird species were thirty-one which climbed to fifty- four this year, while the threatened variety (3)______ from four to six in the same duration. The region also saw a healthy monsoon in 2019, which would have (4)______ impacted the quality of habitat, making it (5)______ to more birds.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 5.
questions.explanation: A better habitat makes the lake 'attractive' to more birds, which explains the rise in their numbers.

questions.text: In the given sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The neighbourhood were getting disturbed with the loud music that was playing at the wedding party in the big bungalow.
questions.explanation: Taken as one unit, the collective noun 'neighbourhood' takes a singular verb: 'The neighbourhood was getting disturbed'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'irrational', with a double 'r'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To fall on deaf ears
options: To be aware of what is going on
questions.explanation: Advice or a request that 'falls on deaf ears' is ignored: nobody pays attention to it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. Today's ______ are only interested in watching movies with the stories they can relate to the cinema.
questions.explanation: The people who watch films are their 'audiences'; the sentence is about what today's viewers want to see.

questions.text: Four jumbled sentences are given. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. Saranda forests, in Singhbum, are a huge catchment for rivers and streams in this state. B. If these forests are opened up for mining purposes the remaining rivers and streams will dry up. C. The state of Jharkand faces water scarcity every summer. D. These forests are India's largest contiguous Sal forests and the current plan says mining should not be allowed in the dense forest as rivers are drying up.
questions.explanation: C names the state and its problem, water scarcity; A introduces the Saranda forests as a catchment for its rivers ('this state'); D describes these forests and the plan against mining; B warns what mining would do to the remaining rivers: CADB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Eat humble pie
options: Eat something which is not tasty
questions.explanation: To 'eat humble pie' is to admit that you were wrong and apologise humbly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. The flyover was closed in October last year for repairs but its reopening has been ______ as it will be ready only in March this year.
questions.explanation: The flyover will be ready only in March, later than planned, so its reopening has been 'delayed'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word FRAGILE
questions.explanation: Fragile means easily broken or damaged; its opposite is 'strong'.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of given sentence. We can buy diamonds, but we cannot buy sympathy.
options: Diamonds can be bought but sympathy can be brought.
Diamonds cannot be bought but sympathy cannot be brought.
Diamonds can be bought but sympathy cannot be brought.
Diamonds can be bought and sympathy cannot be brought.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'Diamonds can be bought but sympathy cannot be brought.': 'can buy' becomes 'can be bought' and 'cannot buy' 'cannot be bought', with 'but' kept for the contrast, and only this option follows that pattern. All four options print 'brought' (from 'bring') in the second clause, a misprint for 'bought'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word IMPROMPTU
questions.explanation: Impromptu means done without planning or preparation; its opposite is 'planned'. 'Unplanned' is a synonym.

questions.text: In the given sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The park was well lighted at night but it was deserted, so it was a bit scared.
options: so it was a bit scared
questions.explanation: 'Scared' describes someone who feels fear; a place that causes fear is 'scary': 'so it was a bit scary'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. INTERSPERSED
questions.explanation: Interspersed means placed here and there among other things: 'scattered'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. "Did you tell your parents “that you would going” for a movie with me this evening?" My friend asked me.
questions.explanation: 'Would' must be followed by a base form ('would go', 'would be going'), so 'would going' is wrong. Of the options only 'that you are going' is grammatical: the present continuous for a plan for the same evening, still in the future when the question is asked.

questions.text: Four jumbled sentences are given. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. The minimum temperature in the national capital dropped yesterday as cold north westerly winds continued to blow in from the hills. B. North India has been witnessing a harsh winter this year. C. However, experts said the minimum temperatures would increase over the next few days due to a cloud cover. D. A favourable outcome of the wind factor was that there was a slight decrease in air pollution levels due to the wind speeds.
questions.explanation: B sets the scene, a harsh winter in North India; A reports the fall in the capital's minimum temperature as cold winds blew in; D gives the one good result of these winds, cleaner air; C, opening with 'However', says temperatures would soon rise: BADC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. MASQUERADED
questions.explanation: To masquerade is to pretend to be someone or something else, to put on an act: 'acted' is the closest of the options.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was the last Viceroy of India who oversaw the creation of the independent states of India and Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Lord Mountbatten, Viceroy from March 1947, oversaw the partition and the transfer of power on 15 August 1947, and stayed on as independent India's first Governor-General until June 1948.

questions.text: In July 2018, a stable body of liquid water was found on Mars using a radar instrument on board the European Space Agency's Mars Express orbiter. The tool that was used for the discovery is called:
questions.explanation: MARSIS, the Mars Advanced Radar for Subsurface and Ionosphere Sounding on board Mars Express, picked up radar echoes that point to a lake of liquid water about 1.5 km below the ice of Mars's south polar cap; the finding was published in July 2018.

questions.text: As of January 2020, who among the following had the distinction of having the highest career batting average in One Day Internationals?
questions.explanation: Ryan ten Doeschate of the Netherlands, who played his 33 ODIs between 2006 and 2011, averaged 67.00: in January 2020 the highest career ODI average among batsmen with at least 20 innings. Virat Kohli's was then about 60.

questions.text: Among various electrical safety devices, one based on the heating effect of electric current is called a:
questions.explanation: A fuse wire, of a metal with a low melting point, heats up and melts when too much current flows, breaking the circuit: it works on the heating effect of electric current.

questions.text: Which of the following parks is India's first 'Mixed World Heritage Site' on UNESCO’s World Heritage list?
questions.explanation: Khangchendzonga National Park in Sikkim was inscribed in 2016 as India's first 'mixed' World Heritage Site, listed for both its natural and its cultural value.

questions.text: As per Article 80 of the Constitution of India, what can be the maximum strength of Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: Article 80 caps the Rajya Sabha at 250 members: 12 nominated by the President and not more than 238 representatives of the States and Union Territories.

questions.text: Which of the following group of scientists was awarded the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine "for their discoveries of how cells sense and adapt to oxygen availability"?
options: William G Kaelin Jr, Sir Peter J Ratcliffe and Gregg L Semenza
Fraser Stoddart, Jean-Pierre Sauvage and Ben Feringa
Kip Thorne, Rainer Weiss and Barry Barish
John B Goodenough, M Stanley Whittingham and Akira Yoshino
questions.explanation: William Kaelin, Peter Ratcliffe and Gregg Semenza shared the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Goodenough, Whittingham and Yoshino won the 2019 chemistry prize, for lithium-ion batteries; Thorne, Weiss and Barish the 2017 physics prize; and Stoddart, Sauvage and Feringa the 2016 chemistry prize.

questions.text: With which of the following is 'Operation Flood' related?
questions.explanation: Operation Flood, launched by the National Dairy Development Board in 1970 under Verghese Kurien, built a national milk grid linking producers to consumers; it is known as the White Revolution.

questions.text: Where is Valmiki Tiger Reserve located?
questions.explanation: Valmiki Tiger Reserve lies in West Champaran district of Bihar, on the border with Nepal. Tadoba-Andhari is in Chandrapur, Ranthambore in Rajasthan and Dudhwa in Lakhimpur Kheri.

questions.text: Which statement best explains why Shillong gets around 200 cm rainfall annually; whereas Cherrapunji, which is around 30 km away (as the crow flies), gets over 1250 cm of rainfall annually?
options: Cherrapunii gets rainfall from rain-laden clouds coming from the Himalayas, whereas Shillong gets rainfall from the Malabar branch of monsoon.
Cherrapunji lies on the leeward side of the Khasi hills and Shillong lies on the windward side of the Khasi hills, and thus, gets only wind and no rain.
The average temperature of Shillong has gone up due to excessive deforestation and pollution.

Cherrapunji lies on the windward side of the Khasi hills and receives rainfall from the Bay of Bengal branch of monsoon, while Shillong lies on the leeward side of the Khasi hills, which forms the rain shadow area.
questions.explanation: Moist winds of the Bay of Bengal branch of the monsoon rise up the southern, windward slopes of the Khasi hills and drop heavy rain at Cherrapunji; Shillong, on the leeward side, lies in a rain shadow and gets far less.

questions.text: Whose birth anniversary is celebrated as National Sports Day every year on 29 August?
questions.explanation: National Sports Day, 29 August, marks the birth anniversary of the hockey player Major Dhyan Chand, born on that day in 1905.

questions.text: What is Gini coefficient used for?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'income inequality': the Gini coefficient measures how unequally income is distributed, from 0 when everyone has the same income to 1 when one person has it all. It is worked out from the distribution of income, but what it measures is the inequality in it, so 'distribution of income' is too general.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides that there shall be a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister as its head?
questions.explanation: Article 74(1) provides for a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at its head to aid and advise the President.

questions.text: With which of the following musical instruments was the musician Palghat Mani Iyer associated?
questions.explanation: Palghat Mani Iyer was a leading mridangam player of Carnatic music.

questions.text: How many times did Mahmud of Ghazni invade India?
questions.explanation: Mahmud of Ghazni is traditionally said to have raided India 17 times, between 1000 and 1027 CE; his raid on the Somnath temple is the best known.

questions.text: As of January 2020, who among the following had the distinction of having scored the most goals at a single tournament in the entire history of FIFA World Cup?
questions.explanation: Just Fontaine of France scored 13 goals at the 1958 World Cup in Sweden, a record for one tournament that still stood in January 2020.

questions.text: Who among the following lifted the ‘WTA Hobart International’ tennis trophy with partner Nadiia Kichenok in January 2020?
questions.explanation: Sania Mirza and Nadiia Kichenok of Ukraine won the women's doubles at the Hobart International in January 2020, in Mirza's first tournament after her return from maternity leave.

questions.text: ______ is a small, portable flash memory card that plugs into a computer’s USB port and functions as a portable hard drive.
questions.explanation: A USB flash drive (pen drive) stores data in flash memory and plugs into a USB port; it is used like a small portable hard drive.

questions.text: Which of the following is the largest delta in the world?
questions.explanation: The Ganges-Brahmaputra delta, in India and Bangladesh, is the largest delta in the world; its seaward part holds the Sundarbans mangrove forest.

questions.text: Which day is celebrated every year as ‘World Environment Day’?
questions.explanation: The UN chose 5 June, the opening day of the 1972 Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment, as World Environment Day; it has been observed every year since 1974.

questions.text: What is ‘Central Equipment Identify Register’?
options: A portal launched by the Government of India to block and trace mobile phones
A portal launched by the Government of India to identify and trace the illegal activities of criminals
A portal launched by the Government of India to enforce income and corporate tax compliance
A portal launched by the Government of India to identify and trace the activities of illegal immigrants
questions.explanation: The Central Equipment Identity Register (CEIR), set up by the Department of Telecommunications, holds the IMEI numbers of mobile phones; through its portal, launched in 2019, a lost or stolen phone can be blocked on every network and traced. (The question's 'Identify' is a misprint for 'Identity'.)

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When was the 120th birth anniversary of Shaheed Udham Singh celebrated in India?
questions.explanation: Udham Singh, who shot Michael O'Dwyer in London in 1940 to avenge the Jallianwala Bagh massacre, was born on 26 December 1899, so his 120th birth anniversary fell on 26 December 2019.

questions.text: As of January 2020, who was the chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission of India?
questions.explanation: Justice H L Dattu, a former Chief Justice of India, chaired the National Human Rights Commission from February 2016 to December 2020, so he held the post in January 2020. Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose became India's first Lokpal in March 2019.

questions.text: In which of the following states/union territories are you more likely to find the natural habitat of the one-horned rhinoceros (Indian Rhino)?
questions.explanation: The greater one-horned rhinoceros lives in the grasslands of the Brahmaputra valley; Assam's Kaziranga National Park holds most of the world's population, and Pobitora, Orang and Manas also have rhinos.

questions.text: ______ is the fastest to read from and write to than the other kinds of storage in a computer.
questions.explanation: RAM is electronic memory that the processor reads and writes directly, much faster than a hard disk, a floppy disk or a CD-ROM, which all depend on moving parts.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Around one hundred ______ across the world participated in the conference.
questions.explanation: Delegates are people sent to represent others at a conference, which fits 'participated in the conference'. 'Clever' and 'intelligent' are adjectives, not nouns, and 'talents' are abilities (or, loosely, gifted people), not representatives at a conference.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. To restart his “cash-strapped” company he decided to apply for a bank loan.
questions.explanation: 'Cash-strapped' means short of money: the company was 'impoverished', made poor, which is why he applied for a loan.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. Gitanjali “did not had” school yesterday because it was a second Saturday.
questions.explanation: 'Did' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'did not have', not 'did not had'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. Bharati told Rakesh to call her when he reached there.
options: “Call her when you have reached here”, Bharati told Rakesh.
“Call him when you are reaching there”, Bharati told Rakesh.
“Call me when you reached there”, Bharati says to Rakesh.
“Call me when you reach there”, Bharati told Rakesh.
questions.explanation: The reported command becomes an imperative: 'her' (Bharati herself) becomes 'me', 'he reached' becomes 'you reach', and the past reporting verb 'told' stays.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in Panchmahal district in Gujarat, India. (1)______ is situated near the historical (2)______ of Champaner, a city which was founded by Vanraj Chavda, the (3)______ prominent king of the Chavda Dynasty, in the 8th century. He named it (4)______ the name of his friend and general Champa, also known later as Champaraj. The heritage site is dotted with forts with bastions ranging (5)______ the hills of Pavagadh, and extending into the city of Champaner.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The singular pronoun 'It' stands for the park, the subject of the sentence before.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in Panchmahal district in Gujarat, India. (1)______ is situated near the historical (2)______ of Champaner, a city which was founded by Vanraj Chavda, the (3)______ prominent king of the Chavda Dynasty, in the 8th century. He named it (4)______ the name of his friend and general Champa, also known later as Champaraj. The heritage site is dotted with forts with bastions ranging (5)______ the hills of Pavagadh, and extending into the city of Champaner.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Champaner is then described as 'a city which was founded by Vanraj Chavda', so it is the historical 'city'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in Panchmahal district in Gujarat, India. (1)______ is situated near the historical (2)______ of Champaner, a city which was founded by Vanraj Chavda, the (3)______ prominent king of the Chavda Dynasty, in the 8th century. He named it (4)______ the name of his friend and general Champa, also known later as Champaraj. The heritage site is dotted with forts with bastions ranging (5)______ the hills of Pavagadh, and extending into the city of Champaner.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The superlative 'most prominent' singles Vanraj Chavda out among the kings of his dynasty; 'more' would need a comparison, and 'chief' and 'main' cannot qualify the adjective 'prominent'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in Panchmahal district in Gujarat, India. (1)______ is situated near the historical (2)______ of Champaner, a city which was founded by Vanraj Chavda, the (3)______ prominent king of the Chavda Dynasty, in the 8th century. He named it (4)______ the name of his friend and general Champa, also known later as Champaraj. The heritage site is dotted with forts with bastions ranging (5)______ the hills of Pavagadh, and extending into the city of Champaner.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: To name something 'after' a person is to give it that person's name.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in Panchmahal district in Gujarat, India. (1)______ is situated near the historical (2)______ of Champaner, a city which was founded by Vanraj Chavda, the (3)______ prominent king of the Chavda Dynasty, in the 8th century. He named it (4)______ the name of his friend and general Champa, also known later as Champaraj. The heritage site is dotted with forts with bastions ranging (5)______ the hills of Pavagadh, and extending into the city of Champaner.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Ranging from' pairs with 'extending into': the forts run from the hills of Pavagadh into the city.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. NEAT
questions.explanation: 'Neat' means tidy and orderly; its opposite is 'messy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. RESPONSIBLE
questions.explanation: 'Responsible' takes the negative prefix 'ir-', as many words beginning with 'r' do ('irregular', 'irrelevant'): 'irresponsible'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. Then he would give one leap, two leaps, through the snow, and sit up again on his hind legs and look all around. B. A grey hare lived in the woods near a village. C. Then he would prick up the other, jerk his whiskers, snuff, and sit up on his hind legs. D. During the winter, when night came, he would prick up one ear and listen.
questions.explanation: B introduces the grey hare; D says that at night he would prick up one ear, C that he would then prick up the other and sit up on his hind legs, and A that he would leap and 'sit up again': BDCA.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Act of giving up the throne
questions.explanation: 'Abdication' is a monarch's giving up of the throne. 'Renunciation' and 'abandonment' are the giving up of anything, and 'resignation' is the leaving of an office or job.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error. Despite of her tiredness Meera went into the kitchen to make some dinner for the children.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' takes no 'of' ('in spite of' does): 'Despite her tiredness'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. According to experts, some sectors remain ______ during these difficult times, including banking and financial services, FMCG, food and technology.
questions.explanation: 'Resilient' means able to withstand or recover quickly from difficulty, as sectors that hold up in hard times are. 'Redundant' means no longer needed, 'repentant' sorry and 'repugnant' offensive.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A person who is blamed for something that someone else has done
questions.explanation: A 'scapegoat' is someone made to take the blame for what others have done.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Witness' is spelt correctly; the others should be 'wealth', 'whimper' and 'wisdom'.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error. Yesterday I searched in every my cupboard for the shirt I couldn’t find.
questions.explanation: 'Every' cannot be followed by the possessive 'my': 'in every cupboard' (or 'in all my cupboards').

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. According to the EPR, the corporation expects such manufacturers to develop a collect back system for plastic waste. B. The Municipal Corporation has introduced the extended producers responsibility (EPR) for producers and generators of plastic waste. C. The producers are persons engaged in manufacture, or import of carry bags, multi-layered packaging and sheets, and persons using them. D. They must formulate a plan to collect re-usable waste generated from their products within a prescribed timeframe.
questions.explanation: B introduces the EPR, C defines the producers, A says what the EPR expects of 'such manufacturers', and D ('They must formulate a plan') adds what they must do: BCAD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. The firing of the missile “not only killed innocent persons and also” created political furore.
options: not only kill innocent persons and also
but killed innocent person and also
not only killed innocent persons but also
questions.explanation: 'Not only' pairs with 'but also', not 'and also': 'not only killed innocent persons but also created political furore'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom. Pull yourself together
questions.explanation: To 'pull yourself together' is to regain control of your feelings and calm down.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Sujata shared the results of her experiment with her colleagues.
options: The results of her experiment are being shared with her colleagues by Sujata.
The results of her experiment were shared with her colleagues by Sujata.
Her colleagues shared the results of her experiment with Sujata.
The results of her experiment can be shared with her colleagues by Sujata.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'shared' becomes 'were shared' with the plural subject 'the results': 'The results of her experiment were shared with her colleagues by Sujata.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. AURA
questions.explanation: An 'aura' is a distinctive quality or glow that seems to surround a person or thing, as a 'halo', a ring of light, does.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'tumultuous', meaning noisy and disorderly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. MANDIBLE
questions.explanation: The 'mandible' is the jaw, especially the lower jaw.

questions.text: Millions of years ago the Indian subcontinent was separated from the mainland by a large sea known as the:
questions.explanation: The Tethys Sea lay between Angaraland in the north and Gondwanaland, of which the Indian plate was part; as the plate drifted north, the sediments laid down in the Tethys were folded up into the Himalayas.

questions.text: Who among the following is NOT an Indian weightlifter?
questions.explanation: Dipika Pallikal is a squash player. Karnam Malleswari, the 2000 Olympic bronze medallist, Mirabai Chanu and Rakhi Haldar are weightlifters.

questions.text: The patriotic song ‘Sare Jahan Se Accha’ was composed by:
questions.explanation: Allama Muhammad Iqbal wrote the poem, published in the weekly 'Ittehad' in August 1904 as 'Tarana-e-Hindi'. Tagore wrote 'Jana Gana Mana', Bankim Chandra Chatterjee 'Vande Mataram' and Bismil Azimabadi 'Sarfaroshi ki tamanna'.

questions.text: Which of the following is a lever that can be moved in several directions to control the movement of an image on a computer monitor or similar display screen?
questions.explanation: A joystick is a lever that pivots in several directions to move a cursor or an image on screen, as in games and flight simulators.

questions.text: Who among the following won the ‘Man-of-the-Match’ award in the series-deciding third ODI in the three-match ODI series played between India and Australia in January 2020?
questions.explanation: Rohit Sharma made 119 and was Player of the Match as India chased down Australia's 286 at Bengaluru on 19 January 2020, winning the deciding ODI by seven wickets and the series 2-1.

questions.text: Which of the following best defines Net National Income?
questions.explanation: Net national income (net national product at market prices) is gross national product less depreciation, the capital used up in production; deducting net indirect taxes as well gives national income at factor cost. GDP less depreciation is net domestic product.

questions.text: Which of the following nation's Prime Minister resigned from his post on 15 January 2020, along with his cabinet after its President called for Constitutional Reforms?
questions.explanation: Dmitry Medvedev and his government resigned on 15 January 2020, the day President Vladimir Putin proposed amendments to Russia's constitution; Mikhail Mishustin succeeded him.

questions.text: Who among the following won the ‘2019 Man Booker International Prize’ for her book 'Celestial Bodies'?
questions.explanation: The Omani writer Jokha Alharthi won the 2019 Man Booker International Prize for 'Celestial Bodies', translated from Arabic by Marilyn Booth. Anna Burns won the 2018 Booker Prize for 'Milkman'.

questions.text: Which of the following converts analogue information into digital form?
questions.explanation: A digitiser, such as a graphics tablet, turns analogue input, like a drawing traced with a stylus, into digital data. A barcode reader reads printed codes, and a gamepad is a game controller.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is NOT true about compounds?
options: The composition of each new substance is always fixed.
The constituents can be separated only by chemical or electrochemical reactions.
Elements react to form new compounds.
questions.explanation: A compound has a fixed composition: its elements combine in a definite proportion by mass. It is a mixture whose composition can vary.

questions.text: Which of the following blood groups is called the ‘Universal Receiver’?
questions.explanation: AB+ blood has neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies in its plasma, and no anti-Rh antibodies, so it can receive red cells of any group; O− is the universal donor.

questions.text: ‘Mohiniyattam’, is a traditional dance which originated in the state of ______ in India.
questions.explanation: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance of Kerala, traditionally performed solo by women.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following years did Mahatma Gandhi launch Champaran Satyagraha?
questions.explanation: Gandhi took up the cause of the indigo farmers of Champaran, in Bihar, in 1917, his first satyagraha in India.

questions.text: As of January 2020, who among the following was the Chief Election Commissioner of India?
questions.explanation: Sunil Arora was Chief Election Commissioner from December 2018 to April 2021, so he held the post in January 2020. V S Sampath, H S Brahma and Om Prakash Rawat held it before him.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a good conductor of electricity?
questions.explanation: Bromine, a non-metal that is liquid at room temperature, is a poor conductor. Silver and copper are metals, among the best conductors, and graphite conducts because each carbon atom in it has a free electron.

questions.text: Which of the following is an economic system in which capital goods are owned by private individuals or businesses and the production of goods and services is based on supply and demand in the general market?
questions.explanation: Under capitalism the means of production are privately owned and output and prices are set by supply and demand in the market; a mixed economy combines private and public sectors.

questions.text: Ram Nath Kovind assumed office as the ___________ President of India on 25th July 2017.
questions.explanation: Ram Nath Kovind, sworn in on 25 July 2017, was the 14th President of India, succeeding Pranab Mukherjee, the 13th.

questions.text: Who among the following can be removed by the process of impeachment?
questions.explanation: Under Article 61 the President can be removed by impeachment for violation of the Constitution, on a charge passed by a majority of two-thirds of the total membership of each House of Parliament.

questions.text: The ______ layer is the upper limit of our atmosphere. It extends from the top of the thermosphere up to 10,000 km (6,200 miles).
questions.explanation: The exosphere, the outermost layer, thins out into space. The troposphere is the lowest layer, the mesosphere lies below the thermosphere, and the ionosphere is the ionised region within the mesosphere and thermosphere.

questions.text: Which of the following Himalayan regions is known as ‘Shivaliks’?
questions.explanation: The Shiwaliks, the southernmost range, are the Outer Himalayas; the Himachal is the Lesser Himalaya and the Himadri the Greater or Inner Himalaya.

questions.text: Which of the following nations has the most powerful passport in the world as per ‘Henley Passport Index 2020’?
questions.explanation: Japan's passport topped the Henley Passport Index of January 2020 with a score of 191, giving access to more destinations without a visa obtained in advance than any other; Singapore came second.

questions.text: Which of the following teams won the ‘FIH Series Finals Hockey Tournament’ in June 2019?
questions.explanation: India won the FIH Series Finals at Bhubaneswar in June 2019, beating South Africa 5-1 in the final.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian states does NOT share its boundaries with Nepal?
questions.explanation: Nepal borders five Indian states: Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Sikkim. Assam does not touch it.

questions.text: Who among the following won the 'BBC Sports Personality of the Year 2019' award?
questions.explanation: The England all-rounder Ben Stokes won BBC Sports Personality of the Year 2019, the year of England's World Cup win and his unbeaten 135 at Headingley in the Ashes.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was elected as the President of the Indian National Congress in the years 1938 and 1939?
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose presided over the Haripura session in 1938 and was re-elected in 1939, defeating Pattabhi Sitaramayya, before resigning that year after differences with Gandhi.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. It is also very sad that ill-treatment is meted out to one of your gifts, and everyone indulges in excess!” B. “I can’t take it anymore,” he complained. “People abuse me and exploit me, and there is no respect for me – no realisation that I am your prasadam to men! C. An ancient story tells us that the God of Food came before the Divine Presence, battered, exhausted, and downcast. D. The Lord smiled and said to him, “Those who abuse you and indulge in excess are destroying themselves.”
questions.explanation: C opens the story with the God of Food coming before the Divine Presence, B begins his complaint, A continues it, and D gives the Lord's reply: CBAD.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. I use baking soda to remove stains from my clothes.
options: Baking soda is being used by me to remove stains from my clothes.
Baking soda is used by me to remove stains from my clothes.
I have been using baking soda to remove stains from my clothes.
Baking soda was used by me to remove stains from my clothes.
questions.explanation: The simple present 'use' becomes 'is used' with the singular subject 'baking soda': 'Baking soda is used by me to remove stains from my clothes.'

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Aanya said, "I've made a rose and honey vanilla dessert for you."
options: Aanya told me that she had made a rose and honey vanilla dessert for me.
Aanya told me that she is making a rose and honey vanilla dessert for me.
Aanya told me that she would make a rose and honey vanilla dessert for her.
Aanya said to me that she was making a rose and honey vanilla dessert for me.
questions.explanation: In reported speech the present perfect 'I've made' becomes the past perfect 'she had made', and 'you' becomes 'me', the listener.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'intriguing', with a 'u' after the 'g'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One fireman died while 14 others had a narrow escape when a part of the factory-cum-outlet of a well-known battery (1)______ firm where they were battling a major (2)______ collapsed following a series of sudden explosions in west Delhi. The brave fireman who had joined the department last year and got married (3)______, was buried under a pile of debris following explosions which were (4)______ by a compressor burst. The fireman died due to (5)______ bleeding and smoke inhalation. It took firemen five hours to pull his body out of the debris.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 1.
questions.explanation: A 'battery manufacturing firm' is a firm that makes batteries; 'manufacturing' describes the kind of firm.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One fireman died while 14 others had a narrow escape when a part of the factory-cum-outlet of a well-known battery (1)______ firm where they were battling a major (2)______ collapsed following a series of sudden explosions in west Delhi. The brave fireman who had joined the department last year and got married (3)______, was buried under a pile of debris following explosions which were (4)______ by a compressor burst. The fireman died due to (5)______ bleeding and smoke inhalation. It took firemen five hours to pull his body out of the debris.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The firemen were battling a major 'blaze', a large and fierce fire.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One fireman died while 14 others had a narrow escape when a part of the factory-cum-outlet of a well-known battery (1)______ firm where they were battling a major (2)______ collapsed following a series of sudden explosions in west Delhi. The brave fireman who had joined the department last year and got married (3)______, was buried under a pile of debris following explosions which were (4)______ by a compressor burst. The fireman died due to (5)______ bleeding and smoke inhalation. It took firemen five hours to pull his body out of the debris.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 3.
questions.explanation: He had joined the department only last year and got married 'recently', a short time ago.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One fireman died while 14 others had a narrow escape when a part of the factory-cum-outlet of a well-known battery (1)______ firm where they were battling a major (2)______ collapsed following a series of sudden explosions in west Delhi. The brave fireman who had joined the department last year and got married (3)______, was buried under a pile of debris following explosions which were (4)______ by a compressor burst. The fireman died due to (5)______ bleeding and smoke inhalation. It took firemen five hours to pull his body out of the debris.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The explosions were 'triggered', that is set off, by a compressor burst.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One fireman died while 14 others had a narrow escape when a part of the factory-cum-outlet of a well-known battery (1)______ firm where they were battling a major (2)______ collapsed following a series of sudden explosions in west Delhi. The brave fireman who had joined the department last year and got married (3)______, was buried under a pile of debris following explosions which were (4)______ by a compressor burst. The fireman died due to (5)______ bleeding and smoke inhalation. It took firemen five hours to pull his body out of the debris.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Excessive' bleeding is bleeding beyond the normal amount. 'Exorbitant' is used of prices, and 'towering' and 'lavish' do not describe bleeding.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. I found the scene of some people making fun of a beggar quite ______.
questions.explanation: People mocking a beggar is a sight that causes disgust: 'repulsive'. 'Admirable' and 'sociable' go against the sense, and 'destructive' does not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. PROVOKE
questions.explanation: To 'provoke' is to stir up anger; to 'appease' is to calm or pacify. 'Encourage' and 'stimulate' are close to 'provoke', and 'beckon' means to signal someone to come.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. PREJUDICE
questions.explanation: 'Prejudice' is an unfair opinion formed in advance: 'bias'. 'Tolerance' and 'justice' are nearly opposite.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. A panel has been formed to look within the security needs of college students.
questions.explanation: To examine or investigate something is to 'look into' it, not 'look within': 'to look into the security needs of college students'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order. A. When we wish to achieve something, we cannot expect success in a moment. B. It is the same with any great achievement. C. It took several years to build Rome and bring it to the state of glory. D. Rome, the greatest city of ancient world was not built in a short time.
questions.explanation: D gives the saying that Rome was not built in a short time, C explains that it took several years, B extends this to any great achievement, and A applies it to us: DCBA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. She is quite capable of looking after herself, “aren't she”?
questions.explanation: A positive statement with 'is' takes the negative tag 'isn't' with the same subject pronoun: 'She is quite capable of looking after herself, isn't she?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Add insult to injury
options: Make a bad situation even worse
Say words that are very offensive
questions.explanation: To 'add insult to injury' is to make a bad situation even worse for someone.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. PERSECUTION
questions.explanation: 'Persecution' is cruel and unjust treatment of people, often for their beliefs or origin: 'oppression'. 'Affliction' is suffering in general, not ill-treatment by others.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Jump on the bandwagon
options: Get involved in an activity because it is likely to succeed
Do an activity that is fun
Do something because circumstances force you to
Get engaged in an activity that is very important
questions.explanation: To 'jump on the bandwagon' is to join an activity or cause because it is popular or looks likely to succeed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. Doctors at the AIIMS Trauma Centre managed to save the life of 12 year old archer Shivangini, “whose were struck” by an arrow in the neck during a practice session.
questions.explanation: 'Who' refers to the person, Shivangini, and the singular past passive is 'was struck': 'struck' is the past participle of 'strike', and 'striked' is not a word.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The scientist, who is known for his ______ ideas on space travel, is much admired.
questions.explanation: A scientist much admired for his ideas on space travel would have 'revolutionary' ones, that is new and far-reaching. 'Ridiculous' and 'malicious' ideas would not win admiration, and 'anarchist' does not describe them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. DISAPPROVE
questions.explanation: To 'disapprove' is to have an unfavourable opinion; to 'commend' is to praise. 'Refuse' and 'oppose' are close in sense to 'disapprove'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. One who tells future from the stars
questions.explanation: An astrologer claims to tell the future from the positions of the stars and planets. A philanthropist gives money to help others, and a miser hoards it.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Movement of people or animals from one area to another
questions.explanation: Migration is the movement of people or animals from one area to another. Acclimatisation is getting used to a new climate or place.

questions.text: In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The performance of our players is worst than I had expected.
questions.explanation: A comparison with 'than' needs the comparative 'worse', not the superlative 'worst': 'is worse than I had expected'.

questions.text: Where is Bishnupur, which is famous for terracotta temples, located?
questions.explanation: Bishnupur, in Bankura district of West Bengal, is known for the terracotta temples built by the Malla kings in the 17th and 18th centuries.

questions.text: How many members of the Rajya Sabha can be nominated by the President of India?
questions.explanation: Under Article 80 the President nominates 12 members of the Rajya Sabha with special knowledge or practical experience of literature, science, art and social service.

questions.text: Which of the following units is used for the measurement of Luminous Intensity?
questions.explanation: The candela is the SI unit of luminous intensity. The mole measures the amount of substance, the ampere electric current and the kelvin temperature.

questions.text: In January 2020, the Yashaswini Scheme for Women Entrepreneurship was launched in Goa. The scheme aims to support female Self Help Groups (SHGs) with interest-free loans up to:
questions.explanation: The Yashaswini scheme, launched near Panaji on 11 January 2020, offers women's self-help groups in Goa interest-free loans of up to ₹5 lakh.

questions.text: Which of the following elements occurs most abundantly in our universe?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe, making up about three-quarters of its ordinary matter by mass.

questions.text: Who among the following is credited with the discovery of neutrons?
questions.explanation: James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932 and received the Nobel Prize in Physics for it in 1935. J J Thomson discovered the electron, and Rutherford the atomic nucleus.

questions.text: Which of the following is a Rabi crop?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives wheat, the one option grown only as a rabi crop: it is sown in winter, from October to December, and harvested from April to June. Bajra and tur (arhar) are kharif crops, sown with the monsoon; NCERT also lists jowar among the kharif crops, though in the southern states it is sown in the rabi season too.

questions.text: In context of computing, what is the full form of URL?
questions.explanation: URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator, the address of a resource on the internet, such as a web page.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following freedom fighters was NOT involved in the Kakori Train Robbery?
questions.explanation: The Kakori train robbery of 9 August 1925 was carried out by revolutionaries of the Hindustan Republican Association, among them Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan and Chandrashekhar Azad. Bhagat Singh was not part of it.

questions.text: The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, lies towards the western margins of ______ hills.
questions.explanation: NCERT describes the Indian (Thar) Desert as lying towards the western margins of the Aravali hills.

questions.text: As of 15 January 2020, which of the following nations is the number one ranked team in the ‘ICC Men's T20I Team Rankings’?
questions.explanation: Pakistan was ranked first in the ICC Men's T20I Team Rankings in January 2020; Australia overtook it in the ICC's annual update of May 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following words was inserted in the Preamble by the Constitution (42nd Amendment) Act, 1976?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble. 'Justice', 'Liberty' and 'Equality' were there from the start.

questions.text: Which of the following is used to receive and send computer files over telephone lines?
questions.explanation: A modem (modulator-demodulator) turns a computer's digital signals into analogue ones that a telephone line can carry, and back again.

questions.text: Who among the following is responsible for preparation of National Income estimates in India?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the Central Statistical Organisation (CSO), which prepared India's national income estimates. In May 2019, before the exam was held (October 2020), it was merged with the NSSO into the National Statistical Office (NSO), which took over this work.

questions.text: Which of the following is a well known place for Chikankari embroidery?
questions.explanation: Chikankari, fine embroidery traditionally done in white thread on light cotton or muslin, is the best-known craft of Lucknow.

questions.text: As of 15 January 2020, who among the following was the number one ranked male tennis player in the ATP rankings?
questions.explanation: Rafael Nadal was ranked number one in the ATP rankings in January 2020; Novak Djokovic took the top place back in February 2020, after winning the Australian Open.

questions.text: Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India was invoked by the Kerala government to file a petition against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA) in the Supreme Court on 14 January 2020?
questions.explanation: Kerala filed an original suit against the CAA under Article 131, which gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction in disputes between the Centre and the states. It was the first state to challenge the Act in the Supreme Court.

questions.text: Who among the following wrote ‘Akbar Nama’?
questions.explanation: The 'Akbarnama', the official history of Akbar's reign, was written by his courtier Abul Fazl; its third volume is the 'Ain-i-Akbari'.

questions.text: Which of the following passes cuts through Pir Panjal range and links Manali and Leh by road?
questions.explanation: The Rohtang Pass, on the Pir Panjal range, carries the Manali-Leh road from the Kullu valley into Lahaul. The Banihal Pass, also in the Pir Panjal, links Jammu with Srinagar instead.

questions.text: Who among the following was the first non-Indian to receive the Bharat Ratna, the highest Indian honour that can be given to civilians?
questions.explanation: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, the 'Frontier Gandhi', received the Bharat Ratna in 1987, the first person who was not an Indian citizen to do so; Nelson Mandela received it in 1990.

questions.text: Who among the following won the ‘Golden Globe 2020 award’ for ‘Best Performance by an Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama’?
questions.explanation: Renée Zellweger won the 2020 Golden Globe for Best Performance by an Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama for playing Judy Garland in 'Judy'.

questions.text: Which of the following teams won the 2018-19 Santosh Trophy?
questions.explanation: Services won the 2018-19 Santosh Trophy, beating the hosts Punjab 1-0 in the final at Ludhiana in April 2019.
