questions.text: Which of the following is a tertiary economic activity?
questions.explanation: Tertiary activities provide services rather than goods, and trade is one of them. Farming and hunting are primary activities, and weaving, which makes a product, is secondary.

questions.text: Who among the following won ICC’s ‘Spirit of Cricket Award’ for the year 2019?
questions.explanation: Virat Kohli won the ICC Spirit of Cricket Award for 2019, announced in January 2020, for asking Indian fans at the World Cup to stop booing Steve Smith and applaud him instead.

questions.text: How many Indian biosphere reserves are included in the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves, as of October 2019?
questions.explanation: As of October 2019, 11 of India's 18 biosphere reserves were in UNESCO's World Network, the latest being Khangchendzonga, added in 2018. Panna joined in 2020.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. MALIGNANT
questions.explanation: 'Malignant' means harmful and likely to spread, as a tumour can be; its opposite is 'benign', harmless. 'Fatal' is close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. Some people think that the credit card culture encourages people to shop compulsively and merely ______ debts.
questions.explanation: Shopping compulsively makes people pile up debts: to 'accumulate' is to gather or build up. 'Formulate' means devise, 'stimulate' rouse and 'simulate' imitate.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. This winter ______ weather conditions have led people to remain indoors.
questions.explanation: 'Adverse' means unfavourable or harmful, as weather that keeps people indoors is. 'Averse' means unwilling ('averse to'), and 'traverse' and 'inverse' do not fit.

questions.text: In the given sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. A Royal Bengal tigress and her three cubs was poison and their carcasses left to rot in the Wildlife Sanctuary in Goa.
options: and their carcasses left to rot
in the Wildlife Sanctuary in Goa
and her three cubs was poison
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'a tigress and her three cubs' takes 'were', and the passive needs the past participle: 'and her three cubs were poisoned'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One complaint parents and teachers have about children these days is that they are simply not interested in (1)______. In his weekly column ‘Down in Jungle land’ Ranjit Lal, an (2)______ offers some useful suggestions. Keeping a dog or cat as a pet (3)______ to be made mandatory. Regular visits to national parks and (4)______ are another way to get children hooked. Treks in wilderness areas are even (5)______ as children can then engage with all kinds of life-forms on their turf.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The column's suggestions (pets, national parks, treks) aim to bring children closer to the natural world, so the noun 'nature' fits after 'interested in'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One complaint parents and teachers have about children these days is that they are simply not interested in (1)______. In his weekly column ‘Down in Jungle land’ Ranjit Lal, an (2)______ offers some useful suggestions. Keeping a dog or cat as a pet (3)______ to be made mandatory. Regular visits to national parks and (4)______ are another way to get children hooked. Treks in wilderness areas are even (5)______ as children can then engage with all kinds of life-forms on their turf.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'An' needs a noun for a person, beginning with a vowel sound, to describe Ranjit Lal: 'an environmentalist'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One complaint parents and teachers have about children these days is that they are simply not interested in (1)______. In his weekly column ‘Down in Jungle land’ Ranjit Lal, an (2)______ offers some useful suggestions. Keeping a dog or cat as a pet (3)______ to be made mandatory. Regular visits to national parks and (4)______ are another way to get children hooked. Treks in wilderness areas are even (5)______ as children can then engage with all kinds of life-forms on their turf.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Needs to be made mandatory' says it ought to be compulsory; 'can', 'will' and 'must' would take the bare 'be', not 'to be'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One complaint parents and teachers have about children these days is that they are simply not interested in (1)______. In his weekly column ‘Down in Jungle land’ Ranjit Lal, an (2)______ offers some useful suggestions. Keeping a dog or cat as a pet (3)______ to be made mandatory. Regular visits to national parks and (4)______ are another way to get children hooked. Treks in wilderness areas are even (5)______ as children can then engage with all kinds of life-forms on their turf.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Places visited along with national parks: 'sanctuaries', protected areas for wildlife, plural like 'national parks' (a singular 'sanctuary' would need an article). 'Sanctity' means holiness, and 'sanctorum' is found only in 'sanctum sanctorum'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One complaint parents and teachers have about children these days is that they are simply not interested in (1)______. In his weekly column ‘Down in Jungle land’ Ranjit Lal, an (2)______ offers some useful suggestions. Keeping a dog or cat as a pet (3)______ to be made mandatory. Regular visits to national parks and (4)______ are another way to get children hooked. Treks in wilderness areas are even (5)______ as children can then engage with all kinds of life-forms on their turf.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Even' goes with a comparative, and the sentence praises treks: they are 'even better' than visits to parks, as children meet wildlife on its own ground.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Bite off more than one can chew
options: To cheat someone and get away
To eat quickly and run away
To take on more than one can deal with
questions.explanation: To 'bite off more than one can chew' is to take on more than one can manage.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. OPULENT
questions.explanation: 'Opulent' means rich and lavish: 'luxurious'. 'Shabby' is nearly its opposite, and 'virulent' means poisonous or bitterly hostile.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. The Arabian Sea region is very important for India as several major ports “are locating” there.
questions.explanation: The ports are situated there, a state rather than an action, so the passive 'are located' is needed: 'several major ports are located there'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Very careful and precise
questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' means very careful and precise about details. 'Tremulous' means trembling, 'tumultuous' noisy and disorderly, and 'garrulous' too talkative.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'deceive': 'e' before 'i' after 'c'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A natural skill at doing something
questions.explanation: A 'knack' is a natural skill or aptitude for doing something.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. For example, our project files were kept pending for a few years. B. However, such hindrances did not stop us from tirelessly working towards the establishment of 450 clinics. C. We initially constructed over 150 clinics. D. But very soon many roadblocks were put in our path of expansion.
questions.explanation: C states the first achievement (150 clinics), D says roadblocks soon followed, A gives an example of them, and B says the hindrances did not stop the work: CDAB.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. Some returned in the 80’s but they were not allowed to reclaim or buy land. B. In the 70’s many Vietnamese living in Cambodia faced deportation after a change in government. C. Their only solution was to live in wooden homes floating on the lake. D. Even today they can be found living on the lake surviving on fishing and tourism.
questions.explanation: B begins with the deportations of the 1970s, A tells of those who returned in the 1980s but could not own land, C gives their only way out (homes floating on the lake), and D says they live there even today: BACD.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Ravi asked, “Ritu, how many sets of class 12 practice papers have you finished?”
options: Ravi asked Ritu how many sets of class 12 practice papers she had finished.
Ravi asked Ritu how many sets of class 12 practice papers was she finishing.
Ravi asked Ritu how many sets of class 12 practice papers had she been finishing.
Ravi asked Ritu how many sets of class 12 practice papers she has been finishing.
questions.explanation: In reported speech the question takes statement order (subject before verb, no question mark), 'you' becomes 'she', and the present perfect 'have finished' moves back to the past perfect 'had finished'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. ENRAGE
questions.explanation: To 'enrage' is to make very angry: 'infuriate'. 'Placate' and 'alleviate' mean soothe and ease, nearly the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Like talking to a brick wall
questions.explanation: Talking to someone is 'like talking to a brick wall' when they pay no attention and give no response: the listener is inattentive.

questions.text: In the given sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Scientist have recently announced that a more effective antidote for snakebite venom has been made.
options: for snakebite venom has been made
questions.explanation: 'Have' needs a plural subject: 'Scientists have recently announced'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. DIVERSE
questions.explanation: 'Diverse' means varied, unlike one another; its opposite is 'identical', exactly alike.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. Rains lashed Delhi and brought the temperature down by a few degrees.
options: Delhi was lashed by rains and the temperature was brought down by a few degrees.
Delhi was being lashed by rain and the temperature was being brought down by a few degrees.
Delhi had been lashed by rain and the temperature had been brought down by a few degrees.
Delhi is being lashed by rain and the temperature was brought down by a few degrees.
questions.explanation: Both active verbs are in the simple past, so both become 'was' + past participle: 'Delhi was lashed by rains and the temperature was brought down by a few degrees.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. Sele, is a near extinct language, “spoken for” just five villages in Nepal, which lie close to Tibet.
questions.explanation: A language is spoken 'in' a place: 'spoken in just five villages in Nepal'.

questions.text: Who is the only Indian to have won the United Nations Award in the field of human rights?
questions.explanation: Baba Amte, who worked for people with leprosy at Anandwan in Maharashtra, received the United Nations Prize in the Field of Human Rights in 1988.

questions.text: What is the full form of PROM?
questions.explanation: PROM is programmable read-only memory: a blank chip that can be written (burned) once, after which it can only be read.

questions.text: Who described the preamble of Indian Constitution as the 'Political horoscope of the Indian Constitution'?
questions.explanation: K M Munshi of the Drafting Committee called the Preamble the 'horoscope' of the sovereign democratic republic. Thakurdas Bhargava called it the soul of the Constitution, and N A Palkhivala its identity card.

questions.text: Who won the ‘Most Valuable Player of the Series’ award in IPL 2019?
questions.explanation: Andre Russell of Kolkata Knight Riders was named the Most Valuable Player of IPL 2019 for his hitting and bowling.

questions.text: ‘Mayurbhanj Chhau’ is a folk dance form of which state?
questions.explanation: Chhau has three styles, named after where they are danced: Mayurbhanj in Odisha, Seraikela in Jharkhand and Purulia in West Bengal. Mayurbhanj Chhau is danced without masks.

questions.text: Which river originates from Tibet and enters India through Arunachal Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra rises in Tibet, where it is called the Yarlung Tsangpo, and enters India in Arunachal Pradesh as the Siang (Dihang).

questions.text: How many districts of Uttar Pradesh started the second phase of Mission Indradhanush 2.0 at the block level on 7 January 2020?
questions.explanation: All India Radio reported on 7 January 2020 that the second round of Intensified Mission Indradhanush 2.0 had begun at block level in 35 districts of Uttar Pradesh. IMI 2.0, launched in October 2019, ran in rounds from December 2019 to March 2020 to immunise children and pregnant women missed by routine immunisation in districts with low coverage.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which battle did Ahmad Shah Abdali defeat the Marathas?
questions.explanation: Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated the Marathas at the Third Battle of Panipat on 14 January 1761.

questions.text: Which company was ranked as the largest profit making PSU in India for the fiscal year 2018-2019?
questions.explanation: The Public Enterprises Survey 2018-19 ranked ONGC as the most profitable central public sector enterprise that year, followed by Indian Oil and NTPC.

questions.text: Garo-Khasi range is located in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: The Garo, Khasi and Jaintia Hills form the Meghalaya plateau.

questions.text: Who was the first Asian player to win the Junior Wimbledon's Boys singles title?
questions.explanation: Ramanathan Krishnan won the Wimbledon boys' singles title in 1954, the first Asian player to do so.

questions.text: Which law states that the volume of an ideal gas at constant pressure is directly proportional to the absolute temperature?
questions.explanation: Charles's law: at constant pressure the volume of a gas is proportional to its absolute temperature. Boyle's law relates volume to pressure at constant temperature, and Avogadro's law volume to the amount of gas.

questions.text: On August 2019, Rambir Singh Khokhar won the ‘Dronacharya award’ in the lifetime category for his contribution in ______.
questions.explanation: Rambir Singh Khokhar, a kabaddi coach, received the Dronacharya Award in the lifetime category in August 2019.

questions.text: Which is the tallest waterfall of India with a height of 1,493 ft?
questions.explanation: Kunchikal Falls, formed by the Varahi river in Shivamogga (Shimoga) district, Karnataka, drops about 455 m (1,493 ft) in a series of cascades and is usually listed as India's highest waterfall.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who threw a bomb in the central legislative assembly along with Bhagat Singh to protest against the Public Safety Bill in 1929?
questions.explanation: Batukeshwar Dutt and Bhagat Singh threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April 1929 and courted arrest, in protest against the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill.

questions.text: On 30 October 2019, CBSE and NCERT, New Delhi developed an Aptitude Test for Senior School Students. What is the name of that test?
questions.explanation: Tamanna (Try And Measure Aptitude And Natural Abilities) is the aptitude test CBSE and NCERT developed to help students of Classes 9 and 10 choose their subjects; there is no pass or fail.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which Indian social activist and politician led the Self-Respect Movement or Dravidian Movement against Brahminism?
questions.explanation: E V Ramasamy, 'Periyar', started the Self-Respect Movement in 1925 against caste and Brahmin dominance. C N Annadurai later founded the DMK, and P Theagaraya Chetty was a founder of the Justice Party.

questions.text: The novel 'Quichotte' was shortlisted for the ‘2019 Booker Prize’. Who is the author of this book?
questions.explanation: 'Quichotte', Salman Rushdie's novel modelled on Cervantes's 'Don Quixote', was on the 2019 Booker Prize shortlist.

questions.text: Which sanctuary is famous for endangered Estuarine Crocodiles conservation in India?
questions.explanation: Bhitarkanika in Odisha's Kendrapara district, a mangrove wetland, is known for its estuarine (saltwater) crocodiles.

questions.text: Which of the following eye disorders is known as ‘lazy eye’?
questions.explanation: Amblyopia, or lazy eye, is poor vision in one eye because the brain favours the other eye in childhood. Myopia is short sight, hypermetropia long sight, and presbyopia the loss of near focus with age.

questions.text: In which year did UNESCO include Yoga in its Intangible Cultural Heritage list?
questions.explanation: UNESCO inscribed yoga on its Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in December 2016.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the given sentence which contains the grammatical error. If India will win this match they will win the series.
questions.explanation: In a first conditional the 'if' clause takes the simple present, not 'will': 'If India wins this match, they will win the series.'

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Placque' is misspelt: the word is 'plaque', a flat tablet fixed to a wall, or the film that forms on teeth.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement’. As we’ve been neighbours, I have known Mrs. Shashi Singh “since more than 16 years”.
questions.explanation: 'For' goes with a length of time ('for more than 16 years'); 'since' goes with a point in time ('since 2004').

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A collection of drawings, documents, etc. That represent a person's, especially an artist's, work
questions.explanation: A portfolio is a set of drawings, photographs or documents that shows a person's, especially an artist's, work. A dossier is a file of papers on one person or subject, and a profile a short description of someone.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in India located near Hospet town in the Karnataka state, India. (1)______ the attractions of Hampi (2)______ beautiful temples, ruins of palaces (3)______ of aquatic structures, ancient market streets, royal pavilions, bastions, royal platforms, treasury buildings...the list is practically (4)______. Most of the visitors to Hampi arrive at the well-connected Hospet Junction railway station, (5)______ about 13km from Hampi. Roads to Hampi are in great shape. Driving all the way to Hampi from the neighbouring cities is not a bad idea either.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Among the attractions of Hampi are ...' introduces some of its many attractions; 'aside', 'along' and 'away' do not fit before 'the attractions'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in India located near Hospet town in the Karnataka state, India. (1)______ the attractions of Hampi (2)______ beautiful temples, ruins of palaces (3)______ of aquatic structures, ancient market streets, royal pavilions, bastions, royal platforms, treasury buildings...the list is practically (4)______. Most of the visitors to Hampi arrive at the well-connected Hospet Junction railway station, (5)______ about 13km from Hampi. Roads to Hampi are in great shape. Driving all the way to Hampi from the neighbouring cities is not a bad idea either.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The sentence is inverted: its subject is the list that follows ('beautiful temples, ruins of palaces ...'), which is plural and described in the present: 'are'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in India located near Hospet town in the Karnataka state, India. (1)______ the attractions of Hampi (2)______ beautiful temples, ruins of palaces (3)______ of aquatic structures, ancient market streets, royal pavilions, bastions, royal platforms, treasury buildings...the list is practically (4)______. Driving all the way to Hampi from the neighbouring cities is not a bad idea either.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Remains' are what is left of old buildings, which sits with 'ruins of palaces': 'remains of aquatic structures'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in India located near Hospet town in the Karnataka state, India. Driving all the way to Hampi from the neighbouring cities is not a bad idea either.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: A list that goes on and on is 'practically endless'; the dots before it point the same way.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Hampi is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in India located near Hospet town in the Karnataka state, India. (1)______ the attractions of Hampi (2)______ beautiful temples, ruins of palaces (3)______ of aquatic structures, ancient market streets, royal pavilions, bastions, royal platforms, treasury buildings...the list is practically (4)______. Driving all the way to Hampi from the neighbouring cities is not a bad idea either.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Located' is the word for where a building or place lies: the station is situated about 13 km from Hampi.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. DISCLOSE
questions.explanation: To 'disclose' is to make known; to 'conceal' is to keep hidden. To 'disguise' is to change how something looks, and to 'disrupt' is to interrupt.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. CONSTRAINT
questions.explanation: A 'constraint' is a limit or restriction on what can be done, a form of 'control'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A group of ships sailing together
questions.explanation: A fleet is a group of ships sailing together. A navy is a country's whole sea force, and vessels and cruisers are ships.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. “Today, respect is shown in different ways,” she said, “students have a more questioning bent of mind.” B. Vidya Subramaniam occupies a small but privileged place in the dance world that has seen the old guard giving place to the new. C. Back in the day, respect meant not sitting on even the same level as one’s gurus but that’s no longer true, especially for those who live in Western milieus. D. For instance, she spoke of how the very idea of ‘respect’ has changed over time.
questions.explanation: B introduces Vidya Subramaniam; D says she spoke of how the idea of 'respect' has changed; C says what respect meant in the past, and A, in her words, what it means today: BDCA.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Intention' is spelt correctly; the others should be 'transition', 'injection' and 'fashion'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement’. Finally, Ananya found her pet kitten “over the top branch of a tree” in their garden.
options: on the top branch of the tree
in a top branch of a tree
across the top branch in the tree
questions.explanation: 'On' is for something supported by a surface, 'over' for something above it: the kitten was 'on the top branch of the tree'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank in the given sentence. Timers at traffic signals, that help motorists save fuel by switching off their engines while waiting, will soon be phased out due to technical ______.
questions.explanation: 'Glitches' are sudden faults or malfunctions, a technical reason for taking the timers out of use.

questions.text: Select the option that is the passive form of the given sentence. She did not forget me even though I have been away for a year.
options: Even though I have been away for a year she did not forget me.
I have not been forgotten even though I have been away for a year.
Though I have been away for a year she has not forgot me.
Even though I have been away for a year she had not been forgotten.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the only option that makes 'me' the passive subject 'I' and keeps the rest of the sentence: 'she did not forget me' and 'she has not forgot me' are still active, and 'she had not been forgotten' makes her the one forgotten. Strictly, the simple past 'did not forget' would become 'I was not forgotten (by her)', which no option gives.

questions.text: Select the option that is the direct form of the given sentence. Brinda told her doctor that she was leaving for Boston the next day.
options: Brinda told her doctor, “I was leaving for Boston tomorrow”.
Brinda said to her doctor, “I am leaving for Boston tomorrow.”
Brinda had told her doctor, “She was leaving for Boston the next day”.
Brinda told to her doctor, “I will be leaving for Boston the next day”.
questions.explanation: In direct speech 'told' becomes 'said to', 'she' becomes 'I', the past 'was leaving' goes back to the present 'am leaving', and 'the next day' becomes 'tomorrow'.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the given sentence which contains the grammatical error. I don’t recognise none of the politicians who have been invited to be the speakers today.
questions.explanation: 'Don't' and 'none' make a double negative: 'I don't recognise any of the politicians ...'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. It took Rohan a long time to “get the hang of” the machine in the new factory.
questions.explanation: To 'get the hang of' something is to learn how to do or use it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Fit as a fiddle
questions.explanation: 'Fit as a fiddle' means in very good health: healthy and strong.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. ALTRUISTIC
questions.explanation: 'Altruistic' means caring unselfishly for others, so its opposite is 'selfish'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. He put it down to dry and went to count his coins. B. When he came back, it seemed like the teapot had moved. C. Akito walked into an old curiosity shop and bought a teapot and took it home. D. Later that day, he cleaned the teapot till it shone like the sun.
questions.explanation: C: Akito buys a teapot and takes it home; D: later that day he cleans it; A: he puts it down to dry and goes off; B: when he comes back it seems to have moved: CDAB.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. FOLIAGE
questions.explanation: 'Foliage' is the leaves of plants taken together: 'greenery'.

questions.text: Which Chola ruler was popularly called ‘Victor of the Ganges’?
questions.explanation: Rajendra Chola I sent an army north to the Ganga and took the title 'Gangaikonda Chola', building a new capital named Gangaikonda Cholapuram.

questions.text: Which of the following is a famous fossil site in India where a full-fledged skeleton of a dinosaur was found?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Wadadham (Wadadam), in Sironcha taluka of Gadchiroli district, Maharashtra, a Jurassic site in the Godavari basin where dinosaur fossils and fossil trees have been found. The complete skeleton usually mentioned with it was found in 1959 at nearby Kothapalli-Pochampally and is kept in Kolkata; Hathnora is known for the 'Narmada Man' skull.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which governor general of India abolished Sati system in 1829 by declaring it an offence?
questions.explanation: Lord William Bentinck's Bengal Sati Regulation (Regulation XVII of 1829) declared sati illegal and punishable in the courts.

questions.text: ‘Sattriya’ is a traditional Hindu classical dance form of which state?
questions.explanation: Sattriya was created by the Vaishnava saint Srimanta Sankardev and kept alive in Assam's sattras (monasteries); the Sangeet Natak Akademi recognised it as a classical dance in 2000.

questions.text: How many agro-climatic zones (ACZ) are characterised by the Planning Commission of India?
questions.explanation: The Planning Commission divided India into 15 agro-climatic regions on the basis of physiography, soils, climate and cropping patterns, for regional agricultural planning.

questions.text: What is the mission life of the Cartosat-3 satellite launched by PSLV C-47 on 27 November 2019?
questions.explanation: ISRO gave Cartosat-3, its third-generation Earth-imaging satellite launched by PSLV-C47 from Sriharikota, a mission life of 5 years.

questions.text: When was the Backward and Minority Communities Employees Federation (BAMCEF) established in India?
questions.explanation: BAMCEF, set up by Kanshi Ram with D. K. Khaparde and Dinabhana, was formally launched in Delhi on 6 December 1978, B. R. Ambedkar's death anniversary.

questions.text: Which famous personality said the following? “Don't take rest after your first victory because if you fail in second, more lips are waiting to say that your first victory was just luck?”
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, to whom this line is widely attributed in collections of his sayings.

questions.text: Which function key displays the Print Preview window in Microsoft Office?
questions.explanation: In Microsoft Word and Excel, Ctrl + F2 opens the print preview (in recent versions, the Print pane of the File tab).

questions.text: In 1930, which scientist was awarded the Nobel Prize for describing the human ABO blood group system?
questions.explanation: Karl Landsteiner received the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering the human blood groups. Albert Claude, Roger Guillemin and George Wald won it for work on the cell, brain hormones and vision.

questions.text: India shares its land boundaries with which countries in the east?
questions.explanation: India's land neighbours are Pakistan and Afghanistan in the north-west, China, Nepal and Bhutan in the north, and Myanmar and Bangladesh in the east.

questions.text: Cinnabar (HgS) is an ore of which metal?
questions.explanation: Cinnabar, mercury(II) sulphide, is the chief ore of mercury; roasting it in air frees the metal.

questions.text: Which Indian writer was awarded the ‘Rabindranath Tagore Literary Prize 2019’?
questions.explanation: Rana Dasgupta won the 2019 Rabindranath Tagore Literary Prize for his novel 'Solo'.

questions.text: The Maharaja Ranjit Singh Gold Cup is associated with ______.
questions.explanation: The Maharaja Ranjit Singh Gold Cup is a hockey tournament. It is not to be confused with cricket's Ranji Trophy, named after K. S. Ranjitsinhji.

questions.text: In which state was the 8th edition of the India-China joint training exercise 'Hand-in-Hand 2019’ held?
questions.explanation: The eighth India-China exercise Hand-in-Hand was held at Umroi, Meghalaya, from 7 to 20 December 2019, with counter-terrorism as its theme.

questions.text: How many elements of India were listed in the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity as of March 2018?
questions.explanation: By March 2018 India had 13 elements on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, the 13th being the Kumbh Mela, inscribed in December 2017.

questions.text: In which year did the JavaScript Programming language come into existence?
questions.explanation: Brendan Eich created JavaScript at Netscape in 1995; it was first called Mocha and then LiveScript.

questions.text: Which of the following companies was conferred with Maharatna status in October 2019?
questions.explanation: In October 2019 the Department of Public Enterprises granted Maharatna status to Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited and to Power Grid Corporation. BPCL, GAIL and SAIL were already Maharatnas.

questions.text: Which Indian banknote released in November 2016 features Mangalyaan on the reverse side?
questions.explanation: The ₹2,000 note of the Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series, issued in November 2016, carries a motif of Mangalyaan, the Mars Orbiter Mission, on its reverse; the new ₹500 note shows the Red Fort.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of the most explosive type of volcano?
questions.explanation: NCERT calls calderas the most explosive of the earth's volcanoes: they erupt so violently that they collapse on themselves instead of building a tall cone. Shield and flood basalt volcanoes pour out fluid lava with little explosion.

questions.text: Which former Indian cricketer was honored with the ‘Bharat Gaurav Award’ by the East Bengal Football Club in 2019?
questions.explanation: East Bengal Club gave its highest honour, the Bharat Gaurav, to Kapil Dev on its Foundation Day in August 2019.

questions.text: Who was conferred with the ‘Female Sportsperson of the Year’ award at the ‘FICCI India Sports Awards 2019’?
questions.explanation: Rani Rampal, captain of India's women's hockey team, was named female sportsperson of the year at the FICCI India Sports Awards in December 2019; the shooter Saurabh Chaudhary won the male award.

questions.text: As per ‘India State of Forest Report 2019’, which state secured first position for the highest growth in forest area in the country?
questions.explanation: The India State of Forest Report 2019 put Karnataka first for the increase in forest cover (1,025 km²), followed by Andhra Pradesh (990 km²) and Kerala (823 km²).

questions.text: When was the first Constituent Assembly election held in India?
questions.explanation: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan, members of the Constituent Assembly were elected in July 1946 by the provincial legislative assemblies.

questions.text: How many parathyroid glands are present on the back side of the thyroid gland in humans?
questions.explanation: Humans have four parathyroid glands on the back of the thyroid, one pair in each of its two lobes; they secrete parathyroid hormone, which raises blood calcium.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Business' is spelt correctly. The others should be 'restaurant', 'memoir' and 'studious'.

questions.text: Select the synonym of the given word. Nebulous
questions.explanation: 'Nebulous' means unclear or ill-defined, as an idea or plan can be: 'vague'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. METROPOLITAN
questions.explanation: 'Metropolitan' describes a big city and its sophisticated ways; its opposite is 'provincial', of the regions outside the capital and often narrow in outlook.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. A city, predominantly made of red sandstone, Fatehpur Sikri (1)______ founded in the 16th century by the Mughal Emperor, Akbar. It is essentially a fortified city (2)______ had been the capital of Akbar (3)______ fifteen years. Now a UNESCO world heritage site (4)______ a famous tourist attraction, it is a fine (5)______ of Mughal architecture.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'Fatehpur Sikri' takes the past passive 'was founded': it was founded in the 16th century.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. A city, predominantly made of red sandstone, Fatehpur Sikri (1)______ founded in the 16th century by the Mughal Emperor, Akbar. It is essentially a fortified city (2)______ had been the capital of Akbar (3)______ fifteen years. Now a UNESCO world heritage site (4)______ a famous tourist attraction, it is a fine (5)______ of Mughal architecture.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun for a thing is 'which': 'a fortified city which had been the capital of Akbar'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. A city, predominantly made of red sandstone, Fatehpur Sikri (1)______ founded in the 16th century by the Mughal Emperor, Akbar. It is essentially a fortified city (2)______ had been the capital of Akbar (3)______ fifteen years. Now a UNESCO world heritage site (4)______ a famous tourist attraction, it is a fine (5)______ of Mughal architecture.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'For' goes with a length of time: 'for fifteen years'. 'Since' and 'from' need a starting point.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. A city, predominantly made of red sandstone, Fatehpur Sikri (1)______ founded in the 16th century by the Mughal Emperor, Akbar. It is essentially a fortified city (2)______ had been the capital of Akbar (3)______ fifteen years. Now a UNESCO world heritage site (4)______ a famous tourist attraction, it is a fine (5)______ of Mughal architecture.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'And' joins two descriptions that sit together: 'a UNESCO world heritage site and a famous tourist attraction'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. A city, predominantly made of red sandstone, Fatehpur Sikri (1)______ founded in the 16th century by the Mughal Emperor, Akbar. It is essentially a fortified city (2)______ had been the capital of Akbar (3)______ fifteen years. Now a UNESCO world heritage site (4)______ a famous tourist attraction, it is a fine (5)______ of Mughal architecture.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: A building that shows a style well is 'a fine example' of it: 'a fine example of Mughal architecture'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Lasting for a very short time
questions.explanation: 'Ephemeral' means lasting for a very short time. 'Infinite' and 'endless' mean the opposite, and 'illusory' means not real.

questions.text: Select the option that is the passive form of the given sentence. The police brought a search warrant when they raided his house.
options: A search warrant was brought by the police when they raided his house.
A search warrant was brought when they raided his house by the police.
The police had raided his house and brought a search warrant.
A search warrant had been brought when the police raided his house.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'brought' becomes 'was brought' with the subject 'a search warrant', and 'by the police' follows the verb; the 'when' clause stays as it is.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. INSTANT
questions.explanation: 'Instant' means happening at once; its opposite is 'gradual', happening slowly over time. 'Prompt' is close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. “Since it falls” on the floor, her dog, a black Labrador, gulped the biscuit down.
questions.explanation: The main verb 'gulped' is in the past, so the reason clause must be in the past too: 'Since it fell on the floor'.

questions.text: Select the option that is the direct form of the given sentence. Nidhi exclaimed that it was a beautiful painting.
options: Nidhi said to the artist, “That looks like a beautiful painting!”
Nidhi said to the artist in surprise, “How beautiful you made that painting!”
Nidhi told him in wonder, “How beautiful!”
questions.explanation: 'Exclaimed that it was a beautiful painting' reports an exclamation, which in direct speech is 'What a beautiful painting!'

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Supportors' is misspelt: the word is 'supporters'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Tending to associate with others of one's kind
questions.explanation: 'Gregarious' describes people or animals that like to be with others of their kind. 'Genial' means friendly and cheerful, and 'harmonious' and 'congruous' mean in agreement.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. Akshay is likely to “take the heat” for having miscalculated the expenses.
questions.explanation: To 'take the heat' is to face criticism or blame for something: here, for the miscalculated expenses.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom. To have a gut feeling
options: To have pain in the abdomen
To feel an instinct or intuition
questions.explanation: A 'gut feeling' is an instinctive sense that something is true, without any reasoning behind it.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. They grew cabbages and carrots in their back yard. B. The family was very poor and was always hungry because there was a war on. C. They also had a chicken, which provided the family with eggs, but still they were hungry. D. Their country had been invaded by a foreign army.
questions.explanation: B introduces the poor, hungry family and the war, and D explains the war (the country had been invaded). A says what they grew, and C, with 'also', adds the chicken and ends on their hunger: BDAC.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. I sow a seed. B. I saw the sapling. C. I saw the sprout. D. I saw the plant.
questions.explanation: A plant grows from a seed to a sprout, then a sapling and then a full plant: ACBD.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the given sentence which contains the grammatical error. Most of voters in Taiwan seem to have once again voted for the democratic party and President Tsai Ing-wen.
questions.explanation: 'Most of' needs a determiner before the noun: 'Most of the voters', or simply 'Most voters'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank in the given sentence. The performances of the notable dancers and guest artists ______ the audience.
questions.explanation: To 'enthral' is to captivate and delight, which is what fine performances do to an audience. 'Immersed' and 'absorbed' are normally said of the audience itself ('absorbed in the performance'), and 'occupied' does not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. This is a class “who is expected to do” exceptionally well in the quiz next week.
options: which are expecting to be doing
questions.explanation: 'Class' here is a group taken as one unit, not a person, so it takes 'which' and a singular verb: 'This is a class which is expected to do exceptionally well'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. RIND
questions.explanation: The 'rind' is the tough outer skin of a fruit such as an orange or a melon: its 'peel'.

questions.text: When was the ‘Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award’ instituted?
questions.explanation: The Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, India's highest sporting honour, was instituted in 1991-92; the chess player Viswanathan Anand was its first recipient. It was renamed the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna in 2021.

questions.text: Who was sworn in as the 11th Chief Minister of Jharkhand on 29 December 2019?
questions.explanation: Hemant Soren of the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha was sworn in as Chief Minister of Jharkhand on 29 December 2019, after his alliance won the state election; he succeeded Raghubar Das.

questions.text: As per state census 2011, which of the following is the least populous state of India?
questions.explanation: The 2011 Census counted about 6.1 lakh people in Sikkim, the fewest of any state.

questions.text: Which player became the first Indian brand ambassador of La Liga (the top tier of Spanish club football) in December 2019?
questions.explanation: In December 2019 La Liga named the cricketer Rohit Sharma its first brand ambassador in India; he was also the first non-footballer it had made a brand ambassador anywhere.

questions.text: On December 2019, the Prime Minister of ______ announced the commencement of the ‘Gandhi Citizenship Education Award’ to be given every year.
questions.explanation: Portugal's Prime Minister, António Costa, announced an annual Gandhi Citizenship Education Prize in December 2019, at a meeting of India's national committee for the 150th anniversary of Gandhi's birth.

questions.text: What was India’s rank in the world in terms of military power as per the ‘Global Firepower Nations Index 2019’?
questions.explanation: The Global Firepower index for 2019 ranked India's military fourth in the world, after the United States, Russia and China.

questions.text: Which festival marks the beginning of the Tibetan New Year?
questions.explanation: Losar is the Tibetan New Year festival. Saga Dawa marks the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and death, and Shoton is Lhasa's yoghurt festival.

questions.text: Which instrument records the waves reaching the surface during an earthquake?
questions.explanation: A seismograph records the seismic waves of an earthquake. A barograph records air pressure, a manometer measures the pressure of a fluid and a chronometer keeps precise time.

questions.text: Which scientist arranged the Periodic Table of Elements in the order of increasing atomic masses?
questions.explanation: Dmitri Mendeleev arranged the elements by increasing atomic mass in his periodic table of 1869. Henry Moseley later showed that atomic number is the better basis.

questions.text: What is the chemical name of ‘oil of vitriol’?
questions.explanation: 'Oil of vitriol' is the old name for concentrated sulfuric acid, H₂SO₄.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year did Motilal Nehru (Chairman) and eight other Congress leaders draft a constitution for India?
questions.explanation: The Nehru Report of 1928, drawn up by a committee chaired by Motilal Nehru, was a draft constitution for India that asked for dominion status.

questions.text: Which planet is made up of thick white and yellowish clouds of sulfuric acid?
questions.explanation: Venus is wrapped in thick clouds of sulfuric acid, which reflect most of the sunlight and make it the brightest planet in our sky.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
questions.explanation: When the exam was held, in October 2020, the Airports Authority of India was a Miniratna (Category I), not a Navratna. Indian Oil was a Maharatna, Hindustan Aeronautics a Navratna and BSNL a Miniratna (Category I).

questions.text: What is the provision of Article 49 of the Constitution of India?
options: Provision for free and compulsory education for children
Protection of monuments and places and objects of natural importance
Prohibition of employment of children (Under the age of 14) in factories and mines
Promotion of international peace and security
questions.explanation: Article 49, a Directive Principle, obliges the State to protect monuments, places and objects of artistic or historic interest declared to be of national importance (the option prints 'natural'). Child labour in factories and mines is barred by Article 24, and Article 51 promotes international peace and security.

questions.text: Which of the following temples has Panchayatana Style of architecture?
questions.explanation: The Gupta-period Dashavatara Temple at Deogarh is in the panchayatana style: a main shrine on a platform with four smaller shrines at its corners.

questions.text: In which language were the Mughal court chronicles written?
questions.explanation: Persian was the language of the Mughal court, and its chronicles, such as the Akbar Nama, were written in it.

questions.text: Which of the following prominent leaders wrote the book ‘Citizen Delhi: My Life, My Times’?
questions.explanation: Sheila Dikshit, Chief Minister of Delhi from 1998 to 2013, published her memoir in 2018 as 'Citizen Delhi: My Times, My Life' (the question swaps the two halves of the subtitle).

questions.text: Who designed the first analog computer in India?
questions.explanation: Samarendra Kumar Mitra designed and built India's first analog computer at the Indian Statistical Institute, Kolkata, in 1953-54.

questions.text: Which of the following monuments has NOT been notified as a National Geo-heritage Monument by the Geological Survey of India (GSI)?
options: Pillow Lava in lron Ore belt at Nomira, Odisha
Nagahill Ophiolite site near Pungro, Nagaland
Gingee Fort Villupuram District, Tamil Nadu
questions.explanation: The Geological Survey of India has notified the pillow lavas at Nomira, the Peninsular Gneiss at Lalbagh and the Nagahill ophiolite near Pungro as National Geo-heritage Monuments. Gingee Fort is a historical fort, not a geological site.

questions.text: In DASD, what is the full form of ‘A’?
questions.explanation: DASD stands for Direct Access Storage Device, such as a hard disk, where data can be reached directly rather than in sequence as on tape.

questions.text: Which child activist became the first Indian to be awarded the ‘Changemaker Award 2019’ (given by the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation) for her work towards abolition of child marriage in Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Payal Jangid of Rajasthan received the Gates Foundation's Changemaker Award at its Goalkeepers awards in September 2019 for her campaign against child marriage.

questions.text: Which former badminton player of India was awarded the ‘Sportstar Lifetime Achievement Award’ in February 2019?
questions.explanation: Prakash Padukone, the 1980 All England champion, received the Lifetime Achievement Award at the Sportstar Aces Awards in Mumbai in February 2019.

questions.text: Which Indian mountain looks like a giant pyramid and has a flat summit area and two peaks?
questions.explanation: Kamet (7,756 m), in the Garhwal Himalaya of Uttarakhand, rises like a giant pyramid topped by a flat summit area with two peaks.

questions.text: Which Indian economist was appointed as the Chief Economist of the World Bank from 2012 to 2016?
questions.explanation: Kaushik Basu was Chief Economist and Senior Vice-President of the World Bank from 2012 to 2016. Raghuram Rajan had earlier been the IMF's chief economist.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Up in arms
questions.explanation: To be 'up in arms' is to be angry about something and protesting against it.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. The police beat a number of protestors last night.
options: A number of protestors had been beaten by the police last night.
A number of protestors were being beaten by the police last night.
A number of protestors has been beaten by the police the night before.
A number of protestors were beaten by the police the night before.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the only option with the right passive verb: the simple past 'beat' becomes 'were beaten', plural to agree with 'a number of protestors'. It also changes 'last night' to 'the night before', which a change of voice does not call for, but the other options change the tense.

questions.text: Select the wrongly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'faithfully', with a double 'l'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. ASSERTION
questions.explanation: An assertion is a confident statement of a fact or belief: a 'declaration'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Smartphones have become an essential part of our lives and their (1)______ usage is now impacting human behaviour. We need to (2)______ think about digital detox! Yes, the concept of disconnecting with (3)______ virtual world is not just a fad. It’s the need of the hour today. The Global Brand Director of the smartphone Vivo in his speech nudged all smartphone users (4)______ a step backward and think. He said, “Let’s (5)______ our mobiles and pledge to be closer and nearer to our loved ones.”

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Usage' is a noun, so an adjective is needed: 'excessive usage', meaning too much use.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Smartphones have become an essential part of our lives and their (1)______ usage is now impacting human behaviour. We need to (2)______ think about digital detox! Yes, the concept of disconnecting with (3)______ virtual world is not just a fad. It’s the need of the hour today. The Global Brand Director of the smartphone Vivo in his speech nudged all smartphone users (4)______ a step backward and think. He said, “Let’s (5)______ our mobiles and pledge to be closer and nearer to our loved ones.”

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 2.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to describe the verb 'think': we need to 'seriously' think about a digital detox.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Smartphones have become an essential part of our lives and their (1)______ usage is now impacting human behaviour. We need to (2)______ think about digital detox! Yes, the concept of disconnecting with (3)______ virtual world is not just a fad. It’s the need of the hour today. The Global Brand Director of the smartphone Vivo in his speech nudged all smartphone users (4)______ a step backward and think. He said, “Let’s (5)______ our mobiles and pledge to be closer and nearer to our loved ones.”

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Virtual world' names one particular thing, the online world, so it takes 'the'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Smartphones have become an essential part of our lives and their (1)______ usage is now impacting human behaviour. We need to (2)______ think about digital detox! Yes, the concept of disconnecting with (3)______ virtual world is not just a fad. It’s the need of the hour today. The Global Brand Director of the smartphone Vivo in his speech nudged all smartphone users (4)______ a step backward and think. He said, “Let’s (5)______ our mobiles and pledge to be closer and nearer to our loved ones.”

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Nudge' takes an object and then 'to' with the base verb: 'nudged all smartphone users to take a step backward'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Smartphones have become an essential part of our lives and their (1)______ usage is now impacting human behaviour. We need to (2)______ think about digital detox! Yes, the concept of disconnecting with (3)______ virtual world is not just a fad. It’s the need of the hour today. The Global Brand Director of the smartphone Vivo in his speech nudged all smartphone users (4)______ a step backward and think. He said, “Let’s (5)______ our mobiles and pledge to be closer and nearer to our loved ones.”

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 5.
questions.explanation: To 'switch off' a mobile is to turn it off, which fits the pledge to be closer to loved ones.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. Lenovo has launched ThinkPad XI Fold, the world’s first foldable laptop which is claimed “to be so durable as” its other devices.
questions.explanation: A comparison of equality uses 'as ... as': 'claimed to be as durable as its other devices'.

questions.text: In the given sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. When I met Akbar Padamsee, one of a pioneers of Indian art, he was 87 but still alert and active.
options: one of a pioneers of Indian art
questions.explanation: 'One of' is followed by 'the' and a plural noun: 'one of the pioneers of Indian art'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. This test is conducted on the fully automated Driving Test Track designed by Maruti Suzuki. B. Each of these specific skills are to be tested and need to be completed successfully in under seven minutes by the candidate. C. It is a fully-automated track having six segments to test specific driving skills. D. The Regional Transport Offices of Delhi have recently introduced the new driving test.
questions.explanation: D introduces the new driving test, A says where it is conducted, C describes the track and its six segments for specific skills, and B says how each of these skills is tested: DACB.

questions.text: In the given sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Your skill lie in cheering up people who are stressed out, wound up or generally just annoyed.
options: who are stressed out, wound up
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'skill' needs a singular verb: 'Your skill lies in cheering up people'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. Padamse worked like a mathematician and was a true ______ who experimented with numerous mediums.
questions.explanation: A 'visionary' is a person with original ideas, which suits an artist who experimented with many mediums. An 'adversary' is an opponent, and 'voluntary' and 'literary' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. SURVEILLANCE
questions.explanation: Surveillance is a close watch kept over someone or something; its opposite is 'neglect'. 'Vigilance' is close in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Stir up a hornet’s nest
questions.explanation: To 'stir up a hornet's nest' is to provoke trouble or anger, usually by raising a touchy matter.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. If the video clip of the murder had not been shared on social media, the world would likely have remained ______ of the tragedy.
questions.explanation: Without the shared clip, the world would not have known of the tragedy: it would have remained 'unaware' of it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. DEMOLISH
questions.explanation: To demolish is to pull down; the opposite is to 'construct', or build.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. GUILE
questions.explanation: Guile is sly cunning used to trick people: 'deceit'. 'Sincerity' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. It is reported that everyday “India witnessing the death” of over 2000 babies aged less than one year.
options: India will be witness the death
questions.explanation: A regular, present fact takes the simple present, and the singular subject 'India' takes 'witnesses': 'India witnesses the death of over 2000 babies'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. That which is no longer useful
questions.explanation: Something no longer needed or useful is 'redundant'. 'Abundant' means plentiful and 'reluctant' unwilling.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. The most well-known among them is the Purple Frog needing immediate protection. B. The Secret Life of Frogs is the first ever film on the Amphibians of India. C. The film has been shot extensively in the Western Ghats. D. It showcases unique species of frogs which are critically endangered.
questions.explanation: B introduces the film, C says where it was shot, D says what it shows (endangered species of frogs), and A names the best known of them: BCDA.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Something that is genuine
questions.explanation: 'Authentic' means genuine, of undisputed origin. 'Unreal' is nearly the opposite.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. “Do you attend the film festival at Goa every year?” he asked.
options: He asked me if I attended the film festival at Goa every year.
He is asking me if I attended the film festival at Goa every year.
He asks me if I attend the film festival at Goa every year.
He had asked me if I was attending the film festival at Goa every year.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with 'if', and after the past 'asked' the present 'attend' moves back to 'attended', with 'you' becoming 'I'.

questions.text: Which article of the Constitution of India mentions that the Lok Sabha must have a Speaker and a Deputy Speaker?
questions.explanation: Article 93 says the House of the People shall choose two of its members to be its Speaker and Deputy Speaker. Article 85 deals with the sessions of Parliament, Article 97 with the salaries of the presiding officers and Article 100 with voting in the Houses.

questions.text: ‘Aatish-i-Chinar’ (Flames of Chinar) is the autobiography of which politician?
questions.explanation: 'Aatish-i-Chinar' is the autobiography of Sheikh Muhammad Abdullah, the 'Sher-e-Kashmir', who led the National Conference and was Prime Minister and later Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.text: Which is the second largest river basin in India that covers 10% of the country’s area?
questions.explanation: Of the four, the Godavari, the largest river of peninsular India, has the biggest basin: about 3.13 lakh sq km, nearly a tenth of India's area. It is usually ranked second after the Ganga's.

questions.text: In a computer, which unit is responsible for processing data and is also called the electronic brain of the computer?
questions.explanation: The Central Processing Unit carries out a program's instructions and processes data, so it is called the brain of the computer. RAM is working memory, the hard disk is storage and the keyboard an input device.

questions.text: What is the range of the intensity scale used in measuring earthquakes?
questions.explanation: Earthquake intensity, judged by the effects seen on the ground, is rated on the Mercalli scale from 1 to 12; magnitude, the energy released, is given on the Richter scale.

questions.text: In which year were the ‘Kalbelia’ folk songs and dances of Rajasthan included in UNESCO’s representative list of Intangible Cultural Heritage?
questions.explanation: The Kalbelia folk songs and dances of Rajasthan were inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

questions.text: ‘Saga Dawa’ is one of the biggest Buddhist festivals. In which one of the following states is it celebrated?
questions.explanation: Saga Dawa, celebrated in Sikkim on the full moon of the fourth month of the Tibetan calendar, marks the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and passing into nirvana.

questions.text: What disease is caused by insulin deficiency?
questions.explanation: Diabetes mellitus results when the pancreas makes too little insulin, or the body responds poorly to it, so glucose builds up in the blood. The other three are autoimmune diseases not caused by a lack of insulin.

questions.text: In the context of the mesosphere, which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: It is directly above the stratosphere.
In this layer temperature rises very rapidly with increasing height.
Meteorites burn up in this layer on entering from the space.
It is the third layer of the atmosphere.
questions.explanation: In the mesosphere, about 50 to 80 km up, the temperature falls with height, to about −100 °C near its top. The other statements are true: it lies directly above the stratosphere, it is the third layer, and meteors burn up in it.

questions.text: With which of the following sports is Bhamidipati Sai Praneeth associated?
questions.explanation: B Sai Praneeth is a badminton player; he won bronze in men's singles at the 2019 World Championships.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was best known for hoisting the Indian National Congress flag at the Gowalia Tank maidan in Bombay during the Quit India Movement?
questions.explanation: Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the Congress flag at the Gowalia Tank maidan on 9 August 1942, as the leaders were being arrested at the start of the Quit India Movement.

questions.text: In which process is a protective zinc coating applied on iron to prevent it from rusting?
questions.explanation: Galvanisation coats iron or steel with zinc, which corrodes in its place and keeps it from rusting.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who introduced the 'Doctrine of Lapse'?
questions.explanation: Lord Dalhousie, Governor-General from 1848 to 1856, used the Doctrine of Lapse to annex states whose rulers died without a natural heir, among them Satara, Jhansi and Nagpur.

questions.text: On 2 December 2019, who became the first female pilot of the Indian Navy?
questions.explanation: Sub-Lieutenant Shivangi joined operational duties at Kochi on 2 December 2019 as the Indian Navy's first woman pilot, flying Dornier aircraft.

questions.text: The Atrial wall of the human heart secretes a very important peptide hormone. What is the name of that hormone?
questions.explanation: The walls of the atria secrete atrial natriuretic factor (ANF), which lowers blood pressure by widening the blood vessels and increasing the loss of salt and water in urine.

questions.text: Which of the following is INCORRECTLY paired?
questions.explanation: Pedology, the science of soils, goes with soil geography; phytogeography, the geography of plants, draws on botany. The other pairs link a branch of geography with its sister discipline.

questions.text: Which Indian actress was chosen for the ‘2020 Crystal Award’ given by the World Economic Forum for spreading awareness about mental health?
questions.explanation: Deepika Padukone received the World Economic Forum's Crystal Award at Davos in January 2020 for her work on mental-health awareness through her Live Love Laugh Foundation.

questions.text: According to the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU), what is India’s rank in the 2019 worldwide Index of Cancer Preparedness (ICP)?
questions.explanation: The Economist Intelligence Unit's 2019 Index of Cancer Preparedness ranked India 19th of the 28 countries it covered; Australia came first.

questions.text: On which day is Constitution Day celebrated every year in India?
questions.explanation: Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas) is observed on 26 November, the day in 1949 when the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution; it has been marked since 2015.

questions.text: Which forest is also referred to as ‘Monsoon Forests’?
questions.explanation: Tropical deciduous forests, which shed their leaves in the dry season, are India's most widespread forests and are called monsoon forests.

questions.text: Which of the following Bollywood veterans was chosen for the 66th Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2018?
questions.explanation: Amitabh Bachchan received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2018, given with the 66th National Film Awards; ill health kept him from their ceremony, and President Ram Nath Kovind presented it to him at Rashtrapati Bhavan on 29 December 2019.

questions.text: Which of the following companies was chosen for the UN Global Climate Action Award in the ‘Carbon Neutral Now’ category in September 2019?
questions.explanation: Infosys won the UN Global Climate Action Award in the 'Carbon Neutral Now' category for its carbon-neutral programme; the award was announced in September 2019 and presented at COP25 in Madrid that December.

questions.text: Who founded the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) in Calcutta?
questions.explanation: Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis founded the Indian Statistical Institute in Calcutta in 1931.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. FURTIVE
questions.explanation: 'Furtive' means done quietly and secretly to avoid notice: 'secretive'. 'Abortive' means failed and 'adhesive' sticky.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Actions speak louder than words
options: What you do reveals the real you
What you don’t say is what you are
What you do is your own business
What you can see may not be true
questions.explanation: 'Actions speak louder than words' means that what people do shows what they are really like more truly than what they say.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. AGILE
questions.explanation: 'Agile' means able to move quickly and easily: 'nimble'. 'Docile' means meek and easily led, and 'guile' is cunning.

questions.text: Select the wrongly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'ambassador', with a double 's'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The choices we make in life determine who we are. One’s life is (1)______ marked by the exemplary choices one has made (2) ______ one’s journey. The mega icon Ratan Tata has described his journey (3)______ being a seven-year-old boy who played his (4) ______ the freedom struggle to being moved by the plight of a family on a two-wheeler which became the genesis of the world’s most (5)______ car the Tata Nano.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The passage holds that our choices shape who we are, so a life is 'often' marked by them; 'rarely', 'never' and 'seldom' contradict that.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The choices we make in life determine who we are. One’s life is (1)______ marked by the exemplary choices one has made (2) ______ one’s journey. The mega icon Ratan Tata has described his journey (3)______ being a seven-year-old boy who played his (4) ______ the freedom struggle to being moved by the plight of a family on a two-wheeler which became the genesis of the world’s most (5)______ car the Tata Nano.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Choices are made 'along' a journey, that is in the course of it.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The choices we make in life determine who we are. One’s life is (1)______ marked by the exemplary choices one has made (2) ______ one’s journey. The mega icon Ratan Tata has described his journey (3)______ being a seven-year-old boy who played his (4) ______ the freedom struggle to being moved by the plight of a family on a two-wheeler which became the genesis of the world’s most (5)______ car the Tata Nano.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'From' pairs with the 'to' that follows: his journey 'from being a seven-year-old boy ... to being moved by the plight of a family'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The choices we make in life determine who we are. One’s life is (1)______ marked by the exemplary choices one has made (2) ______ one’s journey. The mega icon Ratan Tata has described his journey (3)______ being a seven-year-old boy who played his (4) ______ the freedom struggle to being moved by the plight of a family on a two-wheeler which became the genesis of the world’s most (5)______ car the Tata Nano.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 4.
questions.explanation: To 'play one's part in' something is to take part in it: the boy played his part in the freedom struggle.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The choices we make in life determine who we are. One’s life is (1)______ marked by the exemplary choices one has made (2) ______ one’s journey. The mega icon Ratan Tata has described his journey (3)______ being a seven-year-old boy who played his (4) ______ the freedom struggle to being moved by the plight of a family on a two-wheeler which became the genesis of the world’s most (5)______ car the Tata Nano.

Select the most appropriate option for blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Economical' means cheap to buy or run, as the Tata Nano was meant to be; 'economic' means relating to the economy.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. The rising prices of essential food items have placed an “weighty” burden on the poor.
questions.explanation: 'Enormous' keeps the sense of a heavy burden and, beginning with a vowel sound, suits the article 'an' ('an weighty' is wrong). 'Trivial' and 'lightest' reverse the meaning.

questions.text: In the given sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Freedom of expression meaning the right to express one’s own convictions and beliefs.
questions.explanation: The sentence has no main verb: 'meaning' must be 'means': 'Freedom of expression means the right to express ...'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. Behind them come camels carrying drums and small guns. B. The Emperor is escorted by two decorated elephants who head the procession. C. At the end come the platoons of soldiers in rows of two. D. First of all, there is a volley of guns announcing Emperor Bahadur Shah’s entry into the mosque.
questions.explanation: D opens with the volley of guns announcing the Emperor, B describes the elephants at the head of the procession, A the camels 'behind them' and C the soldiers 'at the end': DBAC.

questions.text: In the given sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. My hotel in Goa had a wonderful view of the sea in the window.
questions.explanation: A view is seen 'from' a window, not 'in' it: 'a wonderful view of the sea from the window'.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Sitab asked his mother, “Has it been snowing all night?”
options: Sitab asked his mother if it has snowed all night.
Sitab asked his mother if it is snowing all night.
Sitab asked his mother if it had been snowing all night.
Sitab asked his mother if it was snowing all night.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with 'if', and after the past 'asked' the present perfect continuous 'has been snowing' becomes the past perfect continuous 'had been snowing'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. In order to buy that bicycle, he plans to win some prize money by teaching an illiterate person how to read and write. B. He needs a bicycle to win the bicycle race which would help pay off his father’s debt. C. The film ‘Douch’ is about a young Iranian village boy. D. But the only illiterate person is a 90 year old woman who is ill-tempered and doesn’t wish to learn anything.
