questions.explanation: C introduces the film and the boy, B says why he needs a bicycle, A how he plans to buy 'that bicycle', and D, beginning 'But', gives the snag: CBAD.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. ENIGMA
questions.explanation: An 'enigma' is something mysterious or puzzling; its opposite is 'clarity'. 'Mystery' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Using right and left hand equally well
questions.explanation: An ambidextrous person can use the right and left hands equally well.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. RESERVED
questions.explanation: 'Reserved' means slow to show one's feelings or opinions; its opposite is 'friendly'. 'Reticent' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. The teacher ______ the student for cheating.
questions.explanation: To 'rebuke' is to scold sharply, the fitting response to cheating; 'praised' reverses the sense, and 'refused' and 'invoked' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Having no moral principles
questions.explanation: 'Unscrupulous' means having no moral principles. 'Ethical' is its opposite, and 'mischievous' means playfully troublesome.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A piece of cake
questions.explanation: 'A piece of cake' is something very easy to do.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. Those earning less than Rs.10,000 are ______ from paying income tax.
questions.explanation: To be 'exempted from' a duty, such as paying tax, is to be freed from it.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. The Delhi Police has shot an educational video on Traffic Rules for school students.
options: An educational video on Traffic Rules for school students is being shot by the Delhi Police.
An educational video on Traffic Rules for school students has been shot by the Delhi Police.
An educational video on Traffic Rules for school students had been shot by the Delhi Police.
An educational video on Traffic Rules for school students was being shot by the Delhi Police.
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'has shot' becomes 'has been shot' in the passive: 'An educational video ... has been shot by the Delhi Police.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. India has lost a veteran actor with the “deceased” of Shriram Lagoo.
questions.explanation: 'Demise' means death: 'with the demise of Shriram Lagoo'. 'Deceased' describes or names a dead person, 'bereavement' is the loss felt by those left behind, and 'expired' is a verb form.

questions.text: What is the symbol of Tin?
questions.explanation: Tin's symbol, Sn, comes from its Latin name 'stannum'. Si is silicon, Ta tantalum and Ti titanium.

questions.text: Which of the following banks prints the currency notes in India?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India issues India's currency notes (the Government issues the one-rupee note). They are printed at four presses, two run by the RBI's own subsidiary, Bharatiya Reserve Bank Note Mudran, and two by the Government's Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India.

questions.text: When did the Sarkaria Commission submit its report?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 1988, the year usually given for the report of the Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State relations, set up in June 1983, and the year it was made public. Justice R. S. Sarkaria had handed it to Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi on 27 October 1987, a year that is not among the options.

questions.text: What is the name of the first crude oil pipeline constructed in India?
questions.explanation: Oil India Limited's crude oil pipeline from the Naharkatiya oilfield in Assam to the Nunmati (Guwahati) refinery, commissioned in 1962 and then extended to Barauni in Bihar, was India's first. The HBJ pipeline carries gas, not crude oil.

questions.text: Who among the following took charge as the 39th President of the BCCI in October 2019?
questions.explanation: The former India captain Sourav Ganguly took charge as the 39th President of the BCCI on 23 October 2019.

questions.text: New Delhi's Lotus Temple was designed by an architect from ______.
questions.explanation: The Lotus Temple, the Bahá'í House of Worship in New Delhi, was designed by the Iranian architect Fariborz Sahba.

questions.text: How many person(s) has/have been selected for the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award, 2019?
questions.explanation: Two athletes received the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna for 2019: the wrestler Bajrang Punia and the para-athlete Deepa Malik.

questions.text: The F7 key is commonly used in Microsoft programs such as Microsoft Word, Outlook, etc. for:
questions.explanation: In Microsoft Word and Outlook, F7 runs the spelling and grammar check. F1 opens Help, and F2 renames a selected file or folder in Windows.

questions.text: What was the magnitude of the Indian Ocean Tsunami 2004?
questions.explanation: The undersea earthquake off northern Sumatra on 26 December 2004 that set off the Indian Ocean tsunami had a moment magnitude of 9.1, as the US Geological Survey gives it; some estimates go up to 9.3.

questions.text: During the phenomenon of aphelion, the approximate distance between the earth and the sun is:
questions.explanation: At aphelion, in early July, the earth is farthest from the sun, about 152 million km away; at perihelion, in early January, it is closest, about 147 million km.

questions.text: Bhatiali is the folk music of which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Bhatiali is the folk song of the boatmen of Bengal, sung on the rivers of West Bengal and Bangladesh.

questions.text: What is the approximate speed of sound in distilled water at 25°C (77°F)?
questions.explanation: Standard tables give about 1498 m/s for sound in distilled water at 25 °C, more than four times its speed in air at that temperature (about 346 m/s).

questions.text: Ethiopia’s first satellite was launched from which Country's Space Station in December 2019?
questions.explanation: Ethiopia's first satellite, the Earth-observation satellite ETRSS-1, was launched on a Chinese Long March 4B rocket from the Taiyuan Satellite Launch Center on 20 December 2019.

questions.text: The National Game of Bhutan is:
questions.explanation: Archery is Bhutan's national sport.

questions.text: Which of the following sectors of the economy has the highest share in India's GDP?
questions.explanation: The services (tertiary) sector produces more than half of India's GDP, ahead of industry, of which manufacturing is a part, and agriculture.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India has a provision for the Constitution of Legislatures in States?
questions.explanation: Article 168 provides for a Legislature in every State, made up of the Governor and one or two Houses. Article 163 deals with the Council of Ministers that advises the Governor, 165 with the Advocate-General and 167 with the Chief Minister's duty to keep the Governor informed.

questions.text: Which of the following divisions of plants does NOT have a well differentiated body?
questions.explanation: Thallophyta, the algae, have no well-differentiated body design: no distinct root, stem and leaves. Bryophytes have simple stem- and leaf-like parts, and pteridophytes and gymnosperms are fully differentiated.

questions.text: The famous Gupta period Dashavatara Temple, recognised as one of the earliest Panchayatan temples in north India, is located at:
questions.explanation: The Dashavatara Temple, a Gupta-period Vishnu temple at Deogarh in Uttar Pradesh's Lalitpur district, is among the earliest panchayatana temples in north India: a main shrine with four subsidiary shrines at the corners of its platform. Bhitargaon has a Gupta brick temple, Nachna-Kuthara the Parvati temple and Tigawa the Kankali Devi temple.

questions.text: The novel ‘Chanakya’ which won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 2019 was in which language?
questions.explanation: Joysree Goswami Mahanta's Assamese novel 'Chanakya' won the Sahitya Akademi Award for 2019.

questions.text: Most of the atmospheric Ozone is found in which layer of atmosphere?
questions.explanation: About 90% of the atmosphere's ozone lies in the stratosphere, mostly in the ozone layer, where it absorbs most of the sun's ultraviolet radiation.

questions.text: In the field of computing, what does ENIAC stand for?
questions.explanation: ENIAC, the Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer, completed in 1945 at the University of Pennsylvania, was one of the first general-purpose electronic digital computers.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. “As much as” a hundred children gathered to celebrate Independence Day.
questions.explanation: 'Children' can be counted, so the phrase is 'as many as'; 'as much as' goes with uncountable nouns: 'As many as a hundred children gathered to celebrate Independence Day.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. For thousands of years, humans have been ______ the earth, making scars upon the land.
questions.explanation: 'Making scars upon the land' describes harm, so humans have been 'damaging' the earth.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A dime a dozen
questions.explanation: Something 'a dime a dozen' is very common, and so of little value.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Couch Potato
questions.explanation: A 'couch potato' is a lazy person who spends a great deal of time sitting and watching television.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. We do not want to condemn the ‘word’. It is, after all, a mighty instrument; it is the means by (1)______ we tell each other of our emotions, the way in which we influence others. Words can do (2)______ good but also cause terrible injuries. It is true that at first there was the deed; the word came later. It was in some respects a cultural progress (3)______ the deed became word. But the word was (4)______ a spell, a magical act, and it (5)______ much of its power.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'by', a thing is referred to with 'which': 'the means by which we tell each other of our emotions'. 'That' cannot follow a preposition.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. We do not want to condemn the ‘word’. It is, after all, a mighty instrument; it is the means by (1)______ we tell each other of our emotions, the way in which we influence others. Words can do (2)______ good but also cause terrible injuries. It is true that at first there was the deed; the word came later. It was in some respects a cultural progress (3)______ the deed became word. But the word was (4)______ a spell, a magical act, and it (5)______ much of its power.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 2
questions.explanation: 'Immeasurable' (too great to be measured) good is set against the 'terrible injuries' words can also cause; 'numerable' and 'countable' say the opposite.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. We do not want to condemn the ‘word’. It is, after all, a mighty instrument; it is the means by (1)______ we tell each other of our emotions, the way in which we influence others. Words can do (2)______ good but also cause terrible injuries. It is true that at first there was the deed; the word came later. It was in some respects a cultural progress (3)______ the deed became word. But the word was (4)______ a spell, a magical act, and it (5)______ much of its power.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 3
questions.explanation: The clause gives the moment of the progress: it was progress 'when' the deed became word.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. We do not want to condemn the ‘word’. It is, after all, a mighty instrument; it is the means by (1)______ we tell each other of our emotions, the way in which we influence others. Words can do (2)______ good but also cause terrible injuries. It is true that at first there was the deed; the word came later. It was in some respects a cultural progress (3)______ the deed became word. But the word was (4)______ a spell, a magical act, and it (5)______ much of its power.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 4
questions.explanation: The passage has just said the deed came first and the word later; 'originally' (in the beginning) the word was a spell, a magical act.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. We do not want to condemn the ‘word’. It is, after all, a mighty instrument; it is the means by (1)______ we tell each other of our emotions, the way in which we influence others. Words can do (2)______ good but also cause terrible injuries. It is true that at first there was the deed; the word came later. It was in some respects a cultural progress (3)______ the deed became word. But the word was (4)______ a spell, a magical act, and it (5)______ much of its power.

Select the most appropriate option for blank no. 5
questions.explanation: 'It' is singular, and the present perfect 'has retained' links the word's magical beginnings to now: it still keeps much of that power, as the passage's opening ('a mighty instrument') says. The simple past 'retained' would leave the keeping in the past, 'have retained' needs a plural subject and 'will retained' is ungrammatical.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Steal or misappropriate money
questions.explanation: To 'embezzle' is to steal or misappropriate money placed in one's trust.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Behavior modification techniques are often used to the training of police dogs.
questions.explanation: Techniques are used 'in' training, not 'to' it: 'often used in the training of police dogs'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. There should be ______ punishment for rule breakers.
questions.explanation: 'Severe' (harsh) describes the kind of punishment rule breakers deserve. 'Many' needs a plural noun, 'too' cannot qualify a noun, and 'much' speaks of quantity where the sense calls for how harsh the punishment is.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. Timid
questions.explanation: 'Timid' means lacking courage; its opposite is 'bold'.

questions.text: Select the wrongly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The suffix '-ful' has one 'l': 'respectful'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Combine to form a whole
questions.explanation: To 'integrate' is to combine parts into a whole; 'scatter' and 'disjoin' mean the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. “So much as” you behave like this, the decision of the management against you cannot be revoked.
questions.explanation: 'As long as' (for as long a time as) sets the condition: as long as you behave like this, the decision against you cannot be revoked. 'So much as' means 'even' ('without so much as a word'), and 'As long to' and 'As much to' are not English.

questions.text: Given below are four sentences in jumbled order. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. At the metro station he noticed a homeless man. B. He decided to travel to office by the metro train. C. He sent his damaged car to the garage for repairs. D. Johnny had a car accident.
questions.explanation: D (Johnny's accident) leads to C (the damaged car sent for repairs), then B (so he takes the metro) and A (at the station he notices a homeless man): DCBA.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. The mechanic repaired my bike.
options: My bike was repaired by the mechanic.
My bike has been repaired by the mechanic
The bike is repaired by my mechanic.
The bike was being repaired by my mechanic.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'repaired' becomes 'was repaired': 'My bike was repaired by the mechanic.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Insidious
questions.explanation: 'Insidious' means harmful in a gradual, sly way, so 'crafty' is closest. 'Benevolent' and 'sincere' are near opposites.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Vishnu said, "I am going to the theater this evening."
options: Vishnu said that I am going to the theater this evening.
Vishnu said that he was going to the theater that evening.
Vishnu said that he would go to the theater that evening.
Vishnu said that he was going to the theater this evening.
questions.explanation: After 'said', 'I' becomes 'he', 'am going' becomes 'was going' and 'this evening' becomes 'that evening'.

questions.text: Given below are four sentences in jumbled order. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. A boy tended his master’s dogs near a pond. B. However, he realized that the way he talked to them never made them happy. C. Soon he found the tending and his life there very boring. D. All he could do to kill the boredom was by talking to the dogs.
questions.explanation: A introduces the boy and his work, C says he grew bored, D says talking to the dogs was all he could do against the boredom, and B ('However') adds that his talk never made them happy: ACDB.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains a grammatical error. Our twenty-first century society expects all relevant information to simply be handing to us.
questions.explanation: After 'to be' the passive needs the past participle: 'to simply be handed to us'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. Disillusioned
questions.explanation: 'Disillusioned' means disappointed after losing one's hopes or ideals; its opposite is 'enthusiastic'. 'Disappointed', 'embittered' and 'soured' are near synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Diligent
questions.explanation: 'Diligent' means hard-working and persevering, so 'untiring' is closest. 'Lethargic', 'weary' and 'inattentive' are near opposites.

questions.text: Which of the following parts of the human body releases carbon dioxide, brought in by the blood, from the rest of the body?
questions.explanation: In the alveoli of the lungs carbon dioxide passes out of the blood into the air, to be breathed out, while oxygen passes into the blood. The larynx, trachea and bronchi are air passages, where no gas exchange takes place.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about firewall (in the context of computing) is INCORRECT?
options: It permits network transmission based on a set of rules.
It is a combination of both, software and hardware devices.
It is frequently used to protect a computer network from unauthorised access.
It is unable to permit legitimate communication to pass.
questions.explanation: A firewall, in hardware, software or both, filters network traffic by a set of rules: it lets legitimate communication through and blocks unauthorised access.

questions.text: Which Rajput ruler of Mewar in 1576 fought the Battle of Haldighati and then fled the field on his horse, Chetak?
questions.explanation: Maharana Pratap of Mewar fought Akbar's army, led by Raja Man Singh of Amber, at Haldighati in 1576 and escaped on his horse Chetak. Udai Singh was his father and Amar Singh his son and successor.

questions.text: As of January 2020, who was the chief of the Indian Army?
questions.explanation: General Manoj Mukund Naravane became Chief of the Army Staff on 31 December 2019, succeeding General Bipin Rawat, who became the first Chief of Defence Staff on 1 January 2020. In January 2020 R K S Bhadauria was the Chief of the Air Staff and Karambir Singh the Chief of the Naval Staff.

questions.text: ______ is no longer considered as a planet within Earth's Solar system.
questions.explanation: In 2006 the International Astronomical Union reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet, as it has not cleared the neighbourhood of its orbit.

questions.text: National Sports Day of India is celebrated on 29 August every year in honour of which sportsperson?
questions.explanation: 29 August is the birth anniversary of the hockey player Major Dhyan Chand (born 1905), who won Olympic gold with India in 1928, 1932 and 1936.

questions.text: ‘Rangoli Bihu’ one of the major festival of Assam is celebrated in the month of______.
questions.explanation: Rongali (Bohag) Bihu, the Assamese New Year, falls in mid-April, at the start of the month of Bohag. Kati Bihu comes in October and Magh Bihu in January.

questions.text: Which is the correctly matched option of captain of cricket team and year of World Cup victory?
questions.explanation: Kapil Dev led India to the World Cup in 1983. Imran Khan's Pakistan won in 1992 (Sri Lanka won in 1996), Ricky Ponting's Australia in 2003 and 2007 and Michael Clarke's in 2015; India won in 2011 under M S Dhoni.

questions.text: With which neighboring country does Gujarat share its border?
questions.explanation: Gujarat's international border, along the Rann of Kutch, is with Pakistan's Sindh province. Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh border India's north and east.

questions.text: Who was the chairman of the drafting committee of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: B R Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly, set up in August 1947; K M Munshi and Mohammad Saadullah were among its members.

questions.text: Which American President won the Nobel Peace Prize?
questions.explanation: Barack Obama received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2009. (Theodore Roosevelt, Woodrow Wilson and Jimmy Carter also won it, but are not among the options.)

questions.text: Mughal emperor Shah Jahan got the monument Taj Mahal constructed in memory of his wife ______.
questions.explanation: Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal at Agra in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. Jahanara and Roshanara were his daughters, and Nur Jahan was Jahangir's empress.

questions.text: Which are the biodiversity hotspots of India? (A) Western Ghats (B) North East India (C) Sunderland
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives all three, reading 'Sunderland' as Sundaland, the hotspot that takes in the Nicobar Islands. India has parts of four biodiversity hotspots: the Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, the Himalaya and Indo-Burma (which between them take in North East India), and Sundaland. The Sundarbans, which the printed name might suggest, is not a hotspot.

questions.text: Who wrote the book ‘My Experiments with Truth’?
questions.explanation: 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth' is M K Gandhi's autobiography, which first appeared in Gujarati, in instalments, in the 1920s.

questions.text: The 'transformation curve' is also known as the:
questions.explanation: The production possibility curve, which shows the combinations of two goods an economy can produce with its resources and technology, is also called the transformation curve.

questions.text: The award given to the best coach among coaches of all the different games is known as ______.
questions.explanation: The Dronacharya Award, instituted in 1985, honours sports coaches. The Arjuna Award honours sportspersons, the Dadasaheb Phalke Award is for cinema and the Ashoka Chakra is a gallantry award.

questions.text: ‘Bhagta Parab', a tribal festival that is celebrated between the period of spring and summer, originated in the state of ______.
questions.explanation: Bhagta Parab, held between spring and summer, is a festival of the tribal communities of Jharkhand.

questions.text: In which year did the convention on wetlands, the 'Ramsar Convention', come into force in India?
questions.explanation: The Ramsar Convention entered into force for India on 1 February 1982.

questions.text: The three-carbon molecules broken down from six-carbon molecules of glucose during the first step in the process of nutrition in all organisms is called:
questions.explanation: Glucose, a six-carbon molecule, is first broken down in the cytoplasm into pyruvate, a three-carbon molecule. NCERT describes this as the first step of respiration.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When was the ‘Quit India Movement’ started?
questions.explanation: The All India Congress Committee passed the Quit India resolution at Bombay on 8 August 1942.

questions.text: ______ refers to money that has already been spent and which cannot be recovered.
questions.explanation: A sunk cost has already been incurred and cannot be recovered. Opportunity cost is the value of the best alternative given up, and replacement cost what it would cost to replace an asset now.

questions.text: Which of the following schemes launched by the present government has been correctly matched with its purpose?
options: SUMAN Scheme – Free medicines to pregnant women
SAGARMALA Scheme – To regularise selling of goods at ports
AASHA Scheme – Remunerative prices to ward boys for serving patients
questions.explanation: SUMAN (Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan), launched in October 2019, assures every pregnant woman and newborn at a public health facility free care, medicines included. Ujjwala gives LPG connections, Sagarmala is a port-led development programme and PM-AASHA secures remunerative prices for farmers.

questions.text: What is the name of the force with which earth pulls everything towards itself?
questions.explanation: Gravity, the earth's gravitational force, pulls every object towards the earth's centre.

questions.text: Who among the following is NOT a well known Tabla player in Hindustani classical style of music?
questions.explanation: Amjad Ali Khan is a sarod player, while Latif Ahmed Khan, Swapan Chaudhuri and Zakir Hussain made their names on the tabla.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options select the one that gives their correct order. A. Anush was very afraid of stray dogs. B. Anush’s mother saw the dog chasing her son. C. One evening, when a street dog barked at him, Anush turned and started running. D. The dog ran after him barking loudly and fiercely.
questions.explanation: A introduces Anush's fear of stray dogs, C tells how one evening he ran from a barking dog, D says the dog chased him, and B, his mother seeing the chase, comes last: ACDB.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The invited guests preferred orange juice than hot coffee or chilled grapes.
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' takes 'to', not 'than', before the thing not chosen: 'preferred orange juice to hot coffee or chilled grapes'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. “As many as” I care for her, I still have to disagree with her on this topic.
questions.explanation: 'As much as' introduces a concession of degree, meaning however much I care for her; 'many' goes only with plural countable nouns, not with a verb such as 'care'.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. The coach received the members of the team with great excitement.
options: The members of the team were received by the coach with great excitement.
The members of the team could be received by the coach with great excitement.
The members of the team had been received by the coach with great excitement.
The members of the team was received by the coach with great excitement.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'received' becomes 'were received' with the plural subject 'the members of the team': 'The members of the team were received by the coach with great excitement.'

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Families, particularly those with children and who have the means, are opting to (1)______ from Delhi driven by the increasing air pollution and (2)______ impact on health. Delhi’s Air Quality Index had (3)______ a three-year-low this year, post-Diwali, creating a (4)______ polluted atmosphere which led to (5)______ problems in many, forcing people to wear masks outdoors and install air purifiers at home.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: Families are moving away from Delhi: to 'relocate' is to move to a new place to live.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Families, particularly those with children and who have the means, are opting to (1)______ from Delhi driven by the increasing air pollution and (2)______ impact on health. Delhi’s Air Quality Index had (3)______ a three-year-low this year, post-Diwali, creating a (4)______ polluted atmosphere which led to (5)______ problems in many, forcing people to wear masks outdoors and install air purifiers at home.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
questions.explanation: 'Its' refers back to 'the increasing air pollution', a singular noun; 'it's' means 'it is', and 'their's' is not a word.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Families, particularly those with children and who have the means, are opting to (1)______ from Delhi driven by the increasing air pollution and (2)______ impact on health. Delhi’s Air Quality Index had (3)______ a three-year-low this year, post-Diwali, creating a (4)______ polluted atmosphere which led to (5)______ problems in many, forcing people to wear masks outdoors and install air purifiers at home.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3.
questions.explanation: To 'hit' a level is to reach it: the index had hit a three-year low.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Families, particularly those with children and who have the means, are opting to (1)______ from Delhi driven by the increasing air pollution and (2)______ impact on health. Delhi’s Air Quality Index had (3)______ a three-year-low this year, post-Diwali, creating a (4)______ polluted atmosphere which led to (5)______ problems in many, forcing people to wear masks outdoors and install air purifiers at home.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.
questions.explanation: The adverb 'severely' describes the adjective 'polluted': a severely polluted atmosphere.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Families, particularly those with children and who have the means, are opting to (1)______ from Delhi driven by the increasing air pollution and (2)______ impact on health. Delhi’s Air Quality Index had (3)______ a three-year-low this year, post-Diwali, creating a (4)______ polluted atmosphere which led to (5)______ problems in many, forcing people to wear masks outdoors and install air purifiers at home.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5.
questions.explanation: Polluted air harms the lungs and airways, causing 'respiratory' (breathing) problems, which is why people wear masks outdoors.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Every cloud has a silver lining
options: Something irritating is there in any joyous situation
Something promising is there in any difficult situation
Something disheartening is there in any happy situation
Something interesting is there in any colourful situation
questions.explanation: 'Every cloud has a silver lining' means that even a difficult or unhappy situation has some hopeful side.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A song or music in praise of God
questions.explanation: A hymn is a song of praise to God. An elegy is a poem of mourning, an ode a lyric poem addressed to a person or thing, and an epic a long narrative poem.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Made out of whole cloth
questions.explanation: Something 'made out of whole cloth' is invented entirely, with no basis in fact: wholly false and fabricated. The idiom says nothing about it being believable or convincing.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. PLAUSIBLE
questions.explanation: 'Plausible' means seeming reasonable or likely to be true, so its opposite is 'unlikely'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. There was a huge ______ in the stomach.
questions.explanation: A tumour, an abnormal growth of tissue, can form in the stomach. A tuber is the swollen underground stem of a plant such as the potato, and a tremor is a shaking.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Everyone are very well equipped with his own weapons.
questions.explanation: 'Everyone' is singular and takes a singular verb, as the later 'his' shows: 'Everyone is very well equipped with his own weapons.'

questions.text: Select the synonym of the given word. QUARRELSOME
questions.explanation: 'Querulous', peevish and given to complaining, is the only option close to 'quarrelsome'. 'Ambiguous' means unclear, 'pragmatic' practical and 'opaque' not letting light through.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. ADJUSTMENT
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'balancing': an adjustment is a small change made to get something right or into balance, as when accounts or scales are adjusted. 'Compromising' is arguable, but it fits only the narrower sense of settling a dispute or claim by mutual concession.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. CASUAL
questions.explanation: 'Casual' means happening by chance or done without much thought, so its opposite here is 'planned'. 'Informal' is a synonym of 'casual'.

questions.text: Select the wrongly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'navigation'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The ______ part of this issue is that the investigation officer himself turned out to be the culprit.
questions.explanation: 'Funny' can mean strange or ironic, and the irony here is that the investigating officer himself was the culprit: 'The funniest part of this issue'.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. The traveller inquired, "Will there be a shelter for strangers?”
options: The traveller inquired if there will be a shelter for strangers.
The traveller inquired if there would be a shelter for strangers.
The traveller inquired if would there be a shelter for strangers.
The traveller inquired whether will there be a shelter for strangers.
questions.explanation: A yes-no question is reported with 'if' and the word order of a statement, and 'will' moves back to 'would' after the past 'inquired': 'The traveller inquired if there would be a shelter for strangers.'

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Things which are of the same kind and of the same dimensions
questions.explanation: 'Homogenous', a variant of 'homogeneous', describes things of the same kind throughout. 'Homonymous' means having the same name, and 'homophony' is sameness of sound.

questions.text: What is the normal air pressure at sea level?
questions.explanation: The standard air pressure at sea level is 1013.25 millibars, the same as 1013.25 hectopascals or one atmosphere.

questions.text: Animals of which phylum have jointed legs?
questions.explanation: Arthropoda takes its name from the Greek for 'jointed feet': insects, spiders and crabs all have jointed legs. Molluscs, echinoderms and nematodes do not.

questions.text: Velds are grasslands of:
questions.explanation: The velds (veldt) are the temperate grasslands of southern Africa, mainly South Africa. Australia's are the downs, North America's the prairies and Central Asia's the steppes.

questions.text: How many Grand Slam tournaments are played in a year in tennis?
questions.explanation: Tennis has four Grand Slam tournaments a year: the Australian Open, the French Open, Wimbledon and the US Open.

questions.text: The period of second five year plan in India was:
questions.explanation: The Second Five Year Plan ran from 1956 to 1961; built on P C Mahalanobis's model, it stressed heavy industry. The First Plan ran from 1951 to 1956.

questions.text: World's largest field hockey stadium based on the seating capacity is located in which country?
questions.explanation: When the exam was held (March 2020), the National Hockey Stadium in Lahore, Pakistan, with a capacity of about 45,000, was the world's largest field hockey stadium.

questions.text: Chenchus schedule tribe belongs to which state of India?
questions.explanation: The Chenchus, a forest tribe of the Nallamala hills, live in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh; Telangana is the only one of the two among the options.

questions.text: Which technology do third generation computers use?
questions.explanation: Third-generation computers used integrated circuits. The first generation used vacuum tubes, the second transistors and the fourth microprocessors.

questions.text: India is divided into how many earthquake zones (seismic zones)?
questions.explanation: When the exam was held (March 2020), the Bureau of Indian Standards' seismic zoning map (IS 1893) divided India into four zones, II to V, Zone V being the most active; the old Zone I was merged into Zone II in 2002.

questions.text: Which zone separates the crust and mantle?
questions.explanation: The Mohorovičić discontinuity (Moho) is the boundary between the crust and the mantle. The asthenosphere is a weak layer of the upper mantle, and the stratosphere a layer of the atmosphere.

questions.text: What is the formula of butane gas?
questions.explanation: Butane is the alkane (CₙH₂ₙ₊₂) with four carbon atoms: C₄H₁₀. C₄H₈ is butene.

questions.text: Where were the first Winter Paralympics Games held?
questions.explanation: The first Winter Paralympic Games were held at Örnsköldsvik, Sweden, in 1976.

questions.text: Who won the 2019 Women’s World Rapid Chess Championship?
questions.explanation: Koneru Humpy won the 2019 Women's World Rapid Chess Championship in Moscow in December 2019, beating China's Lei Tingjie in an Armageddon tie-break.

questions.text: What is the radius of the moon?
questions.explanation: The Moon's mean radius is about 1,737 km, that is 1.74 × 10⁶ m, a little over a quarter of the Earth's.

questions.text: Which country has announced setting up of Gandhi Citizenship Education Prize?
questions.explanation: Portugal's Prime Minister, António Costa, announced the annual Gandhi Citizenship Education Prize in New Delhi in December 2019, to mark the 150th anniversary of Gandhi's birth.

questions.text: Who has won DSC Prize for South Asian Literature 2019?
questions.explanation: Amitabha Bagchi won the 2019 DSC Prize for South Asian Literature for his novel 'Half the Night Is Gone'.

questions.text: Who acts as the President during casual vacancy that arises due to death of the President?
questions.explanation: Under Article 65(1), when the President's office falls vacant through death, resignation or removal, the Vice-President acts as President until a new President, who must be elected within six months (Article 62(2)), takes office.

questions.text: Who was the first Chief Election Commissioner of India?
questions.explanation: Sukumar Sen was India's first Chief Election Commissioner (1950-1958) and conducted the first two general elections.

questions.text: In the field of computing, what does VRML stand for?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives VRML's original name: the language for describing 3D virtual worlds on the web was first called the Virtual Reality Markup Language and was soon renamed the Virtual Reality Modeling Language, which is not among the options.

questions.text: Which woman astronaut has set the record for the longest single spaceflight by a woman?
questions.explanation: When the exam was held (March 2020), the record was Christina Koch's 328 days aboard the International Space Station, ending in February 2020; she passed Peggy Whitson's 288 days in December 2019.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was the first Indian to join the Viceroy’s Executive Council?
questions.explanation: Satyendra Prasad Sinha became the first Indian member of the Viceroy's Executive Council in 1909, as Law Member, under the Morley-Minto reforms.

questions.text: The mixed economy is:
options: presence of subsistence and commercial farming
co-existence of traditional and modern industries
a market system of resource allocation, commerce, and trade in which free markets coexist with government intervention
presence of domestic and foreign investments
questions.explanation: In a mixed economy the market allocates most resources while the government also takes part, regulating it and running some enterprises itself; India adopted this model after independence.

questions.text: Which country launched the third ‘Long March-5', the largest carrier rocket of the country, in December 2019?
questions.explanation: China launched the third Long March 5, its largest carrier rocket, from Wenchang on 27 December 2019, carrying the Shijian-20 satellite.

questions.text: Bylakuppe Monastery (Namdroling) is situated in which state of India?
questions.explanation: Namdroling Monastery, a major centre of the Nyingma school of Tibetan Buddhism, is at Bylakuppe, a Tibetan settlement in Karnataka's Mysuru district.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When did Shuja-ud-daulah and Shah Alam sign treaties at Allahabad with Robert Clive?
questions.explanation: Clive signed the Treaties of Allahabad in August 1765: Shah Alam II granted the Company the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, and Shuja-ud-daulah regained Awadh on paying ₹50 lakh.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. TAME
questions.explanation: To 'tame' is to bring under control or calm; 'upset', to disturb or agitate, works against it. 'Control' and 'restrain' are close in meaning to 'tame', and 'sanctify' means to make holy.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Reinventing the wheel
options: Examining circumstances that have already been understood
Wasting one’s time for things that have already been satisfactorily done
Disturbing the system which has already been in use
questions.explanation: 'Reinventing the wheel' is wasting effort on making again something that already exists and works well.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Nakul asked her, "How do you know that Rahul has told it to him?"
options: Nakul asked her that how she has known that Rahul has told that to him.
Nakul asked her how she knew that Rahul had told that to him.
Nakul asked her how she knew that Rahul has told that to him.
Nakul asked her that how she knows that Rahul had told that to him.
questions.explanation: With the reporting verb in the past, 'do you know' becomes 'she knew' and 'has told' becomes 'had told'. A reported question is joined by its own question word ('how'), in statement order, with no 'that' before it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. TARNISH
questions.explanation: To 'tarnish' is to dull a surface or spoil a reputation: to 'damage' it. 'Decorate' and 'heighten' are nearly opposite, and 'appease' means to calm or pacify.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Forest fire always (1)______ by one of two reasons – naturally caused or human-caused. Natural fire is generally (2)______ by lightning, with a very small percentage (3)______ by spontaneous combustion of dry fuel such as sawdust and leaves. (4)______, human-caused fire can happen (5)______ any number of reasons.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: The blank needs a verb that takes no object, agreeing with 'forest fire': it 'happens', the verb the passage uses again in 'human-caused fire can happen'. 'Causes' and 'creates' would need an object (or the passive 'is caused'), and 'takes up' does not fit the sense.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Forest fire always (1)______ by one of two reasons – naturally caused or human-caused. Natural fire is generally (2)______ by lightning, with a very small percentage (3)______ by spontaneous combustion of dry fuel such as sawdust and leaves. (4)______, human-caused fire can happen (5)______ any number of reasons.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
questions.explanation: Natural fire is generally 'caused' by lightning, the passive matching 'naturally caused' in the first sentence.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Forest fire always (1)______ by one of two reasons – naturally caused or human-caused. Natural fire is generally (2)______ by lightning, with a very small percentage (3)______ by spontaneous combustion of dry fuel such as sawdust and leaves. (4)______, human-caused fire can happen (5)______ any number of reasons.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3.
questions.explanation: A very small share of natural fires is 'contributed' (added) by spontaneous combustion; 'gathered', 'achieved' and 'attained' do not describe a cause.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Forest fire always (1)______ by one of two reasons – naturally caused or human-caused. Natural fire is generally (2)______ by lightning, with a very small percentage (3)______ by spontaneous combustion of dry fuel such as sawdust and leaves. (4)______, human-caused fire can happen (5)______ any number of reasons.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.
questions.explanation: 'On the other hand' sets human-caused fire against the natural fire just described.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Forest fire always (1)______ by one of two reasons – naturally caused or human-caused. Natural fire is generally (2)______ by lightning, with a very small percentage (3)______ by spontaneous combustion of dry fuel such as sawdust and leaves. (4)______, human-caused fire can happen (5)______ any number of reasons.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5.
questions.explanation: 'Due to' is a preposition and fits before the noun phrase 'any number of reasons'. 'Because' would need 'of', 'since' here needs a clause, and 'hence forth' (henceforth) means from now on.

questions.text: Select the wrongly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'accommodate', with a double 'c' and a double 'm'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A situation requiring a choice between equally undesirable alternatives or confusions
questions.explanation: A dilemma is a situation in which one must choose between two equally undesirable alternatives.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Unnecessary suspicion and lack of trust against the others are caused by ______.
questions.explanation: 'Prejudice' is an opinion formed without reason or knowledge, and it breeds suspicion and mistrust of others. 'Contentment', 'impartiality' and 'empathy' work the other way.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. PLEASANT
questions.explanation: Something 'pleasant' is agreeable, like something 'refreshing'. 'Tedious', 'exasperating' and 'tiresome' are nearly opposite.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Some of the issues discussed on the media nowadays has no relevance to the nation-building process.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the verb: the subject 'some of the issues' is plural, so it needs 'have no relevance', not 'has'. 'In the media' would be more usual than 'on the media', but the clear grammatical error is the verb.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. The driver had a cloudy look and drove off without taking him. B. He asked a taxi driver to take him to the shopping mall. C. He told the driver that he could pay the fare by card, not in cash. D. He arrived on the outskirts of a city.
questions.explanation: D brings him to the city, B has him ask a taxi driver to take him to the mall, C has him say he can pay only by card, and A gives the driver's response, driving off without him: DBCA.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options pick the one that gives their correct order. A. He was on a pilgrimage to Jerusalem. B. The villagers were kind though doubtful. C. They offered him some food to eat and a room to stay. D. One night, he took rest in a village unfamiliar on the way.
questions.explanation: A introduces the pilgrim, D has him rest one night in a village on the way, B describes the villagers and C, opening with 'They', says what they offered him: ADBC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Falling head over heels
options: Feeling deep sympathy to the needy
Falling deeply in love with someone
questions.explanation: To fall 'head over heels' (in love) is to fall deeply and suddenly in love with someone.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Children need special care and ______ from the side of their parents for making them emotionally strong.
questions.explanation: Children need care and 'attention' from their parents to grow emotionally strong; 'compromise', 'suspicion' and 'reflection' do not fit the sense.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. This android can perform all the programmes perfectly well.
options: All the programmes could have been performed perfectly well by this android.
All the programmes can have been performed perfectly well by this android.
All the programmes can be performed perfectly well by this android.
All the programmes could be performed perfectly well by this android.
questions.explanation: A modal passive is modal + 'be' + past participle, and the tense stays the same: 'can perform' becomes 'can be performed'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A person living in the same age with another
questions.explanation: A contemporary is a person living or active at the same time as another. A confidant is a person one confides in.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. DISPUTE
questions.explanation: To 'dispute' a claim is to argue against it; to 'concede' it is to accept that it is true. 'Quarrel' is close in meaning to 'dispute', and 'impute' means to attribute.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Cats cannot be blamed for its behaviour to their masters as they are tamed so.
questions.explanation: The pronoun must agree with the plural 'cats': 'for their behaviour'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. The selection to the police department raised him “as high to” a kite.
questions.explanation: A comparison of equality takes 'as ... as': 'raised him as high as a kite'.

questions.text: Who won the Sahitya Akademi Award 2019 in Hindi?
questions.explanation: Nand Kishore Acharya received the 2019 Sahitya Akademi Award in Hindi for his poetry collection 'Chheelatey Hue Apne Ko'. Chitra Mudgal won it for 2018, Ramesh Kuntal Megh for 2017 and Nasira Sharma for 2016.

questions.text: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) was established in:
questions.explanation: NABARD was set up by an Act of Parliament on 12 July 1982 as the apex development bank for agriculture and rural development.

questions.text: Jitu Rai is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: Jitu Rai is an Indian pistol shooter and a Commonwealth Games gold medallist.

questions.text: When was the Rovers Cup started?
questions.explanation: The Rovers Cup, one of India's oldest football tournaments, was instituted in Bombay (Mumbai) in 1891, after a forerunner played in 1890.

questions.text: Salsette Island is situated in which state of India?
questions.explanation: Salsette Island, on which most of Mumbai and part of Thane stand, is in Maharashtra.

questions.text: How many Lok Sabha constituencies are there in Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan elects 25 members to the Lok Sabha.

questions.text: GST was introduced by which amendment act of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016 brought in the Goods and Services Tax and provided for the GST Council (Article 279A).

questions.text: Which of the following is one of the sacred books of Buddhism?
questions.explanation: The Tripitaka ('three baskets': the Vinaya, Sutta and Abhidhamma Pitakas) is the Buddhist canon. The Avesta is Zoroastrian, the Kalpa Sutra Jain and the Torah Jewish.

questions.text: Lipulekh Pass is in which state of India?
questions.explanation: Lipulekh Pass, in the Pithoragarh district of Uttarakhand, crosses into Tibet and is a route of the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra.

questions.text: How many people were awarded Padma Vibhushan in 2019?
questions.explanation: Four people received the Padma Vibhushan in 2019: Teejan Bai, Ismail Omar Guelleh (President of Djibouti), Anilkumar Manibhai Naik and Balwant Moreshwar Purandare.

questions.text: Which film won the Golden Globe Awards 2020 for Best Picture - Drama?
questions.explanation: Sam Mendes's war film '1917' won Best Motion Picture - Drama at the Golden Globe Awards in January 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following kingdoms consists of prokaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: In Whittaker's five-kingdom classification, Monera holds the prokaryotes, such as bacteria, whose cells have no membrane-bound nucleus. Animalia, Fungi and Protista are made up of eukaryotic cells.

questions.text: Shore temple is situated in which state of India?
questions.explanation: The Shore Temple, built under the Pallava king Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha), stands at Mahabalipuram in Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: What did Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen discover?
questions.explanation: Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen discovered X-rays in 1895 and received the first Nobel Prize in Physics, in 1901.

questions.text: What is the atomic weight of Lithium?
questions.explanation: Lithium (atomic number 3) has an atomic weight of about 6.94. The other values are those of beryllium (9.012), boron (10.811) and helium (4.003).

questions.text: Who is/was the 13th President of India?
questions.explanation: Pranab Mukherjee, President from 2012 to 2017, was the 13th President of India. APJ Abdul Kalam was the 11th, Pratibha Patil the 12th and Ram Nath Kovind the 14th.

questions.text: Which function key is used for opening help?
questions.explanation: In most programs, pressing F1 opens Help.

questions.text: Which state has launched the Cyber Safe Woman Campaign in January 2020?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra launched the Cyber Safe Woman campaign on 3 January 2020, with the state's cyber police holding awareness sessions across its districts on how to guard against crime online.

questions.text: Lavani is a folk music of which state?
questions.explanation: Lavani, a song-and-dance form performed to the beat of the dholki, is a folk tradition of Maharashtra.

questions.text: In Tibet, the Brahmaputra river is known as:
questions.explanation: In Tibet the Brahmaputra is the Tsangpo (Yarlung Tsangpo). It becomes the Siang or Dihang in Arunachal Pradesh, and the Lohit is one of its tributaries.

questions.text: When was WhatsApp incorporated?
questions.explanation: Jan Koum and Brian Acton founded WhatsApp, and WhatsApp Inc. was incorporated in California in February 2009.

questions.text: Which of the following countries was the runner up in the 2019 ICC Cricket World cup?
questions.explanation: New Zealand were runners-up in the 2019 World Cup: the final at Lord's against England was tied, as was the Super Over, and England won on boundary count.

questions.text: Where is the Dudhsagar waterfalls located?
questions.explanation: Dudhsagar Falls is on the Mandovi river in Goa, near the Goa-Karnataka border.

questions.text: What was the theme of the International Yoga Day 2019?
questions.explanation: The theme of the fifth International Day of Yoga, 21 June 2019, was 'Yoga for Climate Action'.

questions.text: Vivekananda Rock Memorial is in which state of India?
questions.explanation: The Vivekananda Rock Memorial stands on a rock off Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu, where Swami Vivekananda meditated in 1892.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. PENURY
questions.explanation: 'Penury' means extreme poverty.

questions.text: Select the wrongly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Manifestation', with an 'a' after the 'M'.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The manager was referring about the previous instances of loss to the employees during his address.
questions.explanation: 'Refer' takes the preposition 'to', not 'about': 'The manager was referring to the previous instances of loss'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Although they searched for an hour, they were not able to find the ______ easily.
questions.explanation: After an hour's search they could not find 'the location', the place they were looking for. 'Whereabouts' is normally tied to someone or something ('his whereabouts', 'the whereabouts of the shop').

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Art is the use of (1)______, skill and imagination to create something that’s beautiful or emotionally (2)______. This definition needs to be expanded. If you (3)______ a little deeper, you’ll see that any skill can be considered an art, (4)______ if you exercise a little (5)______ and creativity in the process.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: The definition lists what an artist brings to the work, 'creativity', skill and imagination, and the passage ends by pairing imagination with creativity again. 'Intoxication' and 'destruction' make no sense, and 'emotion' would clash with 'emotionally' later in the sentence.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Art is the use of (1)______, skill and imagination to create something that’s beautiful or emotionally (2)______. This definition needs to be expanded. If you (3)______ a little deeper, you’ll see that any skill can be considered an art, (4)______ if you exercise a little (5)______ and creativity in the process.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
questions.explanation: 'Emotionally' needs an adjective describing the work's effect on the viewer: 'emotionally comforting'. 'Creative', 'imaginative' and 'tempting' do not go with it.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Art is the use of (1)______, skill and imagination to create something that’s beautiful or emotionally (2)______. This definition needs to be expanded. If you (3)______ a little deeper, you’ll see that any skill can be considered an art, (4)______ if you exercise a little (5)______ and creativity in the process.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.
questions.explanation: 'Particularly if' means especially if: any skill can be an art, and all the more so when it is done with imagination and creativity.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Art is the use of (1)______, skill and imagination to create something that’s beautiful or emotionally (2)______. This definition needs to be expanded. If you (3)______ a little deeper, you’ll see that any skill can be considered an art, (4)______ if you exercise a little (5)______ and creativity in the process.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5.
questions.explanation: 'Imagination and creativity' echoes the definition the passage opens with; one 'exercises' imagination, not a dream, hope or desire.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Neither fish nor fowl
options: Something which can neither be supplied easily nor be made available readily
Something which can neither be purchased nor be grown
Something which can neither be eaten nor be preserved
Something which can neither be categorized easily nor be accepted befittingly
questions.explanation: 'Neither fish nor fowl' describes something that belongs to no clear category, so it is hard to classify or to fit in anywhere.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. One of the reason behind malnutrition is the improper way of food intake.
questions.explanation: 'One of' is followed by a plural noun: 'One of the reasons behind malnutrition is ...'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. UNWORTHY
questions.explanation: 'Unworthy' means not deserving (of respect, praise or the like), so its opposite is 'deserving'. 'Trustworthy' is the opposite of 'untrustworthy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. “As long to” funding is not made available, our construction dreams have been deferred.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'So long as', a form of 'as long as' (for as long as, provided that), which repairs the 'to' in the phrase and keeps its sense: the construction stays deferred while there is no funding. 'In as much as' (since) would also make a grammatical sentence, but it turns the condition into a reason.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. The lion asked the lioness, "Where will you hide yourself, until I return?”
options: The lion asked the lioness whether she would hide herself, until he returned.
The lion asked the lioness where she will hide herself, until he returns.
The lion asked the lioness where would she hide herself, until he returned.
The lion asked the lioness where she would hide herself, until he returned.
questions.explanation: The question becomes a clause in statement order, 'where she would hide herself': 'will' moves back to 'would', 'you' and 'yourself' become 'she' and 'herself', and 'I return' becomes 'he returned'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. FESTIVITY
questions.explanation: 'Festivity' means joyful celebration.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. The Inspector had already proved the case before the investigation team took charge of it.
options: The case was already proved by the Inspector before the investigation team took charge of it.
The case had already proved by the Inspector before the investigation team took charge of it.
The case had already been proved by the Inspector before the investigation team took charge of it.
The investigation team took charge of the case but the Inspector had already proved before it.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had proved' becomes 'had been proved' in the passive: 'The case had already been proved by the Inspector before ...'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options select the one that gives their correct order. A. The boat floated down the river and reached the other bank. B. Thinking that she was dead, her friends secretly took her and abandoned her in a boat. C. The people on the bank took her to a hospital and saved her. D. Smelling a flower given by the magician, Shweta fell down unconscious.
questions.explanation: D has Shweta fall unconscious, B has her friends think her dead and set her adrift in a boat, A takes the boat to the other bank and C has people there save her: DBAC.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options select the one that gives their correct order. A. Their classmate, Koushal, hardly studied and spent much of his time wasting on prattles. B. He made himself busy by collecting old pens and used papers in order to avoid studies. C. Poonam, the class teacher, was very much loved and respected by her students. D. Three of them were very intelligent and spent most of their time studying with Poonam.
questions.explanation: C introduces Poonam, the class teacher; D says three of her students studied with her; A brings in their classmate Koushal, who hardly studied; B says what he did instead: CDAB.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A person who studies the structure of the earth
questions.explanation: A geologist studies the structure of the earth, its rocks and their history. A geographer studies the earth's surface and places, and a gemologist gemstones.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. In a fog
questions.explanation: To be 'in a fog' is to be confused and unable to think clearly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. Prithvi likes baseball “as long as” she likes cricket.
questions.explanation: The sentence compares how much she likes the two games, so it needs 'as much as': 'Prithvi likes baseball as much as she likes cricket.' 'As long as' is about time or a condition, and 'as many as' goes with countable nouns.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. The wall fell down with a big ______.
questions.explanation: A 'bang' is a sudden loud noise, the sound of a falling wall. A hiss, a screech and a murmur are quite different sounds.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Condition of sleep during certain parts of the year
questions.explanation: Hibernation is the sleep-like state in which some animals pass the winter. Somnambulism is sleepwalking.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. MAESTRO
questions.explanation: A maestro is a master of an art, especially music; an amateur does something without professional skill. A connoisseur is an expert judge of something.

questions.text: What is the height of Tehri Dam?
questions.explanation: The Tehri Dam on the Bhagirathi in Uttarakhand is 260.5 m high, the tallest dam in India when the exam was held (March 2020).

questions.text: Saga Dawa is the festival of which state?
questions.explanation: Saga Dawa, a major Buddhist festival of Sikkim, falls on the full moon of the fourth lunar month and marks the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and parinirvana.

questions.text: What is the relative density of silver?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 10.8, the figure NCERT's Class 9 science textbook uses for silver in its worked example on relative density (density of silver = 10.8 × 10³ kg/m³). Reference tables give about 10.5 for pure silver (10.49 g/cm³), which is not among the options; the key follows the textbook figure.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Raleigh Commission (1902) was appointed to recommend reforms in:
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon appointed the Indian Universities Commission under Sir Thomas Raleigh in 1902 to review university education; its report led to the Indian Universities Act of 1904.

questions.text: Which state ranked first in Sustainable Development Goals Index 2019-20 released by NITI Aayog of India?
questions.explanation: In NITI Aayog's SDG India Index 2019-20, released in December 2019, Kerala ranked first with a score of 70, ahead of Himachal Pradesh.

questions.text: What type of unemployment is generally found in agricultural sector of India?
questions.explanation: In disguised unemployment more people work on the land than are needed, so some could leave without output falling, as on many of India's small family farms.

questions.text: Who has been declared as 'Men’s Player of the Year 2019' by the International Hockey Federation?
questions.explanation: Manpreet Singh, India's captain at the time, was named the FIH Men's Player of the Year for 2019 in February 2020, the first Indian to win the award.

questions.text: Who was the President of India during the emergency of 1975-1977?
questions.explanation: Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed, President from 1974 until his death in February 1977, proclaimed the Emergency in June 1975; B D Jatti was acting President for its last weeks.

questions.text: Who wrote the famous book 'The God of Small Things'?
questions.explanation: Arundhati Roy's 'The God of Small Things' won the Booker Prize in 1997.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When was the Treaty of Amritsar signed?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Amritsar between Maharaja Ranjit Singh and the East India Company, negotiated by Charles Metcalfe, was signed in April 1809 and fixed the Sutlej as the boundary between them. (A second Treaty of Amritsar, of 1846, transferred Kashmir to Gulab Singh.)

questions.text: When was the Secretariat of the SAARC set up?
questions.explanation: The SAARC Secretariat was set up in Kathmandu in January 1987; SAARC itself was founded at Dhaka in December 1985.

questions.text: Proteins are assembled from how many amino acids?
questions.explanation: Proteins are built from 20 standard amino acids, the ones the genetic code specifies.

questions.text: In the field of computing, what does VGA stand for?
questions.explanation: VGA, Video Graphics Array, is the display standard IBM introduced in 1987, with a resolution of 640 × 480.

questions.text: Which of the following types of organisms have an open circulatory system?
questions.explanation: In most molluscs, as in arthropods, blood is pumped into open spaces that bathe the organs (squids and octopuses are exceptions). Annelids and birds have closed circulatory systems, and nematodes have none.

questions.text: When was the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act enacted?
questions.explanation: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978, passed after the Emergency, undid many changes of the 42nd Amendment and removed the right to property from the Fundamental Rights.

questions.text: Dachigam National Park is in which state of India?
questions.explanation: Dachigam National Park, near Srinagar, is the main home of the hangul, the Kashmir stag. Jammu and Kashmir had become a union territory in October 2019, a few months before this exam.

questions.text: Which award has been given to Narthaki Nataraj in 2019?
questions.explanation: The Bharatanatyam dancer Narthaki Nataraj of Tamil Nadu received the Padma Shri in 2019, the first transgender person to receive it.

questions.text: How many Indian states share border with Bhutan?
questions.explanation: Four states border Bhutan: Sikkim, West Bengal, Assam and Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.text: Magnus Carlsen is associated with which game?
questions.explanation: Magnus Carlsen of Norway is a chess player; when the exam was held (March 2020) he was world champion, a title he had held since 2013.

questions.text: Who is the newest Chief of Indian Army in December 2019?
questions.explanation: General Manoj Mukund Naravane took over as Chief of the Army Staff on 31 December 2019, when General Bipin Rawat stepped down to become India's first Chief of Defence Staff.

questions.text: When was the Eden Gardens Stadium, Kolkata established?
questions.explanation: Eden Gardens, the cricket ground in Kolkata, was established in 1864.

questions.text: When was Safari first released by Apple?
questions.explanation: Apple released its Safari web browser in 2003, first as a public beta for Mac OS X in January.

questions.text: Who among the following was one of the recipients of Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award 2019?
questions.explanation: The para-athlete Deepa Malik and the wrestler Bajrang Punia received the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna for 2019. P V Sindhu (2016), Sania Mirza (2015) and Virat Kohli (2018) received it in earlier years.

questions.text: Ustad Alladiya Khan belongs to which gharana of Hindustani music?
questions.explanation: Ustad Alladiya Khan founded the Jaipur (Jaipur-Atrauli) gharana of khayal singing.

questions.text: What is the sex ratio of Kerala as per census 2011?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Kerala had 1,084 females per 1,000 males, the highest sex ratio of any state.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Vanish into the air
questions.explanation: To 'vanish into the air' (more often 'into thin air') is to disappear completely, leaving no trace.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. Shanti asked me, "Why did you keep this smartphone in the bin?"
options: Shanti asked me why I had been keeping that smartphone in the bin.
Shanti asked me why I kept that smartphone in the bin.
Shanti asked me why I was keeping that smartphone in the bin.
Shanti asked me why I had kept that smartphone in the bin.
questions.explanation: In reported speech the question becomes a statement ('why I had kept'), the simple past 'did you keep' moves back to the past perfect, 'you' becomes 'I' and 'this' becomes 'that'.

questions.text: Select the wrongly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'definition'.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. The students have performed a new version of Shakespeare's 'Macbeth'.
options: Shakespeare's 'Macbeth' have been performed by the new version of the students.
A new version of Shakespeare's 'Macbeth' have been performed by the students.
A new version of Shakespeare's 'Macbeth' has been performed by the students.
Shakespeare's 'Macbeth' has been performed by the new version of the students.
questions.explanation: The object 'a new version' becomes the singular subject, so the present perfect 'have performed' becomes 'has been performed', with 'by the students' at the end.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The internet is fast becoming trusted by (1)______ children and adults as reliable and accurate (2)______ of information. Through the internet children now have (3)______ to an almost endless supply of information and opportunity for (4)______. However, there can be real risks and dangers for an (5)______ child.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: 'Both ... and' joins the two groups, children and adults, who trust the internet.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The internet is fast becoming trusted by (1)______ children and adults as reliable and accurate (2)______ of information. Through the internet children now have (3)______ to an almost endless supply of information and opportunity for (4)______. However, there can be real risks and dangers for an (5)______ child.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
questions.explanation: The internet is a 'source' of information, the place it comes from.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The internet is fast becoming trusted by (1)______ children and adults as reliable and accurate (2)______ of information. Through the internet children now have (3)______ to an almost endless supply of information and opportunity for (4)______. However, there can be real risks and dangers for an (5)______ child.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3.
questions.explanation: To 'have access to' something is to be able to reach and use it.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The internet is fast becoming trusted by (1)______ children and adults as reliable and accurate (2)______ of information. Through the internet children now have (3)______ to an almost endless supply of information and opportunity for (4)______. However, there can be real risks and dangers for an (5)______ child.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.
