questions.explanation: Besides information, the internet gives children the chance to communicate with others: 'opportunity for interaction'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The internet is fast becoming trusted by (1)______ children and adults as reliable and accurate (2)______ of information. Through the internet children now have (3)______ to an almost endless supply of information and opportunity for (4)______. However, there can be real risks and dangers for an (5)______ child.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5.
questions.explanation: The risks fall on a child left 'unsupervised', with no adult watching over what they do online.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. Before it was modified, the Law “provided with” the owner could take possession of the goods at any time.
questions.explanation: Of a law, 'provided that' means 'laid down that': 'the Law provided that the owner could take possession of the goods at any time.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. JOVIAL
questions.explanation: 'Jovial' means cheerful and friendly: 'joyous'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. I had a broken bone in the hand which the doctor called a ______ and suggested immediate surgery.
questions.explanation: A broken bone is a 'fracture'; a wound, an infection or contamination is not a break in a bone.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. CHOOSY
questions.explanation: A 'choosy' person is careful about what they choose: 'selective'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. She has shown a great interest towards space science, since her early childhood and a passion to ______ the outer space.
questions.explanation: Someone with a passion for space science wants to 'explore' outer space, that is travel through it to learn about it.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A person who is neither well experienced nor professional
questions.explanation: An 'amateur' does something without professional training or experience. A veteran, an expert and a proficient person are all skilled.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. OBSCURE
questions.explanation: 'Obscure' means unclear or hard to understand, so its opposite is 'clear'. 'Uncertain', 'ambiguous' and 'vague' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options select the one that gives their correct order. A. In the evening, Tejaswini would sing songs praising the Lord. B. She would go to the Lord’s temple twice a day. C. Tejaswini was known in the village for her devotion to the Lord. D. In the morning, she would take with her a pot of milk and a bunch of flowers as offering.
questions.explanation: C introduces Tejaswini and her devotion, B says she went to the temple twice a day, and D and A describe the morning and evening visits in turn: CBDA.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options select the one that gives their correct order. A. One day, a strange crow from the west, landed on one of the branches. B. There was a large mango tree deep inside a thick forest. C. The branches were full of leaves, which crackled when the storm blew. D. Its branches spread in all directions, lobbing a large shadow on the ground.
questions.explanation: B introduces the mango tree, D describes its spreading branches ('Its' refers to the tree), C the leaves on them, and A brings in the crow 'one day': BDCA.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. “As of” you are here with me, who cares about the outcome of the issue.
questions.explanation: 'As long as' means 'since' or 'so long as' here: 'As long as you are here with me, who cares about the outcome'. 'As of' means 'from' a time; 'so long' lacks its 'as', and 'as long to' is not an English phrase.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Take one's hat off to someone
questions.explanation: To 'take one's hat off to' someone is to show admiration or respect for them.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Though she was able to finish the work on time, she couldn't do that out in fear.
questions.explanation: An action done because of fear is done 'out of fear', not 'out in fear'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. EARTHLY
questions.explanation: 'Earthly' means belonging to this world; its opposite is 'celestial', belonging to the sky or heaven. 'Temporal' is close to 'earthly' in meaning.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Something which is considered to be very important
questions.explanation: 'Cardinal' means of the greatest importance, as in 'a cardinal rule'. 'Supplementary' means extra, and 'scanty' and 'meagre' mean too little.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. Thomas is a man of word who have been paying back the borrowed money in instalments.
options: Thomas is a man of word
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'who have been paying back': 'who' refers to 'a man', so the verb must be singular, 'who has been paying back'. The first segment is also open to question, as the idiom is 'a man of his word', but the agreement error is the plain grammatical one.

questions.text: Who among the following was appointed as the Deputy Governor of Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in January 2020?
questions.explanation: Michael Debabrata Patra was appointed a Deputy Governor of the RBI in January 2020, filling the post left vacant when Viral Acharya resigned in 2019.

questions.text: In the context of memory size in computer data storage, one gigabyte is equal to how many megabytes?
questions.explanation: Memory sizes go in powers of 2: 1 GB = 2¹⁰ MB = 1,024 MB.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a credit rating agency in India?
questions.explanation: CRISIL, ICRA and CARE are credit rating agencies registered with SEBI. The RBI is India's central bank, which regulates banks; it does not rate borrowers.

questions.text: Who among the following was conferred with the ‘Dadasaheb Phalke Award 2019’?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Amitabh Bachchan, who was named for the Dadasaheb Phalke Award, India's highest film honour, in September 2019 and received it that December. Officially it was the 50th award, the one for 2018; the award for 2019, announced in 2021, after the exam, went to Rajinikanth, who is not among the options.

questions.text: Who among the following took charge as India’s first Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) on 1 January 2020?
options: Air Chief Marshal Rakesh Kumar Singh Bhadauria
questions.explanation: General Bipin Rawat, who had retired as Chief of the Army Staff the day before, took charge as India's first Chief of Defence Staff on 1 January 2020.

questions.text: Who among the following won ICC’s ‘2019 Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy’?
questions.explanation: Ben Stokes of England won the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy, the ICC's award for the cricketer of the year, for 2019; the award was announced in January 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following articles of the Constitution of India has a provision for financial emergency?
questions.explanation: Article 360 lets the President proclaim a financial emergency when the financial stability or credit of India is threatened. Article 356 deals with President's rule in a state and Article 330 with seats reserved for SCs and STs in the Lok Sabha.

questions.text: Which is the largest uranium producing country in the world?
questions.explanation: Kazakhstan, which has led world uranium mining since 2009, was the largest producer when the exam was held in March 2020.

questions.text: Under which of the following schemes has the Government of India set up a new institution for development and refinancing activities related to micro units?
questions.explanation: MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency) was set up in 2015 under the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana to refinance the lenders that give small loans to micro units.

questions.text: ______ is the term used for breeding of fish in specially constructed tanks and ponds.
questions.explanation: Pisciculture is fish farming. Viticulture is the growing of grapes, and horticulture the growing of fruit, vegetables and flowers.

questions.text: Who among the following scientists invented dynamite?
questions.explanation: Alfred Nobel, the Swedish chemist, invented dynamite and patented it in 1867; his fortune later funded the Nobel Prizes.

questions.text: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly of India?
questions.explanation: Dr B R Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee, set up on 29 August 1947. Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly.

questions.text: Which of the following cities hosted the third edition of the Khelo India Youth Games?
questions.explanation: Guwahati, Assam, hosted the third edition in January 2020, after Delhi (2018, as the Khelo India School Games) and Pune (2019).

questions.text: ‘Gurpurab’ is the most important and sacred festival of the Sikh community. In which of the following months of the Hindu calendar is it celebrated?
questions.explanation: Guru Nanak's Gurpurab, his birth anniversary, is celebrated on Kartik Purnima, the full moon of Kartik (October-November).

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following years did India come under the direct rule of the British crown?
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act 1858, passed after the revolt of 1857, ended the East India Company's rule and placed India directly under the British Crown.

questions.text: The rhythmic rise and fall of ocean water twice in a day is called ______.
questions.explanation: Tides are the regular rise and fall of sea level caused mainly by the Moon's pull, with the Sun's; most coasts have two high tides and two low tides a day.

questions.text: The ‘Kathakali’ dance is a harmonious combination of ______ forms of fine art.
questions.explanation: Kathakali is traditionally described as bringing together five fine arts: literature (sahityam), music (sangeetham), painting (chithram), acting (natyam) and dance (nritham).

questions.text: Which of the following scientists was awarded a Nobel Prize for his services to Theoretical Physics, and especially for his discovery of the Law of the Photoelectric Effect?
questions.explanation: Albert Einstein received the Nobel Prize in Physics for 1921; the citation singled out his law of the photoelectric effect rather than relativity.

questions.text: Who among the following won the ‘Women's World Rapid Chess Championship 2019’?
questions.explanation: Koneru Humpy won the Women's World Rapid Chess Championship in Moscow in December 2019, beating China's Lei Tingjie in an Armageddon tie-break.

questions.text: A hard disk is an example of which type of data storage device?
questions.explanation: A hard disk keeps data with the power off and is not worked on directly by the processor as RAM is, so it is secondary storage; RAM is primary storage.

questions.text: Which of the following teams won the 129th edition of Durand Cup in August 2019?
questions.explanation: Gokulam Kerala beat Mohun Bagan 2-1 in the final in Kolkata in August 2019 to win the 129th Durand Cup.

questions.text: Which of the following is a disease caused by protozoa?
questions.explanation: Kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) is caused by the protozoan Leishmania donovani and spread by sandflies. AIDS, smallpox and rabies are caused by viruses.

questions.text: What was India’s overall rank in the medals tally in the 23rd edition of the Asian Athletics Championship?
questions.explanation: When the exam was held in March 2020, India stood fourth in the medal table of the 23rd Asian Athletics Championships (Doha, April 2019), with three gold medals, behind Bahrain, China and Japan. In June 2020 Gomathi Marimuthu's 800 m gold was annulled for doping, and the revised table puts India fifth.

questions.text: Tummalapalle, believed to have one of the largest uranium reserves in the world, is situated in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Tummalapalle, in the Kadapa (YSR) district of Andhra Pradesh, is where the Uranium Corporation of India mines uranium.

questions.text: Select the alternative that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case there is no improvement select ‘No improvement’. Priya has been working in this school “from June 2017” .
questions.explanation: With the present perfect continuous 'has been working', 'since' gives the point in time the action started from: 'since June 2017'. 'For' goes with a length of time ('for three years').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. KIT
questions.explanation: A kit is a set of tools or equipment for a particular purpose, such as a first-aid kit: 'equipment'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom. Touch all bases
questions.explanation: To 'touch all bases' is to deal with every part of a matter, leaving nothing out: 'include everything'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. VERSATILE
questions.explanation: 'Versatile' means able to adapt to many different uses or tasks; its opposite is 'inflexible'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The Great Stupa at Sanchi is one of the oldest stone structures in India. It was originally commissioned (1)______ Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. Its nucleus (2)______ a simple hemispherical brick structure built (3)______ the relics of the Buddha. It was crowned by the chhatri, a parasol-like (4)______ symbolising high rank, which was (5)______ to honour and shelter the relics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.1.
questions.explanation: A work is commissioned 'by' the person who orders it: 'commissioned by Emperor Ashoka'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The Great Stupa at Sanchi is one of the oldest stone structures in India. It was originally commissioned (1)______ Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. Its nucleus (2)______ a simple hemispherical brick structure built (3)______ the relics of the Buddha. It was crowned by the chhatri, a parasol-like (4)______ symbolising high rank, which was (5)______ to honour and shelter the relics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.2.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'Its nucleus' takes the singular past 'was': 'Its nucleus was a simple hemispherical brick structure'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The Great Stupa at Sanchi is one of the oldest stone structures in India. It was originally commissioned (1)______ Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. Its nucleus (2)______ a simple hemispherical brick structure built (3)______ the relics of the Buddha. It was crowned by the chhatri, a parasol-like (4)______ symbolising high rank, which was (5)______ to honour and shelter the relics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.3.
questions.explanation: The brick dome was built 'over' the relics of the Buddha, covering them.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The Great Stupa at Sanchi is one of the oldest stone structures in India. It was originally commissioned (1)______ Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. Its nucleus (2)______ a simple hemispherical brick structure built (3)______ the relics of the Buddha. It was crowned by the chhatri, a parasol-like (4)______ symbolising high rank, which was (5)______ to honour and shelter the relics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.4.
questions.explanation: The chhatri was a parasol-like 'structure' set on top of the stupa; a bridge, a conduit or a wall is not shaped like a parasol.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The Great Stupa at Sanchi is one of the oldest stone structures in India. It was originally commissioned (1)______ Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. Its nucleus (2)______ a simple hemispherical brick structure built (3)______ the relics of the Buddha. It was crowned by the chhatri, a parasol-like (4)______ symbolising high rank, which was (5)______ to honour and shelter the relics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.5.
questions.explanation: Its purpose is given: the chhatri 'was intended to honour and shelter the relics'.

questions.text: Select the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error. Oh dear! The audio in one of the channel on television is not clear at all.
questions.explanation: 'One of' is followed by a plural noun: 'in one of the channels'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. ANODYNE
questions.explanation: 'Anodyne' means harmless and unlikely to offend or upset anyone: 'benign'. 'Harmful' and 'hostile' are nearly its opposites.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order. A. Mulla Nasruddin opened a hair-cutting salon and was ready to welcome his customers. B. “Mulla,” he said sheepishly, “my new wife is coming home today.” C. “Just take out all the grey strands from my beard and make me look very young.” D. Being the first day, a lot of people came and among them was a man in his early fifties with a flowing beard.
questions.explanation: A introduces the new salon, D the crowd on the first day and the bearded man among them, B has him begin to speak and C gives his request: ADBC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. NEBULOUS
questions.explanation: 'Nebulous' means vague or hazy, not clearly defined; its opposite is 'clear'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Small room where dishes are washed
questions.explanation: A scullery is a small room next to a kitchen where dishes are washed. A pantry and a larder are for storing food, and an ante-room leads into a larger room.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Earthquake inspection ______ that the two ancient buildings that remained intact after the Hiroshima bombing in Tokyo would not withstand a strong tremor.
questions.explanation: An inspection 'revealed', that is brought to light, that the buildings would not withstand a strong tremor.

questions.text: Select the word with the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: 'Impeccable' is spelt correctly; the others should be 'impressionable', 'susceptible' and 'propensity'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. The police was able to find the guilty but “the big fish” escaped.
questions.explanation: 'Big fish' are the important or powerful people in a group: the minor offenders were caught, but the main leaders escaped.

questions.text: Select the option that is the direct form of the sentence. Kirti asked me if I had watched the movie on television the previous night.
options: Kirti asked me, “You had watched the movie on television last night?”
Kirti asked me, “Had you watched the movie on television last night?”
Kirti asked me, “Did you watch the movie on television last night?”
Kirti asked me, “Did I watched the movie on television last night?”
questions.explanation: Back in direct speech the reported past perfect 'had watched' becomes the simple past, the tense for one finished action at a stated time such as 'last night' (reported as 'the previous night'). The yes/no question therefore opens with 'Did you': 'Did you watch the movie on television last night?'

questions.text: Select the alternative that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case there is no improvement select ‘No improvement’. The struggle for climate change “must be prioritised” given that our population is increasing and not decreasing.
questions.explanation: 'Must be prioritised' is a correct passive with 'must', saying the struggle needs to be given priority; the options change the sense or the voice, so no improvement is needed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The reporter asked the politician, “As a woman leader, what are some of the major ______ that you face?”
questions.explanation: A leader 'faces challenges', difficulties that test their ability; 'crunches', 'contests' and 'crashes' do not fit the sense.

questions.text: Select the option that is the passive form of the sentence. The batsman had hit the ball towards the boundary.
options: The ball is hit towards the boundary by the batsman.
The ball is being hit towards the boundary by the batsman.
The ball was hit towards the boundary by the batsman.
The ball had been hit towards the boundary by the batsman.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had hit' becomes the past perfect passive 'had been hit': 'The ball had been hit towards the boundary by the batsman.'

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Person or thing that is the centre of attention
questions.explanation: A cynosure is a person or thing that is the centre of attention or admiration.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error. It is difficult to make out that they are twins because they do not resemble to each other.
options: It is difficult to make out
questions.explanation: 'Resemble' takes its object directly, without 'to': 'they do not resemble each other'.

questions.text: Select the word with the INCORRECT spelling.
questions.explanation: 'Medetative' is misspelt: the word is 'meditative', from 'meditate'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order. A. Waqar instead gave it to Afridi, who went on to score a 37-ball century, the fastest ODI century. B. That was when his teammate Waqar Younis handed him over a bat that belonged to Sachin Tendulkar. C. When Shahid Afridi had flown in to join the Pakistan team 1996, he did not even have a proper bat to play with. D. Sachin had earlier gifted Waqar his bat to take to Sialkot, Pakistan’s world famous sports goods manufacturing capital and get a custom-made one replicated there.
questions.explanation: C sets the scene (Afridi joining the team without a proper bat), B says Waqar handed him a bat that was Sachin's, D explains how Waqar had come to have it, and A says what Afridi did with it: CBDA.

questions.text: Which among the following financial institutions was nationalised in 1949?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India, set up in 1935 as a shareholders' bank, was nationalised on 1 January 1949. PNB was nationalised in 1969, IFCI was set up in 1948 and SIDBI in 1990.

questions.text: Which of the following activities can be classified as a part of secondary sector of an economy?
questions.explanation: The secondary sector turns raw materials into goods, as in manufacturing farm equipment. Tea plantation is primary, and legal consulting and banking are services (tertiary).

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Phodong monastery situated?
questions.explanation: Phodong Monastery, a Buddhist monastery, is in North Sikkim.

questions.text: Which of the following nations won the inaugural ATP Cup tennis tournament in January 2020?
questions.explanation: Serbia, led by Novak Djokovic, won the first ATP Cup, beating Spain in the final in Sydney in January 2020.

questions.text: Who has been appointed the Director General of the National Security Guard (NSG) in October 2019?
questions.explanation: Anup Kumar Singh, an IPS officer, was appointed Director General of the National Security Guard in October 2019.

questions.text: Which one of the following nations finished the year 2019 as the top shooting nation in the world as per the International Shooting Sport Federation’s (ISSF) overall rankings for 2019?
questions.explanation: India ended 2019 at the top of the ISSF's overall rankings, after leading the medal tables at that year's rifle and pistol World Cups.

questions.text: The 2019 Nobel Peace Prize has been awarded to the Ethiopian Prime Minister, Abiy Ahmed Ali, particularly for his efforts to resolve border dispute with:
questions.explanation: Abiy Ahmed received the 2019 Nobel Peace Prize for his work for peace, and above all for his initiative to end the long border conflict with neighbouring Eritrea.

questions.text: Who among the following was chosen as the Time Magazine’s 2019 Person of the year?
questions.explanation: The Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg, then 16, was Time magazine's Person of the Year for 2019, the youngest chosen up to then.

questions.text: Which of the following is an input device that utilises a light-sensitive detector to select objects on a display screen?
questions.explanation: A light pen is a pen-shaped pointing device with a light-sensitive detector in its tip, used to select objects or draw on a display screen.

questions.text: Which of the following nations ‘unintentionally’ shot down a Ukrainian Boeing 737-800 passenger aircraft in January 2020?
questions.explanation: Iran's forces shot down Ukraine International Airlines Flight 752, a Boeing 737-800, soon after it took off from Tehran on 8 January 2020; Iran later admitted it had done so unintentionally.

questions.text: What was the focal theme of the 107th Indian Science Congress held at Bengaluru in January 2020?
options: Science and Technology: Water Resources Development
Science and Technology: Renewable Energy Development
questions.explanation: The 107th Indian Science Congress, held at the University of Agricultural Sciences, Bengaluru, in January 2020, had the theme 'Science and Technology: Rural Development'.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about Sambhar lake is true?
options: It is the highest lake in India.
It was formed due to hypervelocity impact of a comet.
It drains into the Arabian sea.
It is the largest inland salt lake in India.
questions.explanation: Sambhar Lake in Rajasthan is the largest inland salt lake in India. It has no outlet to the sea, and it is Lonar Lake in Maharashtra that was formed by a meteorite impact.

questions.text: Which among the following is the oldest mountain/hill range in India?
questions.explanation: The Aravallis are the oldest fold mountains in India, worn down over a very long time; the Himalayas are among the youngest mountains in the world.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was the Prime Minister of Britain/UK when British Parliament passed an independence bill for India in July 1947?
questions.explanation: The Indian Independence Act was passed by the British Parliament in July 1947, when Clement Attlee of the Labour Party was Prime Minister.

questions.text: The process of impeachment of the President of India can be initiated in:
options: Rajya Sabha but not in Lok Sabha
Lok Sabha but not in Rajya Sabha
Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha or any state legislative assembly
questions.explanation: Under Article 61 the charge for impeaching the President may be brought by either House of Parliament, and the other House investigates it. State legislatures have no part in impeachment.

questions.text: The speed of the Central Processing Unit (CPU) is measured in_________, which represents a CPU cycle.
questions.explanation: A CPU's clock speed is measured in hertz, cycles per second, usually given in megahertz or gigahertz. Kilobytes, gigabytes and terabytes measure storage.

questions.text: Who among the following won ICC’s '2019 ODI Cricketer of The Year' award?
questions.explanation: Rohit Sharma, who scored five centuries at the 2019 World Cup, was named the ICC's ODI Cricketer of the Year for 2019 in January 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following crops is an example of Kharif Crops?
questions.explanation: Cotton is sown at the start of the south-west monsoon and harvested in autumn, a kharif crop. Gram, pea and wheat are rabi crops, sown in winter.

questions.text: In which year did Telangana become the 29th state of India?
questions.explanation: Telangana was carved out of Andhra Pradesh and became India's 29th state on 2 June 2014.

questions.text: With which of the following states/union territories is the Dumhal folk dance associated?
questions.explanation: Dumhal is a folk dance of Kashmir, performed by men of the Wattal community.

questions.text: The earthquake waves are recorded by an instrument called:
questions.explanation: A seismograph records the waves of an earthquake. The Richter scale is not an instrument but a scale for an earthquake's magnitude.

questions.text: Which causative microorganism is responsible for the common cold and influenza (flu)?
questions.explanation: The common cold and influenza are viral infections, caused mainly by rhinoviruses and influenza viruses respectively.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers flows into the Bay of Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Krishna flows east across the Deccan into the Bay of Bengal. The Sutlej, Beas and Ravi belong to the Indus system, which drains into the Arabian Sea.

questions.text: Which among the following states has the highest representation in the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh had 80 Lok Sabha seats when the exam was held (March 2020), the most of any state, against 39 for Tamil Nadu and 25 each for Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. EXPLICIT
questions.explanation: 'Explicit' means stated clearly and fully, leaving no doubt: 'lucid', clearly expressed. 'Equivocal' and 'unintelligible' are nearly opposite.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The simplest way to get proper recognition are through doing things with dedication and sincerity.
questions.explanation: The subject, 'The simplest way', is singular, so the verb must be 'is', not 'are': 'The simplest way to get proper recognition is through doing things'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A person who speaks always in praise of himself
questions.explanation: An egotist is a self-centred person who talks constantly about himself. An evangelist preaches a religion, and a conventionalist follows custom.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Cut to the chase
options: Talking about the important point and leaving out the detail
Sleeping long hours and spoiling the health
Cutting long pieces and spoiling the dish cooked
Stopping unexpectedly and missing the chase
questions.explanation: To 'cut to the chase' is to come straight to the point without wasting time on detail.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Everyone wants to be happy. I also want to be happy (1)______ that's when I am at my best. I know that happiness comes from (2)______ me, not from outside. The (3)______ tools I will have to learn to use here will only work if I understand that I’m in (4)______ of my thoughts, actions and emotions and if I’m willing to do some simple exercises on a (5)______ basis.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: The clause gives the reason for wanting to be happy: 'because that's when I am at my best'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Everyone wants to be happy. I also want to be happy (1)______ that's when I am at my best. I know that happiness comes from (2)______ me, not from outside. The (3)______ tools I will have to learn to use here will only work if I understand that I’m in (4)______ of my thoughts, actions and emotions and if I’m willing to do some simple exercises on a (5)______ basis.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 2.
questions.explanation: Happiness comes from 'within' me, set against 'not from outside'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Everyone wants to be happy. I also want to be happy (1)______ that's when I am at my best. I know that happiness comes from (2)______ me, not from outside. The (3)______ tools I will have to learn to use here will only work if I understand that I’m in (4)______ of my thoughts, actions and emotions and if I’m willing to do some simple exercises on a (5)______ basis.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 3.
questions.explanation: 'Powerful tools' are strong, effective ones that work if used well. 'Affective' means to do with feelings, and 'effortless' does not suit tools one has to learn to use.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Everyone wants to be happy. I also want to be happy (1)______ that's when I am at my best. I know that happiness comes from (2)______ me, not from outside. The (3)______ tools I will have to learn to use here will only work if I understand that I’m in (4)______ of my thoughts, actions and emotions and if I’m willing to do some simple exercises on a (5)______ basis.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 4.
questions.explanation: To be 'in charge of' something is to be in control of it: 'I'm in charge of my thoughts, actions and emotions'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Everyone wants to be happy. I also want to be happy (1)______ that's when I am at my best. I know that happiness comes from (2)______ me, not from outside. The (3)______ tools I will have to learn to use here will only work if I understand that I’m in (4)______ of my thoughts, actions and emotions and if I’m willing to do some simple exercises on a (5)______ basis.

Select the most appropriate option for blank No. 5.
questions.explanation: Exercises done 'on a regular basis' are done regularly, which is how simple exercises work.

questions.text: Select the wrongly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'environment', with no 'o' after the 'i'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. “As long as” they are here, Hari won’t attend the training.
questions.explanation: 'As long as' means while, or provided that, and fits the sentence as it stands. 'So long so' and 'As long that' are not English, and 'so far as' means to the extent that.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. PLACATE
questions.explanation: To 'placate' is to calm someone's anger, so the opposite is 'enrage'. 'Conciliate', 'propitiate' and 'appease' mean the same as 'placate'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. CLOUDY
questions.explanation: 'Cloudy' means not clear, as a cloudy liquid is murky, so the opposite is 'transparent'. 'Indefinite', 'vague' and 'murky' are all close to 'cloudy'.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options select the one that gives their correct order. A. Though John found none, he was not ready to give in. B. He continued the search till noon. C. John wanted to have a big well dug. D. He searched around for workers who would do the job for him without pay.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives CDAB: C states John's aim, D his search for workers who would dig without pay, and A, whose 'none' points back to those workers, says he found none but would not give up, which leads to B, 'He continued the search till noon.' CDBA, putting the long search before the failure, also reads smoothly, but it separates 'none' from 'workers'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. INSTIGATE
questions.explanation: To 'instigate' is to set something going or stir it up, as one may 'kindle' anger or a quarrel. 'Stagnate' is nearly opposite, and to 'instill' or 'imbibe' an idea is to put it in or take it in gradually.

questions.text: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence. Sheetal might have misplaced Mohan’s wallet in their rush.
options: Mohan’s wallet might have been misplaced by Sheetal in their rush.
Mohan’s wallet might be misplaced by Sheetal in their rush.
Mohan’s wallet may be misplaced by Sheetal in their rush.
Mohan’s wallet may have been misplaced by Sheetal in their rush.
questions.explanation: The modal perfect 'might have misplaced' becomes 'might have been misplaced' in the passive: 'Mohan's wallet might have been misplaced by Sheetal in their rush.'

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Painless death given to patients to relieve suffering.
questions.explanation: Euthanasia is the painless killing of a patient suffering from an incurable, painful illness. Euphoria is intense happiness, a euphemism a mild word used in place of a harsh one, and Euphorbia a genus of plants.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Success is the ______ of taking risks, everybody knows.
questions.explanation: A 'by-product' is something that comes about as a result of something else: success follows from taking risks.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Keep a civil tongue
questions.explanation: To 'keep a civil tongue (in one's head)' is to speak politely and not rudely.

questions.text: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence. The storekeeper asked the security, "Did you see the torch I kept here?"
options: The storekeeper asked the security whether he saw the torch he had kept there.
The storekeeper asked the security if he saw the torch he kept there.
The storekeeper asked the security if had he seen the torch he kept there.
The storekeeper asked the security whether he had seen the torch he had kept there.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with 'whether' or 'if' in statement order; after the past reporting verb 'asked', 'did you see' and 'I kept' move back to 'he had seen' and 'he had kept', and 'here' becomes 'there'.

questions.text: In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error. The man with a lost eye have been accused for murder of two girls in his neighbourhood.
options: The man with a lost eye
questions.explanation: The subject 'The man' is singular, so it takes 'has', and 'accused' takes 'of': 'has been accused of murder'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. “Lot of times” she advised him for not being lazy for completing such a tough task.
questions.explanation: 'Lot' needs the article: 'a lot of times' means many times, often. 'A lot of time' would mean a long time, and 'much of time' is not idiomatic.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. People readily accept any ______ of their leaders if supported by the media.
questions.explanation: An 'argument' here is a reason or case put forward: people readily accept what their leaders argue when the media backs it. A 'concession', 'compromise' or 'dispute' does not suit being accepted on the media's support.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options select the one that gives their correct order. A. When Franco was young; he would stay at sea all night. B. Every morning, he would arrive with a big catch of fresh fish and sell it in the market. C. Franco was a fisherman who lived on the beach. D. He had been fishing for as long as he could remember.
questions.explanation: C introduces Franco the fisherman, D says he had fished for as long as he could remember, A goes back to his youth, when he stayed at sea all night, and B tells what he did each morning after: CDAB.

questions.text: In which year was the Soil Survey of India established to carry out scientific surveys of soils?
questions.explanation: The Soil Survey of India was set up in 1956, as the All India Soil Survey Organisation; it grew into the National Bureau of Soil Survey and Land Use Planning, an independent ICAR institute from 1976.

questions.text: Which part of a plant cell traps sunlight to make sugar?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts hold chlorophyll, which absorbs sunlight for photosynthesis. Chromoplasts carry other pigments that colour fruits and flowers, and leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store starch, oils or proteins.

questions.text: In which state of India does the sunrise first appear?
questions.explanation: Arunachal Pradesh, the easternmost state, sees the sunrise first; Dong village in its Anjaw district is known for India's first sunrise.

questions.text: Through a smart movement using a pawn, Himal Gusain outshone grandmaster NR Visakh. Which game are we talking about?
questions.explanation: The pawn is a chess piece and grandmaster a chess title, and Himal Gusain and N R Visakh are Indian chess players.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The first Education Minister of Independent India was ______.
questions.explanation: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was independent India's first Education Minister, from 1947 to 1958; his birthday, 11 November, is observed as National Education Day.

questions.text: To scale Mount Everest, mountaineers need to go to ______.
questions.explanation: Mount Everest stands on the border between Nepal and the Tibet region of China, and climbers approach it from one or the other. Nepal is the only such country among the options.

questions.text: Sankranti, the harvest festival, is celebrated in the month of Magh of the Hindu calendar and is known by different names in different parts of India. What is it called in Gujarat?
questions.explanation: In Gujarat Makar Sankranti is called Uttarayan and is known for kite flying. Lohri is Punjab's festival on its eve, Maghi is the Punjabi name for the day itself, and Pana Sankranti is Odisha's new year in April.

questions.text: Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant in Tamil Nadu is set up in collaboration with:
questions.explanation: Kudankulam's reactors are Russian-designed VVER-1000 units, built with Russia under an agreement India first signed with the Soviet Union in 1988.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Identify the correctly matched pair of the founder and the social/socio-religious organisation founded.
options: Raja Ram Mohan Ray – Arya Samaj
questions.explanation: Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897, naming it after his guru. Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj and Dayanand Saraswati the Arya Samaj.

questions.text: Name the filmmaker who made the Hindi film, ‘Chhapaak’, based on the story of an acid attack victim.
questions.explanation: Meghna Gulzar directed 'Chhapaak' (2020), based on the life of the acid attack survivor Laxmi Agarwal; Deepika Padukone played the lead and co-produced it.

questions.text: When did the Prime Minister of India declare the country as 'Open Defecation Free'?
questions.explanation: On 2 October 2019, Mahatma Gandhi's 150th birth anniversary and the target date of the Swachh Bharat Mission, Prime Minister Narendra Modi declared rural India open defecation free at an event in Ahmedabad.

questions.text: Which of the following is the apex banking institution of India that regulates the monetary policy?
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India, set up in 1935, is the country's central bank and frames and carries out its monetary policy. The other three are commercial banks.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECT statement about Public Distribution System (PDS) in India.
options: From 1997, PDS became TPDS for targeted consumers.
PDS was envisaged in 1967 as a price support programme to help consumers.
Those living below poverty line get food grains at subsidised prices.
PDS has been abandoned in the country since 2007.
questions.explanation: The PDS was never abandoned: in June 1997 it became the Targeted PDS, and when the exam was held (March 2020) it was running under the National Food Security Act, 2013. Histories of the PDS describe it as a price support for consumers during the food shortages of the 1960s.

questions.text: With which of the following sports/games is Smriti Mandhana associated?
questions.explanation: Smriti Mandhana is a cricketer; when the exam was held (March 2020) she was an opening batter for the India women's team.

questions.text: In which of the following place, are the Dilwara temples of Jainism located?
questions.explanation: The Dilwara temples, Jain temples in white marble, the earliest built in 1031, stand at Mount Abu in Rajasthan.

questions.text: Who won the ‘ICC Cricketer of the Year’, ‘ICC Test Player of the Year’ and ‘ICC ODI Player of the Year’ in 2018?
questions.explanation: In the ICC awards for 2018, announced in January 2019, Virat Kohli won all three: Cricketer of the Year (the Sir Garfield Sobers Trophy), Test Player of the Year and ODI Player of the Year, the first player to do so.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who is known as the 'Father of the Nation' in India?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi is called the Father of the Nation; Subhas Chandra Bose addressed him as the 'Father of our Nation' in a radio broadcast in 1944.

questions.text: Which unit of the computer is considered as the brain of the computer?
questions.explanation: The central processing unit carries out program instructions and controls the other units, so it is called the brain of the computer.

questions.text: Which of the following options correctly defines a firewall (in the context of computing)?
options: It is the name of a software.
It is a combination of both, software and hardware devices to permit or deny network transmission based on a set of rules.
It is a combination of software and hardware-based devices to permit any and every network transmission.
questions.explanation: A firewall watches network traffic and allows or blocks it according to a set of security rules; it may be software, hardware or both. A firewall that let every transmission through would do nothing.

questions.text: What is the chemical name of the salt found abundantly in seawater?
questions.explanation: Common salt, sodium chloride, makes up most of the salt dissolved in seawater.

questions.text: The pH of a liquid was found to be 7. Which liquid is it likely to be?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives water: pure water is neutral, with a pH of 7, while acids are below 7 and alkalis above. A solution of common salt is also neutral in theory, which makes 'saline' arguable, but water is the standard example of a neutral liquid.

questions.text: Pablo Picasso, Claude Monet, Salvador Dali, Vincent Van Gogh were famous for their______.
questions.explanation: All four were painters: Picasso and Dalí were Spanish, Monet French and Van Gogh Dutch.

questions.text: Which of the following is the SI unit of thermodynamic temperature?
questions.explanation: The kelvin is the SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature; the degree Celsius is derived from it, and the radian is the unit of plane angle.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year did Lord Curzon order the partition of Bengal?
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon announced the partition of Bengal in 1905; it took effect on 16 October 1905 and was annulled in 1911.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. EXTENSIVE
questions.explanation: 'Extensive' means covering a large area or range; 'intensive' means concentrated on a small one, as in extensive and intensive farming. 'Lengthy' and 'elaborate' are close to 'extensive', and 'intricate' means complicated.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. TRUST (n)
questions.explanation: 'Trust' as a noun is a firm belief in someone's honesty or reliability: 'belief'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Several environmentalists from the city conducted a meet to discuss issues related to the ______ pollution levels created by the growing number of pharmaceutical companies.
questions.explanation: 'Rise' is the noun for an increase, and an increase is 'in' something: 'the rise in pollution levels'. 'Raise' is the verb meaning to lift, and 'rising from' gives the wrong sense.

questions.text: Select the word with the incorrect spelling.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'quarrel', with one 'l' at the end.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One of the most fascinating archaeological sites in Maharashtra, the Ellora Caves, date back (1)______ about 1,500 years ago, and (2)______ the epitome of Indian rock-cut architecture. (3)______ 34 caves are actually Buddhist, Hindu and Jain religious monuments (4)______ in the rock. They were given the (5)______ of World Heritage Site in 1983. Created between the 6th and 10th century, the 12 Buddhist, 17 Hindu and 5 Jain caves carved in proximity at Ellora are proof of the religious harmony prevalent during this period of Indian history.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.1.
questions.explanation: To 'date back to' a time is to have existed since then: the caves 'date back to about 1,500 years ago'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One of the most fascinating archaeological sites in Maharashtra, the Ellora Caves, date back (1)______ about 1,500 years ago, and (2)______ the epitome of Indian rock-cut architecture. (3)______ 34 caves are actually Buddhist, Hindu and Jain religious monuments (4)______ in the rock. They were given the (5)______ of World Heritage Site in 1983. Created between the 6th and 10th century, the 12 Buddhist, 17 Hindu and 5 Jain caves carved in proximity at Ellora are proof of the religious harmony prevalent during this period of Indian history.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.2.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'the Ellora Caves' takes 'are': 'and are the epitome of Indian rock-cut architecture'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One of the most fascinating archaeological sites in Maharashtra, the Ellora Caves, date back (1)______ about 1,500 years ago, and (2)______ the epitome of Indian rock-cut architecture. (3)______ 34 caves are actually Buddhist, Hindu and Jain religious monuments (4)______ in the rock. They were given the (5)______ of World Heritage Site in 1983. Created between the 6th and 10th century, the 12 Buddhist, 17 Hindu and 5 Jain caves carved in proximity at Ellora are proof of the religious harmony prevalent during this period of Indian history.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.3.
questions.explanation: The 34 caves are a definite group, the caves of Ellora already named, so they take the definite article: 'The 34 caves'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One of the most fascinating archaeological sites in Maharashtra, the Ellora Caves, date back (1)______ about 1,500 years ago, and (2)______ the epitome of Indian rock-cut architecture. (3)______ 34 caves are actually Buddhist, Hindu and Jain religious monuments (4)______ in the rock. They were given the (5)______ of World Heritage Site in 1983. Created between the 6th and 10th century, the 12 Buddhist, 17 Hindu and 5 Jain caves carved in proximity at Ellora are proof of the religious harmony prevalent during this period of Indian history.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.4.
questions.explanation: Rock-cut monuments are 'carved' in the rock, as the passage later says of the caves 'carved in proximity at Ellora'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. One of the most fascinating archaeological sites in Maharashtra, the Ellora Caves, date back (1)______ about 1,500 years ago, and (2)______ the epitome of Indian rock-cut architecture. (3)______ 34 caves are actually Buddhist, Hindu and Jain religious monuments (4)______ in the rock. They were given the (5)______ of World Heritage Site in 1983. Created between the 6th and 10th century, the 12 Buddhist, 17 Hindu and 5 Jain caves carved in proximity at Ellora are proof of the religious harmony prevalent during this period of Indian history.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.5.
questions.explanation: A site is given the 'status' of World Heritage Site.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. Ibn Al-Haitham wrote a book in seven volumes namely ‘Kitāb al-Manāẓir’ also known as ‘The Book of Optics.’ B. However, during the medieval period, the notable work of an Arab writer and scientist, Ibn Al-Haitham revolutionised the concept of physics. C. During the ancient period, the development of Physics took place simultaneously with the development of astronomy. D. In this book, Ibn Al-Haitham disproved the ancient Greek concept of vision and introduced a new theory.
questions.explanation: C opens with physics in the ancient period; B turns ('However') to the medieval work of Ibn Al-Haitham; A names his book; D says what 'this book' did: CBAD.

questions.text: Select the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error. Did you know whether we can exchange the dress if my sister doesn’t like it?
questions.explanation: The question is about whether the dress can be exchanged now, so the verb must be present: 'Do you know whether we can exchange the dress if my sister doesn't like it?'

questions.text: Select the alternative that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case there is no improvement select ‘No improvement’. I had “no informations about” the bank strike so I went there yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable and has no plural: 'I had no information about the bank strike'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A large natural or artificial lake used as a source of water supply
questions.explanation: A reservoir is a large natural or artificial lake that stores water for supply. A creek is a narrow inlet or stream, and a pond and a pool are small.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. ALLURING
questions.explanation: 'Alluring' means attractive or tempting.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. A lot of work has gone on “behind the scenes” for the special event which is being planned next week.
questions.explanation: Work done 'behind the scenes' is done in private, out of public view; of the options, 'unknown to everyone' comes closest to this.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. “Hats off to” someone
questions.explanation: 'Hats off to' someone is said to praise or congratulate them, as if raising one's hat in respect.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. “It is mine. I saw it first," claimed one cat. B. Suddenly they spotted a loaf of bread lying beneath a tree. C. Once upon a time, two cats were passing through a street. D. Both pounced upon it and caught the loaf at the same time.
questions.explanation: C introduces the two cats, B has them spot the loaf, D has both pounce on it at once, and A gives the quarrel that follows: CBDA.

questions.text: Select the alternative that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case there is no improvement select ‘No improvement’. Harry and Meghan “have decided to work and become” financially independent.
options: have decided to work and became
have decide to work and become
has decided to work and become
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: the plural subject takes 'have', and 'to work and become' joins two infinitives after 'decided'.

questions.text: Select the option that is the direct form of the sentence. The doctor advised Jaya to put the eye drops into her eyes four times a day from the next day.
options: The doctor had advised Jaya, “From the next day you put the eye drops into your eyes four times a day.”
The doctor advised Jaya, “From tomorrow put the eye drops into your eyes four times a day.”
The doctor advises Jaya, “From the next day put the eye drops into your eyes four times a day.”
The doctor advised Jaya, “From tomorrow put the eye drops into her eyes four times a day.”
questions.explanation: In direct speech 'from the next day' becomes 'from tomorrow' and 'her eyes' becomes 'your eyes', as the doctor speaks to Jaya; the reporting verb stays in the past.

questions.text: Select the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error. They had to wait for the luggages to be put into the cab before they themselves got into it.
options: to be put into the cab
before they themselves got into it
questions.explanation: 'Luggage' is an uncountable noun and has no plural: 'They had to wait for the luggage to be put into the cab'.

questions.text: Select the option that is the passive form of the sentence. The sub-committee is presenting its report in a week’s time.
options: The report of the sub-committee has been presented in a week’s time.
The report of the sub-committee is being presented in a week’s time.
The report of the sub-committee is presenting in a week’s time.
The report of the sub-committee had been presented in a week’s time.
questions.explanation: The present continuous 'is presenting' becomes 'is being presented' in the passive: 'The report of the sub-committee is being presented in a week's time.'

questions.text: Select the wrongly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'expedition'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. ABBREVIATE
questions.explanation: To 'abbreviate' is to shorten; its opposite is to 'expand'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Close fitting cover for a sword or knife
questions.explanation: A sheath is a close-fitting cover for the blade of a sword or knife.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Astronomy enthusiasts and sky gazers will be able to watch six eclipses in 2020, but only three of them are expected to be ______ in India.
questions.explanation: Eclipses that can be seen from India are 'visible' there. 'Evident' means plain to the mind, and 'exposed' and 'revealed' mean uncovered.

questions.text: Which is the largest river island in the world?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Majuli, in the Brahmaputra in Assam, which Guinness World Records lists as the largest river island. (Brazil's Bananal Island, between the Araguaia and the Javaés, is larger by area and is also often given the title, but it is not among the options.)

questions.text: Which of the following is a water soluble vitamin?
questions.explanation: Vitamin C and the B vitamins dissolve in water; vitamins A, D, E and K are fat-soluble.

questions.text: Which of the following is a pension scheme introduced by the Government of India exclusively for senior citizens in May 2017?
questions.explanation: The Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana (PMVVY), launched in May 2017 and run by LIC, is a pension scheme for citizens aged 60 and above. PMMVY is a maternity benefit scheme, PMGSY builds rural roads and PMGAY rural houses.

questions.text: Mekhela Chador' is a traditional dress from the state of:
questions.explanation: The mekhela chador, a two-piece draped garment, is the traditional dress of Assamese women.

questions.text: ______ is the tube that carries urine from the kidney to the urinary bladder.
questions.explanation: Each ureter carries urine from a kidney to the urinary bladder; the urethra carries it out of the body from the bladder.

questions.text: As of January 2020, who held the title of India's youngest chess grandmaster?
questions.explanation: D Gukesh became a grandmaster in January 2019, aged 12 years and 7 months, beating the Indian record Praggnanandhaa had set in 2018; he still held it in January 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a Chola empire temple?
questions.explanation: The Airavatesvara temple at Darasuram, near Kumbakonam in Tamil Nadu, was built by the Chola king Rajaraja II in the 12th century. The Badami cave temples are Chalukya work, the Chennakesava temple at Belur is Hoysala, and the Virupaksha temples are at Pattadakal (Chalukya) and Hampi (Vijayanagara).

questions.text: Flagella are the hair-like structures which act as organelles of locomotion in which of the following organisms?
questions.explanation: Many bacteria swim with flagella. Amoeba moves with pseudopodia and Paramecium with cilia, and a virus has no means of moving on its own.

questions.text: River Sharavati plunges as which of the following waterfalls?
questions.explanation: The Sharavati plunges at Jog Falls in Shivamogga district, Karnataka, also called the Gerusoppe (Gersoppa) Falls. Athirapally and Soochipara are in Kerala, and Hogenakkal is on the Kaveri.

questions.text: In which city is Indian Railway-Rail Coach Factory located?
questions.explanation: Indian Railways' Rail Coach Factory is at Kapurthala in Punjab. Chennai has the Integral Coach Factory, Bengaluru the Rail Wheel Factory and Chittaranjan the Chittaranjan Locomotive Works.

questions.text: What was the weight of the Chandraayan-2 spacecraft launched in July 2019?
questions.explanation: ISRO gives the mass of Chandrayaan-2, put into orbit by the GSLV MkIII-M1 on 22 July 2019, as 3,840 kg, about 3.8 tonnes.

questions.text: In which year was UNICEF founded?
questions.explanation: UNICEF was set up by the UN General Assembly on 11 December 1946, at first to help children after the Second World War.

questions.text: As of Feb 2020, how many members represent the state of Uttar Pradesh in Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh had 80 seats in the Lok Sabha when the exam was held (March 2020), the most of any state.

questions.text: Who among the following is the co-founder of Twitter?
questions.explanation: Jack Dorsey co-founded Twitter in 2006 with Evan Williams, Biz Stone and Noah Glass. Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web, N R Narayana Murthy co-founded Infosys and Bill Gates co-founded Microsoft.

questions.text: As of January 2020, who held the national record in both, 800 m and 1500 m sprint events?
questions.explanation: In January 2020 Jinson Johnson held the national records in the 800 m, set in 2018, and the 1500 m, set in 2019; both are middle-distance races rather than sprints. Muhammad Anas held the 400 m record, Ayyasamy Dharun the 400 m hurdles and Avinash Sable the 3000 m steeplechase.

questions.text: Laterite soil is rich in:
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives iron oxide, the constituent that defines laterite: heavy rain and heat leach away lime and silica and leave behind iron oxide, which makes the soil red, and aluminium compounds. The soil is poor in organic matter, nitrogen, phosphate and calcium; NCERT's Class XI text also says potash is in excess, but iron oxide is what laterite is known for.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book 'Kerala: God's Own Country'?
questions.explanation: 'Kerala: God's Own Country' (2002) is Shashi Tharoor's book on Kerala, illustrated with drawings by M F Husain.

questions.text: Which of the following states is included in the sixth schedule of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: The Sixth Schedule provides for autonomous district councils in the tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. Nagaland, Manipur and Arunachal Pradesh are not covered by it.

questions.text: When is 'International Ozone Day' celebrated?
questions.explanation: 16 September is the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer, marking the signing of the Montreal Protocol on that day in 1987.

questions.text: 'Nibble' in computer terminology is also called _________.
questions.explanation: A nibble is 4 bits, half of an 8-bit byte.

questions.text: Where is the tomb of Sher Shah Suri located?
questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri's tomb stands in an artificial lake at Sasaram in Bihar, where his family held its jagir. Chausa is where he defeated Humayun in 1539.

questions.text: As of January 2020, who was the president of the BCCI?
questions.explanation: Sourav Ganguly became president of the BCCI in October 2019 and held the post in January 2020. Ravi Shastri was then India's head coach.

questions.text: Who among the following received the Padma Bhushan in 2019?
questions.explanation: The Malayalam actor Mohanlal (Mohanlal Viswanathan Nair) received the Padma Bhushan in 2019. That year Bhupen Hazarika was given the Bharat Ratna posthumously and Sunil Chhetri the Padma Shri; Virat Kohli received the Padma Shri in 2017.

questions.text: As of January 2020, who is the managing director of YES Bank?
questions.explanation: Ravneet Gill succeeded the co-founder Rana Kapoor as managing director and CEO of YES Bank in March 2019 and held the post in January 2020; in March 2020 the RBI superseded the bank's board. Aditya Puri then headed HDFC Bank and Amitabh Chaudhry Axis Bank.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The strong Indian batting line-up will ______ a big worry for the visiting cricket team.
questions.explanation: To 'pose' a worry, threat or problem is to create or present it: the batting line-up will pose a big worry for the visitors.

questions.text: Select the option that is the passive form of the sentence. We have chosen the colour of the new car we want to buy.
options: The colour of the new car we want to buy can be chosen by us.
The colour of the new car we want to buy had been chosen.
The colour of the new car we want to buy has been chosen by us.
The colour of the new car we want to buy is being chosen by us.
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'have chosen' becomes 'has been chosen' with the singular subject 'the colour', and 'we' becomes 'by us'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. MEDDLE (v)
questions.explanation: To 'meddle' is to interfere in something that is not one's concern; its opposite is to 'ignore' it, to leave it alone.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. From the outer entrance itself he had noticed that there was no one inside. B. It was quite dark by the time Raman turned into the lane and reached the temple. C. On entering the main temple, he prostrated before the goddess, got up and then sat directly in front of the idol. D. However, an oil lamp which was burning before the idol of Kaali Ma lit up the place and he could go up the steps.
questions.explanation: B brings Raman to the temple after dark; A says he had seen from the entrance that no one was inside; D ('However') says a lamp lit his way up the steps; C says what he did inside: BADC.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The flight was packed. There were (1)______ parents with small children. Specifically, a three-year-old boy (2)______ the row in front of me (3)______ announcing his presence by letting (4)______ ear-piercing shrieks every 45 seconds. I settled (5)______, hoping the kid would calm down.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.1.
questions.explanation: 'There were several parents with small children' says that a number of them were on the packed flight; 'all', 'most' and 'any' do not fit the sentence.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The flight was packed. There were (1)______ parents with small children. Specifically, a three-year-old boy (2)______ the row in front of me (3)______ announcing his presence by letting (4)______ ear-piercing shrieks every 45 seconds. I settled (5)______, hoping the kid would calm down.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.2.
questions.explanation: A seat is 'in' a row: the boy sat in the row in front of the writer.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The flight was packed. There were (1)______ parents with small children. Specifically, a three-year-old boy (2)______ the row in front of me (3)______ announcing his presence by letting (4)______ ear-piercing shrieks every 45 seconds. I settled (5)______, hoping the kid would calm down.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.3.
questions.explanation: The subject, 'a three-year-old boy', is singular and the story is told in the past, so the past continuous is 'was announcing'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The flight was packed. There were (1)______ parents with small children. Specifically, a three-year-old boy (2)______ the row in front of me (3)______ announcing his presence by letting (4)______ ear-piercing shrieks every 45 seconds. I settled (5)______, hoping the kid would calm down.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.4.
questions.explanation: To 'let loose' a shriek or cry is to give it out suddenly and without restraint.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. The flight was packed. There were (1)______ parents with small children. Specifically, a three-year-old boy (2)______ the row in front of me (3)______ announcing his presence by letting (4)______ ear-piercing shrieks every 45 seconds. I settled (5)______, hoping the kid would calm down.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.5.
questions.explanation: To 'settle down' is to make oneself comfortable and quiet, here in one's seat for the flight.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The minister said, “Anyone using drones will have to register them on an ______ portal.”
questions.explanation: Drones fly, so they are registered on an 'aviation' portal, one concerned with flying; 'airport', 'airline' and 'aeroplane' name a place, a company and a kind of aircraft.

questions.text: Select the alternative that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case there is no improvement select ‘No improvement’. Sidharth “want to become” a football player but needs to practice more rigorously.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'Sidharth' takes the singular verb 'wants', as with 'needs' later in the sentence: 'Sidharth wants to become a football player'.

questions.text: Select the word with the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: 'Piety', devotion to religion, is spelt correctly. The others should be 'visibility', 'certainty' and 'notoriety'.

questions.text: Select the option that is the direct form of the sentence. Dhiraj said that he had been to Goa the previous year also.
options: Dhiraj said, “He has been to Goa the previous year also.”
Dhiraj said, “I had been to Goa the previous year also.”
Dhiraj said, “I have been to Goa last year also.”
Dhiraj told, “I went to Goa the last year also.”
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'I have been to Goa last year also', which undoes the reported-speech changes: 'he' becomes 'I', 'had been' goes back to 'have been' and 'the previous year' to 'last year'. Strictly, 'last year' calls for the simple past ('I went'), but the other options keep 'He' or 'the previous year', or use 'told' without an object.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. A common sight now is that on the roads of Yangon antiquated cars move alongside shiny new vehicles. B. A newly-built highway connects Mandalay to the city of Rangoon, now called Yangon. C. Similarly, hurriedly constructed glass-fronted buildings stand next to old colonial structures. D. Yangon is fairly typical of any developing city in Asia, standing as it does at the crossroads of modernisation.
questions.explanation: B introduces Rangoon, now called Yangon; D says Yangon is typical of a developing Asian city at the crossroads of modernisation; A gives one sign of this, old cars beside new ones, and C ('Similarly') another: BDAC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. We enjoyed watching the film because it was a “down–to-earth” depiction of modern life.
questions.explanation: 'Down-to-earth' means practical and realistic, without pretence: the film showed modern life as it is.

questions.text: Select the alternative that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case there is no improvement select ‘No improvement’. I “have prepared” well for the exam and am ready to answer any question.
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'have prepared' suits preparation finished before now that leaves the speaker ready. 'Will prepared' and 'preparing' are ungrammatical here, and 'may prepare' clashes with 'am ready'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. Government by a king or a queen
questions.explanation: A monarchy is government by a king or queen. Oligarchy is rule by a few, aristocracy by a privileged class and plutocracy by the rich.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. RUEFUL
questions.explanation: 'Rueful' means showing sorrow or regret, so its opposite is 'joyful'; 'regretful' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. His guide asked him to “pull up his socks” if he wanted a good rank.
options: take care to be more formal
make a greater effort to improve
give attention to his appearance also
questions.explanation: To 'pull up one's socks' is to make a greater effort to improve one's work or behaviour.

questions.text: Select the segment in the sentence, which contains a grammatical error. Plenty of people likes to celebrate New Year’s eve with their family and friends.
questions.explanation: 'People' is plural, so the verb must be plural too: 'Plenty of people like to celebrate'.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A vertical passageway into a mine
questions.explanation: A shaft is a vertical passage dug down into a mine. An aisle is a passage between rows of seats, and a lobby an entrance hall.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. SURGE
questions.explanation: A 'surge' is a sudden, powerful forward movement or increase: a rush.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. COVE
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'bay': a cove is above all a small, sheltered bay on a coast. The word can also mean a sheltered recess, as in a hillside, which makes 'hollow' arguable, but 'bay' is its main sense.

questions.text: Select the segment in the sentence, which contains a grammatical error. This furnitures has been taken on hire for the function in the college.
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun with no plural form: 'This furniture has been taken on hire'.

questions.text: Which country has ordered to kill camels due to drought in January 2020?
questions.explanation: In January 2020, amid drought and extreme heat, Aboriginal leaders in the APY Lands of South Australia ordered a cull of feral camels that were crowding communities in search of water; marksmen in helicopters shot more than 5,000 in five days. Africa is a continent, not a country.

questions.text: How many districts are there in the Union Territory of Ladakh?
questions.explanation: When the exam was held (March 2020), the Union Territory of Ladakh, formed on 31 October 2019, had two districts, Leh and Kargil.

questions.text: What is the value of g? (g stands for acceleration due to gravitational force of the earth)
questions.explanation: Near the earth's surface the acceleration due to gravity, g, is about 9.8 m/s².

questions.text: The Kumaon Himalayas lie between which two rivers?
questions.explanation: In NCERT's regional division of the Himalayas, the Kumaon Himalayas lie between the Satluj and the Kali. The Punjab Himalayas lie between the Indus and the Satluj, the Nepal Himalayas between the Kali and the Tista, and the Assam Himalayas between the Tista and the Dihang.

questions.text: The words ‘Satyameva Jayate’ on the state emblem has been taken from which Upanishad?
questions.explanation: 'Satyameva Jayate' ('Truth alone triumphs'), written below the State Emblem in Devanagari script, comes from the Mundaka Upanishad.
