questions.text: When was the right to property removed from the list of fundamental rights?
questions.explanation: The Forty-fourth Amendment Act, 1978 deleted the right to property (Articles 19(1)(f) and 31) from the fundamental rights; it is now a constitutional right under Article 300A.

questions.text: The period of 12th Five Year Plan was:
questions.explanation: The Twelfth Five Year Plan ran from 2012 to 2017; it was the last of India's Five Year Plans.

questions.text: Where is the headquarters of South Western Railway?
questions.explanation: South Western Railway, a zone of Indian Railways, has its headquarters at Hubli (Hubballi) in Karnataka. Chennai is the headquarters of Southern Railway and Secunderabad of South Central Railway.

questions.text: Vitamin B Complex consists of how many vitamins?
questions.explanation: The B complex has eight vitamins: thiamine (B1), riboflavin (B2), niacin (B3), pantothenic acid (B5), pyridoxine (B6), biotin (B7), folate (B9) and cobalamin (B12).

questions.text: Who was the founder of Pala Dynasty?
questions.explanation: Gopala, chosen king in Bengal around 750 CE, founded the Pala dynasty; his son Dharmapala succeeded him, and Mahipala and Ramapala were later Pala kings.

questions.text: Who wrote the book 'An era of Darkness'?
questions.explanation: 'An Era of Darkness: The British Empire in India' (2016) is by Shashi Tharoor; it won the Sahitya Akademi Award for English in 2019.

questions.text: Which shortcut key is used for previewing the page before printing?
questions.explanation: In Microsoft Word, Ctrl + F2 shows the print preview of the document.

questions.text: ‘Karmayoddha Granth’ has been written on the life of:
questions.explanation: 'Karmayoddha Granth', a book on the life of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, was released by Home Minister Amit Shah in New Delhi in January 2020.

questions.text: Where is the Sultan Azlan Shah Cup held every year?
questions.explanation: The Sultan Azlan Shah Cup, an international men's hockey tournament, is held in Malaysia, usually at Ipoh.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: India signed Panchsheel Treaty with which country?
questions.explanation: India and China signed the Panchsheel Agreement, with its five principles of peaceful coexistence, on 29 April 1954, in an agreement on trade with the Tibet region.

questions.text: Where was the Pullela Gopichand Badminton Academy founded in 2008?
questions.explanation: Pullela Gopichand founded his badminton academy at Gachibowli, Hyderabad, in 2008.

questions.text: Atomic number of copper is:
questions.explanation: Copper (Cu) has atomic number 29. 23 is vanadium, 25 manganese and 28 nickel.

questions.text: Nobel Peace Prize 2019 winner Abiy Ahmed Ali belongs to which country?
questions.explanation: Abiy Ahmed Ali, Prime Minister of Ethiopia, won the 2019 Nobel Peace Prize, in particular for his initiative to end the border conflict with neighbouring Eritrea.

questions.text: Who has been elected as the new Jharkhand assembly speaker?
questions.explanation: In January 2020 Rabindra Nath Mahto of the JMM was elected Speaker of the fifth Jharkhand Legislative Assembly. Inder Singh Namdhari was the state's first Speaker.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When was the Indian Reform Association formed?
questions.explanation: Keshab Chandra Sen founded the Indian Reform Association in 1870, soon after his return from England, to promote social reform.

questions.text: Minimum Support Price (MSP) of the agricultural crops in India is fixed by the government on the recommendations of the:
options: Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)
questions.explanation: The government fixes Minimum Support Prices on the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP), an attached office of the Ministry of Agriculture.

questions.text: Hirakud dam is in which state?
questions.explanation: The Hirakud Dam is on the Mahanadi near Sambalpur in Odisha.

questions.text: Which company manufactured the first microprocessor 4004?
questions.explanation: Intel launched the 4004, the first commercially available microprocessor, in 1971.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When was the construction of the Rashtrapati Bhavan completed?
questions.explanation: Viceroy's House, now Rashtrapati Bhavan, designed by Edwin Lutyens, took about 17 years to build and was completed in 1929.

questions.text: When did Karnam Malleshwari get the Padma Shri?
questions.explanation: The weightlifter Karnam Malleswari received the Padma Shri in 1999. She had received the Arjuna Award in 1994, and she won bronze at the Sydney Olympics in 2000.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A solution or remedy for all difficulties or diseases
questions.explanation: A panacea is a cure for every ill or difficulty. Medicine, treatment and therapy are remedies for a particular illness.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. A place where wild animals live
questions.explanation: A lair is a wild animal's den or resting place. A hutch is a box for rabbits, a kennel a shelter for a dog, and a cage holds a captive animal.

questions.text: Select the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error. We were busy at the work and went for lunch only at 2.30 pm.
questions.explanation: The set phrase is 'at work', without an article: 'We were busy at work and went for lunch only at 2.30 pm.'

questions.text: Select the alternative that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case there is no improvement select ‘No improvement’. There was “no sign of recognition” on his face when they met after ten years.
questions.explanation: The underlined part is already correct: one shows a 'sign of' something, not a 'sign for' it, and 'no any' is not English.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Valley of Flowers National Park, an Indian national park located in North Chamoli in the state of Uttarakhand, is known for its meadows of endemic alpine flowers and variety of flora. (1)______ richly diverse area is also home (2)______ rare and endangered animals, including the Asiatic black bear, snow leopard, musk deer, brown bear, red fox, and blue sheep. Birds (3)______ in the park include the Himalayan monal pheasant and other (4)______ altitude birds. At 3352 to 3658 meters above sea level, the gentle (5)______ of the Valley of Flowers National Park complements the rugged mountain wilderness of Nanda Devi National Park to the east.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.1.
questions.explanation: 'This' points back to the park just described ('This richly diverse area is also home to...'); 'that' would suggest something more distant, 'these' is plural, and 'which' cannot begin a statement.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Valley of Flowers National Park, an Indian national park located in North Chamoli in the state of Uttarakhand, is known for its meadows of endemic alpine flowers and variety of flora. (1)______ richly diverse area is also home (2)______ rare and endangered animals, including the Asiatic black bear, snow leopard, musk deer, brown bear, red fox, and blue sheep. Birds (3)______ in the park include the Himalayan monal pheasant and other (4)______ altitude birds. At 3352 to 3658 meters above sea level, the gentle (5)______ of the Valley of Flowers National Park complements the rugged mountain wilderness of Nanda Devi National Park to the east.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.2.
questions.explanation: A place is 'home to' the plants and animals that live there.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Valley of Flowers National Park, an Indian national park located in North Chamoli in the state of Uttarakhand, is known for its meadows of endemic alpine flowers and variety of flora. (1)______ richly diverse area is also home (2)______ rare and endangered animals, including the Asiatic black bear, snow leopard, musk deer, brown bear, red fox, and blue sheep. Birds (3)______ in the park include the Himalayan monal pheasant and other (4)______ altitude birds. At 3352 to 3658 meters above sea level, the gentle (5)______ of the Valley of Flowers National Park complements the rugged mountain wilderness of Nanda Devi National Park to the east.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.3.
questions.explanation: 'Found' begins a shortened relative clause, 'birds (that are) found in the park'; 'are found' would give the sentence two main verbs.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Valley of Flowers National Park, an Indian national park located in North Chamoli in the state of Uttarakhand, is known for its meadows of endemic alpine flowers and variety of flora. (1)______ richly diverse area is also home (2)______ rare and endangered animals, including the Asiatic black bear, snow leopard, musk deer, brown bear, red fox, and blue sheep. Birds (3)______ in the park include the Himalayan monal pheasant and other (4)______ altitude birds. At 3352 to 3658 meters above sea level, the gentle (5)______ of the Valley of Flowers National Park complements the rugged mountain wilderness of Nanda Devi National Park to the east.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.4.
questions.explanation: 'High-altitude birds' live far above sea level, as in this park at 3352 to 3658 metres.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. Valley of Flowers National Park, an Indian national park located in North Chamoli in the state of Uttarakhand, is known for its meadows of endemic alpine flowers and variety of flora. (1)______ richly diverse area is also home (2)______ rare and endangered animals, including the Asiatic black bear, snow leopard, musk deer, brown bear, red fox, and blue sheep. Birds (3)______ in the park include the Himalayan monal pheasant and other (4)______ altitude birds. At 3352 to 3658 meters above sea level, the gentle (5)______ of the Valley of Flowers National Park complements the rugged mountain wilderness of Nanda Devi National Park to the east.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No.5.
questions.explanation: The 'landscape' is the look of the land: the valley's gentle landscape is set against the rugged wilderness beside it.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. Just before the sacrifice, however, he noticed that one of the king’s fingers was missing. B. Once when travelling across a forest, the king was captured by a powerful tribe. C. Since it was not acceptable to sacrifice an incomplete person to God, the king was released. D. The tribal priest decided to sacrifice the king to their God.
questions.explanation: B tells how the king was captured, D that the priest decided to sacrifice him, A that the priest then noticed a missing finger ('however'), and C gives the outcome: BDAC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. By accelerating digitisation and leveraging next generation technologies, the life insurance sector can double its ______ to Rupees 70 lakh crores, a study said.
questions.explanation: A sum in rupees fits the sector's 'assets', the value of what insurers hold: they can double their assets to 70 lakh crore rupees. Policies and reports are counted, not valued in rupees, and 'funding' is money supplied by others, not a measure of what the sector holds.

questions.text: Select the word with the incorrect spelling
questions.explanation: 'Systemetic' is misspelt: the word is 'systematic'.

questions.text: Select the segment in the sentence, which contains the grammatical error. No matter what that the mother did the baby didn’t stop crying.
questions.explanation: 'No matter what' takes no 'that': 'No matter what the mother did, the baby didn't stop crying.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. RESILIENT
questions.explanation: 'Resilient' means able to spring back or recover after being bent or hurt; 'supple', bending easily without breaking, is the closest.

questions.text: Select the option that is the passive form of the sentence. Jiya wrote the research paper with the help of her tutor.
options: The research paper is being written by Jiya with the help of her tutor.
The research paper was wrote by Jiya with the help of the tutor.
The research paper can be written by the tutor with the help of Jiya.
The research paper was written by Jiya with the help of her tutor.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'wrote' becomes 'was written' in the passive: 'The research paper was written by Jiya with the help of her tutor.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Madhuri is bringing ______ her sister’s daughter after the death of the child’s parents.
questions.explanation: To 'bring up' a child is to raise and care for it: Madhuri is raising her sister's daughter.

questions.text: Select the word with the correct spelling.
questions.explanation: 'Capricious' (given to sudden changes of mood) is spelt correctly. The others should be 'ecstasy', 'complacent' and 'avalanche'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. OCCUR
questions.explanation: To 'occur' is to happen. 'Hinder' and 'hamper' mean to obstruct, and 'hasten' to hurry.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom. Back in saddle
questions.explanation: To be 'back in the saddle' is to return to one's work or position after a break: to resume duty.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. PRIM
questions.explanation: 'Prim' means stiffly neat and proper; 'dishevelled', untidy in hair or dress, is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. When they read about the proposed strike of buses they said, “We’ll “cross that bridge” when we come to it.”
questions.explanation: To 'cross that bridge when we come to it' is to deal with a problem when it actually arises rather than worry about it in advance; 'solve the problem' is the only option that fits.

questions.text: Select the option that is the direct form of the sentence. Experts said that several steps were being taken to promote foreign trade as it constituted 45% of the country’s economy.
options: Experts are saying, “Several steps were taken to promote foreign trade as it constituted 45% of the country’s economy”.
Experts said, “Several steps should be taken to promote foreign trade as they constitute 45% of the country’s economy”.
Experts said, “Several steps are being taken to promote foreign trade as it constitutes 45% of the country’s economy”.
Experts said, “Several steps had been taken for promoting foreign trade as it constitute 45% of the country’s economy”.
questions.explanation: Turning reported speech back into direct speech restores the speaker's own tenses: 'were being taken' becomes 'are being taken' and 'constituted' becomes 'constitutes', after 'Experts said,'.

questions.text: Select the alternative that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case there is no improvement select ‘No improvement’. Carrots and sweet potatoes “were airdrop for animals starving” during the tragic bushfires in Australia.
options: will be airdropping for animals starving
questions.explanation: After 'were' the passive needs the past participle, 'airdropped'; 'starving' describes animals that were going hungry during the fires.

questions.text: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. Problems in absorption of vitamins is the main cause of vitamin deficiency. B. This is the reason why people with metabolic disorders such as obesity, often suffer from vitamin deficiency. C. Hence, digestion and the absorption mechanism in the body is very important. D. Vitamin deficiency is not just caused by lack of vitamins in the diet.
questions.explanation: D says deficiency is not caused by diet alone, A names the main cause, poor absorption, B draws the consequence for people with metabolic disorders, and C concludes ('Hence') that digestion and absorption matter: DABC.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. EXHALE
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'Inhale', to breathe in, the everyday opposite of 'exhale', to breathe out. 'Inspire' can also mean to breathe in, but only in a technical (physiological) or old-fashioned sense, where its usual pair is 'expire'.

questions.text: Dhimsa is an official folk dance of which state?
questions.explanation: Dhimsa is a group dance of the tribal communities of the Araku Valley in Andhra Pradesh.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a pair of Isobars?
questions.explanation: Isobars have the same mass number but different atomic numbers: calcium-40 has 20 protons and argon-40 has 18.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Nizam Sagar Dam situated?
questions.explanation: The Nizam Sagar Dam, built across the Manjira river under the Nizam of Hyderabad, is in Telangana.

questions.text: Python is a _______.
questions.explanation: Python is a high-level, general-purpose programming language: its code is written in near-English statements, far from the machine's own instructions, and run by an interpreter.

questions.text: Who won the Nobel prize 2019 in literature?
questions.explanation: The Austrian writer Peter Handke received the Nobel Prize in Literature for 2019. Olga Tokarczuk, announced the same day in October 2019, received the postponed prize for 2018; Bob Dylan won in 2016 and Kazuo Ishiguro in 2017.

questions.text: The term 'white revolution' is related with:
questions.explanation: The White Revolution is the rise in India's milk production through Operation Flood, led by Verghese Kurien from 1970.

questions.text: The first Commonwealth Games were held in:
questions.explanation: The first Commonwealth Games, then called the British Empire Games, were held at Hamilton, Canada, in 1930.

questions.text: Atal Bhujal Yojana (ABY) is related to _____________.
questions.explanation: Atal Bhujal Yojana, launched in December 2019 with World Bank support, is a scheme for community-led management of groundwater in water-stressed areas of seven states.

questions.text: How many windows are there on the outside walls of Hawa Mahal of Jaipur?
questions.explanation: The Hawa Mahal, built in 1799 under Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh, has 953 small latticed windows (jharokhas) on its five-storey front.

questions.text: With which game was Khashaba Dadasaheb Jadhav associated?
questions.explanation: K D Jadhav won a wrestling bronze at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics, independent India's first individual Olympic medal.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When was the Muslim League founded?
questions.explanation: The All-India Muslim League was founded at Dhaka on 30 December 1906.

questions.text: What is the approximate length of the navigable inland waterways of India?
questions.explanation: The Inland Waterways Authority of India puts the country's navigable waterways, rivers, canals, backwaters and creeks, at about 14,500 km.

questions.text: Which tissue has heavily thickened lignified walls?
questions.explanation: Sclerenchyma cells have thick walls hardened with lignin and are usually dead at maturity, giving the plant strength, as in the coconut husk. Collenchyma walls are thickened with cellulose and pectin, not lignin.

questions.text: Which country ranked first among 97 countries in breastfeeding rate, according to a new survey conducted by the World Breastfeeding Trends Initiative (WBTi)?
questions.explanation: In the World Breastfeeding Trends Initiative's (WBTi) ranking of 97 countries on their policies and programmes supporting breastfeeding, Sri Lanka came first, the first nation rated 'green'.

questions.text: After which former Indian Prime Minister was Rohtang pass tunnel named, in December 2019?
questions.explanation: On 25 December 2019, Atal Bihari Vajpayee's birth anniversary, the tunnel under the Rohtang Pass was named the Atal Tunnel after him.

questions.text: Who won the Miss World 2019 beauty pageant?
questions.explanation: Toni-Ann Singh of Jamaica was crowned Miss World 2019 in London in December 2019; India's Suman Rao was second runner-up. Vanessa Ponce de León won in 2018 and Manushi Chhillar in 2017.

questions.text: Linux is ______.
questions.explanation: Linux is an open-source, Unix-like operating system built on the kernel Linus Torvalds released in 1991.

questions.text: In which state is the Bankapura Peacock Sanctuary situated?
questions.explanation: The Bankapura Peacock Sanctuary is near Shiggaon in the Haveri district of Karnataka.

questions.text: When did Ibrahim Lodhi become the Sultan of Delhi?
questions.explanation: Ibrahim Lodi succeeded his father Sikandar Lodi as Sultan of Delhi in 1517 and ruled until Babur defeated and killed him at Panipat in 1526.

questions.text: When was a landmark Motor Vehicles Agreement (MVA) for the Regulation of Passenger, Personnel and Cargo Vehicular Traffic signed between sub-grouping of four SAARC nations, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India and Nepal (BBIN)?
questions.explanation: The BBIN Motor Vehicles Agreement was signed by the transport ministers of Bangladesh, Bhutan, India and Nepal at Thimphu on 15 June 2015.

questions.text: Which country publishes the Wisden Cricketers’ Almanack – often labelled the ‘Bible of cricket’?
questions.explanation: Wisden Cricketers' Almanack, an annual first published in 1864, is published in the United Kingdom.

questions.text: The first Regional Rural Bank was established in India in the year:
questions.explanation: Prathama Grameen Bank, set up at Moradabad (Uttar Pradesh) on 2 October 1975, was India's first regional rural bank.

questions.text: The concept of fundamental duties in the Constitution of India was taken from:
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Duties, added as Article 51A by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, were modelled on the Constitution of the former USSR.

questions.text: Which instrument was used to detect gravitational waves for the very first time?
questions.explanation: The two LIGO detectors in the USA recorded the first gravitational waves, from a pair of merging black holes, on 14 September 2015.

questions.text: What is the tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner of India?
options: 6 years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
4 years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
5 Years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
3 years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
questions.explanation: The Chief Election Commissioner holds office for six years or until the age of 65, whichever comes first.

questions.text: In a code language, 'sweet fruits' is coded as 're de', 'mango is sweet' is coded as 'de me ke', 'orange is citrus' is coded as 'ke le pe', 'eat orange' is coded as 'pe ne'. What is the code for the word 'mango'?
questions.explanation: 'Sweet' is the only word in both the first and second phrases, so sweet = de; 'is' is the only word in both the second and third, so is = ke. That leaves mango = me.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the sixth number is related to the fifth number. 42 : 91 :: 84 : ? :: 149 : 198
questions.explanation: 91 − 42 = 49 and 198 − 149 = 49, so each second number is 49 more than the first: 84 + 49 = 133.

questions.text: Seven people, P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are sitting in a straight row, facing north. Only four people sit to the right of P. Only two people sit between P and S. Q is sitting third to the right of V. T is sitting second to the right of V. U is sitting third to the left of T. Who is sitting at the extreme right end of the row?
questions.explanation: With four people to his right, P is third from the left, and S, with two between them, is sixth. V, T (second to V's right) and Q (third to V's right) fit only in places 2, 4 and 5, so U, third to the left of T, is first and R takes the last place: U V P T Q S R. R is at the right end.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? AVXE, DSUH, GPRK, ?, MJLQ
questions.explanation: The first and fourth letters move 3 places forward (A, D, G, J, M; E, H, K, N, Q) and the second and third 3 places back (V, S, P, M, J; X, U, R, O, L): JMON.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 14, 12, 27, 25, 53, 51, ?

Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term is related to the third term. PREPARE : ERAPERP :: COMPARE : ERAPMOC :: DESPAIR : ?
questions.explanation: Each word is written backwards: PREPARE → ERAPERP and COMPARE → ERAPMOC. So DESPAIR → RIAPSED.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 72 × 3 + 48 ÷ 6 - 16= 296
questions.explanation: After interchanging × and ÷: 72 ÷ 3 + 48 × 6 − 16 = 24 + 288 − 16 = 296.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All masks are sanitizers. All handwashes are sanitizers. All sanitizers are medicines. Conclusions: I. All handwashes are medicines. II. All medicines are masks. III. Some medicines are handwashes.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: All handwashes are sanitizers and all sanitizers are medicines, so all handwashes are medicines (I), and so some medicines are handwashes (III). Nothing makes every medicine a mask, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters / number of consonants / vowels in the word) Spider : Web :: Horse : ?
questions.explanation: A spider lives in its web, and a horse is kept in a stable. A den is the home of a wild animal such as a lion.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 8, 10, 17, 19, 35, 37, ?
In a certain code language, ‘TRIFLED’ is written as ‘YQNEQDI’ and ‘BRIEF’ is written as ‘GQNDK’. How will ‘FALTER’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +5 and −1 in turn: TRIFLED → YQNEQDI and BRIEF → GQNDK. So FALTER → KZQSJQ, with A − 1 wrapping round to Z.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? NUZD, LSXB, ?, HOTX, FMRV
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places back every time: N, L, J, H, F; U, S, Q, O, M; Z, X, V, T, R; D, B, Z, X, V. The missing cluster is JQVZ.

questions.text: D $ E means ‘D is the daughter of E’; D @ E means ‘D is the mother of E’; D + E means ‘D is the father of E’; D * E means ‘D is the husband of E’; If P * T $ X + Z, then how is P related to Z?
questions.explanation: P is T's husband, T is X's daughter and X is Z's father, so T is Z's sister and P is Z's sister's husband.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 domestic 2 dozen 3 double 4 doctor 5 down
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: doctor (4), domestic (1), double (3), down (5), dozen (2), as 'doc', 'dom', 'dou', 'dow' and 'doz' follow the alphabet.

questions.text: Six friends (Aman, Biplab, Chirantan, Divya, Elizabeth and Firoz) are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Aman sits third to the left of Biplab. Chirantan is an immediate neighbour of Aman. Elizabeth sits second to the right of Divya. Chirantan is not an immediate neighbour of Divya. Who sits to the immediate left of Biplab?
questions.explanation: Aman, third to Biplab's left, sits opposite him. With Chirantan beside Aman, Divya and Elizabeth (second to Divya's right) can only be Biplab's two neighbours, Divya on his left; Chirantan, not beside Divya, then sits between Aman and Elizabeth, and Firoz between Divya and Aman.

questions.text: Which of the following former Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh passed away in October 2022?
questions.explanation: Mulayam Singh Yadav, founder of the Samajwadi Party and three times Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, died on 10 October 2022. Narayan Dutt Tiwari died in 2018 and Kalyan Singh in 2021.

questions.text: Who among the following became the Member of legislative Assembly of Surma, Tripura in June 2022?
questions.explanation: In the Tripura by-elections of June 2022 the BJP's Swapna Das Paul won the Surma seat.

questions.text: Gopika Varma won the 2018 Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for ______.
questions.explanation: Gopika Varma is a Mohiniyattam dancer; the Sangeet Natak Akademi named her for its 2018 award in that form.

questions.text: Which of the following is a metamorphic rock?
questions.explanation: Quartzite forms when sandstone is changed by heat and pressure. Granite is igneous, and sandstone and shale are sedimentary rocks.

questions.text: Which among the following Bihu is also known as Rongali Bihu?
questions.explanation: Rongali (Bohag) Bihu, in mid-April, marks the Assamese New Year and the coming of spring. Magh Bihu is also called Bhogali Bihu, and Kati Bihu Kongali Bihu.

questions.text: The ____________ provides for measures to deter fugitive economic offenders from evading the process of law in India by staying outside the jurisdiction of Indian courts.
questions.explanation: The Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 lets a special court declare a person a fugitive economic offender and confiscate their property, to deter such offenders from escaping Indian courts by staying abroad.

questions.text: Sultan Johor Cup is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: The Sultan of Johor Cup is an international under-21 men's hockey tournament held in Johor Bahru, Malaysia.

questions.text: Which of the following is a fundamental duty?
options: To renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of men
To renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of any administrative officials
To renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of advocates
To renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women
questions.explanation: Article 51A(e) asks every citizen to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.

questions.text: Harshavardhana tried to cross the Narmada to march into the Deccan, but was stopped by a ruler belonging to the Chalukya dynasty, ______.
questions.explanation: Pulakeshin II, the Chalukya king of Badami (Vatapi), defeated Harshavardhana on the Narmada and kept him out of the Deccan, as his Aihole inscription records.

questions.text: Net Worth = Assets - _______
questions.explanation: Net worth is what remains when liabilities are taken away from assets.

questions.text: Which of the given statements is correct? I. Acid turns red litmus blue. II. Acids are bitter in taste.
questions.explanation: Both statements are false: acids turn blue litmus red (bases turn red litmus blue), and acids taste sour, while bases taste bitter.

questions.text: The folk dance ‘Cheraw’ is primarily associated with which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Cheraw, the bamboo dance, is a traditional dance of Mizoram, in which dancers step in and out of bamboo poles clapped together.

questions.text: In which of the following years did the first elected Parliament come into existence?
questions.explanation: After the first general election of 1951-52, the first elected Lok Sabha was constituted in April 1952 and first met in May 1952. Until then the Constituent Assembly served as the Provisional Parliament.

questions.text: Which are the two social groups in India which are most vulnerable to poverty?
options: Scheduled tribes and Other Backward Classes
questions.explanation: NCERT's economics textbook names scheduled caste and scheduled tribe households as the social groups most vulnerable to poverty in India.

questions.text: The _______ of a country is measured by the development of manufacturing industries.
questions.explanation: NCERT's geography textbook says that a country's economic strength is measured by the development of its manufacturing industries.

questions.text: Which currency notes were demonetised by the government of India in 2016?
questions.explanation: On 8 November 2016 the Government of India withdrew the legal tender of the old ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes.

questions.text: Which of the following activity is related to the tertiary sector of the economy?
questions.explanation: The tertiary (service) sector supports production through activities such as transport, storage, communication, banking and trade. Automobile production and cloth weaving are secondary activities, and fishing is primary.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: He is perhaps best known for his speech at the Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago in 1893. Who is 'he' referred to?
questions.explanation: Swami Vivekananda addressed the Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago in September 1893, opening with 'Sisters and Brothers of America'.

questions.text: The inaugural winners of the Hero Indian Super League (ISL) was ATK, which is a football club based in _________.
questions.explanation: ATK (Atlético de Kolkata), the Kolkata club, won the first Indian Super League in 2014.

questions.text: A dishonest shopkeeper sells rice at the cost price but he uses a faulty weight of 925g for 1000g. Find his gain percentage.
questions.explanation: He gives 925 g for the price of 1000 g, so he gains 75 g on every 925 g: 75/925 × 100 = 8.11%.

questions.text: What is the smallest positive number that should be subtracted from each of 12 and 21 so that 36 is the third proportion to them?
The value of a painting rises from Rs 140000 to Rs 182000. The percent increase in the value of the painting is:
Find the HCF of the cube of 16 and the square of 48.
questions.explanation: 16³ = 2¹² and 48² = (2⁴ × 3)² = 2⁸ × 3², so the HCF is 2⁸ = 256.

questions.text: 24 men complete a work in 9 days. 3 days after they started working, 8 more men joined them. How many days will all of them take to complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation: The work is 24 × 9 = 216 man-days. After 3 days 216 − 72 = 144 man-days remain, which 32 men finish in 144 ÷ 32 = 4.5 days.

questions.text: A solid right-circular cylinder whose radius of the base is 22.5 cm and whose height is 24 cm is melted and moulded in the shape of a right circular cone whose radius of the base is 36 cm. What will be the height of this cone?
questions.explanation: The volumes are equal: π × 22.5² × 24 = (1/3) × π × 36² × h, so 12,150 = 432h and h = 28.125 cm.

questions.text: A person travels three equal distances at the speeds of 2 km/h, 3 km/h and 4 km/h and takes a total time of 52 minutes. The total distance is:
questions.explanation: Each distance d takes d/2 + d/3 + d/4 = 13d/12 hours in all, which is 52/60 hour, so d = 0.8 km and the total distance is 2.4 km.

questions.text: An object moves 15 m in 2.6 min and the next 26 km at a speed of 30 km/h. Find its average speed (in m/sec) for the whole movement.
questions.explanation: The 26 km at 30 km/h takes 52 min, so the whole movement covers 26,015 m in 2.6 + 52 = 54.6 min = 3,276 s: 26,015 ÷ 3,276 = 7.94 m/s.

questions.text: Simplify the following. 30% of [ { (820% of 40 ) – 28} ] % of 600
At what rate of compound interest does a sum of money become 3.375-fold in 3 years, compounding annually?
questions.explanation: (1 + r)³ = 3.375 = 1.5³, so 1 + r = 1.5 and the rate is 50%.

questions.text: A wholesaler has 1000 kg sugar, part of which he sells at 6% profit and the rest at 12% profit. His gain is 10% on the whole. The quantity sold at 6% profit is: (consider up to two decimals)
questions.explanation: By alligation, the quantities sold at 6% and 12% are in the ratio (12 − 10) : (10 − 6) = 1 : 2, so 1000/3 = 333.33 kg is sold at 6%.

questions.text: Balvendra offers two successive discounts of 9% and 4% first and then he also provides a cash discount of Rs.268 on the sale of a CCTV camera. If the marked price of the CCTV camera is Rs.5,000, what is the final price of the CCTV camera for a customer?
questions.explanation: ₹5,000 × 0.91 × 0.96 = ₹4,368, and the cash discount of ₹268 brings it to ₹4,100.

questions.text: Ram and Ramesh run two kilometres and Ram wins by 40 seconds. Ram and Naresh run two kilometres and Ram wins by 650 metres. When Ramesh and Naresh run the same distance, Ramesh wins by 25 seconds. Find the time taken by Ram to run two kilometres.
questions.explanation: If Ram takes t seconds, Ramesh takes t + 40 and Naresh t + 40 + 25 = t + 65. When Ram finishes, Naresh has run 1,350 m: 2000t/(t + 65) = 1350, so 650t = 87,750 and t = 135 s, 2 minutes 15 seconds.

questions.text: Aman can do a piece of work in 78 days. Ram can do this work in 39 days. Aman started the work alone. After how many days should Ram join him, so that the work is finished in 39 days?
questions.explanation: Aman works all 39 days and does 39/78, half the work. Ram does the other half, which takes him 39/2 = 19.5 days, so he joins after 39 − 19.5 = 39/2 days.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The library is the right place “to write an article” from a journal.
questions.explanation: An article 'from a journal' is one already published in it, so it is something to read, and a library is the place to read it; one writes an article 'for' a journal, not 'from' it. 'To find the article' would need a particular article already mentioned.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Swindle
questions.explanation: A swindle is a fraud, a scheme to cheat someone of money by deceit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A cakewalk
questions.explanation: A 'cakewalk' is something very easy to do or win.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. When the separatist tendencies become very active, the unity of any nation can be in __________.
questions.explanation: To be 'in peril' is to be in danger: active separatist tendencies endanger a nation's unity.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Calamity
questions.explanation: A calamity is a disaster, an event that causes great damage or suffering. 'Fortune', 'windfall' and 'prosperity' are nearly its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The treaty was signed by both the parties to retain the “status-quo”.
questions.explanation: The 'status quo' is the existing state of affairs, the current situation, which the treaty is signed to keep.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in the bracket to fill in the blank. Rohan ________ (insufficient) the compassion required to be a doctor.
questions.explanation: To 'lack' something is to be without it or not have enough of it: 'Rohan lacked the compassion'. 'Was deprived' would need 'of'.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the following sentence. You can eat anything you like “accept” the rice pudding.
questions.explanation: 'Accept' (to receive or agree to) is confused here with 'except', meaning 'other than': anything you like except the rice pudding.

questions.text: Identify the spelling error in the given sentence and select the option that rectifies the error. He dared to compeete against the experienced boxer.
questions.explanation: The sentence misspells 'compete'. 'Against', 'experienced' and 'dared' are spelt correctly in it; the other options misspell them.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Last night I played my guitar loudly and the neighbours complain.
questions.explanation: 'Last night' and 'played' put the sentence in the past, so the second verb must be past too: 'the neighbours complained'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Has bigger fish to fry
options: Has easier plans to solve the issue
Has more important work to do
questions.explanation: To have 'bigger fish to fry' is to have more important things to do.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Escalate
questions.explanation: To escalate is to increase or intensify; its opposite is to 'diminish', to make or become smaller. 'Intensify' and 'enlarge' are close to its meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Follow
questions.explanation: To follow is to come after; to 'predate' is to come before. 'Ensue' means to follow, and 'supplant' and 'displace' mean to replace.

questions.text: Select the correct word for the blanks in the given sentence. I need a blue _________ for writing and my brother runs a _________ for dogs.
questions.explanation: 'Pen' fits both blanks: a pen is a writing instrument, and also a small enclosure for animals.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks in the given sentence. Shelley is good at ______ and also has a new ______ of the Oxford dictionary launched last month.
questions.explanation: Shelley is good at 'addition', the arithmetic of adding numbers, and has a new 'edition', a version as published, of the dictionary.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Looking at the stars is a glimpse (1) _________ history. Some of the things we see (2)_________ millions of light-years (3) ________. Everything in the universe (4) ________ a past but stars don't try to hide it. They just (5) _________ shining, for everyone to see.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: A 'glimpse of' something is a brief look at it: looking at the stars is a glimpse of history.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Looking at the stars is a glimpse (1) _________ history. Some of the things we see (2)_________ millions of light-years (3) ________. Everything in the universe (4) ________ a past but stars don't try to hide it. They just (5) _________ shining, for everyone to see.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'some of the things we see' takes 'are': they are millions of light-years away.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Looking at the stars is a glimpse (1) _________ history. Some of the things we see (2)_________ millions of light-years (3) ________. Everything in the universe (4) ________ a past but stars don't try to hide it. They just (5) _________ shining, for everyone to see.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Distance from the viewer is given with 'away': 'millions of light-years away'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Looking at the stars is a glimpse (1) _________ history. Some of the things we see (2)_________ millions of light-years (3) ________. Everything in the universe (4) ________ a past but stars don't try to hide it. They just (5) _________ shining, for everyone to see.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Everything' is singular, so it takes 'has': 'Everything in the universe has a past'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Looking at the stars is a glimpse (1) _________ history. Some of the things we see (2)_________ millions of light-years (3) ________. Everything in the universe (4) ________ a past but stars don't try to hide it. They just (5) _________ shining, for everyone to see.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Keep shining' means go on shining, which suits stars that do not hide their past.

questions.text: C $ D’ means ‘C is the brother of D’ ‘C # D’ means ‘C is the sister of D’ ‘C + D’ means ‘C is the father of D’ ‘C – D’ means ‘C is the mother of D’ If ‘P $ Z + Q $ B’, then how is P related to B?
options: P is the brother of B
P is the father of B
P is the father-in-law of B
P is the paternal uncle of B
questions.explanation: P $ Z: P is Z's brother. Z + Q: Z is Q's father. Q $ B: Q is B's brother, so Z is B's father too. P, the brother of B's father, is B's paternal uncle.

questions.text: Five friends A, B, C, D and E are sitting in a row facing north. E is to the immediate right of D and A is at the extreme left. C is exactly in between A and D. Who will be to the immediate right of E?
questions.explanation: Number the places 1 to 5 from the left, with A at 1. C is exactly midway between A and D, and E is immediately right of D, so D is at 3, C at 2 and E at 4, leaving B at 5, immediately right of E.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 23, 50, 108, 228, ?, 964

Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Monday : Thursday :: Wednesday : ?
questions.explanation: Thursday is three days after Monday, and three days after Wednesday is Saturday.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'we can go' is written as 'ti mi pi', 'can i sit' is written as 'pi ri di' and 'sit and go' is written as 'di si ti'. How will 'and' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: 'Can' is in the first two phrases, so it is 'pi'; 'sit' is in the second and third, so 'di'; 'go' is in the first and third, so 'ti'. In 'sit and go' = 'di si ti' that leaves 'si' for 'and'.

questions.text: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? KSCA, OXWG, ?, WHKS, AMEY
questions.explanation: The first letters move +4 (K, O, S, W, A), the second +5 (S, X, C, H, M), the third −6 (C, W, Q, K, E) and the fourth +6 (A, G, M, S, Y), wrapping round the alphabet. The missing cluster is SCQM.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 91 * 7 * 2 * 4 * 10 * 5
questions.explanation: 91 ÷ 7 = 2 × 4 + 10 − 5, as both sides equal 13.

questions.text: Which of the following options represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1. Expensive 2. Experiment 3. Expertise 4. Expiry 5. Expert
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Expensive (1), Experiment (2), Expert (5), Expertise (3), Expiry (4). 'Expen' comes before 'exper', 'experi' before 'expert', 'expert' before 'expertise', which begins with it, and 'expi' comes last.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All apples are oranges. Some oranges are bananas. All bananas are kiwis. Conclusions: I. Some oranges are kiwis. II. Some oranges are apples. III. Some apples are bananas.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: The oranges that are bananas are kiwis, so some oranges are kiwis (I). All apples are oranges, so some oranges are apples (II). Nothing links the apples to the bananas, so III does not follow.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? DVH, FWM, JZR, LAW, PDB, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move +2 and +4 in turn (D, F, J, L, P, R), the second +1 and +3 in turn (V, W, Z, A, D, E) and the third +5 each time (H, M, R, W, B, G): REG.

questions.text: Eight people, D, E, G, H, M, N, Y and Z are sitting in a straight line, facing north. Y sits at one of the extreme ends of the line. Only two people sit between Y and Z. E sits third to the right of Z. Only four people sit between E and D. G sits at one of the positions to the right of E. N is not an immediate neighbour of Z. H sits second to the right of M. How many people sit to the left of M?
questions.explanation: Number the places 1 to 8 from the left. If Y were at 8, Z would be at 5 and E at 8, Y's own place, so Y is at 1, Z at 4 and E at 7. D, with four people between it and E, is at 2, and G, to E's right, at 8. N cannot sit next to Z, so it takes 6, leaving 3 and 5 for M and H: M at 3, H at 5. Y and D sit to the left of M.

questions.text: Which of the mathematical signs should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct? 12 + 112 ÷ 16 - 8 × 64 = 140
questions.explanation: After interchanging + and ×: 12 × 112 ÷ 16 − 8 + 64 = 84 − 8 + 64 = 140.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 665, 670, 663, 674, 661, 678, ?, 682
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 665, 663, 661 fall by 2, so the next is 659; 670, 674, 678, 682 rise by 4.

questions.text: In a certain code language, the word ‘GLAD’ is written as ZLADG. The word ‘SCAR’ is written as ‘ZCARS’. How is the word ‘LOST’ written in the same code language?
questions.explanation: Z is written first and the word's first letter moves to the end: GLAD → Z + LADG and SCAR → Z + CARS. So LOST → Z + OSTL: ZOSTL.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term. 407 : 37 :: ? : 59 :: 253 : 23
questions.explanation: Each first term is 11 times the second: 407 = 37 × 11 and 253 = 23 × 11. So ? = 59 × 11 = 649.

questions.text: Famous ruler Kanishka belonged to the ____________ dynasty.
questions.explanation: Kanishka was the best-known ruler of the Kushana dynasty; he ruled from Purushapura (Peshawar), and the fourth Buddhist council was held in Kashmir in his reign.

questions.text: All executive actions of the Governor of a state shall be expressed to be taken in the name of ___________.
questions.explanation: Article 166(1) says that all executive action of the Government of a State shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the Governor.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Battle of Buxar was fought in ______.
questions.explanation: At Buxar in October 1764 the East India Company under Hector Munro defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II.

questions.text: Vishu is predominantly celebrated in which of the following states of India?
questions.explanation: Vishu, the traditional new year of the Malayalis, falls in mid-April, on the first day of the Malayalam month of Medam, and is celebrated chiefly in Kerala.

questions.text: From the _______ budget, the practice of showing budget deficit has been discontinued in India.
questions.explanation: The 1997-98 Budget ended the ad hoc Treasury Bills that had financed the budget deficit, from 1 April 1997, and dropped the practice of showing the 'budget deficit'; the fiscal deficit became the main measure.

questions.text: A nation that has positive net exports enjoys a trade____________.
questions.explanation: Positive net exports mean that exports exceed imports: a trade surplus. Imports above exports give a trade deficit.

questions.text: The sun is about ______ km away from the earth.
questions.explanation: The mean distance between the Earth and the Sun is about 150 million km (149.6 million km, one astronomical unit).

questions.text: The 108 feet bronze statue of prosperity in Bengaluru, inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has been built to commemorate whom?
questions.explanation: The 108-foot bronze 'Statue of Prosperity' at Kempegowda International Airport, unveiled by Narendra Modi on 11 November 2022, honours Nadaprabhu Kempegowda, the 16th-century chieftain who founded Bengaluru.

questions.text: Tanjore Balasaraswati was a well-known _______ dancer.
questions.explanation: Tanjore (T.) Balasaraswati was one of the great Bharatanatyam dancers of the twentieth century; she received the Padma Vibhushan in 1977.

questions.text: Give an example of means of personal communication.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives telephone service, which links one person with another, as the post does: personal communication. Television and radio carry the same message to many people at once (mass communication), and a computer is a device that can serve either purpose.

questions.text: Under which of the following articles has the Right to property been shifted as a legal right?
questions.explanation: The 44th Amendment (1978) took the right to property out of the Fundamental Rights and placed it in Article 300-A: no person shall be deprived of property save by authority of law. It is now a constitutional (legal) right.

questions.text: Who among the following political leaders succeeded Venkaiah Naidu to become Vice President of India in August 2022?
questions.explanation: Jagdeep Dhankhar, Governor of West Bengal until July 2022, won the vice-presidential election and took office on 11 August 2022, succeeding M. Venkaiah Naidu.

questions.text: Among the given options, _______is the method of irrigation.
questions.explanation: A canal carries water from a river or reservoir to the fields, a means of irrigation. Double cropping is growing two crops a year on the same land, ploughing prepares the soil, and step (terrace) cultivation is farming on hill slopes.

questions.text: Identify an element that is NOT a semi-metal.
questions.explanation: Caesium is an alkali metal, one of the most reactive metals. Germanium, arsenic and silicon are metalloids (semi-metals), with properties between those of metals and non-metals.

questions.text: Where can you find 70 percent of freshwater resources on the Earth?
options: Antarctica, Greenland and the mountainous regions of the world
Himalayas and the Bay of Bengal
questions.explanation: Of the Earth's small share of fresh water, nearly 70% is locked up as ice sheets and glaciers in Antarctica, Greenland and the mountain regions.

questions.text: Which political leader became Member of Legislative Assembly from Thrikkakara constituency, Kerala in June 2022?
questions.explanation: Uma Thomas of the Congress won the Thrikkakara by-election, held on 31 May 2022 with the result declared on 3 June, after the death of her husband, the sitting MLA P.T. Thomas, in December 2021.

questions.text: Consumers expect better-quality foods with ____________ of nutrients.
questions.explanation: 'Retention' of nutrients means keeping them through processing and storage, which consumers want of better-quality food. Contamination and adulteration spoil food, and exclusion would leave the nutrients out.

questions.text: What are the height of Badminton posts?
questions.explanation: Under the Laws of Badminton the posts are 1.55 m high from the surface of the court; the top of the net is 1.524 m high at the centre.

questions.text: Who among the following is a Bharatanatyam performer?
questions.explanation: Tanjore Balasaraswati was a leading Bharatanatyam dancer. Sitara Devi danced Kathak, Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma Mohiniyattam and Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma Kuchipudi.

questions.text: 40 men can complete a work in 15 days. They started working, and after 5 days 10 more men joined them. In how many days will the total work be completed?
questions.explanation: The work is 40 × 15 = 600 man-days. The first 5 days do 200; the remaining 400 man-days take 50 men 8 days, so the work is done in 5 + 8 = 13 days.

questions.text: If the height of a cylinder is increased by 25%, and the radius of its base is decreased by 15%, then find the percentage increase/decrease in its curved surface area.
questions.explanation: The curved surface area 2πrh changes by the factor 1.25 × 0.85 = 1.0625: an increase of 6.25%.

questions.text: A sum of ₹1,20,000 was invested in a fixed deposit in the year 2019 at the rate of 12% per annum compounding annually. What will its approximate value be in the year 2022?
A and B working together can finish a project in 16 days while B alone can do it in 24 days. In how many days can A alone finish the project?
questions.explanation: A alone does 1/16 − 1/24 = (3 − 2)/48 = 1/48 of the project a day, so A takes 48 days.

questions.text: A policeman spots a thief 120 m ahead, immediately the policeman starts chasing the thief. The policeman runs 26 m in a minute and the thief runs 20 m in a minute. In what time will the policeman catch the thief?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 26 − 20 = 6 m a minute, so he closes the 120 m gap in 120/6 = 20 minutes.

questions.text: An almirah was bought for ₹15,500 and ₹260 was spent on its transportation. At what price should it be sold to gain 20%?

A thief is observed by a policeman from a distance of 420 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The policeman and the thief run at a speed of 25 km/h and 20 km/h, respectively. What is the distance between them after three minutes?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 25 − 20 = 5 km/h, that is 5,000 m in 60 minutes, so in 3 minutes he gains 250 m: 420 − 250 = 170 m.

questions.text: If the LCM of the first 110 natural numbers is N, then find the LCM of the first 115 natural numbers.
questions.explanation: Of 111 to 115, only 113 brings a new factor: it is prime. 111 = 3 × 37, 112 = 2⁴ × 7, 114 = 2 × 3 × 19 and 115 = 5 × 23, and each of these prime powers already divides N (2⁶ = 64 is among the first 110). So the LCM is 113N.

questions.text: A shopkeeper is selling a gift packet of fruits in which he is mixing apples and mangoes. The packet contains total of 12 kg fruits at an average rate of ₹100 per kg. In the packet there are 8 kg of apples at the rate of ₹90 per kg, while there are 4 kg of mangoes at the rate of ₹X per kg. Find the value of ‘X’. Note: All other charges are to be ignored for packing.
questions.explanation: The packet's value is 12 × 100 = ₹1,200. The apples account for 8 × 90 = ₹720, so 4 kg of mangoes cost ₹480 and X = 480/4 = 120.

questions.text: If 12 men can build a wall 60 metres long in 5 days, then what length of a similar wall can be built by 24 men in 2 days?
questions.explanation: The length built goes as men × days: 60 × (24 × 2)/(12 × 5) = 60 × 48/60 = 48 metres.

questions.text: Ramesh was receiving two offers on a book with a marked price of ₹800. Either two successive discounts of 20% each, or two successive discounts of 30% and 10%. How much more must Ramesh have saved if he chose the superior scheme over the other?
questions.explanation: Two discounts of 20% leave 0.8 × 0.8 = 0.64 of the price, a saving of ₹288 on ₹800; 30% and 10% leave 0.7 × 0.9 = 0.63, a saving of ₹296. The better scheme saves ₹8 more.

questions.text: The profit percentage made on an item sold for Rs.1,920 is equal to the loss percentage made on selling the same item for Rs.1,280. What should the item be sold for in order to make a 25% profit?
questions.explanation: Equal profit and loss percentages put the cost midway: (1,920 + 1,280)/2 = ₹1,600, as 320/1,600 = 20% either way. A 25% profit needs 1,600 × 1.25 = ₹2,000.

questions.text: When the price of a Bluetooth earphone is increased by 12%, its sale(number of Bluetooth earphones) is reduced by 20%. What is the net impact on its revenue?
questions.explanation: Revenue = price × number sold, so it changes by the factor 1.12 × 0.8 = 0.896: a 10.4% fall.

questions.text: In 90 litres of a mixture of milk and water, the ratio of milk and water is 4 : 1. How much water should be added in the mixture so that the ratio of milk to water becomes 3 : 1?
questions.explanation: The mixture holds 72 litres of milk and 18 of water. For 3 : 1 the water must be 72/3 = 24 litres, so 6 litres must be added.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. Trouble and disease give us bad ______.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'experiences'; the other options drop the first 'e' or swap letters.

questions.text: Identify the MISSPELT word in the following sentence. In our school, innovative and effective academic and evaluation strategies and intervantions are needed.
questions.explanation: 'Intervantions' is misspelt: the word is 'interventions', with '-ven-'. The other three words are spelt correctly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. “Travel on a” hot dusty train gives me no pleasure.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'Travelling on a': the gerund names the activity and is the natural subject of 'gives', and one travels 'on' a train. The noun 'travel' as printed is also possible, but there is no 'No substitution' option; 'Travel in a' keeps the noun with the less usual preposition, 'at a' is the wrong preposition and 'Travels' cannot be the subject of 'gives'.

questions.text: Complete the sentence by choosing the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. If the answer is “false”, it is _________.
questions.explanation: 'False' means not true: 'untrue'. 'Genuine', 'correct' and 'right' are close to its opposite.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. I visit my school / once a year / to meeting / my former teachers.
questions.explanation: Purpose is shown with the infinitive 'to meet', not 'to meeting': 'I visit my school once a year to meet my former teachers.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom that can be substituted in the following sentence. I am “at sea” after listening to the arguments.
questions.explanation: To be 'at sea' is to be confused and unsure what to do: 'perplexed'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Slack
questions.explanation: 'Slack' means not active or busy, as in 'business is slack': 'inactive'. 'Tight' and 'hyperactive' are close to its opposites.

questions.text: Select the correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. One must do “his work”.
questions.explanation: With the pronoun 'one' as subject, the possessive that follows is 'one's': 'One must do one's work.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment. I thought I finished my work but I realised that all of my work is faulty. I have to “start it over again”.
options: get a pat on the back
go back to the drawing board
questions.explanation: To 'go back to the drawing board' is to start again from the beginning after a plan or piece of work has failed. To 'break new ground' is to do something new, a 'pat on the back' is praise, and to 'break the back of' a task is to finish the hardest part.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets and complete the sentence. The weather is ______ (gloomy) and windy.
questions.explanation: 'Gloomy' weather is dark and dull: 'cloudy'. 'Bright', 'shiny' and 'jovial' are close to its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. She heard a loud humming noise and “guess that it is being an aeroplane”.
options: to guess that it is being the aeroplane
guessed that it was an aeroplane
has guessed that it is aeroplane
questions.explanation: 'Heard' sets the sentence in the past, so the second verb follows it: 'She heard a loud humming noise and guessed that it was an aeroplane.' 'Is being' cannot describe a state like this.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. I had to keep very ________ when the photographer was taking my picture.
questions.explanation: To keep 'still' is to stay without moving, as for a photograph. 'Still' is a homonym: the same word also means 'even now' and names an apparatus for distilling.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in the bracket to fill in the blank. If a person commits a crime with (malice)_________, they did it on purpose.
questions.explanation: 'Malice' is the wish to harm others; its opposite is 'goodwill'. 'Rancour', 'disdain' and 'disgust' are all hostile feelings, close to 'malice' rather than opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence. He was “brusque” and candid in the interview.
questions.explanation: 'Brusque' means short and offhand in speech or manner: 'abrupt'. 'Vociferous' means loud and insistent.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. The engineers finally “destroyed” the ship to its original form.
questions.explanation: To 'destroy' is to ruin; its opposite, which the sentence needs ('to its original form'), is 'restored'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. And you could hardly call it a (1) ________ at all, because Uncle Bob held his (2) _______ as though he had hold of a shovel, and tried to scoop up every ball that came over the net, even those he should have left for Uncle Ted. And then he took off his (3) _______ and played in just his trousers and stockinged feet, and with his face split nearly in two by his grin, he started (4) _______ over the net, and playing on Arnold’s side instead. And the ball would (5) ______on the roof of the house, or land in the rambler roses and bring down a shower of petals, and getting it again Uncle Bob would shake down more petals all over himself, so they’d be in his hair.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: Uncle Bob's clumsy play is the reason one could hardly call it a 'game' at all.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. And you could hardly call it a (1) ________ at all, because Uncle Bob held his (2) _______ as though he had hold of a shovel, and tried to scoop up every ball that came over the net, even those he should have left for Uncle Ted. And then he took off his (3) _______ and played in just his trousers and stockinged feet, and with his face split nearly in two by his grin, he started (4) _______ over the net, and playing on Arnold’s side instead. And the ball would (5) ______on the roof of the house, or land in the rambler roses and bring down a shower of petals, and getting it again Uncle Bob would shake down more petals all over himself, so they’d be in his hair.

questions.explanation: He held his 'racket' as though it were a shovel and tried to scoop up every ball that came over the net.

questions.explanation: He went on playing 'in just his trousers and stockinged feet', so what he took off was his 'shirt'. 'Trousers' and 'pants' contradict the sentence, and taking off a 'belt' would not leave him in just his trousers.
