questions.explanation: A ball 'bounces' on a roof. 'Jump' and 'leap' are what living creatures do, and to 'flake' is to come off in thin pieces.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 73, 74, 66, 93, 29, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are +1, −8, +27 and −64, the cubes 1³, 2³, 3³ and 4³ with alternating signs. The next is +5³ = +125: 29 + 125 = 154.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? CMUZ, FOVB, ?, LSXF, OUYH
questions.explanation: The first letters move +3 (C, F, I, L, O), the second +2 (M, O, Q, S, U), the third +1 (U, V, W, X, Y) and the fourth +2 (Z, B, D, F, H, wrapping round after Z): IQWD.

questions.text: In a code language, 'sweet fruits' is coded as 're de', 'mango is sweet' is coded as 'de me ke', 'orange is citrus' is coded as 'ke le pe', 'eat orange' is coded as 'pe ne'. What is the code for the word 'eat'?
questions.explanation: 'Sweet' is 'de' (in the first two codes), 'is' is 'ke' (the second and third) and 'orange' is 'pe' (the third and fourth). So 'eat', the other word of 'eat orange', is 'ne'.

questions.text: Which of the mathematical signs should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct? 135 ÷ 15 × 27 + 3 - 18 = 252
In a certain code language, ‘MOVE’ is written as ‘NQWG’ and ‘RUST’ is written as ‘SWTV’. How will ‘TASK’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, +2, +1, +2: MOVE → NQWG and RUST → SWTV. So TASK → UCTM.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All apples are cake. All cakes are bananas. Some bananas are fruit. Conclusions: I. Some apples are cake. II. Some bananas are apples. III. Some fruits are bananas.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions II and III follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.
questions.explanation: All apples are cakes, so some apples are cakes (I). As all cakes are bananas, all apples are bananas, so some bananas are apples (II). 'Some bananas are fruit' gives 'some fruits are bananas' (III). All three follow.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? LQOA, ?, LUOE, LWOG, LYOI
questions.explanation: The first and third letters stay L and O; the second moves +2 (Q, S, U, W, Y) and the fourth +2 (A, C, E, G, I): LSOC.

questions.text: ‘Strength’ is related to ‘Weakness’ in the same way as ‘Courage’ is related to ‘________’. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word)
questions.explanation: 'Weakness' is the opposite of 'strength', and 'cowardice' the opposite of 'courage'.

questions.text: ‘A + B’ means ‘B is the paternal grandfather of A’; ‘A @ B’ means ‘B is the brother of A’; ‘A % B’ means ‘B is the daughter of A’; ‘A $ B’ means ‘B is the husband of A’; If A $ B % C @ D + E, then how is E related to A?
questions.explanation: A $ B: B is A's husband. B % C: C is B's daughter. C @ D: D is C's brother, so also B's child. D + E: E is D's father's father, that is B's father. So E is the father of A's husband: her father-in-law.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Horse : Stable :: Birds : ?
questions.explanation: A horse is kept in a stable, and birds live in a nest.

questions.text: Seven people I, II, III, IV, V, VI, and VII are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. I and III are not sitting next to each other. VII is sitting between VI and IV. IV is sitting to the immediate left of I. Only II is sitting between V and III. Who is sitting between I and VII?
questions.explanation: IV sits next to I, and VII between VI and IV, so I, IV, VII and VI sit side by side in that order and IV is between I and VII. The rest fits: V sits on I's other side, then II and III, so I and III are not neighbours.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the sixth number is related to the fifth number. 64 : 16 :: 169 : ? :: 256 : 32
questions.explanation: Each second number is twice the square root of the first: 2 × √64 = 16 and 2 × √256 = 32. So 2 × √169 = 2 × 13 = 26.

questions.text: If A denotes ÷, B denotes ×, C denotes + and D denotes −, then what will be the value of the following equation? 24 B 12 A 8 C 10 D 6 =?
questions.explanation: After replacing the letters: 24 × 12 ÷ 8 + 10 − 6 = 288 ÷ 8 + 10 − 6 = 36 + 10 − 6 = 40.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1. lantern 2. lavish 3. lament 4. latitude 5. lately
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: lament (3), lantern (1), lately (5), latitude (4), lavish (2). 'Lam' comes before 'lan', 'lat' and 'lav', and 'late' before 'lati'.

questions.text: A teacher makes 10 kindergarten children sit in two parallel rows, such that five children are sitting in each row facing each other. Anu, Bobby, Lilly, Tom and Sudha sitting in Row 1 face north, while children Priya, Rama, Uma, Kala and Guna in Row 2 face the south direction. Lilly is facing the immediate neighbour of Guna. Tom sits third to the left of Sudha. Anu does not sit at the corners. Neither Priya nor Rama sits at the corner. Guna sits in the middle of the line. Only one child sits between Lilly and Tom. Kala sits at one of the corners but not facing Sudha. Priya sits to the right of Rama but not immediate. Which child is facing Tom?
questions.explanation: Number the seats 1 to 5 from west to east: Row 1 faces north (its left is west) and Row 2 south (its right is west). Guna sits at 3, so Lilly is at 2 or 4; Tom, third to the left of Sudha, is at 1 or 2, and with one child between Lilly and Tom, Tom is at 2 and Lilly at 4. Priya and Rama, at neither corner, take 2 and 4, and Priya, to Rama's right, is at 2, facing Tom.

questions.text: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 57, 50, 64, ?, 71, 36
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 57, 64, 71 rise by 7 and 50, ?, 36 fall by 7, so the missing term is 43.

questions.text: Which of the following is a paddy crop?
questions.explanation: 'Paddy' is rice, especially rice growing in the field or still in its husk.

questions.text: A budget document that relates to the assets and liabilities in the capital account of the government, is referred as:
questions.explanation: The capital budget accounts for the government's capital receipts and capital expenditure, that is the changes in its assets and liabilities; the revenue budget covers its current receipts and spending.

questions.text: As of November 2022, who is the President of Bharatiya Janata Party, a political party in India?
questions.explanation: Jagat Prakash (J. P.) Nadda was elected BJP president unopposed on 20 January 2020, succeeding Amit Shah, and held the post in November 2022.

questions.text: From the following, which one is NOT the principle of Parliamentary Government of India?
options: Clear division of power among Legislature, Executive and Judiciary
questions.explanation: A strict separation of powers belongs to the presidential system. In India's parliamentary system the executive is drawn from the legislature and is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, the majority party forms the government and the Lok Sabha can be dissolved.

questions.text: The inscriptions of the Pallavas mention a number of local assemblies. These included the ______, which was an assembly of brahmin land owners.
questions.explanation: Pallava inscriptions mention the sabha, an assembly of brahmin landowners, the ur, a village assembly where the landowners were not brahmins, and the nagaram, an organisation of merchants.

questions.text: The bedrock of India's democracy is the rule of law and that means we have to have _________________.
questions.explanation: The rule of law means that everyone, the government included, is bound by the law, and enforcing it needs courts free of executive and legislative control: an independent judiciary.

questions.text: Which mountain range prevents the cold Siberian winds from entering India?
questions.explanation: The Himalayas stand across the north of India and keep out the cold winds from Central Asia and Siberia.

questions.text: Who has replaced Ajit Mohan as the new Indian head of Meta in November 2022?
questions.explanation: Meta named Sandhya Devanathan, until then its vice-president for gaming in Asia-Pacific, to lead Meta India on 17 November 2022, after Ajit Mohan left for Snap; she took charge on 1 January 2023.

questions.text: Which among the following classical dance forms was originally known as Sadir Attam?
questions.explanation: Bharatanatyam was known as Sadir (Sadir Attam), the temple dance of Tamil Nadu, until it was revived and renamed in the 1930s.

questions.text: Economists have found that a poor nation can only progress only if they have good _________.
questions.explanation: NCERT's 'Indian Economic Development' makes this point: industry gives more stable employment than agriculture and promotes modernisation and overall prosperity, so a poor nation needs a good industrial sector to progress.

questions.text: Who among the following was awarded the TTK Memorial Award by Madras Music Academy?
questions.explanation: The Kuchipudi guru Vempati Chinna Satyam received the Music Academy's TTK Award in 1994; the Academy's list of TTK Award recipients names none of the other three.

questions.text: SAMADHAN portal allows online registration with the intent to make justice for workmen simple and quick. Industrial dispute is raised before _______ of the area.
questions.explanation: On the Ministry of Labour and Employment's SAMADHAN portal, workmen, unions and employers raise an industrial dispute online; it goes to the conciliation officer of the area, who tries to settle it under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.

questions.text: Which of these is a micronutrient?
questions.explanation: Iron is needed by the body in small amounts, so it is a micronutrient. Carbohydrates are a macronutrient, and fibre and water are not counted as micronutrients.

questions.text: What was the female literacy rate of India as per the Census 2011?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 put the literacy rate of women at 65.46%, against 82.14% for men and 74.04% overall.

questions.text: What are the products formed when lead reacts with copper chloride?
questions.explanation: Lead is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from its salt: Pb + CuCl₂ → PbCl₂ + Cu.

questions.text: The people of Kashmir dedicates the Navreh festival to Goddess __________ and pay homage to her during the festival.
questions.explanation: Navreh, the Kashmiri Pandit new year on the first day of the bright half of Chaitra, is dedicated to Goddess Sharika, whose shrine is on Hari Parbat in Srinagar.

questions.text: Mirabai Chanu belongs to which of the following state of India?
questions.explanation: Saikhom Mirabai Chanu, the weightlifter who won silver in the women's 49 kg at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, is from Manipur.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: With which country did India had a war in the region of the McMahon line in 1962?
questions.explanation: The India-China war of October-November 1962 was fought along the disputed border, including the McMahon line in the eastern sector (then NEFA, now Arunachal Pradesh).

questions.text: Who hosted the 2011 cricket world cup?
questions.explanation: India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh co-hosted the 2011 Cricket World Cup, which India won in the final at Mumbai's Wankhede Stadium.

questions.text: Aluminium smelting is the ______ most important metallurgical industry in India.
questions.explanation: NCERT's 'Contemporary India II' calls aluminium smelting the second most important metallurgical industry in India, after iron and steel.

questions.text: Find the third proportional to 24 and 12.
questions.explanation: The third proportional x satisfies 24 : 12 = 12 : x, so x = 12²/24 = 144/24 = 6.

questions.text: The two numbers are in the ratio 2:3. If eight is added to each of the numbers, then their ratio changed to 8:11. What are the two numbers?
questions.explanation: (2x + 8)/(3x + 8) = 8/11 gives 22x + 88 = 24x + 64, so x = 12 and the numbers are 24 and 36.

questions.text: Akash can do a piece of work in 74 days. Vishal can do this work in 37 days. Akash started the work alone. After how many days should Vishal join him, so that the total work is finished in 40 days?
questions.explanation: Akash works all 40 days and does 40/74 of the work, so Vishal must do 34/74 = 17/37 of it, which takes him 17 days. He joins after 40 − 17 = 23 days.

questions.text: Rani goes to school from home at a speed of 30 km/h and returns to home at the speed of 20 km/h. If the distance between her home and school is 8 km, then what is the average speed of the whole journey?
questions.explanation: For equal distances the average speed is 2 × 30 × 20/(30 + 20) = 1200/50 = 24 km/h: 16 km in 8/30 + 8/20 = 2/3 hour.

questions.text: Samir purchased 20 dozens of toys at the rate of Rs.372 per dozen. He sold each one of them at the rate of Rs.32. What was his percentage profit?
questions.explanation: Each toy costs 372 ÷ 12 = ₹31 and sells for ₹32, so the profit is 1/31 × 100 = 3.23%, about 3.2%.

questions.text: A company employed 200 workers to complete a certain work in 150 days. In 50 days, only one-fourth of the work was completed. In order to complete the entire work in time, how many additional workers need to be employed?
questions.explanation: 200 workers did 1/4 of the work in 50 days, so the whole work is 200 × 50 × 4 = 40,000 worker-days. The remaining 30,000 worker-days must be done in 100 days, which needs 300 workers: 100 more.

questions.text: The population of a town increased by 10% in the first year and decreased by 10% in the second year. If the population at the end of the second year is 990000, then find the population at the beginning of the first year.
On a winter's day, the average temperature during the day time is 34°C. At night the temperature falls to 8°C. What is the percent decrease?
Find the discount, if the marked price of book is Rs.5000 and sold it for Rs. 4000.
questions.explanation: Discount = marked price − selling price = ₹5,000 − ₹4,000 = ₹1,000.

questions.text: If the difference between the compound and simple interest on a certain sum of money for three years at 8% per annum is Rs.61.60, then find the sum.
Find the average of the square of the following numbers: 5, 8, 9, 12, 15 and 16.
What will be the sum of HCF and LCM of 12 and 16?
questions.explanation: 12 = 2² × 3 and 16 = 2⁴, so the HCF is 4 and the LCM 48: 4 + 48 = 52.

questions.text: There was a discount of 10 percent on sling bags. Mayuri bought a sling bag and got a 5 percent extra discount for paying cash. She paid Rs. 2565. What was the price tag on the sling bag?
questions.explanation: After 10% and then 5% off she pays 0.9 × 0.95 = 0.855 of the price tag: 2565 ÷ 0.855 = ₹3,000.

questions.text: Suresh sold his mobile phone to Mohan for ₹29,700 at a gain of 10%. What was the cost price of the phone for Suresh?
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. The robbers were “captured” and brought to the jail.
questions.explanation: 'Captured' means caught and held; its opposite is 'released', set free. 'Seized' is close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She needs to be ________ if she wants to stand up to her bullies.
questions.explanation: To stand up to bullies she needs to be 'bolder', braver; 'blonder', 'balder' and 'boulder' only sound alike.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. A couple of parrots __________ on the telephone wires.
questions.explanation: Birds 'perch' when they settle on a wire or a branch. Parrots do not fly 'on' wires, 'seeded' does not fit, and 'waited' says nothing about where they settled.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. The child made “a wry face” when he was denied entry into the museum.
questions.explanation: To 'make a wry face' is to twist the face in dislike or disappointment, as a child refused entry would.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Tasty
questions.explanation: 'Insipid' means lacking flavour, the opposite of 'tasty'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. A feeling comes over one that so much evil and misfortune _______ the world that a little more or less does not make much difference.
questions.explanation: 'Evil and misfortune', joined by 'and', take a plural verb, and the sentence is in the present ('comes', 'does not make'): 'so much evil and misfortune shadow the world'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Baffle
questions.explanation: To 'baffle' is to puzzle completely, to 'confuse'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Be in seventh heaven
questions.explanation: To 'be in seventh heaven' is to be extremely happy.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The doctors always wear a “right and suitable” uniform.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'decent', in the sense of proper and of an acceptable standard: 'The doctors always wear a decent uniform.' 'Fit' also means suitable, but in that sense it is normally followed by 'for' or 'to' ('fit for duty', 'fit to eat') rather than placed before a noun on its own; 'virtuous' describes moral character and 'nice' only pleasantness.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in past perfect tense. A. Fortunately, the movie had not been starting on time. B. Fortunately, the movie was not starting on time. C. Fortunately, the movie had not started on time. D. Fortunately, the movie did not start on time.
questions.explanation: The past perfect is 'had' + past participle: C, 'Fortunately, the movie had not started on time.' A is in the past perfect continuous, B in the past continuous and D in the simple past.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. He asked me “if I have anything” to say.
questions.explanation: After a past reporting verb ('asked'), the present 'have' moves back to the past in reported speech: 'He asked me if I had anything to say.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Officious
questions.explanation: 'Officious' means too eager to assert authority or to interfere; 'timid', shy and lacking confidence, is the opposite. 'Obtrusive' is close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Conveneince' is misspelt: the word is 'convenience', ending '-ience'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Accomplish
questions.explanation: To 'accomplish' a task is to 'achieve' or complete it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Twenty five years ago, few people realised that computers (1)___________ about to become part of our daily lives. This short period of time has seen (2)__________ changes, in business, education and public administration. Jobs which took weeks to complete in the past are now carried out in minutes. People who spent all day copying and checking calculations are now freed from these (3)_________ tasks. Students have become as familiar with hardware and software as their parents were with pencils and exercise books. Computerisation of public records has enabled government departments to analyse the needs of citizens in detail. Some of us may wonder, (4)_________, life has really improved as a result of these changes. Many jobs disappeared, for example, when intelligent machines took over the work. Employers complain that clerical (5)________ have become dependent on calculators and cannot do simple arithmetic.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 1.
questions.explanation: 'Computers' is plural and the sentence is in the past ('realised'): 'computers were about to become part of our daily lives'.

questions.explanation: 'Clerical staff' are the office workers who once did such calculations by hand.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question marks (?) in the given series? 1, 9, 25, 49, ?, ?, 169, 225, 289
questions.explanation: The terms are the squares of the odd numbers: 1², 3², 5², 7², then 9² = 81 and 11² = 121, then 13², 15² and 17².

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. GTNS, OPVA, WLDI, ? , MDTY
questions.explanation: The first, third and fourth letters each move 8 forward, wrapping round after Z (G, O, W, E, M; N, V, D, L, T; S, A, I, Q, Y), and the second moves 4 back (T, P, L, H, D): EHLQ.

questions.text: ‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’; ‘A & B’ means ‘A is the father of B’; ‘A # B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’; Which of the following options means 'P is the mother of L'?
questions.explanation: P @ R & S # L: P is R's wife, R is S's father and S is L's sister. So R is L's father too, and P, his wife, is L's mother.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Arc : Circle :: Cockpit : ?
questions.explanation: An arc is a part of a circle, and a cockpit, where the pilot sits, is a part of an airplane.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1. Chair 2. Charm 3. Chauffer 4. Chain 5. Change
questions.explanation: Chain comes before Chair (n before r), and Chair before Change (i before n); then come Charm and Chauffer (r before u after 'cha'): 4, 1, 5, 2, 3.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 81, 88, 102, ?, 151, 186
questions.explanation: The differences are 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, the multiples of 7: 102 + 21 = 123, and 123 + 28 = 151 checks.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter-cluster series? UH, SD, OZ, MV, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move back 2 and 4 in turn (U, S, O, M, I), and the second letters move back 4 each time (H, D, Z, V, R): IR.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 12 × 108 – 36 ÷ 6 + 18 = 48
In a certain code language, ‘PROVED’ is written as ‘65’and ‘REMOVER’ is written as ‘81’.How will ‘DEVOUR’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet minus 15: PROVED is 16 + 18 + 15 + 22 + 5 + 4 = 80, and 80 − 15 = 65; REMOVER is 96, and 96 − 15 = 81. DEVOUR is 4 + 5 + 22 + 15 + 21 + 18 = 85, so 85 − 15 = 70.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered 1, 2 and 3. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: 1. All cottons are silks. 2. All silks are wools. 3. All wools are jutes. Conclusions: 1. Some jutes are silks. 2. Some wools are cottons. 3. Some jutes are cottons.
questions.explanation: Cottons lie within silks, silks within wools and wools within jutes. So some jutes are silks, some wools are cottons and some jutes are cottons: all three follow.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 2 : 1 :: 54 : 3 :: 16 : ?
questions.explanation: Each first number is twice the cube of the second: 2 × 1³ = 2 and 2 × 3³ = 54. As 16 = 2 × 2³, the missing number is 2.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Engineer : build :: Physician : ________
questions.explanation: An engineer's work is to build, and a physician's work is to cure.

questions.text: Five people, K, L, M, N, and O are sitting in a straight row, facing north. L is sitting on the immediate left of N. M is sitting on the immediate left of L. N is sitting on the immediate left of O. K is sitting on the extreme right end of the row. Who is sitting in the exact middle of the row?
questions.explanation: M is to L's left, L to N's left and N to O's left, and K is at the right end, so from the left the row is M, L, N, O, K. N sits in the middle.

questions.text: In a certain language, DANGER is coded as REGNAD, DETAIL is coded as LIATED, how will DOCTOR be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each word is written in reverse: DANGER → REGNAD and DETAIL → LIATED. So DOCTOR → ROTCOD.

questions.text: If ‘+’ means ‘÷’, ‘÷’ means ‘-’, ‘-’ means ‘×’, and ‘×‘ means ‘+’. Which of the following will be the value of the expression? 63 ÷ 84 + 7 - 6 × 48

Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Rajesh is sitting second to the right of Ramesh. Ramesh is sitting to the immediate left of Suresh. Nimesh is sitting second to the right of Jayesh. Paresh is sitting second to the right of Rajesh. Jayesh is the immediate neighbour of Rajesh and Paresh. Who is sitting between Ramesh and Paresh?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's right is anticlockwise. Going round to the right from Ramesh, the order is Ramesh, Suresh, Rajesh, Jayesh, Paresh, Nimesh, so Nimesh sits between Paresh and Ramesh.

questions.text: Which among the following metals is the best conductor of heat?
questions.explanation: Silver conducts heat better than any other metal, ahead of copper and gold; iron and sodium are much poorer conductors.

questions.text: Mekapati Vikram Reddy, who became Member of Legislative Assembly from Atmakur constituency in Andhra Pradesh, in June 2022, belongs to ________ political party.
questions.explanation: Mekapati Vikram Reddy of the YSR Congress Party won the Atmakur by-election in June 2022, held after the death of his brother, the state minister Mekapati Goutham Reddy.

questions.text: Who among the following became the Chief Minister of Uttarakhand in March 2022?
questions.explanation: Pushkar Singh Dhami, Chief Minister since July 2021, was sworn in for a second term on 23 March 2022 after the BJP won the state election.

questions.text: Who among the following was awarded the Padma Shri for the contributions in Kathak?
questions.explanation: Sunayana Hazarilal, a Kathak dancer of the Janakiprasad (Banaras) gharana, received the Padma Shri in 2011.

questions.text: When a household’s income falls below the amount required to sustain basic living standards (food, shelter, housing), is called ________.
questions.explanation: Absolute poverty is an income below what is needed for basic needs such as food, clothing and shelter. Relative poverty is measured against the living standards of others in the same society.

questions.text: The Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill, 2021 proposes to increase the age of girl from 18 to______years.
questions.explanation: The Prohibition of Child Marriage (Amendment) Bill, 2021, introduced in the Lok Sabha in December 2021, proposed raising the minimum age of marriage for women from 18 to 21, the same as for men.

questions.text: Who was the mascot for the 2020 National Games of India?
questions.explanation: Rubigula, a flame-throated bulbul (Goa's state bird), was unveiled in early 2020 as the mascot of the National Games Goa was to host that year; Covid-19 postponed them. Savaj the lion was the mascot of the 2022 Games in Gujarat and Ammu the hornbill of the 2015 Games in Kerala.

questions.text: Aim of last (twelfth) five year plan was:
options: Faster, Sustainable, and More Inclusive Growth
questions.explanation: The Twelfth Five Year Plan (2012-17) had as its aim 'Faster, More Inclusive and Sustainable Growth'.

questions.text: Which one of the following is the oldest football competition in India?
questions.explanation: The Durand Cup, first held in 1888, is the oldest football tournament in India and in Asia.

questions.text: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development(NABARD) aims at providing credit and other facilities for the promotion and development of _______ industries.
questions.explanation: NABARD provides credit and other support for agriculture and rural development, including small-scale, cottage and village industries in rural areas.

questions.text: Who breaks down waste into smaller particles?
questions.explanation: Detritivores such as earthworms break detritus (dead plant and animal remains) into smaller particles, the step of decomposition called fragmentation.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In December 1929, under the presidency of ______, the Lahore Congress formalised the demand of 'Purna Swaraj'.
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the Lahore session of December 1929, which adopted complete independence (Purna Swaraj) as the Congress's goal.

questions.text: Under which Article of the Constitution does a citizen have the freedom to practice any profession or occupation?
questions.explanation: Article 19(1)(g) gives every citizen the right to practise any profession, or to carry on any occupation, trade or business.

questions.text: Who among the following met the Buddha to get his advice on the proposed attack on Vajjis?
questions.explanation: Ajatashatru of Magadha, wishing to attack the Vajjis, sent his minister Vassakara to the Buddha for advice.

questions.text: Which among the following dance forms is a unique dance form as the performers are dressed as women and is popular in the parts of Odisha?
questions.explanation: In Odisha's Gotipua, young boys dressed as girls dance in praise of Jagannath and Krishna; the form is a forerunner of Odissi.

questions.text: The climate of India is described as the ______ type.
questions.explanation: India's climate is described as the monsoon type, marked by the seasonal reversal of the winds.

questions.text: Major aspect of Green revolution is that, it has made India _____________.
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution of the late 1960s, with high-yielding seeds, irrigation and fertilisers, raised wheat and rice output enough to make India self-sufficient in food grains.

questions.text: Who has been appointed as the Chairman and Managing Director of the India Trade Promotion Organization in October 2022?
questions.explanation: Pradeep Singh Kharola, a retired IAS officer and former Civil Aviation Secretary, was appointed Chairman and Managing Director of the India Trade Promotion Organisation in October 2022, for two years.

questions.text: Find the greatest number that will divide 57, 93 and 191 so as to leave the same remainder in each case.
questions.explanation: The number must divide the differences 93 − 57 = 36, 191 − 93 = 98 and 191 − 57 = 134. As 36 = 2² × 3², 98 = 2 × 7² and 134 = 2 × 67, their HCF is 2.

questions.text: The fourth proportional of the numbers 0.002, 0.04 and 0.0006 is ________.
P, Q, and R can do a piece of work in 38 days. Q and R can do the work in 76 days. Find the number of days in which P can complete the same work.
questions.explanation: P alone does 1/38 − 1/76 = 2/76 − 1/76 = 1/76 of the work a day, so P takes 76 days.

questions.text: R goes to the post office from home covering a distance of 5 km and 400 metres in half an hour, and then goes to office covering a distance of 25 km and 750 metres in 90 minutes. What is his average speed from home to office in km/h?
questions.explanation: Total distance = 5.4 + 25.75 = 31.15 km and total time = 0.5 + 1.5 = 2 hours, so the average speed is 31.15 ÷ 2 = 15.575 km/h.

questions.text: If 'x' is divisible by 3 and 2, then 2x³ + 3x² is divisible by :
questions.explanation: x is a multiple of 6, say x = 6k. Then 2x³ + 3x² = x²(2x + 3) = 36k²(12k + 3) = 108k²(4k + 1), always divisible by 108. With x = 6 it is 540, which 72, 214 and 428 do not divide.

questions.text: The discount on a toy is 15%. A successive discount of 15% is also offered. What is the effective discount on the toy
questions.explanation: Two successive discounts of 15% leave 0.85 × 0.85 = 0.7225 of the price, so the effective discount is 27.75% (15 + 15 − 15 × 15/100).

questions.text: A board 100 cm long is trimmed to 86 cm. What percentage has been removed?
Find the average of the numbers 517, 139, 195, 176 and 192.
Rohan and Sohan can complete a piece of work in 10 days and 12 days, respectively. If they work on alternate days, starting with Sohan, in how many days will the whole work be completed?
questions.explanation: Take the work as 60 units: Rohan does 6 a day and Sohan 5. Each two-day pair does 11 units, so 5 pairs (10 days) do 55, and on day 11 Sohan does the last 5: 11 days.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'subservient', meaning too ready to obey others.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in the brackets to fill in the blank. We ____________ (agree) to talk to terrorists.
questions.explanation: 'Refuse' is the opposite of 'agree': 'We refuse to talk to terrorists.' 'Grant', 'admit' and 'allow' are close to agreeing.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Dense
questions.explanation: 'Dense' means closely packed, so its opposite is 'sparse', thinly scattered. 'Compact' is close to 'dense'.

questions.text: The sentence given below has one misspelt word. Spot the INCORRECTLY spelt word and select its correct spelling. Inkompetent employees of our company need to be sacked.
questions.explanation: 'Inkompetent' is misspelt: the word is 'incompetent', with a 'c', meaning lacking the ability to do a job well.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Not only composition, but also the wrong choice of Sridhar as the singer “destroyed the sweetness on the song”.
options: destroyed the sweetness of the song
destroyed the sweetness in the song
destroyed the sweetness by the song
destroyed the sweetness around the song
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'of', the usual preposition for a quality that belongs to something: 'the sweetness of the song', as in 'the beauty of the painting'. 'In' is sometimes heard ('there is a sweetness in the song') but is less natural after 'destroyed the sweetness', and 'on', 'by' and 'around' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Perfume
questions.explanation: A perfume is a pleasant smell and a stench a strong, foul one. 'Redolence' and 'fragrance' are close to 'perfume'.

questions.text: Select the word that is similar in meaning to the underlined word. My boss maintained a very “parochial” view of the world.
questions.explanation: 'Parochial' means having a narrow, limited outlook, concerned only with local matters.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Ample
questions.explanation: 'Ample' means enough or more than enough: 'abundant'. 'Insufficient' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Prosperity
questions.explanation: Prosperity is success and flourishing, especially in money matters; of the options only 'failure' is opposed to it. 'Money' and 'wealth' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To go through fire and water
questions.explanation: To 'go through fire and water' is to face great dangers or hardships, often for someone else's sake.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Taste of your own medicine
options: Have the same bad treatment that you have given to others
Try to manage something which went wrong
Extremely pleased and excited about something
questions.explanation: To get 'a taste of your own medicine' is to receive the same unpleasant treatment you have given others.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Mrs. Meera and family / received his letter / a week ago.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: 'a week ago' places the action in the past, so the simple past 'received' is right; 'his' refers to someone other than the subject (the letter's writer), so it need not agree with 'Mrs. Meera and family', an accepted way of naming a household.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Who “penned” this book on the history of India’s partition?
questions.explanation: 'Penned' (wrote) is already correct: the book has been written, so the simple past fits. 'Write' and 'pen' are base forms, which cannot follow 'Who' here, and 'publicise' changes the sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence. He went to the “tomb” of his father to pay his tribute.
questions.explanation: A tomb is a place where a dead person is buried, so 'grave' is closest. A mortuary keeps bodies before burial, and a funeral is the ceremony.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The Board of Doctors declared that the patient might take time to _____________.
questions.explanation: To 'come round' is to regain consciousness. 'Look round' means to inspect a place, and 'come across' to find by chance.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The major goal of renewable energy deployment in India is to drive economic (1)________, improve energy security, increase access to electricity, and (2)_________ climate change. Sustainable development is attainable via the use of sustainable energy and by giving residents (3)________to inexpensive, dependable, sustainable, and contemporary energy. Strong government backing and an increasingly favourable economic scenario have propelled India to the (4)________ of the world's most promising renewable energy sectors. The government has devised regulations, initiatives, and a welcoming atmosphere to (5)_________international investment and rapidly expand the country's presence in the renewable energy sector.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Renewable energy is meant to drive economic 'growth', alongside improving energy security and access to electricity.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The major goal of renewable energy deployment in India is to drive economic (1)________, improve energy security, increase access to electricity, and (2)_________ climate change. Sustainable development is attainable via the use of sustainable energy and by giving residents (3)________to inexpensive, dependable, sustainable, and contemporary energy. Strong government backing and an increasingly favourable economic scenario have propelled India to the (4)________ of the world's most promising renewable energy sectors. The government has devised regulations, initiatives, and a welcoming atmosphere to (5)_________international investment and rapidly expand the country's presence in the renewable energy sector.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Renewable energy is meant to 'reduce', that is lessen, climate change; 'increase' is the opposite of the aim.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The major goal of renewable energy deployment in India is to drive economic (1)________, improve energy security, increase access to electricity, and (2)_________ climate change. Sustainable development is attainable via the use of sustainable energy and by giving residents (3)________to inexpensive, dependable, sustainable, and contemporary energy. Strong government backing and an increasingly favourable economic scenario have propelled India to the (4)________ of the world's most promising renewable energy sectors. The government has devised regulations, initiatives, and a welcoming atmosphere to (5)_________international investment and rapidly expand the country's presence in the renewable energy sector.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Giving residents 'access' to energy is letting them obtain and use it; 'excess' sounds alike but means too much.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The major goal of renewable energy deployment in India is to drive economic (1)________, improve energy security, increase access to electricity, and (2)_________ climate change. Sustainable development is attainable via the use of sustainable energy and by giving residents (3)________to inexpensive, dependable, sustainable, and contemporary energy. Strong government backing and an increasingly favourable economic scenario have propelled India to the (4)________ of the world's most promising renewable energy sectors. The government has devised regulations, initiatives, and a welcoming atmosphere to (5)_________international investment and rapidly expand the country's presence in the renewable energy sector.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: To be propelled 'to the forefront' is to be brought to the leading position.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The major goal of renewable energy deployment in India is to drive economic (1)________, improve energy security, increase access to electricity, and (2)_________ climate change. Sustainable development is attainable via the use of sustainable energy and by giving residents (3)________to inexpensive, dependable, sustainable, and contemporary energy. Strong government backing and an increasingly favourable economic scenario have propelled India to the (4)________ of the world's most promising renewable energy sectors. The government has devised regulations, initiatives, and a welcoming atmosphere to (5)_________international investment and rapidly expand the country's presence in the renewable energy sector.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Welcoming regulations are meant to 'attract', that is draw in, international investment.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FIRST’ is coded as 79191921 and ‘TIME’ is coded as 219145. How will ‘BETTER’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Letters in odd places are written as their place in the alphabet plus 1, and letters in even places as their place: F I R S T → 7 9 19 19 21 and T I M E → 21 9 14 5. So B E T T E R → 3 5 21 20 6 18: 352120618.

questions.text: ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the father of B’; ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’; As per which of the following expressions ‘S is the wife of P’?
questions.explanation: P + Q: P is Q's father. Q × R: Q is R's brother. R ÷ S: R is S's daughter. P is R's father, so S, R's other parent, is R's mother: S is P's wife.

questions.text: Which of the mathematical signs should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct? 360 × 8 - 320 + 72 ÷ 5 = 85

A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a row facing North. G is to the immediate right of E. G is sitting to the extreme right of the row. A is sitting to the third place from the left of E. B is sitting to the immediate right of A. C is sitting to the right of B. D is sitting to the immediate left of A. Who is sitting to the extreme left of the row?
questions.explanation: Numbering the seats 1 to 7 from the left: G is at 7 and E at 6. A is third to the left of E, at 3, with B at 4 and D at 2; C, to B's right, is at 5, which leaves seat 1 for F.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 24 × 108 – 36 ÷ 6 + 18 = 84
questions.explanation: After interchanging ÷ and –: 24 × 108 ÷ 36 − 6 + 18 = 72 − 6 + 18 = 84.

questions.text: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 18, 20, ?, 128, 514, 2572

Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 12 : 3 :: 28 : 7 :: 32 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second number is the first divided by 4: 12 ÷ 4 = 3 and 28 ÷ 4 = 7. So 32 ÷ 4 = 8.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Broken 2 Bread 3 Bridge 4 Bride 5 Broom
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Bread (2), Bride (4), Bridge (3), Broken (1), Broom (5). 'Bre' comes before 'Bri' and 'Bro', 'Bride' before 'Bridge' ('e' before 'g'), and 'Brok' before 'Broo'.

questions.text: Amir, Bunty, Leslie, Pradeep, Eshan, Faiz, Gaurav and Harish are sitting around a square table facing the centre of the table. Some of them are sitting at the corners, while some are sitting at the exact centre of the sides. Pradeep sits third to the right of Gaurav. Pradeep sits at one of the corners. Bunty sits second to the right of Faiz. Faiz does not sit at any of the corners. Bunty is not an immediate neighbour of Pradeep. Harish is an immediate neighbour of Amir. Harish does not sit at any of the middle of the sides. Only one person sits between Harish and Leslie. Who sits third to the right of Amir?
questions.explanation: As all face the centre, each one's right runs anticlockwise. Numbering the seats to the right from Pradeep's corner (0): Gaurav is at 5, a side. Faiz, at a side, must be at 1 with Bunty at 3: Faiz at 3 would put Bunty in Gaurav's seat, and Faiz at 7 would put Bunty next to Pradeep. Harish, at a corner next to Amir, can only be at 6 with Amir at 7. With one person between Harish and Leslie, Leslie is at 4 (seat 0 is Pradeep's), which leaves Eshan at 2. Third to the right of Amir (7) is seat 2: Eshan.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. KILT, OMPX, SQTB, WUXF, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places forward from one cluster to the next, wrapping round after Z: K, O, S, W, A; I, M, Q, U, Y; L, P, T, X, B; T, X, B, F, J. The next cluster is AYBJ.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Ore : Metal :: Milk : ?
questions.explanation: Metal is obtained from ore, and curd is made from milk.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘HEALTH’ is written as ‘CGJJVN’ and 'CHARGE' is written as 'CJEGIT'. How will ‘HOURSE’ be written as in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward and each half of the word is then reversed: HEALTH → JGC NVJ → CGJ JVN and CHARGE → EJC TIG → CJE GIT. So HOURSE → JQW TUG → WQJ GUT: WQJGUT.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the statements. Statements: All camels are fractals. No fractal is a tube. All pianos are camels. Conclusions: I. Some tubes are camels. II. No piano is a tube.
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: All pianos are camels, all camels are fractals and no fractal is a tube, so no piano is a tube (II). For the same reason no camel is a tube, so I is false.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter-cluster series? HSU, JQO, LOI, NME, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move 2 forward (H, J, L, N, P), the second 2 back (S, Q, O, M, K), and the third are the vowels in reverse order (U, O, I, E, A): PKA.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 1995, 1895, 1695, 1395, ?
questions.explanation: The terms fall by 100, 200 and 300, so the next fall is 400: 1395 − 400 = 995.

questions.text: Who was the flag bearer for India for the opening ceremony of the Asian Games 2018?
questions.explanation: The javelin thrower Neeraj Chopra carried India's flag at the opening ceremony of the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta, where he went on to win gold.

questions.text: Who took over as the Director of Intelligence Bureau on 24 June 2022?
questions.explanation: On 24 June 2022 the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet named Tapan Kumar Deka, a 1988-batch IPS officer of the Himachal Pradesh cadre, Director of the Intelligence Bureau, succeeding Arvind Kumar, whose term ended on 30 June 2022.

questions.text: Yuki Bhambri is related to which of the following game?
questions.explanation: Yuki Bhambri is an Indian tennis player; he won the boys' singles at the 2009 Australian Open.

questions.text: Which among the following instruments is used to measure the humidity of the air or a gas?
questions.explanation: A hygrometer measures humidity. An anemometer measures wind speed, a bolometer radiant heat and a hydrometer the density of liquids.

questions.text: Rajagriha was the capital of Magadha for several years. Later the capital was shifted to ______.
questions.explanation: Rajagriha (present-day Rajgir, in Bihar) was Magadha's early capital; the capital later moved to Pataliputra, present-day Patna.

questions.text: Only Indian citizen above the age of __________ years are eligible for the appointment of the Governor of a State.
questions.explanation: Under Article 157 a person must be a citizen of India and have completed 35 years of age to be appointed Governor of a State.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a freshwater lake in India?
questions.explanation: Sambhar in Rajasthan is a salt lake, India's largest inland saline lake. Bhimtal (Uttarakhand), Loktak (Manipur) and Barapani, or Umiam (Meghalaya), are freshwater lakes.

questions.text: Which of the following folk dances is associated with the state of Tamil Nadu?
questions.explanation: Kummi is a Tamil Nadu folk dance in which women dance in a circle, clapping to the rhythm of their songs, at festivals such as Pongal. Lavani belongs to Maharashtra.

questions.text: ___________was passed in 2019 and as a result of which the security of Prime Minister of India and other former Prime Ministers was restricted.
questions.explanation: The Special Protection Group (Amendment) Act, 2019 limited SPG cover to the Prime Minister and the immediate family living with them, and to a former Prime Minister and family for five years after leaving office.

questions.text: Pick the odd one out (Hint: textile industry)
questions.explanation: Silk, cotton and woollen industries all make textiles; the electrical industry does not.

questions.text: Darshana Jhaveri received the Padma Shri for which dance form?
questions.explanation: Darshana Jhaveri, one of the Jhaveri sisters of Mumbai, is a Manipuri dancer and scholar; she received the Padma Shri in 2002.

questions.text: Total value of final goods and services produced______ domestic territory during an accounting year is domestic income.
questions.explanation: Domestic income counts what is produced within the country's domestic territory in the year, by residents and non-residents alike; adding net factor income from abroad gives national income.

questions.text: Which article of the Constitution of India abolishes the concept of ‘untouchability’ and prohibits its practice in any shape or form?
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes 'untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form; enforcing any disability arising out of it is an offence punishable by law.

questions.text: Who among the following was sworn in as chief minister of Goa in March 2022?
questions.explanation: Pramod Sawant was sworn in as Chief Minister of Goa for a second term on 28 March 2022, after the state's assembly election.

questions.text: The famous Pushkar Fair of Rajasthan is held _______ in a year.
questions.explanation: The Pushkar Fair is held once a year, in the Hindu month of Kartik (October-November), ending on Kartik Purnima.

questions.text: The Fifth five year plan of India, was focused on :
questions.explanation: The Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-79) aimed at the removal of poverty ('Garibi Hatao') and the attainment of self-reliance.

questions.text: At independence, about 75 percent of India's population was dependent on ____________.
questions.explanation: At independence India's economy was mainly agricultural: about three-quarters of its people depended on farming for a living, far more than on manufacturing, services or mining.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was one of the “Lal-Bal-Pal” of the freedom movement of India?
questions.explanation: Lal-Bal-Pal were the Extremist leaders Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal.

questions.text: The species that ______ a bare area are called pioneer species.
questions.explanation: In ecological succession the first species to colonise a bare area, such as lichens on bare rock, are the pioneer species.

questions.text: What is the rank of India in terms of Human Development Index 2021?
questions.explanation: In the Human Development Report 2021/22, released in September 2022, India ranked 132nd of 191 countries, with an HDI value of 0.633.

questions.text: A store is running a 'Buy 4 Get 1 Free' promotion scheme. What is the net discount percentage?
questions.explanation: The customer pays for 4 items and gets 5, so 1 item in 5 is free: 1/5 × 100 = 20%.

questions.text: A train crosses another train running at the same speed in the opposite direction in 5 seconds. If the speed of the first train is doubled and the speed of the second train is halved, then the time taken by the trains to cross is ___________ seconds.
questions.explanation: With both trains at speed v, their combined length is 2v × 5 = 10v. At 2v and v/2 the relative speed is 2.5v, so they cross in 10v ÷ 2.5v = 4 seconds.

questions.text: What is the least value of x so that the 5-digit number 725x3 becomes divisible by 9?
questions.explanation: The digit sum is 7 + 2 + 5 + x + 3 = 17 + x, and the least x that makes it a multiple of 9 is 1 (sum 18).

questions.text: The cash difference between the selling prices of an article at a profit of 5% and 10% is Rs.5. The ratio of the two selling prices is:
questions.explanation: The two selling prices are 105% and 110% of the cost: 105 : 110 = 21 : 22.

questions.text: The average marks of eight students is 7. It was found that marks of one student was taken as 10 instead of 6. Find the correct average.
questions.explanation: The total was 8 × 7 = 56; corrected, it is 56 − 10 + 6 = 52, and 52 ÷ 8 = 6.5.

questions.text: P and Q can complete a work in 8 days, Q and R in 12 days, and R and P in 15 days. How many days will R alone take to complete the work?
questions.explanation: Adding the three pairs, 2(P + Q + R) = 1/8 + 1/12 + 1/15 = 33/120, so P + Q + R do 11/80 of the work a day. R alone does 11/80 − 1/8 = 1/80, so takes 80 days.

questions.text: Anish can do a piece of work in 88 days. Yug can do this work in 66 days. Anish started the work alone. After how many days should Yug join him, so that the work is finished in 44 days?
questions.explanation: Anish works all 44 days and does 44/88 = 1/2 of the work. Yug does the other half in 66/2 = 33 days, so he joins after 44 − 33 = 11 days.

questions.text: A, B and C are three batsmen of a cricket team. Given is the ratio of the runs scored by them in a certain match. A ∶ B = 6 : 7 and B ∶ C = 5 ∶ 6. At the end of the match, A, B and C together scored 856 runs. The number of runs scored by B is:
questions.explanation: Making B 35 in both ratios, A : B : C = 30 : 35 : 42, which adds up to 107. 856 ÷ 107 = 8, so B scored 35 × 8 = 280.

questions.text: Compound interest is charged on a certain sum for 2 years at 10% rate per annum, compounding annually. If the amount becomes ₹605, then the principal (in ₹) is:
In a city, there are 12000 voters. Out of them, 30% voted for A, 25% voted for B and 40% voted for C. Determine the number of voters that did not vote for any of these three participants.
questions.explanation: 30 + 25 + 40 = 95% voted for the three, so 5% of 12000 = 600 did not.

questions.text: After allowing a discount of 10% on its marked price, the value of a washing machine is Rs.28,800. If no discount is allowed, then the shopkeeper gains 25%. The cost price of the washing machine is:
questions.explanation: The marked price is 28,800 ÷ 0.9 = ₹32,000, which is 125% of the cost: 32,000 ÷ 1.25 = ₹25,600.

questions.text: Two trains start at the same time from two stations and proceed toward each other at the speed of 40 km/h and 45 km/h, respectively. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 20 km more than the other. Find the distance between the two stations.
questions.explanation: The faster train covers 45 − 40 = 5 km more every hour, so the 20 km difference builds up in 4 hours. The distance is (40 + 45) × 4 = 340 km.

questions.text: A, B and C invested ₹10,000, ₹15,000 and ₹20,000 respectively. After one year each of A and B invested ₹5,000 more, while C withdrew ₹10,000. What will be the ratio of profit of A, B and C after three years from starting?
The compound interest on ₹10,00,000 at 3% per annum, compounding annually is ₹92,727. The number of years required for this is:
questions.explanation: 1.03³ = 1.092727, so in 3 years ₹10,00,000 grows to ₹10,92,727, which is ₹92,727 of interest.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Diminish
questions.explanation: To 'diminish' is to become smaller or less; its opposite is 'grow'. 'Decline' means much the same as 'diminish'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the capitalised word in the given sentence. We paid her a FLEETING visit before leaving the country.
questions.explanation: 'Fleeting' means lasting a very short time: 'brief'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Be riding high
options: A person who is a pilot
questions.explanation: To 'be riding high' is to be very successful or popular.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Very few animals / was / as faithful as / the dog.
questions.explanation: The subject 'Very few animals' is plural, so the verb must be 'were', not 'was'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A vicious cycle
options: When one problem causes another problem
questions.explanation: A 'vicious cycle' (or vicious circle) is a chain of events in which one problem causes another, which in turn makes the first worse.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. Having a party is a bad idea “because the neighbours are complain”.
options: because the neighbours has been complaining
questions.explanation: 'Are complain' is not a verb form. The complaints would follow the party, so the future 'will complain' fits; 'has been complaining' does not agree with 'neighbours', and the past perfect 'had complained' does not suit the present 'is a bad idea'.

questions.text: Complete the sentence with the most appropriate synonym of the word in brackets. The ________ (glowing) fireflies lit up the field like city lights at night.
questions.explanation: 'Dazzling' means shining brightly, close to 'glowing'. 'Devious', 'furious' and 'gracious' have nothing to do with light.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. History is not only a very vast subject ________ very intriguing.
questions.explanation: 'Not only' is paired with 'but also': 'not only a very vast subject but also very intriguing'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Antagonist
questions.explanation: An 'antagonist' is an opponent: an 'adversary'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Cruel
questions.explanation: 'Cruel' means causing pain without pity; its opposite is 'sympathetic'. 'Unkind' is close in meaning to 'cruel'.

questions.text: The sentence given below has one misspelt word. Spot the INCORRECTLY spelt word and select its correct spelling. There are some venmous snakes which spit and hiss when they are cornered.
questions.explanation: 'Venmous' is misspelt: the word is 'venomous', from 'venom'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He used to ___________ letters to his parents from Bangalore.
questions.explanation: The verb needed is 'write', to put words on paper; 'right', 'rite' and 'wright' sound the same but mean other things.

questions.text: Identify the correctly spelt sentence.
options: Egypt is famous for its pyramid.
Egypt is famous for its piramid.
Egypt is famous for its peryamid.
Egypt is famous for its peramid.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'pyramid'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Rising prices “are causing great concern on Indian economists” at the present moment.
options: are causing a great concern to Indian economists
are causing great concern to Indian economists
are causing a great concern for Indian economists
questions.explanation: Something causes concern 'to' people, not 'on' them, and 'great concern' here takes no article: 'Rising prices are causing great concern to Indian economists'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in the bracket to fill in the blank. She looks like a young Sigourney Weaver and plays the (naïve) ___________heroine well, if a little too credulous for my taste.
questions.explanation: 'Naïve' means innocent and lacking experience of the world; its opposite is 'sophisticated'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A puzzle is a game, challenge, or toy that (1)________ one’s inventiveness or knowledge. The solver of a puzzle is supposed to (2)___________ parts together logically to arrive at the correct or enjoyable solution to the challenge. Crossword puzzles, word-search puzzles, number puzzles, relational puzzles, and logic puzzles are examples of puzzle (3)________. Puzzles are frequently developed for fun purposes, but they may also result from (4)_________ mathematical or logical challenges. In such circumstances, its answer might make an important (5)_________ to mathematical research.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: A puzzle is a challenge: it 'tests' a person's inventiveness or knowledge.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A puzzle is a game, challenge, or toy that (1)________ one’s inventiveness or knowledge. The solver of a puzzle is supposed to (2)___________ parts together logically to arrive at the correct or enjoyable solution to the challenge. Crossword puzzles, word-search puzzles, number puzzles, relational puzzles, and logic puzzles are examples of puzzle (3)________. Puzzles are frequently developed for fun purposes, but they may also result from (4)_________ mathematical or logical challenges. In such circumstances, its answer might make an important (5)_________ to mathematical research.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: The solver has to 'fit' the parts together logically to reach the solution.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A puzzle is a game, challenge, or toy that (1)________ one’s inventiveness or knowledge. The solver of a puzzle is supposed to (2)___________ parts together logically to arrive at the correct or enjoyable solution to the challenge. Crossword puzzles, word-search puzzles, number puzzles, relational puzzles, and logic puzzles are examples of puzzle (3)________. Puzzles are frequently developed for fun purposes, but they may also result from (4)_________ mathematical or logical challenges. In such circumstances, its answer might make an important (5)_________ to mathematical research.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: Crosswords, word-search and logic puzzles are kinds, or 'genres', of puzzle.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A puzzle is a game, challenge, or toy that (1)________ one’s inventiveness or knowledge. The solver of a puzzle is supposed to (2)___________ parts together logically to arrive at the correct or enjoyable solution to the challenge. In such circumstances, its answer might make an important (5)_________ to mathematical research.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: Puzzles may also come from 'significant', that is serious, mathematical or logical problems, which is why an answer can matter to research.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A puzzle is a game, challenge, or toy that (1)________ one’s inventiveness or knowledge. The solver of a puzzle is supposed to (2)___________ parts together logically to arrive at the correct or enjoyable solution to the challenge. Crossword puzzles, word-search puzzles, number puzzles, relational puzzles, and logic puzzles are examples of puzzle (3)________. Puzzles are frequently developed for fun purposes, but they may also result from (4)_________ mathematical or logical challenges. In such circumstances, its answer might make an important (5)_________ to mathematical research.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: To 'make an important addition to' research is to add something of value to it.

questions.text: If ‘+’ means ‘÷’, ‘÷’ means ‘-’, ‘-’ means ‘×’, and ‘×‘ means ‘+’. Which of the following will be the value of the expression? 32 ÷ 64 + 8 - 5 × 36
questions.explanation: After replacing the signs: 32 − 64 ÷ 8 × 5 + 36 = 32 − 40 + 36 = 28.

questions.text: In a certain code language,' Tango is dance' is written as 'de be le', 'dance is practice' is written as 'le be ke' and 'let’s dance' is written as 're le'. How will 'practice' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: 'Dance' is in all three phrases and 'le' in all three codes, so dance = le; 'is' is in the first two, whose other common code word is 'be'. That leaves 'practice' = 'ke'.

questions.text: Six persons H, R, J, S, N and B are sitting in a row facing North. B is not sitting beside J, who is sitting at the extreme right. H is the immediate neighbour of N and B. N is not sitting beside S and J. R is the immediate neighbour of S and J. Who is sitting to the immediate right of B?
questions.explanation: J is at the right end, R next to J and S next to R, as R neighbours both. H sits between N and B, and N cannot sit next to S, so from the left the row is N, H, B, S, R, J. Facing north, S is to B's immediate right.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 7, 21, 25, ?, 131, 917
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 3, ?, 27, 44, 63, 86, 115
Which of the following letters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter series? I, K, O, U, C, ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +2, +4, +6, +8, +10, wrapping round after Z: I → K → O → U → C, and C + 10 = M.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No carrots are beets. Some carrots are gingers. Some gingers are beets. Conclusions: I. All beets are gingers. II. Some gingers are carrots. III. Some beets are carrots.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: 'Some carrots are gingers' converts to 'some gingers are carrots', so II follows. 'No carrots are beets' makes III false, and nothing says every beet is a ginger, so I does not follow.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term. 625 : 35 :: ? : 27 :: 361 : 29
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 18 + 72 ÷ 12 × 36 - 12 = 132
Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? WGVQ, CWHY, ?, OCFO, USRW
questions.explanation: The first letters move +6 (W, C, I, O, U), the second +16 (G, W, M, C, S), the third +12 (V, H, T, F, R) and the fourth +8 (Q, Y, G, O, W), wrapping round after Z: IMTG.

questions.text: In a certain code language INVADE is written as ‘LRYEGI’ and CATER is written as ‘FEWIU’. How will WIRING be written in the same code language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +3 and +4 in turn: INVADE → LRYEGI and CATER → FEWIU. So WIRING → ZMUMQK.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Army : Land :: Navy : ?
questions.explanation: An army fights on land, as a navy fights on water, at sea.

questions.text: Seven people Z, H, B, W, S, R, and G are sitting in a straight row, facing north. Only two people sit to the left of S. Only two people sit to the right of H. Only H sits between G and Z. Only S sits between W and G. B sits at the extreme right of the row. Who sits at the extreme left of the row?
questions.explanation: Numbering the seats 1 to 7 from the left: S is at 3, H at 5 and B at 7. G and Z sit either side of H (4 and 6), and W and G either side of S (2 and 4), so G is at 4, Z at 6 and W at 2. R takes seat 1, the extreme left.

questions.text: ‘A = B’ means ‘A is the son of B’; ‘A * B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A % B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’; ‘A $ B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’; If ‘X $ D = M * N’, then how is M related to X?
questions.explanation: X $ D: X is D's sister. D = M: D is M's son. M * N: M is N's mother. So M is the mother of D and of his sister X.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Train 2 Truck 3 Transport 4 Travel 5 Trade
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Trade (5), Train (1), Transport (3), Travel (4), Truck (2). 'Trad' comes before 'Trai', 'Trai' before 'Tran', 'Tran' before 'Trav', and 'Tra' before 'Tru'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/ number of consonants / vowels in the word) Labourer : Spade :: Sculptor : ?
questions.explanation: A labourer digs with a spade, as a sculptor carves with a chisel.

questions.text: Which of the following is a secondary sector activity?
questions.explanation: Secondary activities turn raw materials into finished goods, as manufacturing does. Mining, forestry and quarrying take resources directly from nature, so they are primary activities.

questions.text: What are Kho-Kho players sitting in the squares called?
questions.explanation: In kho-kho, eight players of the chasing side, the chasers, sit in the squares along the central lane, facing alternate ways; the ninth, the active chaser, runs after the defenders.

questions.text: Which two categories of age group are considered in Khelo India Youth Games?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'Under 17 and Under 21', the two age groups in which the Khelo India Youth Games of 2019 (Pune) and 2020 (Guwahati) were held. The edition held in Haryana in June 2022, the last completed before the exam, had a single under-18 category instead.

questions.text: Kelucharan Mohapatra was related to which classical dance form?
questions.explanation: Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra of Odisha was a leading exponent of Odissi and did much to revive the dance in the 20th century.

questions.text: ______ the then Minister of Agriculture had been a key person in bringing the new agricultural technology to India under Green Revolution
questions.explanation: C. Subramaniam, Union Minister of Food and Agriculture in the mid-1960s, backed the high-yielding seeds and new farm practices of the Green Revolution. M. S. Swaminathan and B. P. Pal were agricultural scientists, not ministers.

questions.text: The council of ministers in a state are appointed on the advice of the ___________.
questions.explanation: Under Article 164(1) the Governor appoints the Chief Minister, and the other ministers on the Chief Minister's advice.

questions.text: GNP stands for ___________.
questions.explanation: GNP is gross national product: GDP, the value of the final goods and services produced within a country in a year, plus net factor income from abroad.

questions.text: Who among the following is related with Mohiniyattam?
questions.explanation: Kanak Rele was a leading Mohiniyattam dancer and scholar who founded the Nalanda Dance Research Centre in Mumbai. Manjit Bawa and Shanti Dave are known as painters and Ratan Thiyam as a theatre director.

questions.text: How is the vegetation affected by construction of large dams?
options: The plants produce nodules to produce nitrogen-fixing bacteria.
Vegetation gives rise to oxygen under aerobic conditions.
The growth of fungus is a lot.
The submerged vegetation rots under anaerobic conditions and gives rise to large amounts of methane, which is also a greenhouse gas.
questions.explanation: The vegetation drowned by a dam's reservoir rots under water without oxygen (anaerobic conditions) and gives off large amounts of methane, a greenhouse gas.

questions.text: Which among the following Union Ministers of India inaugurated the 25th National Conference on e-Governance (NCeG) held in Katra, Jammu & Kashmir in November 2022?
questions.explanation: Dr Jitendra Singh, then Union Minister of State whose charge included Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, inaugurated the 25th NCeG, its silver jubilee edition, at Katra on 26 November 2022.

questions.text: NITI is abbreviation for_________.
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog, the National Institution for Transforming India, replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015.

questions.text: Ghiyasuddin Balban ruled in India in which of the following period?
questions.explanation: Ghiyasuddin Balban ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1266 to 1287.

questions.text: Which project is built for hydel power production and irrigation in the Sutlej river basin?
questions.explanation: The Bhakra Nangal project on the Sutlej, with the Bhakra dam in Himachal Pradesh and the Nangal dam in Punjab, provides hydroelectric power and irrigation. Hirakud is on the Mahanadi, Nagarjuna Sagar on the Krishna and Sardar Sarovar on the Narmada.

questions.text: Which among the following started “Bharat Jodo Yatra” in September 2022?
questions.explanation: Rahul Gandhi of the Indian National Congress set out on the Bharat Jodo Yatra from Kanyakumari on 7 September 2022; it ended in Srinagar on 30 January 2023.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Non-Cooperation-Khilafat Movement began in January ______.
questions.explanation: In NCERT's account the Non-Cooperation-Khilafat Movement began in January 1921, after the Congress adopted the programme of non-cooperation at its Nagpur session in December 1920.

questions.text: When governments legally obliged food producers to add extra nutrients to particular foods or categories of foods it is called ___________ .
questions.explanation: Food fortification is adding micronutrients such as iron, iodine or vitamins to foods; when the law requires it, it is mandatory fortification. Adulteration is debasing food with inferior substances.

questions.text: Which among the following festivals is also celebrated to remember King Mahabali in Kerala?
