questions.explanation: Onam, Kerala's harvest festival, marks the yearly homecoming of the legendary King Mahabali. Vishu is the Malayalam New Year, Ugadi the Telugu and Kannada New Year and Puthandu the Tamil New Year.

questions.text: Fundamental Rights was borrowed from the Constitution of .
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Rights in Part III of the Constitution draw on the Bill of Rights in the Constitution of the United States.

questions.text: Who took over as the new President of India International Centre (IIC) in June 2022?
questions.explanation: Former Foreign Secretary Shyam Saran took over as President of the India International Centre on 23 June 2022, succeeding N. N. Vohra.

questions.text: Which technology is used by doctors to advise his patients sitting at a distance of thousands of kilometers from them?
questions.explanation: Telemedicine uses telecommunication, such as video calls, for doctors to advise and treat patients at a distance.

questions.text: A dealer marks his goods 30% higher than their cost price. In order to sell his goods at a no profit no loss basis, what discount percentage should he allow (correct up to 2 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: On a cost price of 100 the marked price is 130. Selling at cost needs a discount of 30 on 130: 30/130 × 100 = 23.08%.

questions.text: 25 doctors can diagnose 75 patients in 5 hours. If five doctors leave the job, then how many patients can be diagnosed in 6 hours?
questions.explanation: One doctor diagnoses 75/(25 × 5) = 0.6 patients an hour, so 20 doctors in 6 hours diagnose 20 × 6 × 0.6 = 72.

questions.text: How many digits will be there after the decimal point in the product of 0.124 and 1.0204?
questions.explanation: The factors have 3 and 4 decimal places, so the product has 3 + 4 = 7: 124 × 10204 = 1265296 does not end in 0, so 0.1265296 keeps all seven.

questions.text: P can do a piece of work in 15 days, while Q can do it in 10 days. If they work on alternate days beginning with P, in how many days will the work be finished?
questions.explanation: Each two-day cycle does 1/15 + 1/10 = 1/6 of the work, so 10 days finish 5/6. On day 11 P does 1/15, leaving 1/6 − 1/15 = 1/10, which Q finishes on day 12.

questions.text: A cop sees a thief at a distance of 120 m. He starts chasing the thief who is running at a speed of 6 m/sec. The cop is chasing him with a speed of 8 m/sec. Find the distance covered by the thief before the cop catches him.
questions.explanation: The cop gains 8 − 6 = 2 m a second, so he closes the 120 m in 60 seconds. In that time the thief runs 6 × 60 = 360 m.

questions.text: A police officer follows a thief who is at a distance of 800 m from him. If they run at the speeds of 8 km/h and 7 km/h, respectively, what distance (in metre) does the police officer run to catch the thief?
questions.explanation: The officer gains 8 − 7 = 1 km/h, so he closes the 0.8 km in 0.8 hours, running 8 × 0.8 = 6.4 km = 6400 m.

questions.text: The largest distance between any two points on a sphere is 6 units. What is the volume of the sphere?
questions.explanation: The largest distance is the diameter, so r = 3: V = (4/3)π × 3³ = 36π cubic units.

questions.text: The average weight of 10 workers travelling in a boat is increased by 2.8 kg when one of the workers, who weighs 58 kg, is replaced by a new worker. Find the weight of the new worker.
questions.explanation: The total weight rises by 10 × 2.8 = 28 kg, so the new worker weighs 58 + 28 = 86 kg.

questions.text: A year ago, Ram’s income was Rs.20000 per month and expenditure was Rs.16,000 per month. Now if his income is increased by 10% and expenses increased by 15%. What would be the net change in his savings per month?
questions.explanation: Savings were ₹20,000 − ₹16,000 = ₹4,000. Now income is ₹22,000 and expenditure ₹18,400, so savings are ₹3,600: a fall of ₹400.

questions.text: ₹1,20,000 becomes ₹1,50,528 in two years at a certain rate of compound interest, compounding annually in an investment scheme. In the same scheme, the sum of ₹P is invested and it becomes ₹3,51,232 in three years. What is the value of P?

In 2021, in a city 30% of the people were vaccinated by Covid 19 vaccinations in the month of June, 50% of the remaining in July and 20% of the remaining in August. Still 84000 are left for vaccination. Find the total population of the city.(Everyone in the town is eligible for the vaccination)
questions.explanation: After June 70% are left, after July 35% and after August 35% × 0.8 = 28%. 28% of the population is 84,000, so it is 3,00,000, that is 3 lakh.

questions.text: P and Q together can complete a piece of work in 20 days. Q and R together can complete it in 30 days. If P is twice as good a workman as R, then in how many days can Q alone complete it?
questions.explanation: Subtracting the two rates, P − R = 1/20 − 1/30 = 1/60 of the work a day. With P = 2R, R = 1/60 and P = 1/30, so Q = 1/20 − 1/30 = 1/60: Q alone takes 60 days.

questions.text: Calculate the fourth proportional of 6, 10 and 12.

The present population of a town is 95,000. The population increases by 15% in the first year, increases by 20% in the second year and decreases by 12% in the third year. Find the population of the town after three years.
A cloth merchant bought 42 shirts, each at a price of ₹520. He sold each of them for ₹548. Find his percentage profit on each shirt. (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanation: The profit on each shirt is ₹548 − ₹520 = ₹28, and 28/520 × 100 = 5.38%.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in the brackets to fill in the blank and complete the sentence. The best way to motivate someone for their hard work is to __________ (criticise) them for their little accomplishments.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'criticise' is 'praise', which suits motivating someone for their accomplishments. 'Blame' and 'censure' are close to 'criticise'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence. When the owner stopped paying the workers, a lot of them went “rogue”.
questions.explanation: A 'rogue' is a dishonest or lawless person, close to a 'ruffian', a violent, lawless one: unpaid workers who went rogue turned unruly. 'Naughty' is too mild, 'reconnoitre' means to survey and a 'reformer' improves things.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Vacate
questions.explanation: To 'vacate' a place is to leave it: 'depart'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. What does kangaroos / eat? / They are / quite strong.
questions.explanation: 'Kangaroos' is plural, so the auxiliary must be 'do': 'What do kangaroos eat?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. I believe you are “impartial” while making decisions.
questions.explanation: 'Impartial' means not favouring either side: 'fair'. 'Biased' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The advocate who “appeared to the accused” was least hopeful of the case.
questions.explanation: An advocate appears 'for' the party they represent: 'The advocate who appeared for the accused was least hopeful of the case.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Though technology has advanced, environmental problems still have a drastic_________ on mankind.
questions.explanation: Problems have a drastic 'impact', a strong effect, on mankind. 'Result' and 'purpose' do not fit 'have a ... on', and 'assume' is a verb.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks and make the sentence meaningful. She was _______ for the wrong _______ of the past.
questions.explanation: 'Fined' means made to pay a penalty, and 'deeds' are acts: 'She was fined for the wrong deeds of the past.' 'Find' and 'did' are the wrong forms, and 'duds' are things that fail.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom that can be substituted in the following sentence. He is not a great leader but, he has the “gift of gab”.
questions.explanation: To have 'the gift of gab' is to be able to talk easily and persuasively.

questions.text: Select the MISSPELT word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'tolerance', with a 'c'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. The “causes” of war in the country are very pathetic.
questions.explanation: 'Causes' bring something about; the opposite is 'consequences', the results that follow from it. 'Factors' is close to 'causes'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. He has got this notorious reputation of “teasing and making fun of people.”
questions.explanation: To 'pull someone's leg' is to tease them, making fun of them in a joking way.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Pure
questions.explanation: 'Pure' means clean and unspoilt; its opposite is 'tainted', spoilt or contaminated. 'Virtuous' is close to 'pure'.

questions.text: Identify the MISSPELT word in the following sentence. Since there are numerous topics of discusions with varying requirements, specific disciplines and age range require distinct interactive learning strategies.
questions.explanation: 'Discussions' has a double 's' before '-ion'; 'discusions' is misspelt.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. This trailer “gives a sneak peak of the magnum opus” that has been created by the southern film industry.
options: gives a sneak peek of the magnum opus
give a sneak peak of the magnum opus
gives a sneak peak on the magnum opus
questions.explanation: A 'sneak peek' is a quick look in advance; a 'peak' is a summit. The singular 'This trailer' keeps 'gives', and the preview is 'of' the film.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Buck (1)________ over against the sled, (2)_________, sobbing for breath, helpless. This was Spitz’s opportunity. He sprang upon Buck, and twice his teeth sank into his (3)_________ foe and ripped and tore the flesh to the bone. Then Francois’ lash (4)_________, and Buck had the satisfaction of watching Spitz receive the worst whipping as yet (5)_________ to any of the team.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Buck, 'sobbing for breath, helpless', is 'exhausted', worn out. 'Exterminated' means wiped out, and 'excited' and 'eloquent' do not fit a helpless dog.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Buck (1)________ over against the sled, (2)_________, sobbing for breath, helpless. This was Spitz’s opportunity. He sprang upon Buck, and twice his teeth sank into his (3)_________ foe and ripped and tore the flesh to the bone. Then Francois’ lash (4)_________, and Buck had the satisfaction of watching Spitz receive the worst whipping as yet (5)_________ to any of the team.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: An exhausted, helpless Buck cannot fight back: he is an 'unresisting' foe.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Buck (1)________ over against the sled, (2)_________, sobbing for breath, helpless. This was Spitz’s opportunity. He sprang upon Buck, and twice his teeth sank into his (3)_________ foe and ripped and tore the flesh to the bone. Then Francois’ lash (4)_________, and Buck had the satisfaction of watching Spitz receive the worst whipping as yet (5)_________ to any of the team.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Francois' lash 'descended', that is came down, on Spitz as punishment, as the whipping in the next clause shows.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Buck (1)________ over against the sled, (2)_________, sobbing for breath, helpless. This was Spitz’s opportunity. He sprang upon Buck, and twice his teeth sank into his (3)_________ foe and ripped and tore the flesh to the bone. Then Francois’ lash (4)_________, and Buck had the satisfaction of watching Spitz receive the worst whipping as yet (5)_________ to any of the team.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: A whipping is 'administered', that is given as a punishment, to a dog of the team. 'Advertised' and 'automated' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Painter : Brush : : Doctor : ?
questions.explanation: A painter works with a brush, and a doctor with a stethoscope.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. CLARITY : DMBSJUZ :: PRICE : QSJDF :: RAINBOW :?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 1 place forward: CLARITY → DMBSJUZ and PRICE → QSJDF. So RAINBOW → SBJOCPX.

questions.text: Five people are sitting around a circular table facing outwards- L, M, N, O and P. P is sitting to the immediate right of L. M is sitting second right from P. N is the immediate neighbour of P and M. Who is sitting to the immediate left of L?
questions.explanation: Facing outwards, each person's right is the next seat clockwise (seen from above). Clockwise from L: P is on L's right, M is second to P's right, and N, next to both P and M, sits between them, leaving O: L, P, N, M, O. O, the next seat anticlockwise from L, is on L's immediate left.

questions.text: Which of the following term will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? XZVU, UYST, ? , OWMR, LVJQ
questions.explanation: The first letters move 3 places back (X, U, R, O, L), the second 1 back (Z, Y, X, W, V), the third 3 back (V, S, P, M, J) and the fourth 1 back (U, T, S, R, Q). The missing cluster is RXPS.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (5, 9, 450); (7, 12, 840)
questions.explanation: The third number is ten times the product of the first two: 5 × 9 × 10 = 450 and 7 × 12 × 10 = 840. Likewise 6 × 9 × 10 = 540; the other sets would need 960, 770 and 1300.

questions.text: In a code language, 'red ribbon' is coded as 'cu du', 'apple is red' is coded as 'nu mu cu', 'radish is white' is coded as 'mu ku ru', 'eat radish' is coded as 'ru pu'. What is the code for the word 'white'?
questions.explanation: 'Red' is the word common to the first two phrases and 'cu' their common code, so red = cu; likewise is = mu (second and third) and radish = ru (third and fourth). In 'radish is white' = 'mu ku ru', that leaves white = ku.

questions.text: K, L, M, N, S, and P are 6 friends sitting around a circular table facing the centre. P is third to the left of S. K is to the immediate left of S. K and L are sitting opposite each other. M is sitting to the immediate right of S. Who is sitting opposite M?
questions.explanation: In a ring of six, the seat third to S's left is the one opposite S, so P faces S. K is on S's immediate left and L opposite K; M is on S's immediate right. N takes the last seat, between K and P, which is opposite M.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? USRP, OMLJ , IGFD , CAZX ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 6 places back from one cluster to the next, wrapping round after A: U, O, I, C, W; S, M, G, A, U; R, L, F, Z, T; P, J, D, X, R. The next cluster is WUTR.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 77, 77, 79, 237, 241, ?
In the following equation, which mathematical operations when sequentially placed will make the equation true? 20*4*8*10*5
questions.explanation: 20 ÷ 4 × 8 < 10 × 5, as 5 × 8 = 40 is less than 50. The other options give 5 + 8 = 13 = 50, 40 > 50 and 80 ÷ 8 = 10 > 50, all false.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 45, 76, ?, 168, 229

A @ B means ‘A is the sister of B’. A & B means ‘A is the brother of B’. A # B means ‘A is the wife of B’. A ^ B means ‘A is the mother of B’. A + B means ‘A is the father of B’. If A & C + E ^ G # I & K + M @ O, then which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: C is the maternal grandfather of G.
O is the daughter of K.
M is the daughter of K.
K is the father of O.
questions.explanation: A is C's brother, C is E's father, E is G's mother, G is I's wife, I is K's brother, K is M's father and M is O's sister. M, a sister, is K's daughter, and O, M's sibling, is K's child, so K is O's father; but O's sex is not given, so 'O is the daughter of K' cannot be said to be correct. C, the father of G's mother, is G's maternal grandfather.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 heated 2 healed 3 heaped 4 hedge 5 helmet
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: healed (2), heaped (3), heated (1), hedge (4), helmet (5). The three 'hea' words differ at the fourth letter, 'l' before 'p' before 't', and 'hea' comes before 'hed' and 'hel'.

questions.text: In a certain code language,‘HAUNT’ is written as ‘KVXIW’ and ‘BURNT’ is written as ‘EPUIW’. How will ‘THROW’ be written in the same code language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +3 and −5 in turn: HAUNT → KVXIW and BURNT → EPUIW. So THROW → W C U J Z: WCUJZ.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 49 + 16 ÷ 7 - 36 × 16 = 92
questions.explanation: After interchanging × and +: 49 × 16 ÷ 7 − 36 + 16 = 112 − 36 + 16 = 92.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All books are plastic. Some plastic are cups. All cups are glass. Conclusions: I. Some plastic are books. II. All plastic are cups. III. Some cups are glass.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions II and III follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.
questions.explanation: All books are plastic, so some plastic are books (I). All cups are glass, so some cups are glass (III). 'Some plastic are cups' does not make all plastic cups, so II does not follow.

questions.text: The Parliamentary form of government is also referred to as the ________ model.
questions.explanation: India's parliamentary system follows the Westminster model, named after the seat of the British Parliament, in which the executive is drawn from the legislature and answerable to it.

questions.text: Which is the smallest union territory of India area-wise?
options: Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
questions.explanation: Lakshadweep, a group of islands in the Arabian Sea with about 32 sq km of land, is the smallest union territory by area.

questions.text: Various Industrialists came together in 1944 and drafted a joint proposal for setting up a planned economy in India. It is famously known as the ___________ Plan.
questions.explanation: The Bombay Plan of 1944, drawn up by industrialists including J.R.D. Tata and G.D. Birla, proposed a planned economy with a large role for the state.

questions.text: People involved in ______ sector, process the primary materials and convert them into finished goods.
questions.explanation: The secondary sector turns raw materials from the primary sector into finished goods, as in manufacturing.

questions.text: The Pey Jal Survekshan under ________ was launched by Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs in September, 2022.
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs launched the Pey Jal Survekshan in September 2022 under AMRUT 2.0 (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation), to survey water supply, used-water management and water bodies in the mission's cities.

questions.text: Gangaur Festival is celebrated in honour of the Goddess ________ mostly by the womenfolk of Rajasthan.
questions.explanation: Gangaur honours Gauri, a form of Parvati, whom the women of Rajasthan worship for marital happiness.

questions.text: Nalanda University was established by __________ in the 5th century.
questions.explanation: Kumaragupta I of the Gupta dynasty founded the monastic university at Nalanda, in Bihar, in the 5th century.

questions.text: The host and winner state for the Khelo India Youth Games 2020 edition is ________ .
questions.explanation: Guwahati, Assam, hosted the third Khelo India Youth Games in January 2020, and Maharashtra topped the medal table with 78 golds and 256 medals.

questions.text: El Nino is a phenomenon in which a warm ocean current that flows past the ______ coast, in place of the cold current, every 2 to 5 years.
questions.explanation: In an El Nino year a warm current replaces the cold Peru (Humboldt) current off the coast of Peru, changing the weather far across the Pacific.

questions.text: A _______________ is a group of people who come together to contest elections and hold power in the government.
questions.explanation: A political party is a group of people who come together to contest elections and hold power in the government, on agreed policies and programmes.

questions.text: The recently released book “Madam Sir” narrates the story of which of the following woman IPS officers?
questions.explanation: 'Madam Sir' (2022) is the memoir of Manjari Jaruhar, a 1976-batch IPS officer and Bihar's first woman IPS officer.

questions.text: In India, which programme provides food grains and other essential commodities at subsidised prices in rural and urban areas?
questions.explanation: Under the Public Distribution System the government sells food grains and other essentials at subsidised prices through ration (fair price) shops.

questions.text: As of November 2022, who among the following is the Administrator of Lakshadweep, India?
questions.explanation: Praful Khoda Patel was the Administrator of Lakshadweep in November 2022, a post he had held since December 2020 alongside that of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu.

questions.text: Loans create _____, as they have to be returned to the lender in a certain period of time.
questions.explanation: A loan is a debt that the borrower must repay, usually with interest, so it is a liability; assets are what a person or firm owns.

questions.text: Who among the following received the Parishad Samman by the Delhi government?
questions.explanation: The Kathak dancer Shovana Narayan has received the Parishad Samman, which the Sahitya Kala Parishad, the Delhi government's cultural wing, gives to eminent Delhi-based artists.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following was the main argument put forward by the British for the partition of Bengal in 1905?
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon's government said Bengal was too large to govern well, so the partition was presented as an administrative convenience; nationalists saw it as a way to divide Hindus and Muslims and weaken the movement in Bengal.

questions.text: Which gas is released on burning of natural gas?
questions.explanation: Natural gas is mostly methane, which burns in oxygen to give carbon dioxide and water: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O.

questions.text: Janaki Prasad is associated with which Gharana of Kathak?
questions.explanation: Janaki Prasad founded the Banaras gharana of Kathak, known for its natwari (dance) syllables, with little use of tabla or pakhawaj bols.

questions.text: What comes at the top of the food guide pyramid?
questions.explanation: Fats, oils and sugars form the small tip of the food guide pyramid, to be eaten sparingly; grains form its wide base.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
questions.explanation: The 2010 Winter Olympics were held in Vancouver, Canada; London hosted the 2012 Summer Olympics. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.text: If 17% of 630 = 35% of x, then what is the value of x?
A bought a number of mangoes at 2 for ₹5 and an equal number at 3 for ₹5. To make a profit of 20% she should sell a dozen for:
questions.explanation: Buying 6 of each costs 6 × 5/2 + 6 × 5/3 = 15 + 10 = ₹25 for a dozen. A 20% profit means selling a dozen for 25 × 1.2 = ₹30.

questions.text: The ratio of the third proportional of P and Q and the fourth proportional of P, Q and R is 5 : 6, then Q : R is:
questions.explanation: The third proportional of P and Q is Q²/P and the fourth proportional of P, Q and R is QR/P. Their ratio, Q²/P : QR/P, is Q : R, so Q : R = 5 : 6.

questions.text: By selling a refrigerator for Rs.28,448, a shopkeeper makes a profit of 12%. If the profit is reduced to 8%, what is the new selling price of the refrigerator?
questions.explanation: The cost price is 28,448 ÷ 1.12 = ₹25,400. At 8% profit the price is 25,400 × 1.08 = ₹27,432.

questions.text: Height of a plant increases at the rate of 2% per annum. If its present height is 1.2 m, then what wil be the height of plant after three years ?
questions.explanation: After three years of 2% growth: 1.2 × 1.02³ = 1.2 × 1.061208 = 1.27345 m, or 1.273 m to three decimal places.

questions.text: Two trains start at the same time from Mumbai and Delhi, and proceed towards each other at the speeds of 15 km/h and 26 km/h respectively. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 99 km more than the other. The distance between the two stations is:
questions.explanation: The faster train covers 26 − 15 = 11 km more every hour, so a 99 km difference means they met after 9 hours. Together they covered (15 + 26) × 9 = 369 km.

questions.text: Find the square of Z. Z is the remainder when the smallest 4-digit number exactly divisible by 24 and 36 is divided by 40.
questions.explanation: The LCM of 24 and 36 is 72, and the smallest 4-digit multiple of 72 is 72 × 14 = 1008. 1008 = 40 × 25 + 8, so Z = 8 and Z² = 64.

questions.text: Two numbers P and Q are such that the sum of 10% of P and 5% of Q is one-fourth of the sum of 15% of P and 25% of Q. Find the ratio of P to Q.
Find the third proportional of 5 and 11.
questions.explanation: The third proportional of a and b is b²/a: 11² ÷ 5 = 121 ÷ 5 = 24.2.

questions.text: A can do a piece of work in 40 days and B can do the same work in 80 days. They work together for 20 days, how much of the work is left to complete?
questions.explanation: Together they do 1/40 + 1/80 = 3/80 of the work a day, so in 20 days they do 60/80 = 3/4 of it, and 1/4 is left.

questions.text: How many prime numbers exist between 50 and 80?
questions.explanation: The primes between 50 and 80 are 53, 59, 61, 67, 71, 73 and 79: seven.

questions.text: In a circular race of 500 m length, A and B start with speeds of 4 m/sec and 5 m/sec, respectively, at the same time from the same point. After how much time will they meet for the first time at the starting point while running in the same direction?
questions.explanation: A completes a lap every 500 ÷ 4 = 125 seconds and B every 500 ÷ 5 = 100 seconds. Both are at the start together after the LCM of 125 and 100, 500 seconds.

questions.text: Find the difference between the average of the cube of first 5 natural numbers and the average of the square of first 5 natural numbers.
Pawan bought a pair of jeans from the store when they were giving a 20 percent discount. If the regular price of the pair of jeans was Rs. 1800, then how much did Pawan pay with the discount?
Marked price of a table is listed at Rs.1,880. If it’s sold at a discount 15%, then what is the selling price of the table?
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Gratitude
questions.explanation: 'Gratitude' is thankfulness; its opposite is 'thanklessness' (ingratitude). 'Appreciation' is close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank. He is a good soul. Although the _________ of his shoe is worn out, he never asks anyone to help him with money.
questions.explanation: The 'sole' is the underside of a shoe; it sounds like 'soul', used earlier in the sentence. 'Soil' is earth and a 'seal' a stamp or fastening.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Don’t sit on this bench as “it is just painted”.
questions.explanation: A just-finished action with a present result takes the present perfect, with 'just' after 'has', and the bench is acted on, so the passive: 'as it has just been painted.'

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'manipulate'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Better the devil you know than the devil you don’t.
options: Do not trust unknown and known devils.
Being good is better with evil people.
Being cruel is better with known people.
It is easier to be in a known bad situation than being in an unknown worse situation.
questions.explanation: The proverb means it is wiser to put up with a familiar difficulty than to risk an unknown one that may be worse.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Will-o-the-wisp
questions.explanation: A will-o'-the-wisp, the flickering marsh light that seems to lead travellers on but can never be reached, is a hope or goal that cannot be attained.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. As I review the events of my past life, I realise how________ are the influences that shape our destinies.
questions.explanation: 'Subtle' means delicate and hard to notice: only on looking back does one see the influences at work. 'Artless' means simple and 'crude' rough, and 'trumpet' is not an adjective.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The monitor of “the class don't know” the answer.
questions.explanation: The subject, 'the monitor', is singular, so the present tense takes 'doesn't know'; 'knew' cannot follow 'don't', 'doesn't' or 'didn't'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The operation is to be distinguished from other forms of heart surgery and, in particular, from the repair of openings between the _______.
questions.explanation: The auricles (atria) are the two upper chambers of the heart, and an opening between them is a defect that surgeons repair. 'Oracles', 'oculus' and 'oracle' have nothing to do with the heart.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Presumable
questions.explanation: 'Presumable' means likely, reasonable to suppose; its opposite is 'improbable'. 'Reasonable' and 'credible' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Confuse
questions.explanation: To 'confuse' someone is to 'puzzle' or bewilder them. 'Compose' means to calm or to create.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Deficient
questions.explanation: 'Deficient' means lacking, not enough: 'insufficient'. 'Sufficient' and 'abundant' are its opposites.

questions.text: The sentence below is divided into four segments. Select the option that has an error of tense. I think India will win the 20-20 cricket match.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: 'I think' states a present opinion, and the future event it is about takes 'will win'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Scanty
questions.explanation: 'Scanty' means too little; its opposite is 'abundant', more than enough. 'Meagre' is a synonym.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. If you (1) __________ yourself with the good and righteous, they can only (2) _________ you up. If you (3) ___________ yourself with the others, they will (4) _______ you down into the doldrums of mediocrity, and they will keep you there, but only as long as you (5)_________ it.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: To 'surround yourself with' people is to keep their company, which the parallel 'If you ... yourself with the others' repeats.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. If you (1) __________ yourself with the good and righteous, they can only (2) _________ you up. If you (3) ___________ yourself with the others, they will (4) _______ you down into the doldrums of mediocrity, and they will keep you there, but only as long as you (5)_________ it.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Good people can only 'raise you up', the opposite of the 'drag you down' that follows.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. If you (1) __________ yourself with the good and righteous, they can only (2) _________ you up. If you (3) ___________ yourself with the others, they will (4) _______ you down into the doldrums of mediocrity, and they will keep you there, but only as long as you (5)_________ it.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Encircle yourself with' repeats the sense of 'surround yourself with' from the first sentence, now with 'the others'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. If you (1) __________ yourself with the good and righteous, they can only (2) _________ you up. If you (3) ___________ yourself with the others, they will (4) _______ you down into the doldrums of mediocrity, and they will keep you there, but only as long as you (5)_________ it.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: To 'drag' someone down is to pull them to a lower level, here into 'the doldrums of mediocrity'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. If you (1) __________ yourself with the good and righteous, they can only (2) _________ you up. If you (3) ___________ yourself with the others, they will (4) _______ you down into the doldrums of mediocrity, and they will keep you there, but only as long as you (5)_________ it.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: They keep you there only as long as you 'permit', or allow, it.

questions.text: If A denotes +, B denotes −, and C denotes ×, then what will be the value of the following equation? 20 C 5 A 3 C 2 B 16

Six friends Sarthi, Pari, Vani, Kabir, Arshi, and Kamal,are sitting in a circle. All of them are facing the centre.Sarthi sits second to the left of Pari. Vani sits third to the right of Kabir. Arshi is an immediate neighbour of Pari and Kabir. Who sits fourth to the left of Vani?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, each person's left runs clockwise. Arshi sits between Pari and Kabir, and Vani, third to the right of Kabir, sits opposite him; Sarthi, second to the left of Pari, then fits only if the clockwise order is Kabir, Arshi, Pari, Vani, Sarthi, Kamal. Counting four to the left of Vani: Sarthi, Kamal, Kabir, Arshi.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? FSCW, HQEU, JOGS, LMIQ, ?
questions.explanation: In each cluster the first and third letters move 2 forward and the second and fourth 2 back: F, H, J, L, N; S, Q, O, M, K; C, E, G, I, K; W, U, S, Q, O. The next term is NKKO.

questions.text: O,P,Q,R and S are sitting on a circular table facing towards the centre. R is sitting to the immediate left of S. Q is sitting to the immediate right of O. S is the immediate neighbour of R and O. P is sitting to the immediate left of R. Who is sitting to the immediate right of Q?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, each person's left runs clockwise. Clockwise the order is S, R, P, Q, O: R is to S's left, P to R's left, S between R and O, and Q to O's right. The person to Q's immediate right is P.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. REALITY : YEALITR :: SCIENCE : ECIENCS :: ADVERSE : ?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters change places: REALITY → YEALITR and SCIENCE → ECIENCS. So ADVERSE → EDVERSA.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 96, 48, 60, 30, 42, 21, ?
questions.explanation: The terms are halved and increased by 12 in turn: 96 ÷ 2 = 48, 48 + 12 = 60, 60 ÷ 2 = 30, 30 + 12 = 42, 42 ÷ 2 = 21, and 21 + 12 = 33.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 12, 23, 45, 56, 78, 89, 111, 122, ?
questions.explanation: The differences alternate +11 and +22: 12, 23, 45, 56, 78, 89, 111, 122, and then 122 + 22 = 144.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. GLOW: SOMF :: LIKE: NRQX :: SAVE: ?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on) and the four letters are then moved −1, 0, +1 and +2: GLOW → TOLD → SOMF and LIKE → ORPV → NRQX. So SAVE → HZEV → GZFX.

questions.text: In a certain code language, STAR is coded as 58, and ALARM is coded as 45. How will STAGE be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded as the sum of its letters' places in the alphabet: STAR = 19 + 20 + 1 + 18 = 58 and ALARM = 1 + 12 + 1 + 18 + 13 = 45. So STAGE = 19 + 20 + 1 + 7 + 5 = 52.

questions.text: A @ B means ‘A is the sister of B’. A & B means ‘A is the brother of B’. A # B means ‘A is the wife of B’. A ^ B means ‘A is the mother of B’. A + B means ‘A is the father of B’. If A & C + E ^ G # I & K + M @ O, then which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: K is the father of O.
I is the son of E.
M is the daughter of K.
C is the maternal grandfather of G.
questions.explanation: A is C's brother, C is E's father, E is G's mother, G is I's wife, I is K's brother, K is M's father and M is O's sister. E is I's mother-in-law, not his mother, so 'I is the son of E' is not correct; K is O's father, M is K's daughter and C, E's father, is G's maternal grandfather.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? ADLU, EGOO, ? , OMUE, UPXA
questions.explanation: The first letters are the vowels A, E, I, O, U in order and the fourth letters the same vowels backwards; the second letters move 3 forward (D, G, J, M, P) and so do the third (L, O, R, U, X). The missing term is IJRI.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed) (9, 14, 161); (12, 18, 210)
questions.explanation: The third number is 7 times the sum of the other two: (9 + 14) × 7 = 161 and (12 + 18) × 7 = 210. Likewise (29 + 17) × 7 = 322; the other sets would need 441, 420 and 308.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1. TOPOLOGY 2. TOPIC 3. TOPAZ 4. TOUR 5. TORTILLA 6. TORN
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: topaz (3), topic (2), topology (1), torn (6), tortilla (5), tour (4). 'Topa' comes before 'topi' and 'topo', 'top' before 'tor' and 'tou', and 'torn' before 'tort'.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: All bangles are coins. All coins are anklets. All anklets are lockets. Conclusions: I. All lockets are bangles. II. Some lockets are coins.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: Bangles lie inside coins, coins inside anklets and anklets inside lockets, so all coins are lockets and some lockets are coins (II). Lockets need not all be bangles, so I does not follow.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 104 ÷ 13 + 60 - 5 × 2 = 115
questions.explanation: After interchanging ÷ and −: 104 − 13 + 60 ÷ 5 × 2 = 104 − 13 + 24 = 115.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘ENTITY’ is written as ‘UOFAVK’ and 'EQUITY' is written as 'VRFAVK'. How will ‘ESCAPE’ be written as in that language?
questions.explanation: Each half of the word is reversed, and then the letters of the first half move 1 forward and those of the second half 2 forward: ENT ITY → TNE YTI → UOF AVK and EQU ITY → UQE YTI → VRF AVK. So ESC APE → CSE EPA → DTF GRC: DTFGRC.

questions.text: What was the targeted economic growth rate as per the Sixth Five year plan?
questions.explanation: The Sixth Five Year Plan (1980-85) aimed at a growth rate of 5.2% a year in gross national product.

questions.text: What is the minimum age of a candidate to become the president of India?
questions.explanation: Under Article 58 a candidate for President must be a citizen of India, have completed 35 years of age and be qualified for election to the Lok Sabha.

questions.text: Public debt is burdensome if it ___________ future growth in output.
questions.explanation: Interest and repayment come out of future taxes, which cut people's disposable income, and government borrowing draws on savings that could have gone into private investment. To the extent that this lowers capital formation and so future growth in output, the debt is a burden on future generations.

questions.text: Who became the youngest speaker in the history of the Maharashtra State Assembly in July 2022?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Rahul Narwekar of the BJP, elected Speaker of the Maharashtra Legislative Assembly on 3 July 2022. Some reports then called him the youngest to hold the post; others call him the second-youngest, after Shivraj Patil, who was elected to it at 42. Either way he is the only option who became Speaker in July 2022.

questions.text: In which of the following climates you cannot grow a rubber crop?
questions.explanation: Rubber grows best in hot, wet equatorial lands and, where conditions allow, in tropical and sub-tropical areas too; it needs heavy rain and high temperatures, which polar regions lack.

questions.text: Who became the Member of Legislative Assembly from Andheri East constituency in Maharashtra, India in November 2022?
questions.explanation: Rutuja Latke of the Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) won the Andheri East by-election of 3 November 2022, held after the death of her husband, the sitting MLA Ramesh Latke; the result was declared on 6 November.

questions.text: Which is the second most populated state of India as per the Census 2011?
questions.explanation: By the 2011 Census Maharashtra, with about 11.2 crore people, is the second most populous state after Uttar Pradesh (about 20 crore); Bihar is third.

questions.text: Given among the following,______is a food crop
questions.explanation: Rice is a food crop, grown to be eaten. Jute and cotton are fibre crops, and rubber is a plantation crop grown for its latex.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Resolution of Non-Cooperation movement was confirmed in the annual session of the Indian National Congress at ___________ in December 1920.
questions.explanation: A special session at Calcutta in September 1920 adopted the Non-Cooperation programme, and the annual session at Nagpur in December 1920 confirmed it.

questions.text: Which of the following dancer won a Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2004?
questions.explanation: Jatin Goswami, a Sattriya dancer and guru from Assam, received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Sattriya dance in 2004.

questions.text: The Sattriya dance, one of the classical dances of India depicts the teachings of which of the following religions?
questions.explanation: Sattriya, created by the saint Srimanta Sankardeva in Assam and kept alive in the Vaishnava monasteries called sattras, presents the teachings of Vaishnavism, a tradition of Hinduism.

questions.text: Karaga, one of the oldest festivals of ____________, is celebrated in honour of Goddess Shakti.
questions.explanation: The Bengaluru Karaga, held at the Dharmaraya Swamy temple at the Chaitra full moon, is one of the city's oldest festivals; the Thigala community celebrates it in honour of Draupadi, worshipped as a form of Shakti.

questions.text: What obstructs the South-West monsoon winds which come from the Arabian Sea while flowing towards the Intertropical Convergence Zone?
questions.explanation: The Arabian Sea branch of the south-west monsoon strikes the Western Ghats, which force the winds to rise and bring heavy rain to their windward, western slopes.

questions.text: Which is the largest Democracy in the world?
questions.explanation: India, which has the largest electorate of any country, is the world's largest democracy. China is a one-party state, and the USA and Brazil have far fewer voters.

questions.text: The Satavahana kingdom was established about how many years ago?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 2100, following the school account in which the Satavahanas became powerful in western India about 200 years after the Cholas, Cheras and Pandyas rose in the south around 2300 years ago. Historians date the dynasty's beginnings anywhere from the third to the first century BCE.

questions.text: The 35th National Games of India were held in which year?
questions.explanation: The 35th National Games were held in Kerala from 31 January to 14 February 2015.

questions.text: Saikhom Mirabai Chanu is an _______________.
questions.explanation: Saikhom Mirabai Chanu of Manipur is a weightlifter; she won silver in the women's 49 kg at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.

questions.text: Chemical formula for the marble is ______.
questions.explanation: Marble is metamorphosed limestone, made of calcium carbonate, CaCO₃. CaO is quicklime, Ca(OH)₂ slaked lime and CO₂ carbon dioxide.

questions.text: ______is the fluid content inside the plasma membrane.
questions.explanation: The cytoplasm is the fluid within the plasma membrane in which the cell's organelles lie; mitochondria are organelles, and chromatin lies within the nucleus.

questions.text: _______________intends to provide skill development and placement oriented training across the entire textile value chain, excluding Spinning and Weaving in the organized sector.
options: MPLADS (Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme)
questions.explanation: Samarth, the Ministry of Textiles' Scheme for Capacity Building in Textile Sector approved in 2017, offers demand-driven, placement-oriented skilling across the textile value chain except spinning and weaving in the organised sector.

questions.text: In a certain rectangle, the ratio of length to width of the rectangle is 3 : 2 and the area is 150 cm². The perimeter of the rectangle is:
questions.explanation: With length 3k and width 2k, 6k² = 150, so k = 5: the sides are 15 cm and 10 cm and the perimeter is 2 × (15 + 10) = 50 cm.

questions.text: If A is the average of first 5 natural numbers and B is the average of first 5 natural numbers which are perfect squares, then what is the average of A and B?
20 men can finish a piece of work in 5 days, whereas it takes 24 women to finish it in 5 days. If 30 men and 12 women undertake to complete the work, how many days will they take to complete it?
questions.explanation: The work is 20 × 5 = 100 man-days or 24 × 5 = 120 woman-days, so a man does 1/100 and a woman 1/120 of it a day. Together 30/100 + 12/120 = 0.3 + 0.1 = 0.4 of the work a day, so 1 ÷ 0.4 = 2.5 days.

questions.text: The diameter and height of a cylindrical tower are 10 m and 21m, respectively. What will be the cost of painting its curved surface, at the rate of Rs.8 per m²? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Curved surface = 2πrh = 2 × 22/7 × 5 × 21 = 660 m², so the cost is 660 × 8 = ₹5,280.

questions.text: The Rajdhani train travels in a straight line at a constant speed of 75 km/h for a particular distance ‘d’ and then travels another distance equal to ‘2d’ at a constant speed of 100 km/h in the same direction as earlier. Find the average speed of the train during the whole journey?
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 3d ÷ (d/75 + 2d/100) = 3 ÷ (1/75 + 1/50) = 3 ÷ (5/150) = 90 km/h.

questions.text: In a school, the ratio of boys to girls is 7 : 11. If there are 3420 students in the school, then how many girls are there in the school? (There are only boys and girls in the school.)
questions.explanation: Girls are 11 of every 18 students: 3420 × 11/18 = 190 × 11 = 2090.

questions.text: Applied to a bill for Rs. 10000 the difference between a discount of 30 percent and two successive discounts of 22 percent and 8 percent is:
questions.explanation: A single 30% discount leaves ₹7,000. Discounts of 22% and 8% leave 10,000 × 0.78 × 0.92 = ₹7,176. The difference is ₹176.

questions.text: The greatest number, by which when the numbers 1658 and 2038 are divided, the remainders are 7 and 6, respectively, is:
questions.explanation: The number must divide 1658 − 7 = 1651 and 2038 − 6 = 2032 exactly, so it is their HCF: 1651 = 127 × 13 and 2032 = 127 × 16, and 13 and 16 have no common factor, so the HCF is 127.

questions.text: A trader mixes 26 kg of raw salt which costs Rs.2 per kg with 30 kg of raw salt which costs Rs.3.60 per kg. If he sells the mixture for Rs.3 per kg, find his gain%.

A, B, and C can complete a work in 4 days, 8 days, and 16 days respectively. If all three work on alternate days such that A works on first day, B works on second day, C works on third day and A works on fourth day and so on, then find the number of days in which 175% of the work is done.
questions.explanation: A does 1/4, B 1/8 and C 1/16 of the work a day, so each 3-day round does 4/16 + 2/16 + 1/16 = 7/16. 175% of the work is 7/4 = 28/16, exactly four rounds: 12 days.

questions.text: Two successive price increases of 5% and 5% of an article are equivalent to a single price increase of:
In which ratio a trader must mix two quantities of ₹18 per kg and ₹27 per kg, so that the price of the mixture becomes ₹25 per kg?
questions.explanation: By alligation, the ₹18 and ₹27 kinds are mixed in the ratio (27 − 25) : (25 − 18) = 2 : 7.

questions.text: A man purchased 25 litres of milk at the cost price of Rs.25 per litre. Now he added 5 litres of water to it and sold the mixture at the cost price. Find the profit percentage for the man.
questions.explanation: He pays 25 × 25 = ₹625 and sells 30 litres at ₹25: ₹750. Profit = 125/625 × 100 = 20%.

questions.text: A discount of 20% on one article is the same as a discount of 25% on another article. The marked price of article can be?
questions.explanation: 20% of the first marked price equals 25% of the second, so the prices are in the ratio 25 : 20 = 5 : 4. Of the options only ₹100 and ₹80 are in that ratio: 20% of 100 = 25% of 80 = 20.

questions.text: Which number is one less than the sum of all the prime factors of 2310?

Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. “Nalini was not satisfy with her birthday dress”, but she wore it anyway.
options: Nalini was not satisfied for her birthday dress
Nalini was not satisfied with her birthday dress
Nalini were not satisfied by her birthday dress
questions.explanation: After 'was' the verb must be the past participle 'satisfied', and one is satisfied 'with' something: 'Nalini was not satisfied with her birthday dress'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Abolish
questions.explanation: To 'abolish' is to put an end to a law, system or practice; its exact opposite, 'establish', is not offered, and 'construct', to build or set up, comes nearest. 'Eradicate' is close to 'abolish' in meaning, and 'reverberate' (echo) and 'pontificate' (speak pompously) are unrelated.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Experiences lead you towards the most fascinating “stage of your living” that you will cherish forever.
questions.explanation: 'Stage of your living' is not idiomatic; 'part of your life' is the natural phrase for something one will cherish forever.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Sam shall went to / the office tomorrow to / get back his original documents / lying with the staff.
questions.explanation: A modal such as 'shall' takes the base form of the verb: 'Sam shall go to', not 'shall went'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. White elephant
options: Something that costs a lot of money but has no useful purpose
A big lie that is concealed from all
questions.explanation: A 'white elephant' is a possession that costs a great deal to keep but is of no real use.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word to fill in the blank in the sentence. Deceive; My mother said, “Don’t ________ yourself, Adi. Pay attention to your studies.”
questions.explanation: To 'deceive' is to trick or mislead: 'Don't trick yourself' means don't fool yourself.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Worthless
questions.explanation: 'Worthless' means having no value or use; its exact opposites ('valuable', 'useful') are not offered, and 'productive', yielding useful results, comes nearest. 'Ineffective' is close to 'worthless', and 'insult' and 'kind' are unrelated.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The captain “feels very proudly” as his team has won the match.
questions.explanation: 'Feel' is a linking verb, so it takes an adjective, not an adverb, and 'feels' agrees with the singular subject: 'The captain feels very proud'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank. There was a big hole in the wall which they are trying to close. It took a ___________ day for them to do the job.
questions.explanation: 'Whole', meaning entire, sounds like 'hole' but differs in spelling and meaning: 'It took a whole day'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. The novelist depicted the moral “decay” of the society through his novels.
questions.explanation: Moral 'decay' is a decline in standards: 'degeneration'. 'Integrity' is nearly its opposite, and 'conviction' and 'indignation' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Culpable
questions.explanation: 'Culpable' means deserving blame: 'guilty'. 'Absolved', 'vindicated' and 'acquitted' all mean cleared of blame.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Mandatory
questions.explanation: 'Mandatory' means required by rule; its opposite is 'optional'. 'Imperative', 'requisite' and 'unavoidable' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Identify the correctly spelt sentence.
options: Scientists are looking for alternative energy to save non-renewable resources.
Scientists are looking for alternative energy to save non-reneable resources.
Scientists are looking for allternative energy to save non-renewable resources.
Scientists are looking for alternetive energy to save non-renewable resources.
questions.explanation: The words are spelt 'alternative' and 'non-renewable'; the other sentences have 'non-reneable', 'allternative' and 'alternetive'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Like oil and water
options: Two people who like each other
Two people who are different from each other
Two people who are similar to each other
Two people who like to work with each other
questions.explanation: People who are 'like oil and water' are so different that they do not mix or get along.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Ockupation' is misspelt: the word is 'occupation', with 'cc'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Amidst all the chaos and suffering caused by the pandemic, there are some positive stories of grit, (1)__________ and bravado. Some businesses understood the needs of the times to make (2)________profits. Businesses diversified and (3)________successful. Although there are numerous stories of people and business owners (4)__________ due to lockdowns, this small percentage of success stories is like the light at the end of the (5)___________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The positive stories are of grit, 'persistence' (keeping on despite difficulty) and bravado, qualities that go together.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Amidst all the chaos and suffering caused by the pandemic, there are some positive stories of grit, (1)__________ and bravado. Some businesses understood the needs of the times to make (2)________profits. Businesses diversified and (3)________successful. Although there are numerous stories of people and business owners (4)__________ due to lockdowns, this small percentage of success stories is like the light at the end of the (5)___________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Businesses that understood the needs of the times made 'huge' profits, in keeping with the success stories.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Amidst all the chaos and suffering caused by the pandemic, there are some positive stories of grit, (1)__________ and bravado. Some businesses understood the needs of the times to make (2)________profits. Businesses diversified and (3)________successful. Although there are numerous stories of people and business owners (4)__________ due to lockdowns, this small percentage of success stories is like the light at the end of the (5)___________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The passage is in the past tense ('understood', 'diversified'), so the businesses 'were' successful.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Amidst all the chaos and suffering caused by the pandemic, there are some positive stories of grit, (1)__________ and bravado. Some businesses understood the needs of the times to make (2)________profits. Businesses diversified and (3)________successful. Although there are numerous stories of people and business owners (4)__________ due to lockdowns, this small percentage of success stories is like the light at the end of the (5)___________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Set against the few success stories are the many of people and businesses 'suffering' due to lockdowns.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Amidst all the chaos and suffering caused by the pandemic, there are some positive stories of grit, (1)__________ and bravado. Some businesses understood the needs of the times to make (2)________profits. Businesses diversified and (3)________successful. Although there are numerous stories of people and business owners (4)__________ due to lockdowns, this small percentage of success stories is like the light at the end of the (5)___________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'The light at the end of the tunnel' is the idiom for a sign of hope after a hard time.

questions.text: Seven people, A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a straight row, facing north. A sits second from the left. Only two people sit between A and C. Only three people sit between D and F and D is an immediate neighbour of A. B is an immediate neighbour of D and E is not an immediate neighbour of C. How many people sit between A and G?
questions.explanation: A is 2nd from the left and C 5th. D, beside A with three people between D and F, must be 3rd (1st would put F on C's seat), so F is 7th, and B, beside D, is 4th. E, not beside C, is 1st and G 6th: E A D B C G F. Between A and G sit D, B and C.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 1, 3, 6, ?, 20, 37
questions.explanation: The differences are 2, 3, 5, 9, 17, which grow by 1, 2, 4, 8: 6 + 5 = 11, then 11 + 9 = 20 and 20 + 17 = 37.

questions.text: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. F is an immediate neighbour of A. D sits second to the right of E. B is an immediate neighbour of E and sits second to the right of C. F sits second to the right of D. A is not an immediate neighbour of E. Who sit between E and A from the right of A?
questions.explanation: As all face the centre, each one's right runs anticlockwise. Anticlockwise from E the order is E, B, D, A, F, C: D is second to E's right, F second to D's right, B beside E and second to C's right, and A beside F but not E. Going right from A: F and C, then E.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘DEVOUR’ is written as ‘WGEQFT’ and ‘VARIED’ is written as ‘ECIKVF’. How will ‘BLANKET’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Letters in odd places become their opposites (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on) and letters in even places move 2 forward: DEVOUR → WGEQFT and VARIED → ECIKVF. So BLANKET → YNZPPGG.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 10, 27, 78, 231, ?, 2067
questions.explanation: Each term is 3 times the one before minus 3: 231 × 3 − 3 = 690, and 690 × 3 − 3 = 2067.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 54 + 18 ÷ 9 - 36 × 16 = 88
questions.explanation: After interchanging × and +: 54 × 18 ÷ 9 − 36 + 16 = 108 − 36 + 16 = 88.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. MEMBRANE : LDLAQZMD :: PRIVILEGE : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place back: MEMBRANE → LDLAQZMD. So PRIVILEGE → OQHUHKDFD.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? CPFG, ENHE, ?, IJLA, KHNY
questions.explanation: The first and third letters move 2 forward (C, E, G, I, K and F, H, J, L, N) and the second and fourth 2 back (P, N, L, J, H and G, E, C, A, Y): GLJC.

questions.text: If ‘–‘ means ‘division’, ‘+’ means ‘multiplication’, ‘×’ means ‘addition’ and ‘÷’ means ‘subtraction’, which of the following equations is correct?
questions.explanation: After replacing the signs: 20 ÷ 4 × 6 − 9 + 4 = 30 − 9 + 4 = 25. The other equations give 22, −3 and 33, not 21, 8 and 32.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 pilot 2 pivot 3 pipette 4 pigeon 5 pigment
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: pigeon (4), pigment (5), pilot (1), pipette (3), pivot (2). 'Pige' comes before 'pigm', and 'pig', 'pil', 'pip' and 'piv' follow the alphabet.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. ACBO : PCDB :: JLKM : NLMK :: KJIH : ?
questions.explanation: Each cluster is reversed and every letter moved one place forward: ACBO → OBCA → PCDB and JLKM → MKLJ → NLMK. So KJIH → HIJK → IJKL.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All beds are tables. All cots are tables. All tables are taps. Conclusions: I. All cots are taps. II. Some taps are tables. III. Some beds are cots.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: Cots are tables and tables are taps, so all cots are taps (I); as all tables are taps, some taps are tables (II). Beds and cots both lie inside tables but need not overlap, so III does not follow.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? XTEB, UQHE, RNKH, ?, LHQN
questions.explanation: The first and second letters move 3 back (X, U, R, O, L and T, Q, N, K, H) and the third and fourth 3 forward (E, H, K, N, Q and B, E, H, K, N): OKNK.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term. 18 : 45 :: ? : 60 :: 30 : 75
questions.explanation: In each pair the first number is two-fifths of the second: 18 = 2/5 × 45 and 30 = 2/5 × 75. So ? = 2/5 × 60 = 24.

questions.text: In a code language, 'dark colors' is coded as 'yu nu', 'days are bright' is coded as 'wu tu ku', 'nights are dark' is coded as 'ku nu pu', 'paint bright' is coded as 'wu ru'. What is the code for the word 'days'?
questions.explanation: 'Are' is in 'days are bright' and 'nights are dark', whose common code is 'ku'; 'bright' is in 'days are bright' and 'paint bright', whose common code is 'wu'. That leaves 'tu' for 'days'.

questions.text: On the basis of status of development, how are resources classified?
questions.explanation: By status of development, resources are classed as potential, developed (actual), stock and reserves. Biotic and abiotic is a classification by origin, renewable and non-renewable by exhaustibility, and individual, national and international by ownership.

questions.text: The 101st constitution amendment act of the Indian Constitution introduced the system of _________.
questions.explanation: The 101st Amendment Act, 2016 introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST), which replaced many central and state indirect taxes with a single tax: 'one nation, one tax'.

questions.text: Sunanda Nair completed her PhD from University of Mumbai for her thesis in "Intrinsic Lyrical Feminism" in which dance form?
questions.explanation: Dr Sunanda Nair, a Mohiniyattam dancer and disciple of Kanak Rele, earned her PhD from the University of Mumbai, under Rele's guidance, for a thesis on the intrinsic lyrical feminism of Mohiniattam.

questions.text: Who was appointed as the chairperson of Law Commission of India in November 2022?
questions.explanation: Justice Rituraj Awasthi, former Chief Justice of the Karnataka High Court, was appointed chairperson of the 22nd Law Commission of India in November 2022.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about the Joint Session of the Parliament of India?
options: So far, Joint sittings of the two Houses have taken place on three occasions.
The President can summon both the Houses to meet for the Joint Session.
The Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Vice President) presides over a Joint Session.
Joint session is held to resolve a deadlock between the two Houses of the Parliament.
questions.explanation: Under Article 118(4) the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over a joint sitting, not the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. The other statements hold: the President summons a joint sitting under Article 108 to resolve a deadlock, and there had been three (1961, 1978 and 2002) when the exam was held (February 2023).

questions.text: As of November 2022, who is the President of Nationalist Congress Party, a political party in India?
questions.explanation: Sharad Pawar, who founded the Nationalist Congress Party in 1999, was its President in November 2022.

questions.text: Which of the following dances is performed by women from the countryside villages of Malwa region in Madhya Pradesh?
questions.explanation: In the Matki dance of Malwa, women dance balancing earthen pots (matkis) on their heads at weddings and other celebrations. Padayani and Thirayattam belong to Kerala and Dandiya Raas to Gujarat.

questions.text: Export of manufactured goods ______ trade and commerce.
questions.explanation: Manufactured goods sold abroad expand trade and commerce and bring in foreign exchange.

questions.text: Which of the following is an INCORRECT match, concerning players and the State/UT they were born?
questions.explanation: Mithali Raj was born in Jodhpur, Rajasthan (to a Tamil family), not in Tamil Nadu. Anjum Chopra was born in New Delhi, Saina Nehwal in Hisar, Haryana, and Sania Mirza in Mumbai, Maharashtra.

questions.text: The chemical formula of washing soda is _______.
questions.explanation: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O. Ca(OH)₂ is slaked lime, Na₂SO₄ sodium sulphate and NaHCO₃ baking soda.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an example of a public sector company?
questions.explanation: The National Stock Exchange is not a government company: it was promoted by financial institutions and is owned by them and other investors. SAIL, ONGC and BHEL are central public sector enterprises.

questions.text: Currency notes and coins are called fiat money. They are also called _____.
questions.explanation: Currency notes and coins are legal tender: no one in the country may refuse them in settlement of a payment.

questions.text: The fundamental duties are defined under which Article of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 51A, in Part IVA (added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976), lists the fundamental duties.

questions.text: Bajrang Punia won the Bronze Medal by defeating Daulet Niyazbekov in which tournament?
questions.explanation: Bajrang Punia beat Kazakhstan's Daulet Niyazbekov in the men's freestyle 65 kg bronze-medal bout at the Tokyo Olympics 2020, held in 2021.

questions.text: The cytoplasm has _______ such as ribosomes, mitochondria, and golgi bodies.
questions.explanation: Organelles, such as ribosomes, mitochondria and Golgi bodies, are the specialised structures within the cytoplasm of a cell.

questions.text: Who among the following was the founder of the Vakataka Dynasty?
questions.explanation: Vindhyashakti founded the Vakataka dynasty in the Deccan in the 3rd century AD; Pravarasena I was his son and successor.

questions.text: Buddha Purnima, celebrated by the devotees of Gautam Buddha, is celebrated in the Hindu month of _______________.
questions.explanation: Buddha Purnima falls on the full moon of Vaisakha (April-May), which Buddhists mark as the day of the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and death.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In 1928, the _____ was founded at a meeting in Ferozeshah Kotla ground in Delhi. Amongst its leaders were Bhagat Singh, Jatin Das and Ajoy Ghosh.
questions.explanation: The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association was founded in 1928 at a meeting at Ferozeshah Kotla in Delhi; Bhagat Singh, Jatin Das and Ajoy Ghosh were among its leaders.

questions.text: West Bengal shares its longest border with which country?
questions.explanation: West Bengal's border with Bangladesh, about 2,200 km long, is far longer than its borders with Nepal and Bhutan; the state does not touch Myanmar.

questions.text: Three of the following four are auxiliaries to trade, and therefore form a group. Which is the one that does not belong to that group?
questions.explanation: Transport, warehousing, insurance, banking and advertising help trade along and are called auxiliaries to trade. Agriculture is a primary activity that produces goods.

questions.text: A river is running at 2 kmph. A boat goes 40 km upstream from A to B and also returns back from B to A in total 10 hours. The speed of the boat in still water is:
In a race of 1000 m, John beats Khan by 120 m. If the speed of John is 40 km/h, then the speed of Khan is:
questions.explanation: While John runs 1000 m, Khan runs 880 m, so Khan's speed is 40 × 880/1000 = 35.2 km/h.

questions.text: A can repair 11 benches in an hour and B can repair 5 benches in an hour. Determine how much time they will require to repair 64 benches when they work together?
questions.explanation: Together they repair 11 + 5 = 16 benches an hour: 64 ÷ 16 = 4 hours.

questions.text: Akash can do a piece of work in 21 days and Diya can do the same work in 63 days. Find the time required to complete the same work if they work on alternate days and Akash starts the work.
questions.explanation: Each two-day pair does 1/21 + 1/63 = 4/63 of the work. After 15 pairs (30 days) 60/63 is done, and the remaining 3/63 = 1/21 is one day of Akash's work: 31 days.

questions.text: In two ways, a shopkeeper deceives his customer. He dilutes pure honey by 20% with water and raises the price of honey by 15%. He pays Rs.30 per kg for 40 kg of pure honey. What is his total profit from selling it?
questions.explanation: 40 kg of pure honey costs 40 × ₹30 = ₹1,200. Adding 20% water makes 48 kg, sold at ₹30 × 1.15 = ₹34.50 a kg: 48 × 34.50 = ₹1,656. Profit = 1,656 − 1,200 = ₹456.

questions.text: In a trip, Kiran travelled 50 miles per hour for 3 hours on bike. Further he travelled by car for 2 hours at 65 miles per hour. He stopped for 2 hours for rest. After rest he travelled on bike for 4 hours at 80 miles per hour to reach his destination. Find Kiran’s average speed for the entire journey. (in miles per hour) (Rounded off to two places of decimals)
questions.explanation: Distance = 50 × 3 + 65 × 2 + 80 × 4 = 150 + 130 + 320 = 600 miles; time, with the 2-hour rest, = 3 + 2 + 2 + 4 = 11 hours. 600 ÷ 11 = 54.5454..., which SSC's key gives as 54.54 (cut off at two places; rounded, it would be 54.55).

questions.text: In 2010, the population of a country was 256080000. By 2020, the population had increased by 10 percent. The population in 2020 is:
The present population of a village is 50,000. Due to migration to cities, the population decreases at the rate of 5% every year. Find the population of the village after 2 years.
If the rate of interest be 16% per annum for the first year, 20% per annum for the second year and 15% per annum for the third year, then find the compound interest on Rs.15,000 for three years.

The marked price of a mobile phone is ₹16,500. A festival discount of 8% is allowed on it. Further, for cash payment a second discount of 5% is given. The cash payment, in rupees, that is to be made for buying the mobile phone is:
Find the LCM of the greatest 2-digit number divisible by 12 and the smallest 2-digit number divisible by 8.
questions.explanation: The greatest 2-digit multiple of 12 is 96 and the smallest 2-digit multiple of 8 is 16. As 96 = 6 × 16, the LCM is 96.

questions.text: A grocer sells rice at a profit of 15% and uses weights that are 20% less than the market weights. The total profit earned by him will be:
questions.explanation: For the price of 1 kg he gives 800 g, so he receives 1.15 times the cost of 1 kg for goods costing 0.8 of it: 1.15/0.8 = 1.4375, a profit of 43.75%.

questions.text: The third proportional to 0.1 and 0.12 is :
questions.explanation: The third proportional to a and b is b²/a = 0.12²/0.1 = 0.0144/0.1 = 0.144.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The old man think his younger daughter was mocking him.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'the old man' needs a singular verb, 'thinks', or, to match 'was mocking', the past 'thought'; 'think' is wrong either way.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The article _________ several experts on the subject.
questions.explanation: To 'cite' is to quote or name someone as an authority: an article cites experts. 'Sights', 'sites' and 'sits' sound alike but do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. During an office tour to Mumbai, I “chanced to meet” an old friend.
questions.explanation: To 'run into' someone is to meet them by chance: 'I ran into an old friend.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Steady
questions.explanation: 'Steady' means firm and unchanging; 'wavering' (unsteady, undecided) is its opposite. 'Undeviating' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Substitute the underline word with its appropriate synonym. The crew of the ship was “attacked”.
