questions.explanation: To 'assault' is to attack violently, so 'assaulted' can replace 'attacked'.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them contains a spelling error. Select the option that rectifies the error. According to a study by BBC across 66 different sports, five out of every six sports now give equal prize money to men and women at the world champonship level.
questions.explanation: 'Champonship' is misspelt: the word is 'championship'. The other options misspell 'women', 'different' and 'across', which the sentence spells correctly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Everyone was shocked to see the old man upset and “unkempt”.
questions.explanation: 'Unkempt' means messy and untidy in appearance. The other pairs do not describe how someone looks.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. In the fast lane
questions.explanation: To be 'in the fast lane' is to live an exciting, hectic life full of activity; the idiom is not about actual speed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym for the given word. False
questions.explanation: 'False' means not true: 'untrue'. 'Genuine' and 'correct' are nearly its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Enmity
questions.explanation: 'Enmity' is the state of being enemies: 'hostility'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Neha has ______ and won’t come to work for a few days.
questions.explanation: 'Flu' (influenza) is the illness. A 'flue' is a chimney duct, 'flew' is the past tense of 'fly', and 'floo' is not a word.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Penny wise and pound foolish
options: Serious about wealth but never working hard
Careful in trivial matters but wasteful in large
Good at spending but bad at earning
questions.explanation: Someone 'penny wise and pound foolish' is careful with small sums but wasteful with large ones.

questions.text: Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. After the teacher chose groups, John and Sara (was selected as partners for project), yet Sarah did most of the work.
options: have selected as a partners for a project
were selected as partners for a project
has selected as a partner for a project
had selected as partners for project
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'John and Sara' takes 'were', the sense needs the passive 'were selected', and the singular 'project' needs an article: 'were selected as partners for a project'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'cautious'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. Summer camp is a terrific idea used primarily by schools to (1)______ pupils to acquire and master new skills. It is an (2)______ outdoor activity. Many parents offer to enrol their kids in summer camps so they can participate in (3)_______ activities, discover their talents and passions, and broaden their horizons. Summer camps are (4)_____ for all children for ten to fifteen days by various schools or other organisations. These summer camps (5)________ entertaining educational activities like fitness classes, hobby improvement classes, learning lectures, sports activities, musical performances, etc. The pupils' general development and growth are benefitted from these summer camps.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank 1.
questions.explanation: Summer camps are meant to 'assist' (help) pupils to acquire new skills; 'hinder' is the opposite, and 'accelerate' and 'examine' do not fit.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. Summer camp is a terrific idea used primarily by schools to (1)______ pupils to acquire and master new skills. It is an (2)______ outdoor activity. Many parents offer to enrol their kids in summer camps so they can participate in (3)_______ activities, discover their talents and passions, and broaden their horizons. Summer camps are (4)_____ for all children for ten to fifteen days by various schools or other organisations. These summer camps (5)________ entertaining educational activities like fitness classes, hobby improvement classes, learning lectures, sports activities, musical performances, etc. The pupils' general development and growth are benefitted from these summer camps.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Summer camp is an 'organised' (planned and arranged) outdoor activity.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. Summer camp is a terrific idea used primarily by schools to (1)______ pupils to acquire and master new skills. It is an (2)______ outdoor activity. Many parents offer to enrol their kids in summer camps so they can participate in (3)_______ activities, discover their talents and passions, and broaden their horizons. Summer camps are (4)_____ for all children for ten to fifteen days by various schools or other organisations. These summer camps (5)________ entertaining educational activities like fitness classes, hobby improvement classes, learning lectures, sports activities, musical performances, etc. The pupils' general development and growth are benefitted from these summer camps.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank 3.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'numerous' (many), which suits the plural 'activities' and the passage's point that camps offer a wide range of them. 'Much' goes with uncountable nouns and 'few' would undercut the point; 'more' could pass only with an implied comparison, which the passage does not set up.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. Summer camp is a terrific idea used primarily by schools to (1)______ pupils to acquire and master new skills. It is an (2)______ outdoor activity. Many parents offer to enrol their kids in summer camps so they can participate in (3)_______ activities, discover their talents and passions, and broaden their horizons. Summer camps are (4)_____ for all children for ten to fifteen days by various schools or other organisations. These summer camps (5)________ entertaining educational activities like fitness classes, hobby improvement classes, learning lectures, sports activities, musical performances, etc. The pupils' general development and growth are benefitted from these summer camps.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Summer camps are 'held' (organised) for ten to fifteen days.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. Summer camp is a terrific idea used primarily by schools to (1)______ pupils to acquire and master new skills. It is an (2)______ outdoor activity. Many parents offer to enrol their kids in summer camps so they can participate in (3)_______ activities, discover their talents and passions, and broaden their horizons. Summer camps are (4)_____ for all children for ten to fifteen days by various schools or other organisations. These summer camps (5)________ entertaining educational activities like fitness classes, hobby improvement classes, learning lectures, sports activities, musical performances, etc. The pupils' general development and growth are benefitted from these summer camps.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The camps 'arrange' (organise) activities such as fitness classes, lectures and sports.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He decided not to go for the picnic as he was feeling a little____________.
questions.explanation: To be 'under the weather' is to feel slightly unwell, a reason to miss a picnic. 'As right as rain' means perfectly well, 'head in the clouds' lost in daydreams, and 'the calm before the storm' a quiet spell before trouble.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. “I am born in the United States”, yet I consider myself Indian.
options: I was born in the United States,
I was born at the United States,
I was born in United States,
questions.explanation: Birth is a completed past event, so it takes the simple past passive 'was born', and the country's name keeps 'the' after 'in': 'I was born in the United States, yet I consider myself Indian.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Sluggish
questions.explanation: 'Sluggish' means slow and inactive; its opposite is 'active'. 'Lethargic' is close in meaning to 'sluggish'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He received a __________ during the ceremony.
questions.explanation: A 'medal' is the award given at a ceremony. 'Metal', 'meddle' (interfere) and 'mettle' (courage) sound alike but mean different things.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. Betray
questions.explanation: To 'betray' someone is to be disloyal to them and expose them to harm; to 'protect' them is the opposite. 'Disloyal' is close to 'betray' in meaning, and 'sympathy' and 'adverse' are not its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Spick and span
questions.explanation: 'Spick and span' means neat, clean and well kept.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Blaze the trail
options: Be first to do something important
questions.explanation: To 'blaze the trail' is to be the first to do something new and important, showing others the way.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the capitalised word in the given sentence. I had the PRIVILEGE of meeting the magistrate.
questions.explanation: A 'privilege' here is a special honour or advantage: meeting the magistrate was an 'honour'.

questions.text: Identify the correctly spelt sentence.
options: Celastial objects are not visible to the naked eye.
Kelestial objects are not visible to the naked eye.
Celesteal objects are not visible to the naked eye.
Celestial objects are not visible to the naked eye.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'celestial', meaning of the sky or outer space.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. Nyra have/ been taking / dance classes / this year.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'Nyra' needs the singular auxiliary: 'Nyra has been taking dance classes this year.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Cherish
questions.explanation: To 'cherish' is to hold dear and value highly; 'admire' (to regard with warm approval) is not an exact match but is the only option close to it. 'Condemn', 'abandon' and 'neglect' point the opposite way.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. I was “startled” by his entry into the hall.
questions.explanation: 'Startled' means suddenly surprised or alarmed: 'frightened'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The objective of Robotics “are to interrogate” smart machines that can help people in a variety of ways.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'the objective' takes 'is', and the aim of robotics is to 'develop' (build) smart machines, not to interrogate them: 'The objective of Robotics is to develop smart machines'.

questions.text: The sentence given below has one misspelt word. Spot the INCORRECTLY spelt word and select its correct spelling. A trimphant smile appeared on his face.
questions.explanation: 'Trimphant' is misspelt: the word is 'triumphant', meaning joyful at a victory or success.

questions.text: Select the correct word for the blanks in the given sentence. He _________ to success after winning a lottery and _________ is everyone’s favourite flower.
questions.explanation: 'Rose' fits both blanks: the past tense of 'rise' (he rose to success) and the flower. 'Rise' is in the present tense, and 'got' and 'zenith' do not suit the flower.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It is often said that (1) _______ you want a pet to look up to you, get a dog. If you want a pet that looks straight (2) ________ you, get a horse. For an animal that looks down (3) _________ you, the cat must surely (4) _______ this description. Cats are their own bosses. They have little or no regard for anyone or anything. If you have (5) ________ looked closely at the cat, you will observe that it looks at you from the corner of its eyes, almost condescendingly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The clause sets a condition for the advice 'get a dog', so it needs 'if', the pattern the next sentence repeats ('If you want a pet ...').

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It is often said that (1) _______ you want a pet to look up to you, get a dog. If you want a pet that looks straight (2) ________ you, get a horse. For an animal that looks down (3) _________ you, the cat must surely (4) _______ this description. Cats are their own bosses. They have little or no regard for anyone or anything. If you have (5) ________ looked closely at the cat, you will observe that it looks at you from the corner of its eyes, almost condescendingly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: One looks 'at' a person: the horse 'looks straight at you', between the dog that looks up to you and the cat that looks down on you.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It is often said that (1) _______ you want a pet to look up to you, get a dog. If you want a pet that looks straight (2) ________ you, get a horse. For an animal that looks down (3) _________ you, the cat must surely (4) _______ this description. Cats are their own bosses. They have little or no regard for anyone or anything. If you have (5) ________ looked closely at the cat, you will observe that it looks at you from the corner of its eyes, almost condescendingly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: To 'look down on' someone is to regard them as inferior, which suits a cat that eyes you 'almost condescendingly'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It is often said that (1) _______ you want a pet to look up to you, get a dog. If you want a pet that looks straight (2) ________ you, get a horse. For an animal that looks down (3) _________ you, the cat must surely (4) _______ this description. Cats are their own bosses. They have little or no regard for anyone or anything. If you have (5) ________ looked closely at the cat, you will observe that it looks at you from the corner of its eyes, almost condescendingly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: To 'fit a description' is to match it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It is often said that (1) _______ you want a pet to look up to you, get a dog. If you want a pet that looks straight (2) ________ you, get a horse. For an animal that looks down (3) _________ you, the cat must surely (4) _______ this description. Cats are their own bosses. They have little or no regard for anyone or anything. If you have (5) ________ looked closely at the cat, you will observe that it looks at you from the corner of its eyes, almost condescendingly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Ever' means at any time: 'If you have ever looked closely at the cat'. 'Never' would contradict the observation that follows.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BREAD is written as ‘BED19’, ‘IRONY’ is written as ‘IOY32’, how will ‘SHARP’ be written as in that language?
questions.explanation: The code keeps the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters and adds the places of the 2nd and 4th: BREAD → B, E, D and R + A = 18 + 1 = 19; IRONY → I, O, Y and R + N = 18 + 14 = 32. So SHARP → S, A, P and H + R = 8 + 18 = 26: SAP26.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1. micro 2. minute 3. miles 4. mimic 5. miniature
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: micro (1), miles (3), mimic (4), miniature (5), minute (2). After 'mi', 'c' comes before 'l', 'm' and 'n', and 'mini' comes before 'minu'.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 89, 214, ?, 773, 1285, 2014
questions.explanation: The differences are the cubes 5³ = 125, 6³ = 216, 7³ = 343, 8³ = 512 and 9³ = 729: 214 + 216 = 430, and 430 + 343 = 773.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? ZYXW, STUV, RQPO, ?, JIHG, CDEF
questions.explanation: Backward and forward runs of four letters alternate. The backward runs start at Z, R and J and the forward runs at S, ?, C, each 8 letters before the one before it, so the missing run starts at S − 8 = K and goes forward: KLMN.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All trees are walls. No wall is a door. Some doors are rooms. Conclusions: I. Some rooms are walls. II. No trees are doors. III. All walls are trees.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: All trees are walls and no wall is a door, so no tree is a door (II). The rooms that are doors cannot be walls, and nothing places any other room among the walls, so I does not follow; nor need every wall be a tree (III).

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Doctor : Hospital :: Engineer : ?
questions.explanation: A doctor works in a hospital; an engineer works on a site. 'Construct' is what an engineer does, not a place.

questions.text: Seven people I, J, K, L, M, N and O, are sitting in a straight row, facing the north. Only five people sit to the left of M. J sits third to the left of O. O is not an immediate neighbour of M. K sits to the immediate right of N. I sits fourth to the right of J. Who sits at the extreme right end of the row?
questions.explanation: Five sit to M's left, so M is sixth from the left. With O third to the right of J and I fourth to the right of J, J, O and I sit at 1, 4 and 5 (J at 2 would put O next to M, and J at 3 would put O in M's seat). N and K take 2 and 3, K to N's right, which leaves L at 7, the right end.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 31 : 14 :: 23 : 10 :: 39 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the first minus 3, halved: (31 − 3)/2 = 14 and (23 − 3)/2 = 10. So (39 − 3)/2 = 18.

questions.text: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Ken is sitting to the immediate right of Joe. Joe is sitting third to the left of Ben. Kat is sitting to the immediate right of Ben. Jen is the immediate neighbour of Ben and Ken. Who is the immediate neighbour of Ken and Mel?
questions.explanation: Joe is third from Ben, so they sit opposite each other. Ken sits on Joe's right and Kat on Ben's right; Jen, a neighbour of both Ben and Ken, sits between them, and Mel takes the last seat, between Kat and Joe. Going round: Joe, Ken, Jen, Ben, Kat, Mel, so Joe sits between Ken and Mel.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. RXUT, VVYX, ZTCB, ?, HPKJ
questions.explanation: The first letters move +4 (R, V, Z, D, H), the second −2 (X, V, T, R, P), the third +4 (U, Y, C, G, K) and the fourth +4 (T, X, B, F, J), wrapping round after Z: DRGF.

questions.text: Which two numbers(not digits), from the given options, should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? (48 ÷ 3 + 6) ÷ 11 = 81 − 27 ÷ 3 × 5
In a certain code language, ‘CHURCH’ is written as ‘FKXUFK’ and ‘MUMBAI’ is written as ‘PXPEDL’. How will ‘TEMPLE’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward: CHURCH → FKXUFK and MUMBAI → PXPEDL. So TEMPLE → WHPSOH.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 60 ÷ 3 × 20 – 15 + 12 = 6
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 11, 35, 69, 209, 417, ?
Which of the following award is not awarded on the National sports Day?
questions.explanation: The Arjuna, Dronacharya and Dhyan Chand Awards are National Sports Awards, traditionally presented on National Sports Day, 29 August, Major Dhyan Chand's birth anniversary. The Param Vir Chakra is India's highest military gallantry award.

questions.text: In which year was the Minimum Wages Act introduced in India?
questions.explanation: The Minimum Wages Act, 1948 lets the government fix minimum rates of wages for workers in scheduled employments.

questions.text: Which of the following dancers is related with Kathakali?
questions.explanation: Kunchu Kurup (Thakazhi Kunchu Kurup) was a celebrated Kathakali actor from Kerala. Darshana Jhaveri is a Manipuri dancer, Shovana Narayan a Kathak dancer and Vempati Chinna Satyam a Kuchipudi guru.

questions.text: The Criminal Procedure _________, allows police officers or prison officers to collect certain identifiable information (such as fingerprints, biological samples) from convicts or those who have been arrested for an offence.
questions.explanation: The Criminal Procedure (Identification) Act, 2022 lets police and prison officers take measurements such as finger and palm prints, photographs, iris and retina scans and biological samples of convicts and arrested persons. It replaced the Identification of Prisoners Act, 1920.

questions.text: In which year was the term ‘secular’ added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity' to the Preamble.

questions.text: Blossom shower is common in _________.
questions.explanation: Blossom showers are pre-monsoon showers in Kerala and nearby areas that make the coffee plants flower; the similar 'mango showers' of Kerala and coastal Karnataka help mangoes ripen early.

questions.text: What is the chemical name of baking soda?
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium hydrogencarbonate, NaHCO₃. Sodium carbonate is washing soda (as its decahydrate), and calcium sulphate hemihydrate is plaster of Paris.

questions.text: _________ provides supporting services in the main areas of industrial and agricultural production, domestic and foreign trade and commerce.
questions.explanation: Infrastructure, such as power, transport, communication, water supply and banking, is the support system on which production on farms and in factories, and trade at home and abroad, depend.

questions.text: A reaction in which reactants combine to form products and again products recombine to form reactants is called __________ reaction.
questions.explanation: In a reversible reaction the products can react to give back the reactants, so the reaction runs both ways.

questions.text: Which House of the States participate(s) in the election of the President of India?
options: Neither Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council
Both, Legislative Assembly and Legislative Council
questions.explanation: Under Article 54 the President is elected by the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and of the Legislative Assemblies of the States (and of Delhi and Puducherry). Members of the Legislative Councils have no vote.

questions.text: In which of the following year did Australia Host the Commonwealth Games?
questions.explanation: Of these years, Australia hosted the Commonwealth Games in 2018, at the Gold Coast in Queensland. The 2014 Games were held in Glasgow, those of 2002 in Manchester and those of 1998 in Kuala Lumpur.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a component of the Green Revolution?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives minimum support price. The Green Revolution's components were farm technologies and practices: high-yielding seeds, fertilisers and other chemicals, irrigation and multiple cropping. Support prices, introduced in the mid-1960s to encourage farmers to adopt the new seeds, were a price policy that came alongside it, though some accounts count them as part of the wider strategy.

questions.text: Who among the following became Member of Legislative Assembly from Mokama, Bihar in India, in November 2022?
questions.explanation: Neelam Devi of the RJD won the Mokama by-election, counted on 6 November 2022. The seat had fallen vacant when her husband, Anant Singh, was disqualified after a conviction in an arms case.

questions.text: International trade agreements have __________ as parties.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'two or more countries': international trade agreements are made between countries, setting terms such as tariffs and quotas. In international law 'state' also means a sovereign country, but here it stands beside cities and provinces, the units within a country.

questions.text: Who has been elected as the Chairperson of the Audit Bureau of Circulations (ABC) for 2022-2023?
questions.explanation: Pratap Pawar, chairman of the Sakal Media Group, was elected Chairman of the Audit Bureau of Circulations, which certifies the circulation of publications, for 2022-23.

questions.text: In ______, a crisis in the balance of payments led to the introduction of economic reforms in India.
questions.explanation: In 1991 India's foreign exchange reserves fell to barely enough for a few weeks of imports; the crisis led to the New Economic Policy of liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation, launched that July.

questions.text: A shopkeeper offers a pen free on buying every dozen pens. Calculate % discount offered by the shopkeeper. Cost price of all the pens is same.( rounded off to one decimal place)
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 7.6%: the buyer pays for 12 pens and gets 13, a discount of 1/13 of the price, or 7.69%, which the key cuts short; rounded off to one decimal place it would be 7.7%, which is not an option.

questions.text: Two trains start at the same time from Bangalore and Chennai and proceed towards each other at the speeds of 80 km/h and 95 km/h. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 180 km more than the other. The distance between Bangalore and Chennai is:
questions.explanation: The faster train gains 95 − 80 = 15 km every hour, so the 180 km lead takes 12 hours. Together they cover (80 + 95) × 12 = 2,100 km.

questions.text: M, N, and O can do work in 22, 24, and 16 days respectively. If they work for a day alternately such that M works on the first day, N works on the second day, O works on the third day and then again M works on the fourth day and so on, then in how many days approximately, the work will be completed?
questions.explanation: Taking the work as 528 units (the LCM of 22, 24 and 16), M, N and O do 24, 22 and 33 units a day, 79 in each 3-day round. Six rounds (18 days) give 474 units, and M and N add 46 on days 19 and 20, leaving 8 units, which O finishes in 8/33 of day 21: about 20.2 days, or 20.

questions.text: Abhi has a solid sphere of diameter 10 cm. He cuts it into two equal halves and decides to paint it. The painting cost per square cm is Rs.10. Which of the following is the approximate difference between the painting cost of the sphere and the hemispheres? (Use π = 22/7, rounded off to two decimal places.)
questions.explanation: Cutting adds two flat circular faces of radius 5 cm: 2πr² = 2 × 22/7 × 25 = 1100/7 = 157.14 cm². At ₹10 per cm² the difference is 11000/7 = ₹1,571.43.

questions.text: If the price of petrol becomes Rs.110/litre from Rs.95/litre, by how much percentage the consumption of petrol should be reduced by Ravi so that his expenditure remains the same? (correct up to two decimals)
questions.explanation: To keep spending the same, consumption must fall by (110 − 95)/110 × 100 = 1500/110 = 13.64%.

questions.text: The greatest number that can exactly divide 1560 and 2040 is X. What is the value of 121 - X?
The fourth proportional 6, 9, 18 is:
Three bicycles are bought for Rs.16,500 and the transport cost per bicycle is Rs.200. What should be the selling price (in Rs.) of each bicycle to have a profit of 8%?
questions.explanation: Total cost = 16,500 + 3 × 200 = ₹17,100. For an 8% profit the three must sell for 17,100 × 1.08 = ₹18,468, or ₹6,156 each.

questions.text: If a man climbs a hill at 6 km/h on the journey from foot to top of the hill and returns at 10 km/h, then find his average speed for the journey (in km/h).
questions.explanation: For equal distances the average speed is 2 × 6 × 10/(6 + 10) = 120/16 = 7.5 km/h.

questions.text: Vinod buys an article and sells it at a loss of 5%. If he would have bought it for 20% less and sold it for Rs.25 more, he would have gained 20%. What was the original cost price?
questions.explanation: With cost price x he sells at 0.95x. Bought at 0.8x with a 20% gain, the selling price would be 0.96x, which is 0.95x + 25, so 0.01x = 25 and x = ₹2,500.

questions.text: The present population of a city is estimated to be 10 lakh and is expected to increase to 12.10 lakh during the next 2 years. The uniform annual rate of growth is:
questions.explanation: (1 + r)² = 12.10/10 = 1.21, so 1 + r = 1.1 and the rate is 10% a year.

questions.text: The percentage equivalence of the fraction ¾ is:

In a circular race of 625 m, X and Y start from the same point, at the same time and at speeds of 36 km/h and 54 km/h, respectively. When will they meet again for the first time on the track if they are running in the opposite directions?
questions.explanation: 36 km/h = 10 m/s and 54 km/h = 15 m/s. Running in opposite directions they close at 25 m/s, so they first meet after 625/25 = 25 seconds.

questions.text: The average marks obtained by Mahesh in five subjects is 62 and he obtains 71 marks in the sixth subject. What is the average of the marks secured by Mahesh in all six subjects?

The marked price of a woollen jacket is Rs.800. The shopkeeper allows a discount of 10% on every item. Due to off-season, the shopkeeper allows additional discount of 5% on jacket. Find the selling price of the jacket?
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Keep a straight face
options: Look serious though you want to laugh
questions.explanation: To 'keep a straight face' is to look serious while trying not to laugh.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Attain
questions.explanation: To 'attain' is to achieve or reach a goal. 'Abandon' means give up, 'destroy' ruin and 'commence' begin.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The play usually needs half an hour for its preparation and makeup, and its performance ___________ within ten minutes.
questions.explanation: The sentence describes what usually happens ('usually needs'), so the simple present 'ends' matches it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Most often, child labour occurs when families _______ financial challenges or uncertainty – whether due to poverty, sudden illness of a caregiver or job loss of a primary wage earner.
questions.explanation: Families 'face' financial challenges. 'Contend' would need 'with', and 'emulate' (imitate) and 'happen' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Quiet
questions.explanation: 'Quiet' means calm and silent; 'commotion' is a noisy disturbance. 'Stillness' is a synonym, and 'compose' and 'completely' are unrelated.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. It is better to end up certain matters than________ a dead horse.
questions.explanation: To 'beat a dead horse' is to waste effort on a matter that is already settled or cannot be changed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. While I was driving the car, my brother “talked over phone” to his kid.
questions.explanation: An action in progress at the same time as 'I was driving' takes the past continuous, and the phrase is 'over the phone': 'my brother was talking over the phone to his kid'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. “Incompetent” people keep on blaming others for their failures.
questions.explanation: 'Incompetent' means lacking the skill to do something well: 'inefficient'. 'Incongruous' means out of place and 'inevitable' unavoidable.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Salient
questions.explanation: 'Salient' means most noticeable or important; its opposite is 'negligible', too small to matter. 'Noteworthy', 'striking' and 'clear' are close to synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The cat couldn’t find a _________ place for its kittens in the backyard of the house.
questions.explanation: A 'proper' place is a suitable one. 'Stern' (strict), 'drastic' (extreme) and 'vague' (unclear) do not describe a place for kittens.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homophone of the given word. Ate
questions.explanation: 'Ate', the past tense of 'eat', sounds exactly like 'eight' but differs in spelling and meaning. 'Hate' and 'weight' begin with a different sound.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'pioneer'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Robinson Crusoe “puzzles” when he discovered a footprint in the sand.
questions.explanation: 'Discovered' sets the sentence in the past, and Crusoe is the one confused, so the passive past 'was puzzled' is needed: 'Robinson Crusoe was puzzled when he discovered a footprint in the sand.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Restore
questions.explanation: To 'restore' is to bring back or repair; to 'destroy' is to ruin. 'Recover' is close in meaning, and 'random' and 'productive' are unrelated.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word ‘doubtful’ from the following sentence. He was in a dilemma about the completion of the project investigation because of his health issues.
questions.explanation: To be in a 'dilemma' is to be unsure which way to decide, the sense of 'doubtful'; the other three words carry no doubt. ('Dilemma' is a noun, so it matches the sense rather than the part of speech.)

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The world is becoming increasingly (1)_______. Since 2007, more than half of the world’s population has been living in cities, and that share is (2)_______ to rise to 60 per cent by 2030. Cities and metropolitan areas are powerhouses of economic growth—(3)_______ about 60 per cent of global GDP. However, they also account for about 70 per cent of global carbon emissions and over 60 per cent of (4)________ use. Rapid urbanisation is resulting in a growing number of slum dwellers, inadequate and (5)________ infrastructure and services, worsening air pollution and unplanned urban sprawl.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says more than half the world's people have lived in cities since 2007: the world is becoming increasingly 'urbanised'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The world is becoming increasingly (1)_______. Since 2007, more than half of the world’s population has been living in cities, and that share is (2)_______ to rise to 60 per cent by 2030. Cities and metropolitan areas are powerhouses of economic growth—(3)_______ about 60 per cent of global GDP. However, they also account for about 70 per cent of global carbon emissions and over 60 per cent of (4)________ use. Rapid urbanisation is resulting in a growing number of slum dwellers, inadequate and (5)________ infrastructure and services, worsening air pollution and unplanned urban sprawl.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: A share expected in the future, by 2030, is 'projected' to rise.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The world is becoming increasingly (1)_______. Since 2007, more than half of the world’s population has been living in cities, and that share is (2)_______ to rise to 60 per cent by 2030. Cities and metropolitan areas are powerhouses of economic growth—(3)_______ about 60 per cent of global GDP. However, they also account for about 70 per cent of global carbon emissions and over 60 per cent of (4)________ use. Rapid urbanisation is resulting in a growing number of slum dwellers, inadequate and (5)________ infrastructure and services, worsening air pollution and unplanned urban sprawl.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Cities are powerhouses of growth because they produce, or are 'contributing', about 60 per cent of global GDP.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The world is becoming increasingly (1)_______. Since 2007, more than half of the world’s population has been living in cities, and that share is (2)_______ to rise to 60 per cent by 2030. Cities and metropolitan areas are powerhouses of economic growth—(3)_______ about 60 per cent of global GDP. However, they also account for about 70 per cent of global carbon emissions and over 60 per cent of (4)________ use. Rapid urbanisation is resulting in a growing number of slum dwellers, inadequate and (5)________ infrastructure and services, worsening air pollution and unplanned urban sprawl.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Resource use', the use of natural resources such as energy, water and materials, is the cost cities carry alongside their carbon emissions.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The world is becoming increasingly (1)_______. Since 2007, more than half of the world’s population has been living in cities, and that share is (2)_______ to rise to 60 per cent by 2030. Cities and metropolitan areas are powerhouses of economic growth—(3)_______ about 60 per cent of global GDP. However, they also account for about 70 per cent of global carbon emissions and over 60 per cent of (4)________ use. Rapid urbanisation is resulting in a growing number of slum dwellers, inadequate and (5)________ infrastructure and services, worsening air pollution and unplanned urban sprawl.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Rapid urbanisation strains infrastructure and services, leaving them inadequate and 'overburdened', loaded beyond their capacity.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Elephant : Herd :: Fish : ?
questions.explanation: A group of elephants is a herd, and a group of fish is a 'shoal'.

questions.text: As of November 2022, who is the Union Minister for Communications & Electronics and Information Technology in India?
questions.explanation: Ashwini Vaishnaw held both the Communications and the Electronics and Information Technology portfolios in November 2022, and still when the exam was held (February 2023); he had held them, with Railways, since July 2021.

questions.text: What is the major constituent of cellular energy transfer systems?
questions.explanation: Phosphorus, as phosphate, is the key part of ATP (adenosine triphosphate), the molecule cells use to store and pass on energy; the energy is released when a phosphate group is split off.

questions.text: The principle of Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Rights in Part III of the Constitution were modelled on the Bill of Rights of the United States Constitution.

questions.text: Roads linking a state capital with different district headquarters are known as ______. These roads are constructed and maintained by the State Public Works Department (PWD) in State and Union Territories.
questions.explanation: State Highways connect a state's capital with its district headquarters and are built and maintained by the state's Public Works Department. District Roads link a district's headquarters with other places in the district.

questions.text: How does white silver chloride turn grey in sunlight?
options: Due to the decomposition of silver chloride into silver and chlorine by light
Due to the displacement of silver chloride to silver oxide
Due to rusting of silver in the presence of oxygen
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the decomposition of silver chloride by light: sunlight splits it into grey silver and chlorine (2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl₂), as NCERT explains it. That decomposition is strictly also a redox change (silver ions are reduced and chloride ions oxidised), but the key's option names the actual process.

questions.text: Iron and steel are ________industry.
questions.explanation: Industries are classed by their raw material: the iron and steel industry, like cement and aluminium, uses minerals (iron ore, coking coal, limestone) and is mineral-based, while cotton and jute textiles and sugar are agro-based.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in the brackets to fill in the blank. Don't try to walk __________ (after) you can crawl.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'after' is 'before': one should not try to walk before one can crawl, that is, before mastering the basics.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. At the drop of a hat
options: Force someone to behave in a disciplined manner
questions.explanation: To do something 'at the drop of a hat' is to do it at once, without hesitating.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks in the given sentence. I ______ the gift of my aunt and she ______ money from my father.
questions.explanation: To 'accept' a gift is to take it, and to 'expect' money from someone is to look forward to receiving it. 'Except' means to leave out, which fits neither blank.

questions.text: The sentence given below has one misspelt word. Spot the INCORRECTLY spelt word and select its correct spelling. A unanimos consent of all the shareholders was required to approve the merger.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'unanimous', meaning agreed by everyone.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the highlighted idiom in the given sentence. The marriage of my elder brother has been “on the cards” for some time now.
questions.explanation: Something 'on the cards' is likely to happen: 'probable'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. There is only one thing that ________ with us that cannot be taken away: to act with courage and dignity and to stick to the ideals that have given meaning to life.
questions.explanation: The relative clause refers to the singular 'one thing' and states a lasting truth ('cannot be taken away'), so it takes the singular simple present 'remains'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. You should take your car in for a service “because it has starting to make weird noises”.
options: because it had starting to make weird noises
because it has start to make weird noises
because it's starting to make weird noises
questions.explanation: 'Has' as a helping verb takes a past participle ('has started'), never the bare -ing form; the present continuous 'it is starting', shortened to 'it's starting', says what the car has begun to do now.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. In his moment of “despair”, I am with him.
questions.explanation: 'Despair' is the complete loss of hope, a state of great unhappiness: 'misery'. 'Hope' and 'contentment' are nearly its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word ‘liberate’ from the following sentence. There is a famous saying by Rousseau which says that man is born free but he is surrounded by the clutches of slavery in society.
questions.explanation: To 'liberate' is to set free, so 'free' is the word in the sentence closest to it in meaning; 'clutches' and 'slavery' name what one is freed from.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Rosie became an expert in the field of “painting by her”.
questions.explanation: 'By herself' (alone, without help) needs the reflexive pronoun, which agrees with 'Rosie'; the gerund 'painting' follows 'the field of'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Courtesy
questions.explanation: 'Courtesy' is polite, considerate behaviour; its opposite is 'crudeness', rudeness or a lack of refinement. 'Generosity' is close to it in spirit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Cheerless
questions.explanation: 'Cheerless' means dull and depressing: 'gloomy'. 'Bright' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The instructions on the bottle say – open the packet and poured the contents into hot water.
questions.explanation: The instructions are in the imperative, and 'and' joins two commands, so both verbs take the base form: 'open the packet and pour the contents'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Discersive' is misspelt: the word is 'discursive', meaning moving from one subject to another.

questions.text: Select the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to the given word. Benevolent
questions.explanation: 'Benevolent' means kind and well-meaning; its opposite is 'malevolent', wishing harm to others. 'Benign' and 'magnanimous' are close to 'benevolent'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The effect (1)________ on the mind by travelling depends entirely on the mind of the traveller and on the way in which he conducts himself. The chief idea of one very common type of traveller is to see as many objects of (2)__________ as he possibly can. If he can only after his return home say that he has seen such and such a temple, castle, picture gallery, or museum, he is perfectly (3)_______. Therefore, when he arrives at a famous city, he (4)______ it, so that he may get over as quickly as possible the task of seeing its principal sights, entered them by name in his notebook as visited or, in his own phraseology ‘done’, then hurry on to another city which he treats in the same (5)________ way.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'produced': an effect is usually said to be 'produced on' the mind. 'Created' is close in meaning and arguable, though it suggests an effect someone sets out to make; 'appeared' has no passive to go with 'by travelling', and 'ingrained' means fixed deep, not caused.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Objects of interest' are the sights worth seeing, such as the temples and galleries the passage goes on to list.

questions.explanation: He wants to get the sightseeing over 'as quickly as possible', so he 'rushes through' the city. 'Visits' says nothing of that haste, 'browses through' suggests a leisurely look, and 'comes across' means finds by chance.
