questions.explanation: 'Unceremonious' means hasty and without proper attention, the way he hurries through each city. 'Disinterest' is a noun, 'lack lustre' (lacklustre) means dull rather than hurried, and 'nonchalant' (calmly unconcerned) misses his haste.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term. 104 : 13 :: ? : 37 :: 168 : 21
questions.explanation: 104 ÷ 13 = 8 and 168 ÷ 21 = 8, so each first term is 8 times the second: 37 × 8 = 296.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 2880, 480, 96, ?, 8, 4
In a certain code language, ‘DANCE’ is written as ‘AECDN’, ‘MUSIC’ is written as ‘IUCMS’, how will ‘SONG’ be written as in that language?
questions.explanation: The vowels come first and then the consonants, each group in alphabetical order: DANCE → AE + CDN and MUSIC → IU + CMS. So SONG → O + GNS: OGNS.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some paints are brushes. All brushes are easels. Some easels are tables. Conclusions: I. Some brushes are tables. II. Some paints are easels. III. Some easels are brushes.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: Some paints are brushes and all brushes are easels, so some paints are easels (II); as all brushes are easels, some easels are brushes (III). Brushes and tables need not overlap, so I does not follow.

questions.text: Which of the mathematical signs should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct? 72 - 6 + 2 × 216 ÷ 24 = 420
questions.explanation: After interchanging − and ÷: 72 ÷ 6 + 2 × 216 − 24 = 12 + 432 − 24 = 420.

questions.text: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? DKBN, ENWS, ?, GTMC, HWHH
questions.explanation: The first letters move 1 place forward (D, E, F, G, H), the second 3 forward (K, N, Q, T, W), the third 5 back (B, W, R, M, H) and the fourth 5 forward (N, S, X, C, H). The missing cluster is FQRX.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 790 + 5 ÷ 58 × 5 – 96 = 352
Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? AZME, CYOG, ?, GWSK, IVUM
questions.explanation: The first letters move 2 places forward (A, C, E, G, I), the second 1 back (Z, Y, X, W, V), the third 2 forward (M, O, Q, S, U) and the fourth 2 forward (E, G, I, K, M). The missing cluster is EXQI.

questions.text: Which of the following options will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 103, 110, 105, ?, 107, 114, 109

Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. QUEST : VUGWS :: REACH : JECGT :: SOLVE : ?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and each letter moved 2 places forward: QUEST → TSEUQ → VUGWS and REACH → HCAER → JECGT. So SOLVE → EVLOS → GXNQU.

questions.text: ‘P % Q’ means ‘P is the brother of Q’. ‘P + Q’ means ‘P is the daughter of Q’. ‘P = Q’ means ‘P is the son of Q’. ‘P # Q’ means ‘P is the wife of Q’. If L + M % N = O # P, how is P related to L?
questions.explanation: L is the daughter of M, M the brother of N, N the son of O, and O the wife of P. So N and his brother M are P's sons, and P, the father of L's father M, is L's father's father.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘MARINE’ is coded as ‘100’ and ‘NORMAL’ is coded as ‘126’. How will ‘REALM’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each code is twice the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet, minus 20: MARINE 13 + 1 + 18 + 9 + 14 + 5 = 60 and 2 × 60 − 20 = 100; NORMAL 14 + 15 + 18 + 13 + 1 + 12 = 73 and 2 × 73 − 20 = 126. REALM: 18 + 5 + 1 + 12 + 13 = 49 and 2 × 49 − 20 = 78.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 pointed 2 pollen 3 populate 4 popular 5 podium
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: podium (5), pointed (1), pollen (2), popular (4), populate (3). 'Pod' comes before 'Poi', 'Poi' before 'Pol' and 'Pol' before 'Pop'; 'popular' and 'populate' first differ at the seventh letter, 'r' before 't'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Friend : Foe :: Die : ?
questions.explanation: 'Foe' is the opposite of 'friend', and the opposite of the verb 'die' is 'live'.

questions.text: Six friends M, N, O, P, Q and R, are sitting in a row facing South. N is exactly in between P and Q. O is to the immediate left of R. M is to the immediate right of P. If Q is at the extreme left of the row, then who is sitting to the immediate left to O?
questions.explanation: Counting from the friends' own left, Q is first. N is exactly between P and Q and M is to P's immediate right, so Q N P M take the first four seats (a wider gap, Q _ N _ P M, leaves no two adjacent seats for O and R). O sits to R's immediate left in the last two: Q N P M O R. M is to O's immediate left.

questions.text: Eight people, D, E, G, H, M, N, Y and Z are sitting in a straight line, facing north. Y sits at one of the extreme ends of the line. Only three people sit between Y and Z. E sits second to the right of Z. Only three people sit between E and D. G sits at one of the positions to the left of D but not at an extreme end of the line. M is not an immediate neighbour of Z. N sits second to the right of H. How many people sit to the left of H?
questions.explanation: If Y were at the right end, Z would be 4th, E 6th and D 2nd, leaving no seat left of D for G that is not an end. So Y is 1st, Z 5th, E 7th, D 3rd and G 2nd. N is second to the right of H: H 4th and N 6th, since H 6th and N 8th would put M in 4th, next to Z. The line is Y G D H Z N E M, with three people to H's left.

questions.text: Base changes the colour of the red litmus to ______.
questions.explanation: Bases turn red litmus blue; acids turn blue litmus red.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In 1873, he founded the Satya-Shodhak Samaj. Who is referred to as 'he' here?
questions.explanation: Jyotirao (Jyotiba) Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in Pune in September 1873 to work for the rights of the lower castes and of women. 'He' rules out Savitribai Phule, his wife and fellow reformer.

questions.text: At Devaprayag the Bhagirathi is Joined by ______.
questions.explanation: At Devprayag in Uttarakhand the Bhagirathi meets the Alaknanda, and from there the combined river is called the Ganga.

questions.text: Who took over as the Chief of Army Staff on April 30, 2022?
questions.explanation: General Manoj Pande took over as Chief of the Army Staff on 30 April 2022, succeeding General Manoj Mukund Naravane; he was the first officer from the Corps of Engineers to head the Army.

questions.text: Who looks after the development, maintenance and management of inland water ways in India?
questions.explanation: The Inland Waterways Authority of India, set up in 1986, develops and regulates India's inland waterways for shipping and navigation, including the National Waterways.

questions.text: Who among the following politicians became the President of India in July 2022?
questions.explanation: Droupadi Murmu was elected the 15th President of India in July 2022 and sworn in on 25 July 2022, succeeding Ram Nath Kovind.

questions.text: Personal Disposable income is money that is available for household consumption,__________ and spending after accounting for income tax.
questions.explanation: Personal disposable income is what households have left after paying direct taxes such as income tax; it is either spent on consumption or saved.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides for 'protection against arrest and detention in certain cases’?
questions.explanation: Article 22 protects against arrest and detention in certain cases: a person arrested must be told the grounds, may consult a lawyer and must be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours.

questions.text: Disadvantage of the industrial development is _________.
questions.explanation: Industries release harmful gases, effluents and waste into the air, water and soil, so pollution is a drawback of industrial growth; the other options are benefits.

questions.text: As of November 2022, who is the Union Minister of Information & Broadcasting and Youth Affairs & Sports in India?
questions.explanation: In November 2022 Anurag Singh Thakur held both the Information and Broadcasting and the Youth Affairs and Sports portfolios in the Union Cabinet, which he had taken over in July 2021.

questions.text: If there is need for four labourers and seven are working, then what kind of unemployment are the extra three labourers suffering from?
questions.explanation: In disguised unemployment more people work at a task than it needs, so the extra workers add nothing to output: withdrawing the three would not reduce production.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of indirect tax?
questions.explanation: GST is levied on the supply of goods and services and passed on to the buyer in the price, so it is an indirect tax. Gift tax, corporation tax and property tax fall directly on the person who pays them.

questions.text: Limestone, chalk and marble are different forms of ______.
questions.explanation: Limestone, chalk and marble are all forms of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃).

questions.text: The annual festival of Gangaur, celebrated by the married women of Rajasthan, is observed in the Hindu month of ________.
questions.explanation: Gangaur, the worship of Gauri (Parvati) by Rajasthani women, is celebrated in Chaitra (March-April), beginning the day after Holi.

questions.text: Which country won the maximum gold medal in the 2020 Summer Paralympics?
questions.explanation: China topped the medal table at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, held in 2021, with 96 gold medals; Great Britain and the United States followed.

questions.text: ‘Arthashastra’ was written by:
questions.explanation: The 'Arthashastra', a treatise on statecraft and economics, is attributed to Kautilya (Chanakya), adviser to Chandragupta Maurya. Vishakhadatta wrote the 'Mudrarakshasa' and Megasthenes the 'Indica'.

questions.text: Alarmel Valli is an exponent of which of the following classical dance forms?
questions.explanation: Alarmel Valli of Chennai is a leading Bharatanatyam dancer of the Pandanallur style.

questions.text: In which sport is the field often oval with a rectangular area in the middle, that is 22 yards (20.12 metres) by 10 feet (3.04 metres) wide?
questions.explanation: Cricket is played on an oval field with the 22-yard pitch, the rectangle the batters run between, at its centre.

questions.text: The ________ is the sole link of communication between the Cabinet and the Governor.
options: Chairman of State Public Service Commission
questions.explanation: Under Article 167 the Chief Minister must pass on to the Governor the decisions of the Council of Ministers and any information the Governor calls for, which makes him the link between the two.

questions.text: C. V. Chandrasekhar was awarded the Padma Bhushan for his contribution in ______________.
questions.explanation: Prof. C. V. Chandrasekhar, a Bharatanatyam dancer, choreographer and teacher trained at Kalakshetra, received the Padma Bhushan in 2011.

questions.text: Find the absolute difference between the greatest 3-digit number and the smallest 4-digit number divisible by 12, 25 and 18.
questions.explanation: The LCM of 12, 25 and 18 is 900. The greatest 3-digit multiple of 900 is 900 and the smallest 4-digit multiple 1800: 1800 − 900 = 900.

questions.text: A shopkeeper announces the following three discount schemes on the purchase of an article. Which of these schemes is the best scheme for a customer? A. Two successive discounts of 15% and 18%; B. Buy 6 articles and get 2 free; C. A flat discount of 30%
options: Both schemes A and C give the same discount
questions.explanation: A: the customer pays 0.85 × 0.82 = 0.697 of the price, a discount of 30.3%. B: 8 articles for the price of 6, a discount of 2/8 = 25%. C: 30%. Scheme A gives the most.

questions.text: On mixing two classes A and B of students having average marks 50 and 80, respectively, the average marks obtained is 60. Find the respective ratio of the students in the classes A and B.
A can paint 5 chairs in an hour and B can paint 3 chairs in an hour. Determine how much time they will require to paint 40 chairs when they work together.
questions.explanation: Together they paint 5 + 3 = 8 chairs an hour, so 40 chairs take 40 ÷ 8 = 5 hours.

questions.text: The weights of two persons A and B are in ratio of 5 : 3 respectively. If the weight of A increases by 5% and the total weight of A and B becomes 92 kg with an increase of 15%, then find the percentage increase in the weight of B. (Correct to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanation: Before the increase the total was 92 ÷ 1.15 = 80 kg, so A weighed 50 kg and B 30 kg. A rises 5% to 52.5 kg, leaving 92 − 52.5 = 39.5 kg for B: an increase of 9.5/30 × 100 = 31.67%.

questions.text: If a right circular cone of height 24 cm has a volume of 392 π cm³, then the curved surface area is:
questions.explanation: (1/3)πr² × 24 = 392π gives r² = 49, so r = 7 cm. The slant height is √(7² + 24²) = √625 = 25 cm, and the curved surface area πrl = π × 7 × 25 = 175π cm².

questions.text: If you are buying one jacket at ₹2,500 and buying two similar jackets at ₹4,500, then find the discount percentage. (Marked price of one jacket is ₹2500)
questions.explanation: Two jackets at the marked price cost 2 × ₹2,500 = ₹5,000. Paying ₹4,500 is a discount of ₹500, or 500/5,000 × 100 = 10%.

questions.text: A police officer follows a thief who is at a distance of 800 m from him. If they run at a speed of 8 km/h and 7 km/h, respectively, how long does the police officer have to run to catch up with the thief?
questions.explanation: The officer gains 8 − 7 = 1 km/h, so closing the 0.8 km gap takes 0.8 hours, in which he runs 8 × 0.8 = 6.4 km = 6400 m.

questions.text: A sum of money amounts to ₹14,112 at the rate of 20% per annum compounded annually for 3 years. Find the sum of money.

A thief started running at a speed of 15 m/s, after running for 12 sec a policeman started running to catch the thief in the same direction at a speed of 20 m/s. How many metre will the policeman run to catch the thief?
questions.explanation: In 12 seconds the thief gets 15 × 12 = 180 m ahead. The policeman gains 20 − 15 = 5 m/s, so he catches up in 180 ÷ 5 = 36 seconds, running 20 × 36 = 720 m.

questions.text: If the radius of a sphere is increased by 5%, what percentage increase takes place in the surface area of the sphere?
questions.explanation: Surface area varies as the square of the radius: 1.05² = 1.1025, an increase of 10.25%.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. This nation is _________ to each of its citizens.
questions.explanation: 'Fair', meaning just or treating everyone alike, fits; its homophone 'fare' is the price of a journey. 'Feel' and 'fur' make no sense here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Truth
questions.explanation: 'Falsity', the quality of being false or untrue, is the opposite of 'truth'. 'Reality' is close to it in meaning, and 'loyalty' and 'lay' are unrelated.

questions.text: Select the option with the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. They waited for him in the “adjcent” room.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'adjacent', meaning next to or adjoining.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Blend
questions.explanation: A 'blend' is a mixture of things combined into one: a 'fusion'. 'Disunity' and 'scatter' are nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the word to fill in the blank in the given sentence. Shyam ________ an _________ letter from his employer.
questions.explanation: 'Received' follows 'i before e except after c', and 'acknowledgment' is as accepted a spelling as 'acknowledgement'; every other option misspells at least one of the two words.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. It is quite comprehensible that now young people's minds are constantly being reshaped by the media's constant meddling of certain “unfathomable” ideas and moral standards.
questions.explanation: 'Unfathomable' means impossible to understand; its opposite is 'comprehensible', able to be understood.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. A leading actor has said in a new interview that “nepotism” does not matter, and she is the best example of that.
questions.explanation: 'Nepotism' is favouring relatives or friends, especially in giving jobs: 'favouritism'. The other three options mean fairness, its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The teacher asked me to tell him “what is his name”?
questions.explanation: In reported speech a question becomes a statement, with the subject before the verb and the tense moved back after the past 'asked': 'what his name was.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He seized a thief by his __________ and forced him to answer.
questions.explanation: A 'collar' is the band round the neck of a shirt or coat, by which a person can be seized. 'Choler' means anger and a 'caller' is someone who calls.

questions.text: Select the correct idiom that can substitute the italicised group of words in the given sentence. Prof. Ram Prasad was an environmental activist, and apparently, he became “annoying and irritating” to leather factories over the years.
questions.explanation: 'A thorn in the flesh' is a person or thing that keeps annoying or troubling someone. 'A vexed question' is a much-debated problem, 'a slow coach' a slow person and 'an uphill task' a hard one.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence. The moral failure was the result of his “lassitude”.
questions.explanation: 'Lassitude' is physical or mental tiredness, a lack of energy: 'weariness'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The child _____________ not guilty of shoplifting.
questions.explanation: To 'plead not guilty' is to deny a charge formally in court; none of the other verbs goes with 'not guilty'.

questions.text: Select the correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. Slow and steady “wins the race”.
questions.explanation: A proverb states a general truth, so it takes the simple present, and the single idea 'slow and steady' takes the singular 'wins'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The shield used by the / warrior have been one / made of strong iron.
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular 'the shield', so the verb must be 'has been', not 'have been'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom that can be substituted in the following sentence. The robber “showed a clean pair of heels” when the policeman came nearer.
options: stole and ran away with heels
stood so as to show the heels
showed how clean the heels were
questions.explanation: To 'show a clean pair of heels' is to run away fast, as the robber did when the policeman came near.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Transformation of a sentence means (1) ___________ the words or forms of the sentence without changing (2) ___________ meaning. Such changes can be in the form (3) __________ changes from negative sentences into assertive, interrogative or exclamatory sentences and vice versa (4) ________ change in narration or change in voice or changes from simple to (5) _________ or complex sentences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: When 'mean' says what something involves, it takes the -ing form: transformation 'means changing' the words, matching 'without changing' later in the sentence. 'Mean to change' would mean 'intend to change', which does not fit.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Transformation of a sentence means (1) ___________ the words or forms of the sentence without changing (2) ___________ meaning. Such changes can be in the form (3) __________ changes from negative sentences into assertive, interrogative or exclamatory sentences and vice versa (4) ________ change in narration or change in voice or changes from simple to (5) _________ or complex sentences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Its' refers to the singular 'sentence': the transformation keeps the sentence's meaning.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Transformation of a sentence means (1) ___________ the words or forms of the sentence without changing (2) ___________ meaning. Such changes can be in the form (3) __________ changes from negative sentences into assertive, interrogative or exclamatory sentences and vice versa (4) ________ change in narration or change in voice or changes from simple to (5) _________ or complex sentences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'In the form of' introduces the kinds of change that follow.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Transformation of a sentence means (1) ___________ the words or forms of the sentence without changing (2) ___________ meaning. Such changes can be in the form (3) __________ changes from negative sentences into assertive, interrogative or exclamatory sentences and vice versa (4) ________ change in narration or change in voice or changes from simple to (5) _________ or complex sentences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Or' adds another alternative to the list of possible changes: change in narration, or in voice, and so on.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Transformation of a sentence means (1) ___________ the words or forms of the sentence without changing (2) ___________ meaning. Such changes can be in the form (3) __________ changes from negative sentences into assertive, interrogative or exclamatory sentences and vice versa (4) ________ change in narration or change in voice or changes from simple to (5) _________ or complex sentences.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: By structure, sentences are simple, compound or complex; after 'from simple to' the passage names the other two.

questions.text: Eight people are sitting in two parallel rows with 4 people each in such a way that there is equal distance between adjacent persons. In row I – A, B, C and D are seated and all of them are facing south. In row II – V, X, Y and Z are seated and all of them are facing north. B is the only neighbour of A and A sits exactly opposite Y. V sits at the extreme left end of their row and is exactly opposite C. D sits to the immediate left of C and exactly opposite X. Who sits at the immediate left of Y?
questions.explanation: Number the columns 1 to 4 from the west. Row II faces north, so V, at its left end, is in column 1, with C opposite; row I faces south, so its left is east and D is in column 2, opposite X. A, with B its only neighbour, is in column 4 (B in 3), opposite Y, so Z is in column 3: facing north, Y has Z on its immediate left.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 universe 2 unicorn 3 understood 4 unhappy 5 uniform
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: understood (3), unhappy (4), unicorn (2), uniform (5), universe (1). 'Und' comes before 'unh' and 'uni', and among the 'uni' words 'unic' comes before 'unif' and 'univ'.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some tapes are glue. Some glue are paints. All paints are computers. Conclusions: I. Some tapes are paints. II. All glue are paints. III. Some glue are computers.
questions.explanation: Nothing links the tapes to the paints, so I does not follow, and only some glue are paints, so II does not follow. The glue that are paints are computers, as all paints are, so some glue are computers (III).

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? BSWG, CTXE, DUYC, ?, FWAY
questions.explanation: The first three letters move one place forward from cluster to cluster and the last moves two back: B, C, D, E, F; S, T, U, V, W; W, X, Y, Z, A; G, E, C, A, Y. The missing cluster is EVZA.

questions.text: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 63, 60, 66, 57, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are −3, +6, −9 and +12: 57 + 12 = 69.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. KBT : PEU :: UQA : ZTB :: FJR : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +5, +3, +1: KBT → PEU and UQA → ZTB. So FJR → KMS.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 112 - 14 ÷ 40 + 4 × 18 = 40
questions.explanation: After interchanging ÷ and −: 112 ÷ 14 − 40 + 4 × 18 = 8 − 40 + 72 = 40.

questions.text: In a code language, ‘our son’s car’ is coded as ‘fu da be’, ‘son’s birthday today’ is coded as ‘la fu ja’, ‘today our match’ is coded as ‘he da la’. What is the code for the words ‘car match’?
questions.explanation: 'Son's' is in the first two phrases, so it is 'fu'; 'our' is in the first and third, so 'da'; 'today' is in the second and third, so 'la'. That leaves 'be' for 'car' and 'he' for 'match'.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 1, 5, 17, 53, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is three times the one before plus 2: 1 × 3 + 2 = 5, 5 × 3 + 2 = 17, 17 × 3 + 2 = 53 and 53 × 3 + 2 = 161.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 45 * 15 * 13 * 52 * 26 * 37
A @ B means ‘A is the husband of B’. A & B means ‘A is the mother of B’. A # B means ‘A is the daughter of B’. A % B means ‘A is the sibling of B’. If R # P @ W % F & K, then how is R related to K?
questions.explanation: R is the daughter of P, P is the husband of W, W is the sibling of F and F is the mother of K. So W, P's wife, is R's mother and the sister of K's mother: R is K's mother's sister's daughter.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (40, 175, 15); (30, 133, 11)
questions.explanation: In each set the second number is 7 times the difference of the other two: 7 × (40 − 15) = 175 and 7 × (30 − 11) = 133. Likewise 7 × (25 − 12) = 91.

questions.text: Six people A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre. E is sitting second to the right of B. F is the immediate neighbour of B and A. D is sitting second to the left of F. Who is sitting to the immediate right of C?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, each person's right runs anticlockwise. F sits between B and A; if F were on B's right, A would take E's seat, second to B's right, so clockwise the order is B, F, A, D (second to F's left), E, C. C has E on its immediate right.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘PEOPLE’ is written as ‘QEOQME’ and ‘MONKEY’ is written as ‘NOOLEZ’. How will ‘SILVER’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each consonant moves one letter forward and each vowel stays: PEOPLE → QEOQME and MONKEY → NOOLEZ (Y counted as a consonant). So SILVER → TIMWES.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? ZLJI, XJHG, VHFE, ?, RDBA
questions.explanation: Each letter moves two places back from one cluster to the next: Z, X, V, T, R; L, J, H, F, D; J, H, F, D, B; I, G, E, C, A. The missing cluster is TFDC.

questions.text: Who among the following was the court poet of Harshavardhana and the author of ‘Harshacharita’?
questions.explanation: Banabhatta, the court poet of Harshavardhana in the 7th century, wrote the 'Harshacharita', an account of the king's life, and the prose romance 'Kadambari'.

questions.text: Who was recognized as the Global Peace Ambassador at the India International Conclave 2022?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Babita Singh; press reports of April 2022 say she was named Global Peace Ambassador at the India International Conclave 2022 in New Delhi.

questions.text: How many points advantage must a freestyle wrestler must have against his/ her opponent for the bout to be declared over?
questions.explanation: In freestyle wrestling a bout ends by technical superiority when one wrestler leads by 10 points; in Greco-Roman wrestling the margin is 8.

questions.text: In India Green Revolution was led by :
questions.explanation: M.S. Swaminathan led the Green Revolution in India in the 1960s, bringing in high-yielding varieties of wheat and rice. Norman Borlaug, whose semi-dwarf wheat from Mexico India adopted, is credited with the Green Revolution worldwide.

questions.text: Which of the following is known as the Flying Sikh of India?
questions.explanation: Milkha Singh, the sprinter who came fourth in the 400 m at the 1960 Rome Olympics, was known as 'the Flying Sikh'.

questions.text: Skill India Mission was launched under the flagship of______________.
options: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
questions.explanation: The Skill India Mission, launched on 15 July 2015, is run by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.

questions.text: The Sattriya Dance in Assam is inspired by ________.
questions.explanation: Sattriya was created by the Vaishnava saint Srimanta Sankardev as part of the Bhakti movement in Assam, and kept alive in the sattras (monasteries).

questions.text: What is the atomic mass of Nitrogen?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen, atomic number 7, has an atomic mass of about 14 u: its common isotope has 7 protons and 7 neutrons.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In 1866, who among the following founded the East India Association in London?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji founded the East India Association in London in 1866 to put Indian views and grievances before the British public.

questions.text: Rukmini Devi Arundale won various accolades in which dance form?
questions.explanation: Rukmini Devi Arundale revived Bharatanatyam and founded the Kalakshetra academy at Adyar, Chennai, in 1936; she received the Padma Bhushan in 1956.

questions.text: Which article of the Indian Constitution states that India is a ‘Union of States'?
questions.explanation: Article 1(1) reads 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States'.

questions.text: Pick the odd one out. (Hint: farm processes)
questions.explanation: Ploughing, sowing and spraying (crops with pesticides or fertilisers) are steps in growing a crop; eating is not a farm process.

questions.text: Under article 100(3) of the Constitution of India, the quorum to constitute a sitting of either House of Parliament is ____________ of the total number of Members of the House.
questions.explanation: Article 100(3) fixes the quorum of either House at one-tenth of its total number of members.

questions.text: Which of the following is a symptom of bacterial infection?
questions.explanation: Fever is the body's common response to a bacterial infection. Cardiac arrest and heart attack are heart conditions, and a fracture is a broken bone.

questions.text: The total surface area of a cube whose side is 0.75 cm is:
questions.explanation: Total surface area = 6a² = 6 × 0.75² = 6 × 0.5625 = 3.375 cm².

questions.text: The compound interest, compounded annually, on Rs.30,000 at 9% per annum is Rs.5,643. The time period (in years) is:
After the successive discounts of 10% and 12% on the marked price of an item, it is sold for Rs.9,504, then the marked price is ________.
questions.explanation: The price paid is 0.9 × 0.88 = 0.792 of the marked price, so the marked price is 9,504/0.792 = ₹12,000.

questions.text: A vendor buys 20 apples for Rs.300 and sells them at 15 for Rs.300. How many apples should be bought and sold to earn a profit of Rs.300?
questions.explanation: Each apple costs 300/20 = ₹15 and sells for 300/15 = ₹20, a profit of ₹5 each, so a profit of ₹300 needs 300/5 = 60 apples.

questions.text: A scooter's value was reduced by 20 percent and is now worth Rs. 72000. What was its original price?
questions.explanation: 80% of the original price is ₹72,000, so the price was 72,000/0.8 = ₹90,000.

questions.text: The score of the eleven players of a cricket team is as follows. 12, 9, 52, 34, 30, 22, 0, 56, 16, 27 and 72. Find the average score of the team.
questions.explanation: The eleven scores add up to 330, and 330/11 = 30.

questions.text: Mohan and Sohan are going from same place at 8 km/h and 9 km/h respectively. If Mohan and Sohan are going in the same direction, then what is the distance between Mohan and Sohan after 4.5 h?
questions.explanation: Going the same way, they draw apart at 9 − 8 = 1 km/h, so after 4.5 h they are 4.5 km apart.

questions.text: Find the fourth proportional to 7, 4 and 7.

Kapil, Mohan, and Raju can do a piece of work separately in 18, 36, and 54 days. They started the work together but Mohan left the work 8 days before the completion of work and Raju left the work 6 days before the completion of the work. Find the (approximate) time in which the work is completed.
questions.explanation: If the work takes T days, Kapil works T days, Mohan T − 8 and Raju T − 6: T/18 + (T − 8)/36 + (T − 6)/54 = 1. Multiplying by 108: 6T + 3T − 24 + 2T − 12 = 108, so 11T = 144 and T ≈ 13 days.

questions.text: Find the ratio in which rice at Rs.120 per kg is mixed with rice at Rs.155 per kg to get a mixture worth Rs.135 a kg.
questions.explanation: By alligation the ratio is (155 − 135) : (135 − 120) = 20 : 15 = 4 : 3.

questions.text: Amol raised the price of their products by 20 percent. How much discount should they give so as to sell the products on no gain no loss basis?
questions.explanation: A price raised to 120 must come back to 100, a discount of 20/120 = 1/6 of the new price, that is 50/3 percent.

questions.text: The HCF of two numbers is 6 and their LCM is 253080. If one of the numbers is 4218, what is the second number?
questions.explanation: The product of the two numbers equals HCF × LCM: 6 × 253080/4218 = 1518480/4218 = 360.

questions.text: Ramesh and Naresh start running on a circular track of length 1920 metres from the same point simultaneously in the same direction with speed of 40 m/sec and 64 m/sec. After how much time from the start will they meet for the first time anywhere on the track?
questions.explanation: The faster runner gains 64 − 40 = 24 m a second and first catches up when he has gained a full lap: 1920/24 = 80 seconds.

questions.text: The highest common factor and the least common multiple of 432, 648 and 576 are ________ and ________, respectively.
By selling a computer for Rs.26,000, a man gains 4%. If he sells the computer for Rs.19,000, then his loss will be:
Samreen and Garima completed a piece of work together in 8 days. If Samreen can complete the same work in 10 days working independently, in how many days will Garima complete the same work alone?
questions.explanation: Garima does 1/8 − 1/10 = 1/40 of the work a day, so alone she takes 40 days.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Face the music
options: Listening to melodies from music albums
To face the unpleasant consequences of one's actions
questions.explanation: To 'face the music' is to accept the unpleasant consequences of what one has done.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'tendency', ending in '-ency'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Queer
questions.explanation: 'Queer' in its older sense means odd or unusual: 'strange'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. Some passengers “misplaced their luggages” before boarding the train.
questions.explanation: 'Luggage' is an uncountable noun and has no plural: 'Some passengers misplaced their luggage before boarding the train.'

questions.text: Fill in the blanks with the correct homophone. ____________ of anything is destructive in nature.
questions.explanation: An 'excess' (too much) of anything is harmful. 'Access' (a way in) sounds alike, and 'axes' and 'axis' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Land with unoccupied possession “is pretending to be” more valuable.
questions.explanation: 'Is likely to be' (will probably be) suits the singular subject 'land'; 'are likely to be' needs a plural subject, and land cannot 'pretend'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in simple past tense. A. Arun knew the concepts of geometry. B. Arun had been knowing the concepts of geometry. C. Arun had known the concepts of geometry. D. Arun was knowing the concepts of geometry.
questions.explanation: The simple past is the plain past form of the verb: 'Arun knew'. B is in the past perfect continuous, C in the past perfect and D in the past continuous.

questions.text: Select the correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. She is married “with a doctor”.
questions.explanation: One is married 'to' a person, not 'with' one: 'She is married to a doctor.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. As a boy, Charles was a “boor” who bullied other kids in his neighbourhood.
questions.explanation: A 'boor' is a rude, ill-mannered person; the opposite is a 'gentleman', a courteous, well-mannered man. 'Creep', 'blighter' and 'scum' are all terms of contempt.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Competent
questions.explanation: 'Competent' means having the skill or ability needed: 'capable'. 'Unfit' and 'unskilled' are its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Royal road
questions.explanation: A 'royal road' is an easy way to reach a goal, as in 'There is no royal road to learning': achieving something without trouble.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Perplex
questions.explanation: To 'perplex' is to puzzle or make something confusing; the opposite is to 'simplify'. 'Complex' is close in meaning, and 'classify' is unrelated.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks and make the sentence meaningful. She hurt her ________ and _______.
questions.explanation: The 'heel' (the back of the foot) and the 'toe' are parts of the foot. 'Heal' (to cure) and 'tow' (to pull) sound the same but mean something else.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in the bracket to fill in the blank. My stomach is so _______ (empty) I couldn't possibly eat more.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'empty' that suits a stomach that can take no more is 'overfed'. 'Teeming' means swarming with living things, 'flush' level or well supplied with money, and 'drained' is close to 'empty'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The oldest hub of carpet weaving in India is Mirzapur in Bhadohi district of Uttar Pradesh. The Ganga (1)________ past this town with its ghats, ancient temples and waterfalls. The genesis of carpet making in Mirzapur can be (2)_________ to the Mughal emperor, Akbar, in the 16th century. A (3)________ of Persian carpet weavers, it is said, on its way to the Mughal court was (4)_______ and injured by dacoits on the Grand Trunk Road. The weavers were rescued and given shelter by local villagers. The master weaver of the group decided to settle down here and share his skills with his (5)_______. That is how the renowned carpet industry of Mirzapur took root.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 1.
questions.explanation: A river 'flows' past a town.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The oldest hub of carpet weaving in India is Mirzapur in Bhadohi district of Uttar Pradesh. The Ganga (1)________ past this town with its ghats, ancient temples and waterfalls. The genesis of carpet making in Mirzapur can be (2)_________ to the Mughal emperor, Akbar, in the 16th century. A (3)________ of Persian carpet weavers, it is said, on its way to the Mughal court was (4)_______ and injured by dacoits on the Grand Trunk Road. The weavers were rescued and given shelter by local villagers. The master weaver of the group decided to settle down here and share his skills with his (5)_______. That is how the renowned carpet industry of Mirzapur took root.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 2.
questions.explanation: To 'trace' something to a source is to find where it began: carpet making in Mirzapur goes back to Akbar's time.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The oldest hub of carpet weaving in India is Mirzapur in Bhadohi district of Uttar Pradesh. The Ganga (1)________ past this town with its ghats, ancient temples and waterfalls. The genesis of carpet making in Mirzapur can be (2)_________ to the Mughal emperor, Akbar, in the 16th century. A (3)________ of Persian carpet weavers, it is said, on its way to the Mughal court was (4)_______ and injured by dacoits on the Grand Trunk Road. The weavers were rescued and given shelter by local villagers. The master weaver of the group decided to settle down here and share his skills with his (5)_______. That is how the renowned carpet industry of Mirzapur took root.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 3.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'caravan', a company of travellers journeying together, which suits a group of weavers 'on its way to the Mughal court' and attacked on the road. 'Band' (a group of people) is possible but lacks the sense of travelling, and 'crowd' and 'army' do not fit.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The oldest hub of carpet weaving in India is Mirzapur in Bhadohi district of Uttar Pradesh. The Ganga (1)________ past this town with its ghats, ancient temples and waterfalls. The genesis of carpet making in Mirzapur can be (2)_________ to the Mughal emperor, Akbar, in the 16th century. A (3)________ of Persian carpet weavers, it is said, on its way to the Mughal court was (4)_______ and injured by dacoits on the Grand Trunk Road. The weavers were rescued and given shelter by local villagers. The master weaver of the group decided to settle down here and share his skills with his (5)_______. That is how the renowned carpet industry of Mirzapur took root.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 4.
questions.explanation: To 'waylay' people is to stop and attack them on their way, as the dacoits did on the Grand Trunk Road.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The oldest hub of carpet weaving in India is Mirzapur in Bhadohi district of Uttar Pradesh. The Ganga (1)________ past this town with its ghats, ancient temples and waterfalls. The genesis of carpet making in Mirzapur can be (2)_________ to the Mughal emperor, Akbar, in the 16th century. A (3)________ of Persian carpet weavers, it is said, on its way to the Mughal court was (4)_______ and injured by dacoits on the Grand Trunk Road. The weavers were rescued and given shelter by local villagers. The master weaver of the group decided to settle down here and share his skills with his (5)_______. That is how the renowned carpet industry of Mirzapur took root.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 5.
questions.explanation: The villagers who rescued and sheltered the weavers were their 'benefactors' (helpers); the master weaver repaid them by sharing his skills.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 riddle 2 river 3 rightful 4 ring 5 risk
questions.explanation: All five begin 'ri', so the third letters decide: riddle (d), rightful (g), ring (n), risk (s), river (v): 1, 3, 4, 5, 2.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘EXAM’ is written as ‘625214’ and ‘TEST’ is written as ‘2162021’. How will ‘ASSESSMENT’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as its place in the alphabet plus one: EXAM → 6, 25, 2, 14 and TEST → 21, 6, 20, 21. So ASSESSMENT → 2, 20, 20, 6, 20, 20, 14, 6, 15, 21: 22020620201461521.

questions.text: Six family members Viraaj, Deepu, Noor, Prince, Suman and Taran are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Viraaj is sitting to the immediate right of Noor. Prince is an immediate neighbour of both Viraaj and Deepu. Suman is sitting third to the right of Viraaj. Noor is sitting second to the left of Prince. Who is the immediate neighbour of Deepu and Viraaj?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, right is anticlockwise. Viraaj is on Noor's right, and Noor, second to the left of Prince, puts Prince next to Viraaj on the side away from Noor, with Deepu beyond Prince. Suman, third to the right of Viraaj, sits opposite him, and Taran between Suman and Noor. So Prince sits between Deepu and Viraaj.

questions.text: In a certain code language, FATHER is written as ‘IFWMHW’, and SISTER is written as ‘VNVYHW’. How will ‘UNCLE’ be written in the same code language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +3 and +5 in turn: FATHER → IFWMHW and SISTER → VNVYHW. So UNCLE → X S F Q H: XSFQH.

questions.text: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Brianna is sitting second to the right of Mark. Felix is sitting second to the left of Mark. Ann is the immediate neighbour of Brianna and Felix. James is sitting third to the left of Brianna. Afreen is sitting second to the right of James. Who is sitting between Afreen and Ann?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, left is clockwise. Brianna and Felix sit second to the right and second to the left of Mark, with Ann between them, opposite Mark. James, third to the left of Brianna, is next to Mark on Felix's side, and Afreen, second to the right of James, takes the seat between Mark and Brianna. Clockwise: Mark, James, Felix, Ann, Brianna, Afreen, so Brianna sits between Afreen and Ann.

questions.text: Which two numbers(not digits) should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct? 56 ÷ 16 × 8 + 45 × 13 = 697
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 24 – 36 × 5 + 108 ÷ 18 = 18
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark and complete the given number series? 125, 88, 63, 46, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are −37, −25 and −17, which shrink by 12 and then 8; shrinking next by 4, the difference is −13: 46 − 13 = 33.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. GSLC, AMOF, UGRI, ? , IUXO
questions.explanation: The first two letters move back 6 (G, A, U, O, I and S, M, G, A, U, wrapping round after A) and the last two forward 3 (L, O, R, U, X and C, F, I, L, O). The missing cluster is OAUL.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? ?, LSEO, NRDN, PQCM, RPBL
questions.explanation: From term to term the first letter moves +2 (J, L, N, P, R) and the other three −1 (T, S, R, Q, P; F, E, D, C, B; P, O, N, M, L). So the first term is JTFP.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’, ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the father of B’ and ‘A x B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’. How is R related to S if Q + R – P x N – S?
questions.explanation: Q + R: Q is R's sister; R – P: R is P's father; P x N: P is N's brother, so N is also R's child; N – S: N is S's father. So R is S's father's father.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: All mobiles are computers. Some computers are furniture. Some furniture are tables. Conclusions: I. Some tables are computers. II. Some mobiles are furniture.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: Some computers are furniture and some furniture are tables, but the tables may all lie outside the computers, so I does not follow; the computers that are furniture need not include any mobiles, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. TIDE: RRAU :: REST : PVPF :: GAME : ?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves back 2 and the third back 3; the second becomes its opposite letter (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on) and the fourth the letter before its opposite: TIDE → RRAU and REST → PVPF. So GAME → E Z J U: EZJU.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Education : Teacher :: Treatment : ?
questions.explanation: A teacher gives education, as a doctor gives treatment.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 5, 31, 161, 811, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is five times the one before plus 6: 5 × 5 + 6 = 31, 31 × 5 + 6 = 161 and 161 × 5 + 6 = 811, so 811 × 5 + 6 = 4061.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed) (25, 280, 45) (18, 192, 30)
questions.explanation: The middle number is four times the sum of the other two: (25 + 45) × 4 = 280 and (18 + 30) × 4 = 192. Likewise (12 + 25) × 4 = 148; the other sets would need 144, 152 and 268.

questions.text: "to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so" is stated under______.
questions.explanation: Article 51A(d), one of the Fundamental Duties added by the 42nd Amendment (1976), asks every citizen to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.

questions.text: On the banks of which river was the war between Harshavardhana and Pulakeshin II fought?
questions.explanation: The Chalukya king Pulakeshin II stopped Harshavardhana's advance into the Deccan in a battle on the banks of the Narmada, recorded in the Aihole inscription.

questions.text: In shot put, the shot which is a metal ball weighs how many kg for men and women?
questions.explanation: The men's shot weighs 7.26 kg (16 lb) and the women's 4 kg.

questions.text: How many pathways are constructed as independently organized conducting tubes in plants?
questions.explanation: Plants have two such pathways: the xylem, which carries water and minerals up from the roots, and the phloem, which carries the products of photosynthesis from the leaves to other parts of the plant.

questions.text: The tenure of the UPSC members is .
options: 6 years or age of 65 whichever is earlier
questions.explanation: Under Article 316(2), a member of the UPSC holds office for six years or until the age of 65, whichever comes first.

questions.text: The ultimate goal of Mission Indradhanush is to ensure full immunization with all available vaccines for children up to _________ years of age.
questions.explanation: Mission Indradhanush, launched in December 2014, aims at full immunisation with all available vaccines for children up to two years of age and for pregnant women.

questions.text: What was the term of 10th Five Year Plan?
questions.explanation: The Tenth Five-Year Plan ran from 2002 to 2007; the Eleventh followed, from 2007 to 2012.

questions.text: Who among the following inaugurated 2-day PM Kisan Samman Sammelan of India in October 2022?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the two-day PM Kisan Samman Sammelan at the IARI campus, Pusa, New Delhi, on 17 October 2022, and released the twelfth instalment of PM-KISAN there.

questions.text: In India, in relation to Census, what is the full form of NPR?
questions.explanation: NPR is the National Population Register, a register of the usual residents of the country, prepared under the Citizenship Act, 1955 and its 2003 rules; it was first compiled in 2010 with the house-listing phase of Census 2011.

questions.text: Which sector runs nearly 60 percent of dispensaries in India?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the private sector. NCERT's Class 11 economics text on infrastructure notes that the private sector runs more than 70 per cent of India's hospitals and nearly 60 per cent of its dispensaries.

questions.text: Saga Dawa is primarily celebrated by which of the following communities of India in Sikkim?
questions.explanation: Saga Dawa, the holiest month of the Tibetan Buddhist calendar, is celebrated by Buddhists in Sikkim to mark the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and parinirvana.

questions.text: Microfinance is a _______ service.
questions.explanation: Microfinance is a financial service: small loans, savings, insurance and the like for low-income people who lack access to ordinary banking.

questions.text: Bihu is the popular dance form of which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Bihu, danced at the Bihu festivals, especially Rongali Bihu in April, is the folk dance of Assam.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) was founded at ______ in Delhi.
questions.explanation: The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association was founded at a meeting of revolutionaries in the ruins of Feroz Shah Kotla, Delhi, in September 1928, when Bhagat Singh and his comrades added 'Socialist' to the name of the older Hindustan Republican Association.

questions.text: Who is the new Managing Director of the National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) effective August 8, 2022?
questions.explanation: Rajkiran Rai G, MD and CEO of Union Bank of India until May 2022, took charge as Managing Director of NaBFID, the development finance institution for infrastructure, on 8 August 2022.

questions.text: In India, the Green Revolution increased the production of which of the following?
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution of the late 1960s, built on high-yielding seeds, fertilisers and irrigation, raised the output of food grains, above all wheat.

questions.text: Which among the following elements behaves like alkali metals as well as halogens in its properties?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen has one valence electron, like the alkali metals, and can lose it to form H⁺; like the halogens it is one electron short of a full shell, gains one to form H⁻ and exists as diatomic molecules.

questions.text: In which year the Asian Games were held for the second time in India?
questions.explanation: New Delhi hosted the first Asian Games in 1951 and the ninth, India's second, in 1982.

questions.text: What is used to measure the magnitude of an earthquake?
questions.explanation: The Richter scale, devised by Charles Richter in 1935, gives an earthquake's magnitude from the seismograph record. An anemometer measures wind speed and a gravimeter gravity.

questions.text: Who won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in Manipuri in 2018?
questions.explanation: Akham Lakshmi Devi received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 2018 for Manipuri dance; the awards were announced in July 2019.

questions.text: The ratio of two numbers is 4 : 5 and their HCF is 6. Their LCM is:
questions.explanation: The numbers are 4 × 6 = 24 and 5 × 6 = 30. As 4 and 5 have no common factor, the LCM is 4 × 5 × 6 = 120.

questions.text: A toy is bought for Rs.950 and sold at Rs.1140. Find the gain percentage.
Reeta can do a piece of work in 14 days and Geeta can do the same work in 21 days. How many days Reeta and Geeta take together to complete the same work?
questions.explanation: Together they do 1/14 + 1/21 = (3 + 2)/42 = 5/42 of the work a day, so they take 42/5 = 8.4 days.

questions.text: Find the greatest number which on dividing 1780 and 2452 leaves the remainder 4 in each case.
questions.explanation: The number must divide 1780 − 4 = 1776 and 2452 − 4 = 2448 exactly. 1776 = 48 × 37 and 2448 = 48 × 51, and 37 and 51 have no common factor, so the HCF is 48.

questions.text: The total surface area of a cuboid is 4200 cm² . If the length and breadth of the cuboid are 15 cm and16 cm, then find the height of the cuboid.

Sumati travelled from point A to point B at 475 m/min. The moment that Sumati reached point B, Rachna set off from point B, at a speed 1.6 times the speed at which Sumati travelled and reached point C. If the total distance covered from A to C through B was 45.6 km and the time taken from when Sumati started from point A to when Rachna reached point C was 75 minutes, what is the distance between A and B?
questions.explanation: Rachna's speed is 1.6 × 475 = 760 m/min, so with AB = d km, d/0.475 + (45.6 − d)/0.76 = 75 minutes. Multiplying by 3.8: 8d + 5(45.6 − d) = 285, so 3d = 285 − 228 = 57 and d = 19 km.

questions.text: In a golf club, 90% of members are men and the remaining are women. The average height of men is 170 cm and the average height of women is 165 cm. Find the average height of the club members.
A can do a piece of work in 18 days. B can do this work in 24 days. A started the work alone. After how many days should B join him, so that the work is finished in 15 days?
questions.explanation: A works all 15 days and does 15/18 = 5/6 of the work. B must do the other 1/6, which takes him 24/6 = 4 days, so he joins after 15 − 4 = 11 days.

questions.text: Find the distance covered by a car moving at a speed of 48 km/h for 3 hours 15 minutes.
questions.explanation: 3 hours 15 minutes is 3.25 hours, so the distance is 48 × 3.25 = 156 km.

questions.text: After giving a discount of 25 percent, selling price of an article becomes Rs. 9510. What is the marked price of the article?
questions.explanation: The selling price is 75% of the marked price, so the marked price is ₹9,510 ÷ 0.75 = ₹12,680.

questions.text: The average marks in geography exam of a class of 25 students are 64. If the marks of three students were misread as 44, 46 and 61 in lieu of the actual marks 54, 64 and 67 respectively, then find the correct average.
questions.explanation: The total read was 25 × 64 = 1600. The true marks add (54 + 64 + 67) − (44 + 46 + 61) = 185 − 151 = 34 more, so the correct average is 1634/25 = 65.36.

questions.text: What will be the difference in the compound interest if a sum of Rs.12,000 is compounded annually and half-yearly at an annual rate of 10% for a period of 2 years? Note :Round off the decimal to the nearest number.
questions.explanation: Annually: 12,000 × 1.1² = 14,520, so the CI is ₹2,520. Half-yearly, at 5% for 4 half-years: 12,000 × 1.05⁴ = 14,586.075, so the CI is ₹2,586.075. The difference, ₹66.075, rounds to ₹66.

questions.text: Teena spends 30% of her salary on food, 30% of the rest on fuel and saves the remaining Rs.4,900. What is Teena’s salary?
questions.explanation: After food 70% of the salary is left, and after fuel 70% of that, 49%. So 49% of the salary is ₹4,900 and the salary is ₹10,000.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. The company of friends made her feel ________ (cranky), as she was all alone in her apartment.
questions.explanation: 'Cranky' means irritable and bad-tempered; its opposite is 'cheerful', which fits a mood lifted by friends.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Fascinating
questions.explanation: 'Fascinating' means extremely interesting. 'Revolting' means disgusting and 'intimidating' frightening.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Symbolise
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'hide'. To symbolise is to represent or stand for something, bringing it to view through a sign; 'hide', to keep out of sight, is the only option that runs against that, though the two are not exact opposites. 'Link', 'slide' and 'align' are unrelated.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'frequent', with no 'k'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Silver tongue
options: Speaking with an eloquent expression to convince people
questions.explanation: A 'silver tongue' is a gift for eloquent, persuasive speech.

questions.text: The given sentence is divided into three segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'no error' as your answer. She have / left by the time / I reach home.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'she' cannot take 'have'; with 'by the time I reach home' the sense needs the future perfect: 'She will have left by the time I reach home.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Splendid
questions.explanation: 'Splendid' means magnificent or very impressive: 'spectacular'. 'Authentic' means genuine and 'enticing' attractive.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Public enemy number one
options: Someone who is the greatest threat to a group or community
questions.explanation: 'Public enemy number one' is the person or thing seen as the greatest threat to a group or community.

questions.text: Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully: Shakespeare was both a dramatist (better than) a poet.
questions.explanation: 'Both' pairs with 'and': 'Shakespeare was both a dramatist and a poet.' 'As well as' does not follow 'both'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I “am been working here” for the past ten years.
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and continues ('for the past ten years') takes the present perfect continuous: 'I have been working here for the past ten years.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Dignify
questions.explanation: To 'dignify' is to give honour or worth to something; to 'condemn' is to censure it as wrong, the reverse of honouring it. 'Adorn' (decorate) is close in sense to 'dignify'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homophone to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. These ornaments are “coated with gold”.
questions.explanation: To 'gild' is to coat with a thin layer of gold, so it is the word for the underlined words (the sentence would then read 'are gilded'). 'Guild', which sounds the same, is an association of craftsmen or merchants.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence to make it a meaningful sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. One must “not only have the ability to read voraciously but have” the necessary training in comprehending and remembering all the relevant details.
options: not only have the ability for read voraciously but also have
not only have the ability to read voraciously but also had
not only have the ability to read voraciously but also have
questions.explanation: 'Not only' pairs with 'but also': 'One must not only have the ability to read voraciously but also have the necessary training'. 'For read' and the past 'had' are wrong.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Scientists are able to quickly _________ the outbreak through a new immunisation.
questions.explanation: To 'quash' is to put an end to or suppress: the new immunisation lets scientists stamp out the outbreak quickly. One quenches thirst or a fire, and a quest is a search.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The ability to think clearly and calmly while addressing an 1. ______ is neither inborn nor difficult to develop. The presence of an audience should act as a stimulus and not as a 2. ______ to thought. Audience fright can be overcome through training and practice. Even great speakers 3. ______ stage fright and self-consciousness. Every speaker gets worked up and experiences strain, shock, and excitement before he or she begins to talk. But every speaker who is struggling to gain 4. ______ should remember that all meritorious public speaking is accompanied by a little 5. ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: A speaker addresses an 'audience', the word the next sentence takes up: 'The presence of an audience'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The ability to think clearly and calmly while addressing an 1. ______ is neither inborn nor difficult to develop. The presence of an audience should act as a stimulus and not as a 2. ______ to thought. Audience fright can be overcome through training and practice. Even great speakers 3. ______ stage fright and self-consciousness. Every speaker gets worked up and experiences strain, shock, and excitement before he or she begins to talk. But every speaker who is struggling to gain 4. ______ should remember that all meritorious public speaking is accompanied by a little 5. ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: The audience should act as a stimulus and not as a 'hindrance', an obstacle, to thought.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The ability to think clearly and calmly while addressing an 1. ______ is neither inborn nor difficult to develop. The presence of an audience should act as a stimulus and not as a 2. ______ to thought. Audience fright can be overcome through training and practice. Even great speakers 3. ______ stage fright and self-consciousness. Every speaker gets worked up and experiences strain, shock, and excitement before he or she begins to talk. But every speaker who is struggling to gain 4. ______ should remember that all meritorious public speaking is accompanied by a little 5. ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: Even great speakers 'experience', that is feel, stage fright and self-consciousness.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The ability to think clearly and calmly while addressing an 1. ______ is neither inborn nor difficult to develop. The presence of an audience should act as a stimulus and not as a 2. ______ to thought. Audience fright can be overcome through training and practice. But every speaker who is struggling to gain 4. ______ should remember that all meritorious public speaking is accompanied by a little 5. ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: A speaker fighting stage fright struggles to gain 'confidence'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The ability to think clearly and calmly while addressing an 1. ______ is neither inborn nor difficult to develop. The presence of an audience should act as a stimulus and not as a 2. ______ to thought. Audience fright can be overcome through training and practice. Even great speakers 3. ______ stage fright and self-consciousness. Every speaker gets worked up and experiences strain, shock, and excitement before he or she begins to talk. But every speaker who is struggling to gain 4. ______ should remember that all meritorious public speaking is accompanied by a little 5. ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: Good public speaking comes with a little 'nervousness', the stage fright the passage is about.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘heart games’ is coded as ‘alarm coffee’, ‘wrap’ is coded as ‘bottle’, and ‘wrap games’ is coded as ‘bottle coffee’. What is the code word for ‘heart’?
questions.explanation: 'Games' is common to 'heart games' and 'wrap games', and 'coffee' to their codes, so games = coffee. That leaves heart = alarm (and wrap = bottle, as given).

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 15 : 4 :: 21 : 6 :: 42 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is a third of the first, less 1: 15/3 − 1 = 4 and 21/3 − 1 = 6. So 42/3 − 1 = 13.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Argentina : Peso :: Japan : ?
questions.explanation: The peso is Argentina's currency, as the yen is Japan's.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? CJEZ, ?, WFYV, TDVT, QBSR
questions.explanation: The first and third letters each move back 3 (C, Z, W, T, Q; E, B, Y, V, S) and the second and fourth back 2 (J, H, F, D, B; Z, X, V, T, R), wrapping round after A. The missing cluster is ZHBX.

questions.text: Which of the numbers(not digits) should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct? 108 ÷ 9 × 16 + 12 - 27 = 126
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 44 - 96 × 4 ÷ 3 + 58 = 30
In a certain code language, 'ARGUE’ is written as '22620926' and 'BEACH' is written as '1924262225'.How will 'ACCEL' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and each letter written as its place counted from Z (A = 26, B = 25 and so on): ARGUE → E U G R A → 22 6 20 9 26 and BEACH → H C A E B → 19 24 26 22 25. So ACCEL → L E C C A → 15 22 24 24 26: 1522242426.

questions.text: Six friends M, N, O, P, Q and R are sitting in a straight row facing north. Exactly three people are sitting to the left of N. O is sitting immediately to the right of N. M and P are immediate neighbours of Q such that M is the fourth to the left of O. Where is R seated?
options: Second to the left of N
Third to the right of P
Third to the left of O
questions.explanation: With three people to its left, N is 4th from the left and O, on its right, 5th. M, fourth to the left of O, is 1st, so Q, with M and P as neighbours, is 2nd and P 3rd. That leaves R 6th: M, Q, P, N, O, R, so R is third to the right of P.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? ACEG, BDFH, ? , DFHJ, EGIK
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place on from cluster to cluster (A, B, C, D, E; C, D, E, F, G and so on), so after BDFH comes CEGI.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 power 2 pour 3 powder 4 pointed 5 polite
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: pointed (4), polite (5), pour (2), powder (3), power (1). 'Poi' comes before 'pol', 'pou' and 'pow', and 'powd' before 'powe'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Goldsmith : Ornaments :: Sculptor : ?
questions.explanation: A goldsmith makes ornaments, as a sculptor makes a bust; stone is the sculptor's material, not what he makes.

questions.text: Six people J, K, L, M, N and O are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. J sits second to the right of N. O is an immediate neighbour of M and J. K sits second to the left of L. Who sits to the immediate right of O?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left is clockwise. J is two seats anticlockwise of N, with O next to J and M next to O, so K, second to the left of L, must sit between N and M and L between J and N: clockwise N, K, M, O, J, L. The seat to O's right (anticlockwise) is M's.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by two conclusions. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All tables are woods. All woods are paints. No paint is a steel. Conclusions: 1. All steels can be woods. 2. Some paints are steels.
questions.explanation: All tables are woods and all woods are paints, but no paint is a steel, so no wood is a steel either: steels cannot be woods (1 does not follow), and 2 contradicts the third statement.

questions.text: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 1, 5, ?, 25, 41, 61
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 16, 23, 34, 47, 64, ? , 106
questions.explanation: The differences are the successive primes 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23: 64 + 19 = 83, and 83 + 23 = 106.

questions.text: ‘A + B’ means ‘B is the father of A’; ‘A – B’ means ‘B is the mother of A’; ‘A @ B’ means ‘B is the brother of A’; ‘A * B’ means ‘B is the son of A’; If A * B + C @ D – E, then how is E related to A?
questions.explanation: A * B: B is A's son. B + C: C is B's father, so A is B's mother and C's wife. C @ D: D is C's brother, and D – E: E is D's mother, so C's too. E is A's husband's mother: her mother-in-law.

questions.text: An instrument that can detect the presence of a current in a circuit is known as ______.
questions.explanation: An ammeter, connected in series, measures the current in a circuit and so shows whether one flows. An odometer measures distance travelled, a speedometer speed and a hygrometer humidity.

questions.text: Who has sworn in as 50th Chief Justice of India?
questions.explanation: Justice D Y Chandrachud was sworn in as the 50th Chief Justice of India on 9 November 2022, succeeding U U Lalit, the 49th.

questions.text: Radha Sridhar won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2018 in ______.
questions.explanation: Radha Sridhar received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 2018 (announced in July 2019) for Bharatanatyam.

questions.text: Powers, authority and responsibilities of Municipalities are dealt under which schedule?
questions.explanation: The Twelfth Schedule, added by the 74th Amendment (1992), lists 18 matters for municipalities under Article 243W; the Eleventh Schedule lists those of panchayats.

questions.text: Which political leader quit Indian National Congress following differences with party leadership in May 2022?
questions.explanation: Kapil Sibal resigned from the Congress in May 2022 and filed his Rajya Sabha nomination from Uttar Pradesh as an independent backed by the Samajwadi Party.

questions.text: How many types of Bihu festival are celebrated in Assam?
questions.explanation: Assam celebrates three Bihus: Bohag (Rongali) Bihu in April, Kati (Kongali) Bihu in October and Magh (Bhogali) Bihu in January.

questions.text: The concepts of Dhamma was popularized by which of the following Mauryan kings?
