questions.explanation: After the Kalinga war Ashoka spread his dhamma, a code of moral conduct, through his rock and pillar edicts and officers called dhamma-mahamattas.

questions.text: The Dronacharya Sports Award is given to the________.
questions.explanation: The Dronacharya Award honours coaches whose trainees have achieved outstanding results in international sport.

questions.text: Planning Commission was established under ________on March 15, 1950
questions.explanation: The Planning Commission was set up on 15 March 1950 by a resolution of the Government of India, with Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru as its first chairman.

questions.text: Availability of _______ during winter months due to the western temperate cyclones helps in the success of rabi crops.
questions.explanation: Western disturbances, temperate cyclones from the Mediterranean region, bring winter rain (and snow in the hills) to north-west India, which helps wheat and the other rabi crops.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: On September 1948 the Indian army intervened and took control of which princely state?
questions.explanation: In 'Operation Polo', the police action of 13-18 September 1948, the Indian Army ended the Nizam's resistance, and Hyderabad joined India.

questions.text: Which Indian organisation is responsible for collecting data on poverty in the country?
options: Office of Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India
questions.explanation: Poverty in India has been estimated from the household consumer expenditure surveys of the National Sample Survey Organisation (since 2019 part of the National Statistical Office), which collects the data; the Planning Commission worked out the official estimates from them.

questions.text: The council of ministers is collectively responsible to the ________.
questions.explanation: Article 75(3) makes the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the House of the People, the Lok Sabha.

questions.text: The classical text, Hasthalakshana Deepika, is associated with which Indian classical dance form?
questions.explanation: Hastalakshana Deepika is the Kerala text on hand gestures (mudras) that Kathakali follows; its 24 basic mudras are the root of the dance's gesture language.

questions.text: Government goods and services that aren't sold directly to the consumers, for example defence goods, roads are categorised under:
questions.explanation: Public goods, such as defence and roads, are provided by the government for everyone's use rather than sold to individual buyers, and one person's use does not keep another from using them.

questions.text: What is an area of dry land that lies on the leeward side of a mountain called?
questions.explanation: Moist winds drop their rain on the windward slope, so the sheltered leeward side gets little rain and is called a rain-shadow area.

questions.text: The national level cricket championship, Ranji Trophy, began in __________.
questions.explanation: The Ranji Trophy, named after K S Ranjitsinhji, began in the 1934-35 season; Bombay won the first final.

questions.text: The National Food and Security Act of 2013 (NFSA2013) provides subsidised food grains to _______ of India's rural population.
questions.explanation: The National Food Security Act, 2013 covers up to 75% of the rural population and up to 50% of the urban population for subsidised food grains under the Targeted Public Distribution System.

questions.text: Select the second step of decomposition.
questions.explanation: Decomposition goes through fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification and mineralisation, so leaching, in which water-soluble nutrients seep down into the soil, is the second step.

questions.text: Any person in-charge of or employed in a child care institution, who subjects a child to corporal punishment shall be liable under__________.
questions.explanation: Section 82 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 makes it an offence for a person in charge of or employed in a child care institution to subject a child to corporal punishment.

questions.text: The LCM of 192 and 480 is 60 more than the 100 times of X. What is the value of X?
Divide Rs.500 among A, B, C and D so that A and B together get thrice as much as C and D together, B gets 4 times what C gets and C gets 1.5 times as much as D. The value of B’s share is:
questions.explanation: A + B = 3(C + D) and the total is ₹500, so C + D = ₹125. With C = 1.5D, 2.5D = 125, so D = ₹50, C = ₹75 and B = 4 × 75 = ₹300.

questions.text: A’s speed is 30% more than that of B. If A and B run a race on a 117 m length race, what part of the length of the race should A give B as a head start, so that the race ends in a dead heat?
questions.explanation: The speeds are in the ratio 13 : 10, so while A runs 117 m, B runs 90 m. B needs a start of 117 − 90 = 27 m.

questions.text: A certain sum of money fetches simple interest of Rs.4,016.25 at the rate of 7% per annum in 5 years. What is the sum?
A person drives for 320 kms in 8 hours, cycles for 40 kms in 5 hours and then walks for 40 kms in 7 hours. Find the average speed of the driver.
Two years ago, the population of a town was 66000. The population increased by 5% in the first year and decreased by 5% in the second year. Find the present population of the town.
questions.explanation: 66,000 × 1.05 = 69,300 after the first year, and 69,300 × 0.95 = 65,835 after the second.

questions.text: The radius of the base of a conical vessel is 5 cm and its height is 24 cm. The vessel is full of water. This water is poured into a cylindrical vessel having the base radius 10 cm. The depth of the water in the cylindrical vessel is:
questions.explanation: The cone holds (1/3)π × 5² × 24 = 200π cm³, so in the cylinder π × 10² × h = 200π and h = 2 cm.

questions.text: Three partners A, B and C started a business and decided to share the profit in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5, respectively. If the share of B is Rs.7,50,000, then calculate the total profit.
questions.explanation: B's 3 parts of 10 are ₹7,50,000, so one part is ₹2,50,000 and the total profit ₹25,00,000.

questions.text: P can do as much work as Q and R together can do. P and Q can together do a piece of work in 8 hours and 24 minutes and R can do it in 42 hours. Find the time (in hours) that Q needs to do the work alone.
questions.explanation: 8 hours 24 minutes is 42/5 hours, so P and Q do 5/42 of the work an hour and R does 1/42. As P = Q + R, 2Q + 1/42 = 5/42, so Q = 2/42 = 1/21 of the work an hour: 21 hours.

questions.text: Salary of a person is first decreased by 40 percent and then increased by 40 percent. What will be the percentage decrease in the salary ?
questions.explanation: 0.6 × 1.4 = 0.84 of the salary is left, a decrease of 16%.

questions.text: Find the total surface area of a cylinder whose height is 8.5 mm and the base diameter is 10 mm.
questions.explanation: With radius 5 mm and height 8.5 mm, the total surface area is 2πr(r + h) = 2π × 5 × 13.5 = 135π mm².

questions.text: Excluding the stoppages, the speed of a truck is 90 km/h and including the stoppages, the speed of the truck is 36 km/h in a journey. For how many minutes does the truck stop per hour?
questions.explanation: Stopping costs the truck 90 − 36 = 54 km of running an hour, which at 90 km/h takes 54/90 × 60 = 36 minutes.

questions.text: A dealer offers 20% discount on all dolls. He offers a further discount of 5% on the reduced price to those customers who pay in cash. How much will a customer pay in cash for a doll worth Rs.1,800?
In a storm 243 trees were left standing out of 300 trees in a garden. What is the percentage decrease in number of trees?
If 6 men or 8 women can reap a field in 21.5 days. How long will 14 men and 10 women take to reap it?
questions.explanation: 6 men do as much as 8 women, so a woman does 3/4 of a man's work, and 14 men and 10 women equal 14 + 7.5 = 21.5 men. The field takes 6 × 21.5 = 129 man-days: 129/21.5 = 6 days.

questions.text: The average of the cube of the first 4 natural numbers is:
Rita buys a toy car for Rs.12,000 and sells it for Rs.14,500. What is her gain percent? (rounded off to two digits after decimal)
The sentence given below has one misspelt word. Spot the INCORRECTLY spelt word and select its correct spelling. Too much bureacracy suppresses creativity.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'bureaucracy', from 'bureau' and '-cracy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The mob “broke up” the norms of the country.
questions.explanation: To 'violate' norms is to break them; 'broke up' means came apart or ended, which does not fit. 'Invade' and 'disturb' are not past tense, and norms are not 'damaged'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The skeleton of an unknown person has been hanging on the tree __________ last Wednesday.
questions.explanation: 'Since' gives the point in time from which an action has continued: 'has been hanging ... since last Wednesday'. 'For' needs a length of time, such as 'for a week'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Hesitation
questions.explanation: 'Hesitation' is a pause from doubt or unwillingness, so 'reluctance' is closest. 'Readiness' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the correct word for the blanks in the given sentence. There is a provision of _________ delivery in every courier service whereas a child can __________ his feelings at the age of 2 years or so.
questions.explanation: 'Express' fits both blanks: 'express delivery' is fast delivery, and to 'express' feelings is to show them in words or actions.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. The second wave of the pandemic left everyone “in the doldrums”.
questions.explanation: To be 'in the doldrums' is to be in low spirits, or in a state where nothing moves forward.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Dream
questions.explanation: A 'dream' is something imagined; its opposite is 'reality'. 'Delusion', 'fancy' and 'imagination' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Colossal
questions.explanation: 'Colossal' means extremely large: 'immense'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. His ancestors are “native” to this place.
questions.explanation: 'Native' means belonging to a place by birth; its opposite is 'foreign'. 'Innate' means inborn, close to 'native'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Where the shoe pinches
questions.explanation: 'Where the shoe pinches' is where the real difficulty or trouble lies.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. She couldn’t “get over with Thomas due to” his addiction to alcohol.
options: get at with Thomas due to
get along with Thomas due to
get off with Thomas due to
get rid with Thomas due to
questions.explanation: To 'get along with' someone is to have a friendly relationship with them, which his drinking prevented. To 'get over' something is to recover from it, and 'get rid' needs 'of'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. For the last three years, / Sunita had been running / private hostels near this university.
questions.explanation: 'For the last three years' runs up to the present, so it needs the present perfect continuous: 'Sunita has been running private hostels'. The past perfect 'had been running' needs a later past event to refer to.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The suffix '-ful' has one 'l', as in 'powerful', 'grateful' and 'doubtful': the word is 'wilful' (American 'willful').

questions.text: Identify from the following options the word which is OPPOSITE in meaning to the given word. Opaque
questions.explanation: 'Opaque' means not letting light through; its opposite is 'transparent'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The life (1) ______ of a banana is a colourful one; it starts with a deep green, changes to a delicious yellow and ends at an unappetizing brown. Bananas, like most fruits, produce and (2) ________ with an airborne hormone called ethylene. This hormone helps to signal the ripening process. An unripe fruit is hard and acidic. It is likely to possess a greenish (3) ________ due to the presence of chlorophyll. When a fruit comes into contact (4) _________ ethylene, the acids in the fruit start to break down, it becomes softer and the green chlorophyll is (5) _______ and replaced, in the case of bananas, with a yellow hue.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: A banana's 'life cycle' is the sequence of stages it passes through, from green to yellow to brown.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The life (1) ______ of a banana is a colourful one; it starts with a deep green, changes to a delicious yellow and ends at an unappetizing brown. Bananas, like most fruits, produce and (2) ________ with an airborne hormone called ethylene. This hormone helps to signal the ripening process. An unripe fruit is hard and acidic. It is likely to possess a greenish (3) ________ due to the presence of chlorophyll. When a fruit comes into contact (4) _________ ethylene, the acids in the fruit start to break down, it becomes softer and the green chlorophyll is (5) _______ and replaced, in the case of bananas, with a yellow hue.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Bananas produce ethylene and 'react' with it: the hormone signals the ripening process.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The life (1) ______ of a banana is a colourful one; it starts with a deep green, changes to a delicious yellow and ends at an unappetizing brown. Bananas, like most fruits, produce and (2) ________ with an airborne hormone called ethylene. This hormone helps to signal the ripening process. An unripe fruit is hard and acidic. It is likely to possess a greenish (3) ________ due to the presence of chlorophyll. When a fruit comes into contact (4) _________ ethylene, the acids in the fruit start to break down, it becomes softer and the green chlorophyll is (5) _______ and replaced, in the case of bananas, with a yellow hue.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Hue' means colour, as in the passage's later 'a yellow hue': chlorophyll gives an unripe fruit a greenish hue.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The life (1) ______ of a banana is a colourful one; it starts with a deep green, changes to a delicious yellow and ends at an unappetizing brown. Bananas, like most fruits, produce and (2) ________ with an airborne hormone called ethylene. This hormone helps to signal the ripening process. An unripe fruit is hard and acidic. It is likely to possess a greenish (3) ________ due to the presence of chlorophyll. When a fruit comes into contact (4) _________ ethylene, the acids in the fruit start to break down, it becomes softer and the green chlorophyll is (5) _______ and replaced, in the case of bananas, with a yellow hue.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Come into contact with' is the fixed phrase.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The life (1) ______ of a banana is a colourful one; it starts with a deep green, changes to a delicious yellow and ends at an unappetizing brown. Bananas, like most fruits, produce and (2) ________ with an airborne hormone called ethylene. This hormone helps to signal the ripening process. An unripe fruit is hard and acidic. It is likely to possess a greenish (3) ________ due to the presence of chlorophyll. When a fruit comes into contact (4) _________ ethylene, the acids in the fruit start to break down, it becomes softer and the green chlorophyll is (5) _______ and replaced, in the case of bananas, with a yellow hue.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Like the acids, the chlorophyll breaks down: it is 'broken up' and replaced by a yellow hue. The other phrasal verbs do not describe a substance breaking apart.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’, ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the father of B’, ‘A x B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’ and ‘A & B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’. How is N related to R if N & P – Q + T x R?
questions.explanation: N & P: N is P's wife. P – Q: P is Q's father. Q + T: Q is T's mother. T x R: T is R's brother. So Q is R's mother, P is Q's father and N is Q's mother: N is R's mother's mother.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? UNEO, TLBK, SJYG, ?, QFSY
questions.explanation: The first letters move back 1 (U, T, S, R, Q), the second back 2 (N, L, J, H, F), the third back 3 (E, B, Y, V, S) and the fourth back 4 (O, K, G, C, Y), wrapping round the alphabet: RHVC.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Colour : Green :: Figure : ?
questions.explanation: Green is a kind of colour, and a triangle is a kind of figure (a closed shape).

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘AROUND’ is written as ‘PSBFPW’ and 'ARTIST' is written as 'USBVUK'. How will ‘AUTHOR’ be written as in that language?
questions.explanation: The first three letters move one place on and are reversed, and the last three move two places on and are reversed: ARO → BSP → PSB and UND → WPF → FPW; ART → BSU → USB and IST → KUV → VUK. So AUT → BVU → UVB and HOR → JQT → TQJ: UVBTQJ.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 1, 9, 65, 457, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 7 times the one before plus 2: 1 × 7 + 2 = 9, 9 × 7 + 2 = 65, 65 × 7 + 2 = 457, and 457 × 7 + 2 = 3201.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct? 87 × 24 ÷ 12 – 16 + 14 = 176

Six students Lucy, Lorraine, Simran, Dolly, Vikas and Frances are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Lucy is sitting second to the left of Frances. Lorraine is sitting second to the left of Lucy. Vikas is sitting to the immediate right of Lorraine. Simran is sitting second to the left of Vikas. Dolly is an immediate neighbour to Lucy. Who is sitting between Frances and Lorraine?
questions.explanation: As all face the centre, each one's left runs clockwise. Clockwise from Frances: Frances, Dolly, Lucy, Vikas, Lorraine, Simran. Lucy is second to Frances's left, Lorraine second to Lucy's left, Vikas just to Lorraine's right, Simran second to Vikas's left and Dolly beside Lucy, so Simran sits between Frances and Lorraine.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 18 : 3 :: 55 : 4 :: 334 : ?
questions.explanation: Each first number is the cube of the second less 9: 3³ − 9 = 18 and 4³ − 9 = 55. As 334 = 343 − 9 = 7³ − 9, the missing number is 7.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘SHIP’ is written as ‘T17O’ and 'KITE' is written as 'L29D'. How will ‘HOPE’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves one place on, the middle two become the sum of their places in the alphabet, and the last moves one place back: SHIP → T, 8 + 9 = 17, O and KITE → L, 9 + 20 = 29, D. So HOPE → I, 15 + 16 = 31, D: I31D.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question marks (?) in the given series? 1, 3, 4, 7 , ? , ? , 29
questions.explanation: From the third term on, each term is the sum of the two before it: 1 + 3 = 4, 3 + 4 = 7, 4 + 7 = 11, 7 + 11 = 18 and 11 + 18 = 29.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 gather 2 garbage 3 gamble 4 garnish 5 gastronomy
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: gamble (3), garbage (2), garnish (4), gastronomy (5), gather (1). 'Gam' comes before 'gar', 'gas' and 'gat', and 'garb' before 'garn'.

questions.text: Which of the mathematical signs should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct? 320 × 8 - 216 + 72 ÷ 5 = 184
Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. KRBP, IPHV, GNNB, ? , CJZN
questions.explanation: The first letters move back 2 (K, I, G, E, C), the second back 2 (R, P, N, L, J), the third forward 6 (B, H, N, T, Z) and the fourth forward 6 (P, V, B, H, N), wrapping round the alphabet: ELTH.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All pencils are erasers. All pens are erasers. All erasers are scales. Conclusions: I. All pens are scales. II. All erasers are pencils. III. Some erasers are pens.
options: Only conclusion I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: All pens are erasers and all erasers are scales, so all pens are scales (I); and as every pen is an eraser, some erasers are pens (III). The erasers need not all be pencils, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Success : Failure :: Probably : ?
questions.explanation: 'Failure' is the opposite of 'success', and 'definitely' (certainly) the opposite of 'probably' (likely but not certain). 'Perhaps' is close in meaning to 'probably'.

questions.text: Six people P, Q, R, S, T, and U are sitting on a wall facing the South. Only Q is sitting between P and S. U is the immediate left of R. T is sitting to the right of S. Q is to the immediate right of P. Only U is between T and R. Who is sitting to the immediate right of S?
questions.explanation: From the six's own left to right: Q sits just to P's right with only Q between P and S, so P Q S; U sits just to R's left with only U between T and R, so T U R; and T is to S's right: P Q S T U R. T sits immediately to S's right.

questions.text: Who is elected as the first woman member of Rajya Sabha in India from Nagaland in April 2022?
questions.explanation: S Phangnon Konyak of the BJP, elected unopposed in March 2022 and sworn in on 4 April 2022, is the first woman to represent Nagaland in the Rajya Sabha.

questions.text: Chhath Puja is dedicated to which of the following Gods?
questions.explanation: Chhath Puja, celebrated mainly in Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern Uttar Pradesh, is dedicated to the Sun god, Surya, and Chhathi Maiya; devotees make offerings to the setting and the rising sun.

questions.text: When did the first phase of Green Revolution started?
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution began in the mid-1960s, when high-yielding varieties of wheat and rice were introduced with fertilisers and irrigation, first in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.

questions.text: The _________th Amendment (in the year 2020),of Indian Constitution extended the reservation of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
questions.explanation: The Constitution (104th Amendment) Act, 2019, in force from 25 January 2020, extended the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and the state assemblies by ten years, to 2030, and ended the nomination of Anglo-Indian members.

questions.text: Microfinance institution provides financial services to_____________ individuals.
questions.explanation: Microfinance institutions give small loans, savings and other financial services to low-income people who have little access to regular banks.

questions.text: Fundamental Duties were included in the Indian constitution on the recommendation of ____________.
questions.explanation: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended the Fundamental Duties, which the 42nd Amendment added to the Constitution as Article 51A in Part IV-A.

questions.text: What is the primary motive of a private sector entity?
questions.explanation: A private sector firm is owned and run by private individuals mainly to earn a profit, whereas public sector enterprises aim at public welfare.

questions.text: Who became the second lieutenant governor of Jammu and Kashmir?
questions.explanation: Manoj Sinha took over as Lieutenant Governor of the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir in August 2020 from Girish Chandra Murmu, the first, who had held the post since October 2019. R K Mathur was the first Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh.

questions.text: Which of the following is primarily NOT associated with the folk-dance forms of Punjab?
questions.explanation: Lavani is a folk dance of Maharashtra. Luddi, Giddha and Bhangra are folk dances of Punjab.

questions.text: The waste we generate is ______. I. Biodegradable II. Non-biodegradable
questions.explanation: The waste we generate is of both kinds: biodegradable waste such as food and paper, which microbes break down, and non-biodegradable waste such as plastic and glass, which they do not.

questions.text: Who among the following was conferred a Doctorate by the Akhil Bharatiya Gandharva Mahavidyalaya in 1981?
questions.explanation: The Odissi guru Kelucharan Mohapatra was conferred a doctorate by the Akhil Bharatiya Gandharva Mahavidyalaya in 1981.

questions.text: Article 157 of the Constitution of India, states which of the following qualifications to be fulfilled for a person to be appointed Governor of a state? (i) He/She should be an Indian citizen. (ii) He/She should have completed 35 years of age.
questions.explanation: Article 157 makes a person eligible to be appointed Governor only if he or she is a citizen of India and has completed 35 years of age, so both apply.

questions.text: Which is the outermost layer of the earth composed of crust and upper mantle?
questions.explanation: The lithosphere, the rigid outer shell of the earth, is made up of the crust and the uppermost part of the mantle; the softer asthenosphere lies below it.

questions.text: Sports Authority of India was formed in which year?
questions.explanation: The Sports Authority of India was set up in 1984, after the 1982 Asian Games in New Delhi.

questions.text: Whose prashasti was found on the Ashokan pillar at Allahabad?
questions.explanation: The Ashokan pillar at Allahabad carries the prashasti (eulogy) of the Gupta king Samudragupta, composed by his court poet Harishena.

questions.text: Main aim of Green Revolution was to ___________.
options: increase the production of High Yielding Variety of food crops
decrease the consumption of Chloro Floro Chemicals
increase the total area of land
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution aimed to make India self-sufficient in food grains by raising output with high-yielding varieties of wheat and rice, backed by fertilisers and irrigation.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The second round table conference was held in ______.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives December 1931: the second Round Table Conference, which Gandhi attended for the Congress, sat in London from 7 September to 1 December 1931, so it closed in December. None of the other dates falls within it; the first conference sat from November 1930 to January 1931.

questions.text: Milk and face cream are examples of ______.
questions.explanation: Milk and face cream are emulsions: fine droplets of one liquid (fat or oil) dispersed in another (water).

questions.text: Which of the following cannot be considered as a health infrastructure indicator?
questions.explanation: Infant mortality, maternal mortality and life expectancy measure the health of a population; the cost of living is an economic measure of prices.

questions.text: As per FIFA rules, the circumference of a football ball used in official sanctioned matches must measure between:
questions.explanation: Under the Laws of the Game, the ball for official matches must have a circumference of 68 to 70 cm, about 27 to 28 inches.

questions.text: In a village, the population increased from 12,500 to 15,000 in a year. What is the percentage increase in population in a year?
Three cubes each of volume 4096 cm³ are joined end to end to form a new solid. What is the surface area of the new solid?
questions.explanation: Each cube has side ∛4096 = 16 cm, so the new solid is a 48 × 16 × 16 cuboid: 2(48 × 16 + 16 × 16 + 48 × 16) = 2 × 1792 = 3584 cm².

questions.text: A train travelling at the speed of 65 km/h leaves Bombay at 10:00 A.M. and another train travelling at the speed of 76 km/h starts at 12:00 P.M. in the same direction. At what distance (in km) from Bombay will they be together?
questions.explanation: By 12:00 P.M. the first train is 2 × 65 = 130 km ahead. The second gains 76 − 65 = 11 km/h, so it catches up after 130/11 hours, at 76 × 130/11 = 9880/11 ≈ 898.18 km from Bombay.

questions.text: Sohan invested Rs.6,250 for future and he gets Rs.15,552 after 5 years. If the interest is compounded yearly, then what is the rate of interest?
questions.explanation: 15,552/6,250 = 2.48832 = 1.2⁵, so the amount grows by 20% a year.

questions.text: The mean proportional between 0.09 and 0.64 is:
questions.explanation: The mean proportional is √(0.09 × 0.64) = 0.3 × 0.8 = 0.24.

questions.text: After allowing a discount of 12% on its marked price, the selling price of a mobile phone is Rs.22,352. If no discount is allowed, then the shopkeeper gains 25%. The cost price of the mobile phone is:
questions.explanation: The marked price is 22,352/0.88 = ₹25,400. Selling at that price gains 25%, so the cost price is 25,400/1.25 = ₹20,320.

questions.text: A container contains 36 litres of water. From this container, 6 litres of the content were taken out and replaced by oil. This process was repeated two times. How much water is inside the container?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 25 litres, reading 'repeated two times' as two operations in all. Each draws off a sixth of the liquid and replaces it with oil, so 5/6 of the water stays: 36 × (5/6)² = 25 litres. Three operations would leave 36 × (5/6)³ ≈ 20.83 litres, which is not an option.

questions.text: A boat can travel at a speed of 15.5 km/h in still water. If speed of the stream is 4.5 km/h, then how much time will it take to go 76 km downstream and 104.5 km upstream?
questions.explanation: Downstream the boat goes 15.5 + 4.5 = 20 km/h and upstream 15.5 − 4.5 = 11 km/h: 76/20 + 104.5/11 = 3.8 + 9.5 = 13.3 hours, that is 13 hours 18 minutes.

questions.text: Sidhu wants to join a college and finds the rating of 9 out of 10 for campus placements and 8 out of 10 for teaching. Based on his requirement Sidhu gives 55% weightage to campus placements, and 45% weightage to teaching. The final rating of the college out of 10 is:
questions.explanation: The weighted rating is 0.55 × 9 + 0.45 × 8 = 4.95 + 3.6 = 8.55.

questions.text: A coffee maker with a marked price of Rs.4,500 is available on successive discounts of 20%, 10% and 5%. Find the selling price of the coffee maker.
Rakesh can do a piece of work in 45 days and Manoj can do the same work in 90 days. Find the time required to complete the same work if they work on alternate days and Rakesh starts the work.
questions.explanation: In each two-day cycle they do 1/45 + 1/90 = 3/90 = 1/30 of the work, so 30 cycles, 60 days, complete it.

questions.text: A shopkeeper sells one-fourth of his goods at a profit of 20%, another one-fourth at a profit of 25%, and another one-fourth at a profit of 10% and the rest at a loss of 5%. His overall profit percentage is:
questions.explanation: With the goods in four equal parts, the overall profit is the average of the four: (20 + 25 + 10 − 5)/4 = 50/4 = 12.5%.

questions.text: 2 years ago, the value of my car was ₹ 3,62,500. If the value depreciates by 2% every year, then now its value (in ₹) is :
Raju can do a piece of work in 10 hours and Ram can do it in 15 hours. In how much time will they finish the whole work working together?
questions.explanation: Together they do 1/10 + 1/15 = 5/30 = 1/6 of the work an hour, so they finish it in 6 hours.

questions.text: The radius of a hemisphere is 14 cm. Its curved surface area (in cm²) will be: (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: The curved surface area of a hemisphere is 2πr² = 2 × 22/7 × 14 × 14 = 1232 cm².

questions.text: Three bells commence tolling together and toll at intervals of 8 sec, 10 sec and 12 sec respectively. In 30 min, how many times do they toll together?
questions.explanation: LCM(8, 10, 12) = 120 seconds, so the bells toll together every 2 minutes: 30 ÷ 2 = 15 times in 30 minutes, plus once at the start, 16.

questions.text: The sentence given below has one misspelt word. Spot the INCORRECTLY spelt word and select its correct spelling. She wraped the gift in a gift paper.
questions.explanation: 'Wrap' doubles its final 'p' before '-ed': 'wrapped'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. When we went to the cinema, the film “already started”.
questions.explanation: The film started before they reached the cinema, an earlier past action, so the past perfect is needed: 'the film had already started'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. He goes to Shimla every year but this year he was going to Goa.
options: He goes to Shimla every year
questions.explanation: The sentence is set in the present ('He goes ... every year'), and 'this year' is a present arrangement, so the present continuous is needed: 'but this year he is going to Goa'.

questions.text: Select the appropriate idiom that can replace the underlined phrase in the following sentence. He is experienced and “full of wisdom” as he is teaching chemistry at a university at a very young age of 25.
options: an old head on young shoulders
a frog in a small pond
questions.explanation: 'An old head on young shoulders' describes a young person with the wisdom of someone older, as a university teacher of 25 is. A 'silver fox' is an attractive grey-haired man.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Serpentine
questions.explanation: 'Serpentine' means winding like a snake: 'zigzag'. 'Nascent' means just beginning, and 'prosthetic' means artificial, of a body part.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. “Between the 11 members of the team”, there was great discord and this led to their dismal performance.
options: Between the 11 member off the team
Among the 11 members of the team
Between the 11 members in the team
Beside the 11 members of the team
questions.explanation: 'Between' is used of two, 'among' of more than two: 'Among the 11 members of the team'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Solitary
questions.explanation: 'Solitary' means alone or single: a solitary tree is a single one, standing by itself.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in the brackets to fill in the blank and complete the sentence. I don't want to offend him, so I'm hesitant to say or do anything ___________ (polite).
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'polite' is 'rude': not wanting to offend him, the speaker hesitates to say or do anything rude. 'Kind' is close to 'polite'; 'abrupt' (curt) only suggests a lack of politeness, and 'bluff' means frank and direct but good-natured.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Fish out of water
options: Not feeling comfortable in a new environment
questions.explanation: A 'fish out of water' is someone who feels uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Misfortune
questions.explanation: 'Misfortune' is bad luck; its opposite is a 'blessing', a piece of good fortune. 'Affliction' is close in meaning to 'misfortune'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'messenger', with 'e' after the 'm', a double 's' and a 'g'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Compact
questions.explanation: 'Compact' means closely packed together, or as a verb to press together; its opposite is 'expand'. 'Compress' is close in meaning to it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Her “progress” is unparalleled with that of any other teacher.
questions.explanation: 'Progress' here is improvement: 'betterment'. A 'plight' and a 'dilemma' are difficult situations.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word to fill in the blank in the sentence. Compulsion; Some people have a disorder from which comes the ________ to check doors and ensure that they are properly locked.
questions.explanation: A 'compulsion' is a pressure or need to do something, close to an 'obligation'. 'Passion' is strong feeling and 'exertion' effort.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. Because I had to catch the train, and as we were short on time, “I forget to pack my toothbrush for our vacation”.
options: I have forget to pack my toothbrush for our vacation
I forgot to pack my toothbrush for our vacation
I have forgot to pack my toothbrush for our vacation
questions.explanation: The sentence tells of a past event ('I had to catch the train', 'we were short on time'), so the simple past is needed: 'I forgot to pack my toothbrush'. 'Have forget' and 'have forgot' are not standard forms.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. My breath is halted, like gasping for air (1) ______ crying far too long and hard. It is like a hiccup, with a shivering sharpness (2) ______ nerves. It is like icicles running (3) ______ your spine or aluminum in your mouth, an eerie amount of emotions that cannot compare (4) ______ the actual feelings you’ve managed to live (5) ______. I just watched you die; I say to myself silently.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Gasping for air comes 'after' crying far too long and hard.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. My breath is halted, like gasping for air (1) ______ crying far too long and hard. It is like a hiccup, with a shivering sharpness (2) ______ nerves. It is like icicles running (3) ______ your spine or aluminum in your mouth, an eerie amount of emotions that cannot compare (4) ______ the actual feelings you’ve managed to live (5) ______. I just watched you die; I say to myself silently.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'A shivering sharpness of nerves': 'of' ties the sharpness to the nerves that feel it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. My breath is halted, like gasping for air (1) ______ crying far too long and hard. It is like a hiccup, with a shivering sharpness (2) ______ nerves. It is like icicles running (3) ______ your spine or aluminum in your mouth, an eerie amount of emotions that cannot compare (4) ______ the actual feelings you’ve managed to live (5) ______. I just watched you die; I say to myself silently.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Icicles running 'down' your spine is a chill felt along the back, as in 'a shiver down the spine'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. My breath is halted, like gasping for air (1) ______ crying far too long and hard. It is like a hiccup, with a shivering sharpness (2) ______ nerves. It is like icicles running (3) ______ your spine or aluminum in your mouth, an eerie amount of emotions that cannot compare (4) ______ the actual feelings you’ve managed to live (5) ______. I just watched you die; I say to myself silently.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Compare' takes 'to' here: emotions that cannot compare to the actual feelings.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. My breath is halted, like gasping for air (1) ______ crying far too long and hard. It is like a hiccup, with a shivering sharpness (2) ______ nerves. It is like icicles running (3) ______ your spine or aluminum in your mouth, an eerie amount of emotions that cannot compare (4) ______ the actual feelings you’ve managed to live (5) ______. I just watched you die; I say to myself silently.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: To 'live through' something is to experience it and come out the other side: the feelings you have managed to live through.

questions.text: In a code language, 'dark colors' is coded as 'yu nu', 'days are bright' is coded as 'wu tu ku', 'nights are dark' is coded as 'ku nu pu', 'paint bright' is coded as 'wu ru'. What is the code for the word 'nights'?
questions.explanation: 'Dark' is in 'dark colors' and 'nights are dark', so it is 'nu'; 'are' is in 'days are bright' and 'nights are dark', so it is 'ku'. That leaves 'pu' for 'nights'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. FVL : MXI :: PCJ : KES :: DKN : ?
questions.explanation: In each pair the second cluster's first letter is the first cluster's third letter moved 1 forward, its second letter the second moved 2 forward and its third the first moved 3 forward: FVL → MXI (L + 1, V + 2, F + 3) and PCJ → KES (J + 1, C + 2, P + 3). So DKN → OMG (N + 1, K + 2, D + 3).

questions.text: If ‘+’ means ‘÷’, ‘–’ means ‘+’, ‘×’ means ‘ - ‘ and ‘÷’ means ‘×’, what will be the value of the following expression? [ { ( 49 × 12 ) - ( 6 ÷ 2 ) } + ( 4 - 3 ) ] ÷ 5

In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’, ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’, ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the father of B’ and ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the son of B’. If P × Q × R + D ÷ S – B, then which of the following statements is NOT correct?
questions.explanation: P is Q's father, and Q is the father of R and D (R is D's brother). S, D's mother, is Q's wife and B's mother, so B is a child of Q and S. P is therefore B's father's father, not B's mother's father; the other three statements hold.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? ETAX, FRDT, GPGP, ?, ILMH
questions.explanation: The first letters move +1 (E, F, G, H, I), the second −2 (T, R, P, N, L), the third +3 (A, D, G, J, M) and the fourth −4 (X, T, P, L, H): HNJL.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 9, 35, 91, 189, 341, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is the sum of the cubes of two consecutive numbers: 2³ + 1³ = 9, 3³ + 2³ = 35, 4³ + 3³ = 91, 5³ + 4³ = 189 and 6³ + 5³ = 341. Next comes 7³ + 6³ = 343 + 216 = 559.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. BELF, WZTN, RUBV, ? , HKRL
questions.explanation: The first and second letters move 5 places back each time (B, W, R, M, H and E, Z, U, P, K), and the third and fourth 8 places forward (L, T, B, J, R and F, N, V, D, L), wrapping round the alphabet: MPJD.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term. 6 : 109 :: ? : 257 :: 10 : 501
questions.explanation: Each second term is half the cube of the first, plus 1: 6³/2 + 1 = 109 and 10³/2 + 1 = 501. As 257 = 512/2 + 1 and 512 = 8³, the missing term is 8.

questions.text: Five people E, F, G, H and I are sitting in a straight row, facing north. There are only three people sitting to the left of H and only three people sitting to the right of F. E sits on the immediate left of F and only two people sit on the left of G. Who is sitting on the extreme right end of the row?
questions.explanation: Three people to the left of H puts H fourth from the left, and three to the right of F puts F second. E sits on F's left, so first, and G, with two people to its left, is third. I takes the fifth place, at the right end: E F G H I.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question marks (?) in the given series? 119, 117, 114, 109, ? , 91, ?, 61

Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All gels are boats. All pumps are boats. All boats are ships. Conclusions: I. All pumps are ships. II. All ships are gels. III. Some ships are pumps.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: All pumps are boats and all boats are ships, so all pumps are ships (I), and so some ships are pumps (III). Nothing says that every ship is a gel, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Which of the mathematical signs should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct? 17 + 112 ÷ 16 - 8 × 64 = 175
Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 eagle 2 eager 3 eastern 4 earth 5 earring
questions.explanation: 'Eager' comes before 'eagle' ('e' before 'l' in the fourth place), and both before the 'ear-' words; 'earring' comes before 'earth' ('r' before 't'), and 'eastern' comes last: 2, 1, 5, 4, 3.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) New Delhi : India :: Kyiv : ?
questions.explanation: New Delhi is the capital of India; likewise Kyiv is the capital of Ukraine.

questions.text: Six students Kabir, Messi, Ronaldo, Sharon, Raj and Moosa are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Moosa is sitting second to the left of Sharon. Kabir is sitting second to the left of Moosa. Ronaldo is sitting to the immediate left of Kabir. Raj is sitting to the immediate left of Moosa. Messi is an immediate neighbour to Sharon and Moosa. Who is sitting between Ronaldo and Messi?
questions.explanation: Going round to the left from Sharon: Messi, Moosa (second to her left), Raj (on Moosa's left), Kabir (second to Moosa's left) and Ronaldo (on Kabir's left), who is then on Sharon's right. Messi sits between Sharon and Moosa, so Sharon sits between Ronaldo and Messi.

questions.text: In a code language, 'MORBID' is written as ‘61’ and ‘PARIAH’ is written as ‘53’. How will 'RAVISHED' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word's code is the sum of its letters' places in the alphabet: MORBID = 13 + 15 + 18 + 2 + 9 + 4 = 61 and PARIAH = 16 + 1 + 18 + 9 + 1 + 8 = 53. So RAVISHED = 18 + 1 + 22 + 9 + 19 + 8 + 5 + 4 = 86.

questions.text: Bank rate is the rate at which:
options: Central Bank borrows loan from Government
Commercial banks lend loan to Central bank
Commercial banks lend loan to Government
Central bank lends loan to commercial banks.
questions.explanation: The bank rate is the rate at which the central bank, in India the Reserve Bank, lends to commercial banks; raising it makes credit dearer across the economy.

questions.text: The term Stumping is related to which of the following sports?
questions.explanation: Stumping is a way of dismissing a batter in cricket: the wicketkeeper puts down the wicket while the batter is out of the crease and not attempting a run.

questions.text: Who among the following was elected as Member of Rajya Sabha from Himachal Pradesh, India in March 2022?
questions.explanation: Sikander Kumar of the BJP, then Vice-Chancellor of Himachal Pradesh University, was elected unopposed to the Rajya Sabha from Himachal Pradesh in March 2022, on Anand Sharma's retirement.

questions.text: Which term did Robert Hooke coin when he observed slices of cork, under a simple magnifying device?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke saw tiny box-like compartments in a thin slice of cork in 1665 and called them 'cells'.

questions.text: What is the name of Arunachal Pradesh's first greenfield airport?
questions.explanation: Donyi Polo Airport at Hollongi, near Itanagar, opened in November 2022 as the state's first greenfield airport; its name joins the Sun (Donyi) and the Moon (Polo).

questions.text: Which is one of the bi-product formed when sodium sulphate reacts with barium chloride?
questions.explanation: Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → BaSO₄ + 2NaCl: a double displacement reaction that gives a white precipitate of barium sulphate, with sodium chloride left in solution.

questions.text: Which of the following folk-dance forms is NOT predominantly performed in the Indian state of Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: Rouf (Rouff) is a women's folk dance of Kashmir. Tamasha, Lavani and the Koli dance of the fishing community belong to Maharashtra.

questions.text: Industrial development is a precondition for ______of unemployment.
questions.explanation: The line is from the NCERT Class 10 geography textbook's chapter on manufacturing industries: industries create jobs, so industrial development is a precondition for eradicating unemployment and poverty.

questions.text: Before being elected as the 15th President of India, Draupadi Murmu was the Governor of which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Draupadi Murmu was Governor of Jharkhand from 2015 to 2021, the state's first woman Governor, before she was elected President in July 2022.

questions.text: Sharad Purnima is associated with the Goddess ________ in some parts of India.
questions.explanation: Sharad Purnima, the full moon of the month of Ashvin, is kept in Bengal, Odisha and Assam as Kojagari Lakshmi Puja, in honour of the goddess Lakshmi.

questions.text: How many rulers of Dakshinapatha were defeated by Samudragupta?
questions.explanation: Harishena's Prayag prashasti (the Allahabad pillar inscription) names twelve rulers of Dakshinapatha whom Samudragupta defeated and then allowed to rule again.

questions.text: Who was the first Indian to receive the medal and Diploma of the French association Archives Internationales de la Danse?
questions.explanation: The dancer Mrinalini Sarabhai, founder of the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts in Ahmedabad, was the first Indian to receive the medal and diploma of the Archives Internationales de la Danse.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: _________ and ___________ formed the Swaraj Party within the Congress to argue for a return to council politics.
questions.explanation: C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party in 1923, after the Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn, to contest the council elections and oppose British policies from within.

questions.text: In badminton singles, at the beginning of the game (0-0) and when the server’s score is even, the server serves from which side of the court?
questions.explanation: Under the Laws of Badminton the server serves from the right service court with 0 or an even number of points, and from the left with an odd number.

questions.text: Although there was a category of industries left to the private sector, the sector was kept under state control through a system of licenses. No new industry was allowed unless a license was obtained from the government. The above lines are about which of the following?
questions.explanation: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 reserved some industries for the state and kept the private sector under state control through industrial licences.

questions.text: According to the 2011 Census of India, the state of Bihar was the ______ most populated state of India .
questions.explanation: At the 2011 Census Bihar, with about 10.4 crore people, was the third most populous state, after Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra.

questions.text: According to which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India can the Supreme Court review its own judgements or orders?
questions.explanation: Article 137 empowers the Supreme Court to review any judgement it has pronounced or order it has made, subject to law and to rules made under Article 145.

questions.text: Make in India scheme was launched by Government of India in year ___________.
questions.explanation: The Make in India initiative was launched on 25 September 2014 to encourage manufacturing and investment in India.

questions.text: What does Part IVA of the Indian Constitutions deal with?
questions.explanation: Part IVA, added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, has a single article, Article 51A, which lists the Fundamental Duties of citizens.

questions.text: Which rocks are formed from solidification and cooling of magma?
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks form when molten magma, below the surface or as lava above it, cools and solidifies; granite and basalt are examples.

questions.text: Tina puts Rs. 48000 in a bank account. She takes it out 6 years later, it is now worth Rs. 60000. The percent increase is:
If the price of petrol is increased by 25 percent, then how much should a person decrease the consumption to keep the expenditure same?
questions.explanation: To keep the expenditure the same, consumption must fall by 25/(100 + 25) × 100 = 20%.

questions.text: A shopkeeper buys some fruits at a discount of 10% on the marked price. For selling the item he increases the marked price. If he wants to get a profit of 25% after allowing a discount of 15%, then by what percentage should his marked price be greater than the original marked price? (Correct to a nearest whole number)
questions.explanation: Take the original marked price as 100: the cost is 90, and a 25% profit needs a selling price of 112.5. After a 15% discount the new marked price must be 112.5/0.85 = 132.35, about 32% above the original.

questions.text: The average age of a certain number of students in a college club is 20 years. Later, 27 new students, whose average age is 22 years, joined the club. 12 students, whose average age is 19 years, left the club. As a result of this change, the average age of all the students increases by 2 years. What is the present number of students in the club?
questions.explanation: With n students at first: 20n + 27 × 22 − 12 × 19 = 22(n + 15), so 20n + 366 = 22n + 330 and n = 18. Now there are 18 + 27 − 12 = 33.

questions.text: What is the length of the longest pole that can be placed in a room 12 m long, 8 m broad and 3 m high (correct up to 2 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: The longest pole runs along the room's diagonal: √(12² + 8² + 3²) = √(144 + 64 + 9) = √217 ≈ 14.73 m.

questions.text: 20 women can finish a piece of work in 16 days and 16 men can finish it in 15 days. What is the ratio of the working efficiency of a man and a woman?
questions.explanation: The work is 20 × 16 = 320 woman-days or 16 × 15 = 240 man-days, so a man does 320/240 = 4/3 of a woman's work: 4 : 3.

questions.text: An overcoat is sold for Rs.1,260 at successive discounts of 16% and 25%. Find the marked price of the overcoat.
questions.explanation: Marked price × 0.84 × 0.75 = ₹1,260, so the marked price is 1,260/0.63 = ₹2,000.

questions.text: A hemispherical bowl is made of thick steel, whose thickness is 0.50 cm. If the outer diameter of the bowl is 43 cm, then the volume of the bowl is:
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the volume of the space inside the bowl: the inner radius is 43/2 − 0.5 = 21 cm, so V = (2/3) × (22/7) × 21³ = (2/3) × (22/7) × 9261 = 19404 cm³. (The steel itself would be only about 1419 cm³, which is not among the options.)

questions.text: The cost price of 1 kg of sugar is Rs.50. A shopkeeper sells it at Rs.55 per kg. In order to raise his profit, the shopkeeper weighs only 900 grams in place of 1 kg. Determine the percentage profit (Approximate) earned by the shopkeeper.
questions.explanation: The shopkeeper gives 900 g, which cost him ₹45, for ₹55: profit = 10/45 × 100 = 22.2%, about 22%.

questions.text: A girl walks to a park situated 350 m from her house. It took her 3 mins to reach the park and 4 mins to return. What is the average speed of the girl (in km/h)?
questions.explanation: She covers 350 × 2 = 700 m in 3 + 4 = 7 minutes, that is 100 m a minute or 6,000 m an hour: 6 km/h.

questions.text: P and Q together can complete a work in 21 days. Q alone can complete it in 84 days. If efficiency of Q becomes double, then in how many days approximately will P and Q together complete the work?
questions.explanation: P does 1/21 − 1/84 = 3/84 = 1/28 of the work a day. With Q's rate doubled to 2/84 = 1/42, together they do 1/28 + 1/42 = 5/84 a day and take 84/5 = 16.8, about 17 days.

questions.text: 2 numbers differ by 9 and their product is 2430. Find the HCF of the numbers.
questions.explanation: x(x + 9) = 2430 gives x = 45, so the numbers are 45 and 54 (45 × 54 = 2430), whose HCF is 9.

questions.text: Which relation is correct for 6 : 11 and 8 : 9?
questions.explanation: Cross-multiplying, 8 × 11 = 88 is greater than 6 × 9 = 54, so 8/9 > 6/11 (about 0.89 against 0.55).

questions.text: If a + b : b + c : c + a = 2 : 3 : 5 and a + b + c = 20, then the value of c is:
questions.explanation: The three sums add up to 2(a + b + c) = 40, so they are 8, 12 and 20. Then c = (a + b + c) − (a + b) = 20 − 8 = 12.

questions.text: The least multiple of 7, which leaves a remainder of 4, when divided by 6, 9, 15 and 18 is:
questions.explanation: The LCM of 6, 9, 15 and 18 is 90, so the number is 90k + 4. For k = 1, 2, 3 and 4 that gives 94, 184, 274 and 364, and the first multiple of 7 among them is 364 = 7 × 52.

questions.text: If the difference between the compound interest, compounding annually and the simple interest on a certain sum of money at 5% per annum for 3 years is Rs.183, then what is the sum of money invested?

A deposited a total of Rs.25,500 in a bank in the names of his grandsons P and Q who are presently 13 years and 14 years old, respectively. He divided his money in such a way that they get equal amounts upon attaining the age of 25 years. If the bank gives interest at a rate of 4% p.a. compounded annually, then how much has been deposited in Q’s name?
questions.explanation: P's money grows for 12 years and Q's for 11, so P's share × 1.04¹² = Q's share × 1.04¹¹, that is Q's share = 1.04 × P's share. Then 2.04 × P's share = ₹25,500, so P's share is ₹12,500 and Q's ₹13,000.

questions.text: The speed of a boat along and against the current are 16 km/h and 12 km/h, respectively. The speed of the current is:
questions.explanation: The speed of the current is half the difference of the two speeds: (16 − 12)/2 = 2 km/h.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. The supervisor is ________ (ruthless) in his behaviour with the workers.
questions.explanation: 'Ruthless' means without pity: 'merciless'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Esteem
questions.explanation: To 'esteem' is to respect or admire, and as a noun it means respect. 'Abuse' and 'ridicule' are nearly its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. It is hard to believe that many smokers didn’t “go cold turkey” even after they got lung cancer.
questions.explanation: To 'go cold turkey' is to quit an addictive habit, such as smoking, suddenly and completely. (The option's 'Quite' is a misprint for 'Quit'.)

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Her bookstore flourished / because / she picks / a good location.
questions.explanation: The sentence is in the past ('flourished'), so the reason must be in the past too: 'because she picked a good location'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word to fill in the blank. Welter was an “honest” worker, whereas Rodriguez was ___________.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'honest' is 'corrupt', dishonest for gain. 'Candid' is close in meaning to 'honest', and 'erupt' is a verb.

questions.text: Choose the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'parlour', with an 'r' after the 'a'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. They took a while to “establish the threat”.
questions.explanation: A threat that takes a while to notice has to be 'recognised', that is identified; to 'establish' is to set up or prove, and to 'manifest' is to show.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Dispel
questions.explanation: To 'dispel' is to drive away or scatter, so its opposite is 'integrate', to bring together into a whole. 'Scatter' and 'remove' are close to 'dispel'.

questions.text: A part of the given sentence which has been underlined may contain a spelling error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the spelling error. If there is no error, select ‘No error’. Some of the islands in the Bay of Bengal are still “inaccesible” to the scientists.
questions.explanation: The word is spelt 'inaccessible', with a double 'c' and a double 's'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Blunt
questions.explanation: 'Blunt', of an edge or point, means not sharp: 'dull'. 'Sharp' is its opposite.

questions.text: Choose the option that can substitute the underlined segment correctly and complete the meaning of the sentence. Meenakshi looks “very beautiful” in her blue dress.
questions.explanation: 'Gorgeous' means very beautiful. 'Lavish' means rich or extravagant, and 'lively' full of energy.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The pleasure created by the poet was primarily “until his exaggerated descriptions”.
questions.explanation: The poet created pleasure by means of his descriptions: 'through his exaggerated descriptions'. 'Until' refers to time and does not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Arrogant
questions.explanation: 'Arrogant' means proud and self-important; its opposite is 'humble'. 'Haughty', 'superior' and 'scornful' are close in meaning to 'arrogant'.

questions.text: Fill in the blanks with the correct homophone. His eyes _______ up with fascination when he saw his idol standing in front of him.
questions.explanation: Eyes 'light up' with pleasure or excitement, and the past tense is 'lit': 'His eyes lit up'. 'Lye' is an alkaline solution and 'lite' an informal spelling of 'light' meaning low in calories.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment in the given sentence. “Without any question”, Naresh is my good friend.
questions.explanation: 'Beyond a doubt' means certainly, which is what 'without any question' says.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The automobile industry is one of the (1) _______ industries at the global level. It plays a crucial role in the development of the global economy because of the high revenues and increased customer demands. The automobile industry helps to (2)_________ economic development of the country; therefore, it is widely recognised as a major economic sector. The automobile industry consists of multiple companies (3)__________ in car manufacturing, as well as the ones involved in marketing and distribution of automobile products, such as cars, buses, vans, trucks, motorcycles, mopeds and (4)_______ bicycles. The global automobile industry incorporates several large car manufacturers’ blocs that work (5)______ at the global level.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The automobile industry is one of the 'leading' industries, among the foremost in the world.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The automobile industry is one of the (1) _______ industries at the global level. It plays a crucial role in the development of the global economy because of the high revenues and increased customer demands. The automobile industry helps to (2)_________ economic development of the country; therefore, it is widely recognised as a major economic sector. The automobile industry consists of multiple companies (3)__________ in car manufacturing, as well as the ones involved in marketing and distribution of automobile products, such as cars, buses, vans, trucks, motorcycles, mopeds and (4)_______ bicycles. The global automobile industry incorporates several large car manufacturers’ blocs that work (5)______ at the global level.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: To 'foster' development is to encourage and promote it; 'block' and 'arrest' would stop it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The automobile industry is one of the (1) _______ industries at the global level. It plays a crucial role in the development of the global economy because of the high revenues and increased customer demands. The automobile industry helps to (2)_________ economic development of the country; therefore, it is widely recognised as a major economic sector. The automobile industry consists of multiple companies (3)__________ in car manufacturing, as well as the ones involved in marketing and distribution of automobile products, such as cars, buses, vans, trucks, motorcycles, mopeds and (4)_______ bicycles. The global automobile industry incorporates several large car manufacturers’ blocs that work (5)______ at the global level.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Companies 'specialised' in car manufacturing are those that concentrate on it, as against the ones in marketing and distribution.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The automobile industry is one of the (1) _______ industries at the global level. It plays a crucial role in the development of the global economy because of the high revenues and increased customer demands. The automobile industry helps to (2)_________ economic development of the country; therefore, it is widely recognised as a major economic sector. The automobile industry consists of multiple companies (3)__________ in car manufacturing, as well as the ones involved in marketing and distribution of automobile products, such as cars, buses, vans, trucks, motorcycles, mopeds and (4)_______ bicycles. The global automobile industry incorporates several large car manufacturers’ blocs that work (5)______ at the global level.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The list is of automobile products, so the bicycles are 'motorised' ones, with engines, like the mopeds before them.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The automobile industry is one of the (1) _______ industries at the global level. It plays a crucial role in the development of the global economy because of the high revenues and increased customer demands. The automobile industry helps to (2)_________ economic development of the country; therefore, it is widely recognised as a major economic sector. The automobile industry consists of multiple companies (3)__________ in car manufacturing, as well as the ones involved in marketing and distribution of automobile products, such as cars, buses, vans, trucks, motorcycles, mopeds and (4)_______ bicycles. The global automobile industry incorporates several large car manufacturers’ blocs that work (5)______ at the global level.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Manufacturers' blocs are groups that work together, 'collaboratively'; 'single-handedly' contradicts the idea of a bloc.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: Some watches are clocks. All clocks are black. All black are big. Conclusions: I. Some watches are big. II. Some watches are black.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: Some watches are clocks and all clocks are black, so some watches are black (II). As all black things are big, those watches are also big (I). Both follow.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 78 + 3 ÷ 26 - 8 × 24 = 25
questions.explanation: After interchanging × and +: 78 × 3 ÷ 26 − 8 + 24 = 9 − 8 + 24 = 25.

questions.text: A @ B means ‘A is the sister of B’. A & B means ‘A is the brother of B’. A # B means ‘A is the wife of B’. A ^ B means ‘A is the mother of B’. A + B means ‘A is the father of B’. If U ^ Q ^ R @ N & C ^ I@ J @ A, then which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: C is the daughter of Q.
Q is the maternal grandfather of I.
J is the daughter of C
Q is the mother of N.
questions.explanation: U ^ Q ^ R makes Q the mother of R; R @ N & C makes R, N and C siblings, so N and C are also Q's children, and C ^ I makes C a woman, Q's daughter. J, I's sister, is C's daughter. Q is a woman, so she is I's maternal grandmother, not grandfather.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 13, 4, 17, 8 ,21 ,16, 25 ?
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 13, 17, 21, 25 (adding 4) and 4, 8, 16 (doubling). The next term of the second is 16 × 2 = 32.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 12, 24, 48, 84, 132, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 12, 24, 36 and 48, rising by 12 each time; the next is 60: 132 + 60 = 192.

questions.text: In a certain language, RAT is coded as 3, BOTTLE is coded as 6, how will MOBILE be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded by its number of letters: RAT has 3 and BOTTLE 6. MOBILE has 6.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed) (45, 24, 231) (65, 47, 198)
questions.explanation: In each set the third number is 11 times the difference of the first two: (45 − 24) × 11 = 231 and (65 − 47) × 11 = 198. Likewise (46 − 13) × 11 = 363.

questions.text: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Raj is the immediate neighbour of Liam and Maria. Siddharth is sitting to the second right of Maria. Tanya is sitting to the third left of Liam. Nathan is sitting to the immediate left of Liam. Who is the immediate neighbour of Siddharth and Maria?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left runs clockwise. Clockwise from Liam: Nathan (his immediate left), Siddharth, Tanya (third to his left), Maria and Raj, who sits between Maria and Liam; Siddharth is then second to Maria's right. Tanya sits between Siddharth and Maria.

questions.text: Seven friends A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circle facing towards the centre. D is sitting third to the right of A and immediately left of G. Only B is sitting between G and E. C is sitting to the immediate left of F. Who is sitting second to the left of G?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left runs clockwise. Clockwise the order is A, E, B, G, D, F, C: D is third to A's right and just left of G, only B sits between G and E, and C is just left of F. Second to the left of G is F.

questions.text: In a certain code language, TIRED is coded as 56, and FRESH is coded as 56. How will HEAVEN be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded by the sum of its letters' places in the alphabet: TIRED = 20 + 9 + 18 + 5 + 4 = 56 and FRESH = 6 + 18 + 5 + 19 + 8 = 56. HEAVEN = 8 + 5 + 1 + 22 + 5 + 14 = 55.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? WKRF, VLQG, TNOI, ? , MUHP
questions.explanation: The first letters move back 1, 2, 3 and 4 places (W, V, T, Q, M), the second forward 1, 2, 3 and 4 (K, L, N, Q, U), the third back (R, Q, O, L, H) and the fourth forward (F, G, I, L, P). The missing term is QQLL.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Glass 2 Glycerine 3 Glare 4 Glow 5 Glamorous
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Glamorous (5), Glare (3), Glass (1), Glow (4), Glycerine (2). 'Glam' comes before 'Glar' and 'Glas', and 'Gla' before 'Glo' and 'Gly'.

questions.text: If ‘+’ means ‘-’, ‘÷’ means ‘+’, ‘-’ means ‘×’, and ‘×‘ means ‘÷’. Which of the following will be the value of the expression? 81 × 9 + 21 - 7 ÷ 147
questions.explanation: After replacing the signs: 81 ÷ 9 − 21 × 7 + 147 = 9 − 147 + 147 = 9.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. PENSION : NENSIOP :: QUALITY : YUALITQ :: PRODUCT : ?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters change places: PENSION → NENSIOP and QUALITY → YUALITQ. So PRODUCT → TRODUCP.

questions.text: Which of the following letters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter series? B, C, G, P, F, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 1, 4, 9 and 16 places forward (the squares), counting on past Z to A: B → C → G → P → F. Moving 25 places on from F gives E.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. NEAR: KJEG :: SAME: FFQT :: EARN: ?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters are each replaced by the letter whose place in the alphabet adds up with theirs to 25 (N 14 → K 11, R 18 → G 7; S 19 → F 6, E 5 → T 20); the second letter moves 5 places forward and the third 4. So EARN → TFVK.

questions.text: The Dronacharya Award for coaches started in which year?
questions.explanation: The Dronacharya Award, India's award for sports coaches, was instituted in 1985.

questions.text: The _________ refers to the excess of government’s revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.
questions.explanation: Revenue deficit = revenue expenditure − revenue receipts. Fiscal deficit is total expenditure less receipts other than borrowing, and a revenue surplus is the reverse of a revenue deficit.

questions.text: What is the name of the first Indian tribal president?
questions.explanation: Droupadi Murmu, a Santhal from Odisha, became the first President of India from a Scheduled Tribe when she was sworn in on 25 July 2022.

questions.text: What is different about castor seeds?
options: It is the only rabi crop
It is neither rabi nor kharif
It is both rabi and kharif crop
questions.explanation: Castor seed is grown both as a rabi and as a kharif crop, in different regions and seasons.

questions.text: Songkran is a Buddhist festival. This festival is celebrated for several days in the month of _______.
questions.explanation: Songkran, the Thai New Year, is celebrated over several days in mid-April (13 to 15 April), with water thrown in the streets and visits to Buddhist temples.

questions.text: As per the 73rd and 74th amendment India has ______-tier government system.
questions.explanation: The 73rd and 74th Amendments (1992) gave constitutional status to panchayats and municipalities, making local government a third tier below the Union and the States; the 73rd also set up panchayats at three levels, village, intermediate and district.
