questions.text: Which of the following has been conferred the Kalidas Samman in February 2022?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives M. Venkateshkumar: Madhya Pradesh's Kalidas Samman for classical music to this Hindustani vocalist from Karnataka was reported in the first week of February 2022. Kumar Gandharva, Zia Mohiuddin Dagar and Bhupen Khakhar received the award in the 1980s and 1990s and had died long before 2022.

questions.text: Which state has the highest sex ratio as per the Census 2011?
questions.explanation: Kerala had the highest sex ratio in the 2011 Census, 1,084 females per 1,000 males.

questions.text: Shevroy Hills and the Javadi Hills are located to the __________.
questions.explanation: In NCERT's account of the Eastern Ghats, the Shevaroy Hills (near Salem) and the Javadi Hills, both in northern Tamil Nadu, lie to the south-east of the range.

questions.text: Who among the following became Member of Legislative Assembly from Bochahan, Bihar in India, in April 2022?
questions.explanation: Amar Kumar Paswan of the RJD won the Bochahan by-election, whose result was declared on 16 April 2022, defeating the BJP's Baby Kumari; the seat had fallen vacant on the death of Musafir Paswan of the Vikassheel Insaan Party.

questions.text: Jagoi and Cholom are the two main divisions in which of the following classical dance forms?
questions.explanation: Jagoi, the gentle style, and Cholom, the vigorous style danced with drums and cymbals, are the two main divisions of Manipuri dance.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India mandates the position of a Vice President of India?
questions.explanation: Article 63 says 'There shall be a Vice-President of India'. Article 53 vests the executive power of the Union in the President.

questions.text: For the first time in the world, the Five-Year Plan (1928–32), was implemented by ___________ in Soviet Union.
questions.explanation: The Soviet Union's first Five-Year Plan (1928-32) was launched under Joseph Stalin; it was the first such national plan in the world.

questions.text: Swachh Bharat Mission was launched in year ____________.
questions.explanation: The Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on 2 October 2014, Mahatma Gandhi's birth anniversary.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following major incidents occurred in 1919?
questions.explanation: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre in Amritsar took place on 13 April 1919. Bengal was partitioned in 1905, the Champaran movement was in 1917 and the Non-Cooperation Movement began in 1920.

questions.text: The 12th Five-Year Plan aims to achieve annual average economic growth rate of ___________.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 8.2 per cent, the average growth target the Planning Commission set for the Twelfth Plan (2012-17) in September 2012, down from the 9 per cent of its Approach Paper; the National Development Council approved a slightly lower 8 per cent in December 2012.

questions.text: The sound waves having frequencies less than ________ Hz are called infrasonic waves.
questions.explanation: Sound below 20 Hz, the lower limit of human hearing, is infrasonic; above 20,000 Hz it is ultrasonic.

questions.text: The mascot of 2022 National games of India is based on which animal?
questions.explanation: The mascot of the 36th National Games, held in Gujarat from 29 September to 12 October 2022, was Savaj, an Asiatic lion.

questions.text: In plants cell, ______ are primarily organelles in which materials such as starch, oils and protein granules are stored.
questions.explanation: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store starch, oils and proteins. Chromoplasts carry the pigments that colour fruits and flowers, and vacuoles hold the cell sap.

questions.text: Anand with his family travelled from Guntur to Rajahmundry by car at a speed of 50 km/h and returned to Guntur at a speed of 60 km/h. The average speed for the whole journey is: (Consider up to two decimal places)
questions.explanation: For equal distances the average speed is 2 × 50 × 60/(50 + 60) = 6000/110 = 54.5454... km/h; cut off at two decimal places, 54.54 km/h.

questions.text: A dealer fixed the price of an article 40% above the cost of production. While selling it he allows a discount of 20% and makes a profit of Rs.72. Find the cost of production (in Rs.) of the article.
questions.explanation: With cost C, the marked price is 1.4C and the selling price 1.4C × 0.8 = 1.12C. The profit 0.12C = 72, so C = Rs. 600.

questions.text: A rectangular ground 90m long and 42 m wide has two cross roads in its centre. The road parallel to the length is 7 m wide and the other road is 3 m wide, both roads are perpendicular to each other. The cost of laying the bricks at the rate of Rs.25 per m², on the roads, will be:
questions.explanation: The roads cover 90 × 7 + 42 × 3 − 7 × 3 = 630 + 126 − 21 = 735 m², counting the crossing once. At Rs. 25 per m² the cost is 735 × 25 = Rs. 18,375.

questions.text: Which type of numbers are NOT co-prime?
questions.explanation: Co-prime numbers have no common factor but 1. Two consecutive even numbers always share the factor 2, while two different primes, two consecutive numbers and two consecutive odd numbers (both odd and only 2 apart) have none.

questions.text: The ratio of alcohol to water in three types of drugs of equal quantity is 2 : 5, 5 : 9 and 8 : 13 respectively. Equal quantity of all the three drugs is mixed. Find the ratio of alcohol to water after mixing .
questions.explanation: Taking 42 units of each drug, the alcohol is 12 + 15 + 16 = 43 units and the water 30 + 27 + 26 = 83 units: 43 : 83.

questions.text: Find three numbers in the ratio of 6 : 4 : 10 such that the sum of their squares is equal to 3800.
questions.explanation: With the numbers 6k, 4k and 10k: 36k² + 16k² + 100k² = 152k² = 3800, so k² = 25, k = 5, and the numbers are 30, 20 and 50.

questions.text: In a panchayat election an independent candidate got 28% of the total votes polled and was declared the winner. The rest of the votes were equally divided among the candidates of three national parties. If the total votes polled were 1200, how many votes did the each candidate of national party get?
questions.explanation: The winner got 28% of 1200 = 336 votes, leaving 1200 − 336 = 864 for the three national-party candidates: 864 ÷ 3 = 288 each.

questions.text: A car covers the first 35 km in 15 minutes and the next 45 km in 25 minutes. What is the average speed of the car?
questions.explanation: The car covers 35 + 45 = 80 km in 15 + 25 = 40 minutes, two-thirds of an hour: 80 × 60/40 = 120 km/h.

questions.text: A can complete 3/4th of the work in 9 days and B can complete 2/5th of the work in 12 days. With the help of C, all three together complete the whole work in 60/11 days and earn Rs. 330. If money is shared in the ratio of work done, then find the difference in the share of C and the share of A.
questions.explanation: A does the whole work in 9 × 4/3 = 12 days and B in 12 × 5/2 = 30 days. All three do 11/60 of it a day, so C does 11/60 − 5/60 − 2/60 = 4/60. As all work the same days, Rs. 330 is shared 5 : 2 : 4: A gets Rs. 150 and C Rs. 120, a difference of Rs. 30.

questions.text: The price of 2 tables is equal to the price of 5 chairs. If price of a chair is Rs. 500, then what is the average price of 6 tables and 9 chairs?
questions.explanation: A table costs 5 × 500/2 = Rs. 1,250. 6 tables and 9 chairs cost 7,500 + 4,500 = Rs. 12,000, and 12,000 ÷ 15 = Rs. 800.

questions.text: The single discount equivalent to the successive discounts of 30 percent, 15 percent and 5 percent is:
questions.explanation: After the three discounts the price is 0.70 × 0.85 × 0.95 = 0.56525 of the original, so the single discount is 100 − 56.525 = 43.475 percent.

questions.text: If a number 'a' is divisible by 6 and 21, then 5a is divisible by :
questions.explanation: A number divisible by 6 and 21 is a multiple of their LCM, 42, so 5a is a multiple of 210. The others need not divide it: for a = 42, 5a = 210.

questions.text: The total cost price of a book and pen is Rs.371. If the book cost price is 12% more than the pen, find the cost price of the pen.
questions.explanation: With the pen at x, the book costs 1.12x: 2.12x = 371, so x = Rs. 175.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Initial
questions.explanation: 'Initial' means at the beginning; its opposite is 'terminal', at the end. 'Inaugural' is close to 'initial'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Let the cat out of the bag
questions.explanation: To 'let the cat out of the bag' is to give away a secret, usually by mistake.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. They “eating” “three” apples “after” last “night's” dinner.
questions.explanation: The sentence has no finite verb: 'They eating' needs the past tense, 'They ate three apples after last night's dinner.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Latent
questions.explanation: 'Latent' means present but hidden or not yet developed; its opposite is 'obvious'. 'Dormant' is close to 'latent'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Salty
questions.explanation: 'Saline' means containing salt, that is 'salty'. 'Feline' means of cats and 'prim' stiffly proper.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Adamant
questions.explanation: 'Adamant' means refusing to change one's mind: 'stubborn'. 'Lax' and 'flexible' are its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Advancement in science and technology in many areas ________ the lives of people more advanced than the ancient times.
questions.explanation: The subject 'Advancement' is singular and the verb takes an object ('the lives of people'), so the active 'has made' fits; 'have made' needs a plural subject, and 'was made' and 'is made' are passive.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'mischievous', with 'ie' and no 'i' after the 'v'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate set of words to complete the sentence. While teaching my son how to drive a car, I told him if he didn’t hit the _______ in time he would _________ the car’s side mirror.
questions.explanation: A 'brake' stops a car, and to 'break' is to smash or damage: he must hit the brake in time or he would break the mirror.

questions.text: Select the correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Many people across the globe “have been effected” by the pandemic.
questions.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to act on or harm; 'effect' as a verb means to bring about. With the plural 'people': 'have been affected'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Sow wild oats
questions.explanation: To 'sow (one's) wild oats' is to behave wildly or irresponsibly while young, especially to have many casual sexual relationships.

questions.text: Identify the correctly spelt sentence.
options: The water cycle is a circular process.
The water cycle is a circuler proces.
The water cycle is a circqlar process.
The water cycle is a circular proces.
questions.explanation: Only this sentence spells both 'circular' and 'process' correctly; the others have 'circuler', 'circqlar' or 'proces'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Rare
questions.explanation: 'Rare' means not often found or seen; of the options its opposite is 'usual'. 'Unique' is close to 'rare'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Propagate
questions.explanation: To 'propagate' is to spread or multiply; 'deplete', to reduce in number or amount, runs against it. 'Disseminate', 'spread' and 'communicate' are close to 'propagate'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The “reported alarm” of the earthquake scared every citizen of the country.
questions.explanation: It was a report that caused alarm: 'The alarming report of the earthquake scared every citizen of the country.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Humans have (1)________ that animals do not have a life and maybe exploited in any way they see fit, but this (2)________ is incorrect and must be altered before it is too late. We fail to recognise that the pain we (3)________ on animals will come back to haunt us, and no matter how (4)_______ the discovery we make by causing harm to animals, it will be futile. It can never (5)_________ the human actions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Humans have 'assumed', that is taken for granted without proof, that animals do not have a life.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Humans have (1)________ that animals do not have a life and maybe exploited in any way they see fit, but this (2)________ is incorrect and must be altered before it is too late. We fail to recognise that the pain we (3)________ on animals will come back to haunt us, and no matter how (4)_______ the discovery we make by causing harm to animals, it will be futile. It can never (5)_________ the human actions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The belief just described is a point of view, a 'perspective', which can be wrong and can be altered; a 'fact' cannot be incorrect.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Humans have (1)________ that animals do not have a life and maybe exploited in any way they see fit, but this (2)________ is incorrect and must be altered before it is too late. We fail to recognise that the pain we (3)________ on animals will come back to haunt us, and no matter how (4)_______ the discovery we make by causing harm to animals, it will be futile. It can never (5)_________ the human actions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: One 'inflicts' pain on someone, that is makes them suffer it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Humans have (1)________ that animals do not have a life and maybe exploited in any way they see fit, but this (2)________ is incorrect and must be altered before it is too late. We fail to recognise that the pain we (3)________ on animals will come back to haunt us, and no matter how (4)_______ the discovery we make by causing harm to animals, it will be futile. It can never (5)_________ the human actions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'No matter how significant the discovery' means however important it may be, which makes the point that it is futile all the same.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Humans have (1)________ that animals do not have a life and maybe exploited in any way they see fit, but this (2)________ is incorrect and must be altered before it is too late. We fail to recognise that the pain we (3)________ on animals will come back to haunt us, and no matter how (4)_______ the discovery we make by causing harm to animals, it will be futile. It can never (5)_________ the human actions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: No discovery can 'justify' the human actions, that is show them to be right.

questions.text: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 7, 21, 35, ?, 63
questions.explanation: The terms go up by 14 each time (7 × 1, 7 × 3, 7 × 5 and so on): 35 + 14 = 49, and 49 + 14 = 63.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 235, 271, ?, 349, 391, 435
Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Fountain 2 Found 3 Fond 4 Focus 5 Follow
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: focus (4), follow (5), fond (3), found (2), fountain (1). 'Foc', 'fol' and 'fon' follow the alphabet, and 'found' comes before 'fountain' as d comes before t.

questions.text: Which of the mathematical signs should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct? 17 + 98 ÷ 14 - 8 × 68 = 179
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 120 ÷ 15 + 60 - 4 × 2 = 135
In a certain code language, ‘EARTH’ is written as ‘AERHT’ and ‘VENUS’ is written as ‘EVNSU’. How will ‘PLANT’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first two letters change places, the middle one stays and the last two change places: EA-R-TH → AE-R-HT and VE-N-US → EV-N-SU. So PL-A-NT → LP-A-TN: LPATN.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. STATEMENTS: A. All boxes are pans. B. Some boxes are jugs. C. Some jugs are glasses. CONCLUSIONS: I. Some glasses are boxes. II. No glass is a box. III. Some jugs are pans.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: Some boxes are jugs and all boxes are pans, so those jugs are pans: some jugs are pans (III). Nothing links glasses to boxes, so neither I nor II follows on its own.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. PJM : LHM :: NSV : UQK :: JTW : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves back 3, 2 and 1 places and the cluster is then reversed: PJM → MHL → LHM and NSV → KQU → UQK. So JTW → GRV → VRG.

questions.text: 8 friends A, B, C, D, E, F, G, and H are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. A is the immediate neighbour of B and C. H is the immediate neighbour of F and G. D is sitting to the immediate left of B. E is sitting to the immediate right of C. A and H are sitting opposite each other. Who is sitting immediate right of B?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, left is clockwise. B and C sit on either side of A, and D, on B's immediate left, must be on the side away from A, so B is on A's left; E sits on C's right. Going clockwise: E, C, A, B, D, with H opposite A between F and G. The person on B's immediate right is A.

questions.text: Anil, Bunty, Choubey, Dishant, and Eshan are five students sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Dishant sits to the immediate right of Anil. Choubey is not sitting next to Dishant or Anil. Eshan is sitting to the immediate right of Choubey. Who is sitting to the immediate right of Dishant?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, right is anticlockwise. Of the five seats only the one across from the pair Anil-Dishant is next to neither, so Choubey sits there; Eshan, on Choubey's right, is next to Anil, and Bunty takes the seat between Choubey and Dishant, on Dishant's right.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (13, 150, 17); (10, 130, 16)
questions.explanation: The middle number is five times the sum of the other two: (13 + 17) × 5 = 150 and (10 + 16) × 5 = 130. Likewise (8 + 19) × 5 = 135; the other sets would need 130, 145 and 150.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter-cluster series? EU, CS, YQ, SO, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters go back 2, 4, 6 and 8 places (E, C, Y, S, K), wrapping round after A, and the second letters go back 2 each time (U, S, Q, O, M): KM.

questions.text: ‘A – B’ means ‘B is the mother of A’; ‘A # B’ means ‘B is the sister of A’; ‘A $ B’ means ‘B is the husband of A’; If A – B # C – D $ E, then how is E related to A?
questions.explanation: B is A's mother and C is B's sister; D is C's mother, and so B's too, and E is D's husband. So E is A's mother's father.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Slavery : Liberty :: Hate : ?
questions.explanation: Liberty is the opposite of slavery, as love is the opposite of hate.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? PBXJ, TFJX, ?, BNJX, FRXJ
questions.explanation: The first two letters each move +4 (P, T, X, B, F and B, F, J, N, R), wrapping round after Z, and the last two alternate between XJ and JX: XJXJ.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘cat pen’ is coded ‘tin de’, ‘animal tiger’ is coded as ‘sin xe’, and ‘pen tiger’ is coded as ‘de xe’, What is the code word for ‘cat’?
questions.explanation: 'Pen' is in the first and third messages, so it is 'de'; 'tiger' is in the second and third, so it is 'xe'. That leaves 'tin' for 'cat'.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of the electric potential difference?
questions.explanation: The volt is the SI unit of electric potential difference: one joule of work per coulomb of charge. The watt is the unit of power, the ampere of current and the joule of energy.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Name the movement that started at Naxalbari in Darjeeling district in West Bengal in 1967.
questions.explanation: The Naxalite movement takes its name from the peasant uprising at Naxalbari, in Darjeeling district of West Bengal, in 1967.

questions.text: Sudip Roy Barman became Member of Legislative Assembly from _____ constituency in June 2022.
questions.explanation: Sudip Roy Barman, who had left the BJP for the Congress, won the Agartala seat in Tripura in the by-election held on 23 June 2022.

questions.text: During which season do North-east trade winds dominate India?
questions.explanation: In the winter (cold weather) season the north-east trade winds prevail over India, blowing from land to sea, so the season is largely dry over most of the country.

questions.text: Which of the following is a summer cropping season in India?
questions.explanation: Zaid crops, such as watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber and fodder crops, are grown in the short summer season between the rabi and kharif seasons.

questions.text: Which of the following Union Territories does NOT have a lieutenant governor?
questions.explanation: Daman and Diu was run by an Administrator, not a Lieutenant Governor, and since January 2020 has been part of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, also under an Administrator. Delhi, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Puducherry each have a Lieutenant Governor.

questions.text: Name the disorder tied to body image distortion in adolescence.
questions.explanation: Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder, usually beginning in adolescence, in which a distorted view of one's own body leads to severe restriction of food.

questions.text: What was the birth rate of India in 2017?
questions.explanation: The Sample Registration System put India's crude birth rate for 2017 at 20.2 live births per 1,000 people, down from 20.4 in 2016.

questions.text: Who among the following players received the Arjuna Award for the year 2001?
questions.explanation: Parminder (also spelt Parmender) Singh, the basketball player, was among the recipients of the Arjuna Award for 2001.

questions.text: A situation in which the government may spend an amount equal to the revenue it collects is :
questions.explanation: In a balanced budget the government's expenditure equals its revenue; a deficit budget spends more than it collects and a surplus budget less.

questions.text: The central theme of which of the following classical dance forms are the love stories of Krishna and Radha?
questions.explanation: The Ras Lila, the love of Radha and Krishna, is the central theme of Manipuri dance, which grew out of Vaishnava devotion in Manipur.

questions.text: Who among the following Mauryan emperors was known by the name of Piyadassi?
questions.explanation: Ashoka calls himself 'Devanampiya Piyadasi' (beloved of the gods, of gracious look) in his edicts; the Maski edict names him as Ashoka.

questions.text: Startup India Seed Fund Scheme (SISFS) was launched by ________ on 19th April 2021.
questions.explanation: Piyush Goyal, then Minister of Commerce and Industry, launched the Startup India Seed Fund Scheme on 19 April 2021, with ₹945 crore to give startups early-stage funding.

questions.text: Geographically, which is the smallest state of India?
questions.explanation: Goa, about 3,702 sq km, is the smallest state of India by area.

questions.text: The Halda festival is primarily celebrated in which of the following states of India?
questions.explanation: Halda is a festival of the Lahaul area of Himachal Pradesh, in which people gather with burning cedar twigs at a common bonfire and pray to the goddess of wealth.

questions.text: In which year was the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) established by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports set up the Target Olympic Podium Scheme in September 2014 to support India's best medal prospects for the Olympics.

questions.text: Yamini Krishnamurthy has won various accolades in which form of dance?
questions.explanation: Yamini Krishnamurthy was a leading dancer of both Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi.

questions.text: The main focus of the First Five Year Plan was to develop the __________sector like agriculture.
questions.explanation: The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) put agriculture, a primary-sector activity, first, with irrigation and power projects to raise food output.

questions.text: How many Fundamental rights are provided by Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Constitution provides six Fundamental Rights; the right to property, once the seventh, was removed from the list by the 44th Amendment in 1978.

questions.text: Who has been appointed as India's next High Commissioner to Canada in September 2022?
questions.explanation: In September 2022 the Ministry of External Affairs named Sanjay Kumar Verma, then India's Ambassador to Japan, as the next High Commissioner to Canada.

questions.text: If 2P = 3Q = 5R and P + Q + R = 6200, then the difference between P and R is:
questions.explanation: Take 2P = 3Q = 5R = k: P = k/2, Q = k/3 and R = k/5, so P + Q + R = 31k/30 = 6200 and k = 6000. P = 3000 and R = 1200, a difference of 1800.

questions.text: Anil and Bablu can do a given piece of work in 50 days, Bablu and Candy can do the same work in 60 days, and Anil, Bablu, and Candy complete it in 30 days. Find the number of days required by Bablu to finish the total work.
questions.explanation: Anil does 1/30 − 1/60 = 1/60 of the work a day, so Bablu does 1/50 − 1/60 = (6 − 5)/300 = 1/300 a day and takes 300 days.

questions.text: From place A to B, which are 50 km apart, T covers half of the distance in 20 minutes. What should be his speed (in km/h) in the second half so that his average speed from A to B is 80 km/h?
questions.explanation: At 80 km/h the 50 km should take 50/80 h = 37.5 minutes. The first 25 km took 20 minutes, leaving 17.5 minutes = 7/24 h for the other 25 km: 25 ÷ (7/24) = 600/7 ≈ 85.7 km/h.

questions.text: A buys 150 gm gold for Rs.6,00,000 and gives 6% as making charges. What should be the selling price per 10 gm to have a profit of 6%?
questions.explanation: With 6% making charges the cost is ₹6,00,000 × 1.06 = ₹6,36,000, and a 6% profit makes the selling price ₹6,36,000 × 1.06 = ₹6,74,160 for 150 gm. Per 10 gm: 6,74,160 ÷ 15 = ₹44,944.

questions.text: The population of a country increases by 8% in the first year, depreciates by 10% in the second year and again increases by 6% in the third year. If the present population is 6 crore, find the population growth after 3 years.

Due to delay in submission of an assignment the marks of Suhani were decreased by 10 percent and she got 135 marks. What could have been her marks in the assignment, if there was no delay in submission?
questions.explanation: 135 marks is 90% of the full marks, so without the cut she would have had 135 ÷ 0.9 = 150.

questions.text: An aeroplane flies along the four sides of a square field at the speeds of 150 km/h, 300 km/h, 450 km/h and 600 km/h. Find the average speed of the plane around the field.
questions.explanation: Each side is the same distance d, so the average speed is 4d divided by d/150 + d/300 + d/450 + d/600 = 25d/1800: 4 × 1800/25 = 288 km/h.

questions.text: The average of the following numbers is 25. Find the value of X. 24, 30, 12, 18, 20, 10, 40, X
questions.explanation: The eight numbers add up to 8 × 25 = 200, and the seven given add up to 154, so X = 200 − 154 = 46.

questions.text: If a conical vessel has a radius of 4 cm and volume of 16π cm³, then its curved surface area is:
questions.explanation: 1/3 × π × 4² × h = 16π gives h = 3 cm, so the slant height is √(4² + 3²) = 5 cm and the curved surface area πrl = π × 4 × 5 = 20π cm².

questions.text: A class teacher conducted a unit test in the class. If out of 30 students, 14 students scored 80 and rest 16 students scored 65, then what is the weighted average score?
What will be the remainder when 3²⁷ is divided by 26?
questions.explanation: 3³ = 27 leaves 1 when divided by 26, so 3²⁷ = (3³)⁹ leaves 1⁹ = 1.

questions.text: The product of 2 numbers is 1890 and the numbers differ by 3. Find the LCM of the numbers.
questions.explanation: The numbers are 42 and 45 (42 × 45 = 1890). Their HCF is 3, and as HCF × LCM = product, the LCM is 1890 ÷ 3 = 630.

questions.text: Seema purchased a boat that cost her for Rs.3200 and marked price is Rs.4000. How much discount she get ?
questions.explanation: The discount is the marked price less the price paid: ₹4,000 − ₹3,200 = ₹800.

questions.text: The marked price of a product is Rs. 1000. If it is sold at 7 percent discount and the dealer earns 50 percent profit, then what is the cost price of the product?
questions.explanation: The selling price is 93% of ₹1,000 = ₹930, which is 150% of the cost: 930 ÷ 1.5 = ₹620.

questions.text: Find the compound interest on Rs.1,000 at 20% per annum for one year if interest is compounded half-yearly.
questions.explanation: Compounded half-yearly, 20% a year is 10% for each of two half-years: ₹1,000 × 1.1² = ₹1,210, so the interest is ₹210.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'achieve'; 'mischief', 'perceive' and 'receive' are spelt correctly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Pull yourself together
questions.explanation: To 'pull yourself together' is to get control of your feelings and calm down after being upset.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Arun has experienced severe mental and emotional turmoil, as well as interpersonal ________ at times.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'numbness': the sentence is about feelings, and emotional numbness, a loss of feeling towards other people, often goes with severe emotional turmoil. 'Fatigue' is arguable, but 'interpersonal' fits a loss of feeling for others better than tiredness; 'dizziness' is physical and 'symptoms' too vague to fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Early
questions.explanation: 'Early' means before the usual or expected time, so 'beforehand' (in advance) is closest. 'Late' and 'tardy' are its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Flatter
questions.explanation: To 'flatter' is to praise someone too much in order to please them; the opposite is to 'insult'. 'Adulate' and 'cajole' are close to 'flatter'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. Watching the singer perform live at the concert ________ (alert) the audience for a moment.
questions.explanation: To 'alert' people is to make them watchful; the opposite is to 'distract' them, to draw their attention away. 'Shunned' means avoided, and 'called' and 'summoned' are not opposites of 'alerted'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks and make the sentence meaningful. I taught my son the ________ way to tie a ________.
questions.explanation: 'Right' means correct, and a 'knot' is what is tied in a string or lace; 'write' and 'not' sound the same but make no sense here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. When I was young, “I can memorise lessons faster than Mohan.”
options: I could memorise lessons faster to Mohan
I could memorise lessons faster than Mohan
I can memorise lessons faster to Mohan
questions.explanation: 'When I was young' sets the sentence in the past, so 'can' becomes 'could', and a comparison takes 'than', not 'to': 'I could memorise lessons faster than Mohan.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Obstruct
questions.explanation: To 'obstruct' is to get in the way of something: to 'block' it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I was “very much surprised” to see Mariam at the party.
questions.explanation: 'Astonished' means greatly surprised, and says 'very much surprised' in one word. 'Aghast' means shocked and horrified, which is more than surprise.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Encircle
questions.explanation: To 'encircle' is to surround and so enclose; the opposite is to 'exclude', to shut out. 'Embrace' is close to 'encircle'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. Even though his car was badly damaged in the accident, Rohan did “not turn a hair”.
questions.explanation: Someone who does 'not turn a hair' stays completely calm and shows no sign of being upset or afraid.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Dad, will you get me a box of crayons / on your way home? Teacher told us yesterday, “You must bring / a box of crayons with you to the drawing class./ Or I will not be let you stay in the class.”
options: Or I will not be let you stay in the class”.
on your way home? Teacher said yesterday, “You must bring
Dad, will you get me a box of crayons
a box of crayons with you to the drawing class.
questions.explanation: 'Will not be let you stay' mixes the passive 'be let' with an object: it should be 'Or I will not let you stay in the class.' The other parts are correct (the options print the second one with 'said' for the sentence's 'told us').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. Those who have________ (humility) will definitely fall down.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'humility' is 'pride', and, as the proverb has it, pride goes before a fall.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Advertising (1) _______ initially meant to make people aware of the goods available in the market. It was as simple as announcing what you have in your store or the services you offer on your (2) ______. Over the years, advertising has evolved into a major industry that goes beyond informing, persuading and influencing. It is a form of brainwashing consumers. Advertising has become a type of culture with ardent followers. In the process, it attracts enviable attention from manufacturers and service providers who fancy an (3) _______ over their competitors. Unfortunately, in keeping with the ever-increasing demands of the manufacturers, the advertisers have resulted in creating unnecessary wants and (4) _______ consumption in most of us. This is a craving for harmful products that we are better off without. It (5) ______ on our minds rendering us completely irrational. The billboards (hoardings), television and radio advertisements target us from a very early age, forming our view of the world as we grow into adults. The buzzwords in advertising are, ‘you are cool and sophisticated’ if you use this or that product.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The passage tells what advertising once was, so the past singular 'was' is needed: 'Advertising was initially meant to make people aware'.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: Some doctors are scholars. All scholars are intelligent. All intelligent are smart. Conclusions: I. Some doctors are smart. II. All scholars are smart.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: The doctors who are scholars are intelligent and so smart, so some doctors are smart (I). Every scholar is intelligent and every intelligent person is smart, so all scholars are smart (II).

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘heaven plate’ is coded as ‘flower rage’, ‘curtain kingdom’ is coded as ‘computer blanket, ‘kingdom plate’ is coded as ‘blanket rage’, and ‘heaven curtain’ is coded as ‘flower computer’. What is the code word for ‘kingdom’?
questions.explanation: 'Kingdom' is in 'curtain kingdom' and 'kingdom plate', whose only common code word is 'blanket'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, FUTURE is written as ‘KWYWWG’, and SHREWD is written as ‘XJWGBF’. How will ‘SAILOR’ be written in the same code language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +5 and +2 in turn: FUTURE → KWYWWG and SHREWD → XJWGBF (W + 5 wraps round to B). So SAILOR → XCNNTT.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 112 - 8 + 96 ÷ 16 × 20 = 0

A,B,C,D,E and F are six friends sitting around a circular table, facing the centre of the table. B is the immediate neighbour of C and E. A is the immediate neighbour of F and D.F is sitting to the immediate left of C. Who is sitting between A and E?
questions.explanation: B sits between C and E, and A between F and D. With F next to C, the order round the table is E, B, C, F, A, D, so D sits between A and E.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed) (15, 16, 155); (12, 13, 125)
questions.explanation: The third number is 5 times the sum of the first two: (15 + 16) × 5 = 155 and (12 + 13) × 5 = 125. Likewise (18 + 12) × 5 = 150.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word.) (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Guilt : Innocence ::Jovial : ?
questions.explanation: 'Innocence' is the opposite of 'guilt'; the opposite of 'jovial' (cheerful) is 'gloomy'.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? CXGZ, FUJW, IRMT, ?, OLSN
questions.explanation: The first and third letters move 3 forward (C, F, I, L, O and G, J, M, P, S) and the second and fourth 3 back (X, U, R, O, L and Z, W, T, Q, N): LOPQ.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 double 2 doctor 3 domestic 4 domicile 5 document
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: doctor (2), document (5), domestic (3), domicile (4), double (1). 'Doct' comes before 'docu', 'doc' before 'dom', 'dome' before 'domi', and 'dom' before 'dou'.

questions.text: Nicole is Dion’s sister. Vanessa is Dion’s mother. Raj is Vanessa’s father. Anjali is Raj’s mother. Paul is Raj’s father. How is Vanessa related to Nicole?
questions.explanation: Nicole is Dion's sister and Vanessa is Dion's mother, so Vanessa is Nicole's mother; the other relations do not matter.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. HIGH: SGRJ :: MOVE: NMCG :: BEAT: ?
questions.explanation: The first letter becomes its opposite (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on), the second moves 2 back, the third becomes its opposite and then moves 2 back, and the fourth moves 2 forward: HIGH → SGRJ and MOVE → NMCG. So BEAT → YCXV.

questions.text: Six friends are sitting in a circle. All of them are facing the centre.Palak is an immediate neighbour of Kumud. Jhalak sits third to the left of Mehak. Rahat sits fourth to the right of Jhalak. Kumud sits second to the right of Chahak. Who sits third to the right of Rahat?
questions.explanation: As all face the centre, each one's left runs clockwise. Clockwise the order is Mehak, Palak, Kumud, Jhalak, Chahak, Rahat: Jhalak is opposite Mehak, Rahat is on Mehak's immediate right, Kumud is second to Chahak's right and Palak sits beside Kumud. Third to the right of Rahat, the seat opposite, is Kumud.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? MKLJ, NLMK, OMNL, ? , QOPN
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward from one cluster to the next: OMNL → PNOM, and PNOM → QOPN.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 20 + 34 - 81 × 9 ÷ 2 = 36
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 3, 5, 9, ? , 33, 65
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before minus 1: 9 × 2 − 1 = 17, then 17 × 2 − 1 = 33 and 33 × 2 − 1 = 65.

questions.text: In which of the following locations can you build large dams to generate hydel power?
questions.explanation: Hydel power needs a large fall of water, so big dams are built across rivers in hilly terrain, where deep valleys and fast-flowing rivers give the height and flow needed.

questions.text: Who is the new Secretary of The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) effective from 1st August 2022?
questions.explanation: Himanshu Pathak took charge as Secretary of the Department of Agricultural Research and Education and Director General of ICAR on 1 August 2022, succeeding Trilochan Mohapatra.

questions.text: Mitochondria have ______ membrane coverings.
questions.explanation: A mitochondrion is bounded by two membranes: a smooth outer one and an inner one folded into cristae.

questions.text: Which of the following martial dances is related to Uttarakhand?
questions.explanation: Choliya (Chholiya) is the sword dance of Kumaon in Uttarakhand, performed at weddings. Thang-ta is from Manipur, Kalaripayattu from Kerala and Gatka from Punjab.

questions.text: ___________ is used to control the demand and supply of money.
questions.explanation: Credit control is the set of tools, such as the policy rates, the reserve ratios and open market operations, with which the Reserve Bank of India regulates the supply of and demand for money and credit.

questions.text: Who among the following became the 49th Chief Justice of India in August 2022?
questions.explanation: Justice Uday Umesh Lalit was sworn in as the 49th Chief Justice of India on 27 August 2022, succeeding N. V. Ramana. The other three are senior advocates.

questions.text: In which layer of the earth do natural earthquakes occur?
questions.explanation: Natural earthquakes take place in the lithosphere, the rigid outer shell of crust and upper mantle, where stress built up in the rocks is released along faults.

questions.text: The proportion of India's GDP contributed by the ___________ sector increased in the period from 11.8 per cent in 1950-51 to 24.6 per cent in 1990-91.
questions.explanation: Industry's share of GDP grew under the Five-Year Plans of those years, while agriculture's share fell. Services already made up a far larger share than 11.8% in 1950-51, and 'defence' is not a sector of the economy.

questions.text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution talks about the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
questions.explanation: Article 149 sets out the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor General; Article 148 creates the office.

questions.text: __________is the chairperson of National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog, as on November 2022.
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister is the ex officio chairperson of NITI Aayog, and Narendra Modi was Prime Minister in November 2022 and when the exam was held (January 2023).

questions.text: ______________(ODOP) aims to reap the benefit of scale in terms of procurement of inputs, availing common services and marketing of products.
questions.explanation: The One District One Product (ODOP) approach picks a product for each district so that its producers gain scale in buying inputs, sharing common services and marketing; the PM Formalisation of Micro food processing Enterprises (PMFME) scheme adopts this approach.

questions.text: In how many phases was the last Census of 2011 conducted in India?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 was taken in two phases: house-listing and housing census (April to September 2010) and population enumeration (9 to 28 February 2011).

questions.text: The Brabourne Cricket Stadium is located in which of the following state of India?
questions.explanation: The Brabourne Stadium, home of the Cricket Club of India, is at Churchgate in Mumbai, Maharashtra.

questions.text: To develop scientific temper and humanism is a:
questions.explanation: Article 51A(h) makes it a Fundamental Duty of every citizen to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.

questions.text: When did Ashoka, the Mauryan ruler, die?
questions.explanation: Ashoka, who came to the throne in about 268 BC, is generally held to have died in about 232 BC.

questions.text: The couple who won Padma Bhushan in 2009 for Bharatanatyam is ______________.
options: K.V. Sampath Kumar and Vidushi K.S. Jayalakshmi
Vannadil Pudiyaveettil Dhananjayan and Shanta Dhananjayan
questions.explanation: The Bharatanatyam dancers V. P. Dhananjayan and Shanta Dhananjayan, trained at Kalakshetra, received the Padma Bhushan in 2009.

questions.text: Jeev Milkha Singh’s became the first player from India to join the European Tour in 1998. He won: (i) four European Tour Titles (ii) four Japan Golf Tour titles (iii) six Asian Tour tiles
questions.explanation: Jeev Milkha Singh, the first Indian on the European Tour (1998), had won four European Tour, four Japan Golf Tour and six Asian Tour titles when the exam was held (January 2023), so all three are true.

questions.text: Which industry do cotton, jute, silk, woollen textiles, sugar and edible oil, etc. belong to ?
questions.explanation: These industries take their raw materials from agriculture: cotton, jute, silk and wool for textiles, sugarcane for sugar and oilseeds for edible oil.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In ______, the East India Company acquired a charter from the ruler of England, Queen Elizabeth I, granting it the sole right to trade with the East.
questions.explanation: Queen Elizabeth I granted the East India Company its charter on 31 December 1600, giving it the sole right among English merchants to trade with the East.

questions.text: The harvest festival ‘Nabanna’ is celebrated in _________ .
questions.explanation: Nabanna ('new rice') is the harvest festival of West Bengal, held when the new paddy is gathered in and celebrated with dishes of the new rice.

questions.text: Two successive discounts of 50 percent and 40 percent are equivalent to a single discount of ______.
questions.explanation: The price paid is 0.5 × 0.6 = 0.3 of the marked price, so the single discount is 70%.

questions.text: Given that 15% of X’s income = 20% of Y’s income = 30% of Z’s income. The sum of their incomes is ₹9,000. If Y spends ₹2,200 from his income, then Y’s saving is:
Find the HCF of 2800 and 756.
questions.explanation: 2800 = 2⁴ × 5² × 7 and 756 = 2² × 3³ × 7, so the HCF is 2² × 7 = 28.

questions.text: A and B can complete a piece of work in 8 days and 16 days respectively. If A and B work on alternate days, starting with B, in how many days the work will be completed?
questions.explanation: Take the work as 16 units: A does 2 a day and B 1. Each pair of days (B, then A) does 3 units, so 10 days do 15 units, and B finishes the last unit on day 11.

questions.text: P and Q together can do a job in 15 days. P is thrice as efficient as Q. In how many days can P alone do the job?
questions.explanation: P does 3 units a day and Q 1, so the job is 15 × 4 = 60 units, and P alone takes 60 ÷ 3 = 20 days.

questions.text: A dishonest retailer sells his goods at a profit of 18% by weighing 800 g instead of 1 kg. Find his actual gain percentage.
A certain number is subtracted from each of the numbers 20,24 and 29. After subtraction, those numbers are in proportional. What is the number subtracted?
questions.explanation: (20 − x)(29 − x) = (24 − x)² gives 580 − 49x = 576 − 48x, so x = 4. Then 16, 20 and 25 are in continued proportion, as 16 × 25 = 20².

questions.text: Simplify the following expression. [7 ÷ 2 × (8.35 + 1.3 + 2.42)]
There are 75 boys and 45 girls in a class. If the average weight of boys is 60 kg and the average weight of girls is 40 kg, then find the average weight of the whole class.
What is the fourth proportional to 0.12, 0.16 and 0.21?
The speed of a swimmer in downstream is 23km/h. If the speed of the swimmer in upstream is 14 km/h, then what is the speed of the stream?
questions.explanation: Speed of the stream = (downstream − upstream)/2 = (23 − 14)/2 = 4.5 km/h.

questions.text: The population of a village increases by 0.2% in the first year, it increases by 0.4% in the second year, and due to some disease, it decreases by 0.4% in the third year. What will be its population after 3 years, if in the beginning of the first year it was 2000 (rounded off to two decimal places)?
A sum of Rs.2,100 is invested for 1 year at 20% per annum, interest compounded half-yearly. Find the compound interest.
questions.explanation: Half-yearly, the rate is 10% for each of 2 periods: 2,100 × 1.1² = Rs.2,541, so the compound interest is Rs.441.

questions.text: On a tool whose marked price is Rs.280, a discount of 15% is offered. Due to a calculation mistake, the shopkeeper gives the customer Rs.20 extra. What is the effective discount percentage on the tool for the customer?
questions.explanation: The discount is 15% of 280 = Rs.42, and with the Rs.20 extra the customer saves Rs.62: 62/280 × 100 = 22.14%, about 22.1%.

questions.text: Select the correct word for the blanks in the given sentence. He has a __________ nature and the rainforest is a __________ of forest found on earth.
questions.explanation: 'Kind' fits both blanks: as an adjective it means caring ('a kind nature') and as a noun a type ('a kind of forest'). 'Type', 'caring' and 'rude' each fit only one blank.

questions.text: Substitute the underlined words with the option that is closest in meaning to it. “Do not pay attention to” his words.
questions.explanation: To 'ignore' something is to pay no attention to it: 'Ignore his words.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A man of means
options: A well-mannered man with noble behaviour
A wealthy man with lots of money and assets
Someone who is an iconic personality for youngsters
Someone who has earned a lot of fame
questions.explanation: A 'man of means' is a rich man, one with money and property.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate spelling that can correctly substitute the misspelt underlined segment in the given sentence. His part in the affair was quite open and “abboard”.
questions.explanation: 'Aboveboard' means open and honest, with nothing hidden: 'quite open and aboveboard'. 'Aboard' means on a ship or vehicle.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The children sat by the “hearth” to keep away the cold.
questions.explanation: The 'hearth' is the floor of a fireplace, so to sit by the hearth is to sit at the 'fireside'. A 'tandoor' and an 'oven' are for cooking, and a 'convent' is a religious house.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Local
questions.explanation: 'Local' means belonging to one's own place or area; its opposite is 'foreign', from another country or place.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence to make it a meaningful sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. The patients “are shifted to another hospital that same evening as this hospital caught fire”.
options: were shifted at others hospital that same evening as this hospital caught fire.
were shifted to another hospital that same evening as this hospital caught fire.
were shifted to another hospital that same evening as this hospital catch fire.
questions.explanation: The fire was in the past ('that same evening', 'caught fire'), so the verb must be the past passive 'were shifted', with 'to another hospital'. 'At others hospital' is ungrammatical, and 'catch' breaks the tense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Those songs were a great relief for Mohan during his long and _________ bus journey.
questions.explanation: A long bus journey is 'tiring', which is why the songs were a relief. 'Tolerable' and 'plausible' do not fit the sense, and 'reprimanding' means scolding.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in the bracket to fill in the blank. Do any of you ________ (object to) the decision?
questions.explanation: To 'object to' something is to oppose it; the opposite is to 'approve of' it: 'Do any of you approve of the decision?'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into three segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Don’t panic! / We won’t leave you alone in trouble / when you travelling with us.
options: We won’t leave you alone in trouble
questions.explanation: The continuous tense needs the helping verb 'are': 'when you are travelling with us' (or 'when you travel with us').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Entrap
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'implicate'. The two are not exact synonyms, but both can mean drawing someone into trouble: to 'entrap' is to trap or trick someone into a crime or difficulty, and to 'implicate' is to involve someone in a crime or wrongdoing. 'Trim', 'regulate' and 'glorify' have nothing to do with either.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'refrigeration', with no 'd'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Grease someone’s palm
options: To give a loan to someone
To borrow money from an official
To lend money to an official
questions.explanation: To 'grease someone's palm' is to bribe them, paying them quietly to get something done.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. “Where is my _________ ?” cried the boatman.
questions.explanation: A boatman rows with an 'oar'. 'Or' and 'o'er' (over) sound the same but make no sense here, and 'oat' is a cereal grain.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Lovely
questions.explanation: 'Lovely' means very pleasant or beautiful; 'lousy' means very bad or poor. 'Pretty', 'attractive' and 'hunky' are close to 'lovely'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Dandelion is a widely distributed weed of the daisy family, (1) _____ a rosette of leaves and large bright yellow flowers followed (2) ______ globular heads of seeds with downy tufts. I also reminded them that April is designated as the Month of (3) _____ Military Child. Not many would know that 15 April is the day when we wear purple, or so to say, we ‘purple (4) ________’ to express our solidarity and support (5) ______ the strength and sacrifices of our children, while their fathers are deployed at Siachen Glacier, deserts and on our borders.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'With' means having: a weed of the daisy family 'with a rosette of leaves and large bright yellow flowers'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Dandelion is a widely distributed weed of the daisy family, (1) _____ a rosette of leaves and large bright yellow flowers followed (2) ______ globular heads of seeds with downy tufts. I also reminded them that April is designated as the Month of (3) _____ Military Child. Not many would know that 15 April is the day when we wear purple, or so to say, we ‘purple (4) ________’ to express our solidarity and support (5) ______ the strength and sacrifices of our children, while their fathers are deployed at Siachen Glacier, deserts and on our borders.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Followed by' gives the order of growth: the flowers are followed by globular heads of seeds.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Dandelion is a widely distributed weed of the daisy family, (1) _____ a rosette of leaves and large bright yellow flowers followed (2) ______ globular heads of seeds with downy tufts. I also reminded them that April is designated as the Month of (3) _____ Military Child. Not many would know that 15 April is the day when we wear purple, or so to say, we ‘purple (4) ________’ to express our solidarity and support (5) ______ the strength and sacrifices of our children, while their fathers are deployed at Siachen Glacier, deserts and on our borders.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'The Military Child' stands for military children as a class, and such a name takes 'the': 'the Month of the Military Child'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Dandelion is a widely distributed weed of the daisy family, (1) _____ a rosette of leaves and large bright yellow flowers followed (2) ______ globular heads of seeds with downy tufts. I also reminded them that April is designated as the Month of (3) _____ Military Child. Not many would know that 15 April is the day when we wear purple, or so to say, we ‘purple (4) ________’ to express our solidarity and support (5) ______ the strength and sacrifices of our children, while their fathers are deployed at Siachen Glacier, deserts and on our borders.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: To 'purple up' is to wear purple in support of military children, as the passage says: 'we wear purple, or so to say, we purple up'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Dandelion is a widely distributed weed of the daisy family, (1) _____ a rosette of leaves and large bright yellow flowers followed (2) ______ globular heads of seeds with downy tufts. I also reminded them that April is designated as the Month of (3) _____ Military Child. Not many would know that 15 April is the day when we wear purple, or so to say, we ‘purple (4) ________’ to express our solidarity and support (5) ______ the strength and sacrifices of our children, while their fathers are deployed at Siachen Glacier, deserts and on our borders.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Support is given 'for' someone or something: 'solidarity and support for the strength and sacrifices of our children'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. GKP : FHK :: BJS : AGN :: DIX : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move back 1, 3 and 5 places in turn: G → F, K → H, P → K and B → A, J → G, S → N. So D → C, I → F, X → S: CFS.

questions.text: Which of the numbers(not digits) should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct? 216 ÷ 9 × 16 + 24 - 27 = 126

Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (17, 153, 81) (19, 171, 81)
questions.explanation: In each set the second number is the first times 9 and the third is the square of that multiplier, 9² = 81: 153 = 17 × 9 and 171 = 19 × 9. Likewise 135 = 15 × 9, with 81.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Smell : Nose :: Colours : ?
questions.explanation: Smell is sensed through the nose, and colours are seen with the eyes.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question marks (?) in the given series? 10, 20, 15, ?, ?, 30, 25, 35, 30
questions.explanation: The steps alternate +10 and −5: 10, 20, 15, 25, 20, 30, 25, 35, 30. The missing terms are 25 and 20.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter-cluster series? MNA, WDB, EVA, KPB, OLA, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move forward 10, 8, 6, 4 and 2 places (M, W, E, K, O, Q, wrapping round after Z), the second move back 10, 8, 6, 4 and 2 (N, D, V, P, L, J), and the third alternate A and B: QJB.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 9, ?, 33, 50, 69, 92, 121
questions.explanation: The differences are consecutive prime numbers: 9 + 11 = 20, 20 + 13 = 33, 33 + 17 = 50, 50 + 19 = 69, 69 + 23 = 92 and 92 + 29 = 121.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II & III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some doctors are tigers. All tigers are umbrellas. Some umbrellas are buses. Conclusions: I. Some doctors are umbrellas. II. Some tigers are umbrellas. III. Some buses are umbrellas.
options: Both conclusions I and III follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions II and III follow.
questions.explanation: The doctors who are tigers are umbrellas, so some doctors are umbrellas (I). All tigers are umbrellas, so some tigers certainly are (II), and 'some umbrellas are buses' means some buses are umbrellas (III).

questions.text: Seven people S, F, A, G, D, H, and T are sitting in a straight row, facing north. Only two people sit to the right of G. F is third to the right of A. S is the immediate neighbour to D and A. G is the immediate neighbour to F and H. Who sits at the extreme right of the row?
questions.explanation: With two people to G's right, G is fifth from the left, with F and H on either side. If F is fourth, A is first and the row is A, S, D, F, G, H, T; if F is sixth, A is third and the row is D, S, A, H, G, F, T. Either way T sits at the extreme right.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘LAST’ is written as ‘NCQR’ and ‘CAKE’ is written as ‘ECIC’. How will ‘JUMP’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first two letters move 2 forward and the last two 2 back: LAST → NCQR and CAKE → ECIC. So JUMP → LWKN.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 8 + 32 ÷ 16 × 11 - 5 = 22
questions.explanation: After interchanging + and ×: 8 × 32 ÷ 16 + 11 − 5 = 16 + 11 − 5 = 22.

questions.text: Preethi arranges different colours of teddy bears in her bedroom in two parallel rows facing each other such that four teddies are in each row. Orange, Yellow, Grey and Brown teddies are in Row 1 facing north, while Red, White, Black and Pink teddies are in Row 2 facing south. Orange teddy is adjacent to the Grey teddy. Pink teddy does not face the Orange one. White teddy faces the one that is second to the right of the Grey teddy. The Black one is second to the right of the Pink teddy. The Brown teddy is not at any of the corners. The Orange teddy is not at any of the extreme ends. The Grey teddy faces the Red one. How many teddies are there between Red and White teddies?
questions.explanation: Orange and Brown take the two middle places of Row 1, and Grey, next to Orange, needs a teddy second to its right, so Row 1 runs Grey, Orange, Brown, Yellow from west to east. Red faces Grey and White faces Brown; Black is second to Pink's right (westward in Row 2), so Black faces Orange and Pink faces Yellow. Row 2 runs Red, Black, White, Pink: one teddy between Red and White.

questions.text: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? GYCQ, ICZR, ?, MKTT, OOQU
questions.explanation: The first letters move 2 forward (G, I, K, M, O), the second 4 forward (Y, C, G, K, O, wrapping round after Z), the third 3 back (C, Z, W, T, Q) and the fourth 1 forward (Q, R, S, T, U): KGWS.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Flower 2 Flow 3 Floor 4 Flour 5 Flame
questions.explanation: Flame comes first ('a' before 'o'). Of the 'Flo' words, Floor ('o') comes before Flour ('u') and Flow ('w'), and Flow before Flower: Flame, Floor, Flour, Flow, Flower, that is 5, 3, 4, 2, 1.

questions.text: ‘X – Y’ means ‘X is the brother of Y’ ‘X # Y’ means ‘X is the daughter of Y’ ‘X * Y’ means ‘X is the father of Y’ ‘X $ Y’ means ‘X is the wife of Y’ If ‘A $ B – D * C’, then how is A related to D?
options: A is the sister-in-law of D
A is the sister of D
A is the daughter of D
A is the son of D
questions.explanation: A is the wife of B, B is the brother of D, and D is the father of C. So A is the wife of D's brother: D's sister-in-law.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘TEA’ is coded as 26 and ‘DANCE’ is coded as 27. How will ‘CROWN’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word's code is the sum of its letters' places in the alphabet: TEA = 20 + 5 + 1 = 26 and DANCE = 4 + 1 + 14 + 3 + 5 = 27. So CROWN = 3 + 18 + 15 + 23 + 14 = 73.

questions.text: How many nations (including EOR and ROC teams) participated in the 2020 Summer Olympics?
questions.explanation: The Tokyo 2020 Summer Olympics, held in 2021, had teams from 206 nations: 205 National Olympic Committees, among them the ROC (the Russian Olympic Committee, competing in place of Russia), and the IOC Refugee Olympic Team (EOR).

questions.text: It connects all types of computers across the world. Which communication technology is being spoken about here?
questions.explanation: The Internet is the worldwide network of networks that links computers of every kind across the world.

questions.text: Which among the following pairs of ore-metal is incorrect?
questions.explanation: Cinnabar (mercury sulphide) is the chief ore of mercury, not nickel. Bornite is an ore of copper, magnetite of iron and galena of lead.

questions.text: After the passage of which Constitutional Amendment Act, are there now six fundamental rights?
questions.explanation: The 44th Amendment Act of 1978 removed the right to property from the Fundamental Rights (repealing Article 31 and deleting Article 19(1)(f)) and made it a legal right under Article 300A, leaving six fundamental rights.

questions.text: Which of the following is the largest tributary of the Indus river?
questions.explanation: The Chenab, formed by the Chandra and the Bhaga in Himachal Pradesh, is the largest tributary of the Indus.

questions.text: Among the given options, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment doesn't patronise _____________.
questions.explanation: The e-Shram portal, a national database of unorganised workers launched in August 2021, belongs to the Ministry of Labour and Employment. Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, the e-Anudaan grants portal and the National Portal for Transgender Persons are run by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

questions.text: As per 2011 census, which Indian state has the lowest literacy rate?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Bihar had the lowest literacy rate of any state, about 62%.

questions.text: As of December 2022, who among the following is the Governor of West Bengal, India?
questions.explanation: C. V. Ananda Bose was appointed Governor of West Bengal on 17 November 2022 and sworn in on 23 November, so he held the office in December 2022. Jagdeep Dhankhar, the earlier Governor, had become Vice-President in August 2022; Mamata Banerjee was then Chief Minister of West Bengal and Ashok Gehlot of Rajasthan.

questions.text: Which of the following Metals of Harappan civilization got from present-day Rajasthan and Oman?
questions.explanation: The Harappans obtained copper from the Khetri area of Rajasthan and, it seems, from Oman, where copper with the same traces of nickel as Harappan artefacts has been found.

questions.text: ___________war took place during fourth five year plan.
questions.explanation: The Fourth Five Year Plan ran from 1969 to 1974, and the India-Pakistan war that led to the creation of Bangladesh was fought in December 1971.

questions.text: Bathukamma, a flower festival, is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Bathukamma, for which women arrange seasonal flowers in tiers and then immerse them in water, is the floral festival of Telangana, held over nine days before Dussehra.

questions.text: In India, the Industrial Policy Resolution was passed in the year ______ for the first time.
questions.explanation: Independent India's first Industrial Policy Resolution was announced on 6 April 1948; the second followed in 1956.

questions.text: The maximum strength of the Lower House of Parliament is:
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 552, the maximum the Constitution set: up to 530 members from the states and 20 from the union territories (Article 81), and up to 2 Anglo-Indians the President could nominate (Article 331). The 104th Amendment (2019) did not extend that nomination, which ended on 25 January 2020, so when the exam was held in January 2023 the maximum was 550, which is not among the options.

questions.text: __________ is defined as the body’s ability to function efficiently and effectively in work and leisure activities, to be healthy, to resist diseases and to meet emergency situations.
questions.explanation: Physical fitness is this overall ability of the body; aerobic fitness and muscular endurance are only parts of it, and mental fitness concerns the mind.

questions.text: E Krishna Iyer was related to which classical dance form?
questions.explanation: E. Krishna Iyer, a lawyer and freedom fighter, performed Bharatanatyam himself and campaigned for its revival in the 1920s and 1930s, when the anti-nautch movement opposed the dance.

questions.text: National Income = C (household consumption) + G(____________) + I (investment expense) + NX (net exports).
questions.explanation: By the expenditure method, national income (GDP) is household consumption + government expenditure + investment + net exports: Y = C + G + I + NX.

questions.text: Ranji Trophy is related to which of the following game?
questions.explanation: The Ranji Trophy, named after the cricketer K. S. Ranjitsinhji, is India's premier domestic first-class cricket championship.

questions.text: Which among the following received the Kerala Sangeet Natak Academy fellowship (1974)?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma, the Mohiniyattam dancer from Kerala. Sources differ on her 1974 honour from the Kerala Sangeetha Nataka Akademi: some call it the Akademi's fellowship, others its award, with the fellowship in 1992. Shovana Narayan is a Kathak dancer and Mahaboob Subhani a nadaswaram player.

questions.text: Which of the following monuments has been declared a national monument by the Prime Minister of India in November 2022?
questions.explanation: At a programme at Mangarh Dham in Banswara district, Rajasthan, on 1 November 2022, the Prime Minister was widely reported to have declared it a national monument. The hill is where troops under British command killed Bhil followers of Govind Guru on 17 November 1913.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Mahatma Gandhi returned to Indian in January ______.
questions.explanation: Gandhi returned to India from South Africa on 9 January 1915, the date now marked as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.

questions.text: A thief started running after seeing a policeman at a distance of 225 m. Instantly, the policeman started chasing the thief. The thief and the police ran at the rate of 9 km/h and 10 km/h respectively. Find the distance between them after 4.2 min.
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 10 − 9 = 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s on the thief. In 4.2 min = 252 s he gains 252 × 5/18 = 70 m, so the gap is 225 − 70 = 155 m.

questions.text: A man gives two successive discounts of 8 percent and 6 percent on a chair, which has the marked price of Rs. 1200. How much would be the selling price of the chair?
Pinky fills her car tank with 20 liters of petrol. She goes on a journey and end up with just 5.5 liters of petrol left in the tank. What is the percent change in the petrol in the tank?
questions.explanation: The petrol falls by 20 − 5.5 = 14.5 litres, and 14.5/20 × 100 = 72.5%, a decrease.

questions.text: On 10 February 2014, a train leaves Delhi at 6 a.m. and reaches Jainagar at 10 a.m.. Another train leaves Jainagar at 8 a.m. and reaches Delhi at 11:30 a.m.. At what time do the two trains cross each other?
questions.explanation: Let the distance be D. The first train takes 4 hours (speed D/4) and the second 3½ hours (speed 2D/7). By 8 a.m. the first has covered half the way; the other half closes at D/4 + 2D/7 = 15D/28 an hour, which takes (D/2) ÷ (15D/28) = 14/15 hour = 56 minutes: 8:56 a.m.

questions.text: A car runs 450 km on 35 litres of petrol. How many kilometres can the car run on 25 litres of petrol (rounded off to two decimal places)?
questions.explanation: The distance is proportional to the petrol: 450 × 25/35 = 2250/7 = 321.43 km.

questions.text: Anay does the 5/11th part of the work in 10 days and Rohan does the 5/6th of the same work in 15 days. They started together but Rohan left the work 5 days before the completion of the work and Anay completed the work. Find the number of days after which Rohan left work.
questions.explanation: Anay alone takes 10 × 11/5 = 22 days and Rohan 15 × 6/5 = 18 days. If the work lasts T days, Rohan works T − 5: T/22 + (T − 5)/18 = 1, so 9T + 11T − 55 = 198 and T = 253/20. Rohan left after 253/20 − 5 = 153/20 days.

questions.text: A and B alone can do a piece of work in 7 days and 14 days respectively. In how many days the work will be completed if they both work on alternate days starting with A?
questions.explanation: A does 1/7 = 2/14 of the work a day and B 1/14, so every two days 3/14 is done. After 8 days 12/14 is done, and on the 9th day A finishes the remaining 2/14.

questions.text: A shopkeeper marks his goods 12% above the cost price and allows 6% discount. What profit percentage does he make?
questions.explanation: The selling price is 1.12 × 0.94 = 1.0528 times the cost price, a profit of 5.28%.

questions.text: In a pharma company, a scientist is mixing the purified form of Acetone and Toluene to invent some medicine. The cost of the solution obtained after mixing Acetone and Toluene is Rs.16 per litre. Acetone costs Rs.14 per litre to the scientist. Due to storage issue, Toluene’s cost is expensive than Acetone to the scientist. The ratio of Toluene to Acetone in the solution is 4 : 1. What is the cost of Toluene per litre (in ₹) to the scientist?
questions.explanation: With Toluene and Acetone in the ratio 4 : 1, (4T + 14)/5 = 16, so 4T = 66 and T = ₹16.5 a litre.

questions.text: If a rectangle has 10 cm long diagonal and perimeter 28 cm, then the area of the rectangle is:
questions.explanation: Length + breadth = 28/2 = 14 and length² + breadth² = 10² = 100. Then 2 × length × breadth = 14² − 100 = 96, so the area is 48 cm².

questions.text: In an election, Rashika and Nikita were against each other. Rashika received 54% votes and won the election by 1280 votes. How many total votes were cast in the election?
questions.explanation: Nikita received 100 − 54 = 46%, so the margin of 1280 votes is 8% of the total: 1280 × 100/8 = 16000.
