questions.text: How much approximate amount will be received on a principal of ₹40,000 at the rate of 8% per annum to be compounded half yearly at the end of one and half years?
questions.explanation: Compounded half-yearly, the rate is 4% for each of 3 half-years: 40,000 × 1.04³ = 40,000 × 1.124864 = ₹44,994.56, about ₹44,995.

questions.text: The average of first five prime number is:
questions.explanation: The first five primes are 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11; their sum is 28, and 28 ÷ 5 = 5.6.

questions.text: A sum of Rs.9,350 was taken as a loan. This is paid in two equal instalments. If the rate of interest is 20% per annum compounded annually, then what is the value of each instalment?
questions.explanation: The loan is the present value of the two instalments x: x/1.2 + x/1.2² = 9,350, so x × 2.2/1.44 = 9,350 and x = 9,350 × 1.44/2.2 = ₹6,120.

questions.text: If a seven-digit number 42971K2 is divisible by 44, then the value of K is:
questions.explanation: 44 = 4 × 11. For 11, the digits in odd places (4 + 9 + 1 + 2 = 16) and in even places (2 + 7 + K = 9 + K) must differ by a multiple of 11, so K = 7; and 72 is divisible by 4.

questions.text: If Ram, Robert and Rahim started a firm by investing ₹50,000, ₹30,000 and ₹40,000 respectively for the same time period, then the ratio of the share of Rahim to that of Robert is _______, out of the profit of ₹18,000.
questions.explanation: For the same period, profit is shared in the ratio of the investments: Rahim : Robert = 40,000 : 30,000 = 4 : 3.

questions.text: Complete the sentence by choosing the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. When you “look” at something you __________ it.
questions.explanation: To 'look' at something is to turn one's eyes to it, that is to 'see' it. 'Hear' and 'touch' belong to other senses, and 'ignore' is the opposite.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in past perfect tense. A. I read a lot about mythology. B. I had been reading a lot about mythology. C. I was reading a lot about mythology. D. I had read a lot about mythology.
questions.explanation: The past perfect is 'had' + past participle: D, 'I had read a lot about mythology.' A is the simple past, B the past perfect continuous and C the past continuous.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. One night, a hunter________ near a river when he began to dream.
questions.explanation: An action in progress when a shorter past action happened takes the past continuous: 'a hunter was sleeping near a river when he began to dream'.

questions.text: Identify the MISSPELT word in the following sentence. As they only require minimal supervision and support, naturally bright learners are largely unaffected by classroom dinamics.
questions.explanation: 'Dinamics' is misspelt: the word is 'dynamics', with a 'y'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. The entire economy “has been effected” by the riots in the state.
questions.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to influence or harm, while the verb 'effect' means to bring about; the singular subject 'economy' keeps 'has': 'The entire economy has been affected by the riots.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. “Blunt” objects will not have that much impact.
questions.explanation: Of objects, 'blunt' means without a sharp edge or point, so its opposite is 'sharp'. 'Torrid' means very hot and 'lame' weak or limping.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Sage
questions.explanation: A 'sage' is a wise person, and as an adjective 'sage' means wise; its opposite is 'foolish'.

questions.text: Fill in the blanks with the correct homophone. Before planning a trip, considering the ___________ for the trip is necessary.
questions.explanation: The 'fare' is the price paid for a journey, which is worth considering before a trip. 'Fair' sounds the same but means just, or an event with stalls and rides.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Done for
questions.explanation: Someone who is 'done for' is ruined, in serious trouble or about to fail.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom that can be substituted in the following sentence. The new Prince is “not fit to hold a candle to” his dead father.
questions.explanation: Someone who is 'not fit to hold a candle to' another is far inferior and cannot be compared with them: the new Prince is no match for his father.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. To stay healthy, “you must keep away from smoking.”
options: you can keep away from smoking.
you will keep away from smoking.
you may keep away from smoking.
questions.explanation: 'Must' gives the strong necessity the advice needs: to stay healthy, one has to keep away from smoking. 'Can', 'will' and 'may' express ability, the future and permission, which weaken it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Glimpse
questions.explanation: A 'glimpse' is a brief look, and so is a 'glance'. To 'gawk' is to stare rudely, and 'vision' is the power of sight.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Consientious' is misspelt: the word is 'conscientious', with 'sc' as in 'science'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The farmers used to _______ seeds by this time.
questions.explanation: To 'sow' seeds is to plant them. 'Sew' (stitch) and 'so' sound the same but do not fit, and 'soe' is not a word.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. Extravagant
questions.explanation: 'Extravagant' means spending too much; its opposite is 'frugal', careful and economical with money. 'Mean' also suggests unwillingness to spend, but as a fault (stingy) rather than the plain opposite, and 'wasteful' is a synonym.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Great Depression was a severe (1) ______ economic depression in the decade (2) _______ World War II. In most countries the depression (3) _______ in about 1929 and lasted until the late 1930s or early 1940s. It was the longest, most widespread, and deepest depression of the 20th century. In the 21st century, the Great Depression is commonly used as an example of how far the world's economy can (4) _________. The depression originated in the U.S. Economic historians usually (5) ________ the start of the Great Depression to the sudden devastating collapse of US stock market prices on 29 October 1929, known as Black Tuesday; some dispute this conclusion, and see the stock crash as a symptom, rather than a cause, of the Great Depression.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The depression struck 'most countries', so it was a 'worldwide' depression, not one confined to a city, a state or a nation.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Great Depression was a severe (1) ______ economic depression in the decade (2) _______ World War II. In most countries the depression (3) _______ in about 1929 and lasted until the late 1930s or early 1940s. It was the longest, most widespread, and deepest depression of the 20th century. In the 21st century, the Great Depression is commonly used as an example of how far the world's economy can (4) _________. The depression originated in the U.S. Economic historians usually (5) ________ the start of the Great Depression to the sudden devastating collapse of US stock market prices on 29 October 1929, known as Black Tuesday; some dispute this conclusion, and see the stock crash as a symptom, rather than a cause, of the Great Depression.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Preceding' means coming just before: the decade before World War II. 'Proceeding' means going on, and 'succeeding' would put it after the war.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Great Depression was a severe (1) ______ economic depression in the decade (2) _______ World War II. In most countries the depression (3) _______ in about 1929 and lasted until the late 1930s or early 1940s. It was the longest, most widespread, and deepest depression of the 20th century. In the 21st century, the Great Depression is commonly used as an example of how far the world's economy can (4) _________. The depression originated in the U.S. Economic historians usually (5) ________ the start of the Great Depression to the sudden devastating collapse of US stock market prices on 29 October 1929, known as Black Tuesday; some dispute this conclusion, and see the stock crash as a symptom, rather than a cause, of the Great Depression.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The depression 'started' in about 1929 and lasted until the late 1930s; 'ended' contradicts 'lasted until'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Great Depression was a severe (1) ______ economic depression in the decade (2) _______ World War II. In most countries the depression (3) _______ in about 1929 and lasted until the late 1930s or early 1940s. It was the longest, most widespread, and deepest depression of the 20th century. In the 21st century, the Great Depression is commonly used as an example of how far the world's economy can (4) _________. The depression originated in the U.S. Economic historians usually (5) ________ the start of the Great Depression to the sudden devastating collapse of US stock market prices on 29 October 1929, known as Black Tuesday; some dispute this conclusion, and see the stock crash as a symptom, rather than a cause, of the Great Depression.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'decline', the usual word for an economy falling: the Great Depression shows how far the world's economy can decline. 'Slip' usually suggests a smaller fall, too mild for the deepest depression of the century, and 'negate' and 'backtrack' do not fit an economy.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Great Depression was a severe (1) ______ economic depression in the decade (2) _______ World War II. In most countries the depression (3) _______ in about 1929 and lasted until the late 1930s or early 1940s. It was the longest, most widespread, and deepest depression of the 20th century. In the 21st century, the Great Depression is commonly used as an example of how far the world's economy can (4) _________. The depression originated in the U.S. Economic historians usually (5) ________ the start of the Great Depression to the sudden devastating collapse of US stock market prices on 29 October 1929, known as Black Tuesday; some dispute this conclusion, and see the stock crash as a symptom, rather than a cause, of the Great Depression.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: To 'attribute' something to a cause is to regard it as caused by it: historians attribute the start of the depression to the stock-market crash of 1929.

questions.text: In a code language, 'You can go' is written as 'na re te', 'You come inside' is written as 'se te pe', 'He can go inside' is written as 're pe na ke'. What is the code for the word 'He' in that language?
questions.explanation: 'You' (te) is common to the first two messages, 'can go' (na re) to the first and third, and 'inside' (pe) to the second and third. The one code left in 're pe na ke' is 'ke', for 'He'.

questions.text: A # B means ‘A is the brother of B’; A @ B means ‘A is the daughter of B’; A & B means ‘A is the husband of B’; A % B means ‘A is the wife of B’; A * B means ‘A is the son of B’; If P@M%H#A@G&B, then how is B related to P?
questions.explanation: P is M's daughter and M is H's wife, so H is P's father. H is the brother of A, who is G's daughter, so G is H's parent, and G is B's husband, so B is H's mother: P's father's mother.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and sixth number is related to fifth number. 9 : 56 :: 12 : ? :: 5 : 12
Which of the following letters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter series? J, S, B, K, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter is 9 places after the one before, wrapping round after Z: J + 9 = S, S + 9 = B, B + 9 = K and K + 9 = T.

questions.text: Five people X, Y, Z, T and U are sitting in a straight row, facing north. There are only two people to the right of Z and only three people to the right of Y. There are only three people to the left of T. Who is sitting in the exact middle of the row?
questions.explanation: Only two people to Z's right put Z third from the left, the middle of the five. (Y, with three to the right, is second from the left, and T, with three to the left, fourth.)

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 32, 35, ?, 47, 56, 67
questions.explanation: The differences are 3, 5, 7, 9, 11: 35 + 5 = 40, and 40 + 7 = 47 checks.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Garage 2 Garnish 3 Gourmet 4 Garland 5 Gastronomy
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Garage, Garland, Garnish ('gara-', 'garl-', 'garn-'), then Gastronomy ('gas-') and Gourmet ('go-'): 1, 4, 2, 5, 3.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 27 + 36 × 32 – 8 ÷ 20 = 151
questions.explanation: After interchanging ÷ and −: 27 + 36 × 32 ÷ 8 − 20 = 27 + 144 − 20 = 151.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. SCIENCE : RAHCMAD :: CAPTAIN : BYORZGM :: COUNTRY : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move −1 and −2 in turn: SCIENCE → RAHCMAD and CAPTAIN → BYORZGM. So COUNTRY → BMTLSPX.

questions.text: If ‘+’ means ‘-’, ‘÷’ means ‘+’, ‘-’ means ‘×’, and ‘×‘ means ‘÷’. Which of the following will be the value of the expression? 45 × 5 + 27 ÷ 81 - 3
questions.explanation: After replacing the signs: 45 ÷ 5 − 27 + 81 × 3 = 9 − 27 + 243 = 225.

questions.text: ‘Intelligent’ is related to ‘Foolish’ in the same way as ‘Expert’ is related to ‘________’. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word)
questions.explanation: 'Foolish' is the opposite of 'intelligent', and an 'amateur', who lacks skill or training, is the opposite of an 'expert'.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All mirrors are combs. All clips are combs. All combs are brushes. Conclusions: I. All clips are brushes. II. All mirrors are brushes. III. Some brushes are clips.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: Mirrors and clips are all combs, and every comb is a brush, so all clips are brushes (I) and all mirrors are brushes (II). As every clip is a brush, some brushes are clips (III).

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 19216, 9604, 4800, 2396, 1196, ?, 295
questions.explanation: Each term is half the one before, minus 4 and 2 in turn: 19216 ÷ 2 − 4 = 9604, 9604 ÷ 2 − 2 = 4800 and so on. So 1196 ÷ 2 − 4 = 594, and 594 ÷ 2 − 2 = 295 checks.

questions.text: Kirti, Suman, Shubh, Kanak, Pari, Charu, Shlok and Shivi are sitting around a square table facing the centre of the table. Some of them are sitting at the corners, while some are sitting at the exact centre of the sides. Kirti sits third to the left of Shubh. Kirti sits at one of the corners. Kanak sits second to the right of Pari. Pari does not sit at any of the corners. Pari is not an immediate neighbour of Kirti. Suman is an immediate neighbour of Charu. Suman does not sit at any of the middle of the sides. Only three people sit between Suman and Shlok from either sides. Who sits third to the left of Shlok?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, each person's left is the next seat clockwise. With Kirti at a corner, Shubh is three seats anticlockwise of her, at the middle of a side; Pari takes the only free middle seat not next to Kirti, three seats clockwise of her, and Kanak sits two seats anticlockwise of Pari. Suman, at a corner opposite Shlok and next to Charu, fits only beside Shubh, with Charu beside Kirti. Clockwise the table runs Kirti, Kanak, Shlok, Pari, Shivi, Shubh, Suman, Charu, so third to Shlok's left is Shubh.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? VCFS, RGJO, NKNK, ?, FSVC
questions.explanation: The first letters move −4 (V, R, N, J, F), the second +4 (C, G, K, O, S), the third +4 (F, J, N, R, V) and the fourth −4 (S, O, K, G, C): JORG.

questions.text: In a code language,'he called them' is written as 'ka ba ma', 'i was called' is written as 'ga va ba' and 'he was hungry' is written as 'ka va da'. What is the code for the word 'hungry' in that language?
questions.explanation: 'he' (ka) is common to the first and third messages, 'called' (ba) to the first and second, and 'was' (va) to the second and third. The one code left in 'ka va da' is 'da', for 'hungry'.

questions.text: Who among the following became the Chief Minister of Tripura in May 2022?
questions.explanation: Manik Saha of the BJP was sworn in as Chief Minister of Tripura on 15 May 2022, after Biplab Kumar Deb resigned.

questions.text: Meenakshisundaram Pillai was widely recognised for which form of dance?
questions.explanation: Pandanallur Meenakshisundaram Pillai, after whose village the Pandanallur style is named, was one of the great gurus of Bharatanatyam; Rukmini Devi Arundale was among his pupils.

questions.text: Which of the following programmes launched by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to promote sports culture in India has 12 verticals?
questions.explanation: The Khelo India scheme of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports was notified in October 2017 with 12 verticals, among them play field development, talent search and development, and sports for women; from 2021-22 they were merged into five components.

questions.text: __________is the central bank of India.
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India, set up in 1935 and nationalised in 1949, is India's central bank: it issues the currency and regulates the banks. SEBI regulates the securities market.

questions.text: The co-contribution of the Government of India under Atal Pension Yojana (APY) is available for _______.
questions.explanation: Under Atal Pension Yojana the Government paid 50% of a subscriber's contribution, up to ₹1,000 a year, for five years (2015-16 to 2019-20), to eligible subscribers who joined by 31 December 2015 and were neither income-tax payers nor covered by a statutory social security scheme.

questions.text: Dhangari Gaja is a folk dance of ________.
questions.explanation: Dhangari Gaja is danced by the Dhangar shepherds of Maharashtra, above all in Solapur district.

questions.text: __________five year plan of Government of India (2012–17) was India's last Five Year Plan.
questions.explanation: The Twelfth Five Year Plan (2012-17) was the last: the Planning Commission was replaced by the NITI Aayog in January 2015, and no plan followed it.

questions.text: The ______ is the site of the complete digestion of carbohydrates, proteins and fats.
questions.explanation: In the small intestine the pancreatic juice, bile from the liver and the intestinal juice complete the digestion of carbohydrates, proteins and fats, and the villi absorb the digested food.

questions.text: Two main objectives: 'removal of poverty' (Garibi Hatao) and 'attainment of self-reliance' was proposed in the ___________ Five year plan.
questions.explanation: The Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-79) set removal of poverty (Garibi Hatao) and the attainment of self-reliance as its two main objectives.

questions.text: Identify the writ by the virtue of which the Court directs a detained person to be brought before it to examine the legality of his detention.
questions.explanation: Habeas corpus ('you should have the body') orders that a detained person be brought before the court, which then examines whether the detention is lawful. Mandamus commands a public authority to do its duty, certiorari quashes a lower court's order and quo warranto asks by what right a person holds a public office.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Prarthana Samaj was established in ______ in Bombay.
questions.explanation: The Prarthana Samaj was founded in Bombay in 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang, inspired by Keshab Chandra Sen; M G Ranade and R G Bhandarkar later became its leading figures.

questions.text: Who was the first captain of India Hockey Team in Olympics?
questions.explanation: Jaipal Singh Munda captained the Indian hockey team at the 1928 Amsterdam Olympics, India's first Olympic hockey tournament, which India won.

questions.text: Identify the element used in making solar cells.
questions.explanation: Solar cells are made mostly of silicon, a semiconductor that gives an electric current when light falls on it. Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin, not an element.

questions.text: The line that separates crust from the mantle is known as___________
questions.explanation: The Mohorovičić (Moho) discontinuity, named after the Croatian seismologist Andrija Mohorovičić, is the boundary between the crust and the mantle, where seismic waves suddenly speed up.

questions.text: _________ is used to manufacture fertilizers, synthetic fibers, plastics, adhesives, paints, and dyes.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives sulphuric acid, the most widely used industrial chemical, whose uses run from fertilisers (superphosphate, ammonium sulphate) to fibres such as rayon, plastics, paints, pigments and dyes. Nitric acid also goes into fertilisers, dyes and some plastics and fibres, so it is arguable, but sulphuric acid is the usual answer for so broad a list.

questions.text: In which of the following states of India does the ‘Sonepur Cattle Fair’ take place?
questions.explanation: The Sonepur Cattle Fair (Harihar Kshetra Mela) is held each year from Kartik Purnima at Sonepur in Saran district, Bihar, where the Gandak meets the Ganga.

questions.text: According to the report published by the National Survey of India, what is the literacy rate of India in 2022?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 77.7%, the literacy rate of persons aged seven and above found by the National Statistical Office's survey 'Household Social Consumption on Education in India' (NSS 75th round, July 2017 to June 2018). The question's 'National Survey of India' and 'in 2022' are loose: the survey is the NSO's, and its data are from 2017-18.

questions.text: Who became the Chief Minister of Goa after March 2022 elections?
questions.explanation: Pramod Sawant of the BJP, Chief Minister since March 2019, was sworn in for a second term on 28 March 2022 after the Goa Assembly election.

questions.text: The Great Stupa of Sanchi was built during the reign of which of the following kings?
questions.explanation: The Great Stupa at Sanchi was first built in brick by the Mauryan emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE; it was enlarged in stone, and its gateways added, under later dynasties.

questions.text: Respecting the national anthem and national flag is:
options: a fundamental right of every citizen
an ordinary duty of every citizen
a fundamental duty of every citizen
a legal right of every citizen
questions.explanation: Article 51A(a), added by the 42nd Amendment (1976), makes it a fundamental duty of every citizen to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.

questions.text: On purchasing a cell phone in cash, a shopkeeper gives a discount of 7.5%. The marked price of the cell phone is Rs. 18000. What is the value of discount?
Two trains of lengths 250 metres and 400 metres are running at speeds of 40 km/h and 30 km/h, respectively. If they are moving in the same direction, they will cross each other in __________ minutes.
questions.explanation: Moving the same way, the faster train gains 40 − 30 = 10 km/h, or 10,000/60 m a minute, and must cover 250 + 400 = 650 m: 650 × 60/10,000 = 3.9 minutes.

questions.text: Vinay professes to sell rice at its cost price but uses the weight of 1600 gm in place of 2 kg. What is his percentage gain?
questions.explanation: He gives 1600 g for the price of 2000 g, gaining 400 g on every 1600 g: 400/1600 = 25%.

questions.text: Susan can do the binding work of 100 books in 20 hours. Susan and Pragati together can do binding work of 600 books in 80 hours. In how much time Pragati alone can do the binding of 60 books?
questions.explanation: Susan binds 100/20 = 5 books an hour and the two together 600/80 = 7.5, so Pragati binds 2.5 an hour and needs 60/2.5 = 24 hours.

questions.text: A shopkeeper purchased wheat at Rs.20 per kg and rice at Rs.80 per kg. He sold 80 kg of wheat at Rs.22 per kg and 20 kg of wheat at Rs.21 per kg. Furthermore, he sold 40 kg of rice at Rs.95 per kg and 60 kg of rice at Rs.93 per kg. Find his total profit in this deal.
questions.explanation: Wheat: 100 kg cost ₹2,000 and sold for 80 × 22 + 20 × 21 = ₹2,180, a profit of ₹180. Rice: 100 kg cost ₹8,000 and sold for 40 × 95 + 60 × 93 = ₹9,380, a profit of ₹1,380. In all ₹1,560.

questions.text: What is the value of 100 ÷ 10- [-2 + {-9 + (3 - 6 of 2)}]?
The in‐radius of a triangle is 8 cm and the sum of the lengths of its sides is 60 cm. The area of the triangle (in cm²) is:
questions.explanation: The area of a triangle is its in-radius times its semi-perimeter: 8 × 30 = 240 cm².

questions.text: The distance between the two Cities A and B is 800 km. A train covers the journey from A to B at 60 km per hour and returns to A at a uniform speed of 40 km per hour. Find the average speed of the train during the whole journey.
questions.explanation: For equal distances the average speed is 2 × 60 × 40/(60 + 40) = 4800/100 = 48 km/h.

questions.text: After reducing 2 percent, a dining set costs Rs. 17640. Its original price is:
questions.explanation: 98% of the original price is ₹17,640, so the price was 17,640 ÷ 0.98 = ₹18,000.

questions.text: The difference between the compound interest, compounding annually and the simple interest accrued on an amount of Rs.18,000 in 2 years was Rs.720. What was the rate of interest per annum?

A, B, and C can complete a work in 15, 30, and 20 days respectively. A left the work 1 day before the work was completed and B left 2 days before the completion of the work. Find the number of days required to complete the whole work.
questions.explanation: If the work takes T days, A works T − 1 days, B T − 2 and C all T: (T − 1)/15 + (T − 2)/30 + T/20 = 1. Multiplying by 60, 4T − 4 + 2T − 4 + 3T = 60, so 9T = 68 and T = 68/9 days.

questions.text: A candidate who gets 50 percent marks fails by 100 marks but another candidate who got 78 percent marks gets 30 percent more than the passing marks. The maximum marks is:
questions.explanation: With maximum marks M, the pass mark is 0.5M + 100, and 78% of M is 1.3 times it: 0.78M = 0.65M + 130, so 0.13M = 130 and M = 1000.

questions.text: A man can row 9 km/h in still water. In a stream which is flowing at 4 km/h, it takes total 9 hours to row to a place and back to the starting point. How far is the place from starting point?
questions.explanation: Downstream the speed is 9 + 4 = 13 km/h and upstream 9 − 4 = 5 km/h: d/13 + d/5 = 9 gives 18d/65 = 9, so d = 32.5 km.

questions.text: Arun bought 3 shirts at the rate of Rs.175 per shirt and 6 trousers at the rate of Rs.250 per trouser. What is the average price of all the clothes?

The population of a city increases at a rate of 2% for the first 2 years and then, decreases at a rate of 4% for the third year. What will be the population after 3 years if the present population of the city is 62,500?
If incomes of Reeta and Geeta are Rs.1,600 and Rs.2,400 respectively, then by what percentage is the income of Geeta more than the income of Reeta?
questions.explanation: Geeta earns ₹800 more, which is 800/1,600 = 50% of Reeta's income.

questions.text: Identify and correct the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence The flora and fauna of the Anaimalai hills are uneeque to its region.
questions.explanation: The misspelt word is 'uneeque'; the correct spelling is 'unique'. The other options misspell words ('fauna', 'flora', 'region') that the sentence spells correctly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Called for
questions.explanation: 'Called for' means required or needed: 'the situation called for quick action'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The coach said / that Shreyas / had practicing on / the lawn tennis court.
questions.explanation: 'Had' needs a past participle, not an '-ing' form: 'had practised on' (or 'had been practising on').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. When someone waves a white flag, it signifies that they “want to tolerate” to the other party.
questions.explanation: A white flag is the sign of surrender, so 'want to surrender' fits; 'tolerate' takes no 'to' and makes no sense here, and the plural 'they' keeps 'want'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Nothing equalled the “grief” I felt at the death of my pet cat.
questions.explanation: 'Grief' is deep sorrow, especially at a death: 'anguish'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. After he finished eating his lunch, the boy sitting next to me __________ intently at me.
questions.explanation: Only 'stared' goes with 'intently at me': to stare is to look fixedly at someone.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The melodious song reminded Revathi “on the nostalgic moments of” her past.
questions.explanation: One is reminded 'of' something, and the moments are 'of' her past: 'reminded Revathi of the nostalgic moments of her past'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. It takes two to tango
options: Two people crossing the street together
A conflict where both people are at fault
Two people are needed for any game
questions.explanation: 'It takes two to tango' means that when something goes wrong between two people, both share the blame.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Alight
questions.explanation: To 'alight' is to get down from a vehicle, or to come down and settle as a bird does: to 'descend'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. The boys are very (hyper) _________ today.
questions.explanation: 'Hyper' means over-excited and restless; its opposite is 'tranquil', calm and peaceful.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Savage
questions.explanation: 'Savage' means fierce and untamed; its opposite is 'tame'. 'Wild' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Endurance
questions.explanation: 'Endurance' is the power to keep going through hardship; 'indolence', laziness and the avoidance of effort, is its opposite. 'Patience', 'persistence' and 'tolerance' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the correct pair of homonyms to fill in the blanks. The river ______ provide a reserve _______ for minerals that enrich the soil’s fertility.
questions.explanation: 'Bank' is a homonym: the land along a river, and a store kept for later use: 'The river banks provide a reserve bank for minerals'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word to fill in the blank in the sentence. Rigid The new education scenario is not ________ but practical.
questions.explanation: 'Rigid' means fixed and unbending: 'stiff'. The sentence sets it against 'practical'; 'flexible' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'vacuum', with one 'c' and a double 'u'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The room looked as though a (1) __________ had swept through it. The storm had blown (2) _________ the French doors during the night, and the wind and the rain had wreaked havoc, (3) _________ everything before it. A few (4) _________ pages of the report lay on the wet rug, but the rest of the pages had obviously been carried (5) _________ by the wind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The room was in such a mess that a 'hurricane', a violent storm, might have swept through it; the next sentence speaks of the storm.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The room looked as though a (1) __________ had swept through it. The storm had blown (2) _________ the French doors during the night, and the wind and the rain had wreaked havoc, (3) _________ everything before it. A few (4) _________ pages of the report lay on the wet rug, but the rest of the pages had obviously been carried (5) _________ by the wind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The storm had 'blown open' the French doors, letting the wind and rain in.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The room looked as though a (1) __________ had swept through it. The storm had blown (2) _________ the French doors during the night, and the wind and the rain had wreaked havoc, (3) _________ everything before it. A few (4) _________ pages of the report lay on the wet rug, but the rest of the pages had obviously been carried (5) _________ by the wind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The wind and rain wreaked havoc, 'scattering' (throwing in all directions) everything before them.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The room looked as though a (1) __________ had swept through it. The storm had blown (2) _________ the French doors during the night, and the wind and the rain had wreaked havoc, (3) _________ everything before it. A few (4) _________ pages of the report lay on the wet rug, but the rest of the pages had obviously been carried (5) _________ by the wind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Loose' pages are ones that have come away from the rest of the report; 'lose' is a verb.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The room looked as though a (1) __________ had swept through it. The storm had blown (2) _________ the French doors during the night, and the wind and the rain had wreaked havoc, (3) _________ everything before it. A few (4) _________ pages of the report lay on the wet rug, but the rest of the pages had obviously been carried (5) _________ by the wind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The rest of the pages had been 'carried away', taken off, by the wind.

questions.text: Six students Tanya, Roop, Johar, Soma, Manvi and Deep are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Soma is sitting second to the right of Deep. Soma is an immediate neighbour of both Manvi and Johar. Roop is sitting second to the left of Johar. Deep is an immediate neighbour of both Johar and Roop. Who is the immediate neighbour of Tanya and Deep?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, each person's right runs anticlockwise. Deep sits between Johar and Roop, and Soma, second to Deep's right, is Johar's other neighbour, so Johar is on Deep's right and Roop on Deep's left (second to Johar's left, as stated). Going right from Deep: Johar, Soma, Manvi, Tanya, Roop, so Roop sits next to both Tanya and Deep.

questions.text: Which two numbers(not digits) and two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 100 × 5 – 110 ÷ 2 + 12 = 210
questions.explanation: After interchanging 5 and 2 and the signs + and −: 100 × 2 + 110 ÷ 5 − 12 = 200 + 22 − 12 = 210.

questions.text: A @ B means ‘A is the husband of B’. A & B means ‘A is the mother of B’. A # B means ‘A is the daughter of B’. A % B means ‘A is the sister of B’. If R # L % G @ V & P, then how is L related to P?
questions.explanation: R # L: R is L's daughter. L % G: L is G's sister. G @ V: G is V's husband, and V & P: V is P's mother, so G is P's father. L, his sister, is P's father's sister.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. HALF: SFOT :: DAMP: WFNJ :: AREA: ?
questions.explanation: The first and third letters become their opposites (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on), the second moves +5 and the fourth becomes its opposite minus 1: HALF → S, F, O, U − 1 = T and DAMP → W, F, N, K − 1 = J. So AREA → Z, W, V, Z − 1 = Y: ZWVY.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/consonants/vowels in the word). Cosmology: Universe :: Morphology : _________
questions.explanation: Cosmology is the study of the universe, and morphology the study of the form and structure of living things.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘DESIGN’ is written as ‘TFEPIK’ and 'DESIRE' is written as 'TFEGTK'. How will ‘DEVICE’ be written as in that language?
questions.explanation: Each half of the word is reversed, then the first half moves +1 and the second +2: DES → SED → TFE and IGN → NGI → PIK, IRE → ERI → GTK. So DEV → VED → WFE and ICE → ECI → GEK: WFEGEK.

questions.text: Six people A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre. C is sitting second to the left of E. B is the immediate neighbour of E and F. A is sitting second to the right of B. Who is sitting between B and A when considered from the right of B?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, each person's right runs anticlockwise. B sits next to E; if B were on E's left, F would take the seat second to E's left, which is C's. So B is on E's right with F on B's right, and A, second to the right of B, sits beyond F. Between B and A, from B's right, sits F.

questions.text: In a certain code language, FLAME is written as ‘LPGQK’, and BURNT is written as ‘HYXRZ’. How will ‘FRIED’ be written in the same code language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +6, +4, +6, +4, +6: FLAME → LPGQK and BURNT → HYXRZ. So FRIED → LVOIJ.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1. HALOGEN 2. HAIRY 3. HAIKU 4. HAND 5. HAMPER 6. HANK
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Haiku (3), Hairy (2), Halogen (1), Hamper (5), Hand (4), Hank (6). 'Haik' comes before 'Hair', 'Hai' before 'Hal', 'Ham' before 'Han', and 'Hand' before 'Hank'.

questions.text: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 182, 132, 90 ,56, ? ,12, 2
questions.explanation: Each term is the product of two consecutive numbers: 13 × 14 = 182, 11 × 12 = 132, 9 × 10 = 90, 7 × 8 = 56, so 5 × 6 = 30, then 3 × 4 = 12 and 1 × 2 = 2.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? ?, CSAT, BPVM, AMQF, ZJLY
questions.explanation: From one term to the next the first letters move −1 (C, B, A, Z), the second −3 (S, P, M, J), the third −5 (A, V, Q, L) and the fourth −7 (T, M, F, Y), wrapping round the alphabet. One step before CSAT is D, V, F, A: DVFA.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 64 - 16 × 25 ÷ 80 + 10 = 59
Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. WGVJ, CCBP, IYHV, ?, UQTH
questions.explanation: The first, third and fourth letters move 6 places forward and the second 4 back, wrapping round the alphabet: W, C, I, O, U; G, C, Y, U, Q; V, B, H, N, T; J, P, V, B, H. The missing term is OUNB.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: Some chairs are bedsheets. All cots are chairs. All pillows are bedsheets. Conclusions: I. Some pillows are chairs. II. Some cots are bedsheets.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: All pillows are bedsheets, but only some bedsheets are known to be chairs, so the pillows may lie wholly outside the chairs: I does not follow. All cots are chairs, but they need not fall in the part of the chairs that are bedsheets: II does not follow.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 0, 7, 26, 63, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is one less than a cube: 1³ − 1 = 0, 2³ − 1 = 7, 3³ − 1 = 26, 4³ − 1 = 63, so 5³ − 1 = 124.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed) (10, 300, 40); (12, 192, 20)
questions.explanation: The middle number is six times the sum of the other two: (10 + 40) × 6 = 300 and (12 + 20) × 6 = 192. Likewise (18 + 20) × 6 = 228; the other sets would need 276, 174 and 180.

questions.text: Which of the following is a professional table tennis player?
questions.explanation: Manika Batra is an Indian table tennis player, the women's singles gold medallist at the 2018 Commonwealth Games. Parupalli Kashyap and Aparna Popat play badminton, and Saurav Ghosal squash.

questions.text: Ruler of which dynasty built the Kandariya Mahadeva temple in 999?
questions.explanation: The Kandariya Mahadeva temple at Khajuraho, dedicated to Shiva, was built by the Chandela kings of Bundelkhand. The NCERT Class 7 history textbook credits it to King Dhangadeva in 999; many historians date it to the early eleventh century, under Vidyadhara.

questions.text: Which article of Indian constitution is related with Protection of interests of minorities?
questions.explanation: Article 29 protects the interests of minorities: any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture of its own has the right to conserve it.

questions.text: The prime themes of Kathak are tied to which of the following cults of Hinduism?
questions.explanation: Kathak's themes come mainly from the Vaishnava Bhakti tradition: the stories of Krishna, Radha and the gopis from texts such as the Bhagavata Purana. Buddhism is not a cult of Hinduism at all.

questions.text: Cycas and Pinus are which type of plants?
questions.explanation: Cycas and Pinus are gymnosperms: their seeds are naked, not enclosed in a fruit, and are usually borne on cones.

questions.text: What helps in the cultivation of rabi crops?
questions.explanation: Mahawat is the light winter rain that western disturbances bring to north-west India; small in amount, it is valuable for rabi crops such as wheat.

questions.text: The Finance Commission of India submits its report to _________.
questions.explanation: The Finance Commission reports to the President, who under Article 281 has its recommendations laid before each House of Parliament with a memorandum on the action taken.

questions.text: Which state has the lowest sex ratio as per the Census 2011?
questions.explanation: Haryana had 879 females per 1,000 males in the 2011 Census, the lowest sex ratio of any state.

questions.text: Which of the following is an output of farming?
questions.explanation: Seen as a system, farming takes inputs such as seeds, fertilisers, machinery and labour, and its outputs are crops and products such as wool, dairy and poultry.

questions.text: Which Union Minister of State addressed the inaugural function of 4th National Young Superintendents of Police Conference and Police Expo in September 2022?
questions.explanation: Nityanand Rai, then Minister of State for Home Affairs, addressed the inaugural function of the 4th National Young Superintendents of Police Conference and Police Expo, held by the BPR&D with FICCI in New Delhi on 29 September 2022.

questions.text: A microfinance loan is defined as a collateral-free loan given to a household having annual household income up to Rs. ______.
questions.explanation: Under the RBI's microfinance framework of March 2022, a microfinance loan is a collateral-free loan to a household whose annual income is up to ₹3,00,000.

questions.text: ____________ (NRLM) is a poverty alleviation project implemented by the Government of India.
questions.explanation: The National Rural Livelihood Mission (Aajeevika), launched by the Ministry of Rural Development in 2011, works through self-help groups of the rural poor; it is now the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-NRLM.

questions.text: Which is the last Five year plan that was put to effect in India?
questions.explanation: The Twelfth Five Year Plan (2012-17) was the last: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission in 2015, and the plans were not continued.

questions.text: Gaddam Padmaja Reddy won Padma Shri for which dance form?
questions.explanation: Gaddam Padmaja Reddy of Telangana, a Kuchipudi dancer and guru, received the Padma Shri in 2022.

questions.text: Who has been appointed as the Director of the Forest Research Institute in March 2022?
questions.explanation: Dr Renu Singh, an Indian Forest Service officer of the 1990 batch, joined as Director of the Forest Research Institute, Dehradun, on 28 March 2022; A. S. Rawat, Director General of ICFRE, had held additional charge of the post.

questions.text: Captain Roop Singh Stadium is located in which of the following city?
questions.explanation: Captain Roop Singh Stadium is a cricket ground in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh, where Sachin Tendulkar scored the first double century in men's one-day internationals in 2010.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Why was the year 1757 an important year for the English East India Company in India?
options: In 1757 the English East India Company got control over Hyderabad by defeating the Nizam in the Battle of Plassey.
In 1757 the English East India Company got control over Madras by defeating Nawab Siraj-ud-daulah in the Battle of Plassey.
In 1757 the English East India Company got control over Oudh by defeating Nawab Siraj-ud-daulah in the Battle of Berar.
In 1757 the English East India Company got control over Bengal by defeating Nawab Siraj-ud-daulah in the Battle of Plassey.
questions.explanation: At the Battle of Plassey in 1757 Robert Clive's forces defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-daulah, giving the Company control over Bengal.

questions.text: Which among the following festivals is also known as Dala Puja devoted to worshiping the sun is traditionally celebrated by the people of Bihar?
questions.explanation: Chhath, also called Dala Chhath, is Bihar's festival of the Sun god, when devotees offer prayers to the setting and the rising sun, often standing in a river.

questions.text: M.S.Swaminathan (father of Green Revolution in India), was ______by profession.
questions.explanation: M. S. Swaminathan was an agricultural scientist, a plant geneticist whose work with high-yielding wheat and rice led India's Green Revolution.

questions.text: Which among the following statements is incorrect?
options: The melting point of ice decreases with decrease in pressure.
Spherical Shape of liquid droplets is due to the property of surface tension in liquids.
Evaporation takes place only on the surface of liquids.
Liquids at high altitudes boil at lower temperature due to low atmospheric pressure at high altitudes.
questions.explanation: Ice contracts as it melts, so a rise in pressure lowers its melting point and a fall in pressure raises it slightly. The other three statements are correct.

questions.text: A man spends 87% of his income. His income increased by 18% and he increased his expenditure by 17%. His savings will then be increased by : (Consider up to two decimals only)
questions.explanation: Take the income as 100: spending 87, saving 13. Then income is 118 and spending 87 × 1.17 = 101.79, so saving is 16.21. Increase = 3.21/13 × 100 = 24.69%.

questions.text: Mohan walks on a circular track 1500 metre in circumference. If the speed of Mohan is 75metre/min, then what is the time taken by Mohan to cover one round of track?
Successive discounts of 10%, 15% and 20% amount to a single discount of:
questions.explanation: 0.90 × 0.85 × 0.80 = 0.612 of the price is paid, so the single discount is 1 − 0.612 = 0.388, or 38.8%.

questions.text: If radius of a cylinder is increased by 20% keeping the height unchanged, then by what percent does the volume of the cylinder increase?
questions.explanation: The volume πr²h varies as r² when h is fixed: 1.2² = 1.44, an increase of 44%.

questions.text: Find the fourth proportional to 7x - 1, 9x + 5 and 8x + 1, if x = 3.
questions.explanation: With x = 3 the numbers are 20, 32 and 25. 20 : 32 = 25 : d gives d = 32 × 25/20 = 40.

questions.text: Two objects were sold for ₹9,900 each. One object was sold at a loss of 10% and the other object was sold at a gain of 10%. The net gain or loss in the whole transaction is:
questions.explanation: The cost prices are ₹9,900/0.9 = ₹11,000 and ₹9,900/1.1 = ₹9,000, ₹20,000 in all, against ₹19,800 received: a loss of ₹200.

questions.text: A shopkeeper marks his goods 12 percent above cost price, but allows 12 percent discount for cash. His net gain or loss percent is:
questions.explanation: The selling price is 1.12 × 0.88 = 0.9856 of the cost: a loss of 1.44%.

questions.text: What is the compound interest (in ₹ , rounded off to two decimal places) on ₹ 20,000 in two years at 4% per annum, the interest being compounded half-yearly?
questions.explanation: Half-yearly the rate is 2% for 4 periods: ₹20,000 × 1.02⁴ = ₹20,000 × 1.08243216 = ₹21,648.64, so the interest is ₹1,648.64.

questions.text: The average marks obtained in a subject by 60 students in a class is 82. The average marks of boys and girls in that subject are 75 and 85 respectively. The number of boys in the class is:
The salary of Neeta is first increased by 13% and then it is decreased by 13%. What is the change in her salary?
questions.explanation: 1.13 × 0.87 = 0.9831 of the salary: a decrease of 1.69% (13²/100).

questions.text: Two containers with equal capacity have milk and water in the ratio of 3 : 4 and 3 : 1 respectively. If both the containers are emptied into a bigger container having the capacity to contain the whole mixture, then what is the ratio of milk to water in the bigger container?
questions.explanation: Take 28 litres in each. The first holds 12 litres of milk and 16 of water, the second 21 of milk and 7 of water: 33 : 23.

questions.text: A and B undertake to do a piece of work for Rs. 330. A can do it in 11 days and B can do it in 22 days. With the help of C, they finish it in 6 days. How much should C be paid for his work?
questions.explanation: In 6 days A does 6/11 of the work and B 6/22 = 3/11, leaving 2/11 for C: ₹330 × 2/11 = ₹60.

questions.text: Two numbers are in the ratio of 2 : 3. Their HCF and LCM are 21 and 126, respectively. What is the difference of these two numbers?
questions.explanation: The numbers are 2 × 21 = 42 and 3 × 21 = 63, whose LCM is 126, so the difference is 21.

questions.text: A and B together can do a piece of work in 12 days, B and C together in 15 days, C and A together in 20 days. If A, B and C work together, then how many days will be required to do the same work?
Mohan goes to office from home at a speed of 20 km/h and returns to home from office at a certain speed. If the average speed is 24 km/h, then what is the speed while returning?
questions.explanation: Over equal distances the average speed is 2uv/(u + v): 2 × 20 × v/(20 + v) = 24 gives 40v = 480 + 24v, so v = 30 km/h.

questions.text: The smallest number which when reduced by 5, is divisible 12, 16, and 18 is:
Laxman marks his goods at 60% above the cost price and allows a discount of 20%. What is his gain/loss percentage?
questions.explanation: The selling price is 1.6 × 0.8 = 1.28 of the cost: a profit of 28%.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Counsel
questions.explanation: 'Counsel' is advice or guidance. 'Scintillate' means to sparkle.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Protest
questions.explanation: To 'protest' is to object to something; the opposite is to 'support' it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Plead
questions.explanation: To 'plead' is to beg earnestly, as is to 'beseech'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlying word in the given sentence and complete the sentence. In the debate competition he scored less due to his “banal” arguments, while his opponent won because of his __________ arguments.
questions.explanation: 'Banal' means dull and unoriginal; its opposite is 'novel', new and original, which suits the winner's arguments.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Blank
questions.explanation: A 'blank' space is empty; the opposite is 'filled'. 'Filed' (put in a file) is a different word.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The reign of Akbar “was the one glorious periods” in Indian history.
options: was one of the glorious periods
were one of the glorious period
was one of the glorious period
questions.explanation: 'One of' takes a plural noun, and the singular subject 'the reign' takes 'was': 'was one of the glorious periods'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Mike talks in an American ________.
questions.explanation: An 'accent' is a way of pronouncing a language: 'an American accent'. 'Assent' is agreement, and 'ascent' a climb.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. He will give you / good advice if / you will ask him.
questions.explanation: In a first conditional the 'if' clause takes the simple present, not 'will': 'if you ask him'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. “If you not ready with the song”, it is better to let them know.
options: If you could not be ready with the song
If you were not ready with the song
If you would not be ready with the song
If you are not ready with the song
questions.explanation: The 'if' clause needs a verb, and with 'it is better' in the main clause it takes the simple present: 'If you are not ready with the song'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'amplification'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Spill the beans
options: Tell something that should be kept secret
questions.explanation: To 'spill the beans' is to reveal a secret.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word to fill in the blank in the sentence. Daunt; My coach said, “Failures didn’t ________ the hero.”
questions.explanation: To 'daunt' is to discourage or intimidate: 'Failures didn't discourage the hero.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Back to square one
options: To hope something happens the way you want it to
Having to start all over again
questions.explanation: To be 'back to square one' is to have to start all over again after an attempt has failed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. He’s “in and out” in town making plans.
questions.explanation: To be 'out and about' is to be up and active, going from place to place: 'He's out and about in town making plans.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Isolation and loneliness (1) ________ by the Covid-19 pandemic and lockdown policies negatively (2) _______ the mental health of the public throughout the entire globe. These result in an increase in emotional (3) __________, (4) __________ of hopelessness and extreme anxiety, which are (5) _______ by variations in emotional responses and style of living.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Isolation and loneliness were 'caused' by the pandemic and the lockdowns, that is brought about by them.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Isolation and loneliness (1) ________ by the Covid-19 pandemic and lockdown policies negatively (2) _______ the mental health of the public throughout the entire globe. These result in an increase in emotional (3) __________, (4) __________ of hopelessness and extreme anxiety, which are (5) _______ by variations in emotional responses and style of living.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Negatively impacted the mental health' means affected it badly; the other verbs do not take 'mental health' as their object in this sense.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Isolation and loneliness (1) ________ by the Covid-19 pandemic and lockdown policies negatively (2) _______ the mental health of the public throughout the entire globe. These result in an increase in emotional (3) __________, (4) __________ of hopelessness and extreme anxiety, which are (5) _______ by variations in emotional responses and style of living.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Emotional stress' is the usual pairing; 'anxiety' would repeat 'extreme anxiety' later in the sentence, and 'death' and 'state' do not fit.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Isolation and loneliness (1) ________ by the Covid-19 pandemic and lockdown policies negatively (2) _______ the mental health of the public throughout the entire globe. These result in an increase in emotional (3) __________, (4) __________ of hopelessness and extreme anxiety, which are (5) _______ by variations in emotional responses and style of living.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Feelings of hopelessness' is the natural phrase, and it is an emotion the sentence lists; 'notion', 'idea' and 'concept' are thoughts, not feelings.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Isolation and loneliness (1) ________ by the Covid-19 pandemic and lockdown policies negatively (2) _______ the mental health of the public throughout the entire globe. These result in an increase in emotional (3) __________, (4) __________ of hopelessness and extreme anxiety, which are (5) _______ by variations in emotional responses and style of living.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The stress and anxiety are 'accompanied by', that is go along with, variations in emotional responses and style of living.

questions.text: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? HSCQ, JVZR, ?, NBTT, PEQU
questions.explanation: The first letters move 2 places forward (H, J, L, N, P), the second 3 forward (S, V, Y, B, E), the third 3 back (C, Z, W, T, Q) and the fourth 1 forward (Q, R, S, T, U). The missing cluster is LYWS.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: All leaves are plants. All plants are trees. All trees are big. Conclusions: I. Some trees are leaves. II. All leaves are big.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: Every leaf is a plant, every plant a tree and every tree big, so all leaves are trees and all leaves are big (II). As all leaves are trees, some trees are leaves (I). Both follow.

questions.text: Six students A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table, all facing opposite to the centre. D is to the immediate right of E, who is to the immediate right of F. A is the immediate neighbour of D and C. Who among the following is sitting second to the left of E?
questions.explanation: Facing outwards, a person's right is the next seat clockwise. Clockwise the order is F, E, D (E to F's right, D to E's right), then A next to D and C next to A, leaving B between C and F: F, E, D, A, C, B. To E's left, anticlockwise, come F and then B.

questions.text: Which of the mathematical signs should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct? 15 ÷ 5 × 27 + 3 - 9 = 51
questions.explanation: After interchanging ÷ and +: 15 + 5 × 27 ÷ 3 − 9 = 15 + 45 − 9 = 51.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed) (264, 43, 19); (132, 27, 15)
questions.explanation: In each set the first number is 11 times the difference of the other two: (43 − 19) × 11 = 264 and (27 − 15) × 11 = 132. Likewise (39 − 23) × 11 = 176.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘HOUSE’ is coded as IQVUF and ‘GARDEN’ is coded as HCSFFP. How will ‘ORANGE’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1 and +2 in turn: HOUSE → IQVUF and GARDEN → HCSFFP. So ORANGE → PTBPHG.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 946 ,721 ,552 ,? ,350 ,301
Which of the mathematical signs should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct? 105 ÷ 15 × 54 + 6 - 18 = 222

‘F – G’ means ‘F is the brother of G’; ‘F * G’ means ‘F is the sister of G’; ‘F + G’ means ‘F is the father of G’; ‘F $ G’ means ‘F is the mother of G’; If ‘H $ I + J – K’, then how is H related to K?
questions.explanation: H is the mother of I, I is the father of J and J is the brother of K. So K is also I's child, and H, the mother of K's father, is K's paternal grandmother.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. BRIGHT : DTKIJV :: DANGER : FCPIGT :: FOREST : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: BRIGHT → DTKIJV and DANGER → FCPIGT. So FOREST → HQTGUV.

questions.text: Which of the following letters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter series? B, D, E, G, H, J, ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +2 and +1 in turn: B, D, E, G, H, J, so the next is J + 1 = K.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Difficult 2 Differentiate 3 Dissolve 4 Dilute 5 Distance
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Differentiate (2), Difficult (1), Dilute (4), Dissolve (3), Distance (5). 'Diffe' comes before 'Diffi', 'Dif' before 'Dil', 'Dil' before 'Dis', and 'Diss' before 'Dist'.

questions.text: Seven people Q, R, Y, W, T, E, and U are sitting in a straight row, facing north. Only three people sit to the left of R. U sits at the extreme right. Only two people sit between Q and R. T is the immediate neighbour of R and Y. W is the immediate neighbour of Q and E. Who sits at the centre of the row?
questions.explanation: R is 4th from the left and U 7th. Two people sit between Q and R, so Q is 1st. W, next to Q and E, is 2nd and E 3rd; T, next to R and Y, is then 5th and Y 6th: Q W E R T Y U. R sits at the centre.

questions.text: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 32, 34, ?, 212, 850, 4252

Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. NEST: OVHU :: STIR : TGRS :: BAKE : ?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters move one place forward and the two middle letters become their opposites (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on): NEST → OVHU (E↔V, S↔H) and STIR → TGRS (T↔G, I↔R). So BAKE → CZPF (A↔Z, K↔P).

questions.text: In a certain code language, FLASH is written as ‘INDUK’, and GAMES is written as ‘JCPGV’. How will ‘TRUST’ be written in the same code language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +3 and +2 in turn: FLASH → INDUK and GAMES → JCPGV. So TRUST → WTXUW.

questions.text: Lui-Ngai-Ni is celebrated as a seed sowing festival by the people of ___________.
questions.explanation: Lui-Ngai-Ni, celebrated on 15 February, is the seed-sowing festival of the Naga tribes of Manipur and marks the start of their year.

questions.text: Name the facility available for sale and purchase of goods through internet and fax.
questions.explanation: E-commerce is the buying and selling of goods and services over electronic networks such as the internet.

questions.text: Anindita Neogy Anaam has been awarded with______________.
questions.explanation: Anindita Neogy Anaam, a Kathak dancer based in the United States, received the National Nritya Shiromani award at the 10th Cuttack Mahotsav in Odisha in January 2019.

questions.text: net exports = total exports -_______.
questions.explanation: Net exports are the value of a country's exports minus the value of its imports.

questions.text: On heating gypsum at ______, it losses water molecules and becomes calcium sulphate hemihydrate.
questions.explanation: Heated at 373 K, gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O) loses water and becomes calcium sulphate hemihydrate (CaSO₄·½H₂O), that is plaster of Paris.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following books was written by Dayanand Saraswati?
questions.explanation: Swami Dayanand Saraswati, founder of the Arya Samaj, wrote 'Satyarth Prakash' (1875). 'Gitanjali', 'Kabuliwala' and 'Stray Birds' are Rabindranath Tagore's.

questions.text: Which is the least populated state in India as per the Census 2011?
questions.explanation: The 2011 Census counted about 6.1 lakh people in Sikkim, the fewest of any state; Mizoram had about 11 lakh and Goa about 14.6 lakh.

questions.text: The total number of sports in the 36th edition of the National Games 2022 of India were _______________.
questions.explanation: The 36th National Games, held in six cities of Gujarat from 29 September to 12 October 2022, had 36 sports.

questions.text: ______ are a kind of waste disposal system of the cell.
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane-bound sacs of digestive enzymes that break down worn-out cell parts and foreign material, the cell's waste disposal system.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for an independent office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
questions.explanation: Article 148 provides for a Comptroller and Auditor General of India, appointed by the President and removable only like a Supreme Court judge, which keeps the office independent of the executive.

questions.text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagged off the first Vande Bharat Express Train on which route in South India?
questions.explanation: On 11 November 2022 the Prime Minister flagged off the Chennai-Mysuru Vande Bharat Express at Bengaluru, the first Vande Bharat train in South India and the fifth in the country. It runs between Chennai and Mysuru by way of Bengaluru.

questions.text: Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi launched the ‘Jal Shakti Abhiyan : ______ ’ campaign on World Water Day, 2021. Fill the blank space with appropriate option.
questions.explanation: 'Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain', launched on 22 March 2021, urges people to catch the rain where it falls and when it falls, by building and repairing rainwater harvesting structures.

questions.text: The first seven Five Years Plans gave importance to _____.
questions.explanation: Among the goals of the Plans (growth, modernisation, self-reliance and equity), the first seven Five Year Plans stressed self-reliance: not importing goods, food above all, that India could produce itself.

questions.text: Pushkar Singh Dhami, who became the chief minister of Uttarakhand state of India in March 2022, belongs to ________ political party.
questions.explanation: Pushkar Singh Dhami of the Bharatiya Janata Party first became Chief Minister of Uttarakhand in July 2021 and was sworn in for a second term in March 2022, after the party won the state election.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers discharge its water into the Arabian sea?
questions.explanation: The Narmada flows west through a rift valley into the Arabian Sea at the Gulf of Khambhat. The Mahanadi, Krishna and Ganga flow into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.text: Who among the following is NOT a Kathak dancer?
questions.explanation: Ananda Shankar, son of the dancer Uday Shankar, was a musician known for blending Indian and Western music. Sitara Devi, Gopi Krishna and Shambhu Maharaj were Kathak dancers.

questions.text: Who was the captain of the Indian hockey men’s team in the 1936 Berlin Olympics?
questions.explanation: Dhyan Chand captained the Indian hockey team that won the gold medal at the 1936 Berlin Olympics, beating Germany 8-1 in the final.

questions.text: Under which of the following articles is the abolition of titles recognised?
questions.explanation: Article 18 abolishes titles: the State may confer none except military and academic distinctions. Article 17 abolishes untouchability.

questions.text: Actual growth rate during tenth five year plan of India was ___________.
questions.explanation: The Planning Commission's Eleventh Plan document records an average growth of 7.6% a year for the Tenth Plan (2002-07), against a target of 8% and the highest of any Plan until then; some later sources give 7.7%.

questions.text: P, Q and R can complete a task in 20, 30, and 60 days, respectively. How many days will it take to finish the work if P is helped by Q and R every third day?
questions.explanation: In each 3 days P does 3/20 of the task, and Q and R, on the third day, 1/30 + 1/60 = 1/20 more: 4/20 = 1/5 in all. The task takes 5 such spells, 15 days.

questions.text: A discount of 4.5 percent is given to the customer on marked price of an article. A girl bought the article for Rs. 191. The marked price of the article is:
questions.explanation: The girl pays 100 − 4.5 = 95.5% of the marked price: 191 ÷ 0.955 = Rs. 200.

questions.text: A shopkeeper buys 10 fans and sells 8 fans at the cost price of 10 fans. What is the profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Taking each fan to cost 1, the 8 fans sold cost 8 and fetch 10, a profit of 2 on 8: 2/8 × 100 = 25%.

questions.text: Average score of 11 players of a cricket team in a one day match is 32. The runs scored by the ten players are 11, 51, 2, 96, 21, 33, 0, 32, 9 and 14. What is the score of 11th player?
questions.explanation: The 11 players scored 11 × 32 = 352 runs in all and the ten listed scores add up to 269, so the 11th player scored 352 − 269 = 83.

questions.text: There are only two candidates in an election. A person got 40 percent votes and lost by 50 votes. Assuming that there were no invalid votes, the total number of votes are :
questions.explanation: The winner got 60% of the votes and the loser 40%, so the 50-vote margin is 20% of the votes: 50 × 100/20 = 250.

questions.text: What would be the (Approximate) compound interest (in Rs.) on the principal amount of Rs.10,000 for 2 years at an interest rate of 16% per annum (compounding is done half-yearly)?
questions.explanation: Compounded half-yearly, the rate is 8% for each of 4 half-years: 10,000 × 1.08⁴ = 10,000 × 1.36048896 = Rs. 13,604.89, so the interest is about Rs. 3,604.

questions.text: A solution consists of 50 litres of pure milk. 10 litres of milk is replaced with equal quantity of water. Again 10 litres of the mixture is substituted by 10 litres of water and this operation is repeated one more time. Find the quantity of milk in the final solution.
questions.explanation: 10 litres are replaced three times, and each time 40/50 = 4/5 of the milk stays: 50 × (4/5)³ = 50 × 64/125 = 25.6 litres.

questions.text: If a natural number when divided by 2,3, and 4 leaves a remainder of 1 in each case, then what is the smallest possible three digit natural number?
questions.explanation: The number is 1 more than a multiple of LCM(2, 3, 4) = 12. The smallest such three-digit number is 12 × 9 + 1 = 109, as 12 × 8 + 1 = 97 has two digits.

questions.text: A thief started running at a speed of 12 m/s, after running for 10 sec a policeman started running to catch the thief in the same direction at a speed of 14.5 m/s. What is the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief?
questions.explanation: In 10 seconds the thief gets 12 × 10 = 120 m ahead. The policeman gains 14.5 − 12 = 2.5 m a second, so he catches up in 120/2.5 = 48 seconds.

questions.text: In a town there are 5500 people who can vote in an election. If the number of male voters increases by 11% and female voters increases by 20%, then the number of voters becomes 6330. Find the initial number of male and female voters, respectively, in the town.
questions.explanation: With m male voters and 5500 − m female voters, 1.11m + 1.2(5500 − m) = 6330, so 6600 − 0.09m = 6330 and m = 3000. There are 5500 − 3000 = 2500 female voters.

questions.text: When Ashish finishes a certain work, he gets a total wage of Rs. 70. When Kanika finishes the same work, he gets a total wage of Rs. 165. The daily wages of Ashish and Kanika are Rs. 3.5 and Rs. 5.5 respectively. If both of them do it together, what is the cost of the work?
questions.explanation: Ashish takes 70 ÷ 3.5 = 20 days and Kanika 165 ÷ 5.5 = 30 days. Together they do 1/20 + 1/30 = 1/12 of the work a day, so they take 12 days and are paid 12 × (3.5 + 5.5) = Rs. 108.

questions.text: Identify the MISSPELT word in the following sentence. In some regions of the world, child poverty remains a serious issue, significently in relation of the geospatial and living standards in which children grow up.
questions.explanation: 'Significently' is misspelt: the word is 'significantly', from 'significant'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. “Keep an eye on” the situation around, and take your decision accordingly.
questions.explanation: To 'keep an eye on' something is to watch it closely and continually.

questions.text: The given sentence is divided into three segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'no error' as your answer. It will take / 5 minutes to / preparing a cup of tea.
questions.explanation: 'Take ... to' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'It will take 5 minutes to prepare a cup of tea.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom that can be substituted in the following sentence. My son was disappointed with his failure, but he “took heart” and tried again
questions.explanation: To 'take heart' is to feel encouraged or more confident, which is why the son tried again.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Accuse
questions.explanation: To 'accuse' is to charge someone with wrongdoing; to 'defend' is to speak up for them. 'Incriminate', 'charge' and 'allege' are close in meaning to 'accuse'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The _______ of this beautiful garden is so exciting.
