questions.explanation: 'Sight' here means the view of something: seeing the garden is exciting. A 'site' is a place, to 'cite' is to quote, and 'slight' means small.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence to make it a meaningful sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. The first step towards the prevention of cybercrimes “will obviously to promote awareness about criminal activities” and tighten up security.
options: would obviously been to promote awareness about criminal activities
would obviously be to promote awareness about criminal activities
would obviously be to promote awareness for criminal activities
questions.explanation: The modal 'would' needs the base verb 'be' before the infinitive: 'would obviously be to promote'. 'Would been' is ungrammatical, and awareness is 'about' (or 'of') criminal activities, not 'for' them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. These products _________ for a long time.
questions.explanation: As a verb, 'last' means to stay in use or keep going: the products last a long time. As an adjective it means final, hence a homonym. 'Lust', 'lost' and 'least' do not fit.

questions.text: Complete the sentence by choosing the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. When you want to “leave”, you ___________ the building.
questions.explanation: To 'exit' a building is to leave it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. Many instances of corruption have been reported by “authorities posted theyre”.
options: authorities in which were posted theyre
questions.explanation: 'Theyre' should be the adverb 'there', meaning in that place: 'authorities posted there'. 'No substitution' keeps the misspelling, and the other two keep it and add an ungrammatical relative clause.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Grumble
questions.explanation: To 'grumble' is to complain in a low, discontented way; to 'praise' is to express approval, its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Commerce
questions.explanation: 'Commerce' is the buying and selling of goods, that is 'trade'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'magnificent'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word in the following sentence. He is a “spendthrift” and spends money lavishly.
questions.explanation: A 'spendthrift' wastes money; a 'miser' hoards it and spends as little as possible. The noun 'spendthrift' needs a noun for its opposite: 'careful' and 'mean' are adjectives, and 'wicked' is unrelated.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The build up to the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, which (1)__________ on July 23 and finished on August 8, as defined by cautious optimism, as well as a slew of (2)___________ that came with staging the Games under tight safety standards and without (3)____________ during the COVID-19 outbreak. While Indian competitors had shown enough potential to (4)_________ expect a big return of medals in the Games, the disappointments of Rio 2016 lingered. What happened was that India delivered its best-ever performance at the Games, beginning with Mirabai Chanu's silver medal in weightlifting on the first day and culminating with Neeraj Chopra's (5)__________ gold medal in javelin throw on the country's last day of competition in Tokyo.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: The Games 'began' on July 23 and 'finished' on August 8: the simple past matches 'finished'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The build up to the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, which (1)__________ on July 23 and finished on August 8, as defined by cautious optimism, as well as a slew of (2)___________ that came with staging the Games under tight safety standards and without (3)____________ during the COVID-19 outbreak. While Indian competitors had shown enough potential to (4)_________ expect a big return of medals in the Games, the disappointments of Rio 2016 lingered. What happened was that India delivered its best-ever performance at the Games, beginning with Mirabai Chanu's silver medal in weightlifting on the first day and culminating with Neeraj Chopra's (5)__________ gold medal in javelin throw on the country's last day of competition in Tokyo.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: Staging the Games under tight safety rules brought worries, which fits 'anxiety' and the 'cautious optimism' before it; 'certainty' and 'enjoyment' contradict it, and 'configuration' makes no sense here.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The build up to the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, which (1)__________ on July 23 and finished on August 8, as defined by cautious optimism, as well as a slew of (2)___________ that came with staging the Games under tight safety standards and without (3)____________ during the COVID-19 outbreak. While Indian competitors had shown enough potential to (4)_________ expect a big return of medals in the Games, the disappointments of Rio 2016 lingered. What happened was that India delivered its best-ever performance at the Games, beginning with Mirabai Chanu's silver medal in weightlifting on the first day and culminating with Neeraj Chopra's (5)__________ gold medal in javelin throw on the country's last day of competition in Tokyo.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: Because of the pandemic the Tokyo Games were held without 'spectators'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The build up to the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, which (1)__________ on July 23 and finished on August 8, as defined by cautious optimism, as well as a slew of (2)___________ that came with staging the Games under tight safety standards and without (3)____________ during the COVID-19 outbreak. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: To 'legitimately' expect something is to expect it with good reason, here the potential the athletes had shown.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The build up to the 2020 Tokyo Olympics, which (1)__________ on July 23 and finished on August 8, as defined by cautious optimism, as well as a slew of (2)___________ that came with staging the Games under tight safety standards and without (3)____________ during the COVID-19 outbreak. While Indian competitors had shown enough potential to (4)_________ expect a big return of medals in the Games, the disappointments of Rio 2016 lingered. What happened was that India delivered its best-ever performance at the Games, beginning with Mirabai Chanu's silver medal in weightlifting on the first day and culminating with Neeraj Chopra's (5)__________ gold medal in javelin throw on the country's last day of competition in Tokyo.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: Neeraj Chopra's javelin gold was 'historic': India's first Olympic gold in athletics.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: • All rats are lions • Some rats are jackals • No jackal is mongoose Conclusions: I. Some jackals are lions II. Some rats are not mongoose III. No mongoose is a lion
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I, II or III follows
questions.explanation: The rats that are jackals are also lions, so some jackals are lions (I); being jackals, those rats are not mongooses, so some rats are not mongooses (II). Nothing links mongooses to lions, so III does not follow.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? SFJW, QHLU, ?, MLPQ, KNRO
questions.explanation: The first letters move 2 back (S, Q, O, M, K), the second 2 forward (F, H, J, L, N), the third 2 forward (J, L, N, P, R) and the fourth 2 back (W, U, S, Q, O). The missing cluster is OJNS.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BORED’ is written as ‘YLIVW’ and ‘FIGHT’ is written as ‘URTSG’. How will ‘PRINT’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on): BORED → YLIVW and FIGHT → URTSG. So PRINT → KIRMG.

questions.text: In a code language, ‘corrupt men' is coded as 'vu ka', 'he is corrupt' is coded as ‘hu na vu', 'she is serious' is coded as 'po na du', and 'she faints' is coded as 'po gu'. What is the code for the word 'serious'?
questions.explanation: 'Corrupt' is common to the first two sentences, so it is 'vu'; 'is' is 'na' (second and third) and 'she' is 'po' (third and fourth). That leaves 'du' for 'serious'.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question marks (?) in the given series? 156, 144, 133, 123, 114, ?, 99, ?, 88, 84
questions.explanation: The differences are −12, −11, −10, −9, ..., falling by one each time: 114 − 8 = 106, 106 − 7 = 99, 99 − 6 = 93 and 93 − 5 = 88.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 branch 2 brunch 3 bracket 4 brass 5 bread
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: bracket (3), branch (1), brass (4), bread (5), brunch (2). The first three all begin 'bra', so their fourth letters, c, n, s, decide the order.

questions.text: Which two signs, from the given options, should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 210 ÷ 7 × 320 ÷ (16 − 4 × 15 × 17) = 15 + 5

Six friends P, Q, R, S, T and U are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. P sits second to the right of U. R sits third to the right of Q. S and R both are the immediate neighbours of P. Who sits between Q and U?
questions.explanation: Going round to the right from U the seats are U, R, P, S, Q, T. P is second to the right of U with R and S beside him; R must be the one between U and P, since R sits opposite Q and the seat opposite P's other neighbour is U's. T takes the last seat, between Q and U.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? DFGI, JLMO, PRSU, VXYA, ?
questions.explanation: Within each cluster the letters step +2, +1, +2 (D F G I), and each cluster starts 6 letters after the last: D, J, P, V, then B (wrapping round after Z). So BDEG.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 3840, 384, ?, 8, 2, 1
questions.explanation: Each term is divided by 10, 8, 6, 4 and 2 in turn: 384 ÷ 8 = 48, 48 ÷ 6 = 8, 8 ÷ 4 = 2 and 2 ÷ 2 = 1.

questions.text: Seven people, E, F, G, H, I, J and K are sitting in a straight row, facing north. H is sitting fourth to the left of I. K is sitting third to the left of F. J is sitting third to the right of F. G is sitting fourth to the right of K. Who sits at the third position from the left end of the row?
questions.explanation: J is third to the right of F and K third to its left, so K, F and J sit 1st, 4th and 7th from the left, and G, fourth to the right of K, sits 5th. H, fourth to the left of I, must then be 2nd with I 6th, leaving the 3rd place for E.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. GENERAL : 7514518112 :: RELATION : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as its place in the alphabet: G E N E R A L → 7 5 14 5 18 1 12. So R E L A T I O N → 18 5 12 1 20 9 15 14: 1851212091514.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the sixth number is related to the fifth number. 4 : 96 :: 13 : ? :: 9 : 161
questions.explanation: Each number's square plus 80 gives its pair: 4² + 80 = 96 and 9² + 80 = 161. So 13² + 80 = 169 + 80 = 249.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 30 + 54 ÷ 18 - 48 × 16 = 58
questions.explanation: After interchanging × and +: 30 × 54 ÷ 18 − 48 + 16 = 90 − 48 + 16 = 58.

questions.text: Which scheme was launched by Indian government for creation of self employment opportunities for unemployed educated youth?
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister's Rozgar Yojana, launched on 2 October 1993, helped educated unemployed young people set up their own enterprises; in 2008 it was merged with the Rural Employment Generation Programme into the PMEGP.

questions.text: Who among the following was the founder of the Mauryan Empire?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan Empire in the late fourth century BCE after overthrowing the Nandas; Ashoka was his grandson. Samudragupta and Chandragupta II were Gupta rulers.

questions.text: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu; This is an example of _________ reaction.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives displacement: iron, being more reactive than copper, displaces it from copper sulphate solution, and NCERT uses this very equation as its example of a displacement reaction. Strictly it is also a redox reaction (iron is oxidised and copper ions are reduced), but 'displacement' is the textbook classification.

questions.text: Garba folk dance belongs to which of the following states of India?
questions.explanation: Garba, danced in circles during Navratri around a lamp or an image of the goddess, is a folk dance of Gujarat.

questions.text: Which state of India hosted the 2015 National Games of India?
questions.explanation: Kerala hosted the 35th National Games in January-February 2015, with Thiruvananthapuram as the main venue.

questions.text: In 2019-20, India had ______ km of broad gauge railway lines.
questions.explanation: Indian Railways' figures for 31 March 2020, the end of 2019-20, give 63,949.26 route km of broad gauge, about 63,950, out of 67,956 route km in all (2,402 km of metre gauge and 1,604 km of narrow gauge).

questions.text: In India, Information Technology Act was passed in the year _______.
questions.explanation: The Information Technology Act, 2000, India's main law on electronic records, e-commerce and cybercrime, was passed in 2000; it was substantially amended in 2008.

questions.text: Which Indian Cricketer is known as "The Wall" ?
questions.explanation: Rahul Dravid was called 'The Wall' for his solid, patient defensive batting.

questions.text: Who among the following was elected as the President of Board of Control for Cricket in India(BCCI) in October 2022?
questions.explanation: Roger Binny, a member of India's 1983 World Cup-winning team, was elected unopposed as BCCI President on 18 October 2022, succeeding Sourav Ganguly.

questions.text: India's first lavender festival was inaugrated in ___________ in May 2022.
questions.explanation: India's first lavender festival was held at Bhaderwah in Doda district, Jammu and Kashmir, in May 2022, organised by CSIR-IIIM under the CSIR Aroma Mission and inaugurated by Union Minister Jitendra Singh.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: He wrote ‘Vande Mataram’ as a hymn to the motherland. Who is 'he' referred to?
questions.explanation: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote 'Vande Mataram' and included it in his novel 'Anandamath' (1882).

questions.text: What should be the minimum age for being a member of Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Article 84(b) requires a member of the Lok Sabha to be at least 25 years old; for the Rajya Sabha the minimum is 30.

questions.text: C₂H₅OH is the chemical formula of _________________.
questions.explanation: C₂H₅OH is ethanol (ethyl alcohol), the alcohol with two carbon atoms.

questions.text: Who,in August 2022, was appointed as the Secretary to the President of India?
questions.explanation: In August 2022 the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet appointed Rajesh Verma, a 1987-batch IAS officer of the Odisha cadre, as Secretary to President Droupadi Murmu; he succeeded Kapil Dev Tripathi.

questions.text: The _______ committee was set up to make recommendations about the fundamental duties.
questions.explanation: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended adding Fundamental Duties to the Constitution; the 42nd Amendment did so the same year, as Article 51A.

questions.text: All banks which are included in the ________Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 are Scheduled Banks.
questions.explanation: Banks listed in the Second Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 are scheduled banks.

questions.text: One third of a journey is covered at the rate of 30 km/h, one fourth at the rate of 50 km/h and the rest at 60 km/h. Find the average speed for the whole journey. (Correct to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanation: Over one unit of distance the time is (1/3)/30 + (1/4)/50 + (5/12)/60 = 1/90 + 1/200 + 1/144 = (40 + 18 + 25)/3600 = 83/3600 hour, so the average speed is 3600/83 = 43.37 km/h.

questions.text: If 27 : 81 :: x : 63, then find the value of x.
A solid metallic sphere of radius 21 cm is melted and moulded into small right circular cones, each of radius 7 cm and height of 3 cm. The number of such cones is:
questions.explanation: The sphere's volume is (4/3)π × 21³ = 12,348π cm³ and each cone's (1/3)π × 7² × 3 = 49π cm³, so 12,348 ÷ 49 = 252 cones.

questions.text: The LCM of 30, 36 and 40 is divided by 10. The result is X's square. Find the value of X.

A silver shop owner claims that he is selling silver at ₹65/g when cost price is ₹70/g, but he is giving 900 mg instead of 1 g. The percentage of profit or loss of the shop owner (correct to 2 decimal places) is:
questions.explanation: He charges ₹65 for 900 mg, which cost him 0.9 × 70 = ₹63. Profit = 2/63 × 100 = 3.17%.

questions.text: Arun applied for a job of English teacher in a school. In the test for the job, he scored 9 in speaking, 8 in listening, 6 in writing, and 7 in interview. For calculating the final score, weights of 4, 3, 3 and 4 were assigned to speaking, listening, writing and interview respectively. What is the weighted average score of Arun? (Round off to two decimal places)

A shopkeeper offers the following three discount schemes. Which scheme(s) has/have the maximum discount percentage? I. Two successive discounts of 5% and 20% II. Buy 6, get 2 free III. Buy 6, get 4 free
questions.explanation: I: 1 − 0.95 × 0.80 = 0.24, a 24% discount. II: 2 free out of 8 is 25%. III: 4 free out of 10 is 40%, the largest.

questions.text: A certain sum becomes ₹26,980 in 3years and ₹40,280 in 8 years at simple interest. Find the rate of interest.
The difference between a discount of 30% and two successive discounts of 17% and 13% on Rs.5,000 is ________.
questions.explanation: A 30% discount is ₹1,500. Successive discounts of 17% and 13% leave 0.83 × 0.87 = 0.7221 of the price, a discount of 27.79%, or ₹1,389.50. The difference is ₹110.50.

questions.text: Sanju can do a piece of work in 17 days and Rohan can do the same work in 68 days. Find the time required to complete the same work if they are working on alternate days and Sanju starts the work on first day.
questions.explanation: Take the work as 68 units: Sanju does 4 a day and Rohan 1, so each two-day pair does 5. After 13 pairs (26 days) 65 units are done, and on day 27 Sanju does the last 3 units in 3/4 of a day: 26¾ = 107/4 days.

questions.text: A child aged 8 years is weighs 20 kg. By the time the child is 15 years old, he weighs 42 kg. What is the percent increase in the weight?
If 30 + 180 ÷ 30 × 6 – 15 – 16 – 60 ÷ n – 15 = 0, then the value of n is:
Two sprinters cover the same distance at the speed of 18 km/h and 20 km/h, respectively. Find the distance travelled when one takes 15 minutes longer than the other.
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Witty
questions.explanation: 'Witty' means clever and amusing; its opposite is 'stupid'. 'Smart' is close in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Honest
questions.explanation: 'Corrupt' (dishonest, open to bribes) is the opposite of 'honest'. 'Frank' and 'open' are near-synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The waiters were quick to “replenish” their stock of food.
questions.explanation: To 'replenish' a stock is to fill it up again: 'The waiters were quick to fill up their stock of food.'

questions.text: Identify the spelling error in the given sentence and select the option that rectifies the error. It is necessary for candidates to carry their examination addmit cards with them.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'admit', with one 'd'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. The annual extraction of this ________ costs around $10,000,000.
questions.explanation: An 'ore' is rock from which a metal is extracted. 'Or' and the poetic 'o'er' (over) sound the same but make no sense here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Bury the hatchet
questions.explanation: To 'bury the hatchet' is to end a quarrel and make peace.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Rover had eaten the pie before we gets home.
questions.explanation: 'We' takes 'get', not 'gets', and after the past perfect 'had eaten' the sentence needs the simple past: 'before we got home'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence. Her “debonair” combined with quick wit added to her oratory skills.
questions.explanation: 'Debonair' means confident, stylish and charming: 'charming'. 'Churlish' (rude) is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Chew someone out
questions.explanation: To 'chew someone out' is to scold them angrily.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The farmer _____________ up and saw a tractor approaching him.
questions.explanation: 'Looked up' (raised his eyes) leads to 'saw a tractor approaching'; 'sit' is the wrong tense beside 'saw', and 'bent up' and 'cleared up' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in the bracket to fill in the blank. You have ________ (built up) a lot of muscles by going to the gym.
questions.explanation: To 'build up' muscle is to gain it: 'You have gained a lot of muscles by going to the gym.' 'Enhanced', 'elevated' and 'boosted' do not go with muscles.

questions.text: Identify and correct the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. The monkies were snatching food from the passengers in the bus.
questions.explanation: A noun ending in a vowel followed by 'y' just adds 's' in the plural: 'monkeys'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word from the given options. My grandmother, a “pious” lady, died peacefully in her village.
questions.explanation: 'Pious' means deeply religious: 'devout'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Men “never have managed” to abolish wars up to now but maybe they will find a way in future.
questions.explanation: In the present perfect the adverb 'never' goes between the auxiliary and the main verb: 'Men have never managed to abolish wars'.

questions.text: Select the correct word for the blanks in the given sentence. Venga boys is a famous musical _________ of the country and Madhu gave me a _________ on my birthday.
questions.explanation: 'Band' fits both blanks: a musical band is a group of musicians, and a band, such as a wristband, can be a birthday gift. 'Group' does not suit the second blank, nor 'ring' the first.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The feeling of affection comes only if trust and respect are (1)________. Without trust and respect, you feel that the other is (2)________ to make you unhappy and/or does not wish well for you and hence you can never feel attraction for him/her. You always see each other as being in (3)________. And that is why today in the family, you find that people have been living together for years and years and still don’t feel (4)________ to each other, because that basic trust and respect are missing. Affection comes when we (5)_______ that two or more persons want to make each other happy. Then for the first time, we feel that we are related to the other person. This feeling is called affection.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Affection comes only when trust and respect are 'ensured', that is made certain.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Without trust and respect, you feel the other is 'trying' to make you unhappy.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The feeling of affection comes only if trust and respect are (1)________. Without trust and respect, you feel that the other is (2)________ to make you unhappy and/or does not wish well for you and hence you can never feel attraction for him/her. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: People without trust see each other as being in 'opposition', on opposite sides.
