Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Affection comes when we 'recognise', that is realise, that the persons want to make each other happy.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘OXFORD’ is written as ‘OODFRX’ and ‘KILLING’ is written as ‘IIGKLLN’. How will ‘SOLUTION’ be written as in that language?
questions.explanation: The vowels come first and then the consonants, each in alphabetical order: OXFORD → OO + DFRX and KILLING → II + GKLLN. So SOLUTION → IOOU + LNST: IOOULNST.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 9 : 27 :: 12 : 48 :: 6 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first divided by 3: 9² ÷ 3 = 27 and 12² ÷ 3 = 48. Likewise 6² ÷ 3 = 12.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Marching 2 Marble 3 Matching 4 Maker 5 Major
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Major (5), Maker (4), Marble (2), Marching (1), Matching (3). 'Maj' comes before 'Mak' and 'Mar', 'Marb' before 'Marc', and 'Mar' before 'Mat'.

questions.text: If ‘–‘ means ‘division’, ‘+’ means ‘multiplication’, ‘×’ means ‘addition’ and ‘÷’ means ‘subtraction’, which of the following equations is correct?
questions.explanation: After replacing the signs: 10 ÷ 2 × 3 − 9 + 2 = 15 − 9 + 2 = 8. The other equations come to 22, 33 and 24.5, not 21, 32 and 33.

questions.text: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? AEHJ , DHKM , ? , JNQS , MQTV
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward from one cluster to the next: A, D, G, J, M; E, H, K, N, Q; H, K, N, Q, T; J, M, P, S, V. The missing cluster is GKNP.

questions.text: In a code language, 'dark colors' is coded as 'yu nu', 'days are bright' is coded as 'wu tu ku', 'nights are dark' is coded as 'ku nu pu', 'paint bright' is coded as 'wu ru'. What is the code for the word 'colors'?
questions.explanation: 'Dark' is the word common to 'dark colors' (yu nu) and 'nights are dark' (ku nu pu), so 'dark' is 'nu' and 'colors' is 'yu'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Annual : Semi-annual:: Monthly : ?
questions.explanation: Semi-annual means every half year, twice a year; every half month, about twice a month, is fortnightly (every two weeks).

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? AETO, CGRM, ?, GKNI, IMLG
questions.explanation: The first letters run A, C, E, G, I and the second E, G, I, K, M (2 places forward each time); the third run T, R, P, N, L and the fourth O, M, K, I, G (2 places back). The missing cluster is EIPK.

questions.text: L is the husband of O. Q is the mother-in-law of O. P is the sister of L. P is married to R. R has one son T. How is Q related to T?
questions.explanation: Q is the mother-in-law of O, L's wife, so she is the mother of L and of his sister P. T is the son of P and her husband R, so Q is T's mother's mother.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. AFHO : CHIP :: QDXM : SFYN :: ADGH : ?
questions.explanation: The first two letters move 2 places forward and the last two 1 place: AFHO → CHIP and QDXM → SFYN. So ADGH → CFHI.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 104 ÷ 13 + 78 - 3 × 2 = 143

Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All flowers are leaves. All leaves are stems. Some stems are roots. Conclusions: I. Some stems are leaves. II. Some flowers are roots. III. Some leaves are flowers.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: Every leaf is a stem, so some stems are leaves (I); every flower is a leaf, so some leaves are flowers (III). The stems that are roots need not include any flower, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 53, 56 ,50 ,?, 47 ,62
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 53, 50, 47 fall by 3 and 56, ?, 62 rise by 3, so ? = 59.

questions.text: Seven people are sitting in a movie theatre watching a movie facing North. D is sitting towards right of A but towards left of G. Y is sitting towards right of C and towards left of A. Z is sitting towards left of F and is second from the right end. Who is sitting second from the left end?
questions.explanation: C, Y, A, D and G sit in that order from the left. Z is second from the right with F somewhere to its right, so F is at the right end and the row is C, Y, A, D, G, Z, F: Y is second from the left.

questions.text: There are 8 people sitting in a circle facing the centre: A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H. A is sitting to the immediate right of G and immediate left of E. Second to the right of E is C. D is sitting to the immediate left of C. F is sitting to the immediate left of G. H is the immediate neighbour of F and B. Who is sitting to the immediate right of B?
questions.explanation: Going round to each person's right, the order is F, G, A, E, D, C, B, H and back to F: A sits between G and E, C is second to the right of E with D between them, F is on G's left, and H sits between B and F. So H is to the immediate right of B.

questions.text: What type of unemployment will be generated by the agricultural sector in case when it employs additional labourers only for some time of the year like the harvest season?
questions.explanation: Seasonal unemployment arises when work is available only at certain times of the year, as on farms at sowing and harvest. In disguised unemployment more people work than are needed, so removing some would not lower output.

questions.text: A ____________is a deposit account opted for by many who wish to save a certain part of their earnings.
questions.explanation: A savings account is a bank deposit account for keeping part of one's earnings safe while it earns interest. Shares and debentures are securities, and a loan is money borrowed.

questions.text: Export of goods enhances ______.
questions.explanation: Exports are paid for in foreign currency, so they add to a country's foreign exchange earnings.

questions.text: Who became the Member of Legislative Assembly from Dhamnagar constituency in Odisha, India in November 2022?
questions.explanation: Suryabanshi Suraj of the BJP won the Dhamnagar by-election held on 3 November 2022, defeating Abanti Das of the BJD; the seat fell vacant on the death of his father, the sitting MLA Bishnu Charan Sethi.

questions.text: India's first-ever SAI Centre of Excellence for mountain terrain biking and bicycle motocross is to be set up in _____________.
questions.explanation: In March 2022 the Sports Ministry announced India's first SAI National Centre of Excellence for mountain terrain biking and bicycle motocross (BMX) in Shimla, Himachal Pradesh, to be set up with the state government.

questions.text: Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards (Akademi Puraskar) carries ______________.
options: Rs 1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh) along with a Tamrapatra and Angavastram
Rs 50,000/- along with a Tamrapatra and Angavastram
questions.explanation: When the exam was held (January 2023), the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Akademi Puraskar) carried ₹1,00,000 with a tamrapatra (copper plaque) and an angavastram (shawl); the higher Akademi Fellowship carried ₹3,00,000.

questions.text: The State Government under Consumer Protection Act 2019, by notification, shall establish a _________,in each district of the State.
questions.explanation: Section 28 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 has the State Government set up, by notification, a District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (the District Commission) in each district. Above it are the State and National Commissions.

questions.text: The _________ was set up in 1963 with responsibilities in the field of seed production, particularly the foundation stock of HYV seeds.
questions.explanation: The National Seeds Corporation, a Government of India undertaking under the Ministry of Agriculture, was set up in March 1963 to produce foundation and certified seed.

questions.text: Which of the following former Chief Economic Advisors has been appointed as the full time member of National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog in November 2022?
questions.explanation: Arvind Virmani, Chief Economic Adviser from 2007 to 2009, was appointed a full-time member of NITI Aayog in November 2022 and took charge on 16 November.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Why did Mohammed Ali Jinnah, Madan Mohan Malaviya and Mazhar Ul Haq resign from the Imperial Legislative Council?
options: to protest against the Rowlatt Act
to protest against the Simon commission
questions.explanation: The three resigned from the Imperial Legislative Council in 1919 in protest against the Rowlatt Act, which let the government imprison people without trial.

questions.text: Foods with starch in them will turn blue- black when they come in contact with ___________.
questions.explanation: Iodine turns blue-black with starch, the standard test for starch in food.

questions.text: Kati Bihu, one of the three Bihu festivals of Assam, is celebrated in the month of ____________.
questions.explanation: Kati (Kongali) Bihu falls in mid-October, in the Assamese month of Kati, while the paddy is still growing. Bohag (Rongali) Bihu falls in April and Magh (Bhogali) Bihu in January.

questions.text: The members of a Vidhan Parishad are elected for a term of ________ years.
questions.explanation: A Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) is a permanent house: each member serves six years, and one-third of the members retire every second year.

questions.text: What are the volcanoes which have not erupted for a very long time but might erupt in future called?
questions.explanation: Dormant volcanoes have not erupted for a long time but may erupt again; extinct ones are not expected to erupt again, and active ones erupt from time to time.

questions.text: Which of the following was the capital of Vajji Mahajanapada?
questions.explanation: Vaishali was the capital of the Vajji (Vrijji) confederacy. Anga was itself a mahajanapada, with its capital at Champa, and Pataliputra was a later capital of Magadha.

questions.text: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment was made according to the recommendation of __________, set up in 1976.
questions.explanation: The Swaran Singh Committee, set up in 1976, recommended Fundamental Duties for citizens; the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added them to the Constitution as Article 51A.

questions.text: In a football match, the length of a pitch must be between_______ and 120m.
questions.explanation: Under the Laws of the Game the touchline must be 90 m to 120 m long (100 to 130 yards); for international matches the range is 100 m to 110 m.

questions.text: The Ghodemodini dance is a folk dance form associated with ________.
questions.explanation: Ghode Modni, the 'horse dance' of Goa, is performed at Shigmo by dancers wearing wooden horse frames and carrying swords, recalling the region's warriors.

questions.text: Sri Lanka is separated from India by the ______.
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait, between Tamil Nadu and northern Sri Lanka, separates the two countries. The Isthmus of Kra is in Thailand, the Strait of Gibraltar separates Spain and Morocco, and the Isthmus of Panama joins the two Americas.

questions.text: Which two gases are released when lead nitrate is heated?
questions.explanation: Heated lead nitrate decomposes into lead oxide, brown nitrogen dioxide and oxygen: 2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂.

questions.text: Rajneesh deposited Rs.3,00,000 in a bank for three years. What will be the final amount if the rate of interest is 8% compounded annually?

The average temperature of a certain city on different days is as follows: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday = 42°; Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday = 44°; What is the temperature on Friday if the ratio of the temperature on Monday and Friday is 3: 5?
questions.explanation: The two sums are 4 × 42 = 168 and 4 × 44 = 176, so Friday is 8° warmer than Monday. With Monday : Friday = 3 : 5, the 2 parts of difference are 8°, so one part is 4° and Friday is 5 × 4 = 20°.

questions.text: Find the third proportional to 16 and 320.
questions.explanation: The third proportional to a and b is b²/a = 320²/16 = 1,02,400/16 = 6,400.

questions.text: The price of a commodity increases by 10% from 2020 to 2021 and it again increases by 15% from 2021 to 2022. The difference in the prices in 2020 and 2022 is ₹35. What is the price of the commodity (in ₹) in 2021 (rounded up to one decimal place)?
questions.explanation: If the 2020 price is P, the 2022 price is P × 1.1 × 1.15 = 1.265P, so 0.265P = 35 and P = 35 ÷ 0.265 ≈ 132.08. The 2021 price is 1.1P = 38.5 ÷ 0.265 ≈ ₹145.28, or 145.3 to one decimal place.

questions.text: An electric geyser is sold at Rs.7,100 after reducing Rs.244 in addition to two successive discounts of 15% and 4% on the marked price. Find the marked price (in Rs.) of the geyser.
In a discount scheme, there is 50% discount on the marked price of Rs.500, but at the end it is sold for Rs.200. What additional discount did the customer get?
questions.explanation: After the 50% discount the price is ₹250; selling at ₹200 takes off ₹50 more, which is 50/250 = 20% of the reduced price.

questions.text: An article is marked at Rs.7,500 and available at a discount of 12%. The shopkeeper gives another off-season discount to the buyer and sell the article for Rs.5,400. Find the off-season discount. (Correct to two decimals places.)
questions.explanation: After 12% off the price is 7,500 × 0.88 = ₹6,600. Selling at ₹5,400 is a further ₹1,200 off: 1,200/6,600 × 100 = 18.18%.

questions.text: The material of a solid right circular cylinder is converted into the shape of a solid cone of equal radius. If the height of the cylinder is 8.8 cm, then the height of the cone is:
questions.explanation: The volumes are equal and so are the radii: πr² × 8.8 = (1/3)πr²h, so h = 3 × 8.8 = 26.4 cm.

questions.text: From 2011 to 2014, a town’s population is increasing at the rate of 2% annually. If its population was 13,265 in 2014, then what would have been its population (Approximately) in 2011?
A stock of food is enough for 315 men for 48 days. For how many days the same stock of food is enough, if 45 more men join?
questions.explanation: The food lasts 315 × 48 = 15,120 man-days; for 315 + 45 = 360 men that is 15,120 ÷ 360 = 42 days.

questions.text: If the number 40 is increased by 40%, then what will be the actual increase?
questions.explanation: The increase is 40% of 40 = 0.4 × 40 = 16.

questions.text: Find the square of the sum of the digits of the smallest number divisible by both 18 and 24.
questions.explanation: The LCM of 18 (2 × 3²) and 24 (2³ × 3) is 2³ × 3² = 72. Its digits add up to 7 + 2 = 9, and 9² = 81.

questions.text: A man can row upstream at 12 km/h and downstream at 20 km/h. Find the man’s rowing speed in still water, and the rate of current.
questions.explanation: Speed in still water = (20 + 12)/2 = 16 km/h; rate of the current = (20 − 12)/2 = 4 km/h.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The road “which connected for” two villages is now deserted.
questions.explanation: 'Connect' takes a direct object, with no 'for', and the past tense suits a road that is now deserted: 'The road that connected the two villages is now deserted.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank with the synonym of the underlined word. The casual nature of the student “destroyed” his studies and ________ his future.
questions.explanation: 'Ruined' means the same as 'destroyed': his casual nature destroyed his studies and ruined his future.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Succinct
questions.explanation: 'Succinct' means brief and to the point; its opposite is 'lengthy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Cluster
questions.explanation: A 'cluster' is a group of similar things close together; its opposite is a single 'individual'. 'Group' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Despise
questions.explanation: To 'despise' is to look down on or 'hate'. 'Revere', to respect deeply, is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the correct idiom that can substitute the italicised group of words in the given sentence. Will humanity overcome the greed of leaders all around the world? This is the “most important issue to be discussed” today.
options: burn the candle at both ends
burn a hole in the pocket
questions.explanation: A 'burning question' is an urgent issue that everyone is discussing: 'This is the burning question today.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. The construction _________ was far from his home.
questions.explanation: A 'site' is the place where something is built or happens. To 'cite' is to quote, a 'sight' is a view or the power of seeing, and 'cyte' is only a word ending meaning a cell.

questions.text: Select the sentence that contains the MISSPELT word from the given options.
options: Both of them were best friends, now they are at daggers drawn.
As if to fill the small hours of that cold night with warm thoughts, I picked up the book and started browsing.
Without the slightest warning, something new breaks into your life that you may be completely unconscious of.
The gist of the quote was that all reasonable men addopt themselves to the world.
questions.explanation: 'Addopt' is misspelt: the saying's verb is 'adapt' (to fit in with), and even 'adopt' has a single 'd'. 'Daggers', 'browsing' and 'unconscious' are correctly spelt.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate spelling that can correctly substitute the misspelt underlined segment in the given sentence. He “aquiesced” to the plans his parents had made for him.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'acquiesced', with 'cq': he accepted his parents' plans without protest.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. The pot calling the kettle black
options: Preparing the tea without boiling water
People are guilty of the very fault they identify in others
Speaking strangely in an official meeting
questions.explanation: 'The pot calling the kettle black' describes someone who criticises another for a fault they share.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate set of words to complete the sentence. I will not spend a single ______ on a bottle of perfume until I know that I love its ________.
questions.explanation: A 'cent' is a coin of very small value and a 'scent' is a smell: not a single cent until I know that I love its scent. 'Sent' is the past of 'send'.

questions.text: Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Wear rubber gloves while chopping chillies (as it could irritate the skin).
options: as these could irritate the skin
as they can irritate the skin
as it would irritate the skin
as these would irritate the skin
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'as they can irritate the skin': the plural 'chillies' needs a plural pronoun, so 'it' is wrong, and 'can' states a general fact about what chillies do. 'As these could irritate the skin' is also grammatical, but 'they' is the plain pronoun for a noun just named, and the tentative 'could' suits a general fact less well than 'can'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. “He very pleased” that you have passed with distinction.
questions.explanation: The sentence has no verb: the adjective 'pleased' needs 'is'. 'He is very pleased that you have passed with distinction.'

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. We “must” “acknowledge” the fact that we “had been” “visited” Paris many times with friends.
questions.explanation: 'Had been visited' is passive, which makes no sense with 'we' as the visitors; the present perfect fits experience that counts now: 'we have visited Paris many times with friends'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. He was “curious” to know his result.
questions.explanation: 'Curious' means eager to know: 'inquisitive'. 'Indifferent', not caring, is nearly its opposite.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. I think that perhaps the sky is a (1) ________ sea of fresh water and we, (2) _________ walking under it, walk on top of it; perhaps we see everything (3) __________ down and the earth is a (4) ________ of sky, so that when we die, we fall and (5) _______ into the sky.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The writer imagines the sky as a 'huge' sea of fresh water, as vast as the sky itself.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. I think that perhaps the sky is a (1) ________ sea of fresh water and we, (2) _________ walking under it, walk on top of it; perhaps we see everything (3) __________ down and the earth is a (4) ________ of sky, so that when we die, we fall and (5) _______ into the sky.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Instead of' walking under it, we walk on top of it: the writer imagines the world turned over.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. I think that perhaps the sky is a (1) ________ sea of fresh water and we, (2) _________ walking under it, walk on top of it; perhaps we see everything (3) __________ down and the earth is a (4) ________ of sky, so that when we die, we fall and (5) _______ into the sky.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Upside down' means with the top at the bottom: perhaps we see everything inverted.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. I think that perhaps the sky is a (1) ________ sea of fresh water and we, (2) _________ walking under it, walk on top of it; perhaps we see everything (3) __________ down and the earth is a (4) ________ of sky, so that when we die, we fall and (5) _______ into the sky.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'A kind of sky' means a sort of sky: the earth would be a sky of its own.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. I think that perhaps the sky is a (1) ________ sea of fresh water and we, (2) _________ walking under it, walk on top of it; perhaps we see everything (3) __________ down and the earth is a (4) ________ of sky, so that when we die, we fall and (5) _______ into the sky.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: If the sky is a sea, then when we die we fall and 'sink' into it, as things sink in water.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? DCAB, ? , NMKL, SRPQ, XWUV
questions.explanation: The first letters move +5 (D, I, N, S, X), and each cluster is that letter followed by the letters 1, 3 and 2 places before it: D C A B, N M K L. So the missing cluster is I H F G: IHFG.

questions.text: Which of the following interchanges of signs would make the given equation correct? 192 ÷ 16 + 8 × 25 − 95 = 26
Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 demolish 2 demon 3 destroy 4 decor 5 detour
questions.explanation: Decor (dec-) comes first, then demolish and demon ('demol-' before 'demon'), destroy (des-) and detour (det-): 4, 1, 2, 3, 5.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (13, 390, 6); (9, 180, 4)
questions.explanation: The middle number is five times the product of the other two: 13 × 6 × 5 = 390 and 9 × 4 × 5 = 180. Likewise 11 × 7 × 5 = 385; the other sets would need 225, 160 and 540.

questions.text: A @ B means ‘A is the spouse of B’. A & B means ‘A is the father of B’. A # B means ‘A is the mother of B’. A % B means ‘A is the sister of B’. If H @ V & K % Q # F, then how is H related to F?
questions.explanation: Q # F makes Q F's mother, and K is Q's sister. V & K makes V the father of K, and so of Q, and H, V's spouse, is their mother. So H is F's mother's mother: maternal grandmother.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 1, 5, 16, 41, 87, 161, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 4, 11, 25, 46, 74, which grow by 7, 14, 21, 28. The next difference is 74 + 35 = 109: 161 + 109 = 270.

questions.text: Six people M, N, O, P, Q and R are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre. Q is the immediate neighbour of M and R. N is sitting third to the left of Q. O is the immediate neighbour of R and N. R is sitting second to the left of N. Who is sitting between M and N when considered from the right of N?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, going left is going clockwise. N, third to the left of Q, is opposite Q; R, second to the left of N, is next to Q; O sits between R and N; and M, Q's other neighbour, leaves P between M and N. Clockwise the order is Q, M, P, N, O, R, so counting to the right of N, P sits between N and M.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 132, 154, 176, ?, 220
questions.explanation: Each term is 22 more than the one before (11 × 12, 11 × 14 and so on): 176 + 22 = 198, and 198 + 22 = 220.

questions.text: In a certain code language, If CAB is coded as 75 and DIP is coded as 52, how will FLY be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter takes its place counted from Z (A = 26, B = 25 and so on) and the values are added: CAB = 24 + 26 + 25 = 75 and DIP = 23 + 18 + 11 = 52. So FLY = 21 + 15 + 2 = 38.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. ONCE: LLVS :: LIST: OQFD :: PACK: ?
questions.explanation: Each letter becomes its opposite letter (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on) and then moves back 0, 1, 2 and 3 places: ONCE → LMXV → LLVS and LIST → ORHG → OQFD. So PACK → KZXP → KYVM.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 24 + 36 × 32 – 8 ÷ 20 = 148
Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. RBWP, TWYR, VRAT, ?, ZHEX
questions.explanation: The first, third and fourth letters each move +2 (R, T, V, X, Z; W, Y, A, C, E; P, R, T, V, X) and the second moves −5 (B, W, R, M, H), wrapping round after A. The missing cluster is XMCV.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All books are hard. Some hard are stone. Some stone are cars. Conclusions: I. Some hard are books. II. All hard are stone. III. Some cars are stone.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.
Both conclusions II and III follow.
questions.explanation: All books are hard, so some hard things are books (I); some stone are cars, so some cars are stone (III). That some hard things are stone does not make all of them stone, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. A sits to the immediate left of C. E sits third to the right of D. D is an immediate neighbour of C. B is an immediate neighbour of both E and F. Who is the immediate neighbour of C and E?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, left is clockwise. A is to C's immediate left, so D, C's other neighbour, is on its right. E, third to the right of D, is then next to A, and B, a neighbour of both E and F, takes the seat beyond E, with F between B and D. Going round: C, A, E, B, F, D, so A sits between C and E.

questions.text: In a code language, 'PAPER' is written as ‘QCSIW’ and ‘BOARD’ is written as ’CQDVI’, how will 'PENCIL' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, +2, +3, +4, +5 in turn: PAPER → QCSIW and BOARD → CQDVI. So PENCIL → Q G Q G N R (L + 6 = R): QGQGNR.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/consonants/vowels in the word). Bouquet : Flower :: Chain : __________
questions.explanation: A bouquet is made up of flowers, as a chain is made up of links.

questions.text: Under which scheme, 5 Crore LPG (Liquified Petroleum Gas) connections were provided to Below Poverty Line (BPL) families?
questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, launched on 1 May 2016, set out to give 5 crore deposit-free LPG connections, in the names of the women of the households, to BPL families over three years (2016-17 to 2018-19).

questions.text: The winter rain in Tamil Nadu is due to the _____.
questions.explanation: In winter the north-east trade winds blow from land to sea over most of India, so the season is dry; on the Tamil Nadu coast they arrive from the Bay of Bengal carrying moisture, and bring rain.

questions.text: Mopin is the cultural festival of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Mopin is the main agricultural festival of the Galo people of Arunachal Pradesh, held in April for a good harvest and prosperity.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India empowers the President of India to pardon in case of punishment or sentence?
questions.explanation: Article 72 gives the President the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment, or to suspend, remit or commute a sentence. Article 161 gives a Governor a similar power.

questions.text: Kelucharan Mohapatra won recognition in which dance form?
questions.explanation: Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra of Odisha was the leading guru of Odissi and did much to revive the dance in the twentieth century.

questions.text: _______ is an asset pledged by a borrower, to a lender as security for a loan.
questions.explanation: Collateral is an asset a borrower pledges to a lender as security; if the loan is not repaid, the lender may take it.

questions.text: Who has been appointed as the Deputy Election Commissioner of India in October 2022?
questions.explanation: Ajay Bhadoo, a Gujarat-cadre IAS officer, was appointed Deputy Election Commissioner in early October 2022. Rajiv Kumar was then the Chief Election Commissioner, a post Sunil Arora and O P Rawat had held before him.

questions.text: Who was India’s flag-bearer for the closing ceremony of the 18th Asian Games 2018?
questions.explanation: Rani Rampal, captain of the women's hockey team that won silver, carried India's flag at the closing ceremony of the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta; Neeraj Chopra carried it at the opening.

questions.text: The term towards faster and more inclusive growth was coined in which Five year plan?
questions.explanation: 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth' was the title and theme of the Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007-12).

questions.text: Hockey India League (HIL) started in which of the following year?
questions.explanation: The Hockey India League's first season was played from 14 January to 10 February 2013; Ranchi Rhinos won it.

questions.text: Identify the correct statement about nuclear fission.
options: The nucleus of a heavy atom, when bombarded with low-energy neutrons, can be split apart into lighter nuclei.
Nuclear fission is the coming together of high-energy electrons and low-energy neutrons.
The nucleus of a low-energy atom, when bombarded with high-energy neutrons, can be split apart into lighter nuclei.
The nucleus of a low-energy atom, when bombarded with high-energy neutrons, can be split apart into heavier nuclei.
questions.explanation: In nuclear fission a heavy nucleus, such as that of uranium-235, absorbs a slow (low-energy) neutron and splits into two lighter nuclei, releasing energy and more neutrons.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When did the infamous Jallianwala Bagh incident take place?
questions.explanation: On 13 April 1919, Baisakhi day, troops under Reginald Dyer fired on an unarmed crowd gathered in the Jallianwala Bagh at Amritsar.

questions.text: Identify the Mauryan king who gave up conquest after winning a war.
questions.explanation: Moved by the slaughter of his war in Kalinga, Ashoka gave up conquest by war and turned to spreading dhamma.

questions.text: India has second largest ______ network in the world, aggregating to about 62.16 lakh km (2020–21).
questions.explanation: India's road network is the world's second largest, after that of the United States.

questions.text: According to the 2011 census, what is the population density (per square km) of India?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 put India's population density at 382 persons per square km, up from 325 in 2001.

questions.text: As of November 2022, who was the Chief Minister of Gujarat before elections held in 2022?
questions.explanation: Bhupendra Patel became Chief Minister of Gujarat in September 2021, succeeding Vijay Rupani, and held the office in November 2022; after the BJP won the December 2022 election he was sworn in again.

questions.text: Under which Five Year Plan in India, the implementation of the Family Planning Programme was amongst the major targets of the Plan?
questions.explanation: India's family planning programme began in 1952, in the First Plan, but the Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-74) made it one of its major targets, giving it the highest priority as a time-bound programme with targets for bringing down the birth rate.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a source of protein?
questions.explanation: Lemon is valued for its vitamin C and has little protein; fish, meat and milk are good sources of protein.

questions.text: The Kathakali dance form originated in which part of India?
questions.explanation: Kathakali, the dance-drama known for its elaborate make-up and costumes, comes from Kerala in the south.

questions.text: On which date was Andhra Pradesh formed?
questions.explanation: Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 November 1956 under the States Reorganisation Act, when the Telugu-speaking areas of Hyderabad State were joined to Andhra State, which had been carved out of Madras State on 1 October 1953.

questions.text: A and B together can do a piece of work in 21 days. B and C together can do it in 24 days. A and C together can do it in 33 days. In how many days approximately will A, B and C finish it together?
questions.explanation: Adding the three pairs, 2(A + B + C) = 1/21 + 1/24 + 1/33 = (88 + 77 + 56)/1848 = 221/1848 of the work a day. So A, B and C together do 221/3696 a day and take 3696/221 ≈ 16.7, about 17 days.

questions.text: A and B together can do a piece of work in 20 days, while B alone can finish it in 25 days. How many days will A take to complete the same work alone?
questions.explanation: A alone does 1/20 − 1/25 = (5 − 4)/100 = 1/100 of the work a day, so A takes 100 days.

questions.text: Priya allows 5 percent discount on the marked price of her goods and still earns a profit of 18 percent. What is the cost price of an item, if its marked price is Rs. 944?
questions.explanation: The selling price is 95% of ₹944 = ₹896.80, which is 118% of the cost: 896.80 ÷ 1.18 = ₹760.

questions.text: Find the fourth proportional of 3 hours 20 minutes, 1 hour 50 minutes, and 6 hours 20 minutes.
questions.explanation: In minutes the terms are 200, 110 and 380, so the fourth proportional is 110 × 380/200 = 209 minutes = 3 hours 29 minutes.

questions.text: In a circular race of 5000 m, starting from the same point, the speeds of two contestants A and B are 36 km/h and 54 km/h, respectively. The difference between the time taken (in seconds) to meet for the first time when they are running in the opposite directions and when they are running in the same direction?
questions.explanation: The speeds are 10 m/s and 15 m/s. Running in opposite directions they first meet after 5000/(10 + 15) = 200 s, and in the same direction after 5000/(15 − 10) = 1000 s. The difference is 800 s.

questions.text: A ream of 500 pages is bought for ₹280, and packets of 25 pages are made from it. Each packet is sold for ₹18. Find the percentage profit or loss. (Rounded off up to one decimal place).
questions.explanation: The ream makes 500/25 = 20 packets, sold for 20 × ₹18 = ₹360. The profit is ₹80 on ₹280: 80/280 × 100 = 28.6%.

questions.text: The diameter of a hemisphere is 6 cm. The ratio of the magnitudes of its curved surface area to the total surface area is:
questions.explanation: The curved surface area is 2πr² and the total surface area, with the flat circle, 3πr², so the ratio is 2 : 3 whatever the radius.

questions.text: Find the sum of the digits of the greatest number that can exactly divide 288 and 432.
questions.explanation: 288 = 2⁵ × 3² and 432 = 2⁴ × 3³, so their HCF is 2⁴ × 3² = 144, whose digits add up to 1 + 4 + 4 = 9.

questions.text: Three number are in the ratio of 4 : 5 : 6, and their LCM is 180. Their HCF is:
questions.explanation: The numbers are 4x, 5x and 6x, whose LCM is 60x = 180, so x = 3. As 4, 5 and 6 have no common factor, the HCF is x = 3.

questions.text: If ratio of X to Y is 3 : 4, then determine the relation between X and Y.
options: Both X is 75 percent of Y and Y is 133.33 percent of X
questions.explanation: X = 3/4 of Y = 75% of Y, and Y = 4/3 of X = 133.33% of X.

questions.text: A shopkeeper offers three successive discounts of 15%, 30% and 4% on an article. If the article is marked at ₹1,950, what is its selling price (in ₹, rounded off to the nearest tens)?

The average of sales of an electronics shop in the years 2001, 2002, 2003 and 2004 is 1850, and that for the years 2002, 2003, 2004 and 2005 is 2125. If the sales in 2005 are1200, then find the sales in 2001?
questions.explanation: The 2001-04 total is 4 × 1850 = 7400 and the 2002-05 total 4 × 2125 = 8500. They share 2002-04, so sales in 2005 exceed sales in 2001 by 1100, and sales in 2001 = 1200 − 1100 = 100.

questions.text: The population of a village increases by 12½ % in the first year and decrease by 8% in the second year. If the present population of village is 3200, then what will be the population of the village after 2 years?
questions.explanation: 3200 × 1.125 = 3600 after the first year, and 3600 × 0.92 = 3312 after the second.

questions.text: Determine the fourth proportional to 11.6 m, 9.2 m, 32.8 m. (Consider up to two decimals)
questions.explanation: The fourth proportional is 9.2 × 32.8/11.6 = 301.76/11.6 = 26.01 m.

questions.text: Afzal's monthly income is Rs.35,000. He spends 20% of his monthly income on food, 30% on clothes, and 15% on rent. How much money does Afzal save monthly?
A woman gains 30 percent by selling an article for a certain price. If she sells it at double price, then the profit made is :
questions.explanation: Take the cost as 100: the selling price is 130, and double that is 260, a profit of 160 on 100, or 160%.

questions.text: The average of 11 numbers is 7.5. What should be the 12th number added to them to make the average 8.5?
questions.explanation: The 11 numbers add up to 11 × 7.5 = 82.5, and 12 numbers averaging 8.5 add up to 102, so the 12th is 102 − 82.5 = 19.5.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Reckon
questions.explanation: To 'reckon' is to think or consider: 'I reckon he is right.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. He has given us no reason to “be prestigious” of him.
questions.explanation: To 'be suspicious of' someone is to distrust them, which fits 'no reason to'. 'Prestigious' means having high status and makes no sense here.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. Tomorrow is a/ holiday for all /except me as/ I will writing my exam.
questions.explanation: After 'will' the continuous form needs 'be': 'I will be writing my exam' (or simply 'I will write my exam').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He visited his mother _________ after she was discharged from the hospital.
questions.explanation: 'Now and then' means from time to time: he visited his mother occasionally after she left hospital. 'By and by' means before long, and 'more or less' almost.

questions.text: Select the correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. “Let I” clear the doubts, if any.
questions.explanation: 'Let' is followed by an object pronoun: 'Let me clear the doubts, if any.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Noble
questions.explanation: A 'noble' person has high principles and a bearing that commands respect, so 'dignified' is closest. 'Humble' means modest.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'reference'.

questions.text: Select the correct word for the blanks in the given sentence. Health is a state of __________ being, and a _________ is used to draw water from the ground.
questions.explanation: 'Well' fits both blanks: 'well-being' is a state of good health and happiness, and a well is a hole dug to draw water from the ground. 'Tubewell' fits only the second blank.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Erudite
questions.explanation: 'Erudite' means having or showing great learning; its opposite is 'ignorant'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlying word in the given sentence and complete the sentence. He was __________ by his brother’s attitude, but his mother’s words “calmed” him.
questions.explanation: The blank needs the opposite of the underlined 'calmed': he was 'agitated' (upset) by his brother's attitude until his mother's words calmed him. 'Solaced' means comforted, close to 'calmed'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Explore all avenues
options: Try out every possibility to get a result
questions.explanation: To 'explore all avenues' is to try every possible way of getting a result.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Spinning one’s wheels
options: To do a lot of work for achieving something
To make a lot of effort without achieving anything
To talk about oneself for achieving something
questions.explanation: To be 'spinning one's wheels' is to put in a lot of effort without making any progress, like a car whose wheels spin without moving it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. He planned a weeklong _________ down the Nile.
questions.explanation: A 'cruise' is a voyage for pleasure. 'Crews' (the people who work a ship) sounds the same, and 'cruse' is an old word for a small jar.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Obvious
questions.explanation: 'Obvious' means easy to see or understand; its opposite is 'cryptic', obscure or puzzling. 'Plain' and 'clear' are synonyms.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Amla tree is (1) ________ to be thousands of years old. It is called aamaleki and dhaatri in Sanskrit. Its botanical name is Emblica Officinalis. The amla tree is a medium (2) _________ tree with citrus fruits. It is found almost everywhere in India (3) ________ for some very high mountainous regions. It is found (4) ________ in Madhya Pradesh. The leaves are very small and have a close (5) ________ to those of Gulmohar. The amla tree has slender branches which grow upwards and surround the trees on all sides.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: 'Is considered to be' means is believed to be: the amla tree is believed to be thousands of years old.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Amla tree is (1) ________ to be thousands of years old. It is called aamaleki and dhaatri in Sanskrit. Its botanical name is Emblica Officinalis. The amla tree is a medium (2) _________ tree with citrus fruits. It is found almost everywhere in India (3) ________ for some very high mountainous regions. It is found (4) ________ in Madhya Pradesh. The leaves are very small and have a close (5) ________ to those of Gulmohar. The amla tree has slender branches which grow upwards and surround the trees on all sides.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: A 'medium-sized' tree is one of middle size; the other options make no sense with 'medium'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Amla tree is (1) ________ to be thousands of years old. It is called aamaleki and dhaatri in Sanskrit. Its botanical name is Emblica Officinalis. The amla tree is a medium (2) _________ tree with citrus fruits. It is found almost everywhere in India (3) ________ for some very high mountainous regions. It is found (4) ________ in Madhya Pradesh. The leaves are very small and have a close (5) ________ to those of Gulmohar. The amla tree has slender branches which grow upwards and surround the trees on all sides.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: 'Except for' brings in the exception: the tree grows almost everywhere in India apart from some very high mountain regions.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Amla tree is (1) ________ to be thousands of years old. It is called aamaleki and dhaatri in Sanskrit. Its botanical name is Emblica Officinalis. The amla tree is a medium (2) _________ tree with citrus fruits. It is found almost everywhere in India (3) ________ for some very high mountainous regions. It is found (4) ________ in Madhya Pradesh. The leaves are very small and have a close (5) ________ to those of Gulmohar. The amla tree has slender branches which grow upwards and surround the trees on all sides.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: 'Found abundantly' is the usual way of saying a plant grows in large numbers somewhere: the tree is plentiful in Madhya Pradesh. 'Lavishly' means generously or extravagantly, 'profusely' is used mostly of what pours out freely (bleeding, sweating, apologising), and 'wholly' means completely.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Amla tree is (1) ________ to be thousands of years old. It is called aamaleki and dhaatri in Sanskrit. Its botanical name is Emblica Officinalis. The amla tree is a medium (2) _________ tree with citrus fruits. It is found almost everywhere in India (3) ________ for some very high mountainous regions. It is found (4) ________ in Madhya Pradesh. The leaves are very small and have a close (5) ________ to those of Gulmohar. The amla tree has slender branches which grow upwards and surround the trees on all sides.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: To 'have a close resemblance to' something is to look much like it: amla leaves look much like those of the gulmohar.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 19 * 5 * 5 * 220 * 2 * 10

In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: Some raisins are grapes. All grapes are apples. All raisins are fruits. Conclusions: I. Some fruits are apples. II. Some apples are raisins.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: The raisins that are grapes are also apples, and every raisin is a fruit, so some fruits are apples (I) and some apples are raisins (II): both follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, BLUSH is written as ‘EPXWK’, and SPLASH is written as ‘VTOEVL’. How will ‘SPRITE’ be written in the same code language?
questions.explanation: The letters move 3 and 4 places forward in turn: BLUSH → EPXWK and SPLASH → VTOEVL. So SPRITE → V T U M W I: VTUMWI.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 123, 88, 127, 94, 131, 100, ?, 106, 139
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 123, 127, 131, ?, 139 rise by 4 and 88, 94, 100, 106 by 6. The missing term is 131 + 4 = 135.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘You Are Kind’ is written as ‘hat me ga’. ‘She Is Smart’ is written as ‘fe ta nou’. ‘She Is Kind’ is written as ‘fe ta ga’. How is the word ‘Kind’ written in the same code language?
questions.explanation: 'Kind' is in the first and third messages, and 'ga' is the only code common to both.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Baker : Bread :: cobbler : ________
questions.explanation: A baker makes bread, and a cobbler makes and mends shoes.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed) (261, 54, 25); (270, 45, 15)
questions.explanation: The first number is 9 times the difference of the other two: (54 − 25) × 9 = 261 and (45 − 15) × 9 = 270. Likewise (82 − 50) × 9 = 288.

questions.text: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Ali is sitting third to the right of Naeem. Syed is sitting second to the left of Ali. Sara is the immediate neighbour of Ali and Syed. Shenaz is second to the right of Ali. David is sitting third to the right of Syed. Who is sitting between Sara and David?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, each student's left is the next seat clockwise. Clockwise from Ali the order is Ali, Sara, Syed, Naeem, Shenaz, David, so Ali sits between Sara and David.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 108 ÷ 27 × 54 – 40 + 34 = 48
questions.explanation: After interchanging ÷ and ×: 108 × 27 ÷ 54 − 40 + 34 = 54 − 40 + 34 = 48.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. RSXE, VNBI, ZIFM, ? , HYNU
questions.explanation: The first, third and fourth letters move 4 forward (R, V, Z, D, H; X, B, F, J, N; E, I, M, Q, U) and the second 5 back (S, N, I, D, Y): DDJQ.

questions.text: Six students A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. D is to the immediate right of E and E is to the immediate right of F. A is the immediate neighbour of D and C. Who among the following is sitting second to the right of B?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, each student's right is the next seat anticlockwise. Clockwise the order is F, B, C, A, D, E (D on E's right, E on F's right, A between D and C), so second to the right of B is E.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replaces the question mark (?) in the given series? 7, 36, 66, ?, 129, 162
‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the son of B’; ‘A & B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A # B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’; Which of the following options means 'R is the sister of P'?
questions.explanation: P @ Q & R # S: P is Q's son, Q is R's mother and R is S's daughter. P and R are both Q's children and R is female, so R is P's sister.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? CMHO, DPMV, ?, FVWJ, GYBQ
questions.explanation: The first letters move 1 forward (C, D, E, F, G), the second 3 (M, P, S, V, Y), the third 5 (H, M, R, W, B) and the fourth 7 (O, V, C, J, Q): ESRC.

questions.text: Which of the following options represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1. Breeze 2. Breech 3. Breather 4. Breed 5. Breathe
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Breathe (5), Breather (3), Breech (2), Breed (4), Breeze (1). 'Breathe' comes before the longer 'Breather', 'Breat' before 'Bree', and 'Breec' before 'Breed' before 'Breez'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. BEAM : YVZN :: WORD : DLIW :: PLAN : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter becomes its opposite (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on): BEAM → YVZN and WORD → DLIW. So PLAN → KOZM.

questions.text: Who won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in Kuchipudi in 2018?
questions.explanation: Pasumarthy Ramalinga Sastry received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Kuchipudi for 2018, announced in July 2019. Radha Sridhar received the 2018 award for Bharatanatyam.

questions.text: Which political leader won the bypoll election from Jubarajnagar constituency in Tripura, in June 2022?
questions.explanation: Malina Debnath of the BJP won the Jubarajnagar by-election in June 2022, held after the death of the CPI(M) MLA Ramendra Chandra Debnath.

questions.text: __________scheme aims to provide measures for Comprehensive Rehabilitation for Welfare of Transgender Persons.
options: Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Education
Scheme for Medium Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise
Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise
Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Entity
questions.explanation: SMILE (Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise), a scheme of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment launched in February 2022, includes a sub-scheme for the comprehensive rehabilitation of transgender persons.

questions.text: Excessive use of synthetic fertilizers leads to:
questions.explanation: Overuse of synthetic fertilisers degrades the soil, upsetting its chemical balance and harming the micro-organisms that keep it fertile.

questions.text: In ancient times the area to the south of the_____ river was known as Magadha.
questions.explanation: Magadha, in present-day south Bihar, lay south of the Ganga; its capitals were Rajagriha and later Pataliputra.

questions.text: In the game of football, the distance between the goalposts is _________ whereas the distance from the lower edge of the crossbar to the ground is _________.
questions.explanation: Under the Laws of the Game the goalposts are 7.32 m (8 yards) apart, and the lower edge of the crossbar is 2.44 m (8 feet) above the ground.

questions.text: How many Schedules are there in the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Constitution has 12 Schedules. It began with 8; the Ninth was added in 1951, the Tenth in 1985, and the Eleventh and Twelfth by the 73rd and 74th Amendments in 1992.

questions.text: Three of the following four are examples of mammalia, and therefore form a group. Which is the one that does not belong to that group?
questions.explanation: The penguin is a flightless bird. The platypus (an egg-laying mammal), the kangaroo (a marsupial) and the flying fox (a fruit bat) are mammals.

questions.text: In the post-independence period, who won the 1st individual Olympic Medal for India in 1952?
questions.explanation: Khashaba Dadasaheb Jadhav won a bronze medal in freestyle wrestling at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics, independent India's first individual Olympic medal.

questions.text: The Bhil tribe living in the ________ controlled the mountain passes between the north and the Deccan. I. Western Ghats II. Eastern Ghats
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the Western Ghats only. The Bhils live across western and central India, including the northern Western Ghats around Khandesh and the Dangs; they are not a people of the Eastern Ghats.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India states that the Attorney General for India will be appointed by the President?
questions.explanation: Article 76 provides for an Attorney General for India, appointed by the President. Article 123 deals with ordinances, Article 12 defines 'the State' and Article 115 covers supplementary grants.

questions.text: The Eighth Five Year Plan of India got delayed due to ___________.
questions.explanation: The Eighth Plan was due to start in 1990, but the fast-changing political situation at the Centre held it up; 1990-91 and 1991-92 were treated as annual plans, and the plan ran from 1992 to 1997.

questions.text: What is the number of electrons found in the outermost shell of the halogens?
questions.explanation: The halogens (group 17: fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine) have seven electrons in their outermost shell, one short of a stable octet.

questions.text: The Gochi festival is predominantly celebrated in which of the following states of India?
questions.explanation: Gochi (Gotsi), held in February in the Lahaul valley of Himachal Pradesh, celebrates the birth of a son in the past year.

questions.text: Who is the next High Commissioner of India to the United Kingdom as announced in August 2022?
questions.explanation: On 23 August 2022 the Ministry of External Affairs named Vikram Doraiswami, then High Commissioner to Bangladesh, as the next High Commissioner to the United Kingdom, succeeding Gaitri Issar Kumar.

questions.text: The light of the sun takes about ______ minutes to reach the earth.
questions.explanation: Light from the sun, about 150 million km away, reaches the earth in about 8 minutes 20 seconds.

questions.text: Which among the following dance forms is not associated with Chhattisgarh?
questions.explanation: Bhagoria is a festival and dance of the Bhils of western Madhya Pradesh. Panthi, Pandwani and Saila belong to Chhattisgarh.

questions.text: The selling price of 28 items is equal to the cost price of 16 items. What is the profit or loss percent? (correct to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanation: The SP of 28 items equals the CP of 16, so on 28 items the loss is the CP of 12: 12/28 × 100 = 42.86% loss.

questions.text: Two numbers are in the ratio of 5 : 9, and their LCM is 405. Find the numbers.
questions.explanation: The numbers are 5k and 9k with LCM 45k = 405, so k = 9: 45 and 81.

questions.text: A person went to a place at a speed of 20 km/h and came back at a speed of 30 km/h. During this journey, if the time taken is 2 hours, determine the distance of that place.
The average weight of 45 students of a school is 55 kg. If the weight of the teacher is included, the average weight rises by 300 grams. Find the weight of the teacher.
questions.explanation: The new average is 55.3 kg, so the teacher weighs 55 + 46 × 0.3 = 55 + 13.8 = 68.8 kg.

questions.text: Raj takes twice as much time as Sujay and thrice as much time as Ronak to finish a piece of work. If Sujay can do the work alone in 6 days, then in how many days all three together can finish the same work.
questions.explanation: Sujay takes 6 days, so Raj takes 12 and Ronak 4. Together they do 1/6 + 1/12 + 1/4 = (2 + 1 + 3)/12 = 1/2 of the work a day: 2 days.

questions.text: Allowing 15 percent and 6 percent successive discount, the selling price of an article becomes Rs. 9588, then the marked price is:
A can complete 2/5th part of the work in 12 days and B can complete 7/8th part of the same work in 21 days. Find the number of days in which A and B together can complete the work.
questions.explanation: A alone takes 12 ÷ 2/5 = 30 days and B 21 ÷ 7/8 = 24 days. Together they do 1/30 + 1/24 = (4 + 5)/120 = 3/40 of the work a day: 40/3 days.

questions.text: If 15 percent of 40 percent of a number is 30, then what is the number?
What is the greatest possible length of scale to measure exactly, the following? 15 feet, 12 feet 9 inches, 16 feet 3 inches, and 23 feet 6 inches
questions.explanation: In inches the lengths are 180, 153, 195 and 282. Their HCF is 3 (180 = 2² × 3² × 5, 153 = 3² × 17, 195 = 3 × 5 × 13, 282 = 2 × 3 × 47), so the longest scale is 3 inches.

questions.text: Veer buys 200 guavas for Rs.1,800. Some of these guavas are rotten and are thrown away. He sells the remaining guavas at Rs.14 each and makes a profit of Rs.230. The percentage of guavas thrown away is:
questions.explanation: He receives 1,800 + 230 = Rs. 2,030, so he sells 2,030 ÷ 14 = 145 guavas and throws away 55: 55/200 × 100 = 27.5%.

questions.text: The diameter of the base of a right circular cylinder is 56 cm, and its height is 18 cm. The area of the curved surface of the cylinder is: (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: The radius is 28 cm: curved surface = 2πrh = 2 × 22/7 × 28 × 18 = 3168 sq cm.

questions.text: Successive discounts of 10%,15% and 20% amount to a single discount of:
questions.explanation: A price of 100 becomes 100 × 0.9 × 0.85 × 0.8 = 61.2, so the single discount is 38.8%.

questions.text: If a ∶ b = 5 ∶ 1, then what is the value of 3a + 4b ∶ 3a - 4b?
In what ratio should lentils costing Rs.77.50/kg be mixed with lentils costing Rs.83.50/kg to get the average price of Rs.80/kg of the resulting mixture?
questions.explanation: By alligation, cheaper : dearer = (83.50 − 80) : (80 − 77.50) = 3.5 : 2.5 = 7 : 5.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. I studied a book on the “study of stars”.
questions.explanation: Astronomy is the study of stars and other heavenly bodies. Geology studies the earth's rocks and meteorology the weather.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence to make it a meaningful sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. The COVID-19 pandemic “pose innumerable challenges to our education system, and engineering education was no exception”.
options: posed innumerable challenges to our education system, and engineering education was no exception.
have been posing innumerable challenges to our education system, and engineering education is not any exception.
posed innumerable challenges to our education system, and engineering education is not a exception.
questions.explanation: The second clause is in the past ('was no exception'), so the verb must be past too: 'posed innumerable challenges'. The last option has 'a exception' and changes the tense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence. He distracted him while his partner “burgled” his shop.
questions.explanation: To 'burgle' a place is to break in and steal from it, so 'looted' is the nearest.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence to make it a meaningful sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. A new kind of pollution that “is acquiring serious dimensions was noise pollution”.
options: have been acquiring serious dimensions is noise pollution.
is acquiring serious dimensions is noise pollution.
have acquiring serious dimensions is noise pollution.
questions.explanation: The sentence is in the present ('is acquiring'), so the main verb should be 'is', not 'was': 'A new kind of pollution that is acquiring serious dimensions is noise pollution.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given below to fill in the blank in the following sentence. Toying; My cat, Mili loves ______ with the toy mouse.
questions.explanation: To 'toy' with something is to play with it idly: 'Mili loves playing with the toy mouse.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Risk life and limb
options: In danger of death or serious injury
questions.explanation: To 'risk life and limb' is to do something that puts one in danger of death or serious injury.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Vanquish
questions.explanation: To 'vanquish' is to defeat thoroughly; to 'surrender' is to give in to an opponent, the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Mean
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'greedy': 'mean' can describe someone unwilling to give or share, which is close to 'greedy', though its nearer synonyms are 'stingy' and 'miserly'. 'Mode' is a different kind of average, and 'unconscious' and 'wise' are unrelated.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in the bracket to fill in the blank. I can’t forget the (convivial)___________ atmosphere at the college reunion.
questions.explanation: 'Convivial' means friendly and lively; 'antisocial' is its opposite. 'Affable', 'hospitable' and 'lively' are close to it.

questions.text: Identify the correctly spelt sentence.
options: The collector is the district magistrate in admiinistration.
The collector is the district magistrate in administration.
The collector is the district magistrate in adminestration.
The collector is the district magistrate in addministration.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'administration'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Circamference' is misspelt: the word is 'circumference'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in the brackets to fill in the blank. We live on the ________ (centre) of the city.
questions.explanation: The 'outskirts' are the outer parts of a city, the opposite of its centre. 'Interior', 'middle' and 'downtown' are close to 'centre'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The immense talent / we having at our disposal is / impressive to say the least.
options: we having at our disposal is
questions.explanation: 'Having' cannot be the verb of the clause: it should be 'we have at our disposal'.

questions.text: Select the correct pair of words for the blanks in the given sentence. ________ are the prime resource of a country and a tea is served in a _________.
questions.explanation: 'Cattle' (cows and oxen) are a prime resource, and a 'kettle' is a pot for boiling water or tea; the two words sound alike.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Accidents resulting from (1)______ driving have become a daily affair. The speed maniacs responsible for most of them escape (2)______ after knocking down a person, they speed away before anyone can take down the number of their vehicle. It is often young people from affluent families, not even eligible for a driving licence, who (3)______ in reckless driving. The penalties imposed for reckless driving are much too (4)______ to be effective. The penalty for reckless driving should be raised and the general public should be made (5)______ of the consequences of reckless driving.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 1.
questions.explanation: Accidents come from 'reckless' driving, the phrase the passage repeats later.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Accidents resulting from (1)______ driving have become a daily affair. The speed maniacs responsible for most of them escape (2)______ after knocking down a person, they speed away before anyone can take down the number of their vehicle. It is often young people from affluent families, not even eligible for a driving licence, who (3)______ in reckless driving. The penalties imposed for reckless driving are much too (4)______ to be effective. The penalty for reckless driving should be raised and the general public should be made (5)______ of the consequences of reckless driving.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 2.
questions.explanation: Drivers who speed away before their number is taken escape 'punishment'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Accidents resulting from (1)______ driving have become a daily affair. The speed maniacs responsible for most of them escape (2)______ after knocking down a person, they speed away before anyone can take down the number of their vehicle. It is often young people from affluent families, not even eligible for a driving licence, who (3)______ in reckless driving. The penalties imposed for reckless driving are much too (4)______ to be effective. The penalty for reckless driving should be raised and the general public should be made (5)______ of the consequences of reckless driving.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 3.
questions.explanation: To 'indulge in' something is to give way to it: young people indulge in reckless driving.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 4.
questions.explanation: The penalties are too 'lenient', that is too mild, to be effective, which is why the next sentence says they should be raised.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.
