The penalty for reckless driving should be raised and the general public should be made (5)______ of the consequences of reckless driving.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 5.
questions.explanation: The public should be made 'aware of' the consequences, that is informed of them; 'aware' takes 'of'.

questions.text: Six students Jason, Tushar, Anand, Stacey, Steven and Max are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Jason is sitting third to the right of Tushar. Anand is sitting second to the left of Jason. Steven is an immediate neighbour of Anand and Jason. Max is sitting to the immediate right of Jason. Stacey is to the immediate left of Tushar. Who is sitting between Max and Steven?
questions.explanation: With six seats, Jason (third to Tushar's right) sits opposite Tushar. Facing the centre a person's left is clockwise, so clockwise from Tushar the order is Tushar, Stacey, Max, Jason, Steven, Anand: Jason sits between Max and Steven.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question marks (?) in the given series? 31, 33, 36, 41, 48, ? , ?
questions.explanation: The differences are the prime numbers 2, 3, 5, 7, so the next two are 11 and 13: 48 + 11 = 59 and 59 + 13 = 72.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FLY’ is coded as 43 and ‘HAT’ is coded as 29. How will ‘BEACH’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word's code is the sum of its letters' places in the alphabet: FLY = 6 + 12 + 25 = 43 and HAT = 8 + 1 + 20 = 29. So BEACH = 2 + 5 + 1 + 3 + 8 = 19.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H are sitting around a square table facing the centre of the table. Some of them are sitting at the corners while some are sitting at the exact centre of the sides. E sits third to the left of G. E sits at one of the corners. B sits second to the right of F. F does not sit at any of the corners. F is not an immediate neighbour of E. H is an immediate neighbour of A. H does not sit in any of the middles of the sides. Only three people sit between H and C from either sides. If all the persons are made to sit in alphabetical order in a clockwise direction starting from A, then how many places does B shift in either direction with respect to its previous position?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre a person's left is clockwise. G sits third to E's right in a side-middle, F takes the other middle seat not next to E, B is second to F's right, H sits at the corner opposite C with A beside it: clockwise, E, B, C, F, D, G, H, A. Seated alphabetically clockwise from A's seat, B takes the next seat, E's old one, so it moves 1 place.

questions.text: ‘Near’ is related to ‘Close’ in the same way as ‘Distant’ is related to ‘________’. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word)
questions.explanation: 'Near' and 'close' mean the same, and so do 'distant' and 'away' (far off).

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 10, 0, 20, 10, 30, 20, 40, 30, ?
questions.explanation: Two series alternate, each rising by 10: 10, 20, 30, 40 and 0, 10, 20, 30. The next term belongs to the first: 50.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All chocolates are biscuits. All chips are biscuits. All biscuits are potatoes. Conclusions: I. All chips are potatoes. II. All potatoes are chocolates. III. Some potatoes are chips.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: All chips are biscuits and all biscuits are potatoes, so all chips are potatoes (I), and so some potatoes are chips (III). Nothing says every potato is a chocolate, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Extra : inadequate :: Appear : ?
questions.explanation: 'Extra' (more than needed) is the opposite of 'inadequate' (not enough); the opposite of 'appear' is 'disappear'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the sixth number is related to the fifth number. 27 : 189 :: 32 : ? :: 18 : 126
questions.explanation: Each second number is 7 times the first: 27 × 7 = 189 and 18 × 7 = 126. So 32 × 7 = 224.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. FYBL, CVFP, ZSJT, ? , TMRB
questions.explanation: The first and second letters move 3 back (F, C, Z, W, T and Y, V, S, P, M), the third and fourth 4 forward (B, F, J, N, R and L, P, T, X, B, wrapping round after Z): WPNX.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Ranked 2 Ragging 3 Rack 4 Rainbow 5 Radar
questions.explanation: All five begin 'Ra', and their third letters c, d, g, i, n give the order Rack, Radar, Ragging, Rainbow, Ranked: 3, 5, 2, 4, 1.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter-cluster series? GS, EU, AW, UY, MA, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move back 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 places (G, E, A, U, M, C, wrapping round), and the second move 2 forward each time (S, U, W, Y, A, C): CC.

questions.text: If ‘A’ means ‘subtraction’, ‘B’ means ‘division’, ‘C’ means ‘multiplication’, and ‘D‘ means ‘addition’, then what will be the value of following expression? 8 A 80 B 16 C 90 D 21
In a code language, 'She will come' is written as 'vu de ja', 'Come and eat' is written as 'te vu ma', 'all will eat' is written as 'ma nu ja'. What is the code for the word 'all' in that language?
questions.explanation: 'Come' is in the first two sentences, coded 'vu'; 'will' in the first and third, 'ja'; 'eat' in the second and third, 'ma'. The word left in 'all will eat' is 'all', so its code is 'nu'.

questions.text: Which of the mathematical signs should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct? 192 - 16 + 18 × 6 ÷ 24 = 96
questions.explanation: After interchanging − and ÷: 192 ÷ 16 + 18 × 6 − 24 = 12 + 108 − 24 = 96.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’, ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the father of B’, ‘A x B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’ and ‘A & B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’. How is N related to V if N x L – T & G + V?
questions.explanation: N is the brother of L, L is the father of T, T is the daughter of G and G is the mother of V. So T and V are children of L and G, L is V's father and N is V's father's brother.

questions.text: The SEVA app was launched by which of the following ministers to track coal dispatch?
questions.explanation: Piyush Goyal, then the minister in charge of coal and power, launched SEVA (Saral Eindhan Vitaran Application) in May 2017: Coal India's app that shows power-sector consumers how much coal has been dispatched.

questions.text: Which among the following Vedas is the oldest?
questions.explanation: The Rig Veda is the oldest of the four Vedas; the Sama, Yajur and Atharva Vedas came later.

questions.text: __________was introduced during fifth five year plan.
questions.explanation: The Minimum Needs Programme, introduced in the Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-79), aimed to provide basic services such as elementary education, rural health, drinking water, rural roads and housing.

questions.text: SME stands for small and ___________ enterprises.
questions.explanation: SME stands for small and medium-sized enterprises: firms below set limits of size, such as the number of employees or turnover.

questions.text: Which of the following was the first BCCI president?
questions.explanation: R. E. Grant Govan was the first president of the Board of Control for Cricket in India, founded in 1928; Anthony De Mello was its first secretary.

questions.text: As of November 2022, who among the following is the Governor of Andhra Pradesh, India?
questions.explanation: Biswabhusan Harichandan was Governor of Andhra Pradesh from July 2019 to February 2023, so also in November 2022. Anusuiya Uikey was then Governor of Chhattisgarh and Bhagat Singh Koshyari of Maharashtra.

questions.text: The maximum inflation in India was recorded in the year ___________ at 25.2 per cent was mainly attributed to the failure of kharif crops in the previous year and also to the hike in crude oil prices in the previous year.
questions.explanation: 1974-75 had India's highest annual inflation rate since independence, 25.2% (Economic Survey 2002-03), after poor rains hit the harvests and world oil prices rose sharply in 1973-74; it was still the highest when the exam was held (January 2023).

questions.text: Raut Nacha, Panthi and Soowa are famous dance styles of which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Raut Nacha, Panthi and Suwa (Soowa) are folk dances of Chhattisgarh.

questions.text: The age of the subscriber under Atal Pension Yojana (APY) should be between_______.
questions.explanation: The Atal Pension Yojana is open to citizens aged 18 to 40, who contribute until 60 for a guaranteed pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 a month.

questions.text: What is the emerging magma from a volcano onto the earth’s surface called?
questions.explanation: Magma that reaches the earth's surface is called lava. Ash is fine rock fragments blown out in an eruption, and pyroclastic flows are fast currents of hot gas and rock that sweep down a volcano's slopes.

questions.text: Which Constitutional Amendment introduced the fundamental Duties?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976), on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation, added Part IVA, Article 51A, listing the Fundamental Duties.

questions.text: In 2015, MN Subramaniam Endowment Award - The Music Academy Madras was awarded to______________.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the Bharatanatyam dancer Alarmel Valli: her own website lists The Music Academy's M.N. Subramaniam Endowment Award among her honours for 2015, and the Academy also chose her for its Natya Kala Acharya award for 2015.

questions.text: The celebrations for Paryushan Parv is held for _____ days by the Digambara sect of Jains.
questions.explanation: The Digambara Jains keep Paryushan as Das Lakshana Parva for ten days, one for each of the ten virtues; the Svetambaras keep it for eight.

questions.text: _______________ is an indicator used by experts to gauge the number of people dying prematurely due to a particular disease.
questions.explanation: The Global Burden of Disease (GBD) measures the number of people dying prematurely from a disease and the years they spend disabled by it.

questions.text: How many High Courts are there in India as of 2022?
questions.explanation: India had 25 High Courts in 2022; the newest, for Andhra Pradesh, was set up in 2019.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When was the Harijan Sewak Sangh founded as a result of the Poona Pact?
questions.explanation: Gandhi founded the Harijan Sevak Sangh (first called the Anti-Untouchability League) in September 1932, after the Poona Pact.

questions.text: The Avogadro's number is 6.022 X _________
questions.explanation: Avogadro's number, the number of particles in one mole, is 6.022 × 10²³.

questions.text: Who was the flag bearer for India for the closing ceremony of the Asian Games 2018?
questions.explanation: Hockey captain Rani Rampal carried India's flag at the closing ceremony of the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta; Neeraj Chopra was the flag bearer at the opening.

questions.text: In which of the following union territories was the highest literacy rate recorded in 2011?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Lakshadweep had the highest literacy rate among the union territories, about 91.8%.

questions.text: Where will you find plastids in a leaf cell?
questions.explanation: Plastids, such as chloroplasts, are organelles that lie in the cytoplasm of plant cells.

questions.text: Jiya gets a discount of 30 percent and 10 percent on a bill. The total discount she got is:
questions.explanation: Successive discounts of 30% and 10% leave 0.7 × 0.9 = 0.63 of the bill, so the total discount is 37%.

questions.text: The cost price of 2 pens and 3 notebooks is ₹220 and the cost price of 2 pens and 4 notebooks is ₹250. Find the ratio between the cost price of the pen and the notebook.
questions.explanation: Subtracting the two equations, a notebook costs ₹250 − ₹220 = ₹30, so 2 pens cost 220 − 90 = ₹130 and a pen ₹65. 65 : 30 = 13 : 6.

questions.text: The least number which should be added to 1845 to make it divisible by 3, 4, 5 and 6 is:
questions.explanation: LCM(3, 4, 5, 6) = 60. 1845 = 60 × 30 + 45, so adding 60 − 45 = 15 gives 1860, which all four divide.

questions.text: A person can row 66 km downstream in 6 h and 72 km upstream in 8 h. What is the speed of the current?
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 66 ÷ 6 = 11 km/h and upstream speed = 72 ÷ 8 = 9 km/h, so the current is (11 − 9)/2 = 1 km/h.

questions.text: Sonal, Kriti, and Priti together can complete a piece of work in 6 days while Kriti and Priti can do the same work separately in 30 and 18 days, then in how many days Sonal alone can do the same work?
questions.explanation: Sonal does 1/6 − 1/30 − 1/18 = (15 − 3 − 5)/90 = 7/90 of the work a day, so alone she takes 90/7 days.

questions.text: The marked price of a general study book is Rs.800. If it is sold at 15% and 20% successive discounts, then find its selling price.
The volume of a hemisphere is 32 times the volume of a sphere with radius 3 units. the diameter of the hemisphere is ___________ units.
questions.explanation: The sphere's volume is (4/3)π × 3³ = 36π, so the hemisphere's is 32 × 36π = 1152π. (2/3)πR³ = 1152π gives R³ = 1728, R = 12 and a diameter of 24.

questions.text: A sum of money is paid back in two annual instalments of Rs.1,25,000 each. If rate of interest is 6% per annum and interest is compounding annually, then find the sum borrowed.(Consider round up integral value)
questions.explanation: The sum is the present value of the two instalments: 1,25,000/1.06 + 1,25,000/1.06² = 1,17,924.53 + 1,11,249.56 = ₹2,29,174 to the nearest rupee.

questions.text: A fruit vendor purchases oranges at Rs.150, Rs.90 and Rs.75 per kg. These oranges purchased at three different prices are mixed in the ratio 4 : 5 : 6 respectively, and are sold at a profit of 40%. Find the selling price (in Rs.) of oranges per kg.
questions.explanation: The mixture costs (4 × 150 + 5 × 90 + 6 × 75)/15 = (600 + 450 + 450)/15 = ₹100 a kg; with a 40% profit it sells at ₹140 a kg.

questions.text: If the price of oil increases by 25 percent and Arpit increase the expenditure on oil by 10 percent, then by how much percent will he reduce the quantity of oil purchased?
questions.explanation: Quantity = expenditure ÷ price, so it becomes 1.10/1.25 = 0.88 of the old quantity: a 12% reduction.

questions.text: In a trapezium, the lengths of opposite parallel sides are 12 cm and 8 cm respectively, and the shortest distance between them is 16 cm, Find the area of the trapezium.
questions.explanation: Area = ½ × (sum of the parallel sides) × height = ½ × (12 + 8) × 16 = 160 cm².

questions.text: In an election Santosh got 24000 more votes than Mantosh. If Mantosh and Santosh got 30% and 40% of the total votes respectively. Find the total number of votes cast.
questions.explanation: Santosh's 40% and Mantosh's 30% differ by 10% of the votes, which is 24,000, so the total is 2,40,000.

questions.text: Students' strength of a co-educational School is 3,000. If the ratio of the number of boys to the number of girls in the school is 4 : 1, then what is the mean proportion of the number of boys and girls in the School, given that only boys and girls are students in the school?
questions.explanation: There are 3,000 × 4/5 = 2,400 boys and 600 girls; their mean proportional is √(2,400 × 600) = √14,40,000 = 1,200.

questions.text: If a natural number when divided by 5,6 and 7 leaves a remainder 4 in each case,then what is the smallest possible three digit natural number?
questions.explanation: LCM(5, 6, 7) = 210, so such numbers are 210k + 4. The smallest with three digits is 210 + 4 = 214.

questions.text: The average of 8 numbers is 24. If one of the numbers is excluded, the average becomes 22. Find the excluded number.
questions.explanation: The 8 numbers add up to 8 × 24 = 192 and the other 7 to 7 × 22 = 154, so the excluded number is 192 − 154 = 38.

questions.text: What is the difference between the compound interest, compounding annually and simple interest on ₹8,300 at 10% per annum for 2 years?
questions.explanation: For 2 years the difference is P(r/100)² = 8,300 × (10/100)² = ₹83.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. The authority tries to “subjugate” the marginalised people.
questions.explanation: To 'subjugate' is to bring under control and oppress; its opposite is 'liberate', to set free. 'Subordinate' and 'enslave' are close to 'subjugate'.

questions.text: Choose the option that can substitute the underlined segment correctly and complete the meaning of the sentence. The grandmother asked Rita to close the window as she suddenly started “feeling extremely cold”.
questions.explanation: 'Freezing' means feeling extremely cold: 'she suddenly started freezing'. 'Frosting' and 'icing' are a cake's sugar coating, and 'cold' cannot follow 'started' on its own.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Throw caution to the wind
questions.explanation: To 'throw caution to the wind' is to act boldly, ignoring the risk. 'Careful' and 'be cautious' are its opposites, and 'carefree' means free of worry, not taking a risk.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Hasty
questions.explanation: 'Hasty' means done too quickly, without enough care; its opposite is 'cautious'. 'Reckless', 'brisk' and 'quick' are close to 'hasty'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in simple past tense. A. Last year, I have travelled to Japan. B. Last year, I was travelling to Japan. C. Last year, I travelled to Japan. D. Last year, I had been travelling to Japan.
questions.explanation: The simple past uses the plain past form of the verb: 'Last year, I travelled to Japan.' A is in the present perfect, B the past continuous and D the past perfect continuous.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Celebrate
questions.explanation: To 'celebrate' a person or deed is to honour or praise it publicly; to 'disgrace' is to bring shame or dishonour on it. 'Manipulate', 'instigate' and 'tabulate' have nothing to do with honour.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. This blue shirt you “have wearing” really looks expensive.
questions.explanation: The present continuous is 'be' + '-ing', and 'you' takes 'are': 'This blue shirt you are wearing really looks expensive.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Beautiful
questions.explanation: 'Pretty' means attractive, a synonym of 'beautiful'. 'Dull' and 'drab' are nearly opposite, and 'homely' means cosy or, in American usage, plain.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word to fill in the blank in the sentence. Casual Sita wore a ________ yet stunning dress at the birthday party of her son.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'regular', in the sense of ordinary or everyday, which is what 'casual' means of clothes: a casual yet stunning dress. 'Regular' is not a usual synonym of 'casual' (in 'casual work' the two are opposites), but 'temporary' fits only that other sense and 'formal' is the opposite here.

questions.text: A part of the given sentence which has been underlined may contain a spelling error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the spelling error. If there is no error, select ‘No error’. Technology has become an “indespensable” element in our day-to-day activities.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'indispensable' (absolutely necessary), with 'i' after the 'd'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Appearanse' is misspelt: the word is 'appearance'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the italicised idiom in the given sentence. “Hold your horses !” said Mom as I reached for a cookie. “They are still too hot to eat.”
questions.explanation: 'Hold your horses' means wait, be patient: the cookies are still too hot to eat.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in the brackets to fill in the blank and complete the sentence. The water was too ________ (profound) to take a swim.
questions.explanation: 'Profound' here means deep; its opposite, 'shallow', fits: the water was too shallow to swim in.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Heyday
questions.explanation: A 'heyday' is the time of greatest success or vigour: one's 'prime'. 'Yesteryears' means past times in general.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Residents of Victorian Street in Thornton (1)___________ disturbed last night by an unusual accident. At eleven o’clock a car broke down near the end of the street and the driver left his vehicle (2)___________ while he went on with his journey by taxi. An hour later, the car’s alarm went off when it was hit (3)___________ a stolen van. The engine of the van blew up, so the thief tried to drive away in the car. But he gave up when the car would not (4)___________ and (5)___________ a bicycle instead.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'Residents' and 'last night' need the plural past 'were': the residents were disturbed.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Residents of Victorian Street in Thornton (1)___________ disturbed last night by an unusual accident. At eleven o’clock a car broke down near the end of the street and the driver left his vehicle (2)___________ while he went on with his journey by taxi. An hour later, the car’s alarm went off when it was hit (3)___________ a stolen van. The engine of the van blew up, so the thief tried to drive away in the car. But he gave up when the car would not (4)___________ and (5)___________ a bicycle instead.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The driver left his car 'there', near the end of the street, while he went on by taxi. 'Their' is a possessive and 'then' refers to time.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. But he gave up when the car would not (4)___________ and (5)___________ a bicycle instead.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: In the passive the doer is introduced by 'by': the car was hit by a stolen van.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Residents of Victorian Street in Thornton (1)___________ disturbed last night by an unusual accident. At eleven o’clock a car broke down near the end of the street and the driver left his vehicle (2)___________ while he went on with his journey by taxi. An hour later, the car’s alarm went off when it was hit (3)___________ a stolen van. The engine of the van blew up, so the thief tried to drive away in the car. But he gave up when the car would not (4)___________ and (5)___________ a bicycle instead.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: After the modal 'would (not)' comes the base form of the verb: the car would not 'start'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Residents of Victorian Street in Thornton (1)___________ disturbed last night by an unusual accident. At eleven o’clock a car broke down near the end of the street and the driver left his vehicle (2)___________ while he went on with his journey by taxi. An hour later, the car’s alarm went off when it was hit (3)___________ a stolen van. The engine of the van blew up, so the thief tried to drive away in the car. But he gave up when the car would not (4)___________ and (5)___________ a bicycle instead.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The thief gave up on the car and took a bicycle instead: he 'stole' it, in the past tense like 'gave up'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term. 512 : 10 :: ? : 11 :: 1331 : 13
questions.explanation: The first term of each pair is the cube of 2 less than the second: 512 = 8³ with 8 + 2 = 10, and 1331 = 11³ with 11 + 2 = 13. So ? = (11 − 2)³ = 9³ = 729.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? -1, 0, 3, 8, 15, ?
questions.explanation: The terms are n² − 1 for n = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (the differences are 1, 3, 5, 7, 9), so the next is 5² − 1 = 24.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No ties are pants. All pants are shirts. All ties are shirts. Conclusions: I. Some shirts are ties. II. Some shirts are pants. III. Some ties are shirts.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: All pants are shirts, so some shirts are pants (II). All ties are shirts, so some ties are shirts (III) and, turned round, some shirts are ties (I). 'No ties are pants' rules out none of them.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Car : Seat belt :: Fan : ?
questions.explanation: A seat belt is a part of a car, as a blade is a part of a fan.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) and complete the given number series? 5, 293, 437, 509, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 288, 144 and 72, halving each time, so the next is 36: 509 + 36 = 545.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘CRAZE’ is written as ‘DTDDJ’, ‘GLORY’ is written as ‘HNRVD’, how will ‘FAME’ be written as in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, +2, +3, +4 and +5, wrapping round after Z: CRAZE → DTDDJ and GLORY → HNRVD. So FAME → F+1, A+2, M+3, E+4 = GCPI.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. CAPTURE : PACERUT :: BANKING : NABGNIK :: CHARITY : ?
questions.explanation: The first three letters are reversed and so are the last four: CAP|TURE → PAC|ERUT and BAN|KING → NAB|GNIK. So CHA|RITY → AHC|YTIR: AHCYTIR.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1. RAY 2. RAVISH 3. RATIONAL 4. RATABLE 5. RASH 6. RAPTURE
questions.explanation: All begin with 'RA': RAP comes before RAS, RAT, RAV and RAY, and RATABLE (a) before RATIONAL (i). The order is RAPTURE, RASH, RATABLE, RATIONAL, RAVISH, RAY: 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 720 * 24 * 4 * 100 * 40 * 20
Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? XDZA, VFXC, ? , LPNM, DXFU
questions.explanation: The first and third letters move back 2, 4, 6 and 8 places and the second and fourth forward 2, 4, 6 and 8: X → V → R → L → D, D → F → J → P → X, Z → X → T → N → F and A → C → G → M → U. The missing term is RJTG.

questions.text: Seven friends M, N, O, P, Q, R and S are sitting on a straight bench facing towards east. P is sitting exactly at the middle position. Only four friends are sitting to the left of M. Only Q is sitting between R and S. O is sitting third to the right of S. Who is sitting at the second place from the right end?
questions.explanation: Facing east, the left end is north. P is 4th from the left and M 5th (four to his left). With O three places to the right of S, S can only be 3rd and O 6th; then Q is 2nd and R 1st, leaving N 7th. The order is R, Q, S, P, M, O, N, so O is second from the right end.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘GOLDEN’ is written as ‘MPHPGF’ and 'GERMAN' is written as ‘SFHPCO'. How will ‘GLOBAL’ be written as in that language?
questions.explanation: Each half of the word moves forward and is reversed, the first half by 1 and the second by 2: GOL → HPM → MPH and DEN → FGP → PGF; GER → SFH and MAN → PCO. So GLO → HMP → PMH and BAL → DCN → NCD: PMHNCD.

questions.text: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Jitender is an immediate neighbour of both Shahid and Jaya. Komal is sitting second to the right of Shahid. Tarun is sitting third to the left of Jaya. Vijay is an immediate neighbour of both Komal and Jaya. Who is the immediate neighbour of Jitender and Tarun?
questions.explanation: Jitender sits between Shahid and Jaya, and Komal, second to Shahid's right, fits only with Shahid on Jitender's right; Tarun sits opposite Jaya. Going round to the right: Jitender, Shahid, Tarun, Komal, Vijay, Jaya. Shahid sits between Jitender and Tarun.

questions.text: ‘A # B’ means ‘B is the sister of A’; ‘A @ B’ means ‘B is the brother of A’; ‘A % B’ means ‘B is the daughter of A’; ‘A $ B’ means ‘B is the husband of A’; If A $ B % C # D @ E, then how is E related to A?
questions.explanation: A $ B: B is A's husband. B % C: C is B's daughter. C # D: D is C's sister, so also B's daughter. D @ E: E is D's brother, so a son of B and his wife A: E is A's son.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? BDPY, HITB, ?, TSBH, ZXFK
questions.explanation: The four letters move +6, +5, +4 and +3 each time, wrapping round after Z: B → H → N → T → Z, D → I → N → S → X, P → T → X → B → F and Y → B → E → H → K. The missing term is NNXE.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 18 + 60 ÷ 15 × 24 - 12 = 84
‘Kharchi Puja’ is primarily celebrated in which of the following states of India?
questions.explanation: Kharchi Puja, the week-long festival of the fourteen gods, is held at the Chaturdasha Devata temple in Old Agartala, Tripura, in the month of Ashadha.

questions.text: The Reserve Bank of India was established on _______.
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India began operations on 1 April 1935, under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

questions.text: Who has been awarded Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in the year 2016 for the contribution to Chhau?
questions.explanation: Gopal Prasad Dubey, a Seraikella Chhau dancer and guru from Jharkhand, received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Chhau for 2016.

questions.text: _________are an example of public goods and services.
questions.explanation: Public goods such as roads are provided for everyone, and one person's use does not stop others from using them. Clothes, cosmetics and biscuits are private goods, bought for one's own use.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: During which movement did Chauri-Chaura incident happen?
questions.explanation: At Chauri Chaura, in Gorakhpur district, a crowd set fire to the police station in February 1922, killing the policemen inside; Gandhi then called off the Non-Cooperation Movement.

questions.text: As per Consumer Protection Rules, 2021, National Commission shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where value of the goods or services paid as consideration exceeds ____________________.
questions.explanation: Under the Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021, the National Commission hears complaints where the value paid exceeds ₹2 crore; State Commissions hear those from ₹50 lakh to ₹2 crore, and District Commissions those up to ₹50 lakh.

questions.text: ___________________ is associated with spoilage, development of off-flavors, deterioration of textures, discoloration and loss of nutritional value.
questions.explanation: Food deterioration is the loss of quality in food: spoilage, off-flavours, changes in texture and colour, and loss of nutrients. Preservation and conservation aim to prevent it.

questions.text: Area wise the largest state of India is ______.
questions.explanation: Rajasthan, about 3.42 lakh km², is the largest state by area, followed by Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.

questions.text: Amongst the following, which boxing weight class is the heaviest?
questions.explanation: In order of weight these classes run pinweight, flyweight, featherweight and lightweight, so lightweight is the heaviest.

questions.text: How many player play at a time in a Kabaddi match from one team?
questions.explanation: Each kabaddi team has seven players on the court at a time.

questions.text: Which of the following dynasties controlled the Silk Route during post Mauryan period?
questions.explanation: The Kushanas, who ruled Central Asia and north-west India about 2,000 years ago, controlled much of the Silk Route. The Cheras, Satavahanas and Shungas ruled in the far south, the Deccan and the Ganga valley.

questions.text: Who won the bypoll election and became Member of Legislative Assembly from Brajarajnagar constituency in Odisha, India in 2022?
questions.explanation: Alaka Mohanty of the BJD won the Brajarajnagar by-election held on 31 May 2022 (counted on 3 June), which followed the death of her husband, the sitting MLA Kishore Mohanty.

questions.text: As of March 2022, which of the following dance forms is in the category of a classical dance by the Sangeet Natak Akademi?
questions.explanation: Manipuri is one of the classical dances the Sangeet Natak Akademi recognises. Bihu is a folk dance of Assam, and Kalbeliya and Ghoomar are folk dances of Rajasthan.

questions.text: Which of the following does not come from sugarcane?
questions.explanation: Honey is made by bees from the nectar of flowers. Khandsari (an unrefined sugar), molasses and sugar all come from sugarcane juice.

questions.text: Which part of the Constitution of India deals with the Panchayat?
questions.explanation: Part IX (Articles 243 to 243-O), added by the 73rd Amendment, 1992, deals with the Panchayats. Part IX-A deals with the Municipalities.

questions.text: Who has been appointed as the Permanent Representative of India to the United Nations in June 2022?
questions.explanation: Ruchira Kamboj was named India's Permanent Representative to the United Nations in New York in June 2022, succeeding T. S. Tirumurti. The other three held the post earlier.

questions.text: A man, who practices running, covers the first half of the distance at 4 km/h and the remaining half of the distance at 6 km/h. What is his average speed?
questions.explanation: For two equal distances the average speed is 2 × 4 × 6/(4 + 6) = 48/10 = 4.8 km/h.

questions.text: Three years ago, Rahul borrowed a sum of money at compound interest rate of 10% per annum compounding annually. If the present value of that borrowed money is Rs.11,979, how much money was borrowed by Rahul?
In 65 litres of a mixture of kerosene and petrol, the ratio of kerosene to petrol is 3 : 2. In order to make this ratio 4 : 5, how many litres of petrol should be added to the given mixture?
questions.explanation: The mixture has 39 litres of kerosene and 26 of petrol. For 4 : 5, petrol must be 39 × 5/4 = 48.75 litres, so 48.75 − 26 = 22.75 litres is added.

questions.text: A dealer marks an air-conditioner for ₹1,20,000 and allows a discount of 12% on it. What is its selling price (in ₹)?
A number is increased by 8% and then, the increased number is decreased by 8%. What is the net increase or decrease in the number?
If books bought at prices ranging from Rs.200 to Rs.350 are being sold at prices ranging from Rs.300 to Rs.450, what is the highest possible profit that might be made in selling 8 books?
questions.explanation: The highest profit comes from buying at ₹200 and selling at ₹450: ₹250 a book, or ₹2,000 on 8 books.

questions.text: If a number 'a' is divisible by 18 and another number 'b' is divisible by 12, then (a² - b²) is divisible by :
questions.explanation: With a = 18m and b = 12n, a² − b² = 324m² − 144n² = 36(9m² − 4n²), always a multiple of 36. For a = 18 and b = 12 it is 180, which 48 and 40 do not divide, and for a = 18 and b = 24 it is −252, which 30 does not divide.

questions.text: Find the ratio of the total surface area to curved surface area of a cylinder whose radius is 20 cm and height 50 cm.
questions.explanation: TSA : CSA = 2πr(r + h) : 2πrh = (r + h) : h = 70 : 50 = 7 : 5.

questions.text: Ram wants to paint all the walls and ceiling of his reading room personally. He started painting his room and after painting the area of 16 m², a paint tin of 4 litres is exhausted. How many paint tins are required to paint the remaining area, if the total area of his room to be painted is 176 m²?
questions.explanation: One 4-litre tin covers 16 m². The remaining 176 − 16 = 160 m² needs 160 ÷ 16 = 10 tins.

questions.text: If x and y are inversely proportional to each other and x = 27 when y = 7, then what is the value of x when y = 21?
questions.explanation: xy stays constant: 27 × 7 = 189, so x = 189 ÷ 21 = 9.

questions.text: A thief moving at 40 km/h covers a distance in 5 hours 15 minutes. If the police chasing him cover the same distance at 50 km/h, then how long will the police take to cover the same distance?
questions.explanation: The distance is 40 × 5¼ = 210 km; at 50 km/h it takes 210/50 = 4.2 hours, that is 4 hours 12 minutes.

questions.text: An umbrella is bought at Rs.80 and sold at Rs.68. What is the percentage of loss?

The average weight of 20 people is 75 kgs. The average weight of 10 people out of them is 70 kgs. The average weight of 5 people out of the remaining people is 75 kgs. Find the average weight of 5 people remaining in the end.
questions.explanation: The total is 20 × 75 = 1500 kg. The first 10 weigh 700 kg and the next 5 weigh 375 kg, so the last 5 weigh 1500 − 1075 = 425 kg, an average of 85 kg.

questions.text: A is thrice as good a workman as B. A started the work and they worked together on alternate days and finished the work in 24 days. The number of days taken by A alone to finish the work was:
questions.explanation: If B does 1 unit a day, A does 3. Over 24 alternate days each works 12, doing 36 + 12 = 48 units, so A alone takes 48 ÷ 3 = 16 days.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. My boss “have insured” me that my salary will be credited next week.
questions.explanation: The singular 'boss' takes 'has', and to 'assure' someone is to tell them something so as to remove their doubt. To 'insure' is to cover with insurance and to 'ensure' is to make certain.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Obvious
questions.explanation: 'Obvious' means plain and clear; 'ambiguous', open to more than one meaning, is the opposite. 'Evident' and 'apparent' are synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Enormous
questions.explanation: 'Enormous' means very large; its opposite is 'negligible', so small as not to matter. 'Mammoth' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Gloomy
questions.explanation: 'Gloomy' means sad or dejected: 'unhappy'. 'Blissful', 'hopeful' and 'light' are nearly opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Stratified
questions.explanation: 'Stratified' means arranged in layers (strata): 'laminated', made of layers. 'Scattered' and 'ungraded' are nearly opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Josephine confessed that she “couldn’t stand another hour out” daylight.
questions.explanation: One cannot stand another hour 'of' something: 'she couldn't stand another hour of daylight'.

questions.text: Identify the correctly spelt sentence.
options: Human personality is classifide into three types- introvert, extrovert and ambivert.
Human persunality is clasified into three types- introvert, extrovert and ambivert.
Human personality is classified into three types- introvert, extrovert and ambivert.
Human personality is classfied into three types- introvert, extrovert and ambivert
questions.explanation: Only this sentence spells both 'personality' and 'classified' correctly; the others have 'classifide', 'persunality' and 'clasified', or 'classfied'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. Henry worked for a few years as a “sargent” in the army.
questions.explanation: The army rank is spelt 'sergeant'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Annoyance
questions.explanation: 'Annoyance' is the feeling of being irritated, a mild form of 'anger'. 'Hatred' is much stronger and 'agony' is great pain.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. My brother became very “frail” after his long sickness.
questions.explanation: 'Frail' means weak and delicate; the opposite is 'strong'. 'Feeble' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. The “strict” measures employed by the government ensured there was peace.
questions.explanation: 'Strict' measures are severe ones: 'austere'. 'Liberal' is nearly the opposite, and 'orthodox' (conventional) and 'valiant' (brave) do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Lay hands on
options: To touch or grasp someone, often with the threat of violence
To gently lay one’s hand on someone
questions.explanation: To 'lay hands on' someone is to seize or attack them; the phrase also means to find or get hold of something.

questions.text: Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully: Distribute these fruits and desserts (WITHIN) the girls, the boys and the teachers.
questions.explanation: 'Among' is used for sharing between more than two people or groups: 'Distribute these fruits and desserts among the girls, the boys and the teachers.'

questions.text: Select the correct idiom that can substitute the italicised group of words in the given sentence. To succeed in competitive exams is not “an easy task”.
questions.explanation: 'Child's play' is something very easy: 'To succeed in competitive exams is not child's play.' A 'cat's paw' is a person used by another, a 'black sheep' the disgrace of a group and a 'bed of thorns' a hard situation.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Inevitably, my approach will often be a personal one; how the idea grew in my mind, what shapes it took, how it (1) _________ me and affected my action. There will also be some (2) __________ personal experiences which have nothing to do with the subject in its wider aspects, but which coloured my mind and influenced my approach to the whole problem. Our judgments of countries and peoples are based on many factors; among them our personal contacts, if there have been any, have a (3)________ influence. If we do not personally know the people of a country we are apt to misjudge them even (4) ________ than otherwise, and (5) ________them entirely alien and different.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The verb is in the past tense, like 'grew', 'took' and 'affected' around it: 'how it influenced me and affected my action'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Inevitably, my approach will often be a personal one; how the idea grew in my mind, what shapes it took, how it (1) _________ me and affected my action. There will also be some (2) __________ personal experiences which have nothing to do with the subject in its wider aspects, but which coloured my mind and influenced my approach to the whole problem. Our judgments of countries and peoples are based on many factors; among them our personal contacts, if there have been any, have a (3)________ influence. If we do not personally know the people of a country we are apt to misjudge them even (4) ________ than otherwise, and (5) ________them entirely alien and different.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: An adverb is needed before the adjective 'personal': 'some entirely personal experiences', experiences wholly his own.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Inevitably, my approach will often be a personal one; how the idea grew in my mind, what shapes it took, how it (1) _________ me and affected my action. There will also be some (2) __________ personal experiences which have nothing to do with the subject in its wider aspects, but which coloured my mind and influenced my approach to the whole problem. Our judgments of countries and peoples are based on many factors; among them our personal contacts, if there have been any, have a (3)________ influence. If we do not personally know the people of a country we are apt to misjudge them even (4) ________ than otherwise, and (5) ________them entirely alien and different.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: A 'marked' influence is a clear, noticeable one; the adjective goes before 'influence'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Inevitably, my approach will often be a personal one; how the idea grew in my mind, what shapes it took, how it (1) _________ me and affected my action. There will also be some (2) __________ personal experiences which have nothing to do with the subject in its wider aspects, but which coloured my mind and influenced my approach to the whole problem. Our judgments of countries and peoples are based on many factors; among them our personal contacts, if there have been any, have a (3)________ influence. If we do not personally know the people of a country we are apt to misjudge them even (4) ________ than otherwise, and (5) ________them entirely alien and different.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Than' needs a comparative: 'we are apt to misjudge them even more than otherwise'.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Pollution 2 Popular 3 Population 4 Pocket 5 Pool
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Pocket (4), Pollution (1), Pool (5), Popular (2), Population (3). 'Poc' comes before 'Pol', 'Pol' before 'Poo' and 'Poo' before 'Pop', and 'Popular' comes before 'Population' as r comes before t: 4, 1, 5, 2, 3.

questions.text: If ‘$’ means ‘addition’, ‘@’ means ‘subtraction’, ‘#’ means ‘multiplication’, and ‘&‘ means ‘division’. What will be the value of the following expression? 54 & 6 # 2 $ 8 @ 4
questions.explanation: With the symbols replaced: 54 ÷ 6 × 2 + 8 − 4 = 9 × 2 + 8 − 4 = 18 + 8 − 4 = 22.

questions.text: Five friends S, U, K, N, and M are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. K is the immediate neighbour of S and M. S is not the immediate neighbour of U. N is not the immediate neighbour of M. Who is the immediate neighbour of K and N?
questions.explanation: K sits between S and M. S's other neighbour cannot be U, so it is N, and U takes the last seat, between M and N: S, K, M, U, N round the table. N is then not beside M, as required, and S sits next to both K and N.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed) (174, 14, 15); (228, 24, 14)
questions.explanation: The first number is 6 times the sum of the other two: (14 + 15) × 6 = 174 and (24 + 14) × 6 = 228. Likewise (45 + 19) × 6 = 384.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter-cluster series? KU, NT, PS, SR, UQ, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move +3 and +2 in turn (K, N, P, S, U, then X), and the second letters move one place back (U, T, S, R, Q, then P): XP.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 5, 8, 16, 19, 38, ?, 82
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 26 - 13 + 18 ÷ 54 × 24= 31

Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. MUSIC : NFHRX:: DANCE : WZMXV:: CONCERT : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on): MUSIC → NFHRX and DANCE → WZMXV. So CONCERT → XLMXVIG.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘the shirt is dirty’ is coded as '3525', ‘exercise regularly’ is coded as '89' and ‘comb your hair’ is coded as '444'. How will ‘empty your vessel’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded as its number of letters: 'the shirt is dirty' → 3, 5, 2, 5 and 'comb your hair' → 4, 4, 4. So 'empty your vessel' → 5, 4, 6: 546.

questions.text: ‘D + E’ means ‘D is the sister of E’. ‘D – E’ means ‘D is the husband of E’. ‘D × E’ means ‘D is the father of E’. ‘D ÷ E’ means ‘D is the daughter of E’. If, L ÷ R + T ÷ W – M, then how is T related to L?
questions.explanation: L ÷ R: L is R's daughter. R + T: R is T's sister. T ÷ W: T is W's daughter (and W − M: W is M's husband). R, a woman whose daughter is L, is L's mother, and T is her sister: L's mother's sister.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 100, 80, 63, 49, 38, 30, ?
questions.explanation: The differences fall by 3: 20, 17, 14, 11, 8, then 5, so 30 − 5 = 25.

questions.text: P, Q, R, S, T and U are sitting in a circle facing opposite to the centre. S is sitting to the immediate right of R and immediate left of U. Q is sitting between R and P. T is sitting to the immediate right of U and immediate left of P. Who is sitting to the immediate right of P?
questions.explanation: Facing outward, each person's right is the next seat clockwise. S is right of R and left of U, and T is right of U and left of P, so going clockwise the seats are R, S, U, T, P, with Q in the sixth seat between P and R. Q is at P's immediate right.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: Some flats are houses. All houses are buildings. All buildings are gardens. Conclusions: I. Some flats are gardens. II. All flats are buildings.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: Some flats are houses, every house is a building and every building a garden, so those flats are gardens: I follows. Nothing says the other flats are buildings, so II does not.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. HELLO : QNNGJ :: NAMASTE : GVUCOCP :: SALAM : ?
questions.explanation: Each word is reversed and every letter moved 2 places forward: HELLO → OLLEH → QNNGJ and NAMASTE → ETSAMAN → GVUCOCP. So SALAM → MALAS → OCNCU.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. PQHI, ? , TULM, VWNO
questions.explanation: The first pair moves on two letters each time (PQ, RS, TU, VW), and so does the second (HI, JK, LM, NO): RSJK.

questions.text: In a certain language, COFFEE is coded as 12 and FOUR is coded as 8. How will ANDROID be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: The code is twice the number of letters: COFFEE has 6 (12) and FOUR 4 (8). ANDROID has 7, so 14.

questions.text: Who among the following become Member of Parliament from Rampur, Uttar Pradesh in June 2022?
questions.explanation: In the Rampur Lok Sabha by-election of June 2022 (counted on 26 June), the BJP's Ghanshyam Singh Lodhi won the seat Azam Khan had vacated. Dinesh Lal Yadav 'Nirahua' won the Azamgarh by-election held at the same time.

questions.text: Which word among these was added in the preamble during the 42nd amendment?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

questions.text: Plants that do not have well-differentiated body design fall in this group. The plants in this group are commonly called algae. This group is ______.
questions.explanation: Thallophyta are the plants without a well-differentiated body, the algae, such as Spirogyra and Ulothrix. Bryophytes, pteridophytes and gymnosperms have more differentiated bodies.

questions.text: Who has been appointed as the new Chief Justice of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh in October 2022?
questions.explanation: Justice Ali Mohammad Magrey was appointed Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh on 11 October 2022, succeeding Justice Pankaj Mithal, who moved to the Rajasthan High Court; Justice P B Varale was appointed Chief Justice of Karnataka the same day.

questions.text: Pick the odd one out (Hint: Millets)
questions.explanation: Ragi (finger millet), bajra (pearl millet) and jowar (sorghum) are millets; the potato is a tuber.

questions.text: Identify the place in India where tropical cyclones originate from.
options: Bay of Bengal and Indian ocean
questions.explanation: The tropical cyclones that strike India form over the north Indian Ocean, most of them in the Bay of Bengal and fewer in the Arabian Sea, which is also part of the Indian Ocean.

questions.text: Which among the following waves is not an electromagnetic wave?
questions.explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons, charged particles that electric and magnetic fields deflect. Ultraviolet, infrared and gamma rays are all electromagnetic waves.

questions.text: The second edition of 'Khelo India National Winter Games 2021' was inaugurated in Jammu and Kashmir's __________ district on 26 February 2021.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Gulmarg, where Prime Minister Narendra Modi opened the second Khelo India Winter Games by video on 26 February 2021. Gulmarg is a ski resort in Baramulla district rather than a district itself, but none of the other places was the venue.

questions.text: Which of the following classical dances has its origin in Assam?
questions.explanation: Sattriya was created by the Vaishnava saint Srimanta Sankardev and preserved in Assam's sattras (monasteries); the Sangeet Natak Akademi recognised it as a classical dance in 2000.

questions.text: Who officially opened the Summer Olympics Games 2020?
questions.explanation: Emperor Naruhito of Japan declared the Tokyo 2020 Olympics open on 23 July 2021; the Games had been postponed by a year because of the Covid-19 pandemic.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following Satyagraha was led by Dr. BR Ambedkar?
questions.explanation: Dr B R Ambedkar led the Mahad Satyagraha of March 1927 for the right of Dalits to draw water from the public Chavdar tank at Mahad. The Kheda Satyagraha (1918) and the Individual Satyagraha (1940) were Gandhi's.

questions.text: The Medaram Jatara Festival is a ____-day long festival celebrated by Koya tribe.
questions.explanation: The Medaram (Sammakka Saralamma) Jatara of the Koya tribe, held every two years at Medaram in Telangana's Mulugu district, lasts four days, from the arrival of the goddesses Saralamma and Sammakka to their return to the forest.

questions.text: Subsidies are provided by the government keeping in mind the _____________ of public.
questions.explanation: Subsidies are given for the welfare of the people: the government pays part of the cost of essentials such as food, fertiliser and cooking gas so that people pay less for them.

questions.text: Hymns of the Rigveda are known as __________.
questions.explanation: The hymns of the Rigveda are called suktas: 1,028 of them, arranged in ten mandalas (books).

questions.text: In which year the planning commission was set up in India?
questions.explanation: The Planning Commission was set up by a Cabinet resolution on 15 March 1950, with Jawaharlal Nehru as its chairman.

questions.text: As per census 2011, which union territory of India has the highest literacy rate?
questions.explanation: In Census 2011 Lakshadweep had the highest literacy rate among the union territories, 91.85%, ahead of Daman and Diu (87.10%), Chandigarh (86.05%) and Puducherry (85.85%).

questions.text: Abhinandan Saroja National Award was started on the birthday of ______________.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Saroja Vaidyanathan, the Bharatanatyam guru who founded Ganesa Natyalaya in Delhi in 1974 and received the Padma Bhushan in 2013. The press release for the 2021 award, given to the dancer Aparna Satheesan, says the award was started on her birthday.

questions.text: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) is the flagship scheme of the ____________.
options: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME)
questions.explanation: The Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, launched in 2015 for skill training, is the flagship scheme of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, carried out through the National Skill Development Corporation.

questions.text: _________ model was followed in the first five year plan.
questions.explanation: The First Five Year Plan (1951-56) was based on the Harrod-Domar model, which ties growth to saving and investment; the Second followed P C Mahalanobis's model.

questions.text: In India, who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner?
questions.explanation: Under Article 324(2) the President appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and the other Election Commissioners.

questions.text: A number ‘y’ when divided by 225 leaves 33 as the remainder. The same number when divided by 15 leaves ‘z’ as the remainder. The value of z is:
questions.explanation: y = 225k + 33, and 225 = 15 × 15 is divisible by 15, so y leaves the same remainder as 33: 33 = 2 × 15 + 3, so z = 3.

questions.text: A trader offers an 8% discount on all his goods and still make a 15% profit. If an item is marked with a price of ₹250, the cost price is:
questions.explanation: The selling price is 92% of ₹250 = ₹230, which is 115% of the cost price: 230 ÷ 1.15 = ₹200.

questions.text: Krishan bought first and second item for ₹150 and ₹300 respectively. He sold the first item at 20% profit, and the second item at 20% loss. Find his overall profit or loss percentage. (Rounded off to two decimal places)
questions.explanation: The first item sells for ₹180 and the second for ₹240: ₹420 for a cost of ₹450. The loss is ₹30, and 30/450 × 100 = 6.67%.

questions.text: 12% of the voters in an election did not cast their votes and 2% of the casted votes were declared invalid. In this election, there were only two candidates. The winner by obtaining 46% of the total registered voters defeated his opponent by 1,044 votes. What was the total number of voters registered in the election?
questions.explanation: With V voters registered, 0.88V voted and 0.98 × 0.88V = 0.8624V votes were valid. The winner got 0.46V and the loser 0.8624V − 0.46V = 0.4024V, so the margin is 0.0576V = 1,044 and V = 18,125.

questions.text: What is the LCM of two co-prime numbers whose product is 323?
questions.explanation: Co-prime numbers have HCF 1, so their LCM equals their product: 323 (= 17 × 19).

questions.text: A certain number is added to each of the numbers 11,15,19 and 25. After addition, these numbers are in proportional. What is the number added?
The average of 29 observations is 40. If the average of the first 15 observations is 38, and that of the last 15 observations is 45, then the 15th observation is:
questions.explanation: All 29 total 29 × 40 = 1,160. The first 15 total 15 × 38 = 570 and the last 15 total 15 × 45 = 675; the 15th is counted in both, so it is 570 + 675 − 1,160 = 85.

questions.text: The marked price of an item was Rs. 4000 but the shopkeeper offered a double discount of 5 percent and 7 percent. In how much did he finally sell the item?

Two friends are running on a circular track of 720 m. They started from the same point and are moving in the same direction with speeds of 1.5 m/s and 3.5 m/s. After how much time will they cross each other for the second time?
questions.explanation: The faster runner gains 3.5 − 1.5 = 2 m a second, so he passes the slower one every 720/2 = 360 seconds (6 minutes); the second crossing comes after 12 minutes.

questions.text: A can do a piece of work in 51 days and B can do the same work in 34 days. Find the time required to complete the same work if they work on alternate days and A starts the work.
questions.explanation: Take the work as 102 units: A does 2 a day and B 3. Each pair of days does 5 units, so 20 pairs (40 days) do 100, and on day 41 A does the last 2.

questions.text: What should be added to the each numbers 9, 22, 14, and 32 so that the obtained numbers are proportional?

A shopkeeper sells rice. He buys it at a rate 15% less than the selling price. His total sales value for a month is Rs.5,50,000 and he pays Rs.8,000 as rent of the shop at the start of the month. His profit percentage in the month is ________.
questions.explanation: The rice costs 85% of ₹5,50,000 = ₹4,67,500, and with the ₹8,000 rent the cost is ₹4,75,500. The profit is ₹74,500, and 74,500/4,75,500 × 100 = 15.67%, about 15.7%.

questions.text: Ramesh and Naresh start running at speeds of 26 km/h and 18 km/h respectively towards each other, they meet after one hour and 45 minutes. How far (in metres) were they from each other when they started running?
questions.explanation: They close at 26 + 18 = 44 km/h, so in 1.75 hours they cover 44 × 1.75 = 77 km = 77,000 m.

questions.text: If the radius of a cylinder is 7 m and its total surface area is 440 m², then find the height of the cylinder. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Total surface area = 2πr(r + h) = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × (7 + h) = 44(7 + h) = 440, so 7 + h = 10 and h = 3 m.

questions.text: In an assembly election, a candidate got 72% of the total valid votes. 1.2% of the total votes were declared invalid. If the total number of voters is 3,32,000, then the number of valid votes polled in favour of this candidate is: (Consider integral part only)
Identify the correctly spelt sentence.
options: It is believed that a catarpillar can become a butterfly.
It is believed that a caterpillar can become a butterfly.
It is believed that a catterpillar can become a butterfly.
It is believed that a caterpilar can become a butterfly.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'caterpillar': 'cater-' with one 't', then 'pillar' with a double 'l'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Adversity
questions.explanation: 'Adversity' means hardship or misfortune. 'Allegiance' is loyalty, and 'progress' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The flyover that “connecting” the two cities is broken.
questions.explanation: A lasting fact about the flyover needs the simple present, and 'connects' agrees with the singular 'flyover': 'The flyover that connects the two cities is broken.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the italicised word in the given sentence. The “miser” hated spending money.
questions.explanation: A miser hoards money; the opposite is a 'spendthrift', who spends it wastefully. 'Tightwad', 'scrooge' and 'skinflint' all mean a miser.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Wrangle for an ass’s shadow
questions.explanation: To 'wrangle for an ass's shadow' is to quarrel over something trivial, of no real value.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Bargain
questions.explanation: A 'bargain' is an agreement in which each side gives something in return: a 'deal'.

questions.text: Select the correct pair of words for the blanks in the given sentence. My teacher asked me to read ________ and also _________ my best friend to celebrate his birthday in the school.
questions.explanation: 'Aloud' means in a voice others can hear, and 'allowed' means permitted: the teacher asked me to read aloud and allowed my friend to celebrate his birthday.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The cloth is _________ to touch so it is not suitable for apparels.
questions.explanation: 'Coarse' means rough to the touch, which is why the cloth is unsuitable for clothes; 'soft' and 'smooth' would make it suitable.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. They have decided to visit Konark, “have they”?
questions.explanation: A positive statement takes a negative tag, made with its auxiliary 'have' and the pronoun 'they': 'They have decided to visit Konark, haven't they?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Eradicate
questions.explanation: To 'eradicate' is to destroy completely; the opposite is to 'conserve', to protect and keep. 'Abolish' is close in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Quietness
questions.explanation: 'Quietness' is a state of calm and stillness; 'agitation', a state of disturbance and excitement, is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'persist', with an 's' where 'Percist' has a 'c'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. If the charge that he conspired / to raze a building is valid,/ there is great deal to answer for.
options: there is great deal to answer for
If the charge that he conspired
to raze a building is valid
questions.explanation: 'A great deal' needs the article: 'there is a great deal to answer for'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Indian society is a complex mix of ________ cultures, people and languages.
questions.explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun 'cultures': 'diverse', meaning varied. 'Diversity' and 'diversion' are nouns and 'diverges' a verb.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Snake in the grass
questions.explanation: A 'snake in the grass' is a treacherous person who pretends to be a friend.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The death penalty, often known as capital (1)________, is the most severe form of punishment that may be meted out to an individual under any criminal legislation in (2)________anywhere in the world. The legal (3)_________through which the state uses its power to take an individual's life is known as the death penalty. It has (4)_________ since the establishment of the State itself. The (5)__________ of independence heralded the beginning of a new era in India's judicial system.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Capital punishment' is the usual name for the death penalty.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The death penalty, often known as capital (1)________, is the most severe form of punishment that may be meted out to an individual under any criminal legislation in (2)________anywhere in the world. The legal (3)_________through which the state uses its power to take an individual's life is known as the death penalty. It has (4)_________ since the establishment of the State itself. The (5)__________ of independence heralded the beginning of a new era in India's judicial system.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'In existence' means existing: it is the severest punishment under any criminal law that exists anywhere in the world.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The death penalty, often known as capital (1)________, is the most severe form of punishment that may be meted out to an individual under any criminal legislation in (2)________anywhere in the world. The legal (3)_________through which the state uses its power to take an individual's life is known as the death penalty. It has (4)_________ since the establishment of the State itself. The (5)__________ of independence heralded the beginning of a new era in India's judicial system.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The death penalty is the legal 'method', or process, through which the state takes a person's life.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The death penalty, often known as capital (1)________, is the most severe form of punishment that may be meted out to an individual under any criminal legislation in (2)________anywhere in the world. The legal (3)_________through which the state uses its power to take an individual's life is known as the death penalty. It has (4)_________ since the establishment of the State itself. The (5)__________ of independence heralded the beginning of a new era in India's judicial system.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The death penalty 'has existed' since the State itself was established; 'considered', 'authorised' and 'published' would need 'been' or an object to make sense.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The death penalty, often known as capital (1)________, is the most severe form of punishment that may be meted out to an individual under any criminal legislation in (2)________anywhere in the world. The legal (3)_________through which the state uses its power to take an individual's life is known as the death penalty. It has (4)_________ since the establishment of the State itself. The (5)__________ of independence heralded the beginning of a new era in India's judicial system.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The 'birth', or beginning, of independence heralded a new era; 'end' and 'enlightenment' do not fit, and 'verity' means truth.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘OUTGROW’ is written as ‘56GRPX’ and 'THINNER' is written as '37NNFS'. How will ‘THOUGHT’ be written as in that language?
questions.explanation: The first three letters become the sum of their places in the alphabet, and of the last four the first two stay while the last two move one place on: OUT → 15 + 21 + 20 = 56 and GROW → GRPX; THI → 20 + 8 + 9 = 37 and NNER → NNFS. So THO → 20 + 8 + 15 = 43 and UGHT → UGIU: 43UGIU.

questions.text: Which of the following options will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 57, 63, 71, ?, 93, 107
questions.explanation: The differences rise by 2: 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. So 71 + 10 = 81, and 81 + 12 = 93.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Dog : Four :: Sparrow : ?
questions.explanation: A dog has four legs and a sparrow two.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 132 ÷ 6 – 24 × 5 + 9 = 43
questions.explanation: After interchanging + and ×: 132 ÷ 6 − 24 + 5 × 9 = 22 − 24 + 45 = 43.

questions.text: Which of the following letters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter series? F, D, J, B, N, Z, ?
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: F, J, N move 4 places forward (6, 10, 14), so the next is 18, R; D, B, Z move 2 places back.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1. Elegant 2. Emerald 3. Elaborate 4. Elasticity 5. Elephant
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Elaborate (3), Elasticity (4), Elegant (1), Elephant (5), Emerald (2). 'Elab' comes before 'Elas', 'Ela' before 'Ele', 'Eleg' before 'Elep', and 'El' before 'Em'.

questions.text: 6 people P, Q, R, S, T, and U are sitting on a wall facing North. P is to the immediate left of Q. R is to the immediate right of Q. Only S is sitting between R and T. U is sitting to the immediate right of T. Who is sitting between Q and S?
questions.explanation: From the left: P, Q and R (P to Q's left, R to its right), then S, the only one between R and T, then T and U: P Q R S T U. R sits between Q and S.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 14 : 4 :: 18 : 6 :: 22 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second number is half the first, less 3: 14 ÷ 2 − 3 = 4 and 18 ÷ 2 − 3 = 6. Likewise 22 ÷ 2 − 3 = 8.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Rupee : India :: Dollar : ?
questions.explanation: The rupee is the currency of India, and the dollar that of the United States of America.

questions.text: In a certain code language ACCOUNT is written as ‘EBGNYMX’ and MANOR is written as ‘QZRNV’. How will PATTERN be written in the same code language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +4 and −1 in turn: ACCOUNT → EBGNYMX and MANOR → QZRNV. So PATTERN → TZXSIQR.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. JRY, GOV, DLS, AIP, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back every time: J, G, D, A, X; R, O, L, I, F; Y, V, S, P, M. The next cluster is XFM.

questions.text: ‘C / D’ means ‘C is the sister of D’. ‘C < D’ means ‘C is the husband of D’. ‘C @ D’ means ‘C is the father of D’. ‘C + D’ means ‘C is the son of D’. If P @ Q + R / S < T, how is T related to Q?
questions.explanation: P is Q's father and Q is R's son, so R, being a sister (of S), is Q's mother. S, R's brother, is T's husband, so T is the wife of Q's mother's brother.

questions.text: If ‘+’ means ‘-’, ‘-’ means ‘÷’, ‘÷’ means ‘×’, and ‘×‘ means ‘+’. Which of the following will be the value of the expression? 117 – 13 ÷ 6 + 24 × 26

Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No keys are phones. All keys are clips. Some keys are tables. Conclusions: I. Some clips are not phones. II. Some tables are not phones. III. Some clips are tables.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: Every key is a clip and no key is a phone, so some clips are not phones (I). The keys that are tables are not phones (II), and they are clips, so some clips are tables (III). All three follow.

questions.text: Seven people F, H, K, G, J, D, and L are sitting in a straight row, facing north. Only two people sit to the right of G. Only two people sit to the left of J. H sits between G and J. K sits between J and L. F sits between G and D. Who sits at the extreme right of the row?
