questions.explanation: Counting seats from the left, G is 5th (two people to its right) and J 3rd (two to its left), so H is 4th. K, between J and L, is 2nd and L 1st; F, between G and D, is 6th and D 7th. D sits at the extreme right.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 23629, 23593, 23568, ?, 23543, 23539
questions.explanation: The differences are 36, 25, 16, 9 and 4, the squares of 6 down to 2: 23568 − 16 = 23552, and 23552 − 9 = 23543.

questions.text: Which of the following type of unemployment is there in rural areas? I. Seasonal Unemployment II. Disguised Unemployment
questions.explanation: Both are common in rural India: seasonal unemployment, as farm work is available only in some months of the year, and disguised unemployment, as more members of a family work on its farm than are needed.

questions.text: The golden quadrilateral super highways connect Delhi, __________, Chennai, and Mumbai.
questions.explanation: The Golden Quadrilateral super highways link India's four metropolitan cities: Delhi, Kolkata, Chennai and Mumbai.

questions.text: According to Megasthenes, how many gates were there in Pataliputra?
questions.explanation: Megasthenes, the Greek envoy at Chandragupta Maurya's court, wrote that the wall around Pataliputra had 570 towers and 64 gates.

questions.text: Which Article authorises the President to appoint the Governor of a State as the administrator of an adjoining Union territory?
questions.explanation: Article 239(2) lets the President appoint the Governor of a State as the administrator of an adjoining Union territory; in that role the Governor acts independently of the State's Council of Ministers.

questions.text: Whom has the Union Home Ministry appointed as the new Commissioner of Delhi Police in July 2022?
questions.explanation: Sanjay Arora, a 1988-batch Tamil Nadu cadre IPS officer then heading the ITBP, was appointed Commissioner of Delhi Police on 31 July 2022, succeeding Rakesh Asthana, and took charge on 1 August 2022.

questions.text: In ______ method of calculating national income, we calculate the aggregate annual value of goods and services produced (if a year is the unit of time).
questions.explanation: The product (value added) method adds up the value of the goods and services produced in the economy in a year; the income and expenditure methods are the other two ways of measuring national income.

questions.text: The deadline for the abolition of the reservation of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the year 2020 was extended for further _________years.
questions.explanation: The 104th Amendment (2019) extended the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and the State Assemblies (Article 334), due to end in January 2020, by 10 years, to January 2030.

questions.text: Kunchu Kurup is widely recognised for which dance form?
questions.explanation: Thakazhi Kunchu Kurup was one of the great Kathakali actors of Kerala.

questions.text: Which political leader won the by-poll election from Champawat constituency in Uttarakhand, in May 2022?
questions.explanation: Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, who had lost his own seat of Khatima in the 2022 Assembly election, won the Champawat by-poll held on 31 May 2022 by more than 55,000 votes; the result was declared on 3 June.

questions.text: The base of the ecological pyramid is usually broad and it narrows towards the _______.
questions.explanation: The producers at the base are the largest level, and each higher trophic level is smaller, so the pyramid narrows towards the top carnivores at its apex.

questions.text: The theme of the 6th International Day of Yoga-2020 was ______.
options: Yoga at Home and Yoga with Family
Be with Yoga, Be at Home!
questions.explanation: The 6th International Day of Yoga, 21 June 2020, fell during the Covid-19 pandemic; its theme, 'Yoga at Home and Yoga with Family', asked people to practise at home rather than at mass gatherings.

questions.text: Radha Reddy and Raja Reddy are famous proponents of which dance?
questions.explanation: Raja and Radha Reddy, a husband-and-wife pair, are leading Kuchipudi dancers and teachers.

questions.text: Which of the following is a benefit of the Green Revolution?
options: decrease in food grain stock of government
Increase in the price of food grains
Increase in the import of food grains
questions.explanation: High-yielding seeds, fertilisers and irrigation raised the output of wheat and rice so much that India became self-sufficient in food grains and could build up buffer stocks.

questions.text: Which of the following is one of the principal advantage of using a solar cell?
options: It has metal in the outer area.
questions.explanation: NCERT gives this as the principal advantage of solar cells: they have no moving parts, need little maintenance and work without any focusing device.

questions.text: Gangotri Glacier lies in which state?
questions.explanation: The Gangotri Glacier, the source of the Bhagirathi (Ganga), is in Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand.

questions.text: Third Five Year plans were aimed at making India ________.
questions.explanation: The Third Five Year Plan (1961-66) aimed at making the Indian economy self-reliant and self-generating.

questions.text: The first Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna award was given to which of the following sports person?
questions.explanation: The chess grandmaster Viswanathan Anand received the first Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, for 1991-92.

questions.text: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the abolition of titles?
questions.explanation: Article 18 abolishes titles: the State may confer none except military and academic distinctions, and no citizen may accept a title from a foreign State.

questions.text: Who among the following wrote the song Vande Mataram?
questions.explanation: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote 'Vande Mataram', which appeared in his novel 'Anandamath' (1882).

questions.text: The Bumchu festival is primarily celebrated in which of the following states of India?
questions.explanation: Bumchu, the festival of the sacred water pot, is held at the Tashiding Monastery in western Sikkim.

questions.text: The fourth proportional to 16, 26 and 32 is:
Jack can do a piece of work in 30 days. Ryan can do this work in 14 days. Jack started the work alone. After how many days should Ryan join him, so that the work is finished in 15 days?
questions.explanation: Jack works all 15 days and does 15/30 = 1/2 of the work. Ryan does the other half in 14/2 = 7 days, so he joins after 15 − 7 = 8 days.

questions.text: The average weight of 100 employees in a company is 62 kg and that of the remaining 25 employees is 52 kg. Find the average weight of all the employees in the company.
questions.explanation: The total weight is 100 × 62 + 25 × 52 = 6,200 + 1,300 = 7,500 kg for 125 employees, so the average is 7,500/125 = 60 kg.

questions.text: In how many years ₹4,000 will amount to ₹5,324 at 10 percent per annum compound interest, compounded annually?
After allowing a discount of 10% on its marked price, the value of a mobile phone is Rs.20,250. If no discount is allowed, then the shopkeeper gains 20%. The cost price of the mobile phone is:
questions.explanation: The marked price is 20,250/0.9 = Rs.22,500. Selling at that price gains 20%, so the cost price is 22,500/1.2 = Rs.18,750.

questions.text: The price of an article is reduced by 10% but the daily sale of the article is increased by 20%. The net effect on the daily sale receipts is:
questions.explanation: The receipts become 0.9 × 1.2 = 1.08 times what they were: an increase of 8%.

questions.text: If a train 90-m-long crosses a platform of 210-m-long in 20 sec, then what is the speed of the train?
questions.explanation: The train covers 90 + 210 = 300 m in 20 seconds: 15 m/s = 15 × 18/5 = 54 km/h.

questions.text: A man saves 25% of his monthly income. Due to a 20% increase in his income, his expenditure also increases by 20%. Now he can save Rs.1,500 per month. Find his original monthly income.
questions.explanation: With an income of x he spends 0.75x. After the rise he earns 1.2x and spends 0.9x, saving 0.3x = 1,500, so x = Rs.5,000.

questions.text: Ram and Lakshman can complete a work in 15 and 20 days, respectively. If Bharat, Ram and Lakshman all are working together, then they can complete the work in 5 days. How long will Bharat take to finish the work?
questions.explanation: Bharat does 1/5 − 1/15 − 1/20 = (12 − 4 − 3)/60 = 1/12 of the work a day, so he takes 12 days.

questions.text: Two trains A and B of lengths 190 m and 195 m are running at speeds of 50 km/h and 76 km/h, respectively, towards each other on parallel tracks. In how much time will they cross each other?
questions.explanation: Moving towards each other, they close at 50 + 76 = 126 km/h = 35 m/s, and cover 190 + 195 = 385 m in 385/35 = 11 seconds.

questions.text: The price of a car is Rs.2,50,000. In the first year, its value depreciates by 10%, and in the second year, it depreciates by 15%. What will be the value of the car after 2 years?
Rakesh sells two watches for Rs.2,530 each, gaining 15% on one and losing 15% on the other. Find his approximate gain or loss percentage in the whole transaction.
questions.explanation: When two articles sell at the same price, one at x% gain and the other at x% loss, the net is a loss of x²/100 per cent: 15²/100 = 2.25%. (The cost prices are 2,530/1.15 = Rs.2,200 and 2,530/0.85 ≈ Rs.2,976.47.)

questions.text: Select the correct combination and order of mathematical signs to replace ‘*’ such that the equation is balanced: 172 * 86 * 14 * 2 = 30
A bike rider covers 100 km at a speed of 75 km/h. At what speed does the rider have to drive for the next one hour to get an average speed of 90 km/h?
questions.explanation: The first 100 km take 100/75 = 4/3 hours. An average of 90 km/h over 4/3 + 1 = 7/3 hours means 210 km in all, so the next hour must cover 110 km: 110 km/h.

questions.text: In a college canteen, food items were collected to serve 96 students for 5 days. But due to new admissions, 64 more students joined. Now, for how many days the food items would last?
questions.explanation: The food is enough for 96 × 5 = 480 student-days. With 96 + 64 = 160 students it lasts 480/160 = 3 days.

questions.text: Select the appropriate idiom that can replace the underlined phrase in the following sentence. Geet “talks incessantly” about cycling in her town.
options: has a bee in her bonnet
questions.explanation: To 'have a bee in one's bonnet' about something is to be obsessed with it and keep talking about it: 'Geet has a bee in her bonnet about cycling in her town.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks in the given sentence. The vice chancellor is supposed to ______ the gathering tonight, and Seema was late as she could not find the ______ of Geeta.
questions.explanation: 'Address' fits both blanks: as a verb, to speak formally to a gathering, and as a noun, the place where someone lives.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. We are (last) __________ in line.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'last' is 'foremost', that is first: 'We are foremost in line.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. I have to save this coupon “in case I come back to the store tomorrow”.
options: in case I came back to the store tomorrow
if in case I come back to the store tomorrow
in case I will come back to the store tomorrow
questions.explanation: After 'in case' a future possibility takes the simple present, so the sentence is correct as it stands; 'will come' is wrong after 'in case', and 'if in case' repeats itself.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Indebted
questions.explanation: To be 'indebted' to someone is to owe them gratitude, that is to be thankful.

questions.text: The sentence given below has one misspelt word. Spot the INCORRECTLY spelt word and select its correct spelling. You need to give tremendus input for excellence.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'tremendous'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Cramped
questions.explanation: 'Cramped' means uncomfortably small or confined; 'extensive', large in extent, is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. A thin layer of substance called soil “maintains the level” of the Earth and is where plant roots are found.
questions.explanation: Soil is the thin layer that 'covers the surface' of the Earth; it does not maintain the Earth's level.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Prashant is “obstinate” by nature.
questions.explanation: 'Obstinate' means stubbornly refusing to change one's mind, as does 'adamant'. 'Pliable' and 'flexible' are its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Residents of the area are still trying to come to terms with the ___________ of the disaster.
questions.explanation: 'Enormity' here means the great scale and seriousness of something bad: the residents are still taking in how grave the disaster was. 'Heinousness' and 'atrocity' are used of wicked acts, and 'duress' means pressure or threats.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Sustain
questions.explanation: To 'sustain' is to support something or keep it going; to 'obstruct' is to block or hinder it. 'Continue' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Her knowledge of English are very limited.
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular 'knowledge' ('of English' only describes it), so the verb must be 'is': 'Her knowledge of English is very limited.'

questions.text: The sentence given below has one misspelt word. Spot the INCORRECTLY spelt word and select its correct spelling. The number of bankrupcies was especially high last year.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'bankruptcies', keeping the 't' of 'bankrupt'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. He has a “nasty” habit of picking his nose.
questions.explanation: 'Nasty' here means very unpleasant or disgusting, close to 'despicable'. 'Laudable' means praiseworthy and 'indolent' lazy.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. I understood why these highly (1) ___________ professionals remained in the closet. I was one of (2) _________. We could not deny our (3) __________ experiences and senses. Yet our training was in many ways diametrically (4) _________ to the information, experiences and beliefs we had accumulated. So we remained (5) _________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Highly trained professionals' are people with long, thorough training, which the passage goes on to call 'our training'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. I understood why these highly (1) ___________ professionals remained in the closet. I was one of (2) _________. We could not deny our (3) __________ experiences and senses. Yet our training was in many ways diametrically (4) _________ to the information, experiences and beliefs we had accumulated. So we remained (5) _________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The object pronoun 'them' refers back to the professionals: 'I was one of them.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. I understood why these highly (1) ___________ professionals remained in the closet. I was one of (2) _________. We could not deny our (3) __________ experiences and senses. Yet our training was in many ways diametrically (4) _________ to the information, experiences and beliefs we had accumulated. So we remained (5) _________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Our own experiences' stresses that the experiences were the writer's and colleagues' personal ones; 'his', 'theirs' and 'hers' cannot follow 'our'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. I understood why these highly (1) ___________ professionals remained in the closet. I was one of (2) _________. We could not deny our (3) __________ experiences and senses. Yet our training was in many ways diametrically (4) _________ to the information, experiences and beliefs we had accumulated. So we remained (5) _________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Diametrically opposite' means completely contrary: their training ran against what they had experienced and come to believe.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. I understood why these highly (1) ___________ professionals remained in the closet. I was one of (2) _________. We could not deny our (3) __________ experiences and senses. Yet our training was in many ways diametrically (4) _________ to the information, experiences and beliefs we had accumulated. So we remained (5) _________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Like those who 'remained in the closet', they 'remained quiet', that is silent, about it. 'Quite' is a different word, an adverb meaning fairly or completely.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘STORY’ is written as ‘ZSPUT’ and 'MUSIC' is written as 'DJTVN'. How will ‘PRINT’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is reversed and every letter moved one place forward: STORY → YROTS → ZSPUT and MUSIC → CISUM → DJTVN. So PRINT → TNIRP → UOJSQ.

questions.text: If ‘+’ means ‘×’, ‘÷’ means ‘-’, ‘-’ means ‘+’, and ‘×‘ means ‘÷’. Which of the following will be the value of the expression? 12 + 5 - 24 × 3 ÷ 5
questions.explanation: After replacing the signs: 12 × 5 + 24 ÷ 3 − 5 = 60 + 8 − 5 = 63.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question marks (?) in the given series? 101, 110, 122, 137, ? , 176, ?
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 96 × 8 + 27 ÷ 6 - 12 = 162
questions.explanation: After interchanging × and ÷: 96 ÷ 8 + 27 × 6 − 12 = 12 + 162 − 12 = 162.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Naughty 2 Nasty 3 Nail 4 Name 5 Natural
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Nail (3), Name (4), Nasty (2), Natural (5), Naughty (1). All begin 'Na', so the third letters, i, m, s, t, u, decide the order.

questions.text: There are seven people in a family. A is married to C. A has two children, B and E. A is the mother of B and E. B is the wife of L. P is the wife of E. L has one daughter G. E has one daughter K. How is C related to K ?
questions.explanation: A is the mother of B and E and is married to C, so C is their father. P is E's wife, so E is K's father and C is K's father's father. (The family described has eight members, not seven; the relation is unaffected.)

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Ludo : Dice :: Cricket : ?
questions.explanation: Ludo is played with dice; cricket is played with a bat.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter-cluster series? CC, XD, SE, NF, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move 5 places back, wrapping round after A: C, X, S, N, I. The second letters run C, D, E, F, G. The next cluster is IG.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question marks (?) in the given series? 1, 3, 6, 10, ?, ?, 28, 36, 45, 55
Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? FJOT, GIPS, ?, IGRQ, JFSP
questions.explanation: The first letters run F, G, H, I, J; the second J, I, H, G, F; the third O, P, Q, R, S; the fourth T, S, R, Q, P. The missing cluster is HHQR.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 34 : 5 :: 13 : 2 :: 27 : ?
questions.explanation: The first number is 7 times the second, minus 1: 5 × 7 − 1 = 34 and 2 × 7 − 1 = 13. Since 27 = 4 × 7 − 1, the answer is 4.

questions.text: Five people P, Q, R, S, and T are sitting in a straight row facing North. P is sitting to the immediate right of S. S is sitting between T and P. Q is sitting at the extreme left of the row. R is sitting to the immediate right of Q. Who is sitting between Q and T?
questions.explanation: Q is at the left end with R immediately to Q's right; S sits between T and P with P on S's right, so the row from the left is Q, R, T, S, P. R sits between Q and T.

questions.text: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. F is an immediate neighbour of A. D sits second to the right of E. B is an immediate neighbour of E and sits second to the right of C. F sits second to the right of D. A is not an immediate neighbour of E. Who sit between D and C from the right of D?
questions.explanation: Going round to the right from E, the order is E, B, D, A, F, C: D is second to the right of E, F second to the right of D, and B, next to E, is second to the right of C. Had B sat on E's other side, C would take the seat between D and F and A would end up next to E. Going right from D, A and F sit between D and C.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Denmark : Copenhagen :: Kenya : ?
questions.explanation: Copenhagen is the capital of Denmark; Nairobi is the capital of Kenya.

questions.text: In a certain language, TRAVEL is coded as GIZEVO, POLICY is coded as KLORXB, how will FAMILY be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on): TRAVEL → GIZEVO and POLICY → KLORXB. So FAMILY → UZNROB.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some silks are cottons. All cottons are jutes. Some jutes are not silks. Conclusions: 1. Some jutes are silks. 2. All silks are jutes. 3. All cottons are silks.
questions.explanation: The silks that are cottons are also jutes, so some jutes are silks (1). Nothing says that every silk is a jute or that every cotton is a silk, so 2 and 3 do not follow.

questions.text: ______ is the first state in India which has made roof top rainwater harvesting structure compulsory to all the houses across the state.
questions.explanation: A Tamil Nadu law of 2003 made rooftop rainwater harvesting structures compulsory for all buildings in the state, with penalties for defaulters; NCERT's Class 10 geography book names it the first state to do so.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In ______ the Muslim League had moved a resolution demanding “Independent States” for Muslims in the north-western and eastern areas of the country.
questions.explanation: The Muslim League's Lahore Resolution of March 1940 demanded 'independent states' for Muslims in the north-western and eastern regions of the country.

questions.text: The __________, 2019 is an Act of the Parliament of India criminalising triple talaq.
options: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
questions.explanation: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 makes instant triple talaq (talaq-e-biddat) void and illegal and punishes it with up to three years in prison.

questions.text: In its first phase, The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act initially covered how many districts before it was extended?
questions.explanation: NREGA came into force in 200 of the most backward districts on 2 February 2006; it was extended to 130 more districts in 2007 and to every rural district from 1 April 2008.

questions.text: Identify the correct statement with respect to Earth.
options: The diameter of the equator increases till the poles.
The radius of earth increases from the poles to the equator.
The diameter of earth decreases from the poles to the equator.
The radius of earth decreases from the poles to the equator.
questions.explanation: The Earth is slightly flattened at the poles and bulges at the equator, so its radius grows from about 6,357 km at the poles to about 6,378 km at the equator.

questions.text: Which Sub-Section of Fundamental Duties talks about the duty to cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired our national struggle for freedom?
questions.explanation: Article 51A lists the Fundamental Duties; clause (b) is the duty to cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom. Clause (a) is to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.

questions.text: __________ are foreign currency assets held by the central banks of countries.
questions.explanation: Foreign exchange reserves are the foreign-currency assets a central bank holds (India's, held by the RBI, also include gold, SDRs and its reserve position in the IMF).

questions.text: In Cricket, what is the distance between two wickets?
questions.explanation: The two sets of stumps stand 22 yards (20.12 m) apart, the length of the pitch.

questions.text: Which among the following festivals is also known as the festival of winter season?
questions.explanation: Gaan-Ngai (Chakan Gaan-Ngai), the winter post-harvest festival of the Zeliangrong Nagas, chiefly of Manipur, has a name usually glossed as 'winter festival' ('gaan', winter or the dry season; 'ngai', festival). Moatsu is the Ao Nagas' festival after sowing, Wangala the Garos' harvest festival and Chapchar Kut the Mizos' spring festival.

questions.text: The second phase of green revolution in India existed from ______________.
questions.explanation: In the first phase of the Green Revolution (mid-1960s to mid-1970s) high-yielding seeds were used mainly in the richer states such as Punjab; in the second phase, mid-1970s to mid-1980s, they spread to more states and more crops.

questions.text: Inamgaon village is located in which state of India?
questions.explanation: Inamgaon, a Chalcolithic farming settlement of the Jorwe culture, lies on the Ghod river in Pune district, Maharashtra.

questions.text: What is a group of industries that tend to come together to make use of the advantages offered by the urban centers known as ?
questions.explanation: Agglomeration economies are the savings firms make by clustering in and around a city, where they share its markets, banks, transport, labour and services.

questions.text: Whom has Samir Venkatapathy Kamat replaced as the new Chairman of Defence Research and Development Organisation in August 2022??
questions.explanation: Samir V Kamat succeeded G Satheesh Reddy as Chairman of DRDO in August 2022; Reddy was made scientific adviser to the Defence Minister.

questions.text: Zo Mal Lok, is the famous dance associated with which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Zo-Mal-Lok is a Lepcha folk dance of Sikkim that acts out the sowing, reaping and harvesting of paddy.

questions.text: Where does hydrarch succession take place?
questions.explanation: Hydrarch succession begins in water or wet areas and moves from hydric towards mesic conditions; xerarch succession begins in dry areas.

questions.text: The period of first five year plan was between__________.
questions.explanation: India's First Five-Year Plan ran from 1951 to 1956 and gave priority to agriculture.

questions.text: Gopal Prasad Dubey won Padma Shri in which dance form?
questions.explanation: Gopal Prasad Dubey of Seraikela, Jharkhand, a leading exponent of Seraikela Chhau, received the Padma Shri in 2012.

questions.text: In India, the Executive power of the state is vested in ______.
questions.explanation: Article 154 vests the executive power of a state in the Governor, who exercises it directly or through officers subordinate to him.

questions.text: Which of the following state won the maximum number of silver medals in the 2015 National Games of India?
questions.explanation: At the 2015 National Games, held in Kerala, the host state won more silver medals than any other team (over 45, against Haryana's 40); Madhya Pradesh and Goa won far fewer.

questions.text: Which political leader succeeded Bandhu Tirkey to become Member of Legislative Assembly from Mandar, Jharkhand in June 2022?
questions.explanation: Shilpi Neha Tirkey of the Congress won the Mandar by-election in June 2022; the seat fell vacant when her father, Bandhu Tirkey, was disqualified after his conviction in a disproportionate-assets case.

questions.text: Compound interest of Rs.21,515 is received on sum of Rs.65,000 in a period of three years. What was the rate of interest on which the sum was being compounded annually?
Mona purchased two handbags for Rs.1,500 each. She sold these bags, gaining 8% on one bag and loss 4% on the other. Find her gain or loss percent in the whole transaction.
questions.explanation: The bags sell for 1,500 × 1.08 = ₹1,620 and 1,500 × 0.96 = ₹1,440, ₹3,060 in all against a cost of ₹3,000: a gain of ₹60, or 2%.

questions.text: A vegetable seller has a faulty weight of 2 kg which is 100g less than the actual weight. He sold 2 kg of potatoes to a customer using the same faulty weight for Rs.44. The cost price of potatoes to the seller was Rs.18 per kg. How much profit did he earn on selling the potatoes?
questions.explanation: The faulty '2 kg' weight weighs only 1.9 kg, so the customer got 1.9 kg, which cost the seller 1.9 × 18 = ₹34.20. Profit = 44 − 34.20 = ₹9.80.

questions.text: Umesh and Ramesh can complete a work in 28 and 21 days, respectively. Starting with Umesh, they work on alternate days. In how many days will the work be completed?
questions.explanation: Take the work as 84 units: Umesh does 3 a day and Ramesh 4, so each two-day pair does 7. 84 ÷ 7 = 12 pairs, which finish the work exactly at the end of day 24.

questions.text: Find the average of all prime numbers up to 40.(Correct to 2 decimal places)

In a sports club, 86% of the members are men and 14% of the members are women. If the average age of the men is 25 years and the average age of the women is 35 years, then what is the average age (in years) of all the members?
By selling an article for Rs.880, a shopkeeper gains 10%. Due to reduction on sales, he allows a discount of 25% on previous selling price. His gain/loss percentage during the sale is:
questions.explanation: The cost is 880 ÷ 1.1 = ₹800. The sale price is 880 × 0.75 = ₹660, a loss of ₹140, which is 140/800 = 17.5%.

questions.text: The length of a train is 150 metres. In 3 seconds, it passes a man moving at a speed of 2 km/h in the same direction as the train. Determine the train's speed.
questions.explanation: The relative speed is 150/3 = 50 m/s = 50 × 18/5 = 180 km/h. As the train and the man move the same way, the train's speed is 180 + 2 = 182 km/h.

questions.text: In an election between two candidates, the candidate getting 70% of the votes polled is elected by a majority of 16,000 votes. The number of votes polled in favour of the winning candidate is:
questions.explanation: The majority is 70% − 30% = 40% of the votes = 16,000, so 40,000 votes were polled and the winner got 70% of them, 28,000.

questions.text: Prasad alone can complete a work in 144 days. How many people were required with the same efficiency as Prasad to complete the same work in 16 days?
questions.explanation: The work is 144 person-days, so 144 ÷ 16 = 9 people are needed.

questions.text: Find the volume of the hemisphere whose radius is 5.5 cm. (upto two decimal points)
Which of the following pairs of numbers are relatively prime?
questions.explanation: Two numbers are relatively prime when their HCF is 1. 39 = 3 × 13 and 68 = 2² × 17 share no factor; in each other pair both numbers are even.

questions.text: Prakash can swim at a speed of 32 km/h in upstream and 44 km/h in downstream. What is the speed of the current?
questions.explanation: Speed of the current = (downstream − upstream)/2 = (44 − 32)/2 = 6 km/h.

questions.text: Abdul’s salary is Rs.1,50,000 per month. He spends 10% of his salary on paying the school fees. He got an increment of 3% in his salary in the month of July, but the school fee was hiked by 5% the same month. What will be the net change in his saving in the month of July if the other expenditures are the same?
questions.explanation: The fees are 10% of ₹1,50,000 = ₹15,000. The salary rises by 3% of ₹1,50,000 = ₹4,500 and the fees by 5% of ₹15,000 = ₹750, so the saving rises by 4,500 − 750 = ₹3,750.

questions.text: When the same number is subtracted from each of 6, 8, 12 and 20, the resulting numbers are in proportion. The number subtracted is:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. We must learn to “negotiate” with every difficult situation in life.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'disagree': to negotiate is to talk with others in order to reach agreement, and 'disagree' is the only option that runs the other way ('discuss' and 'bargain' are near-synonyms and 'practice' is unrelated). In this sentence 'negotiate' really means 'deal with', which has no true opposite among the options.

questions.text: The sentence given below has one misspelt word. Spot the INCORRECTLY spelt word and select its correct spelling. Her husband's death left a vacum in her life.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'vacuum', with one 'c' and a double 'u'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The patient / look / a little more cheerful / this morning
questions.explanation: 'The patient' is a singular subject, so the simple present verb takes 's': 'The patient looks a little more cheerful this morning.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Recede
questions.explanation: To 'recede' is to move back or withdraw; its opposite is to 'advance', to move forward.

questions.text: Fill in the blank in the following sentence using the ANTONYM of the word given in the brackets. Can you _____ the UNO cards on the table? (gather)
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'gather' (bring together) is 'spread' (lay out over an area): 'Can you spread the UNO cards on the table?' 'Collect' is a synonym of 'gather'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The husband “promised the earth” to his wife.
questions.explanation: To 'promise the earth' is to promise far more than one can possibly give.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Proficient
questions.explanation: 'Proficient' means competent or expert: 'skilful'. 'Inadequate' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'marriage', with 'ia' before the 'ge'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. It is believed that God is _________.
questions.explanation: 'Omnipresent' means present everywhere at once, as God is believed to be. 'Omnivorous' means eating both plants and animals.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Hades is the god of the underworld and “wealth” in Greek mythology.
questions.explanation: 'Wealth' means 'riches': Hades ruled the underworld and the riches beneath the earth. 'Debts' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The enthusiastic readers are “eagerly waiting of the quick” completion of her forthcoming novel.
questions.explanation: The verb 'wait' takes 'for' before what is awaited: 'eagerly waiting for the quick completion of her forthcoming novel'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. He had _________ (Enough) time to finish the task.
questions.explanation: 'Enough' means as much as is needed: 'sufficient'. 'Insufficient' is its opposite.

questions.text: Choose the appropriate meaning of the underlying idiom. She wants to reach the target “by hook or by crook.”
options: By one or the other means
questions.explanation: 'By hook or by crook' means by any means at all, fair or unfair.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. Sea levels “have been risen” all around the world threatening natural calamities like tsunamis, floods, etc.
questions.explanation: 'Rise' takes no object, so it has no passive ('have been risen'); the present perfect continuous 'have been rising' describes a rise that began in the past and is still going on.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. We all must agree on the fact that life is “fragile”.
questions.explanation: 'Fragile' means easily broken or weak; of the options 'healthy' is its opposite, while 'infirm' and 'weak' are synonyms.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There are over 9000 species of birds on this planet (1) ________of which over 1360 are found in India alone. 81 species of birds (2)________endemic to India. Because birds are found everywhere, and in all (3)________zones, their sizes, shapes and wings are (4)________ according to the needs of their habitat. For instance, eagles and hawks have massive soaring wings with primary feather that (5)________out and allow them to soar high in the sky.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Out of which' picks a part from the whole: of the more than 9,000 species, over 1,360 are found in India.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There are over 9000 species of birds on this planet (1) ________of which over 1360 are found in India alone. 81 species of birds (2)________endemic to India. Because birds are found everywhere, and in all (3)________zones, their sizes, shapes and wings are (4)________ according to the needs of their habitat. For instance, eagles and hawks have massive soaring wings with primary feather that (5)________out and allow them to soar high in the sky.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'species of birds' and a present fact take 'are': '81 species of birds are endemic to India'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There are over 9000 species of birds on this planet (1) ________of which over 1360 are found in India alone. 81 species of birds (2)________endemic to India. Because birds are found everywhere, and in all (3)________zones, their sizes, shapes and wings are (4)________ according to the needs of their habitat. For instance, eagles and hawks have massive soaring wings with primary feather that (5)________out and allow them to soar high in the sky.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Birds live in all 'climatic' zones, from hot to cold, which is why their sizes, shapes and wings differ.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There are over 9000 species of birds on this planet (1) ________of which over 1360 are found in India alone. 81 species of birds (2)________endemic to India. Because birds are found everywhere, and in all (3)________zones, their sizes, shapes and wings are (4)________ according to the needs of their habitat. For instance, eagles and hawks have massive soaring wings with primary feather that (5)________out and allow them to soar high in the sky.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Their bodies are 'adapted', that is suited, to their habitats; 'adopted' means taken up as one's own.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There are over 9000 species of birds on this planet (1) ________of which over 1360 are found in India alone. 81 species of birds (2)________endemic to India. Because birds are found everywhere, and in all (3)________zones, their sizes, shapes and wings are (4)________ according to the needs of their habitat. For instance, eagles and hawks have massive soaring wings with primary feather that (5)________out and allow them to soar high in the sky.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The primary feathers 'spread out', opening wide, so that eagles and hawks can soar.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? MRFL, RYKS, ?, BMUG, GTZN
questions.explanation: Each letter moves forward through the alphabet, wrapping round from Z to A: the first letters by 5 (M, R, W, B, G), the second by 7 (R, Y, F, M, T), the third by 5 (F, K, P, U, Z) and the fourth by 7 (L, S, Z, G, N). The missing cluster is WFPZ.

questions.text: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 2, 10, 30, ?, 130
Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? YWUS, RPNL, ? , DBZX, WUSQ
questions.explanation: Within each cluster the letters go 2 places back (Y, W, U, S), and the first letters go 7 places back from one cluster to the next, wrapping round from A to Z: Y, R, K, D, W. The missing cluster is KIGE.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 grape 2 grown 3 grass 4 gross 5 grind
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: grape (1), grass (3), grind (5), gross (4), grown (2). 'Grap' comes before 'gras', 'gra' before 'gri' and 'gro', and 'gros' before 'grow'.

questions.text: Which two numbers, from the given options, should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 95 ÷ 19 × 112 ÷ (4 × 4 + 3) + 5 = 24
Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term. 80 : 17 :: ? : 13 :: 185 : 38
questions.explanation: The first number divided by 5, plus 1, gives the second: 80 ÷ 5 + 1 = 17 and 185 ÷ 5 + 1 = 38. So ? ÷ 5 + 1 = 13 gives ? = 60.

questions.text: ‘A + B’ means ‘B is the mother of A’; ‘A # B’ means ‘B is the sister of A’; ‘A @ B’ means ‘B is the brother of A’; ‘A % B’ means ‘B is the daughter of A’; If A # B @ C % D + E, then how is E related to A?
questions.explanation: B is A's sister and C is B's brother, so C is A's brother. D is C's daughter and E is D's mother, so E is C's wife: A's brother's wife.

questions.text: If signs ‘+’ and ‘-’ and numbers 14 and 6 are used interchangeably, then which of the following equation would be correct?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs and the numbers, 6 + 14 × 2 − 18 becomes 14 − 6 × 2 + 18 = 14 − 12 + 18 = 20. The other three give 8, 14 and 106 instead of 4, 30 and 20.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 109, 122, 148, ?, 239, 304
questions.explanation: The differences are multiples of 13: +13, +26, +39, +52, +65. So 148 + 39 = 187, and 187 + 52 = 239.

questions.text: Seven people P,Q,R,S,T,U and V are sitting in a straight line adjacent to each other, facing the north (not necessarily in the given order). R is sitting to the immediate right of U. U is sitting third to the right of P. There are only four persons sitting between P and T. Q is the immediate neighbour of V and U. Who can be the immediate neighbour of S?
questions.explanation: R sits immediately right of U, so Q, who sits next to both U and V, is on U's left with V to Q's left, and P, third to the left of U, completes the run P, V, Q, U, R. With four people between P and T, the line is either P V Q U R T S or S P V Q U R T, so S's neighbour is T or P, and only T is among the options.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘MOBILE’ is coded as ‘18’ and ‘TELEVISION’ is coded as 30. How will ‘COMPUTER’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded as three times its number of letters: MOBILE (6) → 18 and TELEVISION (10) → 30, so COMPUTER (8) → 24.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'GATE' is written as ‘TZGV’ and 'PASS' is written as 'KZHH'. How will 'HOME' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y and so on): GATE → TZGV and PASS → KZHH, so HOME → SLNV.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some beans are potatoes. All carrots are potatoes. All gourds are potatoes. Conclusions: I. Some gourds are beans. II. Some carrots are gourds. III. Some potatoes are gourds.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: All gourds are potatoes, so some potatoes are gourds (III). The beans that are potatoes need not be gourds, and the carrots and gourds may be separate groups of potatoes, so I and II do not follow.

questions.text: Seven girls Rita, Sita, Gita, Mita, Anita, Binita, and Sunita are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Rita and Gita are not sitting next to each other. Sunita is sitting between Binita and Mita. Mita is sitting to the immediate left of Rita. Sita is sitting between Anita and Gita. Who is sitting to the immediate left of Anita?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, Mita is to Rita's immediate left, Sunita (between Binita and Mita) to Mita's left, and then Binita. Sita sits between Anita and Gita in the three seats left, and Gita cannot be next to Rita, so going on round to the left come Gita, Sita and Anita, and Rita is to Anita's immediate left.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/ number of consonants / vowels in the word) Binocular : View :: Spanner : ?
questions.explanation: Binoculars are used to view distant things, and a spanner is used to grip and turn nuts and bolts: each pair is a tool and what it does.

questions.text: The term ‘Shido’ is used in Judo for ________.
questions.explanation: In judo a 'shido' is a minor penalty for a small infringement, such as passivity or a false attack; the major penalty is 'hansoku-make', disqualification.

questions.text: Who resigned as Chief minister of Maharashtra following Supreme Court of India not admitting the stay petition of Shiv Sena against the Motion of no confidence in June 2022?
questions.explanation: Uddhav Thackeray resigned as Chief Minister of Maharashtra on 29 June 2022, after the Supreme Court declined to stay the Governor's call for a floor test in the Assembly; Eknath Shinde was sworn in the next day.

questions.text: __________ is an indication of the total borrowings needed by the government.
questions.explanation: The fiscal deficit, total expenditure less total receipts other than borrowings, is the gap the government must fill by borrowing, so it indicates its total borrowing requirement.

questions.text: Budget is a statement of estimated receipts and expenditures of the government in respect of every ___________.
questions.explanation: The Budget, the 'annual financial statement' of Article 112, sets out the government's estimated receipts and expenditure for each financial year, which in India runs from 1 April to 31 March.

questions.text: Shri Bhagwant Mann became the Chief Minister of _____ state/union territory of India in March 2022.
questions.explanation: Bhagwant Mann of the Aam Aadmi Party was sworn in as Chief Minister of Punjab in March 2022, after the party won the state's Assembly election.

questions.text: Who was elected as the first woman speaker of Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly in March 2022?
questions.explanation: Ritu Khanduri Bhushan, BJP MLA from Kotdwar, was elected unopposed as Speaker of the Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly on 26 March 2022, the first woman to hold the post since the state was formed.

questions.text: Articles ___________ in Part VI of the Constitution deals with the organisation, composition, duration, officers, procedures, privileges, powers and so on of the state legislature.
questions.explanation: Chapter III of Part VI, Articles 168 to 212, deals with the state legislature: its constitution, duration, officers, conduct of business, privileges and legislative procedure.

questions.text: Mohiniyattam dance is performed by women in honour of the Hindu god __________ in his incarnation as the enchantress Mohini.
questions.explanation: Mohiniyattam, the classical dance of Kerala, takes its name from Mohini, the enchantress form taken by Vishnu, and is traditionally danced by women.

questions.text: Aryabhatta was India's first artificial satellite in space, launched in the year ______.
questions.explanation: Aryabhata, India's first satellite, built by ISRO, was launched from the Soviet Union on 19 April 1975.

questions.text: The first layer of earth’s atmosphere is ______.
questions.explanation: The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere, in which weather occurs; above it lie the stratosphere, the mesosphere and the thermosphere.

questions.text: Ganesh Chaturthi, celebrated in the honour of God Ganesh, is observed in the Hindu month of _________.
questions.explanation: Ganesh Chaturthi falls on the fourth day (chaturthi) of the bright half of the Hindu month of Bhadrapada, in August or September.

questions.text: The rate at which the Reserve Bank is ready to buy or rediscount bills of exchange or other commercial papers is called the ______. .
questions.explanation: The Bank Rate is the standard rate at which the Reserve Bank buys or rediscounts bills of exchange and other eligible commercial paper (Section 49 of the RBI Act, 1934). The repo and reverse repo rates apply to short-term lending and borrowing against government securities, and the CRR is a share of deposits kept with the RBI.

questions.text: NH₄Cl is the chemical formula for which of the following elements?
questions.explanation: NH₄Cl is ammonium chloride, a compound of the ammonium ion (NH₄⁺) and the chloride ion (Cl⁻), not an element. Silicon dioxide is SiO₂, potassium nitrate KNO₃ and carbonyl dichloride COCl₂.

questions.text: Which of the following city hosted the 2022 Commonwealth games?
questions.explanation: Birmingham, England, hosted the 2022 Commonwealth Games in July and August 2022. Gold Coast hosted the 2018 Games, Glasgow those of 2014 and Delhi those of 2010.

questions.text: How many Schedules are there in the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: The Constitution of India has 12 Schedules: it had eight when adopted, and amendments added the Ninth (1951), the Tenth (1985), and the Eleventh and Twelfth (1992).

questions.text: The Moth ki Masjid was built in the reign of ______ ruler.
questions.explanation: The Moth ki Masjid in south Delhi was built around 1505 by Miyan Bhoiya, wazir (chief minister) of Sultan Sikandar Lodi, who ruled from 1489 to 1517.

questions.text: In a school, there are 200 students. If the ratio of the number of boys and the number of girls is 9 : 1, then find the mean proportion between the number of boys and that of girls in the school.
questions.explanation: There are 200 × 9/10 = 180 boys and 20 girls, and their mean proportional is √(180 × 20) = √3600 = 60.

questions.text: Which number should be subtracted from 17, 30, 22 and 40 so that the obtained numbers may become proportional?

A company offers different types of discounts schemes. (i) Two successive discounts of 10% and 20%; (ii) Buy 1 get 1 free; (iii) Buy 5 get 3 free; (iv) Buy 5 get 6; Which scheme has the minimum discount percentage?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives (iv), reading 'Buy 5 get 6', which unlike (ii) and (iii) does not say 'free', as paying for 5 and getting 6: 1 free in 6 = 16.67%, the smallest. The others are (i) 1 − 0.9 × 0.8 = 28%, (ii) 1 free in 2 = 50% and (iii) 3 free in 8 = 37.5%.

questions.text: A thief noticing a policeman from a distance of 500 metres starts running at a speed of 8 km/h. The policeman chased him with a speed of 11 km/h. What is the distance run by the thief before he was caught? (Rounded off to two decimal places, if required)
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 11 − 8 = 3 km/h, so he closes the 0.5 km gap in 0.5/3 = 1/6 hour. In that time the thief runs 8 × 1/6 = 4/3 km = 1,333.33 metres.

questions.text: A person buys the stock of a company at Rs.12,000. If he sells that stock (a year later) he gets Rs.15,000. Determine the percentage profit earned.

A park had an average of 30 children playing on weekdays and an average of 60 children playing on weekends. Find the average number of children playing per day in the park for the month of June beginning with a Saturday.
questions.explanation: June has 30 days; starting on a Saturday, it has 5 Saturdays and 5 Sundays, so 10 weekend days and 20 weekdays. The average is (20 × 30 + 10 × 60)/30 = 1,200/30 = 40.

questions.text: The population of a town 3 years ago was 84000. Due to migration to cities, it decreases every year at the rate of 10 percent. The present population of the town is :
questions.explanation: After three years of 10% decrease: 84000 × 0.9³ = 84000 × 0.729 = 61236.

questions.text: The least value of 'a' for which the number 638a435 is completely divisible by 3 is:
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 3 when its digit sum is: 6 + 3 + 8 + a + 4 + 3 + 5 = 29 + a, and the least a that makes this a multiple of 3 is 1 (30).

questions.text: If 18 percent of A is equal to 40 percent of B, then what is the ratio of A : B?
The shopkeeper gave 50 percent discount on marked price of Rs.750. What will be the selling price ?
questions.explanation: A 50% discount on ₹750 leaves 750 × 0.5 = ₹375.

questions.text: If Ramesh walks at a speed of 15 km/h, instead of 12 km/h, he would have walked 2 km more in the same time. What is the actual distance (in km) travelled by Ramesh at 12 km/h in the same time?
questions.explanation: The extra 3 km/h covers the extra 2 km, so the time is 2/3 hour, and at 12 km/h he covers 12 × 2/3 = 8 km.

questions.text: Work done by two men is equal to work done by three women, and work done by five women is equal to work done by seven boys. If 16 men can finish a work in 2 days, then in how many days the work will be completed by two boys?
questions.explanation: 2 men = 3 women, so 1 man = 1.5 women; 5 women = 7 boys, so 1 woman = 1.4 boys and 1 man = 2.1 boys. The work is 16 × 2 = 32 man-days = 67.2 boy-days, so 2 boys take 33.6 days.

questions.text: The smallest number exactly divisible by 104, 78 and 260 is P. If P + 40 = Q², then what is the positive value of Q?
Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence. The officer was not aware of the “sedulous” espionage.
questions.explanation: 'Sedulous' means showing steady care and effort: 'diligent'. 'Sedate' (calm) and 'seduce' only look alike.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We may _______ an example or two.
questions.explanation: To 'cite' an example is to quote it in support of a point. 'Site' (a place), 'sight' (vision) and 'side' only sound alike.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. I have waiting / anxiously / for my / exam results.
questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous needs 'been': 'I have been waiting anxiously for my exam results.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Obedient
questions.explanation: 'Obedient' means willing to do as one is told; its opposite is 'disobedient'. 'Docile' and 'disciplined' are close in meaning, and 'meekness' is a noun.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The study of ancient writings and scriptures
questions.explanation: 'Palaeography' is the study of ancient writing and manuscripts. Alchemy was the forerunner of chemistry, geology is the study of the earth, and ornithology the study of birds.

questions.text: Select the correct idiom to substitute the underlined word segment in the following sentence. When the teacher asked him about the homework, he started “speaking vaguely to avoid talking about it” .
options: searching the bird in the bush
questions.explanation: To 'beat around the bush' is to avoid coming to the point by talking vaguely: 'he started beating around the bush'.

questions.text: Select the MISSPELT word.
questions.explanation: 'Farnish' is misspelt: the word is 'furnish'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence. Wordsworth wished to work on his poems in “solitude”.
questions.explanation: 'Solitude' is the state of being alone, away from others: 'seclusion'. 'Satiety' is the state of being full, and 'slumber' is sleep.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Rajiv “helps his friends of solve” real-life problems with several methods and approaches.
questions.explanation: 'Help' takes an object followed by 'to' and a verb (or the bare verb): 'helps his friends to solve'. 'Of', 'for' and 'in' cannot introduce the verb, and 'help' does not agree with 'Rajiv'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. The businessman agreed “to grease the palm of” the bank manager for a loan.
questions.explanation: To 'grease someone's palm' is to bribe them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. Late morning, we took a “stroll” along the beach.
questions.explanation: To 'stroll' is to walk in a slow, relaxed way: to 'saunter'. To scamper, sprint and jog are all to move quickly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The doctor instructed the patient to ______ up and down his house as an exercise.
questions.explanation: To 'walk up and down' a place is to walk back and forth in it, a light exercise a doctor might prescribe.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. It is surprising to see _________ (stale) apples available throughout the year.
questions.explanation: The bracketed 'stale' points to its opposite: what is surprising is 'fresh' apples all year round, apples being a seasonal fruit. 'Old' and 'musty' mean much the same as 'stale', and 'stuffy' is said of air or a room.

questions.text: Select the option in which all the words are spelt correctly.
options: My aunty arrivved at my home on the eve of Diwali.
My aunty arrived at my home on the eve of Diwali.
My aunty arived at my home on the eve of Diwali.
My aunty arriived at my home on the eve of Diwali.
questions.explanation: 'Arrive' has a double 'r' and a single 'i' and 'v': 'arrived'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. The curry was very ________ (distasteful). I ate it all.
questions.explanation: 'Delicious', very pleasant to taste, is the opposite of 'distasteful' and fits 'I ate it all'. 'Refined' means processed or elegant, 'enchanting' charming and 'intoxicating' causing drunkenness or excitement; none is the opposite of 'distasteful' said of food.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The set of relationships between people, (1) __________ their social position and roles, is referred to as society or human society. The people of a region, country, or even the (2) _________ world are referred to as a society. A society, as used in the sense of an organisation, is a group of people bound together by functional (3) _________, and may include qualities such as national or cultural identity, social solidarity, language or hierarchical organisation. Patterns of relationships between individuals who (4) __________ a common culture and institutions define human societies. A society, like other organisations or groups, permits its members to fulfil wants or wishes that they could not (5) _________ on their own.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Society is the set of relationships between people, 'including' their social position and roles: the positions and roles are part of what is described.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The set of relationships between people, (1) __________ their social position and roles, is referred to as society or human society. The people of a region, country, or even the (2) _________ world are referred to as a society. A society, as used in the sense of an organisation, is a group of people bound together by functional (3) _________, and may include qualities such as national or cultural identity, social solidarity, language or hierarchical organisation. Patterns of relationships between individuals who (4) __________ a common culture and institutions define human societies. A society, like other organisations or groups, permits its members to fulfil wants or wishes that they could not (5) _________ on their own.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Even the entire world' widens the series region, country, world to its fullest extent; 'absolute world' is not idiomatic, and 'illiterate' and 'primitive' make no sense here.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The set of relationships between people, (1) __________ their social position and roles, is referred to as society or human society. The people of a region, country, or even the (2) _________ world are referred to as a society. A society, as used in the sense of an organisation, is a group of people bound together by functional (3) _________, and may include qualities such as national or cultural identity, social solidarity, language or hierarchical organisation. Patterns of relationships between individuals who (4) __________ a common culture and institutions define human societies. A society, like other organisations or groups, permits its members to fulfil wants or wishes that they could not (5) _________ on their own.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: A society is bound together by functional 'interdependence', its members relying on one another for different needs. 'Mutualism' is a term from biology, and 'qualities' and 'exchange' do not fit 'bound together by functional'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The set of relationships between people, (1) __________ their social position and roles, is referred to as society or human society. The people of a region, country, or even the (2) _________ world are referred to as a society. A society, as used in the sense of an organisation, is a group of people bound together by functional (3) _________, and may include qualities such as national or cultural identity, social solidarity, language or hierarchical organisation. Patterns of relationships between individuals who (4) __________ a common culture and institutions define human societies. A society, like other organisations or groups, permits its members to fulfil wants or wishes that they could not (5) _________ on their own.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The members of a society 'share' a common culture and institutions; they do not oppose, protect or divide them.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The set of relationships between people, (1) __________ their social position and roles, is referred to as society or human society. The people of a region, country, or even the (2) _________ world are referred to as a society. A society, as used in the sense of an organisation, is a group of people bound together by functional (3) _________, and may include qualities such as national or cultural identity, social solidarity, language or hierarchical organisation. Patterns of relationships between individuals who (4) __________ a common culture and institutions define human societies. A society, like other organisations or groups, permits its members to fulfil wants or wishes that they could not (5) _________ on their own.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: A society lets its members fulfil wants they could not 'accomplish', that is achieve, on their own.

questions.text: In a code language, 'ECTOPIC' is written as ‘71’ and ‘EDIFY’ is written as ‘49’. How will 'ECONOMY' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded as the sum of its letters' places in the alphabet: ECTOPIC = 5 + 3 + 20 + 15 + 16 + 9 + 3 = 71 and EDIFY = 5 + 4 + 9 + 6 + 25 = 49. So ECONOMY = 5 + 3 + 15 + 14 + 15 + 13 + 25 = 90.

questions.text: Five people Q, R, S, T and U are sitting in a straight row, facing north. S is an immediate neighbour of both T and R. R is an immediate neighbour of Q. If Q is at the extreme right end of the row, then who is sitting at the extreme left end?
questions.explanation: Q is at the right end with R next to Q, and S sits next to both R and T, so from the right the row runs Q, R, S, T. That leaves U at the left end: U, T, S, R, Q.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘AGENT’ is coded as ZHGOG and ‘CHAIR’ is coded as XICJI. How will ‘FAITH’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters become their opposite letters (A↔Z, T↔G), the second moves +1, the third +2 and the fourth +1: AGENT → ZHGOG and CHAIR → XICJI. So FAITH → UBKUS.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. CAPABLE : PACELBA :: AUCTION : CUANOIT: : CAREFUL : ?
questions.explanation: The first three letters are reversed and then the last four: CAP ABLE → PAC ELBA and AUC TION → CUA NOIT. So CAR EFUL → RAC LUFE: RACLUFE.

questions.text: ‘A + B’ means ‘B is the father of A’ ‘A – B’ means ‘B is the mother of A’ ‘A # B’ means ‘B is the sister of A’ ‘A & B’ means ‘B is the wife of A’ If A # B + C & D – E, then how is E related to A?
questions.explanation: B is A's sister and C is B's father, so C is A's father; D is C's wife, so A's mother; and E is D's mother, so A's mother's mother.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Distinct 2 Discipline 3 Different 4 Distinguish 5 Disregard
questions.explanation: 'Dif-' comes before 'dis-', so Different is first; then Discipline (disc-), Disregard (disr-), Distinct and Distinguish ('distinc-' before 'disting-'): 3, 2, 5, 1, 4.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term. 8 : 520 :: 9 : ? :: 10 : 1010
questions.explanation: Each number is cubed and added to itself: 8³ + 8 = 520 and 10³ + 10 = 1010. So 9³ + 9 = 729 + 9 = 738.

questions.text: Which of the two numbers (Not digits) should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct? 42 ÷ 3 × 6 + 9 - 7 = 23
questions.explanation: After interchanging 3 and 6: 42 ÷ 6 × 3 + 9 − 7 = 7 × 3 + 2 = 23.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All tops are bottoms. All pullovers are bottoms. All bottoms are pants. Conclusions: I. All pullovers are pants. II. All pants are tops. III. Some pants are pullovers.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: Every pullover is a bottom and every bottom is a pant, so all pullovers are pants (I), and so some pants are pullovers (III). Nothing makes every pant a top, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? ZDFA, CIMJ, ?, ISAB, LXHK
questions.explanation: The first letters move +3 (Z, C, F, I, L), the second +5 (D, I, N, S, X), the third +7 (F, M, T, A, H) and the fourth +9 (A, J, S, B, K), wrapping round after Z. The missing cluster is FNTS.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. PLC : EOT :: DLG : IOH :: HCN : ?
questions.explanation: The cluster is reversed and its letters moved +2, +3 and +4: PLC → CLP → EOT and DLG → GLD → IOH. So HCN → NCH → PFL.

questions.text: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 4, 36, 144, ?, 900, 1764
questions.explanation: The terms are the squares of 2, 6, 12, 20, 30 and 42 (1 × 2, 2 × 3, 3 × 4 and so on), so the missing term is 20² = 400.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 13, 30, 47, ?, 81, 98, 115, 132
questions.explanation: Each term is 17 more than the one before: 47 + 17 = 64, and 64 + 17 = 81.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter-cluster series? EE, GF, JH, OK, VO, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move +2, +3, +5, +7 (the primes), so +11 next: V + 11 = G, wrapping round after Z. The second letters move +1, +2, +3, +4, so +5 next: O + 5 = T. The next cluster is GT.

questions.text: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Arun is the immediate neighbour of Krishna and Boby. Shama is the immediate neighbour of Ajay and Suman. Ajay is to the immediate left of Boby. Who is to the immediate right of Boby?
questions.explanation: Arun and Ajay both sit next to Boby, so they are his two neighbours. Ajay is to his immediate left, which leaves Arun to his immediate right (the table runs Krishna, Arun, Boby, Ajay, Shama, Suman).

questions.text: If ‘A’ means ‘subtraction’, ‘B’ means ‘division’, ‘C’ means ‘multiplication’, and ‘D‘ means ‘addition’, then what will be the value of following expression? 28 A 80 B 16 C 5 D 21
In which among the following states did Priyanka Gandhi Vadra joined "Bharat Jodo Yatra" for first time in November 2022?
questions.explanation: Priyanka Gandhi Vadra first walked in the Bharat Jodo Yatra on 24 November 2022, from Borgaon in Khandwa district, Madhya Pradesh, the day after the march entered the state from Maharashtra.

questions.text: In India, _________ was the final approval authority for the five year plans.
questions.explanation: The National Development Council, chaired by the Prime Minister with the Chief Ministers of the states among its members, gave the final approval to each Five-Year Plan drafted by the Planning Commission.

questions.text: Which of the following monetary instruments of RBI is qualitative in nature?
questions.explanation: Moral suasion, persuading banks through advice and appeals, is a qualitative (selective) tool. The cash reserve ratio, the bank rate and open market operations are quantitative tools that act on the total volume of credit.

questions.text: The Arjuna award started in which year?
questions.explanation: The Arjuna Award, the Government of India's award for outstanding performance in sport, was instituted in 1961.

questions.text: What is the phenomenon of heavy showers with thunder occurring in the West Bengal region during the hot weather season called?
questions.explanation: Kalbaisakhi, the 'calamity of the month of Baisakh', are the violent evening thunderstorms with heavy showers of West Bengal and Assam in the hot weather season. Mango showers are the pre-monsoon showers of Kerala and Karnataka, and the loo is the hot, dry wind of the northern plains.

questions.text: The Shumang Leela festival is associated with which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Shumang Leela, a traditional form of theatre performed in an open courtyard, belongs to Manipur.

questions.text: ____________ Veda, shortest among the four Vedas, holds a divine status in Hindu tradition and is a collection of melodies and chants.
questions.explanation: The Sama Veda is a collection of melodies (samans) for chanting at sacrifices; nearly all of its verses are taken from the Rig Veda.

questions.text: Which state won the maximum number of bronze medals in the 36th edition of the National Games 2022 of India?
questions.explanation: At the 36th National Games in Gujarat (September-October 2022) Maharashtra won 39 gold, 38 silver and 63 bronze medals, the most bronzes and the most medals overall; Services topped the table on golds.

questions.text: Only the ________ can make the proclamation of emergency in India.
questions.explanation: Only the President can proclaim an emergency: a national emergency under Article 352, the failure of constitutional machinery in a state under Article 356 and a financial emergency under Article 360.

questions.text: What is the name of the first woman inspector general to head the Rapid Action Force of the Central Reserve Police Force?
questions.explanation: Annie Abraham, of the CRPF's first batch of women officers (1987), was named Inspector General of its Rapid Action Force in November 2022, the first woman to head it; Seema Dhundiya was made IG of the Bihar sector at the same time.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In 1877, Viceroy Lytton organised a Durbar to acknowledge ______ as the Empress of India.
questions.explanation: Lord Lytton's Delhi Durbar of 1 January 1877 proclaimed Queen Victoria Empress of India (Kaiser-i-Hind).

questions.text: What do you call organisms made of more than one cell?
questions.explanation: Organisms made of many cells are multicellular; those of a single cell, such as amoeba, are unicellular.

questions.text: Which Part of the Constitution of India deals with the powers and functioning of the Supreme Court of India?
questions.explanation: Part V (The Union) deals with the Supreme Court in Chapter IV, 'The Union Judiciary' (Articles 124-147). Part VI covers the states, Part X the scheduled and tribal areas and Part XI relations between the Union and the states.

questions.text: Bhama Kalapam is the classical dance-drama associated with which Indian classical dance form?
questions.explanation: Bhama Kalapam, the dance-drama about Satyabhama attributed to Siddhendra Yogi, is the best-known work of the Kuchipudi tradition.

questions.text: Who received a gold medal for choreography for the Ballet Folklorico of Mexico?
questions.explanation: Mrinalini Sarabhai, the Bharatanatyam and Kathakali dancer who founded the Darpana Academy in Ahmedabad, was given a gold medal by the Mexican government for her choreography for the Ballet Folklórico of Mexico.

questions.text: People of what age and above are included while calculating adult literacy rate?
questions.explanation: The adult literacy rate is the share of people aged 15 and above who can read and write with understanding, the definition UNESCO uses.

questions.text: Which of the following is "NOT" a major wheat producing state?
questions.explanation: Goa grows little wheat; its main food crop is rice. Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Haryana are among India's leading wheat producers.

questions.text: The Government’s flagship programme ‘Make in India’ completed how many years on September 25, 2022?
questions.explanation: Make in India was launched on 25 September 2014, so on 25 September 2022 it completed 8 years.

questions.text: Items such as cars, clothes, chocolates, which are directly sold to the consumers are :
questions.explanation: Goods such as cars, clothes and food items, bought and used by individuals, are private goods: anyone who does not pay can be kept from using them. Public goods, such as national defence, benefit everyone at once.

questions.text: In an election between two candidates, the one who gets 75% of the votes is elected by a majority of 520 votes. What is the total number of votes polled?
