questions.explanation: The winner gets 75% and the loser 25%, so the majority is 50% of the votes polled: 50% is 520 votes, and the total is 1040.

questions.text: Kiran lent Rs.5,00,000 to Kishore, which gets compounded annually at the rate of 12% per annum. Kishore lent the amount to Kavya on simple interest at the rate of 15% per annum. What is the difference in the interest earned by Kiran and Kishore after 3 years?

If Akash can do a piece of work in 63 days and Disha can do the same work in 84 days. They worked together for 12 days and after this Disha left the work and Akash completed the remaining work, then find the total number of days required to finish the work.
questions.explanation: Together they do 1/63 + 1/84 = 7/252 = 1/36 of the work a day, so in 12 days they finish 1/3 of it. Akash does the other 2/3 in 2/3 × 63 = 42 days: 12 + 42 = 54 days in all.

questions.text: X bought a dozen pencils for a total of Rs 60 and 20 pens for Rs 200. Find the total average cost of the stationery X bought.
The marks obtained by seven students are 70, 85, 95, 86, 74, 83 and 67. What is the average marks obtained by them?
A shopkeeper gives a discount of 12% on the marked price of an item. If the selling price of item is Rs.13,200, then what is the marked price of the item?
questions.explanation: The selling price is 88% of the marked price: 13,200 ÷ 0.88 = ₹15,000.

questions.text: Calculate the area of a rhombus with diagonals of 7 cm and 6 cm.
questions.explanation: The area of a rhombus is half the product of its diagonals: ½ × 7 × 6 = 21 cm².

questions.text: Reeta goes to office from home at a speed of 40 km/h. If she return to home from office at a speed of 60 km/h, then what is her average speed?
questions.explanation: For equal distances the average speed is 2 × 40 × 60/(40 + 60) = 4800/100 = 48 km/h.

questions.text: The marked price of an A.C. is ₹48,000. The shopkeeper allows a discount of 12% and gains 10%. If no discount is allowed, find his gain percentage.
questions.explanation: The selling price is 48,000 × 0.88 = ₹42,240, so the cost price is 42,240 ÷ 1.1 = ₹38,400. Selling at ₹48,000 gives a gain of 9,600/38,400 = 25%.

questions.text: The speed of a boat in still water is 50 percent more than it's speed in upstream. If the boat takes 20 minutes to reach point Q from point P in downstream, then how much time will it take to reach point P from point Q in upstream?
questions.explanation: With boat speed b and stream speed s, b = 1.5(b − s) gives b = 3s, so the upstream speed is 2s and the downstream speed 4s. Upstream is half as fast, so the trip takes 2 × 20 = 40 minutes.

questions.text: If a natural number when divided by 4,5 and 6 leaves a remainder 3 in each case, then what is the smallest possible three digit natural number?
questions.explanation: LCM(4, 5, 6) = 60, so the number is 60k + 3. The smallest three-digit one is 60 × 2 + 3 = 123.

questions.text: A vendor sells 40 percent of oranges he had and throws away 10 percent of the remainder. Next day he sells 50 percent of the remaining and throws away the rest. What percent of his oranges does the vendor throw?
questions.explanation: Of 100 oranges he sells 40 and throws away 10% of the other 60, that is 6. Of the 54 left he sells 27 and throws away 27, so he throws away 6 + 27 = 33, or 33%.

questions.text: Raju buys an old mobile for Rs.3,200 and spends Rs.800 on its repairs. If he sells the mobile for Rs.4,800, his gain per cent is:
If l∶m=2∶7,m∶n=3∶4 and n∶k=14∶5, then l∶m∶n∶k is:
questions.explanation: Make the shared terms equal: l : m = 2 : 7 = 6 : 21, m : n = 3 : 4 = 21 : 28 and n : k = 14 : 5 = 28 : 10. So l : m : n : k = 6 : 21 : 28 : 10.

questions.text: A Bluetooth speaker is sold for ₹3,500 cash, or ₹1,000 cash down payment and the balance in 3 equal annual instalments. If rate of interest is 12.5% per annum and interest is compounding annually, then find the amount of instalment. (correct to 2 decimal places)
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Jovial
questions.explanation: 'Jovial' means cheerful and good-humoured; its opposite is 'gloomy'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'cancellation'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the following sentence. The accident made his face look “horrible”.
questions.explanation: 'Horrible' means very unpleasant or shocking to look at; its opposite is 'pleasant'. 'Ugly' and 'frightful' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Education, no doubt, _______ bring about the all-round development of a child.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'education' needs 'aims', and 'aim' takes 'to' before a verb: 'Education, no doubt, aims to bring about the all-round development of a child.' ('Aim at' would need 'bringing'.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Earned
questions.explanation: To have 'earned' something is to have 'gained' it by work or merit.

questions.text: Select the appropriate idiom that can replace the underlined phrase in the following sentence. He is “straightforward and honest” and that’s why everyone appreciates him.
questions.explanation: A person who is 'an open book' hides nothing and is easy to understand, which fits 'straightforward and honest'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. Locating directions through the location of stars and constellations is a ________ (handy) way at the sea.
questions.explanation: 'Handy' means convenient and 'useful': reading the stars is a useful way of finding directions at sea.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. You do not “have access” to this content currently.
questions.explanation: To 'have access to' something is to be able to see or use it, so the sentence is correct as it stands. 'Excess' means too much, and 'permission' would need 'to access'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Brave
questions.explanation: 'Brave' means ready to face danger: 'daring'. 'Timid' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Machines can only “accomplish a maximum set of tasks”, as machines do not hold any thought process of their own.
options: accomplish a valued set of tasks
accomplish a gist set of tasks
accomplish a restricted set of tasks
accomplish a difficult set of tasks
questions.explanation: Machines with no thought process of their own can do only a limited range of tasks, so 'restricted' fits; 'only ... a maximum set' contradicts itself.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He said that / he had want / to read a / novel by Enid Blyton.
questions.explanation: The past perfect takes the past participle: 'he had wanted to read a novel by Enid Blyton'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. Many bosses at workplace consider their “subordinate” on equal planes.
questions.explanation: A 'subordinate' is someone lower in rank; the opposite is a 'superior'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. The boy has “benevolence” towards animals.
questions.explanation: 'Benevolence' is kindness and goodwill; its opposite is 'cruelty'. 'Kindness' is a synonym.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Technological innovations have led to marked improvements in (1) ___________, productivity, quality, inclusion and competitiveness in extension of financial services, especially in the area of digital lending. However, there have been (2) __________ consequences on account of greater reliance on third-party lending service providers mis-selling to the unsuspecting customers, concerns over (3) _________ of data privacy, unethical business conduct and illegitimate operations. While the current share of digital lending in overall credit pie of the financial sector is not significant for it to affect financial stability, the growth momentum has (4) ___________ stability implications. The larger issue here is protecting the customers from widespread unethical practices and (5) ___________ orderly growth.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Technology brings gains in 'efficiency', which sits with productivity and quality in the list.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Technological innovations have led to marked improvements in (1) ___________, productivity, quality, inclusion and competitiveness in extension of financial services, especially in the area of digital lending. However, there have been (2) __________ consequences on account of greater reliance on third-party lending service providers mis-selling to the unsuspecting customers, concerns over (3) _________ of data privacy, unethical business conduct and illegitimate operations. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'However' brings in the drawbacks: consequences no one meant, that is 'unintended' ones.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Data privacy is violated by a 'breach', a concern listed with unethical conduct and illegitimate operations.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Technological innovations have led to marked improvements in (1) ___________, productivity, quality, inclusion and competitiveness in extension of financial services, especially in the area of digital lending. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'While' sets the small present share against the growth momentum, whose implications for stability are 'compelling', strong enough to demand attention.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The larger issue here is protecting the customers from widespread unethical practices and (5) ___________ orderly growth.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The larger aim is to protect customers while 'ensuring' orderly growth; the other three options would work against that growth.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 35 + 21 – 192 ÷ 32 × 7 = 154
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 78 * 39 * 46 * 5 * 10 * 2
questions.explanation: 78 ÷ 39 + 46 = 5 × 10 − 2, as both sides equal 48.

questions.text: Six people are sitting in two parallel rows with 3 people each, in such a way that there is equal distance between adjacent persons. P, O and T are seated in the same row facing South. A, E and R are seated in the same row facing North. E sits at the extreme right end of their row and is exactly opposite T. A sits at the extreme left end of their row and is exactly opposite O. (Persons facing south are exactly opposite to persons facing north) Who sits at the centre of the row of people facing South?
questions.explanation: Facing north, E is at the east end of the row and A at the west end, so R is in the middle. T, opposite E, is at the east end of the south-facing row and O, opposite A, at the west end, which leaves P at the centre.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FACTOR’ is written as ‘DBGTQV’ and 'FAMILY' is written as 'NBGANK’. How will ‘FATHER’ be written as in that language?
questions.explanation: Each half of the word is reversed, then the first half moves +1 and the second +2: FAC TOR → CAF ROT → DBG TQV, and FAM ILY → MAF YLI → NBG ANK. So FAT HER → TAF REH → UBG TGJ: UBGTGJ.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 8, 14, 26, 50, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the previous one minus 2: 8 × 2 − 2 = 14, 14 × 2 − 2 = 26, 26 × 2 − 2 = 50 and 50 × 2 − 2 = 98.

questions.text: Which of the following options will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 52, 86, 121, ?, 194, 232

Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. PEAR : EPRA :: LION : ILNO :: BEAT : ?
questions.explanation: The first two letters swap and the last two swap: PE AR → EP RA and LI ON → IL NO. So BE AT → EB TA: EBTA.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. NGC : OJH :: BQJ : CTO :: PTC : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, +3 and +5: NGC → OJH and BQJ → CTO. So PTC → QWH.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? ARHT, YOJW, WLLZ, ?, SFPF
questions.explanation: The first letters move 2 back (A, Y, W, U, S), the second 3 back (R, O, L, I, F), the third 2 forward (H, J, L, N, P) and the fourth 3 forward (T, W, Z, C, F): UINC.

questions.text: Eight people, D, E, M, P, T, W, Y and Z are sitting in a straight line, facing north. D sits third from the left end of the line. Only one person sits between D and Z. P sits third to the right of Z. Only two people sit between P and W. E sits to the immediate right of Y. M does not sit at any of the extreme ends of the line. What is the position of T from the right end of the line?
questions.explanation: Numbering the seats 1 to 8 from the left, D is 3, so Z is 1 or 5. Z at 5 would put P at 8 and W at 5, Z's own seat; so Z is 1, P is 4 and W is 7. Y and E take 5 and 6, and M, not at an end, takes 2, leaving T at 8: first from the right end.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘POWDER’ is written as ‘QPXEFS’ and ‘SHAMPOO’ is written as ‘TIBNQPP’. How will ‘PERFUME’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: POWDER → QPXEFS and SHAMPOO → TIBNQPP. So PERFUME → QFSGVNF.

questions.text: ‘P % Q’ means ‘P is the brother of Q’. ‘P + Q’ means ‘P is the daughter of Q’. ‘P = Q’ means ‘P is the son of Q’. ‘P # Q’ means ‘P is the wife of Q’. If L = M # N % O + P, how is L related to P?
questions.explanation: L is the son of M, M is the wife of N, N is the brother of O and O is the daughter of P. So N is P's son and L, the son of N and M, is P's son's son.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (16, 350, 19) (14, 310, 17)
questions.explanation: The middle number is 10 times the sum of the other two: (16 + 19) × 10 = 350 and (14 + 17) × 10 = 310. Likewise (13 + 19) × 10 = 320.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1. FAWN 2. FAVOUR 3. FATHER 4. FATIGUE 5. FAT 6. FATE
questions.explanation: FAT comes first, then FATE and FATHER by their fourth letters (E, H), then FATIGUE (I); FAVOUR (V) and FAWN (W) follow: 5, 6, 3, 4, 2, 1.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All boys are tomatoes. Some tomatoes are ladders. No ladder is small. Conclusions: I. Some boys are not tomatoes. II. Some ladders are tomatoes. III. Some boys are ladders.
questions.explanation: Some tomatoes are ladders, so some ladders are tomatoes (II). All boys are tomatoes, so I is false, and nothing links the boys to the ladders, so III does not follow.

questions.text: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? FOWC, KWLI, ?, UMPU, ZUEA
questions.explanation: The first letters move 5 forward (F, K, P, U, Z), the second 8 forward (O, W, E, M, U), the third 11 back (W, L, A, P, E) and the fourth 6 forward (C, I, O, U, A): PEAO.

questions.text: In which year did the Indian gymnast Dipa Karmakar participate in the Olympics?
questions.explanation: Dipa Karmakar competed at the 2016 Rio de Janeiro Olympics, the first Indian woman gymnast to qualify for the Games, and finished fourth in the vault final.

questions.text: Which Union Minister of India launched the Transport 4 All Challenge Stage-2 in 2022?
questions.explanation: Hardeep Singh Puri, then Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs, launched Stage 2 of the ministry's Transport 4 All Challenge, which invites start-ups to build solutions to cities' public transport problems, at an online event on 9 November 2022.

questions.text: Skill India is an initiative launched by the government in________to train over 40 crore Indians in different industry-related jobs.
questions.explanation: The Skill India mission was launched on 15 July 2015, World Youth Skills Day, with the aim of training over 40 crore people in different skills by 2022.

questions.text: What is the maximum length of the tennis racquet for professional play?
questions.explanation: The Rules of Tennis limit a racquet's overall length, handle included, to 29 inches (73.7 cm).

questions.text: What is the Indian postal network famous for in the world?
options: It is the oldest postal network
It is the smallest postal network
It is the largest postal network
It is the cheapest postal network
questions.explanation: India Post, with over 1.5 lakh post offices, most of them in villages, is the largest postal network in the world.

questions.text: As per the Census 2011, which is the second least populous state in the country?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Sikkim (about 6.1 lakh people) had the smallest population of the states and Mizoram (about 11 lakh) the second smallest; Arunachal Pradesh had about 13.8 lakh and Meghalaya about 30 lakh.

questions.text: As a result of Green Revolution, import of food crops was_________ in India,.
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution, from the late 1960s, raised wheat and rice output with high-yielding seeds, fertilisers and irrigation, so India came to need far fewer food imports.

questions.text: Who inaugurated Bengaluru Tech Summit 2022?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the 25th Bengaluru Tech Summit by video on 16 November 2022.

questions.text: What is the atomic number of Carbon?
questions.explanation: A carbon atom has 6 protons, so its atomic number is 6; 7, 8 and 9 are those of nitrogen, oxygen and fluorine.

questions.text: What is the name of the largest waterfall in Kerala?
questions.explanation: Athirappilly Falls, about 25 m high on the Chalakudy river in Thrissur district, is Kerala's largest waterfall; Vazhachal is a smaller fall about 5 km upstream. Dudhsagar is in Goa and Kunchikal in Karnataka.

questions.text: Pandit Birju Maharaj was associated with which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: Pandit Birju Maharaj (1938-2022) was a leading Kathak dancer and guru of the Lucknow gharana.

questions.text: Who among the following had termed the Right to Constitutional Remedy as a ‘soul of the constitution’?
questions.explanation: B.R. Ambedkar called Article 32, the right to constitutional remedies, the very soul and heart of the Constitution, since it lets citizens move the Supreme Court to enforce their Fundamental Rights.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Name the Bengali reformer and book writer who supported widow remarriage.
questions.explanation: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, the Bengali educationist and writer, campaigned for widow remarriage, which the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act of 1856 made legal.

questions.text: Which Five Year Plan Focused on rapid industrialization of heavy & basic industries?
questions.explanation: The Second Five Year Plan (1956-61), built on P.C. Mahalanobis's model, stressed rapid industrialisation through heavy and basic industries.

questions.text: Applied to a bill of Rs. 10000 the difference between a discount of 32 percent and two successive discounts of 20 percent and 12 percent is:
questions.explanation: A 32% discount on ₹10000 is ₹3200. Successive discounts leave 10000 × 0.8 × 0.88 = ₹7040, a discount of ₹2960. The difference is ₹240.

questions.text: By selling 25 articles for a rupee a man gains 20%. How many for a rupee did he buy?
questions.explanation: Each article sells for ₹1/25 at a 20% gain, so it cost (1/25) ÷ 1.2 = ₹1/30: he bought 30 for a rupee.

questions.text: If 45 men can do a work in 30 hours, then in how many hours will 20 men do the same work?
questions.explanation: The work takes 45 × 30 = 1350 man-hours, which 20 men finish in 1350 ÷ 20 = 67.5 hours.

questions.text: Two trains start at the same time from Vijayawada and Calcutta and proceed towards each other at the speed of 24 km/h and 42 km/h, respectively. When they meet, it is found that one train has travelled 140 km more than the other. The distance between the two stations is: (Consider up to two decimals)
questions.explanation: The faster train gains 42 − 24 = 18 km every hour, so the 140 km lead takes 140/18 = 70/9 hours. Together they cover (24 + 42) × 70/9 = 66 × 70/9 = 513.33 km.

questions.text: Two buckets are filled with milk and water in the ratio of 4 : 1 and 7 : 2. If these mixtures are mixed in the ratio of 1 : 5 respectively, then the resulting mixture will have water and milk in the ratio of:
A number is first increased by 20% and then reduced by 20%. What would be the percentage change in the number?
questions.explanation: 1.2 × 0.8 = 0.96, a decrease of 4%.

questions.text: A trader gains 10% after selling an item at a 15% discount on the marked price. The ratio of cost price and the marked price is:
Kuldeep is twice as efficient as Manish to do a work. Working together they can finish a piece of work in 36 days. Kuldeep alone can finish the work in:
questions.explanation: Kuldeep does 2 units a day to Manish's 1, so the work is 3 × 36 = 108 units, and Kuldeep alone takes 108 ÷ 2 = 54 days.

questions.text: A can do as much work as B and C together can do. A and B can together do a piece of work in 7 hours 12 minutes and C can do it in 36 hours. Find the time (in hours) that B needs to do the work alone.
questions.explanation: As A = B + C, A and B together do the work of 2B + C. They do 1/7.2 = 5/36 of it an hour and C does 1/36, so 2B = 4/36, B = 1/18 and B alone takes 18 hours.

questions.text: How much time a person take to cover a distance of 300 metre, if he runs at a speed of 10 km/h?
questions.explanation: 10 km/h is 10000 m in 3600 seconds, so 300 m takes 300 × 3600/10000 = 108 seconds, that is 1 min 48 sec.

questions.text: Simplify the following. {8.4 ÷ 12 × [(27 - 6)² ÷ 3] (7 - 5)}
Ram covers 500 km distance in 20 hours in traffic; he covered some distance by bike at 30 km/h, and rest by car at 20 km/h. The distance covered by bike (in km) is:
questions.explanation: With x km by bike, x/30 + (500 − x)/20 = 20. Multiplying by 60: 2x + 1500 − 3x = 1200, so x = 300.

questions.text: 16 m, 14 m and 10 m are the dimensions of a room. Find the length of the greatest possible scale to measure all dimensions exactly.
questions.explanation: The longest scale that measures each length exactly is their HCF: HCF(16, 14, 10) = 2 m.

questions.text: Revanth sold 8 shirts for a total profit of Rs.480 and 12 shirts for a total profit of Rs.160. At what profit per shirt should he sell the remaining 20 shirts so that he gets an average profit of Rs.20 per shirt?
questions.explanation: An average profit of ₹20 on 40 shirts is ₹800 in all. He has made ₹480 + ₹160 = ₹640, so the other 20 shirts must bring ₹160, that is ₹8 each.

questions.text: According to the wildlife census, there were 550 panthers in 2021 in Rajasthan. If it is expected to increase by 2 percent the next year, then what is the population of the panthers in the year 2022?
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks and make the sentence meaningful. The _______ from my window is of the ________.
questions.explanation: 'Scene' is the view and 'sea' the body of water; 'seen' and 'see' are forms of the verb: 'The scene from my window is of the sea.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom that can be substituted in the following sentence. The fate of the accused “hangs in the balance”.
questions.explanation: Something that 'hangs in the balance' is still undecided, its outcome uncertain.

questions.text: Select the correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. They “is going” to Delhi with their friends.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'they' takes 'are': 'They are going to Delhi with their friends.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Jaded
questions.explanation: 'Jaded' means tired or bored after having too much of something; its opposite is 'renewed', refreshed and restored.

questions.text: The sentence given below has one misspelt word. Spot the INCORRECTLY spelt word and select its correct spelling. Ashish was flabbrgasted when we told him about our latest achievement.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'flabbergasted', meaning greatly astonished.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. It was a “perilous” journey.
questions.explanation: 'Perilous' means full of danger: 'dangerous'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Immune
questions.explanation: 'Immune' means protected from or not affected by something, that is 'resistant'; 'sensitive' and 'vulnerable' are near opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Vicinity
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'remote', far away, the only option opposite in sense to 'vicinity', nearness or the area close by, though it is an adjective (the matching noun would be 'remoteness'). 'Adjacent' and 'proximity' are close to 'vicinity' in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The student repeatedly “referred about one particular” author during his presentation.
questions.explanation: The verb 'refer' takes 'to': 'The student repeatedly referred to one particular author during his presentation.'

questions.text: Select the correct pair of synonyms to fill in the blanks. Seema was shivering, and her body was almost ________ due to the long exposure to ________ winds from the mountains.
questions.explanation: Long exposure to 'icy', freezing cold, winds left her body almost 'frozen', which fits her shivering; the other pairs describe warm, dry or wet conditions.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homonym of the given word. Idol
questions.explanation: 'Idle' (not working, lazy) sounds the same as 'idol' (an image that is worshipped, or a person much admired) but differs in spelling and meaning. Such sound-alike words are strictly homophones, which 'homonym' also covers in its broad sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Bone to pick
options: Having a fond memory to tell
Cleaning the floor for any garbage
Having a complaint that needs to be discussed
questions.explanation: To have 'a bone to pick' with someone is to have a complaint to discuss with them.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Condolance' is misspelt: the word is 'condolence'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. The young girl was “so afraid of her seniors” that she refused to go to school.
questions.explanation: 'Afraid' takes 'of': 'so afraid of her seniors' is correct as it stands.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The teacher will / certainly help you / if you will / ask her.
questions.explanation: An 'if' clause about the future takes the simple present, not 'will': 'if you ask her'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A beautiful spectacle for anyone to (1)_________ would be the crowds that throng to see the Indian cricket team playing, whether it be in India or in other parts of the globe. This (2)__________ is the occasion where the spirit of oneness is all pervasive. India with all its diversity (3)_________ be seen either rejoicing or moaning depending on the sway of the game (4)__________ watched. Unity in diversity is (5)_________ in all its glory.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: To 'behold' is to see or look at, which suits a spectacle: 'for anyone to behold'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A beautiful spectacle for anyone to (1)_________ would be the crowds that throng to see the Indian cricket team playing, whether it be in India or in other parts of the globe. This (2)__________ is the occasion where the spirit of oneness is all pervasive. India with all its diversity (3)_________ be seen either rejoicing or moaning depending on the sway of the game (4)__________ watched. Unity in diversity is (5)_________ in all its glory.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Undoubtedly', without doubt, stresses the claim that this is the occasion when the spirit of oneness is everywhere.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A beautiful spectacle for anyone to (1)_________ would be the crowds that throng to see the Indian cricket team playing, whether it be in India or in other parts of the globe. This (2)__________ is the occasion where the spirit of oneness is all pervasive. India with all its diversity (3)_________ be seen either rejoicing or moaning depending on the sway of the game (4)__________ watched. Unity in diversity is (5)_________ in all its glory.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Only a positive modal fits: India 'could be seen' rejoicing or moaning. 'Shouldn't', 'won't' and 'shan't' contradict the sense.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A beautiful spectacle for anyone to (1)_________ would be the crowds that throng to see the Indian cricket team playing, whether it be in India or in other parts of the globe. This (2)__________ is the occasion where the spirit of oneness is all pervasive. India with all its diversity (3)_________ be seen either rejoicing or moaning depending on the sway of the game (4)__________ watched. Unity in diversity is (5)_________ in all its glory.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Being watched' is the passive present participle: the game that is being watched at the time.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A beautiful spectacle for anyone to (1)_________ would be the crowds that throng to see the Indian cricket team playing, whether it be in India or in other parts of the globe. This (2)__________ is the occasion where the spirit of oneness is all pervasive. India with all its diversity (3)_________ be seen either rejoicing or moaning depending on the sway of the game (4)__________ watched. Unity in diversity is (5)_________ in all its glory.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Unity in diversity is 'witnessed', that is seen, in all its glory.

questions.text: In a certain code language,‘CHILL’ is written as ‘HDNHQ’ and ‘HARSH’ is written as ‘MWWOM’. How will ‘DEVIL’ be written in the same code language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +5 and −4 in turn, wrapping round the alphabet: CHILL → HDNHQ and HARSH → MWWOM. So DEVIL → IAAEQ (V + 5 wraps round to A).

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? KDN, JEO, GHQ, ?, UTX, LCC
questions.explanation: Wrapping round the alphabet, the first letters move back 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 (K, J, G, B, U, L), the second forward 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 (D, E, H, M, T, C) and the third forward 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 (N, O, Q, T, X, C). The missing term is BMT.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 3, 11 ,27, 59 ?
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before plus 5: 3 × 2 + 5 = 11, 11 × 2 + 5 = 27, 27 × 2 + 5 = 59 and 59 × 2 + 5 = 123.

questions.text: A @ B means ‘A is the sister of B’. A & B means ‘A is the brother of B’. A # B means ‘A is the wife of B’. A ^ B means ‘A is the mother of B’. A + B means ‘A is the father of B’. If U + Q ^ R @ N & C ^ I@ J # A, then which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: A is the son of C.
Q is the mother of N.
U is the maternal grandfather of R.
C is the daughter of Q.
questions.explanation: U is Q's father, and Q is the mother of R, whose sibling N is C's brother; so C (a mother, hence female) is Q's daughter and U is R's maternal grandfather. C is the mother of I and of I's sister J, who is A's wife, so A is C's son-in-law, not her son.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? NOTK, LQQN, ? , HUKT, FWHW
questions.explanation: The first letters move −2 (N, L, J, H, F), the second +2 (O, Q, S, U, W), the third −3 (T, Q, N, K, H) and the fourth +3 (K, N, Q, T, W). The missing term is JSNQ.

questions.text: In a certain code, ‘Love And Light’ is written as 513. ‘I Love Sugar’ is written as 437 and ‘Sugar And Spice’ is written as 614. What is the digit code for the word ‘Love’?
questions.explanation: 'Love' is the only word in both 'Love And Light' (513) and 'I Love Sugar' (437), and 3 is the only digit in both codes. By the same reasoning 'And' is 1 and 'Sugar' 4.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some fans are big. All big are coats. Some coats are flat. Conclusions: I. All fans are big. II. Some coats are big. III. Some flats are coats.
options: Both conclusions II and III follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.
questions.explanation: All big are coats, so some coats are big (II); some coats are flat, so some flats are coats (III). Only some fans are big, so I does not follow.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 5, 9, 25, 97, 481, ?
Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. ROSE : 36303810 : : LILY : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as twice its place in the alphabet: ROSE = 18, 15, 19, 5 → 36 30 38 10. So LILY = 12, 9, 12, 25 → 24 18 24 50: 24182450.

questions.text: Which of the following options represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1. Leave 2. Learn 3. Leap 4. Lease 5. Least
questions.explanation: All five words begin 'Lea', so the fourth letter decides: p (Leap), r (Learn), s (Lease, Least) and v (Leave); 'Lease' comes before 'Least' as e comes before t. The order is 3, 2, 4, 5, 1.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 7 * 10 * 280 * 2 * 10 * 80

Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. A sits to the immediate left of C. E sits third to the right of D. D is an immediate neighbour of C. B is an immediate neighbour of both E and F. Who sits to the immediate right of F?
questions.explanation: As all face the centre, each person's left is the next seat clockwise. A is on C's left, so D, C's other neighbour, is on C's right; E, third to D's right, sits opposite D, next to A; B sits next to E and F takes the last seat. Clockwise: C, A, E, B, F, D, so B is on F's immediate right.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 124 - 8 + 96 ÷ 16 × 20 = 12

Six friends are sitting in a circle facing the centre. They are P, Q, R, S, T and U. P is the immediate neighbour of T and S. S is sitting to the immediate left of Q. U is sitting to the immediate right of Q. R is the immediate neighbour of U and T. Who is sitting to the immediate right of T?
questions.explanation: As all face the centre, each person's left is the next seat clockwise. S is on Q's left and U on Q's right; P sits between S and T, and R between T and U. Clockwise: Q, S, P, T, R, U, so P is on T's immediate right.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. FACTORY : AFTCYRO :: FASHION : AFHSNOI :: EXPLAIN : ?
questions.explanation: The first two letters swap, the next two swap and the last three are reversed: FA CT ORY → AF TC YRO and FA SH ION → AF HS NOI. So EX PL AIN → XE LP NIA: XELPNIA.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (6, 9, 324); (5, 8, 240)
questions.explanation: The third number is the product of the first two times 6: 6 × 9 × 6 = 324 and 5 × 8 × 6 = 240. Likewise 10 × 6 × 6 = 360.

questions.text: What is the strong, hot and dry local wind that blows in the northern parts of the country in the months of May and June called?
questions.explanation: The loo is the strong, hot, dry wind that blows over the northern plains in the afternoons of May and June. Mango showers and blossom (cherry blossom) showers are pre-monsoon rains of the south, and kalbaisakhi the evening storms of Bengal and Assam.

questions.text: What do you call the distance between the centre of the nucleus and the outermost shell of an isolated atom?
questions.explanation: Atomic size, or atomic radius, is taken as the distance between the centre of the nucleus and the outermost shell of an isolated atom.

questions.text: Based on the projects identified in City Water Balance Plans,__________ (CWAP) will be devised.
questions.explanation: Under AMRUT 2.0 each city's City Water Balance Plan sets out its water sources, demand, supply and service gaps; the projects to close those gaps make up its City Water Action Plan (CWAP), which the state rolls into a State Water Action Plan.

questions.text: Who among the following is believed to be the author of ‘Natyashastra’?
questions.explanation: The Natyashastra, the ancient Sanskrit treatise on drama, dance and music, is attributed to the sage Bharata (Bharata Muni).

questions.text: Who among the following became Member of Legislative Assembly from Gopalganj, Bihar in India, in November 2022?
questions.explanation: Kusum Devi of the BJP won the Gopalganj by-election of November 2022 (polling on 3 November, counting on 6 November), held after the death of the sitting BJP MLA Subhash Singh.

questions.text: Which article of Indian Constitution is related with the Conduct of business of the Government of a State?
questions.explanation: Article 166 covers the conduct of business of the Government of a State; Article 77 is its counterpart for the Government of India.

questions.text: The price of one unit of foreign currency in terms of domestic currency is called ______.
questions.explanation: The nominal exchange rate is the price of one unit of foreign currency in domestic currency, such as rupees per dollar. The real exchange rate compares the prices of goods abroad and at home.

questions.text: Vempati Chinna Satyam received recognition in which dance form?
questions.explanation: Vempati Chinna Satyam was a Kuchipudi guru and choreographer who founded the Kuchipudi Art Academy in Madras (Chennai).

questions.text: Which country has the longest written constitution?
questions.explanation: India's Constitution is the longest written constitution of any sovereign country.

questions.text: Match the following: a) Cereals and Grains i) lentil; b) Milk and meat ii) rice; c) Fats and sugars iii) fish; d) Pulses and legumes iv)ghee
questions.explanation: Rice is a cereal (a-ii), fish goes with milk and meat as food from animals (b-iii), ghee is a fat (c-iv) and the lentil is a pulse (d-i).

questions.text: ____________ is a kharif crop in north and rabi crop in south India.
questions.explanation: NCERT notes that sesamum (til) is a kharif crop in the north and a rabi crop in the south, while castor is grown both as a rabi and as a kharif crop.

questions.text: Which of the following spring festivals is celebrated in Goa?
questions.explanation: Shigmo (Shigmotsav), Goa's spring festival, is celebrated in Phalguna with folk dances and processions. Mim Kut is a Mizo festival held after the maize harvest, and Losar is the Tibetan New Year.

questions.text: The width of the lobby marked on the sides of the kabaddi playfield is:
questions.explanation: A lobby 1 m wide runs along each side of the kabaddi playfield; it comes into play only once a struggle between a raider and a defender begins.

questions.text: On November 26, 1949, Dr. Rajendra Prasad signed the document as president of the assembly. Which document is being referred to here?
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India on 26 November 1949 (now Constitution Day), and its President, Dr Rajendra Prasad, then signed it to authenticate it. The members signed it on 24 January 1950, and it came into force on 26 January 1950.

questions.text: Receipts of the government which create liability or reduce financial assets are termed as ___________.
questions.explanation: Capital receipts, such as borrowings, recovery of loans and disinvestment, either create a liability or reduce the government's financial assets; revenue receipts do neither.

questions.text: Which Indian state has the lowest population density as per the Census 2011?
questions.explanation: By the 2011 Census Arunachal Pradesh had the lowest population density of any state, 17 persons per sq km.

questions.text: Who took oath as the new Chief Minister of Maharashtra in June 2022?
questions.explanation: Eknath Shinde was sworn in as Chief Minister of Maharashtra on 30 June 2022, after Uddhav Thackeray resigned; Devendra Fadnavis became his Deputy Chief Minister.

questions.text: Indian weightlifter Saikhom Mirabai Chanu created history in 2021 when she became the first Indian weightlifter to clinch a silver medal at the ________.
questions.explanation: Mirabai Chanu won silver in the women's 49 kg at the Tokyo Olympics on 24 July 2021, India's first Olympic silver in weightlifting; Karnam Malleswari had won bronze in 2000.

questions.text: As a country develops, it undergoes ‘structural changes'. Which of the following is a indicator of these structural changes?
options: The share of the industrial sector in GDP decreases
The share of agriculture in GDP declines
The share of agriculture in GDP increases
The share of agriculture in GDP becomes more than 50 percent
questions.explanation: As an economy develops, the share of agriculture in GDP falls while the shares of industry and services rise.

questions.text: Charaka is known as the father of __________.
questions.explanation: Charaka, the ancient physician credited with the Charaka Samhita, a founding text of Ayurveda, is often called the father of Ayurveda or of Indian medicine.

questions.text: A person covers a certain distance by bullet train at 84 km/h and returns back to the starting point by bus at a speed of 66 km/h. Find the average speed of the person for the whole journey.
questions.explanation: For equal distances the average speed is 2 × 84 × 66/(84 + 66) = 11,088/150 = 73.92 km/h.

questions.text: If a shopkeeper wants to give 20% discount on the cost price of the article, then he has to sell it for Rs.400. If he sells it at Rs.520, then his gain percentage is:
questions.explanation: Selling at 20% below cost gives ₹400, so the cost price is 400 ÷ 0.8 = ₹500. Selling at ₹520 gains ₹20, which is 20/500 × 100 = 4%.

questions.text: Mohan buys a chair at Rs.1,200. If he sells it at Rs.1,440, then what is the profit percentage?

Manish can do a piece of work in 7 days while Anil can do the same piece of work in 6 days. The wage for full work is Rs. 390, If they both work together to complete the work, then find the earnings of Manish.
questions.explanation: Their one-day work is 1/7 and 1/6, in the ratio 6 : 7, and the wage is shared in that ratio: Manish gets 6/13 × 390 = ₹180.

questions.text: The ratio of expenditure to saving of a person is 7:3. If the income increases by 12% and the expenditure increases by 8%, then by what percentage his savings will increase? (Correct to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanation: Take income 10, expenditure 7 and saving 3. The new income 11.2 and new expenditure 7 × 1.08 = 7.56 leave a saving of 3.64, an increase of 0.64/3 × 100 = 21.33%.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs represents the co-prime numbers?
questions.explanation: 15 = 3 × 5 and 94 = 2 × 47 share no factor. 141 = 3 × 47 shares 3 with 15 and with 51, and 235 = 5 × 47 shares 5 with 15.

questions.text: The smallest number that is exactly divisibly by 12, 15, 18 and 27 is:

In a circular race of 625 m, A and B start from the same point, at the same time and at speeds of 90 km/h and 72 km/h, respectively. After how much time will they meet again for the first time on the track if they are running in the same directions?
questions.explanation: 90 km/h = 25 m/s and 72 km/h = 20 m/s. Running the same way, A gains 5 m/s and first meets B again after gaining a full lap: 625 ÷ 5 = 125 seconds.

questions.text: 615 coins consist of one rupee, 50 paise and 25 paise coins. Their values are in the ratio of 3 : 5 : 7, respectively. Find the number of 50 paise coins.
questions.explanation: The numbers of coins are in the ratio 3/1 : 5/0.5 : 7/0.25 = 3 : 10 : 28. That is 41 parts, so one part is 615 ÷ 41 = 15 and there are 10 × 15 = 150 coins of 50 paise.

questions.text: Find the volume of a right circular cylinder whose curved surface area is 1012 cm² and circumference of base is 22 cm. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: 2πr = 22 cm gives r = 3.5 cm, and 2πrh = 1012 cm² gives h = 1012 ÷ 22 = 46 cm. Volume = πr²h = 22/7 × 3.5 × 3.5 × 46 = 38.5 × 46 = 1771 cm³.

questions.text: What is the yearly rate of compound interest, compounding annually at which a principal becomes Rs.500 in two years and Rs.700 in three years?
questions.explanation: Each year's amount is (1 + r) times the year before: 700/500 = 1.4, so the rate is 40%.

questions.text: If 30 copies of a compact disc (CD) cost Rs.140, how much will 24 copies of the same CD cost?
questions.explanation: Each CD costs 140/30, so 24 cost 140 × 24/30 = ₹112.

questions.text: The marked price of a fan is Rs. 1850 and the shopkeeper allows a discount of 9.5 percent on it. The selling price of the fan is:

Jaishankar borrowed a sum of money from his employer at the rate of 8% per annum compound interest, compounded annually. He would have to pay ₹58,320 after a period of two years to finish the loan. How much did he borrow?
A man’s working hours per day were increased by 25% and his wages per hour were increased by 20%. By how much percent were his daily earnings increased?
questions.explanation: Daily earnings are hours times the hourly wage, so they become 1.25 × 1.20 = 1.5 times: a 50% increase.

questions.text: A person drives a car for 4 hours at the speed of 75 kmph and for next 6 hours at the speed of 90 kmph. Find the average speed of the car during the entire journey.
questions.explanation: Total distance = 4 × 75 + 6 × 90 = 300 + 540 = 840 km in 10 hours: 84 kmph.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hit the sack
options: To go to bed in order to read
To go to bed in order to write
To go to bed in order to sleep
Go to bed in order to sit
questions.explanation: To 'hit the sack' is to go to bed to sleep.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Hierarchial' is misspelt: the word is 'hierarchical'. 'Cognisant' is the British spelling of 'cognizant'.

questions.text: Complete the sentence with the most appropriate synonym of the word in brackets. Tell everyone to clear the ________ (hallway) as the bride and her father have arrived.
questions.explanation: An 'aisle' is a passage between rows of seats, such as the one a bride walks down with her father, so it is the option nearest to 'hallway' (a passage) here. A driveway and an avenue are roads, and a stage is a platform.

questions.text: Identify the correctly spelt sentence.
options: He is a leading manufakturer in the clothing industry.
He is a leading manufacturer in the clothing endustry.
He is a leading manufacturer in the clothing industry.
He is a leading manufacturer in the clothing indostry.
questions.explanation: Only this sentence spells both 'manufacturer' and 'industry' correctly; the others have 'manufakturer', 'endustry' and 'indostry'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Shabby
questions.explanation: 'Shabby' means worn and run-down, or mean and dishonourable; its opposite is 'respectable'. 'Dilapidated', 'miserable' and 'impoverished' are close to 'shabby'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate alternative to replace the underlined segment in the given sentence. They met yesterday, “haven’t they”?
questions.explanation: A positive statement in the simple past ('met') takes a negative tag made with 'did': 'They met yesterday, didn't they?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in the bracket to fill in the blank. His _________ (repulsive) behaviour could not be ignored.
questions.explanation: 'Repulsive' means causing disgust or offence; of the options only 'innocuous', harmless and inoffensive, comes near its opposite. 'Logical', 'ambitious' and 'faithful' are unrelated.

questions.text: Which of the following options is most similar in meaning to the given word? Allude
questions.explanation: To 'allude' to something is to refer to it, usually indirectly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid tribute to Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru on his “death day”.
questions.explanation: The yearly return of the date of someone's death is their 'death anniversary', the usual term in English.

questions.text: Replace the word in bold in the given sentence with its ANTONYM. Reforms were also made in the “tedious” technicalities of the feudal law.
questions.explanation: 'Tedious' means too long, slow or dull, and so tiresome; its opposite is 'exciting'. 'Drab', 'tiring' and 'boring' are close in meaning to 'tedious'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. His ashes were deposited in a golden _______.
questions.explanation: An 'urn' is a vase, especially one that holds a dead person's ashes. 'Earn' and 'yearn' are verbs that only sound like it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Sailor
questions.explanation: A 'mariner' is a sailor. A prosecutor brings a case in court, an enterpriser runs a business and a trainer teaches skills.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Guess “that vessel holds” the least water?
questions.explanation: 'Guess' introduces an indirect question that picks one vessel out of several, so 'which' is needed, and the singular 'vessel' takes 'holds': 'Guess which vessel holds the least water?'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. I hope / you will / helped me / this weekend.
questions.explanation: After 'will' a verb takes its base form: 'you will help me', not 'helped me'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Out of the woods
questions.explanation: To be 'out of the woods' is to be out of danger or difficulty.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. I hope you will find this series (1)_______ in developing language skills of the learners through diverse reading (2)______ such as fairy tales, fables, classics, adventure, biography, drama and so on. The prose pieces (3)_______ for intensive language study while the poems (4)________ enable children to develop an ear for (5)_______ and rhythm.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 1.
questions.explanation: The writer hopes readers will find the series 'helpful' in developing the learners' language skills.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. I hope you will find this series (1)_______ in developing language skills of the learners through diverse reading (2)______ such as fairy tales, fables, classics, adventure, biography, drama and so on. The prose pieces (3)_______ for intensive language study while the poems (4)________ enable children to develop an ear for (5)_______ and rhythm.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 2.
questions.explanation: Fairy tales, fables, classics, adventure, biography and drama are kinds, or 'genres', of reading.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. I hope you will find this series (1)_______ in developing language skills of the learners through diverse reading (2)______ such as fairy tales, fables, classics, adventure, biography, drama and so on. The prose pieces (3)_______ for intensive language study while the poems (4)________ enable children to develop an ear for (5)_______ and rhythm.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 3.
questions.explanation: The prose pieces 'are meant for', that is intended for, intensive language study.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. I hope you will find this series (1)_______ in developing language skills of the learners through diverse reading (2)______ such as fairy tales, fables, classics, adventure, biography, drama and so on. The prose pieces (3)_______ for intensive language study while the poems (4)________ enable children to develop an ear for (5)_______ and rhythm.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 4.
questions.explanation: 'Will' is the only option that can be followed by the base form 'enable': 'the poems will enable children'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. I hope you will find this series (1)_______ in developing language skills of the learners through diverse reading (2)______ such as fairy tales, fables, classics, adventure, biography, drama and so on. The prose pieces (3)_______ for intensive language study while the poems (4)________ enable children to develop an ear for (5)_______ and rhythm.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 5.
questions.explanation: Poems give children an ear for 'rhyme and rhythm', the sound patterns of verse.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 2, 12, 36, ?, 150, 252

‘A + B’ means ‘A is the father of B’; ‘A − B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’; If ‘P − R × Q + S’, then which of the following statements is true?
options: P is the sister-in-law of R.
P is the sister-in-law of Q.
Q is the sister-in-law of P.
P is the sister-in-law of S.
questions.explanation: P is R's wife, R is Q's brother and Q is S's father. P is the wife of Q's brother, so P is Q's sister-in-law.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? XFCJ, ADFH, ?, GZLD, JXOB
questions.explanation: The first letters move 3 forward (X, A, D, G, J), the second 2 back (F, D, B, Z, X), the third 3 forward (C, F, I, L, O) and the fourth 2 back (J, H, F, D, B), wrapping round the alphabet: DBIF.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (4, 8, 256); (2, 9, 144)
questions.explanation: In each set the third number is 8 times the product of the first two: 4 × 8 × 8 = 256 and 2 × 9 × 8 = 144. Likewise 6 × 9 × 8 = 432.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Cup : Crockery :: Sharpener : ?
questions.explanation: A cup is an item of crockery, and a sharpener an item of stationery.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term. APTITUDE : BQUJUVEF : : ANALOGY : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 1 place forward: APTITUDE → BQUJUVEF. So ANALOGY → BOBMPHZ.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. STOP, VVSU, YXWZ, ?, EBEJ
questions.explanation: The first letters move 3 forward (S, V, Y, B, E), the second 2 (T, V, X, Z, B), the third 4 (O, S, W, A, E) and the fourth 5 (P, U, Z, E, J), wrapping round after Z: BZAE.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All pillows are bed. Some beds are cupboards. All cupboards are wood. Conclusions: I. Some beds are pillows. II. Some cupboards are beds. III. All wood are cupboards.
options: Both conclusions II and III follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.
questions.explanation: All pillows are beds, so some beds are pillows (I); some beds are cupboards, so some cupboards are beds (II). All cupboards are wood, but that does not make all wood cupboards, so III does not follow.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 24 × 16 + 8 – 36 ÷ 18 = 30
questions.explanation: After interchanging + and ÷: 24 × 16 ÷ 8 − 36 + 18 = 48 − 36 + 18 = 30.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 1, 9, 41, 169, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 4 times the one before plus 5: 1 × 4 + 5 = 9, 9 × 4 + 5 = 41 and 41 × 4 + 5 = 169, so 169 × 4 + 5 = 681.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘HUMAN’ is written as ‘HVMBN’ and ‘BEING’ is written as ‘BFIOG’. How will ‘NURSE’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The second and fourth letters move 1 place forward and the rest stay: HUMAN → HVMBN and BEING → BFIOG. So NURSE → NVRTE.

questions.text: In a certain code language,‘CRAVE’ is written as ‘HVFZJ’ and ‘ROUND’ is written as ‘WSZRI’. How will ‘BIRDY’ be written in the same code language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +5, +4, +5, +4, +5: CRAVE → HVFZJ and ROUND → WSZRI. So BIRDY → GMWHD (Y + 5 wraps round to D).

questions.text: Kirti, Suman, Shubh, Kanak, Pari, Charu, Shlok and Shivi are sitting around a square table facing the centre of the table. Some of them are sitting at the corners, while some are sitting at the exact centre of the sides. Kirti sits third to the left of Shubh. Kirti sits at one of the corners. Kanak sits second to the right of Pari. Pari does not sit at any of the corners. Pari is not an immediate neighbour of Kirti. Suman is an immediate neighbour of Charu. Suman does not sit at any of the middle of the sides. Only three people sit between Suman and Shlok. Who is an immediate neighbour of Kanak?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, each person's left is the next seat clockwise. Number the seats clockwise from Kirti's corner (1) to 8, so the corners are 1, 3, 5 and 7: Shubh, with Kirti third to his left, is in 6; Pari, in a middle seat not next to Kirti, in 4; and Kanak, second to her right, in 2. Suman, at a corner opposite Shlok and next to Charu, fits only in 7, with Charu in 8, Shlok in 3 and Shivi in 5, so Kanak's neighbours are Kirti and Shlok.

questions.text: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Prem is an immediate neighbour of Nolan and Suraj. Madhu is sitting third to the right of Prem. Suraj is sitting second to the right of Madhu. Raj is an immediate neighbour of Madhu and Nolan. Steve is sitting third to the right of Nolan. Prem is sitting second to the right of Steve. Who is the immediate neighbour of Raj and Prem?
questions.explanation: Madhu is opposite Prem, and Suraj, second to Madhu's right, is then one of Prem's neighbours, so Nolan is the other; Raj sits between Madhu and Nolan, and Steve opposite Nolan. Going round to the right from Prem: Prem, Nolan, Raj, Madhu, Steve, Suraj. Nolan sits between Raj and Prem.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct? 785 – 125 + 12 ÷ 6 × 39 = 574
Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 vehicle 2 verify 3 vegan 4 venom 5 vein
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: vegan (3), vehicle (1), vein (5), venom (4), verify (2). 'Veg' comes before 'veh', 'veh' before 'vei', 'vei' before 'ven', and 'ven' before 'ver'.

questions.text: What is India’s rank in world population as of 2022?
questions.explanation: In 2022 India had the world's second largest population, after China; the UN expected India to overtake China by the end of April 2023.

questions.text: How many elements are there in the modern periodic table?
questions.explanation: The modern periodic table has 118 elements, up to oganesson (atomic number 118); the last four were named in 2016.

questions.text: As per Article 279A of the amended Constitution of India, the GST Council which will be a joint forum of the Centre and the States, shall consist of the following members: (i) Union Finance Minister (ii) The Union Minister of State, in-charge of Revenue or finance (iii) The Minister In-charge of finance or taxation or any other Minister nominated by each State Government
questions.explanation: Under Article 279A, inserted by the 101st Amendment in 2016, the GST Council consists of the Union Finance Minister as Chairperson, the Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance, and the Minister in charge of Finance or Taxation, or another Minister, nominated by each State Government.

questions.text: During Green Revolution, farmers cultivated crops using______ of seeds.
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution of the late 1960s rested on High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, with fertilisers and assured irrigation.

questions.text: Which Union Minister of India inaugurated the Entrepreneurship Cell and Centre of Innovation at C-DOT campus, Delhi in November 2022?
questions.explanation: Ashwini Vaishnaw, then Union Minister for Communications, Electronics and IT and for Railways, inaugurated the Entrepreneurship Cell and Centre of Innovation at C-DOT, the Department of Telecommunications' research centre, in November 2022.

questions.text: Which of the following states was the host of the 83rd National Table Tennis Championship, 2022?
questions.explanation: Meghalaya hosted the 83rd Senior National Table Tennis Championships, held at Shillong from 18 to 25 April 2022.

questions.text: Who became the first ever woman chief of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)?
questions.explanation: Madhabi Puri Buch took charge as Chairperson of SEBI in March 2022, the first woman to head it.

questions.text: Which article of Indian Constitution provides for right to freedom of speech?
questions.explanation: Article 19(1)(a) guarantees every citizen the freedom of speech and expression.

questions.text: Which of the following is an extension of the Indian Ocean?
questions.explanation: The Arabian Sea is the north-western arm of the Indian Ocean. The Aral Sea is a lake in Central Asia, the Yellow Sea part of the Pacific and the Caribbean Sea part of the Atlantic.

questions.text: A famous Tamil epic, the Silappadikaram was composed by a poet named Ilango, around ______ years ago.
questions.explanation: NCERT's Class 6 history book dates the Silappadikaram, Ilango's Tamil epic about the merchant Kovalan and his wife Kannagi, to about 1800 years ago.

questions.text: Makar Sankranti is celebrated by the Sindhi community by which of the following names?
questions.explanation: Sindhis call Makar Sankranti 'Tirmoori', when parents send sesame sweets to their married daughters; Lal Loi, their Lohri, falls the day before.

questions.text: How many players on each side are allowed on the field at a time in the game of Kabaddi?
questions.explanation: A Kabaddi team has seven players on the court at a time, with the rest of the squad as substitutes.

questions.text: In which state was the first jute mill of India set up?
questions.explanation: India's first jute mill was set up in 1855 at Rishra, on the Hooghly near Kolkata, in West Bengal.

questions.text: Who among the following won awards and recognitions for the development of Kathak dance form?
questions.explanation: Shovana Narayan is a leading Kathak dancer and a Padma Shri awardee. Kelucharan Mohapatra was an Odissi guru and Uday Shankar a pioneer of modern Indian dance.

questions.text: The total value of _______ goods and services produced in a year, indicates national income.
questions.explanation: National income counts only final goods and services; counting intermediate goods as well would count their value twice.

questions.text: After Independence, Indian Parliament has accepted the ____________ pattern of society as the objective of social and economic policy.
questions.explanation: In December 1954 Parliament accepted the 'socialistic pattern of society' as the objective of social and economic policy.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Veer Lakhan Nayak, a legendary tribal leader from __________ participated in Quit India Movement and was hanged by the Britishers in 1943.
questions.explanation: Laxman Naik (Nayak), a tribal leader of Koraput in Orissa (now Odisha), led a Quit India march on the Mathili police station in August 1942 and was hanged in Berhampur jail on 29 March 1943.

questions.text: Chu Faat is the folk dance of which of the following North-Eastern states of India?
questions.explanation: Chu Faat is a Lepcha dance of Sikkim, performed in honour of Mount Khangchendzonga (Kanchenjunga) and its peaks.

questions.text: ______ is to assess the service level compliance of the city with respect to quality, quantity, and coverage of water supply, sewerage and septage management, extent of reuse & recycle of used water and conservation of water bodies.
questions.explanation: Pey Jal Survekshan, run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs under AMRUT 2.0, assesses cities' water supply, sewerage and septage management, reuse of used water and conservation of water bodies; its ground survey began in December 2022.

questions.text: The HCF and LCM of two natural numbers are 7 and 84, respectively. If one of the numbers is 7, then the difference between the two numbers is:
questions.explanation: The product of the two numbers equals HCF × LCM = 7 × 84, so the other number is 7 × 84 ÷ 7 = 84. The difference is 84 − 7 = 77.

questions.text: A manufacturer sells his product at 10% profit to the distributor and the distributor sells it to the customer at 5% profit. If the cost price to the customer is Rs.11,500, determine the profit (in Rs.) (neglect the fraction) earned by the manufacturer.
questions.explanation: The customer pays 1.10 × 1.05 = 1.155 times the manufacturer's cost: ₹11,500 ÷ 1.155 = ₹9,956.71. His 10% profit is ₹995.67, or ₹995 without the fraction.

questions.text: A person driving to a store travels 100 metres in 200 seconds. Then he went to another store driving another 200 metres in 400 seconds. What is his average speed (in m/s)?
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = (100 + 200) ÷ (200 + 400) = 300 ÷ 600 = 0.5 m/s.

questions.text: A, B, and C can complete a work in 9 days and B can do the same work in 18 days. If B takes 33.33% less time than C, find the time taken by C to complete the work.
questions.explanation: 33.33% less is one-third less, so B's 18 days are two-thirds of C's time: C takes 18 × 3/2 = 27 days. (A then does 1/9 − 1/18 − 1/27 = 1/54 of the work a day, so the figures agree.)

questions.text: A manufacturer offers a 25% discount on the marked price of a product. The retailer offers another 28% discount on the reduced price. What is the single discount equivalent to the two discounts offered?
questions.explanation: Successive discounts of 25% and 28% equal 25 + 28 − (25 × 28)/100 = 53 − 7 = 46%.

questions.text: How much interest would Sonia have to pay on a loan of Rs.25,000 at the rate of 12% p.a. compounded quarterly for the period of 1 year (rounded off to two decimal places)?
questions.explanation: Compounded quarterly, the rate is 3% for 4 periods: 25,000 × 1.03⁴ = 25,000 × 1.12550881 = ₹28,137.72, so the interest is ₹3,137.72.

questions.text: How many metallic spheres, each of diameter 3 cm, should be melted to mould into a solid cylinder of diameter 4 cm and height 54 cm?
questions.explanation: Each sphere holds (4/3)π × 1.5³ = 4.5π cm³ and the cylinder π × 2² × 54 = 216π cm³, so 216π ÷ 4.5π = 48 spheres.

questions.text: After giving a discount of 28 percent the selling price of an article is Rs. 13392. The marked price of the article is:
questions.explanation: The selling price is 72% of the marked price: ₹13,392 ÷ 0.72 = ₹18,600.

questions.text: Radha takes a loan of Rs.4,00,000 at 14% per annum compound interest, compounded half-yearly. What is the interest that she repays after 2 years?
questions.explanation: Compounded half-yearly, the rate is 7% for 4 periods: 4,00,000 × 1.07⁴ = 4,00,000 × 1.31079601 = ₹5,24,318.40, so the interest is ₹1,24,318.40.

questions.text: Two trains of equal lengths take 13 seconds and 26 seconds, respectively, to cross a pole. If these trains are moving in the same direction, then how long will they take to cross each other?
questions.explanation: If each train is L long, their speeds are L/13 and L/26 a second, so in the same direction the faster gains L/13 − L/26 = L/26 a second. Passing takes 2L: 2L ÷ (L/26) = 52 seconds.

questions.text: Manoj buys 15 pencils for Rs.12 and sells them at the rate of Rs.1.50/pencil. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Each pencil costs ₹12 ÷ 15 = ₹0.80 and sells for ₹1.50, a profit of ₹0.70: 0.70/0.80 × 100 = 87.5%.

questions.text: In a circular race of 1200 m, A and B start from the same point, at the same time with speeds of 27 km/h and 45 km/h, respectively. After how much time will they meet again for the first time on the track when they running in the same direction?
questions.explanation: 27 km/h = 7.5 m/s and 45 km/h = 12.5 m/s. Running the same way, B gains 5 m/s on A, so B gains a full lap of 1200 m in 1200 ÷ 5 = 240 seconds.

questions.text: In a chemistry laboratory, there are two varieties of some acid. Variety A costs Rs.80 per litre, while variety B costs Rs.100 per litre. In what proportion must a scientist mix both the varieties A and B, so that the mixture becomes worth Rs.92 per litre?
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She liked _________ flat.
questions.explanation: 'Their' is the possessive: the flat belonging to them. 'There' is an adverb of place, and 'they're' and 'they are' add a verb.

questions.text: Select the correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. It is “more hot now”.
questions.explanation: 'Hot' is a one-syllable adjective, so its comparative is 'hotter', not 'more hot': 'It is hotter now.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Your work “diary will of benefit” if you use it and keep all the information updated.
questions.explanation: The sentence lacks a verb after 'will': 'Your work diary will be of benefit if you use it and keep all the information updated.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Forbore
questions.explanation: 'Forbore' is the past tense of 'forbear', to hold back from doing something: 'refrain'. 'Submit', 'yield' and 'surrender' all mean to give in.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The situation in which a disease is spread by touching someone or something
questions.explanation: 'Contagion' is the spreading of a disease by touch or close contact. 'Infected' describes someone who has caught a disease, 'fatal' means causing death and 'malleable' easily shaped.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. On the ball
options: Sceptic of changes or developments and thoughtful to react to them
Aware of any changes or developments and quick to react to them
Aware of any changes or developments but avoid to react to them
Unaware of any changes or developments and lazy to react to them
questions.explanation: To be 'on the ball' is to be alert: aware of what is happening and quick to respond.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We saw a ______ in the city last year.
questions.explanation: The blank needs a noun after 'a': a 'gnu' is a large African antelope, the wildebeest. 'Knew' is a verb, 'new' an adjective and 'no' a determiner.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Bleak
questions.explanation: Besides bare and cheerless, 'bleak' can mean lacking in warmth or kindliness, cold and forbidding, as in a bleak look; 'cordial', warm and friendly, is its opposite. 'Desolate' is close in meaning to 'bleak'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the capitalised word in the given sentence. They tried to get official SANCTIONS for the scheme.
questions.explanation: Here 'sanctions' means official approval for the scheme: 'permissions'.

questions.text: Identify the correctly spelt sentence.
options: There were two seperte sections of students in my school.
There were two separate sections of students in my school.
There were two sepearte sections of students in my school.
There were two seperate sections of students in my school.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'separate', with 'a' after the 'p'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'inadvertent', with 'e' after the 'v'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Smith will / be learning / French when / they are arriving.
questions.explanation: After 'when', a future event takes the simple present, not the present continuous: 'Smith will be learning French when they arrive.'

questions.text: In the given sentence, a word is given in brackets. Select the most appropriate synonym of the word to fill in the blank. The teacher has ___________ (admitted) the student’s sincere apologies.
questions.explanation: To 'acknowledge' an apology is to accept it, the sense 'admitted' has here. 'Executed', 'neglected' and 'denied' do not fit.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Darwin planned to (1)_____ a book describing his (2)_________. He spent nearly twenty years (3)________ the matter for his book, which was to deal with every known fact concerning the problem of the species. Unluckily for Darwin, a naturalist named Wallace had been (4)_______ over the same problems and had reached the same solution. He sent Darwin an essay which almost word for word repeated Darwin’s own ideas.
