Yet Wallace, who was an (5)_________, had been working far away in the Malay Archipelago, whilst Darwin had not left England for several years.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank 1.
questions.explanation: Darwin planned to 'write' a book; to 'scribble' is to write hastily or carelessly.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Darwin planned to (1)_____ a book describing his (2)_________. He spent nearly twenty years (3)________ the matter for his book, which was to deal with every known fact concerning the problem of the species. Unluckily for Darwin, a naturalist named Wallace had been (4)_______ over the same problems and had reached the same solution. He sent Darwin an essay which almost word for word repeated Darwin’s own ideas. Yet Wallace, who was an (5)_________, had been working far away in the Malay Archipelago, whilst Darwin had not left England for several years.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank 2.
questions.explanation: The book was to describe his 'discoveries', the ideas he later found Wallace had reached too.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Darwin planned to (1)_____ a book describing his (2)_________. He spent nearly twenty years (3)________ the matter for his book, which was to deal with every known fact concerning the problem of the species. Unluckily for Darwin, a naturalist named Wallace had been (4)_______ over the same problems and had reached the same solution. He sent Darwin an essay which almost word for word repeated Darwin’s own ideas. Yet Wallace, who was an (5)_________, had been working far away in the Malay Archipelago, whilst Darwin had not left England for several years.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank 3.
questions.explanation: He spent nearly twenty years 'collecting' the matter, that is the material, for his book.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Darwin planned to (1)_____ a book describing his (2)_________. He spent nearly twenty years (3)________ the matter for his book, which was to deal with every known fact concerning the problem of the species. Unluckily for Darwin, a naturalist named Wallace had been (4)_______ over the same problems and had reached the same solution. He sent Darwin an essay which almost word for word repeated Darwin’s own ideas. Yet Wallace, who was an (5)_________, had been working far away in the Malay Archipelago, whilst Darwin had not left England for several years.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank 4.
questions.explanation: To 'think over' a problem is to consider it carefully, as Wallace had done before reaching the same solution.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Darwin planned to (1)_____ a book describing his (2)_________. He spent nearly twenty years (3)________ the matter for his book, which was to deal with every known fact concerning the problem of the species. Unluckily for Darwin, a naturalist named Wallace had been (4)_______ over the same problems and had reached the same solution. He sent Darwin an essay which almost word for word repeated Darwin’s own ideas. Yet Wallace, who was an (5)_________, had been working far away in the Malay Archipelago, whilst Darwin had not left England for several years.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank 5.
questions.explanation: 'An' needs a vowel sound, which leaves 'artist' and 'explorer'; a naturalist working far away in the Malay Archipelago was an 'explorer'.

questions.text: Which of the following letters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter series? F, P, I, S, L, V, ?
questions.explanation: Two series alternate, each moving 3 letters forward: F, I, L and P, S, V. The next letter of the first series is L + 3 = O.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BUS’ is coded as 42 and ‘COT’ is coded as 38. How will ‘DRUM’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded as the sum of its letters' places in the alphabet: BUS = 2 + 21 + 19 = 42 and COT = 3 + 15 + 20 = 38. So DRUM = 4 + 18 + 21 + 13 = 56.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/consonants/vowels in the word). January: 31::March: ________
questions.explanation: January has 31 days, and so does March.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? EHGD, FGHC, GFIB, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move forward (E, F, G, H), the second back (H, G, F, E), the third forward (G, H, I, J) and the fourth back (D, C, B, A): HEJA.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Book 2 Bowl 3 Board 4 Boundary 5 Botanical
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Board (3), Book (1), Botanical (5), Boundary (4), Bowl (2). All begin 'Bo', so the third letters a, o, t, u, w settle the order.

questions.text: A @ B means ‘A is the husband of B’. A & B means ‘A is the mother of B’. A # B means ‘A is the daughter of B’. A % B means ‘A is the sibling of B’. If R % Y & D @ G # M, then M’s son-in-law is the ________ of R.
questions.explanation: G is M's daughter and D is G's husband, so D is M's son-in-law. D is the son of Y, and Y, a mother, is R's sister, so D is R's sister's son.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘candy grass’ is coded as ‘producer dog’, ‘feature cable’ is coded as ‘bug remote’, ‘grass feature’ is coded as ‘dog bug’, and ‘candy cable’ is coded as ‘producer remote’. What is the code for ‘candy’?
questions.explanation: 'Candy' appears in 'candy grass' and 'candy cable', and the only code common to 'producer dog' and 'producer remote' is 'producer'.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 12 × 6 + 9 ÷ 3 - 4 = 25
questions.explanation: After interchanging × and ÷: 12 ÷ 6 + 9 × 3 − 4 = 2 + 27 − 4 = 25.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. FUNS : JZJN :: STOP : WYKK :: DISK : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +4, +5, −4 and −5: FUNS → JZJN and STOP → WYKK. So DISK → HNOF.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, 42, 56, 72, ?
questions.explanation: The terms are 1 × 2, 2 × 3, 3 × 4 and so on up to 8 × 9 = 72, so the next is 9 × 10 = 90.

questions.text: Seven people, A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a straight row, facing north. A sits second from the left. Only two people sit between A and C. Only three people sit between D and F and D is an immediate neighbour of A. B is an immediate neighbour of D and E is not an immediate neighbour of C. Who sits to the extreme right?
questions.explanation: A is 2nd from the left and C 5th. D, next to A, cannot be 1st (F would then be 5th, C's place), so D is 3rd and F 7th. B, next to D, is 4th; E, not next to C, is 1st and G 6th, so F sits at the extreme right.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 24 + 54 ÷ 18 - 48 × 16 = 40
questions.explanation: After interchanging × and +: 24 × 54 ÷ 18 − 48 + 16 = 72 − 48 + 16 = 40.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All hands are fingers. All legs are fingers. All fingers are toes. Conclusions: I. All toes are fingers. II. Some toes are hands. III. Some toes are legs.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: All hands and all legs are fingers, and all fingers are toes, so some toes are hands (II) and some toes are legs (III). It does not follow that all toes are fingers (I).

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term. 4 : 250 :: 5 : ? :: 6 : 1290
questions.explanation: Each number is paired with its fourth power minus 6: 4⁴ − 6 = 256 − 6 = 250 and 6⁴ − 6 = 1296 − 6 = 1290. So 5⁴ − 6 = 625 − 6 = 619.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark(?) in the given series? 286, 231, ?, 151, 126, 111
questions.explanation: The differences are −55, −45, −35, −25, −15, shrinking by 10: 231 − 45 = 186, and 186 − 35 = 151.

questions.text: Six girls D, K, M, P, R and S are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre. S is sitting third to the left of R. P is sitting to the immediate right of R and to the immediate left of D. M is sitting to the immediate left of R. K is sitting to the immediate right of S and to the immediate left of M. If D and K exchange their places, Who will be sitting to the immediate right of D?
questions.explanation: Going round the table to the left from R: R, M, K, S, D, P. After D and K exchange places the order is R, M, D, S, K, P, so M sits to D's immediate right.

questions.text: When exports are higher than imports, it is known as a situation of _______.
questions.explanation: When the value of exports exceeds that of imports, a country has a trade surplus; a trade deficit is the reverse.

questions.text: Articles ________ to ________ enunciates the qualifications, functions of the President and his/her tenure, election, method of re-election, and impeachment among others.
questions.explanation: Articles 52 to 62, in Part V of the Constitution, deal with the President: the office, executive power, election, term, qualifications, oath, impeachment and the filling of vacancies.

questions.text: A ____________ balance of trade is one in which the value of domestic goods exported exceeds the value of foreign goods imported.
questions.explanation: A balance of trade is favourable (a surplus) when exports exceed imports and unfavourable when imports exceed exports.

questions.text: What is the minimum age required to become a member of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Under Article 84(b) a member of the Lok Sabha must be at least 25 years old; for the Rajya Sabha the minimum is 30.

questions.text: Khelo India Youth Games was formerly known as _______________.
questions.explanation: The first edition, in New Delhi in 2018, was the Khelo India School Games; from the 2019 edition in Pune it became the Khelo India Youth Games.

questions.text: The public sector was the focus of the _________ and planned on bringing rapid industrialization in the country.
options: third five year plan in India
fifth five year plan in India
first five year plan in India
second five year plan in India
questions.explanation: The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61), drawn up on P C Mahalanobis's model, stressed rapid industrialisation, with heavy industry in the public sector.

questions.text: Who among the following political leaders became Member of Parliament from Sangrur constituency, Punjab in June 2022?
questions.explanation: Simranjit Singh Mann of the Shiromani Akali Dal (Amritsar) won the Sangrur Lok Sabha by-election in June 2022, held after Bhagwant Mann gave up the seat on becoming Chief Minister of Punjab.

questions.text: The 23rd National Youth Festival to commemorate the birthday of Swami Vivekanand was held at___________.
questions.explanation: The 23rd National Youth Festival was held in Lucknow from 12 to 16 January 2020; the festival opens on 12 January, Swami Vivekananda's birthday, which is National Youth Day.

questions.text: Who was named as the new Chief Secretary of Delhi in April 2022?
questions.explanation: Naresh Kumar, a 1987-batch IAS officer of the AGMUT cadre and until then Chief Secretary of Arunachal Pradesh, was named Chief Secretary of Delhi in April 2022.

questions.text: According to which of the following laws, heat produced by an electric current is directly proportional to the resistance of the conductor, the square of the current, and the time for which it flows?
questions.explanation: Joule's law of heating gives the heat produced as H = I²Rt. Hooke's law is about elastic stretching, Coulomb's about the force between charges and Faraday's about electromagnetic induction and electrolysis.

questions.text: How many Indian dances have been recognised by the Sangeet NatakAkademi as classical dance forms as of May 2022?
questions.explanation: As of May 2022 the Sangeet Natak Akademi recognised eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Odissi and Sattriya.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Indian National Congress was founded in:
questions.explanation: The Indian National Congress was founded in December 1885; its first session met in Bombay, with W C Bonnerjee as president.

questions.text: At the age of__________, Mahavira left home and went to live in a forest in search of enlightenment.
questions.explanation: Vardhamana Mahavira, the 24th tirthankara of the Jainas, left home at the age of thirty and lived a hard life in the forest for twelve years before attaining enlightenment.

questions.text: Dree, an agricultural festival of Arunachal Pradesh, is celebrated in the month of ________.
questions.explanation: Dree, the agricultural festival of the Apatani of the Ziro valley, is celebrated in July; since 1967 its main celebration has been held on 5 July.

questions.text: The nucleus is separated from _______ by a nuclear membrane.
questions.explanation: The nuclear membrane (nuclear envelope) separates the nucleus from the cytoplasm around it.

questions.text: National Film Award for Best Choreography for the movie Vishwaroopam was awarded to______________.
questions.explanation: Pandit Birju Maharaj won the National Film Award for Best Choreography (60th awards, for 2012) for the song 'Unnai Kaanadhu Naan' in Kamal Haasan's 'Vishwaroopam'.

questions.text: The Companies (Amendment) Bill, 2020 was introduced in Lok Sabha by which minister?
questions.explanation: Anurag Singh Thakur, then Minister of State for Finance and Corporate Affairs, introduced the bill in the Lok Sabha on 17 March 2020; it sought to decriminalise minor procedural defaults under the Companies Act, 2013. (Nirmala Sitharaman was the minister in charge of it.)

questions.text: Burmese is the official language of which neighbouring country of India?
questions.explanation: Burmese (the Myanmar language) is the official language of Myanmar. Nepali is the official language of Nepal and Dzongkha that of Bhutan.

questions.text: Autumn season in India comes under which among the following month interval?
questions.explanation: October and November, between the withdrawal of the monsoon and the onset of winter, form the post-monsoon or autumn season. June to September is the monsoon, December to February winter and March to May summer.

questions.text: On what does the pressure and wind system of any area depend?
options: Distance from the sea and latitude
Latitude and altitude of the place
Longitude and distance from the sea
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives latitude and altitude, as the NCERT Class 9 geography textbook ('Climate') puts it: latitude sets the planetary pressure belts and the winds between them, and air pressure falls with altitude. Distance from the sea, which that text treats as a separate control of climate (continentality), also shapes local winds such as land and sea breezes, so the key is the textbook answer rather than the only factor.

questions.text: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 6 and 3024, respectively. If one of the numbers is 54, then find the other number.
questions.explanation: The product of two numbers equals HCF × LCM: 6 × 3024 = 18,144, and 18,144 ÷ 54 = 336.

questions.text: Two trains A and B are 155 km apart on a straight line. One train starts from A at 7:00 A.M. and travels towards B at 20 km/h. Another train starts from B at 8:00 A.M. and travels towards A at a speed of 25 km/h. At what time will they meet?
questions.explanation: By 8:00 A.M. the first train has covered 20 km, leaving 135 km. Closing at 20 + 25 = 45 km/h, they meet 135 ÷ 45 = 3 hours later, at 11:00 A.M.

questions.text: Which of the following is divisible by 24?
questions.explanation: A number divisible by 24 must be divisible by both 8 and 3. In 2856 the last three digits, 856, are divisible by 8 and the digit sum, 21, by 3: 2856 = 24 × 119. In the others the last three digits, 940, 458 and 860, are not divisible by 8.

questions.text: Priyank buys an unfurnished flat for Rs. 6000000. He furnished it and eventually sells it for Rs. 12000000. The percent increase in the price of the flat is:
questions.explanation: The price rose from ₹60,00,000 to ₹1,20,00,000; the increase of ₹60,00,000 equals the original price, which is 100%.

questions.text: A and B together can complete a work in 8 days. A alone can complete it in 16 days. If B works at 50 percent efficiency, then in how many days A and B together will complete the work?
questions.explanation: B alone does 1/8 − 1/16 = 1/16 of the work a day; at 50% efficiency that is 1/32. Together they do 1/16 + 1/32 = 3/32 a day, so the work takes 32/3 days.

questions.text: If the third proportion to 8 and 18 is same as the fourth proportion to 2, 81 and x² + 2x + 2, then find the value of x.
questions.explanation: The third proportional to 8 and 18 is 18² ÷ 8 = 40.5. The fourth proportional to 2, 81 and (x² + 2x + 2) is 81(x² + 2x + 2) ÷ 2, so x² + 2x + 2 = 1, that is (x + 1)² = 0 and x = −1.

questions.text: Two persons P and Q working together can do a piece of work in 18 days. Q alone can do it in 36 days. Q started the work, and after working for 6 days he left the work. P then took up the remaining work. How many days will P take to complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation: P alone does 1/18 − 1/36 = 1/36 of the work a day. Q's 6 days do 6/36 = 1/6 of it, leaving 5/6, which P finishes in 5/6 × 36 = 30 days.

questions.text: Ratnesh purchased a bike for Rs.64,000 and sold it for Rs.60,000. What is the percentage loss faced by Ratnesh?

A shopkeeper has found that the selling price of the product is 90% of the cost price. The selling price is Rs.90 per kg, so in order to get a profit, he weighs only 800 grams in place of 1 kg. Determine the profit (in Rs.) earned by the shopkeeper on selling 1 kg of this product?
questions.explanation: The selling price, ₹90 a kg, is 90% of the cost, so the cost is ₹100 a kg. For '1 kg' he hands over 800 g, which cost him ₹80, and charges ₹90: a profit of ₹10.

questions.text: The average of six consecutive odd numbers is 68. What is the cube of the difference between the highest and the lowest numbers?
questions.explanation: Six consecutive odd numbers averaging 68 are 63, 65, 67, 69, 71 and 73. The highest and lowest differ by 10, and 10³ = 1000.

questions.text: A seller announced 30% discount on the marked price of a fan. If the selling price of the fan is Rs.2,800, then the marked price of the fan was:
questions.explanation: The selling price is 70% of the marked price: 2,800 ÷ 0.7 = ₹4,000.

questions.text: In an election between two candidates, the one who gets 58% of the votes polled is elected by a majority of 4,032 votes. What is the total number of votes polled?
questions.explanation: The loser gets 42%, so the majority is 58% − 42% = 16% of the votes polled: 4,032 ÷ 0.16 = 25,200.

questions.text: After a discount of 15% on the marked price, the profit is 5%. What percent discount on the marked price be there to have 8% profit (rounded off to one decimal place)?
questions.explanation: 0.85 × MP = 1.05 × CP. For 8% profit the selling price is 1.08 × CP = 1.08 × 0.85/1.05 × MP ≈ 0.874 × MP, so the discount is about 12.6%.

questions.text: A man borrows a certain sum of money and pays it back in 2 years in two equal instalments. If Compound Interest is reckoned at 5% per annum in case of annual compounding and he pays back annually Rs.882, what sum did he borrow?
questions.explanation: The sum borrowed is the present value of the two instalments: 882 ÷ 1.05 + 882 ÷ 1.05² = 840 + 800 = ₹1,640.

questions.text: In 4 h, a boat goes 12 km along the stream. It covers 6 km against the stream in the same time. The speed of the boat in still water (in km/h) is:
questions.explanation: Downstream the boat makes 12 ÷ 4 = 3 km/h and upstream 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5 km/h. Its speed in still water is the average: (3 + 1.5) ÷ 2 = 2.25 km/h.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Alienate
questions.explanation: To 'alienate' is to make someone unfriendly or estranged; to 'reconcile' is to bring people back together. 'Alter' and 'alternate' are about change, and 'renounce' means to give up.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The “collision” was witnessed by the pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A 'collision' is a crash, two things striking each other with force: a 'violent accident'. The other phrases have nothing to do with a crash.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Dogs are the most adorable and lovable “beings to tie”.
questions.explanation: Dogs are kept as pets, so 'pets to keep' gives the sense the sentence needs: 'the most adorable and lovable pets to keep'. 'Beings to tie' makes no sense, and 'animals to play' would need 'with'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'receipt', with 'ei' after 'c' and a silent 'p'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Eligible
questions.explanation: 'Eligible' means meeting the conditions for something: 'qualified'. 'Efficient' and 'sufficient' mean something else, and 'disinterested' means impartial.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Dutyful' is misspelt: the word is 'dutiful', as the 'y' of 'duty' becomes 'i' before '-ful', as in 'plentiful' and 'merciful'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Ponderous
questions.explanation: 'Ponderous' means slow and clumsy because of great weight; its opposite is 'graceful', moving smoothly and lightly. 'Obligated', 'swollen' and 'adverse' are not opposites of it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Bear a grudge
options: To consider people with kindness and care
To feel angry against somebody for a past incident
To entertain the guests with utmost happiness
To feel satisfied with the achievements
questions.explanation: To 'bear a grudge' is to go on feeling resentment against someone for something they did in the past.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He is usually calm but today he appears rather ___________.
questions.explanation: 'But' sets today against his usual calm, so the blank needs a word opposite in sense: 'disturbed'. 'Quiet', 'undisturbed' and 'relaxed' all mean much the same as calm.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in past tense form. Aksa Thomas comes to attend the session so early.
options: Aksa Thomas came to attend the session so early.
Aksa Thomas has come to attend the session so early.
Aksa Thomas may come to attend the session so early.
Aksa Thomas will come to attend the session so early.
questions.explanation: The simple present 'comes' becomes the simple past 'came'. 'Has come' is the present perfect, and 'may come' and 'will come' are not past forms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Gate-crasher
options: A person who enters an event without any invitation
A cobra that lives in gardens
questions.explanation: A 'gate-crasher' is someone who goes to a party or event without being invited.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. This certainly was a “feeble” attempt to capture the culprit.
questions.explanation: 'Feeble' means weak; its opposite is 'powerful'. 'Enviable', 'refraining' and 'treble' (threefold) are not opposites of it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Ample
questions.explanation: 'Ample' means enough or more than enough: 'sufficient'. 'Sample' and 'temple' only look and sound like it, and 'entertain' is unrelated.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in the brackets to fill in the blank. The increasing population of a country can be a_______ (affliction) for the development of a country.
questions.explanation: An 'affliction' is a cause of suffering, and a 'bane' is a cause of great trouble or harm. A 'boon', a blessing, is the opposite, and 'boom' and 'brittleness' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. APJ Abdul Kalam was born in a middle class family. He was a short boy _______ ordinary looks.
questions.explanation: 'Rather' (somewhat) qualifies 'ordinary': 'a short boy with rather ordinary looks'. 'Either' and 'neither' need 'or' and 'nor', and 'with as' is not grammatical.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Reaching the stall from which the sound was emanating, he saw that it was deserted. It was festooned (1)________ flowers: blue-bells and foxgloves and harebells and daffodils, but also with violets and lilies. The use and function of these flowers is chiefly (2)_______; they bring pleasure; they can be given to a loved one as a token of admiration and affection, and the sound they make is pleasing (3) ________ the ear. Also, they catch the light (4) ________ delightfully. Dustan could not but observe that the colour of sunlight glittering through the purple crystal was inferior in both (5) ________to that of her eyes.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: A stall is 'festooned with' flowers, that is decorated with them; the sentence goes on 'but also with violets and lilies'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Reaching the stall from which the sound was emanating, he saw that it was deserted. It was festooned (1)________ flowers: blue-bells and foxgloves and harebells and daffodils, but also with violets and lilies. The use and function of these flowers is chiefly (2)_______; they bring pleasure; they can be given to a loved one as a token of admiration and affection, and the sound they make is pleasing (3) ________ the ear. Also, they catch the light (4) ________ delightfully. Dustan could not but observe that the colour of sunlight glittering through the purple crystal was inferior in both (5) ________to that of her eyes.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The flowers are used chiefly for decoration and enjoyment, 'decorative and recreational', as the next clause says: 'they bring pleasure'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Reaching the stall from which the sound was emanating, he saw that it was deserted. It was festooned (1)________ flowers: blue-bells and foxgloves and harebells and daffodils, but also with violets and lilies. The use and function of these flowers is chiefly (2)_______; they bring pleasure; they can be given to a loved one as a token of admiration and affection, and the sound they make is pleasing (3) ________ the ear. Also, they catch the light (4) ________ delightfully. Dustan could not but observe that the colour of sunlight glittering through the purple crystal was inferior in both (5) ________to that of her eyes.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: A sound is 'pleasing to' the ear: 'pleasing' takes 'to'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Reaching the stall from which the sound was emanating, he saw that it was deserted. It was festooned (1)________ flowers: blue-bells and foxgloves and harebells and daffodils, but also with violets and lilies. The use and function of these flowers is chiefly (2)_______; they bring pleasure; they can be given to a loved one as a token of admiration and affection, and the sound they make is pleasing (3) ________ the ear. Also, they catch the light (4) ________ delightfully. Dustan could not but observe that the colour of sunlight glittering through the purple crystal was inferior in both (5) ________to that of her eyes.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'So' intensifies the adverb: 'they catch the light so delightfully'. 'Such' goes before a noun, 'much' does not qualify an adverb this way, and 'more' would need a comparison.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Reaching the stall from which the sound was emanating, he saw that it was deserted. It was festooned (1)________ flowers: blue-bells and foxgloves and harebells and daffodils, but also with violets and lilies. The use and function of these flowers is chiefly (2)_______; they bring pleasure; they can be given to a loved one as a token of admiration and affection, and the sound they make is pleasing (3) ________ the ear. Also, they catch the light (4) ________ delightfully. Dustan could not but observe that the colour of sunlight glittering through the purple crystal was inferior in both (5) ________to that of her eyes.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The sentence compares the colour of the light with that of her eyes, so the blank needs words about colour: 'hue and shade'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) 2D : Triangle :: 3D : ________
questions.explanation: A triangle is a two-dimensional (2D) shape and a hemisphere a three-dimensional (3D) one. A square and a rectangle are 2D shapes, and 'figure' names no particular shape.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 63 ÷ 3 × 21 – 15 + 12 = 6
questions.explanation: After interchanging ÷ and ×: 63 × 3 ÷ 21 − 15 + 12 = 9 − 15 + 12 = 6.

questions.text: Six people M, N, O, P, Q and R are sitting in a straight row, facing north. O is sitting to the immediate right of N. P is sitting to the immediate right of O. Q is sitting to the immediate right of P. R is sitting to the immediate left of N. If there are only five people sitting to the right of M, who is at the extreme right end of the row?
questions.explanation: R, N, O, P and Q sit in that order from left to right. With five people to M's right, M is at the left end: M, R, N, O, P, Q, so Q is at the extreme right.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by two conclusions numbered 1 and 2. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No red is black. All blues are black. No blue is pink. Conclusions: 1. No blue is red. 2. No red is pink.
questions.explanation: Every blue is black and no red is black, so no blue is red: 1 follows. Nothing links red with pink (only blue is kept apart from pink), so 2 does not follow.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Gardener : Harrow :: Farmer : ?
questions.explanation: The pairs are a worker and a tool for working the soil: a harrow breaks up and levels it, and the farmer's plough turns it over. Water, seed and land are not tools.

questions.text: ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’; ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’; If B × D ÷ F − H + J ÷ S, then which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: H is the son of D.
J is the sister of H.
F is the sister of D.
B is the husband of the sister of F.
questions.explanation: B is D's husband, D is F's sister, F is H's mother, H is J's brother and J is S's sister. H is the son of F, D's sister, so H is D's nephew, not son; the other three statements hold.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? XERJ, THPK, ?, LNLM, HQJN
questions.explanation: The first letters move 4 back (X, T, P, L, H), the second 3 forward (E, H, K, N, Q), the third 2 back (R, P, N, L, J) and the fourth 1 forward (J, K, L, M, N): PKNL.

questions.text: Which of the following interchange of numbers(not digits) would make the given equation correct? 15 ÷ 5 × 12 + 6 = 65 − 35
questions.explanation: After interchanging 6 and 12: 15 ÷ 5 × 6 + 12 = 18 + 12 = 30, which equals 65 − 35.

questions.text: In a code language, ‘fast track him’ is coded as ‘le pa da’, ‘we give fast’ is coded as ‘da jo he’, ‘track my order’ is coded as ‘vu ba le’. What is the code for the word ‘him’?
questions.explanation: 'Fast' is in the first two messages and 'da' is the only code common to both; 'track' is in the first and third, where 'le' is common. The remaining word of the first message, 'him', is 'pa'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 1 : 36 :: 2 : 49 :: 4 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second number is the square of 5 more than the first: (1 + 5)² = 36 and (2 + 5)² = 49. So (4 + 5)² = 81.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 98, 93, 89, ?, 84
questions.explanation: The differences are −5, −4, −3, −2: 89 − 3 = 86, and 86 − 2 = 84.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1. track 2. trace 3. trade 4. treasure 5. triangle
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: trace (2), track (1), trade (3), treasure (4), triangle (5). 'Trace' comes before 'track' (e before k), 'trac' before 'trad', and 'tra' before 'tre' and 'tri'.

questions.text: Kirti, Suman, Shubh, Kanak, Pari, Charu, Shlok and Shivi are sitting around a square table facing the centre of the table. Some of them are sitting at the corners, while some are sitting at the exact centre of the sides. Kirti sits third to the left of Shubh. Kirti sits at one of the corners. Kanak sits second to the right of Pari. Pari does not sit at any of the corners. Pari is not an immediate neighbour of Kirti. Suman is an immediate neighbour of Charu. Suman does not sit at any of the middle of the sides. Only three people sit between Suman and Shlok from either sides. Who does NOT sit at any of the corners?
questions.explanation: Kirti, at a corner, is three seats from Shubh, so Shubh sits at the middle of a side; Pari sits at a middle and Kanak two seats from her, so Kanak does too. Suman sits at a corner with Charu beside her, so Charu is at the middle of a side, leaving the corners to Kirti, Suman, Shlok (opposite Suman) and Shivi.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 5, 7, 12, 21, 35, 55, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 2, 5, 9, 14, 20, which grow by 3, 4, 5, 6. The next difference is 27: 55 + 27 = 82.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? BVFY, FRJU, JNNQ, ?, RFVI
questions.explanation: The first and third letters move 4 forward (B, F, J, N, R and F, J, N, R, V) and the second and fourth 4 back (V, R, N, J, F and Y, U, Q, M, I): NJRM.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘CLOAKED’ is written as ‘39’and ‘FLANK’ is written as ‘32’.How will ‘FLOCKED’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet minus 12: CLOAKED = 3 + 12 + 15 + 1 + 11 + 5 + 4 = 51 and 51 − 12 = 39; FLANK = 44 and 44 − 12 = 32. FLOCKED = 6 + 12 + 15 + 3 + 11 + 5 + 4 = 56, so 56 − 12 = 44.

questions.text: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act,(MGNREGA) Government of India, comes under the flagship of ______________.
options: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
questions.explanation: MGNREGA, which guarantees 100 days of wage employment a year to rural households whose adults volunteer for unskilled manual work, is run by the Ministry of Rural Development.

questions.text: Which article of the Indian Constitution provides for right to education?
questions.explanation: Article 21A, added by the 86th Amendment in 2002, makes free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 a fundamental right.

questions.text: Which dynasty ruled over Delhi during 1290 to 1320?
questions.explanation: The Khalji dynasty ruled the Delhi Sultanate from Jalaluddin Khalji's accession in 1290 until 1320, when Ghiyasuddin Tughluq founded the Tughluq dynasty.

questions.text: Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellow ( Akademi Ratna) has been awarded to ______________.
questions.explanation: The Sattriya dancer and guru Jatin Goswami of Assam was elected a Fellow of the Sangeet Natak Akademi (Akademi Ratna), its highest honour, in 2019, among the Fellows for 2018. Tankeswar Hazarika Borbayan received the Akademi's award for Sattriya for the same year, not the Fellowship.

questions.text: Which among the following is an “S” shaped ocean?
questions.explanation: The Atlantic Ocean, between the Americas on the west and Europe and Africa on the east, is shaped like the letter S.

questions.text: The Sport Jallikattu belongs to which Country?
questions.explanation: Jallikattu, in which young men try to hold on to a running bull, is a sport of Tamil Nadu in India, held at the Pongal festival.

questions.text: What is the minimum age required to be appointed as the Governor of State?
questions.explanation: Under Article 157 a Governor must be a citizen of India who has completed 35 years of age.

questions.text: The Green Revolution in India was initiated in the 1960s by introducing high-yielding varieties of _________.
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution of the 1960s spread high-yielding varieties of wheat and rice, grown with fertilisers and assured irrigation.

questions.text: Which Union Minister of India inaugurated largest South Asian film market-Film Bazaar in November 2022?
questions.explanation: Anurag Singh Thakur, then Minister of Information and Broadcasting, inaugurated the 2022 Film Bazaar, held alongside the 53rd International Film Festival of India in Goa, on 21 November 2022.

questions.text: How is the distribution of species done in stratification?
questions.explanation: Stratification is the vertical distribution of species at different levels, as trees, shrubs and herbs occupy the top, middle and bottom layers of a forest.

questions.text: Koli is the folk dance of which of the following Indian states?
questions.explanation: Koli is a dance of Maharashtra's Koli fishing community; its movements imitate rowing and the waves.

questions.text: Who introduced the concept of poverty line in pre-independent India?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji was the first to discuss a poverty line in pre-independence India: he priced the diet given to prisoners to arrive at a 'jail cost of living'.

questions.text: Which of the following element has atomic number 12?
questions.explanation: Magnesium (Mg) has atomic number 12. Calcium (Ca) is 20, oxygen (O) 8 and helium (He) 2.

questions.text: What is the last step in the process of manufacturing of steel?
options: heating limestone, coke and iron in a blast furnace
questions.explanation: Iron ore, coke and limestone are heated in a blast furnace to give pig iron, which is refined into liquid steel; the steel is then shaped by rolling, pressing, casting or forging.

questions.text: Who became the foreign secretary of India in May 2022?
questions.explanation: Vinay Mohan Kwatra took charge as Foreign Secretary on 1 May 2022, succeeding Harsh Vardhan Shringla.

questions.text: How many players on each side are allowed on the field at a time in the game of Volleyball?
questions.explanation: A volleyball team has six players on the court at a time.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Bahadur Shah Zafar and his sons were arrested by the British officials from __________ in Delhi.
questions.explanation: After the British retook Delhi in September 1857, Bahadur Shah Zafar and the princes took refuge at Humayun's Tomb, where the cavalry officer William Hodson took them prisoner.

questions.text: Father of Green Revolution in the world is :
questions.explanation: Norman Borlaug, the American agronomist whose high-yielding dwarf wheat varieties spread from Mexico to India and Pakistan, received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.

questions.text: National income accounting is a bookkeeping system to measure the level of the country's ______activity in a given time period.
questions.explanation: National income accounting records a country's output, income and spending over a period, which measures the level of its economic activity.

questions.text: A man's weekly wage was Rs. 1200, but now he earns Rs. 1800. What is the percent increase in the man's wage?
Three cubes, each of side 5 cm, are joined end to end. What is the total surface area of the resulting cuboid?
questions.explanation: The cuboid is 15 cm × 5 cm × 5 cm, so its surface area is 2(15 × 5 + 5 × 5 + 15 × 5) = 2 × 175 = 350 cm².

questions.text: Akhil, Sahil and Amit can do a certain work in 64 days. While Akhil and Sahil can do the same work in 80 days, then in how many days can Amit do the same work?
questions.explanation: Amit alone does 1/64 − 1/80 = (5 − 4)/320 = 1/320 of the work a day, so he takes 320 days.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT correct?

Mohan and Sohan started running from the points P and Q at the same time towards each other. The speeds of Mohan and Sohan are 24km/h and 18km/h respectively. If they meet after 10 min, then what is the distance between P and Q?
questions.explanation: Running towards each other they close at 24 + 18 = 42 km/h, so in 10 minutes they cover 42 × 10/60 = 7 km.

questions.text: Samantha takes 3 hours to travel from place X to place Y at a speed of 75 miles per hour. She takes 2 hours to travel from place Y to Z with 30% increased speed. Find her average speed during the entire journey.
questions.explanation: X to Y is 3 × 75 = 225 miles; Y to Z is 2 × 97.5 = 195 miles (75 raised by 30%). Average speed = (225 + 195)/5 = 420/5 = 84 miles per hour.

questions.text: If a: b is 4 : 6 and b : c is 10 : 11, then c : a is :
questions.explanation: Making b equal: a : b = 20 : 30 and b : c = 30 : 33, so a : b : c = 20 : 30 : 33 and c : a = 33 : 20.

questions.text: The present population of a city is 92,61,000. If it has been increasing at the rate of 5% per annum, find its population 3 years ago.

A retailer announces a discount of 40% for selling a food processor marked at ₹86,000. The cost price of the food processor is 60% below the marked price. He offers a further discount of 10% if the buyer presents his membership card of the retailer’s store. The profit of the retailer with the membership card scheme is what percentage of the profit of the retailer without the membership card scheme?

After a certain time period, a sum of Rs.24,000 invested in a bank will amount to Rs.26,460 when the compound rate of interest is 5% p.a., being compounded annually. In how many months will it amount to Rs.26,460?
questions.explanation: 26,460/24,000 = 1.1025 = 1.05², so it takes 2 years, or 24 months.

questions.text: Two trains, starting at the same time from two stations 100 km apart are travelling towards each other and they cross each other at a distance of 70 km from one of the stations. What is the ratio of their speeds?
questions.explanation: In the same time one train covers 70 km and the other 100 − 70 = 30 km, so their speeds are in the ratio 70 : 30 = 7 : 3.

questions.text: A dealer buys 50 chairs for ₹50,000 but 20 of them are damaged. He decides to sell each of the damaged chair at 3/4th of the selling price of normal chair. What should be the selling price of normal chair so that he may make a profit of 35% on the whole transaction?
questions.explanation: He needs ₹50,000 × 1.35 = ₹67,500 in all. With x the price of a normal chair, 30x + 20 × 3x/4 = 45x = 67,500, so x = ₹1,500.

questions.text: The population of a village reduced from 15,750 to 14,490 because of the outbreak of the Covid-19 pandemic. What is the percentage decrease in the population of that village?
A is twice as efficient as B and takes 45 days less than B to complete a job. Find the number of days in which they can finish the job together.
questions.explanation: A takes half B's time: if A takes t days, B takes 2t, and 2t − t = 45, so A takes 45 days and B 90. Together they do 1/45 + 1/90 = 3/90 = 1/30 of the job a day: 30 days.

questions.text: Anand covers a distance of 20 km at the speed of 4 km/h and he covers remaining distance at the speed of 5 km/h in 5 hours. What is the average speed (in km/h) of Anand for the whole journey?
questions.explanation: The first 20 km take 20/4 = 5 hours and the rest, 5 × 5 = 25 km, another 5 hours. Average speed = 45/10 = 4.5 km/h.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Raining cats and dogs
options: Cats and dogs getting wet in rain
questions.explanation: 'Raining cats and dogs' means raining very heavily.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Anger
questions.explanation: 'Fury' is wild or violent anger. 'Frenzy' is wild excitement, 'dismay' distress and 'delight' great pleasure.

questions.text: Identify the correctly spelt sentence.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Mathematics'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Dowry completely violates women's rights and denies them “similar opportunities” in society.
questions.explanation: Dowry denies women 'an equal standing', that is equal status, in society, which fits a sentence about their rights; the other options make no sense here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given below to fill in the blank in the following sentence. Imminent The king was changing his hiding place every now and then because of ______ danger to his life.
questions.explanation: 'Imminent' means about to happen: 'approaching' danger is danger drawing near, which is why the king kept moving.

questions.text: The sentence given below has one misspelt word. Spot the INCORRECTLY spelt word and select its correct spelling. She comes from an illustrios political family.
questions.explanation: 'Illustrios' is misspelt: the word is 'illustrious', meaning famous and well regarded.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Austere
questions.explanation: 'Austere' means stern and severe in manner; 'genial' means friendly and cheerful. 'Stiff' and 'gruff' are close to 'austere'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. It is of “paramount” importance that you read the instructions before attempting the test.
questions.explanation: 'Paramount' means more important than anything else, so 'of paramount importance' is 'of central importance'. The other options are verbs.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Scintillating
questions.explanation: 'Scintillating' means sparkling or brilliant, so 'dark' is its opposite; 'bright', 'wonderful' and 'amazing' are close to it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Level playing field
questions.explanation: A 'level playing field' is a situation that is fair to everyone, where all compete on equal terms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Anne’s eye _____ is very good for someone of her age.
questions.explanation: 'Eye sight' (usually written 'eyesight') is the ability to see. 'Cite' and 'site' only sound like 'sight', and 'side' does not fit.

questions.text: Choose the sentence that is in simple past tense. A. My uncle broke his promise to keep up with the trend of being healthy. B. My uncle had been breaking his promise to keep up with the trend of being healthy. C. My uncle had broken his promise to keep up with the trend of being healthy. D. My uncle was breaking his promise to keep up with the trend of being healthy.
questions.explanation: 'Broke' is the simple past. B is in the past perfect continuous, C in the past perfect and D in the past continuous.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. You might be wrong, you can’t always be ________.
questions.explanation: 'Right' means correct, the opposite of 'wrong'; 'rite' (a ceremony) and 'write' sound the same but do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The lizard “moves from one whole to another and eats” insects hidden in the hole.
options: moves from one whole to another and eat
moves from one to another and eats
moves from one hole to another and eats
moves from one hole to another but eats
questions.explanation: The lizard moves between holes, so 'whole' (complete) must be its homophone 'hole', as at the end of the sentence; the singular subject keeps 'eats'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A perfect society in which people work well with each other and are happy
questions.explanation: A 'utopia' is an imagined perfect society. A 'dystopia' is its opposite, a society full of suffering.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Cancer is a disease in which some of the body’s cells grow (1)_______ and spread to other parts of the body. Cancer can start (2)______ anywhere in the human body, which is made up of trillions of cells. Normally, human cells grow and multiply (through a process called cell division) to (3)______ new cells as the body needs them. When cells grow old or become damaged, they die, and new cells take their place. Sometimes, this orderly process (4)______ down, and abnormal or damaged cells grow and multiply when they shouldn’t. These cells may form tumours, which are lumps of tissue. Tumours can be cancerous or (5)_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 1.
questions.explanation: Cancer cells grow 'uncontrollably', without the checks that limit the growth of normal cells.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Cancer is a disease in which some of the body’s cells grow (1)_______ and spread to other parts of the body. Cancer can start (2)______ anywhere in the human body, which is made up of trillions of cells. Normally, human cells grow and multiply (through a process called cell division) to (3)______ new cells as the body needs them. When cells grow old or become damaged, they die, and new cells take their place. Sometimes, this orderly process (4)______ down, and abnormal or damaged cells grow and multiply when they shouldn’t. These cells may form tumours, which are lumps of tissue. Tumours can be cancerous or (5)_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 2.
questions.explanation: Cancer can start 'almost' anywhere in the body, that is in nearly any part of it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Cancer is a disease in which some of the body’s cells grow (1)_______ and spread to other parts of the body. Cancer can start (2)______ anywhere in the human body, which is made up of trillions of cells. Normally, human cells grow and multiply (through a process called cell division) to (3)______ new cells as the body needs them. When cells grow old or become damaged, they die, and new cells take their place. Sometimes, this orderly process (4)______ down, and abnormal or damaged cells grow and multiply when they shouldn’t. These cells may form tumours, which are lumps of tissue. Tumours can be cancerous or (5)_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 3.
questions.explanation: Cell division is how the body 'forms' new cells. 'Formulate' is used of plans and ideas, and 'shape' and 'build' do not suit the process.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Cancer is a disease in which some of the body’s cells grow (1)_______ and spread to other parts of the body. Cancer can start (2)______ anywhere in the human body, which is made up of trillions of cells. Normally, human cells grow and multiply (through a process called cell division) to (3)______ new cells as the body needs them. When cells grow old or become damaged, they die, and new cells take their place. Sometimes, this orderly process (4)______ down, and abnormal or damaged cells grow and multiply when they shouldn’t. These cells may form tumours, which are lumps of tissue. Tumours can be cancerous or (5)_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 4.
questions.explanation: An orderly process that fails 'breaks down', that is stops working properly.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Cancer is a disease in which some of the body’s cells grow (1)_______ and spread to other parts of the body. Cancer can start (2)______ anywhere in the human body, which is made up of trillions of cells. Normally, human cells grow and multiply (through a process called cell division) to (3)______ new cells as the body needs them. When cells grow old or become damaged, they die, and new cells take their place. Sometimes, this orderly process (4)______ down, and abnormal or damaged cells grow and multiply when they shouldn’t. These cells may form tumours, which are lumps of tissue. Tumours can be cancerous or (5)_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 5.
questions.explanation: A tumour that is not cancerous is 'benign'. 'Malignant' means cancerous, and 'benevolent' (kind) and 'mild' are not used of tumours in this sense.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'NATION' is written as ‘MZGRLM’ and 'PRINTS' is written as 'KIRMGH'. How will 'BOTTLE' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite letter (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on): NATION → MZGRLM and PRINTS → KIRMGH. So BOTTLE → YLGGOV.

questions.text: In a certain code, the word ‘TEACHER’ is written as ‘RCYAFCP’. The word ‘SCHOOL’ is written as ‘QAFMMJ’. How is the word ‘SUBJECT’ written in the same code?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places back: TEACHER → RCYAFCP and SCHOOL → QAFMMJ. So SUBJECT → QSZHCAR.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? SDR, XHU, CLX, ?, MTD, RXG
questions.explanation: The first letters move 5 forward (S, X, C, H, M, R), the second 4 forward (D, H, L, P, T, X) and the third 3 forward (R, U, X, A, D, G), wrapping round after Z: HPA.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary? 1. FLOWER 2. FLETCHER 3. FLORIST 4. FILTER 5. FLEUR
questions.explanation: FILTER comes first (FI before FL). FLETCHER comes before FLEUR (T before U), and FLORIST before FLOWER (R before W): 4, 2, 5, 3, 1.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term. 4 : 74 :: 6 : ? :: 7 : 353
questions.explanation: Each second term is the cube of the first plus 10: 4³ + 10 = 74 and 7³ + 10 = 353. So 6³ + 10 = 226.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 1, 4, 27, ?, 3125
questions.explanation: The terms are 1¹, 2², 3³, ?, 5⁵, so the missing term is 4⁴ = 256.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 5, 8, ?, 23, 35, 50, 68
questions.explanation: The differences rise by 3: +3, +6, +9, +12, +15, +18. So the missing term is 8 + 6 = 14, and 14 + 9 = 23.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/ number of consonants / vowels in the word) Doctor : Hospital :: Astronomer : ?
questions.explanation: A doctor works in a hospital, and an astronomer in an observatory.

questions.text: Sitara Devi was famous for which of the following classical dance forms?
questions.explanation: Sitara Devi (1920-2014) was a celebrated Kathak dancer; Rabindranath Tagore hailed her as 'Nritya Samragini', empress of dance.

questions.text: What is the share of India in the world's water resources?
questions.explanation: India has about 4% of the world's water resources, against about 2.45% of its surface area and about 16% of its population (the figures NCERT gives).

questions.text: Who inaugurated the new Durbar Hall at Raj Bhavan in Malabar Hill, Mumbai, in February 2022?
questions.explanation: President Ram Nath Kovind inaugurated the rebuilt Durbar Hall of Raj Bhavan, Mumbai, on 11 February 2022.

questions.text: The Shunga dynasty was established by whom among the following rulers?
questions.explanation: Pushyamitra Shunga, commander of the last Mauryan king Brihadratha, killed him in about 185 BCE and founded the Shunga dynasty. Agnimitra was his son and successor.

questions.text: Who among the following has been honoured with Padma Shri for the extensive contribution in Mohiniattam?
questions.explanation: Kanak Rele, the Mumbai dancer and scholar of Mohiniyattam, received the Padma Shri, and in 2013 the Padma Bhushan.

questions.text: In India, the stagnation in agriculture during the colonial rule was permanently broken by the ________.
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution of the late 1960s, built on high-yielding seeds, fertilisers and assured irrigation, ended the stagnation that colonial rule had left in Indian agriculture.

questions.text: As of November 2022, Basavaraj Bommai is the chief minister of _____ state of India.
questions.explanation: Basavaraj Bommai was Chief Minister of Karnataka from July 2021 to May 2023, so also in November 2022.

questions.text: In Andhra Pradesh, who is the Chairman of the state business Advisory Committee?
options: The Finance Minister of the state
The Chief Minister of the state
questions.explanation: The Business Advisory Committee of the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly, which recommends how much time the House gives to its business, meets under the Speaker as its chairman, as in the Lok Sabha.

questions.text: Electrolysis of water is an example of ______.
questions.explanation: An electric current splits water into hydrogen and oxygen (2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂): one compound breaks into simpler substances, a decomposition reaction.

questions.text: Articles 25 to 28 of the Indian Constitution refer to the:
questions.explanation: Articles 25 to 28 make up the right to freedom of religion: freedom of conscience and of religion, freedom to manage religious affairs, freedom from taxes that promote a religion, and freedom from compulsory religious instruction in certain institutions.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In February _____, Mahatma Gandhi decided to withdraw the Non-Cooperation Movement.
questions.explanation: Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922, after a mob set fire to the police station at Chauri Chaura on 4 February, killing the policemen inside.

questions.text: Unemployment is measured in India on the methods prescribed by the:
questions.explanation: Unemployment in India is measured by the concepts the National Sample Survey Organisation (now part of the National Statistical Office) set out for its surveys: usual status, current weekly status and current daily status.

questions.text: If 42 ÷ 2 + m × 3 – 22 ÷ 11 + 3 = 28, then the value of m is:
questions.explanation: Division and multiplication first: 21 + 3m − 2 + 3 = 28, so 3m = 6 and m = 2.

questions.text: A and B can complete a work in 18 days and 27 days, respectively. They start working together and after 8 days, A leaves. In how many days B complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation: Take the work as 54 units: A does 3 a day and B 2. In 8 days together they do 8 × 5 = 40 units, and B finishes the other 14 in 14 ÷ 2 = 7 days.

questions.text: If the ratio of the radius and height of a cylinder is 3 : 2 and radius is 21 cm, then the curved surface area (in cm² ) is: ( Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: The height is 21 × 2/3 = 14 cm, so the curved surface area is 2πrh = 2 × 22/7 × 21 × 14 = 1848 cm².

questions.text: The radius of a cylindrical vessel is increased by 50% and the height is decreased by 50%.What is the change in its volume?
questions.explanation: V = πr²h, so the new volume is 1.5² × 0.5 = 1.125 times the old one: a 12.5% increase.

questions.text: A thief running at 7 km/h is chased by a policeman, whose speed is 8 km/h. If the thief is 85 m ahead of the policeman, then the time required for the policeman to catch the thief will be:
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 8 − 7 = 1 km/h, so he closes 85 m = 0.085 km in 0.085 hours = 0.085 × 60 = 5.1 minutes.

questions.text: In an alloy of 60 grams, the ratio of gold and copper is 2 : 1. How much more of copper should be added to make the ratio 1 : 2?
questions.explanation: The alloy has 40 g of gold and 20 g of copper. For a ratio of 1 : 2 the copper must be 80 g, so 60 g more is needed.

questions.text: A and B together do a piece of work in 12 days, B and C in 15 days, and C and A in 20 days. In how many days can they finish the work if all of them work together?
questions.explanation: Adding the three pairs, 2(A + B + C) do 1/12 + 1/15 + 1/20 = (5 + 4 + 3)/60 = 1/5 of the work a day, so A, B and C together do 1/10 and finish in 10 days.

questions.text: 14 men can build a 55 m long wall in 5 days. What length of a similar wall can be built by 21 men in 4 days?
questions.explanation: 14 × 5 = 70 man-days build 55 m, so 21 × 4 = 84 man-days build 55 × 84/70 = 66 m.

questions.text: Abdul paid ₹5,832 after some years to a bank. He took ₹5,000 loan at the rate of 8% per annum to be compounded annually. Find the time (in years).
The greatest number of three digits that is divisible by 3,12, 24 and 36 is:
questions.explanation: LCM(3, 12, 24, 36) = 72. 999 = 72 × 13 + 63, so the greatest three-digit multiple of 72 is 72 × 13 = 936.

questions.text: R buys two cars of same prices. He sells one at a profit of 12% and the other at a loss of 8%. His overall percentage of profit or loss is :
questions.explanation: With equal cost prices, the overall result is the average of the two: (12 − 8)/2 = 2% profit.

questions.text: A policeman starts chasing a thief who is at a distance of 600 metres. The speeds of the policeman and the thief are 12 km/h and 10 km/h respectively. In what time will the thief be caught?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 12 − 10 = 2 km/h, so he closes 600 m = 0.6 km in 0.6 ÷ 2 = 0.3 hours = 18 minutes.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underline segment in the given sentence. Ever since that leak of private emails, everything the CEO has done has been “viewed with suspicion”.
questions.explanation: To be 'under a cloud' is to be under suspicion or out of favour: everything the CEO has done has been under a cloud. The other phrases carry no such meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. In order to keep ___________ I jog for 45 minutes daily.
questions.explanation: 'Fit' is a homonym: here it means healthy ('keep fit'), but it also means a sudden attack, as in 'a fit of coughing'. 'Feat' (an achievement) and 'feet' make no sense here, and 'fitt' is not how the adjective is spelt.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The principal “went a step farther” to declare 12th June as a holiday for the entire group of schools.
questions.explanation: 'Further' is used of extent or degree, so going beyond what was expected is going 'a step further'; 'farther' is for physical distance. 'Further more' is not used this way, and 'goes' breaks the past tense.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences is an example of present progressive tense?
options: Why has he delayed the work?
Why were you worried about that?
Why is he crying like that?
Why had he been staying in Delhi for such a long time?
questions.explanation: The present progressive (continuous) is 'is/am/are' with the '-ing' form: 'Why is he crying like that?' The others are in the present perfect, the simple past and the past perfect continuous.

questions.text: Which of the following options is most similar in meaning to the given word? Magnificent
questions.explanation: 'Magnificent' means impressively beautiful or splendid: 'grand'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Titan
questions.explanation: A 'titan' is a person or thing of great size, strength or importance: a 'giant'. 'Puny' and 'midget' are nearly opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given below to fill in the blank in the following sentence. Static; Society is not a/an ______ but a dynamic entity.
questions.explanation: 'Static' means unchanging or without movement, and so does 'inert', which contrasts with 'dynamic': 'Society is not an inert but a dynamic entity.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. Although my friends begged me, “I chose not to go for the reunion”.
options: I choose no to go for the reunion.
I chose not to go to the reunion.
I have chose not to go for the reunion.
questions.explanation: 'Go for' is used with an activity ('go for a walk'), but one goes 'to' an event or a place: 'I chose not to go to the reunion.' 'Choose no' and 'have chose' are ungrammatical.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. She was embarrassed because “her friends were laughing on her.”
options: her friends were laughing to her
her friends were laughing at her
her friends were laughing upon her
questions.explanation: To mock someone is to laugh 'at' them: 'her friends were laughing at her'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. The employer is too________ (generous) to give a bonus to the employees.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'generous' is 'stingy', unwilling to give or spend: an employer too stingy to give a bonus. 'Kind' and 'caring' are close to 'generous'.

questions.text: Identify and correct the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. Many people were enduering mental agony and health issues with the change in lifestyle.
questions.explanation: 'Enduering' is misspelt: the word is 'enduring'. The other options are themselves misspellings of 'agony', 'mental' and 'health'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate antonym of the bracketed word to fill in the blank. The land near arid regions is not _________ (barren) enough for growing crops or any kind of vegetation.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'barren' is 'fertile', able to grow crops: the land is not fertile enough for vegetation. 'Arid' and 'stark' are close to 'barren'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. All his attempts to save the wounded animal turned out to be “futile”.
questions.explanation: 'Futile' means having no useful result: 'unsuccessful'. 'Worthwhile' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the appropriate idiom that can replace the underlined word/phrase in the following sentence. Grandmother “revealed the secret”.
options: let the cat out of the bag
let the chips fall where they may
questions.explanation: To 'let the cat out of the bag' is to reveal a secret, often by accident.

questions.text: Choose the sentence that contains correct spellings.
options: The sage said that life is nothing but a journey of comprimises.
The sage said that life is nothing but a journey of compromises.
The sage said that life is nothing but a journey of comprommizes.
The sage said that life is nothing but a journey of compormises.
questions.explanation: Only the second sentence spells 'compromises' correctly; the others have 'comprimises', 'comprommizes' and 'compormises'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. One of the greatest (1)_________ to textiles is light. It is a form of energy that can fade colour and cause chemical and physical (2)_____________of textile fibres. Exposure to both, natural and ultra violet light can threaten the (3)__________ of textiles. Light damage occurs progressively. You must have noticed at home that the most faded folds of curtains are the first to (4) _______ and fall apart. Fading of colours and alterations of hues are the (5)_________ easy-to-detect signs of light damage.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Light fades colours and damages fibres, so it is one of the greatest 'threats' to textiles.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. One of the greatest (1)_________ to textiles is light. It is a form of energy that can fade colour and cause chemical and physical (2)_____________of textile fibres. Exposure to both, natural and ultra violet light can threaten the (3)__________ of textiles. Light damage occurs progressively. You must have noticed at home that the most faded folds of curtains are the first to (4) _______ and fall apart. Fading of colours and alterations of hues are the (5)_________ easy-to-detect signs of light damage.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Light causes the chemical and physical 'degradation', or breaking down, of fibres; 'mortification', 'disgrace' and 'embarrassment' are kinds of shame.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. One of the greatest (1)_________ to textiles is light. It is a form of energy that can fade colour and cause chemical and physical (2)_____________of textile fibres. Exposure to both, natural and ultra violet light can threaten the (3)__________ of textiles. Light damage occurs progressively. You must have noticed at home that the most faded folds of curtains are the first to (4) _______ and fall apart. Fading of colours and alterations of hues are the (5)_________ easy-to-detect signs of light damage.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Light can threaten the 'longevity', that is the long life, of textiles.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. One of the greatest (1)_________ to textiles is light. It is a form of energy that can fade colour and cause chemical and physical (2)_____________of textile fibres. Exposure to both, natural and ultra violet light can threaten the (3)__________ of textiles. Light damage occurs progressively. You must have noticed at home that the most faded folds of curtains are the first to (4) _______ and fall apart. Fading of colours and alterations of hues are the (5)_________ easy-to-detect signs of light damage.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The most faded folds are the first to 'shred', tear into strips, and fall apart; 'distill', 'desolate' and 'irate' do not fit.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. One of the greatest (1)_________ to textiles is light. It is a form of energy that can fade colour and cause chemical and physical (2)_____________of textile fibres. Exposure to both, natural and ultra violet light can threaten the (3)__________ of textiles. Light damage occurs progressively. You must have noticed at home that the most faded folds of curtains are the first to (4) _______ and fall apart. Fading of colours and alterations of hues are the (5)_________ easy-to-detect signs of light damage.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Fading and changed hues are the 'earliest', that is the first, easy-to-detect signs of light damage.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter-cluster series? FZ, GA, JZ, OA, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move +1, +3, +5 (F, G, J, O), so +7 gives V; the second letters alternate Z and A, so Z comes next: VZ.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed) (40, 10, 150); (65, 35, 150)
questions.explanation: The third number is 5 times the difference of the first two: (40 − 10) × 5 = 150 and (65 − 35) × 5 = 150. Likewise (55 − 10) × 5 = 225.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ZERO is coded as 64, and FIVE is coded as 42. How will ELEVEN be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word's code is the sum of its letters' places in the alphabet: ZERO = 26 + 5 + 18 + 15 = 64 and FIVE = 6 + 9 + 22 + 5 = 42. So ELEVEN = 5 + 12 + 5 + 22 + 5 + 14 = 63.

questions.text: If ‘P’ means ‘addition’, ‘Q’ means ‘subtraction’, ‘R’ means ‘multiplication’, and ‘S‘ means ‘division’. What will be the value of the following expression? 76 P 42 S 6 Q 22 P (8 R 15)
questions.explanation: After replacing the letters: 76 + 42 ÷ 6 − 22 + (8 × 15) = 76 + 7 − 22 + 120 = 181.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question marks (?) in the given series? 11, 33, 66, 110, 165, ?, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 22, 33, 44, 55, rising by 11, so the next two are 66 and 77: 165 + 66 = 231 and 231 + 77 = 308.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. BOTH: WJEQ :: FACE:SXVT :: KING: ?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite letter (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on) moved 2 places back: B → Y → W, O → L → J, T → G → E and H → S → Q, and FACE becomes SXVT the same way. So K → P → N, I → R → P, N → M → K and G → T → R: NPKR.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark(?) in the given series? 56000, 14000, 2800, ?, 140, 35, 7

Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All bottles are cups. All cups are plates. Some plates are tables. Conclusions: I Some cups are bottles. II Some plates are cups. III Some tables are plates.
options: Both conclusions II and III follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.
questions.explanation: All bottles are cups, so some cups are bottles (I); all cups are plates, so some plates are cups (II); and some plates are tables, so some tables are plates (III). All three follow.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 42 + 14 ÷ 28 × 98 - 14 = 105
Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Straight 2 Strict 3 Stamp 4 Sticker 5 Streaming
questions.explanation: Stamp (st-a) comes first, then Sticker (st-i); the 'str' words follow by their fourth letters, Straight (a), Streaming (e) and Strict (i): 3, 4, 1, 5, 2.

questions.text: Eight colleagues A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H are sitting in a circle facing the centre, not necessarily in the same order. G sits third to the left of D. E is third to the left of G. H sits to the immediate right of D. B is second to the right of E. F is an immediate neighbour of E. F is third to the left of C. Who is sitting on the immediate left of D?
