questions.explanation: Number the seats 0 to 7 going to D's left, with D at 0: G is at 3, E at 6, H at 7 (D's right), B at 4, F at 5 (seat 7, E's other neighbour, is H's) and C at 2, as F is third to C's left. A takes the seat left over, 1, on D's immediate left.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters / number of consonants / vowels in the word) Rat : Rodent :: Crocodile : ?
questions.explanation: A rat is a rodent, and a crocodile a reptile.

questions.text: In a certain language, ADVICE is written as VDAECI and BELONG is written as LEBGNO. How will BETTER be written in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each half of the word is reversed: ADV ICE → VDA ECI and BEL ONG → LEB GNO. So BET TER → TEB RET: TEBRET.

questions.text: G + H means ‘G is the sister of H’; G × H means ‘G is the father of H’; G ÷ H means ‘G is the son of H’; G – H means ‘ G is the daughter of H’; If P – J + D ÷ S, then how is J related to S?
questions.explanation: P – J: P is J's daughter; J + D: J is D's sister; D ÷ S: D is S's son. J, the sister of S's son, is S's daughter.

questions.text: Six friends (Aman, Biplab, Chirantan, Divya, Elizabeth and Firoz) are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Aman sits third to the left of Biplab. Chirantan is an immediate neighbour of Aman. Elizabeth sits second to the right of Divya. Chirantan is not an immediate neighbour of Divya. Who sit between Aman and Biplab from the left of Aman?
questions.explanation: Number the seats 0 to 5 going to Biplab's left, with Biplab at 0: Aman, third to his left, is at 3. Whichever of 2 and 4 Chirantan takes, the only free seats two apart for Divya and Elizabeth (two to Divya's right) are 1 and 5, so Divya is at 1, Chirantan, not beside her, at 4, Elizabeth at 5 and Firoz at 2. Going left from Aman: Chirantan, Elizabeth, then Biplab.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? GPQU, FQRT, ?, DSTR, CTUQ
questions.explanation: The first letters move 1 back (G, F, E, D, C), the second and third 1 forward (P, Q, R, S, T and Q, R, S, T, U) and the fourth 1 back (U, T, S, R, Q): ERSS.

questions.text: The famous Nauchandi Fair happens once a year in the state of ______________.
questions.explanation: The Nauchandi Mela is held every year at the Nauchandi ground in Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, around the Chandi Devi temple and the dargah of Bale Miyan, which stand almost opposite each other.

questions.text: As per November 2022, who is the Chief Economic Advisor of India?
questions.explanation: V. Anantha Nageswaran became Chief Economic Adviser on 28 January 2022, after Krishnamurthy Subramanian's term ended in December 2021, and held the post in November 2022 and when the exam was held (January 2023).

questions.text: Who was the Prime Minister during the Eighth Five Year Plan?
questions.explanation: The Eighth Five Year Plan (1992-97) was launched under P. V. Narasimha Rao, Prime Minister from 1991 to 1996; Manmohan Singh was his Finance Minister.

questions.text: Who sworn in as the 49th Chief Justice of India in August 2022?
questions.explanation: Justice Uday Umesh Lalit was sworn in as the 49th Chief Justice of India on 27 August 2022, succeeding N. V. Ramana, the 48th.

questions.text: Jatin Ghoswami won numerous awards for his contribution in which dance form?
questions.explanation: Jatin Goswami of Assam is a Sattriya dancer and guru; he received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Sattriya in 2004 and the Padma Shri in 2008.

questions.text: Development of ________ was the motto of the first five year plan in India.
questions.explanation: The First Five Year Plan (1951-56) gave the top priority to agriculture, with irrigation and power, to meet the food shortage after Partition.

questions.text: Which among the following metals has the highest electrical conductivity?
questions.explanation: Silver conducts electricity better than any other metal; copper and gold come next.

questions.text: Who among the following lit the Olympic cauldron in the Summer Olympics 2020?
questions.explanation: The tennis player Naomi Osaka lit the cauldron at the opening ceremony of the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, held on 23 July 2021 after a year's delay for Covid-19.

questions.text: Swachh Bharat Mission was launched to fulfil the vision of a cleaner India by _______.
questions.explanation: The Swachh Bharat Mission, launched on 2 October 2014, aimed at a clean India by 2 October 2019, Mahatma Gandhi's 150th birth anniversary.

questions.text: What is the minimum age requirement to be elected as President of India?
questions.explanation: Under Article 58 a candidate for President must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old and qualified for election to the Lok Sabha.

questions.text: The football club Mohun Bagan was founded in which year?
questions.explanation: Mohun Bagan Athletic Club was founded in Calcutta on 15 August 1889.

questions.text: The fundamental duties in the Indian Constitution are taken from which country’s Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Duties (Article 51A, added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976) were inspired by the Constitution of the former USSR.

questions.text: Which of the following is an exclusive martial dance form of Manipur?
questions.explanation: Thang-Ta, Manipur's martial art of the sword (thang) and spear (ta), is also performed as a ritual dance. Bihu is from Assam, Kummi from Tamil Nadu and Kerala, and Danda Jatra from Odisha.

questions.text: Neonatal mortality rate refers to the number of deaths during the first ________ of life per 1000 live births in a given year or other period.
questions.explanation: The neonatal period is the first 28 days of life; the neonatal mortality rate counts the deaths in it per 1,000 live births.

questions.text: Which of the following comes under Mollusca?
questions.explanation: The octopus is a mollusc, like snails and squids. The turtle is a reptile, Musca (the housefly) an insect and the stingray a cartilaginous fish.

questions.text: Identify the only natural satellite of Earth.
questions.explanation: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite. Callisto and Io (printed 'Lo') are moons of Jupiter, and Titan is Saturn's largest moon.

questions.text: __________ are things a firm owns.
questions.explanation: Assets are what a firm owns, such as cash, buildings and machinery; liabilities, including loans and debentures, are what it owes.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: General Dyer took command during the martial law in which year?
questions.explanation: Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer took command at Amritsar in April 1919 and ordered the firing at Jallianwala Bagh on 13 April; martial law was proclaimed in parts of Punjab that month.

questions.text: What helps in expanding trade and commerce and brings in foreign exchange?
questions.explanation: Exports of manufactured goods expand trade and commerce and earn foreign exchange; imports spend it.

questions.text: Which of the following archaeological sites is NOT located in present day India?
questions.explanation: Mehrgarh, a Neolithic site near the Bolan Pass, is in Balochistan, Pakistan. Mahagara is in Uttar Pradesh, Chirand in Bihar and Hallur in Karnataka.

questions.text: A can run 1 km in 4 min, and B can cover the same distance in 4 min 10 sec. By what distance can A beat B in a 1 km race?
questions.explanation: A runs 1 km in 240 seconds and B in 250. In A's 240 seconds B covers 1000 × 240/250 = 960 m, so A wins by 40 m.

questions.text: A sum of money doubles itself at compound interest in 10 years. In how many years will it be four times at the same rate of interest?
questions.explanation: At compound interest the money doubles every 10 years, so it doubles again in the next 10: four times in 20 years.

questions.text: The marked price of a chair was Rs.5,000. The shopkeeper was offering a discount of 20%, but on further bargaining agreed to offer a successive discount and finally sold the chair for Rs.3,600. What was the second discount offered by the shopkeeper?
questions.explanation: After the first discount the price is 5,000 × 0.8 = ₹4,000. 3,600/4,000 = 0.9, so the second discount is 10%.

questions.text: If 90 is divided into two parts in the ratio of 2:3, then what are the values of two parts?
The weight of five boys is recorded as 22.450 kg, 24.150 kg, 24.720 kg, 28.530 kg and 25.150 kg. What is the average weight of all the five boys?
A bus covered a distance of 72 km in 60 min. What is the speed of the bus in km/h?
questions.explanation: 60 minutes is 1 hour, so the speed is 72 km/h.

questions.text: A hemisphere of lead of radius 5 cm is cast into a right circular cone of height 75 cm. If the volume of cone and hemisphere are equal, then what will be the radius of the base of the cone?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 1.8 cm, the exact radius to one decimal place: (2/3)π × 5³ = (1/3)πr² × 75 gives 250/3 = 25r², so r² = 10/3 and r = √(10/3) ≈ 1.83 cm.

questions.text: A, B, and C start running simultaneously, starting from a point, around a circular track of length 900m, with respective speeds of 3m/s, 5m/s, and 6m/s. A and B run in the same direction while C runs in the opposite direction of the other two. After how much time will they meet for the first time?
questions.explanation: A and B close on each other at 5 − 3 = 2 m/s, so they meet every 900/2 = 450 s; A and C at 3 + 6 = 9 m/s, every 100 s; B and C at 5 + 6 = 11 m/s, every 900/11 s. All three first meet at the LCM of these, 900 s = 15 minutes.

questions.text: The difference between two numbers is 1086. When we divide the larger number by the smaller we get six as quotient and six as remainder. Find the larger number.
questions.explanation: If the smaller number is x, the larger is 6x + 6, and 5x + 6 = 1086 gives x = 216. The larger is 6 × 216 + 6 = 1302.

questions.text: After getting two successive discounts Rupa got a dress at Rs. 1619.20, whose marked price is Rs. 2000. If the second discount is 8 percent, then the first discount is:

A and B together can do a piece of work in 20 days, and B and C together can do the same work in 100 days. If B alone can do the same work in 140 days, then in how many days will A and C together can complete the same work?
A can do a piece of work in 4 days, while B can do it in 8 days. If they work on alternate days beginning with A, then in how many days will the work be completed?
questions.explanation: A does 1/4 of the work a day and B 1/8, so each two-day pair does 3/8. After 4 days 6/8 is done, and A finishes the remaining 2/8 on day 5.

questions.text: If a diamond ring is sold for ₹5,94,320, then a woman will get a loss of 5%. At what price should she sell it so that her profit becomes 25%?
In a panchayat election, there were two candidates A and B. Candidate A got 42% of the votes and lost to B by 8000 votes. What is the total number of votes?
questions.explanation: B got 58%, so the margin is 58% − 42% = 16% of the votes, which is 8000: the total is 8000 ÷ 0.16 = 50000.

questions.text: Select the correct word for the blanks in the given sentence. My father loves to read a ________ and wants to _________ flight tickets for Delhi.
questions.explanation: 'Book' fits both blanks: as a noun, something to read, and as a verb, to reserve tickets.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Doleful
questions.explanation: 'Doleful' means sad and mournful, so its antonym is 'joyous'. 'Dismal' is close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the following sentence. In “edition” to snacks, please bring cold drinks.
questions.explanation: The phrase is 'in addition to', meaning as well as; an 'edition' is one version of a book or newspaper.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Despise
questions.explanation: To 'despise' is to regard with strong dislike or contempt, so 'dislike' is the nearest. 'Treasure' and 'like' are nearly its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. “Does it” difficult to drive a lorry through a crowded narrow lane?
questions.explanation: 'Difficult' is an adjective and needs the verb 'be', not 'do': 'Isn't it difficult to drive a lorry through a crowded narrow lane?' 'Aren't it' breaks agreement, and 'Would it difficult' still lacks 'be'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. In the blink of an eye
options: To allow someone to move fast
questions.explanation: Something that happens 'in the blink of an eye' happens very fast, almost instantly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The teacher ___________ another picture in the slide to explain his point of view.
questions.explanation: To explain his point the teacher 'inserted', that is added, another picture in the slide. 'Excluded' is the opposite, and 'extracted' and 'obtained' do not fit 'in the slide'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. An arm and a leg
questions.explanation: Something that costs 'an arm and a leg' is very expensive.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Seceade' is misspelt: the word is 'secede', to withdraw formally from a union or organisation.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. One day, an old man was walking through the forest ________suddenly he heard someone crying for help.
questions.explanation: An action in progress ('was walking') cut into by a sudden event is joined to it with 'when': 'was walking through the forest when suddenly he heard someone crying for help.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Annoy
questions.explanation: To 'annoy' is to irritate. 'Delight' is its opposite, and 'testify' and 'suppress' are unrelated.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Tomorrow in the exam hall, I “am” “busy” “writing” “answers”.
questions.explanation: 'Tomorrow' points to the future, so 'am' should be 'will be': 'Tomorrow in the exam hall, I will be busy writing answers.'

questions.text: Select the correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Ever since young, we were taught that we “can” obey our elders.
questions.explanation: Being taught to obey elders expresses a duty, which takes 'should': 'we were taught that we should obey our elders.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. Due to the attack his vital organs _______ functioning.
questions.explanation: 'Ceased' (stopped) fits: his vital organs stopped functioning. 'Seized' sounds similar but means grabbed, 'sized' means measured or sorted by size, and 'seas' is a noun.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Cynical
questions.explanation: A 'cynical' person expects the worst of people and things, so the antonym is 'optimistic'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Mirrors (1) ________ used since ages. It is said that Archimedes used huge mirrors to focus the heat of the sun’s rays on enemy ships to burn them. The same (2) _______ is used in solar cookers, where mirrors are used to reflect and focus the sun’s rays onto cooking containers. Astronomers use huge concave mirrors to focus starlight. The mirrors used in telescopes are polished by giving a thin coat of silver or aluminium to the glass. With the telescopes, astronomers can see the heavenly bodies, but even without the telescopes one can see the moon. A full moon shining (3) ________ is a beautiful sight. But it is also a puzzle, because if the sun and the moon both give the same light, then why is the moonlight more pleasant?The reason is that the moon reflects very (4) ______ sunlight, in fact, only seven per cent of the light it receives. The earth reflects about half of the radiation that it receives from the sun. Imagine how bright the earth must be looking from the moon! One can even read a book on the moon in the earthlight. However, you do not have to travel all the way to the moon to realise how strong the earth's light is. Observe the crescent moon soon after the new moon. The bright crescent is illuminated by the sun. The rest of the moon is illuminated by earthlight. In other words, the light reflected by the earth is falling on the moon. This is being reflected back to us and is strong enough to show the moon (5) _______. As the crescent increases in size, this effect disappears.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Mirrors' is plural and the use runs from the past to now ('since ages'), so the present perfect passive 'have been used' fits.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 1248, 887, 598, 429, ?, 259, 234
Which of the mathematical signs should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct? 72 - 12 + 8 × 6 ÷ 24 = 30
questions.explanation: After interchanging − and ÷: 72 ÷ 12 + 8 × 6 − 24 = 6 + 48 − 24 = 30.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Brown 2 Brand 3 Brunch 4 Branch 5 Brimming
questions.explanation: All begin with 'Br': Branch and Brand share 'Bran', and c comes before d; then come Brimming (bri-), Brown (bro-) and Brunch (bru-): 4, 2, 5, 1, 3.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters / number of consonants / vowels in the word.) Uttar Pradesh : Lucknow :: Odisha : ?
questions.explanation: Lucknow is the capital of Uttar Pradesh, and Bhubaneswar the capital of Odisha.

questions.text: E – F means ‘E is the mother of F’; E ÷ F means ‘E is the father of F’; E + F means ‘E is the sister of F’; E × F means ‘E is the brother of F’; If T × U ÷ D × C, then how is T related to C?
questions.explanation: T × U: T is U's brother. U ÷ D: U is D's father. D × C: D is C's brother, so U is C's father too, and T, U's brother, is C's father's brother.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (8, 280, 5); (11, 308, 4)
questions.explanation: The middle number is 7 times the product of the outer two: 8 × 5 × 7 = 280 and 11 × 4 × 7 = 308. Likewise 13 × 7 × 7 = 637.

questions.text: Six friends (Aman, Biplab, Chirantan, Divya, Elizabeth and Firoz) are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Aman sits third to the left of Biplab. Chirantan is an immediate neighbour of Aman. Elizabeth sits second to the right of Divya. Chirantan is not an immediate neighbour of Divya. Who sits between Biplab and Firoz?
questions.explanation: Among six, third to the left is directly opposite, so Aman faces Biplab. With Elizabeth second to Divya's right, and Chirantan beside Aman but not beside Divya, the only order going round to Biplab's left is Biplab, Divya, Firoz, Aman, Chirantan, Elizabeth. Divya sits between Biplab and Firoz.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. COURAGE : EQWTCIG : : POWER : RQYGT : : WISDOM : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: COURAGE → EQWTCIG and POWER → RQYGT. So WISDOM → YKUFQO.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘TRIP’ is coded as GIRK and ‘FAST’ is coded as UZHG. How will ‘HOME’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on): TRIP → GIRK and FAST → UZHG. So HOME → SLNV.

questions.text: In a certain code language, If BROTHER is coded as 14 and ACTIVE is coded as 12, how will CHOCOLATE be coded in that langugae?
questions.explanation: The code is twice the number of letters: BROTHER has 7 letters (14) and ACTIVE 6 (12). CHOCOLATE has 9, so 18.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 26 - 13 + 39 ÷ 117 × 24= 31
Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? BTWH, DRUJ, FPSL, ?, JLOP
questions.explanation: The first and fourth letters move 2 forward (B, D, F, H, J and H, J, L, N, P), and the second and third 2 back (T, R, P, N, L and W, U, S, Q, O): HNQN.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All cats are rats. Some rats are white. All white are milk. Conclusions: I. Some rats are cats. II. Some white are rats. III. Some milk are white.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.
Both conclusions II and III follow.
questions.explanation: All cats are rats, so some rats are cats (I). Some rats are white, so some white are rats (II). All white are milk, so some milk are white (III). All three follow.

questions.text: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 24, 26, ?, 164, 658, 3292

Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. A sits to the immediate left of C. E sits third to the right of D. D is an immediate neighbour of C. B is an immediate neighbour of both E and F. Who sits second to the left of A?
questions.explanation: A is at C's immediate left, so D, C's other neighbour, sits at C's right, and E, third to D's right, sits next to A. B, beside both E and F, takes the seat after E. Going round to C's left: C, A, E, B, F, D, so B sits second to A's left.

questions.text: Which of the following letters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter series? F, P, X, D, H, ?
questions.explanation: Counting the letters' places and carrying on past Z (D = 30, H = 34), the steps are +10, +8, +6, +4, +2: F (6), P (16), X (24), D (30), H (34), then 36, which is J.

questions.text: Which Five-year Plan focused on infrastructure development, that is, power and transport?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the First Plan (1951-56). It is best remembered for its stress on agriculture, but the largest shares of its planned outlay went to irrigation and power (about 27%) and to transport and communications (about 24%).

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an example of metamorphic rocks?
questions.explanation: Granite is an igneous rock, formed as magma cools slowly below the surface. Quartzite (from sandstone), gneiss (often from granite) and schist (from shale) are metamorphic rocks.

questions.text: Which of the following is not one of the five basic food groups suggested by the Indian Council of Medical Research?
questions.explanation: ICMR's five food groups are cereals and grains, pulses and legumes, milk and meat products, fruits and vegetables, and fats and sugars. Carbohydrates and proteins are nutrients, not food groups.

questions.text: The Governor of State possesses the pardoning power under which Article of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: Article 161 gives the Governor power to grant pardons, reprieves and remissions, and to suspend, remit or commute sentences, for offences against State laws; Article 72 gives the President such powers.

questions.text: Mysuru Dasara Festival is a ______-day festival celebrated in Karnataka.
questions.explanation: Mysuru Dasara, Karnataka's state festival (Nadahabba), runs for ten days: the nine nights of Navaratri and Vijayadashami, the day of the Jamboo Savari procession.

questions.text: FIH Men's Hockey World Cup 2018 was organised by which country?
questions.explanation: India hosted the 2018 Men's Hockey World Cup at the Kalinga Stadium, Bhubaneswar, in November-December 2018; Belgium won it.

questions.text: Raja Harishchandra, a movie directed by Dadasaheb Phalke in 1913, is considered as first full lenth film of _________ .
questions.explanation: Dadasaheb Phalke's silent film 'Raja Harishchandra' (1913) is regarded as India's first full-length feature film.

questions.text: Who among the following artists has won Padma Vibhushan Award in 2000?
questions.explanation: The Odissi guru Kelucharan Mohapatra received the Padma Vibhushan in 2000; Birju Maharaj had received his in 1986.

questions.text: How many nations had participated in the Asian Games 2018?
questions.explanation: All 45 member nations of the Olympic Council of Asia took part in the 2018 Asian Games, held at Jakarta and Palembang, Indonesia.

questions.text: Which of the following is a fundamental duty?
options: To endanger public property and to abjure violence
To safeguard public property and to expose violence
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
To safeguard public property and to accept violence
questions.explanation: Article 51A(i) makes it a fundamental duty 'to safeguard public property and to abjure violence', that is, to renounce it.

questions.text: ___________substituted the planning commission in India.
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog)
questions.explanation: The National Institution for Transforming India (NITI Aayog), set up on 1 January 2015, replaced the Planning Commission.

questions.text: Duralumin is an alloy made up of aluminium and ___________.
questions.explanation: Duralumin is mostly aluminium with about 4% copper and small amounts of magnesium and manganese; light and strong, it is used in aircraft.

questions.text: N. Biren Singh became the chief minister of __________ state of India in March 2022.
questions.explanation: N. Biren Singh of the BJP was sworn in as Chief Minister of Manipur for a second term in March 2022, after the state's assembly election.

questions.text: Which among the following is the oldest vedas?
questions.explanation: The Rigveda, a collection of over a thousand hymns, is the oldest of the four Vedas; the Sama, Yajur and Atharva Vedas came later.

questions.text: In which year was the first cement plant setup in India?
questions.explanation: India's first cement plant was set up in Chennai (then Madras) in 1904.

questions.text: In which year was the National Population Policy (NPP), the central government's second population policy formulated in India?
questions.explanation: The National Population Policy 2000 came after the first such policy, of 1976. It aimed to bring fertility down to replacement level by 2010 and to stabilise the population by 2045.

questions.text: In economics, CRR stands for _______.
questions.explanation: CRR, the Cash Reserve Ratio, is the share of its net demand and time liabilities that a bank must keep with the RBI as cash.

questions.text: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana account can be opened by the parents of a girl child or legal guardians, any time before the girl child attains ___________.
questions.explanation: A Sukanya Samriddhi account can be opened for a girl by a parent or legal guardian at any time until she turns 10.

questions.text: Who has been appointed as India’s Ambassador to Slovak Republic in October 2022?
questions.explanation: In October 2022 Apoorva Srivastava, then India's Consul General in Toronto, was named India's next Ambassador to the Slovak Republic.

questions.text: The folk dance ‘Lambadi’ is associated with which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Lambadi is the dance of the Lambadi (Banjara) people of Andhra Pradesh: the women dance in mirror-studded costumes while the men sing and drum.

questions.text: On dividing a number by 42, we get 120 as the quotient and 0 as the remainder. On dividing the same number by 41, what will be the remainder?
questions.explanation: The number is 42 × 120 = 5040, and 5040 = 41 × 122 + 38, so the remainder is 38.

questions.text: In a race around a circular track an athlete runs at 10 m/sec in the first round, at 20 m/sec in the second round and at 30 m/sec in the third round. Find his average speed (in m/sec) for the race. (correct to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanation: Each round is the same distance d, so the average speed is 3d ÷ (d/10 + d/20 + d/30) = 3 ÷ (11/60) = 180/11 = 16.36 m/sec.

questions.text: The selling price of 40 articles is equal to the cost price of 60 articles. Find the gain percentage.
questions.explanation: Selling 40 articles brings in the cost of 60, a gain of the cost of 20: 20/40 × 100 = 50%.

questions.text: Ramesh borrowed some money and agreed to pay-off by paying Rs.4,565 at the end of the first year and Rs.6,534 at the end of the second year. If the rate of compound interest is 10% per annum, find the amount borrowed by Ramesh.
questions.explanation: The sum borrowed is the present value of the two payments: 4,565/1.1 + 6,534/1.1² = 4,150 + 5,400 = ₹9,550.

questions.text: Pankaj offers a cash discount of Rs.250 first and then two successive discounts of 8% and 5% on the sale of a chair. If the marked price of the chair is Rs.4,250, what is the final price of the chair for a customer after the given discount scheme?
questions.explanation: After the cash discount the price is 4,250 − 250 = ₹4,000; then 4,000 × 0.92 × 0.95 = 3,680 × 0.95 = ₹3,496.

questions.text: The ages of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 8, respectively. After 8 years, the ratio of their ages will be 3 : 4. What is the sum of their present ages?
questions.explanation: With ages 5x and 8x, (5x + 8)/(8x + 8) = 3/4 gives 20x + 32 = 24x + 24, so x = 2. The ages are 10 and 16 years, 26 in all.

questions.text: In a 8000 m race around a circular stadium having a circumference of 2000 m, the fastest runner Rohan and the slowest runner Soham starting from the same point and reach the starting point together at the end of the 10th minute, for the first time after the start of the race. If Rohan runs at twice the speed of Soham, what is the time taken by Rohan to finish the race?
questions.explanation: Soham takes twice as long as Rohan for a lap, so they are first together at the start when Rohan has run two laps and Soham one: 10 minutes. Rohan's 2000 m lap takes 5 minutes, so the 8000 m race, 4 laps, takes him 20 minutes.

questions.text: Three runners Aman, Ramesh and Naresh run a race, with Aman finishing 48 metres ahead of Ramesh and 68 metres ahead of Naresh. In another race of same length, Ramesh finishes 25 metres ahead of Naresh. Each runner travels the entire distance at a constant speed. Find the length of the race.
questions.explanation: When Aman finishes a race of L metres, Ramesh has run L − 48 and Naresh L − 68. Ramesh beats Naresh by 25 m, so (L − 68)/(L − 48) = (L − 25)/L: L² − 68L = L² − 73L + 1200, so 5L = 1200 and L = 240 metres.

questions.text: The average of the first 16 natural numbers is:
In an election, a candidate who gets 70% of the votes is elected by a majority of 500 votes. What is the total number of votes?
questions.explanation: With two candidates the winner gets 70% and the loser 30%, so the majority of 500 is 40% of the votes: 500 ÷ 0.4 = 1250.

questions.text: Riya can complete a piece of work in 12 days, Reeta in 18 days and Geeta in 24 days. Reeta and Geeta worked together for 6 days and then Geeta was replaced by Riya. In how many days altogether was the work completed?
questions.explanation: Reeta and Geeta do 1/18 + 1/24 = 7/72 of the work a day, so 42/72 = 7/12 in 6 days. Reeta and Riya do 1/18 + 1/12 = 5/36 a day, so the remaining 5/12 takes (5/12) ÷ (5/36) = 3 days: 9 days altogether.

questions.text: A, B, and C can do a piece of work in 42, 56, and 63 days respectively. They started the work together but A left the work 10 days before the completion of the work while B left the work 12 days before the completion. Find the number of days (approximate) to complete the whole work.
questions.explanation: Taking the work as 504 units (the LCM of 42, 56 and 63), A, B and C do 12, 9 and 8 units a day. If it takes T days, 12(T − 10) + 9(T − 12) + 8T = 504, so 29T = 732 and T = 25.2, about 25 days.

questions.text: The marked price of an AC is Rs. 36800. The shopkeeper offers an off season discount of 11 percent on it. The selling price of the AC is:
questions.explanation: The selling price is 89% of the marked price: 36,800 × 0.89 = ₹32,752.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Camouflage
questions.explanation: To 'camouflage' is to hide or disguise something; the opposite is to 'reveal' it. 'Cloak' and 'disguise' are synonyms, and a 'bluff' is a pretence.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Each and every individual has the_______ to follow her/his own religion.
questions.explanation: 'Freedom' fits: everyone is free to follow a religion of his or her choice. 'Compulsion' and 'expulsion' say the opposite, and 'economy' makes no sense here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The subsequent QR codes will “helping you access” the data.
questions.explanation: A modal such as 'will' takes the base form of the verb: 'The subsequent QR codes will help you access the data.'

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the following sentence. The cowboys were injured badly as they were involved in a “dual”.
questions.explanation: A 'duel' is a fight between two people; 'dual' means having two parts. A 'duet' is music for two, and to 'dwell' is to live somewhere.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Rain on someone’s parade
options: To spoil and ruin a happy moment
To restore the disturbed law and order situation
To blame and hurt an innocent child
To test and check a brilliant student
questions.explanation: To 'rain on someone's parade' is to spoil a happy moment or plan for them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. What “is the qualities” of a good teacher?
questions.explanation: The subject 'the qualities' is plural, so the verb must be 'are': 'What are the qualities of a good teacher?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Sensitive
questions.explanation: 'Sensitive' means quick to feel or respond; 'numb' means without feeling. 'Understanding' and 'diplomatic' are close to 'sensitive' in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Miss the boat
options: Fail to take advantage of an opportunity
It is late for the boat
questions.explanation: To 'miss the boat' is to lose an opportunity by acting too late.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Brazen
questions.explanation: 'Brazen' means bold and without shame. 'Meek' and 'courteous' are nearly opposite, and 'loyal' is unrelated.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. He was supposed to __________ this work.
questions.explanation: 'Supposed to' takes the base form of a verb: 'He was supposed to do this work.' 'Due' and 'dew', which sound like 'do', are an adjective and a noun, and 'doux' describes a sweet wine.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Nadir
questions.explanation: The 'nadir' is the lowest point; its opposite is the 'zenith', the highest point. An 'abyss' is a deep chasm, close in sense to 'nadir'.

questions.text: Select the correct word for the blanks in the given sentence. My sister _________ lift a box of 5 kilograms and I have a _________ of carrot juice.
questions.explanation: 'Can' fits both blanks: the modal 'can lift' (is able to lift), and a 'can' of juice, a metal container. 'Could' fits only the first blank and 'bottle' only the second.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. I will driving/ you to/ the station/ in the morning.
questions.explanation: After the modal 'will' the verb takes its base form: 'I will drive you to the station in the morning.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Sombre
questions.explanation: 'Sombre' means dark, gloomy or sad, and 'doleful' means sorrowful.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'intermittence', with a double 't'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Indian Army, also known as the Bhartiya Thal Sena, is the armed forces' (1)____________ component. It grew from the East India Company's military forces, eventually (2)__________ the British Indian Army and, after independence, the Indian Army. It is regarded as the world's second-largest active army. The Indian Army's purpose is to ensure national (3)__________ and preserve India's sovereignty, territorial integrity, and harmony against external (4)____________ and intimidation. It also entails offering humanitarian assistance and support to the (5)_________ public during natural catastrophes and unforeseen times.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: The Army (the Thal Sena, 'thal' meaning land) is the 'land-based' arm of the armed forces, beside the navy and the air force.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Indian Army, also known as the Bhartiya Thal Sena, is the armed forces' (1)____________ component. It grew from the East India Company's military forces, eventually (2)__________ the British Indian Army and, after independence, the Indian Army. It is regarded as the world's second-largest active army. The Indian Army's purpose is to ensure national (3)__________ and preserve India's sovereignty, territorial integrity, and harmony against external (4)____________ and intimidation. It also entails offering humanitarian assistance and support to the (5)_________ public during natural catastrophes and unforeseen times.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: The Company's forces grew into the British Indian Army: 'eventually becoming' it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Indian Army, also known as the Bhartiya Thal Sena, is the armed forces' (1)____________ component. It grew from the East India Company's military forces, eventually (2)__________ the British Indian Army and, after independence, the Indian Army. It is regarded as the world's second-largest active army. The Indian Army's purpose is to ensure national (3)__________ and preserve India's sovereignty, territorial integrity, and harmony against external (4)____________ and intimidation. It also entails offering humanitarian assistance and support to the (5)_________ public during natural catastrophes and unforeseen times.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: The Army's purpose is to ensure national 'security' and preserve the country's sovereignty.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Indian Army, also known as the Bhartiya Thal Sena, is the armed forces' (1)____________ component. It grew from the East India Company's military forces, eventually (2)__________ the British Indian Army and, after independence, the Indian Army. It is regarded as the world's second-largest active army. The Indian Army's purpose is to ensure national (3)__________ and preserve India's sovereignty, territorial integrity, and harmony against external (4)____________ and intimidation. It also entails offering humanitarian assistance and support to the (5)_________ public during natural catastrophes and unforeseen times.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: The Army guards the country against external 'aggression', an attack by another country, which pairs with 'intimidation'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Indian Army, also known as the Bhartiya Thal Sena, is the armed forces' (1)____________ component. It grew from the East India Company's military forces, eventually (2)__________ the British Indian Army and, after independence, the Indian Army. It is regarded as the world's second-largest active army. The Indian Army's purpose is to ensure national (3)__________ and preserve India's sovereignty, territorial integrity, and harmony against external (4)____________ and intimidation. It also entails offering humanitarian assistance and support to the (5)_________ public during natural catastrophes and unforeseen times.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: It helps the 'general' public, that is ordinary people, during disasters.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All stems are leaves. All fruits are leaves. All leaves are trunks. Conclusions: I. All fruits are trunks. II. All trunks are stems. III. Some trunks are fruits.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: Every fruit is a leaf and every leaf is a trunk, so all fruits are trunks (I), and so some trunks are fruits (III). Nothing says every trunk is a stem, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? BGR, CIV, ELZ, HPD, LUH, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move +1, +2, +3, +4 (B, C, E, H, L), so +5 gives Q; the second move +2, +3, +4, +5 (G, I, L, P, U), so +6 gives A, wrapping round after Z; the third move +4 (R, V, Z, D, H), giving L: QAL.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. QPON : RRRR :: IJGK : JLJO :: PKON : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, +2, +3 and +4: QPON → RRRR and IJGK → JLJO. So PKON → QMRR.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 83, 299, 424, 488, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 216, 125 and 64, that is 6³, 5³ and 4³. The next is 3³ = 27: 488 + 27 = 515.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. BIND : FFKH :: ROMP : VLJT :: SPUN : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +4, −3, −3 and +4: BIND → FFKH and ROMP → VLJT. So SPUN → WMRR.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 11 * 10 * 10 * 240 * 2
questions.explanation: 11 × 10 + 10 = 240 ÷ 2, as both sides equal 120.

questions.text: Seven people, A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a straight row, facing north. A sits second from the left. Only two people sit between A and C. Only three people sit between D and F and D is an immediate neighbour of A. B is an immediate neighbour of D and E is not an immediate neighbour of C. Who sits to the extreme left?
questions.explanation: A is 2nd from the left, so C is 5th. D, beside A, cannot be 1st (F would then be 5th, C's place), so D is 3rd and F 7th, and B, beside D, is 4th. E is not beside C, so E takes the 1st place rather than the 6th: E sits at the extreme left.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘grasshopper ant’ is coded as ‘ja do’, ‘seed blade’ is coded as ‘ju fo’, ‘blade ant’ is coded as ‘fo do’, and ‘grasshopper seed’ is coded as ‘ja ju’. What is the code for ‘blade’?
questions.explanation: 'Blade' is in 'seed blade' (ju fo) and 'blade ant' (fo do), and 'fo' is the only code word common to both.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 48 + 36 - 81 × 9 ÷ 2 = 66
Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? DHVY, GKSV, ?, MQMP, PTJM
questions.explanation: The first and second letters move 3 forward (D, G, J, M, P and H, K, N, Q, T), and the third and fourth 3 back (V, S, P, M, J and Y, V, S, P, M): JNPS.

questions.text: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. F is an immediate neighbour of A. D sits second to the right of E. B is an immediate neighbour of E and sits second to the right of C. F sits second to the right of D. A is not an immediate neighbour of E. Who sits to the immediate left of E?
questions.explanation: Numbering the seats to the right of E from 1 to 5: D is 2 and F is 4. If B were E's left neighbour (5), C would be 3 and no seat beside F would be left for A; so B is 1, C is 5 and A is 3. C sits to E's immediate left.

questions.text: Looking at a photograph, Anjali said, “He is the only son of my father.” How is the man in the photograph related to Anjali?
questions.explanation: The only son of Anjali's father is Anjali's brother.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term. 13 : 225 :: 16 : ? :: 17 : 361
questions.explanation: Each second number is the square of 2 more than the first: (13 + 2)² = 225 and (17 + 2)² = 361. So (16 + 2)² = 324.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 10, 11, 15, 42, 58, 183,?
questions.explanation: The differences are 1, 4, 27, 16, 125: cubes of odd numbers (1³, 3³, 5³) alternating with squares of even numbers (2², 4²). The next is 6² = 36: 183 + 36 = 219.

questions.text: In a certain code the word ‘BARK’ is numerically coded as 5132. The word ‘BEND’ is numerically coded as 5749. How is the word ‘BEARD’ numerically coded in the same code?
questions.explanation: Each letter keeps its own digit: B = 5, A = 1, R = 3 and K = 2 from BARK, and E = 7, N = 4 and D = 9 from BEND. So BEARD = 5 7 1 3 9: 57139.

questions.text: Which of the following options represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1. Glob 2. Globule 3. Global 4. Globe 5. Gloom
questions.explanation: Glob comes first, as three of the others begin with it; then Global, Globe and Globule by their fifth letters (a, e, u); Gloom, with 'o' as its fourth letter, comes last: 1, 3, 4, 2, 5.

questions.text: The World Chess Champion Vishwanathan Anand belongs to which Country?
questions.explanation: Viswanathan Anand, India's first grandmaster, won the world chess title in 2000 and held it again from 2007 to 2013.

questions.text: As of 10 April 2022, how many general elections have been held to the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: The first general election to the Lok Sabha was held in 1951-52 and the seventeenth in 2019; the eighteenth came only in 2024.

questions.text: Plastids containing ______ pigment chlorophyll are called chloroplasts.
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are the plastids with the green pigment chlorophyll; colourless plastids are leucoplasts, and those with yellow, orange or red pigments chromoplasts.

questions.text: Who among the following was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2001?
questions.explanation: The Bharatanatyam dancer Alarmel Valli received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Bharatanatyam for 2001.

questions.text: ____________, who lived in the court of Kanishka, composed a biography of the Buddha, the Buddhacharita.
questions.explanation: Ashvaghosha, a poet in the court of the Kushana king Kanishka, wrote the Buddhacharita in Sanskrit.

questions.text: _____ restrict/s imports and help/s domestic producers from foreign competition. (A) Tariffs (B) Quotas
questions.explanation: A tariff (a tax on imports) makes foreign goods dearer and a quota caps the quantity that may be imported: both cut imports and shield domestic producers.

questions.text: Which industry does aluminium smelting belong to?
questions.explanation: Aluminium smelting turns alumina from bauxite into aluminium metal, a non-ferrous metallurgical industry; NCERT calls it India's second most important metallurgical industry, after iron and steel.

questions.text: Which of the following is an outer planet of the solar system?
questions.explanation: Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars, the rocky planets nearest the Sun, are the inner planets; Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, beyond the asteroid belt, are the outer planets.

questions.text: Which of the following dance forms is associated with Sikkim?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Tashi Sabdo, described as a Bhutia folk dance of Sikkim performed with the white ceremonial scarves (khadas) given on auspicious occasions. Bhangra is from Punjab, and Kolattam, a stick dance, from Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.

questions.text: The Goods and Services Tax, Act commenced from________.
questions.explanation: The Goods and Services Tax came into force on 1 July 2017, replacing many central and state indirect taxes.

questions.text: How many elements were known when Mendeleev started his work?
questions.explanation: When Mendeleev began his work 63 elements were known; he arranged them by atomic mass and their properties in his periodic table of 1869.

questions.text: Which neighbouring country of India is NOT a part of Commonwealth Games?
questions.explanation: China is not a member of the Commonwealth, so it does not take part in the Commonwealth Games; Bangladesh, Pakistan and Sri Lanka are Commonwealth members.

questions.text: Which of the following harvest festivals is primarily celebrated by the people of western Odisha?
questions.explanation: Nuakhai, at which the first rice of the new crop is offered to the deity, is the main harvest festival of western Odisha. Onam is Kerala's harvest festival, Wangala that of the Garos of Meghalaya, and Gudi Padwa the Marathi new year.

questions.text: Which of the following is a stroke use in swimming?
questions.explanation: Butterfly is one of the four competitive swimming strokes, with freestyle, backstroke and breaststroke.

questions.text: The 42nd Amendment Act in 1976 inserted which new Part in the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added Part IV A, whose Article 51A lists the Fundamental Duties of citizens.

questions.text: Which political leader won the bypoll election from Gola Gokarannath constituency in Uttar Pradesh, in November 2022?
questions.explanation: The BJP's Aman Giri won the Gola Gokarannath bypoll of 3 November 2022, held after the death of his father, the sitting MLA Arvind Giri; he defeated the Samajwadi Party's Vinay Tiwari.

questions.text: Who has been appointed as the Governor of West Bengal in November 2022?
questions.explanation: The President appointed C. V. Ananda Bose, a retired IAS officer, Governor of West Bengal on 17 November 2022. He succeeded Jagdeep Dhankhar, who had become Vice-President; La. Ganesan, Governor of Manipur, had held additional charge in between.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Jallianwala Bagh massacre happened in 1919. Where is Jallianwala Bagh located?
questions.explanation: Jallianwala Bagh is in Amritsar, Punjab, where General Dyer's troops fired on an unarmed crowd on 13 April 1919.

questions.text: The interest rate at which the Reserve Bank absorbs liquidity from banks against the collateral of eligible government securities under the LAF is called the ______.
questions.explanation: Under the Liquidity Adjustment Facility the repo rate is what the RBI charges when it lends to banks against government securities, and the reverse repo rate what it pays when it absorbs their surplus funds against such securities.

questions.text: S buys sugar for Rs.40 per kg and sells at Rs. x per kg. Due to a fault in the weighing machine, it shows 1 kg when the actual weight is 800 gm. What is the value of x per kg if his profit percentage is 30%?
questions.explanation: He hands over 800 g for every '1 kg', so what he sells for ₹x costs him 0.8 × 40 = ₹32. A 30% profit gives x = 32 × 1.3 = ₹41.6.

questions.text: The radius of a hemisphere is 21 cm. Its volume (in cm³) will be: (Use π = 22/7)
M can do a piece of work in 12 days and N in 24 days. They begin together, but M leaves the work 6 days before the completion of the work. Find the total number of days to complete the entire work.
questions.explanation: If the work takes T days, N works all T days and M the first T − 6: (T − 6)/12 + T/24 = 1, so 2T − 12 + T = 24 and T = 12.

questions.text: The population of a village is 24000. If it is expected to decrease by 4 percent the next year, then what will be the population of the village next year?
Ravi can decorate a wall in 6 hours, while Ankita can decorate the same wall in 10 hours. In how many hours will they decorate the wall working simultaneously?
questions.explanation: Together they decorate 1/6 + 1/10 = 8/30 = 4/15 of the wall an hour, so they take 15/4 = 3.75 hours.

questions.text: A dealer marked the price of an item 45% more than its cost price and sold it by allowing a discount of 20%. Find his profit percentage.
questions.explanation: The selling price is 1.45 × 0.8 = 1.16 times the cost price: a 16% profit.

questions.text: In a bag of rice of Rs.70 per kg, two different types are mixed. First type of rice is 8 kg in quantity of Rs.60 per kg, while the second type of rice is 4 kg in quantity. What is the price per kg of the second type of rice?
If the length of a rectangle is reduced by 15% and breadth is increased by 10%, what is the percentage change in the area of the rectangle?
questions.explanation: The new area is 0.85 × 1.10 = 0.935 of the old, a decrease of 6.5%.

questions.text: A store announces the following three schemes to sell its articles. Which of these gives the maximum discount to the buyer? A. Two successive discounts of 20% and 24% B. Buy 5 get 3 free C. Buy 13 get 7 free
questions.explanation: A: 1 − 0.8 × 0.76 = 0.392, a 39.2% discount. B: 3 free out of 8, 37.5%. C: 7 free out of 20, 35%. A gives the most.

questions.text: Rani goes to school from home at a certain speed and returns to home at the speed of 50 km/h. If the distance between her home and school is 20 km and the average speed of the whole journey is 37.5 km/h, then what is her speed from home to school?
questions.explanation: Over equal distances the average speed is 2uv/(u + v): 2 × u × 50/(u + 50) = 37.5 gives 100u = 37.5u + 1875, so u = 30 km/h.

questions.text: What principal will amount to Rs.5,324 in 2 years, when the interest is compounded at 10% per annum, compounding annually?
A bike takes 3 hours to cover a distance of 162 km. What distance will it cover in 5 hours?
questions.explanation: The speed is 162 ÷ 3 = 54 km/h, so in 5 hours it covers 54 × 5 = 270 km.

questions.text: A dishonest merchant uses a false weight of 200 gm instead of 250 gm. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: He charges for 250 g but gives 200 g: profit = 50/200 × 100 = 25%.

questions.text: If a : b = 2 : 7 and 343 is the third proportional to a and b, then the value of b – a is:
questions.explanation: With a = 2k and b = 7k, the third proportional is b²/a = 49k²/2k = 24.5k = 343, so k = 14, a = 28, b = 98 and b − a = 70.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. “If we have to sending a mail today”, we shall get a reply in two days.
options: If we would send a mail today
If we send a mail today
If we will send a mail today
If we have sending a mail today
questions.explanation: A condition about the future takes the simple present after 'if', with the future in the main clause: 'If we send a mail today, we shall get a reply in two days.'

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in past tense form. The home nurse is expecting a salary hike from the relatives of the new family.
options: The home nurse will be expecting a salary hike from the relatives of the new family.
The home nurse expects a salary hike from the relatives of the new family.
The home nurse was expecting a salary hike from the relatives of the new family.
The home nurse has been expecting a salary hike from the relatives of the new family.
questions.explanation: The present continuous 'is expecting' becomes the past continuous 'was expecting'.

questions.text: Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. The thief who (have taken the pony) was found guilty by the jury.
questions.explanation: The taking came before the jury's verdict, which is in the past ('was found'), so the past perfect is needed: 'who had taken the pony'. 'Took' cannot follow 'has' or 'have'.

questions.text: Select the MISSPELT word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'extreme'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To be in the doldrums
options: To be in high energy and happiness
To be in low and dull spirits
questions.explanation: To be 'in the doldrums' is to be low in spirits, dull or inactive; the doldrums are the calm belt of ocean near the equator where sailing ships were becalmed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I am born and ___________ in a cultured family.
questions.explanation: 'Born and bred' means born and brought up in a place or family; 'bred' is the past participle of 'breed'. 'Bread', 'bare' and 'beard' only look or sound similar.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Cease
questions.explanation: To 'cease' is to stop; its opposite is to 'commence', to begin. 'Terminate', 'stop' and 'quit' are synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. There is a “few rice left in” the cooker.
questions.explanation: 'Rice' is uncountable, so it takes 'little', not 'few', which goes with plural countable nouns: 'There is a little rice left in the cooker.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. The best thing since sliced bread
questions.explanation: 'The best thing since sliced bread' is said of a new invention or idea thought to be excellent.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to complete the given sentence. Mechanical Engineering students from IIT, Madras, have developed an unnamed sailing boat that can reach any given destination __________.
questions.explanation: A boat that reaches any destination by itself, without a crew, does so 'autonomously', that is independently of human control.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in the brackets to fill in the blank. Consuming coffee every day can have _______ (negative) effects on one’s health.
questions.explanation: 'Adverse' means harmful or unfavourable, as in 'adverse effects'. 'Hospitable' means welcoming, 'despairing' hopeless and 'arbitrary' random.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Instead of studying rules and definitions, Helen “acquired” language through experience and habit.
questions.explanation: To 'acquire' a language is to obtain or gain it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in the bracket to fill in the blank. She was too (feeble)__________ to leave her room.
questions.explanation: 'Feeble' means weak, so its antonym is 'strong'; 'wimpy', 'effete' and 'asthenic' all mean weak.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECT spelling from the given sentence and select its correct spelling. Voting allows every citezen to have a say in choosing who should run the government.
questions.explanation: 'Citezen' is misspelt: the word is 'citizen'. The other options are themselves misspellings of 'allows', 'choosing' and 'government'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Contagion
questions.explanation: 'Contagion' is the passing of a disease from one person to another, that is its transmission.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. A low-pressure area characterised by rapid and frequently damaging air circulation is what (1)_______ cyclones. Storms and (2)_______ weather are frequently present during cyclones. In the Northern hemisphere, the air moves counter clockwise, (3)_______, in the Southern hemisphere, it moves clockwise. Extratropical cyclones, sometimes known as temperate cyclones, and tropical cyclones are the two (4)_______ under which cyclones fall. The name ‘Cyclone’ comes from the Greek word ‘Cyclos’ which means a snake's coils. Henry Paddington came up with the term because tropical storms in the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal (5)______ coiled sea serpents.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank 2.
questions.explanation: Cyclones bring storms and 'unfavourable', that is bad, weather.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. A low-pressure area characterised by rapid and frequently damaging air circulation is what (1)_______ cyclones. Storms and (2)_______ weather are frequently present during cyclones. In the Northern hemisphere, the air moves counter clockwise, (3)_______, in the Southern hemisphere, it moves clockwise. Extratropical cyclones, sometimes known as temperate cyclones, and tropical cyclones are the two (4)_______ under which cyclones fall. The name ‘Cyclone’ comes from the Greek word ‘Cyclos’ which means a snake's coils. Henry Paddington came up with the term because tropical storms in the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal (5)______ coiled sea serpents.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank 3.
questions.explanation: 'Whereas' sets the two hemispheres in contrast: counterclockwise in the north, clockwise in the south.

Henry Paddington came up with the term because tropical storms in the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal (5)______ coiled sea serpents.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank 4.
questions.explanation: Extratropical and tropical cyclones are the two 'categories', or classes, into which cyclones fall.

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. A low-pressure area characterised by rapid and frequently damaging air circulation is what (1)_______ cyclones. Storms and (2)_______ weather are frequently present during cyclones.
