Select the most appropriate answer for blank 5.
questions.explanation: The name comes from the storms' likeness to coiled sea serpents: they 'resemble' them.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Doctor : Stethoscope :: Blacksmith : ?
questions.explanation: A doctor's working tool is the stethoscope; a blacksmith's is the anvil, on which he hammers hot metal.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All pencils are houses. All houses are cars. All cars are trucks. Conclusions: I. Some houses are pencils. II. Some cars are houses. III. Some trucks are cars.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions II and III follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.
questions.explanation: All pencils are houses, so some houses are pencils (I); all houses are cars, so some cars are houses (II); all cars are trucks, so some trucks are cars (III). All three follow.

questions.text: Which of the following options will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 7, 14, 28, 56, ?, 224, 448
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before: 56 × 2 = 112, and 112 × 2 = 224.

questions.text: ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’. ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’. ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’. ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’. ‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the son of B’. If C ÷ D @ E × F – G, how is C related to G?
questions.explanation: C is D's sister, D is E's son, E is F's husband and F is G's mother. So C and G are both children of E and F, and C is G's sister.

questions.text: In a certain code language, the word ‘FAME’ is written as ‘IDPH’. The word ‘PINK’ is written as ‘SLQN’. How is the word ‘RUDE written in the same code language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward: FAME → IDPH and PINK → SLQN. So RUDE → UXGH.

questions.text: Eight people, D, E, G, H, K, L, S and T are sitting in a straight line, facing north. E sits fourth from the right end of the line. No one sits between G and E. G sits third to the right of H. Only five people sit between K and H. L sits to the immediate right of T. S does not sit at any of the extreme ends of the line. How many people sit between S and D?
questions.explanation: Numbering the seats 1 to 8 from the left, E is at 5. G, next to E and third to the right of H, must be at 4 with H at 1 (G at 6 would put H at 3, with no seat six places away for K). So K is at 7, T and L take 2 and 3, and S, not at an end, takes 6, leaving D at 8. Only K sits between S and D.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 2, 4, 6, 10, 14, ?, 26, 34, 42
questions.explanation: The differences come in pairs, 2, 2, 4, 4, 6, 6, 8, 8: 14 + 6 = 20 and 20 + 6 = 26.

questions.text: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? DKBN, EMYP, ?, GQST, HSPV
questions.explanation: The first letters run D, E, F, G, H; the second K, M, O, Q, S (+2); the third B, Y, V, S, P (−3); the fourth N, P, R, T, V (+2). The missing cluster is FOVR.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 3 × 144 – 6 ÷ 40 + 20 = 52
questions.explanation: After interchanging ÷ and −: 3 × 144 ÷ 6 − 40 + 20 = 72 − 40 + 20 = 52.

questions.text: In a certain code language, If FLED is coded as 3921 and GIFT is coded as 46317, how will HUNK be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as its place in the alphabet minus 3: FLED → 3, 9, 2, 1 and GIFT → 4, 6, 3, 17. So HUNK → 5, 18, 11, 8: 518118.

questions.text: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. A sits to the immediate left of C. E sits third to the right of D. D is an immediate neighbour of C. B is an immediate neighbour of both E and F. How many persons sit between C and B from either side?
questions.explanation: A sits on C's left, so D, C's other neighbour, sits on C's right; E, third to D's right, sits opposite D, next to A. B sits between E and F, so going round to the left from C the order is C, A, E, B, F, D. Two people sit between C and B either way (A and E, or D and F).

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 14 * 3 * 8 * 8 * 6 * 7
questions.explanation: ×, +, −, =, × gives 14 × 3 + 8 − 8 = 6 × 7, as both sides equal 42.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (10, 450, 5); (8, 360, 5)
questions.explanation: The middle number is the product of the other two times 9: 10 × 5 × 9 = 450 and 8 × 5 × 9 = 360. Likewise 7 × 3 × 9 = 189.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Mountain 2 Mould 3 Monster 4 Mouth 5 Moving
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Monster (3), Mould (2), Mountain (1), Mouth (4), Moving (5). 'Mon' comes before 'Mou', 'Moul' before 'Moun' and 'Mout', and 'Mou' before 'Mov'.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? BWGV, CUJR, DSMN, EQPJ, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters run B, C, D, E, F; the second W, U, S, Q, O (−2); the third G, J, M, P, S (+3); the fourth V, R, N, J, F (−4). The next cluster is FOSF.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. MEMORY : NFNPSZ : : BRAIN : CSBJO : : DREAM : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: MEMORY → NFNPSZ and BRAIN → CSBJO. So DREAM → ESFBN.

questions.text: Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT) 2.0 guidelines have been formulated with the aim of assisting states making our cities _____________.
questions.explanation: AMRUT 2.0, launched in October 2021, aims to make cities 'water secure' and self-sustaining, with tap water for every household and the reuse of treated used water.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution deals with the Right against Exploitation?
questions.explanation: Articles 23 and 24 make up the Right against Exploitation: Article 23 bans traffic in human beings and forced labour, and Article 24 bars children under 14 from work in factories, mines and other hazardous employment.

questions.text: Identify the element that is NOT a metalloid.
questions.explanation: Xenon is a noble gas. Germanium and tellurium are metalloids, like boron, silicon, arsenic and antimony, and polonium is often counted with them.

questions.text: Which of the following is correct regarding net national product?
questions.explanation: Net national product is gross national product less depreciation, the wear and tear of capital during the year.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which organization was founded in 1867 in Bombay?
questions.explanation: The Prarthana Samaj was founded in Bombay in 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang, inspired by Keshab Chandra Sen. The Theosophical Society was founded in New York in 1875 and the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897, and the Young Bengal Movement grew up around Henry Derozio in Calcutta.

questions.text: In 2015, the Planning Commission was replaced with the ___________.
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015.

questions.text: Norman Borlaug, father of Green Revolution in the world, was ________ (in terms of nationality).
questions.explanation: Norman Borlaug, the American agronomist whose high-yielding dwarf wheat drove the Green Revolution, won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian ministers hosted LeadIT summit with Sweden on the sidelines of United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP27)?
questions.explanation: Bhupender Yadav, Union Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change when the exam was held (January 2023), co-hosted the LeadIT (Leadership Group for Industry Transition) Summit with Sweden at COP27 in Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt, on 15 November 2022.

questions.text: As per Railway Yearbook 2019–20, what is the length (in km) of narrow gauge in India?
questions.explanation: On 31 March 2020, the end of the year the Year Book covers, Indian Railways had about 1,604 route km of narrow gauge out of 67,956 route km, against 2,402 km of metre gauge and the rest broad gauge.

questions.text: In which of the following countries was the ICC U19 Cricket World Cup 2022 organised?
questions.explanation: The ICC Under-19 Cricket World Cup 2022 was held in the West Indies in January and February 2022; India won it, beating England in the final.

questions.text: Which of the following states uses the bamboo drip irrigation system?
questions.explanation: In Meghalaya farmers have for some 200 years carried stream and spring water down the hills in bamboo pipes, delivering it drop by drop to their plants.

questions.text: Phooldei, a harvest festival, is primarily celebrated in which of the following states of India?
questions.explanation: Phool Dei is a festival of Uttarakhand, held on the first day of the month of Chaitra (mid-March), when children put flowers and rice on the doorsteps of homes.

questions.text: The National Commission for Women was set up as statutory body in January _________.
questions.explanation: The National Commission for Women was set up on 31 January 1992 as a statutory body under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.

questions.text: Deficiency of which of the following causes weak bones and tooth decay?
questions.explanation: Calcium, with phosphorus, makes bones and teeth hard; too little of it weakens the bones and leaves the teeth prone to decay.

questions.text: Who received the Best Dance director Award from the Assam Government?
questions.explanation: Jatin Goswami, the Sattriya dancer and guru, received the Government of Assam's Best Dance Director award for 1997-98; he was given the Padma Shri in 2008.

questions.text: Kusukuntla Prabhakar Reddy, became Member of Legislative Assembly from _____ constituency in Telangana, in November 2022.
questions.explanation: Kusukuntla Prabhakar Reddy of the Telangana Rashtra Samithi won the by-election to the Munugode Assembly seat in Telangana in November 2022.

questions.text: In the context of Basketball, which of the following statements is correct?
options: A player is to be substituted within 20 seconds.
Two teams of five players are required to start a game.
Each basketball must have weight of minimum 700 grams
The basketball game was invented in 1981.
questions.explanation: A basketball game is played between two teams of five players each on court. A full-size ball weighs about 567-650 g, not at least 700 g, and James Naismith invented the game in 1891, not 1981.

questions.text: Who among the following can issue ordinance when the state legislature is not in session and he is satisfied that immediate action is required?
questions.explanation: Under Article 213 the Governor can promulgate an ordinance when the state legislature is not in session and he is satisfied that immediate action is needed; Article 123 gives the President the same power for Parliament.

questions.text: ______ was the capital of Magadha for several year before is was shifted to Pataliputra.
questions.explanation: Rajagriha (Rajgir), ringed by hills, was Magadha's capital under kings such as Bimbisara and Ajatashatru; the capital later moved to Pataliputra.

questions.text: The world famous dancer Gulabo Sapera is known for which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: Gulabo Sapera is the best-known performer of Kalbelia, the dance of Rajasthan's Kalbelia snake-charmer community; she received the Padma Shri in 2016.

questions.text: Evaluate the following. 75 - 50 ÷ 5 of 2 + 36 ÷ 6 of 4 × 2 (18 - 5 of 2)
A and B together can complete a work in 26 days. A alone can complete it in 52 days. If B works at 50 percent efficiency, then in how many days A and B together will complete the work?
questions.explanation: B alone does 1/26 − 1/52 = 1/52 of the work a day, and 1/104 at 50% efficiency. Together they do 1/52 + 1/104 = 3/104 a day, so they need 104/3 days.

questions.text: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 150 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and policeman run at the speed of 11km/h and 12km/h, respectively. What is the distance between them after 6 minutes?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 12 − 11 = 1 km/h, that is 100 m in 6 minutes (1/10 hour), so the gap falls from 150 m to 50 m.

questions.text: Ravi sold two bikes for ₹ 42,188 each. On one bike he gained 20% while on the other he lost 20%. How much per cent does he gain or lose overall?
questions.explanation: With equal selling prices, a 20% gain on one and a 20% loss on the other give an overall loss of 20²/100 = 4%: the bikes cost 42,188/1.2 + 42,188/0.8 = ₹87,891.67 and fetched ₹84,376.

questions.text: The average of 15 results is 60. If the average of the first eight results is 58, and that of the last six is 62, then find the ninth result.
questions.explanation: The total is 15 × 60 = 900; the first eight add up to 8 × 58 = 464 and the last six to 6 × 62 = 372. The ninth is 900 − 464 − 372 = 64.

questions.text: What is the LCM of 6 and 110?
What is the surface area (in cm²) of a sphere whose diameter is 21 cm?
questions.explanation: The radius is 10.5 cm, so the surface area is 4πr² = 4 × 22/7 × 10.5 × 10.5 = 1386 cm².

questions.text: What is the discount percentage on ‘Buy 5 Get 3 Free’?
questions.explanation: The buyer pays for 5 items and gets 8, so 3 of every 8 are free: 3/8 × 100 = 37.5%.

questions.text: An amount of ₹8,00,000 is needed after 2 years to buy a car. The amount deposited in a bank gives 8% per annum interest. What should be the approximate amount to be deposited in present in the bank to meet the requirement; if the interest is compounded annually?
questions.explanation: The deposit P must grow to ₹8,00,000 in 2 years at 8%: P = 8,00,000 ÷ 1.08² = 8,00,000 ÷ 1.1664 = ₹6,85,871 (approximately).

questions.text: A trader marks his goods at 50 percent above the cost price and allows a discount of 30 percent. What is his gain percent?
questions.explanation: The selling price is 1.5 × 0.7 = 1.05 times the cost price: a gain of 5%.

questions.text: If 18 workers can lay a road in 15 h, then how many more workers are required to lay the same road in 9 h?
questions.explanation: The road takes 18 × 15 = 270 worker-hours, so finishing in 9 h needs 270 ÷ 9 = 30 workers, 12 more than 18.

questions.text: A batsman in his 13th inning makes a score of 85 runs and there by increases his average by five runs. What is his average after 13th innings?
questions.explanation: If the average after 12 innings is x, then 12x + 85 = 13(x + 5), so x = 20 and the average after the 13th innings is 25.

questions.text: In a circular race of 2,700 m, P and Q start from point A in opposite directions at speeds of 23 km/h and 49 km/h, respectively. What is the time taken by them to meet for the first time?
questions.explanation: Running in opposite directions they close at 23 + 49 = 72 km/h = 20 m/s, so they first meet after 2,700 ÷ 20 = 135 seconds.

questions.text: What is the change in the curved surface area of a cylinder when we double the radius and the height is halved?
questions.explanation: The curved surface area is 2πrh; with radius 2r and height h/2 it is 2π(2r)(h/2) = 2πrh, unchanged.

questions.text: Rishabh bought some T-shirts at 3 for ₹252, and sold them at 5 for ₹200. Find his gain or loss percentage.
questions.explanation: Each T-shirt cost 252 ÷ 3 = ₹84 and sold for 200 ÷ 5 = ₹40, a loss of 44/84 × 100 = 52.38%, about 52.4%.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. There was “palpable” tension in the negotiation room.
questions.explanation: 'Palpable' means so strong that it can be felt or noticed: 'detectable'. The other options mean hard or impossible to notice.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He is determined to__________ any kind of task to prove his talent.
questions.explanation: To 'undertake' a task is to take it on, which suits someone determined to prove his talent. 'Escape' and 'avoid' mean the opposite, and one 'entrusts' a task to someone else.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence to make it a meaningful sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. Patients “who do previous heart attacks and those with cardiac failure are at a higher risk of having” a cardiac arrest.
options: who have had previous heart attack and they with cardiac failure are at a higher risk of having
who have had previous heart attacks and those of cardiac failure are at a higher risk of having
who have had previous heart attacks and those with cardiac failure are at a higher risk of having
questions.explanation: 'Do' cannot stand for 'have had': patients 'who have had previous heart attacks' are set beside 'those with cardiac failure'. The other options make 'attacks' singular, put 'they' for 'those', or change 'with' to 'of'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Dodge
questions.explanation: To 'dodge' is to avoid something by a quick movement or by a trick, as in dodging tax, so of the options 'cheat' comes nearest. 'Determine', 'announce' and 'advice' are unrelated.

questions.text: Select the correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’. The patient “had died” before the doctor came.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had died' marks the earlier of two past events: the death came before the doctor's arrival. The sentence is correct as it stands.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The patient suffered an epileptic _________.
questions.explanation: A 'seizure' is a sudden attack of illness, as in epilepsy. 'Caesar', 'scissors' and 'sizar' (a student given help with college costs) only sound like it.

questions.text: Select the option with the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. In order to find the “anamoly”, scientists had to repeat the experiment over a hundred times.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'anomaly': something that departs from what is normal or expected.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. My friend Ragini /shall completed/ her task/ by then.
questions.explanation: 'By then' calls for the future perfect, 'shall have completed'; 'shall' cannot be followed by the past form 'completed'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Sublime
questions.explanation: 'Sublime' means of the highest excellence, so great as to inspire awe; its opposite is 'ordinary'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom that can be substituted in the following sentence. She knows Spanish “after a fashion”.
options: only after the fashion is done
questions.explanation: To do something 'after a fashion' is to do it to some extent, but not very well: she knows a little Spanish.

questions.text: Fill in the blanks with the correct homophone. I _______ some essential items from the supermarket.
questions.explanation: 'Bought', the past tense of 'buy', fits. A 'bout' is a short spell or contest, a 'boat' a vessel and a 'bot' a software robot.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. We “hope these measure will take us” further to a good position.
options: hopes these measures will take us
hope these measures will take us
hope those measure will take us
questions.explanation: 'These' is plural, so the noun must be too: 'these measures'. 'We' takes 'hope', not 'hopes', and 'will' takes the base form 'take'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A herculean task
questions.explanation: A 'herculean task' needs great strength or effort, like the labours of Hercules: a tough job.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Historigraphy' is misspelt: the word is 'historiography', the writing of history. 'Periphery', 'fractural' (to do with a fracture) and 'antagonistic' are spelt correctly.

questions.text: In the given sentence, a word is given in brackets. Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word to fill in the blank. The boss wanted complete information. He asked about every ___________ (huge) detail.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'huge' is 'minute' (tiny): he asked about every minute detail. 'Mighty' and 'significant' are close to 'huge' in sense, and 'solid' does not fit.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. I looked out (1) ________ the city. The sun hung low in the sky, shining weakly (2) _______ the clouds, casting long shadows on the grass. I realised that it would be (3) _______ soon. The sun would set, finally, the (4) _______would rise in the sky. Another day (5) _______ end. Another day lost.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: To look out 'across' the city is to look over it from one side to the other.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. I looked out (1) ________ the city. The sun hung low in the sky, shining weakly (2) _______ the clouds, casting long shadows on the grass. I realised that it would be (3) _______ soon. The sun would set, finally, the (4) _______would rise in the sky. Another day (5) _______ end. Another day lost.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The weak sun shone 'through' the clouds, from behind them; 'though' is a conjunction.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. I looked out (1) ________ the city. The sun hung low in the sky, shining weakly (2) _______ the clouds, casting long shadows on the grass. I realised that it would be (3) _______ soon. The sun would set, finally, the (4) _______would rise in the sky. Another day (5) _______ end. Another day lost.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: With the sun low and about to set, it 'would be dark soon', as the next sentence explains.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. I looked out (1) ________ the city. The sun hung low in the sky, shining weakly (2) _______ the clouds, casting long shadows on the grass. I realised that it would be (3) _______ soon. The sun would set, finally, the (4) _______would rise in the sky. Another day (5) _______ end. Another day lost.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: As the sun sets, 'the moon' rises in the sky to take its place.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. I looked out (1) ________ the city. The sun hung low in the sky, shining weakly (2) _______ the clouds, casting long shadows on the grass. I realised that it would be (3) _______ soon. The sun would set, finally, the (4) _______would rise in the sky. Another day (5) _______ end. Another day lost.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The passage is in the past ('I realised that it would be dark soon. The sun would set'), so 'another day would end' keeps the sequence of tenses.

questions.text: Eight people, D, E, M, P, T, W, Y and Z are sitting in a straight line, facing north. M sits at one of the extreme ends of the line. Only two people sit between M and E. D sits third to the right of E. Only four people sit between D and T. Z sits to the immediate right of P. W does not sit at any of the extreme ends of the line. How many people sit to the right of Y?
questions.explanation: M must be at the left end (at the right end, D would have to sit in M's seat). Then E is fourth from the left, D seventh and T second; P and Z take the fifth and sixth seats, W, who is not at an end, the third, and Y the eighth. Y is at the right end, so nobody sits to the right of Y.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? AFIN, EJMR, ?, MRUZ, QVYD
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places forward every time: A, E, I, M, Q; F, J, N, R, V; I, M, Q, U, Y; N, R, V, Z, D. The missing cluster is INQV.

questions.text: Which of the following options will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 3, 8, 18, 38, ?, 158, 318
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before plus 2: 38 × 2 + 2 = 78, and 78 × 2 + 2 = 158.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘DAINTY’ is written as ‘GCKQWB’ and ‘PROMISE’ is written as ‘SUQPKVG’. How will ‘CERTAIN’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each consonant moves 3 places forward and each vowel 2: DAINTY → GCKQWB (Y + 3 wraps round to B) and PROMISE → SUQPKVG. So C E R T A I N → F G U W C K Q: FGUWCKQ.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 jumping 2 juice 3 jumble 4 jupiter 5 junior
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: juice (2), jumble (3), jumping (1), junior (5), jupiter (4). 'Jui' comes before 'jum', 'jumb' before 'jump', and 'jun' before 'jup'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 9 : 11 :: 29 : 21 :: 37 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is half of 13 more than the first: (9 + 13)/2 = 11 and (29 + 13)/2 = 21. So (37 + 13)/2 = 25.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. OL, VE, CX, JQ, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move 7 places forward (O, V, C, J, Q) and the second 7 places back (L, E, X, Q, J), wrapping round the alphabet. The next pair is QJ.

questions.text: Which two signs and two numbers (not digits) should be interchanged in the following equation to make it correct? 19 ÷ 14 + 7 × 2 × 4 = 80
questions.explanation: After interchanging 4 and 19, and + and ÷: 4 + 14 ÷ 7 × 2 × 19 = 4 + 76 = 80.

questions.text: Seven people K, L, M, N, O, P and Q, are sitting in a straight row, facing the north. Only four people sit to the left of P. Q sits third to the left of N. N is not an immediate neighbour of P. M sits third to the left of L. K sits to the immediate left of M. Who sits at the extreme left end of the row?
questions.explanation: P is fifth from the left. N cannot sit fourth or sixth, next to P, and needs a seat three places to its left for Q, so N is seventh and Q fourth. M third to the left of L then fits only with M third and L sixth, K second, and O in the first seat, at the extreme left.

questions.text: ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’. ‘A / B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’. ‘A ^ B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’. ‘A % B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’. ‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the son of B’. If U ^ V / W + X % Y, how is U related to Y?
questions.explanation: U is V's husband and V is W's mother; W is X's brother and X is Y's sister, so Y is also V's child. U is Y's father.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 113, 114, 110, 119, 103, 128, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are the squares 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36 with alternating signs: +1, −4, +9, −16, +25, −36. So 128 − 36 = 92.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 36 + 27 – 75 × 5 ÷ 25 = 24
questions.explanation: After interchanging – and +: 36 − 27 + 75 × 5 ÷ 25 = 9 + 15 = 24.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FLEET’ is written as ‘TFMFF’, ‘OUTLET’ is written as ‘TOVUMF’, how will ‘LABOUR’ be written as in that language?
questions.explanation: The last letter moves to the front, followed by the first letter, and each letter in between moves 1 place forward: FLEET → T F MFF and OUTLET → T O VUMF. So LABOUR → R L BCPV: RLBCPV.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. ZINCKY : XGLAIW :: ZIGZAG : XGEXYE :: JOCKEY : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places back: ZINCKY → XGLAIW and ZIGZAG → XGEXYE. So JOCKEY → HMAICW.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Author : Pen :: Carpenter : ?
questions.explanation: An author writes with a pen, and a carpenter cuts wood with a saw: each is the worker's tool.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All birds are cows. Some cows are hens. Some dogs are birds. Conclusions: I. Some dogs are hens. II. No hens are birds. III. Some cows are dogs.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: Some dogs are birds and all birds are cows, so some dogs are cows, that is some cows are dogs (III). Nothing links the hens to the dogs, or rules out hens that are birds, so I and II do not follow.

questions.text: Who among the following personalities received the Padma Shri award in the year 2008 for his contributions in Odissi dance?
questions.explanation: Gangadhar Pradhan (1948-2010), the Odissi guru who founded the Orissa Dance Academy in Bhubaneswar, received the Padma Shri in 2008. Shambhu Maharaj, Kalka Prasad and Ramlal Bareth are known for Kathak.

questions.text: Use of bauxite as a raw material is mainly for which industry?
questions.explanation: Bauxite is the main ore of aluminium, so it is the chief raw material of the aluminium industry.

questions.text: Which state/Union Territory hosted the Lusofonia Games in the year 2014?
questions.explanation: Goa hosted the third Lusofonia Games, for Portuguese-speaking countries and territories, in January 2014.

questions.text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated Arunachal Pradesh’s first greenfield airport in which city?
questions.explanation: On 19 November 2022 Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Donyi Polo Airport at Hollongi, near Itanagar, Arunachal Pradesh's first greenfield airport.

questions.text: The Hampi Utsav is celebrated every year in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: The Hampi Utsav is held at Hampi, the ruined capital of the Vijayanagara Empire, in Karnataka.

questions.text: Workers who own and operate an enterprise to earn their livelihood are known as _________.
questions.explanation: Workers who own and run their own enterprise to earn a living are self-employed; those paid a regular wage by an employer are regular salaried workers, and those hired by the day are casual labourers.

questions.text: Which of the following is the chemical formula of washing soda?
questions.explanation: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O: sodium carbonate crystallised with ten molecules of water.

questions.text: Consider a market structure where the number of firms is large, there is free entry and exit of firms, but the goods produced by them are not homogeneous. Such a market structure is called ______.
questions.explanation: Many firms, free entry and exit, and products that are similar but differentiated are the marks of monopolistic competition. Under perfect competition the goods would be homogeneous.

questions.text: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 was passed in 2019 and came into force in ___________.
questions.explanation: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019, which replaced the Act of 1986, came into force in July 2020, most of its provisions on 20 July 2020.

questions.text: Aga Khan Gold Cup is associated with which of the following Sports?
questions.explanation: The Aga Khan Cup, or All India Aga Khan Gold Cup, is a hockey tournament with more than a century of history, long played in Bombay (Mumbai). (A football club tournament called the Aga Khan Gold Cup was held in Dhaka from the late 1950s to the early 1980s, but football is not among the options.)

questions.text: Emperor Ashoka was the son of ________.
questions.explanation: Ashoka was the son of Bindusara and the grandson of Chandragupta Maurya, the founder of the Maurya Empire.

questions.text: The upper house of a state legislature is known as ________.
questions.explanation: In a state with two Houses, the upper house is the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) and the lower house the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha). Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha are the Houses of Parliament.

questions.text: What was the actual growth rate of the seventh five year plan of India?
questions.explanation: The Seventh Five-Year Plan (1985-90) aimed at growth of 5% a year and achieved about 6%.

questions.text: As of November 2022, who is the Union Minister for Health in India?
questions.explanation: Mansukh Mandaviya was Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare in November 2022, having taken charge of the ministry in July 2021.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In ______, James Mill, a Scottish economist and political philosopher, published a massive three-volume work, A History of British India.
questions.explanation: James Mill's 'The History of British India', in three volumes, was published in 1817.

questions.text: Sharodi Saikia is an Indian classical dancer known for ________ dance form.
questions.explanation: Sharodi (Sarodi) Saikia of Assam is a Sattriya dancer and teacher. Sattriya grew out of the Vaishnava monasteries (sattras) of Assam.

questions.text: Rule of Law is the foundation of any _________, which means that no person is above the law.
questions.explanation: The rule of law, under which the same laws apply to everyone and no one is above them, is a foundation of democracy; autocracy and dictatorship put a ruler above the law.

questions.text: Visakhapatnam is the ____________ landlocked and well-protected port.
questions.explanation: NCERT's geography text describes Visakhapatnam, on the Andhra Pradesh coast, as the deepest land-locked and well-protected port in India.

questions.text: Dead Sea is bordered by which two countries?
questions.explanation: The Dead Sea lies between Jordan to the east and Israel and the West Bank to the west.

questions.text: The value of an Apple laptop depreciated from Rs.1,33,100 to Rs.72,900 in 3 years. Find the yearly rate of depreciation. (Correct to 2 decimal places.)
questions.explanation: 72,900/1,33,100 = 729/1331 = (9/11)³, so the value falls to 9/11 of itself each year: a depreciation of 2/11 = 18.18% a year.

questions.text: In a mixture of 624 litres, the ratio of milk and water is 5∶3. The amount of water to be further added to the mixture so as to make the ratio of the milk to water 5∶4 will be:
questions.explanation: The mixture holds 624 × 5/8 = 390 litres of milk and 234 of water. For 5 : 4 the water must be 390 × 4/5 = 312 litres, so 312 − 234 = 78 litres must be added.

questions.text: A man sold two pens at Rs.12 each. On one, he gained 20% and on the other, he lost 20%. On the whole, he:
questions.explanation: The pen sold at a 20% gain cost 12 ÷ 1.2 = ₹10 and the one sold at a 20% loss 12 ÷ 0.8 = ₹15. He paid ₹25 and got ₹24, a loss of ₹1.

questions.text: Two trains of same length are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions with speeds of 54 km/h and 90 km/h respectively. They cross each other in 12 sec. Find the length (in metres) of each train.
questions.explanation: Moving towards each other the trains close at 54 + 90 = 144 km/h = 40 m/s. In 12 seconds they cover 480 m, the two lengths together, so each train is 240 m long.

questions.text: The Time taken by Anjali to finish a piece of work is four times the time taken by Ron and Three times the time taken by John. If all three of them work together, it takes them 4 days to complete the entire work. How much time Ron alone take to finish the work?
questions.explanation: If Anjali takes 12t days, Ron takes 3t and John 4t. Together they do 1/(12t) + 1/(3t) + 1/(4t) = 8/(12t) = 2/(3t) of the work a day, so they take 3t/2 = 4 days: t = 8/3, and Ron alone takes 3t = 8 days.

questions.text: Calculate the cost to paint a water tank in the shape of a sphere having a radius of 7 cm, if the cost of painting is Rs.4.5/cm² . (π = 22/7 )
questions.explanation: The surface area is 4πr² = 4 × 22/7 × 7² = 616 cm², so painting costs 616 × 4.5 = ₹2,772.

questions.text: Mohan and Sohan invested Rs.3,000 and Rs.4,000 respectively in a property and after 6 month Sohan withdraws. If in the end of the year their profit is Rs.540, then what is the profit earned by Mohan?
questions.explanation: Their shares go as capital × time: 3,000 × 12 : 4,000 × 6 = 36,000 : 24,000 = 3 : 2, so Mohan gets 540 × 3/5 = ₹324.

questions.text: Two trains running in the same direction at 110 km/h and 90 km/h completely pass one another in 54 sec. If the length of the first train is 130 metres, then find the length of the second train.
questions.explanation: Running the same way the trains close at 110 − 90 = 20 km/h = 50/9 m/s, so in 54 seconds they cover 50/9 × 54 = 300 m, both lengths together. The second train is 300 − 130 = 170 metres long.

questions.text: Find the mean proportional of 0.75 and 3?
questions.explanation: The mean proportional of a and b is √(ab) = √(0.75 × 3) = √2.25 = 1.5.

questions.text: If a reduction of 10% in the price of rice enables a person to obtain 22 kg more for ₹250, then the original price of rice per kg is:
questions.explanation: The 10% cut saves ₹25 on ₹250, and that ₹25 buys the extra 22 kg, so the reduced price is ₹25/22 a kg. The original price is (25/22) ÷ 0.9 = 125/99 ≈ ₹1.26 a kg.

questions.text: The HCF and LCM of 2 numbers are 32 and 192. One of the numbers is 64. Find the absolute difference between the numbers.
questions.explanation: The product of two numbers equals the product of their HCF and LCM, so the other number is 32 × 192 ÷ 64 = 96, and 96 − 64 = 32.

questions.text: The expenses on rice, petrol and oil of a family are in the ratio 8 : 11 : 6. If the prices of these items are increased by 10%, 20% and 30%, respectively, then the total expenses of the family on these items are increased by:
questions.explanation: Take the expenses as 8, 11 and 6, 25 in all. After the rises they are 8.8 + 13.2 + 7.8 = 29.8, an increase of 4.8/25 = 19.2%.

questions.text: A school manager decides to build a new school building in 40 days. He employs 100 men in the beginning and 100 men after 35 days and completes the construction within the stipulated time. If he had not employed the additional men, how many days behind schedule would the school building have been completed?
questions.explanation: The work is 100 × 35 + 200 × 5 = 4,500 man-days. 100 men alone would need 4,500 ÷ 100 = 45 days, 5 days behind schedule.

questions.text: ₹12,000 becomes ₹15,972 in a certain period of time at the rate of 10% per annum on compound interest, compounding annually. Find the period of time.
questions.explanation: 15,972 ÷ 12,000 = 1.331 = 1.1³, so the money grows for 3 years.

questions.text: The marked price of a hair dryer is Rs.10,550. The shopkeeper offers a discount of 18% on it. Find its selling price.
What is the volume of a cone whose height is 24 cm and radius is 14 cm?
Fill in the blanks with appropriate homonym. At a particular _________ of life, the body goes through some unnecessary changes.
questions.explanation: A 'stage' of life is a step or phase in it. The other sense of 'stage', a raised platform, does not fit, and neither 'plane' nor 'plain' makes sense here.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Jiten and Hiru “loves” to “eat” “French fries” for “lunch”.
questions.explanation: Two subjects joined by 'and' take a plural verb: 'Jiten and Hiru love to eat French fries for lunch.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homonym of the given word. Blue
questions.explanation: 'Blew', the past tense of 'blow', sounds exactly like 'blue' but differs in spelling and meaning. Such sound-alike words are strictly homophones, which 'homonym' also covers in its broad sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. Mr. Saxena has “espoused” a child from an orphanage.
questions.explanation: One 'adopts' a child, taking it in as one's own. To 'espouse' is to take up a cause or belief, 'adapted' means changed to suit, and 'adepted' is not a word.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Accurate
questions.explanation: 'Accurate' means correct and exact, and so dependable; of the options only 'unreliable' is opposite in sense. A 'heist' is a robbery, 'proficient' means skilled, and a 'fiesta' is a festival.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. His seat was the _________ in our row.
questions.explanation: 'The' and the comparison with the whole row call for the superlative 'farthest'. 'Further' is comparative, and 'near to' and 'far' do not fit after 'the'.

questions.text: The sentence given below has one misspelt word. Spot the INCORRECTLY spelt word and select its correct spelling. Abreviations are not understood by everyone.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'abbreviations', with a double 'b'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Put forth
questions.explanation: To 'put forth' is to bring forward or show, as in putting forth an idea; its opposite is to 'conceal', or hide.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. No one can “exterminate” poverty from this world.
questions.explanation: To 'exterminate' is to destroy completely: 'eradicate', to root out.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. We had to move slowly through the “narrow” alley.
questions.explanation: A 'narrow' alley leaves little room: it is 'cramped'. 'Imminent' means about to happen, 'dreary' dull, and 'maximum' the greatest.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. We should also learn “to trust what he says”. After all, he is a reformed person now.
options: to give someone the benefit of the doubt
to wrap our head around something
questions.explanation: To 'give someone the benefit of the doubt' is to believe what they say although it cannot be proved, which suits a reformed person.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The manager “have get hot under the collar” when the workers demanded higher wages.
questions.explanation: To 'get hot under the collar' is to become angry. The past tense 'got' matches 'demanded'; 'have get' is ungrammatical, 'get' is the wrong tense, and the other two options drop 'hot'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The bufotoxin present on a toad's skin can irritate you but touching a toad “shall not cause” you warts.
questions.explanation: A general statement about what will happen takes 'will', and 'touching a toad' is a singular subject, so 'do not cause' does not agree: 'touching a toad won't give you warts'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Manifest
questions.explanation: 'Manifest' means clear or obvious: 'apparent'. 'Cryptic' and 'concealed' are near opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The minister reached the venue of the programme before time which __________ wonder and awe among the organisers.
questions.explanation: The minister's early arrival 'created', that is caused, wonder and awe among the organisers.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 784, 568, 443, ?, 352
questions.explanation: The differences are 216, 125, 64 and 27, the cubes of 6, 5, 4 and 3: 443 − 64 = 379, and 379 − 27 = 352.

questions.text: X and Z are sisters. Y is the brother of Z. S is the daughter of Z. T is the brother of S. T is married to U. How is Y related to S?
questions.explanation: Z is a sister, so she is S's mother, and Y, Z's brother, is S's mother's brother.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 8, 17, 36, ?, 154
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before plus 1, 2, 3 and 4 in turn: 8 × 2 + 1 = 17, 17 × 2 + 2 = 36, 36 × 2 + 3 = 75 and 75 × 2 + 4 = 154.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 dream 2 drown 3 drone 4 dropped 5 drama
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: drama (dra-), dream (dre-), then the three 'dro-' words by their fourth letter, drone (n), dropped (p) and drown (w): 5, 1, 3, 4, 2.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? YSEA, WQGC, UOIE, ?, QKMI
questions.explanation: The first and second letters move 2 places back (Y, W, U, S, Q; S, Q, O, M, K) and the third and fourth 2 places forward (E, G, I, K, M; A, C, E, G, I). The missing cluster is SMKG.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by two conclusions. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some trains are buses. No bus is a car. Some cars are bikes. Conclusions: 1. Some bikes are cars. 2. Some bikes are trains.
questions.explanation: Some cars are bikes, so some bikes are cars: conclusion 1 follows. The bikes are linked to the trains only through cars and buses, and no bus is a car, so 'some bikes are trains' is possible but not certain: 2 does not follow.

questions.text: Which two numbers (not digits), from the given options, should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 158 − 64 × 6 ÷ 2 = 4 × 15 ÷ 3
questions.explanation: After interchanging 6 and 4: 158 − 64 × 4 ÷ 2 = 158 − 128 = 30, and 6 × 15 ÷ 3 = 30.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? ABDG, DEGJ, ? , JKMP, MNPS
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward from one cluster to the next: A, D, G, J, M; B, E, H, K, N; D, G, J, M, P; G, J, M, P, S. The missing cluster is GHJM.

questions.text: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. F is an immediate neighbour of A. D sits second to the right of E. B is an immediate neighbour of E and sits second to the right of C. F sits second to the right of D. A is not an immediate neighbour of E. Who is sitting between D and E?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's right is anticlockwise. Going anticlockwise, the clues give E, B, D, A, F, C round the table (with B on E's other side, A would sit next to E), so B sits between D and E.

questions.text: Five people A, B, C, D, and E are sitting in a straight row facing the North. A is sitting to the immediate left of C. Only C is sitting between A and E. B is sitting to the right of E. D is sitting to the right of B. Who is sitting at the extreme left of the row?
questions.explanation: A is to C's immediate left and only C sits between A and E, so A, C, E sit in that order; B is to E's right and D to B's right, so the row is A, C, E, B, D, with A at the left end.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 72 - 36 × 4 ÷ 6 + 24 = 42

Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Resistance : Ohm :: Energy : ?
questions.explanation: The ohm is the unit of resistance, as the joule is of energy. The volt measures potential difference and the watt power.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. LEAP : KFZQ :: CLOS : BMNT :: EJOT : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move −1, +1, −1, +1: LEAP → KFZQ and CLOS → BMNT. So EJOT → DKNU.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘STORK’ is written as ‘URROO’ and ‘ASHES’ is written as ‘CQKBW’. How will ‘BUNKE’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +2, −2, +3, −3 and +4: STORK → URROO and ASHES → CQKBW. So BUNKE → DSQHI.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 46 : 11 :: 30 : 7 :: 50 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the first minus 2, divided by 4: (46 − 2) ÷ 4 = 11 and (30 − 2) ÷ 4 = 7. So (50 − 2) ÷ 4 = 12.

questions.text: In a code language, 'LEAF' is written as ‘EZDK’ and ‘PLANT’ is written as ’SMZKO’, how will 'FLOWER' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is written backwards and each letter moved one place back: LEAF → F A E L → EZDK and PLANT → T N A L P → SMZKO. So FLOWER → R E W O L F → QDVNKE.

questions.text: In India, Inter-religion marriages are performed under this Act:
questions.explanation: The Special Marriage Act, 1954 provides for a civil marriage between any two people, whatever their religion, without either having to convert.

questions.text: The green revolution in India started in the late 1960s in _______.
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution, built on high-yielding varieties of wheat and rice, began in the late 1960s in Punjab, with Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh.

questions.text: What are the industrially developed urban centers usually surrounded by?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives an agricultural rural hinterland: an industrial city is ringed by countryside that supplies it with food, raw materials and workers and buys its goods. Coastal and seaport hinterlands belong to ports.

questions.text: What is the term used for people who regularly move in and out of poverty line?
questions.explanation: The churning poor move in and out of poverty regularly, such as small farmers and seasonal workers. The chronic poor are always or usually poor, and the occasionally poor are rich most of the time but sometimes hit a patch of bad luck; the churning and occasionally poor together are the transient poor.

questions.text: The ________ allocates ranks and portfolios to the ministers in the states.
questions.explanation: The chief minister decides who becomes a minister, at what rank, and which portfolios each holds. The Governor formally appoints the ministers and allocates business among them (Articles 164 and 166), but does so on the chief minister's advice.

questions.text: Identify a dwarf planet from the following list.
questions.explanation: In 2006 the International Astronomical Union reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet, as it has not cleared the neighbourhood of its orbit. Neptune, Mercury and Mars are planets.

questions.text: _______ Fundamental duties are listed in Article ______ of Part IV A of the Indian Constitution.
questions.explanation: Article 51A in Part IVA lists 11 Fundamental Duties: ten added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) and the eleventh by the 86th Amendment (2002).

questions.text: 2020 Summer Paralympics was hosted by _______________.
questions.explanation: Tokyo, Japan hosted the 2020 Summer Paralympics, held in August and September 2021 after a year's delay because of Covid-19.

questions.text: The term "LBW" Is related to which sport?
questions.explanation: LBW, leg before wicket, is a way of being out in cricket.

questions.text: The person or entity writing the cheque is known as the payer or _________.
questions.explanation: The drawer writes and signs the cheque; the drawee is the bank on which it is drawn, and the payee the person to be paid.

questions.text: Sher Khan defeated Humayun at Chausa in ______.
questions.explanation: At Chausa, near Buxar in Bihar, Sher Khan (later Sher Shah Suri) defeated Humayun in 1539, and again at Kannauj in 1540.

questions.text: Which of the following was a provincial capital under the rule of Ashoka? I. Taxila II. Ujjain
questions.explanation: Under Ashoka, Taxila in the north-west and Ujjain in Avanti were both provincial capitals, as were Tosali in Kalinga and Suvarnagiri in the south.

questions.text: Who has been appointed as the 16th Attorney General of India in September 2022?
questions.explanation: In September 2022 the President appointed R Venkataramani Attorney General for India for three years from 1 October 2022, succeeding K K Venugopal.

questions.text: Who was the Presidential candidate of India by opposition parties in June 2022?
questions.explanation: In June 2022 the opposition parties named Yashwant Sinha their joint candidate for the presidential election, which the NDA's candidate, Draupadi Murmu, won in July 2022.

questions.text: Which of the following organization governs the international trade?
options: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
Securities and Exchange Board of India
questions.explanation: The World Trade Organization, set up on 1 January 1995, deals with the rules of trade between nations. The ILO deals with labour, UNESCO with education, science and culture, and SEBI regulates India's securities market.

questions.text: A specific place of an organism in the food chain is called as _____________.
questions.explanation: Each step of a food chain is a trophic level, the place an organism occupies in it: producers, then primary, secondary and tertiary consumers.

questions.text: ___________ is the chemical formula of ethanoic Acid.
questions.explanation: Ethanoic (acetic) acid is CH₃COOH; CH₃OH is methanol.

questions.text: Makar Sankranti marks the beginning of ‘Uttarayana’ and is celebrated on ______________.
questions.explanation: Makar Sankranti, when the sun enters Makara (Capricorn), falls on 14 January in most years (15 January in some).

questions.text: Which of the following dance types is NOT associated with Jharkhand?
questions.explanation: Lavani is a song-and-dance form of Maharashtra. Phagua and Mardana Jhumar are folk dances of Jharkhand, and common lists of the state's dances include Agni as well.

questions.text: Which among the following Indian Classical Dancer has been awarded Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellow ( Akademi Ratna)?
questions.explanation: The Odissi and Bharatanatyam dancer Sonal Mansingh was made a Fellow of the Sangeet Natak Akademi (Akademi Ratna) for 2018, announced in July 2019.

questions.text: The ratio of the weight of Ram, Shyam and Mohan is 7 : 8 : 5 respectively. The average weight of Ram, Shyam and Mohan is 80 kg. What is the average weight of Ram and Shyam ?
questions.explanation: The total weight is 3 × 80 = 240 kg in the ratio 7 : 8 : 5, so one part is 12 kg: Ram weighs 84 kg and Shyam 96 kg, an average of 90 kg.

questions.text: In a 500 m race, P runs at 2 kmph. P gives Q a head start of 20 m and still beats him by 60 seconds. Find the speed of Q.
questions.explanation: P runs 500 m at 2 km/h in 0.25 h = 900 s. Q runs 480 m in 900 + 60 = 960 s, at 0.5 m/s = 1.8 km/h.

questions.text: A batsman scored 96 runs which included 2 boundaries and 6 sixes. What percent of his total score did he make by running between the wickets?
questions.explanation: Boundaries and sixes give 2 × 4 + 6 × 6 = 44 runs, so 96 − 44 = 52 were run: 52/96 × 100 = 54.166...%, printed as 54.16 percent.

questions.text: The marked price of a toy is Rs.1,600. If the shopkeeper declares a discount of 10% and then 10% cash discount, then what is the selling price of the toy?

The valuation of a house depreciates at the rate of 10% in a year, compared to its value at the beginning of that year. If the current value of the house is ₹40,00,000, then what will be the value of house after three years?
Reeta says that she sells her goods at the cost price. If she uses 80 gram weight instead of 100 gram, then what is her profit percentage?
questions.explanation: She gives 80 g for the price of 100 g, gaining 20 g on every 80 g: 20/80 × 100 = 25%.

questions.text: Suman and Arun together can finish a piece of work in 96 days, Arun and Rahul in 48 days, and Rahul and Suman in 80 days, then Rahul, Suman, and Arun jointly can finish the same work in approximately how many days?
questions.explanation: Adding the three pairs: 2(S + A + R) = 1/96 + 1/48 + 1/80 = (5 + 10 + 6)/480 = 21/480 of the work a day, so the three together do 21/960 a day and take 960/21 ≈ 45.7, about 46 days.

questions.text: The average weight of 10 persons increases by 7.9 kg when a new person replaces one of them weighing 20 kg. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.explanation: The total rises by 10 × 7.9 = 79 kg, so the new person weighs 20 + 79 = 99 kg.

questions.text: Anand can row 8 km/h in still water. It takes him thrice as long to row up as to row down the stream. Find the speed of the stream.
questions.explanation: With the stream's speed s, rowing up takes three times as long, so the downstream speed is three times the upstream: 8 + s = 3(8 − s), 4s = 16 and s = 4 km/h.

questions.text: On a certain principal, the compound interest, compounded annually, for the second year at 20% per annum is Rs.1,300. The principal is (consider nearest integral value):
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives ₹5,416, the option nearest the exact answer: the second year's interest is 20% of the amount after one year, so 0.2 × 1.2P = 0.24P = ₹1,300 and P = 1,300 ÷ 0.24 = ₹5,416.67, which is strictly ₹5,417 to the nearest rupee.

questions.text: Two cars start taking laps of a circular track of 3.6 kms at the same time of 12:00 PM. They start from the same point and they are moving in the same direction. Their speeds are 72 kmph and 90 kmph respectively. At what time will the cars meet again?
questions.explanation: The faster car gains 90 − 72 = 18 km/h on the other, so it gains a full lap of 3.6 km in 3.6/18 = 0.2 h = 12 minutes: they meet again at 12:12 PM.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. The local police were working “hand in glove” with Federal Bureau of Investigation to find the reasons behind the murder.
options: To have liking for each other
questions.explanation: To work 'hand in glove' with someone is to work in close association with them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate spelling that can correctly substitute the misspelt underlined segment in the given sentence. Who will “adjuddicate” on this matter?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'adjudicate', with a single 'd' in '-judi-': to judge or decide a matter formally.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Timid
questions.explanation: 'Timid' means lacking courage, easily frightened: 'fearful'. 'Bold', 'adventurous' and 'forthcoming' are nearly opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Disdain
questions.explanation: 'Disdain' is the feeling that someone or something is unworthy of respect; its opposite is 'respect'. 'Antipathy', 'scorn' and 'dislike' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The price of fuel is “declining” as the elections are approaching.
questions.explanation: A price that is 'declining' is falling, that is 'decreasing'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The blind man can perform / wonderfully well even though / he was old now.
questions.explanation: 'Can perform' and 'now' set the sentence in the present, so the last part needs the present tense: 'he is old now'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Bounce something off someone
options: Distribute materials to the poor and the needy
Discuss ideas with someone to get their views
Select members for something without their consent
Throw stones at others without any reason
questions.explanation: To 'bounce something off someone' is to share an idea with them to hear what they think of it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. An unexpected power failure which “happened besides the recording” disheartened all of them.
questions.explanation: 'Besides' means in addition to; a power failure that happens while something is going on happens 'during' it.

questions.text: Identify from the following options the word which is OPPOSITE in meaning to the given word. Valiant
questions.explanation: 'Valiant' means brave; its opposite is 'cowardly'. 'Heroic' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. The soldiers exhibited their ____________ (courage) during the war.
questions.explanation: 'Valour' is great courage, especially in battle. 'Candour' is frankness, 'timidity' the opposite of courage, and an 'anchor' holds a ship in place.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He fell unconscious due to a snake bite, so the doctor quickly gave him __________.
questions.explanation: An 'antidote' counteracts a poison such as snake venom. An antibiotic fights bacteria, an antigen provokes an immune response, and an antiquary studies or collects antiques.

questions.text: The sentence given below has one misspelt word. Spot the INCORRECTLY spelt word and select its correct spelling. He picked up his lugage and crossed the road.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'luggage', with a double 'g' in the middle.

questions.text: Select the correct pair of homonyms to fill in the blanks. The Prime Minister __________ the nation asking for the ________ of the traitors.
questions.explanation: 'Address' is a homonym: as a verb it means to speak to ('addressed the nation') and as a noun the place where someone lives ('the address of the traitors').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. I think he is the _________ person for this job.
questions.explanation: 'Right' here means suitable: 'the right person for this job'. 'Write', 'rite' and 'wright' sound the same but mean to put words on paper, a ceremony and a maker.

questions.text: Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. People in temperate (country pay little attention) to mangroves.
questions.explanation: 'Temperate' describes a group of countries, so the noun is plural, 'countries', and the plural subject 'people' takes 'pay': 'People in temperate countries pay little attention to mangroves.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. While stone sculptures and reliefs (1)_________ the exterior of great religious monuments for many centuries, bronze sculptures of the gods were probably a later development. In southern India, kings and queens of the Chola dynasty were well- known patrons of great Hindu (2)________. Marvellous bronze sculptures were worshipped in the temple context, and carried through the streets in (3)___________ during religious festivals. Such great temple festivals, involving massive carts that transport divine images, still (4)___________ today throughout India, and major celebrations may draw hundreds of thousands of participants. Such images were popular during the Chola dynasty because people increasingly wanted a more intimate, emotional relationship with the gods. These ideas were (5)___________ to the religious movement known as ‘Bhakti’, a personal and emotional experience of divinity.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Stone sculptures and reliefs 'ornamented', that is decorated, the outside of the great monuments.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. While stone sculptures and reliefs (1)_________ the exterior of great religious monuments for many centuries, bronze sculptures of the gods were probably a later development. In southern India, kings and queens of the Chola dynasty were well- known patrons of great Hindu (2)________. These ideas were (5)___________ to the religious movement known as ‘Bhakti’, a personal and emotional experience of divinity.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The Chola kings and queens were patrons of great Hindu 'temples', the setting in which the next sentence places the bronzes.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Images are carried through the streets during festivals in 'processions'.

questions.explanation: Such festivals still 'occur', that is take place, throughout India today.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: These ideas were 'central' to the Bhakti movement: they lay at its heart.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. TDKV, MWOZ, FPSD, ? , RBAL
questions.explanation: The first letters move back 7 (T, M, F, Y, R), the second back 7 (D, W, P, I, B), the third forward 4 (K, O, S, W, A) and the fourth forward 4 (V, Z, D, H, L), wrapping round the alphabet: YIWH.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1. Tasty 2. Tackle 3. Tamarind 4. Tadpole 5. Tagline
questions.explanation: All five begin with 'Ta', so the third letters decide: Tackle (c), Tadpole (d), Tagline (g), Tamarind (m), Tasty (s), that is 2, 4, 5, 3, 1.

questions.text: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Marshal is sitting second to the left of Sandra. Carol is sitting second to the right of Sandra. Shashi is the immediate neighbour of Sandra and Carol. Sahil is sitting third to the left of Sandra. Jade is sitting third to the left of Carol. Who is sitting between Marshal and Carol?
questions.explanation: Going round to Sandra's left, the order is Sandra, Jade, Marshal, Sahil, Carol, Shashi: Marshal second to her left, Carol second to her right, Shashi between Sandra and Carol, Sahil third to her left and Jade third to Carol's left. Sahil sits between Marshal and Carol.

questions.text: Six people J, K, L, M, N and O are sitting in a straight row, facing north. O and N are sitting at the extreme ends of the line. There are only three people to the right of K and only three people to the left of J. O is sitting second to the left of K. M is sitting in between J and N. Who is sitting in between O and K?
questions.explanation: From left to right: O, L, K, J, M, N. K is third (three people to his right), J fourth (three to his left), O second to K's left at one end, N at the other end and M between J and N, which leaves L between O and K.

questions.text: ‘Flow’ is related to ‘Stagnant’ in the same way as ‘Fall’ is related to ‘________’. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word)
questions.explanation: Stagnant water does not flow, so 'stagnant' is the opposite of 'flow'; the opposite of 'fall' is 'rise'.

questions.text: In a certain code language BANTER is written as ‘EZQSHQ’ and HAVEN is written as ‘KZYDQ’. How will ADVENT be written in the same code language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +3 and −1 in turn: BANTER → EZQSHQ and HAVEN → KZYDQ. So ADVENT → D C Y D Q S: DCYDQS.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’, ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the father of B’, ‘A x B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’, ‘A & B’ means ‘A is the son of B’ and ‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’. How is G related to N if N x P @ Q – L x M & G?
questions.explanation: N is the brother of P, P the sister of Q, Q the father of L, L the brother of M and M the son of G. G is the mother of M and L, so Q's wife; Q is N's brother, so G is N's brother's wife.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 35 + 21 – 168 ÷ 28 × 7 = 154
Which of the following letters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter series? D, B, X, R, J, ?
questions.explanation: The letters move back 2, 4, 6 and 8 places: D (4), B (2), X (24), R (18), J (10). Moving back 10 from J, wrapping round the alphabet, gives Z.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All tubes are pipes. All switches are pipes. All pipes are boards. Conclusions: I. All switches are boards. II. All boards are tubes. III. Some boards are switches.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: All switches are pipes and all pipes are boards, so all switches are boards (I), and so some boards are switches (III). Nothing makes every board a tube, so II does not follow.

questions.text: In a code language, 'DEVOTE' is written as ‘71’ and ‘DIALECT’ is written as ‘54’. How will 'DIESEL' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet: DEVOTE = 4 + 5 + 22 + 15 + 20 + 5 = 71 and DIALECT = 4 + 9 + 1 + 12 + 5 + 3 + 20 = 54. DIESEL = 4 + 9 + 5 + 19 + 5 + 12 = 54.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 45 + 3 ÷ 27 - 9 × 18 = 14
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 2, ?, 10, 14, 18, 22, 26, 30
questions.explanation: Each term is 4 more than the one before: 2 + 4 = 6, and 6 + 4 = 10.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term. 18 : 30 :: ? : 66 :: 54 : 102
questions.explanation: Each second number is twice the first minus 6: 18 × 2 − 6 = 30 and 54 × 2 − 6 = 102. So ? × 2 − 6 = 66 gives 36.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Poem : Poet :: Shoes : ?
questions.explanation: A poet makes poems; a cobbler makes and mends shoes.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 40, 40, ?, 58, 76, 100,130
The ___________ has the authority to regulate microfinance in India.
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India regulates microfinance in India, including the NBFC-MFIs (non-banking finance companies that specialise in it).

questions.text: Which was not the part of Original Indian Constitution that was adopted in the year 1950?
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, Article 51A) were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976. The emergency provisions, the Directive Principles and the Fundamental Rights were in the Constitution as adopted on 26 November 1949, which came into force on 26 January 1950.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Bastar Rebellion in central India broke out in ______.
questions.explanation: The Bastar rebellion (the Bhumkal), led by Gunda Dhur, broke out in 1910 against the colonial government's reservation of the forests of the Bastar state.

questions.text: Pawan Hans Helicopters Limited provides helicopter services to whom in its off-shore operations?
questions.explanation: Pawan Hans was set up in 1985 chiefly to give helicopter support to the oil sector's offshore exploration, and its helicopters fly ONGC's crews and supplies to ONGC's offshore rigs and platforms. ONGC also owned 49% of the company when the exam was held (January 2023).

questions.text: Which of the following is a type of earthquake wave?
questions.explanation: P-waves (primary waves) are earthquake body waves, the fastest and the first to arrive; S-waves and surface waves are the other kinds. There are no D-, B- or C-waves.

questions.text: Which of the following famous bollywood personalities won the by-elections in April 2022 to become the Member of Parliament from Asansol, West Bengal?
questions.explanation: Shatrughan Sinha won the Asansol Lok Sabha by-election in April 2022 as the Trinamool Congress candidate. Babul Supriyo, whose resignation had left the seat vacant, won the Ballygunge Assembly by-election in the same round.

questions.text: Indian Olympic Association was formed in which year?
questions.explanation: The Indian Olympic Association was formed in 1927.

questions.text: What is the timeframe of the second five year plan of India?
questions.explanation: The Second Five-Year Plan ran from 1956 to 1961 and, built on P. C. Mahalanobis's model, stressed heavy industry. The First ran from 1951 to 1956.

questions.text: _________five year plan was launched with specific objective of “Growth with Stability”
questions.explanation: The Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-74) set out to achieve 'growth with stability' and progressive self-reliance.

questions.text: As of November 2022, who among the following is the Governor of Uttar Pradesh, India?
questions.explanation: Anandiben Patel became Governor of Uttar Pradesh in July 2019, succeeding Ram Naik, and was in office in November 2022. Arif Mohammad Khan was then Governor of Kerala.

questions.text: When was the Supreme Court of India inaugurated?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court of India was inaugurated on 28 January 1950, two days after the Constitution came into force; it first sat in the Chamber of Princes in the Parliament building.

questions.text: Which of the following folk dances is associated with Jammu and Kashmir?
questions.explanation: Kud is a ritual folk dance of the Jammu region, performed at night to thank the local deities (Lok Devtas). Jawara belongs to Madhya Pradesh, Bhavai to Gujarat and Rajasthan, and Hojagiri to Tripura.

questions.text: The motto of Asian Games 2018 was _______________.
options: Play for Peace, Progress and Prosperity
questions.explanation: The motto of the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta and Palembang was 'Energy of Asia'. 'Ever Onward' is the standing motto of the Asian Games as a whole, and 'Diversity Shines Here' was the slogan of the 2014 Games in Incheon.

questions.text: Under which scheme, an overdraft (OD) facility up to Rs. 10,000 is available to eligible account holders?
questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana accounts carry an overdraft facility, raised from ₹5,000 to ₹10,000 in September 2018.

questions.text: Who among the following was the last king of the Mauryan empire?
questions.explanation: Brihadratha, the last Mauryan king, was killed by his general Pushyamitra Shunga, who founded the Shunga dynasty (about 185 BCE).

questions.text: Which Indian state has the second lowest literacy rate as per the Census report 2011?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Bihar had the lowest literacy rate (about 61.8%) and Arunachal Pradesh the second lowest (about 65.4%), just below Rajasthan (about 66.1%).

questions.text: If the proportion of fine particles is relatively higher in soil, then it is called ______ soil.
questions.explanation: Soil with a larger share of fine particles is clayey; a larger share of big particles makes it sandy, and a mix of sand, clay and silt is loamy.

questions.text: Which of the following artist has received the Soviet Land Nehru Award?
questions.explanation: The Kathak maestro Pandit Birju Maharaj received the Soviet Land Nehru Award, among many honours that include the Padma Vibhushan (1986).

questions.text: A boat's speed in still water is 9 km/h, while the stream’s speed is 1.5 km/h. A man rows to a location 105 km away and then returns to his starting position. The total time taken by him is:
questions.explanation: Downstream the boat makes 9 + 1.5 = 10.5 km/h and upstream 9 − 1.5 = 7.5 km/h. Time = 105/10.5 + 105/7.5 = 10 + 14 = 24 hours.
