questions.text: A retailer purchased some goods for ₹1,280 and he sold one-third at a loss of 15%.At what gain percentage should the remaining be sold, so as to gain 15% on the whole transaction?
questions.explanation: The gains on the two parts, weighted by their shares of the cost, must average 15%. With a gain of x% on the remaining two-thirds: (1/3)(−15) + (2/3)x = 15, so (2/3)x = 20 and x = 30%.

questions.text: A sofa-set is offered for sale at three successive discounts of 10%, 5%, and 2%. Find the net selling price of the sofa-set, if its marked price is ₹18,000.

Ratio of Copper and Gold in first and second alloy are 3 : 4 and 2 : 5 respectively. 14 kg of the first alloy is mixed with 21 kg of the second alloy. Find the ratio of Copper and Gold, respectively, in the new mixture.
questions.explanation: The first alloy holds 14 × 3/7 = 6 kg copper and 8 kg gold, the second 21 × 2/7 = 6 kg copper and 15 kg gold. Copper : gold = 12 : 23.

questions.text: P can do a piece of work in 200 days. Q and R can do the same work in 100 days. P, Q and R started the work together and they worked together for 40 days and then Q left the work and P and R together finished the remaining work in 40 days. Find the number of days in which Q alone can do the total work.
questions.explanation: In 40 days P, Q and R do 40 × (1/200 + 1/100) = 3/5 of the work. P and R finish the other 2/5 in 40 days, so together they do 1/100 a day and R alone 1/100 − 1/200 = 1/200. Q and R together do 1/100 a day, so Q alone does 1/100 − 1/200 = 1/200 a day: 200 days.

questions.text: If a shopkeeper offers a 10% discount, he makes a 10% profit. Under the same conditions, if he offers a 25% discount, then how much percentage of profit or loss will he get?
questions.explanation: 0.9 × marked price = 1.1 × cost, so the marked price is 11/9 of the cost. At 25% off he gets 0.75 × 11/9 = 11/12 of the cost: a loss of 1/12, or 8.33%.

questions.text: Find the greatest possible length which can be used to measure exactly the lengths 8 m 75 cm, 1.75 m and 12 m 20 cm.
questions.explanation: The lengths are 875 cm, 175 cm and 1,220 cm. 875 = 5³ × 7, 175 = 5² × 7 and 1,220 = 2² × 5 × 61, so their HCF is 5 cm.

questions.text: The difference between simple and compound interests compounded annually on a certain sum of money for 2 years at 4% per annum is Rs.80. The sum (in Rs.) is:
In an election between A and B, B secured 16,200 votes and defeated A by 8% of the total votes. If there are no invalid votes, what is the difference in votes between A and B?
questions.explanation: B won by 8% of the votes, so B got 54% and A 46%. 0.54 × total = 16,200 gives a total of 30,000, and the margin is 8% of it, 2,400.

questions.text: The average of 7 natural numbers is 70. Among them six numbers are 32, 69, 72, 65, 79, 48. What is the seventh number?
questions.explanation: The seven numbers add up to 7 × 70 = 490 and the six given ones to 365, so the seventh is 490 − 365 = 125.

questions.text: The area of a right-angled triangle is 42 cm². If its perpendicular is equal to 10 cm, find the length of its base.
questions.explanation: ½ × base × 10 = 42, so base = 84 ÷ 10 = 8.4 cm.

questions.text: The fourth proportional to 3,5,9 is:
A solid sphere is cut into two equal halves. What is the ratio of the total surface area of each hemisphere to that of the solid sphere?
questions.explanation: Each hemisphere has a curved surface of 2πr² and a flat face of πr², 3πr² in all, against the sphere's 4πr²: 3 : 4.

questions.text: Find the mean proportional between 256 and 484.
questions.explanation: Mean proportional = √(256 × 484) = 16 × 22 = 352.

questions.text: A car driver is driving car at a speed of 70 km/h and a bus is moving 35 metres ahead of him. After 15 seconds, the bus is 40 metres behind of him. Find the speed of the bus.
questions.explanation: The car gains 35 + 40 = 75 m on the bus in 15 seconds, so it is 5 m/s, or 18 km/h, faster. The bus runs at 70 − 18 = 52 km/h.

questions.text: A and B can complete a piece of work in 18 days and 12 days, respectively. They work on alternate days till the work gets completed. How long (in days) would it take A and B to complete the work, starting with A on the first day?
questions.explanation: Take the work as 36 units: A does 2 a day and B 3. Each two-day pair does 5 units, so 7 pairs (14 days) do 35, and A finishes the last unit in half a day: 14.5 days.

questions.text: In an election contested by two parties, party A secured 16 percent of the total votes more than party B. If party B got 25200 votes and there are no invalid votes, by how many votes did party B lose the election?
questions.explanation: A got 16% of the votes more than B, so B got 42% and A 58%. 0.42 × total = 25,200 gives 60,000 votes, and the margin is 16% of that, 9,600.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. The doctor had to go with operation as Raj’s condition was very _________ (comical).
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'comical' is 'serious', and a serious condition is one that calls for an operation.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word to fill in the blank in the sentence. Yields Binu’s land _________ high quality of wheat and grams.
questions.explanation: 'Yields' here means 'produces': the land produces good wheat and grams.

questions.text: Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Nishtha writes very well, (didn't she)?
questions.explanation: A positive statement in the simple present takes a negative tag with 'does' and the subject's pronoun: 'Nishtha writes very well, doesn't she?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Brittle
questions.explanation: 'Brittle' means hard but easily broken; 'resilient' means able to withstand shocks and recover. 'Delicate' is close in meaning to 'brittle'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Blow one’s own trumpet
questions.explanation: To 'blow one's own trumpet' is to praise oneself, boasting of one's own achievements.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Dazzling
questions.explanation: 'Dazzling' means extremely bright or impressive: 'brilliant'. 'Murky' and 'dull' are nearly opposite.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. While my wife / cooked the food, / I writing / a book.
questions.explanation: 'Writing' needs a helping verb: 'I was writing a book' (or 'I wrote a book').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. He had created a “cocoon” of human activities - conversation, interaction, affection - and it filled his life like an overflowing soup bowl.
questions.explanation: A cocoon is a protective covering; 'encasement', a case or covering that encloses something, is the closest.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'technique'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word to fill in the blank. He “borrowed” money from his father and ________ it to his friend to help him.
questions.explanation: To borrow is to take money that must be returned; the opposite, to give it for a time, is to 'lend': 'lent'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The manager decided to _________ the meeting, as many of the members were not present.
questions.explanation: To 'call off' a meeting is to cancel it, which suits a meeting with too few members present.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Applaud
questions.explanation: To 'applaud' is to praise or approve; to 'denounce' is to condemn publicly. 'Commend' and 'approve' are synonyms.

questions.text: Select the appropriate idiom that can replace the underlined phrase in the following sentence. As he is never on time, he “regrets uselessly” on missing the flight.
questions.explanation: To 'cry over spilt milk' (printed 'split') is to regret uselessly something that cannot be undone.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. VPN allows us to use the internet anonymously “to value our safety” and our identity.
questions.explanation: Anonymity online protects its users: it is used 'to ensure our safety and our identity'. 'Value' does not say what anonymity does, 'improve' does not fit 'our identity', and 'derogate' (belittle) goes against the sense.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Munoo began (1)_________. He felt resentful and disheartened, thinking how he hated his uncle. But he saw that the fellow on the steel horse, who had been the cause of his (2)_________, had come to grief fifty yards ahead, having collided with a calf (3) __________ among the crowds of men and women near the fruit shops at the crossroads. So he walked along reassured, forgetful still but sufficiently cautious, with (4) _________ ahead of him, another on the row of shops, and an occasional glance behind, to see that there was not another steel horse, or bicycle, as the juggler (5)_________it, following.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Began' is followed by a to-infinitive (or an -ing form), not a bare infinitive, a past form or a perfect participle: 'Munoo began to cry'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Munoo began (1)_________. He felt resentful and disheartened, thinking how he hated his uncle. But he saw that the fellow on the steel horse, who had been the cause of his (2)_________, had come to grief fifty yards ahead, having collided with a calf (3) __________ among the crowds of men and women near the fruit shops at the crossroads. So he walked along reassured, forgetful still but sufficiently cautious, with (4) _________ ahead of him, another on the row of shops, and an occasional glance behind, to see that there was not another steel horse, or bicycle, as the juggler (5)_________it, following.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: After the possessive 'his' a noun is needed: 'the cause of his punishment'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Munoo began (1)_________. He felt resentful and disheartened, thinking how he hated his uncle. But he saw that the fellow on the steel horse, who had been the cause of his (2)_________, had come to grief fifty yards ahead, having collided with a calf (3) __________ among the crowds of men and women near the fruit shops at the crossroads. So he walked along reassured, forgetful still but sufficiently cautious, with (4) _________ ahead of him, another on the row of shops, and an occasional glance behind, to see that there was not another steel horse, or bicycle, as the juggler (5)_________it, following.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: A calf is an animal, so the relative pronoun is 'that' (or 'which'): 'a calf that strayed among the crowds'. 'Who' is used for people, and 'whom' and 'whose' cannot be the subject of 'strayed'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Munoo began (1)_________. He felt resentful and disheartened, thinking how he hated his uncle. But he saw that the fellow on the steel horse, who had been the cause of his (2)_________, had come to grief fifty yards ahead, having collided with a calf (3) __________ among the crowds of men and women near the fruit shops at the crossroads. So he walked along reassured, forgetful still but sufficiently cautious, with (4) _________ ahead of him, another on the row of shops, and an occasional glance behind, to see that there was not another steel horse, or bicycle, as the juggler (5)_________it, following.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: To keep 'an eye on' something is to watch it: one eye on his uncle ahead of him, another on the row of shops.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Munoo began (1)_________. He felt resentful and disheartened, thinking how he hated his uncle. But he saw that the fellow on the steel horse, who had been the cause of his (2)_________, had come to grief fifty yards ahead, having collided with a calf (3) __________ among the crowds of men and women near the fruit shops at the crossroads. So he walked along reassured, forgetful still but sufficiently cautious, with (4) _________ ahead of him, another on the row of shops, and an occasional glance behind, to see that there was not another steel horse, or bicycle, as the juggler (5)_________it, following.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The juggler's naming came before the moment the passage describes, so the active past perfect fits the past narration: 'as the juggler had called it'. The passives 'have been called' and 'had been called' cannot take 'the juggler' as subject and 'it' as object, and 'has called' clashes with the past narration.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 9, 17, ?, 57, 89, 129
questions.explanation: The differences rise by 8 each time: 9 + 8 = 17, 17 + 16 = 33, 33 + 24 = 57, 57 + 32 = 89 and 89 + 40 = 129.

questions.text: Which letter cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? YAFU, CRRE, ?, KZPY, OQBI
questions.explanation: Each letter moves forward a fixed number of places, wrapping round after Z: the first by 4 (Y, C, G, K, O), the second by 17 (A, R, I, Z, Q), the third by 12 (F, R, D, P, B) and the fourth by 10 (U, E, O, Y, I). The missing cluster is GIDO.

questions.text: Eight people, A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H are sitting in a straight line, facing north. Only three people sit to the right of A. Only one person sits between A and B. Only four people sit between B and D. F sits to the immediate right of D. C is neither an immediate neighbour of B nor D. E sits second to the right of G. How many people sit between H and A?
questions.explanation: Numbering the seats 1 to 8 from the left, A is 5th. B is then 3rd or 7th, with four people between him and D; F sits on D's right, which rules out D 8th, so B is 7th, D 2nd and F 3rd. C, next to neither B nor D, is 4th, and E second to the right of G puts G 6th and E 8th, leaving H 1st: D, F and C, three people, sit between H and A.

questions.text: In a certain code language, the word ‘FORM’ is numerically coded as 25. The word ‘SUIT’ is numerically coded as 96. How is the word ‘RING’ numerically coded in the same code language?
questions.explanation: Each word's code is the sum of its letters' places in the alphabet with the digits reversed: FORM = 6 + 15 + 18 + 13 = 52 → 25 and SUIT = 19 + 21 + 9 + 20 = 69 → 96. So RING = 18 + 9 + 14 + 7 = 48 → 84.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 128 - 8 + 96 ÷ 16 × 20 = 16
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 4, 9, 17, 35, ?, 139
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before, plus and minus 1 in turn: 4 × 2 + 1 = 9, 9 × 2 − 1 = 17, 17 × 2 + 1 = 35, 35 × 2 − 1 = 69 and 69 × 2 + 1 = 139.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FRUIT’ is written as ‘HTUKV’ and ‘TWEAK’ is written as ‘VYECM’. How will ‘VOWEL’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first, second, fourth and fifth letters move 2 places forward and the middle letter stays: F R U I T → H T U K V and T W E A K → V Y E C M. So V O W E L → X Q W G N: XQWGN.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All waters are inks. All glues are inks. All inks are pens. Conclusions: I. All glues are pens. II. All pens are waters. III. Some pens are glues.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: All glues are inks and all inks are pens, so all glues are pens (I), and so some pens are glues (III). Nothing says that every pen is a water, so II does not follow.

questions.text: ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’; ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; If R + T × S – P ÷ Q + N, then which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: Q is the mother of T.
P is the mother of Q.
T is the brother of S.
R is the wife of T.
questions.explanation: R is T's wife, T is S's brother, S is P's husband, P is Q's mother and Q is N's wife. So Q, the daughter of P and S, is T's niece, not his mother; the other three statements are true.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the sixth number is related to the fifth number. 4 : 30 :: 7 : ? :: 6 : 56
questions.explanation: The second number is (n + 1) × (n + 2) for the first number n: 4 → 5 × 6 = 30 and 6 → 7 × 8 = 56. So 7 → 8 × 9 = 72.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Bat : Cricket :: Racquet : ?
questions.explanation: Cricket is played with a bat, and tennis with a racquet.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? FPA, HSB, IVD, KYE, ?, NEH
questions.explanation: The first letters move +2 and +1 in turn (F, H, I, K, L, N), the second +3 each time, wrapping round after Z (P, S, V, Y, B, E), and the third +1 and +2 in turn (A, B, D, E, G, H): LBG.

questions.text: ‘Expand’ is related to ‘Stretch’ in the same way as ‘Contract’ is related to ‘________’. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word)
questions.explanation: 'Stretch' means much the same as 'expand', and 'shrink' as 'contract'.

questions.text: Ten friends went to a restaurant to have their lunch and sat in two parallel rows facing each other, such that five members are sitting in each row. K, L, M, N, O are sitting in Row 1 facing north, while persons F, G, H, I, J in Row 2 face south. N is facing the neighbour of J. Two persons sit between J and H. I sits in the middle of the line. G does not sit at any of the corners; G is neither facing M nor K. K sits to the left of M but not immediate left. J is the immediate neighbour of the person who is sitting at the corner. N does not sit at any of the corners. L is sitting second to the left of N. How many persons are sitting between J and G?
questions.explanation: Number the seats 1 to 5 from the west. I is 3rd in Row 2; J sits next to a corner seat with two people between him and H, so J and H are 2nd and 5th or 4th and 1st, and G, not at a corner, takes the other of seats 2 and 4. N, not at a corner, faces a neighbour of J, so N is 3rd in Row 1 and L, second to his left, 1st. If J were 4th, G (2nd) could face neither K nor M, so K and M would sit side by side in seats 4 and 5, which is ruled out; so J is 2nd and G 4th, and only I sits between them.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary? 1. MISTER 2. MASTER 3. MARTYR 4. MISTRESS 5. MARTHA
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: MARTHA (5), MARTYR (3), MASTER (2), MISTER (1), MISTRESS (4). 'Marth' comes before 'Marty', 'Mar' before 'Mas', and 'Miste' before 'Mistr'.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 64 * 140 * 2 * 4 * 10
questions.explanation: With =, ÷, + and −: 64 = 140 ÷ 2 + 4 − 10, as the right side is 70 + 4 − 10 = 64.

questions.text: The Industrial Policy Resolution,1956 classified the industries into _________ categories.
questions.explanation: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 sorted industries into three categories (Schedules A, B and C): those reserved for the State, those in which the State would progressively take the lead, and the rest, left mainly to private enterprise.

questions.text: A Feature of Indian contitution i.e. Centrifugal form of federalism where the centre is stronger than the states is based on which model?
questions.explanation: The Indian federation, with its strong Centre, follows the Canadian model rather than the American one: as in Canada, the residuary powers rest with the Centre and the heads of the states (in India, the Governors) are appointed by the Centre.

questions.text: Sonal Mansingh was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for which of the following classical dance forms?
questions.explanation: Sonal Mansingh, who dances both Odissi and Bharatanatyam, received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Odissi in 1987.

questions.text: What is the literacy rate among the males in India as per the Census 2011?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 put the literacy rate of males at 82.14%, against 65.46% for females and 74.04% overall.

questions.text: Atal Pension Yojana (APY), a pension scheme for citizens of India, is focused on the_______sector workers.
questions.explanation: The Atal Pension Yojana, launched in 2015 and administered by the PFRDA, is aimed mainly at workers in the unorganised sector, who have no formal pension.

questions.text: What is the standard height of a volleyball net from the ground for the men’s team?
questions.explanation: A volleyball net stands 2.43 m high for men and 2.24 m for women.

questions.text: Bhopal lake, one of the largest artificial lake of its time was built in which century?
questions.explanation: The Upper Lake of Bhopal, the Bhojtal, was created in the 11th century under the Paramara king Raja Bhoj, after whom it is named.

questions.text: Which of the following is not present in a nucleus?
questions.explanation: The nucleus holds the nucleolus and the chromosomes, made of DNA, which carry the genes. Vacuoles are sacs in the cytoplasm, outside the nucleus.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following acts passed by the Britishers disallowed Indians from possessing arms?
questions.explanation: The Indian Arms Act of 1878, passed under the Viceroy Lord Lytton, barred Indians from keeping arms without a licence, while Europeans were exempt.

questions.text: Who among the following has won the Balasaraswathi award for the year 2019?
questions.explanation: The Balasaraswathi award, the Tamil Nadu Eyal Isai Nataka Manram's all-India award for dance, for the year 2019 went to the Bharatanatyam dancer Alarmel Valli.

questions.text: Who was appointed as the new Chairman of CBSE in February 2022?
questions.explanation: On 14 February 2022 the Ministry of Education gave the charge of Chairman of CBSE to Vineet Joshi, then also Director General of the National Testing Agency, in place of Manoj Ahuja.

questions.text: Who among the following was the first ruler of the Sunga dynasty?
questions.explanation: Pushyamitra Sunga, the commander of the last Mauryan king Brihadratha, killed him and founded the Sunga dynasty in about 185 BCE.

questions.text: As of November 2022, who among the following is the Chief Minister of Delhi?
questions.explanation: Arvind Kejriwal was Chief Minister of Delhi in November 2022, in office since February 2015. V. Narayanaswamy had been Chief Minister of Puducherry until 2021, Pema Khandu was Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh and Manoj Sinha Lieutenant Governor of Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.text: Per capita income for a nation is calculated by dividing the country's national income by its _____________.
questions.explanation: Per capita income is the national income divided by the population: the average income per person.

questions.text: From which among the following countries Independence of judiciary has been borrowed in the Indian Constitution ?
questions.explanation: India took the independence of the judiciary, along with judicial review and fundamental rights, from the Constitution of the United States.

questions.text: Eden Gardens cricket ground is located in which of the following city?
questions.explanation: Eden Gardens, one of the oldest and largest cricket grounds in India, is in Kolkata.

questions.text: Sodium is kept in which of the following?
questions.explanation: Sodium reacts vigorously with water and with the oxygen and moisture in air, so it is stored under kerosene, with which it does not react.

questions.text: Karkidaka Vavu Bali of _________ is a Hindu ritual to appease ancestors.
questions.explanation: Karkidaka Vavu Bali is performed in Kerala on the new-moon day (vavu) of the Malayalam month of Karkidakam, when people make offerings (bali) to their ancestors, often on river banks and beaches.

questions.text: Green Revolution was originated in _________.
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution began in Mexico, where Norman Borlaug bred high-yielding, disease-resistant wheat from the 1940s; his dwarf varieties were later brought to India.

questions.text: In March, a shopkeeper has launched a discount scheme for 20% discount on the purchase of jeans and 12% discount on a coat. Also, he is offering 5% discount on using SBI card only to pay. Anand bought jeans of marked price of Rs.1,200 and a coat of marked price of Rs.4,500. How much does he have to pay if he pays through an HDFC Bank card?
questions.explanation: Only the SBI card earns the extra 5%, so with an HDFC card Anand pays 0.8 × 1,200 + 0.88 × 4,500 = 960 + 3,960 = ₹4,920.

questions.text: Akhil can complete a piece of work in 26 days. Sakshi and Akhil both can complete the same work in 20 days. They started together but Sakshi left after working for 6 days. Find the number of days in which Akhil will complete the remaining work.
questions.explanation: Take the work as 260 units: Akhil does 10 a day and the two together 13, so Sakshi does 3. In 6 days together they do 78 units, and Akhil does the remaining 182 in 182/10 = 91/5 days.

questions.text: If 24 women can complete a work in 16 days, in how many days 32 women will complete the same work?
questions.explanation: The work is 24 × 16 = 384 woman-days, so 32 women take 384 ÷ 32 = 12 days.

questions.text: If a person weighing 40 kg joins, then the average weight of a group increases by 1 kg. If the weight of this person had been 28 kg, then the average weight of the group would have decreased by 1 kg. The actual average weight of the group is:
questions.explanation: The 12 kg difference between the two weights moves the new average by 1 + 1 = 2 kg, so the new group has 12 ÷ 2 = 6 people and the original group 5. Then 5A + 40 = 6(A + 1), so A = 34 kg.

questions.text: The distance ‘d’ a moving body travels, varies directly with time ‘t’. When a train travels 120 miles in 3 h, then how many miles would it travel in 8 h?
questions.explanation: The speed is 120 ÷ 3 = 40 miles an hour, so in 8 h the train covers 40 × 8 = 320 miles.

questions.text: If the simple interest on a sum of money for two years at 5% per annum is Rs.50, then what is the compound interest when compounding annually at the same rate and for the same time?
questions.explanation: Simple interest for 2 years at 5% is 10% of the sum, so the sum is ₹500. CI = 500 × (1.05² − 1) = 500 × 0.1025 = ₹51.25.

questions.text: A toy car costs Rs. 1800. Its price is reduced to Rs. 1500 in the sale. By what percentage was the price reduced?
questions.explanation: The price falls by ₹300, which is 300/1800 × 100 = 50/3 percent of the original price.

questions.text: The LCM of the three numbers 120, 240 and 480 will be:
questions.explanation: 120 and 240 both divide 480, so the LCM of the three numbers is 480 itself.

questions.text: A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 380 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The thief and policeman run at the speed of 25 m/sec and 30 m/sec respectively. What is the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 30 − 25 = 5 m every second, so he closes the 380 m gap in 380 ÷ 5 = 76 sec.

questions.text: A shopkeeper decided the price of 2 sarees and 4 shirts to be ₹1,600.With the same money one can buy 1 saree and 6 shirts. If I want to buy 12 shirts how much shall I have to pay?
questions.explanation: 2 sarees + 4 shirts = 1 saree + 6 shirts, so a saree costs as much as 2 shirts. Then ₹1,600 buys 2 × 2 + 4 = 8 shirts, a shirt costs ₹200, and 12 shirts cost ₹2,400.

questions.text: Find the number of solid spheres, each of diameter 6 cm, that can be made by melting a solid metal cylinder of height 12 cm and diameter 6 cm.
questions.explanation: The cylinder's volume is π × 3² × 12 = 108π cm³ and each sphere's (4/3) × π × 3³ = 36π cm³, so 108π ÷ 36π = 3 spheres.

questions.text: A and B are two typists. One afternoon, they were each given 80 pages for typing. They divided the work equally, but B finished 40 minutes before A, who took 4 hours for the same. The next afternoon, they were again given 121 pages to type. However, this time they decided to divide the work such that they finished typing simultaneously. How many pages did A have to type?
questions.explanation: For the same number of pages A takes 4 h (240 min) and B 40 min less (200 min), so their speeds are in the ratio 200 : 240 = 5 : 6. To finish together they share the 121 pages 5 : 6, and A types 121 × 5/11 = 55 pages.

questions.text: Tina gets a discount of 15 percent on a grinder whose marked price is Rs. 8200. Since she pays cash, she gets an additional 3 percent discount too. How much does she pay?
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Add fuel to the flames
options: At the slightest signal or provocation
Making a bad situation even worse
questions.explanation: To 'add fuel to the flames' is to make a bad situation even worse, as fuel makes a fire burn more fiercely.

questions.text: Fill in the blanks with appropriate homonym. If you want to __________ the world, you should be the one to take the first step.
questions.explanation: To 'change the world' is to alter it, that is make it different; the other senses of 'change' (coins, a transfer, a switch) do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given below to fill in the blank in the following sentence. Austere; My uncle said, “Think about a monk who lives a ______ life”.
questions.explanation: 'Austere' means severely simple and strict: a monk lives a strict life, without comforts. 'Luxurious' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Affluent classes live a life high on the _________.
questions.explanation: To live 'high on the hog' is an idiom for living in luxury, as the rich do.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Computers are able to process _________ amounts of data in mere seconds.
questions.explanation: 'Massive' means very large: computers process huge amounts of data. The other options do not describe size or amount.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Deseive' is misspelt: the word is 'deceive', with 'c' and 'ei'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The surveyor wrote a report on the property after doing an “on-field evaluation”.
questions.explanation: A property is inspected at the place itself, and the usual term for that is an 'on-site assessment', an evaluation made at the site. 'On-field' is used of sport, and the 'off-site' and 'off-field' options reverse the sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. During the lockdown, many families “were barely able to make both the ends meet”.
options: can manage to make both the ends meet
could make both the ends meet
barely managed to make ends meet
were making both the ends meet
questions.explanation: The idiom is 'make ends meet' (manage on one's income), without 'both the', and 'barely managed' keeps the past sense: 'many families barely managed to make ends meet'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The students arranged an open _________ on the topic of pandemics and social life after them.
questions.explanation: An open 'debate' is a public discussion of a topic. 'Debase' means to lower in value, and 'drought' and 'debt' do not fit the sense.

questions.text: Which of the following options is most similar in meaning to the given word? Seize
questions.explanation: To 'seize' is to take hold of suddenly or by force, that is to 'catch'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in simple past tense. A. I was calling you some time back to resolve this issue. B. I had been calling you some time back to resolve this issue. C. I have called you some time back to resolve this issue. D. I called you some time back to resolve this issue.
questions.explanation: The simple past is the verb's past form alone: 'I called you'. A is in the past continuous, B in the past perfect continuous and C in the present perfect.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Ready
questions.explanation: 'Ready' also means prompt and quick to respond (a 'ready' reply); 'unresponsive', slow or failing to react, is its opposite in that sense. 'Set' means much the same as 'ready', and 'holistic' and 'humble' are unrelated.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. “To insure peace and calm”, the government imposed a countrywide curfew for three days.
options: In to ensure peace and calm
questions.explanation: To 'ensure' is to make certain; to 'insure' is to cover against loss with insurance. The curfew was meant to make sure of peace: 'To ensure peace and calm'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The manager would like to talk to the team member about “an important” issue immediately.
questions.explanation: 'Important' and 'significant' both mean of great consequence; 'an' becomes 'a' before the consonant sound of 'significant'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in the bracket to fill in the blank. He carried his method into every detail of life and lived on his earnings with extreme _________ (frugality).
questions.explanation: 'Frugality' is careful, sparing use of money; its opposite is 'luxury', costly comfort and indulgence.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. STATEMENTS: A. All pencils are sticks. B. Some sticks are notes. C. All diaries are notes. CONCLUSIONS: I. Some notes are diaries. II. Some sticks are pencils. III. Some diaries are sticks.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.
questions.explanation: All pencils are sticks, so some sticks are pencils (II), and all diaries are notes, so some notes are diaries (I). No statement links diaries with sticks, so III does not follow.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 120, 121, 128, 141, 160, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 1, 7, 13, 19, rising by 6 each time, so the next is 25: 160 + 25 = 185.

questions.text: ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’; ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the husband of B’; ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’; If P ÷ Q – R + S – T × U, then which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: P is the mother-in-law of U.
Q is the mother of S.
questions.explanation: P is Q's sister, Q is R's mother, R is S's brother, S is T's mother and T is U's husband. U's mother-in-law is T's mother, S, while P is the sister of S's mother, so 'P is the mother-in-law of U' is not correct. The other three statements hold.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. FWCD, HQEF, JKGH, ? , NYKL
questions.explanation: The first, third and fourth letters each move 2 forward (F, H, J, L, N; C, E, G, I, K; D, F, H, J, L), and the second moves 6 back, wrapping round after A (W, Q, K, E, Y). The missing cluster is LEIJ.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. PJE : RNK :: DHN : FLT :: AMS : ?
questions.explanation: The three letters move +2, +4 and +6: P → R, J → N, E → K and D → F, H → L, N → T. So A → C, M → Q, S → Y: CQY.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 25 + 8 ÷ 40 – 20 × 25 = 10

Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. James is sitting second to the right of Peter. Charles is sitting second to the left of Peter. Sam is sitting third to the right of James. Tom is sitting second to the right of Sam. Ashley is an immediate neighbour of Charles and James. Who is sitting between Ashley and Tom?
questions.explanation: Number the seats 0 to 5 going to Peter's right, with Peter at 0: James is at 2, Charles at 4 (second to Peter's left), Sam at 5, Tom at 1, and Ashley in the seat left over, 3, between Charles and James. James sits between Ashley (3) and Tom (1).

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 29, 65, 95, 119, ?, 149, 155
questions.explanation: The differences are 36, 30, 24, 18, 12, 6, falling by 6: 119 + 18 = 137, and 137 + 12 = 149.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 instant 2 invite 3 ingrained 4 initiate 5 intimate
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: ingrained (3), initiate (4), instant (1), intimate (5), invite (2), as 'ing' comes before 'ini', 'ins', 'int' and 'inv'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BRAND’ is written as ‘DTYPF’ and ‘TOWER’ is written as ‘VMYCT’. How will ‘STUDY’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Consonants move 2 forward and vowels 2 back: B R A N D → D T Y P F and T O W E R → V M Y C T. So S T U D Y → U V S F A (Y + 2 wraps round to A).

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (14, 231, 19) (7, 154, 15)
questions.explanation: The middle number is 7 times the sum of the other two: (14 + 19) × 7 = 231 and (7 + 15) × 7 = 154. Likewise (13 + 17) × 7 = 210.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? BMYU, YJVR, ?, SDPL, PAMI
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back at every step: B, Y, V, S, P; M, J, G, D, A; Y, V, S, P, M; U, R, O, L, I. The missing cluster is VGSO.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘TERMINATOR’ is written as ‘ROTANTERMI’ and ‘SUPERMAN’ is written as ‘NAMRSUPE’. How will ‘AVENGERS’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is split in half, and the second half is reversed and written first: TERMI NATOR → ROTAN TERMI and SUPE RMAN → NAMR SUPE. So AVEN GERS → SREG AVEN: SREGAVEN.

questions.text: Five friends (A, B, C, E and F) are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. F is sitting to the immediate right of C. A is sitting to the immediate left of C. E is sitting to the immediate right of F. Who is sitting to the immediate right of B?
questions.explanation: Going round to the right from C: F (on C's immediate right), then E (on F's immediate right), then B in the only seat left, then A, who is on C's immediate left. So A is on B's immediate right.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Three : Triangle :: Four : ?
questions.explanation: A triangle has three sides, and a rectangle has four.

questions.text: Fast food is often packed with fat and ___________.
questions.explanation: Fast food is high in fat and in 'empty calories', energy from sugar and refined starch that brings few vitamins, minerals or fibre. Iron, nutrients and calcium are what such food tends to lack.

questions.text: Identify the general formula for alkenes.
questions.explanation: Alkenes have one carbon-carbon double bond, so their general formula is CₙH₂ₙ (ethene, C₂H₄; propene, C₃H₆). Alkanes are CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ and alkynes CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.

questions.text: In India, a Small-scale industry is defined with reference to the ___________.
options: Maximum investment allowed on the assets of a unit.
questions.explanation: Small-scale industries in India have been defined by a ceiling on investment in fixed assets such as plant and machinery, not by the number of workers or owners; since 2020 annual turnover has been used as well.

questions.text: Which among the following festivals is the worship of 14 Gods and is celebrated in the month of July?
questions.explanation: Kharchi Puja, held at Old Agartala in Tripura in July (the month of Ashadha), is the worship of the fourteen deities (Chaturdasha Devata), the dynastic gods of the Tripuri people. Bonalu is a Telangana festival of the goddess Mahakali, and Losar the Tibetan new year.

questions.text: When was the initial 10 Fundamental Duties added to the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment of 1976, on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation, added ten Fundamental Duties in Article 51A (Part IV-A); the 86th Amendment of 2002 added an eleventh.

questions.text: Which Schedule of the Constitution of India deals with Union, State and Concurrent lists?
questions.explanation: The Seventh Schedule divides the subjects of legislation between the Union List, the State List and the Concurrent List (Article 246).

questions.text: India lies in which part of Asia?
questions.explanation: India is the largest country of South Asia, the region south of the Himalayas that also includes Pakistan, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and the Maldives.

questions.text: Who among the following hosted the 2019 South Asian Games?
questions.explanation: Nepal hosted the 13th South Asian Games in December 2019, with Kathmandu as the main venue.

questions.text: What is power, the most visible form of energy, which is often identified with progress in modern civilization, commonly called?
questions.explanation: Electricity is the power most visible in daily life and is often taken as a sign of progress; its consumption per person is used as a measure of development. Coal, oil and other fossil fuels are among the sources from which it is generated.

questions.text: In which year was the first edition of the Khelo India School Games held?
questions.explanation: The first Khelo India School Games, for under-17 athletes, were held in New Delhi from 31 January to 8 February 2018; later editions were renamed the Khelo India Youth Games.

questions.text: A co-operative bank in India, is registered under the States___________ Act.
questions.explanation: A co-operative bank is a co-operative society registered under its state's Co-operative Societies Act (or, if it works in more than one state, under the Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002); its banking business is regulated by the RBI.

questions.text: A telecommunication industry includes satellites, closed computer networks and________.
questions.explanation: Telecommunication carries voice and data over a distance, through telephone lines, satellites, computer networks and wireless networks. Induction cookers, tube wells and air conditioners are not means of communication.

questions.text: What happens at the inter tropical convergence zone?
options: The southwest and northwest trade winds converge
The southwest and northwest trade winds diverge
The southeast and northeast trade winds converge
The southeast and northwest trade winds converge
questions.explanation: At the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone, a low-pressure belt near the equator, the north-east trade winds of the northern hemisphere and the south-east trade winds of the southern hemisphere meet, and the air rises.

questions.text: As of November 2022, who is the Union Minister for Food Processing Industries in India?
questions.explanation: Pashupati Kumar Paras held the Food Processing Industries portfolio from July 2021 to March 2024, so he was the Union Minister in November 2022 and when the exam was held (January 2023). Hardeep Singh Puri then held Petroleum and Natural Gas, Nityanand Rai was Minister of State for Home Affairs, and R K Singh held Power.

questions.text: Chang Lo tribal dance is performed by the Chang tribe of ____________.
questions.explanation: Chang Lo, also called Sua Lua, is a dance of the Chang Naga tribe of Nagaland, once performed to celebrate victory over enemies and now at festivals such as Poanglem.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Name of the three of the following is often used together as a group. Pick the odd one out.
questions.explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal, the leading Extremists of the Congress, were known together as 'Lal-Bal-Pal'. Dadabhai Naoroji was a Moderate.

questions.text: Who holds the honour of being the Tirumala Tirupati Devastanam's Astana Nartaki?
questions.explanation: The Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams made Yamini Krishnamurthy, the Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancer from Andhra Pradesh, its Asthana Nartaki (resident dancer).

questions.text: The Startup India Initiative, launched on ___________ has rolled out several programs with the objective of supporting entrepreneurs.
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the Startup India initiative on 16 January 2016, with an action plan of simpler compliance, funding support and tax benefits for start-ups.

questions.text: Chaudhary Ajit Singh, who passed away in 2021, was the founder of which of the following parties?
questions.explanation: Chaudhary Ajit Singh, son of the former Prime Minister Charan Singh, founded the Rashtriya Lok Dal and led it until his death in May 2021. The Samajwadi Party was founded by Mulayam Singh Yadav and the Bahujan Samaj Party by Kanshi Ram.

questions.text: Ashvaghosha who composed ‘Buddhacharita’ lived in the court of ______.
questions.explanation: Ashvaghosha, the Buddhist poet who wrote the 'Buddhacharita', a life of the Buddha in Sanskrit, lived at the court of the Kushan king Kanishka.

questions.text: The average salary of all the workers in a factory is Rs.3,000. Among these workers, there are 12 higher officers and their average salary is Rs.12,000. The average salary of the remaining workers is Rs.2,500. The total number of the workers is ______.
The population of a town is increasing at 5% per annum. What will be the population of the town after 2 years, if the present population is 16000?

A and B can together finish a work in 30 days. They worked together for 20 days and then B left. After another 20 days, A finished the remaining work. In how many days can A alone finish the whole work?
questions.explanation: Together A and B do 1/30 of the work a day, so in 20 days they do 2/3. A finishes the remaining 1/3 in 20 days, so he alone would take 60 days.

questions.text: A, B and C together can complete a piece of work in 40/3 days. All three started working at it together and after 5 days A left. Then B and C together completed the remaining work in 17 days. Find the number of days (approximately) in which A alone can complete the total work.
questions.explanation: Together they do 3/40 of the work a day, so in 5 days 15/40 = 3/8 is done. B and C finish the other 5/8 in 17 days, doing 5/136 a day, so A does 3/40 − 5/136 = (51 − 25)/680 = 13/340 a day and alone takes 340/13 ≈ 26 days.

questions.text: Find the remainder when the smallest 6-digit number divisible by 12, 15 and 25 is divided by 9.
questions.explanation: LCM(12, 15, 25) = 300, and the smallest 6-digit multiple of 300 is 334 × 300 = 100200. Its digit sum is 3, so it leaves a remainder of 3 when divided by 9.

questions.text: A train travels from Delhi to Dehradun at the speed of 120 km/h and from Dehradun to Delhi at the speed of 130 km/h. What is the average speed during the whole journey?
questions.explanation: For equal distances the average speed is 2 × 120 × 130/(120 + 130) = 31200/250 = 124.8 km/h.

questions.text: The marked price of a bedsheet is 14 percent more than its cost price. If a discount of 14 percent is given on the marked price. What is the gain or loss percent?
questions.explanation: The selling price is 1.14 × 0.86 = 0.9804 of the cost price, a loss of 1.96%. (A rise and then a fall of the same x% always leave a loss of x²/100 = 14²/100 = 1.96%.)

questions.text: Find the mean proportional between 18 and 32.
questions.explanation: The mean proportional of a and b is √(ab) = √(18 × 32) = √576 = 24.

questions.text: An almirah was brought for Rs.14,360 and Rs.240 was spent on its transportation. At what price should it be sold, to gain 15%?
questions.explanation: The cost with transport is 14,360 + 240 = ₹14,600, and a 15% gain needs 1.15 × 14,600 = ₹16,790.

questions.text: Ravish travelled the first 20 km of an entire distance at a speed of 12 km/h; the next 25 km at a speed of 10 km/h and the remaining distance at a speed of 15 km/h. If his overall average speed was 13.5 km/h, what was the distance that Ravish travelled at a speed of 15 km/h?
questions.explanation: Let the last part be x km. The time is 20/12 + 25/10 + x/15 = 25/6 + x/15 hours, so 45 + x = 13.5 × (25/6 + x/15) = 56.25 + 0.9x. Then 0.1x = 11.25 and x = 112.5 km.

questions.text: A car covers a distance of 1080 km in 240 minutes. What is the speed of the car in m/sec?
questions.explanation: 240 minutes is 4 hours, so the speed is 1080/4 = 270 km/h = 270 × 5/18 = 75 m/sec.

questions.text: Om decided to order 12 percent more millet flour for his bakery than last year. If he ordered 240 kg last year, then how much quantity of millet flour should he order this year?
questions.explanation: 12% more than 240 kg is 240 × 1.12 = 268.8 kg.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hang in there
questions.explanation: 'Hang in there' is said to encourage someone to keep going through a hard time: don't give up.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Transient
questions.explanation: 'Transient' means lasting only a short time; its opposite is 'permanent'. 'Temporary' and 'perishable' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Confident
questions.explanation: 'Confident' means sure of oneself and unafraid; of the options only 'cowardly', lacking courage, runs against it. 'Undaunted' and 'bold' are close to it in meaning, and 'carefree' is unrelated.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To put a spoke in one’s wheel
options: To thwart someone in execution of one’s design
To leave someone without any provision
questions.explanation: To 'put a spoke in someone's wheel' is to hinder their plans, to thwart them.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Necesity' is misspelt: the word is 'necessity', with one 'c' and a double 's'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence. One should enjoy “liberty” with duties in mind.
questions.explanation: 'Liberty' means freedom, the right to act and think as one chooses.

questions.text: Select the correct pair of words for the blanks in the given sentence. Computer has a ________ memory and my father prefers _________ to digital payments.
questions.explanation: A 'cache' is a small, fast store of memory in a computer, and 'cash' is money in notes and coins, the alternative to digital payments. The two words sound alike.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Significant
questions.explanation: 'Significant' means important; its opposite is 'paltry', small and worthless. 'Prominent' and 'distinct' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Aghast
questions.explanation: 'Aghast' means filled with horror or shock: 'horrified'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We ____________ the mathematical issue with zest and vigour.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'solved', the usual verb for a mathematical problem or issue. 'Settled' and 'cleared up' can also be said of an issue, but they suit a dispute or a confusion rather than a mathematical question, and 'remedied' suits a fault.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. The farmer “has been work” since 8 a.m. today and he’s not completed the work yet.
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and is still going on ('since 8 a.m.', 'not completed the work yet') takes the present perfect continuous: 'has been working'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The garbage _____ empties into a big bin.
questions.explanation: A 'chute' is a sloping channel down which things such as rubbish slide; it sounds like 'shoot'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. I am give / a speech on / emerging economic dynamics / in the program.
questions.explanation: After the auxiliary 'am' the verb takes the -ing form: 'I am giving a speech on emerging economic dynamics in the program.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. I went there to say goodbye to him but “he refuse to meet me.”
options: he has refused to meet me
questions.explanation: The sentence is in the past ('I went'), so the second clause needs the simple past too: 'he refused to meet me'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A lot of research has (1)______ that reptiles and amphibians are cold-blooded (2)______. By the term cold-blooded animals, we (3)_______ that they cannot control their body temperature like we can. A reptile’s skin is dry and scaly, (4)______ the skin of an amphibian is wet and smooth. Most reptiles spend much of their time (5)______ on land. Most amphibians live in or around water.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Has' needs a past participle, and research 'proves' a fact: 'A lot of research has proved that ...'. 'Tell' is not a participle, and 'talked' and 'spread' do not fit with 'that' here.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A lot of research has (1)______ that reptiles and amphibians are cold-blooded (2)______. By the term cold-blooded animals, we (3)_______ that they cannot control their body temperature like we can. A reptile’s skin is dry and scaly, (4)______ the skin of an amphibian is wet and smooth. Most reptiles spend much of their time (5)______ on land. Most amphibians live in or around water.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Reptiles and amphibians are 'animals', and the next sentence takes up the same phrase ('By the term cold-blooded animals'); 'organisms' is too general here, and they are neither birds nor plants.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A lot of research has (1)______ that reptiles and amphibians are cold-blooded (2)______. By the term cold-blooded animals, we (3)_______ that they cannot control their body temperature like we can. A reptile’s skin is dry and scaly, (4)______ the skin of an amphibian is wet and smooth. Most reptiles spend much of their time (5)______ on land. Most amphibians live in or around water.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'By the term ..., we mean that ...' is the usual way of explaining what a term means.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A lot of research has (1)______ that reptiles and amphibians are cold-blooded (2)______. By the term cold-blooded animals, we (3)_______ that they cannot control their body temperature like we can. A reptile’s skin is dry and scaly, (4)______ the skin of an amphibian is wet and smooth. Most reptiles spend much of their time (5)______ on land. Most amphibians live in or around water.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Whereas' joins two clauses that contrast: dry, scaly skin against wet, smooth skin. 'Contrary' and 'conversely' cannot join two clauses, and 'similarly' gives the wrong sense.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A lot of research has (1)______ that reptiles and amphibians are cold-blooded (2)______. By the term cold-blooded animals, we (3)_______ that they cannot control their body temperature like we can. A reptile’s skin is dry and scaly, (4)______ the skin of an amphibian is wet and smooth. Most reptiles spend much of their time (5)______ on land. Most amphibians live in or around water.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Crawling', moving close to the ground, is the usual word for how reptiles move on land (the name comes from the Latin for 'creep'); 'walking' is not the usual word for it, 'jumping' does not suit them, and 'dragging' needs an object.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘MANTLE’ is written as ‘JZKGIV’ and ‘TINKER’ is written as ‘QRKPBI’. How will ‘DERIVE’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Letters in the odd places move 3 back and those in the even places become their opposite letters (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on): MANTLE → J Z K G I V and TINKER → Q R K P B I. So DERIVE → A V O R S V: AVORSV.

questions.text: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Shirley is sitting second to the right of Leena. Diana is sitting fifth to the right of Shirley. Violet is sitting third to the right of Diana. Abdul is sitting second to the left of Diana. Vikram is sitting third to the left of Leena. Who is sitting between Vikram and Diana?
questions.explanation: Counting seats to the right from Leena (0): Shirley is 2, Diana 2 + 5 = 7, that is 1, Violet 1 + 3 = 4, Abdul 1 − 2 = −1, that is 5, and Vikram 0 − 3 = −3, that is 3. So the order to the right is Leena, Diana, Shirley, Vikram, Violet, Abdul, and Shirley sits between Vikram and Diana.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 naughty 2 natural 3 national 4 nagging 5 napping
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: nagging (4), napping (5), national (3), natural (2), naughty (1). 'Nag' comes before 'nap', 'nap' before 'nat', 'nati' before 'natu', and 'nat' before 'nau'.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? DKLX, EMOU, FORR, ?, HSXL
questions.explanation: The first letters move +1 (D, E, F, G, H), the second +2 (K, M, O, Q, S), the third +3 (L, O, R, U, X) and the fourth −3 (X, U, R, O, L): GQUO.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. YCLE, DWQJ, IQVO, ?, SEFY
questions.explanation: The first, third and fourth letters move 5 forward and the second 6 back, wrapping round the alphabet: Y, D, I, N, S; C, W, Q, K, E; L, Q, V, A, F; E, J, O, T, Y. The missing cluster is NKAT.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Painter : Brush :: Gardener : ?
questions.explanation: A painter works with a brush, and a gardener with a rake, the long-handled tool for gathering leaves and levelling soil.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and fourth term is related to the third term. SECURITY : 19ECURIT25 :: ENHANCED : 5NHANCE4 :: USAGE : ?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters are replaced by their places in the alphabet and the letters between are kept: S ECURIT Y → 19 ECURIT 25 and E NHANCE D → 5 NHANCE 4. So U SAG E → 21 SAG 5: 21SAG5.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 30 * 2 * 20 * 13 * 67
questions.explanation: 30 × 2 + 20 − 13 = 60 + 20 − 13 = 67. None of the other combinations balances the equation.

questions.text: In a code language, 'dark colors' is coded as 'yu nu', 'days are bright' is coded as 'wu tu ku', 'nights are dark' is coded as 'ku nu pu', 'paint bright' is coded as 'wu ru'. What is the code for the word 'paint'?
questions.explanation: 'Bright' is in the second and fourth messages, and 'wu' is the only code common to both, so 'bright' is 'wu' and 'paint' is 'ru'.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 54 × 6 – 36 ÷ 12 + 27 = 24

Seven people, A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a straight row, facing north. A sits second from the left. Only two people sit between A and C. Only 3 people sit between D and F and D is an immediate neighbour of A. B is an immediate neighbour of D and E is not an immediate neighbour of C. Who sits to the immediate right of C?
questions.explanation: Numbering the seats 1 to 7 from the left: A is 2 and C is 5. D is next to A; at 1 it would put F at 5, C's seat, so D is 3 and F is 7. B, next to D, is 4. E may not sit next to C, so E is 1 and G is 6: G is on C's immediate right.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 589, 588, 583, ?, 433, -192
questions.explanation: The differences are −1, −5, −25, −125, −625, the powers of 5: 583 − 25 = 558, and 558 − 125 = 433.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘A + B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’, ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the father of B’, ‘A x B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’ and ‘A & B’ means ‘A is the son of B’. How is T related to G if T + Q – R x H & G?
questions.explanation: T is Q's sister, and Q is the father of R, whose brother H is the son of G. So H's parents are Q and G, which makes G Q's wife, and T is G's husband's sister.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the sixth number is related to the fifth number. 7 : 1000 :: 4 : ? :: 12 : 3375
questions.explanation: Each second number is the cube of 3 more than the first: (7 + 3)³ = 1000 and (12 + 3)³ = 3375. So (4 + 3)³ = 343.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 0, 6, 24, 60, 120, ?
questions.explanation: The terms are n³ − n for n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5: 0, 6, 24, 60, 120. The next is 6³ − 6 = 210.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All beds are tables. All cots are tables. All tables are taps. Conclusions: I. All cots are taps. II. Some taps are beds. III. Some taps are cots.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: Beds and cots both lie within tables, and tables within taps. So all cots are taps (I), and as all beds and all cots are taps, some taps are beds (II) and some taps are cots (III).

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The tribal group called 'Santhals' rose in revolt in _______.
questions.explanation: The Santhal rebellion (Santhal Hul) broke out in 1855 under the brothers Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu, against zamindars, moneylenders and British rule in the Rajmahal hills.

questions.text: Which of the following industries is reserved for the manufacture of items exclusively in the public sector?
questions.explanation: Since the 1991 industrial policy and later changes, only atomic energy and railway operations remain reserved for the public sector.

questions.text: India has inland navigation waterways of ________ km in length.
questions.explanation: India has about 14,500 km of inland waterways (rivers, canals, backwaters and creeks), only part of which mechanised vessels can use.

questions.text: Which Constitutional Amendment introduced the compulsory education to children between the age group of 6 to 14?
questions.explanation: The 86th Amendment (2002) inserted Article 21A, which makes free and compulsory education a fundamental right of children aged 6 to 14.

questions.text: The constellation 'Ursa Major' is also known as _________.
questions.explanation: Ursa Major is the Great Bear; seven of its brightest stars form the Big Dipper, or Saptarishi. The Hunter is Orion, the Queen Cassiopeia and the Chained Maiden Andromeda.

questions.text: The _______________ mandates the requirement of POSH policy, in order to prevent sexual harassment against women in the workplace and also to protect them .
options: “The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act,2019"
“The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition, and Redressal) Act, 2013”.
“The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Protection, Prohibition, and Redressal) Act, 2014”
questions.explanation: The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, the POSH Act, requires employers to set up an Internal Complaints Committee to hear such complaints.

questions.text: As on April 2021, how many states have a Legislative Council?
questions.explanation: In April 2021 six states had a Legislative Council: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh. Jammu and Kashmir's council was abolished in 2019, when the state became a union territory.

questions.text: Who sworn in as the Central Vigilance Commissioner (CVC) in August 2022?
questions.explanation: Suresh N Patel, who had been acting Central Vigilance Commissioner, was sworn in as CVC by President Droupadi Murmu on 3 August 2022.

questions.text: In India, Microfinance activities gained prominence in the early _______.
questions.explanation: Microfinance spread in India in the early 1990s, after NABARD's pilot Self-Help Group-Bank Linkage Programme of 1992 linked groups of poor borrowers, mostly women, to banks.

questions.text: Name the suicidal bags of the cell.
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are called the suicide bags of the cell: their digestive enzymes can break down the cell itself when it is damaged.

questions.text: The First Formula 1 Race in India was held in ______.
questions.explanation: India's first Formula 1 race, the Indian Grand Prix, was held at the Buddh International Circuit in Greater Noida on 30 October 2011.

questions.text: Uttar Pradesh shares its international boundary with which country?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh's only international border is with Nepal, to its north.

questions.text: __________is considered as the backbone of development in general.
questions.explanation: Manufacturing turns raw materials into goods of higher value, helps modernise agriculture, creates jobs outside farming and earns foreign exchange through exports, which is why it is called the backbone of development in general.

questions.text: During the Chaliha Sahib festival, Sindhis observe a ________-day fast to show their devotion to Lord Jhulelal.
questions.explanation: Chaliha (Chaliho) Sahib is a 40-day observance of Sindhi Hindus in honour of Jhulelal, held each year in July and August; 'chaliha' means forty.

questions.text: Which team has won the highest number of Ranji Trophy titles?
questions.explanation: Mumbai (earlier Bombay) had won the Ranji Trophy 41 times when the exam was held (January 2023), far more than any other team.

questions.text: Who among the following Congress leaders of India retired from Rajya Sabha in March 2022?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives P Chidambaram, though he did not leave the House in March 2022: on 31 March 2022 the Rajya Sabha bade farewell to 72 members retiring between March and July 2022, among them Chidambaram, whose Maharashtra term was due to end in July (he was elected again, from Tamil Nadu, in June). Of the others, Rahul Gandhi sat in the Lok Sabha, Supriya Sule was an NCP member of the Lok Sabha, and K Kamaraj died in 1975.

questions.text: The Muttaraiyar held power in the Kaveri delta. They were subordinate to the Pallava kings of _______.
questions.explanation: The Muttaraiyar, chiefs of the Kaveri delta, were subordinates of the Pallavas, whose capital was Kanchipuram. Vijayalaya of the Chola family took the delta from them in the middle of the ninth century.

questions.text: Identify the acid that convert zinc into zinc sulphate.
questions.explanation: Zinc reacts with dilute sulphuric acid to give zinc sulphate and hydrogen: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂.

questions.text: Gunakanta Dutta Borbyan was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in which dance form?
questions.explanation: Gunakanta Dutta Borbayan, a khol player and teacher trained at the Notun Kamalabari Satra of Majuli, received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Sattriya, the classical dance of Assam's satras.

questions.text: Which of the following dances is performed in Goa?
questions.explanation: Fugdi is a folk dance of Goa and the Konkan coast, performed by women in a circle. Jhoomar is from Punjab, Cheraw (the bamboo dance) from Mizoram and Karma from the tribal belt of Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh.

questions.text: A shopkeeper listed the marked price of a table at Rs.2500. If he sold it at 20% discount and 10% additional discount, then what is the selling price of the table?
The average cost of an apple, an orange and a mango is Rs.36. The average cost of an apple and an orange is Rs.28 and that of an orange and a mango is Rs.32. The cost of an orange (in Rs.) is:
questions.explanation: Apple + orange + mango = 3 × 36 = 108, apple + orange = 2 × 28 = 56 and orange + mango = 2 × 32 = 64. The last two together count the orange twice: 56 + 64 − 108 = 12.

questions.text: Find the mean proportional between 4 and 900.
questions.explanation: The mean proportional of a and b is √(ab) = √(4 × 900) = √3600 = 60.

questions.text: Find the third proportional to 8 and 12
questions.explanation: The third proportional x satisfies 8 : 12 = 12 : x, so x = 12²/8 = 144/8 = 18.

questions.text: The average weight of a truck and four cars is 48 kg, which is reduced by 1 kg if the weight of the truck is excluded. What is the weight of the truck?
questions.explanation: The truck and four cars weigh 5 × 48 = 240 kg and the four cars alone 4 × 47 = 188 kg, so the truck weighs 240 − 188 = 52 kg.

questions.text: Yash can do a piece of work in 49 days and Naman can do the same work in 35 days. Saurav can do the same work in 7 days. Find the total days required to complete the same work if they work on alternate days such that Yash works on the first day, Naman works on the second day, Saurav work on the third day and then again Yash works on the fourth day and so on.
questions.explanation: Take the work as 245 units (the LCM of 49, 35 and 7): Yash does 5 a day, Naman 7 and Saurav 35, so each 3-day round does 47. Five rounds (15 days) do 235, leaving 10; Yash does 5 on day 16 and Naman the last 5 in 5/7 of a day: 16 + 5/7 = 117/7 days.

questions.text: Rs.11,500 is borrowed at compound interest at the rate of 5% per annum, compounding annually. What will be the amount to be paid after 2 years?
A shopkeeper sells his old stock at 25 percent loss on cost price, but uses 30 percent less weight. What is his percentage profit or loss (consider up to two decimals)?
questions.explanation: Take the cost of the full weight as 100. He charges 75 (25% below cost) but gives only 70% of the weight, which costs him 70: profit = 5/70 × 100 = 7.14%.

questions.text: A truck's value is reduced by 17 percent and is now worth Rs.33,32,948. What was its original price?
questions.explanation: 83% of the original price is ₹33,32,948, so the price was ₹33,32,948 ÷ 0.83 = ₹40,15,600.

questions.text: What is the number which, when increased by 20, is completely divisible by 18, 56 and 42?
questions.explanation: LCM(18, 56, 42) = 2³ × 3² × 7 = 504, so the least such number is 504 − 20 = 484.

questions.text: The greatest number which can divide 286, 1001 and 2420 is X. What is the value of X/2?
How many cubes of side 4 cm can be formed by melting a solid metallic cuboid of length 12 cm, breadth 8 cm and height 8 cm?
questions.explanation: The cuboid's volume is 12 × 8 × 8 = 768 cm³ and each cube's 4³ = 64 cm³: 768 ÷ 64 = 12 cubes.

questions.text: In a 4 km race, A, B and C, each running at uniform speed, secured first, second and third position, respectively. If A beats B by 1 km and B beats C by 1 km, then by how many metres does A beat C in the same race?
questions.explanation: When A finishes 4 km, B has run 3 km. C runs 3 km while B runs 4, so by then C has run 3 × 3/4 = 2.25 km: A beats C by 4 − 2.25 = 1.75 km = 1750 m.

questions.text: What is the value of 35m/s in term of km/h?
The population of a town was 2,50,000 three years ago. If it has increased by 3%, 4% and 6% in the last 3 years, find the present population of the town.
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Everything Priyanka did in her academic _________ ended in vain.
questions.explanation: 'Attempts', that is efforts, is the noun that fits: everything she tried in her studies came to nothing. 'Adamants' and 'attends' make no sense here, and 'attestations' are formal confirmations.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Lose your marbles
questions.explanation: To 'lose your marbles' is to go mad, or to lose your good sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Benefit
questions.explanation: A 'benefit' is an advantage or gain. 'Genesis' means origin, 'rapture' great joy, and 'injury' is nearer the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Dominate
questions.explanation: To 'dominate' is to control or have power over; its opposite is to 'surrender', to give up control. 'Rules', 'orders' and 'command' are close in meaning to 'dominate'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word to fill in the blank. Children were “amused” by the puppet show, but they were _________ with the Chairman’s speech.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'amused' (entertained) is 'bored', which the contrast with 'but' calls for. 'Gratified' and 'charmed' are close to 'amused'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. “The students ran quick” to get on the train.
questions.explanation: 'Ran' is a verb, so it takes the adverb 'quickly', not the adjective 'quick': 'The students ran quickly'. The other two options make the verb disagree with its subject or change the tense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. Sivasubramanian Iyer was not “perturbed”, nor did he get angry with his wife, but instead, served me with his own hands and sat down beside me to eat his meal.
questions.explanation: 'Perturbed' means troubled or upset: 'disturbed'. 'Composed' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. The weathermen felt that it was “more hotter” today.
questions.explanation: 'Hotter' is already the comparative of 'hot', so adding 'more' makes a double comparative: 'it was hotter today'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. This bodyguard was like a “firewall” for the leader.
questions.explanation: A 'firewall' here is a protective barrier, and so is a 'bulwark', a defensive wall or a person who shields another. A 'vanguard' leads the way rather than shields.
