questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The software detected an anomaly cause by the virus.
questions.explanation: The anomaly was caused by the virus, so the past participle is needed: 'an anomaly caused by the virus'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'auspicious', ending in '-ious'.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them contains a spelling error. Select the option that rectifies the error. Macaroni penguins have a distenctive yellow feather crest on their forehead.
questions.explanation: 'Distenctive' is misspelt: the word is 'distinctive'. The other options are themselves misspellings of 'forehead', 'penguins' and 'crest'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Bite off more than you can chew
options: Take on a task that you cannot finish
questions.explanation: To 'bite off more than you can chew' is to take on a bigger task than you can manage.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. As a student of medicine, you have to learn the “terminologies” by heart.
questions.explanation: 'Terminology' is the set of special words and expressions used in a subject such as medicine: 'special expressions'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Exhaust
questions.explanation: To 'exhaust' is to use up or drain completely; to 'restore' is to bring back or replenish. 'Empty' and 'burn' are close to 'exhaust'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. The Sentinelese, the world's most remote tribe have (1)_______ the interest of millions of people. They (2)_____ on North Sentinel, a little island covered with forests that is about the size of Manhattan. They continue to reject any interaction with outsiders and assault anyone who (3)_______. The Sentinelese hunt, collect, and fish in the forest (4)________ the coast. They build boats, unlike the nearby Jarawa tribe, who only makes (5)______ thin outrigger canoes that are ‘too narrow to fit two feet in’. Since they are guided and propelled using a pole similar to a punt, these can only be used in shallow waters.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank 1.
questions.explanation: To 'spark' interest is to set it off: the remote tribe has sparked the interest of millions. 'Enrolled' and 'affected' do not fit, and 'provoke' is used mostly of a strong or unwelcome reaction.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. The Sentinelese, the world's most remote tribe have (1)_______ the interest of millions of people. They (2)_____ on North Sentinel, a little island covered with forests that is about the size of Manhattan. They continue to reject any interaction with outsiders and assault anyone who (3)_______. The Sentinelese hunt, collect, and fish in the forest (4)________ the coast. They build boats, unlike the nearby Jarawa tribe, who only makes (5)______ thin outrigger canoes that are ‘too narrow to fit two feet in’. Since they are guided and propelled using a pole similar to a punt, these can only be used in shallow waters.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank 2.
questions.explanation: The Sentinelese 'reside', that is live, on North Sentinel, the island the sentence goes on to describe.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. The Sentinelese, the world's most remote tribe have (1)_______ the interest of millions of people. They (2)_____ on North Sentinel, a little island covered with forests that is about the size of Manhattan. They continue to reject any interaction with outsiders and assault anyone who (3)_______. The Sentinelese hunt, collect, and fish in the forest (4)________ the coast. They build boats, unlike the nearby Jarawa tribe, who only makes (5)______ thin outrigger canoes that are ‘too narrow to fit two feet in’. Since they are guided and propelled using a pole similar to a punt, these can only be used in shallow waters.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank 3.
questions.explanation: They attack anyone who 'approaches', that is comes near them; the other verbs need an object or do not fit the sense.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. The Sentinelese, the world's most remote tribe have (1)_______ the interest of millions of people. They (2)_____ on North Sentinel, a little island covered with forests that is about the size of Manhattan. They continue to reject any interaction with outsiders and assault anyone who (3)_______. The Sentinelese hunt, collect, and fish in the forest (4)________ the coast. They build boats, unlike the nearby Jarawa tribe, who only makes (5)______ thin outrigger canoes that are ‘too narrow to fit two feet in’. Since they are guided and propelled using a pole similar to a punt, these can only be used in shallow waters.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank 4.
questions.explanation: They hunt and fish in the forest 'along' the coast, that is the forest that runs beside it.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. The Sentinelese, the world's most remote tribe have (1)_______ the interest of millions of people. They (2)_____ on North Sentinel, a little island covered with forests that is about the size of Manhattan. They continue to reject any interaction with outsiders and assault anyone who (3)_______. The Sentinelese hunt, collect, and fish in the forest (4)________ the coast. They build boats, unlike the nearby Jarawa tribe, who only makes (5)______ thin outrigger canoes that are ‘too narrow to fit two feet in’. Since they are guided and propelled using a pole similar to a punt, these can only be used in shallow waters.

Select the most appropriate answer for blank 5.
questions.explanation: Canoes 'too narrow to fit two feet in' are 'extremely' thin. 'Exclusively' would repeat 'only', and 'abundantly' and 'knowingly' do not describe thinness.

questions.text: Eight friends P, Q, R, S, T, U, V and W are sitting in two rows facing each other. Each row has four persons. Q and R are sitting in front of each other. R is the immediate neighbour of S and T. W is sitting to the immediate left of T. W and U are diagonally opposite. V and Q are not next to each other. Who is in front of T?
questions.explanation: R sits between S and T, with W to T's immediate left, so one row runs W, T, R, S. In the other row Q faces R and U faces S (diagonally opposite W); V, who is not beside Q, faces W, leaving P facing T.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. KSW : NUX :: AGP : DIQ :: EOV : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +3, +2 and +1: K S W → N U X and A G P → D I Q. So E O V → H Q W: HQW.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FAVOUR’ is written as ‘RUOVAF’ and ‘REVEAL’ is written as ‘LAEVER’. How will ‘MIRACLE’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is written backwards: FAVOUR → RUOVAF and REVEAL → LAEVER. So MIRACLE → ELCARIM.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? SEJW, QGMT, OIPQ, ? , KMVK
questions.explanation: The first letters fall by 2 (S, Q, O, M, K), the second rise by 2 (E, G, I, K, M), the third rise by 3 (J, M, P, S, V) and the fourth fall by 3 (W, T, Q, N, K): MKSN.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘HUSBAND’ is written as ‘DNABSUH’ and ‘CLEARLY’ is written as ‘YLRAELC’. How will ‘HARBOUR’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is written backwards: HUSBAND → DNABSUH and CLEARLY → YLRAELC. So HARBOUR → RUOBRAH.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 24 + 36 - 81 × 9 ÷ 2 = 42
Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Jacket 2 Japanese 3 Jabbed 4 Jackpot 5 Janitor
questions.explanation: All five begin with 'Ja': Jabbed (b), then Jacket and Jackpot (c, with 'Jacke' before 'Jackp'), Janitor (n) and Japanese (p): 3, 1, 4, 5, 2.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. SURGERY : TVSHFSZ :: SILENCE : TJMFODF :: SOCIETY : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: SURGERY → TVSHFSZ and SILENCE → TJMFODF. So SOCIETY → TPDJFUZ.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 1483, 2369, ?, 4141, 5027, 5913
Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? RHWC, QKVF, ? , OQTL, NTSO
questions.explanation: The first letters fall by 1 (R, Q, P, O, N), the second rise by 3 (H, K, N, Q, T), the third fall by 1 (W, V, U, T, S) and the fourth rise by 3 (C, F, I, L, O): PNUI.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some trees are fish. All fishes are goats. No goat is a flower. Conclusions: I. Some trees are goats. II. Some fishes are not flowers. III. Some flowers are not goats.
questions.explanation: The trees that are fish are goats, so some trees are goats (I). Every fish is a goat and no goat is a flower, so no fish is a flower and some fishes are not flowers (II); and no flower is a goat, so some flowers are not goats (III).

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the % signs and to balance the given equation. 42 % 7 % 5% 10 % 3
questions.explanation: 42 ÷ 7 × 5 = 10 × 3, as both sides equal 30.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 1, 2, 2, 4, 3, 6, 4, 8, ?
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 1, 2, 3, 4 in the odd places and 2, 4, 6, 8 in the even places, so the next term is 5.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (17, 136, 40); (11, 198, 90)
questions.explanation: The middle number is the first times one-fifth of the third: 17 × 40/5 = 17 × 8 = 136 and 11 × 90/5 = 11 × 18 = 198. Likewise 12 × 45/5 = 12 × 9 = 108.

questions.text: Startup India was launched under the ___________.
options: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
questions.explanation: Startup India, launched in January 2016, is run by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry's Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT, then called DIPP).

questions.text: It is used in making gunny bags, mats, ropes, yarn, carpets and other artefacts. Which crop is being spoken about here?
questions.explanation: Jute, the 'golden fibre', grown mainly in West Bengal, gives a long, coarse, strong fibre that is spun into the sacking of gunny bags.

questions.text: Who among the following has received Rajiv Gandhi Puraskar, Indira Priyadarshini Samman and Rotary International Award?
questions.explanation: The Kathak dancer Shovana Narayan received the Rajiv Gandhi Award for Excellence and a Rotary International Vocational Award in 1992, and the Indira Gandhi Priyadarshini Samman in 1996. N. Rajam is a violinist, Mahaboob Subhani a nadaswaram player and Zia Mohiuddin Dagar a rudra veena player.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT related with the primary sector of economy?
questions.explanation: Banking is a service, part of the tertiary sector. Forestry, dairy and fishing draw directly on natural resources, so they belong to the primary sector.

questions.text: The intervention of the government whether to expand demand or reduce it constitutes the __________ function.
questions.explanation: Government spending and taxes that expand demand in a slump or curb it when prices rise steady the economy: this is the budget's stabilisation function.

questions.text: Sattriya, is the classical dance form of which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Sattriya was created by the Vaishnava saint Srimanta Sankardeva in Assam and kept alive in its monasteries (sattras); the Sangeet Natak Akademi recognised it as a classical dance in 2000.

questions.text: What makes the imported goods more expensive?
questions.explanation: A tariff is a tax on imports: it raises the price buyers pay for imported goods, which is why governments use it as a trade barrier.

questions.text: Which Shiv Sena leader from India was elected as Member of Rajya Sabha from Maharashtra in July 2022?
questions.explanation: Sanjay Raut of the Shiv Sena won one of Maharashtra's six Rajya Sabha seats in the vote of 10 June 2022, and his fourth term began on 5 July 2022. Vinayak Raut was a Shiv Sena member of the Lok Sabha.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a Cricketer?
questions.explanation: Saina Nehwal is a badminton player, an Olympic bronze medallist in 2012. Sachin Tendulkar, Javagal Srinath and Rahul Dravid played cricket for India.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which region did the Swadeshi Movement have the strongest impact on people?
questions.explanation: The Swadeshi Movement began in 1905 against Lord Curzon's partition of Bengal and was strongest there, with the boycott of British goods and the burning of foreign cloth.

questions.text: In a badminton singles game, if both the players are on 29 points then at what point will one of them win the game?
questions.explanation: A badminton game goes to 21 points, but from 20-all a side must lead by two, up to a limit: at 29-all the side that wins the 30th point wins the game.

questions.text: The term of the Lok Sabha, unless dissolved is _____ from the date appointed for its first meeting.
questions.explanation: Under Article 83(2) the Lok Sabha runs for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless dissolved sooner; during an emergency Parliament may extend it by up to a year at a time.

questions.text: What is the white precipitate formed in the reaction of sodium sulphate and barium chloride?
questions.explanation: Na₂SO₄ + BaCl₂ → BaSO₄ + 2NaCl: insoluble barium sulphate falls out as the white precipitate, while sodium chloride stays in solution.

questions.text: Ravikirti composed prashasti of which of following Chalukya rulers?
questions.explanation: Ravikirti, court poet of the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II, composed the Aihole inscription (634-35 CE) in his praise.

questions.text: Loo is a characteristic feature of which season?
questions.explanation: The loo is the hot, dry, dusty wind that blows by day across the northern plains of India in May and June, at the height of summer.

questions.text: How many balanced meals of average size each day should adolescents have?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives three: the usual advice for teenagers is three balanced main meals a day (breakfast, lunch and dinner), with healthy snacks in between.

questions.text: As per the Census 2011, what was the literacy rate in India?
questions.explanation: Census 2011's provisional totals put India's literacy rate (people aged seven and above) at 74.04%, the figure usually quoted: 82.14% for men and 65.46% for women. The final tables gave about 73%, which no other option is near.

questions.text: Buddha Purnima, celebrated by the devotees of Gautam Buddha, is known as Saga Dawa in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Sikkim celebrates Buddha Purnima as Saga Dawa, on the full moon of the fourth month of the Tibetan calendar, with prayers and processions at its monasteries.

questions.text: Who was appointed as the first female Director General of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) in August 2022?
questions.explanation: Nallathamby Kalaiselvi, an electrochemist who had headed CSIR-CECRI at Karaikudi, was appointed the first woman Director General of CSIR in August 2022.

questions.text: The product of 2 numbers is 6750 and their LCM is 450. If difference between the numbers is equal to their HCF, then find the smaller number.
questions.explanation: HCF = product ÷ LCM = 6750 ÷ 450 = 15. Writing the numbers as 15a and 15b with a and b coprime, ab = 6750/225 = 30 and a − b = 1, so a = 6 and b = 5: the numbers are 90 and 75.

questions.text: X gets on a lift at the ground floor which goes up at speed of 30 floors per minute whereas Y gets on another lift at the same time on the 50th floor which goes down at the speed of 45 floors per minute. At which floor will their paths cross?(lifts are moving without stopping at any floor)
questions.explanation: The lifts close in on each other at 30 + 45 = 75 floors a minute, so they meet after 50/75 = 2/3 minute, when X has gone up 30 × 2/3 = 20 floors: the 20th floor.

questions.text: Two athletes A and B are running on a circular track of length 1800 m from the same starting point at the same starting time,at the speeds of 9 m/s and 6 m/s, respectively. At how many distinct points will they meet while running in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Their speeds are in the ratio 9 : 6 = 3 : 2. Running in opposite directions, they meet at 3 + 2 = 5 distinct points on the track.

questions.text: Mehul buys a car for Rs. 560000. He renovates it and eventually sells it for Rs. 640000. The percent increase in the price of the car is:
If the length of the longest diagonal of a cube is 6√3 cm, then find the volume of the cube.
questions.explanation: The longest diagonal of a cube of side a is a√3, so a = 6 cm and the volume is 6³ = 216 cm³.

questions.text: The total amount after 3 quarters would be Rs.13,310. If the rate of interest is 40% per annum and compounding is performed quarterly, determine the present value (in Rs.).
questions.explanation: 40% a year is 10% a quarter, so P × 1.1³ = 13,310, that is 1.331P = 13,310 and P = ₹10,000.

questions.text: Rs.12,600 is divided among 15 labourers. There are 7 men, 3 women and 5 boys. If each woman receives three times as much as each boy, and each man receives seven times as much as each boy, the share of each woman is ________.
questions.explanation: If each boy gets x, each woman gets 3x and each man 7x: 7 × 7x + 3 × 3x + 5 × x = 63x = ₹12,600, so x = ₹200 and each woman gets ₹600.

questions.text: Find the compound interest on a sum of ₹50,000 at the rate of 6% per annum to be compounded half yearly at the end of 2 years. (Approximate to the nearest integer.)
questions.explanation: 6% a year compounded half-yearly is 3% for each of 4 half-years: 50,000 × 1.03⁴ = 50,000 × 1.12550881 = ₹56,275.44, so the interest is about ₹6,275.

questions.text: The marked price of a fan is 25% more than its cost price. If a discount of 12% is given on the marked price, then the gain per cent is:
questions.explanation: On a cost of 100 the marked price is 125, and 12% off leaves 125 × 0.88 = 110: a gain of 10%.

questions.text: If 3:5 = x:75 , then what is the value of x?

Aarav and Durga together can do a piece of work in 33 days. They worked together for 15 days and then Aarav left the work and Durga alone finished the remaining work in 30 days. Find the number of days in which Aarav alone can do the total work.
questions.explanation: In 15 days the pair does 15/33 = 5/11 of the work, so Durga does the other 6/11 in 30 days and would take 55 days alone. Aarav's daily share is 1/33 − 1/55 = 2/165, so he alone takes 165/2 days.

questions.text: If a person buys 15 pencils for ₹12, and sells 12 pencils for ₹15, find the gain or loss percentage.
questions.explanation: Each pencil costs 12/15 = ₹0.80 and sells for 15/12 = ₹1.25, a gain of 0.45/0.80 × 100 = 56.25%.

questions.text: There is 16 percent discount on a dozen pairs of trousers marked at Rs. 5000. How many pair of trousers can be bought with Rs. 2100?
questions.explanation: A dozen pairs cost 5,000 × 0.84 = ₹4,200, or ₹350 a pair, so ₹2,100 buys 2,100/350 = 6 pairs.

questions.text: A train is running at a speed of 129 km/h on a straight railway track, and a small car on a parallel road is running at a speed of 60 km/h. How long (in seconds, rounded off to the nearest integer) will the train take to cross the car completely if the train is 943 m long and they are running in the same direction? Ignore the length of the car as compared to the length of the train.
questions.explanation: The train gains on the car at 129 − 60 = 69 km/h = 69 × 5/18 m/s, so it passes the car in 943 × 18/(69 × 5) = 16974/345 ≈ 49.2, about 49 seconds.

questions.text: Which of the given pairs form a co-prime numbers pair?
questions.explanation: Co-prime numbers have no common factor but 1: 11 is prime and does not divide 21. The other pairs share the factors 21, 9 and 3.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'imaginary'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I still enjoyed the week “despite of the weather”.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' is a preposition and takes no 'of' ('in spite of' does): 'despite the weather'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. An axe to grind
questions.explanation: To have 'an axe to grind' is to have a private, often selfish, reason for doing or saying something.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks and make the sentence meaningful. My ______ gives me fresh coffee every _______.
questions.explanation: A 'maid' is a woman servant ('made' is the past of 'make'), and the coffee comes every 'morning' ('mourning' is grief over a death).

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Exciting
questions.explanation: 'Electrifying' means thrilling, intensely exciting. 'Dreary' is nearly the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Eager
questions.explanation: 'Eager' means keenly wanting something; 'indifferent' means having no interest or concern.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Invincible
questions.explanation: 'Invincible' means impossible to defeat; 'vulnerable' means open to attack or harm.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. The fire fighters were able “to put out” the fire in the industrial unit.
questions.explanation: To 'put out' a fire is to extinguish it, so the sentence is correct as it stands; 'put off' means postpone.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Differences among the various groups do not ______ well for the future of the peace treaty.
questions.explanation: To 'augur well' is to promise a good outcome. An 'auger' is a boring tool and an 'ogre' a monster of folk tales.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. The District Collector, Mr Kaushalendra Kumar, “are visiting the site” for inspection.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'The District Collector', one person; 'Mr Kaushalendra Kumar' only names him, so the verb is singular: 'is visiting the site'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Get the picture
questions.explanation: To 'get the picture' is to understand a situation.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Conquer
questions.explanation: To 'conquer' is to overcome or 'defeat'. 'Surrender' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in past perfect tense. A. The participants practised a lot for play. B. The participants had practised a lot for play. C. The participants had been practising a lot for play. D. The participants were practising a lot for play.
questions.explanation: The past perfect is 'had' + past participle: B, 'The participants had practised a lot for play.' A is the simple past, C the past perfect continuous and D the past continuous.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Freedom
questions.explanation: 'Bondage' is the state of being a slave or captive, the opposite of 'freedom'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Delhi National Zoological Park, which opened in 1959, is (1.) ________ next to the well-known Old Fort. One of the top zoos in the entire Asian continent, it stands out for its (2.) ________ to give the animals and the birds housed there a habitat that is as close to natural as possible. With a total area of 214 acres, it is perfect for picnics, (3.) ________ in the winter. The National Zoological Gardens in New Delhi are home to over 2,000 different animal and bird (4.) ________. These animals and birds, which originate from many areas such as Africa, America, Australia, etc., (5.) _______ a home at this zoo. The Mughal Kos Minar serves as the Delhi Zoo's entrance.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The zoo 'is located', that is situated, next to the Old Fort.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: It stands out for its 'efforts', its attempts, to give the animals a habitat close to the natural one. 'Effects' are results.

These animals and birds, which originate from many areas such as Africa, America, Australia, etc., (5.) _______ a home at this zoo. The Mughal Kos Minar serves as the Delhi Zoo's entrance.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The park suits picnics 'especially', that is above all, in the winter.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'These animals and birds' takes the plural present 'find': they 'find a home at this zoo'.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 5, 13, 29, ?, 125, 253
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before plus 3: 5 × 2 + 3 = 13, 13 × 2 + 3 = 29 and 29 × 2 + 3 = 61; then 61 × 2 + 3 = 125 and 125 × 2 + 3 = 253.

questions.text: Six girls D, K, M, P, R and S are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre. S is sitting third to the left of R. P is sitting to the immediate right of R and to the immediate left of D. M is sitting to the immediate left of R. K is sitting to the immediate right of S and to the immediate left of M. Who is sitting at the third position from the left of D?
questions.explanation: As all face the centre, each girl's left runs clockwise. Clockwise the order is D, P, R, M, K, S: P is to R's right and D's left, M to R's left, and K between M and S, so S is third to the left of R. Counting to the left of D: P, R, M.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. ?, HLEJ, JNGL, LPIN
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward from one cluster to the next: H → J → L, L → N → P, E → G → I and J → L → N. Going back 2 from HLEJ gives FJCH.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All gloves are bats. All stumps are bats. All bats are balls. Conclusions: I. All stumps are balls. II. Some balls are gloves. III. Some gloves are stumps.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: Gloves and stumps both lie inside bats, and bats inside balls, so all stumps are balls (I) and some balls are gloves (II). Gloves and stumps need not overlap, so III does not follow.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. RAIN : SZJM :: FALL : GZMK :: JUMP :?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, −1, +1, −1: RAIN → SZJM and FALL → GZMK. So JUMP → KTNO.

questions.text: Which of the mathematical signs should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct? 3 + 78 ÷ 13 - 9 × 117 = 126
questions.explanation: After interchanging + and ×: 3 × 78 ÷ 13 − 9 + 117 = 18 − 9 + 117 = 126.

questions.text: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 19, 21, ?, 134, 538, 2692

Seven people, A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a straight row, facing north. A sits third to the left of D. D sits to the extreme right. Only two people sit between A and F. B is an immediate neighbour of F. Only 1 person sits between C and D. G is not an immediate neighbour of A. How many people sit between F and C?
questions.explanation: Numbering the seats 1 to 7 from the left: D is at 7 and A at 4. F is three seats from A, so at 1, with B at 2, and C is at 5. G cannot sit next to A (3 or 5), so G is at 6 and E at 3: F B E A C G D. Between F and C sit B, E and A: 3.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Peanut 2 Peasant 3 Peacock 4 Peach 5 Pencil
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Peach (4), Peacock (3), Peanut (1), Peasant (2), Pencil (5). 'Peach' comes before 'Peacock' ('h' before 'o'), 'Peac' before 'Pean' and 'Peas', and 'Pea' before 'Pen'.

questions.text: ‘G + H’ means ‘G is the daughter of H’. ‘G – H’ means ‘G is the husband of H’. ‘G × H’ means ‘G is the brother of H’. If the relationships in a family are represented as: A + Q – R + K − Y, then how is K related to A?
questions.explanation: A is the daughter of Q, Q is the husband of R, R is the daughter of K, and K is the husband of Y, so male. R is A's mother and K is R's father: K is A's mother's father.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. ARCS : ENHN :: GHAT : KDFO :: MUSK : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +4, −4, +5, −5: ARCS → ENHN and GHAT → KDFO. So MUSK → QQXF.

questions.text: Which of the following letters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter series? T, R, P, N, L, J, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter is 2 places before the one before it: T, R, P, N, L, J, H.

questions.text: In a certain coded language, ‘distant face’ is coded as ‘human sad’, ‘face stairs’ is coded as ‘sad overpower’, ‘distant cup’ is coded as ‘human tea’, and ‘stairs cup’ is coded as ‘overpower tea’. What is the code word for ‘face’?
questions.explanation: 'Face' is in the first two phrases ('distant face' and 'face stairs'), whose only common code word is 'sad'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the sixth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the third term is related to the fourth term. 169 : 182 :: 225 : 240 :: ? : 306
questions.explanation: Each pair is a square and its root times the next number: 13² = 169 and 13 × 14 = 182; 15² = 225 and 15 × 16 = 240. As 306 = 17 × 18, the missing number is 17² = 289.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘TRUTH’ is coded as UQVSI and ‘FIRST’ is coded as GHSRU. How will ‘WHITE’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, −1, +1, −1, +1: TRUTH → UQVSI and FIRST → GHSRU. So WHITE → XGJSF.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 72 × 3 + 32 ÷ 4 - 16= 136
questions.explanation: After interchanging × and ÷: 72 ÷ 3 + 32 × 4 − 16 = 24 + 128 − 16 = 136.

questions.text: Sphalerite is the ore of which of the following metals?
questions.explanation: Sphalerite (zinc blende) is zinc sulphide, ZnS, the chief ore of zinc.

questions.text: ______ are present only in plant cells.
questions.explanation: Plastids, such as chloroplasts, occur in plant cells but not in animal cells; mitochondria, the nucleus and the Golgi apparatus are found in both.

questions.text: Nishagandhi Nritya Utsav is celebrated in which state of India?
questions.explanation: The Nishagandhi Dance Festival is held by Kerala Tourism in Thiruvananthapuram, at the Nishagandhi open-air auditorium.

questions.text: Which of the following oilseeds is grown both, as a rabi crop and a kharif crop?
questions.explanation: Castor seed is grown both as a rabi and as a kharif crop. Groundnut is a kharif crop, and linseed and mustard are rabi crops.

questions.text: On which of the following issues, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha don’t enjoy equal powers?
options: Impeaching the Judges of the Supreme Court and High Court
questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha cannot reject or amend a money bill: it can only make recommendations within 14 days, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject (Article 109). On constitutional amendments and on the impeachment of the President or the removal of judges the two Houses have equal powers.

questions.text: Which hills in Meghalaya receive the maximum rainfall?
questions.explanation: The Khasi Hills hold Mawsynram and Cherrapunji (Sohra), among the wettest places on Earth. The Aravalli, Nilgiri and Shivalik ranges are not in Meghalaya.

questions.text: Which country surrounds Tripura from west, north and south sides?
questions.explanation: Bangladesh borders Tripura on the north, west and south; only its eastern side adjoins the rest of India, Assam and Mizoram.

questions.text: Theme of eleventh five year plan in India, was ___________.
questions.explanation: The Eleventh Five Year Plan (2007-12) had the theme 'Towards Faster and More Inclusive Growth'.

questions.text: The 36th edition of the 2022 National Games of India was held in the state of _______________.
questions.explanation: Gujarat hosted the 36th National Games from 29 September to 12 October 2022.

questions.text: The total value of goods and services traded is considered to be the _________ of trade.
questions.explanation: Services cannot be measured in tonnes, so the volume of trade is taken as the total value of the goods and services traded. Composition is the mix of things traded and direction the countries traded with.

questions.text: Alarmel Valli a classical dancer who received the Padma Bhushan is known for ______________.
questions.explanation: Alarmel Valli is a Bharatanatyam dancer of the Pandanallur style; she received the Padma Shri in 1991 and the Padma Bhushan in 2004.

questions.text: Article 17 of the Constitution of India deals with ______.
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form. Equality before law is Article 14, abolition of titles Article 18 and the right to education Article 21A.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a part of revenue budget of the government?
questions.explanation: The revenue budget holds the revenue receipts (tax and non-tax) and the revenue expenditure, plan and non-plan. Capital expenditure, plan or non-plan, belongs to the capital budget.

questions.text: The Rig Veda is a collection of ________ hymns.
questions.explanation: The Rig Veda has 1,028 hymns (suktas), counting the 11 Valakhilya hymns, arranged in ten books (mandalas).

questions.text: Who among the following became the chief minister of Uttar Pradesh in March 2022?
questions.explanation: Yogi Adityanath was sworn in for a second term as Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh on 25 March 2022, after the BJP won the state election.

questions.text: Who has been elected as the lifetime president of Yuvajana Sramika Rythu Congress Party in July 2022?
questions.explanation: On 9 July 2022, the last day of its plenary, the YSR Congress Party elected its founder Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, then Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh, its president for life. (In September 2022, after the Election Commission questioned the post, the party said he had turned it down.)

questions.text: ______was an Act passed to make a provision for levy and collection of tax on intra-State supply of goods or services.
options: The Central Goods and Services Tax Act
The Central Gifts and Services Tax Act
The Central Goods and Secured Tax Act
The Cost of Goods and Services Tax Act
questions.explanation: The Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 provides for the Centre's levy and collection of tax on intra-State supplies of goods or services; the States levy SGST on the same supplies, and inter-State supplies come under the IGST Act.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Awadh was annexed by the British in ______.
questions.explanation: Lord Dalhousie annexed Awadh in February 1856, charging its ruler Wajid Ali Shah with misgovernment.

questions.text: Famous Indian Boxer Mary Kom is from which state?
questions.explanation: M. C. Mary Kom, a six-time world champion and bronze medallist at the 2012 Olympics, is from Manipur.

questions.text: Which among the following festivals is also known as "Festival of Festivals"?
questions.explanation: Nagaland's Hornbill Festival, held every December at Kisama near Kohima, brings together the festivals of the Naga tribes and is called the 'Festival of Festivals'. Chapchar Kut is a Mizo festival, Moatsu an Ao Naga one and Wangala a Garo festival of Meghalaya.

questions.text: In a store, an item with an MRP of Rs.28,500 is available at a discounted price of Rs.27,645. What is the percentage of discount given on that item?
The length of the rectangle is three times its breadth. If its length is decreased by 7 cm and breadth is increased by 7 cm, its area is increased by 21 cm². The length of the first rectangle is:
questions.explanation: With breadth b and length 3b: (3b − 7)(b + 7) − 3b² = 14b − 49 = 21, so b = 5 cm and the length is 15 cm.

questions.text: A sum of Rs.P was borrowed and paid back in two equal yearly instalments, each of Rs.35,280. If the rate of interest was 5% per annum and interest is compounding annually, then the value of P is ________.
questions.explanation: P is the present value of the two instalments: 35,280/1.05 + 35,280/1.05² = 33,600 + 32,000 = ₹65,600.

questions.text: A five-digit number 32054 is divisible by 11. If the digits are rearranged in increasing order, then the new number which is formed will be divisible by:
questions.explanation: In increasing order the digits give 02345, that is 2345. It ends in 5, so it is divisible by 5; it is odd, its digit sum 14 is not a multiple of 3, and (5 + 3) − (4 + 2) = 2 is not a multiple of 11.

questions.text: 30 men cut 50 trees in 10 h. If 10 men leave the job, how many trees will be cut in 15 h?
questions.explanation: The 50 trees take 30 × 10 = 300 man-hours. The 20 men who stay work 20 × 15 = 300 man-hours, so they cut 50 trees.

questions.text: Find the fourth proportional to the numbers 36, 48 and 90.
In a mixture of 60 litres, the ratio of milk and water is 2 : 3. What amount of water must be added to make the ratio of milk and water 1 : 2?
questions.explanation: The mixture has 24 litres of milk and 36 of water. For 1 : 2 the water must be 48 litres, so 12 litres are added.

questions.text: What is the average of the first six even numbers?
questions.explanation: The first six even numbers are 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12: 42/6 = 7.

questions.text: A person can row 88 km downstream in 11 h, and 72 km upstream in 12 h. What is the speed of the current?
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 88/11 = 8 km/h and upstream speed = 72/12 = 6 km/h, so the current is (8 − 6)/2 = 1 km/h.

questions.text: Suman buys 40 kg of wheat at Rs.12.50/kg and 30 kg of wheat at Rs.14/kg. At what rate per kg should he sell the mixture to gain 5% on the whole?

Kapil and Prakash together can do a piece of work in 45 days. Prakash and Pihu together can do it in 60 days. Kapil and Pihu together can do it in 60 days. In how many days will Kapil, Prakash and Pihu finish it together?
questions.explanation: Adding the three pairs: 2(Kapil + Prakash + Pihu) = 1/45 + 1/60 + 1/60 = (4 + 3 + 3)/180 = 1/18 of the work a day. Together they do 1/36 a day and finish in 36 days.

questions.text: The weight of a baby is increased from 3.2 kg to 6 kg in 3 months. The percent increase in weight of the baby is:

Munaf and Surya start simultaneously at the same point on a circular track and run along the track in the same direction. The point on the track at which they meet for the 31st time is the same as that at which they meet for the 43rd time. If the ratio of the speed of the faster boy to that of the slower one is n : 1, where ‘n’ is a natural number, which of the following is NOT a possible value of ‘n’?
questions.explanation: With speeds n : 1 in the same direction, the faster gains a lap at each meeting, and the meetings fall in turn at n − 1 equally spaced points. The 31st and 43rd meetings coincide only if n − 1 divides 43 − 31 = 12: it does for n = 5, 4 and 3 (4, 3 and 2), but not for n = 6 (5).

questions.text: In an election between two candidates, one who gets 64% of the votes polled is elected by a majority of 4,340 votes. What is the total number of votes polled? (considering that all the polled votes are valid)
questions.explanation: The winner's majority is 64% − 36% = 28% of the votes, so the total is 4,340/0.28 = 15,500.

questions.text: The average of 9 numbers is 15. If the average of the first five numbers is 13 and the average of the last five numbers is 17, then what is the fifth number?
questions.explanation: The first five numbers add up to 65 and the last five to 85. Together they count the fifth number twice, so it is 65 + 85 − 9 × 15 = 150 − 135 = 15.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Omnipresent
questions.explanation: 'Omnipresent' means present everywhere, which is close to 'universal'.

questions.text: Choose the sentence that is in simple past tense: A. I was giving some of the chocolates to my younger sister. B. I had been giving some of the chocolates to my younger sister. C. I had given some of the chocolates to my younger sister. D. I gave some of the chocolates to my younger sister.
questions.explanation: The simple past is the plain past form of the verb: 'I gave'. A is in the past continuous, B in the past perfect continuous and C in the past perfect.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. Dishonest people always________(deceive) others.
questions.explanation: To 'deceive' people is to make them believe something false, that is to 'cheat' them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I asked Rita “that how far her school was”.
options: then how far her school was
questions.explanation: A reported wh-question takes no 'that': the question word joins the clause, which keeps the order of a statement and the past 'was' after 'asked': 'I asked Rita how far her school was.'

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'passion', with a double 's'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Awkward
questions.explanation: 'Awkward' means clumsy, lacking skill or ease: 'unskillful'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word in the following sentence. He “neglected” his duties and was dismissed from his job.
questions.explanation: To 'neglect' duties is to fail to give them attention; the opposite is to have 'attended' (to) them. 'Ignored' and 'scorned' are close in meaning to 'neglected'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. My mother was________at my negligence and scolded me.
questions.explanation: A mother who scolds over negligence is angry: 'furious'. 'Thrilled' and 'pleased' are the opposite feeling, and 'energetic' does not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Light at the end of tunnel
options: Something that signals the end of a difficult situation
An opening at the end of a matter
New light coming out from darkness
questions.explanation: 'Light at the end of the tunnel' is a sign that a long, difficult period is coming to an end.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Retain
questions.explanation: To 'retain' is to keep, including keeping something in the memory; in that sense its opposite is 'forget'. 'Maintain' is close to 'retain', and 'restore' and 'attain' are not opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom in bold in the given sentence. Because the shop is closing down, most of the stock is going “for a song”.
options: Something that is soothing to your ears
questions.explanation: Something that goes 'for a song' is sold very cheaply, as the stock of a shop that is closing down is.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. The goods being sold are of “inferior” quality.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'inferior' (lower in quality) is 'superior'. 'Anterior' means at the front, 'exterior' outside and 'ulterior' hidden.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Benign
questions.explanation: 'Benign' means kind and gentle; its opposite is 'wicked'. 'Favourable' and 'friendly' are close to 'benign'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The way someone talks and behaves “introduces the characteristics” of a person.
questions.explanation: The way someone talks and behaves 'defines the personality' of a person: it shows what kind of person they are. 'Effects' is a misuse of 'affects', and 'postulates' means assumes.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Notebook software is included (1)___________ the SMART Board Interactive Whiteboard device. This programme includes a (2)____________ of tools for differentiating education. Professors and students can write on the SMART Board screen using a digital pen or (3)_________ finger if they have a SMART Board. Notebook files may be saved in various formats, printed, emailed, or posted, providing students with a total (4)____________ to course materials. Essentially, having a SMART Board available may (5)_________ everything that can be done on a computer.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: Software that comes as part of a device is included 'with' it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Notebook software is included (1)___________ the SMART Board Interactive Whiteboard device. This programme includes a (2)____________ of tools for differentiating education. Professors and students can write on the SMART Board screen using a digital pen or (3)_________ finger if they have a SMART Board. Notebook files may be saved in various formats, printed, emailed, or posted, providing students with a total (4)____________ to course materials. Essentially, having a SMART Board available may (5)_________ everything that can be done on a computer.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: 'A number of tools' means several tools; 'a total', 'a limit' or 'a design of tools' does not make sense.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Notebook software is included (1)___________ the SMART Board Interactive Whiteboard device. This programme includes a (2)____________ of tools for differentiating education. Professors and students can write on the SMART Board screen using a digital pen or (3)_________ finger if they have a SMART Board. Notebook files may be saved in various formats, printed, emailed, or posted, providing students with a total (4)____________ to course materials. Essentially, having a SMART Board available may (5)_________ everything that can be done on a computer.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: The possessive 'their' refers back to the professors and students: 'a digital pen or their finger'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Notebook software is included (1)___________ the SMART Board Interactive Whiteboard device. This programme includes a (2)____________ of tools for differentiating education. Professors and students can write on the SMART Board screen using a digital pen or (3)_________ finger if they have a SMART Board. Notebook files may be saved in various formats, printed, emailed, or posted, providing students with a total (4)____________ to course materials. Essentially, having a SMART Board available may (5)_________ everything that can be done on a computer.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: Students are given 'access to' course materials, that is the means to reach and use them.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Notebook software is included (1)___________ the SMART Board Interactive Whiteboard device. This programme includes a (2)____________ of tools for differentiating education. Professors and students can write on the SMART Board screen using a digital pen or (3)_________ finger if they have a SMART Board. Notebook files may be saved in various formats, printed, emailed, or posted, providing students with a total (4)____________ to course materials. Essentially, having a SMART Board available may (5)_________ everything that can be done on a computer.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: To 'enhance' is to improve: a SMART Board may improve everything that can be done on a computer.

questions.text: Seven people D, E,F,G,H,I and J are sitting in a straight row, facing north. Only three people sit between D and H. E sits fourth to the left of J. Only D is between E and I. J sits third to the right of F. Who sits at the second position from the right end of the row?
questions.explanation: E is fourth to the left of J and J third to the right of F; with E, D and I side by side, the only order that seats everyone is I, D, E, F, G, H, J from the left, with three people between D and H. H is second from the right.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 6, 10, 19, 35, ? , 96
questions.explanation: The differences are 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, the squares of 2 to 6: 35 + 25 = 60 and 60 + 36 = 96.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered 1, 2 and 3. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some shoes are slippers. Some slippers are socks. All socks are sandals. Conclusions: 1. Some sandals are shoes. 2. Some sandals are slippers. 3. Some socks are shoes.
questions.explanation: Some slippers are socks and all socks are sandals, so some slippers are sandals: 2 follows. The shoes that are slippers need not be the slippers that are socks, so 1 and 3 do not follow.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 18 : 4 :: 36 : 16 :: 27 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first divided by 9: 18 ÷ 9 = 2 and 2² = 4; 36 ÷ 9 = 4 and 4² = 16. So 27 ÷ 9 = 3 and 3² = 9.

questions.text: Six friends (Aman, Biplab, Chirantan, Divya, Elizabeth and Firoz) are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Aman sits third to the left of Biplab. Chirantan is an immediate neighbour of Aman. Elizabeth sits second to the right of Divya. Chirantan is not an immediate neighbour of Divya. Who sits between Aman and Elizabeth?
questions.explanation: Aman, third to the left of Biplab, sits opposite him. With Elizabeth second to the right of Divya and Chirantan next to Aman but not to Divya, the only arrangement, going round to the left from Biplab, is Divya, Firoz, Aman, Chirantan, Elizabeth. Chirantan sits between Aman and Elizabeth.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘fruit hat string’ is coded as ‘worm bee wheel’, ‘hat fruit’ is coded as ‘bee worm’, and ‘string hat’ is coded as ‘wheel bee’. What is the code word for ‘fruit’?
questions.explanation: 'Hat' is in all three phrases and 'bee' in all three codes, so hat = bee. Then 'hat fruit' = 'bee worm' gives fruit = worm (and string = wheel).

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Virology : Viruses :: Cardiology : ?
questions.explanation: Virology is the study of viruses; cardiology is the study of the heart.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 120 + 18 × 40 – 10 ÷ 20 = 172
Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? GMPJ, HLOK, IKNL, JJMM, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters run G, H, I, J, K; the second M, L, K, J, I; the third P, O, N, M, L; the fourth J, K, L, M, N. The next cluster is KILN.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘PARENT’ is written as ‘148’ and ‘WRANGLE’ is written as ‘160’.How will ‘GRANTED’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded as twice the sum of its letters' places in the alphabet: PARENT = 16 + 1 + 18 + 5 + 14 + 20 = 74 → 148 and WRANGLE = 80 → 160. GRANTED = 7 + 18 + 1 + 14 + 20 + 5 + 4 = 69 → 138.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 20, 24, 33, ?, 107, 228, 397
questions.explanation: The differences are the squares of the primes 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13: 4, 9, 25, 49, 121, 169. So 33 + 25 = 58, and 58 + 49 = 107.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? BDGF, ACFE, ? , YADC, XZCB
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place back each time: B, A, Z, Y, X; D, C, B, A, Z; G, F, E, D, C; F, E, D, C, B. The missing cluster is ZBED.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 culture 2 cult 3 cultivate 4 cupid 5 cumin
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: cult (2), cultivate (3), culture (1), cumin (5), cupid (4). 'Cult' is the shortest, 'culti' comes before 'cultu', and 'cum' before 'cup'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. IFHO : LCEK :: HIJK : KFGG :: QLGK : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +3, −3, −3, −4: I → L, F → C, H → E, O → K and H → K, I → F, J → G, K → G. So QLGK → TIDG.

questions.text: A is married to Z. Z has 3 children L, M and N. Z is not the father of the children. P is the mother of A. L is the husband of D. M has 2 daughters H and J. How is Z related to P?
questions.explanation: Z is not the father of the children, so Z is their mother and A's wife. P is A's mother, so Z is P's daughter-in-law.

questions.text: Which is NOT the correct statement about the Governor?
options: He appoints the Chief Minister and other Ministers.
He has the power to grant pardons, reprieves and forgive the death penalty of a person
He may issue Ordinances under certain circumstances
The state executive power is vested with the Governor.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives this statement, on the textbook reading of Articles 72 and 161: only the President can pardon a death sentence, while a Governor can grant pardons, reprieves, respites and remissions and can suspend, remit or commute a sentence, a death sentence included, but cannot pardon one. A Supreme Court ruling of August 2021, on Article 161 and Section 433A of the CrPC, was widely reported as letting a Governor pardon prisoners including those on death row, but the other three statements are plainly correct (Articles 164, 213 and 154).

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year did Congress and Muslim League signed the Lucknow pact?
questions.explanation: In the Lucknow Pact of December 1916 the Congress and the Muslim League agreed on joint demands for self-government, and the Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims.

questions.text: __________ can be visualized as a functional unit of nature, where living organisms interact among themselves and also with the surrounding physical environment.
questions.explanation: This is NCERT's definition of an ecosystem: the living organisms of an area and the physical environment they interact with, working as one unit.

questions.text: What is the Full Form of BCCI?
options: Board of Control of Cycling in India
Board of Control for Cricket in India
questions.explanation: BCCI stands for the Board of Control for Cricket in India, the body that runs cricket in the country.

questions.text: India's first five-year plan was launched in ______.
questions.explanation: India's First Five-Year Plan ran from 1951 to 1956 and gave priority to agriculture.

questions.text: Apart from the Cash Reserve Ratio, banks are also required to keep some reserves in liquid form in the short term, referred as __________
questions.explanation: Besides the cash reserve ratio, held with the RBI, banks must keep a set share of their deposits in liquid assets such as cash, gold and approved government securities: the Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR).

questions.text: In which year was the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) passed?
questions.explanation: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was passed in 2005 and renamed after Mahatma Gandhi in 2009; it guarantees a rural household 100 days of wage employment a year.

questions.text: President of India appointed senior advocate ______ as the next Attorney-General for India in September 2022.
questions.explanation: In September 2022 the President appointed R Venkataramani Attorney General for India for three years from 1 October 2022, succeeding K K Venugopal.

questions.text: Who was the prime minister of India when the fundatmental duties were included in the Indian constitution?
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, Article 51A) were added by the 42nd Amendment of 1976, on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation, when Indira Gandhi was Prime Minister.

questions.text: Green Revolution mainly revolves around ___________.
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution of the mid-1960s rested on the High Yielding Varieties Programme (1966): high-yielding seeds of wheat and rice, used with fertilisers, pesticides and irrigation.

questions.text: Who was the coach of the U-19 Indian cricket team at the ICC U19 World Cup 2022?
questions.explanation: Hrishikesh Kanitkar was head coach of the India team, captained by Yash Dhull, that won the ICC Under-19 World Cup 2022 in the West Indies.

questions.text: Thiruvathira festival is mainly celebrated in which of these states?
questions.explanation: Thiruvathira is a festival of Kerala, held in the Malayalam month of Dhanu (December-January), when women perform the Thiruvathirakali dance.

questions.text: What is used for manufacturing synthetic fibers, synthetic rubber, plastics, dye-stuffs, drugs and pharmaceuticals?
questions.explanation: Petrochemicals, obtained from crude oil and natural gas, are the raw material for synthetic fibres, synthetic rubber, plastics, dyes, drugs and pharmaceuticals.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a sedimentary rock?
questions.explanation: Granite is an igneous rock, formed from magma that cooled slowly below the surface. Sandstone and shale are sedimentary rocks, and loess, fine silt laid down by the wind, is grouped with them.

questions.text: Who has been appointed as the Revenue Secretary by the Indian government in October 2022?
questions.explanation: In October 2022 the government named Sanjay Malhotra, then Secretary of the Department of Financial Services, officer on special duty in the Department of Revenue, to become Revenue Secretary when Tarun Bajaj retired on 30 November 2022; he took charge on 1 December 2022.

questions.text: Who presented the Criminal Procedure (Identification) Bill, 2022 on March 28 in Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Ajay Kumar Mishra, Minister of State for Home Affairs, introduced the Criminal Procedure (Identification) Bill, 2022 in the Lok Sabha on 28 March 2022, to replace the Identification of Prisoners Act, 1920.

questions.text: According to Megasthenes, the guards of Chandragupta rode _________ decorated with gold and silver during royal processions.
questions.explanation: Megasthenes, the Greek envoy at Chandragupta Maurya's court, described royal processions in which the emperor's guards rode elephants decorated with gold and silver.

questions.text: Kalbelia is a famous folk dance of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Kalbelia is the dance of Rajasthan's Kalbelia community of snake charmers; UNESCO inscribed the Kalbelia folk songs and dances of Rajasthan on its intangible heritage list in 2010.

questions.text: Which of the following festivals celebrates the harvest season in August – September?
questions.explanation: Onam, the harvest festival of Kerala, falls in the Malayalam month of Chingam (August-September). Makar Sankranti and Lohri come in January and Baisakhi in April.

questions.text: The fourth proportional to 3, 12, 14 is:
An iron ball of radius 21 cm is melted and recast into spherical balls of radius 7 cm. Find the number of spherical balls.
questions.explanation: Volumes go as the cube of the radius: (21/7)³ = 3³ = 27 balls.

questions.text: Find the sum of the digits of the smallest 6-digit number divisible by 18, 24 and 25.
questions.explanation: LCM(18, 24, 25) = 2³ × 3² × 5² = 1800. 100000 ÷ 1800 = 55.6, so the smallest 6-digit multiple is 56 × 1800 = 100800, whose digits add up to 1 + 8 = 9.

questions.text: A vegetable vendor does his sales using a weight which is 12% less than the actual weight and earns a profit of 32% on the cost price. Find the total profit percentage?
questions.explanation: He gives 880 g for every 1,000 g he charges for, at 1.32 times the cost price: 1.32 × 1000/880 = 1.5, so his total profit is 50%.

questions.text: A and B can complete a work in 18 days and 36 days respectively. They work together for 8 days and then A leaves. How many days will B take to complete the rest of the work?
questions.explanation: Together they do 1/18 + 1/36 = 1/12 of the work a day, so 8/12 = 2/3 in 8 days. B does the remaining 1/3 in 36 ÷ 3 = 12 days.

questions.text: What is the average of the first 10 multiples of 3?
questions.explanation: The multiples 3, 6, ..., 30 are evenly spaced, so their average is (3 + 30)/2 = 16.5.

questions.text: If the price of potatoes increases by 10 percent, then by how much percent a user has to cut down on his consumption of potatoes, so that the expenditure on potatoes remains unchanged?
questions.explanation: Consumption must fall by 10/110 × 100 = 9.09%, about 9.1 percent, since 1.1 × (1 − 1/11) = 1.

questions.text: The current value of a car is ₹ 8,50,000 and its value is depreciating at the rate of 10% per annum. What will be its value (in ₹ ) after 4 years?
What is the faulty weight used by a dishonest shopkeeper instead of the original weight of 1 kg to get a profit of 25%?
questions.explanation: Selling at the cost price, the shopkeeper gains 25% if he gives w grams for every 1,000: 1000/w = 1.25, so w = 800 grams.

questions.text: A, B, and C can complete a work in 30, 60, and 120 days respectively. A left the work 10 days before the work was completed and B left 5 days before the completion of the work. Find the number of days required to complete the whole work.
questions.explanation: If the work takes T days, A works T − 10, B T − 5 and C T days: (T − 10)/30 + (T − 5)/60 + T/120 = 1. Multiplying by 120: 4T − 40 + 2T − 10 + T = 120, so 7T = 170 and T = 170/7 days.

questions.text: Mr. Sharma spends 15% of his total income on rent and 75% of the remaining part on other expenses and still saves Rs.1,700 monthly. What is his monthly income?
questions.explanation: After rent he has 85% of his income and saves a quarter of it: 0.85 × 0.25 = 0.2125 of the income = ₹1,700, so the income is 1,700 ÷ 0.2125 = ₹8,000.

questions.text: Arjun rides his bike 10 km at an average speed of 30 km/h, and again travels 14 km at an average speed of 25 km/h. What is his average speed (approx.) for the entire trip?

Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. When the last Tsar of Russia (were arrested by revolutionaries), he and his family were hiding at a palace near St. Petersburg; now that palace is open to tourists.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'the last Tsar' takes 'was', and the past passive matches 'were hiding': 'was arrested by revolutionaries'.

questions.text: Select the correct word for the blanks in the given sentence. Sushant is a very _________ person and the _________ of first ten natural numbers is 5.5.
questions.explanation: 'Mean' fits both blanks: a mean person is unkind or stingy, and the mean (average) of 1 to 10 is 55/10 = 5.5.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Consistent
questions.explanation: 'Consistent' means unchanging: 'constant'. 'Evolve', 'change' and 'alter' are all verbs of changing, the opposite idea.

questions.text: Select the correct word for the blanks in the given sentence. The tree has a brown __________ and the dogs __________ at the stranger.
questions.explanation: 'Bark' fits both blanks: the outer covering of a tree trunk, and the sound a dog makes.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given below to fill in the blank in the following sentence. Pamper My grandmother said, “Don’t ______ the kid. He will get spoiled”.
questions.explanation: To 'pamper' or 'coddle' a child is to indulge and over-protect it, which spoils it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. This is an “olden” building of historical importance.
questions.explanation: 'Olden' is used only in set phrases such as 'olden days'; a building of historical importance is 'ancient'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The peon / was brought / a cup of / coffee for Naina.
questions.explanation: The peon did the bringing, so the verb must be active: 'The peon brought a cup of coffee for Naina.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Earn
questions.explanation: To 'earn' is to receive money or reward in return for work. 'Lose' and 'surrender' are near opposites, and 'accord' means to grant.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Fit as a fiddle
questions.explanation: 'Fit as a fiddle' means in very good health.

questions.text: The sentence given below has one misspelt word. Spot the INCORRECTLY spelt word and select its correct spelling. Some diseases are due to neurologikal disorders.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'neurological', with 'eu' and a 'c': relating to the nerves and the nervous system.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The private ______ has contributed immensely to the country’s economy.
questions.explanation: The 'private sector' is the part of the economy run by private businesses rather than by the government.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Take it with a grain of salt
options: To calculate things with utmost precision
To misinterpret that the real situation is hidden
To understand that something is likely to be untrue
To imagine that someone is working against you
questions.explanation: To 'take something with a grain of salt' is to doubt it, accepting that it may not be wholly true.

questions.text: Fill in the blank by selecting the meaningful and correctly spelt word from the given options. Nowadays, the police get a long _________ of drug peddlers every day.
questions.explanation: The police get a long 'list' of names. 'Lest' means for fear that, 'least' is the superlative of 'little', and 'leest' is not a word.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Hope
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'hope' is 'despair', the complete loss of hope.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Generous
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'generous' is 'selfish'; 'liberal' and 'selfless' are close in meaning to 'generous'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. An initiative has been (1) ________ in the educational reform sector in form of Social and Emotional Learning (SEL). This novel (2) ________ helps students to understand and manage their own emotions. The students (3) ________ and learn in a constructive manner. This concept (4) ________ momentum with the publication of the best seller by Daniel Goleman titled ‘Emotional Intelligence: Why it can matter more than IQ’. It (5) _______ the enhancement of the given competencies: speaking and listening, cooperative skills and problem solving.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'started': an initiative is started, or launched, and the passage presents SEL as a novel concept that went on to gain momentum. 'Established' goes more naturally with something set up to last, such as an institution or a system, and 'discovered' and 'reckoned' do not fit.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. An initiative has been (1) ________ in the educational reform sector in form of Social and Emotional Learning (SEL). This novel (2) ________ helps students to understand and manage their own emotions. The students (3) ________ and learn in a constructive manner. This concept (4) ________ momentum with the publication of the best seller by Daniel Goleman titled ‘Emotional Intelligence: Why it can matter more than IQ’. It (5) _______ the enhancement of the given competencies: speaking and listening, cooperative skills and problem solving.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: SEL is a new idea, a 'novel concept'; the passage goes on to call it 'this concept'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. An initiative has been (1) ________ in the educational reform sector in form of Social and Emotional Learning (SEL). This novel (2) ________ helps students to understand and manage their own emotions. The students (3) ________ and learn in a constructive manner. This concept (4) ________ momentum with the publication of the best seller by Daniel Goleman titled ‘Emotional Intelligence: Why it can matter more than IQ’. It (5) _______ the enhancement of the given competencies: speaking and listening, cooperative skills and problem solving.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: The students 'interact', dealing with one another as they learn; the skills named later are speaking, listening and cooperating.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. An initiative has been (1) ________ in the educational reform sector in form of Social and Emotional Learning (SEL). This novel (2) ________ helps students to understand and manage their own emotions. The students (3) ________ and learn in a constructive manner. It (5) _______ the enhancement of the given competencies: speaking and listening, cooperative skills and problem solving.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: An idea 'gains momentum' when it spreads and grows in influence, as SEL did after Goleman's best seller.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. An initiative has been (1) ________ in the educational reform sector in form of Social and Emotional Learning (SEL).
