It (5) _______ the enhancement of the given competencies: speaking and listening, cooperative skills and problem solving.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: SEL 'incorporates', that is includes, the development of the competencies listed.

questions.text: Six friends Amit, Bunty, Vaibhav, Harshit, Pulkit and Gagan are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre. Bunty is the immediate neighbour of Harshit and Vaibhav. Amit is the immediate neighbour of Pulkit and Vaibhav. Who is the immediate neighbour of Amit and Gagan?
questions.explanation: Bunty sits between Harshit and Vaibhav, and Amit between Vaibhav and Pulkit, so the order round the table is Harshit, Bunty, Vaibhav, Amit, Pulkit, with Gagan in the sixth seat between Pulkit and Harshit. Pulkit sits next to both Amit and Gagan.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 24 - 8 + 12 ÷ 48 × 36 = 23
In a certain language, EARLY is coded as HDUOB, GAMES is coded as JDPHV. How will INDEX be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward, wrapping round after Z: EARLY → HDUOB and GAMES → JDPHV. So INDEX → LQGHA.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: All doors are walls. All walls are rooms. All rooms are flats. Conclusions: I. Some flats are doors. II. All walls are flats.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: All doors are walls, all walls are rooms and all rooms are flats, so all walls and all doors are flats. II follows, and as all doors are flats, some flats are doors: I follows too.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed) (360, 65, 25); (216, 44, 20)
questions.explanation: The first number is 9 times the difference of the other two: (65 − 25) × 9 = 360 and (44 − 20) × 9 = 216. Likewise (35 − 13) × 9 = 198.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘live life happily’ is coded as '447', ‘everyone is here’ is coded as '824' and ‘be grateful’ is coded as '28'. How will ‘count your blessings’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each digit is the number of letters in a word: live (4), life (4), happily (7) → 447, and be (2), grateful (8) → 28. So count (5), your (4), blessings (9) → 549.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 4, 7, 12, 19, 28, 39, 52, 67, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are the odd numbers 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15; the next is 17: 67 + 17 = 84.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. WBL, DIS, KPZ, RWG, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 7 places forward, wrapping round after Z: W, D, K, R, Y; B, I, P, W, D; L, S, Z, G, N. The next cluster is YDN.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 25 + 200 ÷ 8 × 16 – 48 = 77
questions.explanation: After interchanging ÷ and ×: 25 + 200 × 8 ÷ 16 − 48 = 25 + 100 − 48 = 77.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 4, 24, 30, 180, 186, ?

Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Colour : Red :: Vehicle : ?
questions.explanation: Red is a colour, and a truck is a kind of vehicle.

questions.text: ‘A ^ P’ means ‘A is the husband of P’. ‘A % P’ means ‘A is the father of P’. ‘A = P’ means ‘A is the sister of P’. ‘A & P’ means ‘A is the daughter of P’. If F & G = H ^ J, then which of the following is correct?
options: F is the daughter of J.
G is the mother of J.
J is the wife of G’s brother.
questions.explanation: F is G's daughter, G is H's sister and H is J's husband. So J is the wife of H, who is G's brother.

questions.text: V, W, X, Y, Z, A, B and C were sitting around a square table facing the centre. Some of these were sitting at corners and some were sitting at exact centre of the sides.C was to the immediate right of W. B was third to the left of Z. A was the immediate neighbour of X and C. Z, not at any corner, was the immediate neighbour of W and Y. Who among the following was sitting third to the right of A?
questions.explanation: C sits on W's immediate right, so W cannot be on Z's left (C would need Z's seat): W is on Z's right and Y on Z's left. Going round to the right from Z come W, C, A (next to C) and X; going left come Y, a free seat and B, third to Z's left, so V takes the free seat. Going round to the right from A: X, B, V.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. FALLEN : TJPOCG :: DANGER : XJKQCE :: CABLES : ?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and its letters moved +6, +5, +4, +3, +2, +1: FALLEN → NELLAF → TJPOCG and DANGER → REGNAD → XJKQCE. So CABLES → SELBAC → YJPECD.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) and complete the following letter-cluster series? UH, BD, IA, PY, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move 7 places forward (U, B, I, P, W), wrapping round after Z, and the second move back 4, 3, 2 and 1 (H, D, A, Y, X): WX.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Pillow 2 Pile 3 Pint 4 Picked 5 Pickle
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Picked (4), Pickle (5), Pile (2), Pillow (1), Pint (3). 'Picke' comes before 'Pickl' (e before l), 'Pic' before 'Pil' before 'Pin', and 'Pile' before 'Pill'.

questions.text: Which among the following political leaders succeeded Raghav Chadha to become Member of Legislative Assembly from Rajinder Nagar, Delhi in June 2022?
questions.explanation: Durgesh Pathak of the Aam Aadmi Party won the Rajinder Nagar by-election in June 2022; the seat had fallen vacant when Raghav Chadha was elected to the Rajya Sabha.

questions.text: Which Part of the Constitution of India contains within it the powers and functions of the Union Public Service Commission?
questions.explanation: Part XIV (Services under the Union and the States) deals with the Public Service Commissions in Articles 315 to 323; Article 320 sets out their functions.

questions.text: RUSA , is the central government’s contribution to further the promise held by the rich expanse of India’s state universities. RUSA stands for:
questions.explanation: RUSA, the Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan, is a centrally sponsored scheme launched in 2013 to fund higher-education institutions run by the states.

questions.text: The famous Losoong festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Losoong, the Sikkimese new year of the Bhutia community, is held in December at the end of the harvest season, with masked cham dances at the monasteries.

questions.text: During the Chola period, muvendavelan and araiyar were titles of ______.
questions.explanation: NCERT's Class 7 history describes how Chola kings honoured some rich landowners with titles such as 'muvendavelan' (a velan, or peasant, serving three kings) and 'araiyar' (chief).

questions.text: Guru Pankaj Charan Das is a famous proponent of which Indian classical Dance?
questions.explanation: Guru Pankaj Charan Das, who came from Odisha's mahari (temple dancer) tradition, is regarded as the 'Adi Guru' of Odissi.

questions.text: In India, it is the only industry in the country, which is self-reliant and complete in the value chain i.e., from raw material to the highest value added products. Which industry is being spoken about here?
questions.explanation: NCERT's Class 10 geography says this of the textile industry: India grows the fibres and spins, weaves and makes up the cloth and garments itself, so the whole chain is in the country.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was the founder of the ‘Khudai Khidmatgars’ non-violent movement?
questions.explanation: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, the 'Frontier Gandhi', founded the Khudai Khidmatgars ('Servants of God') in the North-West Frontier Province in 1929.

questions.text: Cyclostomes are jawless ______.
questions.explanation: Cyclostomes, the lampreys and hagfishes, are vertebrates with a circular sucking mouth and no jaws (the superclass Agnatha).

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The first complete census of an Indian city was conducted in 1830 by __________.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Henry Walter, a British magistrate at Dacca, who counted the city's people in 1830. James Rennell was the surveyor who mapped Bengal, John Graunt a 17th-century English student of London's death records and Eratosthenes a Greek geographer.

questions.text: National development council (NDC) was set up in_________ in India.
questions.explanation: The National Development Council was set up on 6 August 1952 to bring the states into the making of the Five Year Plans.

questions.text: In November 2021, which of the following dancer won a Padma Shri for the contribution in Arts?
questions.explanation: Manjamma Jogati (Jogathi), a performer of Karnataka's Jogati folk dance, received the Padma Shri for 2021 at the ceremony in November 2021. Chutni Devi and Shanti Devi received theirs for social work, and Sumitra Mahajan the Padma Bhushan for public affairs.

questions.text: Whose tenure has been extended by one year as the Chief of Research and Analysis Wing (R&AW) in June 2022?
questions.explanation: In June 2022 the government extended Samant Kumar Goel's term as chief of R&AW by one year, to June 2023.

questions.text: Which of the following is correct regarding Personal Disposable Income?
options: Personal Disposable Income ≡ Personal Income + Personal tax payments – Non-tax payments
Personal Disposable Income ≡ Personal Income – Personal tax payments – Non-tax payments
Personal Disposable Income ≡ Personal Income – Personal tax payments + Non-tax payments
Personal Disposable Income ≡ Personal Income + Personal tax payments + Non-tax payments
questions.explanation: What households can spend or save is their personal income less what they pay the government, both personal taxes (such as income tax) and non-tax payments (such as fines): PDI = PI − personal tax payments − non-tax payments.

questions.text: Which among the following elements has the least atomic radius?
questions.explanation: Atomic radius shrinks across a period as the nuclear charge grows. Li, Be, B and O are all in period 2, and oxygen lies farthest to the right.

questions.text: In which of the following International Olympic Committee’s session, Tomas Bach’s Olympic Agenda 2020+5 was discussed?
questions.explanation: Olympic Agenda 2020+5, Thomas Bach's roadmap of 15 recommendations to 2025, was approved at the 137th IOC Session, held online in March 2021.

questions.text: Which water body surrounds India in the west?
questions.explanation: The Arabian Sea lies to the west of the Indian peninsula and the Bay of Bengal to the east; the Indian Ocean is to the south.

questions.text: In the Indian constitution, Right to equality has ________ articles in it.
questions.explanation: The Right to Equality is Articles 14 to 18: equality before law, no discrimination, equal opportunity in public employment, abolition of untouchability and abolition of titles.

questions.text: A salesman buys 15 articles for Rs.10 and sells 10 articles for Rs.15. Determine the percentage profit earned by the salesman.
Sohan and Rohan together can do a piece of work in 18 days. If Sohan alone can do the same work in 27 days, then how many days Rohan alone takes to complete the same work?
questions.explanation: Rohan does 1/18 − 1/27 = (3 − 2)/54 = 1/54 of the work a day, so he takes 54 days.

questions.text: The average of the first four prime numbers that are odd is:
questions.explanation: The first four odd primes are 3, 5, 7 and 11: (3 + 5 + 7 + 11)/4 = 26/4 = 6.5.

questions.text: A, B, and C can do a piece of work in 8, 4, and 16 days respectively. How many days will A take to complete the entire work if A is assisted by B and C both on every second day?
questions.explanation: Day 1, A alone: 1/8. Day 2, A, B and C: 1/8 + 1/4 + 1/16 = 7/16. After day 3 (A alone) 1/8 + 7/16 + 1/8 = 11/16 is done, and the remaining 5/16 at 7/16 a day takes 5/7 of day 4: 3 + 5/7 = 26/7 days.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers is NOT divisible by 16?
questions.explanation: A number is divisible by 16 when its last four digits are: 7776 = 16 × 486, 5168 = 16 × 323 and 8016 = 16 × 501, but 6826 = 16 × 426 + 10.

questions.text: In an election between two candidates, One candidate got 48% of the total valid votes. 18% of the votes were invalid. If the total number of votes was 17500, then what was the number of valid votes the other candidate got?
questions.explanation: Valid votes = 82% of 17,500 = 14,350. The other candidate got the remaining 52% of them: 0.52 × 14,350 = 7,462.

questions.text: A trader gains 12% after allowing a discount of 20% on the marked price of an article. Find his profit percentage if the article is sold at marked price allowing no discount.
questions.explanation: If the cost price is 100, the selling price is 112 = 80% of the marked price, so the marked price is 140 and selling at it gives a 40% profit.

questions.text: In an election between three candidates A, B and C, 80% of the registered voters voted and all the votes were valid. Candidate B got 50% less votes than A, and the difference between the number of votes secured by B and C was 10000. If B got 10% more votes than C, then the number of voters registered on the voting list is:
questions.explanation: B − C = 10% of C = 10,000, so C = 1,00,000 and B = 1,10,000; B has half of A's votes, so A = 2,20,000. The 4,30,000 votes cast are 80% of the register: 4,30,000 ÷ 0.8 = 5,37,500.

questions.text: Two trains having lengths 550 m and 650 m are running parallel to each other in opposite directions at speeds of 68 km/h and 40 km/h, respectively. In how much time (in seconds) they will cross each other?
questions.explanation: Together the trains cover 550 + 650 = 1,200 m at a relative speed of 68 + 40 = 108 km/h = 30 m/s: 1,200 ÷ 30 = 40 seconds.

questions.text: Without stoppages a train travels a certain distance with an average speed of 75 km/h and with stoppages it covers the same distance with an average speed of 65 km/h. How many minutes per hour does the train stop?
questions.explanation: In each hour the train covers 65 km instead of 75 km. At 75 km/h the missing 10 km would take 10/75 × 60 = 8 minutes, the time it spends stopped.

questions.text: When the same number is subtracted from each of 7, 9, 11 and 15, the resulting numbers are in proportion. The number subtracted is:
questions.explanation: (7 − x)(15 − x) = (9 − x)(11 − x) gives 105 − 22x = 99 − 20x, so x = 3; the numbers 4, 6, 8, 12 are in proportion, as 4 : 6 = 8 : 12.

questions.text: Lara deposited Rs.8,000 in a bank, which pays her compound interest at the rate of 10% per annum compounded half-yearly. What is the amount she will receive after 18 months?

X was offering two successive discounts of 12 percent and 8 percent on an item while Y was offering flat 20 percent discount on the same item. What is the difference between overall discount given by X and Y?
questions.explanation: X's overall discount is 12 + 8 − (12 × 8)/100 = 19.04%, against Y's 20%: a difference of 0.96 percent.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. How she “managed of escaping from” the situation was inexplicable.
questions.explanation: 'Manage' takes the to-infinitive, and one escapes 'from' a situation: 'How she managed to escape from the situation was inexplicable.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Wild goose chase
questions.explanation: A 'wild goose chase' is a hopeless or pointless pursuit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. As he opened the window the sun ___________ directly fell on his face.
questions.explanation: The sun's 'rays' fell on his face; 'raze' (to destroy), 'race' and 'raise' sound alike but do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Auspicious
questions.explanation: 'Auspicious' means promising good fortune, so 'fortunate'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Mr. Advani was happy to “push the boat out” for his daughter’s wedding.
questions.explanation: To 'push the boat out' is to spend a lot of money on a celebration, such as a daughter's wedding.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. They enjoyed ________ the sun rising from the hills.
questions.explanation: 'Enjoy' is followed by a gerund (the -ing form), not 'to' or 'in': 'They enjoyed watching the sun rising from the hills.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the capitalised word in the given sentence. Isabel listened with extreme respect to this ADMONITION.
questions.explanation: An 'admonition' is a warning or piece of earnest advice, which is what 'counsel' means; 'council' is a body of people that advises or governs.

questions.text: Select the correct pair of words for the blanks in the given sentence. I will ________ a new purse from the shop on the ________ pass road.
questions.explanation: One 'buys' (purchases) a purse, and a 'by-pass' (bypass) road goes round a town: 'buy' and 'by'. 'Bye' is a farewell.

questions.text: Fill in the blank in the following sentence using the ANTONYM of the underlined word. We believe that this incident has been “exaggerated” so ___________ it.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'exaggerate' (overstate) is 'understate', to make something seem smaller than it is.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. I can't say for sure/ what make him/ think of such an/ outrageously absurd idea.
questions.explanation: 'What' is the singular subject of 'make', so the verb should be 'makes' (or, in the past, 'made'): 'what made him think of such an outrageously absurd idea'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Curtail
questions.explanation: To 'curtail' is to cut short or reduce, so its opposite is 'amplify', to enlarge; 'restrict' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Over 80% of India's transportation fuel “are exchanged”.
questions.explanation: 'Fuel' is an uncountable noun, so '80% of ... fuel' takes a singular verb, and the sense is that India brings most of its transport fuel from abroad: 'is imported'.

questions.text: Identify the correctly spelt sentence.
options: I saw the catalogue of D Décor in Capital Mall yesterday.
I saw the cattalogue of D Décor in Capital Mall yesterday.
I saw the catologue of D Décor in Capital Mall yesterday.
I saw the catalogoue of D Décor in Capital Mall yesterday.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'catalogue', with one 't' and the ending '-logue'.

questions.text: The sentence given below has one misspelt word. Spot the INCORRECTLY spelt word and select its correct spelling. The aproximate value of my property is ₹2 lakh.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'approximate', with a double 'p'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Outgoing
questions.explanation: An 'outgoing' person is friendly and sociable; the opposite is 'introverted', shy and inward-looking.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Miss Caroline was no more (1)__________ twenty-one. She had bright auburn hair, pink (2)__________, and wore crimson finger-nail polish. She also (3)__________high-heeled pumps and a red-and-white (4)__________dress. She looked and smelled (5)__________a peppermint drop.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'No more than twenty-one' compares her age with a number, so 'than'; 'then' refers to time.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Miss Caroline was no more (1)__________ twenty-one. She had bright auburn hair, pink (2)__________, and wore crimson finger-nail polish. She also (3)__________high-heeled pumps and a red-and-white (4)__________dress. She looked and smelled (5)__________a peppermint drop.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Bright auburn hair and 'pink cheeks' describe her face; pink ears or eyebrows would be odd details.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Miss Caroline was no more (1)__________ twenty-one. She had bright auburn hair, pink (2)__________, and wore crimson finger-nail polish. She also (3)__________high-heeled pumps and a red-and-white (4)__________dress. She looked and smelled (5)__________a peppermint drop.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The passage is in the simple past ('had', 'wore', 'looked'), so 'She also wore high-heeled pumps'; 'worn' would need 'had'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Miss Caroline was no more (1)__________ twenty-one. She had bright auburn hair, pink (2)__________, and wore crimson finger-nail polish. She also (3)__________high-heeled pumps and a red-and-white (4)__________dress. She looked and smelled (5)__________a peppermint drop.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: A 'striped' dress has stripes; 'stripped' is the past tense of 'strip', to take off a covering.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Miss Caroline was no more (1)__________ twenty-one. She had bright auburn hair, pink (2)__________, and wore crimson finger-nail polish. She also (3)__________high-heeled pumps and a red-and-white (4)__________dress. She looked and smelled (5)__________a peppermint drop.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Like' compares her with a noun phrase, 'a peppermint drop'; 'as if' would need a clause.

questions.text: Six people U, V, W, X, Y, and Z are sitting in a circle facing opposite to the centre. U is sitting third to the right of Y. W is sitting to the immediate left of U. W is sitting third to the left of V. Z is not sitting next to U. Who is sitting between W and Y?
questions.explanation: In a circle of six, third to the right is the seat opposite, so U is opposite Y and V opposite W, with W next to U. Of the two seats left, one is next to U, so Z takes the other, between W and Y.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 kind 2 kite 3 knit 4 king 5 kindle
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: kind (1), kindle (5), king (4), kite (2), knit (3). 'Kind' comes before 'kindle', which begins with it, and 'kind' before 'king' as d comes before g.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? XCMQ, YDNR, ?, AFPT, BGQU
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward from one cluster to the next: X, Y, Z, A, B; C, D, E, F, G; M, N, O, P, Q; Q, R, S, T, U. The missing cluster is ZEOS.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All bags are rubber. Some rubber are chairs. All chairs are tables. Conclusions: I. Some rubber are bags. II. Some chairs are rubber. III. Some chairs are tables.
options: Both conclusions I and III follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions II and III follow.
questions.explanation: 'All bags are rubber' gives some rubber are bags (I), 'some rubber are chairs' gives some chairs are rubber (II), and 'all chairs are tables' gives some chairs are tables (III). All three follow.

questions.text: Which of the mathematical signs should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct? 144 - 12 + 18 × 6 ÷ 24 = 96
questions.explanation: After interchanging − and ÷: 144 ÷ 12 + 18 × 6 − 24 = 12 + 108 − 24 = 96.

questions.text: ‘A + B’ means ‘B is the brother of A’; ‘A – B’ means ‘B is the sister of A’; ‘A % B’ means ‘B is the daughter of A’; ‘A & B’ means ‘B is the wife of A’; If A & B % C + D – E, then how is E related to A?
questions.explanation: A & B: B is A's wife. B % C: C is B's daughter. C + D: D is C's brother. D – E: E is D's sister. So E is a daughter of B and her husband A: A's daughter.

questions.text: Seven friends are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. T is an immediate neighbour of K and U. S is sitting immediate right of K. W is an immediate neighbour of U and M. Who is sitting third to the left of K?
questions.explanation: T sits between K and U, and W between U and M, so K, T, U, W and M sit in a row; S is on K's other side. Facing the centre, S on K's right puts T, U and W on K's left, so W is third to the left of K.

questions.text: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 6, 24, 60, 120, ?
questions.explanation: The terms are 1 × 2 × 3, 2 × 3 × 4, 3 × 4 × 5 and 4 × 5 × 6, so the next is 5 × 6 × 7 = 210.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Kite : Claw :: Horse : ?
questions.explanation: A kite, the bird of prey, grips with its claws, and a horse stands on its hooves. 'Strong', 'fast' and 'power' are qualities, not parts of the body.

questions.text: In a certain code language,‘GHOST’ is written as ‘JCRNW’ and ‘FIRED’ is written as ‘IDUZG’. How will ‘RIFLE’ be written in the same code language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +3, −5, +3, −5, +3, wrapping round the alphabet: GHOST → JCRNW and FIRED → IDUZG (E − 5 = Z). So RIFLE → UDIGH.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. PAE : HCQ :: ESH: KUF :: FDN : ?
questions.explanation: The cluster is reversed and its letters moved +3, +2, +1: PAE → EAP → HCQ and ESH → HSE → KUF. So FDN → NDF → QFG.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? QJKE, SHIG, UFGI, ?, YBCM
questions.explanation: The first and fourth letters move forward 2 (Q, S, U, W, Y; E, G, I, K, M) and the second and third back 2 (J, H, F, D, B; K, I, G, E, C): WDEK.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘SLOWLY’ is written as ‘TMNXMZ’ and 'FRIEND’ is written as ‘ GSHDOE’. How will ‘BORING’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each vowel moves one letter back and each consonant one letter forward: SLOWLY → TMNXMZ and FRIEND → GSHDOE. So BORING → CNSHOH.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 62498, 61874, ?, 60644, 60038, 59438

Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (11, 78, 15); (12, 90, 18)
questions.explanation: The middle number is three times the sum of the outer two: (11 + 15) × 3 = 78 and (12 + 18) × 3 = 90. Likewise (13 + 19) × 3 = 96.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 10 * 18 * 19 * 2 * 1 * 217
Government of India has approved a new Central Sector Scheme entitled “National Beekeeping & Honey Mission (NBHM)” which is associated to_______revolution.
questions.explanation: The National Beekeeping and Honey Mission, approved in 2020, promotes scientific beekeeping to bring about a 'Sweet Revolution'.

questions.text: ______ are a narrow belt of high altitude (above 12,000 m) westerly winds in the troposphere. Their speed varies from about 110 km/h in summer to about 184 km/h in winter.
questions.explanation: Jet streams are narrow bands of fast westerly winds high in the troposphere. A derecho is a long line of storms with straight-line winds, and hurricanes and whirlwinds are rotating storms.

questions.text: After independence, India launched its First fiver year plan in ______.
questions.explanation: India's First Five Year Plan ran from 1951 to 1956, with the emphasis on agriculture.

questions.text: Which Indian dancer among the following was the Youngest recipient of Padma Vibhushan in 2003?
questions.explanation: Of the four, only Sonal Mansingh received the Padma Vibhushan in 2003. Uday Shankar received it in 1971, Birju Maharaj in 1986 and Kelucharan Mohapatra in 2000.

questions.text: What is the chemical formula of Calcium Carbonate?
questions.explanation: Calcium carbonate, found as limestone, chalk and marble, is CaCO₃. CaSO₄ is calcium sulphate and CaO calcium oxide (quicklime).

questions.text: Which vitamin is also known as Thiamin?
questions.explanation: Thiamine is vitamin B1; B2 is riboflavin, B3 niacin and B12 cobalamin.

questions.text: Who took oath as the Governor of Meghalaya in October 2022?
questions.explanation: Brigadier (retd) B. D. Mishra, then Governor of Arunachal Pradesh, was sworn in as Governor of Meghalaya on 4 October 2022, taking additional charge when Satya Pal Malik's term ended.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Gandhi-Irwin pact was signed in which year?
questions.explanation: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed on 5 March 1931; Gandhi suspended the Civil Disobedience Movement and attended the Second Round Table Conference.

questions.text: The last article of the Constitution of India has been given the number _______. (as on May 2022).
questions.explanation: The Constitution's articles run to Article 395 ('Repeals'); articles added later are numbered within that range, such as 21A.

questions.text: As of November 2022, who is the Union Minister for Education in India?
questions.explanation: Dharmendra Pradhan was the Union Minister of Education in November 2022, and still when the exam was held (January 2023); he had held the post since July 2021.

questions.text: Which union territory has the highest sex ratio as per the 2011 Census?
questions.explanation: Puducherry had 1,037 females per 1,000 males in the 2011 Census, the highest sex ratio of the union territories.

questions.text: __________ is celebrated as Gujarati New Year in India.
questions.explanation: Bestu Varas, the day after Diwali, is the Gujarati New Year. Vishu is Kerala's new year, Losar the Tibetan new year and Losoong the new year of Sikkim's Bhutias.

questions.text: Primary raw material for sugar industry is _______.
questions.explanation: Sugar mills crush sugar cane, India's main source of sugar; they stand near the cane fields because cut cane soon loses its sucrose.

questions.text: Which among the following classical dance forms was introduced in the 16th century by Vaishnava saint Mahapurusha Sankaradeva?
questions.explanation: Sattriya grew out of the dance-dramas Srimanta Sankaradeva (1449-1568) created for the Vaishnava monasteries (sattras) of Assam. Kuchipudi is from Andhra Pradesh, Odissi from Odisha and Manipuri from Manipur.

questions.text: In which city is the Mohun Bagan Athletic club situated?
questions.explanation: Mohun Bagan Athletic Club, founded in 1889, is in Kolkata.

questions.text: Who hosted the FIFA World Cup 2022?
questions.explanation: Qatar hosted the 2022 FIFA World Cup in November and December 2022, the first held in the Arab world.

questions.text: Removal of president of the country from the office is known as _______.
questions.explanation: Under Article 61 the President can be removed by impeachment for violation of the Constitution, on a charge passed by two-thirds of the total membership of each House in turn.

questions.text: Who among the following Greek rulers sent Megasthenes to the court of Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.explanation: Seleucus I Nicator sent Megasthenes as his envoy to Chandragupta Maurya's court at Pataliputra; Megasthenes described India in his 'Indica'.

questions.text: Manish bought an air conditioner for Rs.46,875, its value is depreciating at the rate of 8% yearly. What will be the price of the air conditioner after 3 years?
An increase of 25 percent in the price of onions enables a woman to buy 5 kg less for Rs. 200. The increased price of onions per kg is:
questions.explanation: A 25% rise means ₹200 buys 1/1.25, or 80%, as much: 20% less. That 20% is 5 kg, so she used to buy 25 kg and now buys 20 kg, at ₹200 ÷ 20 = ₹10 per kg.

questions.text: A person travels in a car for 600 km at an average speed of 50 km/h and 100 km at 100 km/h, and finally reaches his destination by travelling 50 km at a speed of 25 km/h. Determine the average speed during the whole journey.
questions.explanation: Distance = 600 + 100 + 50 = 750 km and time = 12 + 1 + 2 = 15 hours, so the average speed is 750/15 = 50 km/h.

questions.text: There are 90 female members and 60 male members in a club. If the average age of female members is 35 years, and the average age of male members is 45 years, then find the average age (in years) of the whole club?
The radius of a cone is 5 cm and its slant height is 16 cm. It's total surface area (in cm²) will be:
questions.explanation: Total surface area = πr(l + r) = (22/7) × 5 × (16 + 5) = 22 × 5 × 3 = 330 cm².

questions.text: Ruby bought 20 buttons for Rs.1. How many buttons she must sell for Rs.1 in order to get a profit of 25%?
questions.explanation: Each button costs ₹1/20; with a 25% profit it must sell for ₹1.25/20 = ₹1/16, so 16 buttons for ₹1.

questions.text: A and B together can do a piece of the work in 50 hours, B and C together can do the same work in 75 hours and A and C together can do the same in 25 hours. Find the time in which A, B, and C together will complete the task.
questions.explanation: Adding the three pairs: 2(A + B + C) = 1/50 + 1/75 + 1/25 = (3 + 2 + 6)/150 = 11/150, so A + B + C do 11/300 of the work an hour and finish it in 300/11 hours.

questions.text: Find the difference between the greatest and the smallest 4-digit numbers exactly divisible by 36 and 48.
questions.explanation: LCM(36, 48) = 144. The greatest 4-digit multiple is 144 × 69 = 9936 and the smallest 144 × 7 = 1008; 9936 − 1008 = 8928.

questions.text: Robin travels one-fourth of the distance at 20 km/h, another one-fourth at 10 km/h, and the remaining distance at 80 km/h. Find Robin's average speed for the entire distance (correct to 2 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: Taking the distance as 4d, the time is d/20 + d/10 + 2d/80 = (4d + 8d + 2d)/80 = 14d/80. Average speed = 4d ÷ 14d/80 = 320/14 = 22.86 km/h.

questions.text: The marked price of an item was Rs. 100000, but the shopkeeper offered a double discount of 20 percent and 10 percent. At what price did he finally sell the item?
If 2³⁰⁵ + 303 is divided by 9, then the remainder is:
questions.explanation: 2⁶ = 64 leaves remainder 1 on division by 9 and 305 = 6 × 50 + 5, so 2³⁰⁵ leaves the same remainder as 2⁵ = 32, which is 5. 303 leaves 6 (its digit sum), and 5 + 6 = 11 leaves 2.

questions.text: The marked price on an item was Rs 2000/- but the shopkeeper offered a discount of 20 percent. How much did he finally sell the item for?
In how many years will ₹800 amount to ₹926.10 at 10% per annum, compounded half-yearly?
questions.explanation: Compounded half-yearly the rate is 5% a half-year: 800 × 1.05ⁿ = 926.10 gives 1.05ⁿ = 1.157625 = 1.05³, so n = 3 half-years, 1.5 years.

questions.text: If a + b = 25 and a – b = 7, then determine the mean proportion of a and b.
questions.explanation: a = (25 + 7)/2 = 16 and b = 9, so the mean proportional is √(16 × 9) = 12.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Compassionate
questions.explanation: 'Compassionate' means feeling pity and concern for others; its opposite is 'cruel'. 'Merciful' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence. An oxygen cylinder is used to deliver oxygen through the patient’s nasal “orifice”.
questions.explanation: An 'orifice' is an opening, such as the mouth or a nostril.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Feeble
questions.explanation: 'Feeble' means weak; its opposite is 'sturdy', strong and solidly built. 'Weak' is a synonym.

questions.text: The sentence below is divided into four segments. Select the option that has an error of tense. I has been / visiting my / family and relatives / during the winter vacation.
questions.explanation: The verb form is wrong: with 'I' the present perfect continuous takes 'have been', not 'has been': 'I have been visiting my family and relatives during the winter vacation.' The other segments are correct.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. My uncle has an “extremely large” bungalow which has six bedrooms, five bathrooms and four living rooms.
questions.explanation: 'Enormous' means extremely large, and it fits the article 'an' before it. 'Meagre' means scanty, 'great' would need 'a', and 'oversize' means bigger than the standard size.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. Siraj-ud Daula’s defeat can be attributed to “a snake in the grass”.
questions.explanation: A 'snake in the grass' is a deceitful person who pretends to be a friend. The idiom names any such person, not only a disloyal soldier.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the bracketed word to fill in the blank. The medicine was so __________ (sweet) that a man had to choose sugar along with it.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'sweet' is 'sour', which is why sugar was needed with the medicine. 'Rancid' and 'stale' describe food gone off and 'fetid' a foul smell.

questions.text: Select the option in which all the words are spelt correctly.
options: The sage preached that we are accountable to God in this life.
The sage preached that we are akountable to God in this life.
The sage preached that we are accuuntable to God in this life.
The sage preached that we are acountable to God in this life.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'accountable', with a double 'c' and 'ou'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He indeed is intelligent who ______ this and succeeds in making all work truly great.
questions.explanation: The verb must match 'succeeds', the simple present in the singular: 'notices'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Skulptor' is misspelt: the word is 'sculptor'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Ideal
questions.explanation: 'Ideal' means perfect, the best possible, which is closest to 'excellent'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. I visited the hospital to “enquire about eyes surgery”.
questions.explanation: A noun used to describe another noun stays singular: 'eye surgery', not 'eyes surgery'. 'Enquired' cannot follow 'to', and 'enquire for' takes the wrong preposition.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To call in question
questions.explanation: To 'call in question' is to cast doubt on something, that is to challenge it.

questions.text: Complete the sentence using correct pair of words from the options given. My brother _______ _______ apples during his fast.
questions.explanation: 'Ate', the past tense of 'eat', and 'eight', the number, sound alike: 'My brother ate eight apples during his fast.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. One certain benefit of online communication either through email or even communicating through WhatsApp nowadays is that there is a (1) ______ dependence on paper. It is said that to make a ton of paper 17 trees have to be cut down. With the already existing demand for paper to meet (2) _____ needs, it would be horrendous to keep (3) ______ the demand for paper worldwide. Online communication is a boon as many documents are now sent by mail through PDF, Microsoft Word or the JPEG format. This means that there is certainly a (4) _______ in the use of paper due to online communication. Many people read online newspapers nowadays, which means there is a decline in the number of people buying offline versions of (5) ________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Online communication means less use of paper, so there is 'less' dependence on it; 'restless', 'crest' and 'dress' make no sense here.
