questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. MUZHIK : KVXIGI :: QUACKY : OVYDIW :: ZEBECK : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move −2, +1, −2, +1, −2, −2: MUZHIK → KVXIGI and QUACKY → OVYDIW. So ZEBECK → XFZFAI (B − 2 wraps round to Z).

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘CLUTCH’ is written as ‘DNXXHN’ and ‘CREDIT’ is written as ‘DTHHNZ’. How will ‘WALLET’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves forward by its place in the word, +1 to +6: CLUTCH → DNXXHN and CREDIT → DTHHNZ. So WALLET → W+1, A+2, L+3, L+4, E+5, T+6 = XCOPJZ.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. HS, PK, XC, FU, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move 8 forward (H, P, X, F, N) and the second letters 8 back (S, K, C, U, M), wrapping round the alphabet: NM.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘COMBAT’ is written as ‘NPDVCD’ and 'CREATE' is written as 'FSDGVC'. How will ‘CREDIT’ be written as in that language?
questions.explanation: Each half of the word is reversed, then the first half moves +1 and the second +2: COM → MOC → NPD and BAT → TAB → VCD. So CRE → ERC → FSD and DIT → TID → VKF: FSDVKF.

questions.text: Select the option that represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in an English dictionary. 1. PURVEY 2. PURSE 3. PURPLE 4. PURELY 5. PUTTER 6. PUSTULE
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: Purely (4), Purple (3), Purse (2), Purvey (1), Pustule (6), Putter (5). 'Pure' comes before 'Purp', 'Purs' and 'Purv', and 'Pus' before 'Put'.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation. 14 * 1 * 15 * 75 * 21 = 30
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 5, 11, 23, 47, 95, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before plus 1: 5 × 2 + 1 = 11, 11 × 2 + 1 = 23 and so on, so 95 × 2 + 1 = 191.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All cans are dogs. Some dogs are rats. Some rats are apples. Conclusions: I. No cans are dogs. II. Some rats are not dogs. III. Some apples are rats.
questions.explanation: Some rats are apples, so some apples are rats: III follows. All cans are dogs, so I is false, and nothing places any rat outside the dogs, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Eight people, A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H are sitting in a straight line, facing north. Only three people sit to the left of A. B sits third to the right of A. Only four people sit between B and D. F sits to the immediate right of G. C does not sit at any of the extreme ends of the line. E sits at one of the positions to the right of H. How many people sit between H and A?
questions.explanation: A is 4th from the left and B 7th; D, with four people between it and B, is 2nd. G and F take 5th and 6th, the only adjacent seats left. C, not at an end, is 3rd, and E to the right of H puts H 1st and E 8th. D and C sit between H and A.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. DGS : PEC :: NST : QQM :: EHK : ?
questions.explanation: The letters are reversed and then moved −3, −2, −1: DGS → SGD → PEC and NST → TSN → QQM. So EHK → KHE → HFD.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? QCSD, ?, WGQZ, ZIPX, CKOV
questions.explanation: The first letters move +3 (Q, T, W, Z, C), the second +2 (C, E, G, I, K), the third −1 (S, R, Q, P, O) and the fourth −2 (D, B, Z, X, V): TERB.

questions.text: ‘P % Q’ means ‘P is the brother of Q’. ‘P + Q’ means ‘P is the daughter of Q’. ‘P = Q’ means ‘P is the son of Q’. ‘P # Q’ means ‘P is the wife of Q’. If A + B % C = D # F, how is F related to A?
questions.explanation: A is the daughter of B, B is the brother of C, C is the son of D, and D is the wife of F. So F is the father of C and B, and B is A's father: F is A's father's father.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 54 × 8 – 48 ÷ 12 + 27 = 24

Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (6, 135, 9) (13, 261, 16)
questions.explanation: The middle number is 9 times the sum of the outer two: (6 + 9) × 9 = 135 and (13 + 16) × 9 = 261. Likewise (7 + 17) × 9 = 216.

questions.text: Which of the following options will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 416, 341, 276, ?, 176, 141, 116

Eight people are sitting in two parallel rows with 4 people each, in such a way that there is equal distance between adjacent persons and people of one row are facing the people of other row. In Row I – 6, 7, 8 and 9 are seated and all of them are facing south. In Row II – 1, 2, 3 and 4 are seated and all of them are facing north. 9 sits next to the person at the extreme left end of their row and is exactly opposite 4. 3 sits at the extreme left end of their row and 2 is his immediate neighbour. Who sits at the extreme right end of the row facing North?
questions.explanation: Row II faces north, so its left end is the west end; Row I faces south, so its left end is the east end. 9 sits next to the east end of Row I, in the third seat from the west, with 4 opposite. 3 takes the west end of Row II and 2 the seat beside him, which leaves 1 at the east end, the right end of the row facing north.

questions.text: Who among the following personalities has won the Padma Shri for her contributions in Kathakali dance form in the year 2019?
questions.explanation: Milena Salvini, the Italian-born French dancer and teacher who co-founded the Centre Mandapa in Paris, received the Padma Shri in 2019 for her work for Kathakali. Shovana Narayan is a Kathak dancer, and Geeta Kapoor and Vaibhavi Merchant are film choreographers.

questions.text: Cow Dung is used in agriculture as a _______.
questions.explanation: Cow dung is used as manure, an organic fertiliser that returns nutrients and organic matter to the soil.

questions.text: In which city is the cricket stadium M Chinnaswamy located?
questions.explanation: The M. Chinnaswamy Stadium is in Bengaluru, Karnataka.

questions.text: In which of the following Parts of the Constitution of India are Fundamental Rights embodied?
questions.explanation: Part III of the Constitution (Articles 12 to 35) sets out the Fundamental Rights. Part IV holds the Directive Principles, Part I the Union and its territory, and Part II citizenship.

questions.text: Who among the following became Member of Legislative Assembly from Khairagarh, Chhattisgarh in India, in April 2022?
questions.explanation: Yashoda Verma of the Congress won the Khairagarh by-election, counted on 16 April 2022, which followed the death of the sitting MLA, Devwrat Singh.

questions.text: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the Jal Jeevan Mission in __________.
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the Jal Jeevan Mission, which aims to give every rural household a tap water connection, on 15 August 2019.

questions.text: On which festival does people of North India worship goddess Lakshmi and lord Ganesha together?
questions.explanation: At Diwali, Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth, and Ganesha, the remover of obstacles, are worshipped together in the Lakshmi Puja.

questions.text: Which means of transport is now being used to transfer crude oil, petroleum products and natural gas?
questions.explanation: Pipelines carry crude oil, petroleum products and natural gas from oil and gas fields to refineries, fertiliser factories and power plants.

questions.text: Which waterway connects the Atlantic Ocean with the Pacific Ocean?
questions.explanation: The Panama Canal, across the Isthmus of Panama, links the Atlantic and the Pacific. The Suez Canal links the Mediterranean with the Red Sea, and the Kiel Canal the North Sea with the Baltic.

questions.text: Which dancing legend was the youngest recipient of Padma Bhushan in 1992?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Sonal Mansingh, the Bharatanatyam and Odissi dancer, the only one of the four to receive the Padma Bhushan in 1992; her biographies describe her as the youngest recipient that year.

questions.text: According to the Article 243 of the Constitution of India, ________ means an institution of self-government constituted under article 243B, for the rural areas.
questions.explanation: Article 243(d) defines 'Panchayat' as an institution of self-government constituted under Article 243B for the rural areas.

questions.text: Lakshya Sen is a player of which sport?
questions.explanation: Lakshya Sen is a badminton player: he won the men's singles bronze at the 2021 World Championships and gold at the 2022 Commonwealth Games.

questions.text: What best describes bulimia?
questions.explanation: Bulimia (bulimia nervosa) is an eating disorder in which bouts of binge eating are followed by purging, such as making oneself vomit.

questions.text: Prior to the country’s independence, India was particularly known for its ____________ industries.
questions.explanation: Before independence India was well known for its handicraft industries, such as cotton and silk textiles and metal and precious-stone work, which declined under colonial rule.

questions.text: Which of the following organisations conducts the sample surveys for calculating poverty line in India?
questions.explanation: Poverty in India has been estimated from the household consumption expenditure surveys of the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO).

questions.text: Who has been appointed as the Director General of National Investigation Agency by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC) in June 2022?
questions.explanation: Dinkar Gupta, a 1987-batch IPS officer of the Punjab cadre and a former Punjab police chief, was appointed Director General of the NIA in June 2022.

questions.text: India accounts for how much of total world’s surface area?
questions.explanation: India's area, about 3.28 million sq km, is about 2.4% of the world's total geographical area.

questions.text: ______ spent a lot of time at Harshavardhana's court and left a detailed account of what he saw.
questions.explanation: The Chinese pilgrim Xuan Zang (Hiuen Tsang) spent years at Harshavardhana's court in the 7th century and wrote a detailed account of it. Faxian came in the time of Chandragupta II, and Yijing after Harsha's death.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year was Jhansi annexed by Lord Dalhousie under the policy Doctrine of Lapse?
questions.explanation: NCERT dates the states annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse as Satara (1848), Sambalpur (1850), Udaipur (1852), Nagpur (1853) and Jhansi (1854). Jhansi was taken after Raja Gangadhar Rao died without a natural heir.

questions.text: Find the smallest number divisible by the numbers 8, 16, 20 and 32.

Two trains, 140 m and 160 m in length, are running towards each other on parallel lines, one at the speed of 40 km/h and the other at 50 km/h. In how much time will they be clear of each other from the moment they meet?
questions.explanation: Running towards each other, the relative speed is 40 + 50 = 90 km/h = 25 m/s. They must cover 140 + 160 = 300 m: 300 ÷ 25 = 12 seconds.

questions.text: The average attendance at a cricket club dropped from 5640 last year to 3820 this year. What was the percent decrease from last year to this year?
A book is listed at Rs. 300, with a discount of 20 percent. What additional discount must be offered to bring the selling price to Rs. 216?
questions.explanation: After 20% off the price is 300 × 0.8 = ₹240. Bringing it to ₹216 takes off ₹24 more, which is 24/240 × 100 = 10%.

questions.text: The weight of a liquid varies directly with its volume. A liquid that weighs 12 kg has volume of 3 litres. What will be the weight of a liquid that has volume 4 litres?
questions.explanation: The liquid weighs 12 ÷ 3 = 4 kg a litre, so 4 litres weigh 4 × 4 = 16 kg.

questions.text: Arun bought a laptop from Sanchit for Rs.1,12,500. Sanchit earned a profit of 25% on the laptop. Raman sold the laptop to Sanchit at a gain of 20%. How much did Raman pay to buy the laptop?
questions.explanation: Sanchit's cost was ₹1,12,500 ÷ 1.25 = ₹90,000, the price Raman sold at. Raman gained 20%, so he paid ₹90,000 ÷ 1.2 = ₹75,000.

questions.text: A bus can run 20% faster than a bike. Both start from the same place at the same time and reach the same destination 60 km away at the same time. On the way, however, the bus stops at the stations for 10 minutes. The speed of the bike is:
questions.explanation: If the bike runs at v km/h, the bus runs at 1.2v and still arrives together after stopping 10 minutes (1/6 hour): 60/v − 60/(1.2v) = 1/6, so 10/v = 1/6 and v = 60 km/h.

questions.text: A can do a piece of work in 72 days and B in 90 days. They worked together for 30 days and then B left. Find the days taken by A to finish the remaining work.
questions.explanation: Together they do 1/72 + 1/90 = 9/360 = 1/40 of the work a day, so 30/40 = 3/4 of it in 30 days. A does the remaining 1/4 in 72 ÷ 4 = 18 days.

questions.text: A company offers three types of successive discounts: First offer: 25% and 5%, Second offer: 20% and 10%, Third offer: 15% and 15%. Which offer is the best for a customer?
questions.explanation: The single equivalent discounts are 1 − 0.75 × 0.95 = 28.75%, 1 − 0.8 × 0.9 = 28% and 1 − 0.85 × 0.85 = 27.75%, so the first offer takes off the most.

questions.text: If x is directly proportional to y and x = 10 when y = 8, then what is the value of x when y = 36?
questions.explanation: x/y stays constant: x = (10/8) × 36 = 45.

questions.text: A number is increased by 30% and then again increased by 30%. By what percentage should the increased number be reduced so as to get back the original number?
questions.explanation: After two 30% rises the number is 1.3 × 1.3 = 1.69 times the original, so it must lose 0.69 of 1.69: 0.69/1.69 × 100 = 40.828...%, which the option gives as 40.82%.

questions.text: If a shopkeeper mixes two types of pulses worth Rs.80 per kg and Rs.95 per kg, in the ratio 2:3, then what is the average cost of the mixture?
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Lonely' changes its 'y' to 'i' before '-ness': 'loneliness'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. Ultimately it turned out to be a “fair” decision.
questions.explanation: 'Fair' here means just and impartial: 'unbiased'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Due to increased international travel, the tourism sector has grown to be “a global tracker” to the global economy.
questions.explanation: The tourism sector adds a great deal to the world economy: it is 'a substantial contributor to' it. A 'tracker' follows things, which does not fit 'to the global economy'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. This day next year / I will having a conference with / the international board / discussing the environment.
options: I will having a conference with
questions.explanation: The future continuous needs 'be' after 'will': 'I will be having a conference with ...'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. In dire straits
questions.explanation: To be 'in dire straits' is to be in a very bad or difficult situation.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Drowsy
questions.explanation: 'Drowsy' means half asleep: 'sleepy'. 'Restive' means restless, and 'stimulant' and 'active' are near its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the italicised words in the given sentence. It was “a difficult task” to complete a relay run of 5 km in minutes yet our team managed to do it successfully.
questions.explanation: A 'Herculean effort' is one that needs great strength or determination. A 'kangaroo court' is an unfair trial, 'seeing pink elephants' is hallucinating from drink, and an 'Achilles heel' is a weak point.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Fatuity
questions.explanation: 'Fatuity' is foolishness; its opposite is 'sapience', wisdom. 'Folly' means the same as 'fatuity'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word to fill in the blank in the sentence. Procure It is very difficult to _________ food and fuel for daily necessities for people living below poverty line in the world.
questions.explanation: To 'procure' is to obtain, especially with some effort: it is difficult to obtain food and fuel.

questions.text: The sentence given below has one misspelt word. Spot the INCORRECTLY spelt word and select its correct spelling. The play depicts a futuristec society.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'futuristic', from 'future'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. Rapid deforestation may put the lives of many indigenous communities “in a danger.”
questions.explanation: 'Danger' is uncountable here and the fixed phrase takes no article: to put lives 'in danger'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Neglect
questions.explanation: 'Neglect' also means to fail to do something through carelessness or forgetting ('he neglected to lock the door'), so 'remember' is the option that runs against it. 'Slight', 'omit' and 'overlook' all mean much the same as 'neglect'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. In the olden days, when people went on pilgrimages, they created a feeling of belonging towards all, “convey” a message of brotherhood among all they came across.
questions.explanation: The participle 'conveying' adds what the pilgrims did as they created that feeling: 'they created a feeling of belonging towards all, conveying a message of brotherhood'. 'Conveyed' or 'have conveyed' would be a second main verb after a bare comma, which needs 'and', and 'has conveyed' does not agree with 'they'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks in the given sentence. The minister was supposed to ______ the gathering located at the ______ of Hotel Mao Inn.
questions.explanation: 'Address' fits both blanks: to address a gathering is to speak to it, and a hotel's address is where it is. 'Deliver' and 'speech' need other words ('deliver a speech'), and 'treat' does not suit the second blank.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks and make the sentence meaningful. My ________ intention was to have a good time in the excellent _______.
questions.explanation: 'Sole' means only, and 'weather' is the state of the air outside; 'soul' and 'whether' are words that sound the same but mean something else.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The beach is often (1) ________ to as nature's most (2) _______ tourist spot. Going to the beach allows you to take in all of nature's splendour, which includes a (3) _________ of (4) _________ sights. The beach is the perfect place where I can sit, relax and enjoy the (5) ________ and beautiful natural surroundings.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: A beach is 'referred to as' a tourist spot; 'called', 'named' and 'associated' do not go with 'to as'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The beach is often (1) ________ to as nature's most (2) _______ tourist spot. Going to the beach allows you to take in all of nature's splendour, which includes a (3) _________ of (4) _________ sights. The beach is the perfect place where I can sit, relax and enjoy the (5) ________ and beautiful natural surroundings.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'A plethora of' means a great many: 'a plethora of captivating sights'. 'A kind of' would need a singular noun, and 'view' and 'means' do not fit.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The beach is often (1) ________ to as nature's most (2) _______ tourist spot. Going to the beach allows you to take in all of nature's splendour, which includes a (3) _________ of (4) _________ sights. The beach is the perfect place where I can sit, relax and enjoy the (5) ________ and beautiful natural surroundings.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Captivating' (charming, delightful) suits sights that make up 'nature's splendour'; 'rare' clashes with 'a plethora of'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The beach is often (1) ________ to as nature's most (2) _______ tourist spot. Going to the beach allows you to take in all of nature's splendour, which includes a (3) _________ of (4) _________ sights. The beach is the perfect place where I can sit, relax and enjoy the (5) ________ and beautiful natural surroundings.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The beach is a place to sit and relax, so its surroundings are 'peaceful'. 'Polluted' clashes with 'beautiful', and 'cognizant' (aware) describes people.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 19, 21, 25, 33, ?, 81, 145
questions.explanation: The differences double: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64. So 33 + 16 = 49, and 49 + 32 = 81 checks.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. BQZJ, ELCM, HGFP, ? , NWLV
questions.explanation: The first, third and fourth letters move 3 forward (B, E, H, K, N; Z, C, F, I, L; J, M, P, S, V) and the second moves 5 back (Q, L, G, B, W): KBIS.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the * signs and to balance the given equation. 30 * 95 * 5 * 32 * 4 * 497
Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? ZTQM, YSPL, ?, WQNJ, VPMI
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 1 back from one term to the next: ZTQM, YSPL, XROK, WQNJ, VPMI.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 24 + 120 ÷ 8 × 16 – 48 = 36
questions.explanation: After interchanging ÷ and ×: 24 + 120 × 8 ÷ 16 − 48 = 24 + 60 − 48 = 36.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 7, 13, 28, 55, 112, ?
Select the option that is related to the fourth term in the same way as the first term is related to the second term and the fifth term is related to the sixth term. 8 : 6 :: ? : 12 :: 343 : 21
questions.explanation: Each pair is a cube and three times its cube root: 2³ = 8 and 2 × 3 = 6; 7³ = 343 and 7 × 3 = 21. Since 12 = 4 × 3, the missing term is 4³ = 64.

questions.text: Six students are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Vendyll is sitting fourth to the right of Leander. Michael is sitting third to the right of Vendyll. Gandhar is sitting second to the left of Michael. Yogita is sitting third to the right of Gandhar. Rocky is the immediate neighbour of Vendyll and Yogita. Who is sitting between Leander and Vendyll?
questions.explanation: Numbering the seats 1 to 6 to the right: Leander 1, Vendyll 5, Michael 2, Gandhar 6 and Yogita 3, leaving Rocky at 4, between Yogita and Vendyll. On the short side, only Gandhar sits between Leander and Vendyll.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must NOT be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Drum : Percussion :: Guitar : ________
questions.explanation: A drum is a percussion instrument, and a guitar is a string instrument.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘COVER’ is written as ‘18522153’ and ‘STINK’ is written as ‘111492019’. How will ‘PLATE’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as its place in the alphabet, in reverse order: COVER → R18 E5 V22 O15 C3 = 18522153 and STINK → K11 N14 I9 T20 S19 = 111492019. So PLATE → E5 T20 A1 L12 P16 = 52011216.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word) Sharp : blunt :: Dim : ?
questions.explanation: 'Blunt' is the opposite of 'sharp', and the opposite of 'dim' is 'bright'.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 chair 2 chain 3 charm 4 charge 5 charcoal
questions.explanation: 'Chain' comes before 'chair' (n before r); then come 'charcoal', 'charge' and 'charm' (c, g, m after 'char'): 2, 1, 5, 4, 3.

questions.text: ‘A @ B’ means ‘A is the son of B’; ‘A & B’ means ‘A is the mother of B’; ‘A # B’ means ‘A is the daughter of B’; Which of the following options means ‘Q is the wife of S'?
questions.explanation: P @ Q & R # S: P is Q's son, Q is R's mother and R is S's daughter. So Q and S are R's parents, and Q, the mother, is S's wife.

questions.text: Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No coats are pants. All pants are shirts. Some shirts are coats. Conclusions: I. No coats are shirts. II. Some shirts are pants. III. Some pants are coats.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: No coat is a pant, so III is false, and some shirts are coats, so I is false. All pants are shirts, so some shirts are pants: only II follows.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘RESPECT’ is written as ‘EECPRST’, ‘HONOUR’ is written as ‘OOUHNR’, how will ‘COURAGE’ be written as in that language?
questions.explanation: The vowels come first and then the consonants, each group in alphabetical order: RESPECT → EE + CPRST and HONOUR → OOU + HNR. So COURAGE → AEOU + CGR = AEOUCGR.

questions.text: Six persons Hema, Rekha, Jaya, Sushma, Nimmi and Barkha are sitting in a row facing north. Barkha is not sitting beside Jaya and jaya is sitting at the extreme right. Only Hema is sitting between Nimmi and Barkha. Nimmi is not sitting beside Sushma and Jaya. Only Rekha is sitting between Sushma and Jaya. Who is sitting to the immediate right of Barkha?
questions.explanation: Jaya is at the right end with Rekha next to her and Sushma next to Rekha. Hema sits between Nimmi and Barkha in the three seats left, and Nimmi is not beside Sushma, so from the left: Nimmi, Hema, Barkha, Sushma, Rekha, Jaya. Sushma is to Barkha's immediate right.

questions.text: The Council of States also known as _________.
questions.explanation: The Council of States is the Rajya Sabha, the upper house of Parliament; the House of the People is the Lok Sabha.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which university was established in 1857?
questions.explanation: The University of Bombay (now the University of Mumbai) was founded in 1857, together with the universities of Calcutta and Madras. Punjab University dates from 1882 and Allahabad University from 1887.

questions.text: Who among the following founded the Shunga dynasty?
questions.explanation: Pushyamitra Shunga, a general of the last Maurya king Brihadratha, overthrew him and founded the Shunga dynasty. Agnimitra was his son, and Devabhuti the last Shunga king.

questions.text: In India, the workforce population does NOT include people of _______.
questions.explanation: NCERT's Class IX economics counts the workforce population as people aged 15 to 59, so 14-year-olds are not included.

questions.text: As per Consumer Protection Rules, 2021, District Commissions shall have jurisdiction to entertain complaints where the value of the goods or services paid as consideration ______.
options: does not exceed ten lakh rupees
does not exceed fifty lakh rupees
does not exceed one lakh rupees
questions.explanation: Under the Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021, District Commissions hear complaints where the consideration paid does not exceed ₹50 lakh. State Commissions take ₹50 lakh to ₹2 crore, and the National Commission above ₹2 crore.

questions.text: Who has been appointed to the post of Executive Director for India at the International Monetary Fund (IMF) as announced in August 2022??
questions.explanation: In August 2022 the government named Krishnamurthy V. Subramanian, Chief Economic Adviser from 2018 to 2021, India's Executive Director at the IMF for three years from 1 November 2022, succeeding Surjit Bhalla.

questions.text: How many Fundamental Duties are mentioned in the Indian constitution? (As on May 2022)
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added ten Fundamental Duties in Article 51A and the 86th Amendment (2002) an eleventh, on giving children aged 6 to 14 opportunities for education.

questions.text: Rasheswar Saikia Barbayan is related with ______________ dance.
questions.explanation: Rasheswar Saikia Barbayan of Assam was a guru of Sattriya, the dance of Assam's Vaishnava monasteries (sattras); he received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for it in 1980.

questions.text: Which non-conventional energy source is/are available in India?
questions.explanation: India has all three: wind and solar power on a large scale, and tidal energy potential in the Gulfs of Khambhat and Kutch and in the Sundarbans.

questions.text: Who among the following is the founder of the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Yunus founded the Grameen Bank, a pioneer of small loans to the rural poor, and shared the 2006 Nobel Peace Prize with it.

questions.text: The chemical name of the acid present in vinegar is called ______.
questions.explanation: Vinegar is a dilute (about 5-8%) solution of acetic acid, also called ethanoic acid.

questions.text: The hot weather season is also the season for localised thunderstorms, associated with violent winds, torrential downpours, often accompanied by hail. In West Bengal, these storms are known as the ______.
questions.explanation: The violent evening thunderstorms of the hot season in Bengal and Assam, the nor'westers, are called 'kaal baisakhi', the calamity of the month of Baisakh. The loo is the hot, dry wind of the northern plains.

questions.text: Which political leader from Jammu and Kashmir, India started a 3-day visit to Kishtwar-Doda belt in November 2022?
questions.explanation: Ghulam Nabi Azad, a former Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir, began a three-day outreach visit to the Doda and Kishtwar districts in late November 2022. He had left the Congress in August 2022 and launched his Democratic Azad Party in September 2022.

questions.text: ______ ≡ Sum total of gross value added of all the firms in the economy
questions.explanation: Adding up the gross value added (output minus intermediate goods) of every firm in the economy gives GDP. GNP adds net factor income from abroad, and NNP then subtracts depreciation.

questions.text: The South Asian Games was first held in which year?
questions.explanation: The South Asian Federation (SAF) Games, now the South Asian Games, were first held in Kathmandu, Nepal, in 1984.

questions.text: Thrissur Pooram festival It is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Thrissur Pooram, with its caparisoned elephants and the Kudamattam display of parasols, is held at the Vadakkunnathan temple in Thrissur, Kerala.

questions.text: Vitamin C is an ______.
questions.explanation: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is an antioxidant: it protects cells from damage by free radicals.

questions.text: The horizontal rows of squares in chess are called _______.
questions.explanation: In chess the horizontal rows are ranks (numbered 1 to 8) and the vertical columns are files (a to h).

questions.text: Which of the following can be considered as a major hub of Information Technology industry in India?
questions.explanation: Bengaluru, India's leading centre of information technology firms, is often called the country's Silicon Valley.

questions.text: Find the mean proportional between 3 and 27.
questions.explanation: Mean proportional = √(3 × 27) = √81 = 9.

questions.text: A thief steals a car at 3:30 p.m. and drives it at 80km/h. The theft is discovered at 4:00 p.m. and the owner sets off in another car at 90km/h. When will he catch the thief?
questions.explanation: By 4:00 p.m. the thief is 80 × ½ = 40 km ahead. The owner gains 90 − 80 = 10 km/h, so he catches up in 40 ÷ 10 = 4 hours, at 8:00 p.m.

questions.text: The average age of 14 students and their teacher is 20 years. If the teacher is excluded, then their average age reduces by 1.5 years. The teacher’s age is:
questions.explanation: All 15 together total 15 × 20 = 300 years. Without the teacher the 14 students average 18.5, a total of 259, so the teacher is 300 − 259 = 41.

questions.text: The HCF of 1020, 850 and 1156 is:
How much time does Rani take to cover a distance of 200 m, if she runs at a speed of 15 km/h?
questions.explanation: 15 km/h = 15 × 5/18 = 25/6 m/s, so the time is 200 × 6/25 = 48 seconds.

questions.text: Aman covers a distance of 15 km in 3 hours and a distance of 20 km in 2 hours. What is the average speed of Aman?
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = (15 + 20) ÷ (3 + 2) = 35 ÷ 5 = 7 km/h.

questions.text: S can complete a task in 50 days, T can complete it in 40 days and M can complete it in 30 days. S can work on all days of the week; T can work only on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday while M can work only on Saturday and Sunday. The work is started on Monday. In how many weeks it will be completed?
questions.explanation: Take the work as 600 units: S does 12 a day, T 15 and M 20. A week gives 7 × 12 + 3 × 15 + 2 × 20 = 169 units, so 507 after 3 weeks. In the fourth week Monday to Friday add 27 + 12 + 27 + 12 + 27 = 105: the total is 585 after Thursday and 612 on Friday, so the work ends during the fourth week.

questions.text: A bat is bought for Rs.750 and sold at a loss of 8%. What is its selling price?
Successive discounts of 13 percent and 19 percent are equivalent to a single discount of :

The ratio of the cost price to the marked price of a table is 3:4. The shopkeeper gives two equal successive discounts of 25% on the marked price and sells the table for Rs.2,250. Find the loss during this transaction.
Divide the LCM of the 35 and 42 by the HCF of 32 and 40.
Find the mean proportional between 9 and 25.
questions.explanation: Mean proportional = √(9 × 25) = √225 = 15.

questions.text: In how many years will Rs.12,500 become Rs.21,600 at the rate of 20% per annum on compound interest when interest is compounding annually?

Under simple rate of growth, the population (P units) of a city becomes 1.5 times of P in 10 years. In how many years, the population of the city would become double (2 times P) under the same growth rate?
questions.explanation: Simple growth adds 0.5P in 10 years, or 0.05P a year. Doubling means adding P in all, which takes P ÷ 0.05P = 20 years.

questions.text: During the first year, the population of a city increased by 5% and during the second year, it diminished by 4%. At the end of the second year, its population was 30,240. The population at the end of the first year was:
questions.explanation: The second year's 4% fall left 30,240, so the population at the end of the first year was 30,240 ÷ 0.96 = 31,500.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank with the synonym of the underlined word. The film was a “funny” adaption of an old classic. The ________ depiction was well received by the audience.
questions.explanation: 'Humorous' means funny: a funny adaptation is a humorous depiction. 'Trendy', 'nervous' and 'tropical' have other meanings.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in the brackets to fill in the blank. She is a direct _________ (ancestor) of Queen Victoria.
questions.explanation: A descendant comes later in a family line, the opposite of an ancestor: 'a direct descendant of Queen Victoria'. 'Primogenitor', 'antecedent' and 'forerunner' are close to 'ancestor'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Steal someone’s thunder
options: To follow a successful person’s instructions
To take the credit for something someone else did
To find it difficult to choose between two alternatives
questions.explanation: To 'steal someone's thunder' is to take the credit or attention that someone else's work or idea deserved.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Conviction
questions.explanation: A conviction is a firmly held belief; 'doubt' and 'suspicion' are nearly its opposites.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. Johnson wrote a drama in which he discusses the “study of chemistry in a medieval fashion”.
questions.explanation: Alchemy, the medieval forerunner of chemistry, sought among other things to turn base metals into gold. Rhetoric is the art of persuasive speech, lexicography the making of dictionaries and anthropology the study of humankind.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'curriculum', with a double 'r'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. The talk was not “understandable” .
questions.explanation: 'Understandable' (able to be understood) already fits the sentence, so no substitution is needed: 'comprehensible' only means the same, 'comprehended' is a past participle and 'comprehensive' means complete or wide-ranging.

questions.text: Select the correct pair of words for the blanks in the given sentence. Jharkhand is a major ________ producing state in India whereas the union territory of Jammu & Kashmir is a ________ place.
questions.explanation: Jharkhand is a leading coal-producing state, and Jammu & Kashmir is known for its cold climate: 'coal; cold'.

questions.text: Select the correct idiom that can substitute the italicised group of words in the given sentence. Soma has “made a mess of” her financial affairs.
options: made a mountain out of a molehill
questions.explanation: To 'make a hash of' something is to do it badly, to make a mess of it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. William couldn’t stop _____________ against the comments of the officer.
questions.explanation: To 'react against' something is to respond to it with opposition. 'Respond' takes 'to', not 'against', and 'opening' and 'starting' do not fit the sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Just
questions.explanation: 'Just' means fair and right, so its opposite is 'unfair'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The technician has found it / extremely difficult to fix / the error in the programme.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: 'it' stands for 'to fix the error' after 'found', the present perfect 'has found' suits a singular subject, and 'programme' is the British spelling.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence. He and his family members live in “prosperity”.
questions.explanation: 'Prosperity' is the state of being wealthy and successful, so 'richness' is closest. 'Poverty' and 'hardship' are its opposites, and a loft is a room under a roof.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. They found it difficult to extract “relevent” information from the officer.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'relevant'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Why does a person become overconfident? The reason lies in over assessment of his capabilities. Sometimes people over assess their (1) _________ and jump into situations that are beyond their control. Napoleon Bonaparte who became Emperor of France would say that the word ‘impossible’ was common only (2) _______ fools. The overconfident Napoleon invaded Russia in the winter of 1812. This proved to be a big disaster. Overconfidence generally (3) ______ people into misadventures, endangering their chances in life. It is wisely said that any achievement is a result of two factors – one’s personal planning and support from the external world. People take into account only their planning, generally ignoring external factors. As a result they are unable to (4) ________ future developments. Hence, a great risk of failure. Then there is the question: how can one manage overconfidence? The formula is very simple. Before making a decision, discuss the matter with other informed people with an objective mind and when it is proved that you are about to go off the path, accept reality and say without delay, “I was wrong”. Overconfidence is a (5) ________ characterising people who lack the virtue of modesty. Modesty makes you a realist; you become a person who is cut down to size. People of this kind become very cautious; before taking an action they assess the whole situation. They adopt a realistic approach.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: People over-assess their 'competence', their ability, as the passage's 'over assessment of his capabilities' says.
