questions.text: Select the correct combination of mathematical signs to sequentially replace the % signs and to balance the given equation. 48 % 12 % 5 % 5 % 4
questions.explanation: After replacing the signs in order: 48 ÷ 12 × 5 = 5 × 4, as both sides equal 20.

questions.text: In a certain code language, BRAVE is coded as 48, and SPEAR is coded as 59. How will VICTOR be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded as the sum of its letters' places in the alphabet: BRAVE = 2 + 18 + 1 + 22 + 5 = 48 and SPEAR = 19 + 16 + 5 + 1 + 18 = 59. So VICTOR = 22 + 9 + 3 + 20 + 15 + 18 = 87.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed) (11, 20, 341); (25, 33, 638)
questions.explanation: The third number is 11 times the sum of the first two: (11 + 20) × 11 = 341 and (25 + 33) × 11 = 638. Likewise (12 + 32) × 11 = 484.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? XEJT, UHMQ, ?, ONSK, LQVH
questions.explanation: The first and fourth letters move back 3 (X, U, R, O, L and T, Q, N, K, H) and the second and third move forward 3 (E, H, K, N, Q and J, M, P, S, V): RKPN.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: All notebooks are pink. All pinks are shirts. Some shirts are trousers. Conclusions: I. All trousers are notebooks. II. Some trousers are pink.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: All notebooks are pink and all pinks are shirts, but only some shirts are trousers, so nothing ties trousers to pinks or notebooks: neither conclusion has to be true.

questions.text: A # B means ‘A is the brother of B’; A @ B means ‘A is the daughter of B’; A & B means ‘A is the husband of B’; A % B means ‘A is the wife of B’; A * B means ‘A is the son of B’; If M*G@K@B%A*W, then how is A related to G?
questions.explanation: M is the son of G, G the daughter of K, K the daughter of B, B the wife of A and A the son of W. B and A are K's parents, and K is G's mother, so A is G's mother's father.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘TRAVEL’ is written as ‘156’, ‘PERSON’ is written as ‘174’, how will ‘ALMOND’ be written as in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded as twice the sum of its letters' places in the alphabet: TRAVEL = 2 × 78 = 156 and PERSON = 2 × 87 = 174. ALMOND = 1 + 12 + 13 + 15 + 14 + 4 = 59, so it is 2 × 59 = 118.

questions.text: Six candidates Anand, Balu, Charan, Dinesh, Emran and Farhad were seated on a circular table for group discussion at equal distance, facing the centre of the circle. Dinesh is the immediate neighbour of Emran and Balu while Charan is the immediate neighbour of Anand and Farhad. If Farhad is to the immediate right of Balu, then who is on the immediate right of Dinesh?
questions.explanation: Dinesh sits between Emran and Balu, and Charan between Anand and Farhad; Farhad, on Balu's immediate right, joins the two groups. Going round to the right the order is Emran, Dinesh, Balu, Farhad, Charan, Anand, so Balu is on Dinesh's immediate right.

questions.text: Six friends (P, Q, R, S, T and U) are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. P sits second to the right of U. R sits third to the right of Q. S and R both are the immediate neighbours of P. Who sits between Q and P?
questions.explanation: Counting seats to the right of U, P is second, so its neighbours S and R take the first and third. R sits opposite Q (third to its right); if R took the third seat, Q would need U's seat, so R is first, S third, Q fourth and T fifth. S sits between Q and P.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? AKED, ENGE, ?, MTKG, QWMH
questions.explanation: The first letters move +4 (A, E, I, M, Q), the second +3 (K, N, Q, T, W), the third +2 (E, G, I, K, M) and the fourth +1 (D, E, F, G, H): IQIF.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 50, 60, 51, 62, 54, 66, 59, 72, ?
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 60, 62, 66, 72 rise by 2, 4, 6, and 50, 51, 54, 59 by 1, 3, 5, so the next term is 59 + 7 = 66.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. EXPLAIN : AEILNPX :: MEDICAL : AEICDLM :: PRIVACY : ?
questions.explanation: The vowels come first and then the consonants, each group in alphabetical order: EXPLAIN → AEI + LNPX and MEDICAL → AEI + CDLM. So PRIVACY → AI + CPRVY: AICPRVY.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Bread 2 Brain 3 Break 4 Broom 5 Bridge
questions.explanation: Brain (bra-) comes first; Bread and Break share 'brea', and d comes before k; Bridge (bri-) and Broom (bro-) follow: 2, 1, 3, 5, 4.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 112 - 14 ÷ 40 + 8 × 12 = 64
questions.explanation: After interchanging ÷ and −: 112 ÷ 14 − 40 + 8 × 12 = 8 − 40 + 96 = 64.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. DOWN: VKCL:: ARMY: YHMA :: HOME:?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by the letter whose place in the alphabet is 26 minus its own: D (4) → V (22), O (15) → K (11), W (23) → C (3), N (14) → L (12), and likewise ARMY → YHMA. So HOME → R (18), K (11), M (13), U (21): RKMU.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 23, 24, 50, 153, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is the one before times n plus n, for n = 1, 2, 3, 4: 23 × 1 + 1 = 24, 24 × 2 + 2 = 50, 50 × 3 + 3 = 153 and 153 × 4 + 4 = 616.

questions.text: __________ (NPS) is a voluntary, defined contribution retirement savings scheme to enable the subscribers to make optimum decisions regarding their future through systematic savings.
questions.explanation: NPS is the National Pension System, regulated by the Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA): subscribers contribute through their working life to build savings for retirement.

questions.text: ‘Gonph’ dance is a famous folk dance of which state?
questions.explanation: Goff (also spelt Gonph) is a folk dance of Goa performed at the Shigmo festival: dancers holding coloured cords tied to a central point weave them into a braid and then undo it.

questions.text: Which of the following is not an essential Qualification for the candidature of President?
options: Qualified for election as a member of the House of the People
questions.explanation: Under Article 58 a candidate for President must be a citizen of India, have completed 35 years of age and be qualified for election as a member of the House of the People (Lok Sabha). No educational qualification is laid down.

questions.text: In India, the responsibility of conducting the decadal census rests with which ministry?
questions.explanation: The census is conducted under the Census Act, 1948 by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India, which comes under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

questions.text: Identify the third layer of soil from top.
questions.explanation: From the top, a soil profile has the top soil, the sub soil, the substratum of weathered parent rock material and, at the bottom, the unweathered parent bedrock.

questions.text: The Hemis festival is predominantly celebrated in ________.
questions.explanation: The Hemis festival is held at Hemis Monastery in Ladakh to mark the birth anniversary of Guru Padmasambhava, with masked Cham dances.

questions.text: Which five year plan was running in India during the 1971 Indo-Pak war?
questions.explanation: The Fourth Five Year Plan ran from 1969 to 1974, so the war of December 1971 fell within it.

questions.text: In India, the first phase of the green revolution was from mid ______ upto mid ______.
questions.explanation: NCERT dates the first phase of the green revolution from about the mid-1960s to the mid-1970s, when high-yielding seeds were used mainly in the richer states and for wheat; the second phase ran from the mid-1970s to the mid-1980s.

questions.text: The Asian Games 2018 was held in which of the following country?
questions.explanation: The 2018 Asian Games were held in Jakarta and Palembang, Indonesia.

questions.text: Aparna Satheesan was honoured with the prestigious Bharata Shastra Nritya Praveena National Award for her outstanding performance in which dance form?
questions.explanation: Aparna Satheesan, a US-based classical dancer, was given the Bharata Shastra Nritya Praveena National Award in November 2021, at a festival held by the All India Dancer's Association in Bhilai, for her performances in Kuchipudi.

questions.text: What is the diameter and weight of the discus used in a discus thrown in Men's category?
questions.explanation: The men's discus weighs 2 kg and is about 22 cm (219-221 mm) across; the women's weighs 1 kg.

questions.text: In 2019, with ______ million tonnes of crude steel production, India ranked 2nd among the world crude steel producers.
questions.explanation: By World Steel Association figures India produced about 111 million tonnes of crude steel in 2019, second only to China.

questions.text: Which among the following elements has atomic number 33?
questions.explanation: Arsenic has atomic number 33. Neon's is 10, iodine's 53 and barium's 56.

questions.text: The __________ has the sole authority to issue banknotes in India.
questions.explanation: Under Section 22 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, the RBI has the sole right to issue banknotes in India; one-rupee notes and coins are issued by the Government.

questions.text: Who has been appointed as Vice Chairman of NITI AAYOG from 1 May 2022?
questions.explanation: The economist Suman Bery took over as Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog on 1 May 2022, succeeding Rajiv Kumar, and held the post when the exam was held (January 2023).

questions.text: As the Mauryan empire was so large, different parts were ruled differently. The area around ______ was under the direct control of the emperor.
questions.explanation: The emperor ruled the area around the capital, Pataliputra, directly; other areas were ruled from provincial capitals such as Taxila and Ujjain.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: To defend the Khalifa's temporal powers, a Khilafat Committee was formed in Bombay in ______.
questions.explanation: A Khilafat Committee was formed in Bombay in March 1919 to defend the Ottoman Khalifa's temporal powers; the Ali brothers, Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali, led the movement.

questions.text: Which of the following pair of cell - shape is correct? I. Red blood cells - Spherical shape; II. Muscle cells - Spindle shape
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives both, as NCERT's Class 8 science book shows human red blood cells as spherical and muscle cells as spindle-shaped. (Strictly, a red blood cell is a biconcave disc, so only II is exact.)

questions.text: Which of the following duties was NOT added by the 42nd amendment to the Indian Constitution?
options: To provide opportunities for education to one’s child or ward between the ages of six and fourteen years
To value and preserve the rich heritage of the country’s composite culture
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
questions.explanation: The duty to provide opportunities for education to one's child between six and fourteen (Article 51A(k)) was added by the 86th Amendment in 2002. The other three are among the ten duties the 42nd Amendment added in 1976.

questions.text: Who was approved as the non-executive part time chairman of Yes Bank by Reserve Bank of India in September 2022?
questions.explanation: In September 2022 the RBI approved Rama Subramaniam Gandhi, a former RBI Deputy Governor, as Yes Bank's non-executive part-time chairman for three years.

questions.text: Ankita bought some toys at 10 percent discount on the original price. The original price of each toy was Rs. 50. If she made a total savings of Rs. 450, then how many toys did she buy?
questions.explanation: Each toy was 10% of ₹50 = ₹5 cheaper, so a saving of ₹450 means 450 ÷ 5 = 90 toys.

questions.text: A cyclist and a jogger cover a certain distance at a certain speed. If the jogger covers one-third of the distance covered by cyclist in double of the time as that taken by the cyclist, the ratio of the speed of the jogger to that of the cyclist is:
questions.explanation: Speed is distance over time: the jogger covers 1/3 of the distance in twice the time, so his speed is (1/3) ÷ 2 = 1/6 of the cyclist's: 1 : 6.

questions.text: A woman buys an item for Rs.950 and sells it for Rs.1,150. What is her percentage profit (rounded off to the nearest integer)?

On an item, a shopkeeper offers a discount of 7.5% on the marked price and a cashback of ₹10 per item. He still earns ₹5 per item. If ₹x is the marked price of each item, then, what is the cost price (in ₹) of each item?
questions.explanation: After the discount and the cashback he receives 0.925x − 10. A profit of ₹5 on that means the cost price is 0.925x − 10 − 5 = 0.925x − 15.

questions.text: The expenditure of a man is 70% of his income. If his income will successively increase by 20% and 50%, then his new expenditures is how much percentage more/less than his previous expenditure, so that his new savings become 2.5 times of the previous savings?
questions.explanation: Take an income of 100: expenditure 70, savings 30. The new income is 100 × 1.2 × 1.5 = 180 and the new savings 2.5 × 30 = 75, so the new expenditure is 105, which is (105 − 70)/70 × 100 = 50% more.

questions.text: A bicyclist travels 20 miles in 2 h and 30 min and 10 miles in 1 h 15 min. Find the average speed in miles per hour.
questions.explanation: 30 miles in 2 h 30 min + 1 h 15 min = 3.75 h: 30 ÷ 3.75 = 8 miles per hour.

questions.text: Sakshi and Komal together can complete a work in 10 days. Komal can complete the same work in 22 days. They started working together but Sakshi left the work after 3 days and Komal completed the remaining work alone. Find the total number of days in which the work is completed.
questions.explanation: Together they do 1/10 of the work a day, so 3/10 in 3 days. Komal does the remaining 7/10 alone in 7/10 × 22 = 15.4 days, so the total is 3 + 15.4 = 18.4 = 92/5 days.

questions.text: A bank offers compound interest at the rate of 10% per annum when interest is compounded half-yearly. A customer deposits Rs.3,200 each on 1st January and 1st July of a year. At the end of the year, what will be the amount received by customer as interest?
questions.explanation: Half-yearly the rate is 5%. The January deposit earns for two half-years: 3,200 × 1.05² = ₹3,528; the July deposit for one: 3,200 × 1.05 = ₹3,360. Interest = 3,528 + 3,360 − 6,400 = ₹488.

questions.text: What is the difference between compound interests on ₹5,000 compounded yearly and half-yearly for 1 year at 4% per annum?
questions.explanation: Yearly: 5,000 × 4% = ₹200. Half-yearly, at 2% for two periods: 5,000 × (1.02² − 1) = 5,000 × 0.0404 = ₹202. The difference is ₹2.00.

questions.text: A fast local train takes 30 minutes less than a slow local train for a journey of 60 km. If the speed of the slow local train is 20 km/h less than the speed of the fast local train, what is the speed of the slow local train?
questions.explanation: With the slow train at v km/h, 60/v − 60/(v + 20) = 1/2 h, so 1,200/[v(v + 20)] = 1/2 and v(v + 20) = 2,400, giving v = 40 km/h.

questions.text: A person travels from one place to another at 180 km/h and returns to the starting point by the same route at 240 km/h. If the total time taken is 6 h, then find the distance between two places.

The length, breadth and the height of a cuboid are 24 cm, 18 cm and 12 cm respectively. It is melted to make smaller cubes. If the length of the side of the cube is 6 cm, then what is the number of cubes formed?
The numbers 73, 115 and 185 are divided a by number to leave the same remainder. Find the greater possible such number.
questions.explanation: The divisor must divide the differences 115 − 73 = 42, 185 − 115 = 70 and 185 − 73 = 112, so the greatest is HCF(42, 70, 112) = 14; each number leaves remainder 3.

questions.text: As shopkeeper using a faulty weight while professes to sell the article at cost price and gains a profit of 25%. Find the faulty weight he uses for 1000 g.
questions.explanation: To gain 25% while charging the cost price, he must hand over goods worth 100/125 of what he is paid for: 1,000 × 100/125 = 800 g.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in future tense form. We were holding the things with a strong rope.
options: We will be holding the things with a strong rope.
We have been holding the things with a strong rope.
We were being holding the things with a strong rope.
We are holding the things with a strong rope.
questions.explanation: The past continuous 'were holding' becomes the future continuous 'will be holding' in the future tense.

questions.text: Select the correct word for the blanks in the given sentence. A _________ is a nocturnal animal and a _________ is needed for the game of cricket.
questions.explanation: 'Bat' fits both blanks: a bat is a nocturnal flying mammal, and a bat is what the batter uses in cricket.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Her face was _____ after seeing the house in such condition.
questions.explanation: After 'was' the blank needs an adjective: 'blue', here meaning sad or downcast. 'Blew' is the past tense of 'blow', and 'bedew' (to wet with drops) and 'brew' are verbs.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. She “has barely made it” to the airport, when she heard the news of her dad’s accident.
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect, and 'barely ... when' ties it to the simple past 'heard': 'She had barely made it to the airport when she heard the news.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate set of words to complete the sentence. I want to see the Dussehra ___________ in Delhi, what is the second-class railway ______ from Agra to Delhi.
questions.explanation: A 'fair' is a festive gathering with stalls and shows, and a 'fare' is the price of a journey: the Dussehra fair, the railway fare.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Flash in the pan
options: Someone who helps others when they are in need, with no discussion for compensation, and no thought of a reward
Something that looks promising in the beginning but fails to deliver anything in the end
Not willing or wanting to change from your normal way of doing something
A place where people gather to buy and sell inexpensive goods
questions.explanation: A 'flash in the pan' is a sudden show of promise or success that comes to nothing.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Autonomy
questions.explanation: 'Autonomy' is the freedom to govern or manage oneself; its opposite is 'dependency', reliance on others.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Your health could suffer if you spend more time “with the automobiles”.
questions.explanation: Health suffers from too much screen time, that is time spent 'in front of electronic devices'. 'In backlog of' is not a phrase, 'besides' means 'in addition to', and one does not spend time 'after' devices.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Compact
questions.explanation: 'Compact' means closely packed together: 'dense'. 'Expand' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Go the extra mile
questions.explanation: To 'go the extra mile' is to make more effort than is expected or required.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. Prince Charles became “a youngest heir to the throne” at the age of seven.
options: the youngest heir to an throne
the youngest heir to the throne
a youngest heir to a throne
questions.explanation: A superlative such as 'youngest' takes 'the', and the throne meant is a particular one: 'the youngest heir to the throne'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Insipid
questions.explanation: 'Insipid' means lacking flavour (or interest), so its opposite is 'tasty'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'phenomenon'.

questions.text: Identify and correct the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. The flovers in the garden seemed as if they refused to bloom for spraying pesticides on them.
questions.explanation: 'Flovers' is misspelt; the word is 'flowers'. 'Pesticides', 'bloom' and 'refused' are already spelt correctly in the sentence.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word from the given options. The “benevolent” lady donated her estate for the welfare of the city.
questions.explanation: 'Benevolent' means kind and generous; 'gracious', kind and courteous, is closest. 'Charming' means pleasing, not kind.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The most common health conditions (1)_______ people today include heart disease, stroke, diabetes, and cancer. When people are experiencing these conditions, they (2)_________ the illness side of the spectrum. Lifestyle factors that put you at risk for developing these conditions include smoking, alcohol substance use disorder, lack of exercise, sleep (3)________, and a diet rich in processed foods, sugar, saturated fat, and artificial flavours. An (4)______ weight is another factor that can put one at risk for these conditions, especially carrying extra weight (5)______ your midsection.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 1.
questions.explanation: The conditions 'facing' people today are the ones they have to deal with. 'Looking' would need 'at', and 'towards' and 'against' make no sense here.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The most common health conditions (1)_______ people today include heart disease, stroke, diabetes, and cancer. When people are experiencing these conditions, they (2)_________ the illness side of the spectrum. Lifestyle factors that put you at risk for developing these conditions include smoking, alcohol substance use disorder, lack of exercise, sleep (3)________, and a diet rich in processed foods, sugar, saturated fat, and artificial flavours. An (4)______ weight is another factor that can put one at risk for these conditions, especially carrying extra weight (5)______ your midsection.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 2.
questions.explanation: People with these conditions 'fall into' the illness side of the spectrum, that is they belong to it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The most common health conditions (1)_______ people today include heart disease, stroke, diabetes, and cancer. When people are experiencing these conditions, they (2)_________ the illness side of the spectrum. Lifestyle factors that put you at risk for developing these conditions include smoking, alcohol substance use disorder, lack of exercise, sleep (3)________, and a diet rich in processed foods, sugar, saturated fat, and artificial flavours. An (4)______ weight is another factor that can put one at risk for these conditions, especially carrying extra weight (5)______ your midsection.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 3.
questions.explanation: 'Sleep deprivation', not getting enough sleep, is the usual phrase for this risk; 'poverty' and 'impoverishment' are about money.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The most common health conditions (1)_______ people today include heart disease, stroke, diabetes, and cancer. When people are experiencing these conditions, they (2)_________ the illness side of the spectrum. Lifestyle factors that put you at risk for developing these conditions include smoking, alcohol substance use disorder, lack of exercise, sleep (3)________, and a diet rich in processed foods, sugar, saturated fat, and artificial flavours. An (4)______ weight is another factor that can put one at risk for these conditions, especially carrying extra weight (5)______ your midsection.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 4.
questions.explanation: 'An unhealthy weight' is the risk factor; 'unhygienic' and 'contaminated' describe dirt, and 'empirical' means based on observation.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The most common health conditions (1)_______ people today include heart disease, stroke, diabetes, and cancer. When people are experiencing these conditions, they (2)_________ the illness side of the spectrum. Lifestyle factors that put you at risk for developing these conditions include smoking, alcohol substance use disorder, lack of exercise, sleep (3)________, and a diet rich in processed foods, sugar, saturated fat, and artificial flavours. An (4)______ weight is another factor that can put one at risk for these conditions, especially carrying extra weight (5)______ your midsection.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 5.
questions.explanation: Extra weight carried 'around' the midsection is fat round the waist.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. YOUR: XPEJ :: TONE: SPLW :: BANK: ?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves 1 back and the second 1 forward; the third becomes the letter before its opposite (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on) and the fourth the letter after its opposite: YOUR → X P E J (U↔F, F − 1 = E; R↔I, I + 1 = J) and TONE → S P L W. So BANK → A B L Q (N↔M, M − 1 = L; K↔P, P + 1 = Q): ABLQ.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. COMFORT : OCFMTRO :: CONTROL : OCTNLOR :: DIGITAL : ?
questions.explanation: The word is split into two pairs and a group of three; each pair is swapped and the three are reversed: CO MF ORT → OC FM TRO and CO NT ROL → OC TN LOR. So DI GI TAL → ID IG LAT: IDIGLAT.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘cart light’ is coded as ‘straw handle’, ‘plug light’ is coded as ‘toes handle’, and ‘cart plug’ is coded as ‘toes straw’. What is the code word for ‘cart’?
questions.explanation: 'Cart' is in the first and third messages, and 'straw' is the only code word common to both. ('Light' is 'handle' and 'plug' is 'toes'.)

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 1, 6, 31, 156, ? , 3906
questions.explanation: Each term is 5 times the one before plus 1: 156 × 5 + 1 = 781, and 781 × 5 + 1 = 3906.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 72 × 6 + 18 ÷ 5 - 9 = 93
questions.explanation: After interchanging × and ÷: 72 ÷ 6 + 18 × 5 − 9 = 12 + 90 − 9 = 93.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 33, 47, 44, 58, 56, 70, 69, ?

Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed) (20, 30, 450); (35, 25, 540)
questions.explanation: The third number is 9 times the sum of the first two: (20 + 30) × 9 = 450 and (35 + 25) × 9 = 540. Likewise (7 + 18) × 9 = 225.

questions.text: In a certain code language, FORCE is coded as 47, and GREEN is coded as 49. How will FLAVOUR be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word's code is the sum of its letters' places in the alphabet: FORCE = 6 + 15 + 18 + 3 + 5 = 47 and GREEN = 7 + 18 + 5 + 5 + 14 = 49. So FLAVOUR = 6 + 12 + 1 + 22 + 15 + 21 + 18 = 95.

questions.text: Six people are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Kaya is the immediate neighbour of Jaya and Tara. Sonal is the immediate neighbour of Priya and Swati. Sonal is sitting immediate right of Priya, Tara and Swati are not sitting immediately next to each other. Who is sitting to the immediate left of Priya?
questions.explanation: Kaya sits between Jaya and Tara, and Sonal between Priya and Swati, so the two groups of three fill the six seats. Tara may not sit next to Swati, so she sits next to Priya; Sonal is on Priya's right, so Tara is on her left.

questions.text: Six colleagues A, B, C, D, E and F are having lunch together on a circular table at equal distance, facing the centre of the circle. D is the immediate neighbour of E and B while C is the immediate neighbour of A and F. If A is to the immediate left of E, then who is on the immediate left of C?
questions.explanation: D sits between E and B, and C between A and F, so the two groups of three fill the six seats, with A next to E. Going round to the left from E one reaches A, then C, then F: F is on C's immediate left.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? EZF, GXH, KTL, QNR, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move +2, +4, +6, +8 (E, G, K, Q, Y), the second −2, −4, −6, −8 (Z, X, T, N, F) and the third +2, +4, +6, +8 (F, H, L, R, Z): YFZ.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 42 + 16 ÷ 7 - 36 × 16 = 76
questions.explanation: After interchanging × and +: 42 × 16 ÷ 7 − 36 + 16 = 96 − 36 + 16 = 76.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? ZACF, WXZC, ? , QRTW, NOQT
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back at every step: Z, W, T, Q, N; A, X, U, R, O; C, Z, W, T, Q; F, C, Z, W, T. The missing cluster is TUWZ.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: All bottles are bags. Some bags are pencils. Some pencils are sharpeners. Conclusions: I. Some sharpeners are bottles. II. Some bottles are pencils.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: All bottles are bags, but the bags that are pencils need not include any bottle, and the pencils that are sharpeners need not either. So neither 'some sharpeners are bottles' nor 'some bottles are pencils' must be true.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 manner 2 manage 3 masculine 4 magic 5 matter
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: magic (4), manage (2), manner (1), masculine (3), matter (5). 'Mag' comes before 'man', 'mana' before 'mann', and 'mas' before 'mat'.

questions.text: ‘A + B’ means ‘B is the father of A’; ‘A # B’ means ‘B is the sister of A’; ‘A @ B’ means ‘B is the brother of A’; If A @ B # C + D + E, then how is E related to A?
questions.explanation: B is A's brother and C is B's sister, so A, B and C are siblings. D is C's father, and so A's father, and E is D's father: E is A's father's father.

questions.text: Jagoi is a major style of which of the following forms of Indian classical dance?
questions.explanation: 'Jagoi' is the Meitei word for dance, and the classical Manipuri dance goes by it: its Ras Lila, for instance, is called Jagoi Raas.

questions.text: Identify a way to reduce the pollution caused due to burning of fossil fuels
options: By lowering the temperature of burning
By increasing the efficiency of the combustion process
By increasing the number of carbon molecules
questions.explanation: More efficient combustion burns the fuel more completely, so less fuel is needed for the same work and less carbon monoxide, soot and unburnt fuel is released.

questions.text: Tapan Kumar Pattanayak won the Sangeet natak Akademi Award in which dance form?
questions.explanation: Tapan Kumar Pattanayak (Patnaik), a guru of the Seraikela style of Chhau from Jharkhand, received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Chhau for 2018.

questions.text: Who was the first Indian to conquer the English Channel from Dover to Calais in 1958, and also the only man to swim the oceans of the five continents in one calendar year in 1966?
questions.explanation: Mihir Sen swam the English Channel from Dover to Calais in 1958, the first Indian to do so, and in 1966 swam the Palk Strait, the Strait of Gibraltar, the Dardanelles, the Bosphorus and the Panama Canal.

questions.text: Rs. 2000 banknote of Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series has ______ motif on its back.
questions.explanation: The reverse of the ₹2000 note of the Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series carries a motif of the Mangalyaan, India's first mission to Mars. Rani ki Vav is on the new ₹100 note, the Sun Temple, Konark on the ₹10 and the Red Fort on the ₹500.

questions.text: Who commissioned India's first indigenous aircraft carrier INS Vikrant in Kochi in September 2022?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi commissioned INS Vikrant, built at Cochin Shipyard, on 2 September 2022.

questions.text: Which latitude line passes through the middle of India influencing the climate of the country?
questions.explanation: The Tropic of Cancer runs through the middle of India, from the Rann of Kachchh to Mizoram; the part south of it is tropical and the part north of it subtropical.

questions.text: During the reign of which of the following Mauryan kings, the Kalinga War was fought?
questions.explanation: The Kalinga War (about 261 BCE) was fought in Ashoka's reign; its bloodshed, which he regrets in his Rock Edict XIII, turned him towards the dhamma.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When was the first complete Census conducted in India?
questions.explanation: The first complete, synchronous census of India was taken in 1881, under Lord Ripon; the earlier count of 1872 was not taken all at once.

questions.text: Who has been appointed as the “State Brand Ambassador” of Uttarakhand government in August 2022?
questions.explanation: In August 2022 Uttarakhand's Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami formally named the cricketer Rishabh Pant, who was born in Roorkee, the state's brand ambassador, to draw young people towards sport and health; the choice had first been announced in December 2021.

questions.text: The President of India is elected by _________.
options: Only the Members of State Legislative Assemblies
Only the elected members of both Houses of Parliament
Only the members' of Council of States
the Elected Members of both Houses of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies.
questions.explanation: Under Article 54 the President is elected by an electoral college of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and of the Legislative Assemblies of the States (including Delhi and Puducherry).

questions.text: Which of the following is the thanksgiving festival of Maharashtra, where bulls are honoured as they are considered indispensable to farming?
questions.explanation: At Pola, a farmers' festival of Maharashtra, bulls and oxen are bathed, decorated and worshipped in thanks for their work in the fields. Gudi Padwa is the Marathi new year, and Kala Ghoda an arts festival in Mumbai.

questions.text: Original text of the Indian Constitution contained ______ articles.
questions.explanation: The Constitution as adopted in 1949 had 395 articles in 22 parts, and 8 schedules.

questions.text: Which of the following was one of the main objectives of the Seventh Five-Year Plan?
options: Increase in production of Food Grains
questions.explanation: The Seventh Plan (1985-90) put its stress on 'food, work and productivity': raising food-grain production, creating jobs and raising productivity.

questions.text: Moss and Marchantia comes under which of the following?
questions.explanation: Mosses and the liverwort Marchantia are bryophytes, small land plants without vascular tissue that need water for fertilisation.

questions.text: Revenue receipts are __________ as they do not lead to a claim on the government.
questions.explanation: Revenue receipts, such as taxes and other non-tax revenue, create no claim on the government, so they are non-redeemable; borrowings, a capital receipt, must be repaid.

questions.text: During emergency which fundamental rights cannot be suspended?
questions.explanation: Since the 44th Amendment (1978), the enforcement of Articles 20 and 21 (protection in respect of conviction for offences, and protection of life and personal liberty) cannot be suspended during an emergency.

questions.text: In which among the following states, Arabica coffee grown in India?
questions.explanation: Arabica coffee is grown mainly in Karnataka, India's leading coffee state, in the hills of Chikkamagaluru, Kodagu and Hassan, and also in Kerala and Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: ________________falls under the Ministry of textiles.
options: MPLADS (Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme)
questions.explanation: Samarth, the scheme for building skills in the textile sector, is run by the Ministry of Textiles. The Ambedkar Social Innovation and Incubation Mission belongs to the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, MPLADS to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, and the Merchandise Exports from India Scheme to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

questions.text: Which State won the Vijay Hazare Trophy in 2017-18?
questions.explanation: Karnataka beat Saurashtra by 41 runs in the final in Delhi on 27 February 2018 to win the 2017-18 Vijay Hazare Trophy.

questions.text: A shopkeeper allows a discount of 40% on his articles and still makes a profit of 20%. How much cost price does shopkeeper pay for an article whose marked price is ₹ 2,400?
questions.explanation: With 40% off, the selling price is 60% of ₹2,400 = ₹1,440. A 20% profit means ₹1,440 = 1.2 × cost, so the cost price is ₹1,200.

questions.text: A man covers a certain distance by scooter at 64 km/h and he returns to the starting place riding a bicycle at 16 km/h. Find the average speed for the whole journey.
questions.explanation: For equal distances the average speed is 2 × 64 × 16/(64 + 16) = 2048/80 = 25.6 km/h.

questions.text: 5 women can complete a work in 8 days, while 8 children take 10 days to complete the same work. How many days will 2 women and 4 children take to complete the work?
questions.explanation: The work is 5 × 8 = 40 woman-days or 8 × 10 = 80 child-days, so 1 woman does the work of 2 children. 2 women and 4 children equal 4 women, who take 40 ÷ 4 = 10 days.

questions.text: A can paint a painting in 12 days. B can paint the same in 8 days. C can paint the same in 10 days. Find the (approximate) number of days in which the painting can be painted by A if he is accompanied by both B and C together on alternate days and A starts painting on the first day alone.
questions.explanation: A does 1/12 a day and A, B and C together 1/12 + 1/8 + 1/10 = 37/120, so each two-day round does 10/120 + 37/120 = 47/120. After 4 days 94/120 is done; day 5 (A alone) brings it to 104/120, and the last 16/120 takes 16/37 = 0.43 of day 6: about 5.4 days.

questions.text: The population of bears in a city has been growing at 3% every year. If the present population of bears in the city is 21,218, what was the population of bears two years ago?
questions.explanation: Two years ago the population was 21,218 ÷ 1.03² = 21,218 ÷ 1.0609 = 20,000.

questions.text: The income of a person is ₹95,000 and his expenditure is ₹75,000. If his income is increased by 18% and the expenditure by 12%, then what will be the percentage increase in his saving?
Mohan is selling a table at Rs.2,832. If his profit is 18%, then what is the cost price of the table?
questions.explanation: The selling price is 118% of the cost, so the cost price is 2,832 ÷ 1.18 = ₹2,400.

questions.text: In how much time (in years) would ₹80,000 amount to ₹1,17,128 at 10% per annum rate of interest, compounded yearly?
5 bells start commencing together at 9 AM. They ring at the intervals of 12 seconds, 18 seconds, 24 seconds, 36 seconds and 45 seconds. At what time do the bells ring together again?
questions.explanation: The bells ring together again after LCM(12, 18, 24, 36, 45) = 2³ × 3² × 5 = 360 seconds, that is 6 minutes: at 9:06 AM.

questions.text: A cone of radius 9 cm and height 15 cm is melted and made into a cylinder of height 45 cm. The diameter of the cylinder is:
questions.explanation: The volumes are equal: (1/3) × π × 9² × 15 = π × r² × 45, so 405 = 45r², r² = 9 and r = 3 cm. The diameter is 6 cm.

questions.text: A car covered 240 km in 5 h. If it travels with half of its usual speed, then how much more time will be taken to cover the same distance?
questions.explanation: The usual speed is 240/5 = 48 km/h; at 24 km/h the trip takes 240/24 = 10 h, which is 5 h more.

questions.text: X bought 40 pencils for a total of Rs 180 and bought 2 dozens of pens for Rs 180. Find the difference between the price of one pen and one pencil.
questions.explanation: A pencil costs 180/40 = ₹4.50 and a pen 180/24 = ₹7.50, so the difference is ₹3.

questions.text: How many prime numbers are there between 40 and 50?
questions.explanation: Between 40 and 50 the primes are 41, 43 and 47: three. (42, 44, 46 and 48 are even, 45 is divisible by 5 and 49 = 7 × 7.)

questions.text: A dealer allowed a discount of 20 percent on marked price of Rs. 72000 on an article and incurred a loss of 10 percent. What discount should he allow on the marked price, so that he gains Rs. 440 on the article?
questions.explanation: With 20% off, the price is 0.8 × 72,000 = ₹57,600, a 10% loss, so the cost is 57,600/0.9 = ₹64,000. A gain of ₹440 needs a price of ₹64,440, a discount of 7,560 on 72,000: 10.5%.

questions.text: Identify the correctly spelt sentence.
options: The events arranged or organised in order of time are known as chronoligal order.
The events arranged or organised in order of time are known as chronological order.
The events arranged or organised in order of time are known as chronologikal order.
The events arranged or organised in order of time are known as chronoloigal order.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'chronological'; the other sentences have 'chronoligal', 'chronologikal' and 'chronoloigal'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Timid
questions.explanation: 'Timid' means lacking courage; its opposite is 'bold'. 'Diffident', 'shy' and 'fearful' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Blast
questions.explanation: To 'blast' is to blow up with explosives.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I “regarded” my brother on passing his graduation examination.
questions.explanation: To 'congratulate' someone is to praise them for an achievement, such as passing an examination; 'regarded' does not fit the sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Liability
questions.explanation: A 'liability' is something owed or a burden; its opposite is an 'asset', something of value.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank. In many road accidents people break their bones mainly because their vehicle ___________ fails.
questions.explanation: 'Brake', the device that stops a vehicle, sounds the same as 'break' earlier in the sentence: when a vehicle's brake fails, people break bones.

questions.text: Select the correct word for the blanks in the given sentence. Sivakashi is famous for its ___________ box industry, and I am unable to find a __________ for my purple dress.
questions.explanation: 'Match' fits both blanks: a matchbox, and a 'match', something that goes well with the dress.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Truthfully speaking, the victories of peace and harmony have a more _________ impact on human civilisation than the so-called victories of war.
questions.explanation: A 'lasting' impact is one that endures. 'More' cannot go with 'superior' or 'greater', which are already comparatives, and 'transient' (short-lived) goes against the sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Purchasing furniture at a low cost “could not involve abandoning” design or quality.
questions.explanation: The sentence means that a low price ought not to cost design or quality: it 'should not entail (involve) sacrificing (giving up)' them. The other options do not make sense here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Colloquial
questions.explanation: 'Colloquial' language is that of ordinary conversation: 'conversational'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in future tense form. There are multiple facilities available for reaching the island.
options: There will be multiple facilities available for reaching the island.
There have been multiple facilities available for reaching the island.
There had been multiple facilities available for reaching the island.
There were multiple facilities available for reaching the island.
questions.explanation: The future of 'there are' is 'there will be'; the other options are in the present perfect, past perfect and simple past.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Permenent' is misspelt: the word is 'permanent'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Rancid
questions.explanation: 'Rancid' describes stale, spoiled fat or food, such as butter gone off; its opposite is 'fresh'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. At your beck and call
options: To have absolute control over someone
To have no control over someone
To call someone and then deny
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives this meaning, which looks at the idiom from the side of the one giving the orders: someone who is 'at your beck and call' is always ready to do whatever you ask, so you have them under your control. None of the other options comes close.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A night owl
options: A person who prefers to be awake late at night
questions.explanation: A 'night owl' is a person who likes to stay awake and active late at night.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The companies in the present era (1) _________ priority, during recruitment, to the candidates who have Emotional Intelligence. EI is the ability to understand, analyse and control emotions. Possessing very high EI creates a (2) __________ impact on a person’s life. People who have EI always maintain emotional stability even in difficult situations. They can be nice even in socially awkward situations. As they are very good at controlling emotions, they make others feel (3) __________. It is proven that it will make leaders more effective as they understand the feelings of teammates. It allows one (4) ________ impactfully with others. Stress and conflict can be handled so easily. As it allows great empathy towards others, they can be very good at interpersonal relationship. These people strengthen the relationship (5) _________ the people with their interaction and coordination both in personal and professional life. Companies are well aware of the benefits with the employees who have EI.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Companies' is plural, and the present continuous suits 'in the present era': 'are giving priority'. 'Is giving' and 'has been giving' are singular, and 'have been given' is passive.

As it allows great empathy towards others, they can be very good at interpersonal relationship. questions.text: Six girls D, K, M, P, R and S are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre. S is sitting third to the left of R. P is sitting to the immediate right of R and to the immediate left of D. M is sitting to the immediate left of R. K is sitting to the immediate right of S and to the immediate left of M. Who is the immediate neighbour of K and D?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, each girl's left is the next seat clockwise. Clockwise from R the order is R, M, K, S, D, P: M is on R's left, K on M's left, S third to R's left, and P on R's right with D on P's right. S sits between K and D.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 42 + 12 ÷ 24 × 84 - 14 = 91

Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/consonants/vowels in the word). Pediatrician : Children :: Dermatologist : ?
questions.explanation: A paediatrician treats children, and a dermatologist treats disorders of the skin.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 lonely 2 longitude 3 lovely 4 lounge 5 locker
questions.explanation: In dictionary order: locker (5), lonely (1), longitude (2), lounge (4), lovely (3). 'Loc' comes before 'Lon', 'Lone' before 'Long', and 'Lou' before 'Lov'.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? UERB, RHOE, ?, LNIK, IQFN
questions.explanation: The first and third letters move back 3 each time (U, R, O, L, I and R, O, L, I, F) and the second and fourth move forward 3 (E, H, K, N, Q and B, E, H, K, N): OKLH.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (20, 90, 10); (25, 135, 10)
questions.explanation: In each set the second number is 9 times the difference of the first and third: (20 − 10) × 9 = 90 and (25 − 10) × 9 = 135. Likewise (18 − 10) × 9 = 72.

questions.text: Which of the following interchange of numbers (not digits) would make the given equation correct? 8 × 15 ÷ 3 + 14 − 4 = 26
questions.explanation: After interchanging 4 and 8: 4 × 15 ÷ 3 + 14 − 8 = 20 + 14 − 8 = 26.

questions.text: A @ B means ‘A is the husband of B’. A & B means ‘A is the mother of B’. A # B means ‘A is the daughter of B’. A % B means ‘A is the sister of B’. If G % V @ K & P and G # S % M, then how is S related to P?
questions.explanation: V is K's husband and K is P's mother, so V is P's father. G is V's sister and S's daughter, so S is a parent of P's father, and as M's sister S is female: P's father's mother.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 7, 50, 351, 2458, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 7 times the one before plus 1: 7 × 7 + 1 = 50, 50 × 7 + 1 = 351, 351 × 7 + 1 = 2458 and 2458 × 7 + 1 = 17207.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? DBA, JHG, PNM, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 6 places on: D, J, P, V; B, H, N, T; A, G, M, S. The next term is VTS.

questions.text: Three Statements are given followed by Three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some cabbages are rocks. All rocks are wheels. No wheel is a scissor. Conclusions: I. All cabbages are wheels. II. Some rocks are wheels. III. Some wheels are not scissors.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Both conclusions I and III follow.
Both conclusions II and III follow.
questions.explanation: All rocks are wheels, so some rocks are wheels (II). No wheel is a scissor, so some wheels are not scissors (III). Only some cabbages are known to be rocks, so I does not follow.

questions.text: Eight people are sitting in two parallel rows with 4 people each in such a way that there is equal distance between adjacent persons and they are facing each other. In row I – L, M, N and O are seated and all of them are facing south. In row II – P, Q, R and S are seated and all of them are facing north. N sits next to the person at the extreme right end of their row and is facing R. S sits at the extreme left end of their row. Q sits to the immediate right of R and is facing L. O sits at the extreme left end of their row. Who sits at the extreme right end of the row of people facing South?
questions.explanation: Row I faces south, so its right end is the west end; row II faces north, so its right end is the east end. Numbering the seats 1 to 4 from west to east: N is in seat 2 of row I, facing R in seat 2 of row II; Q, on R's right, is in seat 3, facing L; O is at row I's left end, seat 4. That leaves M in seat 1, the right end of the row facing south.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘MONTH’ is written as ‘141213719’ and ‘YEAR’ is written as ‘222269’. How will ‘WEEK’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as its place in the reversed alphabet (A = 26, Z = 1): MONTH → 14, 12, 13, 7, 19 and YEAR → 2, 22, 26, 9. So WEEK → 4, 22, 22, 16: 4222216.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BUYER’ is written as ‘CSZCS’ and ‘CHILD’ is written as ‘DFJJE’. How will ‘DEATH’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, −2, +1, −2, +1: BUYER → CSZCS and CHILD → DFJJE. So DEATH → ECBRI.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. UCE : FEX :: PGS : TIS :: HKR : ?
questions.explanation: Each cluster is reversed and its letters moved +1, +2 and +3: UCE → E C U → FEX and PGS → S G P → TIS. So HKR → R K H → SMK.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 7, 17, ?, 137, 407, 1217
Sadanam P.V Balakrishnan won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in which dance form?
questions.explanation: Sadanam P.V. Balakrishnan, a Kathakali actor from Kerala, received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Kathakali.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was the first Indian to be recruited in Indian Civil Service in British India?
questions.explanation: Satyendranath Tagore, Rabindranath Tagore's elder brother, was selected for the Indian Civil Service in 1863, the first Indian to join it.

questions.text: In badminton each game consist of how many points?
questions.explanation: Under rally-point scoring a badminton game goes to the first side to reach 21 points, with a two-point lead needed at 20-all, up to a cap of 30.

questions.text: Who was the first flag bearer for India in the Olympics?
questions.explanation: The sprinter Purma Banerjee carried India's flag at the opening ceremony of the 1920 Antwerp Olympics, the first Indian flag bearer at the Games.

questions.text: Rs. 50 banknote of Mahatma Gandhi (New) series has base colour of ______.
questions.explanation: The ₹50 note of the Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series, issued in 2017, has a fluorescent blue base colour, with Hampi's stone chariot on the reverse.

questions.text: Which of the following is a classical dance form from Andhra Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Kuchipudi takes its name from the village of Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh's Krishna district. Bharatanatyam comes from Tamil Nadu, Mohiniyattam from Kerala and Manipuri from Manipur.

questions.text: Maha Shivratri is celebrated in the honour of the Hindu deity, Lord Shiva in the Hindu month of ________.
questions.explanation: Maha Shivratri falls on the 14th night of the waning moon in Phalguna, in February or March; calendars that end the month at the new moon count the same night in Magha.

questions.text: The plan between fifth five year plan and sixth five year plan is known as ______.
questions.explanation: The Janata government ended the Fifth Plan a year early, in 1978, and brought in the Rolling Plan (1978-80), which ran until the Sixth Plan (1980-85) began.

questions.text: According to Xuan Zang, the ___________ of Nalanda Buddhist monastery asks new entrants difficult questions which were very difficult to answer
questions.explanation: Xuan Zang, who studied at Nalanda, wrote that its gatekeeper put hard questions to those who wished to enter, and only those who could answer them were admitted.

questions.text: As on October 2022, who is the General Secretary of the Communist Party of India ?
questions.explanation: In October 2022 the CPI's General Secretary was D. Raja, who had held the post since July 2019 and was re-elected at the party congress in Vijayawada that month. Sitaram Yechury led a different party, the CPI(M).

questions.text: Skill India Mission's Governing Council is chaired by the ________.
questions.explanation: The National Skill Development Mission (Skill India), launched in July 2015, is steered by a Governing Council chaired by the Prime Minister, with a Steering Committee and a Mission Directorate below it.

questions.text: The contribution made by each sector of the economy into GDP is called ______.
questions.explanation: The share that each sector (agriculture, industry and services) contributes to GDP is called the structural composition of the economy.

questions.text: In Nomadic herding, herdsmen move from place to place with their animals for _______ and _______ along defined routes.
questions.explanation: Nomadic herders of semi-arid and arid lands move with their animals along set routes in search of fodder and water.

questions.text: Who among the following was elected as Member of Rajya Sabha from Tripura, India in September 2022?
questions.explanation: Former Chief Minister Biplab Kumar Deb won the by-election of 22 September 2022 for Tripura's Rajya Sabha seat, which Manik Saha had given up after becoming Chief Minister in May 2022.

questions.text: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the ‘protection of life and personal liberty’?
questions.explanation: Article 21 says no person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except by procedure established by law. Article 19 covers freedoms such as speech, Article 20 protection in respect of conviction for offences, and Article 22 protection against arrest and detention.

questions.text: Which of the following case is NOT a criminal law case?
questions.explanation: A divorce is a civil matter, settled between the parties in a civil court. Murder, theft and dowry harassment are crimes, prosecuted under criminal law.

questions.text: Name the state which has the highest female literacy rate in India as per census 2011.
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Kerala had the highest female literacy rate, about 92%, ahead of Mizoram.

questions.text: In human body, the food passes through a continuous canal which begins at ______ and ends at anus.
questions.explanation: The alimentary canal runs from the buccal cavity (mouth) through the food pipe, stomach, small and large intestines and rectum to the anus.

questions.text: Tamil Nadu coast gets a large portion of its rain during ________ and __________.
questions.explanation: The Tamil Nadu coast gets much of its rain in October and November, from the retreating (north-east) monsoon winds, which pick up moisture over the Bay of Bengal.

questions.text: A and B can complete a work separately in 10 days and 15 days, respectively. B alone work for 3 days and then he left the work. In how many days will A finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation: In 3 days B does 3/15 = 1/5 of the work. A finishes the remaining 4/5 in 4/5 × 10 = 8 days.

questions.text: Find the product of the numbers whose HCF and LCM are 8 and 40 respectively.
questions.explanation: The product of two numbers equals HCF × LCM = 8 × 40 = 320.

questions.text: John borrowed some amount of money from a bank at the rate of 10% per annum on compound interest for which interest is compounded annually. If he repaid his loan by paying ₹21,961.50 at the end of 4 years, what is the amount he borrowed?
A bus travels from station P to station Q at a speed of 70 km/h, and from station Q to station P at a speed of 90 km/h. What is the average speed of the bus during the entire journey?
questions.explanation: For equal distances the average speed is 2 × 70 × 90/(70 + 90) = 12,600/160 = 78.75 km/h.

questions.text: Sonal and Arjun together can finish a piece of work in 57 days, Arjun and Rohan in 38 days, and Rohan and Sonal in 38 days, then Sonal, Arjun, and Rohan together can finish the same work in how many days?
questions.explanation: Adding the three pairs: 2(S + A + R) = 1/57 + 1/38 + 1/38 = 2/114 + 3/114 + 3/114 = 8/114, so the three together do 4/114 = 2/57 of the work a day and take 57/2 = 28.5 days.

questions.text: On selling a table fan at Rs.2,827.06, the value of gain is 14% more than the value of loss incurred on selling it at Rs.2,230. In order to gain 14%, the selling price will be:
The ratio between the fourth proportional of 7, 5 and 3 to the third proportional of 7 and 13 is:
questions.explanation: Fourth proportional: 7 : 5 = 3 : x gives x = 15/7. Third proportional: 7 : 13 = 13 : y gives y = 169/7. The ratio is 15/7 : 169/7 = 15 : 169.

questions.text: A cylindrical tank has a capacity of 5632 m³. If the diameter of its base is 16 m, find its depth.
questions.explanation: The radius is 8 m, so the depth is V/(πr²) = 5632 ÷ ((22/7) × 64) = 5632 × 7/1408 = 28 m.

questions.text: A shopkeeper sells goods at a profit of 12% and uses a weight which is 15% less than the original weight. Find his total percentage gain. (Correct to 2 decimal places)
questions.explanation: He gives 85 units for the price of 100 and adds 12%: gain = 112/85 − 1 = 27/85 = 31.76%.

questions.text: If A ∶ B = 5 ∶ 6 and B ∶ C = 6 ∶ 7, then (A + B) ∶ (B + C) ∶ (C + A) is:

In a circular race of 400 m in length, A and B start at speeds of 10 m/s and 16 m/s, respectively, at the same time from the same point. After how much time will they meet for the first time at the starting point when running in the same direction?
questions.explanation: A completes a lap every 400/10 = 40 s and B every 400/16 = 25 s. Both are back at the start together after LCM(40, 25) = 200 s.

questions.text: What is the length of the longest pole that can be placed in a room of dimensions 10 m × 10 m × 5 m?
questions.explanation: The longest pole runs along the room's diagonal: √(10² + 10² + 5²) = √225 = 15 m.

questions.text: A clothing store announced a discount of 30 percent on shirts. Rivaan wanted to save Rs. 810 in discount. How many shirts should he buy to do so, if marked price of each shirt is Rs. 540?
questions.explanation: Each shirt saves 30% of ₹540 = ₹162, so ₹810 ÷ ₹162 = 5 shirts.

questions.text: A train 120 m long passes a bridge in 18 seconds moving at a speed of 60 km/h. Find out the length of the bridge.
questions.explanation: 60 km/h = 50/3 m/s, so in 18 s the train covers 300 m, its own length plus the bridge: 300 − 120 = 180 m.

questions.text: A dealer marks his goods 15% above the cost price. Then he allows 20% discount on it. What will be his loss percentage?
questions.explanation: The selling price is 1.15 × 0.80 = 0.92 of the cost, a loss of 8%.

questions.text: Number 350 is increased by 20% and then decreased by 25%. Find the new number.
The average cost of 10 items is Rs.89. If one item costs Rs.35, then find the average cost of remaining 9 items (in Rs.).
questions.explanation: The 10 items cost 10 × ₹89 = ₹890; without the ₹35 item the other 9 cost ₹855, an average of ₹95.

questions.text: Due to illness the weight of a person has reduced from 80 kg to 64 kg in a month. The percent decrease in the weight of the person is:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Bed of roses
questions.explanation: A 'bed of roses' is a pleasant, easy situation, as in 'life is not a bed of roses'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Bag and baggage
questions.explanation: To leave 'bag and baggage' is to leave with all one's belongings.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Alas! The forest turned into a ______ land.
questions.explanation: 'Bare' means empty or uncovered: the forest became bare land. 'Bear' sounds the same but means the animal or to carry, and 'beer' and 'buyer' make no sense here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. The turtle can live in water “as well as land.”
questions.explanation: A turtle lives 'in' water but 'on' land, so the second phrase needs its own preposition: 'in water as well as on land'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Baldness is “quite very usual” among youngsters these days.
questions.explanation: 'Quite very' doubles up two intensifiers. Of the options only 'getting very common' keeps the sense that baldness is widespread: 'Baldness is getting very common among youngsters these days.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Conceal
questions.explanation: To 'conceal' is to hide. 'Manifest', 'disclose' and 'confess' all mean to reveal.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. Her “lively” demeanour makes her the ideal choice for this job.
questions.explanation: 'Lively' means full of energy and cheer; its opposite is 'gloomy', dull and low in spirits.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Cruel
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'cruel' is 'kind'. 'Brutal' and 'savage' are synonyms of it.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'solvent'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Steadfast
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'dishonest': 'steadfast' means firm and faithful, and 'unwavering', 'immobile' and 'dependable' are all close to it in meaning, so 'dishonest' (not to be trusted) is the only option that runs against it, though not an exact opposite such as 'wavering' or 'disloyal'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks and make the sentence meaningful. They were not ______ to eat during the _______.
questions.explanation: 'Allowed' means permitted ('aloud' means out loud), and a 'break' is a pause ('brake' stops a vehicle): 'They were not allowed to eat during the break.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The possible results of an action
questions.explanation: 'Ramifications' are the possible consequences of an action or decision. 'Causation' is the causing of something, and 'implementation' the carrying out of a plan.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Bankrupt
questions.explanation: 'Bankrupt' means unable to pay one's debts: 'insolvent'. 'Well-off' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. Nandu will / leave for the airport / as soon as / a taxi arrive.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'a taxi' needs a singular verb: 'as soon as a taxi arrives'.

questions.text:

A natural gas barrier in the upper atmosphere called the ozone layer (1.) _________ people and other living things from the sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation. Ozone exists in tiny concentrations (2.) _________ the atmosphere, but the majority (about 90%) is found in the stratosphere, a layer that is 10 to 50 kilometres (3.) _________ the surface of Earth. questions.text:

questions.explanation: To 'block out' rays is to stop them getting through, which the ozone layer does to most of the sun's UV rays.

questions.text:

A natural gas barrier in the upper atmosphere called the ozone layer (1.) _________ people and other living things from the sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation.
