Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The finding belongs to the past ('In the 1970s'), so the past tense 'learnt' is needed.

questions.text: In this question, three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: All fans are bulbs. All bulbs are tube lights. Some tube lights are new. Conclusions: I. All fans are new. II. All tube lights are fans.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: All fans are bulbs and all bulbs are tube lights, so all fans are tube lights; but only some tube lights are new, and they need not include any fan, so I does not follow. That all fans are tube lights does not make all tube lights fans, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. ROOT : QQTV :: STEM : VGUO :: LEAF : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward and the new letters are written in the order 2nd, 3rd, 1st, 4th: ROOT → TQQV → QQTV and STEM → UVGO → VGUO. So LEAF → NGCH → GCNH.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? AJRZ, DMTC, ?, JSXI, MVZL
questions.explanation: The first, second and fourth letters each move 3 places forward (A, D, G, J, M; J, M, P, S, V; Z, C, F, I, L) and the third 2 places (R, T, V, X, Z): GPVF.

questions.text: 'A + B’ means ‘A is the son of B’ ‘A – B’ means ‘A is the sister of B’ ‘A × B’ means ‘A is the brother of B’ ‘A ÷ B’ means ‘A is the wife of B’ If A + B ÷ C × D – E + F, then which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: A is the grandson of F.
A is the son of C.
E is the brother of B.
D is the daughter of F.
questions.explanation: A is the son of B, B is the wife of C, C is the brother of D, D is the sister of E and E is the son of F. So C, D and E are F's children, A is C's son and F's grandson, and D is F's daughter. E is the brother of B's husband, her brother-in-law, not her brother.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FINGER’ is written as ‘HHPIDT’ and ‘DESTINY’ is written as ‘ FDUVHPA’. How will ‘GRANTED’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each vowel moves 1 place back and each consonant 2 places forward: FINGER → HHPIDT and DESTINY → FDUVHPA (Y wraps round to A). So GRANTED → I T Z P V D F: ITZPVDF.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 136 ÷ 17 + 102 - 3 × 2 = 187

Seven people A, H, D, F, T, E, and G are sitting in a straight row, facing north. Only three people sit to the left of E. G and H are immediate neighbours of E. A sits at the extreme right of the row. D is the immediate neighbour of A. F sits second to the left of E. Who sits at the extreme left of the row?
questions.explanation: With three people to the left of E, E is fourth from the left, with G and H in the third and fifth places. A is at the right end (seventh) with D beside A (sixth), and F is second to the left of E (second). T takes the only place left, the left end.

questions.text: 6 Friends F, U, K, S, M, and A, are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. A and S are immediate neighbours of K. F is sitting opposite to K. S is not a neighbour of F. M is an immediate neighbour of A and F . Who is the immediate neighbour of A and F if M and S exchange their positions?
questions.explanation: Put K in one seat and F opposite; A and S take the seats either side of K. M sits next to both A and F, so M is between them, and U takes the last seat, between F and S. When M and S exchange seats, S sits between A and F.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘find a solution’ is coded as '418', ‘be attentive’ is coded as '29' and ‘answers are correct’ is coded as '737'. How will ‘check the question’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded by its number of letters: find (4) a (1) solution (8) → 418 and answers (7) are (3) correct (7) → 737. So check (5) the (3) question (8) → 538.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following set. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed) (216, 12, 15) (432, 23, 31)
questions.explanation: The first number is 8 times the sum of the other two: 8 × (12 + 15) = 216 and 8 × (23 + 31) = 432. Likewise 8 × (14 + 24) = 304.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 Seminar 2 Semolina 3 Senior 4 September 5 Serious
questions.explanation: 'Semi' comes before 'Semo', and 'Sem', 'Sen', 'Sep' and 'Ser' follow the alphabet: Seminar, Semolina, Senior, September, Serious, the order given.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 3, 21, 147, ?, 7203
questions.explanation: Each term is 7 times the one before: 147 × 7 = 1029, and 1029 × 7 = 7203.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Mumbai : Maharashtra :: Bhopal : ?
questions.explanation: Mumbai is the capital of Maharashtra; Bhopal is the capital of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 213, 216, 225, 240, 261, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 3, 9, 15, 21, rising by 6, so the next is 27: 261 + 27 = 288.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? LPKT, NNMR, PLOP, ?, THSL
questions.explanation: The first and third letters move 2 places forward (L, N, P, R, T; K, M, O, Q, S) and the second and fourth 2 places back (P, N, L, J, H; T, R, P, N, L): RJQN.

questions.text: In the Indian Constitution 'the abolition of untouchability’ provision is mentioned in _________.
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form. Article 14 guarantees equality before the law, Article 19 the six freedoms and Article 32 the right to move the Supreme Court.

questions.text: What is the colour of the flame when magnesium burns in the presence of oxygen?
questions.explanation: Magnesium burns in oxygen with a dazzling white flame, forming magnesium oxide.

questions.text: Who among the following Gupta rulers was hailed as 'Indian Napoleon' because of his military achievements?
questions.explanation: The historian V. A. Smith called Samudragupta the 'Napoleon of India' for the conquests recorded in Harisena's Allahabad Pillar inscription.

questions.text: E.Krishna Iyer is associated with which form of dance?
questions.explanation: E. Krishna Iyer, a lawyer and freedom fighter, championed the revival of Bharatanatyam (then called sadir) in the 1920s and 1930s and was a founder member of the Madras Music Academy.

questions.text: In India, the population census is conducted once every _________.
questions.explanation: The Census of India is taken once every ten years, as in 1991, 2001 and 2011.

questions.text: Which of the following country is not a part of the Lusofonia Games?
questions.explanation: The Lusofonia Games are for Portuguese-speaking nations and territories: Portugal and Macau (host of the first Games, in 2006) are members, and India, through Goa, which hosted the 2014 Games, also takes part. Germany has no part in them.

questions.text: Radio broadcasting started in India in 1923 by the _____.
questions.explanation: The Radio Club of Bombay made India's first radio broadcast in June 1923.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India talks about Superintendence, direction and control of elections?
questions.explanation: Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission.

questions.text: As of November 2022, who among the following is the Lieutenant Governor of Delhi, India?
questions.explanation: Vinai Kumar Saxena became Lieutenant Governor of Delhi in May 2022, succeeding Anil Baijal, and held the post in November 2022. Manoj Sinha was Lieutenant Governor of Jammu and Kashmir, and Arvind Kejriwal Delhi's Chief Minister.

questions.text: Which among the following festival marks the menstruation period of the Goddess Kamakhya in Assam?
questions.explanation: The Ambubachi Mela, held each June at the Kamakhya temple in Guwahati, marks the goddess's yearly menstruation; the temple stays shut for three days. Moatsu is a festival of the Ao Nagas, Chapchar Kut of Mizoram and Wangala of the Garos.

questions.text: The_________ industry covers a wide range of products from transistor sets to television.
questions.explanation: The electronics industry makes goods ranging from transistor sets and televisions to telephones, radar and computers, as NCERT's geography text describes it.

questions.text: Three of the following four are examples of Coelenterata phylum, and therefore form a group. Which is the one that does not belong to that group?
questions.explanation: The liver fluke is a flatworm (phylum Platyhelminthes). Sea-pens, brain corals and sea anemones are coelenterates (Cnidaria).

questions.text: __________launched on 25th June 2015 , intends to provide housing for all in urban areas by year 2022.
options: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana
questions.explanation: The Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban), launched on 25 June 2015, aimed at housing for all in urban areas by 2022.

questions.text: In which of the following places was the Indian Grand Prix-4 held in June 2021?
questions.explanation: The Athletics Federation of India held the fourth Indian Grand Prix of 2021 at the National Institute of Sports (NIS) in Patiala on 21 June 2021.

questions.text: A ____________ is a barrier across flowing water that obstructs, directs or retards the flow, often creating a reservoir, lake or impoundment.
questions.explanation: A dam holds back, directs or slows a river's flow, often forming a reservoir behind it. A meander is a loop in a river's course, a tributary a stream that joins a larger river, and a moat a ditch round a fort.

questions.text: Who won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in Bharatnatyam in 2018?
questions.explanation: Radha Sridhar received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Bharatanatyam for 2018; the awards were announced in July 2019.

questions.text: Which Union Minister launched the India water pitch-pilot-scale start-up challenge in March 2022?
questions.explanation: Hardeep Singh Puri, then Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs, launched the India Water Pitch-Pilot-Scale Start-up Challenge on 12 March 2022 under AMRUT 2.0, to support start-ups in the water sector.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the _________, an organisation that attempted to reform Hinduism.
questions.explanation: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875; it called for a return to the Vedas.

questions.text: As per RBI, in India, services sector accounted for ___________ of the GDP in the 1980s.
questions.explanation: The RBI's Report on Currency and Finance puts the services sector at 38.6 per cent of India's GDP in the 1980s and 44.3 per cent in the 1990s.

questions.text: Rahul travels a certain distance at a speed of 4 km/h and returns at a speed of 3 km/h via same route. What was his average speed for the entire journey (correct to 2 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: For equal distances the average speed is 2 × 4 × 3/(4 + 3) = 24/7 = 3.43 km/h.

questions.text: A can do a piece of work in 8 days and B in 24 days. They begin together, but 4 days before the completion of the work, A leaves. Find the number of days taken by A and B to complete the entire work.
questions.explanation: If the work takes t days, A works t − 4 days and B all t: (t − 4)/8 + t/24 = 1, so 3t − 12 + t = 24 and t = 9.

questions.text: What is the difference between the compound interest on Rs.5,750 for one year at 16% per annum compounded yearly and compounded half-yearly?
questions.explanation: Yearly: 16% of ₹5,750 = ₹920. Half-yearly, at 8% a half-year: 5,750 × (1.08² − 1) = 5,750 × 0.1664 = ₹956.80. The difference is ₹36.80.

questions.text: The volumes of two cones are in the ratio of 3 : 2 and their radii are in the ratio 3 : 4. The ratio of their heights is:
questions.explanation: A cone's volume is proportional to r²h, so the heights are in the ratio (3/2) ÷ (3/4)² = (3/2) × (16/9) = 8/3, that is 8 : 3.

questions.text: In an election, there were two candidates A and B. The total number of voters in the constituency was 90000 and 70% of the total votes were polled. If 60% of the polled votes were cast in favour of A, how many votes were received by B?
questions.explanation: 70% of 90,000 = 63,000 votes were polled. B received the other 40%: 0.4 × 63,000 = 25,200.

questions.text: The curved surface area of a sphere is 1386 cm² . The volume of this sphere is:

The ratio of milk and water in two containers of 20 litres and 36 litres are in the ratio 3 :7 and 7 : 5, respectively. What will be the ratio of milk and water if the two containers are mixed together?
questions.explanation: The first container holds 6 litres of milk and 14 of water (3 : 7 of 20), the second 21 of milk and 15 of water (7 : 5 of 36). Together: 27 : 29.

questions.text: The square of 28 is divided by the largest number that can exactly divide both 42 and 56. What is the result?
questions.explanation: The HCF of 42 and 56 is 14, and 28² ÷ 14 = 784 ÷ 14 = 56.

questions.text: The price of petrol is raised to Rs.96.5 per litre from Rs.92 per litre. What is the percentage increase in price of petrol?
The third proportional to 24 and 36 is:
questions.explanation: The third proportional to a and b is b²/a = 36²/24 = 1296/24 = 54.

questions.text: Under a discount scheme, after allowing a discount of 20%, there is still a gain of 10%. The marked price is what percentage more than the cost price?
questions.explanation: 0.8 × marked price = 1.1 × cost price, so the marked price is 1.375 times the cost price: 37.5% more.

questions.text: Harshi bought a new sweatshirt at the store, when they were giving a 40 percent discount. If the marked price of the sweatshirt was Rs. 2999, then how much did Harshi pay with the discount?
questions.explanation: Harshi paid 60% of the marked price: ₹2,999 × 0.6 = ₹1,799.40.

questions.text: A man sold two chairs for Rs.475 each, gaining 25% on one and losing 20% on the other. Had he sold the two chairs for Rs.575 each, what would have been his gain/loss percentage (rounded off to the nearest integer)?
questions.explanation: The cost prices were 475/1.25 = ₹380 and 475/0.8 = ₹593.75, ₹973.75 in all. Selling both for ₹575 brings ₹1,150, a gain of ₹176.25, or 176.25/973.75 × 100 = 18.1%, about 18%.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We would _______to travel by train rather than bus due to the poor road conditions in the village.
questions.explanation: 'Would prefer to' goes with 'rather than' to state a choice: 'We would prefer to travel by train rather than bus'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The participants “are rehearse” their roles.
questions.explanation: 'Are' needs the '-ing' form to make the present continuous: 'The participants are rehearsing their roles.' 'Are rehearsed' is passive, and 'has been' does not agree with the plural subject.

questions.text: Select the option with the correct spelling to replace the underlined word in the given sentence. She hit him in a moment of “abomination”.
questions.explanation: Only 'aberration' (one 'b', double 'r') is spelt correctly, and it fits the sentence: a moment of aberration is a brief lapse from one's normal behaviour. The underlined 'abomination' (something hateful) is itself a real word but makes no sense here; the options are all spellings of 'aberration'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Anxious
questions.explanation: 'Anxious' means worried; its opposite is 'unconcerned'.

questions.text: Identify the correctly spelt sentence.
options: My grandfather planted couliflower in the garden.
My grandfather planted kauliflower in the garden.
My grandfather planted cauleflower in the garden.
My grandfather planted cauliflower in the garden.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'cauliflower'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. Music is a therapy for everyone – plants, birds, animals and human-beings – to flourish and “rejuvenate”.
questions.explanation: To 'rejuvenate' is to make fresh or lively again: 'refreshen'. 'Prosper' matches 'flourish', the other verb in the phrase, not the underlined word.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. After one’s own heart
options: Having a face as one's own
Having likes and dislikes dissimilar to one’s own
Having likes and dislikes far to one’s own
Having likes and dislikes similar to one’s own
questions.explanation: Someone 'after one's own heart' shares one's tastes and ways: their likes and dislikes are similar to one's own.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Our soldiers have being / making a clean sweep of the / sheep and poultry on the route.
options: sheep and poultry on the route
making a clean sweep of the
questions.explanation: 'Have being' should be 'have been': the present perfect continuous is 'have been making'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the italicised word in the given sentence. It is “absurd” to argue about this.
questions.explanation: 'Absurd' means foolish or unreasonable; its opposite is 'reasonable'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. ________ men command respect.
questions.explanation: 'Holy' means saintly or devoted to God. 'Holey' means full of holes, 'holly' is a shrub and 'wholly' an adverb meaning entirely.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Sumptuous
questions.explanation: 'Sumptuous' means splendid and costly-looking: 'lavish'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to substitute the underlined group of words in the given sentence. Once in a year, the management of the institute “surveys” the whole situation.
questions.explanation: To 'take stock of' a situation is to review it carefully, which is what 'surveys' means here; none of the other options means that. ('The management' may take a plural verb, as collective nouns can in British English; treated as singular it would read 'takes stock of'.)

questions.text: Select the correct pair of words for the blanks in the given sentence. My cousin likes ________ root and ________ around the bush is one of the idioms in English.
questions.explanation: 'Beet' is the vegetable (beetroot), and 'beat around the bush', to avoid coming to the point, is the idiom.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. He confessed about his affairs as the _________ made him sleepless.
questions.explanation: 'Guilt' is the feeling of having done wrong, which kept him awake. To 'gild' is to coat with gold, a 'guild' is an association of craftsmen or traders, and 'gilled' means having gills.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. “The students were boring” by the lecture delivered on environmental issues.
questions.explanation: People who feel the effect of something dull are 'bored' by it (the past participle); 'boring' describes the thing itself: 'The students were bored by the lecture'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Children especially (1)________ avoid such foods or try to reduce intake and instead, eat healthy food for (2)____ growth. Schools can (3) _______ the quality of the food being sold in the canteens and also ensure that the children bring wholesome nutrition food (4)________ home. (5)________ should be appointed to check the calories content and food value of food served in the canteens and setting definite tiffin patterns.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Should' gives advice: children especially should avoid such foods.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Children especially (1)________ avoid such foods or try to reduce intake and instead, eat healthy food for (2)____ growth. Schools can (3) _______ the quality of the food being sold in the canteens and also ensure that the children bring wholesome nutrition food (4)________ home. (5)________ should be appointed to check the calories content and food value of food served in the canteens and setting definite tiffin patterns.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Healthy food is eaten for 'proper' growth, that is right and normal growth.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Children especially (1)________ avoid such foods or try to reduce intake and instead, eat healthy food for (2)____ growth. Schools can (3) _______ the quality of the food being sold in the canteens and also ensure that the children bring wholesome nutrition food (4)________ home. (5)________ should be appointed to check the calories content and food value of food served in the canteens and setting definite tiffin patterns.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Schools can 'monitor', or keep a check on, the quality of the food sold in their canteens.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Children especially (1)________ avoid such foods or try to reduce intake and instead, eat healthy food for (2)____ growth. Schools can (3) _______ the quality of the food being sold in the canteens and also ensure that the children bring wholesome nutrition food (4)________ home. (5)________ should be appointed to check the calories content and food value of food served in the canteens and setting definite tiffin patterns.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Children bring food 'from' home to school.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Children especially (1)________ avoid such foods or try to reduce intake and instead, eat healthy food for (2)____ growth. Schools can (3) _______ the quality of the food being sold in the canteens and also ensure that the children bring wholesome nutrition food (4)________ home. (5)________ should be appointed to check the calories content and food value of food served in the canteens and setting definite tiffin patterns.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Dieticians, experts in diet and nutrition, are the ones to check the calories and food value of canteen food.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. (The words must be considered as meaningful English words and must not be related to each other based on the number of letters/number of consonants/vowels in the word.) Meghalaya : Shillong :: Kerala : ?
questions.explanation: Shillong is the capital of Meghalaya, and Thiruvananthapuram is the capital of Kerala.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 23, 27, 35, ?, 63, 83, 107
questions.explanation: The differences are 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, rising by 4: 35 + 12 = 47, and 47 + 16 = 63.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 561 ÷ 11 × 22 + 6 – 25 = 158
In a certain code language, ‘STATION’ is written as ‘UVYVGMP’ and 'TRIUMPH' is written as ‘VTGSORJ’. How will ‘HOLIDAY’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each consonant moves 2 places forward and each vowel 2 places back: STATION → UVYVGMP and TRIUMPH → VTGSORJ. So H O L I D A Y → J M N G F Y A (Y + 2 wraps round to A): JMNGFYA.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘TABLE’ is written as ‘£@6#%’, ‘LARK’ is written as ‘#@28’ and ‘BUCKET’ is written as ‘6$+8%£’. How will ‘CLARET’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter has its own symbol, in the same order: TABLE gives T = £, A = @, B = 6, L = #, E = %, LARK adds R = 2 and K = 8, and BUCKET adds U = $ and C = +. So CLARET is +#@2%£.

questions.text: Which letter-cluster will replace the question mark (?) to complete the given series? CTUJ, EVWL, ?, IZAP, KBCR
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward every time: C, E, G, I, K; T, V, X, Z, B; U, W, Y, A, C; J, L, N, P, R. The missing cluster is GXYN.

questions.text: Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? 115, 102, 107, 94, 99, ?

Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. PENALTY : QFOBMUZ :: OFFENSE : PGGFOTF :: NERVOUS : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 1 place forward: PENALTY → QFOBMUZ and OFFENSE → PGGFOTF. So NERVOUS → OFSWPVT.

questions.text: There are 7 people sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre - A, B, C, D, E, F, and G. A is sitting to the immediate right of C and immediate left of D. G is sitting to the immediate left of C and immediate right of F. E is sitting to the immediate left of F and immediate right of B. B is sitting second right of A. Who is the immediate neighbour of A and B?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's right is anticlockwise. Going anticlockwise, the clues give B, E, F, G, C, A, D round the table, so D sits between A and B, and B is second to A's right as stated.

questions.text: Which of the following terms will replace the question mark (?) in the given series? MQEV, ? , QOIT, SNKS, UMMR
questions.explanation: The first letters move +2 (M, O, Q, S, U), the second −1 (Q, P, O, N, M), the third +2 (E, G, I, K, M) and the fourth −1 (V, U, T, S, R). The missing term is OPGU.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F, and G are sitting in a straight row facing the North. A is sitting in the centre of the row. G and E are sitting at the ends of the row. B is sitting to the immediate left of A. F is sitting to the immediate right of G. D is sitting to the immediate left of E. C is sitting to the second left of E. Who is sitting between G and B?
questions.explanation: F is to the immediate right of G, so G is at the left end and E at the right end. From left to right the row is G, F, B, A, C, D, E, so F sits between G and B.

questions.text: Which option represents the correct order of the given words as they would appear in the English dictionary? 1 inside 2 inertia 3 instruction 4 insight 5 individual
questions.explanation: 'Individual' (ind-) comes before 'inertia' (ine-), then the 'ins-' words: 'inside' and 'insight' share 'insi-' and d comes before g, and 'instruction' (inst-) comes last: 5, 2, 1, 4, 3.

questions.text: A @ B means ‘A is the sister of B’. A & B means ‘A is the brother of B’. A # B means ‘A is the wife of B’. A ^ B means ‘A is the mother of B’. A + B means ‘A is the father of B’. If X + T ^ M # G & C ^ K @ H ^ Q, then which of the following statements is NOT correct?
options: G is the son-in-law of T.
G is the father of K.
C is the mother of H.
X is the maternal grandfather of M.
questions.explanation: X is T's father, T is M's mother, M is G's wife, G is C's brother, C is K's mother, K is H's sister and H is Q's mother. So G is K's maternal uncle, not father; the other three statements are true.

questions.text: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some computers are phones. All phones are calculators. All calculators are i-pads. Conclusions: 1. Some i-pads are computers. 2. All calculators are phones. 3. Some i-pads are phones.
questions.explanation: The computers that are phones are calculators and so i-pads, so some i-pads are computers (1). Every phone is an i-pad, so some i-pads are phones (3). Not every calculator need be a phone, so 2 does not follow.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct? 48 - 96 × 4 ÷ 3 + 58 = 34
questions.explanation: After interchanging ÷ and ×: 48 − 96 ÷ 4 × 3 + 58 = 48 − 72 + 58 = 34.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deals with the state executive?
questions.explanation: Articles 153-167, in Chapter II of Part VI, deal with the state executive: the Governor, the Council of Ministers and the Advocate-General.

questions.text: The 'Method of Election of the president' in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the ______ constitution.
questions.explanation: The method of electing the President is among the features borrowed from the Irish Constitution, along with the Directive Principles and the nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha.

questions.text: Mohiniyattam is a solo classical dance form related to which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance of Kerala, traditionally performed solo by women.

questions.text: Which Indian origin Sikh has been given New South Wales Australian of the Year award 2023 for supporting the community affected by floods, bushfires, drought and Covid-19?
questions.explanation: Amar Singh, founder of the charity Turbans 4 Australia, was named the 2023 New South Wales Local Hero in the Australian of the Year Awards (announced in November 2022) for relief work in floods, bushfires, drought and the Covid-19 lockdowns.

questions.text: In India, in which year was the National Food for Work Programme scheme launched?
questions.explanation: The National Food for Work Programme was launched in November 2004 in 150 of the most backward districts; it was later folded into the employment scheme under NREGA.

questions.text: Makar Sankranti is celebrated as Pedda Panduga in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: In Andhra Pradesh, Makar Sankranti is called 'Pedda Panduga', the big festival.

questions.text: Pick the odd one out (Hint: fiber crops)
questions.explanation: Cotton, jute and hemp are fibre crops; rubber is grown for its latex, not for fibre.

questions.text: The mode of nutrition in which organisms take in nutrients from dead and decaying matter is called ______ nutrition.
questions.explanation: Organisms such as fungi that take in nutrients in solution from dead and decaying matter show saprotrophic nutrition.

questions.text: 'Mother of Mohiniyattam' is a docu-fiction based on ______.
questions.explanation: 'Mother of Mohiniyattam' (2019), directed by Vinod Mankara, is about Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma, the dancer known by that title for reviving Mohiniyattam.

questions.text: Budget documents classify total expenditure into ________________.
questions.explanation: Indian budget documents long divided total expenditure into plan and non-plan expenditure, as NCERT's economics textbook describes; the Union Budget dropped that split from 2017-18.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following was the main demand of the peasant movement of Kheda?
options: Free irrigation facility to be provided
questions.explanation: In 1917-18 the peasants of Kheda in Gujarat, hit by crop failure and a plague epidemic, could not pay the land revenue and demanded that its collection be relaxed; Gandhi led their satyagraha.

questions.text: In India, during October-November, with the apparent movement of the sun towards the south, the ______ over the northern plains becomes weaker.
questions.explanation: As the sun moves south in October-November, the monsoon trough (the low-pressure trough over the northern plains) weakens, and the south-west monsoon winds begin to retreat.

questions.text: Techniques of making silk were first invented in China around ______ years ago.
questions.explanation: SSC's key follows NCERT's Class 6 history textbook, which dates China's invention of silk-making to about 7000 years ago; archaeologists' dates for the earliest silk vary.

questions.text: Which of the following player was the highest scorer in the final match of cricket world cup 1983?
questions.explanation: Krishnamachari Srikkanth made 38, the highest score of the 1983 World Cup final at Lord's, which India won by 43 runs.

questions.text: Which country hosted the Asian Athletics Championship in 2019?
questions.explanation: The 2019 Asian Athletics Championships were held in Doha, Qatar, in April 2019.

questions.text: Lime stone is the raw material of _________, among the given industries.
questions.explanation: Cement is made mainly from limestone, with silica and gypsum, so cement plants are set up near limestone deposits.

questions.text: The Supreme Court of India passed a judgment in ________ in which it declared the practice of Triple Talaq as unconstitutional and the practice of the same be void.
questions.explanation: In Shayara Bano v. Union of India (August 2017), the Supreme Court set aside instant triple talaq (talaq-e-biddat) by a 3-2 majority.

questions.text: At independence, about ______ percent of the India’s population was dependent on agriculture.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 75 per cent: at independence India's economy was mainly agrarian, with about three-quarters of the population depending on agriculture for a living.

questions.text: H₂SO₄ is the chemical formula for __________.
questions.explanation: Sulphuric acid, H₂SO₄, is called oil of vitriol. Green vitriol is ferrous sulphate, blue vitriol copper sulphate and muriatic acid hydrochloric acid.

questions.text: A batsman makes a score of 97 runs in 15th inning and thus increases his average by 5. Find his average after 15th inning.
questions.explanation: If the average after 14 innings was x, then 14x + 97 = 15(x + 5), so x = 22 and the average after the 15th inning is 27.

questions.text: The population of a town increased from 145000 to 200000 in a decade. What will be the simple growth rate percent of population per annum?
questions.explanation: The population grew by 55000 on 145000 in 10 years: 55000/145000 × 100 = 37.93%, or 3.793% a year.

questions.text: A can paint seven chairs in an hour and B can paint four chairs in an hour. Determine how much time they will require to paint 55 chairs when they work together.
questions.explanation: Together they paint 7 + 4 = 11 chairs an hour, so 55 chairs take 55 ÷ 11 = 5 hours.

questions.text: A sum of Rs.1,875 at 4% per annum increased to Rs.2,028 in certain time. If interest is compounded yearly, then what is the time period?
questions.explanation: 2,028/1,875 = 1.0816 = 1.04², so the sum was compounded for 2 years.

questions.text: 37 is what percentage of 55? (correct up to two decimal places)
questions.explanation: 37/55 × 100 = 67.2727…, which is 67.27% to two decimal places.

questions.text: The current population of a city is 125000. If the population grows at the rate of 2% per year, what will be the population of the city after 3 years?
The marked price of a washing machine is Rs.23,500 and the shopkeeper sold it for Rs.20,915. What is the percentage of discount offered by the shopkeeper?
A dealer professes to sell his goods at a loss of 16%, but weights 750 gm in place of a kg weight. Find his total profit percentage.
questions.explanation: Take the cost of 1 kg as ₹100. He charges ₹84 (16% below cost) but gives only 750 g, which cost him ₹75: profit = 9/75 × 100 = 12%.

questions.text: The LCM of 32 and 40 equals to 9 less than the square of X. Find the positive value of X.
In a linear race of 1000 m, Saloni beat Shweta by 100 m, while Shweta beat Sonam by 150 m. By how many metres does Saloni beat Sonam, in the same race?
questions.explanation: When Shweta runs 900 m, Sonam runs 900 × 850/1000 = 765 m. So when Saloni finishes 1000 m, Sonam has run 765 m: Saloni wins by 235 m.

questions.text: Four prime numbers are arranged in ascending order. The product of the first three numbers is 255 and that of the last three is 1955. The largest prime number is:
questions.explanation: 255 = 3 × 5 × 17 and 1955 = 5 × 17 × 23, so the four primes are 3, 5, 17 and 23, and the largest is 23.

questions.text: A boy travelled from the home to the college at the rate of 35 km/h and walked back at the rate of 3 km/h. If the whole journey took 6 h 30 min, then the distance of the college from the home (correct to 2 decimal places) is:
Find the mean proportional between 0.64 and 0.81.
A farmer has 10 Parrots and 40 horses. Find the average number of legs per animal.
questions.explanation: The animals have 10 × 2 + 40 × 4 = 180 legs among 50 of them: 180 ÷ 50 = 3.6.

questions.text: With a 10% discount on the marked price, a seller earns a 5% profit. If the marked price is increased by 5% and two successive discounts of 5% each are offered, how much percentage profit does the seller earn?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 10.5%, the option nearest the exact answer. With the marked price ₹100, the cost is 90 ÷ 1.05 = ₹85.71 and the new price is ₹105 × 0.95 × 0.95 = ₹94.76, a profit of 9.05/85.71 × 100 ≈ 10.56%.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. As of now, they have finished the “construction of the ground flour”.
questions.explanation: 'Flour' is ground grain; a level of a building is a 'floor': 'the construction of the ground floor'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I “was delight in” the moment I saw her.
questions.explanation: 'Was' needs the adjective 'delighted', and 'the moment' (as soon as) needs no 'in': 'I was delighted the moment I saw her.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. Jack met with a/an _____ (deadly) accident.
questions.explanation: 'Fatal' means causing death, the same as 'deadly': 'a fatal accident'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Solitary
questions.explanation: 'Solitary' means alone or liking to be alone; 'gregarious' means fond of company. 'Lone' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym for the underlined word in the given sentence. The pearls produced in that oyster farm have lost all their “lustre”.
questions.explanation: 'Lustre' is the soft shine of a surface, such as a pearl's: 'shine'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The person in ragged clothes sleeping on the street is a ____________ man.
questions.explanation: Ragged clothes and sleeping on the street point to a man with no home: 'homeless'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. The country has an “abundant” supply of minerals.
questions.explanation: 'Abundant' means more than enough: 'ample'. 'Sparse' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. The whys and wherefores
questions.explanation: 'The whys and wherefores' are the reasons behind something.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Acceptance
questions.explanation: 'Acceptance' is agreeing to take something; its opposite is 'rejection'.

questions.text: The sentence given below has one misspelt word. Spot the INCORRECTLY spelt word and select its correct spelling. He wishes to be an orthopidic surgeon.
questions.explanation: 'Orthopidic' is misspelt: the word is 'orthopaedic' (British spelling), relating to the treatment of bones and muscles.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. My aunt Geeta, / is knowing / my friend Rudransh / very well.
questions.explanation: 'Know' is a stative verb and is not used in the continuous form: 'My aunt Geeta knows my friend Rudransh very well.'

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Spead' is misspelt (the word is 'speed' or 'spread'); 'task', 'salt' and 'brand' are correct.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Captivity
questions.explanation: 'Captivity' is being held prisoner; its opposite is 'liberty', freedom.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. What _________ of a movie is this?
questions.explanation: 'Kind' is a homonym: the noun means a type or sort, the sense needed here, and the adjective means gentle or caring.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The Conjuring is not a movie for the _______ of heart.
questions.explanation: 'Not for the faint of heart' means not for timid or easily frightened people, which suits a horror film.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The blockade of the national highways leading to the Manipur valley, called by the United Naga Council (UNC), has been in place since 1 November. This has severely affected life in the State, with shortages and (1)__________ costs of essential supplies such as fuel and food, even as demonetisation has (2)__________ problems. Blockades like this are not new to Manipur. In 2011, there was initially a hundred-day- plus blockade enforced by Kuki-led groups, and countered later by Naga groups, which together had a (3)__________ effect on life in Manipur. This time the blockade is in place to oppose the creation of new districts by the OkramIbobi Singh government. On 9 December it issued a (4) __________ notification for the creation of seven new districts by bifurcating seven (of a total of nine) districts. This decision had as much to do with long-pending demands — in particular, for a new Kuki-majority district to be carved out of the larger Senapati hill district — as with easing administrative access to (5)__________ areas from the district headquarters.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Shortages go with 'escalating', that is rising, costs of fuel and food.

questions.explanation: Demonetisation 'exacerbated', that is worsened, the problems the blockade had caused.
