markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Among three numbers, the second number is half of the first number and the third number is 4 less than the second number. If the average of the first and third numbers is 16, what is the second number?
questions.explanation: With the second number x, the first is 2x and the third x − 4. (2x + x − 4)/2 = 16, so 3x = 36 and x = 12.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 5 years.
After successive discounts of 26% and 22.5%, an item was sold at a profit of 24%. If the cost price of the item was ₹925, what was the marked price (in ₹) of the item?
questions.explanation: SP = 925 × 1.24 = ₹1,147. The two discounts leave 0.74 × 0.775 = 0.5735 of the marked price, so MP = 1,147/0.5735 = ₹2,000.

questions.text: A class teacher conducted a unit test in the class. If out of 25 students, 11 students' average score is 77 and rest 14 students' average score is 69, then the weighted average score is:
ABCD is a quadrilateral in which diagonal BD = 62 cm, AL ⊥ BD and CM ⊥ BD, such that AL = 14.3 cm and CM = 17.7 cm. The area of the quadrilateral ABCD is:
Ravish had ₹1,500 with him. Sunaina had 24% more money than what Ravish had, while Sanatan had 10% less money that what Sunaina had. How much money did Sanatan have?
A park has an average number of 420 visitors on Sunday and 120 on other days. The average number of visitors per day in a month of 30 days beginning with Sunday, is:
questions.explanation: A 30-day month beginning on a Sunday has 5 Sundays (days 1, 8, 15, 22 and 29): (5 × 420 + 25 × 120)/30 = (2,100 + 3,000)/30 = 170.

questions.text: When x is added to each of 2, 3, 30 and 35, then the numbers obtained in this order are in proportion. What is the second largest part in the proportion?
questions.explanation: (2 + x)/(3 + x) = (30 + x)/(35 + x) gives (2 + x)(35 + x) = (3 + x)(30 + x), so 70 + 37x = 90 + 33x and x = 5. The numbers are 7, 8, 35 and 40; the second largest is 35.

questions.text: The average of 20 results is 15 and the average of other 25 results is 24. What is the average of all the results?
How long (in months) will it take a sum of money invested at 5% per annum on simple interest to increase its value by 22.5%?
questions.explanation: A 22.5% gain at 5% a year takes 22.5/5 = 4.5 years = 54 months.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
In a code language, 'PARENT’ is written as 'PWRANT' and 'SING' is written as 'SENG'. How will 'TERMINATE' be written in the same language?
questions.explanation: Consonants stay and each vowel moves 4 places back: A → W, E → A, I → E (PARENT → PWRANT, SING → SENG). So TERMINATE → TARMENWTA.

questions.text: EJDI is related to CHBG in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, JOIN is related to HMGL. To which of the following is NSMR related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places back: E → C, J → H, D → B, I → G, and JOIN → HMGL the same way. So N → L, S → Q, M → K, R → P: LQKP.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts,decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All juices are burgers. Some burgers are chocolates. Conclusions: (I) Some burgers are juices. (II) Some juices are chocolates.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: All juices are burgers, so some burgers are juices (I). The burgers that are chocolates need not include any juice, so II does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘MUST’ is coded as ‘7913’ and ‘TALE’ is coded as ‘8672’. What is the code for ‘T’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: T is the only letter in both words and 7 the only digit in both codes, so T = 7.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only 2 people sit between A and C when counted from the right of C. B sits 2nd to the left of C. F sits immediate on the right of D. E is not an immediate neighbour of C. Who sits immediate to the right of A?
questions.explanation: B is second to C's left and A has two people between it and C on C's right. F on D's right then puts D next to C, and E, not beside C, takes the seat on A's right: going round to each person's left the order is C, G, B, E, A, F, D.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 216 219 224 227 232 ?
questions.explanation: The differences alternate +3, +5: 232 + 3 = 235.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) of the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 15 + 9 ÷ 2 – 63 × 3 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging: 15 − 9 × 2 + 63 ÷ 3 = 15 − 18 + 21 = 18.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘rep sho pel’ means ‘goats are bleating’; ‘sho jin ken’ means ‘goats and cows’ and ‘met rep pi’ means 'dogs are mad'. What is the code for ‘are’ in that code language?
questions.explanation: 'are' is the only word common to the first and third sentences, and 'rep' the only code common to both, so are = rep.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 6 × 4− (60 ÷ 5) + 15 + (33÷ 3)× 2 = 59 (Note: Interchange should be done of entire number and not individual digits of a given number)

8 is related to 33 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 11 is related to 45. To which of the following is 24 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is four times the first plus 1: 8 × 4 + 1 = 33 and 11 × 4 + 1 = 45. Likewise 24 × 4 + 1 = 97.

questions.text: EJ68 is related to OT55 in a certain way. In the same way, KP47 is related to UZ34. To which of the following is QV29 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 10 places forward and the number falls by 13: E → O, J → T, 68 → 55; K → U, P → Z, 47 → 34. So Q → A and V → F (wrapping round after Z), and 29 → 16: AF16.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). G sits to the immediate left of B. A sits to the immediate left of D. D sits second to the left of E. C sits third to the left of B. How many people sit between B and D when counted from the left of D?
questions.explanation: G is on B's immediate left and C third to B's left; D, second to E's left with A on its own left, fits only with E in the seat between G and C. Going round to each person's left: B, G, E, C, D, A, F. From D's left, A and F come before B: 2 people.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 9, 43; 13, 63
questions.explanation: The second number is five times the first minus 2: 9 × 5 − 2 = 43 and 13 × 5 − 2 = 63. Likewise 17 × 5 − 2 = 83.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? HKR, DGN, ZCJ ,VYF, ?
questions.explanation: Every letter moves 4 places back each time, wrapping round from A to Z: H, D, Z, V, R; K, G, C, Y, U; R, N, J, F, B. The next cluster is RUB.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘ZERO’ is coded as ‘2468’ and ‘OILY’ is coded as ‘5679’. What is the code for ‘O’ in that language?
questions.explanation: O is the only letter in both words and 6 the only digit in both codes, so O = 6.

questions.text: Which of the following is the legislative organ of the Union Government?
questions.explanation: Parliament (the President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha) is the Union's legislature; the executive and the judiciary are the other two organs.

questions.text: Which type of coal is found in Damodar valley?
questions.explanation: The Damodar valley coalfields, such as Jharia, Raniganj and Bokaro, hold Gondwana coal that is mostly bituminous, including the coking coal used for steel.

questions.text: Which of the following are building blocks of proteins?
questions.explanation: Proteins are chains of amino acids joined by peptide bonds.

questions.text: In which the following sports do caddies play the role of helper for the player?
questions.explanation: In golf a caddie carries the player's clubs and advises on the course.

questions.text: Under which category did Ricky Kej secure his third Grammy award?
options: Best Audio Album of the year
questions.explanation: Ricky Kej's third Grammy, in 2023, was for Best Immersive Audio Album, for 'Divine Tides', shared with Stewart Copeland; his first two were for Best New Age Album.

questions.text: What is the total length of 'Atal Tunnel', which is located in Himachal Pradesh state?
questions.explanation: The Atal Tunnel under the Rohtang Pass, opened in October 2020, is 9.02 km long.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the famous novel,‘One Amazing Thing’?
questions.explanation: 'One Amazing Thing' is a novel by Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni (spelt 'Divakurni' in the option).

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The ‘Servants of India Society’ was founded by which of the following freedom fighters?
questions.explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in Pune in 1905 to train workers for national service.

questions.text: _______, which translates to 'dance of the enchantress,' stands out as one of the most captivating expressions in the Indian classical dance repertoire.
questions.explanation: Mohiniyattam, Kerala's classical dance, takes its name from Mohini, the enchantress form of Vishnu.

questions.text: Who among the following Mughal emperors had a great interest in paintings?
questions.explanation: Mughal painting reached its height under Jahangir, a keen patron and connoisseur whose court artists included Abul Hasan and Ustad Mansur.

questions.text: Which of the following states in India had the LOWEST poverty ratio in 2011-2012 as per the Economic Survey 2013-14, released by the Ministry of Finance, Government of India?
questions.explanation: In the Tendulkar-method estimates for 2011-12 that the survey reports, Kerala's poverty ratio (about 7%) was lower than Haryana's (about 11%), Gujarat's (about 17%) and Karnataka's (about 21%).

questions.text: According to the Indian calendar, the March and April months are known as ___________.
questions.explanation: In the traditional Indian seasons, Vasanta (spring) spans the months Chaitra and Vaisakha, roughly March and April; Jyaistha-Asadha is about May-June, Asvina-Kartika September-October and Magha-Phalguna January-February.

questions.text: Name the Sri Lankan Buddhist text that provides details of the Mauryan empire.
questions.explanation: The Dipavamsa and the Mahavamsa, Pali chronicles of Sri Lanka, describe Ashoka and the Mauryas. The Divyavadana and the Ashokavadana are Sanskrit Buddhist texts, and the Parishishtaparvan is Hemachandra's Jain work.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the Sangeet Natak Akademi is/are true? 1. The Sangeet Natak Akademi has been functioning as the apex body of the performing arts in the country. 2. The main objective of the Akademi is to coordinate and collaborate with the government and performing artists. 3. The Sangeet Natak Akademi comes under the Ministry of Culture of the government of India.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives all three. The Akademi describes itself as the apex body of the performing arts in the country and is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Culture; it pursues its objectives by coordinating and collaborating with the governments and art academies of the states, which statement 2 loosely restates.

questions.text: How much amount is provided per month as assistance to the female head of the family under the Gruha Lakshmi Scheme launched by the Karnataka Government in July 2023?
questions.explanation: Karnataka's Gruha Lakshmi scheme pays ₹2,000 a month to the woman head of each eligible family.

questions.text: What is the salt measurement in hypersaline lagoons?
questions.explanation: NCERT's Class 12 Biology gives the salt concentration (salinity, in parts per thousand) as less than 5 in inland waters, 30 to 35 in the sea and more than 100 in some hypersaline lagoons.

questions.text: Who among the following became the Chairperson of the Parliamentary Committee on Science and Technology, Environment, Forests and Climate Change as on 30th September 2023?
questions.explanation: Jairam Ramesh, a Congress member of the Rajya Sabha, chaired the committee and was renominated to the chair when the committees were reconstituted in September 2023.

questions.text: Chhath Puja falls in which month of the Hindu calendar?
questions.explanation: Chhath Puja falls on the sixth day of the bright half of Kartika, six days after Diwali.

questions.text: Which of the following is a NOT a feature of the Indian Parliamentary form of Government?
options: Non membership of the ministers in Legislature
questions.explanation: In India's parliamentary system ministers must be members of Parliament (a non-member must become one within six months). Dissolution of the Lok Sabha, the Prime Minister's leadership and majority-party rule are all features of it.

questions.text: The Bara Imambara in Lucknow was built in the year 1784 by ________.
questions.explanation: Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula of Awadh built the Bara Imambara in Lucknow in 1784, partly as a famine-relief work.

questions.text: What is the process of a substance changing directly from a solid to a gas without passing through the liquid state called?
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas, as with camphor, naphthalene or dry ice.

questions.text: Which of the following is the quality of the public goods?
questions.explanation: Public goods are non-rivalrous (one person's use does not reduce what is left for others) and non-excludable.

questions.text: What is the player who sits at the centre of the rectangular field in Kho Kho called?
questions.explanation: In kho-kho the chasing side's players sit in the squares of the central lane, facing alternate ways, while one active chaser pursues the defenders.

questions.text: Which of the following is the national fruit of Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives jackfruit, which is commonly listed as Sri Lanka's national fruit.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Shree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam (SNDP), founded in 1903, to carry on the work of social reform was active in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Sree Narayana Guru founded the SNDP Yogam in 1903, with Dr Palpu, for the uplift of the Ezhavas of Kerala.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given phrase. Jump on the bandwagon
options: To oppose the idea of a group gaining popularity
To support ideas that are less popular
To join or support something which is gaining popularity
questions.explanation: To 'jump on the bandwagon' is to join or support something because it is becoming popular.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the underlined spelling error. Participating in the “marthon” was a challenging experience.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'marathon'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who loves music
questions.explanation: A melophile is a lover of music. An astrophile loves stars, and a discophile collects gramophone records.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The Rungrado is the “large” football stadium in the world.
questions.explanation: Comparing one stadium with all others in the world calls for the superlative: 'the largest'. 'Most largest' doubles the superlative.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If we want to promote national integrity in our country, then we must desist our tendency of “taking up with” others.
questions.explanation: To 'look down upon' others is to regard them as inferior, the tendency that harms national integrity.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'noctambulism', sleepwalking, like 'somnambulism'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Whimsical
questions.explanation: 'Whimsical' means acting on sudden fancies; its opposite is 'practical'. 'Fickle' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. “Mahira is an more efficient” and hardworking employee of her company.
questions.explanation: 'More' needs a comparison, and 'efficient' begins with a vowel sound: 'Mahira is an efficient and hardworking employee'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill the blank. The strike, that the truck association called, caused a minor _________ of food in our village.
questions.explanation: A 'dearth' is a scarcity: the strike caused a shortage of food.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The company implemented a new __________ to improve efficiency.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'strategy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Pay off old scores
questions.explanation: To 'pay off old scores' is to take revenge for an old wrong.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word to fill in the blank. Desist Every Indian should ____ from acts of corruption.
questions.explanation: To 'desist' is to stop doing something: to 'refrain', which also takes 'from'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option with the correct usage of the preposition to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. UNESCO’s mission is to contribute to the building of a culture of peace, the eradication of poverty, sustainable development and “intercultural dialogue with education”, the sciences, culture, communication and information.
questions.explanation: UNESCO's mission statement speaks of 'intercultural dialogue through education, the sciences, culture, communication and information': these are the means by which the dialogue is built.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Avoid
questions.explanation: To 'avoid' something is to keep away from it: to 'evade' it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) had _________ that the city would witness rainfall on Thursday.
questions.explanation: The weather office had 'forecast', or predicted, rain.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: The carpenter kept furniture in the backyard of his house.
The carpenter kept the furniture in a backyard of his house.
The carpenter kept the furniture in backyard of his house.
The carpenter kept a furniture in the backyard of his house.
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is uncountable and takes no 'a', and the backyard of his house is a particular one, so 'the backyard': 'The carpenter kept furniture in the backyard of his house.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Where have you ______ all this time?
questions.explanation: 'Have' takes the past participle 'been': 'Where have you been all this time?' 'Bean' and 'bin' only sound similar.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homonym to fill in the blank. During the _____ of Queen Victoria, England made all-round progress.
questions.explanation: A monarch's period of rule is a 'reign'; 'rain' and 'rein' sound the same but mean something else.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. John searched thoroughly but could not find his coat nowhere in the house.
questions.explanation: 'Not' and 'nowhere' make a double negative: 'could not find his coat anywhere in the house'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We should always _________ our best to help others.
questions.explanation: A modal such as 'should' takes the base form of the verb: 'We should always do our best'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Our (1)_____ revolve around our work. For the most part, males have to labour with their hands in order to (2)_____ themselves. But everyone needs to work in some (3)_____. It provides honour and credit to us. Nothing in life can be accomplished without it. Man is great only because of his labours. (4)________ comes from work. The secret to success is this. Nobody can advance without labour. It truly is the (5)_______ idea of existence. Without it, life is even less meaningful.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Our lives revolve around our work': work is at the centre of our lives.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Our (1)_____ revolve around our work. For the most part, males have to labour with their hands in order to (2)_____ themselves. But everyone needs to work in some (3)_____. It provides honour and credit to us. Nothing in life can be accomplished without it. Man is great only because of his labours. (4)________ comes from work. The secret to success is this. Nobody can advance without labour. It truly is the (5)_______ idea of existence. Without it, life is even less meaningful.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: People labour with their hands to 'support' themselves, that is to earn their living.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Our (1)_____ revolve around our work. For the most part, males have to labour with their hands in order to (2)_____ themselves. But everyone needs to work in some (3)_____. It provides honour and credit to us. Nothing in life can be accomplished without it. Man is great only because of his labours. (4)________ comes from work. The secret to success is this. Nobody can advance without labour. It truly is the (5)_______ idea of existence. Without it, life is even less meaningful.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'In some capacity' means in some role or position.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Our (1)_____ revolve around our work. For the most part, males have to labour with their hands in order to (2)_____ themselves. But everyone needs to work in some (3)_____. It provides honour and credit to us. Nothing in life can be accomplished without it. Man is great only because of his labours. (4)________ comes from work. The secret to success is this. Nobody can advance without labour. It truly is the (5)_______ idea of existence. Without it, life is even less meaningful.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Glory comes from work', in keeping with the honour and credit the passage says work brings.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Our (1)_____ revolve around our work. For the most part, males have to labour with their hands in order to (2)_____ themselves. But everyone needs to work in some (3)_____. It provides honour and credit to us. Nothing in life can be accomplished without it. Man is great only because of his labours. (4)________ comes from work. The secret to success is this. Nobody can advance without labour. It truly is the (5)_______ idea of existence. Without it, life is even less meaningful.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Work is the 'fundamental', or basic, idea of existence.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Rice worth ₹84 per kg and ₹96 per kg is mixed with a third variety of rice in the ratio 1 : 1 : 2. If the mixture is worth ₹99 per kg, the price of the third variety per kg is:
questions.explanation: With the third variety at ₹x: (84 + 96 + 2x)/4 = 99, so 180 + 2x = 396 and x = ₹108.

questions.text: The average of six numbers is 30. If one number is excluded, the average becomes 28. Find the excluded number.
questions.explanation: The six numbers add up to 6 × 30 = 180 and the remaining five to 5 × 28 = 140, so the excluded number is 40.

questions.text: On selling a book for ₹348, a shopkeeper loses 13%. In order to gain 22%, he must sell that book for:
questions.explanation: ₹348 is 87% of the cost price, so CP = ₹400. A 22% gain needs 1.22 × 400 = ₹488.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 4 years.

Air is leaking from a spherical-shaped advertising balloon at the rate of 24 cubic feet per minute. If the radius of the balloon is 8 feet, how long would it take for the balloon to empty? Round your answer to the nearest minute. Use the approximate of value of π, that is 3.14.
questions.explanation: Volume = (4/3) × 3.14 × 8³ = 2,143.57 cubic feet. At 24 cubic feet a minute it empties in 2,143.57/24 ≈ 89.3, about 89 minutes.

questions.text: What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹360 in 3 years at 8% per year rate of interest?
The scale of a map is given as 1:250. Two cities are 6.5 km apart on the map. The actual distance between them is
questions.explanation: On a 1:250 scale each unit on the map stands for 250 on the ground: 6.5 km × 250 = 1625 km.

questions.text: The average of 20, 40, 60, 80, 100, 120 and 140 is:
questions.explanation: The seven numbers add up to 560, and 560/7 = 80 (the middle term of an evenly spaced list).

questions.text: The average income of 25 persons is ₹2,400 and that of another 20 persons is ₹1,500. The average income of all of them together is:
A boat can travel at a speed of 13 km/h in still water. If the speed of the stream is 4 km/h, find the time taken by the boat to go 68 km downstream.
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 13 + 4 = 17 km/h, so 68 km takes 68/17 = 4 hours.

questions.text: If 45% of the sum of the two numbers is equal to 60% of the difference between the two numbers, find the ratio of the smallest number to the greatest number.
questions.explanation: 0.45(a + b) = 0.6(a − b) gives 45a + 45b = 60a − 60b, so 105b = 15a and a = 7b. Smaller : greater = 1 : 7.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13, can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (1, 16, 5) (2, 19, 7)
questions.explanation: The middle number is the sum of the other two plus 10: 1 + 5 + 10 = 16 and 2 + 7 + 10 = 19. Likewise 8 + 4 + 10 = 22.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All lions are cheetahs. Some cheetahs are tigers. Conclusions: (I) Some tigers are not cheetahs. (II) All cheetahs are lions.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: Some cheetahs are tigers, but nothing says whether any tiger lies outside the cheetahs (I), and all lions being cheetahs does not make all cheetahs lions (II). Neither follows.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? CHK, GKO, ? , OQW, STA
questions.explanation: First letters move +4 (C, G, K, O, S), second letters +3 (H, K, N, Q, T) and third letters +4 (K, O, S, W, A): KNS.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 28 − 4 × 5 + 36 ÷ 9 + 2 × 3 = 53 (Note: Interchange should be done of entire number and not individual digits of a given number)
In a certain code language, ‘CREATE’ is coded as ‘84’ and ‘FLOP’ is coded as ‘56’. What is the code for ‘PURPOSEFULLY’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: Each word's code is 14 times its number of letters: CREATE (6) = 84 and FLOP (4) = 56. PURPOSEFULLY has 12 letters: 12 × 14 = 168.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 16 − 4 × 2 ÷ 3 + 6= ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 16 + 4 ÷ 2 × 3 − 6 = 16 + 6 − 6 = 16.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: •All hands are legs. •Some hands are eyes. Conclusion (I): All legs are hands. Conclusion (II): Some legs are eyes.
options: Both Conclusions I and II follow
Neither Conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: The hands that are eyes are also legs, so some legs are eyes (II). All hands being legs does not make all legs hands (I). Only II follows.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘use the force’ is coded as ‘gp sb cn’ and ‘force is strong’ is coded as ‘hv sk gp’. How is ‘force’ coded in that language?
questions.explanation: 'force' is the only word in both sentences and 'gp' the only code in both, so force = gp.

questions.text: NKBI is related to PIDG in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, SMFG is related to UKHE. To which of the following is UPQR related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The letters move +2, −2, +2, −2: NKBI → PIDG and SMFG → UKHE. So UPQR → WNSP.

questions.text: 192 is related to 38 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 270 is related to 51. To which of the following is 258 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is the first divided by 6, plus 6: 192 ÷ 6 + 6 = 38 and 270 ÷ 6 + 6 = 51. Likewise 258 ÷ 6 + 6 = 49.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 4, 7, 11, 18, 29, 47, 76, ?, 199
questions.explanation: Each term is the sum of the two before it: 47 + 76 = 123, and then 76 + 123 = 199.

questions.text: M, N, O, P, Q, R and S are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). P is sitting fourth to the right of N. Q is sitting third to the left of O. M is sitting to the immediate right of Q. R is sitting to the immediate right of N. How many people are sitting between P and S when counted from the left of S?
questions.explanation: Going round to the right from N the order is N, R, Q, M, P, O, S: P is fourth to N's right, R next to N, and Q (with M on its right) third to O's left. Counting from S to its left, only O comes before P: 1 person.

questions.text: RQ 45 is related to TS 50 in a certain way. In the same way, UX 19 is related to WZ 24.To which of the following is CF 68 related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Both letters move 2 places forward and the number rises by 5: RQ 45 → TS 50 and UX 19 → WZ 24. So CF 68 → EH 73.

questions.text: A, B, C, L, M, Y and X are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). C sits fourth to the left of M. Only one person sits between L and Y when counted from the left of L. Only one person sits between Y and X when counted from left of Y. Only two people sit between A and Y when counted from the right of A.Who sits third to the right of B?
questions.explanation: Y is two seats to L's left and X two seats to Y's left; Y is three seats to A's right, and C four seats to M's left. Going round to the right from L: L, M, A, X, C, Y, B. Third to the right of B is A.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: 'Waiting for a Visa' is a 20-page autobiography of _________________.
questions.explanation: 'Waiting for a Visa' is B. R. Ambedkar's short autobiographical account of the untouchability he faced.

questions.text: Which of the following is the residential place of Buddhist priests?
questions.explanation: A vihara was a monastery where Buddhist monks lived; a chaitya was a prayer hall and a stupa a mound over relics.

questions.text: Which of the following is an artificial port in India?
questions.explanation: Chennai is one of India's oldest artificial ports. Mumbai is a natural harbour, Kolkata a riverine port and Deendayal (Kandla) a tidal port.

questions.text: Which of the following possesses the largest isolated single cell?
questions.explanation: An unfertilised ostrich egg is the usual example of the largest single cell; a brain and a whale are made of many cells, and an amoeba is a tiny single cell.

questions.text: The National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building (NPCSCB) envisaged by the Central Government is called _____________.
questions.explanation: Mission Karmayogi, approved by the Union Cabinet in 2020, is the National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building.

questions.text: Name the Union territory with the lowest density of population as per Census of India 2011.
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census the Andaman and Nicobar Islands had the lowest population density of the Union territories, 46 persons per km².

questions.text: Which festival commemorates the death of Hussain Ibn Ali?
questions.explanation: Muharram, above all Ashura, its tenth day, mourns the martyrdom of Husain ibn Ali, the Prophet's grandson, at Karbala in 680 AD.

questions.text: Which of the following instruments is played by Shreya Bhattacharjee, an eminent musician from Assam?
questions.explanation: Shreya Bhattacharjee, a young tabla player from Assam, received the Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Bal Puraskar (art and culture) in 2023.

questions.text: Which of the following dance forms emotes a play through dancing in which the song is customarily in Manipravala language?
questions.explanation: Mohiniyattam, Kerala's classical dance, is performed to songs in Manipravalam, a blend of Malayalam and Sanskrit.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following Commissions was set up to investigate the incident of Jallianwala Bagh in 1919?
questions.explanation: The Hunter Committee (the Disorders Inquiry Committee), set up in October 1919, inquired into the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

questions.text: Which of the following national income aggregates is generally recognised as National Income of a country?
options: Gross Domestic Product at Factor Cost
Net National Product at Factor Cost
Gross National Product at Market Prices
Net National Product at Market Prices
questions.explanation: National income is the Net National Product at factor cost.

questions.text: In a food chain of Algae-Shrimp-Fish-Bird, if the energy available at the bird is 4 kJ, then the energy available at the shrimp is:
questions.explanation: By the ten per cent law only about a tenth of the energy passes to the next level, so going down the chain: bird 4 kJ, fish 40 kJ, shrimp 400 kJ.

questions.text: Who among the following has been appointed as the new Director General of the Geological Survey of India (GSI) in June 2023?
questions.explanation: Janardan Prasad took charge as Director General of the Geological Survey of India in June 2023, succeeding S. Raju.

questions.text: According to the census of India 2011, which union territory from the following has the highest sex ratio?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Puducherry had the highest sex ratio of the Union territories, 1,037 females per 1,000 males.

questions.text: The Directive Principles of State Policy are considered fundamental in the governance of the country, but they are not enforceable by any court. This concept is mentioned in which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 37 says the Directive Principles shall not be enforceable by any court but are fundamental in the governance of the country.

questions.text: From which state in India did the legendary volleyball player Jimmy George hail?
questions.explanation: Jimmy George, the volleyball player, came from Peravoor in Kannur district, Kerala.

questions.text: Find the acceleration (in m/s²) of a body which accelerates from 5 m/s to 10 m/s in 2 seconds.
The Mawsynram receives the highest average annual rainfall in the world. It is located in which hills?
questions.explanation: Mawsynram lies in the East Khasi Hills district of Meghalaya.

questions.text: Pulakeshin II was the famous ruler of which of the following dynasties?
questions.explanation: Pulakeshin II was the greatest king of the Chalukyas of Badami; he halted Harsha's advance at the Narmada.

questions.text: In Maikal hills, which of the following minerals is deposited?
questions.explanation: NCERT names the Amarkantak plateau, the Maikal hills and the Bilaspur-Katni plateau as important bauxite areas.

questions.text: The ________ Polo Club is the home of the Ezra Cup event, the world’s oldest polo tournament, started in 1880.
questions.explanation: The Calcutta Polo Club, set up in the 1860s and among the oldest polo clubs in the world, is the home of the Ezra Cup.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Home Rule League Movement of Bal Gangadhar Tilak had its base across Karnataka and Maharashtra, but excluding which of the following?
questions.explanation: Tilak's Home Rule League, founded at Belgaum in April 1916, worked in Maharashtra (except Bombay city), Karnataka, the Central Provinces and Berar; Annie Besant's league covered the rest of India.

questions.text: For the development of agriculture, a new department, Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi was established by which of the following Sultans of Delhi?
questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Tughlaq set up the Diwan-i-Amir-Kohi, a department of agriculture, to bring more land under cultivation.

questions.text: Who presides over the House in absence of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker in the Indian political system?
options: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court
questions.explanation: When both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are absent, a member of the panel of chairpersons nominated by the Speaker presides over the Lok Sabha.

questions.text: Who is the first Indian Female Dancer to receive the highest Padma award, Padma Vibhushan?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Sonal Mansingh, who received the Padma Vibhushan in 2003 and is the only one of the four to have received it. Strictly she was the second woman dancer to receive it, after T. Balasaraswati in 1977.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. He bought strange vintage car on auction from the customs department.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'strange vintage car': 'car' is a singular countable noun and needs an article, 'a strange vintage car'. ('At auction' is the more usual phrase, but 'on auction' is also met, so the missing article is the clear error.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined idiom/phrase in the given sentence. The salesman informed the customers that if they had any questions, they could “drop a line”.
questions.explanation: To 'drop (someone) a line' is to send a short letter or note.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. His business was so successful that Mark was able to _________ at the age of 50.
questions.explanation: His success let Mark 'retire', stop working, at 50.

questions.text: Select the option with the correct spelling to replace the underlined word in the given sentence. As the roller coaster reached its highest point, a surge of “addrenalline” coursed through her veins, making her heart race with excitement.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'adrenaline'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Wine glass is very “fragile;” you must handle it with care.
questions.explanation: 'Fragile' means easily broken: 'delicate'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Please bring some milk from ______ refrigerator in the kitchen.
questions.explanation: A particular refrigerator, the one in the kitchen, takes the definite article 'the'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Tara has been playing / cricket with her friends / since noon.
questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous with 'since' and a point of time is correct: 'Tara has been playing cricket with her friends since noon.'

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. “Just when they reach” the airport, the flight had departed from the runway.
questions.explanation: The earlier action takes the past perfect and the later one the simple past: 'Just before they reached the airport, the flight had departed.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Sathish remained unwavering in the face of the assaulting gang, standing as resolute as ________.
questions.explanation: 'As resolute as steel' compares firmness to steel; 'steal' (to rob), 'still' and 'stall' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word. As long as I live, I shall be “obliged” to my Uncle.
questions.explanation: To be 'obliged' is to be grateful; its opposite is 'thankless', ungrateful.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Though Amal took continuous medication, he was not able to __________________ his injury.
questions.explanation: To 'heal' an injury is to make it well; 'heel' (part of the foot), 'hill' and 'hail' only sound alike.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four parts. Identify the part that contains a grammatical error. Surprisingly!/ dark chocolates/ are most bitterer/ in taste.
questions.explanation: 'Most bitterer' is a double comparison: 'are more bitter' (or 'most bitter').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The company's new product received “affirmative” feedback from customers.
questions.explanation: 'Affirmative' feedback is 'positive' feedback.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. I had never saw/ such a sight/ before I visited Switzerland.
questions.explanation: 'Had' takes the past participle: 'I had never seen such a sight'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'hectic'.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the underlined spelling error. The “permisible” limit of vehicle speed has been increased in India by the Road Transport Corporation.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'permissible'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who is mentally ill
questions.explanation: 'Lunatic' (an old word, now considered offensive) means a mentally ill person; a psychiatrist and a psychologist treat the mind, and a mercenary is a soldier for hire.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. She confided in me “on her anxious”, whispering her secrets between sips of coffee.
questions.explanation: One confides in someone 'about' something, and after 'her' a noun is needed: 'She confided in me about her anxiety.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate phrase to replace the underlined word. She is feeling “unwell” today, so she will not be going to work.
questions.explanation: To be 'under the weather' is to feel slightly unwell.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. She told me / her name but / I'm not remembering / it now.
questions.explanation: 'Remember' is a stative verb and is not used in the continuous: 'I don't remember it now.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. These letters are not intended to dominate your way of thinking or to persuade you to _____ 1____ to the way the writer thinks or feels. It is really a dialogue ______ 2_____ two friends talking about their problems. You must have observed the state of our society, and that there must be a _____ 3______ transformation in the way human beings live, their relation to each other, and in every way possible. We are deeply concerned for our students. The teacher is the _____ 4_____ important person in the school, for on her or him depends the future welfare of mankind. As the society is disintegrating, these schools must be centres for the regeneration ____ 5___ the mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: To 'conform to' is to fall in with: the letters do not ask you to think as the writer does. 'Confirm' only looks similar.

questions.text:

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
