They were (2)______ occupied in gymnastics and acquired an (3)______ which to us is truly (4)______. But after some millions of years of this arboreal paradise, their numbers increased to the point where the supply of coconuts was no longer (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: They were 'perpetually', that is constantly, occupied in gymnastics.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Man, it would seem, has (1)______ from arboreal apes. They lived a happy life in tropical forests, eating coconuts when they were hungry, and throwing them at each other when they were not. They were (2)______ occupied in gymnastics and acquired an (3)______ which to us is truly (4)______. But after some millions of years of this arboreal paradise, their numbers increased to the point where the supply of coconuts was no longer (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Constant gymnastics gave them 'agility', nimbleness of movement.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Man, it would seem, has (1)______ from arboreal apes. They lived a happy life in tropical forests, eating coconuts when they were hungry, and throwing them at each other when they were not. They were (2)______ occupied in gymnastics and acquired an (3)______ which to us is truly (4)______. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: An agility which to us is truly 'astonishing', that is amazing.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Man, it would seem, has (1)______ from arboreal apes. They lived a happy life in tropical forests, eating coconuts when they were hungry, and throwing them at each other when they were not. They were (2)______ occupied in gymnastics and acquired an (3)______ which to us is truly (4)______. But after some millions of years of this arboreal paradise, their numbers increased to the point where the supply of coconuts was no longer (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: As their numbers grew, the supply of coconuts was no longer 'adequate', that is enough.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: A container has 72 litre of pure milk. One–third of the milk is replaced by water in the container. Again, one–third of the mixture is extracted and an equal amount of water is added. What is the ratio of milk to water in the new mixture?
questions.explanation: Each replacement leaves 2/3 of the milk: 72 × 2/3 × 2/3 = 32 litres of milk and 40 litres of water. 32 : 40 = 4 : 5.

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 70 kg and 36 kg is:
The sum of two natural numbers is 80 and their HCF is 10. How many such pairs of numbers are possible?
questions.explanation: Write the numbers as 10a and 10b with a and b coprime: a + b = 8 gives (1, 7) and (3, 5), while (2, 6) and (4, 4) share a factor. So there are 2 pairs: 10 and 70, 30 and 50.

questions.text: Find the average of all the numbers between 21 and 70 which are divisible by 3 and leave the remainder 2.
questions.explanation: The numbers that leave remainder 2 on division by 3 are 23, 26, …, 68. They are evenly spaced, so their average is (23 + 68)/2 = 45.5.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 6% per year rate of interest for 2 years.
Ankur sells a box to Sunita earning a profit of 20%. Sunita sold it to Mohit with a 9% profit. Mohit sold it to Anjali for ₹24,525 thereby gaining 25%. At what price (in ₹) did Ankur buy the box?

The price of a pencil is increased by ₹2 this year and ₹2 in the previous year. The price of a pencil is now 30% more than the price in the previous to the previous year. How much is the price of the pencil now in ₹?
questions.explanation: With P the price two years ago, the price now is P + 4 = 1.3P, so 0.3P = 4 and P = ₹13.33. The price now is 13.33 + 4 = ₹17.33.

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 70 kg and 38 kg is:
A metallic cone of radius 12 cm and height 36 cm is melted and made into spheres of radius 3 cm each. How many spheres are there?
questions.explanation: The cone holds (1/3)π × 12² × 36 = 1,728π cm³ and each sphere (4/3)π × 3³ = 36π cm³, so 1,728π ÷ 36π = 48 spheres.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 5 years.
Find the curved surface area and total surface area, respectively, of a cylinder of radius of base 28 m and height 40 m.
The simple interest on a certain sum at the rate of 12.5% p.a. for 3 years and 6 months is ₹6,750 less than the principal. Find out the principal.
questions.explanation: The interest for 3.5 years at 12.5% is 43.75% of the principal, so the principal exceeds it by 56.25%: 0.5625P = 6,750 and P = ₹12,000.

questions.text: P and Q walk along a circular track in opposite directions. P completes two rounds of the track in 1 minute and Q completes three rounds of the track in the same time. They start from the same point and walk for 2 minutes. How many times will they meet on the track between start time and end time?
questions.explanation: Walking in opposite directions they gain a full lap on each other 2 + 3 = 5 times a minute, so they meet every 1/5 minute: 10 times in 2 minutes. The 10th meeting falls at the end time itself (both are back at the start), so 9 fall between start and end.

questions.text: OD 11 is related to KH 15 in a certain way. In the same way, ID 5 is related to EH 9. To which of the following is LK 3 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves 4 places back, the second 4 places forward and the number rises by 4: O → K, D → H, 11 → 15 and I → E, D → H, 5 → 9. So L → H, K → O and 3 → 7: HO 7.

questions.text: Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: Some gums are candies. No candy is a ball. Conclusions: (I) Atleast some candies are gums. (II) No ball is a gum.
questions.explanation: 'Some gums are candies' converts to 'some candies are gums' (I). The gums that are candies are not balls, but nothing is said of the other gums, so II need not follow.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F, and G, are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only 2 people sit between A and B when counted from the left of A. Both G and F are immediate neighbours of A. C sits immediate to the left of E. Only 2 people sit between D and G when counted from the right of D. How many people sit between E and F when counted from the left of F?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left is clockwise. Clockwise from A the seats are A, F, D, B, E, C, G: B is third to A's left, F and G flank A, C is immediately left of E and G is third to D's right. Counting to the left of F, D and B come before E: 2 people.

questions.text: OGMI is related to LDJF in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, SKQM is related to PHNJ. To which of the following is VNTP related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back: O → L, G → D, M → J, I → F and S → P, K → H, Q → N, M → J. So VNTP → SKQM.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘GOLF’ is coded as ‘1286’ and ‘WOLF’ is coded as ‘6428’. What is the code for ‘W’ in that language?
questions.explanation: O, L and F are in both words, as are 2, 6 and 8 in both codes. The letter left in WOLF is W and the digit left in its code is 4, so W = 4.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 92 + 36 – 28 + (42 ÷ 3) – (22 × 4) = 10 (Note: Interchange should be done of entire number and not individual digits of a given number)

Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All pens are razors. All razors are creams. Conclusions: (I) All pens are creams. (II) All creams are razors.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow
questions.explanation: All pens are razors and all razors are creams, so all pens are creams (I). 'All razors are creams' does not make every cream a razor, so II does not follow.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/ subtracting /multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 23, 230; 46, 460
questions.explanation: The second number is 10 times the first: 23 × 10 = 230 and 46 × 10 = 460. Likewise 52 × 10 = 520.

questions.text: 4 is related to 15 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 15 is related to 48. To which of the following is 7 related following the same logic?(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The second number is 3 times the first plus 3: 4 × 3 + 3 = 15 and 15 × 3 + 3 = 48. Likewise 7 × 3 + 3 = 24.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? DHC, GKF, JNI, MQL, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward: D, G, J, M, P; H, K, N, Q, T; C, F, I, L, O. The next cluster is PTO.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 39 ÷ 3 − 11 + 45 × 17 = 171
In a certain code language, 'BEST' is coded as '9715' and 'CLUB' is coded as '8762'. What is the code for 'B' in the given code language?
questions.explanation: B is the only letter in both words and 7 the only digit in both codes, so B = 7.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘TIME’ is written as ‘3629’ and ‘BEND’ is written as ‘4582’. How is ‘E’ written in that code language?
questions.explanation: E is the only letter in both words and 2 the only digit in both codes, so E = 2.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 42, 48, 54, 60, 66, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 6 more than the one before: 66 + 6 = 72.

questions.text: The original non-metamorphic rock that undergoes profound physical or chemical changes leading to the formation of a metamorphic rock is known as:
questions.explanation: A protolith is the original rock from which a metamorphic rock forms. Regolith is the loose material over bedrock, and laterite a deeply weathered soil.

questions.text: According to the Census of India 2011, what was the total population of India?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 counted about 121 crore people: 1.21 billion.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty mentioned in the Indian constitution?
options: To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom
To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
To obey parents and discharge our family responsibilities
To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, National Anthem
questions.explanation: Article 51A lists the Fundamental Duties; obeying parents is not one of them. The other three options are duties (a), (b) and (c).

questions.text: Which of the following are the amounts of nutrients in a keto diet?
options: High protein and fat, carbohydrates in a low amount
Only taking high number of vitamins and minerals
High carbohydrate, proper amount of protein and low fat
High amount of fat, adequate protein and low carbohydrate
questions.explanation: A ketogenic diet is high in fat, moderate in protein and very low in carbohydrate, so the body burns fat for energy.

questions.text: Padma awardee Arjun Singh Dhurve is related to which of the following folk dances?
questions.explanation: Arjun Singh Dhurve of Dindori, Madhya Pradesh, received the Padma Shri in 2022 for keeping alive the dance and songs of the Baiga tribe.

questions.text: Magnolia and Laurel trees are found in which type of forest in India?
questions.explanation: NCERT names magnolia, laurel, cinchona and wattle among the trees of the temperate forests (sholas) of the southern hills, part of India's montane forests.

questions.text: Duare Ration Scheme, which has been deemed legally void by the high court, was launched by which of the following states?
questions.explanation: West Bengal launched its Duare Ration (ration at the doorstep) scheme in 2021; in September 2022 a Calcutta High Court division bench held it ultra vires the National Food Security Act, 2013.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In 1927, where was the conference against colonial oppression and imperialism, in which Jawaharlal Nehru participated on behalf of Indian National Congress, held?
questions.explanation: Nehru represented the Indian National Congress at the Congress of Oppressed Nationalities in Brussels in February 1927, which founded the League against Imperialism.

questions.text: Who became the first Indian woman to be inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame?
questions.explanation: Diana Edulji, a former India captain, was inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame in 2023, the first Indian woman to be so honoured.

questions.text: In January 2023, who was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Bihar for the ninth time?
questions.explanation: Nitish Kumar was sworn in as Chief Minister of Bihar for a record ninth time on 28 January 2024, after rejoining the NDA. (The question's 'January 2023' is a year out; none of the others has held the post nine times.)

questions.text: The ‘Rath Yatra’ festival of Puri is celebrated as the sacred journey of which of the following Hindu deities?
questions.explanation: Puri's Rath Yatra takes Lord Jagannath, with Balabhadra and Subhadra, by chariot to the Gundicha Temple.

questions.text: Who among the following personalities from the Carnatic Music correctly represent the ‘Trinity of Carnatic Music'?
options: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri
MS Subbalakshmi, DK Pattammal and ML Vasanthakumari
Manambuchavadi Venkatasubbayyar, Tyagaraja and Muthuswami Dikshitar
questions.explanation: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri, contemporaries of the late 18th and early 19th centuries, are the Trinity of Carnatic music.

questions.text: Who is the chairman of the State Planning Board?
questions.explanation: A state's Planning Board is chaired by its Chief Minister, as the Planning Commission was by the Prime Minister.

questions.text: The Ashokan inscriptions of Afghanistan are written in Aramaic and ________ scripts.
questions.explanation: Ashoka's inscriptions in Afghanistan, such as the bilingual rock inscription at Kandahar, are in Greek and Aramaic.

questions.text: Revenue account includes items related to the _______.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives all three: government accounts in India are kept on a cash basis, so the revenue account takes in every revenue receipt and expenditure of the year, including arrears that belong to earlier years and amounts paid in advance for later ones. (In accrual accounting, as in an income and expenditure account, only items of the current year belong, which would point to 'current financial year'.)

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a cropping season in India?
questions.explanation: India's cropping seasons are kharif, rabi and zaid; 'Fang' is not one of them.

questions.text: Which book has been authored by Rabindra Bharali?
options: The Forgotten Forms of Hindustani Music
questions.explanation: Rabindra Bharali, a musicologist, wrote 'The Forgotten Forms of Hindustani Music' (2008), on lesser-known forms such as chaturang and trivat. 'The Music Room' is Namita Devidayal's memoir.

questions.text: How many gold medals did Maharashtra win to top the medal tally at the 37th National Games event held in Goa?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra topped the 37th National Games in Goa (2023) with 80 gold medals, 228 in all.

questions.text: The element with atomic number 59 lies in which block of the Periodic Table?
questions.explanation: Atomic number 59 is praseodymium, a lanthanide; the lanthanides fill the 4f orbitals and belong to the f-block.

questions.text: Which bonding material was mainly used to join the stones or bricks of 'The Great Bath' of the Harappan Civilisation?
questions.explanation: The floor of the Great Bath at Mohenjodaro was made watertight with bricks set on edge in a mortar of gypsum.

questions.text: Andal was one of the most famous women ___________ saints.
questions.explanation: Andal, the only woman among the twelve Alvars, was a Tamil Vaishnava poet-saint. The Nayanars were devotees of Shiva.

questions.text: Which of the following awards is NOT conferred for excellence in dance?
questions.explanation: The Lalit Kala Akademi honours the visual arts. The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and the Kalidas Samman both count dance among their fields, and the Padma Shri is given in every field.

questions.text: As per Census of India 2011, which of the following states has the highest child sex ratio (in the age group of 0-6 years)?
questions.explanation: In Census 2011 Mizoram's child sex ratio, about 970 girls per 1,000 boys aged 0-6, was the highest of these four: Chhattisgarh and Kerala were in the 960s and Rajasthan below 890.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which reform was initiated by Lord Ripon for the welfare of labourers?
questions.explanation: The Indian Factories Act of 1881, passed under Lord Ripon, was India's first factory law: it barred children under seven from factories and limited the hours of child workers.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. She showed this plant and talked about “it’s medicinal properties”.
questions.explanation: The possessive of 'it' is 'its', with no apostrophe ('it's' means 'it is'); a plant's healing qualities are its 'medicinal properties'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in simple future tense form. I loved.
questions.explanation: The simple future is 'will' + the base form: 'I will love.' 'I love' is the simple present and 'I had loved' the past perfect.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. “It’s really __________ to incorporate changes at the last minute,” she said.
questions.explanation: After 'it's really' the blank needs an adjective: 'really difficult'. 'Difficulty' is a noun, and 'most difficult' does not follow 'really'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank. The judge declared that the red car went ___________ than the blue car.
questions.explanation: 'Than' needs the comparative, and for distance it is 'farther': 'went farther than the blue car'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Embarrassment' is spelt correctly; the others should be 'occasion', 'receive' and 'accommodate'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word 'yelling' in the given sentence. The shouting and exclaiming gestures of Smita led to the whispering regarding her behaviour, and everyone in the party started monitoring her.
questions.explanation: 'Yelling' is loud shouting; its opposite in the sentence is 'whispering'. 'Shouting' and 'exclaiming' are close in meaning to it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. An axe to grind
options: To have a selfish reason that influences the actions
To tackle a problem in a bold and direct fashion
questions.explanation: To have 'an axe to grind' is to have a private, selfish reason for what one does.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. One of them contains an error. Select the segment that contains the error from the given options. She has been speaking / to him on / the subject / many times.
questions.explanation: 'Many times' counts completed occasions, which takes the present perfect, not the continuous: 'She has spoken to him on the subject many times.'

questions.text: The given sentence is divided into three segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. If there is no error, select ‘No error’. She learnt / how to play a piano / when she was in Class 6th.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives this segment: playing a musical instrument takes 'the', 'how to play the piano'. ('Class 6th' mixes 'Class 6' and 'the 6th class', but is common in Indian English.)

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. She always wears a “bizzare” combination of clothes.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'bizarre', meaning very strange.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. Despite the setbacks, the team decided to persevere and keep working on the project, believing it could be a _______ for their company.
questions.explanation: A 'game-changer' is something that changes a situation decisively. The others mean something very hard to find, avoiding the point, and a hopeless search.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The act of transferring one's authority to another
questions.explanation: Delegation is the act of entrusting one's authority or duties to another.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. It is worth noting that the “possible from him” being voted as the class monitor is next to zero.
questions.explanation: After 'the' a noun is needed, followed by 'of': 'the possibility of him being voted as the class monitor'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'course'.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. The speech you made today was “sillier” and irrelevant.
questions.explanation: Nothing is being compared, so the positive degree is needed, matching 'irrelevant': 'silly and irrelevant'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the given word. Merciful
questions.explanation: 'Merciful' means showing kindness and forgiveness; its opposite is 'cruel'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'isolated' from the given sentence. A Greek mythological story says that Echo was the most beautiful nymph who lived in the lovely and lonely mountains of Greece and is believed to be garrulous too.
questions.explanation: 'Isolated' means remote and solitary: the 'lonely' mountains.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Evasive
questions.explanation: 'Evasive' means avoiding a direct or honest answer; its opposite is 'truthful'. 'Elusive' and 'obscure' are close to synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Diligent
questions.explanation: 'Diligent' means hard-working: 'industrious'. 'Lazy' is its opposite.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In a small village, lived a milkmaid ______1______ sold the milk that she ____2_____ from her cows. She _____3_____ carry the milk in a big mud pitcher. One day, as she was walking _____4_____ the big pitcher full of milk on her head, she started to imagine all the things she wished to do with the money she would _____5______ from selling the milk.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is the relative pronoun for a person, the subject of 'sold': 'a milkmaid who sold the milk'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In a small village, lived a milkmaid ______1______ sold the milk that she ____2_____ from her cows. She _____3_____ carry the milk in a big mud pitcher. One day, as she was walking _____4_____ the big pitcher full of milk on her head, she started to imagine all the things she wished to do with the money she would _____5______ from selling the milk.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The milk that she 'got', that is obtained, from her own cows; she did not buy it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In a small village, lived a milkmaid ______1______ sold the milk that she ____2_____ from her cows. She _____3_____ carry the milk in a big mud pitcher. One day, as she was walking _____4_____ the big pitcher full of milk on her head, she started to imagine all the things she wished to do with the money she would _____5______ from selling the milk.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Would' expresses a past habit: 'She would carry the milk in a big mud pitcher.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In a small village, lived a milkmaid ______1______ sold the milk that she ____2_____ from her cows. She _____3_____ carry the milk in a big mud pitcher. One day, as she was walking _____4_____ the big pitcher full of milk on her head, she started to imagine all the things she wished to do with the money she would _____5______ from selling the milk.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: She was walking 'with' the big pitcher on her head.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In a small village, lived a milkmaid ______1______ sold the milk that she ____2_____ from her cows. She _____3_____ carry the milk in a big mud pitcher. One day, as she was walking _____4_____ the big pitcher full of milk on her head, she started to imagine all the things she wished to do with the money she would _____5______ from selling the milk.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: One 'earns' money by selling something: the money she would 'earn' from selling the milk.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Three cubes of sides 1 cm, 6 cm and 8 cm are melted to form a new cube. Find one-fourth of the surface area of the new cube.
questions.explanation: The new cube's volume is 1 + 216 + 512 = 729 cm³, so its side is 9 cm and its surface area 6 × 81 = 486 cm². One-fourth of that is 121.5 cm².

questions.text: An item was sold for ₹40 with a profit of 15%. If it were sold for ₹36, then what would have been the percentage of profit or loss? (rounded off to 1 decimal places).
questions.explanation: The cost price is 40/1.15. Selling at ₹36 gives 36 × 1.15/40 = 41.4/40 = 1.035 times the cost: a profit of 3.5%.

questions.text: The average of 7 numbers is 10.8. If the average of the first three be 10.5 and that of the last three is 11.4, find the value of the middle number.
questions.explanation: Total of all 7 = 7 × 10.8 = 75.6; first three = 31.5 and last three = 34.2. The middle number is 75.6 − 31.5 − 34.2 = 9.9.

questions.text: The lengths of two sides of a parallelogram are 6 cm and 20 cm. What is the sum of the squares of the diagonals of the parallelogram (in cm²)?
questions.explanation: In a parallelogram the sum of the squares of the diagonals is 2(a² + b²) = 2(6² + 20²) = 2 × 436 = 872 cm².

questions.text: If 5 + x, 2x + 7, 6x + 9 and y are in proportion when x = 2, then find the value of y.
questions.explanation: With x = 2 the terms are 7, 11, 21 and y. In proportion 7 : 11 = 21 : y, so y = 11 × 21/7 = 33.

questions.text: The average of 11 consecutive numbers is 30. The smallest number among these is:
questions.explanation: The average of 11 consecutive numbers is the middle (6th) one, 30, so the smallest is 30 − 5 = 25.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹4000 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
The average of 10 observations is 46. It was realised later that an observation was misread as 42 in place of 142. Find the correct average.
questions.explanation: The total was 10 × 46 = 460; correcting 42 to 142 adds 100, so the correct average is 560/10 = 56.

questions.text: On a circular race track of 2500 m, Sahil and Reena are running in the same direction at speeds of 27 km/h and 45 km/h, respectively. After how much time will they meet each other for the first time?
questions.explanation: Running the same way, Reena gains 45 − 27 = 18 km/h = 5 m/s on Sahil. They first meet when she has gained a full lap: 2500/5 = 500 seconds.

questions.text: Two trains of lengths 108 metre and 112 metre are running at speeds of 45 km/h and 54 km/h, respectively, towards each other on parallel tracks. In how many seconds will they cross each other?
questions.explanation: Towards each other the relative speed is 45 + 54 = 99 km/h = 99 × 5/18 = 27.5 m/s. They cover 108 + 112 = 220 m in 220/27.5 = 8 seconds.

questions.text: The average age of 6 children and their father is 13 years, and this average is reduced by 4 years if the father is excluded. How old is the father?
questions.explanation: All 7 together total 7 × 13 = 91 years; the 6 children alone average 9, a total of 54. The father is 91 − 54 = 37.

questions.text: If the radius of a right circular cylinder is decreased by 40% and its height is increased by 75%, its volume will be decreased by:
questions.explanation: Volume varies as r²h: 0.6² × 1.75 = 0.36 × 1.75 = 0.63 of the original, a decrease of 37%.

questions.text: The marked price of an item is 50% more than its cost price. The shopkeeper offers two successive discounts of 10% and 15%. What is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Taking the cost as 100, the marked price is 150 and the selling price 150 × 0.9 × 0.85 = 114.75: a profit of 14.75%.

questions.text: By selling an article for ₹20, a dealer makes a profit of 10%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹, rounded off to two decimal place) so as to make a profit of 25%?
questions.explanation: The cost price is 20/1.1 = 200/11 ≈ ₹18.18. For a 25% profit he must sell at 1.25 × 200/11 = 250/11 ≈ ₹22.73, an increase of 250/11 − 20 = 30/11 ≈ ₹2.73.

questions.text: In how many years will ₹4,000 invested at the rate of 18% per annum simple interest amounts to ₹5,800?
questions.explanation: The interest is 5,800 − 4,000 = ₹1,800, and one year earns 4,000 × 18/100 = ₹720, so it takes 1,800/720 = 2.5 years.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹4000 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 2 years.
TOVR is related to UPWS in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, QLSO is related to RMTP. To which of the following is NIPL related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: TOVR → UPWS and QLSO → RMTP. So NIPL → OJQM.

questions.text: Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: Some books are notes. All notes are copies. Conclusions: (I) Some books are copies. (II) No books is copies.
questions.explanation: The books that are notes are also copies, so some books are copies (I). II contradicts I, so it cannot follow.

questions.text: S, U, B, J, E, C and T are sitting around a circular table facing the center (but not necessarily in the same order). C is sitting to the immediate right of T. U is an immediate neighbour of both T and E. Only one person is sitting between C and S when counted from the right of C. B is sitting to the immediate left of E. Who are the immediate neighbours of J?
questions.explanation: Going round to the right the order is B, E, U, T, C, J, S: C to T's immediate right, U between T and E, B to E's immediate left, and S second to the right of C, which leaves J between C and S. J's neighbours are S and C.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. BCD, FGH, JKL, NOP, ?
questions.explanation: Each cluster is three consecutive letters, and each starts 4 places after the last one began: B, F, J, N, R. The next is RST.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘rose are similar’ is written as ‘ki ko ku’ and ‘rose has thorns’ is coded as ‘ke ki ka’. How is ‘rose’ coded in that language?
questions.explanation: 'rose' is the only word in both phrases and 'ki' the only code in both, so rose = ki.

questions.text: 23 is related to 62 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 37 is related to 104. To which ofthe following is 19 related, following the same logic?(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The second number is three times the first minus 7: 23 × 3 − 7 = 62 and 37 × 3 − 7 = 104. Likewise 19 × 3 − 7 = 50.

questions.text: P, Q, R, S, T and U are six friends sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order), having their breakfast. U is sitting exactly between Q and S and is third to the right of T. R is sitting to the immediate left of S. Who is the immediate neighbour of both P and R?
questions.explanation: With six seats, U third to the right of T sits opposite T. Q and S flank U, and R is to S's immediate left, so going round to the right from T the order is T, R, S, U, Q, P. P's neighbours are Q and T, and R's are T and S: T sits next to both.

questions.text: AS 9 is related to UU 2 in a certain way. In the same way, BT 6 is related to VV −1. To which of the following is HG 9 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves 6 back, the second 2 forward and the number falls by 7: AS 9 → UU 2 and BT 6 → VV −1. So HG 9 → BI 2.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series? 263, 268, 278, 293, 313, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 5, 10, 15, 20, rising by 5 each time, so the next is 25: 313 + 25 = 338.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘ORANGE’ is written as ‘LIZMTV’ and ‘PURPLE’ is written as ‘KFIKOV’. What is the code for ‘MAGENTA’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its mirror in the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y, ...): O → L, R → I, A → Z and so on. MAGENTA becomes NZTVMGZ.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘she can sing’ is written as ‘dq tk dp’ and ‘sing with me’ is writtenas ‘az dq js’. How is ‘sing’ writtenin the given language?
questions.explanation: 'sing' is the only word in both sentences and 'dq' the only code in both, so sing = dq.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/ subtracting /multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 34, 24; 85, 75
questions.explanation: In each pair the second number is 10 less than the first: 34 − 10 = 24 and 85 − 10 = 75. Likewise 66 − 10 = 56.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) of the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 17 – 9 + 20 × 4 ÷ 5 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 17 + 9 − 20 ÷ 4 × 5 = 17 + 9 − 25 = 1.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘written on paper’ is written as ‘ma rc gp’ and ‘paper and pen’ is writtenas ‘hk ma bo’. How will ‘paper’ be writtenin that language?
questions.explanation: 'paper' is the only word in both phrases and 'ma' the only code in both, so paper = ma.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 39 + 3 ÷ 12 − 33 × 11 =?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 39 − 3 × 12 + 33 ÷ 11 = 39 − 36 + 3 = 6.

questions.text: This question has two statements followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the given statements. Statements: Some metres are litres. No litre is a gram. Conclusions (I) Some grams are not metres (II) All grams being metres is a possibility.
questions.explanation: No litre is a gram, but the metres that are not litres may or may not be grams, so all grams being metres is possible (II follows) and 'some grams are not metres' is not certain (I does not follow).

questions.text: At which of the following places is the Lalbagh Flower Show organised, where thousands of flower varieties are put on display in different forms with a particular theme (which changes every year) during the exhibition?
questions.explanation: The Lalbagh Flower Show is held at the Lalbagh Botanical Garden in Bengaluru, around Independence Day and Republic Day.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the autobiography 'Lone Fox Dancing: My Autobiography'?
questions.explanation: 'Lone Fox Dancing: My Autobiography' (2017) is Ruskin Bond's account of his life.

questions.text: Stunted growth, which is common in children growing up in extreme poverty, is a sure sign of ____________.
questions.explanation: Stunting, being too short for one's age, is the mark of long-term undernutrition in childhood.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a service of micro finance institution?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives micro deposit. Microfinance is usually described as micro loans (microcredit), micro savings and micro insurance, and India's microfinance companies (NBFC-MFIs) may not accept deposits from the public; but savings are themselves a kind of deposit, so the line between the two options is thin.

questions.text: The ‘Mangla’ oil field is located in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: The Mangala oil field, discovered by Cairn in 2004, is in Barmer district of Rajasthan.

questions.text: When did Bindusara ascend the Maurya throne?
questions.explanation: Bindusara succeeded his father Chandragupta Maurya in about 297 BCE (dates for this period are approximate).

questions.text: According to Census of India 2011, which is the largest religious community in India?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Hindus made up about 79.8% of India's population, the largest religious community.

questions.text: To which of the following classes of compounds does cyclohexane belong?
questions.explanation: Cyclohexane is a saturated ring of six carbon atoms with no aromatic character, so it is an alicyclic compound; benzene, by contrast, is benzenoid aromatic.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following years did the battle of Plassey take place?
questions.explanation: At Plassey, on 23 June 1757, the East India Company under Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal.

questions.text: Women's Reservation Bill 2023 [The Constitution (One Hundred Twenty-Eighth Amendment) Bill, 2023] was introduced in Lok Sabha on __________________.
questions.explanation: The Constitution (One Hundred Twenty-Eighth Amendment) Bill, reserving a third of seats for women, was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 19 September 2023, the first day in the new Parliament building; it passed the Lok Sabha on 20 September and the Rajya Sabha on 21 September.

questions.text: Which of the following Union Territories of India marks the lowest poverty in National Multidimensional Poverty Index: A Progress Review 2023?
questions.explanation: In NITI Aayog's 2023 review (NFHS-5 data, 2019-21) 0.85% of Puducherry's people were multidimensionally poor, against 1.11% in Lakshadweep, 3.43% in Delhi and 3.52% in Chandigarh.

questions.text: By what name is the species of Scaphopoda Mollusca 'Dentalium' commonly known?
questions.explanation: Dentalium belongs to the Scaphopoda, molluscs with tapering tubular shells open at both ends, commonly called tusk shells.

questions.text: Which Indian actress from the following, is also a popular dancer and received the Smita Patil Memorial award for her role in the movie Damini?
questions.explanation: Meenakshi Seshadri, a trained classical dancer, played the title role in 'Damini' (1993), the year she received the Smita Patil Memorial Award.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India provides for the promotion of international peace and security?
questions.explanation: Article 51, a Directive Principle, asks the State to promote international peace and security, keep just and honourable relations between nations, respect international law and settle disputes by arbitration.

questions.text: Which Hindustani classical musician is credited with popularising the Sarangi as a solo classical instrument?
questions.explanation: Pandit Ram Narayan made the sarangi, long an accompanying instrument, a solo concert instrument.

questions.text: The Narora ________ Power Station is located in Uttar Pradesh.
questions.explanation: The Narora Atomic Power Station is on the Ganga in Bulandshahr district of Uttar Pradesh.

questions.text: Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma is associated with which of the following dances?
questions.explanation: Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma was a Kuchipudi dancer, famous for female roles such as Satyabhama.

questions.text: _________ was/were the mascot(s) of the Women’s Asian Hockey Champions Trophy in 2023.
questions.explanation: Juhi, an elephant, was the mascot of the 2023 Women's Asian Champions Trophy, held in Ranchi and won by India.

questions.text: Groundwater is an important source of water. The top level of the groundwater layer is called:
questions.explanation: The water table is the upper surface of the saturated zone of groundwater.

questions.text: Sanchi stupa was rediscovered in the year ________ by General Henry Taylor.
questions.explanation: General Henry Taylor, a British officer, was the first Westerner to record the Sanchi stupa, in 1818.

questions.text: If the server manages to land a legal serve and the receiver is unable to return the ball, it is known as an ace and the server gets the point. Which of the following sport is referred here?
questions.explanation: In tennis an ace is a legal serve the receiver fails to touch, winning the point for the server.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Where of the following was Bal Gangadhar Tilak’s Home Rule Movement active?
questions.explanation: Tilak's Home Rule League, founded at Belgaum in April 1916, worked in Maharashtra (except Bombay city), Karnataka, the Central Provinces and Berar; Annie Besant's league covered the rest of India.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following cities was the headquarters of Theosophical Society established in British India?
questions.explanation: The Theosophical Society moved its headquarters to Adyar, Madras (now Chennai), in 1882.

questions.text: Which of the following Parts of the Indian Constitution mentions about the relations between the Union and the States?
questions.explanation: Part XI (Articles 245 to 263) deals with the relations between the Union and the States.

questions.text: In November 2023, who was appointed as the Chief Information Commissioner of India?
questions.explanation: Heeralal Samariya was sworn in as Chief Information Commissioner on 6 November 2023.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelled sentence.
options: The liberian told the childrean to return their boooks by Friday.
The librarian told the children to return their books by Friday.
The libraian told the childrean to return their books by Friday.
The librarian told the childern to return their books by Fryday.
questions.explanation: Only this sentence spells 'librarian', 'children', 'books' and 'Friday' correctly.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'efficient'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence. She is an “epitome” of grace.
questions.explanation: An 'epitome' is a perfect example of a quality: 'example'.

questions.text: Change the following into superlative degree. She is taller than other girls in the class.
options: In the class she is taller than other girls.
She is the tallest girl in the class.
No other girl in the class is as tall as she.
She is tall girl in the class.
questions.explanation: 'Taller than other girls in the class' becomes, in the superlative degree, 'She is the tallest girl in the class'. 'No other girl ... as tall as she' is the positive degree.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. The ________(sarcastic) comments by her husband made her feel uncomfortable, and she decided to walk out of the relationship.
questions.explanation: 'Sarcastic' remarks mock and wound; the opposite is 'gracious', kind and courteous.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The speaker delivered an “engaging” speech that inspired the audience.
questions.explanation: 'Engaging' means attractive and holding the attention: 'captivating'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The 100-year-old banyan was blown off in the storm last night.
questions.explanation: A tree knocked over by the wind is 'blown down' (or uprooted); 'blown off' is said of something carried away from a surface, such as a roof or a hat.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The teacher “called up the class” due to the sudden snowstorm.
questions.explanation: To 'call off' is to cancel, as a sudden snowstorm would make the teacher do; to 'call up' is to telephone or summon.

questions.text: Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence to make it grammatically correct. Meerut is “farthest” from Delhi.
questions.explanation: Meerut is not compared with any other place, so the positive degree is needed: 'Meerut is far from Delhi.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The dog / eager wagged / its tail when / it saw its owner.
questions.explanation: A verb is modified by an adverb: 'The dog eagerly wagged its tail when it saw its owner.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The soldiers / sacrifice their lives / to guarding / the nation and its boundaries.
questions.explanation: The infinitive of purpose takes the base form of the verb: 'sacrifice their lives to guard the nation'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given phrase. Reading between the lines
options: Avoiding reading and engaging in gossips
Understanding a deeper or hidden meaning
questions.explanation: To 'read between the lines' is to find a meaning that is implied rather than stated.

questions.text: Identify the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in brackets. The teacher commended the student for his (diligent) efforts.
questions.explanation: 'Diligent' means hard-working and careful; its opposite is 'lazy'. The other three are its synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She had a ______ for creating beautiful artwork.
questions.explanation: A 'talent' for something is a natural ability: 'a talent for creating beautiful artwork'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Meticulous
questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' means showing great attention to detail: 'precise'. 'Negligent' and 'careless' are its opposites.

questions.text: Select the correct idiom to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence. Roma was “the dearest child of her parents.”
options: At sixes and sevens with her parents
The apple of her parents’ eyes
The star of her parents’ eyes
The body and soul of her parents
questions.explanation: 'The apple of someone's eye' is the person they cherish most.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase. One who is a newcomer
questions.explanation: A 'neophyte' is a newcomer or beginner. A polyglot speaks many languages, a nepotist favours relatives and a narcissist is excessively self-admiring.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical/spelling error. According to Mr. Sharma / the news have come / as another blow / to the family members.
questions.explanation: 'News' is uncountable and takes a singular verb: 'the news has come'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The sudden plot twist in the story added an element of __________ that kept readers on the edge of their seats.
questions.explanation: Only 'ambiguity', uncertainty about what will happen, could keep readers on the edge of their seats; monotony, predictability and redundancy would bore them.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word. Majority of communication satelites are placed in geostationary orbits around the earth, which means that their speed matches the rate of its rotation.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'satellites', with a double 'l'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Despite her background role in the past, Ms Navalnaya has always been a crucial supporter of (1)....... husband and was instrumental in getting him out of Russia for (2)....... treatment when he was poisoned with Novichok nerve agent in 2020. She has been (3)........... as the 'First Lady' of the Russian opposition. And Alexei said himself that he could not continue his increasingly desperate and one-sided fight against the Kremlin without her. Their very public love story and family life - they have two children - (4)......... seen as an inspiration for their supporters. Yulia Ambrosimova was born in Moscow in 1976, daughter of the respected scientist Boris Ambrosimov. As economics graduate, she had a career in banking but (5)........ her job to bring up their two children when Alexei rose to prominence as an opposition politician.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Ms Navalnaya supported her own husband, so the singular possessive: 'her husband'.

As economics graduate, she had a career in banking but (5)........ her job to bring up their two children when Alexei rose to prominence as an opposition politician.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: He had been poisoned with a nerve agent, so she got him out of Russia for 'urgent' treatment.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'She has been described as' the 'First Lady' of the Russian opposition: a label others have given her.
