questions.text: What will be the ratio of simple interest earned by a certain amount at the same rate of interest for 12 years and that for 15 years?
questions.explanation: With the same principal and rate, simple interest is proportional to the time: 12 : 15 = 4 : 5.

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 66 kg and 36 kg is:

A shopkeeper offered following four different discount schemes for buyers on an item. A. Two successive discounts of 8% B. A discount of 11% followed by a discount of 5%. C. Successive discounts of 13% and 3% D. A discount of 16%. If Rajiv wants to purchase the item from this shop at minimum price, he should opt for the discount scheme:
questions.explanation: The share of the price left after each scheme: A 0.92 × 0.92 = 0.8464, B 0.89 × 0.95 = 0.8455, C 0.87 × 0.97 = 0.8439 and D 0.84. D leaves the lowest price.

questions.text: A metallic sphere with a radius of 35 cm is melted and subsequently transformed into several small solid cones, each having a diameter of 14 cm and a height of 4 cm. How many cones are formed as a result of this process?
Reena buys an iron for ₹900 and sells it at a loss of 12%. What is the selling price of the iron?
If the average of the first 15 multiples of 9 is x, then x is:
questions.explanation: The multiples 9, 18, …, 135 are evenly spaced, so their average is (9 + 135)/2 = 72.

questions.text: If the HCF of 156 and 96 is expressible in the form of 156 × 12 + 96A, then the value of A is:

A student saves an average of ₹4,000 per month for the first three months. How much should be saved (in ₹) on an average per month over the next 9 months to average ₹4,375 per month over the whole year?
questions.explanation: The year needs 12 × 4,375 = ₹52,500. The first three months gave 3 × 4,000 = ₹12,000, so the other 9 months need ₹40,500: ₹4,500 a month.

questions.text: The speed of a car is 81 km/hr. The distance covered by the car in 24 seconds is:
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 8% per year rate of interest for 2 years.
The speed of a boat in still water is 12 km/h and the stream flows at a speed of 3 km/h. The distance travelled in the boat downstream in 24 minutes is:
questions.explanation: Downstream the boat goes 12 + 3 = 15 km/h; in 24 minutes (2/5 hour) that is 15 × 2/5 = 6 km.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 as a sum borrowed at 9% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
The price of an article is reduced by 40% and its sale is increased by 80%. Find the net effect on revenue.
questions.explanation: Revenue = price × sales: 0.6 × 1.8 = 1.08, an increase of 8%.

questions.text: JA 88 is related to OF 77 in a certain way. In the same way, DT 55 is related to IY 44.To which of the following is LH 33 related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 5 places forward and the number falls by 11: J → O, A → F, 88 → 77 and D → I, T → Y, 55 → 44. So L → Q, H → M and 33 → 22: QM 22.

questions.text: PUQV is related to RWSX in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, JOKP is related to LQMR. To which of the following is MRNS related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: PUQV → RWSX and JOKP → LQMR. So MRNS → OTPU.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BUYS’ is coded as ‘5173’ and ‘YOLK’ is coded as ‘6458’.What is the code for ‘Y’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: Y is the only letter in both words and 5 the only digit in both codes, so Y = 5.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘−’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged and ‘+’ and ‘×’ are interchanged? 7 + 5 ÷ 4 + 5 ÷ 36 − 4 × 7 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 7 × 5 − 4 × 5 − 36 ÷ 4 + 7 = 35 − 20 − 9 + 7 = 13.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? JLF, KOI, LRL, MUO, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move forward 1 (J, K, L, M, N), second letters forward 3 (L, O, R, U, X) and third letters forward 3 (F, I, L, O, R): NXR.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No crow is a parrot. No parrot is sparrow. Conclusions: (I) No crow is a sparrow. (II) No parrot is a crow.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: No crow is a parrot, so no parrot is a crow (II). Crows and sparrows are each kept apart from parrots, but nothing links crows to sparrows, so I does not follow.

questions.text: Given below are two sets of numbers. In each set of numbers, a certain mathematical operation on the first number results in the second number. Which of the options follows the same operation as given in the question? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (21, 10) (87, 43)
questions.explanation: The second number is (first − 1)/2: (21 − 1)/2 = 10 and (87 − 1)/2 = 43. Likewise (27 − 1)/2 = 13.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BASE’ is coded as ‘2416’ and ‘SOUP’ is coded as ‘3719’. What is the code for ‘S’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: S is the only letter in both words and 1 the only digit in both codes, so S = 1.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F, and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order).Only 2 people sit between G and A when counted from the right of G.Only 2 people sit between E and D when counted from the right of E.E is an immediate neighbour of A.Only 2 people sit between B and C when counted from the left of C. What is the position of F with respect to B?
questions.explanation: Counting to the right from G, the only seating that fits is G, B, E, A, C, D, F: two people (B, E) sit between G and A, two (A, C) between E and D, E is next to A, and counting left from C two (A, E) sit between C and B. To B's left come G and then F, so F is second to the left of B.

questions.text: Six students Amit, Shivam, Dinesh, Kamlesh, Nihar and Roshan are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Amit is sitting to the immediate right of Shivam. Dinesh is sitting second to the right of Shivam. Nihar is an immediate neighbour of both Dinesh and Roshan. Who is sitting to the immediate right of Roshan?
questions.explanation: Going to the right from Shivam: Shivam, Amit, Dinesh. Nihar must take the seat after Dinesh (Amit is on his other side) and Roshan the one after Nihar, which leaves Kamlesh, on Roshan's immediate right.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All lakes are rivers. All rivers are dams. Conclusions: (I) At least some dams are lakes. (II) All rivers are lakes.
questions.explanation: All lakes are rivers and all rivers are dams, so all lakes are dams and some dams are lakes (I). That all lakes are rivers does not make all rivers lakes, so II does not follow.

questions.text: 10 is related to 99 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 14 is related to 195. To which of the following is 22 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is related to its square minus 1: 10² − 1 = 99 and 14² − 1 = 195. So 22² − 1 = 483.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 13 21 33 49 ? 93
In a certain code language, ‘find this clue’ is written as ‘ak dh fk’ and ‘clue for you’ is written as ‘sg fk bo’. How is ‘clue’ written in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'clue' is the only word in both sentences and 'fk' the only code in both, so clue = fk.

questions.text: If the Glycemic Index (GI) of a specific food is from 70 to 100, then the type of that food is:
questions.explanation: A glycaemic index of 70 or more marks a high-GI food; 56 to 69 is medium and 55 or less low.

questions.text: In the final match of the Asian Games _________ held in Jakarta, Indonesia, India secured gold by defeating South Korea with a score of 2-1 in football.
questions.explanation: India beat South Korea 2-1 in the football final of the 1962 Asian Games in Jakarta to win the gold.

questions.text: As per the World Happiness Index 2023, which of the following countries secured the highest rank?
questions.explanation: In the World Happiness Report 2023 Nepal ranked 78th, the highest of these four; Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh were all placed below 100th.

questions.text: The 'Secular' word in the Indian Constitution was added to the constitution by __________ Constitutional Amendment Act.
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added the words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.

questions.text: Hariharan was conferred the Padma Shri in 2004 for his contribution to which of the following fields?
questions.explanation: Hariharan, the playback and ghazal singer, received the Padma Shri in 2004 for art (music).

questions.text: Atmospheric temperature usually decreases with altitude, but sometimes this phenomenon gets reversed in the troposphere. This phenomenon is known as _________.
questions.explanation: When temperature rises with height instead of falling, the air has a temperature inversion, common on calm, clear winter nights.

questions.text: Diwan-i-Am, containing the marble canopy ornamented with beautiful panels of pietra dura work, is a part of which monument?
questions.explanation: The Diwan-i-Am of Shah Jahan's Red Fort in Delhi has a marble canopy over the emperor's throne, set off by pietra dura panels.

questions.text: The 2011 census was the ____________ official survey conducted in India.
questions.explanation: The 2011 census was India's 15th, counting from the first in 1872, and the 7th since Independence.

questions.text: Which of the following characteristics was used by Aristotle to classify animals?
questions.explanation: Aristotle grouped animals by where they lived: on land, in water or in the air.

questions.text: Which of the following are recognised as final goods while estimating the gross domestic product in India? a. Wheat purchased for making roti in a house b. Wheat purchased for making roti in a hotel c. Tea bags used to make tea in a house d. Tea bags used to make tea in a university hostel canteen
questions.explanation: Goods households buy for their own use are final goods. Wheat bought by a hotel and tea bags used by a canteen go into a service they sell, so they are intermediate goods.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following social reformers established the ‘Prarthana Samaj’ in Bombay in 1876?
questions.explanation: Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj in Bombay, with M. G. Ranade and R. G. Bhandarkar among its leaders. (The Samaj dates from 1867, not 1876 as the question has it.)

questions.text: Which of the following is a crop grown in Rabi season in India?
questions.explanation: Wheat is sown in winter and harvested in spring: a rabi crop. Soyabean, maize and rice are chiefly kharif crops.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct postulates of Dalton’s atomic theory? A. All matter is made up of atoms. These atoms participate in chemical reactions. B. Atoms might be created or destroyed during a chemical reaction. C. Atoms of different elements vary in mass and chemical properties. D. Compounds are combination of atoms in the ratio of whole or fractional numbers. E. A compound will always have constant relative number and kind of atoms.
questions.explanation: Dalton held that atoms can be neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction (so B is wrong) and that they combine in ratios of small whole numbers, not fractions (so D is wrong). A, C and E are his postulates.

questions.text: What is the name of the German Chancellor who visited India in February 2023?
questions.explanation: Olaf Scholz, Germany's Chancellor from December 2021 to May 2025, visited India in February 2023. Angela Merkel was his predecessor.

questions.text: The famous novel ‘The house of blue mangoes’ is written by:
questions.explanation: 'The House of Blue Mangoes' (2002) is David Davidar's first novel.

questions.text: Who among the following Portuguese travellers visited the Vijayanagar empire during the reign of Krishnadevaraya?
questions.explanation: Domingo Paes, a Portuguese traveller, visited Vijayanagara around 1520 and described Krishnadevaraya's court. Nikitin was Russian, and Varthema and Nicolo de Conti were Italians.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In 1905, Hindus and Muslims tied ‘Rakhi’ on each other’s hands to show their unity and their protest against the _________.
questions.explanation: On 16 October 1905, the day the Partition of Bengal took effect, Rabindranath Tagore called on Hindus and Muslims to tie rakhis on each other as a sign of unity.

questions.text: ‘Alarippu’ is the first dance item of which of the following Indian classical dance forms?
questions.explanation: Alarippu, an invocatory piece of pure dance, opens a traditional Bharatanatyam recital.

questions.text: As on February 2024, who among the following is the Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways?
questions.explanation: Sarbananda Sonowal became Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways in July 2021 and held the post in February 2024.

questions.text: When did India declare itself a Sovereign, Democratic and Republic state with the adoption of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Constitution, adopted on 26 November 1949, came into force on 26 January 1950, when India became a sovereign democratic republic.

questions.text: The famous Sanskrit grammar book 'Mahabhasya' was written by:
questions.explanation: Patanjali's Mahabhashya is the great commentary on Panini's grammar, the Ashtadhyayi.

questions.text: As per the Constitution of India, every Governor, before entering upon his office, will make and subscribe an oath in the presence of the ________.
options: Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.explanation: Under Article 159 a Governor takes the oath before the Chief Justice of the state's High Court or, in his absence, its senior-most judge available.

questions.text: Who among the following founded his Kuchipudi Art Academy at Madras in 1963?
questions.explanation: Vempati Chinna Satyam founded the Kuchipudi Art Academy in Madras in 1963 and did much to make Kuchipudi a classical stage form.

questions.text: The Tunga and Bhadra are tributaries of which river?
questions.explanation: The Tunga and the Bhadra meet at Koodli in Karnataka to form the Tungabhadra, which joins the Krishna.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Gold is “much” costly than any other metal.
questions.explanation: 'Than' needs a comparative: 'Gold is more costly than any other metal.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The writer's __________ prose resonated with readers, evoking powerful emotions.
questions.explanation: Prose that moves readers to powerful emotions is 'eloquent'; 'banal' and 'mundane' mean dull and 'sporadic' occasional.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Idle
questions.explanation: 'Idle' means not working or in use: 'unoccupied'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The teacher emphasised the importance of ___________ correct grammar and punctuation in our writing.
questions.explanation: A preposition takes the gerund: 'the importance of using correct grammar'.

questions.text: Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error. The “beutiful” flowers bloomed in the garden.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'beautiful'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank. The orator declared that the women are ___________ than the men.
questions.explanation: 'Than' calls for the comparative, which 'intelligent' forms with 'more': 'more intelligent than the men'.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options..
options: A lot of books and notes placed on order looks most fascinating.
A lot of books and notes placed in order look fascinating.
A lot of books and notes place in order look most fascinating.
A lot of book and notes placed in order looks most fascinating.
questions.explanation: 'A lot of books and notes' is plural and takes 'look'; they are 'placed in order' (arranged), not 'on order' (requested from a supplier), and 'place' would need to be the participle 'placed'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined segment in the given sentence. It's important to bring up “sensitive” topics in a respectful manner.
questions.explanation: 'Sensitive' here means delicate, needing careful handling; of the options its opposite is 'strong'. 'Considerate' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She ______ the book to her friend.
questions.explanation: The past tense of 'lend' is 'lent': 'She lent the book to her friend.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The scientific study of the structure and form of animals and plants
questions.explanation: Morphology is the study of the form and structure of living things; biology, botany and zoology are the sciences of life, plants and animals as a whole.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. We “talked over” the matter for two hours; unfortunately, we could not reach a decision.
questions.explanation: To 'talk over' a matter is to discuss it.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The train is running / late by six hours / so it / cannot make over the time.
questions.explanation: Lost time is regained with 'make up': 'so it cannot make up the time' (or 'make up for lost time'). 'Make over' means to transfer or remodel.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'Mechanical'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The croissant was _________, as was the coffee.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'excellent', praise that the coffee shares ('as was the coffee'). 'Inferior' could also describe both, though it usually names a comparison ('inferior to'); 'ambitious' and 'eloquent' describe people.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Like a dying duck in a thunderstorm
questions.explanation: 'Like a dying duck in a thunderstorm' describes someone who looks dejected and helpless.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Amit, the stand-up comedian, delivered a “hilarious” performance.
questions.explanation: 'Hilarious' means extremely funny; its opposite is 'serious'.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.
options: The Nile is the most long river in the world of a length of approximately 6650 km.
The Nile is the longest river in the world with a length about approximately 6650 km.
The Nile is the longest river in the world with a length of approximately 6650 km.
The Nile is the long river in the world with a length about approximately 6650 km.
questions.explanation: The superlative of 'long' is 'longest', and a length is 'of' a figure: 'with a length of approximately 6650 km'. 'About approximately' says the same thing twice.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank. Jack always looks handsome, even if he is a __________ out of style.
questions.explanation: 'A little' before an adjective or phrase means slightly: 'a little out of style'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. High-altitude climbing poses “significant” risks due to factors like altitude sickness, hypothermia and extreme weather conditions.
questions.explanation: 'Significant' means important or considerable; its opposite is 'inconsequential'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Doves _________ in the sky above me.
questions.explanation: Birds 'soar', fly high in the air; 'sore' (painful) sounds the same but means something else.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It is true that strangers meeting for the first time seem to feel ____1____ if they do not engage _____ 2_____ small talk. Usually, this is ______3______ and even necessary if strangers are to size each other up. But, this small talk aside, what are some _____4______ rules for general conversation? In the first place, certain _____5_____ should be taboo. Kitchen topics, bus time-tables and other dull or specialised things should be barred from general discussion.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: After 'feel' an adjective is needed: strangers feel 'uncomfortable' if they make no small talk.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It is true that strangers meeting for the first time seem to feel ____1____ if they do not engage _____ 2_____ small talk. Usually, this is ______3______ and even necessary if strangers are to size each other up. But, this small talk aside, what are some _____4______ rules for general conversation? In the first place, certain _____5_____ should be taboo. Kitchen topics, bus time-tables and other dull or specialised things should be barred from general discussion.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: One 'engages in' small talk.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It is true that strangers meeting for the first time seem to feel ____1____ if they do not engage _____ 2_____ small talk. Usually, this is ______3______ and even necessary if strangers are to size each other up. But, this small talk aside, what are some _____4______ rules for general conversation? In the first place, certain _____5_____ should be taboo. Kitchen topics, bus time-tables and other dull or specialised things should be barred from general discussion.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Small talk is 'harmless and even necessary': the passage is defending it before turning to topics that should be barred.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It is true that strangers meeting for the first time seem to feel ____1____ if they do not engage _____ 2_____ small talk. Usually, this is ______3______ and even necessary if strangers are to size each other up. But, this small talk aside, what are some _____4______ rules for general conversation? In the first place, certain _____5_____ should be taboo. Kitchen topics, bus time-tables and other dull or specialised things should be barred from general discussion.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Elementary' rules are basic ones; 'alimentary' has to do with digestion.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It is true that strangers meeting for the first time seem to feel ____1____ if they do not engage _____ 2_____ small talk. Usually, this is ______3______ and even necessary if strangers are to size each other up. But, this small talk aside, what are some _____4______ rules for general conversation? In the first place, certain _____5_____ should be taboo. Kitchen topics, bus time-tables and other dull or specialised things should be barred from general discussion.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Certain 'subjects', that is topics, should be taboo, as the kitchen topics and timetables that follow show.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: In an experiment to determine the refractive index of water, a student took five sets of observations and got the values for the refractive index of water as 1.32, 1.37, 1.36, 1.39 and 1.31. What is its average value?

In an NCC camp, the average weight was 72 kg. If 5 cadets having average weight 76 kg leave and 11 cadets of average weight 79 kg join the group, the average weight of the cadets in the group increases by 0.6 kg. The number of cadets, initially in the group was:
By selling an item for ₹ 125, S earns 12% profit. What is the cost of the item (in ₹)? (Correct up to 2 decimal digits)
questions.explanation: Selling price = 1.12 × cost, so cost = 125/1.12 = ₹111.61.

questions.text: After how many years will a sum of ₹8,925 at simple interest fetch a total amount of ₹12,941.25 at the rate of 9% per annum?
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 8% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
The least number of five digits which is exactly divisible by each one of the numbers 12, 15 and 18 is:
questions.explanation: LCM(12, 15, 18) = 180. 10000 ÷ 180 is about 55.6, so the least five-digit multiple is 56 × 180 = 10080.

questions.text: Find the average of the numbers 1, −1, 0 and 2.
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 as a sum borrowed at 9% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
The price of a book is first increased by 10% and then again by 20%. If the price of the book after both increments is ₹33, then the original price (in ₹) of the book is:
questions.explanation: Original price × 1.1 × 1.2 = 33, so the original price = 33/1.32 = ₹25.

questions.text: The average score in the Mathematics exam of a class of 60 students is 52. A group of 8 boys with an average score of 40 left the class and another group of 10 boys with an average score of 43 joined the class. What is the new average score of the class? (correct to one decimal place)
If the speed of a boat going downstream is 40 km/h and its speed going upstream is 20 km/h, then find the speed of the stream (in km/h).
questions.explanation: Speed of the stream = (downstream − upstream)/2 = (40 − 20)/2 = 10 km/h.

questions.text: IRIG is related to OXOM in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, DLEC is related to JRKI. To which of the following is SBUS related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 6 places forward: I → O, R → X, G → M and D → J, L → R, E → K, C → I. So S → Y, B → H, U → A (wrapping round after Z) and S → Y: YHAY.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'FIRE' is coded as '9571' and 'ROAD' is coded as '2146'. What is the code for 'R' in the given code language?
questions.explanation: R is the only letter in both words and 1 the only digit in both codes, so R = 1.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘pass the ball’ is coded as ‘bq tr vl’ and ‘ball is red’ is coded as ‘hx vo bq’. How is ‘ball’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'ball' is the only word in both sentences and 'bq' the only code in both, so ball = bq.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 16 ÷ 4 + 18 − 14 × 7 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 16 × 4 − 18 + 14 ÷ 7 = 64 − 18 + 2 = 48.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (17, 10, 95) (2, 11, 21)
questions.explanation: The third number is five times the first plus the second: 17 × 5 + 10 = 95 and 2 × 5 + 11 = 21. Likewise 10 × 5 + 6 = 56.

questions.text: Seven friends, A, B, C, D, E, F and G, are sitting around a table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). B is to the immediate right of F, and A is to the immediate right of B. E is an immediate neighbour of both F and D, while G is an immediate neighbour of both D and C. Who is sitting to the immediate right of A?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, each person's right is anticlockwise. Reading to the right the order is C, G, D, E, F, B, A (B right of F, A right of B; E next to F and D; G between D and C), and the circle closes with C to the immediate right of A.

questions.text: EMHD is related to GOJF in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, IQLH is related to KSNJ. To which of the following is LTOK related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: EMHD → GOJF and IQLH → KSNJ. So LTOK → NVQM.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All vases are portraits. Some portraits are flowers. Conclusions: (I) All flowers are vases. (II) Some flowers may be portraits.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follow
Both conclusion I and II follow
questions.explanation: Some portraits are flowers, so some flowers are portraits and II ('may be') follows. Nothing says every flower is a vase, so I does not follow.

questions.text: What should come in place of ‘?’ in the given series? 17, 32, 93, 460, 3213, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is the one before times the next prime, minus that prime: 17 × 2 − 2 = 32, 32 × 3 − 3 = 93, 93 × 5 − 5 = 460, 460 × 7 − 7 = 3213, and 3213 × 11 − 11 = 35332.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘–’ and ‘×‘ are interchanged and ‘+’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 99 + 9 – 19 × 59 ÷ 29 = ?
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series based on the English alphabetical order? EVD, ITH ,MRL ,QPP, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +4 (E, I, M, Q, U), second letters −2 (V, T, R, P, N) and third letters +4 (D, H, L, P, T): UNT.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘under the impression’ is written as ‘ly ga po’ and ‘first impression matters’ is writtenas ‘ka mo po’. How will ‘impression’ be writtenin that language?
questions.explanation: 'impression' is the only word in both phrases and 'po' the only code in both, so impression = po.

questions.text: 8 is related to 62 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 11 is related to 119. To which of the following is 15 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is related to its square minus 2: 8² − 2 = 62 and 11² − 2 = 119. So 15² − 2 = 223.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: Some pigs are frogs. All bats are pigs. Conclusions: (I) At least some bats are frogs (II) All pigs are bats.
questions.explanation: The pigs that are frogs need not include any bats, so I does not follow; all bats are pigs, but not every pig need be a bat, so II does not follow.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). B sits second to the right of E, who is second to the right of C. G sits third to the left of D, who is not an immediate neighbour of F. A sits second to the right of D. What is the position of E with respect to C?
questions.explanation: 'E is second to the right of C' is one of the statements. (All of them fit one arrangement: going to the right, C, D, E, A, B, G, F.)

questions.text: The condition when the amount of dissolved oxygen in a water body is alarmingly decreased is called:
questions.explanation: Hypoxia is a dangerously low level of dissolved oxygen in water; anoxia is its complete absence.

questions.text: Which among the following data was used to compute the estimates in the national Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) Baseline Report?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index Baseline Report (2021) is based on the National Family Health Survey-4 (2015-16).

questions.text: Which of the following statements is/are true about the Iron Age? 1 The establishment of large cities took place on the basis of sizeable surplus. 2 The ceramic associated with this age was Painted Grey Ware. 3 The Indus Valley Civilization flourished during the Iron Age
questions.explanation: Painted Grey Ware is the pottery of the Iron Age in the Ganga plain, and that age's surplus supported the rise of large cities, so 1 and 2 are true. The Indus Valley Civilisation was a Bronze Age culture, so 3 is false.

questions.text: As per the Periodic Labour Force data 2023, which of the following states recorded the highest unemployment rate in urban areas for the age group 15 years and above?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Himachal Pradesh as having the highest urban unemployment rate (persons aged 15 and above) of these four states in the Periodic Labour Force Survey data for 2023.

questions.text: ‘Running for My Life: One Lost Boy’s Journey from the Killing Fields of Sudan to the Olympic Games’ an autobiography depicting the struggle for life to success in life is written by who among the following personalities?
questions.explanation: 'Running for My Life' is the autobiography of Lopez Lomong, one of Sudan's 'Lost Boys', who became a US Olympic runner.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The All-India Kisan Sabha was founded in Lucknow in April _______ with Swami Sahjanand Saraswati as the president.
questions.explanation: The All-India Kisan Sabha was founded at Lucknow in April 1936, with Swami Sahajanand Saraswati as its president.

questions.text: In badminton, how high above the ground is the net positioned at the edges?
questions.explanation: A badminton net is 1.55 m (5 feet 1 inch, about 5.1 feet) high at the edges, over the doubles side lines, dipping to 1.524 m (5 feet) at the centre.

questions.text: Kudumbashree is a poverty eradication and women empowerment programme. In which state of India does this programme operate?
questions.explanation: Kudumbashree, launched by the Kerala government in 1998, is a network of women's neighbourhood groups for poverty eradication and women's empowerment.

questions.text: Who among the following musicians was a member of Navratnas of Akbar?
questions.explanation: The singer Tansen was one of the nine gems (Navratnas) of Akbar's court. Amir Khusrau and Nizamuddin Auliya belong to the Delhi Sultanate period.

questions.text: What is the specific field of study focused on examining extinct animals?
questions.explanation: Palaeontology studies the life of the past, extinct animals among it, through fossils; glaciology studies ice and gemology gemstones.

questions.text: Under which of the following Articles is Right to Equality mentioned?
questions.explanation: Articles 14 to 18 of the Constitution set out the Right to Equality; Articles 19 to 22 are the Right to Freedom.

questions.text: The Sun Temple at Konark, the Khajuraho Temple in Madhya Pradesh and the recently constructed Ram Temple in Ayodhya are examples of temples designed in which style of temple architecture?
questions.explanation: All three are built in the Nagara style of north India, with a curving shikhara over the sanctum; Konark belongs to its Kalinga (Odisha) branch.

questions.text: Who among the following appoints the Acting Chief Justice in the absence of the Chief Justice of India?
options: Senior most Judge of the Supreme Court
questions.explanation: Under Article 126, when the Chief Justice of India is absent or the office is vacant, the President appoints one of the other Judges of the Supreme Court as Acting Chief Justice.

questions.text: Which Indian classical dance form has composition in Meitei language?
questions.explanation: Manipuri, the classical dance of Manipur, uses compositions in Meitei, the state's language. Sattriya is from Assam, Chhau from eastern India and Bharatanatyam from Tamil Nadu.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following leaders died after being hit by sticks while protesting against the Simon Commission?
questions.explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai was struck in a police lathi charge while leading a protest against the Simon Commission at Lahore in October 1928, and died of his injuries that November.

questions.text: Padma Shri awardee (2023) Guru K Kalyanasundaram Pillai is an exponent of which of the following classical dance genres?
questions.explanation: K. Kalyanasundaram Pillai is a Bharatanatyam guru. Sattriya is a dance of Assam, Kathak of north India and Kathakali of Kerala.

questions.text: In which of the following years was India the host of Women's T20 World Cup Cricket?
questions.explanation: India hosted the 2016 ICC Women's World Twenty20, played alongside the men's tournament.

questions.text: In Union Budget 2023-24, an aspirational Blocks Programme covering how many blocks has been launched?
questions.explanation: The Union Budget 2023-24 cites the Aspirational Blocks Programme, launched in January 2023, which covers 500 blocks and aims to bring essential government services to everyone in them.

questions.text: Which of the following represents the chemical formula for sulphur hexafluoride?
questions.explanation: Sulphur hexafluoride has one sulphur atom and six ('hexa') fluorine atoms: SF₆.

questions.text: The founder of Bahmani kingdom who assumed the title of ‘Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah’ was _________.
questions.explanation: Hasan Gangu founded the Bahmani kingdom in the Deccan in 1347 and took the title Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah.

questions.text: ‘NISHTHA’ stands for ____________.
options: National Initiative for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Advancement
National Inauguration for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Advancement
National Inauguration for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Assessment
National Initiative for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Assessment
questions.explanation: NISHTHA, the national training programme for school heads and teachers launched in 2019, is the National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement.

questions.text: A famous hill station 'Ranikhet' is located on which mountain?
questions.explanation: Ranikhet, in Almora district of Uttarakhand, is a hill station in the Kumaon Himalaya.

questions.text: Which type of tea in large amount is exported from India to importing countries?
questions.explanation: Black tea (CTC and orthodox) makes up the great bulk of India's tea exports.

questions.text: Vangpui Kut festival is organised for _______ days in Mizoram to celebrate the glory of Mizo culture and traditions.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives two days for the Vangpui Kut festival, held in Mizoram to celebrate Mizo culture and traditions.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. The “princepal” of the college announced his early retirement today.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'principal', the head of a college.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. Overfishing and destructive fishing practices threaten the “sustainability” of marine resources and ecosystems.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'indefensibility', the opposite of 'sustainability' in its sense of being able to be upheld or defended (as in a sustainable argument); reasonableness and justifiability are close to that sense, and equanimity is unrelated. In this sentence the word means the ability to be kept up over time, for which none of the options is a true opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence. A “conscious” understanding of the environmental issues can bring positive changes in human life.
questions.explanation: 'Conscious' here means aware: 'mindful'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. “By definition, making a pictogram” is to present and visualise data.
options: To make a pictogram by definition
In making a pictogram, the definition
questions.explanation: 'The purpose of a pictogram is to present and visualise data' says what a pictogram is for. (The option misprints 'pictogram' as 'pictorgram'.)

questions.text: Rectify the error in the given sentence by selecting the correct spelling from the options provided. The chord of my voilin is not tuned properly.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'violin'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate degree of comparison to fill in the blank. Hunny is _____ person in his family.
questions.explanation: Comparing one person with everyone else in his family needs the superlative with 'the': 'Hunny is the tallest person in his family.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She _______ to be understood by the society.
questions.explanation: To 'seek' (past 'sought') to do something is to try to do it: she tried to be understood.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Harmony
questions.explanation: 'Harmony' is agreement; its opposite is 'discord'. Unity, concord and accord are near-synonyms.

questions.text: If someone mentions that 'the ball is in your court', what does this idiom imply?
options: It's time to play a sport.
It's your turn to make a decision or take action.
questions.explanation: 'The ball is in your court' means it is now your turn to decide or act.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. I have been / looking by my / cream sweater for / a few weeks now.
questions.explanation: One looks 'for' something one has lost: 'I have been looking for my cream sweater for a few weeks now.'

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'rhetorical'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Rain cats and dogs
questions.explanation: To 'rain cats and dogs' is to rain very heavily.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. It was an interesting chat with an European gymnast that changed my mindset towards the sport.
questions.explanation: 'European' begins with a 'yoo' sound, a consonant sound, so it takes 'a': 'a European gymnast'.

questions.text: Which of the following options is similar in meaning to the given word? Pensive
questions.explanation: 'Pensive' means deep in thought: 'thoughtful'.

questions.text: Select the correct option of the given sentence. Vishnu is the more courageous than all other boys in the class.
options: Vishnu is much more courageous than all other boys in the class.
Vishnu is most courageous than all other boys in the class.
Vishnu is more courageous than all other boys in the class.
Vishnu is the most courageous than all other boys in the class.
questions.explanation: A comparative followed by 'than' takes no 'the': 'Vishnu is more courageous than all other boys in the class.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The speaker requested the audience to pay _________.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is to 'pay attention'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. How long / have you / been learn / English now?
questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous needs the -ing form: 'How long have you been learning English now?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The council never _________ the new complex to be constructed, nor did local residents.
questions.explanation: The council did not want the complex built, and neither did the residents: 'never wanted the new complex to be constructed'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Food prices in Switzerland are “expensiver to” the rest of Western Europe.
questions.explanation: The comparative of 'expensive' is 'more expensive', and a comparison takes 'than': 'more expensive than the rest of Western Europe'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The ship struck the iceberg (1) _____ its side while it was still moving forward. In a few (2)_____, six great holes were made in the steel. Water rushed in, not in one place, but in separate places covering the Titanic hundred feet. The steel doors were therefore (3)_____ . Captain Smith soon understood that (4)______ could save the ship. He ordered the wireless officer to send out the ship’s position and the letters CQD, which is the call for help. It told the world that the Titanic was (5)_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The ship struck the iceberg 'with' its side: the side was what hit it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Water rushed in, not in one place, but in separate places covering the Titanic hundred feet. The steel doors were therefore (3)_____ . Captain Smith soon understood that (4)______ could save the ship. He ordered the wireless officer to send out the ship’s position and the letters CQD, which is the call for help. It told the world that the Titanic was (5)_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'In a few moments' fits the speed of the damage, done while the ship was still moving.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The ship struck the iceberg (1) _____ its side while it was still moving forward. In a few (2)_____, six great holes were made in the steel. Water rushed in, not in one place, but in separate places covering the Titanic hundred feet. The steel doors were therefore (3)_____ . questions.explanation: With water rushing in at many separate places, the steel doors were 'useless'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The ship struck the iceberg (1) _____ its side while it was still moving forward. In a few (2)_____, six great holes were made in the steel. Water rushed in, not in one place, but in separate places covering the Titanic hundred feet. The steel doors were therefore (3)_____ . questions.explanation: Captain Smith understood that 'nothing' could save the ship, so he called for help.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The ship struck the iceberg (1) _____ its side while it was still moving forward. In a few (2)_____, six great holes were made in the steel. Water rushed in, not in one place, but in separate places covering the Titanic hundred feet. The steel doors were therefore (3)_____ . questions.explanation: The CQD call for help told the world that the Titanic was 'sinking'.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: During the evening patrolling, a policeman noticed a thief snatching a lady’s mobile phone at a distance of 200 m. The thief starts running at a speed of 15 km/hr. If the policeman is chasing him at a speed of 16 km/hr, then the time taken to catch the thief is:
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 16 − 15 = 1 km/h on the thief, so closing 200 m = 0.2 km takes 0.2 hours = 12 minutes.

questions.text: There are two types of dal. Type 1 dal costs ₹100 per kg and type 2 dal costs ₹120 per kg, respectively. If both the dal are mixed in the ratio 2 : 3, find the cost of the mixed dal per kg.
When 80% of a number is added to 80, the result is the same number. Find the number.
Find the HCF of the numbers 216, 360 and 504.

A borrows ₹7,500 for 4 years at 8% p.a. simple interest. B borrows the same amount at simple interest of 9% for the first year, 10% for the second year and 6% for the next two years. What is simple interest paid by A and B in total (in ₹)?
Aditya bought a mobile for ₹21,500 and sold it for ₹18,500. Find the loss percentage (up to two decimal places) in the complete process.
In a box, Refrigerator covers and Washing Machine covers are in the ratio of 7 : 11. If the Washing Machine covers are 660, how many Refrigerator covers are there?
questions.explanation: Refrigerator covers = 660 × 7/11 = 420.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 9% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
P, Q and R start running around a circular track and complete one round in 18, 22 and 30 seconds, respectively. In how much time will they meet again at the starting point?
questions.explanation: They meet again at the start after the LCM of 18, 22 and 30 seconds: 2 × 3² × 5 × 11 = 990 seconds = 16 min 30 sec.

questions.text: The average of runs scored by a player in 22 innings is 40 runs. How many runs should he score in the 23rd innings so that his average is increased by 6 runs?
questions.explanation: The 22 innings total 22 × 40 = 880 runs. An average of 46 over 23 innings needs 23 × 46 = 1,058 runs, so he must score 1,058 − 880 = 178.

questions.text: What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹240 in 4 years at 8% per year rate of interest?
The average of 42 numbers is 25 and that of other 28 numbers is 40. What is the average of all the numbers?

This question has two statements followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the given statements. Statements: All jugs are taps. Some taps are hats. Conclusions: (I) Some taps are jugs. (II)All hats are jugs.
questions.explanation: All jugs are taps, so some taps are jugs (I). The hats that are taps need not be jugs, so II does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘MELT’ is coded as ‘6284’ and ‘TUNE’ is coded as ‘9758’. What is the code for ‘T’ in that language?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 8, the only digit in both codes: T is in both words, so its digit must appear in both codes, and none of the other options does. (E is in both words too, so the codes should share two digits; as printed the question is flawed.)

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘SANE’ is coded as ‘5168’ and ‘GOAT’ is coded as ‘6437’.What is the code for ‘A’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: A is the only letter in both words and 6 the only digit in both codes, so A = 6.

questions.text: What should come in place ofthe question mark (?) in the given series? 5 ,15, 45, 135 ,405 ,?
questions.explanation: Each term is 3 times the one before: 405 × 3 = 1215.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (5, 40, 7) (12, 65, 5)
questions.explanation: The middle number is the product of the other two plus 5: 5 × 7 + 5 = 40 and 12 × 5 + 5 = 65. Likewise 3 × 3 + 5 = 14.

questions.text: I, J, K, L, M, N and O are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). J sits fourth to the right of I. K sits to the immediate right of J. L sits to the immediate right of I. N sits fourth to the left of M. M is not an immediate neighbour of K. How many people sit between O and N when counted from the right of O?
questions.explanation: Going right from I the seats run I, L, _, _, J, K, _. M cannot sit next to K, and in the first gap M would put N (fourth to its left) on K's seat; so M takes the second gap, N the seat after K and O the first gap: I, L, O, M, J, K, N. Counting right from O, M, J and K sit before N: three people.

questions.text: DG 25 is related to FH 21 in a certain way. In the same way, GI 19 is related to IJ 15. To which of the following is MI 24 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves 2 places forward, the second 1 place forward and the number falls by 4: DG 25 → FH 21 and GI 19 → IJ 15. So MI 24 → OJ 20.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘×’ are interchanged and ‘−’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 14 ÷ 12 − 2 + 2 × 16 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 14 − 12 ÷ 2 × 2 + 16 = 14 − 12 + 16 = 18.

questions.text: Find the missing term in the below series: B2, C3, E5, G7, __, M13, Q17.
questions.explanation: Each letter is followed by its place in the alphabet, and the places are the prime numbers 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17. The missing term is K11.

questions.text: UKCT is related to QGYP in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, LPBR is related to HLXN. To which of the following is DGYJ related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places back: UKCT → QGYP and LPBR → HLXN (B wraps round to X). So DGYJ → ZCUF.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some potatoes are tomatoes. No tomato is an onion. Conclusions: (I) Some tomatoes may be potatoes. (II) No potato is an onion.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Some potatoes are tomatoes, so some tomatoes are potatoes and I follows. The potatoes that are not tomatoes may be onions, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (8, 24, 12) (16, 20, 5)
questions.explanation: The middle number is the product of the other two divided by 4: 8 × 12 ÷ 4 = 24 and 16 × 5 ÷ 4 = 20. Likewise 19 × 12 ÷ 4 = 57.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Exactly three people are sitting between A and B when counted from the right of A. Exactly two people are sitting between D and G when counted from the left of G. B is not an immediate neighbour of G. D is sitting to the immediate left of B. Exactly three people are sitting between E and F when counted from the right of E. B and E are not immediate neighbours. How many people are sitting between E and G when counted from the right of E?
questions.explanation: B is fourth to A's right and D immediately left of B; G, with two people between it and D counting from G's left, is third to D's right. In the seats left, F must be fourth to E's right and E cannot sit beside B, so going right from A the order is A, E, C, D, B, F, G. Counting right from E, C, D, B and F sit before G: four people.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘COPY’ is coded as ‘2465’ and ‘PLAN’ is coded as ‘3759’. What is the code for ‘P’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: P is the only letter in both words and 5 the only digit in both codes, so P = 5.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 3 – 2 ÷ 8 × 4 + 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 3 + 2 × 8 ÷ 4 − 2 = 3 + 4 − 2 = 5.

questions.text: Identify the correct statement with reference to the Padma awards.
options: The names of the awardees are never published in the Gazette of India.
The total number of Padma awards to be given in a year should not more than 150.
The Padma Awards are given annually.
The Padma award can be used as a suffix or prefix to the awardees’ name
questions.explanation: The Padma awards are announced every year on the eve of Republic Day. Their number is capped at 120 a year (not counting posthumous and foreign awardees), the names are published in the Gazette of India, and the award may not be used as a prefix or suffix to a name.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an element of weather?
questions.explanation: Temperature, pressure, humidity, wind, cloudiness and rainfall are the elements of weather; plants are not.

questions.text: In which of the following years India hosted the Women's Asia Cup ODI Cricket?
questions.explanation: The 2006 Women's Asia Cup, an ODI tournament, was played in Jaipur in December 2006; India won it.

questions.text: The famous English novel ‘Em and the Big Hoom’ is written by:
questions.explanation: 'Em and the Big Hoom' (2012) is Jerry Pinto's first novel, about a Bombay family living with the mother's mental illness.

questions.text: The Prime Minister in India is ________.
options: the Supreme Commander of Armed Forces
questions.explanation: In India's parliamentary system the President is the nominal executive and the Prime Minister, who heads the Council of Ministers, the real executive. The President is the Supreme Commander of the armed forces.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a component of revenue receipt?
options: Fees paid for the registration of property
questions.explanation: Revenue receipts neither create a liability nor reduce assets: taxes such as GST, fees and grants. A loan from the World Bank must be repaid, so it is a capital receipt.

questions.text: Organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry is included in which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 48, a Directive Principle, asks the State to organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines.

questions.text: 0.25 g of an organic compound, on treatment with fuming nitric acid followed by AgNO₃, gave 0.22 g of AgBr. The percentage of bromine in the compound is ______.
questions.explanation: By the Carius method, % Br = (80/188) × (0.22/0.25) × 100 = 37.45%, 80 and 188 being the molar masses of Br and AgBr.

questions.text: In Union Budget 2023-24, annual production of 5 MMT under Green Hydrogen Mission is to be targeted by the year ___________ to facilitate transition of the economy to low carbon intensity.
questions.explanation: The Union Budget 2023-24 set the National Green Hydrogen Mission a target of 5 MMT of annual production by 2030.

questions.text: According to the Census of India-2011, what is the share of workforce engaged in the agriculture sector?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 census 54.6% of India's workforce was engaged in agriculture, as cultivators or agricultural labourers.

questions.text: Alarmel Valli was associated with which of the following dances?
questions.explanation: Alarmel Valli is a Bharatanatyam dancer of the Pandanallur style.

questions.text: When protein-rich gelatinous egg white is heated, it turns to solid white due to:
questions.explanation: Heat unfolds the proteins of egg white (denaturation), and they bind together into a solid white mass.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent?
questions.explanation: Humayun's tomb in Delhi, built in 1570, was the first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent; the tombs of Itimad-ud-Daulah and Safdarjung came later.

questions.text: In which of the following Indian states is the M.A. Chidambaram Stadium located?
questions.explanation: The M. A. Chidambaram Stadium is at Chepauk in Chennai, Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: In April 2023, who was appointed as the chairman of the National Technical Research Organisation (NTRO) by the centre?
questions.explanation: Arun Sinha, an IPS officer who had been an adviser at the National Technical Research Organisation, was appointed its chairman in April 2023.

questions.text: In which of the following states are the Nor Westers known as ‘Bardoisila’?
questions.explanation: In Assam the Nor'westers, violent evening thunderstorms of the hot season, are called 'Bardoisila'; in West Bengal they are 'Kalbaisakhi'.

questions.text: Rani ki Vav is a UNESCO world heritage monument, situated in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Rani ki Vav, a stepwell on the Saraswati at Patan in Gujarat, became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2014.

questions.text: According to the Census 2011, what was the annual population growth rate of India (in percentage)?
questions.explanation: The 2011 census put India's average annual exponential growth rate for 2001-2011 at 1.64%, down from 1.97% in 1991-2001.

questions.text: Usha Barle, who won Padma Shri 2023, is popularly associated with which genre of music?
questions.explanation: Usha Barle of Chhattisgarh, a singer of Pandwani, the sung narration of the Mahabharata, received the Padma Shri in 2023.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following statements is/are correct? A)Balshastri Jambhekar started the first Anglo- Maratha newspaper - ‘Durpun’, in 1832. B)He is remembered as the father of Marathi journalism. C)Balshastri Jambhekar published the first Marathi monthly magazine - ‘Digdurshun’ in 1840.
questions.explanation: Balshastri Jambhekar started 'Darpan', the first Marathi newspaper, printed in English and Marathi, on 6 January 1832, and the first Marathi monthly, 'Digdarshan', in 1840; he is called the father of Marathi journalism. All three statements are correct.

questions.text: Which of the following organisms is used in bread and alcohol industries?
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments sugars into ethanol and carbon dioxide: the gas makes bread dough rise, and the ethanol is the basis of the alcohol industry.

questions.text: What is the collection of Vedic hymns or ‘mantras’ called?
questions.explanation: A Samhita is the collection of the mantras or hymns of a Veda, such as the Rig Veda Samhita.

questions.text: The Indian Forest Service was created under the All India Service Act, 1951 in ______.
questions.explanation: The Indian Forest Service was set up in 1966 under the All India Services Act, 1951, alongside the IAS and the IPS.

questions.text: Bathukamma festival is celebrated in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Bathukamma, a festival of flowers celebrated by women in the autumn, is Telangana's state festival.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Tranquil
questions.explanation: 'Tranquil' means calm and peaceful; its opposite is 'unquiet'. 'Serene' and 'composed' are synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I couldn't believe how _______ the math problem was; it took me hours to solve it.
questions.explanation: A problem that took hours to solve was 'complicated'. The blank needs an adjective describing the problem, not the adverbs 'simply' or 'easily'.

questions.text: In the given sentence, one of the four underlined words is incorrectly spelt. Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word. She “dabbled” in “drawing” and painting, but “scalpture” was her “favourite” medium.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'sculpture'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Commence
questions.explanation: 'Commence' means to begin: 'start'.

questions.text: Read the following sentence and select its future tense form from the options given below: Sarah and Fidha entered into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
options: Sarah and Fidha are entering into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
Sarah and Fidha had entered into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
Sarah and Fidha were entered into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
Sarah and Fidha will enter into an agreement to share the resources that are currently accessible.
questions.explanation: The simple future 'will enter' puts the agreement in the future; the other options are the present continuous, the past perfect and an ungrammatical passive.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling to fill in the blank. Wedding is an auspicious _______ for all.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'occasion'.

questions.text: Select the correct indefinite article to fill in the blank. My neighbour is ______ passionate photographer.
questions.explanation: 'Passionate' begins with a consonant sound, so it takes the indefinite article 'a'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Confession is good for the soul ________________ after the soul has been claimed.
questions.explanation: 'Even after' stresses that confession is still good at a point where it might seem too late; 'since', 'though' and 'still' do not fit before 'after' here.

questions.text: Identify the word with a spelling error in the following sentence. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. In Shakespeare’s play ‘Hamlet’, Hamlet’s flaw is defined as procrustineition.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'procrastination'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error. Ms. Malathi is old much to join a college now.
questions.explanation: The phrase is 'much too old': 'Ms. Malathi is much too old to join a college now.'

questions.text: Select the sentence with the most appropriate comparative degree.
options: She is the most talented musician in the orchestra.
She is more talented musician in the orchestra.
She is the talent of all musicians in the orchestra.
She is the talentedest musician in the orchestra.
questions.explanation: Comparing one musician with all the others in the orchestra takes the superlative with 'the': 'She is the most talented musician in the orchestra.' 'More talented' would need 'than', and 'talentedest' is not a word. (The question's 'comparative degree' means the degrees of comparison in general.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She was a ________, ________ __________astronaut.
questions.explanation: Adjectives of opinion come before those of size or build, and origin comes last: 'a smart, tall, Indian astronaut'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym for the given word. Species
questions.explanation: A 'species' is a kind or 'type', especially of plant or animal.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the bracketed word in the sentence given below. Surrounded by lush greenery, the house stood _____________ (submissively) atop a hill.
questions.explanation: 'Submissively' means meekly, yielding to others; its opposite is 'proudly'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. When Mr. Bhanot was told a few years back that he needed to lose _____ or face health problems, he transformed his life with the _________ of a personal trainer.
questions.explanation: One loses 'weight' to avoid health problems, here with the 'help' of a personal trainer.

questions.text: Based on the situation in the sentence, choose the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. You cannot _________________ before replicating your successes and achievements multiple times; otherwise, people will deem your success a stroke of dumb luck.
questions.explanation: To 'rest on your laurels' is to rely on past success without further effort; a single success could be put down to luck.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Shebna decided to take “a break in social media”, but she found it difficult to disconnect completely.
questions.explanation: One takes 'a break from' something: 'a break from social media'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Callous
questions.explanation: 'Callous' means unfeeling and hard-hearted; its opposite is 'tender'.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. Mary is the “quieter” student of the class.
questions.explanation: Comparing one student with the whole class needs the superlative, and 'quiet' normally forms it with '-est': 'the quietest student of the class'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Let the cat out of the bag
options: To not allow a cat into the bag
To release a cat out of a bag
To buy a cat and a bag
questions.explanation: To 'let the cat out of the bag' is to reveal a secret, usually by accident.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Education is fundamental for achieving full human potential, developing an equitable and (1)__________ society, and promoting national development. Providing universal (2)__________ quality education is the key to India’s continued ascent, and leadership on the global stage in terms of economic growth, social justice and equality, scientific advancement, national integration, and cultural preservation. Universal high-quality education is the best way (3)__________ for developing and maximising our country's rich talents and resources for the good (4)__________ the individual, the society, the country and the world. India (5)___________ the highest population of young people in the world over the next decade, and our ability to provide high-quality educational opportunities to them will determine the future of our country.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'An equitable and just society': 'just' (fair) pairs naturally with 'equitable'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Education is fundamental for achieving full human potential, developing an equitable and (1)__________ society, and promoting national development. Providing universal (2)__________ quality education is the key to India’s continued ascent, and leadership on the global stage in terms of economic growth, social justice and equality, scientific advancement, national integration, and cultural preservation. Universal high-quality education is the best way (3)__________ for developing and maximising our country's rich talents and resources for the good (4)__________ the individual, the society, the country and the world. India (5)___________ the highest population of young people in the world over the next decade, and our ability to provide high-quality educational opportunities to them will determine the future of our country.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: One provides 'access to' something: 'universal access to quality education'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Education is fundamental for achieving full human potential, developing an equitable and (1)__________ society, and promoting national development. Providing universal (2)__________ quality education is the key to India’s continued ascent, and leadership on the global stage in terms of economic growth, social justice and equality, scientific advancement, national integration, and cultural preservation. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'The best way forward' means the best course of action from here on.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Education is fundamental for achieving full human potential, developing an equitable and (1)__________ society, and promoting national development.
