markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Rajeev saves 75% of his monthly income. If his monthly expenditure is ₹37,500, then his monthly saving (in ₹) is:
questions.explanation: Expenditure is the other 25% of the income, so saving (75%) is three times it: 3 × ₹37,500 = ₹1,12,500.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 3% per year rate of interest for 5 years.
Water in a conical flask with radius 7 cm and height 48 cm is poured into a cylindrical flask with radius 14 cm. The water level in the cylindrical flask is:
questions.explanation: The volume stays the same: (1/3)π × 7² × 48 = π × 14² × h, so 784π = 196πh and h = 4 cm.

questions.text: By selling an article for ₹19, a dealer makes a profit of 10%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹, rounded off to two decimal place) so as to make a profit of 40%?
questions.explanation: The cost price is 19/1.10 = ₹17.27. A 40% profit needs a selling price of 19 × 1.40/1.10 = ₹24.18, so the price must rise by ₹5.18.

questions.text: Raj prepares a 60 gm mixture by combining two ingredients X and Y. The cost of ingredient X is ₹80 per 5 gm, and the cost of ingredient Y is ₹80 per 10 gm. Ingredients X and Y are mixed in a manner that the cost of the resulting mixture is ₹14 per gm. What is the quantity of ingredient X (in gm) in the mixture?
questions.explanation: X costs 80/5 = ₹16 a gm and Y 80/10 = ₹8 a gm. By alligation X : Y = (14 − 8) : (16 − 14) = 3 : 1, so X = 60 × 3/4 = 45 gm.

questions.text: In a scheme, a shopkeeper offers 4% discount if you buy three or more products. Ritu buys three bottles of guava juice for ₹330. If the shopkeeper still makes a profit of 10%, find the profit he would make if had sold it without discount (rounded off to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanation: The cost is 330/1.10 = ₹300. Without the 4% discount the price would be 330/0.96 = ₹343.75, a profit of 43.75/300 × 100 = 14.58%.

questions.text: A person has to cover a distance of 8 km in 1 hour. If he covers one-fourth of the distance in one-third of the total time, then what should his speed (in km/h) be to cover the remaining distance in the remaining time so that the person reaches the destination exactly on time?
questions.explanation: He covers 2 km in 20 minutes, which leaves 6 km for the remaining 40 minutes (2/3 hour): 6 ÷ 2/3 = 9 km/h.

questions.text: Which of the following options is equal to the LCM of 12, 36, 72, 144, 288 and 576?
questions.explanation: 576 = 2⁶ × 3², and 12, 36, 72, 144 and 288 all divide it, so the LCM is 576 itself.

questions.text: The average height of 50 students in a class was 105 cm. A group of five students with an average height of 95 cm were admitted to this class. What is the average height (in cm) of the class of 55 students? (correct to the nearest integer)
Walking at a speed of 5.4 km/h, Rohit takes 40 minutes to reach his school from his home. What time will he take if he walks 8 km/h?
questions.explanation: The distance is 5.4 × 40/60 = 3.6 km; at 8 km/h it takes 3.6/8 = 0.45 hour = 27 minutes.

questions.text: A hemispherical bowl of internal radius 24 cm contains liquid. The liquid is to be filled into cylindrical container of diameter 8 cm and height 12 cm. What is the number of containers that are necessary to empty the bowl?
questions.explanation: Bowl: (2/3)π × 24³ = 9,216π cm³. Each container: π × 4² × 12 = 192π cm³. 9,216/192 = 48.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 5% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
15 kg rice costing ₹60 per kg and 8 kg rice costing ₹55 per kg are mixed with 7 kg rice costing ₹40 per kg. Find the average per kg price of mixed rice.
A tradesman marks his goods 25% above the cost price and allows his customers 12% reduction on their bills. What percentage profit does he make?
questions.explanation: On a cost of 100 the marked price is 125, and 12% off leaves 125 × 0.88 = 110: a profit of 10%.

questions.text: A earns ₹88 per hour and works for 10 hours. B earns ₹95 per hour and works for 8 hours. The ratio of per day wages of A to B is:
In a certain code language, ‘WANT’ is coded as ‘8163’ and ‘THAN’ is coded as ‘3468’. What is the code for ‘H’ in that language?
questions.explanation: T, A and N are in both words, as are 3, 6 and 8 in both codes. The letter left in THAN is H and the digit left in its code is 4, so H = 4.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘PAID’ is coded as ‘3195’ and ‘GRAB’ is coded as ‘2346’.What is the code for ‘A’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: A is the only letter in both words and 3 the only digit in both codes, so A = 3.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some plants are spices. No spice is a lentil. Conclusions: (I) Some lentils are plants. (II) Some spices are plants.
questions.explanation: 'Some plants are spices' means some spices are plants, so (II) follows. Nothing is said about lentils and the plants that are not spices, so (I) need not follow.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? ADG, JMP, SVY, BEH, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move 9 places forward each time (A, J, S, B, K, wrapping round after Z), and each group is three letters 3 apart: KNQ.

questions.text: DZRG is related to HDOD in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, LHLA is related to PLIX. To which of the following is TPFU related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The first two letters move 4 places forward and the last two 3 back: DZRG → HDOD (Z wraps round to D) and LHLA → PLIX. So TPFU → XTCR.

questions.text: DBCA is related to HDFB in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, BACD is related to DBFH. To which of the following is FDAC related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter's place in the alphabet is doubled: D(4) → H(8), B(2) → D(4), C(3) → F(6), A(1) → B(2). So F(6) → L(12), D → H, A → B and C → F: LHBF.

questions.text: 21 is related to 189 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 35 is related to 315. To which of the following is 43 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 9: 21 × 9 = 189 and 35 × 9 = 315. Likewise 43 × 9 = 387.

questions.text: Seven people R, S, T, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). R is sitting third to the right of D. Only one person is sitting between G and E when counted from the left of G. S is sitting to the immediate right of T. Only one person is sitting between G and T when counted from the right of G. Who is sitting third to the right of F?
questions.explanation: Going round to each person's right (anticlockwise, facing the centre): G, D, T, S, R, E, F. T is second to G's right with S on T's right, E is second to G's left and R third to D's right. Third to the right of F is T.

questions.text: Six friends - A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table facing away from the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). F is an immediate neighbour of both B and C. D is sitting second to the right of B. A is sitting to the immediate right of D. Who among the following is sitting to the second to the left of F?
questions.explanation: Facing away from the centre, each person's right is clockwise. Going round to the right: B, E, D, A, C, F, so D is second to B's right, A is on D's right and F sits between C and B. Second to the left of F is A.

questions.text: 18 is related to 74 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 22 is related to 90. To which of the following is 25 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 4 and 2 is added: 18 × 4 + 2 = 74 and 22 × 4 + 2 = 90. Likewise 25 × 4 + 2 = 102.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘CASH’ is coded as ‘2486’ and ‘HIRE’ is coded as ‘3257’.What is the code for ‘H’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: H is the only letter in both words and 2 the only digit in both codes, so H = 2.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All shirts are pants. All pants are watches. Conclusions: (I) All pants are shirts. (II) All shirts are watches.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: All shirts are pants and all pants are watches, so all shirts are watches (II). Nothing says every pant is a shirt, so (I) does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FOIL’ is coded as ‘1974’ and ‘LIFE’ is coded as ‘7291’. What is the code for ‘E’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: F, I and L are in both words, as are 1, 7 and 9 in both codes. The letter left in LIFE is E and the digit left in its code is 2, so E = 2.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 35 + 60 ÷ 12 × 4 − 12 = 203
What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘×‘ are interchanged and ‘−’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 5 + 625 − 25 × 75 ÷ 65 =?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 5 × 625 ÷ 25 + 75 − 65 = 125 + 75 − 65 = 135.

questions.text: What should come in place of ‘?’ in the given series? 14, 30, 93, 470, 3297, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is the one before times n, plus n, with n running through the primes 2, 3, 5, 7, 11: 14 × 2 + 2 = 30, 30 × 3 + 3 = 93, 93 × 5 + 5 = 470, 470 × 7 + 7 = 3297. Next: 3297 × 11 + 11 = 36278.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was the pioneer of 'Bhoodan Movement'?
questions.explanation: Vinoba Bhave began the Bhoodan (land-gift) movement in 1951 at Pochampally, in present-day Telangana, asking landowners to give land to the landless.

questions.text: A particular cell present in the excretory system of flatworms, which helps them removing waste materials is the:
questions.explanation: Flatworms such as planarians remove wastes through flame cells, whose beating cilia (the 'flame') drive fluid into the excretory tubules.

questions.text: The rock-cut temple of Shiva built by Krishna I is found at which of the following places?
questions.explanation: The Kailasa temple at Ellora, cut from a single rock, was built under the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I in the 8th century.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Bhadaravi Poonam Mela organised every year in the Nilkanth Mahadev temple premises in Babra?
questions.explanation: Babra is a town in Amreli district, Gujarat; 'Bhadarvi Poonam' is the full moon of Bhadarvo, the Gujarati name for the month of Bhadrapad.

questions.text: Which of the following cities is known as the Steel City in India?
questions.explanation: Jamshedpur in Jharkhand, which grew up around the Tata steel works, is known as the Steel City of India.

questions.text: As per the Constitution (Ninety-First Amendment) Act, 2003, the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, shall NOT exceed:
options: 25% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
10% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
20% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
questions.explanation: The 91st Amendment added Article 75(1A): the Council of Ministers, Prime Minister included, may not exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha.

questions.text: The concept of Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of _____________.
questions.explanation: The Concurrent List, like freedom of trade and commerce and the joint sitting of Parliament, was borrowed from the Australian Constitution.

questions.text: In Dholavira, which of the following materials is extensively used as a building material?
questions.explanation: Unlike most Harappan cities, which were built of brick, Dholavira in the Rann of Kutch was built largely of stone.

questions.text: Who became the first woman to command the Armed Forces Transfusion Centre, Delhi Cantt, which is the largest blood transfusion centre of the Armed Forces in Nov 2023?
questions.explanation: Colonel Sunita B.S. took command of the Armed Forces Transfusion Centre, Delhi Cantt, in November 2023, the first woman to do so.

questions.text: In which of the following year did India win the ICC T20 Men's Cricket World Cup?
questions.explanation: India won the first ICC T20 World Cup, in South Africa in 2007, beating Pakistan in the final; its second title came in 2024.

questions.text: Consider the following statements in the context of the Vedas. 1.The Vedas are called Shruti. 2.The Rigveda consists of ten Mandalas. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The Vedas are 'Shruti', what was heard or revealed, as against 'Smriti', what is remembered; the Rigveda's hymns are arranged in ten books, the Mandalas.

questions.text: Which of the following government initiatives focuses on skill development to reduce open unemployment among youth in India?
options: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)
questions.explanation: PMKVY, launched in 2015, trains young people in job skills. MGNREGA guarantees wage work, PM KUSUM promotes solar pumps for farmers and Swachh Bharat is about sanitation.

questions.text: When was the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar, an award given by the Sangeet Natak Akademi to outstanding artists under 40 who have demonstrated talent in the fields of music, dance and theatre, started?
questions.explanation: The Sangeet Natak Akademi instituted the Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar in 2006.

questions.text: In a metro station, it was observed that on an average 20 people per minute were using the escalator to reach at a height of 15 metres. Calculate the power of the escalator assuming the average mass of people to be 50 kg and acceleration due to gravity to be 10 m/s².
questions.explanation: Power is the work done (mgh) per second: (20 × 50 × 10 × 15)/60 = 2,500 W = 2.5 kW.

questions.text: In which state are the Gua and Noamundi iron ore mines located?
questions.explanation: Gua and Noamundi are iron-ore mines in the West Singhbhum district of Jharkhand.

questions.text: What is the rank of Sri Lanka in the Global Hunger Index (GHI) 2023?
questions.explanation: Sri Lanka ranked 60th of 125 countries in the Global Hunger Index 2023; India was 111th.

questions.text: Indian classical musician, Ustad Rashid Khan was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2022 for his contribution to which of the following music categories?
questions.explanation: Ustad Rashid Khan, of the Rampur-Sahaswan gharana, was a Hindustani classical vocalist; he received the Padma Bhushan in 2022.

questions.text: In which of the following classical dance forms are the actors’ faces painted to symbolise the type of character they are playing?
questions.explanation: Kathakali, Kerala's dance-drama, paints the actors' faces in set colours for each type of character, such as green (pacha) for noble heroes.

questions.text: How many titles did West Bengal win in the Santosh Trophy events up to the 2022-23 season?
questions.explanation: Up to the 2022-23 season Bengal had won the Santosh Trophy, the national football championship for state teams, a record 32 times, the last in 2016-17.

questions.text: The climatic diversity of India is characterised by its distinctiveness, and one of the following factors does NOT contribute to it is ______________.
questions.explanation: Longitude decides a place's local time, not its climate. Latitude and relief (topography) shape temperature, winds and rainfall, and vegetation affects local humidity and temperature.

questions.text: What is the primary acid found in citrus fruits like oranges and lemons?
questions.explanation: Citrus fruits owe their sour taste mainly to citric acid. Tartaric acid is found in grapes and tamarind, lactic acid in curd and acetic acid in vinegar.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides provision for appointment of the same person as the Governor for two or more states?
questions.explanation: Article 153 provides a Governor for each State, and its proviso, added by the Seventh Amendment (1956), allows the same person to be Governor of two or more States.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following Governor-Generals declared 'Sati' practice as illegal?
questions.explanation: Lord William Bentinck's Bengal Sati Regulation of 1829 made sati illegal, with the support of Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

questions.text: Which of the following fictional towns is mentioned in the English novel ‘In Custody’ written by Anita Desai?
questions.explanation: Anita Desai's 'In Custody' (1984) is set in Mirpore, where the Hindi lecturer Deven teaches. Kanthapura is Raja Rao's village, Malgudi R. K. Narayan's town and Lilliput Swift's island.

questions.text: In 1992, which organisation launched Self Help Group – Bank Linkage Programme?
questions.explanation: NABARD launched the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme in 1992, linking self-help groups of the poor to bank credit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word ‘Illuminate’ from the given sentence. The toughest and most typical question in the examination was to elucidate a particular theory related to friction in physics.
questions.explanation: To 'elucidate' is to make clear or explain: to 'illuminate'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The manager decided to “disclose a secret” and address the issue at the team meeting.
options: hit the nail on the head
questions.explanation: To 'spill the beans' is to reveal a secret.

questions.text: The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. If I was a king, I would have tried my best to remove poverty from my country.
questions.explanation: An imagined condition takes the subjunctive 'were' with every subject: 'If I were a king'.

questions.text: The given sentence has an error. Select the option that rectifies the error. The students were asked to turn up their assignments by Friday.
questions.explanation: To 'turn in' work is to hand it in; to 'turn up' is to arrive or appear.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Captivity
questions.explanation: 'Captivity' is being held prisoner; its opposite is 'liberty', freedom.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. They was / celebrating their / Silver wedding anniversary / next month in Dubai.
questions.explanation: The plural 'they' takes 'were': 'They were celebrating'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Everyone in the room was in “a jolly” and relaxed mood.
questions.explanation: Nothing is being compared, so the positive degree 'a jolly and relaxed mood' is right; 'more jollier' is a double comparative.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word..
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'opportunity'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She treats her juniors _____ contempt.
questions.explanation: One treats someone 'with' contempt.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Chaotic
questions.explanation: 'Chaotic' means in complete disorder; its opposite is 'systematic'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The blanket gifted by my granny is “softer” and cozy.
questions.explanation: Nothing is being compared, and the adjective must match 'cozy' in degree: 'soft and cozy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. By next summer, they will be _____ their house.
questions.explanation: 'Will be' with the -ing form makes the future continuous: 'they will be renovating their house'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'occasion', with one 's'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Out of spirits
questions.explanation: To be 'out of spirits' is to be low or sad: gloomy.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The new employee is really trying to fit in, but sometimes he feels “out of place and uncomfortable”.
questions.explanation: 'A fish out of water' is someone uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings.

questions.text: Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence. Almost as wide as he was tall, he had a “voracious” appetite for food and drink and a rollicking personality to match.
questions.explanation: 'Voracious' means wanting great quantities and never satisfied: 'insatiable'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence. Urban people have a “bombastic” lifestyle, which is very different from those of rural folks.
questions.explanation: 'Bombastic' means pompous and inflated, high-sounding but with little substance: 'pretentious'.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. The police informed the statesman that the goons were up to something “mischievious”.
questions.explanation: There is no 'i' after the 'v': 'mischievous'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The unexpected guest at the party was “a bull in a China shop”.
questions.explanation: 'A bull in a china shop' is someone clumsy and careless who causes damage.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In recent years, the central and state governments in India have been taking special steps to __1__ foreign companies to invest in India. Industrial zones, called Special Economic Zones (SEZs), are being __2__. SEZs have world-class facilities, including electricity, water, roads, transport, storage, recreational, and educational facilities. Companies that set up production units in the SEZs do not have to pay taxes for an initial period of five years. The government has also __3__ flexibility in the labour laws to attract foreign investment. In recent years, the government has allowed companies to __4__ many of these provisions. Instead of hiring workers on a regular basis, companies hire workers 'flexibly' for short periods when there is __5__ pressure of work. This is done to reduce the cost of labour for the company. However, some foreign companies are not satisfied, and they are demanding more in labour laws, citing the need for greater operational efficiency.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The governments want to 'attract' foreign companies to invest, as the passage says again later ('to attract foreign investment').

However, some foreign companies are not satisfied, and they are demanding more in labour laws, citing the need for greater operational efficiency.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: SEZs with world-class facilities are being 'set up', that is established; 'wound up' and 'dismantled' mean the opposite.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The government has 'allowed' flexibility in the labour laws to attract foreign investment.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Find the average of the the first 15 multiples of 5.
questions.explanation: The first 15 multiples of 5 run from 5 to 75, so their average is (5 + 75)/2 = 40.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 3% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
The mean of the first 7 odd prime numbers is (rounded off to two decimal places):
questions.explanation: The first seven odd primes are 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19, which add up to 75. 75/7 = 10.71.

questions.text: The cost price of some table lamps is ₹25,000. The shopkeeper will get ₹15,000 more If he sells these table lamps for ₹1,200 per lamp instead of ₹900 per lamp. Find the selling price of 23 table lamps if he earned 21% profit.
questions.explanation: ₹300 more a lamp brings ₹15,000 more, so there are 15,000/300 = 50 lamps, costing 25,000/50 = ₹500 each. At 21% profit one sells for ₹605, so 23 sell for 23 × 605 = ₹13,915.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 5% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
Ravi walks a circular track of 1680m in circumference. If the speed of Ravi is 140m/min, then the time to cover one round is equal to:
questions.explanation: One round takes 1680/140 = 12 minutes.

questions.text: A train 315 m long is running at a speed of 54 km/h. What time will it take to cross a pole on its route?
questions.explanation: 54 km/h = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s. To pass a pole the train covers its own length: 315/15 = 21 s.

questions.text: Find the LCM of 9, 21 and 63
questions.explanation: 63 = 3² × 7 contains both 9 = 3² and 21 = 3 × 7, so the LCM is 63 itself.

questions.text: A’s salary increases by 60% and then decreases by 30%. On the whole, A’s salary is increased by ______?
questions.explanation: A 60% rise and then a 30% fall multiply the salary by 1.6 × 0.7 = 1.12: a net increase of 12%.

questions.text: If the cost price of an article is 70.5% of its selling price, what is the profit percentage (rounded off to 1 decimal place)?
questions.explanation: Taking the selling price as 100, the cost price is 70.5 and the profit 29.5, so the profit percentage is 29.5/70.5 × 100 = 41.84%, or 41.8%.

questions.text: Find the fourth proportional of 4a + 7, 11a + 3 and 6a if a = 2.
questions.explanation: With a = 2 the numbers are 15, 25 and 12. The fourth proportional x satisfies 15 : 25 = 12 : x, so x = 25 × 12/15 = 20.

questions.text: The average weight of 16 containers is 80 kg. If 8 new containers are added, the new average increases by 2.5 kg. The average weight of the 8 new containers is:
questions.explanation: The 16 containers weigh 16 × 80 = 1,280 kg and all 24 weigh 24 × 82.5 = 1,980 kg. The 8 new ones weigh 700 kg: 87.5 kg on average.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13, can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (18, 16, 34) (21, 43, 64)
questions.explanation: In each set the third number is the sum of the first two: 18 + 16 = 34 and 21 + 43 = 64. Likewise 32 + 10 = 42.

questions.text: Six people—A, B, C, D, E, and F—are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). A is an immediate neighbour of both E and F. C is second to the left of F. B is not is an immediate neighbour of E. What is the position of D?
options: Second to the right of B
questions.explanation: C is second to the left of F, so the seat on F's immediate left lies between F and C; A, who sits between E and F, must be on F's right, with E next to A. B cannot sit next to E, so B takes the seat between F and C and D the one between C and E: D is immediately to the left of C.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 56 ÷ 8 × 45 + 4 − 23 = 164
JJDA is related to QQKH in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, ENHE is related to LUOL. To which of the following is TTNK related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 7 places forward: J → Q, D → K, A → H and E → L, N → U, H → O. So T → A (wrapping round after Z), N → U and K → R: AAUR.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘LOST’ is coded as ‘5197’ and ‘TURN’ is coded as ‘4562’. What is the code for ‘T’ in that language?
questions.explanation: T is the only letter in both words and 5 the only digit in both codes, so T = 5.

questions.text: 127 is related to 218 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 3 is related to 10.To which of the following is 29 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each pair is two consecutive cubes plus 2: 127 = 5³ + 2 and 218 = 6³ + 2; 3 = 1³ + 2 and 10 = 2³ + 2. So 29 = 3³ + 2 goes with 4³ + 2 = 66.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘EXIT’ is coded as ‘1937’ and ‘ZERO’ is coded as ‘6829’.What is the code for ‘E’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: E is the only letter in both words and 9 the only digit in both codes, so E = 9.

questions.text: FRNQ is related to LXTW in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, XJFI is related to DPLO. To which of the following is VHDG related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 6 places forward: F → L, R → X, N → T, Q → W and X → D (wrapping round after Z), J → P, F → L, I → O. So V → B, H → N, D → J and G → M: BNJM.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘÷’ and ‘+’ are interchanged and ‘−’ and ‘×’ are interchanged? 13 − 3 ÷ 4 − 9 ÷ 10 − 3 × 20 + 5= ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 13 × 3 + 4 × 9 + 10 × 3 − 20 ÷ 5 = 39 + 36 + 30 − 4 = 101.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘car is fast'’ is written as ‘gq ip eb’ and ‘fast and furious’ is writtenas ‘hp qm ip’. How is ‘fast’ writtenin the given language?
questions.explanation: 'fast' is the only word in both sentences and 'ip' the only code in both, so fast = ip.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). G sits third to the right of A. D sits third to the right of G. E is an immediate neighbour of both A and F. C sits third to the right of F. How many people sit between E and D when counted from the right of E?
questions.explanation: Placing G third to A's right, D third to G's right, E between A and F, and C third to F's right gives, going round to each person's left: A, D, C, B, G, F, E. Counting rightwards from E, F, G, B and C come before D: 4 people.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 33, 37, 46, 62, 87, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 4, 9, 16 and 25, the squares of 2 to 5, so the next is 6² = 36: 87 + 36 = 123.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All papers are files. All files are secret. Conclusions: (I) All papers are secret. (II) All secrets are files.
questions.explanation: All papers are files and all files are secret, so all papers are secret (I). Nothing says every secret thing is a file, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All oranges are apples. Some apples are kiwis. Conclusions: (I) Some oranges are not kiwis. (II) All apples are oranges.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow
questions.explanation: Nothing links the oranges to the kiwis: every orange may or may not be a kiwi, so I does not follow. All oranges being apples does not make all apples oranges, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? EFD, JKI, OPN, TUS, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 5 places forward from one cluster to the next: E, J, O, T, Y; F, K, P, U, Z; D, I, N, S, X. The next cluster is YZX.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Tirot Sing was the leader of which of the following revolts?
questions.explanation: Tirot Sing, a Khasi chief, led the Khasi uprising against the British in the Khasi Hills (1829-33).

questions.text: In India, who introduced the idea of the poverty line for the first time?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji was the first to discuss a poverty line: he priced a prisoner's diet to arrive at a 'jail cost of living'.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following years did Lord Curzon announce the partition of Bengal?
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon announced the partition of Bengal in 1905; it took effect on 16 October 1905 and was annulled in 1911.

questions.text: ___________ dance is embedded in the stories from the epics Mahabharata, Ramayana and Puranas.
questions.explanation: Kathakali, the dance-drama of Kerala, draws its stories from the Ramayana, the Mahabharata and the Puranas.

questions.text: In which language was 'Mudraraksha' play written by Vishakhadatta?
questions.explanation: Vishakhadatta's 'Mudrarakshasa', a political drama about Chanakya and Chandragupta Maurya, is written in Sanskrit.

questions.text: The Dravidian style of temple architecture can be largely seen from which part of India?
questions.explanation: The Dravidian style of temple architecture belongs to southern India; the Nagara style is the northern one.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a qualification/eligibility to become the President of India?
options: Must be qualified for election as a member of the house of the people
Must have completed the age of thirty-five years
Must be a citizen of India
Must hold any office of profit
questions.explanation: Under Article 58 a President must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old and qualified for election to the Lok Sabha, and is not eligible while holding an office of profit under the government.

questions.text: Which of the following dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate finally annexed Jaunpur into the empire of Delhi Sultanate?
questions.explanation: Bahlul Lodi defeated Husain Shah Sharqi and annexed the Sharqi kingdom of Jaunpur to the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.text: The property by virtue of which carbon can form a C-C covalent bond is called _______.
questions.explanation: Catenation is carbon's ability to bond with other carbon atoms into long chains and rings. Tetravalency is its valency of four.

questions.text: Losoong festival is predominantly celebrated in Sikkim by which of the following tribes?
questions.explanation: Losoong, the Sikkimese new year marking the end of the harvest, is chiefly a festival of the Bhutias.

questions.text: ________ received Padma Shri 2017 award for being an exponent of Nagpuri folk dance Jhumar.
questions.explanation: Mukund Nayak, a Nagpuri folk singer and dancer from Jharkhand, received the Padma Shri in 2017.

questions.text: In 2018, Ganesh and Kumaresh Rajagopalan won the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Carnatic instrumental music. For playing which instrument did they win this award?
questions.explanation: Ganesh and Kumaresh Rajagopalan are a Carnatic violin duo; their Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 2018 was for the violin.

questions.text: Which of the following diseases is detected by the Widal test?
questions.explanation: The Widal test detects antibodies against Salmonella Typhi, the bacterium that causes typhoid.

questions.text: To which state does the Indian tennis player Sumit Nagal belong?
questions.explanation: Sumit Nagal, the tennis player, comes from Jhajjar in Haryana.

questions.text: Which Indian Member of Parliament was given the 'India UK Outstanding Achievers Honour' in January 2023?
questions.explanation: Raghav Chadha, then the Aam Aadmi Party's Rajya Sabha MP, received the honour in London in January 2023, in the government and politics category.

questions.text: Which of the following events and their hosts is correctly matched?
options: ICC World Cup Men Cricket 2015 – India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh
ICC World Cup Men Cricket 2019 – England and Wales
ICC World Cup Men Cricket 2007 – England
ICC World Cup Men Cricket 2011 – Australia and New Zealand
questions.explanation: England and Wales hosted the 2019 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup. The 2015 edition was held in Australia and New Zealand, 2011 in India, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, and 2007 in the West Indies.

questions.text: Layers of varying thickness are found in which type of rock?
questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks form as layers of sediment are laid down and compacted, so they show layers (strata) of varying thickness.

questions.text: The Panchpatmali mineral deposit region is located in which state from the following?
questions.explanation: Panchpatmali, in Koraput district of Odisha, is one of India's largest bauxite deposits, mined by NALCO.

questions.text: Constipation could be a sign that the person in suffering from a lack of ___________.
questions.explanation: Dietary fibre (roughage) adds bulk and helps food move through the gut; too little of it leads to constipation.

questions.text: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution are borrowed from which country's constitution?
options: The Constitution of the Soviet Union
The Constitution of the United Kingdom
The Constitution of the United States
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV) were borrowed from the Irish Constitution.

questions.text: In 2023, the Government of India has proposed to set up how many new ‘Waste to Wealth’ plants under GOBARdhan?
questions.explanation: The Union Budget 2023-24 proposed 500 new 'waste to wealth' plants under GOBARdhan: 200 compressed biogas plants and 300 community or cluster-based plants.

questions.text: Who wrote the novel 'The Catcher in the Rye'?
questions.explanation: 'The Catcher in the Rye' (1951) is J. D. Salinger's novel, narrated by Holden Caulfield.

questions.text: What does M stand for in BHIM-UPI?
questions.explanation: BHIM stands for Bharat Interface for Money, the UPI app of the National Payments Corporation of India.

questions.text: As per Census 2011, what is the literacy rate of India?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 put India's literacy rate at 74.04%: 82.14% for men and 65.46% for women.

questions.text: Which is the largest agro-based Industry of India?
questions.explanation: The cotton textile industry, which draws its raw cotton from the farm, is India's largest agro-based industry.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'calendar'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Spanish person are well known worldwide / for their warm hospitality / and food.
options: Spanish person are well known worldwide
questions.explanation: The singular 'person' cannot take 'are' or stand for a whole nation: 'Spanish people are well known worldwide'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. They reinvested in their trades and indulged in “unobtrusive” consumption at home.
questions.explanation: 'Unobtrusive' means not attracting attention; its opposite is 'conspicuous'. 'Obscure' and 'faint' are close to synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Universal high-quality education is the best way forward for developing and maximising our country's rich talents and resources for the “good in the individual”, the society, the country and the world.
questions.explanation: The phrase is 'for the good of': 'for the good of the individual, the society, the country and the world'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. My mother always __________________ to help people.
questions.explanation: To 'go the extra mile' is to make more effort than is expected; 'turns a deaf ear' (refuses to listen) contradicts 'to help people'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Recluse
questions.explanation: A 'recluse' lives apart from others and avoids company; as an adjective the word means 'solitary'. 'Sociable' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Intractable
questions.explanation: 'Intractable' means hard to control or deal with: 'defiant'. 'Compliant' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelled sentence.
options: The athlete ran quickley across the finish line.
The athlete ran quickly across the finish line.
The athlet ran quicly across the finnish line.
The athelete ran quicly across the finish line.
questions.explanation: Only this sentence spells 'athlete', 'quickly' and 'finish' correctly.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: Having belief in yourself is the big key to success.
Having belief in yourself is the biggest key to success.
Having beliefs in yourself is the bigger key to success.
Having belief in yourself is the most bigger key to success.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'the biggest key to success': the superlative, which ranks belief in yourself above every other key. 'The big key' is not ungrammatical in itself, though it reads oddly; 'the bigger key' needs a 'than', and 'the most bigger' doubles the comparison.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. It is being asked why there has been no _________ taken yet.
questions.explanation: An 'action' is what is taken: 'no action taken yet'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Indeed, Jack is one of “the clever” men I have ever met.
questions.explanation: 'One of the' takes a superlative and a plural noun: 'one of the cleverest men I have ever met'.

questions.text: Identify the sentence with an error with respect to the use of present tense.
questions.explanation: The present continuous needs its auxiliary: 'She is singing romantic songs'. The other three sentences are correct.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.
options: It is strange to see a guy shouting in the mall without any reason.
It is too stranger to see a guy shouting in the mall without any reason.
It is too stranger to see a guy shouting in the mall beside any reason.
It is too stranger to see a guy shout in the mall without any reason.
questions.explanation: 'Too' goes with the positive degree, not 'stranger', and 'beside any reason' should be 'without any reason'. Only 'It is strange to see ...' is correct.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling error of the underlined word. Preserving our planet's biodiversity is essential for the health and “susteinability” of ecosystems and human life.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'sustainability'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. It is “all one” whether I go today or tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'It is all one' means it makes no difference: 'just the same'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Constant efforts to achieve something
questions.explanation: 'Perseverance' is continued effort to achieve something despite difficulty. 'Perspicacious' means shrewd, a 'euphemism' is a mild word for a harsh one, and to 'recant' is to take back a statement.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The street is crowded. You could easily get lost in this _________.
questions.explanation: A 'maze' is a confusing network of paths in which one gets lost; 'maize' (corn) only sounds the same.

questions.text: Which of the following words is a synonym of 'Evanescent'?
questions.explanation: 'Evanescent' means quickly fading or passing: 'fleeting'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It (1)_______ no discriminations to nationality, race, religious beliefs, class or political opinions. It endeavours to (2)_______ the suffering of individuals, being guided solely by (3)_______ needs, and to give priority to the (4)______ urgent cases of distress. It promotes mutual understanding, friendship, cooperation and lasting peace (5)_____ all people.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The subject 'It' is singular and the passage is in the simple present ('endeavours', 'promotes'): 'It makes no discriminations'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It (1)_______ no discriminations to nationality, race, religious beliefs, class or political opinions. It endeavours to (2)_______ the suffering of individuals, being guided solely by (3)_______ needs, and to give priority to the (4)______ urgent cases of distress. It promotes mutual understanding, friendship, cooperation and lasting peace (5)_____ all people.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: To 'relieve' suffering is to ease it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It (1)_______ no discriminations to nationality, race, religious beliefs, class or political opinions. It endeavours to (2)_______ the suffering of individuals, being guided solely by (3)_______ needs, and to give priority to the (4)______ urgent cases of distress. It promotes mutual understanding, friendship, cooperation and lasting peace (5)_____ all people.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The needs are the individuals' own: 'their needs'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It (1)_______ no discriminations to nationality, race, religious beliefs, class or political opinions. It endeavours to (2)_______ the suffering of individuals, being guided solely by (3)_______ needs, and to give priority to the (4)______ urgent cases of distress. It promotes mutual understanding, friendship, cooperation and lasting peace (5)_____ all people.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Priority goes to 'the most urgent cases', the superlative after 'the'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It (1)_______ no discriminations to nationality, race, religious beliefs, class or political opinions. It endeavours to (2)_______ the suffering of individuals, being guided solely by (3)_______ needs, and to give priority to the (4)______ urgent cases of distress. It promotes mutual understanding, friendship, cooperation and lasting peace (5)_____ all people.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Peace 'amongst all people': 'amongst' is used for relations within a group of more than two.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Akhil bought two articles at ₹4,500 each. He sold one article at a 12% gain but had to sell the second article at a loss. If he had suffered a loss of ₹395 on the whole transaction, then what was the selling price of the second article?
questions.explanation: The two articles cost ₹9,000, so with a loss of ₹395 they sold for ₹8,605. The first sold for 4,500 × 1.12 = ₹5,040, so the second for 8,605 − 5,040 = ₹3,565.

questions.text: There are two groups C and D of a class consisting of 32 and 40 students, respectively. If the average weight of group C is 60 kg and that of group D is 33 kg, then find the average weight of the whole class.
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 5% per year rate of interest for 5 years.

A vessel contains 80 litres of a mixture of alcohol and water in the ratio of 3 : 7. If 40 litres of the mixture is taken out from the vessel and replaced with 40 litres of water, then the ratio of alcohol and water becomes:
questions.explanation: The 80 litres hold 24 litres of alcohol and 56 of water. Taking out half leaves 12 and 28; adding 40 litres of water makes 12 : 68 = 3 : 17.

questions.text: A boat can travel at a speed of 42 km/hr in still water. If the speed of the stream is 3 km/hr, how much time (in hours and minutes) will be taken by the boat to go 157.5 km downstream, and then 78 km upstream?
questions.explanation: Downstream at 42 + 3 = 45 km/h, 157.5/45 = 3.5 hours; upstream at 42 − 3 = 39 km/h, 78/39 = 2 hours. Total 5.5 hours: 5 h 30 min.

questions.text: If apples and pears in a basket are in the ratio of 5 : 8, then find the percentage of pears (correct to two decimal places) in the basket.
questions.explanation: Pears are 8 parts out of 5 + 8 = 13: 8/13 × 100 = 61.54%.

questions.text: b is the sum of two quantities, one of which varies inversely as the square of a² , and the other of which varies directly as a. Identify the relationship between a and b if b = 49 when a = 3 or 5.
questions.explanation: Take b = k/a² + ma (the printed 'square of a²' means a²). b = 49 at a = 3 and at a = 5 gives k + 27m = 441 and k + 125m = 1,225, so 98m = 784, m = 8 and k = 225: b = 8a + 225/a².

questions.text: The average weight of two persons A and B is 70 kg. Another person C joins A and B and the average weight now becomes 72 kg. If another person D, whose weight is 2 kg less than that of C, replaces A, then the average weight of B, C and D becomes 70 kg. Find the weight of A (in kg).
A man bought an article for ₹500 and sold it for ₹400. Find his loss percentage.
The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 65 kg and 39 kg is:
Two numbers are in the ratio of 7:9 and their LCM is 630. Find the numbers
questions.explanation: The numbers are 7k and 9k, whose LCM is 63k = 630, so k = 10: 70 and 90.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
In a certain code language, ‘COST’ is coded as ‘5971’ and ‘SALE’ is coded as ‘8692’. What is the code for ’S’ in that language?
questions.explanation: S is the only letter in both words and 9 the only digit in both codes, so S = 9.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: Some mats are carpets. All carpets are sheets. Conclusions: (I) Some mats are sheets. (II) All sheets are carpets.
questions.explanation: The mats that are carpets are sheets, so some mats are sheets (I). All carpets being sheets does not make all sheets carpets, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (5, 14, 24) (9, 6, 24)
questions.explanation: Twice the first number plus the second gives the third: 2 × 5 + 14 = 24 and 2 × 9 + 6 = 24. Likewise 2 × 11 + 12 = 34.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts,decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All eggs are chickens. No chicken is a hen. Conclusions: (I) All chickens are eggs. (II) No egg is a hen.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Every egg is a chicken and no chicken is a hen, so no egg is a hen (II). All eggs being chickens does not make all chickens eggs, so I does not follow.

questions.text: CTVU is related to EVXW in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, BKGI is related to DMIK. To which of the following is SAEH related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: CTVU → EVXW and BKGI → DMIK. So SAEH → UCGJ.

questions.text: Seven friends - P, Q, R, A, X, Y, and Z - are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Y is sitting sixth to the right of Q. P is sitting third to the left of Y. A has Q and X as immediate neighbours. Z is to the immediate right of P. Who is sitting to the immediate right of R?
questions.explanation: With seven seats, sixth to Q's right is Q's immediate left, so Y sits there. Clockwise round the table: Q, Y, R, Z, P, X, A (facing the centre, each person's left is the next seat clockwise): P is third to Y's left, Z on P's right, A between Q and X, and R in the last seat. Y is on R's immediate right.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘life is rude’ is written as ‘tp ck gn’ and ‘this isn’t life’ is written as ‘gn dl sb’. How is ‘life’ written in that code language?
questions.explanation: 'life' is the only word in both sentences and 'gn' the only code in both, so life = gn.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? AZB, BYC, CXD, DWE ,?
questions.explanation: The first letters run A, B, C, D, E; the middle letters Z, Y, X, W, V; the last letters B, C, D, E, F. The next term is EVF.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only 2 people sit between B and D when counted from the left of D. E and C are immediate neighbours of A. G sits immediately to the right of F. Only 1 person sits between F and E when counted from the right of E. Who sits immediately to the left of F?
questions.explanation: Clockwise round the table: D, G, F, B, E, A, C (facing the centre, each person's left is the next seat clockwise). Counting left from D, G and F come before B; F is two seats to E's right with G on F's right, and A sits between E and C. B is on F's immediate left.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'HOST' is coded as '2846' and 'TEAM' is coded as '3587'. What is the code for 'T' in the given code language?
questions.explanation: T is the only letter in both words and 8 the only digit in both codes, so T = 8.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 25 – 45 × 9 ÷ 5 + 20 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 25 + 45 ÷ 9 × 5 − 20 = 25 + 25 − 20 = 30.

questions.text: 5 is related to 77 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 9 is related to 137. To which of the following is 3 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is 15 times the first plus 2: 15 × 5 + 2 = 77 and 15 × 9 + 2 = 137. Likewise 15 × 3 + 2 = 47.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 7 ? 22 37 57 82
VDIZ is related to ZGKA in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, HNAS is related to LQCT. To which of the following is BJWP related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The letters move +4, +3, +2, +1: VDIZ → ZGKA and HNAS → LQCT. So BJWP → FMYQ.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 121 + 1 – 6 ÷ 16 × 8 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 121 − 1 + 6 × 16 ÷ 8 = 121 − 1 + 12 = 132.

questions.text: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court of India propound the Basic Structure Doctrine of the Constitution?
options: Kesavanad Bharati vs. State of Kerala Case
Indira Gandhi vs. Raj Narayan Case
Golakhnath vs. State of Punjab Case
Maneka Gandhi vs Union of India Case
questions.explanation: In Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) the Supreme Court held that Parliament may amend the Constitution but not alter its basic structure.

questions.text: According to the Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023, which union territory has the least percentage of poor?
questions.explanation: In NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index: A Progress Review 2023 (data for 2019-21), Puducherry had the lowest share of multidimensionally poor people among the union territories.

questions.text: In 1527, Babur defeated Rana Sanga, the Rajput ruler of Mewar in the Battle of ________.
questions.explanation: Babur defeated Rana Sanga at Khanwa in 1527, a year after his victory at the First Battle of Panipat.

questions.text: Pushyamitra Sunga's capital was at:
questions.explanation: Pushyamitra Sunga, who overthrew the last Maurya king, ruled from Pataliputra, the old Mauryan capital.

questions.text: Who among the following was awarded the Sansad Ratna Award 2023 and represents the Indian National Congress in Lok Sabha from West Bengal?
questions.explanation: Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury, then the Congress MP for Baharampur in West Bengal and the party's leader in the Lok Sabha, was among the 2023 Sansad Ratna awardees. The other three were also honoured that year, but Kuldeep Rai Sharma was a Congress MP from the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, and Bidyut Baran Mahato (Jharkhand) and Sudhir Gupta (Madhya Pradesh) BJP MPs.

questions.text: Identify the Kuchipudi dancer, actor and film producer who won the best choreography award at the 68th National Film Awards 2022.
questions.explanation: Sandhya Raju won the National Film Award for Best Choreography at the 68th awards for the Telugu film 'Natyam'.

questions.text: Fugdi is famous dance of the state of _________.
questions.explanation: Fugdi is a folk dance performed by women in Goa and the Konkan region.

questions.text: Tanras Khan is associated with which of the following gharanas?
questions.explanation: Tanras Khan, a nineteenth-century khayal singer at the court of Bahadur Shah Zafar, is a leading figure of the Delhi gharana.

questions.text: The North-South National Highway Corridor connects which two UTs/States of India?
questions.explanation: The North-South Corridor of the National Highways Development Project runs from Srinagar in Jammu and Kashmir to Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: What is the primary role of autotrophic organisms in an ecosystem?
options: Producing organic matter from inorganic substances
Preying on other organisms for food
questions.explanation: Autotrophs such as green plants make organic food from inorganic substances (carbon dioxide and water) using sunlight: they are the ecosystem's producers.

questions.text: Which of the following water bodies are also known as nurseries of the ocean?
questions.explanation: Estuaries, where rivers meet the sea, are rich in nutrients and shelter the young of many marine fish and shellfish, hence 'nurseries of the ocean'.

questions.text: What is the term for a dome-shaped monument that contains sacred relics in Buddhism?
questions.explanation: A stupa is a dome-shaped mound built over relics of the Buddha or other revered figures. A chaitya is a prayer hall and a vihara a monastery.

questions.text: Who wrote the novel ‘Amrit Aur Vish’?
questions.explanation: Amritlal Nagar's Hindi novel 'Amrit Aur Vish' won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1967.

questions.text: According to the standard definition of Census of India, the marginal worker is a person who works for less than _______ days in a year.
questions.explanation: The Census of India counts as a marginal worker anyone who worked for less than 183 days (six months) of the year; 183 days or more makes a main worker.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The ‘Agaria’ community of the 19th century was associated with which of the following industries?
questions.explanation: The Agarias of central India were iron smelters, who made iron in small clay furnaces.

questions.text: Who inaugurated 'Vibrant Village Program' in april 2023?
questions.explanation: Union Home Minister Amit Shah launched the Vibrant Villages Programme for border villages at Kibithoo, Arunachal Pradesh, in April 2023.

questions.text: Why are wealth taxes and gift taxes treated as paper taxes in India?
options: Tax payers need to fill out forms only in paper and submit returns.
They do not generate much revenue in comparison to others.
They are paid only by government employees, members of the Parliament and Legislative assemblies.
It is not mandatory for the government to collect these taxes.
questions.explanation: Wealth tax and gift tax have never brought in much revenue, which is why they are called 'paper taxes'.

questions.text: Where is the Kala Ghoda Arts Festival organised every year?
questions.explanation: The Kala Ghoda Arts Festival is held every year in Mumbai's Kala Ghoda art district.

questions.text: What is the charge of an electron?
questions.explanation: An electron carries a negative charge; protons are positive and neutrons neutral.

questions.text: The ‘Dhansiri’ and ‘Subansiri’ are the tributaries of ________ River.
questions.explanation: The Subansiri joins the Brahmaputra from the north and the Dhansiri from the south, both in Assam.

questions.text: The Border-Gavaskar trophy is played between _________.
questions.explanation: The Border-Gavaskar Trophy, named after Allan Border and Sunil Gavaskar, is contested in Test cricket between India and Australia.

questions.text: Which of the following reports is considered as a piecemeal effort to provide resilience to the successful working of federal system?
questions.explanation: The Sarkaria Commission (set up in 1983) reviewed Centre-state relations and suggested ways to make the federal system work better. The Kothari Commission was on education; the Thakkar and Kapur Commissions inquired into the assassinations of Indira Gandhi and Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Banaras session of the Indian National Congress in 1905 was presided over by _________.
questions.explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale presided over the 1905 Banaras session of the Congress.

questions.text: Excessive bleeding from wounds may happen due to lack of ____.
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is needed to make the blood's clotting factors, so a lack of it can cause excessive bleeding.

questions.text: Anahat Singh is associated with which of the following sports events?
questions.explanation: Anahat Singh is one of India's leading young squash players.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Siva is a hard worker. He works ___________.
questions.explanation: 'Hard' is itself the adverb here: 'He works hard.' 'Hardly' and 'scarcely' mean almost not, which contradicts 'a hard worker'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. You can do your work well within the stipulated time and be more productive if you learn to keep video games “at the length of your arm.”
questions.explanation: The idiom is 'at arm's length': to keep something at a safe distance.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to substitute the underlined word segment in the given sentence. If the two families could “forget their past quarrels” forever, both could benefit immensely.
questions.explanation: To 'bury the hatchet' is to end a quarrel and make peace.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'parallel'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. There have been “numerous” attempts made by the citizens to restore parity.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'most numerous', with 'most' in its sense of 'very' (as in 'a most welcome change'), stressing how many attempts there were. 'Numerous attempts' alone is also correct English, so 'No substitution' is arguable too; 'more numerous' would need a comparison.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. I could _____ the reason for being _____.
questions.explanation: 'Find' (discover) and 'fined' (made to pay a penalty) sound alike: 'I could find the reason for being fined.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who brings a legal action against someone in court.
questions.explanation: A plaintiff brings a case against another person, the defendant, in a court of law.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase. In the “absence of government rule”, riots have broken out all over the country and everything is in a state of complete chaos.
questions.explanation: 'Anarchy' is disorder due to the absence of government or authority. Dictatorship, oligarchy and monarchy are all forms of rule.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Siliguri “has joined the nation to celebrate” the golden jubilee of the first conquest of Mount Everest by an Indian.
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'has joined' suits a recent action that still matters, and 'to celebrate' gives its purpose: the sentence is already correct.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Presumably
questions.explanation: 'Presumably' means probably, as one may reasonably suppose; its opposite is 'unlikely'. 'Certainly' only makes it stronger.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The detail given by the instructor was the ______ one.
questions.explanation: After 'the' the superlative fits: 'the most updated one'.

questions.text: Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence. The prisoners were living in “appalling” conditions.
questions.explanation: 'Appalling' means shocking or dreadful.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate homophone to fill in the blank. Looking up, she realised she had swum __________ than she’d thought.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'farther', the comparative traditionally used for physical distance; 'than' rules out the superlatives 'farthest' and 'furthest'. 'Further' is also used for distance, especially in British English, so it is arguable too.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: The myriad of possibilities unfolds when an artist embarks on the journey of creative experimentation.
A myriad of possibilities unfolds when the artist embarks on the journey of creative experimentation.
A myriad of possibilities unfolds when an artist embarks on a journey of creative experimentation.
The myriad of possibilities unfolds when the artist embarks on a journey of creative experimentation.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the sentence with the indefinite article throughout, as suits a general statement about any artist: 'A myriad of possibilities unfolds when an artist embarks on a journey of creative experimentation.' The versions with 'the' are not ungrammatical, but they presume a particular artist or journey already known to the reader.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He sings good / among all the / contestants in / the singing competition.
questions.explanation: 'Sings' needs an adverb: 'He sings well'. 'Good' is an adjective.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The recommendations of the committee / regarding changes in the eligibility criteria / was not accept.
options: regarding changes in the eligibility criteria
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'recommendations' takes 'were', and the passive needs the past participle: 'were not accepted'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The habit of reading is highly advantageous to us intellectually, emotionally and spiritually. As one gets into the habit of reading, one gets mental (1)________. It helps us acquire (2)________and attain intellectual (3)_________. Reading takes away our (4)_________. Reading can bring (5)__________ in our sorrowful times and guide us in our duties.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Reading gives 'mental satisfaction', in keeping with the passage's praise of it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The habit of reading is highly advantageous to us intellectually, emotionally and spiritually. As one gets into the habit of reading, one gets mental (1)________. It helps us acquire (2)________and attain intellectual (3)_________. Reading takes away our (4)_________. Reading can bring (5)__________ in our sorrowful times and guide us in our duties.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Reading helps us 'acquire knowledge', the usual pairing.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The habit of reading is highly advantageous to us intellectually, emotionally and spiritually. As one gets into the habit of reading, one gets mental (1)________. It helps us acquire (2)________and attain intellectual (3)_________. Reading takes away our (4)_________. Reading can bring (5)__________ in our sorrowful times and guide us in our duties.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Reading brings 'intellectual expansion': it broadens the mind, the opposite of 'stagnation'.
