markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 3% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
Raghav covers a distance of 45 km in 1 hour 40 minutes. Assuming he maintains a constant speed throughout his journey, what is Raghav’s speed (in m/s)?
questions.explanation: 45 km in 1 hour 40 minutes is 45,000 m in 6,000 seconds: 45,000/6,000 = 7.5 m/s.

questions.text: A sum of money amounts to ₹7,436 after 6 years and ₹9,460 after 10 years at the same rate of simple interest. Find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.explanation: The 4 years from year 6 to year 10 add ₹9,460 − ₹7,436 = ₹2,024 of interest, ₹506 a year. The principal is 7,436 − 6 × 506 = ₹4,400, so the rate is 506/4,400 × 100 = 11.5%.

questions.text: A shopkeeper buys 15 mobiles and sells 12 mobiles at the cost price of 15 mobiles. If the shopkeeper sells all the mobiles at the same price at which he sold the 12 mobiles in the first case, what is the profit percentage?
questions.explanation: 12 mobiles sell for the cost of 15, so each sells at 15/12 = 1.25 times its cost price: a profit of 25%.

questions.text: Find the arithmetic mean of 5, 15, 25, 26, and 27.
The average of nine consecutive numbers is 45. The largest number among these numbers is:
questions.explanation: The middle (fifth) of nine consecutive numbers equals their average, 45. The largest is four more: 49.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 5% per year rate of interest for 6 years.

Distance between A and B is 1200 km. If they start moving towards each other at same time, they will meet in 24 hrs. If A starts 10 hrs after B, then they will meet after another 20 hrs. What are their respective speeds?
questions.explanation: Together they cover 1,200 km in 24 hours, so a + b = 50 km/h. In the second case B travels 30 hours and A 20: 20a + 30b = 1,200, so 20 × 50 + 10b = 1,200, b = 20 and a = 30 km/h.

questions.text: A can contains a mixture of two liquids, grape juice and pineapple juice in the ratio 13 : 11. When 8 litres of the mixture is drawn off, and the can is filled with pineapple juice, the ratio becomes 13 : 14. How many litres of pineapple juice was initially contained in the can?
questions.explanation: Let the can hold 13k litres of grape and 11k of pineapple juice. Drawing off 8 litres removes 13/3 of grape and 11/3 of pineapple, and 8 litres of pineapple go back in: (13k − 13/3) : (11k − 11/3 + 8) = 13 : 14 gives 39k = 117, so k = 3 and there were 11 × 3 = 33 litres of pineapple juice.

questions.text: If the average of 53 consecutive even numbers is 1280. Find the difference between the smallest and the largest number.
questions.explanation: 53 consecutive even numbers span 52 steps of 2, so the largest is 52 × 2 = 104 more than the smallest.

questions.text: Find the volume of the largest right circular cone which is inscribed in a hollow cube of length 6 units and is standing on its base.
questions.explanation: The largest cone in a cube of side 6 has base radius 3 and height 6: V = (1/3)π × 3² × 6 = 18π units³.

questions.text: Find the HCF of 576,324 and 360
questions.explanation: 576 = 2⁶ × 3², 324 = 2² × 3⁴ and 360 = 2³ × 3² × 5. The HCF takes each common prime to its lowest power: 2² × 3² = 36.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/ subtracting /multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 18, 29; 49, 60
questions.explanation: In each pair the second number is the first plus 11: 18 + 11 = 29 and 49 + 11 = 60. Likewise 84 + 11 = 95.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 6, 12, ?, 144, 720 ,4320, 30240
questions.explanation: Each term is the one before multiplied by 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7 in turn: 6 × 2 = 12, 12 × 3 = 36, 36 × 4 = 144.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some horses are goats. All goats are jackals. Conclusions: (I): Some horses are jackals. (II): All jackals are goats.
questions.explanation: The horses that are goats are also jackals, so some horses are jackals (I). All goats being jackals does not make all jackals goats, so II does not follow.

questions.text: GNJF is related to IPLH in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, KRNJ is related to MTPL. To which of the following is OVRN related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: GNJF → IPLH and KRNJ → MTPL. So OVRN → QXTP.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘BLUE’ is coded as ‘5193’ and ‘CABS’ is coded as ‘3246’.What is the code for ‘B’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: B is the only letter in both words and 3 the only digit in both codes, so B = 3.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All kites are eagles. All eagles are birds. Conclusions: (I) All birds are kites. (II) Some birds are eagles.
questions.explanation: Every eagle is a bird, so some birds are eagles (II). Nothing makes every bird a kite, so I does not follow.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? MSN, LRM, KQL, JPK, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place back each time: M, L, K, J, I; S, R, Q, P, O; N, M, L, K, J. The next cluster is IOJ.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘MILK’ is coded as ‘5642’ and ‘LIKE’ is coded as ‘8425’. What is the code for ‘E’ in that language?
questions.explanation: I, L and K are in both words, as are 2, 4 and 5 in both codes. The letter left in LIKE is E and the digit left in its code is 8, so E = 8.

questions.text: Five friends, Ashish, Bipin, Chandu, Dinesh and Emmanuel, went on a trek. On the mountain top, they lit a campfire and sat around it in a circle facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). It was recalled that there was only one person sitting between Ashish and Chandu, while Chandu himself was sitting second to the left of Bipin. If Dinesh was an immediate neighbour of both Chandu and Bipin, who was sitting to the immediate right of Ashish?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left is clockwise. Clockwise from Bipin: Bipin, Dinesh, Chandu (second to Bipin's left, with Dinesh beside both), Emmanuel, Ashish (one person between Ashish and Chandu). Ashish's immediate right, anticlockwise, is Emmanuel.

questions.text: 4 is related to 41 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 9 is related to 91. To which of the following is 13 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 10 and 1 added: 4 × 10 + 1 = 41 and 9 × 10 + 1 = 91. So 13 × 10 + 1 = 131.

questions.text: ZMJI is related to UIGG in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, TIMN is related to OEJL. To which of the following is PHJI related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The letters move back 5, 4, 3 and 2 places: ZMJI → UIGG and TIMN → OEJL. So PHJI → KDGG.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only three people sit between E and F when counted from the left of E. Only three people sit between G and D when counted from the right of D. A sits to the immediate right of G. C is an immediate neighbour of D as well as F. Who sits second to the left of B?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, left is clockwise. Clockwise the order is E, A, G, B, F, C, D: three people between E and F counting from E's left, three between D and G counting from D's right, A to G's immediate right and C between D and F. Second to the left of B is C.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘SOAP’ is coded as ‘4729’ and ‘POSE’ is coded as ‘9257’. What is the code for ‘E’ in that language?
questions.explanation: S, O and P are in both words, as are 2, 7 and 9 in both codes. The letter left in POSE is E and the digit left in its code is 5, so E = 5.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? (8÷ 2)× 11 −9× 3 + (51÷ 17) × 6 = 30 (Note: Interchange should be done of the entire number and not individual digits of a given number.)
questions.explanation: As printed the left side is 4 × 11 − 27 + 3 × 6 = 35. Interchanging 11 and 6: 4 × 6 − 27 + 3 × 11 = 24 − 27 + 33 = 30.

questions.text: The elements in Group 17 of the periodic table are known as:
questions.explanation: Group 17 (fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine and astatine) are the halogens, the 'salt-formers'.

questions.text: How many other members are there in the Finance Commission EXCEPT, Chairman?
questions.explanation: Under Article 280 the Finance Commission has a Chairman and four other members, appointed by the President.

questions.text: ‘The Best Mistakes of My Life’ is an autobiography of which Indian Actor?
questions.explanation: 'The Best Mistakes of My Life' (2018) is the autobiography of the actor Sanjay Khan.

questions.text: Who among the following are the target beneficiaries for the ‘Vishwakarma Yojana’ launched by Government of India on 17 September 2023?
options: Individuals skilled in traditional folk dance
Individuals skilled in traditional folk songs
questions.explanation: PM Vishwakarma supports artisans and craftspeople who work with their hands and tools in 18 traditional trades, such as carpenters, potters and blacksmiths.

questions.text: A tunnel that runs through the cell wall between two plant cells is known as:
questions.explanation: Plasmodesmata are channels through plant cell walls that link the cytoplasm of neighbouring cells.

questions.text: As per Census 2011, which of the following union territories has the highest percentage of rural population?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census about 32% of Puducherry's people lived in rural areas, against about 25% in Daman and Diu and under 3% in Delhi and Chandigarh.

questions.text: The process by which a water body gradually becomes enriched with nutrients and minerals, mainly phosphorus and nitrogen, leading to enormous growth of algae on the surface of the water, thus decreasing the amount of dissolved oxygen in the water is known as:
questions.explanation: Eutrophication is the over-enrichment of water with nutrients such as nitrates and phosphates; the algal blooms it causes use up the dissolved oxygen.

questions.text: Who among the following married the Mughal emperor Jahangir in 1611 and received the title ‘Nur Jahan’?
questions.explanation: Mehrunnisa married Jahangir in 1611; he called her Nur Mahal and later Nur Jahan, 'light of the world'.

questions.text: During the Mauryan society, Megasthenes divided the Indian society into seven distinct groups. In which distinct group were the ‘king’s counsellors’ placed?
questions.explanation: Megasthenes listed seven classes: philosophers, farmers, herdsmen, artisans, soldiers, overseers and, seventh, the councillors and assessors who advised the king.

questions.text: Thetakudi Harihara Vinayakram, who became the first Carnatic musician to win a Grammy, is known for playing which musical instrument?
questions.explanation: Vikku Vinayakram plays the ghatam, a clay-pot percussion instrument; he shared the 1992 Grammy for Mickey Hart's album 'Planet Drum'.

questions.text: Which of the following banking institutions played an instrumental role in financial inclusion through microfinance loans and their expansion in India?
options: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
questions.explanation: NABARD launched the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme in 1992, the main channel of microfinance in India.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a tributary of Godavari River?
questions.explanation: The Kameng is a tributary of the Brahmaputra, flowing from Arunachal Pradesh into Assam. The Manjra, Indravati and Pranhita all join the Godavari.

questions.text: Deodhar Trophy is given in ________.
questions.explanation: The Deodhar Trophy is an Indian domestic one-day cricket competition.

questions.text: Which state topped the medal tally at the 37th National Games event held in Goa?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra topped the medal table at the 37th National Games, held in Goa in 2023.

questions.text: What solution should be used to test for the presence of starch in food?
questions.explanation: Iodine solution turns blue-black when starch is present.

questions.text: According to Article 51A of the Indian Constitution, it is the fundamental duty of every person to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and ______________________.
questions.explanation: Article 51A(c) makes it a fundamental duty to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India.

questions.text: Who introduced ‘Objective Resolution’ in the Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly on 13 December 1946; it was adopted on 22 January 1947.

questions.text: Which of the following ministries has launched the National Career Service Portal (www.ncs.gov.in) ?
options: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions
questions.explanation: The National Career Service portal was launched in 2015 by the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

questions.text: The Buland Darwaza was the structure built by Akbar at which of the following places in India?
questions.explanation: Akbar built the Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri to mark his conquest of Gujarat.

questions.text: Bhangra and Giddha dance forms are associated with which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Bhangra (danced mainly by men) and Giddha (by women) are folk dances of Punjab.

questions.text: Which of the following options contains groups of cropping seasons in India?
questions.explanation: India's three cropping seasons are rabi (winter), kharif (monsoon) and zaid (the short summer season between them). Podu and jhum are forms of shifting cultivation.

questions.text: Who among the following led the Indian delegation to attend the 56thAnnual General Meeting of the Board of Governors of Asian Development Bank (ADB) along with Investor/ Bilateral and other associated meetings, in Incheon, the Republic of Korea, from 2 to 5 May 2023?
questions.explanation: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman led India's delegation to the ADB's 56th Annual Meeting in Incheon in May 2023.

questions.text: On which of the following days is National Integration Day observed?
questions.explanation: National Integration Day is observed on 19 November, Indira Gandhi's birth anniversary.

questions.text: Raja and Radha Reddy were awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2000 for giving a new dimension to which dance form?
questions.explanation: Raja and Radha Reddy are leading exponents of Kuchipudi, the classical dance of Andhra Pradesh.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following freedom fighters was associated with the series of nine articles known as ‘New Lamp for Old’?
questions.explanation: Aurobindo Ghose's 'New Lamps for Old' (1893-94), a series of articles in the Bombay paper Indu Prakash, criticised the moderate politics of the Congress.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Jurisdiction
questions.explanation: 'Jurisdiction' is the official power to make legal decisions and to govern: 'governance' is closest.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who travels from place to place, especially for work
questions.explanation: An 'itinerant' travels from place to place, especially for work. A 'vagrant' has no settled home or job, a 'nomad' belongs to a wandering community and a 'pilgrim' journeys to a holy place.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The dancer / performed weird / but the music was / highly enchanting.
questions.explanation: A verb is modified by an adverb: 'performed weirdly', not 'performed weird'.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: If you want to have a sound working knowledge of Japanese, you must read this book.
If you want to have sound working knowledge of the Japanese, you must read this book.
If you want to have a sound working knowledge of the Japanese, you must read this book.
If you want to have an sound working knowledge of Japanese, you must read this book.
questions.explanation: A language takes no article ('knowledge of Japanese'; 'the Japanese' are the people), and 'sound' takes 'a', not 'an': 'a sound working knowledge of Japanese'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence. Success demands hard work, “diligence” and perseverance.
questions.explanation: 'Diligence' is careful, persistent work: 'effort'. 'Indolence' (laziness) is its opposite.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains anerror in phrasal verb. Bindu asked Arya to fill out for / her so that she could / take care of / her sick father.
options: Bindu asked Arya to fill out for
questions.explanation: To 'fill in for' someone is to do their work in their place; 'fill out' means to complete a form: 'Bindu asked Arya to fill in for her'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The restaurant's menu featured a variety of __________ dishes.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'delicious'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Head in the clouds
options: Thinking about the sky and clouds
questions.explanation: Someone with their 'head in the clouds' is a daydreamer, out of touch with practical matters.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'parliament'.

questions.text: Choose the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank meaningfully. His _______________ is a brilliant student.
questions.explanation: 'Son', a male child, fits the sentence; 'sun' sounds the same but means the star.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Woodcutting involves the removal of useless trees first, ________ by medium and finest quality timber trees.
questions.explanation: The medium and finest quality trees are removed after the useless ones: 'first, followed by'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I always prefer a small, cosy cottage ______ a high-rise apartment.
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' takes 'to' before the thing not chosen: 'prefer a small, cosy cottage to a high-rise apartment'.

questions.text: Change the following sentence into positive degree. Sushma is one of the smartest girls in the class.
options: Sushma is smarter than any other girls in the class.
Few girls in the class are as smart as Sushma.
No other girl is as smart as Sushma.
Sushma is the smart girl of the class.
questions.explanation: 'One of the smartest' puts Sushma among a few at the top; in the positive degree that is 'Few girls in the class are as smart as Sushma'. 'No other girl is as smart' would make her the smartest.

questions.text: Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence. Shylock, the Jewish moneylender, and Antonio, the rich Merchant of Venice “loathed” each other.
questions.explanation: 'Loathed' means hated intensely: 'abhorred'.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Choose the correct alternative. She is “late” than we expected.
questions.explanation: 'Than' needs the comparative: 'She is later than we expected.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment in the given sentence. Sarvana failed in the examination last week and is “in extreme depression” these days.
questions.explanation: To be 'in the doldrums' is to be low in spirits. 'In the red' is in debt, 'in the lurch' left in difficulty and 'in cold blood' without pity.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelled sentence.
options: The audiance applauded the musicans performance.
The audiance applauded the musician's perfomance.
The audience applauded the muzicians performance.
The audience applauded the musician's performance.
questions.explanation: The correct spellings are 'audience', 'musician's' and 'performance'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of ‘clarify’ in the sentence given below. The last question of the examination paper confused me when it asked to illustrate the Pythagoras’ theorem with the help of examples.
questions.explanation: To 'illustrate' is to make clear, especially with examples: the sentence's word closest to 'clarify'.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 3% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
Find the LCM of 8, 12, 18, 24 and 36.
questions.explanation: 8 = 2³, 12 = 2² × 3, 18 = 2 × 3², 24 = 2³ × 3 and 36 = 2² × 3². The LCM takes the highest powers: 2³ × 3² = 72.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 3% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
Maria buys a dress for ₹3,000. She could not decide between a discount of 35% and three successive discounts of 20%, 10% and 5%. The difference between both discounts (in ₹) is:
questions.explanation: A single 35% discount takes off ₹1,050. The successive discounts leave 3,000 × 0.8 × 0.9 × 0.95 = ₹2,052, taking off ₹948. The difference is ₹102.

questions.text: Geeta went to her home town at a distance of 270 km from her house. She started her journey at 10:00 a.m. and reached the destination at 02:00 p.m. by travelling 20 km by cab at a speed of 60 km/h and 240 km by train running at a speed of 80 km/h. She covered the remaining distance by an auto to reach her place. What was the speed of the auto?
questions.explanation: From 10:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. is 4 hours. The cab took 20/60 = 1/3 hour and the train 240/80 = 3 hours, leaving 2/3 hour for the remaining 270 − 260 = 10 km: 10 ÷ 2/3 = 15 km/h.

questions.text: Shikha sells a bookshelf to Vansh at a loss of 5%, Vansh sells the same bookshelf to Swarnima at a profit of 10%, and Swarnima sells the same bookshelf to Nikhil at a loss of 20%. If Nikhil purchased the bookshelf for ₹16,720, then what was the cost (in ₹) of the bookshelf for Shikha?
The average age of a husband and wife, and their child 3 years ago, was 27 years, and that of the wife and the child 5 years ago was 20 years. The present age of the husband is:
questions.explanation: Three years ago the three ages totalled 3 × 27 = 81, so now they total 81 + 9 = 90. Five years ago the wife and child totalled 2 × 20 = 40, so now 50. The husband is 90 − 50 = 40 years old.

questions.text: Rohit made a profit of 22% when he sold a jacket for ₹7,930. Find the cost price of the jacket.

15 kg of superior quality of wheat is mixed with 5 kg of inferior quality of wheat. The price of superior quality and inferior quality wheat is ₹80 and ₹60, respectively. Find the average price per kg of the mixture.
The average age of a class of 39 students is 15 years. If the age of the teacher be included, then the average increases by 3 months. Find the age of the teacher.
questions.explanation: The 39 students total 39 × 15 = 585 years. With the teacher the 40 average 15 years 3 months (15.25 years), a total of 610, so the teacher is 610 − 585 = 25.

questions.text: The average age of 40 students in a class is 12 years. The average age of the students increased by 4 months due to 20 new admissions in the class. The average age of the newly admitted students is:
questions.explanation: The 40 students total 40 × 12 = 480 years. Afterwards 60 students average 12 years 4 months (37/3 years), a total of 740. The 20 newcomers total 260 years: an average of 13 years.

questions.text: What is the single equivalent price increase for two successive price increases of 12% and 18% on an article?
questions.explanation: 1.12 × 1.18 = 1.3216: a single increase of 32.16%.

questions.text: On a 200-m-long circular track, two people start from the same point, at the same time, at speeds of 12 km/h and 15 km/h, respectively. After how much time will they meet again for the first time if they are running in the same direction?
questions.explanation: Running the same way, the faster gains 15 − 12 = 3 km/h = 5/6 m/s. They meet again when he has gained one lap of 200 m: 200 ÷ 5/6 = 240 seconds.

questions.text: The sum of length and breadth of a rectangle is 68 m and the ratio of length and breadth is 11:23. What is the area of the rectangle (in m²)?
questions.explanation: Length = 68 × 11/34 = 22 m and breadth = 68 × 23/34 = 46 m, so the area is 22 × 46 = 1012 m².

questions.text: If p is directly proportional to q and is p = 7 when q = 6, then what is the value of p when q = 21?
questions.explanation: p = kq with k = 7/6, so when q = 21, p = 7/6 × 21 = 24.5.

questions.text: BEAR is related to YBXO in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, WATCH is related to TXQZE. To which of the following is LOTUS related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back: B → Y, E → B, A → X, R → O. So L → I, O → L, T → Q, U → R and S → P: ILQRP.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘−’ and ‘×‘ are interchanged and ‘+’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 28 ÷ 18 + 6 × 6 − 4 = ?
questions.explanation: After the interchanges: 28 + 18 ÷ 6 − 6 × 4 = 28 + 3 − 24 = 7.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 25000, 5000, 1000, 200, 40, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is the one before divided by 5: 40 ÷ 5 = 8.

questions.text: 12 is related to 61 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 15 is related to 76. To which of the following is 16 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is five times the first plus 1: 12 × 5 + 1 = 61 and 15 × 5 + 1 = 76. Likewise 16 × 5 + 1 = 81.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘they are smart’ is written as ‘bt mt rt’ and ‘she is smart’ is written as ‘rt kt st’. How is ‘smart’ written in the given code language?
questions.explanation: 'smart' is the only word in both sentences and 'rt' the only code in both, so smart = rt.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? GKS, MQY, SWE, YCK, ?
questions.explanation: Every letter moves 6 places forward each time, wrapping round after Z: G, M, S, Y, E; K, Q, W, C, I; S, Y, E, K, Q. The next cluster is EIQ.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (12, 77, 5) (21, 87, 3)
questions.explanation: In each set the middle number is the product of the other two plus their sum: 12 × 5 + 12 + 5 = 77 and 21 × 3 + 21 + 3 = 87. Likewise 15 × 7 + 15 + 7 = 127.

questions.text: Seven people R, S, T, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). G is sitting second to the right of E. Only one person is sitting between G and R. Only one person is sitting between R and T. F is sitting second to the left of D. D is an immediate neighbour of T. How many people are sitting between S and T when counted from the left of S?
questions.explanation: Taking the seats anticlockwise, the direction of each person's right: E, S, G, F, R, D, T. G is second to E's right, one person sits between G and R and one between R and T, D is next to T and F is second to D's left. Going left from S, only E sits before T: one person.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 45 − 33 ÷ 3 × 4 + 67 = 22
In a certain code language, ‘JOKE’ is coded as ‘NIOY’ and ‘TRICKY’ is coded as ‘XLMWOS’. What is the code for ‘SPEAKERS’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +4 and −6 alternately, wrapping round the alphabet: J → N, O → I, K → O, E → Y. So S → W, P → J, E → I, A → U, K → O, E → Y, R → V and S → M: WJIUOYVM.

questions.text: Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: All crocs are frogs. All crocs are turtles. Conclusions: (I) All turtles are frogs. (II) At least some frogs are crocs.
questions.explanation: All crocs are frogs, so some frogs are crocs (II). Crocs are both frogs and turtles, but nothing says every turtle is a frog, so I does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 253 stands for ‘chairs are old’, 378 stands for ‘make good chairs’ and 546 stands for ‘lady is old’. Which of the following stands for ‘are’ in the same code language?
questions.explanation: 'chairs' is in the first two sentences and 3 in both their codes; 'old' is in the first and third, which share 5. That leaves 2 for 'are'.

questions.text: Six people A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). E is sitting second to the left of C. C is an immediate neighbour of both A and B. F is sitting third to the right of A. How many people are sitting between D and C when counted from the left of D?
questions.explanation: Taking the seats anticlockwise, the direction of each person's right: C, B, F, D, E, A. E is second to C's left, C sits between A and B, and F is third to A's right (with A on C's right, F would land on E's seat). Going left from D, F and B sit before C: two people.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All bongos are sitars. No cymbal is a sitar. Conclusions: [1] All sitars are bongos. [2] Some bongos are cymbals.
questions.explanation: Every bongo is a sitar and no cymbal is a sitar, so no bongo is a cymbal and 2 is false. All bongos being sitars does not make all sitars bongos, so 1 does not follow either.

questions.text: QFRG is related to NCVK in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, KZZO is related to HWDS. To which of the following is ETHW related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The first two letters move 3 places back and the last two 4 forward: Q → N, F → C, R → V, G → K. So E → B, T → Q, H → L and W → A (wrapping round): BQLA.

questions.text: In India, documented by a study, in which level of education is the majority of the population unemployed?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives graduates and post-graduates. In India the unemployment rate rises with education: the India Employment Report 2024 of the ILO and the Institute for Human Development put it at 29.1% for young graduates in 2022, against 3.4% for young people who could not read or write.

questions.text: In June 2023, which state Government launched a project named ‘Pride’ to provide employment opportunities to the transgender community in diverse and innovative sectors?
questions.explanation: Kerala launched the 'Pride' project in June 2023, run by the Kerala Knowledge Economy Mission and the Social Justice Department, to find jobs for transgender people.

questions.text: In the South Indian temples, the pyramidal tower is called the _________.
questions.explanation: In South Indian (Dravidian) temples the pyramidal tower over the sanctum is the vimana; in North Indian (Nagara) temples it is the shikhara.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of the office of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)?
options: Investigating and reporting on financial transactions
questions.explanation: The CAG audits the accounts of the Union and the states and reports on them to the President and the Governors, who lay the reports before the legislatures (Article 151).

questions.text: Coimbatore, which is located in the state of ________, is famous for the cotton textile industry.
questions.explanation: Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu, called the 'Manchester of South India', is a centre of the cotton textile industry.

questions.text: Which of the following States/Union Territories is included in the ‘Areas of Inadequate Rainfall’ of India?
questions.explanation: NCERT's division of India by rainfall puts Ladakh, with most of western Rajasthan and parts of the Peninsula, among the 'Areas of Inadequate Rainfall', with less than 50 cm a year. Haryana is among the 'Areas of Low Rainfall' (50 to 100 cm), and Meghalaya and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands get heavy rain.

questions.text: Hampi Utsava is a colourful cultural festival that emulates the ethos and grandeur of which of the following empires?
questions.explanation: Hampi Utsava, held at Hampi in Karnataka, recreates the splendour of the Vijayanagara Empire, whose capital Hampi was.

questions.text: Which of the following are edible polysaccharides?
questions.explanation: Starch, alginates, pectins and chitosans are all edible polysaccharides. Each of the other options includes something that is not a polysaccharide: actin and myosin are proteins, glucose is a monosaccharide and sucrose a disaccharide.

questions.text: In December 2023, which former Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) CEO and MD joined the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (IIT Bombay) as Head of Translational Research and Entrepreneurship?
questions.explanation: Rajesh Gopinathan, TCS's CEO and MD until 2023, joined IIT Bombay in December 2023. N. Chandrasekaran, his predecessor at TCS, chairs Tata Sons.

questions.text: Which of the following is a molecular compound?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is made of molecules held together by covalent bonds. NaCl, MgSO₄ and CaO are ionic compounds, made of ions rather than molecules.

questions.text: Eutrophication is a condition where excessive growth of algal bloom occurs on the surface of a water body because of abundant nutrients. Which of the following are the key nutrients for eutrophication?
questions.explanation: Excess nitrogen and phosphorus, from fertiliser run-off and sewage, feed the algal blooms.

questions.text: Mangalampalli Balamuralikrishna was an Indian Carnatic singer born in Sankaraguptam village of which state?
questions.explanation: Mangalampalli Balamuralikrishna was born in 1930 at Sankaraguptam in the East Godavari district of Andhra Pradesh.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘The Hungry Tide’?
questions.explanation: 'The Hungry Tide' (2004), set in the Sundarbans, is by Amitav Ghosh.

questions.text: The Parliamentary form of Government is a key feature given in the Indian Constitution and its provisions are detailed in Articles _____________ of Part V (Chapter II).
questions.explanation: Articles 79 to 122, Chapter II of Part V, deal with Parliament.

questions.text: Which of the following countries hosted the ACC Under-19 Asia Cup cricket in the year 2023?
questions.explanation: The 2023 ACC Under-19 Asia Cup was held in the UAE in December 2023; Bangladesh beat the hosts in the final at Dubai.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was the first President of Indian National congress?
questions.explanation: Womesh Chandra Banerjee (W. C. Bonnerjee) presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress, at Bombay in December 1885.

questions.text: Which of the following raw materials is NOT used to prepare the baking soda?
questions.explanation: Baking soda (NaHCO₃) is made from sodium chloride, water, carbon dioxide and ammonia: NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ + NH₃ → NH₄Cl + NaHCO₃. Sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) is what baking soda gives on heating, not a raw material for it.

questions.text: In the year 2010, Commonwealth Games was hosted by which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: Delhi hosted the 2010 Commonwealth Games.

questions.text: ‘Dollu Kunitha’ is primarily a folk dance of which of the following Indian states?
questions.explanation: Dollu Kunitha, a vigorous drum dance, is a folk dance of Karnataka.

questions.text: What is the duration for which a member of a House of Legislature of a State is, without permission of the House, absent from all meetings, thereof the house may declare his seat vacant?
questions.explanation: Under Article 190(4), if a member of a state legislature is absent from all its meetings for 60 days without its permission, the House may declare the seat vacant.

questions.text: Odissi dancer ____________ was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2022 in the dance category.
questions.explanation: The Odissi guru Niranjan Rout was chosen for the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 2022.

questions.text: Who among the following was the famous ruler of the Gauda Kingdom?
questions.explanation: Shashanka ruled Gauda (Bengal) in the early 7th century and killed Harsha's brother Rajyavardhana. Grahavarman was the Maukhari king of Kannauj and Rudradaman a Shaka ruler of western India.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Select the INCORRECT statement from the following.
options: The first cotton textile mill in India was established in Bombay in 1854.
The development of the cotton textile industry in Britain led to the decline of Indian textile producers.
Cotton clothes made in England had driven Indian clothes out of the markets of Europe and America in the beginning of the 20th century.
The Sale and Devang communities of South India were famous for weaving.
questions.explanation: English cotton goods drove Indian textiles out of their markets in Europe, America and Africa by the beginning of the 19th century, not the 20th. The other three statements are correct.

questions.text: According to the census of India 2011, which of the following states has the highest percentage of rural population?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 census about 89% of Bihar's people were rural, against about 86% in Assam, 78% in Uttar Pradesh and 68% in West Bengal.

questions.text: The famous Jain temple of Dilwara, built by Solanki rulers, is located at which place?
questions.explanation: The Dilwara temples stand at Mount Abu in Rajasthan; the earliest was built in 1031 by Vimal Shah, a minister of the Solanki king Bhima I.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word in the given sentence. Such specifications have revived our designers and manufacturers, whereas this new arrangement will “free” them.
questions.explanation: To 'free' is to release; its opposite is 'restrain'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'appraisal'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. 'Hold someone's feet to the fire'
options: Agree upon a shared venture with full conviction
Take big risks without knowing the consequences
Insist that someone fulfil their promises or obligations
questions.explanation: To hold someone's feet to the fire is to press them to keep their promises or do their duty.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can complete the given sentence. Recent research says that most of our cottage industries lack finance. Thus, they are ____________.
questions.explanation: 'Thrown out of gear' means put out of working order: without finance the industries cannot run smoothly.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. A hospital's “hygine” is the standard against which cleanliness is measured.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'hygiene'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Active community involvement _____________ a sense of belonging and contributes to the overall well-being of society.
questions.explanation: To 'foster' is to encourage or develop: involvement fosters a sense of belonging.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. The miracle of “resurection” is not medically proven.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'resurrection', with a double 'r'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The team with a high motivation level succeeded in its project despite of the challenges it faced.
options: despite of the challenges it faced.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' takes no 'of': 'despite the challenges', or 'in spite of the challenges'.

questions.text: The given sentence has an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. India is not on war with Pakistan.
questions.explanation: The phrase is 'at war': 'India is not at war with Pakistan.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. The “mellow” tune of the flute soothes me.
questions.explanation: 'Mellow' means soft and pleasant; its opposite is 'harsh'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. This boy performed / extremely good / in the / dance competition.
questions.explanation: 'Performed' is a verb, so it takes the adverb: 'extremely well', not 'extremely good'.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. It is “easiest” to stay calm than to protest.
questions.explanation: 'Than' compares two things, so the comparative 'easier' is needed; 'more easier' doubles it.

questions.text: Select the appropriate option to fill in the blank. I haven't seen him _______ last week.
questions.explanation: 'Since' goes with a point in time ('last week'); 'for' would need a length of time.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Disposed
questions.explanation: To dispose of something is to get rid of it; its opposite is 'retained', kept.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Some types of ________ suck blood.
questions.explanation: A leech is a worm that sucks blood; to 'leach' is to drain out of soil.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Nagamani, a brave student, lodged a F.I.R. against the criminal.
questions.explanation: 'F' is read 'ef', which begins with a vowel sound, so 'an F.I.R.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Sloppy
questions.explanation: 'Sloppy' means careless and untidy; 'dashing' means smart and stylish. 'Untidy' is a synonym.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that has a grammatical error. He will have to / knuckle up really seriously, / if he wants to / crack the upcoming deal.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb is 'knuckle down', to start working seriously; 'knuckle up' does not have this meaning.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Throughout human history, there have been numerous, strange and unexplainable events that have occurred on our (1)______. From mysterious disappearances to bizarre natural phenomena, these (2)_____ continue to captivate our imagination and spark curiosity. On 30 June 1908, a massive explosion (3)______ in the remote Tunguska region of Siberia. The (4)_____ of the explosion is still debated, but it is believed to have been caused by a meteor or comet. Another fascinating phenomenon, the Bermuda Triangle is a region in the western part of the North Atlantic Ocean where ships and planes have mysteriously (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The events have occurred on 'our planet', the Earth.
