markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Amithab has scored an average of 72 runs in his six interschool matches. In the next match, he scored 96 runs. What is his revised average score?
questions.explanation: Six matches at 72 make 6 × 72 = 432 runs; with 96 more the total is 528 over 7 matches: 528/7 = 75.428...

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
The average weight of a group of 8 people is 70 kg. After a new person joins the group, the average weight becomes 72 kg. What is the weight (in kg) of the new person?
questions.explanation: The total rises from 8 × 70 = 560 kg to 9 × 72 = 648 kg, so the new person weighs 648 − 560 = 88 kg.

questions.text: A person invested a certain sum of money at 6% per annum simple interest and another sum at 8% per annum simple interest at the same time. After 4 years, he received interest ₹1,560 from both sums. One-fifth of the first sum is equal to one-sixth of the second sum. Find the total sum invested.
questions.explanation: One-fifth of the first sum equals one-sixth of the second, so the sums are 5k and 6k. A year's interest is 0.06 × 5k + 0.08 × 6k = 0.78k, and 4 × 0.78k = 1,560 gives k = 500. Total = 11k = ₹5,500.

questions.text: The side of a square exceeds the side of another square by 3 cm and the sum of the areas of the two squares is 225 cm² . Find the sum of the perimeter (in cm) of both squares.
questions.explanation: With sides x + 3 and x: (x + 3)² + x² = 225, so x² + 3x − 108 = 0 and x = 9. The sides are 12 cm and 9 cm, and the perimeters add up to 4 × (12 + 9) = 84 cm.

questions.text: A well with an internal diameter 10 m is dug to a depth of 10 m. Earth taken out of it is spread all around the well to a width of 12 m to form an embankment. What is the height (in m, rounded off to 2 decimal places) of the embankment?
questions.explanation: Earth dug out = π × 5² × 10 = 250π m³. The embankment is a ring from radius 5 m to 5 + 12 = 17 m, of area π(17² − 5²) = 264π m². Height = 250π/264π = 0.947 ≈ 0.95 m.

questions.text: What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹360 in 2 years at 8% per year rate of interest?
Raima saves 14% from her income of ₹35,000. How much is her expenditure (in ₹)?

A thief is noticed by a policeman from a distance of 150 m. The thief starts running, and the policeman chases him. The thief and the policeman run at the rate of 8 m/s and 10 m/s, respectively. Find the distance travelled by the thief before being caught.
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 10 − 8 = 2 m/s on the thief, so he closes the 150 m gap in 75 seconds. In that time the thief runs 8 × 75 = 600 m.

questions.text: A dealer marked the price of an item 30% above the cost price. He allowed two successive discounts of 15% and 20% to a particular customer. As a result, he incurred a loss of ₹696. At what price did he sell the item to the customer?
questions.explanation: With cost price C, the selling price is 1.3C × 0.85 × 0.8 = 0.884C, a loss of 0.116C = ₹696. So C = ₹6,000 and the selling price is 0.884 × 6,000 = ₹5,304.

questions.text: The average of 70 values is 40. If each value is multiplied by 20, what will be the changed average?
questions.explanation: Multiplying every value by 20 multiplies the average by 20: 40 × 20 = 800.

questions.text: If the radius of the base of a right circular cylinder is reduced to one-third, keeping the height same, what is the ratio of the volume of the reduced cylinder to that of the original?
questions.explanation: V = πr²h, so with the height unchanged the volume varies as r²: (1/3)² = 1/9, a ratio of 1 : 9.

questions.text: If two kinds of resins costing ₹160 per kg and ₹210 per kg are mixed in the ratio of 2 : 3, then find the cost (in ₹) of the mixture per kg.

A length of a violin string varies inversely with respect to the frequency of its vibrations. The frequency of a 14-inch-long violin string is 450 cycles per second. Find the frequency of a 12-inch violin string.
questions.explanation: Length × frequency stays the same: 14 × 450 = 6,300, so a 12-inch string vibrates at 6,300/12 = 525 cycles per second.

questions.text: KB 9 is related to ED 2 in a certain way. In the same way, XF 11 is related to RH 4. To which of the following is UH 8 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves 6 back, the second 2 forward and the number falls by 7: K → E, B → D, 9 → 2 and X → R, F → H, 11 → 4. So U → O, H → J and 8 → 1: OJ 1.

questions.text: 326 is related to 335 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 419 is related to 428. To which of the following is 566 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is the first plus 9: 326 + 9 = 335 and 419 + 9 = 428. Likewise 566 + 9 = 575.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘TREE’ is coded as ‘POCD’ and ‘FOOT’ is coded as ‘BLMS’. How will ‘MIND’ be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: The letters move back 4, 3, 2 and 1 places: TREE → POCD and FOOT → BLMS. So M → I, I → F, N → L and D → C: IFLC.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre(but not necessarily in the same order). F is sitting third to the left of A. A is sitting second to the left of G. G is sitting to the immediate right of E. B is sitting to the immediate left of D. What is the position of F with respect to E?
questions.explanation: Going round the table to each person's left from E: E, A, D, B, F, C, G. This fits every clue (G to E's immediate right, A second to G's left, F third to A's left, B to D's immediate left), and F is three places to E's right.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘apple pen card’ is coded as ‘136’, ‘doctor no apple’ is coded as ‘243’ and ‘card is blocked’ is coded as ‘695’. How is ‘apple’ coded in the given code language?
questions.explanation: 'apple' is the only word in both the first and second sentences and 3 the only digit in both their codes, so apple = 3.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? PKQ ,OJP, NIO ,MHN, ?
questions.explanation: Every letter moves one place back each time: P, O, N, M, L; K, J, I, H, G; Q, P, O, N, M. The next cluster is LGM.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) of the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 45 × 3 + 9 – 18 ÷ 1 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 45 ÷ 3 − 9 + 18 × 1 = 15 − 9 + 18 = 24.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series? 255, 248, 241, 234 ,227, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 7 less than the one before: 227 − 7 = 220.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All doors are locks. Some locks are handles, Conclusions: (I) All handles are locks. (II) No door is a handle.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: Only some locks are said to be handles, and nothing is said of handles that are not locks, so I does not follow. The doors may or may not be among the locks that are handles, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: All cabbages are roses. All cabbages are tulips. Conclusions: (I) At least some tulips are roses. (II) All roses are cabbages.
questions.explanation: Every cabbage is both a rose and a tulip, so some tulips are roses (I). Nothing says every rose is a cabbage, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 11 × 7 − 48 + 6 ÷ 37 = 106
In a certain code language, ‘LIKE’ is coded as ‘4682’ and ‘BEAM’ is coded as ‘1358’.What is the code for ‘E’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: E is the only letter in both words and 8 the only digit in both codes, so E = 8.

questions.text: LQ87 is related to VA55 in a certain way. In the same way, QV59 is related to AF27. To which of the following is BG49 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Both letters move 10 places forward (wrapping round after Z) and the number falls by 32: L → V, Q → A, 87 → 55 and Q → A, V → F, 59 → 27. So B → L, G → Q and 49 → 17: LQ17.

questions.text: In a code language, ‘I want food’ is written as ' sickota dongre dujubu’, ‘I want drink’ is written as ‘bluto sickota dujubu', ‘food and drink’ is written as ‘dongre peppin bluto’, then what is the code for the word 'peppin' in this language?
questions.explanation: 'I want' is in the first two sentences, so 'sickota' and 'dujubu' stand for 'I' and 'want'; that leaves food = dongre and drink = bluto. The code left over in the third sentence, 'peppin', is 'and'.

questions.text: T, N, S, P, R and M are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). S is sitting second to the left of T. Only two people are sitting between S and R. M is not the immediate neighbour of S. P is sitting second to the right of R. How many people are sitting between N and M, when counted from the right of N?
questions.explanation: Going round the table to each person's left from T: T, N, S, P, M, R (S second to T's left, R opposite S, P second to R's right, M not beside S). Counting from N to the right, T and R come before M: two people.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 11, 66; 26, 156
questions.explanation: The second number is 6 times the first: 11 × 6 = 66 and 26 × 6 = 156. Likewise 18 × 6 = 108.

questions.text: The weaker warm storms that grow stronger over time are finally converted into huge storms or hurricanes. Which of the following climate regions is the origin of such hurricanes?
questions.explanation: Hurricanes are tropical cyclones: they form over warm tropical seas, whose surface water above about 27 °C supplies the heat and moisture that let a weak storm grow.

questions.text: Which type of loan is supported by MUDRA?
questions.explanation: MUDRA (Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency), set up in 2015, supports loans to non-corporate, non-farm small and micro enterprises under the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana.

questions.text: India launched the ‘National Social Assistance Programme’ in:
questions.explanation: The National Social Assistance Programme, with old-age pension, family benefit and maternity benefit schemes, was launched on 15 August 1995.

questions.text: The Iron Age site named Tekwada is located in _________.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Maharashtra, where Tekwada is one of the excavated sites with Iron Age remains.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Bissu Mela organised to thank Santoora Devi for the good harvest?
questions.explanation: The Bissu Mela of the Jaunsari people, held in the Jaunsar-Bawar area (Chakrata) of Uttarakhand's Dehradun district, honours the goddess Santoora Devi at harvest time.

questions.text: In Union Budget 2023, a sub-scheme of which of the following Yojanas has been proposed with the investment of ₹6,000 crore to enable activities of fishermen, fish vendors and micro and small enterprises?
questions.explanation: The Union Budget 2023-24 announced a new sub-scheme of the PM Matsya Sampada Yojana, with a targeted investment of ₹6,000 crore, for fishermen, fish vendors and micro and small enterprises.

questions.text: How many chances does a high jumper get for overcoming a certain height?
questions.explanation: A high jumper has three attempts at a height; three failures in a row put the athlete out of the competition.

questions.text: In Harappan civilisation, cities were planned with the streets generally oriented along the __________ directions.
questions.explanation: Harappan streets ran roughly north-south and east-west, the cardinal directions, crossing at right angles in a grid.

questions.text: In june 2022, Eknath Sambhaji Shinde became the Chief Minister of which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Eknath Shinde was sworn in as Chief Minister of Maharashtra on 30 June 2022.

questions.text: Which Census decade recorded the highest population growth rate (in terms of percentage) in India?
questions.explanation: India's population grew fastest in the 1961-1971 decade, by 24.80%, slightly more than in 1971-1981.

questions.text: To which of the following groups do whales belong?
questions.explanation: Whales breathe air through lungs, are warm-blooded and suckle their young: they are mammals, not fish.

questions.text: Who among the following received the Padma Shri 2021 for Panthi folk dance?
questions.explanation: Radhe Shyam Barle of Chhattisgarh received the Padma Shri in 2021 for Panthi, the folk dance of the Satnami community.

questions.text: The term 'Aus', 'Aman' and 'Boro' are associated with which crop in India?
questions.explanation: In West Bengal farmers grow three crops of rice (paddy) a year, called 'aus', 'aman' and 'boro'.

questions.text: What is the percentage of 's' character in the carbon atom of acetylene?
questions.explanation: Each carbon in acetylene (HC≡CH) is sp hybridised, one s and one p orbital, so it has 50% s character (sp² has 33.33%, sp³ 25%).

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct statement about the Rajya Sabha?
options: It is known as the Council of the States.
It is known as the lower house of the parliament.
All the members are directly elected by the people.
The term of the members is for 5 years.
questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is the Council of States, Parliament's upper house. Most of its members are elected indirectly by the state legislative assemblies, for six years.

questions.text: Anorexia Nervosa is an eating disorder characterised by _________. a) an abnormally heavy body weight b) an intense fear of losing weight c) a distorted perception of weight d) trying to lose weight by exercising excessively
questions.explanation: Anorexia nervosa involves a distorted perception of one's weight and efforts such as excessive exercise to lose weight. Sufferers have an abnormally low (not heavy) body weight and an intense fear of gaining (not losing) weight.

questions.text: Buddhadev Dasgupta was a famous instrumentalist of which of the following instrument?
questions.explanation: Pandit Buddhadev Dasgupta, a disciple of Radhika Mohan Maitra, was one of the leading sarod players of his time.

questions.text: Which of the following Mughal emperors issued silver coins in the honour of his wife Mehrunnisa?
questions.explanation: Mehrunnisa became Jahangir's queen, Nur Jahan, in 1611; Jahangir had coins struck in her name, a rare honour for a Mughal queen.

questions.text: The author of the Hindi novel ‘Kohre Mein Kaid Rang’ is:
questions.explanation: Govind Mishra won the 2008 Sahitya Akademi Award for his Hindi novel 'Kohre Mein Kaid Rang'.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following founded the 'Satyashodhak Samaj' in 1873?
questions.explanation: Jyotirao (Jyotiba) Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in Pune on 24 September 1873 to fight caste discrimination.

questions.text: Rabindranath Tagore referred to ____________ as Nritya Samragini, which translates to 'the empress of dance'.
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore gave the Kathak dancer Sitara Devi the title 'Nritya Samragini' after seeing her dance as a girl.

questions.text: Which of the following Fundamental Rights entails trafficking of human beings and forced labour?
questions.explanation: The Right against Exploitation (Articles 23 and 24) bans trafficking in human beings and forced labour (Article 23) and the employment of children in hazardous work (Article 24).

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal?
questions.explanation: Sir William Jones founded the Asiatic Society in Calcutta on 15 January 1784.

questions.text: Ujjwala was the mascot of which national sports event held in 2023?
questions.explanation: Ujjwala, a sparrow standing for Delhi, was the mascot of the first Khelo India Para Games, held in New Delhi in December 2023.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a physiographic division of India?
questions.explanation: NCERT divides India into six physiographic divisions: the Himalayan Mountains, the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Indian Desert, the Coastal Plains and the Islands. The Tibetan Plateau lies beyond the Himalayas, in Tibet.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. Rohit asked Nita what was the most “intriguing” book she has read recently.
questions.explanation: The instruction, as SSC printed it, is missing a word (most likely 'ANTONYM'). SSC's key gives 'tedious', dull and tiresome, the opposite of 'intriguing', fascinating; it is also the only option that makes sense in the sentence, and none of the options means the same as 'intriguing'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word..
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'occurrence'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The ancient Greeks and pagans used to worship natural _________ as Gods and Goddesses.
questions.explanation: The ancients worshipped natural 'elements', such as the sun, wind, water and fire, as gods and goddesses.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Most women are “facing the same problem” when it comes to job satisfaction because of the pay parity in institutions.
questions.explanation: To be 'in the same boat' is to share the same difficult situation with others.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Rose painted the most beautifullest picture ever at the art class today!
questions.explanation: 'Beautiful' takes 'most' for its superlative: 'the most beautiful picture'. 'Most beautifullest' is a double superlative, and 'beautifullest' is not a word.

questions.text: Correct the underlined part of the sentence. This mango is “bitterer”.
questions.explanation: Nothing is compared with the mango, so the positive degree is needed: 'This mango is bitter.'

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Inflamous' is not a word; the spelling is 'infamous', well known for something bad. 'Kerbstone' is the British spelling of 'curbstone'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. one who does something for pleasure
questions.explanation: A hedonist is one who lives for and pursues pleasure. (One who takes up an activity for pleasure rather than pay is an 'amateur', which is not among the options.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. Raju is “lazy” and smart, but he does not attend the classes.
questions.explanation: 'Lazy' means unwilling to work; its opposite is 'industrious', hard-working. 'Lax' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He pressed the _________ just in time to avoid the accident.
questions.explanation: A vehicle is stopped with its 'brake'; 'break' sounds the same but means something else.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. Even if an unlaced shoe is spotless, it is not “neat”.
questions.explanation: 'Neat' means clean and tidy; its opposite is 'soiled', made dirty.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence..
options: The traffic on the highway was heavy during an evening.
A traffic on the highway was heavy during an evening.
The traffic on a highway was heavy during an evening.
The traffic on the highway was heavy during the evening.
questions.explanation: The highway and the evening are particular ones, so both take 'the': 'The traffic on the highway was heavy during the evening.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. My brother asked me, "Can I exchange “my phone from you”?"
questions.explanation: Of the options only 'with' goes with 'exchange': 'Can I exchange my phone with yours?' 'Since', 'off' and 'within' do not.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Any declarations or practices of religious “antipathy” against ethnic minorities in a democratic country should not be tolerated.
questions.explanation: 'Antipathy' is a deep-seated dislike or hostility: 'enmity'.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in future perfect tense form. I hope you wash all the clothes before you come into the house again.
options: I hope you will have wash all the clothes before you come into the house again.
I hope you shall wash all the clothes before you come into the house again
I hope you will have washed all the clothes before you come into the house again.
I hope you will be washing all the clothes before you come into the house again.
questions.explanation: The future perfect is 'will have' + past participle: 'will have washed'. 'Will have wash' uses the wrong form of the verb, and 'will be washing' is the future continuous.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word...
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'depressed'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Everyone disliked the new CEO, Kushal, but nobody is ready to “put themselves in dangerous situation” by telling him their feelings.
questions.explanation: To 'bell the cat' is to take on a dangerous task for the good of all: here, telling the disliked CEO what everyone feels.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: The intrepid explorer stumbled upon the uncharted cavern deep within the heart of the rainforest.
An intrepid explorer stumbled upon an uncharted cavern deep within the heart of the rainforest.
The intrepid explorer stumbled upon an uncharted cavern deep within a heart of the rainforest.
An intrepid explorer stumbled upon the uncharted cavern deep within a heart of the rainforest.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the sentence with 'an' for the explorer and the cavern, both met here for the first time, and 'the heart of the rainforest' (it has only one). The version with 'the' throughout is not ungrammatical, but it presumes an explorer and a cavern already known to the reader; 'a heart of the rainforest' is wrong.

questions.text: Read the sentence given below and identify if there is an error in it. The error can be in any segment of the sentence which are marked A, B, C, and D. Select option D if there is 'No error'. (A) She sings / (B) the song / (C) beautiful in the party / (D) No error.
questions.explanation: A verb is modified by an adverb: 'She sings the song beautifully', so the error is in C.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I am calling to thank you _________ the present you sent.
questions.explanation: One thanks someone 'for' something: 'thank you for the present'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Newspapers are like mirrors (1)___________ the diverse facets of society, capturing the voices, stories, and events that define our shared human experience. They serve as a forum (2)___________ dialogue, debate, and discussion, amplifying voices from all walks of life and fostering (3)___________ sense of community. Beyond reporting news, newspapers also celebrate achievements, highlight cultural (4)___________, and showcase human resilience in the face of adversity. They are archives of history, chronicling the triumphs and trials of generations, and serving as a reminder of how far we have come and how much further we can go. In an age of digital transformation, newspapers continue to (5)___________, adapting to new mediums while upholding the core values of journalism: accuracy, integrity, and accountability.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Mirrors reflecting the diverse facets of society': the '-ing' participle describes the mirrors.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The individual weights (in kg) of six boys are 55, 56, 57, 60, 59 and 55. A new boy joins the group, and the mean weight of the group becomes 62 kg. Find the weight of the new boy (in kg).
questions.explanation: The six boys weigh 55 + 56 + 57 + 60 + 59 + 55 = 342 kg. Seven boys averaging 62 kg weigh 7 × 62 = 434 kg, so the new boy weighs 434 − 342 = 92 kg.

questions.text: The average age of four boys Shikhar, Mukesh, Anil, and Anish is 25 years. If the ages of Shikhar, Mukesh, and Anil are 15, 25, and 29 years, then what is the age (in years) of Anish?
questions.explanation: The four total 4 × 25 = 100 years and the other three 15 + 25 + 29 = 69, so Anish is 100 − 69 = 31.

questions.text: A man on a tour of 400 km, travels the first 120 km at 80 km/h and the next 150 km at 75 km/h. If he must spend less than 5 hours in the tour, what is the minimum speed at which he has to travel for the remaining distance?
questions.explanation: The first 120 km take 120/80 = 1.5 hours and the next 150 km take 150/75 = 2 hours. The remaining 130 km must take under 1.5 hours, so the speed must be above 130 ÷ 1.5 = 86.666… km/h, which SSC's key gives as 86.66 km/h.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 6 years.

Ajit walks around a circular field at the speed of two rounds per hour, while Mohit runs around it at the speed of 10 rounds per hour. They start in the same direction from the same point at 6.30 a.m. Find the time at which they cross each other.
questions.explanation: Mohit gains 10 − 2 = 8 rounds an hour on Ajit, so he gains a full round and passes him after 1/8 hour = 7 minutes 30 seconds: at 6:37:30 a.m.

questions.text: There are 98 women in a group and their average weight is 52 kg. If 7 women of average weight 60 kg leave the group and two new women of average weight 80 kg join the group, then what will be the new average weight of women in the group now?
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
Which of the following is true about average?
options: The average of six consecutive even integers is an even natural number
The average of six consecutive odd integers is an odd natural number.
The average of six consecutive odd integers is an even integer.
The average of six consecutive odd integers is an odd integer.
questions.explanation: Six consecutive odd integers are a, a + 2, …, a + 10 with a odd; their average is a + 5, an even integer. (Six consecutive even integers average a + 5 with a even, an odd number.)

questions.text: Simple interest on a given sum for 3 years at a rate of 17% per year is ₹7,140 less than the simple interest on the same sum for 5 years. Find the sum.

The number of schools in a city is directly proportional to the population of the city. In 2020, there were 125 schools and the population of the city was 1,80,000. In 2023, the number of schools in the city is 180. What is the percentage increase in the population of the city from 2020 to 2023?
questions.explanation: The population rises in the same proportion as the number of schools: from 125 to 180 is a rise of 55/125 = 44%.

questions.text: By selling an article for ₹19, a dealer makes a profit of 25%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹) so as to make a profit of 50%?
questions.explanation: Cost price = 19/1.25 = ₹15.20. A 50% profit needs a price of 15.20 × 1.5 = ₹22.80, a rise of ₹3.80.

questions.text: The marked price of a table is ₹10,500, and it was sold for ₹9,450. Find the percentage discount for this transaction.
A teacher wanted certain groups of students with exactly 10 or12 or 15 members. What minimum number of students must be there in the class to make the required groups?
questions.explanation: The class must divide exactly into groups of 10, of 12 or of 15, so the smallest class is LCM(10, 12, 15) = 60.

questions.text: Find the total surface area of hemisphere of radius 6.3 cm.
questions.explanation: Total surface area of a hemisphere = 3πr² = 3 × 22/7 × 6.3 × 6.3 = 374.22 cm², about 374.2 cm².

questions.text: ADKR is related to CBMP in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, GXQL is related to IVSJ. To which of the following is OPYD related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The letters move +2, −2, +2, −2: A → C, D → B, K → M, R → P and G → I, X → V, Q → S, L → J. So O → Q, P → N, Y → A (wrapping round) and D → B: QNAB.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘×’ are interchanged and ‘−’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 100 − 4 ÷7 + 5 × 12 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 100 ÷ 4 − 7 × 5 + 12 = 25 − 35 + 12 = 2.

questions.text: BI54 is related to XE64 in a certain way. In the same way, DK76 is related to ZG86. To which of the following is FM43 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places back and the number rises by 10: B → X, I → E, 54 → 64. So F → B, M → I and 43 → 53: BI53.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 247 258 280 313 357 ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 11, 22, 33, 44, so the next is 55: 357 + 55 = 412.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘HARD’ is coded as ‘1596’ and ‘CARD’ is coded as ‘5689’. What is the code for ‘C’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: A, R and D are in both words, as are 5, 9 and 6 in both codes. The letter left in CARD is C and the digit left in its code is 8, so C = 8.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (34, 22, 63) (61, 76, 144)
questions.explanation: The third number is the sum of the first two plus 7: 34 + 22 + 7 = 63 and 61 + 76 + 7 = 144. Likewise 45 + 41 + 7 = 93.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series based on the English alphabetical order? DKO, GJL, JII, MHF ,?
questions.explanation: First letters move +3 (D, G, J, M, P), second letters −1 (K, J, I, H, G) and third letters −3 (O, L, I, F, C): PGC.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: All ants are balls. All ants are dolls. Conclusions: (I) Some balls are dolls. (II) All dolls are ants.
questions.explanation: Every ant is both a ball and a doll, so some balls are dolls (I). Nothing says every doll is an ant, so II does not follow.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). F sits third to the left of A. D sits to the immediate left of A. C sits second to the right of A. Only E sits between A and C. When counted from right of A, who sits to the immediate left of B?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, left runs clockwise. F is opposite A, D on A's immediate left, E on its immediate right and C next to E, so clockwise from A the order is A, D, B, F, C, E. F sits to B's immediate left.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 69 − 36 × 6 ÷ 12 + 5 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 69 + 36 ÷ 6 × 12 − 5 = 69 + 72 − 5 = 136.

questions.text: 13 is related to 38 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 15 is related to 44. To which of the following is 26 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is three times the first minus 1: 13 × 3 − 1 = 38 and 15 × 3 − 1 = 44. Likewise 26 × 3 − 1 = 77.

questions.text: P, Q, R, S, T and U are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). R is sitting to the immediate left of P and immediate right of T. Q is sitting to the immediate left of T. U is sitting to the immediate left of Q. P is sitting to the immediate left of S. Who is sitting to the immediate right of S?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, left runs clockwise. R is on P's left and T's right, Q on T's left, U on Q's left and P on S's left, so clockwise the order is P, R, T, Q, U, S. U sits to S's immediate right.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some pizzas are burgers. Some pizzas are sausages. Conclusions: (I) At least some sausages are burgers. (II) Some sausages are pizzas.
questions.explanation: Some pizzas are sausages, so some sausages are pizzas (II). The pizzas that are burgers and those that are sausages need not overlap, so I does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘joy salt area’ is coded as 'sd vt de' and ‘area kit care’ is coded as ‘vt fu pv’. How is ‘area’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'area' is the only word in both sentences and 'vt' the only code in both, so area = vt.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘TASK’ is coded as ‘3762’ and ‘CAST’ is coded as ‘2436’. What is the code for ‘K’ in that language?
questions.explanation: T, A and S are in both words, as are 3, 6 and 2 in both codes. The letter left in TASK is K and the digit left in its code is 7, so K = 7.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is/are correct according to the Census of India-2011? (a) A person aged seven years or above, who can both read and write with understanding in any language, is treated as literate. (b) A person who can only read but cannot write is not literate.
questions.explanation: The 2011 Census counts a person aged seven or above who can both read and write with understanding in any language as literate; one who can only read is not.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct about Ribosomes? Statement A: Ribosomes have no membrane. Statement B: Digestive hydrolytic enzymes are present in Ribosomes. Statement C: These are called suicidal bags. Statement D: Ribosomes play an important role in protein synthesis.
options: Only statements A, B and C
questions.explanation: Ribosomes have no membrane and are the sites of protein synthesis. Digestive hydrolytic enzymes, and the name 'suicidal bags', belong to lysosomes.

questions.text: Which of the following award did Pandit Ravi Shankar win for four times?
questions.explanation: The sitar maestro Ravi Shankar won four Grammy Awards: for 'West Meets East' with the violinist Yehudi Menuhin, 'The Concert for Bangladesh', 'Full Circle: Carnegie Hall 2000' and, after his death, 'The Living Room Sessions Part 1'.

questions.text: In May 2023, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been awarded the highest honours by the Pacific island nations of Papua New Guinea and ______________.
questions.explanation: In May 2023 Papua New Guinea made Narendra Modi a Grand Companion of the Order of Logohu and Fiji a Companion of the Order of Fiji, each country's highest honour.

questions.text: The Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY) was launched by which Ministry of Government of India in the year 2016?
options: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
questions.explanation: PMRPY, a Ministry of Labour and Employment scheme run through the EPFO, encouraged employers to take on new workers by having the government pay the employer's provident-fund contribution for them.

questions.text: Which of the following articles mentions about the Appropriation Bills in the state legislature?
questions.explanation: Article 204 provides for the Appropriation Bill in a State Legislature; Article 114 is its counterpart for Parliament.

questions.text: A molecule with the chemical formula C₂H₆ is a/an _______ molecule.
questions.explanation: C₂H₆ is ethane, the two-carbon alkane; methane is CH₄, propane C₃H₈ and butane C₄H₁₀.

questions.text: Who is the recipient of Padma Vibhushan 2000 for reviving the Odissi Classical dance form?
questions.explanation: Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, who led the revival of Odissi, received the Padma Vibhushan in 2000.

questions.text: Which of the following is a public sector industry in India?
questions.explanation: SAIL is a government-owned public sector company; Bajaj, Hindustan Unilever and Tata Steel (TISCO) are private.

questions.text: Which of the following states launched Mukhya Mantri Vriksh Sampada Yojana in March 2023?
questions.explanation: Chhattisgarh launched the Mukhya Mantri Vriksh Sampada Yojana on 21 March 2023, World Forestry Day, to encourage farmers to plant commercially valuable trees on their land.

questions.text: Nife layer of earth is situated in the ________.
questions.explanation: In Suess's division of the Earth's layers, SIAL is the upper crust, SIMA lies below it, and NIFE (nickel and iron) is the core.

questions.text: In which of the following months is the Tuluni festival celebrated in Nagaland by the Sumi tribe?
questions.explanation: Tuluni, the main festival of the Sumi Nagas, is celebrated in July.

questions.text: Who among the following was the first Law and Justice Minister of independent India?
questions.explanation: B. R. Ambedkar was independent India's first Law Minister, in Nehru's first cabinet.

questions.text: Which city hosted the XXII Commonwealth Games 2022?
questions.explanation: Birmingham, in England, hosted the 22nd Commonwealth Games in 2022.

questions.text: Which of the following crops that spread to northern India in the early years of the 17th century was NOT mentioned in the Ain-i-Akbari in the lists of crops in northern India?
questions.explanation: NCERT notes that tobacco reached the Deccan first and spread to northern India in the early 17th century, and that the Ain-i-Akbari does not list it among the crops of northern India.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
questions.explanation: France gave the Constitution the republic and the ideals of liberty, equality and fraternity, not the President's functions. The other pairs are right: the rule of law from Britain, the Concurrent List from Australia and 'procedure established by law' from Japan.

questions.text: In tennis, what is a 'love' score?
options: The highest possible score in a game
The score when the game is tied
The score when a player wins the first point in a game
The score when a player has zero points
questions.explanation: In tennis 'love' means zero: a player who has not yet won a point in the game is on love.

questions.text: Which of the following was the first subcontinental empire?
questions.explanation: The Mauryan Empire, founded by Chandragupta Maurya, was the first to bring most of the subcontinent under one rule.

questions.text: The Indian Bureau of Mines (IBM) was established in the year ________.
questions.explanation: The Indian Bureau of Mines was set up on 1 March 1948; it now works under the Ministry of Mines.

questions.text: What are the three components of the empowerment model in SAPAP of SHGs?
options: Social mobilisation, economic development, and education
Collective empowerment, capital formation, and poverty eradication
Social mobilisation, capital formation, and capacity building
Public resource allocation, capacity building, and microfinance
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives social mobilisation, capital formation and capacity building as the three components of the empowerment model of SAPAP (the South Asia Poverty Alleviation Programme), which organised the poor into self-help groups.

questions.text: What cellular structure is responsible for breaking down and recycling cellular components and molecules?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes hold hydrolytic enzymes that break down worn-out organelles and other molecules for reuse.

questions.text: 'Yakshagana', the famous folk dance, is associated with which state?
questions.explanation: Yakshagana, a folk dance-drama of coastal Karnataka, combines dance, music and dialogue.

questions.text: The famous Qila-i-Kuhna (mosque of the old fort) was built by:
questions.explanation: Sher Shah Suri built the Qila-i-Kuhna mosque inside the Purana Qila in Delhi.

questions.text: ‘Getting A Grip: On My Body, My Mind, My Self’ is an autobiography by who among the following tennis icons?
questions.explanation: 'Getting a Grip' (2009) is the memoir of Monica Seles, the former world number one.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The College of Fort William was established at ______ under British rule.
questions.explanation: Lord Wellesley founded the College of Fort William at Calcutta in 1800 to train British officials in Indian languages.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. You know that I am fond of reading / and also that all books are my favourite / but you don’t know that this is one of / my favourite book.
options: You know that I am fond of reading
but you don’t know that this is one of
and also that all books are my favourite
questions.explanation: 'One of' takes a plural noun: 'one of my favourite books'.

questions.text: Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error. The worlds you and I belong to are very “defferent”.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'different'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Vague
questions.explanation: 'Vague' means not clearly stated or defined: 'indefinite'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Fluctuate
questions.explanation: To 'fluctuate' is to rise and fall irregularly; its opposite is to stay 'steady'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'superannuation', with one 'p'.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the options given.
options: Neither the boy nor the mother could identify the man.
Neither a boy nor a mother could identify the man.
Neither the boy nor a mother could identify a man.
Neither a boy nor the mother could identify a man.
questions.explanation: The boy, the mother and the man are particular people, so each takes the definite article: 'Neither the boy nor the mother could identify the man.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The space or room that is at the top of a building or just below the main roof
questions.explanation: An attic is the space or room just below the roof of a building.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. We “can observed from” the poll that the award is likely to go to the horror movie director this year.
questions.explanation: A modal such as 'can' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'We can observe from the poll'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. Getting a sudden promotion and increment in my current profile was like _________.
questions.explanation: 'A bolt from the blue' is a sudden, unexpected event, like an unlooked-for promotion.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Extensive
questions.explanation: 'Extensive' means large in extent or range; its opposite is 'limited'.

questions.text: Select the option with the correct spelling to replace the underlined word in the given sentence. Development does not take place in a “vaccum”.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'vacuum': one 'c' and two 'u's.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. He is the “healthy” person I have ever met in life.
questions.explanation: 'The … I have ever met' calls for the superlative, and 'healthy' forms it with '-iest': 'the healthiest person'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Amplify
questions.explanation: To 'amplify' is to enlarge or increase; its opposite is to 'contract'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. Stephan, however, contrived / to put away / his departure / for eighteen months.
questions.explanation: To postpone is to 'put off': 'contrived to put off his departure for eighteen months'. 'Put away' means to store something or set it aside.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Her decision, / given the complex circumstances, / was too impulsively made.
questions.explanation: SSC's key marks 'was too impulsively made', presumably for the more natural 'was made too impulsively'. An adverb before the participle ('a hastily made decision') is also acceptable English, so this is a point of style rather than a clear error.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Chetan's room is clean / than Ram's room because / Chetan cleans it more often than Ram.
options: Chetan cleans it more often than Ram
questions.explanation: 'Than' needs the comparative: 'Chetan's room is cleaner than Ram's room'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. Our ______ has so many magnificent tourist destinations, with unimaginable potential, yet to ____ fully explored.
questions.explanation: A noun is needed after 'Our', and 'yet to' takes the base form: 'Our country has so many … destinations … yet to be fully explored.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Expand
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'expand' is 'shrink'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I could make out from my son's voice that he was _____ as his exam did not go well.
questions.explanation: His exam had gone badly, so he sounded 'sad'; 'rejected' and 'abrogated' do not fit, and nothing points to confusion.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Once in a blue moon
questions.explanation: 'Once in a blue moon' means very rarely.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. She went on a quest for ancient things ___(1)____ could have a soul of their own, something ___(2)___ Aladdin's lamp that was home to a genie. She searched flea markets, met with art dealers and even went to excavation sites. She ___(3)__ searching for something that would have seen some ancient history when an ___(4)___, ___(5)___, ___(6)____ apothecary table caught her attention. It was perhaps owned by a __(7)____, ___(8)___, __(9)____ woman who was a wise medic but was deemed a witch.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'that', the usual relative pronoun for a clause defining things: 'ancient things that could have a soul of their own'. ('Which' is also used in such clauses, especially in British English; 'who' is for people and 'whose' is possessive.)

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. She went on a quest for ancient things ___(1)____ could have a soul of their own, something ___(2)___ Aladdin's lamp that was home to a genie. She searched flea markets, met with art dealers and even went to excavation sites. She ___(3)__ searching for something that would have seen some ancient history when an ___(4)___, ___(5)___, ___(6)____ apothecary table caught her attention. It was perhaps owned by a __(7)____, ___(8)___, __(9)____ woman who was a wise medic but was deemed a witch.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Something like Aladdin's lamp': 'like' means similar to.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. She went on a quest for ancient things ___(1)____ could have a soul of their own, something ___(2)___ Aladdin's lamp that was home to a genie. She searched flea markets, met with art dealers and even went to excavation sites. She ___(3)__ searching for something that would have seen some ancient history when an ___(4)___, ___(5)___, ___(6)____ apothecary table caught her attention. It was perhaps owned by a __(7)____, ___(8)___, __(9)____ woman who was a wise medic but was deemed a witch.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The past continuous fits an action under way when something else happened: 'She was searching … when an … apothecary table caught her attention.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. She went on a quest for ancient things ___(1)____ could have a soul of their own, something ___(2)___ Aladdin's lamp that was home to a genie. She searched flea markets, met with art dealers and even went to excavation sites. She ___(3)__ searching for something that would have seen some ancient history when an ___(4)___, ___(5)___, ___(6)____ apothecary table caught her attention. It was perhaps owned by a __(7)____, ___(8)___, __(9)____ woman who was a wise medic but was deemed a witch.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blanks numbered 4, 5 and 6 respectively.
questions.explanation: 'An' needs a word beginning with a vowel sound, so 'antique' comes first, and colour comes last, next to the noun: 'an antique, heavy, chestnut brown apothecary table'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. She went on a quest for ancient things ___(1)____ could have a soul of their own, something ___(2)___ Aladdin's lamp that was home to a genie. She searched flea markets, met with art dealers and even went to excavation sites. She ___(3)__ searching for something that would have seen some ancient history when an ___(4)___, ___(5)___, ___(6)____ apothecary table caught her attention. It was perhaps owned by a __(7)____, ___(8)___, __(9)____ woman who was a wise medic but was deemed a witch.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blanks numbered 7, 8 and 9 respectively.
questions.explanation: SSC's key follows the order that puts size, then shape or build, before age, as Cambridge's grammar does: 'a small, hunch-backed, old woman'. (Lists that put age before shape would give 'small, old, hunch-backed'.)

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The average weight of 12 students and two teachers is 55 kg. When one teacher weighing 68 kg is included in the group, then the average weight of the group (in kg) is:
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 56 kg, the option nearest the answer: the 14 weigh 14 × 55 = 770 kg, so with the 68 kg teacher the 15 average 838/15 ≈ 55.87 kg, or 56 to the nearest kg. (It is exactly 56 if the 55 kg average is of the 12 students alone: (12 × 55 + 68)/13 = 728/13 = 56.)

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹940 for 3 years at 5% per annum.
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 5% per year rate of interest for 2 years.

In a group of 260 people, one-fourth are women, two-fifth are men and the rest are children. The average age of women is five-sixth of the average age of men, average age of children is one-third of the average age of men. If the average age of men is 48 years, what is the average age of the group in years?
A man bought an article for ₹500 and sold it for ₹600. Find his profit percentage.
Aniruddh invested ₹15,000 in the shares of a company. The shares rose by 15% one day and fell by 10% on the other day. What is the current value (in ₹) of Aniruddh’s investment?
Find the ratio of the curved surface areas of two cones if the diameters of the bases are equal and slant heights are in the ratio 5 : 3.
questions.explanation: Curved surface area = πrl. Equal diameters mean equal radii, so the areas are in the ratio of the slant heights, 5 : 3.

questions.text: The difference between discounts on a bill for ₹22,500 under two schemes, a discount of 40% and two successive discounts of 36% and 4%, is:
questions.explanation: 40% of ₹22,500 = ₹9,000. Successive 36% and 4% leave 0.64 × 0.96 = 0.6144 of the bill, a discount of 22,500 × 0.3856 = ₹8,676. The difference is ₹324.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 6% per year rate of interest for 4 years.

Two classes took the same test. One class of 20 students made an average grade of 85%, the other class of 30 students made an average grade of 70%. The average grade for all students across both classes is:
A and B are running in the same direction at the speeds of 9km/h and 3km/h, respectively, on a circular track of length 27 km. They will meet again after:
questions.explanation: Running the same way, A gains 9 − 3 = 6 km/h on B. They meet again when A has gained one full lap: 27/6 = 4.5 hours.

questions.text: In the what ratio must a shopkeeper mix 2 types of rice worth ₹80/kg and ₹100/kg, so that the average cost of the mixture is ₹95/kg?
If the cost price of 30 books is same as the selling price of 20 books, then the gain percentage is:
questions.explanation: The selling price of 20 books is the cost of 30, so on 20 books the gain is the cost of 10: 10/20 × 100 = 50%.

questions.text: If 12 : x :: x : 27 and 25 : y :: y : 36, where x and y are both positive numbers, then find x : y.
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series based on the English alphabetical order? PAX, RCV, TET, VGR, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +2 (P, R, T, V, X), second letters +2 (A, C, E, G, I) and third letters −2 (X, V, T, R, P): XIP.

questions.text: This question has two statements followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the given statements. Statements: All bags are purses. No purse is a wallet. Conclusions (I) At least some wallets are purses. (II) No bag is a wallet.
questions.explanation: All bags are purses and no purse is a wallet, so no bag is a wallet (II). I contradicts 'No purse is a wallet'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘MONK’ is coded as ‘1238’ and ‘HONK’ is coded as ‘8326’. What is the code for ‘H’ in that language?
questions.explanation: O, N and K are in both words, as are 2, 3 and 8 in both codes. The letter left in HONK is H and the digit left in its code is 6, so H = 6.

questions.text: RZ31 is related to TB25 in a certain way. In the same way, JR46 is related to LT40. To which of the following is GO18 related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Both letters move 2 places forward and the number falls by 6: R → T, Z → B, 31 → 25 and J → L, R → T, 46 → 40. So GO18 → IQ12.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘÷’ and ‘+’ are interchanged and ‘−’ and ‘×’ are interchanged? 17 ÷ 27 × 7 − 9 + 3 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 17 + 27 − 7 × 9 ÷ 3 = 17 + 27 − 21 = 23.

questions.text: Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: All chocolates are juices. No juice is a biscuit. Conclusions: (I) No chocolate is a biscuit. (II) No biscuit is a juice.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: All chocolates are juices and no juice is a biscuit, so no chocolate is a biscuit (I). 'No juice is a biscuit' also means 'No biscuit is a juice' (II). Both follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'FOUR' is coded as '3157' and 'RENT' is coded as '2384'. What is the code for 'R' in the given code language?
questions.explanation: R is the only letter in both words and 3 the only digit in both codes, so R = 3.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). A is sitting third to the left of B. C is sitting second to the right of F. A is sitting to the immediate left of C. D is not an immediate neighbour of C. What is the position of B with respect to E?
questions.explanation: A is opposite B (third to the left at a table of six) and to C's immediate left, and F is second to C's left. D and E take the two seats beside B, and D cannot sit next to C, so going clockwise the order is C, A, F, D, B, E: B is to E's immediate right.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged and ‘−’ and ‘×’ are interchanged? 4 − 6 × 27 ÷ 72 + 6 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 4 × 6 − 27 + 72 ÷ 6 = 24 − 27 + 12 = 9.

questions.text: 43 is related to 87 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 63 is related to 127. To which of the following is 52 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is twice the first plus 1: 2 × 43 + 1 = 87 and 2 × 63 + 1 = 127. Likewise 2 × 52 + 1 = 105.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g., 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (8, 320, 4) (1, 70, 7)
questions.explanation: The middle number is ten times the product of the other two: 8 × 4 × 10 = 320 and 1 × 7 × 10 = 70. Likewise 2 × 2 × 10 = 40.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘she is intelligent’ is written as ‘le me re’ and ‘she is studious’ is written as ‘re de me’. How is ‘studious’ written in the given code language?
questions.explanation: 'she' and 'is' are in both sentences, as are 'me' and 're' in both codes. The word left in the second sentence is 'studious' and the code left is 'de'.

questions.text: Seven people P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). S is sitting third to the left of V. T is sitting second to the right of S. P is sitting fourth to the right of Q. U is sitting second to the left of P. What is the position of R with respect to T?
questions.explanation: Going clockwise (to each person's left) the order is V, T, P, S, U, R, Q: S is third to V's left, T second to S's right, and only this seat for P puts it fourth to Q's right with U second to its left. R is third to T's right.

questions.text: What should come in place of ‘?’ in the given series? 5040, 6064, 6576, 6832, 6960, ?
questions.explanation: The differences halve: 1,024, 512, 256, 128, so the next is 64: 6,960 + 64 = 7,024.

questions.text: The property of rock or soil that indicates the ability of allowing fluids to flow through it is called:
questions.explanation: Permeability is the ease with which water or other fluids pass through rock or soil.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution mentions that, “There shall be paid to the Judges of the Supreme Court, such salaries as may be determined by the Parliament by law, and until provision in that behalf is so made, such salaries as are specified in the Second Schedule”?
questions.explanation: Article 125 provides for the salaries of the Judges of the Supreme Court: as Parliament fixes by law, and until then as the Second Schedule specifies.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECT pair.
questions.explanation: The blossom shower, which makes coffee flowers bloom, falls in Kerala and nearby areas, not Andhra Pradesh. Nor'westers are West Bengal's Kalbaisakhi, Bardoisila is their name in Assam, and mango showers fall in Kerala and coastal Karnataka.

questions.text: In which state is the Jhumming cultivation known as Dahiya?
questions.explanation: NCERT lists 'Bewar' or 'Dahiya' as Madhya Pradesh's names for slash-and-burn cultivation, which is called jhumming in the north-east.

questions.text: Who among the following became the first Indian to win a gold medal at the World Athletics Championships event?
questions.explanation: Neeraj Chopra won the men's javelin at the 2023 World Athletics Championships in Budapest, India's first gold at the championships.

questions.text: Which food is a good source of complete protein?
questions.explanation: Egg protein contains all nine essential amino acids in good proportion, so it is a complete protein. Lentils are low in methionine and rice in lysine, and spinach has little protein.

questions.text: Gulbarga and Bidar style of architecture was patronised by which of the following dynasties?
questions.explanation: Gulbarga, and later Bidar, were the capitals of the Bahmani kingdom, whose rulers built the mosques, tombs and forts there.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Captain Hawkins visited India during the reign of:
questions.explanation: William Hawkins of the English East India Company reached Jahangir's court in 1609.

questions.text: Who is the writer of the novel ‘A Suitable Boy’?
questions.explanation: 'A Suitable Boy' (1993) is Vikram Seth's novel.

questions.text: The first ICC Women's T20 Cricket World Cup was hosted by ________.
questions.explanation: The first ICC Women's World Twenty20 was held in England in 2009, alongside the men's tournament.

questions.text: Darshana Jhaveri, a famous Manipuri dancer, was awarded the Padma Shri in which of the following years?
questions.explanation: Darshana Jhaveri, the youngest of the Jhaveri sisters, received the Padma Shri in 2002.

questions.text: Who was named as the president of Shiv Sena (Shinde Group) during the party's national executive meeting in Mumbai in February 2023?
questions.explanation: In February 2023, after the Election Commission recognised his faction as the Shiv Sena, the party's national executive in Mumbai named Eknath Shinde its chief leader. The other three belong to Uddhav Thackeray's faction.

questions.text: Kishori Amonkar, one of the finest classical singers of Hindustani music, was from which state?
questions.explanation: Kishori Amonkar, of the Jaipur-Atrauli gharana, was born in Bombay (Mumbai), Maharashtra.

questions.text: Which of the following initiatives of the Government of India promises 100 days of guaranteed wage employment to all the rural households who volunteer to do unskilled manual work?
options: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme
Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan
questions.explanation: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 guarantees every rural household that asks for unskilled manual work 100 days of wage employment a year.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was NOT associated with the ‘Prarthana Sabha’?
questions.explanation: The Prarthana Samaj was founded in Bombay in 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang, with M. G. Ranade and R. G. Bhandarkar among its leaders; Mahatma Gandhi had no part in it.

questions.text: The Maukharies ruled over ________ in western Uttar Pradesh, which later on replaced Pataliputra as the political centre of northern India.
questions.explanation: The Maukharis ruled from Kanauj, which in time replaced Pataliputra as the political centre of northern India.

questions.text: Which type of molecules show dipole-dipole interaction?
questions.explanation: Dipole-dipole forces act between molecules with permanent dipoles, such as HCl: the partly positive end of one attracts the partly negative end of another.

questions.text: In September 2023, which Chief Minister of an Indian state won the Lee Kuan Yew Exchange Fellowship for his distinguished contribution to public service?
questions.explanation: In September 2023 Singapore's Lee Kuan Yew Exchange Fellowship was conferred on Assam's Chief Minister, Himanta Biswa Sarma.

questions.text: Match list I of cell organelles with their functions in list II. List I: (a) Endoplasmic reticulum (b) Vacuoles (c) Golgi apparatus (d) Mitochondria List II: (i) for packaging of materials synthesised near the ER and dispatching them to various targets. (ii) generates ATP. (iii) are storage sacs for solid or liquid contents. (iv) serve as channels for the transport of proteins.
questions.explanation: The ER serves as channels for transporting proteins, vacuoles are storage sacs, the Golgi apparatus packages materials made near the ER and dispatches them, and mitochondria generate ATP.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith was founded by Shiv Prasad Gupta and Bhagwan Das in the year _______.
questions.explanation: Kashi Vidyapith in Varanasi was founded in 1921, during the Non-Cooperation Movement, and inaugurated by Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.text: From which of the following countries was the concept of the Fundamental Duties borrowed?
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Duties, added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, were inspired by the Constitution of the USSR (Russia).

questions.text: For how many days is the Chhat Puja celebrated?
questions.explanation: Chhath Puja lasts four days: Nahay Khay, Kharna, the evening offering to the setting sun and the morning offering to the rising sun.

questions.text: Air and National Defence are examples of which of the following goods?
questions.explanation: Public goods are non-rival and non-excludable: one person's use does not reduce another's and no one can be kept from using them, as with air and national defence.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following personalities said, “What I object to is the ‘craze’ for machinery as such. The craze is for what they call labour-saving machinery. Men go on ‘saving labour’ till thousands are without work and thrown to the open streets to die of starvation.”?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi said this in 1924: he objected not to machines as such but to labour-saving machinery that left thousands without work.

questions.text: 'Gaur Maria' dance is performed in which of the following state?
questions.explanation: Gaur Maria, the bison dance of the Bison Horn Maria of Bastar, belongs to Chhattisgarh.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase. Something that has the quality of being easily broken
questions.explanation: Something 'brittle' is hard but breaks easily.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. I heard management is planning to transfer me to another department and demote me. I need to confirm if this is true by hearing it “directly from the person involved” and from my manager.
questions.explanation: To hear something 'straight from the horse's mouth' is to hear it from the person directly involved.

questions.text: Select the word that is OPPOSITE in meaning to the underlined word in the given sentence. The name should also be “beneficial” to a strong, long-lasting marketing campaign.
questions.explanation: 'Beneficial' means helpful; its opposite is 'detrimental', harmful.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. Although she is “virtuous” in her deeds, people misinterpret her because of her open and bold nature.
questions.explanation: 'Virtuous' means morally good; its opposite is 'wicked'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'conceive': 'e' before 'i' after 'c'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. There has been / an increase of the number / of road / accidents recently.
questions.explanation: A rise is an 'increase in' something: 'an increase in the number of road accidents'.

questions.text: Select the option that has used the correct tense.
options: Yesterday, we was painting the door when a neighbour stopping by to say hello.
Yesterday, we will be painting the door when a neighbour stops by to say hello.
Yesterday, we are painting the door when a neighbour stop by to say hello.
Yesterday, we were painting the door when a neighbour stopped by to say hello.
questions.explanation: An action in progress in the past takes the past continuous, 'we were painting', and the action that interrupted it the simple past, 'stopped by'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I checked the ____________ to see if it will rain or not.
questions.explanation: Rain is a matter of the 'weather'; 'whether' introduces a choice.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He was constantly / gazing on the / crime scene to / find some clues.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives this segment: the usual preposition after 'gaze' is 'at', 'gazing at the crime scene'. 'Gaze on' or 'upon' is also found, mostly in literary writing, but the other three segments have no error.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The coaches decided to _____ the regulations more strictly because the candidates were not paying attention during their training sessions.
questions.explanation: Rules are 'enforced': the coaches decided to apply them more strictly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I have a __________ for reading and want to become a writer when I grow up.
questions.explanation: A strong love of something is 'a passion for' it: 'a passion for reading'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. Solving the riddle given by our teacher is “farther” beyond our capacity.
questions.explanation: 'Far' as an adverb means 'by a great amount': 'far beyond our capacity'. 'Farther' compares distances.

questions.text: Select the correct idiom to substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence. Sean is notorious for “revealing the secrets” about the company.
questions.explanation: To 'spill the beans' is to reveal secret information.

questions.text: Rectify the sentence by selecting the correct spelling of the underlined word from the options. He was startled by the loud “thander” during the storm.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'thunder'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can replace the underlined segment in the given sentence. No sooner had they left “their home that it started” raining heavily.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner' is followed by 'than', not 'that', and the past 'started' matches 'had left': 'No sooner had they left their home than it started raining heavily.'

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the error in the usage of the future tense in the given sentence. Shivani go to school tomorrow for prize distribution.
options: Shivani will go to school tomorrow for prize distribution.
Shivani has gone to school tomorrow for prize distribution.
Shivani goes to school tomorrow for prize distribution.
Shivani had gone to school tomorrow for prize distribution.
questions.explanation: The question asks for the future tense: 'Shivani will go to school tomorrow'. 'Goes' is the simple present, and 'has gone' and 'had gone' cannot refer to tomorrow.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Osmium is “heavy” metal in the periodic table.
questions.explanation: Compared with every other metal, osmium needs the superlative with 'the': 'the heaviest metal'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word from the options to fill in the blank. Adithya ordered a juicy _________________ cooked to perfection at the highway restaurant.
questions.explanation: A 'steak' is a thick slice of meat; 'stake' (a post, or a share) only sounds the same.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Excessive
questions.explanation: 'Excessive' means more than is reasonable; its opposite is 'moderate'. 'Inordinate' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error. The scientist made an “appauling” discovery about the environmental impact of the drug.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'appalling', with a double 'p' and a double 'l'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It was just before noon on June 26, 1975, and my friend and I were out exploring the bustling by-lanes of Delhi’s Karol Bagh, unaware that the Emergency had been declared, and that it would change our lives in ways we could have never ___1___. Though Indira Gandhi had herself announced the Emergency in a national broadcast at 8 am, IST, the news took its own time to reach the common people who went about their business as always. However, two hours into our outing, we ___2___ something was wrong. The pavement shops began to thin out as we watched and the bigger outlets too looked ready to ___3___; many of them worked behind half-downed shutters. We were young but fancied ourselves as political animals, which at the time was shorthand for being passionately anti-Congress and anti-Indira. There was no way we were going to head home without knowing what had happened. There was already considerable excitement in our small friends’ circle over two ___4___ developments: the June 12, 1975 Allahabad high court ruling unseating Indira for electoral malpractices and the Congress’s unexpected defeat in the State election in Gujarat. The Supreme Court had allowed Indira to continue as prime minister but that did not ___5___ our joy; it was a technical reprieve that did not lessen the political blow she had received.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The Emergency changed their lives in ways they could never have 'imagined'.
