questions.explanation: The court ruling and the election defeat were 'landmark' developments: events of great importance.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It was just before noon on June 26, 1975, and my friend and I were out exploring the bustling by-lanes of Delhi’s Karol Bagh, unaware that the Emergency had been declared, and that it would change our lives in ways we could have never ___1___. Though Indira Gandhi had herself announced the Emergency in a national broadcast at 8 am, IST, the news took its own time to reach the common people who went about their business as always. However, two hours into our outing, we ___2___ something was wrong. The pavement shops began to thin out as we watched and the bigger outlets too looked ready to ___3___; many of them worked behind half-downed shutters. We were young but fancied ourselves as political animals, which at the time was shorthand for being passionately anti-Congress and anti-Indira. There was no way we were going to head home without knowing what had happened. There was already considerable excitement in our small friends’ circle over two ___4___ developments: the June 12, 1975 Allahabad high court ruling unseating Indira for electoral malpractices and the Congress’s unexpected defeat in the State election in Gujarat. The Supreme Court had allowed Indira to continue as prime minister but that did not ___5___ our joy; it was a technical reprieve that did not lessen the political blow she had received.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court's technical reprieve did not 'dampen', or lessen, their joy.

questions.text: Lokesh received an amount of ₹10,500 in 5 years, including simple interest, on a principal amount of ₹7,500. What would be the total amount he receives if the interest rate is increased by 4%?
If the height of a triangle is increased by 20% and the base is increased by 12%. What is the new area (in cm²) if the old area of the triangle was 200 cm²?
questions.explanation: Area is half the base times the height, so it is multiplied by 1.2 × 1.12 = 1.344: 200 × 1.344 = 268.8 cm².

questions.text: An item is listed for ₹450 with 15% trade discount. Find the amount of trade discount.
questions.explanation: Trade discount = 15% of ₹450 = ₹67.50.

questions.text: The management batch of a college has two sections, A and B. Section A has 22 students and their average marks are 75, whereas section B has 30 students and their average marks are 60. What are the average marks of the whole batch? (Round off to two decimal places)
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
A solid cylinder has a total surface area of 352 cm². Its curved surface area is one-eighth of the total surface area. The radius (in cm) of the cylinder is: [Use π = 22/7]
questions.explanation: The curved surface is 352/8 = 44 cm², so the two ends take 352 − 44 = 308 cm²: 2πr² = 308, πr² = 154 and r² = 49 (π = 22/7), so r = 7 cm.

questions.text: 24 boys and a certain number of girls appeared for an exam. The average score of the boys was 42 and the average score of the girls was 34, while the combined average score was 38. How many girls appeared for the exam?
Find the least number which when divided by 20,25,35 and 40 leaves remainders 14,19,29and 34, respectively.
questions.explanation: Each remainder is 6 less than its divisor (20 − 14 = 25 − 19 = 35 − 29 = 40 − 34 = 6), so the number is LCM(20, 25, 35, 40) − 6 = 1400 − 6 = 1394.

questions.text: What should be subtracted from 30, 56, 40 and 76 so that the remaining numbers may be proportional?
questions.explanation: Subtracting 4 leaves 26, 52, 36 and 72, and 26 : 52 = 36 : 72 = 1 : 2.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 2 years.
The average of 17 results is 62. The average of the first eighth is 48 and that of the last eighth is 84, the ninth result is:
questions.explanation: The total is 17 × 62 = 1054. The first eight total 8 × 48 = 384 and the last eight 8 × 84 = 672, so the ninth is 1054 − 384 − 672 = −2.

questions.text: The cost price of 12 bananas is equal to the sale price of 10 bananas. What is the percentage of profit?
questions.explanation: Selling 10 bananas brings in the cost of 12: a profit of 2 on a cost of 10, or 20%.

questions.text: In a jeep driving at a speed of 9 m/s, a thief is fleeing on a straight road. He is being pursued by a police officer riding a motorbike at a speed of 10 m/s. How long would it take a police officer to apprehend the burglar if there is a 100 m instantaneous distance between the vehicle and the motorbike?
questions.explanation: The motorbike gains 10 − 9 = 1 m/s on the jeep, so it closes the 100 m in 100 seconds.

questions.text: In an examination, there are four subjects of 100 marks each. A student scores 78% in the first subject, 75% in the second subject and 90% in the third subject. She scored 85% in aggregate. Her percentage of marks in the fourth subject is:
questions.explanation: 85% of 400 is 340 marks in all. 78 + 75 + 90 = 243, so the fourth subject gives 340 − 243 = 97 marks out of 100: 97%.

questions.text: A train travels at a speed of 120 km/h. How many metres will it travel in 60 minutes?
questions.explanation: 60 minutes is 1 hour, so the train covers 120 km = 120000 m.

questions.text: Rajneesh drove his car at a speed of 99 km/h for 2 hours and then he took a rest for one hour. Then, he further drove for 3 hours at a speed of 60 km/h. What was Rajneesh’s average speed (in km/h) during his entire journey?
questions.explanation: Distance = 99 × 2 + 60 × 3 = 198 + 180 = 378 km. The time, rest included, is 2 + 1 + 3 = 6 hours: 378/6 = 63 km/h.

questions.text: LIFE is related to NKHG in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, SLOPE is related to UNQRG. To which of the following is DUAL related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: L → N, I → K, F → H, E → G. So D → F, U → W, A → C, L → N: FWCN.

questions.text: 394 is related to 242 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 461 is related to 309. To which of the following is 428 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is 152 less than the first: 394 − 152 = 242 and 461 − 152 = 309. Likewise 428 − 152 = 276.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'JARS' is coded as '3175' and 'SIDE' is coded as '4832'. What is the code for 'S' in the given code language?
questions.explanation: S is the only letter in both words and 3 the only digit in both codes, so S = 3.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘bring cold water’ is coded as ‘qh pw ut’ and ‘water is pure’ iscoded as ‘mk zv qh’. How is ‘water’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'water' is the only word in both sentences and 'qh' the only code in both, so water = qh.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). C is sitting second to the left of A. Only one person is sitting between B and C when counted from right of B. E is sitting third to the right of F. D is sitting to the immediate left of E. The position of how many persons excluding A will remain unchanged if all the persons are arranged in the English alphabetical order in clockwise direction, starting from A, keeping the position of A unchanged?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, each person's left is clockwise. Clockwise from A the seats are A, F, C, G, B, E, D, which fits every clue (C second to A's left, one person between B and C counting from B's right, E third to F's right, D to E's immediate left). In alphabetical order clockwise from A they would hold A, B, C, D, E, F, G, so only C keeps its place.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘POT’ is coded as ’15-14-19’ and ‘SPLIT’ is coded as ’18-15-11-8-19’. What is the code for ‘PERFORM’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is coded as its place in the alphabet minus 1: P (16) → 15, O (15) → 14, T (20) → 19. So PERFORM → 15-4-17-5-14-17-12.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? BFL, HLR, NRX, TXD, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 6 places forward from one cluster to the next, wrapping round after Z: T → Z, X → D, D → J: ZDJ.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 60 × 12 − 6 ÷ 4 + 15 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 60 ÷ 12 + 6 × 4 − 15 = 5 + 24 − 15 = 14.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘WILD’ is coded as ‘3197’ and ‘LOVE’ is coded as ‘2346’. What is the code for ‘L’ in that language?
questions.explanation: L is the only letter in both words and 3 the only digit in both codes, so L = 3.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘−’ and ‘+’ are interchanged and ‘÷’ and ‘×’ are interchanged? 13 ÷ 4 + 16 × 2 − 21 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 13 × 4 − 16 ÷ 2 + 21 = 52 − 8 + 21 = 65.

questions.text: This question has two statements followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the given statements. Statements: Some hoops are cows. All cows are bulls. Conclusions: (I) Some bulls are hoops. (II) Some hoops are bulls.
questions.explanation: The hoops that are cows are also bulls, so some hoops are bulls (II), and so some bulls are hoops (I). Both follow.

questions.text: 13 is related to 104 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 17 is related to 136. To which ofthe following is 23 related, following the same logic?(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The second number is 8 times the first: 13 × 8 = 104 and 17 × 8 = 136. Likewise 23 × 8 = 184.

questions.text: P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). T sits to the immediate right of V. S sits second to the right of Q. U is an immediate neighbour of both V and S. P sits second to the left of U. Who is sitting to the immediate left of R?
questions.explanation: Going round the table to each person's left from U: U, S, P, Q, R, T, V. Then T is to V's immediate right, S second to Q's right, U between V and S and P second to U's left; T sits to R's immediate left.

questions.text: HP21 is related to XF34 in a certain way. In the same way, KS72 is related to AI85. To which of the following is NV39 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 16 places forward (wrapping round after Z) and the number rises by 13: H → X, P → F, 21 → 34; K → A, S → I, 72 → 85. So N → D, V → L and 39 → 52: DL52.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 3 16 66 201 406 ?

Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statement(s) is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: No chair is a recliner. No recliner is a sofa. No recliner is a mat. Conclusions: (I) No chair is a sofa. (II) Some mats are sofa.
questions.explanation: The statements only keep chairs, sofas and mats apart from recliners; they say nothing about how chairs, sofas and mats relate to one another. So neither conclusion follows.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Shuddhi Movement to reconvert to the Hindu fold the converts to other religions, was started by which of the following organisations?
questions.explanation: The Arya Samaj, founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875, ran the Shuddhi movement to bring converts back into the Hindu fold.

questions.text: Who is the author of ‘Temple Tales: Secrets & Stories of India’s Sacred Places’?
questions.explanation: 'Temple Tales: Secrets and Stories from India's Sacred Places' (2019), a book for children, is by the journalist Sudha G. Tilak.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the book named 'Streepurushtulna'?
questions.explanation: Tarabai Shinde wrote 'Stree Purush Tulana' (1882), a sharp critique of how society treated women.

questions.text: From which of the following countries has the Indian Constitution borrowed the procedure of making amendments in the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The procedure for amending the Constitution, like the election of members of the Rajya Sabha, was borrowed from the Constitution of South Africa.

questions.text: Which of the following was NOT found in the Harappan excavation sites?
questions.explanation: Harappan sites have yielded dwelling houses, public buildings such as granaries, and the Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro, but no public hospital.

questions.text: The Constitution of India has borrowed many provisions from different countries as well as from the Government of India Act of ___________.
questions.explanation: Much of the Constitution, including the federal scheme, the office of Governor, the Public Service Commissions and the emergency provisions, came from the Government of India Act, 1935.

questions.text: Which of the following Union Territories has the lowest population as per the Census of India 2011?
questions.explanation: Lakshadweep, with 64,473 people in 2011, is the least populous Union Territory.

questions.text: Squash player Anahat Singh belongs to which city in India?
questions.explanation: Anahat Singh, born in 2008, is a squash player from Delhi; she was the youngest member of India's team at the 2022 Commonwealth Games.

questions.text: Which of the following is considered unicellular green algae?
questions.explanation: Chlamydomonas is a single-celled green alga that swims with two flagella. Cladophora and Oedogonium are many-celled filaments, and Chlorophyta is the name of the whole green-algae group.

questions.text: The structure of methanol is CH₃OH. This kind of representation is known as _________.
questions.explanation: A condensed structural formula writes each carbon with its attached atoms in a row, as in CH₃OH, instead of drawing every bond.

questions.text: Which of the following pollutants is responsible for the acidification of ocean?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide absorbed by sea water forms carbonic acid, which lowers the ocean's pH.

questions.text: The Integrated Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Bill, 2023 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 11 August 2023, which amends the ________________________.
options: Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) Act, 2015
Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) Act, 2016
Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) Act, 2017
Integrated Goods and Services Tax (IGST) Act, 2014
questions.explanation: The Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act dates from 2017, when GST began; the 2023 Bill amended it to tax online gaming supplied from outside India.

questions.text: Which raga was composed by music emperor Mian Tansen to bring rain?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Megh Malhar. Ragas of the Malhar family are sung in the monsoon and said to bring rain, and tradition credits Tansen with one of them, Miyan ki Malhar; of the options only Megh Malhar is a Malhar raga.

questions.text: Muscle cells and muscle fibres are developed from embryonic precursor cells known as:
questions.explanation: Myoblasts are embryonic precursor cells that fuse to form the long, many-nucleated fibres of skeletal muscle.

questions.text: VP Dhananjayan and Shanta Dhananjayan were honoured with Rukminidevi Memorial Award in 2009 for which of the following Indian classical dance forms?
questions.explanation: V.P. and Shanta Dhananjayan, who trained under Rukmini Devi Arundale at Kalakshetra, are Bharatanatyam dancers and teachers.

questions.text: Which of the following temples is NOT an example of Nagara style of architecture?
questions.explanation: The Kailasanatha temple at Kanchipuram, built by the Pallavas, is in the southern Dravida style. The Konark Sun temple, the Lingaraja temple and Khajuraho's Kandariya Mahadeva temple are Nagara temples.

questions.text: Which of the following is the headquarter of East Central Railway?
questions.explanation: East Central Railway has its headquarters at Hajipur in Bihar.

questions.text: Lachhu Maharaj has been associated with which dance form?
questions.explanation: Pandit Lachhu Maharaj, of the Lucknow gharana, was a Kathak dancer who also choreographed Hindi films.

questions.text: In September 2023, at the BRICS Innovation Forum in Moscow, who among the following, who is a Chief Innovation Officer from Telangana, received the World Innovation Award?
questions.explanation: Shanta Thoutam, Telangana's Chief Innovation Officer, received the World Innovation Award at the first BRICS Innovation Forum in Moscow, for her contribution to Sustainable Development Goal 4 (quality education).

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a religious festival?
questions.explanation: Gandhi Jayanti, on 2 October, is a national holiday marking Mahatma Gandhi's birth. Good Friday, Guru Purab and Muharram are Christian, Sikh and Islamic observances.

questions.text: According to the Census of India 2001, how much percentage of the immigrant population was from Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 2.9%. The 2001 Census recorded more than 5 million immigrants, 96 per cent of them from neighbouring countries, chiefly Bangladesh (3.0 million), Pakistan (0.9 million) and Nepal (0.5 million).

questions.text: To which state does Indian shooter Abhinav Bindra belong?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Uttarakhand: Abhinav Bindra, India's first individual Olympic gold medallist (10 m air rifle, Beijing 2008), was born in Dehradun. His family is Punjabi, so Punjab is also arguable.

questions.text: According to Koeppen’s Scheme of climatic regions of India, in which of the following states is the ‘BWhw’ and ‘BShw’ type climate found?
questions.explanation: Both are found in Rajasthan: BWhw (hot desert) in its far west, and BShw (semi-arid steppe) in parts of western Rajasthan, as well as north-western Gujarat and Punjab.

questions.text: Dhamma is the __________ word for the Sanskrit word ‘Dharma’.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Prakrit: 'dhamma' is the Prakrit form of Sanskrit 'dharma', the word Ashoka used in his inscriptions. Pali, the language of the Buddhist canon, is itself a Prakrit and also uses 'dhamma', so 'Pali' is arguable too.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Rahul speaks fluently English / although he makes / quite a lot of mistakes /while writing.
questions.explanation: The adverb follows the object, not the verb: 'Rahul speaks English fluently'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person or entity that is unable to pay debts.
questions.explanation: An 'insolvent' person or firm cannot pay its debts. A recluse lives apart from others, and an insurgent rebels against authority.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank and make the sentence meaningful. Sheetal has been studying engineering for five years, ____________________ countless hours to her coursework.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'dedicating'.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the underlined spelling error. The impacts of climate change on different sectors of society are “interelated”.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'interrelated', with a double 'r'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. His dog did not _________ when thieves were slashing the _________ of his precious tree.
questions.explanation: 'Bark' fits both blanks: a dog barks, and bark is a tree's outer covering.

questions.text: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
options: I wish I had eraser to erase all the mistakes in my life.
A young boy offered her his seat.
I have a lot of work to complete.
This is a very difficult task to accomplish.
questions.explanation: 'Eraser' is a countable noun and needs an article: 'I wish I had an eraser'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. We / enjoyed lunch / he gave / us.
questions.explanation: The lunch is a particular one, the one he gave, so it needs 'the': 'We enjoyed the lunch he gave us.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. If you don’t have a lump sum to ______ in a fixed deposit, you can surely opt for a long-term recurring deposit.
questions.explanation: One 'invests' a lump sum in a fixed deposit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. The meteorological department predicted “heavy” rain over the coming days.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'heavy' rain is 'light' rain.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. As the orchestra played, the audience was “mesmerised” by the beautiful melodies.
questions.explanation: 'Mesmerised' means held spellbound, with all attention on the music; 'abstracted' means inattentive, with the mind elsewhere.

questions.text: Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence to make it grammatically correct. Only “the beautiful” painting is to be displayed in the exhibition.
questions.explanation: 'Only' picks out one painting from all the rest, so the superlative is needed: 'Only the most beautiful painting is to be displayed'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Please bring two bananas and the piece of cake from the market.
questions.explanation: Any piece of cake will do, so the indefinite article is needed: 'and a piece of cake'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He couldn't attend the meeting _________ he was sick.
questions.explanation: Being sick is the reason he missed the meeting, so 'because'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Green thumb
questions.explanation: Someone with a 'green thumb' is good at growing plants.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Fatigued
questions.explanation: 'Fatigued' means very tired.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Proficient
questions.explanation: 'Proficient' means skilled and competent: 'accomplished'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence. His performace in the play was outstanding.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'performance'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. Despite their differences, the counties found common ground and “buried the hatchet”.
options: To seek revenge in the future
questions.explanation: To 'bury the hatchet' is to end a quarrel and make peace.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Exactly the same words as were used originally.
questions.explanation: 'Verbatim' means in exactly the same words as the original.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Sniffer dog Tucker uses (1)________ nose to help researchers find out why a killer whale population off the northwest coast of the United States is (2)________ the decline. He searches for whale faeces floating on the surface of the water, which are then collected for examination. He is one of the elite team members of detection dogs used by scientists studying a (3)________ of species including right whales and killer whales. Conservation canines are fast becoming indispensable tools for biologists according to Aimee Hurt, associate director and co-founder of Working Dogs for Conservation, (4)________ in Three Forks, Montana. Over the last few years, though, so many new conservation dog projects have sprung up that Hurt can no (5)________ keep track of them all. Her organisation’s dogs and their handlers are fully booked to assist field researchers into 2012.

questions.text: A person sees another person snatching a chain from a lady, at a distance of 300 metres. He starts running and catches the thief by running at 10 km/h after running a total distance of 1.5 km. The speed at which the thief was running was:
questions.explanation: While the man runs 1.5 km at 10 km/h (0.15 hours), the thief, 300 m ahead, runs 1.5 − 0.3 = 1.2 km. 1.2 ÷ 0.15 = 8 km/h.

questions.text: The greatest possible length of a scale that can exactly measure a cloth of lengths 250 cm, 420 cm and 710 cm is:
questions.explanation: The longest scale is the HCF of the lengths: 250 = 2 × 5³, 420 = 2² × 3 × 5 × 7 and 710 = 2 × 5 × 71, so the HCF is 2 × 5 = 10 cm.

questions.text: The average age of 14 students and their teacher is 18 years. If the teacher's age is excluded, the average reduces by 1 year. What is the teacher's age?
questions.explanation: All 15 together total 15 × 18 = 270 years and the 14 students 14 × 17 = 238 years. The teacher is 270 − 238 = 32.

questions.text: A wholesale dealer announced during the festival season that they are offering 'buy 4 shirts, get one free', then find the net discount percentage given by the dealer.
questions.explanation: The buyer gets 5 shirts for the price of 4, so 1 shirt in 5 is free: a discount of 1/5 = 20%.

questions.text: An investment grows by 15% in the first month, 20% in the second month, and then decreases by 10% in the third month. If the initial investment was ₹5000, then the final amount (in ₹) is:
A runner runs 300 metres race in 36 seconds. The runner’s speed in km/h is:
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 8% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
If the average marks of three batches of 40, 50 and 60 students, respectively, is 50, 60 and 75, then the average marks of all the students is:

In an amusement park, all rides are equally priced, and the entry ticket for the park costs an additional ₹180. Rohan had 15 rides and paid a total of ₹1,380 for his visit to the park. How much (in ₹) in all would Rohan have to pay for his visit to the amusement park if he had opted for 20 rides?
questions.explanation: Without the ₹180 entry ticket, 15 rides cost ₹1,200, so ₹80 a ride. With 20 rides: 20 × 80 + 180 = ₹1,780.

questions.text: Vipul, Ashima, and Priya invested a total of ₹21,000 at 3%, 6%, and 5% per annum, respectively, on simple interest. If at the end of the year, all three persons received an equal amount of interest, then the amount (in ₹) invested by Ashima is:
questions.explanation: If each earns interest I, the sums are I/0.03 + I/0.06 + I/0.05 = 70I = 21,000, so I = ₹300. Ashima's sum = 300/0.06 = ₹5,000.

questions.text: The cost price of 25 balls is the same as the selling price of 20 balls. Find the profit percentage.
questions.explanation: The selling price of 20 balls buys 25, so the profit on 20 balls is the cost of 5: 5/20 × 100 = 25%.

questions.text: The batting average of a cricket player for 40 innings is 60 runs. His highest score in an innings exceeds his lowest score by 110 runs. If these two innings are excluded, the average score of the remaining 38 innings is 58 runs. Find his highest score.
questions.explanation: The 40 innings total 40 × 60 = 2,400 and the other 38 total 38 × 58 = 2,204, so highest + lowest = 196. With highest − lowest = 110, the highest is (196 + 110)/2 = 153.

questions.text: If the diagonal of a rectangle is 16 cm long and its perimeter is 48 cm long, find the area of the rectangle.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 160 cm², from the usual working: l + b = 24 and l² + b² = 16² = 256, so 2lb = 24² − 256 = 320 and lb = 160. Strictly, no rectangle has these measurements: a 16 cm diagonal allows a perimeter of at most 32√2 ≈ 45.3 cm, and (l − b)² = 256 − 320 would be negative.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 3 years.

4 is related to 32 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 11 is related to 88. To which of the following is 6 related, following the same logic? (Note: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 - Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 8: 4 × 8 = 32 and 11 × 8 = 88. So 6 × 8 = 48.

questions.text: VOJP is related to SLGM in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, XQLR is related to UNIO. To which of the following is ZSNT related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back: V → S, O → L, J → G, P → M. So Z → W, S → P, N → K and T → Q: WPKQ.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No book is a copy. All stones are books. Conclusions: (I) No copy is a stone. (II) All books are stones.
questions.explanation: No book is a copy and every stone is a book, so no stone is a copy and no copy is a stone (I). All stones are books, but not every book need be a stone, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only three people are sitting between C and G when counted from the right of C. E is sitting third to the left of G. Exactly one person is sitting between E and F when counted from the left of E. D is sitting to the immediate left of B. How many people are sitting between A and D when counted from the left of A?
questions.explanation: G is fourth to the right of C, E third to the left of G and F second to the left of E, with C between them; D, immediately left of B, and A fill the other seats. Going left (clockwise) from C the order is C, F, A, G, B, D, E, so from A's left G and B sit before D: two people.

questions.text: M, N, O, P, Q, R and S are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Q is an immediate neighbour of both R and P. M sits second to the left of R. O sits second to the left of M. S is not an immediate neighbour of O. The position of how many persons will remain unchanged if all persons are arranged in alphabetical order in a clockwise direction starting from ‘M’?
questions.explanation: M is second to the left of R and O second to the left of M. Q cannot sit on R's left (P would need M's seat), so Q is on R's right with P beyond it; S, not next to O, takes the seat on R's left, and N the seat between M and O. Clockwise the order is already M, N, O, P, Q, R, S, so all seven keep their places.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series based on the English alphabetical order? YDY, WGT ,UJO ,SMJ, ?
questions.explanation: First letters go back 2 (Y, W, U, S, Q), second letters forward 3 (D, G, J, M, P) and third letters back 5 (Y, T, O, J, E): QPE.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘MANAGE’ is coded as ‘IKEREQ’ and ‘RACE’ is coded as ‘IGEV’. What is the code for ‘SYMPHONY’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and each letter moved 4 places forward: MANAGE → EGANAM → IKEREQ and RACE → ECAR → IGEV. SYMPHONY → YNOHPMYS → CRSLTQCW.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 647 614 581 548 515 ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 33 less than the one before: 515 − 33 = 482.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (9, 63, 7) (27, 189, 21)
questions.explanation: The middle number is 7 times the first and 9 times the third: 9 × 7 = 63 = 7 × 9 and 27 × 7 = 189 = 21 × 9. Likewise 45 × 7 = 315 = 35 × 9.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? (15 ÷ 3)× 11 + 48 −21 × 2 + 8 = 57 (Note: Interchange should be done of the entire number and not individual digits of a given number.)
In a code language, 'HWCY' is coded as ‘KBJH’ and 'REPU' is coded as ‘UJWD’. How will 'AXMQ' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move forward 3, 5, 7 and 9 places, wrapping round after Z: HWCY → KBJH and REPU → UJWD. So AXMQ → DCTZ.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 18 ÷ 5 + 8 × 4 − 3 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 18 × 5 − 8 ÷ 4 + 3 = 90 − 2 + 3 = 91.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘DONE’ is coded as ‘7139’ and ‘TERM’ is coded as ‘6874’.What is the code for ‘E’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: E is the only letter in both words and 7 the only digit in both codes, so E = 7.

questions.text: Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: Some branches are leaves. Some leaves are cables. Conclusions: (I) Atleast some cables are branches. (II) Some cables are leaves.
questions.explanation: Some leaves are cables, so some cables are leaves (II). Branches and cables are linked only through leaves, which may be different ones, so I does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'CAREER' is coded as ‘EBTFGS’ and 'CARING' is coded as ‘EBTJPH’. How will 'CENTER' be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: The letters move forward 2 and 1 places alternately: CAREER → EBTFGS and CARING → EBTJPH. So CENTER → EFPUGS.

questions.text: FD7 is related to KI12 in a certain way. In the same way, PN18 is related to US23. To which of the following is AY21 related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 5 places forward (Y wraps round to D) and the number rises by 5: FD7 → KI12 and PN18 → US23. So AY21 → FD26.

questions.text: The last Chalukyan King, defeated by the Rashtrakuta King Dantidurga, was ___________________.
questions.explanation: Dantidurga overthrew Kirtivarman II, the last Chalukya king of Badami, in the mid-eighth century and founded the Rashtrakuta empire.

questions.text: A disease like COVID-19 is a kind of:
questions.explanation: COVID-19 is caused by a coronavirus believed to have passed to humans from animals, which makes it a zoonotic disease.

questions.text: Who among the following is the dance guru from Odisha credited with having revived the Odissi dance form?
questions.explanation: Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra led the twentieth-century revival of Odissi. Birju Maharaj was a Kathak master.

questions.text: As per Census 2011, which of the following states has the highest percentage of Buddhist population in India?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 census Buddhists were about 27% of Sikkim's population, the highest share of any state.

questions.text: Which of the following harvest and cultural festivals is celebrated by the Tamil community every year in January?
questions.explanation: Pongal, the Tamil harvest festival, falls in mid-January at the start of the Tamil month of Thai. Vishu is Kerala's new year and Theyyam a ritual dance of Kerala.

questions.text: In 2023, which repository is proposed to be set up in a digital epigraphy museum, with digitisation of one lakh ancient inscriptions in the first stage?
questions.explanation: The Union Budget 2023-24 announced a 'Bharat Shared Repository of Inscriptions' in a digital epigraphy museum, with one lakh ancient inscriptions digitised in the first stage.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In 1836, _______ became the Governor General of India.
questions.explanation: George Eden, Lord Auckland (later Earl of Auckland), was Governor-General from 1836 to 1842; the First Anglo-Afghan War began during his term.

questions.text: In which year was the first Senior Women's National Football Championship held in India?
questions.explanation: By the All India Football Federation's account, the first edition of the championship was held in Manipur in 1992 (the 1991-92 season).

questions.text: The GV Raja Memorial Trophy, Sir Ashutosh Mukherjee Trophy and Santosh Trophy are related to which of the following sports in India?
questions.explanation: The Santosh Trophy is India's national football championship for state teams; SSC's key places the GV Raja Memorial and Sir Ashutosh Mukherjee trophies in football as well.

questions.text: In February 2023, who was appointed as the new Governor of Himachal Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Shiv Pratap Shukla was appointed Governor of Himachal Pradesh in February 2023.

questions.text: The temperature of −273.15°C is called _________.
questions.explanation: −273.15 °C is 0 K, absolute zero, the lowest temperature possible.

questions.text: As per Article 163 of the Constitution of India, any advice tendered by Ministers to the ________ shall not be inquired into in any court.
questions.explanation: Article 163(3): whether, and what, advice was tendered by Ministers to the Governor shall not be inquired into in any court. Article 74(2) says the same of advice to the President.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who is properly known as the ‘Grand Old Lady’ of the Independence Movement?
questions.explanation: Aruna Asaf Ali, who hoisted the Congress flag at Gowalia Tank in Bombay at the start of the Quit India Movement in 1942, is remembered as the 'Grand Old Lady' of the Independence Movement.

questions.text: Which of the following river valleys is NOT known for coal deposits in India?
questions.explanation: India's Gondwana coal lies in the valleys of the Damodar, Son, Mahanadi, Godavari and Wardha; the Satluj valley has no coal deposits of note.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following cities was the first successful textile mill established in India in the year 1854?
questions.explanation: C. N. Davar's Bombay Spinning and Weaving Company, started in Bombay in 1854, was India's first successful cotton textile mill.

questions.text: The Directive Principles of State Policy are influenced by which of the following?
questions.explanation: Several Directive Principles carry Gandhian ideals: village panchayats (Article 40), cottage industries (Article 43), prohibition (Article 47) and cow protection (Article 48). The idea of Directive Principles itself came from the Irish Constitution.

questions.text: The amount of dissolved oxygen in water becomes lowest at what time of the day?
questions.explanation: Through the night plants and animals in the water use up oxygen in respiration with no photosynthesis to replace it, so dissolved oxygen is lowest around dawn.

questions.text: Chitti Babu is a famous player of which of the following musical instruments?
questions.explanation: Chitti Babu was a celebrated Carnatic veena player.

questions.text: Which of the following awards was conferred upon the Chhau dancer Siba Prasad Das in 2022?
questions.explanation: Siba Prasad Das, a Chhau dancer from Odisha, was among the artists named for the Sangeet Natak Akademi Amrit Award in 2022, a one-time honour for artists over 75 who had received no national honour.

questions.text: Which of the following microfinance units were established in India at the time of independence?
questions.explanation: Rural cooperative credit societies date back to the Co-operative Credit Societies Act of 1904. Self Help Groups (linked to banks from 1992), Grameen-model banks and Joint Liability Groups all came later.

questions.text: The Early Vedic economy was primarily based on_________ activity.
questions.explanation: The Rig Vedic people were mainly pastoral, with cattle as their chief wealth; agriculture became the mainstay in the Later Vedic period.

questions.text: Select the correct combination of famous palaces and their locations in Rajasthan.
questions.explanation: Lalgarh Palace is in Bikaner. Umaid Bhawan Palace is in Jodhpur, Rambagh Palace in Jaipur and the Taj Lake Palace in Udaipur.

questions.text: Who is the author of the novel ‘Life and Death of Sambhaji’ published in the year 2021?
questions.explanation: 'Life and Death of Sambhaji' (Ebury Press, 2021) is by Medha Deshmukh Bhaskaran.

questions.text: What does Age Structure represent?
options: The number of females per 100 males in a given area at a specified time period
The proportion of persons in different age groups relative to the total population
The number of females per 1000 males in a given area at a specified time period
A measure comparing the portion of a population composed of dependents with the portion that is in the working age group
questions.explanation: Age structure is the share of people in each age group of a population. The other options describe sex ratios and the dependency ratio.

questions.text: The percentage of sunlight energy absorbed by the green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem is about _______.
questions.explanation: Green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem capture only about 1% of the sunlight falling on their leaves and convert it into food energy.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. Although our new boss knew he was wrong, he was too “obstinate” to accept that.
questions.explanation: 'Obstinate' means stubbornly refusing to change one's mind; its opposite is 'flexible'. 'Adamant' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Procrastination
questions.explanation: 'Procrastination' is putting things off; its opposite is 'eagerness' to get on with them. 'Hesitance' and 'hawing' are close to synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Like a bat out of hell
questions.explanation: To go 'like a bat out of hell' is to go extremely fast and recklessly.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. He is “truest” to his words.
questions.explanation: Nothing is being compared, so the positive degree: 'He is true to his words.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. This is the best novel / I have read, / in a very long time.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: 'the best novel I have read in a very long time' pairs the superlative with the present perfect.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Seizing the opportunity, Akhil decided to “take the bull with the horns”.
options: take the bull at the horns
take the bull on the horns
take the bull by the horns
take the bull in the horns
questions.explanation: The idiom is 'take the bull by the horns': to face a difficulty boldly.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. He was studying in the “dimmer” light.
questions.explanation: No comparison is being made, so the positive degree: 'in the dim light'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. Her “austere” lifestyle reflected her minimalist approach to living.
questions.explanation: 'Austere' means severely plain and serious, without comfort or luxury; of the options 'sombre' (sober and serious) comes closest, and 'luxurious' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Please _____ with me for a while
questions.explanation: To 'bear with' someone is to be patient with them; 'bare', 'bar' and 'bairn' (a child) do not fit.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The sky is covering / with dark clouds and / I hope soon it / will begin to rain.
questions.explanation: The clouds cover the sky, so the sky takes the passive: 'The sky is covered (or is being covered) with dark clouds'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. You seem to be “mean” to your seniors.
questions.explanation: 'Mean' here means unkind; its opposite is 'sympathetic'. 'Rude' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Heba “dropped of the club unexpectedly” to say hello and catch up.
questions.explanation: To 'drop by' a place is to pay it a short, informal visit: 'Heba dropped by the club unexpectedly'.

questions.text: Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error in the given sentence. Women and children were often employed in the textile industry during the first “centuary” of industrialisation.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'century'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. _________ we gave them was some homemade ice cream.
questions.explanation: 'What' introduces a noun clause meaning 'the thing that': 'What we gave them was some homemade ice cream.'

questions.text: The given sentence is divided into three segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. If there is no error, select ‘No error’. The committee has careful / considered the report which you sent us / and has decided to take action.
options: considered the report which you sent us
and has decided to take action.
questions.explanation: The verb 'considered' needs an adverb: 'The committee has carefully considered the report'.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling error in the following sentence. In his persuit of excellence, he forgot to take care of his health.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'pursuit'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Sam and Teena / had wondering / what to do this weekend.
questions.explanation: 'Had' cannot take the -ing form on its own: 'had been wondering' (past perfect continuous) or 'were wondering'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The rising interest in and concern about animal welfare resulted in legislative laws and the formation of The Animal ____________ Committee in many nations.
questions.explanation: Committees that oversee how animals are treated, for example in research, are called Animal Ethics Committees.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. at top of your lungs
questions.explanation: To shout 'at the top of your lungs' is to shout as loudly as you can.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Language is a powerful device that (1)____________ communication and interaction between individuals. It serves as a crucial tool for expressing thoughts, emotions, and ideas. (2)____________ richness of language can be observed in various forms, including spoken and written interaction. People employ language to convey their intentions, share knowledge, and build relationships. It is a fundamental aspect of human interaction and plays a vital role in shaping societies and cultures. Without language, cooperation would be (3)___________, as it serves as the foundation for collaboration and understanding among diverse communities. Furthermore, language is dynamic and stationary, evolving over time to adapt to changing environments. New words are (4)____________ into the vocabulary, reflecting advancements in technology, science and culture. The ability to modify and adapt language is a key aspect of linguistic competence. (5)____________, the importance of language cannot be underestimated. It is a fundamental tool for human expression and interaction, facilitating the exchange of ideas and the formation of connections among people.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Language 'facilitates', that is makes easier, communication and interaction.
