questions.text: A product having an MRP of ₹29,800 is on sale for ₹28,608 in-store. How much of a discount is being offered on the product?
The mean proportional between the numbers p and q is 8. Which of the following pairs of numbers can be the values of p and q?
questions.explanation: The mean proportional of p and q is √(pq), so pq = 8² = 64. Of the pairs, only 16 × 4 = 64.

questions.text: Three students of class VII participated in a race during a school sports day. In a 1 km race, A wins the race with B by 100 m, and in a 300 m race, B beats C by 50 m. Then in the race of 1 km, with what margin will A beat C?
questions.explanation: When A runs 1,000 m, B runs 900 m. B and C run in the ratio 300 : 250, so while B runs 900 m, C runs 900 × 250/300 = 750 m. A beats C by 1,000 − 750 = 250 m.

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 72 kg and 39 kg is:

The average weight of a certain number of apples in a basket was 0.5 kg. If 10 apples with an average weight of 0.7 kg are removed from the basket and 5 apples with an average weight of 0.6 kg are added to the basket, then the average weight of the apples in the basket decreases by 0.1 kg. What was the initial number of apples in the basket?
questions.explanation: With n apples the total is 0.5n kg. Removing 10 × 0.7 = 7 kg and adding 5 × 0.6 = 3 kg leaves 0.5n − 4 kg in n − 5 apples at 0.4 kg each: 0.5n − 4 = 0.4n − 2, so n = 20.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 as a sum borrowed at 9% per year rate of interest for 5 years.
By selling an article for ₹20, a dealer makes a profit of 10%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹, rounded off to two decimal place) so as to make a profit of 35%?
questions.explanation: The cost price is 20/1.10 = ₹18.18. A 35% profit needs a selling price of 20 × 1.35/1.10 = ₹24.545, so the price must rise by ₹4.545, about ₹4.55.

questions.text: The average mark in an exam was 60. Due to some assessment errors, the marks of 115 students had to be changed from 85 to 50 each, and the new average is 55. The total number of students who appeared in the examination was:
questions.explanation: Each of the 115 changes lowers the total by 35, a fall of 115 × 35 = 4,025. The average falls by 5, so there were 4,025/5 = 805 students.

questions.text: The average weight of 30 male workers in a company is 62.5 kg and that of the remaining 20 female workers is 54.5 kg. The average weight of the total workers in the company is:

The original breadth of a rectangular box is 25 cm. The box was then remade in such a way that its length was increased by 30% but the breadth decreased by 20% and the area increased by 100 cm². What is the length (in cm) of the new box?
questions.explanation: With length L, the area goes from 25L to 1.3L × 20 = 26L, a rise of L cm². So L = 100 and the new length is 1.3 × 100 = 130 cm.

questions.text: What is the ratio between the area of a square having side of 6 cm and that of the rhombus having diagonals of 8 cm and 6 cm?
questions.explanation: Square: 6² = 36 cm². Rhombus: ½ × 8 × 6 = 24 cm². 36 : 24 = 3 : 2.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 8% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
Find the HCF of 90, 230 and 325.
questions.explanation: 90 = 2 × 3² × 5, 230 = 2 × 5 × 23 and 325 = 5² × 13; the only common factor is 5.

questions.text: A man sold an article for ₹237, there by gaining 18.5%. The cost of the article (in ₹) was:
questions.explanation: The selling price is 118.5% of the cost, so the cost = 237/1.185 = ₹200.

questions.text: Seven people P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). S is sitting to the immediate left of Q. V is sitting third to the left of S. R is sitting third to the right of T. U is sitting second to the left of R. How many people are sitting between S and R when counted from the right of R?
questions.explanation: Seated clockwise (each person's left, facing the centre): Q, S, P, R, V, U, T, which meets every condition. Going from R to its right (anticlockwise), only P sits before S: one person.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E and F are six friends sitting around a circular dinner table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). E is an immediate neighbour of F. B is sitting second to the left of A. D is sitting to the immediate right of F. Who is sitting third to the left of A?
questions.explanation: Seated clockwise (each person's left, facing the centre): A, C, B, D, F, E, with B second to A's left, D to F's immediate right and E beside F. In a circle of six, third to the left of A is the seat opposite A: D.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘played the piano’ is written as ‘lo le li’ and ‘sparkles a piano’ is coded as ‘lu li la’. How is ‘piano’ coded in that language?
questions.explanation: 'piano' is the only word in both phrases and 'li' the only code in both, so piano = li.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All actors are singers. All singers are dancers. Conclusions: (I) At least some singers are actors. (II) Some dancers may not be singers.
questions.explanation: All actors are singers, so some singers are actors (I). Nothing says every dancer is a singer, so it remains possible that some dancers are not singers (II). Both follow.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 348 350 354 360 368 ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 2, 4, 6, 8, so the next is 10: 368 + 10 = 378.

questions.text: 312 is related to 104 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 363 is related to 121. To which of the following is 375 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is divided by 3: 312 ÷ 3 = 104 and 363 ÷ 3 = 121. Likewise 375 ÷ 3 = 125.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? SRQ ,ONM, KJI, GFE, ?
questions.explanation: Each group is three consecutive letters in reverse, and each group starts 4 letters before the last one: S, O, K, G, C. The next group is CBA.

questions.text: DJFL is related to HNJP in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, GMIO is related to KQMS. To which of the following is IOKQ related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places forward: DJFL → HNJP and GMIO → KQMS. So IOKQ → MSOU.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘PURE’ is coded as ‘3792’ and ‘BURP’ is coded as ‘9537’. What is the code for ‘B’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: P, U and R are in both words, as are 3, 7 and 9 in both codes. The letter left in BURP is B and the digit left in its code is 5, so B = 5.

questions.text: This question has two statements followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the given statements. Statements: Some stones are hurting. Some stones are beautiful. Conclusions: (I) Some beautiful stones are hurting. (II) Some hurting stones are beautiful.
questions.explanation: The stones that are hurting and the stones that are beautiful may be different stones, so neither conclusion follows.

questions.text: 22 is related to 132 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 35 is related to 210. To which of the following is 18 related following the same logic?(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 6: 22 × 6 = 132 and 35 × 6 = 210. Likewise 18 × 6 = 108.

questions.text: PWSO is related to RYUQ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, MTPL is related to OVRN. To which of the following is JQMI related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: PWSO → RYUQ and MTPL → OVRN. So JQMI → LSOK.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘×‘ are interchanged and ‘−’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 18 ÷ 6 + 5 × 14 − 7 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 18 − 6 × 5 + 14 ÷ 7 = 18 − 30 + 2 = −10.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘COKE’ is coded as ‘1357’ and ‘JOKE’ is coded as ‘5673’. What is the code for ‘J’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: O, K and E are in both words, as are 3, 5 and 7 in both codes. The letter left in JOKE is J and the digit left in its code is 6, so J = 6.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 304 ÷ 3 + 55 × 5 − 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 304 × 3 − 55 ÷ 5 + 2 = 912 − 11 + 2 = 903.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘write this sentence’ is coded as ‘aw pm nl’ and ‘this is mine’ is coded as ‘nl wb cd’. How is ‘this’ coded in that code language?
questions.explanation: 'this' is the only word in both sentences and 'nl' the only code in both, so this = nl.

questions.text: Who received the National Nritya Shiromani award 2019 for promoting Kathak dance form across the world?
questions.explanation: The US-based Kathak dancer Anindita Neogy Anaam received the National Nritya Shiromani award at the 10th Cuttack Mahotsav in Odisha in January 2019, for preserving and promoting Kathak across the world.

questions.text: Which Indian dynasty is associated with the creation of highly skillful bronze sculptures?
questions.explanation: The Cholas are famed for their bronzes, cast by the lost-wax method; the dancing Shiva, Nataraja, is the best known.

questions.text: Which Ministry of India launched the Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY)?
options: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Labour and Employment launched PMRPY in 2016; through the EPFO, the government paid part of employers' provident-fund contributions for new employees to encourage hiring.

questions.text: Which famous medieval singer was born in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh in the year 1506?
questions.explanation: Tansen, the singer of Akbar's court and one of its 'nine gems', was born near Gwalior; 1506 is one of the years given for his birth.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following wars took place in the year 1761?
questions.explanation: The Third Battle of Panipat, between the Marathas and Ahmad Shah Abdali, was fought on 14 January 1761. Wandiwash was fought in 1760, the Second Battle of Panipat in 1556 and Buxar in 1764.

questions.text: In June 2023, who was appointed as the new Research and Analysis Wing (RAW) chief?
questions.explanation: Ravi Sinha, a 1988-batch IPS officer, was appointed chief of RAW in June 2023, succeeding Samant Goel.

questions.text: Which great Indian classical dancer choreographed the songs for Madhuri Dixit in 'Devdas' and 'Dil To Pagal Hai' movies?
questions.explanation: The Kathak maestro Pandit Birju Maharaj choreographed Madhuri Dixit's dances in 'Dil To Pagal Hai' (1997) and 'Devdas' (2002), including 'Kaahe Chhed Mohe'.

questions.text: Who was the successor of Vima Kadphises in Kushana dynasty?
questions.explanation: Vima Kadphises was succeeded by Kanishka, the greatest Kushana ruler. Kujula Kadphises founded the dynasty; Kharavela ruled Kalinga and Menander was an Indo-Greek king.

questions.text: In which year was the first-ever motion to remove a Supreme Court Justice signed by the members of Parliament?
questions.explanation: The motion to remove Justice V. Ramaswami, the first against a Supreme Court judge, was signed by 108 Lok Sabha members in 1991; when it was put to the vote in 1993 it failed.

questions.text: The Sarda River rises in the ________ glacier in the Nepal Himalayas.
questions.explanation: NCERT's 'India: Physical Environment', which this question follows, says the Sarda (Saryu) rises in the Milam glacier in the Nepal Himalayas, where it is called the Goriganga, and is known as the Kali along the India-Nepal border. (The Milam glacier itself lies in Uttarakhand's Pithoragarh district.)

questions.text: Minor points called 'Yuko' are part of which of the following sports?
questions.explanation: A 'yuko' was a minor score in judo, below 'waza-ari' and 'ippon'.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In 1917, Mahatma Gandhi started his first satyagraha in India against the forced cultivation of indigo by Europeans in which of the following districts of British India?
questions.explanation: Gandhi's Champaran Satyagraha (1917), in Bihar, took up the cause of peasants forced by European planters to grow indigo under the tinkathia system.

questions.text: International Day of Non-violence is observed on ___________.
questions.explanation: Since 2007 the UN has marked 2 October, Mahatma Gandhi's birthday, as the International Day of Non-Violence.

questions.text: What is Gross Domestic Product (GDP) in the context of National Income Accounting?
options: The total income of a country's government
The total exports of a country
The total savings of a nation
The total value of all goods and services produced within a country's borders in a specific period
questions.explanation: GDP is the market value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given period, usually a year.

questions.text: What is the product of the following chemical reaction? NaCl + H₂O + CO₂ + NH₃
questions.explanation: In the Solvay process sodium chloride, water, carbon dioxide and ammonia react to give sodium hydrogencarbonate (NaHCO₃), baking soda, and ammonium chloride.

questions.text: For which English novel was Ruskin Bond honoured with the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1992?
options: Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra
questions.explanation: Ruskin Bond received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1992 for 'Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra'. 'The Room on the Roof', his first novel, won the John Llewellyn Rhys Prize.

questions.text: Which of the following communicable diseases is caused by bacteria?
questions.explanation: Cholera is caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae. Influenza and dengue are caused by viruses, and malaria by a protozoan, Plasmodium.

questions.text: What is the frequency (f) of a wave with a period of 0.04 seconds?
questions.explanation: Frequency is the reciprocal of the period: f = 1/T = 1/0.04 = 25 Hz.

questions.text: After the ________ of Hakim Mirza, Kabul was annexed by Akbar and given to Raja Man Singh as ‘jagir’.
questions.explanation: Akbar's half-brother Mirza Muhammad Hakim ruled Kabul; Akbar annexed it after Hakim's death in 1585.

questions.text: Which of the following iron and steel plants is located in Odisha?
questions.explanation: Rourkela Steel Plant, set up with German help, is in Odisha. Bokaro is in Jharkhand, Vijayanagar in Karnataka and Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh.

questions.text: At which sports event in India is the Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy awarded?
questions.explanation: The Raja Bhalindra Singh Trophy goes to the state or team that tops the medal table at the National Games.

questions.text: Suspended solids in water can increase the haziness of the water. Which of the following represents the measurement of haziness of water?
questions.explanation: Turbidity is the cloudiness of water caused by suspended particles; salinity is its salt content.

questions.text: In which region of Bangladesh do the Chakma people predominantly live, among the country's various indigenous ethnic groups?
questions.explanation: The Chakmas, mostly Buddhist, live mainly in the Chittagong Hill Tracts in south-eastern Bangladesh.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In January 2024, Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid tributes to Savitribai Phule on her birth anniversary. In which field did Savitribai Phule make significant contributions, as highlighted by Prime Minister Modi?
questions.explanation: Savitribai Phule, born on 3 January 1831, opened schools for girls in Pune with Jyotirao Phule from 1848 and worked against caste and gender discrimination.

questions.text: If a citizen is helping the government in protecting the monuments in his/her area, which of the following fundamental duties is he/she performing?
options: Valuing and preserving the rich heritage and culture
questions.explanation: Article 51A(f) asks every citizen to value and preserve the rich heritage of the country's composite culture; protecting monuments serves that duty.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I will try to _______ because he is a good friend of mine.
questions.explanation: To 'get someone off the hook' is to free them from trouble or blame, which one would try to do for a good friend.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. He was not able to answer as the question was “ambiguous”.
questions.explanation: 'Ambiguous' means open to more than one meaning; its opposite is 'clear'.

questions.text: The bat flew silently through the night, searching for insects to eat. The bat in this context refers to _______.
options: a measurement unit in digital information systems
the act of delivering a forceful strike or hit
a wooden tool utilised in sports like baseball or cricket
a mammal known for nocturnal flight and insect consumption
questions.explanation: 'Flew silently through the night, searching for insects' points to the animal: the bat is a flying mammal that hunts insects at night.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a spelling error. This item is in the public domain / and can be used, / copied and modefied / without any restrictions.
options: This item is in the public domain
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'modified'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. My teacher's _______ (stern) warning made all the students quiet and calm.
questions.explanation: 'Stern' means serious and strict: 'strict'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The teacher asked us to _________ our homework by tomorrow.
questions.explanation: 'Asked us to' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'to complete our homework'.

questions.text: Identify the word with a spelling error in the following sentence. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. She had swam the English Channel twice.
questions.explanation: 'Had' takes the past participle, and the forms are 'swim, swam, swum': 'She had swum the English Channel twice.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. Samira is a lady who needs “extrinsic” motivation and will not work on her own.
questions.explanation: 'Extrinsic' means coming from outside, as opposed to 'intrinsic': 'outward'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate present tense form of the verb to fill in the blank. They __________ football every day.
questions.explanation: A habit ('every day') takes the simple present, and the plural 'they' takes 'play'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The allowance that is given by a husband to his wife on separation
questions.explanation: Alimony is the allowance paid to a spouse after separation or divorce.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The library books were long __________________, their pages bearing the weight of the passage of time.
questions.explanation: Library books kept past their return date are 'overdue'; 'long overdue' fits pages that bear the weight of time.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I remember________ when she used to wash dishes in a restaurant.
questions.explanation: 'I remember the time when ...' recalls a period in the past; 'when' points to a time.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word. She recieved a beautiful surprise from her partner.
questions.explanation: 'Recieved' is misspelt: the word is 'received' ('i' before 'e' except after 'c').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. Thousands of people were “killed by” the train accident that took place last Wednesday.
questions.explanation: People are killed 'in' an accident, not 'by' it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Dolphins are named among the “intelligent” animals on earth.
questions.explanation: 'Among' points to a group, so the superlative is needed: 'among the most intelligent animals on earth'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Caught in a time warp
options: To remain unchanged from a time in the past
To avoid talking about what’s important
questions.explanation: Someone or something 'caught in a time warp' has not changed from an earlier time, as if time had stood still.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. In the beauty contest, Parul won the award for being the “beautiful” one.
questions.explanation: Winning the award picks out one of all the contestants, so the superlative: 'for being the most beautiful one'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option with the correct usage of the preposition to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. World Press Freedom Day will be dedicated to the importance of journalism and “freedom in expression” in the context of the current global environmental crisis.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is 'freedom of expression', as in 'freedom of speech'.

questions.text: Change the following sentence into positive degree. Mercury is the smallest planet in the solar system.
options: The most smallest planet in the solar system is mercury.
Mercury is smaller than any other planet in the solar system.
No other planet is as small as Mercury in the Solar System.
Mercury is the smallest planet than any other one.
questions.explanation: A superlative becomes positive with 'No other ... as ... as': 'No other planet is as small as Mercury.' 'Smaller than any other' is the comparative degree.

questions.text: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
options: She saw an excellent episode of the series.
After a tiring day, I had a cup of coffee with Sudhir.
There is a man sitting beside cat.
She asked an easy question, and I took an hour to crack it.
questions.explanation: A singular countable noun needs an article: 'sitting beside a cat' (or 'the cat').

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Forests provide essential ecosystem services (1)__________ benefit both the environment and human society. One crucial service is carbon sequestration, as forests absorb and store large amounts of carbon dioxide, helping mitigate climate change. Additionally, forests regulate water cycles (2)__________ influencing precipitation patterns and maintaining water quality. (3)__________, forests offer recreational opportunities, cultural significance, and economic benefits through timber production and (4)__________. Thus, preserving and sustainably managing forests is imperative for maintaining these (5)__________ ecosystem services.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun 'that' introduces the clause describing the services: 'services that benefit both the environment and human society'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Forests provide essential ecosystem services (1)__________ benefit both the environment and human society. One crucial service is carbon sequestration, as forests absorb and store large amounts of carbon dioxide, helping mitigate climate change. Additionally, forests regulate water cycles (2)__________ influencing precipitation patterns and maintaining water quality. (3)__________, forests offer recreational opportunities, cultural significance, and economic benefits through timber production and (4)__________. Thus, preserving and sustainably managing forests is imperative for maintaining these (5)__________ ecosystem services.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Forests regulate water cycles 'by' influencing precipitation: 'by' with an -ing form gives the means.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Forests provide essential ecosystem services (1)__________ benefit both the environment and human society. One crucial service is carbon sequestration, as forests absorb and store large amounts of carbon dioxide, helping mitigate climate change. Additionally, forests regulate water cycles (2)__________ influencing precipitation patterns and maintaining water quality. (3)__________, forests offer recreational opportunities, cultural significance, and economic benefits through timber production and (4)__________. Thus, preserving and sustainably managing forests is imperative for maintaining these (5)__________ ecosystem services.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Moreover' adds a further point to those already made, following 'Additionally' in the sentence before.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Forests provide essential ecosystem services (1)__________ benefit both the environment and human society. One crucial service is carbon sequestration, as forests absorb and store large amounts of carbon dioxide, helping mitigate climate change. Additionally, forests regulate water cycles (2)__________ influencing precipitation patterns and maintaining water quality. (3)__________, forests offer recreational opportunities, cultural significance, and economic benefits through timber production and (4)__________. Thus, preserving and sustainably managing forests is imperative for maintaining these (5)__________ ecosystem services.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Economic benefits come 'through timber production and ecotourism'; degradation and deforestation are harms, not benefits.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Forests provide essential ecosystem services (1)__________ benefit both the environment and human society. One crucial service is carbon sequestration, as forests absorb and store large amounts of carbon dioxide, helping mitigate climate change. Additionally, forests regulate water cycles (2)__________ influencing precipitation patterns and maintaining water quality. (3)__________, forests offer recreational opportunities, cultural significance, and economic benefits through timber production and (4)__________. Thus, preserving and sustainably managing forests is imperative for maintaining these (5)__________ ecosystem services.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: An adjective is needed before 'ecosystem services': 'vital', meaning essential.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: A thief is spotted by a policeman at a distance of 300 m. the policeman chases the thief at speed of 10 km/h and the thief is running at a speed of 11 km/h, then the distance between them after 12 minutes is:
questions.explanation: The thief is faster by 11 − 10 = 1 km/h, so in 12 minutes (1/5 hour) he gains 0.2 km = 200 m. The gap grows to 300 + 200 = 500 m.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 2 years.

A solid metallic sphere of radius 15 cm is melted and recast into solid spherical balls of radius 3 cm each. What is the ratio of the surface area of the original sphere to the sum of the surface areas of all the balls?
questions.explanation: By volume the sphere makes (15/3)³ = 125 balls. Surface areas: 4π × 15² : 125 × 4π × 3² = 225 : 1125 = 1 : 5.

questions.text: As part of the partial work from home process, Amita went to office every 2nd day, Amrita went to office every 3rd day, and Tosita went to office every 6th day, respectively. All three went to office on 31 October 2021. On how many days did all three attend office on the same date during the remaining two months of the year?
questions.explanation: All three are in together every LCM(2, 3, 6) = 6 days. November and December have 61 days, and the sixth, twelfth, ..., sixtieth day after 31 October fall within them (the last is 30 December): 10 days.

questions.text: A student's final grade is determined by their final examination scores (weighted at 60%) and a final project score (weighted at 40%). If the student scores 75 in the final examination and 90 in the project, then the final grade of the student is:

A trader sells 25 kg of rice at ₹1,400. A customer asks for 15% discount. The shopkeeper agrees to it but instead of 1 kg he gives 10% less rice. What is the effective discount that the customer gets (correct to one decimal place)?
questions.explanation: The customer pays 85% of the price for 90% of the rice, so the effective price is 0.85/0.9 = 94.4% of the original: a discount of about 5.6%.

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 67 kg and 38 kg is:
The ratio of the incomes of Rama and Ganga is 4 : 3 and the ratio of their expenditures is 3 : 2. If each person saves ₹2,700, then find their expenditures, respectively.
questions.explanation: With incomes 4x, 3x and expenditures 3y, 2y: 4x − 3y = 2,700 and 3x − 2y = 2,700. Subtracting gives x = y, so x = y = 2,700 and the expenditures are ₹8,100 and ₹5,400.

questions.text: The average of nine consecutive integers is 54. The second largest of these numbers is:
questions.explanation: Nine consecutive integers averaging 54 run from 50 to 58, so the second largest is 57.

questions.text: In an election between A and B, A gets double the votes of B and wins with a margin of 150 votes. 10% of votes were invalid. What is the total number of votes polled in the election?
questions.explanation: A = 2B and A − B = 150, so B = 150 and A = 300: 450 valid votes. These are 90% of the votes polled, so 450/0.9 = 500 were polled.

questions.text: A sum of ₹312 was divided among 100 boys and girls in such a way that each boy gets ₹3.60 and each girl ₹2.40. The number of girls is:
questions.explanation: With b boys: 3.60b + 2.40(100 − b) = 312, so 1.2b = 72 and b = 60. The other 40 are girls.

questions.text: Two trains 280 metres and 260 metres long, respectively, are running towards each other on parallel lines, one at the speed of 58 km/hr and another at the speed of 50 km/hr. How much time (in seconds) will they take to cross each other?
questions.explanation: Moving towards each other, their relative speed is 58 + 50 = 108 km/h = 30 m/s. They cover 280 + 260 = 540 m in 540/30 = 18 seconds.

questions.text: Raman purchased an iron at a cost of ₹2,400 and sold it to Rohan at a loss of 8%. Rohan sold it to Soham at a gain of 12.5%. At what price should Soham sell the iron to gain 15%?
questions.explanation: Rohan paid 2,400 × 0.92 = ₹2,208 and Soham paid 2,208 × 1.125 = ₹2,484. For a 15% gain Soham must sell at 2,484 × 1.15 = ₹2,856.60.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹4000 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 5 years.
In a certain code language, ‘CORNER’ is written as ‘REORNC’ and ‘BUDGET’ is written as ‘TEUDGB’. How will ‘DEVICE’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The code takes the 6th, 5th, 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 1st letters: CORNER → R E O R N C and BUDGET → T E U D G B. So DEVICE → E C E V I D: ECEVID.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All pens are markers. Some erasers are pens. Conclusions: (I) Some markers are erasers. (II) All markers are pens.
questions.explanation: Some erasers are pens and all pens are markers, so those erasers are markers: some markers are erasers (I). Nothing says every marker is a pen, so II does not follow.

questions.text: CJ16 is related to EL26 in a certain way. In the same way, MT42 is related to OV52. To which of the following is HO11 related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward and the number rises by 10: C → E, J → L, 16 → 26, and M → O, T → V, 42 → 52. So HO11 → JQ21.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 16 ÷ 8 + 13 + 36 × 18 − 3 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 16 × 8 − 13 − 36 ÷ 18 + 3 = 128 − 13 − 2 + 3 = 116.

questions.text: In a code language, 'FORK' is coded as ‘GLWD’ and 'CAVF' is coded as ‘DXAY’. How will 'TRHA' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, −3, +5, −7, wrapping round the alphabet: F → G, O → L, R → W, K → D. So T → U, R → O, H → M and A → T: UOMT.

questions.text: JMGI is related to QTNP in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, GJDF is related to NQKM. To which of the following is DGAC related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 7 places forward: J → Q, M → T, G → N, I → P. So D → K, G → N, A → H, C → J: KNHJ.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 2, 3, 6, 12, 10, 21, 14, ?
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 2, 6, 10, 14 (+4) and 3, 12, 21 (+9). The next term of the second is 21 + 9 = 30.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). D sits third to the left of E. G sits second to the left of B. Only E sits between F and G. A is not an immediate neighbour of D. Who sits fourth to the right of C?
questions.explanation: Going round the table to each person's left from E: E, F, C, D, B, A, G. Then D is third to the left of E, G second to the left of B, only E sits between F and G, and A is not next to D. Counting four places to C's right (F, E, G, A) gives A.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/ subtracting /multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 22, 31; 26, 35
questions.explanation: The second number is the first plus 9: 22 + 9 = 31 and 26 + 9 = 35. Likewise 38 + 9 = 47.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘car drive steady’ is coded as ‘mi ku pa’ and ‘steady is safe’ is coded as ‘tu an mi’. How is ‘steady’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'steady' is the only word in both sentences and 'mi' the only code in both, so steady = mi.

questions.text: 3 is related to 8 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 24 is related to 35. To which of the following is 99 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: 3 = 2² − 1 goes to 3² − 1 = 8, and 24 = 5² − 1 goes to 6² − 1 = 35. So 99 = 10² − 1 goes to 11² − 1 = 120.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some flutes are violins. Some violins are tablas. All tablas are sitars. Conclusions: (I): Some violins are sitars. (II): Some flutes are tablas.
questions.explanation: The violins that are tablas are also sitars, so some violins are sitars (I). The flutes that are violins need not be among the violins that are tablas, so II does not follow.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? BDG, EGJ , HJM, KMP, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward from one cluster to the next: K → N, M → P, P → S: NPS.

questions.text: Seven friends, A, B, C, D, E, F and G, are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order) . D is an immediate neighbour of both A and F. B is sitting to the immediate right of F. C is sitting second to the left of A. G and E both are C’s immediate neighbours and G is not an immediate neighbour of A. Who is the immediate neighbour of both B and D?
questions.explanation: Going round the table to each person's left from D: D, A, E, C, G, B, F. This fits every clue (B to F's immediate right, C second to A's left, G and E beside C, G not beside A), and F sits between B and D.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 35 × 7 ÷ 6 + 3 − 14 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 35 ÷ 7 × 6 − 3 + 14 = 30 − 3 + 14 = 41.

questions.text: Where was the inaugural match of the first edition of the Women's Premier League (WPL) organised in the year 2023?
questions.explanation: The first WPL match, Mumbai Indians against Gujarat Giants on 4 March 2023, was played at the DY Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai.

questions.text: The cytoplasmic zone surrounding the Golgi complex possesses no cell organelles. This zone of clear cytoplasm is called:
questions.explanation: The clear, organelle-free cytoplasm around the Golgi complex is the zone of exclusion. Cytosol is the fluid of the cytoplasm in general, cytosine a nitrogen base and cytochromes respiratory proteins.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT included in the three main dimensions of the New Industrial Policy, 1991, announced by the Government of India?
questions.explanation: The New Industrial Policy of 1991 rested on liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation (LPG); urbanisation was not one of them.

questions.text: When was India’s first ever budget presented?
questions.explanation: India's first budget was presented on 7 April 1860 by James Wilson, the finance member of the Viceroy's council.

questions.text: Udit Narayan was conferred the Padma Bhushan in 2016 for which of the following fields?
questions.explanation: Udit Narayan is a film playback singer; his 2016 Padma Bhushan was in Art (playback singing).

questions.text: If an Indian citizen is denied entry to a public place because of his caste, which of the following Fundamental Rights is denied to him?
questions.explanation: Article 15(2), part of the Right to Equality, bars any restriction on a citizen's access to shops, public restaurants, hotels and places of public entertainment, or use of places of public resort, on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was one of the founders of the Indian National Congress in 1885?
questions.explanation: Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant, helped found the Indian National Congress, which first met in Bombay in December 1885.

questions.text: ‘Ram Navami’ is celebrated in India to commemorate the:
options: return of Lord Rama from forest.
coronation ceremony of Lord Rama as a king.
questions.explanation: Ram Navami, on the ninth day of the bright half of Chaitra, marks the birth of Lord Rama.

questions.text: Which river is known as ‘Langchen Khambab’ in Tibet?
questions.explanation: The Sutlej, which rises near Rakas Tal close to Mansarovar, is known as Langchen Khambab in Tibet.

questions.text: As per the reforms of the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2023, how many minerals have been removed from the list of atomic minerals?
questions.explanation: The 2023 amendment took six minerals off the list of atomic minerals: lithium, beryllium, titanium, niobium, tantalum and zirconium.

questions.text: Who was the highest run scorer in Men’s World Cup cricket - 2019?
questions.explanation: Rohit Sharma scored 648 runs, with five centuries, at the 2019 World Cup, one more than David Warner's 647.

questions.text: ‘Chakyar Koothu’, the folk dance form in which the entire story is presented by a single performer, primarily belongs to which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Chakyar Koothu, in which a single Chakyar performer narrates stories from the epics, is a temple art of Kerala.

questions.text: In February 2024, who took an oath as the 12th Chief Minister of Jharkhand?
questions.explanation: Champai Soren was sworn in as Chief Minister of Jharkhand on 2 February 2024, after Hemant Soren resigned.

questions.text: National Prophylaxis Program, which was launched in 1970 as an immediate remedial measure to address which of the following medical conditions /diseases caused by nutritional deficiencies?
questions.explanation: The National Prophylaxis Programme against Nutritional Blindness (1970) gives young children large doses of vitamin A, whose deficiency causes night blindness and can lead to permanent blindness.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution directs the Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor?
questions.explanation: Article 163 provides a Council of Ministers, headed by the Chief Minister, to aid and advise the Governor.

questions.text: The approximate number of water molecules present in 9 gm of water is _____.
questions.explanation: 9 g of water is 9/18 = 0.5 mole, and a mole holds 6.022 × 10²³ molecules: 0.5 × 6.022 × 10²³ = 3.011 × 10²³.

questions.text: K Kalyanasundaram Pillai was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, 1999, for his contribution to which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: K. Kalyanasundaram Pillai, a Bharatanatyam guru, received the 1999 Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for that dance form.

questions.text: ‘The Blue Umbrella’, ‘The Cherry Tree’, ‘The Hidden Pool’ are novels written by who among the following authors?
questions.explanation: 'The Blue Umbrella', 'The Cherry Tree' and 'The Hidden Pool' are all by Ruskin Bond.

questions.text: Who among the following was defeated by Babur in the Battle of Khanwa in 1527 CE?
questions.explanation: At Khanwa in 1527 Babur defeated Rana Sanga of Mewar; Hasan Khan Mewati and Medini Rai fought on Sanga's side. Ibrahim Lodi had fallen at Panipat in 1526.

questions.text: Which of the following sectors had the largest percentage of workforce in urban India in the year 2019-2020?
questions.explanation: In 2019-20 the service sector employed the largest share of urban workers, ahead of industry; agriculture's share in towns and cities is small.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Bal Gangadhar described ______ as a diamond of India.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Gopal Krishna Gokhale. Tilak, his political rival, is quoted as calling him 'this diamond of India, this jewel of Maharashtra' in his tribute when Gokhale died in 1915.

questions.text: A portion of landmass from the shore line up to the shelf break that is submerged under shallow water is known as:
questions.explanation: The continental shelf is the gently sloping, shallowly submerged edge of a continent, from the shore to the shelf break, where the continental slope begins.

questions.text: What is the overarching programme introduced in the Union Budget, 2018-19 by Government of India, for the school education sector?
questions.explanation: Samagra Shiksha, announced in the 2018-19 Union Budget, merged the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan and Teacher Education into one scheme for school education from pre-school to Class 12.

questions.text: Harshvardhan's ambitions of extending his power to Deccan and South India were stopped by:
questions.explanation: The Chalukya king Pulakesin II defeated Harsha on the Narmada, as his Aihole inscription records, and so stopped Harsha's advance to the south.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. I have lived with my parents / in Mumbai / in a residential flat / yet two years.
options: I have lived with my parents
questions.explanation: A length of time with the present perfect takes 'for': 'I have lived ... for two years', not 'yet two years'.

questions.text: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. Mosquito means small fly. It has a transmitter segmented body and a _________________ of wings. Male mosquitoes mainly feed on plant ________________.
questions.explanation: Wings come in a 'pair', and male mosquitoes feed on plant 'nectar'; only the females feed on blood.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. Many fraud companies _____ (deceive) innocent customers and earn millions of dollars.
questions.explanation: To 'mislead' is to deceive: to make someone believe what is untrue.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. She “prepares an unique” dish in the cooking competition and won it.
questions.explanation: The sentence is in the past ('won it'), so 'prepared'; and 'unique' begins with a 'yoo' sound, so it takes 'a'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. A fox and an hyena were spotted in the animal reserve.
questions.explanation: The 'h' in 'hyena' is sounded, so it takes 'a': 'a fox and a hyena'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given proverb. Bite the bullet
options: To be the first to attack someone
To face up to trouble with fortitude
To buy something with no prior inspection
To take the blame for something one didn't do
questions.explanation: To 'bite the bullet' is to face something difficult or unpleasant with courage.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence. I “graciously” welcomed my boss at my birthday party.
questions.explanation: 'Graciously' means kindly and courteously; 'nicely' is the closest. 'Courageously' and 'bravely' mean with courage, 'cleverly' with skill.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. To his “surprise”, it swung back at his touch.
questions.explanation: 'Surprise' is the feeling caused by something unexpected; of the options only 'shock' is close.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The questions in part B looks “difficult” than the questions in part A.
questions.explanation: Two things are compared with 'than', so the comparative 'more difficult' is needed; 'difficultier' is not a word. (Strictly, the plural 'questions' also needs 'look', but that word is not underlined.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. The soldiers “are all on their toes and anxiously waiting” for the orders to start marching towards the enemy.
options: all on their fingers and anxiously waiting
all on their toes and anxiously dancing
questions.explanation: To be 'on one's toes' is to be alert and ready, which fits soldiers anxiously waiting to march.

questions.text: What is the correct substitution for the word ‘screw’ in the idiom ‘Hit the screw on the head’?
questions.explanation: The idiom is 'hit the nail on the head': to describe something exactly right.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Futile
questions.explanation: 'Futile' means producing no result: 'useless'.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. We have pledged our “allegance” to the nation.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'allegiance'.

questions.text: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
options: She always cuts out unhealthy snacks.
Can you cut through the traffic to get here on time?
They need to cut down the old tree in the garden.
The manager cuts the discussion to address an urgent matter.
questions.explanation: To end a discussion early is to 'cut it short': 'The manager cuts the discussion short'. 'Cut out', 'cut through' and 'cut down' are used correctly in the others.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Ephemeral
questions.explanation: 'Ephemeral' means lasting a very short time: 'transient'. 'Permanent' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The student received an __________ for his outstanding performance.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'accolade', an award or mark of praise.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. We have perhaps never seen an “ablest” series of advocates than these ten standing in a row.
questions.explanation: With 'than' the comparative is needed, and 'an' needs a vowel sound: 'an abler series of advocates than these ten'. 'More able' would need 'a'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He had always wanted to work for himself; so, last year he _________ his job at the bank and is now running a tool business.
questions.explanation: To 'leave' a job is to quit it. 'Cleft' means split and 'bereft' deprived, and one does not 'halt' a job.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence. The chef's delicious recipies are a favourite among the restaurant's patrons.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'recipes'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate degree of comparison to fill in the blank. Work in this office is done in the _________ way.
questions.explanation: 'The' before the blank calls for the superlative: 'the least efficient way'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Are you familiar with the movie ‘Jurassic Park’? Do you recall the enormous dinosaurs? Do you know that there is still a mammal that is as big and amazing as them? Blue whales are the world’s largest living things and (1)________ vast oceanic expanses. The adult is more than 100 feet long and (2)_____ more than 190 metric tons. According to scientists, a blue whale’s heart weighs as much as a car while its tongue weighs as much as an elephant! They eat meat, but they don’t have teeth. They gulp and swallow huge quantities of krill and shrimp for their diet. Their mouths have bristles that look like combs and remove water while keeping their food (3)_______. Whales are social animals that live in ‘pods’, which are made up of more females than males. They take care of their children. Another female takes over and cares for the calf if one mother is unable to provide it with milk. Their bond is very strong, and they cry when another whale dies. The male makes sure that everyone in the pod gets their fair share of food. Whistles, clock-like sounds, and songs—frequent, high-pitched sounds—are the means by which the whales (4)_________ with one another. It assists them in locating one another, locating the position of the pod, searching for prey, and attracting mates. Every pod has a distinctive song that sets it apart from the others. These songs can be heard for not only hours, but also days (5)_______ miles of ocean.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: Blue whales 'inhabit', that is live in, vast oceanic expanses.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: A solid cuboid with dimensions 2 m × 4 m × 10 m is melted to form small solid cubes of side 8 cm. How many such cubes can be formed?
Raman paid ₹18,656 for a mobile phone, after a single discount of 12%. If Raman is given successive discounts of 4% and 8%, then how much Raman would pay?

A boat can travel at a speed of 28 km/h in still water. If the speed of the stream is 4 km/h, what is the average speed (in km/h) of the boat if it travels 192 km downstream, stops there for one hour and then returns to the starting point?
questions.explanation: Downstream at 28 + 4 = 32 km/h takes 192/32 = 6 hours; upstream at 28 − 4 = 24 km/h takes 8 hours. With the hour's stop, 384 km takes 15 hours: 384/15 = 25.6 km/h.

questions.text: Find the value of 5 + 32 ÷ 2 + 6 × 2.5.
questions.explanation: Division and multiplication first: 5 + 16 + 15 = 36.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 6% per year rate of interest for 5 years.
A mixture contains 8 kg of tea costing ₹295 per kilogram and 10 kg of tea costing ₹250 per kilogram. The average price per kilogram (in ₹) of the mixture is:

In a school, the average salary of 12 teachers was ₹71,400. If the average salary of the teachers, principal and vice principal was ₹89,500, then what was the average salary of the principal and vice principal (in ₹)?
questions.explanation: All 14 together earned 14 × 89,500 = ₹12,53,000 and the 12 teachers 12 × 71,400 = ₹8,56,800. The principal and vice principal earned the other ₹3,96,200: an average of ₹1,98,100.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 6% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
Find the average of the prime numbers lying between 68 and 91.
questions.explanation: The primes between 68 and 91 are 71, 73, 79, 83 and 89. Their sum is 395, so the average is 395/5 = 79.

questions.text: A rectangular sheet of paper of length 10π cm and width 5 cm is rolled along its length (width of the sheet becomes the height of the cylinder) to form a cylinder. What would be the radius of the cylinder?
questions.explanation: Rolled along its length, the 10π cm side becomes the circumference: 2πr = 10π, so r = 5 cm.

questions.text: If two numbers are 6.25% and 25% more than a third number, respectively, then the first number is how much per cent of the second number?
questions.explanation: Taking the third number as 100, the two numbers are 106.25 and 125. 106.25/125 × 100 = 85%.

questions.text: A dishonest dealer professes to sell his goods at cost price but uses a false weight and thus gains 15%. For a kilogram he uses a weight of ____ grams.
questions.explanation: Charging for 1,000 g while giving w g gains (1,000 − w)/w = 15%, so w = 1,000/1.15 = 869.57 grams.

questions.text: If 2744 identical small spheres are made out of a big sphere of radius 7 cm, then what is the surface area of each small sphere?
questions.explanation: Volume goes with the cube of the radius: 2744 = 14³, so each small sphere has radius 7/14 = 0.5 cm. Its surface area is 4π × 0.5² = π cm².

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 67 kg and 37 kg is:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? RVQ, OSN, LPK ,IMH, ?
questions.explanation: Every letter moves 3 places back each time: R, O, L, I, F; V, S, P, M, J; Q, N, K, H, E. The next cluster is FJE.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: All cocktails are mocktails. Some cocktails are juices. Conclusion (I): Some mocktails are juices. Conclusion (II): Some juices are not cocktails.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follow
questions.explanation: The cocktails that are juices are also mocktails, so some mocktails are juices (I). Every juice may be a cocktail, so II does not follow.

questions.text: EJGL is related to INKP in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, KPMR is related to OTQV. To which of the following is NSPU related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places forward: E → I, J → N, G → K, L → P and K → O, P → T, M → Q, R → V. So NSPU → RWTY.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). F is sitting second to the left of B. F is sitting third to the left of D. B is sitting to the immediate right of E. A is sitting third to the left of E. A is sitting to the immediate right of G. What is the position of F with respect to E?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left is the next seat clockwise. Going clockwise from E the order is E, F, C, A, G, D, B: B is to E's immediate right, F second to the left of B and third to the left of D, A third to the left of E and to G's immediate right. So F is to E's immediate left.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13, can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (18, 3, 54) (21, 4, 84)
questions.explanation: In each set the third number is the product of the first two: 18 × 3 = 54 and 21 × 4 = 84. Likewise 14 × 2 = 28.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘solve the puzzle’ is written as ‘sp di cy’ and ‘puzzle is tricky’ is coded as ‘qp vt di’. How is ‘puzzle’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'puzzle' is the only word in both sentences and 'di' the only code in both, so puzzle = di.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All carrots are onions. No onion is a tomato. Conclusions: (I) No carrot is a tomato. (II) All onions are carrots.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: All carrots are onions and no onion is a tomato, so no carrot is a tomato (I). 'All carrots are onions' does not make all onions carrots, so II does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘ train was late’ is coded as ‘ch px zt’ and ‘journey by train’ is coded as ‘fk zt bu’. How is ‘train’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'train' is the only word in both sentences and 'zt' the only code in both, so train = zt.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘×’ are interchanged and ‘−’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 55 × 16 − 4 ÷7 + 3 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 55 + 16 ÷ 4 − 7 × 3 = 55 + 4 − 21 = 38.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘GULF’ is coded as ‘7391’ and ‘FANS’ is coded as ‘2438’.What is the code for ‘F’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: F is the only letter in both words and 3 the only digit in both codes, so F = 3.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 36÷ 2 + 4× 8 −11× 3 + 28 = 49 (Note: Interchange should be done of the entire number and not individual digits of a given number.)
HLQC is related to KOTF in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, WTAN is related to ZWDQ. To which of the following is FXCM related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward: H → K, L → O, Q → T, C → F and W → Z, T → W, A → D, N → Q. So FXCM → IAFP (X wraps round to A).

questions.text: P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are sitting around a circular table, facing towards the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). P is an immediate neighbour of both T and U. S is sitting second to the right of P. Immediate neighbours of R are U and Q. S is not an immediate neighbour of U. Who is sitting to the immediate left of Q?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left is the next seat clockwise. S is second to P's right, so P's right-hand neighbour is T (U may not sit next to S) and U is on P's left. Clockwise from P: P, U, R, Q, V, S, T, with R between U and Q. V is to Q's immediate left.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series? 97, 88, 85, 76, 73, ?, 61
questions.explanation: The differences alternate −9 and −3: 97, 88, 85, 76, 73, 64, 61.

questions.text: 3 is related to 24 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 4 is related to 60. To which ofthe following is 6 related, following the same logic?(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: Each number goes to its cube minus itself: 3³ − 3 = 24 and 4³ − 4 = 60. So 6³ − 6 = 210.

questions.text: Which of the following was authored by Harisenacharya?
questions.explanation: The Brihatkatha Kosha, a collection of Jain stories, was written by the Jain monk Harisena (Harisenacharya) in the 10th century. Lilavati is Bhaskara II's, the Rajatarangini Kalhana's and the Brihat Katha Manjari Kshemendra's.

questions.text: The state religion of Bangladesh is:
questions.explanation: Bangladesh's Constitution makes Islam the state religion (Article 2A), while guaranteeing equal status to the other religions.

questions.text: What is the major purpose of the Salal Dam located on Chenab River in Jammu and Kashmir?
questions.explanation: The Salal project on the Chenab, in Reasi district, is a run-of-the-river hydroelectric project of NHPC.

questions.text: Which of the following phyla contains Leech?
questions.explanation: The leech is a segmented worm, like the earthworm, and belongs to the phylum Annelida.

questions.text: Who among the following was ‘Senani’ in the Rig Vedic period?
questions.explanation: In the Rig Vedic tribe the senani led the army in war; the priest was the purohita.

questions.text: In July 2023, Tribhuvaneshwar Saran Singh Deo was appointed as Deputy Chief Minister of which of the following states?
questions.explanation: T. S. Singh Deo was made Chhattisgarh's first Deputy Chief Minister in mid-2023, under Chief Minister Bhupesh Baghel.

questions.text: In weight lifting, when an athlete misses all three attempts in the snatch or the clean and jerk, failing to post a total, it is known as _________.
questions.explanation: A weightlifter who fails all three attempts in either lift posts no total and is said to have 'bombed out'.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Moplah Uprising, an organised opposition of Muslim cultivators, occurred in which modern state of India?
questions.explanation: The Moplah (Mappila) uprising of 1921 took place in Malabar, now part of Kerala.

questions.text: The union list from the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution consists of how many subjects as of May 2024?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 100, the figure many study guides quote for the Union List (97 subjects originally). Counts differ by source, because entries have since been added and removed: the GST amendment of 2016, for one, dropped entries 92 and 92C.

questions.text: In February 2023, there have been protests in Punjab to release a group of Sikh prisoners who have been in jail for more than 30 years since militancy was wiped out in Punjab in the 1990s. What are these prisoners called?
questions.explanation: 'Bandi Singhs' is the name given to Sikh prisoners held since the years of militancy in Punjab, whose release Sikh groups have long demanded.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which among the following is considered the first experiment of Satyagraha by Gandhiji in India?
questions.explanation: Gandhiji's first satyagraha in India was at Champaran in Bihar in 1917, for the indigo farmers; Ahmedabad and Kheda followed in 1918.

questions.text: Bhavnath Mahadev fair is held every year in which of the following places?
questions.explanation: The Bhavnath Mahadev fair is held at Mahashivratri at the Bhavnath temple at the foot of Mount Girnar, Junagadh (Gujarat).

questions.text: As per the 2001 Census, what is the specific age, for a person to be called literate?
questions.explanation: In the 2001 Census a person aged 7 or above who can read and write with understanding in any language counts as literate.

questions.text: A section of an active fault that has produced earthquakes in the past but is now quiet and is believed that the fault segment is capable of producing earthquake on some other basis is known as:
questions.explanation: A seismic gap is a stretch of an active fault that has slipped in past earthquakes but has been quiet for a long time, and is expected to produce one again.

questions.text: When was the Wildlife Protection Act passed?
questions.explanation: The Wildlife (Protection) Act was passed in 1972.

questions.text: Which of the following is a traditional game of India?
questions.explanation: Kabaddi is an ancient Indian game; basketball, football and volleyball came from abroad.

questions.text: Who became the first folk artist from India to walk the Cannes red carpet in 2022?
questions.explanation: Mame Khan, a Rajasthani folk singer, walked the red carpet at the 2022 Cannes Film Festival as part of India's official delegation.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about Viharas is/are correct? a)Viharas consist of a verandas, cell and hall around the walls of the hall. b)Ajanta cave and Nashik cave are important parts of Vihara architecture.
questions.explanation: Viharas, the monks' dwellings, have a hall with cells cut into the walls around it and a veranda in front; the caves at Ajanta and Nashik include well-known viharas.

questions.text: Who amongst the following stated the Grameen model of microfinance?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Yunus founded the Grameen Bank in Bangladesh, which lends small sums to the rural poor without collateral; he and the bank shared the 2006 Nobel Peace Prize.

questions.text: Anita Sharma, Sangeet Natak Akademi Award winner, is an exponent of ________ dance form.
questions.explanation: Anita Sharma, a Sattriya dancer from Assam, received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Sattriya for 2014.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book called ‘Beneath the Surface: My Story’?
questions.explanation: 'Beneath the Surface: My Story' is the autobiography of the American swimmer Michael Phelps.

questions.text: Sonal Mansingh is a famous proponent of which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: Sonal Mansingh is best known for Odissi, though she also trained in Bharatanatyam.

questions.text: The Mahananda River rising in the ________ is a tributary of Ganga.
questions.explanation: The Mahananda rises in the Darjeeling hills and flows through West Bengal and Bihar to join the Ganga from the left, at Godagari just inside Bangladesh.

questions.text: A group of natural substances with variable phenolic structures, which are found in fruits, vegetables, and grains is called:
questions.explanation: Flavonoids are plant compounds with variable phenolic structures, found in fruits, vegetables, grains, tea and wine.

questions.text: If four resistances of 4 ohm each are connected in parallel, what will be their effective resistance?
questions.explanation: In parallel, 1/R = 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 + 1/4 = 1, so R = 1 ohm.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Leisure activities are activities that people ___________ in during their free time while they are not working.
questions.explanation: People 'engage in' an activity: they take part in it.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'forgetful', with one l.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. The weather was “absolutley” perfect for the outdoor event.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'absolutely'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Corroborate
questions.explanation: To 'corroborate' a statement is to confirm or 'support' it.

questions.text: Select the option that has used the correct tense.
options: By the time we arriving at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.
By the time we arrive at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.
By the time we arrived at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.
By the time we arrives at the party, they had been waiting for over an hour.
questions.explanation: The past perfect continuous 'had been waiting' goes with the simple past in the time clause: 'By the time we arrived'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I have never seen so beautiful a landscape than this one.
questions.explanation: 'So … a' is followed by 'as', not 'than': 'so beautiful a landscape as this one'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Searing
questions.explanation: 'Searing' means extremely hot; its opposite is 'freezing'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Meticulous
questions.explanation: 'Meticulous' means very careful about detail. 'Regardless', in its sense of heedless or careless, is its opposite; the other three are terms of praise.

questions.text: Recognise the sentence with the correct transitive verb form of break. A. The cyclone broke the window. B.The window broke. C. The cyclone caused the breaking of window. D.The cyclone caused the broken window.
questions.explanation: A transitive verb takes an object: in 'The cyclone broke the window', 'broke' has the object 'the window'. In B 'broke' has no object, and C and D use a noun or a participle, not the verb.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Prem is an excellent chess player. He is the _______ student of the class too.
questions.explanation: 'The' before the blank and the comparison with the whole class call for the superlative: 'the most intelligent student'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. It is a common perception / that the rich sometimes / despise poor.
questions.explanation: 'The' with an adjective names a whole class of people: 'despise the poor', like 'the rich' earlier in the sentence.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. His sudden resignation left the company “in a very difficult situation and to have to make a hard decision” as they scrambled to find a replacement.
options: between a rock and a hard place
questions.explanation: To be 'between a rock and a hard place' is to face a choice between two difficult options.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. an open book
options: someone who gives advice based on theory not practice
a person of whom her mother is extremely proud
a person or thing that is easy to learn about and understand
questions.explanation: Someone who is 'an open book' hides nothing and is easy to understand.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Sushil, who recently joined our school / was awarded the Gold Cup / as he worked hardly / throughout the year.
options: Sushil, who recently joined our school
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' means scarcely; the adverb for working with effort is 'hard': 'as he worked hard'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Boisterous
questions.explanation: 'Boisterous' means noisy and lively; its opposite is 'quiet'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A post without any remuneration
questions.explanation: An honorary post is one held without pay.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. BBC Media has shown exponenteal growth in their revenue this year.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'exponential'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase. Belonging or pertaining to an individual from birth
questions.explanation: A congenital condition is present from birth; 'congenial' means pleasant.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Though people are becoming health-conscious these days, (1)________ simple lifestyle habits they are prone to fatal diseases. (2)________ a new study published in ‘The Journal of the American College of Cardiology’, (3)________ food more sparingly is linked to a lower risk of heart disease, heart failure , and ischemic heart disease. A significant risk factor for cardiovascular disease, high blood pressure, is demonstrated to be correlated (4)________ high sodium intake. As per the research, a person’s individual sodium intake over time may be predicted by how (5)____ they salt their food. It is found that people who do not put a little additional salt to their food very often had a much lower risk of heart disease event regardless of lifestyle factors and pre-existing disease.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: A noun phrase ('simple lifestyle habits') needs the preposition 'because of'; 'because' introduces a clause.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The average weight of 20 boys in a class is 65 kg and that of remaining 35 boys is 32 kg. What is the average weight of all the boys in the class?
The LCM of 140,180 and 240 is:
The average of five numbers, where the difference between any two consecutive numbers is 5, is 215. Find the least number.
questions.explanation: Five numbers 5 apart have their average in the middle, so they are 205, 210, 215, 220 and 225; the least is 205.

questions.text: A policeman sees a thief at a distance of 100 m and starts chasing him at a speed of 6 m/s while the thief runs at a speed of 5 m/s. What is the distance (in m) covered by the thief when he is caught?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 6 − 5 = 1 m every second, so he closes the 100 m in 100 seconds. In that time the thief runs 5 × 100 = 500 m.

questions.text: Two stations A and B are 1800 km apart. A train starts from A towards B at 7 A.M. at a speed of 100 km/h. Another train starts from B towards A at 8 A.M. on the same day at a speed of 325 km/h. At what time will they cross each other?
questions.explanation: By 8 A.M. the first train has run 100 km, leaving 1700 km. The trains close it at 100 + 325 = 425 km/h, taking 1700/425 = 4 hours: they cross at 12 noon.

questions.text: A sum of money invested at simple interest becomes 5 times in 12 years. How many times will it become in 27 years?
questions.explanation: Becoming 5 times means the interest is 4 times the sum in 12 years, so 1/3 of the sum a year. In 27 years the interest is 9 times the sum, so the amount is 10 times.

questions.text: Due to a fault in the voting machine, the invalid votes are counted in votes of the candidate B, who gets 5 times the invalid votes. A gets the votes 8 times the invalid votes and wins the election by 28. What is the total number of votes polled?
questions.explanation: Let the invalid votes be x. B's own votes are 5x, and with the invalid ones counted in he has 6x; A has 8x. So 8x − 6x = 28 gives x = 14, and the votes polled are 8x + 5x + x = 14x = 196.

questions.text: What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹240 in 3 years at 4% per year rate of interest?
What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹240 in 3 years at 8% per year rate of interest?
