markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: In a mixture of 60 litres, milk and water are in the ratio 7 : 3. If 3 litres of water be added, find the ratio of milk and water in the new mixture.
questions.explanation: The mixture has 42 litres of milk and 18 of water. With 3 more litres of water it is 42 : 21 = 2 : 1.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 8% per year rate of interest for 5 years.

Three red lights on the same road start blinking at the same time and blink repeatedly after every 4, 6 and 8 minutes, respectively. How many times will they blink together in an interval of 3 hours, excluding blinking together at the starting moment?
questions.explanation: They blink together every LCM(4, 6, 8) = 24 minutes. 180 ÷ 24 = 7.5, so 7 times in 3 hours after the start.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
A man sold an article for ₹247.50, thereby gaining 12.5%. The cost of the article (in ₹) was:
The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 70 kg and 35 kg is:
By selling an article for ₹20, a dealer makes a profit of 10%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹, rounded off to two decimal place) so as to make a profit of 40%?
questions.explanation: Cost price = 20/1.1. For a 40% profit he must sell at (20/1.1) × 1.4 = 28/1.1 = ₹25.45, an increase of ₹5.45.

questions.text: The average of the present ages of P and Q is 56 years and their ages are in the ratio 5:3. What will be the age of Q seven years hence?
questions.explanation: Their ages add up to 2 × 56 = 112, so Q is 3/8 × 112 = 42 now and 49 in seven years.

questions.text: The ratio of income to expenditure of a family is 18:15. Find the savings if the income of the family is ₹81,000.
questions.explanation: Savings are 18 − 15 = 3 of the 18 parts of income: 81,000 × 3/18 = ₹13,500.

questions.text: A car travels from Kanpur to Delhi at an average speed of 60 km/h and returns at an average speed of 90 km/h. Find the average speed of the car in the whole journey.
questions.explanation: Over equal distances the average speed is 2 × 60 × 90/(60 + 90) = 10,800/150 = 72 km/h.

questions.text: The average weight of three friends Ram, Ramesh and Shyam is 76 kg. Somesh joins them and the average weight of the four friends becomes 74 kg. If Mohan, whose weight is 2 kg more than that of Somesh replaces Ramesh, the average weight of Ram, Shyam, Somesh and Mohan becomes 68 kg. Find the weight of Ramesh.
questions.explanation: Ram + Ramesh + Shyam = 228 kg, and with Somesh 4 × 74 = 296, so Somesh is 68 kg and Mohan 70 kg. Ram + Shyam = 4 × 68 − 68 − 70 = 134, so Ramesh = 228 − 134 = 94 kg.

questions.text: A tunnel elevator can carry a maximum of 15 passengers with an average weight of 81 kg. However, four persons beyond the maximum capacity entered the elevator, resulting in an average weight of 82 kg and causing it to be overloaded. Find the average weight (in kg) of the additional four persons.
questions.explanation: 15 × 81 = 1,215 kg and 19 × 82 = 1,558 kg, so the four extra persons weigh 343 kg: 343 ÷ 4 = 85.75 kg each on average.

questions.text: In a 5-km race, A beats B by 750 metres and C by 1260 metres. By how many metres does B beat C in the same race?
questions.explanation: When A finishes 5,000 m, B has run 4,250 m and C 3,740 m. While B runs 5,000 m, C runs 3,740 × 5,000/4,250 = 4,400 m, so B wins by 600 m.

questions.text: The curved surface area of a cylinder is three-fifth of its total surface area. Find the ratio between the height and radius of the cylinder.
questions.explanation: 2πrh = (3/5) × 2πr(h + r) gives 5h = 3h + 3r, so 2h = 3r and h : r = 3 : 2.

questions.text: DFIE is related to CGHF in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, MOFC is related to LPED. To which of the following is GRRP related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The letters move −1, +1, −1, +1: D → C, F → G, I → H, E → F and M → L, O → P, F → E, C → D. So G → F, R → S, R → Q, P → Q: FSQQ.

questions.text: Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: No teacher is a male. No male is an Engineer. Conclusions: I. No teacher is an Engineer. II. Some male are teachers.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: Two negative statements give no definite conclusion about teachers and engineers, so I does not follow; and as no teacher is a male, II cannot follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'CHOSEN' is coded as ‘YTMIWN’ and 'COMMON' is coded as ‘YMOOMN’. How will 'CLIENT' be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: Each letter's place in the alphabet and its code's place add up to 28: C (3) → Y (25), H (8) → T (20), N (14) → N (14). So CLIENT → YPSWNH.

questions.text: 8 is related to 93 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 10 is related to 117. To which of the following is 14 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The number is multiplied by 12 and 3 taken away: 8 × 12 − 3 = 93 and 10 × 12 − 3 = 117. So 14 × 12 − 3 = 165.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘did we know’ is written as ‘kp as th’ and ‘we solve this’ is written as ‘nk kp bo’. How is ‘we’ written in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'we' is the only word in both sentences and 'kp' the only code in both, so we = kp.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? EBF, IGG, MLH, QQI ,?
questions.explanation: First letters move +4 (E, I, M, Q, U), second letters +5 (B, G, L, Q, V) and third letters +1 (F, G, H, I, J): UVJ.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘EACH’ is coded as ‘6138’ and ‘CAME’ is coded as ‘1396’. What is the code for ‘M’ in that language?
questions.explanation: E, A and C are in both words, as are 6, 1 and 3 in both codes. The letter left in CAME is M and the digit left in its code is 9, so M = 9.

questions.text: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. Select the pair in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the given pairs. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 6, 42; 9, 63
questions.explanation: The second number is 7 times the first: 6 × 7 = 42 and 9 × 7 = 63. Likewise 13 × 7 = 91.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 39, 47, 55, 63, 71, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 8 more than the one before: 71 + 8 = 79.

questions.text: Seven people P, U, L, M, A, G and E are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). P is sitting third to the left of M. G is sitting second to the right of M. Only one person is sitting between M and A when counted from the left of M. L is sitting to the immediate right of G. Only one person is sitting between L and E . Who is sitting to the immediate left of U?
questions.explanation: Counting to the right from M: M, E, G, L, P, A, U. G is second to the right of M and L to G's immediate right; P is third and A second to the left of M; E, with one person between it and L, takes the seat between M and G, and U the one left over. A is to U's immediate left.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘toy is new’ is coded as ‘bz tq gl’ and ‘give me toy’ is coded as ‘hx vm tq’. How is ‘toy’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'toy' is the only word in both sentences and 'tq' the only code in both, so toy = tq.

questions.text: T, U, V, W, X, and Y are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). U is sitting third to the right of V, who is sitting second to the left of W. Y is not an immediate neighbour of U. T is sitting to the immediate left of V. Who is sitting to the immediate left of T?
questions.explanation: Counting to the right from V: V, Y, W, U, X, T. W is second and U third to the right of V, and T to V's immediate left; Y, not beside U, takes the seat between V and W, and X the one between U and T. X is to T's immediate left.

questions.text: CA 19 is related to ID 14 in a certain way. In the same way, ML 53 is related to SO 48. To which of the following is GD 8 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: First letters move +6 (C → I, M → S), second letters +3 (A → D, L → O) and the number falls by 5 (19 → 14, 53 → 48). So GD 8 → MG 3.

questions.text: Read the given statement(s) and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: Some cups are glasses. No cup is a plate. Conclusions: (I) No glass is a plate. (II) Some glasses are not cups.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: The cups that are glasses are not plates, but other glasses may be, so I does not follow; and every glass may be a cup, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘÷’ and ‘−‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘+’ are interchanged? 12 × 96 − 24 + 8 ÷ 38 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 12 + 96 ÷ 24 × 8 − 38 = 12 + 32 − 38 = 6.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 56 − 33 × 3 ÷ 4 + 36 =?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 56 + 33 ÷ 3 × 4 − 36 = 56 + 44 − 36 = 64.

questions.text: The National Food Security Act (NFSA) was enacted in which year by the Government of India?
questions.explanation: The National Food Security Act, 2013 entitles up to 75% of the rural and 50% of the urban population to subsidised foodgrains.

questions.text: Prerana Shrimali received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in which of the following years for her contribution to the Kathak dance form?
questions.explanation: The Sangeet Natak Akademi gave Prerana Shrimali its award for Kathak for the year 2009.

questions.text: According to the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare 2022-23, which state of India is the largest producer of sugarcane?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh grows the most sugarcane in India, well ahead of Maharashtra and Karnataka.

questions.text: India won its first Olympic gold in hockey in which of the following years?
questions.explanation: India won its first Olympic hockey gold at Amsterdam in 1928, with Dhyan Chand its top scorer.

questions.text: As per HDI 2021, which of the following neighbouring countries of India had the highest female life expectancy at birth?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the Maldives, whose overall life expectancy at birth, 79.9 years, is the highest of these four countries in the UNDP's Human Development Report 2021-22.

questions.text: From 13 September 2023, DMK MP Tiruchi Siva has been appointed the chairperson of the Committee on _______________.
questions.explanation: When Parliament's standing committees were reconstituted with effect from 13 September 2023, Tiruchi Siva, a DMK member of the Rajya Sabha, was named chairperson of the Committee on Industry.

questions.text: Which of the following Rights is mentioned in Article 21 of the Indian Constitution?
options: Right against Exploitation: Prohibition of trafficking in human beings and forced labour
Right to Freedom of Religion: Freedom to manage religious affairs
Right to Freedom: Protection of life and personal liberty
Right to Equality: Equality before law
questions.explanation: Article 21, protection of life and personal liberty, is one of the Right to Freedom articles (19 to 22).

questions.text: How much money was allotted by the Gujarat government in August 2023 for the One District, One Product (ODOP) Programme to promote its indigenous products at the international level?
questions.explanation: Gujarat's ₹58 crore grant of August 2023 went to more than 25 handicraft products from 21 districts, among them Patan's Patola and Jamnagar's Bandhani.

questions.text: The Sahitya Akademi award winning novel ‘Zindaginama’ was written by:
questions.explanation: Krishna Sobti won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1980 for her Hindi novel 'Zindaginama'.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which among the following years was Hindu widow remarriage declared legal in India?
questions.explanation: The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856, championed by Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, made the remarriage of Hindu widows legal.

questions.text: Gabbro is an example of which type of rocks?
questions.explanation: Gabbro is a coarse-grained intrusive igneous rock, formed as magma cools slowly deep underground.

questions.text: The remains of Great Bath have been found from the excavation at which of the following Harappan sites?
questions.explanation: The Great Bath was found at Mohenjodaro, in Sindh.

questions.text: Which of the following peaks is NOT located in the Himalayan mountains?
questions.explanation: Kalsubai, the highest peak in Maharashtra, is in the Sahyadri (Western Ghats). Nanda Devi, Kamet and Annapurna are Himalayan peaks.

questions.text: Annapurna Devi is associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.explanation: Annapurna Devi, daughter of Ustad Allauddin Khan, was a celebrated player of the surbahar, the bass sitar.

questions.text: What is the length of the men's kabaddi court?
questions.explanation: A men's kabaddi court measures 13 m × 10 m; the women's is 12 m × 8 m.

questions.text: In the context of microfinance in India, the concept of SHG-BLP is used. What does L stand for in SHG-BLP?
questions.explanation: SHG-BLP is the Self Help Group-Bank Linkage Programme, begun by NABARD in 1992 to link self-help groups to bank credit.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who regarded Vedas as the source of all knowledge and known for the slogan ‘Go back to the Vedas’?
questions.explanation: Swami Dayanand Saraswati, who founded the Arya Samaj in 1875, held the Vedas to be the source of all true knowledge and called for a return to them.

questions.text: What is the retirement age of Judges serving at the Supreme Court of India?
questions.explanation: Under Article 124(2) a Supreme Court judge holds office until the age of 65; High Court judges retire at 62.

questions.text: Rigveda is the earliest specimen of:
questions.explanation: The Rigveda, composed in early Vedic Sanskrit, is among the oldest texts in any Indo-European language.

questions.text: The famous ‘Tripartite struggle’ for supremacy occurred between which of the following powers?
questions.explanation: The Gurjara-Pratiharas, the Rashtrakutas and the Palas fought for control of Kannauj from the 8th to the 10th century.

questions.text: Who among the following is worshipped as Nataraja before many classical dance performances in India?
questions.explanation: Nataraja, 'lord of dance', is Shiva in his form as the cosmic dancer.

questions.text: Chithirai festival of Tamil Nadu is dedicated to which of the following Goddesses?
questions.explanation: Madurai's Chithirai festival celebrates the marriage of the goddess Meenakshi to Sundareswarar (Shiva).

questions.text: Which gas is released when you combine vinegar and baking soda in a balloon, causing it to inflate?
questions.explanation: The acetic acid in vinegar reacts with sodium bicarbonate to release carbon dioxide, which fills the balloon.

questions.text: Four resistors of equal resistance R each are connected in various possible ways both in series and/or parallel to get different combined resistances. Which of the following values of resistance cannot be achieved by using all the four resistors?
questions.explanation: All four in series give 4R and all in parallel 0.25R; two in parallel plus two in series give 0.5R + 2R = 2.5R, and three in parallel plus one in series R/3 + R ≈ 1.33R. The nine values possible with all four are 4R, 2.5R, 1.67R, 1.33R, R, 0.75R, 0.6R, 0.4R and 0.25R, so 2R cannot be made.

questions.text: Which of the given options is rod-shaped, carries genetic information, is visible only at cell division and is present in the nucleus?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes, threads of DNA and protein in the nucleus, carry the genes and are seen as rod-shaped bodies only when the cell divides.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. They were / interested / on / learning new languages.
questions.explanation: 'Interested' takes 'in': 'They were interested in learning new languages.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The project “fell besides due to lack” of funding and support.
questions.explanation: To 'fall through' is to fail to happen: 'The project fell through due to lack of funding and support.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Sarah / will singing / at the concert / on Saturday.
questions.explanation: 'Will' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'Sarah will sing at the concert on Saturday.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. The White man had to swallow his bombast and “have completed the journey in mortified”.
questions.explanation: After 'had to' both verbs take the base form, and 'in' needs a noun: 'had to swallow his bombast and complete the journey in mortification'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the following word. Reluctant
questions.explanation: 'Reluctant' means unwilling or hesitant.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The management gave “kudos” to Jithin for his performance.
questions.explanation: 'Kudos' is praise for an achievement.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'colloquial'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The way she elaborated on every detail with precision impressed everyone _____ the meeting.
questions.explanation: Something happens 'at' a meeting: 'impressed everyone at the meeting'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. I hope that / yesterday's lunch / at Rahul's place / was at your liking.
questions.explanation: The idiom is 'to one's liking': 'I hope that yesterday's lunch at Rahul's place was to your liking.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The new intern was eager to learn the _________ of the corporate world.
questions.explanation: To 'learn the ropes' is to learn how a job is done or how things work.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. While she / was watched / the movie, / her phone rang.
questions.explanation: The action was in progress, so the past continuous active is needed: 'While she was watching the movie, her phone rang.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Hamper
questions.explanation: To 'hamper' is to 'hinder', to get in the way of something.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Panacea
questions.explanation: A 'panacea' is a remedy for all ills: a cure-all.

questions.text: Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined idiom in the given sentence. Everyone says that waking up early in the morning is beneficial for our health and overall well-being. But it is “easier said than done”.
options: to start performing better than before
not as easy as it seems to be
questions.explanation: 'Easier said than done' means harder than it sounds: not as easy as it seems.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate verb / verb phrase to fill in the blank. In 2030, advancements in technology ________________ the way we live, work and interact with each other.
questions.explanation: An action going on at a future time takes the future continuous, 'will be reshaping'; technology does the reshaping, so the passive forms do not fit, and the present perfect 'have reshaped' does not suit a future year.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. The flight was about to take off when suddenly the authorities came to ensure the record of the “maintanance” department.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'maintenance'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. During the meeting, the employer's _________ was clear as he calmly addressed each team member's concerns and provided insightful solutions.
questions.explanation: A possessive ('the employer's') must be followed by a noun: 'composure', calmness.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. The “lenient” ways of the manager prompted substandard work from his subordinates.
questions.explanation: 'Lenient' means tolerant and not strict: 'easygoing'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. My sister-in-law is the most succeeded for all the industrialists in this country today.
questions.explanation: The superlative of the adjective is needed, with 'of' for the group: 'the most successful of all the industrialists'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A phobia is an irrational fear of an object, situation or living thing. While fear is (1)_______ natural response to danger, phobias often occur (2)____________ response to something unlikely to cause real harm. Phobias are (5)______________ by significant distress and often cause a person to avoid the source of their fear or suffer from extreme anxiety when faced with it. Someone experiencing a phobia that is interfering with everyday life should consider undergoing treatment for their phobia, as outcomes for professional care are typically favourable.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Will' needs a verb, and one feels or 'experiences' fear: 'will experience intense fear and anxiety'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A phobia is an irrational fear of an object, situation or living thing. While fear is (1)_______ natural response to danger, phobias often occur (2)____________ response to something unlikely to cause real harm. In some cases, a person with a (3)___________ will meet the diagnostic criteria for a specific phobia, which is a type of anxiety disorder. Someone with a specific phobia will (4)_________ intense fear and anxiety when confronted with the source of the phobia, which could include blood, heights or specific animals like dogs. Phobias are (5)______________ by significant distress and often cause a person to avoid the source of their fear or suffer from extreme anxiety when faced with it. Someone experiencing a phobia that is interfering with everyday life should consider undergoing treatment for their phobia, as outcomes for professional care are typically favourable.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Phobias 'are characterised by', that is marked by, significant distress.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 65 kg and 38 kg is:

360 toffees are distributed among Pushkal, Quadir and Rustam in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. After distribution, Quadir gives 20% of his toffees to Pushkal and Rustam gives 25% of his toffees to Pushkal. What is the new ratio of toffees with Pushkal, Quadir and Rustam?
questions.explanation: The 360 toffees are first shared 80, 120 and 160. Pushkal then gets 20% of 120 = 24 and 25% of 160 = 40, so the shares become 144, 96 and 120 = 6 : 4 : 5.

questions.text: Reena sells an article at 12% below its cost price. Had she sold it for ₹540 more, she would have gained 15%. At what price should she sell the article to gain 20%?

A fast train takes 1 hour less than a slow train for a journey of 96 km. If the speed of the slow train is 8 km/h less than that of the fast train, then find the speeds of the fast train and slow train respectively.
questions.explanation: With the fast train at f km/h, 96/(f − 8) − 96/f = 1, so f² − 8f − 768 = 0 and f = 32. The slow train runs at 24 km/h: 96/24 − 96/32 = 4 − 3 = 1 hour.

questions.text: A car travels 80 km at the speed of 20 km/h and the next 30 km at the speed of 30 km/h. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: The car takes 80/20 + 30/30 = 5 hours for 110 km: 110/5 = 22 km/h.

questions.text: There are 40 students in a class. Their average weight is 60 kg. Two students left the class. Then the average weight is reduced by 500 g. Find the weight of the two students who left the class (in kg).
questions.explanation: The class weighed 40 × 60 = 2,400 kg; the 38 left weigh 38 × 59.5 = 2,261 kg. The two who left weighed 2,400 − 2,261 = 139 kg.

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 66 kg and 38 kg is:
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹4000 as a sum borrowed at 3% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
The centroid of a ∆XYZ is G. The area of ∆XYZ is 45 cm². The area of ∆GYZ is:
questions.explanation: The lines from the centroid to the vertices divide a triangle into three triangles of equal area, so ∆GYZ = 45/3 = 15 cm².

questions.text: A person got an article at 22% discount, if he got no discount, then he had to pay ₹1,760 more. How much did he pay (in ₹) for the article?
questions.explanation: The 22% discount is the ₹1,760 saved, so the marked price is 1,760/0.22 = ₹8,000 and he paid 78% of it: ₹6,240.

questions.text: By selling 20 cakes, a shopkeeper earns selling price of 4 cakes. Determine the profit percentage.
questions.explanation: The profit on 20 cakes is the selling price of 4, so their cost is the selling price of 16. Profit = 4/16 × 100 = 25%.

questions.text: R earns ₹55,000 per month and his annual expenditure is ₹4,50,000. What is his percentage of savings per annum?

The mean of marks secured by 3 students in grade A of class XI is 83, that of 4 students of grade B is 76 and that of 5 students of grade C is 85. What will be the mean of marks of the students of three grades of Class XI?
What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹240 in 2 years at 16% per year rate of interest?
The HCF of 513,1134 and 1215 is:
questions.explanation: 513 = 3³ × 19, 1134 = 2 × 3⁴ × 7 and 1215 = 3⁵ × 5. The highest common factor is 3³ = 27.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All pencils are remotes. Some pencils are ACs. Conclusions: [1] Some ACs are remotes. [2] All remotes are Acs.
questions.explanation: Some pencils are ACs, and every pencil is a remote, so those ACs are remotes: [1] follows. Nothing says every remote is an AC, so [2] does not.

questions.text: Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation mathematically correct? 15 × 14 – 8 + 12 ÷ 4 = 5

Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All leaves are trees. Some trees are plants. Conclusions: (I) Some leaves are plants. (II) All leaves are trees.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: 'All leaves are trees' is given, so II follows. The trees that are plants need not include any leaves, so I does not follow.

questions.text: A, B, C, L, M, Y and X are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only two people sit between B and L when counted from the right of L. X sits to the immediate left of Y. A sits to the immediate right of M. Y is an immediate neighbour of L. Who sits fourth to the right of C?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, going round to the right of L: L, M, A, B, C, X, Y. Y must be on L's left (on L's right, X would need L's seat), X to Y's left and B third to L's right, which leaves M then A in the two seats after L. Fourth to the right of C is M.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘÷‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘−’ are interchanged? 48 × 16 − 20 ÷ 21 + 7 = ?
In a certain code language, if HOUSE is coded as 67 and GROUND is coded as 83, then how will KITCHEN be coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter takes its position counted from Z (Z = 1, A = 26) and the values are added: HOUSE = 19 + 12 + 6 + 8 + 22 = 67 and GROUND = 20 + 9 + 12 + 6 + 13 + 23 = 83. KITCHEN = 16 + 18 + 7 + 24 + 19 + 22 + 13 = 119.

questions.text: ‘NQRP’ is related to ‘TWXV’ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, ‘FHIG’ is related to ‘LNOM’. To which of the following is ‘LOPN’ related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 6 places forward: N → T, Q → W, R → X, P → V, and FHIG → LNOM. So LOPN → RUVT.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question (?) in the following series? 4 ,-27, -58, -89 ,-120 ,?
questions.explanation: Each term is 31 less than the one before: −120 − 31 = −151.

questions.text: 16 is related to 176 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 21 is related to 231. To which of the following is 33 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 11: 16 × 11 = 176 and 21 × 11 = 231. So 33 × 11 = 363.

questions.text: L, M, N, O, P, Q and R are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Only three people are sitting between R and O when counted from the left of R. Only M is sitting between L and N. N is an immediate neighbour of O. P is sitting third to the right of L. Who is sitting second to the left of O?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, going round to the left of R: R, L, M, N, O, P, Q. With three seats between R and O on R's left, N next to O and only M between L and N, L, M and N must fill those three seats. P, third to L's right, is O's left neighbour, so Q is second to O's left.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of numbers. 48 : 42
questions.explanation: The product of the first number's digits plus 10 gives the second: 4 × 8 + 10 = 42. Likewise 6 × 3 + 10 = 28; the other pairs do not fit (48 would give 42, not 24; 69 gives 64 and 65 gives 40).

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? SXG, QVI, OTK, MRM ,?
questions.explanation: First letters move back 2 (S, Q, O, M, K), second letters back 2 (X, V, T, R, P) and third letters forward 2 (G, I, K, M, O): KPO.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘COPY’ is coded as ‘2846’ and ‘APES’ is coded as ‘7321’. What is the code for ’P’ in that language?
questions.explanation: P is the only letter in both words and 2 the only digit in both codes, so P = 2.

questions.text: MHPL is related to OJRN in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, PKSO is related to RMUQ. To which of the following is SNVR related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: MHPL → OJRN and PKSO → RMUQ. So SNVR → UPXT.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'MASTER' is coded as '917032', and 'STREAK' is coded as '372159'. What is the code for ‘K’ in 'STREAK'?
questions.explanation: MASTER and STREAK share S, T, R, E and A, and their codes share 9, 1, 7, 3 and 2. The letter left in STREAK is K and the digit left in its code is 5, so K = 5.

questions.text: 'Sange Meel Se Mulaqat' is the documentary of which famous musician?
questions.explanation: 'Sange Meel Se Mulaqat', made by Goutam Ghose, is a documentary on the shehnai maestro Ustad Bismillah Khan.

questions.text: Kaal Baisakhi belongs to which state from the following?
questions.explanation: Kalbaisakhi, 'the calamity of the month of Baisakh', is West Bengal's name for the violent evening thunderstorms (nor'westers) of the hot season.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is NOT true about Plastids?
options: Starch, oils and protein granules are stored in chromoplasts.
questions.explanation: Starch, oil and protein granules are stored in leucoplasts, the colourless plastids; chromoplasts hold pigments. Plastids do have their own DNA and ribosomes, and the chloroplast's matrix is the stroma.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT associated with the Iron Age in India?
questions.explanation: The Mehrauli iron pillar dates from the Gupta period (about AD 400), long after India's Iron Age. Iron smelting, Painted Grey Ware and Northern Black Polished Ware all belong to the Iron Age.

questions.text: Which of the following types of emergencies is declared under Article 360 of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 360 provides for a Financial Emergency; a National Emergency is declared under Article 352 and President's Rule in a state under Article 356.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is/are correct about the Union Government budget in India? a. The Budget reflects the vision of the government in fulfilling the aspirations of people. b. The Budget is the summary report of the financial performance of the government in power. c. The Budget provides details of expenditures meted out by various Union Government ministries.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives all three. The Union Budget sets out the government's priorities and details each ministry's expenditure; b is looser, as the Budget is chiefly a statement of estimates for the coming year, though it also reports the previous year's actual receipts and spending.

questions.text: Who among the following adopted the policy of consolidation in place of expansion by eliminating the rebels?
questions.explanation: Ghiyasuddin Balban chose to consolidate the Delhi Sultanate rather than expand it, crushing rebels and enemies with his policy of 'blood and iron'.

questions.text: Which material was largely used to build the stupa at Piprahwa in Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The stupa at Piprahwa, where a casket of Buddhist relics was found, is built of bricks.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following committees was set up to investigate into the infamous Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
questions.explanation: The Hunter Committee (the Disorders Inquiry Committee) was set up in 1919 to inquire into the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

questions.text: In the animal kingdom, which of the following phyla includes animals with a segmented body?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Annelida, the phylum of ring-segmented worms such as the earthworm, whose bodies show metameric segmentation. Arthropods have segmented bodies too, so Arthropoda is also arguable; molluscs are not segmented.

questions.text: Which edition of the Pro Kabaddi League was started in December 2023?
questions.explanation: The 10th season of the Pro Kabaddi League began on 2 December 2023.

questions.text: Which of the following war dances is performed in Ngada festival and is a performed by the tribes of Nagaland?
questions.explanation: Ngada is the harvest festival of the Rengma Nagas, and the Rengma war dance is performed during it. Jawara is from Madhya Pradesh, Dalkhai from Odisha and Garadi from Puducherry.

questions.text: A ______ happens in chess when a player gives up material during the initiation to seek some kind of compensation.
questions.explanation: A gambit is an opening in which a player sacrifices material, usually a pawn, for compensation such as faster development or the initiative. Castling is a move of the king and a rook.

questions.text: Two masses of 1 kg and 2 kg were dropped from a height of 3.2 metres. Their respective velocities just before touching the ground will be: (Assume acceleration due to gravity g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Without air resistance every body falls with the same acceleration, whatever its mass: v = √(2gh) = √(2 × 10 × 3.2) = √64 = 8 m/s for both.

questions.text: _________was launched by the Government of India in 2020 to make the country and its citizens independent and self-sufficient in all respects.
questions.explanation: The Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan (self-reliant India campaign) was announced in May 2020.

questions.text: ‘The Namesake’, ‘Unaccustomed Earth’ and ‘The Lowland’ are novels written by who among the following authors?
questions.explanation: 'The Namesake' and 'The Lowland' are Jhumpa Lahiri's novels, and 'Unaccustomed Earth' is her collection of short stories.

questions.text: In June 2023, which country conferred the ‘Order of the Nile’ award on Narendra Modi?
questions.explanation: Egypt conferred the Order of the Nile, its highest state honour, on Narendra Modi during his visit to Cairo in June 2023.

questions.text: How many components are there in the New India Literacy Program (NILP) scheme launched by the Union Ministry of Education in March 2023?
questions.explanation: The New India Literacy Programme has five components: foundational literacy and numeracy, critical life skills, basic education, vocational skills development and continuing education.

questions.text: From which of the following countries has the Indian Constitution borrowed the concept of the Concurrent List?
questions.explanation: The Concurrent List was borrowed from the Australian Constitution, as was the joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament.

questions.text: According to National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023 (A Progress Review), what was the proportion of population in multidimensional poverty (Headcount Ratio) in urban India in 2019-2021?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023 puts urban India's headcount ratio at 5.27% in 2019-21, down from 8.65% in 2015-16.

questions.text: When is the National Unity Day celebrated in India?
questions.explanation: National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas) is observed on 31 October, the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

questions.text: The igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks are interconvertible through a continuous process called:
questions.explanation: The rock cycle is the continuous process by which igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks change into one another.

questions.text: Mallika Sarabhai was honoured with the Padma Bhushan in 2010 for her contribution to which of the following fields?
questions.explanation: Mallika Sarabhai, a Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam dancer, received the Padma Bhushan in 2010 for her work in dance.

questions.text: In which of the followings years was the National Population Policy of India released?
questions.explanation: India's National Population Policy was released in 2000, with the long-term aim of a stable population by 2045.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options: A teacher from South explained the theory in the detailed manners.
The teacher from an South explained a theory in a detailed manner.
The teacher from the South explained the theory in a detailed manner.
The teacher from a South explained the theory in the detailed manner.
questions.explanation: A region takes the definite article, 'the South', and 'in a detailed manner' is the set phrase; 'an South' and 'the detailed manners' are wrong.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The CEO came up with a groundbreaking strategy to _______________ new markets and capitalise on emerging trends.
questions.explanation: To 'break into' a market is to enter it successfully; 'break down', 'break off' and 'break out' mean collapse, stop and erupt.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment without changing its meaning in the given sentence. Family planning programs play a crucial role in promoting reproductive health and empowering individuals to make informed choices, “contributing to sustainable population growth” and a healthier society.
questions.explanation: 'Promoting a viable population increase' keeps the meaning: 'viable' matches 'sustainable' and 'increase' matches 'growth'. 'Explosion', 'unbalanced' and 'discouraging' change the sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank. They needed a __________ answer for every question.
questions.explanation: Nothing is being compared, so the positive degree 'precise' fits after 'a'; 'preciser' is not standard English.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Haste
questions.explanation: 'Haste' is hurry; its opposite is 'delay'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. The walls of the marriage hall were “covered by” beautiful purple curtains.
questions.explanation: A surface is 'covered with' the material that covers it: 'covered with beautiful purple curtains'.

questions.text: Based on the situation in the given sentence, select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment. Having known to the facts, the manager “disregarded the arguments of” the customer.
questions.explanation: To 'turn a deaf ear' to something is to refuse to listen to it, which is what the manager did.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'Pamper' from the given sentence. I always feel that nuclear families always mollycoddle their kids without directing them to the correct path or denying their unrealistic demands.
questions.explanation: To 'mollycoddle' is to pamper or overindulge.

questions.text: Select the sentence that contains a spelling error.
options: He has made significant improvement in the last few weeks.
Despite his formidable appearance, he possesses a kind heart.
They had been disgrantled with the company due to various reasons.
We saw a pride of lions nonchalantly roaming in the forest.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'disgruntled'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Vigorous
questions.explanation: 'Vigorous' means strong and active: 'energetic'.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the underlined word. She has a “magnificient” personality.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'magnificent'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. He was able to do _____(tedious) jobs and hence decided to be in the airline service, which demanded 12 long hours of service.
questions.explanation: 'Tedious' means dull and tiresome; its opposite is 'delightful'. 'Irksome' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Change the following sentence into positive degree. Yash is not better than Harsh.
options: Yash is as good as Harsh.
Yash is not good than Harsh.
Yash and Harsh both are good.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'Yash is as good as Harsh', the usual positive-degree form of 'not better than' (strictly, 'not better' also allows 'worse'). 'Not good than' and 'best than' are ungrammatical, and 'both are good' drops the comparison.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. The children were excited to ride the “carusel.”
questions.explanation: The standard spelling is 'carousel' ('carrousel' is a less common variant).

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. If 2023 was ___ year consumers helped stave off a recession with an unexpected surge in spending, many economists _________ 2024 will be the time shoppers finally tighten their belts.
questions.explanation: 'The year' points to a particular year, defined by the clause that follows, and economists 'predict' what 2024 will bring.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. Playing ‘hide-n-seek’ is the one of the “fond” memories of my childhood.
questions.explanation: 'One of the' is followed by a superlative: 'one of the fondest memories'. 'Most fondest' is a double superlative.

questions.text: The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with a grammatical error. I left my / coat in the / hospital when I / had visit Alex.
questions.explanation: 'Had' needs the past participle, not the base form: 'when I visited Alex' or 'had visited', not 'had visit'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The old man shared his __________ wisdom with the young generation.
questions.explanation: 'Sagacious' means wise and shrewd, which suits an old man's wisdom; 'frivolous', 'ephemeral' and 'trivial' do not.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Contrary
questions.explanation: 'Contrary' means opposite in nature; its opposite is 'similar'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Clear as mud
questions.explanation: 'Clear as mud' is said ironically of something not clear at all: very difficult to understand.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. We should remember that all religions (1)________ good conduct in life, the foundation of which should rest on (2)_________. Without the basis of morality, philosophy would remain mere polemics, and religion would be (3)_________ and vain. Nobody can say that he is religious unless he is (4)_________ and unselfish. It is realised that by constant endeavour through thought, word and deed, one could (5)_________ absolute peace of mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: All religions 'preach', that is teach and urge, good conduct in life.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. We should remember that all religions (1)________ good conduct in life, the foundation of which should rest on (2)_________. Without the basis of morality, philosophy would remain mere polemics, and religion would be (3)_________ and vain. Nobody can say that he is religious unless he is (4)_________ and unselfish. It is realised that by constant endeavour through thought, word and deed, one could (5)_________ absolute peace of mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Good conduct should rest on 'ethics', moral principles, which the next sentence calls 'the basis of morality'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. We should remember that all religions (1)________ good conduct in life, the foundation of which should rest on (2)_________. Without the basis of morality, philosophy would remain mere polemics, and religion would be (3)_________ and vain. Nobody can say that he is religious unless he is (4)_________ and unselfish. It is realised that by constant endeavour through thought, word and deed, one could (5)_________ absolute peace of mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Without morality religion would be 'meaningless' and vain, as philosophy would be mere polemics.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. We should remember that all religions (1)________ good conduct in life, the foundation of which should rest on (2)_________. Without the basis of morality, philosophy would remain mere polemics, and religion would be (3)_________ and vain. Nobody can say that he is religious unless he is (4)_________ and unselfish. It is realised that by constant endeavour through thought, word and deed, one could (5)_________ absolute peace of mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Being religious goes with being 'truthful' and unselfish.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. We should remember that all religions (1)________ good conduct in life, the foundation of which should rest on (2)_________. Without the basis of morality, philosophy would remain mere polemics, and religion would be (3)_________ and vain. Nobody can say that he is religious unless he is (4)_________ and unselfish. It is realised that by constant endeavour through thought, word and deed, one could (5)_________ absolute peace of mind.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Constant endeavour is how one gains something, so one could 'acquire' absolute peace of mind; 'scatter', 'forfeit' and 'divide' go against the sense.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 9% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
Raju sold 4 laptops at a rate of ₹1,54,005 all together and incurred a loss of 25%. At what rate should he sell the laptops to gain a profit of 25%?
questions.explanation: The cost price is ₹1,54,005 ÷ 0.75 = ₹2,05,340. For a 25% profit he must sell the laptops for ₹2,05,340 × 1.25 = ₹2,56,675.

questions.text: A vendor wants to gain 25% by adding water to milk and selling the mixture at the cost price. Find the ratio of water and milk in the mixture.
questions.explanation: Selling at cost price, all the gain comes from the water: to gain 25% he must sell 125 litres for the price of 100 litres of milk, so water : milk = 25 : 100 = 1 : 4.

questions.text: A sum of ₹2,380 is lent out into two parts, one at 25% p.a. and another at 20% p.a. . If the total annual income is ₹500, find the money (in ₹) lent at 25% rate.
The highest common factor of 84 and 108 is:
questions.explanation: 84 = 2² × 3 × 7 and 108 = 2² × 3³; the common factors give 2² × 3 = 12.

questions.text: What is the area of the remaining portion of a circle of radius 14 cm when a square with maximum possible area inscribed in it is removed from it? (Use π= 22/7)
questions.explanation: The circle's area is (22/7) × 14² = 616 cm². The largest inscribed square has the diameter, 28 cm, as its diagonal, so its area is 28²/2 = 392 cm². 616 − 392 = 224 cm².

questions.text: The speed of a boat in still water is 15 km/h and the speed of the current is 3 km/h. How much distance (in km) can be covered going downstream in 12 minutes?
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = 15 + 3 = 18 km/h; in 12 minutes (1/5 hour) the boat covers 18/5 = 3.6 km.

questions.text: A person travels equal distances with speeds of 3 km/hr, 4 km/hr and 8 km/hr, respectively, and takes a total of 425 minutes. What is the total distance (in km) travelled?
questions.explanation: With each part d km: d/3 + d/4 + d/8 = 17d/24 hours = 425/60 hours, so d = 10 and the total distance is 3 × 10 = 30 km.

questions.text: The marked price of a folding bed is ₹18,000. Aman bought it after two successive discount of 15% and 10%. He spent ₹830 on transportation and sold it for ₹18,440. Find his profit.

A hemispherical bowl is 264 cm round at the brim. Suppose that the bowl is half-full of beverage. If the beverage is served in hemispherical glasses 6 cm in the diameter at the top, how many people would be served?
questions.explanation: 2πr = 264 gives the bowl's radius as 42 cm. Half its volume is ½ × (2/3)π × 42³ = 24,696π cm³, and each glass holds (2/3)π × 3³ = 18π cm³, so 24,696π ÷ 18π = 1372 people are served.

questions.text: If the volume and surface area of a sphere are numerically the same, then find the volume (in cm³) of its semi − sphere. (correct to two places of decimals, use π = 3.14)
questions.explanation: (4/3)πr³ = 4πr² gives r = 3 cm. The hemisphere's volume is (2/3)π × 3³ = 18π = 18 × 3.14 = 56.52 cm³.

questions.text: The average age of 12 men is increased by 6 years when three of them, whose ages are 36, 40 and 44 years, are replaced by 3 persons. What is the average age of the 3 persons?
questions.explanation: The total rose by 12 × 6 = 72 years. The three men replaced total 36 + 40 + 44 = 120 years, so the three newcomers total 192: an average of 64 years.

questions.text: If the cash difference between the selling price of an item at a gain of 3% and 6% is ₹9, which of the following options is the correct ratio between the selling prices?
questions.explanation: At gains of 3% and 6% the selling prices are 1.03 and 1.06 times the cost price, so their ratio is 103 : 106 whatever the cost (here ₹300, since 3% of it is ₹9).

questions.text: The average age of a group of 32 women is 60 years and that of another group of 40 men is 33 years. The average age of the two groups mixed together is:

In a student council election, there were three contestants. All the voters participated in the voting and 10% of votes were declared invalid. The contestants got the votes in the ratio 8 : 7 : 5. If the second candidate in the list got 4725 votes, the total number of valid votes is:
questions.explanation: The second candidate's 7 parts are 4725 votes, so one part is 675. The valid votes are 8 + 7 + 5 = 20 parts: 20 × 675 = 13,500.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 6% per year rate of interest for 4 years.

Two vessels, A and B, contain spirit and water in the ratio 3 : 4 and 5 : 3, respectively. Find the ratio in which these two mixtures be mixed to obtain a new mixture in vessel C containing spirit and water in the ratio 4 : 3.
questions.explanation: Spirit is 3/7 of A, 5/8 of B and must be 4/7 of the mixture. By alligation A : B = (5/8 − 4/7) : (4/7 − 3/7) = 3/56 : 8/56 = 3 : 8.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘MOVE’ is coded as ‘3917’ and ‘EAST’ is coded as ‘4692’. What is the code for ‘E in the given code language?
questions.explanation: E is the only letter in both MOVE and EAST, and 9 the only digit in both 3917 and 4692, so E = 9.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All planets are rocks. All rocks are lakes. Conclusions: (I) All planets are lakes. (II) All rocks are planets.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: All planets are rocks and all rocks are lakes, so all planets are lakes (I). Nothing says every rock is a planet, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Seven friends, Kamala, Raveena, Amruta, Nisha, Gautami, Bhavana and Triveni, are sitting in a circular dining table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Raveena is sitting second to the right of Nisha. Gautami has Kamala and Triveni as immediate neighbours. Triveni is sitting third to the left of Nisha. Amruta is not an immediate neighbour of Nisha. Who is seated fourth to the left of Bhavana?
questions.explanation: Triveni is third to Nisha's left and Raveena second to her right. Gautami and Kamala cannot both fit in the one seat between Triveni and Raveena, so going left from Nisha come Kamala, Gautami, Triveni; Amruta cannot sit beside Nisha, so she takes the seat after Triveni and Bhavana is on Nisha's right. Four seats to Bhavana's left: Nisha, Kamala, Gautami, Triveni.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘father makes tea’ is coded as ‘ib fx ey’ and ‘tea and coffee’ is coded as ‘kr ey wn’. How is ‘tea’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'tea' is the only word in both sentences and 'ey' the only code in both, so tea = ey.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 8 + 2 – 1 × 1 ÷ 1 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 8 − 2 + 1 ÷ 1 × 1 = 8 − 2 + 1 = 7.

questions.text: M, N, O, P, Q and R are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). N sits to the immediate right of R. M sits second to the right of N. P sits second to the right of M. O sits third to the right of P. Who sits to the immediate right of Q?
questions.explanation: Going round to the right from R: N, O, M, Q, P. M is second to N's right and P second to M's right; O, third to P's right, takes the seat between N and M, which leaves Q between M and P. P is to Q's immediate right.

questions.text: PLRN is related to QMSO in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, LHNJ is related to MIOK. To which of the following is HDJF related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: P → Q, L → M, R → S, N → O. So HDJF → IEKG.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘×’ are interchanged and ‘÷’ and ‘−’ are interchanged? 15 ÷ 5 + 8 − 4 × 7 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 15 − 5 × 8 ÷ 4 + 7 = 15 − 10 + 7 = 12.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 24, 73; 27, 82
questions.explanation: The second number is three times the first plus 1: 24 × 3 + 1 = 73 and 27 × 3 + 1 = 82. Likewise 33 × 3 + 1 = 100.

questions.text: 519 is related to 781 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 642 is related to 904. To which ofthe following is 485 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting / multiplying etc., to 13 canbe performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is related to itself plus 262: 519 + 262 = 781 and 642 + 262 = 904. So 485 + 262 = 747.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? GGB, HHD ,IKH, JPN, ?
questions.explanation: First letters run G, H, I, J, so next is K; second letters move +1, +3, +5 (G, H, K, P), so next is P + 7 = W; third letters move +2, +4, +6 (B, D, H, N), so next is N + 8 = V: KWV.

questions.text: FI29 is related to TW49 in a certain way. In the same way, LO38 is related to ZC58. To which of the following is RU65 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 14 places forward (wrapping round after Z) and the number rises by 20: F → T, I → W, 29 → 49 and L → Z, O → C, 38 → 58. So R → F, U → I and 65 → 85: FI85.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following series? 1,17, 33, 49, 65 ,?
questions.explanation: Each term is 16 more than the one before: 65 + 16 = 81.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘GIFT’ is coded as ‘5197’ and ‘FIST’ is coded as ‘4157’. What is the code for ‘S’ in that language?
questions.explanation: GIFT and FIST share I, F and T, and 5197 and 4157 share 1, 5 and 7. The letter left in FIST is S and the digit left in its code is 4, so S = 4.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FLOAT’ is coded as ‘14238’ and ‘BLOAT’ is coded as ‘23849’. What is the code for ‘F’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: FLOAT and BLOAT share L, O, A and T, and 14238 and 23849 share 2, 3, 4 and 8. The letter left in FLOAT is F and the digit left in its code is 1, so F = 1.

questions.text: The sister of Harshavardhana Rajyashri was married to___________, the king of Maukhari dynasty of Kanyakubja.
questions.explanation: Rajyashri, Harshavardhana's sister, was married to Grahavarman, the Maukhari king of Kanauj (Kanyakubja).

questions.text: Sarhul is an agricultural festival of tribals, which is primarily celebrated in the Indian state of ________.
questions.explanation: Sarhul, a spring festival in which the blossoms of the sal tree are worshipped, is celebrated mainly by the tribes of Jharkhand.

questions.text: Which of the following states had benefitted by the Indira Gandhi Canal?
questions.explanation: The Indira Gandhi Canal, which starts at the Harike Barrage in Punjab, carries water into the Thar Desert of western Rajasthan.

questions.text: What is Cash Reserve Ratio?
options: Percentage of deposits that a bank must keep as cash reserves with the central bank
Percentage of deposits that a bank must keep as cash reserves with any bank
Percentage of deposits that a central bank must keep as cash reserves with the government
Percentage of deposits that a central bank must keep as cash reserves with the bank
questions.explanation: The Cash Reserve Ratio is the share of its deposits that a bank must keep as cash with the central bank (in India, the Reserve Bank of India).

questions.text: Which of the following mountain peaks is a part of the Himalayas?
questions.explanation: Kamet (7,756 m) is in the Garhwal Himalaya of Uttarakhand. Kalsubai and Taramati are in the Western Ghats of Maharashtra, and Dhupgarh is the highest point of the Satpura range.

questions.text: What is the primary gas responsible for the leavening effect in bread when yeast ferments sugars?
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments sugars into alcohol and carbon dioxide; the bubbles of carbon dioxide make the dough rise.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT related to goals of Fundamental Duties of Indian Citizens?
questions.explanation: Article 51A asks citizens to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals, the National Flag and the National Anthem, to cherish the ideals of the freedom struggle and to value and preserve the country's heritage; 'courage' is not among the duties.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following signed a pact with Lord Irwin on March 5, 1931?
questions.explanation: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact, signed on 5 March 1931, ended the first phase of the Civil Disobedience Movement, and Gandhi went on to attend the Second Round Table Conference.

questions.text: The digestive enzymes inside lysosomes are made by:
questions.explanation: The digestive enzymes in lysosomes are proteins made by the rough endoplasmic reticulum.

questions.text: ________was well known for creating fusion art by adapting European theatrical techniques to Indian classical dance combined with Indian folk and tribal dance.
questions.explanation: Uday Shankar created a fusion style of dance, adapting European theatrical techniques to Indian classical dance with elements of folk and tribal dance.

questions.text: Which of the following is the style of temple architecture that is widely favoured in northern India?
questions.explanation: The Nagara style, with its curving shikhara, prevails in northern India; the Dravida style is the south's.

questions.text: In the inaugural year of the Nehru Cup event for football in 1982, which team emerged as the winner of the first edition?
questions.explanation: Uruguay won the first Nehru Cup, held in Kolkata in 1982, beating China in the final.

questions.text: S Abdul Nazeer was appointed as the Governor of _______ in February 2023.
questions.explanation: S. Abdul Nazeer, a retired Supreme Court judge, was appointed Governor of Andhra Pradesh in February 2023.

questions.text: Who was the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India for the 2011 Indian Census?
questions.explanation: Dr C. Chandramouli was the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India for the 2011 Census.

questions.text: Which team won the Women's Asian Hockey Champions Trophy in 2023?
questions.explanation: India won the 2023 Women's Asian Champions Trophy at Ranchi, beating Japan 4-0 in the final.

questions.text: According to Census 2011, what is the sex ratio of India?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 recorded 943 females per 1,000 males in India.

questions.text: 'My Country My Life' is the autobiography of:
questions.explanation: 'My Country My Life' (2008) is the autobiography of L. K. Advani.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following systems was the charge of collecting the revenue and paying it to the Company given to the village headman, rather than the zamindar?
questions.explanation: Under the Mahalwari system, introduced in the North-Western Provinces in 1822, the village headman collected the revenue of the whole village (mahal) and paid it to the Company.

questions.text: Helium gas can be converted to the liquid form by the _______.
questions.explanation: Helium atoms are non-polar, so the only forces between them are weak London (dispersion) forces; these are what let helium be liquefied.

questions.text: Which Tamil superstar founded the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) political party in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry on 2 February 2024 with the slogan 'Pirappokkum Ellaa Uyirkkum' (All are equal by birth)?
questions.explanation: The actor Vijay launched Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam on 2 February 2024. Kamal Haasan's party is Makkal Needhi Maiam, founded in 2018.

questions.text: A river is capable of forming which of the following landscapes when the river is in its middle course?
questions.explanation: In its middle course a river flows over gentler slopes and swings from side to side in meanders. V-shaped valleys and waterfalls belong to the upper course, deltas to the mouth.

questions.text: Kalamandalam Krishnan Nair was a notable figure in which of the following classical dance forms of India?
questions.explanation: Kalamandalam Krishnan Nair was one of the great Kathakali artists of Kerala.

questions.text: Pandit Arvind Thatte belongs to which of the following gharanas?
questions.explanation: The harmonium player Arvind Thatte, a disciple of Pandit Jasraj since 1981, belongs to Jasraj's Mewati gharana.

questions.text: Who was the famous Venetian traveller of the 13th century who visited Kerala?
questions.explanation: Marco Polo of Venice visited the Malabar coast of Kerala late in the 13th century. Nicolo Conti was a 15th-century Venetian, Varthema (Barthema) came from Bologna in the 16th century, and Abdur Razzaq was a 15th-century Persian envoy.

questions.text: Who among the following is the ex-officio Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha as on 10 October 2023?
questions.explanation: The Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha; Jagdeep Dhankhar has held the office since August 2022.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank School classrooms have _________ very little over the last century.
questions.explanation: Classrooms have 'changed' very little: the sentence is about how little they have altered in a century.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He is waiting / at airport to receive / Mr. Smith, who is / coming from South Africa.
questions.explanation: A particular airport takes the article: 'He is waiting at the airport'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He cheated in the [A] / examination, making his [B] / already-falling academic [C] / credentials worst. [D]
questions.explanation: 'Making his credentials worse' needs the comparative: credentials that were already falling became 'worse', not 'worst'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Entice
questions.explanation: To 'entice' is to attract or tempt; its opposite is to 'repulse', to drive away.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. He “gnashed his teeth” at his son's actions.
questions.explanation: To 'gnash one's teeth' is to show anger or rage.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. The new almirah is “big” than this one.
questions.explanation: A comparison with 'than' takes the comparative: 'bigger than this one'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank. We are entering a point where technology will change at __________ speeds.
questions.explanation: 'Extreme' is spelt correctly; the others should be 'inferior', 'moderate' and 'supreme'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Run errands
options: To go out to buy or do something
To participate in a race through unfair means
To finish running before the end point
To do something incorrectly or erroneous in haste
questions.explanation: To 'run errands' is to make short trips to buy or do things, often for someone else.

questions.text: Identify the ODD word from the given options.
questions.explanation: Carom, table tennis and billiards are indoor games played on a table or board; golf is played outdoors on a course.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Leisure activities can improve an individual's physical and mental health by ________ stress, and offering a pleasurable experience.
questions.explanation: Leisure improves health by 'relieving', that is easing, stress.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. My friend, / Priya looks more cheerful today / as she celebrates her birthday.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct as it stands: 'Priya looks' agrees, 'more cheerful today' compares her with her usual mood, and 'as she celebrates' gives the reason.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Conscious
questions.explanation: 'Conscious' means aware; its opposite is 'unaware'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains anerror in phrasal verb. Tina dropped behind of / college and / went straight / into a good job.
questions.explanation: To leave college before finishing is to 'drop out of' it: 'Tina dropped out of college'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. The rivals in the institution _____ (fabricated) evidence and manipulated the whole dataset.
questions.explanation: 'Fabricated' evidence is 'forged': made up to deceive.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. The concert was “canceeled” due to rain.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'cancelled'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'endangered'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate degree of comparison to fill in the blank. Many ornithologists believe that the northern mocking birds are __________ wild birds in the jungle.
questions.explanation: A comparison with all the wild birds in the jungle takes the superlative: 'the noisiest'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. Our _____ conducted a _____ to get everyone's opinion.
questions.explanation: The head of a school is the 'principal' (a 'principle' is a rule), and a survey of opinion is a 'poll' (a 'pole' is a post).

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. Arun asks Smita to copy the contents of the document “word by word”.
questions.explanation: To copy something exactly, in the same words, is to copy it 'word for word'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM to substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. In what ways do you find technological advancements “beneficial” to your daily life?
questions.explanation: 'Beneficial' means helpful or advantageous; of the options only 'unfavourable' is opposite in meaning.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Dolphins 1_________ regarded as the friendliest creatures in the sea, and stories of them helping drowning sailors have been common since Roman times. The more we 2____________ about dolphins, the more we realise that their society is more complex 3__________ people previously imagined. They look 4____________ other dolphins when they are ill, care for pregnant 5___________ and protect the weakest in the community, as we do.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The plural subject takes 'are': 'Dolphins are regarded as the friendliest creatures'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Dolphins 1_________ regarded as the friendliest creatures in the sea, and stories of them helping drowning sailors have been common since Roman times. The more we 2____________ about dolphins, the more we realise that their society is more complex 3__________ people previously imagined. They look 4____________ other dolphins when they are ill, care for pregnant 5___________ and protect the weakest in the community, as we do.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'The more we learn about dolphins, the more we realise': the present tense, like 'realise'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Dolphins 1_________ regarded as the friendliest creatures in the sea, and stories of them helping drowning sailors have been common since Roman times. The more we 2____________ about dolphins, the more we realise that their society is more complex 3__________ people previously imagined. They look 4____________ other dolphins when they are ill, care for pregnant 5___________ and protect the weakest in the community, as we do.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'More complex' is followed by 'than'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Dolphins 1_________ regarded as the friendliest creatures in the sea, and stories of them helping drowning sailors have been common since Roman times. The more we 2____________ about dolphins, the more we realise that their society is more complex 3__________ people previously imagined. They look 4____________ other dolphins when they are ill, care for pregnant 5___________ and protect the weakest in the community, as we do.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: To 'look after' is to take care of: dolphins look after others when they are ill.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Dolphins 1_________ regarded as the friendliest creatures in the sea, and stories of them helping drowning sailors have been common since Roman times. The more we 2____________ about dolphins, the more we realise that their society is more complex 3__________ people previously imagined. They look 4____________ other dolphins when they are ill, care for pregnant 5___________ and protect the weakest in the community, as we do.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Dolphins care for pregnant 'mothers'; the other options are all male.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 67 kg and 36 kg is:
