At what rate percent per annum on simple interest will ₹760 amount to ₹912 in 5 years?

Trader A gives a single discount of 45% and Trader B gives two successive discounts of 35% and 10% on an identical item of the same marked price. If the discount given by A is ₹539 more than the discount given by Trader B, then what is the marked price (in ₹) of the item?
questions.explanation: B's two discounts leave 0.65 × 0.9 = 0.585 of the price: a single discount of 41.5%. A's 45% is 3.5% more, so 3.5% of the marked price is ₹539 and the price is ₹15,400.

questions.text: 141 is divided into two parts in such a way that the one-eighth part of the first and one-ninth part of the second are in the ratio 5 : 6. Find the first part.
questions.explanation: x/8 : y/9 = 5 : 6 gives 6x/8 = 5y/9, so x : y = 20 : 27. 141 in 47 parts is 3 a part, so the first part is 60.

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 66 kg and 35 kg is:
Anil sells sugar at cost price but uses false weights and thus makes 20% profit. How many grams of sugar does he give in 1 kilogram?
questions.explanation: Selling at cost price, his 20% profit comes from giving less: he charges for 1000 g but gives 1000/1.2 = 833.33 g.

questions.text: A car can cover 275 km in 5 hours. If its speed is reduced by 5 km/h, then how much time will the car take to cover a distance of 250 km?
questions.explanation: Speed = 275/5 = 55 km/h. Reduced to 50 km/h, 250 km takes 250/50 = 5 hours.

questions.text: The radius of a cylinder is doubled due to which the volume of the new cylinder also gets doubled. The height of the new cylinder is what percentage of the old cylinder?
questions.explanation: V = πr²h. With the radius doubled, π(2r)²H = 2πr²h, so 4H = 2h and H = h/2: 50% of the old height.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹4000 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
By selling an article for ₹20, a dealer makes a profit of 10%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹, rounded off to two decimal place) so as to make a profit of 50%?
questions.explanation: Cost = 20/1.1 = ₹18.18. For a 50% profit the price must be 1.5 × 18.18 = ₹27.27, an increase of ₹7.27.

questions.text: The largest number that can divide 147,183 and 271 leaving remainders 11,13 and 16, respectively, is:
A hemispherical bowl with diameter 14 cm has to be painted inside and outside. How much it will be charged at the rate of ₹20 per 40 cm²?
questions.explanation: Inside and outside together are twice the curved surface: 2 × 2πr² = 4 × (22/7) × 7² = 616 cm². At ₹20 per 40 cm², that is ₹0.50 a cm²: 616 × 0.5 = ₹308.

questions.text: The number of heads on the farm, as determined by the farmer, was 60. When he counted, he discovered there were 150 legs. If all that was present were pigeons or horses, and every horse on the property had four legs while every pigeon had two, how many horses were there on the property?
questions.explanation: If all 60 were pigeons there would be 120 legs. Each horse adds 2 more, and there are 30 more: 15 horses.

questions.text: The average of seven consecutive numbers is 95. Find the middle number in the series of seven consecutive numbers.
questions.explanation: In an odd run of consecutive numbers the middle number equals the average: 95.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 6% per year rate of interest for 5 years.
A 240 m long train crosses a man walking at a speed of 4.5 km/h in the opposite direction in 12 seconds. What is the speed (in km/h) of the train?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 240/12 = 20 m/s = 72 km/h. Moving towards each other their speeds add, so the train runs at 72 − 4.5 = 67.5 km/h.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 14 ÷ 7 − 27 × 9 + 12 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 14 × 7 + 27 ÷ 9 − 12 = 98 + 3 − 12 = 89.

questions.text: 14 is related to 93 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 6 is related to 37. To which of the following is 11 related, following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is 7 times the first minus 5: 14 × 7 − 5 = 93 and 6 × 7 − 5 = 37. So 11 × 7 − 5 = 72.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘like my pet’ is written as ‘nj kj lk’ and ‘pet is wet’ is writtenas ‘lk mk bt’. How is ‘pet’ writtenin the given language?
questions.explanation: 'pet' is the only word in both sentences and 'lk' the only code in both, so pet = lk.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some lights are fans. Some fans are beds. Conclusions: (I) Some lights are beds. (II) All beds are fans.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusion I and II follow
questions.explanation: Two 'some' statements give no definite link between lights and beds, so I does not follow; 'some fans are beds' does not make all beds fans, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 10 , 99; 21, 440
questions.explanation: In each pair the second number is the square of the first minus 1: 10² − 1 = 99 and 21² − 1 = 440. Likewise 30² − 1 = 899.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘bring hot food’ is coded as ‘ud lp sj’ and ‘food is tasty’ is coded as ‘sj xk jt’. How is ‘food’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'food' is the only word in both sentences and 'sj' the only code in both, so food = sj.

questions.text: EX04 is related to ZS16 in a certain way. In the same way, UN06 is related to PI36. To which of the following is WP07 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 5 places back (E → Z wrapping round, X → S) and the number is squared (4 → 16; 6 → 36). So W → R, P → K and 7 → 49: RK49.

questions.text: What should come in place of ‘?’ in the given series? 16, 8.5, 9.5, 15.75, 33.5, ?

Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the center (but not necessarily in the same order). F is sitting fourth to the right of D. E is sitting second to the left of F. B is sitting to the immediate left of G. A is not an immediate neighbour of F. How many people are sitting between C and D when counted from the right of D?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, right is anticlockwise. Going right from D the seats are D, A, E, C, F, B, G: F is fourth to D's right, E second to F's left, B to G's immediate left, and A, kept away from F, takes the seat next to D. From D rightwards to C, A and E sit between: two.

questions.text: A, B, P, Q, Y and Z are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Q sits to the immediate left of B. Y sits to the immediate right of B. A sits second to the right of B. P sits second to the right of A. Who sits third to the right of Z?
questions.explanation: Going right (anticlockwise) from B the seats are B, Y, A, Z, P, Q, which puts Q to B's immediate left. Third to the right of Z: P, Q, then B.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘good bright boy’ is coded as ‘xd yf vj’ and ‘boy is lazy’ is coded as ‘sb xd ql’. How is ‘boy’ coded in the given language?
questions.explanation: 'boy' is the only word in both sentences and 'xd' the only code in both, so boy = xd.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All roses are lilies. Some lilies are sunflowers. Conclusions: (I): Some roses are sunflowers. (II): All lilies are roses.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: The lilies that are sunflowers need not be roses, so I does not follow; all roses being lilies does not make all lilies roses, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: What should come in place of question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? XJP, VMN, TPL, RSJ, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move back 2 (X, V, T, R, P), second letters forward 3 (J, M, P, S, V) and third letters back 2 (P, N, L, J, H): PVH.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'BUY' is writtenas ‘ACTVXZ’ and 'CAP' is writtenas ‘BDZBOQ’. How will 'BOX' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as the letters just before and after it: B → AC, U → TV, Y → XZ. So BOX → AC NP WY: ACNPWY.

questions.text: GYEV is related to DBBY in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, XHVE is related to UKSH. To which of the following is LTJQ related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The letters move −3, +3, −3, +3: G → D, Y → B (wrapping round), E → B, V → Y. So L → I, T → W, J → G and Q → T: IWGT.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 5 ÷ 4 − 3 × 1 + 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 5 × 4 + 3 ÷ 1 − 2 = 20 + 3 − 2 = 21.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an example of a ‘Lagoon’?
questions.explanation: Chilika and Pulicat are coastal lagoons, and Kolleru, between the Krishna and Godavari deltas, began as one. Nainital is a freshwater lake in the Kumaon Himalaya, far from the sea.

questions.text: Sekrenyi festival of Nagaland is celebrated annually in the month of ______ as part of the Mini Hornbill Tribal Festival which is a celebration of purification accompanied with feasting and singing.
questions.explanation: Sekrenyi, the Angami Nagas' festival of purification, is celebrated in February.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following social organisations was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875?
questions.explanation: Swami Dayananda Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875.

questions.text: Purushottam Dadheech, a renowned Kathak dancer who had been honoured with Padma Shri award for 2020, is associated with which of the following places?
questions.explanation: Purushottam Dadheech, a Kathak guru from Madhya Pradesh, received the Padma Shri in 2020.

questions.text: What was the amount earned by BCCI from the sale of five teams in the inaugural Women’s Indian Premier League (WPL) in January 2023?
questions.explanation: The five Women's Premier League franchises sold for a combined ₹4,669.99 crore in January 2023.

questions.text: As on February 2024, Yanthungo Patton is the Deputy Chief Minister of which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Yanthungo Patton has been Deputy Chief Minister of Nagaland since 2018.

questions.text: Which of the following is a mineral deficiency disease?
questions.explanation: Goitre is caused by a lack of iodine, a mineral. Scurvy and rickets come from a lack of vitamins C and D, and marasmus from a lack of protein and energy.

questions.text: What does WFI stand for in the context of sports?
questions.explanation: WFI is the Wrestling Federation of India, the national body for the sport.

questions.text: Which of the following options has all vector quantities?
options: Force, Velocity, Momentum, Weight and Acceleration
Force, Velocity, Momentum, Energy and Power
Power, Momentum, Energy, Speed and Work
Force, Velocity, Momentum, Energy and Acceleration
questions.explanation: Force, velocity, momentum, weight (a force) and acceleration all have direction as well as size. Energy, power, speed and work are scalars.

questions.text: According to Article _____, there shall be equality of opportunities for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment to any office under the State.
questions.explanation: Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity for all citizens in public employment.

questions.text: The name of the autobiography of Saina Nehwal is called:
options: Playing to win, my life on and off court
questions.explanation: Saina Nehwal's autobiography is 'Playing to Win: My Life... On and Off Court' (2012). 'Straight from the Heart' is Kapil Dev's, 'Playing It My Way' Sachin Tendulkar's and 'Unbreakable' Mary Kom's.

questions.text: Which event brought about a profound change in Ashoka’s administrative policy?
questions.explanation: The bloodshed of the Kalinga War led Ashoka to give up conquest by war for rule by dhamma.

questions.text: While estimating Gross Domestic Product, the monetary value of only final goods are considered because ___________. a. its immobility, the active economic flow is ended. b. of the issues of double counting c. the value added at each stage of the production process is included
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives only b: counting intermediate goods as well would count their value twice. (Statement c makes a closely related point, since a final good's value already includes the value added at each stage, so 'b and c' is arguable.)

questions.text: The model of 'Quasi Federal' form of government in Indian constitution is borrowed from which country?
questions.explanation: The federation with a strong Centre, which makes India's Constitution quasi-federal, was borrowed from Canada.

questions.text: Dappu dance is a famous dance form of which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Dappu is a folk dance of Andhra Pradesh, performed to the beat of the dappu drum.

questions.text: With reference to ‘slash and burn’ agriculture, which of the following names is NOT related to Odisha?
questions.explanation: NCERT gives Pama Dabi, Koman and Bringa as Odisha's names for slash and burn farming. Roca is its name in Brazil.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Under which of the following Acts, was Warren Hastings appointed as the Governor-General of Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Regulating Act of 1773 created the post of Governor-General of Bengal, and Warren Hastings was the first to hold it.

questions.text: The Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram was built during the reign of the _________ king Narasimhavarman II.
questions.explanation: The Shore Temple was built under the Pallava king Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha).

questions.text: Epilepsy is a disorder that affects which of the following parts of the human body?
questions.explanation: Epilepsy is a disorder of the brain: bursts of abnormal electrical activity in brain cells cause seizures.

questions.text: In the PM-SVANidhi Scheme (2020), the urban street vendors are eligible to avail a Working Capital Loan up to 10,000 with a tenure of:
questions.explanation: PM SVANidhi's first working capital loan, up to ₹10,000, is repaid over one year in monthly instalments.

questions.text: Sahaswan gharana of Rampur was established by whom among the following personalities?
questions.explanation: Ustad Inayat Hussain Khan founded the Rampur-Sahaswan gharana of Hindustani vocal music.

questions.text: Mica is which type of mineral?
questions.explanation: Mica is a non-metallic mineral, valued in the electrical and electronics industries for its insulating properties.

questions.text: In its 279th report released in April 2023, the Law Commission of India has recommended the provision of which law to be retained?
questions.explanation: The Law Commission's 279th report, on the law of sedition, recommended keeping Section 124A of the IPC, with amendments.

questions.text: National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was passed in which of the following years?
questions.explanation: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was passed in 2005 and came into force in 2006.

questions.text: The architectural marvels, temples of Gangaikonda-Cholapuram, were built by which of the following king?
questions.explanation: Rajendra Chola I built Gangaikonda Cholapuram as his new capital, with its great temple, after his campaign to the Ganga.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'explanation'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined phrase. This “sentence can have multiple meanings”. Could you please specify what it means?
questions.explanation: Something that can be understood in more than one way is 'ambiguous'. 'Homogeneous' means all of one kind, 'amorphous' shapeless and 'heterogeneous' made up of different kinds.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence. My mother asked me “who did accompany me” to the airport.
questions.explanation: A reported question takes statement form, with no auxiliary 'did', and its verb in the past after 'asked': 'who accompanied me'. 'Must accompanied' and 'accompany' are the wrong forms, and 'whom I was accompanied' makes no sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Restraint
questions.explanation: 'Restraint' is holding oneself back: 'self-control'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym for the given word. Fusion
questions.explanation: 'Fusion' is the joining of things into one: a 'blend'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word. The new syllabus of Final Semester of MBA is very “difficult”.
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'difficult' is 'easy'.

questions.text: The given sentence is divided into four parts. One of them contains a grammatical error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. He was acquitted to / a cyber crime / on the basis of evidence / given to the court.
questions.explanation: One is 'acquitted of' a charge or crime: 'He was acquitted of a cyber crime'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The situation was “out of hand”. So, the manager called the police station for help.
questions.explanation: 'Out of hand' means out of control: 'uncontrollable'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Foremost
questions.explanation: 'Foremost' means most important; its opposite is 'unimportant'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. One of the “most horrified serials” of the Indian television industry was broadcast twenty years ago.
questions.explanation: 'Horrifying' describes what causes horror; 'horrified' describes the person who feels it. 'One of the' takes a superlative: 'most horrifying serials'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. This is going to be overwhelming for you as you have “taken on work beyond your capabilities”.
options: bitten off more than you can chew
questions.explanation: To 'bite off more than you can chew' is to take on more than you can manage.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. His decision to quit his stable job and travel the world was driven by a sudden “caprice”.
questions.explanation: A 'caprice' is a sudden change of mind: an 'impulse'.

questions.text: Select the option that has an error in the use of phrasal verb.
options: Pushpa came across an old photo in the album and asked me to recognise the face in it.
Please suggest me some tips to get out nervousness.
Back up your essential files. Technology is only sometimes reliable.
Please turn up the heater. The weather is too cold today .
questions.explanation: To overcome something is to 'get over' it: 'tips to get over nervousness'. 'Came across', 'back up' and 'turn up' are used correctly.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The gold watch / look really expensive / and is not affordable / for common people.
questions.explanation: The subject 'The gold watch' is singular, so 'looks really expensive'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. She is studying / the medicine / at university / to become a doctor.
questions.explanation: A subject of study takes no article: 'She is studying medicine'.

questions.text: Rectify the following sentence by selecting the correct spelling of the underlined word from the options. Life is a collection of “ephmeral” moments.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'ephemeral', lasting a very short time.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. It has been / noticed that / across all his faults, / he is admired.
questions.explanation: 'Across' makes no sense here; the sense needs 'despite' (or 'for'): 'despite all his faults, he is admired'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Bilingual children are “so intelligent than” those who speak just one language.
questions.explanation: 'Than' follows a comparative, and the comparative of 'intelligent' is 'more intelligent': 'more intelligent than'.

questions.text: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. Leif Erikson is a Viking ________ believed to have sailed from the Green Lands to Vinland. Vinland is now thought to be the northern tip of Canada's Newfoundland island where ________ found evidence of Erikson's ________ in 1960s.
questions.explanation: A Viking who sailed to new lands is an 'explorer', and evidence of his 'settlement' is what 'archaeologists' would find.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The newspaper is one of the significant signs of (1) ________ civilisation. It is the most popular form of reading in the (2) ________ times because it interests all sorts of people. It is full of political news, sports and commercial news, as well as articles by well-known writers. A newspaper keeps us (3) ______ entertained and informed. In these days of democracy, public opinion rules everywhere. (4) ________ government can long withstand the pressure of a strong public opinion. It is, therefore, quite clear that the press controls public opinion, and public opinion, in turn, controls the government. Ultimately, the press controls the government. It acts as an interpreter between the government and the people and brings the rulers and the ruled (5) ________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The newspaper is a sign of 'modern' civilisation, of the present age. 'Prehistoric' and 'ancient' point to the distant past, and 'monolithic' (made of one block) does not fit.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The newspaper is one of the significant signs of (1) ________ civilisation. It is the most popular form of reading in the (2) ________ times because it interests all sorts of people. It is full of political news, sports and commercial news, as well as articles by well-known writers. A newspaper keeps us (3) ______ entertained and informed. In these days of democracy, public opinion rules everywhere. (4) ________ government can long withstand the pressure of a strong public opinion. It is, therefore, quite clear that the press controls public opinion, and public opinion, in turn, controls the government. Ultimately, the press controls the government. It acts as an interpreter between the government and the people and brings the rulers and the ruled (5) ________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'In the present times' means nowadays: the passage says the newspaper is the most popular form of reading today.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The newspaper is one of the significant signs of (1) ________ civilisation. It is the most popular form of reading in the (2) ________ times because it interests all sorts of people. It is full of political news, sports and commercial news, as well as articles by well-known writers. A newspaper keeps us (3) ______ entertained and informed. In these days of democracy, public opinion rules everywhere. (4) ________ government can long withstand the pressure of a strong public opinion. It is, therefore, quite clear that the press controls public opinion, and public opinion, in turn, controls the government. Ultimately, the press controls the government. It acts as an interpreter between the government and the people and brings the rulers and the ruled (5) ________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Both' pairs with 'and': 'keeps us both entertained and informed'. 'Either' would need 'or', and 'nor' needs 'neither'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The newspaper is one of the significant signs of (1) ________ civilisation. It is the most popular form of reading in the (2) ________ times because it interests all sorts of people. It is full of political news, sports and commercial news, as well as articles by well-known writers. A newspaper keeps us (3) ______ entertained and informed. In these days of democracy, public opinion rules everywhere. (4) ________ government can long withstand the pressure of a strong public opinion. It is, therefore, quite clear that the press controls public opinion, and public opinion, in turn, controls the government. Ultimately, the press controls the government. It acts as an interpreter between the government and the people and brings the rulers and the ruled (5) ________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'No government can long withstand' strong public opinion: hence, as the passage goes on, the press controls the government.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The newspaper is one of the significant signs of (1) ________ civilisation. It is the most popular form of reading in the (2) ________ times because it interests all sorts of people. It is full of political news, sports and commercial news, as well as articles by well-known writers. A newspaper keeps us (3) ______ entertained and informed. In these days of democracy, public opinion rules everywhere. (4) ________ government can long withstand the pressure of a strong public opinion. It is, therefore, quite clear that the press controls public opinion, and public opinion, in turn, controls the government. Ultimately, the press controls the government. It acts as an interpreter between the government and the people and brings the rulers and the ruled (5) ________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: To bring people 'together' is to unite them: the press brings the rulers and the ruled together.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: A man covers the first half of the journey at the speed of 60 km/h and the remaining at the speed of 84 km/h. What is his average speed (in km/h)?
questions.explanation: For two equal distances the average speed is 2 × 60 × 84/(60 + 84) = 10,080/144 = 70 km/h.

questions.text: The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 66 kg and 37 kg is:

A person has to cover a distance of 8 km in 1 hour. If he covers one-fourth of the distance in one-third of the total time, then what should his speed (in km/h) be to cover the remaining distance in the remaining time so that the person reaches the destination exactly on time?
questions.explanation: One-fourth of 8 km is 2 km, covered in 20 minutes. The other 6 km must take the remaining 40 minutes (2/3 hour): 6 ÷ 2/3 = 9 km/h.

questions.text: A man bought a bullock and a cart for ₹10,000. He sold the bullock at a gain of 30% and the cart at a loss of 20%, thereby gaining 2% on the whole. Find the cost of the bullock.
The mean of the first 8 odd natural numbers is:
questions.explanation: The first n odd numbers add up to n², so the first 8 add up to 64 and their mean is 64/8 = 8.

questions.text: A closed cylindrical tank of height 280 cm and base radius 70 cm is to be made from a metal sheet. The required sheet for the same, in m², is:
questions.explanation: A closed cylinder needs 2πr(h + r) = 2 × 22/7 × 70 × (280 + 70) = 1,54,000 cm² of sheet, which is 15.4 m².

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 3% per year rate of interest for 2 years.

In view of Diwali, Rajnee, an electronics shop owner, offers a discount scheme to her customers that on buying 15 decorative bulbs, they get 5 decorative bulbs free. What is the effective percentage discount given by Rajnee to her customers?
questions.explanation: The customer pays for 15 bulbs and gets 20, so 5 of every 20 are free: 5/20 = 25%.

questions.text: The price of 24 movie tickets is ₹768. How much (in ₹) will 32 movie tickets cost? [Assume that all tickets here are equally priced]
questions.explanation: One ticket costs 768 ÷ 24 = ₹32, so 32 tickets cost 32 × 32 = ₹1,024.

questions.text: 2 kg of copper at ₹15 per kg is mixed with 3 kg of zinc at ₹20 per kg. Find the average price of the mixture.
A man spends 12% of his income on food, 18% on children’s education, and 70% of the remaining on house rent. What percentage of his income is he left with?
questions.explanation: Food and education take 30%, leaving 70%. Rent takes 70% of that, 49% of the income, so 70 − 49 = 21% is left.

questions.text: How many kilograms of tea, costing ₹250 per kg must be mixed with 25 kg of tea costing ₹400 per kg so that there may be a profit of 10% on selling the mixture at ₹330 per kg?
questions.explanation: To gain 10% at ₹330, the mixture must cost 330/1.1 = ₹300 a kg. By alligation the teas at ₹250 and ₹400 go in the ratio (400 − 300) : (300 − 250) = 2 : 1, so 2 × 25 = 50 kg of the cheaper tea.

questions.text: Find the greatest number that exactly divides 12, 24 and 40.
questions.explanation: The greatest number dividing all three is their HCF: 12 = 2² × 3, 24 = 2³ × 3 and 40 = 2³ × 5, so the HCF is 2² = 4.

questions.text: NGMI is related to LEKG in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, QJPL is related to OHNJ. To which of the following is TMSO related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places back: N → L, G → E, M → K, I → G, and QJPL → OHNJ likewise. So TMSO → RKQM.

questions.text: 49 is related to 96 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 54 is related to 106. To which ofthe following is 36 related following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 canbe performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is twice the first minus 2: 49 × 2 − 2 = 96 and 54 × 2 − 2 = 106. Likewise 36 × 2 − 2 = 70.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 52 + 44 − 38÷ 2 + 13× 4 − 26 = 97 (Note: Interchange should be done of entire number and not individual digits of a given number)
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? ABC, EFG, IJK, MNO ,?
questions.explanation: The clusters start at A, E, I and M, four letters apart, each followed by the next two letters. The next starts at Q: QRS.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘All men fight’ is coded as ‘AO EI UH’ and ‘men shave everyday’ is coded as ‘MN TP EI’. How is ‘men’ coded in that code language?
questions.explanation: 'men' is the only word in both sentences and 'EI' the only code in both, so men = EI.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: A. No caps are hats. B. Some hats are helmets. Conclusions: I. All helmets are caps. II. Some helmets are hats.
questions.explanation: No cap is a hat, so the helmets that are hats cannot be caps: I does not follow. 'Some hats are helmets' gives 'some helmets are hats' (II).

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. [6/5], [3/2], [9/5],[21/10], [12/5], ?
questions.explanation: In tenths the terms are 12/10, 15/10, 18/10, 21/10 and 24/10, rising by 3/10 each time, so the next is 27/10.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘CURD’ is coded as ‘2436’ and ‘DOGS’ is coded as ‘3719’. What is the code for ‘D’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: D is the only letter in both words and 3 the only digit in both codes, so D = 3.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘find the key’ is written as ‘so hd sm’ and ‘key to success’ is writtenas ‘gj so la’. How is ‘key’ writtenin the given language?
questions.explanation: 'key' is the only word in both sentences and 'so' the only code in both, so key = so.

questions.text: HPML is related to MURQ in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, CJGF is related to HOLK. To which of the following is RZWV related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 5 places forward, wrapping round after Z: H → M, P → U, M → R, L → Q, and CJGF → HOLK likewise. So R → W, Z → E, W → B and V → A: WEBA.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘HOME’ is coded as ‘7519’ and ‘MUST’ is coded as ‘6782’. What is the code for ‘M’ in that language?
questions.explanation: M is the only letter in both words and 7 the only digit in both codes, so M = 7.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). C sits second to the left of E, who is third to the left of A. G sits third to the right of B, who is not an immediate neighbour of F. D sits second to the right of B. How many people sit between D and A when counted from the left of D?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left is clockwise. The only seating that fits is, clockwise from A: A, G, D, E, B, C, F (E third to A's left, C second to E's left, D second and G third to B's right, and B between E and C, away from F). Counting leftwards from D: E, B, C and F come before A, so four people sit between them.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 2 ÷ 70 × 2 – 30 + 30 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 2 × 70 ÷ 2 + 30 − 30 = 70 + 30 − 30 = 70.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 27, 109; 31, 125
questions.explanation: The second number is four times the first plus 1: 27 × 4 + 1 = 109 and 31 × 4 + 1 = 125. Likewise 36 × 4 + 1 = 145.

questions.text: Eight friends, J, K, L, M, N, O, P and Q are sitting around a round table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). K is an immediate neighbour of both Q and M. N is an immediate neighbour of both P and J. L is sitting immediately right to J. K is sitting at the immediate left of Q and is second to the right of O. Who is sitting to the immediate right of M?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left is clockwise. Clockwise the order is K, M, O, L, J, N, P, Q: K is immediately left of Q and second to the right of O, with M as its other neighbour; L sits to J's right and N between J and P. The person to M's immediate right is K.

questions.text: A person having stunted growth and discoloured hair is most probably suffering from ________________.
questions.explanation: Stunted growth and discoloured hair are signs of kwashiorkor, caused by a lack of protein in the diet.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was the chief guest of India's first Republic Day in 1950?
questions.explanation: Sukarno, the first President of Indonesia, was the chief guest at India's first Republic Day on 26 January 1950.

questions.text: Which of the following dance forms is primarily associated with Eastern India states like Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal?
questions.explanation: Chhau is performed in three styles named after their homes: Mayurbhanj in Odisha, Seraikela in Jharkhand and Purulia in West Bengal.

questions.text: In the case of reptiles, their heart is not properly divided in to four chambers i.e., it consists of two auricles and an incompletely divided ventricle. Which of the following is an example of a reptile having a four-chambered heart?
questions.explanation: Crocodiles are the exception among reptiles: their heart has four fully separated chambers.

questions.text: Maitraka dynasty was founded in which part of India?
questions.explanation: The Maitraka dynasty was founded by Bhatarka in Saurashtra (Gujarat), with Valabhi as its capital: western India.

questions.text: Which of the following is the autobiography of Bhishma Sahni?
questions.explanation: 'Aaj Ke Ateet' is the autobiography of the Hindi writer Bhisham Sahni, author of 'Tamas'; it was published after his death.

questions.text: Which of the following crops is grown in the Kharif season in India?
questions.explanation: Soyabean is sown with the monsoon rains and harvested in autumn: a kharif crop. Barley and mustard are rabi crops, and cucumber is grown in the short zaid season.

questions.text: Samrat Choudhary and Vijay Kumar Sinha became the Deputy Chief Minister of ________________ on 28 January 2024.
questions.explanation: Samrat Choudhary and Vijay Kumar Sinha of the BJP became Bihar's Deputy Chief Ministers when Nitish Kumar was sworn in again as Chief Minister with BJP support on 28 January 2024.

questions.text: Which of the following was the first Regional Rural Bank of India?
questions.explanation: Prathama Bank, set up at Moradabad in Uttar Pradesh on 2 October 1975 with Syndicate Bank as its sponsor, was India's first Regional Rural Bank.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following years was the 'Quit India Movement' launched?
questions.explanation: The Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942 at the Bombay session of the All India Congress Committee.

questions.text: The elements that are liquid at room temperature (25°C) are:
questions.explanation: Bromine and mercury are the only elements that are liquid at 25°C; chlorine and helium are gases.

questions.text: Sonu Nigam was awarded the Padma Shri in 2022 for which of the following fields?
questions.explanation: The playback singer Sonu Nigam received the Padma Shri in 2022 in the field of Art.

questions.text: In which year was the Multi-dimensional Poverty Index launched in India?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog released India's National Multidimensional Poverty Index, a baseline report, in November 2021.

questions.text: For transporting water from one place to another, some man-made structures used to distribute water to a place far away are known as:
questions.explanation: Aqueducts are man-made channels or bridges that carry water over long distances. An aquifer is a water-bearing layer of rock; an aquiclude holds water but does not let it flow, and an aquifuge neither holds nor passes it.

questions.text: Valabhi type of Nagara temples are generally ___________ in shape, with a roof that rises into a vaulted chamber.
questions.explanation: Valabhi-type Nagara temples are rectangular buildings whose roof rises into a vaulted chamber.

questions.text: Which team won the Ultimate Kho-Kho League Season 2 event?
questions.explanation: Gujarat Giants won Season 2 of Ultimate Kho Kho, beating Chennai Quick Guns 31-26 in the final at Cuttack in January 2024.

questions.text: Who was the chairman of the drafting committee of the Constituent Assembly of India?
questions.explanation: Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly; Rajendra Prasad was the Assembly's President.

questions.text: Who among the following was the first Indian representative in modern Olympics?
questions.explanation: Norman Pritchard competed for India at the 1900 Paris Olympics and won two silver medals in athletics.

questions.text: Which of the following awards is NOT sponsored by the Madhya Pradesh government?
questions.explanation: The Tagore Ratna was a one-time honour of the Sangeet Natak Akademi, the national academy, marking Tagore's 150th birth anniversary. The Devi Ahilya, Kishore Kumar and Tulsi Samman are Madhya Pradesh government awards.

questions.text: The Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur iron ore belt lies in which of the following groups of states?
questions.explanation: The Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur iron ore belt lies in Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra; the Bailadila hills of Bastar are part of it.

questions.text: Which Articles of the Constitution of India provide for a parliamentary form of government at the Centre?
questions.explanation: Articles 74 and 75 (a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the President, collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha) set up the parliamentary system at the Centre; Articles 163 and 164 do so in the states.

questions.text: Article __________ A supplements the 11th fundamental duty of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 86th Amendment (2002) added Article 21A, the right to free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14, and the 11th Fundamental Duty, Article 51A(k), for parents to provide them opportunities for education.

questions.text: Who among the following founded the Saluva dynasty of Vijayanagara empire?
questions.explanation: Saluva Narasimha Deva Raya, a general who took the throne from the last Sangama kings, founded the Saluva dynasty, the second of Vijayanagara's four dynasties.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word(s) in the given sentence. Manik said that it is mandatory that “each student pay” his/her tuition fees every month.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'each student pays': 'each student' is singular and takes a singular verb. Formal English also allows the subjunctive 'pay' after 'it is mandatory that', as the sentence has it, but there is no 'no substitution' option; 'paid', 'students' and 'paids' are wrong.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. The microscopic chip that emits a uniqe signal has been embedded into your arm.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'unique'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'fulfil' ('fulfill' in American English).

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. I want to buy the “less” expensive bike, but with the best mileage.
questions.explanation: The bike is chosen from all bikes, not between two, so the superlative is needed, matching 'the best mileage': 'the least expensive bike'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who rules with absolute power and authority
questions.explanation: A dictator is a ruler with absolute power and authority.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Bheem has been shown in the popular culture as someone who “eats in large quantity”.
questions.explanation: To 'eat like a horse' is to eat a great deal; to 'eat like a bird' is to eat very little.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Benevolent
questions.explanation: 'Benevolent' means well-meaning and kind.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that has a grammatical error. The thieves had no alternative / but to acquiesce with / the orders of / the police.
questions.explanation: 'Acquiesce' takes 'in' (or 'to'), not 'with': 'but to acquiesce in the orders of the police'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The most effective way to enhance your vocabulary is to “look to” unknown words in a dictionary.
questions.explanation: To 'look up' a word is to search for it in a dictionary.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Once the seminar was over, the host “gave up” the certificates to the active participants.
questions.explanation: To 'give away' prizes or certificates is to hand them out; to 'give up' is to stop or surrender.

questions.text: Rectify the error in the given sentence by selecting the correct spelling from the options provided. The nights of King Arthur were known for their chivalry.
questions.explanation: A knight is a mounted soldier of noble rank; 'nights' only sounds the same.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The teacher asked us to ___________ the main idea of the passage in the exam.
questions.explanation: To 'summarise' is to state the main idea briefly; 'conclusion' is a noun and cannot follow 'to'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Careful
questions.explanation: 'Careful' means taking care to avoid harm: 'cautious'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. He is known for his “humility”.
questions.explanation: 'Humility' is modesty; its opposite is 'pride'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Poonam used a rubber band to keep the pencils together. 'Band' here means ____________.
options: a long rigid piece of wood or metal
a range of values or frequencies within a series
a thin ring of rubber used for holding things together
questions.explanation: A rubber band is a thin ring of rubber used to hold things together.

questions.text: Select the appropriate option that can substitute the underlined idiom in the given sentence. The entire audience “was all ears” when the Indian-born American economist started giving a speech.
options: was willing to exit the show
was arguing in favour of both sides
questions.explanation: To be 'all ears' is to listen eagerly.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Despite the challenges,/ they ultimate achieved / their goal of launching / their startup.
questions.explanation: 'Achieved' is a verb, so it needs the adverb 'ultimately', not the adjective 'ultimate'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The head coach declared that the player “who will score the most points” in the game will clinch the trophy this year.
options: who have score the maximum points
who were score the maximum points
questions.explanation: In a clause about the future that depends on another future ('will clinch'), English uses the simple present: 'the player who scores the maximum points'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Three big fat rats once found a new use for _____1_____ tails. During the night, they came ______2_____ into the larder and found a jar with treacle in it. But the jar had a ____3___ neck, and try as they might, the rats could not reach the treacle either with their mouths or their paws. At last, a bright idea ______4______ one of them. He climbed onto the jar and let his tail hang down into the treacle. Then he pulled it out nicely coated with treacle and allowed the two rats to lick it _____5_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The tails belong to the rats, so the possessive 'their' is needed: 'a new use for their tails'. 'There' is an adverb and 'it's' means 'it is'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Three big fat rats once found a new use for _____1_____ tails. During the night, they came ______2_____ into the larder and found a jar with treacle in it. But the jar had a ____3___ neck, and try as they might, the rats could not reach the treacle either with their mouths or their paws. At last, a bright idea ______4______ one of them. He climbed onto the jar and let his tail hang down into the treacle. Then he pulled it out nicely coated with treacle and allowed the two rats to lick it _____5_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The rats came 'creeping' into the larder at night, moving slowly and quietly.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Three big fat rats once found a new use for _____1_____ tails. During the night, they came ______2_____ into the larder and found a jar with treacle in it. But the jar had a ____3___ neck, and try as they might, the rats could not reach the treacle either with their mouths or their paws. At last, a bright idea ______4______ one of them. He climbed onto the jar and let his tail hang down into the treacle. Then he pulled it out nicely coated with treacle and allowed the two rats to lick it _____5_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The rats could not reach the treacle because the jar had a 'narrow' neck.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. But the jar had a ____3___ neck, and try as they might, the rats could not reach the treacle either with their mouths or their paws. At last, a bright idea ______4______ one of them. He climbed onto the jar and let his tail hang down into the treacle. Then he pulled it out nicely coated with treacle and allowed the two rats to lick it _____5_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: An idea 'strikes' someone when it comes suddenly into their mind: 'a bright idea struck one of them'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Three big fat rats once found a new use for _____1_____ tails. During the night, they came ______2_____ into the larder and found a jar with treacle in it. But the jar had a ____3___ neck, and try as they might, the rats could not reach the treacle either with their mouths or their paws. At last, a bright idea ______4______ one of them. He climbed onto the jar and let his tail hang down into the treacle. Then he pulled it out nicely coated with treacle and allowed the two rats to lick it _____5_______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The two rats licked the treacle 'off' the tail.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Ravi goes to college from his village at the speed of 5km/h and returns at the speed of 4km/h. If he takes 9 hours in all, find the distance (in km) between the village and the college.
questions.explanation: Time = d/5 + d/4 = 9d/20 = 9 hours, so d = 20 km.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 5 years.

A borrows ₹89,500 for 3 years at 7% p.a. simple interest. B borrows the same amount at simple interest of 9% for the first year, 8% for the second year, and 7% for the third year. What is the total simple interest (in ₹) paid by A and B?

Two trains running towards each other on parallel tracks, at speeds of 45 km/hr and 51 km/hr, take 21 seconds to cross each other. If the length of one train is 290 m, then the length (in m) of the other train is:
questions.explanation: Moving towards each other, the relative speed is 45 + 51 = 96 km/h = 80/3 m/s, so in 21 seconds they cover 560 m, the sum of their lengths. The other train is 560 − 290 = 270 m.

questions.text: The average weight of a certain number of students in a group was 72 kg. If 11 students, with an average weight of 76 kg each, leave the group, and 5 students, each with an average weight of 79 kg, join the group, the average weight of the students in the group decreases by 0.6 kg. The number of students initially in the group was:
questions.explanation: With n students at first, the new total is 72n − 11 × 76 + 5 × 79 = 72n − 441 for n − 6 students averaging 71.4 kg. 71.4(n − 6) = 72n − 441 gives 0.6n = 12.6, so n = 21.

questions.text: The average of 9 numbers is 3. If the average of the first 8 of these numbers is 2, the 9th number is:
questions.explanation: The 9 numbers total 9 × 3 = 27 and the first 8 total 8 × 2 = 16, so the 9th is 27 − 16 = 11.

questions.text: The ratio of the present ages of Ram and Shyam is 3 : 4, and 4 years ago the ratio was 2 : 3. What will be the ratio of the ages of Ram and Shyam 4 years from now?
questions.explanation: Let the ages be 3x and 4x: (3x − 4)/(4x − 4) = 2/3 gives 9x − 12 = 8x − 8, so x = 4 and the ages are 12 and 16. In 4 years: 16 : 20 = 4 : 5.

questions.text: Find the area of the quadrilateral ABCD, the coordinates of whose vertices are A(6,-3),B(-4,-2),C(3,1) and D(5,0)?
Find the average of 300, 129, 49, 120 and 102.
A cylindrical disc of thickness 1 cm is made by melting two solid cylinders of radii 4 cm and 5 cm, and length 6 cm and 4 cm, respectively. The radius of the new cylinder is:
questions.explanation: The volume is unchanged: π(4² × 6 + 5² × 4) = 196π cm³. A disc 1 cm thick has volume πr² × 1, so r² = 196 and r = 14 cm.

questions.text: By selling an article for ₹20, a dealer makes a profit of 10%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹, rounded off to two decimal place) so as to make a profit of 20%?
questions.explanation: Cost price = 20/1.1 = ₹18.18. A 20% profit needs a selling price of 1.2 × 18.18 = ₹21.82, an increase of ₹1.82.

questions.text: What sum (in ₹) will earn a simple interest of ₹240 in 4 years at 12% per year rate of interest?
The least number of square tiles required to pave the ceiling of a room 525 centimetre long and 378 centimetre broad is:
questions.explanation: The largest square tile has side HCF(525, 378) = 21 cm, so (525/21) × (378/21) = 25 × 18 = 450 tiles.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 53, 52, 39, 38, ?, 24
questions.explanation: The terms fall by 1 and 13 alternately: 53 − 1 = 52, 52 − 13 = 39, 39 − 1 = 38, 38 − 13 = 25 and 25 − 1 = 24.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? TKU, UNP, VQK, WTF, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move +1 (T, U, V, W, X), second letters +3 (K, N, Q, T, W) and third letters −5 (U, P, K, F, A): XWA.

questions.text: GY 16 is related to DV 23 in a certain way. In the same way, OD 11 is related to LA 18. To which of the following is LW 13 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back and the number rises by 7: G → D, Y → V, 16 → 23. So L → I, W → T and 13 → 20: IT 20.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some carrots are radishes. Some cucumbers are radishes. Conclusions: I. All cucumbers are carrots. II. Some cucumbers are carrots.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Carrots and cucumbers each overlap radishes, but nothing links carrots with cucumbers, so neither 'all' nor 'some cucumbers are carrots' is certain.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (12, 4, 160) (6, 11, 157)
questions.explanation: The third number is the sum of the squares of the first two: 12² + 4² = 144 + 16 = 160 and 6² + 11² = 36 + 121 = 157. Likewise 14² + 7² = 196 + 49 = 245.

questions.text: P, Q, R, S, T and U are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). P is second to the left of T. Q is an immediate neighbour of both U and P. S and P are immediate neighbours. Who among the following has both T and U as his immediate neighbours?
questions.explanation: Going clockwise (to the left, for people facing the centre): T, S, P, Q, U, R. P is second to T's left; Q sits between P and U, so S takes the seat between T and P, and R the last seat, between U and T.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘TALE’ is coded as ‘5173’ and ‘AIDS’ is coded as ‘6452’.What is the code for ‘A’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: A is the only letter in both words and 5 the only digit in both codes, so A = 5.

questions.text: Which of the following interchanges of signs would make the given equation correct? 15 − 54 × 18 + 16 ÷ 2 = 44

Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All parrots are eagles. No parrot is a crow. Conclusions: (I) No eagle is a crow. (II) All crows are parrots.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: No parrot is a crow, so no crow is a parrot and II is false. Eagles that are not parrots may or may not be crows, so I does not follow either.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'EAGER' is writtenas ‘CGGTG’ and 'LEARN' is writtenas ‘GNAPT’. How will 'HINDI' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first two letters swap, the middle one stays and the last two swap; then each swapped letter moves 2 places forward: EAGER → AEGRE → CGGTG and LEARN → ELANR → GNAPT. So HINDI → IHNID → KJNKF.

questions.text: 18 is related to 80 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 23 is related to 100. To which ofthe following is 36 related, following the same logic?(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
UBIP is related to YFMT in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, IPWD is related to MTAH. To which of the following is OVCJ related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places forward: U → Y, B → F, I → M, P → T, and W → A, wrapping round. So OVCJ → SZGN.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘PLAY’ is coded as ‘4831’ and ‘CLAY’ is coded as ‘1824’. What is the code for ‘C’ in that language?
questions.explanation: L, A and Y are in both words, as are 8, 1 and 4 in both codes. The letter left in CLAY is C and the digit left in its code is 2, so C = 2.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the center (but not necessarily in the same order). G is sitting third to the left of E. A is sitting to the immediate left of G. D is the immediate neighbour of A and B. F is sitting to the immediate left of C. How many people are sitting between F and D when counted from the right of F?
questions.explanation: Going clockwise (to the left, for people facing the centre) from E: E, C, F, G, A, D, B. Counting to F's right from F, C, E and B come before D: three people.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘–’ and ‘×’ are interchanged and ‘÷’ and ‘+’ are interchanged? 6 − 8 ÷ 12 + 3 × 9 + 3 ÷ 17 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 6 × 8 + 12 ÷ 3 − 9 ÷ 3 + 17 = 48 + 4 − 3 + 17 = 66.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: After which of the following Acts did India come to be governed in the name of the British crown?
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act, 1858, passed after the revolt of 1857, ended the East India Company's rule: India was thereafter governed by and in the name of the British Crown.

questions.text: Who was the Indian match referee in the ICC - T20 World Cup 2021 tournament?
questions.explanation: Javagal Srinath, India's member of the ICC Elite Panel of Match Referees, was one of the four match referees at the 2021 T20 World Cup.

questions.text: In general, deficit is considered as a ________ concept.
questions.explanation: A deficit is measured over a period, such as a year, so it is a flow; debt, the deficits accumulated up to a point in time, is a stock.

questions.text: Which of the following dances of Goa is performed to celebrate the victory of the Maratha warriors over the Portuguese?
questions.explanation: Ghode Modni, a horse dance performed at Shigmo by men wearing horse frames and carrying swords, commemorates the victory of the Maratha warriors (the Ranes of Sattari) over the Portuguese.

questions.text: What is the approx width of broad-gauge railway network in India?
questions.explanation: India's broad gauge is 1.676 m (5 ft 6 in) between the rails; of the options, 1.6 metres is the closest.

questions.text: A coastal area was flooded with sea water and resulted in heavy salt deposits in the nearby area. After a few days, it was observed that many plants died. Based on these statements, which of the following is the most probable cause of the plant deaths? A. Plants died due to infection from sea water borne germs. B. Plants died due to absence of sunlight. C. Plants died due to plasmolysis in the plant cells. D. Plants died because they were eaten by sea organisms.
questions.explanation: The salt made the soil water more concentrated than the cell sap, so water left the root cells by osmosis and their cytoplasm shrank away from the cell wall: plasmolysis.

questions.text: The Universal Adult Franchise in Indian Constitution is applicable to Indian Citizens from the age of _______________.
questions.explanation: Under Article 326, as amended by the 61st Amendment (1988), every citizen aged 18 or over may vote; the age was 21 before.

questions.text: The PM-SVANidhi Scheme (2020) is run by which Ministry of the Government of India?
options: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
questions.explanation: PM SVANidhi, the micro-credit scheme for street vendors launched in June 2020, is run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

questions.text: In which stadium did Indian cricketer Saurav Ganguly take off and waive his t-shirt?
questions.explanation: Ganguly took off his shirt and waved it from the Lord's balcony after India won the NatWest Series final against England in July 2002.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was appointed as the Viceroy of India in place of Lord Wavell in February 1947?
questions.explanation: In February 1947 Attlee announced that Lord Mountbatten would succeed Lord Wavell as Viceroy; he took office in March 1947.

questions.text: Which of the following age groups is considered as working population or working age in India?
questions.explanation: India's census counts the population aged 15-59 years as the working-age group (international usage often takes 15-64).

questions.text: The Bidar Fort of Karnataka is irregularly ______ in shape.
questions.explanation: Bidar Fort, built by the Bahmani sultan Ahmad Shah I from 1429, is laid out as an irregular rhomboid on the edge of the Bidar plateau.

questions.text: When was National Judicial Commission Bill, which is a private member bill to regulate the appointment of judges through the National Judicial Commission, introduced in Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: The National Judicial Commission Bill, 2022, a private member's bill moved by CPI(M) MP Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya, was introduced in the Rajya Sabha on 9 December 2022.

questions.text: Which musical duo is part of the Khayal singing lineage of the Banaras Gharana?
options: Salamat Ali and Nazakat Ali Khan
questions.explanation: The brothers Rajan and Sajan Mishra were khayal singers of the Banaras gharana.

questions.text: Who among the following deciphered the Brahmi Script of the Mauryan period?
questions.explanation: James Prinsep, an officer of the East India Company's mint, deciphered Brahmi in 1837, which made Asoka's inscriptions readable.

questions.text: According to Indian Meteorology, which of the following is NOT a season experienced in India?
questions.explanation: Indian meteorology recognises four seasons: the cold weather season, the hot weather season, the southwest monsoon season and the retreating monsoon season. There is no 'equatorial season'.

questions.text: Which of the following can be a basis of difference between a salamander and a house-wall lizard apart from their habitat?
questions.explanation: The house lizard is a reptile with dry, scaly skin; the salamander is an amphibian with moist skin and no scales. Both are cold-blooded, lay eggs and have three-chambered hearts.

questions.text: The IUPAC name of CH₃-(CH₂)₁₈-CH₃ is ________.
questions.explanation: The chain has 1 + 18 + 1 = 20 carbon atoms, and the alkane with 20 carbons is icosane (eicosane); dodecane has 12, decane 10 and triacontane 30.

questions.text: A party recognised by the Election Commission of India that secures at least ________ of the total votes in the General Election to Lok Sabha or Legislative Assembly in four or more states in addition to winning four Lok Sabha seats is called a National Party.
questions.explanation: Under the Election Symbols Order, 1968, one way to become a National Party is to win at least 6% of the valid votes in four or more states at a Lok Sabha or assembly election and also win four Lok Sabha seats.

questions.text: Hornbill festival is organised every year in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Nagaland holds the Hornbill Festival every year from 1 to 10 December at Kisama, near Kohima.

questions.text: Which of the following novels is NOT written by Aravind Adiga?
questions.explanation: 'The English Teacher' (1945) is by R. K. Narayan. 'The White Tiger', 'Last Man in Tower' and 'Selection Day' are Aravind Adiga's.

questions.text: The Mughal emperor, Babur was a devotee of the ______Sufi Silsila.
questions.explanation: Babur, like the Timurids before him, followed the Naqshbandi order and revered its Central Asian master Khwaja Ubaidullah Ahrar.

questions.text: Bawris are traditionally used for:
questions.explanation: Bawris (baolis) are stepwells, traditionally used to store rainwater and recharge groundwater, especially in Rajasthan.

questions.text: Which of the following Kathak dancers received the Padma Shri of 2022?
questions.explanation: The Kathak sisters Kamalini and Nalini Asthana of Agra received the Padma Shri together in 2022.

questions.text: At the Sansad Ratna Awards 2023, who among the following received the Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Lifetime Achievement Award?
questions.explanation: The Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Lifetime Achievement Award at the Sansad Ratna Awards 2023 went to T. K. Rangarajan, a former two-term Rajya Sabha member of the CPI(M).

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He dropped out / at his friend's house / on his way home / the day before yesterday.
questions.explanation: To 'drop out' is to withdraw; a casual visit to a friend's house is 'dropped in' (or 'dropped by').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate expression that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. Sonali is “contemplating” whether to accept the offer from Saanvi or not; she is still not in a position to be able to arrive at a decision.
questions.explanation: To 'chew the cud' is to think something over slowly and carefully, as Sonali is doing.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. I am / cleaning the sofa / when she called me.
questions.explanation: An action in progress when something else happened takes the past continuous: 'I was cleaning the sofa when she called me.'

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word to fill in the blank. Arvind wanted to bake a cake for Riya's birthday, so he mixed the ______________, eggs and butter.
questions.explanation: A cake is made with 'flour', ground grain; 'flower' sounds the same but means a bloom.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling error in the given sentence. The student received an A+ for her exellent performance.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'excellent'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The __________ of the scientific experiment raised questions about the validity of the results.
questions.explanation: 'Ambiguity', being open to more than one reading, is what would cast doubt on the results; transparency and meticulousness would support them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Inspire
questions.explanation: To 'inspire' is to stimulate someone to feel or act; 'daunt' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The teacher checked / whether each of them / have a blanket / as it was a cold night.
options: as it was a cold night
questions.explanation: 'Each of them' is singular and takes a singular verb: 'has (or had) a blanket', not 'have'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. She is / as more intelligent as / her brothers are.
questions.explanation: Equality is shown with 'as … as' and the positive degree: 'She is as intelligent as her brothers are.'

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'peripheral'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Raghav, who “studies tourism” at present, is planning to go abroad after his graduation.
questions.explanation: An action going on around the present takes the present continuous: 'who is studying tourism at present'.

questions.text: Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence. The disposal of “hazardous” waste in hospitals and factories is a serious problem and needs to be taken care of urgently.
questions.explanation: 'Hazardous' means risky or harmful: 'dangerous'. 'Benign' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The student leader has _____ politics recently.
questions.explanation: One 'enters' politics, that is, takes it up.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence. The gardener's meticulous care ensured the vibrent colours of the flowers.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'vibrant'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Please put the dishes in the _________ after you finish eating.
questions.explanation: Dirty dishes go in the 'sink'; 'sync' and 'cinque' only sound similar.

questions.text: You overhear someone say, "He's always on cloud nine." What does this idiom mean in the given context?
questions.explanation: To be 'on cloud nine' is to be extremely happy.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of ‘scanty’ in the sentence given below. India has varied regions which have excess, moderate and deficient rainfall all through the year.
questions.explanation: 'Scanty' means less than is needed: 'deficient', as in deficient rainfall.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The society / of the / our place / is good.
questions.explanation: 'The' and 'our' cannot both stand before 'place': 'The society of our place is good.'

questions.text: Select the present perfect tense of the verb given in the brackets to fill in the blank. Alex _______ (study) two programming languages.
questions.explanation: The present perfect is 'has' or 'have' with the past participle; with the singular 'Alex' it is 'has studied'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the sentence. She was deeply “effected by” the news, to the point of tears.
questions.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to influence or move, and one is 'affected by' something: 'deeply affected by the news'. As a verb, 'effect' means to bring about.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It was one January morning, very early — a pinching, frosty morning — the cove all grey ____ 1 ____ hoar-frost and the ripple lapping softly on the stones. The captain had _____ 2____ earlier than usual and set out down the beach. Mother was upstairs with father and I was _____ 3____ the breakfast table against the captain’s return when the parlour door opened and a man stepped in on whom I had never set my eyes before. He was a pale, tallowy creature, wanting two fingers of the left hand, and ______ 4____ he wore a cutlass, he did not look much like a fighter. I had always my eye open for seafaring ______ 5_____ with one leg or two, and I remember this one puzzled me.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The cove was 'grey with hoar-frost': 'with' names what covers it and makes it grey, as in 'white with snow'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It was one January morning, very early — a pinching, frosty morning — the cove all grey ____ 1 ____ hoar-frost and the ripple lapping softly on the stones. The captain had _____ 2____ earlier than usual and set out down the beach. Mother was upstairs with father and I was _____ 3____ the breakfast table against the captain’s return when the parlour door opened and a man stepped in on whom I had never set my eyes before. He was a pale, tallowy creature, wanting two fingers of the left hand, and ______ 4____ he wore a cutlass, he did not look much like a fighter. I had always my eye open for seafaring ______ 5_____ with one leg or two, and I remember this one puzzled me.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'The captain had risen earlier than usual': 'risen' is the past participle of 'rise', to get up.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It was one January morning, very early — a pinching, frosty morning — the cove all grey ____ 1 ____ hoar-frost and the ripple lapping softly on the stones. The captain had _____ 2____ earlier than usual and set out down the beach. Mother was upstairs with father and I was _____ 3____ the breakfast table against the captain’s return when the parlour door opened and a man stepped in on whom I had never set my eyes before. He was a pale, tallowy creature, wanting two fingers of the left hand, and ______ 4____ he wore a cutlass, he did not look much like a fighter. I had always my eye open for seafaring ______ 5_____ with one leg or two, and I remember this one puzzled me.
