Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: To 'lay' the table is to set it, and 'lay' takes an object: 'I was laying the breakfast table'. 'Lying', from 'lie', takes no object.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It was one January morning, very early — a pinching, frosty morning — the cove all grey ____ 1 ____ hoar-frost and the ripple lapping softly on the stones. The captain had _____ 2____ earlier than usual and set out down the beach. Mother was upstairs with father and I was _____ 3____ the breakfast table against the captain’s return when the parlour door opened and a man stepped in on whom I had never set my eyes before. He was a pale, tallowy creature, wanting two fingers of the left hand, and ______ 4____ he wore a cutlass, he did not look much like a fighter. I had always my eye open for seafaring ______ 5_____ with one leg or two, and I remember this one puzzled me.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Though' introduces a contrast: though he wore a cutlass, he did not look much like a fighter.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. It was one January morning, very early — a pinching, frosty morning — the cove all grey ____ 1 ____ hoar-frost and the ripple lapping softly on the stones. The captain had _____ 2____ earlier than usual and set out down the beach. Mother was upstairs with father and I was _____ 3____ the breakfast table against the captain’s return when the parlour door opened and a man stepped in on whom I had never set my eyes before. He was a pale, tallowy creature, wanting two fingers of the left hand, and ______ 4____ he wore a cutlass, he did not look much like a fighter. I had always my eye open for seafaring ______ 5_____ with one leg or two, and I remember this one puzzled me.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Seafaring men' are sailors, and only people fit 'with one leg or two'; birds, plants and flowers do not.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: If 4% of (A + B) is equal to 28% of (A – B), then find A : B.
By selling an article for ₹19, a dealer makes a profit of 20%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹, rounded off to two decimal place) so as to make a profit of 40%?
questions.explanation: Cost price = 19 ÷ 1.2 = ₹15.833. At 40% profit the price is 15.833 × 1.4 = ₹22.167, an increase of 22.167 − 19 = ₹3.17.

questions.text: A 725 m long train passes through a 235 m long tunnel in 48 sec. Find the speed of the train.
questions.explanation: The train covers its own length plus the tunnel's, 725 + 235 = 960 m, in 48 s: 20 m/s = 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h.

questions.text: A train travelling at a speed of 60 km/h leaves station A at 7:00 a.m. and another train travelling at a speed of 84 km/h starts from station A at 9:30 a.m. in the same direction on a parallel track. At what distance (in km) from station A and after how many hours of travel of the second train will they be together? Express your answer in the same order.
questions.explanation: By 9:30 a.m. the first train is 2.5 × 60 = 150 km ahead. The second gains 84 − 60 = 24 km/h, so it draws level after 150/24 = 6.25 hours, 84 × 6.25 = 525 km from A.

questions.text: The average weight of a group of 20 women was calculated as 58.5 kg and it was later discovered that the weight of one of the women was read as 35 kg, whereas her actual weight was 65 kg. What is the actual average weight of the group of 20 women?
questions.explanation: The total was 65 − 35 = 30 kg too low, so the average rises by 30/20 = 1.5 kg: 58.5 + 1.5 = 60 kg.

questions.text: A merchant has 5000 kg of Basmati rice. He sells some part of this Basmati rice at 20% profit and the rest at 35% profit. He gains 29% in the entire transaction. What is the quantity sold at 20% profit and 35% profit, respectively?
questions.explanation: By alligation the quantities sold at 20% and 35% are in the ratio (35 − 29) : (29 − 20) = 6 : 9 = 2 : 3: 2,000 kg and 3,000 kg of the 5,000 kg.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 4 years.
A shopkeeper makes a 15% profit on a sale. He would have made 18%, if he had sold it for Rs.18 more. The cost price of the article is:
questions.explanation: The extra ₹18 is 18% − 15% = 3% of the cost price, so the cost price is 18 × 100/3 = ₹600.

questions.text: Find the HCF of 24, 36 and 60.
questions.explanation: 24 = 2³ × 3, 36 = 2² × 3² and 60 = 2² × 3 × 5. The factors common to all three give 2² × 3 = 12.

questions.text: Sunil, Basid, Vikram, and Kuldeep receive salaries in the ratio of 3 : 7 : 8 : 13. If the difference between the salaries of Sunil and Basid is ₹2,000, then what is the difference between the salaries (in ₹) of Vikram and Kuldeep?
questions.explanation: Basid's 7 parts minus Sunil's 3 is 4 parts = ₹2,000, so one part is ₹500. Kuldeep's 13 minus Vikram's 8 is 5 parts = ₹2,500.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 5 years.
A class of 30 students appeared in a test. The average score of 12 students is 80, and that of the rest is 70. What is the average score of the class?
If tea that costs ₹7.50 per kg is mixed with tea that costs ₹10.50 per kg in the proportion of 2 :1 then, what is the cost (in ₹) of the resultant mixture per kg?
Manpreet offers two successive discounts of 12% and 8% on the sale of a sweater to his customers on the occasion of Diwali. What is the equivalent single percentage discount offered by Manpreet?
questions.explanation: Successive discounts of a% and b% equal a + b − ab/100: 12 + 8 − 0.96 = 19.04%.

questions.text: A person deposited ₹2,500 in a bank that pays 8% simple interest. He withdrew ₹1,000 (from amount) at the end of the first year. What will be his balance after 4 years?
questions.explanation: After the first year the balance is 2,500 + 200 = ₹2,700, and ₹1,700 after the withdrawal. Three more years at 8% add 1,700 × 8 × 3/100 = ₹408: ₹2,108.

questions.text: 10 is related to 75 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 6 is related to 47. To which of the following is 15 related following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by 7 and 5 is added: 10 × 7 + 5 = 75 and 6 × 7 + 5 = 47. Likewise 15 × 7 + 5 = 110.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 456 × 4 − 3 ÷ 11 + 70 =?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 456 ÷ 4 + 3 × 11 − 70 = 114 + 33 − 70 = 77.

questions.text: MJHI is related to TQOP in a certain way. In the same way, GDBC is related to NKIJ. To which of the following is XUST related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 7 places forward: M → T, J → Q, H → O, I → P. So X → E, U → B, S → Z and T → A (wrapping round after Z): EBZA.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘×‘ are interchanged and ‘–’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 17 + 77 – 7 × 37 ÷ 47 = ?
In a certain code language, ‘VOLT’ is coded as ‘3517’ and ‘TURN’ is coded as ‘2348’. What is the code for ‘T’ in that language?
questions.explanation: T is the only letter in both words and 3 the only digit in both codes, so T = 3.

questions.text: Seven people R, S, T, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). T is sitting to the immediate right of G. R is sitting to the immediate right of E. Only two people are sitting between D and S when counted from the right of S. E is an immediate neighbour of S. If F is not an immediate neighbour of S, who is sitting third to the left of F?
questions.explanation: Clockwise round the table: S, T, G, F, D, R, E (facing the centre, each person's left is the next seat clockwise). E cannot sit to S's left, as R, to E's right, would then take S's seat; and F, kept away from S, sits beside D. The three seats to F's left are D, R and E.

questions.text: Six friends are sitting on a circular table, facing towards the centre (but not necessarily in the same order) . X is to the immediate left of Z and W is to the immediate right of Y. Z and U are separated by only one person sitting between them. W is an immediate neighbour of U. Only V is sitting between Z and Y. Who among the following are the immediate neighbours of U?
questions.explanation: Clockwise round the table: Z, X, U, W, Y, V (facing the centre, each person's left is the next seat clockwise). X is on Z's left, so V and then Y are on Z's right; W sits to Y's right, and U, next to W, is two seats from Z. U's neighbours are X and W.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘make some noise’ is written as ‘ja sp ko’ and ‘noise is painful’ is writtenas ‘la ma sp’. How will ‘noise’ be writtenin that language?
questions.explanation: 'noise' is the only word in both sentences and 'sp' the only code in both, so noise = sp.

questions.text: In the following number-pairs, the second number is obtained by applying certain mathematical operations to the first number. Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) 8, 30; 12, 46
questions.explanation: The second number is four times the first minus 2: 8 × 4 − 2 = 30 and 12 × 4 − 2 = 46. Likewise 16 × 4 − 2 = 62.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All shirts are trousers. No trouser is a belt. Conclusions: (I) No shirt is a belt. (II) Some belts may be trousers.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: All shirts are trousers and no trouser is a belt, so no shirt is a belt (I). II cannot follow: as no trouser is a belt, no belt can be a trouser.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'BORDER' is coded as ‘OBDRRE’ and 'BEYOND' is coded as ‘EBOYDN’. How will 'BURDEN' be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: The letters of each pair are swapped: BO RD ER → OB DR RE and BE YO ND → EB OY DN. So BU RD EN → UB DR NE: UBDRNE.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: Some whales are sharks. No shark is a dolphin. Conclusions: (I) No dolphin is a shark. (II) Some sharks are whales.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: 'No shark is a dolphin' converts to 'no dolphin is a shark' (I), and 'some whales are sharks' to 'some sharks are whales' (II). Both follow.

questions.text: Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given series to make it logically complete? EMU, DNT, COS, BPR, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move back one (E, D, C, B, A), second letters forward one (M, N, O, P, Q) and third letters back one (U, T, S, R, Q): AQQ.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 10, 22, 46, 94, 190, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before plus 2: 10 × 2 + 2 = 22, 22 × 2 + 2 = 46, and so on to 190 × 2 + 2 = 382.

questions.text: CE 77 is related to IK 87 in a certain way. In the same way, GJ 52 is related to MP 62. To which of the following is BG 43 related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 6 places forward and the number rises by 10: C → I, E → K, 77 → 87. So B → H, G → M and 43 → 53: HM 53.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'BRIGHT' is coded as '371562', and 'GIRTHS' is coded as '653782'. What is the code for ‘B’ in 'BRIGHT'?
questions.explanation: R, I, G, H and T are in both words, and 3, 7, 5, 6 and 2 in both codes. The letter left in BRIGHT is B and the digit left in its code is 1, so B = 1.

questions.text: The autobiography of which of the following actors is titled ‘The Substance And The Shadow: An Autobiography’?
questions.explanation: 'The Substance and the Shadow', published in 2014, is the autobiography of the actor Dilip Kumar.

questions.text: Which Indian dancer of the Manipuri style won the Tagore Award for Cultural Harmony in 2014?
questions.explanation: Rajkumar Singhajit Singh, a senior guru of Manipuri dance, received the Tagore Award for Cultural Harmony for 2014 (presented in 2019).

questions.text: Which edition of the Intercontinental Cup event was played in India in 2023?
questions.explanation: The 2023 Intercontinental Cup, held in Bhubaneswar, was the football tournament's third edition, after those of 2018 and 2019; India won it.

questions.text: The Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) is an example of the ________ industry.
questions.explanation: SAIL is owned and run by the government, which makes it a public sector industry; a joint sector one is owned jointly by the state and private firms.

questions.text: Which classical dance form is performed by the renowned artists; Sitara Devi, Rohini Bhate, Pandit Munnalal Shukla, Kumudini Lakhia and Uma Sharma?
questions.explanation: Sitara Devi, Rohini Bhate, Munnalal Shukla, Kumudini Lakhia and Uma Sharma are all exponents of Kathak.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When was the All Bengal Students Conference held in the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the All Bengal Students' Conference in Calcutta in 1928, which set up the All Bengal Students' Association.

questions.text: In the context of microfinance, what does ‘S’ stand for in SHG?
questions.explanation: SHG stands for Self-Help Group: a small group, often of women, that pools its savings and lends to its members.

questions.text: As per Article 51A of the Constitution of India, Fundamental Duty (h) is to develop the ________________, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
questions.explanation: Article 51A(h) asks every citizen to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.

questions.text: What is the name of Formula E’s first ever race in India, which was hosted in collaboration with the Telangana government?
questions.explanation: India's first Formula E race was the Hyderabad E-Prix of February 2023, run on a street circuit in Hyderabad with the Telangana government.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is/are FALSE for the Harappan town planning? 1. Most of the towns have citadel in harappan civilization. 2. Every town had a temple in Harappan civilization. 3. Every building was made of sand stone in Harappan civilization.
questions.explanation: Statements 2 and 3 are false: no temples have been found in Harappan towns, and their buildings were mostly of baked brick, not sandstone. Many towns did have a raised citadel, so 1 is true.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Ramoshi Uprising of 1824 took place in which of the following present states of India?
questions.explanation: The Ramoshis, a community of the Western Ghats, rose against British rule in the 1820s around Satara and Pune, in present-day Maharashtra.

questions.text: In October 2023, Maharashtra government planned which of the following schemes to overhaul its medical system after the death of 38 patients in Nanded?
questions.explanation: In October 2023, after the patient deaths at the government hospital in Nanded, Chief Minister Eknath Shinde announced a 'New Healthcare Vision 2035' to overhaul the state's public health system.

questions.text: A process like river bifurcation can create valuable landforms for the environment, providing growth of vegetation. An example of such landform is _____.
questions.explanation: Near its mouth a river bifurcates into distributaries that spread silt into a delta, fertile land that supports rich vegetation.

questions.text: According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021, which Union Territory has the lowest proportion of poor?
questions.explanation: In NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021 (baseline report), Puducherry had the lowest share of poor people among the Union Territories, 1.72%.

questions.text: The Taj Mahal was built by who among the following?
questions.explanation: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal at Agra in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

questions.text: During which centuries did several Buddhist pilgrims and scholars travel to China on the historic 'silk route'?
options: First, second and third centuries AD
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the first to third centuries AD, when Buddhism first reached China along the Silk Route and monks began carrying its texts there. (Pilgrims went on travelling the route in later centuries too.)

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India specifically addresses the qualifications for the office of the President?
questions.explanation: Article 58 sets the qualifications for election as President; Article 56 deals with the term of office and Article 60 with the oath.

questions.text: Non-polar molecules possess _______.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives an instantaneous dipole moment: a non-polar molecule has no permanent dipole, but the momentary shifting of its electrons creates short-lived dipoles, the source of London dispersion forces. ('No dipole moment' is also arguable, as a description of its net, permanent state.)

questions.text: In which state is Kawal Wildlife Sanctuary located?
questions.explanation: Kawal Wildlife Sanctuary, also a tiger reserve, is in northern Telangana.

questions.text: Who among the following was the most important god of the Aryans?
questions.explanation: Indra, god of rain and war, is the most important god of the Rig Veda, with about a quarter of its hymns addressed to him.

questions.text: Who among the following led the Parliamentary delegation to participate in the 9th BRICS Parliamentary Forum in September 2023?
questions.explanation: Harivansh Narayan Singh, Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, led India's delegation to the 9th BRICS Parliamentary Forum in Johannesburg in September 2023.

questions.text: __________ was the pioneer who modified the Hawaiian slide guitar to play classical ragas.
questions.explanation: Brij Bhushan Kabra was the first to adapt the Hawaiian slide guitar to play Hindustani classical ragas.

questions.text: Select the synthetic indicator from among the given options.
questions.explanation: Methyl orange is made in the laboratory; turmeric, litmus (from lichens) and red cabbage juice are natural indicators.

questions.text: In which state is 'Bhogali Bihu' festival celebrated?
questions.explanation: Bhogali or Magh Bihu, the harvest festival held in January, is celebrated in Assam.

questions.text: Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence. She accused her sister of being “vindictive” when she was trying to defame her.
questions.explanation: 'Vindictive' means wanting revenge: 'revengeful'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. When pigs fly
questions.explanation: 'When pigs fly' describes something that will never happen.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence. The artist's unique technique added a touch of individiuality to the painting.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'individuality'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Apple of one's eye
questions.explanation: The 'apple of one's eye' is a person or thing one holds very precious.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. The children were “merry” than usual on Sunday.
questions.explanation: 'Than' needs the comparative: 'merrier than usual'. 'More merrier' doubles the comparative.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Blunt
questions.explanation: A 'blunt' person speaks plainly, without regard for others' feelings: the closest option is 'insensitive'. 'Tactful' is its opposite.

questions.text: Change the following sentence into superlative degree. No other mountain in the world is as high as the Mount Everest.
options: No other mountain is highest than Mount Everest.
Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world.
Mount Everest is higher than any other mountain in the world.
Mount Everest is high mountain in the world.
questions.explanation: 'No other mountain is as high as Mount Everest' becomes, in the superlative degree, 'Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world'.

questions.text: Select the sentence with the most appropriate use of preposition.
options: Reetu slept all through the history class.
Reetu slept all during the history class.
Reetu slept all into the history class.
Reetu slept all in the history class.
questions.explanation: 'All through' means from beginning to end: Reetu slept throughout the class.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. The children's laughter was filled with “exuberant” joy.
questions.explanation: 'Exuberant' means full of unrestrained energy and cheer; its opposite is 'repressed', held back.

questions.text: Read the sentence given below and identify if there is an error in it. The error can be in any segment of the sentence which are marked A, B, C, and D. Select option D if there is 'No error'. (A) Ritika angrily / (B) spoke to Kartik / (C) after the meeting / (D) No error.
questions.explanation: 'Ritika angrily spoke to Kartik after the meeting' is correct as it stands.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Placing a huge magnet atop the temple “pose to being” the biggest hurdle for the masons.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'posed to be': the sentence needs a finite verb in the past ('Placing a huge magnet atop the temple posed to be the biggest hurdle'), and of the four options only it supplies one. 'Pose to being', 'poses for being' and 'posing as be' are ungrammatical; in everyday English 'proved to be' would be the natural phrase.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. My grandparents live in a beautiful house _________ the countryside.
questions.explanation: One lives 'in' the countryside.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. They “looked out the matter and found” the root cause of the problem.
options: looked until the matter and found
looked into the matter and found
looked unless the matter and found
looked of the matter and found
questions.explanation: To 'look into' a matter is to investigate it.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The farm cattle is grazing in the field when the tiger attacked.
questions.explanation: 'Cattle' is plural, and the attack was in the past: 'The farm cattle were grazing in the field when the tiger attacked.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Enmity
questions.explanation: 'Enmity' is hostility; its opposite is 'friendship'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The loud thunder _______ the children, making them cry.
questions.explanation: Thunder that makes children cry has 'frightened' them.

questions.text: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in future tense form. Since next Friday, the team of three members has been tracking the animal.
options: From next Friday, the team of three members have been tracking the animal.
From next Friday, the team of three members are tracking the animal.
From next Friday, the team of three members will be tracking the animal.
Since last Friday, the team of three members had tracked the animal.
questions.explanation: The future continuous 'will be tracking' puts the action in the future, with 'from next Friday' marking when it begins.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A monsoon is traditionally a seasonal reversing wind (1)________________ by corresponding changes in precipitation but is now (2)___________ describe seasonal changes in atmospheric circulation and precipitation associated (3)_______________ annual latitudinal oscillation of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) between its limits to the north and south of the equator. Usually, the term monsoon (4)___________ refer to the rainy phase of a seasonally changing pattern, although technically there is also a dry phase. The term is also sometimes used to (5)_________________ locally heavy but short-term rains.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: A wind 'accompanied by' changes in precipitation: the past participle, used in a passive sense.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A monsoon is traditionally a seasonal reversing wind (1)________________ by corresponding changes in precipitation but is now (2)___________ describe seasonal changes in atmospheric circulation and precipitation associated (3)_______________ annual latitudinal oscillation of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) between its limits to the north and south of the equator. Usually, the term monsoon (4)___________ refer to the rainy phase of a seasonally changing pattern, although technically there is also a dry phase. The term is also sometimes used to (5)_________________ locally heavy but short-term rains.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The term 'is now used to describe' wider changes: 'used to' plus the verb, after 'is'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A monsoon is traditionally a seasonal reversing wind (1)________________ by corresponding changes in precipitation but is now (2)___________ describe seasonal changes in atmospheric circulation and precipitation associated (3)_______________ annual latitudinal oscillation of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) between its limits to the north and south of the equator. Usually, the term monsoon (4)___________ refer to the rainy phase of a seasonally changing pattern, although technically there is also a dry phase. The term is also sometimes used to (5)_________________ locally heavy but short-term rains.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Changes 'associated with' the annual oscillation of the ITCZ.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A monsoon is traditionally a seasonal reversing wind (1)________________ by corresponding changes in precipitation but is now (2)___________ describe seasonal changes in atmospheric circulation and precipitation associated (3)_______________ annual latitudinal oscillation of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) between its limits to the north and south of the equator. Usually, the term monsoon (4)___________ refer to the rainy phase of a seasonally changing pattern, although technically there is also a dry phase. The term is also sometimes used to (5)_________________ locally heavy but short-term rains.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'the term monsoon' takes 'is used to refer to'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A monsoon is traditionally a seasonal reversing wind (1)________________ by corresponding changes in precipitation but is now (2)___________ describe seasonal changes in atmospheric circulation and precipitation associated (3)_______________ annual latitudinal oscillation of the Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) between its limits to the north and south of the equator. Usually, the term monsoon (4)___________ refer to the rainy phase of a seasonally changing pattern, although technically there is also a dry phase. The term is also sometimes used to (5)_________________ locally heavy but short-term rains.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Used to' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'used to describe'.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Atul sold two sacks of rice for ₹19,200 each. On one, he gained 20% and on the other, he lost 20%. Find his gain or loss percentage in the whole transaction.
questions.explanation: The first sack cost 19,200/1.2 = ₹16,000 and the second 19,200/0.8 = ₹24,000. Cost ₹40,000, sale ₹38,400: a loss of ₹1,600, or 4%.

questions.text: Riya offers 12% discount on all her goods and offers an additional discount of 6% to those customers who pay in cash. How much will a customer have to pay for a fan marked for ₹2,400 if he pays in cash?
questions.explanation: Successive discounts of 12% and 6%: ₹2,400 × 0.88 × 0.94 = ₹1,985.28.

questions.text: Rice worth ₹43/kg and ₹67/kg are mixed with a third variety in the ratio 2 : 1 : 5. If the mixture is worth ₹96/kg, the price (in ₹) of the third variety of rice per kg will be:
questions.explanation: Take 2 kg, 1 kg and 5 kg: the 8 kg of mixture is worth 8 × 96 = ₹768, so 86 + 67 + 5x = 768, 5x = 615 and x = ₹123 a kg.

questions.text: In a 100-marks test, the average of marks scored by 50 students was found to be 65. Later on, it was discovered that a score of 88 was misread as 68. Find the correct average.
questions.explanation: The total rises by 88 − 68 = 20, so the average rises by 20/50 = 0.4: 65 + 0.4 = 65.40.

questions.text: A thief saw a policeman, and he started running at a speed of 18 m/s. After 12 seconds, the policeman starts running behind the thief at a certain speed. If the policeman covered 864 meters distance to reach the thief, then the speed (in m/s) of the policeman is:
questions.explanation: In 12 seconds the thief gets 18 × 12 = 216 m ahead. The policeman's 864 m takes as long as the thief's 864 − 216 = 648 m, i.e. 648/18 = 36 s, so his speed is 864/36 = 24 m/s.

questions.text: Three numbers are in the ratio of 6:7:3 and their LCM is 3654.Their HCF is:
questions.explanation: The numbers are 6x, 7x and 3x, so their LCM is 42x = 3654 and x = 87. As 6, 7 and 3 have no common factor, the HCF is x = 87.

questions.text: Two trains, 148 m and 152 m long, are running towards each other on parallel lines at 62 km/h and 46km/h, respectively. In what time will they be clear of each other from the moment they meet?
questions.explanation: Moving towards each other, the relative speed is 62 + 46 = 108 km/h = 30 m/s. They must cover 148 + 152 = 300 m: 300/30 = 10 seconds.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
In a college, 20% of the number of boys are equal to the three-fourth of the number of girls. What is the ratio of boys and girls in that college ?
The ratio of the present age of A and B is 3 : 1. Five years ago, the ratio of their ages was 5 : 1. The age of A (in years) after eight years will be:
questions.explanation: Let the ages be 3x and x. (3x − 5)/(x − 5) = 5 gives 3x − 5 = 5x − 25, so x = 10 and A is 30. In eight years A will be 38.

questions.text: The average monthly expenditure of a family was ₹8,600 during the first three months, ₹9,750 during the next four months and ₹9,920 during the last five months of a year. If the total savings during the year was ₹65,300, the average monthly income (in ₹) of the family was:
A sum invested at 5% simple interest per annum grows to ₹806 in 6 years. If the amount remains the same, how much will it grow at a 12% simple interest rate in 5 years?
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 7% per year rate of interest for 5 years.
The average monthly income of A and B is ₹3,590. The average monthly income of B and C is ₹4,250. The average monthly income of A and C is ₹6,500. What is the monthly income of C?
A man sells an article at a certain price and suffers a loss of 20%. If he sells the article at ₹100 more, he gets a profit of 30%. Find the cost price of the article (in ₹).
questions.explanation: Going from a 20% loss to a 30% profit is a swing of 50% of the cost price, which is ₹100: so the cost price is ₹200.

questions.text: What should come in place of ? in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? ACE ,FHJ, KMO, PRT , ?
questions.explanation: First letters move 5 places forward (A, F, K, P, so next U), and within each cluster the letters go up by two (ACE, FHJ): UWY.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the center (but not necessarily in the same order). C is sitting to the immediate right of E. D is sitting third to the left of C. A is the immediate neighbour of B and C. F is not the immediate neighbour of E. What is the position of G with respect to A?
questions.explanation: Going round to the right from E the seats are E, C, A, B, F, D, G (C on E's immediate right, D third to C's left, A between C and B, and F, who is not next to E, beside D). Counting to A's left: C, E, G, so G is third to the left.

questions.text: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). A is sitting second to the right of E. Only one person is sitting between D and A. B is sitting third to the right of G. F is an immediate neighbour of B. How many people are sitting between D and E when counted from the left of E?
questions.explanation: Going round to the right from E the seats are E, C, A, G, D, F, B (A second to E's right, D two seats beyond A, B third to G's right with F beside it). Counting to E's left: B, F, then D, so two people sit between them.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some chickens are hens. No hen is an egg. Conclusions: (I) No chicken is an egg. (II) All hens are chickens.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: The chickens that are hens are not eggs, but nothing is said about any other chickens, so I does not follow. Nothing says every hen is a chicken, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: HFLI is related to OMSP in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, KIOL is related to RPVS. To which of the following is MKQN related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 7 places forward: H → O, F → M, L → S, I → P, and KIOL → RPVS likewise. So MKQN → TRXU.

questions.text: What should come in place of '?' in the given series? -12, +24, -48, +96, ?, +384
questions.explanation: Each term is the one before multiplied by −2: +96 × (−2) = −192, and −192 × (−2) = +384.

questions.text: In a code language, 'COLONY' is coded as '48' and 'INTERCHANGE' is coded as '88'. How will 'MOUNTAIN' be coded in the same language?
questions.explanation: The code is 8 times the number of letters: COLONY (6 letters) → 48 and INTERCHANGE (11) → 88. MOUNTAIN has 8 letters: 64.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: No bus is a car. No car is a truck. Conclusions: (I) No car is a bus. (II) No truck is a car.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: A universal negative works both ways: 'No bus is a car' means no car is a bus (I), and 'No car is a truck' means no truck is a car (II). Both follow.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 39 ÷ 3 – 24 + 60 × 12 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 39 × 3 + 24 − 60 ÷ 12 = 117 + 24 − 5 = 136.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘WING’ is coded as ‘2618’ and ‘NEAT’ is coded as ‘3469’. What is the code for ‘N’ in that language?
questions.explanation: N is the only letter in both words and 6 the only digit in both codes, so N = 6.

questions.text: JM12 is related to EH15 in a certain way. In the same way, QT34 is related to LO37. To which of the following is SV 23 related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Both letters move 5 places back and the number rises by 3: JM12 → EH15 and QT34 → LO37. So SV 23 → NQ26.

questions.text: 7 is related to 30 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 14 is related to 100. To which of the following is 22 related following the same logic? (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is 10 times (the first minus 4): 10 × 3 = 30 and 10 × 10 = 100. So 22 → 10 × 18 = 180.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘I swim fast’ is coded as ‘cp lk bs’ and ‘may I go’ is coded as ‘ap sb lk’. How is ‘I’ coded in that code language?
questions.explanation: 'I' is the only word in both sentences and 'lk' the only code in both, so I = lk.

questions.text: In a code language, 'CAKE' is written as ‘ACIG’ and 'GOLD' is written as 'EQJF'. How will 'WIRE' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move −2, +2, −2, +2: CAKE → ACIG and GOLD → EQJF. So WIRE → UKPG.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying etc. to 13, can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (4, 35, 11) (1, 82, 61)
questions.explanation: In each set the middle number is the sum of the other two plus 20: 4 + 11 + 20 = 35 and 1 + 61 + 20 = 82. Likewise 13 + 20 + 20 = 53.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 5 ÷ 6 × 3 – 4 + 11 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 5 × 6 ÷ 3 + 4 − 11 = 10 + 4 − 11 = 3.

questions.text: In which state/union territory is Losar celebrated to mark the start of the new year in that region?
questions.explanation: Losar, the Buddhist new-year festival, is celebrated in Ladakh.

questions.text: Who was the captain of Royal Challengers Bangalore in the Women's Premier League event 2023?
questions.explanation: Smriti Mandhana captained Royal Challengers Bangalore in the first Women's Premier League in 2023.

questions.text: As of 31st October 2023, the senior-most member (in terms of age) in the 17th Lok Sabha, Shafiqur Rahman Barq represents which political party?
questions.explanation: Shafiqur Rahman Barq, MP for Sambhal in Uttar Pradesh, belonged to the Samajwadi Party.

questions.text: With reference to medieval Indian architecture style, what is ‘Pietra Dura’?
options: Decorating the walls with floral designs made of semi-precious stones
Oil paintings on the walls of Taj Mahal
Fine quality clothes used by the Mughals
Sculpture art of the Mauryan period
questions.explanation: Pietra dura is the inlay of cut and polished semi-precious stones in marble to form floral designs, as on the Taj Mahal.

questions.text: What is the chemical formula for sodium bicarbonate?
questions.explanation: Sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) is NaHCO₃. Na₂CO₃ is sodium carbonate (washing soda), NaOH sodium hydroxide and NaCl common salt.

questions.text: How many countries share their land borders with India?
questions.explanation: India shares land borders with seven countries: Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Myanmar.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following books is written by Dadabhai Naoroji?
options: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji's 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901) set out his drain theory: that British rule was draining India's wealth.

questions.text: The chemical compound present in turmeric is:
questions.explanation: Curcumin gives turmeric its yellow colour; capsaicin is the hot compound in chillies.

questions.text: Which of the following dynasties established the Vijayanagara kingdom in fourteenth century?
questions.explanation: Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty founded the Vijayanagara kingdom in 1336; the Saluva, Tuluva and Aravidu dynasties followed.

questions.text: With which sport is Sanjana Bathula associated?
questions.explanation: Sanjana Bathula is an Indian roller speed skater; she was part of India's women's 3000 m relay squad at the Hangzhou Asian Games in 2023.

questions.text: The historical fiction ‘The Glory of Patan’ by KM Munshi was originally written in which Indian language?
questions.explanation: K. M. Munshi wrote 'Patan ni Prabhuta' in Gujarati; 'The Glory of Patan' is its English translation.

questions.text: The Rabi season of agriculture begins in October-November and ends in __________.
questions.explanation: The rabi season begins with the onset of winter in October-November and ends in March-April; its cool weather suits wheat, gram and mustard.

questions.text: On which date did Punjab abolish the Legislative Council?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 1 January 1970, the date usually given for the abolition of Punjab's Legislative Council, its upper house, under the Punjab Legislative Council (Abolition) Act, 1969.

questions.text: Which Union Territory had minimum literacy rate as per 2011 Census?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Dadra and Nagar Haveli had the lowest literacy rate of the Union Territories, about 76%.

questions.text: Kanak Rele, who established Nalanda Dance Research Centre, was a performer of which of the following classical dance forms of India?
questions.explanation: Kanak Rele, who founded the Nalanda Dance Research Centre in Mumbai, was a leading exponent of Mohiniyattam.

questions.text: Who among the following established the Indore gharana?
questions.explanation: The Indore gharana of Hindustani vocal music was founded by Ustad Amir Khan.

questions.text: The red colour of tomatoes is due to the presence of:
questions.explanation: Lycopene, a red carotenoid pigment, colours ripe tomatoes.

questions.text: Which of the following is one of the features of capital goods?
questions.explanation: Capital goods, such as machinery and buildings, are durable: they are used in production over many years.

questions.text: In 1976, in which Part of the Indian Constitution under Article 51A were Fundamental Duties added?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) added Part IV A, whose Article 51A lists the Fundamental Duties.

questions.text: What is the decreasing order of the Padma awards?
options: Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, Padma Vibhushan
Padma Shri, Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan
Padma Bhushan, Padma Shri, Padma Vibhushan
Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan, Padma Shri
questions.explanation: Padma Vibhushan ranks highest, then Padma Bhushan, then Padma Shri.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following acts introduced the system of dyarchy in the provincial administration in India?
options: The Government of India Act of 1909
The Government of India Act of 1947
The Government of India Act of 1935
The Government of India Act of 1919
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act, 1919 (the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) introduced dyarchy in the provinces; the 1935 Act ended it there.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is/are correct about the famous place Mawsynram? A. It is the wettest place on the earth. B. It is located in Meghalaya state of India.
options: Neither A nor B is correct.
A and B both are correct.
questions.explanation: Mawsynram, in Meghalaya's East Khasi Hills, receives the highest average annual rainfall of any place on earth, so both statements are correct.

questions.text: Who was the founder of the Mauryan dynasty?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Mauryan dynasty in the late 4th century BC; Bindusara and Ashoka were his son and grandson.

questions.text: In which part of India is cool mountain climate observed?
questions.explanation: The Himalayan regions of the north have a cool mountain climate, as temperatures fall with altitude.

questions.text: The Pharmacy (Amendment) Bill, 2023 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 3 August 2023, which amends the ____________.
questions.explanation: The Bill amends the Pharmacy Act, 1948, which regulates the profession of pharmacy, so that pharmacists registered under the Jammu and Kashmir Pharmacy Act, 2011 can be registered under it.

questions.text: Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error. The “accideent” on the highway caused a long traffic jam.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'accident'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Accepting how wonderful you truly are and incorporating this _______ into your attitude and personality is perhaps one of the most difficult things to do in life.
questions.explanation: Accepting how wonderful you are is an 'insight', an understanding, to build into your attitude; 'folly', 'craziness' and 'glitch' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error. The rainbow only appears after a “hurican”.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'hurricane'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A piece of cake
options: A cake that broke into pieces
A cake which is sold as a piece
A slice of cake for eating
questions.explanation: 'A piece of cake' is something very easy to do.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Cultural heritage is the lifeblood of any ________ and serves as a link between generations.
questions.explanation: Cultural heritage links the generations of a 'civilisation'; 'believe' is a verb, and 'lethargy' and 'birthright' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'consistent'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'pursue' from the given sentence. Dr. Kalam's success in the field of science has inspired young Indians to dream big and chase those dreams with immense hard work.
questions.explanation: To 'pursue' a dream is to 'chase' it.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a phrasal verb error. Mrs. Premlatha asked / Malini to hand down / all the / payment slips.
questions.explanation: To 'hand down' is to pass something on to a later generation; slips are 'handed in' (submitted) or 'handed over'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. My secretary is disposed of / discuss everything in great detail / before she begins / the actual work.
questions.explanation: 'Disposed to' (inclined to) takes a verb: 'My secretary is disposed to discuss everything'. 'Disposed of' means got rid of.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Please listen to all announcements _______.
questions.explanation: Announcements should be listened to 'attentively', with full attention.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He is _________ tired to finish his homework.
questions.explanation: 'Too … to' says a quality is excessive for a result: 'too tired to finish'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Energy
questions.explanation: 'Energy' is the 'power' to act or work.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. One of them contains an error. Select the segment that contains the error from the given options. Neither Smith / nor Rose / were in / the classroom.
questions.explanation: With 'neither … nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject, here the singular 'Rose': 'Neither Smith nor Rose was in the classroom.'

questions.text: Select the sentence that has a grammatical error.
options: He works as a software developer.
The sun rises in the east.
We watches movies every Friday night.
questions.explanation: 'We' takes the plural verb: 'We watch movies every Friday night.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The detective's job was to “discern” the truth from the web of lies.
questions.explanation: To 'discern' is to 'perceive' or recognise clearly.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The workers had been repairing / the mall road in / town for / several days now.
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and is still going on 'now' takes the present perfect continuous: 'The workers have been repairing'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Ecstatic
questions.explanation: 'Ecstatic' means extremely 'happy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word The project’s tight deadline and complex requirements made it a “gruelling” task for the team.
questions.explanation: A 'gruelling' task is exhausting and demanding: 'challenging'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate verb form to fill in the blank. Arun __________ his bicycle to school every day.
questions.explanation: A habitual action takes the simple present, and the singular subject 'Arun' takes 'rides'.

questions.text: What does it imply when people say to ‘read between the lines’?
options: To skip initial and final lines in a paragraph
To read with an ability to infer the meaning
questions.explanation: To 'read between the lines' is to infer a meaning that is not stated openly.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. My next pet, Ari, was a pigeon. He became convinced that he was not a bird at all and refused to ____ 1 ___. If he wanted to get on a table or a chair, he stood below it, cooing until someone picked him up. He would even try to come ____ 2____ walks with us. This, however, we had to stop for, _____ 3____ you carried him on your shoulder or else you let him walk behind. If you let him walk, you had to slow down your own ______ 4_____ to suit his, for should you get too far ahead, you would find him running after you, cooing frantically, his chest pouted out with ______5_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Convinced that he was not a bird, Ari refused to 'fly': he waited to be lifted onto tables and chairs instead.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. My next pet, Ari, was a pigeon. He became convinced that he was not a bird at all and refused to ____ 1 ___. If he wanted to get on a table or a chair, he stood below it, cooing until someone picked him up. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: One goes 'on' a walk: he would even try to come on walks with us.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. My next pet, Ari, was a pigeon. He became convinced that he was not a bird at all and refused to ____ 1 ___. If he wanted to get on a table or a chair, he stood below it, cooing until someone picked him up. If you let him walk, you had to slow down your own ______ 4_____ to suit his, for should you get too far ahead, you would find him running after you, cooing frantically, his chest pouted out with ______5_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Either' pairs with 'or else' to offer two choices: either you carried him or else you let him walk behind.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. My next pet, Ari, was a pigeon. He became convinced that he was not a bird at all and refused to ____ 1 ___. If he wanted to get on a table or a chair, he stood below it, cooing until someone picked him up. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: You slowed your own 'pace', your walking speed, to suit his; 'peace', 'piece' and 'space' make no sense here.
