If you let him walk, you had to slow down your own ______ 4_____ to suit his, for should you get too far ahead, you would find him running after you, cooing frantically, his chest pouted out with ______5_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Left behind, he ran after you with his chest puffed out in 'indignation', anger at being treated unfairly.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: A policeman chases a thief. The speed of the policeman and thief are 10 kmph and 8 kmph, respectively. If the policeman started 15 minutes late, find the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief.
questions.explanation: In the 15 minutes the thief gets 8 × 15/60 = 2 km ahead. The policeman gains 10 − 8 = 2 km/h on him, so he takes 2/2 = 1 hour: 60 minutes.

questions.text: A shot-put made of iron with a diameter of 12 cm is melted into a solid cylinder with a height of 2 cm. What is the diameter of the cylinder made?
questions.explanation: The shot-put's volume is (4/3)π × 6³ = 288π cm³. With height 2 cm, πr² × 2 = 288π, so r² = 144, r = 12 cm and the diameter is 24 cm.

questions.text: An oil dealer had three types of oil. 403 litres of the first kind, 434 litres of the second kind and 465 litres of the third kind. Find the maximum volume of oil, filled in each barrel, if equal number of barrels are filled.
questions.explanation: The largest volume that divides all three exactly is their HCF: 403 = 31 × 13, 434 = 31 × 14 and 465 = 31 × 15, so 31 litres.

questions.text: The marked price of a scooter is ₹1,80,000. The shopkeeper gave a scheme discount of 4% on ₹1,20,000 and 2.5% on the remaining amount. The selling price (in ₹) of the scooter is:
Rohan deposited ₹500 for 2 years, ₹650 for 4 years and ₹1,300 for 6 years, at the same rate of interest. He received the total simple interest of ₹1,140. What is the rate of interest per annum?
In an election contested by two candidates, one candidate got 25% of the total votes and still lost by 20,000 votes. Find the total number of votes cast? (all votes are valid)
questions.explanation: The winner got 75% and the loser 25%, so the margin, 50% of the votes, is 20,000: 40,000 votes were cast.

questions.text: A policeman follows a thief, who is 150 metres ahead of him., and they run at the speed of 6 km/h and 5 km/h, respectively.What distance does the policeman cover to catch up with the thief?
questions.explanation: The policeman gains 6 − 5 = 1 km/h, so he closes the 150 m (0.15 km) in 0.15 hours. In that time he runs 6 × 0.15 = 0.9 km = 900 metres.

questions.text: A dishonest shopkeeper claims to sell rice at the cost price of ₹95 per kg, but the weight he uses has 1 kg written on it, while it actually weighs 950 gm. The profit he thus earns on selling rice having an actual weight of 95 kg rice is:
questions.explanation: Each '1 kg' he sells is 950 g, so 95 kg of rice goes out as 95/0.95 = 100 'kg' for 100 × 95 = ₹9,500. It cost him 95 × 95 = ₹9,025: a profit of ₹475.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2500 as a sum borrowed at 6% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
A right circular cone of height h and radius R is cut by a plane parallel to the base at a distance h/4 from the base. The ratio of the curved surface areas of the resulting cone to the frustum is:
questions.explanation: The cone cut off at the top has height 3h/4, so its radius and slant height are 3/4 of the original's and its curved surface is (3/4)² = 9/16 of the whole. The frustum has the other 7/16: 9 : 7.

questions.text: Find the area of a square whose diagonal is of 14 cm length.
questions.explanation: Area of a square = diagonal²/2 = 14²/2 = 98 cm².

questions.text: The mean (rounded off to two decimal place) of the first 6 odd prime numbers is:
questions.explanation: The first six odd primes are 3, 5, 7, 11, 13 and 17. Their sum is 56, and 56/6 = 9.33.

questions.text: The average of the sales of an electronics shop in the years 1991, 1992, 1993 and 1994 is 2000, and that for the years 1992, 1993, 1994 and 1995 is 2200. If the sales in 1995 are 1800, find the sales in 1991.
questions.explanation: The 1991-94 total is 4 × 2000 = 8000 and the 1992-95 total 4 × 2200 = 8800. The difference, 800, is the 1995 sales minus the 1991 sales, so 1991 = 1800 − 800 = 1000.

questions.text: In the first 5 overs of a T-20 international cricket match, the run rate was only 5.6. What should be the run rate (approximately) in the remaining 15 overs to reach a target of 185 runs?
questions.explanation: 5 overs at 5.6 an over gave 28 runs, so 185 − 28 = 157 are needed from 15 overs: 157/15 = 10.466… an over, and 10.46 is the nearest option.

questions.text: In a mock test conducted by a coaching institute, 20 students average scored 75% marks and the remaining 15 students average scored 54% marks. Find the average score.
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3500 as a sum borrowed at 5% per year rate of interest for 5 years.
TAHO is related to XELS in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, HOVC is related to LSZG. To which of the following is NUBI related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places forward: T → X, A → E, H → L, O → S and H → L, O → S, V → Z, C → G. So N → R, U → Y, B → F and I → M: RYFM.

questions.text: 12 is related to 59 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 17 is related to 79. To which ofthe following is 24 related, following the same logic?(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbersinto its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The second number is four times the first plus 11: 12 × 4 + 11 = 59 and 17 × 4 + 11 = 79. Likewise 24 × 4 + 11 = 107.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (20, 76, 91) (87, 41, 123)
questions.explanation: The third number is the sum of the first two minus 5: 20 + 76 − 5 = 91 and 87 + 41 − 5 = 123. Likewise 84 + 47 − 5 = 126.

questions.text: What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 140 × 2 − 4 ÷ 56 + 82 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 140 ÷ 2 + 4 × 56 − 82 = 70 + 224 − 82 = 212.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order? EGC, IFG, MEK, QDO, ?
questions.explanation: First letters move 4 forward (E, I, M, Q, so U); second letters 1 back (G, F, E, D, so C); third letters 4 forward (C, G, K, O, so S): UCS.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusion(s) logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: Some metals are iron. Some iron are steel. Conclusions: (I) Some metals are steel. (II) All steel are iron.
questions.explanation: The iron that is metal need not be the iron that is steel, so (I) does not follow; and 'some iron are steel' leaves room for steel that is not iron, so (II) does not follow either.

questions.text: Rajan, Pragyan, Kamal, Sachin, Ashok, Narendra, and Laksh are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Rajan sits 3rd to the right of Narendra. Kamal sits 2nd to the right of Rajan. Ashok is an immediate neighbour of Narendra. Pragyan sits to the immediate right of Sachin. Who is sitting 3rd to the left of Narendra?
questions.explanation: Going round to the right from Narendra: Narendra, Sachin, Pragyan, Rajan, Laksh, Kamal, Ashok. (Rajan is third to his right and Kamal second to Rajan's right; only with Ashok on Narendra's left do Sachin and Pragyan find two adjacent free seats.) Third to Narendra's left is Laksh.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘FAST’ is coded as ‘6842’ and ‘TILE’ is coded as ‘5761’.What is the code for ‘T’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: T is the only letter in both words and 6 the only digit in both codes, so T = 6.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘checked his mirror’ is written as ‘aw ar ae’ and ‘book inevitably mirror’ is coded as ‘al aw ao’. How is ‘mirror’ coded in that language?
questions.explanation: 'mirror' is the only word in both sentences and 'aw' the only code in both, so mirror = aw.

questions.text: P, Q, R, S, T, U, V and W are sitting around a circular table facing the centre(but not necessarily in the same order). P is sitting to the immediate right of V and third to the left of U. S is sitting fourth to the right of Q, who is not an immediate neighbour of P and T. Q is sitting to the second right of U. R is sitting to the immediate right of Q and second to the left of P. How many people are sitting between R and T when counted from the left of T?
questions.explanation: Going round to the right from P: P, S, T, U, W, Q, R, V. (V is on P's left and U third to P's right; Q is second to U's right, R next to Q and S fourth from Q; T cannot sit beside Q, so T takes the seat between S and U.) Counting leftwards from T, S, P and V come before R: three.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some hooks are rags. All rags are bottles. Conclusions: (I) Some bottles are hooks. (II) All bottles are rags.
questions.explanation: Some hooks are rags and all rags are bottles, so some hooks are bottles: (I) follows. There may be bottles that are not rags, so (II) does not.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 34 51 85 102 136 ?
GMIE is related to HNJF in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, KQMI is related to LRNJ. To which of the following is NTPL related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 1 place forward: G → H, M → N, I → J, E → F and K → L, Q → R, M → N, I → J. So NTPL → OUQM.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘will make you’ is written as ‘ft fy fd’ and ‘you see what’ is writtenas ‘fi fo ft’. How will ‘you’ be writtenin the given language?
questions.explanation: 'you' is the only word in both sentences and 'ft' the only code in both, so you = ft.

questions.text: Calculate the revenue receipts from the following information. Revenue deficit= 2.80% of GDP Revenue expenditure= 10.80% of GDP
questions.explanation: Revenue receipts = revenue expenditure − revenue deficit = 10.80% − 2.80% = 8.00% of GDP.

questions.text: How many cities have been selected to be developed as sustainable and responsible destinations as per the Swadesh Darshan 2.0 scheme launched by the Union Ministry of Tourism in January 2023?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 30, the number of cities (in 15 states) reported as shortlisted for the first phase of Swadesh Darshan 2.0. Later official lists of its destinations are longer.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In 1928, who among the following wrote the Congress Party’s Nehru Report, a future constitution for independent India, based on the granting of dominion status?
questions.explanation: The Nehru Report (1928), which asked for dominion status, was drafted by an All Parties Conference committee chaired by Motilal Nehru, after whom it is named; Jawaharlal Nehru was its secretary.

questions.text: The autobiography 'Wings of Fire' chronicles the life of which notable Indian personality?
questions.explanation: 'Wings of Fire', written with Arun Tiwari, is A.P.J. Abdul Kalam's autobiography.

questions.text: In animal cells, the breakdown of very long chain fatty acids through β-oxidation is conducted by which of the following organelles?
questions.explanation: Peroxisomes shorten very long chain fatty acids by β-oxidation; mitochondria oxidise the shorter chains.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes the nature of the Indian Constitution?
options: Very rigid and difficult to amend
questions.explanation: The Constitution is a blend of rigidity and flexibility: some provisions can be amended by a simple majority of Parliament, others need a special majority, and some also need ratification by half the states.

questions.text: Which programme, that was introduced in the year 2000-2001, aims to offer homes, drinking water, primary education and basic healthcare in rural areas?
options: The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
questions.explanation: The Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana, launched in 2000-01, funded primary health, primary education, rural shelter, rural drinking water, nutrition and rural electrification.

questions.text: Which of the following dances is traditionally performed by the males of three adjacent states - Jharkhand, Odisha and West Bengal?
questions.explanation: Chhau is danced by men in three styles: Purulia in West Bengal, Seraikella in Jharkhand and Mayurbhanj in Odisha.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following revolutionaries, who was arrested in Lahore conspiracy case by the British Government of India, was martyred in the hunger strike of 63 days in jail?
questions.explanation: Jatindra Nath Das, arrested in the Lahore Conspiracy Case, died in Lahore jail on 13 September 1929, on the 63rd day of his hunger strike.

questions.text: The term 'foot fault' is associated with which of the following games?
questions.explanation: In tennis a foot fault is called when the server's foot touches the baseline or the court inside it before the ball is struck.

questions.text: Which of the following dams is a part of the Damodar Valley Corporation?
questions.explanation: Maithon Dam, on the Barakar, is one of the Damodar Valley Corporation's dams. Rihand is in Uttar Pradesh, Koyna in Maharashtra and Salal, on the Chenab, in Jammu and Kashmir.

questions.text: When a large amount of carbon dioxide dissolves in a water body, the water becomes acidic because of the formation of which of the following acids?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide reacts with water to form carbonic acid (H₂CO₃), which makes the water acidic.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECT pair of molecule/formula units and their molar mass from the following.
questions.explanation: HNO₃ has a molar mass of 1 + 14 + 3 × 16 = 63, not 62. NaCl (23 + 35.5 = 58.5), CH₄ (12 + 4 = 16) and HCl (1 + 35.5 = 36.5) are right.

questions.text: The Patkai hills are part of the ____________ mountains.
questions.explanation: The Patkai hills, on the India-Myanmar border, belong to the Purvachal, the eastern hills of the Himalayas, with the Naga, Manipur and Mizo hills.

questions.text: In which of the following events did India get its first individual Olympic gold medal?
questions.explanation: Abhinav Bindra won the 10 m air rifle gold at Beijing 2008, India's first individual Olympic gold.

questions.text: In the 1991 Census, which state was the highest in rank in terms of literacy rate and held higher than the national average of literacy rate?
questions.explanation: In the 1991 Census Kerala had the highest literacy rate, 89.81%, against the national 52.21%.

questions.text: Raga Deepak has been associated with which famous musician?
questions.explanation: Legend has it that Tansen, the musician of Akbar's court, sang Raga Deepak so well that the lamps lit themselves.

questions.text: As per Article 181, the ___________ can not preside while a resolution for his removal from office is under consideration in State Legislative Assembly.
questions.explanation: Under Article 181 the Speaker (or the Deputy Speaker) of a State Legislative Assembly may not preside while a resolution for his removal from office is under consideration.

questions.text: The 'Bathukamma' festival is associated with which state?
questions.explanation: Bathukamma, a floral festival celebrated by women during Navaratri, is the state festival of Telangana.

questions.text: Which organelle contains ribosomal RNA and is involved in the production of ribosomes?
questions.explanation: The nucleolus, inside the nucleus, makes ribosomal RNA and assembles the subunits of ribosomes.

questions.text: Who was the court poet of king Harshavardhana?
questions.explanation: Banabhatta, author of the 'Harshacharita' and 'Kadambari', was Harshavardhana's court poet. Ravikirti served the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II.

questions.text: Balban’s rule as an absolute despot led to which of the following events?
questions.explanation: Balban, who ruled as an absolute monarch, broke the power of the Chahalgani, the Forty Turkish nobles.

questions.text: Which of the following institutes/projects is declared as a masterpiece of oral and intangible heritage of humanity by UNESCO in May 2001?
questions.explanation: Kutiyattam, the Sanskrit theatre of Kerala, was among the first Masterpieces of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity proclaimed by UNESCO in May 2001.

questions.text: In September 2023, after the retirement of Incumbent Sanjay Kumar Mishra, who was appointed as In-charge Director of ED?
questions.explanation: Rahul Navin, a 1993-batch IRS officer and Special Director of the ED, was made its in-charge Director in September 2023 when Sanjay Kumar Mishra's term ended.

questions.text: Which of the following architectural elements is excluded from the construction sites of the Indus Valley Civilisation?
questions.explanation: The Harappans built with baked and sun-dried bricks and used gypsum mortar, but iron was unknown to them: theirs was a Bronze Age civilisation.

questions.text: One of the four underlined words in the given sentence is incorrectly spelt. Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word. Let us “appreciate”, support and “contribute” our might to the “promotional” efforts of the “comunity”.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'community'.

questions.text: Select the option that has an error in the use of phrasal verb.
options: Clean up the mess in the kitchen. It is unhygienic.
We look forward to seeing you during the event.
To earn a significant profit, you are advised to deal in electronic items.
Why does she break out with all her near and dear ones?
questions.explanation: To end a relationship with someone is to 'break up with' them; 'break out' means to begin suddenly or to escape.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. The company plans to “expand” its operations into global markets soon.
questions.explanation: To 'expand' is to make larger; its opposite is 'restrict', to keep within limits.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Triumph
questions.explanation: The opposite of 'triumph' (success) is 'failure'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word. I cannot see without my “glasses”.
options: A device used to correct the defects of vision
questions.explanation: 'Glasses' here are spectacles: lenses in a frame that correct defects of vision.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the idiom from the options given below. To show the white feather
questions.explanation: To 'show the white feather' is to show cowardice.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. After their disagreement, they decided to “saparate” their belongings and part ways.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'separate'.

questions.text: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.
options: An unexpected power failure completely foiled an plan of the team.
An unexpected power failure completely foiled the plan of the team.
A unexpected power failure completely foiled the plan of a team.
An unexpected power failure completely foiled a plan of a team.
questions.explanation: SSC's key picks 'foiled the plan of the team'. 'An' goes before a vowel sound and 'a' before a consonant sound, so 'an plan' and 'a unexpected' are wrong; 'a plan of a team' is not ungrammatical, but a particular plan of a particular team takes 'the'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. My brother trains young girls at the football academy, whereas I gets a handsome salary to teach mathematics at the same place.
options: to teach mathematics at the same place
questions.explanation: The subject 'I' takes 'get', not 'gets': 'whereas I get a handsome salary'.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. The bread was “drier” and stale.
questions.explanation: Nothing is being compared, so the positive degree is needed, like 'stale': 'The bread was dry and stale.'

questions.text: In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. Johannes Gutenberg invented the first printing press that could print thousands of ______________ a day. This made books cheaper and information ______________ widely available.
questions.explanation: 'Thousands of' needs a plural noun, 'pages', and the comparison with the time before the press calls for 'more widely available'.

questions.text: In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative. All in all, he had the “more splendid” collection of antique paintings ever.
questions.explanation: 'Ever' compares the collection with all others, which needs the superlative: 'the most splendid collection of antique paintings ever'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The scientist conducted a series of experiments to _______ his hypothesis.
questions.explanation: Experiments are carried out to 'verify', that is confirm, a hypothesis.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Reverent
questions.explanation: 'Reverent' means feeling or showing deep respect: 'respectful'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I “long from travel” outside the country, dreaming of adventures among the towering Alps and basking in the turquoise waters of the Caribbean.
questions.explanation: For an action one yearns to do, 'long' takes a to-infinitive: 'I long to travel outside the country'. 'Long for' normally takes a plain noun ('long for home'), and 'long from' and 'long at' are not used.

questions.text: Rectify the sentence by selecting the correct spelling from the options. All the political parties of India appaer lost in the physical exercise of fighting elections.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'appear'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A building where animals are butchered
questions.explanation: An abattoir is a slaughterhouse, where animals are killed for meat.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. They all felt that the movie was truly “captivating” and unforgettable.
questions.explanation: 'Captivating' means charming and attractive; its opposite is 'repugnant', causing strong dislike.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Although she is usually / rude with everyone, / she behaved nice / with all of us today.
questions.explanation: The verb 'behaved' needs an adverb: 'she behaved nicely'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. She is “someone who always discourages our enthusiasm;” therefore, we have decided to keep our distance from her.
questions.explanation: A 'wet blanket' is someone who spoils other people's enthusiasm or fun.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Goddess Shailputri is the first form of Goddess Durga, who is worshipped ____(1)___ Navaratri. In this form, she is worshipped as the daughter of ___(2)__ Himalayas. She is the goddess ___(3)____ nature and is adorned with flowers. She ___(4)__ a bull and holds a trident in one hand and a lotus flower in another. During Navaratri, nine different forms of Durga are worshipped. Durga is a ___(5)__, ___(6)___, ___(7)___ deity who is also known as Adishakti—the energy that manifested to create the universe.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'During' names the period in which something happens: 'worshipped during Navaratri'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Goddess Shailputri is the first form of Goddess Durga, who is worshipped ____(1)___ Navaratri. In this form, she is worshipped as the daughter of ___(2)__ Himalayas. She is the goddess ___(3)____ nature and is adorned with flowers. She ___(4)__ a bull and holds a trident in one hand and a lotus flower in another. During Navaratri, nine different forms of Durga are worshipped. Durga is a ___(5)__, ___(6)___, ___(7)___ deity who is also known as Adishakti—the energy that manifested to create the universe.

Select the most appropriate article to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Names of mountain ranges take 'the': 'the daughter of the Himalayas'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Goddess Shailputri is the first form of Goddess Durga, who is worshipped ____(1)___ Navaratri. In this form, she is worshipped as the daughter of ___(2)__ Himalayas. She is the goddess ___(3)____ nature and is adorned with flowers. She ___(4)__ a bull and holds a trident in one hand and a lotus flower in another. During Navaratri, nine different forms of Durga are worshipped. Durga is a ___(5)__, ___(6)___, ___(7)___ deity who is also known as Adishakti—the energy that manifested to create the universe.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Of' links the goddess to what she presides over: 'the goddess of nature'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Goddess Shailputri is the first form of Goddess Durga, who is worshipped ____(1)___ Navaratri. In this form, she is worshipped as the daughter of ___(2)__ Himalayas. She is the goddess ___(3)____ nature and is adorned with flowers. She ___(4)__ a bull and holds a trident in one hand and a lotus flower in another. During Navaratri, nine different forms of Durga are worshipped. Durga is a ___(5)__, ___(6)___, ___(7)___ deity who is also known as Adishakti—the energy that manifested to create the universe.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The passage describes her in the simple present ('holds a trident'), so 'She rides a bull'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Goddess Shailputri is the first form of Goddess Durga, who is worshipped ____(1)___ Navaratri. In this form, she is worshipped as the daughter of ___(2)__ Himalayas. She is the goddess ___(3)____ nature and is adorned with flowers. She ___(4)__ a bull and holds a trident in one hand and a lotus flower in another. During Navaratri, nine different forms of Durga are worshipped. Durga is a ___(5)__, ___(6)___, ___(7)___ deity who is also known as Adishakti—the energy that manifested to create the universe.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blanks number 5.
questions.explanation: An adjective of origin follows adjectives of opinion or quality, so 'Indian' comes last: 'a powerful, radiant, Indian deity'.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Sharad invested two equal amounts for 6 years and 3 years at the rate of 7% and 9% per annum, respectively. The sum of their simple interest is ₹1,587. The invested amount (in ₹) by Sharad is:
questions.explanation: With P in each, the two interests total P × 7 × 6/100 + P × 9 × 3/100 = 0.69P, so 0.69P = 1,587 and P = ₹2,300. The two equal amounts total ₹4,600.

questions.text: In a park there are rabbits and pigeons in the ratio 4 : 9. If legs are counted, the total number of legs is 340. Find the number of rabbits.
questions.explanation: Rabbits have 4 legs and pigeons 2: 4 × 4x + 2 × 9x = 34x = 340, so x = 10 and there are 4 × 10 = 40 rabbits.

questions.text: By selling an article for ₹19.5, a dealer makes a profit of 10%. By how much should he increase his selling price (in ₹, rounded off to two decimal place) so as to make a profit of 50%?
questions.explanation: CP = 19.5/1.1 = ₹17.727. For a 50% profit the price must be 1.5 × 17.727 = ₹26.59, an increase of 26.59 − 19.5 = ₹7.09.

questions.text: The speed of a boat in still water is 13 km/h and the speed of the stream is 4 km/h. How much more time will it take in going upstream than ingoing downstream a distance of 68 km? (Correct to the nearest minute)
questions.explanation: Upstream the boat makes 13 − 4 = 9 km/h and downstream 13 + 4 = 17 km/h. 68/9 − 68/17 = 7.556 − 4 = 3.556 hours, about 3 h 33 min.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹2000 as a sum borrowed at 9% per year rate of interest for 2 years.

In a circular race of 1500 m, P and Q start from the same point and at the same time, at speeds of 20 km/h and 35 km/h, respectively. After what time will they meet for the first time on the track if they are running in the same direction?
questions.explanation: Running the same way, Q gains 35 − 20 = 15 km/h = 25/6 m/s on P. They meet when Q has gained one full lap: 1,500 × 6/25 = 360 seconds.

questions.text: Three numbers are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5 and their HCF is 60. The numbers are:
questions.explanation: The numbers are 3k, 4k and 5k, whose HCF is k (3, 4 and 5 have no common factor). With k = 60 they are 180, 240 and 300.

questions.text: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹3000 as a sum borrowed at 9% per year rate of interest for 3 years.
The average weight of a family of five members (in kg) whose weights are 40 kg, 49 kg, 56 kg, 68 kg and 35 kg is:
The average of the numbers 253, 245, 325, 120 and 115+2K is 212. Find the average of the numbers 353, 354, 225, 220 and 110+3K.
The lengths of the two diagonals of a rhombus are 20 cm and 23 cm. What is the area (in cm²) of the rhombus?
questions.explanation: Area of a rhombus = ½ × d₁ × d₂ = ½ × 20 × 23 = 230 cm².

questions.text: The marked price of a chair is ₹1,800 and a discount of 18% is offered on the marked price. What additional discount must be offered to the customer now to bring the net price to ₹1,220? (Correct to two places of decimals.)
questions.explanation: After 18% off the price is 0.82 × 1,800 = ₹1,476. To bring it to ₹1,220 the further discount is 256/1,476 × 100 = 17.34%.

questions.text: Two candidates contested in an election. One of them secured 62.5% of the total votes and won by 996 votes. What is the total number of votes cast?(all votes are valid)
questions.explanation: The winner had 62.5% and the loser 37.5%, so the margin is 25% of the votes: 996 ÷ 0.25 = 3,984.

questions.text: The average weight of a class of 115 students is 52.4 kg. If the average weight of the 63 boys is 60 kg, then find the average weight (in kg) of the girls in the class. (Rounded off to one decimal place)
questions.explanation: All 115 students weigh 115 × 52.4 = 6,026 kg and the 63 boys 63 × 60 = 3,780 kg. The 52 girls weigh 2,246 kg: 2,246/52 = 43.2 kg.

questions.text: The average score obtained by 64 boys and a certain number of girls in a test is 59.15, while the average score obtained by the boys is 55.25. If the average score of the girls is 68.75, then how many girls appeared for the test?
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation mathematically correct? 49 + 7 × 10 ÷ 6 – 3 = 73

10 is related to 102 following a certain logic. Following the same logic, 13 is related to 171. To which of the following is 16 related, following the same logic? (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding / subtracting / multiplying, etc., to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first plus 2: 10² + 2 = 102 and 13² + 2 = 171. Likewise 16² + 2 = 258.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the English alphabetical order ? HAF, KDI, NGL, QJO, ?
questions.explanation: Every letter moves 3 places forward each time: H, K, N, Q, T; A, D, G, J, M; F, I, L, O, R. The next cluster is TMR.

questions.text: What will come in the place of the question mark (?) in the following equation if ‘+’ and ‘−’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 90 − 6 + 69 ÷ 54 × 27 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 90 + 6 − 69 × 54 ÷ 27 = 96 − 138 = −42.

questions.text: What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series? 162 184 206 228 250 ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 22 more than the one before: 250 + 22 = 272.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘Do you follow’ is coded as ‘MP TQ IX’ and ‘How are you’ is coded as ‘TQ LV IJ’. How is ‘you’ coded in that code language?
questions.explanation: 'you' is the only word in both sentences and 'TQ' the only code in both, so you = TQ.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘MICE’ is coded as ‘6481’ and ‘RICE’ is coded as ‘1584’. What is the code for ‘R’ in the given code language?
questions.explanation: I, C and E are in both words, as are 1, 4 and 8 in both codes. The letter left in RICE is R and the digit left in its code is 5, so R = 5.

questions.text: S, T, U, V, W and X are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). W sits second to the right of U. T sits second to the right of W. X sits to the immediate right of T. Who sits to the immediate right of X?
questions.explanation: Numbering the seats to the right from U (0): W is at 2, T at 4 and X at 5. The next seat to the right of X is U's.

questions.text: Six students Dhiraj, Mohan, Lokesh, Param, Rohan and Suresh are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Rohan is sitting second to the right of Suresh. Param is sitting third to the right of Rohan. Param is an immediate neighbour of both Lokesh and Suresh. Mohan and Lokesh are immediate neighbours. Who is the immediate neighbour of both Dhiraj and Mohan?
questions.explanation: Numbering the seats to the right from Suresh (0): Rohan is at 2 and Param at 5, beside Suresh. Lokesh, Param's other neighbour, is at 4, Mohan beside him at 3, and Dhiraj at 1. Rohan, at 2, sits between Dhiraj and Mohan.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement(s). Statements: Some creepers are stones. Some stones are buds. Conclusions: (I) Some buds are stones. (II) No creeper is a bud.
questions.explanation: 'Some stones are buds' converts to 'some buds are stones', so I follows. Nothing links creepers to buds, so II does not.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding/subtracting/multiplying to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (16, 3, 27) (10, 19, 37)
questions.explanation: The third number is the sum of the first two plus 8: 16 + 3 + 8 = 27 and 10 + 19 + 8 = 37. Likewise 7 + 25 + 8 = 40.

questions.text: UDLT is related to XGOW in a certain way based on the English alphabetical order. In the same way, ZIQY is related to CLTB. To which of the following is IQYH related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward (Y wraps round to B): UDLT → XGOW and ZIQY → CLTB. So IQYH → LTBK.

questions.text: ACDB is related to ZXWY in a certain way. In the same way, EGHF is related to VTSU. To which of the following is IKLJ related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y and so on): ACDB → ZXWY and EGHF → VTSU. So IKLJ → RPOQ.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘clean the room’ is written as ‘rt yp fs’ and ‘room is good’ is coded as ‘sw rt la’. How is ‘room’ coded in the given language
questions.explanation: 'room' is the only word in both sentences and 'rt' the only code in both, so room = rt.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some actors are dancers. Some dancers are singers. Conclusions: (I) Some actors are singers. (II) No singer is a dancer.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: Actors and singers are each linked only to some dancers, so I need not follow. II contradicts 'some dancers are singers'. Neither follows.

questions.text: On boiling an egg, why does the outer part become opaque and white?
options: The heat causes a change in the crystal structure of egg yolk.
The heat causes a change in the structure of egg protein.
The heat causes denaturation, hardening the albumin and colouring it opaque white
The heat causes a reaction of the egg with water and makes it opaque.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the fuller answer: heat denatures albumin, the egg-white protein, whose unfolded molecules bind into a firm mesh that scatters light, so the clear white turns opaque white. (The statement that heat changes the structure of egg protein describes the same process less fully.)

questions.text: The first post-independence National Games were hosted by which of the following cities?
questions.explanation: The first National Games after independence were held at Lucknow in 1948.

questions.text: Which of the following National Parks is located in Madhya Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Bandhavgarh National Park is in Umaria district, Madhya Pradesh. Periyar and Silent Valley are in Kerala, Nanda Devi in Uttarakhand.

questions.text: R Muthukannammal, who was awarded the Padma Shri in 2022, is a ______________ dancer.
questions.explanation: R. Muthukannammal of Viralimalai, Tamil Nadu, received the Padma Shri in 2022 for Sadir, the temple dance tradition from which Bharatanatyam developed.

questions.text: Calculate the Body Mass Index (BMI) of a person whose weight is 50 kg and height is 1.5 m.
questions.explanation: BMI = weight ÷ height² = 50 ÷ 1.5² = 50 ÷ 2.25 = 22.2 kg/m².

questions.text: On 27th october 2019, Dushyant Chautala took an oath as Deputy Chief Minister of which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Dushyant Chautala of the Jannayak Janta Party was sworn in as Deputy Chief Minister of Haryana on 27 October 2019, alongside Chief Minister Manohar Lal Khattar.

questions.text: Which of the following states of India marked the lowest in National Multi-dimensional Poverty Index: A Progress Review 2023?
questions.explanation: In NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index: A Progress Review 2023, Kerala had the lowest share of multidimensionally poor people (0.55%), ahead of Goa (0.84%), Tamil Nadu (2.20%) and Sikkim (2.60%).

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Where was the Hindu college established in the year 1791 to teach ancient Sanskrit texts?
questions.explanation: Jonathan Duncan, the East India Company's Resident, founded the Sanskrit College at Banaras (Varanasi) in 1791 for the study of Hindu law and philosophy.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECT pair of cropping season and related crop from the following.
questions.explanation: Paddy (rice) is mainly a kharif crop, sown with the monsoon. Wheat is the main rabi crop, and maize and soyabean are kharif crops.

questions.text: The Ganesh-rath is one of the finest monolithic temples at _____________.
questions.explanation: The Ganesha Ratha is one of the Pallava monolithic rock-cut temples at Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram), Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: The average separation between the sun and the earth in terms of light years is 8.311 minutes. Here, minutes indicate:
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives distance: like the light year, the light minute is a unit of distance, the distance light travels in one minute (about 1.8 crore km), so 8.311 light minutes measures how far the Sun is. (The figure is also the time light takes to reach the Earth, which makes 'time' tempting.)

questions.text: The famous Hindi novel ‘Maila Aanchal’ is written by:
questions.explanation: 'Maila Aanchal' (1954), a landmark of the regional (aanchalik) Hindi novel, was written by Phanishwar Nath Renu.

questions.text: Which of the following is an Indian folk dance?
questions.explanation: Bihu is the folk dance of Assam. Mohiniyattam, Bharatanatyam and Sattriya are among India's classical dances.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a part of the capital receipts?
questions.explanation: Tax revenue is a revenue receipt. Borrowing, disinvestment and the recovery of loans either create a liability or reduce an asset, so they are capital receipts.

questions.text: Which of the following is the compound with the chemical formula H₂SO₄?
questions.explanation: H₂SO₄ is sulfuric acid. Sulfurous acid is H₂SO₃, hydrogen sulfide H₂S and nitric acid HNO₃.

questions.text: According to Article 74(1), who is at the head of the Council of Ministers?
questions.explanation: Article 74(1) provides a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at its head to aid and advise the President.

questions.text: The officer known as Diwan belonged to which of the following departments of the Mughal empire during Akbar’s reign?
questions.explanation: Under Akbar the diwan (diwan-i-kul) was in charge of revenue and finance.

questions.text: Who among the following personalities was the recipient of the Lata Mangeshkar Award for Music 2021, presented by the Madhya Pradesh government?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh's National Lata Mangeshkar Award for 2021 went to the playback singer Kumar Sanu; it was presented in Indore in September 2022.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Behdienkhlam Festival celebrated, in which the young men make a symbolic gesture of driving away of the evil spirit, plague and disease by beating the roof of every house with bamboo poles?
questions.explanation: Behdienkhlam is celebrated by the Pnar (Jaintia) people, above all at Jowai in Meghalaya's Jaintia Hills.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Jyotiba Phule belonged from which state?
questions.explanation: Jyotirao (Jyotiba) Phule, the social reformer who founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in Pune in 1873, was from Maharashtra.

questions.text: The word ‘Megalith’ comes from two ________ words; ‘megas’ means great and ‘lithas’ means stone.
questions.explanation: The word is Greek: 'megas', great, and 'lithos', stone. Megaliths are large stones, often set up to mark burial sites.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles on Fundamental Duties was added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: Article 51A (Part IVA), added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, lists the Fundamental Duties.

questions.text: Which country won the 4th Asian Kho-Kho Championship 2023 event in the Men's category?
questions.explanation: India won the men's title at the 4th Asian Kho-Kho Championship at Tamulpur, Assam, in March 2023, beating Nepal in the final; the Indian women also won.

questions.text: The Hindu temples ‘Hinglaj Mata’ and ‘Katasraj’ are located in which neighbouring country of India?
questions.explanation: Hinglaj Mata is in Balochistan and the Katas Raj temples are in Punjab, both in Pakistan.

questions.text: Where was Global Technology Summit 2022 held?
questions.explanation: The 2022 Global Technology Summit, hosted by Carnegie India with the Ministry of External Affairs, was held in New Delhi from 29 November to 1 December 2022.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. Rakesh committed the mistake, and he must be “convicted”.
questions.explanation: To be 'convicted' is to be found guilty; its opposite is 'acquitted', found not guilty.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. A “detrimental” attitude can always be cured with a cordial approach.
questions.explanation: 'Detrimental' means causing harm: 'damaging'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. It is essential that you “act in accordance” with the rules and regulations of the organisation.
questions.explanation: 'Comply with' means act in accordance with. 'Observe', 'obey' and 'fulfill' do not take the 'with' that follows.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He needs to ___________ as his exams are approaching.
questions.explanation: To 'hit the books' is to study hard. To 'hit the sack' is to go to bed and to 'learn the ropes' is to learn how a job is done; 'bury himself in' needs an object.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. By next December / we will has lived / in this city for 28 years.
questions.explanation: After 'will' the verb takes its base form: 'we will have lived' (future perfect).

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. It is impossible to think of Lady Stranleigh as an “ordinary” mother.
questions.explanation: 'Ordinary' means usual or commonplace.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. “If you do not followed the rules”, you will not be allowed to stay at this hostel.
options: If you should not follow the rules
If you do not follow the rules
If you cannot be following the rules
questions.explanation: After 'do not' the verb takes its base form: 'If you do not follow the rules'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. A Gita is considered / to be a dialogue between / the Pandava prince, Arjuna, / and Lord Krishna.
questions.explanation: A particular, well-known text takes the definite article: 'The Gita is considered to be a dialogue ...'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to replace the underlined word in the following sentence. The officer was “polite” to the workers.
questions.explanation: 'Humble' (modest and respectful in manner) is the closest of the options to 'polite'; 'officious' means bossily interfering, and 'harsh' and 'adamant' do not fit.

questions.text: Which of the following sentences contains an error in the use of a phrasal verb?
options: Can you please take care for my belongings for some time?
While visiting the library, I came across an interesting book.
Let's call off the picnic as there is a possibility of heavy rain.
It is wise to put up with one's quarrelsome neighbours.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb is 'take care of', not 'take care for'. 'Came across', 'call off' and 'put up with' are used correctly.

questions.text: The given sentence is divided into four segments. Select the option that has the segment with the grammatical error. Mahesh and his workers / will have been worked / on the project / for a long time.
questions.explanation: Mahesh and his workers are doing the work, so the active future perfect continuous is needed: 'will have been working'.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the underlined word. "Today's “whether” is very pleasant", said Maya.
questions.explanation: 'Weather' is the state of the atmosphere; 'whether' introduces alternatives.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'calendar'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence. Mita is “smart” than many other kids in the school.
questions.explanation: With 'than' the comparative is needed: 'smarter than many other kids'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. “After she will get her degree”, she moved to Germany.
questions.explanation: The main clause is in the past ('moved'), so the time clause takes the past too: 'After she got her degree'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. In accordance to / the factual data, / serious measures are required / to control the loss.
questions.explanation: The phrase is 'in accordance with': 'In accordance with the factual data'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and complete the phrase/idiom. When Jane realised that she had made a serious mistake at work, she knew she had to face the ______and take responsibility for her actions.
questions.explanation: To 'face the music' is to accept the consequences of one's actions.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The billionaire knows how to _____ money.
questions.explanation: Money is something one 'makes' (earns); one does not 'do', 'form' or 'develop' money.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The “lavish” party had a luxurious atmosphere and elegant decorations.
questions.explanation: 'Lavish' means extravagant, spent or provided in great, even excessive, quantity; of the options only 'excessive' is close. 'Middling' and 'simple' are nearer its opposite.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Credit cards originated in the 1920s in the US, with European references dating back to 1890. John Biggins, 1.______ of the first bank-issued credit card, invented the 'Charge-It' programme in 1946, 2.______ bank customers and local merchants. In 1950, Diners Club introduced their credit card in the US, 3.___________ customers to pay restaurant bills without cash. American Express 4._______ their first credit card in 1958, while the Bank of America introduced the Bank America Card (now Visa) in 1958. Visa, now known as the Visa International Service Association, is accepted in over 150 countries, making it one of the most 5._______ credit cards available.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Biggins 'invented' the Charge-It programme, so he was the 'inventor' of the first bank-issued card.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Credit cards originated in the 1920s in the US, with European references dating back to 1890. John Biggins, 1.______ of the first bank-issued credit card, invented the 'Charge-It' programme in 1946, 2.______ bank customers and local merchants. In 1950, Diners Club introduced their credit card in the US, 3.___________ customers to pay restaurant bills without cash. American Express 4._______ their first credit card in 1958, while the Bank of America introduced the Bank America Card (now Visa) in 1958. Visa, now known as the Visa International Service Association, is accepted in over 150 countries, making it one of the most 5._______ credit cards available.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The programme linked bank customers with local merchants: 'connecting' them.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The card let customers pay restaurant bills without cash: 'allowing' them to.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: A card company 'issues' a credit card: American Express 'issued' its first in 1958.

Credit cards originated in the 1920s in the US, with European references dating back to 1890. Visa, now known as the Visa International Service Association, is accepted in over 150 countries, making it one of the most 5._______ credit cards available.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Accepted in over 150 countries, Visa is one of the most 'universal' (widely accepted) cards.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Atul sells goods to a customer at a profit of P%. If the cost price of the goods for the customer is ₹1,50,000 and Atul makes a profit of ₹30,000, then what is the value of P?
questions.explanation: The customer's cost price is Atul's selling price, ₹1,50,000, so Atul's cost price is 1,50,000 − 30,000 = ₹1,20,000 and P = 30,000/1,20,000 × 100 = 25.

questions.text: ‘The Palace of Illusions’, a rendition of the Hindu epic ‘Mahabharata’, was written by which of the following novelists?
questions.explanation: 'The Palace of Illusions' (2008) by Chitra Banerjee Divakaruni retells the Mahabharata from Draupadi's point of view. Pratibha Ray's 'Yajnaseni' also tells Draupadi's story, but in Odia.

questions.text: G Krishnakumar was appointed chairman of which of the following in 2023?
options: Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited
questions.explanation: G. Krishnakumar took charge as Chairman and Managing Director of Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) on 17 March 2023.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: ______________ was the first Indian woman to write an autobiography and also the first to do so in Bengali in her book titled ‘Aamar Jiban’, which was published in 1876.
questions.explanation: Rassundari Devi, a housewife who taught herself to read in secret, wrote 'Amar Jiban' (1876), regarded as the first autobiography in Bengali and the first full-length autobiography by an Indian woman.

questions.text: Where is the Vivekanand Rock Memorial situated?
questions.explanation: The Vivekananda Rock Memorial, completed in 1970, stands on a rock in the sea off Kanyakumari, Tamil Nadu, where Swami Vivekananda meditated in December 1892.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Under which Act was the rule of British Crown established over India?
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act, 1858, passed after the revolt of 1857, ended the East India Company's rule and transferred the government of India to the British Crown.

questions.text: The Kolar region of Karnataka is famous for which mineral from the following?
questions.explanation: The Kolar Gold Fields in Kolar district, Karnataka, were among the oldest and deepest gold mines in India; they were closed in 2001.

questions.text: In Fencing, a contest between the two fencers is known as:
questions.explanation: In fencing a 'bout' is the contest between two fencers. A parry blocks the opponent's blade, a riposte is the attack that follows a parry, and a remise renews an attack straight after it has been parried.

questions.text: In which year has the Government of India instituted Arjuna Award to recognise outstanding achievement in national sports events?
questions.explanation: The Arjuna Award, given by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports for outstanding performance in sports, was instituted in 1961.

questions.text: ‘Atla Taddi’, a festival celebrated by married and unmarried women alike to seek the blessings of Devi Gauri for a long and happy married life and a suitable groom, respectively, is celebrated in ____________.
questions.explanation: Atla Taddi is a festival of Telugu women in Andhra Pradesh (and Telangana), held on the third night after the full moon of Ashvayuja: they fast, offer small dosas (atlu) to Gauri and break the fast after seeing the moon.

questions.text: PT Usha was elected as the president of which association in December 2022?
questions.explanation: P. T. Usha was elected unopposed as president of the Indian Olympic Association in December 2022, the first woman to head it.

questions.text: What is the full form of UPSC?
questions.explanation: UPSC is the Union Public Service Commission, the constitutional body (Articles 315-323) that recruits for the all-India and central services.

questions.text: To which of the state does Sattriya classical dance belong?
questions.explanation: Sattriya, created by the Vaishnava saint Srimanta Sankardev and kept alive in Assam's sattras (monasteries), was recognised as a classical dance by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a function of money?
questions.explanation: Money replaced barter, the direct exchange of goods for goods. Its functions are to serve as a medium of exchange, a unit of account, a store of value and a standard of deferred payment.

questions.text: According to the Census of India 2011, what was the population density recorded in Bihar?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Bihar had a population density of 1,106 persons per km², the highest of any state.

questions.text: Which Indian musician is associated with the tabla?
questions.explanation: Zakir Hussain, son of the tabla player Alla Rakha, was the best-known tabla maestro of his time. Bismillah Khan played the shehnai and Ravi Shankar the sitar, and Ilaiyaraaja is a film composer.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: On whose advice did Gandhiji spend a year travelling around British India to know the people of India?
questions.explanation: When Gandhi returned from South Africa in 1915, Gopal Krishna Gokhale, whom he regarded as his political guru, advised him to spend a year travelling around India, observing, before taking any public stand.

questions.text: Which of the following fundamental duties was added to the Indian Constitution by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002?
options: To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem
To protect and to improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures
To provide opportunities for education to his/her child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years
To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom
questions.explanation: The 86th Amendment (2002) added Article 51A(k), the duty of a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to a child or ward aged six to fourteen, and inserted Article 21A, the right to education. The other three duties date from 1976.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam was a great man with a high level of ________.
questions.explanation: 'Intellect', the power of reasoning and understanding, is what 'a high level of' naturally measures in a great mind like Kalam's; 'wise boredom' and 'clever fatigue' make no sense.

questions.text: The following sentence contains some errors. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. The forses that genarate conditions conduciive to crime and riiots are stronger in urban communities than in rurral areas.
options: The forsec that genarate conditions conduciive to crime and riots are stronger in urban communities than in rurall areas.
The forces that genereta conditions conducieve to crime and riotts are stronger in urban communities than in rural areas.
The forces that generate conditions conducive to crime and riots are stronger in urban communities than in rural areas.
The forces that genarete conditions conduciive to crime and riots are stronger in urban communities than in ruraal areas.
questions.explanation: The correct spellings are 'forces', 'generate', 'conducive', 'riots' and 'rural'; only this option has all of them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I found my teacher’s points “casual and informal” in the group discussion.
questions.explanation: 'Free and easy' means informal and relaxed. 'Fair and square' is honest, to 'foot the bill' is to pay, and 'flesh and blood' is a human being or one's family.

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. One who is all powerful.
questions.explanation: 'Omnipotent' means all-powerful; 'omnipresent' is present everywhere and 'omniscient' all-knowing.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Ramesh “is owning” a beautiful house in Noida.
questions.explanation: 'Own' is a stative verb and is not used in the continuous: 'Ramesh owns a beautiful house in Noida.'

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. When Nisha will have finished her task?
questions.explanation: A question puts the auxiliary before the subject: 'When will Nisha have finished her task?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. He “push the bushes” aside and went a little farther.
questions.explanation: The sentence is in the past ('went'), so 'push' must be 'pushed': 'He pushed the bushes aside and went a little farther.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Copying someone else’s work and trying to submit it as your own
questions.explanation: 'Plagiarism' is passing off someone else's work as one's own. 'Polygamy' is having more than one spouse, a 'preamble' an introduction and 'extempore' speaking without preparation.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Beauty of it
questions.explanation: 'The beauty of it' is what is especially good or advantageous about something: its good points.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. The girl was “manacled” and locked in the room.
questions.explanation: To be 'manacled' is to have one's hands chained: 'fettered'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. Addiction of drugs proved “detrimental” for his health.
questions.explanation: 'Detrimental' means harmful; its opposite is 'beneficial'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Plunge
questions.explanation: To 'plunge' is to jump or fall headlong, as into water: 'dive'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The plural of 'tomato' is 'tomatoes'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’. I used a variety of sources to find the “more cheap” flight.
questions.explanation: Picking one flight out of many needs the superlative, and a one-syllable adjective takes '-est': 'the cheapest flight'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. All the members of my family are planning to visit Jammu and Kashmir this Novembur.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'November'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Ravi will go to the England.
questions.explanation: The names of most countries take no article: 'Ravi will go to England.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate response in the given situation of the eve of a battle to fill in the blank. The commander: “Honourable Emperor, all the troops have lined up for the battle and are awaiting your orders.” Emperor Chandragupta Maurya: “______________________.”
options: You should learn how to talk to an emperor.
We are ready for the pilgrimage.
questions.explanation: With the troops lined up and awaiting orders on the eve of battle, the fitting reply is an order: 'We will march at dawn.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. We prefer going to movies “once in a blue moon.”
questions.explanation: 'Once in a blue moon' means very rarely.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. My father told me / that in his childhood / he was walking / to school every day.
questions.explanation: A habit in the past takes the simple past or 'used to', not the past continuous: 'he walked (or used to walk) to school every day'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. Today’s question paper felt “like a cakewalk”.
questions.explanation: A 'cakewalk' is something very easy to do.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. Modern football (1)________in Britain in the 19th century. Since before medieval times, ‘folk football’ games had been played in towns and villages according to local customs and with a (2)_______of rules. Industrialisation and (3)________, which reduced the amount of leisure time and space available to the working class, combined with a history of legal prohibitions against particularly (4)________ and destructive forms of folk football to undermine the game’s status from the early 19th century onward. However, football was taken up as a winter game between residence houses at public (independent) schools such as Winchester, Charterhouse and Eton. Each school had its own rules; some allowed limited handling of the ball and others did not. The (5)_________in rules made it difficult for public schoolboys entering university to continue playing except with former schoolmates.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: Modern football 'originated', had its beginnings, in 19th-century Britain; 'culminated' would mean it reached its peak there.

questions.text:

Modern football (1)________in Britain in the 19th century. Each school had its own rules; some allowed limited handling of the ball and others did not. The (5)_________in rules made it difficult for public schoolboys entering university to continue playing except with former schoolmates.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: Folk games were played by local custom 'with a minimum of rules', that is, with very few rules.

Each school had its own rules; some allowed limited handling of the ball and others did not. The (5)_________in rules made it difficult for public schoolboys entering university to continue playing except with former schoolmates.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: 'Industrialisation and urbanisation', the growth of factories and towns, together cut the leisure time and space left to the working class.

questions.text:

Modern football (1)________in Britain in the 19th century. Since before medieval times, ‘folk football’ games had been played in towns and villages according to local customs and with a (2)_______of rules.
