Each school had its own rules; some allowed limited handling of the ball and others did not. The (5)_________in rules made it difficult for public schoolboys entering university to continue playing except with former schoolmates.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: Laws prohibited 'violent and destructive' forms of folk football; 'violent' pairs with 'destructive', while 'calm' contradicts it.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. Modern football (1)________in Britain in the 19th century. Since before medieval times, ‘folk football’ games had been played in towns and villages according to local customs and with a (2)_______of rules. Industrialisation and (3)________, which reduced the amount of leisure time and space available to the working class, combined with a history of legal prohibitions against particularly (4)________ and destructive forms of folk football to undermine the game’s status from the early 19th century onward. However, football was taken up as a winter game between residence houses at public (independent) schools such as Winchester, Charterhouse and Eton. Each school had its own rules; some allowed limited handling of the ball and others did not. The (5)_________in rules made it difficult for public schoolboys entering university to continue playing except with former schoolmates.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: Each school had its own rules, so the 'variance' (difference) in rules made it hard for schoolboys to play together at university.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: By selling an article for ₹5,280, Geeta lost 12%. For what amount should she sell it to make a profit of 12%?
questions.explanation: A 12% loss means ₹5,280 is 88% of the cost price, so CP = 5,280/0.88 = ₹6,000. A 12% profit needs 1.12 × 6,000 = ₹6,720.

questions.text: Suresh could save 20% of his income. But 4 years later, when his income increased by 40%, he could save the same amount only as before. By how much percentage did his expenditure increase?
questions.explanation: Take the income as 100: saving 20, expenditure 80. The new income is 140 and the saving still 20, so expenditure is 120, a rise of 40/80 = 50%.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded a reform organisation in 1875 that attempted to reform Hinduism. What was it called?
questions.explanation: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj at Bombay in 1875; it called for a return to the Vedas. The Prarthana Samaj was founded by Atmaram Pandurang, the Satyashodhak Samaj by Jyotirao Phule and the Brahmo Samaj by Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

questions.text: The Brihadeswara Temple at Tanjavur built by:
questions.explanation: The Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, was built by the Chola king Rajaraja I and completed in about 1010 AD.

questions.text: What is the minimum voting age for the citizens of India?
questions.explanation: Under Article 326, as amended by the 61st Amendment (1988), every citizen aged 18 or over may vote; the age was 21 before.

questions.text: The four Nattuvanars namely Ponaiyah, Vadivelu, Sivanandam and Chinnaiya, who are renowned as Tanjaore Bandhu shaped up the modern day ___________.
questions.explanation: The Tanjore Quartet, the brothers Chinnaiya, Ponnaiya, Sivanandam and Vadivelu at the Thanjavur court in the early 19th century, set the order of items of the Bharatanatyam recital that is still followed.

questions.text: In February 2023, Uttar Pradesh government launched a/an _____ called Family ID-One Family One Identity.
questions.explanation: In February 2023 Uttar Pradesh opened the portal for its 'Family ID - One Family One Identity' scheme: for families with a National Food Security ration card the ration card number serves as the Family ID, and other families apply on the portal for a 12-digit Family ID.

questions.text: Why are intermediate goods NOT included in the calculation of national income?
options: Including intermediate goods would result in double counting.
Intermediate goods are not produced within the country's borders.
Including intermediate goods would decrease the value of national income.
Intermediate goods are not important for measuring economic activity.
questions.explanation: Intermediate goods are used up in making final goods, so their value is already included in the value of the final goods; counting them again would count the same output twice.

questions.text: According to the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021,India’s rank is ________ out of 109 countries.
questions.explanation: In the Global MPI 2021, released by UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative in October 2021 and covering 109 countries, India was placed 66th.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of a bank statement?
options: To transfer funds to another account
To have locker facility in the bank
questions.explanation: A bank statement lists every deposit, withdrawal and charge on an account over a period, with the balance, so the holder can keep track of money coming in and going out.

questions.text: The Konark Dance Festival (KDF) has been held at Konark since 1986 between ___________ every year.
questions.explanation: The Konark Dance Festival is held every year from 1 to 5 December at the open-air auditorium near the Sun Temple, Konark.

questions.text: Identify the southernmost range of the Himalaya from the following.
questions.explanation: The Shiwaliks, the Outer Himalayas, are the southernmost of the ranges; to their north lie the Lesser Himalaya (Himachal) and the Greater Himalaya (Himadri), and the Trans Himalaya lies beyond.

questions.text: The novel ‘Train to Pakistan’ was written by ______.
questions.explanation: Khushwant Singh's 'Train to Pakistan' (1956) is set in a Punjab border village during the Partition of 1947.

questions.text: Popular Bollywood actor Kriti Sanon is a trained __________ dancer.
questions.explanation: The actor Kriti Sanon is a trained Kathak dancer and has learnt the classical dance of north India since childhood.

questions.text: In which of the following cities was the final match of the 2022 Vijay Hazare Trophy held?
questions.explanation: The final of the 2022-23 Vijay Hazare Trophy was played at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad, on 2 December 2022; Saurashtra beat Maharashtra by five wickets.

questions.text: Who started the chemical revolution in the 18th century by naming oxygen and helping to organize chemical nomenclature?
questions.explanation: Antoine Lavoisier named oxygen and hydrogen, explained combustion as a reaction with oxygen, and with others drew up a system of chemical names (1787). Priestley isolated oxygen but called it 'dephlogisticated air'.

questions.text: Aman Sehrawat became the first Indian to win a gold medal in World Wrestling Championship in which category?
questions.explanation: At Pontevedra, Spain, in October 2022, Aman Sehrawat won the 57 kg freestyle title at the U-23 World Wrestling Championships, the first Indian to win gold at that event.

questions.text: Independence Day is celebrated every year in Pakistan on ________.
questions.explanation: Pakistan celebrates its Independence Day on 14 August, the day before India's. 23 March is Pakistan Day, marking the Lahore Resolution of 1940.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian musicians was called ‘Mallika-e-Ghazal’?
questions.explanation: Begum Akhtar, the singer of ghazal, dadra and thumri, was called 'Mallika-e-Ghazal', the queen of ghazal.

questions.text: The word ‘yorker’ is related to which sport?
questions.explanation: In cricket a yorker is a ball pitched at or near the batter's feet, hard to hit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I wish we had ______ come here.
questions.explanation: 'I wish' with the past perfect expresses regret about the past: 'I wish we had never come here.' The other words do not fit between 'had' and 'come'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Carnal
questions.explanation: 'Carnal' means of the body and its desires; its opposite is 'spiritual'. 'Material', 'temporal' and 'somatic' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Fail to function normally
questions.explanation: To 'malfunction' is to fail to work normally. To maltreat is to treat cruelly, to mangle is to crush out of shape, and to manipulate is to control cleverly or unfairly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given phrase. All of a sudden
questions.explanation: 'All of a sudden' means suddenly: quickly and unexpectedly.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. My daughter was / invited to lunch / hosted by the Governor / at his residence.
questions.explanation: The name of a meal takes no article in general ('invited to lunch'), but a particular meal, here the one hosted by the Governor, takes one: 'invited to a lunch hosted by the Governor'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'rectify'.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. The “maintenence” department did a fabulous job.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'maintenance'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank. The novel’s intricate plot and rich character development kept readers ________(committed) from the beginning to the end.
questions.explanation: Readers 'committed' to a book are held by it: 'engaged'. 'Secluded', 'detached' and 'dismantled' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. These things are very “hard to swallow”.
questions.explanation: Something 'hard to swallow' is difficult to believe or accept.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. The decision to go on a trip after my vacations was the ________.
questions.explanation: 'The icing on the cake' is something good added to what is already good, here the trip after the vacations.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The new software / consists from / several features / and tools.
questions.explanation: 'Consist' takes 'of': 'The new software consists of several features and tools.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. It's easy to say that you'll start exercising every day, but it is ______________.
questions.explanation: 'Easier said than done' describes something that is easy to talk about but hard to do, such as exercising every day.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. Uncle Joe is ___________________(reputable) for spending 10 years of his youth in prison due to armed robbery.
questions.explanation: 'Reputable' means well thought of; 'notorious' means famous for something bad, as Uncle Joe is for his armed robbery.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. If you work hard, you secure good marks.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'you secure': a condition about a likely future result takes 'will' in the main clause, 'If you work hard, you will secure good marks.' (The simple present is also used for general truths, but the textbook rule expects 'will' here, and no other part has an error.)

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who is skilled in making maps
questions.explanation: A 'cartographer' makes maps. A calligrapher writes decoratively, a curator looks after a museum's collection, and a cacographer writes or spells badly.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. Sita loves her “glass container in which she has many fish.”
questions.explanation: An 'aquarium' is a glass tank in which fish and other water creatures are kept.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’. His claim to be the “smartly” kid in the school was a bit hyperbole!
questions.explanation: Comparing him with every kid in the school needs the superlative of the adjective: 'the smartest kid in the school'. 'Smartly' is an adverb.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Easily set on fire
questions.explanation: 'Inflammable' (like 'flammable') means easily set on fire. Innocuous means harmless, ingrained deep-rooted and inimical hostile.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. She has / bought / a car / two years ago.
questions.explanation: The present perfect is not used with a definite past time such as 'two years ago': 'She bought a car two years ago.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Students put their heart and soul into studies while (1)________ for examinations. They prepare the syllabus by giving many revisions, making important points on flash cards, preparing notes throughout the year. They read reference books in order to score good marks in the examination. This is the demanding (2)________ of all the students who are appearing in the examinations. But, most students feel tensed on the day before an examination. Everyone is in a state of (3)________ as to what questions would be asked in the paper and whether they could write their answers properly to get good marks. Such overthinking is the cause of (4)________ which definitely affects their performance. They should revise the subject regularly and should not keep their doubts pending. This will not create a (5)________ of backlog and they will get sufficient time to resolve their problem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Students study hard while 'preparing' for examinations, which the next sentences describe: revisions, flash cards and notes.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Students put their heart and soul into studies while (1)________ for examinations. They prepare the syllabus by giving many revisions, making important points on flash cards, preparing notes throughout the year. They read reference books in order to score good marks in the examination. This is the demanding (2)________ of all the students who are appearing in the examinations. But, most students feel tensed on the day before an examination. Everyone is in a state of (3)________ as to what questions would be asked in the paper and whether they could write their answers properly to get good marks. Such overthinking is the cause of (4)________ which definitely affects their performance. They should revise the subject regularly and should not keep their doubts pending. This will not create a (5)________ of backlog and they will get sufficient time to resolve their problem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Revising, making flash cards and notes all year make up a 'routine', a regular pattern of work, and a demanding one.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Students put their heart and soul into studies while (1)________ for examinations. They prepare the syllabus by giving many revisions, making important points on flash cards, preparing notes throughout the year. This will not create a (5)________ of backlog and they will get sufficient time to resolve their problem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Not knowing what questions will be asked is a state of 'uncertainty'; 'confidence' and 'assurance' contradict the students' tension.

Students put their heart and soul into studies while (1)________ for examinations. This will not create a (5)________ of backlog and they will get sufficient time to resolve their problem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Overthinking causes 'anxiety', worry about what is to come, which affects their performance; 'agitation' is outward restlessness, and 'peace' and 'comfort' contradict the sense.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Which of the following Indian playback singers received the Bharat Ratna in 2001?
questions.explanation: Lata Mangeshkar received the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 2001, the same year as the shehnai maestro Bismillah Khan.

questions.text: Which of the following cricket players wrote the autobiography ‘Playing It My Way’?
questions.explanation: 'Playing It My Way' (2014), written with Boria Majumdar, is Sachin Tendulkar's autobiography.

questions.text: In which city is the India Gate situated?
questions.explanation: India Gate in New Delhi, designed by Edwin Lutyens, was built as the All India War Memorial to the soldiers of the British Indian Army who died in the First World War.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who authored the book ‘Poverty and Un-British Rule in India’ in 1901, which was highly critical of the economic impact of British Rule?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji's 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901) set out his drain theory: that British rule was draining India's wealth to Britain.

questions.text: The efforts of Malayalam poet Vallathol Narayana Menon and dancer and guru Kalyanikutty Amma brought back and gave a new life to the dance form __________________.
questions.explanation: Mohiniyattam, Kerala's classical dance for women, had almost died out when Vallathol, who founded the Kerala Kalamandalam in 1930, brought it into its teaching; Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma, one of its students, spent her life reviving it and is called the mother of Mohiniyattam.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Where was All Indian Muslim League formed in 1906?
questions.explanation: The All India Muslim League was founded at Dhaka on 30 December 1906, at a meeting held during the session of the All India Muhammadan Educational Conference there.

questions.text: Which of the following writers wrote the autobiography ‘Truth, Love and a Little Malice’?
questions.explanation: 'Truth, Love and a Little Malice' (2002) is the autobiography of the writer and journalist Khushwant Singh.

questions.text: In 2023, a three-day All-India Taekwondo Championship was organized in _________ to mark 50 years of Korea-India diplomatic relations.
questions.explanation: The championship, held by the Sports Authority of India with the Korean Cultural Centre India, was played at the Indira Gandhi Stadium in New Delhi in February 2023, the 50th year of India-Korea diplomatic relations.

questions.text: The outward remittances under the Reserve Bank of India’s ____________ made a strong comeback in the first quarter of FY23 as Indians increased spending on international travel, maintenance of close relatives and gifts.
questions.explanation: Under the RBI's Liberalised Remittance Scheme (2004), resident individuals could send up to US$250,000 abroad in a financial year when the exam was held (September 2023), for permitted purposes such as travel, study, gifts and the maintenance of relatives.

questions.text: The Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) scheme provide loans up to ________ to the non-corporate, non-farm small and micro entrepreneurs. (As of April 2023).
questions.explanation: When the exam was held (September 2023), MUDRA loans came in three categories: Shishu up to ₹50,000, Kishore up to ₹5 lakh and Tarun up to ₹10 lakh, so the ceiling was ₹10 lakh. A Tarun Plus category, up to ₹20 lakh, was added in October 2024.

questions.text: The ____________ maestros who revived the art form in the late 1940s include Kelucharan Mohapatra and Raghunath Dutta.
questions.explanation: Kelucharan Mohapatra and Raghunath Dutta, with gurus such as Pankaj Charan Das, Deba Prasad Das and Mayadhar Raut, rebuilt Odissi, Odisha's classical dance, from the temple dance of the maharis and the gotipua tradition.

questions.text: Which of the following is true about disposable income in relation to personal income?
options: Disposable income is equal to personal income.
Disposable income is always less than personal income.
Disposable income is always greater than personal income.
Disposable income can be greater or less than personal income, depending on taxes and deductions.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'always less': personal disposable income is personal income minus the direct taxes and the fees and fines that households pay to the government. An economy always makes such payments, so its disposable income is less than its personal income and can never be greater.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the process of calorimetry?
options: Measuring the amount of compressive strength
Measuring the amount of heat energy transferred
questions.explanation: Calorimetry measures the heat given out or taken in during a physical or chemical change, usually from the change in temperature of a known mass of water in a calorimeter.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years?
questions.explanation: Article 45, as substituted by the 86th Amendment (2002), directs the State to provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six; the same amendment made education from 6 to 14 a fundamental right (Article 21A).

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog was set up on 1 January 2015 by a Union Cabinet resolution, in place of the Planning Commission, so it is neither constitutional nor statutory. The Election Commission (Article 324), the Finance Commission (Article 280) and the UPSC (Article 315) are constitutional bodies.

questions.text: According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index of NITI Aayog 2021, which of the following states has less than 1% multidimensionally Poor of its total population?
questions.explanation: In NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index (baseline report, 2021) Kerala had the lowest share of multidimensionally poor people, 0.71%; Punjab, Telangana and Maharashtra were well above 1%.

questions.text: According to the Hindu calendar, Holi is celebrated on _____________.
questions.explanation: Holi falls on the full moon (purnima) of the month of Phalguna, usually in March: Holika Dahan is lit that night and colours are played the next day.

questions.text: Which Indian sprinter bagged two gold medals, one each in the men's 100 and 200-metre races at the Flanders Cup 2023 athletics meet?
questions.explanation: Amlan Borgohain won both the 100 m and the 200 m at the Flanders Cup 2023, the International Antwerp Athletics Gala at Merksem, Belgium, in June 2023.

questions.text: Who became the first Indian javelin ace to win the gold at the Zurich Diamond League?
questions.explanation: Neeraj Chopra won the Diamond League final in Zurich in September 2022 with a throw of 88.44 m, the first Indian to win a Diamond League title.

questions.text: Which curve examines the relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of money wage changes?
questions.explanation: The Phillips curve, from A. W. Phillips's 1958 study of British data, shows an inverse relation between the rate of unemployment and the rate of change of money wages.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. When I was in high school / I participated in several extracurricular activities / such as the debate team and the school newspaper / which help me developed my communication and writing skills.
options: When I was in high school
which help me developed my communication and writing skills
such as the debate team and the school newspaper
I participated in several extracurricular activities
questions.explanation: After 'help me' the verb takes its base form, and the activities belong to the past: 'which helped me develop my communication and writing skills'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The rise in temperature is playing havoc with India’s “rainfall which is pertinent” for India’s agriculture sector.
questions.explanation: 'Pertinent' means relevant to the matter at hand; rainfall that matters a great deal to farming is 'significant' for it. 'Who' is used for people, and 'decant' and 'mendicant' make no sense here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. Sameera has been in ________ since she got selected for a highly paid job at a multinational company.
questions.explanation: To be in 'seventh heaven' is to be extremely happy, as Sameera is after landing a well-paid job.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined segment in the given sentence. I hope you “break a leg” at your performance tonight!
questions.explanation: 'Break a leg' is said to wish a performer good luck: it means 'perform well'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Winning the championship was a dream come true for the team, but being awarded the MVP trophy was ______________.
questions.explanation: 'The icing on the cake' is something good added to what is already good, here the trophy on top of the championship. A 'silver lining' is the hopeful side of a bad situation.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. We requested grandmother to “extend” her visit.
questions.explanation: To 'extend' a visit is to lengthen it; to 'curtail' it is to cut it short.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Simon “is afraid of closed space.”
questions.explanation: 'Claustrophobia' is the fear of closed or confined spaces; xenophobia is a fear or dislike of foreigners and hydrophobia a fear of water.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Magnificent
questions.explanation: 'Magnificent' means splendid or impressive: 'glorious'. 'Modest' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: The sentence given below contains some spelling errors. Select the option that has the correct spellings. Appliications of subjects like Physiks and chemmistry in our dayly life also have higher visibelity than those of Biology.
options: Applicasions of subjects like Physiks and Cemistry in our dayly life also have higher visibility than those of Biology.
Appliications of subjects like Physics and chemistry in our dayly life also have higher visibelity than those of Biology.
Applications of subjects like Physics and Chemistry in our daily life also have higher visibility than those of Biology.
Applicacions of subjects like Physics and chemmistry in our daily life also have higher visibilety than those of Biology.
questions.explanation: The correct spellings are 'applications', 'physics', 'chemistry', 'daily' and 'visibility'.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. The weather “is” “cold” tonight than “it” “was” yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Than' needs the comparative: 'The weather is colder tonight than it was yesterday.'

questions.text: Select the option that correctly rectifies the underlined spelling error in the given sentence. Little children are afraid to go to school because of the “agrassive” seniors who tend to bully them.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'aggressive', with a double 'g' and a double 's'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The scratches on her hands were clear signs of domestic violence, ______ and said that she got scratched by barbed wire fencing.
questions.explanation: The second half contrasts with the first: the scratches pointed to violence, 'yet she lied' and blamed the fencing, with 'she' as the subject of both 'lied' and 'said'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Rahul’s sister says that “my brother is the best dancer in the city”.
options: her brother is the best dancer in the city
my brother was the best dancer in the city
her brother was the best dancer in the city
his brother was the best dancer in the city
questions.explanation: Reporting the sister's words, her 'my brother' becomes 'her brother'; with the reporting verb 'says' in the present tense, 'is' does not change: 'Rahul's sister says that her brother is the best dancer in the city.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement required’. A wonder in the plant kingdom, the Great Banyan Tree of the AJC Bose Botanical Garden at Shibpur in Howrah, “occupies a unique position in” the world records.
options: being occupied a unique position of
questions.explanation: No improvement: the singular subject 'the Great Banyan Tree' takes 'occupies', 'a unique' is right because 'unique' begins with a consonant sound, and a place is held 'in' the records.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The cholera is a frightful disease.
questions.explanation: The names of most diseases take no article: 'Cholera is a frightful disease.'

questions.text: The sentence given below has spelling errors. Select the sentence without spelling errors. Knowledge and awareness about my own self has to preceede my knowledge of things other than me.
options: Knowledge and awareness about my own self has to preceede my knowledge of things other then me.
Knowledge and awareness about my own self has to precede my knowledge of things other than me.
Knowlegde and awareness about my own self has to preceede my knowlegde of things other than me.
Knowledge and awarenes about my own self has to preceede my knowledge of things other than me.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'precede', to come before; the other sentences keep 'preceede' and also misspell 'than', 'knowledge' or 'awareness'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. If Peter said he would get that book for you, he will do it. He always ________.
questions.explanation: To 'keep one's word' is to do what one has promised.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. It “has raining” very hard and he has a very large umbrella to keep off the rain-drops.
questions.explanation: 'Has' is not followed directly by an '-ing' form; the present continuous 'is raining' matches the present 'has' in the second clause.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Shiya had more “grit” than her other siblings.
questions.explanation: 'Grit' is courage and determination in the face of difficulty: 'courage'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error. (A) The twins are / (B) often told that / (C) they are resembling / (D) each other.
questions.explanation: 'Resemble' is a stative verb and is not used in the continuous: 'they resemble each other'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. Each essay is set (1)______ against its background and made simpler by providing (2)_______ summary and critical commentary, short notes on textual issues, and (3)__________ of important critical and theoretical issues under the heading essay topics. (4)_____ of the most commonly used terms in the literature is given at the end and meant to serve as ready reference. This book will cater the (5)_______ of students of literature and teachers teaching this course.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: To 'set off' something against a background is to place it where it shows up clearly: each essay is presented against its background.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. Each essay is set (1)______ against its background and made simpler by providing (2)_______ summary and critical commentary, short notes on textual issues, and (3)__________ of important critical and theoretical issues under the heading essay topics. (4)_____ of the most commonly used terms in the literature is given at the end and meant to serve as ready reference. This book will cater the (5)_______ of students of literature and teachers teaching this course.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The possessive 'its' refers back to the essay: the book provides its summary and critical commentary.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. Each essay is set (1)______ against its background and made simpler by providing (2)_______ summary and critical commentary, short notes on textual issues, and (3)__________ of important critical and theoretical issues under the heading essay topics. (4)_____ of the most commonly used terms in the literature is given at the end and meant to serve as ready reference. This book will cater the (5)_______ of students of literature and teachers teaching this course.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: A study guide offers 'discussions of' important critical and theoretical issues; 'chats' is too casual, and 'mindset' and 'thinking' do not fit a section of a book.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. Each essay is set (1)______ against its background and made simpler by providing (2)_______ summary and critical commentary, short notes on textual issues, and (3)__________ of important critical and theoretical issues under the heading essay topics. (4)_____ of the most commonly used terms in the literature is given at the end and meant to serve as ready reference. This book will cater the (5)_______ of students of literature and teachers teaching this course.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: A list of the commonly used terms of a subject, given with their meanings at the end of a book, is a 'glossary'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. Each essay is set (1)______ against its background and made simpler by providing (2)_______ summary and critical commentary, short notes on textual issues, and (3)__________ of important critical and theoretical issues under the heading essay topics. (4)_____ of the most commonly used terms in the literature is given at the end and meant to serve as ready reference. This book will cater the (5)_______ of students of literature and teachers teaching this course.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: A book caters to the 'needs' of its readers, what a course requires of them; 'whims' and 'desires' are passing wishes, and 'feelings' do not fit.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: According to Census of India 2011, what was the total population of India (approx)?
questions.explanation: The 2011 Census put India's population at 1,210.85 million, about 121 crore.

questions.text: Chhau is a major dance tradition of India. In which of the following Indian states is the dance form NOT prevalent?
questions.explanation: Chhau has three styles, named after where they are danced: Seraikella in Jharkhand, Purulia in West Bengal and Mayurbhanj in Odisha. It is not a tradition of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text: In November 2022, which state became the first North-East state to approve Mental Health and Social Care Policy?
questions.explanation: The Meghalaya cabinet approved the State Mental Health and Social Care Policy at the end of November 2022, making Meghalaya the first state in the North-East with such a policy.

questions.text: In which state is Vishakhapatnam Port located?
questions.explanation: Visakhapatnam Port, one of India's major ports on the east coast, is in Andhra Pradesh.

questions.text: Who among the following is the Indian classical dancer who masters both Bharatanatyam and Odissi dancing style?
questions.explanation: Sonal Mansingh trained in Bharatanatyam and then in Odissi under Kelucharan Mohapatra, and performs both. Padma Subrahmanyam is a Bharatanatyam dancer, Shovana Narayan a Kathak dancer and Guru Bipin Singh a Manipuri dancer.

questions.text: Which bacteria was discovered by Barry Marshall and Robin Warren that colonises the human stomach and causes chronic superficial gastritis ulcers?
questions.explanation: Barry Marshall and Robin Warren showed that the bacterium Helicobacter pylori causes gastritis and peptic ulcers, and received the 2005 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for it.

questions.text: What is a prominent trend in the microfinance sector in India?
questions.explanation: Microfinance lenders increasingly use mobile banking and digital payments, paying loans straight into borrowers' bank accounts and taking repayments digitally. The other options describe the opposite of the sector: its small, collateral-free loans need little paperwork, it relies more, not less, on digital technology, and most of its borrowers are women.

questions.text: The famous coal mining region ‘Korba’ is located in which state of India?
questions.explanation: Korba, in Chhattisgarh, is one of India's largest coalfields and a centre of coal-fired power generation.

questions.text: What do you mean by balanced budget?
questions.explanation: A budget is balanced when the government's expected expenditure equals its expected revenue; spending less than it receives gives a surplus budget, spending more a deficit budget.

questions.text: Rajgir Mahotsav is a beautiful representation of history, religion, art and culture. It is a three-day celebration in ____________.
questions.explanation: The Rajgir Mahotsav, a three-day festival of music and dance, is held at Rajgir in Nalanda district, Bihar.

questions.text: The famous novel ‘The God Of Small Things’ is written by ______________.
questions.explanation: 'The God of Small Things' is Arundhati Roy's first novel; it won the Booker Prize in 1997.

questions.text: The Men's Junior Hockey Asia Cup 2023, which was won by India, was held at _________.
questions.explanation: The 2023 Men's Junior Asia Cup was played at Salalah, Oman, in May and June 2023; India beat Pakistan 2-1 in the final for their fourth title.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In the context of the Revolt of 1857, Mangal Pandey belonged to which Bengal native Infantry?
questions.explanation: Mangal Pandey was a sepoy of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry; he attacked his officers at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857 and was hanged in April.

questions.text: Which of the following countries did India beat in the final to win the 2021 SAFF Championship?
questions.explanation: India beat Nepal 3-0 in the final of the 2021 SAFF Championship, played at Malé, Maldives, in October 2021.

questions.text: Vinesh Phogat became the first Indian woman wrestler to win how many medals at World Championships?
questions.explanation: Vinesh Phogat won bronze at the World Championships in 2019 and 2022, the first Indian woman wrestler with two World Championship medals.

questions.text: What is the purpose of the Cultural and Educational Rights?
options: To protect the language, culture, and religion of the minority communities
questions.explanation: The Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29 and 30) let any section of citizens conserve its distinct language, script or culture, and let minorities, religious or linguistic, set up and run educational institutions of their choice.

questions.text: In optics, which term refers to the opening of the diaphragm of a lens that spatially limits the propagation of light?
questions.explanation: The aperture is the opening, set by the diaphragm, through which light enters, so it limits the light passing. A collimator makes rays parallel, the apostilb is an old unit of luminance and a meniscus is a lens convex on one side and concave on the other.

questions.text: In which city is the Rajghat memorial situated?
questions.explanation: Raj Ghat, on the bank of the Yamuna in Delhi, marks the spot where Mahatma Gandhi was cremated on 31 January 1948.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In the 1939 Tripuri Congress Presidential Election, Pattabhi Sitaramayya was defeated by:
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose was re-elected Congress president in January 1939, defeating Pattabhi Sitaramayya, whom Gandhi backed; Gandhi called the defeat his own. Bose presided at Tripuri in March 1939 and resigned the next month.

questions.text: In which year was the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganization Act passed?
questions.explanation: Parliament passed the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act in August 2019; from 31 October 2019 it divided the state into two Union territories, Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The toddler decided to make a mess because he wanted to ______ the attention of its parents.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'seek': to seek attention is to try to get it, as in 'attention-seeking', which is what the toddler is doing. 'Elicit' normally takes a response, reaction or information as its object, and 'elicit attention' is found mainly in technical writing; 'please' and 'extract' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Glimpse
questions.explanation: A 'glimpse' is a brief look, and so is a 'glance'; to stare, examine or observe is to look long or closely.

questions.text: Identify the sentence that contains correct spellings in the given context.
options: She acid the test despite being sleep-deprived from studying for nearly 24 hours straight.
She acad the test desspite being sleep-deprived from studying for nearly 24 hours straight.
She aced the test daspite being sleep-deprived from studying for nearly 24 hours strait.
She aced the test despite being sleep-deprived from studying for nearly 24 hours straight.
questions.explanation: The correct spellings are 'aced' (did very well in), 'despite' and 'straight' (without a break); 'acid', 'acad', 'desspite', 'daspite' and 'strait' are wrong here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The teacher assured: “You have completed your homework, __________?”
questions.explanation: A positive statement takes a negative question tag with the same auxiliary: 'You have completed your homework, haven't you?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. A _________________(distinct) sense of restlessness was bothering me when I left the cemetery.
questions.explanation: 'Distinct' means clear and definite; its opposite is 'vague', unclear: 'a vague sense of restlessness'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. With cloud streaming, people can play games from a / internet-connected device, avoiding the need for pricey / dedicated hardware such as a game console.
options: dedicated hardware such as a game console
With cloud streaming, people can play games from a
internet-connected device, avoiding the need for pricey
questions.explanation: 'Internet-connected' begins with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an', not 'a': 'from an internet-connected device'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Keep someone at arm’s length
options: To avoid becoming too close or friendly with someone
Having energy again after being tired
questions.explanation: To 'keep someone at arm's length' is to avoid becoming close or friendly with them.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error. (A) This fridge / (B) comes including / (C) a 5-year / (D) warranty.
questions.explanation: A product 'comes with' what is included: 'This fridge comes with a 5-year warranty.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who looks at the dark side of life
questions.explanation: A 'pessimist' expects the worst; an 'optimist' is the opposite, and an 'idealist' pursues high ideals.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Many “a things are” used for the show.
questions.explanation: 'Many a' takes a singular noun and a singular verb: 'Many a thing is used for the show.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’. This film is a non-stop riot that many cite as one of the “funny” films of all time.
questions.explanation: 'One of the ... films of all time' ranks the film among all others, so it needs the superlative: 'one of the funniest films of all time'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'transmissible'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who regards the whole world as his country
questions.explanation: A 'cosmopolitan' is a citizen of the world, at home anywhere; a pacifist opposes war, a contemporary lives at the same time as another, and a celibate abstains from marriage and sex.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. The team played / really well, but / they lose the game / in the final minutes.
questions.explanation: The sentence tells of a past event ('played'), so the second verb must be past too: 'they lost the game'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. The school shall reopened / after summer / vacations of / one month.
questions.explanation: A modal such as 'shall' takes the base form of the verb: 'The school shall reopen'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. They waited with “anxiety” for the final results.
questions.explanation: 'Anxiety' is worry or unease; its opposite is 'calmness'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. Jack took on three jobs at once but soon realised he had _____________.
options: taken it with a grain of salt
bitten off more than he could chew
questions.explanation: To 'bite off more than one can chew' is to take on more than one can manage, as Jack did with three jobs at once.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. The CEO has _____________ than worrying about individual customer complaints.
questions.explanation: To have 'bigger fish to fry' is to have more important matters to deal with.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. I know it was wrong to distract his friends, but ________.
options: all’s fair in love and war
all’s unfair in love and war
questions.explanation: The proverb 'all's fair in love and war' excuses any tactic in a contest one cares about; the other options change its fixed wording.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. (1)___ the breakfast table the next morning, there was no sign of my wife. I (2)___ she was sleeping late, but Gladolia, upon being questioned, only (3)___ her head, (4)___ something, and turned the whites of her eyes up to the ceiling. I was glad when the meal was (5)___ and hurried to the library for another try at that story.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: One sits 'at' a table, so the scene opens 'at the breakfast table'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. (1)___ the breakfast table the next morning, there was no sign of my wife. I (2)___ she was sleeping late, but Gladolia, upon being questioned, only (3)___ her head, (4)___ something, and turned the whites of her eyes up to the ceiling. I was glad when the meal was (5)___ and hurried to the library for another try at that story.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'concluded': from her absence the narrator inferred that she was sleeping late, and 'conclude' is the verb for judging something true from the evidence. 'Decided' can also mean 'came to think', so it is arguable, but its usual sense is making a choice; 'accepted' and 'examined' do not fit.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. (1)___ the breakfast table the next morning, there was no sign of my wife. I (2)___ she was sleeping late, but Gladolia, upon being questioned, only (3)___ her head, (4)___ something, and turned the whites of her eyes up to the ceiling. I was glad when the meal was (5)___ and hurried to the library for another try at that story.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: One 'shakes' one's head to say no or show one does not know; the past tense 'shook' fits 'only ___ her head'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. (1)___ the breakfast table the next morning, there was no sign of my wife. I (2)___ she was sleeping late, but Gladolia, upon being questioned, only (3)___ her head, (4)___ something, and turned the whites of her eyes up to the ceiling. I was glad when the meal was (5)___ and hurried to the library for another try at that story.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: To 'mutter' is to say something quietly and indistinctly, which fits '___ something'; 'mugged', 'muffed' and 'mutilated' do not.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. (1)___ the breakfast table the next morning, there was no sign of my wife. I (2)___ she was sleeping late, but Gladolia, upon being questioned, only (3)___ her head, (4)___ something, and turned the whites of her eyes up to the ceiling. I was glad when the meal was (5)___ and hurried to the library for another try at that story.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: A meal that is 'over' has ended: he was glad when breakfast was over and hurried to the library.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Ramesh purchased a bag for ₹1,275 and sold it at a gain of 15% but calculated on the selling price. Find the selling price of the bag.
questions.explanation: With the gain at 15% of the selling price, the cost price is 85% of it: SP = 1,275/0.85 = ₹1,500.

questions.text: The novel ‘God of Small Things’ is a creation of which novelist?
questions.explanation: 'The God of Small Things' (1997), which won the Booker Prize that year, is Arundhati Roy's first novel.

questions.text: Which of the following terms best describes the average number of runs a batter makes per 100 deliveries in cricket?
questions.explanation: Strike rate = runs scored ÷ balls faced × 100. Batting average is runs per dismissal, and economy rate is the runs a bowler concedes per over.

questions.text: Yuki Bhambri and Saketh Myneni won the Bangkok Open Challenger title 2023. They are related to which sport?
questions.explanation: Yuki Bhambri and Saketh Myneni are Indian tennis players; they won the men's doubles at the Bangkok Open, an ATP Challenger tournament played at Nonthaburi, Thailand, in January 2023.

questions.text: Deba Prasad Das, Pankaj Charan Das and Gangadhar Pradhan are associated with which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: Deba Prasad Das, Pankaj Charan Das and Gangadhar Pradhan were gurus of Odissi, Odisha's classical dance; the first two were among the gurus who revived the form in the mid-20th century.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental duty listed in the Indian Constitution?
options: To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
To engage in political activities to promote democracy
To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
questions.explanation: Upholding the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India, preserving the heritage of our composite culture, and safeguarding public property and abjuring violence are fundamental duties under Article 51A; political activity is not one of them.

questions.text: As of 2022, 12-feet statue of Adi Shankaracharya, which was unveiled by the Prime Minister of India is located in _________
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi unveiled the 12-foot statue of Adi Shankaracharya at his samadhi at Kedarnath, Uttarakhand, in November 2021.

questions.text: During cell division, the formation of a new cell wall is followed by the accumulation of:
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives phragmoplast: in a dividing plant cell a framework of microtubules, the phragmoplast, gathers between the two daughter nuclei, and vesicles brought to it fuse into the cell plate from which the new cell wall grows. It forms before the plate and keeps re-forming at the plate's growing edge, so the question puts the order loosely, but none of the other options has any part in forming the wall.

questions.text: Bhanu Ji is associated with which of the following Gharanas of Kathak?
questions.explanation: Bhanuji, a devotee of Shiva, is regarded as the founder of the Jaipur gharana of Kathak.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of capital expenditure in the government budget?
questions.explanation: Buying military equipment creates assets, so it is capital expenditure. Interest payments, the upkeep of buildings and subsidies create no assets and are revenue expenditure.

questions.text: FIH Men's Hockey World Cup 2023 was held in which Indian state/UT?
questions.explanation: The 2023 FIH Men's Hockey World Cup was held in Odisha, at Bhubaneswar and Rourkela, in January 2023.

questions.text: An image of which of the following elements is shown by the map of Cyprus from which the element got its name?
questions.explanation: Copper takes its name, through the Latin 'cuprum', from Cyprus, a chief source of the metal in the ancient world; the map of the island on the Cypriot flag is coloured copper-orange for it.

questions.text: The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (PMGKRA) was launched in the year 2020 by which Ministry of Government of India?
options: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
questions.explanation: The Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan, launched in June 2020 to give work to migrant workers who had gone back to their villages during the Covid-19 lockdown, had the Ministry of Rural Development as its nodal ministry.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the Hindi novel ‘Raag Darbari’?
questions.explanation: 'Raag Darbari' (1968), a satire on village politics in Uttar Pradesh, is by Shrilal Shukla; it won the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1969.

questions.text: Who is the first female classical dancer in Indian history to be nominated as a Member of Rajya Sabha, the upper house of the Parliament of India?
questions.explanation: Rukmini Devi Arundale, the Bharatanatyam dancer who founded Kalakshetra in 1936, was nominated to the Rajya Sabha in 1952, the first Indian woman to be nominated to it.

questions.text: What does the term ‘Overdraft’ mean in banking?
options: The process of transferring funds between bank accounts
The maximum withdrawal limit from an ATM
questions.explanation: An overdraft lets an account holder draw more than the balance in the account, up to an agreed limit, as short-term credit on which interest is charged.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of Eastern Ghats peak?
questions.explanation: Mahendragiri, about 1,500 m high in Gajapati district, Odisha, is a peak of the Eastern Ghats. Doddabetta is in the Nilgiris, Anamudi in the Western Ghats and Guru Shikhar in the Aravallis.

questions.text: Indian musician, Pandit Hari Prasad Chaurasia used to play which of the following musical instruments?
questions.explanation: Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is India's best-known player of the bansuri, the bamboo flute of Hindustani classical music.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following was the first major and decisive victory for the East India Company on the soil of India?
questions.explanation: At Plassey in June 1757 Robert Clive's forces defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah, the Nawab of Bengal, helped by Mir Jafar's defection; the victory laid the foundation of British power in Bengal.

questions.text: Which of the following locations receives the most rainfall in India?
questions.explanation: Mawsynram, in the East Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, has the highest average annual rainfall in India; Jaisalmer, in the Thar Desert, is among the driest places.

questions.text: According to the Census of India 2011, what was the literacy rate recorded in Kerala?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Kerala had the highest literacy rate of any state, 94.0%.

questions.text: The Digital Lok Adalat, powered by AI (Artificial Intelligence) and Blockchain, was launched by the then National Legal Services Authority Chairman ___________ during the 18th All India Legal Services Authorities’ meet held in Jaipur in July 2022.
questions.explanation: Justice U. U. Lalit, then Executive Chairman of the National Legal Services Authority, launched the Digital Lok Adalat at the meet in Jaipur in July 2022; he became Chief Justice of India the next month.

questions.text: Which of the following music directors is known as ‘Mozart of Madras’?
questions.explanation: A. R. Rahman, the composer from Chennai (Madras), is widely called the 'Mozart of Madras'.

questions.text: What is the tenure of the Vice-President of India?
options: Until he wants to hold the office
questions.explanation: Under Article 67 the Vice-President holds office for five years from the day he enters upon it, and stays on until a successor takes office.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If I hand her a flower and say, “Give it to mamma,” she “take it” to her mother.
questions.explanation: The singular 'she' takes 'takes' in the present simple, which matches 'hand' and 'say' in this statement of what usually happens.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Divergent
questions.explanation: 'Divergent' means differing or moving apart; its opposite is 'similar' (or 'convergent').

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. “To much” seriousness “hardens the” “world, pinning” it down “with rules.”
questions.explanation: 'Too', not 'to', means more than is wanted: 'Too much seriousness hardens the world'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. He managed to save his father’s business by “the sweat of his brow”.
questions.explanation: To do something 'by the sweat of one's brow' is to do it through one's own hard work.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase. A place where water is collected and stored for future use.
questions.explanation: A 'reservoir' is a natural or artificial place where water is collected and stored; an aquarium holds fish, a sanatorium treats the sick and a resort is a holiday place.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. The new chairman of the company “announced attracted bonus for the employees” on the occasion of the new year.
options: announced an attractive bonus for the employees
announcing attracted bonus for the employees
announced attracting bonus for the employees
questions.explanation: The singular 'bonus' needs the article 'an', and the adjective 'attractive' (appealing) is the word that describes it: 'announced an attractive bonus for the employees'. 'Attracted' and 'attracting' do not mean appealing, and 'announcing' leaves the sentence without a main verb.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error. (A) The institute / (B) have been / (C) divided into / (D) multiple departments
questions.explanation: 'The institute' is singular and takes 'has been': 'The institute has been divided into multiple departments.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. They allowed us to “powder by crushing” the spices, pick over the raisins and lick the stirring spoons.
questions.explanation: To 'grind' spices is to crush them to powder: 'They allowed us to grind the spices'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Mild
questions.explanation: 'Mild' means not harsh or strong: 'gentle'. 'Severe' and 'scathing' are nearly its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. Instead of answering the question directly, the politician kept ___________.
questions.explanation: To 'beat around the bush' is to avoid coming to the point, as the politician did instead of answering directly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Rishi asked Karan “will he get a new football for him?”
options: would he get a new football for him?
if he would get a new football for him.
if would he get a new football for him?
if he will get a new football for him?
questions.explanation: A reported yes/no question is introduced with 'if', puts the subject before the verb, moves 'will' back to 'would' after the past 'asked', and ends with a full stop: 'Rishi asked Karan if he would get a new football for him.'

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'retrospect'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Often
questions.explanation: 'Often' means many times; its opposite is 'rarely'. 'Usually' and 'generally' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The boy whose the sister is ill has left.
questions.explanation: 'Whose' already acts as a determiner, so no article follows it: 'The boy whose sister is ill has left.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. A strong _________ for mathematics and problem-solving can be very useful.
questions.explanation: An 'aptitude' is a natural ability, and it takes 'for': 'a strong aptitude for mathematics'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. My manager forced me to resign from my job as a chef since I underwent a spine surgery. I was depressed and had lost all hope. Later my father motivated me to open my own café and showed me ways to be independent. After all it is true that one should not ____________.
questions.explanation: 'Don't cry over spilt milk' means there is no use regretting what cannot be undone; the writer stopped grieving over the lost job and opened a café.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. He was “quaking in his boots” when he had to give a speech on the stage.
questions.explanation: To be 'quaking in one's boots' is to be very frightened, to tremble with fear.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. If I “will get” good marks, my father will buy me a laptop.
questions.explanation: In a first conditional the 'if' clause takes the present simple and the main clause 'will': 'If I get good marks, my father will buy me a laptop.'

questions.text: Four words of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains a spelling error. Human activities that “release” longlived greenhouse gases into the atmosphere also “leed” to the enhancement of “concentrations” of shorterlived ozone and “particulate” matter in the atmosphere.
questions.explanation: The verb is spelt 'lead': the gases also lead to higher concentrations of ozone and particulate matter.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Fruits and vegetables contain important vitamins, minerals and plant (1)________. They also contain fibre. There are many (2)________ of fruits and vegetables available and many ways to prepare, cook and serve them. A diet (3)_____ in fruit and vegetables can help protect you against cancer, diabetes and heart disease. Eat five kinds of vegetable and two kinds of fruit every day for good health. Most Indians do not eat (4)________ fruit and vegetables. When buying and serving fruit and vegetables, aim for variety to get the most (5)________ and appeal.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The sentence lists useful substances in fruit and vegetables: vitamins, minerals and plant 'chemicals' (phytochemicals). Residue, bacteria and organisms are not what the food is valued for.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Fruits and vegetables contain important vitamins, minerals and plant (1)________. They also contain fibre. There are many (2)________ of fruits and vegetables available and many ways to prepare, cook and serve them. A diet (3)_____ in fruit and vegetables can help protect you against cancer, diabetes and heart disease. Eat five kinds of vegetable and two kinds of fruit every day for good health. Most Indians do not eat (4)________ fruit and vegetables. When buying and serving fruit and vegetables, aim for variety to get the most (5)________ and appeal.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Many varieties of fruits and vegetables' means many different kinds of them; 'traits' and 'characters' are qualities, not kinds.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Fruits and vegetables contain important vitamins, minerals and plant (1)________. They also contain fibre. There are many (2)________ of fruits and vegetables available and many ways to prepare, cook and serve them. A diet (3)_____ in fruit and vegetables can help protect you against cancer, diabetes and heart disease. Eat five kinds of vegetable and two kinds of fruit every day for good health. Most Indians do not eat (4)________ fruit and vegetables. When buying and serving fruit and vegetables, aim for variety to get the most (5)________ and appeal.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: A diet 'rich in' something contains a lot of it: 'a diet rich in fruit and vegetables'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Fruits and vegetables contain important vitamins, minerals and plant (1)________. They also contain fibre. There are many (2)________ of fruits and vegetables available and many ways to prepare, cook and serve them. A diet (3)_____ in fruit and vegetables can help protect you against cancer, diabetes and heart disease. Eat five kinds of vegetable and two kinds of fruit every day for good health. Most Indians do not eat (4)________ fruit and vegetables. When buying and serving fruit and vegetables, aim for variety to get the most (5)________ and appeal.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Enough', as much as is needed, goes straight before the noun: 'do not eat enough fruit and vegetables'. 'Plenty' needs 'of', 'many' does not suit the uncountable 'fruit', and 'some' is unusual in a negative sentence.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Fruits and vegetables contain important vitamins, minerals and plant (1)________. They also contain fibre. There are many (2)________ of fruits and vegetables available and many ways to prepare, cook and serve them. A diet (3)_____ in fruit and vegetables can help protect you against cancer, diabetes and heart disease. Eat five kinds of vegetable and two kinds of fruit every day for good health. Most Indians do not eat (4)________ fruit and vegetables. When buying and serving fruit and vegetables, aim for variety to get the most (5)________ and appeal.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Eating a variety gets the most 'nutrients', which matches the vitamins and minerals the passage began with.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: A shopkeeper bought an oven for ₹25,000 and sold it for ₹29,500. He spent ₹1,500 as overheads. What is his loss or gain percentage (rounded off to the nearest integer)?
A car covers 60 km at a speed of 84 km/h. If the average speed for the whole journey is 72 km/h, then the speed of the car for the next 60 km of the journey is:
questions.explanation: The whole 120 km at 72 km/h takes 120/72 = 5/3 h, and the first 60 km took 60/84 = 5/7 h. The next 60 km take 5/3 − 5/7 = 20/21 h, a speed of 60 ÷ 20/21 = 63 km/h.

questions.text: Seven people, W, D, J, S, H, G and Y are sitting in a straight line, facing south. G sits second to the left of S. G is the immediate neighbour of D and H. Y sits third to the right of D. Only two people sit to the right of W. Who sits at the extreme right end of the line?
questions.explanation: Number the seats 1 to 7 from the right end of the row (the people face south); W is 3rd. G is two seats to S's left with D and H on either side of it, so S can only be 4th (in 1st or 2nd, G or its neighbour would take W's seat; in 5th or beyond, G would be at the left end or past it, without a seat on each side): G is 6th, with D and H in 5th and 7th. Y third to D's right rules out D in 7th (Y would take S's seat), so D is 5th, H 7th, Y 2nd and J 1st, at the right end.

questions.text: In which year was the Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY) launched?
questions.explanation: The Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana of the Ministry of Labour and Employment began in August 2016 to encourage employers to create new jobs: for new employees, the government paid the employer's pension (EPS) contribution, and from April 2018 the employer's whole EPF and EPS contribution.

questions.text: The film based on which of the following novels by Amrita Pritam won the National Film Award?
questions.explanation: Amrita Pritam's Partition novel 'Pinjar' (1950) was filmed by Chandraprakash Dwivedi in 2003, and the film won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film on National Integration. 'Raseedi Ticket' is her autobiography.

questions.text: Who was the Prime Minster of India when the Fundamental Duties were first incorporated in the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Duties (Article 51A, Part IVA) were added by the 42nd Amendment, 1976, on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation, while Indira Gandhi was Prime Minister.

questions.text: Who said the following? “Money is what money does.”
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Walker: economics textbooks usually credit 'Money is what money does', a definition of money by its functions (whatever does the work of money is money), to the American economist Francis A. Walker.

questions.text: Which of the following ports is located in Odisha?
questions.explanation: Paradip, near the mouth of the Mahanadi in Jagatsinghpur district, is Odisha's major port. Haldia is in West Bengal, Kandla (Deendayal) in Gujarat and Tuticorin (V. O. Chidambaranar) in Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: Rohini Bhate, Pandit Munnalal Shukla, Kumudini Lakhia and Uma Sharma are famous exponents of which of the following classical dance forms?
questions.explanation: Rohini Bhate, Pandit Munnalal Shukla, Kumudini Lakhia and Uma Sharma are all noted Kathak dancers and gurus.

questions.text: India played the final of ODI Cricket World Cup 2011 against which country?
questions.explanation: India beat Sri Lanka by six wickets in the 2011 World Cup final at the Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai, on 2 April 2011.

questions.text: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance style belongs to ________________.
questions.explanation: Mohiniyattam, the 'dance of the enchantress', is the classical dance of Kerala, traditionally a solo dance performed by women.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the Indian political party system?
questions.explanation: India has a multi-party system, marked at times by factions, defections and a weak opposition; it has never had a single-party system.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following was the first Satyagraha Movement led by Mahatma Gandhi in British India?
questions.explanation: Champaran in Bihar (1917), against the forced cultivation of indigo, was Gandhi's first satyagraha in India. Kheda followed in 1918 and the Rowlatt Satyagraha in 1919; the Bardoli Satyagraha of 1928 was led by Vallabhbhai Patel.

questions.text: The fundamental vocabulary of __________ dance constitutes mock combat techniques, stylised gaits of birds and animals and movements modelled on the chores of village housewives and mostly performed by male dancers in Eastern India.
questions.explanation: Chhau, danced in Seraikela (Jharkhand), Purulia (West Bengal) and Mayurbhanj (Odisha), draws on mock combat, the gaits of birds and animals and the chores of village women, and is performed mostly by men.

questions.text: The Red Fort is located in:
questions.explanation: The Red Fort (Lal Qila) in Delhi was built by Shah Jahan between 1639 and 1648 as the palace-fort of his new capital, Shahjahanabad.

questions.text: The Goa government launched a new scheme in November 2022 for which of the following?
questions.explanation: In November 2022 Chief Minister Pramod Sawant launched the Mukhyamantri Dev Darshan Yatra Yojana, a free state-funded pilgrimage for older residents, flagging off a busload of pilgrims to Tirupati.

questions.text: Ruturaj Gaikwad became the first batsman in List-A cricket to hit how many sixes in an over?
questions.explanation: In the Vijay Hazare Trophy quarter-final against Uttar Pradesh in November 2022, Ruturaj Gaikwad hit seven sixes in one over from Shiva Singh (one of the balls a no-ball), the first time in List-A cricket, on his way to 220 not out.

questions.text: Camels are found in which type of forests in India from the following?
questions.explanation: NCERT lists camels, with wild asses, foxes and wolves, among the animals of the tropical thorn forests and scrubs of India's dry north-west, such as Rajasthan and Gujarat.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Under whom among the following British Governor-Generals was the new policy of ‘paramountcy’ initiated in British India by the East India Company?
questions.explanation: The policy of 'paramountcy', under which the Company claimed its authority was greater than that of the Indian states, was initiated under Lord Hastings, Governor-General from 1813 to 1823 (not Warren Hastings).

questions.text: Paryushana Parva is a festival of which of the following communities?
