questions.explanation: Paryushana, a period of fasting, reflection and forgiveness held in the month of Bhadrapada, is the most important annual festival of the Jains.

questions.text: Who coined the word ‘cell’ in the 1600s, from the Latin word ‘cellula’, meaning ‘small room’?
questions.explanation: Robert Hooke named the cell in 1665, in 'Micrographia', after seeing the tiny box-like compartments of a thin slice of cork under his microscope.

questions.text: Which of the following is a feature of Micro Finance Institutions?
questions.explanation: Microfinance institutions give small loans and other financial services to poor and low-income people who lack access to ordinary banking.

questions.text: Which of the following States became the overall champions in both the men’s and women’s categories in the 2023 Janjatiya Khel Mahotsav?
questions.explanation: Odisha were the overall champions in both the men's and women's categories at the first Janjatiya Khel Mahotsav, the tribal games held at KIIT, Bhubaneswar, in June 2023.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error and select the option which rectifies that error. The space agency wanted / to test with a chimp / before orbiting a astronaut / in a Mercury capsule.
questions.explanation: 'Astronaut' begins with a vowel sound and takes 'an': 'before orbiting an astronaut'. 'A chimp' and 'a Mercury capsule' are correct.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. They said that “he is not going to call them”.
options: he has not gone to call then
they are not going to call them
he was not going to call them
questions.explanation: After the past reporting verb 'said', the reported clause moves back a tense: 'They said that he was not going to call them.'

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains a misspelt word. For every “endeavour”-whether in the area of “career”, “academics”, music, sports or even in spirituality, it is a long “ardous” journey.
questions.explanation: The misspelt word is 'ardous'; the correct spelling is 'arduous'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The entrepreneur decided to “throw caution to the wind”.
questions.explanation: To 'throw caution to the wind' is to stop worrying about the danger and take a risk.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Tedious
questions.explanation: 'Tedious' means long and boring: 'dreary'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Not fit for eating
questions.explanation: 'Inedible' means not fit to be eaten. 'Inept' means unskilled, 'ineligible' not qualified and 'ineluctable' unavoidable.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. If he had paid / attention to the announcement, / he had not / missed the train.
questions.explanation: A condition about the past takes 'would have' and the past participle in the main clause: 'If he had paid attention to the announcement, he would not have missed the train.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Child’s play
questions.explanation: 'Child's play' is something very easy to do.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. The tour company has included all the activities that you have requested in your “itenarary”.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'itinerary', the planned route or schedule of a journey.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Spill the beans
options: To believe something as it seems
To do things in a fair way
To cry over what is done
questions.explanation: To 'spill the beans' is to tell a secret.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The mother requested the nurse to “keep an eye on” the baby while she went for tea.
options: Watch for the arrival or appearance
questions.explanation: To 'keep an eye on' someone is to watch over and look after them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If you need any help tomorrow, “let him knows.”
questions.explanation: 'Let' takes an object and the bare infinitive: 'let me know'. The other options use 'known' or 'knew'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Helena loves to dig and “played in the dirt” like any other child.
questions.explanation: The two verbs after 'loves to' are parallel: 'Helena loves to dig and play in the dirt'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The development of skills can contribute to structural transformation and economic growth “in enhance employability” and labour productivity and helping countries to become more competitive.
questions.explanation: The means is shown by 'by' and a gerund, parallel with 'helping': 'by enhancing employability and labour productivity and helping countries ...'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Everyone “likes in watch” a magic show.
questions.explanation: 'Like' is followed by a to-infinitive (or a gerund), and the singular 'everyone' takes 'likes': 'Everyone likes to watch a magic show.'

questions.text: The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. He is the better-looking hero in the entire film industry.
options: He is the best-looking hero in the entire film industry.
He is the good-looking hero than the entire film industry.
He is the best-looking hero more than the entire film industry.
He is the good-looking hero in the entire film industry.
questions.explanation: Comparing one hero with all the others in the industry needs the superlative: 'the best-looking hero in the entire film industry'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He is first ______ to his job and then to his family.
questions.explanation: To be 'committed' to something is to be dedicated to it: first to his job, then to his family.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Pretend
questions.explanation: To 'pretend' is to 'feign', to make a false show of something.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Align
questions.explanation: To 'align' is to put in line or in order; 'disrupt', to throw into disorder, is its opposite. 'Position', 'centre' and 'coincide' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. One of her colleagues had agreed to act as the “arbitratore” in finalising the contract.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'arbitrator', a person chosen to settle a dispute.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There will only be two types of human beings in the future: the minority having enormous brains and (1)________ bodies, and the majority with tiny brains and muscular bodies. The size of the average brain will (2)________ diminish; not because of our innate laziness, but because of our over-concern about our physical appearance. In the old days, most people dreamt of having shelter and a stable food supply. As we no longer struggle for the basic (3)________, our dreams focus instead on the search for physical beauty, how to obtain and maintain the ‘ideal body shape’ and healthy life the media promotes. Physical beauty will become the main goal of the majority. They’ll do exercises every day, taking (4)________ to maintain their shape while not noticing that their brains are shrinking. Actually, there is no doubt that they’ll work (5)________ hard to make their brains smaller.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'tiny', which contrasts the minority's bodies with their enormous brains and echoes the passage's own 'tiny brains'. 'Minute' (extremely small) is close in meaning but overstates it for a human body; 'minor' describes importance rather than physical size, and 'cute' describes looks.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There will only be two types of human beings in the future: the minority having enormous brains and (1)________ bodies, and the majority with tiny brains and muscular bodies. The size of the average brain will (2)________ diminish; not because of our innate laziness, but because of our over-concern about our physical appearance. In the old days, most people dreamt of having shelter and a stable food supply. As we no longer struggle for the basic (3)________, our dreams focus instead on the search for physical beauty, how to obtain and maintain the ‘ideal body shape’ and healthy life the media promotes. Physical beauty will become the main goal of the majority. They’ll do exercises every day, taking (4)________ to maintain their shape while not noticing that their brains are shrinking. Actually, there is no doubt that they’ll work (5)________ hard to make their brains smaller.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The brain will 'gradually' diminish, slowly over time; 'properly' and 'appropriately' make no sense here, and 'slightly' would undercut the passage's 'tiny brains'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There will only be two types of human beings in the future: the minority having enormous brains and (1)________ bodies, and the majority with tiny brains and muscular bodies. The size of the average brain will (2)________ diminish; not because of our innate laziness, but because of our over-concern about our physical appearance. In the old days, most people dreamt of having shelter and a stable food supply. As we no longer struggle for the basic (3)________, our dreams focus instead on the search for physical beauty, how to obtain and maintain the ‘ideal body shape’ and healthy life the media promotes. Physical beauty will become the main goal of the majority. They’ll do exercises every day, taking (4)________ to maintain their shape while not noticing that their brains are shrinking. Actually, there is no doubt that they’ll work (5)________ hard to make their brains smaller.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Shelter and a stable food supply, named just before, are the basic 'necessities' of life, the things people cannot do without; 'amenities' and 'facilities' are comforts and services, not food and shelter.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There will only be two types of human beings in the future: the minority having enormous brains and (1)________ bodies, and the majority with tiny brains and muscular bodies. The size of the average brain will (2)________ diminish; not because of our innate laziness, but because of our over-concern about our physical appearance. In the old days, most people dreamt of having shelter and a stable food supply. As we no longer struggle for the basic (3)________, our dreams focus instead on the search for physical beauty, how to obtain and maintain the ‘ideal body shape’ and healthy life the media promotes. Physical beauty will become the main goal of the majority. They’ll do exercises every day, taking (4)________ to maintain their shape while not noticing that their brains are shrinking. Actually, there is no doubt that they’ll work (5)________ hard to make their brains smaller.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: To keep their shape they take 'nutrients', the substances the body needs. 'Nutrition' is nourishment in general, not something one 'takes', and preservatives and additives are put into food.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There will only be two types of human beings in the future: the minority having enormous brains and (1)________ bodies, and the majority with tiny brains and muscular bodies. The size of the average brain will (2)________ diminish; not because of our innate laziness, but because of our over-concern about our physical appearance. In the old days, most people dreamt of having shelter and a stable food supply. As we no longer struggle for the basic (3)________, our dreams focus instead on the search for physical beauty, how to obtain and maintain the ‘ideal body shape’ and healthy life the media promotes. Physical beauty will become the main goal of the majority. They’ll do exercises every day, taking (4)________ to maintain their shape while not noticing that their brains are shrinking. Actually, there is no doubt that they’ll work (5)________ hard to make their brains smaller.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Extremely' intensifies 'hard': they will work very hard at it. 'So hard' is informal unless a 'that' clause follows, and 'rarely' and 'impishly' (mischievously) make no sense with 'hard'.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The monthly income of a person was ₹27,000 and his monthly expenditure was ₹18,000. In the next year, his income increased by 28% and his expenditure increased by 14%. Find the percentage increase in his savings.
How long can a person remain a minister without being a member of either House of the State Legislature?
questions.explanation: Under Article 164(4), a minister who for six consecutive months is not a member of the State Legislature ceases to be a minister at the end of that period.

questions.text: The world’s largest camel fair is held in which of the following cities?
questions.explanation: The Pushkar Fair, held every year in the month of Kartik at Pushkar in Ajmer district, Rajasthan, is known as the world's largest camel fair.

questions.text: Who among the following Indian musicians is the inventor of Mohan Veena?
questions.explanation: The Mohan Veena, a slide guitar adapted for Hindustani music with added sympathetic and drone strings, was created by Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt.

questions.text: Mulk Raj Anand is the author of _____________.
questions.explanation: Mulk Raj Anand's first novel, 'Untouchable' (1935), follows a day in the life of Bakha, a young sweeper. 'The Guide' is R. K. Narayan's, 'The Invisible Man' H. G. Wells's and 'A Passage to India' E. M. Forster's.

questions.text: Which of the following musicians of medieval India is referred to as ‘Tuti-e-Hind’ and is also regarded as the father of qawwali?
questions.explanation: Amir Khusrau, poet and musician of the Delhi Sultanate and a disciple of Nizamuddin Auliya, was called 'Tuti-e-Hind' (the parrot of India) and is regarded as the father of qawwali.

questions.text: The blue green alga Anabaena lives in the leaves of Azolla, a freshwater fern, forming which of the following relationships?
questions.explanation: Anabaena fixes nitrogen for the fern while living sheltered in cavities of its leaves, so both partners benefit: a symbiotic relationship.

questions.text: Who was famous for publishing a formula in 1827 that shows the mathematical relationship between current, resistance and voltage?
questions.explanation: Georg Simon Ohm set out what is now Ohm's law, V = IR, in 'Die galvanische Kette, mathematisch bearbeitet' (1827).

questions.text: Identify the correct pair (name of shifting agriculture and related state) from the following.
questions.explanation: NCERT lists shifting cultivation as 'Bewar' or 'Dahiya' in Madhya Pradesh, 'Podu' in Andhra Pradesh, 'Bringa' in Odisha and 'Kuruwa' in Jharkhand.

questions.text: The Balti dance of ____________ is distinct as it has its own costume, music and songs in the Balti language. The dance is only performed on rare occasions, such as feasts or celebrations.
questions.explanation: The Balti dance belongs to the Balti people of Ladakh, chiefly of Kargil district; their language, Balti, is also spoken across the Line of Control in Baltistan.

questions.text: The Fundamental Duties of Indian Citizens were adopted from the Constitution of which country?
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Duties (Article 51A), added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976 on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation, were modelled on the Constitution of the former USSR.

questions.text: Which state hosted the 36th National Games of India?
questions.explanation: The 36th National Games were held in Gujarat from 29 September to 12 October 2022.

questions.text: Jet streams are a particular form of:
questions.explanation: Jet streams are narrow belts of very fast winds high in the troposphere. There, away from surface friction, the pressure gradient force is balanced by the Coriolis force, so they blow parallel to the isobars as geostrophic winds.

questions.text: According to the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index Report 2022, a total of 415 million people exited multidimensional poverty in India in the last ________.
questions.explanation: The UNDP-OPHI Global Multidimensional Poverty Index 2022 found that about 415 million people in India left multidimensional poverty in the 15 years from 2005-06 to 2019-21.

questions.text: What is the primary function of a commercial bank?
questions.explanation: A commercial bank's main business is accepting deposits from the public and lending them out. Issuing currency, monetary policy and the money supply are the central bank's concern (in India, the Reserve Bank's).

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of revenue receipt in the government budget?
options: Repayment of a loan by a state-owned company
Dividends received from a state-owned enterprise
questions.explanation: Dividends from a public sector enterprise are non-tax revenue, a revenue receipt: they create no liability and reduce no asset. Selling land, recovering a loan and borrowing are capital receipts.

questions.text: Birsa Munda Hockey Stadium was built in which state?
questions.explanation: The Birsa Munda International Hockey Stadium at Rourkela, Odisha, was built for the 2023 Men's Hockey World Cup, which Odisha hosted at Rourkela and Bhubaneswar.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who received the title Pandita from the faculty of Calcutta University for her knowledge of Sanskrit?
questions.explanation: Ramabai, a Sanskrit scholar, was given the titles 'Pandita' and 'Sarasvati' by the faculty of Calcutta University in 1878; she later worked for the education of widows.

questions.text: Rani Machaiah from Karnataka was awarded the Padma Shri for her contribution to popularising ___________ in and outside Karnataka.
questions.explanation: Rani Machaiah of Kodagu received the Padma Shri in 2023 for popularising Ummathat, the traditional dance of Kodava women.

questions.text: Which of the following hills are located in Purvachal?
questions.explanation: Purvachal, the eastern hills, takes in the Patkai hills, Naga hills, Manipur hills and Mizo hills. The Khasi and Jaintia hills belong to the Meghalaya plateau, the Shevroy and Javadi hills to the Eastern Ghats, and Anai Mudi and Doda Betta to the Western Ghats.

questions.text: The mausoleum of the Taj Mahal was designed by _______________.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Ustad Ahmad Lahori, generally credited as the chief architect of the Taj Mahal on the word of his son, Lutfullah Muhandis; Shah Jahan commissioned it. The later story of an Ustad Isa as its designer is poorly attested.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: What was the Swadeshi Movement called in the state of Andhra Pradesh?
questions.explanation: In the Andhra region the Swadeshi Movement (1905-08) was known as the Vande Mataram Movement.

questions.text: ‘Midnight’s Children’ is a novel by which of the following writers?
questions.explanation: Salman Rushdie's 'Midnight's Children' (1981), about children born at the hour of India's independence, won the Booker Prize.

questions.text: Which of the following countries hosted the IBA Women’s World Boxing Championships for the third time in March 2023?
questions.explanation: New Delhi hosted the IBA Women's World Boxing Championships in March 2023, India's third time as host after 2006 and 2018.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Castles in the air
questions.explanation: 'Castles in the air' are daydreams: plans or hopes that are unrealistic and cannot come true.

questions.text: Four words of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains a spelling error. Ongoing climate change, caused by the “acumulation” of greenhouse gases in the “atmosphere”, is happening on a timescale of “decades” to centuries and is driving “environmental” changes worldwide.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'accumulation', with a double 'c'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Laconic
questions.explanation: 'Laconic' means using very few words: 'concise'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Make-up was _______ she hardly wore.
questions.explanation: The main clause is affirmative, so 'something', not 'anything': 'Make-up was something she hardly wore.' 'Anybody' and 'someone' refer to people.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The manager asked me “if I have completed my projects”.
options: if he has completed my projects
if I has completed my projects
if I had completed my projects
if I shall have completed my projects
questions.explanation: After a past reporting verb ('asked'), the present perfect moves back to the past perfect: 'if I had completed my projects'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Pause indecisively
questions.explanation: To 'hesitate' is to pause before acting because one is unsure. To hibernate is to sleep through the winter, to hoist is to raise and to hobble is to walk unsteadily.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error and select the option which rectifies that error. The SNAP-10 A / was launched on 3 April 1965 / on a Atlas-Agena D rocket / from Vandenberg Air Force Base.
questions.explanation: 'Atlas' begins with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an': 'on an Atlas-Agena D rocket'.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the following sentence. He “dispised” the taste of black coffee.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'despised'.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. This car is “lesser” expensive than the “one” I had “come” “to” buy.
questions.explanation: 'Lesser' is itself a comparative, used before a noun ('the lesser evil'); before an adjective such as 'expensive' the word is 'less': 'less expensive than the one I had come to buy'.

questions.text: Select the appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Grasping at straws
options: Holding the last strands of straw
questions.explanation: To 'grasp at straws' is to try anything, however unlikely to work, out of desperation.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. She told me, ________, that she was going to live in New York.
questions.explanation: 'Out of the blue' means unexpectedly, without warning. 'Once in a blue moon' means very rarely and 'black and blue' bruised.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank. The medical procedure was successful, but the patient experienced some minor ________(troubles) during recovery.
questions.explanation: Problems that arise during recovery from a medical procedure are 'complications'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error. (A) It is said / (B) that fortune / (C) favour the / (D) brave.
questions.explanation: 'Fortune' is singular and takes a singular verb: 'fortune favours the brave'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Teenage is that phase of life when “you are proposed to” the world outside.
questions.explanation: To be 'exposed to' something is to come into contact with it, as teenagers do with the world outside. To be 'proposed to' is to receive an offer of marriage.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'experience'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Ravi has little in _____________ with his friend, Senthil.
questions.explanation: To 'have little in common with' someone is to share few interests or qualities with them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Dense
questions.explanation: 'Dense' means closely packed; its opposite is 'sparse', thinly scattered. 'Thick' is a synonym.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The fight of the cobra and the mongoose / is a classic drama often seen in India, / and the outcome was largely the same.
options: The fight of the cobra and the mongoose
is a classic drama often seen in India
and the outcome was largely the same
questions.explanation: The sentence states a general truth in the present ('is a classic drama'), so the last part must be in the present too: 'and the outcome is largely the same'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The little child / wrote his name / quick / on the wall.
questions.explanation: A verb is modified by an adverb: 'wrote his name quickly'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Bone to pick
options: To be angry about something and want to discuss it
questions.explanation: To have 'a bone to pick' with someone is to have a complaint that you want to discuss with them.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Health is the most valuable of all earthly possessions. Without it all the rest are worth (1)_________. To enjoy good health we should refrain from excess in eating. We should eat moderately and devour whatever (2)_____ get. When you sit among many for a dinner, do not reach your hand out (3)______ of all. A little food is sufficient for us. Sound sleep comes of a light stomach. Such a man rises (4)______ in the morning and is at ease with himself. So to (5)_____ good health we should eat moderately, for a man who does not overeat enjoys sound sleep and rises early completely refreshed.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: Health is called the most valuable of all possessions, so without it all the rest are worth 'nothing'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Health is the most valuable of all earthly possessions. Without it all the rest are worth (1)_________. To enjoy good health we should refrain from excess in eating. We should eat moderately and devour whatever (2)_____ get. When you sit among many for a dinner, do not reach your hand out (3)______ of all. A little food is sufficient for us. Sound sleep comes of a light stomach. Such a man rises (4)______ in the morning and is at ease with himself. So to (5)_____ good health we should eat moderately, for a man who does not overeat enjoys sound sleep and rises early completely refreshed.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: 'Whatever ___ get' needs a subject pronoun, and the sentence is about 'we': 'We should eat moderately and devour whatever we get.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Health is the most valuable of all earthly possessions. Without it all the rest are worth (1)_________. To enjoy good health we should refrain from excess in eating. We should eat moderately and devour whatever (2)_____ get. When you sit among many for a dinner, do not reach your hand out (3)______ of all. A little food is sufficient for us. Sound sleep comes of a light stomach. Such a man rises (4)______ in the morning and is at ease with himself. So to (5)_____ good health we should eat moderately, for a man who does not overeat enjoys sound sleep and rises early completely refreshed.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: At a shared dinner one should not be the first to reach for the food: 'do not reach your hand out first of all'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Health is the most valuable of all earthly possessions. Without it all the rest are worth (1)_________. To enjoy good health we should refrain from excess in eating. We should eat moderately and devour whatever (2)_____ get. When you sit among many for a dinner, do not reach your hand out (3)______ of all. A little food is sufficient for us. Sound sleep comes of a light stomach. Such a man rises (4)______ in the morning and is at ease with himself. So to (5)_____ good health we should eat moderately, for a man who does not overeat enjoys sound sleep and rises early completely refreshed.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: A man who sleeps soundly on a light stomach 'rises early in the morning', as the last sentence repeats ('rises early completely refreshed').

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Health is the most valuable of all earthly possessions. Without it all the rest are worth (1)_________. To enjoy good health we should refrain from excess in eating. We should eat moderately and devour whatever (2)_____ get. When you sit among many for a dinner, do not reach your hand out (3)______ of all. A little food is sufficient for us. Sound sleep comes of a light stomach. Such a man rises (4)______ in the morning and is at ease with himself. So to (5)_____ good health we should eat moderately, for a man who does not overeat enjoys sound sleep and rises early completely refreshed.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: 'Enjoy good health' is the usual collocation, used earlier in the passage too ('To enjoy good health'); 'benefit' would need 'from'.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: How many countries participated in the FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022?
questions.explanation: Sixteen teams took part in the 2022 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, held in India in October 2022.

questions.text: ‘Wings of Fire’ is the autobiography of a former president of India. Who is he?
questions.explanation: 'Wings of Fire' (1999), written with Arun Tiwari, is the autobiography of A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, President of India from 2002 to 2007.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Statue of Unity situated?
questions.explanation: The Statue of Unity, of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, stands near Kevadia in Narmada district, Gujarat, facing the Sardar Sarovar Dam.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When was the Defence of India Act enacted?
questions.explanation: The Defence of India Act was passed in 1915, during the First World War, giving the government wide emergency powers of detention and trial.

questions.text: Which festival brings out the fusion rich culture of Chhattisgarh and Odisha?
questions.explanation: Bastar Goncha is Bastar's own form of the Rath Yatra, held at Jagdalpur, Chhattisgarh: by tradition it began after a Bastar ruler's pilgrimage to Jagannath at Puri in Odisha, and it joins that worship to Bastar's own customs, such as the salute fired with bamboo 'tupki' guns.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which flag of the Indian National Congress was adopted in 1931?
options: A two colour flag with charkha made by cloth
A tricolour flag made by Khadi with a Charkha symbol
One colour flag with charkha symbol
A blue colour flag made by cloth
questions.explanation: In 1931 the Congress adopted as its flag a tricolour of saffron, white and green with a charkha (spinning wheel) at the centre.

questions.text: Which of the following vitamins prevents major birth defects of the brain and spine of a newborn baby?
questions.explanation: Folic acid (vitamin B9) taken before and early in pregnancy prevents neural tube defects, such as spina bifida and anencephaly, of the baby's brain and spine.

questions.text: In India, the National Sports Day is celebrated on which date?
questions.explanation: National Sports Day is celebrated on 29 August, the birthday of the hockey player Major Dhyan Chand.

questions.text: Which of the following playback singers of India received the Padma Shri in 2009 and Padma Bhushan in 2016?
questions.explanation: The playback singer Udit Narayan received the Padma Shri in 2009 and the Padma Bhushan in 2016.

questions.text: When the ‘trans-boundary economic activities’ of an economy and depreciation are included into account, the aggregate measure is known as ____________.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives GNP: adding the net factor income from abroad (the 'trans-boundary' activities) to GDP gives GNP, which, being a gross measure, still includes depreciation. The wording is loose, since 'taking depreciation into account' could also be read as deducting it, which would give NNP.

questions.text: Tamil Nadu’s _____________ marked a national record in men’s long jump in the second AFI National Jumps Competition in March 2023.
questions.explanation: Jeswin Aldrin of Tamil Nadu jumped 8.42 m at Ballari, Karnataka, in March 2023, a national record, beating Murali Sreeshankar's 8.36 m.

questions.text: Which mountain range from the following is associated with Rajasthan state?
questions.explanation: The Aravalli Range runs across Rajasthan from south-west to north-east; its highest peak, Guru Shikhar, is at Mount Abu. The Satpura lies in Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, and the Sahyadri is the Western Ghats.

questions.text: According to the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021, which state has the lowest percentage of population being multidimensionally poor?
questions.explanation: In NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021 (baseline report), Kerala had the lowest share of multidimensionally poor people, 0.71%.

questions.text: Which of the following represents disposable income?
options: The income earned by individuals and households after taxes and other deductions
The total income earned by businesses and corporations in an economy
The income earned by individuals through their own business or self-employment
The total income earned by individuals and households before taxes and other deductions
questions.explanation: Disposable income is what individuals and households have left to spend or save after paying taxes and other compulsory deductions.

questions.text: Which of the following states receives rainfall during the winter season?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Tamil Nadu: in the cold season the north-east winds pick up moisture over the Bay of Bengal and blow onto its coast, so it gets rain (its north-east monsoon, October to December) while most of India is dry. Western disturbances also bring light winter showers to north-west India, parts of Rajasthan included, but Tamil Nadu is the state known for winter rainfall.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was our first Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first Prime Minister, from 1947 until his death in 1964. Rajendra Prasad was the first President, and Gulzarilal Nanda twice served as interim Prime Minister.

questions.text: Which state is ranked fourth in India according to the first Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021 report of the NITI Aayog?
questions.explanation: In NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021 (baseline report), Madhya Pradesh had the fourth-highest share of multidimensionally poor people, 36.65%, after Bihar (51.91%), Jharkhand (42.16%) and Uttar Pradesh (37.79%).

questions.text: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the division of powers between the Union and the states?
questions.explanation: The Seventh Schedule, read with Article 246, divides powers between the Union and the states through the Union List, the State List and the Concurrent List.

questions.text: Renowned _____________ folk dance artist Domar Singh Kunwar, who has dedicated his life to preserving the tradition of the dance for over five decades, was awarded the Padma Shri 2023.
questions.explanation: Domar Singh Kunwar of Balod district, Chhattisgarh, a Nacha (Natya Nacha) folk theatre artist, received the Padma Shri in 2023. Raut Nacha is a different dance, of the Raut (Yadav) community, and Pandwani is a ballad form telling the Mahabharata.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Beat around the bush
options: To avoid talking about what is important
questions.explanation: To 'beat around the bush' is to avoid coming to the point.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who is kept captive for fulfilment of demands of money or conditions.
questions.explanation: A 'hostage' is a person held captive until demands, such as a ransom, are met.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Peril
questions.explanation: 'Peril' means serious danger.

questions.text: There is a spelling error in the given sentence. Select the option that contains the INCORRECTLY spelt word. As per manager’s opinion, the laser sprinkler malfuntioned.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'malfunctioned'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Amiable
questions.explanation: 'Amiable' means friendly and pleasant; its opposite is 'unfriendly'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. Rahul speaks easily in front of a small group, but he seems ________ before a large audience.
questions.explanation: To be 'ill at ease' is to feel uncomfortable or nervous, as Rahul does before a large audience.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom for the following sentence. He made the business profitable from unprofitable in about a year of joining.
options: Where there is a will, there is a way
questions.explanation: 'Where there is a will, there is a way': determination finds a way to succeed, as in turning a loss-making business round within a year.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains a misspelt word. “Obesity” is “rapidly” becoming the “leading” cause of “prevantable” deaths in the United States.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'preventable'.

questions.text: Identify and correct the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. Sliding each bead from one side to the other, the student used the abacus to count out the nember of days in a week.
questions.explanation: The misspelt word is 'nember', correctly 'number'. 'Beed', 'Slaiding' and 'abacuss' are misspellings of words the sentence spells correctly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement required’. Very early in the morning, at the beginning of January, Opu was lying in bed “waiting for the sun having rose.”
options: waited for the sun having rose
waiting for the sun to rise
questions.explanation: One waits for something 'to' happen: 'waiting for the sun to rise'. 'Having rose' is wrong in any case (rise, rose, risen), and 'waited' does not fit after 'was lying in bed'.

questions.text: Choose the sentence that contains an error.
options: I love the taste of fresh strawberries in the summer.
She is the winner of the Nobel Peace Prize.
He is chef who specialises in Italian cuisine.
The Earth revolves around the Sun.
questions.explanation: 'Chef' is a singular countable noun and needs an article: 'He is a chef who specialises in Italian cuisine.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement required’. Newton, after seeing the apple falling from a tree, “began to wonder whether if” it moved towards the earth and not upwards towards the sky.
questions.explanation: 'Wonder why' asks for the reason, which is what Newton puzzled over; 'whether if' doubles two words that do the same job.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence. They “serve” stuffed garlic bread and molten chocolate in the birthday party of their son, Parth, last week.
questions.explanation: 'Last week' puts the action in the past, so the simple past 'served' is needed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Barbed
questions.explanation: 'Barbed' words are meant to hurt: 'spiteful', as in a barbed remark.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined segment in the given sentence. I can't believe you “let the cat out of the bag” about my surprise party!
questions.explanation: To 'let the cat out of the bag' is to reveal a secret, often by accident, here the surprise party.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Endless period of time
questions.explanation: 'Eternity' is time without end; 'longevity' is long life.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. Sohan is “the” “older” brother “of my” “best” friend.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'elder': traditional usage keeps 'elder' for comparing members of the same family, 'the elder brother'. 'Older brother' is also common and accepted today, so the error is one of textbook usage; 'an', 'to my' and 'good' correct nothing.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. We think “of the past” history of the world “as fixed” but of the future “as undecided” and open to a “wealth off” possibilities.
questions.explanation: 'Off' should be the preposition 'of': 'a wealth of possibilities'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. My teacher told me that / all that / glitters was not gold.
questions.explanation: A proverb or universal truth keeps the present tense even after a past reporting verb: 'all that glitters is not gold'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. “When” I “bought” the book, I “thought” it “will” be interesting.
questions.explanation: After the past 'thought', the future in the past is 'would': 'I thought it would be interesting.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Education should be free to all because it is a (1)__ human right. It is essential for the (2)___ of a fully functioning society and for the advancement of humanity. While some argue that education should not be free because it has value or that free education would be a (3)__ on taxpayers, the reality is that education is a public good that (4)__ everyone in society. Not only does education provide individuals with the skills and knowledge they need to participate in the workforce, but it also improves social cohesion and creates more (5)__ citizens.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'A fundamental human right' is the usual phrase for a basic right owed to everyone, the passage's case for free education.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Education should be free to all because it is a (1)__ human right. It is essential for the (2)___ of a fully functioning society and for the advancement of humanity. While some argue that education should not be free because it has value or that free education would be a (3)__ on taxpayers, the reality is that education is a public good that (4)__ everyone in society. Not only does education provide individuals with the skills and knowledge they need to participate in the workforce, but it also improves social cohesion and creates more (5)__ citizens.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Education is essential for the 'development' of a fully functioning society, its growth into one.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Education should be free to all because it is a (1)__ human right. It is essential for the (2)___ of a fully functioning society and for the advancement of humanity. While some argue that education should not be free because it has value or that free education would be a (3)__ on taxpayers, the reality is that education is a public good that (4)__ everyone in society. Not only does education provide individuals with the skills and knowledge they need to participate in the workforce, but it also improves social cohesion and creates more (5)__ citizens.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: A 'burden on taxpayers' is a cost they must carry, the objection the passage answers.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Education should be free to all because it is a (1)__ human right. It is essential for the (2)___ of a fully functioning society and for the advancement of humanity. While some argue that education should not be free because it has value or that free education would be a (3)__ on taxpayers, the reality is that education is a public good that (4)__ everyone in society. Not only does education provide individuals with the skills and knowledge they need to participate in the workforce, but it also improves social cohesion and creates more (5)__ citizens.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: A public good 'benefits' everyone in society, which is the passage's point; 'burdens' would contradict it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Education should be free to all because it is a (1)__ human right. It is essential for the (2)___ of a fully functioning society and for the advancement of humanity. While some argue that education should not be free because it has value or that free education would be a (3)__ on taxpayers, the reality is that education is a public good that (4)__ everyone in society. Not only does education provide individuals with the skills and knowledge they need to participate in the workforce, but it also improves social cohesion and creates more (5)__ citizens.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Education gives people the skills to work, so it creates more 'productive' citizens.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The Sakraat festival is celebrated with the ‘Budigali’ or ‘Kalasi’ dance in ___________, where women take part in this dance, carrying decorative pots on their heads.
questions.explanation: A Government of India list of tribal dances (PIB, January 2023) gives Budigali, also called Kalasi, as a dance of the Santhal tribe of Odisha, performed at the Sakraat festival.

questions.text: The National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) is a welfare programme being administered by which Ministry of Government of India?
options: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
questions.explanation: The National Social Assistance Programme, launched on 15 August 1995, pays old-age, widow and disability pensions and other social assistance to poor households, and is run by the Ministry of Rural Development.

questions.text: What is the main source of income for commercial banks?
options: Interest earned on loans and advances
questions.explanation: Banks earn mainly the interest on the loans and advances they make, which is more than the interest they pay on deposits.

questions.text: The Taj Mahal was built by:
questions.explanation: The Mughal emperor Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal at Agra as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal. Humayun, Akbar and Jahangir reigned before him.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following made Ganesh Chaturthi popular as a public celebration in Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak turned Ganesh Chaturthi into a public festival in 1893, to bring people together against British rule.

questions.text: Which country’s Constitution was the inspiration behind the Directive Principles of the Indian Constitution?
options: The Constitution of the United States
The Constitution of the United Kingdom
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV) were borrowed from the Irish Constitution of 1937.

questions.text: When one stone is thrown upwards, what type of energy conversion would occur?
options: Kinetic energy would change to mechanical energy
Potential energy would change to gravitational energy
Mechanical energy would change to kinetic energy
Kinetic energy would change to gravitational potential energy
questions.explanation: As the stone rises it slows down: its kinetic energy is changed into gravitational potential energy, which is greatest at the top of its path.

questions.text: Lack of functional small intestine can cause a malabsorption disorder leading to diarrhoea, malnutrition, weight loss etc. This particular condition is known as:
questions.explanation: Short bowel syndrome results when much of the small intestine is missing or does not work, so nutrients are poorly absorbed. Down syndrome is a chromosomal condition, and hypo- and hyperglycaemia mean low and high blood sugar.

questions.text: In December 2022, Government of India launched Grih Pravesh scheme. This scheme aims to provide benefits to the residents of ____ areas.
questions.explanation: The Grih Pravesh programme, which the Prime Minister launched at Agartala, Tripura, in December 2022, covered over two lakh beneficiaries of the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, Urban as well as Rural.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Indian Industrialists reacted against colonial policies that restricted business activities and formed an organisation in 1927. What was it called?
options: Federation of the Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industries (FICCI)
questions.explanation: The Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) was founded in 1927, with G. D. Birla and Purshottamdas Thakurdas among its founders.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who founded the All-India Forward Bloc Party?
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose formed the All India Forward Bloc in 1939, after he resigned as Congress president.

questions.text: The Constitution allows __________ maximum members in Lok Sabha as of June 2023.
questions.explanation: Article 81 allows up to 530 members from the states and 20 from the Union territories: 550. The two seats for nominated Anglo-Indians (Article 331) lapsed in January 2020 under the 104th Amendment.

questions.text: Which of the following novels is based on the partition of India and was written by Khushwant Singh?
questions.explanation: Khushwant Singh's 'Train to Pakistan' (1956) is set in a Punjab border village at Partition. 'The Great Indian Novel' is Shashi Tharoor's and 'Narcopolis' Jeet Thayil's.

questions.text: Which institution mainly provides financial assistance and support to microfinance institutions in India?
options: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
questions.explanation: SIDBI, the principal financial institution for micro, small and medium enterprises, lends to microfinance institutions for on-lending to small borrowers and supports the sector's development.

questions.text: Mango showers are associated with which two states?
questions.explanation: Pre-monsoon showers in Kerala and coastal Karnataka are called mango showers because they help mangoes ripen early.

questions.text: Lachhu Maharaj is a celebrated ________ dancer.
questions.explanation: Lachhu Maharaj, of the Lucknow gharana and brother of Achchan and Shambhu Maharaj, was a Kathak dancer who also choreographed dances for Hindi films. (The Banaras tabla player Pandit Lachhu Maharaj is a different person.)

questions.text: What is the name of the mascot for the 37th National Games?
questions.explanation: Moga, an Indian bison (gaur), was unveiled in June 2023 as the mascot of the 37th National Games, held in Goa in October and November 2023; the name comes from the Konkani word for love.

questions.text: Manika Batra won bronze medal in Asian Cup tournament. She is related to which sport?
questions.explanation: Manika Batra is a table tennis player; her bronze at the 2022 Asian Cup in Bangkok was the first medal won by an Indian woman at the event.

questions.text: What is the name of the geographic feature that serves as a boundary between India and Sri Lanka?
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait separates Tamil Nadu from northern Sri Lanka. The Strait of Gibraltar lies between Spain and Morocco, and the Dardanelles and the Bosporus are in Turkey.

questions.text: FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022 final was held in which city?
questions.explanation: The final of the 2022 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, held in India, was played at the DY Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai on 30 October 2022; Spain beat Colombia 1-0.

questions.text: The Tata Iron and Steel Company Limited (TISCO) was started in the year ________ at Sakchi in Jharkhand state.
questions.explanation: TISCO was registered in 1907 and built its works at Sakchi, the village that grew into Jamshedpur (renamed in 1919).

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. By the time I turn thirty / I would had visited every / continent in the world and have gained / a wealth of knowledge and experience.
options: By the time I turn thirty
a wealth of knowledge and experience
continent in the world and have gained
questions.explanation: A modal takes the base form 'have', and 'by the time I turn thirty' looks ahead, so the future perfect is needed: 'I will have visited every continent'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error. (A) It is a / (B) state of chaos / (C) since the / (D) chairman resigned.
questions.explanation: With 'since' and a point in time the present perfect is needed: 'It has been a state of chaos since the chairman resigned.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. The apple of one’s eye
questions.explanation: 'The apple of one's eye' is the person one loves and cherishes most: very dear.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Harmony
questions.explanation: 'Harmony' is agreement and peace; its opposite is 'conflict'. 'Unity' is close in meaning to it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Pandemics have often been caused by a disease that “spreads by physical touch or contact.”
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'are contagious': a contagious disease is one that spreads by direct contact. (With the singular 'a disease' the verb would be 'is'; every option begins with 'are'.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. The two neighbours will probably stop fighting “when pigs fly”
questions.explanation: 'When pigs fly' means never: something that is impossible.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Her dedication to her work was _______ what anyone had expected.
questions.explanation: 'Beyond' means further than or exceeding: her dedication went beyond what anyone had expected.

questions.text: There is a spelling error in the given sentence. Select the option that contains the INCORRECTLY spelt word. He was in despare because of the expiry of his licence.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'despair'. ('Licence' is the British spelling of the noun.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Demolish
questions.explanation: To 'demolish' is to pull down; its opposite is 'construct'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Tushar is junior than all his colleagues.
questions.explanation: 'Junior', like 'senior', 'superior' and 'inferior', takes 'to', not 'than': 'Tushar is junior to all his colleagues.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Enchanted
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'appealing': 'enchanted' means charmed or delighted, and 'appealing' (attractive, charming) is the nearest option, though strictly it matches 'enchanting'. 'Disgusted' and 'repelling' are nearly opposites, and 'cursed' (doomed, under an evil spell) carries a sense of harm that 'enchanted' does not.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. By the skin of your teeth
options: To be less affected by criticisms and rebuffs
questions.explanation: 'By the skin of one's teeth' means only just, by a very narrow margin.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error. (A) One of / (B) my brothers write / (C) novels for / (D) leisure.
questions.explanation: After 'one of' the subject is 'one', so the verb is singular: 'One of my brothers writes novels for leisure.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Henry is known / as an excellent writer / and good communicator / in English.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'and good communicator': the second noun has its own adjective, and the 'an' before 'excellent' does not suit 'good', so it takes its own article: 'an excellent writer and a good communicator'. (One article before two nouns that describe the same person is also met, so the sentence as printed is not plainly wrong.)

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The arrangement of events or dates in the order of their occurrence
questions.explanation: 'Chronology' is the arrangement of events in the order in which they happened. Theology is the study of religion, entomology of insects and psychology of the mind.

questions.text: Choose the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. As soon as Rohan learned that he had topped the examination, he was “on cloud nine”.
questions.explanation: To be 'on cloud nine' is to be extremely happy.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence. His research on the migratory patterns of the birds is “run-of-the-mill.”
questions.explanation: 'Run-of-the-mill' means ordinary, not special: 'average'.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. The politician “guaranted” that he would create jobs if elected.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'guaranteed'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The old man distributed his property ________ his ten grandchildren equally.
questions.explanation: 'Among' is used for more than two people, 'between' for two: 'among his ten grandchildren'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'indispensable'. 'Conjuror' is an accepted spelling of 'conjurer'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Medical hand practices have been an integral part of healthcare for centuries, but with technological advancements, machines are (1)________ taking over. Robotic surgeries, for instance, have become increasingly popular, allowing surgeons to perform complex (2)________ with minimal invasive techniques. Machine learning and artificial intelligence have transformed medical diagnosis by analysing large amounts of patient data and providing highly detailed medical images. However, there are still challenges to overcome in the use of these technologies in healthcare. For example, the cost of purchasing and maintaining medical machines can be high, and there are concerns around the ethical use of AI in medicine. Nonetheless, it is clear that medical hand practices are (3)________ to machines, and these developments have the potential to revolutionise the healthcare industry. Additionally, the use of telemedicine and remote monitoring devices allows patients to receive medical care from the (4)________ of their homes, particularly beneficial for those in rural or remote areas. Furthermore, medical machines provide healthcare professionals with real-time information, (5) ________ them to make informed decisions and adjust treatment plans accordingly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: 'Gradually' (step by step) fits machines taking over as technology advances; the others do not describe a change over time.

Furthermore, medical machines provide healthcare professionals with real-time information, (5) ________ them to make informed decisions and adjust treatment plans accordingly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: The sentence is about robotic surgery: surgeons perform complex 'procedures', that is, operations. Diagnosis and analysis are not operations, and therapies are given rather than performed by surgeons.
