markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: If the selling price of 16 bulbs is equal to the cost price of 24 bulbs, what is the profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Take the cost of one bulb as ₹1: 16 bulbs cost ₹16 and sell for ₹24, a profit of ₹8 on ₹16, or 8/16 × 100 = 50%.

questions.text: In some quantity of water ,four times the quantity of milk is added and the quantity of the mixture is now 7.5 litres. How much more milk is to be added to the mixture to have 90% milk in the mixture ?
questions.explanation: Water x and milk 4x make 5x = 7.5 litres, so there are 1.5 litres of water and 6 of milk. For 90% milk the 1.5 litres of water must be 10% of the mixture, which must then be 15 litres: 15 − 7.5 = 7.5 litres more milk.

questions.text: What is the purpose of a savings account?
questions.explanation: A savings account is meant for keeping savings safely while they earn interest; the account meant for frequent, day-to-day business transactions is the current account.

questions.text: According to the Census of India 2011, the female literacy rate was recorded as ________.
questions.explanation: The provisional figures of Census 2011, the ones usually cited, put the literacy rate of females (aged seven and above) at 65.46%, against 82.14% for males.

questions.text: Which of the following crops is most suitable for black soil?
questions.explanation: Black soil (regur), which holds moisture well, is so suited to cotton that it is also called black cotton soil. Soybean is grown on it too, but cotton is the crop it is known for.

questions.text: In India, the ‘Aus’, ‘Aman’ and ‘Boro’ terms are associated with which crop from the following?
questions.explanation: Aus, aman and boro are the three rice (paddy) crops of the year in West Bengal and Assam, harvested in autumn, winter and summer respectively.

questions.text: The President of India conferred the Padma Shri award to Gurcharan Singh for his distinguished service in the field of ______________ in 2023.
questions.explanation: Gurcharan Singh, the Delhi cricket coach who trained many Test and first-class cricketers and received the Dronacharya Award in 1987, was given the Padma Shri in 2023.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who moved the resolution proposing that the National Flag of India be a ‘horizontal tricolour of saffron, white and dark green in equal proportion’?
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the resolution on the National Flag in the Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947, and the Assembly adopted it that day.

questions.text: In which of the following States was the first Janjatiya Khel Mahotsav held?
questions.explanation: The first Janjatiya Khel Mahotsav, a national sports festival for tribal athletes, was held at KIIT, Bhubaneswar, Odisha, in June 2023.

questions.text: Identify the Indian singer who sang the song ‘Ae mere watan ke logon jara akhon mein bharlo paani…’ before the first Prime Minister of India, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru.
questions.explanation: Lata Mangeshkar sang Kavi Pradeep's 'Ae Mere Watan Ke Logon', a tribute to the soldiers who died in the 1962 war with China, in Delhi in January 1963 in Nehru's presence.

questions.text: Which regulatory body in India is responsible for overseeing and regulating Micro Finance Institutions?
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
questions.explanation: Microfinance institutions set up as NBFC-MFIs are regulated by the Reserve Bank of India, whose 2022 rules for microfinance loans also cover the banks and other NBFCs that make such loans. SIDBI and NABARD fund and promote microfinance but do not regulate it.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was the viceroy of India at the time of India’s independence from colonial rule on 15 August 1947?
questions.explanation: Lord Mountbatten, who succeeded Lord Wavell in March 1947, was the last Viceroy; at independence he became the first Governor-General of the Dominion of India.

questions.text: Which of the following is the legislative organ of the Union Government?
questions.explanation: Under Article 79 Parliament, made up of the President and the two Houses, is the Union's legislature; the Cabinet belongs to the executive and the Supreme Court to the judiciary.

questions.text: Due to rapid urbanisation, the human lifestyle has changed severely; obesity is a major health issue in such condition. Which of the following is a reason for obesity?
options: Excessive intake of high calorie foods
Lack of vitamins in regular diet
questions.explanation: Obesity results when more energy is taken in than the body uses, so a habit of eating high-calorie foods leads to fat building up in the body.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Where was Shree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam founded?
questions.explanation: The Sree Narayana Dharma Paripalana (SNDP) Yogam was founded in Kerala in 1903, with Sree Narayana Guru as its president, to work for the social uplift of the Ezhava community.

questions.text: Who is the renowned kathak dancer, student of ‘Pandit Birju Maharaj’ and also served as an officer with Indian Audit and Accounts Services?
questions.explanation: Shovana Narayan, a Kathak dancer trained by Pandit Birju Maharaj, also had a career as an officer of the Indian Audit and Accounts Service.

questions.text: Which of the following Indus Valley sites is now located in Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Harappa, on the Ravi, is in Punjab province, Pakistan. Lothal is in Gujarat, Kalibangan in Rajasthan and Alamgirpur in Uttar Pradesh.

questions.text: In April 2023,Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty made history, becoming the first Indian men’s doubles pair to win a gold medal at the Badminton Asia Championships. Where was this championship held?
questions.explanation: Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty won the men's doubles title at the 2023 Badminton Asia Championships in Dubai on 30 April 2023.

questions.text: Which of the following states has introduced a dedicated Semiconductor Policy 2022-27 with a view to generate at least 2,00,000 new employment opportunities in the state?
questions.explanation: Gujarat, the first state with a dedicated semiconductor policy, announced its Semiconductor Policy 2022-27 in July 2022, aiming at 2,00,000 new jobs over five years.

questions.text: The classical dance style of Bharatanatyam belongs to the state of ____________.
questions.explanation: Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: Which of the following peninsular rivers of India is a west flowing river?
questions.explanation: The Narmada flows west through a rift valley into the Arabian Sea; the Kaveri, Godavari and Krishna flow east into the Bay of Bengal.

questions.text: Which Articles of the Constitution of India deal with the Union and its territory?
questions.explanation: Part I of the Constitution, Articles 1-4, deals with the Union and its territory. Articles 5-11 deal with citizenship, 12-35 with Fundamental Rights and 36-51 with the Directive Principles.

questions.text: ‘The Great Indian Novel’ is a satirical novel by ______.
questions.explanation: Shashi Tharoor's 'The Great Indian Novel' (1989) retells the Mahabharata as the story of India's freedom movement and its aftermath.

questions.text: What is the systematic name of a colourless gas with a faint, ethereal odour called acetylene, widely used for welding?
questions.explanation: Acetylene, C₂H₂, is the simplest alkyne, and its systematic (IUPAC) name is ethyne; it burns with oxygen in the oxy-acetylene torch used for welding.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error. (A) Taylor, Richard, and / (B) Francis plays for / (C) the state / (D) basketball team.
questions.explanation: Subjects joined by 'and' take a plural verb: 'Taylor, Richard, and Francis play for the state basketball team.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Pay an arm and a leg for something
options: Pay a lot of money for something
Give a lot of love and care to someone
Pay a lot of attention to an incident
questions.explanation: To 'pay an arm and a leg' for something is to pay a very high price for it.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. As they driven through the dark, twisting lane / down which they had walked earlier, Lucius heard / the whistling of the night air in his ears.
options: down which they had walked earlier, Lucius heard
the whistling of the night air in his ears.
As they driven through the dark, twisting lane
questions.explanation: 'Driven' is a past participle and cannot stand alone as the verb; the simple past is needed: 'As they drove through the dark, twisting lane'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Trivial
questions.explanation: 'Trivial' means of little importance: 'minor'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Ministry of education has announced that students can ________ the Board Examinations twice.
questions.explanation: In standard English a candidate 'takes' (or sits) an examination and the examiner 'gives' it; 'participate' would need 'in'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. A man of character, he “stuck to his guns” even in the most difficult situations.
options: To do things that would please people
To stand firm against all difficulties and challenges
questions.explanation: To 'stick to one's guns' is to hold firmly to one's position in spite of opposition or difficulty.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined segment in the given sentence. After her husband passed away, Jane had to learn “to bite the bullet” and take care of the household on her own.
options: Run away from a difficult situation
questions.explanation: To 'bite the bullet' is to face something difficult or unpleasant with courage.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase. One who lends money to others at a very high rate of interest.
questions.explanation: A 'usurer' lends money at very high interest. A curator looks after a museum's collection and a numismatist studies or collects coins.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The platinum is a precious metal.
questions.explanation: The name of a metal used in a general sense takes no article: 'Platinum is a precious metal.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. All praised him when he soared in the business world, but the same people ______ him when he failed in business.
questions.explanation: 'But' sets the failure against the praise, so the same people 'criticised' him.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. What “most off” us “want most” “is to” “move forward”.
questions.explanation: The preposition 'of' is needed, not 'off': 'What most of us want most is to move forward.'

questions.text: Select the word which means the same as the group of words given. That which can’t be read.
questions.explanation: Writing that cannot be read is 'illegible'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'acknowledge'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Authentic
questions.explanation: 'Authentic' means genuine or real; its opposite is 'false'. 'Actual' is close in meaning to it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. Please tell me about the meeting ________.
questions.explanation: 'In a nutshell' means briefly, in a few words. 'In a stew' and 'in a spin' mean worried or confused, and 'in a huff' annoyed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Augmented Reality (AR) continues to develop and become more _________ among a wide range of applications.
questions.explanation: 'Pervasive' means spreading widely through something, as AR is spreading through more and more applications.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. The handloom shop at the Ring Road has many kinds of bags, such as paper, leather, cloth and cannvas.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'canvas'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. A/An ________ fellow cannot become an ideal teacher.
questions.explanation: An 'idle' (lazy) person cannot become an ideal teacher; the other options are qualities a good teacher has.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. I considered Geography as “an easier” subject.
questions.explanation: Nothing is compared with Geography, so the positive degree is needed, not the comparative: 'an easy subject'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The most common hazard in forests is forest fire. Forest fires are as old as the forests themselves. They pose a 1.________ not only to the forest wealth but also to the entire regime to fauna and flora seriously disturbing the biodiversity and the ecology and environment of a region. During summer, when there is no rain for months, the forests 2.________ littered with dry senescent leaves and twinges, which could burst into flames ignited by the slightest spark. The Himalayan forests, particularly, Garhwal Himalayas have been burning 3.________ during the last few summers, with colossal loss of vegetation cover of that region. The youngest mountain ranges of the Himalayas are the most 4.________ stretches of the world susceptible to forest fires. The forests of the Western are more 5.________ vulnerable to forest fires as compared to those in the Eastern Himalayas. This is because forests of the Eastern Himalayas grow in high rain density.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.1.
questions.explanation: Fires 'pose a threat' to the forest wealth: they put it in danger.

The forests of the Western are more 5.________ vulnerable to forest fires as compared to those in the Eastern Himalayas. This is because forests of the Eastern Himalayas grow in high rain density.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no.2.
questions.explanation: With no rain for months, the forests 'become' littered with dry leaves and twigs: the verb shows a change of state.

questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'regularly': 'during the last few summers' points to fires that have come back summer after summer. 'Badly' would describe how fierce the fires were, but 'burning badly' is not a natural way to say that of a forest.

questions.explanation: 'Vulnerable' means open to harm, which matches 'susceptible to forest fires': the young Himalayan ranges are among the most vulnerable stretches.

questions.explanation: Fires break out more often in the western forests than in the eastern ones, which get more rain, so they are 'more frequently' vulnerable.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: ₹8,000 becomes ₹9,800 in three years at simple interest rate. If the rate of interest becomes two times of itself, then what will be the amount of the same principle in four years?
By investing ₹12,000 in a scheme, R gets ₹15,500 back in return. What is his percentage of profit?
Who propounded the concept of ‘Rule of Law’?
questions.explanation: A. V. Dicey set out the 'rule of law' in 'Introduction to the Study of the Law of the Constitution' (1885): no one is above the law, and everyone is subject to the ordinary courts.

questions.text: In which state is Vijay Stambh situated?
questions.explanation: The Vijay Stambh (Tower of Victory) in Chittorgarh Fort, Rajasthan, was built by Rana Kumbha of Mewar in the 15th century to mark his victory over Mahmud Khalji of Malwa.

questions.text: Which state passed a bill for the protection of advocates and became the first state to do so?
questions.explanation: The Rajasthan Assembly passed the Rajasthan Advocates Protection Bill in March 2023, making Rajasthan the first state to pass such a measure, to protect lawyers from assault and intimidation linked to their work.

questions.text: Chaoite, Buckminsterfullerene and Graphene are related to which element?
questions.explanation: Chaoite, buckminsterfullerene (C₆₀) and graphene are allotropes of carbon, as are diamond and graphite.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who is credited with the establishment of Servants of India Society?
questions.explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in Pune in 1905 to train Indians for the service of the country.

questions.text: The value of all final goods and services produced within the country during one year is known as __________.
questions.explanation: GDP is the value of all final goods and services produced within a country's territory in a year. GNP adds net factor income from abroad, and the 'net' measures deduct depreciation.

questions.text: Who was the first speaker of the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: G. V. Mavalankar was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha, from 1952 to 1956; M. Ananthasayanam Ayyangar, its first Deputy Speaker, succeeded him.

questions.text: The technique of classical dancing was codified by ______________ in about the 5th century B.C.
questions.explanation: Bharata Muni's Natyashastra, the oldest surviving Indian treatise on drama, dance and music, set down the technique of classical dance.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the novel ‘Animal Farm’?
questions.explanation: 'Animal Farm' (1945), a political fable about a revolution among farm animals, is by George Orwell.

questions.text: According to the Census of India 2011, which of the following states has the lowest population?
questions.explanation: Sikkim, with about 6.1 lakh people, was the least populous state in the 2011 Census; Mizoram, Goa and Manipur each had more than 10 lakh.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following years was the Child Marriage Restraint Act passed?
questions.explanation: The Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929, called the Sarda Act after Harbilas Sarda, who moved it, fixed the minimum age of marriage at 14 for girls and 18 for boys.

questions.text: What is the main reason behind the substantial rainfall during summer on the western coasts of India?
questions.explanation: The moist southwest monsoon winds from the Arabian Sea are forced to rise over the Western Ghats, where they cool and shed heavy orographic rain on the windward western coast.

questions.text: The second edition of Khelo India Youth Games, 2019 was organised in which city?
questions.explanation: The second Khelo India Youth Games were held in Pune, Maharashtra, in January 2019; the first edition, held in New Delhi in 2018, was called the Khelo India School Games.

questions.text: ACF conferred Grandmaster ________ with Player of the Year award, who is only the sixth Indian to break the 2700 Elo-rating mark and the youngest Grandmaster from the country to be rated above 2700.
questions.explanation: D. Gukesh, who crossed 2700 Elo in 2022, received the Asian Chess Federation's Player of the Year award in March 2023 for his 2022 season.

questions.text: Which condition causes bone pain, poor growth, and soft, weak bones that can lead to bone deformities?
questions.explanation: Rickets, usually caused by a lack of vitamin D (or of calcium or phosphate) in childhood, softens and weakens growing bones, leading to pain, poor growth and deformities such as bowed legs.

questions.text: In which Indian musician’s name did the state of Massachusetts in the USA declare April 20th in 1984 as a day in his name?
questions.explanation: In 1984 the US state of Massachusetts proclaimed 20 April Amjad Ali Khan Day in honour of the sarod maestro.

questions.text: Which of the following is an advantage of microfinance institutions in India?
options: Increased reliance on informal lending sources
questions.explanation: Microfinance institutions give small loans and other financial services to low-income households, many of them led by women, who have little access to banks, so they widen financial inclusion. The other options are drawbacks, not advantages.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following statements about Mahatma Gandhi is INCORRECT?
options: Mahatma Gandhi was born in 1869 in Porbandar.
In 1942, he launched the Quit India Movement.
He led the Champaran Satyagraha in 1910.
He led the Dandi Salt March in 1930.
questions.explanation: Gandhi led the Champaran Satyagraha, his first in India, in 1917, not 1910; in 1910 he was still in South Africa. The other three statements are correct.

questions.text: Which university won the first place in the 3rd Khelo India University Games?
questions.explanation: Panjab University, Chandigarh, was the overall champion of the third Khelo India University Games, held in Uttar Pradesh in May-June 2023.

questions.text: In which of the following states of India is the maximum extent of alluvial soil found?
questions.explanation: Alluvial soil covers the whole Ganga plain, so Uttar Pradesh has by far the largest extent of it among the options; Telangana, Karnataka and Maharashtra lie mostly on the Deccan, with black and red soils.

questions.text: The ________ port was developed after Independence to ease the volume of trade on the Mumbai port.
questions.explanation: Kandla, in Kachchh, Gujarat, was the first port developed after Independence, to ease the load on Mumbai after Karachi went to Pakistan at Partition. It has since been renamed Deendayal Port.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'curiosity', without the 'u' of 'curious'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. Riddhi believes in “wearing her heart on her sleeve”. That is why she has so many friends.
options: To wear a badge of honour
To openly and freely express one’s emotions
questions.explanation: To 'wear one's heart on one's sleeve' is to show one's feelings openly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To cross swords
questions.explanation: To 'cross swords' with someone is to fight or argue with them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Virtual worlds are recently new phenomena in that they _________ people to meet and socially interact with others in a variety of online environments.
questions.explanation: To 'enable' people to meet is to make it possible for them, which is what online virtual worlds do; 'forbid' says the opposite, and 'bring' and 'choose' do not give this sense.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. I have seen / a movie / on schooling / yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' names a finished past time, which takes the simple past, not the present perfect: 'I saw a movie on schooling yesterday.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Cheap
questions.explanation: 'Cheap' means low in price; its opposite is 'expensive'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Kavya invited all her friends, “isn’t it?”
questions.explanation: A positive statement in the simple past takes a negative tag with 'did' and the subject's pronoun: 'Kavya invited all her friends, didn't she?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. The deal was ________ for three months.
questions.explanation: To 'put something on ice' is to postpone or suspend it: the deal was put on hold for three months.

questions.text: The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. This is the eldest standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
options: This is the more older standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
This is the most old standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
This is the more elder standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
This is the oldest standing structure of Chola architecture in India.
questions.explanation: 'Eldest' is used only of people, mainly within a family; for a building the superlative is 'oldest'. 'More older', 'most old' and 'more elder' are wrong forms.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. They decided to / travel in train / instead of driving / to New Delhi.
questions.explanation: A means of transport takes 'by' without an article: 'travel by train'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Strengthen
questions.explanation: To 'strengthen' is to make stronger; to 'debilitate' is to weaken. 'Fortify' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Fame
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'shame', disgrace, as the opposite of 'fame', a good name and renown. 'Scandal' also suggests disgrace, but it names the event or talk that causes it, so 'shame' is the closer opposite.

questions.text: Select the sentence that has NO spelling errors.
options: My new phone has a high-resolusion screen and powerful proccessor, which makes it perfect for streming videos and playing games.
My new phone has a high-resollution screen and a powerfull procesor, which makes it perfect for streaming videos and playing games.
My new phone has a high-resolution screen and a powerful processor, which makes it perfect for streaming videos and playing games.
My new phone has a high-resolution screan and powerfull procesor, which makes it perfect for streming videos and playing games.
questions.explanation: Only this sentence spells every word correctly; the others misspell 'resolution', 'screen', 'powerful', 'processor' or 'streaming'.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence. Being a doktor, my sister Meera is prepared for an emergency usually.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'doctor'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. I suppose dancing that well would require a lot of “actual application”.
questions.explanation: 'Practice' is the actual doing or application of something, as against theory, and the repeated exercise that builds skill.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. A music / is a great way / to express / your emotions.
questions.explanation: 'Music' is an uncountable noun and takes no 'a': 'Music is a great way to express your emotions.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. You are an intellectual with a professional degree; you can do wonders as _____________.
questions.explanation: 'The world is your oyster' means you are free and able to achieve whatever you want, which fits a gifted person with a professional degree.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Rashmi works at the hospital, “don’t she?”
questions.explanation: A positive statement in the simple present with a singular subject takes 'doesn't' in the tag: 'Rashmi works at the hospital, doesn't she?'

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Radha will have learnt cooking by the time she will have married.
questions.explanation: A time clause with 'by the time' takes the simple present for a future event, not 'will': 'by the time she gets married'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Fear of closed spaces
questions.explanation: 'Claustrophobia' is the fear of closed spaces; xenophobia is fear of foreigners, hydrophobia of water and zoophobia of animals.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. A cashless India is the first step towards making the dream of digital India a reality. Government is trying to (1)____________ a cashless environment in the country. Demonetisation appears to be a stepping (2)___________ in that direction. To help facilitate this, government even (3)_____________ its own app ‘BHIM’ built for the same purpose. The (4)___________ of conducting online financial transactions is probably the biggest motivator to go digital. You will no longer need to carry wads of cash, plastic cards or even queue up for ATM withdrawals. It’s also safer and easier spending option when you are travelling. Making transactions digitally makes it easy to keep track of your finances. The (5)___________ are enormous for everyone if you leave out the low-income group, which will face a huge challenge. For the rest of the country, it is constructive and simple. However, the convenience of net-banking, m-banking, card or mobile wallet transactions can make you spend more than your budget.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. 1.
questions.explanation: The government is trying to 'create', bring into being, a cashless environment.

questions.explanation: A 'stepping stone' is a step towards a goal: demonetisation as a stepping stone towards a cashless India.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: By selling a cycle for ₹5,800, a man gains 45%. What will be the cost price of the cycle?

Seven people, V, F, D, S, R, C, and P are sitting in a straight line, facing south. Only two people sit between V and P. Only two people sit to the right of V. D sits third to the left of S. P is an immediate neighbour of D and F. C is an immediate neighbour of S. Total how many people sit between S and P?
questions.explanation: Number the seats 1 to 7 from the right end of the row (the people face south). Only two sit to V's right, so V is 3rd; two people between V and P put P 6th, and D and F, its neighbours, in 5th and 7th; D third to the left of S puts S in 2nd (D in 7th would put S in 4th, between V and F, leaving no seat for C beside S), so C is 1st and R 4th. V, R and D sit between S and P: three people.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year did the ‘Battle of Buxar’ take place?
questions.explanation: At Buxar in October 1764 the East India Company's army under Hector Munro defeated the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II. Plassey was fought in 1757 and the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761.

questions.text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mandates that the state should protect every monument or place of artistic or historic interest?
questions.explanation: Article 49, a Directive Principle, obliges the State to protect every monument or place or object of artistic or historic interest declared by or under a law made by Parliament to be of national importance. Article 39A provides for free legal aid, 48A for the environment and 50 for separating the judiciary from the executive.

questions.text: To mark the celebration of Gandhi Jayanti, the _____________ celebrates it as International Day of Non-Violence.
options: South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation
questions.explanation: In June 2007 the UN General Assembly declared 2 October, Gandhi's birthday, the International Day of Non-Violence.

questions.text: Alarmel Valli is a __________ dancer.
questions.explanation: Alarmel Valli, of Chennai, is one of India's leading Bharatanatyam dancers, of the Pandanallur style.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a microfinance institution (MFI) in India?
questions.explanation: Bandhan began at Konnagar, near Kolkata, in 2001 as a microfinance lender and grew into one of India's largest microfinance institutions before it became Bandhan Bank, a universal bank, in 2015. SBI, ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank are mainstream commercial banks.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following is an autobiography by Mahatma Gandhi?
options: The Story of My Experiments with Truth
questions.explanation: Gandhi's autobiography, 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth', was written in Gujarati and serialised in Navajivan from 1925 to 1929. 'My Truth' is Indira Gandhi's, 'Matters of Discretion' I. K. Gujral's and 'My Country My Life' L. K. Advani's.

questions.text: Which of the following has initiated the Village Defence Guards scheme to instil a sense of self protection and ensure the safety and security of villages and infrastructural installations in and around the villages?
questions.explanation: Under the Village Defence Guards scheme, approved by the Union Home Ministry in 2022 and in force in Jammu and Kashmir from August 2022, groups of armed civilian volunteers guard border and remote villages; it replaced the Village Defence Committees of the 1990s.

questions.text: The Sirpur Shrine is situated in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Sirpur, on the Mahanadi in Mahasamund district of Chhattisgarh, is known for the 7th-century brick Lakshmana temple and the remains of Buddhist monasteries.

questions.text: What is the common name for a saturated solution of calcium hydroxide widely used as a raw material in the chemical industry?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives slaked lime, the common name of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂; strictly, its clear saturated solution in water is called limewater. Calomel is mercury(I) chloride, burnt lime (quicklime) is calcium oxide and limestone is calcium carbonate.

questions.text: Who among the following singers is from Andhra Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The playback singer S. Janaki was born in 1938 at Pallapatla in Guntur district, Andhra Pradesh. Usha Uthup was born in Bombay, Asha Bhosle in Sangli (Maharashtra) and Alka Yagnik in Calcutta.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who led the Congress in the second round table conference held in London?
questions.explanation: After the Gandhi-Irwin Pact the Congress took part in the Second Round Table Conference in London (September-December 1931), with Gandhi as its sole representative.

questions.text: According to the Census of India 2011, which state has the second highest sex ratio?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Kerala had the highest sex ratio among the states, 1,084 females per 1,000 males, and Tamil Nadu the second highest, 996.

questions.text: Factor cost is also known as:
questions.explanation: Factor cost is what is paid to the factors of production, the inputs land, labour, capital and enterprise (rent, wages, interest and profit), hence 'input cost'. Unlike market price it leaves out indirect taxes and includes subsidies.

questions.text: Which cell found in the bone marrow acts as a repair system for the body?
questions.explanation: Bone marrow holds stem cells, unspecialised cells that keep dividing and can turn into blood cells and other kinds of cell, replacing worn-out or damaged ones.

questions.text: Which of the following is a famous folk dance of Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Kalbelia, the dance of Rajasthan's Kalbelia snake-charmer community, was inscribed on UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage list in 2010. Chang Lo is a dance of Nagaland, and Daskathia and Pala are performance forms of Odisha.

questions.text: When was the first general election for Lok Sabha held in India?
questions.explanation: India's first general election, to the first Lok Sabha, was held from October 1951 to February 1952.

questions.text: Who among the following female singers has been felicitated with the Bharat Ratna?
questions.explanation: Lata Mangeshkar received the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award, in 2001.

questions.text: Which of the following states of India is the first to receive rainfall from the South West Monsoon?
questions.explanation: The southwest monsoon normally sets in over Kerala around 1 June, its first landfall on the mainland, and then advances northwards.

questions.text: India played in the finals of the 2023 World Test Championship against Australia. Where was this match conducted?
questions.explanation: The 2023 World Test Championship final was played at The Oval, London, in June 2023; Australia beat India by 209 runs.

questions.text: D Gukesh was awarded player of the year award in March 2023. He plays which sport?
questions.explanation: D. Gukesh of Chennai is a chess grandmaster; the Asian Chess Federation named him its Player of the Year in March 2023, after his gold medal on the top board at the 2022 Chess Olympiad.

questions.text: According to the Ministry of Textile 2022-23, which state is the second largest producer of cotton?
questions.explanation: In the Textiles Ministry's provisional estimates for 2022-23 Gujarat produced the most cotton, about 92 lakh bales, and Maharashtra came second with about 80 lakh bales.

questions.text: In which of the following States was the final of the 2023 Intercontinental Cup football championship held?
questions.explanation: The 2023 Intercontinental Cup was played at the Kalinga Stadium, Bhubaneswar, in June 2023; India beat Lebanon 2-0 in the final.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'necessary'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A small shop that sells fashionable clothes
questions.explanation: A 'boutique' is a small shop selling fashionable clothes; 'couture' is the designing and making of such clothes, not a shop.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. The blue is a beautiful colour.
questions.explanation: A colour named in a general sense takes no article: 'Blue is a beautiful colour.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The Nile is the ________ river of the world.
questions.explanation: Comparing the Nile with all the world's rivers needs the superlative 'the longest'; 'more longer' is a double comparative.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Tuntun and her friends dance beautiful.
questions.explanation: 'Dance' is a verb and is modified by an adverb: 'dance beautifully'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. It’s risky to invest all your savings in one company; it’s like _______________.
options: putting all your eggs in one basket
questions.explanation: To 'put all your eggs in one basket' is to risk everything on a single venture.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. Sometimes we have to accept “replacing something with something else”, if we want to move forward.
questions.explanation: Replacing something with something else is a 'change': we sometimes have to accept change to move forward.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Dishevelled
questions.explanation: 'Dishevelled' means untidy, of hair, clothes or appearance; its opposite is 'tidy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I ___________ to many countries to find the source of true happiness.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'travelled' (British usage doubles the final 'l'; American English has 'traveled').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. Irrespective of the chaos in the classroom, our class teacher stays “cool as a cucumber”.
options: Scolds all the students in the classroom
questions.explanation: 'Cool as a cucumber' means calm and composed, even under pressure.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Hazard
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'accident': 'hazard' can mean chance or mishap, as in 'by hazard', and none of the other options is related. In everyday use, though, 'hazard' means a danger or risk, so 'accident' is only a loose synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He is a smug and very ______ person who thinks only about himself.
questions.explanation: An 'egoistic' person thinks only of himself, which fits 'smug'; 'diffident' (shy) and 'humble' are near opposites, and an 'arsonist' sets fires.

questions.text: Select the word segment which substitutes the bracketed word correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. I (am here) since 1981.
questions.explanation: A state lasting from a point in the past up to now, with 'since', takes the present perfect, and 'I' takes 'have': 'I have been here since 1981.'

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. You shall repented tomorrow for your misdeeds.
questions.explanation: A modal such as 'shall' takes the base form of the verb: 'You shall repent tomorrow'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. She “think” Alex is abandoning her.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'She' takes 'thinks' in the simple present, which also matches 'is abandoning'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate segment that can substitute the bracketed word in the following sentence. The bridge that (connecting) the two valleys across the Brahmaputra river has recently been constructed in Arunachal Pradesh.
questions.explanation: The relative clause needs a finite verb, and the bridge, now built, joins the valleys: 'that connects'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. Naina has six children, and I always ________ with their names.
questions.explanation: To 'get mixed up' is to confuse one thing with another, here the six children's names.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. When it comes to planning her wedding, Maria wants ________________.
questions.explanation: 'The whole nine yards' means everything possible, every last detail.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I know that I can count on my best friend to be by my side through ____ and thin.
questions.explanation: 'Through thick and thin' means in good times and bad.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. I do not know how the party ended. I do not want to know. I went (1)___ upstairs, and undressed and (2)___ into bed, and lay there in the burning dark while the last guest gurgled in the hall below about the wonderful evening she had spent. I lay there (3)___ the front door shut after her, and Lavinia’s steps came up the stairs and passed the door to the guest room beyond. And then after a couple of centuries (4)___, the clock struck three and I (5)___ to sleep.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: To go 'straight upstairs' is to go directly, without stopping.

questions.explanation: 'Crawled into bed' is the usual phrase for getting wearily into bed; one does not 'gnaw' or 'peep' into bed.

And then after a couple of centuries (4)___, the clock struck three and I (5)___ to sleep.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. I do not know how the party ended. I do not want to know. I went (1)___ upstairs, and undressed and (2)___ into bed, and lay there in the burning dark while the last guest gurgled in the hall below about the wonderful evening she had spent. I lay there (3)___ the front door shut after her, and Lavinia’s steps came up the stairs and passed the door to the guest room beyond. And then after a couple of centuries (4)___, the clock struck three and I (5)___ to sleep.
