questions.explanation: To 'doze off' is to fall asleep; 'call off' means to cancel, 'take off' to leave the ground and 'put off' to postpone.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The cost price of an item is ₹4,850. What is the profit percentage (rounded off to 1 decimal place) if it is sold at ₹6,680?

Seven people, U, M, K, G, B, R and D are sitting in a straight line, facing south. Only two people sit to the left of B. M sits third to the right of G. U is the immediate neighbour of M and B. D sits to the immediate left of K. Total how many people sit between D and G?
questions.explanation: Counting from the people's own left end: only two sit to B's left, so B is third. U sits between M and B, so U is fourth and M fifth (M cannot be first, with G three places to its left), and G is second. D and K take sixth and seventh, and R the first seat: R, G, B, U, M, D, K. B, U and M sit between G and D: three.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which Indian Mass Movement began with the famous ‘Dandi March’ of Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.explanation: Gandhi's march from Sabarmati to Dandi in March-April 1930, which ended in his breaking the salt law, launched the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.text: The length of the men's kabaddi court is _____ metres.
questions.explanation: A men's kabaddi court measures 13 m by 10 m; the women's court is 12 m by 8 m.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a Directive Principle based on the ideals of Mahatma Gandhi?
options: To promote industrialisation in urban areas
To prohibit intoxicating drinks and drugs that are injurious to health
To promote cottage industries in rural areas
questions.explanation: The Gandhian Directive Principles include organising village panchayats (Article 40), promoting cottage industries in rural areas (Article 43) and prohibiting intoxicating drinks and drugs injurious to health (Article 47). Promoting industrialisation in urban areas is not among them.

questions.text: Which of the following methods is used to calculate national income by summing up the total incomes earned by individuals and businesses in an economy?
questions.explanation: The income method adds up the factor incomes earned in the economy: wages, rent, interest and profits, with the mixed income of the self-employed.

questions.text: What is personal income?
options: The income earned by individuals and households after taxes and other deductions
The total income earned by businesses and corporations in an economy
The income earned by individuals through their own business or self-employment
The total income earned by individuals and households before taxes and other deductions
questions.explanation: Personal income is the income households actually receive from all sources, transfer payments included, before personal taxes are paid; what is left after those taxes is personal disposable income.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who founded the Hindu reform organisation Brahmo Samaj?
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha in Calcutta in 1828; it came to be known as the Brahmo Samaj.

questions.text: Whom among the following Indian singers is known as ‘Gazal King’?
questions.explanation: Jagjit Singh, who took the ghazal to a wide popular audience, is known as the 'Ghazal King'.

questions.text: Dree Utsav is celebrated in the state of ____________.
questions.explanation: Dree is the agricultural festival of the Apatani people of the Ziro valley in Arunachal Pradesh, held every July with prayers for a good harvest.

questions.text: ___________ word of Indian dance is derived from a Sanskrit word and literally means ‘taking towards’.
questions.explanation: 'Abhinaya' comes from the Sanskrit 'abhi' (towards) and 'ni' (to carry or lead): expression that carries the meaning of the dance to the audience.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of the Western Coast Port?
questions.explanation: Mumbai Port is on India's west coast, in Maharashtra; Tuticorin, Paradip and Visakhapatnam are ports on the east coast.

questions.text: What are the three tiers of the Government in India?
options: Union government, Judiciary government and Federal government
Union government, State Government and Federal Government
Union government, State government and Judiciary government
Union Government, State Government and Local Government
questions.explanation: India is governed at three levels: the Union government, the state governments and local government (panchayats and municipalities, given constitutional status by the 73rd and 74th Amendments of 1992).

questions.text: The foundation of Sanchi Stupa was laid by which of the following Kings?
questions.explanation: The Great Stupa at Sanchi was first built by Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE as a brick mound over relics of the Buddha; it was later enlarged and faced with stone.

questions.text: During which months do retreating monsoons occur in India?
questions.explanation: The south-west monsoon withdraws from northern India during October and November, the season of the retreating monsoon.

questions.text: Which is the primary structural component responsible for most of the mechanical strength of the cell wall?
questions.explanation: Cellulose fibres give the plant cell wall most of its strength. Chitin strengthens the cell walls of fungi, glycogen is an animal storage carbohydrate and heparin an anticoagulant.

questions.text: Ball and spring model of chemical bonds obey:
questions.explanation: In the ball-and-spring model the atoms are balls joined by springs, and a stretched or compressed bond pulls back with a force proportional to its change in length, as Hooke's law states.

questions.text: Pandit Janki Prasad was associated with which of the following Gharanas of Kathak?
questions.explanation: Pandit Janki Prasad is regarded as the founder of the Banaras gharana of Kathak.

questions.text: In 2023, Ajay Singh, the chief of SpiceJet was appointed as president of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Ajay Singh, chairman and managing director of SpiceJet, took over as president of ASSOCHAM (the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry of India) in March 2023, succeeding Sumant Sinha.

questions.text: Rohit Sharma became the first ever Indian to play how many T20 cricket matches in October 2022?
questions.explanation: In the second T20I against South Africa at Guwahati on 2 October 2022, Rohit Sharma became the first Indian to play 400 T20 matches, counting internationals, the IPL and domestic games together.

questions.text: Which form of Indian dance is said to be ‘soft and suitable for female presentation’?
questions.explanation: Laasya is the soft, graceful side of dance, associated with Parvati and suited to female presentation; Taandava, Shiva's dance, is its vigorous counterpart.

questions.text: Which of the following oceans is surrounded by the continent of North America and South America to the east?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean has Asia and Australia to its west and North and South America to its east.

questions.text: The famous ‘Pashupatinath Temple’ is located in which country from the following?
questions.explanation: The Pashupatinath Temple, dedicated to Shiva, stands on the banks of the Bagmati in Kathmandu, Nepal.

questions.text: In which of the following years was the first Janjatiya Khel Mahotsav held?
questions.explanation: The first Janjatiya Khel Mahotsav, a national sports festival for tribal athletes, was held at KIIT, Bhubaneswar, in June 2023.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who does not believe in the existence of God
questions.explanation: An 'atheist' does not believe that God exists; a believer does, and a priest and a monk are religious figures.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’. You are the “beautiful” woman I have ever seen.
questions.explanation: A comparison with everyone 'I have ever seen' needs the superlative: 'You are the most beautiful woman I have ever seen.'

questions.text: Choose the option which best expresses the meaning of the given idiom. By fair means or foul
options: To find difficulty in completing some work
To get one’s way with honesty or dishonesty
questions.explanation: 'By fair means or foul' means by any method at all, honest or dishonest.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. My younger daughter, / Kanu prefer / dark chocolate / to yoghurt.
questions.explanation: The subject 'Kanu' (my younger daughter) is singular and takes a singular verb: 'Kanu prefers dark chocolate to yoghurt.'

questions.text: Choose the sentence that contains an error.
options: I saw a movie that was directed by Steven Spielberg.
She is the only person who can solve this difficult math problem.
He is an lawyer who works for a prestigious law firm.
The Great Wall of China is a popular tourist attraction.
questions.explanation: 'Lawyer' begins with a consonant sound, so it takes 'a': 'He is a lawyer who works for a prestigious law firm.'

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Ishita will playing Tennis for her favourite team.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'will playing': the modal 'will' is followed by the bare infinitive, 'Ishita will play (or will be playing) tennis for her favourite team.' The capital in 'Tennis' is also non-standard, but that is a slip of capitalisation, not of grammar.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. He “apologised in her” silently before he pushed deeper into her thoughts.
questions.explanation: One apologises 'to' a person (and 'for' a fault): 'He apologised to her silently'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct (British) spelling is 'behaviour'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Obvious
questions.explanation: 'Obvious' means easy to see or understand: 'clear'. 'Murky', 'ambiguous' and 'opaque' are nearly its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. As phony as a three-dollar bill
questions.explanation: There is no three-dollar bill in US currency, so something 'as phony as a three-dollar bill' is plainly fake.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. They are going to give me a lovely present, but I cannot ____ what it will be.
questions.explanation: The present is a surprise, so the speaker cannot 'guess' what it will be; 'guest' and 'gist' only look similar.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'maintenance'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Determined
questions.explanation: 'Determined' means firm and resolute in a decision: 'decisive'. 'Flexible' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. Ray was “cynical” about love.
questions.explanation: To be 'cynical' about love is to doubt that it is sincere or will last: 'pessimistic'. 'Trusting' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. The company sent out a “questionaire” to its employees to gather feedback on their work environment.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'questionnaire', with a double 'n'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who feeds on human flesh
questions.explanation: A 'cannibal' eats human flesh; a carnivore eats meat in general and an omnivore both plants and animals.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Larger emissions of greenhouse gases “lead to higher concentrations” in the atmosphere.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'emissions' takes the plural present 'lead', which suits a general truth. 'Leaded' is not the past of 'lead', and 'have lead' and 'is lead' are wrong forms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. Ramesh always “blows his own trumpet”.
questions.explanation: To 'blow one's own trumpet' is to boast about oneself, to praise oneself.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. He was “on cloud nine” when he got admission in Cambridge University.
options: available to be called to go to work
questions.explanation: To be 'on cloud nine' is to be extremely happy.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. An examination of a body after death
questions.explanation: A 'post mortem' (an autopsy) is the examination of a body after death; 'post partum' means after childbirth.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. One of the (1)______ tragedies is seeing someone with incredible talent get (2)_______ because he or she lacks some basic skills. This book (3)_______ the number one reason executives derail, and it provides extremely helpful tools to operate in a fast-paced, result-oriented environment. I am impressed by how insightful, (4)_______, well organised and focused it is. It will surely help one (5)______ several difficult situations.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'One of the' is followed by a superlative and a plural noun: 'one of the greatest tragedies'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. One of the (1)______ tragedies is seeing someone with incredible talent get (2)_______ because he or she lacks some basic skills. This book (3)_______ the number one reason executives derail, and it provides extremely helpful tools to operate in a fast-paced, result-oriented environment. I am impressed by how insightful, (4)_______, well organised and focused it is. It will surely help one (5)______ several difficult situations.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: A talented person gets 'derailed', thrown off course, for want of basic skills; the next sentence picks up the same image ('the number one reason executives derail').

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. One of the (1)______ tragedies is seeing someone with incredible talent get (2)_______ because he or she lacks some basic skills. This book (3)_______ the number one reason executives derail, and it provides extremely helpful tools to operate in a fast-paced, result-oriented environment. I am impressed by how insightful, (4)_______, well organised and focused it is. It will surely help one (5)______ several difficult situations.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The book 'addresses', that is, deals with, the main reason executives derail, and then provides tools to help.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. One of the (1)______ tragedies is seeing someone with incredible talent get (2)_______ because he or she lacks some basic skills. This book (3)_______ the number one reason executives derail, and it provides extremely helpful tools to operate in a fast-paced, result-oriented environment. I am impressed by how insightful, (4)_______, well organised and focused it is. It will surely help one (5)______ several difficult situations.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The writer is praising the book ('insightful', 'well organised', 'focused'), so the blank needs another favourable word: 'readable'.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number. One of the (1)______ tragedies is seeing someone with incredible talent get (2)_______ because he or she lacks some basic skills. This book (3)_______ the number one reason executives derail, and it provides extremely helpful tools to operate in a fast-paced, result-oriented environment. I am impressed by how insightful, (4)_______, well organised and focused it is. It will surely help one (5)______ several difficult situations.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: To 'salvage' a situation is to rescue it from going wrong, which is the help the book gives.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: A dealer buys some goods for ₹3,600. If the overhead expenses be 5% of the cost price, then at what price should it be sold to earn 15%?
questions.explanation: With overheads of 5%, the outlay is 3,600 × 1.05 = ₹3,780. A 15% profit on it needs 3,780 × 1.15 = ₹4,347.

questions.text: The 11th Fundamental Duty provides opportunities for education for the ______ age group of children.
questions.explanation: The 11th Fundamental Duty, Article 51A(k), added by the 86th Amendment (2002), asks a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to a child between six and fourteen years of age.

questions.text: As per the Census of India 2011, which Union Territory recorded the lowest population growth rate?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Lakshadweep's population grew by only about 6.3% over 2001-2011, the lowest of the Union territories; Daman and Diu grew by over 50%, Delhi by about 21% and Chandigarh by about 17%.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year were the Arms Act and Vernacular Press Act passed?
questions.explanation: Both were passed in 1878, under Viceroy Lord Lytton: the Vernacular Press Act curbed the Indian-language press, and the Arms Act barred Indians from keeping arms without a licence.

questions.text: In which state of India is Kaziranga National Park located?
questions.explanation: Kaziranga National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for the one-horned rhinoceros, lies on the Brahmaputra floodplain in Assam.

questions.text: By what name are the flat membrane-enclosed sacs present in the Golgi apparatus known?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus is a stack of flat, membrane-bound sacs called cisternae. Cristae are the folds of the mitochondrion's inner membrane, and stroma and lamellae belong to the chloroplast.

questions.text: The Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rojgar Yojana (SJSRY) was launched in the year ________ by Government of India.
questions.explanation: The Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana, an urban self-employment and wage-employment scheme, was launched on 1 December 1997; its name marks the golden jubilee (Swarna Jayanti) of independence.

questions.text: ‘Chapchar Kut’ is a festival from the state of _________. It is celebrated during March after the completion of the most arduous task of Jhum operation i.e., jungle clearing (clearing of the remnants of burning).
questions.explanation: Chapchar Kut, Mizoram's spring festival, is held in March once the jungle has been cleared for jhum (shifting) cultivation.

questions.text: In which event at the 2023 ISSF Junior World Cup Championships did Amanpreet Singh win a gold medal for India?
questions.explanation: Amanpreet Singh won the gold medal in the men's 25 m pistol at the ISSF Junior World Cup in Suhl, Germany, in June 2023.

questions.text: In which of the following States was the 2023 World Squash Championship held?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Tamil Nadu: the world squash event held in India in 2023 was the Squash World Cup, a team event, in Chennai in June 2023, which Egypt won, with India sharing third place with Japan. The PSA World Championships that year were held in Chicago.

questions.text: Mumtaz Khan was named ‘FIH Women’s Rising Star of the Year’ in 2022. She plays which of the following sports?
questions.explanation: Mumtaz Khan, a forward in India's women's hockey team, was named the FIH Women's Rising Star of the Year at the FIH's 2021-22 awards, announced in October 2022.

questions.text: Which of the following is a common financial service provided by Micro Finance Institutions?
options: Investment advisory services for high-net-worth individuals
Small loans to low-income individuals for entrepreneurial activities
questions.explanation: Microfinance institutions give small loans, often without collateral, to low-income people to start or run small businesses; mortgages for luxury homes, wealth advice and credit cards serve better-off customers.

questions.text: The Rathwas, who dwell in the state of ___________, perform the Rathwa dance on the occasion of Holi (festival of colours).
questions.explanation: The Rathwa tribe lives mainly in Chhota Udaipur district of eastern Gujarat, where the Rathwa dance is performed at Holi.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for a governor for each state?
questions.explanation: Article 153 says there shall be a Governor for each State. Article 156 sets the Governor's term, Article 157 the qualifications for the post, and Article 173 those for membership of the State Legislature.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was the first Woman President of Indian National Congress?
questions.explanation: Annie Besant presided over the Calcutta session of 1917, the first woman to do so; Sarojini Naidu, at Kanpur in 1925, was the first Indian woman president.

questions.text: _____________ was a star of the Kathak dance form described as ‘Nritya Samragini’ (the empress of dance) by Rabindranath Tagore.
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore called the young Kathak dancer Sitara Devi 'Nritya Samragini'. Rukmini Devi Arundale, Mrinalini Sarabhai and Mallika Sarabhai are known for Bharatanatyam and other South Indian forms, not Kathak.

questions.text: Which of the following methods is used to calculate national income by summing up the total spending on final goods and services in an economy?
questions.explanation: The expenditure method adds up final spending: consumption, investment, government purchases and net exports. The output (value-added) method adds the value added by each producer, and the income method adds wages, rent, interest and profit.

questions.text: Former Governor of Jharkhand from the year 2004 to 2009, __________, passed away in Lucknow in 2022.
questions.explanation: Syed Sibtey Razi was Governor of Jharkhand from December 2004 to July 2009; he died in Lucknow in August 2022.

questions.text: According to the IUPAC nomenclature system, which functional group is characterised by the presence of a −OH group, usually in a water-like bent shape?
questions.explanation: Alcohols carry the hydroxyl (−OH) group bonded to carbon, and the C−O−H angle is bent, like the H−O−H angle in water. Carbonyls have C=O, amines −NH₂ and esters −COO−.

questions.text: Ajmer Sharif is the shrine of which of the following Sufi saints?
questions.explanation: The Ajmer Sharif Dargah is the shrine of the Chishti Sufi saint Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti; the other three were rulers, not saints.

questions.text: Which of the following Carnatic musicians was the first to receive the Bharat Ratna?
questions.explanation: M. S. Subbulakshmi received the Bharat Ratna in 1998, the first musician to be so honoured. Tyagaraja and Syama Sastri were composers of the 18th and 19th centuries, and K. J. Yesudas had not received it when the exam was held (September 2023).

questions.text: Which of the following is the highest navigable lake in the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Titicaca, on the Peru-Bolivia border at about 3,800 m, is usually called the highest navigable lake in the world. Huron and Superior are Great Lakes of North America, and Como is in northern Italy.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. He felt “priviledged” to have received the country’s greatest honour.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'privileged'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined segment in the following sentence. Hundreds of people were “removed from a place” by the government recently due to a war-like situation.
questions.explanation: To 'evacuate' people is to remove them from a place of danger to safety.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. Buying a home in the city centre will cost you “an arm and a leg”.
questions.explanation: To 'cost an arm and a leg' is to be very expensive.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who has love for mankind OR One who makes an active effort to promote human welfare
questions.explanation: A 'philanthropist' loves mankind and works for the welfare of others, often through charity; an autocrat rules with absolute power.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. From scratch
questions.explanation: To do something 'from scratch' is to start it from the very beginning.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error. (A) Four divided by / (B) two is coming / (C) out to / (D) be two.
questions.explanation: A fixed mathematical fact takes the simple present, not the continuous: 'Four divided by two comes out to be two.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The detective went “the whole nine yards” in his investigation.
questions.explanation: To go 'the whole nine yards' is to do everything possible, all the way.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Many soldiers marched in ________ at the international border.
questions.explanation: Soldiers march 'in uniform', wearing the dress of their service; 'in dress', 'in fabric' and 'in clothes' are not used this way.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. This scripture / has been /translated in / seventy languages.
questions.explanation: A text is translated 'into' another language: 'has been translated into seventy languages'.

questions.text: Select the sentence that has NO spelling errors.
options: The elderly woman was delighted to receive a bouquet of fragrant flowers from her thoughtful grandson, who had come to visit her at the nursing home
The elderly woman was delighted to receive a bouque of fragrant flowers from her thoughtfull grandson, who had come to visit her at the nursing home
The elderly woman was deligted to receive a bouque of fregrant flowers from her thoughtful grandson, who had come to visit her at the nursing home
The elderly woman was delighed to recive a bouquet of fragrant flowers from her thoughtfull grandson, who had come to visit her at the nursing home
questions.explanation: Only the first sentence spells 'delighted', 'receive', 'bouquet', 'fragrant' and 'thoughtful' correctly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She was known for her __________ attention to detail, always making sure everything was perfectly organised and in its proper place.
questions.explanation: 'Fastidious' means very careful about accuracy and detail, which fits making sure everything is perfectly in place. 'Tedious' means boring and 'scornful' contemptuous, and 'exact' does not go with 'attention to detail'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The killing of a king
questions.explanation: 'Regicide' is the killing of a king; fratricide is the killing of a brother, sororicide of a sister and patricide of a father.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. They have less books than I have.
questions.explanation: 'Books' is countable, so the comparison takes 'fewer': 'They have fewer books than I have.' 'Less' goes with uncountable nouns.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Into hot water
questions.explanation: To get 'into hot water' is to get into trouble.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank. The sun was setting over the mountains, painting the sky with ________(energetic) shades of orange and pink.
questions.explanation: 'Vibrant', full of energy and life, is the synonym of 'energetic' and suits strong colours. 'Bright' suits the colours but does not mean 'energetic', and 'faded' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. She was writing / a letter to her grandmother / when the power / gone out.
questions.explanation: 'Gone' is a past participle and cannot stand alone; the interrupting action takes the simple past: 'when the power went out'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Nonchalant
questions.explanation: 'Nonchalant' means casually unconcerned or indifferent; its opposite is 'caring'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Grief
questions.explanation: 'Grief' is deep sorrow, mental 'pain'; pleasure, jollity and content are nearly its opposites.

questions.text: There is a spelling error in the given sentence. Select the option that contains the INCORRECTLY spelt word. The profesor’s niece was planning a pleasant surprise for him.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'professor'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Tim Cook, CEO of Apple who has recently ________(1) India, has some ________ (2) for parents: limit the screen time for children. He says: “Kids are born ________ (3), they’re digital kids now. And it is, I think, important to set some hard rails around it.” Various surveys of Indian children show alarming findings. A Saurashtra University survey of ________ (4) a thousand children and their parents in Rajkot finds that 92% students prefer playing mobile games over playing outside and 78% students ________ (5) to having their phone while having meals. In another survey by Local Circles, nearly 55% of parents admit that their children aged 9-13 have access to a smartphone throughout the day.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'has recently' takes the past participle: 'who has recently visited India'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Tim Cook, CEO of Apple who has recently ________(1) India, has some ________ (2) for parents: limit the screen time for children. He says: “Kids are born ________ (3), they’re digital kids now. And it is, I think, important to set some hard rails around it.” Various surveys of Indian children show alarming findings. A Saurashtra University survey of ________ (4) a thousand children and their parents in Rajkot finds that 92% students prefer playing mobile games over playing outside and 78% students ________ (5) to having their phone while having meals. In another survey by Local Circles, nearly 55% of parents admit that their children aged 9-13 have access to a smartphone throughout the day.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: After 'has some' a noun is needed: 'advice'. 'Advise' and 'suggest' are verbs.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Tim Cook, CEO of Apple who has recently ________(1) India, has some ________ (2) for parents: limit the screen time for children. He says: “Kids are born ________ (3), they’re digital kids now. And it is, I think, important to set some hard rails around it.” Various surveys of Indian children show alarming findings. A Saurashtra University survey of ________ (4) a thousand children and their parents in Rajkot finds that 92% students prefer playing mobile games over playing outside and 78% students ________ (5) to having their phone while having meals. In another survey by Local Circles, nearly 55% of parents admit that their children aged 9-13 have access to a smartphone throughout the day.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Born' is followed here by an adjective describing the kids: 'Kids are born digital', as 'digital kids' in the next clause confirms.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Tim Cook, CEO of Apple who has recently ________(1) India, has some ________ (2) for parents: limit the screen time for children. He says: “Kids are born ________ (3), they’re digital kids now. And it is, I think, important to set some hard rails around it.” Various surveys of Indian children show alarming findings. A Saurashtra University survey of ________ (4) a thousand children and their parents in Rajkot finds that 92% students prefer playing mobile games over playing outside and 78% students ________ (5) to having their phone while having meals. In another survey by Local Circles, nearly 55% of parents admit that their children aged 9-13 have access to a smartphone throughout the day.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'More than' gives a number above a figure: 'a survey of more than a thousand children'. 'Above' takes no 'than', and 'bigger than' and 'closer than' are not used to count people.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Tim Cook, CEO of Apple who has recently ________(1) India, has some ________ (2) for parents: limit the screen time for children. He says: “Kids are born ________ (3), they’re digital kids now. And it is, I think, important to set some hard rails around it.” Various surveys of Indian children show alarming findings. A Saurashtra University survey of ________ (4) a thousand children and their parents in Rajkot finds that 92% students prefer playing mobile games over playing outside and 78% students ________ (5) to having their phone while having meals. In another survey by Local Circles, nearly 55% of parents admit that their children aged 9-13 have access to a smartphone throughout the day.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The clause needs a present-tense verb, like 'prefer' before it, and 'be habituated to' means to be used to: '78% students are habituated to having their phone'.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The percentage profit earned by selling an article for ₹955 is equal to the percentage loss incurred by selling the same article for ₹845. At what price should the article be sold to make a 6% profit?
questions.explanation: Equal percentage profit and loss put the cost price midway between the two prices: (955 + 845)/2 = ₹900. A 6% profit needs 1.06 × 900 = ₹954.

questions.text: Seven people, B, N, M, O, P, Y and S are sitting in a straight line, facing south. Only two people sit between P and S. N is the immediate neighbour of S and M. Only one person sits to the right of P. N sits second to the left of O. Y is an immediate neighbour of P. Total how many people sit between P and M?
questions.explanation: Counting from the left end of the row (their left, as they face south): only one person is to P's right, so P is sixth, and S, with two people between them, is third. N sits beside both S and M; if N were fourth, O (second to N's right) would take P's seat, so N is second, M first and O fourth. Four people sit between M (first) and P (sixth).

questions.text: What is the maximum time gap between two sessions of the State Legislature?
questions.explanation: Under Article 174 the Governor must summon the Legislature so that six months do not pass between its last sitting in one session and its first sitting in the next.

questions.text: In 1951, the first Asian Games was held in which city?
questions.explanation: The first Asian Games were held in New Delhi in March 1951.

questions.text: What is a government budget?
options: A report on the economic growth of a country.
A plan for managing personal finances.
A financial statement of a government's expected revenue and expenditure for a specific period.
A document outlining foreign policy goals.
questions.explanation: A government budget is a statement of the government's estimated receipts and expenditure for a financial year; for the Union, Article 112 calls it the 'annual financial statement'.

questions.text: Who is the author of the novel ‘A Suitable Boy’?
questions.explanation: 'A Suitable Boy' (1993), a long novel set in newly independent India, is by Vikram Seth.

questions.text: What is the meaning of the term ‘Collateral’ in banking?
options: An asset pledged as security for a loan
questions.explanation: Collateral is an asset, such as property or gold, that a borrower pledges to the lender as security; the lender may take it if the loan is not repaid.

questions.text: The word ‘kathak’ is derived from which of the following words?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'story': 'kathak' comes from the Sanskrit 'katha', a story, which is also the root of 'kathaka', a storyteller, the name of the bards who told the epics through music, mime and dance.

questions.text: Which of the following autobiographies was written by Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam, the former president of India?
questions.explanation: 'Wings of Fire' (1999), written with Arun Tiwari, is A. P. J. Abdul Kalam's autobiography. 'Waiting for a Visa' is B. R. Ambedkar's and 'One Life is Not Enough' K. Natwar Singh's.

questions.text: Which Indian musician got the prestigious Academy Award?
questions.explanation: A. R. Rahman won two Academy Awards in 2009, for the original score and the original song ('Jai Ho') of 'Slumdog Millionaire'.

questions.text: In relation to the state of Tamil Nadu, the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Act, 2022 will include the __________ and Kurivikkaran communities in the list of Scheduled Tribes in Tamil Nadu.
questions.explanation: The Act added the Narikoravan and Kurivikkaran communities of Tamil Nadu to the state's list of Scheduled Tribes.

questions.text: Which antibiotic is considered the first miracle drug, used to treat throat infections, meningitis, syphilis and other bacterial infections?
questions.explanation: Penicillin, discovered by Alexander Fleming in 1928 and in wide use from the 1940s, was the first antibiotic to be hailed as a miracle drug. Aciclovir, by contrast, is an antiviral.

questions.text: Which of the following is the Fundamental Law of any country which sets out the framework and the principal functions of various organs of the government?
questions.explanation: A constitution is the fundamental law of a country: it sets out the framework of government and the powers and functions of its organs. An ordinance is a temporary law made by the executive.

questions.text: Jyothi Yarraji created a new national record in 2023 in which of the following sports?
questions.explanation: Jyothi Yarraji broke the national record in the women's 60 m hurdles, an indoor event, more than once in 2023, including 8.13 s for silver at the Asian Indoor Athletics Championships in Astana in February 2023.

questions.text: Which physicist's experiment during a lecture in 1820 showed the connection between electricity and magnetism?
questions.explanation: In 1820 Hans Christian Oersted saw that an electric current in a wire deflected a nearby compass needle, the first evidence that a current produces a magnetic effect.

questions.text: In the performance of ________ dance, on one side raasa dances are performed by women, whereas on the opposite side instrumentalist play the pung choloms (drums) and the karataala (cymbals).
questions.explanation: Manipuri dance pairs the Raas Leela, danced by women, with the cholom dances of male performers, who dance while playing the pung, Manipur's drum (pung cholom), or cymbals (kartal cholom).

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was the founder of the Khudai Khidmatgars, a powerful non-violent movement among the Pathans of North-West Frontier Province?
questions.explanation: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, the 'Frontier Gandhi', founded the Khudai Khidmatgars ('Servants of God') in 1929 to resist British rule non-violently in the North-West Frontier Province.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year was the Vernacular Press Act passed?
questions.explanation: The Vernacular Press Act was passed in 1878, under Lord Lytton, to curb newspapers in Indian languages; Lord Ripon repealed it in 1882.

questions.text: Which state of India is associated with the famous thunderstorms ‘Kaal Baisakhi’?
questions.explanation: Kalbaisakhi (nor'westers) are violent evening thunderstorms of the hot season, around the month of Baisakh (April-May), in West Bengal and the nearby eastern states.

questions.text: According to Ministry of Commerce and Industry (2018-19), which state of India is the largest producer of Rubber?
questions.explanation: By the Rubber Board's figures, Kerala produced about three-quarters of India's natural rubber in 2018-19; the crop needs a hot, wet climate.

questions.text: In which year was the first Khelo India Winter Games held?
questions.explanation: The first Khelo India Winter Games were held in 2020, in two legs: at Leh, Ladakh, from 25 February and at Gulmarg, Jammu and Kashmir, from 7 to 11 March.

questions.text: ‘Losoong’ festival, celebrated by the tribal community in ___________, is usually the time when the farmers rejoice and celebrate their harvest.
questions.explanation: Losoong, celebrated by Sikkim's Bhutia community (as Namsoong by the Lepchas), marks the end of the harvest and the Sikkimese New Year.

questions.text: According to the Human Development Index 2021, which group of neighbouring countries has ranked behind India?
questions.explanation: In the Human Development Index for 2021 (Human Development Report 2021/22), India ranked 132nd of 191 countries; Pakistan (161st) and Afghanistan (180th) ranked below it, while Sri Lanka, China, the Maldives, Bhutan and Bangladesh ranked above.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is true about the Great Bath of the Indus Valley Civilisation?
options: It was used for grain storage.
It was used as the water tank of the city.
It was probably used for religious purpose.
questions.explanation: The Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro, a watertight brick tank with steps at both ends, was probably used for ritual bathing.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. France is a “largest” country.
questions.explanation: Nothing is being compared, so the positive degree follows 'a': 'France is a large country.' A superlative would need 'the'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. Mr Sharma would have left / the station / by this time / tomorrow.
questions.explanation: An action that will be complete by a point in the future ('by this time tomorrow') takes the future perfect: 'Mr Sharma will have left the station by this time tomorrow.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. “Do not “turn a blind eye” to all the mischief your child is up to”, the teacher told the young parent.
questions.explanation: To 'turn a blind eye' to something is to pretend not to notice it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The mother ________ the chips because they were soggy.
questions.explanation: Soggy chips are unpleasant to eat, so the mother 'discarded' them, that is, threw them away.

questions.text: Identify the most appropriate meaning of the given word. Hope
questions.explanation: 'Hope' is a feeling of wanting something to happen: a 'wish'. 'Cynicism' is close to its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Have egg on your face
options: To be made to look foolish or embarrassed
Making a choice between two unpleasant choices
questions.explanation: To 'have egg on your face' is to be made to look foolish or embarrassed, usually by something that turns out badly.

questions.text: The following sentence contains some errors. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. The tiger was tranquiliized in the morning and keept in a cage to avoid disturbannces by human beings.
options: The tiger was tranquilized in the morning and kept in a cage to avoiid disturbaences by human beings.
The tiger was tranquilized in the morning and kept in a cage to avoid disturbances by human beings.
The tiger was traanquilized in the morning and kept in a cage to avoid dissturbances by human beings.
The tiger was tranquiliized in the morning and keept in a cage to avoid disturbances by human beings.
questions.explanation: Only this sentence spells 'tranquilized', 'kept', 'avoid' and 'disturbances' correctly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank. She’s reading a ________(secrecy) novel and can’t wait to find out who the killer is.
questions.explanation: 'Mystery', something secret or unexplained, is the word close to 'secrecy', and a mystery novel is one in which the reader finds out who committed a crime.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The viable of life / depends on a pair / of conflicting realities.
questions.explanation: 'Viable' is an adjective, and the subject needs a noun: 'The viability of life depends on a pair of conflicting realities.'

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I shall be playing for four hours.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'shall be playing', taking the length of time ('for four hours') to call for the future perfect continuous, 'I shall have been playing for four hours', the tense for an action that will have gone on for a stretch of time by a point in the future. The future continuous as printed can be defended, but there is no 'No error' option and none of the other parts could be at fault.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined segment in the given sentence. Our team is all “on the same page” when it comes to our goals for the upcoming project.
questions.explanation: To be 'on the same page' is to agree, to share the same understanding.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Bite the dust
questions.explanation: To 'bite the dust' is to be defeated (or, informally, to fail or die).

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who avoids sensory pleasures and physical comforts
questions.explanation: An 'ascetic' gives up physical comforts and pleasures, often for religious reasons. A frugal person is careful with money, an epicurean seeks pleasure, and a bohemian lives unconventionally.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'confess', with one 'f'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person living in solitude like a saint for religious practices.
questions.explanation: A 'hermit' lives alone, apart from society, often for religious reasons. A heretic holds beliefs against accepted doctrine, and an heir inherits.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Clumsy
questions.explanation: 'Clumsy' means awkward in movement; its opposite is 'graceful'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. No sooner had the sun risen over the horizon “when the birds began” to chirp and the squirrels started to scamper around the park.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner' is followed by 'than', not 'when', and the past 'began' matches 'started': 'No sooner had the sun risen over the horizon than the birds began to chirp.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. During the meeting, he went on a long and angry _______ about how the project was being mismanaged.
questions.explanation: A 'rant' is a long, angry speech, which fits 'long and angry'; a whisper and a mutter are quiet, and a shout is brief.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. I had / a bad habit of / waking up / lately.
questions.explanation: 'Lately' means recently; the adverb for waking after the usual time is 'late': 'I had a bad habit of waking up late.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Chaitnya was __________ from the school due to his misappropriate behaviour.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'expelled', with a double 'l': officially made to leave the school.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Once there was a king named Midas who was granted a (1)________ by Dionysus, the god of wine. For his wish, Midas asked that whatever he (2)________ would turn to gold. Despite Dionysus’ efforts to prevent it, Midas pleaded that this was a fantastic wish, and so, it was bestowed. Excited about his newly-earned (3)________, Midas started touching all kinds of things, turning each item into pure gold. But soon, Midas became (4)________. As he picked up a piece of food, he found he couldn’t eat it. It had turned to gold in his hand. Hungry, Midas groaned, “I’ll starve! Perhaps this was not such an excellent wish after all!” Seeing his dismay, Midas’ (5)________ daughter threw her arms around him to comfort him, and she, too, turned to gold. “The golden touch is no blessing,” Midas cried.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Midas was granted a 'wish', as the next sentence ('For his wish') shows.

Perhaps this was not such an excellent wish after all!” Seeing his dismay, Midas’ (5)________ daughter threw her arms around him to comfort him, and she, too, turned to gold. “The golden touch is no blessing,” Midas cried.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: This is the golden touch: whatever Midas 'touched' would turn to gold.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: His newly-earned 'powers', the ability to turn things to gold, are what he tried out by touching all kinds of things.

questions.explanation: Food turned to gold in his hand, so he could not eat and became 'hungry', as 'Hungry, Midas groaned' confirms.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The daughter who ran to comfort him was his 'beloved', dearly loved, daughter.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The average weight of 20 students of a class was 30.5 kg. After 6 new students joined the class, its average weight increased by 2 kg. Find the average weight of the 6 new students who joined the class (rounded off to one decimal place).
questions.explanation: The 20 students weigh 20 × 30.5 = 610 kg and all 26 weigh 26 × 32.5 = 845 kg, so the 6 new students weigh 235 kg: 235/6 ≈ 39.2 kg.

questions.text: The stretch between Mumbai to Goa of western coast of India is known as _______.
questions.explanation: The Konkan coast is the stretch of the west coast from Mumbai to Goa; the Kannada plain lies south of it, the Malabar coast further south in Kerala, and the Coromandel coast is on the east.

questions.text: Which of the following autobiographies is NOT correctly matched with the concerned cricketer?
options: Playing it My Way – VVS Laxman
The Test of My Life: From Cricket to Cancer and Back – Yuvraj Singh
Straight from the Heart – Kapil Dev
questions.explanation: 'Playing It My Way' is Sachin Tendulkar's autobiography; VVS Laxman's is '281 and Beyond'. The other three are matched correctly.

questions.text: What does El Niño refer to?
questions.explanation: El Niño is the periodic warming of the surface waters of the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, when warm water appears off the coast of Peru in place of the cold Peru current.

questions.text: Where was the 13th Hockey India senior women’s national hockey championship held?
questions.explanation: The 13th Hockey India Senior Women National Championship was held at Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh, from 15 to 26 February 2023.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advice the President in the exercise of the President's functions?
questions.explanation: Article 74(1) provides for a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President. Article 72 is the pardoning power, Article 71 covers disputes over the President's election and Article 77 the conduct of government business.

questions.text: Which of the following is a key objective of Micro Finance Institutions in India?
options: Providing loans exclusively to women entrepreneurs
Promoting financial inclusion and poverty alleviation
questions.explanation: Micro finance institutions give small loans and other financial services to low-income households that banks do not reach, to widen financial inclusion and reduce poverty.

questions.text: _____________ is one of the most important festivals of Kamakhya temple of Guwahati. It is held every year during the monsoon (mid-June) season, when the temple is closed for three days for tantric rites.
questions.explanation: The Ambubachi Mela at Kamakhya marks the goddess's yearly menstruation: the temple stays closed for three days in June and reopens on the fourth. Bihu is Assam's seasonal festival, Baishagu the Bodo spring festival and Me-Dum-Me-Phi the Ahom festival of ancestor worship.

questions.text: In which city is the Kamakhya temple situated?
questions.explanation: The Kamakhya temple stands on Nilachal Hill in Guwahati, Assam.

questions.text: Which of the following statements best defines a Micro Finance Institution (MFI)?
options: MFIs are investment firms that cater exclusively to high-net-worth individuals.
MFIs are non-profit organisations that provide financial services to low-income individuals and small businesses.
MFIs are banks that provide loans only to large corporations.
MFIs are government agencies that regulate the microfinance sector.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the definition that MFIs provide financial services to low-income individuals and small businesses, which is their defining role. Strictly, many Indian MFIs, such as the NBFC-MFIs regulated by the RBI, are for-profit companies, but the other three options describe something else entirely.

questions.text: Mumbai Indians defeated which team to win Women’s Premier League in March, 2023?
questions.explanation: Mumbai Indians beat Delhi Capitals by seven wickets in the final of the first Women's Premier League at the Brabourne Stadium, Mumbai, on 26 March 2023.

questions.text: The Songi Mukhawate dance of ___________ celebrates the victory of truth over falsehood. The name of the dance is derived from the two lion masks worn by two dancers who represent Narasimha, an aspect of Lord Vishnu.
questions.explanation: Songi Mukhawate is a mask dance of Maharashtra, performed on the full moon of Chaitra, in which two dancers wear Narasimha masks.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Where was the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association founded in 1928?
questions.explanation: The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association was founded at Feroz Shah Kotla in Delhi in September 1928, when Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and other young revolutionaries met there and reorganised the Hindustan Republican Association with a socialist aim.

questions.text: Which process is sometimes called "reduction division" because it reduces the number of chromosomes to half the normal number to form sperm and eggs?
questions.explanation: Meiosis halves the chromosome number, so each sperm or egg carries a single set and fertilisation restores the full number. Cytokinesis and karyokinesis are the division of the cytoplasm and of the nucleus.

questions.text: Which chemical element with atomic number 35 has a dark reddish-brown liquid with a burning pungent odour?
questions.explanation: Bromine (atomic number 35) is a dark reddish-brown liquid at room temperature with a choking smell; its name comes from the Greek 'bromos', stench. Chlorine is 17, astatine 85 and tennessine 117.

questions.text: In which year did Pakistan win the Kabaddi (Circle style) World Cup?
questions.explanation: Pakistan won the circle-style Kabaddi World Cup it hosted in February 2020, with the final at Lahore; it was Pakistan's first title, India having won every earlier edition.

questions.text: The North–South corridor, which is a part of the Golden Quadrilateral super highways, links which two cities of India from the following?
questions.explanation: The North–South Corridor runs from Srinagar to Kanyakumari. Strictly it is not part of the Golden Quadrilateral but, with the East–West Corridor, of the next phase of the same National Highways Development Project.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: For which community was a journal Rast Goftar started for the purpose of social-religious reforms?
questions.explanation: Rast Goftar ('Truth-teller'), the Gujarati paper started in 1851 by Dadabhai Naoroji, worked for social and religious reform among the Parsis.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: 26 January was selected as the date of the inauguration of the Constitution because on the same date in 1930, the Indian National Congress had revealed ________________________________.
questions.explanation: After its Lahore session adopted the goal of Purna Swaraj (complete independence) in December 1929, the Congress observed 26 January 1930 as Independence Day; the Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950 to mark that date.

questions.text: What is the name of the scheme launched by Uttar Pradesh government to boost milk production?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh's Nand Baba Milk Mission, announced in 2023, aims to raise milk production and help producers get fair prices through village dairy cooperatives.

questions.text: What is the source of Directive Principles of State Policy?
options: The instrument of instructions from GOI Act 1919
The instrument of instructions from GOI Act 1935
The instrument of instructions from GOI Act 1909
The instrument of instructions from GOI Act 1947
questions.explanation: B. R. Ambedkar likened the Directive Principles to the Instrument of Instructions issued to the Governor-General and the Governors under the Government of India Act, 1935; the idea of the Principles came from the Irish Constitution.

questions.text: How many classical dance forms does the Sangeet Natak Akademi in India officially recognise, as of August 2021?
questions.explanation: The Sangeet Natak Akademi recognises eight classical dances: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Odissi and Sattriya. (The Ministry of Culture's list adds Chhau, making nine.)

questions.text: According to the Human Development Report 2021-22, what is the rank of India among 191 countries?
questions.explanation: The UNDP's Human Development Report 2021-22, released in September 2022, ranked India 132nd of 191 countries.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The Indian team had its “back against the wall”, but managed to fight back.
options: Stuck in a difficult circumstance with no escape
questions.explanation: To have one's 'back against the wall' is to be in a difficult situation with no way out.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. This is the first time / I ate such / a tasty cake.
questions.explanation: 'This is the first time' takes the present perfect: 'This is the first time I have eaten such a tasty cake.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A lover of books
questions.explanation: A 'bibliophile' is a lover of books; a librarian looks after a library.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Tom waited until __________ to start working on his term paper but managed to finish it just in time.
questions.explanation: To do something at 'the eleventh hour' is to do it at the last possible moment.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Cordial
questions.explanation: 'Cordial' means warm and 'friendly'; 'unfriendly' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Bigger fish to fry
options: Having something more important to take care of
Having work more than one’s capacity
To be similar to one’s parents in some way
questions.explanation: To have 'bigger fish to fry' is to have more important matters to attend to.

questions.text: There is a spelling error in the given sentence. Select the option that contains the INCORRECTLY spelt word. The hungery goblin scratched the grammar book with a feather.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'hungry'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The rusty door made a ________ screeching noise.
questions.explanation: A screech is a loud, grating sound, so the noise was 'harsh'; 'soft', 'low' and 'smooth' contradict 'screeching'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The tone of his voice seemed to ______ that he knew more than he was letting on.
questions.explanation: To 'imply' is to suggest without saying directly. To 'incise' is to cut and to 'inculcate' to instil, and 'intent' is not a verb.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Enormous
questions.explanation: 'Enormous' means very large; its opposite is 'tiny'. 'Gigantic' is a synonym.

questions.text: There is a spelling error in the given sentence. Select the option that contains the INCORRECTLY spelt word. The questionnaire appeared to be misrably designed.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'miserably'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. COVID-19 _________ structural weaknesses in health systems worldwide and negatively impacted individuals, societies, and economies.
questions.explanation: The pandemic 'revealed', brought to light, weaknesses that were already there; 'concealed' is the opposite, and 'laid' would need 'bare'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. She “will handling” the baby as tenderly as possible.
questions.explanation: 'Will' takes the bare infinitive: 'She will handle the baby as tenderly as possible.'

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. A old woman suddenly laughed, sounding just like an amused hen.
questions.explanation: 'Old' begins with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an': 'An old woman'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Annoy
questions.explanation: To 'annoy' is to irritate; its opposite is to 'gratify', to please. 'Vex' and 'irritate' are synonyms.

questions.text: Four words of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains a spelling error. All life depends on a healthy planet, but the “interwoven” systems of atmosphere, oceans, “watercourses”, land, ice cover and “biosphere”, which form the natural environment, are “threatned” by human activities.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'threatened'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A storm in a teacup
questions.explanation: 'A storm in a teacup' is a great fuss over something unimportant.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Varun has to ______ his studies for the sake of his ill father.
questions.explanation: To 'sacrifice' his studies is to give them up for the sake of something more important, here his ill father.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Vikram is very stronger than I am.
questions.explanation: A comparative is strengthened with 'much' or 'far', not 'very': 'Vikram is much stronger than I am.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. You are always “try with jump” over the wall.
questions.explanation: 'Always' with the present continuous describes a repeated habit, and 'try' takes a to-infinitive: 'You are always trying to jump over the wall.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. Kasturi went to the garden looking for her mother. Her dog Rex was waiting (1)____ her. Kasturi picked up a stick and threw it. Rex (2)______ the stick and brought it back. Kasturi ran (3)___ the house. Rex chased her. Kasturi ran through the garden and Rex (4)____ her. Mother yelled at both of them. She told them to stay (5)______ of the garden and play somewhere else. Kasturi apologised to her mother. She went for a bike ride while Rex ran next to the bike.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: One waits 'for' someone: 'Rex was waiting for her'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. Kasturi went to the garden looking for her mother. Her dog Rex was waiting (1)____ her. Kasturi picked up a stick and threw it. Rex (2)______ the stick and brought it back. Kasturi ran (3)___ the house. Rex chased her. Kasturi ran through the garden and Rex (4)____ her. Mother yelled at both of them. She told them to stay (5)______ of the garden and play somewhere else. Kasturi apologised to her mother. She went for a bike ride while Rex ran next to the bike.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Rex 'chased' the stick and brought it back: the past tense matches 'brought', and the dog runs after the stick Kasturi threw.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. Kasturi went to the garden looking for her mother. Her dog Rex was waiting (1)____ her. Kasturi picked up a stick and threw it. Rex (2)______ the stick and brought it back. Kasturi ran (3)___ the house. Rex chased her. Kasturi ran through the garden and Rex (4)____ her. Mother yelled at both of them. She told them to stay (5)______ of the garden and play somewhere else. Kasturi apologised to her mother. She went for a bike ride while Rex ran next to the bike.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Rex 'followed' her through the garden: the simple past matches 'ran'. 'Came' would need 'after', and 'obey' and 'listen' are not past forms.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. Kasturi went to the garden looking for her mother. Her dog Rex was waiting (1)____ her. Kasturi picked up a stick and threw it. Rex (2)______ the stick and brought it back. Kasturi ran (3)___ the house. Rex chased her. Kasturi ran through the garden and Rex (4)____ her. Mother yelled at both of them. She told them to stay (5)______ of the garden and play somewhere else. Kasturi apologised to her mother. She went for a bike ride while Rex ran next to the bike.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: To 'stay out of' a place is to keep away from it: 'stay out of the garden and play somewhere else'.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Seven people, C, F, D, K, O, L, and V are sitting in a straight line, facing south. V sits second to the right of F. Only three people sit to the right of O. K is an immediate neighbour of O and D. Only three people sit between L and V. F is not an immediate neighbour of L. Who sits to the extreme left of the line?
questions.explanation: Numbering the seats 1 to 7 from the left end (the people's own left): three people sit to O's right, so O is in seat 4, and K sits between O and D. With K in 3 and D in 2, V (second to F's right) could only be in 7, leaving no seat four away for L; so K is in 5 and D in 6. Then F is in 1, V in 3, L in 7 and C in 2: F, C, V, O, K, D, L, with F at the extreme left.

questions.text: Who inaugurated the 2023 World Squash Championships that was held in India?
questions.explanation: The squash event India hosted in 2023, the Squash World Cup in Chennai in June, was declared open by Udhayanidhi Stalin, then Tamil Nadu's Minister for Youth Welfare and Sports Development. K. N. Nehru, K. Ponmudi and E. V. Velu were also Tamil Nadu ministers at the time.

questions.text: What is ‘Mahawat’ in India?
options: Cold waves during the winter season
Cloud burst during the monsoon season
Cyclonic rainfall during the winter season
Hot and dry winds during the summer season
questions.explanation: Mahawat is the light winter rain that western disturbances, cyclones from the Mediterranean region, bring to north-west India; it is small in amount but valuable for the rabi crops.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the organization of village panchayat?
questions.explanation: Article 40, a Directive Principle, directs the State to organise village panchayats and give them the powers they need to work as units of self-government. Article 38 is on the social order, 45 on early childhood care and education, and 36 defines 'the State' for Part IV.

questions.text: Bharati Shivaji and Kanak Rele are exponents of ______.
questions.explanation: Bharati Shivaji and Kanak Rele are noted exponents of Mohiniyattam, the classical dance of Kerala.

questions.text: Which is the most common ore of oxidised mercury that occurs in granular crusts or veins associated with volcanic activity and hot springs?
questions.explanation: Cinnabar, mercury(II) sulphide (HgS), in which mercury is in its oxidised +2 state, is the chief ore of mercury and forms crusts and veins near volcanic activity and hot springs. It is the only mercury mineral among the options: diaspore and corundum are aluminium minerals and siderite is iron carbonate.

questions.text: Women's World Boxing Championship 2023 was held in which city in India?
questions.explanation: The 2023 IBA Women's World Boxing Championships were held in New Delhi in March 2023, and Indian boxers won four gold medals there.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who is regarded as the ‘Mother of Indian Revolution’?
questions.explanation: Bhikaji Rustom Cama (Madame Cama), who unfurled an early Indian national flag at the International Socialist Congress in Stuttgart in 1907, is called the 'Mother of Indian Revolution'.

questions.text: Which microscopic, single-celled photosynthetic organisms are known as the primary producers of the ocean - the organisms that form the base of the aquatic food chains?
questions.explanation: Phytoplankton, microscopic photosynthetic organisms such as diatoms, are the ocean's primary producers. Zooplankton are animals that feed on them, and bacterioplankton and virioplankton are bacteria and viruses.

questions.text: Which of the following novels is correctly paired with its author?
questions.explanation: 'The Namesake' (2003) is by Jhumpa Lahiri. 'The Shadow Lines' is Amitav Ghosh's, 'Malgudi Days' R. K. Narayan's and 'Train to Pakistan' Khushwant Singh's.

questions.text: Which of the following is a communication mail channel in India?
questions.explanation: NCERT lists six mail channels introduced for quicker delivery in large towns and cities: Rajdhani, Metro, Green, Business, Bulk Mail and Periodical. There is no pink, yellow or red channel among them.

questions.text: Under the umbrella of Ujjwal Bharat Ujjwal Bhavishya–Power @ 2047, the PM inaugurated which of the following 100 MW Solar Projects in Telangana?
questions.explanation: At the 'Ujjwal Bharat Ujjwal Bhavishya - Power @2047' event on 30 July 2022, the Prime Minister dedicated NTPC's 100 MW Ramagundam floating solar project in Telangana to the nation, along with the 92 MW Kayamkulam floating solar project in Kerala.

questions.text: What is the name of the geographic feature that serves as a boundary between Europe and Africa?
questions.explanation: The Strait of Gibraltar separates Spain in Europe from Morocco in Africa and joins the Mediterranean to the Atlantic. The Bosporus and the Dardanelles divide Europe from Asia, and the Strait of Malacca lies between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra.

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of microfinance institutions (MFIs) in India?
options: To promote consumer spending among middle-class households
To offer financial services exclusively to large businesses
To provide small loans to low-income individuals
To facilitate foreign investment in the Indian economy
questions.explanation: Microfinance institutions give small loans, and often savings and insurance, to low-income people who lack access to ordinary banking.

questions.text: Which of the following is true about transfer payments in relation to personal income?
options: Transfer payments are included in personal income.
Transfer payments have no impact on personal income.
Transfer payments are included in personal income only for businesses.
Transfer payments are excluded from personal income.
questions.explanation: Personal income is the income households actually receive, so transfer payments such as pensions, scholarships and unemployment allowances are added to it, although they are not part of national income.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following reformers initially set up a school for girls in Calcutta?
questions.explanation: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar led girls' education in Bengal: he was secretary of the Bethune School, the girls' school founded in Calcutta in 1849, and opened about 35 girls' schools across Bengal in the 1850s. Jyotirao Phule's first girls' school was in Pune (1848).

questions.text: Bharhut Stupa is located in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: The Bharhut stupa, known for its carved railings and gateways of the Shunga period (2nd century BCE), is in Satna district of Madhya Pradesh; many of its sculptures are now in the Indian Museum, Kolkata.

questions.text: The most famous of all Jain festivals, Mahamastakabhisheka is performed every 12 years at the Digambara sacred complex at _______________ in Karnataka.
questions.explanation: The Mahamastakabhisheka, the anointing of the colossal statue of Bahubali (Gommateshwara), is held about every 12 years at Shravanabelagola in Hassan district, Karnataka.

questions.text: Which religion has the maximum number of followers in Bhutan?
questions.explanation: About three-quarters of Bhutan's people follow Buddhism, mainly of the Vajrayana (Tibetan) tradition; Hindus, living largely in the south, are the largest minority.

questions.text: The Madhavpur fair is held at _________.
questions.explanation: The Madhavpur Ghed fair, held around Ram Navami at Madhavpur in Porbandar district, Gujarat, celebrates the marriage of Krishna and Rukmini.

questions.text: The former captain of the Indian women’s hockey team __________ was conferred with the BBC Lifetime Achievement Award for her contribution to Indian sports and inspiring generations of players.
questions.explanation: Pritam Siwach, a former captain of India's women's hockey team, received the BBC Lifetime Achievement Award for 2022 at the BBC Indian Sportswoman of the Year awards in March 2023.

questions.text: Who among the following is a Bharatanatyam and Kathakali dancer?
questions.explanation: Mrinalini Sarabhai trained in both Bharatanatyam and Kathakali and founded the Darpana Academy in Ahmedabad. Padma Subrahmanyam is a Bharatanatyam dancer, Sonal Mansingh is known for Bharatanatyam and Odissi, and Shovana Narayan for Kathak.
