questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of the fundamental rights?
questions.explanation: Article 32 gives the right to move the Supreme Court for the enforcement of the Fundamental Rights; Ambedkar called it the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution. Article 21 protects life and personal liberty, 25 freedom of religion and 29 the interests of minorities.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Existentialism has a reputation for being angst-ridden and gloomy mostly because of its emphasis on pondering the meaningless of existence.
options: on pondering the meaningless of existence
questions.explanation: After 'the' a noun is needed: 'the meaninglessness of existence'. 'Meaningless' is an adjective.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. To “preparing the vine for plant”, it should be cut back to 2 ft.
questions.explanation: Purpose is shown by the infinitive, 'to' with the base form, and a preposition takes the gerund: 'To prepare the vine for planting, it should be cut back to 2 ft.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. The student provided her English teacher a short and _________(incoherent) account of her journey to Shimla with her parents.
questions.explanation: 'Incoherent' means muddled and hard to follow; its opposite is 'lucid', clear and easy to understand.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. I want to / give you / an information about / the missing necklace.
questions.explanation: 'Information' is an uncountable noun and takes no 'an': 'give you some information about the missing necklace'.

questions.text: Identify the most appropriate meaning of the given word. Ancient
questions.explanation: 'Ancient' means very old, as does 'antique'; 'contemporary' and 'recent' are its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. They “are sell their company’s” products to people.
questions.explanation: The present continuous is 'are' with the '-ing' form: 'They are selling their company's products to people.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. Mary is “a ball of fire” and is always engaged in something creative.
options: To be good and beneficial for someone
questions.explanation: A 'ball of fire' is a lively, energetic person.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. By living in a rural area with access to the city, she gets _______________.
options: to keep an ear to the ground
in for a penny in for a pound
questions.explanation: To get 'the best of both worlds' is to enjoy the advantages of two different things at once, here country living and the city.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. “The cats” food bowl was empty, so he meowed incessantly until his owner finally filled it with fresh kibble.
questions.explanation: One particular cat ('he meowed', 'his owner') owns the bowl, so the singular possessive with 'the' is needed: 'The cat's food bowl'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Get your act together
options: Get organised and do things better
questions.explanation: To 'get your act together' is to get organised and start doing things properly.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Unpleasant
questions.explanation: 'Nasty' means unpleasant. 'Nebulous' means vague, 'natal' relates to birth, and 'negligible' means too small to matter.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error. (A) The mother exclaimed / (B) when she saw her son / (C) stumble on the race track, / (D) “Look, he fells!”
questions.explanation: 'Fell' is the past tense of 'fall', and 'fells' belongs to another verb, to fell (cut down) a tree; the mother needs the present of 'fall': 'Look, he falls' or 'he is falling'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’. The conductor said that it was the “worse” quake he ever knew.
questions.explanation: 'The' and 'he ever knew' compare it with every quake he knew, so the superlative is needed: 'the worst quake he ever knew'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. After having invested so much time and energy into the project, we are now “back to square one”.
options: Having to start all over again
questions.explanation: To be 'back to square one' is to have to start again from the beginning after making no progress.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Killing of one’s own father
questions.explanation: 'Patricide' is the killing of one's own father; matricide is of one's mother, filicide of one's child, and suicide of oneself.

questions.text: The sentence given below has spelling errors. Select the sentence without spelling errors. Though we read and hear a lot on green initiattive, we hardly tweak our routines to suite the larger picture.
options: Though we read and hear a lot on green initiatives, we hardly tweak our routines to suit the larger picture.
Throug we read and hear a lot on green initiatives, we hardly tweak our routines to suite the larger picture.
Though we read and hear a lot on green initiatives, we hardly tweek our routines to suite the larger picture.
Though we read and hear a lot on green iniciatives, we hardly tweak our routines to suite the larger picture.
questions.explanation: The correct spellings are 'though', 'initiatives', 'tweak' and 'suit' (to fit); a 'suite' is a set of rooms or things.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank. The athlete’s injury was a ________(defeat) for the team’s chances of winning the championship.
questions.explanation: A 'setback' is a reverse that holds back progress, close in sense to 'defeat' here; 'progression' and 'breakthrough' point the other way.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'irresistible'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'millennium', with a double 'l' and a double 'n'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence. She proposed to write the “life history” of the famous poet.
questions.explanation: A 'biography' is the story of a person's life written by someone else; an autobiography is written by the person themselves.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Democracy is a form of government where the power lies ______(1) the people. It is based on the principles of equality, freedom and the rule of law. In a democratic society, ______(2) have the right to participate in the decision-making process, _________(3) directly or through elected representatives. Democracy also allows for the ________(4) of individual rights and liberties. While democracy is not without its challenges, such as the need to balance competing interests and the risk of ___________(5) movements, it remains one of the most widely embraced forms of government around the world.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: Power 'lies with' the people: it belongs to them.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Democracy is a form of government where the power lies ______(1) the people. It is based on the principles of equality, freedom and the rule of law. In a democratic society, ______(2) have the right to participate in the decision-making process, _________(3) directly or through elected representatives. Democracy also allows for the ________(4) of individual rights and liberties. While democracy is not without its challenges, such as the need to balance competing interests and the risk of ___________(5) movements, it remains one of the most widely embraced forms of government around the world.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: In a democracy it is the 'citizens', the members of the state, who have the right to take part in its decisions.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Democracy is a form of government where the power lies ______(1) the people. It is based on the principles of equality, freedom and the rule of law. In a democratic society, ______(2) have the right to participate in the decision-making process, _________(3) directly or through elected representatives. Democracy also allows for the ________(4) of individual rights and liberties. While democracy is not without its challenges, such as the need to balance competing interests and the risk of ___________(5) movements, it remains one of the most widely embraced forms of government around the world.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: 'Either ... or' joins the two ways of taking part: 'either directly or through elected representatives'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Democracy is a form of government where the power lies ______(1) the people. It is based on the principles of equality, freedom and the rule of law. In a democratic society, ______(2) have the right to participate in the decision-making process, _________(3) directly or through elected representatives. Democracy also allows for the ________(4) of individual rights and liberties. While democracy is not without its challenges, such as the need to balance competing interests and the risk of ___________(5) movements, it remains one of the most widely embraced forms of government around the world.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: Democracy allows for the 'protection' of rights and liberties; 'proscription' means banning and 'delimitation' fixing boundaries.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Democracy is a form of government where the power lies ______(1) the people. It is based on the principles of equality, freedom and the rule of law. In a democratic society, ______(2) have the right to participate in the decision-making process, _________(3) directly or through elected representatives. Democracy also allows for the ________(4) of individual rights and liberties. While democracy is not without its challenges, such as the need to balance competing interests and the risk of ___________(5) movements, it remains one of the most widely embraced forms of government around the world.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: 'Populist' movements, which claim to speak for ordinary people against an elite, are a familiar risk to democracies; 'marginal' or 'negligible' movements would pose little risk.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: What will be the amount due on ₹24,000 in 2 years when the rate of simple interest on successive years is 4% per annum and 5% per annum, respectively?
questions.explanation: Interest for the first year = 4% of ₹24,000 = ₹960 and for the second = 5% of ₹24,000 = ₹1,200. Amount = 24,000 + 960 + 1,200 = ₹26,160.

questions.text: Which of the following countries did India beat to win the Men's Hockey Junior Asia Cup 2023?
questions.explanation: India beat Pakistan 2-1 in the final at Salalah, Oman, in June 2023 to win the Men's Junior Asia Cup for the fourth time.

questions.text: In the realm of soil science, humus is considered:
questions.explanation: Humus is the dark, decaying organic matter in soil, formed from dead plants and animals; it adds nutrients and helps the soil hold water.

questions.text: Which group of crops belong to fibre crops and are produced on a large scale in India?
questions.explanation: NCERT names cotton, jute, hemp and natural silk as India's four major fibre crops. Gram and tur are pulses, tea and coffee beverage crops, and wheat and rice cereals.

questions.text: Name the life-threatening disease caused by protozoa of the genus Trypanosoma that is transmitted to human hosts through the bite of infected tsetse flies.
questions.explanation: Sleeping sickness (African trypanosomiasis) is caused by Trypanosoma brucei and spread by tsetse flies. Chagas disease, caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, is spread by triatomine bugs, and kala-azar by sandflies.

questions.text: Who is an acclaimed Kathak dancer with many awards to his credit?
questions.explanation: Pandit Birju Maharaj of the Lucknow gharana was the leading Kathak dancer of his time. Shiv Kumar Sharma played the santoor, Alla Rakha the tabla and Bismillah Khan the shehnai.

questions.text: ‘Pinjar’ is a novel by ___________.
questions.explanation: 'Pinjar' (1950) is Amrita Pritam's Punjabi novel set against the violence of Partition.

questions.text: When was the Asian Games organised in India for the second time?
questions.explanation: New Delhi hosted the first Asian Games in 1951 and the ninth, India's second, in 1982.

questions.text: Who nominates members to the Rajya Sabha based on their excellence in literature, science, art and social service?
options: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
questions.explanation: Under Article 80 the President nominates 12 members of the Rajya Sabha with special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service.

questions.text: Which Indian musician is associated with the Flute?
questions.explanation: Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is the best-known exponent of the bansuri, the bamboo flute. Zakir Hussain and Alla Rakha played the tabla and Ravi Shankar the sitar.

questions.text: The black soil area of the ________ is known as the Deccan Trap.
questions.explanation: NCERT describes the black soil area known as the Deccan Trap as a distinct feature of the Peninsular Plateau; it is of volcanic origin, so its rocks are igneous.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When did the British East India Company start the ‘permanent settlement system’?
questions.explanation: Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement in Bengal in 1793, fixing the zamindars' land revenue in perpetuity.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The word ‘Swaraj’ was first used by Dadabhai Naoroji in the Congress session held in which place?
questions.explanation: Presiding over the Calcutta session of 1906, Dadabhai Naoroji declared 'Swaraj' (self-government) the goal of the Congress, the first time the word was used from its platform.

questions.text: Chhau, identified by the Ministry of Culture as a classical dance, is prevalent in eastern India and has three distinct forms. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation: Chhau's three styles are named after where they are danced: Seraikela in Jharkhand, Purulia in West Bengal and Mayurbhanj in Odisha. There is no Marwahi Chhau.

questions.text: According to the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index 2022, which of the following states is NOT included in 10 poorest states?
questions.explanation: The Global MPI 2022 (UNDP and OPHI) found Bihar, Jharkhand, Meghalaya, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Assam, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and Rajasthan still among India's ten poorest states in 2019-21; Gujarat was not among them.

questions.text: Which Clause of Article 19 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the ‘right to move freely throughout the territory of India’?
questions.explanation: Article 19(1)(d) guarantees the right to move freely throughout the territory of India; (a) covers speech and expression, (b) peaceful assembly and (c) forming associations or unions.

questions.text: The President of India conferred the Padma Shri award to Sanathoiba Sharma for his distinguished service in the field of ______________ in 2023.
questions.explanation: K. Sanathoiba Sharma, a Thang-Ta guru from Manipur, received the Padma Shri in 2023 (sports) for promoting this traditional Manipuri martial art. Mukna is Manipuri wrestling, Khong Kangjei a Manipuri form of hockey and Yubi Lakpi a Manipuri game played with a greased coconut.

questions.text: Rikham pada dance belongs to which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Rikham Pada (Rikampada) is a folk dance of the Nyishi people of Arunachal Pradesh.

questions.text: Which theory was published by John Dalton in 1808 to explain chemical reactions?
questions.explanation: Dalton set out his atomic theory in 'A New System of Chemical Philosophy' in 1808: elements are made of atoms, atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios to form compounds, and a chemical reaction only rearranges them.

questions.text: What is the main function of money in an economy?
questions.explanation: Money's main function is as a medium of exchange: it removes the barter system's need for a double coincidence of wants.

questions.text: Who among the following designed the India Gate?
questions.explanation: India Gate, the All India War Memorial in New Delhi, was designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens.

questions.text: In 2022, the Centre constituted a committee headed by former Union Agriculture Secretary _______ to look into the issues of minimum support price (MSP).
questions.explanation: In July 2022 the Centre set up a committee under Sanjay Agrawal, former Union Agriculture Secretary, to make MSP more effective and transparent and to promote natural farming and crop diversification.

questions.text: One of the prominent festivals celebrated in ____________ is the ‘Me-Dum-Me-Phi’, i.e., the ancestor worship festival.
questions.explanation: Me-Dam-Me-Phi, the Ahom community's festival of ancestor worship, is celebrated in Assam on 31 January.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Be like chalk and cheese
options: To be completely different from each other
To be very similar to each other
To have a close relation with another person
To be distantly related to each other
questions.explanation: Two people or things 'like chalk and cheese' are completely different from each other.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. Everyone liked the “lively” music being played at the restaurant.
questions.explanation: 'Lively' means full of energy and cheer; its opposite is 'sombre', dark and gloomy.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'forty', without the 'u' of 'four'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined segment in the following sentence. Raymond has opted “the study of religion” as his major subject in graduation.
questions.explanation: 'Theology' is the study of religion. Psephology is the study of elections, philology of the history of languages and psychology of the mind.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom from the given options to fill in the blank. Greta Thunberg _____________ when she dared to question about accountability with respect to global warming and climate change.
options: hit the nail on the head
questions.explanation: To 'hit the nail on the head' is to say exactly what is right about a problem. To 'sow wild oats' is to behave wildly when young, and to 'give the devil his due' is to credit someone one dislikes.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. When Rajesh was going to college, he “meet” with an accident.
questions.explanation: The past continuous sets the background and the simple past gives the event that happened during it: 'he met with an accident'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. “As soon as” I “shall win” the lottery, I “hope” to buy “a Ferrari”.
questions.explanation: A clause of time with 'as soon as' takes the simple present for a future event: 'As soon as I win the lottery'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Some things are meant to be, and death is ______ for humans.
questions.explanation: Death is 'natural', part of the ordinary course of life, for humans; 'edible', 'spiral' and 'viral' make no sense here.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. They complained that their manager was “incompietent” and knew nothing about the project.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'incompetent'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Distinguished
questions.explanation: 'Distinguished' means commanding respect, with a dignified air: 'dignified'. 'Mediocre' is close to its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Periodic
questions.explanation: 'Periodic' means happening at regular intervals; its opposite is 'irregular'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. Manisha saw an old elephant / in the wildlife reserve / while she was / on safari tour.
questions.explanation: 'Tour' is a singular countable noun and needs an article: 'on a safari tour'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. In Nepal, the food is more cheaper than in Sri Lanka.
questions.explanation: 'Cheaper' is already comparative, so 'more cheaper' is a double comparative: 'the food is cheaper'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Most times, he is sitting alone, immersed in his own ______________.
questions.explanation: A 'monologue' is a long speech by one person; sitting alone, he is lost in talking to himself. A synagogue is a Jewish place of worship and a prologue an introduction.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence and select its correct spelling from the given options. He has neither the policies nor the persanol charisma to inspire people.
questions.explanation: The misspelt word is 'persanol'; the correct spelling is 'personal'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The judge wanted to hear “straight from the horse’s mouth”.
options: In close vicinity to the juror
questions.explanation: To hear something 'straight from the horse's mouth' is to hear it directly from the person concerned.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Virtual reality is the creation of a virtual environment “presented to our senses” in such a way that we experience it as if we were really there.
questions.explanation: 'Presented to our senses' is a past participle phrase describing the environment (one that is presented to our senses), so the sentence is correct as it stands.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom from the given options to fill in the blank. Being a journalist, your first duty is to ____________ or else your colleagues might surpass you.
options: keep your ear to the ground
questions.explanation: To 'keep your ear to the ground' is to stay well informed about what is happening, a journalist's first duty.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error. (A) He will come / (B) and receive you / (C) at the station / (D) when you will arrive.
questions.explanation: A clause of time with 'when' takes the simple present for a future event: 'when you arrive'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. She is very good / in playing / the guitar / and singing songs.
questions.explanation: One is good 'at' an activity: 'She is very good at playing the guitar'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Environmental pollution is a growing (1)________ all around the world as it poses significant risks to human health and ecosystems. The (2)________ of environmental pollution vary from natural causes such as volcanic emissions to human actions, including industrialisation, transportation, energy production and agricultural practices. (3)___________ of these activities, pollutants are released into the air, water bodies and soil leading to harmful effects such as respiratory diseases, loss of biodiversity and climate change. One of the primary causes of environmental pollution is human attitudes towards sustainability (4)_______ their lack of environmental awareness. Human activities that harm the environment and ecosystem often result from individual choices (5)_______ driving or using single-use plastics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Pollution is a growing 'concern', a cause of worry, because it poses risks to health and ecosystems.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Environmental pollution is a growing (1)________ all around the world as it poses significant risks to human health and ecosystems. The (2)________ of environmental pollution vary from natural causes such as volcanic emissions to human actions, including industrialisation, transportation, energy production and agricultural practices. (3)___________ of these activities, pollutants are released into the air, water bodies and soil leading to harmful effects such as respiratory diseases, loss of biodiversity and climate change. One of the primary causes of environmental pollution is human attitudes towards sustainability (4)_______ their lack of environmental awareness. Human activities that harm the environment and ecosystem often result from individual choices (5)_______ driving or using single-use plastics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The plural verb 'vary' needs a plural noun: 'The sources of environmental pollution vary'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Environmental pollution is a growing (1)________ all around the world as it poses significant risks to human health and ecosystems. The (2)________ of environmental pollution vary from natural causes such as volcanic emissions to human actions, including industrialisation, transportation, energy production and agricultural practices. (3)___________ of these activities, pollutants are released into the air, water bodies and soil leading to harmful effects such as respiratory diseases, loss of biodiversity and climate change. One of the primary causes of environmental pollution is human attitudes towards sustainability (4)_______ their lack of environmental awareness. Human activities that harm the environment and ecosystem often result from individual choices (5)_______ driving or using single-use plastics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'As a result of these activities' introduces their consequence; 'since', 'however' and 'therefore' cannot be followed by 'of'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Environmental pollution is a growing (1)________ all around the world as it poses significant risks to human health and ecosystems. The (2)________ of environmental pollution vary from natural causes such as volcanic emissions to human actions, including industrialisation, transportation, energy production and agricultural practices. (3)___________ of these activities, pollutants are released into the air, water bodies and soil leading to harmful effects such as respiratory diseases, loss of biodiversity and climate change. One of the primary causes of environmental pollution is human attitudes towards sustainability (4)_______ their lack of environmental awareness. Human activities that harm the environment and ecosystem often result from individual choices (5)_______ driving or using single-use plastics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'And' joins the two causes: attitudes towards sustainability and lack of environmental awareness.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Environmental pollution is a growing (1)________ all around the world as it poses significant risks to human health and ecosystems. The (2)________ of environmental pollution vary from natural causes such as volcanic emissions to human actions, including industrialisation, transportation, energy production and agricultural practices. (3)___________ of these activities, pollutants are released into the air, water bodies and soil leading to harmful effects such as respiratory diseases, loss of biodiversity and climate change. One of the primary causes of environmental pollution is human attitudes towards sustainability (4)_______ their lack of environmental awareness. Human activities that harm the environment and ecosystem often result from individual choices (5)_______ driving or using single-use plastics.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Like' introduces examples: 'individual choices like driving'; 'example' and 'instance' would need 'for'.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: What does the term ‘interest’ refer to in banking?
options: The additional amount earned on a loan or deposit
The amount of money deposited into a bank account
The value of a currency in relation to other currencies
The fee charged for withdrawing money from an ATM
questions.explanation: Interest is the extra amount, over and above the principal, that a lender earns on a loan or a depositor on a deposit; for the borrower it is the cost of borrowing.

questions.text: Bihu is a folk dance of which state?
questions.explanation: Bihu, danced at the Bihu festivals and above all at Rongali (Bohag) Bihu in April, is the folk dance of Assam.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year did Lord Curzon announce the partition of Bengal during the British rule in India?
questions.explanation: Curzon's government announced the partition of Bengal in July 1905, and it took effect on 16 October 1905. It was annulled in 1911.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding the Power Sector’s Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme? 1) The Prime Minister launched the Ministry of Power’s flagship Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme in 2022. 2) This scheme is aimed at improving the operational efficiencies and financial sustainability of distribution companies. 3) From FY 2022-23 to FY 2027-28, the scheme aims to provide financial assistance to DISCOMs. 4)This scheme proposes to provide 25 crore Smart Prepaid meters to consumers all over the country.
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister launched the scheme on 30 July 2022 (1); it aims at the operational efficiency and financial sustainability of the distribution companies (2) and plans about 25 crore smart prepaid meters for consumers (4). Statement 3 is wrong: as approved in 2021, and as it stood when the exam was held (September 2023), the scheme was to run for five years, FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26.

questions.text: ‘Mein Kampf’ is the autobiography of which world personality?
questions.explanation: 'Mein Kampf' ('My Struggle'), published in two volumes in 1925 and 1926, is Adolf Hitler's autobiography and political manifesto.

questions.text: What is the geographic location of the world's largest coral reef, known as the Great Barrier Reef?
questions.explanation: The Great Barrier Reef lies in the Coral Sea off the coast of Queensland, Australia.

questions.text: Popular since ancient eras for the trading of livestock, ___________, which is a month-long event, takes place on the auspicious occasion of Kartik Purnima in the month of November near Harihar Nath temple.
questions.explanation: The Harihar Nath temple places it at Sonepur in Bihar, where the Gandak meets the Ganga: the Sonepur Mela, a livestock fair that begins on Kartik Purnima. The Pushkar fair, also held at Kartik Purnima, is in Rajasthan.

questions.text: How many states were selected in Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan (GKRA) 2020?
questions.explanation: The Garib Kalyan Rojgar Abhiyaan, a 125-day public works campaign launched on 20 June 2020 for migrant workers who had returned home, covered 116 districts in six states: Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Jharkhand and Odisha.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a part of the six communication mail channels in India?
questions.explanation: India Post's six mail channels, introduced for quicker delivery in large towns and cities, are the Rajdhani, Metro, Green, Business, Bulk Mail and Periodical channels. There is no 'Monthly' channel.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a non-debt capital receipt in the government budget?
questions.explanation: A non-debt capital receipt brings in money without creating a liability, as the sale of government assets such as land does. Loans are debt receipts, interest paid is expenditure, and taxes are revenue receipts.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Visva Bharati a famous educational institute was founded in 1921 by:
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore founded Visva-Bharati at Santiniketan in 1921; it became a central university in 1951.

questions.text: How many women boxers from India won gold medals in the Women's World Boxing Championship 2023?
questions.explanation: India won four golds at the Women's World Boxing Championships held in New Delhi in March 2023: Nitu Ghanghas (48 kg), Nikhat Zareen (50 kg), Lovlina Borgohain (75 kg) and Saweety Boora (81 kg).

questions.text: Famous Bollywood actress Hema Malini is a trained ______ dancer.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Bharatanatyam, the classical dance Hema Malini learnt from childhood and is best known for. She later also studied other forms, Kuchipudi under Vempati Chinna Satyam among them, so those options are arguable, but Bharatanatyam is her principal form.

questions.text: Whose prior recommendation is required to introduce money bills in state legislature?
questions.explanation: Under Article 207(1), a Money Bill may be introduced in a state legislature only on the recommendation of the Governor.

questions.text: RK Narayan is the author of _____________.
questions.explanation: R. K. Narayan wrote 'The Guide' (1958). 'Far From the Madding Crowd' is Thomas Hardy's, 'Godan' Premchand's and 'Untouchable' Mulk Raj Anand's.

questions.text: Where is the Qutub Minar situated?
questions.explanation: The Qutub Minar stands at Mehrauli in Delhi; Qutb-ud-din Aibak began it and Iltutmish completed it.

questions.text: Which is the most obvious symptom of infantile jaundice that usually appears between the second and fourth day after birth?
options: Cracking and irritation at the corners of mouth
Yellowing of the skin and the whites of the eyes
Swelling and bleeding of the gums
questions.explanation: Newborn jaundice comes from a build-up of bilirubin and shows as yellowing of the skin and the whites of the eyes. Cracks at the corners of the mouth point to a riboflavin deficiency, and swollen, bleeding gums to scurvy.

questions.text: The Units of Linear momentum are measured in _______.
questions.explanation: Linear momentum = mass × velocity, so its SI unit is kg m/s. (kg m/s² is the unit of force, the newton.)

questions.text: In which of the following cities the 2023 SAFF Championship was held?
questions.explanation: The 2023 SAFF Championship was played at the Sree Kanteerava Stadium in Bengaluru in June and July 2023; India beat Kuwait on penalties in the final on 4 July for their ninth title.

questions.text: Mirabai Chanu was selected as BBC Indian Sportswoman of the Year 2022. She is related to which sport?
questions.explanation: Saikhom Mirabai Chanu, the Tokyo Olympics silver medallist in the women's 49 kg class, is a weightlifter. She won the BBC award for 2021 and again for 2022, the first to win it twice.

questions.text: Punjab state is rich in which natural resource from the following?
questions.explanation: Punjab's plains are made of fertile alluvial soil laid down by its rivers, which with irrigation make it one of India's leading wheat and rice producers.

questions.text: How many schedules are there in our Constitution as of June 2023?
questions.explanation: The Constitution had 12 Schedules in June 2023. It began with 8; the 9th was added in 1951, the 10th in 1985 and the 11th and 12th in 1992.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Diminish
questions.explanation: To 'diminish' is to make or become less: 'weaken'. To 'demote' or 'relegate' is to lower in rank, and to 'prevent' is to stop.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error. (A) We are living / (B) here since / (C) the summer / (D) of last year.
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and is still going on, with 'since', takes the present perfect continuous: 'We have been living here since the summer of last year.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Suresh has been learning Tamil ________ two months.
questions.explanation: 'For' goes with a period of time ('for two months'); 'since' goes with a point of time ('since May').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. Rina’s house is at “a stone’s throw” from the school.
questions.explanation: 'A stone's throw' is a very short distance: the house is close to the school.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'accompaniment': the 'y' of 'accompany' becomes 'i' before '-ment'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Mohan unknowingly “altered salt instead of sugar” to the dessert making it taste terrible.
questions.explanation: Salt is 'added' to a dish: 'added salt instead of sugar'. 'Altered' (changed) does not fit, nor do 'anguished', 'amplified' or 'abridged'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The actor decided to live life “in the fast lane”.
questions.explanation: To live 'in the fast lane' is to lead an exciting, hectic and often risky life; it is not about actual speed.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Sanjana rubbed her eyes hardly.
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' means scarcely; the adverb meaning 'with force' is 'hard': 'Sanjana rubbed her eyes hard.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. I asked my friend to ___________________ against her employers who are doing wrong to her.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'fight fire with fire', to answer an opponent with the same kind of methods, which matches employers 'doing wrong to her'. 'Fight the good fight' (to keep striving for what is right) could also be read into the sentence, but it is about persevering in a just cause rather than hitting back at a wrongdoer; the other two idioms do not fit.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains a misspelt word. The single most important factor that “distinguishes” those of us who “succed” in any “venture” and those of us who don’t is this ‘instant coffee’ “attitude.”
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'succeed', with a double 'e'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. A night alone / in a hotel / can be lonely prospect.
questions.explanation: 'Prospect' is a singular countable noun and needs an article: 'can be a lonely prospect'.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. The “new restaurant” “on Main Street” “is cheap than” “the old one.”
questions.explanation: A comparison with 'than' needs the comparative degree: 'is cheaper than the old one'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. “My” relatives “shall” have “reached” Amritsar “by now.”
questions.explanation: A confident guess about something already done takes 'must have' (or 'will have'): 'My relatives must have reached Amritsar by now.' 'Shall' is not used for such a guess about a third person.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Group of bees
questions.explanation: A group of bees is a 'swarm'; a 'gaggle' is of geese, a 'shoal' of fish and a 'pack' of wolves or dogs.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Crude
questions.explanation: 'Crude' means rough and unpolished; its opposite is 'refined'. 'Primitive' is close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Can you quote any _______ in your favour?
questions.explanation: A 'precedent' is an earlier case or example that can be quoted in support of a claim, as in law.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined segment in the given sentence. Buying a new car can “cost an arm and a leg”.
questions.explanation: To 'cost an arm and a leg' is to be very expensive.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Insist
questions.explanation: To 'insist' is to keep demanding or maintaining something firmly, close to 'persist'. To 'resist' is to oppose, to 'assist' to help, and a 'heist' is a robbery.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There are several reasons why people might 1)_________ that homework is an unnecessary burden on children. Firstly, there is evidence to support the idea that homework 2)_________nothing to improve educational outcomes. Countries such as Finland, where school children are not given homework, regularly top international educational league tables and outperform nations where setting homework is the norm. Secondly, many parents would agree that the school day is already 3)_________, and leaves their children too tired to do further study when they return home. 4)_________, it is recognised that play time is just as 5)_________as study time from the perspective of brain development.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 1.
questions.explanation: After the modal 'might' comes the bare infinitive: 'people might argue'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There are several reasons why people might 1)_________ that homework is an unnecessary burden on children. Firstly, there is evidence to support the idea that homework 2)_________nothing to improve educational outcomes. Countries such as Finland, where school children are not given homework, regularly top international educational league tables and outperform nations where setting homework is the norm. Secondly, many parents would agree that the school day is already 3)_________, and leaves their children too tired to do further study when they return home. 4)_________, it is recognised that play time is just as 5)_________as study time from the perspective of brain development.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 2.
questions.explanation: 'Homework' is an uncountable, singular subject and the sentence states a general fact, so the simple present: 'homework does nothing to improve educational outcomes'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There are several reasons why people might 1)_________ that homework is an unnecessary burden on children. Firstly, there is evidence to support the idea that homework 2)_________nothing to improve educational outcomes. Countries such as Finland, where school children are not given homework, regularly top international educational league tables and outperform nations where setting homework is the norm. Secondly, many parents would agree that the school day is already 3)_________, and leaves their children too tired to do further study when they return home. 4)_________, it is recognised that play time is just as 5)_________as study time from the perspective of brain development.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 3.
questions.explanation: The parents' point is that the school day already takes up enough time and leaves children tired: 'already long enough'. 'Big enough' does not describe a length of time, and 'not enough' contradicts the reason.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There are several reasons why people might 1)_________ that homework is an unnecessary burden on children. Firstly, there is evidence to support the idea that homework 2)_________nothing to improve educational outcomes. Countries such as Finland, where school children are not given homework, regularly top international educational league tables and outperform nations where setting homework is the norm. Secondly, many parents would agree that the school day is already 3)_________, and leaves their children too tired to do further study when they return home. 4)_________, it is recognised that play time is just as 5)_________as study time from the perspective of brain development.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 4.
questions.explanation: After 'Firstly' and 'Secondly', 'Finally' introduces the last reason.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. There are several reasons why people might 1)_________ that homework is an unnecessary burden on children. Firstly, there is evidence to support the idea that homework 2)_________nothing to improve educational outcomes. Countries such as Finland, where school children are not given homework, regularly top international educational league tables and outperform nations where setting homework is the norm. Secondly, many parents would agree that the school day is already 3)_________, and leaves their children too tired to do further study when they return home. 4)_________, it is recognised that play time is just as 5)_________as study time from the perspective of brain development.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank 5.
questions.explanation: Play time is 'just as beneficial as' study time for brain development, which supports the case against homework; 'bad' would contradict it.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Which physiographic division of India from the following is formed of alluvial soil?
questions.explanation: The Northern Plains were built up from the alluvium laid down by the Indus, the Ganga and the Brahmaputra and their tributaries.

questions.text: Laterite soil develops as a result of which of the following reasons?
questions.explanation: Laterite soil forms where high temperature and heavy rainfall go together: the rain leaches away lime and silica, leaving a soil rich in iron oxide and aluminium compounds. Heat alone does not make it.

questions.text: As per the Census of India 2011, which state recorded a negative population growth rate?
questions.explanation: Nagaland was the only state whose population fell between the 2001 and 2011 censuses: its decadal growth was −0.58%.

questions.text: In March 2023, Rajasthan became the first state in India to provide right to ___ for its people.
questions.explanation: In March 2023 the Rajasthan Assembly passed the Rajasthan Right to Health Care Bill, making Rajasthan the first state to give its residents a legal right to health care.

questions.text: Which state has the maximum number of Jute mills (as of 2022)?
questions.explanation: In 2022 West Bengal had by far the largest share of India's jute mills, mostly along the Hooghly near Kolkata, close to the jute-growing areas of the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Born on ____________, Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi whose birthday is celebrated as Gandhi Jayanti, successfully led India’s non-violence movement against the British.
questions.explanation: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi was born at Porbandar, in present-day Gujarat, on 2 October 1869.

questions.text: Which of the following is a white to yellowish solid with a weak aromatic odour purified by the process of sublimation?
questions.explanation: Anthracene, a coal-tar hydrocarbon with three fused benzene rings, is a white to pale yellow crystalline solid that sublimes on heating, so it is purified by sublimation. Titanyl and orthovanadate are ions, and dysprosium is a rare-earth metal.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a spelling error. Several days later, / he received a written / comeunication from the magistrate / that the case has been dropped.
options: that the case has been dropped
questions.explanation: 'Comeunication' is misspelt: the word is 'communication'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A man whose wife is dead
questions.explanation: A 'widower' is a man whose wife has died; a 'widow' is a woman whose husband has died.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. “No sooner did he finished” his examination than he left for his cricket training centre.
options: no sooner than he did finished
questions.explanation: 'Did' takes the base form of the verb: 'No sooner did he finish his examination than he left'. ('No sooner had he finished' would also be correct, but 'had he finish' pairs 'had' with the base form.)

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. They will start their journey after the breakfast.
questions.explanation: The names of meals used in a general sense take no article: 'after breakfast'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Legandry' is misspelt: the word is 'legendary'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Humane
questions.explanation: 'Humane' means kind and compassionate; its opposite is 'cruel'. 'Kind' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'prevention'.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. One of them contains an error. The underlined parts are given as options with some changes. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. He “is good” “at playing” “the guitar” “than” his brother.
questions.explanation: 'Than' needs the comparative: 'He is better at playing the guitar than his brother.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. The company is looking for some ______________(idle) workers who can join the organisation immediately.
questions.explanation: 'Idle' means lazy or not working; its opposite is 'diligent', hard-working.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. He simply continued to “say something in order to convey information” in a calm voice.
questions.explanation: To 'speak' is to say something in order to convey information or express a feeling. To 'dictate' is to say words aloud for someone else to write down.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. After years of rivalry, the two families decided to “bury the hatchet.”
options: To end a quarrel by never talking to each other
To end a quarrel and become friendly
questions.explanation: To 'bury the hatchet' is to end a quarrel and make peace.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. Did / her friend / went to / school yesterday?
questions.explanation: In a question formed with 'did', the main verb takes its base form: 'Did her friend go to school yesterday?'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The Delhi administration is seriously worried about “the warning to civic health” posed by the polluted waters of Yamuna.
questions.explanation: A danger is 'posed', and the noun that goes with 'pose' is 'threat': 'the threat to civic health posed by the polluted waters'. A warning only tells of a danger; 'peril' is close in meaning but does not pair with 'posed' as naturally.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Mohan is respected / by everyone / because he works / hardly.
questions.explanation: The adverb of 'hard' is 'hard': 'he works hard'. 'Hardly' means scarcely, the opposite of what is meant.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Day and night
questions.explanation: 'Day and night' means all the time, continuously: 'They worked day and night to finish the bridge.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Humility
questions.explanation: 'Humility' is a modest view of one's own importance; its opposite is 'arrogance'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. They had been dancing / for an hour / when our dance teacher / had arrived.
questions.explanation: 'Had been dancing' already marks the earlier action, so the action that came after takes the simple past: 'when our dance teacher arrived'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. Jane, please don’t tell me fairy tales; I just want to know the real matter ________.
questions.explanation: 'In a nutshell' means briefly, in a few words, which is what Jane asks for instead of long stories.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The shopkeeper was “sly as a fox” and tried to sell off the old stock.
questions.explanation: '(As) sly as a fox' describes someone cunning and crafty; of the options only 'smart and clever' fits.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Bhanu, the security guard, asks everyone entering my building to show their ________ card.
questions.explanation: An 'identity card' shows who its holder is, which is what a security guard checks at the entrance.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Effective communication is about more than just exchanging information. It's about understanding the emotion and intentions (1)_____ the information. As well as being able to clearly convey a message, you need to also (2)____ in a way that gains the full meaning of what's being said and makes the other person feel heard and understood. For many of us, communicating more clearly and effectively requires learning some (3)_____ skills. Whether you’re trying to improve communication with your spouse, kids, boss, or coworkers, learning these skills can (4)______ your connections to others, build greater trust and respect, and (5)______ teamwork, problem solving, and your overall social and emotional health.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The emotion and intentions 'behind' the information are what lie under it and give rise to it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Effective communication is about more than just exchanging information. It's about understanding the emotion and intentions (1)_____ the information. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Besides conveying a message clearly, one must 'listen' so as to take in the full meaning of what is said and make the speaker feel heard.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The passage recommends learning these skills, so they are 'important' ones; 'boring', 'trivial' and 'wasteful' would undercut it.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The skills strengthen relationships, in line with 'build greater trust and respect': they 'deepen' your connections to others. 'Hamper' and 'disturb' say the opposite.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The sentence lists benefits, so the skills 'improve' teamwork, problem solving and health; 'hasten' does not fit teamwork or health.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: How many elements are listed in the modern periodic table?
questions.explanation: The modern periodic table lists 118 elements, up to oganesson (atomic number 118); the last four were named in 2016.

questions.text: In which of the following States was the third edition of Khelo India University Games held?
questions.explanation: The third Khelo India University Games were held in Uttar Pradesh in May-June 2023, with Lucknow and Varanasi among the host cities.

questions.text: Which country did India beat in the final to win the 2023 Intercontinental Cup Football championship?
questions.explanation: India beat Lebanon 2-0 in the final of the 2023 Intercontinental Cup at Bhubaneswar in June 2023.

questions.text: In which state of India is shifting cultivation known as Bringa?
questions.explanation: Shifting (slash-and-burn) cultivation is called 'Pama Dabi', 'Koman' or 'Bringa' in Odisha, 'Podu' in Andhra Pradesh, 'Bewar' or 'Dahiya' in Madhya Pradesh and 'Jhum' in the north-east.

questions.text: What does the acronym ‘ATM’ stand for?
questions.explanation: ATM stands for Automated Teller Machine, which lets a bank's customers withdraw cash and check balances without a bank clerk.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who had founded the first Women’s University in India?
questions.explanation: Dhondo Keshav Karve founded India's first women's university, the Indian Women's University (now SNDT Women's University), in Pune in 1916.

questions.text: Devendra Jhajharia won which medal/place in World Para Athletics Grand Prix?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives silver: at the World Para Athletics Grand Prix in Morocco in September 2022 Jhajharia took silver in the men's F46 javelin with 60.97 m, behind Ajeet Singh. The question does not name the meeting.

questions.text: In the process of cell division, the formation of phragmoplast between the two daughter nuclei occurs during:
questions.explanation: The phragmoplast forms in a dividing plant cell during cytokinesis, the division of the cytoplasm; it guides the building of the cell plate between the two daughter nuclei.

questions.text: In which type of forests are Mahogany, Rosewood and Cinchona trees found in India?
questions.explanation: Ebony, mahogany, rosewood, rubber and cinchona are the commercially important trees of India's tropical evergreen forests.

questions.text: Lebang Boomani dance is the harvest dance of ____________.
questions.explanation: Lebang Boomani is a harvest dance of the Tripuri people of Tripura.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a directive principle of state policy?
options: Separation of the judiciary from executive
Reside in any part of India
questions.explanation: The right to reside and settle in any part of India is a Fundamental Right, Article 19(1)(e). A uniform civil code (Article 44), protection of monuments (Article 49) and separation of the judiciary from the executive (Article 50) are Directive Principles.

questions.text: In which state is the Sanchi Stupa situated?
questions.explanation: The Great Stupa at Sanchi, begun under Asoka in the 3rd century BC, stands in Raisen district, Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the book, ‘Unfinished: A Memoir’?
questions.explanation: 'Unfinished: A Memoir' (2021) is the actor Priyanka Chopra Jonas's memoir.

questions.text: The official language of which neighbouring country of India is ‘Dhivehi'?
questions.explanation: Dhivehi is the official language of the Maldives.

questions.text: Under which scheme of Airport Authority of India did the Jammu and Kashmir Lieutenant Governor inaugurate UMEED Market Place at Srinagar international airport for supporting local art and artisans of Self Help Groups of J&K Rural Livelihood Mission?
questions.explanation: The UMEED Market Place at Srinagar airport, opened by Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha in August 2022, came under the Airports Authority of India's AVSAR scheme (Airport as Venue for Skilled Artisans of the Region), which gives artisans and Self Help Groups space at airports to sell their products.

questions.text: Who was the Iranian ruler who attacked the city of Delhi and took away an immense amount of wealth in 1739?
questions.explanation: Nadir Shah of Persia sacked Delhi in 1739, in Muhammad Shah's reign, and carried away immense wealth, including the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor.

questions.text: Mahari Dance and Gotipua Dance belongs to which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Both are dances of Odisha: Mahari was danced by the devadasis of the Jagannath temple at Puri, and in Gotipua young boys dressed as girls perform; both fed into Odissi.

questions.text: Which of the following musicians is popularly known as ‘Panchamda’?
questions.explanation: The film composer Rahul Dev (R. D.) Burman, son of S. D. Burman, was known as 'Pancham' or 'Panchamda'.

questions.text: The ‘Mukteshwar’ dance festival is held from 14th to 16th January at the Mukteshwar temple in the state of ___________.
questions.explanation: The Mukteswar Dance Festival, mainly of Odissi, is held every January at the 10th-century Mukteswar temple in Bhubaneswar, Odisha.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. “For an all-too-brief” period “between the late” 1980s and the late 2000s, “a world was” “characterised by” convergence.
questions.explanation: There is only one world, so it takes the definite article: 'the world was characterised by convergence'.

questions.text: The sentence given below has spelling errors. Select the sentence without spelling errors. Let us appriciate, support and contribute our might to the promotional efforts of the community in this direction.
options: Let us appriciate, support and contribute our might to the promotional efforts of the comunity in this direction.
Let us appreciate, suport and contribute our might to the promotional efforts of the community in this direction.
Let us appriciate, support and contribute our might to the promotion all efforts of the community in this direction.
Let us appreciate, support and contribute our might to the promotional efforts of the community in this direction.
questions.explanation: Only this sentence spells 'appreciate', 'support', 'promotional' and 'community' correctly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The team had a _________ with respect to the proposal given by Mr. Albert.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'discussion'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A thing which happens every two years
questions.explanation: 'Biennial' means happening every two years; 'annual' is every year, and 'bi-monthly' every two months or twice a month.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the following sentence. Ramya’s shoes “are polish” by her granddaughter.
questions.explanation: The passive takes 'be' with the past participle: 'Ramya's shoes are polished by her granddaughter.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. I don’t think you should go out in the rain, it's ________.
questions.explanation: It is 'raining cats and dogs' when it is raining very heavily.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To keep one’s temper
questions.explanation: To 'keep one's temper' is to stay calm and not become angry.

questions.text: Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the following sentence. Today’s lecture had a “profond” impact on my friend.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'profound'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To get cold feet
questions.explanation: To 'get cold feet' is to become nervous or afraid about something one had planned to do.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. His “amazing” performance made him famous.
questions.explanation: 'Amazing' means causing great surprise or wonder; its opposite is 'ordinary'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The food was too salty “eat” this morning.
questions.explanation: 'Too' with an adjective is followed by the to-infinitive: 'too salty to eat'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Elegant
questions.explanation: 'Elegant' means stylish and refined in manner or appearance: 'graceful'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I “will going” “on” “an official tour” “next week.”
questions.explanation: 'Will' takes the bare infinitive, so 'will going' should be 'will be going' (or 'will go').

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Shelley and Keats are great writers, but I prefer the last.
questions.explanation: Of two persons the second is 'the latter', not 'the last': 'but I prefer the latter'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Design
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'fabricate': to 'design' is to devise or plan how something is to be made, and 'fabricate' (to devise, construct or make) is the only option close to it; 'destroy' is nearly the opposite, and 'inspect' and 'copy' do not mean this.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase. A person who is known for his hatred towards the entire mankind.
questions.explanation: A 'misanthrope' dislikes humankind in general; a philogynist loves women and an insolvent cannot pay their debts.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Jaya said that she will become topper in her class.
questions.explanation: After the past reporting verb 'said', 'will' becomes 'would', and 'topper' needs the article: 'she would become the topper in her class'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Some / private banks / pay their employees / good.
questions.explanation: The verb 'pay' is modified by the adverb 'well', not the adjective 'good': 'pay their employees well'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Break the ice
options: To say something that makes strangers uncomfortable
To say something that makes people who are meeting for the first time more comfortable
To say something that makes people excited for a group project
To say something mean to people in a group
questions.explanation: To 'break the ice' is to say or do something that relaxes people meeting for the first time.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given phrase. A poem of lamentation on the death of someone loved and admired.
questions.explanation: An 'elegy' is a poem of mourning for someone who has died; an epitaph is the inscription on a tomb, and a soliloquy a speech to oneself.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Language is (1)_______ of the most fundamental aspects of human communication and interaction. It allows people from different cultures to connect and (2) _______ ideas. While many individuals grow up learning just one language, there are a variety of reasons why learning a second language can be beneficial. (3) _________, it can improve cognitive abilities, enhance job prospects and facilitate travel and cultural immersion. (4)________ proficiency in a second language is an invaluable asset for personal growth as well as professional development. Audio-video mediums such as (5)_______ are among the best ways to learn a second language as they allow learners to engage with cultural content.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Language is a single subject ('is'), so it is 'one of the most fundamental aspects'; 'two', 'three' or 'four' of them cannot describe one thing.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. (4)________ proficiency in a second language is an invaluable asset for personal growth as well as professional development. Audio-video mediums such as (5)_______ are among the best ways to learn a second language as they allow learners to engage with cultural content.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Share' is joined by 'and' to 'connect', so it takes the same base form after 'to': 'to connect and share ideas'.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The sentence goes on to list the benefits of a second language, so it is introduced by 'For example'.

questions.explanation: The subject of the sentence is the gerund phrase 'Acquiring proficiency in a second language'.

Language is (1)_______ of the most fundamental aspects of human communication and interaction. It allows people from different cultures to connect and (2) _______ ideas. While many individuals grow up learning just one language, there are a variety of reasons why learning a second language can be beneficial. (3) _________, it can improve cognitive abilities, enhance job prospects and facilitate travel and cultural immersion.
