Audio-video mediums such as (5)_______ are among the best ways to learn a second language as they allow learners to engage with cultural content.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Films have both sound and pictures, so they are audio-video mediums; podcasts are sound only, and books and images have no sound.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: Six people, Karan, Dilip, Rahul, Prabhat, Alok and Sandeep are sitting in a straight line, facing north. Karan sits 2nd from the left end. Dilip sits 3rd to the right of Karan. Rahul sits 2nd to the left of Dilip. Prabhat sits 3rd to the right of Rahul. Sandeep sits 2nd to the left of Prabhat. Who sits 2nd to the right of Karan?
questions.explanation: Karan is 2nd from the left, Dilip 5th, Rahul 3rd, Prabhat 6th and Sandeep 4th, leaving Alok 1st. From the left: Alok, Karan, Rahul, Sandeep, Dilip, Prabhat, so Sandeep sits second to Karan's right.

questions.text: The Padma Shri awardee Guru K Kalyanasundaram Pillai, the man who is keeping an ancient tradition alive,was awarded the Padma Shri 2023 for his contribution to the field of ____________.
questions.explanation: K. Kalyanasundaram Pillai, a Bharatanatyam guru of the Thanjavur tradition, received the Padma Shri in 2023 for his work in Bharatanatyam.

questions.text: Who appoints the State Election Commissioner?
questions.explanation: Under Article 243K the State Election Commissioner, who conducts panchayat elections, is appointed by the Governor.

questions.text: In which river has the National Waterways-2 (NW-2) been developed in India?
questions.explanation: National Waterway 2 is the Sadiya-Dhubri stretch of the Brahmaputra in Assam, about 891 km long.

questions.text: In India, Micro Finance Institutions primarily target which segment of the population?
questions.explanation: Microfinance institutions give small loans and other financial services to low-income households and small businesses that ordinary banks often do not reach.

questions.text: What is the name of the scheme launched by Himachal Pradesh government for dairy farmers?
questions.explanation: In April 2023 Himachal Pradesh's Animal Husbandry Department started 'Sanjeevani', with Bharat Financial Inclusion Ltd (a subsidiary of IndusInd Bank), to give small dairy farmers veterinary care for their livestock at their doorstep.

questions.text: Which of the following States will host the 37th National Games?
questions.explanation: Goa hosted the 37th National Games in October-November 2023, after Gujarat had hosted the 36th in 2022.

questions.text: Kalidas Samman is a prestigious arts award presented annually by the government of ________.
questions.explanation: The Kalidas Samman, named after the Sanskrit poet Kalidasa, has been given by the Government of Madhya Pradesh since 1980 for excellence in the arts.

questions.text: How many countries will participate in ICC 2023 ODI Cricket World Cup?
questions.explanation: Ten teams took part in the 2023 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup, held in India in October-November 2023.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of money?
questions.explanation: Money must be durable, portable and divisible to serve as a medium of exchange and a store of value; something perishable would lose its value as it decayed.

questions.text: ____________ has two traditions: one is the sankeertana (which is the devotional aspect) and the other is the raasa.
questions.explanation: Manipuri dance has two traditions: the Sankirtana, its devotional singing and drumming, and the Raas, the Ras Lila of Radha and Krishna.

questions.text: Which of the following lakes is a saltwater lake ?
questions.explanation: Chilika, on the Odisha coast, is a brackish-water lagoon, the largest in Asia. Superior, Malawi and Titicaca are freshwater lakes.

questions.text: The _______________ of the Indian Constitution defines the Fundamental Duties of Indian Citizens.
questions.explanation: Article 51A, in Part IVA, added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, lists the Fundamental Duties of citizens.

questions.text: What type of vegetation is represented by Sundarbans, the world's largest delta located in the Bay of Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans, in the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta, are the largest mangrove forest in the world; mangroves grow in the tidal, salty swamps of coasts and deltas.

questions.text: The Mumbai High region in Arabian Sea is known for mining ________.
questions.explanation: Mumbai High, an offshore field in the Arabian Sea off the Mumbai coast discovered in 1974, produces petroleum (mineral oil) and natural gas.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which of the following years was the Child Marriage Restraint Act passed?
questions.explanation: The Child Marriage Restraint Act (the Sarda Act), moved by Har Bilas Sarda, was passed in 1929 and came into force in 1930.

questions.text: According to the Census of India 2011, identify the correct pair of State and Union Territories which recorded the highest literacy rate.
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Kerala had the highest literacy rate among the states (about 94%) and Lakshadweep among the Union territories (about 92%).

questions.text: The sal tree assumes great significance in a number of tribal communities scattered across eastern India. For instance, ________ festival is celebrated in honour of the tree in Jharkhand.
questions.explanation: Sarhul, the spring festival of Jharkhand's tribes such as the Oraon and the Munda, worships the sal tree when it blossoms. Karma honours the karam tree.

questions.text: Geto Sora won the Arena Junior (Boys) International Badminton Championship. He belongs to which state?
questions.explanation: Geto Sora, a child badminton player from Arunachal Pradesh, won the under-9 boys' singles title at this junior international championship in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, in December 2022.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian musicians was referred to as ‘Ghazal King’?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Jagjit Singh, the Indian singer widely called the 'Ghazal King' for bringing the ghazal to a mass audience. Mehdi Hassan, also hailed as the king of the ghazal, was Pakistani, as is Ghulam Ali.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: On 8th April 1929, who among the following two revolutionists threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly?
options: Bhagat Singh and Ram Prasad Bismil
questions.explanation: On 8 April 1929 Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw bombs, meant to make a noise rather than kill, into the Central Legislative Assembly in Delhi in protest against the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill, and courted arrest.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. To go away suddenly and secretly in order to escape from somewhere
questions.explanation: To 'abscond' is to leave secretly and in a hurry, usually to escape arrest or a duty. 'Vanish' lacks the sense of escape, and 'extradite' is to hand someone over to another country.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. My friend’s business has grown “by leaps and bounds”.
questions.explanation: To grow 'by leaps and bounds' is to grow very quickly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Peer pressure is bound “to effect most of us” both positively and negatively.
questions.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to influence; as a verb, 'effect' means to bring about: 'bound to affect most of us'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Peculiar
questions.explanation: 'Peculiar' means odd or unusual: 'strange'.

questions.text: Select the sentence that has NO spelling errors.
options: The teacher was impressed with the student’s insightfull analysis of the novel, which demonstrated a deep understanding of the complex theames and motifs.
The teacher was impressed with the student’s insightful analysis of the novel, which demonstrated a deep understanding of the complex themes and motifs.
The teacher was imprresed with the student’s insightul analysis of the novel, which demonstrated a deep understanding of the complex themes and motifes.
The teacher was impresed with the student’s insightful analysis of the novel, which demonstreted a deep understanding of the complex themes and motifs.
questions.explanation: Only this sentence spells every word correctly. The others have 'insightfull' and 'theames', 'imprresed', 'insightul' and 'motifes', or 'impresed' and 'demonstreted'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'writing', with one t.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. Tim joined the family business as he failed in his final degree examination. Seeing the growth of the family business now, it seems like Tim’s earlier failure was “a blessing in disguise”.
options: Something good that isn't recognised at first
questions.explanation: A 'blessing in disguise' is something that seems unfortunate at first but turns out well, as Tim's failure did.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error and select the option which rectifies that error. AI fiction is a constantly / evolving genre that gives us an peek / into the potential upsides and downsides / of intelligent machines.
options: into a potential upside and downside
evolving genre that gives us a peek
questions.explanation: 'Peek' begins with a consonant sound, so it takes 'a', not 'an': 'gives us a peek'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. “If he” “will come” early, “we will” leave “on time”.
questions.explanation: In a first conditional the if-clause takes the simple present, not 'will': 'If he comes early, we will leave on time.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence. I ordered a dozen doughnuts, but the kind baker gave me “a baker’s dozen”.
questions.explanation: A 'baker's dozen' is thirteen: bakers traditionally added one extra item to a dozen.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. They “had two” “bedrooms among” “them, one for” the “girls and one” for the boys.
questions.explanation: Something shared out by two parties takes 'between': the rooms were divided between the girls and the boys, 'two bedrooms between them'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Wisdom
questions.explanation: 'Wisdom' is good judgement; its opposite is 'stupidity'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Jack being the wiser and “bolder among” the two of us, took the lead, carrying the axe on his shoulder.
questions.explanation: Two people are compared, so the comparative 'bolder' stays, and 'among' (for more than two) gives way to 'between'. ('Of the two of us' is the more usual phrasing, but it is not offered.)

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. Many people fought to “put an end to” slavery during the civil war.
questions.explanation: To 'abolish' is to put an end to a system or practice officially, as slavery was abolished.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank. The doctor said that the patient named Rumi is in the ____________________(initial) stage of lung cancer.
questions.explanation: 'Initial' means at the beginning; its opposite is 'terminal', at the final stage. 'Early' means the same as 'initial'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He generally avoids arguments as he is _____ by nature.
questions.explanation: Someone who avoids arguments is 'peaceful' by nature.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. The pandemic has challenged “education systems to ensure learning” continuity, substantially increasing the demands placed on teachers.
questions.explanation: 'Challenge someone to do something' takes the infinitive, so 'education systems to ensure learning' is correct as it stands.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom from the given options to fill in the blank. We broke the traffic rules unknowingly while coming back from the party, now we have to ________ sooner or later.
questions.explanation: To 'face the music' is to accept the consequences of what one has done.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Guard over / making mistakes / by carefully checking / the assigned task.
questions.explanation: One guards 'against' a danger or mistake: 'Guard against making mistakes by carefully checking the assigned task.'

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. ________(1) university or college degree has long been the traditional hallmark of a ________ (2) candidate in the professional arena. While it historically provided the most widely accepted standard of qualification and skill for professionals, many companies today ________ (3) their hiring process and considering a broader list of criteria to judge a candidate’s ability. Organisations are reducing their reliance on college degrees as a sole marker of competence and instead placing greater emphasis ________ (4) the practical skills candidates have acquired through work experience. This shift in hiring is of particular relevance to India, which has the ________ (5) youth population in the world.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'University' begins with a consonant sound (yoo), so it takes 'a', not 'an'; the indefinite article speaks of any such degree in general.

questions.text:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. ________(1) university or college degree has long been the traditional hallmark of a ________ (2) candidate in the professional arena. While it historically provided the most widely accepted standard of qualification and skill for professionals, many companies today ________ (3) their hiring process and considering a broader list of criteria to judge a candidate’s ability. Organisations are reducing their reliance on college degrees as a sole marker of competence and instead placing greater emphasis ________ (4) the practical skills candidates have acquired through work experience. This shift in hiring is of particular relevance to India, which has the ________ (5) youth population in the world.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: An adjective is needed before 'candidate': 'a qualified candidate'.

questions.text:

Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. ________(1) university or college degree has long been the traditional hallmark of a ________ (2) candidate in the professional arena. Organisations are reducing their reliance on college degrees as a sole marker of competence and instead placing greater emphasis ________ (4) the practical skills candidates have acquired through work experience. This shift in hiring is of particular relevance to India, which has the ________ (5) youth population in the world.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'many companies' and the parallel 'and considering' call for the present continuous: 'are changing their hiring process'.

questions.explanation: One places emphasis 'on' something.

questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'largest': the size of a population is described with 'large', so 'the largest youth population'. ('Biggest' is also heard informally; 'longest' does not fit and 'most highest' is a double superlative.)

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: A sum invested at the rate of 6% simple interest per annum grows to ₹1,13,880 in 5 years. What is the simple interest, If the same amount is invested for 8 years at the rate of 9% per annum?
The Gua and Noamundi mines are located in with state of India?
questions.explanation: Gua and Noamundi are iron-ore mines in the West Singhbhum district of Jharkhand.

questions.text: What is a fiscal year?
options: A year that represents the financial reporting period for the government
A year with a surplus in government revenue
A year with a deficit in government revenue
A year in which tax rates are increased
questions.explanation: A fiscal year is the twelve-month accounting period a government uses for its budget and accounts; India's runs from 1 April to 31 March. It says nothing about a surplus, a deficit or tax rates.

questions.text: The Constitution (Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022, was passed in December 2022 and is related to which state?
questions.explanation: The bill, passed by the Rajya Sabha in December 2022 after the Lok Sabha, moved the Gond community in four districts of Uttar Pradesh (Chandauli, Kushinagar, Sant Kabir Nagar and Sant Ravidas Nagar) from the state's Scheduled Caste list to its Scheduled Tribe list.

questions.text: Buddha Purnima is marked on a full moon day in the Hindu month of ____________.
questions.explanation: Buddha Purnima falls on the full moon of Vaisakha (April-May) and marks the Buddha's birth, enlightenment and passing.

questions.text: Which of the following is the official language of Afghanistan?
questions.explanation: Dari (Afghan Persian) is, with Pashto, an official language of Afghanistan. Sinhala is Sri Lanka's language, Burmese Myanmar's and Dzongkha Bhutan's.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who started the temple entry movement in 1927?
questions.explanation: In 1927, the year of the Mahad satyagraha, B. R. Ambedkar began his campaigns against untouchability, among them the struggle for Dalits' right to enter Hindu temples.

questions.text: In which state is Gobind Sagar (Bhakra Nangal Project) located?
questions.explanation: Gobind Sagar, the reservoir formed by the Bhakra Dam on the Sutlej, lies in the Bilaspur and Una districts of Himachal Pradesh; the Nangal dam downstream is in Punjab.

questions.text: Pandit Ravi Shankar is known worldwide for playing which of the following musical instruments?
questions.explanation: Pandit Ravi Shankar was the sitar maestro who made Indian classical music known worldwide. The Mohan veena is Vishwa Mohan Bhatt's instrument and the sarod Amjad Ali Khan's.

questions.text: Which of the following is a dimension of microfinance institutions (MFIs) in India?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives outreach to rural areas: MFIs exist to take small loans and other financial services to low-income households that banks do not reach, many of them in villages, and they are usually judged by their outreach and their sustainability. Loan interest rates also figure in judging them, so the question is loosely worded.

questions.text: Shambhu Maharaj was a renowned guru of which of the following Gharanas of Kathak?
questions.explanation: Shambhu Maharaj, son of Kalka Prasad and brother of Achchan and Lachhu Maharaj, was a leading Kathak guru of the Lucknow gharana.

questions.text: Which is the oldest Stupa of the Buddhist Period?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Sanchi. Its Great Stupa was commissioned by Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE, and his brick stupa survives inside the stone casing added under the Shungas in the 2nd century BCE, making it one of the oldest stone structures in India. Sarnath and Kesariya may also have had stupas in Ashoka's time, but the Dhamek and Kesariya stupas that stand there now, like the Mahabodhi temple at Bodh Gaya, are of the Gupta period or later.

questions.text: Who conducts elections for both the houses of Parliament in India?
questions.explanation: Under Article 324 the Election Commission of India superintends, directs and controls elections to Parliament and the state legislatures, and to the offices of President and Vice-President.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The third battle of Panipat was fought in which of the following years?
questions.explanation: The Third Battle of Panipat, in which Ahmad Shah Abdali defeated the Marathas, was fought on 14 January 1761.

questions.text: Which dance form is associated with Natwari Dance?
questions.explanation: Natwari Nritya, the Krishna dance of the raslila of Brindavan (Natwar is a name of Krishna), is regarded as the old form from which Kathak grew.

questions.text: Birsa Munda hockey stadium is one of the India’s largest hockey stadium. In which state is this stadium situated?
questions.explanation: The Birsa Munda International Hockey Stadium, built for the 2023 men's Hockey World Cup, is at Rourkela in Odisha.

questions.text: The directive principles are largely classified into three broad categories. Which of the following is NOT the part of this classification?
questions.explanation: The Constitution does not classify them, but the Directive Principles are usually grouped as socialistic, Gandhian and liberal-intellectual. 'Authoritative' is not one of the groups.

questions.text: Which of the following countries did India defeat to clinch its maiden Women's Junior Hockey Asia Cup title?
questions.explanation: India won their first Women's Junior Hockey Asia Cup in June 2023 at Kakamigahara, Japan, beating South Korea 2-1 in the final.

questions.text: Which soft metal in group 1 of the periodic table tarnishes within a few seconds of exposure to air?
questions.explanation: Sodium is a soft alkali metal (group 1), easily cut with a knife, that tarnishes within seconds as it reacts with air. Barium and strontium are in group 2, and francium, though in group 1, is radioactive and too rare and short-lived to be seen in bulk.

questions.text: The ‘Ka Shad Mastieh’ or victory dance of the____________ tribe of Meghalaya is an ancient war dance performed during the prominent festival of the tribe.
questions.explanation: Ka Shad Mastieh is an ancient warrior dance of the Khasis of Meghalaya, in which the men dance with swords and stage a mock combat.

questions.text: What is the weight of the ball in handball for men?
questions.explanation: Under the IHF's rules the men's ball (size 3) is 58-60 cm in circumference and weighs 425-475 g; the women's ball (size 2) weighs 325-375 g.

questions.text: Which vitamin is needed for a healthy immune system, low-light vision, and healthy skin?
questions.explanation: Vitamin A is needed by the retina's rod cells to see in dim light, and for healthy skin and immunity; its lack causes night blindness.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Study of sound and sound waves
questions.explanation: 'Acoustics' is the branch of physics that deals with sound and sound waves; physics as a whole is much wider.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The students of class 7 gave their teacher a gift, which was ________ to her.
questions.explanation: An unexpected gift from the class would be 'surprising' to the teacher; 'shocking' suggests something bad, and 'revealing' and 'confusing' do not suit a gift.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Obsession
questions.explanation: An 'obsession' is an interest that fills the mind; 'fascination', an intense interest, is closest. 'Unconcern' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error and select the option which rectifies that error. A lot of adulterants / are chemicals that can lead / to an range of health problems / in both children and adults.
options: to a range of health problems
questions.explanation: 'Range' begins with a consonant sound, so it takes 'a': 'to a range of health problems'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. They would find someone “drive the” wagon back across the desert.
questions.explanation: 'Find someone' is followed by the to-infinitive, and 'wagon' keeps its article: 'find someone to drive the wagon back'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The ball / I kicked / went highly / in the sky.
questions.explanation: 'High' is the adverb of height or direction, while 'highly' means 'very' or 'greatly': the ball 'went high'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. Rajat is known for his notorious nature. He will be friendly to your face but likes ____________.
options: to stab you in the back
to paint the whole town red
to get all bent out of the shape
questions.explanation: To 'stab someone in the back' is to betray them while seeming friendly, as Rajat does.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Barking up the wrong tree
options: To make a bad situation worse
Getting a good start is important
To be mistaken, to be looking for solutions in the wrong place
questions.explanation: To be 'barking up the wrong tree' is to be mistaken about the cause or answer, pursuing the wrong line.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A creature which depends on others
questions.explanation: A 'parasite' is a creature that lives on another and depends on it; the other options name kinds of micro-organism.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. The play I saw last night was a ________.
questions.explanation: A 'smash hit' is a great success. To 'hit the road' is to set out, to 'hit the hay' to go to bed and to 'hit the roof' to become very angry.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He is _________ of many chain snatching cases in Dariyaganj.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'accused', charged with an offence.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Despite the setbacks and obstacles we faced, / our team rallied together and achieved our goals, / which teach us the importance of / teamwork, resilience, and determination.
options: Despite the setbacks and obstacles we faced,
which teach us the importance of
our team rallied together and achieved our goals,
questions.explanation: The sentence is in the past, and 'which' refers back to the whole achievement: 'which taught us the importance of'.

questions.text: Select the option that correctly rectifies the spelling error that is underlined. The “questionaire” used by the researcher was of top quality.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'questionnaire', with a double 'n'.

questions.text: The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. That career competition was the difficultest exam he had ever given.
options: That career competition was the difficultest exam than any he had ever given.
That career competition was the most difficult exam than any he had ever given.
That career competition was the most difficultest exam he had ever given.
That career competition was the most difficult exam he had ever given.
questions.explanation: 'Difficult' forms its superlative with 'most': 'the most difficult exam he had ever given'. A superlative is not followed by 'than any'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom for the following sentence. Shweta organises the sale of handmade pottery at a cheap rate.
options: Having one’s cake and eating it too
Making a fuss out of something
questions.explanation: Something that 'goes for a song' is sold very cheaply.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Guilty
questions.explanation: 'Guilty' means having done wrong; its opposite is 'innocent'.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence and select its correct spelling from the given options. The colours of the rainbow seemed to shine through the trianguler prism as the sun hit the object.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'triangular'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The intrepid group of adventurers climbed the mountain “despite of” bad weather and road closures.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' takes no 'of'; it is 'in spite of' that needs one: 'despite bad weather'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. The airplane “flowed over” the mountains, offering the passengers a breath-taking view of the majestic peaks below.
questions.explanation: The past tense of 'fly' is 'flew'; 'flowed' comes from 'flow'. The airplane 'flew over' the mountains.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Ecstasy
questions.explanation: 'Ecstasy' is overwhelming joy; its opposite is 'despair'. 'Euphoria' is a synonym.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. As a boy, I was always exploring lonely places—neglected gardens and orchards, unoccupied houses, patches of scrub or wasteland, the fields outside the town, the fringes of the forest. On one of my rambles (1)________the bungalow, I pushed my way through a thicket of lantana bushes and stumbled over a thick stone slab, twisting my ankle slightly as I fell. For some time, I sat on the grass massaging my foot. When the pain eased, I looked more (2)________ at the stone slab and was surprised to find that it was a gravestone. It was almost entirely covered by ivy; obviously no one had been near it for years. I tugged at the ivy and some of it came away in my hands. There was some (3)________ lettering on the grave, half-obscured by grass and moss. I could make out a name—Rose—but little more. I sat there for some time, (4)________ over my discovery. I was wondering why ‘Rose’ should have been buried at so lonely a spot when there was a (5)________ not far away.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'behind', the word in Ruskin Bond's original: the ramble took him into the neglected ground at the back of the bungalow, the kind of lonely place he liked to explore. 'Below' would need the bungalow to stand above sloping ground, which the passage does not mention; 'before' (in front of) does not suit a ramble into a thicket, and 'by dint of' means 'by means of'.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: He wondered why Rose lay in so lonely a spot when a 'cemetery', a burial ground, was not far away.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The ratio of principal and amount is 5 : 6 for one year. Find the rate of simple interest per annum?
questions.explanation: The interest for one year is 6 − 5 = 1 part on a principal of 5 parts, so the rate is 1/5 × 100 = 20% a year.

questions.text: What is the most powerful weapon that enables the Parliament to ensure executive accountability?
questions.explanation: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (Article 75(3)); if the House passes a no-confidence motion, the government must resign.

questions.text: Where is the Mahabodhi temple situated?
questions.explanation: The Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya, Bihar, marks the place where the Buddha attained enlightenment; it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.text: Which African leader wrote the autobiography ‘ Long Walk to Freedom’?
questions.explanation: 'Long Walk to Freedom' (1994) is the autobiography of Nelson Mandela, South Africa's first democratically elected president.

questions.text: In which year was the Training of Rural Youth for Self Employment (TRYSEM) scheme launched by Government of India?
questions.explanation: TRYSEM was launched on 15 August 1979 to train rural youth from poor families in skills for self-employment; in 1999 it was merged into the Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana.

questions.text: Under the Chief Minister Learn and Earn Scheme of Madhya Pradesh, the government will NOT provide which of the following?
questions.explanation: The Mukhyamantri Seekho Kamao Yojana (2023) gives youth aged 18 to 29 on-the-job training in companies, with a monthly stipend of ₹8,000 to ₹10,000, to build skills that make them employable. Laptops are not part of it.

questions.text: Dandari (Dancing) troupes perform __________ during the festival of Diwali for a fortnight with participation from Kolam and Raj Gond tribes.
questions.explanation: Gussadi (Ghusadi) is danced by the Dandari troupes of the Raj Gond and Kolam tribes of Adilabad, Telangana, who go from village to village around Diwali wearing peacock-feather headgear.

questions.text: How many gold medals did India win at the ISSF Junior World Cup 2023?
questions.explanation: India topped the medal table at the ISSF Junior World Cup in Suhl, Germany, in 2023, with 6 gold, 6 silver and 3 bronze medals.

questions.text: Which Indian musician personality’s native place is West Bengal?
questions.explanation: Bappi Lahiri was born in Jalpaiguri, West Bengal. Naushad came from Lucknow, O. P. Nayyar from Lahore and Ilaiyaraaja from Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: According to the Census of India 2011, which State/Union Territory has the lowest sex ratio?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Daman and Diu had the lowest sex ratio in the country, 618 females per 1,000 males; Haryana's 879 was the lowest among the states.

questions.text: Which of the following is an autobiography of the famous cricketer Sourav Ganguly?
options: Memories of My Life and Times
questions.explanation: 'A Century Is Not Enough' (2018) is Sourav Ganguly's memoir; 'A Shot at History' is the shooter Abhinav Bindra's.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Consider the following statement about the Government of India Act, 1935. 1. This act was enacted by the British Parliament. 2. This Act was divided into two separate acts for India and Burma Government. 3. This act was commenced from the 1 April 1935. Select the correct statement(s) using the code given below.
questions.explanation: The Act was passed by the British Parliament in 1935 and split into two, the Government of India Act and the Government of Burma Act. Its provincial part came into force on 1 April 1937, not 1935, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.text: Who among the following established a unit of horsepower that is equal to one horse doing 33,000 foot - pounds of work in one minute?
questions.explanation: James Watt defined one horsepower as 33,000 foot-pounds of work a minute, to compare the output of his steam engines with that of draught horses.

questions.text: In which year was the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act passed?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, passed during the Emergency, added 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity' to the Preamble and the Fundamental Duties (Part IVA).

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following leaders led the Revolt of 1857 in Bihar?
questions.explanation: Kunwar Singh, the zamindar of Jagdishpur near Arrah, led the revolt of 1857 in Bihar when he was about eighty.

questions.text: Shri Jagannathji Mela is held at _______.
questions.explanation: The Shri Jagannathji Mela is held at Alwar, Rajasthan, at the Rath Yatra of the city's Jagannath temple, when the deity is taken to Rupbas for his wedding with Janaki.

questions.text: _____________ literally means 'dance of the enchantress'. It is one of the most striking in the Indian classical dance repertoire.
questions.explanation: Mohiniyattam, Kerala's classical dance, is named after Mohini, the enchantress form of Vishnu: 'dance of the enchantress'.

questions.text: The important milestones of the SHG Bank linkage movement was spearheaded by _______ with support from RBI.
questions.explanation: NABARD launched the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme as a pilot in 1992, with the RBI's support, to link self-help groups to bank credit.

questions.text: Narendra Modi Cricket Stadium is one of the premier stadiums in India located at __________.
questions.explanation: The Narendra Modi Stadium, formerly the Sardar Patel Stadium, is at Motera in Ahmedabad, Gujarat.

questions.text: The pre-monsoon showers are known as ________ in Kerala and Karnataka.
questions.explanation: The pre-monsoon showers at the end of summer in Kerala and coastal Karnataka help the mangoes ripen, hence 'mango showers'.

questions.text: Insufficient levels of parathyroid hormone and low amount of calcium in the blood causes which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation: Parathyroid hormone keeps up the calcium level of the blood; too little of it lets the level fall, the condition called hypocalcaemia, which brings muscle cramps and tetany.

questions.text: Team Rest of India won Irani Cup in 2023. Irani Cup was hosted in which state?
questions.explanation: The Irani Cup of March 2023, between Rest of India and the Ranji Trophy champions Madhya Pradesh, was played at the Captain Roop Singh Stadium in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh; Rest of India won by 238 runs.

questions.text: What is a dimension related to the sustainability of microfinance institutions in India?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives dependency on donor funding: a microfinance institution is financially sustainable when its own income covers its costs, so how far it still relies on donor grants and subsidised funds is a standard measure of its sustainability. The other options are criticisms of how such institutions work (little social impact, high profits, excessive interest rates) rather than a dimension of whether one can carry on without outside support.

questions.text: The sentence given below contains some spelling errors. Select the option that has the correct spellings. Memberrs of the asocciation have succesfully climbed several paeks of the Himalayan range.
options: Members of the associattion have succesfully climbed several paeks of the Himalayan range.
Meembers of the associatiion have successfuly climbed several peaks of the Himalayan range.
Members of the associasion have succesfully climbed several paiks of the Himalayan range.
Members of the association have successfully climbed several peaks of the Himalayan range.
questions.explanation: The correct spellings are 'members', 'association', 'successfully' and 'peaks'.

questions.text: Choose the sentence that contains an error.
options: The Mona Lisa is a famous painting by Leonardo da Vinci.
She is the only person who can speak five languages fluently.
He is a doctor who specialises in the treating rare diseases.
I saw the movie that won the Academy Award for Best Picture.
questions.explanation: A gerund followed directly by its object takes no article: 'specialises in treating rare diseases' (or 'in the treatment of rare diseases').

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a spelling error. The conferrence / attempts to / trace the processes and / consequences of climate change.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'conference'.

questions.text: Select the word segment which substitutes the bracketed word correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Mathematics (are not) easy to learn.
questions.explanation: 'Mathematics', the name of a subject, is singular although it ends in -s, and the sentence stays in the present: 'Mathematics is not easy to learn.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The action of formally accusing a public official of a serious offence
questions.explanation: 'Impeachment' is the formal accusation of a high public official, such as a president or a judge, of serious misconduct.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A number which is used to divide another number
questions.explanation: The 'divisor' is the number by which another number, the dividend, is divided; the result is the quotient.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To cut someone some slack
options: Avoid talking about problems till the very end
To not manage someone very strictly or critically
questions.explanation: To 'cut someone some slack' is to make allowances for them and not judge them too strictly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank. Our trainer asked for _______ on her for the next informative session.
questions.explanation: To be 'all eyes and ears' is to watch and listen closely: the trainer wanted everyone's full attention.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. Children below the age of 14 were not allowed to partisipate in the cooking competition.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'participate'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. After I complete my training program / I will have been joining a team of astronauts / and preparing to / embark on a mission to Mars.
options: I will have been joining a team of astronauts
embark on a mission to Mars
After I complete my training program
questions.explanation: The future perfect continuous ('will have been joining') needs a stretch of time up to a future point, which the sentence does not give; an action that will be in progress after the training takes the future continuous: 'I will be joining a team of astronauts and preparing to embark on a mission to Mars.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Blessing in disguise
options: Something that seems good but is harmful for you
Something that seems bad but provides some benefit
Something that cannot be hidden from anyone
Something that remains hidden from everyone
questions.explanation: A 'blessing in disguise' is something that seems unfortunate at first but turns out to be good.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Break
questions.explanation: To 'break' something is to damage it; to 'mend' it is to repair it. 'Divide', 'split' and 'breach' are close to 'break' in meaning.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A place of burial
questions.explanation: A 'cemetery' is a burial ground.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Forthcoming
questions.explanation: 'Forthcoming' means about to happen, so its opposite is 'past'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. I will celebrating New Year at my old residence as usual.
options: at my old residence as usual.
questions.explanation: 'Will' takes the bare infinitive or 'be' with the -ing form: 'I will celebrate' or 'I will be celebrating'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Why don’t / you throw this / paper on the dust bin?
questions.explanation: One throws something 'into' (or 'in') a dustbin, not 'on' it: 'paper into the dustbin'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Beat around the bush
options: To be persistent in pursuing a goal
To avoid addressing a topic correctly
questions.explanation: To 'beat around the bush' is to avoid coming to the point.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Her stories paid _____ to her mother, whom she regarded as the goddess of bravery.
questions.explanation: To 'pay homage' to someone is to honour them publicly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Amicable
questions.explanation: 'Amicable' means friendly and without quarrelling, as in an amicable settlement.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Once, there was a boy who became bored when he watched over the village sheep (1)________ on the hillside. To entertain himself, he sang out, “Wolf! Wolf! The wolf is chasing the sheep!” When the villagers heard the cry, they came (2)________ the hill to drive the wolf away. But, when they arrived, they saw no wolf. The boy was amused when seeing their angry faces. “Don’t scream wolf, boy,” warned the villagers, “when there is no wolf!” They angrily went back down the hill. Later, the shepherd boy cried out once again, “Wolf! Wolf! The wolf is chasing the sheep!” When the villagers came, they saw there was no wolf, they said strictly, “Save your (3)________ cry for when there is really a wolf! Don’t cry ‘wolf’ when there is no wolf!” Later, the boy saw a real wolf sneaking around his flock. Alarmed, he jumped on his feet and cried out as loud as he could, “Wolf! Wolf!” But the villagers thought he was (4)________ them again, and so they didn’t come to help. At sunset, the villagers went looking for the boy who hadn’t returned with their sheep. When they went up the hill, they found him (5)________ as all the sheep were dead.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Sheep 'grazing' on a hillside are feeding on its grass.

Later, the shepherd boy cried out once again, “Wolf! Wolf! The wolf is chasing the sheep!” When the villagers came, they saw there was no wolf, they said strictly, “Save your (3)________ cry for when there is really a wolf! Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The villagers came 'running up' the hill to drive the wolf away; afterwards they 'went back down the hill'.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The villagers mean his cry of alarm: save your 'frightened' cry for when there really is a wolf.

questions.explanation: To be 'fooling' people is to trick them: the villagers thought he was playing the same trick again.
