markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup 2022 matches were NOT held in which state?
questions.explanation: The 2022 FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup, held in India in October 2022, was played at Bhubaneswar (Odisha), Margao (Goa) and Navi Mumbai (Maharashtra); no match was held in Gujarat.

questions.text: Who among the following is one of the co-authors of the book, ‘Cracking The Code:My Journey in Bollywood’?
questions.explanation: 'Cracking the Code: My Journey in Bollywood' was written by the actor Ayushmann Khurrana with his wife, Tahira Kashyap.

questions.text: In 1873, who published the first photograph of nerve tissue stained with the black reaction technique, describing a whole nerve cell?
questions.explanation: Camillo Golgi's 'black reaction', a silver nitrate stain, showed a whole nerve cell with all its branches for the first time; he shared the 1906 Nobel Prize in Medicine with Santiago Ramón y Cajal.

questions.text: In October 2022, Virat Kohli became the first Indian to complete how many runs in T20 cricket history?
questions.explanation: Kohli reached 11,000 runs in all T20 cricket (internationals, IPL and domestic matches together) in the second T20I against South Africa at Guwahati on 2 October 2022, the first Indian to do so.

questions.text: According to Sikh literature, the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev is celebrated on the full moon day of the Indian lunar month ____________.
questions.explanation: Guru Nanak Jayanti (Gurpurab) is celebrated on Kartik Purnima, the full moon of the month of Kartik.

questions.text: Yakshagana is a folk dance that belongs to the state of __________________.
questions.explanation: Yakshagana, a dance-drama of song, dialogue and elaborate costume and make-up, is the traditional theatre of coastal Karnataka.

questions.text: The brick temple of Bhitargaon is situated in which state?
questions.explanation: The Bhitargaon temple in Kanpur district, Uttar Pradesh, built of brick in the Gupta period, is among the oldest surviving brick temples in India.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following movements was founded in Bengal?
questions.explanation: Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in Calcutta in 1897. The Arya Samaj and the Prarthana Samaj began in Bombay, and Jyotirao Phule's Satyashodhak Samaj in Pune.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: On 15 August 1947, the first prime minister of India, Jawaharlal Nehru, raised the Indian National Flag above the _____________of Red Fort in Delhi.
questions.explanation: The Lahori Gate, the Red Fort's main gate, is named for facing towards Lahore; the Prime Minister hoists the flag and addresses the nation from its ramparts every Independence Day.

questions.text: ‘Mandarin’ is the official language of which neighbouring country of India?
questions.explanation: Standard Mandarin (Putonghua) is the official language of the People's Republic of China.

questions.text: Which of the following is used to measure the total output of goods and services in an economy including depreciation during a specific period within country?
questions.explanation: GDP is the value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a period, with depreciation not deducted ('gross'). NDP deducts depreciation, and GNP and NNP count the output of a country's residents rather than of its territory.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT related to the sport of swimming?
questions.explanation: A penalty corner is awarded in field hockey; breaststroke, backstroke and freestyle are swimming strokes.

questions.text: The East-West corridor, which is a part of the Golden Quadrilateral super highways, links which two cities of India from the following?
questions.explanation: The East-West Corridor runs from Porbandar in Gujarat to Silchar in Assam. Strictly it is not part of the Golden Quadrilateral: with the North-South Corridor it is a separate component of the same National Highways Development Project.

questions.text: What is the name of the seventh most abundant metal in the earth's crust, which is derived from the medieval Latin word 'Kalium'?
questions.explanation: Potassium's symbol, K, comes from its Latin name 'kalium', from the Arabic 'qali', the plant ash from which potash was made.

questions.text: What is the aim of Article 44 of the Indian Constitution?
options: To protect every monument or place of artistic or historic interest
To separate judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State
To protect and improve the environment and safeguard the forests and wildlife of the country
To secure for the citizen, a uniform civil code through the territory of India
questions.explanation: Article 44, a Directive Principle, says the State shall endeavour to secure for citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India. The other options are Articles 49, 50 and 48A.

questions.text: Which of the following novels of Kamleshwar was awarded the Sahitya Akademi Award in 2003?
questions.explanation: Kamleshwar received the Sahitya Akademi Award (Hindi) for 2003 for 'Kitne Pakistan', a novel on Partition and its aftermath.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following institutes was founded by MG Ranade and GV Joshi?
questions.explanation: The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha was founded in 1870 by M. G. Ranade, G. V. Joshi and others to put the people's grievances before the government.

questions.text: Roshan Kumari, Shovana Narayan, Maya Rao and Kumudini Lakhia are eminent ______________ artists.
questions.explanation: Roshan Kumari, Shovana Narayan, Maya Rao and Kumudini Lakhia are all noted Kathak dancers and teachers.

questions.text: What is the difference between a debit card and a credit card?
options: Debit cards are used for online transactions, while credit cards are used for in-person purchases.
Credit cards require a PIN, while debit cards require a signature.
Debit cards withdraw money directly from a bank account, while credit cards allow borrowing up to a certain limit.
Debit cards have higher interest rates than credit cards.
questions.explanation: A debit card draws on the money already in the holder's bank account; a credit card lets the holder borrow from the issuer up to a set credit limit and repay later.

questions.text: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Bill, 2022 has included Narikoravan and Kurivikkaran communities in the list of Scheduled Tribes of which state?
questions.explanation: The Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order (Second Amendment) Act, 2022, passed by Parliament in December 2022, added the Narikoravan and Kurivikkaran communities to Tamil Nadu's list of Scheduled Tribes.

questions.text: Which river is also known as Tsangpo?
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra rises in Tibet, where it is called the Yarlung Tsangpo, and enters India in Arunachal Pradesh as the Siang.

questions.text: What is the destination of the water drained off by the Nile river?
questions.explanation: The Nile flows north and empties into the Mediterranean Sea through its delta in Egypt; Lake Victoria is one of its sources.

questions.text: Article 149 of the Constitution deals with _______________.
options: the qualifications required for the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
the term of office of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
the appointment of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India
questions.explanation: Article 149 deals with the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General; the appointment and conditions of service of the office are in Article 148.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Feud
questions.explanation: A 'feud' is a long, bitter quarrel; its opposite is 'harmony', agreement and goodwill.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. All these things happen/ because she do not / pay heed to my words.
questions.explanation: A singular subject takes a singular verb: 'because she does not'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Professor said that “I will be late for the lecture”.
options: he shall be late for the lecture
he is late for the lecture
he would be late for the lecture
he may be late for the lecture
questions.explanation: After the past reporting verb 'said', 'will' moves back to 'would', and the professor's 'I' becomes 'he': 'Professor said that he would be late for the lecture.'

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'embarrass', with a double 'r' and a double 's'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Sell like hot cakes
questions.explanation: To 'sell like hot cakes' is to sell very quickly and in large numbers.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Andrew “will playing” basketball at the college tournament.
questions.explanation: 'Will' cannot be followed by an '-ing' form alone. Of the options only 'is playing' is grammatical, the present continuous for a planned event: 'Andrew is playing basketball at the college tournament.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank. Hardik Pandya hit four ________ fours and scored 72 runs in the match.
questions.explanation: 'Consecutive' means following one after another without a break: four fours in a row.

questions.text: Select the sentence that has NO spelling errors.
options: The doctor presribed some medicine to alleviate my parsistent cough, which has been boathering me for days.
The doctor precribed some medicine to aleviate my persistent cough, which has been bothering me for days.
The doctor prescribed some medicine to aleviate my parsistent cough, which has been boathering me for days.
The doctor prescribed some medicine to alleviate my persistent cough, which has been bothering me for days.
questions.explanation: Only this sentence spells 'prescribed', 'alleviate', 'persistent' and 'bothering' correctly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank. The athlete’s perseverance and mental toughness ________(facilitate) her to overcome adversity and achieve her goals.
questions.explanation: To 'facilitate' is to make possible; in the past tense the word that fits '___ her to overcome' is 'enabled'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Throughout my career as a journalist, / I covered many important stories and / interviewed numerous individuals, which allow me / to share important information and insights with my readers.
options: to share important information and insights with my readers
I covered many important stories and
Throughout my career as a journalist,
interviewed numerous individuals, which allow me
questions.explanation: 'Which' here stands for the whole preceding clause (covering the stories and interviewing the people), so the plural 'allow' cannot be right; with the past 'covered' and 'interviewed' it should be 'which allowed me'. Nor can 'which' stand for 'individuals', as people take 'who'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Harish says / that his sister / loves to play / harmonium.
questions.explanation: A musical instrument after 'play' takes the definite article: 'loves to play the harmonium'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence. Selling, purchasing, and using “an illegally copied” product is a criminal offence.
questions.explanation: 'Pirated' means illegally copied, and as it begins with a consonant sound it takes 'a': 'a pirated product'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The hiring manager has already offered you the job; now, ________________ to accept or decline the offer.
options: the ball is in your court
questions.explanation: 'The ball is in your court' means it is now your turn to act or decide.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Oberon doesn’t like the way Demetrius ________ to Helena. (Credit: A Midsummer Night’s Dream)
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'talks': the sentence retells the play in the present ('doesn't like'), so the present simple fits, and the singular 'Demetrius' takes 'talks'. 'Talked' would also be grammatical for one particular past occasion, but the sentence points to none; 'talking' and 'to talk' cannot follow 'the way Demetrius'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Let sleeping dogs lie
options: Leave an existing situation as it is
questions.explanation: To 'let sleeping dogs lie' is to leave a situation alone rather than stir up trouble.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A cage made for birds. OR A place for keeping the birds in a confined space.
questions.explanation: An 'aviary' is a large cage or enclosure for birds; an apiary is for bees and an aquarium for fish.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Repulsive
questions.explanation: 'Repulsive' means causing strong dislike: 'disgusting'. 'Attractive' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence. The “sergent” brought in a lot of changes as soon as he was given charge.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'sergeant'.

questions.text: The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. The boy told his mother that he saw the most tall giraffe at the zoo.
options: The boy told his mother that he saw the tallest giraffe at the zoo.
The boy told his mother that he saw the most taller giraffe at the zoo.
The boy told his mother that he saw the most tallest giraffe at the zoo.
The boy told his mother that he saw the more taller giraffe at the zoo.
questions.explanation: 'Tall' forms its superlative with '-est': 'the tallest giraffe'. 'Most tall', 'most taller', 'most tallest' and 'more taller' are all wrong.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Call the shots
options: To be a follower that makes less important decision
To be in a position to make decisions that influences a situation
To be in a powerless position that follows orders
To be in a neutral position
questions.explanation: To 'call the shots' is to be the one who makes the decisions and controls what happens.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. That evening we sat in the courtyard of the hotel once more, (1) ________________ the sun sink below the western isles. I told Alexi what had happened that day. I (2) _________________ I could glimpse the grey stone wall of Lismore House (3) _________________ its island hilltop, the red light of the setting sun glinting from the windows, and from there the wasted frame of Jonathan Blake gazing out across the sea, on nothing, his boy waiting for him to die. But it was my (4) _________________, simply the image on my mind, like the image burned on to your eyes when you have (5) _________________ too long at the sun, the passing footprint of a creature long gone.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: They sat 'watching' the sun sink: 'watch' takes an object and a bare infinitive, as in 'watch something sink'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. That evening we sat in the courtyard of the hotel once more, (1) ________________ the sun sink below the western isles. I told Alexi what had happened that day. I (2) _________________ I could glimpse the grey stone wall of Lismore House (3) _________________ its island hilltop, the red light of the setting sun glinting from the windows, and from there the wasted frame of Jonathan Blake gazing out across the sea, on nothing, his boy waiting for him to die. But it was my (4) _________________, simply the image on my mind, like the image burned on to your eyes when you have (5) _________________ too long at the sun, the passing footprint of a creature long gone.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: 'I fancied I could glimpse' means I imagined I could see, which fits the later 'it was my fantasy'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. That evening we sat in the courtyard of the hotel once more, (1) ________________ the sun sink below the western isles. I told Alexi what had happened that day. I (2) _________________ I could glimpse the grey stone wall of Lismore House (3) _________________ its island hilltop, the red light of the setting sun glinting from the windows, and from there the wasted frame of Jonathan Blake gazing out across the sea, on nothing, his boy waiting for him to die. But it was my (4) _________________, simply the image on my mind, like the image burned on to your eyes when you have (5) _________________ too long at the sun, the passing footprint of a creature long gone.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: The house stands 'on' its island hilltop.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. That evening we sat in the courtyard of the hotel once more, (1) ________________ the sun sink below the western isles. I told Alexi what had happened that day. I (2) _________________ I could glimpse the grey stone wall of Lismore House (3) _________________ its island hilltop, the red light of the setting sun glinting from the windows, and from there the wasted frame of Jonathan Blake gazing out across the sea, on nothing, his boy waiting for him to die. But it was my (4) _________________, simply the image on my mind, like the image burned on to your eyes when you have (5) _________________ too long at the sun, the passing footprint of a creature long gone.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: The writer only imagined the scene: 'it was my fantasy, simply the image on my mind'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each blank. That evening we sat in the courtyard of the hotel once more, (1) ________________ the sun sink below the western isles. I told Alexi what had happened that day. I (2) _________________ I could glimpse the grey stone wall of Lismore House (3) _________________ its island hilltop, the red light of the setting sun glinting from the windows, and from there the wasted frame of Jonathan Blake gazing out across the sea, on nothing, his boy waiting for him to die. But it was my (4) _________________, simply the image on my mind, like the image burned on to your eyes when you have (5) _________________ too long at the sun, the passing footprint of a creature long gone.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: The afterimage comes when you have 'stared' too long at the sun; 'stare' takes 'at'.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: A sum of money deposited at simple interest amounts to ₹1,020 in three years and ₹980 in two years. The sum deposited is:
questions.explanation: One year's interest is 1,020 − 980 = ₹40, so two years' interest is ₹80 and the sum is 980 − 80 = ₹900.

questions.text: In which of the following states is there hardly any differences in day and night temperatures?
questions.explanation: The sea keeps Kerala's climate equable, so its day and night temperatures hardly differ; inland states such as Rajasthan, Punjab and Bihar have a much larger daily range.

questions.text: The dancers Padma Subrahmanyam, Alarmel Valli, Yamini Krishnamurthy and Anita Ratnam are great exponents of ____________.
questions.explanation: Padma Subrahmanyam, Alarmel Valli, Yamini Krishnamurthy and Anita Ratnam all made their names in Bharatanatyam (Yamini Krishnamurthy was also a leading Kuchipudi dancer).

questions.text: Which of the following states won the Santosh Trophy in Riyadh in March 2023 after a gap of 54 years?
questions.explanation: Karnataka beat Meghalaya 3-2 in the final in Riyadh on 4 March 2023, their first Santosh Trophy title since 1968-69, won when the state was still called Mysore.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct about Article 129 of the Constitution of India?
options: It provides for the Supreme Court to give advisory opinion to the President.
It provides for the Supreme Court to be a court of original jurisdiction
It provides for the Supreme Court to be a court of record.
It provides for the Supreme Court to be the highest court of appeal.
questions.explanation: Article 129 makes the Supreme Court a court of record, with the power to punish for contempt of itself. Advisory opinions come under Article 143 and original jurisdiction under Article 131.

questions.text: Indian classical vocalist Pandit Jasraj belonged to which of the following musical gharanas?
questions.explanation: Pandit Jasraj was the best-known vocalist of the Mewati gharana.

questions.text: Articles 29-30 of the Constitution of India deals with _______
questions.explanation: Articles 29 and 30 make up the Cultural and Educational Rights: protection of the interests of minorities and their right to set up and run educational institutions.

questions.text: As per the 18th Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), the unemployment rate among females (aged 15 years and above) in urban areas declined to ________ in January-March 2023.
questions.explanation: The Periodic Labour Force Survey's quarterly bulletin for January-March 2023, the eighteenth in the series, put the urban unemployment rate for women aged 15 and above at 9.2%, down from 10.1% a year earlier.

questions.text: Which of the following is connected with daily atmospheric weather changes?
questions.explanation: Almost all weather (clouds, rain, storms) forms in the troposphere, the lowest layer of the atmosphere. The lithosphere and asthenosphere are layers of the Earth, and the stratopause is the boundary at the top of the stratosphere.

questions.text: According to the Census of India 2011, which of the following states has the lowest literacy rate?
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Tripura's literacy rate was about 87.2%, below Goa (88.7%), Mizoram (91.3%) and Kerala (94.0%).

questions.text: In which state is the famous Brihadeshwar temple situated?
questions.explanation: The Brihadeeswara temple at Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, was built by the Chola king Rajaraja I.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of capital receipt in the government budget?
questions.explanation: Selling bonds is borrowing, which creates a liability, so it is a capital receipt. Taxes, profits of public enterprises and grants from abroad are revenue receipts.

questions.text: Which of the abhinayas deals with the use of costumes, jewellery, facial make-up etc?
questions.explanation: Of the four abhinayas of the Natya Shastra, aharya covers costume, ornaments and make-up; angika is the body, vachika speech and song, and sattvika the inner emotional states.

questions.text: Which of the following best defines transfer payments?
options: Payments made to individuals in exchange for their labour or services
Payments made by the government to individuals without any corresponding production of goods or services
Payments made by businesses to their shareholders as a share of profits
Payments made by individuals to the government in the form of taxes
questions.explanation: Transfer payments, such as pensions, scholarships and old-age allowances, are paid by the government without any good or service in return.

questions.text: The Nuakhai festival of ______________ is observed on Panchami Tithi (fifth day) of the lunar fortnight of Bhadrava (August-September), the day after Ganesh Chaturthi.
questions.explanation: Nuakhai, the festival of the new rice harvest, is celebrated mainly in western Odisha.

questions.text: Which country is hosting the ICC 2023 ODI Cricket World Cup?
questions.explanation: When the exam was held (September 2023), India was preparing to host the 2023 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup on its own, played in October and November 2023.

questions.text: In April 2023, Tamil Nadu passed a bill banning which of the following?
questions.explanation: Governor R. N. Ravi gave his assent on 10 April 2023 to the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Online Gambling and Regulation of Online Games Bill, which the Assembly had passed a second time on 23 March 2023 after he returned it.

questions.text: In which stadium was the final match of ODI Cricket World Cup 2011 played?
questions.explanation: India beat Sri Lanka in the 2011 World Cup final, played at the Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai, on 2 April 2011.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: ‘Mitra Mela’ was a revolutionary organisation founded by:
questions.explanation: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and his brother Ganesh founded the Mitra Mela at Nasik in 1899; it became the Abhinav Bharat Society in 1904.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following freedom fighter lawyers from Bengal is known as Deshbandhu?
questions.explanation: Chittaranjan Das, the Calcutta barrister and Swaraj Party leader, was called 'Deshbandhu', friend of the nation.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. He studies the subject known as “the scientific study of insects.”
questions.explanation: 'Entomology' is the scientific study of insects; 'etymology' is the study of the origin of words.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. Harish told me / in the morning / that Gaurav will / come tomorrow.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'that Gaurav will': after the past reporting verb 'told', the reported clause moves back, 'that Gaurav would come tomorrow'. 'Will' is also heard when the event is still to come, but the textbook rule is the backshift.

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the following sentence. The detective and his agent inspected the krime scene yesterday.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'crime'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Cup of tea
questions.explanation: One's 'cup of tea' is something one likes or is good at, usually in the negative: 'Chess is not my cup of tea.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate segment that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence. Iraq was governed by “autocracy” when Saddam Hussain was the President.
questions.explanation: 'Autocracy' is government by one person who holds absolute power.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Ours is ________ house of all the houses in our area.
questions.explanation: 'Of all the houses' needs the superlative, and 'biggest' already is one, so 'more' or 'most' cannot be added: 'the biggest'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'testimonial'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The council president is known “to play devil’s advocate” often.
options: To argue, just for the sake of it
questions.explanation: To 'play devil's advocate' is to argue against a view, not out of conviction but for the sake of argument.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined segment in the given sentence. When it comes to playing the guitar, Jim always “hits the nail on the head”.
questions.explanation: To 'hit the nail on the head' is to get something exactly right.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The company was “on thin ice”.
options: In a precarious or risky situation
questions.explanation: To be 'on thin ice' is to be in a risky or precarious position.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. She performed / the dance routine / perfect, / impressing everyone.
questions.explanation: How she performed needs an adverb: 'performed the dance routine perfectly'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. With all their little comforts destroyed, the survivors were thrown “still farther back into barbarism.”
options: still a little farther into barbarism
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'further': for a figurative distance, as in sliding back into barbarism, 'further' is preferred, with 'farther' traditionally kept for physical distance. Some writers use 'farther' figuratively too, so leaving the sentence as it is is arguable.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Perhaps my family visit the Taj Mahal next month.
questions.explanation: 'Next month' points to the future, so the verb needs 'will': 'Perhaps my family will visit the Taj Mahal next month.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. In America, / most of the people / can speak / the English well.
questions.explanation: The name of a language takes no article: 'can speak English well'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. Butterfly was “attracted” towards the bright flowers.
questions.explanation: To be 'attracted' is to be drawn towards something; its opposite is 'repulsed', driven away.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Please / explain me / how this plan / did not work.
questions.explanation: 'Explain' does not take the person as a direct object: 'explain to me'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Early childhood experiences have a _________ impact on brain development affecting learning, health, behaviour, and, ultimately, productivity and income.
questions.explanation: A 'profound' impact is a deep, far-reaching one, which fits effects that last into learning, health and income; 'superficial' says the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Fragile
questions.explanation: 'Fragile' means easily broken: 'brittle'. 'Sturdy' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. He was “admired” for introducing welfare programmes.
questions.explanation: To be 'admired' is to be regarded with respect and approval; its opposite is 'despised'. 'Appreciated' is close in meaning.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Fingerprinting is the one of the methods of (1)________ using the impression made by the minute ridge formation or patterns found on the fingertips. No two persons have exactly the same (2)________ of ridge patterns, they remain unchanged throughout the life. Fingerprints may be classified and filled on the basis of the ridge patterns, setting up an identification system that is almost (3)________ . Today, law enforcement agencies use computers to (4)________ record fingerprints and to transmit them electronically to other agencies for comparison. By comparing fingerprints of the criminals with the recorded fingerprints, officials can establish (5)________ proof of the presence or identity of a person.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Fingerprinting is a method of 'identification': the passage goes on to speak of an 'identification system' and of proving a person's identity.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Fingerprinting is the one of the methods of (1)________ using the impression made by the minute ridge formation or patterns found on the fingertips. No two persons have exactly the same (2)________ of ridge patterns, they remain unchanged throughout the life. Today, law enforcement agencies use computers to (4)________ record fingerprints and to transmit them electronically to other agencies for comparison. By comparing fingerprints of the criminals with the recorded fingerprints, officials can establish (5)________ proof of the presence or identity of a person.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: No two people share the same 'arrangement' of ridge patterns, that is, the way the ridges are laid out.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Fingerprinting is the one of the methods of (1)________ using the impression made by the minute ridge formation or patterns found on the fingertips. No two persons have exactly the same (2)________ of ridge patterns, they remain unchanged throughout the life. Fingerprints may be classified and filled on the basis of the ridge patterns, setting up an identification system that is almost (3)________ . Today, law enforcement agencies use computers to (4)________ record fingerprints and to transmit them electronically to other agencies for comparison. By comparing fingerprints of the criminals with the recorded fingerprints, officials can establish (5)________ proof of the presence or identity of a person.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Patterns that are unique and never change give a system that is almost 'infallible', incapable of error; 'fallible', 'risky' and 'unreliable' say the opposite.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Fingerprinting is the one of the methods of (1)________ using the impression made by the minute ridge formation or patterns found on the fingertips. No two persons have exactly the same (2)________ of ridge patterns, they remain unchanged throughout the life. Fingerprints may be classified and filled on the basis of the ridge patterns, setting up an identification system that is almost (3)________ . Today, law enforcement agencies use computers to (4)________ record fingerprints and to transmit them electronically to other agencies for comparison. By comparing fingerprints of the criminals with the recorded fingerprints, officials can establish (5)________ proof of the presence or identity of a person.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Computers record fingerprints 'digitally', which is what lets them be sent electronically to other agencies.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Fingerprinting is the one of the methods of (1)________ using the impression made by the minute ridge formation or patterns found on the fingertips. No two persons have exactly the same (2)________ of ridge patterns, they remain unchanged throughout the life. Fingerprints may be classified and filled on the basis of the ridge patterns, setting up an identification system that is almost (3)________ . Today, law enforcement agencies use computers to (4)________ record fingerprints and to transmit them electronically to other agencies for comparison. By comparing fingerprints of the criminals with the recorded fingerprints, officials can establish (5)________ proof of the presence or identity of a person.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: A match gives 'absolute' proof, complete and certain; 'provisional' and 'unconfirmed' would undercut the passage.

markingNote: 3 marks a question; no negative marking in Session-I (Numerical and Mathematical Ability, Reasoning), 1 mark deducted for each wrong answer in Session-II (General Awareness, English).

questions.text: The percentage profit earned by selling an article for ₹1,980 is equal to the percentage loss incurred by selling the same article for ₹1,620. At what price should the article be sold to make a 15% profit?
questions.explanation: Equal profit and loss percentages put the cost price midway: (1,980 + 1,620)/2 = ₹1,800. A 15% profit needs 1.15 × 1,800 = ₹2,070.

questions.text: If 7 N force is applied on a brick and it moves through 5 m, then what will be the work done?
questions.explanation: Work = force × displacement = 7 N × 5 m = 35 J; the SI unit of work is the joule, not the erg.

questions.text: ________________is celebrated in Jharkhand immediately after Diwali on the new moon day in the honour of cattle.
questions.explanation: Sohrai, a harvest festival of Jharkhand's tribal communities, falls at Diwali time in the month of Kartik: cattle are bathed, decorated and worshipped, and houses are painted with Sohrai murals.

questions.text: Which of the dance was immediately preceded by a practice session called sevakali and undertaken in the precincts of a temple?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Kathakali, Kerala's dance-drama: IGNOU's course text on Indian dance says its stage presentation was traditionally preceded by a practice session called sevakali, held in the precincts of a temple. (We could not find the term in other sources.)

questions.text: Which of the following is a duty of the Attorney General of India?
options: To give advice to the Government of India on legal matters
To act as a judge in the Supreme Court
To represent India in international bodies
questions.explanation: Under Article 76 the Attorney General advises the Government of India on legal matters referred by the President and performs other legal duties assigned; a state has its own Advocate General.

questions.text: The cultural heritage of Siddhis from _________ dates back to almost 300 years and their Siddhi Dhamal dance is an exquisite art form.
questions.explanation: The Siddis, a community of East African descent, live in Gujarat chiefly around the Gir forest; their Dhamal, also called Goma, is danced to drums.

questions.text: In which of the following cities was the 2023 IPL final match held?
questions.explanation: The 2023 IPL final was played at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad, on 29 May 2023 (a reserve day, after rain on the 28th); Chennai Super Kings beat Gujarat Titans.

questions.text: What is a budget deficit?
options: The excess of government revenue over expenditure
The amount of money allocated for defence spending
The amount of money allocated for social welfare programmes
The excess of government expenditure over revenue
questions.explanation: A budget deficit is the amount by which the government's expenditure exceeds its receipts; a surplus is the reverse.

questions.text: What is a revenue expenditure?
options: Money spent on day-to-day government operations
Money spent on construction of roads
questions.explanation: Revenue expenditure creates no assets and reduces no liabilities: salaries, subsidies, interest and other day-to-day running costs. Repaying loans, buying assets and building roads are capital expenditure.

questions.text: The holy mountain ‘Kailash’ is located in which neighbouring country of India?
questions.explanation: Mount Kailash, sacred to Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and followers of Bon, stands in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China, near Lake Manasarovar.

questions.text: In which of the following states of India the ‘Loo’ wind does NOT blow during the summer season?
questions.explanation: The Loo is the hot, dry wind of May and June over the plains of north and north-west India, including Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan. Goa, on the west coast, has a humid climate tempered by the sea.

questions.text: The Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 seeks to implement the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES). Which of the following statements is correct about CITES? 1. CITES is an agreement between governments to ensure that international trade in the specimens of wild animals and plants does not threaten the survival of the species. 2. Under CITES, plant and animal specimens are classified into five categories based on the threat to their extinction. 3. The Convention requires countries to regulate the trade of all listed specimens through permits. 4. It also seeks to regulate the possession of live animal specimens.
questions.explanation: CITES sorts species into three Appendices by how threatened they are, not five, so statement 2 is wrong. It is an agreement between governments, trade in listed specimens needs permits, and the 2022 Act also regulates the possession of live specimens: 1, 3 and 4.

questions.text: ‘My Story’ is the autobiography of which female writer?
questions.explanation: 'My Story' is the autobiography of Kamala Das (Madhavikutty), who wrote in English and Malayalam; the Malayalam version is 'Ente Katha'.

questions.text: Which age group of the population are covered under the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) scheme of the Government of India?
questions.explanation: DDU-GKY, the Ministry of Rural Development's placement-linked skilling scheme, is for poor rural youth aged 15 to 35 (up to 45 for women and some other groups).

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was the founder of Naujawan Bharat Sabha?
questions.explanation: Bhagat Singh founded the Naujawan Bharat Sabha at Lahore in March 1926 to rally young people, workers and peasants against British rule.

questions.text: Which gland gets enlarged in the goitre due to which there is a swelling in the front part of the throat?
questions.explanation: A goitre is an enlarged thyroid gland, which sits in the front of the neck; the commonest cause is too little iodine in the diet.

questions.text: In which state is the Bhitari temple situated?
questions.explanation: Bhitari, in Ghazipur district of Uttar Pradesh, is a Gupta-period site known for Skandagupta's pillar inscription; the Gupta brick temple at Bhitargaon, near Kanpur, is also in Uttar Pradesh.

questions.text: Shubman Gill was in the news for creating a record in his sport. What sport does he play?
questions.explanation: Shubman Gill is an Indian cricketer. In January 2023 his 208 against New Zealand at Hyderabad made him the youngest batter to score a double century in one-day internationals.

questions.text: Which of the following does NOT come under Fundamental Duties?
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Duties in Article 51A include respecting the National Anthem, promoting harmony and developing the scientific temper, but not paying taxes.

questions.text: Which of the following institutions bagged the maximum medals at the third edition of Khelo India University Games?
questions.explanation: Panjab University, Chandigarh, topped the medal table at the third Khelo India University Games, held in Uttar Pradesh in May-June 2023, with 69 medals (26 gold); Guru Nanak Dev University was second with 68.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year did the All-India Muslim League move a resolution demanding ‘Independent States’ for Muslims in the north-western and eastern areas of the country?
questions.explanation: The Lahore Resolution, adopted at the Muslim League's Lahore session in March 1940, asked for 'Independent States' in the Muslim-majority north-western and eastern zones.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. A soothe voice must convey both confidence and intimacy, qualities which can be attributed to a few key components.
questions.explanation: 'Soothe' is a verb; the noun 'voice' needs the adjective: 'A soothing voice'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Empathetic
questions.explanation: 'Empathetic' means able to share another's feelings; 'merciless', without pity, is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The police inspector knows the “ins and outs” of the murder case.
questions.explanation: The 'ins and outs' of something are all its details.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error. He told me / that he goes / to the market / to buy a laptop.
questions.explanation: After a past reporting verb the reported verb moves back to the past: 'He told me that he went to the market to buy a laptop.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence. The energetic kitten is playful after having “his” breakfast.
questions.explanation: An animal of unstated sex is 'it', and its possessive is 'its', with no apostrophe; 'it's' means 'it is'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. It is commonly believed / that Democracy is / the best form / of the government.
questions.explanation: 'Government' in the general sense, a system of rule, takes no article: 'the best form of government'.

questions.text: Four words of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains a spelling error. Ozone is a “reactiev” gas that is not only important in protecting us from harmful ultraviolet “radiation” but is also a greenhouse gas and, at high smog-level “concentrations”, harmful to human health and “vegetation”.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'reactive'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains a misspelt word. A “piano” teacher described an “interesting” “encountar” she had with a young lady who came to “inquire” about music lessons.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'encounter'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. The executives were “running around in circles”, without any success.
options: Putting efforts into something that does not give a worthwhile result
questions.explanation: To 'run around in circles' is to work hard without getting anywhere.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Many great people “born” in that small village.
questions.explanation: The sentence needs a passive verb, plural to agree with 'people': 'Many great people were born in that small village.'

questions.text: The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error. He was carefullest while stealing the crown jewels.
options: He was more careful while stealing the crown jewels.
He was most carefuller while stealing the crown jewels.
He was carefuller while stealing the crown jewels.
He was most careful while stealing the crown jewels.
questions.explanation: 'Careful' forms its superlative with 'most', not '-est': 'He was most careful'. 'Carefuller' is not standard, 'most carefuller' doubles the comparison, and 'more careful' turns the superlative into a comparative.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Hesitate
questions.explanation: To 'hesitate' is to pause in uncertainty: to 'falter'.

questions.text: The sentence given below has spelling errors. Select the sentence without spelling errors. We can also contribute to presarvation of water bodies by not dumping our garbage in them.
options: We can also contribute to presarvation of water bodies by not dumpeing our garbage in them.
We can also contribute to preservation of water bodies by not dumping our garbage in them.
We can also contribut to presarvation of water bodies by not dumping our garbage in them.
We can also contribute to presarvation of water bodies by not dumping our garbag in them.
questions.explanation: Only the second sentence spells 'contribute', 'preservation', 'dumping' and 'garbage' correctly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Call it a day
options: To have the greatest day ever
To refer to something as something else
questions.explanation: To 'call it a day' is to stop working, for the day or for good.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Stern
questions.explanation: 'Stern' means strict and severe; its opposite is 'lenient'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. His older brothers were quite willing that he should “went to” sea.
questions.explanation: A modal such as 'should' takes the base form of the verb: 'that he should go to sea'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement required’. It is true that learning English is essential for professionals “to survived” the national and international competitions.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'for surviving', which keeps the sense of purpose: English is essential for surviving the competitions. 'To survived' is wrong because 'to' takes the base form, and the plain correction 'to survive' is not offered; 'to be survive' is ungrammatical, and 'having to survive' would describe the professionals instead of giving the purpose.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The tigress that was killed by the villagers was not only a man-eater, ________ a mother.
questions.explanation: 'Not only' pairs with 'but also': 'not only a man-eater, but also a mother'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Spill the beans
options: Behave or speak in a rash manner
To reveal a secret information unintentionally
questions.explanation: To 'spill the beans' is to let out a secret, often carelessly or too soon.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Photosynthesis is the _______(1) used by plants, algae and some bacteria to turn sunlight into energy. The process chemically _______(2) carbon dioxide and water into food and oxygen. The chemical reaction often ______(3) on a pigment called chlorophyll, which gives plants their green colour. Photosynthesis is also the __________(4) our planet is blanketed in an oxygen-rich atmosphere. Plants absorb carbon dioxide from the __________(5) air and release water and oxygen via microscopic pores on their leaves called stomata.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the 'process' by which plants turn sunlight into energy; the next sentence goes on with 'The process'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. questions.explanation: To 'convert' one thing into another is to change it: carbon dioxide and water are changed into food and oxygen.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. In the delicacy and elaborateness / of its ornament, it is the / more splendid church in Italy.
options: of its ornament it is the
questions.explanation: Comparing the church with all others in Italy needs the superlative: 'it is the most splendid church in Italy'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. The fashion industry is one “of the largest contributors” to global warming.
questions.explanation: 'One of the' is followed by a superlative and a plural noun, so 'one of the largest contributors' is already correct.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. A large chunk of lemon crop grown in the country goes ______ to factories.
questions.explanation: The blank describes how the crop goes to factories, so it needs the adverb 'directly'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Neither Priya nor Rashmi “is planning a” trip.
questions.explanation: With 'neither ... nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject, here the singular 'Rashmi', so 'is planning a trip' is already correct.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. If broadly beneficial immigration is to be sustained, destination countries must acknowledge and _______ the real risks that it raises.
questions.explanation: To 'address' a risk is to deal with it, which is what countries must do after acknowledging it. 'Disregard' contradicts 'acknowledge', and one does not 'speak' or 'perform' a risk.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A place for storing grain
questions.explanation: A granary is a storehouse for grain. A treasury holds money or valuables, an apiary is a place where bees are kept and an aviary a large enclosure for birds.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Demote
questions.explanation: To 'demote' is to move someone to a lower rank, so its opposite is 'elevate', to raise to a higher one.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Astute
questions.explanation: 'Astute' means quick to see how to gain an advantage: 'shrewd'. 'Dull' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. If your kids sleep well, they are likely to behave better.
questions.explanation: The conditional is correct as it stands: the present 'sleep' in the 'if' clause with 'they are likely to behave better' in the main clause.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The man was ______ enough to thank her for all the hard work.
questions.explanation: 'Gracious' means courteous and kind, which suits a man who thanks someone for her hard work. 'Horrid' and 'repellent' are unpleasant, and 'attractive' does not fit 'enough to thank'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Forthright
questions.explanation: 'Forthright' means direct and honest, so its opposite is 'devious', dishonest and scheming. 'Upfront' and 'outspoken' are close in meaning to 'forthright'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'yesterday'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Castle in the air
questions.explanation: A 'castle in the air' is a daydream or plan that is unlikely ever to come true.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. The last straw
options: The last ray of hope in an unfortunate situation
The only option left after a series of unsuccessful attempts
The final problem in a series of problems that makes the situation intolerable
questions.explanation: 'The last straw' is the last of a series of troubles, the one that makes a situation impossible to bear (from 'the straw that broke the camel's back').

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A group of fish
questions.explanation: A group of fish swimming together is a 'school'. A troop is a group of monkeys or soldiers and a litter the young born to an animal at one time.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. The ability to relax and “rejuvenate” promotes wellness.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'suppress', to hold down or stifle: not an exact antonym of 'rejuvenate', to make fresh and lively again, but the only option opposite in sense. 'Replenish' and 'revive' are close to 'rejuvenate', and 'update' is unrelated.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Amoeba is a microscopic single-celled “organism found in” pond water.
questions.explanation: 'A microscopic single-celled organism' is singular, matching 'Amoeba is', and the past participle 'found' describes where it lives, so the sentence is already correct.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The students was given the task of penning down a short write-up.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'the students' takes a plural verb: 'The students were given the task'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Tidy
questions.explanation: 'Tidy' means neat and arranged in order: 'orderly'. 'Muddy' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the option that corrects the misspelt words in the given sentence. We have to relie on meaningful contont now.
options: We have to relie on meaningful content now.
We have to rely on meaningful cuntent now.
We have to rely on meaningful contont now.
We have to rely on meaningful content now.
questions.explanation: The correct spellings are 'rely' and 'content'; only the last option has both.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. When it's your idea, you want to (1) ______ about it all the time. I've had this problem on more than a few occasions now. Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: One 'talks about' an idea; 'express' and 'customise' take no 'about', and 'meet about it' does not fit.

questions.explanation: 'Promoting' one's work is what the writer is wary of overdoing, as the last sentence ('when it's okay to promote') shows.
