questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. All T are N. II. No M is N. Conclusions: I. All T are M. II. Some T are not M.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: All T are N and no M is N, so no T is M. I is therefore false, and II, some T are not M, follows.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Only a few A1 are P5. Only a few P5 are T8. Conclusions: I. Some A1 are T8. II. All P5 can never be T8.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: 'Only a few P5 are T8' means some P5 are T8 and some are not, so all P5 can never be T8: II follows. The A1 that are P5 need not be among the P5 that are T8, so I does not follow.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. NORMAL : PQTOCN :: REGARD : TGICTF :: TRAVEL : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: NORMAL → PQTOCN and REGARD → TGICTF. So TRAVEL → VTCXGN.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘planes get going’ is coded as ‘pn lm pg’, and ‘hard work get’ is coded as ‘kt rk lm’. ‘hard is you’ is coded as ‘ab rk fg’. What can be the code for ‘work’ in that language?
questions.explanation: 'Get', common to the first two phrases, is 'lm', and 'hard', common to the last two, is 'rk'. So 'work' is the remaining code of 'hard work get': 'kt'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 8 : 514 :: 3 : 29 :: 7 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the cube of the first plus 2: 8³ + 2 = 514 and 3³ + 2 = 29. So 7³ + 2 = 343 + 2 = 345.

questions.text: 4 males M1, M2, M3 and M4 are sitting in a row facing towards the west (not necessarily in the same order). 4 females F1, F2, F3 and F4 sitting in a row facing towards the face of these males (not necessarily in the same order). F4 is to the immediate right of F3. One female is sitting between F2 and F3. M3 is diagonally opposite to F2. M2 is second to the right of M4. Which of the following statements can be correct? I. M4 is facing F3. II. M2 is diagonally opposite to F4.
questions.explanation: The males face west, so their right is north, and the females face east, so their right is south. One arrangement that fits every clue, north to south: females F2, F1, F3, F4 and males M2, M1, M4, M3, with M3 and F2 at opposite ends of the two rows. Here M4 faces F3 and M2 is diagonally opposite F4, so both can be correct.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 14 : 19 :: 25 : 32 :: 103 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the first plus the sum of its digits: 14 + 1 + 4 = 19 and 25 + 2 + 5 = 32. So 103 + 1 + 0 + 3 = 107.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, and F are standing in a circle talking, facing the centre of the circle. E is standing immediate right to C. D is standing at the third position towards the left of C. A is standing at the second place towards the right of F. Who is standing to the immediate right of D?
questions.explanation: Going round to the right from C, E comes next and D is third after C (third to C's left is also third to its right among six). A, second to the right of F, then fits only with F between E and D and A just after D, leaving B last: C, E, F, D, A, B. So A is immediately to the right of D.

questions.text: The areas of seven circles C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6 and C7 are compared. The area of C2 is greater than C5 and less than C1. The area of C4 is greater than C7 and less than C6. The area of C5 is more than C6. If the area of C7 is the lowest, then which of the following options is correct?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'C3 > C6'. The statements give C1 > C2 > C5 > C6 > C4 > C7, which rules out the other three options; C3 is known only to be larger than C7, so 'C3 > C6' is the only option that can be true, though the statements do not settle it.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. POEM : TSIQ :: HINT : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places forward: POEM → TSIQ. So HINT → LMRX.

questions.text: After interchanging the given two signs, what will be the value of the following expression? × and ÷; 35 + 5 ÷ 4 × 2 – 15 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging × and ÷: 35 + 5 × 4 ÷ 2 − 15 = 35 + 10 − 15 = 30.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'WATER' is written as 'XBUFSVZSDQ' and ‘MINOR’ is written as ‘NJOPSLHMNQ’. How will 'ROSES' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is the word with each letter moved 1 forward, followed by the word with each letter moved 1 back: WATER → XBUFS + VZSDQ. So ROSES → SPTFT + QNRDR: SPTFTQNRDR.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'TIN' is coded as '27', and 'GO' is coded as '8'. How will 'PALE' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is the cube of the number of letters: TIN → 3³ = 27 and GO → 2³ = 8. So PALE → 4³ = 64.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 13, 39, 156, 780, ?
questions.explanation: The terms are multiplied by 3, 4, 5 and 6 in turn: 780 × 6 = 4680.

questions.text: In a certain code language, '752' means 'copper is strong', '276' means 'iron is strong' and '365' means 'iron and copper'. Find the code for 'and'.
questions.explanation: 'Is strong' is common to the first two (7 and 2), 'iron' to the last two (6) and 'copper' to the first and last (5). So 'and' is 3.

questions.text: Which two numbers (not digits) should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 21 × 3 − 10 + 4 ÷ 7 = 5
Select the letter from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. B, H, M, Q, T, ?
questions.explanation: The letters move forward 6, 5, 4 and 3 places: B → H → M → Q → T. The next step is 2: T → V.

questions.text: Select the option in which the two numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers in the given number pair. 32 : 85
questions.explanation: The second number is 53 more than the first: 32 + 53 = 85, and likewise 24 + 53 = 77.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. ABC2 : HIJ9 :: DEF5 : KLM12 :: OPQ16 : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 7 places forward and the number rises by 7: ABC2 → HIJ9 and DEF5 → KLM12. So OPQ16 → VWX23.

questions.text: The reaction between an acid and a base to give a salt and water is called ______.
questions.explanation: In a neutralisation reaction an acid and a base cancel each other's effect, forming a salt and water.

questions.text: Who among the following was the first Mauryan ruler who tried to spread his message to the people through inscriptions?
questions.explanation: Ashoka was the first ruler who tried to take his message, his dhamma, to the people through inscriptions on rocks and pillars.

questions.text: The book ‘The Immortals of Meluha’ has been written by ______.
questions.explanation: 'The Immortals of Meluha' (2010), the first book of the Shiva Trilogy, is by Amish Tripathi.

questions.text: The Behdienkhlam festival is primarily celebrated in the state of:
questions.explanation: Behdienkhlam is the festival of the Pnar (Jaintia) people of Meghalaya, held at Jowai in July after the sowing, to drive away disease and evil.

questions.text: India got its central bank in ______.
questions.explanation: The Reserve Bank of India, India's central bank, was set up on 1 April 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a fibre crop?
questions.explanation: Hemp is grown for its fibre; cotton, jute, hemp and natural silk are India's major fibre crops. Rubber is a plantation crop grown for its latex, and coffee a beverage crop.

questions.text: Which country won the maximum number of medals at 2020 Summer Olympic Games (played in 2021)?
questions.explanation: The United States won the most medals at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, 113, including 39 gold, ahead of China.

questions.text: Mehrunnisa married Emperor Jahangir in ______.
questions.explanation: Mehrunnisa married Jahangir in 1611 and was given the title Nur Mahal, 'light of the palace'; she later became Nur Jahan, 'light of the world'.

questions.text: Shyam is suffering from Beriberi. This is because he has a deficiency of ________.
questions.explanation: Beriberi is caused by a lack of thiamine, vitamin B1.

questions.text: Which of the following musical instruments is Ustad Zakir Hussain primarily associated with?
questions.explanation: Ustad Zakir Hussain, son and disciple of the tabla maestro Ustad Alla Rakha, was a world-renowned tabla player.

questions.text: Which of the following states has the highest sex ratio in India according to Census 2021?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Kerala. No census was taken in 2021 (it was postponed), so the question rests on Census 2011, in which Kerala had the highest sex ratio of any state, 1,084 females per 1,000 males.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which freedom fighter abolished the Zamindari System in Uttar Pradesh and was elected as the Home Minister in 1955?
questions.explanation: As Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, Govind Ballabh Pant brought in the abolition of the zamindari system in the state; in January 1955 he became Union Home Minister.

questions.text: Growth rate of population refers to the:
options: difference between birth rate and GDP
addition of birth rate and death rate
difference between birth rate and death rate
difference between death rate and GDP
questions.explanation: The natural growth rate of a population is the birth rate minus the death rate.

questions.text: The climate of India is described as which of the following types?
questions.explanation: India's climate is described as the monsoon type, marked by the seasonal reversal of winds.

questions.text: Which of the following teams won the Syed Mushtaq Ali (cricket) Trophy, 2021-22?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu retained the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy in 2021-22, beating Karnataka by four wickets in the final in November 2021.

questions.text: In 1590, the Govind Deva temple of Vrindavan, near Mathura was constructed from ______ sandstone.
questions.explanation: The Govind Deva temple at Vrindavan, built in 1590 under Raja Man Singh of Amber, is of red sandstone.

questions.text: Over which state in India does the Mahanadi basin NOT extend?
questions.explanation: The Mahanadi basin lies mainly in Chhattisgarh and Odisha, with smaller parts in Jharkhand, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh; it does not reach Uttar Pradesh.

questions.text: Which of the following dance forms of India is associated with Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Kalbelia is the folk dance of the Kalbelia community of Rajasthan. Kathak is a classical dance of north India, chiefly Uttar Pradesh, Bharatanatyam belongs to Tamil Nadu and Odissi to Odisha.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: All of the following are freedom fighters of India who were hanged to death on 23 March 1931 in the Lahore conspiracy case, EXCEPT _________.
questions.explanation: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were hanged in Lahore Jail on 23 March 1931. Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated in 1948.

questions.text: Sameer wants to contest Lok Sabha elections in India. At what age can he do that?
questions.explanation: Under Article 84(b) a member of the Lok Sabha must be at least 25 years old.

questions.text: Nirmala Sitharaman launched the Tejasvini scheme for the people of ______ in November 2021.
questions.explanation: Nirmala Sitharaman launched the Tejaswini scheme, which gives young women in Jammu and Kashmir financial help to start their own ventures, at the University of Jammu in November 2021.

questions.text: Athlete's foot is a disease caused by _________.
questions.explanation: Athlete's foot (tinea pedis) is a fungal infection of the skin of the feet.

questions.text: Which article of the Indian Constitution provides freedom to manage religious affairs?
questions.explanation: Article 26 gives every religious denomination the freedom to manage its own religious affairs, to set up institutions and to own and administer property.

questions.text: Who among the following was crowned Miss Universe, 2021?
questions.explanation: Harnaaz Sandhu of India was crowned Miss Universe 2021 in December 2021, the third Indian to win after Sushmita Sen and Lara Dutta. Andrea Meza of Mexico was Miss Universe 2020.

questions.text: Who among the following is India’s last living Sadhir dancer, honoured with Padma Shri in 2022?
questions.explanation: R Muthukannammal of Viralimalai, Tamil Nadu, among the last exponents of Sadhir, the temple dance from which Bharatanatyam developed, received the Padma Shri in 2022.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. I tried to tell him to think of the good times, that “every cloud has a silver lining.”
options: Doing something with thoroughness and passion
Don’t cry over what has happened as it cannot be fixed
Treat people the same way as you want to be treated
Every difficult situation has a hopeful aspect to it
questions.explanation: 'Every cloud has a silver lining' means that even a bad or difficult situation has something hopeful or good in it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Expository
questions.explanation: 'Expository' means meant to explain or describe, as is 'illustrative'. 'Temperamental' means moody, 'obligatory' compulsory and 'dubious' doubtful.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The first printed ______ of this book came in 1933.
questions.explanation: An 'edition' is one printed version of a book, so the first printed edition is its first publication.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Pull someone’s legs
questions.explanation: To pull someone's leg (as the idiom usually goes) is to tease them playfully, often by making them believe something untrue.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who produces beautiful handwriting
questions.explanation: A calligrapher practises calligraphy, the art of beautiful handwriting. A stenographer writes in shorthand, and a typographer designs and arranges printed type.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. He certainly failed to “console” the new king.
questions.explanation: To 'console' is to comfort someone in distress, so its opposite is 'agitate', to upset or disturb. 'Gratify' and 'satiate' mean to please or satisfy.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'simultaneous', ending in '-taneous'; the other three drop, swap or change a vowel in that ending.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. His successful as a lawyer / grew so fast that he soon had / enough money to buy a house.
options: grew so fast that he soon had
enough money to buy a house
questions.explanation: The subject of 'grew' must be a noun, not the adjective 'successful': 'His success as a lawyer grew so fast that he soon had enough money to buy a house.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A state of perfect balance
questions.explanation: 'Equilibrium' is a state of balance between opposing forces. 'Extempore' means without preparation and 'medieval' belonging to the Middle Ages.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Admirable
questions.explanation: 'Admirable' means deserving praise, so its opposite is 'blameworthy', deserving blame.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. The enemies “have cross” the border, treading the soil on which they are to be conquered.
questions.explanation: The present perfect is 'have' with the past participle, and the plural 'enemies' takes 'have': 'The enemies have crossed the border.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Consumers are not ready to purchase this citrus fruit at such a ______ price.
questions.explanation: 'Such a' takes the plain adjective before a noun: 'at such a high price'. 'Higher' would need 'than', 'highest' needs 'the', and 'highly' is an adverb.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Other South African cities only / had one venue for staging exhibitions or / internationals events at highly standard.
options: had one venue for staging exhibitions or
questions.explanation: An adjective before a noun takes no plural ending, and 'standard' needs the adjective 'high', not the adverb 'highly': 'international events of a high standard'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Sparkling
questions.explanation: 'Sparkling' means shining brightly, as 'gleaming' does. 'Dismal', 'muffled' and 'unexciting' suggest dullness.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Please don’t ______ anyone that I came to your birthday party.
questions.explanation: After 'don't' comes the base form of the verb, and 'tell' takes the person told as its object: 'don't tell anyone'. 'Say' needs 'to' before the person ('say to anyone').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Seclude
questions.explanation: To 'seclude' is to keep oneself or someone away from other people, so its opposite is to 'socialize', to mix with others. 'Confine' and 'isolate' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. A sustained decline in Chinese consumption would be even more ______ than the current US-China trade dispute.
questions.explanation: A lasting fall in Chinese spending would be a cause for concern, even more 'worrying' than the trade dispute; the other words do not fit the sense.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In a significant find, the Epigraphy Branch of the Archaeological Survey of India (1) ______ discovered the earliest epigraphic evidence so far for the Saptamatrika cult. It is also (2) ______ earliest Sanskrit inscription to have been discovered (3) ______ South India as of date. Saptamatrikas are a group of seven female deities worshipped in Hinduism as personifying the energy of their respective consorts. The inscription is in Sanskrit and in Brahmi characters and was (4) ______ by Satavahana King Vijaya in 207 A.D. The inscription came to light when some local villagers informed the authorities of the presence of a pillar with some engravings when they were restoring and (5) ______ the local Bheemeshwara temple.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'The Epigraphy Branch' is singular, so the present perfect takes 'has': 'has discovered'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In a significant find, the Epigraphy Branch of the Archaeological Survey of India (1) ______ discovered the earliest epigraphic evidence so far for the Saptamatrika cult. It is also (2) ______ earliest Sanskrit inscription to have been discovered (3) ______ South India as of date. Saptamatrikas are a group of seven female deities worshipped in Hinduism as personifying the energy of their respective consorts. The inscription is in Sanskrit and in Brahmi characters and was (4) ______ by Satavahana King Vijaya in 207 A.D. The inscription came to light when some local villagers informed the authorities of the presence of a pillar with some engravings when they were restoring and (5) ______ the local Bheemeshwara temple.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: A superlative such as 'earliest' takes 'the': 'the earliest Sanskrit inscription'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In a significant find, the Epigraphy Branch of the Archaeological Survey of India (1) ______ discovered the earliest epigraphic evidence so far for the Saptamatrika cult. It is also (2) ______ earliest Sanskrit inscription to have been discovered (3) ______ South India as of date. Saptamatrikas are a group of seven female deities worshipped in Hinduism as personifying the energy of their respective consorts. The inscription is in Sanskrit and in Brahmi characters and was (4) ______ by Satavahana King Vijaya in 207 A.D. The inscription came to light when some local villagers informed the authorities of the presence of a pillar with some engravings when they were restoring and (5) ______ the local Bheemeshwara temple.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'In' goes with a region: discovered 'in South India'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In a significant find, the Epigraphy Branch of the Archaeological Survey of India (1) ______ discovered the earliest epigraphic evidence so far for the Saptamatrika cult. It is also (2) ______ earliest Sanskrit inscription to have been discovered (3) ______ South India as of date. Saptamatrikas are a group of seven female deities worshipped in Hinduism as personifying the energy of their respective consorts. The inscription is in Sanskrit and in Brahmi characters and was (4) ______ by Satavahana King Vijaya in 207 A.D. The inscription came to light when some local villagers informed the authorities of the presence of a pillar with some engravings when they were restoring and (5) ______ the local Bheemeshwara temple.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: A king 'issues' an inscription or edict, that is, has it made and put up: 'was issued by Satavahana King Vijaya'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In a significant find, the Epigraphy Branch of the Archaeological Survey of India (1) ______ discovered the earliest epigraphic evidence so far for the Saptamatrika cult. It is also (2) ______ earliest Sanskrit inscription to have been discovered (3) ______ South India as of date. Saptamatrikas are a group of seven female deities worshipped in Hinduism as personifying the energy of their respective consorts. The inscription is in Sanskrit and in Brahmi characters and was (4) ______ by Satavahana King Vijaya in 207 A.D. The inscription came to light when some local villagers informed the authorities of the presence of a pillar with some engravings when they were restoring and (5) ______ the local Bheemeshwara temple.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Repairing' goes with 'restoring' as work done on an old building: 'restoring and repairing the local Bheemeshwara temple'.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 864, 432, 216, 108,?
questions.explanation: Each term is half the one before: 108 ÷ 2 = 54.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'PAR' is coded as ‘35' and 'GAT' is coded as ‘28'. How will 'FOM' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet: P + A + R = 16 + 1 + 18 = 35 and G + A + T = 7 + 1 + 20 = 28. So F + O + M = 6 + 15 + 13 = 34.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 25 : 125 :: 32 : 160 :: 73 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second number is 5 times the first: 25 × 5 = 125 and 32 × 5 = 160. So 73 × 5 = 365.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (36, 2, 3)(108, 6, 3)
questions.explanation: In each set the first number is 6 times the product of the other two: 2 × 3 × 6 = 36 and 6 × 3 × 6 = 108. Likewise 4 × 2 × 6 = 48; the other sets give 150, 108 and 48 instead of 120, 102 and 28.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. CET : ZBQ :: KVO : HSL :: QRS : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back: C, E, T → Z, B, Q and K, V, O → H, S, L. So Q, R, S → N, O, P: NOP.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statement I: An IT employee working in XYZ company has two children. Statement II: No other employee in XYZ has two children. Conclusion I: Every employee in the company has at least one child. Conclusion II: Some of the employees have more than two children.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: The statements say only who in the company has two children: nothing about whether every employee has a child, or whether anyone has more than two. So neither conclusion follows.

questions.text: What will be the value of the following expression, if ‘+’ and ‘×’ are interchanged and ‘−’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 8 × 10 + 3 − 5 ÷ 6 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 8 + 10 × 3 ÷ 5 − 6 = 8 + 6 − 6 = 8.

questions.text: Select the option in which the pair of letter-clusters share the same relationship as that shared by the given letter-clusters. RS : IH
questions.explanation: Each letter is paired with its opposite in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on): R↔I and S↔H. Likewise T↔G and M↔N.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 72, 66, 63, 57, 54, 48, ?
In a certain code language, 'SEAT' is written as '2' and 'CHARGE' is written as '4'. How will 'ONLINE' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is the number of consonants: SEAT has 2 (S, T) and CHARGE has 4 (C, H, R, G). ONLINE has 3 (N, L, N).

questions.text: Six friends, Kushal, Keshav, Kishan, Kamal, Kanan and Kishore, are of different heights. Keshav is taller than only three other friends. Kishore is taller than Kamal only. Kishan is shorter than Kushal only.Who is the third shortest among all the friends?
questions.explanation: Kamal is the shortest and Kishore the second shortest; Kushal is the tallest and Kishan the second tallest; Keshav, taller than only three, is fourth from the bottom. That leaves Kanan third shortest.

questions.text: Five men O1, O2, O3, O4 and O5 are sitting around a circular table facing opposite to the centre (not necessarily in the same order). Only one man is sitting between O4 and O5 in clockwise direction. Only one man is sitting between O3 and O4 in clockwise direction. O1 is sitting to the immediate left of O3. Who is sitting third from the left of O2?
questions.explanation: Facing outwards, a man's left is the next seat anticlockwise. Counting clockwise from O4 to O5 and from O3 to O4 would put O5 on O3's immediate left, where O1 must sit, so the gaps run clockwise from O5 to O4 and from O4 to O3: clockwise, O5, O2, O4, O1, O3. Counting to the left of O2: O5, O3, then O1.

questions.text: In a certain code language, '254' means 'You are intelligent', '153' means 'Nikhil is intelligent', '398' means 'Naina and Nikhil', then what is the code for 'is' in the same code language?
questions.explanation: 'Intelligent' is common to the first two sentences and 5 to their codes; 'Nikhil' is common to the last two and 3 to theirs. So in '153', 'is' is 1.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some peas are pineapples. No pineapple is a broccoli. All broccolis are potatoes. Conclusions: I. Some peas being potatoes is a possibility. II. All pineapples being potatoes is a possibility.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: No pineapple is a broccoli, but potatoes need not all be broccolis, so peas and pineapples may both be potatoes outside the broccolis: both possibilities hold.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. GA, MU, SO, ?, EC
questions.explanation: The first letters move 6 forward (G, M, S, Y, E) and the second letters 6 back (A, U, O, I, C): YI.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘pinch of salt grey’ is written as ‘ab tr # kp’, ‘grey colour is black’ is written as ‘# jm bk if’ and ‘colour are of track’ is written as ‘gt if ab fr’. How will ‘grey of’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: 'Grey' is common to the first two sentences and '#' to their codes; 'of' is common to the first and third and 'ab' to theirs. So 'grey of' is written 'ab #'.

questions.text: By interchanging the two signs ÷ and + and two numbers 9 and 12 (NOT digits), which of the following equations will NOT be correct? I. 12 × 2 – 72 + 9 ÷ 57 = 69; II. 169 + 13 × 12 ÷ 3 – 9 = 108
questions.explanation: After the interchange, I becomes 9 × 2 − 72 ÷ 12 + 57 = 18 − 6 + 57 = 69 and II becomes 169 ÷ 13 × 9 + 3 − 12 = 117 + 3 − 12 = 108. Both are correct, so neither is wrong.

questions.text: Ajay, Priti, Rakesh, Mehak, Saloni and Yogesh are sitting in a row facing north. Saloni and Yogesh are sitting in the centre. Ajay and Priti are at the ends. Rakesh is sitting to the immediate left of Ajay.Who is sitting to the immediate right of Priti?
questions.explanation: Facing north, left is west. Rakesh is on Ajay's immediate left, so Ajay is at the right end with Rakesh next to him and Priti at the left end. Saloni and Yogesh take the two middle seats, so Mehak sits second from the left, immediately right of Priti.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word and the fourth word is related to the third word. Vehicle : Car :: Food : Pizza :: Crockery : ?
questions.explanation: A car is a kind of vehicle and a pizza a kind of food; likewise a plate is a piece of crockery.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: ____________, popularly known as Punjab Kesari took his last breath on November 17th, 1928
questions.explanation: Lala Lajpat Rai, called 'Punjab Kesari' (the Lion of Punjab), died in Lahore on 17 November 1928, weeks after he was injured in a police lathi charge during a protest against the Simon Commission.

questions.text: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment incorporated Dadra, Nagar and Haveli in the Union of India as a Union Territory?
questions.explanation: The Tenth Amendment Act, 1961 made Dadra and Nagar Haveli a Union Territory. The Twelfth (1962) did the same for Goa, Daman and Diu, and the Fourteenth (1962) for Puducherry.

questions.text: Guru Bipin Singh received ‘Sangeet Natak Akademi Award’ in the year 1966. He was a teacher of _______ dance.
questions.explanation: Guru Bipin Singh (1918-2000) was a leading teacher, choreographer and scholar of Manipuri dance, who founded the Manipuri Nartanalaya in Kolkata.

questions.text: Smart cities and Academia Towards Action and Research (SAAR) scheme was launched by the ______.
options: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
questions.explanation: SAAR is a programme of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and the National Institute of Urban Affairs in which 15 leading architecture and planning institutes document landmark projects of the Smart Cities Mission.

questions.text: In which state of India is the Moatsu festival celebrated every year?
questions.explanation: Moatsu is the festival of the Ao Nagas of Nagaland, held in the first week of May after the sowing season.

questions.text: Which of the following pair of ‘Name of Ruler – Empire’ is correctly matched? I. Mahapadma Nanda – Magadha Empire; II. Ajatasattu – Maurya Empire
questions.explanation: Mahapadma Nanda founded the Nanda dynasty, which ruled the Magadha empire. Ajatasattu (Ajatashatru) was a king of Magadha of the earlier Haryanka dynasty, long before the Mauryas, so only I is correct.

questions.text: How many types of igneous rocks are there?
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks are of two types: intrusive (plutonic) rocks, which cool slowly from magma below the surface, such as granite, and extrusive (volcanic) rocks, which cool fast from lava on it, such as basalt.

questions.text: Which of the following terms is NOT associated with hockey?
questions.explanation: A run out is a way of dismissing a batter in cricket. The scoop, the flick and the hit are strokes in hockey.

questions.text: In which state of India is the Gulbarga Fort situated?
questions.explanation: The fort stands at Gulbarga (now Kalaburagi) in northern Karnataka, the first capital of the Bahmani Sultanate, founded in 1347.

questions.text: Which of the following formulas is correct for Gross Value Added?
options: Gross Value Added = Gross National Product – Subsidies + Taxes
Gross Value Added = Gross Domestic Product – Subsidies + Taxes
Gross Value Added = Gross National Product + Subsidies – Taxes
Gross Value Added = Gross Domestic Product + Subsidies – Taxes
questions.explanation: GVA (at basic prices) is GDP (at market prices) less the taxes on products plus the subsidies on products.

questions.text: ______ is used to get rid of indigestion.
questions.explanation: An antacid is a mild base that neutralises excess acid in the stomach, relieving indigestion and acidity. Analgesics relieve pain, antiseptics stop the growth of germs on living tissue, and antibiotics kill bacteria.

questions.text: Which of the following countries had a higher average population density than India in 2020 as per Food and Agriculture Organization and World Bank population estimates?
questions.explanation: World Bank figures for 2020 put Bangladesh at well over 1,000 people per square kilometre of land, more than twice India's (over 450). Sri Lanka (about 350), China (about 150) and Russia (under 10) were all less densely populated than India.

questions.text: ‘Waiting for a Visa’ is a 20-page autobiography written by _____________.
questions.explanation: B R Ambedkar wrote 'Waiting for a Visa', a short, unfinished account of untouchability drawn mostly from his own experiences, in 1935-36.

questions.text: AR Rahman won the Grammy Awards for which movie?
questions.explanation: A R Rahman won two Grammy Awards in 2010 for 'Slumdog Millionaire': for its soundtrack album and for the song 'Jai Ho'.

questions.text: Shovana Narayan is associated with which classical dance of India?
questions.explanation: Shovana Narayan is a Kathak dancer and teacher, honoured with the Padma Shri.

questions.text: Which Constitutional Amendment Act included Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Forty-second Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, added the Fundamental Duties as Part IV-A (Article 51A).

questions.text: Queen Rudramadevi belonged to which dynasty of India?
questions.explanation: Rudramadevi was a ruler of the Kakatiya dynasty in the 13th century, governing from Warangal (Orugallu) in present-day Telangana.

questions.text: The SI unit of work is ______.
questions.explanation: Work is measured in joules: 1 joule is the work done when a force of 1 newton moves its point of application 1 metre. Pascal is the unit of pressure, hertz of frequency, and the decibel measures sound level.

questions.text: Which of the following is a rabi crop?
questions.explanation: Gram is a rabi crop, sown in winter and harvested in spring. Groundnut, maize and paddy are kharif crops, sown with the monsoon.

questions.text: Which of the following persons was conferred with the 57th Jnanpith Award?
questions.explanation: The Konkani writer Damodar Mauzo of Goa was named for the 57th Jnanpith Award in December 2021, along with the Assamese poet Nilmani Phookan for the 56th. Krishna Sobti, Kedarnath Singh and Amitav Ghosh received earlier Jnanpith Awards.

questions.text: The distribution of the population according to different types of occupation is known as __________.
questions.explanation: Occupational structure is how a population is divided among occupations, such as farming, manufacturing and services. Age composition is its division by age.

questions.text: _______________ is commonly known as imperfect fungi because only the asexual or vegetative phases of these fungi are known.
questions.explanation: Deuteromycetes are called the imperfect fungi because no sexual stage is known for them: they reproduce only by asexual spores (conidia). When a sexual stage is found, the fungus is moved to the Ascomycetes or Basidiomycetes.

questions.text: ______________ is broadly divided into Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the Deccan Plateau: the Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats mark its western and eastern edges, and of the options it is the only one the two Ghats belong to. (NCERT's Class 9 geography divides the Peninsular Plateau into the Central Highlands and the Deccan Plateau.)

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: When Alivardi Khan died in 1756, ______ became the nawab of Bengal.
questions.explanation: Siraj-ud-daulah, Alivardi Khan's grandson, succeeded him as Nawab of Bengal in 1756; he lost the Battle of Plassey to the East India Company in 1757.

questions.text: Which Indian Olympian is associated with golf?
questions.explanation: Aditi Ashok is a golfer; she finished fourth in women's golf at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics. Abhinav Bindra is a shooter, Neeraj Chopra a javelin thrower and Ravi Kumar Dahiya a wrestler.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I __________ walked down the stairs, careful to be as quiet as possible.
questions.explanation: Someone trying to be as quiet as possible walks 'cautiously', with care. 'Furiously' clashes with the quiet, and 'neatly' and 'orderly' do not describe careful movement.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. I am looking forward / to meets you / at the convocation party.
questions.explanation: In 'look forward to', 'to' is a preposition, so it takes a gerund: 'I am looking forward to meeting you'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Escalate
questions.explanation: To 'escalate' is to rise or increase rapidly; to 'plunge' is to fall suddenly and steeply.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Most natural diamonds have some type of______.
questions.explanation: A 'flaw' is a defect or imperfection, which most natural diamonds have. 'Flow', 'flour' and 'floor' look or sound similar but make no sense here.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. The eggs “are warm into” a suitable temperature for the larvae to hatch from eggs.
questions.explanation: The eggs receive the action, so the verb is passive, 'are warmed', and 'to' marks the temperature reached: 'The eggs are warmed to a suitable temperature'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Peterkin readjusted his hat and soon was listening to the conversation with “as much interest” as I was.
questions.explanation: 'Interest' here is uncountable, so it takes 'much', not 'many', and an equal comparison is 'as much ... as': the sentence is correct as it stands.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Delighted
questions.explanation: 'Delighted' means very pleased: 'joyful'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. It was the last ______ of the puzzle.
questions.explanation: A 'piece' is one part of a puzzle. 'Peace' (calm) sounds the same but means something else.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. My father ______ home last week.
questions.explanation: 'Last week' fixes the action in the past, so the simple past is needed: 'My father went home last week'. The present perfect 'has gone' does not go with a past time expression.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A collection of selected writings of various authors
questions.explanation: An anthology is a collection of selected writings by various authors. A trilogy is a set of three related works, a sequel a work that continues an earlier one, and etymology the study of word origins.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'executive'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. By hook or by crook
questions.explanation: To do something 'by hook or by crook' is to do it by any means, fair or unfair.

questions.text: Select the option that corrects the incorrectly spelt words in the given sentence. Her expresion grew blaend again.
questions.explanation: 'Expresion' should be 'expression' and 'blaend' should be 'bland' (without expression or emotion); 'blend' is a different word.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. It’s not possible to ______ this house in this amount.
questions.explanation: To 'renovate' a house is to repair and modernise it, which the sentence says cannot be done for this sum.'Astonish', 'console' and 'bleat' make no sense with a house.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Soon or later, our efforts will be rewarded.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is 'sooner or later', meaning at some time in the future: 'Sooner or later, our efforts will be rewarded.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Bolt from the blue
options: To win a large sum of money
questions.explanation: A 'bolt from the blue' is a sudden, completely unexpected event or piece of news, like lightning from a clear sky.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. I have not saw / your sister since she / came to this city.
questions.explanation: The present perfect is 'have' with the past participle: 'I have not seen your sister since she came to this city.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A short story with a moral
questions.explanation: A parable is a short, simple story told to teach a moral or spiritual lesson. A memoir and a biography are accounts of a life, and an axiom is a statement accepted as true.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Imitate
questions.explanation: To 'imitate' is to 'copy' someone or something.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Variety
questions.explanation: 'Variety' means difference or diversity, so its opposite is 'similarity'. 'Diversity' and 'medley' are close in meaning to 'variety', and 'fusion' is a blending.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Every now and then there are going to be bad days, tough days, moods swings and all things nasty that may put a (1) ______ on our happy days. At any given moment, however, we are the ones who can make a (2)______ between letting these things get in the way or pushing them right out by (3) ______ time in things or people (4) ______ make us happy. I've had this list of things that has made me happy for years now. I made it back in college to help me deal with some difficult times that I faced then. Even today, every now and then when things go (5) ______ I always go back to this, and one or more things listed here always lights me up!

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: To 'put a damper on' something is to make it less cheerful: bad days spoil happy ones.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Every now and then there are going to be bad days, tough days, moods swings and all things nasty that may put a (1) ______ on our happy days. At any given moment, however, we are the ones who can make a (2)______ between letting these things get in the way or pushing them right out by (3) ______ time in things or people (4) ______ make us happy. I've had this list of things that has made me happy for years now. I made it back in college to help me deal with some difficult times that I faced then. Even today, every now and then when things go (5) ______ I always go back to this, and one or more things listed here always lights me up!

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: We 'make a choice between' two courses: letting these things get in the way or pushing them out.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Every now and then there are going to be bad days, tough days, moods swings and all things nasty that may put a (1) ______ on our happy days. At any given moment, however, we are the ones who can make a (2)______ between letting these things get in the way or pushing them right out by (3) ______ time in things or people (4) ______ make us happy. I've had this list of things that has made me happy for years now. I made it back in college to help me deal with some difficult times that I faced then. Even today, every now and then when things go (5) ______ I always go back to this, and one or more things listed here always lights me up!

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Time is 'invested in' things or people, given to them for a return, here happiness. 'Spending' would take 'on' or 'with'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Every now and then there are going to be bad days, tough days, moods swings and all things nasty that may put a (1) ______ on our happy days. At any given moment, however, we are the ones who can make a (2)______ between letting these things get in the way or pushing them right out by (3) ______ time in things or people (4) ______ make us happy. I've had this list of things that has made me happy for years now. I made it back in college to help me deal with some difficult times that I faced then. Even today, every now and then when things go (5) ______ I always go back to this, and one or more things listed here always lights me up!

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'who': a relative pronoun follows the nearer noun of a mixed pair, here 'people'. 'That', which suits things and people together, is not offered, and 'which' would refer to things alone.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Every now and then there are going to be bad days, tough days, moods swings and all things nasty that may put a (1) ______ on our happy days. At any given moment, however, we are the ones who can make a (2)______ between letting these things get in the way or pushing them right out by (3) ______ time in things or people (4) ______ make us happy. I've had this list of things that has made me happy for years now. I made it back in college to help me deal with some difficult times that I faced then. Even today, every now and then when things go (5) ______ I always go back to this, and one or more things listed here always lights me up!

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: When things 'go wrong', that is, turn out badly, the writer turns to the list for cheer.

questions.text: Six people, Ambika, Charu, Riya, Ashi, Rahul and Ajay, are sitting in a straight row facing north (but not necessarily in the same order). Only two people sit between Rahul and Riya. Neither Ajay nor Riya is sitting at any of the corners. Ashi is sitting second to the left of Riya. Ajay and Charu are immediate neighbours. Who is sitting next to Ashi?
questions.explanation: Riya is not at a corner and Ashi is second to her left, so Riya is 3rd, 4th or 5th from the left, with Rahul three seats from her; Riya 5th leaves Ajay and Charu no two seats side by side. The row is then either Ashi, Ambika, Riya, Ajay and Charu (either order), Rahul, or Rahul, Ashi, Ambika, Riya, Ajay, Charu: Ambika sits next to Ashi in both, Rahul only in the second.

questions.text: Select the option in which the two numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers in the given number-pair. 40 : 19 :: ?
questions.explanation: The second number is half the first minus 1: 40 ÷ 2 − 1 = 19. Likewise 28 ÷ 2 − 1 = 13; the other pairs fail (20 ÷ 2 − 1 = 9, 34 ÷ 2 − 1 = 16, 46 ÷ 2 − 1 = 22).

questions.text: Among seven brothers, Aman, Bunty, Chintu, Deepak, Ishan, Hari and Golu, Bunty is taller than only four other brothers. Chintu is taller than Deepak. Aman is taller than Hari. Ishan is taller than only Golu, who is the shortest among all the brothers. Bunty is taller than Aman. Given that no two brothers have the same height, who is the tallest among the seven brothers?
questions.explanation: Bunty, taller than exactly four, is 3rd tallest; Ishan is 6th and Golu 7th. Aman and Hari are both shorter than Bunty, so they are 4th and 5th, leaving the top two places to Chintu and Deepak. As Chintu is taller than Deepak, Chintu is the tallest.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. CA : GH :: TK : ?
questions.explanation: C + 4 = G and A + 7 = H. Likewise T + 4 = X and K + 7 = R: XR.

questions.text: In a certain code language, if star is called moon, moon is called planet, planet is called sun, sun is called solar system, and solar system is called galaxy, then what is the Earth's only natural satellite?
questions.explanation: The Earth's only natural satellite is the moon, and in this code the moon is called 'planet'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. SON : TPO :: BRO : CSP :: BIL : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward: SON → TPO and BRO → CSP. So BIL → CJM.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'GEAR' is coded as '16', 'ANT' is coded as '9' and 'HEART' is coded as '25'. How will 'TEAR' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded as the square of its number of letters: GEAR 4² = 16, ANT 3² = 9 and HEART 5² = 25. TEAR has 4 letters: 16.

questions.text: Which two signs need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 72 − 12 + 8 × 6 ÷ 22 = 32
questions.explanation: With − and ÷ interchanged: 72 ÷ 12 + 8 × 6 − 22 = 6 + 48 − 22 = 32.

questions.text: What will be the value of the following expression, if ‘+’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 5 − 3 ÷ 8 × 12 + 4
questions.explanation: After the interchanges: 5 + 3 × 8 ÷ 12 − 4 = 5 + 24 ÷ 12 − 4 = 5 + 2 − 4 = 3.

questions.text: Six friends are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Aman is sitting second right to Sneha. Tushar is immediate left to Sneha. Ritika is not the immediate neighbour of either Sneha or Tushar. Ritika is sitting second right to Prerna. Sharique is sitting in between Ritika and Tushar. Who is is the immediate neighbour of both Tushar and Prerna?
questions.explanation: Aman is two seats to Sneha's right and Tushar on her left. Ritika, beside neither Sneha nor Tushar, must sit opposite Sneha; Prerna, two seats to Ritika's left, is then on Sneha's right, and Sharique sits between Ritika and Tushar. Sneha sits between Tushar and Prerna.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 39 : 72 :: 217 : 428 :: 135 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is twice the first minus 6: 39 × 2 − 6 = 72 and 217 × 2 − 6 = 428. So 135 × 2 − 6 = 264.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'HALT' is written as 'SZOG', and 'CROM' is written as 'XILN'. How will 'PIGY' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on): HALT → SZOG and CROM → XILN. So PIGY → KRTB.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. No B is L. II. No C is B. Conclusions: I. Some L are C. II. Some B are C.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: 'No C is B' means no B is C, so II is false. The statements link L and C only through B, from which both are excluded, so nothing follows about L and C, and I does not follow either.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 21, 23, 20, 22, 19, 21, ?
In a certain code language, 'RARE' is written as '2' and 'CAT' is written as '1'. How will 'RICKSAW' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded by its number of vowels: RARE has A and E (2) and CAT has A (1). RICKSAW has I and A: 2.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. PC, NA, LY, JW, ?
questions.explanation: Both letters move two places back each time: P, N, L, J, H and C, A, Y, W, U (wrapping round after A). The next term is HU.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. VIOLET : WUJHPNMKFDUS :: RING : SQJHOMHF :: NEED : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by the letter after it and the letter before it: V → WU, I → JH, O → PN, L → MK, E → FD, T → US. So NEED → OM FD FD EC: OMFDFDEC.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 3678 : 3747 :: 1052 : 1121 :: 96 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the first plus 69: 3678 + 69 = 3747 and 1052 + 69 = 1121. So 96 + 69 = 165.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some fans are bulbs. Some bulbs are tube lights. Some tube lights are coolers. Conclusions: I. Some fans are coolers. II. Some tube lights are fans.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Each 'some' statement links only one pair (fans and bulbs, bulbs and tube lights, tube lights and coolers), so nothing definite follows about fans and coolers or about tube lights and fans.

questions.text: What is the duration of a football match (in regular time)?
questions.explanation: A football match lasts 90 minutes of regular time, two halves of 45 minutes; stoppage time and any extra time come on top.

questions.text: What is the total number of periods and groups in the Modern Periodic Table?
questions.explanation: The modern (long-form) periodic table has 7 horizontal rows, the periods, and 18 vertical columns, the groups.

questions.text: In which year did India win its first International Cricket Council(ICC) ODI World Cup?
questions.explanation: India first won the ODI World Cup in 1983 under Kapil Dev, beating the West Indies in the final at Lord's; its second title came in 2011.

questions.text: Bhagwant Mann became the Chief Minister of ________ in March 2022.
questions.explanation: Bhagwant Mann of the Aam Aadmi Party became Chief Minister of Punjab in March 2022, after his party won the state's assembly election.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Sayyid Ahmed Khan founded Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College in _________ in 1875.
questions.explanation: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh in 1875; it grew into Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

questions.text: Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma is known for which classical dance form?
questions.explanation: Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma (1935-2012) was a Kuchipudi dancer famed for female roles, above all Satyabhama in 'Bhama Kalapam'; he received the Padma Shri in 1970.

questions.text: The revenue system of Mughal period during Akbar’s reign was called ______.
questions.explanation: Under Akbar, with Raja Todar Mal, land revenue was assessed by the zabt system: land was measured and the tax fixed in cash from average yields and prices. The iqta belongs to the Delhi Sultanate, and ghari (house tax) and charai (grazing tax) to Alauddin Khalji.

questions.text: The Government of India flagship scheme called UJALA completed 7 years in January 2022. Under this scheme the Ministry of Power distributed ______.
questions.explanation: UJALA (Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All), launched on 5 January 2015 and run by Energy Efficiency Services Limited under the Ministry of Power, distributes LED bulbs to households at low prices.

questions.text: Which of the following is a neighbouring country of India?
questions.explanation: The Maldives, an island nation in the Indian Ocean south-west of India, is one of India's maritime neighbours. Australia, Iran and Russia do not border India.

questions.text: The deficiency of which of the following vitamins causes Pellagra?
questions.explanation: Pellagra is caused by a lack of niacin, vitamin B3; its signs are dermatitis, diarrhoea and dementia.

questions.text: Which Fundamental Right was removed by the Forty-fourth Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: The 44th Amendment (1978) took the right to property, Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31 ('Compulsory acquisition of property'), out of the Fundamental Rights; it is now a legal right under Article 300A.

questions.text: The Constitution of India has given power to the Supreme court to issue certain writs. How many types of these writs are mentioned in the constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 32 empowers the Supreme Court to issue five kinds of writs: habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo warranto.

questions.text: Harmandar Sahib is situated in which city of Punjab?
questions.explanation: Harmandir Sahib, the Golden Temple, the holiest gurdwara of the Sikhs, is in Amritsar.

questions.text: Which of the following books was written by Indian author RK Narayan?
questions.explanation: 'Malgudi Days' is R K Narayan's collection of stories set in the fictional town of Malgudi. 'The White Tiger' is by Aravind Adiga, 'Think Like a Monk' by Jay Shetty and 'The Shadow Lines' by Amitav Ghosh.

questions.text: Who among the following is referred to as ‘Prince of Bhangra’, due to his Bhangra music?
questions.explanation: The Bhangra singer Sukhbir Singh, known simply as Sukhbir ('Gal Ban Gayee', 'Ishq Tera Tadpave'), is called the 'Prince of Bhangra'.

questions.text: Through which of the following states does the Brahmaputra river enter India?
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra, the Tsangpo in Tibet, enters India in Arunachal Pradesh, where it is called the Siang or Dihang, and then flows into Assam.

questions.text: Which of the following is also known as ‘New Stone Age’ in the civilisation history of India?
questions.explanation: The Neolithic ('neo', new; 'lithos', stone) is the New Stone Age, marked by polished stone tools, farming and herding. The Palaeolithic is the Old and the Mesolithic the Middle Stone Age.

questions.text: Mushroom rocks are formed due to _____.
questions.explanation: Mushroom rocks form in deserts where wind-blown sand wears away the lower part of a rock faster than its top, leaving a narrow stem under a broad cap.

questions.text: _____________ is a type of mask dance that tells mythological stories via ferocious martial moves, popular in Odisha.
questions.explanation: Chhau, danced in Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal, enacts stories from the epics with vigorous martial movements. The Seraikela and Purulia styles use masks, while Odisha's Mayurbhanj style is danced without them.

questions.text: Which tax slab is applied in India if Individual taxpayer’s annual taxable income is more than ₹15 lakh?
questions.explanation: When the exam was held (July 2022), income above ₹15 lakh was taxed at 30% under both regimes: the old one, where the 30% slab began above ₹10 lakh, and the new one of Section 115BAC, where it began above ₹15 lakh.

questions.text: Tea cultivation is an example of which type of agriculture system?
questions.explanation: Tea is grown on large estates as a single cash crop for sale, with much capital and hired labour: plantation agriculture.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following British Viceroys partitioned Bengal in 1905?
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon, Viceroy from 1899 to 1905, partitioned Bengal in October 1905; the partition was annulled in 1911, under Lord Hardinge.

questions.text: As per Census 2011, which of the following states of India has the highest population?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 counted about 20 crore people in Uttar Pradesh, the most of any state.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Make (something bad or unsatisfactory) better
questions.explanation: To 'ameliorate' is to make something bad or unsatisfactory better. To 'malign' is to speak ill of someone and to 'castigate' to scold severely.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement reuired’. The “viewing for the” Mount Everest is clearer from here.
questions.explanation: What can be seen from a place is its 'view', which takes 'of', and Mount Everest, a proper name, needs no article: 'The view of Mount Everest is clearer from here.'

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. An immense crowd “had gather” to witness this ceremony.
questions.explanation: The past perfect is 'had' with the past participle: 'An immense crowd had gathered to witness this ceremony.'

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. When it comes to love of sports, he “takes off” his father.
questions.explanation: To 'take after' a parent is to resemble them: 'he takes after his father'. To 'take off' is to remove something or to leave the ground.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Arachic' is misspelt: the word is 'archaic', meaning very old or old-fashioned.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Businesses are asking employees to work from home.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: 'ask' takes an object and a to-infinitive ('asking employees to work'), and 'work from home' is the usual phrase.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. A child in an art museum is like “a bull in a China shop.”
options: A clumsy person in a delicate situation
A person who cries for everything
A person with no moral values
questions.explanation: A 'bull in a china shop' is someone clumsy or careless in a place or situation that needs care.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. An afternoon performance in a theatre or cinema
questions.explanation: A 'matinee' is an afternoon performance in a theatre or cinema. A 'premiere' is the first public performance of a play or film.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. An ability to find ways and directions
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'navigate', to find one's way or plan a route, the only option about finding ways and directions. Strictly the phrase, a noun, describes 'navigation' or a sense of direction, but no option gives that.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. It was a long and dangerous journey in those unsettled days.The pilgrim had to face ______ by land and sea.
questions.explanation: 'Perils' are serious dangers, which a long and dangerous journey by land and sea brings. A 'respite' is a short rest from something unpleasant.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Hesitant
questions.explanation: 'Hesitant' means unwilling or slow to act: 'reluctant'. 'Eager' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. She didn’t knew / that I was out / for some urgent work.
questions.explanation: After 'did' (here 'didn't') the verb takes its base form: 'She didn't know that I was out'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. Many state governments “are facing a” financial crunch.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: the plural subject 'governments' takes 'are', and 'financial' begins with a consonant sound, so it takes 'a'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. I have receive perhaps four / or five such requests during the / course of a typical week.
options: or five such requests during the
questions.explanation: The present perfect is 'have' with the past participle: 'I have received perhaps four or five such requests'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Laconic
questions.explanation: 'Laconic' means using very few words, so its opposite is 'verbose', using more words than needed. 'Pithy', 'brief' and 'terse' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Vanquish
questions.explanation: To 'vanquish' is to defeat thoroughly. To 'acquit' is to free someone from a charge.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Overindulgence in anything may prove ________ to health.
questions.explanation: 'Injurious' means harmful: too much of anything may prove harmful to health. 'Spurious' means false or fake.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the incorrectly spelt words in the given sentence. The table was grased with a lovelly showpiece.
options: The table was grased with a lovvely showpiece.
The table was graced with a lovaly showpiece.
The table was graced with a lovely showpiece.
The table was graced with a lovelly showpiece.
questions.explanation: The correct spellings are 'graced' (adorned) and 'lovely', with a single 'l' before the 'y'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The judges applauded me for my ______ performance at the competition.
questions.explanation: Judges applaud an 'outstanding', that is excellent, performance; 'usual', 'normal' and 'large' give no reason for praise.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Bury the hatchet
options: To make secret preparations to attack
questions.explanation: To 'bury the hatchet' is to end a quarrel and make peace.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Love is often thought to be the highest and most fulfilling emotion that men and women can (1)_____. But it is also thought of in (2)_____ to the various instincts in man. Therefore, we must (3)_____ from the mystical point of view that love is the highest emotion of man and the one emotion that relates man to God. Love on every plane and level of life is an expression of God's will, working and expressing itself in man's consciousness. To express love on any level is good, but to express it as adoration of God is the (4)_____ form of love and brings man into the greatest (5)_____ with his inner self.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Love is an emotion people 'express', that is show; the passage goes on to speak of expressing love on any level.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Love is often thought to be the highest and most fulfilling emotion that men and women can (1)_____. But it is also thought of in (2)_____ to the various instincts in man. Therefore, we must (3)_____ from the mystical point of view that love is the highest emotion of man and the one emotion that relates man to God. Love on every plane and level of life is an expression of God's will, working and expressing itself in man's consciousness. To express love on any level is good, but to express it as adoration of God is the (4)_____ form of love and brings man into the greatest (5)_____ with his inner self.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'In relation to' means with reference to: love is also thought of with reference to man's instincts.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Love is often thought to be the highest and most fulfilling emotion that men and women can (1)_____. But it is also thought of in (2)_____ to the various instincts in man. Therefore, we must (3)_____ from the mystical point of view that love is the highest emotion of man and the one emotion that relates man to God. Love on every plane and level of life is an expression of God's will, working and expressing itself in man's consciousness. To express love on any level is good, but to express it as adoration of God is the (4)_____ form of love and brings man into the greatest (5)_____ with his inner self.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: After 'must' the verb takes its base form, which rules out 'comprehends' and 'acknowledges': 'we must realise', that is understand, that love is the highest emotion.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Love is often thought to be the highest and most fulfilling emotion that men and women can (1)_____. But it is also thought of in (2)_____ to the various instincts in man. To express love on any level is good, but to express it as adoration of God is the (4)_____ form of love and brings man into the greatest (5)_____ with his inner self.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Love expressed as adoration of God is the 'highest' form of love, echoing 'the highest emotion of man' earlier in the passage.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Love is often thought to be the highest and most fulfilling emotion that men and women can (1)_____. But it is also thought of in (2)_____ to the various instincts in man. Love on every plane and level of life is an expression of God's will, working and expressing itself in man's consciousness.
