questions.explanation: NCERT's economics textbook names Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe households as the social groups most vulnerable to poverty; among economic groups it names rural agricultural labour and urban casual labour households.

questions.text: Which of the following determines the colour, texture, chemical properties, mineral, content, and permeability of the soil?
questions.explanation: The parent rock, which weathers to form the soil, decides its colour, texture, chemical properties, mineral content and permeability; climate, relief and time act on what it supplies.

questions.text: Name the ICC Women Cricketer of the year in 2021.
questions.explanation: Smriti Mandhana won the ICC's Rachael Heyhoe Flint Trophy as the Women's Cricketer of the Year for 2021.

questions.text: Which of the following are situated in the nucleus of a cell?
questions.explanation: The chromosomes, which carry the genes, lie in the nucleus. The cytoplasm is the material outside the nucleus.

questions.text: Which of the following is the state of origin of the Sattriya dance form?
questions.explanation: Sattriya was created by the Vaishnava saint Srimanta Sankardeva and grew up in the sattras (monasteries) of Assam.

questions.text: In which state of India are Buddhist cave temples, Barabar Caves, located?
questions.explanation: The Barabar Caves, rock-cut chambers of the Mauryan period, are in the Jehanabad district of Bihar; Ashoka's inscriptions in them give them to the Ajivika sect.

questions.text: Mando festival is related to which state of India?
questions.explanation: The mando is a Konkani song form of Goa, sung to dancing, and the Mando festival celebrates it.

questions.text: As per Census 2011, which of the following is the correct range of population of India?
questions.explanation: The 2011 Census counted about 121 crore people, or 1.21 billion, between 1.2 and 1.3 billion.

questions.text: Bessie Award is a dance award given in which country?
questions.explanation: The Bessies, the New York Dance and Performance Awards, honour dance in New York City; they are named after the dance teacher Bessie Schönberg.

questions.text: Indian Railways ferries which of the following commodities the most as per tonnage, as of April 2022?
questions.explanation: Coal was by far the largest commodity Indian Railways carried by tonnage when the exam was held (July 2022): in 2021-22 it made up nearly half of all freight loaded, about 653 of 1,418 million tonnes, far ahead of iron ore, cement and food grains.

questions.text: S Balachander is famous for playing the ________.
questions.explanation: S. Balachander was a celebrated veena player of Carnatic music.

questions.text: Who is the author of the novel, God of Small Things?
questions.explanation: Arundhati Roy's 'The God of Small Things' won the Booker Prize in 1997.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct? I. Rolling friction is greater than the sliding friction. II. The frictional force exerted by fluids is called drag.
options: Neither I nor II is correct
Both I and II are correct
questions.explanation: Rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction, which is why wheels and ball bearings are used, so I is false. The friction a fluid exerts on a body moving through it is called drag, so II is true.

questions.text: The tertiary sector of Indian Economy is related to ____________.
questions.explanation: The tertiary or service sector covers activities that support production rather than produce goods: transport, communication, trade, banking and other services. Manufacturing and electricity belong to the secondary sector and agriculture to the primary.

questions.text: Rama is suffering from chickenpox. What type of disease is it?
questions.explanation: Chickenpox is caused by a virus, the varicella-zoster virus.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which Indian movement was started to look into the problems of indigo planters in the year 1917?
questions.explanation: In 1917 Gandhi took up the cause of the peasants of Champaran in Bihar, whom European planters forced to grow indigo. The Kheda Satyagraha and the Ahmedabad mill strike followed in 1918.

questions.text: Which of the following persons was a slave-generals of Alauddin Khalji (1296-1316 AD)?
questions.explanation: Malik Kafur, a slave taken in the conquest of Gujarat, became Alauddin Khalji's leading general and led his campaigns into the Deccan and the far south. Ulugh Khan was Alauddin's brother.

questions.text: Which country will host the 2022 Commonwealth Games?
questions.explanation: The 2022 Commonwealth Games were held in Birmingham, England, from 28 July to 8 August 2022.

questions.text: Which Ministry of the Government of India organised ‘Gender Samwaad’ in March 2022?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Rural Development held the third 'Gender Samwaad', a virtual event of its Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) on the mission's work for women, in March 2022, during its Iconic Week around International Women's Day.

questions.text: Who was the first Indian captain to lift the International Cricket Council (ICC) Cricket World Cup?
questions.explanation: Kapil Dev led India to the 1983 World Cup, beating the West Indies in the final at Lord's.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Scholars have / studied the lives of / present-day farmer’s / who practice agriculture.
questions.explanation: 'Farmer's' is a possessive, but the sentence needs the plural noun 'farmers': 'the lives of present-day farmers who practice agriculture'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Her comfort was in her children; / her second son, Rupert, / was especially dear to her.
options: Her comfort was in her children
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: the semicolon joins two closely related clauses, and the commas set off the name 'Rupert'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. I “didn’t wanted” her to go out with her friends.
questions.explanation: After the auxiliary 'did' ('didn't') the verb takes its base form: 'I didn't want her to go out with her friends.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. All Greek to me
questions.explanation: Something that is 'all Greek to me' is impossible for me to understand.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. An arm and a leg
options: In a backward and forward motion
questions.explanation: Something that costs 'an arm and a leg' is very expensive.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. You don’t seem to be ______ happy with this proposal.
questions.explanation: 'Very' is an adverb of degree that strengthens the adjective 'happy'; 'few', 'many' and 'some' go with nouns.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'harness': one 'r', one 'n' and '-ess' at the end.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Malleable
questions.explanation: 'Malleable' means easily bent or shaped; its opposite is 'stiff'. 'Flexible' and 'resilient' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. He indicated that a vigorous recovery programme was being carried out; 90,000 reminders “had been issued and thousands of summons sent.”
options: has been issued and thousands of summons sent
has been issued and thousands of summonses sent
had been issued and thousands of summonses were sent
questions.explanation: The plural of the noun 'summons' is 'summonses', and the plural subject '90,000 reminders' in this past report needs 'had been', not 'has been': '...had been issued and thousands of summonses were sent'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Occurring after the death of the said person
questions.explanation: 'Posthumous' describes something that happens after a person's death, such as an award. 'Effusive' means gushing, 'gregarious' sociable and 'fugitive' running away.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. My husband has committed a very “heinous” crime.
questions.explanation: 'Heinous' means utterly wicked; of the options, its opposite is 'delightful'. 'Gruesome' and 'appalling' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. I am not going to “scold” you anymore.
questions.explanation: To 'scold' is to rebuke angrily: 'chide'. 'Laud' means to praise, 'placate' to calm and 'startle' to surprise.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Beguille' is misspelt: the word is 'beguile', with one 'l', meaning to charm or deceive.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. I liked talking to / you when you was / a small boy.
questions.explanation: In the past tense 'you' takes 'were', even for one person: 'you when you were a small boy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Voracious
questions.explanation: 'Voracious' means wanting great quantities of food: 'greedy'. 'Restrained' and 'moderate' are nearly opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Preserve
questions.explanation: To 'preserve' something is to keep it safe; to 'neglect' it is to fail to look after it. 'Safeguard' and 'treasure' are close to 'preserve' in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I prefer to have lunch with my family ______ Sundays.
questions.explanation: Days of the week take 'on': 'on Sundays', 'on Monday'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. “Shirley have had all her children with” the help of a fertility drug.
options: Shirley had all her children through
Shirley have had all her children by
Shirley has had all her children with
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'Shirley' takes 'has', not 'have', and 'with the help of' is the usual phrase: 'Shirley has had all her children with the help of a fertility drug.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A place where dead bodies are kept for identification
questions.explanation: A morgue is where dead bodies are kept until they are identified or claimed. A crematorium is where bodies are burnt, a tannery where hides are made into leather and a hutch a cage for rabbits.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Feelings of great happiness and excitement
questions.explanation: 'Euphoria' is a feeling of intense happiness and excitement. 'Contentment' is quiet satisfaction, 'decadence' moral decline and 'desolation' great misery.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The role of the school and teachers (1) ______ always been vital in the all-round personality (2) ______ of students. In fact, a teacher is a role (3) ______ influencing every facet of the student’s growth and developing (4) ______ innate potential, in addition to (5) ______ a motivator, guide and friend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'the role', which is singular, so the verb is 'has': 'The role of the school and teachers has always been vital'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The role of the school and teachers (1) ______ always been vital in the all-round personality (2) ______ of students. In fact, a teacher is a role (3) ______ influencing every facet of the student’s growth and developing (4) ______ innate potential, in addition to (5) ______ a motivator, guide and friend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'All-round personality development' is the growth of every side of a student's personality.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The role of the school and teachers (1) ______ always been vital in the all-round personality (2) ______ of students. In fact, a teacher is a role (3) ______ influencing every facet of the student’s growth and developing (4) ______ innate potential, in addition to (5) ______ a motivator, guide and friend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: A 'role model' is a person whom others look up to and copy.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The role of the school and teachers (1) ______ always been vital in the all-round personality (2) ______ of students. In fact, a teacher is a role (3) ______ influencing every facet of the student’s growth and developing (4) ______ innate potential, in addition to (5) ______ a motivator, guide and friend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Their' refers back to the student: the teacher develops the student's own innate potential.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The role of the school and teachers (1) ______ always been vital in the all-round personality (2) ______ of students. In fact, a teacher is a role (3) ______ influencing every facet of the student’s growth and developing (4) ______ innate potential, in addition to (5) ______ a motivator, guide and friend.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'In addition to' is followed by a noun or an '-ing' form: 'in addition to being a motivator, guide and friend'.

questions.text: Select the option that will replace the question mark (?) in the given series. 45, 46, 42, 51, 35, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are +1, −4, +9, −16, +25: the squares 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 with alternating signs. 35 + 25 = 60.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 7 : 42 :: 9 : 72 :: 12 : ?
questions.explanation: Each number is multiplied by one less than itself: 7 × 6 = 42 and 9 × 8 = 72. So 12 × 11 = 132.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. KRA, IQZ, ?, EOX, CNW
questions.explanation: The first letters go back 2 (K, I, G, E, C) and the second and third back 1 each (R, Q, P, O, N and A, Z, Y, X, W). The missing cluster is GPY.

questions.text: Which of the numbers (not digits) should be interchanged in the given equation to make it mathematically correct? 104 ÷ 4 − 6 + 13 × 5 = 22
questions.explanation: After interchanging 13 and 4: 104 ÷ 13 − 6 + 4 × 5 = 8 − 6 + 20 = 22.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘Milk are exhausting’ is coded as ‘# tg 5’, and ‘Are water super milk’ is coded as ‘pa 5 6 #’. What is the code for ‘super’ in that language?
questions.explanation: 'Milk' and 'are' are in both sentences, and '#' and '5' in both codes. That leaves 'pa' and '6' for 'water' and 'super', so 'super' is 'pa' or '6'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'shoes are shining' is coded as '235', 'shining stars rotate' is coded as '458', and 'stars are round' is coded as '829'. How will 'are' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: 'Are' is the only word common to the first and third phrases, and '2' the only digit common to their codes, '235' and '829'.

questions.text: By interchanging the given two numbers (not digits), which of the following equations will NOT be correct? 11 and 17; I. 400 + 17 – 71 × 85 ÷ 11 = 58; II. 1331 ÷ 17 – 50 + 6 × 11 = 173
questions.explanation: After interchanging 11 and 17: I. 400 + 11 − 71 × 85 ÷ 17 = 411 − 355 = 56, not 58; II. 1331 ÷ 11 − 50 + 6 × 17 = 121 − 50 + 102 = 173, which is correct. So only I is not correct.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statement I: All criminals are thieves. Statement II: Rakesh is a thief. Conclusion I: Rakesh is a criminal. Conclusion II: Some thieves may not be criminals.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: Every criminal is a thief, but a thief need not be a criminal: Rakesh may or may not be one, so I does not follow, while some thieves may well not be criminals, so II follows.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'POEM' is written as 'ODQO', 'HARD' is written as 'FQCG'. How will 'RNGC' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and its letters moved +2, −1, +2, −1: POEM → MEOP → ODQO and HARD → DRAH → FQCG. So RNGC → CGNR → EFPQ.

questions.text: A, B, R, D, I, S, and T are sitting around a circular table facing away from the circle. A does not sit adjacent to I and T. B does not sit adjacent to A. R sits fourth to the left of A. D and B sit adjacent to each other. S sits third to the left of I. Who is the immediate neighbour of both T and A?
questions.explanation: A's neighbours can only be D and S: I, T and B may not sit beside A, and R sits fourth to its left. With S on A's left, B and I would need the same seat, so going round to A's left (anticlockwise, as they face outwards) the order is A, D, B, I, R, T, S. S sits between T and A.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'LUNCH' is written as 'NWPEJ', and 'FAITH' is written as 'HCKVJ'. How will 'SPACE' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: LUNCH → NWPEJ and FAITH → HCKVJ. So SPACE → URCEG.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is NOT allowed) (4, 5, 20); (7, 8, 56)
questions.explanation: The third number is the product of the first two: 4 × 5 = 20 and 7 × 8 = 56. Likewise 7 × 12 = 84.

questions.text: Among seven persons A, B, C, D, E, F and G, who are of different ages, D is younger than only A and E. E is younger to A and older than B. C is third youngest. F and G are second youngest and youngest respectively. Who is the fourth eldest?
questions.explanation: D is younger than only A and E, and A is older than E, so A, E and D are the three eldest in that order. C is third youngest, F second youngest and G youngest, which leaves B fourth eldest.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some Parrots are Birds. All Birds are Mammals. Conclusions: I. All Mammals are Birds. II. Some Mammals are Parrots.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: The parrots that are birds are all mammals, so some mammals are parrots (II). 'All birds are mammals' cannot be reversed, so I does not follow.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. RL : OQ :: GO : ?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves back 3 and the second forward 5: R → O and L → Q. So G → D and O → T: DT.

questions.text: C 1 is related to F 4 in a certain way. In the same way, J 6 is related to M 9. To which of the following is P 4 related, following the same logic?
questions.explanation: Both the letter and the number go up by 3: C 1 → F 4 and J 6 → M 9. So P 4 → S 7.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 94, 95, 100, 109, 122, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 1, 5, 9, 13, rising by 4. The next is 17: 122 + 17 = 139.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. SIPL : AQXT :: ADGJ : ILOR :: UMEB : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 8 places forward: SIPL → AQXT and ADGJ → ILOR. So UMEB → CUMJ.

questions.text: Five men Z, X, H, I and J are sitting around a circular table, facing towards the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Z is sitting second to the left of I. H is sitting second to the right of X. J is not the immediate neighbour of Z. Who is sitting third to the right of X?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left is clockwise. With Z second to the left of I and H second to the right of X, the order clockwise is I, H, Z, X, J (the only other fit puts J beside Z). Third to the right of X is I.

questions.text: Which of the following is the fifth state of matter?
questions.explanation: After solid, liquid, gas and plasma, the Bose-Einstein condensate, formed when a gas of bosons is cooled almost to absolute zero, is called the fifth state of matter.

questions.text: Who has been appointed the first deputy managing director of the International Monetary Fund?
questions.explanation: In December 2021 the IMF named Gita Gopinath, then its Chief Economist, as its First Deputy Managing Director, the Fund's second-highest post; she took it up in January 2022 and held it when the exam was held (July 2022). 'First Deputy Managing Director' is the title of the post, which others had held before her.

questions.text: Which famous Kathak dancer was called to perform for Queen Elizabeth II coronation festivities, in 1953 and was awarded with Padma Bhushan in 1970?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Kumari Kamala (Kamala Lakshmi Narayanan), who performed for Queen Elizabeth II during her coronation festivities in 1953 and received the Padma Bhushan in 1970; she took her first lessons in Kathak, from Lachhu Maharaj, but is known chiefly as a Bharatanatyam dancer. No other option fits: Sridevi was born in 1963, Mallika Sarabhai in 1953, and Kanaka Raju is a Gussadi dancer.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book ‘Slumdog Millionaire’?
questions.explanation: Vikas Swarup's first novel, 'Q & A' (2005), was filmed as 'Slumdog Millionaire' and later reissued under the film's title.

questions.text: Who was India's first Olympian who went on to star in Hollywood and Broadway?
questions.explanation: Norman Pritchard, born in Calcutta, won two silver medals in athletics (200 m and 200 m hurdles) for India at the 1900 Paris Olympics, and later acted on Broadway and in Hollywood films as Norman Trevor.

questions.text: The tax imposed on goods imported into and exported out of India is called ______.
questions.explanation: Customs duty is levied on goods imported into or exported out of the country. Excise falls on goods made within it, and corporation tax on companies' profits.

questions.text: Which of the following is the largest moon of Saturn?
questions.explanation: Titan is Saturn's largest moon and the second largest in the solar system. Europa and Carme orbit Jupiter, and Atlas is a small inner moon of Saturn.

questions.text: Chennai Super Kings defeated which team to win IPL 2021?
questions.explanation: Chennai Super Kings beat Kolkata Knight Riders by 27 runs in the final in Dubai on 15 October 2021, for their fourth IPL title.

questions.text: As of April 2022, who is the Chairman of Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: The Vice-President of India is the ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha; in April 2022 that was M. Venkaiah Naidu, Vice-President from August 2017 to August 2022. Om Birla was then the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

questions.text: The Rajya Sabha passed the National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPER) Amendment Bill, 2021. The institutes mentioned in the bill are of national importance and fall under the aegis of the Department of Pharmaceutical, Ministry of ___________________.
options: Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
questions.explanation: The National Institutes of Pharmaceutical Education and Research are institutes of national importance under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, which is part of the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers.

questions.text: Which state has the highest reserves of manganese in India, as of April 2022?
questions.explanation: The Indian Bureau of Mines puts Odisha first among the states for manganese ore reserves and resources, ahead of Karnataka and Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text: Which of the following architectural styles had an entrance gateway called ‘gopuram’?
questions.explanation: The gopuram, a tall, ornate gateway tower, is a hallmark of Dravidian (South Indian) temples. Nagara temples usually have no boundary wall or gateway; their curving shikhara rises over the sanctum.

questions.text: Citric acid is commonly found in __________.
questions.explanation: Citrus fruits such as oranges and lemons owe their sour taste mainly to citric acid; apples contain mainly malic acid.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct? I. Tipu Sultan is also known as the Tiger of Mysore. II. Tipu Sultan ruled over Mysore from 1782 to 1799.
questions.explanation: Tipu Sultan, the 'Tiger of Mysore', succeeded his father Hyder Ali in 1782 and ruled until he was killed defending Srirangapatna in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War in 1799, so both statements are correct.

questions.text: Which Indian musician was conferred with the Lifetime achievement Grammy Award?
questions.explanation: The sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar was named a recipient of the Recording Academy's Lifetime Achievement Award for 2013; he died in December 2012, before it was presented in February 2013.

questions.text: Which freedom fighter of India composed the song, ‘Saare Jahan Se Achha’?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Iqbal wrote 'Saare Jahan Se Achha', first published in 1904 as 'Tarana-e-Hindi'.

questions.text: Which of the following is an employment generation programme in India?
questions.explanation: The Swarna Jayanti Shahari Rozgar Yojana, launched in December 1997, gave the urban poor self-employment and wage employment. Jan Dhan opens bank accounts, Stand Up India gives bank loans to SC, ST and women entrepreneurs, and Suraksha Bima is accident insurance.

questions.text: The green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem capture about ______ of the energy of sunlight that falls on their leaves and convert it into food energy.
questions.explanation: NCERT's Class 10 science text gives about 1% as the share of the sunlight falling on their leaves that green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem turn into food energy.

questions.text: Pulakeshin II was a ruler of which dynasty?
questions.explanation: Pulakeshin II was the greatest ruler of the Chalukyas of Badami (Vatapi); he checked Harshavardhana's advance south at the Narmada.

questions.text: Who among the following rulers of Mewar was defeated by Babur in the Battle of Khanwa (1527 AD)?
questions.explanation: Rana Sanga (Sangram Singh) of Mewar led a Rajput confederacy against Babur and was defeated at Khanwa, near Fatehpur Sikri, in March 1527.

questions.text: Ugadi is an important festival of which state?
questions.explanation: Ugadi, on the first day of Chaitra, is the New Year of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

questions.text: Which of the following was formed to maintain and develop road networks in Indian border areas for easy accessibility and connectivity?
questions.explanation: The Border Roads Organisation, set up in 1960, builds and maintains roads in India's border areas, along with bridges, tunnels and airfields.

questions.text: Kalbelia is a tribal dance form of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Kalbelia, the dance of Rajasthan's Kalbelia community, once snake-charmers, was inscribed on UNESCO's list of intangible cultural heritage in 2010.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India states the 'Right to freedom of speech and expression'?
questions.explanation: Article 19(1)(a) guarantees every citizen the right to freedom of speech and expression. Article 370 gave Jammu and Kashmir its special status, and Article 200 deals with the Governor's assent to state bills.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. In exactly the same words as were used originally
questions.explanation: 'Verbatim' means in exactly the same words as the original, word for word. 'Imprecise' means inexact and 'neutral' impartial.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. He has been presented off honorary awards.
questions.explanation: One is presented 'with' an award, not 'off' it: 'He has been presented with honorary awards.' The option 'honorable awards' misprints the sentence's 'honorary', but that part of the sentence is correct.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Invigorate
questions.explanation: 'Invigorate' means to fill with energy, so its opposite is 'tire'. 'Energise' is close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Both songs have been reworked giving them fresh “impetus”.
questions.explanation: 'Impetus' is a force or stimulus that drives something on, and 'incitement', encouragement to act, is closest. 'Detachment', 'aversion' and 'disfavour' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Monumental' is spelt correctly; the others should be 'wariness', 'disenchantment' and 'awakening'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The weather was so ________ that she couldn’t step out of the house.
questions.explanation: Weather bad enough to keep her indoors is 'terrible'. 'Inept' means unskilled, and 'serious' and 'slight' do not describe weather that way.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. This is “on far a best” ice cream I have ever had.
questions.explanation: 'By far' strengthens a superlative, and a superlative takes 'the': 'This is by far the best ice cream I have ever had.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Reveal
questions.explanation: To 'reveal' is to make known: 'disclose'. 'Veil' and 'darken' suggest the opposite, hiding, and 'curb' means to restrain.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Get cold feet
options: To be in a bad mood
To feel nervous about doing something
questions.explanation: To 'get cold feet' is to lose one's nerve: to feel nervous about doing something one had planned.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. Water “is using in every” cell of your body.
questions.explanation: Water does not use anything; it is used, so the passive is needed, with 'is' for the singular 'water': 'Water is used in every cell of your body.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Gandhiji spent many years _______ Sabarmati Ashram.
questions.explanation: 'At' marks a particular place, here the ashram where Gandhiji lived: 'spent many years at Sabarmati Ashram'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. After all the fuss, the companies “has still not reach” a consensus.
questions.explanation: The plural 'companies' takes 'have', and the perfect tense needs the past participle 'reached': 'the companies have still not reached a consensus'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Food was ______; guides were not to be found, and the enemy dogged them all the way.
questions.explanation: 'Scarce' means in short supply, which fits a hard march without guides. 'Crass' means coarse or stupid, and 'chance' and 'farce' do not fit the sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Serene
questions.explanation: 'Serene' means calm and peaceful, so its opposite is 'agitated'. 'Unperturbed' and 'composed' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The Andes mountains / lay between / Chile and Argentina.
questions.explanation: The verb for being situated is 'lie', in the present tense for a lasting fact: 'The Andes mountains lie between Chile and Argentina.' 'Lay' is its past tense, or a verb meaning to put down.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. My life has ______ meaning without you.
questions.explanation: 'No' goes before a noun to mean 'not any': 'My life has no meaning without you.' 'None' is a pronoun and cannot stand before a noun, and 'has not meaning' and 'has never meaning' are ungrammatical.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. There are some Indian herbs / that possesses a range / of important therapeutic properties.
questions.explanation: 'That' refers to the plural 'herbs', so the verb must be plural: 'herbs that possess a range of important therapeutic properties'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To blaze the trail
options: To mark the end of the movement
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'To start a movement': to blaze the trail is to be the first to do something new and lead the way for others, and of the options only starting a movement carries that sense of pioneering.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. The prospects of surviving any serious illness are improved if the disease is “catching early.”
questions.explanation: A disease does not catch anything; it is caught, so the passive is needed: 'if the disease is caught early'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Nuclear power for civil use is well (1) ______ in India. Since building the two small boiling water reactors (2) ______ Tarapur in the 1960s, its civil nuclear strategy (3) ______ directed towards complete independence in the nuclear fuel cycle, necessarily (4) ______ it is excluded (5) ______ the 1970 Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Nuclear power is 'well established', that is firmly set up and accepted, in India. 'Well founded' would mean justified, which does not suit the sense.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Nuclear power for civil use is well (1) ______ in India. Since building the two small boiling water reactors (2) ______ Tarapur in the 1960s, its civil nuclear strategy (3) ______ directed towards complete independence in the nuclear fuel cycle, necessarily (4) ______ it is excluded (5) ______ the 1970 Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'At' goes before the particular place where the reactors were built: 'reactors at Tarapur'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Nuclear power for civil use is well (1) ______ in India. Since building the two small boiling water reactors (2) ______ Tarapur in the 1960s, its civil nuclear strategy (3) ______ directed towards complete independence in the nuclear fuel cycle, necessarily (4) ______ it is excluded (5) ______ the 1970 Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Since building the two small boiling water reactors ... in the 1960s' calls for the present perfect, the singular 'strategy' takes 'has', and the strategy is directed by others, so the passive: 'its civil nuclear strategy has been directed'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Nuclear power for civil use is well (1) ______ in India. Since building the two small boiling water reactors (2) ______ Tarapur in the 1960s, its civil nuclear strategy (3) ______ directed towards complete independence in the nuclear fuel cycle, necessarily (4) ______ it is excluded (5) ______ the 1970 Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The clause gives the reason for seeking independence in the fuel cycle: 'necessarily because it is excluded' from the treaty.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Nuclear power for civil use is well (1) ______ in India. Since building the two small boiling water reactors (2) ______ Tarapur in the 1960s, its civil nuclear strategy (3) ______ directed towards complete independence in the nuclear fuel cycle, necessarily (4) ______ it is excluded (5) ______ the 1970 Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Excluded' takes 'from': 'excluded from the 1970 Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty'.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. All G are R. II. Some F are G. Conclusions: I. All R are F. II. Some G are F. III. Some F are R.
options: Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: Some F are G and all G are R, so some F are R (III); 'some F are G' also means some G are F (II). Nothing makes every R an F, so I does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'ACID' is written as 'ZBHC' and 'LAND' is written as ‘KZMC’. How will 'GOLD' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place back: ACID → ZBHC and LAND → KZMC. So GOLD → FNKC.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. AND : VHV :: LXY : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move back 5, 6 and 8 places, wrapping round after A: A → V, N → H and D → V. So L → G, X → R and Y → Q: GRQ.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. MA, NZ, OY, PX, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters run M, N, O, P, Q and the second A, Z, Y, X, W, backwards from the end: QW.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘Fakes are not great’ is written as ‘8 6 3 2’ and ‘Tall people are great’ is written as ‘5 3 2 7’. Which one of the following is the possible code for ‘not’ in that code language?
questions.explanation: 'Are' and 'great' occur in both sentences, so their codes are the shared 3 and 2. 'Not' is then 8 or 6, and only 8 is an option.

questions.text: Which two signs need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 26 ÷ 24 + 6 × 27 − 105 = 29
Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. P 2 : R 4 :: D 5 : F 7 :: X 6 : ?
questions.explanation: The letter moves 2 places forward and the number rises by 2: P 2 → R 4 and D 5 → F 7. So X 6 → Z 8.

questions.text: There are five friends, Ram, Shekhar, Sonu, Rinku and Monu, who are sitting at different positions in a row and facing north. Two friends sit between Shekhar and Rinku. Shekhar sits neither in the first position nor the last position of the row. Monu is not an immediate neighbour of Shekhar. Ram sits second to the left of Sonu. Sonu does not sit at the extreme ends of the row. Who is sitting at the middle of the row?
questions.explanation: Shekhar is not at an end and two sit between him and Rinku, so they are 2nd and 5th or 4th and 1st. With Shekhar 4th and Rinku 1st, Sonu (not at an end) would be 2nd or 3rd, leaving no free seat second to his left for Ram; with Shekhar 2nd and Rinku 5th, Sonu is 3rd, Ram 1st and Monu 4th, not next to Shekhar. Sonu sits in the middle.

questions.text: Which two signs need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 2 + 78 ÷ 13 − 4 × 111 = 119
questions.explanation: After interchanging + and ×: 2 × 78 ÷ 13 − 4 + 111 = 12 − 4 + 111 = 119.

questions.text: Seven birds — A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting in a straight row, facing north. D sits third to the right of F, who sits at the second position from the left end. E sits between A and F. G sits to the left of F. B sits in the second position from the right end. Which of the following statements is true?
options: B sits exactly between D and A.
C sits at extreme right end.
F sits at extreme left end.
E sits to the immediate left of D.
questions.explanation: F is 2nd from the left, so G, to its left, is 1st and D, third to its right, is 5th; B is 2nd from the right, 6th. E sits directly between A and F, so E is 3rd and A 4th, which leaves the right end for C: G F E A D B C.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (7, 1, 3); (12, 2, 5)
questions.explanation: In each set the first number is the second plus twice the third: 1 + 2 × 3 = 7 and 2 + 2 × 5 = 12. Likewise 8 + 2 × 11 = 30.

questions.text: In a certain code language, if Delhi is called Mumbai, Mumbai is called Jaipur, Jaipur is called Durgapur, Durgapur is called Chandigarh, and Chandigarh is called Jodhpur, then which city is the capital of Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Jaipur is the capital of Rajasthan, and in this language Jaipur is called Durgapur.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 24, 625, 26, 729, 28, 841, ?
questions.explanation: Two series alternate: 24, 26, 28 rise by 2, and 625, 729, 841 are 25², 27², 29². The next term is 30.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 59 : 14 :: 61 : 7 :: 37 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the sum of the first number's digits: 5 + 9 = 14 and 6 + 1 = 7. So 3 + 7 = 10.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. LAM : AML :: RUK : ?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves to the end: LAM → AML. So RUK → UKR.

questions.text: In certain code language, ‘DID’ is coded as ‘494’, ‘DEAR’ is coded as ‘4518’ and ‘BENT’ is coded as ‘2540’. How will ‘FOR’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is coded as the last digit of its place in the alphabet: D(4) I(9) D(4) → 494, and R(18), N(14), T(20) → 8, 4, 0. So F(6) O(15) R(18) → 658.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All basketball players are tall people. Suman is tall. Conclusions: I. Suman is a basketball player. II. Some tall people are basketball players.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: Being tall does not make Suman a basketball player, so I does not follow. Since all basketball players are tall, some tall people are basketball players (II).

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 18, 36, 25, 50, 39, ?
Vikas has an income of ₹2.5 lakhs. Which of the following tax slabs of India is applicable for him?
questions.explanation: Under both income tax regimes in force when the exam was held (July 2022), income up to ₹2.5 lakh fell in the nil slab, so no tax was due. The other options are the 20%, 10% and 5% rates of higher slabs, written as decimals.

questions.text: Which of the following countries shares their land boundary with India?
questions.explanation: Bhutan borders Sikkim, West Bengal, Assam and Arunachal Pradesh. Indonesia, Vietnam and Uzbekistan have no land border with India.

questions.text: Who among the following athletes won India’s first gold medal in Javelin Throw at the Tokyo Olympics 2020?
questions.explanation: Neeraj Chopra won the javelin gold at Tokyo on 7 August 2021 with a throw of 87.58 m, India's first Olympic gold in athletics.

questions.text: The maximum temperature of the day occurs generally:
questions.explanation: The ground keeps gaining more heat from the sun than it loses until early afternoon, so the day's highest temperature usually comes around 2 p.m., not at noon when the sun is highest.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following statements about Paramhansa Mandalis is INCORRECT?
options: They were primarily interested in breaking caste rules.
Its founders did not believe in God.
It was founded in 1849 in Maharashtra.
They also advocated for widow remarriage and women’s education.
questions.explanation: The Paramhansa Mandali, a secret society founded in Bombay by Dadoba Pandurang, Durgaram Mehtaji and others (in 1849 by most accounts), believed in one God. It worked mainly to break caste rules and also supported widow remarriage and women's education.

questions.text: The heart of a fish has ______ chambers.
questions.explanation: A fish heart has two chambers, one atrium and one ventricle, and pumps blood in a single circuit through the gills to the body.

questions.text: Pramod Sawant took the oath as the Chief Minister of which state in March 2022?
questions.explanation: Pramod Sawant was sworn in as Chief Minister of Goa for a second term on 28 March 2022, after the BJP emerged as the largest party, with 20 of the 40 seats, in the February 2022 Assembly election.

questions.text: Select the correct statement.
options: There are only 2 basic components of a cell-cytoplasm and nucleus.
The cytoplasm and nucleus are enclosed within the cell membrane, also called the plasma membrane.
The membrane separates ribosomes and mitochondria of a cell.
The plasma membrane does not allow inward movement of the substance.
questions.explanation: A cell has three basic parts, the cell membrane (plasma membrane), the cytoplasm and the nucleus, and the membrane encloses the other two. It separates the cell from its surroundings and lets substances pass both in and out.

questions.text: In India, primitive form of cultivation is known as ‘Jhumming’ in the ______.
questions.explanation: Slash-and-burn shifting cultivation is called 'jhumming' in the north-eastern states such as Assam, Meghalaya, Mizoram and Nagaland.

questions.text: Which country is separated from India by the Gulf of Mannar?
questions.explanation: The Gulf of Mannar lies between the south-east coast of Tamil Nadu and the west coast of Sri Lanka.

questions.text: Which of the following laws states that with the temperature remaining constant, the volume of a given mass of a gas varies inversely with the pressure of the gas?
questions.explanation: Boyle's law: at constant temperature, the volume of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure. Charles's law relates volume to temperature at constant pressure, and Graham's law deals with rates of diffusion.

questions.text: Makar Sankranti is celebrated as the ______ long Pongal festival in Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.
questions.explanation: In Tamil Nadu Pongal is kept over four days in mid-January: Bhogi, Thai Pongal (the day of Makar Sankranti), Mattu Pongal and Kaanum Pongal.

questions.text: Which country hosted the ICC Women’s World Cup 2021/22?
questions.explanation: New Zealand hosted the ICC Women's World Cup, put back from 2021 by the pandemic, from March to April 2022; Australia won it.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In 1929, Indian National Congress demanded complete independence under the presidentship of ______.
questions.explanation: At its Lahore session in December 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, the Congress adopted the resolution for Purna Swaraj, complete independence.

questions.text: Every judge of the Supreme Court in India shall hold office until he attains the age of ______ years.
questions.explanation: Under Article 124(2) a Supreme Court judge holds office until the age of 65; High Court judges retire at 62.

questions.text: Which of the following novels was written by the famous Indian novelist Amrita Pritam?
questions.explanation: 'Raseedi Ticket' ('The Revenue Stamp') is by Amrita Pritam, though it is her autobiography rather than a novel. 'Midnight's Children' is by Salman Rushdie, 'Satya ke Prayog' is the Hindi title of Gandhi's autobiography and 'Train to Pakistan' is by Khushwant Singh.

questions.text: In the Indian constitution, the Right to Freedom is covered from ______.
questions.explanation: Articles 19 to 22 make up the Right to Freedom. Articles 14 to 18 are the Right to Equality, 23 and 24 the Right against Exploitation, and 25 to 28 the Right to Freedom of Religion.

questions.text: The Janjira Fort is situated on a small island in the Arabian sea, off the coast of ______.
questions.explanation: Murud-Janjira, the sea fort of the Siddis, stands on an island off Murud in Raigad district, Maharashtra.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. Travelling “is the best” method to utilise time.
questions.explanation: The superlative 'best' takes 'the', and the gerund subject 'Travelling' takes the singular 'is': the sentence needs no change. 'Much best' and 'an best' are not English.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Interfere
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'restrict': to interfere with something is to get in its way and hinder it, and 'restrict' (to limit or hold back) is the nearest of the options, though not an exact synonym. 'Hasten' means to hurry, 'masquerade' to pretend to be someone else and 'activate' to set going.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I was not even ________________ that my friend was ill.
questions.explanation: To be 'aware that' something is so is to know it: the speaker did not even know the friend was ill. 'Brave' and 'cruel' make no sense here, and 'alert' means watchful.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. We've got to have / beefed-up intelligence, / including much strong / human intelligence than before.
questions.explanation: With 'than before' a comparative is needed: 'including much stronger human intelligence than before'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. The small farmers often “need at” borrow money to meet high expenses.
questions.explanation: 'Need' is followed by a to-infinitive, and the plural subject 'farmers' takes 'need', not 'needs': 'The small farmers often need to borrow money'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The blue team ______ the red team to play the game.
questions.explanation: To 'challenge' a team is to invite it to a contest: 'The blue team challenged the red team to play the game.' 'Surrendered', 'compromised' and 'heated' do not fit with 'to play the game'.

questions.text: Select the option that corrects the misspelt words in the given sentence. We will always rember your contribusion.
options: We will always remembar your contributoin.
We will always remember your contribution.
We will always remmember your contrabution.
We will always remembber your contribution.
questions.explanation: The correct spellings are 'remember' and 'contribution'; each of the other options keeps at least one misspelling.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Blissful
questions.explanation: 'Blissful' means full of great happiness, so its opposite is 'miserable'. 'Heavenly' and 'idealised' are close to it in sense, and 'malicious' means spiteful.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He was a ______ man and had no wish to be rich.
questions.explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun 'man': 'poor'. 'Poverty' is a noun and 'poorly' an adverb, and the comparative 'poorer' has nothing to be compared with.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. An opportunity arise, and / he decided to take the / job in Brussels.
questions.explanation: 'Arise' agrees neither with the singular subject 'an opportunity' nor with the past tense 'decided'; the simple past is needed: 'An opportunity arose, and he decided to take the job in Brussels.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. Suggesting that Irish inflation may have a knock-on effect on the euro zone is “fatuous” and absurd.
questions.explanation: 'Fatuous' means silly and pointless, so its opposite is 'sensible'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. All eyes and ears
questions.explanation: To be 'all eyes and ears' is to watch and listen closely: to be very attentive.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Either “you and my” sister is involved in this crime.
questions.explanation: 'Either' pairs with 'or', not 'and', and the verb then agrees with the nearer subject, 'my sister': 'Either you or my sister is involved in this crime.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Government by king or queen
questions.explanation: In a monarchy a king or queen is the head of state. A plutocracy is government by the wealthy, an oligarchy government by a small group, and capitalism an economic system.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Beyond the shadow of a doubt
questions.explanation: 'Beyond the shadow of a doubt' means with complete certainty, leaving no doubt at all.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'bureaucrat': 'bureau' followed by '-crat'.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Germs will always find a way to exploit our human environment.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: the plural 'Germs' goes with 'will always find', and 'a way to exploit our human environment' is well formed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. This style is ideal for men of all ages who wish to convey a “dapper” look.
questions.explanation: 'Dapper' describes a man who is neat and smartly dressed: 'stylish'. 'Messy' and 'filthy' are nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Violation or misuse of what is regarded as sacred
questions.explanation: Sacrilege is disrespectful treatment of something holy. A benediction is a blessing, a remedy a cure and devotion deep love or loyalty.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Rioting broke out after the government “raised” the fuel prices again.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'raised' matches 'broke out': both actions lie in the past, one after the other, so no substitution is needed.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. When it (1)______ to witnessing wars, famines or disease outbreaks on the news, guilt may (2)______ us to volunteer or donate money. Watching the generosity of other people (3)______ play an active role in helping others is also guilt-provoking, which can (4)______ turn activate us to take similar (5)______ thus paying forward.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'When it comes to' is a fixed phrase meaning 'as regards'; the present 'comes' suits a general statement such as this one.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. When it (1)______ to witnessing wars, famines or disease outbreaks on the news, guilt may (2)______ us to volunteer or donate money. Watching the generosity of other people (3)______ play an active role in helping others is also guilt-provoking, which can (4)______ turn activate us to take similar (5)______ thus paying forward.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Guilt may 'inspire', that is move, us to volunteer or donate money. 'Conspire' means to plot and 'expire' to end, and 'desire' does not fit 'us to volunteer'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. When it (1)______ to witnessing wars, famines or disease outbreaks on the news, guilt may (2)______ us to volunteer or donate money. Watching the generosity of other people (3)______ play an active role in helping others is also guilt-provoking, which can (4)______ turn activate us to take similar (5)______ thus paying forward.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Who' begins a relative clause about people and is its subject: 'other people who play an active role in helping others'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. When it (1)______ to witnessing wars, famines or disease outbreaks on the news, guilt may (2)______ us to volunteer or donate money. Watching the generosity of other people (3)______ play an active role in helping others is also guilt-provoking, which can (4)______ turn activate us to take similar (5)______ thus paying forward.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'In turn' means as a consequence, one thing leading to the next: the guilt in turn moves us to act likewise.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. When it (1)______ to witnessing wars, famines or disease outbreaks on the news, guilt may (2)______ us to volunteer or donate money. Watching the generosity of other people (3)______ play an active role in helping others is also guilt-provoking, which can (4)______ turn activate us to take similar (5)______ thus paying forward.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: To 'take action' is to act: we are moved to do similar good deeds. 'Apathy' is the opposite, and 'animation' and 'commotion' do not go with 'take'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'RA + FE' is coded as ‘246', and 'AB + JC' is coded as ‘115'. How will 'AC + BD' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each pair of letters is read as their places in the alphabet written side by side, and the two numbers are added: RA = 181 and FE = 65, 181 + 65 = 246; AB = 12 and JC = 103, 12 + 103 = 115. So AC = 13 and BD = 24: 13 + 24 = 37.

questions.text: After interchanging which two signs will the value of the given expression be ‘37’? 27 + 3 ÷ 81 × 93 – 57

Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some apples are oranges. No orange is a grape. Conclusions: I. Some grapes are apples. II. Some oranges are apples.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Some apples are oranges, so some oranges are apples: II follows. The grapes are kept apart only from the oranges, so nothing is known about grapes and apples, and I does not follow.

questions.text: Eight friends, Jay, King, Lisa, Mon, Nia, Ori, Piu, and Ria are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Jay is sitting second to the right of Piu who is sitting third to the right of King. Mon is sitting second to the left of Ori, who sits between Piu and Jay. Lisa is not a neighbour of King or Nia. Who is sitting to the immediate right of King?
questions.explanation: Counting places to the right of King: Piu is third, Jay fifth, Ori fourth (between Piu and Jay) and Mon second (second to Ori's left). Lisa, not beside King, takes the sixth place, so Nia, not beside Lisa, takes the first and Ria the seventh. Nia sits immediately right of King.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'HINTS' is coded as '5', and 'GRAD' is coded as '4'. How will 'POL' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is the number of letters: HINTS has 5 and GRAD 4, so POL is coded 3.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'ACTION' is written as '36' and 'PIZZA' is written as '25'. How will 'GALLERY' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is the square of the number of letters: ACTION has 6 (6² = 36) and PIZZA 5 (5² = 25). GALLERY has 7: 7² = 49.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) 12 : 225 :: 10 : 169 :: 14 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first plus 3: (12 + 3)² = 225 and (10 + 3)² = 169. So (14 + 3)² = 289.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. DAT: GFA:: BNT: ESA:: PUN: ?
questions.explanation: The three letters move +3, +5 and +7, wrapping round after Z: DAT → GFA and BNT → ESA. So PUN → SZU.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. SB : VY :: GN : ?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves 3 places forward and the second 3 places back: S → V and B → Y. So G → J and N → K: JK.

questions.text: Select the option in which the pair of letter-clusters share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of letter-clusters. ROCK : JDNS
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and its letters moved −1, +1, −1, +1: ROCK → K C O R → JDNS. Likewise WART → T R A W → SSZX.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 12 : 33 :: 31 : 71 :: 79 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is twice the first plus 9: 12 × 2 + 9 = 33 and 31 × 2 + 9 = 71. So 79 × 2 + 9 = 167.

questions.text: 6 boys B1, B2, B3, B4, B5 and B6 are sitting around a rectangular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). Two boys are sitting on each longer side and one boy is sitting on each shorter side of the table. B1 sits second to the left of B6. B4 sits second to the left of B5. B5 is the immediate neighbour of B6 and B2. B5 is not sitting opposite to B4. B1 is not sitting on a shorter side. Which pair of boys is sitting on a shorter side of the rectangular table?
questions.explanation: B6 and B2 flank B5; if B6 were to B5's right, B1 (second to B6's left) would take B2's seat, so going left the order is B5, B6, B4, B1, B3, B2. The two ends are seats three apart and B1 is not at an end; with B6 and B3 at the ends, B4 and B5 would both sit beside B6 and so sit opposite each other, directly across the table, which is ruled out. So B4 and B2 sit on the shorter sides.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'That was his sister' is coded as 'Bo Uv Zs Mn', 'This was his cat' is coded as 'Zs Pt Uv Ga' and 'That was my father' is coded as 'Bo Uv Ex Yz'. What is the code for 'sister' in this code language?
questions.explanation: 'was' is in all three sentences and 'Uv' in all three codes; 'his' is in the first two, so it is 'Zs', and 'That' is in the first and third, so it is 'Bo'. The word left in the first sentence, 'sister', is 'Mn'.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (24, 8, 96) (36, 4, 72)
questions.explanation: The third number is half the product of the first two: 24 × 8 ÷ 2 = 96 and 36 × 4 ÷ 2 = 72. Likewise 12 × 6 ÷ 2 = 36.

questions.text: What will be the value of the given expression if ‘A’ means ‘+’, ‘B’ means ‘–’, ‘C’ means ‘×’, and ‘D’ means ‘÷’? 40 A 30 B 15 C 20 D 5 = ?
questions.explanation: After replacing the letters: 40 + 30 − 15 × 20 ÷ 5 = 40 + 30 − 15 × 4 = 70 − 60 = 10.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. All W are B. II. All M are B. Conclusions: I.Some B are M. II. All W are M. III. All B are W.
options: Only conclusions I and III follow
questions.explanation: All M are B, so some B are M: I follows. W and M both lie within B, but nothing links them to each other, and B may hold things that are not W, so II and III do not follow.

questions.text: The ages of seven girls G1, G2, G3, G4, G5, G6 and G7 are compared. No two girls have the same age. The age of G3 is less than only two girls. The age of G1 is greater than G4 and G7. The age of G6 is the lowest. The age of G5 is not the highest and it is greater than G1. The age of how many girls is greater than G5?
questions.explanation: G6 is the youngest and G3 the third oldest. G5 is older than G1, who is older than G4 and G7, so if G5 were below G3 there would be too few places for them above G6; G5 is second, and as she is not the oldest, G2 is. Only one girl, G2, is older than G5.

questions.text: Identify the number that does NOT belong to the following series. 1.5, 2, 3, 6, 18, 108, 1964
questions.explanation: From the third term on, each term is the product of the two before it: 1.5 × 2 = 3, 2 × 3 = 6, 3 × 6 = 18 and 6 × 18 = 108. The last term should be 18 × 108 = 1944, not 1964.

questions.text: Select the letter-clusters that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. FAN, JDP, NGR, ?, VMV
questions.explanation: The first letters move +4 (F, J, N, R, V), the second +3 (A, D, G, J, M) and the third +2 (N, P, R, T, V): RJT.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which freedom fighter is also known as the ‘Grand Old Man of lndia’?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji, a founder member of the Indian National Congress and three times its president, is known as the 'Grand Old Man of India'. He set out the theory of the drain of India's wealth to Britain.

questions.text: Which organisation of the government of India reports the GDP of the country?
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India
questions.explanation: India's GDP estimates are compiled and released by the Central Statistics Office of the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, which became part of the National Statistical Office in 2019.

questions.text: Which of the following fundamental rights deals with 'Prohibition of Discrimination'?
questions.explanation: Article 15, which prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth, is one of the Right to Equality articles (14 to 18).

questions.text: Uttar Pradesh won the 11th Junior National Men’s Hockey Championship following a 3-1 victory over Chandigarh. Where was the event held?
questions.explanation: The 11th Hockey India Junior Men National Championship was played in December 2021 at Kovilpatti in Tamil Nadu, where Uttar Pradesh beat Hockey Chandigarh 3-1 in the final.

questions.text: ‘Cracking the Code: My Journey to Bollywood’ is the autobiography of _____.
questions.explanation: The actor Ayushmann Khurrana wrote 'Cracking the Code' with his wife Tahira Kashyap; it was published in 2015.

questions.text: At the age of ______, Mahavira left home and went to live in a forest.
questions.explanation: Vardhamana Mahavira, the 24th tirthankara of the Jainas, left home at the age of 30 and lived a hard, lonely life as an ascetic for twelve years before attaining knowledge.

questions.text: Which of the following factors increases the rate of evaporation? I. An increase in surface area; II. A decrease in humidity
questions.explanation: A larger surface exposes more of the liquid to the air, and drier air takes up vapour more readily, so both raise the rate of evaporation.

questions.text: Mahogany tree is found in which of the following types of vegetation?
questions.explanation: Mahogany is a tree of the tropical evergreen (rain) forests, along with ebony, rosewood, rubber and cinchona.

questions.text: How many Grammy nominations have been received by Zubin Mehta as of March 2022?
questions.explanation: The Recording Academy's records list 18 Grammy nominations for the conductor Zubin Mehta, the latest in 2008, and no win.

questions.text: In which district of Rajasthan is the Elephant festival celebrated every year?
questions.explanation: Rajasthan's Elephant Festival, with processions of painted and decorated elephants at Holi, belongs to Jaipur; it has been called off in some years after objections from animal-welfare bodies.

questions.text: Who among the following won the Filmfare Award for Best Choreography for the title song of Sushant Singh Rajput's film Dil Bechara?
questions.explanation: Farah Khan won the Filmfare Award for Best Choreography at the 66th Filmfare Awards (2021) for the title song of 'Dil Bechara'.

questions.text: Which is the longest national highway in India?
questions.explanation: NH-44, which runs north to south from Srinagar to Kanyakumari, is the longest national highway in India.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian cities will co-host the FIH Men’s Hockey World Cup 2023?
questions.explanation: The 2023 FIH Men's Hockey World Cup was played in Odisha in January 2023, at Bhubaneswar and Rourkela.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Quit India movement was started in ______.
questions.explanation: The Congress launched the Quit India movement at its Bombay session on 8 August 1942, with Gandhi's call 'Do or Die'.

questions.text: Name the only Female Muslim ruler of India.
questions.explanation: Razia Sultana ruled the Delhi Sultanate from 1236 to 1240, the only woman to sit on its throne. The other three options are women of early Islamic Arabia who never ruled in India.

questions.text: If unemployment continues to be a long-term feature of a country, then it is called ___________ unemployment.
questions.explanation: Unemployment that persists over a long period as a feature of the economy is called chronic. Structural unemployment comes from a mismatch between workers' skills and the jobs available, and frictional unemployment is the short gap while people move between jobs.

questions.text: Who was appointed as the head coach of the Indian men's cricket team by the BCCI in November 2021?
questions.explanation: The BCCI named Rahul Dravid head coach of the Indian men's team in November 2021, after Ravi Shastri's term ended with the T20 World Cup.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding seasonal unemployment is CORRECT?
options: It happens when people are not able to find jobs during some months of the year.
It happens mainly in urban areas.
If a field requires 4 people, and 7 are employed, then 3 people are seasonally unemployed.
People who do not depend upon agriculture usually face such kind of unemployment.
questions.explanation: Seasonal unemployment is the lack of work in some months of the year, which mainly affects people who depend on agriculture. Seven people on a field that needs four is disguised unemployment.

questions.text: Nita is telling her friend about the smallest planet of our solar system. Which of the following planets is she talking about?
questions.explanation: Mercury, the planet closest to the Sun, is also the smallest planet of the solar system.

questions.text: Which of the following is a dance form of Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: Lavani is a folk dance of Maharashtra, performed to the beat of the dholki. Bhangra is a dance of Punjab and Kathak a classical dance of north India.

questions.text: In a freestanding temple, the mountain-like spire, which can take the shape of a pyramidal tower is called _________.
questions.explanation: The tower over the sanctum of a Hindu temple is a curved shikhara in the northern (Nagara) style and a stepped, pyramidal vimana in the southern (Dravida) style. The garbhagriha is the sanctum itself, the mandapa the hall for worshippers and the vahana the deity's mount.

questions.text: Which of the following cell organelles are NOT present in animal cell?
questions.explanation: Plastids, such as chloroplasts, are found in plant cells but not in animal cells. Ribosomes, lysosomes and mitochondria occur in animal cells.

questions.text: Definition of ‘Money Bills’ is given in which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 110 defines a Money Bill; the Speaker of the Lok Sabha decides whether a bill is one.

questions.text: In October 2021, the Ministry of Civil Aviation launched a scheme which will integrate cargo-related infrastructure in airports of hilly, tribal, and north-east regions. Name the scheme launched by the Ministry of Civil Aviation.
questions.explanation: Krishi UDAN 2.0, announced by the Ministry of Civil Aviation in October 2021, helps move farm produce by air, with a focus on airports in the north-east, hilly and tribal regions. It extended the Krishi UDAN scheme of 2020.

questions.text: Which of the following diseases is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin A?
questions.explanation: Lack of vitamin A causes night blindness. Scurvy comes from lack of vitamin C, and marasmus and kwashiorkor from lack of protein and energy in the diet.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hold the fort
options: To avoid being found guilty of a crime
To take responsibility for a situation temporarily
questions.explanation: To 'hold the fort' is to take charge of things for a while, usually while the person responsible is away.
