questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Writing down your thoughts / can has immense positive / effects on your health.
questions.explanation: A modal verb such as 'can' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'can have immense positive effects', not 'can has'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. It will have “detrimental” effects on the healing process.
questions.explanation: 'Detrimental' means harmful; its opposite is 'benign', harmless or gentle. 'Insidious', 'nasty' and 'baneful' all suggest harm.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Culpable
questions.explanation: 'Culpable' means deserving blame: 'guilty'. 'Innocent' is its opposite, and 'immune' means protected or exempt.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The mystery behind the extinction of the dinosaurs ______ obscure.
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular 'the mystery', not 'the dinosaurs', so it takes 'is': 'The mystery ... is still obscure.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Cryptic
questions.explanation: 'Cryptic' means mysterious or obscure in meaning; its opposite is 'definite', clear and exact. 'Cloudy', 'mystical' and 'fuzzy' are close to 'cryptic'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A place where bees are kept
questions.explanation: An apiary is a place where bees are kept. An archive stores records, a hangar houses aircraft and a granary stores grain.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I think I have left ______ lunchbox at your house.
questions.explanation: Before a noun the possessive determiner 'my' is needed: 'my lunchbox'. 'Mine' stands alone without a noun, and 'I' and 'me' are not possessive.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The lottery is a regular weekly ______ where the drawing of the numbers is done by a little girl.
questions.explanation: 'Recreation' is an activity done for enjoyment, which fits a weekly lottery draw. An 'instalment' is one of the parts in which something is paid or published, an 'irritant' something annoying and a 'theory' an idea that explains something.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. ______ Paul and Jenny are waiting for you in their office.
questions.explanation: 'Both ... and' joins two subjects and takes a plural verb: 'Both Paul and Jenny are waiting'. 'Either' would need 'or', and 'any' and 'all' do not pair with 'and' here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Anita looked ______ the word in the dictionary, but she still did not understand it.
questions.explanation: To 'look up' a word is to search for it in a dictionary or other reference book.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Foods turn brown and crispy when we cook them because for chemical reactions.
questions.explanation: A reason given by a noun phrase takes 'because of': 'because of chemical reactions'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who does a thing for pleasure and not as a profession
questions.explanation: An amateur does something for pleasure, not as a paid profession. An ascetic gives up worldly pleasures, an abattoir is a slaughterhouse and an anarchist rejects all government.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Kangaroo leather is used to make items / that must be strong and flexible hence it is most / common used in bullwhips.
options: Kangaroo leather is used to make items
that must be strong and flexible hence it is most
questions.explanation: The participle 'used' is described by an adverb, not an adjective: 'it is most commonly used in bullwhips'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. He was quick in his anger, but easily “appeased.”
questions.explanation: To 'appease' is to calm someone by giving them what they want: 'pacified'. 'Unsatisfied', 'bugged' and 'dejected' suggest the opposite or a different mood.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'sacrifice', ending in '-fice'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. “Neither of the political parties have had much” interest in environmental causes.
options: Neither of the political parties have had any
Neither of the political parties have much
Neither of the political parties has had much
questions.explanation: 'Neither' takes a singular verb, while the noun after 'of the' stays plural: 'Neither of the political parties has had much interest'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. This Louis Vuitton bag “costed me an arm and a leg.”
questions.explanation: To 'cost an arm and a leg' is to be very expensive.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Her ______ of smell is wonderful.
questions.explanation: Smell is one of the five senses: 'her sense of smell'. A census is an official count of a population.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the incorrectly spelt words in the given sentence. Let us prepare for the upcomng comptitive exams.
options: Let us prepare for the upcomming competive exams.
Let us prepare for the upcoming compititive exams.
Let us prepare for the upcomming competitive exams.
Let us prepare for the upcoming competitive exams.
questions.explanation: The sentence misspells 'upcoming' and 'competitive'. Only 'Let us prepare for the upcoming competitive exams.' corrects both; each of the others still misspells one or both ('upcomming', 'competive', 'compititive').

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. One of the most basic (1)______ of a human is food. Food is grown in various parts of the world according to the climatic (2)______ but one thing that all kinds of crops need (3)______ an exception is water. We all know (4)______ water, sunlight, and nutrition from the soil (5)______ key to a plant’s growth.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'One of the most basic' is followed by a plural noun: 'one of the most basic needs of a human is food'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. One of the most basic (1)______ of a human is food. Food is grown in various parts of the world according to the climatic (2)______ but one thing that all kinds of crops need (3)______ an exception is water. We all know (4)______ water, sunlight, and nutrition from the soil (5)______ key to a plant’s growth.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Crops are grown according to the 'climatic conditions' of a region, the usual phrase; 'climatic weather' would repeat itself.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. One of the most basic (1)______ of a human is food. Food is grown in various parts of the world according to the climatic (2)______ but one thing that all kinds of crops need (3)______ an exception is water. We all know (4)______ water, sunlight, and nutrition from the soil (5)______ key to a plant’s growth.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Every kind of crop needs water 'without an exception', that is in every case.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. One of the most basic (1)______ of a human is food. Food is grown in various parts of the world according to the climatic (2)______ but one thing that all kinds of crops need (3)______ an exception is water. We all know (4)______ water, sunlight, and nutrition from the soil (5)______ key to a plant’s growth.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'That' introduces what we know: 'We all know that water, sunlight, and nutrition ... are key'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. One of the most basic (1)______ of a human is food. Food is grown in various parts of the world according to the climatic (2)______ but one thing that all kinds of crops need (3)______ an exception is water. We all know (4)______ water, sunlight, and nutrition from the soil (5)______ key to a plant’s growth.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The subject lists three things, water, sunlight and nutrition, so the verb is plural: 'are key to a plant's growth'.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 79, 81, 84, 89, 96, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 2, 3, 5 and 7, the prime numbers in order. The next is 11: 96 + 11 = 107.

questions.text: Six boys A, B, C, D, E, and F are sitting in a straight row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). B sits second to the right of D. A sits fourth to the left of F. F is not sitting on the extreme ends of the row. C sits second to the right of B. Who sits second to the right of A?
questions.explanation: A is fourth to the left of F and F is not at an end, so A is first from the left and F fifth. C is second to the right of B, who is second to the right of D, so D, B and C take places 2, 4 and 6, leaving E third: second to the right of A.

questions.text: Among five friends A, B, C, D and E, C is older than only one friend. E is older than D. Only two persons are older than D. B is older than E. Who is the youngest among all the friends?
questions.explanation: C is older than only one friend, so C is fourth by age, and D, with two older, is third. E is older than D and B older than E, so B is first and E second, leaving A fifth, the youngest.

questions.text: Select the option in which the pair of letter-clusters share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of letter-clusters. LAB : BAL :: ?
questions.explanation: The letters are written in reverse order: LAB → BAL. Likewise ONM → MNO.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'FRIGHT' is coded as '860432', and 'HEAR' is coded as '3156'. How will 'EAFT' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter has its own digit: from FRIGHT, F = 8, R = 6, I = 0, G = 4, H = 3, T = 2, and from HEAR, E = 1 and A = 5 (H = 3 and R = 6 agree). So EAFT → 1582.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All snakes are ants. No ant is a lizard. Conclusions: I: Some ants are snakes. II: Some snakes are lizards.
questions.explanation: All snakes are ants, so some ants are snakes: I follows. Every snake is an ant and no ant is a lizard, so no snake is a lizard, and II does not follow.

questions.text: Which two signs need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 2 + 5 − 3 × 6 ÷ 2 = 14
questions.explanation: After interchanging − and ×: 2 + 5 × 3 − 6 ÷ 2 = 2 + 15 − 3 = 14.

questions.text: Six students, Aryan, Shreya, Arshit, Puneet, Kaushal and Harsh, are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Shreya is sitting second to the right of Puneet. Arshit and Harsh are not the immediate neighbours of Shreya. Puneet is third to the right of Aryan. Harsh is sitting second to the left of Kaushal. Who is the immediate neighbour of Shreya and Puneet?
questions.explanation: Puneet is third to Aryan's right, so they sit opposite each other, and Shreya, second to Puneet's right, is next to Aryan. Shreya's other neighbour, in the seat between her and Puneet, cannot be Arshit or Harsh, so it is Kaushal; Harsh, second to Kaushal's left, sits next to Puneet, and Arshit next to Aryan.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'TRICAD' is written as 'FBEJTU', and 'OPQSBG' is written as 'ICURRP'. How will 'ABKLMN' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and its letters moved +2 and +1 in turn: TRICAD → DACIRT → FBEJTU and OPQSBG → GBSQPO → ICURRP. So ABKLMN → NMLKBA → PNNLDB.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) 133 : 666 :: 157 : 786 :: 221 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is five times the first plus 1: 133 × 5 + 1 = 666 and 157 × 5 + 1 = 786. Likewise 221 × 5 + 1 = 1106.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. RAT, UEY, XID, ?, DQN
questions.explanation: The first letters move +3 (R, U, X, A, D), the second +4 (A, E, I, M, Q) and the third +5 (T, Y, D, I, N). The missing cluster is AMI.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'LOWER' is coded as '37', and 'OVER' is coded as '06'. How will 'MELON' be coded in that code language?
questions.explanation: Add the letters' places in the alphabet and reverse the total: LOWER = 12 + 15 + 23 + 5 + 18 = 73 → 37 and OVER = 15 + 22 + 5 + 18 = 60 → 06. MELON = 13 + 5 + 12 + 15 + 14 = 59 → 95.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No phone is mobile. Some mobiles are telephones. Conclusions: I. All phones being telephones is a possibility. II. Some telephones are not mobiles.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: No statement links phones and telephones directly, so all phones being telephones is possible and I follows. All telephones could be mobiles, so II need not follow.

questions.text: Which two signs and two numbers (NOT digits) need to be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 16 + 15 – 25 × 4 ÷ 5 = 20
questions.explanation: After interchanging × and ÷ and the numbers 16 and 25: 25 + 15 − 16 ÷ 4 × 5 = 25 + 15 − 20 = 20.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'CHILDREN' is written as 'OFSEMJID', 'CURTAIN' is written as 'OJBUSVD', and 'LIQUID' is written as 'EJVRJM'. How will 'PERFORMANCE' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed and each letter moved one place forward: LIQUID → DIUQIL → EJVRJM and CURTAIN → NIATRUC → OJBUSVD. So PERFORMANCE → ECNAMROFREP → FDOBNSPGSFQ.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word and the fourth word is related to the third word. Year : Month :: Week : Day :: Minute : ?
questions.explanation: Each pair is a unit of time and a smaller unit it is made up of: a year of months and a week of days. Likewise a minute is made up of seconds.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. GAME : IWSW :: HOPE : JKVW :: SOLO : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +2, −4, +6 and −8: GAME → IWSW and HOPE → JKVW. So S → U, O → K, L → R and O → G: UKRG.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (30, 14, 8); (84, 12, 36)
questions.explanation: In each set the first number is the second plus twice the third: 14 + 2 × 8 = 30 and 12 + 2 × 36 = 84. Likewise 18 + 2 × 45 = 108.

questions.text: The practice of erecting megaliths began about ______ years ago.
questions.explanation: NCERT dates the start of megalith building in the subcontinent to about 3,000 years ago; these stone burial markers are found across the Deccan, south India, the north-east and Kashmir.

questions.text: As of April 2022, which neighbouring country of India shares an international boundary with Ladakh?
questions.explanation: Of the options only Pakistan touches Ladakh, along the Line of Control on its western side; China lies to its north and east. Nepal, Bhutan and Myanmar border states further east.

questions.text: Which of the following is a temperate grassland in Russia?
questions.explanation: The steppes are the temperate grasslands of Eurasia, stretching across Russia, Ukraine and Kazakhstan. The prairies are North America's, while the Amazon and Congo basins are covered by tropical rainforest.

questions.text: Who won the National Nritya Shiromani award 2022?
questions.explanation: Aparna Satheesan, a Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam dancer and a senior disciple of Guru Vyjayanthi Kashi, was chosen for the National Nritya Shiromani Award 2022 for her contribution to Kuchipudi; it was announced in December 2021 for presentation at the 13th Cuttack Mahotsav in Odisha in January 2022.

questions.text: Which of the following types of plant is a seed bearing plant?
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms bear seeds, though not enclosed in a fruit. Thallophytes, bryophytes and pteridophytes have no seeds and reproduce by spores.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was the ruler of Mysore in 1761?
questions.explanation: Haidar (Hyder) Ali took control of Mysore in 1761 and ruled until 1782, followed by his son Tipu Sultan. Baji Rao was a Maratha Peshwa, Murshid Quli Jafar Khan a Nawab of Bengal and Nizam-ul-Mulk the founder of Hyderabad state.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was the accused in the murder of Saunders in 1928?
questions.explanation: Bhagat Singh, with Rajguru, shot the police officer J P Saunders in Lahore in December 1928, to avenge the death of Lala Lajpat Rai; the killing was among the charges in the Lahore Conspiracy Case.

questions.text: Which chemical element does ‘Fe’ stand for in the science periodic table?
questions.explanation: Fe is the symbol of iron, from its Latin name 'ferrum'. Fluorine is F, oxygen O and fermium Fm.

questions.text: Chitti Babu is associated with which musical instrument?
questions.explanation: Chitti Babu (1936-1996) was a leading Carnatic veena player.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The first railway line was from _______ to ________ in India in 1853.
questions.explanation: India's first passenger train ran on 16 April 1853 from Bori Bunder in Bombay (Mumbai) to Thane, about 34 km.

questions.text: ‘The Test of My Life’ is the autobiography of which of the following persons?
questions.explanation: 'The Test of My Life: From Cricket to Cancer and Back' (2013) is Yuvraj Singh's account of his fight with cancer after the 2011 World Cup.

questions.text: Who among the following Indian players is also known as ‘Dhing Express’?
questions.explanation: The sprinter Hima Das is called the 'Dhing Express' after her home village, Dhing, in Nagaon district, Assam.

questions.text: Who became UNDP India's First Youth Climate Champion?
questions.explanation: In January 2022 UNDP India named the content creator and actor Prajakta Koli its first Youth Climate Champion, to raise awareness of climate change among young people.

questions.text: Indian constitution borrowed a cabinet form of governance from ___________.
questions.explanation: The parliamentary system, with a cabinet responsible to the legislature, was borrowed from the British (United Kingdom) model.

questions.text: Which of the following is correct about Nagara or North Indian Temple Style Architecture?
options: There were no tower or shikhara.
There was no Kalasha, the topmost part of the temple.
The garbhagriha is always located directly under the tallest tower.
questions.explanation: In the Nagara style the sanctum (garbhagriha) lies directly beneath the tallest tower, the shikhara. Nagara temples do have shikharas, crowned by an amalaka and a kalasha, and usually lack the elaborate boundary walls and gateways of the Dravida style.

questions.text: Who defeated Prithviraj Chauhan in the second battle of Tarain in 1192 AD?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ghori defeated Prithviraj Chauhan in the second battle of Tarain in 1192, a year after losing the first battle to him.

questions.text: Who among the following was the minister of Agriculture and Farmer's Welfare when the Farm Laws Repeal Bill, 2021 was passed in the Indian Parliament?
questions.explanation: Narendra Singh Tomar was the Union Minister of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare when both Houses passed the Farm Laws Repeal Bill, 2021 on 29 November 2021; he moved it in the Lok Sabha.

questions.text: The period between prorogation of Parliament and re-assembly in a new session is called ___________.
questions.explanation: The gap between the prorogation of a House and its reassembly in a new session is a recess. An adjournment suspends a sitting, dissolution ends the life of the Lok Sabha, and a cut motion seeks to reduce a demand for grants.

questions.text: What is the distance between the stumps and the popping crease at the same end of a Cricket pitch?
questions.explanation: The popping crease is marked 4 feet (1.22 m) in front of the bowling crease, the line on which the stumps stand.

questions.text: In which of the following states of India is the Dree festival celebrated?
questions.explanation: Dree is the agricultural festival of the Apatani people of the Ziro valley in Arunachal Pradesh, held in July with prayers for a good harvest.

questions.text: What is the year whose prices are used to calculate the real GDP called?
questions.explanation: Real GDP values output at the prices of a chosen base year, so that changes reflect quantities produced rather than price rises.

questions.text: Which rivers meet at Devprayag?
questions.explanation: At Devprayag in Uttarakhand the Bhagirathi and the Alaknanda meet to form the Ganga.

questions.text: For the purpose of Census 2011, a person aged ______ and above, who can both read and write with understanding in any language, was treated as literate.
questions.explanation: Census 2011 counted as literate a person aged seven and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language.

questions.text: A balanced diet should meet the RDAs for an individual. State the full form of RDA.
questions.explanation: RDA stands for Recommended Dietary Allowances, the daily amounts of energy and nutrients advised to meet the needs of nearly all healthy people of a given age, sex and activity level.

questions.text: The famous actor Hema Malini is a trained _______ dancer.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Bharatanatyam, the classical form Hema Malini trained in and is best known for. She also studied Kuchipudi, with Vempati Chinna Satyam, which makes that option arguable, but she is described above all as a Bharatanatyam dancer.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The young boy tried to jerk out of the way, / but she grabbed him and began / rubbing the tip of his nose to get the stain off.
options: The young boy tried to jerk out of the way
rubbing the tip of his nose to get the stain off
but she grabbed him and began
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct as it stands: 'tried to jerk out of the way', 'began rubbing' and 'to get the stain off' are all standard English.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Revile
questions.explanation: To 'revile' is to criticise someone in an abusive or angry way, so 'abuse' is the synonym. 'Incite' means to stir up and 'discourage' to put off.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. Stop “flogging a dead horse” and concentrate on your career.
options: To waste time on useless things
questions.explanation: To 'flog a dead horse' is to waste effort on something that is already finished or has no chance of success.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'autocracy', rule by one person with absolute power; it ends in '-cracy', as 'bureaucracy' does.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We need to ______ for next week, so are you in or out?
questions.explanation: To 'make plans' is to arrange what to do, which is what 'are you in or out?' asks the listener to join.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. The plants “readily respond to these stimulus.”
questions.explanation: 'These' is plural, so the noun must be the plural 'stimuli'; the adverb 'readily' and the plural verb 'respond' (agreeing with 'the plants') stay.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Fright
questions.explanation: 'Fright' is sudden fear, so 'dread', great fear, is the synonym. 'Composure' and 'bravery' are nearly opposite, and 'mockery' means ridicule.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. We are all aware that our environment are not what it used to be.
questions.explanation: The subject 'our environment' is singular, so it takes 'is': 'our environment is not what it used to be'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Resonate' is spelt correctly. The others should be 'escapade', 'progression' and 'discovery'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Most of the carbon-trapping mechanisms / that we have identified are / based at limit studies.
questions.explanation: Mechanisms are 'based on' something, not 'at', and the noun 'studies' needs the adjective 'limited': 'based on limited studies'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Incapable of making mistakes or being wrong
questions.explanation: 'Infallible' means incapable of making mistakes. A fatalist believes everything is fated, a fanatic is excessively zealous and a cynic believes people act only from self-interest.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. Half a million dollars is only a “drop in the bucket” to what is required for this industry.
options: unity and functioning together to achieve a goal
A very small part of something big or whole
a person or situation having no hope of positive change
questions.explanation: A 'drop in the bucket' is an amount far too small to matter against what is needed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. This small hut is going to be my ______ for the next three days.
questions.explanation: An 'abode' is a home or a place to live, which is what the hut will be. A legacy is something handed down, a scout someone sent ahead and a loaf a shaped mass of bread.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He believed that he had struck terror in his children's hearts because of his _____________.
questions.explanation: His 'rage', violent anger, is what would strike terror into his children; 'love' and 'calmness' would not, and 'fortune' does not fit the sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Miss Samantha is at the ______ of her popularity.
questions.explanation: The 'peak' is the highest point. 'Peek', a quick look, sounds the same, and 'pick' and 'peck' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Flexible
questions.explanation: Of a person, 'flexible' means willing to change or give way, like 'compliant'; 'defiant', openly refusing to give way, is the nearest opposite. 'Peculiar' and 'reckless' are unrelated.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. As the tree came crashing down, the monkeys “woke up from its sleep” and ran from branch to branch.
questions.explanation: 'The monkeys' is plural, so the pronoun must be 'their': 'the monkeys woke up from their sleep'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The age of the participants ______ an important factor in this competition.
questions.explanation: The subject is 'the age', which is singular, so the verb is 'is'; the phrase 'of the participants' does not change it.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. “No other informations” was conveyed to him.
questions.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable and has no plural form: 'No other information was conveyed to him.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Someone working or acting merely for money or other rewards
questions.explanation: A mercenary works merely for money or reward, as a soldier hired by a foreign army does. A debtor owes money and a contractor agrees to do work under a contract.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Mahalia Jackson was (1) ______ into a preacher's family in 1911, and she grew up in a riverfront shanty in New Orleans. She was motherless at five, working as a maid and laundress in her mid-teens. As a little girl, she would (2) ______ to herself before she went to sleep, "Someday the sun is going to shine down on me in some faraway place." In pursuit of that dream, Mahalia migrated to Chicago when she was still a teenager. She never expected to support herself by singing, and by the time I joined her, the hands she used so expressively in her performances had (3) ______ floors, (4) ______ and helped her earn a living as a hotel maid, factory worker, beautician and florist. But her remarkable (5) ______ brought her more and more invitations to singat funerals, in churches, at concerts. And, through her warm friendly personality and a life based on sound spiritual values and hard work, she eventually found her place in the sun.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: To be 'born into' a family is to be born a member of it: 'was born into a preacher's family in 1911'.

In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In pursuit of that dream, Mahalia migrated to Chicago when she was still a teenager. She never expected to support herself by singing, and by the time I joined her, the hands she used so expressively in her performances had (3) ______ floors, (4) ______ and helped her earn a living as a hotel maid, factory worker, beautician and florist. But her remarkable (5) ______ brought her more and more invitations to singat funerals, in churches, at concerts. And, through her warm friendly personality and a life based on sound spiritual values and hard work, she eventually found her place in the sun.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The quoted words are something she said softly to herself before sleep: she would 'whisper' them. 'Glimmer' and 'prosper' do not describe speech, and 'crisper' is not a verb.

And, through her warm friendly personality and a life based on sound spiritual values and hard work, she eventually found her place in the sun.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Her hands had 'scrubbed' floors, cleaning them by rubbing hard, as she did working as a maid.

And, through her warm friendly personality and a life based on sound spiritual values and hard work, she eventually found her place in the sun.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: She had worked as a laundress, so besides scrubbing floors her hands had 'laundered', that is washed and ironed clothes.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Mahalia Jackson was (1) ______ into a preacher's family in 1911, and she grew up in a riverfront shanty in New Orleans. She was motherless at five, working as a maid and laundress in her mid-teens.
