But her remarkable (5) ______ brought her more and more invitations to singat funerals, in churches, at concerts. And, through her warm friendly personality and a life based on sound spiritual values and hard work, she eventually found her place in the sun.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: It was her remarkable singing 'voice' that brought her invitations to sing at funerals, in churches and at concerts.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'STOPER' is written as 'XNTJJL' and 'GANOPY' is written as 'LUSIUS'. How will 'FITAND' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move 5 forward and 6 back in turn, wrapping round the alphabet: STOPER → XNTJJL and GANOPY → LUSIUS. So F → K, I → C, T → Y, A → U, N → S and D → X: KCYUSX.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 410, 210, 110, 60, 35, ?

Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. H64 : J100 :: L144 : N196 :: U441 : ?
questions.explanation: The number is the square of the letter's place in the alphabet, and the letter moves 2 places forward: H (8) 64 → J (10) 100 and L (12) 144 → N (14) 196. So U (21) 441 → W (23) 529.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. No R is a G. II. All G’s are H. Conclusions: I. No H is a R. II. No G is a R.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: 'No R is a G' converts to 'No G is a R', so II follows. The H that are not G may still be R, so I does not follow.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 803, 844, 885, 926, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 41 more than the one before: 803, 844, 885, 926, and 926 + 41 = 967.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. RS : QT :: AK : ?
questions.explanation: The two letters swap places, then the first moves 2 places back and the second 2 forward: RS → SR → QT. Likewise AK → KA → IC.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'PINT' is coded as '60', and 'HOME' is coded as '42'. How will 'TONE' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet plus 1: PINT = 16 + 9 + 14 + 20 + 1 = 60 and HOME = 8 + 15 + 13 + 5 + 1 = 42. So TONE = 20 + 15 + 14 + 5 + 1 = 55.

questions.text: By interchanging which two signs will the given equation be correct? 11 ÷ 77 + 253 × 23 – 800 = 58
Select the option in which the numbers shares the same relationship as that shared by the numbers in the given set. (32, 70, 108)
questions.explanation: The numbers rise by 38 each time: 32 + 38 = 70 and 70 + 38 = 108. Likewise 42 + 38 = 80 and 80 + 38 = 118.

questions.text: Which two signs need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 96 − 12 ÷ 6 + 3 × 5 = 17
questions.explanation: After interchanging ÷ and −: 96 ÷ 12 − 6 + 3 × 5 = 8 − 6 + 15 = 17.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'GERMAN' is written as 'HFSLZM', and 'RUSTIC' is written as 'SVTSHB'. How will 'DIVIDE' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first three letters move 1 place forward and the last three 1 place back: GERMAN → HFS LZM and RUSTIC → SVT SHB. So DIVIDE → EJW HCD: EJWHCD.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first-letter cluster. CWIS : VBPF ∷ AOLD : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite (A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y and so on) and then moved 2 places back: C → X → V, W → D → B, I → R → P, S → H → F. So A → Z → X, O → L → J, L → O → M, D → W → U: XJMU.

questions.text: Amit, Bablu, Ramesh, Deepak, Imran, Sunil, and Sanju are sitting around a circular table facing opposite to the centre. Amit does not sit adjacent to Imran and Sanju. Bablu does not sit adjacent to Amit. Sanju sits second to the left of Imran. Ramesh sits fourth to the left of Amit. Deepak and Bablu sit adjacent to each other. Who sits immediate right of Amit?
questions.explanation: Facing away from the centre, each person's right is clockwise. The seats beside Amit can hold neither Imran, Sanju nor Bablu, so Deepak and Sunil take them, and with Ramesh fourth to Amit's left only one placing fits: clockwise from Amit, Amit, Sunil, Sanju, Ramesh, Imran, Bablu, Deepak. Sunil is on Amit's immediate right.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in it. (7, 9, 130), (11, 9, ?), (16, 8, 320)
questions.explanation: The third number is the sum of the squares of the first two: 7² + 9² = 49 + 81 = 130 and 16² + 8² = 256 + 64 = 320. So 11² + 9² = 121 + 81 = 202.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'POM' is coded as '43', and 'HAN' is coded as '22'. How will 'BRO' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet minus 1: POM = 16 + 15 + 13 − 1 = 43 and HAN = 8 + 1 + 14 − 1 = 22. So BRO = 2 + 18 + 15 − 1 = 34.

questions.text: Five friends P, Q, R, S and T are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). Q is second to the left of T. S is the immediate neighbour of Q and T. R is not the immediate neighbour of Q. While counting from the left of Q, how many friends are sitting between Q and S?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, each friend's left is clockwise. Q second to T's left with S between them, and R not beside Q, give clockwise from Q: Q, P, R, T, S. So three friends (P, R and T) sit between Q and S counting from Q's left.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some holders are parameters. Some chambers are parameters. Some parameters are not measures. Conclusions: I. Some measures are chambers. II. Some holders are chambers.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Holders and chambers are each linked only to some parameters, which may be different ones, so II does not follow; and 'some parameters are not measures' says nothing about chambers, so I does not follow either.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. BJT, DHV, FFX, ?, JBB
questions.explanation: The first letters move 2 forward (B, D, F, H, J), the second 2 back (J, H, F, D, B) and the third 2 forward, wrapping round after Z (T, V, X, Z, B): HDZ.

questions.text: Among five persons A, B, C, D and E, who are of different ages, A is younger than only D and E. E is younger than D and older than B. C is the youngest. Who is the fourth oldest?
questions.explanation: A is younger than only D and E, so A is third oldest, and D is older than E. B is younger than A and C is the youngest, so from the oldest the order is D, E, A, B, C: B is fourth.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of autotrophs?
questions.explanation: Green plants make their own food by photosynthesis, so they are autotrophs. Animals and most protozoa feed on other organisms, and viruses can multiply only inside living cells.

questions.text: Which of the following terms is NOT associated with cricket?
questions.explanation: A slam dunk is a basketball shot. A maiden (an over with no runs), LBW (leg before wicket) and a yorker are cricket terms.

questions.text: Which of the following festivals marks the start of the Telugu New year?
questions.explanation: Ugadi marks the New Year in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka. Gudi Padwa is the Marathi New Year, while Onam (Kerala) and Pongal (Tamil Nadu) are harvest festivals.

questions.text: In which year did the Bhopal Gas Tragedy take place?
questions.explanation: The Bhopal gas tragedy happened on the night of 2-3 December 1984, when methyl isocyanate gas leaked from the Union Carbide pesticide plant in Bhopal.

questions.text: Most Harappan seals made of _____.
questions.explanation: Most Harappan seals were carved from steatite, a soft stone, and usually bear an animal figure and a line of the Harappan script.

questions.text: Who was the first Indian composer to win the Grammy Award?
questions.explanation: Pandit Ravi Shankar won a Grammy in 1968 with Yehudi Menuhin for 'West Meets East', the first Indian to win one. Zakir Hussain's first came in 1992 ('Planet Drum') and A R Rahman's in 2010.

questions.text: If a fundamental right of a citizen of India is violated, _____.
options: he has to appeal in the Supreme court only
he has to appeal in the district court first
he has the choice of either approaching the Supreme court directly or the High court
he has to appeal in the High court first
questions.explanation: Article 32 lets a person go straight to the Supreme Court to enforce a fundamental right, and Article 226 gives the High Courts the same power, so there is no need to approach a lower court first.

questions.text: Which of the following countries belong to the polar regions?
questions.explanation: Northern Canada lies inside the Arctic Circle, in the north polar region. Colombia straddles the equator and China lies in the low and middle northern latitudes, while Chile's South American territory ends near 56° S, well short of the Antarctic Circle (its claim to part of Antarctica is frozen under the Antarctic Treaty).

questions.text: Kathak is a classical dance form of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Kathak is the classical dance of Uttar Pradesh, with its Lucknow gharana. Bharatanatyam belongs to Tamil Nadu, Manipuri to Manipur and Sattriya to Assam.

questions.text: Mirabai Chanu won the first silver medal for India in weightlifting at the ___________ Olympics 2020.
questions.explanation: Mirabai Chanu won silver in the women's 49 kg weightlifting at the Tokyo Olympics, held in July 2021, India's first Olympic silver in the sport; Karnam Malleswari had won bronze at Sydney 2000.

questions.text: Which of the following measures of money supply is least liquid of all?
questions.explanation: Liquidity falls from M1 to M4: M1 (currency with the public and demand deposits) is the most liquid, and M4, which adds all post office deposits to M3, the least.

questions.text: Damon Galgut was awarded the Booker Prize 2021 for Fiction for his book _____.
questions.explanation: Damon Galgut won the 2021 Booker Prize for 'The Promise'. 'Great Circle' (Maggie Shipstead), 'A Passage North' (Anuk Arudpragasam) and 'The Fortune Men' (Nadifa Mohamed) were also on that year's shortlist.

questions.text: The workforce population includes people between ______ years.
questions.explanation: NCERT defines the workforce population as people from 15 to 59 years of age.

questions.text: Which of the following is a noble chemical element of the modern periodic table?
questions.explanation: Neon is a noble gas, in group 18 of the periodic table. Fluorine is a halogen, nitrogen a group 15 non-metal and silicon a metalloid.

questions.text: Who among the following is popularly known as the ‘Disco King’ passed away in February 2022?
questions.explanation: Bappi Lahiri, the composer and singer who brought disco music into Hindi films, died in Mumbai on 15 February 2022.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following published the book ‘Stripurushtulna’?
questions.explanation: Tarabai Shinde published 'Stri Purush Tulana' (1882), a sharp comparison of how society treated women and men.

questions.text: Kanishka was a ruler of ______ dynasty.
questions.explanation: Kanishka, the best-known Kushana king, ruled from Purushapura (Peshawar) and was a great patron of Buddhism.

questions.text: Who ruled over Delhi after Razia Sultan?
questions.explanation: Balban is the only option who ruled after Razia Sultan (1236-1240), though not directly: Bahram Shah, Alauddin Masud and Nasiruddin Mahmud came between, and Balban took the throne in 1266. Iltutmish, her father, Qutbuddin Aibak and Prithviraj Chauhan all ruled before her.

questions.text: Which of the following campaigns was launched for greywater management in March 2022?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Jal Shakti launched Sujlam 2.0, a campaign for greywater management, on World Water Day, 22 March 2022; the first Sujlam campaign began in August 2021.

questions.text: As of April 2022, what is the official language of India's neighbouring country China?
questions.explanation: China's official language is Mandarin (Standard Chinese). Bengali is the official language of Bangladesh and Burmese of Myanmar, while Sri Lanka's official languages are Sinhala and Tamil.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year through the Indian Official Secrets Act was freedom of press curbed?
questions.explanation: The Indian Official Secrets Act of 1904, passed under Lord Curzon, extended the 1889 law from military to civil matters and so restricted what the press could publish.

questions.text: This layer of soil is dark in colour as it is rich in humus and minerals. It is generally soft, porous and can retain more water. It is called:
questions.explanation: The topsoil, or A-horizon, is the uppermost layer: dark with humus and minerals, soft, porous and able to hold more water. The B-horizon below has less humus, and the C-horizon is broken parent rock above the bedrock.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a function of the State Public Service Commission?
options: It conducts examinations for appointments to the services of the state.
It is consulted in all disciplinary matters affecting a person serving under the government of the state in a civil capacity.
It is consulted on any claim for the award of a pension in respect of injuries sustained by a person while serving under the government of the state.
It is consulted while making reservations of appointments or posts in favour of any backward class of citizens.
questions.explanation: Under Article 320(4) a Public Service Commission need not be consulted on reservations for backward classes made under Article 16(4). Conducting examinations, disciplinary matters and pension claims for injuries are among its functions under Article 320(1) and (3).

questions.text: Which of the following minerals are NOT found in Chota nagpur-belt?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives gold. Coal (Jharia, Bokaro) and iron ore (Noamundi) are the Chota Nagpur belt's chief minerals and chromite occurs in West Singhbhum, while India's gold has come mainly from Karnataka's Kolar and Hutti fields, though the belt does have small gold deposits, such as the mine at Kundarkocha in East Singhbhum.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. After a long and “rigorous” fast the Lord appeared before him.
questions.explanation: 'Rigorous' means strict or severe, so its opposite is 'lenient', mild and tolerant. 'Exhausting' and 'oppressive' lean the same way as 'rigorous'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Most workers “resigns” to join new jobs within the same industry.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'workers' needs a plural verb, and of the options only the simple past 'resigned' agrees with it: 'Most workers resigned to join new jobs'. 'Was resigning' and 'has resigned' are singular forms.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. A tiger’s skull / is similar / to / a lion.
questions.explanation: Like must be compared with like: a tiger's skull is similar to a lion's skull, so the last part should read 'that of a lion' (or 'a lion's').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. My friend, who is a photographer, is ________ a writer.
questions.explanation: 'Also' stands after the verb 'is' and before the words it adds: 'is also a writer'. 'Too' would go at the end of the sentence.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The bank was prepared to ______ chance and lend him 40% of the purchase price.
questions.explanation: To 'take a chance' is to accept a risk in the hope of success: the bank was willing to risk lending him the money.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. People and / there demands / are ever-growing, but / the availability of land is limited.
options: the availability of land is limited
questions.explanation: 'There' is an adverb of place; the possessive 'their' is needed: 'People and their demands are ever-growing'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I'm frustrated with the ______ minded view of history this article presents.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'narrow': a 'narrow-minded' view is one that will not consider other ideas or perspectives, the usual complaint about a one-sided account of history. 'Small-minded' is close in sense but stresses pettiness, and 'wide' and 'bigger' would not be a complaint.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. Caffeine is a diuretic that makes you urinate “more often.”
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: 'more often' is the comparative of the adverb 'often'. 'Oftenly' is not a word, and 'many often' and 'more much often' are ungrammatical.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. I always “smell a rat” when John says that he is going out for extra classes.
questions.explanation: To 'smell a rat' is to suspect that something is wrong or that someone is being deceitful.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The Armenian language has many dialects, some of which cannot be ______ by speakers of other dialects.
questions.explanation: Dialects that have drifted far apart may not be 'understood' by speakers of other dialects; the sentence is about whether they can follow one another.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Someone who is silent or uncommunicative in speech.
questions.explanation: A 'reserved' person says little and is slow to show feelings or opinions. 'Garrulous' and 'voluble' mean the opposite, talkative, and 'imperceptible' means too slight to be noticed.

questions.text: Select the idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Roy's customers think that the council has “become irrational.”
questions.explanation: To 'go bananas' is to become crazy or irrational: 'the council has gone bananas'. 'Browned off' means fed up, 'a piece of cake' something easy and 'too much on their plates' too much to deal with.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Ebullient
questions.explanation: 'Ebullient' means cheerful and full of energy, so its opposite is 'dejected', sad and low in spirits. 'Buoyant' and 'carefree' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. The family can “none long stay” in their big house.
questions.explanation: 'No longer' means not any more, and it stands between the modal and the main verb: 'The family can no longer stay in their big house.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Enraged
questions.explanation: 'Enraged' means very angry: 'furious'. 'Peaceful' and 'elated' are far from it, and 'fortunate' is unrelated.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'foreign', with the 'e' before the 'i'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Flagrant
questions.explanation: 'Flagrant' describes wrongdoing that is shockingly obvious and offensive, as in a flagrant violation: 'atrocious', very wicked or bad. The other three are words of praise.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required.’ Many people believe that women make better nurses “because they are” patient and gentle.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: the plural 'women' takes 'they are', and the present tense suits a belief people hold. 'She is' does not agree with 'women', and 'were' and 'would' shift the tense for no reason.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Strengthen' is spelt correctly. The others should be 'equipment', 'instrumental' and 'reversal'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Many countries are not acting / fast enough to controlled / climate change.
questions.explanation: After 'to' the infinitive takes the base form of the verb: 'fast enough to control climate change'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Elephant Island's name is attributed to (1) ______ its elephant head-like appearance and the sighting of elephant seals (2) ______ Captain George Powell in 1821, one of the (3) ______ sightings. (4) ______, in Russia it is still known under the name (5) ______ by its discoverers in 1821 – Mordvinova Island.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Both ... and' joins the two reasons for the name: the island's elephant-head shape and the sighting of elephant seals.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Elephant Island's name is attributed to (1) ______ its elephant head-like appearance and the sighting of elephant seals (2) ______ Captain George Powell in 1821, one of the (3) ______ sightings. (4) ______, in Russia it is still known under the name (5) ______ by its discoverers in 1821 – Mordvinova Island.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The seals were sighted 'by' Captain George Powell: 'by' names the person who did the action.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Elephant Island's name is attributed to (1) ______ its elephant head-like appearance and the sighting of elephant seals (2) ______ Captain George Powell in 1821, one of the (3) ______ sightings. (4) ______, in Russia it is still known under the name (5) ______ by its discoverers in 1821 – Mordvinova Island.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'One of the' is followed by a superlative: 'one of the earliest sightings'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Elephant Island's name is attributed to (1) ______ its elephant head-like appearance and the sighting of elephant seals (2) ______ Captain George Powell in 1821, one of the (3) ______ sightings. (4) ______, in Russia it is still known under the name (5) ______ by its discoverers in 1821 – Mordvinova Island.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'However' introduces a contrast: whatever the reasons for the English name, in Russia the island goes by another one.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Elephant Island's name is attributed to (1) ______ its elephant head-like appearance and the sighting of elephant seals (2) ______ Captain George Powell in 1821, one of the (3) ______ sightings. (4) ______, in Russia it is still known under the name (5) ______ by its discoverers in 1821 – Mordvinova Island.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: A name is 'given' by the people who name a place: 'the name given by its discoverers in 1821'.

questions.text: Three boys T, R and M are sitting in a row facing towards the north (not necessarily in the same order), and three girls F, G and K are sitting in a row facing towards the face of these boys (not necessarily in the same order). F and R are diagonally opposite to each other. K is not at any of the ends. Which of the following pairs of persons facing towards each other is/are definitely correct? I. GR II. KT
questions.explanation: K is not at an end, so K sits in the middle of the girls' row and F and G take the ends. R is diagonally opposite F, so R sits at the other end of the boys' row, facing G: GR is definite. K faces the middle boy, who may be T or M, so KT is not definite.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. KSZ : PHC :: TNK : ?
questions.explanation: The first two letters become their opposite letters (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on) and the third moves 3 places on: K → P, S → H, Z → C. So T → G, N → M and K → N: GMN.

questions.text: Eight girls A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H are sitting around a circular table facing opposite to the centre (not necessarily in the same order). B is second to the left of D. F is third to the left of B. A is second to the left of F. C is second to the left of A. G is third to the left of E. Three out of the following four options are similar by a certain logic and form a group. Which of the following does NOT belong to that group?
questions.explanation: Facing outwards, the girls sit in this order going round to the left: D, C, B, E, H, F, G, A. In A, C, E; D, B, H; and C, E, F each girl sits second to the left of the one before, but in D, H, G, H is fourth to the left of D.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'GAME' is coded as '78', and 'PNAD' is coded as '105'. How will 'HORN' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each code is three times the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet: GAME = 7 + 1 + 13 + 5 = 26 and 26 × 3 = 78; PNAD = 35 and 35 × 3 = 105. HORN = 8 + 15 + 18 + 14 = 55, and 55 × 3 = 165.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'HALMST' is written as 'IZMLTS' and 'GEASTR' is written as 'HDBRUQ'. How will 'TRAILS' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1 and −1 in turn: H → I, A → Z, L → M, M → L, S → T, T → S. So TRAILS → UQBHMR.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and fourth number is related to third number. 23 : 25 :: 17 : 64 :: 29 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second number is the square of the digit sum of the first: (2 + 3)² = 25 and (1 + 7)² = 64. So (2 + 9)² = 121.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 64, 51, 38, ?, 12, –1
questions.explanation: Each term is 13 less than the one before: 38 − 13 = 25, and 25 − 13 = 12.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. Some games are lands. II. Some toys are games. Conclusions: I. Some toys are not lands. II. Some lands are games.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: 'Some games are lands' converts to 'Some lands are games', so II follows. Nothing in the statements decides whether any toys lie outside the lands, so I does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'WORD' is written as 'CUXJ' and 'MOKE' is written as ‘SUQK’. How will 'IDEA' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 6 places on: W → C, O → U, R → X, D → J and M → S, O → U, K → Q, E → K. So IDEA → OJKG.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 13, 51, 205, 819, 3277, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 4 times the one before, minus and plus 1 in turn: 13 × 4 − 1 = 51, 51 × 4 + 1 = 205, 205 × 4 − 1 = 819, 819 × 4 + 1 = 3277, then 3277 × 4 − 1 = 13107.

questions.text: Select the option in which the two numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers in the given number-pair. 64 : 10 :: ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the sum of the digits of the first: 6 + 4 = 10. Likewise 8 + 4 = 12; the digit sums of 54, 32 and 42 are 9, 5 and 6.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. GROW, FSNX, ETMY, ?, CVKA
questions.explanation: The first letters move back one (G, F, E, D, C), the second on one (R, S, T, U, V), the third back one (O, N, M, L, K) and the fourth on one (W, X, Y, Z, A): DULZ.

questions.text: After interchanging which two numbers will the value of the given expression be ‘173’? 52 – 36 + 141 × 63 ÷ 47

Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. FNNC: CKKZ:: ADRS: XAOP:: BNNL: ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places back: F → C, N → K, C → Z and A → X, D → A, R → O, S → P. So BNNL → YKKI.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. PRO : NOL :: HEL : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move back 2, 3 and 3 places: P → N, R → O, O → L. So H → F, E → B, L → I: FBI.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'BASEBALL' is written as '45' and 'FEEDBACK' is written as '73'. How will 'PRACTICE' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet, written backwards: BASEBALL = 2 + 1 + 19 + 5 + 2 + 1 + 12 + 12 = 54 → 45 and FEEDBACK = 37 → 73. PRACTICE = 16 + 18 + 1 + 3 + 20 + 9 + 3 + 5 = 75 → 57.

questions.text: After interchanging the given two signs and two numbers, what will be the value of the given expression? 15 and 3; + and ÷; 6 ÷ 3 + 5 × 15 – 9 = ?
Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose International airport is situated in _____.
questions.explanation: Kolkata's airport at Dum Dum is named Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose International Airport.

questions.text: The President of India can nominate maximum ______ members of the Anglo-Indian community to the House of the People, if in his opinion it is not adequately represented.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives two, the number in Article 331, under which the President could nominate up to two Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha. The 104th Amendment (2019) did not extend this provision, so it ended on 25 January 2020 and no longer operated when the exam was held in July 2022.

questions.text: ‘An Unsuitable Boy’ is the autobiography of _____.
questions.explanation: 'An Unsuitable Boy' (2017) is the autobiography of the film-maker Karan Johar.

questions.text: Minati Mishra was associated with which classical dance of India?
questions.explanation: Minati Mishra was an Odissi dancer who trained under Kelucharan Mohapatra and received the Padma Shri in 2012.

questions.text: Which of the following terms is NOT associated with Tennis?
questions.explanation: A service break, a set and a volley are all tennis terms; goals are scored in games such as football and hockey, not in tennis.

questions.text: Which water body is present to the south of India?
questions.explanation: The Indian Ocean lies to the south of India; the Arabian Sea is to the south-west and the Bay of Bengal to the south-east.

questions.text: On the basis of age, the population of a nation is generally grouped into ______ broad categories.
questions.explanation: NCERT groups a nation's population by age into three broad categories: children (generally below 15 years), working age (15-59 years) and aged (above 59 years).

questions.text: Bihu is the folk dance form of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Bihu, danced above all at Rongali (Bohag) Bihu in April, is the folk dance of Assam.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following founded Arya Samaj in 1875?
questions.explanation: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875, calling for a return to the Vedas.

questions.text: Which Indian wrestler won a silver medal in Tokyo Olympics 2020?
questions.explanation: Ravi Kumar Dahiya won silver in the men's freestyle 57 kg wrestling at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics. Virat Kohli is a cricketer, Vijender Singh a boxer, and Yogeshwar Dutt won a wrestling bronze in 2012.

questions.text: The aviation sector was inaugurated in India in the year _____ with the establishment of Tata Airlines.
questions.explanation: J R D Tata founded Tata Air Services, later Tata Airlines and then Air India, in 1932; its first flight carried mail from Karachi to Bombay on 15 October 1932.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct? I. Gautama Buddha belonged to a small gana known as the Sakya gana and was a Kshatriya. II. Gautama Buddha passed away at Kusinara.
questions.explanation: Both are true: the Buddha was born into the Sakya gana, a small republic, and was a Kshatriya, and he passed away at Kusinara (Kushinagar).

questions.text: The core of the Great Himalayas is composed of ______.
questions.explanation: The Great (Inner) Himalaya, or Himadri, the highest and most continuous range, has a core of granite.

questions.text: Which ministry launched the Krishi Udan 2.0 scheme to facilitate the movement of agricultural produce?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Civil Aviation launched Krishi UDAN 2.0 on 27 October 2021, waiving airport charges to help carry farm produce by air, especially from the north-east, hilly and tribal regions.

questions.text: Who has been reappointed as the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in October 2021?
questions.explanation: In October 2021 the government reappointed Shaktikanta Das, Governor since December 2018, for a further three years from 10 December 2021.

questions.text: Who among the following won the award for Best Music Direction in Feature Films (Songs) at the 67th National Film Awards?
questions.explanation: D. Imman (printed 'D Immam' in the options) won Best Music Direction (Songs) at the 67th National Film Awards, for the Tamil film 'Viswasam'.

questions.text: Bhagwati Committee (1973) presented a report on ____________.
questions.explanation: The Bhagwati Committee was the government's Committee on Unemployment; its 1973 report assessed unemployment and recommended rural works such as roads, housing, electrification and minor irrigation.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Richard Wellesley was the Governor – General of India from ______.
questions.explanation: Richard Wellesley (Lord Mornington) was Governor-General from 1798 to 1805, when he spread British control through the Subsidiary Alliance.

questions.text: The feature of Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Constitution of ______.
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV) were modelled on the Irish Constitution, as was the method of electing the President.

questions.text: Aqua regia is a freshly prepared mixture of concentrated hydrochloric acid and concentrated nitric acid in the ratio of ______ by volume.
questions.explanation: Aqua regia is three parts concentrated hydrochloric acid to one part concentrated nitric acid by volume; it can dissolve gold and platinum.

questions.text: Qutbuddin Aybak ruled over Delhi from ______.
questions.explanation: Qutbuddin Aibak, founder of the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty, ruled Delhi from 1206 until his death in 1210.

questions.text: Madan Mohan temple is a centrally protected monument. It is situated in which state of India?
questions.explanation: The Madan Mohan temple at Vrindavan, in Mathura district of Uttar Pradesh, is a monument of national importance protected by the Archaeological Survey of India.

questions.text: Typhoid fever is caused by ______.
questions.explanation: Typhoid fever is caused by the bacterium Salmonella Typhi, spread through contaminated food and water.

questions.text: Tooth decay starts when the pH of the mouth is lower than ______.
questions.explanation: Bacteria in the mouth make acids from sugars, and tooth enamel starts to corrode when the pH of the mouth falls below 5.5.

questions.text: ‘Maru Mahotsav’ also known as desert festival is celebrated in ______.
questions.explanation: Maru Mahotsav, the Desert Festival, is held every year at Jaisalmer in the Thar Desert of Rajasthan.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Give someone a taste of their own medicine
options: Mistreat someone in the same way they have treated others
questions.explanation: To give someone a taste of their own medicine is to treat them as badly as they have treated others.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Uttar Pradesh / accounts for about 16 per cent / of the / country population.
questions.explanation: The noun 'country' must be possessive before 'population': 'of the country's population'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We are ______ to the true legacy of humanism, and we must never forget this.
questions.explanation: 'Heirs' are those who inherit something, here the legacy of humanism. 'Hair', 'hares' and 'here' sound alike but do not fit.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. You have to understood what normal political rhetoric looks like.
questions.explanation: After 'have to' the verb takes its base form: 'You have to understand what normal political rhetoric looks like.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. Community leaders were “baffled” by the sudden arrival of the President.
questions.explanation: 'Baffled' means puzzled and confused; its opposite is 'composed', calm and in control. 'Flustered' and 'confused' are near synonyms, and 'thwarted' means prevented from doing something.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the incorrectly spelt words in the given sentence. Our webcite is no longer avaialbale to the users.
options: Our webcite is no longer available to the users.
Our websight is no longer availbale to the users.
Our website no longer available to the users.
Our website is no longer availbale to the users.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives the only option that spells both 'website' and 'available' correctly; the others keep 'webcite', 'websight' or 'availbale'. As printed, the keyed option also leaves out 'is': the full correction is 'Our website is no longer available to the users.'

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. I “has no doubts that there is a lesson” which stands to be learnt from Alice's misfortune.
options: have no doubt that there is a lesson
have had no doubts that their is a lesson
am having no doubts that there are a lesson
questions.explanation: The subject 'I' takes 'have', not 'has': 'I have no doubt that there is a lesson'. The other changes bring in new errors: 'their' for 'there', and 'there are a lesson'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. He was “on cloud nine” after passing the test.
questions.explanation: To be 'on cloud nine' is to be extremely happy.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Discrimination at the basis / of gender is not / acceptable in this office.
questions.explanation: The phrase is 'on the basis of', not 'at the basis of': 'Discrimination on the basis of gender is not acceptable in this office.'

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. Viren “examined careful” all the possibilities of data theft.
questions.explanation: The verb 'examined' needs the adverb 'carefully', not the adjective 'careful': 'Viren carefully examined all the possibilities of data theft.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The RTE Act bears many similarities to the US's No Child Left Behind Act, ______ school accountability, assessment standards and teacher training.
questions.explanation: 'Including' introduces the examples of the similarities: school accountability, assessment standards and teacher training.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I think it is quite ______ that your parents still hold hands.
questions.explanation: After 'it is quite' an adjective is needed: 'adorable', charming. 'Adorably' is an adverb, and 'adore' and 'adores' are verbs.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Slim
questions.explanation: 'Slim' means thin, as does 'skinny'. 'Flashy' means showy, 'rosy' pink or hopeful and 'moody' given to changes of mood.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. You are not supposed “to touch these” books.
questions.explanation: 'Supposed to' is followed by the base verb, and the plural 'books' takes 'these', so the sentence is already correct.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Sporadic
questions.explanation: 'Sporadic' means happening now and then, at irregular intervals: 'infrequent'. 'Regular' and 'methodical' are nearly opposite, and 'ample' means plentiful.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A game in which no one wins
questions.explanation: A game that ends with no winner is a draw.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Evident
questions.explanation: 'Evident' means plain to see; its opposite is 'hidden'. 'Obvious', 'distinct' and 'apparent' are near synonyms.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. The district “woken up to a” thick blanket of snow this morning as the winter entered its most bitter phase.
questions.explanation: 'This morning' places the action in the past, so the simple past 'woke' is needed: 'The district woke up to a thick blanket of snow'. 'Woken' is the past participle.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'beneficial'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. The community members as well as teachers “are presently into” the bus station.
questions.explanation: Being at a place is 'present at', and the subject 'the community members' stays plural ('as well as teachers' does not change it), so 'are present at the bus station'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Crosses, the village (1) ______ Vasili Andreevich lived, consisted of six houses. As soon as they had passed the blacksmith’s hut, (2) ______ last in the village, they realised that the wind was much stronger than they had thought. The road could hardly be seen. The tracks left by the sledge-runners were immediately (3) ______ by snow and the road was only (4) ______ by the fact that it was higher than the rest of the ground. There was a swirl of snow over the fields and the line where sky and earth met could not be (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Where' introduces a place: the village in which Vasili Andreevich lived.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Crosses, the village (1) ______ Vasili Andreevich lived, consisted of six houses. As soon as they had passed the blacksmith’s hut, (2) ______ last in the village, they realised that the wind was much stronger than they had thought. The road could hardly be seen. The tracks left by the sledge-runners were immediately (3) ______ by snow and the road was only (4) ______ by the fact that it was higher than the rest of the ground. There was a swirl of snow over the fields and the line where sky and earth met could not be (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The hut was a particular one, the last in the village, so it takes 'the'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Crosses, the village (1) ______ Vasili Andreevich lived, consisted of six houses. As soon as they had passed the blacksmith’s hut, (2) ______ last in the village, they realised that the wind was much stronger than they had thought. The road could hardly be seen. The tracks left by the sledge-runners were immediately (3) ______ by snow and the road was only (4) ______ by the fact that it was higher than the rest of the ground. There was a swirl of snow over the fields and the line where sky and earth met could not be (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The sledge tracks were immediately 'covered' by the snow, which is why the road could hardly be seen.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Crosses, the village (1) ______ Vasili Andreevich lived, consisted of six houses. As soon as they had passed the blacksmith’s hut, (2) ______ last in the village, they realised that the wind was much stronger than they had thought. The road could hardly be seen. There was a swirl of snow over the fields and the line where sky and earth met could not be (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The road could be 'distinguished', told apart from the fields, only because it was higher than the rest of the ground.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Crosses, the village (1) ______ Vasili Andreevich lived, consisted of six houses. The tracks left by the sledge-runners were immediately (3) ______ by snow and the road was only (4) ______ by the fact that it was higher than the rest of the ground. There was a swirl of snow over the fields and the line where sky and earth met could not be (5) ______.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Could not be' takes the past participle in the passive: 'could not be seen'.

questions.text: The scores of seven batsman B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6 and B7 are compared. The score of B1 is greater than B7 and B3. The score of B6 is neither more nor less than the score of B4 but more than B1. B5 scored less than only one batsman. The score of B7 is not the least score. How many batsman scored more than B4?
questions.explanation: B6 and B4 are equal and both beat B1, which beats B7 and B3. B5 is beaten by only one batsman, so it must be above B6 and B4 (else both would beat it), and the one above it is B2. With B3 last (B7 is not), the order is B2, B5, B6 = B4, B1, B7, B3: two batsmen scored more than B4.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. All M are Q. II. No L is Q. Conclusions: I. No M is L. II. Some L are not M.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: Every M is a Q and no L is a Q, so no M is L (I). As no L is an M, some L are not M (II) follows too.

questions.text: Select the option that will replace the question mark (?) in the given series. 45, 35, 27, 21, 17, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are −10, −8, −6, −4, so the next is −2: 17 − 2 = 15.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘Ashok is big’ is written as ‘pr 6 8’, ‘Huge people are strong’ is written as ‘lm pt 7 @’ and ‘Is big are’ is written as ‘pr pt 8’. What can be the possible code for ‘Ashok people’ in that code language?
questions.explanation: 'Is big' is common to the first and third sentences (pr, 8), so 'Ashok' is 6; 'are' is common to the second and third (pt), so 'people' is lm, 7 or @. Only '6 lm' can be the code.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word and the fourth word is related to the third word. Cricket : Bat :: Hockey : Stick :: Rugby : ?
questions.explanation: Cricket is played with a bat and hockey with a stick; rugby is played with a ball.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and fourth number is related to third number. 7 : 2401 :: 3 : 441 :: 5 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of 7 times the first: (7 × 7)² = 2401 and (3 × 7)² = 441. So (5 × 7)² = 35² = 1225.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'nu vu du' is written as 'Please ask Hamza', 'hu du ru' is written as 'Give water please', and 'tu vu ru' is written as 'Give Hamza Book'. What is the code for the word 'Book' in that language?
questions.explanation: 'Please' is common to the first two sentences (du), 'Hamza' to the first and third (vu) and 'Give' to the last two (ru), so 'Book' is tu.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. RBS : OXN :: OXA : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move back 3, 4 and 5: R → O, B → X, S → N. So O → L, X → T, A → V: LTV.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers in the given set. (131, 142, 153)
questions.explanation: Each number is 11 more than the one before: 131, 142, 153. Likewise 119, 130, 141.

questions.text: After interchanging the given two signs, what will be the value of the given expression? ÷ and ×; 5 + 10 ÷ 8 × 2 – 20
questions.explanation: After interchanging ÷ and ×: 5 + 10 × 8 ÷ 2 − 20 = 5 + 40 − 20 = 25.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. ACL, DFO, GIR, JLU, MOX, ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward: A, D, G, J, M, P; C, F, I, L, O, R; L, O, R, U, X, A (wrapping round after Z). The next cluster is PRA.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'ADULT' is coded as '53' and 'LACK' is coded as '23'. How will 'HEAVEN' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet minus the number of letters: ADULT = 1 + 4 + 21 + 12 + 20 − 5 = 53 and LACK = 12 + 1 + 3 + 11 − 4 = 23. So HEAVEN = 8 + 5 + 1 + 22 + 5 + 14 − 6 = 49.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All scales are pencils. Some pencils are erasers. Conclusions: I: Some scales are erasers. II: Some pencils are scales.
questions.explanation: Every scale is a pencil, so some pencils are scales (II). The pencils that are erasers need not include any scale, so I does not follow.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 81 + 31 ÷ 9 – 7 = 33

Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. SIDE22 : UKFG19 :: SETS15 : UGVU12 :: MINE11 : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward and the number falls by 3: SIDE22 → UKFG19 and SETS15 → UGVU12. So MINE11 → OKPG8.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘sand is hot’ is written as ‘6 8 9’ and ‘grains are white sand’ is written as ‘4 3 9 2’. What is the code for ‘hot’ in that code language?
questions.explanation: 'Sand' is common to both sentences, so it is 9; 'is' and 'hot' share 6 and 8, so 'hot' is 6 or 8.

questions.text: Seven girls V, K, L, P, A, C and N are sitting in a row facing the South (not necessarily in the same order). L is to the immediate left of P. K is at one of the ends. A is the immediate neighbour of K. Only N is between A and C. Only P is between L and C. Which of the following statements is/are correct? I. P is third to the left of A. II. N is to the immediate right of C.
questions.explanation: Taking the girls' own left and right: L, P and C sit together in that order, N is the only one between C and A (A cannot be on P's side), and K, at an end, sits next to A. From their left: V, L, P, C, N, A, K. P is third to the left of A and N is immediately to the right of C, so both are correct.

questions.text: Select the number from the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 482, 239, 158, 131, 122, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are −243, −81, −27, −9, each a third of the one before, so the next is −3: 122 − 3 = 119.

questions.text: Six friends Amit, Bhuvan, Chand, David, Emily and Fedrick are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). Amit sits third to the left of David. David sits to the immediate right of Bhuvan. Bhuvan sits second to the left of Emily. Chand sits second to the right of Fedrick. Who sits second to the right of Amit?
questions.explanation: Going round to the right: Bhuvan, David, Emily, Fedrick, Amit, Chand. Amit sits opposite David (third to his left), and Chand, second to the right of Fedrick, takes the last seat. Second to the right of Amit is Bhuvan.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of Phylum Mammalia of Animal Kingdom?
questions.explanation: A rat is a mammal: it has hair and feeds its young on milk. The hen and pigeon are birds and the crocodile a reptile. (Mammalia is strictly a class of the phylum Chordata, not a phylum.)

questions.text: As per the 2011 Census, arrange the following languages in descending order of Speakers strength: Marathi, Hindi, Maithili.
questions.explanation: In the 2011 Census Hindi had about 52.8 crore speakers (43.6% of the population), Marathi about 8.3 crore (6.9%) and Maithili about 1.4 crore (1.1%).

questions.text: Which Indian actress was also one of the dancer to be honoured with the 'Padma Shri' award in 1968?
questions.explanation: Vyjayanthimala, the Bharatanatyam dancer and Hindi and Tamil film actress, received the Padma Shri in 1968.

questions.text: In the northern and north-western part of India, ______ is the main food crop.
questions.explanation: NCERT calls wheat, the second most important cereal crop, the main food crop of the north and north-western part of the country.

questions.text: Lavani is the dance form of which state?
questions.explanation: Lavani is a song-and-dance form of Maharashtra, performed to the beat of the dholki.

questions.text: Which team won the Indian Super League 2021-22?
questions.explanation: Hyderabad FC won the 2021-22 Indian Super League, beating Kerala Blasters on penalties in the final in March 2022.

questions.text: The terminology ‘direct free kick’ is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: In football a direct free kick, given for fouls such as tripping or handling the ball, can be scored straight from the kick. Hockey has free hits rather than free kicks.

questions.text: Who among the following was conferred the Dadasaheb Phalke Award at the 67th National Film Awards ceremony?
questions.explanation: Rajinikanth received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2019 at the 67th National Film Awards ceremony in New Delhi in October 2021.

questions.text: In which of the following states of India is Gangaur festival celebrated?
questions.explanation: Gangaur, held in honour of the goddess Gauri (Parvati), is a major festival of Rajasthan, celebrated mainly by women.

questions.text: In November 2021, ‘the Duare Ration’ scheme was launched in ______.
questions.explanation: West Bengal's Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee launched 'Duare Ration' (ration at the doorstep), which delivers ration to people's homes, on 16 November 2021.

questions.text: The Mahabodhi Temple is an ancient Buddhist temple. It is situated in which state of India?
questions.explanation: The Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya, Bihar, stands where the Buddha is believed to have attained enlightenment; it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.text: Genghis Khan died in which year?
questions.explanation: Genghis Khan, founder of the Mongol Empire, died in August 1227.

questions.text: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘Selection Day’?
questions.explanation: 'Selection Day' (2016), a novel about two brothers groomed to become cricketers in Mumbai, is by Aravind Adiga, the author of 'The White Tiger'.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following freedom fighters was the first woman to become the Governor of Uttar Pradesh State?
questions.explanation: Sarojini Naidu became Governor of the United Provinces (now Uttar Pradesh) in August 1947, the first woman governor of an Indian state, and held the post until her death in March 1949.

questions.text: The rhythmic rise and fall of ocean water twice in a day is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A tide is the regular rise and fall of the sea, caused mainly by the Moon's pull, about twice a day.

questions.text: What is the draft of legislative proposal that needs to be passed in both houses of Parliament of India to become an Act called?
questions.explanation: A legislative proposal is a Bill; once both Houses pass it and the President assents, it becomes an Act.

questions.text: ______ is the market value of all final goods and services produced within a domestic territory of a country measured in a year.
questions.explanation: GDP is the market value of all final goods and services produced within a country's domestic territory in a year. GNP adds net factor income from abroad, and NNP subtracts depreciation from GNP.

questions.text: Which of the following is a biotic component of ecology?
questions.explanation: Fungi are living organisms (decomposers), so they are a biotic component; sunlight and humidity are abiotic factors.

questions.text: With which of the following musical instruments was Ustad Alla Rakha primarily associated?
questions.explanation: Ustad Alla Rakha, father of Zakir Hussain, was a celebrated tabla player who often accompanied Ravi Shankar.

questions.text: What is Brahmaputra River called in Arunachal Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra is the Tsangpo in Tibet; it enters India in Arunachal Pradesh, where it is called the Dihang (or Siang), and becomes the Brahmaputra in Assam after the Dibang and Lohit join it.

questions.text: Which feature of the Indian Constitution refers to the existence of more than one level of government in the country?
questions.explanation: Federalism means power is shared between more than one level of government: in India, the Union, the states and local governments.

questions.text: Which of the following rulers did NOT belong to Maurya dynasty?
questions.explanation: Bimbisara was a ruler of Magadha of the Haryanka dynasty, before the Mauryas. Chandragupta founded the Maurya dynasty, and Bindusara and Ashoka followed him.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following led of the famous Indigo Revolt in Bengal?
options: Bishnu Charan Biswas and Digambar Biswas
questions.explanation: The Indigo Revolt of 1859-60 began in Nadia district of Bengal, where Bishnu Charan Biswas and Digambar Biswas led the cultivators against the European planters who forced them to grow indigo.

questions.text: With respect to occupation, secondary activities include _______.
questions.explanation: Secondary activities process raw materials into goods or build things, as in manufacturing and construction. Mining and fishing are primary activities and administration a tertiary one.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of metalloid?
questions.explanation: Boron is a metalloid, with properties between those of metals and non-metals. Aluminium, gallium and indium, below it in group 13, are metals.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Discern' is spelt correctly. The others should be 'harass', 'repercussions' and 'appealing'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. I seen a beautiful dress in the market yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' calls for the simple past: 'I saw a beautiful dress'. 'Seen' is a past participle and cannot stand without 'have'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Inception
questions.explanation: 'Inception' is the beginning of something, so its opposite is 'termination', the end. 'Launch' and 'beginning' mean much the same as 'inception'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. It is a “benign” cyst and requires no treatment.
questions.explanation: 'Benign' means gentle or harmless (a benign cyst is not cancerous), so of the options its opposite is 'violent'. 'Mellow' and 'gracious' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Unique
questions.explanation: 'Unique' means being the only one of its kind, or belonging to one alone: what is unique to a place is exclusive to it. 'Typical' and 'regular' are nearly its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Barking up the wrong tree
options: Pursue a course of action that will most likely be futile
questions.explanation: To be 'barking up the wrong tree' is to follow a mistaken idea or course of action, one that will get nowhere.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. They left the car by “the aside of the road and venture toward” the forest.
options: the side of the road and ventured into
the alongside of the road and ventured to
an aside of road and ventured to
questions.explanation: A car is left 'by the side of the road' ('aside' is an adverb, not a noun), and 'left' needs the past 'ventured' to match: 'ventured into the forest'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. His grandfather finds a tiny tiger cub in the forest and “brought his home.”
questions.explanation: The second verb must match 'finds' in tense, so 'brings', and the pronoun for the cub is 'it': 'and brings it home'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Success in any field depends ______ hard work and determination.
questions.explanation: 'Depend' takes 'on': success depends on hard work and determination.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Add fuel to the fire
questions.explanation: To 'add fuel to the fire' is to make an already bad situation worse.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Several pictures and videos have been circulating ______ social media featuring her.
questions.explanation: Posts and videos circulate 'on' social media, as they appear on a platform.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Mylar balloons cause power outages when they come of contact with power lines.
questions.explanation: The phrase is 'come into contact with': 'when they come into contact with power lines'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Only 30 per cent worked in companies where paternity leave was an ______.
questions.explanation: An 'entitlement' is something one has a right to: in those companies paternity leave was the employees' right.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. A nine-judge bench of the Supreme Court unanimously held that Indians have a/an ______ protected fundamental right to privacy.
questions.explanation: A fundamental right is guaranteed by the Constitution, so it is 'constitutionally' protected. 'Permeably', 'indigenously' and 'unethically' make no sense here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Enthrall
questions.explanation: To 'enthrall' is to hold someone's attention completely: to 'captivate'. 'Repulse' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who is outspoken and outgoing
questions.explanation: An extrovert is an outgoing, sociable person who speaks freely. 'Flamboyant' means showy, and a psychic claims powers beyond the senses.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Its always a / beautiful day / in my neighbourhood.
questions.explanation: 'Its' is the possessive; the short form of 'it is' is 'it's': 'It's always a beautiful day'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. The toast “will being ready” in about 15 minutes.
questions.explanation: The modal 'will' is followed by the bare infinitive: 'The toast will be ready in about 15 minutes.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Exclusion
questions.explanation: 'Exclusion' is keeping someone out; its opposite is 'admittance', letting someone in.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Apart from other pollutions, noise pollution – also known as environmental noise or sound pollution – is (1) ______ issue related to human beings and the environment. It may have an (2) ______ on general health. Compressors, generators and pipe handling are the (3) ______ of noise. Long-term (4) ______ to noise can (5) ______ a variety of health hazards.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Apart from other pollutions', noise pollution is 'another' issue; 'another' goes with a singular noun such as 'issue'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Apart from other pollutions, noise pollution – also known as environmental noise or sound pollution – is (1) ______ issue related to human beings and the environment. It may have an (2) ______ on general health. Compressors, generators and pipe handling are the (3) ______ of noise. Long-term (4) ______ to noise can (5) ______ a variety of health hazards.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Noise may have an 'impact', an effect, on general health; 'an issue on' or 'an interest on' health makes no sense.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Apart from other pollutions, noise pollution – also known as environmental noise or sound pollution – is (1) ______ issue related to human beings and the environment. It may have an (2) ______ on general health. Compressors, generators and pipe handling are the (3) ______ of noise. Long-term (4) ______ to noise can (5) ______ a variety of health hazards.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Compressors, generators and pipe handling are where the noise comes from: its 'sources'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Apart from other pollutions, noise pollution – also known as environmental noise or sound pollution – is (1) ______ issue related to human beings and the environment. It may have an (2) ______ on general health. Compressors, generators and pipe handling are the (3) ______ of noise. Long-term (4) ______ to noise can (5) ______ a variety of health hazards.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Exposure to noise' is being subjected to it; long-term exposure is what harms health.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Apart from other pollutions, noise pollution – also known as environmental noise or sound pollution – is (1) ______ issue related to human beings and the environment. It may have an (2) ______ on general health. Compressors, generators and pipe handling are the (3) ______ of noise. Long-term (4) ______ to noise can (5) ______ a variety of health hazards.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Long-term exposure can 'cause', that is bring about, a variety of health hazards.

questions.text: Which two numbers (not digits) should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? (4 × 12 + 15) ÷ 8 – 9 = 0
Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 21, 22, 44, 47, 188, ?
Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. KNA : PMZ :: RSV : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on): K → P, N → M, A → Z. So R → I, S → H, V → E: IHE.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'ROM' is coded as '43', and 'ABK' is coded as '11'. How will 'PNB' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet minus 3: ROM = 18 + 15 + 13 = 46 and 46 − 3 = 43; ABK = 1 + 2 + 11 = 14 and 14 − 3 = 11. PNB = 16 + 14 + 2 = 32, and 32 − 3 = 29.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers in the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (18, 36, 72); (16, 32, 64)
questions.explanation: In each set every number is double the one before: 18, 36, 72 and 16, 32, 64. Likewise 24, 48, 96. In the others 32 × 3 = 96, 28 × 2 = 56 and 76 × 2 = 152 break the pattern.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. ABC6 : DEF15 :: GHI24 : JKL33 :: PQR51 : ?
questions.explanation: Each cluster is followed by the next three letters, and the number is the sum of the letters' places: DEF = 4 + 5 + 6 = 15 and JKL = 10 + 11 + 12 = 33. After PQR come STU, with 19 + 20 + 21 = 60: STU60.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'MK - SP' is coded as '–605', and 'AB - TF' is coded as '–194'. How will 'GM - HK' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each pair of letters is written as their places in the alphabet side by side, and the second number is subtracted from the first: MK - SP → 1311 − 1916 = −605 and AB - TF → 12 − 206 = −194. So GM - HK → 713 − 811 = −98.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the sixth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and the third number is related to the fourth number. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) 11 : 169 :: 13 : 225 :: ? : 361
questions.explanation: Each first number plus 2, squared, gives the second: (11 + 2)² = 169 and (13 + 2)² = 225. As 361 = 19², the missing number is 19 − 2 = 17.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'COVER' is coded as '63', 'BASIS' is coded as '50', and 'WISH' is coded as '59'. How will 'GREECE' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded as the sum of its letters' places in the alphabet: COVER = 3 + 15 + 22 + 5 + 18 = 63, BASIS = 50 and WISH = 59. GREECE = 7 + 18 + 5 + 5 + 3 + 5 = 43.

questions.text: Identify the number that does NOT belong to the following series. 16, 34, 52, 72, 88, 106
questions.explanation: The terms should rise by 18: 16, 34, 52, 70, 88, 106. 72 does not fit; it should be 70.

questions.text: Seven girls G1, G2, G3, G4, G5, G6 and G7 are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (not necessarily in the same order). G6 is second to the left of G1. G7 is second to the left of G6. G5 is third to the right of G2. G5 is not the immediate neighbour of G6. G4 is third to the right of G3. Who is second to the left of G7?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left is the next seat clockwise. Numbering the seats clockwise from G1 (seat 1), G6 is in seat 3 and G7 in seat 5; G5, three seats anticlockwise of G2, must be in seat 6 with G2 in seat 2 (the only other fit, G2 in seat 7, puts G5 in seat 4 beside G6), and G4, three seats anticlockwise of G3, is in seat 4 with G3 in seat 7. Second to the left of G7 is seat 7: G3.

questions.text: Among seven friends Akash, Biraj, Chandan, Dharmesh, Imran, Faisal and Gautam, Biraj is taller than only Dharmesh. Only one person is taller than Faisal. The height of exactly two friends lies in between that of Akash and Chandan. Imran is taller than Gautam. Who is the third tallest person in the group?
questions.explanation: Biraj is taller than only Dharmesh, so they are sixth and seventh, and Faisal is second. Akash and Chandan, with exactly two between them, can only be first and fourth, leaving third and fifth for Imran and Gautam; Imran is the taller, so he is third.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. YZ, BCD, FGHI, ?, QRSTUV
questions.explanation: Each cluster has one letter more than the last, and one letter is skipped between clusters: YZ, (A) BCD, (E) FGHI, (J) KLMNO, (P) QRSTUV.

questions.text: M, N, O, P and Q are standing in a queue to place their order in a restaurant. Only P is standing between M and Q. O is ahead of only N. Who is standing second in the line if there is no other person in the queue?
questions.explanation: O is ahead of only N, so N is fifth and O fourth. M, P and Q take the first three places with P between M and Q, so P is second.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘×’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and also ‘+’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 40 + 10 − 5 × 4 ÷ 5 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 40 ÷ 10 × 5 − 4 + 5 = 4 × 5 − 4 + 5 = 20 − 4 + 5 = 21.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. Some cars are bikes. II. No truck is a car. Conclusions: I. All trucks are bikes. II. All bikes are cars. III. All cars are trucks.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: No truck is a car, so no car is a truck and III is false. Nothing links trucks to bikes, and only some bikes are known to be cars, so neither I nor II follows.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. MJO : NQQ :: TRA : ?
