questions.explanation: The first two letters become their opposites in the alphabet (M → N, J → Q) and the third moves two places on (O → Q). So T → G, R → I and A → C: GIC.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'ACCIDENT' is written as 'JDDBUOFE', 'ABSOLUTE' is written as 'PTCBFUVM', and 'ACCURATE' is written as 'VDDBFUBS'. How will 'SENTENCE' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is split into two halves of four letters; each letter moves one place on and each half is reversed: ACCI → BDDJ → JDDB and DENT → EFOU → UOFE. So SENT → TFOU → UOFT and ENCE → FODF → FDOF: UOFTFDOF.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. No X is G. II. All B are X. Conclusions: I. Some G are B. II. All X are B.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: All B are X and no X is G, so no B is G: I is false. Not every X need be a B, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: The Tamil Nadu coast gets a large portion of its rain during ______.
questions.explanation: The Tamil Nadu coast gets much of its rain in October and November, from the retreating (north-east) monsoon, whose winds pick up moisture over the Bay of Bengal.

questions.text: The government budget gives a statement of the ______.
options: receipts and expenditure of the government
questions.explanation: The budget, the Annual Financial Statement under Article 112, sets out the government's estimated receipts and expenditure for the year.

questions.text: ______ is known as the energy currency of the cell.
questions.explanation: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) stores the energy released in respiration and supplies it to the cell's activities, hence 'energy currency'.

questions.text: Earthworm belongs to which group of animal kingdom?
questions.explanation: The earthworm is a segmented worm of the phylum Annelida, as is the leech. Snails are molluscs, insects arthropods and roundworms nematodes.

questions.text: Who among the following has received the prestigious Bharat Ratna Dr Ambedkar Award 2021?
questions.explanation: Harshaali Malhotra, who played Munni in 'Bajrangi Bhaijaan' (2015) as a child, was presented the Bharat Ratna Dr Ambedkar Award by Maharashtra's Governor, Bhagat Singh Koshyari, at Raj Bhavan, Mumbai, in January 2022.

questions.text: An alliance formed by political parties after elections when no party has been able to get adequate seats to form a clear majority is called ______.
questions.explanation: A coalition is an alliance of parties that together command a majority. Prorogation ends a session of the legislature, and allegiance is loyalty.

questions.text: According to the Indian Constitution, all are fundamental rights, EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: The 44th Amendment (1978) removed the right to property from the fundamental rights; it is now a constitutional right under Article 300A. The rights to equality, to freedom and against exploitation remain fundamental rights.

questions.text: ______ in Gujarat was the emporium of western trade during the Mughal Period.
questions.explanation: In the Mughal period Surat was the chief port of western trade, the gateway for trade with West Asia through the Persian Gulf, and the port from which pilgrim ships sailed for Mecca.

questions.text: Manish Pandey played for which team in IPL 2022?
questions.explanation: Lucknow Super Giants, one of the two new teams in IPL 2022, bought Manish Pandey at the February 2022 auction; he had played for Sunrisers Hyderabad before.

questions.text: In November 2021, who launched Tejasvini and Hausala schemes in Jammu?
questions.explanation: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman launched both at a credit outreach programme at the University of Jammu on 23 November 2021: Tejasvini gives young women up to ₹5 lakh to set up their own ventures, and Hausala supports existing women entrepreneurs.

questions.text: Nati is a folk dance of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Nati, danced in a line or circle at fairs and festivals in districts such as Kullu, is the best-known folk dance of Himachal Pradesh.

questions.text: According to the Census of India 2011, among all the states/UTs Kerala occupied the ______ position in terms of literacy.
questions.explanation: Census 2011 put Kerala's literacy rate at about 94%, the highest of all the states and Union Territories, with Lakshadweep second.

questions.text: Megasthenes, an ambassador, was sent to the court of ______ by the Greek ruler of West Asia, Seleucus Nicator.
questions.explanation: Seleucus Nicator sent Megasthenes as his envoy to Chandragupta Maurya's court at Pataliputra; his account of India is known as the 'Indica'.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who wrote the book ‘Gulamgiri’?
questions.explanation: 'Gulamgiri' (Slavery), published in 1873, is Jyotirao Phule's attack on caste oppression; the same year he founded the Satyashodhak Samaj.

questions.text: Mrinalini Sarabhai is known for which of the following classical dance forms?
questions.explanation: Mrinalini Sarabhai trained in Bharatanatyam and Kathakali, and in 1949 founded the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts in Ahmedabad.

questions.text: In India, which organisation is responsible for collecting data related to unemployment?
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India
questions.explanation: The National Sample Survey Organisation ran India's employment and unemployment surveys, including the Periodic Labour Force Survey from 2017; in 2019 it became part of the National Statistical Office.

questions.text: What is the atomic number of hydrogen in the Mendeleev's periodic table?
questions.explanation: Mendeleev ordered the elements by atomic mass (atomic numbers came later), but hydrogen, the lightest, stood first in his table, and its atomic number is 1: one proton in its nucleus.

questions.text: Who among the following Mughal rulers built the Agra Fort?
questions.explanation: Akbar built the red sandstone Agra Fort from 1565; Shah Jahan later added white-marble buildings inside it.

questions.text: Which of the following festivals is associated with Arunachal Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Solung is the agricultural festival of the Adi people of Arunachal Pradesh. Wangala is a Garo festival of Meghalaya, Pongal is celebrated in Tamil Nadu, and Ugadi is the new year in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka.

questions.text: Which of the following football teams won the Indian Super League 2021-2022?
questions.explanation: Hyderabad FC won the 2021-22 Indian Super League, beating Kerala Blasters on penalties in the final in Goa in March 2022.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian rivers is also referred to as ‘Dakshin Ganga’?
questions.explanation: The Godavari, the longest river of peninsular India, is called the Dakshin Ganga (Ganga of the south) for its length and the area it drains.

questions.text: According to their capacity, roads are classified into how many classes in India?
questions.explanation: NCERT classifies India's roads by capacity into six classes: the Golden Quadrilateral super highways, national highways, state highways, district roads, other (rural) roads and border roads.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book ‘A Suitable Boy’?
questions.explanation: 'A Suitable Boy' (1993), a long novel set in newly independent India, is by Vikram Seth.

questions.text: With which musical instrument is Hariprasad Chaurasia associated?
questions.explanation: Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is a master of the bansuri, the bamboo flute.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi arrive in India from South Africa?
questions.explanation: Gandhi returned from South Africa to Bombay on 9 January 1915, the day now marked as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A gut feeling
questions.explanation: A 'gut feeling' is an instinctive sense that something is so, without conscious reasoning.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. New fashion trends / come onto the / scene periodically.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: the plural 'trends' takes 'come', and to 'come onto the scene' is to appear or arrive.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The weather patterns ______ that we will have a winter season, perhaps a good one.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'the weather patterns' needs a plural active verb: 'suggest'. 'Suggests' and 'has suggested' are singular, and the passive 'have been suggested' does not fit patterns that do the suggesting.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Most of the families in / my research rely at phone calls / for almost all of their communication.
options: for almost all of their communication
my research rely at phone calls
questions.explanation: One relies 'on' something, not 'at' it: 'Most of the families in my research rely on phone calls'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A place for breeding and keeping birds
questions.explanation: An aviary is a large enclosure for keeping birds. A kennel houses dogs, an apiary is where bees are kept and a den is a wild animal's lair.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. My son “has been sleeping” for twelve hours at a stretch.
questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous with 'for twelve hours' describes sleep that began in the past and is still going on, and the singular 'my son' takes 'has': the underlined part is correct.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Smoking is ______ in my office building.
questions.explanation: 'Banned' means officially forbidden. 'Bend', 'band' and 'bated' look or sound alike but do not fit the sense.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Immersive' is spelt correctly. The others should be 'experiences', 'institutionalised' and 'tremendous'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. Our company wants to “collaborate” with your team.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'collude', the only option that means working together with others, though it usually suggests a secret or dishonest purpose that 'collaborate' here does not. 'Repel', 'defy' and 'captivate' are unrelated.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The action of using someone or something as a model
questions.explanation: Imitation is the act of copying someone or something, taking it as a model.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'vehicle'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Go the extra mile
options: Going in search of something better
Going above and beyond whatever is required for the task at hand
questions.explanation: To 'go the extra mile' is to make more effort than is expected or required.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. My friend Jatin usually wears a spectacle.
questions.explanation: Glasses for the eyes are 'spectacles', always plural, so 'a spectacle' is wrong: 'usually wears spectacles'. 'A spectacle' is an impressive sight or show.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Polished
questions.explanation: 'Polished' in the sense of refined and elegant is close to 'cultured'. 'Crude' is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required.’ The main road was entirely blocked till the time the cranes “move the damage” vehicles.
questions.explanation: The past 'was blocked' needs the past 'moved' in the 'till' clause, and the vehicles are 'damaged', a past participle used as an adjective: 'till the time the cranes moved the damaged vehicles'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Scold
questions.explanation: To scold is to criticise someone angrily; the opposite is to 'praise'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Irrational
questions.explanation: 'Irrational' means not based on reason; its opposite is 'reasonable'. 'Illogical' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Divergence
questions.explanation: Divergence is a moving apart; 'confluence' is a coming together. 'Separation' and 'departure' are close to divergence itself.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Doctor Bayley “tripped under some large roots and cuts” her head on a rock.
options: tripped over some large roots and cut
tripped over and above some large roots and cut
tripped upon some larger roots and cuts
questions.explanation: One trips 'over' an obstacle, and the second verb must be past tense like 'tripped': 'tripped over some large roots and cut her head on a rock'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’.I “didn't saw any” point in spending money on new clothes.
questions.explanation: 'Did' (here 'didn't') is followed by the base form of the verb: 'I didn't see any point in spending money on new clothes.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Regular check-ups are (1)___ for a car’s top-notch performance, but did you know that there is a direct link (2)___ your car health and its emissions? A well-maintained car engine is (3)___ efficient and burns less gas, (4)___ reducing airborne emissions. Secondly, tyre pressure (5)___ always match the manufacturer-recommended Pounds Per Square Inch (PSI) rating.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Regular check-ups are 'vital', that is essential, for a car's top-notch performance; 'trivial' and 'nominal' mean unimportant.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Regular check-ups are (1)___ for a car’s top-notch performance, but did you know that there is a direct link (2)___ your car health and its emissions? A well-maintained car engine is (3)___ efficient and burns less gas, (4)___ reducing airborne emissions. Secondly, tyre pressure (5)___ always match the manufacturer-recommended Pounds Per Square Inch (PSI) rating.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: A link joins two things: a link 'between' your car's health and its emissions.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Regular check-ups are (1)___ for a car’s top-notch performance, but did you know that there is a direct link (2)___ your car health and its emissions? A well-maintained car engine is (3)___ efficient and burns less gas, (4)___ reducing airborne emissions. Secondly, tyre pressure (5)___ always match the manufacturer-recommended Pounds Per Square Inch (PSI) rating.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: A well-maintained engine is 'more efficient', a comparison that matches 'burns less gas'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Regular check-ups are (1)___ for a car’s top-notch performance, but did you know that there is a direct link (2)___ your car health and its emissions? A well-maintained car engine is (3)___ efficient and burns less gas, (4)___ reducing airborne emissions. Secondly, tyre pressure (5)___ always match the manufacturer-recommended Pounds Per Square Inch (PSI) rating.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Thereby' means 'by that means': burning less gas thereby reduces airborne emissions.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Regular check-ups are (1)___ for a car’s top-notch performance, but did you know that there is a direct link (2)___ your car health and its emissions? A well-maintained car engine is (3)___ efficient and burns less gas, (4)___ reducing airborne emissions. Secondly, tyre pressure (5)___ always match the manufacturer-recommended Pounds Per Square Inch (PSI) rating.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Must' states a requirement: tyre pressure must always match the recommended rating. 'Have to' would need 'has to' with the singular 'tyre pressure'.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 6, 24, 60, 120, 210, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is the product of three consecutive numbers: 1 × 2 × 3 = 6, 2 × 3 × 4 = 24, 3 × 4 × 5 = 60, 4 × 5 × 6 = 120 and 5 × 6 × 7 = 210, so the next is 6 × 7 × 8 = 336.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. WXYZ, YZWX, ABUV, CDST, ?
questions.explanation: The first two letters move 2 places forward (WX, YZ, AB, CD, EF) and the last two move 2 places back (YZ, WX, UV, ST, QR): EFQR.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'BRAVE' is written as '43' and 'BOTH' is written as '41'. How will 'ABACUS' be written in that code language?
questions.explanation: The code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet minus the number of letters: BRAVE = 2 + 18 + 1 + 22 + 5 = 48 and 48 − 5 = 43; BOTH = 2 + 15 + 20 + 8 = 45 and 45 − 4 = 41. ABACUS = 1 + 2 + 1 + 3 + 21 + 19 = 47, and 47 − 6 = 41.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 264, 288, 312, ?, 360, 384
questions.explanation: Each term is 24 more than the one before: 312 + 24 = 336, and 336 + 24 = 360.

questions.text: Nine people, A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, and I, are sitting in a row facing south. E sits in the middle. Three people sit between E and G. Six people sit between G and B. Three people sit between B and A. F sits second to the right of A. I sits fourth to the left of F. I and E are not immediate neighbours. B and C are not neighbours. H sits to the right of D. Who is sitting fourth to the right of G?
questions.explanation: Number the seats 1 to 9 from left to right as the people face. E is in seat 5 and G at an end. G in seat 9 would put B in 2, A in 6, F in 8 and I in 4, next to E, so G is in seat 1, B in 8, A in 4, F in 6 and I in 2. C cannot sit next to B, so C is in 3, and D and H take 7 and 9 with H to D's right: G I C A E F D B H. Fourth to the right of G is E.

questions.text: Which two numbers (NOT digits) should be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 26 ÷ 2 + 13 × 6 − 4 = 10

Select the option that is related to the fifth word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word and the fourth word is related to the third word. Cup : Coffee :: Glass : Juice :: Bowl : ?
questions.explanation: Each pair is a vessel and what is usually served in it: coffee in a cup, juice in a glass and soup in a bowl.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All cookies are sweet. Some sweets are snacks. Conclusions: I. All sweets are cookies. II. All cookies are snacks.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: Being sweet does not make something a cookie, so I does not follow, and the sweets that are snacks need not include any cookie, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers in the following sets. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (16, 18, 20); (17, 19, 21)
questions.explanation: Each set is three numbers rising by 2: 16, 18, 20 and 17, 19, 21. Only 64, 66, 68 does the same.

questions.text: Select the option in which the pair of letter-clusters share the same relationship as that shared by the given letter-clusters. RN : UQ
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward: R → U and N → Q. Likewise K → N and R → U.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. No B is A. II. No C is B. Conclusions: I. No C is A. II. No A is B. III. Some B are not C.
options: Both conclusions I and II follows
Both conclusions II and III follows
questions.explanation: 'No B is A' converts to 'no A is B', so II follows. 'No C is B' means no B is C, so some B are not C, and III follows. Nothing links C with A, so I does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘HELP’ is coded as ‘851216’ and ‘GRAN’ is coded as ‘718114’. How will ‘FOMS’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as its place in the alphabet: HELP → 8 5 12 16 and GRAN → 7 18 1 14. So FOMS → 6 15 13 19: 6151319.

questions.text: S, T, U, V and W are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). S is the immediate neighbour of T and W. U is to the immediate right of T. V is the immediate neighbour of U and W. Who is sitting to the immediate left of S?
questions.explanation: S sits between T and W, and V between W and U, so the order round the table is T, S, W, V, U. U is on T's immediate right, so S, T's other neighbour, is on T's left; then T is on S's right and W, S's other neighbour, is to the immediate left of S.

questions.text: The height of five students, Aakriti, Kiran, Lisa, Manisha and Rekha, are compared. The height of Kiran is more than only two students. The height of Manisha is immediately greater than Rekha, and Rekha is immediately greater than Kiran. How many students are taller than Rekha?
questions.explanation: Kiran is taller than exactly two students, so Kiran is third tallest. Rekha is immediately taller than Kiran (second) and Manisha immediately taller than Rekha (first), so only Manisha is taller than Rekha.

questions.text: In a certain code language, if blue is called pink, pink is called yellow, yellow is called orange, orange is called red, and red is called violet, then what is the colour of sunflower?
questions.explanation: A sunflower is yellow, and in this code yellow is called orange.

questions.text: Select the option in which the pair of letter-clusters share the same relationship as that shared by the given letter-clusters. TAP : JUN
questions.explanation: TAP written backwards is PAT, and moving each letter 6 places back (wrapping round after A) gives JUN: P → J, A → U, T → N. Likewise FED backwards is DEF, and D → X, E → Y, F → Z: XYZ.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (3, 5, 30); (6, 5, 60)
questions.explanation: The third number is twice the product of the first two: 3 × 5 × 2 = 30 and 6 × 5 × 2 = 60. Likewise 6 × 7 × 2 = 84.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘ × ‘ are interchanged and also ‘–’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 1 × 14 + 30 – 20 ÷ 10 = ?
If &@$! = 8213 and &%# = 860, then what is %#&$ ?
Which famous Rashtrakuta king built the rock-cut temple of Kailash at Ellora?
questions.explanation: The rock-cut Kailasa (Kailash) temple, Cave 16 at Ellora, was built under the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I in the 8th century. Govinda III was a later Rashtrakuta ruler; Bhoja and Jai Chand belonged to other dynasties.

questions.text: Commercial banks keep their deposits with RBI. These deposits are called ______.
questions.explanation: Commercial banks must keep a set share of their deposits with the Reserve Bank of India as reserves; that share is the cash reserve ratio (CRR).

questions.text: Pandit Rajendra Gangani is associated with which classical dance of India?
questions.explanation: Pandit Rajendra Gangani is a Kathak dancer and guru of the Jaipur gharana.

questions.text: With which musical instrument was Ustad Bismillah Khan associated?
questions.explanation: Ustad Bismillah Khan, awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2001, made the shehnai a concert instrument.

questions.text: The popular style of temple architecture in northern India is called ________.
questions.explanation: Nagara is the north Indian temple style, with a curvilinear tower (shikhara) over the sanctum; Dravida is the southern style. The shikhara is a part of the temple, and panchayatana a plan with four subsidiary shrines round the main one.

questions.text: Who took oath as the 28th Chief Minister of Punjab in March 2022?
questions.explanation: Bhagwant Mann of the Aam Aadmi Party was sworn in as Chief Minister of Punjab on 16 March 2022 at Khatkar Kalan, Bhagat Singh's ancestral village. Reports of the oath called him Punjab's 28th Chief Minister; lists that count each person only once make him the 17th.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: Electric charge is a scalar quantity.
Electric charge is a vector quantity.
questions.explanation: Electric charge has magnitude but no direction, so it is a scalar, and the statement that it is a vector is incorrect. Protons carry positive charge and electrons negative.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year did the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II appoint the East India Company as the Diwan of Bengal?
questions.explanation: By the Treaty of Allahabad in August 1765, Shah Alam II granted the East India Company the diwani, the right to collect the revenue, of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.

questions.text: The Sattriya dance has developed from the monasteries of:
questions.explanation: Sattriya, introduced by the Vaishnava saint Srimanta Sankardev, grew up in the sattras, the Vaishnava monasteries of Assam.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a reason for slowing down of the Non-cooperation Movement?
options: Due to the absence of alternative Indian institution, boycott of British institutions posed a problem.
Leaders of the movement shifted their focus towards domestic work thus created a void.
Many lawyers resigned but then absence of income for a longer period of time compelled them to rejoin.
Khadi cloth was often more expensive than mass-produced mill cloth and poor people could not afford to buy it.
questions.explanation: NCERT gives costlier khadi, the slow growth of Indian institutions to replace the boycotted British ones, and lawyers and students drifting back to courts and schools as reasons the movement slowed in the cities; leaders turning to 'domestic work' is not among them.

questions.text: Amoeba acquires its food through the process of ______.
questions.explanation: The flexible cell membrane of Amoeba engulfs food from outside the cell, a process called endocytosis (phagocytosis is its form for solid particles). Exocytosis is the reverse.

questions.text: The part of the Himalayas lying between Satluj and Kali rivers is known as _____.
questions.explanation: In NCERT's regional division, the Kumaon Himalayas lie between the Satluj and the Kali; the Punjab Himalayas, known regionally as the Kashmir and Himachal Himalayas, lie between the Indus and the Satluj.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a pair of micronutrients?
questions.explanation: Fats are a macronutrient, needed in large amounts for energy, so 'calcium and fats' is not a pair of micronutrients. Minerals such as iodine and iron are micronutrients.

questions.text: Half of India’s population lives in just five states. Which of the following is one of those states?
questions.explanation: NCERT, using the 2011 Census, notes that almost half of India's population lives in five states: Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Bihar, West Bengal and (undivided) Andhra Pradesh.

questions.text: The largest dam in India, the Hirakud Dam, is built on which of the following rivers?
questions.explanation: The Hirakud Dam, the longest dam in India, is built across the Mahanadi near Sambalpur in Odisha.

questions.text: Which team has won the season 8 of Pro Kabbadi league?
questions.explanation: Dabang Delhi K.C. won season 8 of the Pro Kabaddi League, beating Patna Pirates 37-36 in the final in February 2022.

questions.text: Who among the following won the Formula One 2022 Bahrain Grand Prix?
questions.explanation: Charles Leclerc of Ferrari won the 2022 Bahrain Grand Prix, the season's opening race, on 20 March 2022; his teammate Carlos Sainz Jr. was second and Lewis Hamilton third.

questions.text: Which of the following Indian festivals celebrates the death of the demon king Ravana at the hands of Lord Rama?
questions.explanation: Dussehra (Vijayadashami) marks Rama's victory over Ravana, whose effigies are burnt on the day. Diwali marks Rama's return to Ayodhya.

questions.text: What is the name of the DIGI-book launched by NITI Aayog’s Atal Innovation Mission (AIM)?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog's Atal Innovation Mission launched the DIGI-book 'Innovations for You' in October 2021; its first edition profiles 45 health-care start-ups from Atal Incubation Centres.

questions.text: Tendulkar Methodology is associated with the estimation of ______ in India.
questions.explanation: The expert group headed by Suresh Tendulkar (2009) set the method the Planning Commission used to draw poverty lines and estimate the share of people below them.

questions.text: Ashoka fought a war to conquer Kalinga. Kalinga was the ancient name of coastal ______.
questions.explanation: Kalinga, the kingdom Ashoka conquered in a war he later regretted, is the ancient name for coastal Orissa (now Odisha).

questions.text: What is the meaning of the term Moraine?
options: Material transported and deposited by glacier
Valley with vertical sides and wide floor
questions.explanation: Moraines are the rock, gravel and clay a glacier carries and deposits. A valley with steep sides and a wide floor is a U-shaped glacial valley, and a tributary valley left high above the main one is a hanging valley.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book ‘Train to Pakistan’?
questions.explanation: 'Train to Pakistan' (1956), a novel set during the Partition of 1947, is by Khushwant Singh.

questions.text: Which of the following is a Fundamental Right?
questions.explanation: The Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) is one of the Fundamental Rights in Part III of the Constitution. The right to vote rests on Article 326 and the election laws, and the right to information on the Right to Information Act, 2005; Part III names neither.

questions.text: Which of the following states has one house in its state legislature?
questions.explanation: When the exam was held (July 2022), Gujarat had only a Legislative Assembly, while Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra also had a Legislative Council.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Glad
questions.explanation: 'Glad' means happy; its opposite is 'gloomy', sad and low in spirits. 'Cheery', 'delighted' and 'joyous' are near synonyms.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. The novels of Jane Austen “give us a” a glimpse into the world of women.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'the novels' takes the plural verb 'give', and the present tense suits a general truth, so the underlined part needs no change. (The sheet prints the article twice, 'a a glimpse'.)

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Caramel is made from several thousand compounds, making it one of the much complex food products.
options: thousand compounds, making it one of
questions.explanation: 'One of the' needs a superlative, and 'complex' forms it with 'most', not 'much': 'one of the most complex food products'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. It were so painful / to give up / my last hope.
questions.explanation: 'It' is singular and takes 'was', not 'were': 'It was so painful to give up my last hope.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Their are numerous / buildings outside our / school premises.
questions.explanation: 'There are' says that something exists; 'their' is the possessive: 'There are numerous buildings outside our school premises.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Bloom
questions.explanation: A 'bloom' is a flower, and to bloom is to flower. 'Fade', 'drop' and 'wither' describe the end of blooming.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Drink a mixture of wormwood oil and olive oil “to got rid of” worms.
questions.explanation: The infinitive takes the base form of the verb: 'to get rid of worms'. 'To got' is not grammatical.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A piece of cake
questions.explanation: 'A piece of cake' is something very easy to do.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Drop in the bucket
options: An extreme overreaction to something very small or insignificant
To be involved in or be a part of something great or revolutionary
Something small and unimportant, especially when compared with something else
An alarming or unexpected announcement, especially an unpleasant one
questions.explanation: A 'drop in the bucket' is an amount too small to make much difference beside what is needed.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A non-professional who is inept at a particular activity
questions.explanation: An amateur does something without being paid for it, and the word is also used of someone who lacks skill at it. An expert is the opposite, and a fatalist believes events are fixed by fate.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. “Strenuous” exercise can result in muscle pain.
questions.explanation: 'Strenuous' means needing great effort; its opposite is 'effortless'. 'Irksome' means annoying and 'impelling' driving forward.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Relapse
questions.explanation: To 'relapse' is to fall back into illness or a worse state after getting better; its opposite is to 'improve'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Having a common centre, as circles or spheres
questions.explanation: Concentric circles or spheres share the same centre. Elliptical means oval, and centrifugal means moving away from a centre.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Please sit down and have breakfast _______ us.
questions.explanation: One has a meal 'with' someone, in their company: 'have breakfast with us'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. My most “vivid” recollection of last summer is the ocean.
questions.explanation: A 'vivid' memory is clear and sharp: 'lucid' (clear). 'Vague' and 'blurry' are nearly opposite, and 'composed' means calm.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. Both of “mine child passed” the examination successfully.
questions.explanation: 'Both' needs a plural noun, and before a noun the possessive is 'my', not 'mine': 'Both of my children passed the examination successfully.'

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Acknowledge' is spelt correctly. The others should be 'precursor', 'religiosity' and 'ancestors'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who can use either hand with ease
questions.explanation: An ambidextrous person can use the right and left hands equally well. Gregarious means sociable, a virtuoso is a highly skilled performer and pedantic means too concerned with minor rules.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. Bring me the finest dress “from an finest” shop.
questions.explanation: A superlative such as 'finest' takes 'the': 'from the finest shop'. 'An' goes only before a vowel sound and never before a superlative.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Latin may be the language that we (1) ______ with the Roman Empire, but the uestion of (2) ______ the Romans spoke Latin or not (3) ______ not have a simple answer. Rome grew from a tiny community in the middle of a culturally diverse peninsula into an empire that reached (4) ______ Britain to Syria. As Rome’s power spread, Romans also interacted with (5) ______ of dozens of other languages

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: To 'associate' one thing with another is to connect them in the mind: we link Latin with the Roman Empire.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Latin may be the language that we (1) ______ with the Roman Empire, but the uestion of (2) ______ the Romans spoke Latin or not (3) ______ not have a simple answer. Rome grew from a tiny community in the middle of a culturally diverse peninsula into an empire that reached (4) ______ Britain to Syria. As Rome’s power spread, Romans also interacted with (5) ______ of dozens of other languages

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Whether' introduces two possibilities, completed here by 'or not': 'whether the Romans spoke Latin or not'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Latin may be the language that we (1) ______ with the Roman Empire, but the uestion of (2) ______ the Romans spoke Latin or not (3) ______ not have a simple answer. Rome grew from a tiny community in the middle of a culturally diverse peninsula into an empire that reached (4) ______ Britain to Syria. As Rome’s power spread, Romans also interacted with (5) ______ of dozens of other languages

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular 'the question', so the helping verb is 'does': 'does not have a simple answer'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Latin may be the language that we (1) ______ with the Roman Empire, but the uestion of (2) ______ the Romans spoke Latin or not (3) ______ not have a simple answer. Rome grew from a tiny community in the middle of a culturally diverse peninsula into an empire that reached (4) ______ Britain to Syria. As Rome’s power spread, Romans also interacted with (5) ______ of dozens of other languages

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'From ... to' gives the extent of the empire: it reached from Britain to Syria.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Latin may be the language that we (1) ______ with the Roman Empire, but the uestion of (2) ______ the Romans spoke Latin or not (3) ______ not have a simple answer. Rome grew from a tiny community in the middle of a culturally diverse peninsula into an empire that reached (4) ______ Britain to Syria. As Rome’s power spread, Romans also interacted with (5) ______ of dozens of other languages

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Romans dealt with the 'speakers' of dozens of other languages, that is with people who spoke them.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and the fifth number is related to the sixth number. 7: 42 :: ? : 110 :: 9 : 72
questions.explanation: Each pair is a number and that number times one less than itself: 7 × 6 = 42 and 9 × 8 = 72. As 110 = 11 × 10, the missing number is 11.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (16, 4, 8); (12, 2, 12)
questions.explanation: In each set the third number is the first divided by the second, times 2: 16 ÷ 4 × 2 = 8 and 12 ÷ 2 × 2 = 12. Likewise 28 ÷ 7 × 2 = 8.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. GOOD : CKKZ :: BEST : XAOP :: COOL : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places back: GOOD → CKKZ and BEST → XAOP. So COOL → YKKH.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘Homonym is antonym’ is coded as ‘# kr pg’, and ‘Antonym are synonym’ is coded as ‘lm pg 6’. What is the code for ‘Antonym’ in that language?
questions.explanation: 'Antonym' is the only word in both sentences and 'pg' the only code in both, so 'antonym' is coded as 'pg'.

questions.text: Select the letter from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. D, F, I, ?, R, X
questions.explanation: As places in the alphabet the series is 4, 6, 9, ?, 18, 24, with differences +2, +3, +4, +5, +6: 9 + 4 = 13, which is M.

questions.text: Among seven sisters Anu, Barsha, Champa, Disha, Emma, Farheen and Geeta; Barsha is elder than only four other sisters. Champa is elder than Disha. Anu is elder than Farheen. Emma is elder than one person only, that is Geeta, who is the youngest among all sisters. Barsha is elder than Anu. Given that no two sisters have the same age, find out who is the eldest sister.
questions.explanation: Barsha is elder than only four sisters, so she is third eldest; Anu, Farheen, Emma and Geeta are younger than her. That leaves Champa and Disha as the two eldest, and Champa is elder than Disha.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. RO : WJ :: PJ : ?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves 5 places forward and the second 5 places back: R → W and O → J. So P → U and J → E: UE.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 425, 442, 459, 476, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 17 more than the one before: 476 + 17 = 493.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'ROMKSG' is written as 'SQPJQD', and 'PNDABC' is written as 'QPGZZZ'. How will 'QJLMTF' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first three letters move +1, +2, +3 and the last three −1, −2, −3: ROMKSG → SQPJQD and PNDABC → QPGZZZ. So QJLMTF → RLOLRC.

questions.text: Four boys A, R, K and M are sitting in a row facing the North (but not necessarily in the same order) and four girls P, Q, L and B are sitting in a row facing these boys (but not necessarily in the same order). B is second to the right of P. K and A are at the ends. P is at one of the ends. K is at the left end of the row. One boy is sitting between A and R. If Q is at one of the ends, then who is L facing?
questions.explanation: Facing north, the boys sit K, R, M, A from the left, with A at the right end and one boy, M, between R and A. The girls face south, so B second to P's right puts P at the end opposite A and B opposite R; Q takes the other end, opposite K, and L faces M.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘ – ‘ are interchanged and also ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 42 + 10 × 5 − 9 ÷ 1 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 42 − 10 ÷ 5 + 9 × 1 = 42 − 2 + 9 = 49.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statement I: All black are green and no green is red. Statement II: All red are pink. Conclusion I:All black are pink. Conclusion II: Some green are pink.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: All black are green and no green is red, so no black is red. Pink is only known to include every red, so black and green may or may not overlap pink: neither conclusion is certain.

questions.text: In a certain code language, '524' means 'are you fine', '785' means 'you come home' and '6271' means 'we are at home'. What is the code for 'come home' in the same language?
questions.explanation: 'You' is in the first two sentences (5), 'are' in the first and third (2) and 'home' in the second and third (7). So 'come' is 8, and 'come home' is coded with 8 and 7: 87.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'WORLD' is written as 'CUXRJ' and 'SMOKE' is written as ‘YSUQK’. How will 'INDIA' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 6 places forward, wrapping round after Z: WORLD → CUXRJ and SMOKE → YSUQK. So INDIA → OTJOG.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statement I: All leopards are cheetahs. Statement II: No cheetah is a cat. Conclusion I: Some cats are leopards. Conclusion II: Some cats are cheetahs.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: Every leopard is a cheetah and no cheetah is a cat, so no leopard is a cat either: both conclusions are false.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘×‘ are interchanged and also ‘−’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 42 + 6 − 3 × 15 ÷ 5 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 42 × 6 ÷ 3 + 15 − 5 = 84 + 15 − 5 = 94.

questions.text: Seven people Pravin, Rahul, Shikhar, Tirtha, Uday, Vinay, and Wasim are sitting in a straight row facing North. Rahul is sitting second left to Tirtha. Tirtha is sitting third left to Wasim. Rahul and Shikhar are not sitting at either of the corners. Uday is the immediate neighbour of Vinay. Vinay is sitting second left from the right corner. Who is sitting to the immediate left of Rahul?
questions.explanation: Rahul sits five places left of Wasim and not at a corner, so Rahul is second, Tirtha fourth and Wasim seventh from the left. Vinay and Uday take the fifth and sixth places and Shikhar, not at a corner, the third, so Pravin sits first, immediately left of Rahul.

questions.text: Select the number from the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 13, 17, 19, 23, 29, ?
questions.explanation: The terms are consecutive prime numbers: the next prime after 29 is 31.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. ACID : IDAC :: CAMP : MPCA :: TRAY : ?
questions.explanation: The two halves of the word swap places: AC ID → ID AC and CA MP → MP CA. So TR AY → AY TR: AYTR.

questions.text: What is a common term used to measure poverty based on the income or consumption levels?
questions.explanation: The poverty line is the minimum level of income or consumption needed to meet basic needs; people below it are counted as poor.

questions.text: In which of the following states is the Panna National Park located?
questions.explanation: Panna National Park, a tiger reserve on the Ken river, is in Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text: As announced in the Union Budget of FY 2022, how many pilot projects are to be set up for coal gasification?
questions.explanation: The Union Budget 2022-23, presented on 1 February 2022, announced four pilot projects for coal gasification and for turning coal into chemicals that industry needs.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs of autobiography and its author is INCORRECT?
options: The Test of My Life - Kapil Dev
Playing It My Way - Sachin Tendulkar
questions.explanation: 'The Test of My Life' is Yuvraj Singh's autobiography, not Kapil Dev's. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.text: India won eight Olympic gold medals in which sport till 2020?
questions.explanation: India's men's hockey team won Olympic gold eight times: in 1928, 1932, 1936, 1948, 1952, 1956, 1964 and 1980.

questions.text: Who launched the International Air Connectivity Scheme (IACS) in 2022?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Jyotiraditya Scindia, the Union Minister of Civil Aviation in 2022, whose ministry launched the scheme, the international arm of UDAN, under which state governments choose and support routes to foreign cities.

questions.text: The Moatsu Festival is a time of great rejoicing as the planting season comes to an end. It is celebrated by the Ao tribes of _________.
questions.explanation: Moatsu is the festival of the Ao Nagas of Nagaland, held in early May after the sowing is done.

questions.text: No person can disrespect the National flag, Constitution of India and the National Anthem under the ______ Act.
options: Prevention of Insults to National Honour
questions.explanation: The Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 punishes insulting the National Flag or the Constitution of India and preventing the singing of the National Anthem.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi lead the Champaran movement against the indigo planters?
questions.explanation: Gandhi's Champaran Satyagraha, for the indigo cultivators of Champaran in Bihar, took place in 1917; it was his first satyagraha in India.

questions.text: Rukmini Devi Arundale was associated with which classical dance of India?
questions.explanation: Rukmini Devi Arundale helped revive Bharatanatyam and founded Kalakshetra in Madras (Chennai) in 1936.

questions.text: The number of deaths per thousand persons in a year is known as ______.
questions.explanation: The death rate is the number of deaths per thousand people in a year; the birth rate counts live births the same way.

questions.text: A traditional basketball team has 12 players, with ______ basketball players on the court at any given time.
questions.explanation: A basketball team has five players on the court at a time; the others are substitutes.

questions.text: Which state is the leading producer of cotton in India, as of April 2022?
questions.explanation: Gujarat was India's largest cotton producer in the 2021-22 season, ahead of Maharashtra and Telangana.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct about endoplasmic reticulum? I. It is a large network of membrane-bound tubes and sheets. II. It is similar in structure to the plasma membrane.
questions.explanation: The endoplasmic reticulum is a large network of membrane-bound tubes and sheets, and its membrane is similar in structure to the plasma membrane, so both statements are correct.

questions.text: ______ was the capital of the Pandya dynasty.
questions.explanation: Madurai was the capital of the Pandyas. Uraiyur was the capital of the early Cholas, and Karur is linked with the Cheras.

questions.text: Brihadeshwara temple at Thanjavur is one of the largest temples in India and is an example of Dravidian architecture during the ______ period.
questions.explanation: The Chola king Rajaraja I built the Brihadeshwara temple at Thanjavur, completed in about 1010 CE.

questions.text: Who among the following Gupta rulers is known as the 'Napoleon of India’?
questions.explanation: The historian Vincent Smith called Samudragupta the 'Napoleon of India' for his many successful military campaigns.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was the first Indian to be selected to the British ‘House of Commons’ on a Liberal Party ticket?
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji won Finsbury Central for the Liberal Party in 1892 and became the first Indian member of the British House of Commons.

questions.text: The largest ocean on Earth is ___________.
questions.explanation: The Pacific is the largest and deepest ocean, covering about a third of the Earth's surface.

questions.text: To become a member of Rajya Sabha, a person should be a citizen of India and at least ______ of age.
questions.explanation: Article 84 requires a member of the Rajya Sabha to be a citizen of India and at least 30 years old; for the Lok Sabha the minimum is 25.

questions.text: His compositions for blockbusters such as Silsila and Chandni are a manifestation of his musical brilliance. Who is he?
questions.explanation: The santoor player Pandit Shivkumar Sharma and the flautist Hariprasad Chaurasia, as the duo Shiv-Hari, composed the music of 'Silsila' (1981) and 'Chandni' (1989).

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Existing or happening in the same time period
questions.explanation: 'Contemporary' means existing or happening at the same time. 'Inbred' means innate or born of close relatives, and 'cosmopolitan' means drawn from many countries.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Confiscated
questions.explanation: To 'confiscate' is to take something away by authority: 'seized'. 'Acquitted' and 'liberated' mean set free.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Details of the housing / services and allowances / has not been announced yet
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'Details' needs a plural verb: 'Details of the housing, services and allowances have not been announced yet.' (The options misprint the second part as 'services and internment'; that part has no error.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. After a long ______, she finally answered my question.
questions.explanation: A 'pause' is a short stop or silence. 'Pass', 'posse' and 'paws' sound alike but do not fit the sense.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The UAE, along with other/ Gulf states, has been being/ making friendly overtures to Iran.
questions.explanation: 'Has been being making' mixes two forms; the present perfect continuous is 'has been making': 'The UAE, along with other Gulf states, has been making friendly overtures to Iran.' The singular 'has' is right, as a phrase with 'along with' does not change the subject's number.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Every other facility can only “be enjoyed with” the benefit of good health.
questions.explanation: After the modal 'can' the passive is 'be' + past participle, so 'can only be enjoyed with' is already correct.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Robust
questions.explanation: 'Robust' means strong and healthy; its opposite is 'weak'. 'Healthy' and 'strong' are its synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Sprightly
questions.explanation: 'Sprightly' means lively and full of energy; its opposite is 'lethargic', sluggish and without energy.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'indefatigable', meaning never tiring.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. A leopard cannot change its spots
options: It is possible to complete a tedious job
being ready to do anything is not common
It is impossible to change who you are
questions.explanation: 'A leopard cannot change its spots' means that a person's basic nature does not change.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. In some institutions, additional teaching / assistants will hired to / teach high school students.
questions.explanation: The future passive needs 'be': 'additional teaching assistants will be hired to teach high school students'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A room in a public building where outdoor clothes or luggage may be left
questions.explanation: A cloakroom is a room where coats, bags and luggage can be left. A hangar houses aircraft, and a courtyard is an open space enclosed by walls or buildings.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Satiate
questions.explanation: To 'satiate' is to satisfy a hunger or desire fully: 'satisfy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The skill of execution is viewed as inseparable from art, and mastery of technical problems is a ______ for producing expressive interpretations.
questions.explanation: A 'precondition' is something that must exist before something else can happen: mastery of technique comes before expressive interpretation.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The prisoners made an elaborate plan to escape ______ the jail.
questions.explanation: One escapes 'from' a place: 'to escape from the jail'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I can’t ______ this pain anymore.
questions.explanation: To 'bear' pain is to endure it. 'Bier', 'boor' and 'beer' sound alike but do not fit.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. I can neither punish him nor reward him for “which he have done.”
questions.explanation: 'What' (the thing that) is needed after 'for', not 'which', and the singular 'he' takes 'has': 'I can neither punish him nor reward him for what he has done.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I can’t fit this teddy bear in my almirah. It is so ______.
questions.explanation: A teddy bear too big for the almirah is 'gigantic', that is huge. 'Petite' means small, the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Heart and soul
questions.explanation: To do something 'heart and soul' is to do it completely, with all one's energy and enthusiasm.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Scientists (1) ______ Oxford University say their experimental coronavirus vaccine (2) ______ been shown in an early trial to prompt a protective immune response in hundreds of people who got the shot. British researchers first began testing the vaccine in April in about 1,000 people, half of (3) ______ got the experimental vaccine. Such early trials are usually designed only to (4) ______ safety, but in this case, experts were also looking to see what kind of immune response was (5) ______ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'At' goes with a place of work or study: 'Scientists at Oxford University'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Scientists (1) ______ Oxford University say their experimental coronavirus vaccine (2) ______ been shown in an early trial to prompt a protective immune response in hundreds of people who got the shot. British researchers first began testing the vaccine in April in about 1,000 people, half of (3) ______ got the experimental vaccine. Such early trials are usually designed only to (4) ______ safety, but in this case, experts were also looking to see what kind of immune response was (5) ______ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The scientists 'say' it now, so the present perfect is needed, and the singular subject 'vaccine' takes 'has': 'has been shown'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Scientists (1) ______ Oxford University say their experimental coronavirus vaccine (2) ______ been shown in an early trial to prompt a protective immune response in hundreds of people who got the shot. British researchers first began testing the vaccine in April in about 1,000 people, half of (3) ______ got the experimental vaccine. Such early trials are usually designed only to (4) ______ safety, but in this case, experts were also looking to see what kind of immune response was (5) ______ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'of', the object form 'whom' refers to the people: 'half of whom got the experimental vaccine'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Scientists (1) ______ Oxford University say their experimental coronavirus vaccine (2) ______ been shown in an early trial to prompt a protective immune response in hundreds of people who got the shot. British researchers first began testing the vaccine in April in about 1,000 people, half of (3) ______ got the experimental vaccine. Such early trials are usually designed only to (4) ______ safety, but in this case, experts were also looking to see what kind of immune response was (5) ______ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Early trials are designed to 'evaluate', that is assess, the vaccine's safety.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Scientists (1) ______ Oxford University say their experimental coronavirus vaccine (2) ______ been shown in an early trial to prompt a protective immune response in hundreds of people who got the shot. British researchers first began testing the vaccine in April in about 1,000 people, half of (3) ______ got the experimental vaccine. Such early trials are usually designed only to (4) ______ safety, but in this case, experts were also looking to see what kind of immune response was (5) ______ .

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The experts wanted to see what immune response the vaccine 'provoked', that is produced; 'reduced', 'lessened' and 'sheltered' do not fit.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. No G is H. II. Some R are G. Conclusions: I. Some H are not G. II. All H are R.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: 'No G is H' also means no H is G, so some H are not G: I follows. No statement links H with R, so II does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'DISK' is written as 'SIKD', and 'MINE' is written as 'NIEM'. How will 'BOLD' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters in places 3, 2, 4 and 1 are written in that order: DISK → S I K D and MINE → N I E M. So BOLD → L O D B: LODB.

questions.text: In a certain code language, if phone is called laptop, laptop is called kettle, kettle is called refrigerator, refrigerator is called charger, and charger is called cooler, then what is used to store food?
questions.explanation: Food is stored in a refrigerator, and a refrigerator is called 'charger'.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 56, 111, 221, 441, 881, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is twice the one before, minus 1: 56 × 2 − 1 = 111, 111 × 2 − 1 = 221, and so on, so 881 × 2 − 1 = 1761.

questions.text: If ‘Red’ is called ‘Blue’, ‘Blue’ is called ‘White’, ‘White’ is called ‘Black’, ‘Black’ is called ‘Pink’, and ‘Pink’ is called ‘Orange’, then what is the colour of milk?
questions.explanation: Milk is white, and 'White' is called 'Black'.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers in the given set. (146, 102, 58)
questions.explanation: Each number is 44 less than the one before: 146 − 44 = 102 and 102 − 44 = 58. Likewise 150 − 44 = 106 and 106 − 44 = 62.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth alphanumeric-cluster in the same way as the second alphanumeric-cluster is related to the first alphanumeric-cluster and the fourth alphanumeric-cluster is related to the third alphanumeric-cluster. MNO13 : QRS17 :: PQR16 : TUV20 :: STU19 : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places forward and the number, the first letter's place in the alphabet, rises by 4: MNO13 → QRS17 and PQR16 → TUV20. So STU19 → WXY23.

questions.text: By interchanging the two numbers 20 and 36, which of the following equations will be correct? I. 55 + 42 – 36 × 20 ÷ 9 = 17 II. 20 ÷ 2 × 36 + 81 – 41 = 400
Select the letter-cluster that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. GAM, DCJ, AEG, XGD, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move back 3 (G, D, A, X, U), the second forward 2 (A, C, E, G, I) and the third back 3 (M, J, G, D, A): UIA.

questions.text: Among five friends Aman, Baman, Chaman, Karan and Tapan, Chaman is older than only one friend. Tapan is older than Karan. Only two persons are older than Karan. Baman is older than Tapan. Who is the youngest among all the friends?
questions.explanation: Only two are older than Karan, so Karan is third; Tapan, older than Karan, is second and Baman, older than Tapan, first. Chaman, older than only one, is fourth, which leaves Aman the youngest.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 68 : 4 :: 130 : 5 :: 350 : ?
questions.explanation: Each first number is the cube of its pair plus the pair itself: 4³ + 4 = 68 and 5³ + 5 = 130. Likewise 7³ + 7 = 343 + 7 = 350.

questions.text: 6 persons A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). A is the immediate neighbour of D and F. F is the immediate neighbour of E and A. B is in the second position from the right end. If D is not at any of the ends, then how many persons are sitting towards the left of D?
questions.explanation: A sits between D and F, and F between A and E, so the four sit as E F A D or D A F E. B is fifth from the left, so the four take places 1 to 4, and as D is not at an end the row is E F A D B C. Three persons sit to the left of D.

questions.text: Which of the numbers (not digits) should be interchanged in the given equation to make it mathematically correct? 4 + 6 × 3 − 5 ÷ 2 = 16
questions.explanation: After interchanging 5 and 6: 4 + 5 × 3 − 6 ÷ 2 = 4 + 15 − 3 = 16.

questions.text: Select the option that will replace the question mark (?) in the given series. 77, 158, 207, 232, 241, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 81, 49, 25 and 9, the squares of 9, 7, 5 and 3. The next is 1² = 1: 241 + 1 = 242.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. RIDE : EIDR :: IDLE : EDLI :: LAMP : ?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters swap places: RIDE → EIDR and IDLE → EDLI. So LAMP → PAML.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. Night Blindness : Vitamin A :: Beri Beri : ?
questions.explanation: Night blindness is caused by a lack of vitamin A, and beri-beri by a lack of vitamin B1 (thiamine), one of the B vitamins.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statement I: Some pastas are pizzas. No pizza is a burger. Statement II: All burgers are nachos. Conclusion I: Some pasta being nacho is a possibility. Conclusion II: All pizza being nacho is a possibility.
options: Both conclusions I and II follows.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: No statement links pastas with nachos, so some pasta being nacho is possible: I follows. Pizzas are only kept out of burgers, so the nachos can still include every pizza: II follows too.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'HOLA' is coded as '16', and 'GRABY' is coded as '25'. How will 'SIX' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded as the square of its number of letters: HOLA (4) → 16 and GRABY (5) → 25. So SIX (3) → 9.

questions.text: Among seven friends P, Q, R, S, T, U and V; U is taller than only three other friends. R is tallest among all friends. T is taller than U. Q is taller than only one person. Only two persons are taller than P. V is taller than Q. Who is the shortest among all the friends?
questions.explanation: R is the tallest. Only two are taller than P, so P is third; U, taller than only three, is fourth, and T, taller than U, is second. Q is sixth and V, taller than Q, fifth, so S is the shortest.

questions.text: What are the projections of varying lengths protruding out of an amoeba’s body, which can appear and disappear, known as?
questions.explanation: Pseudopodia ('false feet') are temporary projections of an amoeba's cytoplasm, used to move and to capture food. A contractile vacuole expels excess water, and Paramecium is another protozoan.

questions.text: What is the minimum age to become Rajya Sabha member?
questions.explanation: Under Article 84(b) a member of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) must be at least 30 years old; for the Lok Sabha the minimum is 25.

questions.text: Who among the following former governors of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was appointed as the Vice-President of The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) in January 2022?
questions.explanation: In January 2022 Urjit Patel, RBI governor from September 2016 to December 2018, was named one of the AIIB's five vice-presidents, for a three-year term.

questions.text: Who among the following musicians has won the Bharat Ratna Award?
questions.explanation: Ustad Bismillah Khan, the shehnai maestro, received the Bharat Ratna in 2001. The other three, masters of the sarangi, the flute and the sarod, had not received it when the exam was held (July 2022).

questions.text: By maternal descent, Mughals were descendants of ?
questions.explanation: Babur, the first Mughal emperor, descended from Timur on his father's side and from Genghis Khan, through Chagatai, on his mother's.

questions.text: Gochi festival is an Indian festival majorly celebrated in ________.
questions.explanation: Gochi is celebrated in February in the Lahaul valley of Himachal Pradesh by families in which a son was born during the previous year.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who set up the Asiatic Society of Bengal?
questions.explanation: Sir William Jones founded the Asiatic Society in Calcutta in January 1784 to promote the study of Asia's history, languages and literature.

questions.text: In which year was the first ICC men’s Cricket World Cup played?
questions.explanation: The first men's Cricket World Cup was held in England in 1975; West Indies beat Australia in the final at Lord's.

questions.text: Which of the following factors does NOT affect the formation of soil?
questions.explanation: Soil forms from parent material under the influence of climate, relief (topography), living organisms and time. A landslide moves soil and rock rather than forming soil.

questions.text: The Barabati Fort is situated in the city of.
questions.explanation: The ruins of Barabati Fort, built by the medieval rulers of Odisha, stand in Cuttack on the bank of the Mahanadi, beside the Barabati Stadium.

questions.text: Which of the following elements of the periodic table has atomic number 1?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen, the lightest element, has one proton in its nucleus, so its atomic number is 1. Nitrogen's is 7, cobalt's 27 and copper's 29.

questions.text: ‘Ace Against Odds’ is the autobiography of which of the following persons?
questions.explanation: 'Ace Against Odds' (2016) is the autobiography of the tennis player Sania Mirza.

questions.text: Which famous Bharatanatyam dancer was awarded with the Padma Bhushan in 1957 and Padma Vibhushan in 1977? Bengali film director Satyajit Ray made a documentary on her.
questions.explanation: Tanjore Balasaraswati received the Padma Bhushan in 1957 and the Padma Vibhushan in 1977; Satyajit Ray's documentary 'Bala' (1976) is about her.

questions.text: Zoroaster was a/an ______ prophet.
questions.explanation: Zoroaster (Zarathustra), the founder of Zoroastrianism, was a prophet of ancient Iran (Persia); the Parsis of India follow his faith.

questions.text: The word agriculture is derived from the Latin words ager and culture. What does ‘ager’ mean?
questions.explanation: NCERT explains 'agriculture' as coming from the Latin 'ager' (or 'agri'), meaning soil, and 'culture', meaning cultivation.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who founded Shantiniketan near Bolpur on 22 December 1901?
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore opened his school at Santiniketan, near Bolpur in West Bengal, on 22 December 1901; it grew into Visva-Bharati. The ashram there had been set up by his father, Debendranath Tagore, in 1863.

questions.text: What is the total number of India’s neighbouring countries?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives nine, the neighbours NCERT's Class 9 geography names: the seven countries that share a land border with India (Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar and Bangladesh) and the two island countries across the sea, Sri Lanka and Maldives. Other lists count differently, depending on what is taken as a neighbour.

questions.text: Which Indian city will host the 2023 International Olympic Committee session?
questions.explanation: In February 2022 the IOC chose Mumbai to host its 2023 session; the 141st IOC Session was held there in October 2023, the first in India since New Delhi in 1983.

questions.text: Which state has the highest reserves of graphite in India, as of April 2022?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Arunachal Pradesh, which holds the largest share of India's graphite resources (about 36% in the National Mineral Inventory of 1 April 2020). In the narrower 'reserves' category (proved and probable) the Indian Bureau of Mines puts Tamil Nadu first, but it is not among the options.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a feature of parliamentary government in India?
options: Membership of the ministers in the legislature,
Presence of nominal and real executives
Collective responsibility of the executive to the legislature
