questions.explanation: The President can dissolve the Lok Sabha on the advice of the council of ministers, and a dissolvable lower house is itself a feature of the parliamentary system. The other three are features of it.

questions.text: In India, the second census of the 21st century was conducted in ______.
questions.explanation: Census 2011, India's 15th census, was the second of the 21st century, after 2001.

questions.text: Who among the following legendary Kathak dancers passed away in January 2022?
questions.explanation: Pandit Birju Maharaj, the Kathak master of the Lucknow gharana, died in Delhi in January 2022, aged 83.

questions.text: Baking soda is the common name of ____________.
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium hydrogencarbonate (sodium bicarbonate), NaHCO₃; washing soda is sodium carbonate.

questions.text: Since which year has the AFSPA been started?
questions.explanation: The Armed Forces (Special Powers) Act was passed in 1958, first for disturbed areas of Assam and Manipur; it gives the armed forces special powers in areas declared 'disturbed'.

questions.text: Jagoi and Cholom are the two main divisions of ?
questions.explanation: Manipuri dance has two main forms: Jagoi, gentle and graceful (lasya), and Cholom, vigorous (tandava).

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Below the belt
questions.explanation: To hit 'below the belt' is to act in a cruel and unfair way, like an illegal low punch in boxing.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Her forty-fourth birthday “had just passed, unnoticed by all but herself.”
options: had just passed, unnoticed by but all herself
has just passed, unnoticed by all herself
has just passed, unnoticed by but all herself
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct as it stands: 'had just passed' fits the past narrative, and 'unnoticed by all but herself' means noticed by no one except her. The options muddle the word order or drop 'but'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. He sat down in a darkly corner and covered his face, and would not say a single word to anyone.
options: and covered his face, and would
He sat down in a darkly corner
not say a single word to anyone
questions.explanation: 'Darkly' is an adverb; the noun 'corner' needs the adjective: 'in a dark corner'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The goons fled after kill a boy in the street.
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'after', the verb takes the '-ing' form: 'fled after killing a boy'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She smashed a ______ of glass with the metal vase.
questions.explanation: A 'pane' is a sheet of glass, as in a window; 'pain' only sounds like it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I have visited ______ coaching institutes in your region.
questions.explanation: 'Many' goes with plural countable nouns such as 'institutes'; 'much' is for uncountable nouns, and 'any' belongs in questions and negatives.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Vanish
questions.explanation: To 'vanish' is to disappear; its opposite is to 'emerge', to come into view.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Acute
questions.explanation: 'Acute' means severe or serious, as in an acute shortage, which is close to 'dire'. 'Chronic' and 'obtuse' are its opposites in other senses.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Keep body and soul together
questions.explanation: To 'keep body and soul together' is to earn just enough to stay alive in hard times.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. That fellow pushed me so hard that my vision got _____ for a second.
questions.explanation: A hard push can leave one's sight 'blurred', that is unclear, for a moment.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I organised my dressing table by putting all the rubber bands ______ the drawer.
questions.explanation: Things are put 'in' a drawer, an enclosed space.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Next month, she “was going to” the institute to study for a master's degree.
questions.explanation: 'Next month' points to the future, so a planned action takes the present continuous: 'she is going to the institute'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. He blew out the candle and “went to sleepy.”
questions.explanation: After 'went to' the noun 'sleep' is needed, not the adjective 'sleepy': 'went to sleep'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Simon had always been an “ardent” follower.
questions.explanation: 'Ardent' means passionate or enthusiastic; 'averse' and 'casual' are nearly its opposites.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Most mainliners do not view modern culture as inherently ______ to religious belief.
questions.explanation: 'Inimical' means hostile or harmful: modern culture is not seen as hostile to religious belief. 'Inchoate' means only just begun and 'inadvertent' unintended.

questions.text: Select the option that corrects the misspelt words in the given sentence. A number of measres have been sugested by her.
options: A number of measrues have been sugessted by her.
A number of measures have been sujjested by her.
A number of measures have been suggested by her.
A number of mesures have been suggested by her.
questions.explanation: The words are 'measures' and 'suggested', with a double 'g'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Outstanding
questions.explanation: 'Outstanding' means exceptionally good; its opposite is 'ordinary'. 'Astounding' and 'remarkable' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'specialist'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. ______ I learned that there was a gift for each child, I was delighted.
questions.explanation: 'When' introduces a clause of time: on learning of the gifts, the speaker was delighted. 'Though' would wrongly suggest a contrast.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Both of my parents are dependent on my salary of their living.
questions.explanation: One depends on something 'for' a living: 'dependent on my salary for their living'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Many forests are cleared to (1) ______ way for palm oil plantations. Palm oil is the most (2) ______ produced vegetable oil and is found in half of all supermarket products. It's cheap, versatile and can be added to (3) ______ food and personal products like lipsticks and shampoo. (4) ______ popularity has (5) ______ people to clear tropical forests to grow more palm trees.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: To 'make way for' something is to clear space for it: forests are cleared to make way for plantations.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Many forests are cleared to (1) ______ way for palm oil plantations. Palm oil is the most (2) ______ produced vegetable oil and is found in half of all supermarket products. It's cheap, versatile and can be added to (3) ______ food and personal products like lipsticks and shampoo. (4) ______ popularity has (5) ______ people to clear tropical forests to grow more palm trees.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Palm oil is the 'most commonly produced' vegetable oil, that is the one produced most widely.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Many forests are cleared to (1) ______ way for palm oil plantations. Palm oil is the most (2) ______ produced vegetable oil and is found in half of all supermarket products. It's cheap, versatile and can be added to (3) ______ food and personal products like lipsticks and shampoo. (4) ______ popularity has (5) ______ people to clear tropical forests to grow more palm trees.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Both' introduces the pair 'food and personal products'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Many forests are cleared to (1) ______ way for palm oil plantations. Palm oil is the most (2) ______ produced vegetable oil and is found in half of all supermarket products. It's cheap, versatile and can be added to (3) ______ food and personal products like lipsticks and shampoo. (4) ______ popularity has (5) ______ people to clear tropical forests to grow more palm trees.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Its', the possessive, refers to palm oil's popularity; 'it's' means 'it is'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Many forests are cleared to (1) ______ way for palm oil plantations. Palm oil is the most (2) ______ produced vegetable oil and is found in half of all supermarket products. It's cheap, versatile and can be added to (3) ______ food and personal products like lipsticks and shampoo. (4) ______ popularity has (5) ______ people to clear tropical forests to grow more palm trees.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: Its popularity has 'prompted', or led, people to clear tropical forests.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 4, 34, 58, 76, 88, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 30, 24, 18, 12, falling by 6, so the next is 6: 88 + 6 = 94.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'PEARL' is coded as '24153', 'EARTH' is coded as '41590' and 'PILE' is coded as '2634'. What is the code for the word 'HEAR' in that language?
questions.explanation: Letter by letter, PEARL → 24153 and EARTH → 41590 give P = 2, E = 4, A = 1, R = 5, L = 3, T = 9 and H = 0, and PILE → 2634 agrees. So HEAR → 0415.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. TOR, ?, VQT, WRU, XSV
questions.explanation: The first letters run T, U, V, W, X, the second O, P, Q, R, S and the third R, S, T, U, V: UPS.

questions.text: Which two signs need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 35 + 7 × 12 − 6 ÷ 2 = 6
questions.explanation: Interchanging − and × gives 35 + 7 − 12 × 6 ÷ 2 = 35 + 7 − 36 = 6.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (8, 4, 1); (12, 4, 5)
questions.explanation: In each set the first number minus the second, minus 3, gives the third: 8 − 4 − 3 = 1 and 12 − 4 − 3 = 5. Only 17 − 8 − 3 = 6 fits; the other sets would need 21, 15 and 20.

questions.text: By interchanging the given two signs ÷ and –, which of the following equations will be correct? I. 143 + 6 × 18 ÷ 45 – 3 = 236; II. 133 – 7 + 16 × 11 ÷ 37 = 158
questions.explanation: With ÷ and – interchanged, I becomes 143 + 6 × 18 − 45 ÷ 3 = 143 + 108 − 15 = 236 and II becomes 133 ÷ 7 + 16 × 11 − 37 = 19 + 176 − 37 = 158, so both are correct.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some festivals are fireworks. No cracker is a firework. No bomb is a festival. Conclusions: I. No bomb is a cracker. II. Some bombs are crackers.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: No statement links bombs with crackers, so neither conclusion follows on its own. But 'No bomb is a cracker' and 'Some bombs are crackers' cover every case between them, so either I or II follows.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statement I: All mobiles are electronics. Statement II: All laptops are electronics. Conclusion I: Some mobiles are laptops. Conclusion II: All mobiles are laptops.
options: Either conclusion I or II follows.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: Mobiles and laptops are both inside electronics, but nothing says they overlap, so neither 'some' nor 'all' mobiles being laptops follows. The two conclusions are not a complementary pair, so 'either-or' does not apply.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. RNP : SOQ :: CSN : DTO :: EJM : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves forward 1: RNP → SOQ and CSN → DTO. So EJM → FKN.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'HAPREB' is written as 'IEUQAW', and 'GBCDFA' is written as 'HFHCBV'. How will 'QRPLAC' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, +4, +5, −1, −4, −5 in turn: HAPREB → IEUQAW and GBCDFA → HFHCBV (A − 5 wraps round to V). So QRPLAC → RVUKWX.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) 125 : 25 :: 64 : 16 :: 216 : ?
questions.explanation: Each first number is a cube and the second the square of the same root: 125 = 5³ and 25 = 5², 64 = 4³ and 16 = 4². So 216 = 6³ gives 6² = 36.

questions.text: Six students, Riya, Mala, Ambika, Kajal, Heena and Sanya, are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (but not necessarily in the same order). Ambika is sitting third to the right of Heena. Riya is the immediate neighbour of Heena and Kajal. Mala is not the immediate neighbour of Heena. Kajal is to the immediate right of Ambika.Who is sitting second to the right of Riya?
questions.explanation: Ambika sits opposite Heena, Kajal to Ambika's immediate right and Riya between Heena and Kajal. Mala cannot sit next to Heena, so she takes the seat beside Ambika and Sanya the one beside Heena. Going right from Riya come Heena and then Sanya.

questions.text: Among five friends P, Q, R, S and T, T is taller than only three other friends. R is the tallest among all friends. Q is taller than only one person. Only two persons are taller than P. Who is the shortest among all the friends?
questions.explanation: R is the tallest and T, taller than three, is second; only two are taller than P, so P is third, and Q, taller than only one, is fourth. That leaves S the shortest.

questions.text: Study the given pattern carefully and select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in it. (8, 4, 48), (3, 6, 36), (8, 6, ?)
questions.explanation: The third number is four times the sum of the first two: (8 + 4) × 4 = 48 and (3 + 6) × 4 = 36. So (8 + 6) × 4 = 56.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'ELITE' is coded as '3', and 'BLUE' is coded as '2'. How will 'ABSENCE' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is the number of vowels: ELITE has E, I, E (3) and BLUE has U, E (2). ABSENCE has A, E, E: 3.

questions.text: In a certain code language, if 'sky' is known as 'earth', 'earth' is known as 'water', 'water' is known as 'air', 'air' is known as 'light', and 'light' is known as 'sound', then what is it that humans breathe in?
questions.explanation: Humans breathe in air, and in this code air is called 'light'.

questions.text: Six books Hindi, Biology, Mathematics, Economics, Physics, Chemistry are placed in two racks facing each other with three books in each rack. Hindi and Chemistry are in the same rack but are not neighbours. Biology is placed exactly opposite to Economics. Biology is just left of Hindi facing South direction. Physics is exactly opposite to Chemistry. Which of the following is placed exactly opposite to Hindi?
questions.explanation: Hindi and Chemistry share a rack without being neighbours, so they are at its two ends, and Biology, just left of Hindi, is in the middle. In the facing rack Economics is opposite Biology and Physics opposite Chemistry, which leaves Mathematics opposite Hindi.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. TNG : RLD :: LAC : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move back 2, 2 and 3: T → R, N → L, G → D. So L → J, A → Y, C → Z: JYZ.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. THROUGH : UJUSZMO :: COSTUME : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move forward 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7: THROUGH → UJUSZMO. So C → D, O → Q, S → V, T → X, U → Z, M → S and E → L: DQVXZSL.

questions.text: The lowest known point on earth is called ________, which is present in the Pacific Ocean.
questions.explanation: The Challenger Deep, at the southern end of the Mariana Trench in the western Pacific, is the deepest known point of the Earth's seabed, nearly 11 km down.

questions.text: Renowned Indian classical dancer Mrinalini Sarabhai was awarded with the _____ in 1965.
questions.explanation: Mrinalini Sarabhai, the dancer who founded the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts in Ahmedabad, received the Padma Shri in 1965 and the Padma Bhushan in 1992.

questions.text: Which of the following sports was NOT played at the 2020 Summer Olympic Games (Held in 2021)?
questions.explanation: Bridge is not an Olympic sport (it was a medal event at the 2018 Asian Games); tennis, basketball and judo were all contested at Tokyo.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The Satnami Movement in Central India had a motive to:
questions.explanation: The Satnami movement, founded by Ghasidas in central India, worked among the leatherworkers and sought to improve their social status.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Under which Act was the Supreme court established in India?
questions.explanation: The Regulating Act of 1773 provided for a Supreme Court at Calcutta (Fort William), which was set up in 1774.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book ‘Fearless Governance’?
questions.explanation: 'Fearless Governance' is by Kiran Bedi, the former IPS officer, and draws on her years as Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry (2016-2021).

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a public sector bank in India?
questions.explanation: Punjab National Bank is a public sector (nationalised) bank; Federal Bank, HDFC Bank and Axis Bank are private sector banks.

questions.text: Which of the following was an integral part of the Indo-Islamic form of architecture?
questions.explanation: Domes and arches, with minarets, were the hallmarks of Indo-Islamic architecture, which brought the arcuate style in place of the older post-and-beam (trabeate) building.

questions.text: Which scheme of Rajasthan launched in 2022 provides the rural girls of the state with scholarship schemes?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Udaan, the Rajasthan government's project with the consulting group IPE Global that keeps rural girls in school by enrolling them at the secondary level and sees that the eligible ones get their scholarships. The project had been running in the state for some years before 2022, the year the question gives.

questions.text: Who among the following was the first ruler of the Gupta dynasty to adopt the grand title of Maharaj-adhiraja?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta I was the first Gupta ruler to take the title Maharajadhiraja; his predecessors Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha were styled Maharaja.

questions.text: As of April 2022, what is the capital of India's neighbouring country Myanmar?
questions.explanation: Naypyidaw has been Myanmar's capital since 2005-06, when the government moved there from Yangon. Dhaka is the capital of Bangladesh and Thimphu of Bhutan.

questions.text: Laho is a folk dance of ________.
questions.explanation: Laho, also called the Chipiah dance, is a folk dance of the Pnar (Jaintia) people of Meghalaya, in which men and women dance with linked arms.

questions.text: Which Article provides freedom to manage its own affairs in matters of religion?
questions.explanation: Article 26 gives every religious denomination the freedom to manage its own affairs in matters of religion, to set up institutions and to own and administer property.

questions.text: Who among the following was the first Indian to win an individual gold medal at the Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic gold, in the 10 m air rifle at Beijing in 2008.

questions.text: Which of the following is the largest gland in the human body?
questions.explanation: The liver is the largest gland in the human body; it makes bile and stores glycogen.

questions.text: Who has the power to abolish or create legislative council in the state?
options: High court of the concerned state
Chief minister of the concerned state
questions.explanation: Under Article 169, Parliament can create or abolish a state's Legislative Council by law, once the state's Legislative Assembly asks for it by a resolution passed by a special majority.

questions.text: Which of the following festivals is devoted to worshiping of the Sun and celebrated mainly by the people of Bihar?
questions.explanation: Chhath Puja, devoted to the Sun god, is celebrated mainly in Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern Uttar Pradesh.

questions.text: Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) was launched in ______.
questions.explanation: Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana began on 1 April 1999, merging IRDP, TRYSEM and other self-employment programmes; it was restructured as the National Rural Livelihoods Mission in 2011.

questions.text: Cobalt therapy is the medical use of ____________ rays from the radioisotope cobalt-60 to treat conditions such as cancer.
questions.explanation: Cobalt-60 gives off gamma rays, which cobalt therapy aims at tumours to kill cancer cells.

questions.text: Amjad Ali Khan is associated with which instrument?
questions.explanation: Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is a sarod player of the Bangash gharana, son of Ustad Hafiz Ali Khan.

questions.text: In coastal areas, during the night, wind blows from land to sea because:
options: low pressure is created on land
high pressure is created at sea
questions.explanation: At night land cools faster than the sea, so the air over land is cooler and at higher pressure than over the water, and the land breeze blows out to sea.

questions.text: ‘Kathakali’ is a classical dance form of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Kathakali is the classical dance-drama of Kerala.

questions.text: Which state is the leading producer of sugarcane in India, as of April 2022?
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh was India's largest producer of sugarcane when the exam was held (July 2022), ahead of Maharashtra.

questions.text: Which organelle is found both in eukaryotic and prokaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes, which make proteins, occur in both prokaryotic (70S) and eukaryotic (80S) cells; Golgi bodies, mitochondria and lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles found only in eukaryotes.

questions.text: Who defeated Maharana Pratap in the Battle of Haldighati in 1576?
questions.explanation: At Haldighati in June 1576 Akbar's Mughal army, commanded by Raja Man Singh of Amber, defeated Maharana Pratap of Mewar.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who runs away from justice or a dangerous situation
questions.explanation: A fugitive is a person who has run away, especially from the law. A sadist enjoys causing pain, an altruist puts others first and an insolvent person cannot pay their debts.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Once in a blue moon
questions.explanation: Something that happens 'once in a blue moon' happens very rarely.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Having or forming a hard outer layer
questions.explanation: 'Crusted' means covered with or forming a crust, a hard outer layer. 'Crunched' and 'crushed' describe pressing or breaking, and 'cursed' is unrelated.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Adamant' (refusing to change one's mind) is spelt correctly; the others should be 'amorphous', 'despotic' and 'contentious'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. I “am not gone” to harm this dog.
questions.explanation: 'Be going to' expresses an intention about the future: 'I am not going to harm this dog.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Ritu had gone out to drink water _______________ her examination started.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had gone' marks the earlier action, and 'before' links it to the later one: she went out to drink water before the examination started.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I feel so lazy and ______ after doing any strenuous work.
questions.explanation: 'Sluggish' means slow and lacking energy, which goes with 'lazy' after strenuous work. 'Lively' and 'bouncing' mean the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Ambitious
questions.explanation: 'Ambitious' means eager to succeed and willing to work for it, so 'lazy' is nearest to its opposite. 'Vigorous', 'dynamic' and 'lively' all suggest energy.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The study of the heart and its action and disease
questions.explanation: Cardiology is the branch of medicine that deals with the heart and its diseases. Pharmacology studies drugs, anthropology human societies and microbiology microorganisms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. My mother is a ______________ and forgiving person.
questions.explanation: 'Compassionate' (feeling and showing sympathy for others) sits naturally with 'forgiving'. 'Respective' means belonging to each separately and does not fit.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. San Francisco is more bigger / than Boston in terms of / population density.
questions.explanation: 'Bigger' is already comparative, so 'more' must go: 'San Francisco is bigger than Boston'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. We have the responsibility “of finding our” daughter.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: 'the responsibility of' takes the gerund 'finding', with 'our daughter' as its object. The options change the sense or break the grammar.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hit the nail on the head
options: To be exactly right about something
questions.explanation: To 'hit the nail on the head' is to describe or judge something exactly right.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Fleeting
questions.explanation: 'Fleeting' means lasting only a very short time, so its opposite is 'lasting'. 'Passing' and 'brief' are synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Propitious
questions.explanation: 'Propitious' means favourable, promising success: 'auspicious'. 'Inimical' (harmful, hostile) is nearly its opposite, and 'cogent' means convincing.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. In the primitive / oceans, / life begins / nearly 3.5 billion years ago.
questions.explanation: 'Nearly 3.5 billion years ago' places the event in the past, so the verb must be simple past: 'life began'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Try to sound more innocent than “sarcastic.”
questions.explanation: 'Sarcastic' means mocking in a bitter, cutting way: 'caustic'. 'Playful', 'mild' and 'rational' lack the sting.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I am ______ willing to sign this contract with your company.
questions.explanation: 'Not' negates the adjective 'willing': 'I am not willing to sign'. 'No' goes before a noun, 'none' is a pronoun and 'nor' joins negative clauses.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Continuous heavy / rainfall may / further worse / the flood situation.
questions.explanation: The modal 'may' needs a verb after it, and 'worse' is an adjective: 'may further worsen the flood situation'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Speech pathologists are (1) ______ in communication disabilities. They work within multidisciplinary health-care teams (2) ______ a variety of hospital and community-based sites. This (3) ______ working with medical, nursing, and allied health professionals such (4) ______ psychologists, occupational therapists, social (5) ______ and physiotherapists.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Speech pathologists are trained specialists, 'experts' in communication disabilities; 'quacks' are fake practitioners.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Speech pathologists are (1) ______ in communication disabilities. They work within multidisciplinary health-care teams (2) ______ a variety of hospital and community-based sites. This (3) ______ working with medical, nursing, and allied health professionals such (4) ______ psychologists, occupational therapists, social (5) ______ and physiotherapists.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: They work 'across' a variety of sites, that is, in many different hospital and community settings.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Speech pathologists are (1) ______ in communication disabilities. They work within multidisciplinary health-care teams (2) ______ a variety of hospital and community-based sites. This (3) ______ working with medical, nursing, and allied health professionals such (4) ______ psychologists, occupational therapists, social (5) ______ and physiotherapists.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'This' takes the present-tense 'includes', matching 'They work' in the sentence before: 'This includes working with...'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Speech pathologists are (1) ______ in communication disabilities. They work within multidisciplinary health-care teams (2) ______ a variety of hospital and community-based sites. This (3) ______ working with medical, nursing, and allied health professionals such (4) ______ psychologists, occupational therapists, social (5) ______ and physiotherapists.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Such as' introduces examples: 'allied health professionals such as psychologists, occupational therapists...'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Speech pathologists are (1) ______ in communication disabilities. They work within multidisciplinary health-care teams (2) ______ a variety of hospital and community-based sites. This (3) ______ working with medical, nursing, and allied health professionals such (4) ______ psychologists, occupational therapists, social (5) ______ and physiotherapists.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Social workers' are professionals who help people with social and personal problems, listed here with the therapists.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. ACADEMY : ZXZWVNB :: FINANCE : URMZMXV :: PACKAGE : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on): ACADEMY → ZXZWVNB and FINANCE → URMZMXV. So PACKAGE → KZXPZTV.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. TOC, SLX, RIS, QFN, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters run T, S, R, Q, P; the second move back 3 (O, L, I, F, C); the third move back 5 (C, X, S, N, I), wrapping round from A to Z. The next cluster is PCI.

questions.text: If '–' stands for '×', '×' stands for '+', '+' stands for'÷' and '÷' stands for '–', then what will be the value of 516 – 2558 + 172 × 12 ÷ 7086?
Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. POK : HLM :: ORT : ?
questions.explanation: The letters are reversed and each moved back 3: POK → KOP → HLM. So ORT → TRO → QOL.

questions.text: In a certain code language, '251' means 'Water is Black', '509' means 'Black Her Eyes' and '981' means 'Eyes Like Water'. Find the code for 'is'.
questions.explanation: 'Black' is in the first two sentences and '5' in their codes; 'Water' is in the first and third, with '1'. So in '251' for 'Water is Black', 'is' = 2.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. LON : RRN :: MAD : ?
questions.explanation: The letters are reversed and moved +4, +3 and +2: LON → NOL → RRN. So MAD → DAM → HDO.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No apples are trees. Some trees are dense. Conclusions: I. Some apples are dense. II. No tree is an apple.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: 'No apples are trees' converts to 'No tree is an apple', so II follows. Nothing links apples to dense things, so I does not follow.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 8, 18, 57, 232,?, 6996
Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 53, 55, 58, 63, ?, 81
questions.explanation: The differences are the prime numbers 2, 3, 5, 7, 11: 63 + 7 = 70 and 70 + 11 = 81.

questions.text: By interchanging the given two signs and two numbers (not digits), which of the following equations will be correct? ÷ and ×, 25 and 12; I. 105 ÷ 10 × 75 + 25 – 12 = 3; II. 75 × 12 ÷ 25 + 14 – 10 = 40
options: Both I and II are correct.
Neither I nor II is correct.
questions.explanation: After interchanging, I becomes 105 × 10 ÷ 75 + 12 − 25 = 14 + 12 − 25 = 1, not 3; II becomes 75 ÷ 25 × 12 + 14 − 10 = 36 + 4 = 40, which is correct.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'TRAIND' is written as 'FPKBSU', and 'POKRSB' is written as 'DUTLPQ'. How will 'ANLCGH' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The word is reversed, then its first three letters move +2 and its last three +1: TRAIND → DNIART → FPKBSU. So ANLCGH → HGCLNA → JIEMOB.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘Grains contain wheat rice’ is coded as ‘8 6 # %’, and ‘Rice are hard grains’ is coded as ‘# pr % lm’. What is the code for ‘grains rice’ in that code language?
questions.explanation: 'Grains' and 'rice' are the only words in both sentences, and '#' and '%' the only codes in both, so 'grains rice' is '# %'.

questions.text: Three males K, J and M are sitting in a row facing towards the south (not necessarily in the same order). Three females R, F and T are sitting in a row facing towards the face of these males (not necessarily in the same order). R is the immediate neighbour of F and T. K is second to the right of M. R is to the immediate left of F. If we arrange the females in the alphabetical order of their names from the left end to the right end, then how many females will face the same male who they faced before this new arrangement?
questions.explanation: The males face south, so K second to M's right puts them K, J, M from west to east. The females face north; R is between F and T and to F's immediate left, so T, R, F from west to east face K, J, M. Rearranged F, R, T from their own left end, they face K, J, M: only R still faces the same male, J.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 225 : 36 :: 257 : 56 :: 358 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is 4 times the digit sum of the first: (2 + 2 + 5) × 4 = 36 and (2 + 5 + 7) × 4 = 56. So (3 + 5 + 8) × 4 = 64.

questions.text: Six persons - Arun, Brij, Chaman, Danish, Evan and Farukh - sit around a circular table facing the centre. Farukh is second to the right of Arun. Danish is second to the left of Chaman. Brij is to the immediate right of Farukh. Who sits third to the left of Ehsan?
questions.explanation: Going round to each person's right from Arun, the order is Arun, Chaman, Farukh, Brij, Evan, Danish. In a ring of six, third to the left is the person directly opposite, so for Evan it is Chaman. (The question's 'Ehsan' is the paper's misprint for Evan.)

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All radios are electronic items. Some speakers are electronic items. Conclusions: I. No radio is a speaker. II. Some radios are speakers.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Either conclusion I or II follows.
questions.explanation: Neither conclusion follows from the statements alone, but 'No radio is a speaker' and 'Some radios are speakers' cover every case between them, so one of the two must be true: either I or II follows.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (4, 5, 81) (2, 5, 49)
questions.explanation: The third number is the square of the sum of the first two: (4 + 5)² = 81 and (2 + 5)² = 49. Likewise (3 + 5)² = 64.

questions.text: Six people, F, G, H, I, J and K, got different marks in their examination. G got more marks than F and K. F got more marks than I, but not the highest marks. G scored more marks than H. K got more marks than J, but fewer marks than H. I got the third-lowest marks. F got more marks than K but less than H. F got 59 marks and K got 46 marks. Who among the following got the highest marks?
questions.explanation: G scored more than H, F and K, while I is below F and J below K, so G is highest. With I third-lowest, the full order is G, H, F, I, K, J.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'SWISS' is written as 'HDRHH', and 'TABOO' is written as 'GZYLL'. How will 'REHAB' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on): SWISS → HDRHH and TABOO → GZYLL. So REHAB → IVSZY.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following freedom fighters of India was assassinated?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi was shot dead by Nathuram Godse in New Delhi on 30 January 1948. Nehru and Tilak died of illness, and Nana Sahib disappeared after the revolt of 1857.

questions.text: ______ was a Sarod player.
questions.explanation: Buddhadev Das Gupta (died 2018) was a sarod player of the Senia gharana, a disciple of Radhika Mohan Maitra. Bhajan Sopori and Shivkumar Sharma played the santoor, and Annapurna Devi the surbahar.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an example of an abiotic component of the ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Animals are living, so they belong to the biotic component of an ecosystem. Soil, wind and rainfall are non-living, abiotic factors.

questions.text: Manu writes about a sea which is so salty that it is very difficult to drown in it. Which sea is it?
questions.explanation: The Dead Sea, between Jordan and Israel, is one of the saltiest bodies of water in the world; its dense, salty water lets people float with ease.

questions.text: Which of the following is the only active volcanic island in India?
questions.explanation: Barren Island in the Andaman Sea is India's only active volcano. Amindivi and Minicoy are coral islands of Lakshadweep, whose old name is the Laccadives.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds are also known as aliphatic compounds?
questions.explanation: Acyclic, or open-chain, compounds, with straight or branched chains of carbon atoms, are also called aliphatic compounds. Aromatic (benzenoid) compounds are cyclic.

questions.text: The Parliament of India is divided into ________ houses.
questions.explanation: Parliament has two Houses, the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) and the House of the People (Lok Sabha); with the President they make up Parliament (Article 79).

questions.text: What does the R stand for in MICR?
questions.explanation: MICR stands for Magnetic Ink Character Recognition, the technology that reads the codes printed in magnetic ink on cheques.

questions.text: Megasthenes was an ambassador who was sent to the court of _____ by the ______ ruler.
questions.explanation: Megasthenes was sent by the Greek ruler Seleucus Nicator as his ambassador to the court of Chandragupta Maurya at Pataliputra; his account of India is the 'Indica'.

questions.text: A person is said to be in marginal employment if s/he has worked for fewer than ______ months in the year preceding the Census.
questions.explanation: The Census counts as marginal workers those who worked for less than 6 months (183 days) of the reference year; those who worked 6 months or more are main workers.

questions.text: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides protection of life and personal liberty ?
questions.explanation: Article 21: no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.

questions.text: What is the length of the side-line in field-hockey?
questions.explanation: A hockey pitch is 91.40 m long and 55.00 m wide; the side-lines are the longer boundary lines and the back-lines the shorter ones.

questions.text: Which of the following novels is authored by EM Forster?
questions.explanation: 'A Passage to India' (1924) is by E M Forster. 'Invisible Man' is by Ralph Ellison, 'Don Quixote' by Cervantes and 'Beloved' by Toni Morrison.

questions.text: To which of the following classes do parrots belong?
questions.explanation: Parrots are birds, and birds form the class Aves: warm-blooded, feathered vertebrates that lay eggs.

questions.text: Which of the following is a traditional masked dance of West Bengal?
questions.explanation: Gambhira, performed in Malda district around the Chaitra festival, includes masked dances of goddesses such as Kali and Chamunda. Kavadi is from Tamil Nadu, Gidda from Punjab and Jawara from Bundelkhand in Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text: The Lai Haraoba Festival is celebrated by the _________.
questions.explanation: Lai Haraoba, 'the merrymaking of the gods', is the ritual festival of the Meiteis of Manipur, held in honour of the Umang Lai deities.

questions.text: Who among the following was the first transgender Bharatanatyam dancer to receive Padma Shri in 2019?
questions.explanation: Narthaki Nataraj, a Bharatanatyam dancer from Tamil Nadu, received the Padma Shri in 2019, the first transgender person to do so. Manjamma Jogati, a Jogati dancer, received it in 2021.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a cause of unemployment in India?
questions.explanation: Slow economic growth, a fast-growing labour force and poor infrastructure all limit the jobs on offer; a lack of housing is a problem of its own, not a usual cause of unemployment.

questions.text: Who among the following was NOT one of Akbar's ‘Navratna’ (nine gems)?
questions.explanation: Rana Amar Singh, Maharana Pratap's son, ruled Mewar and later made peace with Jahangir; he was never at Akbar's court. Raja Man Singh, Abul Fazl and Raja Todar Mal were among the nine gems.

questions.text: Which Mughal monument was built by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb in the memory of his wife, Dilras Banu Begum?
questions.explanation: The Bibi Ka Maqbara ('tomb of the lady') at Aurangabad, modelled on the Taj Mahal, is the tomb of Aurangzeb's wife Dilras Banu Begum. Most accounts say their son Azam Shah had it built during Aurangzeb's reign, while others credit Aurangzeb himself; 'Bibi Tomb' is not a name the monument goes by.

questions.text: As on February 2022, who among the following was recently appointed as the UGC Chairman?
questions.explanation: M Jagadesh Kumar, then Vice-Chancellor of JNU, was appointed Chairman of the University Grants Commission on 4 February 2022, and held the post when the exam was held (July 2022).

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct regarding Simon commission? I. In 1927, the British government in England decided to send a commission headed by Lord Simon to decide India’s Political future. II. The commission had no Indian representative.
questions.explanation: The Indian Statutory Commission, appointed in November 1927 under Sir John Simon (later Lord Simon), was to report on India's constitutional future. All seven of its members were British, so Indians boycotted it with the cry 'Simon, go back'.

questions.text: Which team did Australia defeat in the final of ICC Men’s T20 World Cup final played in November 2021?
questions.explanation: Australia beat New Zealand by eight wickets in the final at Dubai on 14 November 2021 to win their first T20 World Cup.

questions.text: The HVJ pipeline does NOT run through the state of _____.
questions.explanation: The HVJ gas pipeline runs from Hazira in Gujarat through Vijaipur in Madhya Pradesh to Jagdishpur in Uttar Pradesh, with branches to Kota in Rajasthan; it does not reach Karnataka.

questions.text: In March 2022, the _______ campaign was launched by Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, the Union Minister of Jal Shakti, for greywater management.
questions.explanation: Sujalam 2.0, launched by the Ministry of Jal Shakti on World Water Day, 22 March 2022, focuses on greywater management works at institutions such as panchayat buildings, schools, anganwadi centres and health facilities, following Sujalam 1.0 (2021), which built household and community soak pits.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He has a high paying job, ______________ he never seems to have any money.
questions.explanation: 'Yet' joins two clauses that contrast: he earns well but never seems to have money. 'So' would introduce a result, and 'by' and 'from' are prepositions.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. That ship has sailed
questions.explanation: 'That ship has sailed' means the chance has gone: it is too late to do something about it.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who has a long experience of any occupation
questions.explanation: A veteran is a person with long experience in a field or occupation. A practitioner simply practises a profession, 'reverent' means showing deep respect and 'staunch' means loyal.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'entirely': 'entire' plus '-ly'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. An agreement between enemies or opponents to stop fighting, arguing, etc., for a certain period of time
questions.explanation: A truce is an agreement between opponents to stop fighting for a time. 'Unanimous' means all agreeing, 'graft' is bribery or hard work, and a surplus is an excess.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. It feels greatly to be with you at this ceremony.
questions.explanation: 'Feel' is a linking verb here, so it takes an adjective, not an adverb: 'It feels great to be with you at this ceremony.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who knows all
questions.explanation: 'Omniscient' means knowing everything (from the Latin for 'all' and 'knowing'). An anarchist rejects all government.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Yesterday, after a nice walk, we ______ to sit on the bench, watch the birds, and rest for a while.
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' places the action in the past, so the simple past 'decided' is needed.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The ______ of directors will decide the penalty.
questions.explanation: A company is run by its 'board of directors'. 'Bored', which sounds the same, means weary, and 'bowed' and 'braid' make no sense here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Accuracy rates of facial recognition algorithms are ______ low in the case of minorities, women and children, as demonstrated in multiple studies across the world.
questions.explanation: 'Particularly' (especially) shows that the accuracy is low for these groups above all. 'Smoothly', 'carelessly' and 'beautifully' make no sense with 'low'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I prefer to listen to relaxing and ______ music when meditating.
questions.explanation: 'Soothing' means calming, which goes with 'relaxing' and with meditation. 'Abrading', 'fretting' and 'tormenting' suggest irritation or pain.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Erring
questions.explanation: 'Erring' means making mistakes: 'blundering'. 'Flawless' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. “Carrying an umbrella” is not at all a good idea during thunderstorms.
questions.explanation: A gerund phrase can be the subject of a sentence, and 'umbrella' begins with a vowel sound, so 'an' is right: 'Carrying an umbrella is not at all a good idea' needs no change.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The earthy / fragrance of soil / after a first rain / is always refreshing.
questions.explanation: An ordinal such as 'first' takes the definite article: 'after the first rain'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The reality of the effects of rising aviation industry emissions on climate change has been known for decades, yet the industry and its emissions has continued to grow without _________.
questions.explanation: To grow 'without constraint' is to grow without limit or restriction, which is the point of the 'yet' clause. 'Neglect', 'easiness' and 'comfort' make no sense here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Abundant
questions.explanation: 'Abundant' means plentiful, so its opposite is 'scarce'. 'Surplus' and 'rich' are close to its meaning.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. He got afflicted with the disease / when he was / a teenager.
options: He got afflicted with the disease
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: one is 'afflicted with' a disease, and 'when he was a teenager' keeps the past tense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Penniless
questions.explanation: 'Penniless' means having no money: 'broke'. 'Wealthy' is its opposite.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Anthony Abraham, a 34-year-old crane driver, (1) ______ managed to get out of the way of falling steel. Turning around, he could hardly believe the (2) ______ scene that lay before him. Girders were (3) _____ on top of the crane in a haphazard fashion, like gigantic pick up sticks. All he could see of the machine was its rear wheels and a section of what had been the cab. Abraham (4) ______ to the cab, shouting his friend George Burns' name. By then, three other iron workers had reached the (5) ______ of the carnage. One of them yelled, 'George, can you hear me?' Over the din of the diesel engine, a strained voice responded.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: He 'barely' managed to get out of the way, that is he only just escaped the falling steel.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Anthony Abraham, a 34-year-old crane driver, (1) ______ managed to get out of the way of falling steel. Turning around, he could hardly believe the (2) ______ scene that lay before him. Girders were (3) _____ on top of the crane in a haphazard fashion, like gigantic pick up sticks. All he could see of the machine was its rear wheels and a section of what had been the cab. Abraham (4) ______ to the cab, shouting his friend George Burns' name. By then, three other iron workers had reached the (5) ______ of the carnage. One of them yelled, 'George, can you hear me?' Over the din of the diesel engine, a strained voice responded.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The wreck of the crane under the fallen girders was a 'horrible' scene, one he could hardly believe.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Anthony Abraham, a 34-year-old crane driver, (1) ______ managed to get out of the way of falling steel. Turning around, he could hardly believe the (2) ______ scene that lay before him. Over the din of the diesel engine, a strained voice responded.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Girders lying 'in a haphazard fashion, like gigantic pick up sticks' were 'piled' on top of the crane.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Anthony Abraham, a 34-year-old crane driver, (1) ______ managed to get out of the way of falling steel. Turning around, he could hardly believe the (2) ______ scene that lay before him. Girders were (3) _____ on top of the crane in a haphazard fashion, like gigantic pick up sticks. All he could see of the machine was its rear wheels and a section of what had been the cab.
