Over the din of the diesel engine, a strained voice responded.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Shouting his friend's name, he 'raced', that is ran fast, to the cab. 'Halted' would mean he stopped.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Anthony Abraham, a 34-year-old crane driver, (1) ______ managed to get out of the way of falling steel. Turning around, he could hardly believe the (2) ______ scene that lay before him. Girders were (3) _____ on top of the crane in a haphazard fashion, like gigantic pick up sticks. All he could see of the machine was its rear wheels and a section of what had been the cab. Abraham (4) ______ to the cab, shouting his friend George Burns' name. By then, three other iron workers had reached the (5) ______ of the carnage. One of them yelled, 'George, can you hear me?' Over the din of the diesel engine, a strained voice responded.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The 'scene' of the carnage is the place where it happened. 'Sight' sounds like 'site' but means something seen.

questions.text: Select the option that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. NB, OA, PZ, QY, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move forward one (N, O, P, Q, R) and the second letters back one (B, A, Z, Y, X): RX.

questions.text: 6 persons S, O, K, U, T and A are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). S is sitting second to the right of A. Only one person is sitting between O and U. T is sitting to the immediate right of K. Only two persons are sitting between O and A. Who is sitting third to the left of K?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, right is anticlockwise. O sits opposite A (two persons between them) and S second to A's right; the only arrangement that fits the other clues is, anticlockwise from A: A, U, S, O, K, T. Third to the left of K is U.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. REAS : SGDW :: ABRO : BDUS :: MOBI : ?
questions.explanation: The four letters move +1, +2, +3 and +4: REAS → SGDW and ABRO → BDUS. So MOBI → NQEM.

questions.text: There are eight persons, A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H, all having different weights. Only two persons are lighter than F. F is heavier than A but lighter than B. D is lighter than E but heavier than G. H is lighter than A. C is heavier than E. C is not the heaviest person. The weights of the second heaviest and the second lightest persons are 78 kg and 48 kg, respectively. How many persons are lighter than the person who is just lighter than D?
questions.explanation: Only H and A are lighter than F, so from the lightest the order begins H, A, F. G < D < E < C, and as C is not the heaviest, B is: H, A, F, G, D, E, C, B. The person just lighter than D is G, and three persons (H, A, F) are lighter than G.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All cricketers are sportspersons. Some players are sportspersons. Conclusions: I. No cricketer is a player. II. Some cricketers are players.
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: Neither conclusion is certain, as the players who are sportspersons need not be cricketers. But 'No cricketer is a player' and 'Some cricketers are players' form a complementary pair, one of which must be true, so either I or II follows.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. No X is W. II. Some R are X. Conclusions: I.Some W are not X. II. No W is R.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: 'No X is W' means that no W is X either, so some W are not X: I follows. The R that are X are not W, but other R may be W, so II does not follow.

questions.text: If '–' stands for '×', '+' stands for'÷' and '÷' stands for '–', then what will be the value of 812 + 58 – 65 + 26 – 2 = ?

Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 232 : 21 :: 343 : 30 :: 157 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is three times the sum of the first number's digits: (2 + 3 + 2) × 3 = 21 and (3 + 4 + 3) × 3 = 30. So (1 + 5 + 7) × 3 = 39.

questions.text: In a certain code language, if mustard is called fruit, fruit is called potato, potato is called burger, burger is called flower, and flower is called rice, then what is rose?
questions.explanation: A rose is a flower, and a flower is called 'rice' in this code.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 100, 98, 104, 92, 112, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are −2, +6, −12, +20, −30, that is 1 × 2, 2 × 3, 3 × 4, 4 × 5 and 5 × 6 with alternating signs: 112 − 30 = 82.

questions.text: Which of the mathematical signs should be interchanged in the given equation to make it mathematically correct? 12 + 66 ÷ 11 − 4 × 91 = 159
Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 39, 78, 117, 156, ?, 234
questions.explanation: The terms are 39 × 1, 39 × 2, 39 × 3 and 39 × 4, so the fifth is 39 × 5 = 195 (and the sixth 39 × 6 = 234).

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. BDF : ACE :: NPR : MOQ :: VXZ : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves back one: BDF → ACE and NPR → MOQ. So VXZ → UWY.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'TIK' is coded as ‘40', 'PDM' is coded as ‘33'. How will 'RUG' be coded in that code language?
questions.explanation: Each code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet: TIK = 20 + 9 + 11 = 40 and PDM = 16 + 4 + 13 = 33. So RUG = 18 + 21 + 7 = 46.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. KTM : PGN :: ABC : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (their places add up to 27): K → P, T → G and M → N. So ABC → ZYX.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'SHAPE' is coded as 'VKDSH'. How will 'MODEL' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves forward three places: SHAPE → VKDSH. So MODEL → PRGHO.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'ACADEMIC' is written as 'AACEDIMC', 'ABSTRACT' is written as 'ASBRTCAT', and 'ACCURACY' is written as 'ACCRUCAY'. How will 'ABACAS' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters stay and the letters between are swapped in pairs: A CA DE MI C → A AC ED IM C. So A BA CA S → A AB AC S: AABACS.

questions.text: Seven persons – G, M, R, K, L, P and C – are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. The following information is known about them. G is to the immediate right of K, who is third to the left of C. R is adjacent to both C and P. M is not adjacent to G. Who is third to the left of M?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, right is anticlockwise. Anticlockwise from K the order is K, G, L, C, R, P, M: G is immediately right of K, C third to K's right, R between C and P, and M, not beside G, in the last seat. Moving to M's left the seats are P, R and then C, so C is third to M's left.

questions.text: Select the option in which the two numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers in the given number-pair. 248 : 428
questions.explanation: The first two digits swap places: 248 → 428. Likewise 268 → 628.

questions.text: Which of the following animals does NOT have a backbone?
questions.explanation: A spider is an arthropod, an invertebrate with a hard outer covering instead of a backbone. Frogs, humans and pigeons are vertebrates.

questions.text: According to the fundamental duties given in the Indian Constitution, it shall be the duty of every citizen of India to uphold and protect the sovereignty, _____ of India.
questions.explanation: Article 51A(c) makes it a fundamental duty 'to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India'.

questions.text: Which of the following state governments announced a four-year mentorship programme called 'Project Arohan', to provide guidance to students and improve their skills, in February 2022?
questions.explanation: Assam's AROHAN, a mentor-mentee scheme of the state government for meritorious students of its government schools, guides them from Class IX to Class XII; it began in 2022-23.

questions.text: The remains of the dead plants and animals trapped in the layers of rocks are called ______.
questions.explanation: Fossils are the remains or traces of plants and animals preserved in layers of rock, mostly sedimentary rock.

questions.text: Who won the men’s singles title in Australian Open 2022?
questions.explanation: Rafael Nadal beat Daniil Medvedev in the final of the 2022 Australian Open, coming back from two sets down, for his 21st Grand Slam singles title.

questions.text: What is speed?
options: It is the distance covered by an object in a unit time.
It is the velocity of an object per unit time.
It is the force applied on covering a unit distance.
It is the acceleration of an object per unit time.
questions.explanation: Speed is the distance an object covers in unit time, for example metres per second. Velocity is speed in a given direction.

questions.text: The Census of India provides us with information regarding ______.
questions.explanation: The Census of India counts the population and records its features, such as age, sex, literacy and occupation, once every ten years.

questions.text: Which of the following financial institutions of India protects the interests of the investors and facilitates the functioning of the stock market intermediaries?
options: Small Industries Development Bank of India(SIDBI)
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
questions.explanation: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) is the regulator of the securities market: it protects investors' interests and registers and regulates intermediaries such as stockbrokers.

questions.text: Which of the following novels is based on the Member of Parliament (India), Phoolan devi, and written by the author Roy Moxham?
options: Outlaw: India’s Bandit Queen and Me
questions.explanation: Roy Moxham's 'Outlaw: India's Bandit Queen and Me' (2010), a memoir rather than a novel, tells of his friendship with Phoolan Devi, which began with a letter he wrote to her in jail in 1992.

questions.text: Ustad Allarakha Qureshi, also known as Alla Rakha, was associated with which musical instrument?
questions.explanation: Ustad Alla Rakha, father of Zakir Hussain, was a tabla maestro, known for accompanying the sitarist Ravi Shankar.

questions.text: Where does the Eastern Coastal Plain of India lie?
options: Between the Eastern Ghats and the Bay of Bengal
Between the Gulf of Cambay and Cape Comorin
questions.explanation: The Eastern Coastal Plain lies between the Eastern Ghats and the Bay of Bengal. The other options describe stretches of the western coast.

questions.text: Which of the following persons was appointed as the Commissioner of Delhi Police in July 2021?
questions.explanation: Rakesh Asthana, then Director General of the Border Security Force, was appointed Commissioner of Delhi Police on 27 July 2021.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: The ____________ is an Act of the Parliament of the United Kingdom that partitioned British India into two new independent dominions of India and Pakistan in 1947.
questions.explanation: The Indian Independence Act, 1947, passed by the British Parliament in July 1947, created the dominions of India and Pakistan from 15 August 1947.

questions.text: In which year did Babur defeat Rana Sanga at Khanua?
questions.explanation: Babur defeated Rana Sanga of Mewar at Khanua, near Fatehpur Sikri, in March 1527.

questions.text: Ancient Harappan site ‘Lothal’ was found in which state of India?
questions.explanation: Lothal, a Harappan port town known for its dockyard, is in Ahmedabad district, Gujarat.

questions.text: With which of the following Indian classical dance forms was T Balasaraswati associated?
questions.explanation: T Balasaraswati (1918-1984) was a leading Bharatanatyam dancer, from a hereditary family of performers in Tamil Nadu.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi first introduce a nationwide satyagraha in India?
questions.explanation: The Rowlatt Satyagraha of 1919, against the Rowlatt Act, was Gandhi's first nationwide satyagraha; his earlier ones, at Champaran (1917), Kheda and Ahmedabad (1918), were local.

questions.text: Recommended Dietary Allowances = ?
questions.explanation: Recommended Dietary Allowances are set above the average requirement of each nutrient, with a margin of safety added to cover differences between individuals, so that nearly everyone's needs are met.

questions.text: Which of the following sports was NOT played at the 2020 Summer Olympic Games (played in 2021)?
questions.explanation: Cricket was not on the programme of the Tokyo 2020 Games; shooting, football and hockey were. When the exam was held (July 2022), cricket had been played at the Olympics only once, at Paris in 1900.

questions.text: As of April 2022, amongst others, Legislative Councils are present in the states of _____________.
options: Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Gujarat
questions.explanation: In April 2022 six states had a Legislative Council: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh. None of the states in the other options had one, and Delhi is not a state.

questions.text: Who among the following was the founder of the Shunga Dynasty (185 BC - 73 BC)?
questions.explanation: Pushyamitra Shunga, commander of the last Mauryan king Brihadratha, killed him and founded the Shunga dynasty. Agnimitra was his son, and Vasumitra and Bhagabhadra were later kings of the line.

questions.text: Which famous Indian Kathak dancer received the ‘Padma Vibhushan’ in 1986?
questions.explanation: Pandit Birju Maharaj of the Lucknow gharana of Kathak received the Padma Vibhushan in 1986. Rukmini Devi Arundale is known for Bharatanatyam, Mallika Sarabhai for Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam, and Guru Bipin Singh for Manipuri.

questions.text: The Festival of Salhesh is celebrated in the state of:
questions.explanation: The festival of Raja Salhesh, the folk hero and deity of the Dusadh community, is held in the Mithila region of Bihar, with rituals, songs and dance-drama telling his story.

questions.text: When was the latest census conducted in India?
questions.explanation: When the exam was held (July 2022) the latest census was that of 2011; the census due in 2021 had been postponed because of the Covid-19 pandemic.

questions.text: Which of the following neighbours of India has the highest population density?
questions.explanation: Bangladesh, with more than 1,100 people per square kilometre, is among the most densely populated countries in the world, several times denser than Sri Lanka, Pakistan or China.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. My son turned a year older on his birthday recently ______ March 14.
questions.explanation: Dates take 'on': 'on March 14'. 'In' goes with months and years, and 'at' with clock times.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. If you want to help bees, make sure your family don’t use pesticides in your yard.
options: If you want to help bees,
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'make sure your family don't': taken as one household, 'family' takes a singular verb, 'make sure your family doesn't use pesticides'. British usage also allows a plural verb with a collective noun, but the exam follows the singular rule.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He didn't tell me anything ______ that he needed some money.
questions.explanation: 'Except' means apart from: he told me nothing apart from the fact that he needed money. 'Despite' and 'in spite (of)' show contrast, and 'though' joins two clauses.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The study of human mind and behaviour
questions.explanation: Psychology is the study of the human mind and behaviour. Paediatrics is the branch of medicine that deals with children, physiology the study of how the body works, and botany the study of plants.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'library'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Water and minerals “presented to the soil” are absorbed by the roots..
questions.explanation: The adjective 'present' means existing in a place: water and minerals 'present in the soil'. 'Presented to' means formally given to, which does not fit.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who studies insect life
questions.explanation: An entomologist studies insects. A cardiologist treats diseases of the heart, and a naturalist studies nature in general.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Give yourself a ______ and get some rest.
questions.explanation: A 'break' is a short rest: 'give yourself a break'. A 'brake' is a device for slowing a vehicle; the two words sound alike.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. “Keep an eye on” your sister as she might run away.
questions.explanation: To 'keep an eye on' someone is to watch them carefully.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Definite
questions.explanation: 'Definite' means clear and exact: 'precise'. 'General' is nearly its opposite, and 'ample' means more than enough.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The commander abjured his ______to the king.
questions.explanation: To 'abjure' is to renounce solemnly, and what one owes a king is 'allegiance', loyalty: the commander renounced his allegiance to the king.

questions.text: Select the option that corrects the misspelt words in the given sentence. There is a feling of hopelesness among the youth.
options: There is a feeling of hoplesnes among the youth
There is a fealing of hopelesnes among the youth.
There is a feling of hopelesness among the youth.
There is a feeling of hopelessness among the youth.
questions.explanation: 'Feeling' has a double 'e', and 'hopelessness' is 'hope' + 'less' + 'ness', with a double 's' twice.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. All these rules seem to be “irrelevant.”
questions.explanation: 'Irrelevant' means unconnected with the matter or unimportant; of the options, its opposite is 'meaningful'. 'Incidental' is close to it in sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Mr. Pearson interrupted their harmless ______ and reminded them of the seriousness of the situation.
questions.explanation: 'Chatter' is light, idle talk, which suits 'harmless' and contrasts with the seriousness of the situation. 'Guile' is cunning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Impressive
questions.explanation: 'Impressive' means striking or remarkable; its opposite is 'ordinary'. 'Dramatic' and 'significant' are close to it in sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. No spring chicken
options: A person who is no longer young
questions.explanation: 'No spring chicken' describes a person who is no longer young.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The last time this competition was held at 2017.
questions.explanation: Years take 'in', not 'at': 'held in 2017'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Proficient
questions.explanation: 'Proficient' means highly skilled: 'accomplished'. 'Dominant' means most powerful, and 'modest' and 'predictable' are unrelated.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. In the past, (he spent many an hours playing the harp across the) 5th Ave.
options: he spent many an hour playing the harp across the
he spent much hours playing the harp across the
he had spent many an hours playing the harp across the
questions.explanation: 'Many a' (or 'many an') takes a singular noun: 'many an hour'. 'Much' goes with uncountable nouns, and 'hours' is countable.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. A part of me don’t wanted you to go to the party.
questions.explanation: After 'do' the verb stays in its base form, and the past takes 'did': 'A part of me didn't want you to go to the party.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Starting and (1) ______ a positive daily morning routine is an investment and a way to do your best work every day. It also gives you structure, building forward-moving habits and creating momentum for the rest of the day. It helps you to (2) ______ priorities, limit procrastination, keep track of your goals. Your brain is at its (3) ______ in the morning. And you can get your best work and tasks done without struggle. But distractions can get the best of us. You get distracted and procrastinate. You make plans the previous day to get your most (4) ______ task done first thing in the morning, but you don't follow through on them. You are able to get things (5) ______ but not the right things.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The blank pairs with the gerund 'starting', so it too must be an -ing form: 'Starting and maintaining a positive daily morning routine'.

You are able to get things (5) ______ but not the right things.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Helps you to' is followed by the base form, as are 'limit' and 'keep' later in the list: 'establish priorities'.

You are able to get things (5) ______ but not the right things.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: To be 'at its peak' is to be at its best. A 'peek' is a quick look and 'pique' a feeling of irritation.

questions.explanation: An adjective is needed before 'task': 'your most important task'.

questions.explanation: 'Get things done' takes the past participle after 'get' and its object, meaning to have them completed.

questions.text: Marks obtained by the seven students of a tuition class, P, Q, R, S, T, U and V, are mentioned. P scored second highest marks in the class. Marks scored by V were more than only one of the persons. S's score was more than T but less than P. Three people got higher than T and three got lesser than T. Neither R nor Q received the lowest marks. Given that no two students have the same marks, whose marks were the lowest?
questions.explanation: Three score above T and three below, so T is fourth; V, above only one person, is sixth; P is second, and S, between T and P, third. Q, R and U take first, fifth and seventh, and as neither Q nor R is last, U has the lowest marks.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. All X are A. II. Some R are X. Conclusions: I. Some A are R. II. All R are A.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: Some R are X and every X is an A, so those R are A: some A are R (I). The R that are not X may lie outside A, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some pillows are covers. All bedsheets are covers. Conclusions: I. All covers are bedsheets. II. Some pillows are bedsheets.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follow.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: All bedsheets are covers, but there may be covers that are not bedsheets, so I does not follow. Pillows and bedsheets are each linked only to covers and need not overlap, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. CAT : FFA :: ANT : DSA :: SUN : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +3, +5 and +7, wrapping round after Z: C → F, A → F, T → A and A → D, N → S, T → A. So S → V, U → Z and N → U: VZU.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. PRM : INL :: AJK : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places back and the cluster is reversed: PRM → LNI → INL. Likewise AJK → WFG (A wraps round to W) → GFW.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'TALENT' is written as 'VXNBPQ', and 'HORDIN' is written as 'JLTAKK'. How will 'AKRPQB' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +2 and −3 in turn, wrapping round the alphabet: TALENT → VXNBPQ and HORDIN → JLTAKK. So AKRPQB → CHTMSY.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. ABROAD : RBADAO :: DEMAND : MEDDNA :: HONEST : ?
questions.explanation: The first and third letters swap places, and so do the fourth and sixth: ABROAD → RBADAO and DEMAND → MEDDNA. So HONEST → NOHTSE.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 121 : 145 :: 169 : 197 :: 256 : ?
questions.explanation: Each first number is a square, and its pair is the next square plus 1: 11² → 12² + 1 = 145 and 13² → 14² + 1 = 197. So 16² → 17² + 1 = 290.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 10 + 2 × 12 ÷ 6 − 4 = 16
questions.explanation: After interchanging 2 and 4: 10 + 4 × 12 ÷ 6 − 2 = 10 + 8 − 2 = 16.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 503, 509, 521, 539, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 6, 12, 18 and 24: 539 + 24 = 563.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 75 : 63 :: 189 : 171 :: 55 : ?
questions.explanation: Each number minus the sum of its digits gives its pair: 75 − 12 = 63 and 189 − 18 = 171. So 55 − 10 = 45.

questions.text: Select the option in which the two numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers in the given number pair. 135 : 27
questions.explanation: The first number is 5 times the second: 135 = 5 × 27, and likewise 625 = 5 × 125.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'They play Football' is written as 'po la ta', 'They like playing' is written as 'la to zu', 'Football is best game' is written as 'xu po ba cu'.How will ‘Football’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: 'Football' is in the first and third sentences, and the only code they share is 'po'.

questions.text: A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H are sitting around a square table facing the centre of the table. Some of them are sitting at the corners while some are sitting at the exact centre of the sides. F sits third to the left of H. F sits at one of the corners. C sits second to the right of G. G does not sit at any of the corners. G is not an immediate neighbour of F. A is an immediate neighbour of B. A does not sit in any of the middles of the sides. Only three people sit between A and D. Who sits second to the left of D?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left is the next seat clockwise. Numbering the seats clockwise from F's corner as 0, H is at 5 (F is third to H's left), G, in a middle seat not next to F, at 3, and C, second to G's right, at 1. A and D sit at the opposite corners 2 and 6; A needs a free neighbour for B, so A is at 6 with B at 7, D is at 2 and E at 4, second to the left of D.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'ENJOY' is coded as '25' and 'DOCTOR' is coded as '36'. How will 'MILLION' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded as the square of its number of letters: ENJOY has 5 (5² = 25) and DOCTOR 6 (6² = 36). MILLION has 7: 7² = 49.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘×’ and ‘ – ‘ are interchanged and also ‘+’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 10 × 4 + 2 − 5 ÷ 4 = ?
questions.explanation: After the interchanges: 10 − 4 ÷ 2 × 5 + 4 = 10 − 10 + 4 = 4.

questions.text: Five people A, B, C, D and E are sitting in a straight row facing North. E is sitting immediately next to D, C is sitting immediately next to B, and B is not sitting with A who is on the left end of the bench. C is in the second position from the right. E is to the right of D and A. E and C are sitting together. What is the position of E?
options: Immediate neighbour of both A and B
Immediate neighbour of both C and A
Immediate neighbour of both D and B
Immediate neighbour of both D and C
questions.explanation: A is at the left end and C second from the right. E sits next to C, with D immediately on E's left, so E cannot be at the right end (D would need C's seat): E is in the middle, D second from the left and B at the right end. The row is A, D, E, C, B, so E's neighbours are D and C.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'GROW' is written as 'RGWO', 'PINK' is written as 'IPKN'. How will 'HALD' be written in that code language?
questions.explanation: Each pair of letters is swapped: GR OW → RG WO and PI NK → IP KN. So HA LD → AH DL: AHDL.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.BY, ?, DW, EV, FU
questions.explanation: The first letters run B, C, D, E, F and the second Y, X, W, V, U: CX.

questions.text: The breaking up of the rocks on the earth’s surface is called ______.
questions.explanation: Weathering is the breaking down of rocks in place at the earth's surface by physical, chemical and biological processes. A conurbation is a merged urban area, and desertification the spread of desert conditions.

questions.text: The foundation stone of 'Banas Dairy Sankul' scheme in Uttar Pradesh was laid by ______.
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone of the Banas Dairy Sankul, a milk processing plant at Karkhiyaon in Varanasi, on 23 December 2021.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: Fiat money is issued without any backing of an equivalent amount of gold or silver.
Money Multiplier is the ratio of money supply to the reserve money.
In Time Deposits, money can be withdrawn only after maturity or with a penalty before maturity.
Vault cash is also a part of the money supply.
questions.explanation: Money supply counts the currency held by the public and deposits, not the cash that banks keep in their own vaults; vault cash is part of reserve money (high powered money) instead. The other three statements are correct.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: Metals react with oxygen to form basic oxides.
Non-metals do not produce any sound.
questions.explanation: Non-metals are generally brittle, not malleable: solid non-metals such as sulphur break when hammered. Metals form basic oxides, ring when struck where non-metals do not, and lose electrons easily (low ionisation enthalpy).

questions.text: Which of the following dance forms is performed by devotees during the ceremonial worship of Murugan, the Tamil God of War?
questions.explanation: Kavadi Aattam is the ceremonial offering in which devotees of Murugan dance carrying a kavadi, a decorated arch borne on the shoulders. Mayilattam, the peacock dance, is also performed in Murugan temples, but by trained dancers rather than as the devotees' own offering.

questions.text: Who among the following administers the union territories of India?
questions.explanation: Under Article 239 every union territory is administered by the President, acting through an administrator he or she appoints.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following formed the Tattvabodhini Sabha in 1839?
questions.explanation: Debendranath Tagore founded the Tattvabodhini Sabha in Calcutta in 1839 to spread Rammohun Roy's ideas; he later led the Brahmo Samaj.

questions.text: Who among the following was given the title of ‘Uttarapatha Swamin’?
questions.explanation: The Pala king Dharmapala, who placed his nominee Chakrayudha on the throne of Kannauj, is called 'Uttarapathasvamin', lord of the north, by the Gujarati poet Soddhala.

questions.text: Pandit Ravi Shankar is famous for playing which of the following instruments?
questions.explanation: Pandit Ravi Shankar was a sitar player who took Indian classical music to audiences around the world; he received the Bharat Ratna in 1999.

questions.text: Who among the following dancers was the first Odissi dancer of foreign origin to be conferred the Padma Shri in 2006?
questions.explanation: Ileana Citaristi, born in Italy and based in Bhubaneswar, an Odissi and Chhau dancer, received the Padma Shri in 2006.

questions.text: Ocean acidification is the ongoing decrease in the pH of the Earth’s oceans, caused by the uptake of ______________ from the atmosphere.
questions.explanation: Sea water absorbs carbon dioxide from the air, forming carbonic acid, which lowers its pH.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which Act was passed in 1929 prohibiting marriage of girls below 14 and boys below 18 years of age?
questions.explanation: The Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929, known as the Sarda (Sharda) Act after Har Bilas Sarda, who moved it, fixed the minimum age of marriage at 14 for girls and 18 for boys.

questions.text: Vinegar used in cooking contains which of the following compounds?
questions.explanation: Vinegar is a dilute solution, about 5-8 per cent, of acetic (ethanoic) acid in water.

questions.text: With respect to communication, ‘Doordarshan’ in India is a _______.
questions.explanation: Doordarshan is India's public service television broadcaster, part of Prasar Bharati; All India Radio (Akashvani) is the national radio service.

questions.text: How many medals in total did India win at the Summer Olympics 2020 (played in 2021)?
questions.explanation: At the Tokyo 2020 Olympics, held in 2021, India won 7 medals: 1 gold (Neeraj Chopra in the javelin), 2 silver and 4 bronze.

questions.text: Article 23 and Article 24 of the Indian Constitution deal with which of the following Fundamental Right?
questions.explanation: Articles 23 and 24 form the Right against Exploitation: Article 23 bans human trafficking and forced labour, and Article 24 bans employing children below 14 in factories, mines and other hazardous work.

questions.text: Who among the following authors wrote 'Train to Pakistan'?
questions.explanation: 'Train to Pakistan' (1956), a novel about the Partition, is by Khushwant Singh.

questions.text: Kumarakom boat race is the most admired boat race to take place on the Vembanad Lake in September during the ______ festival.
questions.explanation: The Kumarakom boat race, also called the Sree Narayana Jayanthi boat race, is held on Vembanad Lake in Kerala in the Onam season.

questions.text: Where does the Alaknanda river join the Bhagirathi river in India?
questions.explanation: The Alaknanda and the Bhagirathi meet at Devprayag in Uttarakhand, and from there the river is called the Ganga.

questions.text: Ain-i-Akbari which is the third volume of the book ‘Akbar Nama’ deals with ______.
questions.explanation: The Ain-i-Akbari, the third volume of Abul Fazl's Akbarnama, describes Akbar's administration: his court, army, revenue system and provinces. The first two volumes cover his ancestors and the events of his reign.

questions.text: The Indian cricket team won the final match of the 2011 ICC ODI Cricket World Cup Championship by defeating the team from which country?
questions.explanation: India beat Sri Lanka by six wickets in the final at the Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai, on 2 April 2011.

questions.text: Sanjiv Kapoor has been appointed as the new Chief Executive Officer of _____________. His appointment will be effective from 4 April 2022.
questions.explanation: Sanjiv Kapoor, formerly of Vistara and SpiceJet, was named chief executive of Jet Airways by its new owners, the Jalan-Kalrock consortium, in March 2022, with effect from 4 April 2022.

questions.text: India shares its land boundary with ______ in the north-west.
questions.explanation: Pakistan and Afghanistan are India's land neighbours in the north-west. Bhutan lies to the north-east, and Bangladesh and Myanmar to the east.

questions.text: As per Census 2011, which of the following was the most literate state of India?
questions.explanation: Kerala had the highest literacy rate of any state in the 2011 Census, about 94 per cent; Bihar had the lowest.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Flared
questions.explanation: 'Flared' means blazed up brightly, so its opposite is 'darkened'. 'Radiated', 'flamed' and 'glared' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Impolite
questions.explanation: 'Impolite' means rude; its opposite is 'courteous'. 'Uncivil' and 'blunt' are close to it in meaning.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Of or relating to the moon
questions.explanation: 'Lunar' means of or relating to the moon. 'Solar' relates to the sun, 'platonic' describes a friendship without romance, and 'fatal' means causing death.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. A clinical thermometer “consists of a” long, narrow, uniform glass tube.
questions.explanation: A general fact takes the simple present, and the singular subject 'a clinical thermometer' takes 'consists': the sentence is already correct.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Move the goalposts
options: Unfairly alter the conditions or rules of a procedure during its course
To do your research and understand clearly what your goals are
To put a lot of effort into something
To move the goalpost after an attempt has been made to score a goal
questions.explanation: To 'move the goalposts' is to change the rules or conditions of something unfairly while it is under way.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. I have watched a lot of students excel in online courses, taking fully advantage of the convenience.
options: excel in online courses, taking fully
I have watched a lot of students
questions.explanation: 'Advantage' is a noun, so it needs the adjective 'full', not the adverb 'fully': 'taking full advantage of the convenience'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. Stop “crying for the moon” and start coming up with some sensible demands.
options: To make an impractical or unreasonable request
questions.explanation: To 'cry for the moon' is to ask for something impossible or unreasonable.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Artful
questions.explanation: 'Artful' means clever in a cunning way: 'crafty'. 'Prudent' means careful, 'benign' kindly and 'ignorant' lacking knowledge.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Age doesn’t seeming to diminish our capacity to speak, write and learn new things.
questions.explanation: After the auxiliary 'doesn't' the verb takes its base form: 'Age doesn't seem to diminish our capacity...'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Fasting ______ some festivals increases the consumption of fruits.
questions.explanation: 'During' is the preposition for something that happens in the course of an event: 'fasting during some festivals'. 'While' and 'when' are conjunctions that need a clause after them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Da Vinci's paintings reveal an obsessive fascination with ______ rituals, like those of the Freemasons.
questions.explanation: 'Enigmatic' means mysterious, which suits secretive rituals like those of the Freemasons. 'Magnetic', 'pathetic' and 'static' do not fit the sense.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Sometimes we interact to people who are closed-minded and not willing to listen.
questions.explanation: 'Interact' takes 'with', not 'to': 'Sometimes we interact with people who are closed-minded'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A system of government by the wealthy class
questions.explanation: Plutocracy is government by the wealthy. Theocracy is rule by religious leaders, autocracy by one person with absolute power, and democracy by the people.

questions.text: Select the option that corrects the misspelt words in the given sentence. My freind is blessed with perfect gines.
options: My friend is blessed with perfct gines.
My freind is bllessed with perfct gines.
My freind is blesed with perfect genes.
My friend is blessed with perfect genes.
questions.explanation: The correct spellings are 'friend' and 'genes' (the units of heredity); only the last option has both, with 'blessed' and 'perfect' also spelt right.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'television'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. Antibiotics “are one off the” most commonly prescribed drugs in the world.
questions.explanation: 'Off' should be 'of': 'one of the' goes before a superlative and a plural noun, and the plural subject 'antibiotics' keeps 'are'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. She refused to back ______, so she was fired from the company.
questions.explanation: To 'back down' is to give up a demand or position: she would not give way, so she was fired.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. You “is not allowed” to sit here without permission.
questions.explanation: 'You' always takes the plural verb form 'are': 'You are not allowed to sit here without permission.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Tenderness
questions.explanation: 'Tenderness' is gentleness and care: 'kindness'. 'Ruthlessness', 'severity' and 'spitefulness' are nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) ______ the idea of ‘tipping points’ two decades ago.
questions.explanation: An idea is 'introduced' when it is first put forward, and the simple past suits 'two decades ago'. 'Withdrawn' would need 'had', and 'shortened' and 'wounded' do not fit an idea.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Delhi’s meteorology (1) ______ the quantity of chaff burnt play a greater role in (2) ______ air quality than the time chosen by farmers in Punjab to start crop burning, a study argues. Crop burning, a traditional practice in Punjab and Haryana of (3) ______ fields off rice chaff to prepare for winter sowing, begins around October and (4) ______ in November, coinciding with the (5) ______ of southwest monsoon.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'And' joins the two subjects, Delhi's meteorology and the quantity of chaff burnt, which is why the verb is the plural 'play'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Delhi’s meteorology (1) ______ the quantity of chaff burnt play a greater role in (2) ______ air quality than the time chosen by farmers in Punjab to start crop burning, a study argues. Crop burning, a traditional practice in Punjab and Haryana of (3) ______ fields off rice chaff to prepare for winter sowing, begins around October and (4) ______ in November, coinciding with the (5) ______ of southwest monsoon.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: A preposition ('in') is followed by the '-ing' form: a role 'in worsening air quality'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Delhi’s meteorology (1) ______ the quantity of chaff burnt play a greater role in (2) ______ air quality than the time chosen by farmers in Punjab to start crop burning, a study argues. Crop burning, a traditional practice in Punjab and Haryana of (3) ______ fields off rice chaff to prepare for winter sowing, begins around October and (4) ______ in November, coinciding with the (5) ______ of southwest monsoon.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'razing'. To raze is to level something or scrape it bare, as burning clears the fields of rice chaff; 'racing', 'raising' and 'rising' make no sense here.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Delhi’s meteorology (1) ______ the quantity of chaff burnt play a greater role in (2) ______ air quality than the time chosen by farmers in Punjab to start crop burning, a study argues. Crop burning, a traditional practice in Punjab and Haryana of (3) ______ fields off rice chaff to prepare for winter sowing, begins around October and (4) ______ in November, coinciding with the (5) ______ of southwest monsoon.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: Crop burning begins in October and 'peaks', reaches its highest point, in November.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Delhi’s meteorology (1) ______ the quantity of chaff burnt play a greater role in (2) ______ air quality than the time chosen by farmers in Punjab to start crop burning, a study argues. Crop burning, a traditional practice in Punjab and Haryana of (3) ______ fields off rice chaff to prepare for winter sowing, begins around October and (4) ______ in November, coinciding with the (5) ______ of southwest monsoon.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: The burning season coincides with the 'withdrawal', or retreat, of the southwest monsoon in October and November; the blank after 'the' needs a noun.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'O' is coded as '15' and 'ADD' is coded as '9'. How will 'PURE' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is coded as the sum of its letters' places in the alphabet: O = 15 and ADD = 1 + 4 + 4 = 9. So PURE = 16 + 21 + 18 + 5 = 60.

questions.text: P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are seven friends who scored different marks in a test. Scores of only two people lies between the scores of S and P with score of P greater than S. . R scored the highest marks. T scored more than Q. U and V scored second least and the least marks respectively. Who scored the fourth highest marks?
questions.explanation: R is first, U sixth and V seventh. With exactly two people between S and P, and P higher, P must be second and S fifth. T and Q take third and fourth, with T above Q, so Q is fourth.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number. 2041 : 346 :: 5310 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the cube of the first number's digit sum, plus 3: 2 + 0 + 4 + 1 = 7 and 7³ + 3 = 346. So 5 + 3 + 1 + 0 = 9 and 9³ + 3 = 732.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. WUE, XXG, YAI, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move +1 (W, X, Y, Z), the second +3 (U, X, A, D) and the third +2 (E, G, I, K): ZDK.

questions.text: Select the number that will come next in the following series. 2, 4, 7, 11, 16, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 2, 3, 4, 5, rising by 1, so the next term is 16 + 6 = 22.

questions.text: Select the option in which the words share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of words. Money : Wallet
questions.explanation: Money is kept in a wallet, as a letter is kept in an envelope (printed 'Envelop'). A locker keeps things safe, but safety is not kept in it.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All bottles are jugs. All jugs are cups. Conclusions: I. All bottles are cups. II. All cups are bottles.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: All bottles are jugs and all jugs are cups, so all bottles are cups (I follows). There may be cups that are not bottles, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Which of the number (not digits) should be interchanged in the given equation to make it mathematically correct? 12 ÷ 3 − 2 + 5 × 4 = 23
questions.explanation: Interchanging 3 and 2: 12 ÷ 2 − 3 + 5 × 4 = 6 − 3 + 20 = 23.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some belts are leathers. All leathers are skins. Some skins are white. Conclusions: I. Some belts are skins. II. Some belts are white.
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Some belts are leathers and all leathers are skins, so some belts are skins (I follows). The white skins need not include any belts, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) 2 : 16 :: 3 : 81 :: 6 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second number is the first raised to the fourth power: 2⁴ = 16 and 3⁴ = 81. So 6⁴ = 1296.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'ABKN' is coded as '84', and 'PNCL' is coded as '135'. How will 'HONT' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each code is 3 times the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet: ABKN → (1 + 2 + 11 + 14) × 3 = 84 and PNCL → (16 + 14 + 3 + 12) × 3 = 135. So HONT → (8 + 15 + 14 + 20) × 3 = 57 × 3 = 171.

questions.text: Six girls are sitting in two straight rows, facing the North. Their names are Farah, Urvashi, Yukti, Kritika, Neha and Mudita. Farah and Mudita are sitting diagonally opposite. Urvashi is in the top row and to the immediate right of Farah. Kritika is second to the left of Mudita while Yukti and Kritika are not in the same row. Who is sitting diagonally opposite to Yukti?
questions.explanation: Urvashi and Farah are in the top row, so Mudita, diagonally opposite Farah, is in the bottom row with Kritika (second to her left), and Yukti is in the top row. In rows of three, Kritika and Mudita take the bottom row's left and right ends, Farah (diagonal to Mudita) the top left, Urvashi the top middle and Yukti the top right, diagonally opposite Kritika.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. SACRIFY : ARFYICS :: NUMERAL : UEALRMN :: SHALLOW : ?
questions.explanation: The letters in places 2, 4 and 6 come first, then those in places 7, 5, 3 and 1: SACRIFY → A R F, Y I C S. So SHALLOW → H L O, W L A S: HLOWLAS.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘×’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and also ‘+’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 60 + 2 − 3 × 4 ÷ 2 = ?

Six friends are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. Dilip is immediate neighbour of both Priya and Payal. Priti is immediate neighbour of both Mukesh and Leela. Payal is sitting to the immediate right of Mukesh. Who is sitting to the immediate right of Priya?
questions.explanation: Dilip sits between Priya and Payal and Priti between Mukesh and Leela. Facing the centre, a person's immediate right is the next seat anticlockwise, and Payal is on Mukesh's right, so anticlockwise the order is Mukesh, Payal, Dilip, Priya, Leela, Priti. Leela comes next after Priya, on her immediate right.

questions.text: In a certain code language, '456' is written as 'sky is high', '678' is written as 'sky has dark', and '147' is written as 'star is dark'. What is the code for the word 'star' in that language?
questions.explanation: 'Sky' (6) is common to the first two, 'dark' (7) to the last two and 'is' (4) to the first and third, so in '147' the remaining code, 1, stands for 'star'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. CAM : EES :: OAT : QEZ :: TOI : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +2, +4 and +6: C → E, A → E, M → S and O → Q, A → E, T → Z. So T → V, O → S, I → O: VSO.

questions.text: If ORDER = $*5@* and MATTER = 2&33@*, then ROAD = ?
questions.explanation: Letter by letter, ORDER gives O = $, R = * and D = 5, and MATTER gives A = &. So ROAD = * $ & 5.

questions.text: Select the option that will replace the question mark (?) in the given series. 78, 89, 82, 87, 84, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are +11, −7, +5, −3: the prime numbers in falling order, with alternating signs. The next is +2: 84 + 2 = 86.

questions.text: Who will be India’s next Foreign Secretary as announced in April 2022?
questions.explanation: Vinay Mohan Kwatra, then India's ambassador to Nepal, was named the next Foreign Secretary in April 2022 and took charge on 1 May 2022, succeeding Harsh Vardhan Shringla.

questions.text: Which of the following is the least literate state in India according to Census 2021?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Bihar. No census was taken in 2021 (it was postponed), so the question rests on Census 2011, in which Bihar had the lowest literacy rate of any state, 61.8%; Gujarat, Assam and Odisha were all above 72%.

questions.text: ‘Gangaur’ is an Indian festival majorly celebrated in ________.
questions.explanation: Gangaur, in honour of the goddess Gauri (Parvati), is one of Rajasthan's main festivals, celebrated chiefly by women in the month of Chaitra.

questions.text: Which of the following is categorised under slow mass movement in geomorphic processes?
questions.explanation: Creep, the very slow downslope movement of soil, is a slow mass movement, as is solifluction. Earthflows, mudflows and landslides are rapid movements.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Prarthana Samaj or ‘Prayer Society’, a religious and social reform, was found in 1863 at _________.
questions.explanation: Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj in Bombay, with M. G. Ranade and R. G. Bhandarkar among its leaders. The year usually given is 1867, not the 1863 in the question.

questions.text: National Sports Day of India is celebrated on _____________.
questions.explanation: India's National Sports Day, 29 August, marks the birthday of the hockey player Major Dhyan Chand.

questions.text: Who among the following was a Shaka ruler in India (130-150 AD)?
questions.explanation: Rudradaman I, the Shaka (Western Kshatrapa) ruler of about 130-150 AD, is known from his Junagadh rock inscription. Ashoka and Bindusara were Mauryas and Menander an Indo-Greek king.

questions.text: Which part of the Indian Constitution has been drawn from the British Constitution?
options: Fundamental Rights and the Directive Principles of State Policy
Principle of Cabinet Government and the relations between the executive and the legislature
Appointment of state governors by the centre
questions.explanation: Parliamentary (cabinet) government, with the executive answerable to the legislature, came from Britain. Fundamental Rights came from the US Constitution, the Directive Principles from Ireland's, and a federation with a strong centre and governors appointed by the centre from Canada's.

questions.text: According to the Census 2011, which of the following is the third-lowest state in terms of literacy rate?
questions.explanation: In Census 2011 the lowest literacy rates among the states were Bihar's (61.8%), Arunachal Pradesh's (65.4%) and Rajasthan's (66.1%). Madhya Pradesh had 69.3% and Sikkim 81.4%.

questions.text: _______ is a disease which is transmitted by the Aedes mosquito which lays eggs in water-logged places and multiply over time.
questions.explanation: Dengue is spread by the Aedes mosquito, which breeds in stagnant water. Malaria is spread by the Anopheles mosquito, elephantiasis by Culex mosquitoes, and diarrhoea mostly through contaminated food and water.

questions.text: Which type of forest receives more than 200 cm of annual rainfall?
questions.explanation: Tropical evergreen rain forests grow where the annual rainfall is over 200 cm. Temperate mixed forests, the taiga and the tundra get far less.

questions.text: What was the shape of the Great Bath of Mohenjo Daro?
questions.explanation: The Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro is a rectangular tank about 12 m long, 7 m wide and 2.4 m deep, with steps at each end.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: BR Ambedkar wrote a 20-page autobiography about his experiences with untouchability which is known as ____________.
questions.explanation: 'Waiting for a Visa', written in 1935-36, is B. R. Ambedkar's short autobiographical account of the untouchability he faced. 'Courage and Conviction' is General V. K. Singh's autobiography.

questions.text: Kelucharan Mohapatra is associated with _________ dance form of India.
questions.explanation: Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra was a leading Odissi dancer and teacher, who did much to revive the form.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who was the founder of the reform movement, Arya Samaj?
questions.explanation: Swami Dayananda Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in Bombay in 1875. Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj, and M. G. Ranade was a leader of the Prarthana Samaj.

questions.text: What does F stand for in the FRBM Act, 2003 of the Indian economy?
questions.explanation: FRBM stands for Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management; the Act set targets for cutting the government's fiscal and revenue deficits.

questions.text: Which of the following laws is applicable to the force of attraction or repulsion between two point charges?
questions.explanation: Coulomb's law gives the force between two point charges: it is proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of Phylum Annelida of Animal Kingdom?
questions.explanation: Annelids are segmented worms, such as the earthworm and the leech. The honey bee is an arthropod, the squid a mollusc and the kangaroo a chordate (a mammal).

questions.text: Which state government launched the Udaan Project in collaboration with IPE Global which attempts to keep girls in schools through their enrolment at the secondary level while ensuring that the eligible ones among them get their scholarships?
questions.explanation: Udaan is run in Rajasthan by the development consultancy IPE Global with the state government: it helps girls in classes 9 and 10 stay in school and get the government pre-matric scholarships they are eligible for, and also works against child marriage and teenage pregnancy.

questions.text: The World Health Organisation defines adolescents as individuals in the age-group of ______.
questions.explanation: The World Health Organisation defines adolescents as people aged 10 to 19 years.

questions.text: Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma is associated with __________ musical instrument.
questions.explanation: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma made the santoor, a hammered dulcimer from Jammu and Kashmir, a concert instrument of Hindustani classical music.

questions.text: Who is the first Law officer of India?
questions.explanation: Under Article 76 the Attorney-General for India is the country's highest law officer, who advises the Government of India on legal matters.

questions.text: Who among the following rulers was chronicled by Minhaj-i Siraj?
questions.explanation: Minhaj-i Siraj, author of the 'Tabaqat-i Nasiri', chronicled the Delhi Sultanate of his time, including the reign of Razia Sultan (1236-1240). Babur wrote his own memoirs, Abul Fazl chronicled Akbar's reign, and Ghiyasuddin Tughluq ruled (1320-1325) long after Minhaj's time.

questions.text: For which dance form did Aparna Satheesan win the Prestigious National Nritya Shiromani Award 2022?
questions.explanation: Aparna Satheesan, a Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam dancer, was chosen for the National Nritya Shiromani Award 2022 for her contribution to Kuchipudi; it was announced in December 2021 for presentation at the 13th Cuttack Mahotsav in Odisha in January 2022.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Bulky
questions.explanation: 'Bulky' means large and heavy, taking up a lot of space: 'massive'. 'Scanty' and 'airy' point the other way.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. “Hardly had he disappeared that her mother” clomped down the steps, looking for him.
options: Hardly did he disappeared that her mother
Hardly had he disappear that her mother
Hardly had he disappeared when her mother
questions.explanation: 'Hardly' is followed by 'when', not 'that': 'Hardly had he disappeared when her mother clomped down the steps'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. My friend is not ______ for this complicated assignment.
questions.explanation: To be 'suitable for' a task is to be right for it. 'Worthy' takes 'of' and 'entitled' takes 'to', and one is 'comfortable with' a task rather than 'for' it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. But if you ______ to spare before you do catch the bus, be sure to pop in.
questions.explanation: To 'have a moment to spare' is to have a little free time: if there is time before the bus, the listener should drop in.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. Michael nodded and “begun writing at” his pad.
questions.explanation: The second verb must be simple past like 'nodded': 'began' ('begun' is the past participle). One writes 'on' a pad: 'began writing on his pad'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Just try and recall the poor people you “saw on the” streets, on local trains, and in slums on our way back.
questions.explanation: The simple past 'saw' is right for people seen on a past occasion ('on our way back'), so no substitution is needed. 'Seen' alone needs a helping verb, and 'have seeing' is not a verb form.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. An unidentified man on “an bike dropped for” the box outside the building.
questions.explanation: 'Bike' begins with a consonant sound, so it takes 'a', and to 'drop off' something is to leave it somewhere: 'a bike dropped off the box'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Maestro
questions.explanation: A 'maestro' is a master of an art, especially music, a person of outstanding skill: 'genius'. 'Novice', a beginner, is nearly its opposite.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. My mother exclaimed / at how fast / the days had pass.
questions.explanation: After 'had' the past participle is needed: 'the days had passed'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To raise a dust
options: To be satisfied with what you have achieved
To be secretly or inwardly amused
questions.explanation: To 'raise a dust' is to cause a disturbance or confusion, stirring things up as a cloud of dust would.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. “She had no sooner taken a few steps forward that” she suddenly recoiled.
options: No sooner had she taken a few steps forward than
She did no sooner taken a few steps forward than
She did no sooner took a few steps forward than
questions.explanation: 'No sooner' pairs with 'than', not 'that', and when a sentence opens with it the auxiliary comes before the subject: 'No sooner had she taken a few steps forward than she suddenly recoiled.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. One day, the queen was painting when a messenger entered ____________ to convey the king's arrival.
questions.explanation: A messenger hurrying in with news would enter 'breathlessly', out of breath. 'Comparably', 'relatively' and 'enjoyably' make no sense here.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Hundreds of migrants work in private firms in Erode.
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: the plural subject 'Hundreds of migrants' takes the plural verb 'work', and 'in private firms in Erode' is idiomatic.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. “Can all us” sleep in the same room, Mother?
questions.explanation: The subject needs the subject pronoun 'we', not the object pronoun 'us', with 'all' after it: 'Can we all sleep in the same room, Mother?'

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Neither she not I am going to take part in the debate competition.
questions.explanation: 'Neither' pairs with 'nor', not 'not': 'Neither she nor I am going'. ('Am' agrees with 'I', the nearer subject.)

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Fiery' is spelt with the 'e' before the 'r', unlike 'fire'. The others should be 'height', 'believe' and 'foreign'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'solitary', with an 'a'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. You really need to exercise daily, if you want to live a long and ______ life.
questions.explanation: Daily exercise leads to a 'long and healthy life'. Exercise does not make one 'wealthy', and 'marginal' and 'shrieking' make no sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. That lady must “have an axe to grind” that’s why she is not reporting your crime.
questions.explanation: To 'have an axe to grind' is to have a private reason or hidden motive for acting as one does.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Unfeigned
questions.explanation: 'Unfeigned' means genuine or sincere, not pretended, so its opposite is 'pretended'. 'Sincere' and 'genuine' are its synonyms.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. When he died on 27 November 1953, Gladstone O'Neill was (1) ______ recognised as one of the major dramatists of the modern world. Four times a Pulitzer Prize-winner, he had also been (2) ______ the 1936 Nobel Prize for Literature. His plays have been translated into most major languages and read by more people than those of (3) ______ other playwright except W Shakespeare and maybe G Bernard Shaw. O'Neill was a puzzle to his friends – a genuinely shy, brooding, complicated man in whom (4) ______ alternated with touching kindness. He was both, naive and worldly. One biographer found him "sentimental one instant, hard as nails the next." His widow, after 26 years with O'Neill, said, "To (5) ______ his work you must understand the man, for the work and the man are one."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: He was 'universally' recognised, that is by everyone everywhere, as one of the major dramatists of the modern world.

Four times a Pulitzer Prize-winner, he had also been (2) ______ the 1936 Nobel Prize for Literature. His plays have been translated into most major languages and read by more people than those of (3) ______ other playwright except W Shakespeare and maybe G Bernard Shaw. His widow, after 26 years with O'Neill, said, "To (5) ______ his work you must understand the man, for the work and the man are one."

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: A prize is 'awarded' to someone: 'he had also been awarded the 1936 Nobel Prize'.

questions.text: What will be the value of the following expression, if ‘×’ and ‘–’ are interchanged and ‘+’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 200 ÷ 100 × 300 ÷ 200 + 10 − 2 × 40 = ?
Which two numbers need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 27 − 8 × 4 − 3 ÷ 2 = 1
questions.explanation: Interchanging 3 and 4 gives 27 − 8 × 3 − 4 ÷ 2 = 27 − 24 − 2 = 1.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘heart black blue’ is written as ‘8 # ab’, ‘grey are blue’ is written as ‘# pr kt’. How will ‘blue’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: 'Blue' is the only word in both messages and '#' the only code in both, so 'blue' is written as '#'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. TACKLE : TCCMLG :: JACKET : JCCMEV :: NEPTUNE : ?
questions.explanation: The letters in the 2nd, 4th and 6th places move 2 forward and the others stay: TACKLE → TCCMLG and JACKET → JCCMEV. So NEPTUNE → N G P V U P E: NGPVUPE.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers in the given set. (7, 49, 343)
questions.explanation: The set is a number, its square and its cube: 7, 7² = 49, 7³ = 343. Likewise 13, 13² = 169 and 13³ = 2197. (625 is 5⁴, 11³ is 1331 and 3³ is 27.)

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word and the fourth word is related to the third word. Virat Kohli : Cricket :: Saina Nehwal : Badminton :: Viswanathan Anand : ?
questions.explanation: Each player is paired with their sport: Virat Kohli with cricket, Saina Nehwal with badminton and Viswanathan Anand with chess.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. LOB : DQN :: HER : ?
questions.explanation: The cluster is reversed and each letter moved 2 forward: LOB → B O L → DQN. So HER → R E H → TGJ.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 524, 533, 544, 557, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 9, 11, 13, 15, rising by 2: 557 + 15 = 572.

questions.text: The marks of seven students A, B, C, D, E, F and G in a test were given as follows: A's score was exactly between E's and F's scores. B's score was more than only G's score. C's score was immediately more than B's score. F's score was more than E's score and F did not score the highest. Who scored the highest marks in the test?
questions.explanation: B beats only G, so G is last and B sixth, with C just above B. Of D, E, A and F in the top four places, E and A score below F, and F is not the highest, so D scored the highest.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'GRSTB' is written as 'GYXWL', and 'HANDS' is written as 'XISFM'. How will 'MNDET' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each word is reversed and every letter moved 5 forward: GRSTB → B T S R G → GYXWL and HANDS → S D N A H → XISFM. So MNDET → T E D N M → YJISR.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'GEFS' is written as 'HFER' and ‘IBIS’ is written as ‘JCHR’. How will 'STIR' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first two letters move 1 forward and the last two 1 back: GEFS → HFER and IBIS → JCHR. So STIR → TUHQ.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. Some M are Q. II. All V are Q. Conclusions: I. Some Q are M. II. No M is V.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: 'Some M are Q' converts to 'some Q are M' (I). Nothing links M to V, so II need not follow.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All hexagons are pentagons. All pentagons are octagons. All octagons are decagons. Conclusions: I. All decagons are hexagons. II. All hexagons are octagons.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: All hexagons are pentagons and all pentagons are octagons, so all hexagons are octagons (II). I reverses the 'all' statements, which does not follow.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 28, 27, 31, 22, 38, 13, 49, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are −1, +4, −9, +16, −25, +36: the squares 1² to 6² with alternating signs. The next is −7² = −49, and 49 − 49 = 0.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'ACQUIRE' is written as 'QCAUERI', 'ADDRESS' is written as 'DDARSSE', and 'ABILITY' is written as 'IBALYTI'. How will 'ICEBERG' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The first three letters and the last three are each reversed and the middle letter stays: ACQ U IRE → QCA U ERI. So ICE B ERG → ECI B GRE: ECIBGRE.
