questions.text: Five friends N, M, O, P and Q are sitting in a column facing east (but not necessarily in the same order) . O is sitting to the leftmost side. N is the immediate neighbour of M and Q. P is not sitting on any of the end seats. Who is the immediate neighbour of O?
questions.explanation: O sits at one end. M, N and Q sit together with N in the middle, and P is in neither end seat, so P must sit next to O, with M, N and Q filling the other end.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. AEI, EIO, IOU, ?
questions.explanation: Each cluster is three vowels in order, starting one vowel later each time and wrapping round from U to A: AEI, EIO, IOU, OUA.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 3 : 72 :: 21 : 504 :: 36 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second number is 24 times the first: 3 × 24 = 72 and 21 × 24 = 504. So 36 × 24 = 864.

questions.text: Seven boys B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6 and B7 are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). B1 is third to the left of B7. B4 is to immediate left of B1. B2 is second to the left of B6. B6 is not an immediate neighbour of B5. Who are the immediate neighbours of B3?
questions.explanation: Going round to the left from B7 the seats are B7, B2, B5, B1, B4, B3, B6: B1 is third to B7's left, B4 just left of B1, B2 second to B6's left, and B5 is kept away from B6. B3 sits between B4 and B6.

questions.text: Which part of the Constitution of India talks about the Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles of State Policy are in Part IV of the Constitution, Articles 36 to 51. Part III holds the Fundamental Rights.

questions.text: Who among the following was a famous Indian playback singer and an actor too?
questions.explanation: Kishore Kumar was one of Hindi cinema's best-known playback singers and also acted in many films. Pranab Mukherjee was President of India and Sunil Chhetri is a footballer.

questions.text: The Purple Revolution, which was launched in Jammu and Kashmir, is also known as ______.
questions.explanation: The Purple Revolution is the spread of lavender farming in Jammu and Kashmir under CSIR's Aroma Mission, so it is also called the Lavender Revolution, after the crop's purple flowers.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following founded Brahmo Samaj in Calcutta (Kolkata)?
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha, later the Brahmo Samaj, in Calcutta in 1828. Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a cause of rural poverty in India?
options: Lack of alternate employment opportunities other than agriculture
questions.explanation: Migration from villages to towns is mostly a result of rural poverty, as people leave in search of work, rather than a cause of it. Few jobs outside farming, illiteracy and lack of capital all keep rural households poor.

questions.text: Who is the Chairman of Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC) of India?
questions.explanation: The Financial Stability and Development Council, set up in 2010, is chaired by the Union Finance Minister; its members include the heads of the financial regulators such as the RBI and SEBI.

questions.text: The Great Indian Novel is written by the famous politician ________.
questions.explanation: 'The Great Indian Novel' (1989), which retells the Mahabharata as the story of India's freedom movement, is by Shashi Tharoor.

questions.text: Which of the given statements related to the temples of India is correct? I.The Nagara style of architecture is also known as the North Indian style; II.The Dravidian style of architecture is also known as the South Indian style.
questions.explanation: Indian temple architecture has two main styles, Nagara in the north and Dravida in the south, so both statements are correct.

questions.text: The uplifted blocks of block mountains are called ______.
questions.explanation: Block mountains form when faulting lifts some blocks of the crust and lowers others: the uplifted blocks are horsts and the lowered ones grabens.

questions.text: Dantidurga belonged to which dynasty of India?
questions.explanation: Dantidurga founded the Rashtrakuta dynasty in the mid-8th century, overthrowing his overlords, the Chalukyas of Badami.

questions.text: Bagurumba is a folk dance of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Bagurumba is a folk dance of the Bodo people of Assam.

questions.text: The number of persons per unit area gives the measurement of _____.
questions.explanation: Population density is the number of people per unit area, usually given per square kilometre.

questions.text: ‘Ambubachi’ festival of Assam is celebrated in the month of ______ every year.
questions.explanation: The Ambubachi Mela is held every June at the Kamakhya temple in Guwahati, Assam.

questions.text: Harshavardhana (r. 606-647 CE) was a ruler of __________ dynasty.
questions.explanation: Harshavardhana belonged to the Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) dynasty of Thanesar and ruled from Kanauj.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: All India Muslim League was formed in ______.
questions.explanation: The All India Muslim League was founded at Dhaka in December 1906.

questions.text: All the changes in the weather are driven by the ______.
questions.explanation: The sun's heat drives the weather: it warms land, sea and air unevenly, which brings about winds, evaporation and rain.

questions.text: The HVJ gas pipeline from Hazira in Gujarat to Jagdishpur in Uttar Pradesh passes through which state?
questions.explanation: The HVJ gas pipeline is named after its three points: Hazira in Gujarat, Vijaipur in Madhya Pradesh and Jagdishpur in Uttar Pradesh.

questions.text: Tapeworm belongs to which group of the animal kingdom?
questions.explanation: The tapeworm is a flatworm, in the phylum Platyhelminthes. Annelida are segmented worms such as the earthworm, Porifera are sponges and Coelenterata include Hydra.

questions.text: Which of the following is an Indian game of snake boat race?
questions.explanation: Vallam kali is Kerala's traditional boat race, rowed in long 'snake boats'. Kho-kho and mallakhamb are land sports.

questions.text: The judiciary has the power to strike down particular laws passed by the Parliament if it believes that these are a violation of the basic structure of the Constitution. This is called ______.
questions.explanation: Judicial review is the courts' power to strike down a law that violates the Constitution, including its basic structure.

questions.text: Who among the following won a silver medal in the Summer Olympics 2020 (played in 2021)?
questions.explanation: Wrestler Ravi Kumar Dahiya won silver in the men's 57 kg freestyle at Tokyo. Bajrang Punia, Lovlina Borgohain and PV Sindhu won bronze.

questions.text: Who became the new Chief Minister of Punjab in March 2022?
questions.explanation: Bhagwant Mann of the Aam Aadmi Party was sworn in as Chief Minister of Punjab on 16 March 2022, after his party won the state's assembly election.

questions.text: Which of the following gases shields the surface of earth from ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun?
questions.explanation: The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs most of the sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of contact force?
questions.explanation: Muscular force acts only when the body touches the object it moves. Electrostatic, gravitational and magnetic forces act at a distance.

questions.text: Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma is known for which classical dance form?
questions.explanation: Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma is known for reviving Mohiniyattam, Kerala's classical dance, and is often called its mother.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. John ran pretty fast, ______________ he did not win the race.
questions.explanation: The second clause contrasts with the first (he ran fast yet lost), so the linking word must show contrast: 'though', meaning 'but' or 'although'. 'So', 'for' and 'and' do not.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Out of the blue
questions.explanation: Something that happens 'out of the blue' comes without any warning, completely unexpectedly.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. An iron hand
questions.explanation: To rule with 'an iron hand' is to keep strict, firm control.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I like to read the newspaper ______ the morning.
questions.explanation: Parts of the day take 'in': 'in the morning', 'in the evening'; 'at' goes with 'night' and clock times.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. “Garnish” the drink with cranberries or a slice of fresh peach.
questions.explanation: To 'garnish' food or drink is to decorate it: 'embellish'. 'Wend' means to go, 'blemish' is a flaw and 'dismantle' means to take apart.

questions.text: Select the option that rectifies the incorrectly spelt words in the given sentence. Go, rest in the dark shadowe of the graet forest.
options: Go, rest in the dark shadow of the great forest.
Go, rest in the dark shadow of the grate forest.
Go, rest in the dark shaddow of the great forest.
Go, rest in the dark shadowe of the great forest.
questions.explanation: The correct spellings are 'shadow' and 'great'. 'Grate' is a different word (a frame for a fire, or to shred), and 'shaddow' and 'shadowe' are misspellings.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. He “have not been in” the right mental state since 2017.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'he' takes 'has', and the present perfect suits a state lasting 'since 2017': 'He has not been in the right mental state since 2017.'

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Scientists have made dramatic progress in understanding an universe and the mechanisms of biology.
questions.explanation: 'Universe' begins with a 'yoo' sound, so 'an' is wrong; the natural phrase is 'understanding the universe'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We are planning to go to Delhi ______ train.
questions.explanation: Means of transport take 'by' when no article is used: 'by train', 'by bus', 'by air'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Killing one self
questions.explanation: Suicide is the killing of oneself. Regicide is the killing of a king, homicide of a person and matricide of one's mother.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. Once upon a time there was a very rich man “which lived with” his three daughters.
questions.explanation: 'Who', not 'which', refers to a person, and the past tense matches 'there was': 'a very rich man who lived with his three daughters'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Despite the pain in his leg, / Nicholas completed / the marathon.
options: Despite the pain in his leg,
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: 'despite' takes a noun phrase ('the pain in his leg') without 'of', and the simple past 'completed' fits.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Subhash had just returned from “work in” 9 p.m.
questions.explanation: A clock time takes 'at': 'Subhash had just returned from work at 9 p.m.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Insecure
questions.explanation: 'Insecure' means uncertain or anxious about oneself; its opposite is 'confident'. 'Anxious' is close to it in sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. She remained “resolute” in her belief.
questions.explanation: 'Resolute' means firm and determined; its opposite is 'wavering', unsure. 'Inflexible' is close to 'resolute' in sense.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. The merchant distributes work “among the weavers” based on the orders received.
questions.explanation: 'Distribute among' is the right phrase for sharing out between several people, so the sentence needs no change.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'fraction'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Uncanny
questions.explanation: 'Uncanny' means strange or mysterious in an unsettling way: 'spooky'. 'Deranged' means insane and 'reckless' careless of danger.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. This pandemic have / profoundly changed our / way of living.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'this pandemic' takes 'has': 'This pandemic has profoundly changed our way of living.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Brashness
questions.explanation: 'Brashness' is loud, pushy self-confidence; its opposite is 'timidity', shyness and lack of courage. 'Nerve' and 'boldness' are close to it in sense.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. All plants and animals need water to survive. There can be no life (1) ______ earth without water. Why is water (2) ______ important? It is (3) ______ 60 percent of our body weight is made up of water. Our bodies use water in all the cells, organs, and tissues, to help (4) ______ body temperature and (5) ______other bodily functions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
questions.explanation: Life is 'on earth': 'on' is used for the surface of the planet.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. All plants and animals need water to survive. There can be no life (1) ______ earth without water. Why is water (2) ______ important? It is (3) ______ 60 percent of our body weight is made up of water. Our bodies use water in all the cells, organs, and tissues, to help (4) ______ body temperature and (5) ______other bodily functions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
questions.explanation: 'So' stresses the degree: 'Why is water so important?'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. All plants and animals need water to survive. There can be no life (1) ______ earth without water. Why is water (2) ______ important? It is (3) ______ 60 percent of our body weight is made up of water. Our bodies use water in all the cells, organs, and tissues, to help (4) ______ body temperature and (5) ______other bodily functions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.explanation: The sentence gives the reason why water is important: 'It is because 60 percent of our body weight is made up of water.'

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. All plants and animals need water to survive. There can be no life (1) ______ earth without water. Why is water (2) ______ important? It is (3) ______ 60 percent of our body weight is made up of water. Our bodies use water in all the cells, organs, and tissues, to help (4) ______ body temperature and (5) ______other bodily functions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
questions.explanation: Water helps 'regulate', that is control, body temperature.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. All plants and animals need water to survive. There can be no life (1) ______ earth without water. Why is water (2) ______ important? It is (3) ______ 60 percent of our body weight is made up of water. Our bodies use water in all the cells, organs, and tissues, to help (4) ______ body temperature and (5) ______other bodily functions.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
questions.explanation: Water helps 'maintain', that is keep up, the body's other functions.

questions.text: Which two numbers (not digits) and two signs need to be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 14 + 7 ÷ 729 × 81 – 9 = 500
questions.explanation: After interchanging 81 and 9 and the signs ÷ and ×: 14 + 7 × 729 ÷ 9 − 81 = 14 + 7 × 81 − 81 = 14 + 567 − 81 = 500.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 35 + 3 ÷ 3 – 5 + 1 = 40
questions.explanation: After interchanging 1 and 5: 35 + 3 ÷ 3 − 1 + 5 = 35 + 1 − 1 + 5 = 40.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 96, 144, ?, 240, 288
questions.explanation: Each term is 48 more than the one before: 96, 144, 192, 240, 288.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. SAM : UES :: RAT : TEZ :: LOI : ?
questions.explanation: The three letters move 2, 4 and 6 places forward: S A M → U E S and R A T → T E Z. So L O I → N S O.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements Some remotes are batteries. All batteries are chargers. No charger is a cable. Conclusions: I) Some remotes are cables. II) Some batteries are cable.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: All batteries are chargers and no charger is a cable, so no battery is a cable: II is false. The remotes that are batteries cannot be cables, and nothing is said of the other remotes, so I does not follow either.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'PAIDY' is written as 'NYGBW', and 'FORST' is written as 'DMPQR'. How will 'HARKG' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places back: PAIDY → NYGBW and FORST → DMPQR. So HARKG → FYPIE.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'AGC' is coded as '42', and 'BAD' is coded as '16’. How will 'KIC' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is twice the product of the letters' places in the alphabet: AGC → 2 × 1 × 7 × 3 = 42 and BAD → 2 × 2 × 1 × 4 = 16. So KIC → 2 × 11 × 9 × 3 = 594.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. RAB, SZD, TYF, UXH, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters run R, S, T, U, V; the second A, Z, Y, X, W; the third B, D, F, H, J, two places at a time. The next cluster is VWJ.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. COMPUTER : EOOPWTGR :: SHOWER : UHQWGR :: NEEDLE : ?
questions.explanation: Letters in the odd places move 2 forward and those in the even places stay: SHOWER → U H Q W G R. So NEEDLE → P E G D N E: PEGDNE.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (11, 22, 44) (15, 12, 42)
questions.explanation: In each set the third number is twice the first plus the second: 2 × 11 + 22 = 44 and 2 × 15 + 12 = 42. Only (18, 8, 44) fits: 2 × 18 + 8 = 44.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'J' is written as '10' and 'ACT' is written as '24'. How will 'BEAR' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: A word is written as the sum of its letters' places in the alphabet: J = 10 and ACT = 1 + 3 + 20 = 24. So BEAR = 2 + 5 + 1 + 18 = 26.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) 7854 : 5632 :: 8424 : 6202 :: 4444 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second number is the first minus 2222: 7854 − 2222 = 5632 and 8424 − 2222 = 6202. So 4444 − 2222 = 2222.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. PG : DM :: GO : ?
questions.explanation: The pair is reversed and each letter moved 3 places back: PG → G P → D M. So GO → O G → L D: LD.

questions.text: V, W, X, Y and Z are five men sitting in a line facing the South - while M, N, O, P and Q are five ladies sitting in a second line parallel to the first line and are facing the North. W who is immediate next to the left of Y, is opposite Q. X and N are diagonally opposite to each other. Z is opposite to O who is immediate next to the right of M. P who is to the immediate left of Q, is opposite to Y. M is at one end of the line. Who is sitting opposite to N?
questions.explanation: Number the places 1 to 5 from the ladies' left (the men's right). M is at an end with O on her right, so M is 1, O is 2 and Z sits opposite O. P and Q sit side by side with Y and W opposite them, and X and N must be diagonally opposite at the two ends, so N is 5, P 3, Q 4 and X 1. That leaves V at 5, opposite N.

questions.text: Who among the following won the Formula One 2022 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix?
questions.explanation: Max Verstappen won the 2022 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix at Jeddah in March 2022, ahead of Charles Leclerc.

questions.text: Which of the following awards has been conferred upon Kailash Kher?
questions.explanation: The playback singer Kailash Kher received the Padma Shri in 2017.

questions.text: When tax collection exceeds the required expenditure, the budget is said to be in ______.
questions.explanation: When receipts exceed expenditure the budget is in surplus; when expenditure exceeds receipts it is in deficit, and when the two are equal it is balanced.

questions.text: Lactic acid is commonly found in __________.
questions.explanation: Lactic acid is the acid of sour milk and curd. Tomatoes contain oxalic acid and vinegar acetic acid.

questions.text: Which of the following fundamental rights deals with 'Protection of Interests of Minorities'?
questions.explanation: Article 29, 'Protection of interests of minorities', is one of the Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29 and 30).

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which Act passed by British Government of India abolished the Council of India?
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act, 1935 abolished the Council of India, set up under the Government of India Act, 1858, and gave the Secretary of State for India a body of advisers instead.

questions.text: As per Thermodynamics, _________ system cannot exchange both energy and mass with its surroundings.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'isolated', taking 'cannot exchange both' to mean a system that exchanges neither energy nor matter with its surroundings. A closed system exchanges energy but not matter, and an open system exchanges both.

questions.text: According to the data from the economic think-tank, the Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy (CMIE), which of the following states witnessed the lowest unemployment rate as of January 2022?
questions.explanation: CMIE's figures for January 2022 put Telangana's unemployment rate the lowest of the states, at 0.7%, and Haryana's the highest, at 23.4%.

questions.text: Baishagu festival is associated with the state of ____________ in India.
questions.explanation: Baishagu (Bwisagu) is the spring and New Year festival of the Bodo people of Assam, held in mid-April.

questions.text: Raut nacha is performed by mostly tribals of a state of India. Which of the following states is it?
questions.explanation: Raut Nacha is a folk dance of Chhattisgarh, performed by the Raut (Yadav) community of cowherds, a caste rather than a tribe.

questions.text: Who among the following Indian choreographers won the World Choreography Award 2020 and was also nominated for the Emmy Awards?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Suresh Mukund, the Mumbai choreographer who leads the dance crew Kings United; his choreography on NBC's 'World of Dance' was nominated for an Emmy in 2019.

questions.text: Who among the following actresses received the TIME 100 Impact Awards 2022?
questions.explanation: Deepika Padukone received a TIME100 Impact Award in Dubai in March 2022, for her work on mental-health awareness.

questions.text: Inamgaon, an important Archaeological site is situated on ______ river.
questions.explanation: Inamgaon, a Chalcolithic farming settlement east of Pune with Malwa and Jorwe levels, lies on the right bank of the Ghod, a tributary of the Bhima.

questions.text: What is the height of the goal-post according to FIFA?
questions.explanation: The Laws of the Game set the goal at 8 feet (2.44 m) high and 8 yards (7.32 m) wide.

questions.text: Who wrote the book ‘The Legend of Lakshmi Prasad’?
questions.explanation: 'The Legend of Lakshmi Prasad' (2016), a collection of four stories, is by Twinkle Khanna.

questions.text: ______________ is also known as industrial agriculture.
questions.explanation: Intensive farming, which uses large inputs of capital, machinery, fertilisers and pesticides to get the most from the land, is also called industrial agriculture.

questions.text: ___________ has often been called the incubator of Western civilisation.
questions.explanation: The civilisations of ancient Egypt, Greece and Rome grew up around the Mediterranean, whose sea routes carried their trade and ideas, so it is often called the incubator of Western civilisation.

questions.text: _________ was the capital of Chalukya dynasty.
questions.explanation: Badami (Vatapi), in Karnataka's Bagalkot district, was the capital of the early Chalukyas, hence called the Chalukyas of Badami. Kanchipuram was the Pallava capital and Pataliputra and Rajgir were capitals of Magadha.

questions.text: Bharhut Stupa depict the Jataka tales and stories. It is located in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: The Bharhut stupa is in Satna district, Madhya Pradesh. Its carved railings, now largely in the Indian Museum, Kolkata, show Jataka tales with labelled inscriptions.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. An imaginary name assumed by an author
questions.explanation: A pseudonym is a false name an author writes under. Nomenclature is a system of names, an almanac a yearly book of dates and facts, and 'platonic' an adjective.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Hideous
questions.explanation: 'Hideous' means very ugly; its opposite is 'attractive'. 'Disgusting', 'shocking' and 'ghastly' are close to it in sense.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. If he had not dropped out, / he will most certainly have completed / his education by 2023.
options: If he had not dropped out
he will most certainly have completed
questions.explanation: A past unreal condition ('If he had not dropped out') takes 'would have' + past participle in the main clause: 'he would most certainly have completed'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. In the heat of the moment
options: Saying or doing something without thinking due to anger
To share information that was previously concealed
In a confused or befuddled state of mind
questions.explanation: Something said or done 'in the heat of the moment' is done without thinking, while angry or excited.

questions.text: Select the sentence in which all words are correctly spelt.
options: With him he had one of his cheif councellors.
Work is due to comence in the coming year.
Melt the white and dark chocolate in separate bowls.
We did it becuase we felt it our duty to encorage him.
questions.explanation: Only the third sentence is spelt correctly. The others misspell 'chief', 'councillors' (or 'counsellors'), 'commence', 'because' and 'encourage'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We ______ learn to meet adversity gracefully.
questions.explanation: 'Must' expresses necessity and takes the bare infinitive 'learn'. 'Ought', 'have' and 'had' would all need 'to' before 'learn'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. I accidentally “let the cat out of the bag” about your promotion.
questions.explanation: To 'let the cat out of the bag' is to reveal a secret, often by accident.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. He went to bed early to “get up on time” to attend his morning lecture.
questions.explanation: 'On time' means at the right time, punctually, so the sentence needs no change. 'Over time' means gradually, and 'for time' and 'at time' are not idiomatic.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. He sounded like he “were to going” cry.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'was going to': the future seen from the past is 'was going to' + verb, and the indicative 'was' suits something he really seemed about to do ('He sounded like he was going to cry'). Formal English may use the subjunctive 'were' after 'as if' to mark a comparison as unreal, which nothing here suggests; 'going to' alone leaves out the verb 'be'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Educators must roll up their sleeves and do a more best job of teaching critical thinking.
options: Educators must roll up their sleeves
and do a more best job
questions.explanation: 'More best' is a double comparison; the comparative of 'good' is 'better': 'do a better job'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Reliant' is spelt correctly. The others should be 'rudimentary', 'conscious' and 'coalesce'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Grammar is just a natural function of children's brains, “and they apply it to” whatever they find.
questions.explanation: 'It' refers back to the singular 'grammar' and the present 'apply' matches 'is', so the sentence needs no change. 'Them' does not agree with 'grammar', and 'applied' breaks the tense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Can you please ______ this sauce over the pasta?
questions.explanation: To 'pour' is to make a liquid flow out of a container. 'Pore' sounds the same but means a tiny opening, or to study closely ('pore over'), and 'power' and 'purr' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We deplore the use of ______ against innocent people.
questions.explanation: To 'deplore' is to condemn strongly, which fits the use of 'violence' against innocent people.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. August
questions.explanation: As an adjective, 'august' means respected and impressive: 'eminent'. 'Imminent' means about to happen and 'illicit' unlawful.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The panel will / investigate the allegations / owing to the concerned officials.
questions.explanation: The allegations are made 'against' the officials: 'investigate the allegations against the concerned officials'. 'Owing to' means 'because of' and makes no sense here.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. A ______ body will fight off the illness naturally without any medicine.
questions.explanation: A 'healthy' body fights off illness on its own; 'flabby' suggests poor condition, and 'happy' and 'fresh' do not fit the sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Mandate
questions.explanation: A 'mandate' is an official order or the authority to act: 'command'. A request or a question leaves the choice to the other person.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. I do not feel it is a “laudable” plan.
questions.explanation: 'Laudable' means deserving praise, so 'commendable' is a synonym. 'Disrespected', not held in esteem, is the only option opposite in sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. India continues to ____________ the highest amount of e-waste, more than China, the US, Japan and Germany.
questions.explanation: A country 'generates', that is produces, waste.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Words convey meaning, because they are used in human activities in different forms. Different words may (1) ______ the same thing in different languages and this is what is referred to as 'family resemblance.' In other words, languages help us (2) ______ reality and then communicate it to others. There are tens and thousands of languages in the world and all of them help us (3) ______ express ourselves, which in turn, gives meaning to our life. One's mother tongue is (4) ______ for one's literary growth, but if you want to communicate to a wider audience, then you will (5) ______ to reach out to the target audience in a language they understand.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'May' takes the bare infinitive: different words 'may mean' the same thing in different languages.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Words convey meaning, because they are used in human activities in different forms. Different words may (1) ______ the same thing in different languages and this is what is referred to as 'family resemblance.' In other words, languages help us (2) ______ reality and then communicate it to others. There are tens and thousands of languages in the world and all of them help us (3) ______ express ourselves, which in turn, gives meaning to our life. One's mother tongue is (4) ______ for one's literary growth, but if you want to communicate to a wider audience, then you will (5) ______ to reach out to the target audience in a language they understand.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Languages help us 'comprehend', that is understand, reality before we communicate it to others.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Words convey meaning, because they are used in human activities in different forms. Different words may (1) ______ the same thing in different languages and this is what is referred to as 'family resemblance.' In other words, languages help us (2) ______ reality and then communicate it to others. There are tens and thousands of languages in the world and all of them help us (3) ______ express ourselves, which in turn, gives meaning to our life. One's mother tongue is (4) ______ for one's literary growth, but if you want to communicate to a wider audience, then you will (5) ______ to reach out to the target audience in a language they understand.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Languages help us express ourselves 'effectively', that is well, which gives meaning to life. 'Secretly', 'lately' and 'retrospectively' do not fit.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Words convey meaning, because they are used in human activities in different forms. Different words may (1) ______ the same thing in different languages and this is what is referred to as 'family resemblance.' In other words, languages help us (2) ______ reality and then communicate it to others. There are tens and thousands of languages in the world and all of them help us (3) ______ express ourselves, which in turn, gives meaning to our life. One's mother tongue is (4) ______ for one's literary growth, but if you want to communicate to a wider audience, then you will (5) ______ to reach out to the target audience in a language they understand.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The mother tongue is 'essential' for literary growth; the 'but' that follows turns to the need for another language to reach a wider audience.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Words convey meaning, because they are used in human activities in different forms. Different words may (1) ______ the same thing in different languages and this is what is referred to as 'family resemblance.' In other words, languages help us (2) ______ reality and then communicate it to others. There are tens and thousands of languages in the world and all of them help us (3) ______ express ourselves, which in turn, gives meaning to our life. One's mother tongue is (4) ______ for one's literary growth, but if you want to communicate to a wider audience, then you will (5) ______ to reach out to the target audience in a language they understand.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Will have to' expresses a future necessity: 'you will have to reach out'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. GRV : IUE :: XCB : ?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves 2 places forward, the second 3, and the third is replaced by its opposite letter (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on): G → I, R → U, V → E. So X → Z, C → F and B → Y: ZFY.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 339 : 1022 :: 58 : 179 :: 25 : ?
questions.explanation: Each first number times 3, plus 5, gives its pair: 339 × 3 + 5 = 1022 and 58 × 3 + 5 = 179. So 25 × 3 + 5 = 80.

questions.text: Select the option in which the two numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers in the given number pairs. 23 : 529; 26 : 676
questions.explanation: The second number is the square of the first: 23² = 529 and 26² = 676. Likewise 24² = 576; 196 is 14², 400 is 20², and 444 is not a square.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. GRM : MGR :: PAR : ?
questions.explanation: The last letter moves to the front: GRM → MGR. So PAR → RPA.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'HOPE' is written as 'KRSH', and 'RAGF' is written as 'UDJI'. How will 'MNCK' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 3 places forward: HOPE → KRSH and RAGF → UDJI. So MNCK → PQFN.

questions.text: Which two numbers (NOT digits) and two signs need to be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 35 ÷ 4 × 48 + 70 – 10 = 40
questions.explanation: After interchanging 70 and 48 and the signs ÷ and ×: 35 × 4 ÷ 70 + 48 − 10 = 140 ÷ 70 + 48 − 10 = 2 + 48 − 10 = 40.

questions.text: Which two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 9 + 6 ÷ 4 − 5 + 3 = 10
questions.explanation: After interchanging 4 and 3: 9 + 6 ÷ 3 − 5 + 4 = 9 + 2 − 5 + 4 = 10.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 29 : 31 :: 19 : 23 :: 31 : ?
questions.explanation: Each pair is a prime number and the next prime: 29 and 31, 19 and 23. The prime after 31 is 37.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'PAINTS' is written as 'HGMRZK' and 'ROCKY' is written as 'BPXLI'. How will 'HUNTER' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite letter (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on) and the result is reversed: PAINTS → KZRMGH → HGMRZK and ROCKY → ILXPB → BPXLI. So HUNTER → SFMGVI → IVGMFS.

questions.text: Seven students Pawan, Aman, Raman, Sanam, Tanmay, Umang and Vikram took a series of tests. No two students got similar marks. Vikram scored just more than Pawan and Pawan scored just more than Aman. Raman and Tanmay scored the highest and the least marks but not necessarily in the same order. Umang’s score was less than only Raman's score. Sanam’s score was higher than only one person. Whose score was in between the scores of Pawan and Sanam?
questions.explanation: Umang is below only Raman, so Raman is first, Umang second and Tanmay last. Sanam, above only one person, is sixth, which leaves third to fifth for Vikram, Pawan and Aman in that order. Aman, fifth, is between Pawan (fourth) and Sanam (sixth).

questions.text: Six boys G1, G2, G3, G4, G5 and G6 are sitting in a row facing towards the north (not necessarily in the same order). G4 is second to the right of G5. G2 is second to the left of G5. G3 is to the immediate left of G2. G6 is second to the right of G3. How many boys are sitting to the left of G6?
questions.explanation: G3 sits immediately left of G2, G5 two places right of G2 and G4 two places right of G5, so the row from the left is G3, G2, _, G5, _, G4. G6, second to the right of G3, takes the third seat and G1 the fifth, so two boys, G3 and G2, sit to the left of G6.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth alphanumeric-cluster in the same way as the second alphanumeric-cluster is related to the first alphanumeric-cluster and the fourth alphanumeric-cluster is related to the third alphanumeric-cluster. STV20 : WXZ24 :: ABD2 : EFH6 :: IJL10 : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 4 places forward and the number rises by 4: STV20 → WXZ24 and ABD2 → EFH6. So IJL10 → MNP14.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. Some red are mouse. II. No grey is mouse. Conclusions: I. All red are grey. II. No mouse is grey.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: 'No grey is mouse' converts to 'no mouse is grey', so II follows. The red that are mouse cannot be grey, so not all red are grey: I does not follow.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 48, 54, 45, 51, 42, 48, ?
questions.explanation: The steps alternate +6 and −9: 48, 54, 45, 51, 42, 48, then 48 − 9 = 39.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. Some cars are white. II. Some locks are white. Conclusions: I. All white are locks. II. No car is a lock. III. All locks are cars.
questions.explanation: Cars and locks are linked only through some white things, so nothing definite follows about all white things, about all locks, or that no car is a lock: none of the conclusions follows.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. TRO, RQM, PPK, NOI, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move 2 back (T, R, P, N, L), the second 1 back (R, Q, P, O, N) and the third 2 back (O, M, K, I, G): LNG.

questions.text: Six people Akshay, Anurag, Amit, Anubhav, Aryan and Ashish are sitting in a straight row facing North. Neither Akshay nor Amit are sitting at the corners. Amit and Anubhav are immediate neighbour of each other. Aryan is sitting second from the right corner. Only Akshay is sitting in between Anubhav and Ashish. Amit is sitting second to the left of Anurag. Who is sitting in between Anurag and Amit?
questions.explanation: Aryan is fifth from the left. Amit, not at an end, cannot be third (Anurag, two places to his right, would take Aryan's seat) or second (with Anurag fourth, the free seats 1, 3 and 6 cannot hold Anubhav, Akshay and Ashish side by side), so Amit is fourth and Anurag sixth. Then Anubhav is third, Akshay second and Ashish first: Aryan sits between Amit and Anurag.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'BAG' is coded as '71', and 'VICE' is coded as '69'. How will 'LIKE' be coded in that code language?
questions.explanation: The code is the sum of the letters' places counted from Z (A = 26, B = 25 and so on): BAG = 25 + 26 + 20 = 71 and VICE = 5 + 18 + 24 + 22 = 69. So LIKE = 15 + 18 + 16 + 22 = 71.

questions.text: In a certain code language, if 'owl' is known as 'peacock', 'peacock' is known as 'cuckoo', 'cuckoo' is known as 'pigeon', and 'pigeon' is known as 'sparrow', then what would be the name of the bird that sings well?
questions.explanation: The bird that sings well is the cuckoo, and in this code 'cuckoo' is called 'pigeon'.

questions.text: Sangrai is a folk dance of which state of India?
questions.explanation: Sangrai is danced by the Mog community of Tripura at the Sangrai festival in Chaitra, the last month of the Bengali year, to welcome the New Year.

questions.text: India’s southern neighbours across the sea consist of _____ island countries.
questions.explanation: India's southern neighbours across the sea are the two island countries Sri Lanka and Maldives.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Tipu Sultan became the ruler of Mysore in ______.
questions.explanation: Tipu Sultan succeeded his father Hyder Ali, who died in December 1782 during the Second Anglo-Mysore War.

questions.text: ‘Courage and Conviction : An Autobiography’ is the autobiography of which of the following persons?
questions.explanation: 'Courage and Conviction' (2013) is the autobiography of General V K Singh, Chief of the Army Staff from 2010 to 2012.

questions.text: Which of the following festivals is associated with the Kamakhya temple of Guwahati?
questions.explanation: The Ambubachi Mela is held every June at the Kamakhya temple, marking the goddess's yearly menstruation. Mando is a Goan song form and Sunburn an electronic music festival.

questions.text: Which of the following states has bi-cameral Legislature as of March 2022?
questions.explanation: In March 2022 six states had a Legislative Council as well as an Assembly: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh. Odisha, Gujarat and Kerala had only one House.

questions.text: Which of the following states launched the ‘Mukhyamantri Ration Aapke Dwar Yojana’ in October 2021?
questions.explanation: Madhya Pradesh's cabinet approved the 'Mukhyamantri Ration Aapke Dwar' scheme on 19 October 2021: vehicles take ration from the fair-price shop to the villages attached to it, for tribal families in 16 districts.

questions.text: What is a measure of the moisture present in air called?
questions.explanation: Humidity is the amount of water vapour in the air. Precipitation is water falling as rain, snow or hail.

questions.text: Which Article of the Constitution of India under the Directive Principles of State Policy talks about organisation of village panchayats?
questions.explanation: Article 40 directs the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government. Article 48 covers agriculture and animal husbandry, 43 a living wage and 39A free legal aid.

questions.text: The first census of Independent India was conducted in ______.
questions.explanation: The first census after independence was taken in 1951; India's census was held every ten years from 1881 to 2011.

questions.text: Articles _____ in Part VI of the Constitution deal with the components of state legislature.
questions.explanation: Chapter III of Part VI, 'The State Legislature', runs from Article 168 to Article 212.

questions.text: In which language did Banabhatta compose Harshacharita?
questions.explanation: Banabhatta, court poet of Harshavardhana, wrote the 'Harshacharita', a biography of the king, in Sanskrit.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct? I. Converting plant and animal waste including that from kitchen into manure is called composting. II. The method of making compost from kitchen garbage using redworms is called vermicomposting.
options: Neither I nor II is correct.
Both I and II are correct.
questions.explanation: Both are correct: turning plant and animal waste into manure is composting, and making compost with redworms is vermicomposting.

questions.text: TH Vinayakram is associated with which musical instrument?
questions.explanation: T H (Vikku) Vinayakram is a master of the ghatam, the clay pot of Carnatic music; he shared a Grammy for 'Planet Drum'.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a tributary of the Indus river?
questions.explanation: The Son is a tributary of the Ganga. The Kabul, Gilgit and Shyok all join the Indus.

questions.text: _____________ won the ICC Women's Cricket World Cup 2022.
questions.explanation: Australia won the 2022 ICC Women's Cricket World Cup, beating England in the final at Christchurch, New Zealand, in April 2022.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who said, ‘One caste, one religion, one God for humankind’?
questions.explanation: 'One caste, one religion, one God for man' was the message of Sree Narayana Guru, the social reformer of Kerala.

questions.text: The North-South corridor of the Golden Quadrilateral Super Highways links Srinagar and _______.
questions.explanation: NCERT describes the North-South corridor as linking Srinagar in Jammu and Kashmir with Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu, and the East-West corridor Silchar with Porbandar.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct chronological order of early Turkish rulers who ruled over Delhi from the year 1206 to 1290?
questions.explanation: Qutbuddin Aibak ruled from 1206 to 1210, Iltutmish from 1211 to 1236 and his daughter Raziyya from 1236 to 1240.

questions.text: Which cell organelle performs the principal function of packaging materials?
questions.explanation: The Golgi apparatus packages materials made in the endoplasmic reticulum and dispatches them inside and outside the cell.

questions.text: Pushkar lake is situated in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Pushkar Lake, with its many ghats and the Brahma temple, is in Ajmer district.

questions.text: Who among the following won the first ever individual Olympic medal for India?
questions.explanation: K D (Khashaba Dadasaheb) Jadhav won bronze in bantamweight freestyle wrestling at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics, independent India's first individual Olympic medal. Rathore (2004) and Bindra (2008) won theirs later, and P T Usha never won one. (The IOC credits Norman Pritchard's two silvers of 1900 to India, but he is not among the options.)

questions.text: In February 2022, beverage maker Coca-Cola signed ______ as the brand ambassador for Thums Up.
questions.explanation: Coca-Cola India signed Shah Rukh Khan as the brand ambassador for Thums Up in February 2022, launching him in an action-themed campaign.

questions.text: ‘Padma Vibhushan’ winner Pandit Birju Maharaj was a famous _____ dancer.
questions.explanation: Pandit Birju Maharaj (1938-2022) of the Lucknow gharana was a leading Kathak dancer; he received the Padma Vibhushan in 1986.

questions.text: What chemical element does ‘H’ stand for in the science periodic table?
questions.explanation: H is the symbol of hydrogen, element 1. Helium is He, holmium Ho and mercury Hg.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The mountain lion is / one of the slyest and more / elusive animals in the woods.
options: one of the slyest and more
questions.explanation: After 'one of the', both adjectives need the superlative: 'one of the slyest and most elusive animals', not 'more elusive'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Psychologist' is spelt correctly; the others should be 'envisage', 'emergence' and 'transition'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Overrun
questions.explanation: To overrun a place is to invade and occupy it, close to 'inundate', 'storm' and 'invade'; to 'surrender' is to give it up.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Many people may not find the rewards ______ with the time and effort required.
questions.explanation: 'Commensurate with' means in proportion to: the rewards may not match the time and effort required.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. If we don't reverse course now, will anyone take anything we say about justice and ___________ with any seriousness for decades to come?
questions.explanation: 'Righteousness', being morally right, pairs with 'justice'; 'wickedness' and 'dishonesty' are its opposites, and 'mediation' does not fit the pair.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. He is “foaming at the mouth” about the committee's decision.
options: To be enraged and show it
to be upset about something that happened in the past
questions.explanation: To be 'foaming at the mouth' is to be extremely angry and to show it.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Probe
questions.explanation: To 'probe' is to search into or investigate something closely.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. You are looking so “pretty on these” black outfit.
questions.explanation: 'Outfit' is singular, so it takes 'this', not 'these', and one looks pretty 'in' clothes, not 'on' them: 'You are looking so pretty in this black outfit.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He is the patient ______ called you in the morning.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'who', the relative pronoun for a person as the subject of the clause: 'the patient who called you'. 'That' is also used for people in such defining clauses, but 'who' is the preferred form; 'which' is for things and 'whom' is an object form.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. They finally did what / we advice them to do / before the final match.
questions.explanation: 'Advice' is a noun; the verb is 'advise', here in the past tense to match 'did': 'what we advised them to do'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Made in imitation so as to be passed off fraudulently as genuine
questions.explanation: Something 'counterfeit' is a fake made to pass as genuine, such as a forged banknote. 'Authentic' means the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Many people like playing cricket, but _____________ my opinion, it is too chaotic.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is 'in my opinion'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Impure
questions.explanation: 'Sterile' means free from germs or contamination, the opposite of 'impure'; 'contaminated' means much the same as 'impure'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you plant a seed, / you will be noticed / that it takes some / time to grow.
questions.explanation: 'You' are the one who notices, so the verb must be active: 'you will notice that it takes some time to grow'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Back on one’s feet
questions.explanation: To be 'back on one's feet' is to be healthy or successful again after illness or trouble.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. This cruise ship ______ in November and December.
questions.explanation: A ship 'sails', that is travels by sea; 'sells', 'sales' and 'seals' sound or look alike but do not fit.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. If you want to save your money, start living an ______ life.
questions.explanation: An 'economical' life avoids waste and spends with care, which saves money; 'extravagant' and 'indulgent' mean the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Clandestine
questions.explanation: 'Clandestine' means kept or done in secret: 'undercover'. 'Blatant' and 'open' are its opposites, and 'ornate' means richly decorated.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. In India, processed foods “becomes popular in” the 20th century.
questions.explanation: 'In the 20th century' is past time, so the verb takes the past tense, which also suits the plural 'foods': 'processed foods became popular in the 20th century'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Ministry of Defence has (1) ______ the formal Government Sanction Letter (2) ______ grant of permanent commission (PC) to women officers in the Army. “In anticipation, the Army Headquarters had (3) ______ in motion a series of preparatory actions for conduct of the Permanent Commission Selection Board for affected women officers. The Selection Board will be scheduled as (4) ______ as all affected Short Service Commissioned (SSC) women officers exercise their option and complete (5) ______ documentation,” the Army said in a statement.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: A ministry 'issues' a sanction letter, that is sends it out officially.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Ministry of Defence has (1) ______ the formal Government Sanction Letter (2) ______ grant of permanent commission (PC) to women officers in the Army. “In anticipation, the Army Headquarters had (3) ______ in motion a series of preparatory actions for conduct of the Permanent Commission Selection Board for affected women officers. The Selection Board will be scheduled as (4) ______ as all affected Short Service Commissioned (SSC) women officers exercise their option and complete (5) ______ documentation,” the Army said in a statement.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The letter is 'for' the grant of permanent commission: 'for' gives its purpose.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Ministry of Defence has (1) ______ the formal Government Sanction Letter (2) ______ grant of permanent commission (PC) to women officers in the Army. “In anticipation, the Army Headquarters had (3) ______ in motion a series of preparatory actions for conduct of the Permanent Commission Selection Board for affected women officers. The Selection Board will be scheduled as (4) ______ as all affected Short Service Commissioned (SSC) women officers exercise their option and complete (5) ______ documentation,” the Army said in a statement.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: To 'set in motion' is to start a process: the Army had started a series of preparatory actions.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Ministry of Defence has (1) ______ the formal Government Sanction Letter (2) ______ grant of permanent commission (PC) to women officers in the Army. “In anticipation, the Army Headquarters had (3) ______ in motion a series of preparatory actions for conduct of the Permanent Commission Selection Board for affected women officers. The Selection Board will be scheduled as (4) ______ as all affected Short Service Commissioned (SSC) women officers exercise their option and complete (5) ______ documentation,” the Army said in a statement.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'As soon as' means at the moment when: the board will be scheduled once the officers have exercised their option.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. The Ministry of Defence has (1) ______ the formal Government Sanction Letter (2) ______ grant of permanent commission (PC) to women officers in the Army. “In anticipation, the Army Headquarters had (3) ______ in motion a series of preparatory actions for conduct of the Permanent Commission Selection Board for affected women officers. The Selection Board will be scheduled as (4) ______ as all affected Short Service Commissioned (SSC) women officers exercise their option and complete (5) ______ documentation,” the Army said in a statement.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'Requisite' means required: the officers must complete the necessary documentation. 'Unnecessary', 'optional' and 'gratuitous' go against the sense.

questions.text: Identify the number that does NOT belong to the following series. 30, 15, 15, 22.5, 46, 112.5
questions.explanation: Each term is the one before times 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2 and 2.5 in turn: 30 × 0.5 = 15, 15 × 1 = 15, 15 × 1.5 = 22.5, 22.5 × 2 = 45 and 45 × 2.5 = 112.5. So 46 should be 45.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. VOCAL : CVJHS :: TROOF : AYVVM :: RTAGE : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 7 places forward, wrapping round after Z: VOCAL → CVJHS and TROOF → AYVVM. So RTAGE → YAHNL.

questions.text: If ‘White’ is called ‘Blue’, ‘Blue’ is called ‘Red’, ‘Red’ is called ‘Yellow’, Yellow' is called ‘Green’, ‘Green’ is called ‘Black’, ‘Black’ is called ‘Violet’, and ‘Violet’ is called ‘Orange’, then what would be the colour of human blood?
questions.explanation: Human blood is red, and 'Red' is called 'Yellow'.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 632, 637, 644, 653, 664, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 5, 7, 9 and 11, so the next is 13: 664 + 13 = 677.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some mocks are exams. Some exams are banks. No bank is a local. Conclusions: I. Some mocks are local. II. No mock is a local.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation: Nothing links mocks with locals, so neither conclusion follows by itself. But 'some mocks are local' and 'no mock is a local' cannot both be false, so one of the two must hold.

questions.text: Four boys R, S, T and U are sitting in a row, facing towards the south (but not necessarily in the same order). Four girls A, B, C and D are sitting in a row, facing towards the face of these boys (but not necessarily in the same order). C and R are diagonally opposite to each other. A and S are diagonally opposite to each other. T is the immediate neighbour of R. D is the immediate neighbour of C. Who is facing D?
questions.explanation: C and R sit at opposite ends of the two rows, as do A and S; since C and A are both girls, C faces S and A faces R. T sits next to R, leaving U second from S's end, and D sits next to C, in the seat facing U.

questions.text: Which two numbers (not digits) need to be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 83 + 711 – 95 ÷ 9 × 2 = 20

Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. THROW : XPSIU :: QUICK : LDJVR :: LIGHT : ?
questions.explanation: The word is written backwards and each letter moves 1 place forward: THROW → WORHT → XPSIU and QUICK → KCIUQ → LDJVR. So LIGHT → THGIL → UIHJM.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and sixth number is related to the fifth number. 6 : 232 :: 8 : ? : : 10 : 1016
questions.explanation: Each second number is the cube of the first plus 16: 6³ + 16 = 232 and 10³ + 16 = 1016. So 8³ + 16 = 512 + 16 = 528.

questions.text: The speeds of seven cars C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6 and C7 are compared. All cars have different speeds. The speed of C1 is more than only two cars. The speed of C6 is more than C4 and less than C5. The speeds of C2 and C3 are the highest and the lowest, respectively. The speed of C4 is more than C1. The speed of how many cars is less than C7?
questions.explanation: C3 is the slowest, and C1, faster than only two cars, is third slowest. C4 is faster than C1, C6 faster than C4 and C5 faster than C6, with C2 the fastest, so C7 is second slowest: only C3 is slower.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 123 : 616 :: 147 : 736 :: 211 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second number is the first times 5, plus 1: 123 × 5 + 1 = 616 and 147 × 5 + 1 = 736. So 211 × 5 + 1 = 1056.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. GOAL, IMCJ, KKEH, MIGF, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move +2 (G, I, K, M, O), the second −2 (O, M, K, I, G), the third +2 (A, C, E, G, I) and the fourth −2 (L, J, H, F, D): OGID.

questions.text: In a certain code language, '321' means 'cold filtered coffee', '653' means 'very cold day' and '985' means 'day and night'. What is the code for 'very' in the same language?
questions.explanation: 'Cold' is in the first two phrases and 3 in both their codes; 'day' is in the last two and 5 in both their codes. So in 'very cold day' = 653, 'very' is 6.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘grapes are multi red’ is coded as ‘8 6 4 3’, ‘red people eat mango’ is coded as ‘7 4 5 2’ and ‘mango multi apple’ is coded as ‘3 5 0’. How will ‘red apple’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: 'Red' is in the first two phrases, whose codes share only 4; 'mango' is in the last two (shared 5) and 'multi' in the first and third (shared 3). So in 'mango multi apple' = 3 5 0, 'apple' is 0, and 'red apple' is 4 0.

questions.text: After interchanging the given two signs and two numbers, what will be the value of the following expression? ÷ and +; 7 and 15; 5 ÷ 35 + 15 × 6 – 7 = ?
questions.explanation: Interchanging ÷ and + and 7 and 15: 5 + 35 ÷ 7 × 6 − 15 = 5 + 30 − 15 = 20.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word. Canberra : Australia :: Doha : ?
questions.explanation: Canberra is the capital of Australia, and Doha is the capital of Qatar.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No 90s are 80s. Some 90s are 40s. All 80s are 70s. Conclusions: I. All 80s being 40s is a possibility. II. Some 70s are not 90s.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follow.
questions.explanation: The 40s that are 90s cannot be 80s, but the other 40s may take in every 80, so I is a possibility. Every 80 is a 70 and no 80 is a 90, so the 70s that are 80s are not 90s: II follows.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'DETAIL' is written as 'FCVYKJ' and 'HEALTH' is written as ‘JCCJVF’. How will 'MOTION' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +2 and −2 in turn: DETAIL → FCVYKJ and HEALTH → JCCJVF. So MOTION → OMVGQL.

questions.text: Seven girls A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing opposite the centre (not necessarily in the same order). E is second to the right of A. C is the immediate neighbour of E. D is third to the right of C. B is the immediate neighbour of E and A. F is fourth to the right of A. Which of the following statements is correct? I. D is next to the right of G. II. A is third to the left of B.
questions.explanation: Facing away from the centre, each girl's right is clockwise. Clockwise from A the order is A, B, E, C, F, G, D: E is second to A's right with B between them, C is next to E, F fourth to A's right and D third to C's right. D sits just to G's right, so I holds; A is B's immediate left-hand neighbour, not third to her left, so II is false.

questions.text: ‘The Kiss of Life’ is the autobiography of who among the following persons?
questions.explanation: 'The Kiss of Life: How a Superhero and My Son Defeated Cancer' (2016), written by Emraan Hashmi with Bilal Siddiqi, tells of his young son's fight against cancer.

questions.text: In which state of India is Bhogali Bihu festival celebrated?
questions.explanation: Bhogali or Magh Bihu, Assam's harvest festival of feasting and bonfires, is held in mid-January at the end of the harvest season.

questions.text: Paika is a martial folk dance popular in which of the following states?
questions.explanation: Paika, danced with swords or spears and shields, recalls the Paikas, the peasant militia of Odisha's old kingdoms.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book ‘Pride, Prejudice, and Punditry’?
questions.explanation: 'Pride, Prejudice and Punditry: The Essential Shashi Tharoor' (2021) is a collection of Shashi Tharoor's writings.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: A post-anal tail is present in Chordates.
Mollusca is the largest animal phylum.
Ctenophores are commonly known as sea walnuts.
Locust is an example of Arthropoda.
questions.explanation: Arthropoda, not Mollusca, is the largest animal phylum; molluscs form the second largest. The other three statements are true.

questions.text: Which of the following teams won the Ranji trophy for the year 2019-20?
questions.explanation: Saurashtra won their first Ranji Trophy in 2019-20, taking the first-innings lead over Bengal in the drawn final at Rajkot in March 2020.

questions.text: In which of the following years was the Preamble of the Indian Constitution first amended?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 amended the Preamble, adding the words 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity'.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers is also known as 'Bhagirathi' at the place of its origin?
questions.explanation: The Ganga rises as the Bhagirathi from the Gangotri glacier at Gaumukh, and takes the name Ganga at Devprayag, where the Alaknanda joins it.

questions.text: Which of the following railway zones has recently completed 100% electrification of its entire route?
questions.explanation: Konkan Railway completed the electrification of its whole 741 km route, from Roha in Maharashtra to Thokur in Karnataka, in March 2022. (It is run by the Konkan Railway Corporation rather than as one of the zonal railways.)

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who of the following founded the Atmiya Samaj?
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Atmiya Sabha (Society of Friends) in Calcutta in 1815, a forerunner of his Brahmo Sabha of 1828.

questions.text: Aparna Satheesan, who won the prestigious National Nritya Shiromani Award 2022, is associated with which of the following dance forms?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Kuchipudi: Aparna Satheesan, a dancer from Thiruvananthapuram based in the United States, was chosen for the National Nritya Shiromani Award 2022 at the Cuttack Mahotsav in Odisha for promoting Kuchipudi around the world. She also dances Bharatanatyam and trained in Mohiniyattam, but the award was for Kuchipudi.

questions.text: _____________ is a motion moved by a member to cut short the debate on a matter before the House.
questions.explanation: A closure motion, once adopted, ends the debate on a matter so that it can be put to the vote. No-confidence and censure motions are directed at the government, and a privilege motion concerns a breach of parliamentary privilege.

questions.text: The Battle of Khanwa was fought between:
options: Sher Shah Suri and Rana Sangha
questions.explanation: At Khanwa, near Fatehpur Sikri, Babur defeated Rana Sanga of Mewar in March 1527; he had defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat the year before.

questions.text: Which of the following is the oldest Veda?
questions.explanation: The Rigveda, a collection of hymns in ten books (mandalas), is the oldest of the four Vedas; the Samaveda and the Yajurveda draw on its verses.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who became the first Governor–General of India in 1773?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Warren Hastings: the Regulating Act of 1773 made the Governor of Bengal the Governor-General of Bengal, and Hastings was the first to hold the post. Strictly, the title Governor-General of India came only with the Charter Act of 1833, under Lord William Bentinck, who is not an option.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an institutional factor for agriculture?
questions.explanation: Institutional factors concern how land is owned and organised: land tenure, land reforms and the size of fields (holdings). Electricity is a technological or infrastructural input.

questions.text: As per the 2011 census, which of the following states of India has the least population?
questions.explanation: Sikkim, with about 6.1 lakh people in the 2011 census, is India's least populous state; Bihar, Kerala and Chhattisgarh each had more than 2.5 crore.

questions.text: Pandit Ram Narayan was associated with which musical instrument?
questions.explanation: Pandit Ram Narayan made the sarangi, long an accompanying instrument, a solo concert instrument.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of emulsion?
questions.explanation: An emulsion is one liquid dispersed in another: milk is droplets of fat in water. Mist and clouds are a liquid in a gas (aerosols), and a gemstone is a solid in a solid (a solid sol).

questions.text: India won the bronze medal (the only one won by India) in which team sports at the Tokyo Olympics 2020?
questions.explanation: India's men's hockey team beat Germany 5-4 for the bronze at Tokyo, India's first Olympic hockey medal since 1980.

questions.text: _____________ won the women’s singles title at the Swiss Open Super 300 badminton tournament 2022.
questions.explanation: P V Sindhu beat Thailand's Busanan Ongbamrungphan in the final of the Swiss Open in Basel in March 2022.

questions.text: According to the census 2011, the second highest populated metro in India is:
questions.explanation: In the 2011 census, the Greater Mumbai urban agglomeration (about 1.84 crore) was the most populous, followed by Delhi's (about 1.63 crore) and then Kolkata's.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. One of the baby elephants broke “off” from the herd and lost its way.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'away': to 'break away' from a group is to leave it, the usual phrase for an animal straying from its herd. 'Break off' is used mostly of a part coming loose or of ending something, though it is sometimes used of groups too.
