questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Sturdy
questions.explanation: 'Sturdy' means strong and solidly built; its opposite is 'delicate', easily broken. 'Drab' means dull and 'tiny' very small.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. ______ is going to take the responsibility for this failure?
questions.explanation: The blank is the subject of 'is going to take' and stands for a person, so the subject pronoun 'who' is needed. 'Whom' is the object form and 'whose' shows possession.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Pleasant
questions.explanation: 'Pleasant' means giving enjoyment: 'delightful'. 'Awful' and 'sorrowful' are nearly opposite, and 'faithful' means loyal.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who believes in fate
questions.explanation: A fatalist believes that events are fixed by fate and cannot be changed. An optimist expects things to turn out well, a mercenary fights for money and an ascetic gives up worldly pleasures.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To take with a grain of salt
questions.explanation: To take something 'with a grain of salt' is to accept it with some doubt, not believing it completely.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. We usually sleep in bedrooms with the door firmly shuted behind us.
questions.explanation: 'Shut' has the same form in the past tense and past participle: 'with the door firmly shut behind us'. 'Shuted' is not a word.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. You have to constant consider how your personal behaviour is going to impact everyone around you.
options: how your personal behaviour is going
questions.explanation: A verb is described by an adverb, not an adjective: 'You have to constantly consider'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’.(Neither of the leading political parties have had much) success in the southern region.
options: Neither of the leading political parties has had much
Neither of the leading political party has had much
Neither of the leading political parties have had any
questions.explanation: 'Neither' takes a singular verb, while the noun after 'of the' stays plural: 'Neither of the leading political parties has had much success'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The collection and study of postage stamps
questions.explanation: Philately is the collecting and study of postage stamps. Ornithology is the study of birds, and philanthropy is giving to help others.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'bouquet', a bunch of flowers.

questions.text: Select the option that corrects the misspelt words in the given sentence. He maintins the unity and fredom of the suol.
options: He maintains the unity and freedom of the soul.
He maintains the unity and freedomm of the soul.
He maintins the unitty and freedom of the soul.
He maintins the unity and fredom of the soul.
questions.explanation: The sentence misspells 'maintains', 'freedom' and 'soul'. Only 'He maintains the unity and freedom of the soul.' corrects all three; the others keep a misspelling or add a new one ('freedomm', 'unitty').

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Make a living
options: To earn enough money for things you need
questions.explanation: To 'make a living' is to earn enough money to pay for the things you need.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who sells flowers
questions.explanation: A florist sells flowers. A horticulturist grows plants, a chauffeur is paid to drive someone's car and an invigilator supervises candidates in an examination.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Miniature
questions.explanation: 'Miniature' means very small; its opposite is 'mammoth', huge. 'Teeny' and 'miniscule' mean much the same as 'miniature'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Most employers ______ the use of mobile phones during office hours.
questions.explanation: Employers 'prohibit', that is forbid, the use of mobile phones during office hours. 'Submerge' means to put under water and 'cultivate' to grow or develop.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A disturbed state of mind caused by an illness.
questions.explanation: Delirium is a disturbed state of mind, with confusion and restlessness, brought on by illness such as a high fever. A dilemma is a difficult choice and a discrepancy a lack of agreement between facts.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Your infidelity have given me too much pain in life.
questions.explanation: The subject 'infidelity' is singular, so it takes 'has': 'Your infidelity has given me too much pain in life.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. His “wise choice” of men like Wolfe in Canada and Clive in India, and his vigorous measures in managing foreign affairs, made England respected in every part of the world.
questions.explanation: After the possessive 'his' a noun with its adjective is needed, so 'his wise choice of men' is already correct. 'Wisely chosen' and 'wise choose' put a verb form where the noun belongs, and 'wisely choice' an adverb before a noun.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. These colours add a “vivacious” and fairy-like effect to my dress.
questions.explanation: 'Vivacious' means lively and full of spirit, as does 'sparky'. 'Repressed', 'impassive' and 'gloomy' suggest the opposite.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In Andhra Pradesh, low rainfall and increased (1) ______ on borewells have led to soil aridity, while (2) ______ snow and more rainfall has (3) ______ the desertification crisis in Himachal Pradesh. On the other (4) ______, in Rajasthan, canals, tube-well irrigation and shelterbelts have (5) ______ to an increase in the green cover.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Dependence on' borewells, that is relying on them, has dried out the soil. 'Addiction' takes 'to', and 'growth' and 'support' do not fit the sense.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In Andhra Pradesh, low rainfall and increased (1) ______ on borewells have led to soil aridity, while (2) ______ snow and more rainfall has (3) ______ the desertification crisis in Himachal Pradesh. On the other (4) ______, in Rajasthan, canals, tube-well irrigation and shelterbelts have (5) ______ to an increase in the green cover.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: 'Snow' is uncountable, so it takes 'less', which also matches 'more rainfall'; 'fewer' goes with plural nouns.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In Andhra Pradesh, low rainfall and increased (1) ______ on borewells have led to soil aridity, while (2) ______ snow and more rainfall has (3) ______ the desertification crisis in Himachal Pradesh. On the other (4) ______, in Rajasthan, canals, tube-well irrigation and shelterbelts have (5) ______ to an increase in the green cover.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: After 'has' the past participle is needed for the present perfect: 'has deepened the desertification crisis'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In Andhra Pradesh, low rainfall and increased (1) ______ on borewells have led to soil aridity, while (2) ______ snow and more rainfall has (3) ______ the desertification crisis in Himachal Pradesh. On the other (4) ______, in Rajasthan, canals, tube-well irrigation and shelterbelts have (5) ______ to an increase in the green cover.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'On the other hand' introduces a contrast: Rajasthan's green cover has grown while the other two states face desertification.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In Andhra Pradesh, low rainfall and increased (1) ______ on borewells have led to soil aridity, while (2) ______ snow and more rainfall has (3) ______ the desertification crisis in Himachal Pradesh. On the other (4) ______, in Rajasthan, canals, tube-well irrigation and shelterbelts have (5) ______ to an increase in the green cover.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: After 'have' the past participle is needed: 'have led to an increase in the green cover'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the sixth number is related to the fifth number. 3856 : 8563 :: 4893 : ? :: 2873 : 8732
questions.explanation: The first digit moves to the end: 3856 → 8563 and 2873 → 8732. So 4893 → 8934.

questions.text: Six people Ali, Parth, Roy, Minal, Sudhir and Zeeshan are sitting in a straight row facing North. Sudhir and Zeeshan are in the centre. Ali and Parth are at the corners. Roy is sitting to the immediate left of Ali. Who is sitting to the immediate right of Parth ?
questions.explanation: Facing north, Roy can be to Ali's immediate left only if Ali is at the right end, with Roy fifth from the left. Parth is then at the left end and Sudhir and Zeeshan take the third and fourth places, so Minal is second, to Parth's immediate right.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘Flames are bright’ is written as ‘@ # %’ and ‘Bright is sun flames’ is written as ‘* # 7 @’. Which one of the following is the possible code for ‘is’ in that code language?
questions.explanation: 'Flames' and 'bright' are in both sentences and share the codes @ and #, so 'are' is %. 'Is' and 'sun' take * and 7, so of the options only * can be the code for 'is'.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. Some A are B. II. All C are B. Conclusions: I. Some B are A’s is a possibility. II. No C is A. III. All A are C.
questions.explanation: 'Some A are B' means some B are A, so conclusion I is true and certainly possible. Nothing fixes how A and C relate, so neither 'No C is A' nor 'All A are C' must follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'ri ti gi' is written as 'Usha playing cards', 'si ni gi' is written as 'Asha playing tennis' and 'ri si wi' is written as 'cards and tennis'. What is the code for the word 'tennis' in that language?
questions.explanation: 'Tennis' is the only word in both the second and third sentences, and 'si' the only code in both, so 'tennis' is 'si'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'PIZZA' is written as 'QJAAB' and 'BLACK' is written as ‘CMBDL’. How will 'BUZZY' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one place forward, Z becoming A: PIZZA → QJAAB and BLACK → CMBDL. So BUZZY → CVAAZ.

questions.text: Which two signs need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 352 × 8 − 330 + 125 ÷ 4 = 214
A, B, C, D, E, F and G give a test. A scores more than B, C and D. G scores more than E and F. F scores more than A. Who scores the highest in the test?
questions.explanation: F scores more than A, who scores more than B, C and D, and G scores more than F and E, so G scores the highest.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. DGP : WTK :: MOS : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y and so on): D → W, G → T, P → K. So M → N, O → L, S → H: NLH.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (2, 4, 36); (4, 6, 100)
questions.explanation: The third number is the square of the sum of the first two: (2 + 4)² = 36 and (4 + 6)² = 100. Likewise (4 + 4)² = 64.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the sixth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and the third number is related to the fourth number. 1503 : 3004 :: 871 : 1740 :: ? : 142
questions.explanation: The second number is twice the first minus 2: 1503 × 2 − 2 = 3004 and 871 × 2 − 2 = 1740. So ? × 2 − 2 = 142 gives 72.

questions.text: Nine people Asha, Bishal, Carol, Dinky, Emily, Farah, Golu, Harsh, and Itika are watching a movie in a theatre sitting in a straight row facing North. Bishal is at one end of the row. Harsh is seated adjacent to both Farah and Golu. Carol is to the immediate right of Dinky and in the third place to the right of Emily. Asha is on the immediate left of Farah. Farah is in the third place to the left of Bishal. Who are at the ends of the row?
questions.explanation: Farah is third to the left of Bishal, so Bishal is at the right end (ninth) and Farah sixth, with Asha fifth, Harsh seventh and Golu eighth. Carol, just right of Dinky, is third to the right of Emily, which fits only Emily first, Dinky third and Carol fourth, leaving Itika second. The ends are Emily and Bishal.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. A 1 : E 3 :: M 7 : Q 9 :: S 5 : ?
questions.explanation: The letter moves 4 places forward and the number rises by 2: A 1 → E 3 and M 7 → Q 9. So S 5 → W 7.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 6, 9, 7, 10, 8, 11, ?
questions.explanation: The steps alternate +3 and −2: 6, 9, 7, 10, 8, 11, then 11 − 2 = 9.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No atom is a molecule. No molecule is an element. Conclusions: I. It is possible for some atoms to be elements. II. Some elements are molecules.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: No statement links atoms and elements directly, so some atoms being elements is possible and I follows. 'No molecule is an element' rules out II.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘–‘ are interchanged and also ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 40 × 10 − 20 + 10 ÷ 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 40 ÷ 10 + 20 − 10 × 2 = 4 + 20 − 20 = 4.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. ROM : SRT :: PNA : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, +3 and +7: R → S, O → R, M → T. So P → Q, N → Q, A → H: QQH.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. TX, ZD, FJ, LP, ?
questions.explanation: Both letters move 6 places forward each time, wrapping round after Z: T, Z, F, L, R and X, D, J, P, V. The next term is RV.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'POINT' is coded as '11', and 'GRANDST' is coded as '11'. How will 'HEMANT' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Add the letters' places in the alphabet, then the digits of the total: POINT = 16 + 15 + 9 + 14 + 20 = 74 → 7 + 4 = 11 and GRANDST = 7 + 18 + 1 + 14 + 4 + 19 + 20 = 83 → 8 + 3 = 11. HEMANT = 8 + 5 + 13 + 1 + 14 + 20 = 61 → 6 + 1 = 7.

questions.text: In which state of India is the Iravatanesvara temple situated?
questions.explanation: The Iravatanesvara temple, a Shiva temple of the Pallava period built in the reign of Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha), stands in Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu.

questions.text: Which of the following cities existed in the Indus Valley Civilization?
questions.explanation: Harappa, on the Ravi in present-day Pakistan, was the first Indus Valley city to be excavated (1921) and gives the civilisation its other name, the Harappan civilisation. Sanchi is a later Buddhist site and Muziris an ancient port on the Kerala coast.

questions.text: What is the atomic number of Carbon as per Mendeleev's Periodic Table?
questions.explanation: Carbon's atomic number, the number of protons in its nucleus, is 6. Mendeleev himself ordered his table by atomic mass (about 12 for carbon); atomic numbers came later.

questions.text: The study of human populations including their size, composition and distribution across space and the process through which populations change is called ______.
questions.explanation: Demography is the study of human populations: their size, make-up and distribution, and how they change through births, deaths and migration.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs of folk dance and the state associated with is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Ghoomar (Ghumar) is a folk dance of Rajasthan, not Bihar. Giddha is from Punjab, the Wancho dance from Arunachal Pradesh and the Nongkrem dance from Meghalaya.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers rises in the Nepal Himalayas?
questions.explanation: NCERT names the Ghaghara, Gandak and Kosi as the Ganga tributaries that rise in the Nepal Himalaya. The Chenab rises in Himachal Pradesh, as the Chandra and the Bhaga, and the Betwa and Chambal in Madhya Pradesh.

questions.text: How many different levels of courts are there in India?
questions.explanation: India has three levels of courts: the district (subordinate) courts, a High Court for each state or group of states, and the Supreme Court at the top.

questions.text: Aves are warm-blooded animals and have a ______ heart.
questions.explanation: Birds (class Aves) are warm-blooded and, like mammals, have a four-chambered heart that keeps oxygen-rich and oxygen-poor blood apart.

questions.text: Ustad Zakir Hussain is a famous Indian ______ player.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'Table', the paper's spelling of 'tabla': Ustad Zakir Hussain (1951-2024), son of the tabla player Ustad Alla Rakha, was among the world's best-known tabla players.

questions.text: Joint sector industry is one of the classifications of industries on the basis of ______.
options: bulk and weight of raw material
questions.explanation: By ownership, industries are public sector, private sector, joint sector (owned jointly by the state and private parties) and cooperative sector.

questions.text: As per Census 2011, which of the following metro cities was the most populated in India?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 counted Greater Mumbai as India's most populous city, with about 1.24 crore people (about 1.84 crore in its urban agglomeration), ahead of Delhi.

questions.text: Which Indian state government launched Project Sadbhavana in February 2022?
questions.explanation: In February 2022 the Assam government launched Project Sadbhavana, a drive to dispose of long-pending files in the state secretariat at Dispur.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year did Tipu Sultan die defending his capital Seringapatam?
questions.explanation: Tipu Sultan was killed on 4 May 1799 defending Seringapatam (Srirangapatna) against the British in the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.

questions.text: In the Union Budget of India 2022, what percentage of tax has been levied on transfer of digital assets (cryptocurrency)?
questions.explanation: The Union Budget 2022-23, presented on 1 February 2022, taxed income from the transfer of virtual digital assets such as cryptocurrency at 30%, with 1% TDS on such transfers.

questions.text: Ajit Kumar Doval is the fifth and current __________________ to the Prime Minister of India.
questions.explanation: Ajit Kumar Doval became India's fifth National Security Advisor in May 2014, after Brajesh Mishra, J N Dixit, M K Narayanan and Shivshankar Menon, and held the post when the exam was held (July 2022).

questions.text: Which of the following teams won the ICC Women’s World Cup 2021/22?
questions.explanation: Australia won the 2022 ICC Women's World Cup in New Zealand, beating England in the final at Christchurch on 3 April 2022.

questions.text: Padma Subrahmanyam is known for which classical dance form?
questions.explanation: Padma Subrahmanyam is a Bharatanatyam dancer, choreographer and scholar of the Natya Shastra.

questions.text: Which of the following does NOT fall under Non-Chordates?
questions.explanation: Vertebrates are a subphylum of the Chordata. Annelida, Porifera and Mollusca are non-chordate phyla, animals without a notochord.

questions.text: Which of the following is one of the key features of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Constitution divides powers between the Union and the states, which makes federalism one of its key features. It also sets up an independent judiciary and a secular, democratic state, the opposite of the other options.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: ____________ was founded by the Dadoba Pandurang and his brother Atmaram Pandurang in 1863 when Keshub Chandra Sen visited Maharashtra, with an aim to make people believe in one God and worship only one God.
questions.explanation: The description fits the Prarthana Samaj, founded in Bombay by Atmaram Pandurang after Keshub Chandra Sen's visit to promote the worship of one God; the year usually given is 1867, not the 1863 in the question. Satyashodhak Samaj was founded by Jyotiba Phule, Arya Samaj by Dayanand Saraswati and Brahmo Samaj by Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

questions.text: Which planet in the solar system is considered as Earth’s twin?
questions.explanation: Venus is called Earth's twin because it is close to Earth in size and density, and it is the planet that comes nearest to Earth.

questions.text: Who among the following Chola rulers built Nishumbhasudini Goddess temple in Thanjavur?
questions.explanation: Vijayalaya, founder of the Chola line of Thanjavur, took the Kaveri delta from the Muttaraiyar in the middle of the ninth century, built the town of Thanjavur and a temple there for the goddess Nishumbhasudini.

questions.text: What is the name of Mahatma Gandhi’s autobiography ?
options: The Story of My Experiments with Truth
questions.explanation: Gandhi's autobiography is 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth'. 'Justice for the Judge' is Ranjan Gogoi's, 'The Bandit Queen of India' Phoolan Devi's and 'My Music, My Life' Ravi Shankar's.

questions.text: Who among the following is the first Indian Grandmaster to become Women's Chess World Rapid Champion?
questions.explanation: Koneru Humpy won the Women's World Rapid Chess Championship in Moscow in December 2019, the first Indian to do so.

questions.text: The International Sand Art festival is usually held in _______.
questions.explanation: The International Sand Art Festival is held each December on Chandrabhaga beach near Konark, Odisha, alongside the Konark Festival.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The pirates will try to ______ the gold ornaments.
questions.explanation: To 'seize' is to take hold of something by force, as pirates would the gold. 'Cease' means to stop.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words. One who collects coins
questions.explanation: A numismatist collects or studies coins. A philatelist collects stamps and a bibliophile loves books.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. I may sound crazy but I am not an “imbecile.”
questions.explanation: An 'imbecile' is a stupid person, and so is a 'dunce'. A 'sage' is a wise person, 'prudent' means wise and 'credible' believable.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Rescuers used a special device for finding people ______ in collapsed buildings.
questions.explanation: People 'trapped' in collapsed buildings are caught there and cannot get out, so rescuers must find them.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. If nature ______ to degrade, the world’s economic output will suffer sooner or later.
questions.explanation: In a first conditional the 'if' clause takes the simple present, and the singular 'nature' takes 'continues': 'If nature continues to degrade, ...'

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. He pays me six dollars “the month of this” house.
questions.explanation: A rate per period takes 'a' ('six dollars a month'), and the payment is 'for' the house: 'He pays me six dollars a month for this house.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Fatal
questions.explanation: 'Fatal' means causing death: 'deadly'. 'Restorative' means healing, nearly the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word from the given sentence. He leaned left, bringing the “blunt” side of his sword up flat against his palm.
questions.explanation: A 'blunt' edge is not sharp: 'dull'. 'Sharp' and 'keen' are its opposites.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Abstruce' is misspelt: the word is 'abstruse', meaning hard to understand.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A large bundle bound for storage or transport
questions.explanation: A bale is a large bundle of goods, such as cotton or hay, bound for storage or transport. An apiary is a place where bees are kept.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. She was stuck in “his imagination for many a hour as a force” to be reckoned with.
options: his imagination for many hour as a force
his imagination for many an hour as a force
his imagination for many an hours as a force
questions.explanation: 'Many a' takes a singular noun, and 'hour' begins with a vowel sound, so it is 'many an hour'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom. Does my name “ring a bell” for you?
questions.explanation: If something 'rings a bell', it sounds familiar: the speaker asks whether the name reminds the listener of anything.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required.’ The laws of nature “are unbiased,” ensuring that each person benefits from its bounties.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'laws' takes 'are', and the present tense fits 'ensuring that each person benefits', so the sentence is correct as it stands.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. How the students approach / education today has / altered significant.
questions.explanation: The verb 'altered' must be modified by an adverb: 'has altered significantly'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Kick someone when they are down
options: To be angry with or disappointed in someone
To cause further trouble to someone already in a difficult situation
questions.explanation: To 'kick someone when they are down' is to make things worse for someone who is already in trouble.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Definitely' has 'finite' in the middle: de-finite-ly. The other three spell it with an 'a'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I am planning a get together ______ Monday.
questions.explanation: Days and dates take 'on': 'a get together on Monday'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Vicious
questions.explanation: 'Vicious' means cruel or violent; its opposite is 'gentle'.

questions.text: Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. I like reading fictional stories besides write poems.
questions.explanation: 'Besides' is a preposition here, so the verb after it takes the '-ing' form: 'besides writing poems'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. No matter how (1) ______ time you (2) ______ to improve your mental and emotional health, you will still need the company of (3) ______ to feel and function at your best. Humans are social (4) ______ with emotional needs for relationships and positive connections to others. We’re not meant to survive, (5) ______ alone thrive, in isolation.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. (1)
questions.explanation: 'Time' is uncountable, so 'how much time'; 'many' goes with countable nouns.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. No matter how (1) ______ time you (2) ______ to improve your mental and emotional health, you will still need the company of (3) ______ to feel and function at your best. Humans are social (4) ______ with emotional needs for relationships and positive connections to others. We’re not meant to survive, (5) ______ alone thrive, in isolation.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. (2)
questions.explanation: To 'devote' time to something is to spend it on that purpose. 'Promote', 'assess' and 'proceed' do not take 'time' in this sense.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. No matter how (1) ______ time you (2) ______ to improve your mental and emotional health, you will still need the company of (3) ______ to feel and function at your best. Humans are social (4) ______ with emotional needs for relationships and positive connections to others. We’re not meant to survive, (5) ______ alone thrive, in isolation.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. (3)
questions.explanation: 'The company of others' means being with other people; 'some', 'any' and 'few' would each need a noun after them.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. No matter how (1) ______ time you (2) ______ to improve your mental and emotional health, you will still need the company of (3) ______ to feel and function at your best. Humans are social (4) ______ with emotional needs for relationships and positive connections to others. We’re not meant to survive, (5) ______ alone thrive, in isolation.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. (4)
questions.explanation: 'Humans are social creatures': 'creatures' are living beings. 'Kingdoms', 'populations' and 'lives' cannot describe a human.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. No matter how (1) ______ time you (2) ______ to improve your mental and emotional health, you will still need the company of (3) ______ to feel and function at your best. Humans are social (4) ______ with emotional needs for relationships and positive connections to others. We’re not meant to survive, (5) ______ alone thrive, in isolation.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank No. (5)
questions.explanation: 'Let alone' means 'still less': we are not meant even to survive in isolation, still less to thrive.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'GOAL' is coded as '917314', and 'PBKS' is coded as '1841321'. How will 'HAMD' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as its place in the alphabet plus 2: G O A L → 9, 17, 3, 14 and P B K S → 18, 4, 13, 21. So H A M D → 10, 3, 15, 6: 103156.

questions.text: After interchanging the given two signs × and –, what will be the value of the given expression? 10 + 5 – 6 ÷ 2 × 5
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 10 + 5 × 6 ÷ 2 − 5 = 10 + 15 − 5 = 20.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'he is sick' is written as 'blue red pink', 'he wants apple' is written as 'green violet red', and 'apple is tasty' is written as 'blue green yellow'. How will 'tasty' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: 'He' is in the first two sentences, so he = red; 'is' in the first and third, so is = blue; 'apple' in the second and third, so apple = green. The code left in 'apple is tasty' is yellow.

questions.text: Which two numbers need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 22 − 9 ÷ 5 + 10 × 1 = 29
Select the number from the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 137, 125, 113, 101, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 12 less than the one before: 101 − 12 = 89.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. ABC2 : ZYX7 :: PQR21 : KJI26 :: MNO11 : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by its opposite (A↔Z, B↔Y, C↔X and so on) and 5 is added to the number: ABC2 → ZYX7 and PQR21 → KJI26. So MNO11 → NML16.

questions.text: Four girls A, B, C, and D are sitting in a row, facing towards the south (but not necessarily in the same order). Four boys P, Q, R and S are sitting in a row, facing towards the face of these girls (but not necessarily in the same order). P and C are diagonally opposite to each other. A is second to the right of C. S is the immediate neighbour of Q and R. C is facing R. Which of the following pairs of persons facing each other is definitely correct?
questions.explanation: Number the places 1 to 4 from west to east; the girls face south, so their right is west. P and C, diagonally opposite, sit at opposite ends, and A second to the right of C puts C at 4 and A at 2. R faces C at 4, so P is at 1, and S, between Q and R, is at 3, leaving Q at 2, facing A. B and D could sit either way round, so only AQ is certain.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. AY, BX, ?, DV, EU, FT
questions.explanation: The first letters run A, B, C, D, E, F and the second Y, X, W, V, U, T: CW.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 347 : 14 :: 122 : 5 :: 244 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the sum of the digits of the first: 3 + 4 + 7 = 14 and 1 + 2 + 2 = 5. So 2 + 4 + 4 = 10.

questions.text: Identify the number that does NOT belong to the following series. 414, 430, 462, 526, 664, 910
questions.explanation: The differences double: 16, 32, 64, 128, 256. The fifth term should be 526 + 128 = 654, and 654 + 256 = 910; 664 does not fit.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘Heat is waves’ is coded as ‘7 6 @’, and ‘waves are dramatic not’ is coded as ‘3 4 % 7’. What can be the code for ‘Heat’ in that language?
questions.explanation: 'Waves' is in both sentences and 7 is the only code they share, so waves = 7. 'Heat' is then 6 or @, and of these only @ is offered.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. GP : KK :: MN : ?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves 4 forward and the second 5 back: G → K and P → K. So M → Q and N → I: QI.

questions.text: Five professors A, B, C, D and E are sitting in a row facing the North (not necessarily in the same order). A is second to the left of D. Only two professors are sitting between C and E. No professor is sitting to the right of E. How many professors are sitting to the left of D?
questions.explanation: No one sits to the right of E, so E is at the right end (place 5) and C, with two between them, at place 2. A is second to the left of D, so A and D are at 1 and 3, and B at 4. Two professors, A and C, sit to the left of D.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (8, 12, 48); (6, 18, 54)
questions.explanation: The third number is half the product of the first two: 8 × 12 ÷ 2 = 48 and 6 × 18 ÷ 2 = 54. Likewise 4 × 8 ÷ 2 = 16.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. No R is S. II. All X are R. Conclusions: I. Some R are X. II. Some S are X. III. All X are S.
questions.explanation: All X are R, so some R are X: I follows. As no R is S and every X is an R, no X is S, so II and III are both false.

questions.text: In a certain code language, '321' means 'hot branded milk', '653' means 'nice hot day', '985' means 'day and night', then what is the code for 'nice' in the same code language?
questions.explanation: 'Hot' is in the first two sentences, whose common code is 3; 'day' is in the last two, whose common code is 5. In '653' (nice hot day) the code left for 'nice' is 6.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. PRA : SUZ :: GOS : ?
questions.explanation: The first two letters move 3 forward and the third is replaced by its opposite letter: P → S, R → U and A → Z. So G → J, O → R and S → H: JRH.

questions.text: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) is regulated by _________.
questions.explanation: SIDBI, set up in 1990 under its own Act to finance small industries, is an all-India financial institution regulated and supervised by the Reserve Bank of India.

questions.text: As per the Preamble of the Constitution of India, India is a/an ______.
questions.explanation: The Preamble declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic: its head of state is elected, not hereditary.

questions.text: Which of the following universities was founded by Kumaragupta, the ruler of the Gupta dynasty?
questions.explanation: Nalanda mahavihara in Bihar is credited to the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I, in the 5th century CE. Taxila is far older, and the Delhi and Pune universities are modern.

questions.text: Manika Batra is associated with which sport?
questions.explanation: Manika Batra is an Indian table tennis player; she won the women's singles gold at the 2018 Commonwealth Games.

questions.text: According to the Constitution of India, there shall be a Comptroller and Auditor General of India who shall be appointed by the _______.
questions.explanation: Under Article 148 the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed by the President, by warrant under his hand and seal.

questions.text: Khajuraho temple in Madhya Pradesh is an example of ___________ style of temple architecture.
questions.explanation: Khajuraho's temples, built under the Chandela rulers, are in the northern Nagara style, with curved shikharas. Dravida is the southern style, and Vesara, of which Hoysala temples are a form, mixes the two.

questions.text: When a cell divides by meiosis it produces ______ new cells.
questions.explanation: Meiosis has two divisions, so one cell gives four daughter cells, each with half the number of chromosomes.

questions.text: The Inland Vessels Bill, 2021 is associated with the Ministry of ________________.
questions.explanation: The Inland Vessels Bill, 2021, brought by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways and passed by Parliament in July-August 2021, replaced the Inland Vessels Act, 1917 with one law for the whole country.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: What was the original name of Swami Vivekananda?
questions.explanation: Swami Vivekananda was born Narendranath Datta in Calcutta in 1863. Mula Sankara (Mool Shankar) was Swami Dayananda Saraswati's name, and Vardhamana Mahavira's.

questions.text: Limestone, chalk and marble are different forms of ______.
questions.explanation: Limestone, chalk and marble are all forms of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃).

questions.text: Which TMC candidate won the Ballygunge (West Bengal) by-poll election in April 2022?
questions.explanation: Babul Supriyo won the Ballygunge Assembly by-poll for the Trinamool Congress; the result was declared on 16 April 2022. The seat had fallen vacant on the death of Subrata Mukherjee.

questions.text: Which of the following states has the highest reserves of haematite ore in India?
questions.explanation: The Indian Bureau of Mines puts the largest share of India's haematite reserves and resources in Odisha, ahead of Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Karnataka.

questions.text: Alarmel Valli is associated with which classical dance of India?
questions.explanation: Alarmel Valli of Chennai is a Bharatanatyam dancer of the Pandanallur style.

questions.text: ‘Wings of Fire' is a famous autobiography of which Indian scientist?
questions.explanation: 'Wings of Fire' (1999), written with Arun Tiwari, is the autobiography of A P J Abdul Kalam, the missile scientist who later became President.

questions.text: In its longitudinal extent, the Himalaya consists of ______ parallel ranges.
questions.explanation: NCERT describes the Himalaya as three parallel ranges along its length: the Great or Inner Himalaya (Himadri), the Lesser Himalaya (Himachal) and the Shiwaliks.

questions.text: Pulakesin I was the founder of ______ dynasty of South India.
questions.explanation: Pulakesin I founded the Chalukya dynasty of Badami (Vatapi) in the 6th century CE, making Vatapi his capital.

questions.text: Which of the following cell organelles help to keep the cell clean by digesting any foreign material as well as worn-out cell organelles?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes are membrane sacs of digestive enzymes that break down foreign material and worn-out organelles, keeping the cell clean.

questions.text: Who among the following is a famous tennis player?
questions.explanation: Mahesh Bhupathi is a tennis player, winner of several Grand Slam doubles and mixed doubles titles. Neeraj Chopra throws the javelin, Milkha Singh was a sprinter and T C Yohannan a long jumper.

questions.text: The number of live births per thousand persons in a year is called _____.
questions.explanation: The birth rate is the number of live births per thousand people in a year; the death rate counts deaths the same way.

questions.text: MS Subbulakshmi was a famous ________ singer of India.
questions.explanation: M S Subbulakshmi was a Carnatic vocalist, the first musician to receive the Bharat Ratna (1998).

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Mangal Pandey was hanged to death for attacking British officers in Barrackpore on ______.
questions.explanation: Mangal Pandey of the 34th Bengal Native Infantry attacked British officers at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857, the date the blank asks for; he was hanged on 8 April 1857.

questions.text: Pandit Birju Maharaj who passed away in January 2022 was related with which classical dance of India?
questions.explanation: Pandit Birju Maharaj was a Kathak dancer of the Lucknow (Kalka-Bindadin) gharana.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Have a whale of a time
options: A good thing that seems bad at first
Have an exceptionally fun or exciting experience
questions.explanation: To 'have a whale of a time' is to enjoy oneself very much.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Public agencies and nonprofit conservation groups is already working to promote conservation.
questions.explanation: The subject, 'public agencies and nonprofit conservation groups', is plural, so the verb must be 'are': 'groups are already working'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. The thing about anger is that it can either been a helpful emotion or a discouraging one.
options: a helpful emotion or a discouraging one
is that it can either been
questions.explanation: After the modal 'can' a verb takes its base form: 'it can either be a helpful emotion or a discouraging one'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person exhibiting excessive worry about one’s health
questions.explanation: A hypochondriac worries too much about his or her health, imagining illness. A megalomaniac is obsessed with his own power.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. I “work hardly too” earn bread and butter for my family.
questions.explanation: 'Hard' is the adverb for working with effort ('hardly' means scarcely), and purpose is shown by 'to', not 'too': 'I work hard to earn bread and butter for my family.'

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. I was at a party / with some off my / friends in Mumbai.
questions.explanation: The preposition is 'of', not 'off': 'with some of my friends in Mumbai'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Crocodile tears
questions.explanation: 'Crocodile tears' are false tears, a show of sorrow that is not really felt.

questions.text: Select the option that corrects the misspelt words in the given sentence. A baloon may liave the earth with a charg.
options: A balloon may leave the earth with a charge.
A ballon may leave the earth with a chargge.
A balloon may live the earth with a charrge.
A ballun may leave the earth with a charge.
questions.explanation: The correct spellings are 'balloon' (double 'l', double 'o'), 'leave' and 'charge'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'inability': 'in-' with 'ability'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Obedient
questions.explanation: 'Obedient' means willing to obey; 'resistant', refusing to go along, is its opposite. 'Compliant' and 'submissive' are synonyms.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Intricate
questions.explanation: 'Intricate' means having many connected parts or details, that is 'complicated'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. A better plan is “to going and has” a lavish dinner at a fine restaurant.
questions.explanation: 'To' takes the base form of the verb, and 'have' must match 'go': 'A better plan is to go and have a lavish dinner at a fine restaurant.' The options repeat the 'is' printed just before the underlined words.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who feeds on human flesh
questions.explanation: A cannibal eats human flesh. A hedonist lives for pleasure, a stoic bears hardship without complaint and a Samaritan helps people in need.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. All branded shoes are priced “extravagantly.”
questions.explanation: Shoes priced 'extravagantly' are priced far too high, that is 'expensively'. 'Modestly', 'economically' and 'meagerly' point the other way.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. It’s ______ too late to start your own business.
questions.explanation: 'It's never too late' to do something means it can still be done.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. It was impossible ______ guess what he was doing.
questions.explanation: 'Impossible' is followed by the to-infinitive: 'impossible to guess'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Evident
questions.explanation: 'Evident' means plain to see; 'indistinct', not clear, is its opposite. 'Obvious' is a synonym.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A person who believes in or tries to bring about a state of lawlessness
questions.explanation: An anarchist believes in or works for a state without government or law. 'Ephemeral' means short-lived, a 'deluge' is a flood and a 'gazette' an official journal.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The sudden death of our uncle was ______________ for all of us.
questions.explanation: A sudden death is 'tragic', causing great sorrow; 'fragile', 'gentle' and 'dissuasive' do not fit the sense.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Nitrogen is essential to life (1)______ Earth. It is a component of all proteins, and it can be (2)______ in all living systems. Nitrogen compounds are (3)______ in organic materials, foods, fertilisers, explosives and poisons. Nitrogen is crucial to life, (4)______ in excess it can also be (5)______ to the environment.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Life 'on' Earth: 'on' is used for the surface of a planet.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Nitrogen is essential to life (1)______ Earth. It is a component of all proteins, and it can be (2)______ in all living systems. Nitrogen compounds are (3)______ in organic materials, foods, fertilisers, explosives and poisons. Nitrogen is crucial to life, (4)______ in excess it can also be (5)______ to the environment.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: After 'can be' the passive needs the past participle: 'it can be found in all living systems'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Nitrogen is essential to life (1)______ Earth. It is a component of all proteins, and it can be (2)______ in all living systems. Nitrogen compounds are (3)______ in organic materials, foods, fertilisers, explosives and poisons. Nitrogen is crucial to life, (4)______ in excess it can also be (5)______ to the environment.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: Nitrogen compounds are 'present' in, that is found in, organic materials, foods, fertilisers and the rest.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Nitrogen is essential to life (1)______ Earth. It is a component of all proteins, and it can be (2)______ in all living systems. Nitrogen compounds are (3)______ in organic materials, foods, fertilisers, explosives and poisons. Nitrogen is crucial to life, (4)______ in excess it can also be (5)______ to the environment.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'But' introduces the contrast: nitrogen is crucial to life, but in excess it can also do harm.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Nitrogen is essential to life (1)______ Earth. It is a component of all proteins, and it can be (2)______ in all living systems. Nitrogen compounds are (3)______ in organic materials, foods, fertilisers, explosives and poisons. Nitrogen is crucial to life, (4)______ in excess it can also be (5)______ to the environment.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: In excess nitrogen can be 'harmful' to the environment, the contrast with 'crucial to life'.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) 2 : 6 :: 4 : 60 :: 7 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is the cube of the first minus the first: 2³ − 2 = 6 and 4³ − 4 = 60. So 7³ − 7 = 343 − 7 = 336.

questions.text: Six girls, Pooja, Qimat, Reeti, Shweta, Tejaswini and Vineeta, are sitting around a circular table. All of them are facing towards the centre of the table (but not necessarily in the same order). Tejaswini is the immediate neighbour of Vineeta and Reeti. Pooja is to the immediate left of Vineeta. Qimat is fourth to the right of Pooja. Shweta is to the immediate left of Pooja.Who is sitting to the immediate left of Shweta?.
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, a person's left is the next seat clockwise. Clockwise the girls sit Vineeta, Pooja, Shweta, Qimat (fourth to the right of Pooja), Reeti and Tejaswini, who is between Reeti and Vineeta. The next seat clockwise from Shweta is Qimat's.

questions.text: Six persons are sitting in two straight rows, facing north. Their names are Farhan, Utkarsh, Yugal, Krishna, Chaman and Manish. Farhan and Manish are sitting at diagonally opposite ends. Utkarsh is in the top row and to the immediate right of Farhan. Krishna is second to the left of Manish while Yugal and Krishna are not in the same row. Who is sitting at the diagonally opposite end to Yugal?
questions.explanation: Farhan sits at an end of the top row with Utkarsh to his immediate right, so Farhan is at its left end. Manish, diagonally opposite, is at the right end of the bottom row and Krishna, second to his left, at its left end. Yugal is not in Krishna's row, so the top row is Farhan, Utkarsh and Yugal, Chaman sits between Krishna and Manish, and the end diagonally opposite Yugal is Krishna's.

questions.text: After interchanging which two signs will the value of the given expression be ‘356’? 133 + 49 – 16 ÷ 2 × 34
Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. PAN : SCP :: HOP : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +3, +2 and +2: P → S, A → C, N → P. Likewise H → K, O → Q, P → R: KQR.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. ROM, URJ, XUG, AXD, ?
questions.explanation: The first and second letters move 3 forward and the third 3 back: R, U, X, A, D; O, R, U, X, A; M, J, G, D, A. The next cluster is DAA.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the fourth term is related to the third term. TREE : RTEE :: KEEP : EKPE :: SOLO : ?
questions.explanation: Each pair of letters is swapped: TR EE → RT EE and KE EP → EK PE. So SO LO → OS OL: OSOL.

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (NOTE : Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.) (3, 6, 18) (5, 7, 35)
questions.explanation: The third number is the product of the first two: 3 × 6 = 18 and 5 × 7 = 35. Likewise 6 × 14 = 84; the other sets would need 104, 84 and 96.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘Here we go west’ is written as ‘8 6 4 9’, ‘West and east best’ is written as ‘4 @ # pr’ and ‘East direction sun’ is written as ‘# jt qm’. Which one of the following is the possible code for ‘direction east’ in that code language?
questions.explanation: 'West' is in the first two sentences, so it is 4; 'east' is in the last two, so it is #. 'Direction' is then 'jt' or 'qm', so 'direction east' can be '# qm', the only option with #.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some pets are birds. All birds are mats. Conclusions: I. All mats are birds. II. Some mats are pets.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: The pets that are birds are mats, so some mats are pets (II). The mats need not all be birds, so I does not follow.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'IFSP' is written as 'JHTR' and 'MPWF' is written as ‘NRXH’. How will 'TOAD' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, +2, +1, +2: IFSP → JHTR and MPWF → NRXH. So TOAD → UQBF.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No plate is a spoon. Some plates are forks. All forks are knives. Conclusions: I. Some plates are knives is a possibility. II. No spoon is a fork.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: Some plates are forks and all forks are knives, so some plates are certainly knives, and what is certain is also possible: I follows. The forks that are plates are not spoons, but other forks may be, so II does not follow.

questions.text: D 2 is related to H 6 in a certain way. In the same way, L 11 is related to P 15. To which of the following is T 18 related following the same logic?
questions.explanation: The letter and the number both move 4 forward: D → H and 2 → 6, L → P and 11 → 15. So T → X and 18 → 22: X 22.

questions.text: Which two signs need to be interchanged to make the following equation correct? 9 + 3 − 4 ÷ 5 × 2 = 9
questions.explanation: After interchanging + and ÷: 9 ÷ 3 − 4 + 5 × 2 = 3 − 4 + 10 = 9.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 728, 717, 695, 662, 618, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are −11, −22, −33 and −44, so the next is −55: 618 − 55 = 563.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'ANAEMIA' is written as 'AOAENIA', 'AQUEOUS' is written as 'ARUEOUT', and 'LIVELY' is written as 'MIWEMZ'. How will 'EUGENIA' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each consonant moves one letter forward and each vowel stays (Y counts as a consonant: LIVELY → MIWEMZ). So E U G E N I A → E U H E O I A: EUHEOIA.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘POR’ is coded as ‘52’ and ‘AND’ is coded as ‘22’. How will ‘VXB’ be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet plus 3: P + O + R = 16 + 15 + 18 = 49 and 49 + 3 = 52; A + N + D = 1 + 14 + 4 = 19 and 19 + 3 = 22. So V + X + B = 22 + 24 + 2 = 48 and 48 + 3 = 51.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) 12 : 20 :: 8 : 12 :: 34 : ?
questions.explanation: The second number is twice the first minus 4: 12 × 2 − 4 = 20 and 8 × 2 − 4 = 12. So 34 × 2 − 4 = 64.

questions.text: Tanjore Balasaraswati was known for which classical dance form?
questions.explanation: T. Balasaraswati (1918-1984) of the hereditary Thanjavur tradition was among the greatest Bharatanatyam dancers. Bihu is a folk dance of Assam, and Manipuri and Odissi are other classical forms.

questions.text: Which of the following persons won the ‘Best Female Debut’ Award at the 2021 Paralympic Sports Awards 2021?
questions.explanation: The International Paralympic Committee's 2021 Paralympic Sport Awards named the Indian shooter Avani Lekhara the best female debut, for her Tokyo 2020 gold in the women's 10 m air rifle standing SH1 and bronze in the 50 m rifle three positions SH1.

questions.text: Which of the following rivers forms the largest river system of Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: NCERT calls the Luni the largest river system of Rajasthan, west of the Aravallis; it rises near Pushkar and ends in the Rann of Kutch. The Krishna, Narmada and Tapi do not flow through Rajasthan.

questions.text: In human beings, the small intestine is coiled and is about ______ metres long.
questions.explanation: NCERT's Class 7 science text describes the small intestine as highly coiled and about 7.5 m long; it is the longest part of the alimentary canal.

questions.text: Who among the following was the first athlete to represent India in fencing at the Tokyo Olympics 2020?
questions.explanation: C A Bhavani Devi, a sabre fencer from Tamil Nadu, was the first Indian to compete in fencing at the Olympics, at Tokyo 2020. Aditi Ashok is a golfer, P T Usha a sprinter and P V Sindhu a badminton player.

questions.text: A form of financial service which provides small loans and other financial services to poor and low-income households is called ______.
questions.explanation: Microfinance gives small loans (microcredit), savings and insurance to poor and low-income households that ordinary banks do not reach; in India it works largely through self-help groups and microfinance institutions.

questions.text: Which of the following are also called the amphibians of the plant kingdom?
questions.explanation: Bryophytes (mosses and liverworts) live on land but need water for fertilisation, as their sperm swim to the egg, so they are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom.

questions.text: Buddha attained enlightenment at ______.
questions.explanation: Siddhartha Gautama attained enlightenment under the Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya in Bihar. He gave his first sermon at Sarnath near Varanasi and died at Kusinara (Kushinagar).

questions.text: ‘Unfinished: A Memoir’ is the autobiography of ______.
questions.explanation: 'Unfinished: A Memoir' (2021) is the actor Priyanka Chopra Jonas's memoir.

questions.text: Which of the following festivals is celebrated when the annual harvest takes place in Assam?
questions.explanation: Magh (Bhogali) Bihu, in mid-January, marks the end of the harvest season in Assam with community feasts. Lohri is Punjab's festival, Pongal Tamil Nadu's, and Makaravilakku is held at Sabarimala in Kerala.

questions.text: Which of the following is considered to be the fifth state of matter?
questions.explanation: A Bose-Einstein condensate, formed when a gas of bosons is cooled almost to absolute zero so that the particles fall into the same lowest state, is called the fifth state of matter, after solid, liquid, gas and plasma.

questions.text: Which of the following peninsular rivers has the largest drainage basin?
questions.explanation: The Godavari, the longest peninsular river (the 'Dakshin Ganga'), also has the largest drainage basin among the peninsular rivers.

questions.text: A type of unemployment in rural areas when people are not able to find jobs during some months of the year is called ______.
questions.explanation: Seasonal unemployment comes when farm work is available only at sowing and harvest, leaving people without work for part of the year. Disguised unemployment is more people working on a farm than it needs.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Vasco da Gama, a Portuguese explorer came to India in ______.
questions.explanation: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut (Kozhikode) on the Malabar coast in May 1498, opening the sea route from Europe to India round the Cape of Good Hope.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following addressed the Indian National congress as its President in 1887?
questions.explanation: Badruddin Tyabji presided over the third session of the Congress, at Madras in 1887, its first Muslim president. W C Bonnerjee presided over the first session (Bombay, 1885) and Dadabhai Naoroji over the second (Calcutta, 1886).

questions.text: Which team lost to Dabang Delhi KC in the finals of the Pro Kabbadi League season 8?
questions.explanation: Dabang Delhi KC beat Patna Pirates 37-36 in the final of season 8 of the Pro Kabaddi League, in February 2022, for their first title.

questions.text: Soilless agriculture is called _______.
questions.explanation: Hydroponics is growing plants without soil, with their roots in water carrying dissolved mineral nutrients.

questions.text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution enshrines the Right against Exploitation?
questions.explanation: Articles 23 and 24 form the Right against Exploitation: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour, and Article 24 the employment of children in factories, mines and other hazardous work. Article 21 protects life and personal liberty, Article 22 guards against arbitrary arrest and Article 25 gives freedom of religion.

questions.text: What does ‘Chaitya’ in Buddhist architecture refer to?
questions.explanation: A chaitya is a Buddhist prayer hall, usually with a stupa at its far end, as in the rock-cut halls at Karla and Ajanta; a vihara is a monastery where monks lived.

questions.text: As per Census 2011, what is the Total Fertility Rate (an approximate range) in India?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 2.1-2.9: the Sample Registration System put India's total fertility rate at 2.4 children per woman in 2011, the census year.

questions.text: Who among the following is a famous Sitar player?
questions.explanation: Anoushka Shankar, daughter and pupil of Pandit Ravi Shankar, is a sitar player. Pandit Kishan Maharaj was a tabla player and Ustad Ali Ahmad Hussain Khan a shehnai player.

questions.text: As per the Constitution of India, the President of India shall hold office for a term of ______ from the date on which he enters upon his office.
questions.explanation: Under Article 56 the President holds office for a term of five years from the date on which he enters upon his office.

questions.text: Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Mohiniyattam, a graceful solo dance in the lasya style, is a classical dance of Kerala.

questions.text: Which Chola ruler built the Brihadeshwara Temple at Tanjore?
questions.explanation: The Brihadeshwara (Rajarajeshwaram) temple at Thanjavur was built by the Chola king Rajaraja I and completed around 1010 CE.

questions.text: Which state of India has set up District Investment Promotion Agencies (DIPA)?
questions.explanation: In 2021 Odisha decided to set up District Investment Promotion Agencies (DIPAs), chaired by the district collectors and working as district arms of IPICOL, the state's investment promotion agency.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. A keeper or custodian of a museum
questions.explanation: A curator is the person in charge of a museum's or gallery's collection.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence. The list included many “mundane,” routine tasks.
questions.explanation: 'Mundane' means dull and ordinary, so its opposite is 'exceptional'. 'Standard' and 'customary' are close to its meaning.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. The smell of this flower “make me felt dizzy.”
questions.explanation: 'The smell' is singular, so the verb is 'makes', and 'make' is followed by the bare infinitive 'feel': 'The smell of this flower makes me feel dizzy.' (The sheet's underline also takes in 'dizzy.', which the options leave out.)

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Hurdle
questions.explanation: A hurdle is an obstacle, an 'impediment'. 'Progress' and 'aid' are nearly opposite.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Apart from Germany, they also visited Italy and Austria during its business trip.
questions.explanation: The subject 'they' is plural, so the possessive must be 'their': 'during their business trip'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Suspend all the employees “which has been coming” late.
questions.explanation: Employees are people, so the relative pronoun is 'who', and the plural noun takes 'have': 'Suspend all the employees who have been coming late.'

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Any award, honour or laudatory notice
questions.explanation: An accolade is an award or an expression of praise. A 'complement' completes something, and a 'statute' is a law.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Thinking of talent as innate makes our world more manageable and more comfortable as it relieves a person of the _______ of expectation.
questions.explanation: To be relieved of something is to be freed from a weight: seeing talent as inborn frees a person from the 'burden' of expectation.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Agitate
questions.explanation: To 'agitate' is to disturb or excite; its opposite is to 'soothe', to calm. 'Distress' is close to its meaning.

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. But this immortality / will have purchased / at the price of / his immortal part.
questions.explanation: Immortality is what is bought, not the buyer, so the verb must be passive: 'will have been purchased'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'tendency', ending in '-ency'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. As he went through the street on an ______ that morning, he saw a woman with a cat under her arm.
questions.explanation: An errand is a short trip to do a task, such as buying or delivering something; one goes 'on an errand'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Something happening in three years
questions.explanation: 'Triennial' means happening every three years. 'Annual' is every year, 'biennial' every two years and 'millennial' every thousand years.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. We are selling a single orange ______ ₹10 but nobody is ready to buy it.
questions.explanation: The price something is sold at is introduced by 'for': to sell an orange 'for ₹10'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. I had never seen him lose his temper, and he governed our company with “an iron hand.”
questions.explanation: To govern 'with an iron hand' is to keep strict and harsh control.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Residents should keep an / eye out for strangers / acting suspecting in their areas
questions.explanation: The verb 'acting' needs an adverb of manner: 'acting suspiciously', not 'acting suspecting'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. When a plastic comb is rubbed on dry hair, “they acquired a” static charge.
questions.explanation: The subject 'a plastic comb' is singular, so the pronoun is 'it', and a general fact takes the simple present: 'it acquires a static charge'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. “Come rain or shine,” I will go to Paris tomorrow.
options: To come before the decided time
questions.explanation: 'Come rain or shine' means whatever happens, in any circumstances.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Laborious
questions.explanation: Said of a person, 'laborious' means hard-working and industrious, which is what 'assiduous' (diligent, persevering) means. 'Unsophisticated', 'profane' (irreverent) and 'pompous' have nothing to do with effort.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Coca-Cola is to become the new sponsor of the London Eye after (1) ______ a deal to replace France's EDF Energy. The capital's giant Ferris Wheel has been a (2) ______ tourist attraction since it was introduced in 2000, when it was (3) ______ as the Millennium Wheel. It was previously (4) ______ by British Airways before becoming the EDF Energy London Eye in 2011. Coca-Cola will take over in January after (5) ______ a two-year deal with the wheel's owner, Merlin Entertainments, for an undisclosed sum.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: Coca-Cola becomes the sponsor after 'signing' a deal, that is formally agreeing to one.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Coca-Cola is to become the new sponsor of the London Eye after (1) ______ a deal to replace France's EDF Energy. The capital's giant Ferris Wheel has been a (2) ______ tourist attraction since it was introduced in 2000, when it was (3) ______ as the Millennium Wheel. It was previously (4) ______ by British Airways before becoming the EDF Energy London Eye in 2011. Coca-Cola will take over in January after (5) ______ a two-year deal with the wheel's owner, Merlin Entertainments, for an undisclosed sum.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: A 'leading' tourist attraction is one of the most popular: the wheel has been one since it opened in 2000.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Coca-Cola is to become the new sponsor of the London Eye after (1) ______ a deal to replace France's EDF Energy. The capital's giant Ferris Wheel has been a (2) ______ tourist attraction since it was introduced in 2000, when it was (3) ______ as the Millennium Wheel. It was previously (4) ______ by British Airways before becoming the EDF Energy London Eye in 2011. Coca-Cola will take over in January after (5) ______ a two-year deal with the wheel's owner, Merlin Entertainments, for an undisclosed sum.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Known as' gives the name it went by: when it was introduced in 2000 it was called the Millennium Wheel.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Coca-Cola is to become the new sponsor of the London Eye after (1) ______ a deal to replace France's EDF Energy. The capital's giant Ferris Wheel has been a (2) ______ tourist attraction since it was introduced in 2000, when it was (3) ______ as the Millennium Wheel. It was previously (4) ______ by British Airways before becoming the EDF Energy London Eye in 2011. Coca-Cola will take over in January after (5) ______ a two-year deal with the wheel's owner, Merlin Entertainments, for an undisclosed sum.
