Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: The passage is about sponsors: British Airways 'sponsored' the wheel before it became the EDF Energy London Eye.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Coca-Cola is to become the new sponsor of the London Eye after (1) ______ a deal to replace France's EDF Energy. The capital's giant Ferris Wheel has been a (2) ______ tourist attraction since it was introduced in 2000, when it was (3) ______ as the Millennium Wheel. It was previously (4) ______ by British Airways before becoming the EDF Energy London Eye in 2011. Coca-Cola will take over in January after (5) ______ a two-year deal with the wheel's owner, Merlin Entertainments, for an undisclosed sum.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'striking': to 'strike a deal' is the set phrase for reaching an agreement. 'Forging' a deal is also heard, but 'strike' is the usual verb with 'deal', and 'discovering' and 'hedging' do not fit.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. TOM, UMP, VKS, ?, XGY
questions.explanation: The first letters run T, U, V, W, X (+1), the second O, M, K, I, G (−2) and the third M, P, S, V, Y (+3): WIV.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 121, 144, 169, ?, 225, 256
questions.explanation: The terms are the squares of 11 to 16: 11², 12², 13², 14² = 196, 15² and 16².

questions.text: Select the option in which the two numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers in the given number-pair. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) 17 : 19
questions.explanation: 17 and 19 are consecutive prime numbers, 2 apart; so are 29 and 31. 27 is not prime, and neither 43 and 53 nor 31 and 41 are consecutive primes.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'GANT' is coded as '126', and 'PROM' is coded as '186'. How will 'GAIL' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The letters' places in the alphabet are added and the sum multiplied by 3: GANT → (7 + 1 + 14 + 20) × 3 = 126 and PROM → (16 + 18 + 15 + 13) × 3 = 186. So GAIL → (7 + 1 + 9 + 12) × 3 = 87.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. All X are B. II. All N are X. Conclusions: I. All N are B. II. Some B are X.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: All N are X and all X are B, so all N are B (I). As all X are B, some B are X (II). Both follow.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. RL : VJ :: AN : ?
questions.explanation: The first letter moves 4 places forward and the second 2 back: R → V and L → J. So A → E and N → L: EL.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘× ‘ are interchanged and also ‘5’ and ‘9’ are interchanged? 3 + 9 – 6 × 5 ÷ 3 = ?
questions.explanation: After the interchanges: 3 × 5 − 6 + 9 ÷ 3 = 15 − 6 + 3 = 12.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. GAP : EYN :: MAD : KYB :: FILE : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places back: GAP → EYN and MAD → KYB. So FILE → DGJC.

questions.text: By interchanging the given two signs, which of the following equations will NOT be correct? × and –; I. 17 – 21 + 86 ÷ 2 × 13 = 387; II. 10 + 63 – 12 × 259 ÷ 7 = 739
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs, I becomes 17 × 21 + 86 ÷ 2 − 13 = 357 + 43 − 13 = 387, which is correct. II becomes 10 + 63 × 12 − 259 ÷ 7 = 10 + 756 − 37 = 729, not 739.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some mangoes are radish and no radish is an apple. All apples are tomatoes. Conclusions: I: All radish being tomatoes is a possibility. II: Some radishes are tomatoes.
questions.explanation: No radish is an apple, but nothing stops every radish being a tomato that is not an apple, so I is a possibility. No statement links radishes and tomatoes for certain, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Seven boys B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6 and B7 are sitting around a circular table, facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). B3 is second to the left of B6. B1 is third to the left of B3. B7 is third to the left of B6. B4 is not the immediate neighbour of B6. B2 is not the immediate neighbour of B1, B5 is the immediate neighbour of B1 and B6.. Three out of the following four options are similar by a certain logic and form a group. Which of the following does NOT belong to that group?
questions.explanation: Facing the centre, left is clockwise. Going clockwise from B6 the order is B6, B2, B3, B7, B4, B1, B5. In three options each boy is second to the right of the one before (B3, B6, B1; B6, B1, B7; B2, B5, B4); in B7, B4, B1 each is the immediate left neighbour of the one before.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'SLID' is written as 'TMHC', and 'LIST' is written as 'MJRS'. How will 'PILE' be written in that code language?
questions.explanation: The first two letters move 1 place forward and the last two 1 place back: SLID → TMHC and LIST → MJRS. So PILE → QJKD.

questions.text: 6 persons A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a rectangular table (not necessarily in the same order) facing towards the centre. 4 persons are sitting at each corner, and one person is sitting at the middle of each shorter side of the table. B is an immediate neighbour of D and C. F is an immediate neighbour of A and D. E is an immediate neighbour of A and C. F is not sitting at any of the corners. Which of the following pairs represents the persons who are sitting exactly opposite to each other?
questions.explanation: B sits between D and C, F between D and A, and E between A and C, so the order round the table is F, D, B, C, E, A. F is at the middle of one shorter side, so C, three places away, is at the middle of the other, directly opposite F. The corners opposite each other across the centre are D and E, and B and A.

questions.text: Seven friends A, B, C, D, E, F and G have a different number of bikes. D has more bikes than F, but less bikes than G. F has less bikes than A, and A does not have the highest number of bikes. Four persons have more bikes than C. E has the least and D has the third highest number of bikes. B has less bikes than G. Who has the highest number of bikes?
questions.explanation: C is fifth (four have more), E is last and D third. G has more than D, while A is not the highest, F has fewer than D and B fewer than G, so only G can have the most.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 8 : 32 :: 12 : 72 :: 18 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second number is half the square of the first: 8²/2 = 32 and 12²/2 = 72. So 18²/2 = 162.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 16, 32, 14, 19, 37, 21, 22, 42, ?, 25, 47, 35
questions.explanation: Taken in threes, the first terms rise by 3 (16, 19, 22, 25), the second by 5 (32, 37, 42, 47) and the third by 7 (14, 21, ?, 35), so ? = 28.

questions.text: In a certain code language, '693' means 'Neha likes cakes', '135' means 'cakes are sweet', '254' means 'we are girls', then what is the code for 'sweet' in the same code language?
questions.explanation: 'Cakes' is common to the first two sentences and 3 to their codes; 'are' is common to the last two and 5 to their codes. That leaves 1 for 'sweet'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'GRAY' is coded as ‘718125', 'FOMK' is coded as ‘6151311'. How will 'CBHL' be coded in that code language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as its place in the alphabet: G7 R18 A1 Y25 → 718125 and F6 O15 M13 K11 → 6151311. So C3 B2 H8 L12 → 32812.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word and the fourth word is related to the third word. Water : Thirst :: Food : Hunger :: Rest : ?
questions.explanation: Water relieves thirst and food relieves hunger; likewise rest relieves exhaustion.

questions.text: Which of the following dances is popularly known as the Gotipua Dance?
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives Bandha Nritya, the acrobatic part of Gotipua, Odisha's tradition in which young boys dressed as girls dance in praise of Jagannath and Krishna, holding difficult poses called bandha. Garba is from Gujarat, Bhangra from Punjab and Lavani from Maharashtra.

questions.text: Which Article of the Indian Constitution states that ‘The State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India’?
questions.explanation: Article 44, a Directive Principle of State Policy, asks the State to endeavour to secure a uniform civil code. Article 40 deals with village panchayats, Article 42 with just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief, and Article 46 with the interests of weaker sections.

questions.text: What is the total stock of money in circulation among the public at a particular point of time called?
questions.explanation: Money supply is the total stock of money, currency and deposits, held by the public at a point in time.

questions.text: Who is the first Indian woman to win the Grammy Award?
questions.explanation: Tanvi Shah, who wrote the Spanish lyrics of 'Jai Ho' from 'Slumdog Millionaire', shared the 2010 Grammy for Best Song Written for Motion Picture, Television or Other Visual Media.

questions.text: How many General Elections to the Lok Sabha have been held till April 2022?
questions.explanation: The election of April-May 2019 was the 17th general election to the Lok Sabha, counting from the first in 1951-52; the next was not due until 2024.

questions.text: Sri Lanka is separated from India by the ______.
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait, between Tamil Nadu and northern Sri Lanka, separates the two countries. The Strait of Malacca lies between Malaysia and Sumatra, Gibraltar between Spain and Morocco, and the Bering Strait between Russia and Alaska.

questions.text: In which state does the Tapi river originate?
questions.explanation: The Tapi rises near Multai in the Betul district of Madhya Pradesh and flows west through Maharashtra and Gujarat to the Arabian Sea.

questions.text: The Government of India initiated the comprehensive Family Planning Programme in ______.
questions.explanation: The Government of India began a comprehensive Family Planning Programme in 1952, seeing planned families as a way to better individual health and welfare.

questions.text: Under whose captainship did India win all three major ICC trophies in white-ball cricket till 2021?
questions.explanation: Under M S Dhoni India won the ICC World Twenty20 in 2007, the ODI World Cup in 2011 and the Champions Trophy in 2013.

questions.text: Gautamiputra Shri Satakarni was a ruler of which dynasty?
questions.explanation: Gautamiputra Satakarni was the greatest of the Satavahana kings; his mother Gautami Balashri's inscription at Nasik records his victories over the Shakas.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following was a leader of the Khilafat Movement?
questions.explanation: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad was among the leaders of the Khilafat Movement, with the Ali brothers, Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali.

questions.text: Which of the following teams won the first edition of ISL (Indian Super League)?
questions.explanation: Atletico de Kolkata won the first Indian Super League in 2014, beating Kerala Blasters 1-0 in the final.

questions.text: In which state of India is the Nongkrem dance festival celebrated?
questions.explanation: Nongkrem, a harvest thanksgiving festival of the Khasi people, is held at Smit near Shillong in Meghalaya.

questions.text: In which year, did Sher Khan defeat Humayun at Kanauj?
questions.explanation: Sher Khan (later Sher Shah Suri), who had beaten Humayun at Chausa in 1539, defeated him again at Kanauj in 1540 and drove him out of India.

questions.text: Which of the following diseases is caused by insulin deficiency or insulin resistance?
questions.explanation: In diabetes mellitus the pancreas makes too little insulin or the body's cells respond poorly to it, so blood sugar stays high. Beri-beri is caused by a lack of vitamin B1.

questions.text: Who became the first woman Chairperson of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) in 2022?
questions.explanation: Madhabi Puri Buch, earlier a whole-time member of SEBI, became its first woman chairperson in March 2022, succeeding Ajay Tyagi.

questions.text: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) 2005 provides _________ days of assured employment every year to every rural household.
questions.explanation: MGNREGA guarantees at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer for unskilled manual work.

questions.text: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, while presenting Union Budget for 2022-23 announced a programme called ‘Parvatmala’. This programme was announced to develop _______.
questions.explanation: Parvatmala, the National Ropeways Development Programme announced in the 2022-23 Budget, is to build ropeways in hilly areas on a public-private partnership basis, in place of roads where these are difficult.

questions.text: ‘The Race of My Life : An Autobiography’ is the autobiography of which of the following persons?
questions.explanation: 'The Race of My Life' (2013) is the autobiography of the sprinter Milkha Singh, written with his daughter Sonia Sanwalka.

questions.text: The splitting of white light into its component colours is called ______.
questions.explanation: A prism splits white light into its colours because each colour is refracted by a different amount; this splitting is called dispersion.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: After the Revolt of 1857 was put down by Britishers, which Mughal ruler was forced to leave the country?
questions.explanation: After the revolt was put down, the British tried Bahadur Shah Zafar, the last Mughal emperor, and exiled him to Rangoon in Burma, where he died in 1862.

questions.text: Which of the following is known as artificial silk?
questions.explanation: Rayon is made from wood pulp (cellulose) and looks and feels like silk, so it is called artificial silk. Nylon, polyester and acrylic are fully synthetic fibres.

questions.text: Which of the following is a warm current?
questions.explanation: The Gulf Stream carries warm water from the Gulf of Mexico north-east across the Atlantic. The Labrador, Falkland and Canary currents are cold.

questions.text: Which Bharatanatyam dancer became the second youngest dancer to be honoured with the 'Padma Shri' award in 1991?
questions.explanation: Alarmel Valli, a Bharatanatyam dancer of the Pandanallur style, received the Padma Shri in 1991. Hema Malini received it in 2000 and Narthaki Nataraj in 2019.

questions.text: Mukteshwara Temple is a 10th-century Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva, located in __________.
questions.explanation: The Mukteshvara temple at Bhubaneswar, Odisha, a small 10th-century Shiva temple, is known for its carved torana (gateway arch).

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Elizabeth beat her rival with the gold medal in the 2021 summer Olympics.
options: with the gold medal in the
questions.explanation: One beats a rival 'to' a prize, not 'with' it: 'Elizabeth beat her rival to the gold medal'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Grieve
questions.explanation: To 'grieve' is to feel deep sorrow, especially over a death: to 'mourn'. 'Rejoice' is its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Insatiable
questions.explanation: 'Insatiable' means impossible to satisfy, so its opposite is 'fulfilled', that is satisfied. 'Greedy' is close to a synonym.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Green tea is good for not only the health but also for ______ skin.
questions.explanation: Green tea is said to give 'glowing', that is healthy and radiant, skin. 'Caustic' means burning and 'laborious' needing hard work, and skin is not 'emotional'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. “Major hubs of” the information technology industry is the Silicon Valley of Central California.
questions.explanation: The singular verb 'is' and the one Silicon Valley need a singular subject: 'A major hub of the information technology industry is the Silicon Valley'.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. My mother’s sister “work since eight” hours every weekday.
questions.explanation: The singular subject 'my mother's sister' takes 'works', and a length of time takes 'for', not 'since': 'works for eight hours'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'mismatch', with no final 'e'.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. Story of an individual written by himself
questions.explanation: An autobiography is the story of a person's life written by that person; a biography is written by someone else.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. India has joined / the global fight / among tax evasion.
questions.explanation: One fights 'against' something: 'the global fight against tax evasion'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I like eating chocolates, ______ I hate dark ones.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 'but', which introduces an exception to the first clause: chocolates in general are liked, the dark ones are not. 'For' and 'because' would give a reason; 'while' (whereas) can also mark a contrast, though 'but' is the natural link for an exception like this.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required.’ We made sure our new house “were closer” to a good primary school when moving home last summer.
questions.explanation: 'House' is singular, so the verb is 'was': 'our new house was close to a good primary school'. 'Were closed' and 'was closing' change the sense.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The situation turned ugly as the crowd ______ to riot.
questions.explanation: The sentence is in the past ('turned'), so the simple past 'began' is needed; 'begun' is the past participle and would need 'had'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. Some simple changes in eating habits can “alleviate” nausea.
questions.explanation: To 'alleviate' is to make pain or discomfort less severe: to 'relieve'. 'Exacerbate' means the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Chase rainbows
questions.explanation: To 'chase rainbows' is to pursue goals or hopes that can never be realised.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Hold someone or something at bay
options: Trap or corner a person or animal being hunted or chased
To seek punishment for a person or group
Prevent someone or something from moving closer
To thrive or to grow very successfully
questions.explanation: To 'hold someone or something at bay' is to keep them from coming closer or doing harm.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I ______ wish I hadn't invited him.
questions.explanation: 'I almost wish' softens the regret: the speaker very nearly regrets the invitation. None of the other words fits before 'wish'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Alleviate
questions.explanation: To 'alleviate' is to make something less severe, and to 'aggravate' is to make it worse. 'Soothe' and 'ameliorate' are close in meaning to 'alleviate'.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. She is brave than any other girl in the office.
questions.explanation: A comparison with 'than any other' needs the comparative: 'She is braver than any other girl in the office.'

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. Why are you “looking on my” face like this?
questions.explanation: One looks 'at' a person or thing: 'Why are you looking at my face like this?' 'Looked' does not fit after 'are'.

questions.text: Select the option that corrects the incorrectly spelt words in the given sentence. Ventilaton system is mising in this room.
options: Ventiltion system is missing in this room.
Ventilation system is mising in this rum.
Ventilation system is missing in this room.
Wentilation system is mesing in this room.
questions.explanation: The correct spellings are 'ventilation' and 'missing'; the other sentences misspell 'ventilation', 'missing' or 'room'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Ants, like most insects, have (1) ______ are known as compound eyes. This means their eyes have multiple lenses, (2) ______ in general, most species of ant do not have particularly great eyes for seeing (3) ______ far. Ants can detect movement and see the areas around them, but (4) ______ more on senses and information they get from their legs and antennae (5) ______ from their eyes.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'What' introduces a noun clause meaning 'the things that': ants have 'what are known as compound eyes'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Ants, like most insects, have (1) ______ are known as compound eyes. This means their eyes have multiple lenses, (2) ______ in general, most species of ant do not have particularly great eyes for seeing (3) ______ far. Ants can detect movement and see the areas around them, but (4) ______ more on senses and information they get from their legs and antennae (5) ______ from their eyes.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: The eyes have many lenses, 'but' they still do not see well: the two clauses contrast.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Ants, like most insects, have (1) ______ are known as compound eyes. This means their eyes have multiple lenses, (2) ______ in general, most species of ant do not have particularly great eyes for seeing (3) ______ far. Ants can detect movement and see the areas around them, but (4) ______ more on senses and information they get from their legs and antennae (5) ______ from their eyes.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Very' modifies the adverb 'far': ants cannot see 'very far'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Ants, like most insects, have (1) ______ are known as compound eyes. This means their eyes have multiple lenses, (2) ______ in general, most species of ant do not have particularly great eyes for seeing (3) ______ far. Ants can detect movement and see the areas around them, but (4) ______ more on senses and information they get from their legs and antennae (5) ______ from their eyes.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: One 'relies on' something: ants 'rely more on' the senses of their legs and antennae.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Ants, like most insects, have (1) ______ are known as compound eyes. This means their eyes have multiple lenses, (2) ______ in general, most species of ant do not have particularly great eyes for seeing (3) ______ far. Ants can detect movement and see the areas around them, but (4) ______ more on senses and information they get from their legs and antennae (5) ______ from their eyes.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'More' in a comparison is followed by 'than': more on their legs and antennae 'than from their eyes'.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 34, 102, 612, 5508, ?

In a supermarket there are seven toys, A, K, L, P, M, S and T, of different heights. L is taller than S, but shorter than M. K is taller than P. A is taller than only T. L is shorter than only three toys. T is the shortest and M is taller than K. The height of S is shorter than how many toys?
questions.explanation: T is the shortest and A next, and L, shorter than only three, is fourth from the top. As S is shorter than L, those three can only be M, K and P (M > K > P), so S is fifth. S is shorter than four toys: M, K, P and L.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 45, 46, 50, 59, 75, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are the squares 1, 4, 9, 16; the next is 25: 75 + 25 = 100.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'KING' is coded as '16181320', and 'HOP' is coded as '191211'. How will 'STA' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as its place in the reversed alphabet (27 minus its place): K I N G → 16 18 13 20 and H O P → 19 12 11. So S T A → 8 7 26: 8726.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fourth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and fifth number is related to sixth number. 11 : 1000 :: ? : 1728 :: 9 : 512
questions.explanation: Each number is paired with the cube of one less than itself: (11 − 1)³ = 1000 and (9 − 1)³ = 512. As 1728 = 12³, the missing number is 13.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'GREATR' is written as 'OZMIBZ', and 'POINTA' is written as 'XWQVBI'. How will 'FORTAP' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 8 places forward, wrapping round after Z: G → O, R → Z, T → B, A → I. So F O R T A P → N W Z B I X.

questions.text: Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table facing the centre (not necessarily in the same order). A sits third to the left of D. D sits to the immediate right of B. B sits second to the left of E. C sits second to the right of F. Who sits second to the right of A?
questions.explanation: Taking the seats in order to each person's left, the arrangement is D, B, C, A, F, E (and back to D). Going to A's right, C is first and B second.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No basket is a trolley. No trolley is a suitcase. Conclusions: I. Some baskets being suitcases is a possibility. II. Some suitcases are baskets.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows
questions.explanation: Both statements are negative and say nothing about baskets and suitcases together, so the two may or may not overlap: the possibility in I holds, but II is not certain.

questions.text: After interchanging the given two digits 4 and 6, what will be the value of the following equation? 5 + 3 × 4 – 6 ÷ 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging 4 and 6: 5 + 3 × 6 − 4 ÷ 2 = 5 + 18 − 2 = 21.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘×’ and ‘ – ‘ are interchanged and also ‘+’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 27 × 8 − 3 ÷ 4 + 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 27 − 8 × 3 + 4 ÷ 2 = 27 − 24 + 2 = 5.

questions.text: Eight girls A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H are sitting in a row, facing towards the north (but not necessarily in the same order). Neither C nor D is at the extreme ends of the row. H is at the extreme right end of the row. Only E is sitting between D and F. Only G is sitting between F and H. C and A are the immediate neighbours of B.Which of the following statements is/are correct? I. D is fourth to the left of H. II. D is the immediate neighbour of B.
questions.explanation: H is at the right end, with G, F, E and D to its left in that order. B sits between C and A in the first three seats, and as C is not at an end, the row is A B C D E F G H. D is fourth to the left of H, but B is not next to D: only I is true.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. No X is L. II. All M are X. Conclusions: I. No L is X. II. No L is M. III. All M are L.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: 'No X is L' converts to 'No L is X' (I). As every M is an X and no X is an L, no M is an L, so no L is an M (II), and III is false.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'BALL' is coded as '27' and 'BACK' is coded as '17'. How will 'RACE' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: The code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet: BALL = 2 + 1 + 12 + 12 = 27 and BACK = 2 + 1 + 3 + 11 = 17. So RACE = 18 + 1 + 3 + 5 = 27.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. AAI, AEI, AII, AOI, ?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters stay A and I while the middle letter runs through the vowels A, E, I, O, U: AUI.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed) (48, 8, 12); (42, 6, 14)
questions.explanation: The first number is half the product of the other two: 8 × 12 ÷ 2 = 48 and 6 × 14 ÷ 2 = 42. Likewise 22 × 4 ÷ 2 = 44.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'EARTH' is written as '5118208' and 'BOOK' is written as '2151511'. How will 'COUNTRY' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is written as its place in the alphabet: E A R T H → 5 1 18 20 8 and B O O K → 2 15 15 11. So C O U N T R Y → 3 15 21 14 20 18 25: 3152114201825.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. BJ : HP :: TQ : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 6 places forward: B → H and J → P. So T → Z and Q → W: ZW.

questions.text: Select the option in which the pair of letter-clusters share the same relationship as that shared by the given letter-clusters. FAIR : GYJP
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, −2, +1, −2: F A I R → G Y J P. Likewise C R O W → D P P U.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. MET : NGW :: SAF : TCI :: YEL : ?
questions.explanation: The letters move +1, +2 and +3: M E T → N G W and S A F → T C I. So Y E L → Z G O.

questions.text: According to the Indian Constitution, the House of People shall consist of not more than ______ members to represent the Union territories.
questions.explanation: Article 81(1)(b) allows not more than twenty members of the House of the People (Lok Sabha) to represent the Union territories.

questions.text: In which state of India is the Wangala festival celebrated?
questions.explanation: Wangala, the 'hundred drums' festival, is the post-harvest festival of the Garo people of Meghalaya, held in honour of the sun god Saljong.

questions.text: Who among the following Chahamana ruler defeated Sultan Muhammad Ghori in 1191?
questions.explanation: Prithviraja III (Prithviraj Chauhan) defeated Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain in 1191; Ghori defeated him at Tarain the next year.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year was Sati banned in India?
questions.explanation: Lord William Bentinck's Bengal Sati Regulation (Regulation XVII) of 1829 declared sati illegal, a reform Raja Ram Mohan Roy had long campaigned for.

questions.text: Who among the following was the founder of the Rashtrakuta dynasty?
questions.explanation: Dantidurga founded the Rashtrakuta dynasty in the mid-8th century, overthrowing the Chalukyas of Badami. Dhruva, Govinda III and Amoghavarsha were later Rashtrakuta kings.

questions.text: 'The White Tiger provides' a darkly humorous perspective of India’s class struggle in a globalised world. It is written by __________.
questions.explanation: 'The White Tiger', Aravind Adiga's first novel, won the Booker Prize in 2008.

questions.text: In basketball, a free-throw is worth how many points?
questions.explanation: A successful free throw scores 1 point; a field goal scores 2 points, or 3 from beyond the three-point line.

questions.text: Bidar Fort is situated in which state of India?
questions.explanation: Bidar Fort stands in Bidar, in northern Karnataka; the Bahmani sultans made Bidar their capital in the 15th century and rebuilt the fort.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT an example of Pteridophyta?
questions.explanation: Funaria is a moss, a bryophyte. Selaginella, Equisetum (horsetail) and Pteris (a fern) are pteridophytes.

questions.text: The plate movements on earth are classified into ______ types.
questions.explanation: Plate movements are grouped by their boundaries into three types: divergent (plates moving apart), convergent (moving together) and transform (sliding past each other).

questions.text: Who among the following became the Brand Ambassador of Khadi Prakritik Paint in July 2021?
questions.explanation: On 6 July 2021 Nitin Gadkari, then Union Minister for MSME, opened KVIC's automated Khadi Prakritik Paint unit in Jaipur and declared himself brand ambassador of the paint, which is made from cow dung.

questions.text: How many organs of government are there according to the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Constitution sets up three organs of government: the legislature, the executive and the judiciary.

questions.text: The Indian census is generally held every ______.
questions.explanation: India's census is decennial, held once every ten years (1951, 1961 and so on to 2011).

questions.text: As announced in the Union Budget of Financial Year 2022, corporate surcharge was reduced from 12% to ______.
questions.explanation: SSC's key gives 7%: the Union Budget 2022-23, presented on 1 February 2022, cut the surcharge on co-operative societies with income above ₹1 crore and up to ₹10 crore from 12% to 7%, the rate companies in that band already paid. The question calls it the corporate surcharge.

questions.text: As per Census 2011, which of the following union territories of India has the lowest population?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 counted 64,473 people in Lakshadweep, the fewest of any Union territory.

questions.text: ‘Waghya Murali’ dance, associated with Lord Khandoba, originated in which state of India?
questions.explanation: Waghya Murali is a folk dance of Maharashtra performed by the waghyas and muralis, devotees dedicated to Khandoba, whose chief temple is at Jejuri.

questions.text: Who among the following is the first singer to be presented with India’s highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna?
questions.explanation: The Carnatic singer M. S. Subbulakshmi received the Bharat Ratna in 1998, the first musician to be given it. Bismillah Khan, a shehnai player, received it in 2001.

questions.text: Where was the Formula One 2013 Indian Grand Prix held?
questions.explanation: The Indian Grand Prix, held from 2011 to 2013, was run at the Buddh International Circuit in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh.

questions.text: Of the options listed below, the speed of sound is highest in _____ at 25°C.
questions.explanation: Sound travels fastest in solids: at 25°C about 6420 m/s in aluminium, against about 1284 m/s in hydrogen, 1207 m/s in ethanol and 316 m/s in oxygen.

questions.text: The core of the earth is mainly made up of ______.
questions.explanation: The earth's core is made mainly of nickel and iron, which is why it is called the 'nife' layer.

questions.text: PM-DevINE is the Prime Minister’s development initiative for ______ India.
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister's Development Initiative for North-East Region (PM-DevINE) was announced in the Union Budget 2022-23 to fund infrastructure and social development projects in the North-East.

questions.text: As per Census 2011, under which of the following ranges does the literacy rate in India fall?
questions.explanation: Census 2011 put India's literacy rate at 74.04%, within the 70%-75% range.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Who among the following emphasised the worship of God as Nirankar (formless) in Punjab, India?
questions.explanation: Baba Dayal Das founded the Nirankari movement in the 19th century, preaching the worship of God as Nirankar, the formless one. Baba Ram Singh led the Namdhari (Kuka) movement.

questions.text: Starch in potatoes reacts with _____, turning to a blue colour.
questions.explanation: Iodine forms a blue-black complex with starch, the usual test for starch in foods such as potatoes.

questions.text: Indrani Rahman was associated with which classical dance of India? I. Bharatanatyam dance; II. Odissi dance
questions.explanation: Indrani Rahman trained in several classical forms, Bharatanatyam among them, and was one of the first professional dancers to bring Odissi to the stage, performing it in India and abroad.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. The playground was way “large then I had” imagined, and in cleaning it, my back began to ache.
questions.explanation: A comparison needs the comparative 'larger' and 'than', not 'then': 'The playground was way larger than I had imagined.'

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. To foot the bill
questions.explanation: To 'foot the bill' is to pay for something, often on behalf of others.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. “Shall you pass” me that pasta bowl?
questions.explanation: 'Shall' makes offers and suggestions with 'I' or 'we' ('Shall I pass it?'); a polite request to someone else takes 'can' or 'could': 'Can you pass me that pasta bowl?'

questions.text: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. He had begun to dig / diligent along the / low tideline and had / captured two clams.
questions.explanation: 'Dig' is a verb, so it is described by an adverb: 'He had begun to dig diligently along the low tideline'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I ______ your remaining project if you get groceries for me from the market.
questions.explanation: A likely condition in the present ('if you get') takes 'will' in the main clause, the first conditional: 'I will do your remaining project'. 'Would do' would need 'if you got'.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Stringent' is spelt correctly. The others should be 'majestic', 'flexible' and 'faltering'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Which _____ should I take to reach the railway station?
questions.explanation: A 'route' is the way taken to reach a place. A 'root' is part of a plant, 'rote' is learning by repetition and a 'riot' is a violent disturbance.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Writing books about how to ______ on the internet seems like a great idea.
questions.explanation: To 'make a fortune' is to earn a great deal of money, which is why such books seem a great idea.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I can’t control my _____ these days because I got selected for a job.
questions.explanation: Being selected for a job makes one excited, so it is 'excitement' that is hard to control.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The Lebanese army raided the boat and ______ dozens of water bottles, tuna cans, loaves of bread, boxes of Picon cheese and life jackets.
questions.explanation: Raiding the boat, the army 'discovered' (found) what was on board. Things already there cannot be 'created' or 'invented', and one 'learns' facts, not objects.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. My elder brother is so innocent that winning an argument against him is like “shooting fish in a barrel.”
questions.explanation: 'Like shooting fish in a barrel' describes something ridiculously easy to do.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Sacred
questions.explanation: 'Sacred' means holy, set apart for God: 'consecrated'. 'Submissive' means obedient and 'adamant' refusing to change one's mind.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. The study of different skin diseases
questions.explanation: Dermatology is the study of the skin and its diseases. Neurology deals with the nervous system and radiology with X-rays and other imaging.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who is hostile and violent
questions.explanation: An 'aggressive' person is hostile and ready to attack. 'Agreeable' is nearly its opposite, and 'idle' means lazy.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Plausible
questions.explanation: 'Plausible' means seeming reasonable or believable: 'credible'. 'Untenable' and 'irrational' are nearly its opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Hilarious
questions.explanation: 'Hilarious' means extremely funny, so its opposite is 'humourless', lacking any humour.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. A significant number of students volunteers each year for environmental projects.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' means 'many' and takes a plural verb: 'A significant number of students volunteer each year'. ('The number of' would take a singular one.)

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. Time and technology are two important factor that change substances into resources.
questions.explanation: 'Two' needs a plural noun: 'two important factors that change substances into resources'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. Can you (1) ______ a deaf woman writing stories about a war? Well, Laura Redden Searing did this. Moreover, she went to foreign countries to write stories. She was very ill when she was 11 years old. Because of this, she lost her (2) ______. She went to the Missouri School for the Deaf. Laura was 19 years old when she went to work for a newspaper. She wrote about people, places and art. In 1859, most women were just wives and (3) ______. They did not work outside the home; otherwise, their husbands would be angry. Due to this feeling, Laura used a (4) ______ name when she wrote her stories. She called herself Howard Glyndon. She thought that unless she used a masculine name, people would be (5) ______ since they did not think that women should write for newspapers.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: 'Can you imagine ...?' asks the reader to picture something surprising: a deaf woman reporting on a war.

questions.explanation: People who thought women should not write for newspapers would be 'hostile', that is opposed and unfriendly, to her.

questions.text: After interchanging the given two signs, what will be the value of the following expression? × and ÷; 20 + 5 ÷ 6 × 2 – 5
questions.explanation: After interchanging × and ÷: 20 + 5 × 6 ÷ 2 − 5 = 20 + 15 − 5 = 30.

questions.text: The IQ of 7 boys B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6 and B7 is tested and the values are compared. B2 has a higher IQ than B6. B5 has the third lowest IQ. B4 has a higher IQ than 6 boys. B3 has an IQ less than B2. B1 has a higher IQ than B2. B7 has the least IQ. Who has the second highest IQ?
questions.explanation: B4 is highest, B7 lowest and B5 fifth. B1 is above B2, which is above both B3 and B6, so B1 takes the second place and B2 the third.

questions.text: Identify the number that does NOT belong to the following series. 49, 98, 196, 394, 784, 1568
questions.explanation: Each term is double the one before: 49, 98, 196, 392, 784, 1568. 394 should be 392.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: No T is G. Some M are T. Conclusions: I. No G is T. II. All M are G.
options: Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
Both conclusions I and II follow.
questions.explanation: 'No T is G' converts to 'No G is T', so I follows. The M that are T cannot be G, so 'All M are G' is false: only I follows.

questions.text: Select the option in which the numbers shares the same relationship as that shared by the numbers in the given set. (132, 186, 240) (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /deleting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
questions.explanation: The numbers rise by 54 each time: 132 + 54 = 186 and 186 + 54 = 240. Likewise 148 + 54 = 202 and 202 + 54 = 256.

questions.text: After interchanging which two signs will the value of the given expression be ‘35’? 13 + 91 – 3 ÷ 529 × 23

8 persons D, E, F, G, H, I, J and K are sitting around a square table, facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). Four persons are sitting at the corners and four persons are sitting at the middle of the sides of the square table. D is sitting at one side and opposite to K. G is sitting at a corner and to the immediate right of D. D is the immediate neighbour of E and G. I is not the immediate neighbour of H. F is sitting at one side and opposite to H. Who is sitting just diagonally opposite to I?
questions.explanation: D and K sit at the middles of opposite sides, with G at the corner on D's right and E at the corner on D's left; F and H take the other two middle seats and I and J the corners beside K. As I does not sit next to H, I is diagonally opposite E when H sits next to E, or opposite G when H sits next to G; G is not an option, so the answer is E.

questions.text: 6 persons A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a rectangular table, facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). One person is sitting on each of the smaller sides. Two persons are sitting on each of the bigger sides. No person is sitting at the corners. C and F are sitting on the same side. B is sitting opposite to A. F is the immediate neighbour of B. A is sitting second to the left of D. Counting towards the left of D, how many persons are sitting between A and D?
questions.explanation: A sits second to the left of D, so counting towards D's left exactly one person sits between them.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the sixth number in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and the third number is related to the fourth number. 34 : 12 :: 28 : 16 :: ? : 15
questions.explanation: The second number is the product of the first number's digits: 3 × 4 = 12 and 2 × 8 = 16. Likewise 3 × 5 = 15.

questions.text: Identify the number that does NOT belong to the following series. 14, 21, 63, 378, 3402
questions.explanation: The multipliers double: 14 × 1.5 = 21, 21 × 3 = 63, 63 × 6 = 378, so the next term should be 378 × 12 = 4536, not 3402.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'POKER' is written as 'IHDXK' and 'FANDS' is written as 'YTGWL'. How will 'AQBCG' be written in that code language?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 7 places back, wrapping round after A: P → I, O → H, K → D, E → X, R → K. So A → T, Q → J, B → U, C → V, G → Z: TJUVZ.

questions.text: Select the option in which the pair of letter-clusters share the same relationship as that shared by the given pair of letter-clusters. ROP : NMP :: ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places back and the cluster is reversed: ROP → PMN → NMP. Likewise MUG → KSE → ESK.

questions.text: In a certain code language 'who are you' is written as 'Sue Re Nik', 'they is you' is written as 'Pi Re Sor', and 'they are dangerous' is written as 'Pi Nik Zhi'. What is the code for 'dangerous' in that code language?
questions.explanation: 'You' is common to the first two sentences (Re), 'they' to the last two (Pi) and 'are' to the first and last (Nik). So 'dangerous' is Zhi.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word and the fourth word is related to the third word. Pitch : Cricket :: Court : Badminton :: Ring : ?
questions.explanation: Cricket is played on a pitch and badminton on a court; boxing is fought in a ring.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: I. All X are B. II. No C is X. Conclusions: I. Some B are not C. II. All C are B. III. Some X are C.
options: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions II and III follow
questions.explanation: Every X is a B and no X is a C, so the B that are X are not C: I follows. Nothing says every C is a B, so II does not follow, and III contradicts 'No C is X'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘random boys talk’ is written as ‘8 3 P’, ‘talk too much girls’ is written as ‘3 4 2 6’. How will ‘talk’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: 'Talk' is the only word in both sentences and 3 the only code in both, so 'talk' is written as 3.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. BOND, FKRZ, JGVV, NCZR, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters move +4 (B, F, J, N, R), the second −4 (O, K, G, C, Y), the third +4 (N, R, V, Z, D) and the fourth −4 (D, Z, V, R, N), wrapping round the alphabet: RYDN.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'DELHI' is written as 'CDKGH', 'NERVOUS' is written as 'MDQUNTR' and 'SURE' is written as 'RTQD'. What is the code for the word 'MILLION' in that code language?
questions.explanation: Each letter is replaced by the one before it: DELHI → CDKGH and SURE → RTQD. So MILLION → LHKKHNM.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. PV : MQ :: FB : ?
questions.explanation: P moves 3 places back to M and V 5 places back to Q. Likewise F → C and B → W, wrapping round after A: CW.

questions.text: Hariprasad Chaurasia is a _____ player.
questions.explanation: Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia plays the bansuri, the bamboo flute of Hindustani classical music.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: In which year did Bhagat Singh and BK Dutt throw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly?
questions.explanation: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly in Delhi on 8 April 1929, in protest against the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill, and courted arrest.

questions.text: As per the 2011 census of India, population density of which of the following states was less than 100 people per square kilometre?
questions.explanation: The 2011 census put Sikkim's population density at 86 people per square kilometre. Himachal Pradesh had 123, Rajasthan about 200 and Tripura 350.

questions.text: If ‘u’ is the object-distance, ‘v’ is the image-distance and ‘f’ is the focal length of a spherical mirror then which of the following is a correct expression for the mirror formula?
questions.explanation: For a spherical mirror the object distance u, image distance v and focal length f are related by 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. (For a lens it is 1/v − 1/u = 1/f.)

questions.text: 'Red Light On Gaadi Off' campaign was launched by the government of ______.
questions.explanation: The Delhi government launched 'Red Light On, Gaadi Off' in October 2020, asking drivers to switch off their engines at red lights to cut vehicle pollution.

questions.text: Who among the following has been ranked as the richest person in the world, as per the Forbes’ Real-Time Billionaires list 2022?
questions.explanation: Forbes' 2022 World's Billionaires list (April 2022) ranked Elon Musk first, ahead of Jeff Bezos and Bernard Arnault, and he still topped its real-time list when the exam was held in July 2022.

questions.text: Which of the following organisms is responsible for sleeping sickness?
questions.explanation: Sleeping sickness (African trypanosomiasis) is caused by the protozoan Trypanosoma, spread by the bite of the tsetse fly.

questions.text: In which state of India, is the Chapchar Kut festival celebrated?
questions.explanation: Chapchar Kut is Mizoram's spring festival, held after the forest has been cleared for jhum (shifting) cultivation.

questions.text: Rainfall is measured by an instrument called the ______.
questions.explanation: A rain gauge collects and measures rainfall. A barometer measures air pressure, an altimeter height, and a Pirani gauge very low gas pressures.

questions.text: The temples of Khajuraho are a magnificent example of the ______ of the temple.
questions.explanation: The Khajuraho temples, built under the Chandela rulers, are a classic example of the Nagara style of north India, with its curving towers (shikharas).

questions.text: ‘Bhavai’ is the traditional theatre form of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Bhavai is a folk theatre form of Gujarat (also performed in Rajasthan) that mixes dance, music and satire.

questions.text: As per the Union Budget 2022-23, how many new jobs are to be created under the productivity linked incentive scheme in 14 sectors?
questions.explanation: The Union Budget speech of 1 February 2022 said the PLI schemes in 14 sectors had the potential to create 60 lakh new jobs over the next five years.

questions.text: Manuscripts were usually written on:
questions.explanation: Manuscripts in early India were usually written on palm leaves, or on the specially prepared bark of the birch tree.

questions.text: Gatka, a traditional fighting style of the Nihang Sikh warriors, used both for self-defence as well as a sport, has originated from which of the following states of India?
questions.explanation: Gatka, the Sikh martial art of fighting with sticks and swords, comes from Punjab.

questions.text: ‘Total Recall : My Unbelievably True Life Story’ is an autobiography of:
questions.explanation: 'Total Recall: My Unbelievably True Life Story' (2012) is Arnold Schwarzenegger's autobiography. Chris Gayle's is 'Six Machine', Eddie Huang's 'Fresh Off the Boat' and I K Gujral's 'Matters of Discretion'.

questions.text: Where are villi present in the human alimentary canal?
questions.explanation: The inner wall of the small intestine carries finger-like villi, which greatly increase the surface for absorbing digested food.

questions.text: Rajaraja I, the most powerful Chola ruler, became king in ______ C.E.
questions.explanation: Rajaraja I became king in 985 CE; he expanded the Chola kingdom and built the Brihadeshwara (Rajarajeshwara) temple at Thanjavur.

questions.text: Guru Bipin Singh was known for which classical dance form?
questions.explanation: Guru Bipin Singh was a leading guru of Manipuri dance, which he researched, taught and helped spread.

questions.text: The premier iron ore exporting port of India is situated in _____.
questions.explanation: Marmagao (Mormugao) in Goa is India's premier iron ore exporting port.

questions.text: Article 43B was inserted as a _______ in the Constitution of India.
questions.explanation: The 97th Amendment (2011) inserted Article 43B, on promoting co-operative societies, into Part IV, the Directive Principles of State Policy.

questions.text: The Constitution of India states that 'no person shall be eligible for election as President of India unless he has completed the age of ______ years’.
questions.explanation: Under Article 58, a person must be a citizen of India and have completed 35 years of age to be eligible for election as President.

questions.text: If a batsman hits a ball twice other than for the purpose of protecting his wicket or with consent from the opposition then:
options: the batsman is given a warning
a bye of five runs is declared
questions.explanation: Under cricket's Laws, a batter who wilfully strikes the ball a second time, other than to guard the wicket, is out 'hit the ball twice'.

questions.text: The Tendulkar Committee Report (2011-2012) was based on ____________.
questions.explanation: The expert group headed by Suresh Tendulkar reviewed how poverty is measured in India; the Planning Commission's poverty estimates for 2011-12 used its method.

questions.topicName: Modern Indian History and Freedom Struggle
questions.text: Which of the following pairs of name of battle and year is/are correctly matched? I. Battle of Buxar – 1764; II. Battle of Plassey – 1757
questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757 and the Battle of Buxar in 1764, so both pairs are correctly matched.

questions.text: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. At seven began the education that was to making the young boy a citizen and a soldier.
options: boy a citizen and a soldier
that was to making the young
questions.explanation: 'Was to' is followed by the base form of the verb: 'the education that was to make the young boy a citizen and a soldier'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Steady
questions.explanation: 'Steady' means firm and not shaking, so its opposite is 'shaky'. 'Constant' is close in meaning to 'steady'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. He admonished his listeners _________ their wicked ways.
questions.explanation: 'Admonish' takes an object and a to-infinitive: to admonish people 'to change' their ways is to urge them firmly to do so.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence. I want you to give me this contract “in black and white.”
questions.explanation: Something 'in black and white' is set down in writing.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. I am not going to buy ______ toys for you.
questions.explanation: 'These' is the plural demonstrative that goes before a plural noun: 'these toys'. 'This' is singular, and 'them' and 'they' are pronouns that cannot stand before a noun.

questions.text: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'suddenly': 'sudden', with a double 'd', plus '-ly'.

questions.text: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
questions.explanation: 'Dissiminate' is misspelt: the word is 'disseminate', meaning to spread widely.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words. A cage for small animals
questions.explanation: A hutch is a cage or box for small animals such as rabbits. A shed and a hut are small buildings, and a cave is a hollow in rock.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select ‘No improvement required’. Getting a good night’s sleep “has a positively effect” on our wellbeing.
questions.explanation: The noun 'effect' needs the adjective 'positive', not the adverb 'positively', and the singular subject takes 'has': 'has a positive effect'. 'Affect' is usually a verb.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. My sister treats me well in the morning but at night she becomes ______.
questions.explanation: 'But' sets up a contrast with treating me well in the morning, so the blank needs a word for bad behaviour: 'awful'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Gloomy
questions.explanation: 'Gloomy' means dark or sad: 'depressing'. 'Bright' is nearly its opposite, and 'intrepid' means fearless.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. “Many an old story were retold,” and ancient conundrum repeated.
options: Many an old story was retold
Many an old stories were retold
questions.explanation: 'Many a' (or 'many an') takes a singular noun and a singular verb: 'Many an old story was retold'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Long in the tooth
questions.explanation: 'Long in the tooth' means old, too old for something.

questions.text: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. One who is not sure about God’s existence
questions.explanation: An agnostic holds that God's existence cannot be known. A pantheist identifies God with the universe, and 'haggard' means looking exhausted.

questions.text: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Scientific discoveries “is often result” of hard work by many people.
questions.explanation: The plural subject 'scientific discoveries' takes 'are', and 'result' needs the article: 'are often the result of hard work'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. The US has become far more ______ to people with all kinds of food sensitivities and diet regimens.
questions.explanation: To be 'accommodating to' people is to be willing to meet their needs, here their food sensitivities and diets.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Frank has being making / the rounds, advancing a theory / that I believe is not without merit.
options: that I believe is not without merit
questions.explanation: The present perfect continuous is 'has been' with the '-ing' form: 'Frank has been making the rounds'.

questions.text: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. Whatever a writer puts / into a story probably comes with / his own life experience.
questions.explanation: Experience comes 'from' one's life, so 'with' is the wrong preposition: '... probably comes from his own life experience'. The options split the sentence after 'comes', so the error lies in 'with his own life experience'.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. He was “critically” injured in the accident.
questions.explanation: 'Critically' injured means seriously injured: 'severely'. 'Trivially' is nearly the opposite.

questions.text: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. All of my efforts to save her life have gone in ______.
questions.explanation: To go 'in vain' is to go without success. A 'vein' carries blood, and a 'vane' is a blade turned by the wind, as on a weathervane.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In its 47 years of history, ISRO (1) ______ breakthrough work in the field of technology and even (2) ______ many vehicles into space. (3) ______ the last 47 years, ISRO has improvised and developed technology, launching (4) ______ indigenously created vehicles into space (5) ______ form a part of the Indian space journey.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.explanation: The 47 years of history run up to the present, so the present perfect fits: 'ISRO has done breakthrough work'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In its 47 years of history, ISRO (1) ______ breakthrough work in the field of technology and even (2) ______ many vehicles into space. (3) ______ the last 47 years, ISRO has improvised and developed technology, launching (4) ______ indigenously created vehicles into space (5) ______ form a part of the Indian space journey.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.explanation: Vehicles are 'launched' into space; 'launched' shares the 'has' of the first clause: ISRO 'has ... even launched many vehicles'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In its 47 years of history, ISRO (1) ______ breakthrough work in the field of technology and even (2) ______ many vehicles into space. (3) ______ the last 47 years, ISRO has improvised and developed technology, launching (4) ______ indigenously created vehicles into space (5) ______ form a part of the Indian space journey.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.explanation: 'Over the last 47 years' means during that whole period, which suits the present perfect 'has improvised and developed'.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In its 47 years of history, ISRO (1) ______ breakthrough work in the field of technology and even (2) ______ many vehicles into space. (3) ______ the last 47 years, ISRO has improvised and developed technology, launching (4) ______ indigenously created vehicles into space (5) ______ form a part of the Indian space journey.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.explanation: 'Several' goes with a plural countable noun: 'several indigenously created vehicles'. 'Much' is for uncountable nouns, 'lots' needs 'of', and 'very' cannot qualify a noun.

questions.text:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank. In its 47 years of history, ISRO (1) ______ breakthrough work in the field of technology and even (2) ______ many vehicles into space. (3) ______ the last 47 years, ISRO has improvised and developed technology, launching (4) ______ indigenously created vehicles into space (5) ______ form a part of the Indian space journey.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.explanation: 'That' introduces a relative clause about things, here the vehicles: 'vehicles ... that form a part of the Indian space journey'. 'Who' is for people.

questions.text: 6 girls J, K, L, A, B and C are sitting around a square table facing the centre (not necessarily in the same order). 4 girls are sitting in the corners and 2 girls are sitting one each in the middle of two opposite sides of the square. L and C are sitting opposite each other. L is the immediate neighbour of A and B. C is not sitting on the corner. Who are the immediate neighbours of C?
questions.explanation: C is not at a corner, so she sits in the middle of one side and L, opposite her, in the middle of the other. L's neighbours are the two corners on her side, A and B, so the two corners beside C are taken by the remaining girls, J and K.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'TOIR' is coded as '62', and 'HATE' is coded as '34'. How will 'GAYL' be coded in that language?
questions.explanation: Each code is the sum of the letters' places in the alphabet: TOIR = 20 + 15 + 9 + 18 = 62 and HATE = 8 + 1 + 20 + 5 = 34. So GAYL = 7 + 1 + 25 + 12 = 45.

questions.text: Two statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: All Books are Pens. All Pens are Pencils. Conclusions: I. All Books are Pencils. II. All Pencils are Books.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follows.
questions.explanation: All books are pens and all pens are pencils, so all books are pencils (I). The pencils need not all be books, so II does not follow.

questions.text: Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statement I: Some teeth are noses and some noses are hands. Statement II: Some hands are feet. Conclusion I: Some teeth are feet. Conclusion II: All hands are noses.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Neither conclusion I nor II follow.
questions.explanation: The teeth that are noses need not be the noses that are hands, nor those hands the ones that are feet, so I does not follow. Only some hands are known to be noses, so II does not follow either.

questions.text: Select the number from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. 1703, 1668, 1633, 1598, 1563, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is 35 less than the one before: 1563 − 35 = 1528.

questions.text: Select the letter-cluster from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series. LAS, IYR, FWQ, CUP, ?
questions.explanation: The first letters go back 3 (L, I, F, C, Z, wrapping round after A), the second back 2 (A, Y, W, U, S) and the third back 1 (S, R, Q, P, O): ZSO.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'This is my brother' is written as 'Bo UvZs Mn', 'That is my dog' is written as 'Zs Pt Uv Ga', 'This is your father' is written as 'Bo Uv Ex Yz'. How will 'brother' be written in that language?
questions.explanation: 'is' is the only word in all three sentences and 'Uv' the only code in all three; 'my' (in the first two) is 'Zs' and 'This' (in the first and third) is 'Bo'. That leaves 'Mn' for 'brother'. (The sheet prints 'Uv' and 'Zs' run together in the first code.)

questions.text: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of the following sets. (15, 135, 6)(12, 84, 5)
questions.explanation: The middle number is the first times the difference of the first and third: 15 × (15 − 6) = 135 and 12 × (12 − 5) = 84. Likewise 21 × (21 − 6) = 315.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. ACT : KCD :: EAR : OAB :: EYE : ?
questions.explanation: The first and last letters move 10 places forward, wrapping round after Z, and the middle letter stays: A → K and T → D; E → O and R → B. So EYE → OYO.

questions.text: In a certain code language, ‘mould soft gel’ is written as ‘8 6 4’, ‘gel is not hard’ is written as ‘pr kc 8 3’ and ‘hard is grey mould’ is written as ‘kc 3 4 9’. How will ‘grey soft’ be written in that language?
questions.explanation: 'gel' (in the first two) is 8 and 'mould' (in the first and third) is 4, so 'soft' is 6. 'is' and 'hard' (in the last two) are 'kc' and 3, so 'grey' is 9: 'grey soft' is '9 6'.

questions.text: In a certain code language, if wall is called door, door is called window, window is called roof, roof is called ventilator and ventilator is called floor, then what makes a way to a room?
questions.explanation: A door makes a way into a room, and a door is called 'window'.

questions.text: No two of the six friends U, V, W, X, Y and Z, are of the same height. V is taller than only three other friends. Z is only taller than X. W is shorter than U only. Find who is the third shortest among all the friends.
questions.explanation: Z is taller only than X, so X is the shortest and Z the second shortest. V, taller than three, is fourth from the bottom, and U is the tallest with W next. Y fills the third place from the bottom.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the third letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster. GROW : ITQY :: MATE : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves 2 places forward: G R O W → I T Q Y, so M A T E → O C V G.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and the fourth number is related to the third number. 15 : 36 :: 25 : 56 :: 35 : ?
questions.explanation: Each second number is twice the first plus 6: 15 × 2 + 6 = 36 and 25 × 2 + 6 = 56. So 35 × 2 + 6 = 76.

questions.text: Which two numbers (not digits) need to be interchanged to make the given equation correct? 10 × 18 + 216 ÷ 5 – 41 = 21
questions.explanation: After interchanging 18 and 5: 10 × 5 + 216 ÷ 18 − 41 = 50 + 12 − 41 = 21.

questions.text: What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘ – ‘ are interchanged and also ‘×’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged? 20 × 5 − 10 + 5 ÷ 2 = ?
questions.explanation: After interchanging the signs: 20 ÷ 5 + 10 − 5 × 2 = 4 + 10 − 10 = 4.

questions.text: Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-cluster in the same way as the second letter-cluster is related to the first letter-cluster and the fourth letter-cluster is related to the third letter-cluster. MARS : NLBZSQTR :: PLUTO : QOMKVTUSPN :: EARTH : ?
questions.explanation: Each letter becomes the letter after it followed by the letter before it: M → NL, A → BZ, R → SQ, S → TR. So E → FD, A → BZ, R → SQ, T → US and H → IG: FDBZSQUSIG.

questions.text: Six people Sumit, Aamish, Saif, Ashutosh, Anubhav and Piyush are sitting in a straight row facing North. Only one person was sitting left to Piyush. Aamish is not sitting in either corner. Anubhav is sitting immediate left to Saif. Only one person is sitting in between Piyush and Ashutosh. Who is sitting to the immediate left of Ashutosh?
questions.explanation: Piyush has one person to his left, so he is second from the left, and Ashutosh, with one person between them, is fourth. Anubhav and Saif need two adjacent seats, which leaves only the fifth and sixth; Aamish, not at an end, takes the third seat and Sumit the first. So Aamish is to Ashutosh's immediate left.

questions.text: Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series? 819, 829, 840, 852, ?
questions.explanation: The differences are 10, 11, 12 and then 13: 852 + 13 = 865.

questions.text: Who is the author of the book ‘The Great Indian Novel’?
questions.explanation: 'The Great Indian Novel' (1989) is by Shashi Tharoor; it retells the Mahabharata as a satire on India's freedom struggle and the decades after independence.

questions.text: What is the chemical name of battery acid?
